Source: You know, the truth is that this was partially my fault for leading Julien on in the first place. I knew he wasn't the one. I won't torture that poor boy any longer.
You are not one of my usual customers, stranger.
Thank you for helping me. Guendeline is so beautiful! And the necklace. It really brings out the color of her eyes.\n\nI can't wait to tell Mother all about this!
Is there something I can do for you?
Divines watch over you, friend.
Yes, may I help you?
What happened to <<1>> is a shame, but her sacrifice was not in vain.\n\n<<2>> is the only one who can hold Camlorn together.
We can't let Faolchu's curse spread to Aldcroft. Do what you can to help Gloria. \n\nI trust your abilities.
Is this the real world? Or is this yet another trick? I will not let the darkness in ….\n\nWait, this is real, isn't it? You're real. Was it you who woke me?
Thank you for your trust and your faith in me. I won't forget it.
I will do everything I can, even in this strange half-life state, to stop the spread of Reezal-Jul's evil.\n\nPlease, find my staff and give me that chance.
I have told you all I know about what happened here. If anyone knows more, it will be the Spirit Guards who patrol our walls.
We'll be ready to attack on your signal.

Testing the random text to ensure that the text does not appear cut off, missing, or with strange text characters. Now I am just going on and on because I'm trying to fill  in more text in the greeting window.
You startled me! You shouldn't sneak up on a person like that.

Over the years, I've questioned many times whether what I did was right. I wanted to save my soldiers' lives, but I only helped King Ranser spread his curse.\n\nNow, whether right or wrong, I am redeemed. The curse is lifted and the dead can rest.
What have I gotten myself into? If I get killed in battle, it's on your head.

What a fool I've been. How can someone like me compete with someone like Guendeline?\n\nI only hope that she appreciates him and makes him happy. Julien is a very good man and I'm not sure she realizes that.
As if being defeated wasn't tragic enough. I can't believe we have to force the king to surrender.\n\nNonetheless, I can't ask the men to throw away their lives for a lost cause.
You have helped S'rashi when S'rashi's own brother abandoned him, and S'rashi is very grateful.\n\nS'rashi can now pay money to Midnight Union boss, save his skin, yes?
I gather the party didn't turn out the way Her Ladyship planned. \n\nSuits me, to tell the truth.
I guess the party's over, isn't it? \n\nFine with me. Revolting, that was.
This whole thing was so terrible! Who would've known those people were just hiding outside of town planning to take over and only Julianos knows what else!\n\nI'm just glad it's all over.
Where's Heloise? What happened to her?
Please, stay back! I'm so hungry and I don't want to hurt you!
I must return to Alcaire Castle and attempt to set matters straight there, but I will be anxious to hear what you learn.\n\nI hope you find answers at Pariah Abbey.
Are you ready to depart, mortal? Are you ready to step into your nightmares?
This has all been such an ordeal. I feel like there's so much to do now that it's over.
I better get paid when this job is finished. Lanbaar's cart still looks mighty full to me.
Rest assured. I will lead us to victory. You have my word.
I—I cannot believe it! He understood you and he … he just ran away!
I know I should be grateful to you, but my lot in life still hasn't improved.\n\nBut, I should thank you for helping Alcaire.
It's good to see someone who knows how to take care of business.
I have no interest in moving to Wayrest again. Everything is cheaper here in Alcaire.
I still don't trust you, no matter what the gossips say you've done for us.
When it comes right down to it, things never really change.\n\nDon't let anyone tell you otherwise.
I still don't trust you, no matter what the gossips say you've done for us.
Extinguish the brazier. Too many have already died.
I grieve for Sir Croix and all those who died fighting for him, but there was no other way to save the Knights of the Flame.\n\nThank you for doing what I could not.
These caves have been quiet for so long, but the winds have returned and our spirits with them.\n\nYou walk among the living, yet you speak to the dead. Will you help return us to rest?
What evils have you wrought, stranger? What has befallen my dear Toves?
My forebears came to Wayrest before the last war began. \n\nIt's rather nice here, don't you think?
The Daggerfall Covenant means nothing to me. It's political jousting, as far as I'm concerned. \n\nSo long as no one takes away my ale, the king can ally with whoever he wants.
Destroy the focus crystals! I can't move while this binding spell holds me.
The Bloodthorns are holding the Duke in the lighthouse. You'll have to fight your way in there if you really plan to rescue him.
I will do anything I can to stop this darkness from spreading beyond Crestshade.\n\nFind my skull so that I can use it as a focus for my energy.

Ah! An adventurer! Always so inspiring to have someone like you around town. I hoped my son Martin would take up an exciting profession like that, but I'm beginning to think the poor boy just doesn't have it in him.\n\nHe worries me sick, you know.
You've returned. I did not expect this. Dare I hope, though? Do you know the means by which I might be released?
Once, I caught Denthis trying to make nix-hounds glow purple. Why would anyone do that?
Vivec take my brother! He ran off behind this building chanting "Eyes of Akatosh" over and over.
That almost wasn't as fun as I expected it to be. Thank you for coming after me.
Janne has left, and Murk-Watcher is one with the river. Knarstygg and Dro-Dara now return to a life of adventure.\n\nPerhaps you will see us again.
I… saw what you did for Murk-Watcher. I cannot say that I understand, but I respect her right to choose her own fate.\n\nIt is time now for Dro-Dara and I to leave.
<<1>> no longer sings. Have you taken his heart?\n\nHurry. We must move quickly if we are to renew the song.
You coming along was such a blessing.  \n\nTruly the Eight sent you! This will mean so much to Breloth. So much.
More teeth. More teeth. I can't get enough. \n\nMy grandchildren will brag about their ancestors, and show off my trophy necklace.
This one must guard the chickens!\n\nRazha must make sure nothing happens to them!

There was a pulse behind that door. Now it's drumming, drumming, drumming in my head and in my veins.\n\nI think I may need more blood soon. I feel light-headed. Did Balcone seem nervous? Maybe it's me.
You did it. I couldn't believe it when I heard the crash, but you brought the whole place down.\n\nAlmost cost you your life.
I can't thank you enough. So many people in town just want to write her off. \n\nThey're less worried about her welfare than they are about who should take authority of Wind Keep.

What a relief! I wouldn't have been comfortable just abandoning my companions, but if you're going to help them, that frees me up.\n\nAnd let me tell you, it feels good. I'm just not the settling-down type. I know that now.
Sergeant Olfin's impressed. Says you've got guts and you're fast on your feet. \n\nAssuming you can fight, I think we found the hero to finish these ogres off.
Greetings, traveller.\n\nIf you were planning to visit the graveyard behind me, you might want to come back later.
I hear the ogres made their big push and you stopped them cold, took down a whole mess of them.\n\nGore and glory! Good work!
My sword is again broken, but this time for good, and for good purpose. She has forgiven me.\n\nYou have healed a wound that was centuries old.

I'll dismiss the Blackmauls. I'll report my actions to the king. One way or the other, reparations will be made to my victims … even if I have to die to do it.\n\nYou haven't just saved my mind. You've given me a chance to redeem my honor.
If it wasn't for you and Brother Perry, I wouldn't have had the foggiest idea of what to do. Thank Azura for you both.\n\nBrother Perry's going to escort me back to Pariah Abbey. He's so brave.
I can't go home yet. Not until I catch my breath.\n\nYou have to find out who's responsible for this. Whoever it is must pay for what he did to us!
Talk to my wife please. I'm still weak from my ordeal.
You should have killed that Baron Sorick.\n\nThough I suppose that would have just caused more trouble. Maybe what you did was for the best. He's leaving, and my husband's alive.
Go now. Use that scroll near the large fire.\n\nI'll get Durak and myself to the abbey with the Scroll of Return.
That storm spirit! It's incredible!\n\nDid you summon it with the scroll? I've never seen anything like it!
You woke Durak. Incredible. \n\nI have no doubt Azura herself sent you. You will find the Dream Shard, my friend. You will save us.
Please, go to Sister Safia.\n\nAnd may the Divines bless you.
You put out the fire! Maybe this situation is about to start turning around.
Ah, it's you.
You're awake! Oh, thank you for saving our Abbot.
I failed Stormhaven. I failed everyone.
Goblins have killed my comrades. \n\nIt's time for revenge.
Have you found my children?
Hurry! Find the key! \n\nOne of those dead soldiers might have it. Did you check them?
Make it quick. Can't you see I'm bleeding to death here?

I'm awake now—the nightmare is over. My mind is clear. \n\nMemories are confused, but I know I did terrible things. The Midnight Union went horribly bad. So I've disbanded it. That was the right thing to do, wasn't it?
I saw many of my fellow wardens make it to safety. Thank you.\n\nIt's so ironic that we rely on a stranger's help after being attacked by those we considered friends.

Your help with both these matters is much appreciated. Until that damn guillotine's been dismantled, I won't be able to sleep. \n\nAnd more importantly, until the matter in Rivenspire is resolved, the Covenant will be severely weakened.
What's this? Can't you let a man enjoy a moment's rest? Are you telling me King Emeric needs this bench right now?
I've paid my debt in full. Off with you now!
Like I said, if you need to talk to the captain, you'll have to catch him up at the Cloudy Dregs.
I'll be all right. I'm hurt, but I'll live. \n\nBut I think I've been here long enough. I'm heading for points east.
Glad the Abbey sent help. We need it.
Whoever these cultists are, they've taken over the Moonlit Maw.
From now on, I'm protecting this signal fire with my life. \n\nAnyone who wants to put it out will have to go through me.
Pulled it off again, and pulled one over on Ma'jhad Kha to boot!\n\nYou are a character straight out of a storybook. I hope we cross paths again.
If I recall, Barnabe is also on duty with Geon right now. I'm sure that has something to do with his anger.
I must return to Pariah Abbey and rejoin my brothers. Our sacred duty is protecting Menevia. \n\nMay the Divines protect you.
Go. Go!\n\nI'll be fine. You have to help Elvira!

The poison is inside a crate in one of the storage buildings down by the docks but they may move it at any time.\n\nOnce you've poisoned the wine don't forget to come back and tell me all about it. I can't wait to see them swell and die before me.
It's a shame abut the Duchess, but I hear things have settled down at Castle Alcaire. That's a relief.
Unless you have information on the fugitive, I must insist you be on your way.

Search for a pristine Scamp skin, a ritual candle, and a Dremora heart. Then look for Farmer Vanne at Stonebridge Mill.\n\nYou must use the right ingredients in the right order. Only then can you free Farmer Vanne from his enchanted sleep.
You're alive. Were you successful?
Hmm. Aren't you a peculiar specimen …? \n\nWait a minute. You're not a Goblin! I know Goblins inside and out, and you're no Goblin. You're the one from the Watch!
I bet I'm going to be having nightmares for a long time after all this.\n\nTimes like these I miss having my father around.
My next assignment is in Daggerfall. At least it's bigger than Alcaire.
Find my sword. Kill the Omen. Please.
Please, go quickly. My strength has grown, and I must confess, the temptation to try to bind you to me grows as well. \n\nIf you remain, it could be dangerous … for both of us. Just go.
How did the Dwemer Tonal Architects concentrate in this cacophony? It's so noisy here!\n\nHow could they possibly make magicka vibrate in sympathy with their will?
I've studied Dwemeris for so long! I still don't understand them. \n\nTheir thoughts are as alien to me as a Daedra's.
Never have so many Knights of the Flame fallen in a single battle. It's a tragedy.
Things are settling down. Soon, we'll best these filthy ogres.
I saw you went into the mines, and came out with the stench of Goblin.  What news do you have?
It's not a long walk. Please, let's continue. I'm feeling weak.
Not calling you a liar, mind you. People have been seeing strange things of late. If you did see old Arnoit Sidrey, you wouldn't be the first.\n\nGives me the shivers, it does.
I'm sorry, I can't be bothered at the moment. Propylon readings are a hard study and I can't afford interruption.
What? How? \n\nOh, right. The book.
The Nereid is playing with more power than she can handle. We thank you for your help.
The witchmen from the Reach have never paid respect to the call of nature. They must find a way to twist nature to their will.\n\nYou've shown them that the wyresses also know brute force.
Pray for those who perished in fury.\n\nAnd pray for those here now. They must complete the tasks of those who are gone.
I'm told you defeated an Omen of Vaermina.\n\nI pray that Count Hosni recovers quicly.

It seems the crows have departed from Evermore, but the black cloud hasn't. With Bangkorai Garrison taken, there's nothing stopping the Imperials from marching here.\n\nI didn't retake the throne to watch the kingdom fall though. We'll find a way.
Footfalls shift the earth, sending shivering tremors through my roots. You have returned to me.\n\nHave you solved the question of my existence?
The corpse of a miner lays bruised and caked in coagulated blood. Judging by the wounds, this looks to be the work of Goblins.

This mostly illegible journal reads:\n\n"...While mining, we uncovered what appears to be a Daedric structure and artifact. Someone unknowingly activated the artifact, summoning a Dremora. He killed most of us.. by the eight I hope I get out of here."
The Daedric artifact hums idlely.
Your body feels tingly as you approach the propylon.
A letter sits on the table.  It looks recently written in a language you can understand.

"Days have been long and hard, but we're managing everything fine. Ore shipments have been on time and gems have been a nice bonus for us to line our pockets. I should have joined the miner's guild a while ago!"

"One of the night watches spotted a queer sight a couple nights back. Seems there were a couple Goblins not far from the mine entrance. I normally wouldn't worry too much, but a large figure was with them, grunting some sort of nonsense."
I spoke to the captain after you left. He was more than willing to help, after the good turn you gave him.\n\nThe traitor is well within our grasp.
<You see the staff in the man's hand again. Somehow, it has returned.>\n\n<Looking closer, you could almost swear that the dead man is grimacing. His lips have curled into a disdainful sneer.>
Will you be staying in Ebonheart long, serjo? \n\nI'm sure we could make your stay more pleasant.
Staying in Ebonheart long, serjo? \n\nI'm sure I could make your stay more pleasant.
I should have fought harder. I should have protected Master Muzgu.
Quickly! To save Stormhaven, I must die.
You there! Will you let your soul fall into the hands of Daedra?
None of these wasted souls will ever amount to anything. They are what they are. They will never be anything more.
Wh-what … ? Mother, is that you? I'm not ready to get up. Leave me alone … .
The dreugh are thinning out, retreating.\n\nDid you succeed?
I can't believe my sister thinks Ohama had something to do with this! Where is Father? I demand to talk to him!

When you reach the Mages Guild tower, speak to Gabrielle. She understands the need for discretion. I will meet you at the Impervious Vault. \n\nTu'whacca watch over you, wayfarer. Let us hope we can keep the Ansei Wards from falling into enemy hands.
I … should have tried to stop them. I'm sorry, so sorry. What have I done?
Glad you made it back safely, though I get the distinct impression that things did not go well in there ….
Azah … Azah … is that you? What happened? I feel so … dizzy ….
What do I do now? Where do I go? Does the sun still shine above ground? Does the moon still come out at night?\n\nIt's been so long since my life was my own … I-I don't want to leave.
<This tile feels loose.>
Go on now. I can't just twirl my staff and tell the Impervious Vault to open up. I need those reagents.\n\nHurry. I'll meet you at the vault.
Do not worry. I am guarding the Ward of Ansei Radan very carefully.\n\nI will return it to you when you are ready.
Oh, am I ever glad to see you again … do you have a banana? I mean … do you have a potion? To change me back?
Unishi feels sorry for the monkey, but she does what she is asked.
Where is she? I bet that damned cat swindled me. I should have trusted my mother. Magic is no good.
There's no need for me to ask whether the heroes had been raised when you found them.\n\nI only need to know—are they now at rest?
Once the mine's closed, I'll send in a crew to clean out these spiders.\n\nThis mine used to make me gold, now all it does is cost me.

I cannot tell you how relieved I am to hear that the Ansei Ward is safe. I will summon some of the other Ash'abah to come here and help clean out the rest of these Ra-Netu.\n\nYou—you must go after the third Ansei Ward.
Three Ansei Wards protect the Alik'r. You must find the third.
Such sweet nectar you mortals carry in your veins. A shame it goes to waste.
It's my job to keep the beetles in check normally, but something has gotten them riled up. \n\nI'm a farmer, not a warrior. I don't have the weapons or skills to deal with this.
I've got a lot of steel to shape, and little enough fire to temper it.
I'm not going to hang around here much longer. I'll find a nice, quiet job in Sentinel. Maybe get work on the docks!
Speak to me no more. As with the other, the one you slew beneath our very feet, I will be named no longer.\n\nBitterness shall be my drink, and remorse my fruit. Leave me be.
It will take time to restore order to Leki's Blade. Remnants of our old masters must be put aside forever.\n\nJustice was served, and its taste is bitter to me.
Your potential is obvious. I can see you've handled challenges before. Welcome to our school, recruit.\n\nAre you here to prove yourself, as have so many others before you?
Have you made your decision?
If the Withered Hand ever does try to take Bergama, we will now fight twice as hard to defend it. \n\nThis city will persevere. And you will always be welcome here.
Telenger does amazing, valuable work, but it can be dangerous. I heard one of his apprentices vanished on an expedition to Alik'r once.
Out of work, out of water … what a sorry state we're in!
The desert is not meant for the living. Our Yokudan ancestors made a mistake settling here. Now we are paying the price.
We were actually getting ahead for a change, storing extra barrels of water for Sentinel.\n\nEven after we clear the beetles out, we'll be struggling to catch up.

First, you will face the Nedic Peoples. When the Ra Gada first crashed on these shores, the Nedes were first to challenge them.\n\nFight the Nedic soldiers' spirits. Claim their essences, and use them to summon and face their leader, Warchief Haakon.
Though I am glad you understand, I'm sure we can both agree that this business is still dreadful.\n\nUnfortunately, Istah will simply have to remain in the stocks for the time being.
That monstrous creature must have done something to <<1>>!
Bring me that Goblin's head!
Now that you've put the sleep potion in the kegs, we can bargain for Miranda's release. \n\nBut let's find out where she is. Search the counting house for clues to where they're keeping her.
Search the houses for jewels, and collect puffball caps from the dock. Then meet me near the boathouse.\n\nYou could steal clothes from a dead bandit and disguise yourself ….
We are sorry for taking your totem. We are returning it to your camp…\n\nWait a minute … is that you? You certainly look … different.
I think Serge poisoned me. I feel nauseous and weak.\n\nHe taunted me by saying there's a crate of something that would act as an antidote along the east beach. Please hurry!
Oh no! My lady! She's … dead? I should've tried to help her myself!\n\nYou know what this means? Now I have to find a new job!
So Muzgu and the Daedra are dead. \n\nNow what? Can we be done with the killing?
By the First Forge, look at this—a new recruit! You are planning on joining up aren't you?\n\nWait, I'm getting ahead of myself. Welcome to the Wayrest Fighters Guild Hall!
You did it! \n\nThe dreugh are pulling back. Bless you.
My leg! One of these ruffians broke my leg!
Stendarr save us! Did I hear fighting upstairs?

Ah, listen to this. I'm working on a new ballad - here's the end bit.

The Dreamer has awakened,
His former wrath abhorred
With Reason's grace
Dishonor chased
And Hosni's house restored.

It's about you, you know.
You're a better fighter than you look.
Go ahead. If you have the guts to take it, it's yours.
Everything is ready, but I must be certain. When I expel this Daedra, it will be drawn into the cultist—and he will die.\n\nAre you sure you're willing to sacrifice this man?
I hear you've been busy.\n\nIf you've earned a favor from S'Rashi, you should put it to good use. I think he might know stole the Dream Shard.
Hold your nose. The stench just gets worse. Goblins, ogres … there's an army of them down there.\n\nI don't care if King Emeric himself orders it—the Lion Guard advances no further.
Thanks for your help with that gang of thugs.\n\nOn to the next mission! I've got to see to this guard's needs. Good day!
What can I do for you?
Say, I heard you recently arrived from Alcaire.\n\nThere are terrible rumors about Duchess Lakana. Are they true? Was she murdered?
She's coming out of it. I saw her eyes flicker. Azura be praised.
May the Eight bless you. And yes, I'm an Orc and a priest. Orcs can be priests. Though I admit, it's probably not that common a sight.
This one is very grateful that you will be helping his brother.\n\nS'rashi is a good and honest worker for the Midnight Union. He's only fallen on hard times. This one is glad you understand.

Perhaps we can now have a civil conversation. I'm Perry. Brother Perry, traveling through Alcaire on my way back to Pariah Abbey.\n\nIngride Vanne offered me a room for the night. It just happened to be the night the Supernal Dreamers attacked.
Shh! Not right now. Just leave me here for a few more minutes.
Compared to the rest of these people, you're a really generous person. Of course … that's not saying much.
Hosni taking the Dream Shard might explain the presence of those vipers, the Supernal Dreamers. \n\nThat only increases anxiety about Sirali … and my suspicions about Adima.
There must be some way to get through to Hosni.
My Hosni dreams. \n\nIf you go inside, do not disturb him. It would make me angry.
Triumphant, I hope? You certainly have been gone long enough. \n\nWait a minute. Where's the sword?
Now I must find ways to make amends. \n\nI know one thing—the days of the Midnight Union are over.
What's happened? There was a terrible commotion in the manor house. \n\nI think I might try to leave now.
I heard Count Hosni's gone upstairs to his chambers again. \n\nI've never seen a man sleep as much as he does.
What in Oblivion is going on in the manor? \n\nI'd go see myself, but, well—I'm frightened.
Go now. Destroy the aberration. It must be done.
Oh yes, I can sense that you want to be the hero. But to rescue the countess, you will have to come through into my world!\n\nPlease. Do come in!
Lead on. I'll follow.
I feel so empty. Like there's no one here. I am not a person. I'm just a reflection.
You waiting for a tip? \n\nGet a move on and return to Outfitter Wickton, or I will start demonstrating mace attacks on you.

Why did you make him leave? I was this close to reaching the peace of death!\n\nIt has just been a jest—the Daggerfall Covenant, my kingdom, my life. I was never worthy to be king. I'll die here and one more worthy will take my place.
Am I cursed? My home was attacked. This camp was attacked. I don't know where to go or what to do any more.
The Covenant thanks you for joining the war effort! With talented crafters like yourself at our back, there's no challenge we can't overcome.\n\nAkatosh bless your wares, friend.
Is that you again? You're really still alive?\n\nYou have one of their heads to show me?

I've heard the countess is sick or something. I'd go and check on her, but I don't want to catch anything.\n\nIt is a shame though because I've been working for weeks to get her the perfect gift—a miniature pony! She's going to love it!
This blacksmith makes quite a bit of gold. I wonder how much he pays in taxes to the countess.
Oh, it's you. I saw you leaving the countess's house earlier. \n\nI don't mean to intrude, but I simply have to ask. Are you yet another suitor come to seek her hand in marriage?

If the countess has truly lost her mental faculties, someone needs to take custody of the estate.\n\nIf called upon to do so, I would be willing to assume that responsibility, but I would not enjoy it unless she was at my side.

I should curse you mortal, for disturbing our rest, but my spirit has never been at peace.\n\nI've walked these ruins for centuries, cursing the king's name. My father in name, but never in action. He left me here to die.
Be careful. Be vigilant. Trust in Stendarr.

Damned foreigners. Nothing but trouble around here ever since the duke married King Fahara'jad's daughter.\n\nAnd now there's a Redguard army on our doorstep, expecting the Knights of the Flame to just stand aside?
Where's Falhut? Did she run?
This is a terrible day for the descendants of the Greatmothers and Greatfathers.
You've no idea the anguish I'm in... seeing my bones strewn about like rubbish. I can't leave; not with my remains in such a state.

The duchess is likely in her chambers upstairs. For now, just try to win her confidence. I must speak to the duke before we take any drastic actions.\n\nIf you learn any more about her plans, though, let me know right away.

Be cautious in Thoda's camp. It's full of young Redguards who want to prove themselves. Do what you must to prove your mettle, but don't spill any blood if you can avoid it.\n\nWe have to avoid starting a war.
So Missus Nurin was going to join those crazy cultists?\n\nI always knew that lady was a little… off. I got a good feel for people, you know?

Oh, my aching neck .… I haven't been this sore in years, but freedom sure does feel good.

This situation was more dangerous than I realized. You went way beyond the call of duty here, friend.

I can't adequately express my gratitude.
I think Ganise is still searching through the rubble in William's old workshop to the west. \n\nI know it's going to break her heart, but it's time for us to move on. Tell her to come to the house.
So wait a minute. You mean the constable was actually working with the slavers?\n\nI'm confused.
I knew I shouldn't have trusted you. You've handed the village to its enemies on a silver platter.\n\nYou'll see though. You'll all see!
Thank you for setting matters straight. My men are having their wounds treated even now. \n\nWe'll be back on high seas soon—where we belong.
I guess the next thing is start making plans to rebuild. Times like these I wish we had more children—a larger family, you know?\n\nI guess there's always the future.

Soon as you start talking sense, we'll let you out of there, honey.

My poor poor Pascal.

I thought he was acting like a churlish teenager, but it turns out he was just under the infuence of some evil curse.

So now the constable's the one in the stocks? Go figure. I always thought he was a good guy—just acting a little crazy these last few weeks.\n\nI just hope it'll be good for business. Speaking of which, what'll you have?
If they hadn't snuck up behind me, they wouldn't have had a chance.
My family is whole again thanks to you.\n\nYou'll have to excuse me though. I need to go get Lucas ready for bed.
So the farm's all clear? Terrific. Now we just have to rebuild.\n\nI wish we had a bigger family. Hm. You know, my father's not that old. If we could just find an eligible lady ….
Didn't I tell you to leave? Why are you back? Where is my husband? Leave this house! Leave at once!\n\nI can hardly bear the stress. It's just not safe here!
If the slavers come back, you have to let me know in advance.\n\nI need to get my sweet little chickies inside.
The lengths I go to for a free breakfast of biscuits and jam.\n\nMy mother can be a hassle sometimes, but it's a small price to pay to have someone else wash your smallclothes.
She cannot be dead. This cannot be real. My Lakana ….\n\nYou! You spoke with her, didn't you? What do you know of this? Tell me!
The boy's home and she's happy. Back to spoiling the poor kid.\n\nMaybe I can sneak away for a drink soon.
So you survived? I worried you were buried along with the ogres. For collapsing that cavern, you deserve a medal!\n\nUnfortunately though, General Godrun's in no condition to hand out awards.

Regardless of the outcome with this 'Dame Falhut', I do not believe it's safe for Lakana to remain in the Bretons' castle. \n\nI will not break our treaty by ordering an attack, but neither will I leave until I am assured of her safety.
Good day to set sail. My ship's repaired, and even the lighthouse has been relit. \n\nMaybe I'll get to Hammerfell in time after all.
Sounds like King Fahara'jad's envoy is ignoring Dame Falhut and refusing to leave the main gate.\n\nWe're keeping our weapons ready. This may get ugly.
I guess Constable Pascal's not in charge anymore.\n\nMaybe this Knight of the Flame will let me go after the slavers.
Welcome, traveler, to the Wayrest Mages Guild Hall. Do I detect some interest in membership?
I pray for those whose minds were blinded by Vaermina's Omen.\n\nThose who stray from the path of law and order are truly lost.
The victims of Vaermina's treachery are in my heart and prayers.
How many lives were lost to the Fervor? Only Arkay knows.
Peace be with those who are free of Vaermina's Omen.

This Fervor I hear word of is truly the device of a Daedra.\n\nTo take over one's mind? To lack any mercy or compassion for your victims? I can't imagine the cruelty others have endured at the hands of Vaermina's victims.
It's not only the prices at this market that bother me, it's the merchants. All the villagers here annoy me.\n\nI need to move to Wayrest.
So now we have the constable in the stocks? All the same to me as long as it draws the crowds.\n\nSee anything you like?
I cannot believe one of our own is behind the attacks on Duchess Lakana.\n\nThere must be some other explanation. There has to be.
I fear that King Fahara'jad will not be pleased with this outcome. I will do my best to explain the circumstances, but there may be political repercussions.
This decision could not have been easy for you, and it will not be easy on Duke Nathaniel. Sir Hughes is a good man though, and I am glad he will live.

Was that Ingride and Rozenn's voices I heard out there? I'm glad they're safe. \n\nWe'll come down and join them by and by, but Giraud's been having so much fun, I'd hate to spoil it. He'll get tired soon.

I've been holding off these Scamps for hours. It was fun at first, but now I'm feeling a little tired. \n\nSure would be nice to go home and sit in my chair. But I have a duty to do, and by the Eight, I'll kill every last Scamp I see!
Things in Fell's Run have mostly returned to normal, but we remain vigilant against further incursions from Northpoint and the west.
Surely you can see the absurdity of this situation. I hope you will speak to this Sir Hughes or the Duke himself.\n\nPlease, tell them to let me in. I mean no harm. Ask the Duchess.
Princess Lakana is dead. We have failed our king.\n\nIf her murderer is not found and brought to justice, there will be blood.
King Fahara'jad's daughter is dead. This is a sad day for all of Alik'r.\n\nSomeone must pay!
The General let you leave? I thought we'd be carrying you out in pieces.\n\nI am glad you have earned his respect though. You are a strong warrior and always welcome at my campfire.
King Fahara'jad will be devastated. He'll want someone to answer for this.
Aren't you a surprise? <<1>> is the only foe standing between you and total victory.
I hear you might be leaving. But you're coming back, right? An arena without a champion draws no crowds.
So, Count Hosni's releasing the captives. I hope that means back to business as usual.
You don't think I had anything to do with that, do you?
Leveque is upstairs.\n\nJust remember what happened to Roy.
Roy was a good spy, and a good friend. I hope you can finish whatever it was he started.
I'll set aside some lilies for Roy.
It's a shame what happened to Roy. May Tall Papa guide him.

I guess I should probably say "thank you." If you hadn't come, I would have stayed in there forever. \n\nSounds like I'm heading back to Camlorn with my brother. Not too excited about that, but I guess it's the best thing.
<The dog whines and remains next to the Breton's corpse.>
Grenna's at the Rosy Lion Inn.
A focus is required for the ritual to work. This torchbug, born from the soil and sap of the Wyrd Tree, will seek out untainted earth.\n\nLet's hope the corruption hasn't spoiled the entire area.
Are you an agent of King Casimir? I thought Daggerfall had abandoned us.
Captain Aresin wishes a word with you, hero.
I'll secure the docks. Get those assassins!
Go on. I'm sure you'll find that hog of a pig rooting around in the northeast alleys.
You found him! You found my wonderful little Glutton!

Baron Montclair has been defeated and the High King crowned a ruler in Shornhelm, but that doesn't mean Rivenspire has suddenly become safe and secure.\n\nI suggest you travel the roads carefully, friend. You never know what you might run into.
As soon as you catch a werewolf, meet me in the cave across the bay. \n\nI hate to miss the fun of the hunt, but I have to prepare the cave for our reluctant guest.
Damn bandits! The roads have never been this bad! If the Daggerfall Guard hadn't arrived when they did, I'd probably be dead right now!
I'm a little busy.\n\nThe Red Rooks bandits are holding hostages. They're in a house down the lane.
We have orders to clean up this nest of rats.\n\nGood job back there.
A runner sent word that you took care of those bandits. \n\nDamned good of you to help.
Perhaps I was too quick to pass judgment on you.\n\nThese people, including my sister Olyna, owe you their lives.
You caught one. Good. Let's get him into the circle.
What a beast! Right out of my worst nightmares. Thank you for killing the horrible thing.
Thank you. It's a terrible thing to be poor. You're invisible. No one cares.
I've never seen the citizens so agitated. Even the beggars seem nervous these days.
The threat to my husband was a threat to the Daggerfall Covenant as a whole.\n\nOn behalf of my father, King Fahara'jad, and all of Alik'r, I thank you.
Gorak returned in a state of some excitement. \n\nI take it you saw enough action to teach him a thing or two?
That was unexpected. Why did you change your mind?
What are you thinking, bringing that beast in here? Head to the cave before that creature breaks free and starts killing people!
Cultists, bogs, bugs as big as my head … why oh why did I ever leave the city?
Please, you have to help us! That magic stone keeps us bound here. Smash it! That should free us.
A messenger? From Aldcroft, by any chance?\n\nWhat news from there? We heard reports that Camlorn refugees had inundated the town.
By the Eight, why the blazes are you still bothering me?\n\nGo find that damn Dagger and get me back my egg.
I'm working with someone else right now. Go get your own mercenary!
This is my fault. I'm the one who wanted to sell the johads. My father deserved better than this.
Did we do it? Did we actually complete a mission? Quick, talk to Gelvin so he can explain what happened here.
I think Guy and Erwan may be back along the road, west of here.
You can find the hags to the west. Just protect that charm. It is your best defense against Mother Murk.
Sorry, hunter. No more bounties today.
I trust your lizard is still well. Please let it know I asked after it!
I can't thank you enough for your kindness. The pipe must be somewhere in the lighthouse or our cottage. \n\nPlease, be careful.
The others, they're free. I can't leave, but what does that matter? At least Rosalind and the others no longer suffer.
Have you seen Leon? We're worried about him.
I haven't seen Leon since before the attack. I hope he's all right.
I don't know who you are or what you did here. I only know that things are … changing. \n\nThe spirits of Westtry are quieter now.
My husband looks so much better. Thank you for everything.
By the Eight! Whatever you gave him seemed to do the trick. I pray that the madness is well and truly over.
Thanks to you, my nightmare is over. \n\nIt's time to return to Camlorn.
Go to Aldcroft, he says. It'll be safer, he says. I shouldn't have listened to LeBlanc.
I'm ready to go, of course, but first we need clearance from Captain Vistra.
So it did work? It was so quiet after you went in, I worried, but seeing you now, well, I feel so proud, and relieved, of course.

I believe the Eight sent you to Alik'r in this time of grave peril for a reason.\n\nI pray you succeed in recovering the Ansei Wards. If you don't, an army of risen ancestors will march across the land.
I hope the others are all right.
Better get moving. Stay in one place too long, the Bloodthorns'll get you.
See how the past speaks to us! Isn't it amazing? I almost wish I was brave enough—I mean, expendable enough—to go with you to the crypt.
No surprise there. Poor Sarvith, his spells never work as planned. \n\nIt's always the same. One disaster after another.
Ah, this armor brings back such memories. \n\nNow get dressed. There's much to see and the connection to the past won't last long.
Bah, don't worry about me. Just head back to the camp. \n\nGo—no time for questions.
Whatever happens, beloved, I …. \n\nNo, enough. Only the fight matters now.
Good luck, my friend. I'll see you on the battlefield. \n\nNow, let's make that bastard Faolchu pay.
You had the strength to do what no one else could and now I'm free. You have no idea what that means to me.\n\nBut tell me, stranger. Why did you do all of this?
Why am I so out of breath? How far have I run?

These Bloodthorn are nothing more than graverobbers. \n\nTake back the regalia they stole and return each item to its proper tomb. They hide the items in the groundskeeper's cottage south of the Burial Mounds.
Sisters, let me talk to this stranger.\n\nWe are busy. Please make your business quick.
Slay the Bloodthorns. Break their hold over our servants. \n\nOur servants have been loyal and true. Such commitment must not be repaid with slavery.
You've done enough for us already. Please, speak to my son and get some well deserved rest.\n\nI fear this isn't over yet.
The Fighters Guild is recruiting if you're interested in joining. You look like you can handle yourself in a fight. We need people like that.
I believe I can sense the gods returning already. I lost my faith, but you have restored it.
As soon as we've finished moving back into the manor, I'm going to plan a hunting trip. This adventure's got my blood up!
Oh, dear. You shouldn't have risked your life on my behalf.
The blasted zombies just keep coming. I don't know how much longer we can hold out.\n\nI hope Gabrielle finds something to help us sooner rather than later.
Lieutenant Harim's probably near the lighthouse. Be careful as you make your approach. The place is crawling with Bloodthorn cultists.
The circle is just northeast of here, up the trail along the beach. \n\nPlace the talisman in the revelation pool. That should force whatever's inside to come out.
The werewolves were strong, but we were stronger.\n\nThose who died in this fight did so with honor. They have no regrets.
We'll continue to interrogate these cultists until we've learned everything we can about Angof. \n\nWe must find a way to stop him.
Of all Camlorn's heroes, past and present, you may be the craziest. It takes a certain kind of recklessness to take on someone like Faolchu. You have my admiration.
Thank you so much for helping me. \n\nYou really are the hero they say you are.
We are free! This is how it should be.
I need to talk with my father. Go ahead and let Dame Clarique know what happened.
If you can't seal that gate, this will be a very short offensive on our part.
You … you're going to speak to Enneh? Thank you. I just pray that there is some explanation for this ….\n\nIf Casnar is dead … I don't think I can go on.
You missed it! You should have seen the look on Jagnas's face when I arrived!\n\nIt was extremely satisfying.
I knew Casnar was having doubts, but if he decided to back out, he should have at least sent word.\n\nTo put his bride through this is just cruel. Poor Tiela!

Welcome to Bergama, wayfarer! We have the finest musical instruments in all Hammerfell!\n\nIf you want a harp, or lute, or even a drum, you've come to the right place! Though that is not why you are here … is it?

Look at this! You walk in like you own the place, like you fear absolutely nothing.\n\nIf it's a fight you want, though, you've come to the wrong place. This is a place of business. I'm a businessman.
Still here? I tell you, it's urgent that we get to that inn. Don't you know we're out of ale?\n\nNow get that key.
It's so beautiful! Do you see? Things have already changed. The Wyrd Tree has been restored.
Place the candles on my family's graves. \n\nFirst, you'll visit three humble graves. Then you need to find a great monument surrounded by an iron fence. Place the last candle there.
We will see that these dead are consecrated now. They will not rise again.

Some of the Bloodthorn escaped. I'll send a runner to warn Daggerfall.\n\nAt least you stopped their rituals. I'll consider that a victory. Hopefully, that wizard you rescued can help, too. In the meantime, we have a town to clean up.
Unclawed traitor! Ildani should never have trusted you! \n\nYou betrayed this one. The Baandari will know. They will not forget.
Pity we couldn't save everyone with the antidote. \n\nAt least now we know it works. All we need are enough ingredients.
I hope you're able to help <<1>>  find the Guardians.
I'm thinking we're going to need grappling hooks. They're very versatile, you know.
It is finished. The earth's strength shall return now.
Well done. Now the winds will change for foul Angof.
Balance returns. Soon the Wyrd Tree will be safe.
I hope that all of our friends and neighbors are safe.
Ah, someone new to talk to. Are you here for something specific or just to say hello?
I hope you're able to find  <<1>>.\n\nI've never seen her so determined!

So you're the one wreaking havoc down there among those horkers? I've tangled with a Reachman or two in my day, and my helmet's off to anyone who charges into their ranks that way. \n\nDon't suppose you've come to enlist in the town guard, have you?

Welcome back, Arzhela. Good work! First, you ran this kingdom into the ground. Then you dumped it into my lap!\n\nNow, the two of you repay me by sabotaging my plans and destroying any hope we had of surviving the Reachmen attack!
Go away! We don't want any trouble.
What do you wish of us, mortal?
You're back. And in one piece. Lady Laurent has also returned in time for supper, as usual. \n\nAll is right with the world.
Perhaps you'll have another chance to assist me in the future. Until then, good luck to you.
We need to cut down enough of these monsters to clear a path through the camp. \n\nThen we might have a chance to retake the city.
I'd love to join you on the attack, but these troops are green. Most of them have never fought a werewolf, so I'll need to stick with them to show them how. \n\nBut kill a few for me.
The cursed crown is on the left as you enter the vault. \n\nGood luck, I suppose. That's all I have to offer.

See these vines? Corruption runs through them and they choke the sacred stone. Soon, they will tap into the stone's magic and defile it completely.\n\nIf you will help me, I can destroy these foul vines.
Corruption radiates from this … thing. I can feel it worming into my soul. The corruption spreads outward, altering or killing all the forest creatures. We have to destroy it!
I loathe these vines. They reek of death and corruption. But every time I try to deal with them, I'm attacked by cultists or corrupted creatures.
<<1>> told me you would come. I hope this works.\n\nPlease don't let anything happen to me while I destroy these vines.
I don't want to leave the prince alone for long. We'll have to be quick.
That … that was the thing that attacked my father!
The stables are not as busy as they once were. Still, I will care for all beasts that seek shelter within.
Have you come to … no, you're not the provisioner from Sentinel.\n\nI've had to send farther and farther away for simple things such as salt and grain!
Kill these monstrous creatures and avenge my fallen brethren.
When you choose for one, you choose for all. Such is the burden of leadership.
To act … to not act. Each is a choice.
A single decision can define a civilization. Think hard on your legacy, wayfarer, for even small choices can have great consequences.
Not even the grandest hero can escape regret.
What are you still doing in here? You need to chase down that monster and kill it. Kill it dead!
I'm getting out of Evermore and I advise you to do the same if you know what's good for you.
Greetings friend. It's nice to see another fighter around here. Our numbers aren't what they used to be. Live by the sword and all that. \n\nIf you want to join the guild, you should speak to Hareld.

Pardon my intrusion, but I would speak to you on behalf of Queen Arzhela. I am her handmaiden.\n\nThe queen has … heard of your recent accomplishments, and she asked me to make a private request on her behalf.
I think you're ready to advance to journeyman. \n\nYou should travel to Daggerfall to be tested.
We have our fair share of problems with the undead around here. You might have noticed.
You seem to have mastered all the skills of an apprentice. \n\nGo back to Daggerfall and take your journeyman test.

Finally! The Elves came damn near ruining my entire expedition! Of course, Stibbons was really to blame. \n\nRegardless, I'll be glad to get back to studying the ruins instead of skulking around and trying to hide from the Elves.
Still as the stone that walks. Yes.\n\nThey remember, you know! They carry their histories, etched in their flesh!
I just keep asking myself, why in Oblivion would you have decided to help Stibbons?\n\nI have to believe that you were motivated by some deluded sense of pity. I feel sorry … for both of you.
You've returned! What did you find?\n\nWas it jewels? Ivory? Gold?
Thank you for lifting this burden from me. My task here is done.
I can't believe poor Richard is dead. I warned him about rummaging around in those old ruins.
I'm going to make sure these people are taken care of before I leave.\n\nIt's the least I can do.
Poisoned by spiders … be careful. They are attracted to movement.
I've lost track of how long I've waited here … hours, days, weeks. Who can say?
We will need to bless the voice's bud if you intend to go through with this.
What in Oblivion is he thinking? How dare this petty priest question me—the chosen of Arkay? It's obviously because I've earned the god's favor and he hasn't. He's jealous!
Crush some Bloodthorn skulls for me. \n\nFaith and the Covenant!

That's it. The bud is ready. Take it to the girl, Elara.\n\nI can't believe Demara continues to help the Sentinel on this mad scheme. We will all suffer for his generosity in the end. The girl knows nothing of the woods, and it will cost us all dearly.

As the Sentinel, I must warn you that these woods aren't safe. But as Old Gurles, I'm glad to see a friendly face.\n\nI remember when that child wasn't more than a knee's height, and now she's laid out like a corpse.
I should be fine to head back soon. I just need to… figure out how I'm going to skirt the witchmen on my way back through to the docks.
I don't know why we came here… everything that could have gone wrong has gone wrong.
How am I any different from you, deciding who is spared and who dies?\n\nWhat gives you the right to judge me?

I can't believe it. You gave the tools to Tamien? How could you?\n\nNow I'll never get back to Lady Laurent's good graces! I still can't understand—how can she just drop me after so many years' service?
I don't know what Stenwick is planning, but if it'll save my life, I trust him. I don't understand why these wyrd people can't see that!
Don't worry about these fellows.\n\nNothing will get to them while I'm here.
As long as I have the tools of my trade, I can make an honest living. A good tailor is welcome anywhere!
Thanks again for helping Odei. I don't know what I would have done if I had lost him to the wolves.
I have some good news and some bad news. The good news is that the people have begun to rally around the idea of resisting the Red Rooks. \n\nThe bad news is the Red Rooks have taken notice.
Tamien, my son. He's come back? I'd hoped I'd see him before the end. Quickly, though, there's no time. We must act!
I hope the soldiers still live. That mist is deadly. \n\nAnd that fool from Camlorn—what was he thinking? He charged right into the mist after them.
Yes, whatever. Back to it.
Did you teach those Red Rooks a lesson?
The Pearl is the Way and the Guide, the light to the Far Shores and back again, placed by Tall Papa's hand.

Your keen tactical mind and honorable actions have seen us through a tight spot.\n\nThe Saltwalker Company consider us allies for preventing a bad contract, and you've stopped the Withered Hand cold. Well done.
I'm glad we're doing something. \n\nWhen this is all over, we'll be proud of what we accomplished against these … these … ruffians!
Heseph never gave up. And neither will I.\n\nI'll help Sellan rally the townsfolk. We'll make these bastards pay.

Well negotiated, <<1>>. Your keen tactical mind and honorable actions have seen us through a tight spot. The Saltwalker Company consider us allies for preventing a bad contract, and you've stopped the Hand cold.\n\nWe may even recruit them. Well done!
I'll head out and start rallying the townsfolk after you leave and I lock up here.\n\nNo reason to leave an open invitation to those damn bandits.
Meet me at the center of the graveyard. I'll be along shortly.\n\nRemember, I can clear a path for the soldiers, but I can't protect myself and perform the magic.
Win the duel, and I will listen. I value two things: gold and honor.\n \nFor today, at least, I have the luxury of valuing honor over gold.
Begone. I have no use for self-righteous fools. Sound the drum if you wish to fight.

For a moment there, I feared my faith was already proven false. Much hinges on your involvement, but fate has decreed that you will run this race … and that you will win. \n\nAre you willing to test this?
This poor soul doesn't have much time. His blood, it's boiling. \n\nThat bite must have infected him. Even Faolchu wasn't capable of this.
I've learned all I can here. Time to find Sir Lanis. \n\nGood luck.
I hope Sorick was happy to hear the news.\n\nI, on the other hand, have been passing the time chatting to our new friend here. It's rather depressing. I hope the healers get to one of us soon.

You have stepped onto a predetermined path. Fate decrees a duneripper will consume your bones before the end of the day. Deny fate. Slay Istraga.\n\nThen bring me one of her scales as proof of your victory.
If the fortifications don't hold, then the wounded won't have time to fall back to the ships.
What's happened? Some of the people in the town are acting strangely.
Thank Stendarr, you got rid of that cursed spirit.
I don't know if I can make it, but I'll try.
I wouldn't take on that abomination without first dealing with its totems. But I'm sure you know your business better than I do. \n\nDon't worry about me. I'll find Sir Lanis and the others.
Welcome to our humble village. Not many find us by accident, yet … I smell no illness upon you.\n\nMay I ask what brings you here, if not the cure?
Be careful in there. I'd hate to have to include your death in my report.
I just want to go home.
The stone! That's the stone!\n\nRecite the words etched on it. Be precise, for the wrong words will shatter it.
Speak to <<1>>, the lizard breeder. Pick me a winner!
When you're done, find <<1>> in the center of town. He'll want to know the fracas has finally started.\n\nI'll let Marent know you're coming.
Came out here to find lazy bones dying on the job! I'm not having it. No one kills him but me!
<The dog whines and barks at the skull and then looks at you expectantly.>
I have many wonderful lizards to choose from.\n\nWere you looking for something particular?
Get back! I don't want to hurt you too!\n\nGods, bring the change already! I've had enough of this torture!

King Eamond had a stableboy who … kept me informed, but I've heard nothing since the king's death—not even word of who assumed the throne.\n\nHis name is Ramza. Find him and tell him I sent you to help. We cannot allow Bangkorai to fall.
Always new mouths to feed around the village. Well? What're you looking at? I'm not selling anything to anybody.
Shame about Rahannal's injuries, he'd make a good hearth-husband once he's healed up.\n\nThink he's interested?
Did you stop the dancing? The prancing?
As soon I recover, I'm going to Wayrest. I have to warn the king about these people, these Supernal Dreamers.
Oh no! The fact that he is not with you does not bode well. Did you find anything? Was he dead? What about the supply pack?
<The ghost glares at you and does not respond.>

Enter the oasis and look for bite victims. If you find anyone suffering from snake venom, apply the antidote to the victims' wounds, so they can walk out of here.\n\nWhen you're done, bring word to <<1>> near Bergama's entrance.
When the snakes attacked, it was complete chaos. The horses ran away with the wagons … and I ran too.\n\nI know some of the people were bitten. I only hope we are not too late with the antidote.
According to section sixteen of the Sentinel Docks trade regulations, this is a restricted area.\n\nIf you remain here for an extended period of time, I'll be required to place you under arrest.
Find my son, <<1>>, as quickly as you can. \n\nIf he was threatened, he would head for high ground. Look for him on the cliffs above us.
Snakes separated me from my family, and now I'm surrounded.\n\nIs there a clear path to the bridge? I'm scared to leave.

See the product of treachery, traveler! We were guards assigned to the tower watching the pass to Craglorn.\n\nWhen the Imperials invaded, one of our own opened the door. He allowed them to kill us and throw our corpses from the very tower we guarded.
What news do you bring me? Were you able to locate this near-mythical sword?
You must leave this place. The sword is cursed.
Did you find Willie? Or at least his wallet?
The Red Rooks think that they're invincible, but we'll show them! We're going to rise up and take back our town!
<Even asleep, <<1>> appears to be struggling to escape.>
Go! Find the captain.\n\nWhen I recover, I'll head to Koeglin Village in Stormhaven.
It's getting … dark … and cold ….\n\nPlease … save Lorelia ….
All is quiet out here. \n\nDid you find any relics, any sign of the Nereid?
The key will be passed around. Go, we will free ourselves!
That last package arrived just in time.\n\nWe had a few unruly guests who, let's just say, no longer have a care in the world.
I hope <<1>> managed to get out of Sentinel safely.\n\nI heard rumors that the docks were being overrun with the undead!
I hope <<1>> continues to prosper.\n\nMy own business has never been better.

Glad one of us is still nimble. I couldn't get any further up the slope than this.\n\nIn the confusion of your violent entry and exit, they won't notice their papers were disturbed. Sometimes rowdy is better than sly.
A Baelborne always pays for services rendered.\n\nThis place might look like a ruin to you, but it's a part of my family. It's all I have left.
The Baelbornes must never return to Glenumbra.

The bog is to the west, but the place is crawling with cultists and terrible hags. It's not safe.\n\nYou must help my people. We were just looking for a way out of Camlorn. We never meant to get ourselves into even worse danger.
We don't get many folks from the outside. Kerbol likes it that way, and truth be told, so do I.
Speak to me when you're ready to start the event.
You were able to hear the voice of Hermaeus Mora?\n\nThat's unfair. I worked my whole life for such an honor and I hear nothing.
Before you go, mortal. I have something for you. A gift, one might say.
The man practically walked into our camp! The sorriest excuse for a Red Rook bandit I've ever seen.\n\nNow if we could just get him to tell us something useful.
Go! Find the captain. \n\nWhen I recover, I'll head to Koeglin Village in Stormhaven.
Get my family back here safely. I'll tell you exactly where the meeting is happening and how you can disrupt it.\n\nBut first, I need to see my family with my own eyes.
The sooner we discover the Dominion's plans, the better. \n\nInfiltrate their camp, locate their commander, and retrieve any messages you find.
Climb the tower and use the storm rune to put out the signal fires. \n\nQuickly, now. I'll meet you down on the beach after the job is done.
I saw the other scouts run up the stairs toward the tower. \n\nWatch out. The place is crawling with Dominion troops.
Good work extinguishing those signal fires. \n\nYou were clearly in time. There's no sign of an impending Dominion attack.
My bailiffs and I will keep an eye out for any more trouble coming out of Northpoint. I just wish we knew why they did this to us.
Blood-sucking bastards came out of nowhere. We did what we could.
The blood! It won't come out! \n\nWhat … what are you doing here? Captain Janeve needs your help! She chased Tainted-Heart to the southwest along the river.
The bad ones are still here! I can hear them thinking! I can! Make them go away. \n\nThey want to take me to <<1>>. Mother is scared.
My comrades lived when I last saw them. As I … retreated.\n\nPlease, you have to help them. I won't give up the totem I found until I know they're safe.
I'll be all right in a moment. Go light both watchtowers as quickly as you can. It's the signal my people await!
Did you find Willie? Or at least his wallet?
Take that … her … body to the upper balcony. I guess that's what all those harpies are up there waiting for.

Nuwarrah's family has alway been a thorn in my side. Now that I helped save the city, she'll probably host a feast in honor of the deed.\n\nThat could mar my reputation with the Thieves Guild. That woman is impossible.

Constable Agazu is usually patrolling the town square. If you want to help, go talk to her. I'm just a bailiff.\n\nOtherwise, please move along. I have my own duties to perform and I need to get back to them.
Don't listen to their Orcish lies!\n\nThey'll say anything to get you to believe their pathetic complaints.
Thank you for rescuing the townsfolk, friend. Many of my brethren are still missing, but at least a few of them are home, safe and sound.
It's bad enough to kill us and drive us from our homes.\n\nIt's worse still that the sorceress is defiling the graves of our ancestors!

The Seventh Legion is better armed and better organized than the resistance, I expect.\n\nIf one of those were to change, it'd only be a matter of time before they were driven out like the dogs they are.
<<1>> owes you its freedom. May Tall Papa guide your way.
Everyone has to make a living somehow. You go now to make yours and leave me alone with mine.
The gods smiled upon our family when they brought you to our town. May your paths be easier from now on!
This is your doing? You freed my daughter?
Got a boat if you need passage. Can't go around Tamriel, but I can get you to the fishing ports about here.
There are deep waters beneath Hallin's Stand. The Imperials disturbed them, don't you think?
Suna ye sunnabe … you are one of the slave race. How curious.\n\nNevertheless, I will listen to your petition. It has been too long since one has come seeking my knowledge.
I hope you're here to help. We're losing ground to Covenant forces.\n\nWe have to hold the line here, or they'll push us back to Ebonheart and take all of Zabamat.
You're not one of these cursed Daggers, and you're not one of ours. Who are you?
This is the coral's begetting place—its nursery, if you will.\n\nI erect the spine of welcome. You don't look like an egg-crusher.
Follow me or meet me there. Your choice.
Holgunn said you were reliable. I trust his instincts.\n\nAnd I know there is much work to do.
They are brave, my acolytes. Now it comes to me.\n\nOur blood will be the water, our bones the soil.
Go well along the river. And beware the ashes that dry your scales.

Got blades of all kinds, friend—some stronger than others. \n\nYou want some advice? Leave them flimsy-arse scimitars to the locals. Get yourself a bastard sword. They're strong and trustworthy—just like me. Ha!
Someone needs to do something about these damned Imperials! I wish the Guild would let me fight. They speak of neutrality in times of war. It's absurd.
I suppose I should think about closing up shop. The Imperials didn't give me much trouble, but these Redguards … they might take umbrage at the decor.
These Imperials are a cursed nuisance! If they do anything to delay my deliveries, I don't care what the Guild says, I'm going to lay the fire on them.\n\nJust see if I don't.
Daimbert keeps complaining about the Imperials, but I'm just happy they've left us alone. \n\nIf there's anything I can help you with, just ask.
I can't wait to see what Ufa has planned for these Imperials. Sounds like it will be a good time for all involved, unless you're one of them.
It's too bad these Legionnaires didn't carry more coin.\n\nSome folk might frown on looting the dead, but I'm not one of them.
You're no milk-drinker, friend. It took steel to go out and do that. \n\nWith those bound ghosts, Davon's Watch won't fear an invasion again.
I must gather my thoughts before I go to Davon's Watch. I have to report my own brother for necromancy.\n\nBy the Three, I must be strong.
Amazing. This is what it takes to get the Dark Elves working with the Argonians? An erupting volcano?
<You find an arrow carved into the wood of the lamppost.>\n\n<This arrow points north.>
<You find an arrow carved into the wood of the lamppost.>\n\n<This arrow points south.>
<You find an arrow carved into the wood of the lamppost.>\n\n<This arrow points east.>
<You find an arrow carved into the wood of the lamppost.>\n\n<This arrow points west.>
<You find an arrow carved into the wood of the lamppost.>\n\n<This arrow points down.>
Be welcome here, in the nursery of the coral child. You do not have the look of one who crushes eggs.
Can you feel it on your snout? The thunder is building. I believe there are others in the Ashlands who could use my skills. \n\nMay the cool rain touch our scales again, traveler.
It's almost funny, I've never seen Father frightened before. He even corrected great Vivec once!\n\nThank you again.
Thank you again, traveler.
The wind bears the scent of burning metal. I fear there are darker days ahead.
Travel to the northwest and look for Covenant activity.\n\nFind out why they're here and what they're planning. Go swiftly, and go carefully.
Have you dispatched Ahknara, that piece of nchow?
I'm done with the Covenant. I've lost too many friends. I'm too old for this.\n\nIf I make it, I'm going to hang up my sword in Cyrodiil and become a farmer.
A small army stands ready to attack the north while we're waiting for a second army to flank us. Meanwhile, assassins creep through the fort.\n\nThese two weeds share a root beneath the surface.
The Brothers of Strife are too dangerous. I'll keep this from everyone who might want to use it … even Tanval.
Did I just see what I thought I saw? Did <<1>> just merge with that coral thing? Somehow, she's keeping the coral alive. \n\nNow we just have to deal with the witch who tried to kill it.
The heart is yours, yet the coral lives. Once I saw it was dying, I had no choice but to join myself with the coral. \n\nWe are one now. It's not where I expected to end, but these roots go deep.

You must find the remains of those who died fighting the Akaviri. I understand their anger. Imagine dying so close to a blessing of perfection, but missing the touch of Vivec!\n\nAnoint their bones. Put their spirits to rest.
So much work to do. I can't let this mine sit idle forever.
Missing daughters and erupting volcanoes? This town has seen far too much excitement if you ask this Nord.
Ah, blood and fire, haha! Now, that's what I call a happy ending.
I'll just … wait until my knees stop shaking.
<<1>> should be told that our ritual was a success.
Khralek is dead and our spirits are free.
You have medicine? Please, I'll try anything.
Find the captain. Tell Hjolm I was unable to find any Covenant troops while I was scouting to the west.\n\nHe should be somewhere along the road east of the fort.
Speak to whoever you want. The kinhouse is more concerned with the coming plague than searching for people who probably just ran away. But I'm sure a councilor will hear you out.
Heard you helped Vartis near the mountain pass.\n\nWell done. He's one of our better scouts.
This is ill news. But Mournhold will be glad to get it before the Orcs establish a foothold.
Back in Skyrim, mountains know their place. They don't explode and endanger our daughters. Pfah!
<You've taken the contents of this chest.>
You have his inheritance? That's something he'll certainly want to receive. \n\nI'll send word out to get his location, and then I'll send a special courier to ensure this gets to him.
I'm sure my mead-sodden spouse is around here somewhere.
We Dark Elves thought ourselves unassailable in Stonefalls. Now the Covenant stands at our gate, threatening to burn the barn and scatter the guar. \n\nInteresting how the past repeats itself.
You're back. I hope you're here to tell me that my people are just imagining things and everything is fine.
She did it for me, you know. She stood up to the Covenant soldiers because they wanted to, you know, touch me.\n\nIf she had died ….
You will be remembered in this village for all you have done.
Be careful.
I mourn my brother, but I do not regret what you had to do.\n\nThere will be no blood-feud between us.
Let us begin. The Nedes will rue the day they heard the name of Balreth!
It is time. Pray at the brazier. And then stand back.
I'm glad the Othrys family survived. Without them, we'd be out of work.\n\nI only hope we can hold out until reinforcements arrive.
Why try to mend what is already broken beyond repair?
Go, friend. Find the troops at Ash Mountain.\n\nI'll just wait here until they don't notice me, and then I'll make a break for it.
Speak to my son, <<1>>, outside the manor house. Offer to help find Bjorick.\n\nI couldn't bear to lose another son.
Speak to my lord, <<1>>. He's at the manor house north of here, just past the windmill.
Kill every Goblin and spider you meet. If you can distract them, I can slip past and rescue Bjorick.\n\nMeet me here when you're finished.
My bell got rung a bit, so I'm just going to sit here for a while.\n\nMeet me on the north road when the deed is done.
Your attack on those vermin was heroic.\n\nYou made them regret the day they left their stinking dens.
You've acquitted yourself honorably.
You've learned what I knew. Once again, Mavos Siloreth's brilliance will bind Balreth. Where would the mages of this age be without me?\n\nNow stop meddling with my eternal rest.
Good. If we're lucky, we'll survive the next step.
My sons are safe. I'll scold them for getting injured later.\n\nAnd my wife and daughter are safe too. I'm in your debt.
With the shalk gone, I can make a run for what's left of the farm.\n\nGo! Find my family. And be careful.
Looks like it's safe. Please, find the rest of my family.\n\nI'll make a run for the stead now. Good luck.
At Davon's Watch, you helped put the Covenant to shame, but one battle does not win the war.

The nobles seem determined to send you to your death. Surely you don't expect to fight through Lord Montclair's soldiers to get to his stronghold?\n\nI can show you an easier, if dirtier, way to get to your destination.
Welcome to the Dusklight Inn. Not exactly the lap of luxury, but we try to make our customers comfortable. \n\nThe cost of a room's cheap, and if you're as broke as I am, that's all that matters.
<<1>> reminds me of some of our holds in the Rift. This place is much grander, of course. But just like here, there's always some milk-drinker trying to break down our walls.
Hold! What's your business? In case you haven't noticed, friend, we're in the middle of a siege.
I've gathered some of our most skilled fighters here. We're poised to infiltrate the fort as soon as the way is open. \n\nYou're the perfect fit for my plan, my friend.
The guar must've liked the way you smell. Good noses on guar, yes?\n\nAfter all the years I've spent around these pools, all I can smell is sulfur.
If you so much as breathe on me, I will feed you to the snakes. I have had my fill of outlander men.
You are named clan friend of the Mabrigash, and you are welcome in the Vale.

The guar are all over the pools. Don't forget the harnesses. Can't send them home without harnesses.\n\nI'm just going to sit here until I can't hear the screams in my head anymore. I'm sure it won't be long.

Ha! Can you believe that? I heard what Martin said. He's either completely delusional or incredibly naive. \n\nHe's been a troublemaker all his life, and he's not getting out of those stocks anytime soon.
Othrenis is so big, and the undead are everywhere.\n\nI'll never find Eanen's tomb.
Have you seen my damned apprentice? The boy's later than usual today. With my luck, he's probably gone off and gotten the plague.
I'm quite the performer, don't you think? \n\nGo. Tell her I'm here and that I still love her. Oh, the look on her vapid, trusting face!
Eanen, you were always too casual with the commoners. Your dalliances could still stain your reputation. \n\nAnd what is this Ashlander doing here? Shouldn't she be gone?

Where's my husband? By Vivec's beard, if he's drunk and passed out somewhere, I'll leave without him. That no good, useless, piece of kwama cuttle!\n\nOh, hello. You haven't seen my husband around, have you?
I'll shed no tears over the death of that traitor, Rhavil. \n\nHe caused us so much grief, and for what? A few gold coins from the Covenant?
Let me guess. You read the letter.\n\nYou're going to leave me with this crazy woman, aren't you? Curses on you and your family!
That letter should convince Ralden that he needs to act.\n\nWe have the same goals. Remember that. Stay out of my way, and everything will turn out fine.
I can't believe it. Rhavil!
Your offering pleases me.
The Telvanni are the last source of power and comfort here at Heimlyn. Our duty lies here, but I sense yours will take you elsewhere. \n\nWalk with the Three.
The Mabrigash are still suspicious, but the wheels of commerce are turning.
My vengeance is sated.
Unless the Duke himself tells me to make an exception, the library is off-limits.
Please, speak to the others. You'll see that we're committed to recovering our missing family members.\n\nI'm going to get my egg-sister back.
You have to forgive me. I don't trust you. There's only one way for you to earn that trust.\n\nWe need weapons to rescue our people, enough to launch a full assault.
Those are big rats! They should do nicely.\n\nTake them to the door and let them loose. Then we wait. It should be entertaining to watch what happens.
Slit their throats. Throw fireballs at their heads. I don't care. Just get rid of the Maulborn.\n\nWhile you're out there, I'm sure you'll find something about the Llodos plague.

Giron wanted you out of Narsis. You need to get back there and find out why.\n\nDon't worry about those crates. The substance is diluted by now. If they ever find a way to strengthen the plague, that's when you should worry.
Any sign of Giron or Ralden?
Troubled spirits linger upon the Coiled Path.
Come back anytime. The keg's got brothers.\n\nShh! Don't tell the locals. When we bring them across the border, they get taxed as imports. As if we'd sell good mead to the likes of them!
We'll make sure these people receive care.\n\nWhen you have a moment, return to Narsis and speak to Naryu. She has a lead on the name you uncovered. I'll join you as soon as I can.
I'll gather the guards and we'll meet you there.\n\nGood luck, my friend.
Light … the … flame … wells! \n\nHurry!
Not all Dark Elves are lightweights, eh? Ha ha ha!\n\nGood on you, friend. Come back and drink with us any time.
Well, the curse is somewhat contained here.\n\nMaybe you can snuff the thing out at its source.
I'll never forget your kindness. And I'll never do anything like this again.
Did you find any clues? Why would someone would poison Deepcrag Den?

I fear I've done terrible harm to the morale of my people in Ebonheart.\n\nI'll do all I can to convince them to work with House Dres. They've been constant in their defense against the Covenant invaders.
Almalexia's blessings, outsider.
My assistants are resting and recovering now. Thanks to you, we didn't lose a single one.
Your aura portends a great destiny. Go and fulfill it.
Ah, I understand now. You must defeat the <<1>> to break the curse.
All is now clear.\n\nYou must defeat the <<1>> to break the curse.
Tell Sildras what the Poet has said. Vivec says change only occurs.
The Master is confident Sildras can bear his burdens. Tell him.
The Mother attends to greater threats and relies on Sildras to care for her children. Make sure he knows this.
Good, you're still alive. Scout Mamyne told us she sent you into this cave.\n\nVaron says he knows you from Narsis. He and his ally have offered their assistance.
Keep your nose clean in the fortress, outsider.
He's up the road. He could be coming this way.
We can't let the plague get into Mournhold. Think of all those people!\n\nYou must get those shipping manifests.
You'll need to deal with my friends and get the items I want. I may want a Foozle or I may want a Woozle. Who knows!
The sword is still here, radiating a great evil, and in general just being a bit bitchy.
Don't mind me. At least I can almost walk on this leg.
Report to Captain Noris. We're on the verge of losing Vivec's Antlers.

Our warriors guard the huts where the cultists are trapped. Unbolt the cellar doors to gain access.\n\nSo far they've refused to see reason. If it must come to blows with their lieutenants, I understand.
Our stock is a bit low, but I have a few items. A new shipment should arrive in a few days.
Missing Argonians and murdered Dunmer are one thing, but when one of our leaders goes missing, that's quite another.\n\nThe other vicecanons can't ignore this.
Gods, it felt good to bury an axe in their throats! From the prisoners trickling out, I trust you enjoyed yourself as much as I. Did you free them all?
I heard Ruvali scream. She said you chased it down here. \n\nI took a swing at it, but it got away.
You're the one who killed the Worm Cult's lapdogs. <<1>> told you the Worm Cult stole the <<z:2>>, yes? Once they discover its secrets, they'll enslave our entire village.
Is it done? Is <<1>> defeated?
Your service to House Dres and Kragenmoor will be remembered.
Eternal life is full of advantages. No need to pull your blows when training.\n\nWhat do you need, stranger?
He claims a Cat-Man can know sorrow. I should pull out his tongue.\n\nCan a mudcrab mourn? No. When you kill their brood, it's nothing to them. But when they harm someone you love ….
<<1>> presides over the Trial of the Mind, the first challenge. He'll administer the trial to any supplicant.
The power of the Zaht stones is unknowable. Perhaps now Hissmir will be safe.
It's not far. <<1>> keeps a fire burning. You can't miss it.

Hissmir is safe, thanks to you. Come back next year and share a bowl of Hist sap with me. No sooner, or your tongue will rot, your teeth dissolve, and your eyes cloud over with the milk of blindness.\n\nI joke. Your tongue won't rot. Ha!

The mercenaries only make things worse with the Dark Elves. Better if Stormhold is one happy family.\n\nAnd if you plan to start a family, might I suggest a vial of powdered kagouti horn for heightened potency? No? Your loss.
Prices posted on the board. Savings, savings, savings.
You ensured Hissmir's survival. Now we can avoid the horrors of conflict with the Aldmeri Dominion. We'll tend to the pilgrims and the Hist, as we always have and always will.
I am still waiting to see that ring of yours. Impress me!
Got a prime mess here to clean up.\n\nAt least those mechanicals are staying inside the ruin.
What can the Mabrigash do for you, outsider?
Have you done as Ra-shadda asked?
I must get to Sathram.
There is an Argonian village to the east called Lukiul Uxith. I will go there. \n\nLast-to-Water will never forgive me, but at least he is free.
I hope you fall into a pit of guar dung.
Thank you for your service.
Gods, why did I ever set foot in this stinking pit? Was it duty or stupidity?\n\nCome to mock me like the rest, have you? Well, fear not. I have no dignity left.
Those wards keep the Maulborn from getting infected by their plague. \n\nSmash them. And may the plague take them all.
We've all seen what you can do. Not looking for any trouble, stranger.
I don't like the way these mer are looking at me.
We'll keep a watchful eye on our relics. But won't that make them seem valuable to thieves?
Normally, I'd say gold is gold, but when someone tries buying my town, I get nasty.\n\nNever liked Khajiit anyway. Nothing but mangy fur and lice. Not clean, like proper scales.
I've given you what you need. Leave me with my prize. Many days of pleasure ahead.
Captain Doronil made me his second-in-command. We'll have Tal'Deic Fortress in top form by week's end!
Superb work. The Pact stands strong thanks to people like you.
Don't just stand there with your mouth open. You're attracting flies. Speak!
Gah! Don't kill me! Someone, help!
I'll leave <<1>> by tomorrow morning. I want no trouble.
The northeast road always used to be safe. Now that you've stopped those Dominion murderers, perhaps it is again.
Keep your skills sharp, outsider.
I saw how you put those Sentinels in their place. Thanks!
Thank you, I can make it from here. You have a good heart. \n\nI think <<1>> will be pleased with you, even though you didn't finish your path. Find him to the southeast.
