We'll quit this place soon and disappear into the wastes again. The housemen will hunt us. They always do, but they won't catch us.\n\nBid farewell to Tirinaat, if you wish. May your kills be quick and many, traveler.

Kaoc! Right under my snout. Kill her and any of her thugs in your way.\n\nAnd don't get greedy. Don't try to sneak off with that Dominion paychest. That's mine! It's my payment for freeing your Dark Elf friend.
I'm not afraid. Life without Eroni is empty.
I hear you're the one to thank for finally doing something about all this. Some of us appreciate it.

It appears I owe you an apology, as well as my gratitude. My behavior was uncalled for. It's just that my wife … she was all I had. \n\nThanks to you, they've released her body, and we can finally return to Mournhold.
You're back. The wasps weren't too much trouble then?
I can't believe it. The Dominion is in Stormhold.\n\nAnd they were right under our noses the entire time.
Yes! The dead will guard us forever!
You should have taken the keystone, there is nothing left for me here except for these statues. I built them to remember my people, so I could have someone to talk to ….
You must make haste, esteemed leader. If the Dominion troops leave with their treasure, <<1>> will be very unhappy indeed.
It's not every day I get a chance to dissect a Dwarven resonator. Powered by minor soul gems, you know.
We're in your debt, my friend. With the Dominion exposed, the ugly rumors of Argonians preying upon Dark Elves can be put to rest.
It's all going wrong. The cycle has begun anew with hate and bloodshed. Curate Brethis wanted peace, but the others … I had to run.\n\nWhat happened in the cave? Where is the Ashkhan?
You must hurry! Dolril will be dead and the relic will surely be stolen if you don't act quickly!
Come aboard my boat. I will take you across the swamp waters.
Present this writ to your new master. They will train you in the ways of your craft.
I'm not sending any troops into this town. There's no reason to fight these pirates until I have to.\n\nYour friend One-Eye should know that someday, the Pact may be forced to come back here.
I'll make a break for it while you deal with those geodes.\n\nIf we're both lucky, I'll meet you outside the village south of here.
The Trial of the Mind is your first challenge. The Trial is located in a hut on the northwest corner of the pyramid.
The Trial of the Mind is your first challenge. The Trial is located in a hut on the northwest corner of the pyramid.
I plan to head north, past Stormhold, perhaps into Stonefalls, but I will avoid the mire. That is west of here, before one reaches Hissmir.\n\nDo not tell him what I said. The letter will suffice.
The map's all yours. I should have known better. I'm no adventurer!

<<1>> didn't forget about me—but I never read the letters she spoke of. If my wife were alive, I'd ask her what became of those letters.\n\nNow I think it's better not to speculate. My wife is dead and that is the past.
What you've done was no easy task. We have a difficult road ahead of us.
Dendras told me about the Dominion and what you did for us.\n\nIt's a shame Naldyn had to die. Dendras loved him, although he wouldn't admit it.
It's heartening to see people willing to fight for us. I think the Shadowscales are heroes.
I'll pray for an answer to your voice at the shrines.\n\nPraying for prayers! Perhaps Vivec will appreciate how circular that is.
You mentioned J'kur. Did you see him?
We did it! We walked into an inferno and emerged unscathed. We defeated a Brother of Strife!\n\nThis is worthy of an epic … or a monument in Mournhold!
You've done the impossible. I was wise to see the stone in your spirit.\n\nThen again, I'm known for being wise.
We'll hold the line here as long as we can.\n\nNo Scamp will get past us, not as long as we draw breath.
The Altmer harms no one, but by remaining here with her, he harms us all.\n\nI will pray for his safety, but the wispmother must be stopped. Do what you must.
I came to this hallowed place to learn, not to deal with petty thieves.\n\nI'll report you to <<1>>. She won't tolerate vagabonds on this site.
I fear what will happen if we do this, soldier. We'll see fire and death, but I don't see another way.\n\nWhen people ask you about today, tell them that Sadal did it for his people.
Well, we're one step closer to living through this day.\n\nI never thought I'd say that.
Who'd think a mere soldier in the standing army would be up to something like this.\n\nYou ever think about going into business for yourself?
Pray at the fire, soldier. You shall have the honor of ushering in the Chimer's finest hour.
Get out! Out! \n\nBeloved, send this lout away!
You found Risa's amulet! Please, give it to my poor mother.
I'm a bit more at peace, now that I have Risa's amulet. I feel like I can sense her presence sometimes. Like she's watching over me.
Our village is an … unusual place, traveler. You really should talk to <<1>>.
Any luck finding the crystal fragments?
You must recover the shards of my Crystal of Power.
Would you happen to have my shards?
Recover the crystals quickly before more dremora make it through!
Good luck getting those crystals.
The only way to get my crystal back is by killing those deviils. Please make sure there's no blood on the shards, though.
Strange lights emanate from three locations in the ruins above. That's where I'd look for the wards. Once they fall, the way into Vox's lair should be clear.
You should talk to my father, Grandmaster Tanval. He leads House Indoril.

I got really angry when I realized you'd preserved the <<z:1>>. Eternity is a long time, and I wanted to make that decision myself.\n\nBut eternity means I have forever to make the world a better place. So I guess I should thank you.
Yes?
You grace us with your presence, muthsera.\n\nIf this humble servant can assist you, please don't hesitate to ask.
Please don't interrupt me.
I'm happy to be out of that cage.
Thanks for saving me!
Please! Can you get me out of here?
You'll find Noris in the army camp to the west. \n\nIf you end up near the weird yellow rock-trees guarded by giant lobster-bug things, you've gone too far.
I felt a burst of power from the Temple and ventured within, fearing the worst.\n\nBut you've prevailed. What have you discovered?
Missing Argonians and murdered Dunmer are one thing, but to have Vicecanon Hrondar missing, that's a different pot of stew. \n\nThe other vicecanons can't ignore this.
First, Argonians and Dunmer disappear. Now a vicecanon goes missing? \n\nThe other vicecanons can't ignore this.
Thanks Again.
If you banish the wisps, maybe their victims can escape.
Speak with <<1>>. She'll fill you in on the specifics. Don't waste time. The honor of the Dark Brotherhood is at stake.
<<1>> is waiting for you inside the ruins. Hurry.
Sorry, no iron to sell. At least not until the mine gets working again.
Good to see you back again, Adept. The Guild is stronger with you at our side.
I can't wait to get back to Daggerfall for a pint at the Hare and Dragon.
Well, the Lion Guard promised to let me proceed with my research at the tower, but I must wait some indefinite amount of time before Farwatch is deemed "safe."\n\nWhat a crock.
You won't tell anyone I tried to dig through stone, will you?
I am in your debt, stranger. \n\nFare you well.
I feel like someone's torn my insides out. I think I prefer the nightmares and the voices to this ….\n\nOn second thought, no. No, I don't.
The containment cell will hold. \n\nWe won't be disturbed now, as we return to our primary goal of slaughtering sub-human primitives. The Goblins, I mean.
I hope <<1>> is still alive. I heard horrible screams coming from the camp.
The fighting in the Worm Cult camp died down, but I'm hearing screams.
She's alive and at home, at least for now. \n\nAnd for now, that is all I can ask.
Go. Kill the Orc. When my digestion recovers, you will find me in Lukiul Uxith.
If you're traveling through Shadowfen, we may meet again.\n\nWith you, I'm sure it will always be interesting.
One-Who-Breaks-Mountains. The name is well-earned. I told Seven-Bellies you'd gone to face the Orc, but sadly, Pash-Riha has not returned.

The Three weep for the blood spilled today. I'll try to explain what happened to the house members.\n\nTruth to Vivec, I doubt they'll listen to me. Blood calls for blood, and this fight has been going on for a long time.
You should hurry. If you don't, there might not be any Covenant troops left to kill.
I hope Bendyn makes it back alive. He's insane, but he's a good man.
Welcome back to the Hall! Remember your comrades behind the lines next time you're on the front.
You look like you could handle yourself in a fight.\n\nThe Fighters Guild is always looking for more help. Talk to the Hall Steward to join up!
Don't tell me. The less I know, the better. Get to <<1>> right away and report to her. She's waiting in the center of town.
The urns of Nerathren and Faryon are in the chapel beneath this temple.\n\nTake some of their ashes. Then cast them into the eternal flames in the north and south towers.
Just because you can fight doesn't mean you're invincible. Remember that.\n\nNot that I care. But be careful. Or not. Your choice, not mine.
Did you get the stuff from the locked chests?
Thanks for bringing back my guar!\n\nI can tell they're happy to be back. They're giving off their happy musk.
Please, talk to the tree-minder. If there's anything you can do to help us, the Hist will surely reward you.
Diiril was headed for those ruins on the south side of the gorge. \n\nNaryu and I will stay up here until the plague blows away.
The courtyard is under control, but we need to find <<1>>. Search the buildings and find where he's holed up.
Please, leave me to my grief.
Be careful of the hoarvors. They're the giant tick-like creatures burrowing through the muck.\n\nUsually, they're a nuisance, but lately the blood-suckers have been downright dangerous.
Seeing you in action was a privilege, friend.
The Dominion will think twice before setting foot in Shadowfen again.
You did it. And the unfortunate people of Murkwater know they've been avenged.
Use the power of the keystone well, friend.
These <<mz:1>> usually prey on rodents, birds, and other small animals.\n\nNow they're attacking us. That's proof something's wrong with the swamp.
You go on ahead. I'm going to stay here to see if I can learn anymore about the Dominion's plan for Shadowfen. Thank you for keeping the keystone out of their hands.
Welcome to the Fighters Guild. Direct all questions to Hall Steward Nardis. I just oversee the armory.
The Ashlanders haven't attacked again, but the job still isn't done. We need this tunnel collapsed.

I'm worried about <<1>>. Without his spiritual guidance in this time of tragedy, I fear our order will crumble.\n\nStill, he insists we must have the <<2>>, and he could not bear to stand away while others suffer so he remains in Muth Gnaar.
Is it done? I put the Tear of Saint Veloth in a safe place.\n\nNow maybe the Ashlanders will leave us alone.
Ah … the corruption. It's too strong.\n\nWho … who are you? If you're allied with the Daedra, I'll send you back to Oblivion, screaming.
I was in contemplation. It's ill-mannered to intrude. Why have you done so?
Please, leave me to my prayers. They're all I have now.
The Volek daughter can be found at the nearby inn. Look for her there.
My family's townhouse is nearby. Meet me there and we'll settle this.
Were you able to gather any kwama cuttle?
Please don't judge House Dres by the actions of Lady Vox.\n\nI knew she was up to no good, but not blasphemy. Never that.
Vox wasn't always like this. Once, she willingly served the Tribunal and was committed to its cause.
The stocks are south of that beached hulk called the Blasted Breton. You can't miss it.\n\nIn a few days, the smell will lead you there. And no taking his pants. Those are mine!
Please, they need help at the Sulfur Pools.
Thank you for helping our Glorious Expedition for Nord Cultural Exchange.\n\nHopefully, the registrar will call soon. In the meantime, I have leads on where you can take items for trade.
The Temple of Sul sounds extraordinary. I contemplate an expedition of my own.
Are you sure you don't want another goat?
I am really not feeling well … I'm dizzy, and I keep seeing these weird visions … this has been going on for months!
Just in time! We've got a mess on our hands, worse than after a dog eats a cheese wheel.
You may look like someone I met in Stormhold, but make any sudden moves and I'll shred your false skin.
How long was <<1>> a skin-stealer? I fear it will take months to undo the damage wrought by his imposter.
Thank you for helping me. I didn't want to become snake food.\n\nRagara and the others are outside, if you're looking for them.
Face down in the sand isn't the way I wanted to go out. Divines bless you for saving me.
They didn't pay us enough for this job.
Do I still look poisoned? I feel different. Gods, I bet they laid eggs in my head!
You're not half-bad. Got a good sense of honor beneath that hard exterior.
Your claws are sharp, traveler. My spawn does not deserve the kindness you've visited upon his scaly hide.\n\nOn behalf of the rest of us, I thank you.

You know what I'd think if someone asked me where we should look for reinforcements? Summoning the spirits of past Ordinators would have been far down my list.\n\nAnd how does a spirit hold a sword? Are their swords ghostly too?
Word has reached me that Zehtswater Cave is pure again. This means good things for my business.

Door's open. The Dremora didn't pull our stomachs through our nostrils. I call that success.\n\nThe Hist vats are further down the passage. You set them on fire. I'll stick to shadows and find signs of where <<1>> went, yes?
Ysgramor himself would be proud. Glory for the Pact!
Activate the wards while I find Tanval.
I can't face Garyn like this.
I brought this threat about. I know that now. I hope I can help stop it before it's too late.
Until the Ashlander supplies are burning, we have nothing to discuss.
Burn their supplies! Make them suffer as we have suffered.
Thank you for helping us. Make the Vereansu pay for what they did!
The sooner you talk to the Tree-Minder, the better. I'm not sure how much longer we can keep these creatures out of the village.
All's well that ends well, I always say.
We'll rebuild from this attack. Thanks to you, we can continue our holy work.
Return with the stone or die. It's really up to you, mortal.
Ready to begin your next test?
My continued presence in your realm burdens my soul. Complete your task, mortal.
This is the path you must take to bind Sadal. It's neither easy nor straightforward, rather like your mortal lives.
What a capable servant you are!\n\nSo many to disembowel for their intransigence. I'm practically shivering with anticipation!
Let's enter the portal. I long to be done with this.
Sovngarde awaits, my friend. I bet that Brother of Strife can't wait to go.
The death of <<1>> can't be traced to us. You don't need to know why.\n\nConsult the Brothers here if you need advice.
Find a way to kill <<1>> and I'll reward you handsomely.
Looking for information?
We heard a commotion outside. What happened? Did you find my father?
Perhaps life will return to normal now. \n\nNormal, what am I saying? Father's dead. Normal doesn't exist anymore.
Though I speak, do you truly listen? I suppose time will tell.
Though the Shadowscales are the leader's hands, the Speaker and the Listener are the mouth and the ears.\n\nApproach them with respect. Their wisdom is not for the weak-willed.
Watch yourself. This area is dangerous even when there aren't enemy soldiers prowling around.
I got word of what you did in <<1>>. Pushing back the Dominion like that. Impressive work.
You were right … about everything. My wife is as dead as she ever was. It was all simply a lie.
You are kind, stranger, though I don't know why you would do this. \n\nI appreciate your concern nonetheless.
Close those portals before the Scamps overrun us all.
I hear you're the reason we aren't trapped here anymore. If you're ever in Kvatch, look me up. I'll cover your drinks at the arena.

Hey. Hey. Thanks for saving me back in Razak's. You're one of the good ones, you know? You are.

And hey! Hey. I got my leave. I'm not drunk. Just on my leave.

Shh.
Almsivi see you to your destination. With luck, the Dominion won't be so fortunate.
Mavos is about to buckle. Hurry!
My father wasn't at our camp!\n\nWait, where are <<1>> and the others? A tree-minder never leaves a fire untended!
I listen patiently for the worth amongst your words.
Freedom! I felt my soul being released. Divines bless you!

Veloth's hammer allows Vox to strip away the souls of those she slays and imprison them in her misty realm. They lose their memories and grant her almost divine power.\n\nTo challenge Vox, you need to set those souls free.
I don't understand why you're here, but there must be a reason. \n\nI need time. Give me time to think. Speak to my companions.
I … I have feeling in my hands again. My memories. What … what happened to me?\n\nThe Tribunal sent you to free me, didn't they? I knew they would not forsake me to be damned to this place.
Please hurry to Eidolon's Hollow and put a stop to Magistrix Vox's madness.
He's back unharmed! He's still a Goblin, but … well ….
And Dithis has returned. Unharmed, from the looks of his green skin.
You're not with the tribe, are you? Help me!

Daedric Princes are not supposed to meddle in our affairs. My companion thought he had dealt with that threat.\n\nBut that is not your concern. You have done well and earned our approval. Walk in blessings.
The Hist … our link is gone!
Have you come to stop the Dominion soldier who devours my kin?
So, scavenger, have you enjoyed picking through the hamlet's bones? Have you found all the treasures you desire?
That brother-thing dead, my men safe from Scamps … you've proven yourself the very soul of Ysgramor. Well done!
Being dead, I have a certain immunity to Balreth's power. \n\nI'm keenly interested to see what happens in the next few minutes.

In one thing, <<1>> was correct. You are no true Shadowscale. With the traitor revealed, your time here must end.\n\nBut I require one final service, one last judgment. You shall set my children into motion.
You've done the guild a great service here today, one that will not be forgotten.
Father was such a good man. I'm glad he managed to help you.
I can't believe that Tidyn is gone.
My brother went to lead the Goblins away. We're hoping he succeeds and returns safely.\n\nThanks for your help, my friend.
I knew you were game.
I don't suppose the Triumvirate has smiled upon us and the Vicecanons have answered our call? I am a smith, not a diplomat or guardsmen; these intrigues and disruptions are beyond my ken.
Thanks. We had a problem here we just couldn't handle ourselves.
I heard the alarms from the Dominion camp. Is the butcher dead?
Get going. This is no place for the living. Balreth is caged forever … thanks to you.
You can't be here for the reward. I just had it posted.
Remember, friend. Kaasha has provided. Perhaps you will not forget her.
Your skill is legendary, comrade. Stendarr truly has his arm around you. I'm glad you're on our side.
You're starting to make quite the name for yourself, you know.\n\nJust be sure not to be too noticeable. Aelif is worried that the brave mouse will get eaten by the hungry cat.
Together, finally. S'rendarr answered my prayers.
I'd given up hope of ever being free from this place. Now I have to decide what to do with myself.
You'd be a great asset to any Ashlander tribe … if you weren't a heretic, that is.
You'll defeat <<1>>, outsider. May Sithis watch over you.
The sooner you talk to the tree-minder, the better. He's sure to know what's wrong with the swamp.
By Vivec! This is incredible.
This worm was a disappointment to Aelif. He was not much of a fight.

Tanval left me in charge, warming the hilt until the Great Houses choose a permanent commander. Do you have any idea how many meetings I'll have to go to?\n\nAfter I die, I'll give Tanval a beating he won't forget.
As mud is my mother! Njorlund breathes no more. Sithis has called him back to chaos.
When you finish, report to me or to Ordinator Eron in Mournhold.\n\nKill as many of the bastards as you can.
I'm sorry. I didn't mean for anyone to get hurt.
Please find my sister. She has a knack for getting into trouble.
That relic you found will make our reputation. We can't thank you enough. \n\nEr, do you still have my control rod?
I could spend weeks taking this thing apart. \n\nThen it'll take Raynor years to put it back together again.
How strange to see someone out here who's not part of my tribe.
We can't thank you enough for what you've done. I hope my offering helps in your endeavors.
I don't quite know why, but I feel safer with you around.\n\nThank you again.
Give me a moment to catch my breath and I'll meet you outside.
We'll have some tales to tell in Hatching Pools. I hope we see you there.
I'll straighten out the family's affairs here in town, and then we'll see what can be done about the farm.

There's no use going back to Stormhold. I've seen their next assignment for me: a percolating mire. Sounds like a pleasant place, doesn't it?\n\nBy the Three, I pray giant leeches devour me. That would be a blessing.
My memories consume me.\n\nHow I long to return to the Hist.
We'll banish the last few Daedra once we've had time to catch our breath.
After you close these thrice-damned portals, meet me near the central dais.
I'll look for you down the river, comrade. You'll hear from us once we've decoded the journal.
Something tells me we'll see each other again. I look forward to fighting by your side once more.
You and your acts will be duly recorded in the archives. You will live on in the scrolls … forever.
There are books where we go, yes? I love the feel of paper against my skin. The raised texture of illuminated script … like a lover's lips. A lover who will never, ever nag you.
All this wailing and anguish. It sharpens no quills.
The darkness. Thank the Eye for the darkness.
This one knew Sees-All-Colors was responsible.
You've done well. The Golden Eye has what he needs.
It's not that simple. You have to be invited. No invitation, no boat ride to the island. \n\nThe Academy is quite exclusive. Not like the Mages Guild.
If you want to return to Mournhold, just let me know. I exist on this plane to serve.
I've made my decision! If my father sent you to talk me out of this, you can go tell him I'm through speaking to him.
I'm sorry, I'm kind of distracted at the moment. Can I help you?
Glad to see the river has been good to you. Me? I'm going back to Black Marsh.\n\nI'll probably get eaten on the way there. Or trip and fall on a war. Feh.
I've always found the study of Daedra fascinating. It's unfortunate that so much knowledge about them is forbidden by the Tribunal.
You have recovered my sacred skull. Now you can restore my reliquary.
Remember, wine comes in bottles: round, thin bottles. Probably on the ground. Can't miss them.
I hope I come to understand why you did … what you did.
If you need a reminder, touch the vision orb again. The sequence will repeat.
Thanks again for bringing me those supplies.
All those feathers flying! Mother Morrowind, I couldn't stop laughing.
We have a special surprise for our target in our storeroom. A very special something that will bring about a painful end. People will remember what we do, mark my word.
I think I got it from here.\n\nEr, thanks for the help. Maybe I'll get a chance to cast some spells after all.
Is little friend safe?
Just let me know what I can do to help.
Were you successful? Have you forged the weapon? We have more need of it now than ever, my friend. As you well saw.
May Stendarr keep you safe, comrade. We'll have need of your strength in the days to come.
You will always be welcome at the Academy. \n\nEspecially if we're menaced by mystic threats from beyond space and time again.
I'm glad to see you awake.
Pain opens the door to corruption, separating body and spirit. \n\nHealing cannot be complete while the corruptor lurks nearby.
You have slain the rot at my roots. You have restored my clarity.
Welcome. Today, you've protected those who cannot protect themselves.
They didn't expect to see a Dunmer, so I made sure they didn't. I can be stealthy at need.
You should talk to the boss lady. She'll want to debrief you.
The damned dryskins will pay for what they've done!\n\nSomeday, we'll take the fight to their own homes.
Jofnir murdered! The whole guild will hear of this. And Aelif's suspicions.
<<1>> was an excellent master general. He deserved the honor of death on the battlefield.
By the Twin Ravens, I owe you my thanks, mortal.
By my sacred oath, that is the only portion of the performance I am allowed to impart. Seek more knowledge in the mora, where the bittergreen grows thick among the bal.
I can say no more. Seek further knowledge at a cornerclub, and while you're at it, have a mazte for me.
More I cannot say. Seek in the tallest of the bal, where the roobrush and chokeweed grow thickest.
Go carefully, comrade. Uncertain times in Tamriel. Only thing you can be sure of is a good weapon.
I must finish this performance. Please wait.
Look! See! Didn't mention this before, but you have beautiful eyes.\n\nWhen you die, can I eat them? Snack?
I'd keep my snout shut about the Vicecanons while you're here. They aren't exactly well-liked—in fact some of the boys would love to show them their gizzards.
Pardon me. I must begin this translation. These runes … fascinating.
Curse the Mad God. I don't know what game he's playing with you. \n\nBut I do know the stakes.
That was unexpectedly competent. You'd make an adequate house servant.\n\nI don't suppose you'd consider it? The pay is meager, but the fringe benefits are appalling.
Puppy-killer! Come to steal me books? Wha …? Who? Where? What? When? Sometimes why!\n\nSpeak up! Honesty is the best policy, as far as you know.
My task at court is distributing the flesh of the fallen to the citizens of Crow's Wood.\n\nYou are a citizen now. Would you like eyeballs? Tender spleens?
The toll! Paid the toll! Featherless has paid the toll.
Take care of your new vassals, fledgling.
I can't face my partner just yet.\n\nLet me be for now. Let me be.
Who are you and what do you want with me?
Surii finally sent help? The Goblins went crazy and started killing without warning. I barely escaped!
There's grub grass under the western waterfall.\n\nYou'll need to stuff it in a vial and rush it back here. No time to lose on this brew!
That mammoth won't shut up.
What were we talking about? Please, Mistress. Don't hurt me.
Who? What are you? Another phantom come to take me to Sovngarde?
I see you've accepted Svari's invitation. She will be a worthy successor to Tirora. One more step in rebuilding what was destroyed.
Alas, the evil giant Sinmur has returned. Every leaf trembles now. Tell Vigrod everything you saw.
Do you still have business at the prison?
You have my precious crystals! I can smell them. Gimme!
Slay Cloggg and earn my esteem. Oh, and a reward.
Why am I still crying? These are tears of joy.
I'm glad to see you're still alive. Have you found the shards of the Crystal of Power yet?
Have you found the crystals?
Shoo! On with it.
Go away, before I call a guard to deal with you.
<cough> Do you have the crystals?
You saved our lives, but to what end? Our homes are destroyed and Sinmur could come back at any time.
I couldn't bear the thought of leaving my wife for Shor. Thank you.
I'll be honest. I thought I was dead. Thank you, for all you've done.
I can't believe this. Shor's Stone ruined and the Companions' Hall overrun!
I can still smell the blood. It was all over the mine and those foul Reachmen. My mining days are over.
Wish I could've taken a blade to those Quagmire bastards myself.
You'll find <<1>> in the main building. He's seen great things concerning you!
Oh, you're not a Goblin. \n\nIf I had a weapon, I would have flattened all these stinking runts, but they caught me by surprise. I told Surii this was a bad idea!
Thanks for the assist thanks.
I'll make a break for it while you're freeing my guards from those Black Soul Gems.\n\nIf we're both lucky, I'll meet you on top of that hill to the south.
Are we far enough away from those cultists now? I'd rather not run any more, if it's all the same to you.
I shiver to think what those Supernal Dreamers hay have done to me.
I doubt <<1>> took <<A:2>> far from here.
Come, come! Let's find Nord. He hides in building next door.
Thanks again for freeing me.\n\nNow, you should go off and have more adventures. I think I've had my fill of those.
It's good to be free.
You look familiar. Are you?
<<1>> and I are going to rest before we brave the road to Mud Tree.\n\nMaybe you should rest, too. You don't look so well.
Hey, here comes my hero!
Well, this is different. I guess.
Maybe next time, I can fight at your side instead of watching from a distance.\n\nI'd like that.
Prepare yourself for trouble. The lamias will slay you for their supper, if given a chance.
I'm glad Shalidor found you. I need your help.
Who are you? Did Surii send you to kill me?
We'll keep the Dominion trapped in the ruins while you seek <<1>>. And watch out for the lamias! They're territorial and vicious.
Praise the maker! You saved her! As her life is saved, so is mine!
Fallowstone Hall has fallen! There's no hope without the Companions!
I knew she was alive, and I knew you were the one to save her! I'm eternally grateful!
<This Nord was recently and violently killed. His belongings are in disarray.>

Many thanks for for your help but the mine isn't quite up to full production again. It's getting organized again and all, but my shift hasn't gotten back into the mine yet.\n\nSo, I was wondering if you could help me. Again. As it were.
Thanks, friend. Be careful on the roads. The Maulborn are everywhere. If you see one, stab the s'wit or run away. Don't try to talk to these fanatics. You'll get nowhere.
I figured <<1>> would send someone after the totem. Just had to hide nearby and wait for rescue.\n\nAnd here you are. I'm not delirious enough to think she sent you to save me.
What are the Maulborn up to? Why experiment with a plague? It doesn't make sense.
Welcome to Vernim Wood. Dark waters run in this river.
I can feel this body decaying. So much pain. Please, kill me!
A still-beating heart. Either Dajaheel sent you or this is an extraordinary coincidence.\n\nMay I?
Be safe in your travels, and may Tall Papa guide your steps.
Shall we raise the curtain? Begin the first act?
Magnificent! That couldn't have gone better!
Be careful. The blood has called in a pride of sabre cats. They're prowling on the ridge north of the farm.
My friend! I didn't think I'd see you again so soon. Look, I need to see to this wound. I know I can trust you.\n\nWill you go after my girls?
Shor's favor! A friendly face. I managed to get away from the Worm Cult … and now I'm trapped up here!\n\nCan you clear a path for me?
Shor's bones!
If you would like to join the Mages Guild, please visit the closest guild hall.
It seemed urgent. Please don't keep her waiting.
I've nothing left, so these will help a lot. After I've mourned my husband, I'll sell them and use the money to leave this place. It holds too many bad memories.
I hope you can help Yiri. Her father saved my life when we were children.
A slave in such finery? Purloined, no doubt! Grovel suitably for your crimes and I may behead you apace.
We owe you our lives. If ever you travel this way again once we've rebuilt it, you will be an honored guest.
<Gugnar is dead.>
If you gather the <<1>> for the tree-minder's ritual, she'll help <<2>>.
I have been waiting for our brother's return. He is somewhere among the Goblins.\n\nMay he find good mud and plentiful fish.
This foreman will not admit defeat. She's like the iron she mines.\n\nOf course, that doesn't make her wise.
Always sad to see a good man die. Leo's death, just now? Hilarious! Hah.
Bastards just won't lie down and die. Well. I'll see to it we give as good as we get. Ysgramor!
Don't wait for me. I'll be along shortly.\n\nI have some supplies to scrounge up: shovels, food, that sort of stuff. The life of a quartermaster is an exciting one.
The bodies of my egg-siblings were desecrated by <<A:1>>! Until they're whole, I cannot return them to the Hist.
Evacuate, they said.\n\nI'm going to lie here and look at the sky for a while. I think if I stood up, I'd fall down.
Ysgramor must be watching over you, friend. You shouldn't be alive.
Get that fire lit. We'll be ready to go when you get back.
We can take care of ourselves from here. May you swim freely down the river of life.
I wouldn't have thought those milk drinkers would leave their cozy taverns to come down here.\n\nI'll have to get this wound seen to, then. I'm going to need my sword arm!
You're alive! I didn't think it possible!
You need three runestones to unlock the door. Move, you pustulant maggot!
You. Get me out of here.
I've got nothin' more to say to you.
I don't understand why he'd trick us. We followed him here, like lambs to the slaughter.
We knew a man, Old Rory. He went in. When the soldiers dragged him out, he was missing all his bones.\n\nI'll give you until my fire burns out. Then I'm coming in after you.
<The skeleton stands mute before you. It sways slightly with unnatural life, but shows no sign of malicious will.>
You still here?
This won't take long. Patience, friend.
You're not one of the bandits. Help me!
Please, look for my family. I miss my dear Rexus!\n\nAnd Geilund, of course.
I never thought I'd be glad to smell that dog's rotten breath again. Thank Kyne!\n\nSomeone's getting a big steak for dinner. Yes, he is!
Thank you for coming along when you did. Squeak!\n\nEr, excuse me.
You were ordered to leave. What lies beyond this door is not for your eyes.
Go away, little squirrel. Before the shiny stones find you.
Wish me luck, my friend. I'll need it, this time around.
Don't worry, adept. I'll be fine soon enough. Now that you've restored my mind, I just need some rest.
<<<1>> bounces back and forth under your hand. He looks like he wants you to follow.>
Good, you made it.
So, what did you find out?
Welcome to trouble. Our little Captain Rana doesn't know what she's doing.
Thanks for your aid. That was like being touched by Sheogorath.
I'll never look at a cat the same way again.
The mad god Sheogorath can't resist meddling with mortals, eh? His disciples all belong in a cell.

Flesh-walkers rarely visit our dreams, small one. The whorls of your thoughts bring warmth to our own.\n\nSoon we awaken, to nourish ourselves back to health. You must leave, or be dashed against our dreams.
I have the spell prepared. Are you ready to receive it?
Ah, it's so good to meet someone with the right priorities.
The traitor has fled from justice. Right into the arms of her supposed foe, Molag Bal. \n\nHow deep does her treachery go? We must follow her to Oblivion itself!

The messenger found you? I'm glad. I was hoping that we'd meet under better circumstances ….\n\nThis is a sad day for the guild, but I'm glad we'll at least perform this terrible duty together. I still can't believe Sees-All-Colors betrayed us.
That statue, those nests … are we within the Hist's memories? And those creatures … brothers to this Hist!\n\nSomething's wrong. The Hist-brothers seem agitated about these memories.
I have lived to see one of the worst calamities in history ravage our realm. It must be stopped, no matter the cost.
I can't thank you enough for finding my brother.
Find the Earth-Turners. I'm going to sit here and let the fire warm my bones. \n\nMaybe I'll take a few more of them with me before I go.
I'm off to celebrate. Stay moist, friend.
They … came from underground! I saw them drag the others away.
Greetings, friend. What can I do for you?
Find Damar. He can tell you more about what's happening here. I'm not from this village. I know nothing other than what I see.
Why should we run? Can't we fight them?\n\nWhy is everyone so worried? We are Nords and they aren't.
Getting out while the getting's good, eh?\n\nI'm not arguing. Just wish Maesa would put down her tools and join us. My wife's stubborn—she'll be the last to go.
If we actually evacuate, I can down tools and leave in seconds. No reason to stop working now.\n\nSo. There anything you need?
I don't understand any of this. We haven't evacuated since Captain Rana came. Is this some kind of practice evacuation?
Ain't leaving our pigs. No chance. Them damned Daggers would carve them up for bacon.
Don't know why I'm still here. Just spreading the kindling for the damn Daggers.
I'm sure we'll see each other again, friend.
Alms for the homeless?
My guar were lost, and now they're found. Thank you, sun on my scales.
We must evacuate. We'll make our way to Davon's Watch.\n\nIt's always the same. When the waves of war roll in, the people of the earth are lost to the flood.
You are the sun on my scales. I will think of you every day at evening meditation.
We're safe from the Daggers, but we're still in danger. \n\nIt's always this way when war looms.
I will offer myself to the Pact army. The Daggers will regret leaving <<1>> alive.
Confront her, my friend. Perhaps the life of Sees-All-Colors might yet be spared.
What are you waiting for, comrade? Kill her!

I still live! The Countess spoke of my service as a punishment … but truly I am happy just to laze in the river's waters. Merric will make an excellent Guildmaster.\n\nAnd I have you to thank for this. My friend.
I know it's a hard choice, but you must go to the fort or the docks. \n\nLend your strength where you think it's needed most.
We should've sent you to Black Marsh. You weren't meant to be a slave, <<1>>, my son.
<<1>>, I've seen you talking to my daughter without bowing your head. Never do that again!
<<1>>! I heard you talking to <<2>>.\n\nYou're not going to Percolating Mire, are you?
Quickly! Before they kill more of my kin.
Hurry to the docks. Seyne won't last long by herself.
Captain Rana wouldn't let us follow her. She made us turn back. \n\nShe blames herself for Bleakrock. She's not out to stop the Covenant. She's out for redemption.
My new mead really knocked you on your arse! I call that an unqualified success!
Welcome to Dhalmora, little egg.
I'm not sure what to do now. Should we rebuild or should we leave Lower Yorgrim to the giants? I'm just not sure.
I can't wait to tell Haraldar that this Kazok bastard is dead.
The people of Lower Yorgrim will soon come around to my way of thinking. After all, we are what we eat!
What can I do for you?
Give me a few minutes to catch my breath. Head into the keep. I'll join you in a few minutes.
It's good to see some people have open minds. \n\nI hope to see you again, friend.
Kyne bless you, stranger.\n\nCaptain Alhana commands the brigade. She's an excellent leader and a terror with a blade, but they should have been back by now.
Find a way to kill <<1>> and I'll reward you handsomely.
I think my Inga would be pleased that her family name and business will go on. And we're making some damned fine mead, if I do say so myself.

We're in the dark stuck in this cabin. We need to know what's going on out there. Eliminate witches and the enthralled soldiers and search them for anything that might prove useful.\n\nIf you can find the Keepers, we might just have a chance.
Inga would be so happy to see the meadery open again.
I'm glad someone warned Davon's Watch. I just hope it was soon enough.
You're back! Were you able to kill any of those beasts? And did you bring us any of their pelts?
I'm done with Lower Yorgrim. Things were starting to get bad there even before the giants showed up.
I smell fresh Kyne's Breath! It reminds me of when I was a little girl, running through the fields in spring.\n\nI miss those simpler days.
Before we continue, we need to be at our full strength.\n\nI need you to get those sprigs of Kyne's Breath back to Fresgil at the other cabin. Once Droi is cured, we can worry about our next move.
End the witch. For all of us.\n\nDon't worry about me. I'll be fine. This tree's doing a great job of holding me up.
Leave me alone. Just when I thought I'd drunk away all the pain, you tell me about my mother. Looks like I'll need another pint now … maybe four.
Kyne forgave us both this day. We need to repent. But to be in Kyne's favor again! I forgot what that felt like.
We must press on. We'll burn these foul eggs after you clear out the spiders.
I'm sure you have more important things to do than chat with me, comrade.
Please, just leave me alone.
Get to the watchtower as soon as you can. \n\nThere's just no time.
Everywhere you go, the Daggers roll back like an ebbing tide.\n\nStill, there are plenty more. The Pact will need a steady supply of guar-hide armor.
Vivec keep us! The Covenant is raiding along the coast.\n\nI have family in Senie. I wonder if I'll ever see my brother again.
I can't believe I missed the whole battle with the Daggers.\n\nWho am I supposed to fight now? Dark Elf nobles? They can't fight for bull stool, and when you hit them, all they do is whine.
You upheld my honor and the honor of Windhelm. This Ebonheart Pact is worth more than I hoped.\n\nMay all your enemies fall before you!
Do as I say. Leave this place.\n\nYou can't rescue the Keepers. They don't need to be rescued, since they no longer exist.
She's alive … hurt and frightened, but alive.
Were the rumors true? Was it a necromancer after all?
The finest plate in Stonefalls, straight from my father's forge.\n\nYou've never seen the like. I guarantee it.
I'll listen to Bishalus next time. I've got nothing to prove to her.
Please. Don't let Darj down, not after all he's done for us.
Speak to <<1>> in the keep.
Speak to <<1>> in the keep. Better be quick about it.
Go to the soldiers in the Keeper's house. I'm sure they're confused and uncertain about events here.
Thane Mera needs to speak with you. You can find her in front of the palace.
Go. I'll meet you on the docks.

I expect you've come to learn the secrets of the great mages.\n\nThere's ultimately one secret, young woman. Do not compromise. If you believe something is true, you must require the Mundus to act in accordance with your will.
I have no desire to speak with you ever again. Be gone.
Now that you've given me back my life, I have much to think about.\n\nMaybe I'll take some time to rest before I put together another expedition. The Fighters Guild is in your debt, my friend.
War rages in Cyrodiil. We need people like you in the fight.
I said I don't want to discuss it.
Have you finally brought my Crystals back?
Good luck freeing our soldiers. I'll meet you and the soldiers at the barracks when you're finished.
Good luck freeing our soldiers. I'll stay here and wait for the detachment from Windhelm to arrive.
You have demonstrated valor today. Thank you. Please let Thane Mera know what happened and that everything is fine. \n\nI need to consider my brother's plans and how to best counter them.
I need to go. I need to get out of here. Those things are everywhere!\n\nPlease, my friend may still be alive. If you see her, you need to save her.
You must light those watchfires.
Well, I have to say, I'm rather shocked you actually completed the contract with all your bumbling. I don't know what the Night Mother sees in you, but mine is but to obey.
Don't touch me. You stink of life.
Get going. Holgunn is a veteran and a decorated officer. He'll know how to handle the Daggers.
Back already? Did you see King Jorunn?
Finally!  Someone of my stature being held like a dog… preposterous.
No! Keep him away from me!
The spirits of the tombs watch over you, my friend.

Well, well, will miracles never cease. By the panic going on around here, I suspect you were successful. Don't get cocky, get off this boat as they'll be looking for who was responsible. Meet me back at Sanctuary.
Digging away! Puffy little cheeks. What have you found?

And, there you have it, our little oaf may have what it takes to be a productive member of the Brotherhood. With enough hard work and dedication, you may be able to elevate yourself above dead weight. Hey, don't knock it, it's more than I expected!
You! You saved King Jorunn! You certainly know how to make an impression!
You've done it! The immortal story of the Silvenar and the Green Lady has been put right again!\n\nBut tell me, who corrupted Indraseth in the first place? Did you find out?
Our <<1>> is useless! It holds none of the magic it once had, and it's all <<2>>'s fault.\n\nWhat's going to happen to the Silvenar and the Green Lady if the story's changed?
Though I wish you could stay to drive out the remaining Houndsmen, I'm sure you're needed elsewhere.\n\nGood luck on your journey.
Welcome back, champion! What news do you bring from the peaks of lonely Skuldafn?
Any luck acquiring some of that Voljar mead?
Head for Skuldafn as soon as you can.
You have to get past the Worm Cult. Spinner Indinael needs help!
Someone found help. I feared it would soon be too late.
They've taken her inside, haven't they? Are we too late?
<The giant stares at you expectantly.>
So much death ….
You're not one of them. Please, you must help me!
Well? Is it done?
You're right. You've been right about everything. These horrific events must pay forward to a better future.\n\nIf not for my daughter, then for all the daughters and sons of others like me.
My head aches and everything looks blurry.
Why would anyone attack Cragwallow?
Everyone seems confused. Did you find out anything at all?
Save our soldiers, please. We must stop all this senseless death.
Are you another creature come to torment me? I've had enough of this maze!\n\nSpeak, apparition!
He's gone. I can feel it. His presence faded when you struck him down.\n\nBut so is dear Rala. I shouldn't have sent her. She wasn't ready.
Who do you think you are, taking my energy?\n\nYou think defeating me once will be enough to enslave my spirit? I'll see your bones sink into the tar first!

I hope Kireth knows what she's doing. Can we even read Dwemer maps? I guess we'll find out soon enough.\n\nHmm. If I shine a light through the orb, we might be able to see the maps on a nearby rock or wall! Pardon me, I just had the most amazing idea.

I hope Valeric didn't convince you to join our cause. Our battles never end well. True, his father's a bastard, but he's a strong bastard. Valeric can't beat him and those who help us usually die. \n\nBut enough depressing talk! How can Jaruk help you?

The Hound came, seeking solace for his broken heart. The others turned him away when they heard what he wanted. A memory. A chance.\n\nI couldn't. His tale tore at me, and I wove a bit of him into the story. But soon, he became the story.

Stormfist scouts hide in the trees. They ambush us when we least expect it. The giant can help you knock the cowards from their perches. Then kill them and collect any orders they carry.\n\nIf you find something, meet me at the camp to the west.
The giant near the natural wall, just behind me to the west, is ready to help you. Just give him a poke and he'll do the rest.\n\nWe'll launch our attack once you're inside and we hear the signal.
<<1>>'s fate is in your hands.
Thank you again for freeing me from those roots. I don't think I can ever look at vegetables the same way.
I'm lucky to be alive, I guess. But I don't feel lucky. Just sad.
I want to catch whoever's responsible for this.
You got the key? Open the cage!
Any luck finding my sword and shield?
You defeated him. I didn't think it was possible.

I've failed my duties as a spinner. The story comes first, above all emotion. Above all pity. I pitied the Hound, but it was a trap.\n\nAnd now, the Silvenar and the Green Lady will always have, and always should, join as one.

Here is where the Green Lady practiced archery. She practiced with her friend Unthor and her cousin Borodor, but she outstripped them from the very first day. It was then that her aunt, the Green Lady Finoriell, began to take notice of her potential.

This is going to be great! Raynor will sulk for a bit, but what else is new? Soon he'll be inventing something amazing to use in the next ruin! \n\nAnyway, thanks for your help. And feel free to use the lift over there when you're ready to leave.
My mouth is watering just thinking about a nice juicy bear steak
The altars are cleansed! My brothers and sisters will rest again!
You can get into the storeroom now.
I'm not sure we'll use this camp again. It will always bring sad memories of lost friends.

You have been a boon to us. We Keepers would have failed our people if it weren't for you.\n\nWe'll have to continue to refine Rilis' prison, but even the Daedra should have trouble breaking him free from four binding stones.
Shor's, Boulderfall. Hard fighting on familiar ground. I have family here in the Rift, did I ever mention? Just hope they're staying safe.
So much death….
Poor, misguided Valeric. I wonder what weakness drove him to this terrible end? I shall grieve for him. In my own way.
I miss my friends. I don't know if we will ever feel safe in Cragwallow again.
Has the friend of the Silvenar found the distasteful bits? Only then will the path be clear for our friend.
Something you need?
The Commander and I were able to fight our way back to the Tower with the wounded, and now we can regroup.
Speak with Jadvar, inside the cave. But don't get your hopes up.\n\nIf the Three Old Gods require your help, that's between you, them, and the Ternion elders.
You're still alive, congratulations. We may have a chance to repel these invaders after all.
Imiril will live. Go. We need you to handle Rilis.

By Aetherius, we barely managed to contain that lunatic!\n\nVoranil might be right. If these binding stones don't hold, we may need to take drastic action to defeat Rilis. Even if it means making a Daedric pact.

You come to support the slumbering king? When last I saw him, his skin was pale and his breathing shallow. His life force slowly drains away.\n\nIt would take a miracle, or a favor from the Three Old Gods, to save him now.
You seen them strange folk coming and going in the cave cross the way?

The pirates know something is up. Won't be long before they start looking for us.\n\nI think the captain's on the other side of the ship. If we can take her out, the rest will probably give up. I hope.
Y'ffre, Z'en, Auri-El, I beg for mercy! I repent!\n\nYou're not one of those Steel Shrikes, are you? Can you understand me?
The patrols led me in circles. It was a complete waste of time. Have you found anything?
Ready to leave when you are.
Yes! So that's how they do it. A portal. How elegant!\n\nI was hoping they turned into bugs, though. That would have been much more spectacular.
The promise of battle holds no fear for me.
Don't you have a dagger to bloody? Now move along.
Back already? How're the other stormwardens? I can hardly wait to give those Sea Vipers a good thrashing.
The Dreamwalker's work has begun.\n\nIf you wish to observe his progress, pray to our totem spirits. If the Three Old Gods hear you, they will show you images of the Dreamstride.
The family … <<1>>. They need help. Please!
Thank you for saving the Silvenar! I can't believe we all got out alive.\n\nAlmost all. If only Raen could have been with us ….
I thank you for doing what I could not. You saved the Silvenar and protected him from mercenaries and traitors.\n\nI will do my best to keep him alive on our road ahead.
Go, please. Help her. Save who you can!

My wife Jakild and I share the cabin farthest to the north. My brother Kerthor, we don't talk much. He keeps to himself in the cabin near the wayshrine. And my cousin Agnedir lives in the cabin near the springs.
Thank you for helping us. I don't know what I'm going to tell Agnedir's sister.
I should have done something as soon as I saw that helmet. Now my family has paid the price.
Bah, cultists! They are unworthy foes for Ysgramor's Companions. Thankfully, they are your vermin to kill.
Jakild and I are lucky you came along when you did, friend. Once the draugr settle down, we'll get back to work on Bonestrewn Crest.
Brilliantly done. Your waters flow swiftly now, touching many shores.
Please, let our people pass to Sovngarde. They … they must be in so much pain.
You need to get into the mine and shut down whatever they're doing in there. And I need to get out of here.
Vigrod finally set me loose on these fiends! We must not give one inch of ground!
You beat me. I lose to my cursed brother. Again. Perhaps he is the better ruler.\n\nRegardless, in front of my ancestors and my sister, I am undone. Do what you will with me.
Magicka binds my spirit to this place. I can't even see my captors.\n\nLocate the ambassadors who survived the attack. They can help you find me.
At the peak of Skuldafn, upon this holy dragonshrine, the Ebonheart Pact is sealed.\n\nGo, find my son. Let him know that my brother is dead and that we are victorious.
You don't look like one of those tree-cutter Sea Vipers. I'll assume that means you can be trusted.\n\nIs Mariel safe? Is help coming?
Azara was always more interested in exploration than research. She loved breaking into an undiscovered ruin and gathering all the objects she could cart away. I'm going to miss her.
Silvenar is to the north, past Valeguard. The preparations for the handfast are being made, so I can stay here for a little while and recover my strength.\n\nI'll be safe enough.
Charadin might still be alive. Oh, why did I run and leave him?
They were still in Mauloch's shrine when I ran away. I think <<1>> was stabbed by the shaman!\n\nHave mercy, Z'en! Don't let us be parted like this!
King Jorunn is up ahead. Hurry! He needs your help.
Move quickly, or you'll be trapped. The storm waits for neither man or mer.\n\nAn army waits outside. Be ready.
You're back! Did you save the rotmeth?
The traveler departed, ever in search of answers, on a path toward greatness.
I suspect I'll live, though perhaps with permanent, debilitating injuries, confining me to crutches for life.
It's so good to see my sister again. I promise I won't be long, but I need to speak to her. \n\nGo. I will meet you after and we'll stop my brother!

This fiend Thallik Wormfather—he cannot be allowed to hold Wuuthrad! We will get it back. The king's soldier, Captain Hrosta, searches for Wormfather even now. \n\nIn the meantime, you must stop the Daedra coming from Coldharbour.
Hakra said Wuuthrad shattered when you defeated Thallik Wormfather.\n\nAh, do not blame yourself. You fought with the courage of Ysgramor.
You're not as clever as you think, mortal. I will kill you!
Majorn waits for you in the nearby manor. He'll be pleased by your willingness to engage in a proper conversation.
You think you're so clever, mortal. Remember this: I will kill you!
Alchemy. It's not for the faint of heart.
That was exciting!
When this trooper is patched up, I'll move on to the next. You'd better get going.
My friend, we've come a long way from <<1>>. You've known me now in two lives. It's only right you're here as I begin a third when I bond with the Green Lady.\n\nNow, please, enjoy the celebration.
The chamber is right through there, past the barricade. Just be careful of the trolls.
Quiet! The Houndsmen are in the ravine below. I'm here to make certain they don't come up and attack the Silvenar's camp.
You found straw on that thing? We have a lot of farms around here. But … best place to find straw in Riften is at Guridda's stables. Head out the southeast gate, and go left. Can't miss it.
You found straw on that thing? We have a lot of farms around here. But … best place to find straw in Riften is at Guridda's stables. Head out the southeast gate, and go left. Can't miss it.

That thing was carrying pig iron? Strange. I wonder if that was old Gomund.\n\nThere's only one place in Riften to get pig iron - the Scorched Hammer smithy. It's near the center of town, west of the market square.
With your help, I know we can succeed.
Please, don't kill me! You don't understand!
Thank you. I could see no future for Silvenar as long as I was imprisoned there. But the Hound's bonds are broken, now!\n\nQuickly, you must continue your mission.
You can find Commander Yjarnn on the bridge in the middle of town.\n\nGood luck getting any information out of him, though. He won't tell his own troops anything, I doubt he'll tell a stranger.
We will be leaving shortly. Trust me, we will never forget how you saved us.\n\nMay our paths cross again someday.
Freedom exists, as do I, in any state. But my brethren, you must unlock their bonds, one way or another.
I don't understand. None of the refugees will answer my questions. It's like they're hiding something.
Please, apologize on my behalf about the delay. We've had a lot of trouble around here lately.
Please, we need help. Things are bad here.

Look for Thod over near the tents. Maybe someone in the camp knows where he disappeared to. The skeever's late and I'm tired.\n\nIf you find him, send him back here to report to me or Guard Hloenor over there.

All of Silvenar celebrates the handfast, and you should, too. I see your life's paths open before you … your tale does not end here, but continues further on.\n\nKnow that the Bosmer will always be grateful.
Get moving. Those boats won't spontaneously combust on their own.
I love a good party!
I can't believe this happened. Why would someone want to attack a company of royal workers?
What foul Maormer trick is this? Another attempt to loosen my tongue?
You're heading back to Nimalten? Luck on the road, my new friend.
Oh, if you're still looking for Thod, I wouldn't worry about it. He and the Commander headed for the barracks. Thod's getting an earful, I'm sure.\n\nI apologize if we wasted your time.
You do a great service for Rigurt. Rigurt knew he could count on you!
I'll get the mead to Windhelm as soon as possible.
You'll never find those clothes without me. I've hidden them too well.

Do whatever it takes to make the Argonians and Dark Elves happy. We need to get them back here before more people start dying.\n\nI won't allow the Prince's ignorance and ill-founded opinions to lead to the dissolution of the Pact.
Thank you again, friend. But good-bye now. Rigurt has much to do, much to do.
Please hurry. Arithiel saved us. We can't let the Worm Cult kill her.
Pay attention and speak to <<1>>.
I'll set the few troops I have to search out any remaining cultists. If any of those Worms remain behind, we'll find them.
I hope the Silvenar survives the handfast bonding. I know he has great spiritual reserves, but ….\n\nWell, anyway, I'm certain he can handle the celebrations!
I knew you were a hero! The spinners told us everything! \n\nThe celebration's being prepared!
That poor man! Such a terrible thing.
How dare you judge us? We do what we must to survive!
Sweet Tree-Minder. Sinmur is a monster that must be put down.
I'm sorry, I need to watch the road for Worm Cultists. <<1>> can answer your questions.\n\nAnd thank you for stopping. We don't get many visitors.
I'm sure the king will be well pleased to see you again.
His majesty will be pleased to see you again, I'm sure.
If you stay here, the Worm Cult will see us. Go chat with the chieftain Suhlak if you're looking for conversation.\n\nDo me a favor? When you leave, don't step on any twigs.
Well met, friend. Do you bring news?
They want me dead? Let them come. I welcome another chance to prove myself. Fjora bends knee to no man!
Well. This can't possibly go wrong, can it?
Tell Hallfrida not to worry. We'll be back on the walls in a few minutes. Go on, now. I've got to organize this mob.
You're supposed to be in the ….\n\nWait, who're you?
Thanks for helping us. Fildgor's lackeys won't catch us off-guard again.
Be quiet. I don't want them to notice us.
Ah, the murderer's accomplice. I think I'll kill you first.
My wife Asgi is in the mine. I wish I could go help her.

I'm getting tired of being treated like second-class citizens.\n\nThe Nords have turned their backs on my people more times than I can count. It would serve them right if we refuse our aid when they call upon it.

When you get inside the courtyard, you're going to need to find a key to get into the Jarl's manor.\n\nDon't worry about me. I'll catch up with you soon enough. Just be careful in there, all right? Dhalen is dangerous.
I don't mind hard work, but I hate when someone holds a knife to my sister's throat.
Sorry if I was rude. I'm just trying to protect myself and my husband.
The bad Nords are gone now and Hjolard is very happy!
I spoke to my wife. She's a spitfire, let me tell you. She said hello, gave me a hug, and went right back to work.
If Fildgor sends more troops, we'll be ready for them.
Did you hear that? I think the Worm Cult are crawling around on the roof!
We'll do what we must, with no help from you. Dog of the Jarls!
You still here? Are you bothering Hallfrida? What do the Jarls want with my granddaughter?
Oh! Good to see you. I have sad news: Golun is dead. We heard the sounds of a struggle. My soldiers and I arrived too late.
There will be more murders before this is done. I can't put my finger on it, I don't know how I know, but I do. And I grow restless sitting here, unable to act.
I only received my promotion a few weeks ago. First time commanding in the field, yeah? Can't believe it kicked off with … this.
Thanks to you, the hengekeeper made it through. But I thought I'd be able to speak to the matrons if they woke ….\n\nIs the same force preventing me from rooting in Treehenge thwarting me now?

The High Kinlord's power has grown terrifying.\n\nI don't know that we can stop him, though we must. Tamriel is in grave danger if Rilis reaches the surface. Even if we catch him, we'll need to devise a stronger prison than the last one ….
Head south from here. Once you run out of good, dry land go a bit further and you'll hit Stormhold.\n\nLocate Vicecanon Hrondar there; he'll direct you.
You're going to the bandits to get back my silk? So Turil did hire them! I knew it, I knew it!
My silk. Did you find my silk?
I am so relieved. Holguss is fine. He came out, wolfed down some stew and went back to work.
I never saw the Orcthane's followers move so fast! They ran out of here, crying like little babies!
I knew those big goons were nothing but cowards! Now we can get back to work. And for real, this time.
I need help. Things haven't been normal for a long time.
We won't be caught off guard again. We'll protect the King.
Jorunn can't die. The Pact won't hold together without him. May the Tribunal help us all.
There is sorrow here today, but the Companions will recover. And I will remember all of it.
I'll get everyone together and head back in a group. We'll be right behind you.
I'll explain later. We must wake the matrons as soon as possible.
Thanks to your actions here and at Cradlecrush, we should have things back in order very soon.
Greetings, stranger. It looks like you have something for me.
Danus may seem paranoid, even irrational at times, but we owe him our lives.
Please find my friends. I keep thinking about all the awful things that might have happened to them.
I just want to sleep for several days after this ordeal. I think <<1>> wants to talk to you though.
The door to the storage area is inside the shed. Sorry. Careful not to burn your hands on the door.\n\nWe'll try to get the flames out while you're in there.
When you poked your head into that tent, I thought I was going mad. What are the odds we'd meet again here, of all places?\n\nIn case I haven't said it enough already: thank you.
When I saw you on the road, I said to myself "Raynor, your friend is here to save the day again." And you did!
My friend. I'm glad to see you again. We could have used you … wait, those papers. You have some of the delver's notes!
What? Must be a delusion. Nobody down here. I'm not dead yet, Shor!
Strangers. Intruders. All the same. You distract us from our duties.\n\nBegone, before the ritual is disturbed further!
I see no malice within you. Is there compassion in its place, I wonder?\n\nDo you seek to purge the poison within the henge?
No time for pilgrims! We must attend to the departed Green Lady.
What's going on? I feel so strange ….
Will you come to Boulderfall's aid?
Please, my liege-lord. Make haste for Honrich Tower. Whatever darkness grows there must be stopped.
Please hurry. My shipmates may not survive interrogation.
I hear you're helping Danus secure the camp. Many thanks.

We're in your debt. If you ever have need of blades, come speak to me. I guess I should find some more flowery, Thane-like speech, but that's not how grandfather raised me. Speak plain and honest, he said.
The first thing we do is ensure the dead have been given the Rites of Arkay. We'll have to send to Riften for a priest. I'm not going to let another damned necromancer play around here.

We'll hunt Thorulf. You live with a man for a decade, he gives up some secrets. I know places to look for him.\n\nIf we find him, I'll contact you. I can't think of a better mate to have at my side for that fight.
I was told I might find you here. I have an urgent message for you from <<1>>.
Please, hurry. Being trapped here is nothing like resting in the mires of Ouze.
Learn what you can from Sinmur's song. Just know, the skalds may not recognize you for who you are. Some of the dreamers aren't as aware as I.
Get outside and help Sjarakki. I'll keep an eye on Thorulf.
I'm going back to the fishing village. The other survivors need my help, and I must make amends for the acts of my brother.
This seed existed before the Green Pact, before the Bosmer learned to calm their forms. Before the Green Lady and the Silvenar.\n\nIt will heal <<1>>. Take it to her before she dissipates.
The Circle of Iron links me to this world. As long as it exists, I can torment you stupid mortals!
She's waiting for you at the Riften Guildhall in The Rift. Good luck, comrade.

Why are you bothering me? And how did you get in here?\n\nMy guards have apparently gotten lax in their duties again.
Ha! Once the Stormfists knew we had weapons and weren't going to back down, they remembered they had an important engagement somewhere else.
Silly old woman. Don't think I know my tales. Just wait, I'll be the greatest bard the holds have ever seen!
Nimalten reminds me of Bleakrock. All these good people, oblivious to danger. If only we could have protected my daughter.\n\nHave you learned anything?
Get out of here, I'm busy.

We must defeat <<1>> and the Worm Cult once and for all. Are you ready?

Speak to <<1>>. We haven't much time.
You performed a great service for the dead. Thank you.\n\nI look forward to hearing your tales in the halls of Sovngarde one day.

Your heroics today have even succeeded in impressing me, and that is no small thing.\n\nThallik Wormfather and the ghost giant Sinmur are both dead. Mark my words—this will be what King Jorunn's reign will be remembered for.

Go. Save the King. We'll track Fildgor down and wait for you to return.

I hope Telenger has noted my bravery here. Something good must come of this!

You returned! And you have them! Even after all these years, they're still beautiful. Their lovely smiles. The energy flowing through them.\n\nIt's like we were never apart.
We'll recover from all this. At least I hope we will.
The next time our ocean-faring cousins pay us a visit, we won't be unprepared. Many thanks for all your help.
Keep an eye out. Something big's about to happen on Auridon…
The Maormer will think twice before threatening Vulkhel Guard again!
Your look is grim, friend. So they had been turned?
Well, that could have gone better. Maybe it's all that royal "we" nonsense. \n\n"We call upon our ancestors." It's all rather condescending, isn't it?
I'll get these to the Artificer. I'm certain he'll know what to do. The dead of Ezduiin will finally know rest.

Dajaheel's at the main camp, just outside the treeline. She'll get you set.

Stars keep you. I think Cannie will be all right.

The High King has been asking about you. About time, my friend.
Aargh!
My friend, I'm glad you're here. My confrontation nears. Your presence bolsters my courage and gives me hope.

Blood for the Pact! If we had an army of folk like you, the Daggers wouldn't have dared to attack Stonefalls.
Defend me!
To think, all of our research … ruined! It's all those savage cultists' fault!
Wasteful practice. Abhorrent! Oh, pardon. I did not see you arrive.\n\nAre you another pilgrim to Treehenge? Be wary of the cultists. There is no telling when they may strike.
Whose body was this? The flesh reeks. You placed me in one of those Cultists, damn you!
The Silvenar needs help if we're ever going to get to this wedding.

What are you still doing here? Go!

Trinimac guide you.

May Trinimac guide your hand and our blades be raised in battle again.
Good working with you! Hope we meet again sometime less, you know, horrible.
Enjoy the party, mortal.

Ah, well. I suppose you did what you thought was best.
This stuff stinks. But hey, I guess it beats being sick!
I need to work up my nerve to use that stuff. Such a smell!\n\nAre you still here?
I suppose I should be grateful I have the salve. Hendil's son succumbed so quickly. \n\nStars damn this plague.
I knew death would be Estre's fate.
High Kinlady Estre is defeated. Thrice-blessed are we. \n\nWe of the Guild may return to more scholarly matters.
It'll be good to see Firsthold return to normal.
I heard the Queen and the High Kinlord are safe! All thanks to you.
Search the corpses. Personal items. Come back to me.
Vivec's eyes, what's going on in there?

Given all that's happened in Riften, I'll have to mourn my brother later. I appreciate you bringing me the news though.
You were right, it's so much warmer out here. The cold in there. Terrible!
Thank you for telling me of Flavia's death. Knowing is better than always wondering and hoping.
You confirmed my worst fears. I can't thank you for it, but I hope no one ever brings you such unwelcome news.
We barely made it up here before the plague started taking the Maulborn.
Five Maulborn fell to my blade. That ought to help a bit.
All those crates, all those vials of plague …. \n\nMournhold wouldn't have stood a chance.
Oh, no. Allene. My girl. My little girl. \n\nGet away from her! Haven't you done enough?
You're always welcome in Firsthold, my new friend.

Our people owe you a debt of gratitude. With High Kinlady Estre defeated, Queen Ayrenn and High Kinlord Rilis may continue to unite the Aldmeri Dominion.
High Kinlady Estre may be defeated, but there are still those who would oppose the Dominion. The Veiled Heritance is proof of that. High Kinlord Rilis and I still have our work cut out for us here.
Speak to Aelm if you think you can handle a drink. Or ten!
I knew you couldn't hold your drink. But I didn't think it would be so entertaining to watch!
It's good to be back among civilization. Of course, the place certainly needs some tidying up.
Good luck! You'll need it to pass the tests.
You're new, right? Go on in. Just don't let them touch you.
Damned alchemists. Probably inhaled too many fumes.
What happened to me? What was that thing?
Welcome back! Did you miss me? \n\nThere's nothing like a rousing ballad when you're drinking. And when my favorite people buy my drinks, I sing for them!
Many need to mend, I'm happy to see help continues to arrive.
It's good to be back. Perhaps business will pick up after the siege. You never know when a good sword may come in handy.
I hope it won't take long for things to reach a feeling of normalcy again. I thank Auri-El High Kinlord Rilis' life was spared. He'll bring Firsthold back to her former glory.
I knew Estre's life was forfeit the moment she set foot in this city. A true Kinlady should know her place in this world. Consorting with Daedric Princes, hah! It's the surest way to Oblivion.
Feeling much better after the Queen's healers took a look at me. I've even got the shop up and running again!
Damn Auri-El! How could he allow something like this to happen to me?
This one is happy he is alive. But will Firsthold ever be the same? \n\nBura's wares are still here, but where have his customers gone?
Thanks to you, High Kinlord Rilis was saved. It shouldn't be long to get Firsthold back to its former glory.
I suppose I am thankful that Estre is dead. Although I don't agree with the Queen's motives, I'm decidedly more against the worship of Daedric Princes.
Talk to Thane Vofknir.
It was the right thing to do.
Perhaps business will pick up again.
Go away! It's all mine. Sanessalmo said so.\n\nEh. Are you using that weapon? I bet I could get a fair price for it.
We have a lot of work to do to get the town back in shape.
Please, go away. I'm just trying to protect my son.
<He still lives. Nelulin seems to be unconscious.>
Best get on with your business here before Thorulf takes notice, friend.
He left! He just up and left, without a word. That lying, cheating, no good milk-drinker!\n\nIt'll be time for a tavern tour when this is over. He'll sing a higher note if I find him again.
Oh, thank you for saving us.
You have done the Trial. Brave of you.
Quickly! Open the cages before the guards spot you.
I see you have the key. Excellent work. Now free me, please.
Clever work! Now unlock my cage before the cultists spot you.
Are you still here? Are there no more Worm Cultists to kill? Pursue these villains and perhaps we will meet again!
Thank you again.
This is it—let's wipe them out!
If the Farseer welcomes you, then so must I.
Fjora's apparently a dynamo on the battlefield. I've heard stories you wouldn't believe.
I'm much happier working and doing something rather than watching the door at the inn.
I work when I'm happy, and I'm very happy!
My brother Nilus improves. He'll be up and around in no time. Thanks for your help.

Selfora is safe now, and I feel so much better.
I can't hear the ghosts anymore. Did you have something to do with that?
