I don't know why Sarisa involved you in our affairs. As you can see, Rothalens need no help from strangers!
Ignore my mother's grumbling. I know you played some part in our good fortune. My sister won't talk about it, but you have my gratitude at least.
Clever. Very clever. Poor woman. Even taken beyond these walls, no accountant is ever freed from her greed.\n\nI am <<1>>. Welcome to my laboratory.
Ah, what news? Did that scuttlefish bite?
I can't talk right now. Too much to do. Have to get out of this place as soon as I can.
Go away, stranger. You have no business being here.
<<1>> must answer for his crimes.
I'm sick of your insinuations. If you don't want to help, you can just leave!
You got that bastard? Good. At least we managed to protect Raerana.
That bastard! Only thinking of his own blood. Hope the crows have fun with that one.
I almost feel sorry for that alchemist guy. To have that happen to your son. Can't even think about it.
Once again, you have aided my people.
Get away from me! This damned plague probably came from those flea-ridden mud huts of yours.
You'll be disappointed if you've come to visit Falinesti. The Walking City is still missing and something's amiss in the valley.\n\nTake my advice and leave while you can.
What are you doing here? Who are you?
The Site is cursed! I see no profit here, only blood.
Harnald's supposed to send a scout. I hope he hasn't forgotten.
The trouble in the Ragged Hills can't be over yet. <<1>> would have returned.\n\nPlease help her. Mother will kill me if anything happens to her!
Let's clean these guys out!
Harnald is sending a scout here. She knows where the ritual is taking place.
We've heard of the tragedy on the farm. Poor Raerana. She's with family now though. We'll see her through this.

This can't be! I can't sense his presence at all! Too many variables to track … my husband, all of Falinesti. They're so close! So close!\n\nThe Walking City must still be trapped in Oblivion! We have to try again!
Ah, my errand-runner. So good to see you again.
Move along.
Keep moving.
Get moving, please.
Keep moving.
Do not worry about me. Save the ones in the mine.
Hmph. Well done, I suppose.
First Forge! We made it.
Good work! We'll make it through this, I know it.
I'm still in pain, but knowing Daedra won't swarm over us soothes me.\n\nThe Walking City never went to Oblivion! Everyone knows it's on Masser until it is time to return.
Thank you for bringing the news, unhappy as it was. Good day to you.
That is it. We are getting out of this town.
An ill wind blows from Taarengrav. I fear the Worm Cult threatens there as well.
These tunnels will eventually take us to the Towers of Eyes. That's where we'll find the Sentinels.
I wish you the strength of Mara's heart and the protection of Auri-El's scales. Good luck, my friend.
It's a relief not to have to dodge flying boulders anymore.
Did you find anything?
She's sure to be near the manor house at this point. She'll want to be as close to the Queen as she can.
Earn this.
Good work.
Razum-dar trusts you. Do the same for him, and he will not let you down.
I hope you were able to speak to the Canonreeve.
I couldn't help but overhear you speaking with Iroda. You're not the first hopeful to come down the river.\n\nPerhaps I know the answer. Perhaps I would share it with you?
You still here, hero? Go on in.
We're a bit busy here, traveler. If you could just—
I will see you in Skywatch.
The savior of <<1>> returns. Welcome, my friend.
I knew the Maulborn were up to no good. I just knew it.
Does this mean there won't be a cure?
Gold for a poor Dark Elf down on his luck? I need to hire a cart to take my sick mother to Mournhold.
Maulborn bastards! No one should play with our hopes and fears like that.
To think, I was ready to join up with these Maulborn fanatics! They turned my husband into a plague husk and tried to do the same to all of us.
Damn the Maormer! And unreliable crews, on every dock in Tamriel.
Word of Degail and the Maormer reached Anala's ears. This one is glad you found her, but sad the rumors to prove true.
I'm a bit thankful to the Maormer. We won't be out of port for a while. \n\nCan't imagine finding my sea legs in my current condition.
They lied to us. There is no cure. Stay back before I give you the plague.
This damn plague will kill us all.
Have you heard? The plague has spread to Narsis. They're dying in the streets, and the Tribunal can't help them.
I didn't expect you had the muster to just get our defector back. Guess I pegged you wrong.
May Daedric cults always find roads to you. So that I don't have to deal with them.
I heard you found Degail! Lucky girl to have survived. Maormer aren't usually the type to take captives.
Thank you for all you've done. These ancient relics embody all that the Companions stand for.
You back? Let me guess—you can't find Varnedo, either?
Is there anything else this one can convey?
I'm expecting a scout any minute now. He'll help you reach the top and stop the ritual.
Let's keep moving.
Yes, yes. I'm still open. At least as long as I have inventory.
Can I help you with anything?
Out of the way! Can't you see the fire?
So the Maormer are really here. Anala was right. I don't think I'm going to get a good night's sleep again for some time.
I could use someone like you in my organization. Maybe we'll run into each other again.
Sorry, we're a little busy here. Can this wait?
Some rotten little thief stole from my armory when I wasn't looking. You wouldn't know anything about that, would you?
I'm sorry. I'm much too busy to chat right now.
Today would have been a dark one without you.\n\nDo me a favor and don't be so vocal about it, yes? You could cost me my job.
You certainly proved to be Fighters Guild material.
You turned the tide for us, stranger. The Spider Cult failed only thanks to you.
I will always remember your kindness, traveler. The Divines thank you, too!
I am grateful to you for returning my Lady's Aegis.
For returning what was stolen, you have my thanks.
I heard they found my father. And he was safe!\n\nIf you had any part to do with it, I thank you.

Climb the steps to the Throat of the World. There may be Frostheart Blossoms hidden in the snow, but I am not hopeful. It is rare even when you know where to look.

Oh, you're back. I was just leaving. To, um, Valenwood. Yeah.\n\nWell, bye!
Take care in Ivarstead, friend. You're one of the smart ones.
Greetings! I've traveled all of Tamriel to bring the finest armor to the people of Riften. Let me know if I can help fill your protection needs.
Now, don't go around blabbing about my work. Off you go! Farewell!
I'm very busy, as you can see. Did you need something?
Oh, thank you. Because of you, we are alive and rebuilding. The Veiled Heritance will fail as long as people like you are around.
Oh, I am so doomed.
Are you sure you're in the right place?
My family is safe because of you. Thank you.
<The statue is almost flawless, a perfect representation of a living person.>
Done already? You get those bugs?
Damn the Mages Guild. You can do your own dirty work from now on.
Don't worry. Between the Eyes and the Marines, the Daggers won't hold North Beacon for long.
I told you all I know. Haven't seen Varnedo in days, so leave me alone.
Is it done? Do you have it?
You are foolish to dabble in such dark matters, mortal.
Ten cheers for King Jorunn! Ten drinks for Jofarr!
Fly true and strike hard, King's Arrow.
Thanks for getting us out of those crypts. I think I'll do my drinking right here from now on. It's sufficiently Draugr-free.
Two minutes. That's how long we were out of the crypts before those two drunken idiots ran off again. To Oblivion with them. I'm done playing goat-herd!
<Scorch marks indicate that Solvar was burned to death.>
Giruss doesn't like uninvited guests, so you better have a good reason to bother him.
Very impressive. Very impressive indeed. Now that I know your face, I'll be sure to watch for future acts of selfless bravery.
I suppose congratulations are in order.
You've saved the Queen! What else can I say? Well done. Very well done.
Something catch your eye? Something hard to find? Something exotic?

Fine. I get it. You saved some drunks and got the dead to settle down. You're a big hero. Blah blah blah. \n\nNow, will you please leave? The only reason I took this job is because I can't stand the living.
I need healing. Thank you for everything. I'll see you in Shor's Stone.
I hope the Stars—and the Queen—can forgive me. I don't know if I ever will.
I may not see him soon, but I will someday. Thank you.
Please talk some sense into my father. Haven't I made up for my crimes?
I can feel the change burning under my skin. How can it happen so fast?\n\nSacred Y'ffre, forgive us all!
Stay back … I've been bitten. I won't have another fall for my mistakes.
There's no rule against talking to people. At least not yet. And they're not bound by the same orders as I am.\n\nMaybe they can convince you to move on.
I have no more to give you.
Welcome to Skywatch. Your message arrived ahead of you and they're expecting you up at the manse.
I hope you were able to get the warning out.
Do not worry, Razum-dar will be on his way soon. He may even beat you there!\n\nHe just has to change clothes first.
Thanks for coming to visit. I'll never be the same, but I have to confess, I feel like I see more without sight than I did with it.
Poor thing. Just terrible what's happened to her. After what we've been through, I don't feel right leaving her side, not sure if I ever will.
Tell the Baelborne to leave.\n\nDon't make me regret showing you what happened. Please, you must do the right thing.
You've heard Tanion's lies, fancy agent. You've seen what they teach us. Now you need to see what happens after we leave those torture pits.
Sorry, but I'm very busy. I'm going to have to ask you to leave.
Get going, recruit. Don't fail me.
I seem to have found my way into the waiting arms of the Bloodthorn cult again.
Gorak's a worthy addition to the Lion Guard. I have a special assignment in mind that's perfect for him.
Bakkhara thanks you again.
Lucky you came along when you did. I'm not sure I've got the stomach to condemn one of my own men. Sometimes you need a stranger's detachment to get a job done.
You did good. I think you made the right call.
I thought they'd kill us, for sure. Good to be among friends again!
Tell Captain Vistra what happened out there. She doesn't believe me!
I don't know what we would have done if you hadn't come along. \n\nMy wife is pregnant. I'm going to ask her to name the child in your honor.
This one wishes you good luck on Baham's errand.
Good job.
Please don't kill me!
Go on now. Back to the docks with you.\n\nThere's nothing here for the likes of you.
Enjoy your apples. Thanks for eating them.
Go. There are more recruits running the trial. Need to keep watch for them.
<<1>> will be rebuilt, just wait and see. Those vipers won't drive us from this place.
Hey, aren't you the one who chased down the Dominion? Me, I could never go in those ruins. Too many cobwebs.
The Argonians around here started going wild all of a sudden. Something about a hatching.\n\nI've never seen an Argonian egg. Strange, huh?
Heard the Vicecanons had a traitor in their ranks. Goes to show you! It ain't just us rats that like a pretty coin.
One-Eye says you did her a good turn. Not many people she'd admit that about. Impressive.
You're not a Marine, are you? Who are you?
My friends are caged inside the Bloody Witch, Helane's ship. I'm not going anywhere near there!
Go speak with Varustante. She proctors the test of endurance—the trial of the body.
You've been busy, haven't you?
Ilara can't go to the cave! Not again!
Get gone. Don't want to keep the council waiting.
Make way, please. Whinnie and I are eager to be gone.
I'm sorry I shouted at you. Let's just get out of here. The portal should be right where you left it.
My husband stood up to these brutes … and now he's slaving away in the mines.\n\nAll I can do is hope this gets resolved soon and try to keep the Red Rooks from trashing our inn.
I'm old. Give me a moment, kid.
Just … just a minute and I'll be ready … for another round.
<The Speaking Stone lies dormant.>
I can see the main road turning down the way, and it's not as busy as it once was. I'm sure the Houndsmen are to blame.
We heard you were the one who sent the Bloodthorn our way. Damn good work! We'll count this one as a victory when we return to Camlorn.\n\nYou're a hero.
Good luck. You should find my brother Bernard by the bridge to Deleyn's Mill.
Nothing but trouble since we came ashore, I tell you. Nothing but trouble.
I was determined to stop the Red Rooks from destroying Crosswych.
Good luck. May Baan Dar guide you.
Greetings, citizen.
Hello, what's this? Out for a stroll, then? Lovely day for it.
I can't believe that <<1>> was an impostor. He always seemed like a man of decency.
So this <<1>> wanted to take control of an egg …. to control the memory of the Hist … to control the Argonians? He did know the Dunmer did the same thing with just swords, right?
I've heard the Bosmer eat their enemies. Which I guess makes sense, given how disgusting their friends are.
One of the vicecanons was skulking around the Ayleid ruins. Shifty northerner. Probably looking for something to loot. Or drink.
May the hand of Auri-El be always on your shoulder. Guide us through life and protect us from harm.
Go to the village.\n\nI thought I'd seen everything as a guard, but Houndsmen and werewolves are more than I'd bargained for.
Head up to the village, please.\n\nWhat with all the werewolves and <<1>> taken … we're a bit overwhelmed.
Thank Auri-El the Captain's a forgiving woman.
It's over? The nightmare, the spirits?
I'd much rather speak to you in person. I just don't trust these magical projections. Any number of Daedra could be watching.
I heard about Firsthold. I pray the people there are doing all right.
This is so humiliating.
<No one responds.>
Good luck in there. \n\nLike I said, Captain Landare will be able to tell you more. She'll be manning the cordon at the edge of town.
Thank you so much. I could never have done that by myself. Raynor's sleeping right now, but when he wakes up, I'm going to tell him how great his device worked.
You're not one of the regulars here at the Flagon.
<He stares icily at you.>

Be wary, vestige. Our very plane of existence is in peril. The threat of Molag Bal looms across all Tamriel, and chaos spreads in its shadow. \n\nDanger roams the land and will assume many forms. Do not let it catch you off-guard.
That descendant of mine headed to the summit, straight into Drodda's murderous arms. I'm sure he's fine—the Direfrosts are an able-bodied lot.\n\nBut he may need a little help.

You make a mockery of my game, mortal. By all calculations, the mages should be dead by now. But no. They still live.\n\nI must say, however, that my game hasn't been this exciting in a long time. So I grant you the ultimate boon. The right to choose!
A new face! That's a rare occurrence. Welcome to the Everfull Flagon, friend!
Leave me be, stranger. I'm a very busy man.
Well. This is going to set back the order for Firsthold. The High Kinsmen will not be happy.\n\nMaybe I can supplement the order with some product from Greenwater.
I. I didn't know they were with the Heritance! \n\nI support the Queen. Some of my best friends are Khajiit!
Have you been up by Ezduiin? I was working with that Telenger fellow as one of his students. \n\nI had to leave. That mage is unstable, if you ask me. Not worth the trouble.
Are you a marine? You know you have to tell me if you're an official.
Shouldn't you be in the forge, cat? I'm surprised they let you out. It's not break time. \n\nOh. You don't work here, do you? Well, you should. Only thing your kind's good for.
First Silsailen, now here! Is anyplace in Auridon safe?
Get out of town while you can. I am.
I've only been here a week. Had to leave Phaer, leave everything behind. A plague swept through, you know?\n\nFigure I'll make some money, send it home to Hendil. Maybe he can buy supplies.
Bad enough I'm stuck on this garden of an island. But working alongside Khajiit? \n\nTerrible. Mangy, rotten creatures. I bet their meat tastes as bad as they smell.
Work is work, I say. There isn't much of it in Deepwoods. Just hoping I can save some money to send back home to my family.
I just finished a stint at the College of Aldmeri Propriety. Awful place, but I got through it. \n\nFigured I'd see the rest of the island before I go back to Elden Root.
So much death. But perhaps, now, Mathiisen will see a brighter day.
Zurka thinks she will be leaving soon. Auridon has proven a bit too … exciting for the likes of her.
Banished to Oblivion and the man still won't acknowledge me.\n\nWho are you?

We're off to search the second wreck. I'd be obliged if you could follow Jalan's wake and see what's keeping him. Bring him along to the other wreck, so's I can dress him down for being a lazy lackwit. \n\nIf he ain't dead, that is.
What you got there, stranger?
Curse the Daedra. Damn them to drown in the Font of Harmony.
The Eight watch over my poor father.
That Admiral spook, Sithis sink him, seems to control all the skeletons.
Go on, mate. \n\nIf things go well, I hope to help you when you face the Admiral.
<This Altmer is dead. He was badly beaten before his death.>
I pray that this curse will soon be lifted.
Do you have it?
Good choice, mate, giving me the crown. \n\nNow I think I'd best be introducing me crew to their new captain.
My cousin wrote to me about what happened at the Serk. You did a good thing there.
Fish, fish, fish. Little fish in the basket, little fish in the stew. Little fish in the cookpot, I love you.
So many little treasures. A shell, a coin, an amulet. Akkuz finds them all.
Mother says working with your hands is for Bosmer. Stuff that. Anything worth doing is worth doing yourself.
Trade feeds Vulkhel Guard like rain feeds a tree. There's almost as many crates here as there are raindrops in a storm.
Rough ride coming in. Mathad will spend this evening thanking Jode and Jone. They allowed us this passage.
Last time I ride that kind of storm. Damnit, Y'ffre. Why do you have to go and be like that?
Yes? Hmm. I don't recognize you. \n\nPlease go. My wines are available only by appointment.
Welcome to Vulkhel Guard. What can this one procure for you?
I think I saw a ship on the horizon. Didn't catch the flag. But I'd swear the colors were Maormer. \n\nBut they couldn't. Nah.
Welcome back, my friend. Did you find it? Was I right? Was the source of power I sensed one of the fabled Lights of Meridia?
Our house destroyed, our village in ruins. At least I still have my Pirtar.
What a mess. What a mess! I can't imagine what my mother will say when she hears about this.
I'm not sure how, but you did it. Thank you.
It's a good thing you came along when you did. Just when I thought things couldn't get any worse. But you managed to pull us through.
So much water here. So different than this one's homeland. It is beautiful, yes? But also so. Wet.
Sorry, have to have the place looking right. <<1>> wants everything just so for the Queen's visit.
Looking to buy, sell, and trade? You've come to the right place. What do you have in your pack there?
We just got in a shipment of steins from the Woodhearth. Primitive art is so in fashion these days.
You call that bag adequate? I don't call that adequate. Here, let me sell you something before we both get embarrassed.
Was it Glow Dust and Snowberries? Or Glow Dust and Hanging Moss? Oh, apologies. What can I get you?
I sense life. Magicka. Ah, a customer. The best kind of life! What do you need?
So much to do. Please, speak with the Mistress if you're looking to sell.
The Stars welcome you, traveler. Take a moment to look over my arms. I assure you—they are as deadly as they are beautiful.
You are needing a good meal, yes? Everything I serve is sugar-sweet and ready to eat!
I don't recall seeing you around here before. Hmph. You hardly look like club material. Best begone, commoner scum. We're dangerous men!
Mara's Heart, your gear has seen wear. Perhaps a new helm?
I heard Almion was coming to check on me when he died. This is all my fault.
So many of the Marines made it back. Thanks to you.
You look familiar. Were we flirting just a little while ago?
Hail, hero! The King recovers after the attempt on his life. He will see no visitors.
Please, go. I … I want to be alone with the dead right now.
You ever try making a bow out of bones and rocks? Trust me—it's about as fun as it sounds. Thank Auri-El someone's out there gathering lumber.
We are all in your debt, friend. The King needs to rest right now.
I brew fragrant elixirs and delicate blends. What can I get you?
You're going into battle wearing that? Hmph. I know we can do better.
I used to sing for thanes and kings. I danced around and had many fine things.\n\nHow about that! I made a rhyme. I've still got it!
Tell me you're here to buy. Stars know we've got the goods.
If you're working in cloth or leather, I'm your man. What can I get you?
You're here to work metal, yeah? Check my wares before you get your hands dirty. You'll find something worth buying, I guarantee it.
Go with the Tribunal's blessing, in the name of the Lord, Mother, and Wizard.
I knew you would make the right decision. I just hope the three of us are equal to the task that's still ahead of us.
What a cruel game we were forced to play! This one is just grateful that we all survived.
Can't talk. Have to watch the Defender's mutt. Last time I make jokes about a cat owning a dog.
This one tends the grounds. Tries to ignore what the Altmer say. Their words hurt Razigad, like lashes of a whip.
What'll you have?
Hey there! I'll—I'll have another.
What could you possibly want?
Stars, make it quick. I'm waiting for someone.
Don't … don't I know you?
Yes, lowborn? What can I do for you?

If they make you choose a side, you should consider the tree. Er, Pesty. Estre? Yes, that's it.\n\nShe keeps her troops happy, no matter what. A strong morale will win this battle. That, and I feel no pain. Now that's an advantage! Drink!
Find the broken mask I seek, or your outlook is bleak.\n\nRemember my clues, for they'll lead you true without lies or ruse.
I said go away and let me read my book in peace.
No harm shall come to Juline while she is sworn to me.
What is that? Is it the end of the world? Arkay's beard!
So. How did it go?
Ah, the brave hero who broke the spell that bound us! So good to see you again, my friend.
The Mages, they are kind to this one. Even say one day Taranza could become Mage. If she rakes hard enough.
Look at this, dear! The Temple to the gods in Vulkhel Guard. One of the most beautiful spots in all of lovely Auridon. And Xarxes himself seems to be keeping the image from my mind.
Think of the power I could give you if you were to side with me.\n\nOr you could choose another and feel the wrath of the very power of which I speak.
What … what happened? Ugh, my head.
Go, go!\n\nDo what you need to so you can make your decision. There's killing to be done still and the Shadow Court can only amuse us for so long.
What? Like Jilarga doesn't have enough to do everyday. No time for stupid questions.
A muffled voice cries out: \n\n"It's locked and I'm tied up. Please, get the key from my father."
Where's Marq? Did he listen to you?
We came to Velyn Harbor for aid after the Crimson Raiders destroyed my village. It doesn't look like the town is in a much better position than we were. I hate irony.
The cursed shard has been destroyed. Currents of happiness and grief flow through the river this day.
Hhmph. No lavender. Last time I trust that Greenvine liar. Sorry. What can I get you?
The best goods, straight to you from Grahtwood. Hand-hewn by craftsmen at one with the Green.
Who? Go away.
Please forgive me for saying so, but your raiment is ever so … mundane. Why not explore some enchantments?
Stars guide you, traveler. Robes for the discerning spellcaster, right here. With the Brothers in Arms.
Hah! Best armor in Auridon, from the Brothers in Arms. Get it fresh from the forge!
Brothers in Arms armor. You need new leathers? I'm your man.
Why are you so interested in the casks of mead? You should leave them alone.
What? Is it the height? Or that I'm a woman? Either way, stop staring and tell me what you need.
You remind Tuzil of his son's cub. So full of life. This old cat's just good for asking things like 'What can he get you?'
These records are in complete disarray. It's enough to drive a Proctor insane.\n\nUntil the Dominion sends more troops, I'll be here attempting to restore a basic semblance of order.
Brews are always better with meat! But I know, I know. It's an acquired taste.
It's not a party until someone gets eaten! Ha! I'm just yanking your vines. Probably.\n\nSo. Who's hungry?
Welcome. Shall I attend to your account?
And fair day to you. Your account?
This is my beach. Mine! All the treasure here belongs to me!
Diamonds? Rubies? Ziss on them! Nothing but polished rocks. My soul gems are the only stones you'll ever need.
We all have burdens to carry. Why not take on a little bit more, friend?
This one sells the best blades in Tamriel! No jokes, no substitutions, no refunds, just high quality steel. At an affordable price!
Please. No more. I can't take any more ….
Ugh, these sweaty workers. Always getting damp on my chairs.\n\nYou look the respectable sort, though. Get you something?
Stars watch your steps, traveler. As they watch over Telenger!
Oh, thank you so much. I knew Mister Nurin was all right. \n\nThank you for saving him. Thank you. Thank you.
I always knew Rosalie had something like this in her. She has a crazy streak a mile wide.\n\nIf William's back, maybe I'll go back to the farm after all.
This place is a mess.
I'm not sure what's worse. Nightmares about Daedra, or the months of cleaning and rebuilding we have ahead of ourselves.
The house is a mess. Almost wish the fire took it completely. Probably be easier just to build a new one.
We're five and three-times blessed to have you here.\n\nThe loss of so many Marines. Hard to bear. But at least we can bury the dead as victors.
Be quick with your discussions. My patience lessens by the moment.
By the Hist, I'll be more careful next time. If you're ever in Duskwallow Hamlet, my nest is yours!
Father. Why?
Another fragment of my soul lies to the south. It's heavily guarded, so be wary.\n\nI would not fault you for turning back. It only gets tougher from here.
Did <<1>> send you? What's he want now? Shall I strip naked and chase thunderbugs?
Have you spoken to <<1>>?
Amazing to see that old thing in action. To think our ancestors were so clever.
Rulanir didn't deserve that. No one does.
We may be stuck in Coldharbour, but Nelhilda forgave me and we have our souls back! Sovngarde is ours again, when the time finally comes. \n\nI will never forget what you did for us. Thank you.
Thank you for freeing me. For freeing Faindor.\n\nOur tormentors washed him in fire during the day, and he slept only to face the same all over again. I hope that he can rest easy, now.

You've done the impossible! I've seen those Daedric fiends flay the souls of my friends with but a word. Your power must be immense. Dwarfed only by your generosity.\n\nI … the shards have merged and my soul is whole, once more.
We're back, thanks to you. Let's see the Vanguard try to kick us out again!
Damned pirates. Think they can take the Prowler away from me? I'll show them what <<1>> looks like from the yardarm.
<The lieutenant is unconscious.>
I can't tell you how relieved I am to learn you recaptured the lighthouse.\n\nWe've had enough trouble around here already.
When I went to bed last night, I dreamed of a fully laden ship docking in the harbor. I thought it was a good omen.\n\nCouldn't have been more wrong.
This makes little sense. How could pirates capture the largest port on the Long Coast without a fight?
No time for talk! Go deal with those dungheaps!
I'd like to know why <<1>> pulled her Jade Dragoons from <<2>>. Their absence nearly led to the Jackdaws' success.
You're very kind. I'm sorry to make you go to all this trouble. I feel like such a fool. \n\nI don't have much, but I'll pay you what I can.
Thank you for returning my <<1>>. I thought she might make for the boat after she ran away.\n\nYou've saved me quite a bit of trouble, friend. What can I give you in return?
Our stronghold is under attack! The bandits can't enter the longhouse. It would be a massacre.
So, have you decided to help me? My clan can be a powerful ally if you let us.
Stay back! I'll cut you! I really will!\n\nIt's the voices. They make me crazy. Always whispering to me … saying strange things. The voices ….
I hope my first mate didn't get herself captured. \n\nShe's the best I've ever had. If she doesn't come back soon, I'm going after her.
Thank you for rescuing my employees! When all this is over, stop by my tavern. I think you'll like it there.\n\nI'll head back to Haven right after the cat-lord frees it!
With all the excitement of the pirate attack, it seems the Dominion is less interested in the business of a humble innkeeper and his loyal staff.\n\nBut best not to mention it.
Hey you, I need some help.

Pirates routed, delivery made, and you of all people to do it! Strange times, my friend.\n\nI think I'll stretch my legs before heading back to the Prowler. The rest of the crew can handle repairs, for once!
What do we have here?
You heard the prisoner! Head to the entrance and warn the guards!
Do be careful out there. These books are harmless enough, but they aren't the only things flitting about in the dark.
You! Have you come to help me?
Stranger.
Thanks again, friend. Can't wait to reinvest my winnings in a new racer!
My career as a researcher may not be dead after all.\n\nMight even get a promotion. You've saved me from a life in the glass mines, my friend. May the Empyrean Light protect you, wherever you go.
Please, please! Just don't hurt him!
Good luck. As if you'll need it with my Snooks in the lane!
Go! Confront them. Fight! Win!
Thank you again. Look at Leggy go!
They were good little rabbits. Kind and brave. Thank you so much for your promise.
You are urgently needed at Eidolon's Hollow. With my blessing, you can face Vox and survive.
Hopefully we can find Ari … Aranias before she causes any real trouble.
If you reduce Vox's forces and manage to survive, be sure to report back to <<1>> in the camp outside or to <<2>> in Mournhold.\n\nYou'll be rewarded for your assistance.
I heard what you did to the Sentinels. Their egos will be bruised for weeks! Good job.
Any Worm Cultist out to defile our shrine gets a mouthful of arrows. Give a whistle if you see them headed this way.
Yes? What is it now?
So. We should probably get this over with.\n\nYou lead the way.
First chance I've had to catch my breath. You're welcome to any food, bloodkith.
Oh, thank the Eight and whoever else is listening! You're not one of those Red Rook thugs.\n\nAt least, I don't think you're a thug.
Ah, you're the one. Seems we need to have a chat about <<1>>.
I'll just stay down here for now. It's peaceful. Maybe I'll open a bottle of Len's vintage wine while I wait for the trouble to all go away.
I'd love to chat more, but I really must finish this report. My fellows in <<Ac:1>> Mages Guild are chomping at the bit to learn more of our findings!
I refuse to do a lick of work for these Red Rook hooligans.
I am ashamed to say I'd almost given up. But you helped me find my courage.
Oh, don't be cross. You'll find your friend, or you'll die trying. Either way, you won't have to worry about it for much longer.\n\nMortals are so finicky.
<This statue of a male Elf is significantly less worn than the others.>
Hello.\n\nYou aren't an illusion, are you?
Enough. I yield, I yield!
Maybe I am cut out for the <<1>> Guard. Patience and vigilance are the same whether you're fishing or on watch. Not one pirate made it past me!
Woe be to <<1>>! Pact-soldier dooms her to rot in a cell, away from the warm sun!\n\nIs better than missing her head, <<1>> supposes. Goodbye, merciful yet punitive friend.
You did it! The dreugh are pulling back. \n\nBless you.
Did you find Thorn Lodge?
I hope they find Jofnir alive and well.
It might be time for me to go inside, or at least find some shade.
Things should get back to normal now, and that will be good for business.
Ooh, this one looks like a killer. \n\nI like a good killer.
I very much mislike this. Tunnels of earth and rock should not move beneath your feet.
Something doesn't feel right here ….
I always had my eye on <<1>>. He cleans up real nice!
Good thing the captain spotted pirates on our approach. If she hadn't turned us when she did, we'd be decorating the bottom of the bay.
A Dunmer told me he saw the ghost of one of Ysgramor's Companions. Poor guy must be mad.
A giant stomping across the Rift, then bandits on the roads, now Worm Cultists in the city. I'm sleeping with both eyes open from now on.
The shrine is restored!
Hope what I said about Colors can be kept private. I'd hate to get on her bad side.

Come, let me gauge your strengths. I offer training to Fighters Guild members in some of our special techniques.\n\nI also have a few things for sale, but only if you're a member of the appropriate standing.
If it isn't the Wormslayer! Only the best for you, my friend. What can I get you?
Heard what you did on the docks. Fine work, my friend. What can I help you with?
Hey, it's the Wormslayer! A round for the Wormslayer, everyone! No more zombies in the lakes… hic!
Ah, the hero who defeated the Cult on the docks. A pleasure. How may I help you?
At least we now know what the Reachmen wanted in the mine.
Business is picking up. Let me know if you need something.
This bow is the only thing I have left of my wife's. She's returned to the Hist, and I will miss her until I die.\n\nI can't tell you how much it means to hold it once more.
I was thinking I might join the Fighters Guild. See the world, have some adventures.
Well, while we wait for them to decide who the next mayor is going to be, someone has to tidy this place up and make it presentable.
You'll have to excuse me if I don't shed a tear for my dearly departed husband.
My heart goes out to the many victims of this foul tragedy that has befallen <<1>>.\n\nSo! Do you need to buy anything?
Find Healer Dalen at Eidolon's Hollow. He needs those hearts!
With the focusing crystals in hand, I can complete this control rod and safely reactivate the automaton. While you recover the crystals, I'll make the proper adjustments to the construct.
Quality goods. No questions. Get you something?
The crew of the Albatross knows what you did. If the Queen's Own Navy takes us in, we'll make certain everyone else knows, too.
Seems to be no end to this conflict. Cutting the head off the snake would help our cause tremendously.
We're lucky to have you, adept. I'm no Battlemage. I'm much more comfortable in the stacks than in the field.
Well done, Adept. The essence you've gathered will serve us in good stead.\n\nNow imbue this energy into the proper tile.
You're the hero of Faldar's Tooth, right?
My lord is very excited to begin the play. As I am. I adore amateur performances.
The marines and I will take charge here. With any luck, we'll have these beasts cleared out soon enough.

We'll load what we can on the Albatross. If we bring a list of what's left to the Dominion, they can do the heavy lifting.\n\nThe cavern isn't actually spinning, is it? Oh … maybe I'll get to it later. I should sit down.
Make sure you laugh a little. A little bit every day.
From what I've heard things are only getting worse up there. I'd keep my weapon at the ready if I were you.
Byz is happy going back to sweep in warm elf houses and cellars, and not caves of scum.
Thank the Green! Where are you coming from? Silvenar or Arenthia? We've been desperate for reinforcements.
A friend of Aniel's, huh? Welcome to the Knife.
Until we meet again, mortal. I'm sure the master will have more … "activities" planned for you by then.
Oh! Gall and pox! Dame Dabienne wanted me to tell the duke you were coming here.\n\nYou saved me back in Koeglin Village! I'm the messenger … the one in the warehouse.
You go kill Elf, then leave! Toothmaul claim caves now! Care not for Elf wars.
Don't let the priest bore you, my friend. And ask Shazah if you have any questions about this Moon Hallowed business. This one's just happy she understood what her sister was talking about.
May the light of Auri-El bring peace to <<1>>.
This is great! Remember to hold a spot for us on the Spearhead!
I'll just rest here a moment until my head stops swimming. Go on, I'll see you later in Shor's Stone.
Most of the attacks occurred along the northwest road. I'd start there if I were you. And traveler—watch your back.
The locals claim my father hunted bears and other animals in these hills. There must be some clue nearby.
I heard about you! You're the stranger who freed Dabienne from the stocks, aren't you?\n\nSure glad you're here.

Those fools thought they were necromancers. But in their ignorance, they killed and raised everyone inside this facility—not just those condemned to die. If this place wasn't so well hidden, its effects could've spread to <<1>> itself.
We will see you in Rawl'kha, Hallowed.\n\nAnd if she is feeling kind, Shazah will fill in Khali on all she has missed.
Damn Drublog. If I had a weapon, I'd slit a few of their throats before they got me.
Impressive. Thanks for the help! Now to pick up the pieces and rebuild it.
That worked out much better than I thought it would.\n\nI think formal introductions are in order. My name is Tharayya. Pleased to meet you.
There has been so much blood and so much darkness here today. I should attend to these wounded knights.
Did you see how big that thing was? And those teeth!
You made a fool's decision! Did you not see the horror this thing unleashed?
The cultists are inside the ruins but we cannot follow. The doorway is sealed. \n\nThere seems to be a connection between the welkynd stones here and the spirits that guard the gateway.
How did you get here?
How did you find your way in here?
Others came before you. All who enter will die.
They're gone! What powers you must wield!
They lied to us! The damn Maulborn lied to us! Who's going to cure me now?
I guess I'm lucky I never made it into the quarantine. But you know, I don't feel very lucky. I guess I do have the plague ….
I don't believe it. There must be some mistake. The Maulborn want to help us. They said they were here to do good.
I wish I hadn't been right about the Maulborn. I really wanted there to be a cure for this cursed plague.
I hope that's Yngrel's blood I see on you!
I sense the forest more at peace now.
I'm ready. How do we get out of here?
Oh my … that was quite a rush. Thank you for the experience, new friend!
You are not <<1>>, yet you called me here. How?
I … don't think I'll ever forget those screams. I hope he gets back to his family, some day.\n\nGo on. Go get that bastard Wormfather. I can get back to the portal on my own.
<The Guardian's Eye hums at a barely-perceptible pitch.>
I am so worried about my fellow priests at the shrine, but Master Aron told me to stay here until things were safer there.
Do I know you?
Meet me at  <<1>>'s longhouse when you're done. If his answers don't satisfy me, we'll put those locks of hair to good use.
You must be the ones who helped Lienne and Irnand. We got here as soon as we could.
The Worms … ripping my soul apart. Help me!
I can't believe I fell for that. I'm getting soft.
The look on her face was priceless!
Just get me that bottle of wine before I change my mind.\n\nI think I'm going to need a nice, hot bath when this is all over.
If you'll excuse me, I have healing potions to craft.
I don't want to leave Velyn Harbor, but it's too dangerous to stay!
Velyn Harbor's my home! I don't want to leave!
The militia? Are they all right? I tried to lead them, but the Drublog ….
Funny seeing you here.
You tough. Maybe tough enough for Crucible. Maybe not.
It is good to make profit, especially in times of war. The Dominion will pay a good price for these.
Come join us at the Screaming Mermaid when you get a chance. First drink's on me.
Welcome back to the Isles, adept. We must be wary. This part of Sheogorath's realm is twisted and corrupt.
Whatever it is, I didn't do it!
Sorry. Enough troubles of my own right now. Can't deal with any of yours.
Well, you're a notch above our usual clientele. Make yourself at home.
This is outrageous! I am a captain of the Fists of Thalmor! By what authority does a mere sergeant keep me detained?\n\nWhen my superiors hear what happened this day, <<1>> will be court-martialed!
Velyn Harbor's been preparing for my wedding, so I have to take the time to meet with the locals.\n\nDon't worry! I'll still beat you to Dra'bul.
You have your orders, Drublog. Why do you disturb me? Has something gone wrong?
I know you're not a Drublog. You're friends with <<c:1>>, like me. But your trickery did not come fast enough. She's gone.
Please leave me. I wish to mourn my daughter.
What are you waiting for, an invitation? We've got a trap door to explore!
So, you've come to kill me.
Now I need that bath. A nice long soak with a few glasses of this fine wine.\n\nDon't worry. I'll catch up and meet you at the farm.
Careful in there. Drublog Orcs aren't known for their diplomacy.
Allow me to rest, please.
Eager for a fight, eh? I like you.
Hold on.

I thought we had lost you for a little while there. You seemed to be consumed by the dream much as the king was.\n\nAfter he returned though, you slept soundly. I knew you were all right then, so I left you to rest. You needed it.
Give me a chance to rest.
I hear you got <<1>> and her crew out of Saintsport. With her on our side, things become a lot easier.
Give me a chance to recover.
That's a nice disguise, but you don't smell bad enough to be a Sea Drake. What are you doing here?
My father was right … I should never have married a Khajiit.\n\nI wanted to see the world, explore foreign lands, eat exotic foods, not pull my hair out over a moon-sugar addict!
Thank you for agreeing to look for Master Raston. I'm sure he was going to talk to Gulakhan Harrinat. Perhaps he can tell you where Raston's gotten to.
Ah! Please, don't beat me again!
I'm out of shape. Give me a moment.
Are you a minion of the Worm Cult?\n\nI beg you to stop this. You fools are destroying history with every artifact you desecrate.
Choke and die, Sea Drake! I'll spit on your grave.
I don't understand what happened. I feel like my body, my mind, were not my own. A fate worse than death. \n\nThank you for restoring my mind. Now I must restore my honor.
If you're going to kill me, get it over with.
You completed the quest!
You completed the quest!
Good luck. I'll be in Helane's cabin. Don't forget to stop by after Deregor is out.
I'm not telling you anything, scum! What have you done with Captain Lerisa?
I'm off to join my crew, unless you have any burning questions.
<Captain Helane is unconscious but still breathing.>
This is the part where I trust you.
You get into trouble, you're on your own.
The Staff of Arkay. Take it, use it to strike down these blasphemers.

The staff will reveal circles of corruption among the crypts. There lurk the Bloodthorn Cult's abominations, hidden in pockets of Oblivion.\n\nPlant the staff in a circle to draw an abomination into our world. Then destroy it!
The Bloodthorn's perversion of my people is ended. The honored dead are at rest once again.
Our war was a long time ago. Once we've cleared out the cult, we'll rebury any bodies they've defiled. Even Breton dead deserve that dignity.\n\nAlso, I don't want them creeping into town at night.

Alit grease! That's a great idea! Who knew those slimy beasts were good for something? But don't be stingy. You probably need a lot of grease to turn that lever.\n\nOh, and there are two more levers you need to throw or the door won't open.
Out for a stroll, enjoying the scenery?
These cultists are a real nuisance. I'll report back to Captain Kaleen in a bit. Hope the robes helped.
Hrr! This wretched forest has already taken everything precious to <<1>>.\n\nGo away!
You made it. Won over the giant with your charm, no doubt.

Aha! So you returned from Gavaudon with another feather in your cap? Defeating the Ironhand Ogres? Wish I could claim such an accomplishment.\n\nFrankly, it's an honor to know you. Is there anything you need from me?

The Sacred Lady told me to tell you to talk to an Ordinator.\n\nBy the way, two people came by and asked for you. A pretty young woman and a dour old man. They said they had to leave the city, but the woman wanted me to pass on her thanks.
A number of Velyn Harbor's citizens joined the militia after you rescued them.\n\nThey'll protect the town when you're gone. Thank you!
We're being slaughtered here!

Roku spoke of what you did at Velyn Harbor. She says if my champions were dumb enough to challenge you, they deserve their fate.\n\nI'm not as easy to impress. So tell me—why do you trespass in my stronghold?
Just get us home.
Is this not the most magnificent inn? The tapestries are so vibrant, the people so friendly!
I've got nothing to say to you.
Hello, stranger. If you're hungry, I've got extra.
Is Malanie dead? Yes? Maybe now I can earn a living wage. Doubtful on this island, but it must be better than before. Right?
You're not another one of those ruffians, are you? Don't you dare lay a hand on me, or you'll get a good wallop!
You're no Steel Shrike! At least, you don't look it. Did you get caught in their raid too?

Ugh. My insides feel like maggot haggis. Guess that batch was a little too strong. Ah well, the next one will be better!\n\nIt's like my father used to say, "True progress comes from the crashing waves of a maelstrom."
<The monkey screeches happily.>
You made it. Won over the giant with your charm, no doubt.
I only have a moment to talk.
By trusting you with this petition, I acknowledge your actions to save my tribe. I trust you to deliver it intact.
We'll have the Spearhead ready to sail for Betnikh the moment you return with Bhosek's records.
The captain's inside.
Oh. Yes, hello. This is fascinating. Did you know the Dwemer had devices to rapidly mince fruit?
The relic is gone and my people's souls are at rest. I thank you for your choice.
If they do chop off your head, try to keep the blood off the vest. I'll be scrubbing for days elsewise.
You look a proper servant now. Hurry up with those records. I'll be right here, sweeping away.
Hurry on now. You don't want to be whipped. Bhosek's been doing all too much whipping lately.
Tell me more about those firm, deft hands of yours, Jakarn.
This Jakarn is quite charming, for a scoundrel.\n\nBut I do love scoundrels.

Welcome to Endarwe's Museum of Wonder and Antiquities.\n\nNormally, I'd tell you to avoid touching anything, lest you defile my sanctum, but the necromancers that came in before you have already ruined everything.

Go to the mine near the Daggerfall cathedral. Plant the spirit's possessions within the soil that belonged to her family.\n\nThat should awaken her. Then you can learn the truth of this curse and make your decision. Now go!
These two are the ones for me, my friend. You should see what Firn can do with her toes.
Y'ffre's bones! Did you do that to Helthar? That was hilarious!
Go. Leave Helthar alone.
I hear you're to blame for ousting <<1>>. Good riddance. Maybe now the Drublog will settle down and I can finally head back to Jathsogur.\n\nThank you. Not everyone would do what you did.
Before we leave for Betnikh, talk to the crew. Get familiar with them. It'll be a long trip.

<<1>>'s upset about this. We all are! It's bad for business when the mammoths get loose.\n\nAlthough, it does say something about the strength of our brewery, doesn't it? Strong enough to put a mammoth to sleep!
The King is pleased with what you've done here, as am I. You will find a generous reward belowdecks.
You need to get to the Silvenar soon, but you should avoid entering the city before talking to him.

I'll rebuild this manor, but not for my father's sake. I think he and my grandmother caused enough trouble here.\n\nThe new Baelborne manor will be different. It won't be a name to fear anymore. It will be a name to love.
Careful here. These Orcs aren't yet part of the Covenant, but I'm working on that.\n\nFeel free to check out Stonetooth Fortress. Maybe you'll meet a nice Orc.
I hate them all. The Ayleids, necromancers, the Merethic Society, Endarwe, my father; to Oblivion with all of them!
Give that fat bastard my best, eh?
Go, my friend. Without the blessings of Jone and Jode, without the completion of the path of the Mane, Khali is doomed. We must go to Dune, walk the Path. I will meet you there.
Perhaps he'll listen to me. For once. I swear, I think it's a miracle of the Divines that any of his students last past the first year.
Go, my friend. I want my sister back, and I want her back now. The path to her freedom starts in Dune. I will meet you there.
Good luck down there, recruit. Make the bastards pay.
I need to prep for our counterassault. Good luck out there.
Go on. Light it.
I still can't believe you destroyed it. Do you know how many brave soldiers are going to die fighting off the Elves?\n\nI don't even want to look at you.
I see the Countess is out and about town again. \n\nIt certainly makes me feel better about things.
You defeated my cursed body. Never thought I would be free again.\n\nYou have my thanks.
You have courage. Kasan respects that. Even so, you made a grave mistake.\n\nThe Covenant will not use that relic for defense only. Remember my words.
So the Countess is in good health again, and all is well in the village.\n\nHopefully that'll teach people not to get so bent out of shape over a bunch of rumors.

You are formidable to have defeated me in battle. But that was Drodda in control, not I. Find me in Sovngarde if you make your way there. We'll duel again.\n\nIn the meantime, climb to the summit of this Keep and end that cowardly witch, Drodda.
Give the Captain my regards!
Damn it! You know what this means? All these dead cultists? \n\nJust more graves I have to dig.
Sometimes, I miss the swamps of my homeland in the Black Marsh. But it is good to be gone from the dry air of Stros M'Kai.
There's no time! Put out these fires. Now!
Thanks to you, I'm pursuing my love of weapon-making. I'm finally happy and Mother's stopped nagging me to fight.
Remember me? You helped me kill that big snake! I decided to ditch my father's old sword for this beauty.
You're not one of Bhosek's Bloody Fists. Lucky for you.
Did you come with my tonic water?
Not many of us left, huh?\n\nCan't say I'm surprised. It's terrible out there. Doesn't make it any better, though.
We lost so many people. The Tardins, the Elwins, the … oh, I don't want to think about this anymore!
Yes?
We're done here. See if I ever offer to partner up with you again.
A precious Khajiiti relic, sold at some merchant's table. The Bright Moons weep tonight.
Greetings Champion, how may I serve you?
What a terrible omlette! It tastes like ashes.
Kalari will be all right, you will see. Just needs some time to deal with what has happened.\n\nGo, speak to Milk Eyes.
What will I do now? I grew up in Master Hlenir's service.\n\nMaybe I'll go and become a warrior myself.
Go on, you've earned it!
It can't be! My sweet daughter, dead?
I should be able to write three—no, no, five—scholarly dissertations about this Dremora beard pot. They'll make for fascinating reading!
Once you get used to the smell, these clothes are really quite remarkable.
What a marvelous book! I can't wait to read it.
You won, so stop gloating. I'll get into the Academy next season. But know this, you made an enemy of Renus Falvani when you took my invitation.
What truly makes a Nord, I ask you? Well, his weapon for one. His drinking prowess, certainly. But his shield—that's his true companion!\n\nBlast it all, where's that thrice-cursed shield of mine!
I know I made the right decision. I don't belong at some fancy academy. I'm heading back to Lower Yorgrim as soon as I can secure passage.
Father lied to me! He said I was powerful! He said I couldn't be defeated! And then you came along. Oh, just leave me alone!
I heard what he said. I don't know if I could have done it either, soldier. Don't worry about us here. There's no need to sacrifice more lives. We'll pull out as soon as we can.
As soon as folks saw you light up that beacon, I felt the tension drain from the village.
I'm already beginning to plan our next field mission. I'm thinking one of the planes of Oblivion. It's been some time since I perused the stacks in Apocrypha, for example.
May the Empyrean Light of Aetherius light your path.
Stars guide your steps.
Bright moons guide your path.
Jakarn said the gate in that cave is never locked because no one ever makes it past the traps.
Now I am going to have to seal up that cave and drain the well before it can be used again.
What's that in your hands there? Seems you've been busy.
The Sergeant can complain and shout all he wants. With that wound, he won't be doing any more fighting today.
If it's not Goblins, it'll be something else tomorrow. I swear this town is cursed.
Go forth and know that Daggerfall and the crown stands behind you.
Every now and then another straggling ogre comes through. I'm just cleaning up now.\n\nLet's have a drink together when this is all over.
You have been a great help to this community.
Why? Why did you do it? Razum-dar was clear in what he said.
Mercenaries cannot be trusted. And sometimes, neither can <<1>>.
Milk Eyes. Dead on the ground, gnawed by rats? Does Ezzag have to carve you a picture in the sand?
If any of the Bloody Fists ask what you're up to, just tell them you're out for a stroll. Don't mess with the Fists.
Just look at him. He's itching to head for the beach as we speak! Who knows what that little rascal might find?

I'm not accustomed to strangers offering help. My brother and I, we've just had each other for so long.\n\nThe only thing that matters now is <<1>>'s safety. If you find him, tell him to forget the plant. I won't see him hurt trying to save me.
Don't think because I'm wounded that I won't defend myself. The stranglers won't have much to devour after I'm done with you!
<This Redguard died recently.>
Get going, walker. Zurana's in no mood to speak to you further.

The score was sweet. Priceless paintings from Daggerfall. Irina knew where they were coming ashore, Siraj was her muscle, and I was going to fence it.\n\nNow my brother's dead and that bitch is too. Sep bites us all, doesn't he?

You come to destroy my master?\n\nI know what you seek. I would tell you a simple riddle, yet you already have the answer in your possession. That rune you hold is the key to releasing me. The living flesh holds the riddle answer no longer.
Have you found my favorite axe? I long to wield it once again.
With you helping Captain Kaleen, we'll get the goods and be on the sea in no time!
Those are the only people I heard Captain Kaleen mention.
You just saved Jakarn a very public execution. Get moving.
You again? What is it this time?
The baron looks hurt. See if he'll tell you what's going on here.
I've recommended we cease investigation, at least until the dead lie down again.\n\nIt's a miracle any Fists of Thalmor made it out.
You enjoyed every minute of our little adventure. I can tell by the sparkle in your eyes.
Tread lightly. Whatever attacked us is still around.
What can I do for you?
Part of me doesn't want to open the letter, as if the action itself would make the fear of his death a reality.
They're all gone!
Excellent! I can't wait to present this to King Fahara'jad. I'm sure he'll put it to good use!
Go ahead, just speak to it. It can tell you so much about the site.
My friend. It is good to see you again. Please, speak to the woman. Raz will wait for you.
My last arrow. Have to take the rest down the hard way.

Start with Shaman Laganakh. She witnessed Bloodthorn rituals in the Carved Hills. She's waiting by the longhouse south of here.\n\nCultists were also seen at Moriseli, to the north, and Grimfield, west of here.
I heard of your deeds. Glad you destroyed that thing.\n\nLambur was right about you. You're welcome on Betnikh any time.
The relic was here, I saw it!
Please, just leave me be.
Odreth's a good captain. He loves the Rangers more than anyone; they mean the world to him. He takes it personally if anyone tries to interfere with them or their legacy. That's why he's the captain.
Thank you for saving my brother. To know that Sir Hughes is dead and that Vaermina's plot here was thwarted gives me much peace.\n\nI still mourn the loss of my sweet Lakana though.
So first you freed me, and now you saved the king? You certainly do keep busy. You're an inspiration too. \n\nI hope we run into each other again.
Follow my advice and those covert Alessians shouldn't give you any trouble.
I'm going to watch this bridge, make sure nothing else moves in. I can see Amadour feeding a troll or something equally disgusting.
I'm afraid something has happened to Zich. He loves Goblin's Delight and eagerly runs up everytime I make a new batch. I hope he comes by soon.
As if some spirit could scare me. I'll just devote the rest of my life to cheating death. That will show her!
Are you ready to free your friend? Not much time left.
These curatives do wonders to help the wounded. You've saved a great many lives today.\n\nThank you for taking the time to bring this to us.
Thank you again for returning my dear little friend. I hope he doesn't wander off again!
Never thought I'd say it, but I'll be glad to strike a living enemy again.\n\nI've had enough of undead for one day. Maybe for a lifetime!
Go speak to your Artificer, child. He seems quite agitated.
Daughter, enough. I know you are concerned, but I will hear no more of it.
The Clan Mother likes to be obeyed promptly. Remember this, when you are sad you did not listen to Zal-sa.
You have proven your barbaric nature. Be gone.
Murderer! Butcher! You will suffer for your crimes, I promise you!
Please, don't kill me! I have gold. Lots of gold. Kill her. She knows everything!
Pray to Arkay, Orc. Pray hard.
Are you going to murder me, too? Get on with it, then!
Hey, what's a Red Rook doing in our camp! Ha! Just kidding!\n\nYou do look pretty good in that outfit, though.
Is it done? Is the envoy dead?\n\nThen let me out of here so I can go rescue my family!
So, ah … unless there is anything else, I should get back to … ah … helping? Helping the good merchant to her valuables. With her valuables! Yes!

Wait—aren't you the person who rescued Dame Dabienne from those mad villagers? Yes, I'm certain you are! She described you perfectly. \n\nWould you have time? You must tell me everything. I can write a song about you!
I've heard your praises from a number of rescued miners. Well done.
Sounds like those ogres are no longer a threat!\n\nNow we can go on with our lives.
They're finally going to tear down that guillotine! It's about time. I hate living in fear.
Go on. The lamia caves are up ahead.\n\nI need the matriarch dead.
Even my death failed my people.
The wyrd sisters know much more about healing than I do. Thank you for helping them.
Our gambit paid off. The lamias on the shore fled soon after your entrance into the caves.\n\nWe've broken the back of their army, and are free to press the assault against the Maormer.

So word is you went up to Firebrand and hunted down Sir Hughes. \n\nGood to know someone around here had the guts to do the right thing. That bastard didn't deserve to live, not after what he did to our Duchess.
He's trapped. Captured with a snare of Daedric magic. He will be made into the ones you have fought, or killed if proven too weak.\n\nIf you wish to free him, be warned. You may take his place!
This one must find more coin if he is to ever bask in warm sands again!
Something is different. Something has changed.
We must right the wrongs of history and heal the soul of our world. Are you ready to meet your destiny, Vestige?
You are the Hallowed. It is your sacred charge, now, to keep the Claw safe.
Find the Mane, please. Now, of all times, for the Khajiiti people to lose their way … we can't.
My friend! This one is glad to see you. And I am in nowhere near as dire straits as I was last time our eyes met.
I heard you ran the Red Rooks out of town. That should make my work much easier. Thank you.
You killed everyone I love! Why?
I think I might join the Fighters Guild. See the world, have some adventures.
Damn my luck! I chose the wrong time to come home from Greenshade.
Be wary. Drusilla is powerful. You will need all your cunning to overcome her.
This time of year, I'm always worried about the harvest. It's a race to get the food to market before it rots.
I guess we actually did it. The Daggers saved the day. Sort of.
Be careful. Foul magic taints the air. Perhaps your learned friend can shed some light on this dark mystery and help you to bring an end to its source.
By the Eight, why the blazes are you still bothering me?\n\nGo find that damn Gelvin and get me back my egg.
Ahh, my old friend! Couldn't resist another exploration?\n\nBe mindful, this one may be a touch more dangerous. Foul necromancy is at work here.
I think this mercenary band might just have a future, after all.

Search the tents around the ruins. <<1>> said she would meet me at the ruins' entry, straight back from the steps.\n\nTell her not to worry! I will return with Thalmor reinforcements, and drive out these dungy muskarse Sea Vipers!
Bah. With the Dominion in charge at Brindle, you can't walk in town without tripping over an Elf or a cat.
Maybe she wasn't working with the slavers, but there's still something shady about that woman. Mark my words.

I can't believe my eyes. The undead are actually receding. For a while there, I thought we were making a last stand here.\n\nI'm betting it wasn't our brilliant tactics that drove them away though. Conquering Marbruk wasn't their top priority, was it?
This one will remain behind to aid the injured. But you will see Akkhuz-ri again soon.

It seems our circumstances are even worse than I imagined. The corruption of the Shadow Wood expands across the forest. I fear it's too late to contain it.\n\nWe must find the Shade of Naemon himself, here on this plane, if we are to stop him.
What is that smell? It smells like a kennel full of wet dogs. Or wet Nords.
You keep walking around, going in and out. I'm guessing this means you're not going to kill me? That's good.
You fought well, for an outsider.
A good fight, stranger.
When your family needs help, you drop everything and come running. I don't want to let Haraldar down.
Go on. Check out the crypts. We'll handle things up here.
Really now, if you have any questions you can speak to my father. He's at the main camp to the east.\n\nOff you go.
Ah, what a grand and glorious day! I just love the great outdoors!
Why would you return Talmo's banner to him? Dominion heraldry has no place in Vlastarus.
Now that Faolchu is gone, perhaps we can start to heal.
A new chapter in Khajiiti spiritual life begins today, Moon Hallowed. And it is all thanks to you. The monks will write of this day for years to come, and your story will become as legend.
I can't wait to see the lizard's face. He won't ever tease me again!
Get low, and keep quiet. The Centurion sent you, right?
Bright Moons! Please, free me.
Yes! You are no cultist. You have come to save Mahazi! Thank you!
Please, I need to be alone.\n\nI think you can find your own way out.
Ha! These Colovians were like wheat before the scythe.
So, your truthiness overcomes all! My felicitude winds around you like a warm fog.\n\nGive me those meats and I'll expose <<1>>'s perfitudidness.
<The air around the table vibrates gently as the spell holds. The house is protected, for now.>
I feel strong again, fully healed.\n\nWhere's my father? I must go to him.
I think I'll practice on locals before heading to Stormhold.\n\nFirst impressions are everything, as my father used to say.
You impress me, traveller. Few can defeat me in a game of riddles.
I sure appreciate you stepping in to help that mage.
We're going to drive those Red Rooks out of Crosswych, just you wait and see.
This won't end well. And it's all on you, my friend.
Hello there. I hope you don't mind me playing. The music helps soothe the anxiety.
You're going to hand the relic to those fools? I cannot remain with someone who would make such a choice!
Well? Do you want the gold or not?
You're a bigger fool than I thought. You're no shipmate of mine!
You destroyed something that might have brought us peace. You've doomed my brothers. If I never see you again, it'll be too soon!
I cannot sail with someone who willingly dooms enemies to such a fate.
Thanks to you, Camlorn is no longer under Faolchu's mangy paw.
Hello
I'm glad you're all right. <<1>> will speak with you now.\n\nHe forbade me to speak further.
You return! Please, tell me. How did <<1>> die?
Hi
Go … kill the betrayers. Save … Dune.
I'll warn the captain and the others. Hurry to the fortress!
Any luck? I just used my last bandage.
You've returned. You have questions.
I'm too late. Too late.
That bastard followed me in here. Didn't think those big ones could fit into this house. Nasty creatures, really.
I am glad you came through in one piece, Hallowed. Um … perhaps you can help vouch for me to the Queen? She continues to make jokes about treachery. I do not like it.
Your assistance with the Maormer is most appreciated my friend.
What do you want?
So Sir Edmund's in the hot seat now. Hope he handles it better than Sir Hughes did…\n\nAfter everything that's happened, I'm not sure I'm staying in the order anyhow.
Step lightly! Fenlords do not keep lazy servants. They could be on us in a flick of a tail!
Thanks to you, I can rest now.
Jakarn told me what you did. I'm impressed. The Orcs were too, so I've been told.
Well, I guess our little tryst is off for the time being. I'll head back to the ship, as soon as Irien's not looking.\n\nThat woman has nails like a duneripper.
For what it's worth, I think you did the right thing, destroying that relic. Magic that powerful should not be in the hands of Men.
You did a hard thing, the right thing.
It's all right, Matilda. We'll be away soon.
Talk to them if you wish. This is simply how things are, in our clan and others. I understand that, even if I don't accept it.
This one is as he was in life. Merely a mote in the lunar light, floating where the Bright Moons take him. As are we all, in the end.
Felari shall keep you in her prayers to the Bright Moons, my friend.
You should have listened to Captain Kaleen. She was right about the artifact.
I commend you again on choosing to keep the relic for the Covenant. But <<1>> tells me we must hasten to Glenumbra.
You've made it … down here … just to die. Aldmeri dog.
So, we're keeping the artifact. While the captain supports your decision, I'm not sure I agree.\n\nI'm glad I wasn't in your shoes, my friend.
I hear the captain isn't too happy with you about that relic. But at least these Orcs are joining the Covenant.
I have much to discuss with the Bishop and Gharesh-ri, my friend. I'm sure we will see each other again. You are the Hallowed, after all.
The proud city of Daggerfall greets you. Can I help you with something?
Nice work. I'll keep an eye out for more. I'm sure they're coming from Cloud Ruler Temple.\n\nLet Hjorik know you cleaned out this batch.
Urn … dangerous. Cultists summoned terrible … killed them. Take urn to <<1>>. Find <<2>>. Safe with her.
If you knew where a bunch of dangerous criminals were stashing their stolen goods, would you have guts to go check it out?
How did you get through the barrier? Speak quickly, stranger. We're all on edge.
Speak to Vanus Galerion in Skywatch. He's expecting you.
No mystery where to find Lokra. Check the docks. She'll be there, staring at your ship … if she hasn't already snuck aboard.
Welcome to Vulkhel Guard! I must attend my Queen at the moment, but I hope you enjoy your time in my fair city.
I should have done more to fight the vampires. I'll make it up to Sud-Hareem someday.
This wasn't supposed to happen. We were supposed to save At'avar at the last moment.
Well, that was fun, wasn't it? All right, maybe fun isn't the right word. But you were glorious!\n\nAngof is finally dead. We can't thank you enough for what you've done.
Can't you see that I'm trying to read?
I know I saw that book around here somewhere.
Was it twenty coins from the Salted Wings? Or twenty five? \n\nSorry, sorry. A tax collector's work is never done, you know!
Just having a little sip! Don't … don't tell anyone. It's a secret, just you and me.
Oh, excuse me. Just praying for my son. He's on the front lines in Cyrodiil. \n\nI know what he's doing is important, but I can't help but wish he was here at home with me.
Oh, hello! Are you looking forward to the Queen's speech too? Going to be a great moment, a great moment.
Have you seen Doralin? She was supposed to help me set the table. Probably off sneaking a drink again, if I know her.
Marvelous view from up here, don't you think?
A little privacy, please? These are some sensitive materials.
Don't mind Kuzda. She'll be finished soon.
You've done it! You've walked paths in darkness and come out the other side … into the light.

I will admit, Hallowed. The words of the Moon-Bishop affected me deeply. But your victory here … the scent of your return to our living world. The dawn of a new day for our allies. It fills my heart with hope.
Your actions today humbled me, Hallowed. That you would work to secure the future of my people so earnestly … truly, the Bright Moons do shine down upon you.
The Moon Hallowed cannot travel the Two Moons Path with such corruption going on. We need to clean this city for all to be right with our people.
Sorry, hunter. I only had enough for one bounty. I'm saving the rest of my coin for more of this fine brew.
Senche are terribly dangerous beasts. This one tires of the hunt.
By the Green! One of those damned Senche got me.
I'm going to be the one to claim the prize! Even if I have to kill every Senche out here to do it!
Ungh, finally. Soldier, I'm not going to stay conscious much longer. You have to tell the Centurion.
Good to see Dominion troops in Cropsford. I feel safer with armed Altmer around.
You made it out of Ilmyris alive? How … unexpected.
My friend the traveler! Zadala's meeting went well … she hopes she's glad to see you again?
This is my fishing spot. Go find another!
What does my lord command? Wait, who is my lord again? It's all so muddled.
One by one, Naemon and Pelidil exposed my servants to the crystals, until their mortal minds cracked and groaned under the strain.

Dark Moons! These crazy Bosmer make no sense! Hazazi comes to negotiate on behalf of Queen Ayrenn, to hear their grievances, and all they do is dance and jest!\n\nHazazi has only been here a short while and already he hates this village.
<<1>> needs your help. You must go now, before it is truly too late.

This one would ask a favor. If this Thalmor mage turns Razum-dar into a monkey, you must exact vengeance.\n\nOh, and you would need to track down Pelidil on your own. Raz hopes this will not be the case, though.
Those cultists are some nasty pieces of work. Go carefully along that part of the riverbank.

So you're the one who's going to accompany the cat on this guar-brained scheme of his? \n\nI hope you realize what you're up against. These traitors in our city have sought to stir up rebellion since the day King Camoran joined the Dominion.
Thank you for delivering my message to Hissmir.

Another tourist? Rare to have so many visitors in this part of the Valenwood. Didn't you hear? It's much safer behind the shiny new walls of Marbruk. \n\nEven King Camoran hesitates to venture into the Court of the Wilderking.
Kaushur is hoping to leave this wretched place soon. The only ones crueler than the combatants are the odds-makers.
You came from Jorunn's Stand. Did the general send you?
Have you seen the mewling hounds they call warriors here? They are nothing before the might of Lugrun!
Hey there! Bit busy here, if you don't mind. Been a long day.
My cousin died in the arena! He died like a true son of Sovngarde!
You've no idea how thankful I am that you're not a Daedra. The gods are merciful.
I'm already prepared to retake this town once again.
Dawnbreak will be ours. We beat these Daedra once, we can do it again.
Why oh why are you pestering me? Let me enjoy my fire in peace.\n\nShoo now. Shoo.
Please, for the sake of our people, defeat the <<1>>.
Fildgor has departed this place and the spirits return to their eternal sleep. Tell me what happened here.
The moons sometimes force us to walk strange paths. They are not always the most fragrant, swiftest. But, ultimately, they lead us where we should go.
My scales still leak blood, but with time I'll heal. I must document everything that has happened here. \n\nThe people of Murkwater will never forget what you have done for us.
I will watch this path for any suspicious strangers.
Every day that this place is shut down is a day I'm losing gold.\n\nSo what happened out there? Do you bring me good news or bad?
What can I do for you?
Part of me doesn't want to read this diary. I think that would make what happened to my cousin all the more real.
I lost my family! They're all gone!
My sister is going to be so happy that you saved me.
<The guard no longer responds having fallen back into a deep sleep.>
Get out of here. You've worn out your welcome.

The Ra-Netu have returned to the sea. The docks will soon smell of dead fish again instead of dead people.\n\nAnd you! Right off the boat and you slay the necromancer? Surely Tu'whacca sent you to deliver us from this … difficult situation.
Hurry through the Roost upstairs to reach Blackheart's Cove. You'll find the Captain there.

You dealt with the spriggan matron, didn't you? Wish I could have helped.\n\nWe'll wait around until the trolls leave. Without the influence of the matron, they won't stick around here for long. Then we can get back to business.
I made my way back here. On my own. No thanks to Boss Thulvald. \n\nI really need a warm bed in a nice safe inn. And a good meal. And probably a new job.
Good work humiliating my brother! He needed to be taken down a peg.
<Egolor lies on the floor in a pool of his own blood.>
I told you, I'll get the money to Many-Eyes as soon as I can.
Please, no more. I'll get Many-Eyes her money as soon as I can!
Quick, untie me before she returns!
I'll get you back someday.
Good fighting there. Garnikh won't forget you.
Nothing more for you here. Keep moving.
So was the hunt successful? Did you find out what nefariousness our good Commander Yjarnn is up to?

You might want to get back on your boat, seafarer. The dead are crawling from the sea and they have overtaken the docks.\n\nThere is nothing to be done. We just have to pray to Tu'whacca that they wander away.
It took a brave soul to charge in there. I hope your courage was rewarded.
I have spoken for the good of the clan. You are free to tell Lokra whatever you wish.
Perhaps an outsider's opinion will convince Lokra, as she doesn't seem to listen to those of her clan.
Have you met our enemies?
The waters will clear soon, now that you've fixed whatever troubled Alten Corimont.\n\nIt's a sign.

So you found out what that Dominion spy was up to, huh? Glad someone else could. I can't do everything myself.\n\nCleaning up this xanmeer's work enough. Then again, all these ruins need a good cleaning, inside and out, if you catch my meaning.
I'll never admit this to Captain Lerisa, but I think you did the right thing. A Breton king as ambitious as Emeric should not be handed that kind of power.
I can't believe he stood me up. The nerve. I mean… just that I was looking forward. To working with him.\n\nBah! That's it. I'm done!
I've heard you're the one who figured out the Dominion's part in our recent troubles. True? Must be nice.\n\nWell, some of us have troubles of our own, and you don't hear us begging for help.
Fobbing cheats! I just let a full cargo hold of timber go for half its value! I don't like the way these Redguards negotiate.\n\nI'll never get square with S'rashi at this rate.
Well. What are you doing on my boat?
No … don't make me look at him! The Dark Husband is here!
Thanks for freeing us. It's about time we got out of this horrid swamp.
My mind reels with what we've accomplished here. I can't wait to get back to Hatching Pools and spread the tales of your exploits.\n\nThank you!
<This ward prevents any entry into the temple.>
The Bright Moons are with you, Hallowed. Khali will be a credit to her name, leading her people with bravery and strength. And Shazah's wisdom will be more than a match for the Dark Mane's treachery.
You … you're not crazy! You can't be corrupted by the whispers either?
I don't believe a word Jakarn says, but there's just something about him. He's fascinating.
Jakarn's gorgeous. He could rob me any time.
I don't really believe he's a captain. He looks so good I don't care.
You killed them! Those people were my friends. I should've been the one to put down the crazy bastards!
Blood and faith! Are you real? Can you hear me? Please, get me down!
Begone, servant. Do your work and stop bothering me.
You do not carry yourself like a servant. Best see to that, if you wish to avoid a beating.
We did it. We held. But at what cost?
Touch the stone pillar on the rise behind us. \n\nShow me the enemies that you would have me share with your Dominion.
I'm glad Ezzy's going to stick around. I'd have missed that old cat!
Now that <<1>> is out of the way, I'll run this Caravan properly and fairly. You have my word.

For our little operation to work, everybody's gotta watch everybody else. The dealers watch the players, the game bosses watch the dealers, and <<1>> watches the managers. Me? I watch everybody. But today, I'm watching you.
Thank you so much for helping this one, stranger. Tand promises to be a better life mate to Sind.
Bright moons and long life to you, walker-friend. We will remember you, always!
Will my brother learn from this, I wonder? Father is right. He doesn't deserve a husband like Sind.
I cannot wait to see the look on Muzag's face when I return his son to him. It's good to earn points with your boyfriend's father, yes?
You did it. You saved my father.\n\nI'm sorry I ever doubted you. You have more than earned our trust.
Good luck on many travels, my friend. Am sure we will meet once again.\n\nI will spend some time with these monks. Their culture is very fascinating. One wonders what one must do to become one?
You're the mortal who's interfered with my creatures in the bog, aren't you? Don't bother to tell me your name. You won't need it if you continue to trouble me.

I always knew it was the guts of the guardian that gave it powers, but I never dreamed it would be so easy to augment those powers. \n\nDew bugs, thunderbug bellies, and hive seeds. They're everywhere around here!
Unless you have questions of me, I will soon be on my way. We should both search the forest for other signs of Naemon's corruption. \n\nI fear at some point, we will have to confront Naemon himself.
You've made it through alive. The other Keepers must be dead, then.\n\nA part of me wishes it were not so.
The moons shine upon you, friend, and your lizard is spared the stewpot! Congratulations!
