<The corpse of <<1>> has already begun to decay. It will be unrecognizable in a few days.>

The Stormfists have three supply wagons with them. Set them on fire and we'll send the entire camp into panic!\n\nThen light the signal fire and find Fildgor. If he finishes whatever foul ritual he's performing, it will mean the end of the kingdom!
Hurry, champion. I can feel my essence slipping away.
Find that Khajiit! I can't believe she'd turn on her own like this!
I have waited for centuries. And waited … and waited. Do you know how boring that can be?\n\nBut now you are here. Just as Meridia foretold.
I thought we would get to go home after the keystone was found.
I haven't swung my axe once since we got here, and you did all the work. Well at least I'll get paid. Haha.

What I wouldn't do to be in a nice, safe place. A tavern somewhere, maybe. Warm. A pint of ale. Some good company.\n\nInstead, I'm in Coldharbour. If Molag Bal's minions don't kill me, Skordo surely will.
I'm very busy. Can't you tell?
Look for Neramo to the north. Just follow the road and look for his tent.

Very few would dare to enter the Prince of Murder's realm of their own choosing. Your action consists of equal parts bravery and stupidity. I think, in this case, that's exactly what we need.\n\nWe've been waiting for you, planewalker.
You are spikeball champion! This one reminds you that spikeball can be lucrative as a profession, and he would be honored to manage your career.
Who are you? How did you get here? Leave me alone!
Blackheart is dead, but he won't stay that way forever. Let's destroy his skull and prevent him from ever returning.
I'm sorry I lied to you. I … I hope we can still be friends.
Well, go on then. No worries, I'll be fine. They haven't made a cage that can hold this knight. Not yet, at any rate.
Praise to Auri-El! The six Elder Scrolls are all in our possession. We must ensure that they remain with us, where they belong!

This is preposterous! Asteril has risked her life for the Dominion more times than I can count. She is one of my best officers.\n\nI refuse to believe this irresponsible slander until I have spoken with her myself.
If <<1>> survived the Dominion's initial attack, I'm certain he can help.
Spies! There are spies everywhere! And assassins!
Ezreba is grateful for your kindness.
Isn't he cute? We are going to be closer than ever now.
I'm glad you councilled Bowenas well. Everyone deserves a second chance.

Now you are negotiating with a forest spirit who calls himself a king? With all those floating leaves, Hazazi thinks he looks very silly.\n\nDo you really think this is going somewhere? Or is it just a waste of time?
The Hist tree will most likely die soon, but I accept your decision. May the scholars' efforts aid you well against Molag Bal.
I appreciate it when a beautiful monster needs something. That usually means you can trust her.\n\nAt least for a while, anyway.
Now that was a battle worthy of your greatness! Congratulations!
Welcome to Longhaven. Used to be a busier place, before all this trouble with the mist. But we won't let that be an excuse for poor hospitality.
So you made it through the mist. Your will is stronger than I expected.

Reason with this mad Dunmer! You'll have to kill some of the clan, but there are those of us who only want to coexist alongside the living without harm. Wouldn't it be better to have us as allies to call upon?
<The statue holds the Gem of Courage.>
I don't know what that well-dressed man just did, but I'm going to bet it's very bad for us.
<This strange contraption is surprisingly heavy and would take several people to move.>
Don't worry. Girin and I will get in there soon enough.\n\nIn the meantime, keep Indaenir out of trouble.
The kagouti thought themselves clever to coat their tusks with poison, but the Tree knows all. Its roots will soon feed on the kagouti who burned its blood.
<The statue holds the Gem of Courage.>
<The statue holds the Gem of Courage.>

Suit yourself. I'm getting out of here. There's something odd out there. Something strange to the look of the mist ….\n\nAnyway, I'm heading to Woodhearth for a belly full of drink and a soft fur mat.
Defeat the king and be done with it.
Kill me if you must, Orc. I swear, I will rise from the very grave to make an end of you.
Get this door open, Targoth, and let's end this!
How did you do with those Black Daggers?
Go, Targoth. Aid our warchief.
You've returned. What do you have to report?
Thank you for your able council. May bright moons light your path as they light Ezreba's path to forgiveness.
See you in <<1>>. Going to lie down in a bit.
Are you … are you from <<1>>? They said they would send help….
If the gods reward hard work, we've got something coming to us!
With a little luck, we'll have this cleared away before the tide comes in.
Never far from trouble, are you?\n\nWord reached the palace that Aldmeri forces were here, so the king sent me right away. Looked like many of the Elves were already dead. Where did they come from?
How may Manuk be of service? This one has many fine wares.
The prisoner has paid the blood price for his crimes.
You've done a great service to Greenhill. I'd love to talk, but I really have to finish this inventory.
Merani is really improving her archery skills, don't you think?
Sharp claws, this one is very glad Ezreba will stay with us. She is a bright moon in our sky.
Heard what you decided. Glad Ezreba's going to stick around. Like that cat.
You torment me even in death!
Kada wishes you a bright day and pleasant journeys.
You have done us a great service. May the forest always provide for you.
Thalar cannot offer you enough thanks.
Where is Trela? She was supposed to pick up her meats.
The prisoner has paid the blood price for her crimes.
You monster! My murder wasn't enough?
The prisoner has paid the blood price for her crimes.
Necromancy? Beast! Defiler! Arkay hound you to your grave.
The prisoner has paid the blood price for her crimes.
I hate you. I hate you so much. Why would you do this to me?
Did you make it to Haynote?
Well, you got the job done, though you were gentler than I would've been.
I'll never trust the Midnight Union again, I can tell you that.
I can't hold him for long. Go, before he overtakes me. Tell my master we were successful.
Quickly, return to the courtyard. <<1>> must know of our success.
I heard about Bruma. Sounds like Hafza is out of business. Maybe we should give up on this place altogether.
This day has just gone from bad to worse.
Good job in the Haven my friend. That'll make these seas safe for once.
Thanks to you, we'll be able to float the Prowler off this beach at the next high tide.
Ah, to see out of Khajiit eyes again! Zur hates being caged in that dark place.
What are you doing? Kill that thing before it eats me alive!
Hey there. Buy something, for old time's sake?
Hey, good looking. Long time.
Well, now. What brings you to our humble abode?

Well look who's here. The hero of Betnikh! 

If you've come to recruit me, I must decline. I'm done sailing, and there's a rich Breton noble over there who could really use a friend.

Take care of yourself.
Fancy meeting you here. Glad to see you doing well. This is a class above the Screaming Mermaid, I'll give it that.
Now you're a welcome sight!\n\nI'd chat, but Captain Marck has me testing all the rigging before we set sail again. I'd imagine the debacle at Koeglin Lighthouse made him a bit more cautious.
Well look who it is. Well met, my friend!
Oh, it's you. Yeah, I'm not interesting in talking. Go bug Mekag.

I had not expected to see you again! I'm glad you're still alive.\n\nIt was a hard choice, staying with Kaleen or Lambur. Ultimately, I'm doing more serving Fahara'jad than I would as a sword for hire.
If it isn't my fine partner from our expedition in Betnikh.

I think I'm just about done with Neramo. All we've done since I joined him is talk about expeditions, not actually join any.\n\nStill, a berth is a berth. I'll stay with Captain Marck until I find something better.
You! Get out of here. I don't want to see you ever again!
Well met, my friend. You look well.
Well now, a familiar face. How good to see you. Honestly, I'm beginning to wonder if I'm on the wrong ship.
We're here! Daggerfall! At last!\n\nNow I just need to convince Telonil that a cafe is the right investment.
My friend, good to see you! See this hand? It works again. Found a very talented healer in Aldcroft who put the bones right back together.\n\nI've put my sword through a few Elves since. Felt good.
Well now, look who it is. The hero of Betnikh.\n\nI'd wondered if we'd see you again some day. Guess I was right. Lambur owes me dinner.
Oh, it's my dear, brave friend from Stros M'Kai. What a pleasure to see you again.
You are brave to face Kaleen once more. I am glad you have come. She needs more around her who are not blinded by patriotism.
Ah. I erect the spine of respect.
Turn back. You aren't welcome here.
I heard what you said about Grida. Is it true?
Thank you again. I am very much looking forward to returning to my wife.\n\nI hope she will be as happy to see me.
Thank you, again … I hope you understand my confusion. I have waited and mourned so long.\n\nI feel I should be angry at him, but I am just … I am just so happy right now.
Never seen you here before. Just got drafted? What'll you have?
Thank you again. I had forgotten what it feels like to feel free.
No idea what to do with this horse. Fertilizer, perhaps?

Sylvain's fertilizer always doubles my yield. And it smells like roses to boot. Just between you and me, I sometimes roll around in it before spreading it in the field. Sure beats taking my monthly bath.
One day I'll escape from this blasted temple. I'll scour all of Tamriel until I find you. Then, I'll turn you into a hat.
Greetings and welcome to the Mages Guild Hall! What is it that you have there?
If you found me, someone else will. I will be ready.
That doll was my only toy as a child. We had hundreds of adventures together. Being reunited with her has brought me more joy than you can imagine.
I fear that justice would have been better served by my death. \n\nI pray your judgment does not prove to be a mistake for the future of the Covenant.
If you're lost, Cropsford is northeast of here. If you hit Drakelowe Keep, you've gone too far.
If you see Niro again, tell him—very politely, please—that I'll handle it. He doesn't need to worry, and he certainly doesn't need to come here and see me.
I hoped Hisham would be with you, if I saw you again. Fool is still clinging to his dream of farm life.

When I went to sea with Captain Kaleen, I didn't expect it to be quite so lonely. I miss my home. I wonder if I made the right choice.\n\nStill, I'm staying with Lambur. I took this path, and I won't step aside now.

You know, it's strange how memories keep coming back to me. When we first arrived in Wayrest, I didn't remember it at all. Now I'm remembering all sorts of things.\n\nI think I've found a place here with Captain Marck. I owe that to you.
We've a lot to do, rebuilding the camp. But it beats having our innards ripped out by Daedra.
It's a relief to study without the constant demands of the Covenant military. I could not care less about Cyrodiil and Emeric's damned war.
The Crowns have been pushing King Fahara'jad. They seek to ban any Guild member that studies in Eyevea from working with the military. It's just as well, if you ask me.

Ah, wayfarer. Eyevea is like a dream come true! Especially the tradescraft! It's so easy to gather spell components! Do you have any idea how expensive it is to import frost herbs through to Alik'r desert?
A centralized, readily accessible, and above all neutral port for every nation in Tamriel. Research aside, the trading opportunities here are amazing!

You know, if the Guild plays its cards right …. Just think of all the coin we could make in trade. We could find ourselves in a very good position. If the Cyrodiil situation ever stabilizes, of course.

High King Emeric knows well how to play the diplomat. While officially he's been neutral on the topic of Eyevea, he's privately been highly supportive. He knows Guildmaster Vanus values his friendship.
Guildmaster Vanus asked me personally to come! Said he wanted to be sure our kin were represented in the heart of the guild. Can you imagine?
Hah! This place is amazing! Some High Elf just got done telling me, where she comes from, they respect their Mages. Coming to Eyevea feels like coming home.
Me maw cried when I left to come here. Said I'd been stolen by Elves and wizards, and that I'd end up a slave in Oblivion. Hah! As if I could ever be a Daedra's slave!
Ah, a civilized magical society. I've put so many faces to names I've only seen in letters. It will be nice to speak frankly about our craft. And not be the "town seer." Hah!
I've heard the whispers, seen the looks. Some think us Nords are a poor fit for magic. I say, clearly someone has to keep the rest of these fools in line. Hah!

Ahh, adept! This morning I got into an argument with one of those shortie Elves. He was arguing that magic is the most efficient solution to any problem. So I punched him in the face!\n\nWe're going for drinks later. I like this place.
I would have thought Eyevea's return would call out more of our brethren from House Telvanni. But no. Perhaps someday this neutral ground will help draw them back into the fold.
The Tribunal takes a longer view on the conflicts in Cyrodiil. The Three approve of our presence on Eyevea. Sotha Sil himself hopes for a chance to visit, I hear!

The centuries of hatred between my people and … most of Tamriel seems somehow petty in a place like this. There's so much to be gained through collaboration. Perhaps one day, Dark Elves will walk proudly in the lands outside Morrowind.
A secluded island, just for Mages, where we can all do our work in peace. Free from the outside world's politics and horrors. Really? No one else sees this gilded tree for its rotten roots?
My colleagues think this place is far too good to be true. I'm hopeful. I choose to let the river take us where it wants.
This experiment is doomed to failure, mark my words. You've seen the Dark Elves here, right? "All Mages are equals" is a bitter root in my mouth.
This one is so happy to be here! Such an excellent idea. And such delightful fragrances! Sharp claws and Bright Moons to you, adept-who-has-made-this-happen.
Eyevea was a myth, told to tiny Mage cubs. Now you have reached into the past, and legend, and pulled it into the real world. More nonsense like this sounds like an excellent idea!

This one hears others worry about how long Eyevea will last. What does it matter? Gain everything you can now, and worry about whether it will last later. Spend time worrying and you waste the time you have.
Eyevea is ideally placed. A remote but accessible location for the elite to congregate. Well away from the chaos of mainland Tamriel. If you ask me, this is a long overdue asset for the Guild.
Fivefold venerations, adept. All of our people feel great pride in Valaste, for the role she played in your adventure. In her name, High Elves across Tamriel plan to donate tomes to Eyevea's library.
Stars above, Eyevea is a High Elven dream. We gain all the benefits of collaboration with the other races without having to … you know. Actually leave the Summerset Isles. Ideal!
I love this place! I can actually get into real, lively debates about arcano-magical phenomenon. Nothing defers to my wisdom or tries to change the subject.\n\nA Nord even hit me. Amazing!
Being here is quite invigorating, adept. I've been a Greenspeaker for so long …. I'd forgotten you could cast spells to harness fire, or change the weather, or even summon an angry Daedra. Amazing!

After living deep in the Valenwood all my life, it's such a difference to be here on Eyevea. I can see the sky, smell the sea air … I didn't expect allergies, though. Something about these mushrooms …. Choo!
I can't believe you let her stay. The Green damn you, traveler! A cancer at the heart of our wood.
Comrade. It is good to speak with you again.
Just leave me to die. I wouldn't accept your help and you'd be better off not offering.

Thank you for the sand. Sometimes, after a long day, I miss my life with Rasha. Travelling where our whims took us, living by our swords, seeing exciting places every day. But the Way of the Sword is no longer my path.
This one has heard reports. You've kept busy. Good! You fit in now more than ever. \n\nHow did things go?
So, have you decided to help us against the evil Wood Elves?

As far as I can tell, the lamias and the Wood Elves don't get along very well. Even though the snake thing saved me, I'm not sure we can trust either of them.\n\nStill, they may be your best chance for finding a way into this tower.
Kazirra will be very interested in hearing about all this.
The people of Arenthia owe you a great debt, traveler. You will always be welcome within the walls of our city. But your tale does not end here, I think.
You! Yes, you! <<1>> needs you, immediately!
This is an outrage! I demand <<1>> be taken into custody!
We'll take the marines with us when we sail to <<1>>. I hope to see you there.
Any luck securing a copy of the treaty?
The Dominion must understand our position. The free people of <<1>> cannot make enemies with one hand and friends with the other.
She's going to stay. I can't believe you and Bowenas believe she can change! Once you've touched that kind of darkness. The Green take you both!
It doesn't matter. The tempest is coming. Nothing can stop it, not even … her.
<<1>>'s inside resting. You have five minutes.
Ambassador <<1>> isn't here. And if he was, he'd be far too busy to entertain the likes of you.
Is it over? We can stay? I almost find it had to believe.\n\nThank you though. You have no idea how much.
If you've come to tell me I'm going to lose my leg, just turn around and leave.
Balag noticed that you are still here. I can help you with something more?
What have we here? Another would-be champion? \n\nLet me guess. You've come to honor us with a display of prowess mere mortals could only dream of possessing.
There's so much more to learn about Ayleid wells. Unlocking their mysteries will lead to greater understanding of the Ayleids themselves, I'm sure.
The privy is back beyond the gate. Or did you need something else?
Hello my lovely. This is quite the year for talent, as well as beauty.
Thank Akatosh you found my new robes. If I heard another joke about my "holey robes," I think I would have stabbed someone.
Take a tip, friend. Don't stay long in Bruma.
I have digging to do and you're in my way.
Who is this, now? A paying customer, here to cheer on the combatants? Or are you something more?

There's no way I can properly thank you for what you've done. This is the first good luck my clan's had in months. This means we can stay here and start over.\n\nWherever you go, and whatever you do, you'll always be a champion of the Driladan.
I can't afford to wait here much longer. I came to help assist those fleeing the darkness in the forest, but very few have come this way.\n\nI hope this does not mean they have all simply perished.
My silver flute has a much sweeter tone than the one I've been using. I'll be able to lift some spirits with this in hand!
I'm lucky you wandered by when you did. But then again, I'm always lucky.
Thought I was ruined, but that <<1>> says <<2>> will pay for the kwama to live in that cave.\n\nI'm not above taking coin from crazy folk. Might even be enough to repair my ship!
Well, you're back but I know what you're going to say, so don't bother. Cousin Asvorn won't give me any more money. That smug, cheap bastard.
Thank you for news of Tertius. I won't sleep easy until he's back with word of Donus.
You honor me with your presence, walker.
If you touched anything, you'll answer to me.

A great wind blew, and many ships were dashed against Khenarthi's island. But you strengthened the Great Tree, despite her anger! <<1>> thrives once more.\n\nMay your actions show Khenarthi our goal is righteous. May she bless us with favorable winds.
My no-good cousin's not getting any more gold out of me!
You again? Please, I have nothing more to say about it.
MmmMMmmf MMMF!
Please let me know if you find anything. Even if it's just something that confirms she's gone, knowing would be better than this.

Why are you wasting time? My father did not instruct you to relax here and then go after the Withered Hand ….\n\nYou are Ash'abah now. You have a job to do. Go to Tu'whacca's Throne. We will see each other again soon enough.
The Wood Elves have fallen. My eggs shall be returned to my nest and my people shall be safe.\n\nThe Shadow Walkers shall be lost without their leaders. The day is ours!
So you've returned! I thank you again for your help in the Hollow. Dracien and Bakkhara are lost, but I am pleased we remain to tell their stories.
I hope Hannura appreciated the fish. I like to send her some as often as I can.
Plenty of salvage in a town like this; think I'll stick around for a while longer. That dead messenger will slow Marcellus down.
The fish you brought will make a nice meal. Perhaps I should invite some friends over to share.
I know this may not be the way you would normally deal with a problem, but it's the only way to make my clan trust you.\n\nNow, let's go and cause as much chaos as we can!
Begone, bandit. I'll never join <<1>>!
This one … feels odd.
I hope Jafola makes it out of Bruma alive. That town's a sinking ship.
Saldir becomes less reliable all the time. I need to find a new supplier. The wounded here can't wait for Saldir to saunter into town.
I quiver like a leaf in the wind to think of what we'll learn from these ruins.\n\nWe'll be careful, of course. It would be unfortunate to allow something like this to happen again.
I don't know how I feel about these strange bugs. But if <<1>> doesn't mind, who am I to disagree?
What did you see in that temple? I heard it's full of watery spirits!
So much destruction! Thank goodness you were here to help rebuild the ship!
Greetings, O my friend. You are most welcome in our home. Without your intervention, the city might well have been lost.
The docks have been reclaimed?  We are so grateful. \n\nMy father is a kind-hearted man, and without imports the city would starve. I wish the Crowns could see that.
Tu'whacca bless you. Some may name you heretic for striking our risen dead, but in this house you are a hero. Be welcome.
It is our duty as Ash'abah to assist the king if he calls upon us. I only wish he had called on us earlier. \n\nPerhaps this terrible poisoning could have been avoided.
I heard rumors of rats and all manner of lunacy in the Mad God's chateau. How dreadful! We're glad to have you back in Tamriel, safe and sound. Do you need to restock on any provisions?
Cordial greetings and welcome to our tower—an isle of knowledge amidst a vast sea of ignorance.  \n\nHave you come for training?
Well met. I'm the resident librarian. We don't have much, but what we have I care for. \n\nHave you found anything to add to our collection?
Greetings. You stand in the Sentinel Mages Guildhall.  \n\nThis one is curious: what do you have there?
I believe Talia has finished … mixing the potion for your initiation. Speak to her when you are ready to begin the trial.\n\nMay Tu'whacca guide your path, initiate … always.
Welcome, wayfarer. Your exploits on the docks are known to me, but I know that your ways are not our ways. \n\nYou may sit and take rest in our hall, however, and partake of our services.
The Stone Table. Quickly!
This business at the docks gets worse by the hour. If those shambling dungpiles come much farther up the beach we may have to do something about it.
Even if I can save some of these wounded, the Imperials will just kill them another time.

To Oblivion with kwama egg mining. I've worked out a deal with Shatasha to rent the ruins to the Mages Guild for research. \n\nIf that lost city is as big as she says it is, I should be well-off for quite a while.
We fought well, didn't we? I think we might just have a chance at turning this disaster into a successful operation.
You heard Sangur. Get going.\n\nI'm sure I'll be around when you return.
What happened?
Don't judge me. I had a moment of weakness. It won't happen a third time, I promise!
Next time I'm given a mission, you know I'll come looking for you. Be ready, my friend.
Ho there! Can't let you in here.
Oh, hey. Look, you really need to move on. I just need a break, that's all.
Is there anything I can get you? A drink? A little bit of my time?
Hey, thanks for the ale! Don't let me catch you around here again, or something.
Go on, use the portal and get out of here. We'll wait a few more moments for any stragglers that want to escape.
You seem determined to make yourself useful. What strange habits you mortals have.
You're a fool, and you've doomed another fool to unspeakable torment.\n\nIt's no longer my concern. I'll depart this world soon enough.
This war will kill us all, I feel it in my bones.
Do you have my ring?
It'll be tough going without the Captain. Command never really suited me.
Good luck, friend. Save a few ogrims for us. We'll meet you upstairs as soon as we can.
I have no idea why <<1>> would seal himself into that creature's tomb.\n\nBut I suppose he won't be around to undermine my experiments. Hmm!
I didn't think we were going to make it. Thank you.
There, you see? You fit in and no one will stop you from walking away.
You saved many lives today. Azsu will remember you.
A shame the shrine is no longer kindled since the spirit departed. <<1>> will remain here for a little bit, in case the flame returns.
I hear you've done good work, recruit. Once we're off this island, I'll put your name in for a medal.
Speak of Namiira. Our specialist!\n\n<<1>> was just commenting on the difficulties pests present to any plantation. We'll be rid of these vermin in short order, yes? Of course, yes.

Oh! One more thing—Andur scouted out the Orcs' Camp pretty extensively. He might have some useful observations if you ask.\n\nGood luck with the Wood Orcs … and that tricky treethane. Maybe we'll meet again when we find the Wilderking.

You seem to be rather sharp, so I will not pretend that everything is all right.\n\nThe king is dealing with a crisis that threatens his hold on the throne. I would not bother him unless you are willing to help.
I'm still a little banged up, but we'll do our best to rally the troops and meet you upstairs.
Quite the view from up here, don't you think?\n\nIf only the company was equally enjoyable.

If this works, I'll owe the gods an apology. Fill the blood rune and then use it on the three seals.\n\nAfter that, we'll have to deal with the Binding Pool. Hopefully, I'll have figured this out by then. I'll meet you up at the gate to the pool.
Gone … father is gone. Why would <<1>> destroy his own family?\n\nPlease, leave me to my sorrow.
<<1>> knows you'll succeed.\n\nYou hear that, lazy senche? This one could replace the lot of you with <<cm:2>>!
It seems Akkhuz-ri may have hope here. Kazirra mentioned forgiveness, and perhaps helping to rebuild Arenthia will aid this one in atonement.
Well, that was more exciting than Tarrami anticipated!
I've never been more scared. I can't believe <<1>> wants to execute us.
I'm still shaking. <<1>> gave us the death penalty.
Leave me be. The loss of my brother is … difficult to bear.
We're all so grateful to you for freeing us. We were in over our heads.
Nice to see Fort Rayles in Dominion hands. I feel safer already.
You were born under sign of the Lady, weren't you? I can always tell. Buy me a drink, gorgeous?
I should really go check on my father.
Thanks! I'm getting out of here!
I came here to get away from the war. But I see you and the Dominion have brought it to my doorstep.
Yes, yes, the Dominion has taken Fort Rayles. Makes no difference to me. You all track in the same amount of dirt.
This one rejoices that Fort Rayles is in Dominion hands. Honor to you for any part you played in this!
It's about time the Pact took Fort Rayles. Be nice to see new faces in town.
You must leave the moment you are ready. The Ansei Wards are gone and the Withered Hand has already taken to the desert winds. Go now and mete out the king's justice.
Speak to my fellow elders and state your case.\n\nWe will convene when you are done to discuss our options.
Good to see you here. With the Pact in Fort Rayles, I hope things settle down around here. I could use the rest.
Welcome! Saw some Pact soldiers heading toward Rayles. I hope to see a lot more Nord faces around here.

Well met, champion. Your deeds on the docks have done the city a service. You take a great risk in striking the Ra-Netu, but perhaps Tu'whacca's curse does not extend to outsiders. Bah! A matter for priests.
So, the Pact took over Fort Rayles. As long as no historical sites were ruined, I don't care who holds that place.
Now that Fort Rayles is in Pact hands, I hope I get some peace and quiet around here.
When is the Covenant going to take back Fort Rayles?
About time the Covenant started showing up. Fort Rayles needs to be retaken!
For the honor of the Covenant, Fort Rayles must be retaken!
Why hasn't Fort Rayles been retaken? Has the Covenant no more swords?
A lapse in control leads to smugglers brewing skooma. If there's reason, I'll recommend Headwoman <<1>> shut this plantation down.
This one never thought you could best Tholbor, Zara, and Malarel. She is looking forward to ending your lucky streak.
Apparently my husband Farrokh does not know how to bar a door. We dare not go out while our ancestors still walk. \n\nI have asked Tu'whacca for intercession. All we have is prayer now.
Walk with care. Tu'whacca's will has been defied at the docks, and his vengeance will be terrible indeed.
You did the right thing.
We're going to start over. We'll build a better life.
Once we control the portal, we can control the first section of the Chasm.
I wish I could go with you. I'm worried about my companions who've gone inside, but the priestess won't allow me to go in after them.
A magic force bubble? Really? \n\nThanks for getting my brother out of that mess.
Mara be praised! We truly cannot thank you enough for the return of these relics. Walk with Her blessing, feel Her smile on your face, and know always She will be with you.
How strange this feels! To be simply Zur again is … lonely.
I am grateful that you chose to save me. Still, I feel a bit lost. I wish … I wish Zur was still here.
If you can destroy the four focus stones, then we'll be able to control the portal and hold the first segment of the Chasm.
I'm ready to face anything, even the Dremora guarding this Chasm. But Akatosh preserve me, I have a profound fear of heights.
Make sure you destroy all four focus stones, or this war ends here and now. Our mages can't take control of the portal to the second tier while the stones are active.
The forbidden tomes cannot be allowed to cause more harm. Please, you must bring them to the shrine where they can be destroyed.
Move along, move along. I'd prefer if you didn't dawdle around here.
Move along, soldier. Keep this gate open for new arrivals.
Ah, you return to Zan! The siege range is yours to use, walker. Speak with Firamo or Miniel to refresh your memory of how siege weaponry works.
Covered my tracks. Couldn't have found me!
We came here hoping to establish a Dominion naval base, but our "forest of sails" turned into a graveyard.
May Jone and Jode watch over the town of Greenhill, and her people.
You're going to think I'm wandering in my wits, but I could swear I just saw an Orc run through here—wearing nothing but his underclothes!
You did an excellent job! Thanks to you, I was able to complete the ritual and end the vampiric threat once and for all.
May the Bright Moons light your path, Hallowed. You should know, there is an additional task you could undertake. It might improve your chances at Moonmont.
While this temple has been disturbed by outsiders, the light of Jone and Jode still shines down upon it. That cannot be said of all places on Khenarthi's Roost.

Only the dead and the desperate end up in this part of the desert. You are a Redguard, so I would think you know this … either way, you must be a very brave soul. \n\nDo you intend to enter the cursed grounds, the Tears of the Dishonored?
You're just … going to abandon me?
Whatever it is, it can wait. We need to get out of here!
Consult the mission boards for Grand Warlord Sorcalin's latest orders, soldier.
One may fear ghosts, but this one fears starvation more. Give but a little time, and a shop of such wonders will be set up!
I'm busy here. Don't waste my time, soldier.
You resemble a leaf in a tempest, unsure where to turn next. If you need training to find your path, I can help.
Welcome back. Use the siege weapons, if you need practice.
If you're skipping training, head out onto the battlefields and help the Covenant conquer Cyrodiil.
You seem in need of guidance. If you wish to know more of warfare in Cyrodiil, I can start you on the path.
The Harvest Heart has been destroyed. My children are no longer slaves to Molag Bal!
So you are the walker who saved Laughing Moons! <<m:1>>, yes? How novel!\n\nTo think some consider them pests!
Are you ready for the next round?
Are you ready for the next round?
Are you ready for the next round?
Are you ready for the next round?
I'm sorry. I don't have you signed up for a fight at the moment.
Are you ready for the next round?
Are you ready for the next round?
Are you ready for the next round?
Are you ready for the next round?
<Talania Priscus has died.>
Thanks again for getting me out of that bubble of force. \n\nI don't suppose you're coming back to Bravil with us? I feel safer with you around.
Thanks again, friend. \n\nI'm still seeing crocodiles behind every boulder. Brrr.
We're going to camp here until everyone is rested, and then we'll return to Bravil and the chapel.
To Moonmont then, yes? I will try to keep Khali from rushing headlong into danger until you arrive.
We shall see you at Moonmont, my Hallowed.
Please inform the mages that I'll be with them shortly. I know they'll be disappointed, but I need to have a few words with the Groundskeeper, first.
What have they done to my farm? Why would they do this? Animals!
I don't know if I can do what the Veiled Heritants want me to.
Comfortable? Then let's begin. Look deep into the embers as you listen to my voice.
This is not good news.
My homeland ablaze, and the guild split asunder. I never thought I'd live to see the day.
Unbelievable. To think … Ra'zaym was recruited into the guild by Colors herself. To sit here, hear what has been said ….
Were it solely up to me, I'd have her head on a pike.
I bet things are going to get really interesting around here.
We'll contact you again soon, my friend. As soon as we have word of Sees-All-Colors. You can count on it.
When you have collected three gems, you may go to the top of the pyramid to complete the Trial of Spirit.
The statues at the top of this pyramid are dedicated to the challenges we face every day.
The statues dedicated to the challenges we face on a daily basis await you at the top of the pyramid.
I cannot believe she went through with it! \n\nAll I can say is thank Ruptga that I have other daughters. I will not even allow them to talk to Forebears!
You have begun your journey, pilgrim. Ahead lies danger. For now, you face only the light of the moons. Breathe deep of the moon-sugar vapors and open your minds to the Path.
I will gather an immediate accounting of events from those on duty. You had best give the news to the queen.
Ha! This'll make a real story, next time I'm drinking with the other Vinedusk. Thanks for the helping hand.
After he returns to Bramblebreach, Hazazi will request a transfer.
I'll make my way to the Hollow City after I've rested.
I think next I'm going to take my team and go do a nice safe dig on a beach in Auridon. Maybe we'll dig for, you know … clams!
Poke around the camp a bit more. Somebody must know what's eating at Gudarz.
Did I challenge you to a duel? I did, didn't I? Please accept my sincerest apology! \n\nI get a bit feisty when I'm drinking mead.
What a timely arrival. You appear quite well-armed. My mages and I could have a great use for you.
You're the guy who helped killed those wolves! Thank you so much!
I don't know what I'm going to do with myself. Maybe I'll join Naerion's team, if she'll have me. Find someplace nice and quiet to dig. Don't know ….
It's strange. In Coldharbour, my only thought was not of the Daedra, but what if I never saw Galandir again?
Ah, Tamriel! Fresh air, warmth, lower mortality rate; the whole package. I'm heading back to Firsthold, so visit me if you're in the area!
This "Selene" sounds like the ringleader for these Bosmer cowards. Before the day is done, I'll have her killed.\n\nI don't care what Carindon thinks he's researching.
The Bosmer will pay for what they did to the honored Patraud.

These Bosmer are feral, mindless. This "Selene" could be controlling them. There is a powerful blanket of magic covering everything in this forest.\n\nI'm glad our wits are still our own. I intend them to remain that way, if today is to be my last.
Two Mages dead and not a single forest spirit in sight.
There is a potent magical energy beyond this barrier of vines. Maybe it's Carindon's fabled spirit, maybe it's this "Selene." \n\nEither way, I'm not returning to the Guild hall empty-handed.
I'm not sure about this but Warlock Carindon seems to know what he is doing.
Two of my colleagues have returned to the Root so that the rest of us could stand here.\n\nI will honor their memories.
No way I'm going to let Uncle return those relics without me. I bled for this cause. I'm going to see it through.
Without the aid of the local tribes, our power here will remain weak. I hope the Bramblebreach will be but the first to join us.
Always good to see some fresh faces around here. You're welcome to go on in.
Those who honor the ancient Yokudan traditions are always welcome here.
Selene's menace has been neutralized. We are free to dissect and study her.\n\nI had thought the day lost, but this is exquisite.
By Tava's red feathers, these Crowns are foolish, arrogant, and intransigent—but it does my heart good to know that they are not all cold-blooded murderers.
Only in a town patroled by Crowns could this miserable business occur. \n\nIf our brother king exerted more pressure here, this tragedy might have been avoided.
A thousand deaths to the Withered Hand! \n\nTell our brothers and sisters to draw their long knives and ask Onsi's blessing. We Crowns have a new enemy.
I'm going to take Lorwen with us when we go to return the bones. I figure she has some blood in this now, right? I don't think she'd let me leave her behind, either.
Blessings of Tu'whacca be with you. Alas, we have much to do before meting out vengeance to the Withered Hand.
You look weary from the desert sun, and I sense you bear an added weight. \n\nWe Dunmer know about such things.
Necromancy in Bergama? As if we mages did not face enough distrust. Once again, magic must be to blame. Terrible news.
Get out of here … it's not safe.
Please, leave me alone.
Welcome to the Vile Manse.\n\nDo you come to aid me?
By Onsi's bright blade! We don't see many warriors of your stature here in Bergama. Welcome to the guildhall.
Praise Alkosh—the Dominion controls every castle in Cyrodiil! The Warfront board currently has no missions. Consult the other boards for work to be done.

I give thanks to Ruptga for your intercession, wayfarer. Distrust between Crown and Forebear still runs canyon deep, but distrust is not hatred. \n\nYokuda lives in all of us—we must strive to remember it.

I heard the commotion out there and somehow knew it was you. It is good and good to see you, my illustrious friend.\n\nYour arrival comes at a fortuitous time, as we are indeed in dire straits. And it will soon get much, much worse.
Good to be alive today, yes? Fresh goods for you today!
These bags are made in far-off Auridon! What do you say?
Ah, so nice to see people of culture in charge of a city. What can I help you with?
Zetisha has cleaned house. Only Arenthia soldiers, Dominion allies under this roof!
What happened to us?
Did you find my lute? I feel almost naked without it.
We celebrate now, yes? Brew your own or try some of this one's!
We must feast, for we are alive! This one will help you.
We should give the students a moment to rest.
This one will meet you in Skywatch. This one is not worried. He knows there's nothing we cannot handle.
So nice to be back under the eagle banner. What can I get for you?
Who are you? You don't look like a member of the Mages Guild.
This one is offering discount to everyone who fought on our side! She did not see you, but there is still much we can discuss.
Happy to buy, happy to sell.
It is good to see more faces from the Pact in Cropsford. Perhaps we will be safer now.
This one is supposed to tell you that she was neutral in this conflict. In truth? She is very grateful to be beneath the eagle banner again.
As long as you're not here to force me into the army, the Covenant's welcome to Drakelowe Keep.
Now that was some fighting! Managed to get out there and smash a few of the Colovians when no one was watching. Hah! Get you something?
The eagle banner flies again. Good.

The hour of our glory is nigh! Razum-dar forewarned me of your coming, and I have considered our circumstances carefully in light of that.\n\nI have the utmost faith in your capabilities, and I am confident that your arrival is an augur of our victory.
Time to do what we do best, yes? This should be fun.
They … they took my wife.
He'll be all right. We've suffered through worse.
This one is so grateful. Now Ahirunz can find the will to survive.\n\nIf it takes me an eternity, this one shall find a way to return to our children.
My Queen …. I've failed you ….
The <<1>> is just beyond this door, but it's barred from the other side. You need to go all the way around.
It's so good to see a familiar face in this dreadful wilderness. I appreciate that you climbed that tower to rescue me. \n\nA little longer and who knows what Drasilla would have made me do!
I just wanted to keep the dream alive. The dream of my Aldmeri Dominion ….
Ruptga's blessings be upon you, wayfarer. We Crowns move slowly and deliberately—perhaps too slowly at times. Thank you for exposing that pawn of the Withered Hand.
Ahh, good to have our city back again. Damned too-talls, always looking down on us folk.
Thanks unto the Divines for bringing you to Bergama. Dihoq and I were a vulture's wing-beat from poisoning each other!
Well, the King certainly doesn't lack confidence. I can appreciate that. Might put our friend here in his place.\n\nThat'd be delightful to see.
Tu'whacca's breath, what a relief these kidnapings were solved. \n\nOf course, the Withered Hand is still out there, so I suppose I should dry my mouth lest I bring a curse on us.

If you happen to run into any of the workers out there, you tell them they better get their behinds back in here.\n\nI don't care if there are necromancers, zombies, or what … if they don't get back to work, I'm docking last week's pay!

Blasphemy! The Elder Scroll of Mnem has been stolen from our temple. I can tell you of the Elder Scrolls, but you will not feel their holy presence until our scroll returns. Perhaps you can help, once you complete your training.

As you can see, this is a horrible place. They just dump the bodies anywhere, and the predators, these harpies, come to feed on the corpses. \n\nMy Zariya … she does not deserve this. She has done nothing wrong!
Dumac take you, Covenant filth—you, these damn necromancers, and this whole damn desert!\n\nIf my sword arm weren't broken, I'd skin you like a netch!
I hope you find her. I don't know what I'll do if she's not in Vlastarus.
A draft of last year's census went missing just days ago. If my carelessness aided the Withered Hand with these murders … aiyah, I could swallow a sword.
I can't wait to see Eneriell again!
I've served the Magistrate for years. She's not capable of murder! \n\nThere must be some mistake. There must be.
Our Justice is innocent. He will not abide in those stocks for long, I swear it.
We've suspected the Magistrate for years. Embezzlement, paper-crime, and the like. \n\nEven so, I never would have thought her capable of this.
Please hurry. Angiente is not a patient man!
You see Fabanil, tell him not to bother showing up. I never want to see that fool's face again!
Comfortable? Then let's begin. Look deep into the embers as you listen to my voice.
I'll have a good life here, if you remain quiet about my gift.
Our Magistrate consorts with defilers of our dead? This is the ultimate betrayal. \n\nNeed you any more proof that Forebears are not fit to rule?
The Magistrate is the hand of our Forebear king, and she consorts with necromancers? \n\nFahara'jad's rule continues to bring nothing but ruin.
This talk of war … I thought we were done. We got Vanus back. Why can't we just go home?
Later, mate. I got me some killing to do.
So the Magistrate is to blame for all this kidnaping brouhaha? \n\nIn a town this brutish and rustic … one sympathizes.
Well? Did you find Klovag? Is he coming?
I have not the heart to look at the names of the dead. My son was so troubled. I had so much I wanted to tell him.
The Maormer are practically beasts. There are stories about them to make the fur stand on end!
I hear you've been helping the fleet recover from the storm. My family owns a shipping line, yet even I would be hard pressed to work so swiftly when the pressure is on. Bravo.
Sounds like you'll be having some fun of your own.
There were survivors? That's great news! I'm sure no one will mind a few dead miners once they see my trolls in action at the arena!
This one misses Kargand so much. He was always able to bring a smile to this Khajiit's face. His death has left a hole in this one's heart.
Long and long I have seen Sulma's sidelong glances, her nervous paper shuffling. This betrayal is not a surprise. \n\nSadly, I deem her replacement will be no better.
We get invaded, and everybody thinks it's a reason to slack. Not on Tohiba's watch!
Have you seen the Magistrate since her arrest? I suspect she won't live through the night.
Hurry up now! You were the one who said we did not have much time!
This one thinks he is doing better. The voices still speak to Kargand but this Khajiit can ignore them.
So Istah was telling the truth, huh? Don't matter to me—so long as our customers stay alive long enough to pay their debts.
Hhmph. Raz is still angry you disobeyed him. But some of the moon priests here have been most informative about dealing with the circlet from Senalana. Some day, Raz may forgive you.
Sulma had no stone in her bones. If the Withered Hand wishes Bergama razed, let them come. By Onsi's bright blade, I will slay ten and ten before I fall.
Thank you for saving us! If you hadn't come along … well. I expect I'll wake up screaming for the next few years.
It is settled. We shall cross the Chasm and make our way to the planar vortex at the heart of Molag Bal's realm.\n\nNow that you know the plan, I have a special request to make of you.
With the Champions prepared, the Dominion itself begins to heal. We're going to make our way to Dune. The Two Moons Path awaits! I'll see you there, my friend.
Have to hire from Valenwood, find some new dupes to work the delve, and … excuse me! I'm very busy here!
I heard that the Magis … Magit … the, uh, Judge? She's been killing folks? That's a cryin' shame. Better tuck in another pint. Y'know, drowning sorrows … and such.
Good luck, Hallowed. I'm sure I'll see you again soon.
We shall see you at Dune, then. I look forward to our next conversation.
I look forward to speaking again at Dune, Hallowed. May the Green keep you safe as you do the work of the Bright Moons.

Damn shame about the Magistrate, eh? I heard she might even have been cutting deals with the Withered Hand. \n\nThe good news is that the next Magistrate might be even worse, so Samhudah's keeping me on the payroll. How's that for a happy ending?
Thank you for not slaughtering my people back in the forest.\n\nI've decided that I can no longer live like I was. I'm going to join you in your fight. I'm going to get back to Tamriel.
I heard a rumor the Magistrate was feeding the bodies of our departed friends to the risen dead. Tava's red feathers, I can't think of a worse fate than that.
I saw how annoyed she looked! Well done!

So it was the Magistrate who killed all those poor devils? She looks a bit waifish for that sort of work, but I suppose you never can tell. \n\nUncle Thakh won't be happy, at any rate. The dead rarely pay their debts.

You appeared to enjoy the power I gave you. I, too, know how exhilarating the power of death and darkness can be.\n\nAll this and more can be yours whenever you want it. If you join me in this campaign.
Did you recover the sword? We must speak before you go further with it.
I extend the claw of welcome, warrior.

Scourge take them! The Elder Scroll of Chim has been stolen! I can tell you of the Elder Scrolls, but you will not feel their holy presence until our scroll returns. Perhaps you can help, once you complete your training.
I haven't seen my husband since the Dominion attacked. I wonder if he's all right.
I'm a fisherman, not a warrior! I can't take all this bloodshed.

As if we Forebears weren't hated enough, our Magistrate falls in with Tu'whacca's mortal enemy. \n\nI am thinking it is better to walk back to Sentinel with a broken sandal than to stay in Bergama much longer.

So the Magistrate was responsible for all this nonsense? My, my, my. What a dreadful development. \n\nI can't say that I'll miss the attention. Being an outsider while a murdering spree takes place is … unpleasant.
You look like you have something weighing heavy on your mind. Need a good drink to wash it away?
The faster you return with the blood, the faster you get your antidote. And trust me, it's not something you want to put off for too long.
Did you know this town has mead? They'll even feed it to dogs who ask nicely. Good choice, saving these people. Or whatever it is you did. You should've mentioned the mead before.
The hero of the cliffs returns in triumph! I do hope you didn't get too disheveled down there. Fighting alongside the peasants can be rather unpleasant. They really are disgusting creatures.

You descend a hole that only gets deeper and deeper.\n\nUnlike my opponents and I, you can still leave this place. Yet you linger, hoping that you can somehow save the mortals from the Mages Guild. How curious!
Go to Greenheart. Quickly. There is no time to delay.

And we find ourselves here once again … it's so unnatural. It makes me feel queasy.\n\nThe Eldest's heart must be the nexus that ties this plane to ours. I suspect it is also tethered to Naemon's Servant—the one who addressed us.

Did you hear? Ranneth wants to make me their town mage! Alanya loves it here. I think it's the mead. I can be a working spellcaster, instead of a failed student! I can do this! And it's all thanks to you. Thank you.
Goodbye now. It's time for me to rest.
Go on. We need to do this before I lose my nerve.
Our swords have prevailed! All Cyrodiil's forts are in Covenant hands. We have no Warfront missions now, but many others await your attention.
Marasadra just tends to the horses. Leave her be.
With <<1>> defeated we may just meet our recruitment quota.
Thank you, for everything. To kill someone in the name of the Pact, wrongly—unthinkable! If you hadn't been here, this would have turned out much worse. Thank you.
New around here, aren't you? I advise you to have a talk with <<1>>.
The Elder Scroll of Alma Ruma has been stolen! I can tell you of the Elder Scrolls, but this temple is an empty shell until our scroll returns. Perhaps you can help, when your training is done.
After we talked through our little misunderstanding, Ranneth and I agreed that Pircalmo would make a good town mage. I quite like it here! The mead … so delicious!
With those bandits gone, we finally have enough supplies and equipment for the new recruits.
With those bandits driven out I can keep two eyes on the horizon and not worry about what's happening behind me.
In breaking the Shadows Watch, you saved many lives.

I knew Fahara'jad's appointee was to blame for this. It was only a matter of time before the Divines revealed her treachery. Onsi's blessings be upon our Justice Istah for finally bringing her to account.
Well, these Crowns are not quite as dour as I thought. Tears of Zeht, that wedding looks festive!
Make yourself comfortable, stranger. Everything the Manor of Revelry has to offer is yours for the taking.
Why do these things keep happening to me, I wonder?
You must be starving! Try everything. It's all so delicious. I promise, you've never tasted anything like the food we prepare here.
Our pools are warm and inviting. Feel free to take a nice, long soak.
Stibbons really wants to be a hero. Please help him so he doesn't get himself killed.
If you're here to join up with <<1>>, his day is over. \n\nAnd if you stick around, so is yours.
You're going to challenge <<1>>? Word of advice, run while you still got legs.
It just figures that <<1>> would get someone else to do his dirty work.
Why doesn't <<1>> just let us run off <<2>> and his militia rats?\n\nI'm tired of having to tiptoe around them and put up with their sneers.
What are you looking at?
It must be some madness blown in from the south. I wish I could clear my head.\n\nIt's like I can't remember something that I must!
This one's good-for-nothing brother Munyat sleeps all day, but Raban is happy to help you.
High Elf cooking? No, no. Too dry. Wood Elf cooking? Lacks sweet! You will find no better than <<1>>'s authentic Khajiiti cooking.
This one has traveled Tamriel to bring the finest arcana to you.
I generally find the Khajiit's grasp of knowledge lacking, but I'm impressed.
This one sees you have survived many battles. Buy my armor and survive many battles more, yes?
I hope you brought the key. We're ready to make the final push, but we're finished if we can't get inside.\n\nThis is our last chance to save our world. It's all or nothing now.
Close that reinforcement portal so that we can send the rest of our forces inside.\n\nI know you will make me proud!
So it's true then? You have retrieved my bow from the Shade?
Authentic Valenwood hides, certain to protect against Colovian arrows.
I wonder where that worthless boy got to. He should've been back with my herbs by now. Oh, pardon me.
Business is good, if you can keep the Bosmer from stealing everything in sight.
Yazhin complains about thieves, but he leaves his till unlocked.
Spotless woodcraft at fair prices—sanded and polished to a mirror sheen.\n \nCome, look!
These damned cats'll give you tin when you ask for iron. Anything to save a drake. If you're here to do some real metalwork, I'm the Orc you can trust.
The Khajiit have suffered much lately, but they are a lively people. They give hope to us all.
Daedra never sleep and neither do we.
The Fighters Guild will secure the line behind you. We won't give up any ground you gain us. Just get in there and open the way to the Labyrinth.
And here comes the great and marvelous Vanus Galerion—right on schedule and just in time to take all the credit.\n\nI think he wants to talk to you.
Let the King know what you decided so we can get this assault underway already!
How odd. I never imagined my warriors would be pitted against the forces of Molag Bal.\n\nBut have no fear. We are ready to fight when you give the word.
Good drink makes good friends, yes?
She may not believe what we believe, at first. She is my superior within the clergy, and sometimes prideful. But she trusts in the moons. As I do.
It will take more than steel to keep the Colovians at bay.
This one has much to offer. From as far away as the Summerset Isles—enchanting and mystical!
That worked? I mean, I knew that would work. Never doubted my calculations.\n\nUm, good job! The door ahead should be unlocked now.
The darkness is obviously designed to hinder our progress. An interesting conundrum, yes?
And another job performed to perfection by our champion. Well done!\n\nNow hurry through the open door and find the planar vortex. The end of the world isn't going to wait for you, you know.
His wounds … he's in terrible pain. We tried to heal him … but the damage … it's too extensive.
Well? I see you asking the rest of these daintyfoots for help, but you took your time getting to me.\n\nWhat am I? Too short for your precious army?
Your king must be informed. Let him know that we are ready to spill blood and defeat your enemies!
Has the time come to sail into the stormy sea? Do we pillage and plunder the domicile of the Lord of Brutality now?\n\nI'm eager to demonstarte the power of the Bone Crown!
A drunk Nord is worth a dozen of these sober milk-drinkers. Imagine how valuable a sober Nord can be.\n\nI haven't been in a good brawl in a long time. I'm looking forward to it!
Say the word and we will attack the Dark Father by your side.
We had to abandon everything when the Colovians attacked.
The Khajiit have been surprisingly friendly to us.
I think that Khajiit back there was interested in more than friendly conversation.
We need food if we are going to survive.
Where is Shiri? She should have been back days ago!\n\nI never should have taken that girl as an apprentice. Untrustworthy! There is something very sneaky about her.
Can you believe <<1>> agreed to join me?\n\nI've been a one-man act till now, but she's a bright lass and will make a great partner. And, she still holds the key for this chest.
I've been told that Shiri, the scholar's apprentice is on her way back to Bergama, but Scholar Zohreh says she hasn't seen the girl yet.
My father—does he live?
That strange knight says the oddest things. But Vanus and the King seem to trust him, so what can you do?\n\nYou must be the champion that King Dynar said would lead us across the Chasm.

It is an honor to meet you. Prince Azah has told me of your deeds in Sentinel, and I know you have General Thoda's respect as well.\n\nWith you here, I think our chances of surviving this have improved tenfold.

May Y'ffre smile on you! You closed the rifts that bound us here! \n\nYou must stop that Shade though … it seeks to do terrible things to Valenwood. Though I have passed on many years gone now, I still consider Valenwood my home.
I can't believe we got caught up in all of that. I hope Pircalmo understands what it looked like. Thank you for showing up when you did.
I thought you were going to tell that matchmaker to let me off the hook. \n\nNon-bandits. You can't trust them.
Stop! I yield. I admit defeat.
Magic worries me. I can never quite trust all those mage-types. Maybe things will be different now that we have a town mage.
Get your lizard away from me, stranger!
You look lost; probably need some training. I can help you out.
The Green Lady is in Malabal Tor, but rumors of attacks from Redguards have reached us. It's imperative that the Green Lady be kept safe, so that she and the Silvenar may be joined.
This doesn't seem right. Sometimes I wonder if the Vinedusk Rangers understand things more than we do.
We'll talk again in Daggerfall. Look for the loud bunch in the back of the Rosy Lion tavern.\n\nAssuming you don't die in that cave, of course.
Sorry, friend. I have to get back to my companion.

Valenwood is only alive because of you. We are all in your debt, I especially, and having a Silvenar in your debt can be a good thing.\n\nI'll be on my way to Malabal Tor now. I will undoubtedly see you there.
Your loyalty to the crown will be rewarded, my friend. You have my word.\n\nGet in there and free the hostages and then we can go in and spill some Imperial blood.
Well played. I hope Zara wasn't watching. I was hoping she'd pick me to fight in the next division round.
I don't care to make this decision, but I must.
Hail, brother. \n\nWord has reached us that Talia now leads the tribe. Know that we stand ready to fight, should the shadow fall on Bergama.
Not all who come to train at Leki's Blade learn what they thought they might.
You dirty pig! Whatever you do to me, I will be avenged! You people were fools to even set foot upon Alik'r sands .…\n\nWait … you're not an Imperial, are you?
Whatever it is that you people seek to accomplish, your efforts will be to no avail ….\n\nWait … you're no Imperial. Are you with King Fahara'jad's army?
Hail, brother. It is good that you have come. \n\nThe Withered Hand has been here—I can feel it. Stay vigilant.
No time to lose. Send any survivors this way and head to the inner gate!
By the gods, I swear that you infidels will all die. You will find that Redguards are not merciful ….\n\nHold on … you're no Imperial … does this mean we're going to take the city back?
Be at ease. This is but a simple misunderstanding between merchants who bumped carts. No lives will be lost here.
You collaped the tunnel, the army's re-taken the city, and that son of a dog Khorshad is gone.\n\nThis ended far better than I hoped.
Thank you for exercising mercy on me.\n\nI do not believe the Imperials would be so forgiving, so I beseech you … you must slay them all.
This one … cannot speak. My dignity is injured.
The tribe will live and flourish in <<c:1>>. Be proud, you've given our people hope.
I should pray to Y'ffre before the meeting. Is there anything else you need?
Begone, outsider. You have no place here.
Still more tears to close. Very bad. Coldharbour is no good for living.
Once I finish stripping this one, I think I'll go in for a drink.
You're a new face to me, unlike that flappy buzzard over the barn.
I've been found! Oh, but you are neither harpy nor Gold Coast fiend. What a relief!
I have done as you asked, as I knew I must. Now leave me to my grief!\n\nPlease.
Keep one eye to the skies, friend. The harpies like to swoop down and grab whatever's light enough to carry. I've lost two hats and a goat to the feathered villains.
You're alive! I thought they might have taken you too ….
There you are! Impressive work back there. The Maormer didn't know what hit them when our forces stormed in—and I've got my ship back!
You ready to go? I don't know what the Sea Vipers plan, but I doubt we have much time to stop them.
If you wish my company, we should hurry. The Sea Vipers wouldn't commit their forces unless they're certain of success.
Ah, great. The Eagles took over in Pa'alat. Now it's going to be just another boring tavern town under the Queen's thumb.
This Khajiit is glad to hear the Eagles have taken control in Pa'alat. There are too many dark things in the shadows to allow shadows to fester.
Look at this place! We'd better stick together and find a way to get to Molag Grunda and open the Gatehouse.\n\nI think Molag Grunda is barricaded within another room.
With the might of the Mages Guild on our side, perhaps we can finally push back Montclair's soldiers and take back Shornhelm's northern district!
Caution, friend. Not all in town wish the Dominion well.
As if this place weren't dangerous enough, now we've got foreign troops from Brindle in here. What are you going to do about that?
Good to see some faces from home. I feel safer with Castle Brindle in friendly hands.
With the Covenant in charge of Brindle, maybe I'll propose my idea for a wall around Vlastarus to the local commander.
Welcome to the tribe, sister. The wisdom of the Chief was deep as a well. I know his faith in you was deserved.
The Shade—you must kill it if we are to end this.
I need to get away from these birds. With Brindle in friendly hands, maybe they need cooks. First meal would be chicken, if I have my way.
You draw the sword for us all, brother. True honor need … need not be named. Avenge us.
So the Covenant took over Castle Brindle. Is that supposed to make me feel safer? Well, it doesn't.
The Altmer don't seem to think we're capable. Well, we'll show them who can fight!
The Queen and the Silvenar are safe as long as we are on watch.
You bear the tribe's burdens now, sister. Remember—true honor need not be named. Seek not fame or glory, only justice.
Do not look upon me with pity, brother. Hearts such as ours, crowded with great and terrible purpose, have no room for such things.
Fill this poisoned cup with our enemies' blood, brother. All of the Alik'r watches you. May Tava speed your passage.
Word swirls through camp like a dust devil. So you are Ash'abah now? That is good, brother. \n\nTrue honor need not be named. Send the Withered Hand back to Oblivion.
Welcome to the tribe, brother. I regret we have nothing to give but our blessings.
Both Zamyad and Parvenah took to the Far Shores during your trial, brother. I fear we will lose even more swords yet.
If I ever find Donus, I'll return to Cheydinhal. I hope Kirandas hasn't given up hope.
True honor need not be named, brother. May your blade never go thirsty while these fiends still draw breath.
Vikord and I have a wager in play. Just to make things more interesting. Whoever collects the most Dremora hearts wins.
Sinfay thinks she can beat a Nord in a contest? Especially a killing contest? Ha! By the time we're through, I'll have more Dremora hearts than I can carry!

Hail, brother. The poison of Morwha's Bounty has run its course, thank Ruptga. It would take ten and ten to keep me from my work. Rumor swirls across the dunes. Some say there is a vampiric curse staining Leki's Blade, and now we have found proof.
True honor need not be named, brother. My son's sickness broke while you took on the crucible. You are indeed blessed by the Divines!
All praise to Ruptga: it appears my brother will recover. I take your arrival as a gift, brother. Divines willing, we shall fight beside you soon.
Well, well … took you long enough. Gran-gran could have cleared that cave out faster than you did. And she's only got one arm!
I think that little Wood Elf was planning to face Molag Grunda all by herself before Cadwell ran up there. You'd better catch up with them. I'll make sure nothing follows you.
You will help us find a way to forge these dangerous waters and get our troops past the Reaver Citadel. I have total confidence in you.
This looks pretty grim. We'll never find a way into that citadel. I think we should just cut our losses and head home now.
My brother's nervous. So am I. This quest of ours never seems to end!
There's bound to be a way into that place. I mean, besides the front door. I imagine there are a lot of Dremora waiting on the other side of the gate.
I'm impressed, little mortal. Hardly a scratch on you!
You did it again, my fearless friend! Well done!\n\nWith the Dremora caught between my powerful mages and King Dynar's relentless fighters, they won't know which way to turn.
Hurry, now. Get to the upper city and activate the Mages Guild portal.\n\nWithout the help of the mages, this entire endeavor could come crashing down around us.
You're back. Did you tell Brielus? Is he coming for me?
I hear you cleansed the blight. We're mighty grateful.
You've been such a great help! I'm off to see Telenger as soon as I finish this.
I'm exhausted. Find another sparring partner if you're still looking for a fight.
The ritual site is beyond the door. Keep that lodestone close at hand for those ritual horns!

Since both Alasan and Uwafa have been dealt with, the Withered Hand may be considerably weakened.\n\nPerhaps the third Ansei Ward is closer at hand than you realize. If the gods are with you, I believe you will recover it quickly.
Though the memories of Aranias fade, you are—and forever will be—a friend to the Valenwood … and a friend to me.
You have no idea how good this feels! To be whole again, and walk with my own two legs. To have legs at all!
You! You're alive! Just what I need!
Thank you again for returning my brother's coin to me. I'll remember him whenever I feel it in my pocket.
I already told you—I have no wish to suffer at the Taskmaster's hand!

I'd welcome you to Whisper Grove, but it's little more than a city of ash at the moment.\n\nPlease, I don't have time to take care of visitors. My husband Fingaenion here has been injured, and I have an army of Daedra to deal with.
Thank you for giving me closure. I hoped Divyth was still alive, but this is better than always wondering and worrying.
Stranger is good to this one, and to others. Now Khajiit has to do her part.
I'm going to have to figure out how to discretely return all of these things ….

You know where I stand. We have sliced through the enemies' ranks to get this far, and my blades are still at your disposal. \n\nI do not relish fighting, but I have trained since birth for this kind of thing.
I always hated my sister. But I'd never wanted her dead.
That pompous mage told me to keep an eye on her, and that's just what I'm doing. But I have the distinct feeling that I amuse her.\n\nI'm not sure how I feel about that.
I allowed your intrusion because it was obvious this would end in a clash of wills. It proved … enlightening.
I'd really like to be alone. I need to mourn my daughter.
I'm glad you brought the families some closure. Still, I would have liked to end the bastard myself.
You have this one's thanks, stranger. Moons' light be with you by night, always.
<<1>> is glad she could calm her brother down. He did not need to be poisoned by outrage. Your coming has not set all things right, but at least we still have our lives.
Shove something silver and pointy into their furry behinds, traveler. Make sure they know Atrius Axilla sent you!

Thank you, my friend. Prince Azah said you were indispensable. I now see why.\n\nYou do an old soldier a great favor by helping. I hope Shiri is not hurt, and even moreso, I hope that text has not been taken again by the Withered Hand.
Meet me in front of the cathedral when you are ready to launch the attack. Time is no longer on our side.

This is … unthinkable. Shiri came to me only a few months ago, but she seemed so dedicated. Of course she was! She was studying the Ansei Wards …! How could I not have seen this?\n\nI hope we find her before she does something … terrible.
Everyone says you've saved the village from committing a terrible mistake. Thank you, it will make my trading much easier.
Hey, thanks for setting us right.
So, you did it. Summoner Division Champion! It's an honor.\n\nNormally I'd offer my services as your servant, unfortunately Ishalga has reassigned me to other duties.
I understand congratulations are in order. Winning the Sorcerer Division Championship is no small matter! Very impressive.
Won the Division Campionship for the Swordmasters, did you? That's damned impressive. I may place some coin on you for the finals.
Velyn Harbor is rumored to be overrun. I wish you luck. We'll be preparing for Malabal Tor ourselves.
You saved Greenshade and my people are safe. I can't thank you enough.
Is it true? What Cariel speaks? Indaenir, resurrected?
I wish you luck in Malabal Tor. I hope to see you at the joining of the Silvenar and the Green Lady.
It seems a ceremony is in order. Indaenir will meet up with the Green Lady and the two will be united in Silvenar. This one hopes to see you there.
Lord Gharesh-ri spoke of the ceremony between the Silvenar and the Green Lady. This one hopes to be there.
This one wonders where our journeys will take us next. Hopefully not back to Elsweyr so soon.
Sounds like the Dominion leaders will be moving to Malabal Tor. I'll remain to ensure the Heritance regrets setting foot on Greenshade.
A shame I missed out on all the fun. You owe me quite the tale now!

Believe me, I'd have been by your side, but … that Cariel. She's a feisty one. The things she threatened me with if I followed!\n\nI thought the Vinedusks were tough, but the Eyes of the Queen? I'll be happy to stay on their good side.
My guess is Indaenir's next destination will be Malabal Tor. I wonder if he's already met the Green Lady.
Looks like you took care of Naemon. Greenshade is safe now.
I hope our paths cross again under better circumstances.
This one hopes to see you again. Times are rough with Great War and we could use your help securing the Dominion.\n\nKauzanabi-jo only seeks to protect and educate the Lunar Champions.
You're going to duel Erthas, huh? Gilraen thinks he's been allied with the Daedra since long before Whisper Grove. \n\nI wonder if he still bleeds like a Bosmer.
So the word is you're going to put an end to Erthas. Good.\n\nI never liked him, even when he was one of us. Had a haughty air about him. Still, I never expected him to do all this!

Our power—the power of the Ansei Wards—was compromised, and the Alik'r desert was in grave danger … but you stepped in.\n\nYou stopped the necromancers and the Alik'r desert is again safe from the risen dead.
You aided me at <<Ac:1>>. I'd be a fool not to return the favor. Whatever the Sea Vipers plan, we should hurry.
Now that the Imperials are gone, we can pick up the pieces. If the Divines will it, the Imperials will not come here under any other ill tiding.
Know, O wayfarer, how much we have lost. They may be gone but we may never recover.
I hope you slew every one of the Imperials you came across, wayfarer. It would only be fair if such woe would befall them as has us.
We're getting reports in from all over the desert. Withered Hand's crumbling fast.\n\nWe did it, my friend. We did it.
It has reached me that you had a hand in our liberation, wayfarer. Long may you prosper.
We have a new master now—have you not heard? Such a sudden change.
I sense ill-doings in the cemetery, wayfarer. Our masters speak in hushed tones and Fadalia goes missing. I've no patience for such secrecy.
Do not tell anyone, but a sword-brother of mine has heard talk of vampires lurking in Leki's Blade. Vampires! How could such creatures survive in so holy a place? It must be idle gossip.
The Cemetery is off limits to students now, but our groundskeepers remain outside. Odd.
The newly blessed swordsmen are just as quiet as the last. What secrets they tell at the graduation ceremony must be solemn indeed.
Since you won the challenge, I'm bound by our code to let you go. \n\nHowever, the other Ungodly might not be so scrupulous. I hope not, anyway.
Have you visited the graves of the Masters? We have been told to stay away, but It seems somehow easier to breath there now. I always gave it a wide berth before. The solemnity was … oppressive.
My soul lightens—a door has been opened, wayfarer. I know not why, but Leki's Blade feels somehow holier since you arrived.
A new Master … ha. It is about time. Let us hope that they are marginally more competent than Fadalia was.
I'm joyful this has all ended, though I may never rest easily again. Beware of shifting sands, wayfarer.
Hark, wayfarer. Do you suppose the Imperials brought all of these boxes and barrels with them, through the tunnel you destroyed? I'm sure we didn't have this many.
Disciple—I mean, Master Raifa—is at least as skillful as Fadalia was. The school is in good hands.
Abide with me, wayfarer. Tu'whacca's breath, you've won us time for that, at least!
My relief knows no bounds, wayfarer… but the damage they accomplished will be no mean feat to recover from. Zeht's tears, I may be fetching our things for ages!
I won't feign otherwise, wayfarer - it surprises me little that the coward Khorshad brought us to this. By my father's head, he never seemed entirely trustworthy to me.
I rejoice for we who yet live, wayfarer. My legs will never tire, now that we are rid of that menace!
By Tava's red feathers! Did you hear the rumor, wayfarer? Master Fadalia is a vampire! I will sleep with my twice-blessed silver blades close from now on.
The Imperials are like unto sand, wayfarer. As the wind brings them in, it avails us by carrying them away, just the same.
I was in the middle of my prayers when they forced me out of the cemetery. By Ruptga's starry breeches, what could be so important? Please don't tell them I was spying.
Though I know you'll presently be gone, wayfarer, Satakalaam welcomes you to abide as long as you need. Peace be upon you in all your dealings.
Zeht's tears, what are they doing in there? Master Fadalia's face was taut with concern. Did someone deface Ahtar's grave?
I had only just arrived to pray when Master Fadalia and the rest sent me away. I mean no disrespect to our teachers, but they might give us some warning next time.
The school has gone quiet. Has something happened? I saw a small gathering outside the graves—some faces were flushed, others were pale.
We're as ready as we shall ever be.
I have never seen Nabeenam so silent. He has always been stoic, but this is different. It is something about Master Ahtar. Do you suppose someone might have defaced his grave?
I feel a fog has lifted since you arrived, wayfarer. That hidden dread flees and Master Fadalia goes missing. This no coincidence. We must remain vigilant.
By my father's head! The unworthy Imperials have made such a fine mess of things here.
Please, get rid of that creature. But be careful. Her magic is formidable!
So, many interesting sights to see, don't you think?
This one suggests you keep your eyes on your coin purse. The Wood Elves aren't to be trusted.
Shasirba makes such wonderful baked goods. You should try some yourself! Or, some supplies for the road from me?
Khuzi hopes you found that necklace well enough. She'd hate for someone so strong to be distraught.
I'm looking for a present for my sister but there are too many options.
I heard the Queen is in Rawl'kha. I hope I get to see her.
This one is very busy. Maybe another time.
Can you move please? You're blocking my view.
My brother did the right thing. That Altmer was a pompous ass.

You've been beside me in this battle since the beginning. You know I'll do whatever it takes to destroy the Withered Hand.\n\nThat said, Shiri's already proven more than a match for me. We have to win this one, so you need to take the lead.
I slave away in this hot kitchen but Duzal still buys meat pies from Shasirba. I need to learn her secret.
Seems we do more drinking than fighting sometimes, eh comrade?

I will join you, if you wish. \n\nI am no great warrior. I am only a humble priest, but Tu'whacca says I can be of great assistance to you in this battle. He says it is up to you to make this decision though.
Hush now, you'll frighten them. They don't know what awaits us! No one knows … no one knows ….
Seems like just moments ago we were in Dune, yes? It is a good thing Raz is so quick on his feet. Wouldn't want you waiting on him … like we are waiting on the Guildmaster.
I don't know how you managed to pull this off, but the guilds are with you!
I heard <<1>>. Let's fight!
What do you want?
Your skull needs more dents. I can help you with that.
What are you looking at?
The Dremora are fully engaged. If you're going to get the Mages Guild portal working, the time to leave is now.
Once the mages get inside the upper city, the Dremora will be surrounded!
There may be some useful information in these old books, and this map is a remarkable discovery.
Now that my apprentice is back, we can finally get out of here!

This is a day I'll long remember! After months of searching I've finally discovered the location of my ancestral estate. It's not far from here! \n\nAs soon as I pack my things, I'm off to claim my rightful inheritance as the Heir of Direfrost Keep!
