Not to worry, I'll be right behind you! We'll give that Valkynaz the thrashing he so richly deserves!
Hello, um, Maruin wishes to see you. He says you're late for your story.
I pray you can help me, good traveler. They have her, and I'm desperate!
I can finally close my eyes.
Thank you again. The preparations for the wedding have been made, and so far, we have only been hit with tomatoes, and not rocks.

Good show! The portal belongs to us now! \n\nSir Darien and that lovely lizard have gone on ahead. I think he might be a bit intimidated by our prowess on the field of battle, and he's trying to compensate.
You've reminded me of my purpose. I'm sorry I ever forgot it. I hope Laurosse will forgive me.
What we did. Murdering an entire family. Is this what Y'ffre demands?
I'm glad they're dead. I don't care who hears me. Halalin … Halalin won't stop screaming in my head.
At last it is over. At last, I can grieve.
This one sees and knows what you have done here, walker. Your five-clawed assault will be remembered.
Fool that you are, this one is glad for you to have been here. A spotless choice, walker. We still have our temple and our city to keep, yes?
I have heard it said someone opened holes to Oblivion in the middle of Dune and that a five-clawed walker had just the thing to plug up these holes. I wonder who could have done such a thing?

Great! I'm sure the Vinedusks there will appreciate the help, especially with the Mane hanging around.\n\nBodring is in charge there. Find him and let him know I sent you. That way he'll know I haven't forgotten him.
Dune will be sleek again, in time. Especially sleek if five-clawed walkers like yourself fill its streets, this one is thinking.

No army has come, and yet Dune stands free of Daedra. Shimsamu has heard a strange walker, sleek and five-clawed, is to thank for this. Do you think this walker might be available? Or … if this walker had any siblings, that would be fine too.
The Sea Vipers are insane! They're trying to create another hurricane!

Magundim watched you fight, when he could. To have learned it all is impossible to expect, but I think I learned enough to be able to help my city. Perhaps a future with the guard is in store for Magundim, yes?

Dular wonders, walker, if you recall whether certain buildings were intact during your foray into Dune's merchant district. It is best if they all are, of course, but for this reason and that reason, it is better for me if—No, I go too far.

The danger is gone, yes? Can you tell me, walker? If it is safe to walk into the city once more, Yanu-ma has many bellies to fill, she thinks. Perhaps you would like some of what Yanu-ma has to offer, hmm?
I'm flattered by the attention, but I think it's time you were on your way.

Anyone capable of what you've accomplished here should consider membership in the Guild. We could use someone like you.\n\nEspecially since you've proven yourself capable of tackling Daedra and Dark Anchors.
Closing a portal system of that magnitude is no mean feat, even with our assistance. You should consider joining the Guild—we could use someone like you.
Isn't it amazing? The crisis has ended, but our little town will continue. I'm so pleased!
I think I'll keep the tavern open. This safe haven needs to be preserved.
I've decided to stick around. Help turn the Hollow City back into a proper city. Who cares if it just happens to be in the middle of Coldharbour? That just adds a bit of character to the place.
Well, I guess I'm stuck here. Someone has to help feed all these people.\n\nJust my luck, the Hollow City has become a destination spot.
This guild hall is certainly more impressive than many of the posts I've been assigned to. And it feels good to have fighters running around its corridors.
Even far from everything we know, some things remain the same. Potential mages guild candidates, carrying a strange tome or two, picked up on your travels. Care to show me what you have found?
Thank you for your intercession, wayfarer. Between the harpies and the Gold Coasters—well, I might have had to sell this place.
Thank you for muzzling those mercenaries, wayfarer. As with all dogs, a thump on the snout is sometimes required.
I would've liked a few harpy heads mounted on the tavern wall, but at least I can let my horses graze without me guarding them.
By Tava's red feathers, it is well to have a moment's peace unmarred by harpy screeching. I do not know how you did it, wayfarer, but you have my thanks.
Long and long have we suffered under those sellswords, O wayfarer. Would that you had killed them all. Only then would we be truly safe.
Mulama is ruined! The harpies leave and now the dungy Redguard buy no bows! \n\nYou will buy something to ease this one's sorrow, yes?

Ah, the five-clawed walker! Four-Toes is thinking of writing tonight. Could you tell him if you said anything witty, perhaps, while fighting the invaders of Dune? This is important, it is for posterity.\nAs always, I am ready to trade, as well.
Well, well, if it isn't the hero of the Pact. Glad you made it.
Hi, can I help you?

It's good to hear that the harpies have settled, but my blood still boils at the sight of those mercenaries. They'll not have any of my steel as long as I draw breath. \n\nYou, however, are invited to look over my goods.
It is as this one thought! None could stand up to his flashing blades, no. None tried, but the result would be the same!
At last, those harpies are gone! I can't wait to start working on some new outerwear. \n\nYou look eager to begin as well. Can I interest you in any of my goods?
The harpies are gone, but for how long?
Tu'whacca bless you, O wayfarer. At last I can sleep without fear of the sound of wings.
At last, the village returns to normal. Now we can attend to the vital business of removing Andrin from office.
I had hoped you would burn the harpies out, but I suppose bringing those mercenaries to heel is some comfort.
The harpies may be gone, but their tangled nests and foul droppings remain. We have much work left to do.
Zur has found you! This one is so happy now.
Peace with the harpies? May as well make peace with the scorpions and fire beetles as well. \n\nBetter a thousand deaths than to share water with those winged horrors.
I'm grateful for what you've done, O wayfarer. My inn is still in shambles, but at least we can rebuild without fear of further disaster.
Blood and glory, friend. I would have liked to thump some of those harpies with you, but duty calls.
Brave meeting, friend. Good job accounting for those good-for-nothing sellswords. I heard them howling through a stone wall.
Welcome to the Kozanset Fighters Guildhall, traveler. \n\nYou look capable—even dangerous. Have you considered joining the guild?
I can't wait to watch what the Daedra do to you when they finally catch you. I just hope I'm there to see it.
It was good of you to protect the town as you did. \n\nI still wish we'd used our powers to help, by Y'ffre.
Greetings, seeker, and welcome to the Kozanset Mages Guild Hall. I trust you made it here unmolested? The Redguards are not overfond of our presence here.\n\nI am curious: what do you have there?
You again? I knew you were up to no good! Get away from me before I call the guards!
Are you still here? Perhaps you should pull up a rock and help us with our work. Do something useful while you're here.
This one wonders, why are you still here? Don't you have a great mage to rescue or something?
You're going to leave me all alone again, aren't you Alexis?\n\nWell, I forgive you anyway and I'll be right here when you return.
Aldolin cannot be far. If you find him before we do, be wary. He will not yield to you and must be put down like the cur that he is.
About time you got here.
You'll want to talk to Copper, not me. My word has a hefty price.
Excellent. Manthir often peddles his wares here, but right now he is likely at his home just across the market to the east. Look for him there to start.\n\nAnd don't worry, Manthir is a soft one.
If you want to talk to her, I won't stop you. She lives in the next house over.
I can't wait to get back into uniform. Undercover work isn't my cup of tea.

You are the one who killed my brother Uwafa, are you not?\n\nI will grant that you are likely a formidable foe, but once I become a lich, I will burn you to cinders. There's nothing you can do to stop me now.
Thank you. We were on our way to Longhaven when the Argonians struck. Free my companions and meet us there. I'll repay you however I can.
Come see me when you are done with the siege weapons, warrior.
You have done well, traveler. Stand beside Shazah, struggling against the darkness. You have taken your first steps down a difficult path.

All clear? Good. I'll be stationed here indefinitely, for the security of the Dominion, but it's good to know things are safe for now.\n\nI wonder if I could get that Khajiit girl to bring me a snack every once in a while.
All this skulking around, using up valuable energy on apprentice-level illusions. I grow ever more weary. Even Zur's enthusiasm is ebbing.

Y'ffre's bones, I've been seeing flocks of cats scurrying about Dune since the fighting stopped!

Do cats flock? Or is it a "pride" thing? Could you ask one of the Khajiit that?

And if you do, come back and show me the scars.
Don't waste time searching for me after you leave. You'll have larger concerns soon enough.
A Daedra attack! My, my, my. A nasty business that. At least they left my gems intact … mostly.\n\nGet you something?
Steer clear of us Armigers. I don't think your reputation could take it, hero.
Don't mind Craw, she likes messing with people. You seem like you could use a bow. Do you want to go hunting some time?
You again. I always seem to run into you right before I do something I'll probably regret.
It will take time to accept what you have said.\n\nI… This body is so heavy.
Nidras, a thief? And to think I trusted him with our valuables! How embarrassing.
It must be done and I would be most grateful.\n\nYou should know that who or whatever wrote this book bound it to the labyrinth. To traverse one, you need the other.
Ah, you're back. You have the meat pies, yes?

Azdanten has heard of a skooma distillery, that it has been destroyed, that it was in a cave under an old blind walker's well.\n\nOf course, you know Azdanten has had nothing to do with that nonsense. This one is an honest trader, as you well know.
Excuse this one, walker, but her curiosity overcomes her, and she must know! This one hears stories of ghosts, and that they have been exorcised from a local home.\n\nWhat is to be made of it?

I've been hearing stories of bandits in the area!

Our caravan has only two guards for the moment, do you suppose they will be enough?

Some of the Khajiit have been saying the bandits have been dealt with, though. I guess it might not be a problem.

I overheard something a bit absurd from some of the locals.

This town had a local crime lord? The thought is honestly a bit ridiculous.

I can relax a bit, I guess. That's always good news.
Been hearing interesting things, about someone meeting your description dealing with a local ring of bandits, smugglers, drug runners and the like.\n\nNice work.
Now I have to wait for him to summon up the courage to approach me. I wonder how long I'll be waiting this time?
Wait till I tell Mother the news. The rest of her hair will fall out!

The Sea Hawk is just there, on the southern dock. Remember, the silks are likely below deck. And while I know Angore is not aboard, I can't guarantee that his goons won't try to stop you. You look like you can handle yourself though.

Good work! Hostages came out and we attacked. Cut right through the bastards and scoured the city. Just a handful of Imperials holding out now.\n\nI still haven't figured out how they got here though … I'm worried reinforcements may be on the way.

You must hurry. Sooner or later, the Lord of Schemes will become aware that we're closer to our goal than his army realizes.\n\nI'll keep this portal open for as long as I can. That should allow us to bring in a few reinforcements of our own.
I would not enter the mine now for love or gold. There's not enough of either to convince me.
Please, come, browse my wares! I have many fine drinks and brews. Available to one and all!
Have a look! Take all the time you need. And spare me your wary glances! Colovians like myself have a rich history of trade. Really, we do.
You have performed better than I expected, even in the face of unrelenting danger and the worst horrors Oblivion has to offer.\n\nI am impressed.
Speak to your friends, for these moments may be their last. \n\nBut do not tarry too long. Time is fleeting, and each moment is a thief that steals far more than it brings.
What are you doing here? Why aren't you saving my daughter?
Thank you. May the Green keep you safe in your travels.
<A wooden ring on the corpse's decaying hand indicates this must be Zariya. <<1>> may want the ring as a keepsake of his wife.>
Yenadar's grace be upon you. And Kala's prayers go with you as well.
Ah, Nirnroot wine, nectar fit for the gods. As long as they can afford my prices that is!
Woodhearth welcomes you with open arms and warm embrace.
Split-Tongue hears Rakhad no longer hides under the rocks of S'ren-ja.\n\nThis is good news for Split-Tongue, for his tongue was split by Rakhad's minions. It is a small kind of revenge for him, yes?
There are unscrupulous shopkeepers in Woodhearth, but Adaishir is not one of them.
Silly Bosmer. We pluck the wealth from the Valenwood and sell it back to them, and they pay us joyfully.

This one hears all sorts of good news this day!

About this thing and that thing, this friend has a pregnant mate, that friend met someone new in Rawl'kha, and best of all - that stink of skooma is all gone from this one's town!

A good day, yes?

So I found out while those skooma slingers were running out of town that, when they lick their teeth, it's one of those little signs of skooma use.

I had no idea.

Should I just not say anything, or should I tell someone it's okay to want to eat me?
Bury an axe in that Daedric bastard!
This one hopes the Claw will remain safe now, walker.\n\nWhat an end to a pilgrimage, yes? Still—the Claw is safe. This is what matters, this one thinks.
Molag Bal has much to answer for. Remember those who gave their lives today.
I wish I could go with you. I've always wanted to cut down some Daedra on Molag Bal's home turf. But I have confidence you'll get the job done. Good luck.
This one hopes your hands ran red with the blood of the Stonefire.\n\nEither way, you have done the Order of the Claw such a service.
The Claw is safe, yes? \n\nMoons watch over you in your travels. Clearly you have their blessing.
Leave me alone. I don't want to hear anything you have to say.\n\nYou've ruined me. How could someone like you come out on top?

It's you! I remember you! You've filled my pockets! I'll buy you a drink, but you're not exactly my type, ha!\n\nWhat's the matter … not funny? Malacath's bloody teat! A killer like you should laugh more, ha!

Wealth beyond measure, muthsera. Someday … perhaps, someday, I will be ready to meet you in combat. But I have seen that this is not a fate yet for which I am prepared.\n\nYou are like a saint of strife in the arena, muthsera.
Well, plough me sideways. The dung-breathed child won a fight or two.\n\nPat yourself on the back, my hands are busy and you're not worth the sweat of my pits.

Hey, it's my victorious friend! We are friends, right? Damned fine fight!\n\nThey're letting me change divisions! Did you talk to anyone? What did you say about me? You didn't call me a coward, did you? Hah, of course not.

Nonsense. Clearly you're sleeping with the judges. Or you've poisoned the water supply or laced your weapons with filth—or some other trick.\n\nYou're no better than me. You can't be any better than me. It just wouldn't be fair or right.
Keep your head. Clearly I'd lose my arms trying to take it, heh.\n\nI'd rather keep my arms and rejoin the One than lose them to you. It's a hard thing, to lick a stump so close to your face.

Oh, hello. I think we've met, haven't we?

Did you just win something? Are you a fighter? That's very interesting.

I think I've earned enough to make my way back to Wayrest. There's something important waiting for me there, but I can't recall what.

Why do you bother Mazou-dar? You have your earnings.

You already know you cannot bet, walker. Be happy with your money and go.

Why talk to Mazou-dar? He has nothing for you.
Well fought, sera. Well fought, indeed.\n\nDid I bet on you? I'll never say, but ask yourself—do I seem upset? Go on. You've more fights in you, I think.
The spirits spoke of you. Thank you for helping our village. We will provide what support we can to your cause.
I saw bright lights up by the tower. There was something spectactular going on up there. \n\nNo one believes me… but I think it was a battle!
I saw you training a new kind of guardian. Magnificent!
Ah, you ran off without your reward. Here.
The Dominion demands armor, and I provide it. Strongest in Valenwood.
Spare nothing. Waste nothing. The flesh, the hide, the bone: the Green provides.
Say what you will about the Thalmor, they know fine cloth when they see it.
The Thalmor have requisitioned much of his stock, but Puzhbar-jo will provide what he can.
I'm not interested in handling lizards myself. All I care about is the final result of the race.
The new management sounds harsh. Why don't you ease the transition a bit for me? It won't take much, just a few coins.

It seems the merchant with whom I am meeting has been slain, sera. Such a pity. This … dungheap … has been an excellent source of workers for House Telvanni.\n\nSoon, my partner and I will be recalling to Tel Branora to find other such places.
It'll be good to go home!
One thing will never change about Leki's Blade, no matter who the master is. We will still need to read stacks of books every day.

Own no weakness or fault, sera. The caravan's master is dead.\n\nI couldn't be happier. These n'wah slave-merchants always keep such dire, filthy markets. House Telvanni may often be within the ash, but these conditions? Unacceptable to us, always.
By Mauloch! It seems like this dungheap is starting to empty out. Fine by me, these toothless runts were starting to get under my skin.\n\nWant one for the road?
It is a relief to hear that the Caravan is under new management, yes? In celebration, why not buy something?

Oh, five-clawed Khajiit, you are sleek indeed. When next you and this one are in Dune, if you wish for a fine meal and fine company, she will be your host.\n\nCount on that, five-clawed walker. This one had no expectations of you, and you impressed.

Are you the one they sent to aid our cause? Go right on through. This passage will take you to the sanctuary. Major Cirenwe is waiting with further orders. We'll hold this side of the passage to ensure no trouble comes from behind.
I admit I was worried about my cousin, but you have settled the question as to her fate. I'll miss <<1>>, but at least I know what happened to her.
Wolf hide, deer stomach, rucksacks for every occasion.
Make a decision, will you? Mannimarco could return at any moment!
Luala left for training at Tu'Whacca's throne when she was very young. I hope she will agree to see to our plight.
These lands are so lush and green.\n\nAre you looking to trade?
It's so wonderfully warm. A fine day for a bit of trade.
I'm not that bad, tell her I'm not. I can get better.
There are so many dead now. I hope that Luala can bring the Thronekeepers here from Tu'Whacca's Throne.
I have many fine wares for sale and trade.
I will set out for Tava's Blessing as soon as my wounds are set. Thank you for seeking me out.
I'm very glad I was able to find you. Otherwise, my search has yielded nothing. \n\nFrom here, I will journey to the city of Kozanset. Perhaps there are signs of the Withered Hand there.
Come see me when you are done with the siege weapons, warrior.
Thank you for coming, wayfarer. I'm glad you are here.

Well, this has my knickers in a twist! We have a perfectly fine army, but what good is it? Sitting around this side of the Chasm, twiddling its collective thumbs.\n\nIt's rather embarrassing, if truth be told.
Yes, yes, I am far from home. I tired of the smoke and ash of Morrowind and yearned for something new. Now, are you wanting to trade or not?
Oh, thank Y'ffre. I wasn't sure I would find anyone out here. My village needs help. The forest has turned against us!
Astanya can pass word to Her Majesty. Perhaps you can catch a ride on the Prowler. Raz heard Jimila plans to set sail. He suspects she may owe you a favor.
<<1>> is dead, and <<2>> must soon follow. Their fates are tied, you know. For what is a body without the spirit?

Whoever lived here before had a splendid eye for decor. This will suit me just fine.\n\nWe spend so much time worrying about what happens after life when we should be embracing death and the powers that come with it.

The choice of decor was not my own, if that's what you're wondering.\n\nIt would appear that this city had its own worshipers of death. I guess even Meridia did not know everything that went on under her very nose.

The colors in here are so drab. Why did the Groundskeeper send me here? My station requires better accommodations than this!\n\nI can't wait until I'm back home in the Altmer lands. I need to see beautiful colors again.
Rabiza always has the best prices.
The time of battle is fast approaching.\n\nI should have never let myself get comfortable again. Sometimes it's easy to forget that outside these walls, death waits for all of us.

Even though it was a trap, I wish I had had more time to explore the library. Imagine the treasures and knowledge I could have acquired!\n\nAt least Kireth managed to grab a couple of books before we left. I can't wait to start reading them!

It's good to have Raynor back here with me. I … I don't know what I'd do without him.\n\nJust to see him examining maps and thinking up his next device. It makes me really appreciate how far we've come.
Oh, when I find that Stibbons, he … he will hear an earful from me!\n\nHow dare he think he can just vanish and leave me all alone? I'll … he'll … he'll be punished severely for this. Quite severely.

For all the years I've spent researching and looking into just how the planes of Oblivion work, I still find my self astonished at every new discovery.\n\nThat library for instance—I've never experienced a spell quite like that before.
I hear you've been busy, my friend. Good. Very good. \n\nIs that letter for me?
The treethane is just inside. He'll be glad to see you.
We're holding them back, but I took a few hits. Just give me a few minutes to catch my breath.
I can't tell you how glad I am you're here. Something is horribly amiss, and we can't leave this cave without fearing for our lives until it's put right.
I'm sorry for what I did. Isn't it possible to look the other way? Isn't it possible to forgive?
So Treethane Rolon wants you to investigate the violation of the Green Pact. I don't see what there is to investigate. The culprit is plain enough, but I'm happy to help.
Advocate, please take the convicted to the judgment chamber. The Green will decide the fate of the guilty.
It's amazing how similar everything is despite all this time. I suppose there's only so much you can do with hide, bone, and stone.
You have done what we could not—you have restored us to the Green Pact. All is right, even if all is not yet well. Thank you.
Speak with me when you are done with the siege weapons, warrior.
I've been apprised of some concerning news regarding the Maormer operations off the coast.\n\nWe appreciate your efforts, of course. We must also remain focused on the tasks at hand.
Welcome, adept. Mind your step here.
Welcome back, comrade. What news from the field?
Hello, adept. Having a fair day, I hope.
Welcome back, comrade! What's the news?
What is it now?

I'm positively chuffed things have gone so well! To be completely honest, I didn't think we had a ghost of a chance. But then, if we weren't up against overwhelming odds, we wouldn't be heroes, would we?
Aha! I caught you red-handed, Artisan! Thieves just can't help returning to the scene of the crime.
With my heraldic cane back I can show myself in court again. You have my deepest thanks.
Castaril is sleeping peacefully now that you've returned Pluck's pelt. He uses it as a blanket, you know.
Thank you for finding my drinking horn. Cassirion and I drank from it at our wedding. He has forgotten, but I drink to remember.
Everything is here. Wonderful. Allow me a moment to apply our elixir ….
Come to stare at a dying Nord, eh? Hate to disappoint you. None of it's fatal.
The Bishop and Gharesh-ri are already clammoring for my time, my friend. I'm sure we will see each other again. You are the Hallowed, after all.
Who are you? What, you want to chat? Thought this day couldn't get any stranger.

Are you collecting junk for Adamir's little monsters? Good, good.\n\nI make little monsters too. See this? It's a ant-fly-worm beast. I mashed them together and added a pinch of Adamir's life juice. It's an adorably gross little guy, isn't it?
You again? Sorry, I have all the ash I need. Good day!
Nirnroot wine flows again, thanks to you. May the Divines ease your path, wherever you travel!

You are a sight for hollow eyes. Those harpys were going to tear me apart.\n\nBut this isn't over yet. The Roost Mother is just up ahead, and she wields more strength than anyone you've faced so far. Only the Captain himself eclipses her.
You're <<1>>'s friend, right?
You made it! I was beginning to have my doubts, but I trust that the vicereeve will no longer be a threat?
Sounds like we won't need these barricades much longer.
Heard you ran into trouble in <<c:1>>. Sounds like you cleaned up whatever mess the Argonians left.
I haven't seen tracking like that since Haras was leader of the Hounds.
Legend in the Hounds is that there was a Wood Elf named Haras who was the best tracker that ever was. I think you might be in competition for the title now.
You don't understand. He's insane! He'll keep trying to control the undead until he succeeds.
Why did you let <<1>> talk you into this? Do you know how much trouble he's brought to <<Ac:2>>?\n\nMy apologies, his very presence wears at my manners. What do you need?
The captain wants all these supplies catalogued and stowed before we contact the Thalmor. I should really handle this until <<1>> recovers.
If you think you can help us, talk to Treethane Rolon. He is our leader and handles all matters of justice.
Thank you for returning my censer, but I don't know if I want it anymore. There's too many sad memories associated with it now.
Listen, we don't need any more trouble than we already have. But if you want to help, talk to Treethane Rolon.
I once heard Ledronor talking about a great tracker named Haras, from a long time ago. If I didn't know better, I'd think you were him.

This is Brackenleaf's forest you're entering. Pick no fights and respect the shrines and you're welcome to stay as long as you like.\n\nOtherwise, you'll learn quick enough why they call us Brackenleaf's Briars.

You have the blessing—good.\n\nThen with open arms, I welcome you to our family, Brackenleaf's Briars. May you succeed in all your hunts and the great tree keep you in the shade of his leafy branches.
What was it like to fight Master Pellingare's children? Don't tell my boss, but I never liked them.
You're the one who defeated that army down here before, right? We're looking for someone, and could really use your expertise.
You! You're the one who killed my children! You whoreson dog! How dare you show your face here again—I. \n\nHaven't you done enough to my family?

Feel free to return. Soon, I'll have this place looking as grand as it ever did.\n\nAll will be welcome. The locals … perhaps even witches, if they'll look to reform. Drodda claimed that witches are not evil. We'll see.

Brackenleaf is pleased, but you are not finished yet. Each hunter is also prey to another hunter. Wolf hunts tiger and tiger hunts snake and snake hunts wolf.\n\nIt's not enough to hunt your prey. You must also prove stronger than those who hunt you.
Your trial is not complete until you enter my trunk and reach my heart. Are you ready to enter?
We have no quarrel with you, living one. Indeed, we thank you for your part in awakening us. The invaders in the Barrowbough must be stopped!
Survived then, have you? Jolly good, jolly good.

I may not like her, but your Dremora friend has certainly been good to her word. She used her own blood to open the door for us. I've never seen anything like it.\n\nWell, off with you! And remember, we'll be right behind you.
The darkness is obviously designed to hinder our progress. What an interesting conundrum.
Fate brought you to us at this turning point. I'm glad to heed your advice. We must cling to life wherever we find it. You reminded me of that, and I thank you.
Thank you for convincing Erunor to return with us. Thank you so much.
That mage keeps popping up in the strangest places. I'm not sure I trust him. He thinks his boots don't stink, if you take my meaning.\n\nAnyway, I believe he'd like a word with you.
You're trying to go to Coldharbour? I wish I could go with you. I heard there's islands floating in thin air!
The truth is a bitter pill to swallow. Now go. I don't want to speak about this any more.
Do not hasten towards this final hour. Take the time to appreciate the things you have, the friends you have made, and the world that birthed you.
We'll be by your side for the final battle. In the meantime, we'll prepare ourselves and keep the Amulet of Kings safe.
You needn't make the choice now, but when the hour comes, know that we will stand with you and accept your decision.
I'm not going to tell you to put it out of mind. One of these people is going to have to die for you. Can you make that choice, when the time comes?\n\nOr will you fail, to the doom of us all?
Farewell, my brave brother. I will never forget you … and the sacrifice you made for our people.

Magister Wulfdis didn't believe me. He said he was going to have me expelled from the guild if you didn't show up. I'm sure glad you did. \n\nI just hope he doesn't send me out on another impossible assignment.
Good to see you, sera! The Tribunal Priests have been kind enough to open their home to us in our time of need. Try not to break anything.
Hmm. This one smells some magic on you. Do you not sense it? Maybe Magrus licks your face while you sleep! Ha! \n\nWhat is it that you carry?
Praise Vivec! We now possess the six Elder Scrolls. Soon all of Cyrodiil will be ours!
Why, Sameer? Why? You have broken the most sacred tradition of the kingdom!  \n\nNothing can justify such sacrilege. The law is clear, Sameer. Exile. You must leave here now and never return.
Go now. Lord Varen awaits.
I've run these johads since I was a young man. Damned if I'll see them fall to another!
I welcome you to my father's home. Please excuse our scant hospitality. I've been tending to Naseiran day and night, and it leaves little time to prepare for guests.\n\nHow may I aid you?
Good to see you, comrade. Hope you've had ample opportunity to batter around someone deserving.
Welcome, comrade. Help yourself to whatever you need.
Welcome, comrade. A pleasure to share your company again.
What is it, comrade? Make it quick.
Welcome, comrade. The Guild prospers with members like yourself.
Whoever paid off the workers wanted the johads to be out of commission. Sounds like the family has some enemies.
Ahh, it's my comrade in arms! Welcome back to the hall!
I suppose I will have to advance Anenya to the rank of Journeyman now. \n\nGods help us. I hope I don't come to regret this.
Hello hello, comrade! Good to see you!
I'm through being a victim. When my leg heals, I'm heading north, to join the Covenant. Black Daggers won't touch me then.

I feel a measure of peace. I did as much as I could to help my town and the people of Rivenspire.\n\nReezal-Jul was empowering that abomination. Making it stronger. We would not have been able to stop it without your help. I am grateful.
This one would ask if you have found Saifa, but Zaddo sees it in your eyes. Walk your path well.
The moons speak to Saifa. They tell her of your journey, the ceremony, the choice, and the fire.
You'll make the difference here. I've been out in the field for a while now. You get a sense about these things.
We've never had such a thing happen, coming back to battle against Orcs. I'm not the only one eager to leave right away.
Have you seen my father Nedaegar? He's been missing ever since the Orcs attacked.
Now is not the time for us to speak. Listen to the words of Glaras.
Now is not the time for us to speak. Listen to the words of Glaras.
Now is not the time for us to speak. Listen to the words of Glaras.
Your training nears its end. Now to tell you how we capture the enemy's forts and resources.
I'll feel better knowing I didn't leave the mayor of Crestshade completely on her own.\n\nRemember, head into town and look for the mayor's house.

I don't know what you did, but the shades are a bit sluggish. We'll hold off the dig until they return to the ground … if they return.\n\nI should send word back to the Mages Guild. They'll want to know everything.
I'll stay here and warn travelers away from <<Ac:1>>. Don't worry about me, I'll be all right.
What's wrong? What did Varen say?
This <<1>> business is deplorable, so close to <<2>>. No doubt the Mages Guild will take the blame for it all!
You look perplexed. What inscrutable riddles is Varen spouting now?
Sai Sahan wishes to speak with you, Vestige. Be brief. He needs to rest.
I wonder where I should go? What to see? What to do, who to meet?\n\nIt's a little scary, now that I can do it. But I'll figure something out.
The sooner we can get out of this place, the better. I can't take much more of this kind of magical nonsense.
I didn't cut Sanguine Alendil, but I did make a potion from its flowers. I accept the judgment against me.
Will Uta-Tei return to the Hist, or the graht-oaks of her new forest god?\n\nAh. Such discussions are better with a drink in hand.
I would never violate the Green Pact. I have lived by it all my life, it is unthinkable.
Activate the portal in this chamber so that the rest of the troops can join us.
Before we left our home, we thought no good could ever come from Elves.\n\nSometimes it's best to be proven wrong.

I'm not entirely sure what happened, but half of us are dead and we seem to be talking to the Dominion.\n\nAt least all of the tension that's built up seems to be gone. I have a peaceful feeling from this. We will see what happens, it seems.

I-I remember now. I remember it all! Oh gods! What accursed thing did I do? The spell—it trapped me in the tree's form!\n\nIt was a nightmare! Such was the price of my lust for longevity. But now … now I am released!
Not so much arguing anymore. Lots of my friends gone, though.\n\nThat makes me sad.
We have crushed our enemies! All Cyrodiil's keeps belong to the Pact. Consult the other boards for tasks, as we have no Warfront missions now.

You've done well. Permit me to tell you a secret, behind which hides another: Any true Shadowscale is also a true child of the Hist.\n\nThe Hist provides a measure of eternity, true as it also shapes the minds of our people. Think upon this.
Thank you for returning my journal to me. It pains me to think that it ended up in the wrong hands.
This is not how this should have happened … but the Thalmor have said we can stay.\n\nTime will tell if they come with whip and brand. Then we will know how right Slim-Jah was.
The Argonians are innocent of murderous habits, I hear. Good. May we leave this mire to them and move on. \n\nIf you need anything from our supplies, do let me know.
The cursed axe worked even better than I expected!
This is even better than I hoped! Think of all the fringe benefits! I don't need to worry about food, water, or even the heat anymore!\n\nBut most important, I still get to be with my sweet Musi!
Lieutenant Fairfax needs those healing supplies. A lot of our soldiers were wounded in the surprise attack.
You wished me to remain in my home, and I will. But my servants cannot distinguish you from an intruder.\n\nGo … take the portal to the relic thieves, and do not trouble us further.
Hmm. Perhaps if I tweak the mixture ….
<Ragged breathing is the only sound coming from this Bosmer.>
It's time, isn't it?\n\nI'm ready for anything! I can't wait to see what's inside the lair of a Daedric Prince. Is that what he calls it? His lair? Yes, that sounds right!
This trial has been hard on all of us. Please help us find closure, advocate.
Your evidence was indisputable, advocate, but it's still hard to believe. Hurry to the judgment cave. The sooner this is resolved, the better.
Forgive Sai Sahan for his anger. Ultimately it was Lyris's decision, and her sacrifice to make. He'll come to realize that, eventually.
We did it. Tamriel will go on. But what a terrible price we had to pay.
So, this is where our roads diverge.
Are you insane? Don't stop to chat with me, get up there!
It's almost over. There is just one more thing to do. The convicted must be brought to the judgment chamber.
Five-claw! Adusa is glad to see you again, my friend!
Lead on, then. Take me where you will.
You got one of them, but what about the rest? You have to keep digging! Find the full truth!
I'm not surprised at all by how this turned out.
Oh, a fellow member of the guild. Well met. I'm here searching for a few others of our order. I don't suppose you've crossed paths with them, hm?
Any last words for the prisoner?

Mortal, you stand above the sealed ruins of <<1>>. Within is a gateway to <<2>>, where my priestess <<3>> suffers at the hands of Molag Bal. Her pain is so great, it has torn a hole between worlds.\n\nThis injustice must end.
Greetings, outsider. As the will of my Prince is eternal, I heed your call.
Ah, by the look on your face, Adusa assumes you were successful? The vampire commander is dead, yes?
<The sapling does not stir. Its leaves are shriveled and wilted. It looks quite dead.>

Well. How fascinating. It will end a lot of controversy back in Orsinium. \n\nFunny how quick every clan is to claim credit for the work of a gang of bandits. Everyone wants to know who will get the glory.
I heard Gargak is dead. You didn't happen to bring his head back, did you? We could mount it on our walls, here.\n\nIt'd be fitting.
Heard Gargak's dead. Good. Still feels like there's a snake in my guts.\n\nDoesn't feel good, by the way. In case you were wondering, feels pretty bad.
Gargak's dead? That was you? He wasn't so strong after all.
Gargak had a chance to redeem himself in Malacath's eyes after the dual dishonor of failure and poison, but he died.\n\nSounds about right.
Razum-dar was quite adamant that he wanted to see you as soon as possible. \n\nI would prefer not to delay you any longer.
Well, I guess things are settled. Gargak dead, we can get back to our mine and our affairs.\n\nSpeaking of affairs, I'm an armorsmith. If that's your kind of thing, let's talk.
Queen Ayrenn awaits you at Hectahame. Hurry to her aid.
Shakul and I have forged many weapons to defend ourselves. With Gargak dead, we won't need them all for the stronghold.
If Gargak won the duel, our stronghold wouldn't be so weak.\n\nI'm drinking to his memory. Join me, if you've got the coin.
Better to end Gargak's rabble, I suppose. Need anything?
With Gargak dead, things can get back to normal. Hungry? No poison, I swear.
I do not know you. Why are you here? Who sent you?
Adusa wishes she could go with you, but Verandis has other tasks for this one to perform.
Leave me to my suffering! It is only compounded by you standing around gawking like a child.

I was wondering if you were going to make it. I hired one of these little boats to ferry me down the Bay. Whatever it takes to get as far away from that trolls' den as possible.\n\nIt's expensive, but I have the coin to spare now.
If you and Adusa hadn't shown up, we all would have fallen to those monsters.
I made sure we got out of Moira's Hope without incident. Well, the Khajiit helped. A little. But I wouldn't make a big deal about it.
Comrade, you've done it. I am free. Free from Ragnthar's barrier, and that dark cat's shackles.
Stop. I must alert the mayor to all new arrivals.
Forgive me for not getting up. It's been a long day, and I'm ravenous.\n\nIs there something you need? Are you new too?
I thought for sure we were done with all this. I followed the others through the portal, and now look what I've gotten involved with! This looks like the end of the world!
Did I hear that right? We're going to blow the vortex apart?\n\nGreat! But how do we get out of here once the light explodes? Please tell me you have an idea!
If we had known this was happening, maybe my people could have stopped it. Valenwood is part of Nirn, after all.\n\nBut that's probably just wishful thinking.
Are you sure we need to destroy these chains? They add a nice flare to this otherwise dismal setting. Oh very well, let's get to it!
Always be thinking before speaking. An audience enlightened may not be the right audience.
Please! At least make sure they let me loose when the battle starts! I can help fight!
The people eye the north with fearful eyes, but it's from the south that the storm approaches.
All Sentinel will be thrilled at the return of the Memory Stone. It is a sacred relic, you know?\n\nI will tell the king your name so he will know who did this.
Did you really just talk to that crow? You must be drunker than I am …!
Death needs time to grow what it kills.
The Divines saw fit to send you and your friend to save us, but how could they allow something like this to happen in the first place?
Funny boat, funny business. I want to see what's in the hold too.
Moramat has told me what you've already done for us, outlander, but I have to ask… is it done? Is Gargak dead?
Mark the men who would turn this city Imperial. Signal my black-feathered followers to strike. The rest on you lies.
Be careful out there. The bloodfiends are pretty mindless and easy enough to put down, but those vampires are cunning and fast.\n\nAnd then there are the bats. I hate bats.
Give the Captain my regards!
Pray that your decision to save my … sister … wasn't a mistake. I shall look to Arkay for tolerance, but I'm not sure I'll ever accept that this vampire is really Janeve.
So your journey begins. I wish you safe travels. Let our blessing aid you on your path.
<<1>> barred all entry from the cathedral.\n\nSorry, orders.
The scouts you rescued brought reinforcements from <<1>>. We subdued the townsfolk for their own protection.\n\nTell me, what happened in the cathedral?

It seems <<1>> held up his end of the deal. I felt his … absence, I should likely say. I was able to open a portal here without any difficulty.\n\nI tried to tell <<2>> what happened, but he wouldn't listen.
Thanks for saving my hide. They were trying to find a big enough pot to boil me!

And that's why you're my new favorite mortal. When you kill something wonderful, you keep it interesting. Fresh! Dare I say, jovial?\n\nMakes me wonder if I should stick around, see what wonderful things you'll kill next.
What are you doing here? I don't know you.
It's not fair! I never wanted this, any of this, and now I'm to die for it!\n\nBut you're reasonable, aren't you? We can talk about this, work something out?

Ah, there you are! The Groundskeeper said you had a pickup. I assume she was talking about this merry band?\n\nGood to see them alive and well. They are alive … right? Not that I mind the odd zombie. It's the smell I can't abide. Nasty, that.
Do you need directions, hero? The ruins are in the Lorkrata Hills, northeast of Shornhelm, just beyond Traitor's Tor.\n\nNow get moving. Verandis will meet you there.

And so we've come full circle. I led the original Five Companions on a quest to reclaim the Amulet of Kings. At the time, I told myself it was for the good of all Tamriel. \n\nI was wrong and now all the world suffers for my hubris.
Zeht's tears, I thought I could handle this! Mannimarco's sorcery brought back all of the pain and doubt I felt inside the Halls of Torment.
You better keep an eye on me. I'm getting ready to punch Tharn again.
Welcome back! Please pardon the mess.
Have you satisfied your contract? There are fewer Black Daggers to plague us?
I trust you have fulfilled the contract on the Black Daggers.
Well? Here to tell me of piles of Black Dagger corpses left in your wake?
I understand your anger, Vestige, but I hope you will give me the opportunity to make reparations for my transgressions. My intentions are honorable, I promise you.
Varen and I have work to do, but you and I will talk again very soon.
I saw that vampire in action. He's extremely deadly. You're going to have a real battle on your hands when you get up to the house.
You pulled me from the pits of Oblivion. I owe you a debt of honor, small one. And a Titanborn pays her debts.
When the time comes, I will call upon you once more.\n\nI won't advise you to travel safely—I know you too well. But keep your wits about you, and learn.
My sister-in-law is feeling a little better. She's almost back to her old self and talking up a storm. Thanks to you.
I'll stay with Sai and Kasura. Get the ring back to the Harborage. We'll meet you there as soon as we can.
We've done it. We have the ring, and we're one step closer to recovering the Amulet of Kings. We might just pull this off.

The shades seem to have weakened, but that hasn't stopped them from probing this camp.\n\nDoesn't matter how long it takes, we'll keep the mages safe so they can get back to their dig. Orders are orders.
I was beginning to wonder if I'd ever see you again. Any news?
Truly you do the Eight's work. Thank you.
You do Eight's work, traveler. Thank you!
We'll find Sai Sahan, and if Mannimarco gets in our way, I'll chop that sniveling knife-eared puddle of troll piss into little bite-sized pieces.
Sergeant Antieve's at the west gate, by the bridge to Stormhaven.
Sai Sahan served me well for many long years. It saddens me to think of the tortures he endures, I'm heartened to know that he has not been broken.
Thank you.
Thank you.\n\nI've lost track of the days. I feel so hollow.
I'll feel better knowing someone went to check on the mayor of Crestshade.\n\nRemember, head north and look for the mayor's house. That's probably where you'll find her.
Give me a few moments to catch my breath and I'll be back on my feet in no time.

Did I overhear correctly? Fahara'jad asked you to go to Evermore? \n\nSounds like that place is shaping up to be a real trouble spot. I wish I could come along, but the guild's got me doing something else. Probably not nearly so interesting.
I, for one, am very glad Fahara'jad sent you. Many here in Evermore believe the rest of the Covenant has forgotten us.
The attack was sudden and terrible. I don't know what the world is coming to.\n\nThey didn't steal anything, though, and I still need to make a living. So feel free to browse my wares.
You can't believe how tired I am of getting attacked and chased by those Eight-cursed monsters!\n\nI just want to go somewhere safe.
Etienne is dead? And, … Squire Theo says the healer is at fault, and dead.\n\nIt is not truly justice, but it is done.
I'm told there's a dead witch somewhere in the village. Good.\n\nIt's what witches deserve, when this is what they bring.
I've heard about what happened. All of this death all around us, and you killed her, a skilled healer, too. I'll never understand war.
That huge witchman was the Zurric woman's son? Stendarr's Mercy, at least he's dead.\n\nDo you suppose she was some sort of spy? Or did she think she was protecting her home?
What a mess. This whole affair … We should just go, put all this death behind us.
Well, good! Now to clear them all out. All of them, from everywhere.

So I heard you killed her son in front of her, then Squire Theo cut her down.\n\nThat's pretty cold. Be glad she wasn't an Orc, she would've torn Squire Theo's arms off and carved her son's name in your chest.
Medya Zurric delivered my brother's children. She was a good woman and you killed her.\n\nBut my house is still on fire. I guess I don't know what to think anymore.

Medya Zurric was a witch? Well I'm glad she's dead, her and her witchman son! If there were three more of her I'd want them all dead!\n\nLook at my home! Just look at it! She deserves everything she got, I tell you. All of it.
It seems everywhere I land, you turn up. Or is it the other way around?
Can you believe we're standing in King Fahara'jad's palace? You may have to pinch me.
What do we have here? A legend among heroes! You're looking good.
My friend! How good to see you here. Have a drink with us! Help us celebrate!\n\nTelonil worked his magic. We have our own ship. We're a crew again. Soon, we'll be back on the sea.
Once again, well met. I hope you are enjoying the warm air of Sentinel. I find it quite bracing, myself.
My friend! My friend. Oh, it is good to see you. I have had the most horrid month.
I hate my life.
The wind and the water smile upon you, my friend. I had not expected visitors. What brings you once again to the Spearhead?
This one greets you, five-clawed walker. Your reputation grows.
Hey, look who it is. I see you're still kicking. I'm glad, but I'm also jealous.\n\nJust for once, I'd like to leave the boat.
Welcome to the Sisters of the Sand! Enjoy your stay, and let me know if you need anything.
All these clothes. All this jewelry. Whatever is a poor Bosmer to do?

She's gone. Lakana. She was the bravest of us. She was our hope.\n\nI've heard only rumors surrounding her demise. I don't know who cut her down. But mark me, friend … if I find him, he'll suffer a lengthy death.

Have you come to pay your respects? If so, I thank you. I am glad to see you here.\n\nNo man should lose his daughter, least of all a king. It is a sad day for Sentinel, but Lakana lives on. She lives now in our hearts.
Hey, good-looking.
At last. We're finally going to explore a real set of ruins, just Neramo and Clanker and me, and Clanker doesn't take a split.\n\nI'm so looking forward to this.
What an interesting collection of tomes.
You did it. You always do. You have my thanks.
That woman is incredible. She saved my life.
Sentinel. I never thought I'd see it. The world is full of wonders, and thanks to you, I'm seeing them one by one.\n\nToday, I'm going exploring!
I've never been to a market like this. It's so … quaint. Redguards are remarkably polite, considering the war.\n\nYou did well on the docks. Quite well indeed.
My friend! Welcome. I want to introduce you to my wife.
I thought my husband was lost. I mourned. Now he is returned to me, and he has told me everything.\n\nYou have given me back my life and his. Words cannot express my gratitude. Walk with Tall Papa.
Is there a reason you're poking around inside my house? 'Cause I can poke back if I have to.
Thank you for speaking to us, young one.\n\nWe need to speak among ourselves now. The story you tell is quite … disturbing. Now we must decide if it's true.
As promised, I will consider what you've told me.\n\nMy thanks to you for bringing this to our attention.
You have spoken. I have listened.\n\nNow we are finished here. Move along.
I must say it is good to see Queen Arzhela back upon the throne. Hopefully those filthy Reach barbarians won't cut her reign short.
Ah, I have seen you before! Were you not the one who drove the Ra-Netu from Sentinel? \n\nYes, it is you! A thousand thousand thanks, my friend!

You seem very confused, and I am terribly sorry for that, but I'm not lying to you—I've never seen you before.\n\nI hate to be rude, but if this this is the book, would you mind letting me take it back to the Mages Guild?
Queen Arzhela will make a fine ruler … perhaps better, even, than her late husband.
So the duke was fouling his nest right under my tusks. By Mauloch, I knew something smelled rotten. \n\nI won't let it happen again. Trust me.
Thank the Eight our queen has returned. \n\nIt's a small miracle she didn't die of exposure in that drafty old chapel.
The people celebrate now that our absentee queen has retaken the throne.\n\nUnfortunately, joy won't fill an empty stomach or rebuild a home.

Once <<1>> is secured at the <<2>> Mages Guild, I hope to aid <<3>> in locating her Walking City.\n\nTo think, I came here to visit a friend. Yet I leave with a great purpose. Does all adventure have such a strange beginning?
So you found those dirty Orcs in Torog's Spite, eh? Good on you, chum. \n\nNow about these other allegations … I swear I never touched that horse!
Perhaps I shouldn't have used Stibbons' blood …. He must have gotten caught in the spell somehow. Ah well, I'm sure I can figure out a way to undo it eventually.
Impressive … for an outsider.
Well, look at what the wolf dragged in. I certainly wasn't expecting to see you again so soon.\n\nOf course, you're always welcome here, as far as I'm concerned.
Without <<1>>, the soldiers have released us from service. We may continue our pilgrimage.
So the Imperials want this city? I say let them have it. We can all amble away while they're still busy raking up the bird droppings. Auri-El knows that'll take an army.
Thank the Eight I can see the sun again. \n\nI'll never look at those birds the same way, though.
Anisha is depressed. All the tasty crows have flown away. Now she must go back to eating bland dungy porridge.
Thank the Eight—our long black feathery nightmare is over. Now we can go back to complaining about the gulls.
Captain Hjurrun's just around the wall there at the south gate.\n\nI wish I could be there to see the look on his face when you bring him that head. It's gonna be great!
By the Three, our rights and duties. Welcome, comrade. I trust your blade has a few new notches in it?
Welcome to the Evermore Guild Hall, comrade. \n\nThe thrice-cursed Daedra continue to grow in power. You must have the best arms and armor if you are to defeat them.
Hail, comrade. If you happen to slay a daedroth, give it a good kick from me! I'm still nursing a bite wound from my last outing.
Ha har! What's this? Another big-footed pup come up for training? Tell Larhoth all about it.

We can dispense with the small talk. I know why you're here. Even in the nature realm, news travels fast among crows.\n\nGetting to Uela is impossible though. Even if you break her wards, entering her domain will corrupt your soul.
Don't mind the dust—I'm just doing a bit of sorting. \n\nI understand you're a member in good standing. Would you care to look over my wares?
Hmm … I sense you've come to the Mages Guildhall for a reason. What have you got there?
I had a feeling that was going to end in blood—I didn't know it would be like that, though!\n\nI feel bad for my guildmates.
My next personal project … I'm going to figure out how to open two portals at once.
You come seeking knowledge, yes? The Mages Guildhall is the place for you!
If you hear anything of Falinesti in your travels, please send word to <<1>>. I expect I'll be traveling with him for quite some time.\n\nAfter all, I am quite adept at driving off the frost trolls.
You're new, aren't you? I saw you leaving the guest house.\n\nAnything I can do to ease your transition?
Maybe with this Imperial nonsense taken care of we can get some decent provisions. I was maybe one day away from eating my cat.
Welcome to the Marbruk Mages Guild. We recently established this branch, so we're always looking for new members.
Welcome to the Woodhearth Mages Guild. Are you interested in uncovering the forgotten lore of Tamriel?
I'm no fan of the Empire, but if they can wipe out the Reach clans and send me back to my farm … I don't know. Maybe the duke was right.
It is good that you revealed the duke's treachery, wayfarer. It is unclear what became of him, however. Were we in the Alik'r, his punishment would be both public and brutal. \n\nI miss the desert.
I hardly thought Queen Arzhela had the strength to preside over a meal, let alone an entire state. I tell you though—I've never been so happy to be wrong.
Staying in the guest house, are you? I'm sure your induction will go smoothly. Most of them do.
Ah! You're staying with us? How nice! If <<1>> can help you in any way ….
You're new here. Watch yourself, running about and bothering folks. We don't take kindly to nosy people.
I'll recover. Just find the intruders and make them pay!
Greetings, guildmate. It is good to see you still among the living. Take some hard-earned rest or resupply—our battle is far from over.
Well now, that is a relief! To think I might have lived out the rest of my days that way.
Ah, I was told that I might encounter you hereabouts! You do not know of me, but I know of you.
I hear we may be able to return home soon. Is it too much to hope?
Greetings, comrade!
As always, you're welcome to rest and rearm yourself.\n\nDon't tarry too long, though—there's plenty of killing to be done!
So many things to do! Adusa doesn't have enough hours in the day.\n\nPerhaps you could lend a hand, my friend. You help Adusa, yes?
Leave me alone. I'm only here for the wine.
I'm just trying to have a quiet drink.
Can't you just leave a man to his drinks?
What can I do for you?
The Mad Architect waits below.
You've had quite the glimpse into our world. A bit more then Wyress Freyda or myself would ever be comfortable with, but luckily, for all our sakes, you've proven yourself trustworthy.
Sahan doesn't look well at all. Keep an eye on him.

Oh, it's you. So I guess I didn't really mean what I said about taking your legs off. I mean, you'd get mine first, ha!\n\nChampions must be busy people, fighting all the time. So, go on and fight! And fight often!
No need to alarm yourself, friend. This is merely an illusion, and all part of the treethane's plan. \n\nSpeak to Fariel. She'll explain everything.
We've heard a lot about you, Queen's Eye. Have a word with Fariel. She's been waiting for you to arrive.
Thank you for all you've done here. Today has given me a lot to reflect on.
You found them both and returned safely. Thanks to you, I still have a sister.
Stendarr must be in a giving mood today.
I know the Evermore soldiers will appreciate any help I can get. Last I heard, they were spread thin.\n\nAs for me, I may just take the long way around into Evermore.
I hear we're to be allies with the city dwellers now. I suppose if it saves our home, it's for a good cause. Especially with the added bonus of ridding ourselves of the Reachmen.

I'll caution you—don't expect a warm welcome from my sisters in the north. \n\nThey are not accustomed to city dwellers in the wilds, but they need all the help they can get. Whatever it takes to rid these lands of that Hagraven.
This alliance is foreign to us. I think we're all concerned about working together, but at least our common enemy is worth it.
I pray the wyrd can help me. I don't know what the Reachmen did to me, but this darkness they speak of …. It's as if I can feel it. I've never been so scared.
That must be why Elgenie's poultice didn't fully heal me. I wasn't conscious for a while after they captured me. He had time to … to ….\n\nIs what Wyress Delphique says true?
What brings you to my husband's grave? I don't think we ever met.
Did Countess Tamrith give you a poultice for me? I could use a little something to dull this pain.
We meet again, ally of the Viridian Sentinel. Now you seek to subjugate these woods once again. We will see if you can succeed.
What do we have here? I think I see a fellow lover of adventure, and I'm betting it's no accident that you're headed this way.\n\nAm I right? Have Rivenspire's troubles become your troubles too?

Ha! The Baandari scouts said they could see the flames from here! Let's celebrate!\n\nActually, I hope you don't mind, but I went ahead and started celebrating. After everything that's happened here, I deserved a drink. Silver-Paws did, too.
Don't worry about me. We should keep moving. Can't stop moving.
Oh, look at you! This one tells me you're some big winner. That is … impressive. I am impressed.\n\nPlease, retire. I should hope to have some chance of your title.
It is done. No one shall ever suffer at the hands of this accursed creation again.
You have shown me more kindess than I deserve. I shall spend my remaining days attempting to atone and truly honor my son's memory.
The soldiers must stay here. They must hold this position or all will be lost.

My fellow Baandari said they saw the Imperial boats burning down by the water. You have certainly turned things around here.\n\nThe Knight Commander was quite eager to start celebrating. I don't mind humoring her.
Thanks for your intervention at Northglen. \n\nOnce these soldiers recover, we'll mop up any filthy Reachmen that remain.
Stonefalls is lucky to have our strong arms and sharp blades. It must look like home to Molag Bal. At least, that's my explanation for all the anchors.
I've heard some crazy stories, but the way those bandits robbed the town—posing as the constable and his deputy—that's just pure madness.
I have to say, I'm not too keen on having a mayor that was so quick to compromise with bandits. \n\nI know they were holding his wife, but … well, that's another reason I'm not getting married.
So the constable's got her old job back? Am I supposed to offer her a toast? I don't think so.
When a woman opens up to you and really lets herself be vulnerable, that's your chance. You just have to take it.
Gods! What happened to Miss Mondorie is so unfair. It could have been any of us too!
Gods! This bread … it's amazing! I mean, I've never had such good bread!\n\nI think it's the town miller. Ghak really knows his trade.
I've been waiting for my husband to return from Northpoint for weeks. If something happened to him, I just don't know what I would do with myself.
I thought the mayor had fired Agazu because she was an Orc. Sad as all this was, I'm glad to learn that's not the case.
I'm so glad someone will finally listen to me. My husband never wanted to do anything more than share my bed.
What happened to Lady Mondorie is unforgiveable!\n\nSomeone has to do something about Rivenspire's bandit problem. They just have to!
I'm glad Constable Agazu got her job back. She almost drank all my reserves in one night!
I heard the mayor stepped down from office. Who's going to keep the streets clean now?

Thank the moons! As I was just explaining, that thief nearly ran us over. You chased after him.\n\nPlease, tell this fine keeper of the peace what you saw. I'm still sore from the last night I spent in the stocks!
Not to worry, citizen. This fleabitten scoundrel will not trouble you. Jode's Chariot will see to that.
Now that Shornhelm is secure, we can turn our attention to the reports coming in from the rest of Rivenspire. Something definitely unusual is going on out there.
The Eight Divines are running a little behind.\n\nWe mustn't mention it when they arrive. It's important to remain polite when in the presence of divinity.
The Light has shown us the way. It has restored Shornhelm and it will see us through to the ultimate defeat of Baron Montclair.
They came into my house. Tried to take my fire from me.\n\nSo I showed them. The fire is a part of me, now. It will always be inside me!

The priest fears the unknown. That is why he refuses to acknowledge the gift the prince has been given.\n\nBut why do you submit to this priest's direction? Are you a coward, or do you just prefer not to think for yourself?

The town's safe, I guess. It's a wreck, and nobody who was crazy really seems to be getting better.\n\nI guess I need to think about my future from this point. But, let's look on the bright side. Look at how many things I have to sell!
Oh, I suppose I heard the mayor did all this. I suppose he must've gone a little mad.\n\nWe all go a little mad, now and then. Perfectly normal. Do you know when he will be back?
It's at times like these when my commitments as a priest are truly tested. I will support my community and continue prayers until Southpoint is restored to its previous glory.
The constable says my job is just to sit here and look pretty.\n\nI think I'm doing that fairly well.
If you could find a way to get all those corpses back in the ground while you're up there, I sure would appreciate that.\n\nI can't make a living if I can't get into the graveyard!
Pardon my saying so, but you are obviously doing well for yourself. What brought you here?
Finally, the town has started to settle down. Maybe I can hear myself think now.
Deepswimmer just went for one more dive! He came back to find this troll eating all his friends!\n\nPraise the moons you came along! Did you come from the Martyr's Crossing?
Paws of Rajhin tread with you, my friend.
Don't feel bad for me. I got what was coming to me.\n\nI trusted Peras.

That was a timely rescue. If you hadn't come by, slavers would have hauled us halfway across Tamriel by next week.\n\nProbably would've learned a lot from the trip—would've seen a lot, too. As slaves.
Thank you for freeing us. I didn't think bandits would ever want anything with a couple of scholars on a boat.\n\nWhy would you ever board a ship with Peras on it? Come to think of it, why did I?

While you go to Camp Tamrith and help deal with Reezal-Jul, I shall look into the gaps in my memory that you helped uncover. There must be something important in the hills to the east. Why else would the mad Argonian have taken those memories?
I knew my neighbors were innocent! Now maybe things around here can get back to normal.

Of course! You can go to Hallin's Stand! Fabulous idea!\n\nYes, my friend. The key to driving the Imperials out of southern Bangkorai will be finding and … eliminating the Magus General. If you'll track Septima down, we'll be halfway done.
Whatever's in the crypt, it must be destroyed. Whether it be Imperial, undead, Daedra … just kill it. Kill it all.
It is as they say—the Hollow Moon provides, yes?
You look like someone who appreciates strong leadership. That's in short supply around here, but I'm sure you already noticed that.
A good day at the market! Sula will be so happy!
There's usually not much happening in the village, but today's an exception, isn't it?\n\nYou don't need to buy anything, do you?
I thought I recognized you! You were right in the middle of those Imperial bastards. \n\nAnd, hey … didn't you also kill that hag back in Jackdaw Cove? By Stendarr's shield, I'm talking to a legend!
What's taking so long? I can only wait around for so long!
Maybe next time, those maul-brained rock-herders will bring me some food! Squirrels can only last you so long, you know?
Do you smell that? The air here, it's almost sweet.\n\nBe wary. There are vampires about and that smell means they're on the prowl. It's best you didn't wander alone.
… Can't, I can't … I ….
Self sacrifice is rare these days. I hope Captain Gaercroft is finally proud of his daughter. Not that he wasn't. Perhaps now he'll finally show just how much she meant to him.
His shaking has slowed. Perhaps, when he wakes, he will be cured of his addiction.
Tell me, have you seen my nose? I think it must have fallen off somewhere. I can't smell a thing.
Have you found Puddles yet? She enjoys chasing sheep, so you might look for her near livestock.
And what do you want? Come to stare at the fallen warrior?
By the Eight! Can you feel the relic's power, Verandis?
Such foul creatures! I hope no one gets hurt because of me.
And yet again, we will teach someone to guard that which guards its own.
With the Mad Architect gone, I'll admit … this place has a homey look.\n\nI've work to do. If I could learn what he learned—perhaps I could fill his role.
Have to say, a little violence and mayhem always clears my head. It's exhilirating!
Do you smell that? The air here, it's almost sweet.\n\nBe wary. There are vampires about and that smell means they're on the prowl. It's best you didn't wander alone.
We shall see to it that the Viridian Sentinel learns what it means to be a guardian of the woods.
Can I finish my prayer please? I think you have things to do.
You are the one who liberated Hallin's Stand, is it not so? Your deeds are known to us here. Ruptga's blessings be upon you.
Thank you, my friend. For all you've done.\n\nBut it seems our hardship isn't over yet.
Thank you for helping us. There's … not much else you can do.\n\nI hope Gasteau has a plan. Staying here seems … unwise.
We raise hardy horses here in the Rift, and hardier people. Can I interest you in one of our fine animals?
You'll find no better steed in all the Rift! My Pa breeds nothing but the best.
Greetings, walker. This one sees that you have a five-clawed look. You wish to join the Guild, yes?
This place is abysmal. Hardly anything to read. Buzzards squawking day and night. Say … what's that you're carrying?
Hold a moment. What business have you in Bangkorai Garr—oh. A thousand pardons, I didn't recognize you. Welcome back, sir.
This one thinks the knights are lucky the Baandari were here!

I can't thank you enough for ridding Pelin Graveyard of the Prince's treachery. \n\nIt's bad enough that our knights get killed by Imperial dogs. Having them raised as undead is more than I could bear.
I've hired other adventurers to gather more information for my second book, the Bigger Book of Bloodfiends, but I need you for a special task.
Sleek fighting, walker. You and Crazy Eye make a good team.
Watch where you step. Bandit corpses get a little mushy.

The war is far from over, but we've won a crucial battle. Definitely gave the Imperials a black eye. \n\nAnd Evermore is safe. I should return there, but I have a feeling Emeric will want to press on to liberate Southern Bangkorai.
Is that really my great-grandmother's sword? She was a mighty warrior, or so the stories say.
You have it, yes? The treasure?
We raise fine horses in Davon's Watch. Once sold one to Vivec himself. What can I help you with?
Stay your hand and hear my words. Dominion, Pact, Covenant—you're like schoolchildren fighting over marbles, while the world around you is on fire.
Ah, a hatchling in search of wisdom. Are you acquainted with the Mages Guild, my friend? You would do well to join us. What is it that that you carry?
Meet Adusa at Montclair Manor, Five-Claws. It's in Shornhelm's upper city. This one must clean up here first, or Verandis will become very cross. He hates it when we play with our food.
<Cariel's bottle no longer holds a message. It now sits empty, a nonsequiteur for the next passerby.>

Sometimes I wonder if such a narrow field of study has stunted my growth as a mage. Perhaps there's more to life than just portals.\n\nThen I think of how instrumental they were in ending the Blacksap Rebellion. Makes it all worthwhile.

Adusa is so happy she could just purr! The fighting, the blood, the excitement—Adusa hasn't had so much fun in an Elf's age!\n\nAnd, yes, we ended another threat to Rivenspire. That, too. All in all, Adusa had a fine, fine day.
I'm glad you came to your senses about <<1>>. He asked me to verify any ore we find, so here I am.\n\nLet's get this over with.

You! You were the one who slipped that draught into my mug, were you not? I cannot believe I fell for that. \n\nThis isn't right, you know. It was the oppressiveness of Redguard society that drove me to become a bandit. Yes. I blame society.
Leave me alone. I'm only here for the wine.
You know, now that he's gone, I almost miss the way that bailiff stared at my bottom. No one else around here seems to even notice me anymore.
I'm just trying to have a quiet drink.

Yes. I would say our experiment was quite a success. I bet you want another one of those trinkets, don't you?\n\nWell, don't fret. I'm going to craft crates of the things! Look for me on the road. I might even give you one on the house.
Can't you just leave a man to his drinks?
I'm working up the nerve to go back over to my usual chair at the table. I just keep thinking I hear that bailiff coming back.
What can I do for you?
It may take time, but these traitors will have their day in the sun.
Find that man of mine, will you? Next time he wanders off with the pup, he's going to have to get Xandier to drag him back.
You know, when I was attacked by those wolves, the thought crossed my mind that I might never see my Nathalye again. I … I don't know how to thank you.
<<<1>> bounces back and forth and does a little spin. He looks like he wants you to follow.>
The Eight guide you. The jouney there may not be easy.
Montclair started this war, but I plan to finish it. My soldiers will be ready to move at a moment's notice.
I regret I could not give you more, but I have little. Service to Arkay is its own reward.
I can't believe the Knight Commander's willing to give those bows to those backstabbing Baandari. I'm going to report this to … well, to someone.
I'm very sorry. I wish we could do more for the Garrison.
So the brave Baron Dorell is your choice then. I know he's valiant warrior and I expect he will make a wise and honorable king. \n\nKing Alard of Shornhelm. It even has a nice ring to it.
As long as there are rotting corpses, I'll have a job.
My family is indebted to you.\n\nI remember your goodwill after our trial declares me the rightful king of Valenwood.

We've come through much to reach this point. We won a battle for the very soul of Rivenspire.\n\nNow comes the responsibility of rebuilding the kingdom. I hope High King Emeric gives me the opportunity to lead us through the difficulties ahead.

It's a miracle that we survived and triumphed over Montclair. Thanks, in no small part, to my steady leadership.\n\nMay Arkay grant the High King the wisdom to see that I am the best choice to lead Rivenspire.
You have proven most useful, unlike most mortals before you.
Look at that spire. Rather menacing, don't you think? I should be nervous, but the thought of climbing up there … it's pretty exciting!
Interesting item, this Orb of Discourse. I must find a way to use it to determine the location of Sai Sahan.
If anybody can find out where they're holding Sai, the Prophet can. We'll find him.
I'll see you on the other side, my friend. Stay safe out there.
<<1>> is honored! Tell me, what have you brought? Spices? Gemstones, perhaps?
The worst part of ending the Blacksap threat? Now is when I need to be most vigilant. Convincing yourself the snake has no fangs is usually when it learns to constrict.

You were the one who tried to talk me into moving to Shornhelm and doing some honest work, weren't you?\n\nI am so glad I didn't do that. We're making more coin than I ever dreamed possible now. And to think, I almost quit right before the miracle.

I'm expecting you to come back here with at least a few Reachmen heads hanging from your belt. \n\nWe can mount them on the city walls. I wonder what Captain Hjurrun did with old Strastnoc's head … we should get that one up there too.
We need to give you a nickname. Something like "The Knife."\n\nHmm. How about "The Doomsmasher?" That sounds a little dark, I guess. I'll think about it.

After a long talk with the Countess, it was decided that it would be best if I looked for other employment.\n\nI think she was just having a hard time dealing with her feelings for me. I expect she'll get all weepy when I'm gone.
<<<1>> bounces back and forth under your hand. He looks like he wants you to follow.>
The longer I'm here, the better that mead looks. I think I might head back to Fell's Run soon.
Please, look for my family. I miss my dear <<1>>!\n\nAnd <<2>>, of course.
I knew <<1>> wouldn't leave me. We've spent a lot of time in  my wife's homeland of <<2>>, so the unusual fauna here must have spooked him a bit.
So my lady convinced you to help her? Of course she did. She's ever so good at that.\n\nWell, be careful in there. I'll save you some stew for when you get back.
Take good care of the Champions, Hallowed. We are all counting on you. Until Dune, then.
The Champions are in your hands, Hallowed. Keep them safe, and be careful. The path to the Mane is fraught with danger, heartbreak, and sacrifice.
Though I am the last of Alvaren's knights, I remain steadfast in his cause.
I was just about to go in after you. Thought maybe you were stuck in a cage or something.
A new recruit, eh? I hope you can keep pace. The blood will run fast and thick when the vampires attack, and I can't watch your back and mine.
Are you ready to take the sword to these aberrations, Oblivion's own children?
Thanks for helping Garth. I'd offer you something to drink, but we drank it all.
Oh, Divines, it was terrible. The spider queen was huge. She had sixteen legs! Or was I seeing double?\n\nThank you for saving me.
<<1>> is of such importance to <<2>>. I've heard the stories since I was a child, and always wondered what would happen should it be restored.\n\nI suppose I'll learn very soon.
<<1>> has finally arrived. Just in time for the ratification ceremony to begin.\n\nI'm sure she will commend you for your efforts.
I suppose a wanderer like you wouldn't know what "busy" looks like.\n\nI will demonstrate. Feel free to observe. Quietly, and from a distance.
Ohh … Mara bless me. Are you real?
So much death, so many lost dreams. They never told me the world was full of so much grief.\n\nBut there I go again. Gurlarz would be ashamed to hear me carrying on like this.
I already told you. Access to the storeroom is restricted. If you want to get in, show me written orders from the ambassador.
Thank you for returning Firaelion to me. He may be a fool, but he is a sweet one.
Thanks, friend. I was this close to becoming those spiders' next meal. At least I managed to gather some silk for Mendil. She'll have her dress yet. She deserves it.
We have work to do, but with the threat of a briarheart removed, the rest will be easier.
Thanks for all you've done.

I'm not sure how much time I have, but thank you for what you've done. My sacrifice is nothing compared to your brave response to Hircine's challenge.\n\nCan I help you understand this realm, a place of shadow, hunger, and thirst?
My hunter returns, briarheart in hand. Brinarch now roams my Hunting Grounds as prey. His chest, a gaping hollow, a reminder of his weakness. Heed his punishment, pup.
I owe you my sincere gratitude. Why, if Stibbons were stuck as a statue forever, I don't know what I'd do!\n\nIt simply doesn't bear thinking about.
They call this place <<c:1>> because it's where all the refuse ends up. We clear them out now and again, but they always come back.\n\nNecessary evil, I'm told.
I heard something about the wyrd …. In my opinion, it's good news.\n\nThey're far better-equipped to understand what we are fighting than we are, ourselves.
Are you ready? And can you stop thinking so loudly?
If Reezal-Jul escaped, we will have to track him down. He and Montclair both.\n\nI fear Montclair's ambitions may be far greater than simply conquering all of Rivenspire. It's better we stop him now.
Do you have any wine? If I'm to spend the rest of my days in this hole, I think I'll develop a drinking problem.
Neither of us will forget your kindness.

Did I hear that right? You went looking for my necklace? You found it, and brought it back? The Eight preserve us, thank you!\n\nAnd if that loveable galoot doesn't ask me to marry him, I will! You just wait!
Good job. I'm not sure why you got yourself involved in all this, but I don't care. You did well.
