<<1>> shouldn't be hard to track. You can smell him leagues away. But if I leave town, the treethane will send people after me, thinking I'm trying to escape with his bow.\n\nI can't do a thing until I get that bow back.
No. Not <<1>>. I'm such a fool. Clearly the vampire lord saw through our trap. <<1>>'s death is on my head.
Well, my family is at peace now. Thank you so much for your help. You'll always be a friend of the Hinault family.
I just miss them so much. What will I do without them?

Warmth like the sun's. We are free of the Elf-things' prison. We apologize for what we tried to do. \n\nWe were mad with hunger, unable to nourish ourselves within the walls—we were not ourselves. The air feeds us, now.

I heard what happened in Sentinel … it was worse than I feared, but I have faith. \n\nThe people of the Alik'r desert are resilient and unyielding like the sands of the great cliffs and the shores of the Ancestors themselves.
In my mind's eye, I witnessed your battle with the Worm Cult, and with the undead Ansei abominations. Your mission was successful, was it not?
You call this justice? The Vinedusk used you, just as the Dominion used them. You've done nothing but tighten the grasp of tyranny on <<1>>.
This is … ook … terrible! How ever am I going to serve my lady now?\n\nOh, bother! I guess I'd better start packing up the camp.
With all that gold, I'll be able to buy enough balm to cure me. I'll be well again! And have plenty left over for food, and rent, and … oh, Nedras.

I couldn't ask you to risk your life, but you look like you can handle yourself, and truthfully, I wouldn't mind if the Worm Cultists found themselves in a little trouble. \n\nTake this crystal and use it to gather the light from the Ayleid Well.
Oh that mead is going to taste so good. Mead today, a blade tomorrow. That's my plan! Forget that stupid mule!
Yenadar's grace be upon you traveler. And Kala's prayers go with you as well.
The king will know what to do. He listens to his people! The Dominion would be in a better place if he were in charge.
To go back on one's word is a serious thing. If <<1>> cannot construct an embassy, how can she build the Dominion?
You have cleared away the weeds so that I may set down new roots and thrive.\n\nSomeday, I hope I can do the same for another and repeat the cycle.
Bright moons shine on you, friend. This one's belly is full, thanks to you! \n\nNow we must haggle with knights over whose goods are whose. Commerce! Mazurr cannot wait!
You should talk to the Baron. I'm ready to go hit something, but he's been waiting to talk to you before he gives us any new orders.
You picked the right place at the right time, comrade. With so many knights injured here, there's great demand for fighters willing to take their places.
Good work rock-stomping that Imperial trash. Mauloch knows those knights couldn't do it alone.
I was at the garrison when it fell. My vision went red, I went berserk and … well, I don't remember much after that.
Heard the gravedigger has to bury that poor Orc who went missing up near the <<1>>. Such a shame.
I see the Garrison's been retaken. The Guild doesn't take sides in conflicts like this. \n\nAs Ufgabesh the student mage, I say nothing. But as Ufgabesh the Orc, I say "Well done."
When times are darkest, knowledge is what's needed to bring back the light. \n\nWhat's that you have there? A book?
I hear the Garrison has been retaken. Thank you, my friend. I do not think I will see its walls again, but … but I know they are in good hands.
The hill. Climb the hill.
We couldn't have retaken the Garrison without you. \n\nAlas, I haven't time for celebration. More wounded arrive by the hour. May the Eight help us.
With each new wolf, our pack becomes stronger. You're one of us now.
By Zenithar, I have an acute throbbing in my cranium. Could this be what a hangover is like?
Blessings of St. Pelin be upon you, friend. We couldn't have retaken the fort without you.
I thought the Garrison was lost for good. I've never been so glad to be proven wrong.

Truthfully, I think a few days rest are well-deserved on both our parts—not at the seashore, mind you, but perhaps in Wayrest.\n\nUnfortunately though, I am long overdue for an appointment. And as it happens, so are you.
I suppose the Baandari helped a bit. But I hardly think launching a few arrows at retreating Imperials evens the score.

You are a brave soul to go after the king on your own. I applaud your courage. \n\nI will go to Evermore to request additional support. Then I will return. May Ruptga and all the gods be with you until then.
If the Covenant does have a portal down there, it's vital that we close it.\n\nDon't worry about fighting everyone in there. Just focus on finding the portal. Then let the wand do the rest.
This wasn't supposed to happen here. Today should have been a celebration, but instead ….\n\nInstead, none of this officially happened.
Thanks again for killing that blood-stained bandit, Sgolag. Stay vigilant, our enemies will not rest, and we must persevere.
I had my doubts about <<1>>. Not after today.\n\nTravel well, my friend.
Thank you. It will mean a lot to me to have my notes back, at least. Be careful. Aggravated kwama are dangerous, to say nothing of the thunderbugs.
Remember, "the vines are strongest at dusk." The king will know you're a friend.
A final challenge for us both. This should be easy.
Do you accept my power?
Adeena's family may forgive me, but I will never forgive myself.
We need to find Najan.
It is good to be free of him. With my sister gone, there's nothing keeping me here. \n\nI have never seen the sea. Perhaps my days in Bangkorai are over.
What can Sabani get this child of Alkosh?

Whatever you do, keep an eye out for any members of my gang. I can't believe they gave up without a fight, but I can believe they're all holed up somewhere. Probably hiding out until this all blows over.
Our kind live in darkness and feed on life. Walking among us requires forsaking the gods and embracing the blessing of Mother Lamae. Will you proceed?
Sometimes I wonder if Ufa is still here at all. They say he's in hiding, but why?
We don't see a lot of travelers these days. What brought you here?

Were it truly your time, I might invite you to remain here in the Far Shores. You have earned the right to be here.\n\nIt is not your time though, so you must go. Take your liege back, restore him, and then you must all leave the Hall of Heroes.
The sooner this is over the better.
The couple despairs, but all is not lost! Nothing is without hope, until the last breath!\n\nLet me tell you of their child. Come, come!
Everyone owes you so much. We'll never be able to repay you. I, especially, shall pray to the gods for your continued health and good fortune.
You got what you came for! Now leave me be!
Welcome to Trader's Meet, my friend. Come for a selection of rarities, have you?\n\nWell, how about … apples! Guaranteed to be worm-free! They're imported from Glenumbra.
Remember. Move slowly and enter the tunnel one at a time. If we raise any alarms, this mission will be over before it's begun.\n\nGo on. We'll follow right behind you.
Everything you see comes from something I killed myself. In <<1>>, we use what we hunt.
Honor my mother's sacrifice and you will earn my blessing.
I suppose you don't have any jagga, do you? So delicious … if I could, I'd drink it straight from the pig!
My husband spends so much time with his books. I can never pull him away, especially when it's time to hunt.
Talk to my father if you're looking for potions. We don't keep our stock here.
Damned treethane, thinks she knows what's best for <<1>>. Wasn't born here, wasn't raised here. If I didn't know any better, I'd say she's a plant from <<2>>.
I don't know how my neighbors can walk the streets. Everywhere I go, I see where the Jade Butcher's troops killed my friends.
Look for the Packmaster. Just follow the scent. The pounding in your blood will tell you when you're close. You'll find him. I know it. He'll teach you the secrets of Hircine's gift.
What do you want from me? I have nothing more. Nothing! No home, no family. No future ….
You must think as a sword-singer would. Which blade would be most suitable for a warrior who has achieved mastery of his or her technique?

It appears the curse has been lifted. Whatever you did, it must have worked. Now I have all the time I need to study the ruins and piece the whole story together.\n\nDon't worry. I'll mention your name in my book!
When the Imperials invaded, I was deep in my cup. They took my sword before it even left the sheath.
I wondered if someone would find me, before they finished me off.
You don't look like one of the Seventh Legion. Why have you come?
Drink deep from my gift.

Remember, if you find Lleraya, don't talk to her. Don't try to reason with her. Just kill her before she can seduce you with her vampiric wiles.\n\nAnd if you find any survivors, send them back here where we can protect them.
The Briars can always use more skilled hunters. If you think you can prove your mettle, speak with <<1>> in <<2>>.
The wood weeps. Can you hear it too? Is that why you've come?
It is an honor to serve Queen Maraya.
Isn't she beautiful? And so enchanting! Please, sit beside me and we can gaze upon dear Lady Lleraya together.
Please enjoy our attractions. I'm terribly sorry they're so limited at the moment.
The corruption is gone. All of it.
I know you … your spirit, but you belong in this place no more than the others, the invaders.\n\nWhy do you come here? Why do you disturb my rest?

Don't worry about me. I'll throw on some armor and go with Gwendis. Put the old team back together!\n\nBut first I need to leave a flower for the lovely captain here. Give her something to remember me by.
Bah. Silver-Paws is a fool to share sugar with those knights. They pretend they are our friends now. If we are attacked by more Imperials though, we will see their true spots.
You check out the wrecked boats and I'll gather the others.\n\nHopefully, by the time we meet you at the tunnel, you'll have a lead on getting us that key.
Well, the Imperials did not fall for my clever ruse—but Naradani thinks this is not a total loss. This one can think of many uses for Khajiiti decoys. Some of them are even legal!
Welcome to <<1>>. How can I assist you with your import and export needs?
I'm not performing at the moment. I'm sure <<1>> could inform you of the carnival's schedule.
These poultices are Divine-sent. I fear I may have cursed those poor merchants in the throes of my fever. \n\nIf you … if you see them, thank them for me.
Good luck finding <<Amz:1>>!\n\nOnly if you have the time. I realize it's not the most glamorous request.
Care to spend some of that gold you've earned, dearie?\n\nAnd before you ask, I'm all out of boar knuckles. You wouldn't believe the demand on those things.
What are you doing here? You found your spy. The soldiers came for Edouard, all right. I can imagine what they're doing to him. He'll hang, thanks to you.
I'm sorry, but I have nothing to say.
I'll stay here and keep guard over the survivors in my care. But I will also remain vigilant, ready to lend my blade as soon as Baron Alard needs it.
You're all a bunch of tyrants!
Good show! The Wood Elves need to learn their place. Speaking out against Queen Ayrenn is treason!\n\nEspecially when she saved their ungrateful lives.
Without you, we all would be dead now. I pray for our friends who did not survive, and I will also offer prayers of thanks for you.
Take the boat over when your ready.\n\nYou could always head back into Northpoint and see how the town's doing too.
Follow your blood. It will lead you to Rahaja.\n\nPerhaps we will be kin one day.
Yes, how can I help you?
It seems that the only thing more loathesome than <<1>> writing his own opinions for posterity … may be the opinions that he ends up recycling from the scholars who have died here.
Hm. Not my usual type, but business is slow. What can I do for you?
Who are you? What have you done with Niha? What was in that wine?
You're amazing. Just amazing! I hope to be half the warrior as you some day. Thank you for everything.

Now all I have to do is locate that wildlife specimen Azei calls our pet. If only I'd had that monkey <<1>> stuffed when we first found him, we'd know precisely where he is!\n\nAh, well. We could always go back to the <<2>> for another if need be.

You actually survived the destruction of the Doomcrag? That's … remarkable.\n\nI mean, I've seen you do some amazing things. I'll never forget our adventures in Glenumbra. But to walk out of a collapsed mountain? That's really impressive.
You an archer? Nah, I bet you like that personal touch. Axes, right?  \n\nEither way, I've got a weapon for you!
You've brought my business back to life, wayfarer! Soon this sleepy market will be a bustling bazaar again!
My, my, my—what have you done to your clothes? Slaying Imperials is hard on the garments, yes? You should treat yourself to a new wardrobe. Look around—you earned it.
I suppose saving a city is worth a drink.
Big day today! I bagged three Scamps and a very grumpy atronach. You keeping up?
You know, I was in the Imperial army once. Seeing what you did to those Legionaries … makes me glad I deserted.
Hail, comrade. I trust the Daedra culling is proceeding at pace? \n\nRumor has it the God of Schemes has been working double shifts to keep up with you.
I guess a drink or two wouldn't hurt.
Ruptga bless you for ridding the city of those twice-cursed Imperials. I had planned to poison their drinking water, but I suppose your way … sent a message?

Hm. Perhaps your interest is genuine. I will gladly accept your help. From the size and shape, I would say we need four more pieces. The fisherman claimed he was fishing off the western coast when this stone was found. The others might not be far.
Go on now. Find your friend. Let me do my job.

Don't suppose you killed an Imperial carrying a cask of pomegranate wine? Sand snake made off with one before the fighting started. \n\nAh, well. It is a small price to pay for clean streets. Can I get you something?
That's all I know. I swear it. Now move on, would you?
By Mauloch's left fang! Those whoreson dogs! Sons of trolls! The First Forge burn them!\n\nOgre dung!
Get her out of here. I'll cover your retreat.
Shut the door quickly behind you. The sand gets into everything, especially the alchemical equipment.\n\nWhat have you got there? A book?
Nicolene and I will be headed back to Sentinel soon enough. Until then, you should stay and have a drink with us.
Glad to get some fresh air. I can only take the smell of incense for so long, and the Imperials had us locked up for days.
My fellow mages are good folk, but I must confess I'm glad the lock-down is over. If I had to listen to one more debate about the merits of alteration over conjuration, I would have lost my mind.
<Esmaeel lies motionless.>
Khajiit is happy to meet someone who understands us. Malira thought the Elves would be more welcoming.
Why do you encourage her behavior? These blasted cat people need to learn that some customs will not be accepted in the Dominion!\n\nI'm glad it's not people like you making the rules around here.
Ah, the Empire's bane graces us with a visit! Welcome to The Drowsy Owl, friend. I have readied my most lavish suite for you. Only the best for the hero of Hallin's Stand!

You are the hero everyone speaks about, is it not so? There was an Imperial shouting your name as he fled out the back window, and by Tava's red feathers, there was terror in his voice. \n\nWe can but hope he survived. Someone must tell the tale.
As weary as we are, we can't wait to be on the road. I was so eager to see the world when I joined the legion. Now I just want to see home again.
<No new scouting missions are available.>
Next time I get handed a contract with the words mage, magus, wizard, spell or anything even remotely magic-related, I'm just going to quit.
<A few of this dusty journal's pages have their corners folded inward to mark specific entries.>
So where's <<1>>? Did the Daedra get her, or did she escape?

Tall Papa's blessings be upon you, my friend. The Imperials had been lusting for our library for some time. I fear that had you not intervened, they would have taken our books by force. There are those in Cyrodiil quite desperate for such knowledge.

I received word the Imperials have been routed. I pray it is true. \n\nLong and long have been the days since they arrived. Their spell-weavers have been watching us with envious eyes. If we had lost our library to those barbarians….
New good-looking friend has returned! With the <<1>>?
Hmph. It has its own archaic charm, I'll admit.
I don't intend to tell anyone what my brother did. As far as I'm concerned, he died trying to help me, not usurp my throne.
What happened to <<1>> was a tragedy.\n\nI hope that sounds believable. I'll be saying it for the rest of my days.
<No new warfront missions are available.>
<The Bounty board has a spot for me to post my report.>
<No new battle missions are available.>
What a relief. I fared better than most during the occupation. \n\nBut the things that my patrons saw! By Tava's red feathers, I shudder to think of it.

Ah, hello. I always have time for Guild members.\n\nHow may I be of assistance?
Well you made quite a mess out there. Damn glad I don't have to clean it up.
Don't try to reason with <<1>>. Just go with what she says. She's crazy as an Alfiq-raht in heat.\n\nIf you have any questions, ask <<2>>. She's up front with our cart.
If you need my assistance, I shall need to know the nature of your emergency.\n\nOtherwise, it would be prudent of you to reconsider my time, which you are wasting.

By Tall Papa's starry breeches, it is good to be rid of those stinking Imperial curs. I would offer you a drink on the house had they not plundered my cellar. A simple "thanks" will have to suffice.\n\nIt is just a pity that you did not come sooner.
Ha ha ha! Gave him a good scare didn't I? Maybe that'll make him think twice before tearing a flower from the ground.\n\nThat felt good. Some people just have no class.
Thank you for soothing that Wood Elf's temper.\n\nHe would've taken a hand, an arm, or worse, if you hadn't come along.
I should never have sent you to do my own work. I am a strong Orc, and proud. I do not need the help of an outsider.
Don't worry. We won't linger here any longer than we have to.
Oh, yes, come closer …. Hmm … how strong you look with my minion's blood on your hands ….
Please tell my dear sister that I'm still waiting for that apology.
My beloved brother has a better chance of squeezing fire salts from an ice cube than getting an apology from me.
You can have the relic if you want it. Needless to say, I won't be taking it with me. That should get me a discount from Dragonstar Caravans, shouldn't it?
Probably only a matter of time before the Imperials anger everyone. I told my friend he could come with me, but he's too attached to this city.\n\nI suppose I understand that.
Back already, eh? I'm sure my charges are happy to know you tried, even if you couldn't get their things back.\n\nWe'll be able to head out now!
His honor is intact.
Don't dally now. If you take too long, I might just have to retake the garrison without you.
A pleasure to have you with us, friend. I look forward to recovering the valuables from your corpse!
Thanks, mate. Now to find an Imperial's throat to bury this dagger into ….
Thank you. I'm happy to have something to remember my wife by. Now when the winds blow, I will imagine her singing again.
Thank you so much. I hope to wear this on my wedding day.
I am eternally grateful for this act of kindness. With this, my daughter's future is safe.
<<1>> could not wait for you to return. My sister gave him an end befitting a warrior.\n\nKeep the helmet of his foe—we do not need reminders of this folly.
Let me know when you kill a real monster. Or if you'd like to try this monster on for size ….
Thanks for the drink, sweetheart.\n\nMaybe when you bring back the head of a lich I'll buy you one. Probably not.

This one has heard much less unrest. Kitten-headed fools trusting the High Elves to deliver on their promises.\n\nAzimsun will believe this when he sees the truth of it for himself. Too much has been witnessed to be blindly hopeful, yes?

This one hears the most wonderful news, yes? The embassy for all walkers is to be constructed as planned.\n\nVabashi knew all she needed to do was hold fast. There was no break of promise, merely … delays.

This one serves the Dominion well, and knows many others are the same way as he. What happens when all we disgruntled walkers refuse to fight for Elves who do nothing for us? Battles will be lost—this I promise.
Nerien'eth took everything from me.\n\nAnd I won't rest until I take something back.
It's easier to form coherent thoughts when I'm not being stabbed. It's been a long couple of years.\n\nI owe you a debt, friend. I'll never forget what you did for us. For Alanwe.
The others have been singing your praises, but with a little more time, I would have gathered the magicka to free myself.\n\nIn another decade or so. It's hard to concentrate when you're on fire.
Good luck sneaking in through the muck. If you don't manage it, we're all dead.
Please! Don't let them kill me!
I miss Buttons. \n\nWithout him, everything is grey, and each day is worse than the one before.
Go ahead. I do not like being watched while I climb. It is… awkward.
Ha! You are so pathetic … it just makes me laugh. I think we should be friends.\n\nMaybe later, I'll tell you about Buttons and our circle of love.
<He appears to have been dead for some time.>
Clan Mother must be obeyed promptly! Snap to it, you hear? Remember what I said, when you're sad that you didn't listen to me.
Excuse me. Might you be willing to do us a favor and run a message to Evermore Castle?
Thank you for the coin, I'm eternally thankful.
I'll see if I can get closer to the Imperial dogs to surmise their true purpose. Wish me luck, friend.
Thank you for bringing this information to me. I will send word to Evermore right away.
I think before I said I had seen it all …. Well, I was wrong.
Praise Tu'whacca! Is it … is it really him?
I can't believe it! I carried that lockbox around for years!
I'll see you out at those old ruins, partner. If I ever get done straightening out all this garbage, that is.
<The anvil is smooth and featureless, save for the alchemical symbol for "Mundus" stamped on the face.>
Don't get many visitors. If you're here for the ruin, best to turn back. No good's come outta that place in … oh, several hundred years. Give or take a decade or so.
<The orrery is weathered from exposure to the elements. An etching of the alchemical symbol for Aetherius is barely visible on its base.>
<The fountain contains a murky water that never quite stills. The sculpture above is stamped with the alchemical sign for "Aurbis.">
You come to my realm at the appointed time.
You come to me as a pup, unblooded and weak. What makes you think you are worthy to join my pack?
We'll talk again in Davon's Watch. Look for me at the Fish Stink. It's a little tavern run by Hectur the Fish, down by the docks.\n\nThat is, unless your bones end up decorating those Goblins' huts.
Please, don't hurt me again! I don't want to be eviscerated!
Get out of my face. Unless you want me to mangle yours!

I can't even imagine why I went out there. I thought I saw … my husband of all things. But that couldn't be right. He's not even stationed here. I knew it couldn't be him, and yet … I couldn't resist.
Come to share your latest exploits with us, darling? I fear you'll find Lala and Rock rather hard to impress.

Undaunted! Undaunted! We ate … err … are … eh.\n\nWhat the blazes are you? Fresh meat, I see. Come to impress and slay, and to drink wine and spill blood. Harken to my words, young one. You will never achieve half the things this old sword has.

As a famous treasure hunter and expert historian, it's no wonder the Mages Guild specifically asked for me to come along. \n\nI do hope my manservant Stibbons can handle the sights of Coldharbour, though. He's a rather sensitive sort.
The Fighters Guild and the Mages Guild working together? This one never expected to see the day!
The wisdom to work together toward a better understanding of what each arm of the Dominion is doing and what it needs?\n\nThis is for what I had hoped. This is what seems to have occurred.
Molag Bal's realm is one of the most dangerous and inhospitable places in all of Oblivion. We must not take this invasion lightly.
Coldharbour sounds dreadful. How am I ever going to keep my Lady safe in such a dangerous place?
I shall lead the Fighters Guild into this dreadful realm. We'll make the Lord of Schemes pay for attacking Nirn!
Coldharbour! I don't mind admitting that this old dungeon-delver is probably more excited than she should be! I can't wait to see what kinds of artifacts we can recover.
Lovely day. Much lovelier because of the relative peace and quiet I can enjoy.
I should get back to fishing. <<1>>'s foolishness means we all must work harder. I flatten the spine of disapproval at her actions.\n\nYou were right to stop her.

So we have you to thank. That's good, you're good. Cracked open my finest fishwine to celebrate.\n\nThe hardest part is fishing out all the chunks. Ha! Fish. Because it's made from … what was I saying?
I'd rather not get eaten by a daedroth, but I'd dearly love a few of their teeth!
I don't know about you, but I'm ready to break a few Daedric necks.
Our job will be to help Vanus with the portals. We'll need a lot of them to establish supply lines after we start conquering territory.
I wonder if there are any beautiful ladies in Coldharbour? Or is that a different Daedric Prince?

Others would speak to this better than I, but it seems the tree in the plaza is taking well to its cultivation.\n\nMy sister said it would never survive leaving Alinor. This, then, would show what she knows.
You're back, I see. Feel free to practice with the weapons. Talk to Jaleel or Marc if you have questions.
I'm ready to cleave some skulls! Do Daedra have skulls? I imagine they do, depending on which type we run into.
Are there any spells or traps in Coldharbour that could turn me into a chicken? I'd just like a fair warning.
There aren't any Goblins in Coldharbour, are there? I have a profound dislike of the vile creatures.
Our alliance owes you a great debt, friend.
Look what the cat dragged in. You kill anything bigger than a spider yet?
Good to see you! I've been promoted since I saw you last, and my sister Ciranya is in good health. I'll give her your best when I see her.
You showed great courage in Wayrest, dealing with the Midnight Union. We'll always be grateful.

I had a bet with Abzag, here. He wagered you wouldn't cough up the coin for that drink. Good thing you did—I was supposed to kill you if he was right!\n\nWell, I wouldn't have killed you. Maybe thrown you across the bar. I'm pretty strong.

Take caution, fragile mortal! You stand before the great Incendion: Master of the Whiteflame, Bearer of the Burning Heart, Kinlord of ancient Sunhold. I could incinerate you with an intake of my breath!\n\nAnd I have very important work to do.
Inspect my notes, Count Verandis. See if you can find a clue that I overlooked. We need to work together to save the Baroness.
Verandis, you must tell me. Why did this happen to Mother? Of all the people of Shornhelm, why her?\n\nPlease tell me there's a way to save her. You're powerful. You have to do something!
Well look at this! If it isn't the scamp I sent to clear out a dung heap.\n\nHah! Going get a little rough for ya scrap? Sure took you long enough!
You are no Undaunted.\n\nI can imagine your tales of glory. I, too, used to brag about killing dogs and cats.

As an Undaunted, I seek to better myself, but I'm afraid there is little left in this world to challenge me.\n\nPerhaps there are Daedric realms that are more interesting. A dangerous thought, I suppose.

Can't you see I'm eating?\n\nYou young scamps always come to Felvyn for advice when I'm in the middle of something. Tell you what—buy me a drink and I'll give you a tip on making the best use of a blade.
I hear you are giving a hand to the performers. That is great news, maybe my stock won't spoil after all.
The pyrotechnics are a bit much to deal with several times a day, but I find a lot of the first time attendees need a drink after that show.
I can't tell you how glad I am that you found that guy some new stories to tell. I don't think I could've handled any of the old ones one more time.
Brave wayfarer, fellow Undaunted. Welcome to my desert.\n\nI see you remain unslain. A rarity for an Undaunted!
I have to admit, these bugs seem remarkably well trained. I'm still going to keep my distance though.
Oh. You're back. Guess you weren't eaten by ghosts.

You are Undaunted! This one is glad to see a new member. She has nearly run out of bodies to climb over in her glorious rise to the top.\n\nYou will help <<1>> with this, yes? <<2>> has been most uncooperative.
Now that the carnival is in full swing, I can't decide what to focus on! The bugs creep me out but the stories and the magic act are so much fun!

I appreciate the drink. Helps keeps the anxieties under control in the depths of a dungeon.\n\nThis one believes that you are never truly alive unless you are stumbling through a trap or matching wits with a Daedra! So go! Be alive!
I guess the performances aren't so bad. I had no idea you could train insects like you can a dog.

I say, you're awfully quiet for one of the Undaunted. Have you no tongue, or just a dull wit? Ho, ho! Just ribbing you, my friend. Making jokes, sharing laughs! That … that's what we do, right?\n\nI'm sorry. What was I saying?
Good to see you again. Hranir was just telling us about her latest exploits. Get out there and see if you can match them.
So, you know Seeks-Her-Glory? So do I, if you know what I mean. If you buy me a drink, maybe I'll let you in on a little secret.

Why do you idle, Undaunted?\n\nGo jump into a cave. Fight a Daedra or something. Seems to be no shortage of those, these days. Like most things, they'll stop moving when you strike their necks—the ones that have necks.

Oh, look at this one! You think you're tough?\n\nI've seen adventurers like you frozen in terror—at the creatures I've gazed in the eye—and ripped apart. They should call me the Stout! My hands are huge!
Are you drunk, yet? 'Cause I am! Undaunted! Har.\n\nSo. How are things with you?
Hey, fresh meat. My mouth is dry. Get me a drink, or I'll tell Talisse to ring it out of you.\n\nShe'll do it. She has big hands.
I hope my friends aren't being too loud. They're friendly people, really. Once you get to know them. They'd be more friendly if you were an Undaunted.
Not afraid of a fight, eh? Good. We need some more honest warriors here.
Son of a troll … I've earned this nap. Don't judge me.

Plenty for an Undaunted to see and do in Coldharbour, my friend. As long as you like walking headlong into danger. There are creatures here that can slay even the dead.\n\nLet me know if you want to barter for some arms and armor. You'll need them.
Ah, you again. And with every limb intact!\n\nYou continue to surprise.
I got another one ….\n\nHow many Undaunted does it take to cure the sickness that comes after a night at the tavern? Please, I need to know. By the Egg, I'm going to need to know in the morning.
You must be the one Ram told us about. Let me look at you.\n\nYou have strong eyes. A strong soul, I'll bet.
By seed and spleen, the Mages Guild is up to something in Selene's Web.
Welcome to the Hollow City, Undaunted. I'm sure you've found that, like Coldharbour itself, there's plenty here to test yourself against.
So nice to talk to a fellow Undaunted. This one is eager to hear about something other than trees.
By the Green Pact, we Bosmer make horrible drinks.\n\nAt least they get you drunk.

Hello … you! Good to see another Undaunted. I've been drinking my way through all the places Undaunted dwell.\n\nThe drink here is surprisingly strong. An hour ago, I thought I had become a Khajiit. But I was just looking at one. She set me straight.
A fellow Undaunted!\n\nIf you need any equipment, you can speak to me. Yours should be well-worn, by now. If you need any leads on adventures … you can also speak to me. I know of a few places.
This is some strong drink. Burns.\n\nAlmost helps me forget the boredom. I need an adventure.
Getting thrown out of a tavern is a horrible thing—you're deprived of your bar fights—and your bar drinks.\n\nThe secret is to drink and fight—quietly.
Please, don't interrupt. We've much to do to meet the Dominion's expectations in the region.
Our great leaders … are gone, missing. What will we do?
The fight is well and truly lost. Get out of our town, you aren't welcome here.
Who're you? Another Undaunted? A word of warning—stay away from <<1>>. I left it days ago, and the cold still burns.
Ah, a fellow Undaunted! My name is Earrona Kneecapper.\n\nIt's a pleasure to meet you. I hope you find the adventure well in these parts.

Milksop! Come to Velyn Harbor looking for a good bruising? I know just the place. But I can't remember the name.\n\nPerhaps … perhaps if my mug weren't empty, my memory would improve. Fill my mug. Please.
Well, well, well, look who it is? The second bravest member of the Undaunted.\n\nCome treat with me, friend! With me and these lovely ladies!
Oh, are you another Undaunted like <<1>>? He is so brave and strong. I could listen to his tales for hours.
Ah, the new blood! You've come far, my friend!
Talisse was just telling us about you. New blood, she called you. Know what would break that unfortunate epithet? Winning a combat tournament.
You are a friend of the Empress of Bone. You will be allowed to live when the Empress destroys this world and replaces it with nothing but bone.

You're not another fool like Felvyn, here, are you? Thinking I'll jump in his bedchamber after a drink? There isn't enough mead in the world for that.\n\nIsn't enough mead in the world to sate my thirst, either.
I suppose I could construct some Khajiiti statuary, or paint a mural of the Elden Tree.\n\nI will simply have to speak to some of the dignitaries to see what would fit them best.
The Dominion needs … festivals. Something to bolster faith in the Dominion itself, and celebratory of its formation.\n\nAnd every good festival needs costumes. Yes, grand pomp for all.

Presently? I am accounting for what goods we have in the embassy, to better monitor future requisitions.\n\nIf I keep costs low enough, I might be able to hire a replacement for myself, such that I may see some action on my own merit.
You look as fresh as the time I met you, scamp. Does nothing slow you down? I hear you've been making a name for yourself.
This ale's not as good as the grog from the time I ran with Blackheart's crew. But it does its job.
I'm writing my memoirs—a record of my great deeds!\n\nHow about some refreshment, new blood? Hard to write with a parched throat!

I'm looking for work. Know anyone who needs a hauler? I'm real good at breaking down tents, packing them up, and hauling them where they need to be unpacked and pitched.\n\nAnd don't say carnival. I'm done with carnivals.

That's it, then? Seen the world thrice over and none the worse for it, eh? \n\nYou should be ready for anything—and believe you me, the Daedric Princes never rest. They're always mucking about with something or other!
Greetings, walker! Come, sit by the fire and be welcome!
I don't want to think of the outcome had you not been here.\n\nYou kept the king safe. You will always be welcome among the Vinedusk Rangers.
<<1>> … how could this have happened? You had so much greatness within you.\n\nYour future should have been so very bright.

Things have been a lot quieter around here, lately. It's easier for me to move my adventuring supplies, but there's something I miss about having to break an arm every now and then.\n\nI think it's the breaking arms part.

I, Boeuf Sterone, have the best food available for miles! How do I know this? Because it is from right here!\n\nNowhere is it fresher. And it can be so fresh because I no longer need worry about my supply being stolen, so I need not bury it!
Did you know that there was something in those ruins after all? I had no idea! None whatsoever!\n\nIt's enough to drive me to drink, but I only drink when the sky is blue. Fancy one? A drink, I mean.
I wonder if <<c:1>> is worth all the fuss. I certainly hope the queen isn't wasting her time.\n\nHmph. And yours.

I don't know you. Fighters Guild facilities here are intended for members only. We've too much to do and too few to do it to spare anything.\n\nYou should really consider joining us. Our charter benefits all of Tamriel, after all.
Lighting the fire is only part of it, you have to make sure that the guards don't just put it right back out, too!
Do you often storm into the halls of guilds in which you have no membership?\n\nI assure you, that isn't exactly polite. Unless you're here to join our ranks, of course.

Are you familiar with "handfasting?" I'm not entirely certain what it means, but I'd wager <<1>> and <<2>> will be doing it before the month's end.\n\nBetween you and I, they've wanted to handfast each other since the day they met.
It's good to have <<1>> back in <<2>>. I thought he would be trapped in <<Ac:3>> until I was old and gray.\n\nBut that isn't the case. He's here, right now. Safe.

All is well. <<1>> is returned to <<2>>, free of <<3>>'s control. Though I admit, I can hardly call her my apprentice anymore.\n\nNow, we are more like equals. Different roles for us both, but I welcome the change.
I have failed in my duties. Our foes have stolen the Elder Scroll I guarded. Please, recover it!
Find our Elder Scroll, warrior! Seek out those who have stolen it and kill them for this sacrilege!
I heard you're the newest Briar. I'll let you in on a little secret, I was once a Briar too! But I'm too old to rummage around in the forest these days.
Don't just stand there—the Elder Scroll of Ghartok has been stolen! Help your comrades recover it!
You passed the trial? You should speak with Lereluin. My husband is always pleased to meet new Briars.
I am to take Glaras' place when she steps down. I have much to learn and many years to grow before that happens.
I wish I could have stormed <<1>> myself, but I swore my strength to my thane's side. I must resort to indirect measures to protect her.
Hurry to <<1>>. You'll find <<2>> entrenched at the gate to <<3>>.
Be careful in the barrow. Our ancestors went to great lengths to protect their dead.
He went further into the barrow. Be careful. I'll be fine on my own. Put an end to this, and find me in Ivarstead after you do. I owe you a debt for helping me.
I will do a better job of looking after my older brother. He thinks age brings wisdom. Hah!

I call this a successful day. We beat Reezal-Jul and we saved the lovely Captain Janeve.\n\nYou know what would make it even better? If I can convince all these lovely ladies to join me for a drink at the nearest tavern.
What am I going to do? I have to clear all this rubbish before the end of my shift. Ambassador's orders, they said!
It is no use. The High Elves care nothing about their promises to the Khajiit. Nothing will change, no matter how much we shout!
I thought you were on our side! I mean, after all you did for us … er, I mean …. Never mind.
Heed my words, friend. There is more to Montclair's betrayal than the Baron and the Countess know.\n\nI suggest you proceed with caution when you enter the upper city.
The brothers and I appreciate your help, my friend! I know this job might have been a little rough, but we're getting better with every contract. You'll see!

You're the only one who isn't a member of this group. Perhaps you will speak truly. The contract specifies they must do the work promptly and effectively. \n\nI'm not sure what happened, to be honest. Did they do anything worth paying for?
Thanks to you, our reputation remains intact.
I feel better knowing someone is going to try to help the mayor. And I'll go make my report and send more troops this way.
I thank you. Sithis willing, it is not too late to stop the Dominion.
I gave you fair warning. Whether or not you decide to listen, that's up to you.
Did you tell the truth? What are you thinking?

You're smart. Working for the Ring of Daggers has two great benefits. \n\nFirst, we reward our friends generously. Second, we don't worry about trials and laws and silly things like that. Get Althen to Hoarfrost Downs and he will pay for what he did.
Sagabar and I were just making bets on whether you'd return.\n\nLooks like Sagabar's a two-time loser. Did you do it then? Did you kill Gavendien?
You brought Gavendien to justice, eh? I'm glad.\n\nYou know, if you were ever interested in becoming a deputy to the constable. I'm just saying … the job's open.
I hope you made that man suffer. For what he did to Mondorie, he deserved a brutal end. \n\nDamn bandits. Now I'm just hoping my horse comes home.
Oh. Hello, there. You must be new in town ….\n\nI'm sorry, but the jewelry shop is closed for today. Constable Gavendien's orders.
I sure do love fishing. Fishing is fun. I could fish all day.
My husband and the others did what they thought was best. Who knew that dreadful Gavendien would go back on his word?
Poor Rubyn! How will he ever get along without his mother?
Poor mother. She didn't deserve this fate.

Have you come to join us for the final push, Lieutenant? We are all that's left of the King's Guard, but at least we'll take a few Orcs down with us.\n\nAs soon as we see an opening, we're charging into that breach down there.
I guess this is what I deserve. Very well. I accept my fate.
<The wine's aroma makes your mouth water in anticipation.>
I can't believe you recruited Julien. If I could eat my dagger, I would.\n\nI'm really embarrassed. Here I couldn't manage to get a single recruit, and you come behind me and get three.
I've told you everything. Let's not do anything hasty, all right.

Well, my friend, it appears that the book is real and not part of Lleraya's illusion. I believe it will be of great help to us in the trials ahead.\n\nThat said, I have much research to do. Ancient Ayleid isn't my native language, you know.

Ah! A stranger in town. I was just saying how we needed more strangers around here. You know, walking around, bothering people who are just trying to do an honest day's work.\n\nIs that the kind of stranger you are, friend?

The army waits for my signal, out beyond the farms. I want to keep the damage to Northpoint to a minimum. Marching soldiers have a habit of destroying persons and property, even when they're trying to be careful.
I am grateful for your help. I'll steel myself and get out of here shortly.
It's nice out here. No more crawling around crypts, no more undead. No more really heavy armor. No more preaching about Arkay. Nope. No more. I'm done.
This one is glad you are with the Guild at this difficult time. Bear with us, adept.

Go. I need to remain and tend to Darien.\n\nHe claimed the bloodfiends bit him, but I found nothing but bruises and shallow scratches on his body. I see no signs of the vampire's curse, but I want to watch him to make sure he's all right.
Look around you. Does it look like we have time for idle chatter?
So tell me, what news from Verandis? Has Count Ravenwatch's research finally borne fruit?
Baron Montclair must pay for his crimes. I plan to see to it. Personally.\n\nI shall gather my troops and prepare to ascend the Doomcrag.
I'm ready. No, I am more than ready! The time has come to put Baron Montclair down like the crazed dog he has become.
Remember, the man that Montclair was is gone now. He no longer exists. Only the monster remains.\n\nSo don't hold back. Keep him busy until I can join you.
This seems to be <<Cz:1>>. She was concerned … she writes about Arlie's sad smiles. Missing me, no doubt. She brought Arlie flowers … and then, they went to the windmill. Oh dear!
I'll miss <<1>>. She was a good … friend.
With Federic back it's going to be harder to keep Arlie's attention. That doesn't mean I won't try, though! My days of sitting idly by are over!
Our home is yours to stay in, for as long as you like. It's the least we can do.
Now that Federic's returned for good, everything will be right again!

Don't worry. I'm not going to try to skip town or anything. If I wanted to do that, I'd have just spit in your eye and stabbed you in the stomach, and gone along my merry way.\n\nI'm coming … when I feel like it.
Verandis is waiting for you at the Lorkrata ruins. So, what are you still doing here staring at me?

Verandis claims he has a plan to vanquish Montclair, but he hasn't been forthcoming with the details.\n\nStill, he's dealt honorably with us so far. I'm willing to let him take the lead at this point in the campaign.
I'm going to share a secret with you, Adept. I've always felt a bit of a fraud. My teachers always told me how gifted I was, how brilliant, but I never really believed them.
I had a feeling I might see you here. I wasn't sure if I was ready to face you. \n\nYou saw me in such a dark moment. But they taught me how to control the hunger.
Wherever she is, I wonder if Heloise is watching all this. I hope she's at peace.
What are you waiting for? Get on your horse and get to the starting line!
You faced down Montclair and lived to tell about it! I'm envious, you know.

I saw you over there at the stocks talking to Martin. Does that fool still think I'm coming to his rescue? He's like a babe in the woods. \n\nI told him not to wear those fancy boots. It's not my fault he wouldn't listen.
We did it! Now let's get out of here. We can talk more when we get outside.

Look at these people—you'd never guess hundreds of people recently died in a terrible war. \n\nLet them have a moment of happiness, though. You and I know it was only because of Verandis' sacrifice that any of us are still here.

You saved our family and the kingdom, so I guess that makes us doubly in your debt. \n\nAnd if High King Emeric can choose a new ruler for Rivenspire, my daughter should be able to choose her … preferences as well.
A new ruler for Shornhelm. This is a huge moment for Rivenspire.\n\nWe should all be honored to witness such a moment.
Can you believe it? She still won't make up her mind!
Hi there. You know, I just noticed that you have really pretty eyes.\n\nOh, I mean … not that I'm flirting with you or anything. Not unless you want me to.
You know, I think I've decided it's more fun when you don't choose … even when you have to. It's fun having everyone waiting for you to make up your mind.
Go on. Don't wait for me.\n\nBut thank you, though. For, you know. Helping Verandis. Thanks.
Check with the Baron and see if he has anything to report while I consider our next move.
What word of the Mage and her aspects? We can't afford to let the Serpent control another Celestial Guardian.

I would stand here and drink myself to death, but I can't even afford to do that!\n\nMy mother told me that if I became a poet, I would starve to death. When I wrote a book, I thought I had proven her wrong. But it's come to nothing!
And like a faithful hound, you follow on the heels of your master. Should I have you sit? Roll over? Beg? Perhaps later.\n\nFor now, why don't you stand over there and wait for my blessing to begin.
That statue … it's so cold. It feels like the dead of winter.

I can't tell you how much I appreciate you convincing me to enlist. I've come to realize that this is what I was born to be—a soldier.\n\nI also met some soldiers who served under my father. They spoke highly of him. I hope I can honor his memory.

If you decide you want to leave, talk to the captain. I can't think of any reason at all for us to stay here. \n\nI can deal with thieves, pirates, and all manner of vagabonds, but I'm not getting near any undead.

A finer group of soldiers never served in the Shornhelm Guard. Julien and Shuga have both turned out to be valiant warriors.\n\nAnd Martin, that young man is a natural leader. He's a war hero now, too. He saved dozens of lives in battle the other day.

Ah! You're one who killed that old skeever Dark Elf I was seeing! What was his name again …? No matter. He's ancient history now. \n\nI'm sharing a tent with Julien these days, if you catch my meaning. For the time being, at least.

If it isn't Mara's messenger in the flesh! You really saved my love-life. Looking back, I can't imagine what I ever saw in Guendeline. \n\nKhalisah. Now that's the woman of my dreams! It warms my heart to think she's waiting for me back at home.
So you're headed out to the desert too? That works. I got some timber to sell there in Sentinel.\n\nI sure as Oblivion better make more off this trip than the price of your fare.
Any time is a good time for a mug of port.
You know what really chaps my breeches? Montclair's troops stole a whole bunch of the weapons I just completed. \n\nI'll be working for weeks to catch up!

This was once a sacred place devoted to the worship of Akatosh. Now, these sand devils have defiled and destroyed it. It must be cleansed. I plan to call out the Celestial who did this and deal with him.
I see now what the burnt bones told me. Pain, suffering. And hope. The last bone means hope.
Your help has been invaluable, my friend, but I fear that Craglorn's troubles are far from over.
You're back! I was beginning to worry for your safety. Did you find the amulet? Tell me everything that happened!
I'm glad Holgunn sent you. Kyne knows we could use a little luck.\n\nSpeak to Netapatuu if you think you can help.
Please, do not interrupt me. I must open this for you.
Shornhelm has a new ruler? Well, it's about time! Unless that highfaluting High King wants to spend all his time in Rivenspire, we need someone here who can make decisions and get things done.
The High King actually named a single ruler for Shornhelm? Amazing! It's good to have a proper ruler on our throne again.
I can't believe they gave the crown to that silly young woman! She isn't half as worthy as the brave and handsome Baron Dorell.
I can't believe they gave the crown to that overbearing, pompous bore! He isn't half as worthy as the brave and beautiful Countess Tamrith.
I hear we have our own king again. Well, we know how well that worked out the last time.
So the High King gave the crown to Baron Dorell? Well, that figures. Fancy-pants Emeric was never going to award rulership to a woman. That's just not the way it's done.
Greetings and welcome! Do I smell the distinct aroma of vintage lorebooks? Perhaps an ancient scroll? Or is it a musty tome?
It's a good thing you showed up. I wasn't looking forward to rolling down this hill, trying to get to Kragenmoor before the Daggers.

Any knowledge of enemy tactics is a good thing. Perhaps we can use their little trick against the Covenant. Or get the Goblins to attack their camps. \n\nI'll leave that to Holgunn. Me, I don't want to ever see another spider again.
Thanks again for retrieving my wares, traveler. I'll make for Kragenmoor soon enough.
I will keep an eye on the barrier, in case anything changes. You go find Walks-In-Ash!
Smell the ash on the wind? That's the wind of change, set to scour the Daggers from our shores.
I apologize for not being able to speak much at the moment.\n\nMy lovely Celan and I had a rather … rough trip most recently.
This fort is important to the protection of Stonefalls. We have to ensure its safety.
Good thing I'm such a patient woman, so dedicated to my oath. Otherwise I'd be wondering out loud why our commander has gone insane.
Ysgramor guide your blade! Hah!

Don't let the name fool you. Ash Mountain isn't a giant pile of ashes. It's much lovelier than that. It's a looming, active volcano. You can smell the brimstone from here.\n\nSounds compelling, doesn't it?
Still-Water and I have been partners for years. Just business, but you get to know a person after all that time in the wilds. Damn it. I'm going to miss that scaley bastard.
<The Argonian's body is just starting to cool.>
No Hagraven? I was sure there was a Hagraven? Then what was doing all that blasted screeching?
I'll wait here until you return. I want to be around when my drunken spouse gets back so we can discuss how I apparently remind him of a screeching Hagraven.
Almost finished with this row. Crops aren't looking too bad. Considering everything that's happened.
By the Three, Argonians sure take their time. You'd think he was an artist, the way he treats this farm.
Smells delicious. I love Dawn's cooking. I count our blessings that they decided to stay and work for us after the Pact.
I'm working up an old family recipe for later. It's so nice to be appreciated, you know?
Damned well. After the volcanos started acting up, it's gone completely dry. I'm sure I'll be running back and forth to Kragenmoor more than I like.
Now that that's over with, we should return to Camp Tamrith and let <<1>> know that the task is complete.
What happened? I heard a commotion and was about to send a few of the guard to investigate.
What happened? I blacked out.
You're doing me a tremendous service, friend. Those soldiers have been sending couriers to ask what's going on for weeks now. I know they'll be happy to get this dispatch.
Time to crack open another jug of Ungorth. Only thing that makes this bearable.
I wouldn't mind having someone like you on my staff. You fight like a Daedra and have the courage of a dozen guards. If you ever want a real job, come back and see me.
<This is Aera's log book. In it she keeps the names of all Worm Cult agents she has brought to justice.>
I don't know if you delivered my offering to Pariah Abbey or not, but something made a difference. My heart has been lighter in recent days.
May Azura's blessing be with Sergeant Oorga, and with you.
<This massive construct stands dormant, since it is still missing some crucial gears and pistons. An etched panel bears an inscription.>
I'm just going to wait here and rest until the healers come to collect me.
If I thought the Three gave a damn about me, I'd pray for you. Instead I'll wish you good luck and a sharp blade.
I'm already thinking of what to tell the House elite at the next party in Mournhold. I'm trying to decide how thrilling to make the tale. You understand, I'm sure.
Good luck. The Montclair family is one of the oldest in Rivenspire. If they think they can win this conflict, it's a good bet they have something up their sleeves.

Welcome to Hoarfrost Downs. It may just be the dreariest hamlet in Rivenspire, but don't let that scare you away.\n\nActually, this entire kingdom is rather dreary, isn't it? Never mind. I sense you've brought something for me.
Hail, stranger! I don't recognize you. You're not a member of the guild, are you? By Ysgramor's beard, why not?
Please, don't walk away. Don't ignore me. I really need your help. This blasted war has been devastating to us common folk.\n\nCan you spare a few pieces of gold for a poor beggar?
Tell the Baron we're waiting on him. If he needs us, we'll come running.
You have answered well and true. Through the gates, you may proceed.
I don't believe it. This is all some sort of trick, perpetrated by the houses or the Tribunal. The Maulborn can't be responsible for the plague. I simply refuse to accept that.
You can't restart while others are still inside the raid.
The Fighters Guild is here to serve! You know how it is. Hah!
We're proud to be here. No matter what the locals say, the Guild is here to help!

Your word is unquestioned. I am here to command.\n\nThough my blow caused Belronen's death, it was set in motion by another hand. I will aid you in discovering the source of this duel, if you will it.
My lord, the life of one such as Vamen bears no comparison to Belronen Telvanni. Yes, I sought to root corruption from the temple by poisoning that pile of scrib jelly. I'd do it again!

I did nothing but provide opportunity for a heretic to destroy himself. The act of dueling anyone within the temple would undo him. It's only fitting the fetcher did so with the tools I presented, and with such finality.
Good to have a roof here. Fighters Guild camps aren't always so well equipped, you know? Even if we do have to share with the Mages.
Be wary. The Wilderking's influence ebbs, even here in Greenheart. \n\nThe spirits of the forest are confused and angry—even my brethren—they will attack you with no provocation.
Who are you, then? Are you with our esteemed guests, or were you hoping to take shelter under the Skald-King's skirts?
Eagles advance, traveler! And may the Green watch and keep you.
What wonders you will see in the halls of Shad Astula. Oh, how I envy you! To experience it all again for the first time again—that would be marvelous!
Don't hold rudeness against the royals. It's like the scorpion, you know? It's in their nature.
I'll get my brother out of here. Thank you for helping me find him.\n\nI know you can take care of yourself. Just make sure you give these Maulborn a taste of their own bad medicine. For me.
Have you found the pages of my book?
Oh, hello. Do I know you?
The longer you delay, the longer Hazazi must stand here. Go!
Hail, friend. I trust you're gathering an impressive amount of Daedra heads? \n\nRumor has it the God of Brutality has taken notice of your handiwork.
I hear the buzz of fungus growing ….
You did it! You found all my missing family members!

The Bramblebreach village is just south of Marbruk. Hazazi is there. He likes to complain, but he's a good soldier. He just needs someone with a more sophisticated negotiation style. \n\nAnd by the time you get back, Raz will have a lead on the staff!
Thank goodness you came when you did.
Talk to my sister. She's got something to say.
Did you free the captives?
Don't come any closer. I don't want you to get the plague.
Don't touch anything! And try not to breathe too deeply. The affliction, it's everywhere! Everywhere!
Please … more curative … I need more curative ….
Welcome to our guild hall. It's more of a bungalow than a hall, but you get the idea. Have you come seeking membership in the Mages Guild?
Did you manage to close all of the portals?
Thank you for helping the Serk, my friend. The town would have been lost without you.\n\nStill, you shouldn't get too close to me. Just in case.
Forgive the sorry state of our facilities, but we're still reeling from the attack on Haven.\n\nHave you come seeking membership in the Mages Guild?
Welcome to the Elden Root Mages Guild Hall! Impressive, yes? Makes the one in Firsthold look like something of a broom closet. Don't repeat that.\n\nHow can I help you?
A word of caution: if you request a post in the Wood Elf frontier, be prepared to eat liver. At least I think it's liver.\n\nBut wait—you're not part of the Mages Guild, are you?

Don't mind the smell. I think one of those creatures relieved itself on the bookshelf. Charming, yes?\n\nHopefully none of the tomes were damaged. Their loss would be a great tragedy for the Mages Guild.
Did you heal the injured?
If you're seeking the Mages Guild, you've come to the right place. If you're looking for more brutish endeavours, I suggest you speak with someone on the other side of the hall.
Carpets to clean, scrolls to reorganize …. Wood Orcs. Thugs, the lot of them.\n\nBut enough of our troubles. Have you come to join the Mages Guild?
This seems like an odd place for the Mages Guild to set camp, yes? Well, we don't spend all our time in musty old libraries. This swamp pulses with arcane power—we'd be fools to ignore it.

I spent several hours watching the Wood Orcs and evaluating their weaknesses.\n\nAs a whole, their strength is in numbers. As long as you don't take on the entire camp, you should be fine. The chieftain's the one you have to watch out for.
Find those ingredients quickly.\n\nI must stay here to attend to the patient.
Auri-El smiles down on us. Mara's heart beats in your chest. And the bravery of Stendarr guides your hand.

I suspected they might choose to fight. They are not the first clan to seek to settle in this place, and sadly, they will likely not be the last.\n\nHopefully, next time, we might convince them to leave in peace.
Auri-El smiles down on us. Mara's heart beats in your chest. And the bravery of Stendarr guides your hand.

By the Three, these formulae don't look right at all.\n\nI was just collating these volumes—though I hardly see the point. The Mages Guild's expectations are very high. You'll learn that lesson well if you choose to join us.
I knew we could count on you. Just keep your wits about you. The Stormfists possess an unusual amount of cunning for a gang of common thugs.
Welcome to our completely ludicrous "guild hall." If it was up to me I wouldn't be here—but where our banner hangs, so too must a magister.
Good to see you back again, Adept. The Guild is stronger with you at our side.
Is there anything the Mages Guild can do for you my friend?
I don't know how to thank you. Without your help, the Maulborn would have destroyed the Serk.
There's no time for idle chit-chat right now. If you want to stay, you'll have to be quiet.
Good luck finding lodging! With so many petitioners, the inn's turning people away.

I must admit, your help was invaluable. It may not be a cure, but I can certainly use this suppressant to slow the progress of the plague to a crawl.\n\nHopefully, that will give me or the healers in Mournhold time to develop a proper curative.
Waiting is the hardest part. But if we trust in the Three, I'm certain everything will turn out fine.
I'm as busy as a skeever in a trash pit! Do you need something?
Lovely day, isn't it? Ate a bit too much at dinner, though. Haven't had any of Greenshade's snails in a long, long time.\n\nGo on in! There's probably some left over. We always share what we have.
Please, leave me alone. I don't want to talk about what happened here.
Welcome to our hall, fellow member. Please make yourself at home.

Undead? Ha. These are no rotting draugr or mindless skeletons. But it's true. They can't hardly be called living, either.\n\nUntie these bonds and help me stop them. I'll tell you what I can when I'm free.
I can't tell you how flattered I am that you offered your assistance, but please, don't worry about me.\n\nI can clean my own fruit.
I hope you and Gelvin aren't going to disappoint us. The Daggers are counting on your good judgment, friend.
Comrade, welcome back. Remember to keep your blade clean, now.
Come, mortal. Do a favor for this poor, weary spirit.
Don't let that Saravith talk you into anything. The fact that her spell worked at all and there weren't any strange side effects—well, that was just plain lucky, if you ask me.
You were the one? The one that helped the alchemist? Oh, thank you!\n\nMy wife hasn't been cured, but at least the plague won't continue to get worse as long as the suppressant holds out.
Greetings. Have you come to the Ashlands seeking glory and honor? The caverns of Stonefalls hold treasure. And danger. And death. \n\nAhem. Have you heard of them? The Armature? Emberflint?
Old Sorel no longer has any use for these things. Make like the wind and blow, or we shall be forced to exchange harsh words.
Old Sorel Tedas had good taste, don't you think? Too bad what happened to him. He was always nice to me. Liked to talk about politics and the weather.
Old Sorel takes care of us, even now that he's gone. Just don't mention you saw us to the house Elves. They wouldn't understand.
I feel terrible ….

Who knew that the job of a town consul would keep me so busy? I've barely had a chance to have a proper meal, let alone relax with a good book.\n\nBut thanks to you and Nilyne, the suppressant should buy us the time we need to defeat this plague.
Brave little scrib, do you know how to swim?
Aerona has really stepped up as town consul while her brother recovers. He'd better watch out. She may actually be better at the job than he is!

I'm glad you and Aerona didn't give up on me. I'm feeling much better. But Nilyne says her potion has only suppressed the plague, not cured it.\n\nIf you find a way to beat this plague, make sure you send word to us. And thanks for helping my town.

I have my work cut out for me. I need to make enough of the suppressant to treat everyone in the Serk. And then I have to continue trying to find an actual cure.\n\nDamn the Maulborn and their Llodos plague! Damn them to Oblivion and back!
Friend! I'm so glad to see you again.\n\nI've been keeping up my end of the bargain—with Verandis' help, of course.
I can't believe Verandis is really gone.\n\nI'm not sure what we're going to do without him, but we promised to continue the work he started here. That's the best way to honor his memory.
Thank you for sparing me. I may never be my true self again, but I can still serve Rivenspire.
<A slightly overcooked turkey leg, suspiciously uneaten.>

What? Yes? Ah. I see, a traveler. Have you come to the Ashlands looking for profit? House Dres applauds your efforts. \n\nIn fact, we're planning to exploit two new resources soon. Have you heard of the Hightide Hollow? Or Mephala's Nest?
Speak with care as you talk to Helgana. Her injuries are too great. Her soul will soon be with her honored ancestors in Sovngarde. \n\nI am just here to see her on her way.
Please, come … come closer. You need to know. \n\nThe Covenant … portal.
Thank you again. You have no idea how much your generosity has helped us out.\n\nThree watch over you!
Erunor is young for a caretaker, it must be hard on his wife.
Nilyne's suppressant will hold the plague at bay. It has to.\n\nI really don't want to pack up and move my wagon again.
Nilyne says that vile potion she made me drink will keep the plague from turning me into a zombie.\n\nI guess it didn't taste that bad, after all.
I'm glad we decided to come to the Serk. The town alchemist has been very helpful—even if she keeps trying to get me to drink sour milk tea. I never developed a taste for the stuff.
My father meant well, bringing us here, but the Maulborn deceived us all. I fear this plague is going to take us all.
I thought all the guests were in the garden already! My apologies!
Do you see them? Do you see the flowers? They're beautiful … simply beautiful.
Whatever is going on up there, I pray you can resolve it quickly. Good luck.
Mara grant you speed and mercy!
Auri-El watch over you!
Have you heard? The alchemist has come up with a suppressant. It isn't a cure, but at least it gives us a fighting chance against this damn plague.
Quite an event, isn't it? All the best guests, the wine flowing freely ….
My wife … I think the plague has rattled her mind. I pray that she recovers, but I fear the damage may be too severe.
Thanks for your help. Make sure you tell my cousin that I'm all right. If you head south, you won't be able to miss the Serk.\n\nTell her I'll return home as soon as I'm able.
Well, this job was underwhelming.\n\nYou ended up doing all the work! Maybe next time I can actually join you, eh?
So Dethisam and Aerona were right? The Maulborn are nothing more than … common swindlers! I am so angry right now I feel like knocking heads together!
Ah, good to see a fresh face. We villagers can get tired of just looking at each other after a hundred years.
You have done well to stop Tarish-Zi from gathering his cursed army of Anka-Ra.
I'm shaking all over inside. To be attacked in one's own home …! Valenwood is not as safe as it once was, I fear.
Not many of us work with stone. These foundations always need a bit of adjustment when we return.
Good thing we came back! I'm almost out of rotmeth. Nothing like a good dose of local fauna to bring out the best in it, I always say!
Sorry, can I help you? I'm a bit busy here. The Master has given me much to do, and little time to do it.
Talk some sense into that old wizard—if you can!

I heard some men talking in the marketplace. They claimed the Iron Orcs are stirring in the northern hills, like they're preparing for something big. I hope it isn't true. We have enough to worry about right now.
The Artisan, finally caught! Now what will the gossip be about, no?
You stand before me, not wounded and defeated, but proud and courageous.\n\nYou have overcome the trials! But what happened to the betrayer?
If I'd had the Artisan's skill, I would have used it to make enough gold to live somewhere else.
Knowledge for knowledge. That is my price.\n\nWhat have you brought me, Seeker?
Leaving so soon? Tell all your friends about us! Conversation tends to become rather stale down here without a steady supply of fresh faces.
I knew we shouldn't have hired that Bosmer. That was just asking for trouble.\n\nIn any case, how may I help you? Need to make a deposit or withdrawal?
Sister-of-Wind will recover. Breathing normal, body healing. Her dreams were tainted by the injuries.\n\nAlways happy when I help another. Always remember the ones I couldn't save.

Then what are you still talking to me for? Get to Hel Ra Citadel before all the good fighting is done.\n\nAnd if you see those fools who left me behind, tell them I said to go to Sovngarde. And not to enjoy themselves.
Need passage between Auridon and Grahtwood? I have a deal with some privateers. They'll take us across the Lane, free of charge.\n\nSay the word and I'll row us out to meet them.
<The ancient relic on this pedestal thrums with power. As you approach, the distinct taste of salt floods your mouth.>
May the light of Aldmeris guide you and may this whole nightmare be put to rest quickly … and with the least possible suffering.

I have been a soldier all my life, but never have I seen such a dreadful turn of events. Prince Naemon? An army of undead?\n\nIt's fortunate Camoran sent the Vinedusk Rangers, because there are simply too few Dominion troops to defend the city.
Please. Whatever it takes. Find the captain.

I am sorry for the deception. I was uncomfortable dealing with a Daedric Prince. And, I admit it, I was afraid.\n\nI have since embraced my role. Hermaeus Mora's curiosity is insatiable, but his knowledge reaches beyond mortal understanding.
Sorry about not following you in there. Nereids have a reputation for controlling the minds of any mortal that crosses their path. They make my skin crawl.
I have given you all that I am willing for the deeds done here.\n\nYou must stop the Yokudans at all cost. Their presence lingers here no more. Now it is up to you to stop them.
Greetings, Adept. Good to see you in person. I am Vanus Galerion, head of the Mages Guild you so ably serve. I have need of your assistance.
Good luck. Wherever your travels take you next, know that you have the power of Sheogorath to make you strong.
Ah, you return! And with news of the Maulborn. Tell me what the s'wits are up to now.
Navigating the hidden path requires faith—in one's senses and in one's masters.\n\nAbelazer the betrayer made a mockery of both. He was not what he seemed.
The trial of martial knowledge required cooperation and patience. Initiates needed to work together to gather the books. \n\nAbelazer tricked the others into helping him bring about their demise.
I never thought I would see this day. And so soon! Abelazar the betrayer is dead. Thanks to you.
Surely you are a great champion of Sentinel, wayfarer. Your deeds are known to the whole of the court and the spirits beyond the shore.
What else can you take from me? My entire journey is wasted because of you!
What do you want now? My claws?\n\nNo, for they are worth nothing. Forget this one's jest, yes?
I won't report you to the guards. Out of courtesy, you understand? Not because I'm frightened.
Mercenaries next time. Strong ones. That's what I'll bring.
Vivec's quivering backside … again? You already took my gold. What next, the lint in my coin purse?

Making sure the Staff of Magnus is safe in Marbruk is the queen's top priority right now.\n\nBe patient with Captain Sarandil. Raz has heard he is … proud of his city. You are the queen's envoy in this, so be on your best behavior.
Ah, another intrepid traveler visiting our rustic outpost.

Ah, my friend! My children are healthy thanks to your benevolence! Their bellies swell thanks to your generosity!\n\nBut times have not smiled on us since, I fear. Our gold dwindles to a scarce sum ….

Oh, my friend! Thank Mara I've found you once more!\n\nDastards! Miscreants of the very worst cut! As soon as you left they were upon me—beating me, taking the gold you so kindly gave me to feed my poor, starving children!
Ah, walker! The coin you gave me has served me well, but I've, ah … lost it. To the unfeeling ravages of time, yes?\n\nI mean, bandits! The same bandits as before!
We meet again, I'm afraid. Your gold did much to fill my belly, but the moon turns and its hollows gape wide once more.
Ah, the burr-sap! Catch my heel again?
You've saved us from an incredible embarassment. The Fighters Guild needs people like you.
Spare a sword-arm for the Fighters Guild? We need all can get. Axe-, stave-, and hammer-arms are also acceptable.\n\nBow-arms, too. I guess.
As far as I'm concerned, the Fighters Guild should join you. I'll waive all requirements for entry, if you're interested in being a part of something bigger.
You can find the Dominion's best warriors in our ranks. This is why you should join us!
The lizards here say Hissmir is a great trial. Passing it makes you … more lizardy.\n\nHa! I'll tell you what a real trial is—killing Daedra. Join the Fighters Guild and see for yourself.
Our banners represent the blood of members such as you. You strengthen us with your every effort.
You don't look like a pirate! I mean, unless you're trying to look like a pirate. I'm not familiar with the latest fashion.\n\nYou should join the Fighters Guild. Even if you're a pirate.
Please. You need to get that order to my brother in Mournhold as soon as you can.
Go talk to <<1>>. He's at the camp near the old ruins.
If you happen to run into my sister, let her know that I'll make sure she gets her order. Somehow.\n\nJust don't tell her what I really do here. It would break her heart.
Please. Go to Honrich Tower as soon as you can. This is serious.\n\nI've been studying under Elfriede for ten years and I've never seen her so worried about anything.
I'm impressed my apprentice actually found you. Maybe he's smarter than I give him credit for?\n\nWell, I don't want to be hasty. We'll see if he can get himself back here in one piece.

If there's any chance Nahlia is alive, we have to find her.\n\nLook at the scroll and see if you can make anything out of it. I couldn't go after her on my own, but now that you're here, we have to try.

Some of our researchers disappeared a few days ago in the city wing. And the crypt wing … well, we've stayed away from that one. Terrible sounds emanate from there.\n\nI guess what I'm saying is, be careful. It's not just the water that's dangerous.
I hear you defeated Yamanu-ko and her apprentices. \n\nIt will take a long while for the city to get back to normal, but at least it's our city once more.

I'm relieved that the city is safe, but I can't say I'm glad that Yamanu-ko's gone.\n\nShe taught me everything I know about magic. She always warned me about the temptations of power. For her to fall like this ….
<Symbols appear next to pictures of a man instructing a centurion. This could be instructions on how one teaches a centurion to act on its own.>
You've done well. Craglorn is safe, for now. I will remain behind, in case this place becomes unstable again.
Thank you, my friends. Nerien'eth was no longer the man I knew.\n\nPerhaps he never was.

I protested against the bargain. I did not trust the salvation Shada promised.\n\nFor my troubles, Shada cursed me twice. I was forced to drink the water, but to remain conscious, watching as my people slowly went mad under Shada's influence.

I'm happy you found her. That you saved her.\n\nBut … I feel sad, too. The woman I … thought she was—she never existed, did she? In a way, I feel like Hara never came back at all. Maybe I'm being selfish.
Don't just stand there. I know there is some way you can make yourself useful. If nothing else, just go and kill some of those damn Worms.
I've told you all I know. You need to bind the monarch atronachs before we can understand what's happening.
Do not take Zal'ik lightly. Even as he rests now, his power is beyond most have ever faced.\n\nIf you manage to succeed, I will find you at the end of the caves.
Our friend is losing all the things that make her her.\n\nI have tried every known cure for madness, delirium, and memory loss I know. I am afraid all is lost!
Use the Gem of Aetherial Command to bind the two remaining monarch atronachs.\n\nThe flame monarch can be found within the halls of Molavar. The stone monarch is near Balamath.

Servants of the Serpent hired the feared Greycloak mercenaries to capture Kelmen Locke.\n\nThe merceneries hold him in a place called Haddock's Market. When they learn all they can, they plan to hand Kelmen over to the Serpent. We need to rescue him.
This is very bad news.\n\nThe Serpent used the monarchs and their power to create a new atronach—one with the ability to take on the elements of other atronachs.
I don't know what's next for us, but I know this—it's going to be better than Oblivion. I wish Gilraen would stop worrying.

Kind of these Star-Gazers to let us set up shop here in their observatory. I guess it makes them feel safer. I still feel like a kagouti in a glass-blower's shop, though.\n\nBut what brings you all the way up here? Looking to join the Fighters Guild?

You certainly have interesting friends. \n\nI can't say I like sticking my neck out, but you did save me from those bandits. So if you need help finding this Reinhold's Retreat Hara mentioned, I'll do my best.

Reinhold's Retreat. Is that truly what she said? I thought my ears had conspired to fill my mind with the foulest lies, but if you heard the same ….\n\nPerhaps I was meant to be here for reasons other than just stopping Tarish-Zi.
I don't care what you have. <<1>> doesn't leave the stocks unless Magistrate <<2>> tells me himself.

I can't thank you enough. You trusted me, even when I'd failed to show the same trust in you.\n\nI won't make that mistake again. From here forward, we must work together closely if we're to defeat the Serpent.
Thank you for returning our aspects to us. We have discussed among ourselves and concluded that the Lost One is too powerful for us to defeat.\n\nThe best we can hope for is to weaken her.
The Lost One is no longer in control of her actions. Now is the time to strike.
I spend hours every day hunched over my anvil. Good to stretch my muscles for a moment. What can I get you?

Split-Nose and this one are old acquaintances.

That one has troubles of the mind, and has requested this one help him make sense of his mind and self.

Aside from the hoarding, it seems to be going well.
Do as the aspects asked. And hurry. The Serpent gets closer to his goal with every passing moment.
Thank you for recovering <<1>> from the Iron Wheel. <<2>> is grateful she remains his assistant.
You have done for us what we could not do for ourselves. We will remember this.
The Scaled One is gathering our other aspects. We cannot hope to overwhelm him, but we must hope to match him. Our best chance is to face him on an even footing.
