Anything I can get for you, dear? I have a wholesome assortment of stock for the discerning chef.\n\nOf course, if you don't need anything, that's fine too. I enjoy company.
This town needs an arena. My business demands bloodshed, and having some sport on which to bet is always delightful.\n\nThe magistrate is a fool for not building one.
We're through here, mortal. Your presence is no longer required. It would behoove you to leave, in fact.
This doesn't look like the Aetherian Archive. It's going to be hard being the first to the top if you start in the wrong place.\n\nHa! I slay me.

When the High Elves approach you, remember that I warned you. Those women have a strange way of spotting anything related to the Star-Gazers.\n\nAnd guess what? If you're working with Hara, you're related to us now.

I no longer feel the Learned One's presence. Has she finally decided to leave us?\n\nI suppose it was time. I never believed she would stay indefinitely. And with the Great Source gone, perhaps it's time the Firstmages returned to Tamriel.
That mere mortals could best the Mage so easily gives me pause—I question whether that kind of power belongs in mortal hands. But I thank you for your help.

Have you seen the High Elves that were here by any chance?\n\nI was supposed to keep an eye on them, and I only turned away for a moment and now they're gone! Oh, Hara is going to be very angry with me.
<Without the blackened gem, the orrery holds no further interest.>
You … you've been to the upper floors, haven't you?\n\nWhat did you do? I no longer feel the presence of the Learned One.
I saw you enter the upper floors. And I no longer feel the presence of the Learned One. What exactly did you do?\n\nI told you not to go up there! You've irked her and she's left us, hasn't she?
How can I help a fellow Star-Gazer?
You survived a raid into the Citadel? Tell this Khajiit, have you ever considered an exciting career as caravan guard?
The Tribunal protect you for clearing the mountain path.\n\nI didn't think you had the heroic look about you, but clearly I was wrong.

And so you return! None have done so before—I assume you defeated whatever menace awaited within!\n\nThat you return without any of my fellow Redguard pains me. Don't tell me of their fate—I will go and discover for myself.
I see you return, friend! Do you return victorious?\n\nHave you made it to the top of the Aetherian Archive?
Up and about, are we?
Ha! I was worried you'd never wake up. You slept all the way from <<1>>. Right through the hurricane!
Ah! Don't frighten an old man like that!
Back on your feet already? You needn't offer me gold, I only did what anyone should. I helped someone in need.\n\nUnlike some people I could point at ….
Quickly! Before the guards spot you!
Always good to see you, my friend. You are like a cousin to me, truly.
My new friend. I am glad to speak with you again. I have much I wish to discuss.
What is it? Is this about the fish? I took what I paid for!\n\nUm, never mind. What do you want?
What are you talking to me for? You have a course to run. Follow the markers until you reach the end! Talaya will record your time when you're done.
This one likes this course the best. It is the route she took with her father when he was first teaching her to skulk in the shadows.
I think the Khajiit has used some kind of spell to keep me from winning.
<This Dominion marine is dead.>
Ah, you've returned! I trust that my perfidious acolytes have been properly dealt with?
Go. You are needed at the Fort. The Moons have spoken and will not tell you again.
Hjargredda just returned, but she was too shaken up to say very much. What did you find?

Atildel says you're here to help. This one hopes you know what you agreed to. There's some kind of spirit lurking within these caverns—the Gazers call it a "Celestial Serpent"—it will wreak havoc if it ever escapes.\n\nYou cannot let that happen!
Atildel says you're actually going in there. Do you have a death wish?\n\nThe Celestial Serpent himself leads the Scaled Court in these caverns!

Atildel said you were planning to enter these caves. I can't believe she convinced you. We've been trying to get her to leave.\n\nThe Celestial Serpent stalks this place. He has plans for Craglorn—for all of Tamriel.
I demand to be set free!\n\nYou ingrates think this attack on Sanctum Ophidia will go unanswered? The master will digest all of you! Slowly!
Has the little goat finished its work?
Dominion soldiers here? Have you come to free me or kill me? Whichever it is, do it quickly!

Atildel says you're willing to head into those caves—face the Serpent. You've certainly got gumption. Might change your mind if you saw what it did to us.\n\nYou're going to need equipment either way. What do you say? Give me your money.

Did I hear the High Elf correctly? You're going into those caverns?\n\nWe're in no shape to do it, so you might as well. But you'll need some potent soul gems to take those cultists on. Lucky for you, I have a few lying around.
Good luck.
Stendarr defend me!
Thank Jone and Jode. This one thought today would never come.\n\nHe will tell his children about you.

By the Eight, you're alive! You've been gone so long. I was beginning to think I should have tried harder to keep you out of the ruins.\n\nBut tell me, was what I feared true? Was the Scaled Court harvesting more nirncrux?

And so the hero returns. I should have known you were the one to free us. Nerien'eth single-handedly trounced us—even as the entire school stood ready to face him.\n\nBut if someone could defeat him it would be you.
When—if—you succeed, I would speak with you before you leave. I'll wait by the docks.\n\nFear not. No Tenets shall be broken. After all, you honor Sithis with your deeds.
You know what they say—when the Void gives you lemons, squeeze 'em into someone's eyes.\n\nOr is it "squeeze someone's eyes into 'em?" I think both could work, if you put your back into it.
"Whoosh." Elf capons.\n\nHeh.
Have you seen Taara's "charnel gown?" A full suit of armor, complete with a closed helm! Leave it to soldiers to eschew funereal silks.
If you see Eamil embarrassing my family name, I give you leave to slap the smirk from his face.\n\nNo hestitation. Just a sharp smack.
Taara will soon be with her ancestors. Auri-El bless us all.
I hope Norion can forgive me.

I feared what it would take to defeat Nerien'eth—feared that he had grown in strength. He isn't the kind to remain idle. Not when he would slay his wife and destroy everything she held dear for power.\n\nAt least the day is won. You have my thanks.
Garamiel says he's seen those damned gray-hides strip-mining just a few wheels from here. Some of kind of red ore. Makes me wonder what they're doing with it … and how much I could sell it for.

Did you hear about the six-legged, spear-tailed, goat-horned, monster? It was all they talked about around the cooking fire last night.\n\nEither red brittle has gotten into the water supply or people are a lot more gullible than I imagined.
Aetherian light take him! I was so certain I could best Nerien'eth this time. That I had strengthened my spells.\n\nIf you hadn't come back, we'd all be dead. Again.
I'll be all right. You don't have to worry about leaving me alone here.\n\nGo on. Get to Dragonstar and help Cassi. And thanks again.
Some of those you rescued came through here, and I am told many others escaped the city.\n\nHave you rescued all that you can, for now, at least?
We found him—we found him, and we'll need help.\n\nHe slew so many of us.
Wait, I'm not your enemy. I need your help. If we work together, we can put an end to the Serpent's threat once and for all.\n\nShould I continue?
Yes, you caught this one. Again.
Here to swing a pick? If so I'd find another line of work. Mine's shut down till we sort out this whole Orc … snake … thing.
I sense that the darkness within the catacombs has subsided. Tell me, did you find the source of whatever disturbed the dead?
Kelmen should have never confronted her alone. This Cassipia must pay for the blood spilled today!
Regent Cassipia reached for powers that were not hers to acquire.

I admit it. I didn't think our mission stood an Elf's chance in Orsinium of succeeding. But here we are!\n\nYour reputation is rightly deserved. And with any luck, those wards will hold for another thousand years.

Now yours is a face I haven't seen in a long time.\n\nDo you remember me? We met among the mountains of Skyrim. In Eastmarch, if I recall. We walked with giants. Put some brutish Orcs in their place. Good times!
This one has been informed that there are far fewer Daedra in the sewers than there were before. You have closed the portals to Coldharbour, yes?
Are you ready to be certified? I have time if you do.
Please. Hurry to Belkarth. I don't think you should keep the great warrior waiting any longer than is absolutely necessary.
It's good to see you again before the end, my friend. I was just saying one last farewell to my wife before I depart to find my final battle.
Find Skarath and retrieve War-sworn. That Iron Orc is not worthy to carry such a blade.\n\nTitus has earned my weapon a hundred times over. I would see War-sworn in his hands.
<No new commissions are available at this time.>
<No new commissions are available at this time.>
<No new commissions are available at this time.>
<No new commissions are available at this time.>
<No new commissions are available at this time.>
<No new commissions are available at this time.>
If you're ready to be certified, we should begin.
By the kindness of Jone and Jode!\n\nYou squashed that Daedroth! Reminds me of when I was young—batting the other children around like balls of yarn!
No more—I beg you.\n\nWe should never have come. You can keep the woman. We'll tell Fingaenion we found nothing. I swear it!
<You notice a prominent handbill on the requisition board.>\n\n"Certified Crafters, We Want Your Wares! Armor, Weapons, Bows, Jewelry, and Robes! Hone your craft and earn a reward!"
"CITIZENS of the DOMINION, MASTERS of the CRAFT await you in <<Z:1>>! New crafters shall be TRAINED! Accomplished crafters will be CERTIFIED! All at NO COST TO YOU!"
Help me.
You have my thanks. Without you, my husband would likely have been mauled by senches, let alone Daedra.\n\nOnly Dagon left to deal with, now.
Your timing is impeccable, my friend.\n\nI must've slaughtered a hundred of them. Never thought I would see the day, but I haven't the strength to swing my sword.

Fighting an endless sea of foes just isn't the same without a barrel of ale to wash it down. Let's hope Sovngarde is a bit more … hospitable.\n\nThis isn't Sovngarde, is it? I feel like I've been fighting for a week. Are there Daedra in Sovngarde?

I just slew three Daedra with the same laughing face.\n\nHogondar won't believe me, but I think it's the same one. How do you kill something that won't stay dead? Dammit it all! This place doesn't make any sense!
Give this one a moment, please. She just stopped a howling ball of flame with her face. Sobabe was excited to come here, but the Wood Elf was right.\n\nThis is the worst place in the world.
Please don't make me speak.
<Agonized groaning.>
Good to see another mortal step in. Not that we couldn't have handled that ourselves.
Seems like everyone had a pretty unpleasant experience. At least it wasn't Apocrypha.
I've given you my report. Now leave before you give away my position!
Maj awaits you, Undaunted. If you have the constitution to survive her pledges, we will speak again soon enough.
Urgarlag and Glirion are good sorts. They take a little getting used to, but once you start accepting their pledges, you'll see!

This is it, soldier! This is what we've been fighting for—the crown jewel of Cyrodiil, the glorious Imperial City! \n\nNot so impressive, huh? Sadly, our base in the sewers here is the only part of the city that isn't overrun by gods-damned Daedra.
Thank you ever so much. I just can't seem to do these things on my own any more. Old eyes and older bones, ay?

You destroyed the wraith. Not many can say that, friend. You have done his victims, and me a great service. They're free, for now.\n\nUnfortunately, he will be back. He never truly dies. More's the pity, eh?

My greatest desire would be to bring my companions' bodies back, to be buried among their ancestors. But I saw the bodies dragged away by those Daedra. I can't even imagine what will become of them. \n\nMy knife will have to do.

Oh … you've made it? My friend. \n\nThe children are ready for supper, and my time is almost done. Do you see how strong they are? I will give them a strong start. They will do great things. Won't you, my loves?

My sister tells me you found her. She immediately put you to work, didn't she? She's always been good at getting people to help her out.\n\nSo tell me, what did she send you off to find? Some shiny bauble to add to her collection?
You found one, didn't you? I knew you could do it! Thanks!\n\nAnd don't worry, next time I fall into an ancient ruin I'll make sure to come prepared. Maybe even have a plan or something.

A volunteer. I appreciate that kind of go-get-them attitude.\n\nIf you do manage to find either of the missing squads, remind them that they have their orders. I expect them to complete their missions. The outcome of this siege depends on them!
<This tome is bitingly cold to the touch, and lies open to a page that reads, "For those mortals wishing to make a Pact—speak the words, in your own frail tongue, 'come slow and bring four keys.'">
Excellent work in Watcher's Hold. I'll let that oaf <<1>> know if I need any more help.
Ah, greetings, traveler! Hold a moment, won't you? I'm looking for a cave. It would be foul smelling, likely surrounded by scattered bones and such. Have you seen such a place?

It took months to arrange this deal! Everyone was going to profit! \n\nThe Orcs get new ballistae and this one and her partners were going to get a pile of gold! This is what comes from trusting a dishonest Breton smuggler!
A disaster. An unmitigated disaster.
Welcome! Prepare to be transported through time! Look into the past to see the future! Behold, the deeds of the Orcish people!
You helped Lady Laurent reach the summit of Sorrow? What was it like? Did you find all kinds of wonderful treasures?\n\nNo, don't tell me. I really don't want to know.
Excuse me. Have you seen a Nord named Snordan?
Ho there, buy you … I mean buy you … I mean buy me a drink?
Ah, frozen eggs! So crunchy and cold! Yum!\n\nAnd I'm certain that the ritual was a success. The hagraven's curse has been reversed. Another satisfying affair, if I do say so myself!
I hate to see rare antiquities mishandled and poorly used, but I suppose Deechee-Noo knows what she's doing.\n\nAnd I never could say no to that lovely Argonian.
I suppose I should thank you. If you have time, I have some questions about what happened in those ruins.

Maybe Deechee-Noo can help me acquire an exclusive contract with the Mages Guild. That would probably add a touch of authenticity to my wares, and you can't buy that kind of publicity without spending a wagon-full of gold.

Deechee-Noo is a little strange, but she knows how to have a good time!\n\nI did try one of those frozen eggs once myself, though. You know what I got? A chipped tooth! I don't know what she sees in those things.
He spent all that gold to get himself a durzog and now he doesn't even want it? I'll never understand Elves.
It's like a nightmare … what they're doing down there. I managed to sneak away … but someone has to stop them ….
You have my gratitude. We may not be able to save these Orcs from such a terrible fate, but their misfortune could yet bear fruit.
That was an admirable display of logic. I'm glad we can make the best of this unfortunate situation. The constructs will increase production in the quarry a hundredfold!

There are two things my son can't resist—food and battle. When he learned of Ice-Heart's location, he rushed to deal with the warlord personally.\n\nHelp him end the threat and recover the supplies. The unification of the Orc clans depends on it!

I do not wish to delay your journey. I have duties to attend to at the temple and I know King Kurog awaits you at Frostbreak Fortress.\n\nStill, in all my travels, I have never encountered so many troublesome extremists as I have here in Orsinium.

I'll see you back at the keep. Oh, hey! Remind me when you get there. You have to try some of Hearth-Wife Barazal's mountain bear hash. It tastes amazing!\n\nWe'll have a feast! Right after you show the Ice-Heart to the clan chiefs.
You've done us a great service. You'll always be welcome at Tumnosh Stronghold.
An empty crate sits here, waiting for a supply drop.
You're back! Tell me, were you able to recover our sacred banner?
You're heading up to try to get into the fortress?\n\nWell, watch out for the harpies. They've flown off with more of my soldiers than I care to admit.
Shh! Try not to alert the Winterborn down there. We're preparing an ambush, and I don't want it spoiled.

My soldiers will pluck the feathers from those harpies, mark my words!\n\nOh, the king is with you. I didn't notice. I meant no disrespect, King Kurog. My clan and my soldiers are yours to command, always and forever.
The report for the Pact is your concern now. Do not fail in delivering it.
I've given you my report. Now leave before you give away my position!
I can't believe you did it! Old Logronakh sure has an eye for talent, eh Chief?
Oh my … poor Mazhun.
Interesting times ahead. Represent us well to the king, my chief. Never forget your responsibility to your clan.
Vision … fades. And yet, I see you clearly through the fog at life's end. Malacath? Is that you?\n\nNo. I see … I see … Malacath sent you to me, didn't he? That means … his words will not be lost ….
I think I'll go home to the Alik'r Desert after this. Get as far away from Nellic Sterone as I possibly can.
Ah, outsider! I confess I had my doubts, but my forge-wife tells me you were as good as your word.\n\nThank you for helping restore order to the Graystone Quarry.
Just need to rest for a moment. Then I'll head back to camp.\n\nWhen you find my brother and the others, tell them Avreg said to get their tiny tusks back to Orgotha—on the double!
I don't know. After all this, maybe I'm not ready to lead a hunting party quite yet.
Yes, you killed a couple of fool Daedra. Must all peasants be congratulated for doing their work?\n\nWe have the Ruby Throne, but the Elder Scroll is still out there.

Thanks, friend. I can't tell you how much this means. My brother's probably been searching for me—you know how big brothers are.\n\nHe'll take it hard, but he needs to just leave. It would break our mother's heart if neither of us survived.
All this fuss over a hammer. Old ideas, old traditions … what do they bring us but blood and rubble?
If you fail my husband in any way, I will hunt you down and gut you.\n\nFight well, outsider, fight well.
Are the star-crossed lovers bickering again? Or perhaps they are just cross lovers?\n\nThis one has never seen a more ill-suited pair. Azeeda is a kind lady, but that man. He's a shifty one, yes?
I can't believe it. Not only did I leave all my clothes behind on the ship, but I left my comb too!\n\nI might just have to go back.
I don't give a guar's arse whether these logs came from Valenwood or not. When it's this cold, the Green Pact doesn't apply.
Go on. See the wonders of Wrothgar. I'll be at my private cornerclub when you're ready for a new challenge.\n\nJust don't get yourself killed. I still have plans for you!
You see what the chiefs do? How they disrespect my son and refuse to accept his plans? They should consider themselves lucky that only one chief spilled blood this day!
You're not flirting with my wife, are you?
Please, let the forge-mother know my suspicions, but make sure she understands that they are only that. I don't want to start a war with the clan chiefs over idle speculation.
Ah, Kurog's outsider! I'm not sure what you did exactly, but you somehow restored peace to my family and thereby helped my clan.\n\nYou have my thanks.
I have other tasks to do for Bazrag, but perhaps I will see you back at the Clanhold.
A blood-kin chief? This better not be some ride-by-night glory grab. Don't cheapen what you've won for bragging rights.\n\nBut you don't need to hear it said. Uh, chief.
Please hurry, if you can. Semusa-la cannot face General Nedras unless he has heard from Captain Thorasa.
I don't know what to say. I respected Kurog's ideals, his vision … but all of that was built on sand.
I lost my best friend. Then I killed his daughter … the woman I was once supposed to marry.\n\nWhen it rains, it pours … but right now, it feels like it's pouring out an echatere's back half.
Get that <<z:1>> to <<2>>. And thanks. I won't forget your help.

White-Gold Tower belongs to the Empire again, but there's much work left to do. Where has the true Clivia gone? I must speak to the Imperial generals. They'll be … interested to know a Daedra has been leading them.\n\nSo many questions left to ask.
We never seem to run out of Daedra to kill down here. We're just lucky that way.\n\nWho'd you take care of?
Well, did you earn your pay today?
<The Hunting Board has no notices posted.>
Ah, the smell of steam and ash. A strange combination, to be sure, but in this context, I might say it was the scent of victory.\n\nWere you able to extinguish any of the fires?

What are you doing in here? This place is for the weak and the wounded. \n\nYou look perfectly capable. That being the case, I wonder—why aren't you outside trying to retake the temple from those accursed Daedra?
I can't wait to get back into the arena now. The Daedra will be expecting me to fall, but they'll be in for a surprise.
The funny thing is that I've been holding back, fighting defensively because I knew I didn't have any way to heal.\n\nNext bout, the Daedra are going to see the true extent of my abilities.
Look at you, walker, still stalking the streets unscathed. Your step seems a bit heavier though. Are you weighed down with treasures for Aishah?
I'm not going anywhere.\n\nThis isn't going to work twice.
I can't find it. I've looked everywhere, and I can't find it anymore.\n\nIt has to be here!

There you are! I heard the most wonderful scream of agony that really sounded like it was coming from that infernal Scarhea. To hear it suffer was beautiful.\n\nDoes that mean you killed it? Please say yes.
Shining-Eyes stopped in a little while ago. He actually erected the spine of gratitude for sending the shirt. \n\nThey grow to maturity so fast. I remember when he was just a little spotted egg.

Kaoc! This shirt feels like fresh, warm mud. I am embarrassed that my mother asked you to perform such a petty errand, especially because it was my own fault.\n\nAll the same, I erect the spine of gratitude.
Remember. You have to remain stealthy for the spell's effects to be active. \n\nBanish a few of the Veilweavers and then return to let me know if it worked.
Two of my babies are back! Please hurry and find the last one.

I believe that each flesh colossus has several of the sacs I need. Necrotic hoarvor have only one apiece.\n\nWhichever is easiest for you to find and slay; it makes no difference to me. The sacs are basically the same. Good luck.
<The crate contains ample space for deliveries, and a sheaf of manifest papers.>
Don't bother looking for my scouts. Just blow the horn. They'll find you.
As Azaro said, it is good that all was not lost when the ship wrecked, but everything depends on whether they can make it Orsinium in time.\n\nThey are on their way, though, yes?
Ah, you've returned.
<You notice a prominent handbill on the requisition board.>\n\n"Certified Crafters, We Want Your Wares! Potions, Glyphs, Food, and Drink! Hone your craft and earn a reward!"
White-Gold Tower has been home to the Empire since the early First Era. To see Daedra make a mockery of it atop the Ruby Throne burns my soul.
Sister Arminus was right about one thing: you know how to kill Daedra.
Watch your back. Only the Divines know how long these beasts have been lurking here. Empty rooms are never quite empty when Daedra are involved.
Today would have been a dark one without you.\n\nDo me a favor and don't be so vocal about it, yes? You could cost me my job.
The notes you found contain some fascinating information. Have you read them? I, for one, cannot wait to fell these anchors and claim the city for the Pact.\n\nAncestors guide you.

I tell you, soldier, a city like this … it's just foul. The stench in these sewers—what have these people been eating? \n\nHate to say it, but it might be better to let it go to Oblivion. Mind you, those aren't my orders, though.
The Rat heard the announcements for arena fights, and he thought he heard the name "Anthas." \n\nDoes that mean you were able to deliver the poultices?
This one has heard tales of an Arena champion! How delightful. I must confess, I am surprised they let you leave. These Daedra are strange creatures, eh?

Did the Bosmer general send you? Nedras, or whatever his name is?\n\nI hope so. That cranky, little bastard didn't send enough soldiers. Between the Daedra and the other alliances, they're getting chopped down pretty quick.

Even if the city is reclaimed, I suspect my term on the Elder Council has come to an end. \n\nI have a summer home south of the city. If it's still standing, I think I'll spend the remainder of my years down there.
Travel down the river is not cheap. It's a good thing your friend here is a fast talker.
Thank you. I had nearly given up hope. \n\nThe Daedra dragged me to the upper level of one of the houses here. Please, come quickly.
The lock on this Imperial coffer has been broken and all its contents have been removed.
I'd love to do business, but now isn't really a good time.
No sale—the Guard is watching the docks. Come back later and we'll do business.
Not right now. Come back later, when the Guard scrutiny is less intense.
I understand your frustration, but I have too much inventory at the moment.
Sorry, I can't help you right now. Return later and we can work something out.
How good to see you! Unfortunately, now isn't a good time. Come back later when I've moved my stock.
Sometimes the heat is too much, even for me. Perhaps another time.
No, we are closed. And this one's head aches. Come back later. Much later … ulp.
If you'd been here earlier, I'd have given you my full attention. Come back and see me later.
Hmm. I'm at capacity. Come back later.
Oh dear, it seems I've outspent my means! Come back later, will you?
Not right now. The Guard is on to me!
I'd try to help out, but I have my hands full right now. Come back later.
Sorry. Not buying anything until I move what I've got.
Turns out you can have too much of a good thing. Come back later, hmm?
Make yourself scarce. I can't move anything else right now.
Hm. I'm only allowed do business with Enforcers. Talk to Osgug if you want to join.
I'm so sorry, but I only deal in Enforcer business. You should talk to Osgug.
I do business with Enforcers only. Talk to Osgug if you must bother someone about membership.
Oh, I wish I could help you, but this is Enforcer business. Talk to Osgug. He'll get you sorted!
I only deal with Enforcers. Tedious, I know, but those are the rules. Talk to Osgug, if you must.
You should join the Enforcers. It would be an absolute pleasure to do business with you. Talk to Osgug.
Not an Enforcer? Can't help you.\n\nDon't ask about membership. Bother Osgug instead.
We only serve Enforcers. We should serve drinks. What was I saying?\n\nOh yeah, talk to Osgug. He can get you a drink. I mean, he can get you into the Enforcers.
I can't let non-Enforcers in on Enforcer business. Talk to Osgug if you want to join.
Sorry, Enforcers only. Want to buy or sell? Talk to Osgug.
Forgive me, but I only deal in Enforcer business. Talk to Osgug to join.
You want to deal? Become an Enforcer … then we can talk. Osgug will show you what to do.
Oh, I'd love to help you, but you must be an Enforcer first. Talk to Osgug about joining!
Oh dear, this is awkward. You aren't an Enforcer, so I can't do business. You should talk to Osgug.
You want to do business with the Enforcers? Become one. Talk to Osgug.
Enforcer business only. Come back once you've spoken to Osgug.
Go on. Don't worry about me. This is what I want.
I'm sorry to see that you've turned to the life of an outlaw. I'd implore you to change your ways. Nothing good comes of preying on the weak and helpless.
<This will never be recorded.>
Another outsider? Well, at least it's good to see an Orc visiting our village. And you do look more capable than that braggart, Narsis Dren.
That was exhilarating! I'd say we're done here. Another profitable adventure for the famous Narsis Dren!
Keep my beloved safe. Do that and I will be eternally grateful.\n\nFor king and glory!
Ambassador Lazdutha will be here any moment! She said she had documents for me to sign. \n\nAre you ready to give Rigurt the ingredients needed to prepare a romantic evening of Orcish love?

Thanks again for this delightful cheese! I spent time in Windhelm, studying with Cheesemonger Barl, and I developed quite a taste for curdled mammoth cheese.\n\nJust be careful with the echatere cheese. Sometimes just the smell can arouse an eager Orc.
Before all this Orsinium nonsense, people used to respect the privacy of the noble recluse.
May Tall Papa gird your loins, my friend. I believe you'll need all the help you can get when it comes to Orc affection.
Better not get too close with that bear musk! Unless, of course, you're in the market for a hunt-wife ….\n\nRelax, I'm just teasing you!
The Dark Elf wasn't completely honest with us, was he?
We did good work today, my friend! You should be proud!\n\nNow if you'll excuse me, I have to finish my tale and then accept compensation from my adoring public!
And so Lady Laurent makes another fabulous discovery!\n\nNow if I can figure out how to thaw out my man-servant, I can mark this adventure as a success.
I must admit I'm on the edge of my seat to see how this resolves!\n\nDon't worry. I'll keep Torug's relic safe while you talk to Lady Laurent and Kharsthun.
This whole business about being worthy is too tempting a challenge for the average Orc.\n\nI guess we'll need to figure out a way to keep everyone from trying on the Fist.

I've already traced the origins of one of the items to the time of the Dragon War. Isn't that exciting?\n\nAnd I've called upon an alchemist to help me run some tests to determine its composition and physical make up.
Back again? I knew you had a head for business! Shall we complete the deal and get on with our lives?
His lordship didn't make it. Damn. At least he tried to make things right in the end.
While you were up in the signal tower, Skordo did some scouting and he thinks he figured out where Captain Henrisa disappeared to. He went to see if the ambassador was there as well.
I've never … been stabbed before ….

I saw you talking to that milksop, Ethian. He's nothing like his father. Nothing at all.\n\nBut I don't have time for his belly-aching. I need to make sure we don't lose anymore people to the cold and the ice.
I can't believe it. Dead … both of them. I lost my husband to that damn legend and now I've lost my son, too.\n\nOh, Khoruzoth! Why didn't you listen to me, you stupid Orc?

Off with you now! Once the commander is certain that the harpy threat has been dealt with, he'll send me to meet you inside the fort.\n\nUntil then, if you don't mind, I'm going to stay safe and sound right here.

Did I hear that right? They're going to actually trust me with this mission?\n\nIt's about time. I told them how I won every one of my clan's archery tournaments since I was tall enough to hold a bow. I can do this. I know I can.

Soon we leave for Orsinium. The forge-hammer gives my clan hope. I'll see it raised high.\n\nIf my sister can even lift the thing. Wouldn't do for the king's forge-wife to go rump-over-teakettle, would it? Hah!
My poor Ethian. He wasn't a brave man, but he tried to stand up against that vile Henrisa.

Leave the sapling I found alone. I'll use it to prepare and test my elixir while you burn as many of the others as you can.\n\nBy the time you return, I'll have developed a poison powerful enough to eat through the central tree's weakened defenses.
Go and do what you need to do. I'll figure out how to get Alinon down from there.\n\nI'm still trying to figure out how they got him up there, though.
The rest of the Orc soldiers went back to the camp to report in and get new orders. I don't think they actually expected you to find the alchemist.\n\nI guess the joke's on them, huh?
There's nothing else we can do out here. Let's get inside.

Well, thanks for all the help. I have to admit, I couldn't have destroyed the source of the briarhearts without you.\n\nIf you're ever in Orsinium, look for me at the King's Cornerclub. I'll even buy you a drink!
Another mission accomplished! We make a pretty good team, don't we?\n\nIf you need my help again, just whistle. I'm always ready for another adventure!

It pains me to admit it, but mother is right. Again. I do have a bit of a temper, but I'm working on that.\n\nAnyway, I'll sit this one out and let you handle it. Regardless of what happens, you will have my full support.

My request carries a heavy burden. Believe me, I know. But your actions will potentially save innocent lives and bolster the king's standing.\n\nDo not fail me, outsider, and I will make sure that you are greatly rewarded.
Like I said, if you're trying to find another way in, check around back. The stairs near the Mages Guild are supposed to lead to the temple's rear entrance.
The king sent you here to rescue the hostages, didn't he? Of course he did. That's why they recruited heroes, after all, am I right?\n\nListen, I have a plan. It's brilliant! Want to hear it?
We'll be fine, thanks to you. But you need to save Solgra. \n\nTrinimac preserve us, but this temple, this city … we need her!
One of the priests finally managed to open the temple doors.\n\nIt appears that you had the situation mostly well in hand, from what I can see.

That was the last of the fanatics. Your help in this matter is appreciated, but it felt good to run a few through myself.\n\nForge-Mother Alga waits for you outside. She would confer with you about all that happened here today.
Only Chief Bazrag would be this bold!\n\nThe stubborn fool! His actions will no doubt lead to war!

The others went on ahead to the city, in case you're wondering.\n\nI, um, felt kind of responsible for sending you into harm's way, so I waited around to make sure you were all right. And here you are! Right as rain!
Glad you happened along and helped us out. Now if I could just get that ringing out of my head ….
How can my heart hurt so much for someone I never knew?
Please. You've proven my imperfection.\n\nClose the pressure valve. End my suffering.
<The body of <<1>> remains undisturbed.>

Don't you worry about me. I can take care of myself, no matter what my shield-wives think. Besides, you'll kill everything on your way out. I've seen how you fight!\n\nProbably won't be anything left for me by the time you get done out there.
<Nashruth is dead.>
You stand before Malacath, Daedric Prince of Vengeance. Mortals often gawk and grovel. You do not.

You will recognize Kroma when you see her. She is truly favored by Malacath and difficult to miss. She will see that the scroll is safely hidden in a new location. \n\nThe sooner you deliver the scroll, the sooner the danger will pass.

I suggest you start your search in the inn. Gold and dark dealings often go hand in hand with drinking and celebrating.\n\nDon't disappoint me. I hate putting my trust in outsiders. Do everyone a favor and prove me wrong.
<<1>> named you blood-kin, and you did bring her back from <<2>> with a fabled relic of our people.\n\nBut don't get any ideas.
You have done a great service for Malacath and his followers, outsider. Know that the Agra Crun will remember your actions.\n\nNow, go. And may your next battle be glorious.

The caravan should have just entered Wrothgar territory. I can take you as far as the entry gates, but you'll have to make it from there on your own.\n\nThis is important. If those supplies don't reach the city, the smaller clans don't stand a chance.
Even though I'm sad, at least now I know a little about my Khajiit family.
I think we can make it back to the clan now. Thanks for your help.

Do whatever it takes. The chiefs must attend the moot. I trust you won't fail me. When this is over, Wrothgar will finally be forged into a united kingdom!\n\nMeet me at my cornerclub after you finish. All this planning has given me a powerful thirst.
Your task is vital, outsider. If you bungle this mission, you will not only disappoint King Kurog. You will have to answer to me.
Don't mind Razbela. She really does love our beloved, but she takes her role as the king's protector very seriously.\n\nJust do your best and I'm sure everything will turn out all right in the end.

All of the chiefs, united under my banner. It will be a glorious day!\n\nToo bad that traitor Bazrag won't be here to see it. He vanished right after the attack on the temple and hasn't been seen since.

Captain Caudex has already gone ahead with his soldiers to prepare defenses for the Cathedral.\n\nWhen you're ready, we should follow them. It's not exactly close and this ritual is going to take a while.

Seriously, Solgra wants to keep this quiet. Said the situation was sensitive. She especially doesn't want the king to know. When I suggested asking the king for help, she insisted that that would only get more people killed. \n\nJust so you know.

Two things before you go. First, avoid bloodshed on your way into the stronghold. The captives won't be immediately harmed if the Vosh Rakh feel secure.\n\nSecond, I'm not sure which chief was taken. The message I received was purposefully vague.
We lost Durga, but it could've been worse. Orgotha pulled it together quick enough. I hope the hunt-wife doesn't give her too hard a time about all this.\n\nThanks for helping me out in there.
I wonder when they'll let us do this again? I like being part of a hunting party!

Go ahead. Climb down and do what you do best. I'm going to look around up here a little more. I'll catch up with you later.\n\nJust remember, you're looking for an Orc chief, so keep your eyes open down there.

Interesting use of a rope. Remarkably convenient, too. I'm surprised nobody tried that before.\n\nHmm, you're not a prisoner. I know everyone they tossed down here. And you're definitely not with the Vosh Rakh. All right, I give up. Who are you?

The Chamber of Scorn is defended by a mechanism that releases poison gas. We can deal with that, but the solution is rather complex. I employed the best engineers gold could buy, after all.\n\nI'll explain what we need to do once we get inside.
I … I can't believe we made it out of there. Thanks to you.
I'm getting too old for this kind of action.\n\nBut thank you for helping us. I just wish we could have saved Gahar as well.
So, just so you know, if we don't do this exactly right, we're both going to die. No pressure or anything, but I wanted you to know what we're dealing with here.
You there! Open this door. I have had enough of this place and these annoying zealots.
It's hard to find fresh water down here, so I had the lads build this thing. Not much to look at, but it beats straining dead rats out of your morning tea.

We made the right choice. My brother's annoyed that I broke his latest toy, but he'll forgive me—eventually.\n\nOf course, I might have to hit him a few times if he doesn't stop complaining, but such is the burden of being Raynor's sister.
Orcs, Redguards, and Bretons built this place. They buried their dead together.\n\nThey say a bond is formed on the battlefield, even among enemies. Perhaps both sides tired of death in the end.
What have you done! Kireth, I can't believe you destroyed my construct without a moment's hesitation!
Despite the blood spilled, the betrayal? Mortal enemies put aside their past to commemorate two great heroes.\n\nBut Honor's Rest was lost, along with their story. Hatred is harder to forget.
That wasn't so bad. We're almost out of here.\n\nI guess once we get outside, my fate will be in your hands. At least I won't be trapped in my own prison any more.

You saved my life, so I'll go along with this nonsense. For now. Just find Ulsha. She'll prove I had nothing to do with the attack on the temple.\n\nBut if this is a trick, there's nowhere in Oblivion where you'll be able to hide from my wrath.

Don't worry. Chief Bazrag gave us his word, so I'll get him to the high priestess. We'll sneak into Orsinium and no one will even know we're there.\n\nWhen you reach the city, come find me. There's something not right here and it's making me nervous.
I hope that job in Orsinium is still waiting for me. I won't feel better until I'm back in a kitchen and cooking good food for good people again.
I've had enough excitement for one hunt. As soon as I can get these worthless weaklings on their feet, we're heading back to our stronghold.\n\nI just hope we can avoid the Reachmen marauders.

I'm really looking forward to setting up our life in Orsinium. Once we're settled, I plan to learn all about my Orc heritage. Just don't expect me to become some clan chief's hearth-wife.\n\nI'm very happy with Raza and I don't care who knows it!

I don't think gold will ever satisfy <<1>>. When you lose someone you care that much about, it's like a hole in your heart.\n\nLike Scrabbler. What a good echatere … such an amazing crest. But he shouldn't have tried to headbutt a mammoth.
Doesn't matter who's chief. If we aren't prepared for the spring thaw, the echatere will drown beneath the snow.
My time here is at an end. Perhaps Morkul needs a good hunter.
<<1>> fled rather than pay for her crime. I hope she's eaten by wild durzog. It would serve her right.
We'll honor their memory—their sacrifice. Shinji, Baloth, and all the noble heroes who gave their lives here. They shall never be forgotten.\n\nAnd on my honor, neither shall King Joile's treachery.
I have a feeling that the Wood Elf isn't the only one around here who's been lied to.\n\nHurry back. I don't think we have a lot of time before the Vosh Rakh make their move.

The scouts will meet you near Paragon's Remembrance. The old ruin is reportedly an ancient temple to Trinimac, which is why we think the Vosh Rakh have taken up residence there.\n\nFind out what they're planning. The city's future may depend on it.

I'll head out as soon as it's safe. I know how to avoid the guard patrols.\n\nLet's determine what the Vosh Rakh are planning so we can stop them. Maybe that'll make me feel better about all the lies and deceit.
I don't like when people raise their voices. It makes me all queasy inside.
Eveli asked for our help, but all they've done since we arrived is argue and shout at each other.\n\nIf I wanted to see such behavior, I would have remained with my kinhouse back in Auridon.
I won't say a word about you, I swear. Just promise me you'll make these Vosh Rakh maniacs pay.

<<1>> always wrote in a journal. <<2>> is certain his plans to frame her are within. This one saw a map inside his journal. To his bandit camp? Not far, this one can show you.\n\nPlease, find the journal and prove <<2>>'s innocence!
Feast, and drink your fill. We march at dawn. No Savage Son will die with an empty belly.
I shall miss this place. Each day a bed of burning coals, each night a plunge into cool water. It has tempered me, as … uh ….\n\nDon't write that one down. I'm still working out the metaphor.

"To the Occupants of Watcher's Hold,\n\n"Scholars reviewing Daggerfall's royal archives indicate a group of knights were long ago stationed at your location. They were mandated with preventing the Orcs from ever rebuilding Orsinium."
Go. Have you no sense of urgency?\n\nMy beloved's mood has already grown dark. Don't add to his anger as well, outsider.
Are you certain you don't want any?

The Wood Elf has been corrupted by that traitor, Bazrag. I will see them brought to justice. If you happen to find them before I do ….\n\nWell, don't disappoint me. The anger of a king can have deadly consequences, my friend.

King Bazrag's going to pay for any damages the inn sustained when the Orsimer soldier barged in. Even going to give us a break on our taxes for the help we provided.\n\nMaybe things didn't turn out so bad after all.
<Something very powerful snapped the neck of King Emeric's <<z:1>>, then gnawed upon his legs.>\n\n<You spot a messenger's ring proving the bearer's station.>
You found her! You found my Shalda and the others! Oh, thank you. Thank you so much.
The long hours are what get to you. Days like this, you find yourself wishing for a prison break to liven things up.
The mud of sorrow swirls around my ankles and threatens to drag me down.\n\nMy scales are dry with grief for our fallen friend. May the Egg welcome Talviah back into its impregnable shell.

Eveli thinks that our best chance of getting into the ruins undetected is to disguise ourselves as high-ranking members of the Vosh Rakh, and I concur.\n\nIf you check out the group that went west, we'll search in the other direction.
Does this look like a general store? That's my stuff you stole, I'll have you know.\n\nLousy thief.
You stand among the holy words of Trinimac.\n\nRead the scrolls carefully and choose a blessing to help you in the coming trial.
Trinimac's blessing is upon you.\n\nNow, hurry. How fast you complete the trial will determine your level of success. And that is all I have to say on that subject.
Listen well, for I do not like to repeat myself.\n\nTo unlock the door, you need to activate the four switches. The Vosh Rakh inside will try to stop you. You will be timed.

My fellow aficionado of tankards—have you tried the shandy? Its bouquet is like tying yourself naked to a log, hurling yourself from a cliffside, and bouncing through a field of nettles.\n\nMost people think that's a warning. Most people are idiots.
Check with my friend Kalina in the Mages Guild if you need any help figuring out what that letter means.\n\nShe loves that type of stuff.

Perhaps if you looked at the message in a different way, you might discover a pattern of sorts.\n\nIf that doesn't work, you can always visit the outlaw's den. I'm certain that someone down there could help you. Just don't mention I sent you.

Listen, this one is completely innocent. To Orcs, all Khajiit look the same, yes? And I wasn't in the city earlier today. I was especially nowhere near the marketplace.\n\nThis one is not the one you are looking for.
Hmm. The surreality didn't affect you at all. \n\nHave you met Uncle Sheo? That would explain it!
This place is as scary as it is impressive. I suppose we need to get back in there.\n\nYou go first.

Well done, outsider. No. I should say, well done, soldier of Trinimac! You demonstrate unwavering faith and devotion by spilling the blood of a friend in the Warrior God's name.\n\nWelcome to the true path.

I'll stay here and ward the doors so the cultists don't follow you.\n\nGo find the others and tell them about the danger facing the moot. Anyone could be a Vosh Rakh, which is going to make it hard to spot them before they strike. Go! I'll be fine.
Tell me the news that was so important that Talviah had to die. I want to get out of this place as soon as I can.
Thank you for all you've done. We'll need to open another wing before we even think about expanding our collection!\n\nHmm. I wonder if the king would consider it ….
So, I should probably say something about the Lost Barrow, but I really don't remember much about it.

I hope you know what you're doing. Because if you cause any more problems, they're going to run my father and I right out of town.\n\nOf course, if you can set things straight, well, the drinks are on me.
The Rat was entertained! Oh, most entertained. The Daedra … not so much. No, they weren't entertained at all.

Thanks to the timely arrival of the Wood Elf, we were ready for those Vosh Rakh bastards. You should have seen their expressions when we started cutting them down to size. It was glorious!\n\nSo, are there more of these tuskless wonders out there?
There you are! You missed all the fun.
When I get to Orsinium, I'm going to find a strong drink and a hot meal. And I might just skip the meal.
What are you doing up here? Go place the kindlepitch. Honestly, these cultists were not eager to give the place up. I'm sure more are on the way. \n\nSo, yes … urgency.
<Owayine has succumbed to his wounds.>
Ah, outsider. You never cease to surprise me.\n\nI suppose your recent adventures were somewhat trying. Of course, sticking your tusks where they don't belong usually leads to trouble, doesn't it?

My beloved and the forge-mother, everything they do is for the greater good of the Orsimer people. A few lives lost today will save countless thousands tomorrow.\n\nNow go. And I hope we never have to meet as enemies.
We cannot let Kurog get away with this.\n\nWhether his vision for the Orsimer is right or not, there has to be a way to get there that doesn't require the deaths of all the chiefs.
No matter what, you need to get to Solgra before Kurog's soldiers do. She might be our only way to get inside the moot.
Bazrag says he has a plan.
Trinimac has already smiled upon you. May his blessing serve you well in all your adventures!
Eveli saved me. I … I won't forget that.
Sleeping now. Shhh.
Her death was quick, if that makes you feel any better.\n\nWhat in Malacath's name happened out there?
I don't know what's going on, but it probably has something to do with that overly cheerful Wood Elf.\n\nI'm sure Solgra will clear up the situation in no time.
Yes, I was <<1>>'s forge-wife. No, I'm not interested in "continuing the tradition."\n\nI might try Morkul. They need good smiths.
Not sure why you're waiting around this old tomb. Wasn't taking my friend's skull enough?\n\nI built Orsinium with my own two hands. I don't know how haunting works, but I'll figure it out.
Ah, another of the city's benefactors! Thank you so much for your kind contribution. I am sorry to trouble you once again, but ….
I'd like my pendant now, if you don't mind.
I'll return to my tribe. The hagravens will sense their search is hopeless.\n\nPerhaps we can finally go home.
Just hand over the pendant and we can both get on with our lives.
I saw you talking to Youss and Azeeda. He's a nice fellow, but she's a sly one. Not to gossip, but she was flirting with him like we were in a tavern in Shornhelm!
The Imperial City is finally within our grasp! Are you prepared to do your part?
So that's it. We did it. Wait, did I just incinerate thirty some-odd Daedra?
Walk with Malacath's vengeance in your step. May your enemies crumble in your wake.
Speak to General Nesh-Tan. She'll tell you everything you need to know. Good luck.
Speak to General Nesh-Tan. She'll tell you everything you need to know. Good luck.
The city is ripe for conquest. The time has come to claim it.
So? Have you come to a decision on whether you want to help me?
Be careful down there. No telling what else the Daedra are burning. We can't afford to have you added to the pile.

What are you still doing here? Get to the Temple of the One and rescue Egnatius. I have work to do.\n\nI hope that a few headless Dremora will be distraction enough …. Don't have time for anything really sensational.
I'll catch up. I've got to scavenge what I can before I head back. Food especially. We're all a bit tired of smoked rat and boot-leather soup.
You're back! I had faith in your abilities, unlike my superiors. They were ready to either take credit for my idea or disavow your death.\n\nI take it you placed the geodes?
Malacath's ferocity already flows through your veins. May his blessing bring victory in every battle!
Fine work. They're confused and malnourished, but I'll get them out in one piece. You have my thanks.
I'll be off as soon as I can. I'm afraid these old legs aren't what they used to be.

Ah! It's good to see you again. That business in the Cathedral … it makes for quite a story. Too bad we have to take it to the grave. \n\nFeel free to stay here as long as you like. We can always use the help.
Echatere cheese, Lum's ale, a love poem … I can't wait to see what Ambassador Rigurt does with all these … amorous ingredients!
Grandfather's helm! Took it from that ogre's hands, huh?
They say the young think themselves immortal, but I never did. Until now. That's funny, isn't it?
So you've discovered our dark secret. Be glad you are not among us. It is an unnatural burden—one that I carry with great anxiety.
So you've discovered the truth. Good for you.
So Captain Caudex finally shared our secret? I must admit, keeping it to myself was difficult. It's so strange. So exciting!
I'm glad Anatolius shared our secret. He wouldn't admit it, but it weighs on him. I hope you can convince him it's not a bad thing.
What?
I need a few moments to remember the Kurog I once called "Blade-Brother." To wash away thoughts of the chief-slayer and his hagraven of a mother.\n\nWe'll talk more back at the keep.

On your way back, after you've delivered the letters, stop by the King's Cornerclub. Speak to the barkeep and get a bottle of Kurog's favorite ale.\n\nIt's foul stuff, but he loved it. We'll use it to drink to his memory at the service.
When I sent you to find the Captain, I thought you'd shore up some holes in the structure—maybe take down a Daedra or two. I didn't expect you to hold the doors! Good on you, friend!
Tell the Drake I'll follow up with her again soon, if I can. And make sure she gets that key.
If you see him, please tell him how angry I am. Or maybe "disappointed" is better. Just … whatever. You know what I mean. Use your imagination.
You do appear quite capable. However, I will reserve judgment until I've seen how you perform in the arena.
You've returned, at last. Forgive me. I am old—I worry.\n\nIs it done? Is our consecrated oil safe?
Bring that book back to the Drake, and give her my regards. She'll probably have a better idea of what to do with it than I do.\n\nDon't worry about me, I can find my way out from here. I hope.
So? Have you come to a decision on whether you want to help me?
You're leaving, too? I can't blame you. I really can't stay around here much longer. Not after everything that happened.

I know I have you to thank that I lived to see this moment.\n\nEveli filled me in on some of the trials you underwent when investigating the Vosh Rakh base. There were tough decisions to be made, yet here we stand, alive and well.

I'm happy for my people, but I'm sad that we lost the temple. Malacath wins the day and Trinimac fades back into obscurity.\n\nNo! I won't let that happen! As long as I have the breath to speak, I'll spread the word of Trinimac! You'll see!

As soon as I finish this drink, it's back to the Summerset Isles for me. I have so many tales to tell my family.\n\nJust imagine, a scribe who helped crown a new Orc king. My sister will never believe it!
To Kurog's lifeless body, long may it rot!
This is all kind of bittersweet. But I have good ale, good food, and good friends to help me through this.\n\nI couldn't ask for anything more!
I wish my crew back in Daggerfall could see me now! Here I am, sharing food and drink with the king of the Orsimer!
So? Have you come to a decision on whether you want to help me?
Speak to General Nedras. He will tell you everything you need to know. Good luck, walker.
Speak to General Nedras. He'll tell you everything you need to know. Fortune favor you.
Speak to General Aklash. She will tell you everything you need to know. Tu'whacca watch over you.
Speak to General Aklash. She will tell you everything you need to know. Eight protect you.

Thank you for allowing me to attend the funeral. It was good to get to say goodbye to Kurog in my own way.\n\nBazrag said I could keep the cornerclub open. Even retain the current name. I just hope the new king stops in for drink every once in awhile.
You've done everything I could ever have asked of you, my friend, but your service has come to an end.\n\nThe king of the Orsimer thanks you for your help and orders you to get on with your life.
You return! <<1>> and I started toward Orsinium, but we hoped you'd find us on the road.\n\nWere you successful? Have you changed our ill-fate to good fortune?
You came to meet us, just as you promised! I'm happy to see you safe, but it pains me to see you are alone.\n\nWhatever news you bring, give it to <<1>> first. He deserves that much, at least.
I pray you were able to recover something.

My mentor said he could teach me nothing except that "art is a journey." Each attempt an experience, regardless of the result, and that experience can often be art itself.\n\nLet's just … let's both agree that's what this is.
Well this place is homey if, you know … you're a half-starved skeever. You finished causing a ruckus up in the districts?
You made it! You do fine work. I can hear those Ogrim howling from here.

The exile was a Dragon priest? Well, that explains everything! And you killed him?\n\nAs long as you're sure he won't be causing us anymore trouble … but wasn't he dead before you killed him? I just hope he stays that way this time!

This is the Winterborn's final stand. We destroy the briarhearts while Kurog deals with their warlord, Ice-Heart.\n\nIf we succeed, Kurog will have ended a threat that has plagued us for far too long. Maybe then I'll consider accepting him as our king.

Once I've finished disposing of this body, I'll make for the crematorium. It's probably full of cultists. I'll try to thin the herd before you arrive.\n\nBy that I mean I'm going to kill them all, in case that wasn't clear.

I'm glad I ran into you. Maybe you're just the bit of good luck we need to salvage something from this terrible situation.\n\nThe camp is near the shore. You can still see what's left of our fleet from that location.
I'll head back to the camp. I'm liable to freeze to death out here—or worse. If I'm not on the deck of a ship, I'm like a fish out of water.
Clear us a path to the towers and we'll take care of the rest. I promise we'll get the Elf into position safely.\n\nWhether or not she can hit the target, well, that's a whole other question.
It's a wonder any of us survived that storm. It was unnatural, I tell you. Unnatural!
You have sided with the Orc pigs, which makes you our enemy. But why are you helping those animals?\n\nThat is the question you should ask yourself as the Winterborn cut you down.
You go that way and I'll go this way. The alchemist has to be around here somewhere!\n\nAs long as he's got his alchemy bag and that moss, everything will turn out fine.
Don't just stand there and watch me roast! Do something!
Do you have a moment? My father is General Velarius. He … he's missing.
It's no use. None of you people will listen. Whatever the Daedra plot, the Imperial Prison is key.

Pay no attention to the Shrew of Taneth. She'll say the Tel Var stones are "key to locking away the Daedra."\n\nWhy not ask the good Lady Cinnabar how much she plans to charge for each key? More than her horrid books, I'd wager.

Phrastus is wrong about the Tel Var stones. "Don't look at them or they'll ignite … everything is dangerous." No surprise, if you've ever read his … I suppose you can call them books.\n\nIf they're a risk, we should study them to learn why.
Ah, it's good to see you again. I can scarcely believe we survived, let alone succeeded. The Eight have been kind, to you and I at least.

What are you doing here? I thought you were busy helping those beleaguered Imperials in the Nobles District. You should get back to it. They might prove useful.\n\nCome back later—I might have something for you.
Exile? That's harsh! But I guess that you and Forge-Wife Kharza know best.

Master Dren went into the old barrow and told us to wait here. There're probably spiders in there. There're always spiders crawling around the tombs back in Skyrim.\n\nDon't tell Berrice, but I'm kind of afraid of spiders.
Make sure to check in with Sonolia once you've dealt with those beasts. She'll want to know that her clients have been freed.
Ah, there's my favorite werewolf slayer. Welcome back!\n\nSo, how about it? Do you have my pelts?
I'm here on behalf of the king. What are you doing here?\n\nActually, I don't care. Stay out of my way and we're good.
They called my brother the Wild Boar. No king ever tamed him, and he fought for his own reasons. \n\nBut he fought here. For me … for all Orsinium. His sacrifice shouldn't be forgotten.
It is a true honor to meet the Blademaster and his disciples. I hope to visit the Arena, one day. My lord promised me leave … as soon as the siege ends.
I admit I liked the Elf well enough, but your suggestion makes sense. There's no place at Graystone Quarry for a High Elf and his Dwarf constructs.
Razasha went that way, toward those ruins over there.\n\nMe? I'm going the other way. Try to stick to the main road and find cover if I see anyone suspicious. Best of luck to you, stranger.

You told the forge-wife to exile Neramo? Why would you suggest such a thing? He's leaving just when I was starting to like him! What am I going to do now?\n\nWait a moment! You! You're interesting and will probably upset my mother. We should talk ….
You there, we need help. Our caravan … they came out of nowhere and attacked us!\n\nThe Orcs … they need those supplies.
Back from the Sanctum, eh? I hope you gave that grave-raiding skeever-stain a sound beating.\n\nThe company has already settled accounts with Thazeg. You should talk to him if you want your cut.
Ah, back again! I trust your mission was a success? I'm anxious to see these eggs.

Once I get back to my workshop, I'm certain I'll be able to use this data to overcome my earlier setbacks. That should convince Kireth I was right to not give up, yes? Yes!\n\nThis time I'll have a truly stable energy exchange … and much less fire.
That old bauble that you found isn't worth hauling around. Meram will take it off your hands. And for a good price, too!

<The book contains a ritual which imbues Molag Bal's agents with great power. Speaking the following words should bolster the Daedric Prince's champions with his ire.>\n\n"God of Schemes, inflict your brutality upon us."

There aren't a lot of people with the patience to train a durzog, or the strength to survive the experience. But there's something about you …. If you ever get tired of wandering around stabbing things, you might give it a try.

Even now, collections for a new <<1>> have begun. When we've raised the gold, I will ask <<2>> to commission another assault on Thukhozod's Sanctum. There are many more souls there that struggle for freedom.\n\nI hope you are available.

I saw what you did out there. Thanks for helping the clan Orcs.\n\nThe ones in here? I think it's too late to help them. Ice-Heart … he froze them solid. The bastard's got magic the likes of which I've never seen.
Thanks for making sure at least some of the Orc peasants made it out of there safely.\n\nMaybe I'll see you in Orsinium? I can't imagine that an Orc city is that big.

Merchant District's on the city's south side. If you need to buy or sell supplies, there's at least a few honest traders there.\n\nAnd Gulug. You'll find him. Or at least smell him. Like a dead horker, you'll see.
This one would ask you to leave us be. You can plainly see that we aren't yet ready to conduct business.\n\nCome back later. Much later.
What? I paid for the bath. Might as well enjoy it for as long as I can.\n\nNow if you don't mind, I'm going to soak.
These … these laborers eat like locusts. Never seen the like. I have no doubt I'll need your services again soon.
Nothing pleases me more than the return of my text. To think, the world could have been deprived of this brilliant dissertation—by ogres, no less! You've done all of Tamriel a tremendous service.

The wild sighs in relief. This is good, but I sense it is only a temporary respite. Even now, a corruption lurks on the horizon. We must stay vigilant.\n\nI'll stay here a while longer. With this bread. Can't sense a blight on an empty stomach!
Wrothgar's people are safe from the Worm Cult, for now. But the threat will return—it always does. When it does, I am certain that you will rise to defeat it.
With that mechanical beast dead, perhaps Birkhu should dust off the cobwebs and start exploring again!\n\nThen again, the alcohol in this place is very, very good. Perhaps one more drink ….

The caravans have started running again, thank the Eight. With any luck, the Riekr will go back to banging rocks together and sniffing each others' arses. Stay prepared, though. I'm afraid they may be too stupid to keep away for long.
Thank you for what you were able to do, but I need time to pray for our fallen brothers and sisters.

If you find yourself in need of assistance on any of your secret missions for the king, feel free to seek me out.\n\nI'd much prefer to do something—anything—other than carrying messages for the Orcs. I could have stayed home for that.

Good luck with whatever the king wants you to deal with this time.\n\nMe? I think I'm going to go have a soak in the bath house. Sounds like a perfect diversion—at least until they find something worthy for one of my obvious skills and talents.
Have you had a chance to inspect the Morkul forge yet? I've seen more than a few masterpieces drawn from those coals. The Guild could use more weapons like that.

I'll use what resources I have to investigate the attack Orsinium's temple. As for our stronghold, that's a battle for another day. But I swear before the Furious One, Fharun shall be ours again. You can count on that!\n\nNow, where is Chief Bazrag?
Orsinium will ring with the sound of our forge-hammer! We'll show the other clans what a true smith can fashion.

West. That's where all the noise came from.\n\nNot sure what happened to the cultists, but it probably won't be pretty. Still, it's one of our best chances for finding a disguise. We'll look around, too, and meet you inside the ruins.

Looks like you found an amulet, too. But tell me, was I right? Did the echateres get all frolicsome on those cultists?\n\nWait a moment. Your amulet's cracked. You weren't supposed to break it, you know.

Suddenly my mouth is dry, my hands are sweating. Is this how you feel every time you go on an adventure?\n\nWe'll be fine, though. What could go wrong? We're just sneaking into a private meeting of the cult's elite. Gods, what did Eveli talk me into?
Too much attention right now. Come back later.
Sorry, this establishment is closed. Please return later.
Don't be a stranger! Come on back and have a relaxing soak in the baths sometime.\n\nIt would do you good. Nothing washes away the stress of the day like a warm bath!
Don't be alarmed. It's just me. I find this illusion spell to be quite … liberating.\n\nEveli has a plan. You should talk to her before we head out.

Let's continue this fascinating discussion in the dining hall downstairs. I'll meet you there after I make apologies to my guests.\n\nAnd you better have proof to substantiate these wild claims or I might just have you flayed for ruining my good mood.
Hey! You're the one who settled that business out on the coast? With the shipwreck? What a mess that was!
The guild asked me to research Orc clans. I thought the assignment would take me a week.\n\nThat was three years ago.
Have you heard the news? A great hero retrieved the sacred words of Malacath from Fharun Stronghold. Showed those Vosh Rakh a thing or two, I wager!

What in Trinimac's name is going on? Why did Kurog send soldiers after us?\n\nThey acted like we'd done something horrible. I didn't want to worry Eveli, but I was frightened for our lives! I'm just glad you arrived when you did.
Good luck, my friend.\n\nI'll remain here to protect the priests, as Chief Bazrag requested. I'll look forward to hearing how you beat the mad king when you return.
Well, that was quite unexpected.
Everything you see is, in large part, thanks to your efforts! And with a new king on the throne, the future of Orsinium looks bright and gleaming.\n\nWe're going to miss you when you're gone.
They killed the king. He was our people's true hope. Curses be to Malacath.
Finally, Kurog the bastard is dead! Malacath once again fills the hearts of the Orcish people.
You'd think that temple priests would be neater. These manuscripts are all over the place.\n\nStart searching. We've got to find a way into the tunnels.
An honest-to-goodness secret passage.\n\nIf I wasn't terrified, this would be kind of exciting.
I've never been to the city before, but I must say, I'm impressed. I could get used to living in a big, stone keep like this.\n\nHmm, maybe I should declare myself as king!
What were you and Kurog discussing over there? Anything important?\n\nNo, don't tell me. I really don't care. I just want to get this over with so I can get back to my own stronghold.
You have a dark look about you. Kurog's words will do that if you stand still long enough to listen to his nonsense.\n\nDon't worry. This will all be over soon enough, I expect.
You and the king seemed to have a rather serious discussion.\n\nI certainly hope that everything is all right. I'm really looking forward to hearing what Kurog has to say when the moot begins.
Enough talk! The time has come for action!\n\nGo check on Solgra while I see what I can do about rallying some aid from my remaining contacts.
Thanks to you, the Orsimer have a new king, and he's a good king. I owe you for helping my husband, outsider. You'll always have a friend in Orsinium, should you ever need one.
Now this is more like it.\n\nNo harpies. No giant catapults slamming into walls. Just a few peaceful drinks with good friends. This is how it should have been from the moment I got here.
I guess I've got one more battle in me. For Solgra, right?\n\nDamn, I hate how this turned out!
Wait—you left the armlet up there? Up on that damn mountain? That doesn't mean we have to go back up there to get it, does it?
So Torug's Armlet remains on the mountain, eh? Good. Gives me an excuse to head back up there. This damn hill won't beat me twice!

Oh friend! It's so good to see you!\n\nAre you surprised? I told you I was going to find my fortune in the big city. And look! Khajiit clothes! Although, I don't think they had Wrothgar's weather in mind when they designed these.

Dwemer constructs are surprisingly loyal and affectionate, considering that they are machines and all.\n\nWe've more than doubled the efficiency of the quarry already. And worker safety is no longer an issue. I assume the chief will be quite pleased.
These Orcs have a great deal to teach us. The Mages Guild would be foolish to ignore them.\n\nMy advice is this—be polite. The Morkul clan can be … mercurial.
I only need the basic repair kit, but the one on the cart says it's "grand." That must be a lot better.\n\nRight?
I'll punch anything. Even an echatere. Stupid snow rats ….
I watch the horses more closely than I watch my children.
I'll speak with <<1>> when I'm damned well ready.\n\nBest to let her stew on what I've done.
You are a Silencer now, an honored member of our family. I expect you to fill the Dread Father's Void with many, many souls.\n\nGo forth, Silencer, and may your blade never lose its edge.

There goes Josseline, off to who knows where to do who knows what until I have to go and pull her hair out of the fire again.\n\nI could use a drink. A strong drink. Why don't you meet me in Anvil and we'll drink to our success.
Head to the upper levels and search for her villa. It's a bit of a maze, but look for a big garden.\n\nAnd watch for traps. <<1>> is … enthusiastic about her privacy.
Akatosh bless you, outsider. What brings you to our humble town?
Has the light of Akatosh touched you today, friend? If not, let me tell you about the Society of the Dragon.
Do not despair! Akatosh watches over us, always. Lift your weary head and give praise.
May Akatosh and the Divines smile upon you this day and all the days to come! If you're interested, I can tell you all about the Society of the Dragon.
Lord Akatosh, the Dragon God of Time, brings fire in the cold of night and light in the depths of darkness. There's room for you in the Society of the Dragon. All you have to do is say the word.
Proceed to the Chamber of Penance, heretic, or I'll cut you down where you stand. The Grand Chanter doesn't like to be kept waiting. And remember, I'll be right behind you.
Whoa that's a lot of treasure! That's magnificent!

Do you have the ledger? Was it all for naught? Oh, there is so much naught on your face! My heart shrinks in despair.\n\nBut … I am quite bad at reading faces. And in this place, my nose doesn't help. So? Does the stink of victory waft about you?
You're working for my sister, right? How did you find me? No, never mind. Just tell me if you're here to talk or to kill me.
I keep thinking about what you found. If someone stole <<1>>'s dowry, it wasn't the Thieves Guild.\n\nBut we certainly took the fall for it.
<<1>> assured me she would not venture beyond the outskirts of <<2>>. Assured me!\n\nOh, my. With all certainty, she is already captured.
I heard that the pirates demanded a large ransom for Anais. Her family hesitates, but I'm sure they'll turn over the gold before another day goes by. This lesson couldn't have gone any better!
Do recall my humble establishment should you seek to be truly unforgettable.
If you're done exploring the Sanctuary, I heard that Elam wants to see you. Probably has a contract waiting just for you.\n\nGood luck, Initiate!
It'll be good to have the wind in my fur and sea air in my nose again. I can't wait to set sail and put Anvil behind me.
Qamar's been drinking an awful lot of late, but I can't tell if he's celebrating or drowning his sorrows.
You got what you wanted, right? So leave us to finish our game in peace.
Just a few more throws and I'll be even.
People in Abah's Landing say terrible things about the Iron Wheel, but <<1>> remembers my name. He even asks after my children. A gentleman, that one.
The visions don't lie. The fumes confirmed my worst fears. Lyra abandoned the Dark Brotherhood and became the Black Dragon. She betrayed us all.

Finally, we start making some real moves. I'm glad I got to be there to see that.\n\nI say we kill Count Aquilarios as well, but Astara seems to think we need him to find the Black Dragon. He'd better deliver. I still owe her for Cimbar.
"What is the fate of the lawbreaker?"

I hope I can restrain myself from doing too good a job. If I'm not careful, I'll be running the business before three shakes of a kwama's antennas. And then how could we leave for Hammerfell in good conscience?\n\nOh, the dilemmas of a superior mind.

Now that we have jobs, it won't be long until we have enough gold to pay for passage to Sentinel!\n\nUnless Raynor does something that tosses water on the cooking fire, that is. He has a terrible habit of letting his big brain get us into trouble.
I told you I'd hire the crazy Dark Elf. Now go away and let me get back to work.
You make sure the Dark Elf shows up and I'll handle getting drunk arses in the seats to hear her sing. I'll even make that worthless bard come out and clap—strained finger be damned!
With what you paid me, I'll be able to pull out every one of Kireth's misaligned planks, hire a real carpenter to plug the holes, and still make a small profit. So, bottoms up!
This one has not forgotten his promise. Or your generous payment. Raynor may poke as many holes in the old nets as he wishes. This one will buy new nets in the very near future!

If that Dark Elf is as good as you say when it comes to untangling our profit and loss ledgers, I'll give him a raise. And then I'll take him out to celebrate. I can't wait to see how well he handles his mead!
When the lad's ready, send him to see me. I'll expect that forge to be working better by the end of his shift.

You have returned—all of you! Truly, I thought I had sent you into the maw of a dragon frog.\n\nI've heard they can grow as large as a Breton sailing ship. But you must take these things with a pinch of sugar.
We did it, partner! That was exhilarating.\n\nBeyond the part where I thought the Iron Wheel was going to cut me in half.
<<1>> wasn't lying. I figured out all of his tells long ago.\n\nHe knows where they have <<2>>, which means the acting guildmaster has a decision to make about a lockpick.
Nothing went how I'd hoped, but I'm glad you were along for the journey … partner.
This feels like old times.\n\nThe good times, before we realized our old guildmaster would most certainly betray us.
<<1>> said he'd help with invitations. Meet him at his shop, down by the harbor.
I do not often rejoice in the troubles of others. But those two … they are "barnacles on a horker's bow locks," as the sailors say.\n\nSuch an expressive profession.
I'll meet you at <<c:1>>. Or not. I don't think I'll risk my life on <<2>>'s behalf.

Such an audacious display. I look forward to our future dealings.\n\nI will smooth things with the Iron Wheel. <<1>> is their only prisoner to stand trial, now. A shame Taneth's ire shall fall entirely upon my former fiance.
Well? Is there honor among thieves, or will you prove <<1>> wrong?
Always a pleasant journey to Abah's Landing. Head to our <<1>>—the guildmaster awaits.\n\nYour partner and I will be along when she's less expulsive.
It's good to be back. I used to hate this place, when we first moved in. It's really grown on me.

We must move quickly, yes? The dro-m'Athra have a powerful ally in the temple's abbot, Kulan-dro. He is bent past breaking, but he knows this place better than any cat alive. There will be no stopping him if we do not act soon.
The thief from … <<1>>, wasn't it? Why are you here?
As a merchant, the most I can lose is my business. But your guild has lost so much more than that. I am truly sorry.
Head to the Diamond Thimble. You need a change of clothes.
We accomplished what <<1>> wanted, but now she's at the mercy of the Iron Wheel.\n\nI don't know if it was worth it.
<<1>> playing the hero again? I always told her she'd get herself caught or killed.\n\nI won't lose any sleep over this.

Just so we're clear, an "acting guildmaster" has no real power. But it makes you sound important, so we may as well call you that.\n\nAlso, you get the blame if anything goes wrong. You know how it is.

You do good work, friend. If I didn't know any better, I'd say that a true Shark's Tooth painted those sigils! I'm thrilled to see our mark back where it belongs!\n\nI've decided you can live. Only seems fair, what with your help and all.
Go with what speaks to you. The first choice is always the best one.
Years ago, I stole a handkerchief from this place. When I mentioned it to <<1>>, he said "it was better suited to the street urchin you once were."\n\nStill not sure if that's a compliment.
I'll return to <<c:1>> shortly. I just need a bit of time.
Ah, look at all the people here. Merchants, moneylenders, and their many hangers-on. See how they look at me … as their equal.\n\nIt is a wonderful gift you have given me, my friend.
I haven't dressed up like this since my academy.
I can smell the food from here. If they have a pie tent, I may abandon you. Fair warning.
You have that look again.
Please, do not tarry! You cannot miss the social event of the season … nay, the decade!
