A sad day when thieves wish to mete out justice on one of their own.\n\nIt never ends well, you know.
Why are we talking instead of running?
We need to keep moving.
We must hurry. We are no good to <<1>> if we share her cell.
We can't go back for her. We have to get out before they arrest us all.
Saroldo had a small portrait of <<1>>—made of wax, small enough to fit in his hand. Even there, you could see what a vibrant young woman she was.\n\nI fear my ill news took that from her.
Shouldn't you be mingling with the other guests?

I knew <<1>> kept trophies from his heists. I used to smooth it over with the guild—one of his eccentricities, I'd say.\n\nBecoming "<<2>>" hasn't altered his compulsion. He desecrated Danobia's remains—cut off her head. Now, we return the favor.
I think you impressed Shalug. She didn't mention killing you even once during dinner last night.
Bright Moons! Bakhum is ready to set sail when you are, walker.
I'm glad you were part of this. The choice wasn't easy, but it feels like we made the right one.
You should not linger here long, friend. Take this one's advice—you want no part of what is coming. Be smart like Bakhum and leave this business to the Twilight Cantors.
My cousin, <<1>>? Did I mention she's preparing for the wedding in <<2>>'s chambers?\n\nI still say tying herself to some jumped up merchant is a bad idea.
I shall hide, if I must. The Iron Wheel took Saroldo from me—I would sooner die than bring harm to his daughter.
I don't often receive visitors in my garden. Especially the uninvited ones.
This doesn't look good. Maybe the clerk knows what happened to <<1>>.
I need to sample the wine before I mix it in with the milk.\n\nPerhaps a few samples.
I'll wait by the camel. Best of luck inside.\n\nOh, and watch the floors. Deadly traps.
If anyone asks, we never met. Do the same for an Alliance war veteran, would you?

This makes no sense. If <<1>> stole the dowry, why didn't he return to the guild? Could he be injured, or perhaps trapped?\n\nReturn to Abah's Landing. I'll meet you at this "secret retreat" of his. We need to find answers.

People say, "this is not how I imagined my wedding to be." They tell amusing stories of what went wrong, trying to outdo each other's tales.\n\n"Calling the guards on wedding crashers" isn't one I've heard. Why shouldn't it be the story I tell?
<<1>> survived, somehow. He came here and took <<2>>'s dowry for himself. I don't want to believe it, but that's how it seems.\n\nUnless I'm missing something. Am I missing something?
<The camel stares at you.>
I'll meet you at <<c:1>>. I need to figure out what I'm going to tell the others.
<<1>> taught me how to be a thief. I knew him for over a decade. Trusted him.\n\nNot much else to say, is there?

I am glad to admit I was wrong about you. Your will is as strong as any hunter I have ever fought beside. Thank you for helping me defeat Zalar-do.\n\nAnd thank you for putting her victims out of their misery.
This one hears nothing. Sees nothing. This one only sweeps.
Nothing sharpens the claws like dispatching criminals and murderers! And we all survived, which makes the victory that much sweeter.
You'll get <<1>> back.
You have my word. Let me live and I'll never trouble anyone again. I'll go far away. Become a farmer. Just … just let me live!
Do you know how long I've been looking for you?
This one assures you that these goods have been acquired through only legitimate means.
You will buy goods from Khajiit, yes? Good. This one lives to trade.
I'm beginning to think that my memories only see one side of my life in this place.\n\nCome, let's go find that balcony.

And you … you're just as bad as Walks. What gives you the right to break into my home and take my belongings?\n\nI should call for the guard and teach you both a lesson. The Velmont family doesn't take kindly to thieves and traitors.
Find what you can. After that, meet <<1>> near the harbor. She has her own task and will no doubt need your assistance.
<<1>> shall no longer trouble the Thieves Guild.\n\nAnd I can focus on improving our fortunes, rather than dwelling on the past.
Find <<1>> when you're done. She's meeting with <<2>> at his shop.\n\nDid you know he had a shop? I wonder what he sells.
When you find what you need, get out and head back to <<c:1>>.\n\nDon't get caught—and if you do, bite off your tongue before their torture forces you to shriek my name. You'll be fine.
Just get this over with.
Greetings! If hunger has befallen you, perhaps a little sweetroll is the answer.

Don't know why we let <<1>> into <<c:2>>. Always bringing those tonic bottles with him, only you find out too late it's for fur-smoothing, not belly-soothing.\n\nBut my tonsils have never been silkier.
Don't think I've seen you around. Or I could've! I was quite drunk yesterday.\n\nHello again, for the first time.
I can feel the fractures sealing. You did it, didn't you? The tomb is once more secure?

I told you everything I know. I only agreed to deliver the letter because the Khajiit lady was very sweet and she offered me a lot of gold. Someone in the Observatory must know who she is.\n\nNow feel free to go and harass someone else and leave me be.
Seeing Narahni after all these years … I thought that part of me was long gone.
We have so much to talk about, but this one doesn't know where to start.\n\nMaybe she'd like to hear about the latest Investigator Vale book I read …?
If that's everything, I'd like to get back on my horse and return to Castle Kvatch. If I'm gone too long, I suspect Primate Artorius will go ahead and change all the locks.

I'm going to keep an eye on you, hero. I've got a feeling you're going to accomplish great things. Besides, I might need your help again. To complete a contract, maybe. Or for something a little more … personal.\n\nYes, I think I'd like that.
Maybe I will get used to it here. Walks-Softly says I will make new friends, better friends.\n\nBut I do miss Lady Anais.
According to the priest, if the great seal fails, the necromancers will be free to wander the countryside. And if that happens, we'll all be in trouble!
I mean it, don't disturb Narahni's rest. And the upstairs rooms are off-limits to the likes of you.
We are standing inside a treasure vault. A real, actual treasure vault.\n\nYes, yes … there's no actual treasure, but I can still say it, can't I?
<<1>> likes to soak in the city. Gathering information, he calls it. I think the only thing he's soaking in is cheap swill, but he gets the job done. He's expecting you.
We barely made it here alive, yet someone else slipped past the crypt's guardian?\n\nSomething's off.
Do you want to roll around in a big pile of coins? I feel the urge to roll around in a big pile of coins.\n\nNone are here, of course. But you can still smell them.
No better way to test your sartorial skills than to ride a camel while severely overdressed.\n\nIf the chafing is less than excruciating, you're a true master.
I guarantee <<1>> is no friend of the Iron Wheel. He's expecting you at the Diamond Thimble.\n\nAnd he'll be insufferable if you keep him waiting.
Any job you can walk away from is a good one.
I'm not used to this. I have the strangest urge to hug you right now.\n\nNaturally, I'll resist that impulse.
Tashmin has been returned to me. Velsa has been returned to me. My heart sings thanks to the moons above!
This one has so much to talk to mother about. Please, give us a few moments to ourselves.
Why are you still here? I thought you were going to rescue Tash?
Well, boss, it has been my pleasure to show you the ropes. There are always new opportunities arising in Abah's Landing, so I'll expect to see you again soon. I look forward to it!

I know these pirates. They'll ask for a ransom, receive their gold, and Anais will be home before the week's end. With any luck, that will be more than enough time to show her what the life of a slave is really like.\n\nI'll see you back at the Den.

You're really going to let him do this to me? Leave me here like some sort of servant for a gang of disgusting pirates?\n\nI won't be trapped here forever! I'll get away. And then I'll find you and make you pay for this. Oh, you're going to pay!
Glad you decided to join me. These pirates are definitely of the unfriendly persuasion.
Just leave. You're scaring away my dinner.

I feel that a great and terrible burden has been lifted from Abah's Landing, and I would dare to guess that you had something to do with that.\n\nFrom the bottom of my ever-full flagon, you have my thanks.
Was there more? No? Then be off, my barrister will send the usual payment to your guild.
The guildmaster is expecting you. Go on in.
My deepest regrets. My shelves can bear no more. Allow me time to make some room before you return.
This day is busy enough. Come back tomorrow, yes?
It was nice to get to know you, Assassin. And I know it was your pleasure to get to know me.\n\nBe careful in there.
The Moon-Bishops will be anxious to hear that the Lost Cats have been pushed back, but Adara'hai thinks they will have to wait. This one needs some moon-sugar tea and a very, very long bath.
I'll be back on my feet in no time, thanks to you.
The Black Dragon isn't here. I suppose she'll be back soon, if you want to wait.
Bask in the holiness of this sacred place and let your troubles fade away.

This is as good as one of those bawdy Pirate Empress stories! A mysterious warrior looking for a young Nord who was last seen talking intimately with a Chanter! Anvil will be shocked by the news.\n\nBut obviously no one will hear about it from me.
I wonder if I can get a priest to tell me how they keep the fires burning? I hope it's not one of those sacred secrets that they're always going on about.
Ah, now I've lost my train of thought. Well, since you've already interrupted the writing process, what can I do for you?

You're going after the Chanter? Excellent! If I didn't have to get Hilde back to the Sanctuary, I'd go with you. I'd love to give the Chanter a piece of my mind. And by that, I mean kill him.\n\nMake his pain last, Initiate, for a long, long time.
If you ever get tired of running around with that bunch, come back and see me. There's always a place for someone with your skills on my caravans.\n\nI'm just saying.
Please, I'm no threat to you. I simply watch the door!\n\nSix days before I take my pension. I want no trouble, you see?
I won't forget what you said. I won't ever abandon my family again.\n\nJust make sure Chanter Nemus pays for what he tried to do to me.
Away with you! I have cloth of gold to peruse.
Have I told you about my locket? It's the most beautiful locket I've ever owned. I'm going to give it to Falorah as a gift tonight. She'll remember me for this!
<<1>> is bringing me along! I shouldn't be this excited, but I can't help myself.\n\nSee you at the Diamond Thimble.
This plan is unwise. A bit dangerous. But it isn't entirely reckless.\n\nAs thieves, those are often the best plans we can have.
This is folly, all of it. But if I come along, perhaps half of us will survive our certain doom.\n\nI didn't think it was possible to think less of <<1>>, and here she finds a way.

I welcome your help. There is enough glory and adventure for everyone.\n\nJust keep your fins drawn tight. If you draw the Xit-Xaht's attention, I can strike from the shadows and help guide my tribe to safety. In heroic fashion, of course.

I'll stay behind and make sure none of the Cathedral guards get too curious about what we're doing back here. Besides, someone has to show Astara and the others the way inside once they arrive.\n\nSince I'm still recovering, I guess I'll volunteer.
When your time comes, I know Arkay will welcome you with open arms. Until then, stay safe, my friend.
When you're done with the job, don't come back to me. Find <<1>> in <<c:2>>. She can give you your reward.
I, ah, have something I should really go check on. If you'll excuse me.
I just hope the artifacts you recovered will be enough to convince our patrons to continue funding our troubled dig.
To what do I owe the pleasure of this unexpected visit? Can I assume that my little problem has been dealt with?
Find Mirabelle in Anvil Castle. The Count and I have business to discuss.\n\nYour business, Initiate, is murder. Best you get to it.
Well, that's done. I'm just glad I was here to be a part of it. I never did like that glorified, over-important pirate.\n\nNow be a dear and get back to the Sanctuary. Let Astara know what happened.
Akatosh take me, I did not see that coming! You've got a future in this bloody work, mark my words.
I am right behind you, friend. Na-Kesh will die at our hands. Try not to strike a killing blow before I arrive, all right?
Thank the Eight! I've been trying to annoy these clods so they'd check on my bonds. Then I could clobber them on the noggin and make my grand escape. \n\nNo need for heroics on my part, now.
Why are you still here? When you're done, find <<1>> in <<c:2>>. She'll reward you.
It's been a while since I've pulled a simple job. Maybe I'll go down to the harbor, see if anyone has laden pockets.\n\nSomething to warm up the blood, you know?
Of the two of us, I'd say you're looking … Sharper.\n\nHmm, <<1>> was right. Speaking a pun aloud has diminished me as a person.
Hello, partner. I'm happy to inform you I can pick a lock within fifteen seconds.\n\nAs long as nobody's watching.
You know, I think Zeira has some potential as a guildmaster—but don't tell her I said anything of the sort.
I am happy to be an honorary member of this august organization.\n\nThere aren't any dues to pay, are there? I don't pay dues. It's a religious thing.

Serving drinks isn't so bad. The pirates have been surprisingly polite and well-mannered. Well, except for that one who leered at me. But Anya gave her a look and she hasn't bothered me since.\n\nStill, I'll be glad when my shift ends and I get paid.

To think, one of the most brilliant minds in all of Tamriel and I'm reduced to mending nets that smell of sea water and old fish!\n\nI'll persevere, though, don't worry about that. I'll honor my commitment and earn the gold we need to sail to Sentinel.
I've never noticed how beautiful Abah's Landing actually is. Sitting here, watching the city … it reminds me how lucky I am.\n\nAs do you.
The Thieves Guild is restored. I grieve for lost friends and cohorts, but I know they would be pleased to see all of us succeed.
It appears that our adventure is at an end. I will admit, it did not go exactly as planned. But all true adventures include some deep bruises and frantic screaming, right? \n\nI am right, aren't I?
Please. I gave you a way to get into the castle. That's all I can do. My actions this day will haunt me for the rest of my life.\n\nNow leave me alone, please.
You again? You're really starting to chafe my armor. Get out of here before I do something you'll regret.
I don't want to know the details. Believe me, if there was another way ….\n\nJust make sure the Pirate Queen dies. The fate of the Gold Coast depends on it.
Is it time? Has the Dark Brotherhood finally noticed my impeccable work? I'm ready, dark one! I swear, in the name of—wait, I should let you talk first.
You can read the Litany of Blood, just as the Listener foretold.\n\nNow all that you need to do is figure out how to identify the targets described therein and kill them.
I hate fighting four-legged creatures! They're so … stompy.\n\nHilde and I will hold this position and point the others in the right direction as they arrive. Good luck, Assassin!

Did you really have to kill the wamasu? She was just defending her children.\n\nSorry, I—I should not complain. You've got a lot on your mind, what with the Primate and all. We'll wait here and make sure the way remains clear for the others.
Welcome back to Chef Donolon's famous traveling bakery barge! Were you able to gather the ingredients I need to make you your cake?
Are you still here? Don't you have a high-ranking religious leader to murder?
I come to investigate the sounds of battle and what do I find? You, standing over the bodies of our fallen foes.\n\nGood work, Assassin.
Pardon the interruption. I've been looking for you.
Do you make a habit of interrupting business transactions? We have nothing to discuss.
What have you got there? A book?
Hello hello, comrade! Good to see you!
<This Silver Dawn hunter died in a fierce battle.>
<Flowers were expertly and recently picked from this plant without damaging either the plant or the remaining blossoms.>
<This deer was killed while drinking from the pool. Whoever killed it was able to approach unnoticed and make its attack.>

I do not often express gratitude, but you have earned the words. I did not trust you when you first arrived. Honestly, I expected I would need to kill you before long. Instead, I embrace you as Sister.

Discover the link that connects these individuals and you'll find their murderer—hopefully while they're still alive.\n\nDo this for me and I promise you'll like the reward I'm offering. Gold isn't the only favor I'm willing to provide.
You're back. Have you figured out what I should do? Standing around out here in the open is begin to make me nervous.
Enough! I answered your questions and you had your say. Now let me enjoy a few more blessed moments of peace.\n\nThey may be my last, after all.
Well met, pilgrim. Have you come to pray?
Do you mind? I'm trying to enjoy a quiet moment with my wife.
Do you make a habit of accosting strangers at shrines of worship?
Oh, hello! Careful where you step. I just planted some seeds and I'd hate to have to start all over again.\n\nBut you didn't come over to hear me complain. What can I help you with today?
Wait. You two know each other?\n\nOh, this is so embarrassing.

My apprentice wasn't very good at pretending to be bait. She did hook you, though, so Raz supposes that's something.\n\nFinish your business and then we'll talk. Raz is sure we can come to a mutually beneficial arrangement.
You're going to just leave me here? You do know I've been targeted for death, right?\n\nI think this is a horrible plan. And I'm beginning to hate sweetrolls.

Raz has not been this excited in a long time. To think, soon I'll be able to close the book on a murderer who eluded me for years and years.\n\nMeet me outside when you're ready and we'll start tracking.
The only house that fits all of the clues sits in the southeast part of town, far from the main road.\n\nIt would make an excellent hiding spot for a murderer who hands out delicious sweetrolls.
I've not forgotten the favor you've done. I trust our business is concluded and you will allow me to rule the Gold Coast as it should be ruled—free of Fortunata's grasping talons.

Raz has ears as sharp as a dire wolf. This one heard everything you said.\n\nThe Queen would probably frown upon working with the likes of Naryu Virian, but Raz says "the more the merrier." At least until we catch the Sweetroll Killer.

I just want to find out who threatened me, kill them, and go home. Besides, they serve dreadful wine.\n\nThe cat and I need to have a private conversation. Set some ground rules so we don't kill each other. Then we'll meet you in Anvil.

Go on and head over to the Gold Coast Trading Company. Find out what Reman hasn't told us about the Sweetroll Killer. We'll meet you at Engra's Hostel when you're done.\n\nI swear, I'll be plucking cat fur off my leathers for a month after this job.

Raz will work with the lovely Naryu. Make sure the remaining targets get to the hostel safely.\n\nMeanwhile, you go interrogate Reman. Make him talk. Use whatever methods you deem necessary. Just don't tell Raz what they are, yes?

You going after Reman? Good! He's worse than a guar in heat!\n\nTried to get fresh with me when he came to ask about the sweetroll I received. Bet he walked with a limp for a week after I kicked him right where it hurts!
Now I know what my contracts must feel like, having a constant target floating above their heads.\n\nI heard what you told Raz. Let's get to that farm and put an end to the Sweetroll Killer.

This is your fault. I never should have hired you. What was I thinking?\n\nBecause of you, the killer decided that I was a threat. Sent my own sweetroll with a message inside. Then she cut me with her poisoned blade. Now I'm dying. Because of you.

We will meet you at the farmhouse south of town. That is where you said we would find the gardener-murderer yes? Raz hopes there aren't too many farms in that direction. This one gets embarrassed when he accidentally attacks innocent chicken herders.

You're going to leave me alone in this hostel, aren't you? And without a weapon, I bet.\n\nWell, I guess I'll just trust the Commander and assume that I'll still be alive to celebrate with him after you return.

I took your advice and kept myself in the company of others. Though I was a little surprised when your companions here grabbed me from the pub.\n\nI thought I was a goner, but here I am, safe and sound.

It appears your predictions of fate were right. I came to Anvil, breaking my usual routine, and still no sign of this "killer."\n\nI do wonder if this sweetroll I received was merely a gift from someone else?

Have you come to a decision? Have you chosen which fate will come to pass today?\n\nEither those I targeted receive the time to alter their destinies or you kill me and damn them all. Tell us and end the suspense, if you please.
Well, that did not go exactly as Raz had planned. But everyone is safe for now.\n\nThank you, my friend. Raz will make sure Yarmia remains safe and stays away from sweetrolls from now on.

You let her live. I thought I knew you better than that. No one was saved today. We just put off the battle for another day.\n\nJust go. I need to get back to Vvardenfell, anyway. I've had my fill of this tarnished coast.
Oh, hello there! We haven't spoken since Darien … well, since that business in Coldharbour. Have we? I'm just a bit discombobulated. My mind's been somewhere else.
Nothing left … try tomorrow. Perhaps I'll have kicked this illness overboard.

Sweetrolls and a secret group that use predictions and murder to change the future? What will Raz have to deal with next?\n\nBut at least the people we helped are safe and alive. For now, that's good enough for Raz.
I almost died and this is the thanks I get! Raz is making me pack up all our belongings before we head back to Auridon.\n\nAs soon as I get a weapon, I might use it to skin that arrogant cat!
Before I leave, I want to thank you for helping me. Again.\n\nI don't know, hero. If you continue to make a habit of this, I might just have to keep you.
It's no good, I'm dry. Was that your plan? Run me out of stock until tomorrow? Hmph.
The Shadowscale wants to linger? I expected as much. Come, my boat sails to Gold Coast if where you want to go that is.

I'm glad Artorius is dead. Does that make me a bad person?\n\nHe took Mirabelle and Cimbar and the others away from us. Ultimately, their deaths are on his head. I'm glad I was there to see you finish him off, Silencer.
Yes, I sell sweetrolls. But I have nothing to do with this Sweetroll Killer nonsense!

I wonder if he was always this smug, and I just didn't see it. That I could have been so blind—it's an unsettling thought.\n\nAnyway, well done. I had no idea Velidreth would be so dangerous … and fat. I couldn't have done this without you.
We've really stirred up the nest. If we want to rescue Tsatva-Lan and Geel-Ma we'll have to move quickly.
The death you've caused lingers about you. What a pleasant scent!\n\nBut last year's harvest won't feed this year's brood. I'll need something fresh to bestow my boon.
What word of the Mage and her aspects? We can't afford to let the Serpent control another Celestial Guardian.
Bad time for visitors. Lots of omens. Caravans being slaughtered. Hope you're not here to see the sights.
You're back! I was beginning to worry for your safety. Did you find the amulet? Tell me everything that happened!

Undead? Ha. These are no rotting draugr or mindless skeletons. But it's true. They can't hardly be called living, either.\n\nUntie these bonds and help me stop them. I'll tell you what I can when I'm free.
A real Celestial right here in the observatory. It's incredible. What a chance to learn! Do you think she'd obliterate me if I touched her?
Well, this job was underwhelming.\n\nYou ended up doing all the work! Maybe next time I can actually join you, eh?
You have done well to stop Tarish-Zi from gathering his cursed army of Anka-Ra.

I heard some men talking in the marketplace. They claimed the Iron Orcs are stirring in the northern hills, like they're preparing for something big. I hope it isn't true. We have enough to worry about right now.
I heard you brought that Imperial back to the Star-Gazers! Is he as good as rumors claim? I'll have to invite him for some mead at the Crossroads. He's got to have some tales worth hearing!
You stand before me, not wounded and defeated, but proud and courageous.\n\nYou have overcome the trials! But what happened to the betrayer?
I'm already beginning to record the events that have transpired. How exciting! \n\nAs far as we know, this is the first time a Celestial has lingered so long among mortals like this.
Knowledge for knowledge. That is my price.\n\nWhat have you brought me, Seeker?
Divines guide your sword-arm and let your spells strike true. Slay Abelazar the betrayer and grant rest to the Sword-Disciples.

I am sorry for the deception. I was uncomfortable dealing with a Daedric Prince. And, I admit it, I was afraid.\n\nI have since embraced my role. Hermaeus Mora's curiosity is insatiable, but his knowledge reaches beyond mortal understanding.
I wish I could tell you more, but it will fall to you to uncover the Serpent's plan. I will answer what I can.
I have given you all that I am willing for the deeds done here.\n\nYou must stop the Yokudans at all cost. Their presence lingers here no more. Now it is up to you to stop them.
Navigating the hidden path requires faith—in one's senses and in one's masters.\n\nAbelazer the betrayer made a mockery of both. He was not what he seemed.
The trial of martial knowledge required cooperation and patience. Initiates needed to work together to gather the books. \n\nAbelazer tricked the others into helping him bring about their demise.
I never thought I would see this day. And so soon! Abelazar the betrayer is dead. Thanks to you.
The help you provided is most appreciated. Perhaps our paths will cross again.

If there's any chance Nahlia is alive, we have to find her.\n\nLook at the scroll and see if you can make anything out of it. I couldn't go after her on my own, but now that you're here, we have to try.

Some of our researchers disappeared a few days ago in the city wing. And the crypt wing … well, we've stayed away from that one. Terrible sounds emanate from there.\n\nI guess what I'm saying is, be careful. It's not just the water that's dangerous.
I can't believe it. So many dead. Our whole city in ruins. All because of those damned mages.\n\nPlease, you have to help us.

I'm relieved that the city is safe, but I can't say I'm glad that Yamanu-ko's gone.\n\nShe taught me everything I know about magic. She always warned me about the temptations of power. For her to fall like this ….
<Symbols appear next to pictures of a man instructing a centurion. This could be instructions on how one teaches a centurion to act on its own.>
You've done well. Craglorn is safe, for now. I will remain behind, in case this place becomes unstable again.

I protested against the bargain. I did not trust the salvation Shada promised.\n\nFor my troubles, Shada cursed me twice. I was forced to drink the water, but to remain conscious, watching as my people slowly went mad under Shada's influence.

I'm happy you found her. That you saved her.\n\nBut … I feel sad, too. The woman I … thought she was—she never existed, did she? In a way, I feel like Hara never came back at all. Maybe I'm being selfish.
I've told you all I know. You need to bind the monarch atronachs before we can understand what's happening.
Do not take Zal'ik lightly. Even as he rests now, his power is beyond most have ever faced.\n\nIf you manage to succeed, I will find you at the end of the caves.
Our friend is losing all the things that make her her.\n\nI have tried every known cure for madness, delirium, and memory loss I know. I am afraid all is lost!

Servants of the Serpent hired the feared Greycloak mercenaries to capture Kelmen Locke.\n\nThe merceneries hold him in a place called Haddock's Market. When they learn all they can, they plan to hand Kelmen over to the Serpent. We need to rescue him.
This is very bad news.\n\nThe Serpent used the monarchs and their power to create a new atronach—one with the ability to take on the elements of other atronachs.

Kind of these Star-Gazers to let us set up shop here in their observatory. I guess it makes them feel safer. I still feel like a kagouti in a glass-blower's shop, though.\n\nBut what brings you all the way up here? Looking to join the Fighters Guild?

You certainly have interesting friends. \n\nI can't say I like sticking my neck out, but you did save me from those bandits. So if you need help finding this Reinhold's Retreat Hara mentioned, I'll do my best.

Reinhold's Retreat. Is that truly what she said? I thought my ears had conspired to fill my mind with the foulest lies, but if you heard the same ….\n\nPerhaps I was meant to be here for reasons other than just stopping Tarish-Zi.

I can't thank you enough. You trusted me, even when I'd failed to show the same trust in you.\n\nI won't make that mistake again. From here forward, we must work together closely if we're to defeat the Serpent.
Thank you for returning our aspects to us. We have discussed among ourselves and concluded that the Lost One is too powerful for us to defeat.\n\nThe best we can hope for is to weaken her.
The Lost One is no longer in control of her actions. Now is the time to strike.
Many thanks for ridding this place of those ghastly zombies and such. Now my research can begin in earnest!
Blessings of Morwha be upon you, friend. Water is more than simple drink to my people, so my gratitude is two-fold. \n\nPlease look over my goods. I hope you can find something you need.
Thanks for the help. Sali'ma said everything is fine now, but I'm still not going anywhere near that water. Nothing but wine and juice for me from now on.
These dung-headed Daedra worshipers conspired to steal from Sali'ma. The Dark Elf ran into the ruins. This dead one drew a dagger and hesitated.\n\nMalihaz is a son of Alkosh. He does not hesitate.
Some of our fellows have been trickling in—disoriented and afraid. My brother has not been among them. I ask for your prayers. I don't know what I'd do without him.
What are you gawking at? We're just … taking notes. Off with you!
Do as the aspects asked. And hurry. The Serpent gets closer to his goal with every passing moment.
You have done for us what we could not do for ourselves. We will remember this.
The Scaled One is gathering our other aspects. We cannot hope to overwhelm him, but we must hope to match him. Our best chance is to face him on an even footing.
Hail, soldier. Glad to see another comrade in arms. Short on supplies? I've got plenty to sell. Take a look.
Hara's deception was a clever one, even if it only stalled the Serpent for a time. We were all fooled. \n\nI can't be angry. This means we actually stand a chance.

When the High Elves approach you, remember that I warned you. Those women have a strange way of spotting anything related to the Star-Gazers.\n\nAnd guess what? If you're working with Hara, you're related to us now.

Have you seen the High Elves that were here by any chance?\n\nI was supposed to keep an eye on them, and I only turned away for a moment and now they're gone! Oh, Hara is going to be very angry with me.
<Without the blackened gem, the orrery holds no further interest.>
Can you believe it? Hara is the Celestial Thief. She's been among us all this time. It's just like the stories from my childhood!
All this time, the Thief was right here. I always thought there was something odd about Hara. She knew so much for one so young.\n\nStill, never in a thousand years would I have guessed it.
So Hara is the Thief and the Thief is Hara. Now I really do need a drink.
Ah, you've returned! I trust that my perfidious acolytes have been properly dealt with?
Hjargredda just returned, but she was too shaken up to say very much. What did you find?
Has the little goat finished its work?
I just … I just need some time alone. But thank you for helping us.

By the Eight, you're alive! You've been gone so long. I was beginning to think I should have tried harder to keep you out of the ruins.\n\nBut tell me, was what I feared true? Was the Scaled Court harvesting more nirncrux?
You're back? What did you find? No. Better you tell Scattered-Leaves first. He's been waiting for you to return.
I don't like that look on your face. It's bad, isn't it? No, I don't want to hear it. You should talk to Scattered-Leaves.
You're back, but where's Camaarie? Oh no, not Camaarie!
You saw something awful out there, didn't you? Well, at least you made it back in one piece.
Our carts overflow with more wounded than tradegoods these days. And for what? More gold! \n\nThe price of prosperity is high. Too high, if you ask me.
Yes, yes, what is it? I don't have time for all these—\n\nMy apologies. We're just … these are trying times. And doubly so for the Dragonstar Caravan Company. How can I help you?
Here to swing a pick? Well, I'd think about another line of work if I were you. Mine's shut down. Closed until we sort out this whole Orc … snake … situation.

Everyone's talking about "Serpent this" and "Scaled Court that." Honestly, how bad could it be?\n\nDo you know how many snakes I put an arrow through back in my acorn days? Maybe it's just time for me to go snake hunting again.

Skeetees grows weary of watering her roots here in town. These dryskins do nothing but drink, fight, and sing like old frogs. I don't know what will evaporate first—their ale, their gold, or my patience.
Cowards! Boot-licking, snake-loving, rock-headed cowards ….
Hey! You! Wanna hear a joke?
I'll be all right. You don't have to worry about leaving me alone here.\n\nGo on. Get to Dragonstar and help Cassi. And thanks again.
Your help in this task was invaluable. Would you be willing to help me deal another defeat to the Serpent's schemes?
Someone said the Iron Orcs won't be a problem now. Right. If you believe that, I've got a key to the Gold Tower I can sell you.
I sense that the darkness within the catacombs has subsided. Tell me, did you find the source of whatever disturbed the dead?
Kelmen should have never confronted her alone. This Cassipia must pay for the blood spilled today!
Regent Cassipia reached for powers that were not hers to acquire.

I admit it. I didn't think our mission stood an Elf's chance in Orsinium of succeeding. But here we are!\n\nYour reputation is rightly deserved. And with any luck, those wards will hold for another thousand years.
Please. Hurry to Belkarth. I don't think you should keep the great warrior waiting any longer than is absolutely necessary.
It's good to see you again before the end, my friend. I was just saying one last farewell to my wife before I depart to find my final battle.
Find Skarath and retrieve War-sworn. That Iron Orc is not worthy to carry such a blade.\n\nTitus has earned my weapon a hundred times over. I would see War-sworn in his hands.
<You hear sneezing inside the cottage>
<This scroll contains notes about handling the Amber Plasm. Destroying these notes will make it much more difficult for Na-Kesh to create more. This will probably enrage her.>
I heard screaming. My fellow elders, were they …? Never mind. You must go to the summit. Find Na-Kesh and end this.
I'd gather some allies before you try to topple one of those anchors. I'm sure you think you'd do fine, but I really don't want to fill out the paperwork of another dead guild member.
You go ahead. I think I'll linger here a while. Who knows when they'll let me back in.
Honestly, what does a mer have to do to get some peace around here? What do you want now?
The Hall of Wisdom is across from Vivec's Palace. The Archcanon's office is on the second floor. Please, don't keep him waiting!
We haven't met yet, but I'm aware of your accomplishments. You are a useful person to know.\n\nAlas, I am but a humble servant of my patron. She is a far more useful person to know than I.

Where do these undead keep coming from? Have you seen how they gather around the nereids? It's as if they're worshiping them.\n\nI wonder if that's what happens, eventually, when you drink the water. You start worshiping nereids and turn undead.
They … they handed me over to the nereids. My own people!\n\nA sacrifice to Shada they called it. My life … I could feel it slipping away. I don't know how much longer I could have lasted.
I can't believe Klause and the others would have done this. This is all because of the water?
Forgive me. I wore the guise of Hara because I didn't know who to trust, but neither could I rest while the Serpent preyed on the other Guardians.
You're here to laugh at me as well?\n\nI saw what I saw. He was naked as the full moons in a cloudless sky!
About time you got here. What took you so long?
You're here for the New Life Festival? I'm happy to serve as a herald. I can tell you all you need to know!
Did you get the things Naryu wanted? The slavers are returning and plans have changed. Naryu sent me to find you and get the gate key.
Greetings friend. Come to look out over the water? I hope it brings you solace.\n\nThe salt-breeze used to give me hope, but not today.

As Governor of this region, I have questions that need to be answered. We found you among the wreckage of the slaver ship, and we found a strongbox with your name on it in another wreck.\n\nI'll give you the strongbox if you tell me the truth.

"Traveler, beware! An army of unknown warriors has been attacking convoys in the western wilds, while a massive force of atronachs threatens all who take the eastern road. Do not leave the city without military escort!"
Velidreth is close, I can feel it. Tsatva too.\n\nTake what you want from this Lady of Lace, but leave Tsatva-Lan to me.
Please, you must help! There was a terrible accident. My colleague is in grave danger!
At last, I found you! You're needed in Belkarth at once.
An old, leatherbound book rests on the table.
<A small recess has appeared in the stone. It seems to be a latch of some sort.>
<There's a strange rock here with letters carved into it.>

Head to the manor and make sure my brother can't scurry away. We've been discreet, so I doubt he suspects anything. Just tell him you work for me and that I'll be along shortly. \n\nEverything will be just fine.
Do you need something? I'm rather busy at the moment.
What's that sneaky witch talking about? As soon as she sets me free and gives me back my sword, we're done!
Let all who celebrate the New Life know you surpassed the Trial of Five-Clawed Guile.\n\nWalk with Rajhin in your shadow.
Haha! We did it! I bought Tirwin—I can't wait to deliver the news! And the look on Mother's face will be priceless!
Well. Did you get what I asked for, or are you wasting my time?
As soon as I deal with this buffoon of a Nord, we'll make our way to Vivec City.
I can't believe you gave the contract up, no strings attached. You're a saint.

You … I don't recognize you. You've made a terrible mistake in coming here. Do you feel it yet? The cold rush through your veins—the stiffness in your joints? Only a matter of time, now. Only a matter of time.
<This mead bottle has been drained dry.>
<Nords like mead. Must be the right direction.>
<An empty mead bottle. I should look around here.>

And with the signal fires lit and our defenders alerted, Zoreh finally collapsed. Such courage drove our ancestors to victory against the warlord and his band.\n\nTo understand her sacrifice is to understand <<1>>.
Few who walk the War Orphan's Sojourn have your generous nature. May Stendarr guide you and keep you.
That was … that was truly amazing! You saved Lord Vivec! And Vvardenfell! And all of Morrowind!\n\nI don't know what to say. Thank you, my friend. Thank you so very, very much.
Thank you for your contribution. It means so much to those in need.
It takes some pluck to enter a Telvanni tower uninvited. Impressive.\n\nI'm Llayne Sadri, Mouth to the glorious Mistress Dratha. What is it you want, outlander?
Enjoying the food? Show us your appreciation! See if you can put all the clan wives to shame.

I'll see to this lot. After that? Well, I'll have my hands full, I guess. Finding a new crew should be a hoot. "Come get slaughtered by the Camonna Tong!"\n\nAh well. Can always use a few thrill-seekers on the boat. Makes things more exciting.
Bah … killed by a damned Elf. What a way to go.\n\nWell? What are you gawking at, runt? You going to finish me off or what?
Ralasa had every opportunity to avoid this. Take solace in the fact that she forced our hand.

Please, sera, do not hurt me! Wait … who are you? You do not serve the Camonna Tong? Thank the Hist!\n\nYou must help me escape! Two others as well. If those Camonna thugs find us, they will flay us alive!
Checking up on me? I've got this situation handled—cross my heart and all that. Mistress Dratha will be fine. You just go help Llayne, all right?
What has she done? She … she tightened the slavemaster's bindings!
Thank you, stranger. I was near to slitting my own wrists. If it's to be slavery or suicide, I'll take suicide.
I'm terribly sorry about this business with Mertis. I can typically smell a bad deal the minute it walks through the door. Must be losing my edge.
Thank you so much for saving my boy. Don't worry—from now on, I won't let him out of my sight for an instant!
Thanks again for the help, f'lah. That was a tight spot.
What do you want? I don't have time for foolish interruptions.
Your bravery does you credit. Fight well and return safe.
Two orders of cough syrup, three jars of burn cream … business is picking up already! Thanks again for the help, sera.
Balada Nama-ai, traveler.\n\nMay the spirits walk among you as an ally, and your shadow never stray from your feet.
Free at last! I'll admit, I doubted you'd succeed. But those disgusting Iron Hounds released me today without so much as a "begging your pardon."\n\nThank you, friend. Thank you.

Yesterday, I was a slave. Today, I am free. Know that you have the gratitude of Ghamosh gro-Betnikh for as long as you draw breath.\n\nAs for me, I've had enough of this island. I'm bound for Orsinium. Farewell.

Our destination is an old fortress far to the north, accessible only by a small pass in the mountains. There's an Ashlander camp outside of it where we'll be stopping for supplies. We may find out more from them.

This soil is corrupt. The stain of evil pollutes this land and must be scoured clean like a pair of soiled trousers.\n\nToday we ready ourselves for a great cleansing! You hear me evil? You shall be scrubbed into Oblivion by days end!
I don't know who's the bigger fool, me or them. I can't believe I'm paying for this.

What? A girl's got to eat. I'm starving! Nothing but bug-gruel and water for days!\n\nOne of those constables lent me a fishing pole, so I guess they're not all bad. Next time a Dark Elf makes a pass at me, maybe I'll just spill a drink on him instead.
I promise, I'll never doubt the efficacy of alchemical practice again. Leech bloodletting though? Sheer quackery.

Your actions have ensured the safety and prosperity of Tel Mora for years to come. Quite an accomplishment for a wiry youth.\n\nNow if you'll excuse me, I have preparations to make. Many, many preparations.
I wouldn't count Melar out, and neither should you. He's walking again, and probably going to be alive long after I'm pushing up roses. They build them tough in Vvardenfell.
Deliver the relic to Mistress Dratha. She will know what comes next. \n\nAnd I would highly advise against trying to do anything else with it. That could turn out to be … unfortunate.
Oh my, the Scarlet Judge. Here before me. Is this a social visit? If so, perhaps I can polish away some of those good morals. I'll certainly do my best.
Ha! There's nothing finer than a fat cat in chains! Thanks for the assistance, f'lah.
I gave you what you wanted, Hound. Now get out of my house.\n\nI don't care how much the Marshal is paying you. I won't tolerate any more disruptions of my work. Good day!
<Someone killed Constable Mirel and looted his belongings. The dagger in his chest looks to be of Khajiit design.>
I suppose it's time to find a new line of work. Perhaps I'll run for marshal. I couldn't do much worse than the last one, even on ruined legs.

We'll need to set the wards in a specific pattern. You protect me while I set them up and we'll be done with this in no time.\n\nAnd if you're interested in how it works, for a small donation, I can explain the magics of our lords.
This isn't right. Where's the treasure vault? The hidden chambers? This tomb deeply disappoints Narsis Dren.

<This scroll bears the insignia of the Undaunted and a potent spell, conceived of by the renowned Hroltar the Boaster. When invoked the scroll will empower one's enemies with astonishing power.\n\nThe full incantation isn't short on colorful language.>
Just remember that those people down there, crazed as they may be, were once our friends and family.\n\nIf it comes to blows, remember that they were just like us once.
Head on up to the mines and I'll be there shortly.\n\nUnless you change your mind and decide you don't want to get yourself killed. It's not like anyone would blame you.
I did not expect to find another like myself preying upon the mortals here.\n\nWere you drawn to this place in search of salvation as well?
Another tomb? And clear on the other side of Vvardenfell? This sounds dangerous to me, but Narsis Dren is the famous adventurer and all. I'm just here to haul around his very heavy possessions.

I better get Borfree to start packing so we can head for the Veloth tomb. He's sweet but kind of simple. I think it's wonderful that Narsis keeps the poor fellow employed, even though he requires a lot of supervision.

Well it's about damned time! You daffy House Redoran types have … wait, you're not House Redoran. Bah! Should have known better.\n\nYou'd best move on, stranger. This mine's cursed. It'll snatch you up just like poor Thagbruth if you aren't careful.
Barilzar? I think I remember that name. Sotha Sil's apprentice, if I recall. At least, one of his apprentices. The crazy one, I believe.
Go on. Finish your business with Maj, then you can try to impress me.
Oh, this is terrible! Lord Vivec collapsed! Tell me, outlander, were you able to defeat Chodala? Have you brought me his staff? I'm afraid Lord Vivec may not last much longer.

Thanks again for the help. I want to collect some of the tools the looters tried to carry off before I leave.\n\nI wonder why the Tribunal allows bad things to happen? You'd think Vivec could calm Red Mountain and send the moonlet back into the sky.
I'll be sure to let the trade barons know what you did here. All of House Hlaalu should know your name.
There is nothing more to be said between us.

<This pilgrim was killed recently, but aside from the ragged tear across his abdomen and some bite marks, the body is mostly intact. Perhaps the deceased Buoyant Armiger drove the creature off before it could finish its meal.>
<This Buoyant Armiger appears to have died defending the pilgrim laying dead nearby. Her helmet has been removed.>
<It would be impossible to identify whoever this was if it wasn't for the personal effects nearby. The bones have been completely picked clean.>
Once things settle down, I'll pen a ballad in your honor, outlander.\n\nYou have my word it'll stink less than this place when we're done.
You have my thanks, outlander, but that is all.
Ask the Warrior-Poet's questions, outlander.
Captain Artisia Naros is handling the situation at the canton of Molag Mar. If you think you can help, she'll be glad to have you.

This one is thinking we should chase the moons together sometime. You owe it to yourself to taste the sugar at least once, yes?\n\nI am talking about moon-sugar, by the way. Halinjirr is not trying to seduce you.
Good fortune, sera. I trust you'll do the right thing.
I think you've done enough in Seyda Neen, outlander. I suggest you go and visit one of our other fair cities.

You came all the way up here? Even with the warnings? I hope you weren't hurt. I'd feel horrible.\n\nUsually people are too frightened to ever get this far! But still, do you need a bandage? Some tea? The whole ordeal must have been stressful.
I've got to get back to work. No telling when we'll get another rush in here.
I'll wait here a little longer so I can tell the House Guard what happened. Hopefully, they're going to show up soon.
It's good to see you again. Finished exploring the tomb? But where's Narsis? I do miss that Dark Elf terribly, you know.
What a large vault! Imagine the expense that went into hollowing out a space this big.

I must say, that was much more dramatic than when Sotha Sil manipulated his own energy. Of course, he didn't usually drain himself nearly to death.\n\nHmm. Perhaps the next time I see him, I'll suggest that. An interesting experiment, to say the least.

Do what you can for Vivec. I'll pray to Azura for guidance, then I might go and poke around the Archcanon's office. See if he left anything behind that might shed some light on this terrible situation.
The hero approaches! A warrior without peer! Alas, all my gold was squandered on beer!\n\nThe hero is selfless! The hero is kind! The hero won't kill me and rob me blind. I hope.
Please just let the way home be safe …

There is nothing more for us to discuss. You curried our favor by helping us deal with Malur, and then squandered that when you destroyed the formula in some attempt at a righteous display. \n\nI have no further use for you.

Convincing the Ashlanders to let my family settle here will take some doing, but I will follow their customs to the letter—just like you did. I'm certain I can make this work.\n\nThanks again, friend.
The Red Exiles! They've gone mad! Please, you have to do something before they kill Seryn!
You helped bring this fetcherfly into our home. Whatever he and his Redoran overseers do here shall be your doing as well. I pray that you choose your friends wisely.
I've never seen a Dwemer crystal quite this … lively. This promises to be a fascinating investigation.
Do what you need to in order to get Farwen back here safely. We can't waste any time. Possession spirits aren't to be taken lightly.
Take care of yourself. I'm sure we'll meet again … in some other machine-infested ruin.
I wish you good fortune if you enter the tomb. I have no doubt that you will need it.

I am entrusting you with my family's most sacred relic. I pray that my faith in you is not misplaced.\n\nGive it to my descendant. Let the spear grant him the strength he needs to restore our house's honor.
The Forge lies deep in the ruins beyond these wilds. Tread carefully, these woods obey the Reach-hag, Caillaoife. If you hear the sound of crows, it's too late.
That … that—that's it then? They're dead and gone? And that bloody Forge lies quiet as their graves?

The true Ashlanders reject Chodala's claim, but he still commands the loyalty of the Red Exiles. He won't find shelter here. There are many places to hide in the wilds of Vvardenfell, however.\n\nMay Azura walk with you, outlander.

I foresaw your usefulness before you even set foot in Vvardenfell. Now comes a test that will challenge your ability to separate truth from lies.\n\nYou must convince the tribes that Chodala is not the Nerevarine.
You have courage to match Eerika's, at least. Maybe it'll be enough.\n\nThe road leads to the main gate—through the Reachman lines—if it still stands, you'll find our Thane there.
Clear the way to the Jarl's hall. These people can follow after you. I will hold the enemy here as long as I can.
It's not right. It has to be right ….

Agh! Gracious, you nearly gave me a heart attack. You're a Redoran enforcer, aren't you? Look, I'm near to fixing this thing, I promise.\n\nWait. How are you not a mumbling imbecile? Don't bother answering. I can't hear a thing. Ears are plugged, see?
Clear a path through the meddlesome machines in the cavern beyond this antechamber. I will join you at the rift once I've completed my usual transliminal preparations.
Translocating all this material will require considerable—yes?

Ah, the hero of the hour! You have my deepest thanks and most heartfelt compliments. The fact that you fixed it in your clearly addled condition … exemplary work. Just exemplary!\n\nSeems like it's quieted down. I do hope it stays that way.
It plays and plays! But the chords are wrong! Don't you see? It has to be right! It has to be perfect!
Hrmph. Thagbruth nearly bit my hand off when we pulled him out of the mine. I've never seen him like this. Poor bastard.
<The miner no longer speaks. He only hums a melody.>
Chodala … he's gone mad. Sought to make a deal with a Daedric Prince ….
Don't worry about me, friend. Just find Menwendel!
It feels good to breathe in the ash again.\n\nI may carry a limp for the rest of my days, but at least I have days to spare. Thanks again, f'lah.

I'll be honest. I thought we were going to die down there. I'm glad you and Miss Lacroix were able to prove me wrong.\n\nAs for that damned High Elf, well … we'll never be working for him again. He cut and run the moment those mercenaries showed up!

You show great martial skill, sword-friend. I erect the spine of respect.\n\nI regret not killing more of those dryskinned mercenaries, but to see my partner safe and sound … that brings me great joy.
Didn't you hear me? I said scoot!

I wish we didn't have to leave Vos, but it just isn't safe here anymore. I may be a Dark Elf, but I also fell in love with an Argonian … a former slave at that! I'm not exactly on Savarak's good side.

Councilor Eris can be found at the Redoran Kinhouse. And do hurry. He's ever so troubled by our failure to locate young Veya.\n\nIf he finds that an outsider can succeed where the House Guard has failed, so be it.

You helped my sister. Thank you for that. But you don't need to worry about the Red Exiles any more. They're under my control now.\n\nAs for everything else, that's Ashlander business. There's no place for an outlander here.
Work with Captain Brivan as necessary and get me a meeting with my daughter. It's imperative that I get another chance to explain my actions to her.\n\nI'm counting on you, outlander.
What are you—? No! I can't leave. Not yet!\n\nI tried to follow the foreman. I did! But it won't let me. Not until everything is as it should be. Not until everything is perfect!
You might wonder if this whole experience has put me off delving Dwemer ruins for awhile.\n\nIt hasn't. Honestly, this sort of thing happens to me all the time.

Captured by a pack of milk-drinking Elves … humiliating. Sure, they had me outnumbered a hundred to one, but still.\n\nI'm glad Lotaeel made it out, at least. I don't know what I'd do without this stupid lizard following me around.
Naturally, Neramo's trying to renegotiate our delving fee. Unexpected circumstances, he says. I'll show him unexpected circumstances when I ram my quill up his arse!

The Nerevarine remains a promise unfulfilled, and I am as guilty of prideful posturing as every other Failed Incarnate that occupies this hall. \n\nAsk your question and let's be done with this, outlander.

We are the Failed Incarnates, the Ashlanders who proudly proclaimed themselves to be the Nerevarine but were found wanting.\n\nThe Lady of Dawn and Dusk urged us to cooperate, so ask your question, outlander.
Once I was the hope of my people, but then my claim was proven false. Now I wait and I hope for the Nerevarine's return.\n\nState your question, outlander, and I shall do as Azura urges.
What? Who? This one has done nothing! Nothing!
The Ashlands are dangerous, but around Kogoruhn … there's something off. Don't find yourself cursed as well.
<The egg-hand ignores you—absent-mindedly humming a simple tune.>
When I'm able to fight, I'll find the truth. I won't let what happened to her happen to anyone else.
You don't look like one of those crazy cultists and you certainly aren't one of our miners. So by Vivec's holy nose hairs, who in Oblivion are you?
I saw you head across the bridge toward Veya's friends.\n\nSo, how did you fare, outlander? Did you learn anything that might help us find the councilor's daughter?
I hope you will consider working with me again.

If you can, please bring my wife back to me safely. I'd like us to be together when Baar Dau crashes down around us.\n\nFive years of happy marriage and this is how it all ends? I wish Lord Vivec would just do something!
You. Thanks to your nonsense, I'm assigned to guarding the docks, instead of the tower. And if I find the slave who helped you, I'll take care of him. Or her.
Even Kizmar's battered nose can smell the woodsmoke from here! Good work, walker!
What are you doing here?
I can't wait to see the look on Ralasa's face when Muthsera Gothren strips her of her title! And the groveling … the groveling will be delicious!
I really do appreciate everything you've done. Perhaps my career isn't ruined after all.
Did I neglect to pay you …? No, I made a note of it right here.\n\nI have no further business with you and much to do. Off you go!
You stink of incense and hookah smoke. Did that beast Gothren send you?

I think we're done here, don't you? I told you where to find Ashur. He's been passing our notes on to Veya. Just to the north and east, outside of town.\n\nOr is this your way of offering to save me a trip, since you're headed his way?
Don't kick yourself over Ralasa outmaneuvering you. Trust me, you never had a chance.

Your friend considers herself my equal, but in the end it seems she's still just a witless slave. You've been ever so helpful in proving it. My thanks.\n\nNow, what brings you to my chambers, outlander?
I'll send word to all the people of Vvardenfell. Once you've retrieved the signet, we'll meet again in Vivec City.
I did not think an outlander would be so willing to help an Ashlander tribe. We do not have much, but you are always welcome to our fire.

Make sure you don't anger Veya's mentor or even look at her the wrong way. She's grown surprisingly protective of that young woman and if she thinks you pose a danger ….\n\nBesides, I'd hate to see you wind up on the wrong end of one of our writs.
Please, find my children. I think … I think I need to go lay down. It's been a taxing day already.
Sera, I cannot thank you enough for helping me. I wasn't sure if I'd ever leave Tel Aruhn alive.\n\nI'm sorry. I know I've asked too much of you.

It must have been so hard on Father. To have to leave us so often. To keep silent while we grew cold and distant even when he was here ….\n\nIt might seem odd, but I feel hopeful. Father and mother are finally with us. Their memories will live on.
Now we just need to get new miners. Do you know anyone looking for some work?
Thank you, my friend! It will be good to get back to studying this wonderful fungus.

I thought I knew my father. I always thought he hated me, and that's why he was never around. I came to terms with that long ago.\n\nI had a father, and I hated him. Now he's gone. How am I supposed to face what's in that stone knowing I was wrong?
I don't understand. You stopped the experiment. Why do these visions remain?
So, care to tell me what you were doing on that slaver ship?
You don't look familiar, I have no appointments today. Therefore you are unwelcome.
You need to leave.
You have no idea how thankful I am. That thing still haunts my nightmares!
Now I just need to find a good herbal tea. Let me tell you, the work of a Mouth is hard on the throat.
You retrieved the journal. That was competent.
Shor's bones, you were gone a long time. Had me a little worried! But here you are, all in one piece.\n\nSo, don't keep me in suspense. You find those notes I asked for?

Well, it's not exactly a lie. And I don't want things to get out of hand.\n\nI'll arrange a meeting, provided Veya agrees. You let Eris know she's safe. Get him to stop hiring freelancers before someone gets hurt. I'll send word when we're ready.
Naryu goes too easy on Veya. When my master trained me, her word was law and the only acceptable response on my part was "as you command."\n\nBut what do I know. Veya's not my apprentice.
I'll get Veya back to Balmora and try to figure out our next move.\n\nStay alert when you meet with Councilor Eris. There's no telling who's involved in Ulran's exile and subsequent murder.
Your intervention on Firemoth Island was … unexpected. But the slavers' captives are safe. Do you have anything else to report?
I think we're done here, outlander. Move along.
Now that's the proper way to ask a question!\n\nAs a matter of fact, I did notice someone near the lighthouse that night.
ALMSIVI is the ending of words!\n\nI forgot how much I enjoyed the thieving arts! Sneaking into the governor's private quarters brought back fond memories.
I'll need to keep my lies straight. I see a long, grueling audience with the Council ahead of me.
Your knowledge demonstrates both strength and wisdom, outsider. Enter and be welcome.
Sod off. I'm drinking.
Get a move on. Eoki's waiting for you.
I'm not looking for trouble, just food and drink
Better get a move on. The boss hates waiting.
I foresee a profitable partnership as our association deepens, outlander. Now, what have you brought me?
Your understanding of House Indoril serves you well. Enter and share our preserved knowledge.
Well, what are you waiting for? I can't make a break for the cave until you engage the mercenaries. If they aren't busy with you, they'll spot me before I take three steps!
You understand the meaning and purpose of House Dres. Enter our vault and be welcome.
Your understanding of House Hlaalu does you proud, outsider. You may enter and bask in our rich history.
I've never ventured through the exit, so this will be new territory for the both of us. I'll do my best to try and help though.
I can't wait to dig in and see what secrets these ancient tomes contain!
Ulran's … gone.\n\nHow do I make sense of any of this? Maybe Naryu knows what to do.
I'm trusting you to make this right, outlander. I may have lost my son, but I refuse to lose my daughter.
The councilor thinks you can help, but I'm not sure you have the best interests of House Redoran in mind.\n\nMy Warclaws will continue to hunt for Veya. I suggest you stay out of their way.
Get the key to the mine from either the Warclaws commander or the supply yurt, whichever suits your needs. Perhaps you'll find what you seek within Kudanat's depths.

You have to understand. I don't share my House's hatred and distrust of Ashlanders. So, during my normal patrol, when I heard that Ashlanders had come to Balmora and were causing trouble, I was dubious to say the least.
I've told you more than enough. The item you seek is deep in the ruins of Nchuleft.\n\nI provided the information and gave you my warning. What happens next is up to you.
Look, it's no meatballs off my table if you decide to go to Arkngthunch. I'm sure I saw a sonance generator down there. Yes, I'm mostly positive! Find my notes and everything should work out fine.

Someday I'll get my revenge on those vampires, as soon as I come up with a foolproof plan.\n\nIn the meantime, if you're heading into Galom Daeus to retrieve that item, I'd consider it a personal favor if you kill a few of the bastards along the way.
My son is dead and Veya must blame me for Ulran's own failings. I suppose I'm used to that.\n\nThere are things that need to be done. I need your help in these matters, outlander.

Go on. Veya should hear what we learned. We're getting closer to the truth but there's still something missing.\n\nI'll meet up with you after I present my writ. Then we can find out what Ulran's soldiers know.

Let me gather my gear and write a note for Naryu. I'll meet you near the Hlormaren stronghold.\n\nThe more I think about it, the more convinced I am that we'll learn who's responsible for Ulran's death soon. Then blood will flow.

One other thing. Naryu's job concerns House Redoran. That's why she didn't want Veya to accompany her on this one. Veya's grief-stricken, angry, and ready to lash out at anyone and anything. So keep your head low and try not to upset her.
The Festival of Fools is overflowing with all sorts of droll entertainment!\n\nYou know, pranks and gags and silly games. Uncomplicated peasant things! I do so prefer my thinking uncomplicated.
Oh my. Was that—? Did The Twilight Lady claim my mind? \n\nWhat an honor. What a … profoundly disorienting honor.

Well, look at you! I'm impressed! The last person House Dres sent over was so much more … scruffy.\n\nI have a meeting with House Hlaalu shortly, but I think I can spare a few more moments for you. To seal our partnership, you understand.

It is the Festival of Fools! Where fools are noble, and nobles are themselves! Jorunn always believes in leading by example!\n\nWhen you see this one enjoying himself to fullness, are you not inspired to do the same?
The Ahemmusa tribe does not know this Hleran, son of Dranoth. I hope your faith in him is not misplaced.
Time is short. Go to the caves west of Hei-Halai and destroy these Daedric conspirators.\n\nMy children suffered once. They will not suffer again.
Know that the Zainab watch this House-mer, Drelyth, very closely. If the Redorans make a play for Ald'ruhn, he will be the first to die.

So, the Hleran-son plans to settle in Ald'ruhn. I would worry if I thought he stood any chance of surviving. When faced with hardship, the House Dunmer squeal and cry like children. \n\nBelieve me, the Wastes will make a meal of him.
The Erabenimsun will not sit idly by as the Redoran set roots in Ald'ruhn. We will do what we must. Kill who we must.\n\nSkar has but one master—the Ashlanders.
I've been pacing a hole in the floor since you left. It's maddening having to rely entirely on the aid of strangers. And more than a little embarrassing.\n\nTell me you found our shortfall?
Can we hurry this along? I'm extremely busy today.

Despite all the excitement around the recent shipwreck, I'm in here, guarding the governor's office. I suppose someone might want to steal a quill or a stack of parchment, but still.\n\nMy talents are clearly being wasted.
The Jester's Festival has something for everyone!\n\nBarbaric mud fights, Elven prancing, cavorting and carousing like heathens. I'm partial to it, really, just don't tell my wife.
If I can smell you, outlander, then you can be certain the Warclaws have picked up your scent. Leave now and maybe you'll escape with a little flesh still clinging to your bones.

So we travel to Shadowfen. This one hates the smell, and the water, but Kanzin serves Azura. This one will go where she asks we go.\n\nThe lizard, of course, is very excited. Lizards grow excited about these things.

So we now return to the wilds of Shadowfen. I will admit, I am looking forward to a proper soak in the waters of my homeland. After we have dealt with the enemies of our mistress, I may stay awhile.\n\nIt has been long since I licked the tree.
<Blood and entrails are strewn over this stone altar. It is unclear what they belonged to, but they are fresh. Something died here very recently.>

Outsiders? Is her father really that desperate?\n\nLook, tell Eris that Veya's safe and you'll see her soon. But no more outsiders. If the Morag Tong gets skittish, they'll return to the shadows and take Veya with them. They'll only deal with you.
We barely got out of there alive! I can't believe the Overseer's still in there. What's she going to do when the canton sinks into the bay?
You find the key. In the meantime, Vatola and I are going to get reacquainted. I want to hear about what happened when my brother was sent to confront the Ashlanders.
I knew I shouldn't have told Veya the truth. I just made everything worse.\n\nPlease, let us out of here. We have to stop Veya before she does something she'll regret.
Hurry to the Cloudy Dregs Inn. Our situation grows perilous, and Azura is anything but patient.

It appears to have worked. Vivec's energy is restored.\n\nWhile I've never wished them harm, I also never thought I'd help save the life of a Tribunal pretender. Ah well, at least Red Mountain has returned to its slumber.

I can't believe my apprentice might be responsible for causing the Morag Tong to fall out of favor again. And she's not alone in this. I'm right there with her, about to plunge my career into the sewer!\n\nI hope we can talk some sense into her.

I hope Veya realizes that Brivan is loyal to House Redoran above all else. If he did do something to upset her, it was probably for a perfectly good reason. And he was certainly operating under House orders.
What are you gawking at, outlander?
You're not from around here, are you? Tall Papa be praised. I've had about enough of the local gossip.

I'll cause a distraction and try to draw away some of the Warclaws, then I'll meet you inside.\n\nJust be careful in there. Alert too many of the soldiers or mercenaries and we'll have the entire garrison after our beautiful arses.
I said I'd deal with this. Veya is my responsibility. It should be my blade that ends this.\n\nGo. I'll see you back at the safe-house in Balmora.
I can't believe the governor was working with slavers! What an opportunistic cretin! I'm not sure if I'm disgusted or a little jealous of his audacity.

What in the name of the Three are you up to? I thought you worked for Councilor Eris?\n\nYou better have a damn good reason for killing the mercenary leader. I ought to sound the alarm and let her warriors deal with the likes of you.
Well? Did you get my poem?

The Morag Tong agent … she cares deeply for Veya, doesn't she?\n\nIt takes great courage to go against your heart and do what you know is best. You both did that by protecting the council. For that, you have my thanks.

I'm going to drink one more glass of wine to honor Veya's memory, then I'm going to try to forget all about her.\n\nBut I promise not to forget you, hero. Maybe we can do this again sometime. Well, not this exactly. You know what I mean.
This goes against every protocol, but I couldn't let poor Veya bleed to death.\n\nI patched all the holes you people put in her and she should recover, given time.
Things seem quieter around Ashalmawia. Should I be thanking you for that?
Ferhara enjoys a friendly rivalry as much as the next mercenary, but the Releth kitten belongs to the Warclaws, yes?\n\nLet's not get our tails tangled over this, dull claw.
It's not just anyone who can tussle with the Camonna Tong and walk out with all their fingers intact. You obviously know how to handle yourself.
Anyone who helps keep skooma out of Vvardenfell is all right in my book. You've done the citizens of this island a great favor.

I'm sure you're concerned about the kwama egg, but be rest assured that I'm handling it with the greatest of care. You'll be the first to know when the little one hatches! \n\nOh, I am trying not to get too attached you know.
Tell your friend that I counsel patience, for the time being.
The more I consider the implications, the more I wonder about the nature of these strange scrolls. Before I give them to the scribe of White Ridge Barrow, I really must get Stibbons to peruse them.
Poor Stibbons. I suppose we'll get blamed for this, too.\n\nI really hate working for that nasty Breton woman.
Well? Do you want your master's payment or not?

It's good to see you again, sera, but I'm afraid I'll be of no use to you.\n\nMistress Dratha harbors no ill will toward Sun-in-Shadow, but Gothren wields great diplomatic power on issues like this. There's little I can do to break Ralasa's support.
Honor to you, sera.\n\nSorry about your friend's petition. She may ascend to oathman eventually. Of course, with Ralasa speaking for Gothren, she may have to wait for a good long while.
Well, that's over and done with! If I never see another spider, I'll be happy and content!\n\nNow, where did I put the newest Investigator Vale mystery?
Because of you we may finally be free, divines bless you.
Because of you I may now have a future filled with freedom once again. Thank you.

You may not believe this, but I really am happy to see you. I grew rather fond of you while I inhabited that dreadful Dark Elf form. Now you get to see me in all my glory.\n\nAnd soon, you'll be able to witness my greatest achievement!

I do hope you'll forgive my candor, but I must ask—what brings a bumbling outlander to my gathering house? Do you fancy yourself a Telvanni mage? No, I think not. You may take your leave. Immediately.
Well? Why are you still standing here? Go investigate the fungal growth!
Ever since the prisoners were freed from the farmlands, I've been extra busy. So many need my help. But as long as I have beds, all are welcome to stay here. Even you, if you wish.
This one has wares that those ones will not miss.
What happened was terrible, but our work must continue.
<This tile shows the letter "S" as written in the Daedric script.>
<This tile shows the letter "E" as written in the Daedric script.>
<This tile shows the letter "M" as written in the Daedric script.>
My sister thinks Master Fyr can do no wrong. Maybe he can't. But it's not him I'm worried about.\n\nGoing into that rift would be suicide.
Master Fyr sent a runner to inform me of your deeds so that I could include them in my report. Such an amazing endeavor. I'm so jealous!\n\nI am still waiting to deliver it, believe it or not.

I lost you somewhere between the Clockwork City and Vivec, but it was simple enough to trace your energy signature to this Daedric shrine.\n\nUnfortunately, some power is interfering with my efforts to open a portal for you.
Yes, you are strong. I understand Galgalah's interest now. You will make a fine vessel. Ask what you will, but our time is short. Determine your questions wisely.
I … I feel better now. The pain. It's fading. I feel so light. Drifting away. Am I dead?
Thank the Eight, you're alive! \n\nWe didn't know what would happen when we left. We hoped for the best, but feared the worst. It's so good to know you're safe—is Farwen with you?
I'm sorry, I just needed to take a little breather away from everyone. Just … just a bit to get my strength back. Then I'll be as good as normal.

Your actions are selfless and courageous. You have proven yourself worthy of the name friend!\n\nI would buy you a drink to toast it, but my coin is already pledged to the orphanage of my homeland. Come to think, can I borrow some gold to pay for this?
The wounded have all been stabilized, but we lost so many. I'm afraid that the talent of tower shaping will be set back generations by their loss.

My brother and I were studying the Dwarven relics found throughout the cave—and then …. We never should have wandered away from the rest of the shapers.\n\nExcuse me, I can't—I can't talk about this right now.
What a discovery! Those animunculi were resonating in a stable, anharmonic oscillation! It's unprecedented! And it just fell in our laps!\n\nWhat rare fortune!
Those things in the cave, they were like nothing I've ever seen. I've studied Dwarven specimens from the Alik'r Desert, Orsinium, all over. \n\nNever anything like those long-necked … things.

How dare you discipline my dog? He was only trying to appease his master. And I'd never harm a hair on whatever insignificant creature you hold dear.\n\nYou, on the other hand, require a lesson in manners ….

You come before me with an empty sack, but have no fear. As I have written, "Treat your enemies well and your friends even better." Know that I consider you to be a very good friend.\n\nWill you accept the honor I am about to bestow upon you?
I told you what I know about Galgalah. If you still desire to confront him, we will honor your bravery by cutting the spirit from your body.

Interesting. Stibbons summoned forth webs with nary a spider in sight. I've always found Daedric magic to be fascinating.\n\nI wonder, do you think Lady Laurent will let me examine the scrolls long enough to learn a spell or two?
Greetings. My benefactor wishes to speak to you about a matter that could affect the fate of our world.
Mmmfh!
Thank the Eight! To Oblivion with these damned mages. No amount of gold is worth this kind of treatment!
I just received a notice from Divayth Fyr that he will not be accepting any more deliveries from me. Ungrateful s'wit.\n\nOn a positive note, however, he also won't evaporate me, so thank you!
I just need to be patient. My Rosy will come back. At least, I hope she will.
Mind you, I wouldn't say no to some dung mages. If the Telvanni can magic up giant mushrooms, you think they could spare a spell or two helping clean up this mess.\n\nAh well. It's a job.
My son is … dead? No, not Ulran. I … I don't … I won't … believe it.
They left us here … to die. These creatures ignore us now that the battlemages have retreated. Perhaps soon we will be able to crawl to freedom.\n\nGo! Do not draw them here!

It is nice to see a friend. I confess, I am a bit lonesome with Eoki gone. \n\nI have been keeping my ears open, and have not heard anything about any escaping slaves being caught. I hope he makes it home, I do. But still, I miss him every day.
Speak to Traylan or Beleru down the hall if you're looking for work. They'll let you know if they have a suitable job.
You. I remember you. You were at Ald'ruhn. Some say you're a friend to the clans.\n\nDo you wish to prove it?

I recognize you. You paid tribute to the First Ashkhans at Ald'ruhn. Many eyes were upon you, whether you knew it or not.\n\nFor that honor, I will call you friend. Many others would likely do the same were you to help the tribes.
In the mood for a little trip? I can take you to Vvardenfell. Ports of call include Seyda Neen and Vivec City.

You're not welcome here—No, wait. I've seen you before, haven't I? The outlander who gained permission to perform the sacred rite to honor the First Ashkhans. You may walk freely here. \n\nPerhaps you even seek to prove yourself further.
Go and walk among our people. Show them you can be trusted, and you will be rewarded with the favor of the tribes.
Are you here to mock me too? Here to pile yet another indignity upon my well-sculpted shoulders? Do your worst!
The slavers, they're coming back! They're going to punish us severely for this.
This one hopes the slavers all develop skin rashes. Painful, itchy, skin rashes.\n\nIn the meantime, we should be leaving now, yes?

How did I know you were going to show up, hero? Can't get enough of my smiling face, hmm?\n\nI know she tried to murder a kinhouse full of councilors, but Veya deserves to see a friendly face before I send her away.
Naryu thought you might stop by. You probably hate me and I completely understand.\n\nI'm still glad you showed up, though.

Azura's champion … went to the Archcanon's office … to investigate Barbas's activities.\n\nImagine … the Tribunal seeking aid … from an Ashlander … and a servant of Azura. Now I must concentrate. Llevule can answer any questions you have ….
