What? Did you think I was so depressed that I'd drink myself silly and fall into the ocean? Well, I'm neither drunk enough or motivated enough to walk that far.\n\nAnd I prefer my water to be warm and full of bubbles.
No time to talk. I have to assess the smoke damage here.
Do you remember that incident on the Gold Coast? That thing with the sweetroll and the Fate-Bearers?\n\nWell, I received another message.
What did you see in there? Was it awful? No, don't tell me. I really don't want to know.
Did you hear? House Redoran denounced the Morag Tong! Isn't that rich?
Could you spare some gold? A little food? Perhaps a fine pair of shoes?
Do mind the guar! \n\nIsn't country life grand? It's like I'm right back at home in Cyrodiil. Aside from the giant fungi and adorable lizard chickens, of course.
Finally! The Buoyant Armigers say the roads are safe for travel again. I only have to hope the Redas Ancestral Tomb isn't haunted.
So it wasn't my imagination! Next time I complain to the steward about a strange smell, he'd best listen.

Treacherous Hlaalu. Trying to poison us with our own fungus, of all things! They couldn't manage that without someone on the inside.\n\nI'm going to hound that adept's every step until I have my proof.
We keep managing to find each another, don't we, hero?\n\nDeshaan, Eastmarch, the Gold Coast. Even here in Vvardenfell. Gods, it feels like I've known you forever!
Baar Dau is falling and Red Mountain erupts, but Lord Vivec will still protect.

So … how was it? Speak! Do you feel invigorated? Imbued with righteous power? Or perhaps struck dumb with awe by a vision of St. Alessia herself?\n\nGo ahead—reveal to all your holy transmogrification!
Dirt tracked everywhere …. These miners have no respect for this temple. No one wants to kneel in muddy footprints.
Ah, the esteemed Scarlet Judge. What justice are we serving today?

"Once, Lord Vivec met a farmer whose guar had died, making her unable to feed her family or village. So Vivec removed his finery and toiled in the fields until the crop was harvested. Thus we pray for the same humility Lord Vivec showed that day."

"When Sheogorath tricked Baar Dau to hurl itself upon Lord Vivec's city, the Poet-Warrior froze the rogue moon with a single gesture. Overwhelmed by his courage and daring, the moon swore itself to eternal service of the Tribunal and all its works."

"Long after our triumph over the Dwarves, the people wished to build a monument to the heroes of that war. Vivec thanked them, but said that it would be better to dedicate a monument to all people, great and small, who suffered and died in the war."

"In a battle with Mehrunes Dagon, Vivec gave his own silver longsword to the Daedra Lord rather than dishonor himself by fighting an unarmed foe. This so impressed the Dremora that they now share a bond of respect with the followers of the Tribunal."

"Once Vivec awoke to find himself and his followers trapped in hardened ash. Saddened by their suffering, his tears weakened the ash, freeing him to save his people. This is Vivec's heroism—his tender heart provides strength when his might fails."

"Lord Vivec once fought a battle with Ruddy Man, the father of the Dreugh. When he defeated Ruddy Man, Vivec spared his life, on the condition that Ruddy Man and his children would give up their tough hides to serve as armor for the Dunmer."

"Have trust in the Tribunal, for they protect us from our foes. Have love for the Tribunal, for they bring us help in time of need. Give respect to the Tribunal, for their indomitable will and power is the pride of all Dunmer."
We salvaged our dignity by ending Marshal Hlaren's reign of corruption. Perhaps the Scarlet Judge isn't so bad after all.
Lord Viv—I mean, the Scarlet Judge! It's an honor to be in your presence. Don't worry, your secret is safe with us.
Mead tastes best when worries aren't weighing you down. I mean, it tastes great when you're worried too. Mead always tastes great.\n\nI forget what I was trying to say. Oh well, doesn't matter!
You really shouldn't keep Magister Gothren waiting.
The rocks were falling, the kwama attacking. So many lost!
Here to remind me of my mistake? I have no regrets for my decision, outlander. Perhaps in a hundred years I will, but not today.
Leave me, outlander. Let me die in the shame I've brought to Malacath.\n\nHa! Defeated by a lone warrior. Malacath will laugh at our incompetence.
You have a habit of turning up at the most unusual moments, don't you, hero?
Talk to Eoki so we can get on with this. I really don't want to still be here when the slavers return.
I hope the slavers return. I want to rip a few of them apart with my bare hands! Show them what it means to try to enslave a Nord warrior!
We really ought to get a move on, shouldn't we? The slavers could return at any moment!
This one is ready to fight for our freedom! I'm not afraid of the slavers!

The young woman … she killed them all. Didn't say a word. Just walked in, drew her blades, and cut down every soldier who tried to stop her.\n\nAnd her eyes! I never saw such rage as I saw in her eyes.
Why are you still standing here? If I wanted to exchange gold for vacant stares I'd find a skooma den.

What a singular honor! I've never been invited to a Living God's soiree before!\n\nI'm just glad I was able to get all of the webs off my man-servant. I'd hate for him to sully my reputation by making a bad impression.

Pity there was nothing in that sack of blessings for me. At least that rock hanging in the sky didn't fall and bop me on the head.\n\nOh, what am I saying? The night is still young. You might not want to stand so close. Just in case.

I've never been fond of the Living Gods, so I consider this a punishment. The first of many meaningless tasks the Grand Master will give me until he determines that I've suffered enough for the Veya debacle.\n\nOh how I long for a nice, juicy writ!

I am honored to attend such a prestigious event. And in such a lovely city, too!\n\nYou know, this trip has helped me realize that I haven't seen enough of Tamriel. There's nothing stopping me from visiting great cities like this one, thanks to you.

I'm not surprised to see you here. Not one bit. I'm sure you'll continue to do great things for Vvardenfell. \n\nYou should come visit Tel Mora when you have the chance! Though Mistress Dratha has been rather odd about visitors lately ….

I can't believe this. Lord Vivec, right in front of me! The Living God himself!\n\nI hope I don't embarrass myself …. Do you think I might embarrass myself? You know, I think I'll just stand here. Perfectly still. Without moving. That would be good.

I had no idea you were in Lord Vivec's good graces! Perhaps you could put in a good word for me? I'm currently in negotiations with House Redoran about rebuilding a settlement. And have no fear, I'll keep my end of the bargain with the Ashlanders.
<Perhaps the Library of Andule is hidden somewhere in this missing section.>
There's an Armiger injured on the road outside Seyda Neen. So much blood! They—they need help.
I can feel my power for warfare is redoubled! \n\nWhat fury! Let me at them!
Are you prepared to don the mantle of the Whitestrake and strike down your foes for double rewards?\n\nNow is the time! The holiday is all too brief. Bathe in the blood of your enemies!

Do not distract me, stranger. I am imploring the Old Gods to help me settle the restless spirits of this place and it is a conversation only for the faithful.\n\nI must know exactly where to place my wards or evil will prevail.
Grr! Wish I could have crushed their Patriarch's skull myself, but there'll be others!\n\nWe'll settle this once and for all soon enough!
We have so much left to do. Crows to catch, keys to find, prisoners to interrogate …. We have to move faster!
Any who bleeds with me, I call friend. I pray our first drinks together will not be in the Hall of Valor.
I'm sorry. I know I came to help, but I'm … I'm not very good on boats.\n\nI will be fine, really. You go on ahead. Just give me a moment to catch my breath, and I'll catch up with you.
Poor Adeber. I knew something was troubling him … if only I'd spoken to him about it!\n\nExcuse me, I just need a moment.
Is … is it dead?
Keep your belly to the mud, friend. And keep your eyes on your shadow. I will do the same.

Thank you for leading me to Neelo. If what you say is true, I doubt his wards would have protected him for long. You may well have saved his life.\n\nI will put him into protective custody. If his shadow does attack, I will be here to destroy it.
I wish I could take a moment to rest. This experience has taken a considerable toll on me. Unfortunately, there's not a moment to lose. Nocturnal prepares for another strike, I'm sure of it.
I … I don't feel myself, but … I don't care.
This is drudging up so many unpleasant memories. \n\nPlease tell me you've managed to show Bolin some measure of peace.
You're not part of the Mages Guild, are you? Perhaps you would like to be?
You must hurry. This friend of yours needs help—that I can guarantee.

So you're the one swinging a pick for me, right? Good. We need more flash stone—a lot more. And did Razgurug tell you about the pellets?\n\nYou'll have to speak up, mate! My ears are mostly decorative.
<<1>>'s got you looking for metallic fibers? Good. The air in Slag Town's not getting any cleaner.

So you're my forester? Way I hear it, lumbering in the Clockwork City's a lot less satisfying than it is on the outside. Feels like … I don't know. Chopping a writing-slate wrapped in tin? \n\nEh. You'll get used to it.

Greetings. I assume you spoke to Razgurug? Charming fellow. A pity that the Apostles left him to rot down here. Honestly, Slag Town's full of untapped potential.\n\nSpeaking of untapped potential, you're here to ask about the runic residue, correct?
You're the one who's gathering up my satchels, right? Try not to handle them for long. That smell's impossible to wash off.
I see that you returned, but where's Initiate Favar? More importantly, did you get the readings with the perception tabulator?
How dare you interrupt my vigil! What nonsense impels you to such a rash and impetuous action?
I can already feel my strength returning. Thank you.
Did you find it? The contract?
If you're looking for Lord Seht, I don't know where he is. I will find out though. Count on it.
Divayth Fyr wields tremendous power. If our enemy unleashes his shadow on the world, the results could be catastrophic.\n\nYou must warn him before it's too late.
My master waits for you in the Mournhold Tribunal Temple. A word of advice: don't keep him waiting for long.
We'll start over. There has to be a way to acquire the power for the simulated sunlight without taking it from living beings.
This is Lector Naril, talking to you through this speaking tube.\n\nI had such high hopes for you, Sherizar. Why do you defy me?

Well, well … look at you, all full of fleshy-bits. Not a scrap of brass on you, is there? That won't do! That will not do!\n\nI can fix you up. No bother at all! Maybe new feet. You need new feet, don't you?
You shouldn't wander the Wellspring unsupervised. It's dangerous!\n\nThe factotums don't respond well to visitors they haven't been formulated to recognize. And the fabricants, they're just mean.

I just don't understand why my plants won't grow while Chirrhari and Ohtowen have no trouble making things bloom. It's an absolute annoyance!\n\nAnd so are those fabricants. Feel free to smash them to bits on your way through the garden.

Lector Naril's private workshop is restricted, but I don't expect you to find anything. If he catches you snooping around, feign ignorance and beg forgiveness. What's the worst he could do?\n\nHmm, I suppose he could turn you into plant food ….
It feels like I've been protecting this field for hundreds of years, but I'm certain I just entered this realm a day or so ago.

The Great Gear turns in my favor for a change! You have a perception tabulator. Did Adjunct Daro send you to find me? Of course he did!\n\nListen carefully and there might still be time to realign this befouled contraption.

I appreciate your assistance in the Pneumatic Forge, but for now our paths must diverge. The artifact we seek will not remain in one place for long—I can ill afford a delay.\n\nNavigate this absurd ritual. Quickly. I will find you again afterward.
Who are you? Another one of Vile's sniveling agents?\n\nGascone's gone. Now let me return to my mistress in peace ….
What're you doing nosing around here with that ugly beast? Joneif and I haven't done nothing!
Begone, whoever you are! I sealed the door, and it shall remain sealed for as long as necessary!
I know how this looks, but you have to understand. Those shadow cultists meant to slit my throat. I had to leave! My life was in danger, don't you see that?

Hold there, friend of Fyr. I am Proctor Luciana Pullo, of the Clockwork Apostles.\n\nI don't know how you and this egomaniac breached Lord Seht's celestiodrome, but I won't have non-citizens stirring up mischief in the Brass Fortress.
See them? Spirits lurking. Waiting. They mean to trap us in the Jarl's tomb, but what can we do?

Obviously, this mysterious key has to be our first priority. I don't know where it is, or what it does, but if Daedric Princes intend to mount an invasion over it, we can't afford to let it slip through our fingers.

It's so nice to see a familiar face!\n\nWelcome to my new abode. Not quite as impressive as my last one, I'm afraid, but it has its charms. You know, the apostles had quite a lot to say about Slag Town, but I've found very little of it to be true.
So we're citizens now, right? Finally.\n\nNow to find what passes for sujamma in this crazy place.
Still lingering? There's so much to explore! You should be on your way, don't you think?
So that's it? We're citizens now? Wonderful! I can't wait to get started on our next adventure!
If Baldan's thugs find out about this, they'll rust me for sure. Please, don't tell them we spoke.\n\nI hope you find your friend.
I don't know anything else. If you go down there, just be careful. There are worse things than leaky pipes down there. Trust me.
Be gone! This one has nothing else to say to you.

Come to gawk at the birds? Just keep those heels spring-loaded, friend.\n\nThe big one there nearly pecked an apostle's ear off. She said it was due for a replacement anyway, but even so … I'm sure it didn't tickle.
I thank you, walker. Lankin would not have lasted much longer in this dungy place. You will lead me out now, yes?

We have but one more task ahead.\n\nThe geodic dynamo that fuels the galvanic engine needs to be replaced. However, it's located in the regulation chamber … which is protected by a guardian factotum. You'll have to fend it off if I'm to make repairs.
This Raynor Vanos made some very bold claims. If you have evidence of Constable Baldan's crimes, I suggest you produce it.
Spy! Stay back or I'll—! Wait … I know you. The Duke's tall, fat-legged vassal from Crow's Wood! Ha!\n\nWell, we're not in Crow's Wood anymore, Featherless! Go look for shinies somewhere else!
Well? What are you waiting for, future citizen? Go speak to the Clockwork Registrar. I'll call on you again soon. Count on it.
The sequence plaques in your possession have no copies. Please return them to the archive.

Well. That was enlightening. To think, I've been speaking to Sotha Sil's shadow all this time. It seemed so lifelike. Far more advanced than my own, I'm sorry to say. Fascinating.\n\nIt really is too bad we'll all be dead soon.

Headed to Falkreath Hold? Wouldn't mind some well-armed company myself. Ugly rumors going about. Disappearances on the roads. Villages left burned, or abandoned. Hope my kin are safe ….\n\nJust hop in the cart if you're headed my way.
My feathers quiver with inspiration! Tell me, have you found a poem worthy of Lady Blightwing?
I have only a moment more. Even now, I fear we may be too late.

Hail, crow-friend. Yes, I remember you—the wingless bat-killer of Crow's Wood! How could I forget my tallest, clankiest vassal?\n\nI thank you for what you did for our gallant Knight of Marrow. Now, what boon do you seek from the Blackfeather Court?

Ha! Well struck, squire! The Exarchs are in full retreat! Look how they caw like chicks and empty their bowels! The time has come for a counter-attack!\n\nPrepare for your greatest challenge, crow-friend. The Motionless Guardian.
No need to dally, assistant. Just a few more adjustments and the lamp will be fully operational. \n\nYou should inform Lord Fyr of our success.
So Divayth Fyr requested this lamp personally? Fascinating.\n\nI read his thesis on Dwemeric power transmission as a child. First rate scholarship that. I'd love to meet him!
If a guard spots you, just find a basket or something to hide in. Trust me, that'll be a lot easier than trying to take on Sotha Sil's private army all by yourself.\n\nGood luck up there.
Best not keep Sil waiting. I doubt he'll remain here for long.
I don't know about you, but I've really worked up an appetite!\n\nYou know, I got so busy I completely forgot to make something for myself ….
Pleasure doing business with you, friend. Stay shiny, all right?
I'd love to have your business—I've got plenty of filaments. But I understand if you want to a take a more hands-on approach.\n\nSo, what's it going to be?
Ha! I'd pay good money to see the expression on <<1>>'s face when you threatened to set Lord Fyr on him! It feels good to see him brought down a few pegs. Thanks, friend.
You will respect our deal, yes? This one does not need scary wizards destroying his goods. You have your compressor—that is enough. Do not drag Na'jhargo's name through the tar.
Real food! Or near as I can tell, I don't care! Didn't think I'd ever come back for seconds down here.\n\nBren ever needs more of your help, count me in!
I swear, if I have to flip one more fetching switch for one more fetching meeting, I'm just going to exile myself.
So much work to do.\n\nJust keep our conversation to yourself, all right? Last thing I need is to get exiled for blasphemy.
Crank this … I've never had to do this much paperwork. And this isn't even the worst part!
I don't know what exactly we're up against, but it's sure to impress the enclave. Even Urgarlag.\n\nYou'd best take the lead. I'm a pledge-maker, not a pledge-taker.

I couldn't have faced this alone. I was lucky to have you along.\n\nCan you imagine the power Thurvokun must have possessed in life? I need to make sure no one else tries to harness the power in these remains.
Now, we must be cautious. Scalecaller has always been a place of danger, and this disease seems to have only further agitated the creatures that live here.

So that was a Dragon Priest? Terrifying! I don't believe she was even at her full power, which is a frightening thought.\n\nI think, with the aid of my research, I can finally put Zaan the Scalecaller to rest for good.
Warning. Situation critical. Daedric threat rating increased to severe.
First that bastard, Divayth, and now the crows? Your taste in companions grows worse by the hour.\n\nSorry. We're having a very bad day. You mean to enter the Machine District? Why?
No key? You'd best get back in there and settle this business with the crows. The cultists could strike at any moment.
Ode to a Brass Lilly still makes me weep every time I read it. I hope you enjoy it as much as I do.
I really need to get back to this theorem. Good luck finding whatever it is you're looking for.
Please claim your word-form at spool seventeen.\n\nGo forth, and create.

I must attend to the Planisphere. I have much to prepare, and for the first time within my memory I feel the weight of my hours.\n\nStill, you have done much for these sacred halls. What is it that you wish to ask?
Were you successful in your endeavor? I know Lector Trivura isn't always the easiest apostle to convince.
I hope your interaction with the deceased resident was illuminating, and that you found my assistance satisfactory.\n\nMay Sotha Sil bless your many labors.
Resident corpse, Gascone Dusant, memory outlay primed. Submit query.
Reflecting … reflecting ….\n\nOh, I feel positively spring-loaded now! What a kind, generous apostle you are. Which I recall is rather strange.
You risked much to rescue me and my notes. Thank you. Now at least we know a little more about that vile realm.
I will find my own way to Zanon's workshop. Go tell my student that I will arrive shortly.
I've never seen such a farce. What has happened to the state in intellectual curiosity in Clockwork City? I'm simply beside myself.
What's this all about? Why has Kamid called us together? I hope he didn't do something stupid because of his mother's death.

Thank you, my friend. My old bones aren't up to another adventure, but I owe it to Kamid's mother to do whatever I can to keep him safe.\n\nThe Grand Prognosticator spits out fortunes the way a sawmill spits out lumber—all the same until one isn't.
You want to help? I won't refuse—though I don't have anything to give you, if that's what you're after.\n\nThe Vale of Tiers lies to the southwest. If you really want to help, meet me there.
Where have you been? Is Raynor all right? I've been pacing around the Brass Fortress, worried sick and waiting for you to return!

I can't wait to give Kireth a piece of my mind—right after you talk to her. If she's still angry, you can calm her down a bit before I let her know what I really think. No reason for her to hit both of us, after all.
The Prognosticator refuses to talk to me. I request a fortune and receive only silence. Is that what my mother died for?

This one expected to find a way to return home in that cursed realm of shadow, but all Tadari found were creatures that annoyed her.\n\nStill, thank you for setting this one free. You have permission to do so again should the need arise.
<The factotum stands perfectly still, as if awaiting a command.>
These nix-hounds may be part machine, but they're all animal at heart. I care for them the best I can, and love them while they're living, but even I have to put food on the table.

I'll meet you back in Slag Town. We can talk to Palbatan and find out what he knows about the lost treasure.\n\nHe can also tell us about my mother's journal. I think I remember him mentioning Sotha Sil's honored assistant once or twice in the past.

By the word of Seht, I am bound.\n\nNo pronouncements can be furnished without proper statistics to analyze. Please provide the appropriate passphrase or present yourself to a Clockwork Apostle for immediate data collection.
Before you go, Kamid mentioned you found Maliah's journal. He said it contained a passphrase and mentioned Sotha Sil's honored assistant.\n\nIs that true?

I can't believe Palbatan revealed the location. Now we can show my people that the Prognosticator isn't infallible. That we can forge our own destinies.\n\nI'll meet you near the wrecked caravan and we can figure out how to deal with Gear Grinder.
Please, my friend. Return to the Brass Fortress and I'll meet you in Slag Town.\n\nWe'll settle our accounts there and you'll receive your share of the treasure.

I suppose I should get this over with. I just hope I can convince the people of Slag Town that the Prognosticator isn't infallible. We can forge our own futures, despite what some machine predicts with the help of statistics and calculations.

I'm so happy to see that Kamid and you made it back to Slag Town safe and sound. Were you successful? Did you find the—\n\nNo, no, don't tell me. I'll wait and see what Kamid has to say. It's all very exciting!
<Snuffler sniffs noisily.>

Sorry for the clandestine request, but I have words meant for your ears only.\n\nWhat you and Kamid learned, what he convinced Slag Town about the Grand Prognosticator? Well, it's not entirely … accurate.

The Asylum Sanctorium will remain closed for the time being, until I've safely secured the Saints' soul gems.\n\nI may open it to mortal patients again, now that I no longer need fear for their safety.
It's you. You were with Proctor Luciana.\n\nYou're not leaving her to deal with things alone down there are you?

Wonder if Jona will ever realize what's happened. Y'ffre knows she clings to me like a bur when Orinol is—well, was gone. Must be tough being a dog.\n\nDon't you worry though, I'll take care of her. To honor my cousin's memory, if nothing else.
<This brassilisk appears to have run out of power.>

The pipes that transport oil through the Brass Fortress must have some sort of automated system that turns them on and off. That's how Brassie got swept away. Now, if I can just figure out how they work ….

My clan will drink to your health tonight. We've all wanted to head back to gro-Morkul for years, but couldn't do so in honor without our clan's sword. Now we can, thanks to you.\n\nMay Mauloch keep your blade sharp, traveler!
<A glistening metal plate lies in the middle of the road.>
This one did not expect to taste such fine things again in her life. Tubabi will miss the moons a little less tonight.\n\nShe is grateful to Brengolin, and to you.

I'm so proud! I nearly retched just thinking about the last stew, but I held it together. Oh, and I'm glad I did! Brengolin really worked a miracle this time!\n\nWe might just be able to kick the paste after all!
Raz will report to the Queen while you tell the Psijics about Sea Sload and Daedric Princes. Jone and Jode, this one never expected to use such words in a sentence!\n\nGood luck, my friend.
Oracle Marieve appears shaken but otherwise in good health. Still, a visit to Oblivion can rattle even the strongest minds—especially if the trip isn't made of one's own accord.
I'll head out in a little while, after those creatures get bored and wander off.\n\nWhen you find Marieve, tell her that her sisters are worried and want to know that she's all right.
Vanus invited me to stay and rest for a time in this strange and wonderful city. It's much more crowded than I'm used to, but I think I'll take him up on his offer.\n\nAt least for a little while.
I—I can't breathe … I don't breathe. Instead, I whir and click. It's not so different.
By the word of Seht, I am bound.\n\nAwaiting task input. Vocal commands accepted. Please select command one, two, or three.

Made it, at last. At last! Well done, crow-friend. You move quickly for someone with stubby legs and no wings.\n\nNow, I will lock this gate with crow-magic. No one will follow you—I swear it on the Duke's fine plumage!
Yes, what is it? I have much to do. Much to attend to. Speak.
Have you come to gloat? To kick me while I wallow in my own misery? Well, go ahead. I deserve it.
I'm sorry. I can't talk to you right now. I have to—I just … excuse me, please.
I see the Queen's decree has even attracted some of our wayward brethren back to our shores. But make no mistake. Altmer or not, you're as much a newcomer as one of those cats or lizards.

Have you come to hear what the Kinlady has to say as well? I thought her open letter brilliantly captured the mood of Summerset's elite, but the Ascendants know the Queen has her supporters. Even here.

I took time out of my busy schedule to listen to the Kinlady's plan and what does she do? Walks away and leaves us waiting! Only a noble would be so rude.\n\nI hate it when issues remain unsettled. It's bad for business.

One thing you can say about Kinlady Avinisse—she knows how to cater an affair. Have you tried the golden pear punch? It's absolutely ambrosial!\n\nAs one Altmer to another, I can put up with her foibles as long as the drinks continue to flow.
Ah. You must be Lord Fyr's … associate. I'm afraid I can't be seen talking to an outsider. Appearances. I'm sure you understand.\n\nSo, yes … off you go.
Damn it, I wasn't fast enough!
Greetings, resident. Please maintain a safe distance. I am still determining the extent of Proctor Luciana's injuries.

Talk to Leythen. See if he'll be willing to provide us with the name of a priest of Meridia we can call upon. If he won't cooperate, perhaps you can goad him into revealing what we need.\n\nUnfortunately, that's the best idea I've got at the moment.

The next step involves a thorough examination of the strange pearl you and Valsirenn recovered from beneath the Shimmerene monastery. Hopefully, we can learn more about the false Aldarch and the source of the pearl's magic.

Only one of the lesser races would deface a beautiful wall like that. I mean no disrespect, but my statement rings true.\n\nRazum-dar claims the scribble contains a message of some sort, but I just don't see it.
Talk to Bailiff Roland. He apparently enjoys dealing with bothersome newcomers.

I will sign Emile's release papers immediately, but I will also insist on his exile from Summerset.\n\nThe Mages Guild can decide what they want to do to him once he leaves. The Sapiarchs will have nothing more to do with this amateurish farce.

You're doing the right thing. Emile will blame you for this, but I hope you'll forgive him. He suffered an unimaginable trauma. He's not in his right mind.\n\nHe'll recover, I know it. I'll be there for him. Calawende too. We'll get through this.

I know this wasn't easy. While I disagree with your decision, I understand why you made it. I only hope Emile and the Sapiarchs can look past this sordid affair.\n\nAt least Emile will go free. I hope he can make peace with that.

So Emile was innocent after all, yes? I knew something was off. Maybe the Sapiarchs will listen to me next time I find something odd.\n\nBut look at me … patting myself on the back. There are no winners here. Just victims. I need a drink.

Raz was planning to head up north to Eton Nir after talking to these Peryite imbeciles anyway. To check on his old friend.\n\nThe Court of Bedlam's attacks on the other cults were particularly vicious, and this one worries so.

Look Marthine! The sacred scribbles of Peryite have brought another aspirant to our holy fire!\n\nWould you like to hear about Peryite? He may be the Prince of plague and pestilence, but let me explain how that's a lot better than it sounds.
I told Filbert this was a mistake. Peryite protects us, but trying to proselytize on an island where Daedra worship is frowned upon was never a good idea in the first place.

This one deals with all kinds of problems for Queen Ayrenn, but this makes Raz's fur stand on end. Outlawed cults and Daedric Princes. How did Raz get his claws stuck in this particular ball of yarn?\n\nBut do not despair. Raz will be right behind you.

You'll find the shrine toward the back of the grotto. Meridia spreads life and light, but I hope you kill a few of those terrible creatures along the way.\n\nWe'll sneak around and meet you at the shrine. As long as Raz is with me, I should be safe.
He's gone, isn't he?

Emile will try to talk you out of revealing Haladan's plan to the Sapiarchs. He knows it would tarnish Haladan's legacy, and I know he wants to protect me. Don't listen.\n\nI can protect myself. Save Emile. That's what Haladan would want.
I can't stand seeing her like this. I always thought Luciana was, I don't know … indestructible. How could this happen?

Raz has seen many things. Weresharks. Flying tigers. Weresharks on top of flying tigers. But a talking light? Queen Ayrenn will never believe it!\n\nHow much trouble are we in, five-claw? Be honest with old Raz.
Our shrine desecrated, my Prince under attack … how can such things be allowed to happen?\n\nStill, Meridia spoke to you. Go find the Golden Knight and restore Dawnbreaker. They may be our only hope.

My followers murdered. My shrine desecrated. The other Princes, this so-called triad, they must answer for these insults.\n\nBut I sense a question in your mind. Speak, Champion of Coldharbour! Ask what you will of the Prince of Light!

Don't talk to me. Just don't. You had no right to insert yourself into this affair—no right to slander my beloved and undo all we struggled and sacrificed to accomplish.\n\nI will never forgive you for this. Never. Now, go.
<The telescope is set to view the platform's associated constellation. The empty points are where the corrupted stars should be.>
You return, but without the Dawnbreaker. Weren't you able to make contact with Meridia?\n\nForgive my impatience. This inability to remember has me on edge. Go on, tell me what you learned.
I hope your trip was successful. We could use some good news right about now.

My actions have weakened the Crystal Tower and endangered Summerset. I hate to think what else that foul creature forced me to do with its powerful mind magic.\n\nForgive my musings. I'll send word to Alinor so that the Proxy Queen knows to expect you.

It seems the Ritemaster prefers your company in this matter to mine.\n\nBe careful in there. If the yaghra made it onto Artaeum, I can't imagine that one or more of the Sea Sload will be very far behind.
Razum-dar has been investigating Daedric activity across Summerset. He's your best chance for finding a follower of Meridia, despite what Leythen has intimated.
Why must I always surround myself with soft-headed zealots? Why?\n\nOh come now, I don't mean you. I'm talking about Varuni. Pity. I really quite liked her before she started talking.
By the gears, this Divayth Fyr is just … insufferable! Honestly, how do you put up with it?
Go ahead. The Ritemaster is expecting you in the main gallery. I'll be along shortly.
Mmmm, yes? Do I know you?
I can open a portal to the Dreaming Cave, but the ritual will take time and will more than likely draw Mephala's Daedra.\n\nYou need to hold them off until I can find the way back home.
I promise I'll fix Dawnbreaker as soon as we get out of here. So, let's get out of here already.

I hoped you'd say that. I sent Oriandra to my study to review my memory and see if she could translate the ancient words. I even suggested a scholar she could contact. An expert in ancient languages and obscure dialects.\n\nGo. Check on her progress.
<Galidor's business ledger rests on the nightstand, protected by a powerful ward.>

I'll let the Ritemaster know what I proposed. He may not like it, but he's always telling us to utilize every available resource. I think this qualifies.\n\nYou'll find Leythen in Valsirenn's study. See if you can convince him to translate the words.
Be careful, cerum. I've never seen Glardir like this. I don't know what she's capable of.

I do understand how Larydel—Alchemy—doubted I would accept her desire to remain here, among this troupe she loves. Without you, we might never have spoken again.\n\nI haven't lost a brother. I've gained a sister. Thank you for ensuring I knew that.
Fixing the Dawnbreaker was surprisingly easy, by the way. Especially considering that I never repaired a Daedric artifact before.
Well, if it isn't my little sneak. Here to bother your old mentor? Not that I mind your company, of course.
Even as a soulless husk, the Dragon's bones hold formidable power. If Orryn's able to complete the reanimation … let's hurry!
What will we do now? Everyone saw our faces! We'll never be accepted into the troupe.
If I ever get my hands on that mage, I'll rip her to shreds! How dare she ruin our audition like that!
<This podium is used by the announcer.>
I … I'll have to petition the Grand Maestro! Yes, I must. There's no reason this should disqualify us from being selected. No reason at all!
Once again, you have my deepest thanks, ceruval. I don't know what I would have done if they'd taken my boy.
What happened? Where did she go?
Have a care up there on the surface, cerum. All those beautiful gardens and white stones hide a rotten core. Don't trust anyone but yourself.
There you are. I was beginning to worry that you had been swallowed by a salamander.\n\nYou retrieved the boy for us, I see. Well done.
Thanks for the help, friend. Eight only know what those long-leg guards would have done if Arathel killed the Sapiarch.\n\nYou're always welcome down here, all right?

I don't know what to say other than thank you. The Sapiarchs may expel me for all this, but that's something I can live with.\n\nPeople in high places don't have all the answers. The Mother of Rats taught me that. So did you.
What is going on? It was that book, Erudil was bragging about, wasn't it?
All my works and accomplishments finally reduced to dust and lost to time. I hope whatever comes after this life is not so pointless.
Not bad. Not so impressive as killing it the first time, but not bad. I'll make a toast to you when I tell my tale in the Hall of Valor.
Rancid bastard. One death is too kind for him. If I had any descendants, I'd haunt them until they emptied their coffers on resurrections and assassinations.

Now that the immediate danger's passed, Hy will want to get back to combing through the details of what transpired here. It'll be really boring—like, really boring—but since you got us back on speaking terms I'll help Lin and Hy investigate.
The Queen's Eye. How dare he not identify himself when he first arrived! And how dare he accuse my foolish son of something as serious as treason!\n\nThe Queen shall hear of this, mark my words!

I'm not good at apologies, but … I'm sorry for doubting you and Silurie. \n\nMaybe, just maybe, we were wrong to reject her choice to pursue foreign magic. While her methods are unorthodox, they get results.
Got nothing else for you, mate. I'd point you in the direction of some other haunted tomb, but mercifully I don't know any others. I hope to keep it that way.
Ah, you've arrived just in time to see me expose the pastry thief!

You broke more than a dozen statutes with your antics today. Regulations state that I should place you under arrest … but I'm thinking we haven't been following much procedure today anyway.\n\nThank you for your assistance in this investigation.
I'm free … finally. Wait, where am I?

I suppose I did succeed in this expedition. The notes you've given me are written by my hand after all. Though of course that me won't exist now, since you've stopped me, and—.\n\nAnd I'm going to stop now, before my head hurts.
All my classmates and professors are finally coming to their senses! Whatever you did appears to have worked.\n\nDid you really defeat this creature—the Illuminated One?
Damn Vinelore. I can't let her turn Lotus into some sort of monster. I have to find her.

Well, I suppose it's curtain call.\n\nYou've finally figured it out. Well, Andewen figured it out, didn't she? But hey, you put all the legwork in! And here you are, just in time to stop our leading lady from ever performing her starring role.

It appears you've saved Fletch from the brink of death. It brings to mind the story of Temarian, who of course was saved by the nereids of—.\n\nAh, but now is not the time for such tales. Tell me, what has happened?
Years and years, and I never could find you. And here you are, back where it all began. Looking as if you haven't aged a day.\n\nMy friend, what happened to you?
You're not to speak of this to anyone. I have good connections. I can destroy your reputation in Summerset with a word.\n\nNow, begone and let me rest. This armor is heavy.

Ha! I should have expected you to show up in Orsinium some day, given your thirst for adventure.\n\nThe Mages Guild here has made me feel quite welcome! I'm exploring mysteries and magics those short-sighted fools on Artaeum never dreamed of.

Yeah, all right, details. I can see how this might be a bit sketchy, but don't worry. The inn room is well-kept, conveniently located. \n\nI know you adventuring types, wanting a home in every town. This would be a nice addition to your holdings.

Your visage upon my canvas shall be viewed for centuries, I'm sure. Why, maybe one day it will be featured in a gallery with the Queen herself! \n\nIt's really very generous of me. You're quite welcome.
The day artists stop tromping out here to steal Summerset's rarest of plants is the day I'll retire. Sadly, it seems I won't be retiring any time soon.
My mistress doesn't explain herself to me, and she certainly won't explain herself to you.\n\nI assume, though, since the Heart was hidden by the Ritemaster, then only the Ritemaster can retrieve it.
Since you dealt with whatever Vaerelel planted on my land, my alavlin have been downright energetic. It'll take some time to restore their numbers, but they now seem quite eager for the task.
This wasn't my idea, honest! I just did what I was paid to. Just—let me go and I'll tell you everything.

Even in the middle of a forest, I still manage to hear about Tindoria and Vaerelel's little tiffs. And no, I don't want to hear about whatever silly thing happened. I moved here to get away from such nonsense.

Ah, what shall I paint, what shall I paint? Oh, I'm just giddy. So many possibilities, and now I have just the supplies I need to make my newest masterpiece.\n\nHa! I can't wait to see the look on Tindoria's face when she realizes what happened.
I have a lot to answer for. Justice will be done.\n\nThank you for allowing me to reclaim what little honor I had left before I face my judgment.

No matter whether Nocturnal's earl spoke truth or lies, we need to recover the Heart of Transparent Law. I'm sure I hid it somewhere beyond the Daedric barrier.\n\nWas there anything else before you go and check on Darien?
The Ritemaster plans to lead this expedition personally. I'm glad to have him along, but I'm concerned whenever he puts himself at risk.
I'm getting sick and tired of barriers and Daedric interference and … well, Daedra in general.\n\nTalk to the Ritemaster and let's get this started already.

Urlsar's dead and his mutiny along with him. I only wish I had the strength to settle the score myself. If there was any justice in the world he'd have been forced to concede that he'd never drown me in shame. I'll return home with my head held high.

We're as prepared as we can be without knowing exactly where this pathway leads. I've even set wards that will help protect me from the Daedric Princes.\n\nRemember, though, our primary goal is to recover the Heart of Transparent Law.
I remember the words, but I don't know exactly what they mean. Once I begin the spell, be ready for anything.
I just want to find the Heart and get out of this dreadful realm.
This must be the place. I wonder where the old man hid the tower crystal?
These ancient vaults house relics of great power and unusual nature. I sense … yes, K'Tora is here. Be on your guard, friend of Valsirenn.
We'll take things from here. It will take time to restore Sea Keep's strategic viability, but we'll make sure it continues to stand guard over our shores.
Once again, admanen, you have my thanks.\n\nFarewell.
Ah! You come to babble with Babblebrook? When came the killers, I had a look!
We're running out of time. Whatever the Sea Sload searches for in the Ritemaster's mind, I believe it is close to finding it.\n\nHave you brought me the Ul'vor Staff?
What do you want? The revelators already questioned me and cut me loose. I just want to be here if something exciting happens.

It really is too bad about Halimorion. I told him he shouldn't be so free with his politics. It's a different climate now, after all. You have to watch what you say around people.\n\nOn the upside, it's good to be rid of a rival vintner.
Sorry, I didn't really see what happened so I don't think I can help you.

Thank you for informing me about the Augur's whereabouts. I will update our arcane manifest at once.\n\nYou know, despite her many shortcomings, I think Josajeh will be an excellent caretaker. Time will tell, I suppose.
Leave me alone! I can't … just get away from me!

The Crystal Tower exists on multiple planes of reality simultaneously and possesses capabilities we do not fully understand. We must assume that Nocturnal's options are infinite.\n\nI suggest you find Valsirenn and inform her of this development.
Don't worry about me. I'll be fine. Go on ahead and speak to Lorne back at the winery.\n\nBesides, someone will have to help the chief recover his son's body.
You have given me much to consider before I can determine the path ahead of us.\n\nFor now, check on the Ritemaster. Valsirenn took him to Ceporah Tower to utilize the services of the Psijic healers.

The two ogres ahead seem to be the clan leaders. We'll need to defeat them in order to continue on. No easy task, I'm sure. They look to be formidable foes.\n\nI'd advise you to keep your distance, if possible. I'd hate for anyone to become infected.
What … what's happening? Am I …?

You'll find Sotha Sil in his study on the upper levels of Ceporah Tower.\n\nIn the meantime, I'll make sure Valsirenn and the Golden Knight see the Psijic healers. I think we'll need them at their best before too long.

Why are the Daedric Princes always so aloof and ominous? Would it be asking too much to just get a straight answer out of them once in a while?\n\nAh, well. I'll make sure Leythen gets back to Artaeum and meet you there.
It took awhile but the way is open now. Of course, I'm a little concerned about how long it took me to unlock the door.

Sotha Sil waits for you in his study. Tell him about the alliance with the Daedric Princes and ask him if he knows what we can expect to face inside the Crystal Tower.\n\nI'll wait for Darien and Leythen to return.
It was a close call with this mess. Lucky for me you showed up.

Raz will meet you in Alinor. This one and the Proxy Queen have known each other a long time. She loves me like a brother. Of course, she hates her actual brothers, so what does Raz know?\n\nRaz just hopes the Psijic can do what she claims.
I only ask that you do what's right. I have paid my debt to the Direnni, many times over. Please … just let me go.

Thanks so much for the rescue!\n\nI'm Erilthel, the muscle of this operation. Oh, I suppose Seeks already told you that though, didn't he? I'm sure he's bragged all about me and how great of an apprentice I am, the big softy.

I think I'll wait here. Vile let some of his more ferocious minions loose in the cave, and sometimes they don't differentiate between friend and food.\n\nTry not to get killed before you hear what my master has to offer.
<<1>> won't talk to us until this important meeting about the recent events in Summerset is finished.\n\nRigurt hates having to wait around with the twiddling toes and the tapping thumbs!

I couldn't possibly speak to you until the important council meeting has wrapped up. I'm completely inundated with the business of Summerset until the meeting comes to an end.\n\nCome back later and we can conclude our business then.

While Her Majesty conducts the business of the Dominion in distant locations, I abide here to make sure the machinations of government continue to run smoothly.\n\nIf there's something you need, please talk to one of my aids or courtiers.
I hope you aren't here about anything important. My schedule is completely full. I couldn't possibly squeeze you in before the Mid Year Mudcrab Festival.
Why does my muse elude me? I can't channel my inner Nord. If this Ambassador Rigurt can't aid me, I'm afraid we'll have to cancel tonight's performance.
Sometimes I wish the criminals and law-breakers would take a holiday. Then the officers of the Divine Prosecution could catch up on our paperwork.\n\nIs there something you need, newcomer?
You know, perhaps I'll hire Manacar as my bodyguard. The art world can be quite cut-throat in Summerset, and it's not unheard of to face a few dangers.\n\nYes, that sounds just perfect.
Artists these days, who knows what they're thinking. Still, I suppose I can humor her for a little while longer. She did go through all the trouble to meet with me.
Keep Vinelore distracted. I've got an idea.

Ah, so it seems I shall remain with Tableau after all.\n\nI'm sorry you had to get mixed up in this mess, but thank you for helping me see reason. And have no worries, I'll make sure that Tableau ends up all right.
All I have to do is become such a great artist that no one will dare question my relationship with Manacar. And how could I not succeed, with such a motivation?

For such an outstanding artist, Tableau certainly seems to have a wide variety of friends. Stars forbid these attachments get in the way of her debut.\n\nKeeping her stage name is one thing. Her disreputable associates? Quite another.
Great! I'm getting out of here while I still can. If you want to talk, find Mehdze. Good luck getting a word in.
Now, to cherry-pick some nuggets of truth for authenticity, or start from whole cloth without any pesky constraints?

If the Ritemaster of the Psijic Order believes the Crystal Tower may be in some sort of trouble, you must make haste to the College of Sapiarchs. Seek the portal master in Lillandril.\n\nNow go. We have no more time to spare for a newcomer today.
This … this is an abomination. A travesty! Attacking the Sapiarchs? Daedra in the College? It's … highly unusual!\n\nI can't stay here. It's too dangerous!

This is terrible! Please excuse my present state, as I am distraught beyond all rational thought. I never imagined that Daedra would attack our compound. It's madness!\n\nForgive my lapse in protocol. I am Ellimil, Sapiarch of Daedric Fallacies.
Zan'hi does not wish to fight you, walker, but he will if he must.\n\nYou will speak your business, yes?

Upstairs you'll find a key. With it, your Psijic friends can get you to my realm, where I can direct you to the Crystal Tower.\n\nGetting inside, though. For that, you'll need the Resolute Diamonds. Unfortunately, I can't help you with that.
Don't worry about me. I have my husband well in hand.\n\nFind the tower sentinels and we'll meet back in Artaeum. By then the Ritemaster will have a plan in place on how to restore the Crystal Tower.

I'm not sure what I expected when I decided to journey to Summerset, but it sure wasn't this. No rest for the weary and always more work to do.\n\nForgive my lack of manners. Is there something you need?
Not now, friend. I haven't been able to secure work in this city and I fear instead of opportunity, this land of High Elves holds nothing but disappointment for newcomers such as me.
Does this one regret leaving Elsweyr and making the journey to Summerset? No. For Jone and Jode watch over me and bless me with health and good fortune!\n\nHow can Urjurra help you, friend?
Try something rash and Talomar will sprout an arrow from the eye. You've all caused me enough trouble for one day.

The Illumination Academy lies to the east of Lillandril. That's the last known location of the tower sentinels, Hannayel and Imedril. May the eleven virtues of knowledge grant you the speed to reach them before the Court of Bedlam does.
My Mistress will help you. You just need to be patient.\n\nAs for me, I'll return to Artaeum and accept whatever consequences await me. You have my word.
Let's go. We can contact Mephala as soon as we reach my private chamber.

Watch your back. I trust Leythen. Sort of. But you can never tell with the servants of Daedric Princes. Well, except for me. I'm nothing like those people.\n\nAnyway, I'll meet you in the back chambers.
So, the mortal who opposed me wants to speak. If what you say doesn't interest me, I will order Leythen to kill you.
Who would have thought such things possible? A talking dog!\n\nTread carefully, my friend. Raz smells a trap. Or maybe that's just poo.

This one will watch over the pretty Sapiarch and return her to the compound in Lillandril. You should go and find the other one. Ruins tend to be so dusty, and Raz hates to get specks in his nose and fur.\n\nSafe travels, five-claw!
Sorry. They usually let me know when new academics are going to arrive. I'm sure I can find a way to squeeze you in someplace. How long do you plan on staying?
One Daedric scheme fails, even as two more appear to take its place. Such is the way of Oblivion.
Are you sure this Khajiit is trustworthy? I've read "The Adventures of Kazurr Graystripes," you know. He was such a scoundrel!
The spider poison … it's spreading fast. Take this … Resolute Diamond. Don't let the Golden Knight's sacrifice … be in vain ….
Don't worry about me. I may not be fit enough to fight, but I can still walk. I'll head to the closest town and make my report. Just need a moment to catch my breath first.
I can hardly believe it. You found Henrigg and Mindoril! But, where are the others?

Finally this ordeal is over. I'm just glad to be rid of Eslion. Fixing all the damage he caused will leave me little time to dwell on the outcome of his trial, but I hope they plant him where the sun doesn't shine.
You really stuck your neck out for me today, and I don't even know your name—not that I'd remember. I'll never forget what you've done for me though.
I'll stay with these people a while longer, if they'll have me. Best to stick together, and perhaps my standing will shield them from the intolerance my kind have for nebarra.
Let's just hope my betrothed has learned a lesson from all of this. It certainly doesn't pay to go running off with the first vagabond who shows interest.
I'll trust you to keep my little secret. And who knows? Maybe we'll see each other again, somewhere deep within the woods.
Your help has been invaluable. I will never forget the service you have provided, both for these poor adventurers and for me.
I hoped we'd cross paths again, friend. Come, raise a toast with us to Cartorrel. You never knew her, but she'd have welcomed you with open arms.
Ugh, gods, that was … I could feel my skin tightening as that stone drew the moisture out of me like a wineskin. \n\nI don't suppose you have water? My tongue is a whetstone.

He's not fooling me. I can tell something happened. Father's putting on a brave face like he used to whenever I'd ask him about his younger days. He'd smile and deflect the question, but I could see a sadness in his eyes he couldn't hide. His secret.
You want to talk? Now? Looks to me like you've still got a fight to handle.
I don't think now's the time for a chat.

This shrine, Val and I built it for our daughter after she died. High Elves don't bury their dead, but we needed something to remember her by. She loved climbing this tree before the illness took her.\n\nI forgot how beautiful it was.

Sotha Sil needs Oriandra and me to help him maintain the connection from this end. But Leythen once wore the gray robes of the Psijic Order. He'll help you in there.\n\nJust … just try to bring everyone back after you deal with Nocturnal.

I can't recall a time where the Psijic Order confronted a threat such as this. We've dealt with all sorts of problems and cataclysmic events, but this is … different.\n\nI think … I think the Ritemaster would be proud.

Raz never had the urge to travel to Oblivion or visit a magically displaced island, but now Raz feels like the cat who caught the farmer's prized turkey!\n\nIt is good to see you safe, my friend. Now, tell Raz you have a way to save Summerset.
There we are. Much better, yes? Manners are easily forgotten when you're so far removed from society.\n\nForgive the others. They are frightened. We mean you no harm.
I was so close. Spellbreaker was right here, waiting for me to just take it. How could I have let it slip through my fingers?

It's not everyday I see someone take out a Dragon Priest. I would have put good gold on you losing, honestly. Glad to see you prove me wrong.\n\nIt's funny. You did most of the work, but I still need a drink.
I brought Leythen back and what does Valsirenn do? Sends me off without a word or a thank you.\n\nSo when do we head out to assault the Crystal Tower? No one tells me anything around here.
What're we waiting for? Let's get this fight started!
Honor and praise, cerum. Can I help you with something?
Ah, a thousand greetings, honored patron! What a delight! A High Elf deigns to speak with humble Nahdahni! Moons be praised!\n\nHow can this one serve you, noble-walker?
Fairly met, newcomer.\n\nWait, you're the one who was harassing Lirendel earlier. Hmph. I presume you've come to talk about this business with the Orc?

You are strangely consequential, for a mortal. In my calculations, I somehow overlooked your significance. And yet, that has worked to my advantage, for now we have a chance to thwart Nocturnal. And that will be something to savor.
Get us out of here! They're killing us!
With the Maormer down and Admiral Viscarne defeated, I'm sure my citizens will join together and fight. All we have to do is keep Sunhold standing until help arrives.

Nocturnal dares much, attacking my master's realm!\n\nBut here you are, safe and sound. The Crystal Tower. At least, it's the version that exists in the Fields of Regret. Now I really need to get back to barking and biting Nocturnal's minions.
I can't save Kinlady Helenaere with these wounds. It's up to you now.
Please … before I am lost … tell me. What happened? I deserve to know why the tower has done this.
I really must get back to work now. Every moment that my cousin remains sequestered is another moment where I must perform the work of two people. Pleasant travels, wayfarer.

<This scroll contains instructions for a ritual to activate further defenses at the mountain peak. It appears Zaan was unable to finish it before you arrived.\n\nThe final step appears simple enough…>

Not that you'd understand the concept, but the Path to Alaxon requires dedication and complete concentration. I must find the perfect shells or my pigments will be substandard. And do you know what that will do to my art?\n\nExactly!

I was overconfident, I'm afraid. Valsirenn always said I was too sure of my own abilities. I just assumed I'd be able to get back to the protection of the Resolute Anchor before I was unmade.\n\nPity. I would have preferred a more heroic ending.

Transparent Law, it's whole again! I didn't think that was possible. And you stopped Nocturnal. You're back upon Summerset, my friend. The tower itself—it reformed!\n\nBut … but where's Darien … and Leythen …?
Nocturnal's earl was wrong. Meridia's power, it's not gone. Her magic remains strong and vibrant.\n\nThe vessel. The last Light of Meridia … it's me.
Mmm! Just look at these tasty piggies!
Squee! Oink oink oink!
Oink oink!
Not now, please. Your spiritual well being can wait until after my nap.

I believe there's a certain Khajiit who wishes to speak to you. Go on and make sure he hasn't gotten himself into any trouble.\n\nAnd just know, the Psijic Order will always consider you an ally and friend. As will I.
Thank you for helping Renzir see reason. How could he be so blind to Nubani's suffering?

If you're not willing to help, this one suggests you leave. There are darker forces in this cave than mutinying smugglers. Nubani will sail out of Karnwasten as soon as she can.\n\nAnd let Renzir know she will find him soon.

It's good to see you alive and well. Word has already spread about your daring exploits within the Crystal Tower. It's still a little hard to believe, truth be told.\n\nOf course, there's so much left to do. I already have a list as long as my arm.

The time has come for my departure. I've always felt a sense of peace in Artaeum, but also … discomfort. A consistent dilemma within me, which seems to have only grown.\n\nI'll be glad to get back to the Clockwork City. There's much to do.

I … apologize for my assumptions. It's clear you've done much good for Summerset and its people.\n\nThe protection of the Crystal Tower has been the Sapiarch's duty for time immemorial. To change that now feels like we've failed.
We deal with Razum-dar out of respect for our dear cousin, but some days … some days are more trying than others.
Not now, my friend. I just want to grieve for the Ritemaster and maybe drown my sorrows in a bottle or two of pale wine.
I can't believe Nocturnal took my damn sword! And she corrupted it. How is that even possible?\n\nLet me know when you have a plan, because I really want to hit something right about now.

As a member of the Psijic Order, I've counseled with Daedra in the past. But to trust one enough to form an alliance is almost unheard of!\n\nI'll leave it to Valsirenn and the rest of the Conclave to determine the wisdom of such a risky course.
If you're here about the Crystal Tower, too, I'll tell you what I told the Khajiit. Climb the watchtower. You'll get a better view from up there.

The Sapiarchs are in the middle of a very delicate operation up at the Crystal Tower Gatehouse. I probably couldn't stop you, but I'm supposed to do my best to discourage any visitor to the area right now.

The Crystal Tower just started glowing. It's never done that before.\n\nWe thought our ritual of attunement might have caused a reaction, but the Sapiarch of Arcanology says this is something totally different.
The Golden Knight has taken matters into his own hands! He set Leythen free and returned with him to Summerset.
Please help us!
The Battlereeve will receive you in Alinor's Royal Palace.\n\nI do suggest you make all possible haste.
These geysers … while the magic definitely intrigues me, I'd prefer it if Summerset doesn't sink beneath the sea.
Sorry I was such an arse down in Karnwasten, but getting offered to a Sea Sload makes me kind of crazy.\n\nThanks for rescuing me, though.
Thank you for retrieving Indirim's report and getting it to the Battlereeve. I would have hated for the marines to have died in vain.

Hail, weary traveler! Seek ye the torchlit halls of Sovngarde? You will not find them here, alas! Naught but puny Elves and snow-backed wizards dwell in this place!\n\nI am bound for the Whale Bone Bridge, and Tsun's mighty challenge! Join me!

As the Wood Elves say, good hunting! I'm certain the three of you will settle this business quickly. \n\nJust keep your head and stay watchful. The Ghost of the Green has a way of sneaking up on people.
These decks need swabbin'! Get to it!
Welcome aboard, sailor!
Shh! I think I saw something moving out there in the snow!
Did you hear that? Something moving just beyond the light of the campfire. By the Divines, its cold out here!
There, across the waves! Do you see them? Ships! Dozens of them heading toward us. \n\nGird yourself, soldier!
Who are you? Come to jump too? Well, you'll have to wait. My little friend here is just about to take the plunge!
Go speak to Farowel and Tanorian. They can set you up with contracts and get you right to work.
Investigator Vale was wrong? But that means … oh dear. You mean I'm not a daring pirate queen after all? Damn it all.
Investigator Vale was wrong. So that means … oh, thank the Eight! I couldn't take another minute of being a mopey king! Bless you, my friend! Bless you!
Beware the temptations of power, initiate. Countless mages have fallen prey to the allure of legendary artifacts like these fragments.\n\nIn all things, seek peace, simplicity, and detachment.

Haven't you left yet? Don't you have an island full of Altmer to search?\n\nGood luck with that, by the way. I've always said, the Court of Bedlam is too efficient for its own good. Meridia's lackeys were probably wiped out to the last cultist.
Thank the Divines! You aren't one of the monks. Please, let me out of here!
Ah, you've arrived at last. Come, join me.\n\nI assume that my friend in the Divine Prosecution, Justiciar Tanorian, provided you with the details? Or, I should say, the details he was privy to.
Well, go on. Someone needs to talk some sense into that woman before she causes even more problems.
Honestly, why can't you newcomers just return to your own lands? Weren't you happier there?

So you're Manacar's new friend, huh? How touching.\n\nHe's filled me in on all the details. Just know, I had no idea who the Blackbirds were targeting when I agreed to be their fence. Not that I'm pleased about ratting them out.

Slek, my head hasn't hurt this bad since … well, actually, not that long ago. Perhaps my cousin's wedding last month? But then there was that little get together last week ….\n\nNever mind all that. Have you the bottles?
Pardon me, but I'd rather be left alone right now. I'm dealing with a rather personal loss, and not in the mood for conversation.
How healthy you look. I barely remember the feeling of … anything, really, aside from the slight ebb and flow of sluggish blood in and out of brittle veins.

Our trip into the cursed wood wasn't a total failure. I had a brief moment to examine the inscription before Nocturnal's earl usurped our connection.\n\nI think I know what some of the words from the Ritemaster's memory mean.
I just lost my boy! Leave me be!

For what reason do you barge into our home as if you have the right to trespass our lands as you please? You may believe our condition diminishes our station, but we are the rightful rulers of Corgrad. You will offer deference as such.
Come, speak, I have not had civil company in some time. \n\nYou arrive upon a momentous reunion of our filial blood. The day we have so long waited for.
Soon this misery will finally be at an end. I thought this day would never come.\n\nI thought I would go mad.
I'm not paid to talk. Find conversation somewhere else.
The Green Pact makes this work complicated, but a job's a job. I'm sure Y'ffre will forgive me eventually.
Don't sneak up on me! That ghoulish business with the vintner has everyone on edge.
How can such a terrible thing happen in such a beautiful place? I thought this business with the Ghost was all behind us.
Watching these Wood Elves tend grapes is like watching a mother pig suckle her young—both adorable and mildly repulsive at the same time.
Hm. A curious intersection of circumference and crenellation. The height of the brow, the inflection of the temple …. An altogether auspicious arrangement!
I can't believe Nocturnal's earl interfered like that. We're supposed to be allies! Why would she want to stop me from reading that ancient inscription?
A pleasure to work with you on this particular adventure! You have my thanks for what you did for Grog and Miriya. And for saving Oriandra.
Crazy bastard … stabbed me. Gods … this hurts!
It'll never be the same without Cartorrel. She had such a bright personality you could navigate by it. I can't imagine what Wendlain is going through ….
It still hasn't sunk in … what happened. Cartorrel's really gone. \n\nWe all could have died if you and Curtaros hadn't swept in like a fair wind and ferried us to safety.
We consider this matter resolved. You may go as you please.

The Psijic went out of her way to help us. To save us from the mind trap. I'd go with you if I could, but Cainar can only send one of us into that awful place.\n\nMay the blood of your ancestors keep you safe.

You are now free to accept jewelry crafting writs.\n\nBe advised that while the jewelry you create may be beautiful, you'll need to conduct further research if you wish to add the traits most adventurers seek.
Feel free to take a look at my goods. Hopefully something here can help you beat back the shadows.
I may be injured, but my shop is still open. Perhaps it will do you some good, in such troubling times.
If you find my companions, let them know to meet me by the wayshrine, right down the road. And don't worry, I won't run off before you get your reward.
If you're looking for a reward or something, go talk to Miranrel. She's the one who promised you something, right?
Give me a moment. I haven't entirely caught my breath yet.

I feel different. Wait, did I—? I said some terribly improper things, didn't I? Oh … oh, I am so sorry! Please believe me, I'm normally meek as a newborn turtle.\n\nIt's just these romance novels, you see? I … oh, you get the idea.
Right. So, should we get going, or …?
Oh, my dear Eustasia! Look at her shaking. She's positively terrified! What happened?
You heard her. Take your business elsewhere.
Our business is concluded. Good day, citizen.
You induced one of my assistants to leave? How dare you! The sheer presumptuousness of your actions is just—gah! I can't believe this.
Ha! Glad to see someone put the Sapiarch in his place. Ancestors know I could never do it!
She ran off? Then—then that means I'm head assistant! I knew my hard work would pay off one day.

Very well. Our first priority is to those trapped within this prison. Distract the guards while I free them.\n\nShould we successfully escape, we'll head to the gardens next. There, I'll need you to collect any wolfsbane flowers you may find.
You've done what my order could not. Vykosa has fallen, and Tamriel is safe from her malicious intent. The Moon Hunter Pack shall be no more.

<This scroll bears the insignia of the Undaunted and a potent spell, conceived of by the renowned Hroltar the Boaster. When invoked the scroll will empower one's enemies with astonishing power.\n\nThe full incantation isn't short on colorful language.>
Well, isn't this just lovely? Yet another team to compete against!\n\nI'll never get Tarcyr's heart at this rate. I can't believe I came all the way to Hircine's cursed Hunting Grounds for nothing.

Go ahead. Say it. I'm a s'wit, aren't I?\n\nFather tried to warn me, and I just didn't listen. And now here I am, trapped within this cursed realm … or trapped with the guilt of condemning my father to such a fate.

<Balorgh has erected a banner to proclaim victory for his pack. Destroying it will send him into a fury.\n\nAny boons granted from the Golden Indrik Hunts will also be removed from all players for the duration of the fight.>
Please excuse me, but I was rather hoping to finish this next chapter of my book. I hope you understand.
Glad the horse is all right. Though knowing its owner, I don't know how long that'll be the case.
You found my dear, sweet horse! You have my thanks.\n\nAs for the Orc? Bygones, bygones to all of it, stranger. We all have our ways to go.
I suppose that's why Gjadil gave up a life of piracy. She decided a loving family was more important than riches or treasure.\n\nWhat an idiot.
I can't believe I ever looked up to this loony crone. To think she would trick us all, just for some stupid moral lesson!\n\nI just hope such lunacy doesn't run in the family.
To think that Gjadil planned for this outcome from the very start. Who knew the old girl had such a flair for the dramatic? I wonder if she ever thought of joining the theater.

It was a hard battle, but Z'Maja has been defeated. \n\nWe may not have been able to save Cloudrest, but there was no telling what devastation she had planned for the rest of Summerset. You've done this Isle a great service.
Thank you for saving my city. I may be a newcomer, but I've truly grown to love Cloudrest over these past few months. It pains me to see it in this state.

I heard you were able to defeat Z'Maja! I can hardly believe it.\n\nHopefully Cloudrest will stay safe after all that happened. My mother insists she remains. Wants to help rebuild what's left of the rubble.
Kindness glows within you, shining and resplendent. This one sees it. Perhaps you would help a poor Khajiit?
I don't care who's protecting her. She's not going to get away without facing justice. Not this time.
Hey! The whole gang's here! You're just in time to see me off. I was just wrapping up my goodbyes with my favorite Bailiff.
I'm astonished the hulkynd refused to complete this task himself. I'm sure honest work isn't easy to come by for one of his … status.
Did you truly defeat that nasty Sea Sload? Simply marvelous! I shall compose a piece to commemorate your victory.
So you've defeated Z'Maja once and for all, I hear? Good. \n\nNow Cloudrest can finally start to heal. Of course, I'm not going anywhere. There's always a need for a healer on hand.
Do our ancestors still smile upon us? Now that our borders have been taken? Now that we've tainted our homeland with unworthy souls?\n\nAre we still worthy of Summerset …?
Before you ask, the gates of Cloudrest are still barred from visitors. The city is currently being rebuilt. Only those authorized to help with construction efforts can enter.
You're the one who found Cartorrel, aren't you?
To be attacked in our own college! I always thought this was the safest place in the world.\n\nHow will I ever feel secure enough to lose myself in my books and research again?
You come in peace, yes? If not, my Zan'hi will claw you to ribbons!
Old Ways protect you, initiate. Those swamps look very forbidding—but I'm sure it's nothing you haven't faced before.

Well, I guess this is goodbye.\n\nI appreciate you coming to see me off. Thank you … for everything. I deserve this exile, but I don't think I will ever deserve a friend like you. Take care of the Order for me, all right?

Congratulations, ceruval. You now possess all the rights and privileges afforded to members of our order.\n\nContinue your studies, use these powers for the good of all, and you will make this humble teacher very proud indeed.

I will surrender myself to the Psijic Order and face my punishment. Without your intervention, I shudder to think what my recklessness could have done to the fabric of time.\n\nI know you don't want to hear this, but … thank you.
I'll soon be heading back to my homeland of Summerset. Are you interested in passage? We've room for more.

Feels good to have the old flame back again!\n\nI have to say, it feels strange talking to someone I know could kick my arse in a fight, even if it was my shadow self. Just know you're one of a very few, my friend!
Z'Maja is defeated, and the Welkynar are whole once more! Never has there been a greater cause to rejoice. \n\nMy friend, your name shall forever be honored. I swear by the Stars!

I must say, your victory flies in the face of all logic. Never before have I seen a warrior succeed after facing such great odds against them.\n\nStill, if it wasn't for your recklessness, my order may have been no more. Thank you.

I'm surprised you've returned after what transpired. \n\nYes, I know all about your little production. Luckily for you, Alchemy has vouched for your goodwill. It is by her wish alone that I welcome you to the Manor of Masques.

Honor and praise! I'm glad the Stars saw fit to see our paths cross again, my friend.\n\nCloudrest's recovery has been going smoothly, with the help of my order. It'll take time, but I can already see my city coming alive once more.
Who knows? Maybe they'll actually bring you on. That land-owner's an odd one. Of course, hunting down wild-eyed murderers isn't exactly my idea of fun. \n\nAll risk, no alcohol.
You may have an invitation, but your attire is not appropriate for meeting with the Kinlady. In fact, if you don't mind my saying so, you smell a bit … ripe. And not in a good way.
So, five-claw, what sort of reward would be suitable for this occasion?
Please, you must help! I think my cousin Brengas has been captured by werewolves.
You can find the Ritemaster in his study in Ceporah Tower. Go to him and see what you can do to help him remember where he hid the Heart of Transparent Law.

You'll find Sotha Sil in his study on the upper levels of Ceporah Tower.\n\nMeanwhile, I'll go and check in on the Psijic healers and see how Valsirenn and the Golden Knight are doing. I expect we'll need them at their best before too long.

First the Queen issues a decree that changes the status of Summerset from an isolated paradise into a … a tourist attraction! Now monsters! Sea creatures! I've never seen anything like them!\n\nWell, I say let the cat fight them! Better him than me!
I delivered my message so do stop pestering me. I've got one-hundred-and-three unique forms and principles running through my head. If I stop to talk now, hours of work will be lost.
Greetings, my friend. I'm afraid I come with a matter of urgency. \n\nYour presence is needed once more on Artaeum. Hopefully, this shall be our last ordeal to ensure Summerset's prosperity.

Look how the pearls shimmer with dark energy. Isn't it beautiful?\n\nMy Mistress offers a small mercy. Allow her to finish her work and she'll make the deaths of the Psijics fast and painless. But if you interfere, you will all suffer before you die.
So … are we setting out, or should I find a book to read?
You came to visit, just as I hoped. It's good to see you again, my friend.\n\nIt's been quiet here on Artaeum. I've actually had time to breathe, for once. And of course, time to mourn.

I never knew how many curiosities Sotha Sil had hidden away in his study.\n\nIt'll take some time to sort through it all, but it's well worth the effort. These devices could be very useful to the Psijic Order's current research.
And so we meet again, on Artaeum, my home. I knew you would find your way here eventually. Yours is a will not easily constrained.
Thank you for listening, cerum. You'll find the old Psijic Vault on the west side of the island, up against the cliffs. Please, just don't let Ulliceta do anything she'll regret.
Hey, what's this I hear about you smiting Daedric Princes! Here I show you a few tricks of the trade and you go and show me up.\n\nWas it fun? I bet it was fun. Terrifying, but fun.
I did say that we'd only arrive in time to clean up the mess, didn't I? If it means a safer Summerset for all of us, then I'm honored to have played my part. However small.
So you really were an investigator for the Proxy Queen? Or are you an Eye of the Queen? A Psijic? I'm so confused. I could have sworn those papers were forged.
I recognize you. You were the toady Llonas hired to buy me from his mother. I suppose I should be thanking you, even if you didn't intend for me to gain my freedom.
When they say the first step of the journey is the hardest, they weren't kidding. Phynaster, show mercy.
That's the only message I have for you. I'm sure the Relicmaster will be able to tell you more.
Turn back to where you came, stranger, unless you want to vanish like the rest.

What? Sotha Sil let me in. How else am I supposed to lead you through the Fields of Regret and to the Crystal Tower?\n\nNow could we hurry this up, please? Nocturnal's not going to wait forever to tear reality apart, you know.
This winery keeps drawing tourists for all the wrong reasons …. On your way, newcomer.
Join up! See all of Summerset! Never pictured all of Summerset being some bleak, haunted ruin. By Auri-El, I can't wait to be reassigned.
Eldellar insists we can learn something from these arcane skirmishes, but summoning up creatures like this does not put me at ease.
Mind your step, cerum. Eldellar's summoning displays can be … energetic.
You didn't speak to me while whatever was happening was happening, did you? Gracious. I think I was … inebriated! Scandalous!\n\nLook, this isn't even alcoholic!
Welcome to Artaeum, traveler.\n\nI know it can all be a lot to take in at first, so please feel free to ask me any questions. I have quite an extensive knowledge of this island's history.
The last visitor to come to Artaeum compared us to the Mages Guild. A distressing comparison to be sure.
A pox on the traitor's house. I hope Pandermalion rots for the rest of his days.
<No new Conquest missions are available.>
<No new Conquest missions are available.>
<No new Conquest missions are available.>
I do not wish to linger here long, walker. This room brings bad memories.

Congratulations, admanen. I usually avoid gatherings like this, but I'm trying to, I don't know … open up.\n\nFor what it's worth, I told the Sapiarchs what you did for the people of Russafeld. And for me. Thank you again, my friend—for everything.

Quite a party. I must admit, I feel a little out of place. Someone was under the impression that I saved the Illumination Academy. You and I know better, of course.\n\nCongratulations, cerum. Now, if you'll excuse me, I'm just going to try to blend in.
