It appears that my order did discover a cure. And the main component needed … is the heart of one turned by Hircine. By killing Vykosa, we shall ensure my salvation. How serendipitous.\n\nWere you able to find the wolfsbane and belladonna berries?
Finally, that jekosiit has been defeated.\n\nYou've not only saved this keep, but many lives. Vykosa's hunger for power seemed never ending, and this one is glad it has been put to an end.

Too bad the Khajiit didn't need my help. I had a perfectly adequate speech prepared to praise your many talents. Maybe I'll recite it for you later if you want.\n\nYou did good, my friend. Summerset is better for your presence.

Sea Sloads, Daedric Princes, yaghra, crazy cultists … I never expected so many interesting diversions when I first decided to come to Summerset!\n\nYou have my admiration, my friend. May Onsi's bright blade always watch over you!

The quality of ale and wine available in this palace is absolutely amazing! I may move in!\n\nSeriously, it was my pleasure to work with you. Maybe we can do it again some day. After I sober up a bit.

Well, well, well. Looks like another hunter has entered into the competition. Though I suppose a boon from Hircine himself would bring in a big crowd.\n\nI'm just not sure why you're coming around for a little chat.
My, don't you smell delicious. Lucky for you, I promised to keep on my best behavior before starting the hunt. Why don't you run along now?
Staking your claim to Lord Hircine's boon, huh? Good luck! You're going to need it with competition like us.
Don't mind me, I'm just thinking of something to carve on this pillar. It needs to be … evocative. Grandiose!\n\nOh, oh! "Harik was here." Yeah, that's perfect.
We need to keep a lookout for whatever—or whoever—killed this mer. I wouldn't be surprised if we're attacked next.
By defeating Balorgh, you've given my daughter a chance at freedom. Hanu can now join our ancestors and give wisdom to our tribe.\n\nPlease, do not allow her to refuse this opportunity on my behalf.
Well, you certainly look like formidable competition. But rest assured, that indrik heart is as good as ours. Along with Lord Hircine's boon, of course.
Pa says we have to keep on our toes here, and I suggest you do the same. Wouldn't want anyone to wind up killed.
Our business is done. Please tell your friends that Grethaa provides only the best information—as long as the customer can meet my price!

You! This is all your fault! Oh, criminal activity always carries a certain amount of danger, but your questions have brought this wamasu poo down upon our heads!\n\nPoor Eshundir. He didn't deserve this fate.
A thousand greetings, wayfarer, but I do not think we have anything further to discuss. Now go away.

I fear what Shuxaltsei has begun may not be undone by her death alone. We must stop her ritual and forever silence this temple to the old ways. Destroy the altars. Only then can we be certain the high priestess will not get what she wants.
You come to drain the sap from me again, but I have little left to offer your master. \n\nWhen the last of us are bled dry, it will be you who quenches her endless thirst.
Can't get enough of this fine vintage, eh? Well, you're cut off! Come any closer and I'll bash your fangs in!
I can prove that the Lost Legion died in Tsofeer Cavern and that my ancestor was responsible. And we bound the Wuju-Ka!\n\nThis has been a moist day, my friend! Moist in the extreme!

See those pedestals down there? How the cylinders taken from the reliquaries are set upon them? Margus is using them to focus his ritual!\n\nYou might be able to disrupt the ritual if you turn the cylinders so they recede into the pedestals.
Hey, swamp slug! Kassandra sent me to give you a message.
Only one mural remains. You must stay focused. If the truth of the Remnant eludes you here, we may never solve this mystery.\n\nI am counting on you.
I've said as much as I dare. Please, go away before the Blackguards see you!
Look, I told you as much as I dare. Now go away before the Blackguards see you speaking to me. Even this pitiful life is better than no life at all.
I have nothing more to tell you. You should leave now before the Blackguards notice you. Or worse, they notice you talking to me.

So, you're off then? That's all to the good, I guess. I could do with a bit less peril, and I've got a lot of reading to do! The Remnant of Argon—how mysterious! I do love a good mystery.\n\nGive my best to Xukas, and be careful out there, all right?
A villain defeated, a Hist tree renewed, a tribe reborn …. This one will admit, she is impressed.\n\nDo not let it go to your head, though! If there is one thing Zadaza cannot stand, it is vanity.

I owe you my life, friend, and that's a debt I take very seriously.\n\nTo be honest, I think this was my final adventure. Even with Kirstaleth's help, my leg is mangled for good. But I'll find a way to repay you. Count on it.

Well, that makes two pits you've pulled me out of. I just don't think I'm cut out for this sort of work.\n\nMaybe I'll open a meadery in Lilmoth. The bees here in Murkmire are, well … huge. But I'm sure I can make do!
You meet my gaze. Unusual. You either know just enough or nothing at all. What do you want?
My bonding partner is very pleasing, wouldn't you agree? She leads me like a gentle current to a place of great happiness.

Were their Imperial remains in the cavern? If so, were you able to place the sacred candles and help them on their way?\n\nVery good. I suggest you inform Varo Hosidias and claim your reward for a job well done.
Sharp claws and keen eyes, beeko. Until we meet again.

With any luck the thawing of this glacier has revealed the entrance to the Dwemer stronghold.\n\nClear a path through the Goblins for the rest of the crew and we can begin our search for the Wrathstone.

All I can tell you with certainty, is that the Wrathstone was not created by Dwemer. I'm no stranger to ancient civilizations, but much of this discovery remains a mystery to me.\n\nI can't help but feel like we're missing something.
<This conspicuous device protruding from the bridge to the Wrathstone chitters gently as you approach. The center plate looks like it can be depressed.>

Let's hope fortune favors us better this time.\n\nQuintus's records indicate that Garlas Malatar is under this crumbling fort, but the ruins aren't as empty as the Empire believes. The inhabitants are very much alive and under some sort of spell.
The path is clear and both halves of the Wrathstone are securely in hand. In spite of Dwemer machinations and Daedric scheming, we've done it!

<This orderly pile of papers define proper supplication and worship rituals for proper veneration of Meridia. Each page is meticulously written in a precise hand with every letter and line in perfect alignment.>
My betrothed has nice adornments. They will be suitable trophies.

I widen my eye slits in wonder. You contradict everything the tribe taught me about outsiders! I hope the war-chief lets you take the rite of passage. And I hope you make it to the end of the Path.\n\nFor all our sakes.
I'm told we must wait for the hut to be prepared. Who needs a hut? Why not witness the prowess of Ruxol's heir?
The Path of the Lily requires both brains and brawn. Listen to Kishi. Show my people that there is a better way.
It is as the sap-speaker said … a miracle.\n\nThank you, beeko. I name you true-friend to the Root-Whisper tribe. In this place, you are always welcome.
Enter the Path of the Lily whenever you're ready to begin.

Hmph. I erect the spine of deep pride.\n\nThe worth of a Dead-Water warrior lies in the nature of their death. Kaal Jaxsik-Orrn died in glory—a true servant of the Hist. We will burn many bones in Dead-Water Village. All will know her name.
So much death …. Filthy ojels!\n\nOne mural remains. Find it. Go!
Another Hist, another tribe to trade with! All is well in the marsh.
My poor Hanu. I tried to warn her of this fate.\n\nHer soul is now imprisoned, cursed to remain within this savage realm. All because of the actions of that vile Orc.
Good stuff, eh? Goes down smooth and wallops like a raging mammoth!\n\nHey … hey! Tell me a joke! I haven't heard a good joke in ages!
If you're looking for a friendly chat, best be on your way. I didn't set up camp on top of a mountain for the company.
Ugh! Now where did that little bugger run off to …?\n\nYes? Can I help you?
A Hist reawakened. What a remarkable event!

A bit like riding a shark through a cyclone isn't it? Little dizzy, little queasy, feeling lucky to be alive, and maybe considering another go.\n\nTell Jee-Lar I should have his anti-venom soon as I've strained out the chunky bits.
Phew! I recognize that smell. You must be Jee-Lar's assistant. You clearly found the ash basil. Did you bring the dreugh wax as well?
I calibrated the skeevaton to seek out the energy emitted by a soul gem. A powerful one. Follow it and it'll spare you a lot of rooting through scrap.
I don't know what's gotten into Burr. Something about this place spooked him. He's the only one of us with any sense.

I don't know if Haxara will ever tend to our eggs again, but I don't see the harm in letting them visit the uxith. She thinks being near the Hist will help her daughter and I can't say no to her. I don't think I've ever seen her this happy.
The shell of the dream grows thin, Rootmender. Soon it will crack. If you have questions, ask them now.

A word of advice, if I may.\n\nIf you plan to negotiate with Captain Jimila, don't underestimate her. She's always aboveboard and doesn't cheat, but she can be as slippery as a harbor eel. She won't always let you know what's written between the lines.
Show Captain Jimila strength and that you take your job seriously. That's the way to get on her good side, guaranteed.
So many outsiders! What is Lilmoth coming to? I remember when a single dryskin was all we would see in a season, and that was considered a lot!\n\nNow there are more of them than I care to count.

Thank you for all your help, friend-partner. I could speak all day with you about the wonders of Murkmire, but I have work to do and new vossa-satls to craft.\n\nSoon, all Tamriel will fall asleep to the soothing sounds of beautiful frog song!

Please let Famia know I will arrange a meeting with the Dead-Water tribe very soon. You should attend, I think. When you are ready to go, meet me at Bright-Throat Village's southern gate.\n\nSee you soon, beeko.
Hey, that one just ate one of the balls! Did you see it?\n\nMauloch, if this isn't the weirdest tusking place ….
All the Argonians are gathering beneath the tree. You should take the Remnant over, I don't think they can start the ritual without it.
Friend-Famia is waiting for you, I think. Was there something else you needed?
I prepare to leave this place. What more do you want, ojel?

I promise you, I'm done with this life, and with the Blackguards. Just let me go, and I'll never trouble any of you again. You have my word!\n\nPlease, think of my little girl. I can't leave her alone in a world this cruel. She needs me!
The old ways killed my egg-brother, and they will kill you as well, ojel scum.\n\nI look forward to watching as the Path consumes you.
The temple seems quieter and the spines of fear and dread lie flat again. It is done, isn't it?

Kishi must start training the next season of novices immediately. It has been too long since strong, young warriors emerged from the Path of the Lily to take their place in the Dead-Water tribe.\n\nUnder Kishi and Mewah-Jez's tutelage, we will prosper!
What's going on? Do you want me to take you back to Shadowfen now?
Sithis has spared us for another day. I will greet every dawn as if it is my last.

Vampy-bastards can't make a sandwich to spare their lives—not that I would—meats all dry! Got to get my strength up for the bashing to come!\n\nSoon those toothy gits will learn just what this Bosmer is made of. Fists!

The birth of a new tribe! What a marvelous thing to witness.\n\nI could write a volume on all that I've seen today. But you know … I think I will keep this moment, just for me. Thank you, my friend. For everything.
I did not think I would live to see my name no longer disgraced. I know Kishi can teach our hatchlings and our tribe will survive.
I owe you a debt, friend-outsider. Know that you will always find aid with the Dead-Water tribe—at least as long as I serve as our ka-deelith.
I thought you'd understand. A life without the Hist. She doesn't deserve that.
That's right. Keep playing make-believe with the locals.
I sigh with joy. It is as the Sap-Speaker said … a miracle.\n\nThank you, sword-kin. I name you true-friend to the Root-Whisper tribe. In this place, you are always welcome.
You should not linger for long, Rootmender. Already, my tribe's souls make their preparations for the long journey ahead. We have you to thank for it.\n\nFarewell.
I hope you're prepared for this ritual, friend.\n\nI mean, I suppose it's possible that it will be a pleasant romp in some Argonian spirtual paradise … but I doubt it.
The hole Haxara has left in our tribe is still wide, but we will be able to heal now that she has taken her crime with her. You were wise to suggest so.
Hopefully next time we meet, it will be under happier circumstances.\n\nFor now, feel free to talk to Seeks-the-Dark. I'm sure he's just overflowing with gratitude for all that you've done for him!
Do you know what you've accomplished today? The legendary Root-Whisper Village! Awakened once more, because of you!\n\nTell me, have you found any texts? Perhaps a wall carving or two?
Death, darkness, decay. They come to us, unbidden and unwanted. So too is your presence before me.\n\nTell me, what is it you need?
I regret you had to see that. Seekhat Yol is normally a more peaceful, welcoming place to visit.
You enter the land of the Dead-Water tribe, ojel. The elders will not welcome you. Best if you not get involved.
Never been this close to a dryskin. You look weak and fragile.\n\nHow do you survive when the plants in your land try to eat you?
Your steps show determination, and your eyes curiosity. Tell me what you seek, beeko.
I don't mean to be rude but, what?
Oh! You're back! You wanted to know something else? I could talk all day, if you wanted.

Drooler loves that whistle. He comes running whenever we blow it.\n\nI'm sure Varona just got caught up examining an interesting piece of carved stone, but I appreciate you going to check on her. I'll just wait here in case they return.

Shiralas has been much more attentive since we got back. I think she even missed Drooler, if you can believe that.\n\nI may have to get lost more often. I do so love the way she dotes upon me. Anyway, thanks again.
<<<1>> coos excitedly and nods toward Varona.>
Again, you come. You are prepared for the Death-Hunts now?
If you can get Ranja out of this cold, she will share her bedroll with you. For warmth, of course.
I tried to flush out a smaller beast for you, but Kloxu said it must be Fat Gixthi.\n\nHe might have gone easier on you if you had not put all those scorpions in his soup last week!
I am not supposed to tell you, but the neiweets and root-nurses prepared a great feast in your honor. Mmm! I can smell the phlegmwine from here!\n\nHurry and kill the beast so we can celebrate!
Kloxu poured every drop of his hunt-knowledge into your bowl, Mateem. Do not disappoint him.
It is not like Uraz to be late. I wonder what keeps him.
We should not take long here. The sooner we find Uraz, the sooner we can celebrate your hunt!
The outsiders are nearly upon us, Mateem. You must hurry! Talk to the sap-speaker, now!

Welcome, beeko! How good it is to look upon your face.\n\nI would love to chat, but there is still so much work to do before the farm can be in working order. I, ah, wouldn't want to disappoint anyone by shirking my duties ….
Hmm. So you have returned. Not many choose to.\n\nCome then, let us speak.

I simply cannot believe my eyes. The Root-Whisper Village, awakened once more.\n\nToday I have stepped into legend, and before me stands the hero whose name shall be honored in Murkmire for many seasons to come.
I'll make sure to attend the negotiation. You needn't trouble yourself further.
So we meet again. Fortunate for me, I suppose.
Finally, a chance to put Nurhei in his proper place. I hope the Shadowscale makes him eat his tongue! And I hope he chokes on it.
What business have you with the Root-House people?

I see you have taken the dark words of Sithis into your heart, Rootmender. \n\nFrom the nothing of slumber has come something awakened. One day it will be nothing once more, of course. But that is not this day. Well, probably not this day.
Are you ready, friend-outsider? We shall walk the Path as mentor and novice! Then we will prove Mewah-Jez wrong.
Outsiders … they still make my scales crawl. But you walked the Path of the Lily. You have shown both strength and honor.\n\nI shall do the same and aid Kishi as best I can.

You are the first outsider to walk the Path of the Lily. Moreover, you are the first novice to succeed and not die since Bhoki resigned his position as war-teacher.\n\nThank you for doing this, friend-outsider. We will meet back in the village.
I'll stay with the Dead-Water for awhile. I'd like to see more of their perspective. Tree-Minder Pavu is certain to see wisdom where I did not.

Sulosya lives in Alten Meerhleel, across the marshlands to the southwest. Just off the coast.\n\nI hope you find the Skin Taker before they take anyone else. I will rest more easily when they are caught … if I rest at all.
Guhcin, one of my tribe, found the Skin Taker carrying another victim to display. The coward fled without a fight.\n\nIf this murderer interests you, speak to Guhcin in Dead-Water Village.
I may spend my recovery among the Bright-Throats. Observe them.
So? What did—ulp—what did you think?
Give Hostia my regards. Tell her I'll be waiting for her in Orkey's bloody teeth.
The winds have brought you back to me. Is your task complete?
That root-house suitor is very tight skinned. You think she might return for the bonding next season?
It's gone quiet. Does that mean we're finally moving on? I can't feel my ears.
It is appropriate to feel pity for Haxara, is it not? Why do I feel so foolish in my forgiveness? I could not have made the decision in your place.
Did Tharayya convince you to join us? I hope you fare better with the Goblins.

<The armored corpse is not one of the recent aberrations that have been seen in the area. The skin and scales are much paler than most Argonians, It appears to have been healthy, before its recent demise..  >
I recoil in mock disgust. Ojel filth has no place in Dead-Water. Go take a swim in a pool of quicksand, why don't you?
I was expecting to find myself with Ruxol the Infirm, so I prepared accordingly, but this one looks to have twice the vigor.
The bangle on her wrist looks just like the one that belongs to my egg-sister. It's … a little distracting. But I'll put it from my mind!
I'm so happy he liked my seed-doll. It's really special to have a Moss-Skin be so sentimental.
I suggest you return to the Renewal Lodge. I'll meet you there.
My manservant has the unique ability to turn every expedition into an unmitigated disaster!
The manservant isn't looking so well. I don't think the humidity of Murkmire agrees with him.\n\nBut let's get down to business. Were you able to recover Mirdamir's key?

The rites of the Saxhleel … they are not meant to be shared with outsiders. I advise against riding this current, but I will honor our agreement.\n\nOnce one of you fulfills the requirements of preparation, we will begin the ritual of renewal.
And I was so looking forward to visiting Lilmoth. I've heard it's lovely this time of year.
I hope you killed as many of those spineless bastards as you could. The less Blackguards around, the better.
I do hope you're not here to harm this tree, ojel. Because then we would have … issues.
So you are the one Chal-Maht spoke of.\n\nI would like to offer my thanks. Without your intervention, my beloved may have never told me how he felt. Now we plan to bond next season.

Ah, my deek-beeko! So good to see you again.\n\nAs you can see, I have wasted no time. Is not Kud-Nakal lovely? It is my hope that we shall have many beautiful hatchlings together. And that hope is only possible because of you!
All of this conflict … it can't be good for the renewal ritual.
The ojel's voice, it reverberates in my dorsal flange. Most unpleasant.
Please, speak to the ux-deelith. I must prepare myself for the ritual of renewal.
Hurry, beeko. My stomach … it churns like a water-wheel. The truth of the Remnant—it must be close!
I did not think these old eyes would ever see something so grand. The birth of a new tribe and new life for a sleeping Hist.\n\nYou have done very well, beeko. Very well indeed.
Please, don't let me keep you. You have important work to do.

I don't know who was worse—the Blackguards who kidnapped us, or those Dead-Water Nagas they cooped us up with. I think they might have eaten me if things got dire!\n\nThank you for freeing me from that place, friend.

Goblins. Giants. Nagas. I've been captured by all three, and I have to say, I'm getting a bit tired of it. Maybe exploration just isn't for me.\n\nGlad you were there to pull our cheese rolls out of the fire.

I joined Cyrodilic Collections for excitement and a bit of gold, not to be abducted and interrogated like a common hood!\n\nUgh! This place is just a pit. I'm heading back to Anvil first chance I get.

Did my sister tell you she's quitting? Pft. She's always quitting something. First she's excited, then obsessed, and then she hits one little bump and she's over it. I really should stop following her around.\n\nOh well. At least there's food.
I have tried it all. Compliments. Gifts. Declarations of my undying love. And still she refuses to speak to me. She simply flicks her tail and ignores my pleas.
Where is she? Where is Honei?
Back again? Then let us drink to a successful business venture. Frog music for everyone!
The lizards tell Khajiit of the wonders of spear fishing. "So easy!" they tell her. "Kazrala will pick it up in no time at all!"\n\nBut the lizards, they lie.
Jaxsik will make an excellent leader. You chose well, friend-outsider.
A new village needs a powerful leader. They could do worse than Jaxsik, of that I am sure.
I bask in newfound understanding. Under Kishi's guidance, our warriors train to use all their skills, not just their strength and rage.\n\nI am learning much from Kishi. We all are.

The novices take to the new training techniques like mud slugs to water! They show great aptitude at using both their wits and their weapons.\n\nWe have a long way to go, but I have high hopes for the future of the Dead-Water!
Do not bother me, outsider. I must concentrate on my waiting.
My heart soars at your accomplishments, ojel. And at what you have done for the Dead-Water tribe.\n\nI raise the spine of respect in your direction, despite your strange and abhorrent ways.
Hello-hello! So good to see you again! You must tell me all about your adventures alongside Famia. Were they exciting? Was there danger?\n\nI can't wait to hear every detail!
Do I have the look of one who wishes to talk? Begone.
Thank you for letting me see reason. I could never take on this ruffian alone. If I want justice to be done, I'll need to find support!
Perhaps these crude words will be a welcome change to the audiences of my homeland.
You have stopped her honeyed tongue, and opened her eyes to the truth of our words. I erect the spine of gratitude, traveler.
My thanks for calming the waters.
It's so good to see you again, my friend! And Famia told me all about how vital you've been to the success of her latest expeditions.\n\nI knew that you and my sister would get along famously!
This lizard might as well be holding me for ransom. No matter. Once I'm back in Lilmoth, I'm boarding the first ship to Summerset!
I didn't expect you to approach me.
Many thanks for your help, beeko. I thought I'd never get her to change her mind.
The Hist guides us as it has guided you. \n\nWelcome, Rootmender. We have long awaited the decision you must now make.
So, you decided to take up my invitation? Followed me all the way out into the middle of nowhere? I'm flattered, and you're lucky.
If only you would arrive every time a dryskin wishes to play our game. I erect the spine of gratitude, beeko.
I can finally get back to practicing again. Not sure why Chukka-Jee even wished to help that kuuda anyway.
I finally get it! All I needed was for someone to lay it out for me. Thanks, friend!
Sithis hasn't made a meal of you yet, so I guess you're getting acclimated. Of course, you've been devoted in your offerings. Keep the serpent fed and it has little reason to bite.
I can't believe it. The dreaming Hist is … real? I always thought it was just a folktale!
I wonder how Root-Whisper Village feels about visitors? I wouldn't mind getting a look at those newly opened xanmeers ….
Our tribe is more than happy to support our egg-siblings in Root-Whisper Village.
I'm excited to visit the Root-Whisper tribe. It's not everyday that one gets to see a newly awakened Hist.

It is time to leave my home and join with my new tribe in Root-Whisper Village.\n\nI must calm my trembling chin and walk forward with no hesitation. Anything less would be an insult to the Dead-Water name.
I do not mourn! What warrior worth his scales would cry over his egg-sister's departure?
Oh! I was … I wasn't sleeping! I was just—just catching up with my thoughts, that's all. \n\nYou here about the Ebonheart Pact? Speak to <<1>>. She's recruiting just to the south of the docks.
How good it is to see a fellow member of the great Ebonheart Pact! I hope you're spreading the good word about our cause. We could always use more soldiers on the front line.
You wasted no time getting your feet wet since you arrived. Really jumped in with both feet. I'd guess you must be about—oh—neck deep in tribal affairs by now. How's that treating you?
I was hoping I'd rubbed off on you, but here you are still clinging to the meaningless.
Well, beeko. It's time for us to part ways again. Business is calling me elsewhere, but I'm glad you took me up on my little invitation. I hope you feel sufficiently welcomed.

I believe the Hist is instructing me to travel to Root-Whisper Village, but it has always been more difficult for me to interpret such signs than it is for others. I only hope this feeling I have is right. I feel like it is where I belong.
These teams are not evenly matched. Makeusta hasn't even had her third lick of the frog, and they put her in left-field!\n\nNo contest at all.
Make no mistake. I may be in Murkmire, of all places, but I still do not wish to speak with one of your kind.\n\nLeave me.
You with the Blackguards? I already told you fetchers that I'm not interested in joining your little band of merry murderers. I'm just camping up here for a few days, and then I'll be on my way.
My eyes widen in surprise. Why do you come to Blackrose Prison?
The phlegmwine is still bubbling, have some before the bog gasses run dry!
The Xinchei-Konu is finally operational once more! Now I can begin my studies in earnest. Oh, I just cannot thank you enough.

You performed a miracle! A Hist has awakened and a new tribe has emerged from the swamp. It's enough to make my tail spin and spin!\n\nThanks for aiding us in these matters. I will always consider you a friend.
So much agony has taken place here. So much pain.\n\nBut to wallow in such sorrow will only invoke shunatei. We cannot allow what has come to pass stop us from working towards a new tomorrow.
Ah, beeko! The Hist improves with every passing moment, as we knew it would.
There is a strange peace in Root-Whisper. Do you sense it? A serenity that I have felt in no other village, not in all my days of traveling.\n\nThere is a balance here. A deep sense of … peace.

I make a promise. I will protect this village. I will lead this tribe. Through both strength and words, I will honor the memory of Xukas.\n\nAnd I plant myself like a cypress, waiting for the day he returns.
Be careful, yes? This Remnant may still be dangerous.

Nala-do and Zamarak worry like mother cats over newborn kittens. I will be perfectly fine alongside Abnur Tharn.\n\nNow get moving, five-claw! I want you there when I plunge my blade into the Usurper Queen's heart.
Can you believe it, five-claw? Our queen still lives! Now, more than ever, we truly have something to fight for.

It occurs to me that if I can see through the Betrayer's eyes, he might be able to see through mine. Wouldn't want to give away any military secrets, so I'll stay out here and defend the bridge.\n\nJust like at the Battle of Banekin Rum!
This one has much to consider in light of Queen Khamira's revelation. Zamarak thought—no, Zamarak isn't ready to talk about that just yet.\n\nForgive me, walker, but this one needs more time.
Do not rush us, walker. We will go to the city just as soon as we gather what few valuables we have.

Abnur Tharn checks on Cadwell regularly. Find them and see if they can tell you where Zumog Phoom hides.\n\nMeanwhile, I will consult with Gharesh-ri. Review the Khunzar-ri stories before we task Tharn with learning more about the Dragonhorn.

We can't take any chances. Euraxia's final order directs her assassins to murder the last Dragonguard. If the Dragons consider this threat real, we need it on our side. \n\nMeet me west of the city, on the outskirts of Sandswirl Manor.
Go away! Haven't you done enough?
Take care of any outstanding business you may have as quickly as possible. I want to depart for the Halls of Colossus and find the weapon as soon as we can.

I'll take the prefect to Rimmen and see if I can negotiate an alliance between him and Khamira. We could use the help, but I'm not sure our young queen will agree.\n\nMeanwhile, you need to go to the Scar and find that shrine before the assassins do.
Something else, friend? This one has told you all he knows of Khunzar-ri and the Demon. Later, Azargo will recite the Poem of Rajhin in Rimmen, but it is long, repetitive, and frankly, not very good.

Well, now that you have the Dragonhorn, I suppose we should get back to Rimmen and see what Queen Khamira and Chancellor Tharn want us to do next.\n\nYou know, it feels good to be doing something other than trying to rein in Euraxia for a change.
This one is on a break. If you wish to hear another story, come back later.

My memory returns in dribs and drabs, but I'm not sure that's a good thing. If I remember anything helpful, though, I'll let you know.\n\nWhere are my manners? They're waiting for you. Queen Khamira has called another war council in the throne room.
Satarri hopes the story of Khunzar-ri helps you on your quest, traveler.

Thanks for the help, rhook. Now, I don't want to alarm you, but with all the oil and sulfur, this mine could …. Is there a gentler word for explode?\n\nMaybe that's what these Daedra work toward? Jone and Jode. One cataclysm at a time, right?
What is the delay? We should leave for the Halls of Colossus immediately. We must get to the weapon before Euraxia's forces do.

Five-claw! This one is so glad to see you! Great halls, noble guests … very different from Numaia's humble ranch, yes?\n\nThis one has high hopes for Queen Khamira's reign. No stinking poacher would dare invite the wrath of such a ruler!
This Dragonhorn, it is different from the one at Star Haven. It has no light, no energy.
First you save Iokkas' companions from the dangers of Cicatrice. Then you save all of Anequina from the tyranny of Dragons! You are truly remarkable, traveler-friend.
Oh! Vazbi is so happy to—. So happy to see a familiar face!
Before we go further, we must speak.
Damn assassin … she knew her stuff. I saw her fall, though. Thanks … for that.\n\nAfter all these years … why do I suddenly have … so much company?
Heading to S'rendarr's Cradle? I hope you brought your own waterskin. Or you could buy one off me. My rates are reasonable, given the drought.
Because of your help, our companions live.\n\nStill, there is much to do before they are well enough to travel. But do not worry, Iokkas and I will tend to their needs.

Khamira and I must work to win the hearts and minds of the people of Rimmen. And I still need to discover the significance of the Moon Gate of Anequina. Perhaps I'll send some troops to defend the place.\n\nJust in case.

Once this all began, I knew Euraxia would need to be dealt with. But sending Khamira's murdered parents against us …. Death was too easy an end for my half-sister.\n\nI'm concerned that the Dragons continue to work with the necromancers, though.

You found it, didn't you? Right where Aneshi indicated? Good, good!\n\nThis one wishes he was a hero like Khunzar-ri. Then he would accompany you to overthrow the Usurper Queen. But alas, Aneshi is not. Aneshi is just a frail, old caretaker, by Jode!

We came to check on you and tell you that one of the Dragons spotted us. I threw up an illusion, but it won't confuse it for long. We need to get back out there. So you go with Khamira.\n\nGods, I never expected to act so heroic.
I feel like a thousand pieces of gold! Just delightful!\n\nBut poor Khamira. She appears to have the weight of a mammoth on her shoulders. You should talk to her.

Thank you for saving this foolish one. She should have listened to Iokkas and never gone back into those dreadful caverns.\n\nSpeaking of our scaly companion, Najirra hopes he is all right. He sounds so distraught.

Ah, five-claw, just in time. We killed Euraxia, but between the chaos and the shock of seeing my dead parents and Nala-do's sacrifice, I fear my memories of what happened are not as clear as I would like.\n\nTell me what you remember.
Queen Khamira went through a difficult trial just now, but she will be stronger because of it.\n\nThank you for standing beside her, five-claw.

There aren't a lot of us, but the Cygnus Irregulars will stand with Queen Khamira's forces at the Moon Gate of Anequina. If the Dragons or the remaining Euraxians show up there, we'll give them a fight to remember!
This one wants to get into the palace and rendezvous with Queen Khamira as soon as we can.\n\nThe desecration of the royal graves … Nala-do doesn't like it one bit.

Last time I was in Rimmen Palace, it was on … business.\n\nWell, it certainly seems you've sought out bigger game since our time in Hakoshae. A Dragon, I believe? Or several, if the stories I've heard are true.
My portal should take us directly to Rimmen.\n\nI'm almost certain.
Greetings, traveler. I hope you're doing well.

The Hunger was preying on these possessed Imperials. I think we can rule it out as the source of the catastrophe that struck this fort. More than likely it was just drawn to the energies radiating from here.
Can you believe the audacity? Trying to absorb my essence, really!
Good luck with the Proof of Strength! And let me know if you need anything.

Keep an eye out for a letter or a messenger or some such. As soon as I'm ready to head to Elsweyr and move against the Dragons, I'll be in touch.\n\nYou have a particular knack that has served me well. I plan to utilize it again when the time is right.

I need to return to Elsweyr and explain all this to Gharesh-ri. It is not a conversation I look forward to.\n\nPerhaps the annoying old wizard will accompany me. It would serve him right to take the brunt of the Speaker of the Mane's displeasure.
Zha'al, spare a kindness for a priest of Two Moons? Haduras is at the end of his rope, dangling by the scruff.
Nala-do should not be here. This one should be prowling the Sand Behind the Stars and preparing for the Next Pounce, not lingering in this fetid tomb.
Don't dawdle, now! The Proof of Wisdom awaits you back in Hakoshae.
May your ancestors be pleased by your actions, traveler.

Mizzik can't believe the tales he has heard. Dragons, Moon Gates, eclipses! So much excitement you've seen! And so many heroic things you have accomplished.\n\nCertainly a step up from the work we did, yes?

Well, hello, my new playmate! Glad to find someone with their wits still about them. Too many crazies around here. I mean, what self-respecting person goes around chasing butterflies with a net?\n\nEverybody knows you use a hammer.
Let's just keep that little story between us, yeah? Wouldn't want my mother to hear about it. She'd chew my ear off.
Activate the temple relic, five-claw. It will allow me to charge the Combat Dragonhorn.
Tasnasi knows the Stitches isn't home to you, as such, but she's glad to see you visit now and again. She wants you to see it for what it once was, not as you saw it the first time.
Maybe its the Wood Elf in me, but I really do prefer working outside. The one nice thing about working with Jubani is not having to skulk about Dwarven ruins for scrap.
Hey, I know you! At least I think I know you. My memory's a little hazy on anything past the last few days.\n\nYou were on that thing, with Tasnasi? And me. You did that job with us.
"Sorrow is the canvas of the poet," said Bojhii the Misspoken. Mixed metaphors aside, the sentiment is lost on Nazdar. There is no music in his sorrow.
Very good then. And hey, if you're looking for some entertainment for your next soiree? Make sure to seek me out! You won't regret it.
I shall see if Feina-Darak honors her words. Only then can I rest.
It's no surprise Khasda finally got himself killed. No charisma. Let's hope whoever takes his place has some charm. Throw in easy on the eyes, if we're making a list.

Tasnasi's in. Khasda's out. Business goes on all the same. Dull as ever. The matter of Khasda's punishment presents some interesting opportunities … though I don't suppose she'll let him off with a good spanking.
Ah, Zha'al! You are safe! I hope the same may be said about Zargha.
Looking for something?
Thank you, stranger! Kiseravi hopes you will be the one to pass the spirit's test and retrieve the Akaviri relics.\n\nShe's sure you won't end up like the others.
Sizenza should see where to step, her vision showed it true, but she cannot see it now ….
You think that Rideza the Rogue is finished? It's only a matter time before I'm back on the streets. And when that happens, you best watch your back.
Well? Go on and eat it. The smell is making me crazy!
Ishu is so pleased that you were able to find Zinthia. Finally, this one's family can be reunited!

Sarazi will give you a head start. This is sporting, yes?\n\nYou'll see three prowling Khajiit on the Mesa, unless they see you first. Ha! There's a nesting gryphon up there, also. Quillmane. If you really want to impress me, kill him, too!

Thank you again for finding my dog. No easy task, wrangling a feral man-eater like Burtle!\n\nBut in all seriousness, keep his gentle disposition a secret, yes? Walkers do not pay to see dopey, good-natured mongrels.

I appreciate your assistance, my friend. Find out what happened to Gharesh-ri and the others. Then bring word back to me.\n\nMeanwhile, I will try to find a few moments to rest before I meet with the Mane's envoy or worry about the other Dragons.
Jahlar hopes you have a good reason for interrupting his meal.
Azurah bless you, brave rhook.
Yushiha hoped she would see you again, walker. She very nearly didn't. The Moon Gate was a costly victory.
So you've returned. Were you able to capture the Daedric souls?
Did you drink from my disgrace of a blood-sister, walker? If so, you must be thirsty still!
After all this excitement, I could use a nice, long lie down. Come find me if anything significant requires my attention. Otherwise, I need to be alone for awhile.
Remember, you must protect Khamira. At all costs.

Castellan Aneshi will provide the information we require. He has to. Remind him that it is his duty. And that both his Speaker of the Mane and his queen command it.\n\nBut do it gently. Aneshi is quite old for a Khajiit.

The moons come together and the sky grows dark. Ominous, isn't it? And strangely beautiful.\n\nWhere are the Dragons, though? And the remaining Euraxians? I assumed they would have started their push for the Moon Gate by now.

Thank you for looking into this, walker. I can't wait to rub this discovery in that sour-tongued Caldathir's face!\n\nIt's always "Be careful with this!" And "Don't meddle with that!" He's just a fat, old bully!

We may have sundered and redeemed Arum-Khal, but his thralls remain. Ushering those spirits back to Oblivion will keep me busy for some time.\n\nAs for you, you have Azura's eye now. She'll guide you to glory. You need only listen.
I see you met Forky! Been talking about me again, hasn't it? Such a gossip, that one, but you can hear the ocean if you stick it in your ears.\n\nGive it a try!

We accomplished much, but I fear we haven't seen the last of Kaalgrontiid. I must investigate reports coming from the south.\n\nYou, however, have a queen to crown! Take Cadwell with you and make sure he behaves. And tell Khamira … she did admirably.

Hoo, look at you running around like a chicken with its head cut off. Nothing beats a chicken without a noggin. Believe me, I've tried!\n\nYou came awfully close to spoiling my fun though. I like my fun.

This one's heart sings at seeing Khamira crowned queen. Her parents would have been so proud.\n\nThank you, my friend, for getting us to this moment. And for helping Zamarak find his way back to his true calling.
We do not have much time. This one feels his spirit slipping away.\n\nThe dark lich, Arum-Khal, has awakened. He rises like foul smoke from beneath the Ashen Scar.
Thank you for your help, walker. Safe journeys!
There are still Dragons to kill and Euraxians to deal with, but now it is time to celebrate!\n\nTake a few moments, talk to our friends. Then enjoy yourself, Champion. You earned it!
Dagaril-dro thanks you for the mushrooms, walker, and wishes you well in your travels. May you and the old wizard find the truth you seek in the tales of Khunzar-ri.
No! Come back! Sizenza could almost see it! We burn our hair and lay scorched before the Dragons, but what then? What then?
Sizenza has seen you at her temple, faithful. She hopes you will help her with this anchor and save it from the Dragons.

You wield our most sacred weapon now, my child. Walk the path with kindness, humility, and compassion. But in times of darkness, do not hesitate to mete out Azurah's wrath.\n\nRedemption waits on the far side of war. Arum-Khal is proof of that.
Guess I'll need to clean out a few more stalls. With those Bonechime bastards taken care of, we should have a few more furry guests trotting in soon enough.
For the moment it is all this one can do to try and restore peace and order to her temple. Then will come the true test. She knows the Dragons will come to Two Moons and her clowder must be prepared.

Zha'al! Once again Haduras finds you in the thick of the madness! Perhaps you did not leave Two Moons at Tenmar with all your wits about you? You seem to throw yourself at undead and Dragons with reckless abandon.

Destroying Arum-Khal's dark spirit destabilized this realm. You must go, sword-wielder, before it collapses.\n\nDo not worry for Shando-ri. Thanks to you, my vow to destroy the Dark Adept is fulfilled.
Rakhzargo lost his grapes. Best to watch where you step, yes?
Razum is smug. Well, smugger than usual. And this one can only assume that means that you have solved our problem.\n\nPerhaps Kideya's eldest son is good for something after all.
Seems that duty calls, thank the Moons. Raz does not know if he would have survived another day with his oh-so-beloved family.\n\nStill, he can at least stay for one more meal.
J'dathal was curious as to why his daughters were so distraught when Raz first left. Now this one starts to paint the picture, yes?

Perhaps, if you would be so kind, you could get me more skooma while you're down there? We have a lot. A lot a lot a lot.\n\nAnd the colors are starting to fade. I really, really don't want them too! But they are.
Muzzi doesn't understand! This one does as he is told, but these new soldiers still wish to hurt him! \n\nYou hurt the soldiers. Will you hurt Muzzi, too?
Deal with Narilmor! I'll try to keep Quintus under control!

Pardon my candor, but the old wizard kind of frightened me. He was rather intense. And obnoxious. Hasn't quite gotten over the fall of the Empire, I suppose.\n\nIf there's nothing else, I'll be moving on shortly. The work of a courier never ends.

Go on, go on. I'm capable of traveling to Rimmen on my own. We'll meet up at the city gates and go to the palace from there.\n\nI'm relatively certain Euraxia will honor the parley, but be prepared for anything. She's still a Tharn, after all.
Welcome back, comrade. Did you … did you destroy the machine?

Don't worry on my account. Intrepid knights such as ourselves can't be rattled by a turbulent tummy. Or even by Dragons or visions, I dare say!\n\nNow, off you go! Abnur hates to be kept waiting. He's also not fond of being called Abnur, or so he says.
I will finish tending to the wounded here, then order the retreat. Meet us to the south after you recover the documents and get them to Nala-do.
Do not fear for me, walker. I have been Gharesh-ri's agent for most of my life.\n\nI will see you in Riverhold after I take care of my fallen soldiers.
Look upon Mulaamnir and despair, morsel. You have no chance against me. No chance at all.\n\nBut Mulaamnir can be merciful. Come, let us talk.

A parley with the Usurper Queen? I doubt she'll agree to any sort of diplomatic solution, but it will buy us time to replenish our resources.\n\nVery well. Take Tharn and meet with Euraxia. In the meantime, we will rebuild what remains of the militia.
Walker, you arrive at the perfect moment. You will witness our salvation!

Ma'jha-dro must see to his disciples. There is much work to be done in order for Star Haven to recover, and they will need encouragement to face the trials that lie ahead.\n\nMay Bright Moons guide your path, traveler.

Nala-do suggested we refer to you as Dragon-Slayer from now on, but I put a stop to that. Grandiose titles will just distract you from the task at hand.\n\nSpeaking of which, don't you have an old castellan to interrogate?

Go on. Get to the Desert Wind Adeptorium and see what Euraxia wants with the adepts. Remember, it's west of here. And if the main entrance is blocked, look for another way in.\n\nI need another moment to catch my breath, then I'll return to Riverhold.
This one feels the weight of responsibility. It bears down like a boot upon my tail.
You are no longer of any consequence to Zumog Phoom. I suggest you go and bow before Queen Euraxia before she has you thrown to the Dragons.

Then you must exit the catacombs and follow the path north. There you will see the tower.\n\nThis one cannot promise the plan will work, of course. The Dragonhorn is very ancient, very brittle. But we must try, yes? Moons be with us.
What news have you?
My sources indicated that my son's murderer was somewhat … taller. Ah, well.\n\nNow, why in the world should I even consider negotiating with the monster who murdered my dear Javad?
You have my thanks, five-claw. Without your help, we would have surely perished here.
A ladder beyond the broken wall leads outside. After this one takes care of the Grand Adept's remains, he will meet you in Riverhold.\n\nThe Usurper Queen will regret rousing the Desert Wind.
Help me! Don't let Zumog Phoom take my soul!
It cornered J'dathal. Chased his daughters into the field. You have to help them!
I don't know what I ever saw in Raz. I mean, just look at his stupid hair! I can't believe he kept it that way.
It might be best if you leave now, rhook. You played no part in this vagrant's betrayal.
If Raz hadn't just rescued my entire family, I'd have ripped the lungs out of his chest. Even so, he's certainly not leaving here unscathed.

Sleek work, walker! Thanks to you, the Song of Kingdoms is heard once more.\n\nRajhin also wishes you luck on your adventures. Is he not generous? After all, the blessing of a trickster such as him is no small thing.

Thank you for stopping, walker.\n\nYou seem to be a traveler of some strength, no? Strong enough to help save this one's companions? They are trapped in the nearby oasis, surrounded by walking corpses and deadly fumes.

Congratulations on saving all of Northern Elsweyr. Makes our time together seem tame, no?\n\nHopefully I can convince the new queen to take an interest in our museum. After all, there's so much Khajiiti history we have yet to share.

To think that we would next meet in the Palace of Rimmen, of all places!\n\nHopefully I can make some friends among these nobles. After all, the House of Histories is always in need of generous new donors.
Ah! Greetings, walker! Have you come seeking work? There is much to do here in Elsweyr. Much to do!

Then Chevalier Renald is in your debt.\n\nThere's a break in the wall to the west. Invade the Hollowfang stronghold and make for the temple. While you have their attention, I'll search for Grundwulf and rendezvous with you once you're inside.
Dragons. Monsters within and without. Their blood is only fit for the dirt.
<This Hemo Helot is an acrid mixture of alchemical reagents and many creatures' blood. It throbs with vigorous life essence and Daedric energy.>
Once an oathbreaker, always an oathbreaker. Z'en have mercy on Carindon, because the Mages Guild will not.

<This Azureblight seed resembles those you've seen in your ascent through the corruption, except this one has writhing roots sprouting from its cracked shell. Like it's trying to plant itself in the fetid soil.>
A thousand thousand pardons and a thousand more to come for all the ills Azin-jo spoke of you. You were bright and true as Two Moons, and this one was clouded.
More fresh faces on their pilgrimage to the Divine. Who among our preachers graced you with the good word?
Sanctuary can be found at Sunspire Temple, walker. No false Dragons will face Alkosh's wrath.

Fragrant! Gather the urn and take it to our family tomb.\n\nSaviwa usually avoids these crypts because of all the stairs and murderous spirits, so he doesn't know exactly which tomb is ours, but he's marked the location on your map.
Jora-ri remembers seeing urns like these on the Baandari Pedlars' wagons as a boy. I often wondered what it would be like to be nothing more than ashes in an urn.

Hurry and follow Queen Khamira. You must be her King's Claw in there, for this one must help Abnur Tharn hold back the Dragon.\n\nDo not worry. You make an excellent King's Claw. Or maybe we should call you the Queen's Claw, yes?
Star Haven is safe, but the danger is far from over. I fear there is still much to do, walker.
Dusk mushrooms are as rare as they are delicious! I envy the old loremaster. If only someone cared enough to bring me such tasty morsels.
Last I heard, Tasnasi was camped on the north rim of the Scar, but this one doubts she'll stick around for long. The moment Khasda catches wind of her, he'll have her throat slit.
Yes, you hit the Dragon. I'd be more impressed if you had killed it with a bolt through the head or heart, but still ….\n\nNow, why don't you get on with it and finish the job?
Wasn't that a beautiful ceremony? Not quite on the level of the time I attended Molag Bal's first Daedric Titan unveiling and Soul Shriven impalement celebration, but beautiful just the same!

Not to complain, but the old wizard frightens me. He has such piercing eyes. And the way he talked about Dragons made my hair stand on end!\n\nIf there's nothing else, I need to move on. These messages won't deliver themselves.
Would you like to hear the words of our beginnings?

Once, Elsweyr was sixteen distinct kingdoms. Like the many forms of the Khajiit, they worked in harmony to create a peaceful and prosperous land.\n\nBut the Thrassian Plague upset this balance, causing two kingdoms to rule above all.

This one hates the idea of talking to the Usurper Queen. We should be stabbing her in the neck! Still, Nala-do sees the necessity, even if she doesn't like it.\n\nEuraxia will almost certainly betray you, so be careful when you face her, yes?

Think about it, five-claw. Little Princess Khamira survived the execution of the royal family. It's a miracle, by Jode!\n\nWe need to overthrow the Usurper Queen before she tries to rectify the situation. So, get to Riverhold and talk to Abnur Tharn.
Good to see a fellow member of the Aldmeri Dominion! Be sure to keep up the good fight, soldier.
I heard that commotion from halfway across the temple. Nisaazda managed to get that giant sentinel moving after all. She's more dangerous than I gave her credit.
You will? Bless you, brave hero! May Peryite rot your teeth and cover your face in scabies!
Talk to that rambling cultist if you must. Just be careful he doesn't cough on you.
Thank you for helping us, rhook. I didn't want to die in that filthy city.
Thank you, friend. I owe you a drink next time we meet.
If Queen Euraxia has you beheaded, do you mind if I lay claim to your body? It's not quite up to my usual standards, but any dagger in the spleen, wouldn't you agree?
Convince these Khajiit to set me free. And while you're at it, convince them that Peryite is awesome.

Thank you for helping to restore the bloodline of Anequina, walker. It is good to see a Khajiit once again on the throne of Rimmen.\n\nCashia apologizes for all the formality, but she had to be sure before she bestowed the Mane's blessing upon Khamira.

I'm glad that the Cygnus Irregulars were able to lend Queen Khamira our support. Helped make up for all the evil Euraxia brought with her to Elsweyr.\n\nNow, where's the music? I didn't spend the last six years learning Khajiiti waltzes for nothing!
Zha'al! You are like Khunzar-ri and his Kra'Jun! When Khajiit speak of this day, they will utter your names in the same breath!

Azin-jo has not always been Alkosh's best servant, but he has stayed faithful. He has stayed true. Even though his failings make him unworthy of the Great Cat's grace, he is not deserving of death … surely?

I came to Northern Elsweyr with an impossible task. I took command of the militia and sought to free Rimmen from Euraxia's grasp. With your help, we accomplished so much more.\n\nYou have my thanks for that, Champion.
Hmm? Something you need, stranger?
Please, leave me to my suffering. And know that I do this … I do this for love.

I guess I should get comfortable here in the Stitches. Those card sharps in Rimmen probably still want me dead. Eh. They'll forget about all the trouble I put them through. Eventually.\n\nThanks for your help today. You're all right, you know that?
You are clever, for an outsider. Ak'an respects that. Do not threaten Tu'heiba and you and Ak'an will get along.
You! I saw you speaking with that shaveskin before he fled. Where did he go? Where is Jakarn hiding?
Moons light your back, rhook. You dealt wisely and well. If ever I have need of another thief, I'll be in touch.
Fez does not move. Fez does not even breathe! Fez just stays very, very still, yes?
I bless you in the name of the Sleek Shadow! Fortune and fame are yours for the taking!

Queen Khamira. She is all official now. This one supposes that means more messages for Lyrrsazhi to carry.\n\nAh, well. This one was too good at being a spy that no one realized her true calling. Being the queen's messenger isn't the worst job, yes?
It does Bizaku's heart good to see our animals home safe. Moons bless you, walker.
By the Moons, that was a close one. Thank you walker. For everything.
I still can't believe poor Milksop's hide almost wound up on some poacher's wall!\n\nWe owe you, friend. You'll always have friends here on the ranch.
Don't think I'll be raking hay anytime soon. I'm just glad we still have hay to rake!\n\nThanks for everything, friend.
All right, best open that cage quick! Milksop's going to have a heart attack if he stays in there much longer.
A dog? Honestly?\n\nIf I'd known you could make a living showing mutts to people here in Elsweyr, I'd have emptied out all the kennels in Hew's Bane before I left!

Just look at these monsters! Baa'jhan has never seen something so hideous! Aside from his mother-in-law, of course. Ha!\n\nI jest! She is not so ugly. Her temperament, though? Much worse than this lot.
Do you think it's safe to keep such creatures in the middle of town? If that dog escapes again, who knows what it will do?
Huh? Need to head back or something?
Looks like something a bit sweeter has come along. Why don't you get moving?

All hail the greatest diplomatic assistant in Tamriel!\n\nLet us celebrate our accomplishments by drinking mead and exchanging friendly headbutts! Rigurt doesn't consider any mission complete until he can't remember most of what happened.
Tell your friend Rigurt that if another one of his stinking packages arrives here, this one will burn it and scatter the ashes.\n\nIf you don't leave Thadarra's shop, she'll do the same to you.
This Nord had better be finished with his cooking by the time Asaldak arrives. Asaldak does not like to be kept waiting.

Go ahead and bring the instruments to Rigurt in Rimmen. And please give him our regrets. I'm sure he'll understand.\n\nOn second thought, he probably won't. Understanding things has never been Rigurt's strength.
You can bring those instruments to Rigurt in Rimmen, but return them after the contract is satisfied, yes? They're more valuable than anyone in this band of jeeks.
This one believes she will remain here until Ambassador Rigurt and his honorary bell jingle far away from her cat.
Don't mind me. Soon as Razum-dar is ready to leave, I'll be out of your hair.

You know, I wasn't too sure about Thunderboots when he first came to town. Thought he would just cause more trouble than he solved.\n\nBut thanks to the both of you, we can finally put Rideza the Rogue behind bars.

Zumog Phoom is stronger than I anticipated. Or perhaps my powers have degraded more than I realized.\n\nEither way, you arrived just in time. If I had to listen to my half-sister prattle on for an instant longer, I would have chewed my own arm off.
Zamarak always fails the ones who count on him the most.
Those soldiers … were under my command. They died following my orders.\n\nThank you for releasing me from that … ordeal.
What are you still doing here? You're confused, aren't you? I get the feeling that you're a very confused person in general. You have that look about you.

We may be too late. It appears Zumog Phoom has already taken what he needed from Cadwell.\n\nYou check on him. I'll stand back and be ready to act. Just in case the necromancer placed some sort of trap upon our Soul Shriven friend.
Come back and visit us again sometime, friend. Hadamnargo can tell that Gordon really likes you.
Tell Hadamnargo that the only reason his lizard continues to breathe is because Sanzagh allows it. And remind him that these fields still belong to me.

Think you're the cream of the croup, eh? Well, you won't be filling my head with daydreams of sweet, cow squeezings this time. I lapped up every last drop! \n\nNow what are you going to do with all that dry toast, eh? Ha ha ha!
Thank you again for returning my master's wine. If someone brings me the rest of his cursed collectables, he might finally let me leave this place.
Ak'an says you don't need biting. Fine. That's fine. If you find any sugar, bring it back, yes? Or I bite you!

Go, go. Find the blue-skinned fool who wears a cooking vessel as though it was a helmet. I won't try to stop you.\n\nBut if I see you again, I won't hesitate to report your strange behavior to the authorities.
Radah could not find the fork, but he did not need it after all. He looked into the sun and found the darkness. Now they will not find him. Haha!
Zargha caught them all. He ran and ran and ran, but they could not escape him. Now … now he can sleep. He will not mistake the beatings of their wings for Dragons.
Why is it Haduras speaks for the Moon-Bishop? He did not listen when she said we must blind ourselves!\n\nWas it a test? Was Tahari blind to begin with?
Did our Moon-Bishop find the path? Rilasu saw her vanish, but Sizenza did not show her the path … why did she leave us behind? Rilasu would have followed!

What a stench! That's the stink of Coldharbour, walker. How such a fearsome and dangerous creature ended up dead beneath our favorite rocky outcropping, this one does not wish to speculate. Only an extremely powerful mage could summon such a monster!

Look at that! Snapped my knife blade at the hilt trying to skin this strange beast. Its rare hide would be worth a fortune if it wasn't so tough to cut!\n\nI wonder if I have time to run home and get a bone saw?
The wagons can rot. This one makes for the Stitches at the first opportunity.
This one will consider his next meal carefully. Something with leaves, he thinks.
We lost more than half our number. It will take awhile for the caravan to recover.
I'm staying far away from the Weeping Scar. I'd sooner risk Euraxia's dungeons than be made a meal of.
Sizenza knew she would see you again. Not a prophecy, just a feeling.\n\nHow may I be of service?
Zargha feels foolish. Who could fear butterflies? But he cannot look upon them any longer without deep feelings of dread. It didn't used to be this way, but he cannot remember what changed.
Hello? Ah, a familiar scent. You tried to help Radah keep his sight. He regrets that you could not keep him from his foolishness. It's no fault of yours. He was a very determined fool.
Sometimes Tahari feels guilt that she survived the Skooma Cat unscathed, but she is reminded every meal that she nearly lost her sight. She eats with her hands now, just to be safe.

Our Moon-Bishop encourages us to speak about what happened, to let the pain out, but every time Rilasu thinks of her dear friends, she can only see them on the ground … broken. She cheered them to their deaths. How can she forgive it?
Welcome! It is good to see another Khajiit, though you can see we have many here right now.\n\nCome chat with us!

Ah, hello, my fellow Khajiit. Your travels have shown you interesting things, no?\n\nExperience tells me that not all know of their fellow Khajiit, to the point of being unaware of the Alfiq. I am happy to share knowledge of my kind.
Lost? No. Surprised? Maybe … wait. Have you never spoken to a Senche-raht? Yet you are Khajiit …
This one welcomes you, Khajiit! Perhaps you come seeking knowledge from Raiffi? Knowledge that ultimately can help all Khajiit?
What? Oh, hello, Khajiit. Never seen a Pahmar-raht before? Or is there another reason for that stare?
Here you are, saving all of us with your heroic deeds, and what does Runji do? He faints at the first sight of danger!\n\nIf we are to survive, he must become stronger. He must.
Did you hear? Rimmen belongs to the Khajiit again. And Queen Khamira lives! Still, this one suspects that much remains to be done.
The winds bring news of crossed swords at a Moon Gate. With victory there, maybe peace will follow.
Did you hear? They killed a Dragon in Riverhold! A Dragon!

Prefect Calo is a very … complicated person. I think you made the right choice when you sent him to Queen Khamira.\n\nHis soldiers will help bolster our defense of the Moon Gate of Anequina, in case the Dragons move against it.

You are the one who protected Star Haven from the Dragon's wrath, yes?\n\nBright Moons bless you, traveler. If not for your actions, this one would not be alive today. And many others besides, all good friends.
This one wonders why any would even try to teach these ruffians. They don't listen.
Fah! This bloviating moon-priest offered us a meal, but we must listen to his long-winded speeches about gods first?
Zadeva considered making a break for it, but this one's stomach growls with hunger.\n\nZadeva does not like the decision before her.
This priest does not offer me enough to listen to all these words. Food only? Bah!
Ah, my friend. It is good to see you. This is a welcome change of pace, don't you think? Shining faces, regal attire …. \n\nAfter our time in the Ashen Scar, I could use some pomp and pageantry.

You have done much since we last met, traveler!\n\nThis one knew you had a brave heart, but never did he imagine you would become the savior of Elsweyr. Thank the Moons we happened upon the wreckage of your caravan.

Five-claw! Raz heard what you've been up to. And you didn't call your friend to help? Has Raz wronged you in some way? Killing Dragons, moving Moons, putting long-lost heirs back on the throne ….\n\nYou almost make Raz feel inadequate. Almost.
What? You thought this one could not talk?\n\nPah. Outsiders.
There are no words for the regret this one feels.
Alkosh guided your steps on this day.

I heard all about what happened with that mangy beast, Kaalgrontiid. Well done, my friend! I just wish I had been able to join you. It sounds like it was a worthy quest indeed!\n\nAlas, I had to see a Daedric Lord about a mind shriven horse.
Be safe out there, walker. The deep places of Elsweyr hide many dangers. It is best to stay under the sun and moons, yes?

I didn't really expect anyone to help a legion widow out here. The Khajiit don't have much love for the Empire these days; besides, they've got enough of their own problems.\n\nDragons and usurpers and undead. This whole world's coming apart.
Good luck making sense of anything that crazed cat says.
Don't listen to them! Selene has them in her thrall! Free me. There's still time to rectify this! I'll make it worth your while!

Can't say I'm surprised that Carindon tried to renege on our agreement. I knew the moment I met him that he's the type who doesn't do anything that isn't for his own benefit.\n\nI guess Allanwen was prepared for that. Wish she'd clued me in sooner.
I've done as you asked. By Z'en, I expect my freedom.
There's no time. Use the portal … find Khamira and Sai ….\n\nI'll keep … my head low until you bring the Dragonguard back … to the island.
Have no fear. The horse knows the way to the abbey as well as I. We can depart whenever you're ready.

Look what we found, walker! Za'ji has to say, the Dragonguard certainly has style. Though this one did decide to make a few alterations.\n\nNow, what's our next move? What does our Dragon friend have up his scaly sleeve?

And so you save us once again, mask-bearer.\n\nTadali is pleased she was able to guide you, if only for a short time. If you ever lose your way again, just pray to Khenarthi. She is always ready to aid heroes such as you.
Oh, ah. Hello. \n\nZa'ji and I found these uniforms and couldn't resist trying them on. We're forming a new Dragonguard order, right? We thought we should look the part. I hope that's not a problem.
I haven't seen Nahfahlaar, but I don't think he can approach this quarry. The cultists would spot him before he got close.\n\nWe might be on our own for this one.
<Apple is saddled and ready to go.>

The horses will carry us to the nearest port. From there, we can charter a boat and sail to Southern Elsweyr.\n\nThanks to the map you found in Dark Water Temple, it should be easy enough to find Vahlokzin's lair.

You are wise to ally yourselves with me. Laatvulon will not stop until Tamriel is destroyed. He has raised an army and forced my brothers to join his crusade. Those who refuse, die.\n\nHe must be stopped, for the good of my kind as well as for yours.
Five-claw! My head spins from the effort that took. Cadwell made it look so easy.\n\nBy the Moons, though, my heart sings at the sight of you, my friend.
An … island in the sky? I have no words to make sense of that.
You're always welcome to explore the Valley of Blades, but please try your best to not disturb our students. Their training is hard and rigorous. It requires their full attention.
As hesitant as I am to call a Dragon an ally, Nahfahlaar may be our best hope for discovering what these Dragons seek in Pellitine.
Don't concern yourself with me, walker. It's my husband who's in danger, but my sister is here now. She will fix everything.
Vijari knows what he must do. He will not fail you all.
Mask-bearer. The threads of fate led us to Dragonhold. It is fitting that we face Kaalgrontiid together.

I wish I could issue a proclamation and solve all our problems, but it doesn't work that way. For now, we celebrate. Then we must get back to work.\n\nDragons, reunifying Anequina and Pellitine, reestablishing supply lines … there is so much to do!

My dear friend, we have walked the Jonelight Path together, and Zar will be with you in spirit when you face Kaalgrontiid for the final time.\n\nLike Zar, you have the heart of a champion. You will make this one proud!
Even in death, that damn Dragon haunts me! If that aeonstone shatters, Tamriel is doomed!
A moment, if you please. Our battle against Vahlokzin left me quite exhausted.\n\nReturn to the Abbey of Blades and let Kasura know that we succeeded. I will follow as soon as I can.

When a Dragonguard dies, we say a prayer. May your flame burn eternal.\n\nIt's a promise to honor them, a desire for their legacy to live on. And it's an oath that we uphold, to never forget those who came before. An oath I will always honor.
I hate to deliver such horrible news.\n\nStill, it seems Sai Sahan has a plan. You should speak to him.
You did well today. Yahgrondu may not have joined us, but neither will his corpse become a tool of Laatvulon. A small victory, but a victory nonetheless.\n\nDid you discover anything else?

Leave the Dragonguard behind? I hope Queen Khamira knows what she's doing. Still, I understand the precaution. She shows wisdom by formulating an alternate strategy.\n\nThe Dragonguard will stand ready. I'll join you in the portal.
Here for another ship? Last I heard, the Perfect Pounce was still in condition enough to sail. Or perhaps you find her crew lacking?

Let's hope Za'ji takes our offer seriously. He may find it hard to believe that we want his crew to join the Dragonguard. In fact, I'm having a hard time believing it myself. But by Leki, we need them.
Thanks for the generous donation. Let's just make sure this little exchange stays between us, yes?
If our business is concluded, then Darkhu has other customers to attend to. In a city such as Senchal, there's never a moment's rest for one with my talents.
Where in Oblivion did my manifest go? It was on this crate, I'm sure of it!
Adara'hai heard you were being honored in Senchal, walker. She decided to come see for herself.\n\nYou look well. That is a relief.
Bretons. They think that they can get away with anything.
Next time you head to Black Heights, don't take Za'ji. Whenever he sees his mother, he whines about it for days.\n\nLuckily, drinks put him in a better mood. Let's just hope it lasts.
Ziss'vo, Daini! Can you do nothing right? How will we escape now? Just have to—oh!\n\nCan I … can I help you, walker?
Ha! This one thought you brave when you marched against Turo and his slavers. And now this one hears you went to a floating island and bested a Dragon? It makes Safik feel foolish.
Southern Elsweyr certainly isn't my home, but moments like these …. \n\nMaybe it's not so bad to visit for a while longer.
Daini is so glad to see you again! When she and Safik heard about the island in the sky, and your duel with the Dragon … how could she not come? How could she not wish you well!?
This is it. Our kra'jun is now complete. Now we shall end the story that started with Khunzar-ri … one way or another.
I need to find the queen's court historian. I want to make sure Za'ji's antics don't make it into the official record.
Is the ceremony over? Did Za'ji get a medal? Za'ji always wanted a medal ….
From pit fighter to pirate to honored by the queen of Rimmen! Caska can barely contain her excitement!\n\nIf you ever need my help, walker, don't hesitate to ask.
What a moving ceremony! I feel honored to have been … um, honored by the queen. Well, you know what I mean.
Please, Buzinda would like to be left to her grief. If you'll excuse her.
Ah, mask-bearer. I look around my home and see so much activity. The bearded one's minions, they scurry like ants in the moon-sugar. It … vexes me.
Don't expect too much from Ranza. He's a bit addled, if you know what Za'ji means.
Can you believe it? General Meric Renmus, standing right next to me! We studied his tactical withdrawal from Cheydinhal at the Academy!
The queen refuses to begin the ceremony until she has spoken with you, friend. Zamarak suggests you hurry and talk to her.
No matter what the morrow may bring, tonight is for celebration! I'm so proud of Aeliah. And of you and the Dragonguard, of course.\n\nBut I'm especially proud of Aeliah.
Ranza's not an artist, but he's a mighty fine tracker. I'm sure that map will help you find that muskarse in the robes. Maybe Lahini, too, yes?
I don't doubt your sincerity, you understand. Nor your bravery. I just can't take any risks right now, not when Senchal is in such disorder.

I never thought I'd become a Dragon hunter. A wandering bard, perhaps, or maybe even a diplomat.\n\nAh, that's not to say I'm having second thoughts! If this is what it takes to protect my home, then … this is what it takes. No matter the risk.
Well? What are you waiting for? The map is all yours!
The Perfect Pounce awaits, walker. Shall we sail again to the Dragonguard Sanctum?

Strength, skill, and ferocity. The proof of your prowess coats the arena's walls, hot and red.\n\nBut there are more dangers than the foes in this arena. Even with all your might, you stand no chance against the Dragons of Elsweyr.
You're competent, I'll give you that. Enough to slay a Dragon? We'll see.
They are gone, walker! Daini's brother, Malahbu, Galeneth … and Sormund also! Turo took them.
Halt, in the name of the New Moon! Why have you come here?
Well, tan Kyne's backside, am I glad to see you. They didn't get you or Daini did they?
The Dragonguard comes to our aid and the threads intertwine once more.\n\nHizuni has one song left in her, though she may be too weak to sing it. Will you hear it?
Blademaster Sai Sahan awaits you at the Abbey of Blades. We can depart as soon as you're ready.

Do you seek a berth on Sormund's ship, too? Ha. No, you are bound for greater things than deck-swabbing and sail-mending.\n\nAs for Daini? Deck-swabbing and sail-mending sound like a dream come true! Thank you again, my friend.
Bahzahar should be around here somewhere. Just look for a Pahmar with rotten teeth.
Seems Daini finally put her faith in the right person, yes? Thank you for getting us out of that horrible place!

Thanks for the help back there, friend. Not that I couldn't have gotten out of that pickle myself, mind you.\n\nGlad you found the cubs, too. I was worried that, you know … I wouldn't get paid and such.
You have the bell, right? Don't tell Za'ji you dropped it.
Report in, Dragonguard. Were you able to infiltrate Laatvulon's cult?

Kaalgrontiid. A name from the past I hoped never to hear again. Once Laatvulon haunted my dreams, but the shadow cast by his master makes the stub of my horn tremble.\n\nI hope you and your companions are up to the coming challenge, mask-bearer.
Already this one feels a new air of hope breezing through her city. There is so much to do. So much to plan. The future is bright as the Moons, walker.
All right, all right, I admit it! I stole the Perfect Pounce and brought it here to South Guard. \n\nBut I no longer have the ship. I don't!
That's the worst map I ever saw. Good luck finding anything with that scribble.
We have the recruiter's attention. I'll leave it to you to seal the deal.
Vijari, Vijari, comes to thee. He can't see, Dak'radhi.

So you'll get the mask and I'll head to Senchal? Sounds good.\n\nTake care of yourself, all right? No matter how close the mask is, I fear trouble is closer. I don't know what the Dragonguard would do without you.
Have you befriended the Red Beast?

It feels delightful to be about town after so many days hunched over that tapestry. I wouldn't have traded the opportunity for the world, mind you, but my shoulders are tangled in tighter knots than a cat's ball of yarn.\n\nPardon, poor analogy.
I will listen to the Dragonguard's proposition. Laatvulon has his allies. Perhaps it is time that I find my own.

Finding this Dragon will be no easy matter.\n\nPerhaps Za'ji will have a better lay of the land. He's traveled a great deal over the course of his time as a ship captain. At the very least, he may know who we can speak to.
Hey, look who it is! Good to see you again, pal. Marekki and I found ourselves a nice place to relax and have a drink. Nice enough, anyway. Pull up a chair.
You have done well, mask-bearer. Not only did you defeat the Demon from the East, you also turned Tadali's son into a respectable Khajiit.\n\nShe is not sure which feat is more impressive.
Best be quick about your business. Get to Nahfahlaar's Chamber and see what's got Sai Sahan's beard in a tangle.

The Dragonguard! Who's a good for nothing lout now, Mother?\n\nAh, but you must be busy with the Dragon, no? Za'ji will speak to the crew on your behalf if you do not have the time to spare. Leave it to Za'ji!
The Dragonguard were a very strict order, yes? I doubt our crew would do well with too many rules. Perhaps some changes will need to be made.
I have to admit, our Dragonguard does seem a little motley at the moment. Perhaps uniforms would help?
What do you want, smooth-skin?
This one would offer you a drink but… the bottle is almost empty. Also, Zurnash does not like to share.

So, this is Turo's warehouse, such as it is. Formerly my father's warehouse. \n\nComing back … it brings me no joy. I used to play here. Darting between the crates … hiding in barrels. Then, Papa died. Ironic that we rob his grave, yes?

Salutations! Shazar sees that S'rendarr smiles upon your struggles! Such a ceremonious series of circumstances this one cannot summon from memory!\n\nShazar is grateful to have showered before such a celebration.
My friend Skordo uses anger to hide sorrow. I … I do not think ….
Why do you wish to enter the Black Kiergo, friend of Caska? Are you looking for a fight?
Ah, friend of Skordo! Marekki is happy to see you again. Come! Join us, yes?
Fancy seeing you here. Z'en's still watching over your labors I hope.

One Dragon wasn't enough, eh? Well, whatever rustles your leaves. The Green is safe for now, but the Dragons are coming out of the woodwork. Must have smelled blood on the air or … Dragon musk? I don't know. The point is they're here!
Even with Laatvulon killed, there's still plenty of Dragons in Southern Elsweyr. The sooner your Dragonguard can rid us of these blasted beasts, the better.
Daini comes back empty-handed again? Ziss'vo, we will never get out of this place!
About time she got back. We're almost out of soup!
Though you are welcome to come to this shrine, I'd like some time with my thoughts. If you'll excuse me.

For as long as Dragons ravage this land, our Dragonguard will be here to slay them.\n\nI hope you'll continue to do your part as well, my friend. There are no shortages of tasks for someone with your abilities.

Thanks to you, everything turned out better than I ever expected! You helped me show Maezi and Uncle Hizhikar my true worth. Not as a son of Elsweyr or Wrothgar, but as a little of both.\n\nAnd Winks says thank you, too!

Ja'darri? No. It is you, hunter. Dezu. Time blurs. It is the same as before.\n\nI can feel Laatvulon's icy malice permeating this chamber. So this was his prison, was it? And now he has assured that it will be my grave.
