Poor Ra'khajin. It was his destiny to walk these sands, you know. To join with the Pride of Alkosh.\n\nBut greed drenched his heart like a freezing rain, sapping all its warmth. And so it fell on your shoulders to walk this path instead.
Keep a steady shield-arm in there, friend, and listen for the cackling. Those witches are like cats in a house full of mice. All we could do was scramble about … avoiding the claws.

<An aura of cold menace surrounds this eerie wicker pike. Destroying it might have some effect on the Icereach Coven's storm-summoning ritual. Beware, though. Meddling with effigies like this can have terrifying consequences ….>

Part of me will always hate Fennorian for taking this battle from me, but I know in my heart he was right. Had I died here, the Pyre Watch would have died with me.\n\nI have work to do. Doors to seal, graves to consecrate, and teachings to pass on.
<This macabre totem pulses with unholy power. Disturbing it will likely destabilize the necromantic energy of this place, making your foe far more dangerous. Choose wisely ….>
Laatvulon's followers swarm the skies. The longer I remain, the greater chance I will be discovered.\n\nTell me. Have you found Yahgrondu?
That is what happens to those who defy Laatvulon. He kills them then forces their corpse to do his bidding.\n\nPahklok. What shameful arrogance.
Good to see another Wood Elf in this part of the world. I'm still learning the ins and outs of this trade, but the armor I craft is pretty good.\n\nFor a Wood Elf. Or so they tell me.
I have come, for all the good it accomplished.

Oh! Sorry, I barely saw you there. Can I help you?\n\nWait. Where are my manners? Catina Garrana—daughter to Consul Honoria. Former consul, I should say. She passed recently. I'm rambling. Sorry. My head, it's just …. I haven't been sleeping well.
Have you come to plunder what remains of our academy? It matters little. Whatever indignities you plan to visit upon these halls will pale against the curse I put on them.
Welcome! What can Movasso help you with today? Do you need a place to rest? Perhaps food and drink?
There you are! I certainly hope you delivered that token. My lady has a—! Wait, is that Orc yours?
You really should be going, cerum. Our quarry, no matter how fierce, doesn't last forever.

Ah! Greetings, my intimidating but likely gallant friend! Looking for honest work? Well, you've come to the wrong place. I jest, of course! \n\nI have plenty of suitable heroic work for a person of your stature. Interested?
Greetings, rhook!\n\nAh, look at that swagger. A doughty adventurer seeking work, yes? Ha! Tsaraba can always tell.
Thank the Eight, you're back! What did you discover? Is my mother's soul at rest?
Back to mother, eh? Better you than me! If I never step foot inside that temple again, it'll be too soon.
Take care of the little one, walker. I'll do my best to keep the others out of trouble while you're away.
What is it now, hunter?

This one has done her duty and passed along the message. Get to the Dragonguard Sanctum, Sidura has told you. Now her work is done.\n\nIf you need something else, this one will be in the nearest tavern.
Another day, another Dragon hunt. May their corpses nourish the soil of Elsweyr.

Sai Sahan has made me the official liaison between our order and the Shields of Senchal. It's quite an honor!\n\nIt's a little strange that father keeps referring to me as Dragonguard now. Perhaps it's just his way of teasing me.

Za'ji hasn't taken the Perfect Pounce out for a sail in quite some time!\n\nHunting Dragons is important, but this one's true love will always be his ship. Perhaps a short expedition is in order, yes?
Those who hide, those who fight, those who pray to uncaring gods. They all shall know the glory of the New Moon as it rises.\n\nWill you look up in fear, initiate? Or will you rise with it?
Hmm. You have the look of a hunter. Chizbari could use you.
Zhasim has big plans! We spoke of them as we walked around Senchal and waited to meet with those merchants.\n\nIt was a nice walk.
I'm usually more careful with my special ingredients, but when that first sand-whale passed by overhead, I just forgot about everything else.\n\nWere you able to find my lost ingredient bottles?

Tender Claw thinks the note and the subterfuge is so clever, but it never actually works out the way he plans. Such a pitiful thief he is!\n\nThis one should probably collect the disobedient little fur ball now, yes?

Guess we're all Dragonguard official now. Seeing as I've got important work to be doing and you're a new recruit. Seems like you could say I'm your boss. Who's the big shot now, Za'ji?\n\nTime to get off your duff. I got work for you.

I wish I could say I was excited to go home, but I'm going to face a lot of widows and widowers when I go ashore.\n\nNords take bad news better than anyone. But still … delivering a broken shield to a weeping spouse is no walk in the pines.
Wouldn't go much farther, stranger. Won't find nothing but stab-happy bandits and murder birds off the road, there. Mark me!
<The chest contains room for the proof of your Dragonslaying.>
I knew something must have happened to poor J'saad. I warned him not to take that damn stone.
Meetza told me what happened to poor Falls, but thanks so much for finding the others. I just wish I had something to give her family back home in Murkmire.
I think I've had enough of this place. I appreciate what you did, but I think I want to go back to the nice, bug-infested swamp.\n\nMy scales are flaking from all of this dry heat!
We actually got out of there alive, thanks to you!\n\nI just wish Falls had made it, too.
The product is expiring as we speak! Hurry!
I would have robbed you blind if I hadn't gotten tangled up in that sack.
Hold there, traveler. A private event takes place here today. I urge you to move on. Immediately.
I keep checking the chest even though I know it's empty. Even though it hurts to move.
You are new here, yes?\n\nWatch your pockets, walker. Everyone is up to something in Senchal.
The remedy makes my Ania feel better, and that's all that matters.
Thank you again for delivering the product and helping those who need it most. Senchal could use more people like you.
Maezi wrote about a stranger that helped her and my nephew recover this one's stolen moon-sugar. Hizhikar assumes that was you?
Why do you bother this one? Juisa has much work to do. Always cleaning. Always fixing. This one is the only one in this family who works! No one else even offers! Too busy painting. Deadbeats.
Look, whatever happened last night was just the wine talking. That is not who I am. A little too much to drink and these things happen. Let's not make it weird.

This one heard that the cultists' leader is dead. May Merrunz spit fire upon his soul for razing this one's villa.\n\nNow that they are gone … perhaps rebuilding this one's home and fleet may once again be possible.
If word on the trail is true, the cultists who wronged my master have been killed.\n\nHopefully, that means we can put our lives as refugees behind us and start over.

They say the New Moon Cult has been dashed asunder. Their leader dead, and the Dragon destroyed. It will not restore the master's razed property, but it may offer him some comfort.\n\nWhich is more than I can say for this pitiful attempt at a campfire.
I'm finished with you. It appears I'll need to seek justice in Senchal.
Thank you for talking sense into that dirty elf. This one only wanted to be paid fairly for his work.

Thank you. Blademaster Sai Sahan awaits you near Senchal's palace. \n\nI wish I could join your hunt. Unfortunately, I still have many years of training at the Abbey of Blades. The time has not yet come for my own adventures.
We have reached the precipice, my friend. Whatever happens next will decide the fate of our world.\n\nEither way, it has been a pleasure to fight at your side. May Ruptga guide our hearts.
All she talks about is this Khunzar-ri. Doesn't she know any Orc stories?
This one thought to become a moon-singer, when she was a kitten. But, then this one grew up so pretty ….
Ah, meeting a moon-singer on the road is a sign of prosperous journeys. You should thank Khenarthi for your fortune, walker!

Never thought I'd actually get to put any of this knowledge to use, you know? It was all just more stuffy tradition before the Dragons decided bygones aren't bygones.\n\nBet my great-grandfather is raw in the hind over it up in Sovngarde.
Damn these sliding stones. Why do they have to be so heavy? A Pahmar-raht would struggle with these things!\n\nLahini is never going to join the Order of the New Moon at this rate.
Don't bother me, you hear? If you want to join those New Moon fanatics, talk to Shirnama in the attic. If he's even there, that is. He's been wandering about lately.\n\nNow leave me be.
Catina chooses her allies well. That's my clever girl.\n\nFinally, our spirits can rest. Finally.
Whats the difference between a fighter and a gambler? The amount of gold in his pockets!
When we fight, try not to bleed too much. This one can never get the stuff out of his fur.
First a Twilight Cantor comes to our village and now you. We don't get many visitors out here, rhook. Walkers like you are drawn to trouble. Black Heights doesn't need trouble.
If you're ready to travel to the Grinning Horker, climb aboard the cart. We'll be in Eastmarch before you know it.

Once again, thank you for assisting me. Without you, I'd still be locked away. And who knows what damage that harrowstorm would have caused?\n\nFollow this road east and you should reach Solitude in short order. Until we meet again, fare you well.
Get to the temple and evaluate the situation. We'll join you shortly, after I get a more detailed report out of my soldier.
Despite this turn, Svana has the right idea. Our best bet is to retrieve the sacred oil, make more elixir, and distribute it before the harrowstorm strikes the city.
Go on. Go see what the situation at the temple is. We'll catch up.\n\nI'll wait for Svana and make sure nothing threatens her.
Are you fleeing from the affliction as well? \n\nIf you are lost in the darkness, know that you are safe here with us.

Blackreach. To think such a dark and dangerous place has always existed right beneath our feet ….\n\nI want to see it for myself. And I want to determine what the Gray Host is planning. You'll meet me there, though, right? I … could use the help.
Then I am dispensed from this duty. If you want to congratulate me on a job well done, buying me another drink or two would greatly be appreciated.
I didn't think I'd find anyone out here in this frozen wasteland. You, my friend, are a glorious sight.

You don't seem bothered by the cold, stranger. Perhaps you can help us.\n\nWe've been marooned out here in this gods-forsaken place for three days. Our food's run dry and I fear we won't last the night.
As soon as we heard you were caught up in everything going on in Solitude, Captain Mavvok had us set out straightaway. You may not sail with us, but you're crew. And we look after our own.
I could not have said it better myself. Princess Svana will make a fine ruler.
It must be some sort of trick! The high king would never betray us … would he?

I thought I could hole up in that farmhouse forever, but then I realized my mead supplies were dangerously low. That gave me the courage to sneak out and head into town.\n\nNow that the curse is over, I'll head back home soon. After I've … restocked.
That was quite the spectacle. Ahem.\n\nAudiences for the day have concluded. Please remove yourself from the throne room.

Mother always told me stories of growing up in Solitude. But I never expected it to feel like this. All these people! And the buildings are so close together. How does anyone live here without feeling trapped?
It was a cold walk from the Silver Cormorant to Morthal. Well worth it. Never thought I'd feel warm again after that mess.
We heard what happened to the city, my friend. After everything you've done for my crew, it seemed only right that we come to offer our help.
This isn't over. Not from what we learned of the Icereach Coven. \n\nFor now, though, we rest and let the Skald-King make plans. There'll be plenty of time to kill more Reach witches another day.

It warms my heart to see Queen Gerhyld's daughter stepping out of her father's shadow. After the stories I heard, I expected to find a drunk and a wastrel. So far, she appears to be neither of these things.\n\nI'll make Svargrim listen if it kills me.
We just arrived ourselves. I introduced Fenn to Svana, but I haven't had a chance to give her our report. Why don't you do it, partner?
I'm glad to hear Hrolt made it. I'll wait for you to distract them before I try to get out of here.\n\nGive Sister Balra a good thrashing, all right? I think she's in the Dwarven ruins west of here.
Thank you. Help them and anyone else as best you can. I'll do the same. Once you're done with them, I'll find you and we can figure out what to do next.
Go! Take Svargrim down before that storm is unleashed upon the city!
It's now or never! Go help Svana. Make Svargrim pay for betraying his people.
That lying, manipulative witch! She stabbed me!
Well, don't just stand there. Get inside and find the Skald-King! I'll rally the soldiers and be right behind you!

It's good to see you again, my friend. I hope you won't begrudge me a few moments of quiet in my not-yet-completed palace.\n\nWhat do you think of the place, by the way? Just between us, I'm not happy with the throne. It pinches something awful.

It feels strange, representing a hold that may no longer exist. Still, I have seen the results of these harrowstorms up close. I'll do everything in my power to save our kingdom.\n\nThe next time Svana speaks to her father, I'll be right by her side.
After everything I've seen, I can no longer place my faith in Meridia. But I refuse to abandon my friends.
I'm safe in here, but the rest of the temple—it's overrun with monsters! Worse, they're our own priests and pilgrims.\n\nI saw one pilgrim attack poor Larilvor. Ripped at his flesh with her teeth!
What a day of suffering! But Priest Bavian says we may be able to seal the temple and contain the corruption.\n\nWe at least have to try.
No more farmwork for me, ever again. Once a person sees their friends torn apart by skeletal wolves, kinda makes you reconsider your life.

Our priority remains getting a meeting with High King Svargrim. We need him to accept this threat to his kingdom and convince him to help us stop them.\n\nMeet me at the Blue Palace and we can present our findings to the queen.
You found Rasir. Thank you, friend. I'm glad to see he still breathes.\n\nWhat did he tell you?

Thank you for alerting me to this situation. I am eager to see what else you uncover.\n\nI will do what I can, but be as discreet as possible. If you run afoul of my husband, he won't hesitate to return you to Jorunn—and not necessarily in one piece.
Solitude can never be our home. Not like the frontiers of Karthald were. But it has strong walls, and we can bide our time here while we think of what comes next.
You know everything I do. Just let us get back to our game.
Terga never hurt no one. She was a good sailor, and my best friend.\n\nI'll miss her, but at least now we know what became of her. Thanks for seeing this through.
Since we're all friends now, why don't you sit down and buy me a drink? It isn't often you get to consort with royalty.
I won't let what happened to Karthwatch happen anywhere else. If the Reachmen think they can take my homeland, I have an axe that will teach them otherwise.
This place stinks. I miss the fresh air from the mountains of Karthald. At least we're alive.

We've had a long road from Karthwatch to here. But all of us survived the journey unharmed. We're together, thanks to you.\n\nOur town may be gone, but thank the gods Solitude didn't suffer a similar fate.

You actually did it. You freed my pack. Now it's my turn.\n\nIf Exarch Tzinghalis took Fennorian, and I'm pretty sure he did, you'll find them both in the ruined Dwarven tower. It's difficult to get inside if you're not a vampire, but I know a way.
I want to leave this place. Who knows what other horrors await us down here?
He … he ate them. Like it was nothing. \n\nHe ate the pilgrims … even the horses … like it was nothing!
<The priest's eyes stare blankly and she doesn't respond to your greeting.>
I'm glad to see you in one piece, friend. And thank you for saving Rasir. The affliction will subside as we spread the cure to those still affected. \n\nAnd what of Skor?
<This priest has been gruesomely clawed to death>
This is wonderful! A bard and a celebration go together like wine and … wine!
We all lost someone today. A comrade, a father, a friend.\n\nI'm fortunate enough to have gained a good leader, at least. Well, we all have.

If you want to see our next item, you'll have to wait like everyone else. No private previews. You should know the rules. \n\nBut, believe me, you'll want to stick around for this one. It's a head-turner.

…all I'm saying is, if the Jarl doesn't realize he's still paying double regular price, then who am I to tell him?\n\nExcuse me, you're interrupting my conversation. Oh, and have someone clean up this wine.

I hope that Shelaria finds a way to forgive me. I robbed her of a glorious death, yes. But a glorious death would profit this place very little.\n\nThis Unhallowed Grave needs vigilant protectors. I think Kjalnar made that very, very clear.
That machine … it was horrible.
Walker. You and Fennorian did well, to stop the traitor-king. We will make sure no other threats befall the city. We swear it.
Nothing like standing in a crowd of Nords who barely survived a brush with vampires to make you miss Ravenwatch Castle, eh?
This one has already said more than is wise. Please go now.
Private property. Get lost. Wait, a half-giant? Is that … Lyris Titanborn?
Follow those footprints! This thing's not getting away!
You're back! Did you have any trouble setting up the traps?
I hope this investigation wraps up quickly. There's work to be done.

They're taking the cargo to an abandoned lodge in the foothills north of Solitude. Occasionally used it myself when the city guard was being thorough. Want to catch them? Start there.\n\nIf that's all, we're leaving. I'm not losing my head over this.

I met a clever woman who lives in the bog near Morthal. Old Mjolen's a dying breed among the Nords, a practitioner of the old magic. The locals both admire and fear her.\n\nIf anyone can help me untangle the coven's ritual, it's her.

The Reachmen have some ritual pyres burning around the Shadowgreen. Those seem to be the source of the magic that's stirring up the earth. Snuffing them out should disrupt their plans. Their plans being to turn this place into another Red Mountain.
Adusa said that Gwendis was outside the keep waiting for her. Please, find her. Tell her what happened.\n\nI … I need to go.
Ugh, there's no time. Take this. Keep it safe.
The things we do for a good night's sleep.
Looking around Solitude … it puts what happened at Dragon Bridge in perspective. I think the western holds owe you more than they know.
Lady Ninetha and I will manage the hold in the jarl's absence. We shall be fine while he consults with the high king.
She's so cold. I just need to warm her up. Then she'll be as right as rain ….
The dead should never be able to end a life. It's an abomination.\n\nI will pray for Arkay to grant these poor souls peace.
No need to mention me to Princess Svana or the high king, right?

I left Svana back at the Lonely Troll, under the care of that drunken Orc, Maugh. Unless he ignored my rather stern warnings, he should be keeping the princess there.\n\nI'll meet you back in the city once we finish here.
You've got a habit of saving people and places, don't you? I'm not complaining, of course! Merely observing.\n\nI've certainly got my work cut out for me here, anyway. Doing the only good I know how.
Does Jorunn think me so weak that he believes his half-giant can twist my arm and fill my head with lies?\n\nI am not so easily duped, outsider.

I saw the assassin. He moved fast … unbelievably fast. He leaped through the window after stabbing my mother. By that time the guards had gathered, so I guess he decided to flee.\n\nTry to follow his trail. Someone outside must have seen something.

Did you hear the news from Solitude? High King Svargrim betrayed his own people. I suppose the Princess Svana will become jarl now. Maybe even the high queen?\n\nShe seems a good woman, if a tad young.
The inn's straight over that way. Right across from us. If you don't find Eyga, she'll find you. Never met a stranger she didn't need to get acquainted with, whether they like it or not.
This is bad … I didn't even know there were caves beneath the bridge! Why didn't anyone tell me?
Ena acts like I'm made of glass these days, but I feel stronger than ever.\n\nI may have injured my arm, but I can still help Solitude.

Your friend already came and went. I urged him to wait, but he seemed eager to keep one step ahead of you. Cold blood hasn't cooled his youth.\n\nHe found lichen that only grows in Chillwind Depths trampled among strange tracks. You should join him.
You and your associates accuse my husband of outrageous actions. Making deals with monsters? Murder?\n\nI hope you have a damn good reason.

I've come to the conclusion that anything is possible where magic is concerned.\n\nI'm going to look around with Lyris, then return to Old Mjolen to finish studying the witch pike residue. Maybe that will help me understand how the ritual works.
Excuse me, I should report to Solitude.
I can't think of a more fitting send off for my father than Nords of both kingdoms mourning side-by-side. Skyrim may be divided, but at least our honored dead are united in Sovngarde.

We know enough about Tzinghalis's refinement processes to replicate his methods, but we still need a source of netherroot to do so.\n\nTell Svana that if she can keep us supplied, we can produce enough elixir for all the holds in a matter of weeks.
I'm glad to be done with this. Diplomacy and investigation aren't my favorite pass-times. They seem to suit you, though. You stepped up to the task better than I could have hoped.
I hadn't had a moment to honor the fallen of Morthal since you came to my doorstep. Kyne willing, they made their passage to Sovngarde.
Princess—Jarl Svana reminds me more of the queen every passing moment. We're in good hands, I think.

My heart goes out to these people. We are no strangers to conflict back east, but none of our holds have been ravaged by the kind of devastation brought by the Gray Host!\n\nWe are fortunate that you stopped them.

Look what we found, walker! Za'ji has to say, the Dragonguard certainly has style. Though this one did decide to make a few alterations.\n\nNow, what's our next move? What does our Dragon friend have up his scaly sleeve?
Reachmen from the west, pact from the east, monsters from below! This city's cursed!

Solitude's had a rough time of it. Telline and I were planning on heading to Summerset, but I think we could both do some good work here. We can help rebuild and make the city better than it ever was.

Well, you certainly keep busy. \n\nI'm sorry for the loss these people have suffered. My husband and I would like to help however we can. It might not be the retirement I envisioned for us, but it's the right thing to do.

Lightless Hollow is a dangerous place to wander, friend. I've heard rumors of bloodthirsty creatures roaming these tunnels. I fear they might be the ones responsible for a group of missing miners.\n\nIf you value your life, I'd advise you to turn back.
Who are you? Another spy? What did this lying easterner say to you?

The last time we spoke. It was about the men with the job postings. A pair of wolves in sheep's clothing. Trying to blend in, but still rough around the edges. Same with their horses. Sheared mountain mares.\n\nCome from the Reach, I wager.
I truly regret my lack of skill at arms right now. I want to eviscerate those responsible for the queen's death.
My people are scared enough as it is, and these excessive displays are just making things worse. \n\nYou all need to figure this out.

Oh, well done! You handled the princess with skill and aplomb. Saves me the trouble of having to talk her down.\n\nI'd say I'm in your debt, but it was your she-giant that provoked her in the first place.

Chief Urzikh's smart. Brave as they come. But, I've got to tell you … part of me wonders if she went too far with her new mining methods.\n\nProgress, am I right? If you try something new, be ready to take your lumps.
Things here could turn ugly any moment. Go talk to Mazog. Just listen to what she has to say, all right?
The clan waits for me to render a verdict.\n\nHave you given this predicament any more thought?

If you're here to get me to tell you where the key to the mine is, you're out of luck. \n\nUnlike our chief, I care about the safety of our clan. We should never have used alchemy in the first place. I knew this was where Urzikh's methods would lead.

Our enemies circle ever closer, and now even my daughter turns against me. What's next? Will my beloved wife return to accuse me of some heinous crime?\n\nWell, get to it. Tell me about Svana's miraculous elixir before I have the lot of you tossed out.
Don't worry about me. Just need to catch my breath and then I'm heading straight for Solitude. I should let my family know what's become of grandfather.
<Pickle looks at you curiously.>
We'll have the Cormorant cut out before you know it. I'm happy for the work. Gets the blood pumping again.
I couldn't believe my own eyes. Blizzard seemed to come right up out of the ground. Just like that, we were on the ice.\n\nNow we're losing people faster than we're losing feeling in our limbs.

We lost a few good sailors, it's true. Drigsen says she will honor them with a plaque.\n\nBut we all knew the risks when we signed on. Once we get the Cormorant back in the water, we'll make it back to port and carry on.
You're not one of those things!\n\nI didn't think I'd see another living person down here.
Damn it, none of this would have happened if we'd been working the stone with our hands instead of Urzikh's potions.\n\nUgh. I guess we should focus on the task at hand—finding the survivors.
I'm sad to see Mazog endure such a fate. She was as hard a worker as any and cared about this clan. If only she could have consulted the chief before acting on her own, we wouldn't be in this mess.
Finally, a friendly face! I knew Chief Urzikh wouldn't just sit around and let us die. Came close, though. Almost went down the hole when the scaffolding collapsed.\n\nGood thing I'm so nimble, eh?
Why are you still talking to me? Get to Riften and find Lyris Titanborn!
Quickly, traveler! Give me the ingredients so I can make the elixir for my sister!
We can heal the injured, but Meridia's light does nothing for the corrupted.\n\nHopefully, you can find a way to save us from these cursed storms.

Blackreach? Suddenly every legend and camp story from my youth has returned to haunt us!\n\nWhile you and the others charge into the damn abyss, I'll prepare the city. We'll do what we can to keep the people safe.
I haven't seen you before. Are you new to Solitude? Better yet, are you looking for work? If so, you've come to the right person. Let's talk!

Who's this? Strong, sober, well-equipped? The Coterie of Organized Scholars needs adventurers of your stripe! Our research very much depends on it.\n\nOur fieldwork is fascinating, satisfying, and it pays quite … well, there is payment. Interested?
I'm biding my time. I think the Broker has something truly magnificent for the finale. Like a Dragon horn, or a Snow Elf statue.\n\nHa! With the Broker, who knows?
Speak.

You there … are you seeking refuge from the affliction too? This is a safe haven for those of us with werewolf blood who haven't been infected. If you require sanctuary, this is the best chance you'll get.
Thank you again for what you did. We'll never forget the courage you and Viggol displayed. We are in your debt.
After all this, I'm going to Solitude and staying there.
Thanks for saving us back there. I'm going back to the surface where it's safer.

You can take that boat to the Frostbite's hideaway on the Frozen Coast. It's a ramshackle dump. Shacks and tents on shifting ice floes. There's no telling where Nelfthea will be. You'll have to search. Don't spare any raiders who get in your way.
Please, save the others … if you can.

Raynor and I have been in our fair share of impossible situations. But this one? It definitely beats them all, at least when it comes to strangeness. And that's saying a lot when it comes to Dwarven ruins. \n\nThey're usually strange to start.
Everything is a blur. I think I vaguely remember talking with a group of people, but the memory eludes me.

Brilliant! You did it! \n\nI'm incredibly grateful. You can't possibly imagine how uncomfortable it is to be in the wrong temporal configuration. Imagine bowel cramps, except all throughout your body. Absolutely horrid.
I didn't realize how much I missed the cold. The wind biting my cheeks is like a kiss from an old lover. Or a new lover! It's invigorating. \n\nYou have my eternal gratitude, for what it's worth.

I think I'll take a moment to catch my breath. \n\nNo experiment has ever been helped by a nervous disposition. In fact, a great many of them have been thwarted by it. While working with miters, one must maintain a clear head.
I think I'll still need time to come to terms with everything. This was a great deal to take on at once.\n\nI feel tired. Older.

Overseer Urlvar employed a vampire to protect the mine! How dastardly. I believe that explains the missing miners quite succinctly. He must have given the vampire people in exchange for protection for the rest of his workers. But from what, I wonder?

Watch your step, stranger. A couple of so-called ghost hunters laid traps all over the place. They insist that it's to catch spirits haunting the mines.\n\nThey don't leave soon, the only thing they'll be catching is my boot to their backside.

Oh, don't let the rumors scare you. Miners are a superstitious lot, and being this far underground can play havoc with your senses.\n\nIf you need to know anything else about Dusktown or working for the Bitterblade Mining Consortium, just ask.
I've got nothing else to say to you.\n\nNow go away before you get both of us in trouble.
Rigurt hopes these talks go well! \n\nThe Skald-King plans to send him on another mission soon. Hopefully it will be a place where the people are excited to embrace Nord culture!
I had no idea our island hid such horrors. I'll see to it that this evil place stays buried and forgotten.\n\nThe secret dies with Lord Falgravn.
Don't let our soldiers' posture fool you. They're ready to fight—they just need some hope.
Good luck. The fate of Kyne's Aegis is in your hands.

<This scroll bears the insignia of the Undaunted, along with a potent spell conceived by Hroltar the Boaster. When invoked, the scroll will grant one's enemies astonishing power.\n\nThe full incantation contains some colorful language.>

It is finished. You performed well. Better than any other I would have found in Morthal.\n\nThis is more activity than I have grown used to. Perhaps I should find a replacement so Old Mjolen can finally rest.
Everything is ruined … I swear to you, I was only trying to keep my people safe.
Sounds like it's going to be another one of Jarl Morryn's famous political benders. I pity whatever servant has to mop up the cabin when they're finished in there.
Mazog was foolish to stand up to the chief. She paid the price for disobedience.
My friend. You have done so much for the holds of Western Skyrim, I fear it is a debt that can never be repaid. And bringing Freiwen back to us … you will always have my thanks.

I'm sure she'll appreciate your assistance. As for me, I'm getting as far from here as possible until this blows over. Hopefully this blows over soon so I can come back. I prefer Morthal when it's quiet.
After everything we faced at Castle Thorn, I knew it was the right call to bring you along for this. We make quite the team.\n\nSo I hope you don't mind if I make one more request of you.
You know … between our fun with Arkasis and the, let's be frank, horrors we dealt with here, you and I make a pretty good team.\n\nSo I hope you don't mind if I make one more request of you.

<This scroll bears the insignia of the Undaunted and a potent spell, conceived of by the renowned Hroltar the Boaster. When invoked the scroll will empower one's enemies with astonishing power.\n\nThe full incantation isn't short on colorful language.>
Rigurt really knows how to surprise you. Even now, just when I thought there was one of him … there's two!
Every warrior who died defending Kyne's Aegis died with honor.
You dealing with those who killed our queen? Count me in. My sword thirsts for their lives.
Please pardon me while I grieve for our dear queen. She was a friend of mine.
Nothing like a tragedy to bring people closer together.\n\nIn fact, any who need my blades to deal with the queen's killers will find me quite amenable to the idea.
It's a sad day for Solitude. I remember when the king and queen married. Now she's gone?\n\nSomeone will pay dearly for this.
I can't believe it! The queen is dead!\n\nI feel so terrible for her family.

Life is too short to work for a maddening, incompetent … ahem, person.\n\nI mourn for my queen, but her death reminded me that I have better things to do. I've already accepted an offer to work in another's house.

My sister can't stop crying. She claims she dreamed of the queen's death, but passed it off as a nightmare. Now she blames herself.\n\nBad enough that the queen's dead. I understand grief, but having to deal with that and a wailing sister?

I know many here feel devastated by queen's murder. Guilt, shame, and more is being passed around. Some sharpen their blades to go hunt down whatever caused all this.\n\nI understand all that, but I think the wrong lesson is being learned.
The loss of our queen has many grieving and off balance. Many loved her, some called her friend.\n\nBe gentle with those around you here, stranger. And may the Divines guide your path.
I'm ready to rip apart anyone who harms us again. The queen's death … no, just leave me be. Better that way.
I plan to hunt down every single cur who had anything to do with the queen's death.
Ah, I shall revel in the deaths of those who killed our queen. I would not normally care, but I have no doubt that Hircine will smile upon my efforts.

I'm completely sober. I put aside my work on my mead recipe to help with any funeral preparations needed for the queen. \n\nI have no words other than these: none can hide from a Nord seeking righteous vengeance.
I … the words escape me. The queen's dead.
I feel awful for adoring murder mysteries now. The queen's dead. She was the warm heart of this city.\n\nWhat will we do now? Oh, and her family. How terrible they must feel.
I raise the spine of sorrow for the death of Solitude's queen. I admit my curiosity pushes me to learn more of their funerary rites for queens, however.
Blood now runs here as it did where I just came from. Royal blood, too. Is Rathzin cursed to venture to places filled with death?
I'm sorry, I'm not very good company right now. My heart aches for our loss. I haven't slept in days.
The queen's death is what comes of allowing strangers into our lands. She deserved better.

If they'd allowed me to protect the royal family with my spiders, the queen wouldn't be dead. I'm sure of it.\n\nAs it stands, I'm all for any retribution that's coming to those who did this, even if it takes me to Sovngarde sooner rather than later.
I thought the Nords here were dour before the queen got killed. Now they're so much worse! It's sad, of course. Hopefully they have more mead coming in. They'll need it.
I wish the jarl would give the order and send us to the barrow! Who knows what our soldiers are facing down there?
I have seen many things in my time, but never could I have predicted I would soon train adepts of the Mages Guild in the arts of my ancestors.

We made it through, if barely. When the clouds began to gather over Castle Dour, I feared I'd have to witness …. \n\nThank you for stopping it. I don't know that my heart could bear another Karthwatch.

I'll just stay put here until Master Dren shows up. Takes days sometimes. He shows up all dirty and grumpy and yells at me for not coming to look for him.\n\nI just keep offering him stew until he quiets down. Works most of the time.
Hello? Is that you, doughty assistant? Thank Vehk.\n\nYou have the incantation, yes? Read it, quickly! You'll be surprised to hear that life as a bottle does not suit me.
Gods willing, we've reached the end of this awful business. The land has enough scars.

You again. Always where you don't belong. All this foulness began when you showed up. Should have known you were bad news when I found you with that spy. \n\nYou might have the princess duped, but I've got my eye on you.
How long are you going to be loitering around here? I don't trust people with nothing to do.\n\nGet busy or get gone, outsider.

Narsis Dren and the Mystifying Mysterium! No, no. Too repetitious. Narsis Dren and the Madness of Maelmoth! Yes, that's a bit better.\n\nOne can never spend too much time on a title. A book with an inferior title is hardly worth the effort!

I was suspicious of what Rigurt and Jarl Morryn could accomplish. But if Rigurt could destroy a man's faith in a day's work, why shouldn't he be able to resolve the rift between Eastern and Western Skyrim?
Safe travels. And if you ever see Narsis again, be sure to give him a firm kick in the shin for me.
My mother warned me not to worship Daedra, but Meridia seems so pure and bright. Was it all a lie?
Some doubt Meridia, but she rewarded my faith by sparing my life.\n\nThis temple may be lost, but her teachings will live on.
Let the others argue over Meridia's role in this tragedy if they want. All that matters to me is that we're still alive.
There's no escape. Nowhere to run from the evil of these storms or the apathy of our god.\n\nMeridia has abandoned us. I will never speak her name again!
About time I found someone whose spine wasn't bent with age or cowardice. There's trouble on the horizon.

It's good to see you, my friend. Please forgive the mess. The last thing on my mind these past thirty years has been farming, especially after my parents passed.\n\nI guess I'll have to fix the farm up now. Ha! I guess I no longer have excuses.

I've known old Aerolf for a long time. I thought he was frost-touched, but I was wrong. That thing, whatever it is, is real. And, it murdered my sister.\n\nI wonder how many other old stories that I ignored over the years are true.

I've known soldiers and killers in my day, even been friends with a few. I don't know any I'd call evil, but that thing? That thing was evil. That thing killed my dog.\n\nEverybody told me I was crazy. Aerolf is the first one who made sense.
Mazog learned the hard way not to defy the chief. I don't want to end up like her.

You have a great deal of work to do, Antiquarian. Wouldn't you agree? We're all quite busy, truth be told, but I suppose I can make more time for our most promising initiates.\n\nIs there something I can help you with?

Welcome to the Antiquarian Circle! Make no bones about it, you'll be discovering ancient relics in no time! Bones! Get it?\n\nJust a bit of antiquarian humor for you. You see? It's not all dust and dry inkwells. We have fun, too!
Looks like you're relatively healthy and not at all dead or in a stupor. And you do not appear to be a monster. Good.\n\nMove along.
Thank you for all your advice about the Antiquarian Circle. Who knows, maybe we'll have another adventure together!
You should head back inside and speak to Verita. I'm sure she's eager to get you out into the field.\n\nI'll catch up with you later, all right?
Sorry, I'm busy. If you are looking for the chief, she's by the mine entrance.
These wounded require my attention. Speak to Overseer Thulsgreg at the mine entrance if you want to know what happened here.

Your persistence begins to annoy me, mortal. You killed my beloved brother and sister, Tzinghalis and Ulfra. I freed them and you sent them back. Back to the hated Molag Bal!\n\nI will see you suffer for that transgression.
You killed that monster and you retrieved my squad's intelligence! I wish you'd been with us from the beginning.\n\nSee <<1>> for your reward.
Those goats are my entire livelihood. Please bring them home safe and sound once you've made sure those werewolves won't be troubling anyone again.
We're running low on provisions. One way or another, this battle will end soon.
We have to keep our weapons ready. Giants can attack at any time.
Thank Kyne! Please, get us out of here! We had to watch as those hideous creatures killed our friends. I can still hear the screams. I just want to go home.\n\nHow did you even find us down here?
Maybe I just need to be patient. My Muffins will come back. She has to!
No better place to be than Skyrim!
Tusking Skreg. He wouldn't last two swings against me if he fought fair.

So all I have to do is find a Dwarven structure like that you mentioned, and head down. I can scarcely believe I'm to see Blackreach at last!\n\nWhen my name appears in the annals of Imperial history, I will be sure to mention your part in this.
How wonderful to see you again, my friend! I hope you have been continuing to seek knowledge and wisdom. Such is the calling of those who recognize Jhunal as our patron.
If you're headed up that way, watch out for the crazy High Elf lady. She's shrill enough to make even the nastiest critters down here tuck tail and run.
I nearly killed myself opening that portal.

I slow cook my skeever meat for a full day before marinating it in my family's recipe.\n\n My meat is so tender and juicy it'll slide off the bone and right into your mouth. We're eliminating pests and solving hunger! Everyone will love skeever kabobs!

You're not sick, are you? Be careful, if you hang around Tranya and her kind long enough, that might change. I'm truly sorry, but we can't risk letting anyone in. It's too dangerous. \n\nWe can't have more people getting sick.

So much has happened here, but Solitude still stands. And we have the princess to thank for that. And you.\n\nI heard the Skald-King sent help, too. I don't trust him, but I suppose we should be grateful.
After everything that's happened … I don't know.\n\nI can't trust the easterners. But if Princess Svana says they can help us … well, I know I can trust her.
I'm glad to see both you and Rasir made it out alive.
The problem with searching for the truth is sometimes you find it. We're too quick to dismiss our old legends as colorful superstition. They're meant to be warnings. We should listen to them.
Such tribulations we've endured. Kilkreath, Karthald, High King Svargrim … then Solitude almost destroyed by a harrowstorm ….\n\nWe'll survive, though. We're Nords, after all.

Princess Svana has certainly accomplished a lot for someone so young. I wonder, do you think they'll make her Jarl of Solitude? Maybe even the high queen?\n\nI suppose they'll need to call a moot to decide.

Thank you for helping us. Tranya is strong, but I'm glad she had a capable ally to rely on throughout this madness. \n\nWe will miss Skor dearly, but we'd be lost to the affliction were it not for you. Words cannot describe how grateful we are.

I can't believe it. We came here to take advantage of virgin mines and get caught up in vampire schemes that almost brought the entire place down on our heads! Thank Vivec it's over now!\n\nIt is over, right?

Who knew that the scary castle that looms over Blackreach belonged to a vampire? Did you?\n\nI miss the swamp. And the mud. I think I'll collect the wages owed me and go home. If they will let me out of my contract, that is.
Be careful. Skor is not himself. There's nothing left of him inside that mindless beast.
It's been quiet, but I must remain vigilant.
Our supplies are running low. We can't last much longer.
Never trust the people holding the purse strings. They always betray you.
Secret deals with witches and vampires? What's this world coming to?
It's been too long since Freiwen was last in Morthal. The jarl has never looked so happy.
The attacks on our village stopped after Freiwen returned. Curious ….
What happened at Kilkreath Temple, they're calling it a harrowstorm.\n\nI don't know what that is exactly, but it sounds horrifying!
So a bunch of Meridia-loving Daedric cultists got wiped out? So what? Good riddance, I say!\n\nNow maybe we can turn Kilkreath Temple into an actual holy place.
I thought no one would come! You saved many lives today.
I asked for spriggan bark, not thorns in my side. Go find what I need and take it to that useless Wood Elf if you expect to be paid.\n\nEveryone here has brains as dry as their skin.
That's the anointed relic given to the Swords of Solitude, is it not? You have my blessings. May Arkay defend you from those vampires and smite them to dust.
Try not to die.
I will await your findings with baited breath.

Nezashul could talk and talk until we both grow old and his tail grows limp, but scholastic pursuit requires actual pursuit now and again, no? \n\nThis one looks forward to learning what you discover!
I do hope you find something noteworthy. Even if whatever tribe may have occupied the area is long gone, it would be better than having to report that our commission provided nothing.

That white mammoth certainly drew quite a bit of interest! So glad I won. They're so rare! Let's just hope the Broker didn't cover a brown mammoth in talcum powder!\n\nOh, why am I worried? The Broker never lets us down.
The decrees from the Blue Palace are simply absurd. Investigating transfers of suspected stolen property? Who cares where someone got it? If I want it, and they have it, I should be able to buy it!

You know, as great as it is to be here to acquire some of these incredibly rare items, the excitement of being here in disguise is half the fun! You'd be quite shocked to find what I'm wearing under these robes.

Do you know what I wish to see come up for sale? An item that demonstrates who the true rulers of Solitude are. \n\nSomething like a Jarl's ringfinger. Demanding you pay taxes looks foolish when you have one of those on a chain around your neck.
Kyne's mercy … I'm so cold. You're not one of those giants. Run, before you wind up like me.
You smell like burnt oil and metal shavings. Guess you found my colossus and lived to tell the tale.
Unless I miss my guess, the horrors we've seen so far will pale in comparison to what waits behind these doors. But as long as we stick together, we'll make it through.\n\nNow, let's find my sister.
This trip has been so miserable. What wrong with being a Nord who likes a warm hearth and husband?
The critters around here are unusually skittish. I'm growing wary of what it is they're afraid of.
<A single switch that seems to connect to the pumping equipment nearby.>
No … harm? No hitting? No. No! The Wood Elf lies. Everyone lies!\n\nEssenia will beat me. Will kill me! Then bring me back. Then … then kill me again!
Mor Khazgur will become more prosperous under Chief Urzikh. These conflicts are nothing more than growing pains.\n\nShe was right to put Mazog away for good.
Our chief was too soft on Mazog. These new ways are confusing. Nothing wrong with an old fashioned public execution.
Help the others and hurry back … whatever Tzinghalis did, it nearly killed me.
It will take time before the mines are safe again. I fear the consequences of the chief punishing Mazog. Mazog looks out for us. Will she continue to do so after all this?
So far, so good. Just watch the shadows.\n\nI'm a creature of the night, and this place even gives me the creeps!
I've been trying to keep an eye on everyone … make sure no one else disappears.

You're fools if you think you'll survive this place on your own. I've seen what Essenia does to people. You … you have no idea what she's capable of.\n\nThis Wood Elf's friend? Adusa? She's likely dead. Or worse.
Less and less return from the mines each day. Pretty soon, we're going to run out of people. They said this job would be dangerous, but we never expected it to be like this.

I hope Overseer Urlvar rots in a cell down here for the rest of his miserable life for what he did. I don't care about his intentions. He sacrificed good people, my friends, to a monster! That's unforgivable. \n\nWhat a coward.
The Undaunted's always looking for promising people. So if Mordra's a little brusque, don't take it personally.
This one is quite pleased you stopped by, and hopes that you find a guild that appeals to you. Amsaad wishes you many friendships and adventures in your future!
You don't like me, but you don't win all the time. So let's square things up.
I've been to a few diplomatic talks in my time. Bores, the lot of them.\n\nBut after everything you and that frostheel pulled today … this one seems worth my time.
Thanks again, friend. You've given me a sliver of hope in these dark times. \n\nI can't wait to get out on the water again. I'm much more inclined to fish now that I know I get to keep what I catch.

You expect me to let you put a whole boar carcass in your bag and have the meat bruise while you traipse across the countryside? Ha!\n\nNo, no. I'll have the carcass sent over to Rigurt. With proper handling.

You're not sick, did Tranya send you? 

There's a cure for the affliction. I hid a few vials before I went to test it, just in case anything went wrong. Take my instructions, they will lead you to it.

And tell Tranya … Skor is lost.
Please, no more, Blood Queen. My veins run dry … or is it my roots? What's … I can't see!

Finally! We've been waiting for relief for hours! You know I'd help fight the monsters off if not for this damned leg. Doesn't matter. I'm ready to get out of here.\n\nUgh. None of this would have happened if the chief … never mind.
Hamvir looks relieved, but he still hasn't crafted the elixir. If you have the ingredients, please give them to him.\n\nI don't think Hedrynne will last much longer.

Mara bless you for your kind heart, traveler. Find my husband Hamvir at Chillwind Depths. He's a healer, so I'm sure he knows how to help poor Hedrynne. He just might need a little assistance to get it done.

Well, you're not a slit-faced Goblin-thing or a giant bug. Good news for me, eh? Been stuck here since the collapse, and let me tell you—those things are everywhere.\n\nI hope the other workers don't blame the chief for this.
Thank Mauloch! I thought I would die down here. \n\nWho came with you? The chief? Thulsgreg?
The guards here in Solitude are well-trained to deal with any problems. You aren't a problem, are you?
Superstition thrives here in my birth-city of Solitude. Many look to misguided beliefs instead of the guidance of the Divines in these dark days. Let's hope the future brings more light.
The walls of Solitude intrigue me, as they should for any siegemaster who takes their job seriously.
I'm glad Brun is going to live. He went through so much. \n\nBut, is it really a good idea for Freiwen to come back here? After all that she's done. What if her curse comes back and kills us all?

The Dragon Cult's lair, Dragonhome, is further west, as is the altar where you'll place my belongings. You'll need to put me inside your pack so I can direct you and offer guidance. \n\nDon't make a fuss of it.
Come closer, I do not have much time left.\n\nKyne's wards have been dismissed. If Morokei's wrath breaks loose from this place, Skyrim will fall to ruin. You … you must stop this from happening.
After everything you've done for Mor Khazgur, I'm here to return the favor. My clan is unified … we will do what we can to help rebuild Solitude.
You gave those Gray Host bastards a good fight, I'll give you that.\n\nNow that Dark Moon Grotto is safe again, I'm itching to do the same.
The bastards who did this … I'm sorry we didn't get a chance to make them pay for it. But we're done chasing ghosts below ground for now. We're here to help, however we can.
Some folk want to rebuild, but I don't think I'll stay. What those witches did has cursed the very ground under our feet.

As soon as we heard the news, Claudina insisted we come to offer whatever aid we could. Once again, you have proven yourself to be incredibly brave … and downright fearless! \n\nIf there's anything I can do to help, just ask!
We heard that Princess Svana will likely be made jarl. Maybe even high queen. Good. Her mother, Gerhyld, was a fine ruler. Better than her traitorous husband.
The Eversnow may remain, but I'm going to leave. Find somewhere new to start again. There are … too many memories here.
I was born here and I'm going to die here. Hopefully a good long time from now, but I'm not leaving just because a little trouble came our way.
Welcome to the Circle, cerum!\n\nI'm the organization's resident eccentric. So, if you're fond of bizarre, yet completely plausible historical theory, I'm your Elf!
I still can't believe I'm alive. There was a sudden flash, and the floor just crumbled away into an abyss! I was almost swallowed up by it.
Brave meeting, Antiquarian, and welcome to the Circle.\n\nYou have no idea what a relief it is to bring another warrior on board. Not many of us brawling scholars left in the world, it seems.
Must finish. Must clean. All the books in place. Even the secret one.\n\nGo! Go! Must not be seen talking to others. Must clean. Must work.
Master's master will be here soon. Note is in place. He will find what he must.\n\nNow leave! Cannot talk to outsiders or master will have head.

Go on, my brave apprentice. You should have the honor of presenting the evidence to Elle. You certainly worked hard enough for it.\n\nIt's time everyone learns what kind of man Overseer Urlvar really is.

I admit—I underestimated you. Once we heard the fighting begin, I assumed your distraction would be short-lived. The mindless creatures that crawl around this castle aren't known for toying with their prey.\n\nThankfully you survived.
We'll show the Gray Host. We'll show everyone. The Ghostsong clan still has some fight left in it. Just point us at the prey and let us loose!

I should have expected Arana to take up with outsiders. She always rejected the old ways.\n\nThis is no place for one who doesn't hear the spirits of the Reach. You're not worthy to walk these sacred halls.

This still doesn't feel entirely real. I can't believe we found a letter tying Verandis to the Gray Host. From Rada al-Saran of all people! \n\nAt least there's a map. Let's find this damned island and finish this. The cart's waiting.
Go. Help Verandis find the Dark Heart. My hunters will be ready when you call for them.

I'll meet you across the river. Together, we'll find a way to enter that ruin.\n\nSeeing Rada again. It reopened many old wounds. He wasn't always the villain. At least, I like to think he wasn't. Ah, a fool's hope is a dangerous thing.
That void portal up on the portico looks promising. Try using your shard on it.
The darkness, it stirs. Can you feel it?

You found them! Cogline, Indouz, and Jeanard returned not long ago. Thank you. We owe you a great debt.\n\nI hope the Pyre Watch warrior was able to provide the historical information you came looking for.

Bradan can speak to the mood of the Ghostsong clan. Tell him what you told me. I'm sure he'll help us get a meeting with my sister. He's a werewolf, mind you, but I've never had a truer friend.\n\nLook for him at Hroldan Ring. I'll meet you there.
We must stop the ritual. Nathari is leading the Ghostsong clan to destruction.\n\nShe believes that she's fulfilling Namira's ancient command. Nothing will sway her from her course now.

I couldn't help overhear … you're headed to Viridian Watch?  \n\nIf you hadn't just rescued me from certain death, I'd ask to come along. I have wanted to see that place since … well, forever! Alas, I am in no shape for another adventure right now.

Be cautious. Viridian Watch is no place for the reckless.\n\nAny location that might have provided sanctuary to the Gray Host, even centuries in the past, can only be evil. There will be darkness in that place, mark my words.
Be well, wayfarer. As you head into Viridian Watch, may Onsi guide your blade.

I never read anything about a survivor fleeing to Viridian Watch. Not that I keep up on my Gray Host history all that much, but still! That's quite a shocking revelation.\n\nIf you find anything, I hope you'll come back and add it to our records!
<This looks to be an ideal place to plant the Undaunted banner and issue your challenge for the greatest of glory.>
<This looks to be an ideal place to plant the Undaunted banner and issue your challenge for the greatest of glory.>
We are about to travel into the unknown. Take a moment. Speak to our companions. Make whatever peace will calm your soul.\n\nWhen you're ready, we shall enter the portal together.
You're really just going to hurl yourselves through the Void and hope for the best?
This is it then. Everything that happened in Windhelm, Solitude, and Markarth—it all leads to this. To Rada al-Saran.

I can almost understand it. Rada al-Saran's desire, I mean. The unpleasantries of living with this curse have haunted me a long time. The thought of what awaits me in the afterlife fills me with no less dread. \n\nAnyone would seek an escape.
Work is plentiful in the Reach, provided you have the steel required to see the job done.\n\nSo, can I add your name to my list?
Ah, hello, adventurer! I have need of someone with your kind of mettle. It's dangerous work, but there is a reward if you're so inclined. What do you say?
Oh! Hello. Sorry, my mind is elsewhere. My companions and I have been searching for days without success.
There's no way this is worth it. Just throw me back in the nearest cell and let me serve my time. Anything but this.
Huh? Oh, sorry, I wasn't really paying attention.

Run here, run there. I'm more than a messenger, you know. What am I going to tell Ard Caddach that he doesn't already know?\n\nFine. I'll go and play nursemaid to the ard. Have fun in that creepy castle without me.

I'll find a way to deal with Rada. Lady Belain and the Gray Host, I leave in your hands.\n\nStop them from feeding the Dark Heart and it should fall dormant again. With any luck, that will put an end to whatever Rada plans to do with the orrery.

Verandis and I need to talk. A lot. \n\nBut as soon as we're finished, we'll find a way to stop whatever the Gray Host has planned. Rest assured, you'll be the first person we call. We're in this together.

All these so-called tough women and men of the Reach gather here in Markarth, yet none of them will deal with the horrors I witnessed. This army in our land raises storms that drag the souls right out of our people!

You're a fool, Verandis. You always have been.\n\nWhy does Lord Rada al-Saran continue to humor you? We don't need you on the Gray Council. You aren't even fit to be one of Styriche's foot soldiers. Go bother someone else with your nonsense.

How I have missed our endless debates, my friend. Our deep and fascinating discussions about science and philosophy. I look forward to renewing that exchange.\n\nIf you haven't presented yourself yet, you should go see Lord Rada al-Saran.

Enough talk of alliances and mortals. It has been too long since we last saw one another, Verandis. Let us speak of better times, drink the blood offered, and contemplate the tremendous responsibility we bear to keep our people safe.
Everything is ready for you, my lord. We moved your belongings into the study and provided all the reagents you requested. Should you require anything else, please let me know at once.
The Gray Host must be dealt with. When the time comes, I hope you will be at our side. Until then, be well, my friend.
Just go. Please ….
Why spoil the mood? I think … I'm going to take a moment. I haven't done that since Fennorian and I arrived in the Reach.
I hope you're right. If father managed to undo some of the harm the Gray Host caused, I know he'd be at peace with himself. Wherever he is.

Remember, <<1>> loves that whistle. If she hears it, she'll come running! Tell her she's a good girl and she'll warm up to you in no time.\n\n<<1>> just got scared. She can be frightfully skittish at times. I'll wait here in case <<2>> brings her back.
Now that Snowy and I have been reunited, we can return to Hiretta.\n\nI imagine she'll demand an apology. After she hugs her bunny, that is.
<<<1>> wiggles her tail and nods toward <<2>>.>

I'm sure if we burn all traces of the plant and find a way to prevent these reekers from using the mine, we can attempt the restoration ritual again. Karthwasten will be saved.\n\nCome on, let's keep moving.
The Crow-Eye once again have a reason to look at you in admiration, outsider.

This one hates being used. Boss Trenlor needed to be dealt with, but there was no honor in how that played out. I should have expected Freyleth's deception. Still, it twists Adusa's tail.\n\nAt least Kathad seems ready to move on now.
The cart that will take us to the coast will pick us up at Ravenwatch Castle. I'll see you there.
Wonderful. Go bash some monsters, cover yourself in guts and glory, and get yourself a piece of the plunder. Easy as Sundas morning. We clear?

Despite occupying the ruins of their lost civilization, few Reachfolk want anything to do with Dwarven devices. That's why Nolovan intrigued me.\n\nWhile you deal with him, I'll seek out Arana's rebels. If I can't find them, they will surely notice me.

Tell Ard Caddach the news. I want to study this machine a little longer. Something here will shed light on Rada's purpose.\n\nI know Rada won't rest until he saves the Gray Host from its ancient curse—no matter what that means for the rest of us.
Lady Belain … is she dead?
<Reproducing this experiment has already yielded great alchemical results for you.>
I wish I knew where Rada al-Saran disappeared to after he activated the orrery. He went to an awful lot of trouble to awaken the Dark Heart and get his hands on that machine.

Arana will be sorely missed. I could use more enemies like her. \n\nThe best way to honor her memory is to keep peace with the wilders who followed her. We stood together against a common foe. No reason not to keep standing.
You're the one who killed Rada al-Saran? Who helped stop the Gray Host? I had no idea. You should have told me. You're a legend!
Look at me, sharing breaths with a damned outsider. Black days are here again, eh?\n\nGo on, rover. Do what you must and I'll do the same.
<Reproducing this experiment has already yielded great alchemical results for you.>
<Reproducing this experiment has already yielded great alchemical results for you.>
Talk to me, harrier. I want to know what happened to Arana and I want to know now.
Oh, darling, we had fun, but now you really must leave.\n\nI have a clan to rebuild, after all.
The spirits must have plans for me, harrier. Why else put me back here in the Reach? I'll help keep Ard Caddach out of trouble for awhile. After that, we'll see.

Thank you for standing by me. I've made so many mistakes in my long existence, but putting my faith in you was not one of them. You trusted me, even when I was unworthy of that trust.\n\nTell my wards—my family—I'm sorry to break another promise.
Good work, partner. It's always a pleasure to fight by your side. \n\nForgive me for saying this, but I hope we don't need to do that again for quite some time.
After everything that's happened, I think I'll enjoy a nice, quiet month at Ravenwatch Castle. Oh, who am I kidding? I'll be lucky if Adusa lets us rest tonight.
You've done the Ravenwatch proud. I don't suppose you'd accept an assignment to reorder all of Count Verandis's records? No? Well, I can look forward to that later. For now, we celebrate!

Now, I must bid farewell to my beloved wards. I've never been comfortable with goodbyes, but I should realize by now that they're rarely forever.\n\nI won't be joining the festivities, but rest assured I will be watching.

It still doesn't feel real to me. So much has happened since we first met that it feels like a lifetime ago. The nightmare is finally over though. I know I won't wake up to find everything as it was, but there's a new dawn at least.

I think that went well. Don't you? I thought it would be best to keep the speeches short. I'm just glad my father agreed to let me take the lead. I don't know that the ard has the patience for one of the Skald-King's epic toasts.

I cannot think of a time or a tale where a Reachfolk and Nord extended a hand to one another unless each was holding a dagger. This may be the first time such a thing's occurred. \n\nMay it not be the last.
If you told me a season ago that the leader of Western Skyrim would share a dais with the Reach-King, I would've laughed in your face. But, here we are.
That was a heartening display. The Reachfolk are often dismissed as savage and beastly, but they have a strong sense of honor. I know that all too well.
That look on your face. I know curiosity when I see it. Very well. I can spare a few more moments before sending you off on your task.\n\nWhat does the outsider in Ard Caddach's court wish to know?
Lady Belain's designs be damned. We must put a stop to this for the sake of my clan. Maybe for the sake of the entire world.
All right, you got what you came for. Now go to the barrow and do what Arana asked.

Go. I'll meet you back at Rebel's Retreat. I want to say a last prayer for the dead before I leave.\n\nMaybe I can free my sister's soul from the darkness that took her. Give her some modicum of peace.
Get … get away from me, you reeker!\n\nYou think a Reach warrior with only one good leg can't gut you? Well think again!

Our business is done, I think, outsider. Unless, that is, you actually find Bthar-Zel. I've never had the gumption to go and look for it myself.\n\nIf you do find it, come back and tell me all about it next time you're in the neighborhood.

Don't worry. Verandis and I have explored scarier ruins than this and emerged to tell the tale. You just worry about finding that keystone.\n\nI'd hate to fend off hordes of clanking monsters for nothing, you know?
It's good to see you, friend. It seems we of the Reach owe much to you.
The spirits will see you safely to Valthume, harrier. After that? I suggest stealth and a strong blade.
Keep an eye on Verandis, harrier. Rada al-Saran was toying with him. He's got plans for your friend, I think.
Mind the shadows and be on your guard. In addition to the mechanical traps and defenders, we know that Lady Belain is also seeking the keystone.

A hard-won victory. Feel pride, outsider. The Spiritblood clan shall remember your accomplishment for all time.\n\nThough it comes at the loss of our first vateshran. This incursion of the Void into the Hollows concerns all the sisters.

You. The thorn that caused me no small amount of irritation in Solitude. You thought yourself so clever, so stealthy, spying on me from the shadows. But the darkness answers to me.\n\nWhy have you come to this forsaken barrow?
We've reached the door. Well done, my friend.\n\nNow let's go through it and try to catch up to Rada and Lady Belain.
Oh, Verandis, look! It's wonderful! Such pretty lights.
Verandis Ravenwatch. I don't believe we've had the pleasure. I am Pentarch Kovan Indoril.
Verandis, my dear, it has been so long! Where have you been hiding yourself? You're not still pursuing that silly little hobby of yours, are you?
Even where dark water flows deep, the blood of those worthy swirls still. Why is this so, member of the Gray Council?
Do you suppose Eeze ever tires of dancing, Verandis? The girl enjoys frolicking in that fountain almost as much as she enjoys warm blood.
Verandis! How good of you to join us! Come, sit! Have a drink with me!

Finally, a moment to pause and reflect! You've a great deal reflect upon, too. You stopped the Gray Host, restored life to Markarth's dead, saved Tamriel from certain peril … that's a rather long list of accomplishments, I must say.

Not many outsiders appear before Ard Caddach's throne and live to tell the tale. Since you're still alive, you must have won his favor. At least for now.\n\nIn Markarth, you're useful or you're dead. Remember that.

By Namira's knickers—what a fight! I never saw anything refuse to go down like that before. I feel honored to have been a part of it.\n\nI wonder who that was? He seemed grateful when he lost. If I hadn't been a part of it, I wouldn't believe it!

<This scroll bears the insignia of the Undaunted and a potent spell, conceived of by the renowned Hroltar the Boaster. When invoked the scroll will empower one's enemies with astonishing power.\n\nThe full incantation isn't short on colorful language.>
We did it. After everything we saw, I felt that maybe we'd find my father dead. But we saved him.\n\nI can't take credit for too much. You did so much for both of us. I'm eternally in your debt.

You want to find Adusa-daro? You're braver than I am, I'll give you that.\n\nLast I saw, she was near that old Dwarven tower sticking out of the mountain. They say it's an ancient lift. She plans to use it to reach the lair of the Lothid clan.
I hope you find more than she has returned to that place. I'll see you there soon, harrier.

We all appreciate what you've been able to provide so far. If you take on any more writs, I will be here.\n\nOur team shipped the supplies you gave us. You should see the smiles on the faces of those who received them.
So this is Arana's army, then. I hope they make up in courage what they lack in numbers.
The darkness no longer scares me. Bring on the Gray Host. We'll fight to the end.
Ah, you've returned! Did you find the shrine and take part in the ceremony?
Friend, you've done more for my people than most Reachmen know. You've changed my view of outlanders, that's for sure and certain.
Who? Who dares stand before the most honored among the Spiritblood clan? Perhaps you wish to learn? To know better the greatest among us?\n\nGawk upon the names that transcend time.

The whispers speak true. Outsiders roam our lands and now enter our home. You believe yourself strong. Fearless. The creatures born from the spirits shall make you fear them.\n\nWhy do you come to us?

I never saw—er, heard—anyone fight like that blond giant and her companion. A whirlwind, they were!\n\nAnyway, I think they headed to Valthume. Whatever was in that letter they found, it certainly lit a fire under her companion.
That Redguard. What a beard he had! I wouldn't toss him out of my bedroll. At least not immediately.\n\nThey wanted to know about Reach history, so I sent them to find a vateshran at Hroldan Ring.
Thanks, partner. I really want to talk to one of the vateshrans and see if they can tell me more about what's in these documents.\n\nIn the meantime, go to Gloomreach and help Sai.

I never imagined to find the means to summon my Shehai here in the Reach. But thanks to you and Lyris, I finally have my spirit sword.\n\nAnd I have my Snow Lily. There's a song in my heart and life is good!

You overcame the Brimstone Den! I can tell you now that most of the challengers who die in here slip and fall in the lava. Glad to see you have more grace. It's a horrible way to go.\n\nAnyway, the Choosing waits for you through this portal.

I knew Sai could summon his spirit sword. He's the bravest, strongest, most loyal man I've ever met. He just had to focus on what really mattered to him. I just didn't expect it to be … me.\n\nI mean, I knew. But still. Now I really know.

I need to report in to Jarl Svana and the rest of the contingent from Western Skyrim—after I quench my thirst. The road we traveled was long and dusty.\n\nRemember, the Reachwind Ritual Site. That's where you'll find Lyris Titanborn.
Verandis. I heard Rada al-Saran sent for you, but I never expected you to show up. I thought you made your position regarding the Gray Host abundantly clear.
You haven't seen my scullery boy around, have you? Always seems to disappear right when there's work to be done.

Well, what have we here? I thought I was the only one of the Brotherhood out this way. Good to see a friendly face. Might need to grab a Gods-Blind-Me together one night, yeah?\n\nListen, watch your back. Things are about to get really bad.

May I … may I just look at your eyes for a moment? I had a companion once who had eyes just like yours. Not a Khajiit, like you. Foundling senche cub.\n\nOh, how I miss her. She wandered off one day and never came back.
Look around at this place. Have you ever seen anything this grand? So many people all in the same place?\n\nI should've come to see Markarth long before now!

I'm so happy to see a fellow amid all these Reachfolk and other races! I could just hug you! I promised Z'en that I'd try to soften all this dead stone with the bounty of nature.\n\nMaybe it'll help these Reach clans achieve harmony with each other.
You haven't seen a short Reachman with white hair, shaven in odd patterns have you? He escaped his lessons with me again.
Dark things tend to happen when the land is angry. Even some Wilders tend to forget that.
Ach! I can't believe those Eagleseers! How can you have a rebellion if everyone just runs off to do whatever they want?
Your travels have taken you far from Briar Rock, freehand. It's good to see you again.
Not a word from Ard Caddach since we got here … I wish I knew why!
I still think what they say about Markarth and the miracle is some thinblood nonsense. The dead, come back to life? Not even a score of witchmen could do it.

I lived through the rise and falls of clans and kings. But in all my years, never have I heard of anything to the like of what's happened in Markarth. The dead returned to life? Did the gods do this for us?
I feel relived to know the rumors we heard on the road are true. The miracle of Markarth is real! I cannot wait to see the rest of my clan again
Well. I hope my recital filled your heart. I best get on my way. Time and hunger wait for no man.
Begone from here, outsider. I don't want your pity.\n\nI will take my punishment. If the chief demands the Blood Price, then I will pay.
I always feel glad to see you. But I may not cross paths with you for the foreseeable future. Off to new lands!
I have read the entrails' message to you truly, wanderer. Do not think you can change your fate with a second reading.

You saved the Crow-Eye clan, and now the Reach itself. I'm sorry I distrusted you. But in my defense, it's not every outsider that can wipe out an army of vampires and werewolves. You're different from outsiders.\n\nThank you.
You again. Need something else I could explain for you? More lessons in politeness? Perhaps a demonstration on how to wipe your arse?
That fool. We nearly had peace between the Six-Ford and the Eagleseer clans. Now it's lost, all because of some foolish vow.\n\nThe blood that follows will be on his hands.
It's all a mess now, thanks to that Six-Ford's lad.\n\nI suppose I need to go and prepare for the next battle with the hated clan.
Mighty big bollocks on that Six-Ford lad, courting under his father's nose. Almost makes me respect him. Almost.
Madearn and Drisene, all this time … I never knew. My son is a fool for choosing a flimsy promise over the well-being of his clan.

I can hardly believe what just happened. I don't know what to say, or what to think. \n\nI'm relieved, of course, but … was Madearn's promise to me the only thing that dashed our hopes of peace between the Six-Fords and Eagleseers? That troubles me.

I know I threw away any chance of our clans knowing peace. But spirits take me, I couldn't abandon my promise. Words can't be unspoken. Not in the Reach.\n\nEslyn must be hurting. I hope this won't sully our friendship, for the future of our clans.
I was afraid what it might mean to force Madearn to give up his vow to Drisene. Despite it all … I'm glad I didn't have to.

Normally I'd tell you to offer congratulations to the happy couple, but this was a strange affair all around. Hopefully their newfound affection for each other won't falter when they have to return to their holdings.
Strange to hear one of our sacred songs sung by outsiders. But beautiful, as well.\n\nMay the spirits always walk beside you, wanderer.
Hircine speed your hunt, harrier.\n\nJust keep Arana safe. If you take that responsibility lightly, you'll not only answer to me, but to all the free clans.

When a wandering hunter arrives bearing an unexpected bounty, that is a good omen. That's how bonds were forged in the days of our ancestors. We have made such a bond, my friend.\n\nRest well, hunter. You shall find only friends here.

Hmm, impressive grit. A shame the Rites will definitely kill you. This cart can take you to Vateshran Hollows right away. Otherwise, head south to find the cave entrance. I'll send word ahead to my clan mate Caddgarn. Speak to him when you get there.
Arana spoke highly of you, harrier, and I trust her judgment.\n\nThe Wayward Guardians could use your help, if you are willing to fight once more.
I thought the gods had cursed me to that fate. As if exile from my clan was not enough.\n\nBut then you came. I see it now. I have been given a second chance.

What a wonder! That these Wayward Guardians would send you to save the lives of worthless exiles.\n\nBut Ardanir claims that exile need not define us. He says that our stories can take a different path. I never believed that was possible. Thank you.
You emerge! And with your skin and teeth intact. I knew from the moment you approached—this one has promise.\n\nI look forward to seeing the shock on Angair's face when I tell him you passed.
Don't worry about me. I'll be fine. I want to see what else I can learn here. Maybe figure out where Rada and Belain have gone.\n\nYou just focus on talking to Arana.
Hey, Verandis wants to see you. It's about the you-know-who with the Dwarf you-know-what.\n\nGods, I hate this spy stuff! Let's just talk plainly, all right?
There you are. Have you seen Arana? She has an idea about those Reach witch prophecies you heard Lady Belain go on and on about. I think you're going to want to hear what she has to tell you.
Can't fight monsters without a sharp blade. Grab what you need before you head into the Choosing.
The Ard seems to trust you.
I'm not sure who you are, but you seem to have The Ard's ear.
Remember, Verandis is waiting for you in Understone Keep. He's already nervous enough as it is, so don't make him wait for you too long, all right?

It's a good thing I arrived when I did. There are not many who could have completed that spell alone.\n\nFrankly, I'm impressed Calis held it as long as he did. Teleportation is one of the more difficult disciplines to master.

You may not have chosen him, but obviously Hircine has chosen you. You know this, deep inside.\n\nWhere your hunt takes you next, I do not know. But you can always rest here when you need a respite from the chase.
Salutations! Wherever you go, celebrations seem to follow! Even if this one is a bit peasantly. But not everyone can have the refined palate of a royal taster.
