Never thought I'd set foot in Markarth except to conquer it. Strange times. Strange, but not entirely unpleasant.\n\nStill, I'll not get comfortable here. Too much Dwarf workings and old stone. May as well live in a barrow.
In all my years, I have neither seen, nor heard of such a miracle as you've delivered today. You must have Shor's own bond with Mother Wolf for her to carry so many lost pups back here.
So, you and Fennorian managed without me I see. Is it true? That the last of the Gray Host has finally joined his brothers and sisters in the grave?
Outsider, Madearn told me about everything you went through to help stop the handfasting between him and Eslyn. That now seems small in comparison.\n\nI'm so grateful you came to my homeland.
I'm glad to see you, outsider! \n\nI can scarce believe everyone you've drawn to this place. Eslyn and I were just remarking on it as we were … catching up.

It's good to see you once more, friend! I can barely believe the same outsider who helped me was involved in such important work! To see everyone who's been brought here by your deeds is inspiring. And it's good to see Madearn and Drisene.
At the start of this day, it seemed the Ravenwatch was doomed. Now I see it is transforming. Into what, Adusa does not know, but I have great hope.
It's a grand occasion you've delivered us to, outsider. I'm glad Medone and I could be a part of it.
Stay back! If you're one of those invaders, be aware that my fellow rebels are right behind the bend!
Away, stranger! I don't deal with outsiders.
The Thornroots didn't stand a chance against you, outsider.
The next tankard I hoist will be in your honor.
Most people with any sense head the other way when they see Briarhearts and Hagravens.\n\nI guess you're not like most people.
You fought like a true Reachman today, traveler.
I cannot tell you how good it felt to see the Thornroots get what they deserved. Thank you.
That dolt Faorin led us into a slaughter, but I guess Medone and you managed to lead us out. The Hillhunters are not finished yet.
We lost a lot of kin today, but thanks to you there are still some of us left. I'll never forget that.

I should return to the Dark Heart soon. I grow weary if I'm away from it for too long. Plus, I need no additional reasons to nod off as I trudge through the Nighthollow Testament.\n\nUntil next time, my friend.

When you're ready, the nearby cart will take you where you need to go.\n\nI carried that letter, but I wasn't permitted to read the words. Tell me, what insights did the Dread Lady share with you? You can trust me. I'm her prophet, after all.
We go to all the trouble of rescuing my manservant, and the first thing he does is start playing with the slime-blobs again.\n\nWhy do I even bother?
Must … must ….
Thank you for helping the long-hair break the sorcerer's curse. These chambers should stand empty, just as my ancestors proclaimed when they abandoned them long ago.
I'll meet you in Gideon after you collect Sombren and Calia from the temple.\n\nI think we've earned a little relaxation—and a slice or two of cake—after everything we accomplished here.

I need to consider and weigh the options concerning this book. It may hold the key to saving the Ambitions and defeating whatever Dagon has planned. Or reading it could destroy me.\n\nLet me think about it back at the temple, then I'll talk to Eveli.

Well, mercenary, hiring you was the best decision I made in recent days.\n\nNow I'm returning to Leyawiin. I much prefer when all the Ivory Brigade has to worry about is the civil war on our border, pirates, bandits, and the occasional evil monster.
As soon as my legionnaires make one more sweep of the area, we'll be returning to Gideon. You should join us there.\n\nA victory such as this deserves accolades.
I refused to believe … but Farrul … Lovidicus … they were right.

We have to inform Commander Ortin about Councilor Abor's murder. I doubt the assassin is still in the fort, but you never know.\n\nPlus, we need to let him know that the servant is still unaccounted for.
Go, and take the Wood Elf with you. My portal will deposit you near this place she called Elden Root.\n\nI will see you again when the time is right, but not before.

Whew, even the swine stench is just like the real thing. You smell like you just had a bath in pig sweat. And guts. And—well you get the idea. I think the conjurers are having a laugh at your expense.
Watch yourself, stranger. I am part of Councilor Faleria's personal guard. I will not hesitate to cut you down if you threaten her.
I promise to remain in Leyawiin Castle and help comb through the records when the scribe arrives.\n\nAt this point, I want to know why someone is trying to kill us. Maybe even more than you do.
Take the scroll to Councilor Lovidicus. He'll know what to do.\n\nI … I need to take care of my husband right now.
Go away, little blobs! I am not your mother!\n\nOh bother, but how will I ever see to my many duties with these slime balls underfoot?

Blessings of Zenithar to you, laborer. I hope you have prospered since we last crossed paths.\n\nThe Primate was most pleased to learn that the Golden Anvil may shine again. He is eager to meet Gavos as well, when he next visits this temple.
What you have done for us, and others like us, will not be forgotten.   \n\nWe will rest here until the others regain their strength. Be welcome and wallow with us, if you wish.

Do as Councilor Lovidicus ordered, mercenary. While you and Eveli track down the vault, I must redouble my efforts and make sure the legates and the countess remain safe.\n\nMy brigadines will be needed again before all is said and done, I'm sure.

Thank you for a charming time, but this is no place for any self-respecting member of the Dark Brotherhood. Grand battles in broad daylight are hardly the sort of thing assassins should be involved in.\n\nI think I hear the shadows calling. Bye.
By the Egg, that would have been a bad place to die. Thank you for freeing us. I am grateful to feel the sun on my scales once more.
Those limp-finned Sul-Xan did not expect you, did they?\n\nI am dry with anger. But I thank you for the rescue.
Thank you, beek-ojel. Today, we are spared from being prey.

We may have lost the old documents to Vandacia, but the scribe came through and provided us a path ahead.\n\nYou and Eveli should go to Gideon. Talk to Governor Keshu. I'm sure she can pinpoint the location of the ojel-bak.
I can't let Destron's death be for nothing. With this book, I think I can help us defeat Vandacia and once again separate the realms.

I miss Destron and I'll never forget him. But I'm going to try to go on. To help Sombren and learn to control my power. It's what my brother would have wanted.\n\nWe'll be at the Temple of Dibella in Gideon if you need us.
We can take it from here, mercenary. I assume Captain Rian has other tasks for you to accomplish.
Our deal is complete. I have my map, Drathas has his father, and you have your gold. Nice and neat, just how I prefer.\n\nI do not plan to stand around much longer. So if you have questions, ask.

I never actually met with Farrul Lupus directly. Everything was done through an intermediary. A mage named Renna. We can find her at the Mages Guildhall in Riften.\n\nMy brother has a cart we can use to make the journey, or I can just meet you there.
The Borderwatch brigadines stand with you. Everyone I can spare will march to Fort Redmane to help you defeat this threat.
This day might have turned out very badly for all of us if you hadn't come along when you did. Thank you.\n\nIf you ever need a friend, you can count on me.

Now that this Borderwatch gig is all settled, Seeks and I need to get back to the Guild before someone else snags an even bigger job. The legend of Lady Twilight won't be born from resting on my laurels.
If Commander Axius asks what happened to us, do me a favor and tell him we got killed or something. \n\nCall me old fashioned, but unlike Lady Twilight over there, I prefer to be forgotten.
I'm glad we're free, but how much longer are we going to have to wait before the commander retakes the fortress?
I'm glad to know we're soon to see the end of this. But I need to rest up while I can. Once we're back inside, I expect to be at the forge non-stop.

I—um, I'm glad to see you got out of there fine. And it sounds like the Painted Eye are nearly dealt with.\n\nSay, there were others working with you, right? One of them, the Wood Elf—what'd she call herself, Lady Twilight? Is she still around?

You need not tell me what happened in the ruin. We could feel the tremors from all the way out here. Even if it's not destroyed outright, its contents will be irreversibly disturbed.\n\nTell me—was it of Barsaebic influence? Or pre-Alessian?

Good to see you! Your advice paid off. No Minotaurs, monsters, or other misadventures befell me on the way to Gideon.\n\nI might not have found the recognition I hoped for, but I'm safe and sound. The curse of Phalevon's horn is broken.
You should get out of here too, stranger. These people … the Unmakers … they're crazy. I think they're preparing to sacrifice people. Why would anyone want to do such a thing?
I know you can keep the Ambitions safe. Just do whatever you need to take care of their problem. \n\nAnd make sure they don't explode. I really don't want anyone to explode.

I would never turn away anyone in need. We will protect the Ambitions for as long as we can, yet I fear my legionnaires will not be able to hold off Vandacia's forces should they attack.\n\nGo to the Temple of Dibella when you're ready to talk to them.
I … might not have thought this through. I guess I didn't really think things would go this far.\n\nLet me go, and you'll never see me again. I swear it.
Calia and Destron. They have no reason to trust me, not any more.\n\nBut I'll still protect them. And somehow, I'll find a way to earn their trust again.

Sombren was only trying to help us. I know that. But he still led us to that evil place.\n\nWhatever Xynaa was doing to us, though, it siphoned off some of my power. I think I can use my fire now. Control it. At least for a while.

Xynaa didn't want to help. She wanted to kill us! How many more of these fanatics are going to attempt to sacrifice us before all is said and done?\n\nAt least I'm in control of my power for the moment. It may not last, but it's better than nothing.

We can finally greet each other in person, mortal. Before we begin the process that will permit the twins to control their powers, I must ask you a single question.\n\nWhy does one who abhors Mehrunes Dagon care what happens to his Ambitions?
Safe travels, my friend. And if you ever find yourself in Gnisis, feel free to drop by!

I owe you my thanks. And I suppose I should thank Bastian as well. I have a feeling he wouldn't have left me in the cult's hands even after I gave him every reason to.\n\nI truly am sorry for sapping him over the head and leaving him tied up.

By the Three, this whole business really opened my eyes. I always thought true wizardry happened in the laboratories and libraries of Tel Naga. But magic is messy. It's dangerous! A second's hesitation can mean death!\n\nRevus taught me that.
You almost forgot your spoiled spoils! That's all right though, Jad'zirri's brew is usually safe to drink for at least a week. And after that it makes a good vinegar!

It feels good to pray at Zenithar's altar once again. Though, I admit it feels too decadent. After decades of praying on the bare floors of the adytum, I fear I'll never be able to rise from a padded pew.\n\nI keep you and Daluion in my daily prayers.
I believe our business has been concluded. Away with you.
Amnis Manor is that creepy house on the south side of the city. I'll meet you there.

Ah, good to see you again. I made sure Bevene's family made it to Gideon safely. They're in rough shape, but I think they'll make it home.\n\nI'm mulling over some uses for these seeds. I want to make sure this was all worth it.

I don't care about the book. I want nothing to do with it. If the Dark Brotherhood thinks I know anything, they'll come after me. And you as well.\n\nYou should forget about Farrul and Leovic and that book. Forget about them and go far, far away.
What's going on here? I demand to be informed!
The twins will be safe here in Gideon while you and Eveli continue your search. The Black Fin Legion will see to that.

Run along. Go back to your time and put your affairs in order. It won't be long before we meet in battle. When I crush you like the pathetic churl you are.\n\nWe shall see each other again soon enough.
Ha! Write about your heroes, and they shall appear!\n\nI was just outlining all the details of what we saw and heard on our adventure. I don't want to forget a single thing!
Pardons, but as much as this one loves idle chatter, there is much work to be done.

Commander Ortin assures me Talaise is fine, but it's not like her to disappear and shirk her duties.\n\nI worry about her, you know? Since our parents died, we only have each other. Damn it, we have to find her!
Misaba is very busy. Lazy servants, hungry brigadines, and inquisitive strangers make this one's job extremely difficult. \n\nPlease, be off with you.
I suppose now I have to do Talaise's chores as well as my own. She owes me one, and I aim to collect.

After you report to the commander, make contact with Councilors Faleria and Vandacia. Faleria went to Tidewater Cave to get her records, and Vandacia works in the Gideon courthouse.\n\nCracked acorns! I suddenly had the weirdest feeling come over me.

If you plan to save this world, make sure the Ambitions do not fall into the hands of the Dagonists. Giving the cult access to such power would be … unwise.\n\nI shall continue my own investigation in the meantime. Farewell, little mortal.
What are you waiting for? I don't want to stay in this place even a moment longer!

You know, whatever it was that Wood Elf friend of yours mixed up has put more pep in my step than a scrib on a lava flow. I'd love to buy a whole sack of the stuff, but he said I got the last of it.\n\nShame. That stuff would put skooma off the market.

Before we part, allow me to offer you some wisdom.\n\nRemember, as you journey through life … all things must pass in order to begin again. Knowing this simple fact eases pain and suffering. Learn to let go, and what was lost will be reborn.
Greetings, my friend. It is a real pleasure to see you again. And to be seen! It appears that I'm invisible to most people. A blessing in surprise, perhaps.\n\nAt any rate, I hope you are well.
You pulled that off like you were a bloody Cygnus Irregular.\n\nHope you've left some of those Painted Eye for the rest of us. Nothing sadder than trudging back home with a full quiver.

Finally, the strange plot surrounding Farmer's Nook has drawn to a close. But, as with all the best tales, the ending of this story gives rise to many new ones.\n\nShall I introduce—or, rather, re-introduce—you to our newest Hopeful?
Well, Igmund's back, and sore as ever. Did kind of miss his complaining. Gets too quiet otherwise.

Good to see you again. Wasn't sure if I'd get to thank you for what you done. Cylle's home now and there's life in the house. In the whole town again. Quite something.\n\nThere's even going to be a show to celebrate.
It is good to see you safe and well, wayfarer. We are meditating on loss. Join, if you wish.

You know, come to think of it, I missed out on a golden opportunity while my stupid brother was a pig. I've heard they can sniff out rare mushrooms with their snouts. I should have had him find me some before we changed him back.\n\nOh well.

Meet me at Bloodrun Cave. Despite your assurances, we need to determine beyond a shadow of a doubt whether the Dark Brotherhood is behind the murders or not.\n\nI'm still not sure I can trust you. You're an assassin and you only just told me!

Determine the truth by all means, mercenary, but do not fall sway to the Dark Brotherhood's lies.\n\nIt would be better if you strike first and ask questions later, after you flush the vermin from their lair in Bloodrun Cave.

The prisoner used some sort of acid to disable the lock. And look, drops of acid lead toward the basement door.\n\nFollow the trail while I alert the Black Fin Legion. The assassin cannot be allowed to escape.
You! You're the one I don't know. Why are you here? I—I didn't run away again! I promise.
Looks like Prince Vaugr and his crew are due for a burial at sea. Good riddance.

Killing what is already dead grants little satisfaction for me, but sending their fetid souls to Sithis offers some consolation.\n\nI am glad to be rid of Prince Vaugr's wither-bones once and for all.
So, Red Annyce is all finished up with Captain Vaugr then, eh? They don't call her the Crimson Shrike for nothing.

Well met, sister! If I had realized you were in the area, I would have suggested we meet for a meal at the Egg and Hammer. The chef makes a superb mud-hopper stew.\n\nI suppose you're chasing me because of the incident at the courthouse, hmm?

You came back? I never did thank you. For … saving me, I guess. I'm glad you did. Mom is finally starting to listen to me. She's even agreed to teach me some real things about sailing. Isn't that great?
Quick! He went out that window! We need to catch him before he gets away!

Salvitto's Estate is north of Gideon, near Blackwood Lake. I'll meet you there. I want to make a quick stop to check on the twins and let Governor Keshu know what we discovered. And to tell her where we're going.\n\nYou know, just in case.
I'll make sure Salvitto gets to Gideon. Turn him over to Governor Keshu. Then I'll meet you in Leyawiin.
Oh good, I didn't miss you! We don't have much time before that ship departs, so let's get moving.
Ah, wonderful! You look simply ravishing in your new attire. I hope it makes you feel as good as you look!
I'm so happy I could cry. If I could. When I get my new mortal form, I'm going to cry.\n\nThank you for letting me stay!
I … I'm not sure. How do nobles do stuff like this on a regular basis?\n\nGo ahead and choose your outfit. I'll find something eventually.
Get on board before we leave without you. We've got a schedule to keep and this is the last ship heading for the event location.
Remember, if you do decide to talk to the other guests, don't do anything to give away your true identity.\n\nAnd make sure you get some rest. The bunks are in the aft cabin, I think.

Just drop the reekers around the perimeter of the chamber. Once you've placed them, give me the signal and wait for the clouds of stench to clear the room. Then you can set Sombren free.\n\nI hope you can hold your breath, though.
So, Vandacia has let some of his pet nobles come by to gawk at his prize? Away, you vultures!
Thank you for getting me out of that place. I am in your debt.
Hmm. I do not know you. Vandacia and his recruitment drives. I prefer the company of long-standing believers, not raw initiates fresh out of the egg.
I don't remember you. This must be your first time experiencing one of Vandacia's events. You're in for a treat, my friend. An absolute treat!\n\nBut tell me, have you known the councilor long?

I'm all for leaping through strange portals into untold danger, but one of us should return to Leyawiin. Councilor Lovidicus and Captain Rian need to know that the Order of the Waking Flame is our real enemy.\n\nBe careful in there, all right?

Thank you for helping my son. He has grown so much since I last saw him. Now he seems strong. Confident in a way I never expected.\n\nFor now I just want to be rid of this place. Drathas can escort me home.

Let us hurry. We need to investigate the place where my tribe first apprehended the Imperial lieutenant. \n\nHopefully, we can pick up where he left off. And do not worry, if we run into any trouble my quick reflexes will save us.
I'm kind of beat after—croak!—all that. You should talk to my—bok! bok!—sister.

I'm sure that you and my sister have a really interesting story to tell. I'm just not sure I want to hear it.\n\nSecrets of the Longhouse Emperors, Daedra, strange books … I gave up the life of an adventurer to avoid those kinds of complications.

Thank you for your part in this. Our intention was never to frighten the citizens here. But we did not listen to them when they expressed their concerns. We simply went about our business. \n\nThis is just as much our fault.
Our sanctum was spacious, but the world outside … it's huge! I think … I think this is going to take some time to get used to.
Eveli led us through the wilderness and into this city. Everything seems so strange and different. I didn't see any molten rivers, and the sky is an unusual shade of blue.

We need to return to the surface and see how the others fared. The fact that the lures lie dormant now has to be a good sign.\n\nI will hurry back to Naheesh Nurwul and tell her of our bravery and success!

I'm going to stick around and deal with a few more of these Waking Flame cultists. I still have a little anger to work off after that attack on my sanctuary.\n\nI suggest you return to Leyawiin Castle with all due haste.
Ah, my partner in hilarity! Back for more pranks?\n\nI have a great one for you today. A big laugh!

Hutan-Tzel will be forever grateful for your assistance, outsider. Not only that, you've helped us learn a valuable lesson. One we were sorely in need of. \n\nIt's time to look forward to a new future, and not be ensnared by the fear of our past.

My gratitude is overflowing, like a swollen river. If not for you, there would have been many more deaths.\n\nMy punishment awaits me, though I do not know if it will ever feel like enough for all the hurt I caused.

Olik's actions were foolish. These lures have lain dormant for a reason … the magic within them is dangerous. Still, the actions of the past cannot change the present. What is done cannot be undone.\n\nBut we can ensure that no one else gets hurt.
Pain in my arse as she is, I wouldn't trade her for the world. You have my gratitude for finding her.\n\nI'll make sure she doesn't run off again. It just won't be by grounding her.
You talk to the assassin. I'll watch the others.

We did it, friend! We fearlessly pursued the truth, cut through our foes with wamasu-like strength, bested our enemies and came out victorious! \n\nAnd I did not get terribly injured! This is a great day.

I shall inflict my vengeance on these cultists through you, crow-friend! Such impropriety must be punished.\n\nOnce the Court is freed, we will feast on the squishy eyes of these peasants! Come, come! We must hurry!
Work is plentiful in Leyawiin, provided you have the steel required to see the job done.\n\nSo, can I add your name to my list?
Ah, hello, adventurer! I have need of someone with your kind of mettle. It's dangerous work, but there is a reward if you're so inclined. What do you say?

It broke my heart to see my brother like that. His face contorted in hope and fear. When he finally took my hand he was shaking and sobbing. I haven't seen Heseph cry like that since we were children.\n\nI really hurt him.
Back to scrubbing floors and washing dishes for nary a drake. What a glorious life I live.
You must know that Bugtail has not forgiven you, but this one does understand your reasons. Perhaps, one day, we will find accord.\n\nFor now, leave Bugtail to his grief.

Hello again …! Right, the blankness in your eyes reminds me that you do not know this face. Porcelain face.\n\nIt's—oh, wait, Alchemy said that no one should know who I was before. I am Dreamer now. I'm going to be an actor!
Why, if it isn't my favorite juggler of daggers. I knew you took a fancy to me the moment we met, but I didn't expect you to follow me all the way out to Blackwood!
My rival returns! Do you seek to pit your dancing skills against mine once again? Or have you simply come for the beautiful scenery?
How wonderful to see you again. Have you come to spread the wonders of Nord culture to Farmer's Nook? Or did you leave Rigurt behind on this journey?
Out here by the water's safest, if you ask me. Wide open, creaky boardwalks, no surprises.\n\nNow go on. Bother those strange Elves if you must bother somebody.

Good, good. Slivers of bright sun might poke through this storm with your help. \n\nLet's start with Elossi, the Sudden Gust. She lives on the outskirts of town in a hut to the northwest. I should join you so that … she doesn't kill you on sight.

I should have suspected your ultimate goal when I saw you traveling with Nuxul. His reverence for the legend of the Winds is unmatched.\n\nWe were indeed powerful together. So, I understand the appeal. I promise to work with the others, if they agree.
Just pet the dog. It's harmless. Oh, Tertia, you idiot. No wonder he hasn't ….\n\nIs there something you want? I'd like to be left alone right now.
I'll be surprised if you get anything from Otumi-Ra aside from the stench of spirits. Now go. I gave you what you want. And, I have things to do that are actually important.

When this is all over, Lovidicus is going to have much to explain. Why he kept this from the rest of the legates for as long as he did just baffles this one.\n\nAnd now we must stay locked in this castle like common prisoners? Dark Moons, indeed.
Are the legates in danger, too? Or just Lovidicus and the councilors? And what about Countess Caro? I raise the spine of trepidation and hope the brigadines can keep us all safe!
… don't … eat the plate, too …. Just one more …. Those frogs … dancing ….
That did not go nearly as well as I hoped it would. Meer-Ta clearly has his own agenda at the moment.\n\nWe should find Otumi-Ra, though. If we only have the two Winds, it is still better than none.
Great. He is awake. Now, please, convince him to join our cause. Someone with his strength would be invaluable.

Ugh! What horrific stench of dead mules and fried dung have you thrust upon me? All I wish is a gentle slumber under the open skies and upon the … mud. Does not a retired fighter for peace deserve such rest?\n\nSpeak, brigand!

I shall gather my implements of justice and meet you in the village. And probably drink the rest of this ale. For courage!\n\nRemember, place the banner upon the highest cliff above my hut. That'll bring Meer-Ta to the fight.

Ugh, it is good to see you. At least, I think that is you. I could be having ale-visions. Again.\n\nAnyway, you have done it. The Winds have reunited, ready for battle. Because you convinced them. Well, two of them at least.
Look, up above us. Prisoners from the village kept for sick entertainment. How many of them are thought dead, never to return home?\n\nI can release them, but I'll need your help.

I can feel the power surging in me once again. Such a battle!\n\nDo you think you can help me with this thing? In my youth I could topple three such pillars with a swift kick. But all things age, even me!
Destroy that banner, and the pretend warlord's followers will scatter like plague rats. I would see to it myself, but some of these books are fascinating.\n\nThey will go well in my research library.
I wish you adventurers would leave well enough alone. The brigadines have enough troubles to hold at bay without vagabonds stirring up ungodly ruins.
I can't believe Liam's gone. I never should have gotten him involved with this. My parents will never forgive me.
This whole situation … it's gone roots up faster than a Nord eats pie ….

I'll start the search in Leyawiin. That's where Chief Councilor Lovidicus was, last I heard. Think he's helping to govern the city or something.\n\nOnce I get the lay of the land, I'll send word to you. You know, in case you still want to help and all.

You never cease to intrigue me, little mortal. Is that the distinct scent of Mehrunes Dagon and the Deadlands that lingers about you like a cloud of fleshflies?\n\nNever mind about that. Tell me what you learned and how you ended up in Dagon's realm.

Tents, mud, and horse dung. I can't say it's as heroic a setting for a last stand as I imagined. I never thought about the actual smell of a military camp. How could you without ever experiencing it?\n\nBut like these soldiers, I'm ready to fight.

I've never seen Galos like this before. \n\nBevene always had him laughing, smiling. Now he's filled with such hatred. We're going home to bury her, I hope that will help bring peace to what's left of my family.

I can hardly look these Argonians in the face after what the Sul-Xan put us through. I know it wasn't them that tortured us and killed my mother, but they remind me too much of those monsters. I won't be satisfied until the Sul-Xan are wiped out.
Well, at least someone's happy after all this. Don't get me wrong. I'm glad to be alive, but all I feel is numb after all I've been through.
You helped us keep peace with the Argonians, so we'll stand with you. You can count on me and my brigadines.

I know it is a great honor to mince words with the Duke of Crows, but you must hurry, crow-friend! The time is nigh! The Blackfeather Court must not be trapped in this undeserving place for a moment longer.\n\nGo, disrupt their ritual!

I can tell by the look on your face that my tip yielded results. No, I don't want to hear the details. If I get any more involved in this without an actual contract, my matron will skin me alive.\n\nNow go away. I'm trying to be inconspicuous.
You aided our village in its time of need. The Winds deliver aid to you in return. Your enemies will not expect what's coming.\n\nWhen the battle starts at Fort Redmane, we will be at your side.
I've heard talk about Rian Liore. Glad to be working with him. If Vandacia's soldiers test us in battle, they won't stand a chance.
I, the Zephyr Eternal, stand with you against these creatures. They shall tremble in the face of my cunning!
May the currents of the swamp drown your enemies and carry you home! The Third Wind stands ready to slay any who threaten Blackwood.
Glad to see Mirri got her brother free. Gladder still you two bothered with me along the way. I won't soon forget that.
What do you want? Gems, gold, jewels? Whatever you want, it's yours. Just don't harm me!
There you are. On your feet.\n\nI know magical translocation can really upset the stomach. Just take a moment and get your bearings, all right?

You return. I was unsure if we would ever see the hero of Rockgrove again. Yet, here you stand, triumphant.\n\nBefore it closed, a flock of souls flew out from the gate. I sense they have returned to the Hist where they belong. Did you kill Xalvakka?
I cannot believe the strength you showed. A hundred of our warriors would not have the skill you possess.\n\nI admit that I doubted you. I erect the spine of gratitude for your courage.

News travels quickly through the roots. Your triumph over that Sul-Xan horde brings some comfort after all that we lost. And I understand you helped send the souls of my root-siblings back into the cycle. Deepest gratitude.
Since the attack, my wares have behaved strangely. The stones shudder and glow without cause. \n\nBut I promise I have tested each one and they will all work well for your needs.
Please! You've got to help me!
It's no use, stranger. Save yourself if you can. I'm done for.
Please! These Sul-Xan, they're monsters! Don't leave me to die here!

You must have more time on your claws than I do. Plus, it's mighty brave of you to go up against an ancient Argonian curse. \n\nWell, if you really want to help this Lady Laurent, you can find her near the shrine. It isn't too far from here.

Featherless! What a wonderful celebration these wingless giants have thrown in our honor!\n\nWe must fill the sky with our cries of victory. Shriek our accomplishments for all to hear. Shriek! Shriek!

I decided to stop by for the celebration. Try a bit of the local fare before slipping back into the shadows.\n\nI know you're going to miss me, but I have a feeling we'll meet again. People like you usually wind up on a contract eventually.
Welcome, traveler! Why don't you sit back and enjoy the show? I certainly am!
Stand well clear, my friend! My performance is hot, hot, hot!
Care to dance? Take the lead, follow suit, or simply watch and cheer! Whatever tickles your fancy!

I see you managed to reunite Mirri and Liam. I could tell the two of them were close when we met. Thank the Divines for that, because I don't know if she'd have gone to such lengths for us otherwise. No, I think she would have.
Perhaps when this is all over, we can stop hiding. I look forward to proudly proclaiming my place in the Order of the Waking Flame.
I've been Councilor Vandacia's most ardent supporter. Even when some of the others called for a new vision, I urged patience. And see? We'll all soon be rewarded!
The Lord of Fire and Flood has blessed our holdings a thousandfold, yet Vandacia claims that even more will soon be ours.\n\nI can't wait to see what he has brought us here to witness.
It is good to finally see a return on our investment. Vandacia and the order have required a huge amount of gold these past few years … especially since the fall of our beloved Emperor Leovic.
A little piece of Gideon here in the Deadlands. What will Vandacia come up with next?

True Sworn! Vandacia's personal guard! I dealt with them back at Leovic's retreat. The place where I found this strange book. What did Lyranth call it? The Mysterium Xarxes?\n\nJust stay alert. They may not be the only things protecting these halls.
Those Sul-Xan are savages. We owe you and your friend our lives, walker.
Kyne's blessings to you, hero. I did not think we would ever see her sky again.
Looks like Gideon isn't far from here. Once we've tended to our wounds, we'll make our way there. Nice tusking work in there, by the way.
Remind me never to get dressed up for a romp through Oblivion again. This fancy outfit threw off my aim ever so slightly!
So, be honest. I look ridiculous in this outfit, don't I?

I am glad you were able to rescue Liam. I could not look Mirri in the face if she had fished a bitter, old lizard from the mire at the cost of her own loved one.\n\nIf more Dark Elves were like them there would be fewer Argonians like me.
You should join the rest of the guests up at the keep.
Councilor Vandacia better not be wasting our time. I want a true revelation. Why else would I donate so much gold to his cause?
Bother someone else. Can't you see we're having a private conversation?
May the Lord of Destruction grant you power, brother.
We do all the work, but do we get to share in the wine and the eatables? No!\n\nTake your fancy-arse clothes and get to the keep with the rest of the high and mighty.
I need to get the ship ready for the return voyage. I suggest you find your way to the keep before you miss all the festivities.
Thought I was finished there. Mirri too. I was praying to the Three that she wasn't going to share my fate. Someone was listening, because you're a real godsend.
Not now, citizen. Can't you see I have my hands full at the moment? I'm sure a guard or one of my brigadines can assist you.
Apologies. I heard you stumbling about and thought it might be Councilor Jirich.

They sorted out everything at the keep from the sound of things. One less thing to worry about.\n\nStill haven't heard a peep from down the well, though. Starting to think Bertio couldn't find that ring.

The whole affair has left poor Scipion so dreadfully tense, he collapsed from exhaustion as soon as we got back. He has such a fragile disposition. \n\nDon't worry about him, I won't let him out of my sight.

While you sabotage the dead drops and taint his wine, Iulius and I will write a signed letter to make his blood boil. \n\nThen it's just a matter of combing the stinking depths of Leyawiin until we find someone that can put the letter in his hands.
Well, that was my last skewer! Another day serving … mostly satisfied customers!
A murder? Here in the fort? Who would commit such an atrocity?\n\nGo, do what the commander ordered. I have my own duties to perform.

Still standing, chum? Legs aren't wobbling from fear or drink? No, I don't suppose I need worry about that for someone with your epic fortitude.\n\nVoss! Do you see? The villagers join us. Our arrival gives them hope. This is your work!

Ah, you arrive. And you managed to rouse Otumi-Ra. An impressive act, especially for an outsider such as yourself. I feel grateful for your efforts in bringing us back together.\n\nNow, however, we shall see how you fare in a fight.

If I didn't trust Keshu and her Argonians to protect me, I'd flee right now. I'm sure there are plenty of people in Gideon who will want me dead for what I know.\n\nBut, I'm staying. Granna Cerise was a hero, and I won't let her down.

Are you to thank for our freedom? Seeing the crumpled remains of that monster stills the raging river within me. I can now gladly rejoin with the Hist.\n\nYou have only one task left, savior. Smash the sigil stone to close the portal. End this.

Such great relief to be free of that creature. And by an outsider, it seems. Perhaps the tribe will listen now about the risk of isolation. Nice to be vindicated in my death.\n\nOnly one task left for you, ojel. Break the sigil stone and send us home.
Remember, the ruins your friends talked about is north of Gideon.\n\nMay beauty, love, and affection bless you all!

I do not think we will have much trouble rebuilding. Plenty of supplies in the marsh. And, of course, we have the best blacksmith who ever wallowed to craft our tools.\n\nMy spine feels electric from all this hope. Not quite used to it.

I don't even know where to begin. My sister and I haven't seen each other in twenty-five years! She remembers me as a two-year-old child, and I don't remember her at all.\n\nWhat if we have nothing in common besides a name?

There you are! Do you hear the cheers raining upon us like … rain? But warm rain, that moistens the scales and makes such soft muds.\n\nThey call out for the Winds, but that includes you, my friendly killing wanderer. Do not forget what you did.

I offer my upright claws in gratitude for your assistance in freeing the villagers. No creature should remain imprisoned like that. Away from their kin.\n\nStonewastes stands free due to your efforts. Keep your motives hidden. Soak in the praise.

Ah, it's you. I see you made it through relatively unscathed. And you managed to follow my instructions—twice. I saw the banner burn.\n\nQuite the accomplishment for someone who consistently puts themselves on death's threshold.
I do hope Bastian understands that he won't be invited to the wedding. My parents were quite put out at his sudden departure.

Do not worry for your friend. The dryskins of Gideon and the children of the Hist do not always agree, but in the end, they do as the Black Fin Legion says.\n\nIf the Dibella-worshipers come for Faric, they will have to deal with me.
No … no … you go ahead. I am just … going to stay here …. For a bit.
These Imperials show up and suddenly our people go missing? Hist take me, this is no coincidence! If you're here to help, you should kill this dryskin outright!
After we punish this Imperial, I shall claim his shoes as my own.\n\nWhat? They are finely made.

I don't know why Heem-Jas attempts to find help to absolve the Imperials of their obvious guilt. He showed up a month ago and has insisted on performing heroic acts … despite our insistence that we have no need for them.
This is it. Our chance to drive out this warlord Naxhosa and his thieves. The Winds will take back our village once and for all.
The Winds have returned! Naxhosa and his cretins have no chance! They will take back the ruins and our village!
I was out on a hunt when Naxhosa attacked. Now I am ready to return the favor and avenge those that we lost.
I'm nervous. I mean, yes we have the Winds here, but will it be enough? Naxhosa killed Satul-Sa. What if he kills the others?
Naxhosa killed my egg-mate, and ransacked my hut. May the fury of the Winds scatter them like fallen leaves.
The fear is gone. Naxhosa is out, and those we lost can rest now. I hope his defeat spreads like leaves in the fall wind.
I'm … so tired. But, we're free. I plan to wallow in the mud and then bake in the sun. A delightful celebration.
With the Winds at our side, I knew there was nothing we could not achieve.\n\nAnd my thanks to you, friend. I hear that you did much to help our humble village.
I had lost hope before you came. Then, the Winds returned. Like the sun rising to warm my scales, I could feel promise again. Blessings to you and your eggs.
I will write a song about this day, and celebrate the Winds who came to our aid once more.\n\nAnd you, stranger, who took the time to help our small village.

All people must rely on their wisdom to survive these moments of despair. Lashing out thoughtlessly and without preparation can only bring certain death.\n\nStocking up on my fine wares might just be the wisest decision you could make!

Tell Inalieth that Vayzah hopes she is all right and worries for her. This one would have stood up to the innkeeper and made him see reason, had I been here when the coins were taken.\n\nInalieth is no thief.
Who would believe that little boy I brought to Glenumbra would grow up to be such a fine man? His mother would be so proud.
I was told to make sure this letter reached you directly, mercenary. I am to remain until I am sure you have read it.

The Wood Elf awaits you in Leyawiin Castle. She appeared anxious to get on with your investigation and doesn't seem the patient sort.\n\nI suspect she might leave without you if you don't get there soon.
Oh, hey, I almost forgot! I have something for you!
Out with it, I'm too busy for pleasantries and dribble at the moment.
I feel a like a great weight has lifted from my scales. Return any time, wanderer. You always have a home in Rockgrove.
I haven't seen much activity in awhile. It looks like the Sul-Xan have cleared out. Even the geysers are calmer. What could be the meaning of all this?
We can return to our homes safely. All due to your strength. Carry our gratitude on your shoulders wherever you travel.
I'm actually glad you found us. I didn't want to leave without an explanation, but I'm afraid that Calia doesn't have a lot of time.
Isn't it exciting? This is the day we've long been awaiting … the revelation of the Ambitions of Mehrunes Dagon!
Welcome to the celebration, mercenary! There are many here who wish to thank you and share a drink or two.\n\nBut where are Sombren and Calia? I expected you to bring them with you.
Get to Leyawiin Castle as quickly as you can. Eveli wants to move out before that traitor Vandacia beats us to the hidden vault.

I cannot thank you enough for rescuing Clairene. I know I made a dreadful mistake in the past. I promise to make it up to both Clairene and her brother. \n\nBastian seems like a … a good man. I … I will be proud to call him brother, too.

Haven't we already had this conversation, sister? Tell your little Wood Elf friend that we are not her enemy and go find the real killers. \n\nYou know that the Dark Brotherhood doesn't play coy. If this was our doing, we would proudly admit it.
Remember, you'll find Eveli in the governor's mansion in Gideon. She said she'd wait for you before continuing her investigation.

You have my gratitude. Without your help, I would never have discovered how to quell the volcanic vents. Perhaps in time, I will puzzle out how exactly they became active again in the first place. But for now, I am content to merely thwart disaster.

Heroic friend! I am very glad to see you alive and well. It is a shame I could not fight in the fierce battle with you and lend you my incredible strength, but a great warrior such as yourself proved victorious anyway!

A pleasure to see you again. Many brigadines, myself included, have been quite impressed with the stories we've heard of your exploits. I suppose I shouldn't be surprised, given what you did for us at Hutan-Tzel.
This party is exactly how I like them. Keshu the Black Fin really knows how to throw a celebration. Reminds me of the feasts that Otumi-Ra throws. We might be up until the morning frogs sing.
It is time to feast and make merry! Where is the cake? Where is the drink? Point me to the games of strength. None of these dryskin beekos shall leave this party unchallenged!

A day that started in darkness and fear has brought me a miracle beyond imagining. The loss of my family all those years ago almost broke me. To find out now that I am not the only Hallix left? I hardly know what to think.\n\nHow is this possible?
Time to make things right and figure out who was behind this. Let us head to the xanmeer. There is no time to waste!
Report to Governor Keshu in Gideon. I got the impression that time was of the essence.
No! Get back! I need to get out of here!
How did you get in here?! Go! Out of my way!
No! This wasn't supposed to happen!
I should have known better than to come here! Get out of my way!
I don't know how you did it, but I won't forget this!! MOVE!
Ah, little mortal, I was wondering when you were going to arrive. And where did you get that outfit? Is that really what passes for the height of fashion among the Tamriel elite this century?
I told Sombren we should have talked to you before coming out here. But he was so insistent.
I knew it was only a matter of time before the Fang-Furls came for those dryskins. They should have left Blackwood while they still could.
It truly is a tragedy. I hope the Fang-Furls don't think we had anything to do with the Avernos' affairs. Divines forbid!

Come on, we don't have time to talk to my brother right now. \n\nWe need to find Councilor Lovidicus. If he's still alive, we need to do everything possible to keep him that way. If he's not … then Vandacia has to pay.

What a great party! I must ask a favor, though. Please don't let my sister drink too much. She has no tolerance and gets tipsy rather easily. What am I saying! She gets drunk and it's rather amusing.\n\nMaybe it's better if you just let her indulge.

Thanks for getting me out of Vandacia's clutches. I thought I could handle myself, but the cultists took me unaware and would have sacrificed me to Mehrunes Dagon if not for your timely arrival.\n\nGo see Eveli. The twins and I have much to discuss.
You return. I do hope you have good news for me, and that you're not just here to strike up conversation.
Another Ambition? It seems like you're collecting us like a child gathers marbles. Still, how can you be sure he's just like us?
Is this Sombren speaking true? Is he really an Ambition?
If you keep helping us out like this, mom's liable to adopt you, for which I apologize ahead of time.

I watched the councilor head off this morning, the same as every other day. She keeps to a regular schedule. That's why I came to Captain Rian straight away when she failed to show up for her meeting with these nobles.
I'm not sure how I feel about the Ivory Brigade employing mercenaries, but if you can help find Councilor Jirich ….\n\nPlease, do everything you can. The councilor, she's a good person.
Hiring a common sellsword? I thought Captain Rian and his Ivory Brigade were better than that.
Isn't it wonderful? Such a romantic story I've written for myself! But I feel like there's much left to discover. This party is sure to involve some steamy goings on as well.
You made the right decision having Yisara keep me around. We will be very happy together, the muse and the writer!
As pleased as I am by the return of my antique, I do believe that our business was successfully concluded.\n\nI have no further use for you, so toddle off to Steamfont and leave me to my business.

It seems you have done well, little mortal. I hear you killed Mehrunes Dagon's high priest and stopped the planes from merging.\n\nI find you to be … interesting. I will remember that the next time I require the assistance of a mortal agent.
That is the entirety of Keshu the Black Fin's message. She awaits you in Gideon, so dally no longer.
It's good to see you, mercenary. Enjoy yourself at the party. You certainly earned it.
You have the look of someone seeking something, beeko. Perhaps you have been drawn here like me?
Ooo, fancy party. Look at you making friends in all the high and low places!\n\nI bet a few of these folk have a plump pouch in their drawers.
Have you ever seen Sai Sahan?\n\n No, wait, don't tell me! If you have, I'll be jealous!
If I repent fervently enough, Nocturnal may show me mercy.
Try not to draw any unnecessary attention, would you? We already stick out like a sore thumb with Erilthel gaping over the scenery.

It's good to see you, friend. I wanted to make sure you knew how thankful I am for rescuing Stibbons from all that slime. Good help … well, mediocre help … is so hard to replace.\n\nOh, and I heard you saved Blackwood. Congratulations on that.
A party was just what I needed to calm my nerves after what happened at the xanmeer.\n\nIt's sort of refreshing to attend a function where I am not the primary servant doting on the crowd.
The task is finished and the rite is complete. As is our business here.\n\nI must return to the heart of the marsh to deliver the news. Until we meet again. You have my thanks.
Ah, greetings! I heard you're to blame for all this reckless frivolity. No great surprise there, eh? Well done!\n\nI'll try not to knock anything over or set anything on fire. No promises, though!
Honor to you and you house, sera. It's good to see you again.
You should have seen the look on Liam's face when I invited him to this. There, look, you can still see the leftover wide-eyed disbelief!\n\nI can hardly believe it myself.
Mirri said you were involved in some big adventure, but I never thought she meant literally going to war with a Daedric Prince!
The House of Reveries couldn't pass up attending such a lustrous affair, even if we aren't the main attraction.\n\nI always knew you were lead material. Bravo!
You sow the seeds of prosperity wherever you tread, laborer! Zenithar smiles upon your work, as do we all.

I wanted you to know how appreciative I am of what you've done for us. Not only did you reveal Vandacia for the traitor he was, you took him down and saved Blackwood.\n\nCountess Caro and the Chamber of Legates thank you. You're always welcome here.

You're not wearing that dashing outfit I sold you? If today's celebration is not the perfect occasion to dress up, I don't know what is.\n\nPerhaps you should visit my shop again to freshen up your wardrobe, hmm?

Everyone's been talking about the things you've done for Blackwood. I had no idea you'd been so busy! I find myself edified, enlightened, and exhilarated by the tale of your heroics!\n\nPhalevon himself could not have done better.

It is good to see you again. And to learn that your heroism did not end with my friends and I. \n\nI must thank you again for what you did for us. Destroying the Idol of Xulunaht continues to have a lasting impact.
In a party with this many people, I find it quite simple to sneak extra drink unnoticed. A little misdirection and someone's food vanishes from their plate.\n\nJust a little game I play with myself.

I had no plans to leave my cavern, where the magic of the eternal flow. But I had to see this celebration for myself.\n\nIt seems I made a wise decision. The drinks here taste more refined than Otumi-Ra's bug-water. Perhaps I may learn the recipe.
I will bear witness. Do not fail me.\n\nNow, speak to my acolyte and find the cowardly fools who dared to steal from me.
My mother can't fend for herself. I don't know what I was thinking when I agreed with Darene. I need a job that's less likely to get me stabbed in an alleyway or locked up in the city jail.
The mix of Nibenese, Argonian, and Khajiit in this area fascinates me.
So this is what it's like to be part of an audience? It's much more cheerful than watching silently from the shadows. I especially like the clapping and cheering.
This isn't a crime, I'm allowed to be in here.
A word of advice, traveler … if you're trying to get anything done in Gideon, I'd suggest going to Keshu the Black Fin directly.
I erect the spine of gratitude. Do not let Tee-Wan's desire for discretion worry you. \n\nPlease, go to the graveyard. Help him if you can.
I erect the spine of welcome, visitor. Stonewastes is not in the best condition to greet you, but please let us know if we can assist you in any way.
Hmm. I should've seen that coming.\n\nI'd better inform General Keshu. With any luck, Xocin will find Xyria and they can keep each other safe.
That's Xocin. Impulsive as ever. \n\nDon't worry. That wasn't your fault. What's important is that we at least know what's going on now. We are egg-siblings, and we will always look out for him.
Xocin this, Xocin that. I thought you were here to talk about my accomplishments. \n\nGo to Doomvault Porcixid and bother the ambassador there. Leave me be!
I never thought I'd have to watch Borderwatch itself.
The Imperials fail to see how the land itself rebuffs them, yet they keep trying to possess it. This lack of awareness disturbs me.
You look unharmed! I'm so glad.\n\nTell me, did you manage to take any notes inside the ruin?
The dryskin with the shiny head did it, or so I heard. Went into the place of old stones and awakened a dreadful curse.\n\nNo matter. Sithis takes us all in the end.

Right, so turns out vampires are in fact not immune to fire. Who would have thought it?\n\nAnd, I forgot to tell you which part of Elsweyr I was going to again, didn't I? I'm so forgetful—especially when I'm in front of my heroes, I get all nervous!
The dryskins entered the place of stone and awoke an ancient evil. Now a curse hangs over us all!\n\nStupid dryskins.

I told Mirri I'd let it go. She didn't have to take on this problem for me. And drag you along with her. I never wanted to saddle my children with my problems, like my father did with me, but I've gone and done it anyway.
Retrieving the ritual stone is a victory all on its own. Do not question your decision, friend.\n\nI'm closer to being with Xyria again now than I have been in years.

I know I cannot alter your decision, but the choice you have made is truly a shame. No good will come of these eggs. Nocturnal commands death and shadow, and you have only invited more of that into the world.
This is hard enough without you watching, n'wah. Kindly leave my grave in peace.
You have my sincerest thanks. Nocturnal will surely smile upon us both today for helping to save her loyal servants. \n\nShadows cloak your way, friend.

The Blackfeather Court will not forget this insult! The Mistress does not want her favored servants used like puppets.\n\nIf we see any more cultists, we will peck them to ribbons and feast on their eyes. Feast!
You have truly saved Takaano's future as a mage. And Arelette's! Especially Arelette's.
I can't b—bawk … I can't b—bawk—dammit! I can't believe Takaano turned me into a chicken!\n\nNext time we practice I am the one trying out new spells. Bacaw! Oh, lord ….
Can it be? They're gone? And the Winds have returned? \n\nPraise the bark and soil. My egg-mates … they can rest now.
I can hear cheers for the Winds. They succeeded, didn't they?\n\nI knew they would return. The Winds have always protected us.
I still can't believe that Satul-Sa is gone.\n\nBut I hear the Winds out there. Maybe the light on our village is dawning on a new day.
I am sorry that I doubted you, ojel. I heard you aided our village and brought the Winds back to us.\n\nThank you. You've done more than I could.
Now that the Winds are back, we have hope.\n\nI have my life still. Like the trees around me, I can take root and grow from here.
Thank you for all you did. A new season falls on our village.\n\nI will be all right soon. There is a great deal to be done, and I'll make sure I do my part.
You're alive! Were you successful? Did you manage to destroy the Sul-Xan's ritual tools?
The Lut-Eileel bandits are gone and the Winds have returned to us.\n\nMaybe this is a new time for our village. I shouldn't be so hasty to seek out a new home.
I should be more trusting of outsiders, but after the bandit attacks, trust was hard to find.\n\nThank you for your help. It will not be forgotten.
You're back! Did you have any trouble finding the bugs?
May the spirits leave you in peace. Safe travels.

Agh, it's so cold! What do you think you're doing? And it stinks! What did you throw on me?\n\nWait, what's this? A gold piece in my pocket? And in this one, it's my father's ring! I think my luck has changed! This is the start of a new day for Leric!

You're the first bit of hope I've seen in a long while. I don't know if it'll work, but talking to the Winds can't hurt.\n\nGo see Nuxul, near the center of the village. He's overseeing the wounded from the last attack. He'll know what to do next.
No more fortunes for you today, my friend. Looking at the future of one so bright as you makes Zahsbi's eyes hurt.
I think I will just see myself back to Gideon. It turns out that I am not as adventurous as I thought.
I hear ya! Noisy little chits. These ones are always going on about this great treasure they hid. Think they have to shout since my ears aren't what they used to be, but I can hear just fine.
That brief look of repulsion was just a startle response, right? Surely she didn't hate this or lost her good opinion of me.
I knew I never should have let him buy that armor in Senchal. It's awful. But if I tell him to change, it will burst his ego like a deflating netch.

Summerset Isle, the ancestral home of all Elves. Fair warning—our cousins in the Aldmeri Dominion can be a prickly bunch, but our spies indicate something is amiss at the Crystal Tower. They need an outsider's perspective.\n\nSomeone like you.

Seems this portal leads to Blackwood—on the southern border of Cyrodiil. I read an intelligence report about a series of high-profile murders with links to the region. Daedric mischief, too.\n\nA warrior like you could do some real good there.

It appears this one leads to Bleakrock—a frigid Nord holding north of Eastmarch. For this gate to choose such a remote location … something important must be taking place there. The Gallery is beckoning you to face it.\n\nReady to brave the cold?

This portal leads to Elsweyr. The home of the cat-folk is well-worth visiting, especially in light of recent events. Reports indicate that Dragons reemerged there. Dragons! Hard to believe, but it's true.\n\nThe Khajiit could definitely use your help.

That's Khenarthi's Roost—a Khajiiti isle with emerging ties to the Aldmeri Dominion. Sea Elves have been flexing their muscles in that part of the Topal Bay. Competing interests could lead to bloodshed.\n\nSomeone like you could set things right.

Stros M'Kai. It's a fascinating island with rich Dwarven and Redguard history. Alas, it's been largely overrun by pirates.\n\nIf the Gallery elected to open a portal to the island, something extraordinary must be occurring there. So? Ready to set out?

This portal leads to Vvardenfell. Fascinating, given that the Dark Elves only recently opened it to outsiders.\n\nOur spies indicate there might be something wrong with the Dunmer's god-king, Vivec. Anything capable of that is a threat to everyone.

Western Skyrim. A cold place inhabited by colder people. They may disagree, but those Nords need fresh perspective. A group of vampires have mounted a shadow-invasion. I hesitate to think on what they're planning.\n\nIf anyone can stop them, it's you.

Ah, the hero of Leyawiin! Your deeds on our behalf will be remembered.\n\nAnd never fear. I shall talk to the Chamber of Legates about a special medal or whatnot. Perhaps even commission a statue. Your legend will be second only to that of Sai Sahan!
This is a private office. Well, as private as an office could be that has no door, or walls, and barely fits a desk. \n\nI used to work in a much larger bank.

She is here. And I think we angered her. I know I suggested it, but breaking into the home of a great warrior perhaps was not my best idea.\n\nPlease, go ahead and ask for her help against Naxhosa. She has not killed you yet, so that is a good sign.

It seems like you've been rather busy! I heard you would be here today, so I thought I'd stop by. I finally paid off my debt to Larz-Tul, thanks to you. I'm free!\n\nNever thought I'd be able to say that again.
At least we learned how the Knights of the Silver Rose became so tarnished. I will share their tragedy as an object lesson, so this folly will not be repeated.

I admire Lucilla's convictions, even if they're going to get her killed one day. Deserting the legion would be insane if the Empire wasn't in shambles.\n\nThe best I can do for Lucilla is report her as presumed killed in action.
The waters have returned you to me. Tell me, did you witness all there is to witness? Have you been changed by your sojourn?\n\nWhat stories have you fed to the rivers?
I have found that the fight for the nest sometimes begins at the border of the swamp. But this is certainly the farthest I have traveled to defend my home. \n\nI am ready to fight at your side again.
I have to admit, I thought we finished our business with Mehrunes Dagon at Fort Redmane. \n\nAh, well. It's an honor to fight beside you again, mercenary.
I understand that Mehrunes Dagon failed to learn his lesson the first time. So be it. I am nothing if not a patient teacher.
My brigadines stand at the ready. After our embarrassment at Borderwatch we're all eager for another opportunity to prove it was a fluke.\n\nWe beat Dagon at Redmane and we'll beat him here too.
So, yet another battle these old scales must prepare for. A good thing, then, that you recovered my blades. \n\nDo not worry. I will once again be at your side. Whether you see me or not.

I suppose the others will offer encouragement and words of wisdom before we charge into the fray. Feh. You do not require such pablum.\n\nKeep your mind sharp, like when you assisted my victory against Naxhosa. That is the truest weapon you need.

Beek-ojel! No, I am wrong. You are no more an outsider. After the strength showed against Naxhosa, you are of the tribe!\n\nI bet you are ready for even more blood to fall, yes? These cretins do not know the log about to smack them in the face.

Despite the priest's obvious deficits, he was wise enough to enlist your aid in this ordeal. He is of no more use to me, but you I'll be certain to enlist again soon. I'm certain I can provide a more enticing incentive at the least.
Greetings, my master.

Find Arox and meet me at Wretched Spire. I do not know what allies I can convince to join us, but we need more than these few. It will take an army to keep Sombren occupied long enough for the Anchorite to recover all the pieces of the egonymic.

Pssst! Tufeh doesn't want to draw you away from the festivities, but she recognized you. You helped her out by the Reformatory.\n\nDid this one hear you stopped the cultists' plans again? Thank you. You've helped more than just Tufeh's family.
Ah, child, I'm glad you returned. The Crowborne Horror approaches once more. Its essence plagues Tamriel.\n\nIf you have the courage to drive it back again, I have need of your aid.
He didn't even try to stop me. He just looked … resigned.

So, we're all meeting in Leyawiin, was it? \n\nIt'll be good to see everyone gathered in one place and safe. We didn't get much of a chance to assess what happened. This will give us a chance to regroup and discuss.
You must hurry. Sombren will reach Mehrunes Dagon soon if he hasn't gotten to him already.\n\nGood luck and stay safe, my friend.

My minion said you were on your way. Now that you're here, we can get on with our investigation of the cult's activities. The danger posed to your plane of existence hasn't waned and my curiosity has yet to be sated.\n\nAre you ready to continue?
I suppose with lives so brief, any victory is worthy of celebration. Enjoy it while you can.

What are you doing here? You should have summoned the portal and joined my mistress Lyranth in her secret chamber by now.\n\nLuckily, I kept Sweet Daffodil around for such a contingency. He'll whisk you back to the delve in the blink of an eye.
We should return to Fargrave. This place … I don't like it. And Calia and the Anchorite, we need to get them out of here.
We should not remain here. I opened a portal to Fargrave. Let us meet there to discuss what we should do next.
I understand there's a town nearby protected from Dagon's influence. Perhaps I'll start there. Someone should know how to get back to Nirn.
Go ahead. Step through the portal. It will take us to Greenshade, close to where I expect we'll find the Dagonists' camp.\n\nWe can talk more once we get there.
So much greenery and animal life. How do you mortals stand it? Never mind. Rhetorical question.\n\nLet us go deal with the Dagonists and retrieve the relic they took from my lair.
So what brings you to our little outpost, traveler? If you're looking for something specific, I must warn you that my alchemical stocks are severely limited at this point in time.

We infiltrated the Waking Flame base in Fargrave, saw the cataclyst in action, and learned that Sister Celdina plans to create an army of Incarnates with the machine.\n\nAll in all, we learned much about the cult's plans, little mortal.
A letter that conveniently lays out the cult's plans, schematics for some strange device, and my relic. \n\nNot bad for a day's labor. These items tell me much about what the Dagonists are up to.
I didn't know I could do that. Open a portal out of thin air. I just couldn't let Sombren keep hurting Calia. \n\nWell, I guess that proves it. I really am an Ambition, whatever that is.
Ah, dearest mortal. Your companions are already upstairs. As much as I would love to nuzzle the secrets right out of you, Lyranth looked very insistent. You shouldn't keep her waiting.
Release me, flea, or the pain I bring upon you will be as nothing you have ever imagined.
Is that Lyranth the Dremora? I'm impressed, devastator. I didn't imagine your mission would yield such … notable results.

Devastator Rullen. I assume the blade did its job? Of course it did. How else could you capture Lyranth the Dremora. She has been a thorn in our side for much too long. Well done!\n\nBut what about the portal key? Were you able to recover it?
Devastator, you honor me. How can a lowly acolyte serve you?
Devastator Rullen, you've returned. And with a prize, I see. Impressive. We thought for sure that the Dremora got the better of you and your team.\n\nI'm almost glad to see we were wrong.

So, the mortal returns from its mission. And it brings a prisoner? How unexpected. And I assumed Lyranth was more capable. I would never allow myself to be captured by one such as you.\n\nStill, Nokvroz may want to question her before the next test.

My mistress looks terrible! If you turn out to be the cause of her discomfort, I will hunt you down and strike you repeatedly about the head. Repeatedly!\n\nNow go talk to Lyranth. The Dread Lady has more to say to you.

That man. Sombren. He seems familiar … but why did he destroy the emperors? There was so much more I wanted to ask. Especially of Moricar.\n\nI … I can't quite bring myself to call him father. But what Moricar said. Is it true? Am I an Ambition?

Go on. Use your charms to convince Madam Whim to aid us once more.\n\nIn the meantime, I want to try another spell of identification on the twisted rod you recovered from Annihilarch's Summit. I believe I am close to determining its original purpose.
Are you an illusion? Or real? Am I saved?\n\nWe must hurry. It needs life. It could return.
Oh! Lord Sotha Sil, I didn't expect to see you here.

My mind feels like shattered glass, reflecting images from a thousand shards. How can I sort through it all? Years of missing memories, flooding back in mere moments.\n\nWhat happened after I placed the amulet on the altar?

I hoped to punish the Waking Flame for their offenses against my Kyn, but I cannot breach this ward. You must mete out vengeance for me, mortal. Do not disappoint me.\n\nAnd try not to die in Deadlight. We still need to deal with Valkynaz Nokvroz.
Time rarely concerns my kind, but I find myself growing anxious about Sister Celdina's progress. We must hurry and meet up at the base of Annihilarch's Summit.
Another glorious battle, master! You made me so proud!\n\nLyranth doesn't seem happy about your latest victory, however. She's probably just jealous. Talk to her, but tread carefully.
Aren't you just fascinated by the Witchmothers? They have such a sense of wonder and mystery about them. Being here is such a thrill.

I cannot follow you through that portal, master. Those Waking Flame sycophants must be afraid to face my wrath. So be it. I will wait here and groom myself until you return.\n\nThen we can destroy Valkynaz Nokvroz.
What do you speak with this one for? Did Witchmother Taerma not give you a task?

An eternity of agony! This was not what the Prince of Destruction promised. \n\nI did everything the Black Drake commanded. Everything the high priest instructed. And I gave precise orders to my son. So, why the torture? And why is the weapon here?

This is not freedom. No, simply a respite from the darkness.\n\nI remember the traitors at my gates, the blade of the usurper slicing through my flesh. But I hid them away. I did my best to fulfill the bargain.
I cannot imagine what further need you have for the daedrat. Does your backpack require soiling?\n\nThey are not clean creatures.

I almost decided not to accompany Lyranth, but now I'm glad she insisted. How else would I have gotten the opportunity to punish the Longhouse Emperors for what they did to us. And finding the last Ambition? That's just a welcome surprise.
My powers … they're gone. Sombren, he ripped them away from me. And he used Destron to hurt us. How could he do that?\n\nOh, Sombren, what have you become?

Two mortals dead. Tephilaz displaced. Tarvyn wracked by guilt and shame. Too much disruption to the status quo.\n\nYou did well. I do not believe in bindings. If I did, I would choose you. Mortal capability at its best.
Come on, we have to move! The Anchorite and Calia are in trouble!

Not that I would ever doubt my mistress, but you do look exactly like the cultist. A little more lively, but otherwise it's a perfect match.\n\nI'm counting on you to keep the Dread Lady safe in there, understand?
Fargrave has work for those willing to take on a tough job and see it through.\n\nCan I add your name to my list?

I have a keen eye for spotting reliable adventurers in need of some extra work. It's one of the things I'm known for! \n\nSo? Are you the sort of person I think you are? A reliable adventurer looking to make a bit of gold?
There's always opportunities in Fargrave for the ambitious and skilled. Take a contract with the Saraathu Tong and you won't have to fight everyone else for work.
You … are not one of these monsters. Daedra. Tormenters. They … questioned me. Wanted me to demonstrate how to inscribe the runes.\n\nI tried to resist … tell Sister Celdina … I tried ….

Traveling with the Daedra will only bring you harm. I know better than most what they're capable of.\n\nIf you do seek out Vontan, you should have caution in the Fleapits. Desperate people live there who won't mind taking from others.
Time to move out, my friend. I'll meet you at the base of Annihilarch's Summit.
I'll go with you. Admit everything. Just leave me be.
Destroy the Riven Cataclyst, stranger. Undo the work my captors derived from my madness. That will be my escape.\n\nOh, the winds, they roar. I hear them more and more and more!

Mehrunes Dagon needs Sombren's power to take Nirn and merge it with his own realm. You must defeat Sombren before that, and then banish Dagon.\n\nIf the Anchorite cannot do her part, your world is doomed.
What a battle! Glorious! Blood drenches the ground of Destruction's Solace and Mehrunes Dagon's defeat shudders throughout the realm!\n\nTo witness your triumph was my greatest honor, master!

Once the Bladebearers appeared and told me about Fort Grief, it only took a short time to ascertain your exact location and open a portal. This seemed like a safe enough place to regroup. Now tell me what transpired. Did you find the Riven Cataclyst?

You'd better talk to Lyranth about the Riven Cataclyst. Although … I'm not exactly sure what happened back there. I was punching and kicking at the cataclyst machine, trying to make it stop. And then suddenly it did.

I do so adore a conquering hero, my darling! Do you like the welcome I prepared? It was the best I could do on short notice.\n\nLyranth awaits you upstairs, but know that I plan to show you all the pleasures of the House of Whims. Later. No charge.

I have always been fond of Fargrave. One can find such interesting things here. I am rather pleased that you did not allow it to be razed to the ground by Mehrunes Dagon's hordes.\n\nAnd I do find all that talk about conquest and destruction so boring.

You earned my respect, mortal. And that of all my Bladebearers. I hope we will fight by your side again one day. \n\nUntil then, watch over the Anchorite. I made light of Mehrunes Dagon's words, but there is purpose in everything he says.
The Anchorite does her part, I shall do mine. Destroy that abomination, mortal!

We did it! We really did it! You're incredible, you know that? You took on a Daedric Prince and won!\n\nCome on, let's get out of here. I want to go celebrate without the stink of this place in my nose!
Gratitude is a mortal concept. Still, you carried me until I was able to fly once more. That deserves … recognition.\n\nI will simply say this. You are the first mortal I do not wish to eat.
Well, here I am. I know I told you that my fighting days were over. But … this seemed important. Plus, I knew you I would be fighting alongside you. And that made the difference.
What a battle. I will remember it always with great pride.\n\nAs should you, champion. You faced an insurmountable foe and arose victorious. Are you not pleased with such a triumph?
I'm ready for this fight.
Bah! That coward Nokvroz fled Fort Grief before battle was even joined! How am I supposed to bring justice to such a creature?\n\nSpeak to the Foolkiller, master. Perhaps she can help us corner him.
I'll meet you in Fargrave at The House of Whims. Once we talk to Madam Whim and Calia, we can decide who to track down next.
Kynreeve Rynkyus was right to trust you, mortal. I look forward to seeing how your legend grows.

I admit, I'm kind of at a loss. Destroying the cataclysts, fighting Dagon's servants, confronting my own mother … the world was simpler when the mask hid me from myself.\n\nIt's going to take a lot of time to sort through my recovered memories.

Look at these misguided fools! They'll forget this happened as soon as the hangovers kick them in their skulls. But, for now, they're having the best Jester's Festival ever. They can't stop applauding!\n\nI should probably look into that.

I'll go with you to Madam Whim's, too. She knows me and I can smooth over any rough spots once Lyranth and her begin negotiating.\n\nHave you ever witnessed a negotiation between Daedra? It can get … intense.

You want more? I'm giving away an awful lot as part of your free sample, but I am feeling generous today.\n\nSister Celdina leads the Dagonists here in Fargrave. She and Lyranth seem to have it out for one another, though I have yet to ascertain why.
Explain yourself, stranger. The Deadlands isn't a place for chance encounters.

Go to Madam Whim's establishment, the House of Whims. Show her the encoded note and tell her we need it deciphered.\n\nI will meet you there. To make sure we have her undivided attention and that she understands this is more than a mortal's request.
Depart. Gazmod wishes to gaze upon the intriguing mask and reveal its secrets. You hold no interest for us and we do not wish to look upon you.
What was that? It sounded like something exploded in there! We need to get in there and see what's going on.

You owe absolutely nothing, my darling. Lyranth agreed to cover your cost for this bit of inside information. Isn't she a dear?\n\nNow, do tell Gazmod that we miss them here at the House of Whims. The place hasn't been the same without them.

An incredible amount of energy was just unleashed within the keep. Whatever just happened, little mortal, be assured it does not bode well for Fargrave or Nirn. Or for us, for that matter.\n\nWe must go inside, but maintain your caution.
Did you hear what I said, mortal master? Valkynaz Nokvroz prepares to send the most fearsome Daedric troops in all the Deadlands to this nexus city.\n\nThe destruction will be glorious!
You're back and you don't look worse for wear. Did the Unmaker have anything good in its hoard? Was it Xivilian steel?
My friend, you've returned! And in one piece too. \n\nHow was facing the Unmaker? I'll bet it was no problem for you.
Are the seeing stones in place? Did you kill the Unmaker? Tell me everything, my dedication to scientific inquiry demands all the answers you can spare and more.

Well fought, mortal champion. With the defeat of the traitor Nokvroz, our honor is once again unquestioned. And Fargrave remains safe for the independent clans.\n\nYou fight like us, so celebrate like us. Bask in the glory you have earned.
You're back and not even a little bit charred. The sign of an overwhelmingly successful fight. \n\nDo you have the bodies? Is the Mantikora dead?
Oh. It's you. Back already from the Mantikora's lair? Or are you here to ask more questions while the Tong's secrets lie in the claws of that beast?

It's nice to be able to celebrate something. Though, I can't stop thinking about Lyranth out there with all that power. I know I'll be sleeping with one eye open for a good long while. \n\nBut I'm glad I can count on you after all this.
Well! What a journey! Investigator Vale would be proud of us, don't you think?\n\nI wouldn't have wanted to save the world with anyone else besides you. We make a pretty great team.
Go on, enjoy the accolades you deserve. I must go my own way, little mortal.
I was keeping an eye on you—I hope that doesn't sound creepy. I think I saw everything, but scrying is mostly an art. How did it go? Did I miss anything?
Welcome to our tiny outpost. If you're interested in alchemical concoctions, you need to talk to Aurien. I'm just her assistant.
If there is another Riven Catalyst, then we must destroy it. I will insist on being part of this. Obviously I have proven my usefulness.
Take that creature and leave. We are done, mortal.
They say you destroyed Valkynaz Nokvroz, and even escaped Lord Mehrunes Dagon himself. \n\nSurely this is some jest. If not … hmm. Perhaps I misjudged your strength.

Friend! Elisa told me what you did, how you gave her the Redmaiden. I don't know if I can ever repay you. \n\nWe're going to lay low here for a time, then see if we can sneak back into Fargrave. From there, we'll make our way to Nirn and start over.

Surprised to see us? I can hardly believe we made it here in one piece. \n\nBakh and I decided we'll stay here for a time, but I think we'll ultimately travel back to Nirn. I'm feeling good these days, thanks to you.

You've done it! Once I've reset the Grim Warden's matrix you'll be able to call upon it yourself, and—more importantly—I'll be able to disable the spiritual wards and leave this miserable place.\n\nYou have my eternal gratitude.
