I still remember the day you appeared in our vault. I was so scared back then, it felt like everything I knew was burning to ash.\n\nI've grown a lot since then, and I have you to thank for that. It feels like my life is finally just beginning.

I am impressed with you, mortal. You did something many thought was impossible and are still standing at the end of it. When you first brightened the door of the House of Whims, I thought there was something special about you. Something intoxicating.
Oh, it's you. Did Madam Whim send you? \n\nTell her it's not my fault, our lack of progress. My friend here stopped for a … light snack.
A mortal, holding the chains of the infamous Lyranth Foolkiller? I think that says more about Lyranth's overblown reputation than it does about your abilities, devastator. Wouldn't you agree?
Rumors of what you've done have flown across planes. Can't say I'm too surprised after what I saw in that citadel.\n\nDon't know how you see yourself, but you're a hero to the entire Kalmur clan.

We meet again. Heard a story about you. Heard you held off Mehrunes Dagon's attack. Defeated the Prince. Good.\n\nYou did well in Wretched Spire. Clever. Strong. Perhaps I'll need you again. Made a good assistant.

This one is not surprised. You had the courage to enter the Brandfire Reformatory to recover a stranger's sister. Of course you'd be the one to shove those half-witted pyromaniacs back to the pits where they belong.
You, the Magician, defeated Mehrunes Dagon! Again! This is incredible. \n\nI—I need some mead.
This is a grand day, master. I am honored to be here to witness it. \n\nAnd should you ever have need of my fangs or claws, you will always have them.
The tales of our battles and victories will be known to all Bladebearers henceforth. They will be recited with the utmost pride.
I'm sorry, I don't have any other information for you. I hope you find those responsible though!
Repulsive temper carried existence departure. Orbs fastened to no sincerity. Extremity direction unpleasant.\n\nAbility seeks higher. You. Did. Job. Well. Attention suspected great own.

I still taste the blood of my enemies, those I crushed beneath my heel! This prison is an insult! I am a conqueror, a god in my own right! \n\nMy teeth have shred the flesh of hundreds … thousands! I demand the respect I deserve!
Remember, Wretched Spire. In the Deadlands. If you don't meet Lyranth there by the appointed time, Madam Whim won't reduce my debt. Then I'll have done all that running around for nothing.
Neither Madam Whim or I will forget the service you've done for us. Not even after the light has left your body and you've turned to dust.

Our Kyn are reunited. I was given to understand that mortals in this realm were little more than crazed fools who lost their way or clumsy supplicants to the Princes.\n\nI was wrong. You have done well.

I did not expect a mortal could achieve such success, but then perhaps there is more to you than meets the eye.\n\nYou have brought great honor to the Bladebearer clan. And you have earned my respect.
Get away from me.
Ah, you must be that adventurer the Gleaners hired. Luna keeps talking about you. Good, they're taking my job seriously then. You are here about my job, right?
Hey there, mate! You remember me? Calonir! The travel writer. We did a bit of business some time back. You traveled to distant lands, gathered up tales and such. You remember, right?
You are on your way to making a name as big as Airlur and that has earned you some respect. You are an adventurer to watch. What do you require?
Oh! You're the adventurer everyone's talking about. And Luna sent you my way? Maybe I wasn't such a fool for giving up on this job.\n\nHow can I help you?
You're that risk taker the Gleaners use. Are you here about the plants in the Folly? Because they should be in bloom now.

I told Lady Beriel that my assignment was important but not time sensitive only a few hours ago, and she already sends our most successful adventurer my way? She's too kind to me. \n\nHow can I be of assistance to you?

You're that new adventurer the Gleaners are talking about, right? The one who's taken on a lot of difficult jobs?\n\nI'm flattered, of course, but why are you talking to me? And nobody followed you here, did they?
You have proven yourself in realms where most mortals fear to tread.\n\nI will remember your name, mortal. Vame of the Bladebearers would be honored to fight by your side.
Chain-breaker. It is good to see that you survived Ardent Hope.\n\nThough we do not often make such alliances, the Bladebearers will stand with you whenever you call. You have earned this honor.

You know, despite his simple nature, Skrix displays a rare gift for counterfeiting. I can think of countless applications for such a skill. Alas.\n\nFor all their power, the Daedra lack one vital trait: imagination.
I already told you everything I know. Honest! Cross my heart, hope to die, all of that!\n\nYou can stick around for the next auction if you want. Just don't scare off any of the bidders, all right?

You're welcome to take your leave. Getting Jakarn back to my ship and on to his destination shouldn't be a problem after the beatings you gave to the order and those yaghra.\n\nI'd offer you a ride, but I'm chartered to get him delivered straight away.

Za'ji can hardly wait to see the Pounce newly decked and polished! He will take you out for the maiden voyage, if you desire!\n\nPerhaps she will be up to chasing these Sea Elves and swatting their noses for the insult … and those lodestones.
Think you're clever. Clever like Fyr. But when you're dead, Skrix will still be here. Secrets never die. Schemes never end.\n\nEnjoy the victory. Mortals only get a few.
You reunited me with my brothers. I won't forget that.\n\nGood luck with the portal key. We'll keep scouting the Deadlands to keep tabs on our enemies.
Your allies are waiting for you at the House of Whims in Fargrave. It seems that you have some unfinished business in the Deadlands—or so I might have overheard.
Our bargain is done. There is nothing to stop me from removing your head from your neck. \n\nGo away before I remember how long it's been since I have done that.
That's not like any kind of Daedra I've ever seen. We can't let them send it to Fargrave. It'll destroy the city!
My time in the cataclyst was enlightening. I devised a spell that can weaken the Incarnate, but it still poses a deadly threat. Take it down as fast as you can, mortal!
I can't state firmly enough how bad it would have been if Valkynaz Nokvroz and his Incarnates gained control of Fargrave.\n\nYour victory was pivotal to countless futures.
Another three or four hundred years and I'll have an End Times Ash of my own to shade me while I fish. Finally, something to look forward to.
The Constrictions are completed. Your bones are surprisingly resilient, Nirnling. Now, leave me.

I'm sure I would have found my way out of that eventually, but you spared me a lot of embarrassment and dislocated joints.\n\nThanks to you, I can return to my lady a hero deserving of her tender mercies.

The cleanse is successful, as Nzerru's cleanses always are. You must permit to pass what you living ones refer to as … time, I believe. The Golden Panacea writhes within your offal. Nzerru cannot perfect what his tonic has already begun perfecting.
A customer approaches. Is it swordkin to this Elf, Divayth Fyr? If so, my condolences. The Elf is a boor and a skinflint.
Great Vruxynbu has bestowed on you the … the blessing that is his dulcet ardor. Let his … let his quintessence adhere to you as the warm embrace it is.
The ghost is no longer a ghost? Oh, it is just as Master Rrvenk said—the possibilities are boundless!
I thought I told you to begone. You obviously don't know how any of this works, and it's throwing off my whole routine!
So that oily little pest is yours? You should keep it on a shorter leash.\n\nHmph. I assume you take full responsibility for its vicious outburst?
Maggot. You return.

Meet my mistress in the Oblivion city of Fargrave, outside the southern gate. Lyranth said she would wait for you there.\n\nHurry, chosen mortal. The fate of both Fargrave and Nirn hang in the balance.
And so, students of change, you have learned the most important lesson.\n\nI hope you continue to follow its course, learn its ways, and come back to teach me something new.

Noroth focuses too much on the mortals' whims. He adheres to the belief that we cannot wipe them out without disrupting our protection from summoning.\n\nBut they will die soon enough. Protecting them means nothing. If it ends now or later, who cares?

You have my blessing. There is nothing more I can do to aid you on your journey.\n\nMy fire is large enough to share. Stay here and rest in safety for as long as you wish. I do not intend to depart anytime soon.
We don't want any trouble in here. I run a clean establishment with only a small number of roaches.
I want nothing to do with your kind.
Leave me to my drink. I want nothing to do with you.
Adventurer, my mistress demands your presence. You do still carry the encoded note you recovered in the bathhouse, I hope? For your sake.

Vri … does not understand how such an event could come to pass. Mehrunes Dagon has been bested before by his fellow Princes, or thwarted by pretender deities. But to fail before mortals and lesser Daedra?\n\nVri cannot believe it!

By the Master of Tasks! I would've bet every wart in the Pits that Dagon was going to incinerate Nirn to ash. To think he's been rebuked! \n\nThe other Princes will see his failure. Perhaps my lord will profit from his weakness?
All this toil and still so far from my freedom!\n\nValue that, mortal. You may spend your days avoiding death, but at least your path is one of your own choosing.
The Drained are everywhere. It's enough to make your heart ache.
Mehrunes Dagon might have been defeated, but it's a fool who thinks he won't be back. Death and time are inescapable for mortals. To a Daedra, they're inconveniences. At worst.
I don't believe it. Mehrunes Dagon, defeated? Wretched Spire has always been a monument to the ancient victory over the Prince of Destruction. But I never thought such a thing could happen twice!
I am going to find some of those pastries you mortals rave about. I might as well try to make sense of something and I have more of a chance of understanding them, than I do your accomplishments.

My mistress, the Dread Lady, gone? And she didn't take me with her? What did I do to displease her? More importantly, what did you do to make her leave? This is all your fault! It has to be!\n\nOr maybe this is a test? Go away. I need to ponder.
Mehrunes Dagon, defeated by mortals! I did not think such a thing was possible.\n\nMadam Whim seems pleased. Perhaps that will make my existence under her more bearable.

When you helped us in the Sever, I had no idea you'd go on to save all of Nirn too. We're grateful you took the time to pull our sorry hides out of trouble.\n\nElisa's feeling better. We might stay here for a bit to visit Minwileth's family though.
There aren't enough words to thank you for what you've done. Not just for us, for me … but for all of Nirn! \n\nIt's an honor to know you, Champion.
Once again the machinations of the Daedric Princes have been thwarted by you. We might have to start calling you the Twelfth Force.

So, my erstwhile colleague banishes Dagon himself. I must admit I'm impressed. I know only two people who've accomplished the same, and they are worshiped as gods.\n\nJust don't let the victory go to your head. No one likes a conceited braggart.
I'd fight you, but mortals never pose a challenge.

Such a brave one you are. I hope you do solve the Daedra's murder. All I have left is in that filthy town. I would hate to see it burn.\n\nYou will find Noroth on the eastern side of Wretched Spire. You cannot miss him standing over a dead Daedra.
There are fewer rules here than the Grasp professes. You'll go far when you figure out where the gaps are.
Kynareth light your way, fellow traveler.
The planes of Oblivion are closed to you, traveler. Get on with you.
Is only fair the mortal face punishment. Do you know how hard it is to find decent help around here?
Kaluzan the Cowardly? No, Kaluzan the Cretin …. Yes, that has a pleasant ring to it!
Remain compliant. The Grasp has wasted enough time on mortal affairs for one day.
The zombie attacked me! What was I supposed to do? Let it gnaw on me until the Dremora arrived?\n\nHe's the one that left it wandering around. How am I at fault?
I swear on Prince Malacath, corralling the mortals of this place into a fighting force is an impossible task.\n\nThere's not much time and we need combatants!
Keeping me tied up is a waste of everybody's time. The door to the Shambles is right there! They should just let me go!
Now, if you will excuse me, I must get back to my actual work.\n\nRun along to Wretched Spire and tell the Wood Elf not to call on me again.

Quite the celebrity, aren't you? It seems that while I busied myself with other affairs, you assailed the fortress of a Dremora warlord and escaped the Lord of Destruction himself.\n\nIf I'm not careful your reputation may begin to outshine my own.
Ooh, I could look at these shinies all day. But I'm supposed to find a volunteer for an experiment. I don't suppose you have a cold, do you? Or serious allergies?
Tufeh knew you would beat her back, but to be at the portals when she returned home? Maybe the old saying holds true. In Fargrave, there is fortune for all and mercy for none.

More adventures, my darling? Madam Whim hears things. I'd be concerned about facing Mehrunes Dagon again, but you and the Anchorite never cease to surprise me.\n\nReturn here when you're all done. I would love to help you celebrate another victory.

The dockmaster's home overlooks the harbor to the west. Jakarn and I will meet you there.\n\nFirst Quentyn, now this. I hardly know who to trust. Times like these, I take a moment to contemplate the Colossus in the harbor. It helps clear my thoughts.

I'm all right. Fortunately Lady Arabelle was close at hand to protect me from those terrorists. And the rest of the guests managed to retreat into the castle safely.\n\nI suggest you consult with Lady Arabelle as to how we respond to this outrage.
You won't really leave me here, will you? \n\nTell Jakarn I can work to make this right with Lady Arabelle! I'll serve her for life if I have to!

I'm afraid that nothing has changed regarding my attempts to locate the missing medallions. Either they are quite far from us, or something is interfering with the magic.\n\nI hope you had better luck on your end.

I cannot thank you enough. With the idol returned and the light restored, we can ensure the safe passage of many a weary traveler.\n\nIs there any way a priest of humble means could repay you? A blessing perhaps?

Well met. I'm General Quentyn, Fighters Guild.\n\nLooks like there's going to be a delay in Lord Bacaro's conference. I'll have to find a way to make myself useful or I'll go mad. Never could stand sitting around and waiting.

Best of luck finding your friend. A rogue order of knights causing havoc across the island is bad enough, but this sounds worse than I imagined. A dark storm gathers over High Isle.\n\nI will warn my circle and ask them to be on guard.
Well done! Zenithar's blessing surrounds all you do!
Take care. This archipelago is dangerous. My wife and I witnessed that for ourselves.
Huh? I'm off duty, newcomer. Got a complaint? Take it to one of the other guards.
That's some nice-looking gear, wayfarer. Might want to watch it around these parts.\n\nPeople are desperate. Makes them do desperate things.
This is my spot. Find your own spot!
You don't look like a salvager. Come to join up with those so-called knights who've been hanging around, did you?\n\nFeh. I'd rather go hungry than swear myself to the likes of them.
Yes, Za'ji promised not to drink until Queen Ayrenn was safe, but that was before Za'ji saw the Colossus of Gonfalon Bay break apart.\n\nNo one can expect Za'ji to stay sober after that!
I've had enough rest. I promised to ferry High King Emeric safely to High Isle and I failed in that task. \n\nI'm going to help you set it right.

I plan to set out soon to scour the coast for signs of wreckage. If the dockmaster is not to be trusted, we cannot assume he carried out his search.\n\nIf there is any sign of the missing ships, I will find it.
It's so good to see you again! Privette and I were just talking about how you heroically saved her.\n\nShe seems mostly recovered. We hope the Hadolids got the message not to steal friends.

Here's the location where my contact, Tarazka, wants to meet. I hired a wagon to take us there. Hope you don't mind being in close quarters for a bit, my good-looking friend!\n\nHop in and we'll be on our way.
I'm not sure how long my cursed existence will continue, but I feel at rest. \n\nMy trials are over. I'll keep my vigil here and look to welcome death with open arms whenever I'm blessed with it.

Hail, friend. Have you heard about the band of robber knights that waylay travelers on the road to Gonfalon Bay?\n\nI came to High Isle to trade, but getting goods from the interior has become a roll of the dice.
Thanks to you, we can satisfy our client and still have goods to spare. We can find new clients! Grow our network. Take more jobs! Set ourselves up for a lifetime of prosperity and adventure!\n\nOw.

Jakarn was wise to bring another. He will surely use you as an excuse to weasel out of the gold he owes this one. \n\nTarazka is glad to have someone to speak with other than that smoothskin. This one has information for you about his friend.

Such an interesting adventure, don't you think? I must write down the pertinent details. Wouldn't want to forget a moment! And don't fret. I'll make sure to send for you when the situation on High Isle escalates. You're too good not to call on again.
Quite the adventure, eh? I'm not some flashy, showy sort. But I'm careful, and try to be clever.\n\nIt's good to have an ally that values those attributes in a knight.
We have to find Valessea. Just keep an eye out for any of those Ascendant Order bruisers.

Thanks for talking to Tarazka. He's as cranky as ever. Anyway, the prisoner he mentioned must be the lovely Valessea. We need to rescue her!\n\nCome on, let's get inside and find Valessea and her kidnappers!

Isobel is so happy and excited to go off adventuring. I didn't think about her leaving me. Er, us.\n\nOh, but listen to me, I sound selfish. I am so happy for her! You will watch out for her won't you?

It's a shame the Sea Elves have laid claim to this spot. It was an ideal location for clandestine exchanges. Not irreplaceable though. The same can't be said for my sister, which I'm beginning to regret.
Don't think I'm not grateful that you saved my skin. I am. Just owing my life to strangers when my own brother stood by and watched is the definition of galling!

I'm still in shock about poor Arch-Magister Delric. Did you know the Mages Guild asked me to take his place as our delegate to the peace talks?\n\nAnyway, thanks again for helping us. I'm not sure Jakarn would have managed as well on his own.
Guess I'll accompany you and Lady Arabelle to the dockmaster's home. Don't expect too much. If you ask me, Arnauld didn't seem too concerned with finding those ships.

I wouldn't have been able to save my ancestor's soul on my own. And even if we found her treasure first, nothing good comes from cursed treasure.\n\nThat first mate position is still open, by the way.

Now that we're free from Amenos Station, Anton and I can do as we please. We weren't officially processed, so I guess we've gone rogue. Wouldn't be the first time.\n\nMaybe I'll start building another raft.

There is no need for you to linger here. Go track down your associate before he delivers another trap into someone's unwitting hands.\n\nI'll make sure the Skald-King gets this medallion. The Society of the Steadfast need not worry.
Ugh, I can't wait to get out of this place. The Ascendant Order has a lot to answer for. \n\nPlease tell me you found the medallions.
Did you find anything important? I'm sure Valessea can't wait to see it.

Welcome to the arse-end of nowhere! This is the place Valessea described to me, the entrance to Sareloth Grotto. The five medallions must be somewhere inside. Let's hurry and get them back.\n\nYou still have that shell Valessea gave you, right?

Well. I suppose this is meant to be flattering, but it's all rather awkward. I have no idea who that scoundrel is or what he thinks he's doing!\n\nHow much longer do my guards intend to let this spectacle go on?
Who is that fellow? I'm certain I hired no such scoundrel to serve our guests!\n\nI must make sure the guards teach him a lesson. One that he will never forget.
Voluptuous? Curvaceous? Oh, please. Did Elea hire that fellow to make a scene?\n\nShe isn't happy unless everyone is looking at her.
Meet me at Lady Arabelle's camp. I'll introduce the two of you and then you can hand over the medallions. \n\nSee you soon, good-looking!
Far be it for me to tell anyone they ought to get a move on, but the Ascendant Order's sailing toward the alliance leaders and Lady Arabelle needs our help.\n\nThis one sounds important.

Don't worry about me. Go with Lady Arabelle to that cave. I'll find a way to keep myself busy. Like making sure the royals get to that secure location without doing bodily injury to each other along the way.\n\nCome to think of it, better wish me luck!

Well, this is where we part ways, good-looking. We saved Valessea and retrieved the stolen medallions. All that's left is to deliver them! \n\nBe careful out there. I'd be surprised if the Ascendant Order doesn't try to get their hands on them again.
You've finally dredged this poor soul up from the abyss. For that, I'll be forever grateful. You and my heir have earned more fortune than I have to give.
Dame Isobel Veloise. She can choose any order to join, you know.\n\nBut I wonder … she may be better off broadening her experience, her horizons. Time will tell, I suppose.

We did it! We saved Valessea, restored and delivered the medallions, and defeated the Ascendant Champion. Well, most of that was you, but I helped! You're really something else, good-looking.\n\nAnd Lady Arabelle paid me, so I'm satisfied.

Did I hear Lady Arabelle's name? That changes things! I've met her a few times. Fascinating woman. If she's in danger, you must go to her. You can find a boat to Breton waters on the southern dock.\n\nI'll make sure this medallion gets to Queen Ayrenn.
Glad that's all settled. Head for the ship, my dear. Jakarn will split off once you get to Amenos. Meet him in the stockade and he'll fill you in on your next steps.\n\nGood luck!

Once the hunter caught me, Jailer Mannick put me on display. He said the other prisoners should see that running was useless. He would have killed me soon if you hadn't come.\n\nHere's some rare sincerity from me. Thank you so much. I owe you my life.
Welcome to Amenos, wayfarer. Head to the stockade, but remember to watch out for prison gangs, snakes, trolls, alligators, wolves, mudcrabs, and Daedric Princes. \n\nNot necessarily in that order.
Good fortune, wherever your adventures take you!
Amunara will be free eventually, dull-claw. Then this one will exact her revenge. Remember these words.

I shall likely apply to the Order of the Albatross, even if I did not retrieve Sir Brenvale's lute. I fancy myself a bit of a bard, you see. \n\nI've been writing songs and playing the lute since I was in short pants. You should see my two-step!

I do hope Lady Arabelle is safe. She can certainly protect herself, but these Ascendant Order ruffians seem determined to disrupt our peace talks.\n\nHurry, my friend. I shall keep attempting to overcome the counterspells that are hindering my magic.

Looks like I'm going with Lady Arabelle. We'll take care of the mage, you just worry about giving the Ascendant Champion a taste of her own medicine. \n\nWe'll meet up after when High King Emeric is safe.
An adventurer! Thank every single Divine you're here.\n\nI'm a squire without his knight, and she needs our help!

We don't know what the Ascendant Order is doing out there. But hopefully something at one of those locations will lead us to our missing royals.\n\nBut do be careful. I'd hate to see such a capable agent get hurt while assisting me.

That map you borrowed from Duchess Elea's study should come in handy. It marks places the Ascendant Order's been up to no good. \n\nI don't know if the duchess ever actually looked into them, but maybe we should.
If you see that lunkhead Booklover, tell him to get his frostbitten Nord arse back here.\n\nThere's no end of work here and I'm tired of picking up his tasks.
I cannot compromise my anonymity, lest my lady be overcome with emotion. \n\nIt's too soon. Too soon, Nilsmon.
Welcome to your new home. For as long as you last, heh.

Winning the tourney is all well and good, but not strictly necessary for a well-trained and wealthy aspirant such as I.\n\nWhy, I do believe I might get a generous offer to join the Iron Knot within a few days.

House Mornard will hear about what happened here. The good and bad both. \n\nDruids turning the living into coral fodder? A fight between mortal life and nature? There's something strange happening here, but it's beyond my comprehension.

It's not in my nature to give up my own freedom, and I'm not. Piracy isn't the only life out here.\n\nVeslyn and her captain won't see trouble from us and we'll fight by their side. We swear it, on the constancy of the tides.
Can you believe it? An elder? Me? And the mediator between the circle and the spirit of the grove. This is such an honor!

So Isobel will leave High Isle and learn about the wider world. It truly is a brand new day. I'm glad she'll have someone capable like you by her side.\n\nShe's like a second daughter to me. Hmph. Not that you heard me say that.
The bloodmage is vulnerable. After all our hard work, this is it. \n\nYou take the final step, friend. You've earned it.
The two of us work well together, don't you think? I'd love to travel with you, if you'd have me. You seem like the type that goes on lots of adventures. I could learn a lot! Think about it, yeah?
You delivered the letter? What did she say? Did she seem … pleased?

I don't care about his station. I've always loved listening to bards perform, and Adistair's voice is so nice. All I want is to just spend a little time with him. Nothing that my father would disapprove of … much, anyway.
You plan to strike a blow against the Ascendant Order? Good. If you find you need another sword at your side, send for me. \n\nI've always found it hard to leave such tasks in the hands of others.

Ah. There is the scandal for the evening! The well-to-do of High Isle will be talking about the fool who danced on the table for the rest of the season.\n\nI rather think my sister secretly likes the attention.

I trust Lady Arabelle implicitly. If she believes I should accept Lord Bacaro's protection and leave the Ascendant Order to you, then so be it.\n\nBut know that I'd rather help you deal with these villains than get locked away with Ayrenn and Irnskar.
Off again, walker? Za'ji would go with you, but Queen Ayrenn may have need of the Perfect Pounce II. Plus, Caska wants to make sure she is ship-shape.\n\nThe ship, that is. Not the queen.

Mistmouth Cave lies on the northern coast of High Isle. It's a favorite of outlaws and pirates. I'll meet you there. I need to go over some details with Jakarn one more time.\n\nThings tend to go in one ear and out the other with that one, you know.

I can't say I like the idea of hiding out while others hunt down our enemies. But my father taught me a good leader must learn to depend on others.\n\nI look forward to hearing what you and Lady Arabelle find at this cave.

You go on ahead. I'm sure Lady Arabelle is eager for your report.\n\nI'm going to let the guard know what we found in here, for whatever good that might do. And someone should bury these recruits. Not even traitors deserve to rot in a cave.

The letters you found make it clear the Ascendant Order is preparing to launch a major naval attack on All Flags Islet. We must inform Lord Bacaro about this threat.\n\nI'll collect Jakarn and meet you back at Mandrake Manor.

That's not how I would have played it, but I don't expect Arnauld to get very far with all the Ascendant Order knights out there.\n\nLet's get this information back to Lady Arabelle. I'll meet you at the manor.

Mistmouth Cave? I know the place. A good spot to watch the seas and islands to the north and west. I'm not surprised the Ascendant Order might make use of the area.\n\nKeep an eye on Lady Arabelle, will you? She forgets sometimes that she's retired.
I will accompany Jakarn and make sure that Prince Irnskar and the others reach the secure location safely. \n\nThe Ascendant Order won't get the better of me again.
Thanks to you, I think these soldiers may actually see their families again. And maybe they'll take the lessons of this manor and do their part in bringing the war to an end one day.

Young Audrine makes a bold proclamation. While I believe the spirit of this grove spoke through her, I find it hard to imagine that one of our druids could be responsible for unbalancing nature. That goes against everything we believe.
Stonelore Grove and our druidic circle are forever in your debt, adventurer. You will always be welcome in this sacred place.

Chyrisnia and the Sea Elves are as good as their word. After everything we went through, I believe that to my bones.\n\nThank you for getting us out of there. I think I speak for all of us when I say we didn't want to die like that.

I so appreciate your help. Even if you don't know alchemy or healing magic, just helping us learn more could be immensely useful.\n\nGo talk to Armin Demalle at the manor. He's been looking into this malady. You can find him by the south gate.
She … she just had to take center stage, even at the end.
Ryvana and I will continue to study the items we found in the ancient druid circle. Perhaps there's more we can discover about the Ascendant Magus and his plans.
Thank you for aiding Valessea and I in determining the source of the aberrant disturbance in the grove. \n\nIf there's anything I can do to further your investigation, please let me know.
It's over. We have slain the bloodmage, and I am a knight.\n\nWhat a thrilling adventure.

I have nothing else to add, stranger. But if you and Druid Audrine plan to put a stop to the corruption, please let me know if there's anything I can do to help. None of us want to see our beautiful grove destroyed.
You fool, you have no idea what you've done. I was so close to success, and now you've ruined everything!\n\nMany deaths will be on your conscience!
Did I hear Lady Arabelle correctly? She wants to steal a ship and sail through hostile waters? And hope nobody notices?\n\nAll right, I'm in.
Six years. Six years on this godsforsaken island. And now, I'm sailing with the tide.\n\nIt has been a very strange day.
We set sail with the tide! Just have to make sure no one else bumbles their way onto the island.
Thanks again. For everything. Especially the bit about not leaving me hanging upside down in a moony Breton's trap.
I guess you're somebody after all. Doesn't change my opinion none. The Order needs people like me. People who are willing to get their hands dirty.\n\nDon't forget it.

The Ascendant Magus is here! I do hope I get to meet him. I've heard that he is as an inspiring speaker as the Ascendant Lord. They say you can't listen to either of them without discovering new zeal for the cause.
I never thought I'd find myself signing up to fight for any knightly cause. But if the Ascendant Order can bring High King Emeric and his rotten court down a peg or two, I'm willing to take up arms!
Stop right there. Only full members of the order are allowed to attend the meeting.\n\nNew recruits must wait out here until the Magus decides to address you.

You are annoyingly persistent. Well, my foolish adversaries, the Ascendant Order can be persistent, too. Did you really think you'd defeated us when you retrieved your precious royals from Amenos?\n\nAll you did was gather them in one place for me.
What an adventure! I am sure King Jorunn would be proud of the diplomacy I have committed today.\n\nThank you again, friend. Without your help, my scepter of office would still be missing.
Thanks for helping your friend Rigurt straighten things out. If it weren't for you, I don't think I ever would have been paid.

While you head to the Dufort Docks, I'll discuss our plan with the alliance captains. We'll need them for this to succeed.\n\nCaptain Basrush will get you to the island safely. I know for a fact she can't refuse a purse full of gold.

I appreciate your help … and I hope you have the tact to never speak of what happened last night. The Dominion frankly expects more of its diplomats than carrying on like common drunkards.\n\nNow, I need to go lie down.

Thank you for helping Rigurt to sort out this mess he made. The sooner we can all forget about last night's misadventures, the better.\n\nI really don't want any of my colleagues to find out I got arrested.

You're the adventurer who escorted Meryline here? I suppose I should thank you for ensuring her safety. \n\nI'm surprised that you're not a tall tale like the others she invented to get away from her bodyguards when she was younger.
Thank you for what you've done here. Master Viralaine has much to answer for … and now it seems like he'll do exactly that.

I'll tend to her wounds and get Islinne to safety. You must carry this information back to Lady Arabelle at once.\n\nAmenos is no place for a prince to wander alone. And if the other leaders are there, they are also in grave danger.
Thank you for finding me out in the Shoals. Don't worry, once I get some mead in my belly I'll be as right as rain.\n\nI only hope some of my other crewmates made it to shore.
You have my gratitude, hero. I doubt Seraphyne or I would have survived if you hadn't come along when you did.
I can't believe it. We did it. I did it!\n\nI always knew I could use my magic to help people, but now we proved it! I can be an adventurer!
I don't feel right in the head yet. The pay isn't worth all this trouble. I knew working for a mage was a bad idea.

I think I made things perfectly clear, mainlander. I haven't seen Count Damard all day, and Duchess Elea does not care to entertain visitors. \n\nLeave, or I will summon Dufort knights to drag you away.
My faithful steward, an agent of the Ascendant Order? It just goes to show you can never truly trust the household staff.

First we must find the cove where the Nereid's Song is hidden. I have no idea what cove Damard's letter referred to, but Captain Kaleen might.\n\nShe and the other captains are down by the harbor. We'll need them all to crew the ship, I suspect.
Welcome, adventurer! If you're looking for work and prefer to handle jobs on your own, you've come to the right broker.\n\nJust let me know if you're interested.
What do you say, adventurer? Gonfalon Bay could use your help and we pay well.

I believe Ember still wishes to speak with you. I recognize that gleam in her eyes well, the near palpable excitement coming off of her in waves. She must be formulating some kind of plan. Speak with her before she bursts.
We drove the Hadolids back into the mine with everything we had. Swords, fists, rocks. The prisoners even used their pickaxes. But the Hadolids, their claws are just so sharp.
Where did Meryline learn to do something like that? That was completely different from when she would conjure butterflies in the gardens.\n\nThanks to you both, we won't die in here.
Meryline wants to talk to you. Get it over with so I can take her out of these tunnels.
You don't look as surprised as my darling husband. But I do want to thank you for helping him open this vault for me. Makes stealing the treasure out from under him ever so much easier.

Thank you. Meryline told me some of what occurred with the Hadolids. I'd like to believe it was all your doing. But, maybe it's time for me to reconsider my approach to our … discussions. Her magic has its uses.
Put on that trusty outfit before you head inside. If you get caught, we never had this conversation. Understand? Good.
I think we're done here, don't you?

One of these days, I'll figure out where I need to take the Daybreak Gem. Then the treasure of the Daybreak Monks will be mine! Perhaps I'll reach out to you, my friend. You're quite handy to have around when the going gets troublesome.

While you head to Galen to secure Count Stefan's cooperation, I'll work with Lord Bacaro to get the peace talks underway. And I'll continue to watch for signs of the Ascendant Lord. By the time you return, perhaps I'll have uncovered something.
Your hard work paid off, mainlander. We found <<1>> with an entire crate of refined moon-sugar. He's going away for a long time.
'ELLO I AM YOUR FOLLOWER
My battlemages have been waiting for the magic to calm about this damned island. We were getting tossed about on choppy seas until you took the wind out of her sails. \n\nWhere's Taleria …?
We'll be engaging the enemy momentarily. Prepare as you need and get on deck. This ship will be a sitting duck until you're underway, so make it quick.
Reporting in? Not a moment too soon. \n\nGot you marked down. Make sure your compatriots are all here, as well. Timing will be everything, if this mission is to succeed.
You've done a great service to the House of Dufort and all the Systres. Those Dreadsails would have driven us all to ruin if you hadn't flushed them out from their den.\n\nThank you.

High King Emeric looks no worse for wear. In fact, he seems rather happy. Your doing, my friend?\n\nKnow that you impressed me throughout this long ordeal. And it was good to fight alongside my fellow captains instead of against them. Very good.
Find the alliance leaders and get them to the safety of Memorial Hall. We'll take care of things here and buy you some time.
That turned out better than I expected. I'm glad it's over.\n\nIt is over, right? I'm not sure I have another fight in me. At least not today.

I think I can bear this Breton paradise a little longer. Consider it my way of acknowledging everything you did for us. For me.\n\nIf you could go out of your way to save three foolish royals, then I can try to find common ground with my enemies.

We won the day, my friend! And I learned a valuable lesson. Sometimes the enemy of my enemy is my friend. Or at least a helpful acquaintance.\n\nAnd if the peace talks do go on, I will do my best to negotiate in good faith.

Fighting alongside each other? All well and good. Attending a party together? Sure, we're civilized people. But these peace talks …?\n\nIf Lord Bacaro is committed to continuing down this path, I'll follow. I don't hold out much hope, though.
You made quite an impression, my friend. Too bad for you—now all the important people know who to call when they need something done. You'll never have a moment's rest, you poor bastard.
Queen Ayrenn is safe again! Za'ji is grateful. It would have been terribly embarrassing to lose her a second time.\n\nBut the battle is over now, yes? We can all take a rest? Za'ji is exhausted!

This was your doing, I suppose. All those tasty Ascendant Order knights to munch on, and they suddenly turned tail and fled!\n\nProbably for the best. Za'ji was starting to get winded. He's nowhere near as strong as he thinks he is.

We have taken the first step on a long journey. Still, no one ever reaches their destination without taking that step.\n\nI owe you a debt, friend. Because of you, there's still a chance for peace. I promise to take full advantage of this opportunity.

I feel like a child again—looking for the next adventure, wondering what trouble I can get into, glad for my friends beside me to keep me strong.\n\nNow that the mystery is solved, I feel ready to take on all of Tamriel! Nothing can stop me now!

Find Jhaka and bring him home. The love shared between Ember and her little family was nothing short of miraculous. This one hopes it can be restored.\n\nKeep an eye on Ember, would you? She's a clever one, but this one worries for her all the same.
The puffed scrib bits are also a tasty treat. They come with two dipping sauces.

Our business is concluded, is it not? If you don't intend to purchase anything, I would kindly ask you and your friend with the murderous little eyes to leave.\n\nThe bandits you seek operate out of Pulk. Go there and bother them.
Despite everything that happened, we're alive and well. Perhaps Lord Bacaro's dream of peace isn't dead after all. I came here to be polite, but now … who knows?
My father won't believe half of what I tell him happened here. Shor's bones, I hardly believe it myself.\n\nI say enough fighting and talking for today. We should celebrate our victory!

What now, I wonder. Do Ayrenn, Irnskar, and I remain here? Do we leave to resume our royal duties? If I get a choice, I'd rather avoid returning to that torture device they call my throne for as long as reasonably possible.

Lord Bacaro should be at Steadfast Manor. Do hurry before he strikes off with an army of hired knights to join a battle that's already over. \n\nBesides, it's not often I get to send someone good news.
This one's lungs are not as strong as they used to be, but do not fret. Once Jhaka has had a hot meal, a warm bed and a bit of rest, things will be better.

This one hopes you find more answers in Betnikh. Speak to Guruz, see what he can tell you. \n\nAnd take care of Ember. The responsibility of such a task wears on her, Jhaka can tell. Make sure she does not whittle herself down to nothing.

You and Ember have returned the brightness of the moons to Jhaka's eyes. We four have been reunited against all odds. In the past years, huddled in pain or fear, this one nearly lost hope.\n\nBut you ensured we may all find joy once again. Thank you.
I'll be honest, I wasn't sure about you at first. But you've done more to undo what was done to us than I ever did. You're all right.\n\nThanks for reuniting us, and for being a friend to Ember.

Like I said, if you're determined to find those girls, your best bet is to start with the Wood Elf. We handed her off to the vampires in Shadowfen at Black Maw. Not sure if they've moved since then, but it's worth a shot, eh?\n\nGood luck to ya.
Oh, look who it is! I suppose I should have expected to see you here. After all, you were at the last party too!
I did say it'd be nice to bump into you somewhere other than a moldy cave. But I never thought you'd be someone I'd see here.

Time is precious, my friend. I hope you and your friend will make haste to Sentinel to track down Song. \n\nBut do not make the mistake of underestimating the Emerald Eye. Many have paid dearly for such naivete.

You have given all of us an irreplaceable gift. Though we are all grown and far different from how we were as children prowling the streets of Skywatch, the love we share is unchanged by time. You helped reunite us, so our love includes you as well.

The longer we stand here talking, the better my chances that my beloved brother will decide I'm too much trouble to keep alive. \n\nI've said all I can. Go to the Emerald Eye's camp and do what you can to find Song. Please.
All right, enough talk of feelings and growth. Let's plan our next adventure.\n\nStendarr keep us safe, and our coin purses full!

Blessing of Zenithar to you, laborer. It is fitting that the one who worked so tirelessly to restore Zenithar's Abbey should share in the joy of his festival. With you here, prosperity is sure to follow.
I never thought I'd see a sight like this again. Laborers from all of Tamriel, trading their wares and sharing their stories. \n\nThis is what the Abbey was like, before it fell.

I was a bit nervous meeting the Knight Commander, but she's been extremely fair. And Aurelia can't stop gushing about me, which … someday I'll get used to.\n\nGood luck in your next adventure, my friend.
I feel terrible about how this has all turned out. I do hope you go after him.
I don't take bribes, I'm very busy, and before you ask, no. We don't ship Thorn Geckos in bulk.
I can finally say goodbye to the Systres and to slaving over cargo shipments for the Duforts. It's off to the hot winds of Hammerfell for me.
I was hoping to try my new concoction. Still, I love this plan.\n\nKiv forced to live with a group of celibate, contemplative monks? He will hate that. Hah!
So what now? We just wait in here and hope someone comes to our rescue? Feh!
Captain Renwic really was a rather dashing individual. So strong. So many muscles ….\n\nDo finish your business with my manservant. I really do need him to attend to me.
What a trying day! And it was so much worse for poor Lady Laurent! I'm glad you came along to help when you did, my friend. I don't know what I would have done on my own.
Your dedication and devotion are inspiring, dear-heart. \n\nBut, don't spend the entire festival at work. Enjoy yourself! Connect with others! Share in Zenithar's bountiful gifts!
I won't forget what you've done for us.
Damn Sea Elf nearly drowned me with those magic currents. I see Za'ji escaped none the worse for wear. Suppose he is the better swimmer. Not that I'd ever tell him so.

Many greetings, traveler. Truth be told, I'm glad Rayan didn't listen to me. \n\nShows he's coming out of his shell. I just know beneath his mousey visage beats the heart of a poet! Plus, we could use your help against that damned bloodmage.

It does make me a bit sad that Kiv will not appreciate the favor I'm doing for him. Many would pay well to have the time, solitude and space to contemplate their life decisions. \n\nMy hope is that he will emerge all the better for this experience.
I won't forget what you've done for us.
I'm not a total fetcher. Not totally. The ring is where I said it is. \n\nJust don't expect me to be here when you get back. Heh.
Please, I can feel the curse reasserting itself. Trying to steal our memories again.\n\nCarve my beloved's name into the memorial plaque and the curse will be broken, I'm sure of it!
Thank you for looking into this. Aurelia is free to do as she wishes, of course.\n\nBut my daughter is not a knight, and Tamriel is dangerous. I want to see her home safe.
If you're looking for food or drink, just ask at the bar. And Mara smile upon you, friend.
Bye bye. I … I'm a just take a nap here.
You manage to pry that fancypants wine out of his claws?
Look away from poor Halz. He will be right as the rains on the plain, just as soon as he makes his poultice.
Look it here. New meat.
Don't know who those bastards were, or what they wanted. Thanks for jumping in though. \n\nYou really gave them a run for their coins, hah!
For so long the castle, my family, and Isobel were my entire world.\n\nNow look at me. Aurelia Jourvel, merchant sailor! Funny how time and tides will erode every beach, isn't it?
Damn it all. I almost had … I almost had him.

I'm not sure that ship Za'ji found is worthy of the name Perfect Pounce II. Maybe after I whip the new crew into shape, and repair all the leaks ….\n\nAnyway, Za'ji and I are ready to help if you need us. Just say the word.

I apologize for my tardiness, but the work of an arch-magister never ends. I saw Lady Arabelle leave. Pity. I was hoping to speak with her.\n\nAnyway, the Mages Guild decided I would represent them in the upcoming peace talks. You have my invitation?

I wish we'd been there with you, to see her win the Tourney. It's so good to meet you now, though, and to see Bella! \n\nNext time you come by we'll have dinner together and I can tell you all sorts of stories from when she was a little girl!
If I know my Bella, she's been beating herself up about this ring business. Tell her not to worry, all right? If anything's gone awry we'll put it to rights.

When Isobel pledged to travel at your side I was … concerned. But you have more than proven yourself. \n\nAnd I can see it in her eyes. Travel has done wonders for her. So thank you. You've done a great service, to both of my daughters.

Ah, it's you! Please, you've got to help Miss Aurelia! She was snatched by a nasty looking brigand. One of the children ran up to tell me!\n\nIf you hurry, they can't be too far. Apparently she was giving them quite a hard time.
We can talk once we're out of here. Let's keep our heads down and get moving.
Hello, hero. Fancy seeing you at a simple festival with absolutely nothing covert going on. Unless ….

My friend! It is good to see your face among all these strangers. \n\nRaz wants to say that he's skulking around because of some business, but he fears that the lady Naryu might be around here somewhere.

Bet you weren't expecting to see us again, eh?\n\nA lot's happened since we parted ways outside the Coral Cliffs. We made it to Brokerock Mine and met a House Mornard ship at Amenos Station. Two of the pirates are on their way back to their captain.

That sail's seen better days. I wouldn't be surprised if it left with the next gust of wind. I'll have to tell Sergeant Brusic about it later.\n\nGood to see you again by the way. Especially without any druids trying to kill us.

So you managed to get off Amenos? Good for you! \n\nI don't have time to chat, there's a lot of work that needs to get done before we can start making deliveries around Gonfalon. But I'm not complaining. It's better than being sacrificed to some coral.

I am in your debt, my friend. Know that I will negotiate in good faith for a lasting peace—so long as Ayrenn and Irnskar do the same.\n\nAfter we deal with the Ascendant Order, though, I think. Those fanatics threaten all we hope to accomplish here.
It's good to see you again, student of Zenithar.\n\nI have more questions to test your knowledge of my Lord's ways. Answer them correctly, and I'd be glad to pay you once again. What do you say?

Thanks for taking care of Sorinne, chum. I'm a fair card player and a decent drinking companion, but when it comes to the really heavy stuff … well, I'm about as useful as sand in a water skin.\n\nSo, yeah. We all owe you one.

The three of you represent the Gonfalon Chapter's best hopes for a title—I would hate for Sorinne to miss her chance. She's worked so hard to reach this point!\n\nI did not see where she went, but someone in the hall might know.

Hard to believe, but I finally got some help around here—and you'll never guess from who. Brahgas!\n\nThe little scoundrel finally decided to work for a living. I don't want to scare him off honest work, but I'm not going easy on him either!

Razhamad will be waiting for you in the Gonfalon Gaming Hall. And don't worry, he didn't take any offense to you just leaving like that. Everyone's busy around here, we all get it.\n\nJust try to stick around a bit longer this time. It'll be worth it.
Jone and Jode, you did it! Very few players win three matches in a row. Kishka is impressed! And she does not impress easily, I can tell you.\n\nTime for rewards, yes?

We did it!\n\nI don't think I have to worry about seeing Raenobi's face again for a long time. I ran away the first time, but now she's the one with her tail between her legs. I feel like I'm finally free!

You know, you remind me of a young … well, me. Sharp, inquisitive, good-looking. You'll be ready for tournament play in no time!\n\nNow, go see Razhamad. It's time for you to really take your place among us!
Did you deal with those mad druids? Ha, well done! Report back to the broker. She's holding your payment for the job.

This isn't possible. You cheated! That's the only possible explanation. I would never have miscalculated. This is … it's absurd!\n\nI will send a full accounting of this to the Roister's Club leadership! This is preposterous! It's fake! All of it!
How did Varnauld lose? His strategies have never failed!\n\nI … I need to think about this.
I knew it! Varnauld is nothing but a pompous, babbling, bafoon!
My prayers are answered! You return, safe and whole. And I sense that a great evil is no more. \n\nParisse Plouff will want to see you at once, hero.
If you want to know more, look for a sad young woman near the tourney grounds. \n\nOr, look for her best friend and protector, Isobel Veloise. A much more stern woman no doubt hovering nearby.
Do come back and let us, er, Remard know how poor, sweet Aurelia is faring. Imagine, being pursued by both Langley LeTarte and Mortens Runel!\n\nHow exciting!
Are you a follower of the Divines, adventurer? Come to pray or pay your respects? Or maybe you're actually looking for me. Has Wayllod finally found someone to take on my quest?
You pass by and once again see me here. The rivers of your heart are strong and steady. \n\nMy road, as always, is empty, but your face is familiar and that is good.
You're back! I … I really didn't expect to see you again. Well, congratulations on killing old Wildhorn. I know the job broker's got a handsome payment for you!
I'm glad our captain is paying for our release. I want no more part of this island!

Those druids better be pleased they met us on land. Once the captain takes us out to sea proper, any druid I spot is going to feel the swell of my anger. Believe you me. No coral magic's getting in the way of my revenge.

Oh, I see you're already under my protection. Well, it's always good to see a friendly face on the road. I know my friends are happy to see you. Especially after you gave up your coins so easily last time.

I have been told that my brother met his end at your hands during his reckless attack on All Flags Castle. If only I had seen through his schemes sooner, perhaps he might have been saved.\n\nBut I suspect he gave you no choice. That was so his way.

I feel a little out of my depth here. So much trouble came from the medallions I prepared. And then the magical wards I helped raise at Memorial Hall failed to stop the Magus.\n\nNow I'm supposed to turn my efforts to diplomacy?
Sir Brenvale, the golden voiced, the silver-tongued, once the head of the Order of the Albatross.\n\nAt your service, oh gentle folk!
I'm going to stick right here by the Knight Commander.\n\nAt least if I stand here and keep my mouth shut I can't embarrass myself any further.

Did that Dantaine woman send you over here? Best not to get involved with that one, stranger. If she makes one more accusation about false arrests or incompetent jailers, I'll throw her into the stockade personally.
I suppose it's a nice hall. As far as halls go, I mean.
Who left that damn barrel open? It stinks to Oblivion! I think I'm going to retch!
I appreciate the help, friend. A person can't let another person disrespect them and still respect themselves. I think.
Off to Seyda Neen? Kill as many of the Dark Elves that you can. It helps me sleep better.
All right, prisoner. If you have something to trade, maybe we can make a deal.

Such commitment, such purpose! You must be the assistant that Wayllod promised to provide.\n\nWell, he gave you the reagents, correct? All you need to do is enter the Firepot and sprinkle them in a few lava vents. My spells will do the rest.
Meryline's song made the Hadolid's scratching stop? The Overseer will never believe it.
So, you and that Barthel girl helped. Thanks. Now get out there and take care of the rest of them! Can't have their claws mucking around in the mine.
You've a determined air about you, stranger. Could I persuade you to help deal with the active volcanic vents that are popping up across the islands?
The mood in Steadfast Manor seems improved! Even with the revelation of those horrible experiments, at least the patients have an explanation. People's fears grow larger from ignorance.
Praise to the Three, you brought back Roslenn. I don't know the details, and I'm not in the state to hear them. All I know is perhaps now I can rest. Even if just for a few moments.

The one responsible for helping the sick took advantage of them instead. Milagi cannot imagine such depravity.\n\nThank you for returning Roslenn to the manor. Milagi hopes she can finally calm his mind.

Well, I'd say our drink is going to be a resounding success. The gadabouts lazing about High Isle will be lining up to get a taste! And Hilgrim and I will be there to satisfy them!\n\nOnce Hilgrim sleeps off this hangover, of course.
Loshu-Jat sees the light. Loshu-Jat won't stay in the darkness under rocks, she'll go topside and breathe in the moving air.
Who knew that helping people would be this hard on the voice? I feel like I'm going to be drinking ginger tea for the rest of my life!
An adventurer, talking to me? You must be from Wayllod. Here to help with our little problem.\n\nWell, if there is anything I can do to facilitate your work, you only have to ask.
You return! Thank you for saving the eggs you could—the Stonelore Circle appreciates your efforts.\n\nThe job broker should have the payment you require.
Well struck, my friend. The Magus has fallen!\n\nWhat say we head outside and meet up with Lady Arabelle? I imagine she's rather worried about me.
Off to find that flatulent sop, Nilsmon? How that fellow got his position is a mystery to us all.

Good luck in the matches ahead, Tribute master!\n\nIf you are looking for greater challenges, well, as a fellow master, perhaps I can share some of my knowledge. I am no Tribute Founder, but I do know quite a bit.
Do you need counsel, friend? Or have you come from Wayllod about the job I asked him to fill? Be advised, the Society of the Steadfast pays well and always deals fairly with one and all.

You've returned? Oh, that must mean those Ascendant fanatics are finally dead! Thank you. For everything you've done.\n\nI'm sure Parisse Plouff will see to it that you're well rewarded for your work!

Raenobi must admit you have skill. But skill counts for little without cunning.\n\nSorinne is soft … weak. She yields when she should attack. That is why I beat her every time. And that is why I will beat her again today.

You have the brine glands? Oh, excellent! I'm positively brimming with anticipation. \n\nTake them over to the job broker, so that you can prove you actually did what she hired you to do and get paid. And let her know I'm waiting for those glands!
Raenobi's sweets … could they be holding me back? We will see how she fares here at the end of the tournament.
Do I know you? How did I get here? My mind … it's so foggy. Ugh, I think I might be sick.
We all fought well today, against unfathomable odds. The enemies of peace have retreated back into the shadows, thanks to our efforts. And thanks to you.

Serving as an agent for three alliances that really can't stand each other is difficult, but as a neutral party, at least they trust the Fighters Guild. Mostly.\n\nBut you look like you need something. Did Wayllod send you about the job?

The alliance leaders are safe and the remainder of the Ascendant Order's forces are in retreat. Your work, I assume?\n\nThanks to you, the rulers of Tamriel are alive and there is still hope for peace.
I wonder if the Evergrowth will ever talk to me. I suppose I'll need to prove my worth. Maybe find a particularly pleasing tree to contemplate? Or a spectacular blade of grass?

Perhaps I can convince one or more of the knightly orders to join us. The Order of the Albatross is usually willing to leap into a fray.\n\nAh, I implore you to delay until I can coordinate our forces. You cannot take on the Ascendant Order alone!
Did I see you talking to that Dantaine woman? I'd stay away from that one if I were you, stranger. She's been over there bellowing like a banshee since before I started my shift.
Please tell me that Wayllod sent you to help me with my research. I haven't been able to get anywhere with the druids on my own.
Well, I didn't win. And I'm not sure I'll even get an invitation to one of the orders. \n\nBut Malacath's arse, who cares? There's always next year, right? Hahaha.
That's really all I know. Sorry I can't be of more help.\n\nNow if you'll excuse me, these fish won't catch themselves!
Well, now that the tournament is over, the only logical thing to do is start preparing for the next one!\n\nIf I'm to have any chance of beating you, I've really got to up my game!

Razhamad revoked my membership, but he hasn't thrown me out on my ear yet, thank goodness!\n\nI told Gelekh I could help out around the bar. Never heard her laugh so hard, but I think she's game. Brahgas doing hard, honest work. Who'd have thought?

Valessea's arcane skills are very impressive, don't you think? The spells she imbued into the medallions demonstrate subtlety and power.\n\nAs she seeks to learn druidic magic, I am eager to study her techniques. We have much to teach each other!

Whatever the Ascendant Order unleashed on the delegates' ship drained the medallions of the spells I put in place. Fortunately, I was able to restore their various protections.\n\nThe delegates will need them to enter the secure location.
Ah! A city dweller! Have you come to take enjoyment in the wilderness of the Systres Archipelago? Beautiful, isn't it? How do you feel about nature?
Bleh. You stink of that blasted Gonfalon Bay. \n\nMy imbecilic brother and I are in the middle of a discussion. So? Speak up. What do you want?
B'vek, I've never seen a match like that. Teliv bleeds after all.\n\nPerhaps it's time I find proper tutelage elsewhere.
Listen, I heard what Razhamad said about your other skills. Just leave me out of it, all right? If you need to beat someone senseless, Teliv is right there!

You surprise me, champion. And I am rarely surprised.\n\nYou may have saved Brahgas for now, but it won't last long. I suspect he'll make another wager before he even leaves Mournhold. Nonetheless, he is free for now. As promised.
You're the one who played second to Dame Isobel, weren't you? Well done! \n\nNow, if you'll excuse me. The Sapphire Tourney shall not run itself! Haha!
Busy, busy, today, Taz. They are all excited to be the first  to complete the Trials, just for the bragging rights, alone!
For these charges listed, Minasi Nelvilo is sentenced to hang from the neck until dead. \n\nUnless … uh, you best not be stepping in the path of justice.

After the tourney, I'm going to take some time to reassess my investments. Knighthood is prestigious, of course. But at Navire I'd just be a small fish in a big pond.\n\nMmm, fish. I've been craving fish all day.
All's well, I suppose. The mainlander royals are up at the palace, the light at Gonfalon Head's keeping the seas safe, and those robber-knights are at the bottom of the loch. Where they belong.

I admit I didn't expect much from these peace talks. Stuck-up nobles bickering with each other while ordinary folk went on suffering. But maybe things will change now that they've had their own taste of trouble.

I follow the Order of the Albatross. Hmm. I see you have the heart of an adventurer.\n\nStill, the knights of my order are known for their daring deeds and travels. And while I may be young, I've experienced my fair share of danger.
I'm not listening to this sun addled fool, and neither should you. A raft? Pah! Does he think that hasn't been tried before?
This bootless churl refuses to see reason. Kidnap House Mornard guards? Does she want us all to hang?
Bit busy here s'wit. If you want to do me a favor you could always distract that idiot guard. There's only so much talk about my own hanging I can take before it gets on my nerves.
It isn't safe for a new fish in Amenos Station, stranger. Try not to look like an easy target.
Got any gold to spare? Maybe some food? I'll take anything you're willing to part with.

You see the Ghost Ship too? Some will claim it's just superstitious sailors seeing things in the mists, but Dark Elves aren't so quick to dismiss rumors about spirits. We all know a few souls we can't get rid of.
I once heard of a haunted canoe in Murkmire that would cry as it drifted along. Turned out to just be a swamp jelly stuck under the oars.
They say working in a mine is a sweet deal. Food, a safe place to sleep … but I hate the idea of going underground. It's not natural!
Why does everyone look at me so strangely when I ask about eating Hadolids? They look just like shellfish!
It's … incredible. My mouth is bursting with flavor. The dock is spinning. You're spinning! Genalda's spinning. Ah, she's so pretty.\n\nHeh, what a wonderful drink.
Don't believe me? Go see for yourself. The cursed thing is just outside Death's Valor Keep. Ugh! I won't be able to sleep for weeks!

Ah! Friend, it's good to see you again. I hear you were the one who told my squire where the adventure was last time.\n\nMy squire is in another mood, but I'm sure searching for enemies to slay will cheer her up.

Oh, hello again. Thanks for the advice last time. \n\nUnfortunately, the great hero over there wasn't satisfied. Now we're in the exact same position you found us in last time. With my ego-driven master chasing tales and invented monsters.

Oh. You can see me? It takes a keen mind to see someone in my position. Welcome.\n\nYou'll find no rattling chains or slamming doors here, I promise. Just a lost soul, committed to a game that never ends.
I hope those cards bring you as much joy in play as they brought me in the making.
Must be getting rusty. Bah. Good news is, I've got all the time in the world to whip myself back into shape!

Amusements like Tales of Tribute have many lives, my friend, but hey don't truly blossom until players take the reins.\n\nYou find the seams—the imperfections, and you craft entirely new ways of playing. I'll never grow tired of watching games grow!
Just … give me a moment. I'll get to my feet as soon as I can.
You're leaving us? Oh gods. I really am going to die in here.
Please keep a good eye on Meryline. She's a dear friend.
Thank you, champion. Thank you for showing me that our great labors have not been in vain.\n\nI hope that one day you will find an opponent worthy of your skill.
Hello friend! May I call you friend? I don't care. The most wonderful thing just happened to me. You'll never believe it!
Ew, a horrid prisoner! Scat, scat!
Move along, prisoner. I'm a knight of House Mornard and I don't have time for your nonsense.

A prisoner? And out of the stockade? That's against the rules, you know. And you know what happens to prisoners who break the rules? They get banished to the jungle!\n\nYou do not want to get banished to the jungle. Trust me on that.

A new prisoner for the stockade? Welcome to Amenos! The stockade isn't too bad. Unless you're scheduled for processing. Once that happens and you become one of the banished, you can never leave the jungle.\n\nIf you do? Zap! You turn to dust! Really!
The stockade is that way, prisoner. Get back inside or we're going to have a problem.
What can this one do for you, prisoner? And please say nothing. Simargo is very busy.
Go back to the stockade and leave me to my work, prisoner.
Day turned out more eventful than expected. That Kiv was a charmer, don't get me wrong. Would have been. Heh. A lot of fun.\n\nBut I'm glad he got some justice. Live and learn, I suppose.

This door leads to High Isle in the Systres Archipelago.\n\nOur spies believe leaders of the Great Alliances will gather there for a peace summit, but this will draw conspirators. They could plunge Tamriel into deeper chaos … unless you stop them.

When Kamal's Bane foundered on the rocks of Amenos Passage, I could not imagine this hour would come. Yet now the hardest work of all begins.\n\nWell, after the hard work of restoring All Flags Castle is finished. Then the hardest work begins.

Nothing can replace the Spearhead or the crewmates I lost when she went down. But seeing the High King and all these other people alive and well goes a long way toward making things right.\n\nWell … that and Nereid's Song, I suppose.

After a shipwreck, imprisonment, and dangerous battles, Za'ji has earned a little time to relax. And perhaps some recognition for his bravery and skill, yes? Za'ji is the hero of the day! After you, of course. \n\nA drink in your honor!
Good thing I didn't eat you on that Amenos beach, walker. This all would have been a lot harder without you. And no, I don't really eat people. That's just Senche-raht humor. \n\nAs far as you know.
Oh! Maybe you can help!\n\nI've fallen on hard times. I hoped that Zenithar might favor me and help me secure my fortunes, but—well, I don't know how to ask a god for their … anything really.

So, when not busy fighting pirates, I guess you're off saving royalty. Perhaps you just travel where the winds blow.\n\nEveryone here owes you a great debt. Especially myself. The Prowler remains safe and ready to serve the Dominion.

Well done, my friend! What you accomplished here, what you prevented. We all owe you so much more than our thanks and well wishes. If there's anything you ever need from the Stonelore Circle, you only need to ask.
I … I think I've got this. Just a bit more, and I'll have a spell matrix worthy of the greatest magewrights on Artaeum.
I have been carrying barrels all day, but let me guess. You think I am doing it wrong.\n\nMaybe you should carry the barrels.
There is nothing so pleasant as a good book. It can take away troubles and cares for hours. Or so I have found.
Not every day you see the Colossus of Gonfalon Bay shake apart. Not a good sign, if you ask me.
You look sturdy. Perhaps you should think about enlisting in the Systres Guard.
Be at ease. If you have come in search of rest and recuperation, you are in the right place. \n\nI have found the climate of the Systres to be quite salubrious.
I'm not usually one to be overly cautious, but even I have enough sense to know all that volcano business doesn't bode well for Gonfalon Bay. Or anyone.
I wasn't even all that familiar with the Gonfalon Colossus … I haven't been here long. Still, it feels like a hole has been torn from the fabric of my life now that it's gone.
Hey there, traveler. Sorry, I'd love to chat with a tar-grip like you, but these boats aren't going to load themselves. Have a good one!
Hey there. Uhh … why don't you make like a tree and get out of here? I'm working.
Are you a hunter of big game? No, of course not. I mean, look at you. I'm here if you're ever interested in learning the trade.
Beware, traveler. There is nothing for you here on High Isle. Just stormy seas and hungry waves.
Don't mind me. Down on my luck, right now. But things … things are looking up.
It's getting bad around here. There's always smoke on the air … you can't get away from it. But most of these people don't have anywhere else to go. \n\nI think things are going to get worse.
The cards haven't been too friendly to me of late. Thought I'd take a break and clear my head. Maybe get some ale, too.\n\nAlways play better when I've had a couple, know what I mean?
People are nervous, you can tell. There's a simmering unease on every face in Gonfalon Bay. What happened with the Colossus has really shaken everyone up. \n\nStay safe out there, all right?
I'm truly distressed over the fate of the Gonfalon Colossus. What madness! What unimaginable cruelty.
I don't want to help people just to make them grateful to me. But, if these are the sorts of parties adventurers get to attend, I definitely won't complain.
I can't say I terribly enjoy parties, too many opportunities for decisions one might regret later. \n\nBut I suppose if anything is worth celebrating, it is your actions here on High Isle.
I might slip out the back now that the talking is done. Even as a squire I wasn't much for glad-handing.
Bestest friend! I had no idea you were large diplomat, too! Prince Irnskar says you saved the peace talks by saving his life. Twice!\n\nThat is very strong diplomacy! I wish I had thought of that.

As much as I enjoy a party, I still have work to do back on All Flags. And poor Stibbons isn't a spring rooster. All this excitement does terrible things to his already fragile constitution.\n\nIf we disappear, do give our regards to Lady Arabelle.

Well, that was quite something to see! I envy your life of adventure and derring-do, my friend.\n\nSometimes I imagine striking out with nothing but a sword and a good pair of boots … but what would become of Lady Laurent? She'd be lost without me.

What a party! Lots of fancy people here, I've got to be on my best behavior. I promise not to pick anyone's pocket or anything. This is your big day, I'm not going to get in the way of that.\n\nUnless you want to see what's in Emeric's pockets.

Quite an honor you've received from these esteemed figures! I feel confident they only know a small portion of your heroics.\n\nIf these discussions succeed, we could soon see this war end. No more lives thrown away in the pursuit of power.
Oh, hey. Fancy meeting you here.\n\nI was on a supply run, but Razhamad told me to keep an eye out for you. Looks like the final tournament's about to start.
Maybe I'll get a drink before I head back to High Isle. Y'ffre knows you can't find a decent mug of rotmeth anywhere in that damned place.
Back to the stockade, prisoner. It will be your turn for processing and banishment soon enough.

Processed prisoners, I've seen all kinds. Some beg and plead. Others cry like babes dragged from their mothers' breasts. Others get angry, offer gold, make threats.\n\nIt would be sad if I didn't find it so amusing.
I'm going to survive out in that jungle, just to spite them all. Wait and see if I don't. Wait and see.
I'll find a way to make them all pay. Everyone responsible for sending me to this damn dung heap. They'll rue the day. Rue, I say!
Banished to the jungle doesn't sound too terrible, does it? How bad could it be beyond those gates? Probably just a lot of talk to frighten us. Yes, that's it. Just a lot of talk.
An innocent Orc, banished to the wilds of Amenos. What's fair about that?\n\nI hear there are gangs roaming the jungle. Maybe I can join one. Safety in numbers, right?
Stay back! This one was just looking at the gate and regretting the choices that led her to this fate.

Well played! Not that Malilen will remember. She's got more skooma than blood in those veins, I wager. She'll be lucky to make it home with all her teeth intact.\n\nBut enough about her. We have a tournament to win! See you in Elden Root.
Thank you. That match … how you won. That's what I needed. I know I can do this now. I'm not backing down.\n\nGo out there and keep dominating, my friend. I'll do the same!

Good luck in Stormhold. Teliv's protege, Dralcia lacks her teacher's experience, but shares his talent.\n\nNow, I'm off to find Sorinne and Brahgas. I hope they are finding success. Especially Brahgas.
I was curious to see who would win this silly tournament. I have to say, it did not disappoint.\n\nMy congratulations on your part in this little tale.

So you plan to help the Breton, huh? Saving that Anton of hers will be tough. Make sure that any gold she gives you is real. Can't trust a swindler.\n\nOh, and if you see her, say hello for me. And good luck crossing that water! Heh.

You can see the top of the wizard's tower, just above the ring of rocks, over yonder.\n\nLook for a Khajiit lady, Ember, I think her name is. Maybe she knows why things are going strange there. Be careful!
It only took a millennium, but my brother beat me again.\n\nI suppose that it's not totally unreasonable. He did give his life saving Tamriel from the Sload and all ….
You and this druid have our thanks, mortal. You trusted us, and now the balance of nature has been restored.

Veloth keep you safe, hunter. Skilled assistance such as yours is not easily found. It would be a shame to lose out on such a resource.\n\nAnd something tells me we will see each other again, someday.
Marunji thinks you return to him flush with victories! He recognizes the swagger of the victorious Roister. It is much like the walk of one who has just eaten the most delicious honeycomb!

Let me add my thanks to all these accolades, my friend. Your courage and resolve stopped a true villain from gaining terrible power. And you saved many lives. You have the gratitude of the Aldmeri Dominion.\n\nAnd of its queen.

Well done, my friend. Well done! The Daggerfall Covenant will not forget your actions here in the archipelago. And, on a more personal note, neither will I. \n\nNow we can get on with these blasted talks—finally! Thanks to you.

Congratulations, friend. You earned every honor the Society and the other alliances want to bestow on you, as well as the gratitude of the Ebonheart Pact. I'll get the Skald-King to issue a separate proclamation. \n\nHe'll be sorry he missed all this!
Hey, good-looking! Did you miss me?
Roots and thorns confound it! Destroy the trellis sentinels over there! Breaking this spell is a lot harder than it has to be with them in the way.

I hope Dhulef is all right. I won't be able to contact him for a while, not with everything that's happened.\n\nWhy would Archdruid Devyric and the Firesongs do this? So many dead and the enclave is in ruins! Rebuilding alone will take so long.

The logbook describes this island as a Dwarven machine. They wanted to control the weather. Hmm, that explains how it can create storms.\n\nI'll send more of the Mages Guild here to shut it down. This looks like the end of Graven Deep.
So what if I deserted? It was dangerous at the front! I got caught and they sent me here. Where's the justice in that?\n\nAt least I don't have to fight their damn war anymore.
Hey, I saw you on the transport. You and that pretty boy were packed aboard at the last moment.\n\nWell, stay out of my way and we won't have any trouble, you got it?
Hello. If you're looking for the knight commander, the office is just down the hall.
Everyone loves a grand tournament. But no one stops to think about all the work that goes into making it happen.\n\nHungry knights get knocked from their horses. Tell me I'm wrong.
Well. Duchess Elea has rather neglected the castle's library, if you ask me. There were more books here back in her grandfather's day.
Drop your line in the water somewhere else. I'm working here.
No time to talk, stranger. The castle's docks are as busy as I've ever seen them. And the duchess's flagship is moored out in the bay, too.
Just move along, mainlander. I've got no quarrel with you.
This is my first tournament, and I'm impressed. No one seems to do pomp and pageantry quite like Bretons.
Oh, this makes no sense at all. Shorebirds of the Systres should be shelved right here. Who in the world would have moved it?
Think they'll open up the grand melee to all comers this year? I don't have a fancy title to get my name on the list, but I'd love the chance to compete.
Which sword? Hmm … if it's blunted edges, might as well take the heaviest blade you can heft. Knock down your foes over and over until they're too tired to stand back up.
I'm supposed to keep out the riffraff. I have to admit, I'm not quite sure what to make of you.\n\nBest move along, stranger.
You can have the dummy in just a moment. I'm almost finished with it.\n\nMore practice never hurt anyone!
Who's my next opponent? When do we—ah, I apologize. I've been waiting for the master of the lists to send word. But you're not a messenger, are you?
I'm here to fight, and they give me a tent next to the quartermaster and the cookfire? If they mean to insult me they've done a good job.
