Hello there! Welcome to Castle Navire. I don't suppose you're royalty? Nobility? Generally high-born? \n\nToo bad. I was hoping for a truly noteworthy arrival.
Greetings, mainlander. If you're looking for the tourney, just head down the hill to those colorful tents. Or if you're looking for the duchess, she's up in the castle.
No one should be up here, whether free citizen or prisoner, trusty or noble. Move along or I'll toss you in the worst part of the stockade!
Finally got my trusty status, and one of the jailers gave me a fishing pole! As long as I share my catch with Jailer Afronia, I get to keep coming out here. And I get to keep the pole!
I thought I had the library to myself today. I admit I might have lost track of the time.\n\nOr the day, now that I think on it.
This fire is for trusties. Anyone else becomes kindling.
You're new. Well, just you wait. Your turn will come soon enough. I've been processed. Now it's just a matter of time before the jailers haul me off and banish me to the jungle.\n\nLife is so unfair!
I don't want to be banished! Please, tell them! I didn't do it! Please!

Mark my words, my new pamphlet will draw in visitors from all over Tamriel. Nobles and wealthy merchants alike will come to take in the beauty of the Systres Archipelago!\n\nI'll make sure your contribution is not forgotten, of course.
Go! Follow Druid Laurel. We'll cleanse this spirit.\n\nArchdruid Devyric's caused a lot of damage. We can't let him take the seed from us as well.

I hope Frii feels comfortable on Galen. I know the Stonelore Druids will do everything we can to help them and make them feel welcome.\n\nAnd I hope to see you again, my friend. You should visit us on Galen the next time you travel to the archipelago.

Well, by Ruptga's grace and the nature of the waves, I doubt this is the last we'll see of each other. I intend to keep in touch with Druid Laurel and I assume she intends to keep in touch with you, hmm? Luck and clear seas to you.

Please, you must save Wyress Tola. I don't know what you'll encounter in that cave in Hag Fen, but the longer she's with that evil druid, the more worried I become. Be careful, but bring her back to us, please!
Don't trouble yourself with me. I may be old, but I'm not frail. I can make my way back to my sisters on my own.\n\nJust get to Bangkorai and stop the archdruid. That's all I ask.

You and your friends are welcome to recover here in our camp, but I ask that you don't linger longer than you need to. That spirit … I fear you'll make us more of a target. We've lost enough here today. \n\nPlease, just leave us in peace.
Galen. Purpose folds into the leaves. Druid whispers. The song softens. \n\nThank you. The roots twist. Release. Undone.
It's done, five-claw. The Aquilarios Bequest is buried for good. And you saw to it that Roneiia … that Redblade won't be sailing the Abecean ever again.\n\nRaz could use a break.
Begone, sludge! I'm not here to make friends.
Not looking for a conversation, stranger.
You'd be surprised how many people run when we serve them the Y'ffelon Surprise. I wonder why we keep it on the menu.
Hah! That was … magnificent!
Bah, some people just don't appreciate real talent.
Look at that ship! It must be the vessel that carried the Aquilarios Bequest years ago. \n\nWe need a plan, five-claw. Luckily, Raz came with one prepared.

I have some inspections to make, measurements and samples to take, but I'm certain that from what little I've already seen, House Mornard will be quite happy with my report.\n\nI just need to gather all my tools.
I assume your journey to Galen was uneventful, dear? Was Count Stefan receptive to my request?

Za'ji senses a great battle ahead. He will be right there with you, five-claw. Or maybe a little behind you? Or with the Pounce? Yes, someone must guard the Pounce! But Za'ji will be with you in spirit!\n\nNow go. Lady Arabelle is waiting at the manor.
Let's get back to Vastyr with the Eldertide seed. Thanks to Captain Siravaen, we know what the Dreadsails and the Firesong are planning. We can make preparations and be ready before they strike.
Druids? What has my great city come to that we need to beg the druids to help defend it?\n\nStill, Stefan is right. We need the help. Go, mercenary, before I change my mind about this.
Shouldn't you take that relic someplace safe? Everyone seems rather concerned about the silly, old things.
This is nasty business. Pirates and druids attacking the city.\n\nSir Stefan has been expecting you. Go talk to him, mate.
I wish I could go with you, but Archdruid Rahval is right. The Firesong Druids must be scouring Galen for Frii. The spirit trusts me. I have to keep Frii safe.\n\nPlease, friend, save Stefan.

Sir Stefan is more than the scion of House Mornard. He's a bridge between two worlds. Few Bretons have his understanding of both the old druidic traditions and the ways of so-called modern society.\n\nDo whatever you can to save him, druid-kin.
Count Mornard and his son are making plans in the throne room and Sir Stefan wants you there. You should go.

You'll find Count Mornard in the throne room of the castle. If you'll excuse me, I need to check with my scouts and find out if the Firesong or the Dreadsails have been spotted recently. It's been too quiet since the Draoife.

Nothing is ever dull when you're around, my friend. You did good, five-claw. Very good. Now talk to Lady Arabelle so we can figure out how to proceed with the peace talks.\n\nI wonder what we'll tell people about Lord Bacaro.

I really must be going, my friend. Between the Sea Elf and Firesong attacks, and the continuing volcanic activity, Vastyr needs all the help I can bring them.\n\nIf you can look into the Dufort Shipyards and find my messenger, I'd be grateful.

Are we done now, five-claw? Does this mean we can start the talks? The sooner Queen Ayrenn makes peace with the other alliances, the sooner Za'ji and Caska can get back to their real lives. Not that this wasn't fun, but … Za'ji prefers less danger.

I really hate being so … impotent. Ryvana tells me her tincture defers the worst effects of the poison, but I still feel weak … like my blood is on fire.\n\nEnough of my problems. Tell me what you saw when you examined the note and the bottle.
You did so much for the islands, for the druids. I'll never forget how you saved us all. Thank you, my friend.
I do hope Lady Arabelle will be all right. I must send her a gift with my condolences. No wine, of course. Or anything that requires either eating or drinking. Perhaps a nice book ….
Are you from the castle? Can I finally make my delivery and be done with this damn job?

The prophecy holds deep significance for druids. We've been waiting for its promise to manifest for a long, long time.\n\nWe have to hurry. I must administer the antidote to Lady Arabelle and warn her of this betrayal. Meet me back at Mandrake Manor.

Sounds like the Thicket is where we'll find the Bequest. Raz would bet a stack of coins in a Skywatch frog race that Redblade will be there as well.\n\nHe will meet you there, five-claw. Razum-dar has to retrieve some tools for this job.
Hail, Defense Force veteran. Yours is a welcome sight.\n\nThis one is curious. Are you here to chat, or do you wish to test your skills once more?
Congratulations! You are more than welcome to join other game winners in the patrician's suite. \n\nTry the Black Night Cordial, it's delicious!

Dhulef will take Frii to a House Mornard galleon. He'll escort them to Y'ffelon and protect them while we rescue Druid Laurel and the others.\n\nAs for our transportation, we need different arrangements. I'll meet you at the docks soon.

So many good people lost. Rahval, Ellic, my father. But through it all, we endured. Galen is safe now, in no small part because of you. You have my thanks.\n\nI hope I can be as worthy of the title of count as you are of hero, my friend.

For someone who isn't a Sea Elf, you certainly make an impression. The Gilded Blades could use a fighter like you. If you're ever looking for work, look me up. The lordling says the Mad Maiden will always have a berth here if I want it.
I will see you in Vastyr soon. Tell Laurel-friend Stefan what happened here. What we learned. Where we think Laurel has been taken.\n\nI will wait in the city, where the druids gather.

While I take a look around the rest of the vale, you and Frii find the door to the Ivy Throne. It's east of here, almost to the coast. We need to find Archdruid Orlaith and recover the sacred seeds.\n\nGood luck, friend. And guard Frii well.

I'll leave Captains Kaleen and Tsuzo to guard the alliance leaders while we go to Galen. First we protect the regalia. Then we stop Lord Bacaro—or the Ascendant Lord, or whatever he calls himself.\n\nNow get to Vastyr and protect the crown!

Back again for another crack at the trials, are you?\n\nI can't help but marvel at your dedication. You remind me of myself, back when I was first training with Captain Samara. But you've taken to it much quicker than me!

I still can't believe that the person I knew as Lord Bacaro was really the leader of the Ascendant Order and had delusions of being the new Druid King.\n\nAnyway, talk to Lady Arabelle. We have something for you.

Go to Glimmertarn and make sure Laurel and the staff are safe. I'll gather what knights I can spare. See if Captain Siravaen is willing to aid us once more. I have a feeling we'll need all the help we can get to stop Bacaro and his Ascendant Order.

Hi! Good to see you! Oops. Sorry. Still getting used to being back in my own head.\n\nI appreciate everything you did for us. And don't worry. I'll find a way to restore my cousin. I'm sure Druid Fenas will help. Joslin will be her old self in no time.

What am I going to tell my aunt? And how am I going to keep Octin from drifting away in a strong breeze? I'll have to get Druid Fenas to help. We'll work together and we'll figure something out.\n\nI'll fix Octin. Somehow.
Here, take the pouch of soil. There's a beautiful tree by the overlook. Tall and majestic. I think that's the perfect place to honor Frii's wishes. I'll meet you there.
I think I can disarm the trap, but it will take time. Go find Frii and stop whatever mad scheme Lord Bacaro is planning.
Druids! They attacked us! Took Wyress Tola … hurt so many others. I don't understand why they did this.
Those druids said they needed Wyress Tola to open the path. They're insane! I knew we should have been more suspicious when they started setting up camps!

Go to the docks near Castle Tonnere and help Captain Siravaen recover her vessel. I'll escort Archdruid Rahval back to Vastyr and incorporate the druids into our defenses. Join us there as soon as you can.\n\nBy the Green, we will weather this storm.

Let's hope that with Bacaro dead, what remains of the Ascendant Order and the last of the Firesong rebels will no longer be a threat.\n\nNow, go talk with our companions, my dear. They want to have a word with you before we return to Galen.
The Spirit of Root always outgrows its boundaries. Even in this state, it's pushing past our containment spell.
Druid Laurel did this on her own? She should be here, our grove could use her.
We're supposed to outgrow our anger, but make Archdruid Devyric pay for what he did here.
Oh, hello. I thought maybe I'd stay. Just to make sure Veshin is all right when he wakes up. \n\nThat sleeping potion was stronger than I realized.
We may have lost the Chronicle, but my Gwenaelle is safe. And all because Y'ffre chose to send me an outsider. Life is strange, my friend.
I will not forget what you have done for the Eldertide. And I imagine Sir Stefan will not forget what you did for him, either.
Silverbloom! A rare treat. My shimmering sea blossom knows me so well. She is just wonderful. And you're wonderful too. You really should sit. Relax. Maybe shed some armor.
I must stop thinking about Neri. Did I mention she had great hair and the most amazing eyes?\n\nI know. Sure, she betrayed me to a crazed sea witch. But I'm the forgiving sort.

Don't get too used to seeing me around, mercenary. The lordling asked me to remain a little longer and I'm still waiting on the rest of my pay.\n\nAfter that? Back to the open waters. Maybe we'll cross currents again at some point. The sea only knows.

Don't worry, I'll take the seed to Vastyr. I will feel much better knowing both myself and Archdruid Ellic have our circles' seeds safely tucked away within the walls of the city. \n\nI'll be as quick as the wind, druid-kin, I swear to you.
So you're going to help Captain Siravaen? I suppose we could use a Sea Elf warship when the battle starts.\n\nGo, friend, with Y'ffre's blessing.
Not now, dear. We need to use Frii's vortex to escape the rising lava!
Begin the summoning … touch the light … and go. You have served me well, old friend.
The false king is gone, but so is the spirit of the mountain. Without a spirit to calm it, Mount Firesong's rage will continue unchecked.
When you and Druid Laurel are finished, meet me at Mandrake Manor. By that time, I should know what we need to do to get the peace talks under way.

The druid cave is up the cliffs, to the west. Perhaps when you finish whatever you're doing, we can meet up again. You could join Laniwys and I.\n\nWatch for that tyrant Minahel. She doesn't want anyone to have fun.
Ellorien and I just want a little fun. Spice things up a bit, eh? Minahel's just a closed shell.\n\nDon't you get any ideas, though. She's all mine. I know just what she likes.
The ward should be gone now. Let's go through that door and find Frii.
You have important things asked of you. I understand. Responsibility, heavy as rainwater. It soaks, it chills. \n\nGo with strength. The sun will persevere.

I sort of thought Kiko would flap off after we found the treasure, but it looks like he's sticking with me.\n\nJust as well. Seems like things took a turn for the better once it was just the two of us!

You eliminated most of my rivals, adventurer. Even I few I once considered allies. Lady Arabelle was right to involve you in the affairs of the archipelago. Things may have taken a bad turn without your … intervention.\n\nHigh Isle will remember you.
Yves keeps my debt close to his chest. My claws are blunted by all this idle waiting. Does he think I'm foolish enough to play at these tables and prolong my time?
You … you're like me, aren't you? You've got a certain … passion for life, one might say.
Lady Arabelle is going to speak soon. I look forward to hearing what she will say on this auspicious occasion.

A traveler bold enough to approach Gastoc without a hint of fear? Now that is the sort of mettle I'm looking for!\n\nAnd if you're looking for work, I've got as much gold to give you as Galen's got troubles.

Juline Courcelles has jobs for a lone sellsword. For Druid Gastoc and Druid Aishabeh's tasks, you will need the aid of some hearty companions.\n\nThey all pay well. And I can also offer the thanks of House Mornard.

Octin seems much more focused than when he was a drifting ball of light. I know he wanted you to save his cousin, but you made the right choice. Joslin will make an excellent tree, but Octin would have lost himself in the dazzling brilliance.

The Chronicle was so frightened, so angry at what the Firesong did. It tried to help me, but it was confused. Unsure.\n\nI remember becoming a forest wraith. I'll need to write that down. It's a story that should be remembered.
Must…accept…transformation…
Thank you again for your help. I can't abide preventable deaths. But now I won't have to imagine Fauns like little Mohair here getting gobbled up by a hungry wolf.

Can't you see I'm busy? If I owe you cargo, then you'd better start swimming. Had to pitch most of my goods overboard. Damn Sea Elf pirates up north saw to that.\n\nOr are you with that tour organizer? I think I can smell her perfume on you.

Have I ever mentioned how much I detest public speaking? Goes against all my training as a spy and agent of the king. I'm supposed to hear the important bits of dialogue, not recite them. Ah, well. Before all that, I want to share something with you.

Hey, don't sneak up on a guy like that! Can't you see I've been through enough?\n\nIf you're here to ask me to march into those ruins and chase after fuzzy little animals, well, find someone else! It's not worth my life.
Go on. Tell Lady Arabelle everything is set.
The Eldertide seed is already lost to us. I'll see Archdruid Ellic safely to the cathedral. In the meantime, try to find Archdruid Rahval. Protect him. I'll meet back up with you shortly.
Be careful. You have the strength of mountains, but even the sea can wear down stone. Y'ffre's grace guide you quickly to Rahval's side.
This is so … exciting! I've always wanted to attend a function such as this. Stefan used to tell me stories about them. He seemed to hate these sorts of events, but to me they sounded fascinating!
Look at Za'ji, rubbing elbows with kings and queens! This one's mother would be so proud … if she were talking to Za'ji, that is.
Is this what they mean by peace talks? Everyone is talking, but none of it seems to be very important. Maybe we should just find a fighting pit and let them settle things my way.
Plenty of drink and an excuse to celebrate. I'll be there at All Flags Islet.

You've done so much for us, friend. I just wish Archdruid Rahval were here to guide us. I hope we made the right decision to separate the regalia. And that the circles can form a new Draoife sooner rather than later.\n\nEverything is so different now.
How strange. My purpose has been fulfilled, yet I still grow.\n\nTell me, Laurel-friend. How do you choose a purpose? Mortals have none naturally, I am told.

Laurel and Frii remained at Glimmertarn to direct Stonelore stragglers and to avoid the Firesong.\n\nMake speed, friend. If Archdruid Orlaith seeks the Sower mentioned in the Dream, both Laurel and Frii are in danger. I can't bear to lose Laurel, too.
Glimmertarn's the Stonelore village directly north of the city. While you're there, see if the druids are going to come and help defend Vastyr. We could use their numbers. And their magic.
Death should never make anyone happy. Sealord Nalos had to die. Simple as that. Am I glad that my blade tasted his blood at the end? Yes. I had a vow to fulfill and now it's done.

Off with a new purpose, I see. That means Sir Stefan cleared his head and has taken charge of the situation—good. But should I call him Count Stefan now? Do we need the high king to issue a proclamation?\n\nNo matter. Gods speed, friend.

Head east and you'll find an entrance to the old druid tunnels. Damn things were here long before we built the city.\n\nIf you find Ellic and Rahval, send them to the cathedral. We're gathering all the noncombatants there for their safety.
Lady Juline sent word that you'd returned from Embervine. I confess I was worried. It felt like the whole island might split in two, but here you are, fairly unscathed.\n\nGood for you.
Go, Aiven. Turn the druid stones and shine the light of the moons upon these pools.
The artifact within the temporal knot—it has a fate. I am handing it over to a friend. I watch as its siblings take form.\n\nSign it, proxy.
You're back! Please tell me you have news of my son!
Good day, traveler. Is this a chance encounter, or is there something you need me to help you with?
You're back in one piece! That's good. Turns out I still have a lot more research to do about regenerative properties. \n\nBut thank you for the help!
You're back! It eases my mind to know someone put down the monstrosity that attacked me. \n\nNow if only these healers would hurry up and ease my suffering!

Piece of advice, friend. Be careful out in the wilds of Galen. I've seen one slip put good fighters in overgrown graves.\n\nThough you look like you know your business. Shame some in Vastyr aren't as knowledgeable.
Druid Laurel is wise. Turns toward the sun. I am the keeper, the nourisher, the sower. I will wait … a bloom closed against the frost.
As you can see, I'm quite busy. Vastyr is locked in battle with this island. Who do you think fights it? Knights and soldiers? Bah, it's the engineers.\n\nNow what do you want with me?
Do what you promised, mortal. Pour Y'ffre's rain on roots and end the story.\n\nOnly way to save the living … and honor those who died.
Sir Stefan is at Castle Mornard, consulting with the count and preparing the city for the coming attack.\n\nDon't keep him waiting, mate.

Count Leonard set his son a challenging task by placing Galen's defenses in his hands. \n\nStill, bringing you into his confidence shows a remarkable amount of insight for someone of his age and experience.

What strange times we live in! Signs and wonders spring from ancient legend to walk among us. And now we have the tools to crown a new Druid King if we so choose.\n\nWhat should we do with them, I wonder.
Hmm. You there, you look quite capable. Would you be interested in helping seal the volcanic vents on Galen?
Intruders in the castle! How dare they trespass on House Mornard!
He's been through here. I'd know that stench of his anywhere.

Ready for your big moment? Oh, I know you hate these sorts of things. Me, too. But it's not for us. It's for everybody else. Gives them a sense of closure. Like when your ship finally bangs up against the dock after a long voyage.\n\nJust smile, mate!

For such a warlike people, you do seem obsessed with the notion of peace, mercenary. Sure, you and I learned to work together. This time. But the next? We're just as likely to cross swords as break bread.\n\nThat's not a threat. Just an observation.
After all the pain and suffering we've endured lately, I hope the various leaders negotiate in good faith. We've had enough betrayal for one season, I think.
I see you learned from our experience—never let down your client! \n\nDo you think maybe you could put in a good word for me with Count Stefan? I could really use a contact in House Mornard.
Go on, talk to whoever you need to. I'll be here when you have a free moment.
I saw someone handing out expensive glasses of wine. I hope we don't have to return those.
Don't stop to talk to me, partner. There are way more important people at this affair that want your attention!
Is that really Queen Ayrenn? And High King Emeric? My word! Quen told me to be on my best behavior, but this is an opportunity too good to pass up!\n\nWhat? I won't steal anything too noticeable!
I heard Archdruid Rahval named you druid-kin, outsider. If you did as much for the archdruids as you did for my Gwenaelle, I can see how you've earned that title.
I was told this was a celebration, but I think there are too many long faces for that to be true. You'd better give these good folk something to smile about.
The false king awakened and unleashed the spirit of the mountain. He draws upon its power. Soon, nothing will be able to stop the eruption.\n\nWe must hurry.

I assume you'll be heading back to High Isle now? Do give Lady Arabelle my regards and assure her that House Mornard stands ready should the Ascendant Lord and his so-called knights emerge from hiding.\n\nKnights, bah! Cowards, the lot of them.

What a lovely little island this is. The air is almost dewy. Quite different from the sands that I'm used to. Ain't that right, Unu? \n\nAh, yes, this dragon frog is my boon companion. We've been together since he was barely an ember-breathing froglet.

Well, you know what they say. You can't make the world's spiciest dish without singeing a few eyebrows!\n\nAt least, I've always said that. Even in my tried and true spicy recipes, it's never proven untrue!
Thanks for helping get the Mad Maiden freed. If Captain Siravaen says we're going to fight for Vastyr, then that's where we're headed.\n\nYou heard her, let's get to it!
What are we standing around for? Captain says we're headed to Vastyr! \n\nI can't wait to see her put Nalos's head on a spike!
When Chef Rhazeez cooks for me in a private audience, I'll be the talk of the town. \n\nKeeping such innovative company is a luxury few can afford! Yourself included, I presume.

Ah, here I thought I so expertly captured the local culture as to render me invisible. I suppose I shouldn't be surprised. You must have recognized my dashing smile from the tomes I've penned. Ignatius Galenus, famed scholar. Charmed, I'm sure.
Must go … join … it calls me ….
I'm starting to think that I've been underpaid for this job. I didn't expect to have to tolerate so much inane nattering.
Ah! Uh, hand over your poky end. No, no, no, give me your purse or I'll halt. \n\nYour gold. Can I have it. Please?

You have the ring? Good. Please bring it to Frelene. I'm sure you'll find her in Vastyr. Tell her of my fate, but don't worry her overmuch. I want her to know that I'm not suffering. \n\nThank you, my friend. You can't know how much this means.
How does one capture something as beautiful as this vista? Even with magic enchanting my brush, the challenge feels insurmountable.

To get a piece of Jocien back after nearly twenty years … it's like seeing his face again. It's almost as if he's here with me.\n\nI never understood his pull to the sea. But perhaps this is what he meant by its endless mysteries and surprises.
I'll keep an eye on the Firesong from out here, and join you later if I can. Good luck, friend. Guard Frii well.

Heh. I like the course Sir Stefan is charting. I'm happy to play my part and take Frii to Y'ffelon if it puts the Firesong off their guard. The question is whether Frii is willing … and can keep a secret.
Whispers. They're here. Bringing about the doom and destruction. The chill and fire. The end! the whispers bring about the end of all!
It is not the Eldertide way to kneel before any crown of metal. But I admit I will probably spend the rest of my life retelling the story of what I see in this room today.
I do not deserve to be here. No Firesong does. But I will do my best to listen and remember what is said here today.
I've seen my share of rough waters. This business with the Dreadsails and the Firesong was about the worst I can recall.\n\nNice to have smooth sailing again.
Hero. Is there something else I can assist you with?
I have no idea who you are, but you'll pay for this!
Keep Laurel safe, druid-kin. Then find that usurper and kick his arse. He has no right to even touch the sacred regalia, let alone call himself our Druid King!
Lord Bacaro wielded the regalia. Could he really be the new Druid King? I … I don't know what to think about this ….
We tracked Lord Bacaro and his knights into Y'ffre's Path, but lost their trail. Lady Arabelle is still out there searching.

We all knew the captain would come back for us. She's about as affectionate as an ill-tempered shark but she cares for us in her own way. If you hadn't shown up, she would have burned this whole place down trying to save our hides.
You better not be here for the reason I think you're here.

A handsome shrine, isn't it? This is the resting place of the mage Faras Aralen. My grandmother. She passed many years ago, but I hope she approves of me taking up arcane studies too.\n\nShe must, right?
Sea Elves, druids, a smoldering volcano … what is happening on our beloved island?\n\nWhy, I have half a mind to move back to Wayrest!
What is this island coming to? And why doesn't House Mornard do something?

Traveler, I recommend sticking close to the city. Reports of Sea Elf attacks are on the increase and we don't have enough knights to guarantee safety on the roads.\n\nThat's why Galphen requested an escort.

Such a sad and disappointing season in which to live. Our Firesong brothers and sisters have become a dark cloud, blotting out the sun's bright light. If you must leave the city, do remain cautious. The island's dangers are a hundredfold right now.

What a waste. So many people lost in the attack on the city. And for what? Some ancient druid prophecy?\n\nWe're still trying to find everyone who's unaccounted for. I just hope most of them turn up still breathing.

I shall learn what I can about the Dusksabers and their clients. When I have gathered enough information to progress our investigation, I shall contact you.\n\nThe threat is great, but the danger is not imminent. Not yet.
You'll find Sir Stefan in the castle's throne room. Go on ahead. I'll meet you there.

Through this doorway lies the vast library of Scrivener's Hall. Within it are rifts to other planes. We must journey to the Deadlands, there we'll find the staff.\n\nUnfortunately, Valinna won't appreciate our intrusion. Be on your guard.

Here we are, deep within the bowels of Scrivener's Hall. With more time, Keshargo would show you where the most important records are. Alas, we must press on. Valinna's meddling ideology cannot be allowed to fester. We must reclaim the staff.
May the Great Eye lead you safely to the Shrine of the Golden Eye, chosen.

Fate's chosen! The Golden Eye so rarely elevates a mortal, but I can see that you aren't just another of Nirn's common rabble.\n\nHow can I assist you, chosen? Just keep your voice down. Followers aren't appreciated in these lands.
Don't look to me, mainlander. Captain Siravaen is in command here!

We yield, mainlander. The Firesong want no more of this madness.\n\nArchdruid Orlaith led us down a dark path. We want to return to the Green. Rejoin the other circles and end the bloodshed. You have my word on that.

Bring forth the three glyphics and activate their power, mortal. They will call into being the agreement that will bind us and ensure that this is neither a trick nor a coercion. You will help preserve Apocrypha and thereby safeguard Nirn.
Ah, would you care to help me test out some magic I'm working on? I promise it will be amusing, not deadly.
What happened today was a setback, but the knowledge is my burden to bear. No one needs to learn from it except me. \n\nI'll make it right by capturing the Lark of Rosgard. Next time. I swear it!

I feel a little out of my depth here. So much trouble came from the medallions I prepared. And then the magical wards I helped raise at Memorial Hall failed to stop the Magus.\n\nNow I'm supposed to turn my efforts to diplomacy?
Thank the Tribunal, you've returned! What in the name of the Three happened? There was a great rumbling and a burst of some sort of lightning. I feared the worst.
You should have kept your nose to yourself, walker. This does not concern you!
This one and his kin shall return to Elsweyr on light feet, and your name in our stories.\n\nThe Eye of Baan Dar glints with mischief! This one imagines it too is ready to see faraway places.
The news of your good deed will spread all the way to Necrom. We're sure to get an influx of visitors to the temple any day now!\n\nI can't wait to see this shrine returned to its former glory.
Now, it's off to Necrom for me. Don't be offended, but I hope I don't see you there. Not for a writ anyway.

You there! Do you work here? As a notary for the Kwama Consortium of Necrom I demand that you explain why production has halted. \n\nAre you aware of the irreparable harm this is inflicting on our image?
Analyzing. Subject: Unknown. Threat Detection: Unknown. Begin Friendly Introduction. Greetings, I am Protus. Kemel-Ze Security Oversight …. \n\nError. Diagnostic Check …. Error. Error.
The others just passed me. They're safe.\n\nNow, all that remains is to decide the fate of the Talisman of Saint Vorys.
Good luck at the shrine. An outsider like you probably needs all the luck you can get.

The hero of Clockwork City, I should bow to you. \n\nI assume that fool Thoryn sent you here? Well, I have the situation under control. Your presence isn't necessary here and it draws too much attention. Let's not trouble the Gods unduly.

Although the Remnants must abandon this place, do not think your efforts a waste. Staunching a wound is the first step toward recovery.\n\nOur clan will clear out any invaders still left, then begin transporting the Apogee's wisdom to a new home.

The portal in the room downstairs connects to the Endless Library of Apocrypha. Once there, head northwest and meet me at Cipher's Midden. Our research begins there.\n\nSince Curate Gadayn is intent on recovering the relic, he shall accompany us.

I have alerted Leramil to three specific threads of fate that converge in a place known as the Telvanni Peninsula. She will guide you to these locations so you can unmask my hidden adversaries.\n\nGo to the city of Necrom. Leramil awaits you there.

Ah, mortal, I didn't expect to see you in Fargrave. Indeed, I wasn't even certain your kind could travel here.\n\nAs you can see, my fabulous creatures are eager and ready to perform. And as soon as Madam Whim summons us, the show will go on!

I never traveled far from Necrom. Barely left the Telvanni Peninsula and that was just one trip to Mournhold with Abbot Ilvel.\n\nThe abbot has given me a mission, though, and I mean to complete it. Just tell me what to do and I'll follow your lead.
The Stormwing is docked right over there. You can't miss it.
Now, you are a welcome sight! Please tell me the way out of here is clear! We were starting to lose any hope of escape.
Please tell me you're here to rescue us? Barluk's hurt, and I'm a miner, not a healer.
If I ever make it out of this mine I'm going to wring the neck of whoever made my sweet kwama go mad. They didn't deserve this!
What comes next feels mysterious. Perhaps the others will have an idea on how to proceed.\n\nUntil then, you have our gratitude, outworlder. May we fight alongside each other again in the future.
Ah. Hello, traveler. I see you linger in Apocrypha as well.

It is very nice to see you, friend. And with my own two eyes thanks to your aid back in the study! I'm still getting my Nord legs back and I fear this musty tome aroma won't ever leave me, but I am doing much better than when you first found us.

Should have figured an adventurer like you would stick around! Seems we're cut from the same cloth you and I. Apocrypha may seem all doom and gloom, but it has a way of keeping hold of you, and I'm not just talking about the tentacles!

I prefer simple anomalies. This one has become too complex and dangerous for my liking. I'll return the mortal corpse-keeper to Necrom. Perhaps by the time I'm done, the course of fate will have corrected itself.\n\nBut probably not.

I'll return to Necrom with Scruut if Leramil thinks that's for the best. Just stay safe, my friend. And keep Leramil safe, too.\n\nI'll protect this half of the relic and see what more I can learn about Master Shelreni.
My time here in the Cloisters has been … enlightening. I think, after all this, it'd be nice to stretch my legs and explore the plane. I'll do my best to avoid mad cultists and traps, I promise.

Meenai-Shai is back and I'm whole again. This may take some getting used to.\n\nI have grown quite used to speaking my thoughts out loud and going unheard. But, silence is a virtue in a place like this.
A great evil reached out to strike at our order. I must know why. Take young Gadayn into your confidence, adventurer. Together, the two of you may find answers and recover the Fulcrum Obscura.

I wouldn't go that way if I were you, traveler. The study down the road is crawling with horrors and they're sure to spill out!\n\nI only just made it out of there with my life. Hermaeus Mora have mercy.
Our Prince will be happy to hear of your involvement. It's a shame that you can't stay. To study a mind as unswayable as your own would truly be a pleasure.\n\nThink about it. Farewell.

I'm not sure about everything the floating mass of tentacles just told you, but Scruut is correct about one thing. If anyone can help you figure out what's going on here, it's Leramil.\n\nLet's go back and show her what you uncovered.

Master Shelreni has trapped Meln's spirit in a soul gem. You must retrieve that gem or destroy it.\n\nGo to Ald Isra and find Shelreni's aide, Mouth Vabdru. He must have an office in the tower called Tel Vara.
The Prince of Knowledge sent you to help us, didn't he, traveler?

I suggest you begin with the old Tel Rendys Hall, to the southwest of this camp. Captain Zenfis reports that his Dusksabers are having a difficult time there. \n\nIf you can succeed where they have so far failed, I will make it worth your while.

The signs were clear and inarguable. The Remnants have ended. We have known this for some time. This attack only closed and locked the door.\n\nWe will assist in recovering any relics too dangerous to be left behind. Then, we cannot say.
You are fate's chosen, yes? I hear we have you to thank for the salvation of Apocrypha.
Finally, the fever breaks and the corruption dissipates. According to Scruut, we have you to thank.\n\nSo, thank you, traveler.
The air is clear and my head no longer swims or pounds. And the Great Eye has returned to us, so all is good.
What a great day in the Midden, traveler! The One Who Knows communes with us again and Apocrypha returns to normal. This was your doing, yes?

Prepare yourself, proxy. We should both be able to withstand a short visit to the Panopticon, but that does not mean we can ignore the dangers. Steel your mind and harden your will.\n\nWhen you are ready, let us head inside.
Well look at that. You did it! I need to go let Master Shelreni know that the way into the tower is finally open.
The cairns have been activated. Let's return to Leramil's study so she can complete the ritual.
The vault is open to you. Don't let your valiant deeds go unrewarded. I allow very few access to the vault, you know.
Nothing about this job went the way I expected it to. But you stuck around anyway. I didn't expect that.

Being dead and incorporeal isn't how I planned to spend eternity, but being with you is a thousand times better than remaining in Shelreni's clutches. And we delayed her plans for my Black Book.\n\nNow, tell me about your dealings with Hermaeus Mora.
Despite the strange magicka that fills this chamber, I was able to open a portal. It shall take us into the same eye that Torvesard and Blightcrown entered moments ago.\n\nWe must hurry, proxy.

I think I might wait a while before going inside. I don't know how long it will take the Daedra and Hushed of Quires Wind to recover from the madness caused by those corrupted scrolls. Or at least calm down.

Back, and right quick. Brelynn's sent me a piece of her mind—it got here just before you did. Along with the information I wanted from her.\n\nI ought to be careful with you. The last time I had someone so efficient working for me, I lost my eye.

My office is through the north door and the insignia is behind my desk. Use it to unlock the wards in the cavern or you'll never reach the tower.\n\nTel Baro is hard to find. Look for the Cavern of the Tower, east of Ald Isra. The tower is inside.

When dealing with matters of fate, meetings such as this meeting are inevitable.\n\nKnow that I am Torvesard. And know that we need not be adversaries in these matters. I simply seek an ancient dream, barely remembered. Lost knowledge, nothing more.
You horrible fetcher! I can't believe you delivered Harn's message. Leave me alone. I have to figure out how I'm going to get him out of my hair.
Oh! It's you again. Don't worry—I understood Harn's message perfectly!

Well, that was unexpected! I don't have a clue about what any of that meant. Frankly, I wouldn't have it any other way. I'm just happy to be done with that condescending wanderer of realities.\n\nThank you for your help.

I do so appreciate your help in all this. Not everyone gets the chance to learn their own fate in time to do something about it. And as far as possible fates go, that one wasn't nearly as damning as it could have been.

I erased all evidence of this moment … and of the events that led to the loathsome action I was forced to perform. But I could not strip it from my own memory. And now that misstep has borne bitter fruit.\n\nWhat did the Dremora tell you, chosen?

Remember, as long as Shelreni possesses the Black Book, she can complete her rite. If they fully unlock this forgotten secret, multiple realms are doomed.\n\nI shall meet you at the bookshop in Necrom after I complete my investigations.
We'll set off as soon as the feeling returns to our legs. Not sure what we'll say about our absence. Gah-Malz is the one who has to make the report. Feel bad for her.
The faster we head back to the others the faster we're away from this place. It makes my scales itch worse than bog mites.
Decisions to make. We were taken against the pact, but ruffians and vagabonds never care for treaties. I have much to think on.
You're not like the others. No. You're special, aren't you? How interesting.\n\nWho are you?

I've never faced such a convoluted contradiction of fate before. While we learned the cause of the incongruity, I wasn't able to make the necessary corrections. Unfortunately.\n\nAt least we chased off Torvesard and defeated the kynreeve.
I can't believe Keshargo is here. That he's still alive!\n\nAs soon as we find the Itinerant Staff I'm going to ask him how he managed to get away. There's still so much to learn from him.

Please, I have no one else I can turn to. I need help.\n\nI worked as a servant in the towers of Tel Dreloth. Nathyn, the son of Mistress Dreloth, is being kept prisoner there. At least, I think he must be.
Stay back from the ward! Mother says it's already in a weakened state due to the strength of my affliction.\n\nI don't recognize you, stranger. What are you doing with Dacia?

Whoever you are, you've fallen for Dacia's fanciful tale, and now you're enabling her dangerous obsession with my son.\n\nNathyn made his feelings for Dacia perfectly clear in the letter he wrote. Or was that vital piece of information kept from you?

I have yet to find any relevant information concerning the stolen memory, the Hidden Kindred, Torvesard, or how a Daedric Prince was able to invade another Prince's realm. I find this lack of knowledge … vexatious.

The spirit makes a good point. You'd be noticed immediately the moment you tried to get close to Shelreni. If he thinks he can direct you to make a proper spell of concealment, he has more faith in you than I do.\n\nI suppose you should try though.
I'm with you, friend. We have to stop Shelreni, with or without the help of House Telvanni.
What are you waiting for? Do what all good mouths do and converse with the masters in my stead!\n\nMasters Norvora or Foves like to talk. Get one of them to tell you where they stashed Shelreni.
Dacia? Stranger … you shouldn't be here. Too dangerous. Go no further!

Remember, a Dark Elf by a green mushroom in Tel Huulen. Tell her, "both light and shadow can be deadly." She'll reply, "Though only one chases the other." Then hand over the letter and she'll give you gold.\n\nNow go while I lead my pursuers away.
As soon as it's safe, I'm getting as far from this place as I can. Before I fall asleep again. I don't want to hear the chanting anymore … or work while I sleep ….

If Federo and I need your help in the future, we'll be sure to send for you. Reynila fought hard for Sharp's freedom so he might live his life however he wanted. \n\nIt's my job to light the way forward.

You're Sharp's friend? I had feared he spent all those years alone. But he found someone. He found … you.\n\nHis sister, Dimik-ei. So close to freedom. Promise you'll help her. Take her the rest of the way, please. Help her.

This prism is quite marvelous. A smooth crystalline exterior with a—hmm, writhing?—interior. How curious.\n\nOh, if you are waiting for an additional payment, there's none forthcoming. Our agreement did not cover any gratuities.
Are you the surly ruffian who's been pilfering through my things? Mmm, no. You have a different scent.
With that, my work is done. We did good, hero.\n\nYou know, I sometimes visit the tavern in Necrom. Stop by if you're in the area. It would be nice to see you in less professional conditions.
Mevei's going to help me. I have a way forward.\n\nI don't want this to be the last time I see Sharp. It can't be.
Was that you rummaging around upstairs? If you're a new servant, then I hope you learn to respect other people's belongings.\n\nAlso, and I'll try to say this gently, your smell is quite … pungent.

Hmm. Sorry, no time for the likes of you. The masters and mouths are very strict that we talk to no one.\n\nYou don't even want to know what they did to me when they heard I accidentally told an Elf from House Dres where the well was.

What she said changes nothing, by the way. Hezehk still resents scurrying around when told to. Still ….\n\nAll right, then. Back to Fargrave for me. Hope I never see you again, mortal. And keep what I said to yourself. It loses value otherwise.

So, the memories of my past die with Sondivel, the Reformer. May we all forget his name in time.\n\nBut I have answers. More than that, I have Dimik-ei, and Federo and Mevei, and I have you. It's a lot more than I started with.

I miss my comforts and routines from before, sure. But I never had … I don't know … purpose? Fulfillment? Direction?\n\n… Friends? That might be it. I've never had real friends before. Time will tell if I like that better than fine silks.
Thanks for taking that off my hands. Hope it's going to someone who lacks a sense of smell.
I can't thank you enough. Having something to hold over Foves's head presents unlimited opportunities. Now I just need to figure out how best to use them.
We servants work hard to please our masters. We scrub, cook, carry messages.\n\nStill, some people have no problem ransacking through our property whenever they want.
Last I saw Zavaal? He ran deep into the Forum. Have fun with the Darkreaves, if you go in.\n\nNow leave me be, mortal. I have dying to do.
I usually have this spot all to myself. Well, you can have it today, stranger. I don't feel up to fishing.\n\nGood luck to you. I'm going back to bed.
They're still alive in the ruins. Walker, please. Save my family.

Did you hear? Sharp called me his deek-nujei!\n\nI know his memories died with Sondivel, and I think it's for the best, but I'm happy he wants to rebuild. Since he knows nothing, I could tell him anything! … Not that I will. Too much.

The savior of my Clockwork City, I knew you'd be the one I spoke to.\n\nIt's not often that one bound by mortality comes to my attention more than once. Most, like Nilphas Drethan are wisps of smoke in the fires of time.
If you see any Dusksabers in the old hall, tell them Master Shelreni grows impatient. Whatever delays their progress, they need to deal with it. Quickly.
This one's smile is small but genuine. Twelvane expected Researcher An'Xeh to send someone to help Warlock Vanton, but not someone of your reputation.\n\nYou could not have arrived at a better time.
I don't know what you experienced in there, but there were times here where it felt like we were losing Vanton. \n\nI'm glad you managed to keep him from succumbing to Ansuul's trap.
I hope I don't have any nightmares relating to what Vanton endured. My spine is already tense from too many waking terrors.
Thank Julianos, Vanton's quiet again. And you as well!\n\nWhat can I get for the savior of the waking world?

Ohrijha will think only good thoughts for my young friend Dot. She is a smart one. Perhaps she just got distracted or met up with others and decided to travel. \n\nShe did that once - went with some Bandaari to Redfur Trading Post and back!
You may enter. The curate is expecting you.
I wouldn't suggest disobeying the order of Magister Gothren. I've seen him turn a retainer into a mudcrab for a lesser infraction.
I don't understand this necessity for debate. If it were up to me, we'd get right to the vote. Nothing anyone has to say will change my mind about Shelreni.\n\nNow then, is Magister Meln really dead?

If you're intent on flouting Magister Gothren's authority, then I suggest you speak to Masters Foves and Norvora. Neither of them could keep a confidence if their lives depended upon it.\n\nBut if anyone asks, you heard nothing from me.

I forgot how boring my so-called peers can be. Pity Shelreni didn't eliminate a few more of my rivals before we noticed.\n\nBut your master, Meln. I have fond memories of his many antics. That's why I wanted a word with you.
They're letting you inside? Then you can warn them! Tell the masters. They underestimate Master Shelreni at their own peril!

This is bad! Blightcrown killed Master Shelreni and Vaermina took possession of her body! And she walked into Apocrypha!\n\nWe should return to the Necrom Bindery. We must tell Leramil what happened here. She'll know what we need to do.
If you'd asked me how the experiment would end … I never would have guessed. Somewhere, far away, I can almost hear old Mora himself laughing at my expense. \n\nPretentious squidfaced librarian.

You know, I almost didn't show up. Seeing you again brought back so many memories. The idea of returning to Balmora and avoiding this talk certainly crossed my mind.\n\nI can't keep running from this though. We need to talk about Veya.
Not now, dear. We need to use Frii's vortex to escape the rising lava!

You know, it just now occurred to me that Hermaeus Mora himself might not appreciate what the Fateweaver Key has wrought.\n\nRegardless, what do you say? Would you be willing to continue our collaboration?
Being interrupted this much reminds me how much I do, in fact, enjoy my solitary time out in the field. Please, leave me be.
It sounds like you aided these people in the past, yes? Well no matter now. This is a military operation. As you were, outsider.
Please! You've got to help me!
Save yourself if you can! I'm done for.
Please! This Kynmarcher is a monster! Don't leave me to die!
I have to find the shadows and burrow away Daedrat-like. There will be times for standing tall as there will be times to run from the gibbers. Now is the time for burrowing. \n\nIt will be good.
Greetings, stranger. It saddens me to know my son cannot remember me. Still, I'm keeping an eye on him, and perhaps we will journey together.

Leramil says she's feeling better, but I'm not so sure. She's eager to find out what happened after we separated at the Infinite Panopticon, though. You better talk to her and let her know all the details.
You'll have to do this on your own, mortal. I can feel the affliction beginning to take hold. I'll pose a danger to you if I succumb as the other Daedra have.
I wonder if we can even find the Infinite Panopticon again. Let's rendezvous with Leramil at the Necrom Bindery and see what she thinks about all this.
Well, there's our way in. I'm still not sure about this, but I promised Leramil I'd help. Lead on, friend.

I see what you did there. Clever. I suppose I've been taken off the board. A bit of revenge on my part is probably called for.\n\nThe path to the memory Vaermina seeks lies through the Infinite Panopticon. Torvesard will lead her there.
I'm trusting you with Morian. Others may come for the rest of the creatures here, but they won't take care of him. See him to safety. Please.

I am no help to you in my present state. You must locate Vaermina. Destroy Master Shelreni's body before the Prince of Dreams causes irreparable damage to the Panopticon. Gadayn will see me safely back to Cipher's Midden while Scruut accompanies you.

The Great Eye! I can feel his presence again, and not just because he's right over there and wants to speak to you. I wonder when the next boulder is going to drop on us.\n\nGo on. It's not polite to keep the Prince of Fate waiting.

My power remains diminished due to the toxins Peryite's follower polluted Apocrypha with, but you helped me break free of the worst of the miasma.\n\nYou saw the contents of the Glyphic of Hidden Paths. As did Torvesard. I did not expect that.
That stone is the last one from a cluster we made together years ago. When Azandar and I were on the trail of …. Ah, but what does it matter now?\n\nGood luck, and get gone. Please.
Let us conclude our discussion.

You're like a blessing from Zenithar himself.\n\nSolni Nrayn should be at the graveyard in Necrom. As for me, I suppose I'll fashion a splint and hobble my way to a settlement—with the comfort of knowing my professional reputation will remain intact.
I can feel the relief emanating from my aunt's spirit. You've done us a great service, courier.

I wish I could go with you on this, but Scruut is correct. This is a task for fate's chosen, and fate's chosen alone.\n\nGo, but know that I have faith in you. You can recover the glyphic and preserve reality. It is what destiny demands.

The Daedra never bothered us before. The Great Eye always told us we were safe here.\n\nBut that Seeker … there was madness in its eyes. Open sores, a smell of disease … and the screeching … it was awful!

Oathman Balver Bemis. I like the sound of that, don't you? You were instrumental in my ascent to my new station. If you need any favors from House Telvanni, well, ask Spellwright Varsva. But I can guarantee you, I'll put in a good word for you.
Well, I suppose I should start searching for a new retainer. Someone who won't try to poison me, for instance. Especially not in front of a spellwright.
Don't know nothing else. Leave me be.
It appears that Balver is more clever than he lets on. But know that with any slip-up Balver may suffer the same fate as his late master.

I'm both relieved and a bit disappointed that we can't accompany you, my friend. I'll stay with Leramil and Scruut until you return.\n\nI'd pray that the ancestors walk beside you, but now that I think about it, you have Meln. So they already do.

Once again, everyone takes Meln the Mouthless for granted. They all just assume I'm going to agree to go with you on another quest to stop Torvesard?\n\nSure, I don't really have much of a choice in the matter, seeing as you have my gem, but still!
An odd collection of allies for someone so formidable. You may count me among them. At least until our paths once again diverge.\n\nI am ready to enter the Mythos when you are, mortal.

Not us, mortal. Just you. And Meln, I suppose. Only fate's chosen can resolve this, and that's still you.\n\nThe Prismatic Iris Shore is north of here. Meet us in Cipher's Hall after you deal with Torvesard. Then we can update the Chronicle.
I'd only slow you down, friend. My wounds are significant but not life threatening.\n\nPlease, don't let these invaders pillage the Tranquil Catalog.

If this wasn't tangled in my own responsibilities, I would have told Leramil to go float in the Void. Instead, here I am, delivering a message for one of Hermaeus Mora's—the Great Eye's—lesser agents.\n\nPay attention. I only want to say this once.

Do not despair, chosen. Through your efforts, the lost memory was denied Vaermina and Peryite, thus preserving reality. That Torvesard saw part of the secret is regrettable but not catastrophic.\n\nNow return to Leramil's study in Cipher's Midden.
While nothing can bring back the ciphers Akacirn took from us, at least you've put a stop to his mad ambitions. I shudder to think what would have happened if he'd succeeded.

I've given you what you came for. The sooner you depart, the sooner you can deal with Akacirn as you see fit. And allow me to get back to my own concerns.\n\nI have no more patience for mortal troubles.
Tem sees you, chosen proxy of the Great Eye. Adventures, triumphs, that have happened. Or may happen. Or may never happen.\n\nSpeak, and Tem will tell you what you wish to know.
Once again I find you braving the dark season, wanderer. Fearless despite your fear. Yet still cautious, I hope.

You two are a lot more friendly than the mercenaries that came 'round looking for Federo awhile back.\n\n'Course, when they woke me and dragged me out of bed, I was nearly sober. I think. Anyway, they haven't been back since.
Uh, who are you? What do you want?
Hey there. Don't worry, <<1>> is pretty fierce, but he's disciplined.
Hello, stranger. Take care not to tread on the flower. It is a tribute to Ma'nna, my daughter. She loved flowers.
Well, you've caught me appreciating today's take. Not that that's a bad thing, mind you. I'm quite proud of my work.

You defeated Ansuul the Tormentor? Queen of terror and scourge of the waking world? I wish I could give you a discount, but my thanks is all I can offer. \n\nHere, take a look and restock for your future adventures, hero.
Tremble at the—at the, uh … excuse me. You actually look kind of dangerous.

I can count the number of mortals recorded in the Chronicle of Apocrypha on the tips of my tentacles. But here we part ways, ally. All contradictions arising from Vaermina and Peryite's assault on my master are resolved.\n\nFarewell.
Talk to Leramil while I gather my thoughts.\n\nSay a few words indeed.
Uh, hello stranger. Please don't feel obligated to speak to me. You look like someone with more important places to be.
Too late, too late. The door sealed long ago has opened just a crack, but the damage is done. That which was forgotten is now remembered.

Congratulations, my friend. Having your name inscribed in the book of fate isn't a casual honor. I expect it means even greater adventures and accolades are in store for you.\n\nOh, I wonder if my ghostly heart can take it!
I'll be honest and tell you that I didn't want to come here. I hoped to put Sailenmora behind me. \n\nEven if I ended up looking like the hero who stopped the Lark of Rosgard, we both know the truth.
Didn't think we'd meet again so soon, did you?\n\nI heard about this gathering and figured I should stop by.
You, my friend, know how to get things done. Congratulations on saving the Necropolis!
It seems there is more to you than I thought. Well done.
Hey, merc. Looks like you've been keeping busy.\n\nDidn't know the people of this peninsula had it in them to show this kind of gratitude. Color me surprised. I'd say you earned it.

The One Who Knows selected you as fate's champion, and you have done well in your role. I am glad I was able to assist you in this endeavor.\n\nUntil Hermaeus Mora calls upon us again, let us hear what Gadayn has decided to say to the crowd.

I thank you for all you have done for the Necrom Necropolis, champion. But forgive me if I'm even more thankful for how you took Gadayn under your wing. You gave him the chance to meet this terrible test at your side and find his true mettle.

Good to see you again, friend! Amazing to see how influential you've been. Truly remarkable. Now, if you're like me and need a break from conversing, I have a few tomes tucked in my robes for casual reading. Just say the word.
Looks like the mortal is good for more than just crawling through some old books.\n\nActually, Hezehk thinks you did some nice work.
Although the order of the Remnants may have disbanded, we stay in your debt. Only through your actions did we accept our fate. Thank you.

Huzmargo is overjoyed to see you again. Have you given any more thought to becoming an official addition to the Rectory's Chorus? Even a short stay. Perhaps just a century or two? Think it over! The Rectory's doors will always be open to you.

Oh, why does the universe hate me, mortal? A simple task to fix an out-of-sync fate on a backwater world has become an irritant in my primary orb.\n\nGo. Leramil waits in the Necrom Bindery. I'd prefer to wallow in solitude, if you don't mind.
Hopefully we can all return to our normal lives now. And this fetcher can finally shut up about honoring his ancestors.
Finally, I might end the task set upon me and show everyone that I am truly most pious and honorable in my dutiful respects to my ancestors.
Finally, all this talk can settle down. I'll be able to get down to my tasks once more. After I send this hireling on another little errand to keep him busy.
You know, now that I have time to think on it, I really start to think I'm being put on by Spellwright Moran.
Your arrival marked the beginning, and yet where will it all end?
The crisis averted, my spines tell me, for now. You are indeed a brave soul.
Don't keep me here too long. I need to get to Necrom before that fool. He thinks my ancestors will shun me? Ha! I'll show him the right way to honor those who have passed.
Can you believe her? My fellow pilgrim prioritizing anything other than her ancestor's wishes. She should care less what I bring for my family and focus more on her own paltry offerings.
It couldn't have gotten that far. It's not like a book can stand up and walk away, right?

Excellent. Another mortal. I take it you were eavesdropping? So you must have heard what I have to deal with. She can't even remember which book we've been sent to find. Her mind is perpetually stuck on butterflies!
Nassophra is really starting to get on my nerves!\n\nI knew she couldn't tell mortals apart, but I thought she at least had a mind for books!
You should gallop away as fast as you can, this is going to be a big one. That fool won't know what hit him once I've cast my spell.
He thinks that will impress the council? Well, wait till he sees the spell I created! Once the Magisters see this, they'll beg me to join their ranks!

I'm very glad you stopped, not many travelers do along this road. So busy, all a conversation costs is time of which we are all in good supply.\n\nWe are none of us late. Not really. We are all headed toward the same ending and no one rushes there.
<You approach the wheel.>
You have received clearance to enter, outsider. There is no further need for discussion.

The curate and I are busy, outsider. I am eager to hear what he thinks of my book, Ancestors of a Humble Mouth. It's a work in progress, but at least two booksellers have expressed interest.\n\nCome back later.
Speak your mind, Sharp. How does it feel, wrapped in the tendrils of my will? Did it hurt to try and resist? \n\nBe honest with me. You know how I appreciate your candor.

Master Marena revealed her inadequacies when she allowed herself to be captured. The other masters survived. In both cases, House Telvanni won.\n\nIf you plan to chase Shelreni, I suggest you leave now. I'm not going to hold that portal open forever.

The Prince of Fate thinks himself so perfect. But for all his power, he couldn't eliminate the memory he so desperately sought to hide. Not from my dreams, not from his own mind. And now I remember most of it. Only one secret remains to uncover.
Find some other doorway to haunt, little one.
Harn's not getting his money's worth from Cortin.
Never ask for a favor from Harn Orenvi. He'll squeeze everything out of you in return.
What is Ald Isra coming to? Murder right at the entrance to the Assembly of Masters? I'm sure Master Thilse will be shocked when she receives this report.

Well, looks like you certainly dug deeper than I expected. If you think this changes anything, you're sadly mistaken. I'm still a Telvanni master. This is a bump in the road, nothing more.\n\nI do suggest you watch behind you. I have a long memory.

Are you going to climb the shelves with me? Eat with our ears? Listen with our hands!\n\nDon't worry, I'm invisible. Did the spell dance and everything. But if someone does see me, I'll talk like a person. They won't realize that I'm not!
That Morag Tong assassin came out of nowhere. I blinked and she was in the room.\n\nNow she's talking with Master Sulis. I wonder what this is all about.

Greetings, adventurer. Having spent so long trapped away unseen, I'll admit to having been somewhat anxious about attending this ceremony. But, not long ago, someone showed me the virtues of everyday courage. Thank you for that.
You're the talk of the realm, cohort! \n\nAs always, I'm exquisitely pleased that we had the opportunity to work together.
That old man we met tells me tales of your exploits. I appreciate you helping us both in Fathoms Drift.
I was concerned, but my son and I are building new memories together. Thank you.

This door leads to the Telvanni Peninsula in eastern Morrowind.\n\nThe wizards of House Telvanni are known for secrecy and intrigue, but a shadow looms over all of them. A shadow filled with emerald eyes. Be cautious, adventurer.

Thank you, stranger. Alavelis sits in the southeast corner of the peninsula. It may look like a sleepy little mining village, but something dangerous is lurking in the shadows. Be careful.\n\nMeanwhile, I'm contemplating a different occupation.
Ah, you found it. Good luck to you both. I wish him well. \n\nAzandar's time here was brief but memorable. He never quite fit in. But then, the Star-Gazers aren't for everyone.
I appreciate you looking into this, stranger. A Temple prelate should know better than to stand in the way of honoring the ancestors.
See if you can talk some sense into that obnoxious prelate. The longer the Necropolis remains closed, the angrier our ancestors are going to be.
Did I hear that correctly? You're going to the Necropolis of Necrom?\n\nWell, make sure you let that rude prelate know that I'm going to report his lack of decency to the Ordinators at the Temple!
I can't believe it. Are you blessed by the Tribunal? To have achieved so much and saved so many ….\n\nI knew you were capable after you helped me at Kemel-Ze, but this is so much more.
My copy's on the shelf right over there. Honestly, when I woke up this morning I had no idea the day would be so amusing! \n\nThanks, stranger. What a day.
Oh gods! A murder! Right outside the assembly! This doesn't bode well. Maybe it's time I find an exit. My family needs the gold, but it's not worth my life.
I'm afraid none of that makes much sense to me. \n\nAll I can tell you is that Leramil was rather impatient. You better head to Tel Rendys and see what she wants.

My precious little prism wanted to come today and give their regards, but I thought it best to hide them away from prying eyes.\n\nDon't you worry. They have plenty of tea to keep them warm. Do consider visiting, yes? We'd adore the company.

Dreynis wasn't quite what I'd imagined. He didn't even seem the slightest bit bothered by the veritable Daedric war going on behind him. Regardless, we're here for research, not feuding Daedra. The sooner we find it, the better.
Rubbing elbows with the elite of the Telvanni Peninsula? Don't get too important or I might wind up receiving a writ with your name on it one day.

So, hero, I take it you've been up to your old tricks? I'm not sure how much of what I heard I actually believe, but if the danger was as great as they indicated, I'm glad you were on hand to stop it.\n\nJust don't let the attention go to your head.

Nathyn was surprised to hear you were the hero of the peninsula, but I wasn't!\n\nIt's wonderful to see you again, even if we can't be there in person. Projecting in was Sathile's idea, believe it or not!

My mother used her magic to make sure Dacia and I could be here in person. Or as good as.\n\nI can't believe Dacia enlisted the help of such a hero to try to save me. She must really love me! I don't know how I got so lucky.

Happy to see your favorite Watchling in one piece? Not a single frayed tentacle, thanks to you. I don't know how you mortals do it. Gallivanting about all weak and fleshy and susceptible to death. But that makes what you did all the more impressive.

Meddler! Seems you're a natural at getting involved in the affairs that move and shape the planes. I won't bore you with how much celestial energy it's taking to be here right now, but ….\n\nJust know that I'm impressed.

Fancy seeing you here, friend. Should have known you'd poke your nose in more than just my brother's study. You should consider becoming a Gleaner. We're always looking for inquisitive minds and curious gossips. I can even put in a good word.

It's good to see you again, friend. Especially now that I can greet you with more than inky tentacles and tattered pages. You showed my sister and I a kindness that we don't often see in Apocrypha. I hope the rest of your time here has been fruitful.

I'm glad I made it! Would you believe my superiors thought attending this celebration was frivolous? I wouldn't dare miss a chance to thank the savior of Anchre Egg Mine again. \n\nThe Consortium may underestimate the good you did, but I surely won't.

Seems your helpful reach went far beyond my egg mine. Can't say I'm surprised. Malsa and Barluk would've been here to congratulate you, but they're busy getting things ready for reopening. So I hope thanks from an old and grateful overseer will do.
You are one of the most impressive mortals I've ever met. Well done earning a place in the chronicle of fate.
Although the Remnants fell, we take comfort knowing that warriors such as you still roam our plane. You have our gratitude.

This one could not leave these lands without giving thanks to a true friend of the Baandari!\n\nThis one's caravan sends warm tidings as well. We did not know your heroics extended to others on the peninsula as well.

May the blessings of Saint Vorys be upon you! I was hoping you'd say hello. \n\nThe shrine has had an influx of visitors, just as I thought it would. When I heard you would be attending the reopening celebration, I had to come and show my appreciation.

Congratulations! I guess it turns out you were right to be suspicious about the Stormwing. I've heard stories about murder, illness, and cultists infiltrating the catacombs.\n\nA good thing you were there to handle things!

When you came to Ald Isra to ask me about Master Shelreni, I thought I was sending you to your death. Not from malice, mind you! I simply doubted she could be beaten by a wandering adventurer.\n\nI'm pleased to see that I was wrong.
It's good to see you again! I had no idea that what you did in Quires Wind was only one of many labors in Apocrypha. I'm honored to be a part of your story.

Thank you again for returning the Numinous Grimoire to Cipher's Midden and foiling Akacirn's horrible ambitions. Your inscription into the Great Eye's chronicle is well-deserved. Congratulations, traveler.
Thank the ancestors that you decided to help my daughters free me. While I'm still trying to regain my strength, it's comforting to know that you are helping gather the lost pages.

Your aid was invaluable, but of course the tide continues to churn. It's paramount that these pages stay within our family. The secrets they contain could elevate us beyond my father's wildest dreams.
Good to hear you again, traveler. I shudder to think what would've happened had you not come across us and my father's antics, but I find myself with a renewed sense of purpose.

First, you must acquire the Emerald Glyphic. It resides in a vault you can access from three locations. I shall open a portal to each and let fate guide your path.\n\nOnce there, this book will reveal the vault. And this talisman will return you to me.
You'll find Quires Wind on the southern margin of Apocrypha. The part we know about, anyway. Many of us who serve the Great Eye aspire to someday work in those dark and silent halls.

Scruut can tell you all about the process for inscribing her records in the Chronicle of Apocrypha. You should talk with her. She awaits you in my study in Cipher's Midden.\n\nI shall meet you there. I need to discuss our return to Necrom with Gadayn.
Do not delay! There is a large celebration and Curate Gadayn is waiting for you. Take the door to the east.
Well, this is a fine brouhaha, isn't it?
When the Great Eye sent me back to Nirn, I expected to find you splashing around in the waters of fate again.\n\nStill, I hear you finally did it and saved reality. Good job, mortal.

By the ancestors, it's good to see you, friend! Leramil told me of your exploits. Well, most of them. I have a difficult time fathoming all the details. But Leramil's been helping me acclimate my mind to the nigh unknowable. Or something like that.
The Watchling summoned us to witness a new entry get inscribed in the Chronicle of Apocrypha. It must be the record of a truly significant event to demand such an audience!

This is taking forever! Do you think they'll put out some real food soon? Canapes and wine will only keep me going for so long. \n\nWe always have a full banquet when the Assembly of Masters meets. I assumed the conclave would be more … opulent.
I can't imagine what they're discussing in there. We all knew Master Shelreni couldn't be trusted. Better to strip her of her rank and cast her out before she can do any real damage.
Have a drink and relax. I expect the masters to remain locked in discussion for some time.
Did you see Vabdru out there? Pathetic creature. No doubt hoping to save face in light of his master's transgressions. Even if he wasn't involved, he should have chosen a better master.
Dreams and fate and secrets capable of destroying reality? What have you and Shelreni Baro gotten me into? Well, unless you toss away my soul gem, I've got no choice but to go with you.\n\nLucky me.
This is an outrage! I deserve to be in there, at my master's side, listening to the debate and watching them tear Shelreni Baro apart. I'm much too important to be left out here with this rabble.
Only Telvanni masters may proceed into the assembly hall. Until the conclave concludes its business, you're welcome to wait out here.
All the masters are accounted for. And Magister Gothren arrived from Sadrith Mora to personally oversee the conclave. I expect they'll get started inside shortly.

I understand that you may feel sympathetic to the twins, but I assure you…. Playing both sides only delays the inevitable. The heartache. The anger. Two immutable forces destined to collide.\n\nOf course, if that's the goal, I applaud you.

Go on. I'll meet you in Cipher's Midden with Leramil and Curate Gadayn. I'd open a portal for both of us, but the local mortals turn ugly when my kind does that sort of thing in a public space.\n\nWell, they turn uglier, but that's just my opinion.

You know, I almost didn't show up. Seeing you again brought back so many memories. The idea of returning to Balmora and avoiding this talk certainly crossed my mind.\n\nI can't keep running from this though. We need to talk about Veya.
Wait, you're not made of ink. Hmm, you're a mortal. Master Malkhest sent Filer Pix to find one. \n\nIs that you? Did I get it right? Are you a mortal who's here to help?
You made it to the Infinite Archive safely, right? I hope Filer Myx pointed you to Master Malkhest. Myx is a good filer, but a bit forgetful sometimes.
I'll be placing my full translation of Fynboar the Resurrected by the Index for the filers to find. Look there if you want to read it.
[Stares intently.]

I wonder what's to become of this dowry. I could save it for my next bride. Or perhaps I could invest it in some sort of capital venture. Father rarely loosens the purse strings for my ideas, so this is the perfect time to prove myself.
Tribune Alea Idolus, at your service.
I'm sure part of me will miss the comforts of Skingrad, but it will be a long while before I return. There's so much of the world to see. Why stay trapped by the familiar?
I am Nantharion, king in the Dawnwood.
If Ruri was in trouble and needed gold, he should have just asked me. Now all he gets is a cold dungeon cell in Skingrad for his trouble.
You and Orissa were having a rather tense conversation. Nothing amiss, I hope.

Prince Ithelia, the Forgotten Prince. The Prince that Hermaeus Mora so feared that he imprisoned her and erased her from existence. Now she is free and Torvesard searches for her.\n\nI suspect we will see signs of their activity before too long.

Leramil the Wise awaits you amid the outcasts and exiles of this city. We who are chosen to serve the Golden Eye are often regarded with fear and suspicion in these lands. It is better to avoid attention.
Come, proxy. The portal to Apocrypha awaits us. And once on the other side, use the Skein and see if it can pinpoint Ithelia's true location.\n\nShe and Torvesard have much to answer for.
Can you feel it? Reality itself is splitting at the seams! We need to hurry, mortal!
Mahkkin should not gloat, but Ruri has always treated this one rudely. And besides, he could have gotten all of us killed with his scheming.

Well, it's over. I've got the shards, and I didn't get killed or press-ganged into becoming a necromancer.\n\nI didn't even learn a lesson on procrastinating because everything worked out. Like it always does.

Consider your temporary commission suspended, comrade. Though I'd love to have you permanently assigned to my cohort.\n\nI plan to continue to look into the Recollection and Shardmarshal Vargas. I hear there's a Wood Elf in Skingrad doing the same.

I suppose now all that's left to do is figure out why the Recollection attacked. Was it to steal the Staff of Many Paths? Recruit the Oathsworn? Too many Orcs died to leave this a mystery. \n\nI know someone who might have answers.
Beragon and I will be here if you need us.
Back to Oblivion? Well, in for an acorn, in for an oak. I'm with you, friend!
Your path leads to Do'Krin Monastery, fatewalker. You can find it in the southwest part of Reaper's March.
Heard that you did some excellent work for us recently. I knew we could count on you.
A wandering adventurer? You're exactly what I'm looking for. The West Weald Legion is in sore need of anyone who has the courage, skill, and determination to deal with a dire threat.

I'll make sure the West Weald Legion Command hears about the bravery both you and my fallen soldier displayed here today. We'll reclaim Varen's Watch from the Recollection. It's only a matter of time.

I suppose you're off on another adventure now, friend. Know that I appreciate the assistance you provided. And the companionship. If you ever have need of House Ravenwatch, just send the word. We always have time for our friends.

After our visit to the Reliquary of Stars, the Recollection cleared out. I did come across one interesting clue, however. They're particularly interested in ruins in West Weald.\n\nWhich is ironic, since I live in Skingrad.

What Lord Gallio was doing, his father must be rolling in his grave! Dro'vir has agreed to stay on and work for Lady Valente. Destroy these vile grapes and plant our usual seeds.\n\nCan the vineyard be salvaged? This one hopes so.

I don't understand. My brother can't be dead. He just got the lumber camp up and running. He's supposed to return here at the end of the season to meet with more buyers. \n\nI won't believe it. I don't know you. There isn't even proof!
With the will secured, Lady Weatherleah's family will no doubt want to get to the bottom of her absent fortune. This one will need your help to sniff out the hawk amongst the hens.

The estate and its fortune are left to Betu and me? I've always thought that Lady Weatherleah's generosity was unrivaled, but this …. It's almost too much.\n\nI assure you, I'll see to all of Betu's needs. We're family after all.
Finally, it's Sir Klauser's turn. He's a funny little badger, and mostly likes to roll around in the dirt.
Steady yourself as we approach the imposter Uriel. This ruse may not be his only crime. It's increasingly likely that he killed Edric to keep his secret.

Each tear that splits the realm of Apocrypha is like a cut across my eyes! You and Leramil track down Ithelia. I'll gather the Watchlings and see if we can do anything to slow the inevitable destruction of all existence.

While you and our allies place the relics in the prescribed locations, I shall perform a ritual to help strengthen and enhance the spell provided by the One Who Knows.\n\nI shall also think more about what Ithelia showed me before she departed.
