Stay your blade. Whatever Torvesard was hoping to find here appears to be gone. But he might be willing to explain his purpose if you simply give him the opportunity.
That's Master Bogvir? Not what I expected.\n\nYou should follow your master, and guest.

I suppose I should thank you. Even Fennorian came through for me this time. My husband's foul operation is finished and his coven—is that really what he called it?—will scatter before long.\n\nNow begins the hard work of restoring this vineyard.
Finally, this song and dance is over and we can get to business. Do tell your master I look forward to measuring my coin against his.
I just served my last glass. But have no fear. Once I refill my tray, I'll come around again.
If you do talk to Master Bogvir, I suppose it wouldn't hurt to mention that I agree to his terms. Everything's set aside, as he requested.\n\nNow, if you'll excuse me, I need to tend to the auction.
I do not understand. Where is Prince Ithelia? If she escaped, why did she not contact me?\n\nYou! Is this some new trick of the Lord of Fate?

I suppose Leramil and I won't resume our sightseeing in Vvardenfell any time soon. Don't worry, friend—I understand.\n\nI'll return to Necrom and see if there are any rumors about strange new Daedric Princes.
I am pleased we were able to help you, stranger. Hermaeus Mora does not lightly involve mortal champions in his affairs. Your task must be urgent indeed.\n\nI wish you success in your mission.
I wish you a safe journey, traveler. I know not why you have been chosen by fate, but I count myself fortunate to have met you.

Welcome to the Outcast Inn! We had some difficulties recently, but we're open for business and happy to see you. Come on in and rest for a spell. And do try the Sage's Dream! It's an ethereal experience in a glass!\n\nOh, good to see you again, friend!
I suppose all that remains is for us to wait for reinforcements to arrive. And to pay you for the assistance you rendered to us today.

You won't learn anything from those scheming charlatans, that's for sure. Lost memories? Please. Children can weave better stories than that drivel. I'll say it again stranger, you should leave this place. Nothing but rotten memories.
It will be good to get back to Skingrad. I enjoy the outdoors as much as the next person, but this armor starts to chafe when I've been in the heat for too long.
This investigation is terribly stressful. I need some time alone to think.
Surely you can stop running about and relax. The killer has confessed to his crimes. Too bad we cannot ask him why he did it, but who can understand the mind of a murderer anyway?
Another murder? I fear any one of us is at risk. Better not wander off alone.
There's so much work ahead of Dulzush and me. We're going to have to get some new initiates. That's not going to be easy.\n\nI'd ask you to stay, but I think you've done your part for Mauloch.
Speak with the Prince of Fate, mortal. We do not have much time before my power returns and the madness overtakes me again.

Leftwheal is a long way from returning to its former trading glory, but we'll get there. We may look defeated, but I know these people. This is our home. Once our wounds have healed, we'll strike back with a vengeance.

I know little about Bosmer mystical traditions. If Beragon knows a greenspeaker who can be of use, you should seek them out. Find out what you can about the wildburn seed.\n\nI have my own avenues of investigation to follow.

The communique says we need to keep ringing the proper sequence at set intervals until we receive a response or help arrives.\n\nThat responsibility falls to me now. I'll bar the door once you're gone.
I confess, Daedric incursions and wandering Princes are a little outside my typical experience. Perhaps Leramil can make sense of what's going on around here.

I did not expect to meet the Prince of Paths this soon, proxy. Nor did I expect her to look more or less mortal. I … do not know what I expected.\n\nThere is nothing left to learn in Elenglynn. Let us speak outside, under the open sky.
We meet again. Do you know this place, this shrine? Were you drawn to it, just as I was?

Thank you again for saving us down in the winery.\n\nI thought if I ever got out of that cage, I'd leave and never come back. But Lady Valente offered quite the sum to stay. Maybe things really will be different under new management.
There is nothing more to do in this place, mortal. Use the portal and return to your own realm.
Come join a righteous cause, my friend! The Aldmeri Dominion has room for everyone in its ranks!
I came here to find work, but the locals are so high-handed I'm not sure I'll ever fit in.
You look familiar. Pretty sure I saw you talking to Quen. I keep a low profile, so you might not have noticed me.\n\nRegardless, you're here. I'm here. Listen up and you'll be richer for it.
I'm sure you have questions, stranger. You deserve answers. Ask away.

It's done. The Terror of the Weald is no longer a threat. I hope whatever remains of the gang has sense enough to scatter.\n\nI tried to do right by Sutch, getting rid of my curse. Now the place is a ghost town. And I have no idea what to do next.
There are so many questions still unanswered about the Echonir and about the Blind. \n\nThe invasion was just the start. There is something more going on here. This is delightfully interesting!

The more I hear of this, the less I like it. A forgotten Daedric Prince? No wonder Malacath took an interest in this.\n\nThe last thing anyone needs is another power in Oblivion meddling with our world.

A forgotten Daedric Prince? Surely there is some mistake. I know nothing of any missing Princes, and I can assure you I am in a position to know. Unless I was made to forget, as well?\n\nAn intriguing mystery. Good luck, mortal.
The affairs of Daedric Princes are kind of beyond my jurisdiction as a Legion tribune, but if they threaten West Weald they're going to answer to me.

The myriad filaments of conceivability divulged … let me start again. I had a feeling you would be visiting, friend.\n\nI have been neglecting my usual studies to show Gadayn some of my favorite places in the realm—and it has been glorious!

Tribune Alea and Beragon await your arrival at Beragon's townhouse in Skingrad. \n\nBeragon has been studying those relics you found. He seems to think they can help us defeat the Recollection, but I don't see how. We need more swords, not antiques.

Check the locations the Skein of Secrets revealed, friend. We need to find out what Nantharion's doing out there.\n\nAnd if I'm right about another wildburn, we need to stop him before he can destroy West Weald.
You seem like the brave sort. I for one haven't the stomach for blades and beasts, and right now, Leftwheal has more than its fair share.
Let's get out of here before the Recollection figures out what we've been doing. I'll meet you back at my townhouse in Skingrad.

I thought I was done with mortals, but the Great Eye assigned me to assist and observe Leramil—for the foreseeable future! Do you know how long that is? Hermaeus Mora's sight extends very far indeed!\n\nAt least she doesn't annoy me as much as some.

Good to see you, my friend. The townhouse is quiet now that Torvesard, Vargas, and Nantharion have been dealt with. I thought I'd like it this way, but I miss the company.\n\nWe should go traveling together again soon. I could use the excitement.
We'll meet you at the Wendir ruins, comrade. We'll follow you wherever Ithelia's trail takes us.
Know that you have done everything I asked of you and more, chosen. You far exceeded my considerable expectations.\n\nNow, with reality preserved and set right, we have one last matter to deal with.

Here, I'll mark your map. I met the Wood Elves with the covered cart in the hills east of Leftwheal. If you find more of these corrupted seeds, burn them!\n\nAnd don't worry. I'll destroy the one you gave me after I finish examining it.

We stopped Nantharion and prevented a massive wildburn that would have destroyed the rest of West Weald. But Ithelia and Shardmarshal Vargas got away. Let's go back to my townhouse and figure out where we stand.
Hoperoot lies to the north of Vashabar, just before you enter the devastated region. I'll be there, supervising the establishment of our next settlement.\n\nGood luck to you, adventurer.

I need to tell Count Calantius about Nantharion and the Recollection. We need to make sure the West Weald Legion's ready for Nantharion's next move, whatever it is.\n\nGo on back to Beragon's townhouse, comrade. I'm sure I'll see you soon.

We stopped Nantharion and prevented a massive wildburn that would have destroyed the rest of West Weald. But Ithelia and Shardmarshal Vargas got away. Let's go back to my townhouse and figure out where we stand.

I may never get used to fighting Daedra and magic-users, but at least we put an end to Nantharion and his plot to destroy West Weald. That should finish the Recollection.\n\nNow is it too much to hope that Ithelia will take her power and just go away?
I have a feeling this is the start of a long and dangerous journey. Take care of any business you have here in Skingrad while you can, friend. I'll meet you at Wendir.
Maerenah looks … different. But if you're not with the vampires, does it mean it's safe out there? And did you see my husband, Grivier? He hasn't returned from his last excursion.
Why are you helping Maerenah? She's one of them!\n\nAnd Balandrus, the Terror of the Weald … he told me he returned to Sutch because of her. This is all her fault!

I'm something of an expert in codes and ciphers. Whatever message is hidden in the map we found, I'll figure it out. But I'll need some things back at my townhouse for that.\n\nI'll see you in Skingrad, my friend.
You're going to help us? Good. Make the Recollection pay for this with blood.

Remember, life has no meaning without death. That is why the church of Arkay rejects all forms of necromancy.\n\nWe did good work here, but I am ready to return to my duties. I have always found life more orderly within the church than outside it.
I know Rustwall's grounds like the back of my hand. That map shows right where I hid the key.\n\nI'll stay here and continue to watch, just like Captain Leronus told me to do.

Maybe when you get to Beragon's townhouse in Skingrad, this time you can put in a good word for me with the tribune. Let her know you think I'm hale and hardy and ready to return to real duty.\n\nThe Legion needs my sword!
The Skein of Secrets did not lead us astray. If I am not mistaken, Ithelia and her servant Vargas recently used this portal that you have graciously reopened.\n\nWe must follow them.
It was awful! Like the world ripped open … like a tear!\n\nIt swallowed our cart and poor Lazlus … sucked them right in!

I don't understand magic and I know next to nothing about Daedra, but I do know war. This is war, comrade. And there's no one I'd rather face it with than you, Beragon, and Leramil.\n\nFor whatever good it will do, my sword is yours.
Thank you for all your help. I'll gather what supplies we have and help these people get to Skingrad.

Sure, my lifelong friend joined a violent cult, but you and I actually did some real good today. We saved people in Ostumir and kept this seed away from the Recollection.\n\nWhen you're ready, meet Leramil and me at my townhouse in Skingrad.
I don't want to bother you. I'm looking to get away from the war in Cyrodiil, but don't know where to go.
If I'm not mistaken, that portal is exactly what we need. Let's get out of here while we can!

Activating the mirrors in the proper order awakened the portal. I suspect we will find Ithelia and Vargas somewhere on the other side, at the Loom of the Untraveled Road. How it will restore what was lost, though, remains obscure.\n\nAfter you, proxy.
That didn't take long. Now we've got little Daedra popping in with warnings of impending doom?\n\nI told you we had unfinished business.

The wildburn seed grows deep in the ruins. I suggest we split up. I'll lead the Recollection on a merry chase while you and Beragon find the seed. And don't worry, I'm sure we'll meet up along the way.\n\nAnd, Beragon, remember your history.
Now, assistant! We have found the Emblem of the Last King! It's been waiting so long for me to recover it!
I need to take my leave shortly. Narsis should turn up any time now. Perhaps I should go looking for him. In any event, thank you for your help.

We should not linger here. The destruction of the Loom has created new instabilities along the Many Paths. Until they subside, the area around the Loom is dangerous. I do not wish to be lost again in the Many Paths.\n\nUse the portal I opened, proxy.
What is that thing? It's got so many eyes!\n\nNever mind, it wants to talk to you. Go find out what it means by we're all doomed.

I must contact Hermaeus Mora and inform him that Ithelia has regained at least some of her power.\n\nDo not take this as a slight against you. Helping her saved many lives. It was the correct thing to do.

Finally, the storm abates and I can clearly see the Many Paths. I can discern one reality from the next and my mind is clear.\n\nI am myself again. I am Ithelia, Prince of Paths and Mistress of the Untraveled Road.
Well done! I expect we'll be on our way soon. Marriage troubles aside, I'm quite looking forward to our stay in Skingrad. I hope to make it as relaxing as I can for Master Grander.

So, my master has a plan for the Echonir. With the invasion over, I worried they would be left yearning for more excitement. But it appears as though this matter is only beginning. Not your part though, that is over. You did well mortal.
Well met, sera. We receive so few visitors here at Holamayan.
Ah. You must be the guest Abbot Andor told us to expect. If there is anything you need, you simply have to ask.

Baron Carvain and Lady Raxalee will pay for their crimes. And Ontus will survive, despite all the death and suffering they caused just to make a profit.\n\nI couldn't have done it without you, deputy.
Constable Yabren … they busted in right after she arrived. Mercenaries, by the looks of them. I tried to help, but I'm not the fighter I used to be.\n\nThey … they took Yabren!
I won't face the magistrate's justice alone. Oh no. I'll tell them exactly how Carvain was involved. How he hired the mercenaries, told the alchemist to kill the healer and the constable—everything!
Maybe I can blame all this on Raxalee. No one will accept the word of a lizard over that of a true Colovian.

Let's keep news about Abolisher between us until we're back in Skingrad. I don't want thieves or Recollection agents to get any ideas while I'm traveling.\n\nReturn to Beragon's townhouse as soon as you can. I have a feeling this is far from over.

The Blade, the Lamp, and the Skein countered Ithelia's power in ancient times. I think they can do so again.\n\nYou and Beragon are fated to seek the Skein of Secrets in Niryastare. I have my own tasks and shall find you when it is time to finish this.
I almost caught a big one before this monster came splashing down the coast!
That thing stole my fishing rod! Do you know how many fish I need to sell to buy a new one?

I am called the Master of the Tides of Fate. I perceive everything that may come to pass. Yet I cannot select the outcomes I prefer. Choice and chance determine which possibility actually occurs.\n\nSuch as this one. Ithelia is free.
We still have some Daedra stragglers to round up, but my legionaries can handle them. Feel free to take three or four down on your way out, if you're so inclined.\n\nAnd mercenary … thank you.
Clen, we'd better get a drink. Otherwise the rotmeth will be gone and we'll have to carry our fathers home.
I can't tell you the last time I've seen Laeni smile like that. Thank you, traveler. You've changed our lives.
To think this all started with shouting and a traveler walking in from the wilds. Hah! Just look at what you've done for this village.
Belwelas has always tried to teach us to listen when the Singer tells a tale. \n\nPerhaps this … situation will be good for the village.
I'm going to look at this the way I think our ancestors might have. What seems today like the end of a tale might in fact be the start of a new one.
Some of the Recollection who attacked our camp went into the door in the hillside, just over there. They haven't come out while I've been here.
I can't wait for the wedding. You think the village is going to get rot-faced tonight, just wait until after the ceremony!\n\nHaha. Dawn keep you traveler. Well done.
I can't contain my joy, stranger. Laeni will stay here in Vashabar, a proud and vibrant sapling growing amid the grove of her elders.\n\nThe will of the Singer, sung through you.
Respect and deep thanks, traveler. Laeni and Clendagal shall remain in Vashabar. And it's all because of you. \n\nMay Y'ffre guard and keep you in your journey.
This new act we're working on is going to be quite the doozy! Hopefully you can catch it.
Oh … urgh … hello there. Where are you and who are we?

Behold, this season's Jubilee Cake! Decadent and delicious as only a true Chef Donolon recipe can be! Hopefully I have done my father proud and showcased all the skills he taught me.\n\nIn fact, he inspired my version of his ultimate creation.

It's not going to be fun waiting around for word from the Garland Ring. I'm liable to get a rash. Of course, best way to deal with nerves is to keep busy, right? Might be nice to find something to punch.
I feel like there's something I've forgotten. Something important …. Well, it'll come back to me. How can I help you?
Calvo is up in the bell tower? Ringing the bell? He's just trying to look good in front of the captain. I could have gone up there and done that—if I hadn't gotten injured, that is.
Calvo is really up there? Ringing that bell all on his own? Hard to believe. Maybe he really is the best of us.
I hope Calvo survives long enough for Legion reinforcements to arrive. Either way, he's a real hero. I'll make sure to head to Ontus and tell his family what he did for us.
Save me the chastising. I'm sure a fellow necromancer like yourself knows we all have to start somewhere.
The future can change. Tiny things change the future. My wisps see these things and predict what is to come. Perhaps your fortune will be different next time we meet.
You've made it possible for us to rebuild, I thank you for that. I won't forget your heroism.
I hope we're able to gather what's left of our belongings. There are treasured memories buried in the rubble.
The baroness blames herself? She's been good to us, regardless of what happened today. I still trust her.
I'm not sure Leftwheal can come back from this. Perhaps it's time to move on.
We must meditate, walker. It is necessary for the ritual.

To put spirits on the path to redemption. To hold the door even when the shadow of unending night pushes against it. This is my calling.\n\nI have found sure footing in this time, thanks to your guidance. Your company. I would like that to continue.
I am full to the brim with ideas! I am going to be pondering these concepts all the way back to Evermore.
Hello again, friend! Good of you to chat with us. Have you come to speak to us about the Molag Bal Paradox again?
You seek the holy moon-sugar water for purification? These jars have been blessed. Fill your cup as needed, walker.

I briefly imagined you would join our ranks. I even started a design on your armor. Alas, it was not meant to be. Perhaps our paths will cross again.\n\nUntil then, enjoy your adventures with Tanlorin. The Gardener and I will see to the rest.

Comrade! Don't suppose you decided to enlist? The Legion could use you! No? I understand. Still, I'm glad you decided to stop by.\n\nYou're lucky you caught me. As usual, the count has me running hither and yon. Sometimes I barely have time to eat.

We were just talking about you friend! I'm glad you could make time to visit. And I'm glad I was here to see you! Leramil's been showing me around Apocrypha, but I need to return to my duties at the Necropolis soon.\n\nWell, soon-ish.
Another worker out sick, and right after one of my best died in his sleep. You look strong. Interested in making some coin in the quarry, stranger?

Despite rumors to the contrary, Carvain Ranch only hires qualified applicants. Seasoned ranch hands only. We have no time or inclination to train novices. And we especially have no need of … rowdies.\n\nPerhaps you should inquire at the quarry, hmm?
Careful. I saw what the Recollection can do with those barrels. You don't want to be near one when they explode.
It seems my reflection is gaining in power. How shameful to watch at the moment of my failure.\n\nLeave me, pathwalker. Let me fall the way I want to.

You're just another thorn in my side, to be plucked and tossed away. And to think I wrote you off as one of Tan's many flights of fancy. My dear Tanlorin is prone to them, after all.\n\nAnd now they hate me. I suppose I have you to thank for that.
A Daedra, here? Did it say doom? Didn't you just avert one of those?\n\nWell, it clearly is trying to get your attention, waving around its many eye stalks and tentacles. Go see what it wants.
That's a Daedra? Are we under attack? No, no, it definitely spoke to you. It brings a warning, I think.\n\nPlease, go find out what doom I need to worry about next, hero.

Amazing how far we've come since that day I first flagged you down.\n\nI'd like to think I played an integral part to all of this! Being loud enough to catch your attention certainly has its benefits.
I'm a touch nervous to bring this to the Votary Commander and Archmage Galerion. This is … well, this is going to come as quite a surprise. And those two hate surprises. \n\nI'll be fine. Probably.

I can't believe the greenspeaker selected us to join her in Skingrad! I guess it's because you helped us with our betrothal. Thanks again for that, by the way.\n\nStill not sure about a Wood Elf living in a structure that wasn't grown, though.

I still can't believe Nantharion led a rutting Ayleid cult. Consorted with Daedra! Thanks to you, Greenspeaker Darolith will secure Vashabar's future.\n\nSinger hear my prayer, I think that future's going to be bright.

I find it just sweltering, being in the city, don't you? But, I suppose I can weather a little discomfort if it means getting the chance to express my gratitude properly. \n\nAnd it seems there are many others who feel the same!

With Donolon gone, this is our chance to put that pretentious baker and his fancy cakes in their place! When his apprentice fails to present the Jubilee Cake, we'll swoop in and show them how traditional pastry chefs make desserts!
To think Donolon left that kitten to watch over his business. Well, when his apprentice fails to produce a Jubilee Cake for this season, Donolon will be ruined for sure!

Flee while you can, mortal. Save your own life. Just spare a thought for this doomed path if you survive. I suspect we will not last much longer.\n\nI suggest you take the lute berries and run. Good luck.
You're the one Nahlia's been waiting for? You're not what I expected. But perhaps that's just what she needs.
Talk to Maer. Let her know I don't blame her. Tell her … I'm all right.

I hope you don't mind, but we crashed your party. A friendly legionary mentioned it to me and offered to help get Narsis here. Said his name was Caepio, I think. Nice fellow. He really liked my hair.\n\nAs you can see, poor Narsis is still petrified.

Tribune Alea did well when she brought you to help us at Feldagard. All of the Weald is in your debt, mercenary. If not for you, who knows what this Recollection and Daedra business would have led to.\n\nStill, it seems I'm forgetting something ….

Have you ever had a thought suddenly slip away? It's frustrating. Like trying to grasp an eel with an oven mitt.\n\nAnyway, I'm glad I was able to attend this quaint gathering and show Skingrad's appreciation for all you've done.

Now that the celebration is done, I hope Count Calantius and I can resolve any remaining points of contention in our negotiations. Vashabar truly desires peace with Skingrad and the Weald.\n\nThere was something else I meant to ask, but it escapes me.

Deputy. Good to see you. I'm surprised you didn't ask for a larger salary, considering what I now know of your reputation.\n\nI'm glad to see you were able to help all of West Weald, not just solve my problems in Ontus.

Hello, walker. One does not need to be as perceptive as Mizzik Thunderboots to see all the good you have done for West Weald. And such an impressive list of guests!\n\nMizzik hopes to someday be worthy of a gala such as this.

An excellent celebration, my friend! I knew you were amazing after witnessing your exploits at the vineyard, but saving the entire West Weald? Extraordinary!\n\nThere was something else I meant to ask you, but I lost the thought. Ah, well.

The Wood Elf had some nice things to say about you. I even heard the count sing your praises! Someday you must tell me the story of what you did besides end the Terror.\n\nAnyway, I'm not the sort to say this lightly. I'm proud to call you my friend.

I've thrown a wild bit of merry making a time or two at my place in Sutch, but nothing like this! The count of Skingrad is here, for Ruptga's sake!\n\nI can't believe with everything else you accomplished, you had time to help me.
You have what you need, friend. Please be moving along. Best not bring attention to Chirrabi by hanging around.
What am I forgetting? It's right there, but just out of reach! It's so frustrating!\n\nAnd I wasn't invited to the celebration! I never get to go to anything interesting.

I wish I got to attend the celebration. I'd really like to thank the hero of West Weald for all they did. Oh, I'm sure Tribune Alea helped, too. She's very capable.\n\nAnd they held it in a Wood Elf's townhouse! I wonder what was wrong with the palace?

I am going to be able to return to my research with a new perspective on Goblins. Although I might keep my notes to myself for a bit. \n\nMaybe I can stop the next Jerntann by delaying my publications.
This has been a most interesting day, interloper. Almost worth all the stress and lost feathers.

So the Recollection has been defeated and Dawnwood is safe? All of West Weald, I suppose. And Greenspeaker Darolith and Count Calantius are talking. I guess that's good.\n\nStill, maybe it's time for me to return to Valenwood.
So Nantharion was evil and the leader of the Recollection? He fooled us all so well!\n\nAt least Count Calantius is willing to meet with Greenspeaker Darolith. That's a good thing, right?
With negotiations underway with Skingrad, we should also turn our attention to things here in Vashabar. We still need to find a way to reconcile the differences between the Green Pact and the Dawnway

Thank you for not letting Legionary Thania's death be in vain. I feel my strength slowly return every time I look at the fires. \n\nAs soon as help arrives, we'll strike back! Varen's Watch will be ours again in no time.

Any chance I could get you to cast a few investigation spells while you're in there, maybe learn something about this place? \n\nNever mind. Nahlia's giving me a look. Just do what she says and watch her back, got it?
I watched over this dormant library for centuries. Now it's filled with life and joy. I know she would be thrilled by this.\n\nPinfeathers. What do you do once you've outlived your destiny?

The news out of Skingrad is frightening and inspiring in equal measure. The violent cultists and their Daedric allies attempted to conquer this land, but they were defeated. And now the count seeks peace with the Wood Elf town.\n\nInteresting times.

Are the roads safe to travel again? We heard that the Recollection cult has been defeated. Even the Daedra that were rampaging through the wilderness are in retreat. Whoever is responsible for these miracles, we owe them a debt we can never repay.
If you are seeing this, the Crow has set you on the path to learn the art of Scribing. A world of magic awaits you.

The Garland Ring is no more, but it will live on in spirit. I spent years developing connections and resources. Far too much work to give up after one assassination plot.\n\nThe Ring will change, like the seasons. A cycle of renewal.

I see Bogcup remembered their lessons. Found my note, did you?\n\nListen, Hyacinth is the traitor. He must be. When I arrived, he was in the company of Ceythalmor. I hit them with every spell I had, but I barely managed to wound a few and slip away.
This place resonates with the memory of Ulfsild, adventurer. Consider well the power, the trust, she has placed in you.

I'm grateful to you and Tribune Alea. Those Recollection soldiers would've found me eventually. Only so many places to hide down there.\n\nYou're quite impressive for not being part of the Legion. I think I could learn a thing or two from you.
I need to protect my farm. My family! My niece, Bella, went out on her own, and now she's missing. If hiring those hunters will save her life, then I'm going to do it. \n\nEven if Pim hates me.

I really think Nahlia's discovered her calling here in the Scholarium. Worry not, I'll back her up when she talks to the Votary Commander. \n\nThank you for your role in all of this. It's been a singular opportunity, adventurer.

I'm not easily impressed, adventurer. But you've lived up to expectations. Now that all the wings are open I'm just itching for a chance to try Scribing myself.\n\nMaybe write a paper or two. Who knows? The future looks bright, if dusty.

Telling the Votary Commander that a magical being promoted me to steward of the Scholarium might be the strangest conversation I've ever had.\n\nBut! It went well. We're going to share this place with the world. Just like Ulfsild intended.

I think it's good the Gardener disbanded the group. After I saw several people die at the Bone Tree, I can't say that I didn't think about just heading out and away right then. \n\nGlad I stuck around to learn that our work was not lost, nor in vain.
Ugh maybe, oh gods, this hurts. Maybe you're right. You give me the poultice and I'll tell you what I know. It won't help you, anyway.
Why does my Prince allow this mortal to speak with her? Hermaeus Mora and the other betrayers approach. We have no time to waste with mortal nonsense.
Haldain bought us enough time to run away from that awful creature.\n\nI twisted my ankle on a root, but I think I'll be able to walk on it soon.
I'm a bit busy here. \n\nHaldain asked us to leave, but I won't desert anyone else still in the lumber camp.
I'm surprised that hunter can walk bearing the weight of his own self-importance. \n\nPromise me that you'll stop him.
We're so close to getting out of here, but I'm not sure we're going to make it.\n\nI don't think we're the last ones left alive, though. Oh gods! I hope we're not the last ones.
Don't go in there unless you can fight. I thought I was handy with a blade, but I took a claw to the leg. Now I can't even limp out of here.\n\nI knew something like this was going to happen.

It feels like we're close. Whatever Ulfsild hid here will hopefully give you the answers we need.\n\nStay safe and keep an eye out for focal points. If the orcs haven't found it yet, it's likely because it's hidden behind her magics.
Be on your guard down there, mercenary. In addition to the Recollection forces, there were Daedra with Nantharion—as well as a strange woman wearing a hooded cloak!
I believe each of us has been hurting in our own way for years now. But coming back together, even in these circumstances … it's helped us. Well, least it helped me.

I used to believe the Eight had a hand in everything that's happened since that fateful day at Caelum Vineyard. Like it was our punishment for all we had done. Maybe it was, but we all have a choice.\n\nAnd I believe mine is now clear.

Thank you again for saving Val. And for putting up with my antics throughout all of this. The Scarlets are the closest thing to a family I've ever known.\n\nBut maybe it's time to swim in the swamp for a bit.

You know, Marcien's the reason I came here in the first place. They always told me how beautiful the land was. They were right, of course, but I can't help hoping Marcien might stick a little closer to town for a while.\n\nThank you, traveler.

I don't know how to thank you. Not just for saving my life, but for bringing us together to face this. I've spent years trying to run away from who I used to be. But I really needed to turn around and face my past honestly.
It appears that our adventure is at an end. I will admit, it did not go exactly as planned. But all true adventures include some deep bruises and frantic screaming, right? \n\nI am right, aren't I?
It is done, thank Hermorah. This one is relieved to know that the null arca works. All that's left to do is break camp and travel back to the city.\n\nKeshargo is going to miss this sky.

The null arca worked beautifully. Now that this experiment is over, I can market it all over Fargrave. Any pesky artifacts or relics with unwanted effects will no longer be an issue—for an exorbitant price, of course.

You're alive? That's fantastic! It must be over now. I hope Keshargo's not too upset with me for leaving. I abandoned him in the middle of an attack. Even if I beg for forgiveness …. \n\nNo, I was a coward before, I won't be one again.
I'd go with you to find my father, but he specifically told me to stay with my mother. Protect her, you understand? Good luck out there.
No matter how many times you lose a squadron, it never gets any easier. \n\nNo need to stick around, mercenary. I'll be ready to head out myself in another few moments.
I thought I could lead them. Save them. But by the time the fighting was done, I was the only one left standing. \n\nI'll never forget this feeling.
For years, I've devoted myself to the keeping of sacred texts. To think those texts would live on through the actions of our children. Hmm.
If you're hearing this, it means you've found my false book. Cleverly done! And I'm glad to see you're putting the True-Sight Lens to good use. Even if I'm not literally there to see it.
Beragon awaits your timely arrival at his townhouse in Skingrad. Good hunting, mercenary.
To live and die and never see a Twilight Cantor is a blessing. To see one, you should give thanks. To see more than one, you should start to pray.
Keep away from the western side of town. There's a Twilight Cantor yowling with all of Boethra's fury. This one would not wish to stray into her path.

More questions? Those Inquisitors already treated me like a criminal. I will tell you what I told them so I can get back to my nap.\n\nThe cantor moved on. I do not know why. There was never a need for an exorcism here, at least as far as I know.

What a marvel all these trees are! This one's neck aches from gazing up at them. And so tempting to climb. \n\nBut the risk of falling all that way is enough to keep this Khajiit on the ground, ha, ha, ha.
By the Silvenar, <<1>> is quite the handsome human. I could listen to him speak for hours.

That song. That twisting, bending song! The cantor suspected it was a trap and he was right.\n\nMy soul would have bent, too, were it not for the mercy of their blades. What is this? Have you drawn me back to torment me? To do your bidding?
Listening to <<1>> has been enlightening! I had no idea the Reachfolk were such accomplished healers.

Is there something in the wine? The crowd suddenly seems confused, and I hear whispers that indicate many of them believe they just forgot something important.\n\nNo matter. I remember everything! Now, be a dear and introduce me to Count Calantius.

Thanks again for helping me with that problem. If not for you … wait, what happened again? Oh, right, the shadows … and … was there someone else there?\n\nAnyway, you can always drink for free at the Outcast Inn! Or, at least at a deep discount.

Nice party. I didn't know you were so famous.\n\nI was hoping to find a compassionate yet influential patron here to fund my research, but no luck so far. Don't worry, I won't try to wrangle funds from you. I'm much too indebted to you for that.

Ever have one of those moments when you're suddenly sure you forgot something important? Like did I leave the fire burning in the barrack's hearth again? Or where did I put my sword?\n\nProbably nothing. Just one of those feelings, I guess.

We suspected our uncle had a role to play in all this. Very clever, that one. This Garland Ring is a solution we never would have conjured, even in our wildest imaginings.\n\nHmm. One supposes there may be further use for such a group.
The Netch acts in good faith. Some have found its attitude … irksome, but I believe its intentions are pure.\n\nI hope more come to walk these halls with the passion of the Netch.
I never fully understood Ulfsild's mind, you know. She was brilliant, beyond even me. \n\nBut her legacy is no riddle to me. Scribing is a universe all its own. And now it is yours.
Tha—tha—thank you, traveler. I—I can't thank you enough for getting us out of there!
Florian here seems to be suffering the worst from our ordeal. I think all of us will need time to fully recover.\n\nThank you, stranger. You and your friend really came through for us.
Sariyaah and I have been friends for years. It took a lot to convince her to leave Craglorn, so I'll do anything to make her happy here.\n\nI just hope she has enough pets for the time being.
And so another Luminary has blessed the altar. The Scholarium remembers its ancient shape, and wants to return to days of old.\n\nUlfsild would be proud to see her dream breathing new life.
We did it! The Netch, who would have thought?
Look where you are, Not-Ulfsild. At everything you've done. \n\nThere is no moment more buoyant than the culmination of a person's legacy.
Thank you.\n\nNow I'm going to spend the remaining time with my father catching him up on everything.
Thank you again, stranger.\n\nI hope I look all right. I didn't anticipate meeting my father-in-law today.
You are not the same lighthearted presence I met in the darkness, but I feel comforted all the same.

I see you are still at the beck and call of the lying Prince of Fate. I do not seek to be your enemy, mortal. Before we irreversibly cross a threshold from which there is no return, I would reach an understanding between us.
You're brave, adventurer. I wouldn't provoke the Princes unless I had no other choice. \n\nBut this is the Gryphon's task, not mine. In my own way, I'm used to disagreeing with him.

I wonder how long it took Ulfsild and the Gryphon to design these animated armors. We've got constructs aplenty, somewhat like these? \n\nBut I've never seen anything quite like them. I can't wait for our best adepts to study them.

The ally of Skingrad and the hero of West Weald! So good to see you again, adventurer! Well, unless of course, you're here to tell us about another disaster, invasion, or catastrophe.\n\nIf that's the case, please talk to Tribune Alea.
Head to Count Calantius's office in Skingrad. It's close to the chapel.

I must preserve my voice for when my song is needed. But I am prepared for this, walker. Talbira and I are ready to sing.\n\nLead us to Ravith-morna and we will help Zerith-var fulfill the purpose that Azurah has given him.
Come to bathe in Pa'alat's cool waters, too, stranger? Give me a moment to finish my ablution. I was told it was imperative that I do so quickly.
Hey, five-claw! Spare some gold for a humble Khajiit trying to get out Pa'alat?
Ehh. If you're here about the altercation, I did not see a thing.

This one stands with her former sahida. Her equal, if not her better for having learned the song of this Moon-Singer Talbira.\n\nWhich means Viti will stand at your side as well, friend of Zerith-var. This one's voice is yours.

I can already feel the pull on Eyevea. Nothing we can do now will outpace the greed of a Daedric Prince.\n\nI know that this situation is hard to accept, but I wish the Gryphon and the Fox would understand. This isn't a fight we can win.

I suppose I ought to thank you. Count yourself lucky, darling. I've never let anyone see as much of myself as you have.\n\nI don't know what's coming next, but at least I know I'll be facing it whole. You have my gratitude.
The flowers by the river's edge are so pretty. Maybe my tears could help water them. Oh, but they're so far away.
The Gryphon and Nahlia are so much alike! It's like the Gryphon's a knight. Or Nahlia is a gryphon. \n\nWait. Is Nahlia a gryphon?
They came out of nowhere… Hyacinth arrived, then… find Azalea… the flowers…
The drinks here are good, but the people are better. And you're especially to my liking.
The Archmage was a companion of justice. A gentle supporter of the Fox. I cannot express how deep runs my well of respect for this woman.
What do you want with me? Are you just going to drag me back to her?
Hmph. These Wood Elves think they're so perfect, with their pretty little lives in their pretty little forest. None of them deserve it.
Don't worry, you're hardly the first patron to pass out drunk in my tavern. West Weald Wallop hits harder than a guar in heat.

You'll find Beragon on the road outside Ostumir, just to the north of the village. He built a small camp for the survivors. Tell him I sent you.\n\nAnd any aid you can give will be appreciated, traveler. It's rare to find much kindness in this world.

I don't really understand what just happened. Your friend is stranger than a tree with no roots.\n\nYou're free to go, but I'd suggest you both keep a low profile. Elelorn's patience can only be stretched so far.
I still don't trust your friend. She seems sincere now, but I'll wait to see what my wife has to say about it.

With your quest done it's time for me to check in with the Guild. It'll take some time to get everything organized. \n\nDon't worry, I'll update you on my progress when I can. Just wish me luck with the Votary Commander!
This is a test of the interaction camera system.
You have given your vow of mystery.
You have given your vow of charity.
You have given your vow of loyalty.
Don't worry, inheritor. I'll continue to guide Nahlia through the many challenges the Scholarium may present. \n\nIf nothing else, who will help her keep the Netch in line?

I've had my share of strange adventures, but helping you battle Daedra and save all of existence? That's beyond even the stories my little sister Eveli enjoys so much. But I guess this story isn't over just yet!\n\nI'll see you back at my townhouse.
Crossing paths with you outside Moonmont, it seems like a lifetime ago. So much of my world has been changed since we first met. And I am thankful for it every day.
Hah, all this time, the Crow was Ulfsild! Kind of. Sort of. Amazing!\n\nKeep talking to her, we're so close to the end.
I believe in you! I'll see you when you make it back to the Scholarium! Yeah!

There's so much to do, I can't find anything concrete on why the lumber camp was attacked. But I'll find it. I just need to talk to more people and call in more favors. I will figure out why my brother was killed. \n\nI owe him that much.

I'm certain history won't carry on my name. I never sought recognition. I created Scribing to understand magic better. To understand myself better. \n\nBut, of course, my journey did not end when I left the Scholarium.
Seems I underestimated your aid, traveler. Thank you for saving the lives you could.
We owe you a great debt. Should we meet again in safer times, I'll treat you to a frosty one.
You've done us a great service, stranger. If you don't mind my saying, I feel that we're cut from the same cloth. Putting others before ourselves. A wonderful, if tiring, quality. Take care.
I wish I could muster the courage to go back in, fight the raging fires and monstrous beasts myself.
You're the one I saw in Fyrelight Cave. Why do you involve yourself with scum like the Scarlets? Surely you must know what they did. What they took from me!
Are … are you here for my grandmother? You should speak to her before Father throws a fit and makes us move again. He doesn't like it when people come looking for her.
You're here for my mother, I take it? Deal with your business quickly, and keep me and my daughter out of it.

I still can't believe I'm back. I thought I'd be trapped as a pig forever!\n\nAt least your friend made good on her promise, but I'm not sure what to think of her. I don't know if I'll ever be able to eat pork again after this.
I should have been in there with her … stubborn soldier. But brave. \n\nAnyway, you've done more than your share. The Legion will take it from here.
The Recollection will not be deterred. This land is ours by right and by blood. It will be ours, mark my word.

Look for Tribune Alea inside the walls of the estate, in the courtyard.\n\nKnow that the tribune can be somewhat demanding, but she's a fine officer. And I'm sure she'll pay you for any aid you provide. The Legion hires mercenaries all the time.
Mortal! There's precious little time. The fabric of reality continues to shred and tear due to Ithelia's very presence!\n\nLeramil sent me to bring you back at once.
I made this lens so you might see the world as I do. The very warp and weft of magic laid out before me.
Pirsisa saw you complete our task. She must thank you on behalf of all her fallen friends. They'd be happier knowing this expedition wasn't in vain.

I overheard Keshargo talking to you. You brought the knot out of the citadel. That's the best news I've gotten all day. \n\nI was supposed to be the one to run the knot out of there. Thanks for doing what I couldn't.
Xoryn's dead? Good. That saves me a lot of work learning how to fight so I can get revenge.
I heard that you finished what we started. That's a relief.
I saw you put the knot into the null arca.\n\nGuess that means I can stop sharpening this axe soon.
Did we win? I think we won. But what happened to Ithelia? She … changed again, didn't she?\n\nAs fascinating as all this is, I'm ready to see trees and grass and skies of blue again. Let's go home.

Well done, comrade. I don't know about you, but I'm done with broken mirrors and Daedric monsters and old ruins. A flagon of Colovian red to wash the dust of this place from my throat. That's what I need now.

We should not linger here. The destruction of the Loom has created new instabilities along the Many Paths. Until they subside, the area around the Loom is dangerous. I do not wish to be lost again in the Many Paths.\n\nUse the portal I opened, proxy.
Only those authorized by the Guild have access to this portal.\n\nVotary Nahlia said you're good to come and go as you please.
And all this time … book that would … location … meditate on.\n\n… I just need a little more time.
Can't tell you how many times I've wanted to give Ruri a good telling off. Never did like the fellow.

Congratulations. You've accomplished incredible things. Through you, my work finally lives on. Gather any allies you choose.\n\nWe will see if the Crow deems you worthy. If you are the inheritor of the Scholarium. See you on the other side.

This door leads to West Weald in southwestern Cyrodiil.\n\nAn area of wealth and prosperity, West Weald faces increasing tension. Between a fringe Wood Elf cult and the native Colovians, a cataclysmic confrontation approaches. Will you investigate?
Aw, the people are gone. I just had a good conversation with one. She didn't say much, but that's fine.\n\nBring them back!

The strange people are gone. I suspect the sky outside is back to normal now, too. That lady by the fire vanished into thin air, so that's good. Everything is the way it should be again.\n\nBut you're still talking to me.
Oh, thank you so much. My hands cramped from all the strumming. Now the weird things are gone and I can take a break.\n\nMaybe I can charge Brynmir for all that music.

Well, all the weird stuff is gone. I guess this means customers will come back. So it'll get noisy again.\n\nI suppose I could put wax in my ears. I certainly don't want to find someplace else to work.
Time to get back to work. Can't blame my lack of progress on feeling scared any more.\n\nThanks for clearing that up. I guess.
You heard the baron. We've got nothing to hide.
I'm pretty sure I heard Lady Raxalee ask you to please leave.
When this is all over, you must remind me how you convinced me to get involved in a war between the Daedra.
If I survive to tell her this story, my little sister will never believe it.
The threads of fate continue to unravel. Ithelia might be compliant for the moment, but the situation is still untenable. We must see what accord she and the Great Eye can reach.
The smell of burning oil from the barricade makes me feel safe. Odd, huh?\n\nGo chase down those Daedra with Tribune Alea. We're all set here.

We'll get started on repairing the breach right away. It'll be some time before we have a main gate again, but we can build stronger barricades in the meantime.\n\nThank you for saving me. I appreciate your efforts, mercenary.

When Commander Merian looks relaxed, then you know we're safe. He seems quite pleased with you. That's rare, especially since you're a mercenary.\n\nI owe you a debt of gratitude for saving me with that ballista. I hope I can return the favor one day.
Looks like you and that Wood Elf saved more of the people trapped in Ostumir. We can't thank you enough.
When my sister came up that hill, I cried. She said a Wood Elf helped her, but not Beragon. We should've been better neighbors to Valenwood. Maybe then none of this would have happened.
If you find Lirinisse, tell her I'm sorry. The last time we spoke, we argued about some research I'm doing. \n\nIt seems so meaningless now with everything that's happened.
Go on, comrade. You'll find Beragon on the balcony off the upper level. He told me to send you up there the moment you returned.
We're under strict orders not to let any Daedra through. I promise, not a single horned monster will get past us.
I trust Commander Merian with my life. If he says to stand here and hold back Daedra, that's exactly what I'll do. Let them come.
How many Daedra can there be? They seem endless!\n\nFollow Tribune Alea and hunt them down.
I don't know if you have Legion training, but that was good work with the ballista. It thinned out the Daedra forces exactly as planned.
You did it! That ballista crushed those Daedra. I actually feel a little safer now.
Not sure I agree with the commander's strategy, but we're still alive. I guess that's something.
Well, you set my beautiful barricade on fire, but I guess that's part of the plan. I should start finding wood for the next one.

Let's let Snapdragon get settled in. She hates when people hover, but I am certain the Gardener won't leave her side.\n\nI say we get back on the road. I want to give this traitor business some thought, and they'll reach out when they need us.

Wisteria betrayed us and for what? A Ceythalmor plan we know nothing about? I've been struggling to think of something, anything that could help us end this threat. Give us a direction.\n\nSo, imagine my surprise when I got a letter from a ghost.

I was so lost after being oustered. The Garland Ring saved my life. And I'll be forever grateful.\n\nBut now, friend, it's time to travel. There's so much of the world still to see! And I want to see it with you!

Look at us. Just two part-time do-gooders. Hunting spies, saving queens. We could make a decent living of this.\n\nHey, I know I've called you a friend from the moment we met. But I mean it. You might even be my best friend. Just don't tell Hyacinth.

You did it! Hollowjack's physical form has been dispersed. He can't be killed for good, but if you continue to defeat his corporeal form until the festival ends, the veil will strengthen and confine him to Detritus.
I can't thank you enough for your help. Lord Hollowjack did this to me. He must be stopped before he hurts anyone else!
I'm forever in your debt, my friend. I need a moment to compose myself. You need to stop Lord Hollowjack before he destroys anyone else with his terrors.
Tamiit. To know that the spirit of my old mentor now dwells somewhere within Cantor Krin'ze …. \n\nTruly, Azurah moves as the moons do in the sky. In silence, mysterious and profound.

Where one story ends, another begins. If I am still here, it means Azurah still has a purpose for me in this world. That she wants me to walk its length and breadth. And there is only one I want to walk alongside me.\n\nTamiit, shall we?

There is much that pain and shame have kept me from telling you on our travels, tamiit.\n\nBut I can hold back from you no longer. The old wounds of my memories are open now and the pain must be endured.
Krin'ze is safe. The Twilight Cantors are safe. And you are safe, walker, along with Zerith-var.\n\nFor too long I have been prey to my own fears. Now, at last, I can enjoy the twilight hours.

You're a warrior, like me. I assume you know something about how annoying it is to lose. I didn't even make a mistake. Those monsters just killed me! \n\nWell, I'm not going to lie in my proverbial grave and let them get away with it.
This one has no business with you, as far as he can see. Move along, lest you draw the attention of the Torval Curiata.
You are the transient that spoke with Cantor Krin'ze, yes? She instructed you to investigate a phenomenon she witnessed at Moonmont.\n\nThe Torval Curiata would like to know what you have discovered.
I want to lay down my axe and travel someplace more … peaceful. \n\nGood luck to you, friend. I just need to rest a moment before I move on as well. I can barely lift my arms.

Rest assured you'll find yourself in my book's acknowledgments. Which reminds me, I need to get to writing! But do return tomorrow. I believe we've only just unearthed one of many secrets behind the Ayleids and the Daedra.
This ends now! This one forbids you from involving Krin'ze any further in your misdeeds. \n\nViti does not wish to see the Inquisitors take notice and act against the young one.
After the peace talk scandal that killed Caecilius, I heard the alliances banded together to write each affected family an apology. Whatever they wrote wasn't enough for Cato Albus or Vandorallen.
What was it all for? Was Cato ever trying to avenge his son? Or was his only goal to lighten his grief by spreading it to other noble families? \n\nWell, I hope it was worth his while.

I can't see how bad the destruction is, but I can smell it.\n\nIf Orpheon's forces made it this far, they must be closer to the Elder Scroll than I feared. Mentor Huzbedad is the only protection it currently has. We need to help him.

I hope Khafdeed is all right. I heard what happened to Mentor Huzbedad—and I'll mourn him—but hearing and seeing are vastly different experiences. \n\nAll this for an Elder Scroll. Orpheon never should have come here.

My soul and that of Moon-Singer Talbira's … are they the same now? Am I her? Is she me?\n\nI would ask to travel with you and Zerith, but I have so much to figure out now. So much to practice and learn.

I searched for so long in the dark and was pulled along a bent and twisting path. Then you and Zerith-var guided me back to the light. Thank you.\n\nBut others will face paths worse than mine unless you put an end to Ravith-morna.
<Sunbeam relaxes on her bench.>
Could Lirinisse be a criminal? No, I don't believe it!\n\nI lent her coins for lunch at the Sleepy Eaglet just a few days ago. I suppose I'll never be repaid now.
Why would they arrest an arcane tutor? She was a bit sharp-tongued, certainly, but as far as I know, that's not a crime.
My son. My son. My son.
A thousand blessings to you and Zerith-var for saving me. Twice!\n\nViti led us to this place to shelter. She's compiled the most fascinating texts on the Order of the Hidden Moon!
It seems your necromancer friend was afforded some luxuries with his burial.\n\nWhat? After the events at Star Haven Adeptorium, my paws need resting.
Was Zerith-var truly interred here for centuries without wasting away?\n\nWhat a lonely soul. How fortunate he is that you found him! As suited for one another as twin moons.

Pick at the bones of this all place all you like. All you'll end up with is a clawful of dust.\n\nThat's what the Sugar God promises. And you'd better be content with it, or some Inquisitor might threaten to lop off your tail!

Stirk Fellowship. Has a nice ring to it, don't you think? And when next we meet, you and I are going to ring a lot of Worm Cult heads! Just like a hammer striking a bell, that's what we're going to do. For Merric.
You have my word. No more Worm Cult or necromancy for me. I'll disappear as soon as the leaves take full effect.
If our business is concluded, I would appreciate you moving along. There's a certain … musk you adventurer types exude.\n\nI'd prefer it not sink into the woodwork.
We'll be in touch regarding Solstice, friend. Until then, stay safe.

I am very much relieved that my spell succeeded and reached you. And I see you've gathered the alliances. Good, good.\n\nNeedless to say, the Worm Cult captured me. My spell won't last long, so listen closely to my instructions.
Save us from diplomats and Daedric cultists, I say!
Wherever Skordo goes, we follow. I won't let those cultists kill another of my comrades.
This one wants to complain about the smell and the dirt. These Worm Cultists are terrible housekeepers.

Orpheon and his army destroyed everything we built and tried to stomp us out.\n\nNow all that remains of my people look to me for leadership. It's overwhelming. I'm not sure how Mentor Huzbedad managed.
I'll do my best to keep Orpheon's forces from taking the Elder Scroll while you work to remove their threat more directly. \n\nMay the gods you favor look fondly on you today.
The Stirk Fellowship? I suppose it will do until I can suggest something better.

Learning how the Hidden Moon met its end has made quiet the most keen of my sorrows. It does not eclipse my heart to wander these ruins.\n\nI do not gaze at the past, but look forward, and pray the Hidden Moon may yet live again someday.
The Stirk Fellowship? Well, I don't hate it. We could do worse for a name for our combined forces.
The Pact will send champions at least. Perhaps some troops. At least until we know the extent of what the Worm Cult is actually planning.
These wounds keep chasing me, but I am faster. \n\nSiege Master Malthoras is only as strong as his weapons. Destroy them and he becomes master of nothing.
I feel too much and too little. I don't know how we will move on from this, or how anyone could. \n\nI suppose I'll find out.
Mentor Huzbedad is dead. Of all the tragedies and injustices of the day, this stings the worst. \n\nBut Khafdeed will advise us. He was trusted.

It's a shame you didn't leave those deserters for us to deal with in our own way. \n\nMy weapons are sharp and my anger burns with the heat of my ashen home. If I find an enemy alive out there, no one will hold me back.

Try to think in the sun and not the shadow. \n\nWe live. We are not alone. Our purpose is clear. We are the Hel Netu, protectors of the Moth Priests and their scroll. So long as we know who we are we can carry on.
Mentor Huzbedad was Orpheon's last victim. He'd want it to be that way. Especially when his sacrifice kept the scroll from Orpheon's hands.

Apprentice, arrange another coach! We must be off after I finish my tonic. Where is that damn serving wench?\n\nA mage of my standing can't miss the meeting at the Mages Guildhall. It would be unseemly. Hmm. Forget I said that. There is no meeting.
I didn't think today would be this eventful.
With that Daedra gone, we can easily clean up any remaining Worm Cultists.\n\nSounds like you and Skordo—the real Skordo!—have important business on Stirk. Don't worry about us. We'll be fine.
We'll deal with any remaining Worm Cult infestation in the Earth Forge.\n\nGo attend to your business on Stirk. No more shall die here today.
Politics don't interest me. The Guilds are the ones doing the dirty work to keep everyone safe.
I think you asked quite enough questions of Magister Andrelo. She needs to recover her strength for the trip ahead. We can't miss the meeting in Shornhelm.

Stirk Fellowship? Yes, Skordo suggests a good name. I will do my best to lead the Fighters Guild and make Merric proud.\n\nAs soon as we get clarity on the obstacles we face, I'll send for you. Until then, Stendarr keep you safe, comrade.
I appreciate everything you did for Julien and me. When he returns from his tour of duty, we're going to get married!
I'll call on <<1>> sometime soon. I just need to figure out what to say to her.
Do not worry for us. I will not allow my family to get separated again.

You killed him! The Duke of Camlorn is dead because of you. How do you expect to keep all of Glenumbra from falling to the werewolves without his guiding hand?\n\nDo you really think you can save us now? Do you?

Point the amulet at people in Aldcroft. It will reveal if someone is a werewolf or not.\n\nIt pains me to say this, but pay special attention to the refugees from Camlorn. I don't believe they're all what they appear to be.
Surely the Eight sent you to save us. Me, my daughter, we owe you our lives. \n\nDo you always go to such great lengths to help people you don't even know?
I can see it in your eyes. I'm turning. Becoming one of those … things.\n\nNo! I refuse to give in to despair! I want to live, gods damn it! I want to live!

I don't know who I really am any more. Part of me is still alive, in agony. A part of that … abomination!\n\nIf Reezal-Jul were in front of me right now, I swear my hate alone would tear that lizard to shreds!
I apologize for the mess. Master Ahtah's study was recently ransacked.

I knew more of my fellow knights would come to see the insanity Sir Croix means to unleash at Alcaire Castle. \n\nI think we have enough knights now to retake the keep. I've sent them to take up strategic positions.
Testing random greeting text to see if the text cuts off or appears corrupted.

Sometimes they treat me as though I were a child! I may be new to this life, but I'm nobody's child!\n\nWell, except for my mother. And my father, I guess. But that's besides the point. You better go and catch up with Verandis.
I hope this is the right decision. I'd be lying if I said I didn't still have some reservations, but I suppose this'll at least give me a chance to earn some coin.
I never thought Julien would feel the same way I do.\n\nThis isn't a trick, is it? I'm a blacksmith. I have a hammer, you know.
Well? Now that the foolish experiment with the braziers has failed, has the king come to see reason? Does he realize this fight cannot be won?
S'rashi wants to help Captain Marck too, but S'rashi must pay Midnight Union boss, yes?\n\nHelp S'rashi get the money he needs and all will be well.
Sounds like you've got an even livelier party than usual in there.
They're whooping it up even more than usual in there.
You did it! You made it in time! I don't know what we would've done without you.
Where's Heloise? Is she all right? Does she need help?
Please, find the rest of the Hinaults. They couldn't have gone far.\n\nAnd remember, if any of them have been killed, you need to burn their bodies and collect their ashes.
I cannot allow one who committed so grevious a crime to ever serve me again.
It seems you wound up saving me twice. \n\nI wish I knew a proper way to express my level of gratitude.
If the Shornhelm Guard can't clear the roads, they should let the Fighters Guild take care of it. We know how to get things done.

Are you ready for glory, Lieutenant? Our greatest hour is at hand. Those green-skinned beasts think they have us defeated; they'll soon realize how incredibly wrong they are.\n\nHave the contents of Reezal-Jul's packets been poured into the braziers?
As amusing as this will presently be, I promise I will try not to laugh.
Well, this is certainly an interesting turn of events. I'm at a loss for words.
You must kill Sir Croix, or all of this bloodshed will have been in vain.
Despite what he's done, I still hold Sir Hughes in the highest regard.\n\nPlease don't judge him too harshly.
I sense a darkness lifted from the fiery depths.\n\nTell me, have you done the deed?
My poor Toves … but what you did was right. \n\nEven if he now thinks of me with scorn, at least he will be safe.
During the war, there was a shortage of ale. Imagine that! \n\nSome taverns were charging far too much for what little they had.
Living in a city is harder than living out in the country, even though it's safer from invaders.
You don't look like a Bloodthorn cultist. I assume this is a rescue attempt?
I assume you've heard that Martin enlisted in the Shornhelm Guard. I'm glad, but I do worry for his safety. I hope he enlisted for the right reasons.
Dark. Cold. Dry. Worse than death this prison is. But my bindings cannot be broken like a dead branch. \n\nThere is no escape, no release.
I'm almost certain the incantation is "Arkay's Beard," but Akatosh is a more reliable deity.\n\nIt's definitely one of those two. I think.
What can I do for you?
It warms my heart to see all that stuff burning. \n\nYou should be able to get in that cave now to free the rest of the crew. Go for it! I'll be waiting up here to cover their escape.
Knarstygg told me what you have done for Murk-Watcher. \n\nThough this seems dangerously unnatural to Dro-Dara, there is no point in questioning it now.
Ever since you freed us, Murk-Watcher has been sitting out there, just staring at those crocodiles.\n\nIt's strange. They've been leaving her alone. Maybe she's worked some of her old charms on them.

Many drowned when the levees were broken. Others were eaten by the crocodiles.\n\nIt's not the beasts' fault, though. It is their nature to hunt. Their spirits sing a song my heart hears. It is the song of the crocodile.
Did you get everything? The blossoms, the mudcrab claws? Did you forget the wine?
You smell of ogre blood and victory, friend. You have the teeth?
You can't feel what I'm feeling, can you?\n\nSomething beyond this door is singing in my veins. I can feel it in my tainted blood.
Please. You have to finish it. We were so close! \n\nJust those last three support beams and we'd have caved it in. Boom. No more ogres.

You've got to help me! I mean … us. I mean the whole town!\n\nThe countess has gone crazy, and everyone's fighting about who should be in charge. She's the only one who can run this place. We need to help her.
Look at you! I can tell by the look of you, you're traveling around, meeting people, seeing new places.\n\nThat's the life I'm going back to. This plantation is doomed, and my days here are done.
I brought my army here as a favor to King Emeric, but Murtag clan has other battles to fight. We need to finish the Ironhand Ogres and finish them fast.\n\nMay your kills be quick and many, soldier.
Those zombies sure make me nervous.  Please take care of them.
General Godrun has commandered the house at the south end of the camp.\n\nThere's plenty of work to go around. That's for sure.
Please, take my sword to Princess Mira at her crypt.\n\nI pray she forgives me. I cannot rest until she does.
I managed to escape with some relics, so there are only a few left. \n\nIf you can recover them, and look for the Warden who was captured, you'll be answering my prayers.
When I find out who did this to me—to us—I'll kill him.
You have our thanks!\n\nI hope Lord Sorick enjoys his prison cell.
I hope Baron Sorick rots in a dungeon.
The Abbot and Master Altien are safe, right?\n\nMay Azura watch over them, and may her blessings never falter.
We can't create more Dreamless Potions without the Dream Shard.\n\nWithout those potions we, and the king, are vulnerable to the Supernal Dreamers.

Brother Hakam and I were novices together. How will I get on without him?\n\nOf course, returning Abbot Durak here is of even greater importance. I'm sorry to burden you with our troubles, but we're in dire need.
You have triumphed. The threat of Hosni at-Tura's Midnight Union is quelled.\n\nAnd we can return to watching and warding.
You must drink the Dreamstride Potion and free Durak from his dream.
Our allies have betrayed us. The Midnight Union are now enemies—and I failed to see it coming.
Well, get on with it!
Did you find a key? There must be one around here somewhere!
Captain Rama deliberately stole the totem to provoke the Stonechewers.\n\nAs long as that totem remains on the tower, we'll never be rid of those Goblins.
Well? What do you have to show for your efforts? \n\nI tire of waiting.
You have a gentle and generous spirit, stranger. Thank you for helping us.

There is no suitable reward for what you've done. Sorry to say it, but your success has probably earned you more responsibility than reward. \n\nYou'll be hearing from me again sooner than you'd like. I apologize in advance.
Ugurz has your money. I have no way to pay you.
We have nothing else to discuss.

If you're here to join the crew, today's not the day. The ship's still anchored out in the harbor. I'd write down your name, but I just don't feel like it. \n\nToo much to drink last night at the Cloudy Dregs ….
There's a sight for sore eyes, and surely a guiding light for any ships coming into port.\n\nYou saved the lives of a lot of sailors.
You saved me, you saved my crew, you saved Elvira, and you showed up the most notorious slavers on the seas. \n\nI'd bet your name will be pretty well-known after this.
What have we here? A guest who's wandered a bit too far from the party?

It was… it was Ma'jhad Kha. He saw me trying to escape… I thought he had me, but then Elvira stepped in…\n\nThat girl's got sand, but she's no match for Ma'jhad Kha. He dragged her off toward the beach. You have to help her.
Patrolling guards watch the cask of wine at the end of the docks.
Poor Constable Pascal. I have to admit though—I sleep better at night knowing a Knight of the Flame is in charge.
Has this entire city gone mad?

The worst part of this is that these bandits sully the good name of the Knights of the Flame.\n\nIf our leader, Sir Hughes, was here, he'd charge out there and kill all the bandits himself just to make a point.
The Stonechewers' breeding stock has been badly depleted by this foolish conflict. Leave me alone to contemplate this tragedy in solemn silence.
I can't believe I came so close to being … whatever it was they were planning.\n\nI'm not exactly sure, but I'm glad you stopped them.
It worked! I feared that touching the Water Stone would destroy one … or even both of us, but it didn't. \n\nWe merged. We are one. And we are both stronger for it.
Brother against brother is a brutal conflict. \n\nEven in that confrontation, these knights found honor.
Do you need assistence? If not, I'm afraid I'm busy at the moment. Damn, where are those sellswords? I can't fight them on my own.
Never again, honest! I've learned my lesson.
Did you destroy the altar and kill that bastard witchman?

I should be glad we got away, but I'm too angry to think! They've taken the garrison? \n\nThe brutish swine! If there's one thing I do before I die, it's going to be spitting on the corpse of that cowardly wench Septima Tharn.

My roots burrow hungrily into the earth, as if the loamy soil were my only need. \n\nBut I feel a hollowness that I cannot abide. I see a being here I want to remember, but when I try to think, there is nothing.
It's time!
Could I interest you in a game of chance? \n\nI'm told I have terrible luck, but maybe today will be different.
How about a little game of chance? \n\nI have terrible luck, but that's bound to change, right?
Remember, throw the Scamp heads into the nascent portals.\n\nThen meet me in the cave to the north when you're done. If Azura favors us, I'll have rescued Master Muzgu by then.
The poison vial is over there, next to the candles.\n\nBring it to me.
You think you have nothing? Oh, my friend, you always have your soul.

My brother is wasting his time. The raw materials are plentiful here, and their owners are exceedingly poor. It's a buyer's market.\n\nHe always wanted to be someone's savior. He should follow his avarice.
The damned dreugh are everywhere, and these citizens have lost their minds!\n\nThey're attacking dreugh bare-handed. I've saved as many as I can, but that last dreugh wounded me. Help!
I expect the beetles to clear out soon and then we can get back to work.\n\nI'm never overjoyed to get back to work, but I am grateful to fulfill my father's dying wish.
Word has reached me of what happened at the seraglio. I should have seen this coming.\n\nPlease. Tell me you found Prince Azah and he is safe.
This place is such a mess. I'm … it's going to take hours to clean it all up.
Thank you for meeting me.
By the bloody fangs of Mauloch! By the stench of Mauloch's gaping maw!\n\nWhat have you done? How can this be? I'm … free?

Hey—I know you! We killed that crazy old necromancer together—Angof. Remember that midnight talisman we used to break into Cath Bedraud? I still can't believe that worked. \n\nSo I don't suppose you need help with something fun like that?
Yes. I believe Bergama is where you should begin your search for the other two Ansei Wards.\n\nI will keep the Ward of Ansei Radan for now, but I will return it to you when you are ready.
Thank you stranger! I'd go myself, but the streets aren't safe! \n\nKids keep trying to grab me, and one man tied me up and made me dance! Then he even took all the money!
Unishi is pleased to see you again. You have made the deliveries to this one's clients, yes?
Ah! There you are. The Ash'abah who was with you just returned, saying you had become separated.
I couldn't wait any longer. Did you find the pair?\n\nI don't need their ghosts haunting my mine along with all these spiders!
Prince Azah has been anxiously awaiting your return. You should speak to him right away.
I feared that after all these years, my sacrifice would prove to be of no avail, but you performed admirably. \n\nWe cannot kill that necromancer, but he will trouble us no more.
My children hunger. Until you appease them, we have nothing to discuss.
Are you ready for your next lesson?
I brought a bunch of miners from Wayrest with me. I'm the only one who escaped those spiders.\n\nWhat will I tell their families?
The lair's entry is concealed. Let me clear it for you.\n\nHe will be inside. Your strength is greater than mine. Let us hope it is also greater than his.
I do not know that the old master deserved death. We could've saved her, benefited from her experience.\n\nBut I'm sure <<1>> will do her best to fill the void.
Did you speak to <<1>>?
So, you are the one the others spoke of so highly.\n\n<<1>> has brought shame upon Leki's Blade. I would hear your thoughts before adding my own.
What happened at the Magistrate's House? Do you find evidence that she's involved in the disappearances?
You could just talk directly to me, you know. I am standing right here.

In the sand, beetles! Behind the rocks, beetles! Around the johads, beetles! Last night, I woke up and one was in my tent, just … just watching me!\n\nWe can't do our work! Sentinel's going to run out of water!
I'm glad someone's taking care of things.\n\nYou're a rare sort, wayfarer.

In our fight against the Nedes, we saw the raw power of defiance. We came to respect Tamriel and its warriors. \n\nYou must now battle the giant Goblinkin. The Ra Gada's long road to conquest was paved with thousands of these beasts' corpses.
Go on. I will just turn myself in. I suppose this will exonerate Istah. You should speak to him.
I'll do what I must to save <<1>>. But, maybe there's another way besides being covered in spiders again ….
Thank you for killing that Goblin!
Add the sleep potion to the Midnight Union's drinking kegs. That should put the bandits to sleep. \n\nThen search the counting house. We need to know where they're keeping Miranda.
Thanks, stranger. \n\nIf you find any survivors, tell them help will soon be on its way.
Thank you. I feel much better already.
Collect the antidote to that poison before it's too late! \n\nLady Miranda's in the manor house. Use that key I gave you to get in.
Muzgu. Dead. \n\nI thought Azura would protect him. She didn't.
Honor and blood, my friend! How goes the campaign? I don't suppose you've slain any Daedroths yet, eh? I could use a new pair of boots. Ha!
Find Sergeant Stegine. He's up the road in Dreughside.\n\nSo many dead.
I'll compensate the Dreughsiders. I'll leave, stay in Wayrest.\n\nPlease, just let me go free!
We heard everything. \n\nIs it true? Did Baron Sorick really plant the eggs?
You want to fight? You sure about this?
You amuse me. That's worth paying a pittance of a debt.\n\nNow take it and get off my dock.
Praise Azura! You survived.
I heard there was a ruckus down at the docks. They say someone chewed up the Grinder and spit him out.\n\nI'm guessing that someone was you.
I'm thankful that you came along. I thought for sure I'd never see my canopic jar again.
With the Midnight Union affair cleaned up, we won't have to treat any more of their victims. \n\nNow that's something to look forward to.
This one would speak with you for a moment, walker. \n\nYou might be interested in an opportunity to earn some gold by helping someone in need?
Azura go with you, friend. I hope her blessing might dispel the curse of Vaermina's cultists.
This is familiar. I remember you from Alcaire … the Vanne Farm! \n\nFunny we should end up surrounded by Supernal Dreamers again.
I'm glad that's over. We need to get back to Camlorn.\n\nSee you around.
My wife is safe and well—and my son came to me and apologized. \n\nYou are a wonder, and we're blessed to know you.
We must trust in the gods. That's what I do. \n\nI've made many offerings to the Divines in these last dark days.
I'll be traveling back to Wayrest shortly. \n\nIf we see each other there, I don't know you.
I guess I'll never be done thanking you. \n\nI hate to imagine what would have happened if you hadn't defeated the Omen.
Something's different. I wonder what's going on? I don't like it.
The guards are looking rather anxious. Something's changed, hasn't it? And for the better. \n\nI think we might live through this.
We're going to be allowed to leave, aren't we? \n\nIt's over. I can tell.
The world of the living has transgressed. The energy of these relics was used for darkness. \n\nThe portal is closed, but something came through. It must be destroyed.
Do you see? Do you see what I've become? Look at the reflection! \n\nI'm old. I'm fat. And sometimes Argonian! No one will ever admire me again!
I'm sorry. You'll simply have to excuse me. I'm getting to know myself and I'm not who I thought I was.\n\nYou can see it too. Just look. Look in the mirror.

You still here? 

Just tell that crazy Ashton I don't want any more of her worthless stones! 

Do you hear me?
What's the point of opening my mouth to speak?\n\nThere's nothing I can say to end this torment, so I'm just going to stop talking. I mean it.

I appreciate you doing this for me. My wife made me promise to get the refugees out of Crestshade and keep them safe, but I can't stop worrying about her.\n\nCrestshade is directly north of this camp and our house is right in the center of the town.
The Covenant thanks you for joining the war effort! With talented crafters like yourself at our back, there's no challenge we can't overcome.\n \nAkatosh bless your wares, friend.
Please … go away. They're going to see you!\n\nI'm not coming out until I see a head.
