You know what amazes me? As muddy as these pigs get, they're still cleaner animals than the cows.\n\nYou know a cow will stand in its own waste for days. Won't even move unless you make it.
Was there some kind of incident up in front of the countess's manse?\n\nI've been trying to avoid that area lately. It simply reminds me of my failures.
I'm sorry. Am I not allowed to stand here? It's the countess's property, and she certainly hasn't said anything.\n\nSo yes, I'll just stay here as long as I like. Thanks!
A summons was recently sent ordering all Knights of the Flame to return to Firebrand Keep.\n\nFor now, though, I feel my duty is to remain here. Sir Hughes will understand.
I cannot describe the sensation, even as a spirit, of being back in my father's presence.\n\nFate was cruel to us in life, but at long last, we've both found peace. Thank you.
You return—and I sense a diminishing of the evil 'round the tower. \n\nHow did you fare?
I'm acting on orders directly from Sir Hughes. If he wants to make an exception, he'll let me know in due time.\n\nUntil then, the envoy stays out!

Again, you must keep this quiet. The Duke is already overwhelmed and hearing about a spy inside the castle might push him over the edge.\n\nGet past Sir Gregory and into the library, find out who "Almandine" is, and report back to me personally.
Together at last! Thank you, stranger. Now I beg you one final favor - a proper burial, as every decent person deserves.\n\nThe shrine is due north of here, at the entrance to the mine.

I hate to say it, but I'm going to have to speak with the duke about this. The fact that the duchess is sending secret letters to her father is serious cause for concern.\n\nWe need to know exactly what they're planning though.
It is a relief to see you returned. I fear I might have asked too much. \n\nTell me though, did General Thoda have any new insights into the source of these assassination attempts?
Still no sign of Mister Nurin? I told you—he's gone—probably burned up in the fire.\n\nMy heart goes out to the rest of the family, but I have to look out for myself. I'll have to find a new job!

I'm glad you came along. The constable's down by the docks. If he won't listen to reason, try to find the messenger from Alcaire Castle. He can explain everything.\n\nIf you can get me released, the Knights of the Flame will be in your debt.
Fire, Scamps, William disappears, and now strangers on the property ….\n\nThe farmhands all gave up. Maybe I need to give up too. The farm's lost, and my sweet William ….
I gave the constable the message, but he doesn't seem to believe me.\n\nHe put Dame Dabienne in the stocks. Glad I'm not her!

Guards! Guards! Arrest these people!

They're setting up the village! The slavers are going to come back and take us all!

Why aren't you listening to me?
If his treatment of my crew had not been so disrespectful, I might feel a little sorry for the constable.\n\nAs it stands though, I'm quite enjoying this.
Were those Daedra death screams I heard? Music to my ears.\n\nAnd you destroyed those damnable portals too. I think now we'll be safe.

I can't tell you what a relief it is to learn that Pascal's mind is messed up.

I guess that sounds a little strange, doesn't it?

Regardless, I'm grateful for all your help.
Heard you were out there talking to that knight in the stocks. \n\nI'd be careful if I were you. Constable will lock you up too. Sit down and have a drink instead. What'll it be?
You did it. You even got him home in time for dinner.\n\nIt weighs heavily on a mother's heart to worry about her son. I can't thank you enough.
I'm with dad on this. I want to wipe every remnant, every trace of those sick freaks from our farm.\n\nIt's the only way we can start over.
I told you! I don't know anything. Go away!
As embarassing as my mother may be, it breaks my heart that she worries so much.\n\nIt's good that we've put her mind at ease. You should talk to her.
The Knights of the Flame are sworn to protect me and my family. How can I trust any of them now?\n\nFirebrand Keep is to the southeast. Go and bring Sir Hughes to justice. Let none stand in your way!
Here we go again. I'll be hearing about this for years—how I failed to save our son in his darkest hour, and oh, thank the Eight for that stranger ….\n\nI guess it could be worse.

Well done! Frankly, I thought we'd be peeling you off the bottom of a rock, but hey, you made it!\n\nNow's our chance to drive the ogres back into the mountains. We can end this thing! I don't know why the general's hesitating!
Hm. You don't look so dangerous. Yet, you waltz into my camp and pick fights with my soldiers?\n\nTell me why I should not simply cut off your head where you stand?
Of all the ports and over all the years, never a worse time and place to be stuck ashore.\n\nFifty crates of grain bound for Rihad, but right now, it's just rotting in the hold.
Sir Hughes decided to let that Redguard envoy in to speak with the Duke, and the soldiers went back to their camp.\n\nSo things are quiet here … for now.
Hey, you're not going into the warehouse, are you?\n\nConstable promised me that if anyone got to go in there and paint the walls with slaver blood it would be me.
Welcome back to the Hall, my friend.  Our librarians are anxious to pore over your discoveries!
My husband, Sir Gregory, suddenly wants to take me to Wayrest. How very sweet of him!
The Duchess must be kept safe. I will stay here while you speak with Sir Hughes.\n\nI hope he will send additional security to protect her.
King Fahara'jad will never forget the loss of his beloved Lakana, but I hope this man's death will bring him some sense of peace.
A crime was committed and the price had to be paid. I wish it could have been otherwise, but I have done my duty as you chose.

My husband's a little hard of hearing. Not quite in touch with reality either. He thinks he killed that Scamp, but it was actually our cat.\n\nBless his heart though, he certainly means well. Just play along if you will.
Are there any more Scamps down there? Bring them on, I say! 'Scampkiller' is my middle name! \n\nI can still wield a blade just like when I was a young man. Just watch!
I am simply a bailiff here. If you want to help, seek out Constable Agazu. You can find her around the town square.\n\nBut if you add to our woes, stranger, you shall have to answer to me.

These Knights of the Flame, they insult King Fahara'jad by refusing me entry. \n\nI have an urgent message for Duke Nathaniel and I am a close friend of the Duchess. I cannot understand why the Knights are so stubborn.
I apologize for doubting you. You are indeed a worthy duelist.
You're stronger than I expected. You have my respect.
I wouldn't have expected such skill-at-arms from an outsider, but I saw you dueling over there. \n\nGeneral Thoda did too and he would like to speak with you. You will find him through the door.
The <<1>> is the last champion left. \n\nYou know, I think I'll wish you luck.
Now the arena champions are dead, I assume you plan to take their place. \n\nIf not, there goes the business.
I heard the count's having those prisoners released.\n\nNo bad thing, if you ask me.
I told you everything I know. Talk to Martine.
Was that a fight I heard? Looks like you didn't need any help.\n\nLeveque's likely still up there. Go get him.
I'd get that information to <<1>> right away. It's probably important.
<<1>> is the one to talk to.
As I said, talk to the Captain about any suspicions you may have.
Come on! What are you waiting for? Let's go!
<The dog barks and wags his tail in recognition.>
What news? The safety of the royal family depends on this.
I mourn the creatures you were forced to kill. They usually aren't so aggressive.
I'm taking my family to Daggerfall. We'll be safer there.
I will always remember Daggerfall's champion.
Assassins in my port? Thank Tall Papa you were here.
Let's turn that stupid pig into pork chops and be done with it!
A swineherd's life isn't easy, you know. But my pigs love me.

Hold, stranger. If you're going toward Shornhelm, you're doing it at your own risk. \n\nAs much as I'd love to tell you the Shornhelm Guard will keep you safe, that's just simply not the case. We're spread thin and trying to regroup.
I know why you're here, but where I got that amulet is a discussion for another time. \n\nJust be careful. The werewolves won't appreciate having their secrets revealed.
That's everything. I'll have my guards get ready.
Be careful out there. Red Rook bandits might be anywhere.
Talk to the captain. She's in charge.
We were able to get all the villagers through the portal. They're safe in our camp for now.
So it was Angof. I thought I smelled the stench of true evil.
Friend, the poor of Daggerfall owe you our lives. We don't have anything, but if we did, we'd give it all to you.
I learned a hard lesson. I won't turn away anyone who's in trouble again. Not on my watch. Not even a beggar.

I cannot emphasize enough how dangerous this situation has become. If the king does not recover quickly, this may be the end of the Daggerfall Covenant.\n\nI beseech you to do everything in your power to help him.
Now, pay attention to Recruit Gorak. He's a great scholar of our history, and has all the makings of a fine soldier.
By the Eight! He killed them. Get in there and destroy the Duke. I'll make sure he doesn't get past you. Go!
What are you waiting for? The Lion Guard doesn't tolerate sluggards.
You found Bethany! \n\nBut what about the rest of the women? Do you know what the Bloodthorns did with them?
Get to the city quickly. Inform the Lion Guard how to beat Faolchu and they may yet have a chance to take Camlorn back.

Off with you now. Bumnog will help you. Interesting fellow. Always fights fair. Refuses to use weapons against the harpies. Just his fists.\n\nCan't imagine that that works out for him, but he's the only Dagger still here, so what do I know?
Listen, you've helped the Daggers. A lot. And we appreciate it. But before we go back to camp, I need to make sure you understand something.
Did I hear you harassing my workers? Ohama says she sent you to look for a thief among them.\n\nI'm not sure I believe her story, but I'm willing to hear her out.
Lord Diel seems kind of angry. But I'm sure Gelvin can straighten everything out.
We're not warriors. I'm a potter, for Stendarr's sake! We were lucky you came along.
You are ready to face <<1>>.\n\nWait to use the charm until she tries to drain your vitality. The charm will turn her magic against her, revitalizing you.

Greetings, sandwalker. I can tell by that look in your eye … you know lizards. \n\nDo they speak to you? Do you enjoy the feel of their cool scales against your cheek? Yes, you understand. I know you do.
I've lost everything—Poppa, the lighthouse, everything. \n\nHow can I go on?
The lamentations of Westtry's dead have silenced. Thank you, traveler.
Do you have the hawthorn berries? Take them to Muriel. She's in her shop on the town square.
Captain Rosalind! I've been making poultices for the wounded, but I'm out of hawthorn berries.
Captain, I went by your house to check on Leon. \n\nHe was praying, but something wasn't right.
We're lucky you came along. \n\nBut I'm sure our luck won't last. Have you seen the crocodiles around here? We're going to wind up as a meal for one of those monsters.
Well, I guess I've learned a few things they don't even teach in the Lion Guard.
Gada, Gada, Tobr'a… Netu… \n\nNo. That can't be right.
That took longer than I hoped. It's hard to be patient when I know the fate of my kingdom is at stake. \n\nTell me you have good tidings … or did they escape with the Ansei Wards?
Guy and Erwan should be along the south road, the one that splits toward Aldcroft and Camlorn.
Guy and Erwan should be along the south road, the one that splits toward Aldcroft and Camlorn.
Grahla actually agreed? You can look for the door into the past? Well, that's just great. I knew she'd appreciate what I'd done.
Well, at least I can say that Sarvith's spells are consistent. They never fail to fail.
This armor is your key to the past. It belonged to my beloved and was buried in this place of honor. \n\nIt was my beloved's hand that cut Faolchu down.
This isn't an easy choice, I know. I don't envy you. \n\nBut whatever you decide, we're with you.
The orders must be on one of the Alessian soldiers. Find them and meet me back at the camp.
The choice has been made and the end approaches.\n\nI'll join Leon in our home. Come to us after you complete the task.
Curse this darkness! I can't see a thing!\n\nAre you another one of <<1>>'s illusions? Don't think I'm a fool—I know your tricks! Where is <<2>>?
As soon as you capture a <<1>>, take it into the circle at the center of the standing stones.\n\nThen we'll be ready to perform the ritual.
Sir Granden's tomb is in the eastern mounds. \n\nBeware. He was strong in life and will be strong in death.
We made it in, thanks to you. \n\nWith the gate locked, we should be able to hold this position.
It's good to see you. Is there something I can help you with?
You must act with the honors, of course. Replace the relics on their respective altars.
Thank you! You made my wife very happy.\n\nI would have handled this myself, but my wife refused to hear of it. She worries so about me.
Once you acquire my lockbox, please hold onto it until we're safely away from those dastardly bandits.\n\nAnd do be careful. I'd hate to think that someone got hurt trying to help me.
I hear you were instrumental in the defeat of that villain, Angof. Well done!
Is the Duke safe?
That didn't seem right.
We can't fail here. Our families, our homes … we're going to lose everything to that beast.
I always believed in Alinon's research. That's the reason I agreed to help him.\n\nWe hold the key to ending this curse. Let's just hope we're not already too late.
I'd be in terrible trouble if you hadn't come by when you did.\n\nAnd I'm ever so grateful. Really.
Angof's evil flows deeper than the wellspring of this land. This must end quickly.
You made it! I was worried about you.
The siege camp is ours again, but at what cost? And do we have the forces remaining to continue this course of action?\n\nI'm not so sure.
You! I am so glad you made it in time! We are just about to begin the ceremony.\n\nCasnar told me everything, and knowing what you have done, you are the guest of honor!
Do you often just walk into people's houses and snoop around upstairs? \n\nIf my cousin were here, he might not be so friendly. Me … I don't care. I don't really care about anything at this point.
The more I think about it, the more this concerns me. If you find my brother, tell him to come speak with me. \n\nIf he doesn't come soon, I'm going to close up shop and help you search.

Slow down now. You've made your point. Like I said, I'm a businessman. Truth is, I didn't much like the deal I had with Jagnas anyways. \n\nYou'll owe me a favor, but I'll give him a refund, and your boy can get married whenever he likes.
I prayed to the Eight for a miracle. Instead they sent you. \n\nOh, don't look at me like that. I'm joking. Mostly. Now go get that key.
I can feel the oppressive weight of Angof's corruption lifting. I sense the gratitude of the guardians, but I also sense … fear.\n\nAngof's vermin are afraid.
Watch yourself out there. The Ra-Netu are clumsy, but if a few of them get a hold of you … well, I saw what happens, and it is not pleasant.

You did good here. I'm sorry about the bandit's father, but the two of you saved a lot of lives today.\n\nIf you speak to the bandit, let him know we'll look the other way if he decides to slip out of here. Meanwhile, we've got a town to clean up.
Unclawed traitor! Ildani never should have trusted you! \n\nYou betrayed this one. The Baandari will know. They will not forget.
The cure—did it work?
The tension's so thick, the suspense is killing me! I hope Gelvin gets out here soon.
Thanks for helping the people of Deleyn's Mill. Maybe we'll go back and rebuild after things finally calm down.
Be wary of those vines.\n\nWherever they appear, the Bloodthorn cult isn't far behind.

Ha! Strastnoc's head! I thought we were in for a long standoff with that skeever son-of-a-cow. Then you walked up and dropped his head in my lap! \n\nI've been fighting with these milk-drinkers too long. Well met, my friend. Well met.

Aha! You must be the hero whose bold deeds Captain Hjurrun was just recounting. Retaking the lighthouse may seem trivial, but in times like these, it's huge.\n\nSay, you look like someone I've been hearing quite a bit about. Might I ask your name?
Who's that? You again? I told you. I'm not risking my family until we have a way to defend ourselves. Bring me those weapons and I'll open the door.
I do hope you find Lady Laurent quickly and let her know that supper is ready. \n\nI found those little gherkins she likes so much.
This crown is quite a marvel. \n\nBut why is Stibbons acting so strangely? No doubt it's all this open air. He's not cut out for adventuring. I'm sure that's it.
That'll teach those mangy beasts.\n\nNow press forward! We must maintain our momentum.
These werewolves were much tougher than the ones near Aldcroft. Nice work getting us in. \n\nIf you're trying to impress me, you're doing a good job. Keep it up and maybe we'll talk later.
I helped you get this far, so return the favor and free me from this prison.
There you are! I was beginning to worry. It seems that more and more of the dead are rising every minute.\n\nDid you learn anything in the crypt?

It's good to see you again, my friend. The Shornhelm Guard has been helpful, but my mother and little brother have yet to arrive.\n\nBy any chance, did you happen to find them while you were out there?
Safe journeys to you. Wherever your path leads, remember what you've learned at Leki's Blade.
If I can do anything for you, just let me know. I'll do what I can for those who protect our people.
You return! Have Angof's minions fallen before your wrath?
It's awful out there. I hate war. I just hate it!\n\nAnd I want my mother. Why isn't she back yet? I want to go home!
You again? I thought you'd be wearing an iron collar at the bottom of the river by now. \n\nWhat in the blazes do you want?
Greetings.\n\nIt's nice to see another strong guild member around here. Our numbers aren't what they used to be. Live by the sword and all that.

I know her Majesty would appreciate if you gave these matters the highest priority. After you've completed your investigation, come speak to the queen at the Chapel of Saint Pelin. \n\nIf there are problems, she should know as soon as possible.
Nice to see you, comrade. Our numbers aren't what they used to be. Live by the sword and all that.

Well that takes care of that, now doesn't it?\n\nI'm actually quite relieved. It would have been so embarrassing to have been responsible for the fall of Alik'r. After I opened the portal, I considered just leaving and denying that I was ever here.
You have answers? Answers are more to me than water! Answers! Answers!
Poor, craven Stibbons. The truth is, I almost feel for him. Almost.
The riches of Dresan Keep were almost within my grasp!
The wards on the vault entrance have been removed. You are free to go.
What a magnificent find! I doubt Richard appreciated its value, though. He sought treasure, not knowledge.\n\nI'll see that the Dresan Index winds up in the proper hands.
Still hanging around, eh?\n\nDon't suppose your reconsidering that drink? Ah, never mind. We both have things we need to do.
Cut me down before the spiders return!
Well, what are you waiting for? Cut him down!
Once, the Viridian Sentinel stood for something more than a wetnurse to spoiled children. Now, he expects us to train and rear this daughter of the city as our own?\n\nNo. The Sentinel asks too much.
I suspect this priest has fallen from Arkay's favor. That explains why he's making such a big deal out of nothing. \n\nSo what if the holy water burns! That doesn't prove anything!
When you find Angof, hit him once for me.

I've known Stenwick since I was a child. Just because we didn't agree on many things, doesn't mean his burial tradition should be ignored.\n\nWe'll return Elara's body to Evermore. I don't know how royalty prefer to be buried.
I need to finish drawing what energy I can, and then get Elara back to my hut. I've done all I can for her here.
I'm sorry, I wish I could join you in the fight, but someone's got to keep watch on the road in case the Reachmen get reinforcements before we do.
I can't go back in there, I can't fight them… they're relentless!\n\nGods, it's happening again, the long hand of the witchmen closes in all around us.

If you think that I will let them parade me down the streets of Evermore, you're mistaken.\n\nAll I need is a sharp stone and for him to look away, then it will end. You've gained nothing! And I … I have nothing left.

You are like a bottle of iced Collequiva in this dreary desert. Hopefully this will restore Lady Laurent's confidence in me.\n\nI still can't understand—how could she doubt me after so many years' service?
We must gather the motes. Quickly, before they're gone, and the Viridian Sentinel's power with them!
It's been a fine adventure, I must admit.\n\nMay our paths cross again—particularly if we're on our way to a rowdy tavern.
I regret the day I ever involved myself with these Red Rook bastards. \n\nBy the Eight, this ends here!
You … cast my spell? The masking ritual? But why?
Well, champion? Ready to receive your reward?
Gelves and his Red Rooks are worse than a plague. They're worse than Daedra. \n\nIn fact, they're worse than a plague of Daedra!
What answers the call is the Hunger. Has it been sated?

The contract between the Saltwalkers and the Withered Hand was broken before it even began. And those mercs now consider us blood enemies.\n\nI'm tempted to offer you a percentage of the coin we take from them. Tempted.
We're going to get rid of the Red Rooks, aren't we?
You were right. Nothing good ever comes from giving up. We have to fight for what's ours.
The Company has broken off talks with the Hand and we will soon be rich with Satlwalker spoils. You've done yeoman's work, <<1>>. Well done!
We'll get rid of these Red Rooks for good.
Are you ready to begin? \n\nRemember that I can't defend myself while I'm performing the ritual. You have to protect me.
It is true! It is all true! You won the race!\n\nOur fates are unavoidable! Do you know what this means? Do you realize the full extent of this?
I wish I'd been there when you killed Angof. I had to get the others back to safety. I think they'll all recover. \n\nBut I must say … well, congratulations. You really are something.
After what we learned today, I hope Sorick can push the Imperials back for good.
We meet again. Have you looked fate in the eye? Did she blink?
How could this be? All he needed was a splint for his leg after his horse fell on him, and now he's dead! Why would someone kill him?
That's not right. Something strange is going on in this town! You've seen it, haven't you?\n\nThey just took Draven away for their "initiation." It's like some kind of cult!
Watch out for that spirit. Who knows what harm his riddles will cause you!\n\nDon't say I didn't warn you.
The poor fool. He has already joined us in blood, if not in spirit. I guess there's nothing left to do, if his wish is to leave the ritual unfinished.\n\nHe must be put down.
You're back. Any luck?
Go on. Ask whatever you want. It doesn't matter anymore.
Well, that last lizard didn't race so well.\n\nSpeak to <<1>> again. She might know how to help your lizard.
I told <<1>> you'd look him up once you'd helped some folks around Crosswych. \n\nHe's in the center of town.
Give me a moment, and I will find arms and armor that I can carry!
<The dog barks happily.>
Back so soon? \n\nI still have many terrific lizards to choose from. Were you looking for something specific?
It's passed. I'm so ashamed. The feeling comes and goes, but I need to talk to someone, to take my mind off things. Please.

In addition to the public praise, I must express my own appreciation, wayfarer.\n\nYou not only saved the kingdom, you also saved its king. My reign would have been buried in the sands had you not intervened. Thank you.
Sorry, I don't sell our supplies. I'm sure one of the merchants on the other side of town will have what you need.
You're back! I told <<1>> not to worry about you. Unlike some people I could name, you can handle yourself in a pinch.
Glenumbra is pretty, like Valenwood without the jungles … or torchbugs. And all the trees are wrong. Actually, it's nothing like Valenwood. \n\nPretty, though.
Oh no! The fact that he is not with you does not bode well. Did you find anything? Was he dead? What about the … supplies?
It returns! I told you to go!
I've seen peasants making their way out of the oasis. Well done! \n\nSpeak with <<1>> near Bergama's entrance. I'm sure she'd want to know they're safe.
I cannot believe it! Everyone survived! I only regret that it was not me who helped them.\n\nThey hired me for protection, not to run at the first sign of danger.
Good luck, deputy. We'll be watching and once we've identified all the buyers, we'll close in.\n\nThen you'll get your reward.
I knew my faith in you was justified.
Are you ready to help me get to safety now?
Any luck finding the sword yet?\n\nSo few people will work as hard as I do at these things.
I warned you, but still you took the sword! And now you bring it to my tomb? Are you deranged?\n\nThe sword-cursed will return soon. Take the sword away! Quickly!
Please hurry to the cave of Absolutely Certain Death and look for Willie. I'm certain nothing bad could possibly happen to you.\n\nYou'll find it southeast of here.
<Though the braziers have been doused, <<1>> still seems to be struggling in his sleep.>
One of those Primeval Seekers … she came out of nowhere! \n\nPlease! Lorelia is in danger! You've got to go help her!
Be quick and be quiet. It's better if she never realizes we were even here.
Been a lot more guards around than usual. I hope our business hasn't gone awry.
Ever get the feeling you're being watched?\n\nMy father said you can't fight the law. It might be time to start taking his advice!
Have you heard from <<1>> lately? Far more guards are down here than on a normal day.\n\nIf this information has gone out, it could be … uncomfortable … for both of us.
Excellent. Quick work. Now to the Imperial camp, post haste!\n\nI'll hobble after as best I can and support your attacks with harsh language and rude hand gestures.
That … that wasn't such a good idea. It wasn't necessarily a bad idea, but it was most definitely not a good idea.
If the problems with the Reachmen continue, I'll have to start forging weapons instead of horseshoes.
That was immensely satisfying. I've learned a great deal from this experience. \n\nI will not forget.
It appears that Red Rook may have been telling the truth. Or, at least, a version of the truth. Tread carefully. I'm still not sure I completely trust the man.
They're safe. Thank the Divines! And thank you for believing me.\n\nI'll tell you everything I know about the Red Rooks and the Bloodthorns.
Did you get the messages? Take them to Captain Gilame up on the cliffs.
Have you found the others?
I'll send word to Sir Hadir that the situation is stable for now.
Fell's Run will heal. We're a resiliant bunch. And the mayor and I will make sure that nothing like this ever happens again.

Looks like the Captain gave you something to do. She's demanding, but she's fair. And she believes that everyone needs to earn their keep.\n\nJust watch yourself out there. It looks like it's going to get worse before it gets any better.
Is she safe? Did you save Captain Janeve?
Bad things can happen. Bad things do happen. Bad things have happened.\n\nWhy can I hear his whispers?
Renard, Elise, and Laroche all accounted for. I can't thank you enough.\n\nI take it you faced the creature. And your mind is still your own. You're as formidable as that beast is terrifying.
Do not let her win. She ran up the stairs, so be cautious.\n\nHallin's Stand depends upon you!
Please hurry to the cave of Absolutely Certain Death and look for Willie. I'm certain nothing bad could possibly happen to you.\n\nYou'll find it southeast of here.
I had no idea. I should've spent more time checking the rumors, and less time behind my desk.
We've stopped <<1>> here, but my scouts have informed me that they've spotted a force of Imperials heading to <<2>>.
Despite the concerning rumors about bloodfiends to the west and trouble in Northpoint, life here in Fell's Run has returned to normal.\n\nMore or less.
The Fell's Brigade will defend this town! You have my word on that.
Have you found anything yet? The stolen good? The missing Orcs?\n\nGet back out there and figure this out! We're counting on you.
Ah, I was not expecting you. How did you … never mind. What news have you?
Battles are not without their casualties. Be sure to pay them back all the damage they're owed.
Something I can help you with? I'm rather preoccupied, so make it quick.
Did <<1>> send you? She said to meet her here.
The shame I suffer now is eclipsed by my happiness to have my daughter back, safe and sound. Thank you again.
Someone who knows what they want, yes? How can Nasir be of service?
I hear you're responsible for getting the dreugh on our side. Well done. \n\nWith those beasts chopping them up, the Covenant doesn't stand a chance.
What a plan. Vivec preserve us.\n\nAnyway, go ahead with it, if you've got the guts. The Three have guided you so far. Maybe it'll last.
You've been in the belly of the Covenant's beast. Tell me. Is <<1>> safe?
It's good fighting with Tanval again.
My acolytes know what to expect. We've already made preparations.\n\nSpeak to them. Give them the crown. See what true balance means.
The smell of brimstone is strong in my nostrils. Even as a spirit, this place smells of ash and death. Have you done as I asked?
These Imperials haven't hassled me yet. Smart. If they get any ideas, I've kept my shiny pals here nice and sharp. \n\nYou in the market for a new blade? Have a look.
A fellow mage, eh? I can tell from the distracted look. You see, an arcanist's mind is always else ….\n\nI'm sorry, was I saying something?
These Imperials make for excellent practice.\n\nI admit nothing, of course, but I observe to you that practice makes perfect.
You've got steel in your spine. I see why Tanval trusts you.\n\nIt's a damn shame giving up an immortal army, but the walking dead always spook the men.
I don't like the look on your face. What did you find in that cave?
<<1>> is missing? I haven't seen her. \n\nIt wasn't the Argonians, though. They have no reason to hate her, despite her father.
<<1>> has stolen the <<2>>. Even now, it dies. Quickly, into the cave. You must stop her!\n\nI will meet you. Soon. But first I must recover my strength.
The mountain has spoken, and Senie is no more. But we survive, and no hatchlings were lost to the flames.
Normally I hate it when he yanks me around the room with those little spells. But I've never been more grateful to him. Or to you, traveler.
Your kindness towards us is … commendable. You are kinder than I've been towards the Argonian.
You've cured the injured? Then speak to Girvas. \n\nTell him of the goodwill of my people. He is still in the center of town, or at least what remains of it.
Ahknara is atop the bluff? \n\nQuickly, f'lah, use the trapdoor behind me. Slay her before she signals the attack!
While we're waiting for an army to flank us, a second army stands ready to attack to the north. Meanwhile, assassins creep through the fort.\n\nThese two weeds share a root beneath the surface.
With the dreugh on our side, the Covenant is out of luck. \n\nSings-With-Reed saw to that. She's joined with the coral now, and I won't let either one come to harm.
The heart is yours, yet the coral lives. Once I saw it was dying, I had no choice but to merge myself with the coral. \n\nWe are one now: one tree with the same roots.
Did you find the bones and bless them?
Look at all my beautiful kwama! Their beady little eyes, the gentle pulsing of their abdomens. \n\nI can't thank you enough!
Girvas blames the Argonians for taking his daughter? What would that accomplish?\n\nMake this right, traveler.
You ready? Then blow the horn and give that Orc skeever the sharp end.
Oh! My lovely Nord flower. Abducted by Orcs!
I hope you believe my plan is the most reasonable one. It benefits us all in ways that may not be immediately apparent.
Place the skulls on the altar. That will bring Khralek to investigate.\n\nThen kill him, as he killed me.
Did you find Hjolm?
Thanks for your help with all this Maulborn nonsense. Maybe things will get back to normal around here now.
Vartis was headed toward the mouth of the pass west of here.
Ah, you're back. What did you discover?
That mad Telvanni thinks the Argonians took his daughter?\n\nAs my father used to say, Girvas is walking on thin ice in spring.
<You've emptied this chest.>
Hm. Don't get too many seasoned warriors showing up as new recruits, but we'll take you.\n\nOr were you here about something else?
Go. Let the spirits of the past guide you.
I'm sorry you had to witness that. My friend shows great concern for Narsis. Sometimes greater than my own.\n\nWhat can I do for you?
You're back! Do you have the antidote?
You have returned. Is he …?
I ran so fast that I nearly wore the scales from my feet.
You did what was necessary.
Sadal and I are ready to make the sacrifice.
Well done, soldier. Soon we will slay these Nede guar.
The matriarch lives? That's good to hear!\n\nLord Garvas will want to know immediately. You should speak to him at the stead to the north.
Misguided spawn of a rotten egg! Meddling in affairs that don't concern you.
You startled me! Are you just playing tricks on me, dryskin?
What news of my sons? Has Bjorick returned?
I'm going to make one more patrol of the perimeter. I'll meet you back inside the manor house.
Thanks for helping me out of that spot of trouble. I'll follow you to the monastery and help protect the Tear.
We must warn the hold of the imminent Goblin attack. \n\nGo warn Hrogar. I'll find Gar and Bjorick and try to get them to safety.
You've brought my son back to me. I can't thank you enough.
So that's what happened! I remember many mages dying, and there was something about a shield spell. \n\nI grew weak holding him in place. Then there was a bright light. Everything fades after that.
Get moving! Balreth isn't exactly cooperating with us.
Drathyra tells me your actions saved my wife from a painful death.\n\nI am in your debt. And I honor my debts.
The shalk had me trapped up here like nix-hounds hunting a lizard.\n\nThank Vivec the brutes were too stupid to try going around the rock. They just stood down there and snapped at my feet.
The soldiers are gone? Thank Almalexia!\n\nI thought no one would come before they got tired of taunting me. They kept talking about what they'd do with their knives.
Surveying the battlefield? There will be many more. \n\nThe Covenant has only retreated. Now we must drive them out.

The well leads to Shornhelm's waterways. It's a tight squeeze, but it will take you all the way up to the last house in Shornhelm's town limits.\n\nThe only creature you'll need to watch out for are leeches. I'm sure you've dealt with worse.

Did you hear? Martin decided to enlist! Though I will worry for his safety, I really do think this is the best thing for him, and for all of us.\n\nI don't know if you had a hand in this, but if you did, thank you.
Spells and sigils. Bah! Nords don't think much of that sort of thing.
Garyn Indoril awaits you.
Be wary of those who walk in the otherworld. They won't take kindly to your presence.
A fine job. Most of the herd has come home.
You are not one of the women from the Hlaalu outpost. What do you want?
You walked the Coiled Path and survived! Has the Ghost Snake spoken?
So, you were able to talk some sense into Martin? I'm glad.\n\nYou did a good thing. Not many people would take the time to help a common criminal like Martin Dathieu.
Search the tombs to the northeast.\n\nI will slip into the center of Othrenis.
Sound the whistle in front of the kinhouse. Our people will do the rest.
She just stood there, shaking! Ha! After it was all done, she still held her quivering arms out to hold me. \n\nOh, it was profoundly delightful. Who thought death would provide such entertainment?
Yes, it was delightful to watch her grovel. She looked like she wanted to scream and cry, but she was too stunned to speak.\n\nOh, that oaf is here again. How tiresome, Eanen.
The guards heard fighting. I assume you found more inside than just "evidence."
Just give me that letter and let me go. No need to get involved in things that don't concern you, right?\n\nPlease! Let me go!
Head to the Obsidian Gorge and report to Commander Renli.\n\nWe'll join you there shortly. Make sure you leave some of those Maulborn bastards for me. I don't want to miss all the fun.
Speak to him, if you wish. You might as well ask questions of the sea.
The warm-blood is skillful and cunning.
The curse has been driven back into the reliquary. The afflicted are recovering. \n\nI assume we have you to thank for this?
You look a little bloodstained. Smells like Khajiiti blood. Smells like … victory!
Hurry it up already! If I get caught for this, I'll be sweeping streets in Wayrest for the rest of my career.
I thought you were different. Please, just go.\n\nWe'll find my egg-sister and the others on our own.
Can't you see we're in the middle of a very important meeting? The fate of Narsis hangs in the balance, I dare say!
You help me disrupt this meeting and save these people's lives, and I'll find out what Madras knows.\n\nCatch those rats and bring them back here. There's no time to waste.
So, half of Narsis must vanish and plague must threaten the city before Ralden comes to his senses?\n\nAnd it takes an outsider to make him understand. Perhaps my friend isn't fit to lead any more.
I'll gather the guards and follow in your path.\n\nNow go. Find your ally and let's finish this.
I am obliged to call you and that merchant friends of the clan.
I still can't figure out why that Urano fellow kept asking to buy our lumber. He kept saying, "If you sold it to me, how long until you could leave town?"
You did fine work against the Maulborn. Fine work. And without a contract! I'm somewhat impressed.
Excellent. The guardians are here. Time to bind this creature.
Ah, you're a good drinking mate, friend. Come back and join us again sometime.
<<1>> made a <<2>>? Great!\n\nMake sure the survivors get what they need to get out of the keep.
Boril will send me away. I can't blame him. \n\nI'm grateful he didn't tell the workers what I did.
Did you find any clues? Why would someone poison Deepcrag Den?
The Three have not forgotten us.
Go in peace, stranger, but be quick about it.
Make your way south to the reliquary. Talk to <<1>>. He'll know what to do.
Tell <<1>> of our success. \n\nI now return to my eternal task.
The portal is open. The next move is yours.
The portal is open. \n\nDo not delay, Your living warmth is a burden to me.
This pass is too important to allow it to fall into the Maulborn's hands.
If the General seems a bit strange to you, please be discreet. He hasn't been himself lately.
The manifests—did you get them?
So, you have my items, yes? Which do you think I should have?
If the sword had a foot, it would probably be tapping it impatiently.
You're back! Any luck finding my cargo?
Glad to have you on our side. Wipe them out.

<<1>>'s runners told me the Worm Cultists wouldn't surrender. Unfortunate, but no fault of yours. <<2>> is in your debt.\n\nIn truth, I feared the Worm Cult lieutenants went to our cellars on purpose, to work dark magics from within our village.
Tevynni is in charge of things now. But I still manage the stock.
Grim tidings, if <<1>> is missing.
Shor's bones, it's good to see you! The Dominion, right under our noses. Damned insidious.\n\nI have to warn Servyna and Heita-Meen. Quick, untie me!
Do you need me to talk slower? Check … the body … of Ruvali's dead husband. Make sure it doesn't move.
Death is not the worst of fates. Some would consider the necromancers fortunate.
Well done, my ally. Always remember you have the ear of this Dres grandmaster, should you need it.
We're all indebted to you for saving the grandmaster's son.
Necromancers deserve no better.\n\nGo talk to <<1>>, and your eyes will be opened.

This place was built on suffering. If we continue to enslave other races, they'll never stop rising against us.\n\nIt took the devastation of my home and the death of my beloved Tiril to show me this.
You confronted the Dominion at Murkwater? We have a similar problem of our own.
I knew you'd succeed where most had failed.
You've accomplished great things here. Perhaps when future generations commune with the Hist, they'll see your actions.
I keep the Hist sap warm by the fire. Otherwise, it's too thick to drink.\n\nOh, and you must drink the entire bowl at once. If not, we'll learn what you prefer for breakfast. Ha!
Well, you're a blue reed in yellow peat. From out of town, yes? Yes.\n\nYou're in luck, blue reed. Gold runs dry on long journeys, but I've got just the thing to moisten your purse.
Ah, first customer. You see what I've got. Buy if you want.
You have not "pleased the Hist" today. Rather, you fulfilled the Hist's expectations. A subtle distinction, but necessary to comprehend the Hist.
You hammer every day and night, but I haven't seen you smash your hand once!\n\nAre you ready for your journeyman test?
Don't worry—we'll make sure this Ithis Omalor makes it to Mournhold in one piece.\n\nWe're just going to make sure he knows how we feel about him. You know, so there's no confusion.
The last fool that visited us managed to offend almost everyone in the village. Please don't say you're here to finish the job.
<Ra-shadda cannot speak. He's gagged.>
I don't know what to say.
Yeah, thanks. I won't forget your help. Promise.
Saryvn here has told me an interesting tale. Is he telling the truth? He says you were involved.

What was I thinking? Look at this place—a few shabby buildings and a wreck of a ship. It's not a town. It's an overgrown tavern. \n\nThe ship's hold is filled with drunks looking for a fight. Such are the fine citizens of Alten Corimont.
I've seen what the plague does to a body. I won't let it take me. \n\nBut if the wards were destroyed ….
I can see you mean business! I won't press my luck.
Excellent! A person who walks instead of rolls.\n\nCome on, let's get out of here.
Did you recover our stolen relics?
Go see what the fool has to say. He's out on deck. And don't waste my money.
Captain Valec should be inside the keep.
Thank you for your service.
Why are you still here? You have a spy to expose!
Have you found any signs of our missing pilgrims?
I don't believe it. I thought the Sentinels would make mincemeat out of you.
Don't risk your neck on my account.
You really do want to help. An outlander willing to give us a chance. Will wonders never cease?

So the Khajiit didn't lie. I pegged you to make off with the money. I misjudged you.\n\nHere's your Dark Elf. I expect the Dominion's prize will be delivered as payment for my largess. And I have yet another present for you.
Praise Vivec, Halva found you. Whatever's in my home … it isn't my wife.
Yet another murder in Stormhold ….
I heard Gethis died. No surprise there.
The wasps like you now. They shouldn't attack you anymore. Not unless you hit them first.\n\nThey're smart creatures. Certainly smarter than Khajiit!
It's terrible about Gethis. Stormhold used to be a good place to live. We don't deserve this.
Such a loss, all the dead … lost.
You're back, but without the keystone. What happened?
Ah, it is my new friend and leader! What can S'jash do for you?
You're back! Did you manage to deal with our Dwarven problem?
Glad you found the vicecanon. I see he was right about you.
It is over, then? \n\nAnd … the Ashkhan?
Vivec bless your steps, recruit. With talented crafters in the Halls, there's no challenge we can't overcome.
No, get away! \n\nOh, it's you. Did it work? Are they free?
Who thought a letter could perform such miracles?
You've proven yourself.\n\nAnd believe me, that isn't easy to do in my eyes.
Looking for something with a little boost? \n\nIf you have questions, feel free to ask. My brother runs the shop, but I'll answer what I can.
Find Humauta. If there's anyone who knows what to do about the Dominion soldiers occupying my village, it's her.
Please, leave this one to her sorrow.
Rumblings from the mountain have us all on edge. Balreth is up there somewhere. \n\nI hope you've brought good news.
I thought you would talk to Mavos. I did not expect you to bring him along.
Have you sealed the Scamp caves?
The artifact is ready. Do not unseal it until it's time.

For the courtesy <<1>> has shown me, I am honored to have you meet my wife. She tires easily, so please make your visit brief.\n\nYou know, I would be content to remain here with her forever, if it were possible.
<<1>> knows what remains to be done. The moment is almost upon us. I think … I think I'm ready.
You've got both of the essences? Quickly, make your way to <<1>>. She must be ready to perform the ritual by now.
<<1>> will want to see you right away. I'm sure she's ready to perform the ritual now.\n\nBy Azura, you must be a brave one!
We have the essences of wrath and fire from the Daedra. We have the hearts of the dead. We've completed our preparations.\n\nThe ritual can begin.
I hope you have good news for me.
Did you kill the Dreamers? Were you able to recover the crystal shards?
That'll show those cultist, with thier stupid chanting and crystal stealing!
So, where are they?
Well, have you taken it to those cultists and reclaimed my property?
You smell of Oblivion. Have you been killing daedra for me? Please say you were successful…
Take a seat by the fire.\n\nPresently, Almalexia herself will speak to you.
Did you smash a few of those dung-guzzling Worm Cultists yet? No? Oh, well.
Ah, just in time. The Sacred Lady asked us to watch for you.
It's rare for someone to have the honor of a private audience with the Sacred Lady.\n\nI admit, I'm envious. A clerk like myself isn't likely to get that sort of attention.
Spread the fertilizer over the roots of our Hist. As long as I'm with you, our guards will not trouble you.
I won't forget what you've done for us.
Sotha Sil values intelligence and ingenuity. He builds. He maintains. He is the master of his creations.\n\nHe shall test these qualities in you.
What in the nine holds is going on? <<1>> is missing!
The news is most dire. <<1>> is missing!
<<<1>> does not react to your presence.>
Haven't you gone through the portal yet? <<1>> must be waiting for you.
Did you find anything suspicious?
Have I convinced you, then? Are you ready to join up?
I sense you've been meddling with Elven magic. What happened?
Perfect. Just perfect. Julianos must be laughing his divine posterior off.
You won't tell anyone I tried to dig through stone, will you?
The Lion Guard is in your debt, stranger. \n\nI am in your debt.
I really need some rest. When are we going to get out of here?
Gales of Kynareth! We have a working Daedric containment cell!\n\nI'll be the envy of every mage from here to High Rock. Of course, I'll tell them you helped.
Now what? That cult killed all our guards. We'll never get out of here alive!
Be warned. Worm cultists are notorious for slaying travelers and turning them into undead slaves.
Please find my sister, landstrider.\n\nAnd if it's in your power, see that she returns alive.
Has that insect been squashed?
You're new? It's my duty to warn you: there's been a series of murders and kidnappings.\n\nI'd wrap up your business here quickly. Oh, and welcome to Stormhold.
Quickly, speak with Elder Seven-Bellies. Pash-Riha has not returned and his concern grows.
The whole temple shook! What happened?
I've never seen such a thing. That Orc survived what no mortal should.
What do you say? Do you have what it takes? Are you ready to join the fight?
Fine goods for all chain-breakers! C'mon over and take a look, comrade.
I hope you'll be able to get into the manse. If the grandmaster's son isn't rescued, we'll never get rid of the Vanguard.
Ah, it's you again. The child whose soul was stolen.\n\nMy Lady Almalexia is grateful for the aid you gave <<1>>.
Talk to Varon about the next steps. All my brilliant ideas at the moment just involve avoiding the plague.
Please, you must let me take this stuff back to my family, so they don't starve.
I think they're all here!
Thanks to you, the corruption of the swamp will wash away with the spring flood. \n\nI can't wait to get back to scavenging trash again.

Serien plans to keep us out with magic, eh? Well, he's about to face one of the greatest mages in the Pact.\n\nTo take down this ward, Garyn and I will need two foci. They're probably in the storage areas in the courtyard.
Thanks for rescuing our scavengers from those crazed plants.\n\nWe could still use your help. Well, <<1>> asked me to ask for your help, if you've got time.
That was quite a show you gave us. The Dominion certainly won't forget it.
Are you here to help?
The fires of retribution warm the heart, don't they?
The Dominion won't forget this day.
Thanks for helping out with those stranglers. They're ferocious.
You've been gone for some time. How'd it go?
Head into the Ashlanders' tunnel. Use a pickaxe to weaken the supports. We'll hold them off here.\n\nI won't wish you good luck. That's for children and Altmer. I'd rather trust in your skill.
You brought our leader back to us. He may be a bit rough and tumble, but I don't know what we would do without Dolril.
I will go to the top of the xanmeer and begin the ritual. See you there after you've placed the potions.
My family's townhouse is nearby. I'll meet you there.
Alchemists pay handsomely for kwama cuttle.
Gah! Where did you come from?

You must learn Vox's secrets before you can hope to face her as an equal.\n\nSearch for the three anima archives within. Let them pull you into the realm of memory. Let them show you how this little drama came to be.
Did you do it? Yuck! What's all over your boots?
Somehow … somehow I feel better! I don't know what happened, but I feel great!
The cave's smack in the middle of <<1>>. The Dominion's locked it tighter than a High Elf's fundament. Might have to knock a few heads to get past them.
While <<1>> recovers, we should plan to recover this <<2>> from the Dominion. What do you know of its whereabouts?
I need a moment to recover. <<1>> will be eager to hear what happened in there.
Thank you for helping me. I didn't want to become snake food.\n\nRagara and the others are outside, if you're looking for them.
Face down in the sand isn't the way I wanted to go out. Divines bless you for saving me.
They didn't pay us enough for this job.
Do I still look poisoned? I feel different. Gods, I bet they laid eggs in my head!
It seems you've managed to round up my clumsy mercenaries. Thanks for saving them.
How could Neposh have done such a stupid thing?

Looking for the heretic woman? She went into the temple. She's probably haranguing the curate.\n\nShe says she wants to avoid bloodshed, but that's not really in our hands, is it? It's her kin outside the walls preparing to attack, not us.
If you're here about the job, I'm afraid it's already been taken. I can't afford to pay for the same job twice.
You stopped the skin-stealers in <<1>>. I can go home!
These ward stones are the only thing stopping us. Disable them, if you can.
I've betrayed everyone. I've betrayed the entire Pact.
You've started me on the path to redemption. \n\nBy the Three, I will not let the Pact down. Sadal will be bound again!
Thank you for doing what my brothers and I could not.
Thanks for helping clear out that mystic pollution.\n\nWe're back to normal. Just the usual filth from upstream.
Wait! What's happening! I protest! I protest!
You return.
Your results?
You're far too delightful for the horrible death awaiting you. After all, we've grown so close. Such a pleasure should be mine alone to deliver.
It's amazing what you've been able to accomplish.
What tales did the dead men tell, my friend?
Find a way to kill <<1>> and I'll reward you handsomely.
Back so soon? Are the Stonefalls dead drops done?
We wish you luck. I hope you can find my father.
We heard a commotion outside. What happened? Did you find my father?
Now you know the gift Shadowscales bestow upon the worthy—that life itself contains no guarantee beyond suffering.
I'll petition the Night Mother. She's granted me the right to duel you before the enclave.
Keep an eye out for my fool son while you're out there, will you?
I pity the prisoners, but without the keystones, we might not be able to defeat the Dominion.\n\nI received a message. The Dominion made their move against <<1>>.
Do you think she truly loved me? The words we exchanged, they couldn't be said without ….\n\nWhat am I saying … none of it was true.
You found her, didn't you? I felt it. The rain and sun blended together. \n\nKnowing she and I will meet again comforts me. Thank you.
Did you hear? Someone murdered <<1>>.\n\nIf you find out who it was, stick a sword in their guts. We can't offer a bounty, but you'd have our thanks.
Time to go. Always more scouting to do—there's still a war on. I hope you find your path well, my friend.
What happened? If <<1>> is with you, where are the others?
Hurry, Mavos cannot hold Balreth much longer.
Search the mud piles. If the dreugh captured the tree-minders, that's where we'll find them.
Now you know the gift Shadowscales receive from the worthy—that pain may be conquered by ignoring one sense and embracing another.
I'd rather be a warrior with broken fingers than a man with a broken mind.\n\nPlease, set us free.
You set my companions free. What power do you bring to this realm?\n\nCould you release me as well?
In defeating Vox, you have shown the world what the Dunmer are capable of. You honor the memory of Saint Veloth.
Hurry, my friend. The Goblinization spell matrix I cast on him will only last so long.\n\nI don't want to think what would happen if his appearance changed in the middle of that camp.
The Spell Gem will get you into camp, but make sure to avoid the clan's spiders. They'll see right through the illusion and attack.
I ran so fast. I'm still out of breath. Goblins are surprisingly quick when they have something to chase!
The braziers burn atop the Xanmeers' pinnacles. Tell me, what have you learned of the Dominion's plans?
He's gone … he died for the eggs ….\n\nDid it work? Are they safe?
Have you seen our agony? We're not like this. It's torment to endure this way.
I haven't lost a man, but the Scamps have lost twenty. \n\nNow we just need to kill this Brother-thing. It's a good day, my friend.
Go, harrow the prisoners until they divulge their secrets.
We've succeeded where that withered root Doshia failed, comrade.\n\nHere. I will open a portal for us to return.
The last time I saw my father was at the temple.
I'm sure that even in this disaster, Tidyn would see to his duties. Check the town hall.
My brother told us what you did.\n\nSpeak to us no more.
Do I detect the bouquet of <<1>>?
Please speak to the grandmaster. He's sure to listen to the hero of Fort Virak.
Beautiful, wasn't it? <<1>> wanted to consume the power of the Hist, but instead he was consumed.
Sorry, but if you're here to buy iron, the metalworks is running low. A minor labor dispute, that's all.\n\nCome back in a few days, and I'll give you a good deal on iron ingots.
You come to buy from this one, yes? Grandmaster gives us special license to sell and trade. Many fine wares.
Welcome back from the depths, comrade. <<1>> told me you'd have something for me?
You are back. Impressive. Aelif still cannot see what the godless Dwarves might have had.\n\nWhat would they have that <<1>> would want?
Find them. Find their ashes. I'll never find peace until we're together once more.
I felt it! When you used the keystone to free us, it was like shackles fell from my neck.
I see the trophies of some fearsome creatures hanging from your pack. It takes skill to hunt such prey.
Don't worry, outsider. I'll have the antidote ready.
Sithis be with you for purging the corruption from our swamp!\n\nOnce the miasma clears, we can get back to the hunt.
What happened to your spider? \n\nGo catch another one. And try not to be so careless.
That vision! A Dremora woman, talking about Merric. Why would she want my hapless companion?
Their camp is not far. Look for something reeking of their scent. Old clothes, bedding, or the like.
You've returned. I take it you were successful?
Just disturb that nest and the angry kwama warrior will come running. Once you deal with the pitiful creature, we can get out of here.
My sister has a knack for attracting trouble. I'm starting to get worried.
When you see your Nord friends, ask them to send troops and aid. We have plenty of relics.
I can't believe we survived that! You made the right choice, I think. Anything else would have been disaster.
I can't believe you did that … but you've done some pretty amazing things already.
What took you so long? As you can see, I've gotten … well, bogged down.\n\nGo talk to Saervild while I extricate myself.
You've returned. How long ago did we speak? Why have you come?\n\nMy hatchling … something about my hatchling ….
We'll figure out how to banish the rest of these Daedra, you can count on it.
It warms my heart to see the sacred skull back in its reliquary.
Comrade! Thank you for coming so quickly.\n\nWe have need of you. Will you fight by our side?
Stendarr keep you safe, comrade.
The others are safe, but more importantly, you rescued our scrolls, yes?
Look what they've done to the books. They're ruined. \n\nAll that knowledge. Lost.
So much screaming. So much fire.
You heard the Guildmaster. \n\nSees-All-Colors. She murdered Jofnir.
Act quickly. The Dagonites are defiling the sanctuary.
You got an invitation? I can't believe someone just gave you one. I'm going to have mine framed.
Must I repeat myself? This vessel is only for those who have been invited to attend the Shad Astula Academy of Magic.
Great. Just great. This is my luck.
Thank you again, my fine, fine friend. \n\nDon't worry about me. I'm going to sit here and inspect every one of these bottles to make sure they're all still good. For the selling.
We're going to Oblivion to deal with an insane Daedric lord.\n\nNot the best way for a father and son to bond, is it?

Each student undergoes a test to make sure the invitation reached the right person. Students who fail are sent home.\n\nThose three must pass their tests. Morrowind and the Pact need them. I have foreseen it!
Were you able to find any supplies?
I suppose you take this wand and, you know, focus. Your magic. On the clucks.\n\nFrankly, something doesn't feel right about this.
Stay sharp sailor, we're on a very delicate mission here.
What is that thing? B'vek, it wants to eat us!
Hadmar takes little friends back now. I'm sure they can be turned back into big-friend students.
What's that distinctive bottle I see peeking from your pack?
I should've expected trouble. Damn that Daedric Prince.
How was your research trip with the Guildmaster, comrade?
Return to Shad Astula whenever you want. \n\nBring us tales of your exploits. Tell us how you deal with uncanny threats and soul-crushing perils.
Since merging with the Hist, I feel so alive. I've made the right choice.
Are you ready at last? Carethil lurks beneath my roots, scarring them with hatred.
You've been asleep a long time. <<1>> has asked about you—several times, in fact.\n\nWhat happened?
Thank the Three, someone who looks like they can handle themselves in a fight!\n\nMy husband's in danger. Please, help us!
Are you ready? Aelif is ready to get out of the city.
Have you found my son? Others return from the bog, but not <<1>>.
Merric will know what to do. This one is planning to practice her bladework while you two are working inside.
I miss the master general. Tall Papa watch over him.
Please don't damage him … much. He's very dear to me.
Do you bring moisture? What have you learned?
Toll is paid. Paid!
Check in at a guild hall from time to time. I'll do my best to contact you when I've finished.
For someone of your caliber, this mission should be simple, though not without its challenges.
Perhaps you should pay more attention to the task at hand.
Go! Our duke awaits.
The toll! The toll! The featherless one has paid the toll.
Featherless approaches! Approaches!
The Fang crawled into my mind! What have I done? I can't stop it from gnawing my thoughts.\n\nHelp me!
I, for one, am happy with what you did.\n\nBack to working with my hands instead of abusing Goblins. That's much better for an honest day's work.
You're wet, and you stink. You have my reagents?
I don't feel so good.
Have you spoken to the Sage yet? She's very wise. And forgiving! So forgiving.
Play the tune on the instruments hanging from the wall. After I've heard it once, I should be able to play it.
What did you find in the vault?
Do not worry. If the Reach attempt to take Shor's Stone from within, they will fail.
Thanks for freeing us. Can't wait to get out of this place.
Do you have my crystal shards?
It's you. Modified rapture.
Have you defeated <<1>>?
What are you doing standing around here? Go out and find those crystal shards - the realm depends on it!
If you don't find those shards we're all doomed!
Is he dead yet?
Thanks again for helping me with the Dreamers.
<cough> Please I do not have much time. Please retrive the crystals.
Thank Kyne you made it out alive!
Don't leave me like this.
Free me from these cursed vines!
What would Lodunn have done without me, eh? He'd be dead for sure.
The Reach need to be wiped out!
You have the books? Next time we're at a tavern, I'll buy you two drinks!
The other students are waiting to say goodbye. They're on the docks.

Thank you for getting me out of that mine. My husband and I are indebted to you. \n\nOnce things calm down, I'll get you that mead I promised. And it'll be good stuff from Hodmar's private stock, assuming the Goblins haven't stolen it.
Those bastards are to somethng. You should check them out.
No! Get away!\n\nOh, wait. It's you.
Thanks again for freeing me.\n\nNow, you should go off and have more adventures. I think I've had my fill of those.
I knew to expect you, but not one of <<1>>'s soldiers. I take it she's your prisoner? You've interrogated her, yes?
We go flying now! To the big rock! Whoosh!
Still got your nose. Greenhorn.
Have you seen <<1>>? Our scouts spotted the Dominion's main force!
Good luck, my friend.
Please hurry. If the vicecanons arrive before we get the totem, they'll just kill or enslave the Goblins again.\n\nThis was supposed to be a clear stream, but it is now fouled with blood.
Time grows as short as a winter's day. We must act before it's too late.
You've found the others? Was there no sign of Adana?
You saved Narir, thank you! Though none of us will live long now that Sinmur's back.
Please, don't give up, I just know Raena's alive in there, you have to save her!
<This Nord was recently killed. His belongings are in disarray, but a runestone remains clutched in his hand.>
Honor to you and your house, stranger. Have you come to deal with the ills of our poor mine?\n\nIt's a terrible business all around, but you could certainly help us make it less terrible.
This wound isn't getting any better, not with you just standing around.\n\nAre you going to take care of business, or do you need me to hold your hand?
Did you come from the Serk? We sent a guard over there to check on some disturbing rumors we've been hearing.
That's a new look for you. Not certain I like it.
<The body is still warm. The cultist was killed recently.>
Tell Dajaheel what we've learned. I'll look for one of the ritual sites.
My joy, my heart … <<1>> lives! Though who knows when I will be able to provide her and her father safe shelter, at least they both live.
Welcome, welcome, to the Circus of Cheerful Slaughter! \n\nStep right up, my mortal friend. The show is about to begin, and you're the star!
By my father's blade! Is that a spirit?\n\nPerhaps … perhaps it knows where the Cartulary is. Let's get it and get out of here!
Please, traveler. Do what you can for my family.
Great timing, traveler. I won't last long if I don't tend to this wound.\n\nBut … my girls are still out here. Will you look for them?
Pa told us to run. So we ran. I've never been so scared.
Father will know what to do. Grandad taught him everything he knew about surviving in the Rift.
Thank you for your service to the Mages Guild.
I was told I might find you here. I have an urgent message for you from <<1>>.
Thank you. You didn't have to come to my defense, but I am grateful.
<<1>> ordered me to make a list of damage. Because it's important to the Dark Elves to know how many pigs exploded under the giant's feet versus how many burned alive.\n\nBah.

What treachery? The Enchanter claims my liege lord's chambers! How could this ….\n\nBy Meridia's light, I recollect it. The Enchanter decreed us slay our liege lord. We gave chase, our blades flickering like fading Varla stones, and ….
Please help me! I saw you douse the fires. You have to stop the Daedra!
If you want to help us, burn us; otherwise, get out of here and stop Serien.
Please, take the <<1>> to the tree-minder and see if she can help.
I will not speak to one who enslaves others.\n\nLeave. Your reward is forfeit.
Speak to your Dark Elf friends, not to me.\n\nRevel in the gold you earned with the flesh of others.
Well? Get moving! What kind of chateau mouser are you, sitting here while the rat runs free?
I cut down a Reach dog, and saw the smoke column reflected in his dead eyes. Nice work, ya great horker.
Is this the best place to recruit extra hands outside Stormhold? Unbelievable. It's a pit.\n\nAfter this, I go to Bogmother. As if the mother of bogs is a place I want to be.
I must attend to my students' bodies in the antechamber. Please, return what <<A:1>> took from them so they can find peace.

Don't worry about me, friend. It'll take more than losing a foot to send Hoknir to Sovngarde.\n\nWalking back to town was an experience, though. I think I blacked out a few times. Thank Kyne for mead, eh?
I hate running, but we don't have a choice.
My comrades have returned. I erect the spine of gratitude. You are a hero today.
I hope summoning that Dragon priest works. It's the only idea I've got for getting into the barrow.
There were so many of them. We scattered. We thought we'd be safe.
How many times must I explain this? Place the runestones at the entrance to the barrow. Go!
It's the giant crystal above me!
This gives me so much to think about. I'm not sure I'll ever understand.
My brother never was the sharpest sword on the rack, but he's all I've got left.
Thanks for freeing us. Sure will be great to get out of this place.
Head inside. I'll call the others once the room is clear.
I can't wait to get out of here.
Our family is back together. I can never thank you enough.
Thank Kyne! My boat sank off the coast in a storm. It was unnatural. I saw colors I've never seen before. \n\nI drifted for hours on a plank. I thought I was dead.
They're alive! And they're not furry anymore!
Unbelievable! We've spent years searching for the Spinner's shrine, and these filthy creatures have been sitting right on top of it all along!
Go, go on now! He's not frozen anymore.
You've returned! Do you have the book?
Is it over? Are they gone? I don't think I hear them in my head anymore.\n\nYour face still drips with blood.
<<<1>> barks excitedly.>
Free others, then meet me here.
You look good in your new outfit. \n\nJust remember: those wolves down there will sniff through your disguise. Steer clear of them.
Have you spoken to Rana? Seen what we're up against?

A flesh-walker joins our dreams. A welcome diversion, small one, before we rejoin the void.\n\nThough we soon depart, the vicecanon carries our thoughts within her. You must follow, lest we drag you to the void with us.
My friend. You've done so much for Valaste and I. I couldn't let you leave without one last gift.
Admit it … you were surprised, weren't you? The look on your face was precious!
Lead on. Aelif follows.
Who could have known we'd be standing here like this, my friend? You destroyed an artifact of the Prince of Lies. And I … I'm the new leader of the Fighters Guild.
What is that humming sound? Ah! You possess a keystone, yes?\n\nWe long thought them connected to the Hist. Perhaps now we're within the Hist itself, we can know for certain.
The fortress-city of Sancre Tor is one of Cyrodiil's most well-known and regaled sites. It was risky—but clever—for Sai Sahan to have hidden the Amulet in such obvious, plain sight.
Ah, Skyrim! It's been some time since I've seen its people … and its snow.
Look, stranger. I don't deal with your type.
Please, will you help me? I work for the merchant, Damar. He needs your help!
We're in your debt. Most of the refugees already owe you their lives.
You had to go and be the hero at Silaseli, didn't you? Now the area's packed with free roaming beggars, cutting into my margins.
<<1>>. <<2>> was missing you.\n\nThank you for bringing my family back together.
I wish I could feel safe in town, but with the Covenant in Bal Foyen, nowhere is safe.
Where did the Covenant come from?
We return to the Dragon's embrace. You are a guidepost on the river's edge.
You have denied the Daggers our lives. Moisture to you.
Dammit, Colors. The province generals were very clear … but I've known her for so long. What will we do?
Kill her! Such lies she tells! \n\nSees-All-Colors killed Jofnir. She must die!
Thank you for sparing my life, comrade, but my scales are dry with fear.\n\nI believe the council is about to unspare me.
Damn the Covenant. My family was happy.\n\nWell, maybe not happy, but they were content.
That crazy Dark Elf has the heart of a shark.
Bring me the giant's toe as proof that the deed is done. And when you get back, I may have a treat waiting for you!
Did you do it? Did you burn the remains of the giants? And did it work? Are they going to leave us alone now?
Ha! That is a thing of beauty. Kazok's head never looked better!
With the power of the giants, nothing will be able to stop us!
Enter the portal. <<1>> isn't going to kill himself.
So, how did it go?
Has the target met an untimely end?
I've already sampled some of Roruld's first batch of mead. It's very good.
Was your search successful?
Nothing can replace my poor Inga, but what you've done has certainly raised my spirits.
So glad to hear you got those fires lit. I hope Davon's Watch got the warning in time.
The wolves are large and vicious, but their pelts are thick and warm. Good hunting.
You should be able to find Kyne's Breath by the rune stones scattered throughout the grove.

All of my soldiers need to be at full strength before we continue. Head back to the house my soldiers have barricaded. See if they need any more assistance, then come find me. \n\nWe'll figure out what to do with Ormi then.
Find Sahun at the tavern in Windhelm. Since he lost his brother, he's been drowning himself in drink.\n\nI'll be fine here. I just need to catch my breath.
I was a fool to turn your help down when you asked for it.\n\nBy Kyne, I was an even bigger fool to turn my back on my family when they needed me the most. I'll not lose sight of what matters again.
You're not from the Covenant. What are you doing here? It makes no difference. We need all the help we can get.
Comrade, <<1>> has sent me to find you.
We're here. The villagers are safe for the moment.\n\nBut the Covenant's still coming. We've got to get word to Davon's Watch.
Is it true? Did the Daggers get over the walls?\n\nEverywhere I go, they attack. Except Bleakrock. I wasn't there.
They're fighting in the residential quarter, and I'm stuck here.\n\nI better not miss the whole battle.
You're back. Tell me, is King Jorunn well?
How could I have let her do this? Oh, Gena!
The graveyard and cave are to the southwest. I hope we don't have any more skeletons before you can solve this!
I hear the Daggers have siege engines just outside the wall.\n\nIf a catapult shot hits my tent, will I hear it coming? Will father have anything left to bury?
Please, kill it quickly.
You're good news on a foul day, my friend.
Thank the Divines you came when you did. You made the difference here.
Congratulations! For someone who smells of southern decadence, you're fast and strong.\n\nThe race is yours, Champion of Windhelm!
Our business is done. Are you expecting something else?
It was a nightmare! A nightmare!
Well? Do you wish to train or not?
What's taking so long?  Go out there and get my <<m:1>> back!
Thanks for coming. We could have used you sooner, but there's no point dwelling on what might have been.
This was a message from my brother. One I wasn't meant to survive. I feared this day would come.
What news do you bring?
I see you've been asking around, that's good. Do you know what you need to do?
I see you met Thane Oda Wolf-Sister.
I'm glad I'm out of that ridiculous cage.
The Stormfists won't take us by surprise again. You can be sure of that.
I've been watching you, and you have been looking around this boat pretty well. What have you learned?
Have you any idea? Ooh, this is so exciting!
Ok, so what have you discovered and do you have any questions?
I hear you've been working with Thane Mera. How exciting!\n\nMight I ask what you've been doing? No? Very well, then.
Threads are falling into place again. The warp and weft align perfectly in the story!
You've started the story! I thought <<1>> lost in her own world by now. She must want you to play the part!
As I've already told the others, we must look for <<1>> soon, or there's no hope of finding her.\n\nWho will tell the Green Lady her sister's gone then? Who?
I saw you wreaking havoc among the Orcthane's troops. Most impressive!

The totem of Y'ffre is a thing of legend, with many tales woven into its essence. If you use it to fight the Worm Cult's creation, you may yet survive.\n\nSpinner Indinael is counting on you. I hope both of your stories will come to a safe conclusion.
The Worm Cult piled the spriggans' corpses like so much cordwood. Their disrespect knows no bounds.\n\nBurn what's left of the spriggans. You must deny the necromancers the heartwood.

Take down as many Worm Cultists as you like on your way through the cave! They deserve a thousand times more for what they've done!\n\nAs for the creature, use the totem of Y'ffre on it once it's weakened. If you don't, it'll just revive again.
May our humble offerings bring Sheor's mercy upon us. Then, we feast!
You need to use the shalk glad to burn away these roots!
I need those gems! Quickly, now.
Z'en would abandon me in my time of need? After all this, he gives me nothing?
I will mourn my lost friends and fellow workers for a long time.
The singing. The screaming. It was horrible.\n\nThe screaming, not the singing. I rather liked the singing.
I'm not sure we'll ever feel safe here again.
All this death, destruction. It has to stop.
He's gone. I can feel it. His presence faded when you struck him down.\n\nWe don't need to fear his tyranny any longer.
If you wish to speak with Indinael, I suggest you hurry. Something is wrong.

We're going to be famous! We'll have real support and proper recognition! Things are going to be much better for us from now on.\n\nThanks to you. And feel free to use the lift to get out of here whenever you're ready.

Best you do not think too hard about what's in that bottle. Just splash it on the hunters. Every splash saves a life. And don't be stingy. There's a lot more where that came from. \n\nIsn't that right, Cello? Oh yes it is!
This is now your story, where you saved Malabal Tor.
Are you ready to begin the siege of Cradlecrush?
<<1>> was blinded by rage and remorse. He has fallen from the even path, into darkness.
Everything happened so quickly.
Whoever did this will pay!
Let's get out of this place!
Still you pursue me! I tire of your games.\n\nI will call the Hound to take your head as a prize. Begone, before he arrives!
The other spinners wait for you at the <<1>>.
I will be your guide on this journey.

You're right. This is going to work out. I love to go delving without a care, but Raynor can't stand it when everyone mocks him and doesn't take him seriously.\n\nI can understand it. Raynor deserves a little recognition.
Wonderful. These bear steaks will feed a lot of people. Did Old Ironclaw give you any trouble?
Well, you did find a cute little goat for the main course.
The prison's not perfect—yet. But we have time, and Rilis isn't going anywhere.
Smoke fills the sky! From Nimalten to Shor's Stone, the people of the Rift know there's danger coming. Well done, my friend.
Greetings in his name. Always happy to see new faces join us!
So. It is finished.
Not now … sleeping ….
The path is clear, friend of frond and leaf.
What is that stench? Is that coming from you? What did you do, roll around in a wolf den? No offense, but move downwind, please.
<Melril's eyes have glazed over, and his breath hitches. He is not long for Sovngarde.>
As you can see, I am very busy here. Be on your way, please.
Areldur and I will tend to Imiril. Speak to Cirion.
Go to your king. And take the Dreamwalker with you, please.
Shame about the war. Best fishing I ever did was in Skyrim.
Well, we've had a bit of luck!\n\n<<1>> was sniffing around and found some of our props. If we can get the rest back, we won't have to skip our next show!
Don't worry about a thing. I've got everything planned out!
Y'ffre blessed us today. My wife's alive, and we're both back in Deepwoods.
All my fears are coming back, even stronger than before! But Sai needs me. I have to shake this off!\n\nAll right Titanborn, pull yourself together. You can do this.
Do you desire another philosophical discussion?
Alert the heralds. Irnskar's errand runner has returned.
Who are you? Where is <<1>>?
The Three Old Gods watch over this man and grant him a quick, painless journey from this place.
We'll always remember you here, friend. Kyne watch over you!
I'll give you a few minutes to get moving, then I'll see if I can sneak out of the compound. Hopefully, you'll create a large distraction by disrupting the binding stones.

When you disrupt the binding stones with the rune key, the Drublog will likely go berserk. I'll see if I can take a few of them out for you.\n\nI'll make it to the road before they get me, never fear.
You have the soul of Ysgramor and the heart of a giant-killer.\n\nThank you, friend! We'll always remember you.
Selgaard made it home right after you left. Thank you for entering the barrow in his stead.
Collect my burial stones then meet me outside my tomb. The gathered stones may counter their necromantic spells.
I hope your light shines as brightly at Honrich Tower as it has here.
Are the geodes shattered? Please, release those poor souls.
This place is a slaughterhouse! What did you find?
Can't begin to make up for what the Reach bastards have done to my kin. They owe me for the blood paid today.
I accept the King's judgment. Do what you need to. I won't flee. You have my word.
At last. I'd begun to give up hope. Are you a friend to the Bosmer? I cannot see you clearly …. Who are you?
