The Ebonheart Pact is sealed and this threat to Skyrim has ended.\n\nPlease, go and tell my son. Tell him that the battle is won and … tell him about Fildgor.
The storm atronachs congregate whenever the sphere is active for more than a few hours. How fortuitous they carry the thunderstones we need.
Events are spiraling out of control, and as the spinners say, we've "left the story."\n\nWithout you, neither I nor my ambassador would've gotten out of Jathsogur.
You saved Charadin. Bless you!
<Dalaneth looks peaceful in death, despite her many injuries.>
Seems you're worth something after all. Perhaps once the wards are unsealed, they'll consider you a stormwarden recruit.
While you're tracking down the thieves, I'll try to figure out what they took. They can't have made off with everything.
This disaster has convinced me—never leave my library again. Fieldwork is for the young and foolish.

I can never repay you for all you've done. I should throw a grand feast and make you part of my personal guard, but there are still dangers to deal with.\n\nFildgor plans to desecrate my sister's spirit. That must not be allowed to happen.
They're expending a lot of power holding open those portals. Shut them down, and you'll draw Thallik out for sure.
Damn Worms! Driving them out will cost us dearly.\n\nAnd with all that we have accomplished, we still may not have the numbers to win this.
You dare approach me, mortal? I'll carve what's left of you into gaming bones!
You have made your decision. Majorn doesn't take such insults lightly. I expect that you won't have that long to regret your choice before Majorn destroys you.
You dare approach me, mortal? I will carve you into the tiniest of pieces, meat-sack!
Back already? My, you're rather fast … for an assistant.
You again? Got something interesting for me?
You've done well, my friend. I've been tracking your progress.

My friend, you've seen me through many trials and I'm grateful. But uniting my spirituality with the Green Lady's physicality is something I must do myself.\n\nThe celebration continues throughout the city. Enjoy yourself!
Not so loud! I don't want them to notice me.

You've got <<Amz:1>>? Good! Keep them close. I don't know what they're for, but they've got to be important.\n\nBut before that, you've got to defeat the Guardian of Silvenar. It patrols the bridge between here and the city.
Is it gone? Are there any more?
Is it gone? Are there any more?
Is there something else I can tell you?
You can't kill me! Don't you know who I am?
The future rushes toward us at break-neck speed! Quickly, you must continue your mission. Do not worry about me!
The triumvirate is free, and our energies can no longer be used against the rightful rulers of this city.\n\nGo to the Silvenar, now. He will tell you what needs to be done to preserve this moment.
This looks like a back entrance, but it's bolted shut. I think these items around the door frame are part of a puzzle lock. Look around. Maybe there's a clue to the right sequence nearby.
Greetings. What brings you to my pier in the middle of this disaster?
Watch out! Don't you know the Houndsmen are listening?
By the Eight, you are an annoying one!\n\nDo you have a crush on me or something? Let me speak to my friend here. In peace. That means alone.

I'll coordinate my tale with Spinners Einrel and Caerllin. Meanwhile, you must get to the Green Lady!\n\nWe'll take care of getting the Silvenar inside the city. A fitting climax to a terrifying tale.
Ah, the sweet smell of Maormer boats on fire. I quite like the aroma.\n\nSince you're here, may I conclude you've finished your task?
This makes no sense. Who would attack us? Maybe it was the Orcthane and his Stormfist Brigade!
Search for the <<C:1>> on the ship. I'll meet you there, once I've recovered my gear.
I'll make sure the Pact knows of your courage. The fight against Stral. Epic.
I'm afraid you just missed Commander Yjarnn. Again.\n\nHe was in a hurry. He always seems to run when everyone else around here just saunters.
Hello, friend! How long has it been? You remember Rigurt the Brash, leader of the Glorious Expedition for Nord Cultural Exchange? \n\nIt is good to see you again. You are just in time to help.
Welcome to Voljar's Meadery. Please excuse the mess.
What indignity! What utter ….\n\nWhat? Who are you? Leave me alone. I'm not doing anything.
I heard that you've been hard at work.\n\nA powerful troll for the Argonians? Really? That's quite remarkable.
That went amazingly well. I think.
Things return to normal so slowly these days. Is there really a time when everything is as we imagine?
Get out there. Thallik must be put down.
You're back. I hope the skeever hunt went well. Killed all the zombies, made us safe?
The spinners will weave your actions into the story of the Bosmer. I'll see to that myself.\n\nI'm the Green Lady. They'll listen.
I'm honored to be here, but to be honest, I mostly can't wait until the parties start.
We should leave this place. Let the forest have it.
You're not wanted here, outsider. For all we know, you're carrying the plague.
You will swim in the waters of victory. I smell it.
I heard you went through the portal and defeated <<1>>.
I heard you went through the portal and defeated <<1>>.
I'm not sure how I'm supposed to convince the people in Nimalten everything's going to be all right. There's a damned ghost giant roaming the land … things are not going to be all right.
What brings you to my hall? You don't look in need of a thane's help. And if you are with Aera, I am not in need of her help, either.

Do you fully understand what it is you recovered from Sancre Tor? Even without being able to use it, the Amulet of Kings is literally priceless. You would bankrupt kingdoms who would take it only for symbolic value.\n\nDon't get any ideas.
The Thane holds court in the manor hall.
Are you ready to go?
Thanks for helping us get rid of the Orcthane's thugs.
Go on, before Sadri disappears for good.
I'm so happy Asgi made it through this ordeal safely.
What's that smell? It's awful.
Told you something bad was going to happen.\n\nI didn't want you to walk into this trap alone. So I followed you. Good thing, too.
Thanks for helping us. Have some stew. I just made a fresh pot.
The murderer propped Betar up. They wanted us to see him. I'm thinking this was a warning.
You're here to speak to Hallfrida, aren't you? Why do you disturb me? The girl is wild. She needs a strong hand to discipline her.
You! You are the creature who stole my sword?\n\nTime enough to deal with you after this is over. In the meantime, out of my sight!
My friend! I would swear we only spoke days ago. I can see by the look on your face you know of Nimalten's dark times.
I once held a sword and shield. I protected those I cared for in battle.\n\nOn this throne… I feel helpless.
I can see the smoke! Now everybody knows the danger they face. Blood for the Pact!
The matrons are awake! It was much easier to enter, but I still sense … danger.
I'll be fine. Help Voranil!
I don't seem to be making much progress.
Did you retrieve my silk?
My silk! Excellent.
You get that blade, and I'll see Thorulf hung from the highest point in the hall!
I've worked my whole life to achieve this. Thank you for honoring me with your presence.
You're alive! I thought they might have taken you too ….
We're going to get the fort up and running again. My scouts report that there are still Stormfist troops in the area.
Why would you do that? We could have ridden out the entire plague on that supply.
Well, this trip was a disaster.
Snorrvild and I have learned our lesson. No more wilderness for us. I think we'll stick to in-town adventures from now on.
It's always nice to meet new people in exciting places!
Many thanks to you, my friend. If you ever find an artifact that needs deciphering, well, ask my sister.
The Worms won't stand a chance. I hope some of my men still live down there.
Read the notes. You'll understand them better than I will. Plus, I'm dying.
Go quickly! There isn't much time!
If I were flesh again, I'd bring the fight to the Worm Cult!
Listen to the hengekeeper. <<1>> depends on her.
I hear them. The matrons, the leaves, the drops of rain. The whole forest, all around us.\n\nAnd over it all, I can hear the Green Lady.
Head to Pinepeak Caverns. Only you can safeguard Hakra, liege-lord.
You'd better get out of here. You've made enemies here.
Enough dwelling on what I wish had been. We must deal with what is.
You said the undead were taken care of. And Thorulf? Where's that bastard?
Is someone there? What's going on? I can't see!
Had any luck with the song, my new friend? Remember, I'll meet you at the manor when you've learned what you need to.
Take the four points around the fort. Once you raise the banner, soldiers will rally to help you.
She's waiting for you at the Evermore Guildhall in Bangkorai. Good luck, comrade.
Father, why are you still here? Haven't you done enough?
They'll never take me alive, Jarl. Don't worry about me.
This tune is for everyone listening from the Ashlands. Raise your flagons, Dark Elves!
Why did my guards let you in here? I need to have a talk with them about the meaning of the word "guard."\n\nGo away, commoner. If you want to meet with the King or I, petition your Jarl.
I wonder if that old horse would make it to Winterhold? I could set out tonight …
Nimalten reminds me of Bleakrock. All these good people, oblivious to danger. If only we could have protected my husband and son.\n\nHave you learned anything?
I'm close.
The Worm Cult is becoming terribly powerful.
Well done, my friend. May <<1>> never again arise to haunt us!
I've seen what the Reach do to people. I begged Vigrod to let me loose on them. <<1>> can undo some of what they've done, but I want to slit some throats.
Place <<mz:1>> in the holders, then we can enter Abamath's ruins.
She's preparing a ritual space at the Riften Guildhall in The Rift. I'll see you there, Adept. We're so close!
I will protect <<1>> with my life.\n\nWalk in radiance, my friend.
The honored Queen Nurnhilde has spoken on your behalf and granted you entrance to Sovngarde.\n\nStep into the column of light and get on with your business.
The heat will seal the words firmly in the mammoth flesh. I hope so, at least.
Leading the charge as always, eh?\n\nWe've lost many soldiers trying to take these caves. The Worms wield barrels filled with a flammable liquid. If you see barrels ahead, be wary.
May the waters protect you. You will succeed.\n\nRemember, not all foes must be fought. Use your stealth and your wits to avoid fights. Save your strength for the true enemy, Sinmur.
Have you retrieved the shards of Wuuthrad? Without them, Sinmur will be extremely difficult to defeat.\n\nIf you don't have the shards, I suggest you recruit friends to aid you.
I'm getting better?
Thank you for collecting these. I'll give them to the families of the fallen.
How many more will die today? Will any of us live to see our homes again?

The captain's men are as disgusted with her as I am. With the townsfolk willing to testify against her, the Fists of Thalmor will have no choice but to cashier her.\n\nShe'll be locked up until we receive word from Elden Root.
<This Dark Elf woman wears Worm Cultist garb. From the claw marks, it appears she was mauled to death by sabre cats. A look through her pack reveals a blood-stained journal.>
The invaders crossed the bridge! They've taken over the entire town!
We're going to die! We're all going to die!
The captain won't tolerate your presence for long. Leave while you can!
We're not waiting any longer! Velyn Harbor's our town and we're taking it back!
Hasn't your kind done enough!

Listen, if we work quickly, we can cut our losses! Those thieves didn't nab everything. One of the rotmeth bladders is ready to turn, but we're short on a few critical seasonings.\n\nYou're good with animals. Maybe you can help me out?
Together we'll storm Fallowstone Hall and teach those bastards a lesson they'll never forget!
Good luck in there! I don't envy you, so once this is over the drinks are on me!
I was in the brewery when someone struck me on the back of my head. I must've been out for several minutes.\n\nWhoever hit me is still upstairs with the sacred brew. We've got to stop him!
How did you find me? Never mind. That's not important.\n\nThe Sigil. You have to find the Sigil.
She's dead. I can't believe she's dead. What about the Sigil?
Hey there, friend. If you're interested in joining the Fighters Guild, just say the word.
Leave me. I told you what you wanted to know.\n\nYou'll see. You'll see how the lizard fails. Just you wait. I know what I'm talking about.
What are you, my mother?\n\nGet out of here. You're ruining my me time.
What can Laughs do for you? You need something special?
I'll never forget what you and Stormy did for me.\n\nYou saved me. Both of you.
So, are you going to give me the salts or what? I really need them.
Ah, you again. Veldrana's been regaling us with your heroics. Captain Viveka led a Riften Guard patrol out here. We're following up.
Ahh. I'm getting the feeling back in my toes. Ow! Pins and needles! Pins and needles!
Remarkable. I'm not easily impressed, but you've done it.\n\nUricantar, on the other hand—what a waste. Truly.
Without your help here, the tale of Andewen in Ezduiin would have gone very differently, I think.\n\nGood luck in your travels.
You are very kind to help, though you do not seem to know Valeguard's importance. Perhaps <<1>> can explain things for you?
The souls must be released—one way or another.
This one never should have come here. Jiluza misses the sands of Dune.
To think I was excited about coming here. I want to impress Telenger. But I'm not sure my soul is a price I'm willing to pay.
Ezduiin holds no more fascination for me. I wish to be rid of these ruins.
Every stone here unnerves me. I keep expecting a spirit to peer around each corner.
Time's slipping away, friend. If you want to beat my record you need to get out there with that bow.\n\nTalking to me isn't going to help you catch rabbits.
Sure, you could use normal, non-magical, absolutely regular arrows.\n\nOr you could use exciting arrows. Fiery arrows. Arrows that get to go boom!
Please … we need to stop the Maormer ….

This invasion is over! Without the ability to signal their ships, the Maormer won't be able to navigate the shallows. They'll turn around or find themselves swimming back to Pyandonea.\n\nAll of Auridon is in your debt. Well done!
Well, you made short work of that little task. My vengeance is complete.\n\nI thank you, and I owe you a debt. Perhaps we'll see each other again sometime.
You can do it! Beat that lizard at his own game!
You do me a great honor. I miss my three daughters terribly. I'm not whole without them.\n\nBut you give me hope.
Pleased to meet you, I'm sure. These damnable Maormer are not the most charitable of hosts.
Didn't expect to see a friendly face. Get me out of here.
Maormer scum. They took us by surprise. Did the Captain send you?
Please find my friends' bodies and burn them before they rise as vampires!
You risked everything to help me. I won't forget it.
Incredible! Did you see that? Unfortunate that the crystal lattice was destroyed in the process, but it served its purpose well.
Don't suppose you're bringing any reinforcements, are you?
Did you see her? She tried to kill me! \n\nColonwe is an ancestral spirit that haunts this grove. She's always been a mischievous one, but I've never seen her so violent!
Thanks to you and <<1>>, these people will be able to find their eternal rest.
My sisters and I are ready to aid you.
Hmm. You look familiar. Have we met before?
My Sister of Waves lingers just ahead. Go. Find her.
We will make ready to face the lamia queen, and meet you when our spells are ready.
Destroy that thing before it kills the captain!
I've never felt such pain! Ugh, the Maormer are little better than animals!
The Worm Cult might've summoned Mauloch without your intervention. We're all grateful for what you did to stop them.
The Worm Cult sought the Blood of Mauloch? Praise Y'ffre you were here to stop them!
Be strong. The fate of our ancestors' eternal souls rests in your hands now.
<Golun was stabbed repeatedly until he died.>
<<1>> brought the shard you retrieved into the ruins for the final battle.\n\nWith only one shard, you have little chance of defeating Sinmur by yourself.
Despite our losses, we can still turn the tide here!
With you at our side, we'll take back the Hall or die trying!
Please watch over Ande. Don't let anything happen to her!
Any luck?
Andewen got us out of there. She has the scales of Auri-El!
Good luck in there.
I wasn't here long enough to know <<1>>. Her reputation brought me here.
These Worms should never have crawled up from below.
I knew something was up with these guards. An actual member of the First Auridon Marines has shown up. He wanted to speak with you.
Get going, Arrow. If Ash has asked your aid, you've no time to waste chatting with me.
Excellent work! They had it coming.
The camp's not far from here. I doubt the cultists will simply let you take one.\n\nThey never dared enter Treehenge before. I wonder what changed?
A necromancer leads the cultists, sacrificing them to reach my tomb. Each death strengthens the spell he's ready to cast.
I really don't know much about how to get inside Silvenar. I only arrived here with the Silvenar a few hours ago.\n\nHmm … that whole naming thing could get a bit confusing, couldn't it?
Oh, still around? You're a dedicated merchant!
A lighthouse is just a tower of stone. Towers can be rebuilt.
You're a gentle sort. Thank you. I'll see Yiri's taken care of.\n\nYou deal with those Worm Cult bastards.
I know our sound isn't "together" yet, but it will be! See you in Silvenar!
Those drums are the best I've ever had. Now that you've found us, please find them!
We can't perform without instruments! Please find them!
Music brings people together on many different levels, doesn't it?
Well, well. Seems you're the one I should've concerned myself with all along.\n\nI've got my orders, no thanks to those Khajiit. They'll get their just reward soon enough.
She's made it to the crypts? Hmm. Well, at least now she's surrounded by family.
Her Majesty can handle herself, but she can also be reckless. Don't leave her side!
When we spoke last, I said your tale would be forever remembered. It seems our memories must grow longer if we are to keep up with your exploits.
Don't let death and destruction discourage you, friend. For the right coin, this one can make your day.
Fool! Take the shard. It will never profit you.
This Amulet is incredibly important. We will protect it until we are ready to use it.
You're working with Tovisa? I hope you have a plan.
I just want to go home. Get some rest. Read a book.
Have you located my commander?
This time we should burn that giant to ashes. And then scatter the ashes to the winds.\n\nHave you spoken with Vigrod yet?
I hope that's the last we ever see of Sinmur. Vigrod's been looking all over for you.
Telenger is amazing, isn't he? I'd do anything to get his recommendation.
Honor and praise to you. It's always been my dream to work with Telenger. He's quite brilliant. And handsome!\n\nSuch a shame Ezduiin has been such a disappointment.
Telenger's recommendation is a powerful force within the guild. I only hope one day I can earn it.
I'd heard being Telenger's assistant was dangerous. But this!
Everyone here only cares about impressing Telenger. It's all Ejukki hears day in and day out.
I hope someday Telenger will look upon me as he does Andewen. I want to prove myself.\n\nI just don't want to end up like Uricantar.
May your step be silent and fall in shadow, friend.
There you are. Vigrod wants to talk to you, right away.
Are you insane? Can't you see the town is under attack?
You did it! The whole line speaks of your service. The bodies we've got out here will make sure the Daedra stay bottled up in Firsthold.\n\nThank you.
We've got a dozen more strong bodies on the line, traveler! Thank you for bringing word of our troubles to Skywatch.
Ah, at last. Queen Ayrenn is eager to speak with you.
Do you think I should change my hair color? I'm thinking of something in a pink or green.
My agents tell me that three new souls have joined the celebration.
Enough! I'm no match for an Ebonheart brute.
Fine. You win. Give me the goblet.
No more! I'll drink it.
My men and I will try to keep the locals out of the area. There are few things more dangerous than ancestral spirits on a rampage.
Word of advice, friend. Never trust a necromancer.\n\nIf you absolutely have to, think hard, and then walk the other way.
You got here just in time.\n\nBut I know you didn't come in with the investigation team. Who are you?
You shouldn't have a hard time looking for a fight around here. \n\nLuck.
I'm still dead, aren't I? I hoped it was just a bad dream. I sense I still have one more role to play, though.
This audience needs to drink more.
I'm bored. There's too much chatter and not enough rhythm.
I love a good crowd, but there needs to be music!
I'll never be able to face Bar-Neeus again, curse him. His generosity has saved us and we'll rebuild. Only when I can repay him will my shame be lessened. Damn him, and you!
If anyone can retrieve No-Name's precious package, it's you!\n\nWonderful, courageous, admirable you!
Damned undead. If there's anything I can't stand it's a Stars-damned vampire.
Ah, you're back. Good. Sorry, just trying to stay on my feet.
Need to see this woman. No time to talk.
You did it! Congratulations!
Ah, it is a sun-blessed day, no? Is there something I can interest you in?
How goes the search? Still searching, yes? Hmm.
Thought I might make it to Vulkhel Guard, but I just couldn't go any farther.
<<1>> is free! You're so kind to help me.
Will the killers come back? Are we safe here? I can't stop shaking, I'm so afraid!
You've returned! And the bards, stupid though they may be, are alive!
Poor Queen. Razum-dar can't imagine her sitting out the fight willingly. Her retinue must have held her down to keep her from entering the fray.
You've done it! The rest of the lady's entourage has gone on ahead. Did you deal with the mad man?
My friends are in cages in the Worm Cult camp. Will you rescue them? One of the cultists must have the key!
Once again, you've pulled my arse out of the fire. I owe you a round, maybe two, next time you're in Riften.
Dark rumors in town. Too many dark rumors.
Have you heard the rumors of cultists about? Dark times, indeed.
Good luck in your travels, my friend. I'm sure the Nords of Skyrim are grateful for your presence. Just as grateful as I am.
You're lucky you're not a Daedra. I may be an innkeeper, but that doesn't mean I can't adequately protect myself!
The Eight save us! We're surrounded! We're all going to die out here!
Full Moon. This one had errands to run today. Jiyya was lucky enough to be outside the city when High Kinlady Estre arrived.
This might be Iduthal's last mug of amber ale … if the Daedra haven't destroyed this one's supply. \n\nTuinvitar said there's no way he'd let the Dremora get to it. The fool.
Thank you. Thank you so much. I can think again.
The Thane will set you straight. Kyne guide your path.
That's wonderful! Did you swoon? I would have swooned.\n\nMy collection is complete! And I have an autograph! Um … could you ask about a second book?
There's no hope for it! The city's lost. Might as well start looking to move to Skywatch.
They killed my husband! Those bastards ….
Thank you. You've spared my life. I can never repay you. But I swear on my magic, I'll never truck with Daedra again.
Hey there.
What are you doing in my home? Don't you know who I am?
Sorry, help you? I've got a lot of work to do around here.
With the barriers down, Estre will be the next to fall.
Thanks to you, we were able to destroy the wards. I wish you the same luck against High Kinlady Estre.
We've done it! Thank the Eight you showed up.
You've done it! I only wish I could have been of assistance.
You're not one of them. Need your help. Not for me—I'm doomed—but the others….
I'd like to catch up with the Maulborn and give them what they gave the merchants.
How many lives does this Vox have to take? Diiril. The merchants. She needs to pay for what she's done.
What do you want? If it's a favor, I have no time to spare right now.
It's so cold. Can barely move. Never get out of here.\n\nNot sure I want to.
Mara watches over us all. Everything happens according to her plan, though we often don't see it.
Yes, what is it? I'm a busy man.
The afflicted found their way up here while you were inside. But we cut them down. Every one of them.
You almost feel sorry for them. Flesh rotting. Blood boiling.\n\nYep. Almost.
No traces of plague must survive. The bodies have to burn.
Ayrenn's healers have seen to me. I'm alive, thanks to you.
<Velatosse stares at you, her eyes dead inside.>
Auri-El watches over you. You have my thanks for your victory here today.

The Battlereeve tells me Estre is dead. I mourn her loss. \n\nShe is the past. And you, our future. Your service to our people has been exemplary. You have proven yourself a valuable asset to the Aldmeri Dominion.
Having second thoughts?
Yeah?
Filthy Daedra running about our city. It's a disgrace.
Thane Vofknir is a generous man. I'm sure he'll set you on the path.
We're here for your protection. If you're not sick, get out of here.
Nothing to see here. Move along.
Isn't she beautiful? Where has she been all my life? \n\nWe'll be together. Forever.

She has passion, eh? I'll dispatch a messenger tonight. I know a graveyard that's perfect for our rendezvous. \n\nAnd there's a desanctified shrine to a Daedric Prince nearby. The acoustics are incredible. I should do a reading there someday.
My wife and I specialize in weapons. I'd love to show you our wares, only … I can imagine you'd understand why we don't have any right now.
Curse Estre. I knew she was trouble the moment she came to Firsthold. Now look at what she's doing to our beautiful city!
High Kinlady Estre is out of her mind. Worshiping Mehrunes Dagon and corrupting High Kinlord Rilis. The Queen won't have it. Battlereeve Urcelmo is already here. He'll see to Estre's demise.
I'm lucky to have made it out alive. If the Marines hadn't shown up, I'd be face down in the ground by now.
Nothing ever comes of worshiping Daedric Princes. Especially one like Mehrunes Dagon. I can't imagine this bodes well for Estre.
Burakgum never thought it was possible for Firsthold to fall.
Be careful. High Kinlady Estre sure has made a mess of Firsthold. I just hope High Kinlord Rilis is all right.
If Queen Ayrenn didn't care so much about her precious Aldmeri Dominion, this never would have happened.
How could you side with that traitor? Unbelievable!
Oh, my son! I can't believe it. After everything I did to protect him ….
Where am I? What happened?
Have you seen <<1>>? He stepped out for a moment. He said he'd be right back. I hope the undead don't hurt him.
<The statue looks very lifelike.>
I wish I'd been there to help you kill Gullveig. I would've enjoyed that.
It is good to feel the flow of life around me once more.
Speak with Captain Viveka soon. She's impatient to leave.
I see a hero standing before me. You have risen high in my estimation today.
Were you telling the truth? Merormo has trafficed with Daedra?
We sure showed those bastards, eh?
I hope that the merchant's promises are good and he keeps other Hlaalu away from here.
Are you sick? You seem to have lost a lot of weight.
The ghosts are gone, but I'm still woried about my brother Nilus.
<<1>> warned me about the danger this place posed with all of the Maormer about. Poor lass! She deserves better.\n\nIf you deal with those Broken Coast bastards, I'll see she gets it.
What do you want? I'm not leaving till I get what I came for.
Thank the Eight I found you! Teldur has betrayed us!
Please. No more questions. Just leave me alone.
You go on. We'll see you at the Withered Tree.
One of the men in the crew caught. Whatever this is. Thanks for sticking around.
Still around? Good for you.
I comend you for your valor.
Get away from me, cat. I don't know what sort of disease lives in your fur, and I don't want to find out.
I need to make medicine for Barothlas. Explore the valley and find out what's going on there. Maybe someone below knows where the city went.
Oh, it's you again. Did you show good Jorald here that ring you found? I'm sure he would be pleased to know you gave the bandits what they deserved.
These people are lunatics. As soon as Barothlas can walk, Jarakh will return to Velyn Harbor.\n\nThere is no profit to be had here. Perhaps next year.
No telling what'll happen if the cultists complete their ritual. Please help us stop it!
Back already? What about <<1>>? She must still be in the Smokefrost Peaks.
Nice! That'll show 'em!
Get in there and take out those cultists. I don't want to see what happens if they complete their ritual.
You have my thanks for helping Raerana. You're always welcome at The Withered Tree!\n\nAnything I can get you?
We didn't wait long enough after sealing the tears outside. Or maybe there are two Daedroth! Let's wait for the second to come forth, and then the city is sure to follow.
Do what you can. Heldil needs your help.
Honor and praise. I'll need you to speak with Watch Captain Astanya. \n\nJust follow the docks to the west.
Fair day, and welcome to Vulkhel Guard. I need you to speak with Watch Captain Astanya.\n\nFollow the docks to the northeast. Can't miss her.
Welcome, traveler. What brings you to the city?
Welcome to Vulkhel Guard. We're asking all visitors to register their arrival in the city. Security for the Queen, don't you know.
They're all doomed, and I'm next!
You again? Shouldn't you be off running errands somewhere?
Well? If you're here to end me, do it and be done. I'm tired of waiting.
Hurry, traveler. My comrades at the lighthouse. They can't hold out forever. \n\nAnd who knows when the Daggers will decide to off the Orc?
I see it in your face—you have word of my husband. Please tell me!
<You would almost swear this statue could move.>
The Sentinels are connected. If we destroy one, the others will also be blinded for a time.
Estre—the High Kinlady herself? I can't believe it, though I've seen it now with my own eyes.
Ah, peace at last. Or as peaceful as the Rift can be nowadays. I feared the giants would never leave us alone.
I'm very worried about my cooks. I hope you can find whatever's causing the trouble!
I have to admit, I'm impressed. Cool like the scales of Auri-El, you are.\n\nGood luck with the captain.
You're no guard. Thank the Stars. Quickly, we don't have much time.
Explain yourself. What are you doing here?
This town is rotten, down to the roots. Like a Full Moon, the Eyes of the Queen stare down.
Make your way to Tanzelwil at your own pace. Seek out my entourage when you arrive. They'll be able to direct you to me.\n\nAnd good luck, to us both, on the road.
Ah, back again. Answering riddles for Iroda. Want some help with this one?
Raz needs to report our success here. Her Majesty will be pleased.
You should continue to listen to the story of our village. <<1>> has more to tell.
Do you know what happened to my husband Urynnar? Has he been cured?
Thanks again for hunting down my crew. Ungrateful louts.
A Maormer infestation of Auridon could be very, very bad. Anala hates to think of how bad this could be.
Oof. Damn that wine.
Do you have something to say?

You are a bag of miracles, my friend. We are fortunate the Cult did not enthrall you, though perhaps your will would have overcome them anyway.\n\nAs for the Obsidian Husk—I destroyed it while you did battle with Theran.
I warned her. I told her I'd never been on a ship before. I think she was fine with my work.\n\nUntil I threw up on her boots.
I hope all is well. What brings you to back to Fallowstone?
Ivarstead is quite a trek. But if you want the coin, start walking. Ha!
This one imagines you may have some questions. What can Raz tell you?
Please head to the ritual site. No telling what they're up to!
Have you talked to <<1>>? She's been looking for you.
The finest weapons in all the Dominion. Forged right here in Mathiisen. \n\nHot off the anvil. If you will.
Step away from the house, please. The Canonreeve does not want her things disturbed.
Thank you for rescuing me!
So. How'd it go?
I've always hated spiders, but I think today proved that squashing them can be extremely gratifying.\n\nAt any rate, you've been a great help. Two-Blades will probably want to thank you, too.
It's up to you and me, friend!
You turned a crushing defeat into resounding victory, my friend. The Fighters Guild lost many today, but thanks to you, it was not for nothing.\n\nSpeak with Two-Blades when you are able.
Do … do you have them?
I've begun to hear rumors. They say there weren't many survivors. They say my … my father was killed.\n\nHe should have taken this more seriously. I … I can't believe he's gone.
From your look, I think you climbed the stairs to the Throat of the World. Did you find the herb?
I've heard things have calmed down a bit around here.
I can't believe you killed the giant. Really? Wow, uh, that's great.
Nice to see a new face in town. Be careful though. Lots of travelers have been disappearing lately.
Welcome to the Withered Tree. Good luck getting any actual help around here.
Thanks for the daggers, they'll fetch a nice price. I'll be in touch when I have another job for you.
Ow. Damn those Veiled Heritance!
Thank the Divines, I am not a dead man.
Don't you have someplace to be?
I can't stop worrying.
Those bugs are in the hay. All over the place. Go get them!
I'm not taking any more guild money. They want to kill one of their own, they can do it themselves.
Managed to bag my Ranger! And Cariel here has been telling me about your exploits.
If you're going to hang around, pull up a chair and buy us a round.
Defeat Ulfnir, then search him. We must get that crown!
My friends! I'm so pleased zombies didn't eat your faces!
I'm glad to see that business at Skuldafn's dealt with, but a soldier's duty is never done. The Rift needs your help.
Rescue, at last!
Ah, you've found my drunken Nords. I'll take them off your hands. Lead them back out.
<Malsia must have set Solvar aflame when he attacked her.>
The fish have stopped biting for some reason.
You must excuse us, we were just talking about the Queen's upcoming speech.
I'm sorry, I was just speaking with the High Kinlady. And now you've interrupted us. Excuse us, please?
Enjoying the city, I hope? Apologies if the others are a bit distracted. Everyone's on edge today.
This one hopes your new souvenir comes in handy.
Hrmph. Feels like the dead have settled down some. I'm sure that won't last.
Please, lead me out of here.
Palith will come to forgive me in time. I may not ever forgive Eranamo.
Thank you. Thank you for sparing my brother's life.
I never want to see this place again.
I shouldn't have left the village, but I had to know if my daughter's alive.\n\nNow I don't know if I'll live long enough to see her again.
Thank the moons, we're not too late. I hope she still has enough strength to drink.
I know it's not much. But we wanted you to have this sack of supplies. Thank you!
Good luck. If you need us, the Marines have your back.
I only hope you're not too late.
That vile witch. I never liked her.
Bastards! Tall, pale, knife-eared bastards!
So. Did you finish your tour of our little school?
You're a lucky recruit. The Veiled Queen herself will be making a speech in support of the cause. You'll be able to see her firsthand!\n\nAssuming you survive the trials.
Let's get this dispatch back to Aldcroft.
Gorak may be ready one day, but today is not that day.

Oraneth is dead, the ritual broken, yet evil still stirs here. There is a darkness, growing from the earth below, sprouting from a seed of death.\n\nWe have failed. The darkness is coming, with no one to control it ….
Two of my scouts came back. Who was the traitor?
I'll see you dead for this!
Don't leave me here! They'll kill me!
If only my mother could see me now!
Don't lose any sleep over me. The Covenant isn't nearly as bloodthirsty as they say. I hope.
No! Nurad is … This one does not know where these supplies came from. Do not hurt Nurad!
Well done!
Please leave me alone!
Welcome, student.\n\nStudy hard and you'll do well, I'm sure.
Yummy bread. Enjoy it.
An impressive time. You've passed the Veil's trial of endurance.
Mara's heart, you've done good work here. Little wonder Razum-dar trusts you.
You took the wind out of Helane's sails, for sure. No one's ever crossed her that badly before!
Well done! You've proven you have a well-honed mind.
Took them long enough to send reinforcements.
She just wants to get out of here.
You're a full member now. And you're in luck. The Veiled Queen herself will be speaking to the cause.
What were you thinking, coming in here after me? The Bloodthorn will escape!
I'm so happy to have Len back, safe and sound. He said you found him in the mine.
Feeble pup, I'd break you. Run along.
<You notice the nearly invisible seam of a circular disk at the center of the stone.>
That's close enough, stranger. Why do you approach Deepwoods?
Dame Clarique filled us in on what happened. I wish we could have gone in there with you instead of that bandit.
My brother Bernard and his family are coming to live in Daggerfall. He'll miss Deleyn's Mill, but it's safer inside the walls of the city.
We can't trust these conniving sneak-thieves to keep their end of a bargain.
I left my father to help the Eagle's Brook survivors. I was determined to make sure the Red Rooks wouldn't profit from more murder and mayhem.
The shrine is in the middle of the village. The lady's grace is embodied in the green which shelters the stone.
Move along.
Best of luck. Do check in now and again, won't you?
There's a temple to Sanguine out in the swamps. You'd have to be strange in the head to go there on purpose.
I've lived in Stormhold my whole life. Don't understand why all the newcomers make such a big deal out of having to live with Argonians.
I heard you were at Hatching Pools when the Bosmer attacked. I'm glad you were. And I'm glad I wasn't.
It worries me to think of the Dominion watching us from those ruins on the hill. I'm glad you rooted them out.
Come no closer! Why do you approach Deepwoods?
Not many walk these roads lately. What brings you to Deepwoods?
We've retaken the Cove! By Mara! \n\nOw.
Look at our town. So much destruction. So much work to do.
You're a real live person, aren't you? I thought I was all alone out here. I bet you came from that city over there.\n\nCould you help me, please?
Phynaster guide your path.
Are you with the Marines? What happened?

I can see Raynor through this observation window, but he can't hear me. It must be the spell … and I bet the spell didn't affect me because I'm not attuned to whatever catalyst controls the magicka matrix.
I could sure use a mead right about now, but I need to keep a clear head. Otherwise we'll never break this enchantment.

I sense your uncertainty. There is a darkness weighing upon your mind that only serves to deepen your despair.\n\nFear not. The roots of the Mundus are strong, and we are the leaves to gather the sunlight.
Troll's blood, I'm glad you survived that! I am myself again. Drodda had us dancing to her witch's strings.\n\nYou're a hearty one, to best Lord Agomar! Who are you, exactly?

You ask so nicely, but no. Once you begin the game, only victory or defeat can set you free.\n\nYou, however, shall add an element of surprise and excitement to the game. Will you rush bravely into the fray? Or will you turn and run like a coward?
Yes, indeed. Everything is fine here at the Flagon. Plenty of mead, plenty of happy Nords!
I'm here from Firsthold to inspect the weapons. High Kinsman Rilis only wants the best armaments for the First Auridon Marines.
You looking for work? Good luck, friend. \n\nOnly job I could find. And I have to work with furballs and shorties. My mother would be so ashamed.
Hmm. Hate to see good mer like you lumped in with those damn cats. \n\nBut your people come here as cheap labor, same as the Khajiit. They should treat your kind better, I say.
Just got in from Silsailen, needed a new line of work. \n\nPay's lousy. And I have to work with furballs and shorties. But at least it's something.
Hey there, stranger. You here for work?
Enginaire's a good foreman, but she's Altmer. She doesn't know what it's like.
Zurka comes all the way from Dune. She has very lucrative business, one of the best merchants in Elsweyr. \n\nAnd she can't get a single meeting with Condalin or Malanie!
The vault is open. Are you ready?
Sithis blind me! Look who it is! \n\nSeeing you is the first good news since we landed here. If you got in, maybe we can get out.
If you've talked to Pa, then I guess you got work to do.
Please, help them.
Did you find him?
Speak to this creature at your peril. I don't trust it, not a bit.\n\nIf it raises so much as a finger, I'll strike it down.
Go on, mate.\n\nIf things go well, I'll see you when this is all over.
Have you found the Thane's lair yet?
It must be here somewhere. Please, keep looking.
Hrmm. Well, belike you're right, when all's said and done. \n\nNow I'll just have to see what I can do for me new crew, here, with that old shaman's tricks.
I just got back from Narsis. Were you the one who saved the city?

With Meridia's Lights, we can turn the tide of this campaign. Kireth said you came from the Hollow City. We shall go there once everyone has had a chance to rest.\n\nThank you for your help. You know, you remind me of one of my students.
Thank the Eight you found him. Thrice-blessed are you, my savior.
We never should have left Cloudrest. My mother was right.
We're lucky the Marines responded so quickly. Aetherius can wait, if you ask me.
This is unacceptable! And all my husband's fault!
Thank you for getting me out of there. I saw the flames from the road. I could have been trapped in my own home.
I hope you find her.
I feel … strange. Like I've been asleep for a very long time.
My poor, sweet boy.
My head feels less foggy. I may try writing a song or two again.

Place the seeds on the bodies of the dead. Angof said that would help me. Keep me safe.\n\nWhen they force you to make a choice in all this—and they will make you choose—I wouldn't mind an ally who doesn't, you know, want to stab me.
Whatever that rune does, this one wants no part of it.\n\nMaybe you can figure out how to use it to our advantage. Might even provide an edge against the Observer.
You're back I see, with the pieces I need. I hope the guests weren't too much pests.\n\nBut please, Lady Estre wants to speak. Perhaps she'll provide the aid you seek!
I'm a little disoriented. But … did my sister just hit me?

If you manage to kill the champions of both Estre and Thallik, I'm not sure what happens next. No one has ever gotten that far.\n\nJust stay alive and remain wary. Who knows how the Observer will alter the playing field if you get too close to victory.
It will be so nice to rest. Finally, rest.
I just wanted to say … what I mean is ….\n\nOh, bother! I'm not really very good at this. Thank you. For rescuing us, I mean. Thank you so much.
Once you use the death rune, get on with the killing. The transformation doesn't last very long.\n\nIf the power fades, just use the rune again.
You picked Estre to help?\n\nI … I think that's a good idea. She suggested we throw a party when I showed up. I guess it's a little more getting to work for you.
Remember. When the Observer asks for your decision, choose me!
Start by looking for Marq's special brew. If any is left, the smell might make him slightly less crazy.
I hope I never see another bandit again. Horrible people.
Defeat the champion of the warriors and convince An-Jeen-Sakka of the worthiness of your decision.
You may think you are clever, but your actions will come to naught.
Seems you know your way around a battlefield, friend. We could win the war tomorrow if we had a dozen the likes of you.\n\nCan I assume you took the rutter off their hands?
My beach! Mine! Get out of here! \n\nBet you're with those two crazy people. It's not yours. It's mine!

I have long dreamed of kind words and a way out, but I think this task is beyond you, my friend.\n\nThe first phylactery is up ahead, watched by impossible creatures. You cannot defeat them. No one can.
I'm not going anywhere until you find Mister Nurin. I know he's still alive.
Still no sign of William at the farm? I'm sorry to hear that.
Thanks for getting me out of there!
I'm going to have nightmares about this day. Damn the Daedra.
It's a good thing I was out hunting. I was able to warn my family in time.
Kill them. Kill the Dremora and stop the summoning!
What is your decision?
<<1>>! And she's unhurt! The Hist guided you, as I knew it would.\n\nBut did it also guide you to my ruby? Please, tell me!
You're lying! My father never would have done this.

I … I thank you. I didn't … I wasn't expecting you would be so capable. You've ended Anconath's torture, and freed a fragment of my soul.\n\nAre you willing to do more? My soul remains bound, and the Daedra are torturing others.
If you're lucky, you won't die before the amulet starts working, if it ever does.
Is the amulet charged? Did it work?
Well done. Very well done!

A powerful lich guards the last fragment, plucked out of history and summoned by my husband. He's ravaging the soul of one of my students.\n\nI would die again to help that student—but I can't. Please, save him if you can.

I wish Nelhilda would forgive me, but I understand her anger. She has her soul back and her place in Sovngarde is assured. I can hold onto that, and I'll make sure that anyone else who comes here receives whatever aid I can provide.
I never hoped that I would ever be free, but I thank you for unbinding this fragment of my soul.\n\nYou've helped Faindor, too, and that brings me a sense of peace that I am unable to express.
You have freed not only my soul, but the souls of all the students caught in my husband's attack.\n\nYour actions right a wrong that was long overdue.

<<1>> is under pirate attack! Worse, they climbed in through our portholes and breached the hull.\n\nI'll use their blood to swab the decks. Think they'll put more holes in my hull, do they? We had just finished repairs on the last ones!
Greetings, my friend. You did it. The undead fell in their tracks.\n\nThe pirates, they surrendered or fled. A good day.
At least we know what's going on at the lighthouse now.\n\nIt may take a while, but we'll send men down there as soon as we can spare them.

I suppose <<1>>'s death was just, but so many of my people were sickened because of what? An old feud between brothers? This is why you'll never see an Orc wear the Amulet of Kings.\n\nBut the bandits stopped their attacks, so you have my thanks.
Ha! I knew you'd done it the moment those undead fell to tatters!\n\nHalf of the pirates surrendered on the spot. They must've thought whatever you did to the undead would happen to them next!
Look, see? That abandoned boat is my only chance!\n\nPlease, give me my things. I need to get away from here!
I suppose you fancy yourself a hero.
What have you learned? Whose tales are false?
You decided to help those … those … monsters? Instead of my people?\n\nI'm so mad I can't even talk to you right now!
This place … it does strange things to your mind.
Ozor, Salach, and Lidenar are free and Captain Angarthal is dead. I believe this day is getting better.\n\nI may have lost my ship, but you've restored my hope.
I told you I could get out on my own. Thank you for rescuing my employees. Can you make certain <<1>> knows?\n\nI think she was headed back toward Haven.

My contact is no wilting flower. You'll find him on the beach, I'm certain of it.\n\nLook, collect the payment yourself for all your trouble. As long as he doesn't leave without the mixture, we'll still have our side business. That's fair, yes?
Greetings, Orc.
Well, I'd best get back to the Prowler. I expect the <<1>> will want all hands on deck.\n\nNeedn't bother her with this business, right? Right, right.
What do you say, outlander? Do you still stand with <<1>> Stronghold?

You wouldn't know anything about proto-Ayleid literature, would you? I can't be certain if the references in these books are metaphors, or descriptions of actual events.\n\nNo matter, I'll work it out.
I'm so hungry.
Just go about your business quickly, stranger.
You did it! Your little racer won the show.
Oh! You're back. So you weren't eaten by lions, then. Good!\n\nDid you have any luck with the journals?
Good luck with your froggy! Isn't frog racing the best?
Hhmph. Good luck. You'll need it with that creature.
You're lucky Bloodthirster is not competing. Your pathetic beast would not survive!
Did you find everything?
Did you do as you promised? Do my children know peace?
Your Dunmer blood proved true. Vox is defeated, order is restored. Well done.
So, how did it go?
What do you want? I've got to repair these things while I can.
This is not the time to talk. There are trolls in here!
The stronghold survived because of your help. We won't forget this.
Rumor has it you have the Red Rooks on the run. I'll sleep easier when the bandits have left town.
<<1>> won't be back. Knows if he shows his face in Stormhold, he'll get it smacked. Price of starting false rumors, right?
You know, this wine isn't half bad. And this cellar is nice and quiet. Cozy. Comfortable, even.\n\nI think I'm going to live down here forever.
Terrible business down in the ruins, eh?\n\nOoh, I should add it to my report!
Those Red Rooks may be gone, but I still don't think I want to do any work.
So many fleshlings running through the halls. Such obstreperous creatures!\n\nYou seem a fine specimen. I don't think I have one of your kind in my garden.
Rocks. Rocks with eyes. I went to get a closer look, and then she ….\n\nWhy can't I remember?
Acquiring a Daedra's eyeball is a disgusting request, but it will release the binding, I'm certain of it.\n\nAnd if it doesn't, there should be some clean rags at our camp.
Guard duty is tougher than I thought. But I can't let <<1>> down.
Brute-vitar sealed us out. <<1>>'s fellows all dead, killed by dirty snake-ladies. No doubt this Pact-soldier kills poor <<1>> now.\n\nThis swamp, I hate it. Endless woe! Poor <<1>>!
Find Sergeant Stegine. He's up the road, in Dreughside.\n\nSo many dead.
No luck finding our valuables yet? Those Thorns need to be taught a lesson.
If you're looking for the Hall Steward, she's inside.
There's nothing as miserable as wearing heavy armor in the desert heat.\n\nI was born and raised here, but that doesn't make it anymore a comfort.
Welcome to our little circle. I think you'll fit right in. \n\nYou can call me Milady. For now.

These ritual altars remain foreign to me. Dracien believes the Canonreeve is preparing a Worm Cult rite. Some sort of necromancy.\n\nIf this is true, Tamriel is in great danger. One Canonreeve with loyalties to the Worm Cult could mean others.

Look at this hovel. It's like the cavern itself is rotting. And the smell! I can taste it with every breath.\n\nThe Canonreeve must be dabbling in necromancy. She may even be Worm Cult. That would be fantastic.
I'd thank you, but I'm pretty sure you had your own reasons for helping me.
Looks like we won't be putting into <<1>> anytime soon. I don't know how we're going to keep our schedule.
I'm glad to see the Reliquary restored. I suppose I need to find the jar of polish.
Mauloch's teeth, I can't believe Hareld is keeping us away from the docks. \n\nI thought when I joined the Fighters Guild I'd actually, you know, fight.
Wooden walls aren't going to help against what's in that mine!
Is that …? Xuth! You found my bow.
We'll make sure the Red Rooks know they aren't welcome in Crosswych. I think a dagger in the ribs sends that message loud and clear!
I think Tamien Sellan has the right idea. We need to fight back and show these Red Rooks that they can't just march in and take over our town.
You did it! Our way is clear!
Healer Dalen sent word that he arrived at Eidolon's Hollow safely. I'm so relieved.
I've reassembled the spider, but I must be able to control it.\n\nThat reminds me—did you find the crystals?
It may not be much, but <<1>> scraped together a reward. We can't exactly pay you in catapults. Not if we want the Dominion to take us in.\n\nWhat you did for us … we won't forget it.
I await news of your success. Howls of dismay from across the river would be nice.
Ah, you've returned. Do you have the second book?
You're on the right path, Adept. Collect the essence we need to unlock this ancient structure.
I've been sent to ask for your help!
Ah, you're here. As punctual as a thespian. Very good.
We'll take charge from here. With any luck, we can relocate Koth and his tribe somewhere that they don't cause any more trouble. If not, well ….\n\nGoblins should remember their place.
<<1>> said he wanted to speak with you. I'm sure he told me what it was about. Did he tell you?\n\nNo, that's … oh yeah … of course he didn't. He's around here somewhere, but I've forgotten where.
Ahh, it was so good to see their smiling faces. Hear their laughter. Thank you, dearie. Thank you from the bottom of Baan Dar's heart.
I hear they decided to let the Redguard envoy in to speak with the Duke.\n\nI guess there's a chance this thing won't turn into a full-blown battle.
Too many elves! One will kill Byz, he knows it!
Shazah will be able to tell you all you need to know. Watch your steps.
Watch yourself here.
What a pity. The fun is over so soon.
I can't believe I forgot to announce you to the Duke. \n\nI really am sorry. I hope you can forgive me.
Byz say you want talk. Talk.
What did Shazah say? Are we going somewhere?
That was neatly done, the way you got Iriana and Shamal back.
Thanks again for your help. I think I'll stay here and get some strong drink in my belly before braving the roads again.
You've the scent of blood on you. Is the deed done?
No sign of my father yet?
It's you again, isn't it? Do you have the skulls?\n\nBlast, am I talking to a corpse again?
This one is certain the clergy will confirm what we suspect. To think, a Moon Hallowed in our midst!
Research never goes as one expects.
Those raiders are still out there. You're getting cold feet? Typical.

I was so happy to see Sir Hughes escape from whatever darkness held him in thrall, but it seems now, his fate is more unclear than ever. \n\nWhatever he may have done, I would counsel the duke to show mercy. Always mercy.
Just seeing my father's old sword fills me with courage! I can do this, I think!
Such horrific power. My people were helpless before it.
These ruins hold knowledge that has been lost for millennia. Perhaps when this crisis is over….
This is no place for the living. Begone!
Living and yet without a soul. How can this be?
Violation! The living desecrate our sanctuary. Death to all!
Before we go, there is something you should know.
The Three must have sent the Maulborn to help us. They're so kind and generous.
I can't be sick. I refuse to be sick. Peasants get sick, not nobles!
I was so moved by the Maulborn proclamations that I came all this way to join their movement. But they refused my offer to help.
I'm not so sure about this. Some of the Maulborn seem all right, but most of them rub me the wrong way.
Is Yngrel dead? I can see from your face he isn't. Please kill him soon.
Death is a necessary part of life. But some deaths are more necessary than others.
I don't know how to thank you. I don't know what my girls would do without me.
Hello there, stranger. Got something for me?
I can't watch.
What? Are you expecting someone to knit a sweater while we wait for you?\n\nNo one is going to do that! Do I look like I knit?
The Hound is my concern, and mine alone. Yet, I just can't leave the Silvenar in danger.\n\nWhen will he leave me be?
Let's take the fight to these rabble.
That … that was terrifying! I was afraid I'd be stuck in that body forever! Curse you!
That worked perfectly! I can't believe it!
That was quick. Don't tell me something went wrong.
Just clear the way for my messenger in case someone sends reinforcements … or attacks the Dominion elsewhere.\n\nWe'll take back Velyn Harbor, one district at a time.
Hear me out. I've no wish to battle you today.
You not allowed in. Go 'way.
Khajiit has been waiting. You have the weapons?
The Sea Drakes will fall apart without Helane. They'll be at each other's throats in a day.
I've said everything I'm going to say about the attack on Velyn Harbor. I'm certain my superiors will see the wisdom in my actions.
Good to see you again. Redguard invaders in Velyn Harbor doesn't surprise me. But the Drublog clan? They side with the Bosmer in times of war.\n\nWe need to find out what's changed.
Speak to my father. He made the trap for <<c:1>>, so he can break it.\n\nHe's at home in the lower arena. I hope he speaks to you.
Off with you. I am too busy to entertain visitors.
Well, well, well. See that? That's an impressive trap door for a simple farmhouse cellar. \n\nI love it when my hunches pan out!
Quit staring at me. Leave me be or kill me, just get it over with!
Key's probably on him. Go ahead and grab it.\n\nUgh, he smells like rotten grapes. I'm going to get cleaned up. I'll meet you at the farm.
If you can help <<c:1>> again, we'd all be in your debt.
Perhaps we shall fight soon.
You need to fight the rest before you fight the best. Me, being the best.
Beat the brawlers and then I'll see what you're made of.
I've done all I can, but the king seems to slip further away every hour. \n\nI'm afraid there is no way to enter the dream either. There's something different this time—something far more dangerous.
Prove yourself against some brawlers. Perhaps then we can test each other.
I hope you've been busy, friend. My heist is all planned and I'm itching to go.
After you've kicked around the pups, come back here. I'll bite your head off.
What brings you to this trashpit?
That cat is going to get an earful when I find him.
Business should pick up as soon as the Mabrigash get used to our presence.
Who are you? What're you doing here?
Go muck around with the chumps.
Please hurry. Preserving this collection has been my life's work.
Another torturer from Helane, even uglier than the last one.
I pledge my life to helping King Emeric … and to destroying anything, anyone, associated with Vaermina.
Don't know who you are, but you better run if you don't want the Sea Drakes to gut you.
Are you all done?
This bucket is AWESOME.
Who in Oblivion are you?
Get me out of here and I'll owe you.
Disrupt the rituals, kill the cultists. Drain the energy from their defilements.
I sense great power in the staff. You've done well.
What's in those portals, anyway? Never mind. I don't want to know.
I'm going to wait right here. I've got an unnatural aversion to alits and I'm not afraid to admit it. Just let me know when you've found that hidden door.
Go get 'em! I'll leave uniforms around for you once I get my knives into a few more cultists.
I can't face <<1>> without our goods.
Are you ready to head inside?
I recognize you from the stories. You're the one who helped save Count At-Tura, aren't you? He's … an old friend.\n\nI'm glad to make your acquaintance. Don't mind the guillotine. It's just for show.
As soon as I can travel, I'm heading back to the Telvanni coast.
The Drublog will show no mercy. Please, get into the Mages Guild and the Trade Hall quickly.\n\nIf the townsfolk are still alive, you'll find them there.
Why are you still here?
Home at last. I can't thank you enough for saving us!
Oh, it's you. Did you expect me to gush with praise, hmm?\n\nToo bad. I should've stayed in the tree stump ….
Feluz has been a little grumpy without his moon-sugar candy, but it's for the best.\n\nAs soon as there's space in the town square, we'll open a shop. Again, thank you.
Rama, dead. I can't believe it. I'm going to miss the old scoundrel.
Leave me alone. I have to earn my keep around here just like any other person. Malanie doesn't pay me meager wages to lolligag.

This was my first real trial of a full strength potion. I gathered a small horde of thunderbugs, but the elemental energy was too much. The ensuing explosion threw me into the river. \n\nAs you can see, my contingency plan was successful.
Get in there and show them what you're made of.
One less Ayleid Relic to plague our world. Good!
Now for the heist I mentioned earlier ….
Can't wait to get this heist over and be off this rock.
Do be careful where you store that rod. The trigger is sensitive. Were it to discharge prematurely, the results could be dramatic.
Traitor! Out of my sight! How could you keep that thing?
How wonderful. A tourist.
Don't worry about changing in front of me. I won't peek.
Onsi's bones, what is it now?
Oh, I could lounge out here forever. So nice.
You're in my light.
You return with treasures and a ghost. You have been busy.

You'll find the graveyard near the Daggerfall cathedral. I shall meet you there.\n\nAnd know this. My master believes you will make the right decision. That's the only reason we're helping you. If you make the wrong decision, it shall cost you dearly.
Ah, my lowly servant! You're just in time.
Like a rat. On fire.
My friend! Welcome back. Do you have some good news?
I can't catch them! They're too big for me!
Have you seen Captain Kaleen? She's supposed to deliver some papers and I'm getting very impatient.
The city's defenses are turned against the Silvenar! This shouldn't be possible.
When my crew turned traitor, I never thought I'd see Betnikh again. Feels good.
Who are you? You weren't on the excavation team.
Make sure Kalari knows I'm thinking about her, all right? Warms an old man's heart to know a pretty girl thinks well of him.
Go … go now!
Honestly, I don't think I'll ever get used to the way he pops around. But at least he's back in one piece and not complaining—for now.
Go … go now!
Damned Colovians. They pick the most inconvenient times to get brave.\n\nSoldier? Report.
I love a good sneak attack. The look in a man's eye when the knife goes in. Ooh! I just got chills.
I'd shake your hand, but it's covered in steaming shalk guts. But by Baan Dar, why not? Put her there!

Now that the Covenant has that artifact, the Aldmeri Dominion won't dare attack!\n\nYou're a hero. Don't let anyone tell you different. My brothers, and all of the High King's soldiers, owe you their lives.
That poor man. Killed in the street and no one even knows who was responsible?\n\nI think I might pack my things and go visit my cousin in Alcaire.
You were right to destroy that cursed relic. I honor Kaleen, but she has lost her way.\n\nNo one should have that power. Certainly not Fahara'jad.
No. I didn't see the murderer. I'm just one woman. I can't see everything all the time.\n\nOne more person accuses me of neglecting my duty and they're going to get a gauntlet to the face.
A friendly face! Great day for an invasion, isn't it?
The crew of the Spearhead grows again. I did not think to see it so soon. The sun shines on us.
You return. What did you learn of the Bloodthorn plans?
Enjoy your cut, partner. Don't spend it all in one place. As I, no doubt, will.
I will carry the ring with faith to Rawl'kha. The priests there will know just where to tend to it. Thank you again.
I have nothing to say to you.
Kalari will be all right, you will see. Just needs some time to deal with what has happened.\n\nGo, speak to Ezzag.
That was a great job, Baan Dar is very pleased with you!
I should've never let <<1>> leave my side!
If you ever get your hands on more of those fantastic Nord garments, I'd be happy to buy them from you.
That Nord book you gave me was very … colorful. I may have to read it again.
I am once again a man worthy of the blood of my ancestors!\n\nLet's have that shield, then.
Amazing to think he gave his life to destroy that thing. Don't worry about us here. With the vault out of the picture, the Colovians will pull back before long. Good work, soldier.
The sooner you can re-light that tower, the better. People here get nervous whenever it goes out.
I believe Mephala's reaction was proof: the temple is sealed. Well done there, I suppose.
Ahh, traveler. Fivefold venerations upon you. I recognize you from Telenger's description. What brings you to the Falinesti Autumn site?
Welcome to the Falinesti Autumn site, traveler. I'm with the team Telenger has brought. You're just as he described you. What brings you this way?
Welcome to the Falinesti Autumn site. Ghadar is surprised, you are just as Telenger described you. This one is working with the great mage to study the site.
Are you well? That was quite the show.
We'll rebuild the collection. You've done the Society, and by association, all of Tamriel, a great favor.
Less wounded than usual. I'd say we definitely have the ogres on the run now.
Hey, is that the Goblin king's crown? You killed him?
Damn that Angof! One death was not enough for that bastard! Look at the trouble he continues to cause me!
This will be remembered as the fight that turned the tide! \n\nThe General will have moved up to establish a new base at the tower! You go on up.
Thank you.
It is out of my hands now, my friend. It has been an honor serving with you.
There is tension in the air. Can you smell it? Subtle, poisonous. Exciting.
Go, go. Kalari should not have to deal with her father's legacy alone.
We've got a deal.
The little rat is all yours. I'm going to drink even more heavily now.
<<1>>'s been gone for hours. I don't know what I'll do if … if he doesn't come back.
Without that sap, <<1>> might not see another year. Gods willing, this plant'll be his salvation!
<This Redguard died recently. Something is clutched tightly in his hand.>
You've slaughtered Zurana's men. And now you come looking for her blood, yes? \n\nPerhaps there is another way.
Keep moving. I'm in no mood to chat.
I only hope Shagol hasn't lost my best axe forever. This one cannot seem to keep its edge.
You're back! Found anyone else to help us with this heist?
There's three folks Captain Kaleen wants to help with her heist—Crafty Lerisa, Jakarn, and Neramo. She told me about 'em. Who do you want to know about?
Get out of here. We're done.
Off you go. The corn should take just seconds to gather. I'm far too busy thinking to do it myself.
Go on about your business. There's nothing to see here.
Be careful in there! There're things in the shadows.
Another victim of the forest? Or have you been spared its horrors?
I'm thankful that you came along. I would have spent my entire life waiting and wondering what became of my husband.
My cousin never returned from the mines. I'm worried sick.\n\nHe's a miner at Bearclaw Mine. Are you coming from there? I hope he's all right.
You've betrayed me and the Covenant with your actions. I can't stand to be in your company anymore. You'll leave here without me.
As long we have breath in our lungs, we'll keep the Autumn site healthy and growing.
This one overheard. He is called Razum-dar, and on behalf of Queen Ayrenn, he thanks you.
Keep as quiet as you can.\n\nSignal me if you see any suspicious corpses. My arrows will make short work of them.
Start in Grimfield. Warchief Tazgol sent a few scouts to harry the Bloodthorn there until we can deal with them. We need to stop them from raising more zombies.
I knew you couldn't be trusted. What do you think King Emeric will do with that cursed artifact? You should have destroyed it.
Thank tha gods those Colovians are gone now. They wree disturbing my peave something fierce. And I had an anniversary to celebrate, damnit it!

So the true culprit behind Lakana's murder was indeed Vaermina? I'm glad to know her plot against my brother was ultimately thwarted.\n\nI'm glad we spared Sir Hughes as well. I understand he's doing penance at Pariah Abbey.
Though this battle is important, Aiden Direnni expects my blade to lead the assault against a key Alessian camp to the north. \n\nAnd what a glorious battle it will be! I'll be leaving shortly.
I heard a lovely, agonized shriek from Zich. Is it dead?
I can smell the sugar leaf on you. Did you get three leaves?
Yes, yes. Let's get this over with.
At last! <<1>> is defeated! The tortured souls, now avenged! \n\nLong have I waited for this day!
Ahh, such a lovely warmth against the temple stones. So good to smell pumping blood in these halls again.
What is it, Visanne?
Zal-sa is done. You can tell <<1>> that he has quit. \n\n<<2>> may be able to deal with all this work. Zal-sa cannot!
I have nothing else to say to you.
Bandit. Butcher. I am not afraid of you.
We have nothing else to discuss. You will determine your own fate.
Stay your blade, Orc. The fight is over.
Well, what are you waiting for? Put on the disguise and let's get a look at you!
Ah! You are the five-clawed walker who helped at <<1>>, yes?\n\nYour story will buy <<2>> sugar in every city between here and Dune, so thank you!

Don't mind me. I'm just trying to compose something for the Duke and his lady. I understand she has taste and pays good coin.\n\nThat's if they stay together long enough for me to perform. There's a lot of tension in that court right now.
How many innocent people have died in those mines? The Red Rooks must pay.
Seems like the campaign against the ogres never ends!\n\nI heard they're still close to Wayrest.
Have you seen the guillotone in the marketplace? I think they're going to do something about that Dreamer cult.\n\nI'll be glad when this is all over.
This bodes well. With the beach clear we can take the fight to our enemy.
Enter Warcaller Targoth's memories. Witness my fate.
The storms on this island are not natural, and I fear that they play a part in the Maormer plan to attack Malabal Tor.\n\nFind their source and silence them.
Everyone's heard what you did at Firebrand Keep. I'll tell you now, it was a mistake letting that man live, after what he did to the Duchess.
If you have come to help, tend to the wounded first. They may turn if left to die.
And so, it begins. The remainder of the story has yet to be written. It is your story, now.
You have saved the Claw from true darkness. It is your sacred charge, now.
Agh … that hurt. Probably should not have done that, but … you have to find him. Fort Grimwatch is in the Northern Woods, high up the Reaper's March. This one thinks … that is where he's gone.
You arrived at an auspicious time in Crosswych. I came here to examine the citizens for signs of lycanthropy and found the town overrun by bandits.
I won't tell you anything. I won't!
When I get my hands on that useless Shagol, I'll rip his skin off!
I'm going to catch my breath before I head back.\n\nIt sure feels good to have feeling back in my arms and legs again.
There you are. I worried you met your end in the ruins. The souls of the dead still walk, and yet their torment has lessened. What did you do?
I'm still waiting.
You proved yourself capable in Bthzark. I trust you can handle whatever this ruin holds. I will remain at a safe distance.
What kind of game are you and my brother playing? No, don't tell me. Just … be careful.
Fine with me if the Pact controls Brindle. I just don't like them all over my town.
I can't believe this is happening. I think you should put a stop to it.

If you see any soldiers in need, help them out. Any one who falls … the Heritance will just raise them to fight against us.\n\nBut the most important thing is getting to the Mane though. He dies here, that's one more blow to the Dominion.
Akkhuz-ri was right. With Indaenir's talents and your skills, you make a powerful force for goodness.\n\nThough Naemon remains at large, this one believes the tide has already turned.
I know what to do, but you'll need to get me close to those rifts.
Go ahead. Do whatever you have to do. I won't hold it against you. \n\nI've killed a man or two myself who owed me money. It's just the way it goes.
I'll be better next time we meet.
You're strong, I'll give you that.
I'm not sure I want to make a career out of crafting mead, but I sure enjoy drinking the stuff! Come to think of it, I could use a mead right about now.

These orders make it sound like the Stormfists want something from inside the royal crypts. \n\nAnd they were actually signed by Fildgor Orcthane! That means the Skald-King's traitorous brother has returned.

Any questions you have about the job or your compensation should be directed to my father at the main camp to the north east.\n\nNow if you don't mind, I want to enjoy the nature all around us. Time to do more fishing!
If bigots like Talmo had their way, we would all be speaking Altmer.

Before I return this journal to Guifford, I must try to find a way to stop Faolchu. His werewolves can't be allowed to continue their attacks. My brother barely survived his encounter with the creatures.
The end of your journey is in sight, Moon Hallowed. Take the last few steps.
I heard what you said! You told that filthy lizard about our deal! Well, there's no going back now! Give him the ingredients and I'll pay the price.\n\nFancy me trusting some strange wanderer …
The Colovians will never see me. Field craft is my passion, you know?
I hope the Divines will still listen. For At'avar.
Juluda feels so alive! Hah! Bring on more of those Colovian bastards!

So, you've decided to help that drunkard, have you? No, no, do not deny it … your perfitudiousness is as plain as the flagrebex on your wheezax.\n\nGo, give her the meats you hunted. I know the truth, but can't prove it. She wins.
So weak, but still alive. My father. Where is he?
You've saved my career and my life, friend.\n\nWithout my instrument, I'm worthless as a bard. My singing voice sends mudcrabs scurrying away.
Are you prepared to hear my riddle?
I heard you helped my friends in Crosswych. You have my thanks for that.
It was a tough choice, but you made the right one. Good job, my friend.
All that trouble for a hunk of red rock. I hope this is all worth it.
I'm satisfied that fools won't be allowed to tinker with the relic, but I regret the lost opportunity to study it.
Give the husk to Rhea. She needs it for …. I'm sure she'll explain it.
You made the right choice. I wonder if we'll get paid?
Thanks for keeping the relic. You probably saved my brothers' lives!
Your choice was the right one. Do not dwell on it.
We have to focus on retaking Camlorn. It's all we have time for right now.
Marius cares only for himself. When I was dragging you out of that poison he did nothing. In fact, he mocked me!
<<1>> was a great man. He is with Arkay now, watching over us.
Yay
We … we have been betrayed.
We need you back at the fortress. Right now!
I hope you find the supplies we need. Lives depend on it.
May you learn much from these visions.
I … Hallowed, you must know. I would never turn on the Queen that way. These visions Hunal speaks of, they … they could never come to pass in the light of day.
Ho there adventurer! We need all the strong arms we can get, care to join us?
I need time to think. Becoming a bandit and exploring the world was all my brother and I thought about as kids. Now? I just don't know. I hope he's okay still.
So I guess if Sir Hughes killed the duchess then, crazy or not, the duke is going to want him to answer for that.\n\nI guess this means we're going to have to find a new leader ….
<<1>> was worried for a moment, but we've done it. The <<2>> is ours!
Kindly traveler, thank you. I thought I'd never see another friendly face again.
You should have listened to Jakarn. That relic should have been destroyed.
Giving Irien the slip wasn't easy. He said he would be right over.\n\nI wonder if she caught him? I'd pay to see that argument.
While I respect your heroism at Carzog's Demise, I cannot endorse your decision to keep that terrible relic. For once, Jakarn and I agree on something.
How could you give that artifact to humans? Get out of my sight.
I assume my family wasn't especially pleased with an outsider prying into our affairs. \n\nRemember, it was your idea.
You must be ready to leave this place, traveler.
You have done the work of the Moons and the Green both, my new friend. Our people will remember you for this kindness.
You made the right decision. Our homeland is safer with that artifact than without it.
I swore never to sail with you again. But <<1>> has asked me to sail you to Glenumbra, which I will do.
<This Colovian soldier has stopped breathing.>
Was destroying that artifact really the right thing to do? The captain doesn't think so. Still, I'm glad I didn't have to make that decision.
Hey, I heard about what you did at that ruin. Good for you. With that artifact, the Daggerfall Covenant will be stronger than ever.
I wish you clear night skies on your travels, Hallowed.
Get down! Dremora are just up the path.
The Moons send me nothing but woe.
We owe you so much. Finally, the Aldmeri Dominion can truly be called an alliance.\n\nBut, I'm afraid there's no rest for the heroic. I have a message for you.
Never trust an outsider! When Lokra dies in some ancient ruin, you will be to blame. Get out of my sight.
First the Whisperer. Now vampires. You think we'd learn to stay out.
<The Argonian lies unconscious on the ground. A poisoned arrow remains in a fresh wound. It should be removed.>
Come on back after you talk to Sir Lanis.\n\nYou know, if you feel like it.
Our thoughts are with you, Hallowed. May the Green watch over you.
May the end of your Path be marked by no sorrows, no sadnesses.
I don't claim the Bright Moons listen to me, Hallowed … but you are in my prayers.
Time to prepare for the Two Moons Path. Travel well with the Moon Hallowed, my friend.
I smell blood! And do I hear the clacking of senche fangs? You've completed my bounty, haven't you?
Don't worry … don't worry about me.
I don't trust the Pact one bit. Dunmer have always been the black sheep of Elves.
I took the liberty of weaving you into the ward so you can find the grove again.
Apologies for making you travel, but Zadala is already late for her meeting. This one serves the Queen. As you do.
Quiet now, or you'll scare all the fish away.
So many names. So many faces. Such terrible understanding.
The ritual is complete, and the Daedra of Ilmyris guard their very prison. Orthenir is caretaker now, until another comes to take his place.
It is always Hazazi who gets the worst jobs.
Raz looks good in this form. But then, Raz always looks good. Queen Ayrenn could maybe learn a thing or two from this one.
Are you looking to talk to me? You have that look about you.
When you're ready to go, just tell the cat … the queen, I mean. \n\nLike I said, may Baan Dar be with you. I hope you two can pull this off.
Hissmir isn't far. It should be easy to spot, since it contains some of our larger xanmeers. Pyramids, left by the ancients.

My scouts came back singing your praises! They said the Wood Orcs broke quickly after you killed Chieftain Thragdosh and unleashed the guardians.\n\nHmph. I wasn't exactly expecting you to succeed. Seems there's more to you than meets the eye.

I'm keeping watch outside, just in case any of the Exile's remaining forces try to cut us off.\n\nI heard you sowed chaos in there, and the army was able to just sweep in. I wish I could have seen it.
A friendly face? Does this mean the Daedra haven't killed everyone?
At last, someone who isn't trying to kill me.
Are you the Moon Hallowed?
I felt Fildgor's life expire. It left ripples throughout this realm. You killed him, didn't you?
