We all ask ourselves what our purpose is in life, yes? So nice to know yours. So nice to know you are needed.
Can't feel my tail.
As soon as the trolls wander off, we can get the loggers back to work. With the new roads being built and the King's work camp nearby, this place is worth a fortune!
I'm thankful that you came along. I thought for sure I'd never see my <<z:1>> again.
My cousin never returned and I'm worried sick.\n\nHe told me he was going to Icehammer's Vault. Did you come from there? Do you have news about my cousin?
Thank goodness you came by when you did. It would have been terrible to die before I got to see my sister's wedding.
No need to gloat; I saw it all. Clearly my hunters need more training.
Thank you, seafarer. \n\nIt is better if I remain here to supervise as best I can, but I know the king would want to be informed of what has befallen us as soon as possible.
Atarus is pretty dangerous, watch yourself.
The logging chief's cabin is at the other end of the camp. Just make sure you watch out for the trolls and the spriggans.
This should be good.

What madness. Soldiers died thinking our own ranks betrayed us. I'd like to feed those skin-stealers to a wamasu with the flux.\n\nI saw <<1>>'s guard lead him away before the attack. If his guard were skin-stealers, he's in grave danger.
Why don't you face a real warrior?
That was a surprise.
Impressive fighting.

Go find Thane Harvald at the camp. If he has any sense, he'll help us without involving that whiny Prince Irnskar. \n\nI'll deal with Guard Hloenor to make sure she doesn't spread word of this to anyone.
Go on. I must catch my breath, then I will meet you at the warehouse. \n\nThank you, seafarer, and may the gods be with you.
You should always address the king first when we're in the palace. That's not only the custom; it's a matter of respect.
I hear Lokra will be leaving on your ship. Good. She would never have been happy otherwise.
Lokra ignores the wishes of her clan. She fails all of us with her selfishness!\n\nBut I don't blame you. She chose to leave. That is her shame to bear.
Dremora and Shadowed Path cultists. How can we ever hope to defeat such foes?
Life is never certain. I take a torchbug, attach it to my hook, which ends its life, and hopefully, that of a fish as well.\n\nNothing's biting, though. Haven't been for days. It's a sign.
Need help with the trials or something? That's not what I do.\n\nThese xanmeers don't dig themselves out and keep clean of the muck. Neither do the other ruins.
I never thought I'd say this, but I think Lerisa has it wrong.\n\nBretons can't be trusted with an artifact of that power. You should have destroyed it.
Excuse me, but I'm meeting someone. Alone. Please be on your way.
I came here to get away from people. All their talk, talk, talk! Who cares which lizard killed which mer?\n\nI've got enough to worry about without listening to their noise.

There you go. Give the guards a kick and tell them to get to work. I've got cargo to unload.\n\nIf the guards can't help us, look for the dockmaster. Maybe he's got half a brain … unless the zombies have eaten it, of course.
My friend! I didn't think we would meet each other again so soon. I have great news.

Stop! You have no idea what you're doing. Those relics are the property of the Night Mother.\n\nWe felt their emanations the moment you removed them from their resting places, thief. Give them to me or pay the price.
Can it be? Are we really free of this place?

I think you made the right choice after all. The Shadowscales have battled our enemies for years … I should trust them.\n\nAnd I do. Their leader promised I'll be safe and I believe her. I hope to see you again, though. Take care.
The Bright Moons are with you, Hallowed. Shazah will be a credit to her name, leading her people with wisdom. And Khali's strength will be more than a match for the Dark Mane's savagery.
I can barely walk, much less fight.\n\nGo on without me. Find the others who survived. Our leader, Sud-Hareem—I'd bet anything he's still alive. Save him if you can.

I don't think I'd be much use to you in this condition. Go on, leave me here. There may be others who need your help.\n\nAnd if you find a Redguard named Sud-Hareem, tell him I'm here. Tell him I'm waiting for his orders.
Father! Sud-Hareem!\n\nMy father's somewhere nearby. I heard him calling to me. At least, I think I heard him … or was it the whispers? Maybe they're affecting me after all.
We've sent the recruits out to help where they can. \n\nWe'll hold the hall. We will hold!

I sensed the darkness in the heart of the one you fought, but he has already been defeated, has he not? And those like him … they may not all share his darkness.\n\nYou should have me call these people enemies, though?
I'm going to miss old Ezreba. Damned shame.
Be careful. <<1>> is tougher than he looks. And he looks pretty tough.
We've escaped!
You found him! Sheggorath's Tongues, lad. These ones thought you dead! \n\nMuzag's family owes you many thanks, walker-friend. And Tand-ma owes you his life.
If you pass through Dune, please join us for a meal. This family will always call you friend.
You have returned my Tand to me! I don't know how I would have gone on without him. Your kindness will never be forgotten. How did you get him out of there?
Still alive I see! Always good news. Never know what might happen out there.\n\nAm stuidying with the monks. Learning their ways. Very fascinating. Should try it some time.
My lesser minions barely slowed you down. I'm impressed. But you're too late. I've already begun the ritual. Once it ends, my corruption will spread throughout Xal Ithix!
That was fast, but I'm not surprised! Did you find the things we need to build you a guardian?

So you commanded the general to turn around and fight on our behalf instead?\n\nI suppose it makes sense. If the villagers of Vullain remain trapped in the Shadow Wood, why should the general go free? Very well then.

Three of the binding stones are up ahead. Each Keeper defends a stone, so be prepared to face them.\n\nAnd be wary of Rilis. He will no doubt attempt to … speak with you. I will prepare for a direct battle with him and meet you at the fourth stone.
Such a close race! Unfortunately, your little bit of stewmeat did not win.
What … what was that? Thank you for saving me. Did Halindor send you?
I have barely set foot within these hallowed walls and I already feel a thousand times better!\n\nAnd now that you are here, we can determine our next move against the vile Molag Bal.
The Dominion has grown quiet.
Being a scout isn't really my ideal job. I would prefer to be guarding a lively market.

Thanks for rescuing my companions, even though it means I won't be able to sit down for a while. Skordo was so mad at me! He's got me out here keeping watch so I don't get into any more trouble.\n\nMe? I want to be in the tavern.

This city shall serve you well against Molag Bal. Know that every choice you make in Coldharbour will have an effect on the Hollow City.\n\nIt shall be reborn with every person you save, forged into a weapon by your own hands.
This one admires your efforts, but the match is not yours.
I want to punch Tharn in the throat with every fiber of my being, but I'll be civil. Just keep him out of my face.
Arkay preserve us, you're as battered and bruised as a peach in a sack of rocks! Bit of the old derring-do, was it?\n\nNo matter. You'll be needing an escape route, no doubt?
The Elder Scroll of Altadoon has been returned to its rightful place!
I knew it! There's no way she could have been the assassin. See for yourself!

<<1>> found ceremonial garb in the chest behind me. He made it past Dominion guards, but one of their tigers sniffed him out. His wounds weren't too severe.\n\nYou could use the garb to seek out <<2>>. Just keep an eye out for tigers.
I'll answer your questions. As long as they're not spy questions.
Ezreba will leave Greenhill, never to return.
What is it? My husband has just returned home from the tavern. He is very hungry. \n\nIf I don't prepare his dinner quickly … well, I simply do not have time to chat right now.
You did what you thought was best, of course.
Why does the Dominion send Hazazi to places like this?
When you need my warriors we shall be at your side!
I knew that Dremora was going to be interesting.
That troll was not worthy of your greatness. Perhaps you should choose another.
It's you again! The hunters say the mist has lost its sickly tint. Did you find the source?
I have promised to stay my blade for the present. Go on, hear his last words, meaningless as they are.
No more. Please. I'm not like them!
<The statue holds the Gem of Endurance.>
I've got your back, good looking.
Fighting the undead always dulls the sword.
The guar watches carefully. What are the mighty wamasu's intentions?
<The statue holds the Gem of Endurance.>
<The statue holds the Gem of Endurance.>
Hurry, Targoth! Stop this magic!
Free me or kill me, Orc. Do not bore me with words.
Targoth! Our victory is near!
Trust me, the Black Daggers need to die. They're getting too powerful. No one's safe from them.
What are you waiting for? Stop King Renwic before he destroys us!
There is always more work to be done.
Thank you for your able council. May bright moons light your path.
Nice ship.
I'm glad we could help get the Prowler seaworthy. If the Sea Vipers are causing any more trouble, the Dominion needs all the ships it can get.
The gods brought us here for a reason. Damned if I know what it is.
Spotted some Sea Elves watching the ship. They don't look friendly.
Word reached the palace that Aldmeri forces were here, so the king sent me right away. \n\nLooked like many of the Elves were already dead. Where did they come from?
Make your purchase quickly, then go.
Warcaller. Does he live or die?
Can't you see that I'm busy here? Please leave me alone.
I'd suggest you leave, before ….
Dark moons, traveler. She was just trying to keep her love alive!
You looking for more glory? Get going, like Ezreba.
Go away.
You're in my way.
My axe is very sharp.
Have you seen any fresh meat?
What is your will? Does the queen live or die?
It is your choice. Does the priest live or die?
We have the king's child. Does she live? Or die?
Please take care of those necromancers. It gives me the creeps thinking about what they're up to in that cave.
The water weakens <<1>>, but I can't hold him for long. Quickly, go to <<2>>. Tell him I did what must be done.
Go, quickly. I feel <<1>>'s weakness fade. Hurry, tell <<2>> of the plan's success.\n\nBut don't mourn for me, friend. I earned a useful fate. Few can say the same.
Bruma is east of here. Hafza's goods are expensive, but she's the best supplier I can find. I hope the bandits don't come back before I'm restocked.
Good to see you again, my friend! These sea rats came without warning!
Hey there friend. I have a secret, if you promise not to tell, I'll let you in on it.
Your marine friends helped with repairs and protected our sailors from a Sea Viper ambush. Don't know their thoughts on privateers, but I wouldn't turn them away if they decide to sign on.
You have no idea what it feels like to have a Khajiit scratching around inside your head.
The Horns of the Deep! They must be destroyed!
I hope we have time to resupply before leaving Glenumbra. They have a good selection here.
So this is where we part ways, good looking. I still think you made the wrong decision, but I think I'll actually miss you.
This is actually quite fun. Look at him squirm.
We've all agreed. He's going to choose one way or the other. Or we're throwing him off the boat!
The irony is delicious. You could cut it with a knife. Or anything else, for that matter.
Ha. Those ladies are such fools! Jakarn and I have already agreed.\n\nWe're going to run off together and have grand adventures!
Well, if it isn't the hero of Betnikh.
I want to go back to Stros M'Kai, but no one will sail me there. My life couldn't get worse.
I was so certain I wanted to sail with Captain Kaleen. But I still can't believe she was in favor of keeping that awful relic.\n\nI think I might take Lambur's offer and join her crew.
Ah, my friend from Betnikh. I see you are doing well. Have you heard the latest from Daggerfall?
Oh. Don't mind me. Just making sure these cabinets are secure.
I was wondering if we would see you again! I could hug you.
Well. That was an awful lot of drama, wasn't it? I think I'm about done here. It's time to sail on my own boat.\n\nStay safe. We'll meet again.
I never did get to thank you for saving us from Helane's pirates. Wherever you go, friend, I hope you stay safe.
I think my hand's starting to heal. One day, I'm going back to Stros M'kai to take my vengeance on those Sea Drakes.\n\nOnsi watch over you, my friend.
Lambur's starting her own crew. I'm going with her. Now I just need to tell Captain Lerisa.
Oh! Don't do that. Don't sneak up on me.\n\nWhat's this? What am I doing? I'm checking the manifests, of course. As if I would steal something.
Why have you come to Captain Kaleen's ship?

You made a decision. The specifics do not matter. We would not be here if not for you, and Betnikh would be in the hands of a cult.\n\nI do not know if I will sail with Kaleen or Lambur, but I would sail with you any time.
Thanks again. Not getting turned into a zombie is the second best thing to happen to me all day!

I hope the message will give her some solace … and perhaps soften her heart so she will not be so angry when I return.\n\nShe is in Sentinel—possibly in the inn. Tell her I found Sabasad's remains, and that I love her and I will soon be home.
Can you not see that I am reading? Can you not leave me to my book?\n\nPlease. This is all I have left.
You're from off the island, aren't you? I don't serve outsiders.
I don't have any more gold. Give me more time.
Skulreid is in Cropsford. It's a small farm town southwest of Drakelowe Keep. He always pays a good coin for my fertilizer.
I hope the Pact can be trusted to leave Cropsford, and Zenithar's shrine, unmolested.
Yes, strike down the old Elf. His apprentice isn't my size, but she has possibilities.
Welcome to the Wayrest Mages Guild Hall. Do I detect some interest in membership?
Who are you? What do you want?
I never expected to see Covenant soldiers in Cropsford. Not sure how I feel about that yet.
I hope that sand makes Hisham reconsider being a farmer. He should be wielding that old spiked mace of his rather than a shovel.
Daggerfall! I can't believe I'm here. I've read stories, but the city itself is inspiring. I can't wait to go exploring. I think I made the right choice.
It feels good to be on a ship again. There's still much I can't remember, but I feel like being on the open sea will help.\n\nI'm glad you found me when you did.
Please hurry. The Daedra kept my squad alive for a reason, and it can't be a good one.
She's going! We'll be safe now! Truly, you've saved us twice-over.
Comrade.
I had hoped my days of being around Covenant soldiers were far behind me.
You must tell <<Ac:1>> what killed her husband.\n\nTry to stand to the side, just beyond her reach. A simple precaution.
You turn your back on my people? You are dead to me! Dead!\n\nGo and be with your Wood Elf friends ….
To think the Mane would betray us like this.
You've returned! And the Mane is here, unharmed! Jone and Jode are looking down on us.
Move with purpose, slowpaws. Only the fleet of foot survive.
<<1>> will belong to the sea itself before we hand it over to the Maormer! This entire summit is a waste of time.
<<1>> and <<2>> returned just after the skies cleared up. They're a bit damp, but otherwise all right.\n\nMy lookout says I have you to thank.
Thank you for making your services available. I'm confident we can resolve this amicably.
There's much work to be done, but the people of <<1>> are up to the challenge.
Thank you for sending her away. I don't know if I would have felt safe … if I would have felt safe for Lothiel with her in town.
Mercy, please, mercy! Save me from this madwoman!
Move. Unless you don't mind the spatter.
I wonder if you weren't sent by Y'ffre herself. I hope so. \n\nWe can't let these Hollow drive us away. We have to hold this ground. We have nowhere else to go.
This one is honored to know you, Grand Champion. Balag looks forward to seeing you fight in future days.
Congratulations. Your performance was positively inspiring. Perhaps you aren't the greenhorn you appear to be.
I've wasted decades studying Ayleid wells, and I know less now than I did when I started. I'm ready to give up.
Y'ffre's knees! I didn't expect to find you in one piece.
You're full of surprises, lovely. And aren't you the strong one?
With armies marching across Cyrodiil, I pray our priory will be left alone. But war seldom spares the innocent.
Back off; I don't know you.
Can you hear the crowds? They still chant your name! They thirst to see more of you, Grand Champion!
Our scouts say the Hollow have stopped fighting. Some have crumbled into dust. Others have simply wandered off.\n\nI trust this means you destroyed the Watchman?

I recognize you from Indaenir's description. He said you'd be coming this way.\n\nHe had hoped to be here to greet you himself, but he seems to have wandered off again. Regardless, we need your help, if you're willing to offer it.
The bindings … they feel brittle … less powerful ….

Thank you for sending those scribs my way. They mean no harm, they're just skittish from the hurricane.\n\nWith no scribs to protect, the big ones will settle down. Looks like you saved the whole brood.
I hope Asvorn will help me out of this pit. I can't take this much longer.
When Tertius gets back, he's going to be mad about what they've done to our house. I just hope he finds Donus.
What have you done?
Що тепер?

Praise Y'ffre! The miasma has cleared. Yet I sense this begins a new chapter for the Great Tree.\n\nThough the creatures gorged themselves upon its roots, this was a passing instinct. They can be taught to strengthen the Great Tree.
Chorrol's been through a lot. But we're tough. We'll keep rebuilding, no matter how many quakes and monsters hit us.
You saved my life. For that I will always be grateful.
The Divines bless and keep you on this glorious day!
Elsenia told me what you did. You can't know how grateful we both are that you brought us back together.

There is little we can do to help our fellow Ash'abah here now, so we should do as my father wished.\n\nWe should dedicate ourselves to destroying the Withered Hand. They killed my father; I will enjoy the opportunity to even the score.

Go. Find Tzik'nith to the northwest. She shall open the way to the tower for you.\n\nWe shall remain here for now, guarding the Wood Elves' tree. They shall pay dearly to get it back, and my people shall reap the profits!

You're insane to want to go down there. Go speak to Kargand if you won't change your mind. He's led the rest of the Mages Guild contingent into the Hollow.\n\nYou'll find nothing here but darkness and creatures born of it.
I know Hannura will like the fish. Cold-water fish are her favorite.
You looking for someone in particular?
You're back! Tell me everything! Did it go well? Were you able to convince them?
We must find the key. One of these muskarse smugglers might have it.
We need to get moving. This one knows his sister is alive.
Don't ever become successful—it's a killer. Gathering herbs and delivering them all over Cyrodiil is going to be the death of me yet.
I felt the magicka shockwave from here. I take it you destroyed the Engine?
Look, the vapor is clearing up! I don't know what you did, but it worked!\n\nI'll let you tell <<1>> the good news.
My shipmates're gone. Guess they're rebuilding the ship now.
We're on an island, and they have a temple just for water? Khajiiti aren't what I expected.
I've not heard from my foreman for some time. I fear there is trouble at the docks.
I saw smoke rising from the docks. Something is wrong. I feel it.
Did you close the door behind you? Check it again. I heard screaming.
Stay back, wanderer. You are welcome to our camp, but our chief is not entertaining guests.\n\nLike so many of our warriors, he has been poisoned. Only his daughter may disturb his rest.
I hear you're going to match wits with the Mad God! I don't envy you. \n\nMight I suggest looking over my wares before you go? You never know what you might need in the Daedric realms.
An undead scourge shambles from beneath the waves and the mighty Redguards drop their swords. It's either folly or cowardice. I can't decide which is worse.

My people's pride is maddening. I wish to protect the city, but I may well be killed if I try. It is bad enough that I dabble with the arcane—to strike our honored dead would be an unforgivable sin. You must save my kinsmen from themselves.
Welcome to the Sentinel Mages Guildhall. \n\nYou have curious look. Masura-dra is thinking you want to join us. Is this so?

My daughter is … not happy right now. She is as stubborn as her mother was, but … death will not be stayed.\n\nBe assured though, initiate … after you complete the trial, she will help you fight the Hand if you wish.
My brothers and sisters in the Guildhall do not understand why we keep our swords sheathed in the face of the Ra-Netu. It is difficult. But it is a needful discipline, good for fighters such as we.
Once again, we find ourselves in the Shadow Wood. As unpleasant as it is, I think I'm beginning to understand this place. \n\nI think I might know how Naemon's Shade is using it to corrupt the Green.
So you made it through the walking corpse pile? Good work. If you managed that, you may be qualified for membership in the Fighters Guild. You interested?
Was that an explosion just now?\n\nSpeak to the Mage. She's been looking for you.

The holding cells are below the Hall of Judgment. The captured mages should be down there. I'll keep the gate clear until you return. \n\nDon't dawdle, if you please. I'm good, but even I have my limits.
I guess you've figured it out, I'm not really here to "research" the Wilderking. Not for some boring book, anyway.
Please, can you hurry? I don't know how much longer I can take this.
It's done. The bastard's dead. Thank you, your help was invaluable.
Get yourself gone, elf-slave. Your Queen has no power here.
Sorry, the lodge is off-limits to anyone not part of the Pact delegation. Don't give me any trouble. I'm not in the mood.
Welcome to <<1>>! Enjoy our delicious fine wines. And don't forget, every day at sun-down we serenade the moonrise.
Well? Did you get me a drink, or are you still useless?
You never cease to amuse me, mortal. I shall continue to watch your progress with great interest.
And now I fade. Where will I go? What realm will I next call home?
Have you found my ring yet? I don't want to return to my mother without it.
You closed the Daedric portal! Moonhenge is back to its old self, plus a few decorations. But where's the Captain?
We're finally taking control of our own fates again. Long live the Fighters Guild!

I'm not surprised <<1>> sealed herself in that tomb. Everyone knows how she felt about <<2>>.\n\nWhen a puppy follows you day and night, it wants the occasional scratch behind the ears. More fool him!
Hushed voices and furtive glances. This isn't going to be good.
There, you see? You fit in and no one will stop you from walking away. But, as this one said, there are opportunities here for people that fall from the sky.
It is never a good sign when mages keep plans secret. Azsu knows this.
Thank you for the books, but <<1>> does not want you to forget what is owed!
Glad you're up and about, recruit. I'm in need of a scout to head to <<1>>. Most of our fleet foundered to the west, but we've had few survivors trickle in from that direction.
First the hurricane, then rats from the sea. What next, flying mudcrabs?\n\nS'rendarr's mercy, we need more time before the inspection!

Was the treethane as rude to you as she was to me? All I asked was how one might get an audience with the Wilderking, but the way she reacted, you would have thought I was trying to slaughter her children.\n\nDid she treat you any differently?
If you have come to speak with the king, the gods smile upon you, for he is holding court.\n\nDo not presume to waste his time though. He has urgent matters to deal with, and has no time for trifles.
I am so ready to shake the dust of this place from my boots.
I find it pleasing to take in the air of this city once in a while. Even if it means I must subject myself to the presence of Wayrest's less … desireables.

Did you see that? The Maormer mage had activated the barrier on this door to block us from getting to the Binding Pool, but I figured out how to break it!\n\nWhat about you though? Did you repair the seals?
Father's breathing grows ragged. This one doesn't know what else to do.
The stench of fried rat heralds your arrival! Are there any eggs left? Motivating tigers is hungry work.
Akkhuz-ri is not surprised that an Eye of Queen Ayrenn will easily accept what happened.

Oh, a familiar face. This one didn't recognize you at first, but you arrived just in time. Tarrami thought we were done for once <<1>> sentenced us to death.\n\nBut how do we get out of the Hall of Judgment? They're not going to let us simply leave.
Help us please.
Why did I let my brother drag me into this?
This one will make sure Kargand recovers. Thank you for your help in freeing us both.
Please get me out of here. I'd … I'd be really grateful.
Are you scouting Fort Rayles? I'd love to see it in Dominion hands!
Hey there, friend! You look exhausted. Take a rest. We're quite safe here. \n\nThadrig has a mace the size of a ship's mast behind the bar—not that I'd have him use it against the ancestors.
If you plan to loot my family's plantation, I will give you such a thrashing!
I thought I saw an old book or something by a skeleton near the panels. Maybe there's a clue in there.
If you stay, the guards will kill you. Makes no difference to me, but I assume it does to you.
Get out of here, shoo! If the guards spot you, I'll have blood stains to clean too.
Beware the guards, friend. They attack without remorse.
Is the Pact attacking Fort Rayles? I hope there's a lot more of you coming.

You have the king's gratitude, wayfarer. News of your exploits has reached the throne. While we cannot publicly condone violence against our honored dead, the fact remains that you have made the city safe. \n\nAt least for the moment.
The council has discussed what you told us. Debated your words from every angle. Even drew upon Faraniel's arguments from past meetings.\n\nUnderstand that we did not reach our decision lightly.
Oh, no. Don't tell me there's a Pact army coming. More holes in my walls is what that means.
Keep your head down, friend. The guards will attack you on sight.
You address the seneschal of King Fahara'jad's court. Spare me your foreign preambles and tell me your business here.
Watch out for the guards. They attack Pact soldiers on sight.
Be careful. They don't like Pact soldiers around here.
Crude, but effective in your methods. Perhaps you've heard that before.
You again? You are like dung Ishalga cannot shake from her boot.
Is it not enough that you defile our dead? Now you must defile our home as well? Begone.
You are brave to cross my threshold, wayfarer, with your weapons still soaked in my ancestor's blood. I will not have your unclean feet tread dishonor in my home. Please leave.
What am I going to do with you? Possessing this much skooma guarantees a decade in manacles.\n\nWhat aren't you telling me? How much will you cooperate?
How could you destroy this family?\n\nWe are ruined. Ruined!
My brother and I will guard this area. See what you can do about those reinforcement portals.
You have done well. I will burn an offering to Mara for the souls of my slain companions.
You got my brother out of there alive, and for that I thank you. \n\nI'm sure Mara will forgive me for saying it, but he's worth more to me than all the relics in the chapel.
Mara be praised, you've returned! Did you find the relics?
Zur's mind feels empty … silent. I miss Gadris already.
Thank you again for your help. For choosing me. But I wish that both Zur and I could have been saved.
I will scout this area and make sure we destroyed all of the Daedra that got through the portal.
There are two portals being used by the Dremora to transport reinforcements. You have to shut those portals down!
Well, that was invigorating! I love killing Daedra in the morning!
Is this my doom, then? To haunt this island, warning others of a danger I could not defeat?\n\nWhat a miserable non-existence.
Done already? Hmm.
We need trained warriors out on the battlefields, so hurry up.
So soon you've learned all there is to know about siege engines?
I head what you did in Shattered Shoals. Thank you for getting my men out of there.\n\nAnd I understand you helped the Prowler's crew, too?
This one hopes Ezreba finds a new standing on the Two Moons Path.
I'm worried about my dogs. I've called them for dinner, but they haven't come.
I hope this was all worth it. I was so looking forward to turning their minds to jelly.
You and the Champions … excuse me, the candidates. You must make for your next challenge. The Moons tell me that your next destination has been revealed to you.
The temple of the Mourning Springs has been set to right. The moonlight shines upon you.

Only the dead and the desperate end up in this part of the desert. You appear to be neither, so you must be a very brave woman. \n\nDo you intend to enter the cursed grounds, the Tears of the Dishonored?
We weren't prepared for this. The Daedra were too strong, even for our magic. I fear I'll never leave here.
He will not remain discorporated for long. His consciousness will be adrift for a few moments, but that is all.
Back again? What else would you like to know?
Cannot one set up a simple shop in peace? A ghost—one swears it was a ghost, haunting the lower platform.\n\nOh, my shop!
You have your orders. Move along.
Anxiety parches my skin. Too many demands, too few supplies. Are you here to sooth or irritate?
Done already?
You've already been through enough training, warrior, so get out onto the battlefields and help the Covenant take Cyrodiil.
If you're not going to deliver those to Bugbesh, I'll take them back.
Destroy those binding totems while we complete the ritual.
Nasty business, these rats. It is a good thing we have so many cats about. Little pests never stood a chance!
I think you have a fight you need to finish first.
I think you have a fight you need to finish first.
I think you have a fight you need to finish first.
I think you have a fight you need to finish first.
I think you have a fight you need to finish first.
I think you have a fight you need to finish first.
I think you have a fight you need to finish first.
I think you have a fight you need to finish first.
Too weak to move ….
You saved me from a terrible predicament. \n\nI wish you'd been around when I accidentally dropped that slop bucket on the Khajiiti wizard.
I thanked you for saving me from the crocs, and now I can thank you for saving our holy relics.\n\nMara bless you, my friend.
We were waiting to make sure you made it out. I'm glad to see you safe and sound.
It is interesting, yes? Shazah read for so long, she studied so hard … and yet I still feel like I was unprepared for this. She is very grateful she had you at her side, Hallowed.
Your bravery and spirit impresses even Khali. Truly you are the Hallowed. Shazah and I are lucky to have you at our side.

I would love to explore this lost city, but apparently we still have much to do. This planar vortex that Cadwell describes concerns me greatly.\n\nLet's head inside and formulate a new plan to deal with this danger.
Not bad. You're pretty fast.
You look good. How do you feel?

Aranias wants to see the Wilderking. I'm his gatekeeper. To see him, you ask me nicely and then I tell you a story. A story that you take part in.\n\nWhen the story concludes, you are invited to see the Wilderking.
The Divines be praised for your safe return.
I hope you've come bearing good news, comrade.
Ra'zaym hopes you have returned with something to report.
Well? Share your news with the council!
By the Green, share your news and be quick about it.
I'm going to pray long and hard to the Steadfast tonight. Ask him for guidance, and patience.
You must be here for the Trial of Spirit. Know that I am the Loremaster of Haj Uxith. I maintain the traditions and customs of my people.
Are you here for the Trial of Spirit? Then know that I am but a humble farmer, dealing with whatever this strange land throws at me so that I can provide food for my people.
Ah, I see the Trial of Spirit has begun. I am a go-between. I negotiate interactions between my people's two factions, as well as with the other inhabitants of Coldharbour.
I cannot believe this! He should not be here!\n\nAnd how can she go through with this when he made us wait so long?
The moonlight illuminates each of our paths and guides us to where we could go. Did the moon shine similarly for you?
What's this?
What's the delay? Let's get out of here.
Mages always have to talk at the end of the world.
Please, help Vanus.
Thank the Green you could see the relics into Felari's hands. To think, if these lives had been lost for nothing.
Are you from the Covenant army? I didn't expect you quite this soon—and frankly, we're not ready.
Make haste, now. My students and colleagues have travelled far, and we don't have time to waste.
Have you killed those wolves yet? It's vital that you do!
You've done so much. Helped us … what have I done?
We're all accounted for. Good. And now for the final step.
Now there's just one more thing, but it's a doozy.
This is dishonorable.\n\nBut perhaps necessary.
This one has work to do. Warlock Carindon can answer your questions.
By the tip of my staff, this place is fascinating. The flora and fauna are remarkable. And probably dangerous.
Pain is a small price to pay for the lives of two Guild Mages.\n\nThis one's lucky we don't off him like we did his friends.
I'm starting to think that studying in a dusty basement somewhere would be preferable to this place. Let's go.
Let's get moving. I hope the Bosmer are open to conversation.
This isn't going to bring Patraud and Ahainar-jo back, but if we don't get some information out of this Bosmer, their deaths are meaningless.
I'm not going to get up on your account, if that's all right.
The Dominion's enemies strike from within and without. It makes allies like you all the more precious.
Welcome to the fellowship hall. You're not from Bergama, though. Are you from Sentinel? \n\nNo matter, as long as you're a Forebear.
Welcome to the Bergama Crown Fellowship Hall. I do not recognize you, but I see you wear the formal dasha. \n\nI trust you are a Crown from outside the city?

Patraud was a good man. That attack … was unfortunate.\n\nBosmer can be aggressive, but killing without provocation is rare for even the most feral of their kind. The sooner we find this spirit, the better.
Are you new to Bergama? Many of our fellow Forebears have been abducted while the Magistrate does nothing. \n\nKeep your blade near to hand. You may need it.
Greetings, kinsman. \n\nPlease, abide a while. You should avoid the street. Crown dogs masquerading as bailiffs patrol in force.
Take heart, kinsman. Though Sentinel struggles under the Forebear king's yoke, Bergama thrives … or at least it did. Be cautious.
You've done a great service to the Bosmeri and Khajiiti people. A proud service.
Haven't you a home of your own? Go back and suckle at the teat of your Magistrate.
Honor to you and your house, traveler. If it is knowledge you seek, the Guild can provide.

It is good that the Redguard factions are feuding. Were they not so hostile to one another, the Guild would certainly be blamed for the recent disapearances. \n\nRedguard vengeance is … severe. We are wise to keep our distance.
<The Spinner lies silent and still.>
The chains behind me are like tree roots. I cannot pull free.
Greetings, wayfarer. Bergama is a grim place these days, but the Guild Hall always welcomes comrades in arms.
Welcome, walker. Grand Warlord Sorcalin has given me her orders. They can be found on the boards alongside me. Good hunting!
Hail, wayfarer. I apologize for my sparse stock. Many and many of my horses have borne my countrymen to safer cities. I find myself coin-rich and horse-poor for the first time in my life. A pity.

You do me a great honor, entrusting me with this Ansei Ward. I pledge to you, for as long as I live, it will not fall into evil hands again. \n\nNow, only the final Ansei Ward remains. But with Uwafa and Alasan gone, who could have it?
Please. This one does not need trouble. Take what you need and go.
Buy what you need and move on.
Yes, yes. The cats hold the city again. What can I do for you?
Ah, good to see a friendly face. Do not let the soldiers scare you. They will behave under Zetisha's roof.
It feels as if a light is piercing the fog. Perhaps I could fire up my forge again. \n\nI loved crafting weapons and armor. People came from all around to commission my work.
I'm so happy I could just sing!
Drink will help with the fear. Try some?
Mahirr has done as the soldiers asked. Do not ask him to do otherwise.
My students are busy right now. Try another time.
Hallowed, the Queen already has plans to make use of us again. Speak with her, if you would.
I'm just trying to sell some goods here, yeah? What can I do for you?
Ahh, the sweet smell of peace. It fills my nostrils like a fine boquet.
Tinti only sells to Eagle. No exceptions.
Look. Buy. Move on.
The waters of Cropsford run swift and deadly for Pact soldiers. Tred carefully here.
The guild is neutral in this conflict. Muzuli is only here to train who would hear her words.
Well, this should be interesting. You seem to be a little short on friends around here.
I've never seen such cowardice. These cats rolled over at the first sign of trouble. Bah! Sell you something?
I'm just trying to make a living here.

More brave soldiers arrive soon from Marbruk. We will rally them here and prepare to launch a full-scale attack.\n\nWhen your task is done, light the beacon in the lighthouse. That will be our signal to charge in and drive the bastards back to the sea.
We fought so hard for our people. To see him dead by my own hand ….

This one and his beloved mate sought shelter, but there was none to be found. Ernabi, she didn't make it. Now I lack the will to go on.\n\nOur children will grow up without parents. They will be poor and destitute and probably die young and alone.
Go! I don't matter. Ayrenn's all that matters now. Save the Queen!
You destroyed the <<1>>, didn't you? I feel different somehow.
I appreciate that you came to get me. A little longer and who knows what Drasilla would have made me do!
Get out of here! I command you to … just go.
Hail, wayfarer. Be welcome and drink—but not to excess. Forebear treachery runs canyon-deep here. You must keep your wits about you.
No, I haven't been slipping out at night to shank a few of these bastards. Why do you ask?
Hungry? Abject terror will do that to you. I run here every day now to avoid being kidnapped. \n\nIf you want my advice, stay indoors. There's Crown mischief everywhere.
Welcome to the Stone Oasis, O wayfarer. \n\nWe seek no trouble in this place—the streets are dangerous enough. So please do not show your blade.
Now that I have the designs back in hand, the question is how soon can we get the town cleared, and get people back to work on the ships?
Blasphemy! The Elder Scroll of Mnem has been stolen from our temple. I can tell you of the Elder Scrolls, but you will not feel their holy presence until our scroll returns.
I prayed Tu'whacca would guide you.\n\nDid you find Zariya?
The Justice always treated me so kindly. How could he do such a thing?
Istah. I might have known. \n\nMay Onsi pluck the tongue from his perfidious mouth. It will make bitter meat for the vultures.
Thank you for your assistance, wayfarer. \n\nThough the thought that I was serving a traitor like Sulma is sour as milk from a rotting goat.
Istah in the stocks? This whole affair reeks of treachery. The asps responsible will be put to heel—no matter how high they slither.
How could the Dominion have lost Brindle? Heads should be on pikes for that!
Aranias wants to see the Wilderking. I'm his gatekeeper. To see him, you ask me nicely and then I tell you a story. A story that you take part in.
I'd feel safer if Brindle were back in Dominion hands. I hope you're here to make that happen.
Our Justice heaps shame upon himself and all of Ruptga's children. \n\nMay his bones bleach and our memory of him fade.
Istah is in the stocks? I cannot believe a Crown could commit so heinous a sin.
You returned the Great Mage to us. For that, you have my thanks.
Aye, this'll do just fine.
A Crown Justice engaging in petty barbarism? \n\nI'm shocked, truly. See how shocked I am?
What now? Let Klovag know I'm waiting for him.

I have heard that Justice Istah has been placed in the stocks. They say he has done the kidnaping, but Tall Papa's whisper tells me he is accused unjustly. \n\nNow I will have to turn to one of the bailiffs to find my son. Tu'whacca aid me.
<<1>> heard about what happened on Viper Island. Those Maormer, they are not natural, yes? Just thinking about it gives me the shivers.\n\nYou have the spine of Alkosh to face such things!

Such a terrible thing, this storm. Dashed the armada to pieces, or so I've heard.\n\nIf the family fleet weren't in such a sorry state, we'd consider lending a hand. As it is, all we can do is hope for the best.
That Indaenir. He's quite a character.

Thanks for saving those miners! I'm sure they'll tell everyone they meet that my sweet trolls didn't really mean any harm. I can't wait for my sweetums to come back to me. We'll return to the arena in triumph!
Kargand is showing signs of improvement. This one thinks he will recover with time.
Istah burns in the stocks and still Sulma conspires. Something is terribly wrong here.
Have you heard they arrested Justice Istah? I wonder which bailiffs agreed to apprehend him.
Is that everything? My pipe, the wine, the delicious pork … yes, this will do just fine! You Dominion soldiers are useful folk.
This whole thing stinks. I've watched that Justice for months. If he's crooked, I'm a horker. \n\nThat Magistrate is hiding something—and I think I'll find out what it is.
My friend, before you go, Raz would tell you: he leaves now to travel to Senalana, an Ayleid ruin west of Arenthia. The Colovians are still fighting to hold those old stones. This one must know why.
The Justice dishonors all Crowns with such barbarism. Tu'whacca will judge him harshly when Istah dies, I assure you.
By the Eight! I'm so glad to see another living soul!

It is vitally important that we take the Chasm. If we fail, we'll never be able to cross into Molag Bal's inner sanctum and reach the portal to the planar vortex.\n\nCadwell will aid you. He sees the world in a different way, but he's a good man.
Very impressive. Shazah and Khali are lucky to have someone like you as their guardian.
Yes, hello. Unfortunately, I have no time to chat. I own a busy and prosperous mine. Can't get behind in my paperwork.
Istah thumped me for "public drunkenness" once. I say, whats the point of private drunkenness? Those're the folks with real problems, right? Right?
Well done, Hallowed. I know the Queen values your contributions to the Dominion.
I forsee great things in the Khajiiti people's future. It's an honor to have been present for such an important ritual.
Well done! I have every confidence that you're the Moon Hallowed these women need.

So Istah's been clinkity-clanking around in his shiny armor kidnaping folks and hiding their bodies? Alone? I don't buy it. \n\nEither way, Samhudah's still paying me a fortune to stare at a door. So all's well in Mauloch's eyes, eh?

My father sent me away when he found out that I helped you. He couldn't bring himself to end my life, even though that's what the sentence called for.\n\nI've never felt so alone before. What I did though … it was right. It had to be done.
They've put our Justice in the stocks. Akatosh help us. His bailiffs are even more inept than he is.
Why haven't you talked to that other Argonian over there yet?
Poor Istah. Such a stout fellow. \n\nHe never really extended the hand of friendship to Uncle Thakh, though. Perhaps his successor will be more … sociable.

My killer comes to humiliate me once again? Well, know that your luck won't help you here.\n\nI do hope you compete in this game. I so want to get another chance to rip out your heart and pull out your spine!
I'm glad that the Imperial has found someone else to talk to. His haughtiness is suffocating.
Scourge take them! The Elder Scroll of Chim has been stolen! I can tell you of the Elder Scrolls, but you will not feel their holy presence until our scroll returns.
I knew that Crown Istah was untrustworthy, but to murder that many people? \n\nIf he would only confess it would probably go easier for him.
I heard that that oafish Justice was arrested. What a delightful irony! I've been on his list of suspects for some time—I just know it.
You have what I asked for?
Thank you. I'm free again, finally. Time to leave this blasted cave. I hope whatever it was you were hoping to happen does, in fact, happen.

Wait … I know you. Why do you continue to hound me? Didn't you already celebrate your little victory with the pretty little princess, Ayrenn?\n\nDon't tell me you've entered this contest, as well? How … intriguing.
Again you remind me of the monster that I am. You defeated me in life, what more do you ask of me?\n\nWhat do you hope to accomplish by showing up here again?
Truly, I hope we never need change a story so extensively again. Though we spinners can do so, it's usually better to let a tale conclude on its own.\n\nUsually.

What foul magic is this? It's as if we've been plunged into a realm where the blight has taken over. Did you hear that voice? It referred to this as the "Shadow Wood."\n\nWhatever it is, it's not good. Not good at all.
She seemed very upset. Very upset!

Aranias was guided here to take my place, but I believe you were guided here to assure her ascension.\n\nIf you had not come, I fear Andur would have killed us both, leaving the Valenwood wild and vengeful. Many lives would have been lost.

I'm scared. Shouldn't I be feeling confident? I mean, we defeated Andur.\n\nLook at all of this though! I've worked my magic on small pieces of land in the Summerset Isles … but this is an entire forest … a living forest. Tell me I can do this.
What? Are you one of <<1>>'s thugs come to harass me again? You want your arm broken, too?
We came far too close to a tragedy here. If we'd wrongly slain Alanya ….
Back to training for me. Maybe if I ignore them, these louts Gudarz has brought in will go away.
The Elder Scroll of Alma Ruma has been stolen! I can tell you of the Elder Scrolls, but this temple is an empty shell until our scroll returns.
I'd probably be in a stew if it hadn't been for you. Thank you.
Once you put the boot to that spineless Nord we can finally have our camp back.
You don't look like one of these flea-bitten bandits. Have you come to join the actual militia?
Travel to the Labyrinth and stop Aranias.
Istah's collusion with those Forebear dogs has finally born its bitter fruit. May Tu'whacca show him mercy, for we Crowns will not.
This would be quite a charming view if not for all these oafish Crowns muddying it with their drab attire and sour faces. I honestly have no idea how they live like this.
Don't mind me. You seem a bit busy. We can talk later.
We should be wary. The way is guarded.
You know what's best after such a fine meal? A nice soak! The water in our pools is just exquisite!
Take your time and freshen up. The celebration in honor of Stibbons will be starting shortly.
I never thought that nightmare was going to end. Thank you for helping us.
Why should I talk to you?
These little militia bugs do a good job of keeping our camp going, gonna be sad when we run the last of them out.
Isn't it nice that the militia is giving us this camp?
I'm getting real tired of these militia rats.
Stop looking at my tusks. Stop it.

Now that we don't have to worry about overwhelming hordes of reinforcements, we're sending in the main assault force.\n\nWhile they keep Molag Bal's minions busy, you need to navigate the Labyrinth and find the portal to the planar vortex.

Have you selected a companion to accompany you? If you need more time to speak with your friends, please take it. This might be the last chance you get.\n\nWhen you're ready, I'll give you final instructions and we can begin our final assault.
Something's changed. I do not understand what is going on here.
The Fighters Guild is ready. We're prepared to follow you into the very heart of Molag Bal's lair.\n\nWe shall not fail you.
Well, I won't say that wasn't at least a little entertaining, but we're not finished yet.\n\nTime to enter the Labyrinth, old friend.
Let's tear this coward apart! Let's make Molag Bal wish he had never been born!\n\nWait a minute. Are Daedric Princes born? It doesn't matter! He'll wish something when we're done with him!
My people have been used and abused by the Lord of Brutality for long enough. Tonight, Molag Bal will feel the full ferocity of my mighty warriors.
Mistress Kauzanabi-jo will set you on your path, Hallowed. Good luck.
Listen to this, Kireth: "Reach out and touch a brazier to draw forth the fire and launch it in the direction of your choosing."\n\nHow fascinating! I wonder what it means?
Why do Daedra never install guardrails? It's like they want Zur to step into the bottomless chasm and fall to his death.\n\nZur has mentioned how much he hates heights, yes?

I recognize these devices. I've researched them. Even written reports about them. Never saw one in person, though.\n\nThey are marvelous to behold. Only a god could craft an artifact of such brilliance.
I'm ready to show the Dark Lord a little brutality of my own!
I promised to help you if you helped me, and here I am! I do not regret what we did to liberate my clan, and I never will.\n\nDo you smell that? That's the smell of freedom. And it smells wonderful!
You need someone to accompany you into the Dark Lord's lair? You freed the lamias from our prison, let me help free you from yours.
The Crown of Bones' power will grant us victory this day!\n\nI can't wait to see what treasures await us inside the Endless Stair.

This is so exciting! I sat around in a drunken stupor for so long, it feels so good to be finally doing something!\n\nOf course, we are going up against Molag Bal. Maybe I picked the wrong day to stop drinking.

You were a worthy opponent in the Orchard. I'm almost disappointed that we must now fight alongside instead of against each other.\n\nStill, the Crimson-Matron has sent me to honor your agreement, and I shall not fail you.
Ah yes! Did he find you? You must go to Tava's Blessing at once to help the prince!\n\nOh, and speak to Captain Rawan, tell him to send Shiri back here right away. Whether she wants to come or not!
<<1>> rescued me, though I guess I owe you thanks, too.\n\nShe seems nervous—you might want to talk to her.

Tava's Blessing is where the royal navy has its shipyards. You must not let the town fall to the Withered Hand.\n\nBeware of the shifting sands, wayfarer. I hope Rupta guides you quickly to the prince's side.
Get on with it—I can't do anything until you distract my father with a challenge.
We won't be able to use the portal until someone destroys those focus stones.
Another ally is always welcome! Join us! They will not take us—not alive, nor dead!
The matchmaker's interesting. He could sell scales to an Argonian, if you ask me.
Get out of my camp, while you still can.
If it's equipment you want, talk to Elthras. He makes the deals around here.
We won a necessary victory for the Dominion today, and we have you to thank.

I'm getting ready to cart this mead to the Vinedusk Rangers, at the village northwest of here. Everyone here thinks they're crazy, but I've been carting mead to them for ages. As long as they keep buying, they can be as crazy as they want.
Off to adventure in this cave full of bloodthirsty spiders, are you? Awful brave of you, facing so many monsters. Hope you brought some friends!
The Halls of Torment—I've never been there, and for that, I consider myself very fortunate.
It looks like I have a long journey ahead of me.
Your loyalty to the crown will be rewarded, my friend. You have my word.\n\nI can even make this easier for you. Wear this Imperial Armor, and you should be able to walk around the city unnoticed.
That Zara will flirt with anyone, or anything, but put a sword in her hand and watch the limbs fly.
The information you provided was very useful.
Hail, sister. \n\nWord has reached us that Talia now leads the tribe. Know that we stand ready to fight, should the shadow fall on Bergama.
May Tall Papa guide you on your walkabout, wherever your journey takes you.
I am extremely pleased to see you. \n\nI always thought the Imperials were civilized, but the way they've treated us, they're absolutely swine!
Praise Zeht! I can no longer abide these infidels!\n\nDid King Fahara'jad send his army?
Hail, sister. It is good that you have come. \n\nThe Withered Hand has been here—I can feel it. Stay vigilant.
You there! The Maormer attacked <<1>> with their Sea Viper forces. We need every able body for the rescue effort!
Thank the gods. I hope you're not too late. More Imperials are coming into Satakalaam every day. \n\nWe need to take back the city before they dig in.
Perhaps someday we will no longer feel the need to fight each other so readily. We shall see.

You filthy dog! You can hurt me if you wish, but I swear, you will pay for attacking our city .…\n\nTu'whacca's Breath! You are not one of them. Did the king send his army then? These Imperials could launch a full invasion if they are not stopped.

Despite the armor, it is obvious that you are no Imperial, and I rejoice that you have come to my rescue. \n\nThe Imperials have mistreated me, but I deemed it likely that they would seize control of all Alik'r, and there would be nowhere to flee to.
This one will be the next champion. Stay out of my way if you don't like the sight of blood. Especially your own.
I understand why you did what you did. In time, I hope my tribe will as well.
Bless you, traveler. I hope I said nothing to offend you.
Fight or begone. I have no patience for unhatched eggs.
Very good! That is all of the tears. This one is finally done with this nightmare-scape of Dremora and beautiful, though terrifying, bodies of water.
No end to these winged rats. Not that I'm complaining! Every feather's worth a fortune in gold to us now!\n\nYou one of the magistrate's charges? I'm only shooting the ones in town, don't worry.
I've lived in this town for almost thirty years. We've never had any problems with the harpies in all that time.\n\nSomething foul's on the wind. I know it.
Well, it is good you took the lid off when you did. It was getting stuffy in there.
You must leave now. What transpires next is between Hircine and myself.\n\nThank you.
Keep under cover if you want to stay clean and dry. The harpies know no end to their wicked deeds.
Go on in. I'll climb up the building from the outside; the harpies won't hurt me. Meet me on the balcony with whatever you find.
The troops can handle reclaiming the sanctuary, but we can only really end this if we cut off the head. Vicereeve Pelidil is getting further away from us every moment we delay.
Keep an eye out for my soldiers. I'm sure they'll help you hook some Fish Elves.
Give those Maormer a few kicks to the shin, would you?
This place sounds great! My brother says you can buy anything there. And I mean anything.
This one has heard some dark words about Pa'alat's master. He does not know if this Krin Ren-dro can be trusted.
I bet with both flywheels turning, we can get into Molag Grunda's lair.
You should get out of here! This town isn't safe for Daggerfall soldiers.
You must be a scout for the Covenant. Tell your commander that Therich Rorielle will be happy to see the Daggerfall banner fly over Castle Brindle!
Welcome to the tribe, brother. The wisdom of the Chief was deep as a well. I know his faith in you was deserved.

At least it's over now. We stopped the blight from spreading and defeated Naemon's servant … but at such cost.\n\nI worry about our decision to sacrifice the Eldest's Heart. Its absence will be felt, and without a replacement … well, I don't know.
You scouting Castle Brindle? I wish the Covenant would hurry up and take it!
You draw the sword for us all, sister. True honor need … need not be named. Avenge us.
Just get out of here, out! You'll bring the guards down on us!
You bear the tribe's burdens now, brother. Remember—true honor need not be named. Seek not fame or glory, only justice.
Do not look upon me with pity, sister. Hearts such as ours, crowded with great and terrible purpose, have no room for such things.
Fill this poisoned cup with our enemies' blood, sister. All of the Alik'r watches you. May Tava speed your passage.
Word swirls through camp like a dust devil. So you are Ash'abah now? That is good, sister. \n\nTrue honor need not be named. Send the Withered Hand back to Oblivion.
Welcome to the tribe, sister. I regret we have nothing to give but our blessings.
Both Zamyad and Parvenah took to the Far Shores during your trial, sister. I fear we will lose even more swords yet.
If you spot Donus on the way to Cheydinhal, please tell him I'm out here, looking for him.
True honor need not be named, sister. May your blade never go thirsty while these fiends still draw breath.
Go through the portal. We'll make sure this area remains secure.
Take the portal up to the next level. We'll take care of any Dremora stragglers who decide to cause trouble.

Hail, sister. The poison of Morwha's Bounty has run its course, thank Ruptga. It would take ten and ten to keep me from my work. Rumor swirls across the dunes. Some say there is a vampiric curse staining Leki's Blade, and now we have found proof.
True honor need not be named, sister. My son's sickness broke while you took on the crucible. You are indeed blessed by the Divines!
All praise to Ruptga: it appears my brother will recover. I take your arrival as a gift, sister. Divines willing, we shall fight beside you soon.
Ah, I love that song.
We've come too far to be stopped by a few walls.

Ah, little mortal! While it might be entertaining to watch you bumble about the Citadel, I would much rather just see you get about your business.\n\nI'm sure that whatever you have planned will ultimately work in my favor.

Cadwell says that the area beyond the pyramid is known as the Labyrinth. We'll need to go through there to reach the Endless Stair and the planar vortex.\n\nJust keep your wits about you. The Valkynaz is a dangerous opponent.
I knew you'd be able to deactivate the wards. The Fighters Guild troops have already begun our two-pronged attack.
Please let my Brielus know I'm all right. He'll be so worried about me.
Indaenir's waiting for you down in Verrant Morass. He's looking into a blight. I've seen some of the Bosmer from that area, and let me say—better you than me.
You're back! Did you find everything?
I'm hoping to fight in the Summoner Division, but Tholbor's really picky about who makes it to the final rounds.

I know what they're planning!\n\nThrough my Psijic projection, I observed an old ritual site north of <<1>>. The Sea Vipers summoned a powerful creature known as a storm atronach. They're funneling all that energy into their bound <<z:2>>.

It seems the necromancer Alasan underestimated you … I was hiding outside the lighthouse.\n\nAfter you disrupted the ritual, I went in and found Alasan's notes. I think I know where the Withered Hand has taken the third Ansei Ward.
Go to Woodhearth. Trouble stirs from our common enemy.
The Wormies must be here for what's under the Barrowbough. With enough of the little skeletons, they'll be able to dig up the big ones.\n\nI knew I shouldn't have said anything to that <<1>> fellow.
You'll find Ugorz in the Orc stronghold to the east, and Zirani in the Khajiit village in the west. Both were once-flourishing townships—but no longer. They'll need help to escape.
I'll be honest, I never expected so brave a plan from a Dunmer. Nor help from a stranger.
By the Green Pact, they're a tenacious lot!\n\nThe Daedra on the other fronts would have closed on us in that last attack if it weren't for you.
Taskmaster is angry. Taskmaster hates this Khajiit.\n\nBut Taskmaster hates this Khajiit talking to others even more. Go away, or this one will suffer.
I think you got them all! I haven't seen any wisps in a few minutes.

We must hurry to find the prince. That girl Shiri—she is not who we thought she was—she is heartless. Given the chance, I have no doubt she will kill the prince and raise him as her undead thrall.\n\nWe must not allow that to happen.
I am Grexev, lord of this border realm of Coldharbour. How pleasant to meet a mortal of your caliber so willing to kill three tormented souls.\n\nYou would make an excellent Daedra.
Well met, traveler.
Horrible, horrible strangers with sand for souls! May there be no moons in their afterlife!
Sigul-jo is angry. He is right to be so, but it clouds his thoughts and taints his spirit.
Curse every werewolf breathing! This is the last straw, I'm retiring.
Shiri—the scholar's apprentice—have you seen her?\n\nShe had the ancient text from the Withered Hand necromancer at Tava's Blessing … she was supposed to go back to Bergama, but … she never made it.
The pieces are almost all in place.\n\nWe can move against Molag Bal whenever you want. Attack now or gather more forces. The choice is yours.
What happened here? This is terrible. Did the Imperials do this? \n\nI hope Shiri was not here. Did you find any evidence that she visited?
Thank you for speaking with her. Very kind of you to stick your neck out for a stranger.
You told Sarolion? I can't believe you told him about how I felt! That wasn't supposed to happen! Ahem. Maybe I should talk to him too.
It's a lovely day for a fight to the death, isn't it?
I hope you win. If you don't, well .. it was lovely to meet you.

I can't believe it. Zara's tasked me with picking flowers, believe that? I'm a swordsman, not a flower girl! \n\nDamn my tongue, I can't say no to that girl. It's that purr of hers. Damned distracting.
It's good that Naemon's finally put to rest. Terrible what the Veiled Heritance did to him.
It's just as well Naemon's dead. Not to be harsh, but he would have always been a symbol for the rebellious to rally around. Ayrenn may not be perfect, but she has earned our support.
Queen Ayrenn must hear of this.
Remarkable how Valenwood rights itself. We have Silvenar and the Green Lady once more. When they are united, the Dominion will be stronger than ever.
With Naemon and Estre behind us, Queen Ayrenn will focus on Malabal Tor now.
Now to journey to Malabal Tor, another land this one has never seen.
Shazah is enamored with the story, but all Khali sees is the battle missed.
I feel for Queen Ayrenn's loss. She won't show it, but to lose a family member … twice. I can't imagine if I had to lose my beloved a second time.
Damned Heritance. We lost some good rangers out there. They're lucky I can't get near them.
Heh. Don't mind Nara. She's never done well sitting out a battle.\n\nIn the meantime, this isn't a total loss. Cariel is a beautiful Elf, isn't she?
I'm sure Indaenir will fulfill the Silvenar role admirably.
Indaenir's in there. I hope whatever luck guided you at the Pass watches over you now.
Don't mistake the queen's strength for callousness. She knows what's needed of her, as a leader.
Kauzanabi-jo was wrong about coming here. Hopefully, the twins have learned much from this visit.
We wouldn't have been able to fight all those Daedra without you. Gilraen will want to speak with you.

Thanks for all your help. Those Daedra would have slain us if it weren't for you.\n\nYou should speak to Gilraen—that Oblivion Gate is still out there, and I'm sure we could use your help to deal with it.
You have done a great thing ridding the sands of the Withered Hand. Take my ward and meet your friends outside.
I swear, no Maormer will make it past me.
Get away! I am safe here - if you want to help someone, help the hostages.
It's hopeless. Satakalaam is lost to us.
Where did they come from? How could they have taken Satakalaam?
Flee this place, fool! The Imperials will slay you, should they fall upon you.
I traveled long and long to reach Leki's Blade. What road do you come by, O wayfarer? I have heard talk of our honored dead rising to slay us. Idle rumor no doubt.
Swordsmanship runs in the blood of all Redguards—but there is more steel than water in my veins. They will erect a monument to me one day.
It has been some time since Master Fadalia joined us at table. I have counted the days—they are many and many. I wonder who she dines with.
Disciple Tafa says I swing my sword like a woodsman's axe. To Oblivion with that. If it is good enough to fell a tree, it is good enough to fell a man. That is what I say.
I have not seen Peruz since his final blessing. He did not even return to claim his bundle. He simply walked into the desert and disappeared. I hope it was not something I said.

You? You defeated Wildur? He's been our leader for years! This isn't right! You're not even an Ungodly!\n \nThe rules might say that we have to swear loyalty to you, but to Oblivion with that. We're bandits—we break the rules.
I beg your forgiveness, O wayfarer, but I must ask you leave me be. I am entering the most difficult stanza of the swordsman's sun prayer.
Leki speaks to us in this place. Come and contemplate the stones.
Disciple Raifa demands perfection, but tells me nothing! I may as well have stayed in Sentinel.
Disciple—I mean, Master Tafa—is at least as skillful as Fadalia was. The school is in good hands.
I trained with Milahd for many months before his final trials but I have not seen him since. It is a pity. I was a jackal's whisker away from defeating him in our last bout.
Have you come to honor the heroes of the past? Bring only a stout spirit and a worthy sword, wayfarer. Our ancestors care for nothing else.

I still feel the presence of Master Ahtar in this place. Some have even seen him, if rumor is to be believed. A passing shadow only, or faint whispers. I hope it is true. Perhaps I will see him someday.
There is power in this place, wayfarer. The spirits here are strong, but heavy with woe. They are well cared for—what could trouble them so?
Weight and balance are key, O wayfarer. Have you taken up a Breton blade? Onsi keep you if you must bear one in battle. Better to wield a boatman's oar, I say.
This way, the interior of the island has a chamber where I can cast the portal.
Some find fulfillment in wielding the sword—I am content to craft them.

Some may call me foolish, but I tell you—the stone fist of Leki's Blade has tightened its grip of late. I sense something cold … blasphemous. A darkness slithers in the heart of Leki's Blade, wayfarer. If only I knew what it was.
Hail, O wayfarer. Unless you're of a mind to step in, leave me be—I've much for which to account.
There you are. I felt embarrassed at my cowardice, sending you back after this thing after I'd fled. I thought I'd come to help you avenge my companions.
Good luck on the road. And come back some time, you hear?

I know I told you Farvad was probably alive, but in my heart I was sure he had met a grisly end. I'm glad I was wrong. He's strange, but he's a tough old priest. I'm pleased you saved him and recovered his ward.
Welcome to the Guild in Rawl'kha, such as it is.
I am glad you caught up. I am glad you came to the necropolis in the first place.\n\nTu'whacca says you are the one who must stop Shiri from doing this dark deed.
There, there. We'll be fine now. Fine. You helped us, and when the time comes, we'll help you. Somehow.
Sorry, Razum-dar was lost in thought. The Eyes are getting ready for, uh … something this one is not supposed to discuss.
We were so worried about the alliance leaders fighting among themselves, we never saw this coming.
Are you here for <<1>>? She teaches us how to … to fish.\n\nYou should speak with her.
Speak to <<1>>, or get out.
Keep walking, Thalmor ear-licker.
You're unwelcome here. Leave this place.

The walk through that tunnel wasn't pleasant. I never realized how much I hate cramped and crowded spaces.\n\nAnyway, thanks for coming through for us. I was worried we were going to be trapped in here.
All this sneaking and crawling around. It doesn't sit well with me.\n\nStill, the element of surprise provides a sound, tactical approach to the current situation.
Once the mages are in place, we'll have the Dremora on the run! Nothing clears a battlefield like a barrage of lightning and fire!
Y'ffre's bones! Am I glad to see another traveler on this road!\n\nPersonally, I can't wait to get out of here. Something really strange is going on here.

Exciting, eh? Beasties with wings, an angry Valkynaz—you even managed to befriend a Dremora. Clever, that. \n\nI made friends with a Dremora once. We had some grand adventures, right until she tried to cut out my lungs. Oh, those were good times!
Please, once they realize I can't pay, <<1>>'s life will be worth nothing to them!
The hide and my death approach. Please, let me see the white before all goes black.
I shouldn't blame Erinel for leaving. What we had was wonderful, but it was hard, trying to please everyone. I can see how her new life is much simpler.

I'll guard the portal and make sure we maintain control of this location. I may have to take on a Daedroth or two single-handedly, but that's to be expected in my line of work.\n\nSee if you can't cut off the source of those reinforcements, would you?
Just give me a moment to slip out of these bindings. Don't worry about me going alone, I know this forest as well as anyone.
Do not fear, Nielas. We will make it back safely. Fanrel … Fanrel will be fine without us.
I can't stop hearing Halalin screaming. What were they doing to him? I don't want to know.
Blood for blood. The Wood Orcs have learned what it means to cross the Falinesti Faithful.
Fire has blunted this one's claws. May others succeed where I have failed.
Did you not see the smoke? The wise walker would keep far from Dune, yes?
Can claws even catch fire and ice? If the Mages Guild cannot save Dune … what then?
Intriguing place, isn't it? \n\nWhen you get there, look for Nara. I think she's in charge of the small band that went there.
There is nothing to be done. For every Daedroth felled by one of our warriors, two more emerge. It is all too much to witness, especially for unclawed dung such as myself.
A troupe of valiant warriors. An army, with claws and swords and spears. This is what was sent for and for what Shimsamu awaits. We must hold strong, but without such aid, Dune is lost, no?
I'm certain the <<z:1>> will let you bypass the lightning bonds.\n\nMake those filthy Maormer pay for what they did to us.

We are safe here, at least, outside of the notice of Oblivion and whoever called it upon Dune. Many of us here are not walkers of the Two-Moons Path, though. This one wonders if a rabble of merchants unsound in body and spirit can survive this mess.

The dung life heaps upon this one is just too much! You might think, when traveling with your wares, that this thing or that thing will sell for quite a price to the merchants of your home. But nothing can prepare you for a home ablaze!

A walker comes to Dune! Is there anything that can be done for this place? Yanu-ma asks, for she is unclawed in matters concerning Daedra—as are most walkers in Dune, she thinks. All I can do is have food ready for those with claws enough to fight.
Hail, warrior. The guild always welcomes its own, especially when the campaign is going well.\n\nSpeaking of the campaign …. Any news?
The guild is always open to fellow mages … provided no other disasters fall upon Dune.
So many people! When did our quiet little city become a metropolis? But business has been good.
I'm not sure I like that we've turned the Hollow City into an army camp, but I can't complain about the increase in business.
Thanks to the stable portals, for once I'm in no danger of running out of supplies.
I think I liked this place better when there were only five of us living here.
Have no fear, citizen! The Fighters Guild is open for business!
Even far from everything we know, some things remain the same. Potential candidates, curious and adventurous. You should consider joining the Mages Guild.
Come, wayfarer, and abide a while. \n\nWe must enjoy these times of peace before those Gold Coasters come back.
By Onsi's bright blade, if one of those stinking mercenaries lays a hand on me, I'll split him like a dried gourd.
Those damned harpies made off with another of my ponies. By Saint Alessia, another week of this and I'll be walking back to Chorrol barefoot.
The keg goes dry again. Such is the way of things with these Gold Coast mercenaries. A long day of loafing and bullying makes them thirsty as the desert sand.
You're not one of those thrice-damned mercenaries, are you? My husband has already paid you. Begone from here! Go and eat sand!
Business is brisk. These harpies make bows precious, needful things. Everyone becomes an archer!

Walker, tell Four-Toes what you have seen? He has heard screams and the ring of steel, and his heart fills with dread for the city of Dune. This one stands in his stall with his wares, if you wish to trade. Better to die with gold in pocket.
Hello, if you'd like something, please talk to Nellor.
I do not know who's doing more property damage—the harpies or those twice-cursed mercenaries. Either way, I've been pumping the bellows like mad.
Whatever has fallen upon Dune, let them come to Kurnamu-do! Here, we have the advantage of terrain. No assailant shall make it past this one's flashing steel!
These damnable harpies! A seamstress of my quality should not be stuck mending curtains!
The sellswords are not as bad as everyone says. Better to have drunken louts for protection than none at all. Is it not so?
The mercenaries seemed so professional when they arrived. It was quite heartening. But they did not keep their true natures hidden for long.

A desperate man turns his back on wisdom. Better to unleash a pack of rabid hounds than for our magistrate to welcome into town cutthroats like the Gold Coast Mercenaries. \n\nDogs and son of dogs, all of them.
Of all the places for the harpies to strike, they chose our beloved Kozanset. \n\nTall Papa help us.
This inn used to be the jewel of Kozanset. It will take months to recoup our losses—maybe years.
It is good to be out and about. Coldharbour is an inhospitable place, but this one is adaptable.
Harpies, bullies with swords …. Fangs of Sep! What other plagues must we weather?
Welcome to the … the … oh, by Zeht's tears, I cannot do it. My inn is ruined!
Those Gold Coasters are nothing but but a pack of yellow durzogs. Mauloch help this town if real trouble comes knocking.
They should set those good-for-nothing Baandari Khajiiti on the bird-women. By Mauloch, they'd probably enjoy it.
Hail and welcome, comrade. Shake off the sand and relax a moment. I'd say you've earned a rest.
You got what you wanted. Now leave me alone.
Magister Zoellene keeps us cloistered while those oafish mercenaries roam the streets. We wield the power arcane. Should we not use it in defense of our neighbors?
Welcome to the Kozanset Mages Guildhall. \n\nI sense a great deal of magical aptitude in you. Have you come to seek admission into the guild?
What else do you want from me? Blood? Bones?\n\nYou got what you wanted. Everything else I have is mine!
You forced me to give you what was rightfully mine. What more do you want from me?\n\nNow let me get on with my work, please.
This one has nothing more to say. This one is very angry with you. Very angry.
Dearest Alexis, I feel so weak now. I wonder if the Taskmaster has any more of that marvelous energy he gave us earlier. It made me feel so … alive!
You look as though you have seen battle, friend. Tell me, did you find Aldolin?
Hm? I am not paying you for companionship. Run along and retrieve the coin we are owed!
Well, I hope you're happy. What's the phrase? Out of the kettle and into Oblivion? Shackled for life to Farwen ….
That idiot just blew my cover. I respect the Artisan's skill too much to believe that Hendare could find him, so what's your story?
Oh, good. You made it back! My band owes you a debt of gratitude. It isn't often you meet such selfless travelers here.
You are always welcome here, warrior.
I am here with the Queen. For now, the security of this point and surrounds is my responsibility. Please leave me to it.
I will be glad when all this is over. One way or the other.

I was the first of the advance scouts to Dune. I've heard a lot of violence from the Merchant's Quarter, and I've been seeing a lot of smoke. If you're going in, Y'ffre watch your hands - you'll need the help.
There's no reason for you to wait for the authorities to arrive. I doubt you'll retrieve everything in time.
Talk to Thrush. I'm not here in any official capacity.
I am their most beloved. I can feel that.
I apologize in advance for any delay in service. My apprentice Nidras went upstairs to attend to personal business.
I will await you on the other side of the labyrinth.
Thank you kindly. You'll find <<1>> on the west path into town. Hurry back now.
This one greets you, walker! Feel free to peruse this one's wares, as do so many of the good people of S'ren-ja.\n\nAnd should you wish a trade, by all means, let us talk.

This one welcomes you, walker!

You are invited to peruse this one's cart and goods, to see if there is anything you need!

Or, at the very least, anything you like. For if you like, you are invited to buy, yes?
Hello there! Please, linger a moment, tell me of your tales.\n\nI will listen especially well if you are open to trading! What better way to accompany a good story than good food and good coin?

This is one of my favorite caravan routes.

Things are pretty quiet, usually. Lately, though, it's felt like there's a lot of tension in the places we visit.

Interesting times make for good pay, I guess.
Keep away from me. It's bad enough that I'm here.\n\nI don't need types like you distracting me from my work on top of everything.
You've done me a service. I'll make sure that buffoon never sees the inside of Telenger's spellbook. You have my thanks.
You're a bit forward coming into my home in such a manner. Something you need?
Any luck?
My men are itching to soak the sand with Imperial blood. We're just waiting on you. Get those hostages out of the city so we can attack.
We will honor the Ayleid King for his sacrifice this day. We will honor … everyone's sacrifice this day.
Spiders do not worry me. Very large, aggressive ones do.
Whatever you are buying, decide now. I don't have time to waste on just anyone.
If you need food, be quick about it. Don't waste my time.
After you. I shall be right behind you.
You seem surprised, mortal. Did you not suspect my true identity?
