I felt too guilty to spend my cut from those evil bandits so I hid it all outside of town. I assure you, I've learned my lesson. You can have it all and I'll be on my way to start a new life on the straight and narrow.
May the Green keep and provide for you today.
Kala must consider how she will find the coin for travel. That brother of mine … never thinking of anything but the moons!
Have you found it? Without Red Mountain Ash, Thalara cannot make Nirnroot wine.

Forgive Split-Tongue his split tongue, please. Though many mock him, he still sees his friends about this tree, here.\n\nIt is where we tend to meet and talk of our days, walker. Every village must have one, no?

Warm sands, walker. This one invites you to enjoy the shade of our tree and our company, as this one and her friends so often do.\n\nThis one thinks it is better under the tree when certain merchants are no longer screaming and grunting, though!

Khajiit are friendly enough, I guess. But the little things they do when they talk to you ….

I don't know, I always feel like they're thinking about eating me. I just don't find them appetizing, so it feels unfair.

I suppose.
Damn that Molag Bal!
A miserable end to a pilgrimage, walker. This one arrived, to find this Stonefire cult has taken Do'Krin for its own. Moons above, what can be done? What of the Golden Claw?
The situation is far worse than I could have imagined. Maybe we truly aren't safe.
Everything we've done against the Tharns, everything that's happened to our fragile alliance … was it not enough?
Those cultists have certainly made a mess of things, Anil-do has seen. If Anil-do had more five-clawed walkers at his back, Do'Krin could be set aright, and things much better.
Shirai-ma sees such horrible things, even just across the bridge. How can this have happened? The roads were so safe!
You're going to die, milk-drinker!\n\nYou're going to get lanced through your arse, and you'll die on the arena floor in a mess of your own making, because you're not good enough for this arena!
Come closer—let me get a good look at you.\n\nI'll need to remember your face for when they haul your body out with the others. So I can remember to check my bets, ha!
Greetings, serjo. Your performance was impressive. I hope when we next meet it is to cross blades … provided I win my chance to fight you, of course.\n\nTime has yet to yield me this prize.
Stop filthying my air with your breath, or I'll part your head from your neck!

I'm in the wrong division. I keep telling them this but they won't let me change camps!\n\nIf you get into one of the other divisions, put in a word for me? I swear my arm is worth Malacath's attention.

How did an imbecile like you move before me? What kind of a world would permit this? I'm taking this indignation up with … someone.\n\nJust you wait. Your bribery or whatever will be exposed, and I'll be there watching you dragged through the muck.
It seems you will contend before I will.\n\nI hope you keep your head long enough. By the looks of you, yours would be a fine head to be tearing off, heh.

Oh, hello. Have we met?

I'm still trying to earn my way back to Wayrest. Did you fight?

I think you fought. Well, if you're still fighting, good luck! I think we'll both need it.

No, no. If you're fighting you can't place any bets.

This one has seen it happen, it is considered 'cheating', and the beatings those who do this receive are inspiring to behold.

Very inspiring, this one thinks - enough to say 'no, never.'
Hmm. Come here, sera. Let me have a look at you.\n\nI'm considering the guar I'm betting on in this race, you see. You look strong enough. But, well … so does everyone, you see?
Don't worry, Nellor won't be tricking travelers again anytime soon. Thank you for bringing him to justice.
You stirred things up. That race was exhilarating!\n\nI even saw <<1>> and <<2>> talking! Those jackals haven't spoken for ages.
It's the big winner! After a race like that, a body like yours has got to have a massive appetite. What say you slide me some of your winnings?

Ah, a civilized person. My partner and I are here on the typical business of House Telvanni.\n\nPerhaps after I've met my merchant we can speak over sujamma, in my tent? It's rare, seeing another Dunmer so far afield.
Fires in the city! Chaos everywhere! It's only by Arkay's blessing that we were not killed simply for being Colovian.
I've yet to read the latest texts. Have you read them yet? Thinking of all those pages makes my eyes hurt.

Honor to you and your house, sera. I'm here on House Telvanni business, what brings you?\n\nWhatever does bring you, may it be swiftly resolved. This caravan is a mess and its drivers s'wit. It's all I can do not to drown myself in greef.
Gore and glory!\n\nAny time you need a drink, just come to me. The elf-lovers here wouldn't know a good brew if it boiled their faces off.
Warm sands, walker. This unsleek and unfragrant place is an excellent place to sell your goods. Thus, this one remains willing to trade.

You have some claws, Khajiit, this one recognizes that. Do you have all five, perhaps? We shall see as you hunt the walls of Thizzrini.\n\nStill, you seem sleek enough. Sleek and dangerous. This one is glad for your presence, very … amusing.
What is it? Don't they need your help at the sanctuary? Get moving!
So much death and destruction. I don't know why I'm surprised. I never expected Coldharbour to be a walk in the snow.
We meet again, Vestige. I wish to speak with you on a matter of some urgency.
My poor Sayeed. He had no chance.
I'll get better, I swear.
My poor Jalad. He had no chance.
What have you come for pilgrim? Are you looking for me?
Hello, wayfarer. If I am not mistaken, you are the one I was told to look out for.\n\nI was asked to relay a message if I were to see you.
Your time here is done. But others still need to talk to you.
Oh! That was close! I almost put an arrow right between your eyes!\n\nI'm glad I didn't. With so few of us remaining, we need all the help we can get.
If Raz had known you would do so well, he would have scrounged you a nicer reward. Apologies. The Mistral armory is not what it once was.

News of this Indaenir intrigue me. Everyone I've spoken to about him says he possesses a sense beyond even the most talented scout—powers we do not fully understand.\n\nKeep him close. I believe he may be more important to us than we now know.

Did one of our scouts find you and send you this way? It doesn't matter, we're desperately in need of assistance.\n\nIf you are willing to help us, please step inside the cave behind me and speak with our treethane.

You need a citizen to stand in testimony against the accused, as well as physical evidence and a magical omen to bring a case forward. \n\nI recommend talking to my fellow townsfolk and searching the village for evidence.
I did not mean to hurt anyone! It was just a plant!
I'm eager to hear your findings, advocate.
We stand ready to hear your findings, advocate. I encourage you to ask the suspects about any evidence you've found before making an accusation.

We have always been a close-knit community, and many relationships were tried and fragmented in this ordeal. It will take us a while to recover.\n\nNevertheless, we are at peace with the forest once more, and that's all thanks to you.
You are always welcome here, warrior.
We Thalmor have utmost confidence in your ability to uncover the traitor in our midst.\n\nWe have set everything in motion—all you need do is strike the flint, as it were.
Dark clouds gather over Aldcroft. You don't need magicka to see that. But … sorry. You want to talk guild business, I'm sure.
Learn to control your anger and use it to fuel your most powerful attacks! So ends today's lesson. But then, you aren't in the guild yet.
Crosswych needs a stronger Mages Guild presence. Hmm … oh, excuse me! Sorry, just lost in thought. What can I do for you?
Every town can benefit from the Fighters Guild. Crosswych is no different. You looking to join up and make your mark?
That did make sense, didn't it?
Don't make any sudden moves, or I'll give you wings. Arrow wings. Because arrows have feathers? Ah, forget it.
So you're the common trash that Calastil hired to steal my cane?
You. You're that thief Laurosse paid to steal my husband's dog. I hope the rats eat your eyes when they lock you in the dungeon.
How low Earrastel has fallen, dealing with filth like you to take what he wants.

Oh I know, the whole thing seems rather rash and improbable, doesn't it?\n\nBut our methods get results. Bring back the rat parts, and we'll have a little rodent scurrying about in no time. Why, it will be almost lifelike!
Still a little sore, but I'll be strong as a mammoth in no time.
I wish you sharp claws and clear night skies in your travels, Hallowed.

Are you collecting junk for Adamiir's little monsters? Good.\n\nI make little monsters too. See this? It's a ant-fly-worm beast. I mashed them together and added a pinch of Adamir's life juice. It's an adorably gross little guy, isn't it?
Back again, I see. And looking better than ever! I hope you're loaded up with Red Mountain Ash. I can almost taste that Nirnroot wine now. Almost.
My heart lightens to see you again, friend. How did you fare?

Oh! About time you arrived. Listen, Blackheart is down on the shore somewhere.\n\nHe likes to pace the beach when he's on shore leave. And he doesn't find it funny when I point that out to him. Can you blame me for jumping ship?
Use the portal to take the battle to them! I'll hold the ship.
I just guard the barricade. If you have questions, speak with <<1>>.
<<1>> can answer your questions, citizen.
Did the mammoth escape again? You'd be surprised how such a large animal can disappear so quickly.
You're alive! Does that mean—did you kill the troll?
Head to the Barrowbough. <<1>> will get you inside, I'm sure of it.
Can't say where the Albatross will head next, but you're always welcome aboard. None of us will forget what you did here.\n\nAnd <<1>> won't forget, either.

So Treethane Rolon has you looking into the destruction of the sacred flower. \n\nI hope you understand this isn't just about a plant. The Green Pact defines us. Our whole way of life is based on it. I hope you take the investigation seriously.
Thank you for returning my commemorative censer. The Dominion brought Erinel and I together. Now if I could only untangle this line …
I heard you've been made Pact Advocate. Is this true? \n\nI want to help in any way I can. The Green Pact is sacred and the person who broke it must be brought to justice.
Did you get it? Did you find the wasp?
May the great tree Brackenleaf hold you in his leafy embrace, fellow-Briar.
Pray at the brazier of your spirit animal and receive Brackenleaf's blessing. Then return to me for the final initiation.
I do not look forward to running through the sewers. There's a smell you can taste.
Have you, by chance, glimpsed an older gentleman wandering these tunnels?\n\nBalding, paunchy, dressed too well to be gallivanting in the sewers?
I told you not to follow me. I didn't want anyone else to die. Why did you have to follow me?
By the Eight it's cold! I … where am I?
Don't worry. I'm a friend. The disorientation you're feeling is natural. It will pass.\n\nIt's been a while since Glaras sent anyone here. She's been more cautious since the boy Eringor nearly died.

If you want to join my Briars, then there is one more question you must answer. With which of the spirits of the hunt do you feel most closely aligned—the dark deception of the Snake, the dominance of the Tiger, or the cooperation of the Wolf?
We'll keep watch for another decade. We must be certain they will not return.
Welcome back to Coldharbour, old chum. Jolly good to see you! I was afraid you'd snuffed it.
I wonder what Rurelion would say if he knew I was this close to a Dremora?\n\nBut to be completely honest with you, she makes me a little nervous.
The power unleashed by that Daedric fire—astounding! Imagine the spells I could command if I could harness that energy.
You've done much to help the village. None of us will forget you. But now, I must ask you to leave me to my fate.
Erunor? Where is he? He's not coming, is he?
What jolly good fun! I believe the next stop is the Labyrinth, old chum. Shall we toddle off?
We know what you're trying to do. For what it's worth, I wish you luck with it.
It's better to know what happened to my lovely wife than to spend my days wondering.\n\nThank you.
Are you prepared for what awaits you?
Have you listened to everything Lord Varen had to say?
Lord Varen is not finished. Heed his words.
Varen still has something to say to you.
It is done, then? I would not have such courage. In my mind, you are a hero for what you have done.

I can't tell you what a relief it is to have your help. I'll stay here for a little while in case you have any questions, but then I'll head back to Shornhelm.\n\nI'll tell Magister Wulfdis I've dealt with the matter and he'll soon have his relic.
Have I convinced you, then? Are you ready to join up?
Hmm. This one smells some magic on you. Do you not sense it? Maybe Magrus licks your face while you sleep! Ha! \n\nYou should join the Mages Guild. We have much to teach you, walker.
The Elder Scroll of Ghartok is back in our hands, thanks to the courage and strength of our warriors!
Your father's words nearly bring me to tears, so proud am I to serve a king of such courage.\n\nGo forth, Sameer. Go forth and make your father proud.
The ring is ours for the time being. Guard it well.
I thank you for not condemning me. Even if you don't believe me, I appreciate the chance to clear my name.\n\nThough, if you cannot find the thief … I won't think about that yet.
You look like you know your way around a fight. You'd make a good Guild member. Ever consider it?
The Guild is wherever we need to be. One day we'll have guildhouses in every city, but until then, tents will suffice.
Before you ask, yes, Altmer can fight, even here. The Guild welcomes all, and isn't involved in current politics.
Make it quick. The Guild doesn't have time to waste.

There's no denying that some of the workers made some bad decisions. But they're not the one who orchestrated it.\n\nThey were bribed to administer that poison to the johads. They swore they had no idea it would bring disaster upon us!
What do you say, recruit? Have I convinced you? Are you ready to join the fight?

I can't believe it. You mean Anenya was actually telling the truth?\n\nThat girl has failed every assignment I've given her. She doesn't have a shred of natural magic ability, but if you have the Tear of Anurraame, I have to admit, I'm impressed.
Hello! Are you here on business for the Guild?
Victims, that's all we are. If you're not in an army, you're prey.
We are ready to depart this world. So that no touch of the abomination remains, please bury our items here and let them be forgotten.
Zaddo sets you on your path. Saifa sweeps the path with branches. Orthoron scurries through the underbrush. And Hadam-do lights the sky above you.
The moons speak to Saifa. They tell her of your journey with the Elves in darkness.
Good to see you again. Sorry, just trying to keep an eye on our friends out there.
Why would the Wood Orcs attack us? What did we do to them?
My father is getting crazy in his old age. What's so exciting about the mundane world?
Welcome to Brackenleaf's Briars!
I'm preparing a feast in your honor. Heart of the snake, tiger and wolf will be served. With a side of frog legs and mammoth tongue. We spared no expense!
Maintenance of our shrines is one of many duties of a Master Hunter. It may seem mundane, but taking care of the shrine is akin to taking care of yourself.
With all six Elder Scrolls in Covenant hands, our soldiers will defeat every foe we face on the battlefields of Cyrodiil!

<<AC:1>> was sealed for generations. There are many conflicting tales, but all agree that this was the resting place of <<2>>, a powerful necromancer and student of <<3>>.\n\nThe tales said nothing about shades.
Stay back. There's only death ahead. Shades boiled out of the ground and fell upon us.\n\nSo much death.
You made the right choice. Tharn's a snake. You want somebody you can trust at your side.\n\nCome on. Let's go split some skulls and bring Sai home.
Research. All I want to do is research! Why do I always end up in life-or-death situations?\n\nEither <<1>>'s cursed, or I am. Shades, boiling up from the ground? What next, trolls in heat?
You made a wise choice. Brains over … whatever it is that Titanborn has to offer.
The time has come for another foray into Oblivion, Vestige. We have one last ally in need of rescue.
Hurts … so much ….\n\nGo away … don't like you … anymore …
If you encounter trouble, would you please scream so I know to run?
What shall be, shall be. Only justice can restore our village.
I've learned to brew many things since leaving my home waters. Let my great misfortune whet your thirst.
This is all my fault. Oh, Eranas. I'm so sorry.

Be on your guard. In addition to activating ancient defenses, Montclair has somehow awakened the Ayleid guardians that haunt these ruins. You may have to deal with them as well as you make your way into the first portal chamber.
Either you have faith in the pledges of others, or you see things as they truly are. There is no middle ground.

It feels like there's a cloud hanging over the village. I don't like that, not at all—it's bad for life, you see. Inside and outside.\n\nWho can say what will happen from here? Who could know such a thing?
Lots of arguing in the tribe. I don't like that kind of thing.
Greetings, warrior. Grand Warlord Zimmeron has given us much to do. The Pact needs every hero it can get!

There are members of this tribe who are incapable of considering the ramifications of their actions in the long season.\n\nThe Bosmer welcomed us as they did for we are two peoples of two saps. We mirror them, as water does the sky.
You listen to Slim-Jah.\n\nShe knows the truth of things. She will show you.

From what I've read, Argonians are rarely apart from their Hist trees. We couldn't have them plant those eyesores here. Best they're to leave.\n\nOh, and our stores greatly exceed our needs. Browse freely.
There. That's done. The curse is gone. Now the only danger this axe poses is the sharp end.
I cannot believe it! My sweet Musi led you to my bones, didn't she? \n\nThat is true loyalty! Musi and I walked these deserts together in life, and even death cannot change that!
Help! Oh, please, help me! We were attacked. They struck without warning, the backstabbing bastards!
Finally, my child is restored to me! There's still much to be done, but you start with clay before moving on to marble.\n\n<<1>>, if only you could see how wrong you were.
Useless laybouts. Rank amateurs! It was just a simple list of ingredients. How hard can it be?
My wife—where is my wife? Where's Gilraen?

I saw what you did there. That was fantastic! I mean, the fire coated your fingers and then you went swoosh! And the fire flew like an arrow and the tubes lit up and the device came to life! I can't wait to try that!

Doesn't it kind of make sense that a foreigner might have broken the Pact? He tried to do right by it as far as I know, but isn't it hard to hold to something unless you've done so all your life?\n\nAnyway, thanks to you that's settled. Fancy a trade?
That's surprising. I thought he might be involved, but I didn't actually think he was responsible. Poor creature. Someone must have put him up to it.
Lyris wishes to say her goodbyes as well.
We really shook the pillars of Oblivion, didn't we? I'm going to miss you.
I have already said my piece. I have no more words for you. Leave me to my grief.
Don't dawdle. The Daedra could be on us at any moment.
With Aranak gone things won't be the same. We didn't see many traders before him and if word of this gets out I doubt we'll have more.\n\nIt's all just … awful. Poor Khajiit.
Yes, you have found Adusa. Now go away and let me get back to what I was doing.
Whatever the constable does to me, it'll be better than being eaten by a snake. At least … at least I hope so.

Oh, yes, of course the Khajiit destroyed the plant. He's been working for them for ages, smuggling in magical powders through his cart and mixing them into our drinks. That's why I only drink water I've distilled myself.
Fancy that. The foreigner violated a crucial tenet of a culture not his own.\n\nLike that never happens.

You have my gratitude, friend. Let us both remember what happened to these mages. Ambition can carry you to great heights, but when not tempered with patience and wisdom one will often find themselves plummeting to certain doom.
<<1>> kept careful records of her struggle to pierce <<2>>'s seal. They remain scattered in her tower.\n\nFind them. Use them to breach the seal and recover <<3>>.
Well? You should collect <<Az:1>>, yes?

The vampire commander is in the house on top of the hill. As soon as you get up there and start causing a distraction, Adusa will use stealthy-stealth to escape with these townsfolk.\n\nMeet us outside of town when the deed is done.

I'm sorry. Did you want to talk about history? Intriguing subject, isn't it?\n\nI've been in the castle library for days. Fascinating how accounts differ relating to the Siege of Orsinium. The second one, that is.
Thanks for "peace." Malacath would have it end differently.\n\nJust in case, I'll be keeping my axes sharp.
Heard Gargak's still alive, something about a mine. Don't care. Still feels like there's a snake in my guts.\n\nI ever meet him, just him and me, I'll show him how much I like that.
Yeah, I heard. Gargak's not dead, that's great. You did good.\n\nSomeone should filthy his well, show him what it's like.
I'll find a sparring partner from Gargak's bunch. Without poison, there won't be a match for me.

I can't believe it. He was right again. When will I learn not to wager my gold against Razum-dar's instincts?\n\nHe said you would be coming this way. Is it true then? Did you persuade the Wilderking to swear loyalty to Queen Ayrenn?
I don't care about the past. More ore to armor our camp? That's good.\n\nSpeaking of girding, nobody works plate like me. Browse if you like.
It is good you are here. Your talents are needed.
I'm helping Shakul arm the stronghold. We have an early start, if you'd like to trade!
Let me get this straight. Gargak's built another stronghold just across the way, with its own mine? That so? Wonder if he needs a good brewer ….
Gargak's still squatting in that old Imperial tower? Can't be good for trade.\n\nUnless you come to us. Trade?
Less dead is less dead. More mouths to feed, which is fine by me.\n\nHungry? I can help with that.

It is bad luck to owe a life debt to a stranger, so I have decided that you are my friend. Know that my people do not take such things lightly. If by life or death I can serve you, I will do so without hesitation.
This one hates this place. It feels … evil.
You! Come to gloat at my torment? Or is your appearance here a part of it?
The lever's on the wall right over there. \n\nYou're a real life-saver. Can't tell you how glad I am you happened along.
I admit that I didn't trust the Khajiit at first, but she's certainly helped us a lot today. I guess you really can't judge a book by its cover.
You're really going out there? To confront the vampire commander? You're so brave!
Quickly, throw the Prismatic Weapon into the Mortuum Vivicus!
If you're going to the village, get going.
Where am I? It was like I fell asleep, but then there was this terrible pain ….\n\nI remember you. You're the one who helped my husband. Oh, Renoit! Are you all right? Did I hurt you?
I must have a device or construct somewhere in here.\n\nDon't mind us. We'll hold this area. Somehow.
Do whatever you need to do. My brother and I will make sure nothing gets through here.\n\nWe might even be able to test some of Raynor's newest prototypes. That's always good for a laugh!
Well, that was short-lived. Go on, I'll get this bandaged up and get back to the portal. You don't have time to wait around for me.
I always wanted to see a planar vortex up close and personal. Isn't that sky spectacular?\n\nWait, what are we doing here again?
Timing is everything. When will the gifts be opened, I wonder?

This is absurd! I have committed no crime, and they are just going to leave me here … I would say to rot, but I will never get that chance.\n\nI'll be speared through when the city is taken, and then these damned crows will eat my remains!
Do not concern yourself with me. My wounds are only superficial. \n\nThere are many here in greater need of assistance than myself.
Like I said, talk to the crow. It knows more than I do, that's for sure.
When there's no knowledge in the tops of towers, check the bottoms of bottles.
Are you really going out there? To confront the vampire commander? You're so brave!
It's always an honor to have you in our village. Please, make yourself at home for as long as you like.
Friends, foes, and fools … hard to know which is which … or who is who. Choose poorly and wind up dead.
If you're looking for the Captain, you can find her in the camp. Countess Eselde says our primary duty is to always help the common folk, and that's just what we're doing here.
Come to join the battle?
The deed is done. My sister died with dignity and honor, still in the holy light of blessed Arkay.\n\nWe can grieve later. Right now, we still have a war to win.
<<1>> can tell you more. I need to watch the road, warn away travelers.
You should know <<1>> has some sort of position in <<2>>. Seems to think her reputation precedes her. No need to kiss the hem of her robes, but she's far less prickly if you show her some respect.
I'll be fine. There's still a chance to stop this.\n\nAnd after all "<<1>>" has done, you shouldn't feel the need to hold back.
It's not time yet! The mayor said you can't eat me until dinner!

Choice wins again. Really tugs at the heartstrings! Careful with those. Yank too hard, and the blood goes everywhere but up.\n\nI really do admire this town. Shame I can't take it with me. Oh, but can't I? I know just where to put it!
Ready to move on, hero? Verandis sent word to me. I know where we need to go next.
Forgive a foolish old man his ramblings, Vestige. We've no time for fears or regrets, our path is clear.\n\nSai Sahan awaits. Go speak with him.
Mannimarco. Bah! I do not like necromancers. They are ruthless, blasphemous, and egotistical. And those are Mannimarco's best qualities.
I'm worried about Sai. First the Halls of Torment, then the destruction of the Valley of Blades? A lesser man would have already crumbled.
Do you understand what you've done? Without <<1>> in <<Az:2>>, we're stuck here!
What more is there to discuss, comrade? Kill all the Black Daggers you find!
The Black Dagger bandits bring terror and death to the folk of Cyrodiil. You must help us end this.
I wish I could hunt down Black Daggers with you and the other guild members. But I'm stuck in here, handing out contracts. Go kill a few for me.
Despite his … abrasive personality, Tharn could be a useful ally. Sometimes the best way to find out whether you can trust someone is simply to trust them.
It would appear I have little choice in what's to come.
I guess I should thank you for getting me to a safe location. This is a safe location, isn't it? I need to lie down for a bit.
I just need a minute to catch my breath.
You've brought Lyris back! And largely intact, from the look of her.
The Khajiit wants us to leave? Abandon Moira's Hope? I'm not sure how I feel about that.
Go back to the Harborage. Get the ring to safety!
You should leave for the Harborage immediately! More Worm Cultists are most assuredly on their way here!
Our orders were to protect the Mages Guild in their excavation, so you'll have to see to your own defense. We're spread too thin to do anything but guard this camp.
Tragic. He did nothing to deserve such an end. He was the model husband.\n\nAlmost.
The priestess will set you after the relics we lost. I know it.
The priestess will set you straight. Mara's blessings be upon you.
Sai Sahan is alive? Thank the gods! He's a tough old boulder, but even a rock will crack if you strike it in the right place.

I hope you'll forgive me for making assumptions, but … well, you look like someone who knows how to fight. I mean, if not, then you certainly fooled me. \n\nIf you do know how to fight, well then, we could really use your help.
We will rescue Sai Sahan as soon as Tharn's preparations are complete, you have my word.
My poor husband. I miss him so much. But I still have family. We'll put this nightmare behind us. Somehow.
That structure up ahead is your destination. It was designed to be a mockery of one of the greatest architectural pieces of the age.\n\nYou'll find the Mad Architect there.
What a disaster! The blasted creatures came out of nowhere. It happened so fast.\n\nIf you're here to help, speak to Countess Tamrith. She's moving around the camp, tending to the wounded.
One portal to the gates of Evermore right here for you. \n\nGood luck. From what I've heard, you're going to need it.

I don't know if you picked the best time to visit Evermore, but if you know how to use that weapon, I expect you will be treated as an honored guest.\n\nPlease excuse me, though—I must see to my duties.

I was able to grab some of my wares as we fled the horrors in Crestshade. A good merchant must always be ready to help his customers buy and sell, you understand.\n\nAnd I am nothing if not a good merchant.
I've been salvaging a few things here and there. In times like these, you never know what might come in handy!
Squire Theo says Etienne is dead, and this Medya Zurric is the villain responsible.\n\nIt is good she is apprehended. Justice will be seen to.
We should just kill her. It'd save everyone the trouble, and we know she's at fault.\n\nEtienne is dead! She deserves death for that!

I've heard about what happened. It's a shame about what happened to Sir Etienne.\n\nI'm not certain most would have chosen to spare Medya, considering the circumstances. I'm glad you did, even if she was bad.
That Zurric woman let Sir Etienne die and she's still alive?\n\nWhat is Theo thinking? What are you thinking?

Can't say I saw any of this coming. I was sure that sweet old woman was just an apothecary, or something.\n\nThough come to think of it, I did think it was strange her house was on the other side of all the reachmen.
Give me one good reason I shouldn't march over there and take her head off.\n\nGo on, I'll wait.
Let me be clear with you: I don't care whether Medya Zurric lives or dies.\n\nI'm not carrying her. I don't carry witches. She walks. That's all.
I never would've believed Medya Zurric was behind any of this, but there it is.\n\nThis is just horrible. Everything is horrible.
They told us her son was a witchman! And she's still alive, right there? What if another creature comes out of her to kill us all?\n\nIt could happen, I swear it could!
I see you're still alive. I guess that's something.
Watch yourself. Wouldn't want these dead men making off with all the loot.
Watch your back. These dead men are hungry.
I have the ship's security well in hand. You'd do best to deal with the dead on these docks.
I'll protect the ship and Captain Marck. None of these dead men are getting past me.\n\nGet out there and deal with it. Do what you do best.
No dead man is taking our boat. No dead man is getting near Lambur, either.\n\nYou deal with those docks. We'll deal with things here.
It's like Betnikh all over again, isn't it? Like Carzog's Demise. At least this time, they aren't eating our souls.
Someone needs to deal with whatever's happened on these docks, and you're the one I'd trust to do it. Get out there.\n\nWe'll be fine. I'll have bandages ready in case anyone is wounded.
Worry not for us, my friend. This ship will not fall while we guard it.
Find anything interesting rooting around in my clothing?\n\nYou'd best leave.
Was that Queen Arzhela I saw storming into the throne room? She used to come in like that on King Eamond when he was … acting up.\n\nMaybe she's feeling like herself again.
Blessings of Tava be upon you. The magistrate of Bergama sent me hence to explore trade opportunities. \n\nAlas, it seems the people of Evermore have nothing to trade but trouble.
Did you see those witches back there? I followed one here from Hallin's Stand. She tricked me—the dungheap wench! She stole one of the books from the Mages Guild!
No wonder the townsfolk are so glum. Look at this throne room. I've seen more cheer in a mausoleum.
So Queen Arzhela's back in the castle? Something bad has happened, hasn't it?\n\nI thought I could sense trouble in the air even yesterday.
Oh, my beloved queen … if you see her, please tell her she must eat. \n\nSince the king's death, she just isn't taking care of herself.
My estate lies in ashes and the queen does nothing! Thank the Eight that Duke Renchant rules in her stead.
I'll bring <<1>> to <<2>>. I don't know if she'll be happy there, but perhaps the Elden Tree will remind her of Falinesti.\n\nAre you ready to hand over <<3>>? I promise to keep it safe.
I didn't burn down that house! I swears on all ten of my toes!
Stibbons is … Stibbons is a Goblin! Whatever am I going to do with a Goblin manservant?
This is it! Cast the heart into the circle!
Come back and visit anytime. Just don't tell Freyda that I suggested it ….
There may be fewer trolls if you stay out of the dig site. There is a natural path down at the northwestern lip that should take you down near the cave entrance.
Duke Renchant appears to be trying his best. Alas, his best is woefully inadequate.
There is no way I'm going back outside. These fools don't believe me, but I swear on Julianos' little teapot I saw a man get torn to pieces by a flock of crows not ten feet from me. It was horrific!
These foolish, dungy Bretons starve while a banquet flies overhead! Famine? Ha! Anisha eats like a queen! Crow is bony, yes, but tasty!
Curse these crows and their incessant cawing! By Arkay's beard, I thought gulls were bad.

I won't lie to you, friend. Things are grim. The king and his heirs are dead, our forces decimated. Crows are everywhere. People have lost hope. \n\nBring Strastnoc's head to Captain Hjurrun at the south gate. That'll be a big win for us.
Honor to you and your house, sera. Have you come seeking membership in the Fighters Guild?
We have an impressive assemblage of weaponry, is it not so? \n\nMembership in the guild has a great many benefits. You should speak with Steward Vedra.
Greetings. You look like you've got a strong arm. Any interest in signing on with the guild? \n\nYou should speak with Steward Vedra if you've a mind to join up.
Salt and stone, look at this. You swagger well enough, but how good are you with a weapon? If you fight as good as you swagger, you should join up with the Guild.
A wolf tried to eat me once, you know. Just because we're in the nature realm, you think we can be friends now?\n\nMaybe. Did that Hagraven trap your spirit here as well?
Ah, so many musty old tomes to sort and catalog. Some might call this thankless work. Me? I call it paradise.

Hail! Welcome to the Evermore chapter of the prestigious Mages Guild! \n\nI can tell by your eyes you're an avid reader. You've got the mage's squint to be sure. Don't suppose you've got any interest in joining? We're all about the books, you know.
I can tell you this much—with all due respect for the royal guard—Queen Arzhela could not be any safer than she will be under my protection.\n\nI look out for the ladies, you know … queens included.
Whenever you're ready to go to the parley site, let me know and I'll open a portal.\n\nLet's hope that creating portals is the only magic we need today.
Blessings of Julianos be upon you, my friend. Take care on the road. Bangkorai has become a dangerous place as of late.
I'm to travel with <<1>> to <<2>>. I wonder how much it has changed.\n\nDo you know if they still run the boars through its streets? I do miss the running of the boars.
I spent a month trying to convince Kerbol to take me in. Not about to ruin all that work by blabbing off to an outsider.\n\nIf Kerbol wants you to know something, she'd already have told you.
Most of these crates contain fabric and trade-goods, but no food. \n\nSoon I'll be asking the provisioner if he has a decent recipe for shoe leather.
Our guildhouse is new, but with the queen's blessing and your support we will grow quickly.
Gods, the duke could have spared us a few tents when we arrived. \n\nIt's bad enough to be forced from our homes. Now we have to live in squalor.

I signed on as a farm hand just days ago. Then the Reachmen arrived—scores of them. One stabbed my friend with a knife made from an antler! \n\nMark me, I'll return the favor when we're released from this camp.
I would walk on if I were you, stranger. This town is cursed.
Kerbol doesn't like us talking to outsiders. Too much at stake, she says.\n\nIt's a bit silly, I know. But after all she's done for us, how can I refuse her?
I promised to Kerbol, to the village. Please, ask me nothing. I cannot get involved!
Why don't you leave us alone? We came here to get away from people like you!
There is no time! Kill the Titan!
All are welcome among the Fighters Guild, so long as you have a stout heart and little tolerance for the darkness that has seeped into this world. Are you here to join our cause?
Yes! Happy!
I left the Alik'r seeking aid against the Withered Hand—but I see the people of Evermore have their own problems.
It is good that the queen has returned—she has a warm heart, and cares deeply for her people. \n\nBut it will take more than good intentions to reclaim our homes.
Hello! Do you have business for the Guild?
Well, you don't look like much, but you're welcome in the Fighters Guild.\n\nLong as you've got guts and the teeth to take a bite out of Oblivion, that is.
Every day is an adventure when you're part of the Ravenwatch, yes?
I won't forget what you've done for me.
Your actions today impress me. And believe me, it's not an easy feat.
Mannimarco is an egotistical cretin. The only thing more frustrating than a pompous ass in a position of power are those foolish enough to listen to him.
Yet another hopeful? Don't look like much.\n\nIt'd be wise for you to wait a few days to compete. I'll have moved on by then. You might actually have a chance!

Come on now, don't stare. Andoriel and Raz may be enjoying themselves, but this whole thing just makes me uncomfortable.\n\nI have no issue following the treethane's commands; I just hope this is over quickly.
I feel so beautiful and … tall. I could get used to this.

Isabeth was a foolish girl. I should have disciplined her better. Made her stronger. She never followed orders. I knew this way of life would get her killed.\n\nHow can I possibly consent to this alliance with her blood on their hands?
Thank you for helping us. I'm really the one that should have gone back in, not Isa. Hatmi is my sister. Stendarr watch over them and bring you all back safe.
You're no Reachman. Stendarr's finally seen it fit to grant me a little mercy.
I was on my way back to Evermore when I noticed Northglen's been overrun. Those poor souls. Simple farmers. I can't imagine what the Reach have done to them.
The village dweller didn't make it, did she? I didn't think she would.

Even together, my sisters and these soldiers can only prevent these Reachmen from advancing further south.\n\nDefeating the Dark Witnesses for good will require that someone goes deeper into their territory to kill the Hagraven, Uela.
If you're going to finish Isabeth's work, be careful. She's very resourceful, for a city dweller. If the Dark Witnesses have her, they could easily grab you as well.
We should return to my fa—that is, Captain Gaercroft.
Please. Get that amulet as far away from here as possible. I never want to see it again.
We thought we could protect these people, but we were wrong. The vampires overwhelmed us.\n\nCountess Tamrith has been trying to gather the survivors. Talk to her when you get a chance.
This creature disturbs the woods with the Sentinel's binding as a token!\n\nHas the forest not bent to the whims of the Sentinel already? What more can we give?
Well, look who it is! Fancy meeting you here! And you have that look in your eyes. \n\nYes. I'm betting that like myself, Rivenspire's troubles have become your troubles as well. Am I right?
I'll be watching for the flames. If you pull this off, we'll have to celebrate!
Just kill me, you crazy freak.\n\nWait, you're not him. You aren't dancing. Who are you?

I shudder to call any arena more civilized, but this notion of matches being to the death … well, it is concerning. I could live without an arm or leg or eye, but I cannot live without my head!\n\nStill, though, the notion remains tempting.
I thank you for bringing me closure on my son's killer. I know what I have to do now.
I'm sorry, I'm retired.
I fear that Montclair will have a surprise or two waiting for us within the Doomcrag. I suddenly have the feeling that bringing an army up here was a terrible mistake.

I hope it was not a mistake to send the herbalists out to the lake. I knew the knights would need poultices and I wanted to be prepared.\n\nI would never forgive myself if one of my friends was killed, though.
Hail. If you plan to journey to Northglen, be wary.

Our mission is crucial, guildmate. Never forget that. The war effort in Cyrodiil, the raids on our homes, the issues of the common people - none of it will matter if Molag Bal has his way with this world. We can't let that happen.
So now the new constable's going around confiscating people's things like he owns the entire town?\n\nI don't understand why the mayor's not doing anything.
I feel sorry for old Agazu. She must have known this day was coming, but the mayor should have at least given her a warning!
If you ask me, Agazu was never cut out to be constable in the first place. She's better at weighing down a barstool.
I've been waiting for weeks for those new amethysts to come down from the mine! \n\nIf I don't get a new ring, I'm going to be shopping around for a new husband.
Do you think the mayor fired Agazu because she's an Orc? I do. And if that's where this town is headed, I'll be headed to another town.
I do not understand. Why is everything so quiet? Things are changing in this town, and I am concerned that they are not for the better.\n\nPerhaps it is time to move on.
That Bailiff Sagabar is such a dunderhead! He takes three rooms for three nights and then he just tells me he didn't need two of them. \n\nHe gave me back the keys, but he refuses to pay!
<<1>> was such a grimy place. The new mayor is really cleaning things up, don't you agree?
Ah, such a shameful misunderstanding.\n\nPlease tell this guard you saw the thief that ran through here. You wouldn't want to see an innocent Khajiit spend the night in the stocks!
Surely this scoundrel is lying. I chased him here on my own two legs. He was only out of sight for a flick of the tail!

Shornhelm is no longer a city divided. I'm glad we were able to accomplish that before the High King arrived.\n\nAnyway, accept my thanks for the help you provided. I tend to forget to perform such niceties, so you may not hear that from me again.
I do apologize, but I can't speak right now. I must prepare the beds for their arrival.
While you were gone, we liberated the upper city. House Montclair's hold on Shornhelm has been shattered.
The fire warms us when we're cold, but burns us when we're close. No matter how much you feed it, its hunger never ends.\n\nThe fire is sublime.

The remains of the royal family have vacated this place. They return to the land of living to follow the anointed and to avenge their bloodline.\n\nPrince Adrien is the anointed. He too has been blessed to rise again.
The whole town went crazy! It's just inconceivable, impossible, unbearable!\n\nIf this is just how things are here, I need to offload my wares so I can go set up shop elsewhere.
Well! I suppose I can't go back to town, now, can I?\n\nI'll just make myself comfortable here for a while. This sort of thing usually sorts itself out, doesn't it?
I know there's a war afoot and all that, but there's a problem here at the graveyard. \n\nThe corpses are climbing out of their graves! I promise—this isn't my fault! I buried them all real good!
Speak with <<1>>. If he finds you worthy, we may speak again.
I can't stand all the bickering. Bretons and Orcs, accusing each other of terrible things. It's disgraceful!\n\nI remember when we were all just citizens of Fell's Run.
This one thought we were troll food!
Go on, my five-clawed friend! Show him the treasures you recovered from the tomb!
Hello. How about a helping hand? Seem to have gotten myself into some trouble.\n\nNot for the first time.
I need your help!\n\nThese blithering idiots are talking about selling us off into slavery!
By the Divines, have you come to help? Please tell me you'll free me!

You have seen the past through my eyes. You know that all of this is my fault. My involvement altered the power of the relic. I was forced to kill Leila when she became a bloodfiend.\n\nAnd now Montclair seeks to end death and claim Ranser's throne.
I've had some valuables go missing, but I can't believe that any of my neighbors had anything to do with it. We're all friends here.
We gave the Imperials a healthy kick in the buttocks, didn't we? I bet they don't stop running until they're behind the walls of Hallin's Stand!\n\nWe will have to go after them … of course.
As grateful as I am to have Emeric and the Lion Guard here, it's your presence that gives me the most comfort.\n\nWhere you go, hope follows.
Take pity, yes? Khajiit has not eaten in days! My family, they starve on the roadside! Anything you can spare, please!
You look like someone who knows the value of a smart organization. Let me tell you, our noble triumvirate falls far short of the definition of either smart or organized.
Very hungry. Soup smells nice.
I don't get a lot of business from outsiders and my stock is limited, but take a look.
I thought I recognized you! You were right in the middle of those Imperial bastards. Well done, comrade. Stendarr protect you.
Hey, you're one of those Hollow Moon types! What do ya got for me?
Spare some food for an old coin?
The camp is just south of the abandoned Orc settlement.
Thank you for … for your kindness. Once … once I'm strong again, I'll find a way to re … to repay you.

Did the captain give you the poultices? Hang on to them. They heal the user and grant temporary invisibility.\n\nThere should be enough for you as well once you find all the scouts. It wears off rather quickly, so don't use it until the time is right.
My brother sleeps now, and he is quiet. A welcome reprieve, if fleeting. Soon, the shakes will return.
You my friend are a murderer and I should have you arrested. You have slain my hunger!
You found my Puddles!
I don't need your charity, whelp … but I do appreciate it.
We've done it! We've reached the top of the Doomcrag! Now we can finally learn the secret of the ancient Ayleid relic and save my wife.
Verandis, you mustn't say anything. Please! I'm sure this will … this will pass. I just need the stone. Another treatment and I'll be fine.
We are not the woods' master, nor is it ours. It's a rather complicated arrangement, as are most such dependencies.
We're free!\n\nI … had I tears to shed I would weep.

Are the nobles still bickering? Or discussing strategy, as they like to say? Gives me a headache.\n\nI needed to do something, so I decided to look around in here. Seems to be something up ahead, past the angry skeletons.
A team works best together when the members know and trust each other, but I can understand if you're ready to get to work.
Our lives are simple, and our motives pure. There's nothing better than a clear conscience, is there?
Oh divine lord, protector of the eternal balance between life and death, I beseech you … remove this dark curse from your sacred grounds …
I hope you do not intend to sojourn south, wayfarer. The situation is even worse there, I assure you.
The Mad Architect is gone! We've won!
I didn't want it to end this way ….
Greetings, comrade! You come to me with bloodied claws, yes?
Ugh. Are you as anxious as I am to get out of this place?
Hold a moment. What business have you in Bangkorai Garr—oh. A thousand pardons, I didn't recognize you. Welcome back, my lady.
Be quiet, walker! This one listens for sounds of another Imperial raid! Must stay focused!

Have you been to Pelin Graveyard? 

I … I just need a minute. 

Actually, I need a drink.
What did you use to ward against the plague again?
Pay attention, walker! Crazy Eye sees more Imperials coming!
No more bandits to fight. Oh, well.\n\nIt's all right. Was running out of room on my blades for notches.

I'll be honest with you. I didn't think we could retake the garrison. I expected to die here. I was even looking forward to it.\n\nBut my heart is filled with happiness right now. Not for myself, but for the people of Evermore.
Hello, friend. Do you need directions to the inn?

Good. We will set aside differences for the sake of Tamriel.\n\nWe need to know what happened here, and surviving members of the group sent to destroy the Dark Anchor will know best. We must split up and search.
Ah, a hatchling in search of wisdom. Are you acquainted with the Mages Guild, my friend? You would do well to join us.
How dare the fools invade Ravenwatch Castle! Did they really think they could prevail against us?
<The suspicious bottle is empty.>
<<1>> wants to speak with you. I've opened a portal. Step through whenever you're ready.
Montclair's nephew is close. Adusa can smell Rohlbert from here.
Any ore will be back as far we can go. The walls near the entrance are all played out.
She's warming up to me. I can tell.
Look, I've just about had it ….\n\nOh! I'm sorry. I thought you were that lecherous bailiff again. He tries to grope me every time I bring him a drink.
Go on now. Give the trinket a try!

You know, I've been drinking at this inn for years, and I always sit in the same chair. Right over there. But that bothersome new bailiff made me leave. \n\nSaid the table is his and I should just drink over here. What an arse!
I can't say I enjoy this, but knowing <<1>> is trapped inside these walls gives me no small amount of satisfaction.
They're back! And he is in so much trouble! Thank you.
<<1>>! Thank the Divines for you, pup! And you as well, stranger. Did he come and find you? He's such a good boy!
<<<1>> barks excitedly.>
Do you see this? Reachmen all over Northglen! My family ….
What word, my friend? Is Verandis ready for the troops to ascend the Doomcrag?
I rejoice that you still live. Arkay's blessings served you well. Cesabelle has returned. What of the others?
These are all the supplies we have left. If the Imperials want them, they'll have to go through me to get them.
Is there anything I can do for you?

So the bright, young Countess Tamrith is your choice. I know she is thoughtful, humble, and sharp as an assassin's dagger. I am sure she will make a courageous queen.\n\nQueen Eselde of Shornhelm. It even has a nice ring to it.
So little time, so many dead … I'd wager those corpses up at Flyleaf Catacombs are going to be pretty ripe before I get to them.
The king won't keep us here forever. For all his flaws, my cousin believes himself to be a just man.\n\nHe can't leave us here to rot.

Thank you for the vote of confidence, my friend. I promise you, I will do everything in my power to restore Rivenspire to its former glory.\n\nWe will tell stories of your courage to inspire our soldiers. And you will always be welcome here.
Thank you for your faith in me. I will do all that I can to prove I deserve this honor.\n\nAnd you. You will always be welcome in Shornhelm.
Ayleid defenses? That doesn't sound good. Well, I'm sure you can handle it. Just give a holler if there's any way I can lend a hand.
I shall need time to unravel the sorcery that controls this orb.
Anything else?
Keep it under your hat, but I've got something coming up over in Dawnmead, in the little town of Pa'alat. If you find yourself there anytime soon, it'd be a pleasure to work with you again.
Aha! My mercenary friend. Seeing you does me good, but the look on <<1>>'s face, aheh. A price beyond measure.
Well done. You fought like a Vinedusk Ranger.\n\nWith <<1>>'s sons in custody, the Blacksap is dead. Perhaps <<2>> will finally be at peace.
The more I think about it, the more I like this idea of moving to Shornhelm and turning honest. \n\nJust a few more deals and I might even have the coin. I'll start saving up tomorrow.
Look here! If it isn't Strastnoc's bane!\n\nHave you come down to lop off a few more Reachmen heads? There are plenty to go around down these parts.
<<<1>> barks excitedly.>
Our family is back together. I can never thank you enough.
Ironic. We come back to my homeland and I'm the one that falls into a ravine. I used to scale these rocks like they were stairs.\n\nI guess none of us are immune to the ravages of time.
Whatever are you doing in this place? I'm somewhat perplexed by your appearance in this backwater.\n\nStill, it's not as though we can be too picky about our help these days.
My people are lucky to have someone like you standing by the candidates. Well done, Hallowed.
You've done well, Hallowed. I can see the echoes of moonlight hanging in the air. Jone and Jode … they are pleased.
I hope these relics truly help against the undead. Alvaren is confident they will. We shall see.
If you unlock this cage, I'll be your best friend for life.
Make sure to say hello to the grumpy Redguard over there. He may seem cranky, but he's a good man and a better vampire slayer.
If you are done delaying our mission, let the big Nord over there know.
The spider cave is near Camp Tamrith, but I wouldn't want to face the spider queen one-on-one, even if I wasn't a coward with a splitting headache.
I'm never drinking another drop. Just water for me from now on. Well, beer is mostly water. Just water. And beer.
I'm glad this <<1>> business is settled.\n\nBetween the two of us, I'm tired of all this talk of embassies.
The preparations for this ratification ceremony seem endless. But I'm up to the task.

Join me for a cup of mead. A toast to those we've lost. My parents to death and my sister to her crazy dreams. \n\nWe're all going to go sometime. We might as well have a drink or two before it happens.
That's far enough. The storeroom is off limits. <<1>>'s orders.
Please, look for Firaelion in the cave to the north. But be careful. I couldn't bear it if something happened to you, too.
I won't forget how you saved me from the spiders. If there's anything I can ever do for you, please don't hesitate to ask.
This will be a day long remembered.
Thank you, outsider.
Do it. And quickly.

Ah, the proven hunter. I see you have the briarheart, torn from the chest of the Reachman. His punishment for failure is to roam the Hunting Grounds as prey. His chest, a gaping hollow, a reminder of his weakness.
There! See, I told you it would work!
Saw you standing over the body of a dead Wood Elf. Nearly put an arrow in your throat.\n\nGood thing I recognize you.

I have things about as under control in here as they can be.

You should go on ahead - if you can do anything about our entrenchment here, please do.

Our injured soldiers would thank you for it.
My head feels like a thunderbug crawled inside it.\n\nBut I did win our contest. Oblan will bring the laundry for you. Every morning.

Here we have the savior of Shornhelm, I presume? You should know that Baron Dorell and Countess Tamrith have been quite generous in their praise of you. \n\nI trust you were able to close this portal Montclair was using to bring in reinforcements?
My father has many friends in <<1>>. They'll see us out of this mess.
Not sure what's more surprising—that we made it to Shornhelm or that you did. Did you find Marien's necklace?
Oh, hello! Our friend from the road. Nothing like good honest work to make you feel alive, am I right?
By the look of things, you're probably one of the ones fighting the Reachmen. That's good.\n\nWe don't have dissimilar goals, but remember: That doesn't make us friends.
Hey! I'd recognize that bow anywhere. Where did you get that?
<<1>> said the entrance to the vampire's lord lair is in the valley north of town. We need to get there immediately.
Just place my family's ashes in each of the graves. Then I'll say a few words to send them on their way.
It's a great comfort to have you participate in this solemn occasion. I think my little brother would have liked you. A lot.
All that we can do, all that we can become, now that we are free, is halting. We do not know where to begin.

Look for a ship called the Dawn Posset offshore at Northpoint. The first mate, Elvira Derre, should be waiting for you on the docks, ready to leave for Sentinel.\n\nWhen you get there, just make sure the city is safe. Only visit my father if you wish.
Ah, good. You've returned. Sai Sahan has recovered, and there is much to be done.
The people of <<1>> will know what we've done for the Green Pact. The king won't have any recourse but to pardon us all.\n\nYou've done more for the Blacksap Rebellion than you'll ever know.
Why do I think this isn't going to end well—for me?
I've been thinking of Nedras a lot recently. I keep thinking I'll see him come through my door, hear his voice. But never again.
Ah, you return! And I can sense the Ayleid energy you carry, so I don't even need to ask whether you were successful. I hope you caused plenty of trouble for the Worm Cultists.

It's decided, then. I'm going to take up weaponsmithing. My father was always very handy with an anvil. Perhaps I'll try to earn an apprenticeship … sorry, please excuse me. I have a lot of planning to do!
Kala must consider how she will find the coin for travel. That brother of mine … never thinking of anything but the moons!

It's a disgrace. I fought by <<1>>'s side in the civil war. Things got so bad, we had to eat leather cut from our own armor.\n\nEven then, I never heard this amount of whining coming from the High Elves and the Khajiit about their embassy.
Completely unacceptable! If this is what <<1>> thinks of us, we should go back to Elsweyr!

Yours is truly a generous spirit to release me from this dark place, but I would be most ungrateful if I did not tell you the entire truth.\n\nIf I am truly to leave here—to put down new roots and find new life—more is needed to be done.

Dark moons, stranger. While Silver-Paws and dungy Knight-Commander quibble over bow strings and bandages, food stockpiles shrink. \n\nWe must start hunting now, or we will all be dead before the next Tojay moon.
If you ask me, the Baron was too easy on his son. People died. On his watch. Blatant incompetence at its finest.
With so many knights injured here, there's great demand for fighters willing to take their places. Why not join the guild?
Grim scene out there, eh? Almost makes me feel bad for not helping out. \n\nBut hey, adversity builds character, right? Knights like to have character, I hear.
I am new to the Guild, but I think it's the life for me. Paid to fight! Sounds good to me.
My hunting companion was chased by a group of chanting cultists up near the <<1>>. What's this world coming to? I certainly can't make any sense of it.
These knights are fools if they think force of arms alone will retake the Garrison. Without magical assistance they'll be slaughtered.
Do you have a thirst for adventure, for knowledge, for the arcane? You've come to the right place. Join us!
Do not tarry here with the wounded. You must … you must retake the Garrison! Don't let our deaths be in vain.
She's going to kill me. In my sleep. I know she will.
Even now, some of my brother and sister knights call for another assault on the Garrison. But we can't even keep light skirmishers out of our camp. Attacking without reinforcement would be suicide.
Do you have a kill for me, pup? Did you bring me meat?
Thank you for assisting Lady Laurent while I was indisposed. \n\nI hope there are no lingering after-effects. She can be … rather demanding at times.
Daedra take these Imperials. By St. Pelin's blood, I'll see that fort retaken!
I envy my brothers' and sisters' optimism. In its current state, the Order of Saint Pelin could not mount a defense in depth, let alone take back a fortified garrison.

That was an experience I won't be forgetting anytime soon. I'd say that you went beyond the call of duty, but I think you went even beyond that.\n\nOf course, Septima was actually after you, wasn't she?
These cursed Baandari charge us a king's ransom for supplies, then refuse to assist us in reclaiming them? A pox on the lot of them.
Zeht's tears! What has befallen? Who has slain everyone? Where's the king?
Any luck? Did you find the source of the invaders?
I must thank you for the opportunity to see <<c:1>> operate as it did in ancient times. It's all so exciting!
The queen … she's radiant!
My notes? I can't believe it! I thought I'd lost these for good.
Quite impressive, stopping this attack on <<1>>. I'd say it's worthy of our king's notice.\n\n<<2>> is always pleased to meet extraordinary people who arrive in his lands.
You don't look like much. Why would Hircine send you to me as a challenger? Does he mock me? Or is there more to you than meets the eye?
Adeena may forgive me in time, but I will never forgive myself.
So. You killed it.
I wish I had heeded my sister's warnings rather than marry such a monster.
A nightmare from Oblivion visited upon our home. May the Roar of Alkosh burn these invaders away!
What do you think you're doing on my ship? Do you know what I did to the last stowaway I found?
Follow the pull of your blood and you will find the Tomb of the Blood Matron.
May the Father of Owls guide your steps, friend.
Not a lot of people simply walk in and volunteer to help fight with the resistance. Call me a skeptic, I suppose.
Watch your step in there. After all, you don't want to wind up stumbling into the afterlife … the gods don't like that.
I'm glad to be free of that monster's flesh, but I can't rest easy until I've passed from this plane.\n\nI died so long ago—I would give anything to move on.
You did not see me, did you? No one sees the poor, the sick. The oppressed!\n\nYou help these people of Hallin's Stand, but for what? You put yourself in harm's way, but why?
I thought that brute was going to kill me! Thank you, stranger!
Away with you! Can't you see I'm busy?
What … who … how … oh, hello there.
So it's just us mortals from here on in? That's fine with me. I don't mind admitting that the idea of friendly vampires kind of creeps me out.
The Blacksap always knew the best hunting spots …

I sense great determination in you, living one, but very few of the living are foolish enough to trespass in these hallowed halls. \n\nEven fewer are foolish enough to seek entrance into the Chamber of Passage. This is your intention though, is it not?
Blacksap, Dominion? Who are we following now?
My husband would have been heartbroken if I spoke out against the Blacksap. I'm glad they're gone. Now we can all get back to our lives.
What will Cormount become without the Blacksap? There's no future for any of us.
The Blacksap are no more. What a pity.
Our people are doomed. The High Elves will stomp us out.
I know you, sister. You're one of us, even if you don't know it yet. Hircine calls you. His song is in your blood.

It takes a brave soldier to enter the Chamber of Passage, but courage alone is not what defines a warrior. \n\nOne has already breached the chamber without my blessing, but you come behind seeking just that, do you not?

This is an historic moment. You do realize that, don't you? \n\nWe're about to play a significant role in ending the haunting of Traitor's Tor and discovering the truth of King Ranser's final moments!
Finally, a chance for everyone to relax. Join us, if you like.
I appreciated your intervention earlier, but I am sure this conquest can be made without your help.
My beautiful abomination, how you shine in the dark. \n\nNow, listen.
Go upstairs and get the inn key from Darien. Then we can find out what's locked in there and making all that racket.
Brackenleaf's Briars built this shrine, as tribute to the animals of <<1>>.

I sense you have been among that dark ruin, Gil-Var-Delle. Perhaps it was even you who fought back against the vile Worms. If that is true, you must have seen the scarring the land has suffered in that foul place. Maybe you can help me.
The Queen expects you presently. Proceed.
Go on, up the stairs with you. There's no reason to keep the beautiful Lady Lleraya waiting.
My performers can best explain their setbacks. <<1>> is our bug trainer, <<2>> our storyteller, and <<3>> is … well, she's magnificent.\n\nI have to describe her that way. It's in her contract.
Arkay protect you, my child.

The scrolls speak of the principles of Wisdom, Discipline, Sacrifice, and Devotion, and the seasons of life in which I mastered these principles.\n\nPlace them in the proper order in which they were mastered.
I wish I'd known she was in here all this time. The more the merrier, I always say.
Filthy, unclawed Bretons! How hard is it to watch over barrels and crates?
The customs clerk in <<1>> should be able to help you locate my shipment. The client is … not a patient woman, so do hurry.

I must say, Darien certainly has a way with the ladies. That's not how I'd go about extracting information from the enemy, but I can't fault his results.\n\nThe old smuggler's tunnel should lead into the city—if we can get through it.
Moons' blessings, walker. Have you come to help this one save the camp from unclawed Imperials?
Oh, you again. What do you need?
I hope you didn't travel from far away just to see <<1>>. I am not performing at present.\n\nMy magic cannot function safely in front of a crowd. The, uh, stars are out of alignment.
Blasted cat-folk. They dine on sweet rolls while we choke down spoiled porridge. \n\nCan't you hear them? Those hissy laughs of theirs …. It makes me sick. St. Pelin give me temperance.
Forgive me, but I must tend to my flock. <<1>> should be able to answer any questions you have about her carnival.
You reek of kwama juices … why don't you come inside and spend some time with your granny Alyxe? \n\nI'll have a hearty chunky brain stew ready soon, or do you like it spongey and raw?
I promised to keep my husband in line, and that's just what I'm going to do. If he even goes near something that smells like criminal activity, he'll answer to the business end of my broom!
What do you have there? A book?
It's good to see Baron Alard again. He is like a brother to me. It's been weeks since we last saw each other.\n\nI only wish this reunion was under better circumstances.
You have a point, my friend—perhaps we're all in this together.\n\nSeems it's the only way we'll get out of this war alive. Uptight as these High Elves are, they did save our skins.

You and that Wood Elf can lie to yourselves, but the Altmer have a place above all others. It's not a judgment—simply a matter of fact. Our knowledge and contributions to history ensure this.\n\nThat Wood Elf needs to learn his place.
We're the only survivors? I will always remember how you saved me, my father, and my betrothed.
I have more than a few copies, so keep the book as long as you wish. A shame none of them are the translated versions!
I have begun to wonder whether all scholars are as troublesome as this one.
Have you got everything you need?

I'm not sure I can ever forget what happened to my brothers because of what you did, but … you saved Kaleen. You saved Shornhelm, too. I can't discount that.\n\nI guess we'll just have to learn to live with each other.
I can't believe this could possibly be taking you so long. How hard could it be?
Ha! You made it! I never doubted for a moment. I mean, sure, when the top of the entire mountain disappears, you don't expect many people to walk away from that. But here you are!

You looking for a mace, or maybe a bow? You know, for hunting, not, like, fighting.\n\n…Just between you and me, these Imperial skeevers hanging around is killing my business. Nobody wants to be seen arming themselves.
I do not have much to sell, wayfarer. These red-clad brigands took most of my goods as spoils of war. But you are welcome to look over what is left.
Can't talk much. Imperials are always watching. Take my advice—buy some of my expertly crafted armor, then get out of Hallin's Stand altogether.
Next time, let's go shopping. Wouldn't that be more fun?
Fancy a good scrap, like I do? You should join the Guild! Go talk to Hlura—she'll help you out.
Bah. So sick of seeing these Imperial bastards strut past the door like they own the place. If someone doesn't start a riot soon, I may have to do it myself.
By the Three, if you slay Daedra half as well as you slay slack-jawed Imperial conscripts you've got a bright future in the Fighters Guild, f'lah.
I won't ask.

I said, go away! Oh … I beg your pardon. I thought you were one of those oafish Imperials looking for another charm potion. As if such a thing would fool a proud daughter of Hammerfell.\n\nHave you come seeking potions? I offer the best in the city.
You return. Did you have any luck finding the remaining fragments?
Wonderful day for a bloodfiend attack. What can I do for you, citizen?

Thirsty? Ruptga knows those cursed Imperials are. They've nearly drunk me out of a job. Sometimes they even pay. Dogs and sons of dogs, all of them.\n\nI've managed to hide away some of my better stock, though. Interested?
I didn't do it, whatever it was.
You … are kind to make such an offer, my friend. I actually hurt my sword arm slaying my captors. I could use an ally.\n\nIf this lot has harmed Esmaeel, I'll bring this cave down around their heads.
Get her out. I'll be right behind you.
Shut the door quickly behind you. The sand gets into everything, especially the alchemical equipment.\n\nHave you come seeking membership in the Guild?
I knew you'd be back. I also know Naruk is dead. Thank you. Yet again, you've stopped a threat to the city and the Covenant.
This occupation won't last. We Redguards won't labor under an Imperial yoke—it's not in our nature. \n\nTo be honest, I'm surprised the peace has held this long.
I'd stay off the street if I were you. I've seen ill omens in my scrying mirror. \n\nBlood is going to be spilled here in Hallin's Stand. Very soon.
<Esmaeel lies dead.>
People here just don't understand Khajiit. This one came here to try to build a better life, but now Malira just wants to go back to Khenarthi.

Thanks for putting that cat in her place. Those people can be so stubborn.\n\nThe Khajiit need to understand that some of their cultural rituals are taboo to the rest of the Dominion. Those of us who are civilized, anyway.

Welcome to The Drowsy Owl, my friend. I would offer you a bed, but the Imperials have soiled them all. What once smelled of jasmine and rose blossoms now smells of boiled meat and dog. Their stench persists despite our efforts.\n\nMy deepest apologies.
You shouldn't linger, wayfarer. Hallin's Stand is nothing but an Imperial kennel now. I'm bound for the Alik'r as soon as I get the opportunity—you would do well to follow suit.
You did it. It's so good to see their faces again.
<The Scouting board has a place for me to post my report.>

So when I saw you go down for a nap, I decided this partnership was over. I certainly didn't think you were doing your part.\n\nThen the mage suddenly stands up and says he's ready to go, and that I have you to thank for it. Is that true?
Just make sure <<1>> is safe. This one is at her wit's end.
Hail, O wayfarer. I beg you, forgive Khada if she has given you cause for offense. She has a temper, and this Imperial occupation has put a strain on all of us.
Hold. You are no servant of the Empire, are you? \n\nI beg you to forgive my caution, O wayfarer. The red devils have been watching us for days. I fear they will pounce upon us at any moment.
Ah, good, you are not a Daedra. They are this one's enemies, and must not hear this one's plan to escape the vampire skeevers.

An Ayleid artifact, supposedly touched by the gods, will proclaim my sister worthy of becoming the empress of Tamriel.\n\nBut this changes little. There are those who will always question her right to rule.
I'm … myself. Aren't I?
<<1>> shall lead us to glory. Of that, there can be no doubt.
<There's a new notice on the Warfront board.>
<No new bounty missions have been posted.>
<There's a new notice posted to the Battle board.>
Welcome to the Steeping Sun tea house, wayfarer. Please, sit and abide a while. Breathe deep and ease the shoulders.
