I don't have time for those who have no desire to cleanse Tamriel of the filth infesting it from Oblivion.

And the whole 'undead' thing. It is both relatively new and entirely undesired.

Unless you've a desire to join the Guild, that is..?
Ugly business out of the streets, eh? Town's been flip-flopping between Eamond and Fahara'jad for so long…. This is what happens when you don't pick a side.
We're going back to Reaper's March? Ziss! We were just there a month ago! We're going to go broke, I just know it.
Keep your voice down. You never know who might be listening.
This Khajiit is lucky you stayed my hand. When I'm blind with rage like I was, I have a tendency to start swinging my axe.
Please—talk some sense into that Wood Elf. I don't know anything about the Green Pact that he's talking about.\n\nI've been eating flowers my whole life. They're delectable!
The proud Captain Helenus stands atop the walls by the Craglorn Gates. She is no doubt considering her next move after taking our tower. \n\nOur tower!
My soldiers have been returning one at a time. Some still complain of numbness. Some are half-blind. But they're alive; that's what matters.\n\nThank you.
Imperial s'wits. Look what they've done to this beautiful city. It's quiet as death. I can barely hear the goats bleating.
I don't know what's worse: the Imperials strutting around beating people to death, or this vile mead. \n\nI'm inclined to think the latter.
Look who's keeping everyone waiting now.
I've seen enough desert to last a lifetime. Can't wait to get back to the woods, with or without <<1>>.
Thank you. I've asked a lot of you, but it means so much to these refugees.
His honor remains.\n\nLeave me. Go.
I've just been informed of what's happened at Bangkorai Garrison. It seems my timing is impeccable as ever.\n\nSo you're the one who's been helping my cousin Arzhela hold the kingdom together?
Without the danger of losing one's life, how can one know life's true value?\n\nA man must ask himself such things. Contemplation hones the mind as a whetstone hones the blade.
If they hadn't taken us by surprise, I'd have sliced a few of those Imperial dogs to ribbons myself!
You spoke to <<1>>. Did he tell you our plight? Did he tell you all we've lost?
We can't leave Bangkorai until I get my pendant back. Why doesn't my father care about it? Why? I can't believe this has happened to us.
My daughter won't even speak to me. Watch this. <<1>>! <<1>>!\n\nShe's never forgiven me for our problems. Well, I've trouble of my own.
The passing of <<1>> was a sign from Mauloch. This cursed tower holds nothing for us now.
Run along now, little scamp. This is the grown-up table.
I know what you're thinking. Why would a dignified woman like me keep company with lowlifes such as these?\n\nBuy me a drink, and maybe I'll tell you.

Sick and tired of being treated like kitten-headed fools by the Thalmor. They file and deliver their papers, sign us empty promises, and what do we have to show for it?\n\nNothing. Abuse, yes? That is what this is.

So many fellow walkers are upset, disquieted by the silence of the Thalmor when we entreat them for answers.\n\nThis one knows the burden that is documentation. They were prompt with Vabashi's trade permits. She will be patient with them.
Nerien'eth will hear from me before I leave this plane, and he won't like what I have to say.\n\nI have an incendiary vernacular.

I should have seen him coming—Nerien'eth, I mean. I don't care what spells the Daedra gave him—a blade between his eyes ….\n\nI should have stopped him when I could. But I'm glad you did, for all our sakes.
Nerien'eth's fire wasn't so bad, after a time.\n\nMy anger burned brighter.
I have been watching out for you. \n\nIt must be quite an honor to have the high king awaiting your arrival. King Emeric thought you would be here ahead of him, but he has waited for you nonetheless.
Thank you, kind soul. Thank you for sparing my life.
No, no! Why would you kill Buttons? He just wanted to be your friend!

Ah! King Emeric said you might be coming. The Imperials are here. Did you know this?\n\nThe king and his men are preparing for an attack even now, though they are greatly outnumbered. I think it is good that you are here.
How did you get up here? Did you actually go through all those portals?\n\nThat must have been a huge pain-in-the-buttocks! Seriously … I can't believe you did that. What's the matter with you?
<This appears to be the dead body of Sir Dubroc, the leader of the expedition sent to Jackdaw Cove by the Knights of Saint Pelin.>
I've had it. <<1>>? She can sit in the fields and rot for all I care. <<2>> may be able to deal with all this work. Semusa cannot!
We received the word about Sir Dubroc. That was a grisly end for a good soldier.
Please, my family is in desperate need of help!
Thank the gods someone has come. The Imperials, they're up to something strange in the ruins ahead.

Be wary. The Knights of Saint Pelin do what we can to keep these lands secure, but recent events have made this a very dangerous place for travelers.\n\nI have scouts all over Bangkorai but many have failed to report in.
I think I've run out of tears at this point. How could the gods allow this to happen?
Not Emeric. Anyone but Emeric. Please. Please Tu'whacca, have mercy!
This has to be a joke! I travel all the way across the continent, twist my mind in knots over this password, and all that's in here is Willam's old shaving blade?
Nothing down here's in the right place! You know what that means? \n\nIt just means more dumb-dung I got to deal with before I can get out of here.

Best of luck to you. <<1>>'s sealed up tight, and by Azura's own hand. It'll take some doing to get in, never mind thwart Molag Bal, rescue <<2>>, and make your way back here.\n\nSay hello to <<3>> if she's still kicking, will you? It's been an age.
Some would think you're crazy to walk into caves filled with dreugh and Goblins. Me, I think you're either very brave, very stupid—or, most rarely—you're very good at what you do.\n\nWhich is it?

What are you looking at? Did I say you could look at me? I don't think so!\n\nI don't even want you sharing my air. You're a festering boil on the lip of reality! I don't like boils or things that fester! Move on … or do you have a problem with that?
Don't! Please! You're going to eviscerate me, I just know it! I don't want to be eviscerated! It sounds awful!
I thought I was dead. Pieces of my life: family, friends … adventures, regrets. I could see it all. \n\nI can't even begin to tell you how thankful I am you got me out of there.
Whatever it is—don't.
Leave me be, you wretched, joyful young thing. I am old, with little time left in this life. I would not waste what remains talking with the likes of you.
You again? I see you're still sticking your nose in other people's affairs. Well, if you're here to help, I'm not going to turn you away.
Once we get to Coldharbour, it'll be open season on Daedra!

May Auri-El grant us the wisdom to reconsider our individual desires and concur on a halfway-state that best fits all Dominion peoples here in Elden Root.\n\nThis is not a time for strength, or certainty, but a measure of social kinship.
I was skeptical about this summit until I heard that you were involved. You've been of invaluable help to me in the past.
Please don't distract me. If I don't finish packing, Lady Laurent will give me quite the talking to.
Security couldn't be tighter. This should go off without a hitch.
It's great to see you again, old friend! I feel better knowing that you're part of this invasion force.\n\nNow there's something I never expected to be a part of—an invasion force!

Ridiculous, that. The gathering, I mean. Do they not realize that we are endeavouring to satisfy them? Their conflicting demands and ridiculous expectations of time?\n\nTime marches only as it will. Such is its mandate.
We're to move on again. Of course. It is what our tribe does best.
Such bountiful waters … I'll miss fishing these shores.
Well, look who's here. It's nice to see a familiar face! Can you believe that the Mage Guild actually asked for our help? Expert consultants, they called us!
I remember you! I probably wouldn't be standing here today if it weren't for your help. Thanks!
Talk won't get us anywhere. Action! That's what will stop Molag Bal.
It's good to see you again, my friend!

The most painful thing about this scenario is the awareness they must lack of what we have already achieved for <<1>>.\n\nWe do not inform them because their lives are easier for not knowing. And this is the thanks we get.
Find out all you need to know?
Bah! I can't stand this glorified guard duty. Give me a skull to cleave!
You may have saved my life back in Stonefalls, but my master almost killed me for taking that tome!
After getting captured by those Goblins in Stonefalls, I've had my fill of them!
Bah. I don't trust your leader, and I don't trust you.
That's one ugly face you got there. Almost makes me look pretty. Ha ha!
If it isn't the hero of the alliance!
Your record with the Daggerfall Covenant has been exemplary. For that you have the High King's gratitude.
Shornhelm. It may be run-down, rainy, and ravaged by war, but … at least they've got ale!\n\nHow about you buy us another round?
The secret to curing the Baroness lies within this stone shard and the Ayleid relic it once belonged to.
Count Verandis. Hello. It's … um … good to see you. I hope you're well.\n\nWhat am I saying? Of course you're well! You're a vampire! Oh, sorry. Don't mind me. I must have had a little too much wine.
That's all there is to it! Welcome to the fold, scamp! You may one day have as many notches in your axe as I do. \n\nAw, who am I kidding? No you won't! Hah!
Riches and wealth pale in comparison to hard earned glory.\n\nI wouldn't sell my scars for anything in Tamriel.
I see they teach neither judgment, nor manners where you're from. This table is for the Undaunted.\n\nBegone!
I've got no more advice to give. Scurry off and see that you don't get yourself killed.
Thank you for your help with the carnival! The customers are starting to stream on through.
You interested in a drink? We have plenty to go around, considering the carnival is more or less shut down.
I don't even mind that we're not drawing in the crowds yet. I needed a break from that repetitive windbag, Noryon.
Some men call at the inn to meet and talk with strangers. I am not one of those men.
I don't trust those bugs. They haven't done much since I've been here, but I'm going to keep an eye on them all the same.
And that's our special Undaunted song. Did it hurt to hear as much as it did to sing it?
<<1>> is confused. She doesn't remember inviting you to keep her company, yet here you are. Curious.
The magic act is amazing! I can't wait for the Storyteller to get started. I love listening to old fairytales and legends.
This one hopes the Hollow City finds you well, Undaunted.\n\nMeridia's wayward township is many things, but it's never dull. Especially for an Undaunted.
To be honest, I don't mind the carnival not being full operational. I prefer shopping to spectacle.

Greetings, bold adventurer! I am <<1>>, servant of the Daggerfall Covenant and honorary member of the Undaunted. It's truly a pleasure to meet you.\n\nI'm told the newest members buy the drinks around here. What do you say, friend?
The Undaunted have no time for weaklings or beggers.
Quite the tail, eh? Get it? Tail?\n\nSeeks-Her-Glory … has a tail!
You don't look like an Undaunted to me.\n\nGet out of here—while you still can.
Give me an excuse, and I'll eat your brains from your skull and drink your blood.\n\nThis table's for the Undaunted only.
What do you want, dungheap?
Hey, if it isn't my favorite fresh meat! Hope you've seen more combat than I have. Taverns only hold their charm for so long.
I don't know you. I don't want to know you. Go away.
<This Orc is either asleep, or ignoring you.>
This room's for the Undaunted, stranger. Undaunted only.
I have much better things to do than converse with you.
My wit's as quick as my blade.\n\nDon't believe me? Buy me another drink and I'll show you.
I'm reading and you're standing in my light. Be kind and stand somewhere else. Preferably outside so that I won't be forced to look at you.
My scales are dry, my tongue is drier. Though the blood of a miser could quench just as well as a cool drink.
This is a gathering for Undaunted.\n\nAnd you're no Undaunted.
This one doesn't have time for strangers. Sorry. This one has an entire loaf to finish.
If it isn't the new blood! Just in time, too. My mug is empty.
Don't talk to me. I might vomit on your shoes.
This grass itches. Please stop distracting me. I'm waiting for other Undaunted to come along. They're sure to need my advice or my wares.
I can't wait for another adventure to sweep me along.\n\nNothing out here but trees. You can't stab trees. Well, you can. But they don't stab back.
Open air is nicer than I thought it'd be. At first I was angry they threw me out of the tavern. But now pretty good.\n\nNow … pretty good.
I am not entirely sure what's going on outside.\n\nI doubt it really matters, in the grand scope of things—peasants being peasants, I assume.
Dominion troops encroaching on our land? I wish they would all fall off a cliff!
The Dominion soldiers have no right to set up camp outside of town. This is our land, not theirs.
This grass itches and pricks. But it's much better than the cold.
I'm Earrona Kneecapper. If you want to know why they call me that, keep talking.
Unless you're secretly a magic being made of moon-sugar and ale, this one doesn't want to talk to you.\n\nThis one would also speak to Undaunted, but you look the opposite of that.
I think its best you step, away, friend or else I'll have to embarrass you in front of these ladies.
I don't have time for the likes of you.
Do you always walk this close to people you don't know? Never mind, I don't care. Just go away.
No, I don't need any more drinks, thank you.
The Empress of Bone is thirsty. Buy her a drink! Now!
I'll not forget your generosity, my friend.
Excuse me. You are in my light. We are establishing a scene here.\n\nYou are interfering in art. Please leave.

Whatever you intend to do while here, please refrain from interfering with my model.\n\nIt has taken me ages to coerce him into catching the light as he has. Any interruption and he might throw a tantrum and storm off.

I always admired Syrabane. Someday, I hope to be so well-known in Altmeri culture as that particular hero-sorceress.\n\nIt shall not, I expect, be through my diligent bookkeeping and efficient management skills that I become so well-known.
I've killed fools dumber than you before but I'm not sure I've killed anyone uglier. You don't want to be another notch on my axe. Beat it!
I'm in no mood. Leave before I finish my ale or you'll wish you had.\n\nMy drunk arm is a stiff arm, I assure you.
Ale in my belly and a story to pass around. That's all I need in life.
Let me know if you hear of any packing and unpacking jobs, would you?
Dear me! Thrice the champion, is it? Bravo!
You are the one who cleared the Bjoulsae Boys out of Viridian Watch, yes? \n\nHmph. Quickpaw thought they were helping the poor all this time. What a fool I was.
<<1>> seems like a fancy device. I hope it works.\n\nAnd if it doesn't, I trust you'll keep the king safe? He's usually not so reckless.

There won't be much to see, I'm sure. The Ayleids were notorious for their glowing crystals, so I suppose there will be more than a few bright lights.\n\nSounds quite dreary. I can't imagine it will be worth your time at all.
You've been stumbling all over Redfur like a mead-soaked goat. Is there a party somewhere I missed? There had better not be.\n\nI hate missing parties.

I, Boeuf Sterone, have noticed everyone has been acting oddly lately. Is there something happening?\n\nYou can tell your friend Boeuf Sterone if anything is. Trust in Boeuf Sterone, his word is as good as his food.
Hello! I have many fine pots and pitchers, and inside many of them, many fine things to drink.\n\nYou wish to trade for any of these things?
I don't trust this <<1>> one bit. He's an obsequious lickspittle, if you ask me.
Welcome to our humble guildhall, fellow Fighter. How are things out there?\n\nI'm itching to return to active combat.
I'm not doing anything until that coal fire is started. \n\nDon't worry, I'll be able to hear the blast from here.
Welcome, Mage. Feel free to make use of our humble facilities here as you will.\n\nThey are here for Mages Guild use, after all.
Have we met? You seem quite familiar.\n\nI'm demonstrably busy at the moment. It seems a colleague of mine couldn't avoid a simple spiritual possession on <<1>>. You understand, I'm sure.
It's good to see you. <<1>> has been assisting me with a … certain project. Before long, <<2>> will be free to leave <<3>>.\n\nSoon, I'm certain of it.

Ah, my friend from <<1>>. Rest assured, we're doing everything in our power to free my apprentice. <<2>> will not hold her for long.\n\nForgive me, I must return to my calculations. The magic is quite delicate.
I've been supplying the Briars for some time now. But I would be more than happy to take your coin as well.
<<1>> is my husband, and a master hunter. We met each other while stalking the same bear. It was love at first sight!
Good luck in your trials.
Don't ask what happened while you were drunk. It is better not to know.
The Dominion is in need of capable citizens. And by capable, I mean you.
Brendar returned safely thanks to you. I appreciate your kindness and bravery.\n\nHe's waiting at the Horker's Tusk. I believe he wanted to speak to you.
You made it out. That's good to see. What of the necromancer?
I can't believe that <<1>> is dead. She was a good soldier. And a good woman. She will be missed.
Bring this here, take it there. Half the time, it seems they're moving it just to have it moved!
This one brought his family all the way to <<1>>, expecting a place in our own embassy.\n\nInstead, we sit in leaky tents waiting for promises to be fulfilled!
They're going to have a feast for us? Is that what she said? I hope they don't serve any harpy meat. I never want to smell that again.
You should probably speak to Countess Tamrith. I'm not an official member of this triumvirate.
I can't believe this! I should cut my losses with these idiots. Work on my own!
What is going on? Why are the harpies attacking? You look like you can handle yourself, get out there and help.
You've ruined us. We'll have to find a new way to earn a living!
Poor Crestshade! What a disaster!\n\nI was about to head up to that House Ravenwatch stronghold to find help, but for some reason I can't seem to make my legs carry me up these stairs.
Sithis smiles upon <<1>>. Even so, it would appear he has business elsewhere.\n\nI overheard Dominion soldiers. They said they captured <<Ac:2>>. A dark day, indeed.
You sure you know where you're going? If you're looking for a shortcut to Shornhelm, I'd look elsewhere.\n\nI wouldn't walk into these ruins unless I knew what I was getting into.
I'm glad we've had someone like you on our side, from start to finish, if you catch my meaning.

You followed through? Excellent. I worried he'd convince you to set him free, then we'd have had to track down both of you. That would have been unpleasant.\n\nForget that, though. Can't tell you how glad I am to finally have this bastard in custody.
Go on, then. The bandits could be pulling up camp as we speak. If Gavendien gets away, I'll never forgive myself.
I thought that if we just cooperated with them, everything would work out and no one would be hurt.\n\nNow I know. I will never bargain with bandits again.
If I was a few years younger, I'd go after Gavendien myself. That rotten coward. Killing an innocent woman. He deserves to die!
It might be best for you to move on to another town. Hoarfrost Downs is nice this time of year, I understand.
No. I'm not coming. No, I'm not. Don't even ask. I'll come back, but only when Gaillard says it's safe. Yes, that's right. Only when Gaillard says.\n\nGaillard told me to stay right here until then.
I feel terrible. Poor Lauravieve. To die so young and so needlessly. It just isn't right.
Someone needs to find that Gavendien and make him pay!

My mother had a passion for jewels and jewelry, and she built this business up from nothing.\n\nI never thought I'd wind up running it myself. Without her, I'm just not sure I have what it takes. I'm going to try though.
Mark my words. No Orc gets by here as long as the King's Guard still stands.
I don't see anyone from the Ring of Daggers. Does that mean … you've chosen to let me go free?

It's hard for me to relate to someone like Julien. The young men in my home town never even noticed me. I tried to get their attention by challenging them to duels. But when I beat them, that just made it worse.\n\nSo I joined the Shornhelm Guard.
Do your worst, lackey to a foreign crown! I won't tell you anything!

At the moment, we're still trapped beneath Lleraya's veil. See if you can find another tear in the spell so that we can leave this place.\n\nI just hope the book is still with us when the illusion dissipates.

Remember, I'd like to save Northpoint while causing as little death and destruction as possible—except for the Montclairs. Kill as many of them as you like.\n\nJust remind Skordo that this is our city we'll be assailing, not some bandit stronghold.
I am praying for strength and courage. I should not be hiding from those foul creatures. But Arkay bless me, they make my skin crawl.
Good luck. Did I mention there's trolls around there? Frankly, they are worse than ghosts. Meaner and they small really bad.
Darien can't talk right now. I gave him something to relieve his pain. And to quiet him down for a little while.\n\nThe man does love the sound of his own voice.
I'll give the signal. It's time to liberate Northpoint from these monsters.\n\nMeanwhile, go to my manor and evict Montclair's daughter from the premises—with extreme prejudice.
You may not believe this, but that wasn't how I wanted our reunion to play out. But laws were broken. People died. I can't ignore our laws.\n\nNot even to save my son.

Do you believe that man? And to think, I thought him to be dashing and heroic! But enough of such matters. You aren't here to discuss my personal life.\n\nTell me, what news from Count Ravenwatch? Are we ready to march against Montclair?
Rivenspire needs Tamrith and Dorell. They cannot be allowed to perish here.\n\nI need to help get them to safety before I join you up above.
And so everything returns to the way it should be, yes? Only I think the Baroness will be a little less quick to follow in her mother-in-law's footsteps, from now on.
Federic and <<1>> have both left. Perhaps I should leave, as well. Perhaps the Mages Guild has a place for me.
Thank you again, for convincing me to stay. With Federic leaving to join the Covenant, the Edralds will need me more than ever.\n\nAnd … it is good to see Arlie safe and sound.
Such an awful place. I could have lived my entire life without knowing of such things.
I am sorry to see <<1>> go, but it really is for the best. Soon my Arlie will be happily married, and we can all get on with our lives!
How vile! Is that a piece of Goveled's brain on your boot? What are you? Some kind of monster?\n\nOnly joking around, of course. You beat him, huh? I'm impressed.
There you are! I've been looking all over for you.\n\nVerandis requests your presence at the ruins in the Lorkrata Hills, if you aren't too terribly busy at the moment.
I don't know if I'll ever get used to traveling by portal. One moment you're there, the next moment you're here. It's positively disconcerting!
Doubt is insidious. It clouds the mind, makes it hard to think. And what I need, now, is to be thinking clearly!
It's an honor to see you again, my friend. May the gods bless you for all of your days!
Be at ease, friend. You may come anew to the race, just as the spring rains come anew after the winter's snow.\n\nI will review the rules with you again just to be sure that all is clear.
I don't think there's anything more for us to talk about.
Rohlbert is so brave, acting through hired assassins and spies. Let's see how brave he is when Adusa and Five-Claws come to call!
I hope my daughter finds a way to be happy. I know Federic cares for her, but I'm just not sure he'll satisfy her … more adventurous desires.
Don't worry. I'm keeping a tight watch on her. No more odd behavior. She promised! And I intend to hold her to that.
I will never be able to adequately apologize for everything that happened at the estate. But I am very appreciative that you supported our love.
Dulkhi and I will never forget what you did for us. We've never been more in love!
Verandis … why did it have to be you? Damn you, Verandis! Why didn't you tell me what you planned to do?
This must have been a room for prayer or peaceful contemplation when the Ayleids were alive.
The stars have accepted you. I just hope it is not too late.\n\nVolumes of prophecy have been written about the stars, but not even the oracles foresaw these events.
I'm just so happy … I can't stop crying.

Let me take a look at you. So you're the one who dispatched my father's pet Argonian? Well done, by the way. Well done.\n\nI'm so glad you're here. I was becoming dreadfully bored with Ellic and the rest of these silly nobles.
This chamber has a calming effect. I wonder if this was where the pilgrims rested on their way to visit the uppermost chamber?

I can't tell you how much I appreciate you convincing me to enlist. I've come to realize that this is what I was born to be—a soldier.\n\nNot only have I been able to better support my family, but I like to think I've made them proud, too.
Well, we're here all right, but I'm not sure I'm going to be getting off the boat. In fact, I say we just put right back out to sea.

A finer group of soldiers never served in the Shornhelm Guard. Julien and Shuga have both turned out to be valiant warriors.\n\nAnd Martin's distinguished himself, too. I actually think he's got the makings of a strong leader.
Ah! You're one who killed that old skeever Dark Elf I was seeing! What was his name again …?\n\nNo matter. I owe you, though. This soldier business is a lot more fun than being a bandit!

If it isn't Mara's messenger in the flesh! You really saved my love-life. Looking back, I can't imagine what I ever saw in Guendeline. \n\nI finally met my true love during training. Shuga. She's sweet and strong and all the woman I'll ever need.
That old Khajiit lady in the wagon read my palm and told me that is where I needed to be for my luck to change.\n\nI'm staying right here until it does.

With all the trouble brewing outside these walls, I'm expecting a lot of orders for weapons soon. Unfortunately, I'm already overtaxed. We haven't had any steel shipments arrive in ages.\n\nI suppose we have to take the bad with the good.
There are things in these signs I don't understand. When you return, perhaps their meaning will become clearer to me.
I'm afraid the situation in Craglorn grows worse daily. We need every strong sword arm and spellcaster we can recruit.

Many Dwarven religious texts refer to a Dwemer site called Mtharnaz. A high priest named Arnming wrote that he wished to be buried there, "among the masters of the heavenly stone."\n\nHis burial site is our best chance of finding a Skystone amulet.

Be wary. This area is crawling with Worm Cultists. We learned that the hard way when they ambushed us down in the cavern.\n\nGods only know what they're doing down there, but we can't complete our mission.
We are near Fallowstone Hall, hallowed home of the Companions. I would show you around, but this is not your place.
Now that the city is safe and those Montclair miscreants have been banished, I think I'll just sit here for awhile and soak up the ambiance.

Well, at least Shornhelm is safe. For now. But I can't stand the way Baron Dorell and Countess Tamrith bicker. And in public, even!\n\nI wonder when the two of them will decide to settle their differences by the sword?
The High King gave the crown of Shornhelm to Baron Dorell. I mean, King Alard. That's what we call him now. And he looks so handsome in his regal garb!
The High King crowned the Countess! Excuse me, Queen Eselde. That's what we call her now. And she looks beautiful in her regal garb!
I heard we have a queen now. I wonder if things will really get any better.
So the High King gave the crown to Countess Tamrith. Well, that figures! He always had a soft spot for beautiful Eselde.
Welcome to the Shornhelm Mages Guild Hall. Do I detect a budding acolyte in our midst?
Thank the Lord, Mother, and Wizard. You're back! \n\nPlease tell me you've got good news.
Ahh, you're back. Sorry about earlier. I'm feeling better already.\n\nWhat news from the spider hole?
Ah, you're back. Do you have my goods?
Greetings, traveler. You'll go no further up the river here, I'm afraid. A mystical ward bars the path up to Tormented Spire. An unstable ward, at that.
Good luck. Kyne speed you on your way.

Pardon me; I'm seeking a group that will offer me protection on my trip.\n\nI'm a researcher of sorts, seeking out the secrets of Craglorn! But I can't do it all by myself. If you haven't noticed, things haven't been friendly as of late.
We can handle ourselves for now, but I don't know how long we can keep this up.\n\nSee what they need at Vivec's Antlers first. That's the higher priority right now.
Covenant soldiers everywhere. Like an infestation of nasty, stinging mudcrabs. Bah.
Hello, friend.
Report in, soldier. What brings you to Vivec's Antlers?
You arrive alone. Either you didn't find him, or I need a new hunting partner.
My friend! How good to see you again! Did you give the Hagraven a proper thrashing? And did you happen to find my wife's mace?\n\nTell me all is well and we'll drink to our good fortune!

Thank you for returning my mace. My husband always loses things, and he refuses to put on a decent pair of shoes, but I do love him so.\n\nAs soon as he's sober, though, we're going to have a talk about why I remind him of a Hagraven.
Let's look around the perimeter of the camp. The remains of the last soldier must be around there somewhere.
You should be able to find <<1>> toward the front of the camp. That's where I saw him last.

We've been in Stormhaven fighting the Ironhand Ogres for too long. We've got soldiers stationed here, Wayrest … all across eastern Stormhaven, really.\n\nWe need to do our duty for the Covenant, but at some point, we need to go home to Wrothgar.

You don't look like someone who's just wandering by. Please tell me you have word from General Godrun or someone over at Shinji's Scarp.\n\nPlease tell me they're finally sending orders for us to rejoin the main army.
I know that look, friend. Is the task complete? Are Lleraya's remaining vampires destroyed?
I feel better already. Just knowing that I reached out to Azura. I know my father would be pleased as well.
These are dark times, my friend. I only pray that Azura can speed the dawn of brighter days to come.
Remember to bring any messages you find to Captain Gilame up near the tower.
This is a bad time for Kragenmoor, traveler. Are you here on business? If not, you'd best be moving along.
You saved me, and helped free my father's city. I have no doubt you'll put a stop to this madness.
Thrice-blasted nobles! Their coffers keep the kingdom running, but at the first sign of trouble ….

Welcome to Hoarfrost Downs, perhaps the dreariest hamlet in all of Rivenspire. Actually, the entire kingdom is rather dreary, isn't it? \n\nWhat can I do for you? Have you come to join the Mages Guild?
Hail, comrade. You'll have to pardon my appearance. Tangled with a Clannfear recently and this Coldharbour muck stains worse than the snowberry wine.
Baron Dorell sends us out here to get the drop on Montclair, and what happens? The fiend turns half of Northpoint into gibbering monsters and we're stuck waiting for orders!

Fenila's words are incorrect, Lord Vivec, though she clearly believes them. I haven't contacted Belronen for months, and would never have done so without your direction.\n\nWealth has no meaning next to serving you, my lord. This you know to be true.

Lord Vivec, Vamen should be dead on the floor. Belronen wouldn't share the note that temple netch sent his way, but assured me its contents were vile.\n\nOne sworn to the temple, quibbling over coin? You should kill him yourself. My lord.

A tragedy, Lord Vivec. Belronen's death in the temple brings great shame to his house. I had thought reasoned words could dissuade him from the duel.\n\nSuch temper is common to House Telvanni. But it's not my place to question their reliability.

The Wilderking's reign draws to an end. The forest spirits have gone mad, even my own brethren … and he is powerless to stop them. \n\nIntruders enter Greenheart—dark and conflicted souls—they are the harbingers of the Wilderking's death.
Don't tell the Commander who sent you to him. His mood's been an icy squall since Thod failed to report in this morning. The last thing I need is him taking it out on me.
Don't you worry. We'll see those reserves are sent. In the meantime, I have a favor to ask. I have a missive that must reach Vulkhel Guard.
Enjoy the pomp and circumstance, friend. I'll keep the mugs warm for the royals. Heh.
Is my brother ready? I need to get him out of here.
You've made me a happy man. Thank you!
The Maulborn tricked us? Those fetchers!\n\nAnd to think I drank three of their curatives.
I see Aerona has conscripted a new soldier into her private army.
You're not going to find my siblings here. I can tell you that for sure.

It is good to see you, my friend! Greenshade is far more exciting place than Raz expected.\n\nHe hears now that the Staff of Magnus has been stolen? As if these rebellious Bosmer were not trouble enough!
We will always be grateful to you.
We're a family again thanks to you!
You have to help them!
Have you brought me a sweet? I love sweets.
I'm afflicted. I just know it.
So cold … I'm so very cold ….
Who knew that loam and animal skins could make such delightful flooring? I tell you, the stone in most guild halls are murder on my feet. But I do ramble.
You'll find the portals further into the sewers.

You need to convince my sister to leave this place. Then you can deal with the Maulborn.\n\nDestroy their ability to make more of this damn plague. Just be careful. The chamber ahead is crawling with plague husks.
You provide a welcome distraction, friend. The thought of those Jackdaw brutes muddying my floors and soiling my instruments is too much to bear.
You look lost. Can't say I blame you—Elden Root can be quite a labyrinth, but you've found the most important branch! The hall is at your disposal.
It's always nice to meet a fellow pilgrim on the path to enlightenment. There are all manner of secrets tucked away in this forest. Just have a care around the plant-life. It can be … temperamental.
I wish I'd studied my cleansing spells more diligently. It'll take days to wash the dog-stink out of this room. \n\nBut please forgive my grumbling. You're most welcome in our hall.
You have to help them!
What a relief to see a fellow arcanist. I trust that the barbarians across the hall didn't give you too much trouble? Their grunting and laughing and howling is just … incessant.
What a mess. You don't need a tour of the facilities, do you? Judging by the Orc blood on the carpet, I'd wager this isn't your first visit.
It's good to see another mage who's not afraid of the outdoors. While other mages dodder around their guild halls, we sleep under the stars and make new discoveries daily. What an adventure!
Patience. Yes. Painful as it may be to practice, it can be a formidable weapon when mastered.\n\nI just have to keep reminding myself of that.
Yes? It's nice to see you again, of course, but I am kind of in the middle of something here.
If anyone knows how to stop this, the Aldarch will. Go, you have to help her!

The loss of life is always tragic, but death is a critical part of nature's cycles. Some things must perish, so that others may thrive.\n\nSuch is the case here. Though you may mourn for these Bosmer, know that you protected the Valenwood.
If anyone knows how to stop this, the Aldarch will. Go, and may the blessings of the Eight be upon you.
Bah! These classifications are all wrong. We will never unravel the secrets of this place if we can't even label our discoveries properly. Perhaps a new indexing system would help ….
I'm happy that the mine is back under our control, but I can't shake this bad feeling I have.
Another associate climbs aboard our rickety "guild hall." And hey, since you're already a member I don't have to give you my guild recruiting pitch.\n\nPraise Vivec.
Have I convinced you, then? Are you ready to join up?
I knew you figure it out! Please hand the potion to Nilyne so she can inspect your results.
Please, let me teach what I can to Erunor while there's still time. See if you can do something for what's left of our poor village.
Move along, citizen. By order of <<1>>, these godless fanatics and their sorry excuse for a shrine are off-limits until the talks in <<2>> have concluded.
Didn't you hear what I said? Out! The patient needs time to let the potion work its magic.
You did it! Good job! Now give the potion to Nilyne and see what she thinks of your technique.
It's times like these when I wish I had more help around here.\n\nIs there something I can get you?
Glad you aren't scared off like some other folks. You'd think they'd never seen another Bosmer before.
You know, I used to have dreams of becoming an adventurer like you and journeying all over Tamriel … and then I realized, it's so much easier to just stay at home.
Hello there. Welcome to Bramblebreach. If you came to see a festival, I'm sorry. It's the off-season right now.\n\nOf course, you're always welcome to stay and join us for music and dance!
Remember what we talked about and this will all turn out very profitable for everyone involved.
What do you say? Do you have what it takes? Are you ready to join the fight?
The Maulborn curative was a lie? Then that means there's no hope for my wife. No hope at all.
Hello again, my slick-scaled friend. Have you been to Emberflint yet? And did I ever tell you about the Armature?
The Maulborn stink of deceit and treachery. I spit venom in their general direction!
I guess I should be thankful the Maulborn ignored us. Still rude of them, though.
As soon as the plague husks are gone, we're going to go into the catacombs and see what valuables the Maulborn left behind.
Is it hot in here?
Twelve scaly Argonians, all baked in a pie ….

I'm feeling so much better. But Nilyne says her potion has only suppressed the plague, not cured it.\n\nIf you find a way to beat this plague, make sure you send word to us. And thanks for helping our town.
You keep coming back to talk to me. If you're trying to get my attention, you're going to have to do better than that.
Traveler. How goes your survey of Zabamat? Have you found Mephala's Nest, yet?
Helgana will soon be with her ancestors in Sovngarde. The vile Covenant soldiers of Softloam Cavern have seen to that.\n\nMay the Lord, Mother, and Wizard watch her on her journey.
<Pain has overwhelmed Helgana. She stares without seeing.>
So the Maulborn lied to us? That is what I said the moment they first came to the Serk.\n\nDark Elves never listens to Argonians. They yell at us, but they never listen.
You mean there isn't any cure? I guess this is what true disappointment feels like.
What's going on around here? We heard that there is no curative. That it was all a lie.\n\nWhat are my brothers going to do now?
I'll be in to help as soon as I can. Just catching my breath, that's all.
My sweet Mirilir. I would say that I miss him, but I know that I will follow him soon enough. I am ready now.\n\nBut you, you're so kind. Did you find the Nereid's Smile?
I recognize you. You were talking with Urcelmo in the courtyard earlier. I heard about what happened with Astanya … most of us aren't like that. Will you spare a moment for the true Vulkhel Watch?
Thank the Stars. This mudcrab won't stop pinching me. \n\nListen, you have to get to Silsailen! Help them before it's too late.
They've burned the town! Please, please help us!
I knew the curative was too good to be true. Now I suppose the plague is going to kill us all.

Big hullabaloo about this girl, that boy. Pfft! Let them do what they will, I say.\n\n"Hullabaloo"? Where did I pick up such a vulgar word? Must be Bosmer. I'll need to stay out of Elden Root for a while.
I just arrived from Deshaan. Dethisam sent me. Perhaps you've heard of him? He's the consul for the town of Serkamora—the Serk.\n\nI'm here to spread the word and warn people about the Llodos plague.
Talk to Sali'ma. Half of our research team drank the water before we realized what was happening.\n\nEnding whatever curse is on the water might be our only chance to save them.
I was so relieved to get that letter from my cousin. Between knowing that he's all right and hearing that the Maulborn have a cure for this plague, I'm feeling so much better.
We've done nothing to them! Why do they attack us?
Thank you for talking to me. Auri-El only knows what I've had to put up with out here. That old goat won't listen to a word I say!
You can find Erold in our observatory, up on the top of the hill.
<<1>> thought Marbruk was a brand new city, but it is very popular already! Even the royalty visit.

I'd only finished the first trial when the betrayer struck, but it stands to reason that he's in the most secure part of the school—the cavern at the end of the final trial.\n\nYou'll need to complete the trials in order to avenge us.
You approach, knowing what you want! I was once like that, not that long ago. Please, share some gold with poor Kuralit?
You enter my temple once more, Seeker. What knowledge have you brought me?
My word, Queen Ayrenn, visiting Marbruk! A pity the streets hadn't been cleaned up before her arrival.\n\nThat said, what business do you have with us today?
It didn't work. I wasn't able to shield myself from the nightmares.\n\nShe is … she is gone. I couldn't save her.
Ah, you're back! Don't look so gloomy. At least you made it back to fight another day.\n\nMy allies weren't so lucky. Well? You're breathing, aren't you? Get back out there!

So it is true then? Prince Naemon has been raised from the dead and now seeks vengeance by corrupting Valenwood?\n\nGods help us! That makes this even more difficult. And with the undead already outside the city gates, we must act now.
The captain. They … they came at night. We couldn't ….
Hermaeus Mora is waiting to speak to you. Just approach his shrine and listen to what he has to say.
It's true, no rest for the weary.
Good luck, my friend. Wherever your travels take you next, know that you have all of the Guild at your back.
Tu'whacca speed you on your travels, and may the sand not slip beneath your sandals.

Ah. Just the one Raz was waiting for. The queen needs someone who can be entrusted with a … dignified task, and this one cannot currently oblige.\n\nYou would be acting as Ayrenn's personal envoy, but you can be respectable, yes?
Divines bless you, friend! World's a hard place, these days. My eleven children will surely starve today without a morsel to eat.\n\nWon't you spare some gold for an honest man and his poor children?
Five … no, ten! Ten bandits beat me and made off with my belongings! All they left were these rags you see before you. The pain! It is without ending!
By the Egg, I've never felt such hunger. But with no gold to buy it ….
Hey burr-sap! Spare a glint? A peck of shiny gems?
We need to double our membership. This is the third Guild Hall this month to be overrun!
How is the arena here? You think the lizards will let me fight without taking their stupid trial? Looks like a good time. I should ask.
None of these pirates want to join the Fighters Guild. I tried telling them Daedra could be found on the seas, but that just made them nervous.
Did my brother send you? I've been expecting a shipment for more than a week now.
Be careful in there. Those Red Rook bastards are as deadly as they are ugly.
You probably want to talk to one of the crafters.\n\nUnless, of course, you're looking for some hot coals.
I hope you'll forgive me for just accosting you out there like this, but my master sent me to find you. \n\nSomething … terrible has happened and she says we need your help.

Ah! So he did find you? That's good. The Ebonheart Pact needs a hero here. King Jorunn needs a hero here.\n\nThe Worm Cult's leader—Thallik Wormfather—he's a sneaky one, and very dangerous. Whatever he's planning, he must be stopped.
I don't know how you did it, but this water's as clear as the desert sky.\n\nI'm not going to drink any of it, mind you. But it seems safe to touch.

So many people from all over Tamriel called Elinhir home. \n\nEvery morning, the magic students gathered in the city center to practice their spells. I'd open my butcher's stall while dazzling beams of light and color cut through the morning air.
I … need to catch my breath. Good luck against Yamanu-ko ….
That core is looking less stable by the second. We must hurry!

The journal mentioned rain. Nerien'eth must have cast the ritual in an outdoor space. It shouldn't be far.\n\nBe on your guard. He'll show no mercy if we meet, and that Daedric artifact he wields casts an ill aura.
Find Zal'ik and release me from my imprisonment in this place. Then I will share with you what I know about cleansing the water of Shada's curse.
I don't understand. What's happening? Why Hara? Why now?
It wasn't so long ago that I had not even heard of this Worm Cult. Now these Worms are everywhere, killing people, destroying villages ….\n\nThis has to stop.
Who are you? Are you in league with this Thief? I demand that you free me immediately!
You have done what the Yokudans could not. You have slain Zal'ik. You have given me my freedom.\n\nAnd yet, forgive me if I feel no joy. Zal'ik was a brave man. He only wanted to save his people.
This book could hold a cure and even more that we do not yet know.\n\nIt will be invaluable to us.
You didn't die! I mean, of course you didn't die. I had absolute faith in you.
If we're going to learn what happened to the atronachs, you must rescue Kelmen Locke from the Greycloak mercenaries.
You must find and defeat the air monarch. An atronach with the power of three monarch atronachs is just too dangerous.
You turned the tide for us, my friend. I was sure we were done for at least a dozen times today.
Hail, comrade! Quite a hike to get up here, eh? Good! Helps build endurance. You'll need it out here—trust me.

Strange. I've seen these ruins jutting from the waters before. They always seemed so … ordinary. \n\nBut now they're practically humming with energy. And I sense … what is that … my gods, yes! It's some kind of entrance.
It looks a hopeless task to me, but something makes me want to believe Hara would not have sent us here if she wasn't sure we could find whatever it is she needs us to see.
Keep back from the platform.

Use this time to gather your allies, sharpen your skills and hone your reflexes. \n\nWe've won a great victory, but the war has only just begun. When the time is right to go on the offensive against the Serpent, I will call for you to lead us.
The Apex Stone rests below, in the sewers of Elinhir.\n\nThe Seeker's Sight will aid you once you get inside and help you find your way.
Do not fear for us. We will not let the Serpent devour us.\n\nWe will be the crack in the armor. You will be the blade that liberates us.
We must find the Mage's other aspects before the Serpent does.
Welcome to the Diamond Thimble! <<1>>, your new proprietor, at your service.
The Lost One carries our thoughts, as we carry hers. But her mind is corrupted, and she reserves no place of affection for you in her darkened heart.\n\nShe will not hold back. Neither should you.
When we are whole, it will take all of our concentration to resist the Serpent's will.\n\nShould we fail to overcome his grip, you must strike us down. We will do our best to weaken our darker self.
The Warden is dead. His prisoners freed. What fun this has been!\n\nYou've done well, for such a fleeting creature. I have found a new, and very slight, respect for mortal-kind.

You look like danger interests you.\n\nWhat would you say if I knew of a tower of mages that until recently was sealed for centuries, and that was so dangerous that no one has entered the upper halls and lived?
Are you really thinking of helping those crazy High Elves? Well, I guess it's your time to waste.

I don't know what you're up to, and I don't really care. Just stay out of our way. We've got work to do.\n\nYou might want to avoid the upper floors, while you're at it. There's no telling what the Learned One might do.
That mere mortals could best the Warrior so easily gives me pause—I question whether that kind of power belongs in mortal hands. But I thank you for your help.
I'll be returning to Belkarth soon. I just need to finish a few things here first.\n\nI might even bring some of this wine back with me. Stars know we could always use more wine at the observatory.
<An old Dwarven orrery. It contains nothing of interest.>

Another interruption? The Learned One has taught us much since her arrival, but undoing the Archive seal has had a … trying effect on our work.\n\nIf you insist on trampling through our facilities, stay away from the upper floor. For your own good.

We've not had visitors to the Aetherian Archive in a long time. You should know that you pose a risk to yourself by stepping outside this chamber.\n\nThe Learned One does not want outsiders on the upper floors. I would not test her.
This one would not go near the Citadel again for all the moon-sugar in Tamriel.\n\nActually, that's not true.

So you plan on approaching that Citadel, eh? You look like you can take care of yourself, but I'm telling you—no one who's stepped out there has returned, be they scholar, merchant, or warrior.\n\nIt's your life.
You … you plan to venture within?\n\nI do not possess your bravery, but please—many of my friends, scholars, drivers of the caravans, have gone inside and not returned. Help them if you still can.
My friend, you're victorious!\n\nI hope Hel Ra Citadel was fierce enough for you!
The ship's new crew will work out. And if they don't, the captain will send them off to the old mutineers.
It is good to see you up and about. I credit <<1>>'s sweet sea breezes with your recovery!
Leave an old man be!
Rana's waiting for you in the village. Go on. She doesn't bite, though she looks like she might.
Stay back! If the guards see us speak, they'll beat us both!
Do not worry, my friend. The poison will do no lasting harm.\n\nTo her, I mean. She will need to burn her bedsheets.
Welcome to my humble home. What can Magistrate Banu do for you today?
I don't care to sail through corpses. But if I dock at Mistral, they'll inspect my cargo!\n\nWhich is all legitimate, I assure you.
Hm. It seems you did not complete the course. That's no reason to give up, however! Would you like to try again?
Oh the pockets this one picked with her father showing her the way. Such fine memories!
I was the fastest rider in my village. As long as the finish line was less than a league away. The truth is, I'm more of a sprinter.
Satakal's vengeance must be quick as a serpent's strike. You'll find my traitorous acolytes at Scaled Court enclaves throughout the region.
The Moons are pleased, walker. Very pleased.
Any news about our missing guards? We're counting on you to see this through for us.
That look on your face. You look like you've been beaten. They beat me, too—I didn't let it bother me … by the Moons this hurts.\n\nYou're alive, aren't you? Get back in there!
What're you doing down here? Flee, you fool! The Serpent is here, and his Scaled Court runs rampant through these caverns!

You'd best turn around, stranger. The Star-Gazers had reason to suspect Scaled Court activity in these caves, but it's not just the Court—the Celestial Serpent is here! \n\nHe has plans for Craglorn. For all of Tamriel.

What do you want? Have you fools come to your senses? Ready to set me free?\n\nThe master will do it himself after he peels the skin off you! He will not suffer a member of his Court humiliated like this! I will not suffer it!
Little goat is still here? Why? Little goat has work to do! Don't come back until the task is done!
Is the Covenant on our side or the Daedras'? Kill me or free me, but decide quickly.

Did you come looking for the Scaled Court, too? Looks like the bastards have no shortage of enemies.\n\nYou have that look in your eye. If you're planning on going into these caves, you'll need equipment. Just so happens I have some I could sell you.
This place is fascinating, isn't it? As naturally beautiful as the cultists inside are deranged.\n\nSay—while I have you here, how about you take a look at my wares?
Wonder where you've been all this time.

Thanks to the bravery of people such as you, we scholars can do our own part to make the world a better place.\n\nI need to return to Dragonstar. My companions need to know what's happening here. When you find the Scaled Court, show them no mercy.
We were fortunate you arrived when you did. Nerien'eth single-handedly trounced the lot of us, even as we were fully prepared to face him.\n\nYou must be formidable indeed.
We're getting sicker by the minute. Please, hurry!
This is a private matter, and your presence draws attention. I do not require the Wrath of Sithis to escort me beyond our sanctuary.\n\nBut that's not it, is it? Why are you here?
Hey there! Bad news, my friend. Norion is plugged tighter than an Elf with his holes melted shut.\n\nBut when everything's bottled up, the trick is to seal yourself inside.
I hate funerals. The best part happens before I arrive.\n\nBut it doesn't care. Tell me, has it found the meat?
What a terrible day. Such a tragedy. Et cetera, et cetera.
Where is that imbescile?
Yes? Is there something you need?
Gods, I need a drink. Maybe five. I can't face Norion like this.
We gave everything to defeat Nerien'eth. And were it not for the kindness of a stranger, we would be at his mercy—again. You have my thanks, friend.\n\nAt least the day is won.
So that mantikora monster was real? Huh. Maybe I should try to find the wish-granting mammoth those Nord gladiators told me about.
Aetherian light take him! I was so certain I could best Nerien'eth this time. That I had strengthened my spells.\n\nIf you hadn't happened by, we'd all be dead. Again.
Let's not start something we'll both regret. I could use some help and you're going to want to hear what I have to say.
March forth into the streets and teach those fiends a lesson! \n\nLet your faith not waiver, for the gods will be with you.

There are Scaled Court in the mountains, in a cavern the Serpent cultists called "Sanctum Ophidia." I'll meet you there—a group of Gazers remains, but they'll need help.\n\nThe Serpent means to kill us all. Man or mer. He doesn't give a damn.

Speak to my seneschal, Little Leaf. You'll find her to the east, along the road through the northeast passage between Upper and Lower Craglorn.\n\nI would be eternally grateful if you make sure no harm befalls her during her mission.
Ah! This one hates being snuck up on.

Stendarr protect you, friend. If Virmaril is the source of this darkness, then the danger is greater than I expected.\n\nI will seek another way inside. A way that avoids that terrible, insistent voice.
I can't join you for this. One of us needs to return to Belkarth and prepare the city's defenses.\n\nYou and the Thief … avenge Kelmen and stop this mad viper. For all our sakes.
Use the portal and return to the Observatory. I will meet you there.

I knew I could count on you! The smaller creatures should pose little threat, but be warned. One of the fell beasts is of immense size. It slaughtered half of my former companions before I escaped!\n\nI'll follow you inside after you clear the way.
Hah, I knew you'd come back alive. No poncy Elven High Kinlord fancydress mageling was going to stop the likes of you.
Your soul is not free of your body just yet. What of the spirits of the crypt?
You give Sergeant Shaghila new hope. This one is sick of these damn Daedra everywhere. You close those portals and she will feel much better.
I can train and certify blacksmiths, clothiers, and woodworkers. If that sounds like something you'd want, we can get started.
The great warrior, Titus, seeks your counsel.
Perhaps the time has come to find one last battle to fight. I'd rather face a warrior's death while I still have some sense of who I am.

The darkness that shrouds Titus's mind blocks my connection to him. But since you touched my Apex Stone, I can still communicate with you.\n\nYou consider Titus to be a friend. Are you ready to help him?

You must be here to learn a craft, yes? Your alliance covers my considerable fees, allowing me to impart my knowledge at no cost to you.\n\nIf you prove yourself, I'll certify you as competent to fulfill crafting writs.
Zantan would kiss you, but both he and you have not bathed in some time.
You've done me a great service. I had a bad feeling about this job. Never again. The Undaunted can keep their song. I never liked it, anyway.\n\nThat's a lie. Dammit.

<You notice a prominent handbill on the requisition board.>\n\n"The people of West Weald bid you welcome! Masters of the craft await you in <<1>>! New crafters shall be trained! Accomplished crafters will be certified! All at no cost to you!"
"ATTENTION: Covenant Citizens! Masters of the craft await you in <<1>>! Free training for all new to their craft; certification for accomplished crafters! All at no cost to you, citizen!"
I'll never forget what the Daedra did to me—or what you did for me.
All that's left is to destroy the Sigil Stone.\n\nIt will take us, and any who have entered through the Oblivion Gate back to Whisper Grove. If this isn't some kind of Daedric illusion.
We're back, aren't we? Thought that was my last delve. Perhaps it still will be. I'm not sure I could do that twice.
It might not seem like it, but Hogondar is a lonely Nord.

That was it for Brittgerd! I made it back, and I am hanging up the sword for good.\n\nThere are pockets to Oblivion in all corners of this world—they could be anywhere. And I am done with Oblivion. Skyrim is just a little more pleasant.
Sobabe appreciates all you have done. She thinks she is finished with adventuring. She had her fill in Oblivion. Now she will fill with delicious moon-sugar—to forget the battle and the blood.
I have dreamed of trying an Oblivion pie since I first heard about them. But now, I erect the spine of ….\n\nI do not like this.
A bushel of us are quitting. Cowards. For a lot of them, this was their first foray. Wamasu dens and necromancer tombs are much more pleasant than Oblivion. No one believes me.
Appreciate the assist. I can tell you've done this before.
What're you doing? Get your head down before you're spotted!
Are those Imperial reports you're holding? Where did you get them?
Make your introduction to Urgarlag brief. Sparking her ire or her interest could be detrimental to your health.
You met Urgarlag yet? You'll want to if you have an appetite for danger!
These Dremora patrols in the sewers are a great concern. \n\nThey keep surprising our soldiers, and Sergeant Shaghila is worried that they will eventually discover our base.
Hold there, Daedric scum! One more step and I'll …. Oh! It's you again. I have the best news! You go first.
Ah, you return at last. I was beginning to lose hope. Is the storm witch dead? Do you have something of mine?
Kireth knows better than to jump into strange holes. She knows I can't abide small, dark spaces.

I could have saved you a lot of trouble if I had brought my brother's radial component extractor with me. But what can I say? I'm spontaneous!\n\nI'll finish up here and meet you by the main entrance after you get the power core.

You … you brought the king here? Then welcome to our siege camp. Sorry you had to see those damn harpies at work.\n\nI'm not sure King Kurog should be walking around out in the open, but I've got a barrel full of my own worries to deal with.
You're back. I assume Watcher's Hold is in disarray?
Ah! If it isn't my esteemed business partner! \n\nI smell profit, friend … and dog. But mostly profit! Did you find the whistle?
This one cares nothing about Captain Henrisa's pathetic excuses. Her share depended on delivering the goods on schedule. \n\nShe is late, so she gets paid less. There is nothing more to say.

Have you heard? The famous explorer, Lady Laurent, is leading an expedition to find the tomb of the first Orc king, Torug gro-Igron.\n\nProbably all kinds of treasure in a king's tomb—if you were interested in that sort of thing, of course.
Ah, you've returned! How wonderful to see you again.\n\nTell me, were you successful? Did you acquire the items I asked for? Did you get the frozen egg?
I carry only the rarest items from the ancient deserts of Alik'r.\n\nAre you a collector of rare antiquities? If not, then I fear that my wares will be of little interest to you. Have a nice day.
You aren't back with <<1>>. Dammit! I wanted to be wrong.\n\nTell me what did this to him. To all of us. If I have to write epitaphs, I want to get them right.

My potions are more mundane, best used to help around a farm or a homestead. You'd be surprised how many clan wives come by on a regular basis.\n\nIf you want something more suited to an adventuring life, you'll need to talk to Hydalion.

Eggs! Beautiful, glorious eggs! Get your eggs right here! \n\nScramble them, fry them, hard boil them—you can even throw them at people when they annoy you! You can't do that with a tomato! Well, I guess you could, but an egg works so much better!
Great. I can't just leave him out here. I'm going to have to clean up this mess.
Go! Go on! Leave me—damn you! I can take care of myself!
A most surprising collection of items! Each a piece of the puzzle, I'm sure.\n\nThe book likely holds the answers, but it will take considerable time to translate. If it's even possible.
Thank you for explaining matters to the forge-wife, but I'm not surprised by her reaction. I'll make sure that these automatons are put to good use in Orsinium.

So our ambassador finally found you? Took her damn time. But you're here and that's what counts. \n\nWelcome to Orsinium. Isn't it coming along splendidly? Be proud, young one, it's your home, too. Orsimer are unstoppable when we work together.
You were saying something about a betrayer and the stolen supplies?

Well, now that that's done, I guess it's out of the bee hive and back to the hornet's nest. Orsinium. Sometimes I think I have more enemies there than I have out here.\n\nIf you're willing, I'd like you to come back to the city with me.
The constructs don't belong here and they don't belong in Orsinium.
Damn. My master works with some nasty concoctions, so I'm no stranger to bad smells, but you positively reek. Even from over here.\n\nWhere have you been? Crawling around in the sewers?
The now full crate sits here, waiting for you to sign the shipment manifest.
Oh. I heard footsteps and thought you might be my husband coming home at last. I hope Canuldil is all right.
If you really plan to recover our banner, you must be on your guard in the mine.\n\nNot only are the werewolves cunning and fast, but the order placed traps throughout the mine to protect it.
Don't worry. Now that you've dealt with the Reachmen warlord, we'll finish up here.
My warriors have the harpies and the Winterborn on the run! You should have no problems at all reaching the fortress. No problems at all!\n\nFor king and glory!
Do you not smell the danger? Crouch and hide!
What're you doing? Get your head down before you're spotted!
I prefer the blood and sweat of a duel to the death to a test of skill, but I guess it worked out. Gloorig's going to be a fine chieftain.

Assisting with research like this is a noble pursuit. We must educate people.\n\nSure the Riekr bathe in filth and sometimes eat their young, but these behaviors maintain their social structure. Some of their other behaviors are quite advanced.
<<1>> will not lose another clan.\n\nI won't allow it.
Ah, I can smell the all-too-familiar stench of Riekr on you. I'm guessing you have the items Nellic wrote me about. Good.\n\nWhat about Apprentice Mezhun? Any word from him?
As promised, I will attend Kurog's moot. You have my word.
I was fine until I stopped to rest. That's when I noticed that one of those damn Riekrs bit me!
Thanks for rescuing my sister and the other hunters.\n\nBut tell me, were you able to acquire the Riekr chief's totem?
How long are you going to have us standing here? Let's move!\n\nI want my throne room back!

That banekin got me good in my last bout. I took down a clannfear, but that little bastard snuck up on me. Got me bleeding like a pig.\n\nYeah. I suspect that's going to turn out to have been my last fight.
Word of advice—if you mention Trinimac to <<1>>, he'll cut you off.

You must be either brave or foolish to hazard these streets, but I salute you nonetheless as a fellow soldier. \n\nI am looking for my brother. He's about my height, a little younger … has a terrible haircut. Don't suppose you've seen him?

The mighty King Kurog sends greetings and asked me to extend this formal invitation. His mightiness invites you to bask upon his royal presence in the throne room.\n\nHe says he needs a trustworthy ally at his side.
The ambassador? This one hasn't seen the ambassador since she helped me get off the boat.

Treasonous bastards! I just saved their ungrateful arses and this is the thanks I get?\n\nI even showed them Ice-Heart's sword! How can I create a united nation when the chiefs refuse to accept my rule?

As you can see, the clan chiefs can be a contentious lot. They oppose King Kurog at every turn—especially on matters of faith.\n\nBut tell me. Was Kurog successful? Did you defeat the Winterborn warlord?
Don't worry about me. I'll be fine once I catch my breath. Just got the wind knocked out of me a little, that's all.
I'll keep my ears open for Kurog's summons. If anything, I suppose this moot will at least be more interesting than listening to my wives complain about things all day.
I'm glad I found you!
Winter on the range. It's almost poetic. The stillness, the quiet, the cold fit to freeze your … fingers off.
I know the cheers won't last. I'll need to guard against challengers from all sides, to be twice the chief my father was.\n\nBut for now? This feels good. This feels right.
Listen, we both know you're the one who avenged the chief. Happy I could land a few good smacks.\n\nI'll tell <<1>> when she's back. You deserve the credit.
We should get back to Shatul. <<1>> needs the <<z:2>>.
I'm sorry you had to face her alone. I read in the Scroll there would have been … consequences for me had I gotten involved in that battle.\n\nHad to time that portal just right!
So, what have you killed lately?
When you slosh your way through that water outside, don't think about the fact that it's just a big latrine. Makes me glad I don't have to wade through it.\n\nWhat's on your mind?
<No new notices have been posted to the Hunting Board since you last checked.>

I cannot express what this means to me. This district is close to my heart. My family moved here from the Summerset Isles way back in the First Era.  \n\nWe have lived here for generations. I only hope we can remain for generations to come.

There you are. You just missed it. The ground was shaking and it felt like the entire district was about to be plunged into the abyss.\n\nI'm guessing that means you didn't get there in time to stop the ritual?

I was Grand Champion in the arena last year. I never had any real competition. One thing about the Daedra taking over—at least it's a challenge again.\n\nEvery day gets a little harder. Eventually, I'll lose, but until then, I'll keep fighting.
You are a smart one, walker. Aishah can tell these things. She can appraise a person just as she can appraise the goods brought to her to sell.
Thank you for agreeing to help me. I have nowhere else to turn, and … that thing … it must die.\n\nI'm glad you understand.
Thank you for easing a mother's mind. Shining-Eyes does not like it when I treat him like one fresh-from-the-egg, but it is so cold … he should have carried his shirt with him when he went out.
By the Egg, tell me she didn't …. I recognize that shirt you're carrying. My mother sent you, didn't she?\n\nIf my scales were not frozen, they would be purple with embarrassment.

Ah, there you are, my risk-seeking friend. Even when it's been tested before, a spell like this can be unpredictable. I'm glad you didn't get pulled into the Veil yourself.\n\nTell me though, did the spell work? Were you able to banish the Veilweavers?
Well, at least one of my babies is safe. Please, keep looking!
Welcome back. Did you acquire those specimens for me?
I heard the bugle all the way over here. Did my archers' arrows strike true?

The heat of the rocks here is comforting in this cold climate. This one must remain here. He is watching for a ship called the Dawn Posset. It carries very important cargo.\n\nThe ship is many days late now, but Azaro must maintain his vigil.
You are not a Daedra, are you? What do you want?
Knowledge of your enemy's movements is half the battle. The easier half, in my experience.

One thing about the city falling under attack … it may be violent and frightening for most people, but for someone who's worked every day for five years, it's actually relaxing. \n\nJust not having to be at that miserable place … it's liberating.
Please do hurry along. \n\nI hope Gryna's still in the Arboretum, but she could be anywhere by now … or worse, what if she really is dead? It's simply unthinkable.

<You notice a prominent handbill on the requisition board.>\n\n"The people of West Weald bid you welcome! Masters of the craft await you in <<1>>! New crafters shall be trained! Accomplished crafters will be certified! All at no cost to you!"
I don't care how great the Moth Priest says you are. The Palace should be reclaimed under the banner of the Empress Regent.\n\nDon't make a mess of this.
The Priest made us wait all this time … for you? I expected an army. I hope you know what you just signed up for, stranger.

Sister Arminus assures us you're to play a vital role, today.\n\nOf course, she also said that we're standing on a pinion of reality, that we have no idea how lucky we are we haven't been whisked into the cosmic beyond. And then she laughed about it.
Please find Maximinus, if you can. I desperately need that money!
I've always hated spiders, but I think today proved that squashing them can be extremely gratifying.\n\nAt any rate, you've been a great help. Two-Blades will probably want to thank you, too.

Another recruit? We are glad to have you, friend. But I warn you—the city makes Cyrodiil seem like a mid-day wallow in a salt-meadow swamp. There are things here that would rattle Hist roots. Steel yourself.
I dare not stay in one place for long. The Daedra are everywhere. Did General Hal-Rei send you? Speak quickly!

The Rat hopes you find the arena fighters before the Daedra make them fight again. \n\nThey need poultices or the fights won't even be interesting to watch, and that's really what the Rat cares about.
Ezudash wishes you good luck. Clumsy walkers like you always need it, yes? Ha!
May Tava guide your steps, wayfarer. May she take you to the people of this city who are in need, and bless your efforts to help them.\n\nGo now. You have done all you can here.

Watch out for Covenant and Pact soldiers out there. If by some miracle, the district's already captured, blow the horn to let me know. For the gods' damn sake, no one else has. \n\nWhen you're done, report back here. Luck be with you, comrade.
You'll have to excuse my brother. He's a little prickly, but his heart's pure. Perhaps I can make it up to you.\n\nI have some information I think your alliance might find extremely valuable.
Travel down the river is not cheap.
Eyes of Magnus! All I can see is a shadowy form, you are not a Daedra, are you? I hope not. \n\nWhere are you, exactly? What part of the city?
The lock on this Imperial coffer has been broken and it appears someone took any valuables within but left a stack of documents.
Our funds are exhausted. You'll need to come back later.
I'd love to help you, but my hands are tied. New funds won't be available until later. You will come back later, right?\n\nRight?
The till is closed. You Enforcers were just too efficient today.
You'll need to hang on to that contraband just a little longer. The cupboard is bare, as they say.
Ah, Enforcer. I was so looking forward to dealing with you. Alas, you'll have to return later.
I can't accept any more confiscated goods. Come back later. I'll make it up to you. Promise.
I'm closed. Come back another time.
Sorry, my funds have run dry. Kind of like my thirst. I need another drink!
We're all out of funds. No rewards for returned contraband until later.
Another Enforcer looking for payment? Come back later. We're out of funds.
Oh dear. You'll have to come back another time. We've nothing to give you right now.
Sorry. We're, uh, low on gold right now. Come back later.
Ah, we're out of funds right now, but come back later. We'll pay you, I promise!
Don't be angry with me. It's just … we're a little low on gold right now. Come back later, please?
More contraband? A pity, we're all out of gold. But come back later, hmm?
The Guard is not currently distributing rewards. You'll have to return another time.
Glad to see you've decided to join our number. Remember: we exist to protect the weak and the innocent. That is our first and highest calling.
Another outsider? At least you look more capable than that braggart, Narsis Dren.
Remember to keep your eyes open. Look for a key to the vault.\n\nAnd a way to stop the draugr, of course!
My beloved certainly enjoys a good meal! It makes my heart sing to see him so happy!
My friend! Welcome back!\n\nBut tell me, were you able to acquire the ingredients for my evening of Orcish romance?

I may try to actually increase the potency of Woolly's cheese. I know a number of clan chiefs that could use some help when it comes to getting their wives into a receptive mood.\n\nIf you know what I mean.
Look around. Do you think I'd be all the way out here if I wanted company?
This land inspires me! I already have enough ideas to fill an entire book of poetry!
Remember, the more that Rigurt smells of battle and blood, the more attracted Lazdutha will be.\n\nJust be careful. That bear is a monster! That's why we call him the Orc word for death—Norgim.
That was some tale he told. The Dark Elf will probably want to get paid for his efforts.
You're really going to tell the truth, aren't you? That's … appalling!
Well, no matter where the Fist resides, my reputation will definitely increase as news of this spreads.\n\nThank you for your assistance, my friend.
You missed all the drama! While you were unconscious, Lady Laurent and our helpful Orc had a dreadfully intense argument about the Armlet of Torug.\n\nIt was wonderful to watch!
We're starting a new chapter in Orc history, thanks to you.

Isn't this place grand! And they were happy to have a researcher of my caliber join their staff.\n\nFeel free to look around. We have some lovely displays coming together downstairs that show the width and breadth of Orsimer history.
What do you say? Let me pay you for that amulet you found and everybody walks away happy.\n\nAnd breathing.
Go on. The ambassador needs you. I'll do what I can for his lordship.\n\nFunny, I never expected him to try to be a hero. Maybe he isn't a complete milksop after all.
His lordship ran toward that signal tower over there. I wonder why he thinks he'll find the ambassador in such a wretched place?
When this is all over, my father is going to disown me. And I hate to imagine what Lady Sovelle must think of me. There must be some way that I can make all this right.
Can't you see I'm busy? My ships crashed upon the ice and I have a lot on my mind right now.
My stupid son! I can't believe he went off to follow in his father's footsteps, the idiot!
Well, I'll be damned. I remember you! You helped Darien and me, back in Camlorn.\n\nIf you're involved in the commander's plan, I feel more confident already!

"Stand back and stay out of the way, Elf!" They actually said that to me!\n\nWe're surrounded by death and destruction and they're worried that an outsider might show them up! They can take their pride and … sorry, sorry. I'm a little stressed.

Soon we march for Orsinium. Before long, the forge-hammer will once more sing in Morkuldin.\n\nAnd if I can figure out how to work the blood-forge with frostbite spiders, the song will go "clang, clang, splat." Heh.
If you could untie me, I would greatly appreciate it.\n\nAnd would you know if my husband is safe? He's Lord Ethian and I made sure he got off the wrecked ship with a few of the crew and passengers.
Now there's something you don't see every day. A tree growing out of a corpse. I'd say this is what we were looking for.\n\nThis sapling is but a root, however, a small part of a greater whole.
I'm not one hundred percent certain, but I bet I could break the chain holding up the cage with a few well-placed arrows.

I have to admit, those Orc catapulteers can certainly hit a mark!\n\nNow all we need to do is find this alchemist. The Orcs want him inside the fort so he can locate the source of those briarheart warriors.

Well, I'll be damned. I remember you! You helped Darien and me, back in Camlorn. You get around a lot, don't you?\n\nHave you come all this way to help me? Maybe we still have a chance to salvage this mission yet!
The Wood Elf got me out of that cage with a damn fine strike. Damn fine!\n\nAnd you, you handled the briarheart tree perfectly. Well done!

The alchemist was almost roasted alive and he's not even remotely distressed about it. No concern for my feelings at all.\n\nDid he thank me for rescuing him? No. Does he show even a little gratitude? Not one bit!
Best not to keep my mother waiting. \n\nGo. Speak to her. Let's see if her plan sounds better than mine.
My son's bravery borders on stupidity. He would run off and stumble blindly into their trap without the slightest regard for his safety.\n\nWe must not allow that to happen.
Now move along before I get really angry.
Fine. Do things your way. Nobody ever believes the cute Wood Elf.\n\nI'm going to stay here and watch those two, anyway. They're up to something. I'm sure of it!
I … everyone's dead. Maybe … maybe there's still hope for the others. Solgra … she took them with her. Tried to hide in the back. I … I don't know what's happened to Solgra and the others.
I would accompany you on this mission, but my duty demands I remain at the king's side until this danger has passed.\n\nGood luck, outsider.
Show these Malacath fanatics no mercy! They deserve to die painfully and horribly for committing this outrage!
Bazrag plays with the patience of the king.\n\nHe has gone too far this time. We will not let this outrage stand.
