Did Orsinium send you? Are you part of the reinforcements?\n\nThe Winterborn came out of nowhere. It happened so fast. They took our cargo into the hills and the Orc peasants chased them. That's when Chief Bazrag and his warriors arrived.
You got the totem. Good. Wish I could have whacked that Riekr chieftain in the head with it, but I suppose you took care of that, too.
Do you think they remained in these ruins, looking for me?
You have undone my greatest accomplishment. Generations of effort, reduced to parts.\n\nCome then, bottle fly. Trample your dung-stained feet about my workshop.
<The body of <<1>>.>

You don't know how good that feels! Urfon Ice-Heart is finally dead!\n\nImagine you ate too much and, try as you might, you can't get out that really big belch. Then, finally, you let out a thunderous burp. Yeah, that's how I feel right now.
Now, I can finally rest.
You honored those who forged Old Orsinium from nothing. Now you will curse those who caused her fall.
You have done well, outsider. Not only were you able to find this sanctuary, you proved yourself worthy enough to take up the sacred words. \n\nYou should be honored to be so favored by Malacath.

You're the outsider who leaped into the bear's den to fight the Winterborn? Ulsha and the Wood Elf mentioned you.\n\nSurprised you didn't end up all bruised and bloody like the rest of these fools. This is our home, not an amusement for your pleasure!
You brought back my daughter, and she returns with the Hand of Morkul.\n\nNo chief can deny her, now!
I do not know you, yet you approach with great purpose. State your intentions and let Malacath judge your worth.

Ah, it's good to see another Orsimer in this forsaken city! I don't know about you, but I'm so tired of dealing with these fancy-cloaked, self-important weaklings!\n\nOh, you have a letter from the Forge-Mother? Then praise Trinimac and all that.
I think … I think I found my mother.\n\nI was a fool to think my family might still be alive. There are other Khajiit skeletons in here.
Orgotha patched me up. She's almost as good at healing as she is at hunting!

It's time to assemble the Great Moot. I want you to visit the clan chiefs that still haven't accepted my grand vision, talk some sense into them.\n\nGet to them before Bazrag poisons the well and really turns them against me.
The king still wants to have words with you. Don't keep him waiting.
A Great Moot! That sounds so exciting! I really enjoy it when we get to mingle with members of other clans.\n\nPlease don't fail my beloved. He's counting on you, you know!

And my champion returns, still alive and with most of your vital body parts intact! My shield-wives owe me. I told them not to bet against me!\n\nBut enough of that. Were you successful? Are the clan chiefs going to attend the moot?
You're back. Did you find The Rat's message? Well? Sorry to be … I mean … I've just had to do a lot of talking. My ears are ringing, but I'm all right.\n\nDon't look so sour. I think we have a plan.

I had the hardest time finding you. Looked all over the city, even got lost once or twice.\n\nI did find an adorable sweets shop, though. They had these wonderful tiny cakes that were absolutely delicious! Who knew Orc cakes could taste so good?

Thank you for responding so quickly to my summons. Especially considering everything you've been doing to support the king.\n\nDid Eveli tell you that I have a … delicate … situation? I could really use your help again.
Those little savages left me for dead, but I managed to find my way out of there.\n\nFor a bunch of stupid Riekrs, this group was pretty organized.
That Riekr chief was kind of grabby. And his breath smelled like rotten troll fat.\n\nThanks for getting me out of there!
I'm glad you're back. It's starting to get cold out here!\n\nWell, colder, really. I'm not sure how the Orcs and the Nords stand it. Did you find a rope? Was it right where I said it would be?

If I'm still employed when this debacle is over, I must remember to reset and update the various defenses. And I must do something about this well.\n\nSorry, can't help myself. Making improvements, that's just in my nature.

So Kurog's pet shows up again. Are you here to make sure I'm still a prisoner, or has he sent you to cut my throat?\n\nCome on, what are you waiting for? Just kill me and get it over with! Or don't you have the guts for that kind of work?
I'm glad I was able to help get us out of there. I just wish Unsulag was still with us, though.
I'm glad I was able to help us get out of there, but I wish Gahar was still with us.
Really? That was your plan? Let my brother fix the homicidal construct?\n\nYou should have just given a sharp axe to an angry Orc. We'd all be a lot safer.
<<1>> will forgive me for some of the things I said, won't she?\n\nI'm sure she will. I'm sure.
Look at this little guy! He's not a metal monster, no matter what Kireth may think.\n\nHe was just drunk on the excess energy the damaged power core was giving off. I'll have him fixed up in no time!

So <<1>> and <<2>> were pulled into a war neither wanted. They dueled to stop an endless siege. And they died betrayed by the plots of a Breton king?\n\nThese are not the legends I was raised to believe.

As soon as you turn that valve, that timer for the lock reset is going to start. Keep that in your head. There's a pattern, though. It changes daily, but if you take your time and watch carefully, you should be able to figure out the current pattern.
Something isn't right in all this. I hope you can see that.\n\nIn any case, just kill me or let me go, because I'm not letting you turn me over to Kurog.
So now what? I've never taken an Orc chief prisoner before.
I hope that job in Orsinium is still waiting for me. I won't really feel better until I'm back in a kitchen and making good food for good people again.
I don't know what you did, but it's much appreciated.\n\nNow I just need to wake up my weakling companions and get out of here before the Reachmen arrive.

When I was trapped behind the fire and I thought I was going to die, all I could think about was Raza and going back to our home in Shornhelm.\n\nNow? Now I think I want to stay here and learn more about my Orc heritage.
I didn't want to get involved with <<1>>'s concerns. A lot of sharp edges to her.
I'd make a great chief. But then who would herd the echatere?
Leave me to mourn my husband.
How could <<1>> have anything to do with <<2>>'s death? She loved him more than any of his wives. Except me.
It is done? The Beast of the Reach—is she dead?

The Vosh Rakh practically bragged about their plan as they tossed me in that cell. They said it was going to be big and bold and really show the world what Trinimac is all about.\n\nThey didn't tell me any details, but I think it involves the moot.

Speak to Eveli. Convince her that we need her help or many innocent lives will be lost in Trinimac's name.\n\nThen you need to head for Paragon's Remembrance. We can't afford to waste time. The Vosh Rakh aren't going to wait for us, after all.

I hate this situation, I really do.\n\nBeing a hero, that's supposed to be pure and honest. Good is good and evil is evil, you know what I mean? But nothing here is clear cut. I can't tell the good guys from the bad.
<The cultist appears lost in thought.>
Poor <<1>>! Why will none believe that <<2>> stole from the king, not her?

Tomorrow the Savage Sons march to kill ten thousand Bretons.\n\nAnd before we arrive, King Golkarr will crap out another statue of Malacath to line Orsinium's halls. What's a siege without garish celebration?

Do you see how King Joile forces my hand? If I refuse to challenge <<1>>, the Breton king will demand <<2>> do so in my place. My obedience, or my friend's life.\n\nThis is what kings call "leadership."
King Kurog requests the honor of your presence, outsider. My beloved awaits your arrival at the keep, so do not linger. \n\nHis dark mood is bad enough without you disappointing him as well.
So? Tell me what you thought!

Have you ever looked at these statues? I mean really looked at them? Legends carved into bronze or stone. The work of hundreds of hours, likely crafted by people who didn't know a thing about their subject matter.\n\nAnd for what purpose, do you think?

Isn't it amazing? Here I am, a simple commoner, getting to watch history in the making!\n\nI wonder if the new king will let us cater his coronation? The Greedy Gut has the best chef in Orsinium, you know.
Thank you! You saved my Shalda!
You're back. Anything else you need?
You're a pleasant scent in a dank swamp! Eveli was started to get worried and she can't wait to talk to you.\n\nWait, where's Talviah?

I never said thank you. For helping us when we first arrived in Wrothgar, remember? Well, thank you.\n\nIt feels good to finally be doing what we actually came here to do. You won't find better scouts in all of Orsinium—that I know of.
How many times must I tell you? Leave. Me. Alone!

Have you studied the scrolls? Do you know the words of Trinimac and are you ready to enter the Gauntlet?\n\nThe only aid you will receive is the blessing that you choose, so make your selection wisely.
That didn't take long for you to mess up.\n\nYou should avoid… everything. I shouldn't have to tell you that.
I was briefly tempted to ask where you acquired the mug. Then I thought, "why not order more wine?"
You know, come to think of it, maybe the message is in some kind of code. Hey, maybe someone in the Mages Guild could help you decipher that. \n\nI mean, if you need any help, that is.

Remember, the first word of every sentence. If you forget, just come back and this one will remind you for no extra charge. And don't worry. This one never reveals a client's secrets.\n\nNice doing business with you!
Well done. I can see you're no stranger to clockwork opponents. You're good. \n\nUnless it was beginner's luck.
I'll catch up with you in the council chamber. I need to make myself presentable before I follow you in there.
See what you can find in here. We can't let all of this be for nothing.
Anybody could be a Vosh Rakh? That's not fair. That's not fair at all.\n\nHow are we supposed to save the day when we can't tell the good guys from the bad guys?
You've done it, haven't you? <<Cz:1>>—do you have it?
Was the high-and-mighty captain any help, or did she just tell you to tusk off, too?
No, no. You've had your fill. No more secrets. Off! Off with you!

Go tell Kurog what's happening in his own kingdom and don't leave his side until you make him listen. Do whatever you have to, but you have to convince him to postpone the moot.\n\nI'll catch up with you as soon as I can.
You go warn the king. Don't worry, I'll keep the high priestess safe. You can count on me.
When I get to Orsinium, I'm going to look for a hot meal and a strong drink.
You're … a little late.\n\nThey just … left me here to die ….

I am so disappointed in you. I thought when you killed your friend, you did so for Trinimac and our cause. But it seems that it was just a means to an end for you.\n\nIt's good that I see you for what you truly are before I let this go much further.
You learn a lot about healing when you're King Kurog's shield-wife. Looks like my skills apply to outsiders as well.\n\nBut we've wasted enough time. You need to get moving.

What in Malacath's name did they do to you? You had more holes in you than a block of echatere cheese after a skeever attack!\n\nI tended to your wounds as best I could, but I'm kind of surprised you woke up at all.
Get to the temple and make sure the high priestess is all right.
The chief needs me right now more than you do. We'll catch up with you as soon as we can.
You have the taint of Malacath upon you. Have you come to cleanse yourself and receive the blessing of a true god?

The side door leads to the library. If there's an entrance to the tunnels anywhere in the temple, it will be somewhere in that chamber.\n\nAnd don't worry about Eveli. I'll do everything I can to ease her pain.
Going to rest now … I'm very tired ….
The final battle approaches like the wind before a storm. We either stop Kurog now or we die trying.\n\nStrike true and strike often, my friend. And make every strike count!
I don't know what's going on, but Solgra has a gentle heart.\n\nI'm sure this is all just a misunderstanding.
Someday we'll build a proper forge at this site. I'll have more to do than watch icicles form on my nose.
I always knew <<1>>'s rest would be interrupted. Doesn't mean I'm happy about it.\n\nWhat now?
King Kurog's death was a tragedy, but he would want us to complete the work he started. If I might have a minute of your time ….
I think you made your position very clear. I have no interest in talking to someone who calls me a liar and a cheat.
I needed to see for myself. To watch you end it. To show Malacath we are not his playthings.
I don't believe we have anything more to discuss. Away with you!

You'd think that now that Lady Sovelle has gone off to Orsinium she'd send someone to fetch the rest of us!\n\nBut no, her ladyship is probably much too busy to be bothered with something as trivial as helping us shipwrecked survivors!

You'd best be going. I'm not sure how long I can hold this portal open. In fact, I'm not even all that sure how I opened it up to begin with. Huh. Don't make that face, I'm sure it's safe.\n\nGo on, now. I hate long goodbyes.
The <<1>> returned to Orsinium. Truly a glorious day.
Are you headed back to the Imeprial City? Slay a few of those filthy Aldmeri fetchers for me.
Are you headed back to the Imeprial City? Slay a few of those filthy Aldmeri fetchers for me.
Show our enemies no mercy. People fear the Daedra—I would have them fear us more.
Your general was telling you to keep an eye out for me, right? Here I am.
"He came to her with his …." Oh. Well, that's colorful.\n\nMara's mercy, what a waste of paper.
It's about time.\n\nYou didn't find him either? Damn. We may be too late.
You're …? Whoa! Wait! I'm not with Molag Bal's army, I swear!
Good, you're back. Gave the Xivkyn a good thrashing, I hope. Did you place the auricular geodes?
You bear the mark of the pretender and false god, Trinimac. Give in to your fury and receive the blessing of a true god!
I'm counting on you to get these people out of here. Our people, our way of life, won't die like this. I won't let it.\n\nMeet me back at your headquarters when you're done.
You escaped! Thank the Eight.\n\nThe Daedra know about this place. We shouldn't linger.
Mark me—we'll hold this garrison until Molag Bal and his minions leave the city. He's going to pay for every drop of blood he's spilled.

You're back! Were you able to get everything Rigurt requested? Oh, yes! I can smell the echatere cheese from here!\n\nPlease, don't keep the ambassador waiting! He's anxious to prepare a romantic meal and impress the woman he loves.
You're back. Find my grandfather's helm?
Well? Any requests?
Lord Arkay, guide my mace, that I might smite your enemies. Guide my steps on the path of the righteous, then give me rest at last.
Is there some reason you're staring at me?
It's good to know there are other survivors out there. We haven't seen many new faces these past months. Not living, anyway.
I must say it's good to see a fresh, living face in these barracks. We haven't much, but I might be able to sneak you a spoonful or two.

You fought valiantly, bravely. Maybe the best display of martial skill I've ever seen. I just wish we weren't forced to become king slayers.\n\nKurog and his mother are dead, but look at the price he made us pay.
I have one more task for you. Will you help me?
Any problems with the switch? I hope not, I can't quite pull that off twice.
You haven't seen any legionaries that seem out of place, have you? He'd be shorter than I am, lean, with very little hair.
Your combat skills are quite impressive. If they are impressive enough, this could turn out to be very interesting. Very interesting indeed ….
There is so much more at stake than lives and property, my child. The Daedra wish to destroy the very fabric of our faith! We cannot let that happen.
Raise the book into the light. The spell should weave the ciphers into a translated text. I think. Please hurry—this is difficult to maintain ….
Your general was telling you to keep an eye out for me, right? Here I am.

Did you hear? I'm going to stay here and help King Bazrag!\n\nStill not sure what I'll be doing, but he mentioned forming an archery unit. I'll get my own squad! I'll have to think up a clever name. Something dashing!

Bazrag the king. As much as I respect and trust Bazrag, the whole idea of another king fills me with a certain amount of dread.\n\nThat said, Trinimac wants a united Orsimer, so I guess this is really for the best. Funny, that's what Kurog wanted, too.
Another king? Well, I suppose that makes sense. A united Orsimer is certainly stronger than isolated clans.\n\nI guess you could say Kurog got his wish after all.
Another king? These Orcs just don't learn their lesson, do they?\n\nAh, well. I suppose Bazrag won't be as bad as Kurog. He couldn't be. At least, I hope he'll do a good job.
Orcs and their kings. They're almost as bad as the Bretons and High Elves.\n\nSpatter mud on their clothes and they need to have them cleaned, just like the rest of us.
Bazrag let them crown him as king? I never saw that coming!
King Bazrag? I guess it has a sort of ring to it. I just hope he knows what he's getting into.
Your general was telling you to keep an eye out for me, right? Here I am.
Are you headed back to the Imeprial City? Argonians make very fine boots. Slay some for me, eh?
Are you headed back to the Imperial City? Do not let yourself come to harm, friend. Make those Pact and Covenant fools do the dying for you.
Are you headed back to the Imperial City? May Onsi guide your blade to the Pact and Dominion's throats.
Are you headed back to the Imperial City? We need warriors like you back in the fight!
I wonder if Bazrag has any interest in a cornerclub. We wouldn't even need to change the name or anything.

Your courage and resilience in the face of adversity do you honor, my friend. If not for you, the clan chiefs and I wouldn't be standing here. And I certainly wouldn't be king.\n\nHmm, so this is all your fault, isn't it?

<<1>> told me she sent you after <<2>> … and our trade permit.\n\nThe permit is very important. If you find it, bring it to us on the road to Orsinium. But <<2>> is the light of my eyes. Please, find her.
Have you found <<1>> yet?\n\nPlease hurry. She may be hurt … and that permit won't walk to Orsinium on its own.
The legionaries scoff at my concern for these "scraps of paper"—what few remain anyway. Feh. I'm sure the moment they realize there's no structure for their compensation, they'll reconsider.
What an undeniable aroma! Let's see … bones … more bones … a slightly different bone … some sticky goop to hold it all together.\n\nMy friend, you have outdone yourself!
Well, what're you still doing up here? Those ballistae aren't going to burn themselves.
Have a care around those traps. Been a while since I oiled those springs. They're a little creaky.

I told Chief Gloorot that this was a cursed location, but he wouldn't listen. No one ever listens to old Shab.\n\nSay, you're one of those Argonians, aren't you? I never met an honest-to-Malacath lizard before.

Look at those catapults fly!\n\nI'm amazed the towers can withstand the punishment. The Bretons must have used Orc crafters and they built that place to last. But never fear. The Winterborn won't have a fort to protect them for much longer!
You made it. Excellent.\n\nI am sorry about the mess, but this cultist was not very forthcoming. All I got was this map. What did you find?
It's too bad about his lordship, but I could really use a warm tavern right about now.
Well, at least the ambassador is safe and sound. I wonder if I can find a ship going back to Wayrest in the Orc city? I could even work for my passage, if they need an able body.
You and the king have come to our aid? We're honored.\n\nBut we've been trapped in here for too long. We still have a mission to complete!
What a tragedy. All those perfectly good ships turned into so much kindling. The gods can be cruel at times, and that's the honest truth.

You think you are clever, burning tiny saplings. But they are mere children compared to our beloved tree.\n\nYour actions do not surprise me. Orcs and allies, all believe they are stronger than the Reach. Foolish, even to the end.
So … I don't suppose you … maybe … might have seen Alinon … on your way back. Maybe?
I don't care who's in charge here—you must listen! The Imperial Prison has descended into carnage. Everything else is a distraction!
You look weary, my friend. Why not have a seat? Stay and talk a while.

All done in the Arboretum? No, I thought not. Best get back to it. We need to get that tome out of the Daedra's hands.\n\nThings here are complicated. Come back later—maybe I'll have something for you.
Petition the king? What an interesting suggestion. I wonder what Chief Ramash would say about that.
Master Dren headed toward the Orc village. Said something about wanting to let them know that he saved them from the draugr.\n\nThat Master Dren, he's a real hero!
I hear you freed those hostages. Good work. Once we get them a new set of clothes and a hearty meal, they'll be ready to get to work.\n\nSonolia's been looking for you. You should go speak with her.
Back already? Excellent! I assume you've got something for me?
I swore I'd never thank a Breton—not after what your king did to my home. But when I finally go to the Ashen Forge, I'll tell Malacath a tale of the Dragon who slew the Beast.\n\nThat's all you get.
Your pardon, but I must confer with my lord—as it seems you must with yours.
Petition the king? What kind of solution is that? It's clear you have no understanding of how a true Orc solves a problem.
You don't look particularly religious. You're not a member of the Vosh Rakh, are you?\n\nStupid question, I know. If you were a member of the cult, you wouldn't tell me.
You sound almost as fine and fancy as the Elf. I like that. Maybe we can get together later and you can teach me some of those fine and fancy words.
The remains of the caravan and the surviving members of the crew are just down the road.\n\nI don't know where the marauders took the stolen cargo, but maybe someone in the crew saw where they went.
My grandfather told me ghost stories about Thukhozod when I was just a pup—stories that his grandfather told him. Way I hear it, this Gorlar the Dark's even worse. Be careful out there.
Oh, thank Auri-El. I had hoped that Guruzug would seek you out again. I hope you're ready for another trip to Coldperch Cavern.
Oh thank the Three! As you may have surmised, my experiment still needs … minor adjustments. Another batch of readings from Zthenganaz should be just the trick.
You did good work in there. Now make another smart decision and sell that amulet to Meram.
Glad to see you back—and with only a few bite marks, too. I'll admit it, I'm impressed.\n\nAny luck in the Kennel?
Thank Malacath, you have returned! I knew you would be able to escape <<1>>'s lair.\n\nHave you done what you promised?
I wonder how the Winterborn knew we were coming? It was like they were waiting for us when we came through the Merchant's Gate.
It's a good day, friend! I've got gold in my pocket and a full mug in my hand!\n\nSo, what can I do for you?

What's this about? If you aren't here to use the baths, it must be about my tonics.\n\nWell, I can assure you. My tonics are guaranteed to cure whatever ails you. It just takes time … and … and multiple applications!
You're back. From the smell, I'd say you were successful. Am I right?
I assume you've found my missing pages?\n\nHand them over and I'll see what I can do with them.

You need not speak … I feel a great cleansing has occurred. The wild is free of corruption, for a time.\n\nActually, it might just be me. I had some really good bread and that always makes me sleepy. Were you successful?
The winds sigh in relief. I trust that you bring good news?
Hmm? Oh, it is you. You have been gone a long time. It has been a long time hasn't it? Sorry. Birkhu has been, you know … occupied.\n\nWere you successful? Is Nyzchaleft destroyed?
I've seen a few bedraggled travelers stagger into the city. Muddy and bruised, but no worse for the wear. I suppose I have you to thank for that?

Thank you again for saving the temple priests. I don't even want to imagine how things might have turned out without your intervention.\n\nI look forward to talking to you again under better circumstances.
Sorry for shouting at you. It must be this city. Makes me want to walk fast and speak loudly.\n\nOh, you must remember me! The caravan? The Winterborn ambush? Thanks again for helping us with that.
It's wonderful to see you again, my friend, but I really wish the king would find someone else to serve as a messenger.\n\nI have so many other talents that could greatly benefit Orsinium.
The Morkul clan is a loyal friend to the Fighters Guild. You'll fit right in, I'm sure.\n\nJust mind your tongue around the forge-wife—she's got Mauloch's own temper.

We have to rendezvous with the rest of our clan, those who escaped the attack on the stronghold. Then we'll send out messengers and shine torches in every dark corner until we have the answers you seek.\n\nMay Malacath guide our blades!
We do good work here … great work! But we're idiot children compared to our ancestors. Morkuldin once produced weapons fit for gods, but now we settle for kings.\n\nAh, well. I should get back to it.

I've got good news, disappointing news, and downright awful news.\n\nThe good, Bazrag's instructions were easy to follow. The disappointing, I have no idea how to find the entrance and there's no way to get inside without being attacked once we do.
All right. We can do this. We just sneak in, find out what we need to know, and get out.\n\nI mean, it's just a meeting. We have these amulets. We'll be fine. Right?

I was hoping you'd come by. I made sure to wear my favorite fragrance so that the innkeeper's daughter would notice me.\n\nShe's a feisty one! She should come and soak with me sometime. Do her a world of good, it would.
We'll continue this discussion in the dining hall below. I can't wait to hear what proof you have to substantiate these wild claims.
Pull up a seat by the hearth, friend. I could use the company.
Did you hear? There's some kind of trouble at Fharun Stronghold.

What in Trinimac's name is going on? Why did Kurog send soldiers after me?\n\nThey acted like I'd done something horrible. I didn't want to show it, but I was frightened for my life! I'm just glad you arrived when you did.
This was just an adventure until now.\n\nWe were strong, fearless. But to lose one of our own … I don't know if I can handle this.
Have you seen any good game animals around? I haven't had any luck all day.
Just as the grand city nears completion, the king has died. If I wasn't so busy, I'd be weeping in the street right now.
Hail the king! He's just what this city and the Orc people need. It's time for Trinimac to reign again!
Kurog and his love for Trinimac is what's hurting this whole region.
Be on your guard. Kurog's soldiers are everywhere.
I love books! I wonder if they have any copies of Investigator Vale in here?\n\nAnyway, I'll look around over here.
I just came for the celebratory feast.\n\nI'll say this for Kurog, his hearth-wife knows how to roast a tasty mammoth!

I came to listen to Kurog, just like you asked. Don't blame me if I fall asleep, though.\n\nStill, it's nice to see how Orsinium has come along. The stone from our quarry truly makes this a remarkable city!
I'm all out of patience for Kurog and his political games. How much longer does he plan to keep us here?\n\nI have a clan to run, you know.
I'll listen to what Kurog has to say.\n\nUnlike some of my fellow clan chiefs, I'm willing to find wisdom in even the most unexpected places.
What are you doing? Taking in the sights while everything crumbles around us?\n\nYou need to get to the temple and you need to get there now!
My husband, the king. I'm not sure how I feel about that.\n\nI suppose I'll have to get used to it. It's not like he can refuse the throne now that he's accepted it. At least, I don't think he can.
Werewolves, harpies—what's next? Probably an enraged pack of lamias with banekin riding atop their backs!\n\nYou know, that actually might be fun. I'll send word to you when they finally get here.

If this is what it means to be a hero, I'm pretty sure I'm done with that dream.\n\nI've had enough of death, of seeing my friends get hurt. Kurog. He's going to pay for this. I swear on my mother's bow, he's going to pay.
So we're taking Torug's Armlet back to Orsinium? Good. Do you need someone to deliver it? I mean, I'd be happy to take it. It'll be tough with my ankle and all, but I'll take the risk.
So Torug's Armlet's headed to Orsinium, huh? Doesn't matter. I don't care if there's nothing up there but a kick in the tusks. I'm going to reach the top of this hill. Count on it!

Dwemer constructs can be surprisingly affectionate. For mindless machines, that is.\n\nWe're helping to put the finishing touches on the city. The king will probably make me a duke or something after he sees how hard these little fellows work!
I'd thought Morkul would want nothing to do with the Mages Guild. I admit, their skill with enchanting surprised me.\n\nBest to keep an open mind.
I guess you took the long way.
Artorius challenged the Brotherhood and paid the ultimate price. Let his death serve as a lesson to any who would oppose us.
Decided to take me up on that offer of a drink? Good! I don't mind drinking alone, but I could use the company.\n\nBesides, Howler just gets mean when he's had a few mugs of ale.
This message is to <<1>>. It's about an arrest order. <<2>>'s arrest order.\n\nShe isn't working with the Iron Wheel, she's their next target!
Your foul words have consequences, heretic. The Grand Chanter has ordered you to appear before him.
Hah, back with treasure. Good work!

The Thieves Guild, restored to Abah's Landing? I am most grateful for your timely and unexpected assistance!\n\nYou see, my bountiful warehouse was taken from me by some conniving and nefarious individual.
Excellent work in the Iron Wheel's headquarters.\n\nDon't tell <<1>> I said that.
A most regrettable welcome, for I have such unfortunate tidings! What I soon reveal shall be quite distressing to hear—for this, I offer my gravest and most humble apology!
I escorted Anais out of the pirate lair and back to her mansion, where she's safe and sound and no doubt planning how to flay me alive at the first opportunity.

I'd prefer you deprived my shirker of his outfit, but if you're averse to saving coin, I will sell you one directly.\n\nBe warned, the disguise won't do you any good within the Iron Wheel's headquarters.
New-Sister! Welcome! Welcome! You need anything, anything at all, you come to me, yes?

I know I've given you a hard time since you joined, but I mean it when I say this. Good luck, New-blade. I wish it were me going after the Black Dragon. But if not me, I suppose that you'll do.\n\nFinish her for us … Assassin.
I only wish I was there to see Qamar's face when he opens his stash and finds it empty!
I don't think it's wise for us to be seen together, especially if you plan to rob Qamar.
Like your hands attached? Then don't touch my gold.
I'm on my break, leave me to my game.
Find your own broom. The last one I loaned out is in the belly of an assassin beetle.

I can't explain it, but I have a feeling that this is the place. Perhaps a residual effect of breathing so much of the fumes? I've only enough resin left for a few more precious seconds, so let's hope I'm right about this location.

A contract for Governor Fortunata, hmm? Don't let your guard down around her. She goes from all charm to all knives at the drop of a hat. \n\nI'll be working Anvil Castle myself for a while. Maybe I'll see you around.
<When you knock on the door, there is no response.>
I'm eager to learn what kind of position you secured for Kireth, but she should hear it from you first.
All right, I'm ready to hear the news now. What kind of job did you sign me up for? Bodyguard? Spy for the Pact? Private chef for a visiting dignitary?\n\nTell me, tell me, tell me!
If you have any other friends who need employment, I suggest they try their luck in Kvatch.
These pirates can get kind of wild when they've poured a few drinks down their gullets. That's why I love this place!

You look strong and sober. Want a job?\n\nThe Rowdy Guar skirted a hurricane off Khenarthi's Roost. Oddest thing, just came out of nowhere and we took some damage. I need someone who can hold a board and hammer a nail. Preferably at the same time.
An entire day's catch, lost to the hungry sea. So many wasted fish!\n\nJode punishes me for expecting a spoiled Dark Elf to perform the work of an honest Khajiit.
Ysmir's beard, those vile rumors will be the death of us! Don't the pirates know it takes constant attention to detail to keep a bank running smoothly?
I have to admit, I never expected to see you again. Were you able to recover our stolen ingots?
You will recover <<1>>, I'm certain.\n\nWhich is good, because I already paid for the wine we're all to drink upon your successful return!
No Iron Wheel patrols near the docks. The coast is quite literally clear.
I know that look. That's your "tell <<1>> to do something" look. Why do none of you believe I'm retired?\n\nI could say it slowly. "Ree. Tired." Did it stick this time?
Think I'll stay here for a bit. Don't want to decorate the guildmaster's boots.
We should make haste.
There you are! You heard about the wedding?\n\nThis is our chance to repay <<1>> for selling out the Thieves Guild.
Oh. Hello. <<1>> sent word I should expect you.
I heard <<1>>'s plan. It's terrible, of course.\n\nBut we'll get to ruin a wedding.
Something about that soldier ….\n\nNo matter. You should hurry.
You certainly don't belong. Who are you, and why are you here?
We should head to Abah's Landing. The least we can give you is answers.
You mentioned <<1>> had an offer for the Thieves Guild?
Ra'ham! Bisi'ja hala va—! Oh. I am sorry. Adara'hai thought you were someone else. You have caught us at a … delicate time. Forgive me.
Thank you for the invitation. The wedding was exceptional, if you put aside <<1>>'s capture by the Iron Wheel.
Have you decided who to bring to the wedding?
<<1>> is gone. Just … gone.
Foolishness, from the start. So stubborn. If she'd listened, she wouldn't be in this mess.
I informed the others about the wedding. We shouldn't blame ourselves for what happened.\n\n<<1>> told us to leave. We all understand that.

Everybody wants to be one of the Shark's Teeth, eh? All right. Take this paint and a map of the grotto. Just place our sigil at the spots shown on the map to mark our territory. Simple, right?\n\nJust don't tusk it up. Or else.
Ah, my unlikely savior returns! <<1>> sent word of your stylistic needs.
My, my. You don't exactly clean up, but you look absolutely roguish.\n\nI'll need my own outfit for the wedding—something with a covered face.
What's wrong with me? I'm a High Elf. I'm not supposed to cry.
Fashionably late is good. But normal late is very, very bad. We should get moving.
I've never been to a wedding this extravagant. I wonder what they'll have inside. Dancers, musicians, jugglers?
When they invite you in, the rich and powerful thrust food in your hands. They like to prove how much they have, and how better it is than yours.\n\nAnd yes, I'm hungry.
We're wasting time. Let's go inside before anyone realizes how little we belong.
Look at you! Such impeccable fashion belongs on the other side of this gate.\n\nThough I am a fool to request it, might I have your invitation?
You'll find my notes in the strongbox. Go on, then. Let me finish my drink in peace.
I do hope <<1>> knows what she's doing.
I've had enough of the Iron Wheel. Let's do our best to avoid them.
<<1>> is doing her part. We must still do ours.\n\nCome, let's go to the wedding.
What does <<1>> think she's doing? We should have cut our losses as soon as we realized <<2>> was <<3>>.
You are a friend to Saroldo's daughter? This must be much for her to take in. Please, ask what you will.
Are you lost? Wedding's in the other direction.
We need more time. There must be another way out of this room. <<1>> always loved his secrets.

Oh, here's a tip. Don't let my boss push you around. Shalug likes to think of herself as the biggest, baddest, brashest thug in Abah's Landing, but she'll respect you more if you don't put up with any of her gruff.
You will talk to Bakhum? Oh, praise Alkosh! This one carries a heavy burden!
My father died protecting her from the Iron Wheel, and she tried to steal my inheritance? I feel seasick.

Oh, walker … Bakhum did not expect this. This is no simple sickness—it's the work of dro-m'Athra. You must go! This one can hear Lorkhaj's song already. Can you hear it? The tapping?\n\nThis one is sorry for bringing you here. Flee while you can!
Excuse me, I only speak to people with a sense of culture.
Thank you for swaying <<1>>'s heart. I will earn her forgiveness. This, I swear to you.
If you don't leave, I shall have my servant escort you out.
Get me that bottle and I'll tell you whatever you'd care to know about <<1>>.
If I may, there is an alternate path inside the tomb. It is likely full of traps, guardians, and prodigious quantities of dust.\n\nA small price to avoid the Iron Wheel.
Spare coins for an Alliance War veteran?
Where's <<1>>?
There is nowhere to go. Surrender peacefully and I will have <<1>> treat you with mercy.\n\nOr not. I have a wedding to attend.
Empty. All that for nothing.\n\nNo, that's wrong. There might be a trail that leads us to the dowry. We just need to look around.
I know how <<1>> survived Malooc's Path.
I told the guild about <<1>> betraying us. <<2>> took it in stride, <<3>> gave me a hug, and <<4>> walked off without a word.\n\nAll in all, better than expected.

You proved your strength of will in Longhaven, and you proved it here in Hrota Cave. You have the determination of a true hunter.\n\nWe may not have saved the vampire's victims, but at least we spared them from eternal torment.

This one hoped you would say that. We made a most-excellent team in the past.\n\nRaz suggests we split up to cover more ground. Locate the Captain and the items. And if you find her before I do, please give her my regards—right in the heart, yes?
<<1>> has information you'll want to hear. I sent him to <<c:2>>'s library.
You must help me! I told this hateful cat everything I know! I was just following orders! You don't say no to a woman like Captain Apinia.

This is a singular honor, friend. Only the most notable adventurers received this invitation. Read it and follow its directions.\n\nMay your audience with King Kurog prove profitable to both you and Orsinium.

This is Anais's room. You'll find the amulet made from my scale in there.\n\nStrange, there's also a young Argonian in there. He claims that he's a friend of Anais, but he's doing the work of a servant. He didn't raise an alarm, though, so that's good.
You're right on time. What did our esteemed guildmaster tell you?
Well? Did <<1>> survive the storm?
<<1>> said I should wait for you when I was finished.\n\nWell … I'm finished.
So, you got <<1>> to spill a secret. At best, a minor accomplishment.\n\nHe didn't send you to that powdered hornbill, did he? "Buy a special uniform to fit in?"
My only ambition is to keep my wife happy. I will not leave this place. Not until the day I die.
Had a feeling you'd stop by. Did you know <<1>> was looking for you? "Something urgent," he said.

Hear there's pockets ripe for the picking in Orsinium. Bit of a frontier, yeah? But which bounty hunter will chase you into the cold?\n\nOrcs, maybe. Nords as well. It's … it's a bad idea, come to think of it.
The amulet fairly hums with spiritual energy! Now, return to the tomb and use it to recharge the great seal!

My uncle went to town, but he should be back shortly if you need something. I'm still learning the business and I'm not allowed to do anything.\n\nMy uncle says I don't have a head for numbers. I say as long as my head looks pretty, what else matters?
Is this what happiness feels like? Yes, I suppose it is.
This one never dared hope … but our love is still strong and pure.
I'm not used to being ordered about by a clandestine organization, so let's get this over with. I'd prefer to conclude our business and forget all about that dreadful ritual I had to perform.

Always a pleasure watching you work, hero. You never notice, but I come around to check on you from time to time. What can I say? You intrigue me.\n\nAnd one of these nights, I'll sneak into your room, and—oh, purely for a social visit, I assure you!
Walks-Softly says I can be whatever I want to be, but all I want to do is go home.

I can't … I can't go back in there. I don't care about the reward or the city. I just can't go back in there!\n\nI saw those horrors and it's even worse than the priest said! Hew's Bane is doomed! Doomed!
Don't recall seeing you before. So many new people coming through. Makes my head spin!
There must be a way across.\n\nI wonder if I can climb the walls? I'd need to find grips on the cliff, there ….
You've been busy. Did you realize you've provided the Thieves Guild with a lucrative opportunity?\n\nProbably not. It's all right, I won't even imply you're thick. That's how lucrative.
Of all the times to take my advice, she decides to do so now.
She just stepped out into nothing. As though she knew it would hold her.\n\nMaybe she did. That's confidence I wish I had.

Good, you're here. I want to learn whether <<1>>'s dowry was truly stolen from her family tomb. If it was, we find out who did … and if it wasn't, we complete the heist that <<2>> began.\n\nWhat's she going to do, send a second Iron Wheel?
Got your latest cut of the profits right here, boss.
What? I must have something in my eye. Mold spore or something. It's this damn cistern! Who lives in a cistern? I can't wait to get back to my garden.
Tears of happiness flow freely and make my fur all frizzy! I have so much to tell my dear, sweet Tashmin!
This one is as nervous as a newborn kitten!
You actually came back. Does that mean you did that favor I asked about?

Soon we should teach you to spot a tail, and shake one. It is not Khajiit dancing I am referring to, though I am told I am great partner.\n\nYou will need to be quite aware of your surroundings on a heist. There is often little room for error.

I'll escort Anais out of here and back to her mansion. She'll be home in time for the evening meal. I just hope that my compassion teaches her to reexamine her life and her business.\n\nI'll see you back at the Thieves Den.

Even though you talked Walks-Softly into letting me go, don't think that absolves you of your guilt in this matter. I was kidnapped! By pirates!\n\nYou and that lizard are going to pay for this insult. Oh yes, you're both going to pay!
What sights one sees if one simply opens his eyes and looks around.\n\nPull up a chair and let us while away the time with a strong and tasty beverage.
Oh, I do so hate waiting … and yet I love it. The anticipation is half the delight!

My client lost a shipment of personal goods when his courier was attacked near the swamps. Nothing he couldn't afford to lose, mind, but he's a bit broken up about his late wife's necklace. See what you can do for him, will you?
Assassin! I hoped I might run into you here.
This one thinks she could use a drink of water ….
At least the Grand Sermonizer won't be spreading any more lies about the Brotherhood.
The Black Dragon's chambers are close. Come. Let me open the door for you.
Even far from the sands of Alik'r, I always find comfort in a place of worship.
Your interest in this young Nord woman has certainly piqued my curiosity. Tell me who she is and I'll tell you what I saw.
The fires to the Divines are so pretty! I wonder how they keep them burning all the time? And where do they get all that fuel? So many questions! I guess that's what religion is all about.

The peace and solitude here is conducive to writing. My memoirs are coming along amazingly well. I have led an interesting life, after all.\n\nOne day I'll publish them. Then you can buy a copy and read them for yourself.
We'll meet you back at the Sanctuary. But Hilde and I need to have a very long talk first.
Looks like you found your friend. And all her limbs are still attached. Are you ready to return to Anvil now?
It means a lot that you still want me to be a part of the family. I won't let you or Kor down again.\n\nJust make sure Chanter Nemus pays for what he tried to do to me.
I don't know why we're here, but I don't think I've ever seen <<1>> this … concentrated.
<<1>> wants to speak with you.
Have you heard <<1>>'s plan to kill off her own Thieves Guild?\n\nGo on, ask her. I'll wait.
Greetings, friend. Do you mean to enter the ruins? I should warn you, you will be wading into a river of blood. I am here to go on a bold and ferocious rampage.

If I had known I'd have to do manual labor, I never would have joined the Brotherhood! But I found a way into the Cathedral that isn't locked up tight. It just took some digging.\n\nNo, really. Some actual digging.
You have returned. Arkay guided you well. What news have you of Exulus?
The Thieves Guild is getting back on its feet, but we need to remind people we're still active.\n\nNormally, the Job Board in <<c:1>> has work listed. I have one for you now, though.
What? Oh! You're not dead! I mean, that's good, but you completed the job, right?
You've returned! Were you successful? Can we return to the dig site and continue our work?

That's all, assassin. We've met, you've heard what I want you to do, and I've paid my gold. Next time I see you, I expect to hear that Commander Scipio is dead.\n\nAnd that Count Carolus was frightened so badly that he soiled his pantaloons.

I arrive in response to the Black Sacrament and look who I find.\n\nAn interesting turn of events, don't you agree? One contract comes into conflict with another and you're caught in the middle. That makes you the ideal candidate to sort things out.

Poison. If you ask me, that's a fitting end for the Pirate Queen of Anvil.\n\nAdd it to a decanter of her favorite wine and then visit the Governor in her chambers. Tell her that you completed her contract and she's sure to share a drink with you.
Feel free to prove me wrong out there. Honestly, I think our best gladiators are getting bored.
We must not linger, friend. We have elders to save and great peril to face.

You joined the Thieves Guild? You'd best take interest in thieving. There's a Tip Board in <<c:1>>—lists all the little jobs we need done.\n\nI have one for you now, if you aren't off to somewhere more important.
I was just thinking about you. Where we'd be if you hadn't taken that job from Quen.\n\nI hope you realize how important you are to the guild. Even Velsa, but she'd never admit it.
With the dowry returned, the Iron Wheel should soon leave Hew's Bane.\n\nDo you suppose they'll be off to threaten all the thieves in Taneth?
<<1>> back, the Iron Wheel returning to Taneth, and now I'm part of the Thieves Council.\n\nAnd they said I'd never make anything of myself if I left the academy.
Maybe I'll set up a little shop down here. Just in case I get bored back in my garden.\n\nBut I'm still retired—understand?
I knew the Thieves Guild would be triumphant! I just kept my opinion to myself until it seemed safe and prudent to share it.

Oh, you just missed it! My rendition of "Rememberings" from the Dark Elf musical "Guars" brought the house down! It's a sad, touching number with a few light moments, but I've never seen a crowd laugh so hard. I guess I really nailed the high notes.

Have I mentioned how much I appreciate what you did for us? Working on the forge has really been quite relaxing!\n\nIt all starts with a proper cleaning of the bellows. How all those rats got in there, I can't imagine, but they were baked to a crisp!
Coin? Spare a coin?\n\nAnything … just one coin ….
It's so good to see Zeira again.
Again, you have my thanks. Hopefully we will meet again—preferably in a dark and terrifying cave. Full of scary fish. I am much better at fighting fish. Trust me.
I find that a visit to these graves is almost as uplifting as a stroll through the Cathedral.
I said move along! The castle's closed. If I have to tell you again, I'll have you sent to the arena to have some respect beaten into you.
First you show up, then another one? Maybe the Brotherhood heard my prayers after all.

Word of advice. Urges aside, the Dark Brotherhood prefers to keep a low profile. Just remember—kill an innocent, get noticed.\n\nMy sources say that recruiting is happening here in Anvil. I'll be at the docks if you want to talk some more.
Tell me, Assassin, what did you see?

I'm glad Artorius is dead. Does that make me a bad person?\n\nHe took Mirabelle and Cimbar and the others away from us. Ultimately, their deaths are on his head. I'm glad I was there to see you finish him off, Silencer.
The faster you collect the ingredients I need, the sooner you'll get to taste my delicious Jubilee Cake. Don't worry, I'll still be here when you get back.
You're working today? Better free up more gold before you get back.
Have you come seeking membership in the Guild?
Hello! Are you here on business for the Guild?
I suppose it's going to be a lot quieter around here now, Silencer.

Fortunata, the Black Dragon, Artorius … that's an impressive set of kills you've collected, Silencer.\n\nRemember, there will always be a place for you in our Sanctuary. I just wish Green-Venom-Tongue and the others were here to celebrate with us.

I do not often express gratitude, but you have earned the words. I did not trust you when you first arrived. Honestly, I expected I would need to kill you before long. Instead, I embrace you as Brother.

You look rather well … equipped. Your weapons, of course. Don't want to get booted from an establishment for using the wrong words again.\n\nAre you here about my notice? If that's the case, you're the first suitable candidate to approach me.

I love wandering the merchant stalls. Examining all the goods that we helped bring to the Gold Coast.\n\nI get a certain amount of pleasure from experiencing the result of all my paperwork and negotiations.
Not you, too? Can't you people just leave me alone?\n\nI come out here to think and all I get is suspicious glances and unfounded accusations.
I hope you find your friend. If she happens by, I'll let her know you were looking for her.
Perhaps I didn't make myself clear when we last spoke. I would like you to leave. Look for your brown-haired woman elsewhere.
Not to be rude, but I have so much to do. Perhaps we could talk later.
The trick's on you, Sweetroll Killer! The commander is going to beat you silly!\n\nWait. Why isn't Raz drawing his weapon? I don't understand.
Raz can't wait to show you his secret headquarters. Meet us in the room above the enchanter's shop when you're ready and we'll figure out how to squash this Sweetroll Killer.

Raz told me how you helped him in the past.\n\nSorry I ran off earlier. I'm new to this Queen's Eyes stuff. You kind of surprised me when you started mentioning the threatening sweetrolls. I thought I had somehow blown my cover.

Raz knew you would find us! It's not much, but it's private.\n\nThe enchanter is an old friend. I helped her out once when an enchantment went bad. Made most of Raz's fur fall out. Very embarrassing. Still, now we get this comfy meeting place.
It was right in front of Raz's nose the entire time!\n\nStill, all this thinking makes Raz's head hurt.

Patience. Your Speaker explained a great deal to me about what is expected in this course of events. When the time is right, I will share what I know. In the meantime, stop haunting my foyer like some hungry midnight wraith.
If Raz knew Naryu was here, he would have brought flowers. Or wine. This one heard she likes a good bottle of wine. Or maybe a new dagger?\n\nTell the truth. Raz's fur is sleek and shiny, yes?

If you and your Brotherhood comrades sent me that sweetroll, I'm truly disappointed. I thought you'd realize by now that I don't take kindly to threats.\n\nBesides, it's hard enough to look good in tight leather without being tempted by tasty pastries.

Good. We're all here. Now the real fun can start.\n\nRaz and I have been discussing our options. At least when I can get him to take his eyes off the mermaid. I'm eager to see who the murderer really is. Mostly so I can kill him.

Mermaids … but now to business, yes?\n\nRaz thinks we should gather the killer's targets. Put them all in one location and set a trap. See if the Beautiful Darkness over there agrees or if she has a better idea.

I'm still alive, so that's good, right? I suppose the Commander was correct in his decision not to let me have a weapon. I have had a few bad experiences with sharp objects in the past.\n\nBut shouldn't you talk to the others? We need a plan, don't we?

Damn the Sweetroll Killer! We were able to save all of the targets we knew about—all except for the gardener, Louna. She's disappeared without a trace.\n\nI'm beginning to really dislike this soothsaying maniac with the pastry fetish.

Raz must happily report that we found almost all of the killer's targets. The only one still missing is the Dark Elf gardener. Perhaps this villain isn't as formidable as Raz had feared.\n\nBut you have other news for us, yes?
I thought I heard someone sneaking around the enchanter's shop, but I never saw anyone—murderer or otherwise.\n\nProbably a good thing considering Raz wouldn't give me a weapon.

Naryu is right, you know. The Fate-Bearers will come for them. All of them. It's what we do.\n\nStill, while there's even the slimmest chance that you can save these people, can you risk not taking it? Can you?

Raz understands the logic that the Dunmer proposed. But to not even try? That is not this one's way.\n\nPerhaps it is time Raz goes back to the Queen. He will let her know that the one who killed our people so many years ago is taken care of.
I know this is hard. Making life and death decisions always is.\n\nBut if we let her walk away, she'll just come back for us. And more people will die. Do you want that on your head?
Oh, hello again. It's been awhile, hasn't it? I wasn't expecting to see you here.
Raz is happy to report that the crazy Dark Elf kept her word. She provided the antidote and we saved the targeted people.\n\nRaz couldn't have done it without your help, my friend!
Well look who's here! Afraid I'd leave without giving you a goodbye kiss?

Of little use is horse and cart once we reach borders of the Marsh. From there, we ride a riverboat to sacred place.\n\nThe flow of the waterways, like swimming in my hatching pool or tracking a guar through mud. You worry not.

The Black Dragon, killed by our Assassin's hand. I knew she wouldn't be able to take you down!\n\nSad we lost another Brother, but at least that threat has been dealt with. And soon we'll visit Artorius and put an end to this whole sordid affair.
Not now, Assassin. We need to determine our best course of action to foil Artorius and the Order of the Hour.\n\nCome back later, after I've had an opportunity to meet with the Speaker.
You did it. I knew you would. The Night Mother truly favors you.\n\nI just wish the Dread Father hadn't called for Venom so soon.
Look, you wanted something to do. I gave you something, so go do it.\n\nUnless you can't handle it. You going to confirm my suspicions or prove me wrong?

What a day. I've killed a lot of people in my life, but I have the feeling that this one won't wash out easily.\n\nDo yourself a favor and look in on your friends from time to time. A lot can go wrong if you're not paying attention. Trust me.
They could have had the decency to leave us a ladder or something. Never trust a crazy spider-cultist to have your best interests in mind.
Bring what I desire to earn your brew. Harvest the strongest creature in any delve for its exquisite flavor!\n\nAlso guts. And a pumpkin. Almost as important.
The stars have accepted you. I just hope it is not too late.\n\nVolumes of prophecy have been written about the stars, but not even the oracles foresaw these events.

I didn't put any stock in the words of those Star-Gazers until I saw my first sand giant. It cut a horse in half. I haven't run so fast since I was stealing meat on the streets of Riften.\n\nNow we're all listening a bit more closely.

Many Dwarven religious texts refer to a Dwemer site called Mtharnaz. A high priest named Arnming wrote that he wished to be buried there, "among the masters of the heavenly stone."\n\nHis burial site is our best chance of finding a Skystone amulet.
I heard something happened to Hara. I'm really scared. I'm thinking about returning to Mournhold.
Talk to Sali'ma. Half of our research team drank the water before we realized what was happening.\n\nEnding whatever curse is on the water might be our only chance to save them.
Listen closely. You were right to help Titus. Had Tarish-Zi been able to gather his forces, there would have been nothing you could do to stop them.
You can find Erold in our observatory, up on the top of the hill.

I'd only finished the first trial when the betrayer struck, but it stands to reason that he's in the most secure part of the school—the cavern at the end of the final trial.\n\nYou'll need to complete the trials in order to avenge us.
Hara seems to have a great amount of faith in you, my friend. I'll make sure your name is never forgotten by history.
You enter my temple once more, Seeker. What knowledge have you brought me?

Who are you? How have you come to avenge us? You will find few allies here.\n\nAbelazar the betrayer has turned all of the Sword-Disciples into thralls. He would have turned me as well, if I had been less of a coward.
Hermaeus Mora is waiting to speak to you. Just approach his shrine and listen to what he has to say.
Forgive me. I did not know any other way to contact you without revealing myself. Even now, the Serpent's followers, the Scaled Court, are searching for me.

At this point, I'm not looking for a cure. These waters make you insane. Muttering this "Shada this" and "Shada that" nonsense. Not to mention trying to rip out your throat.\n\nDo what you have to do and just get any survivors out of there.

Please, help. I was with the research team that was sent to investigate this wing of the temple.\n\nThe others drank the water, but Nahlia and I refused to drink it. They attacked me, and then they captured Nahlia and took her deeper into the wing.
I don't know how you did it, but this water's as clear as the desert sky.\n\nI'm not going to drink any of it, mind you. But it seems safe to touch.

So many people from all over Tamriel called Elinhir home. \n\nEvery morning, the magic students gathered in the city center to practice their spells. I'd open my butcher's stall while dazzling beams of light and color cut through the morning air.
I … need to catch my breath. Good luck against Yamanu-ko ….
That core is looking less stable by the second. We must hurry!
Find Zal'ik and release me from my imprisonment in this place. Then I will share with you what I know about cleansing the water of Shada's curse.
I don't understand. What's happening? Why Hara? Why now?
Who are you? Are you in league with this Thief? I demand that you free me immediately!
You have done what the Yokudans could not. You have slain Zal'ik. You have given me my freedom.\n\nAnd yet, forgive me if I feel no joy. Zal'ik was a brave man. He only wanted to save his people.
This book could hold a cure and even more that we do not yet know.\n\nIt will be invaluable to us.
If we're going to learn what happened to the atronachs, you must rescue Kelmen Locke from the Greycloak mercenaries.
You must find and defeat the air monarch. An atronach with the power of three monarch atronachs is just too dangerous.
Hail, comrade! Quite a hike to get up here, eh? Good! Helps build endurance. You'll need it out here—trust me.

Strange. I've seen these ruins jutting from the waters before. They always seemed so … ordinary. \n\nBut now they're practically humming with energy. And I sense … what is that … my gods, yes! It's some kind of entrance.
It looks a hopeless task to me, but something makes me want to believe Hara would not have sent us here if she wasn't sure we could find whatever it is she needs us to see.

Use this time to gather your allies, sharpen your skills and hone your reflexes. \n\nWe've won a great victory, but the war has only just begun. When the time is right to go on the offensive against the Serpent, I will call for you to lead us.
The Apex Stone rests below, in the sewers of Elinhir.\n\nThe Seeker's Sight will aid you once you get inside and help you find your way.
Do not fear for us. We will not let the Serpent devour us.\n\nWe will be the crack in the armor. You will be the blade that liberates us.

Would you just look at these small alcoves. How marvelous! Hewn after the fall of the city, no doubt. Late Merethic Era, I should think. No, no. Earlier than that. I just …. \n\nYou're not following any of this, are you? Typical.
Please, wayfarer, take a moment to replenish your supplies. You'll need them in there, of that I have no doubt.
I don't like this. I don't like being out here. We're too exposed! We should head back.
This one does not like us abandoning the camp. Not safe leaving our valuables behind. Malihaz needs more eyes … or a twin brother. Something.

My brother drank some of that water. There was so much shouting! And he put his hands around my throat! If not for Malihaz, Ruptga knows what would have happened.\n\nStill, I love my brother. If you see him, please … be kind.
I trust that you've come to harass us like the others. Let me save you the effort. Until such time as we're physically removed, we will remain here to conduct our research. Now begone.
We must find the Mage's other aspects before the Serpent does.
The Lost One carries our thoughts, as we carry hers. But her mind is corrupted, and she reserves no place of affection for you in her darkened heart.\n\nShe will not hold back. Neither should you.
When we are whole, it will take all of our concentration to resist the Serpent's will.\n\nShould we fail to overcome his grip, you must strike us down. We will do our best to weaken our darker self.
Hold it! This is Covenant territory, stranger. We'll take your coin, but if you make any sudden moves we're going to have a problem—clear?
Are you really thinking of helping those crazy High Elves? Well, I guess it's your time to waste.
I'll be returning to Belkarth soon. I just need to finish a few things here first.\n\nI might even bring some of this wine back with me. Stars know we could always use more wine at the observatory.
<An old Dwarven orrery. It contains nothing of interest.>
Without Hara, I fear we will all be swallowed by the darkness. Please help her.
I just heard what happened to Hara. What could this mean? Could it be that the Scaled Court has agents even among the Star-Gazers?
Satakal's vengeance must be quick as a serpent's strike. You'll find my traitorous acolytes at Scaled Court enclaves throughout the region.
Any news about our missing guards? We're counting on you to see this through for us.
Little goat is still here? Why? Little goat has work to do! Don't come back until the task is done!
Hurry! Up the hill! He's feeding my companions to the trolls!

Thanks to the bravery of people such as you, we scholars can do our own part to make the world a better place.\n\nI need to return to Dragonstar. My companions need to know what's happening here. When you find the Scaled Court, show them no mercy.
You're going into the Valley of Scars? You're certainly braver than I am.
Good luck, and may Tall Papa bring you and our friends back safely.
I wish I was healthy enough to go with you. Just promise you'll bring my Camaarie back to me in one piece.
If you get a chance, make those Iron Orcs pay for what they did to us. A little blood for blood, know what I mean? It's only fair.
You're one of those who fought the Scaled Court? Beat back the Iron Orcs? Thanks for that, I guess.\n\nNow if you only could do something about those Dragonstar Caravan Company criminals ….
The Scaled Court seems to have lost the will to fight. I hear we have you to thank for that. \n\nAll of Dragonstar is in your debt.

The hero of Skyreach! And not a moment too soon. I was this close to taking a job as a carpenter, and I hate wood. It's full of splinters—and squirrels! Tree skeevers, I call them. \n\nSorry, I'm rambling. But at least the mine is back in business.
Now that all that business with the wild serpent is over, maybe we can get back to the real issue at hand. This town is woefully lacking a proper brewer.
Skeetees has decided to linger awhile longer. Especially now that the Scaled Court menace no longer looms like a wamasu over a nest of durzog cubs.
The Iron Orcs won't bother us again. The Dragonstar Caravan Company will make certain of that!
Hey, I know you! Wanna hear my joke again? Guaranteed to be as funny as the last time you heard it or the next one's free!
Let's not start something we'll both regret. I could use some help and you're going to want to hear what I have to say.
I'll stay here and make sure the spawning pools can be used again. Until the Serpent's plans have been thwarted, I'm sure our paths will cross again.
Can't believe we've got to reinforce the walls. Again. By Mauloch's mighty molars, I hate those Iron Orc bastards.

Stendarr protect you, friend. If Virmaril is the source of this darkness, then the danger is greater than I expected.\n\nI will seek another way inside. A way that avoids that terrible, insistent voice.
I can't join you for this. One of us needs to return to Belkarth and prepare the city's defenses.\n\nYou and the Thief … avenge Kelmen and stop this mad viper. For all our sakes.
Use the portal and return to the Observatory. I will meet you there.

I knew I could count on you! The smaller creatures should pose little threat, but be warned. One of the fell beasts is of immense size. It slaughtered half of my former companions before I escaped!\n\nI'll follow you inside after you clear the way.
The great warrior, Titus, seeks your counsel.
Perhaps the time has come to find one last battle to fight. I'd rather face a warrior's death while I still have some sense of who I am.

The darkness that shrouds Titus's mind blocks my connection to him. But since you touched my Apex Stone, I can still communicate with you.\n\nYou consider Titus to be a friend. Are you ready to help him?
You must … you must move quickly. Na-Kesh is mad. She will drown my fellow root-keepers in her amber brew. Please … hurry!
A hireling! Can you believe it?\n\nNot much of a title, I know, but I've spent a lifetime earning it.
Well? Pick it up! Did you expect me to magically waft it over to you?
Outlander! Archcanon Tarvus sent me to find you.
I'm certain my patron looks forward to meeting you. She has great plans for the Scaled Court.
For all his blather, I never caught the name of the indecent Imperial.\n\nIf he was Argonian, I'd call him "Rants-Without-Pants." Ha!

I couldn't have done much better myself, hero. Good work down there! There's one more thing to do, if you're up to it.\n\nTime is short, but I have something to tell you. You've earned that much at least.

The New Life Festival was once a celebration of Magnus, the sun god. I have a book—you're welcome to read about the history, if you care to.\n\nBut I'd rather tell you about the celebrations. Very few involve a chance of paper cuts!
Please, dryskin, do what Naryu asks. She's our best hope for getting out of this terrible place.

Ah, I see you have been tramping through the mud. Feel free to stamp your feet. Despite my best efforts, I have come very close to completing a task.\n\nIn truth, I enjoy sweeping the dock. Counting the ripples in the water … it feels like home.
There is no record of your arrival. You're a blank slate. Let Vvardenfell be the place where you write a new story. Just write it far from Sedya Neen.\n\nGood luck, outlander.
If you find <<1>>, please tell him … tell him I didn't flee, that I sought aid.\n\nPlease tell him.
Please, hurry to Belkarth. Hara needs your help.
Ah! I'm glad to see you made it back in one piece. So, what have you learned? Anything?
You know where to go and what to do. Look for the dolmens—the Worm Cult often congregates nearby.

You know what true boredom is? Spending endless hours looking at the exact same spot! I'd give my left foot to be able to turn my head!\n\nDid you find her? Did you find the evil witch who cast this damn spell on me?
Rajhin would applaud your swiftness! Though, he might instead pick the pocket of one distracted by your prowess.\n\nTruly, the best thieves come and go with the wind.
All you have to do is get my mother to sign Tirwin's servitude obligation over to you! Then we can declare her freedom and our love! \n\nShe and I … not—you know.
You have my price. Tirwin isn't going anywhere without it.
My hapless protector aside, were you able to find the Goblins? Did you recover my pack and the sword?
You decided not to help me, didn't you? I knew I shouldn't have gotten my hopes up.
Now, all that's left to do is wait ….
When I call out the warlord's approach, light the signal fires. Move as fast as Zoreh—faster than the desert wind.
Those walking the War Orphan's Sojourn have you to thank for clearing their path.
Thank the Three, you've returned! Lord Vivec can't hang on much longer. Please, you have to help him!
I smell fish. Have you brought fish?

I know what you're thinking. I'm not exactly pleased either, but Mistress Dratha insisted this was the only way. \n\nI'm sorry if you feel I wasn't honest with you, but either way, I owe you my thanks once again.
Don't just sit there, stuff yourself with food and drink!
There you are. I heard about Mabkir. Damn shame.\n\nWhere's Khartag? Dragging arse, as usual?
Ralasa adores cakes. I doubt you'll have any trouble delivering them, but keep your guard up.

There you are! I gave Mistress Dratha some chokeweed bitters to slow the effect of the spores, but this is like binding a troll's hands with fishing twine.\n\nDid you bring the toxin sample I asked for? I can't brew an antidote without it.
We escaped, but not without loss.\n\nThis place … it does nothing but break things. It nearly broke me.

There you are. Sorry to check up on you. I knew you had the situation well in hand, but Ninave practically kicked me out. Said not to come back without Seythen. I'm glad I won't be going back empty-handed.
Did I hear you correctly? Are you going to find my boy? Oh, Three bless you! Bring him back safe, please!
Someone without wings and razor-sharp teeth! There's a sight for sore eyes.
My mentor used her wealth to better others, not herself. Having inherited her manor, I now do the same.
Let me guess, Menaldinion was an insufferable ass and refused to apologize.
Please, you've got to hurry. Torvayn was a monster. I don't want to meet whoever they send to replace him!
I'd walk softly if I were you. You're one false accusation away from joining us here.

I'm going to take a moment to make an assumption. You're somewhat versed in fighting, or at the very least defending yourself. It's your aura … and the swagger, that give it away.\n\nAre you looking for work by chance?

I do hope our friend Farwen is all right. Her religion and gods interest me greatly, though my giving nature is often beholden to so many worthy causes I am without means to support hers.\n\nPerhaps once we are paid for this mission, I will learn more.
Finally we're starting!\n\nTry not to damage my land any more than it already is.
If you plan to bring down Marshal Hlaren, you'd best get on with it. I'm feeling the urge to punch someone again.
Why are you still here? Run along. Go back to your tea peddling friend. Shoo!
I would remind you that I have a bargain to make. You can choose to accept your reward or not, it doesn't much matter to me.

Kren and I will march these crooks back to Suran. They'll stay in the prison they were kind enough to finance.\n\nIt might be a while until they get a trial, but we'll be sure to keep them comfortable. Might even give them cots to sleep on!
Do you have the Stones of Cold Fire?
What do you plan to do now that you've put an end to the big, bad marshal? I personally have quite a few fun things in mind. If you have gold to spend, that is.
I do not suffer fools or vigilantes. Begone before I find a reason to arrest you, f'lah.
Hey, who let you in here? I'm quite busy at the moment. Come back another time.
<Someone killed Constable Mirel and looted his belongings. The dagger in his chest looks to be of Khajiit design.\n\nPerhaps some of the constable's belongings remain close by.>

Greetings, my friend. You cut quite the dashing figure in my old regalia! \n\nAnother spectacular victory for the Scarlet Judge, eh? I will miss donning the cowl, but it does me good to know that my final adventure helped liberate the people of Suran.

Go on. See what mischief that creature has planned for us. Just be careful. From the cast of its shadow, I'd say it's either a rabid ogrim or maybe an ardent hagraven.\n\nI've never had much luck when it comes to hagravens ….

We really do have things well in hand, I assure you.\n\nIt's only a matter of time before my Redoran kinsmen arrive, truly. They wouldn't dare leave a renowned second-deputy prefect like me waiting for long.

You did it! My egg-hands started stumbling out of the mine a few minutes ago. They've got some bumps and scrapes and more than a few headaches, but otherwise no worse for the wear.\n\nWhat happened down there?
Ah, it's good to see you again!\n\nAvo and I are fine now, thanks to your efforts—and the efforts of the Scarlet Judge. Soon we'll be moving on, but not before we've sold our goods. Farewell!
Father and I wouldn't have our wagon, our belongings, or possibly even our lives without the help of you and the Scarlet Judge. Thank you. We'll never forget what you did for us.
You are brave to tread here. I was brave once myself. How I miss the thrill of living.
Glad to see Narsis wasn't eaten by a ghost! I wonder where he ran off to in such a hurry, though?\n\nI bet Elfbetta knows. Narsis tells her everything.

Narsis shot out of that tomb so fast! Just like that time my sister laughed so hard and mead spurted out her nose! Narsis was so excited, he went to find a mage to open a portal. Told us to meet him there.\n\nBorfree, pack up! We need to move!

Good luck in there, and mind the kwama. None of this will make a damn bit of difference if you wind up bug-food.\n\nThey're normally gentle as newborn lambs. 'Course, lambs don't have pincers the size of hedge shears. Just be careful, all right?

Consult with the Archcanon to decide our next course of action. This Ashlander thief must be dealt with before my condition dooms my people.\n\nNow leave me. If my concentration wavers, Vvardenfell is doomed.
You a talker or a gawker? Might earn a busted lip either way.

Pay no attention to this Ashlander. She's been blathering on about Lord Vivec's condition and how she can help, but I'm certain it's a trick of some sort.\n\nI was just about to have her thrown out of the city—or possibly tossed to the slaughterfish.

Another looter? You want a taste of my steel, too?\n\nNo, wait—I remember you. You borrowed one of our Blessing Stones. Well, the Archcanon returned it after Lord Vivec was finished with it, so no need to fret about that.
Finally! I thought you might have been eaten!\n\nIs it done? Did you take care of that madman, Drovos?
Tell your Armiger allies they need not chase us from these lands. Our time here is nearly finished.
<This Buoyant Armiger appears to have died defending the pilgrim laying dead nearby. Her helmet is spattered in a viscous ichor that smells of month-old fish.>
That's it then? You've dealt with whatever was attacking our pilgrims?
Be wary, traveler. Pilgrims have been attacked on these roads. Should you encounter violence, don't hesitate to call on us. We're here to protect you.
So? Will you keep this one's secret? Halinjirr would not last long in a Hlaalu prison.
You made it. Good. We have a great deal to talk about in a short period of time.
Did you need something else? A skooma baron you'd like to report, perhaps? No? Then move along.

Ah, hello again, my friend! All's well in Gnisis, yes? I heard the bustle of the town when I returned home. It would seem our work in the mine was a success! What a relief.\n\nCare to join me for—? Wait, what are you doing all the way out here?

I love seeing new faces! For a while, it was just the same old miners and the occasional traveling merchant. Thought Carellon might have to shut this place down.\n\nLook at me, talking your ears off! What can I get you?
Did you find what you were looking for in the mine?

Ah, Narsis! Always rushing here and there. Oh, how I love him!\n\nI am glad to see he did not leave you in that dusty old tomb. You wouldn't believe how many apprentices he tends to lose along the way.
Pity that old scroll didn't include some sort of map.

You've walked the streets of the Clockwork City and you stood in the presence of two Daedric Princes. But you still have work to do, assistant.\n\nTalk to Vivec. You must return his divine energy to him before he fades from existence.
See what Vivec can tell us about Barbas—while he's still able to talk.
I'll head to Gnisis just as soon as I've gathered my wits.
What if it comes back? Please, get me out of here!
Our business has concluded. The monetary reward is not all you have earned. Hlaalu will remember this. For now, however, it is best that we let things die down.

My family fought alongside the Ashlanders to bring down the great Emperor Crab here on this very soil. To think with all my studying I never knew such an important fact about my own history.\n\nBut what of the family connection to Ald'ruhn?
Tread carefully in our camp, outlander. You may walk among us as a guest, but you are not Velothi.
Another successful expedition! There were hiccups, yes. But a few bruises and one broken limb are a small price to pay for a find like this.\n\nSpeaking of our find, do you have the prism?

Oh! Lord Thanlen must have found us a bodyguard after all. You'd have to be crazy to wander around here with all the ghosts—unless you knew what you were doing.\n\nLucky for you, this case seems standard. Just some mad spirits in need of final rest.
You know, this is the first time I've enjoyed the smell of Vvardenfell air. You know it smells like? It smells like being alive.\n\nThanks for all the help down there.

You surprise me, child of Vehk. All here assembled say you are both courteous and brave—rare qualities among the "civilized" Dunmer.\n\nYou showed us respect. I will do the same by asking you directly—what really brings you to Ald'ruhn?

I sometimes forget the courage and vigor of the flesh. The years harden us—make us cold and suspicious. On behalf of my family, I beg your forgiveness.\n\nWhat brings you to our forsaken tomb? Yours is the only living heart that knows our sad tale.
