Beware this cursed place! These wilds belong to the Reachmen and minotaurs now. They're dragging anyone they find to break the red stone and work their infernal Forge.\n\nIf the hagraven, Caillaoife, finds you in her wilds they'll get you too.

I heard others found sanctuary in Falkreath. I might head there too. Wait for safer times. Anywhere far away from this cursed place … before I wind up like the others.\n\nYou've seen what I mean. The look in their eyes? Like hungry wolves.

This proves that Chodala's unfit to lead the Ashlanders. And his claim that he's the Nerevarine—preposterous!\n\nThat hasn't stopped him and his followers from causing great harm, however. Seryn went after him. Please, go help her.
Hurry, Mortal. Even now, Chodala's support for his false claim intensifies. You need to be there when he stands before the Wise Woman and reveal his divine delusions.

Friend, take up my cause. I beg you. Send word to Whiterun—to Riften—to anywhere! Falkreath Hold is falling! \n\nAn army of beastmen batters our gates … we aren't long for Sovngarde, but our kinsmen can carry Shor's vengeance in our stead.
I—I'm sure you did all you could … I just wish I'd been by his side before the end.\n\nThe Reachmen are retreating. We've broken the siege, thanks to you.
The song is calling! You hear it, don't you? I can see it behind your eyes … swimming in there. Can you see the melody? The harmony? Please, you have to see it.

I'm sorry, but I'm not going to be of much use. Even if I could hear the tones, I wouldn't know how to arrange them.\n\nYou must have heard or seen something on your trip down here, right? Clues of some kind? Just try to remember.

The Telvanni decided to honor me with membership in their great house. This tower was their idea of a gift. \n\nTheir choice of location was … portentous, let's say. For them. My own auspices are far brighter.

I will open a portal from here to allow you to exit. I'll linger here a while longer, but you needn't concern yourself with my safety.\n\nIf you ever find yourself near my tower, do stop by. You're entertaining. Capable.
I do wish I could have done a more thorough study of the resonator. What do you think they would do with such a device? Enslavement perhaps? No … not enslavement. That's too obvious.

Kwama, Breton, queen, egg-hand—all the same. All just meat. They killed her. Killed their own queen.\n\nDo you see what it does? What it's doing? Broken. All broken. Just the mine for now, but soon? Everywhere.
I have … nothing more to say … to an outlander.
It's you! Hist be praised!\n\nSavarak set those Black Snail thugs on us. A half dozen of them. I tried to …. Sorry, just let me catch my breath.
Thank the Three Vimy got me out. Those mercenaries planned to … to use me as bait for those damned Dwarven machines.\n\nBe careful in there, or you'll wind up with a shattered leg too.

My brother and I signed on with Neramo because we needed the money. We knew it would be dangerous, but nothing like this. If Vimy hadn't rescued us, we'd be dead as tailless guars.\n\nI don't know how we're going to get Daren out of here.
I erect the spine of warning, stranger. Do not seek to harm those I protect, and I will not seek to harm you.
Ugh. More visitors? I have those atronachs out there for a reason. Can't you see there's no room?\n\nOh for Vehk's sake, never mind. What do you want from us?
I've been requested to summon you to Lord Eris Releth, outsider.\n\nI understand you've been tasked with a very important job from him and he's eager to hear results.
Veya joined the Morag Tong? Has the House really caused her so much pain that she agreed to become part of a cult of assassins?
What? Who? This one is just here to haul cargo!
Do not look upon me, stranger, for I am surely cursed. Greed blinded me, and innocent lives have suffered. Yet I was spared. \n\nPerhaps this unending guilt is meant to be my punishment.
Did you find Nevena? Where—that's her diary … she's been carrying it around for weeks. Never left her side ….\n\nShe's gone, isn't she?

When you find Veya's friends, remember to keep your distance. You just want to spot the note carrier and follow him to whoever's receiving these messages. That's the key to locating Veya. \n\nIf you can't do it, don't worry. The House can handle it.
Greetings, friend. You seem troubled. Please, let me explain.
My wife decides to run out and chase some damned looters in the middle of a disaster! Who does that sort of thing? You'd think Lord Vivec's Overseer would have a clearer head!
Are you addled? I said piss off! Go smoke your skooma somewhere else.
This should be funny. Kizmar loves to watch the little Dark Elves shouting and running around.
Our business is concluded. Go back to Sadrith Mora or wherever it is you came from.

Ah, greetings. I'm sorry you had to see that. Magister Gothren's really quite charming once you get to know him.\n\nHonestly, he wouldn't have yelled if Ralasa's little snoop, Captain Giravel, hadn't interfered!
Please tell me you have good news.
I sincerely hope you haven't come to bother me with more questions.
This one is sorry, but she has work to do.

Hello, can I help you? Wait a moment—you're one of those hirelings House Redoran pays to harass us simple folk.\n\nLook, all Veya wants to do is find out what happened to her brother. Too bad the House doesn't seem to care a s'wit about any of that.
Here's a bit of free advice—if you cross Ralasa Delvi, you cross Magister Gothren. Believe me when I say you do not want to cross Magister Gothren.
Magister Gothren is a very demanding mer and I have little time to cater to inane petitions or gossip with the riff-raff. Speak your business or begone.

You have done much for me and for Vvardenfell. But as the warrior says, "Do not think the battle is over when the enemy is dead. The hearts and minds of the people must also be won."\n\nI must ask you for one more service.
I see triumph in your eyes and hear metal in your bag. Have you brought what I asked?
Were you able to recover my memories? It's important they understand.
It is good to see you. I am trying hard not to sink into despair, stuck in here with nothing to do, nothing to read.
Why was he so obsessed with that little stone? Did he tell you what he wanted it for?
So, are we in the clear?
Any luck with that blasted nix-ox?
Well, he's finally gone. Not that he was ever here to begin with.
What happened? Were you able to stop him?
Let me guess, you ran away? Honestly, I can't blame you.
There you are! I knew my master would show you mercy. \n\nDo you have something for me?
Good luck in there, bear cub. Kyne only knows what's clanking around those ruins.

I have to admit, when I saw you I thought, "What the tusk are you doing down here?"—pardon my Orcish.\n\nDid you really follow me across the continent? That shows commitment. Kind of creepy, but still, a lot of commitment.

Look. I know you're helping Councilor Eris. But if that map falls into House Redoran hands, I'll probably have to kill you.\n\nNothing personal, mind you. We're already having a bit of trouble with the house and we'd rather not make matters worse.
I agree with Ulran's assessment. It certainly sounds like someone led him into a situation guaranteed to make him fail.\n\nI can't believe he put this burden on Veya, though. What was Ulran thinking?
I informed the governor that the captives we rescued from Firemoth Island are safe and sound. Do you have anything you'd like to add?
The deputy governor's errand runner. Now what?
Do you mind? Your dirty foot coverings are contaminating my pond.
You go ahead. We don't want to set tongues to wagging by leaving the shop together.
Now, to get my lies straight. With the guards and Slavemaster Arenim slain, I'm sure I can come out ahead.
Halt, Intruder! Only those who demonstrate a keen and thorough understanding of the values of House Redoran may be granted access to this vault.
Yeah? You need something? If not, you might want to clear off. We're doing a little business here, and it ain't exactly legal.
I don't like drinking with strangers. Tusk off.
Explore the shrine, gather the relics, and return to me. I promise to reward you for your efforts.
Halt, intruder! Before entering this vault, you must demonstrate that you understand the goals and beliefs of House Indoril.
By the Three! You really shouldn't sneak up on a person like that.\n\nIf you're working with those mercenaries, I assure you—you won't take me without a fight!
Halt! Only those who understand the value and thinking of House Dres may enter this vault of knowledge.
Stop! Intimate knowledge and understanding of House Hlaalu is required to enter this vault.

What do you think of my luxurious accommodations? It's got dirt and rock, fungus and a paltry fire … all the comforts of home.\n\nAnyway, you said you had information about my brother, Ulran? What did you find out?
Was the Library of Andule in the location revealed by our model? And was it filled with ancient knowledge once thought lost?
I appreciate your aid in all this. With your help, I know we can clear Ulran's name and avenge his death.

The captain reported that he had seen you in the area. There are also multiple reports that Veya has been spotted.\n\nTell me, have you seen my daughter? I won't sleep well until she's home, safe and sound.
Well, look what the cats almost dragged in. I'm not sure what happened in the cave, but I suspect you have a lot to answer for, outlander.

If I'd realized how popular this camp was going to be with outlanders, I would have moved the tribe ages ago.\n\nYou don't appear to be one of the heretical invaders, but looks can be deceiving. What do you seek, stranger?

If you're another pilgrim looking for charity, I suggest you move along. I have neither the time to waste nor the gold to spare. I'm currently between employment and my own funds have become dangerously depleted.
I feel like such a puny snowback, hiding here in Molag Mar!\n\nBut you don't want to hear about my troubles. What can this broken Nord do for you?

Damned vampires! I'll find a way to make them pay for what they did to my brother, I swear it on the Tribunal and any Daedra willing enough to listen!\n\nWhat do you want? Can't you leave a person to her anger and her grief?
And so the outlander returns. As we discussed in the swamp, I expected you to return with Veya or present me with a time and place for us to meet.\n\nTell me, outlander, which is it to be?

The good Captain Brivan appears to be more involved in Ulran's fate than I had imagined.\n\nHe never struck me as the type to use murder and deceit to get ahead, but that's the problem with greed. It causes decent people to make stupid choices.
So you think my brother's soldiers might be able to tell us what happened the day he was exiled? I hope you can make them break their code of silence.\n\nAnd what was that you said about Brivan?
Naryu told me what you found in the Ashlander mine. I can't imagine what Veya must be going through right now, but she shouldn't be alone. That's why I came looking for you.

Oh, another doting vassal! I simply am the most adored creature in the world, aren't I? But it is my burden to bear.\n\nYou no doubt want to thank me for this wondrous celebration. Very thoughtful. Thank away.
The hour grows late, child. Dusk gives way to night. Let us conclude our business.

You stand before Jorunn, Skald-King! Do not be shaken by this one's presents. Only cowherds and concealers of fowl coops have reason to fear Jorunn's hugieness!\n\nJoin us in inebriating this momental day!
A fire rages in your heart—that much is clear. Careful that it does not consume you. Our First Ashkhan, Nalor, favors the cautious heart.

The flock returns to the shepherd. You have earned my favor, mortal, but the task is not yet finished.\n\nThese craven fools that accost my children must suffer. I trust that Rhea's visions revealed their location ….
"Those who labor long prosper. Those who hunt long starve." These are the words of our First Ashkhan, Akami.\n\nYou honor him with this gift.

The Urshilaku salute you, n'wah. Ashlander or no, you have proven to be wise and valorous.\n\nOur First Ashkhan, Lammak, herald of the Nerevarine, treasured wisdom and valor above all else. His spirit welcomes you as a friend. As do we.
A gift of blood and steel pleases us. More importantly, it pleases the spirit of our First Ashkhan, Shadar.\n\nYou have the tribe's respect. For now.
Short by more than a third. Someone is going to pay—that goes without question, but who?\n\nOh! Sorry, I'm a bit preoccupied. Did you need something?
An outlander? I can never seem to get enough of your kind here.\n\nYou're welcome in Vvardenfell, of course. Just obey the laws and refrain from causing trouble and you'll get along just fine.
I don't believe we've had the pleasure, I'd certainly remember a striking figure such as yourself.\n\nWhy don't you make yourself comfortable? The celebration's just getting started, you know?
Run away, outlander. All you'll find here is a painful death.
This one is most grateful to be free. To be trapped with Daedra is not how this one wishes to serve Azura.\n\nThank you for the rescue. Soon, we will strike back.
To be trapped forever in a realm of Oblivion would have dried my scales, hero. I extend the spine of gratitude. My mistress was wise to trust in you, though she is rarely wrong.
They're alive. That means there's still a chance to find out what happened to Ulran. Let's talk to Vatola and see what he can tell us.
I've never seen that look on Veya's face before.\n\nGet the key and let us out, please. You don't know what those crazed cultists are capable of!
I bring an urgent message from Rhea Opacarius, chief oracle of the Twilight Queen, Azura.
I've done everything the Lady of Dawn and Dusk instructed me to, but now Vivec's fate is in your hands.\n\nDo what you can, outlander, and do it quickly.
Please tell me you found Veya. I can already feel the cold steel of the executioner's blade on the back of my neck!

If you're looking for my husband, I'll tell you the same thing I told that brazen young woman. The council is meeting outside Balmora and Brivan is protecting the councilors.\n\nNow if you don't mind, I've had more than enough excitement for one day.
Leave me alone.
Have you also come to do a bit of trading? If you love gold and rumors as much as I do, you'll love this place.

I don't like the looks of this. Brivan is using Warclaws to patrol the garrison instead of Redoran soldiers. Either House forces are stretched thinner than I thought or Brivan wants to justify the use of mercenaries to the council.
Get going. We'll meet back at the safehouse in Balmora.
The deputy governor is waiting for you in the governor's office. It's been rather quiet in there.
Sorry, friend. We have nothing else to discuss. If you want this letter, you'll have to bring back that poem.

Veya died quickly. I didn't want her to suffer any more than she already had. This was for the best. If I keep telling myself that, maybe I'll eventually believe it.\n\nAnd my head's still attached to my beautiful neck, so that's something, right?

I suppose you want me to thank you, too. Whatever for? I'm just here because Naryu threatened me with unspeakable deeds. And not the good kind, mind you.\n\nGoodbye, outlander. Try not to have your name end up on one of my writs.
No end to those fetching Daedra. Cut one down, three more are summoned in its place.\n\nTraylan send you, or you just attracted to the scent of Daedra blood?
One, two, three, four …. Yup, seems like you still have all of your limbs. I guess that means you were able to do the job?
I hope you're here to report your success. Can't afford to have skooma invade Vvardenfell.
It's very important I get that research to further my studies. I hope you've come to tell me of your success.
There is no greater virtue than ambition, but I'm afraid Sun-in-Shadow's enthusiasm has rubbed a few of our number the wrong way.
As much as a good run from a Daedric ruin really gets the blood pumping, I wish we had been more successful. We lost a few of the apprentices and I never did locate any relics or treasures.
That was terrifying. I never want to see another spider again.\n\nPerhaps I'll take some dance lessons, though. Just in case.
I trust you're not here to waste my time. That would end badly … for you.
If you come to ask me if I oppose Sun-in-Shadow's rise in rank, the answer is no. Nor does Mistress Dratha.\n\nNow, if you'll excuse me, I must get back to Tel Mora.
How dreadful! Spiders are bad enough, but that melody … Daedra have no ability to follow a sheet of music!
I think it's working. One more strong assertion and that should do it!
We have nothing else to discuss. Begone.
It's about fetching time. Well?
Some of the young borders here are refugees. Some are young constables. All need my help.\n\nYou're welcome here too, if you wish. There's always room for those in need.
I don't think Master Fyr really means to end my service to him … surely he's just preoccupied.
You may take this boat to Tel Fyr. Daynea will be there assisting our master. She always was the lucky one.\n\nI must stay and wait for my audience with the priests.
You really should get back in there and deal with Vile's hound.
Galgalah took Farwen from us, but it would have been so much worse if you hadn't come along.
No one needs to know what actually happened to Galgalah. I … I have things under control.
The eyes and ears of the Warrior-Poet returns! And just in time for the gathering crowd!\n\nWere you able to locate the Archcanon's Signet?
Do not be fooled by the man outside. Galgalah is not a spirit to be taken lightly.\n\nThose he's sent to Valenvaryon are already dead, though their bodies may lie convincingly.

Well, that was certainly the oddest experience I've ever had. Not the most terrifying, of course, but certainly the oddest.\n\nIf you think this was bad, I have a word of advice. Never enter a temple of Mehrunes Dagon without a proper sacrifice.
I really have nothing further to tell you. Seek my benefactor if you wish to satisfy your curiosity.
You're saving my life here, friend! I don't dare refuse the order, but I also don't want to meet a displeased Telvanni.
Oh, you there! Have you seen my netch floating around anywhere? Her name's Rosy and I'm just worried sick about her.

What are you looking at? I'm not getting paid to look at your ugly mug.\n\nAnd watch your step. I just finished shoveling a strider dung pile the size of a nix-ox. Wouldn't want to get any on your respectable personage.
That look … you have bad news to deliver, don't you?\n\nTalk to my husband, then. I'm not ready to hear it.

Ah, it is nice to see you, my friend. I confess, I get a bit lonesome.\n\nI made arrangements for my Eoki to be in a better situation, well treated. I know he is deeply angry with me, but I have hopes of making him happy again soon.
Still interested? Or have I scared you off already?
May the stars guide you through ash and storm, or some other such nonsense.
Everything we need the land will provide. As it has always been.
Someday, you should think about traveling to Vvardenfell. A fascinating land, if I do say so myself.
This is our promised land. As it provides, so does it test our strength and our will. We must never forget the old ways, lest we grow frail. And weakness is death.
It was wise of you to seek the favor of my people. Less so, perhaps, to aid the Hleran. But I suppose we shall see what comes of that in time.\n\nIs there something I can do for you?
Why does the Hist drop so much mud in my clear waters?\n\nCareful with that one, stranger. There's something dangerous about that Naryu, but I can't wrap my tail around it.
This one made the long journey because he heard the Dark Elves no longer kept slaves. Now Kirrsi thinks that was just a lie to get me to Vvardenfell.
Clarity emerges … like sunlight breaking through the clouds ….\n\nBarbas must have replaced the Archcanon weeks ago … all to set the wheels in motion to steal my divine energy ….

It was the councilor's daughter—Veya! She barged inside like a mad woman! I heard the clash of steel, screams and shouts. It was terrifying! And then the soldiers started filling the streets!\n\nDon't go in there. It's not safe!

I'm a man of patience, but even I have limits. I haven't started my study of the Redas Ancestral Tomb and I've been here an entire week!\n\nThe only common ground I have with these miners is a tolerance for dust and darkness.
Who did I offend to get this post? I can't see the Magister, the steward gives me the barest access to her books, and I can't focus with that smell!
That new adept demanded unrestricted access to the mistress's books. Between you and me, I think he's a spy.

Holy writ states that at the battle of Heldon, fierce Pelinal's face and hair were covered in the blood of righteously slaughtered Ayleids. \n\nAnoint yourself likewise in honor of his prowess, and return to me.
Between marshals and vigilantes, how much more justice does Suran need?
How dare you walk around town like you own the place. It's our job to protect the villagers, not yours!
Marshal Hlaren seems to arrest every stranger she can find. Will you look into it?
Everyone tries to guess the identity of the Scarlet Judge. But those of us immersed in the mysteries of the Tribunal know the truth.
You're not a cultist. At least, you sure aren't dressed like one.\n\nYou're walking into a dangerous place, hero. You must be here for a reason.
Take a relaxing sea voyage, they told me. You'll love Vvardenfell, they told me. Dark Elves might seem haughty, but they're really friendly, they told me.\n\nYou know what? They all lied.
This is no way to treat a Nord! And a shield maiden, no less!\n\nWhen I get my hands on our slavers, they're going to wish they had left me to drown in the sea!
My egg-sister told me that discount voyage was too good to be true. But did I listen? No. I wanted to see the land of the Dark Elves.\n\nDense as a log, as my egg-brother used to say ….
You will free us, yes? No, that's not part of Naryu's plan. Not yet, anyway?

These Ashlanders and their wild superstition! They speak of spirits who take the bodies of mortals as their own, using them as puppets. Half-truths and exaggerated nonsense to scare off fools.\n\nDo I look like a fool to you? That was rhetorical.
You must pardon me a moment. I require focus while I commune with the Old Gods. They will show me the Jahida of this place and guide my placement of their protective wards.

You're a godsend. Brought down the wrath of Shor on these crows picking his bones.\n\nYou'll find no warriors here, but if the Reachmen are so eager to have their hearts cut out, we're happy to oblige them!
Damn you, Gascone. Damn you for making us do this ….
There's no one more deserving of the title Thane. You won't be soon forgotten.
You're madder than a cave bear in heat for doing this alone, but I won't stop you. Just watch your back, eh?
You're back! Good.\n\nOur magus erected a powerful ward on the door and … wait. I know that expression. You bring grim tidings, don't you? Adeber is dead.

Be careful with that notebook, friend. Wouldn't want your shadow to get all murdery too.\n\nPersonally, I'm done with Daedric artifacts. It's back to Valenwood for Wenridil. Going to find a nice, cozy root to hide in until this all blows over.
I am sorry I doubted you. I am … often frightened by the unknown. And what I said was true, right? Shadows are killing my friends?
Lead on, my friend. I only hope that my egg-brother has not done something rash.

I meant what I said before. Be cautious around Divayth Fyr.\n\nAs a student of the Old Ways, I certainly respect Fyr's dedication to learning. The breadth of his knowledge is as vast as the oceans. But knowledge without prudence breeds catastrophe.
Terari said you had gone to retrieve a black soul gem for my procedure. Take it to her if you have it. I don't want to linger another moment in this failing body.
Pull the switch when you're ready to initiate the transfer. Just be prepared in the all-too-likely event Sovor loses control.
Hist be praised—you've returned. Do you have my animo core?
Hey there! <<1>>'s looking for someone to do some mining. You look tough—you should talk to him.
I don't know if you noticed, but Slag Town could use a lot of help. If you've got a minute, you should talk to <<1>>. He'll have a task for you. Guarantee it.
Have you talked to <<1>>? Always got plenty of work here in Slag Town.
Have you spoken with <<1>>? I asked him to find someone to help with a job. I dare say you're a perfect candidate. You should talk to him.
Hey there. I told <<1>> about a job you might be interested in. Track him down and he'll give you the details.

It happened again! This time an initiate entered the portal and failed to return. To make matters more dire, he forgot to take his perception tabulator with him. I'm afraid we're going to get nothing useful from this excursion.
Away you filthy crows! Shoo, shoo!
You have my word ….
Unless you have the contract I requested, we have nothing more to discuss.
Gascone managed to skirt the edge of my wrath for centuries. I'm anxious to close the vault on this. Permanently.\n\nI assume your sponsor, Provost Varuni, has a less logical resolution in mind.
Greetings, my friend. I come bearing news. I've learned more about the unknown enemy we faced on the isle of Dranil Kir.
Honor to you and your house, sera. My lord, Divayth Fyr, would speak with you at once.
We're doing the right thing? A life given willingly for the greater good … it's the logical solution, isn't it?
This is Lector Naril, talking to you through this speaking tube.\n\nI assume that you and Sherizar have been exploring the Wellspring. We've built something impressive here, don't you think?

Ah. You smell that? Me neither. That's why we have Snuffler! Best tracking hound you'll ever meet.\n\nI think he likes you! See how his pincers are twitching like that? They only do that when he's happy … or preparing to kill something.

Idrono will be grateful for the fungi samples, even if he seems agitated. He gets that way during the harvest.\n\nMake sure to bring him safe ones, though. My notes can help you identify the various types we grow.

A new apprentice? How curious. And are those samples of Chirrhari's mushrooms? Excellent! I've been anxious to taste the new harvest.\n\nHmm. Texture similar to guar hide. Flavor equivalent to wet moss. Not what I hoped for.
Interruptions are counterproductive. The Seventh Law of Gears teaches us that.\n\nWell, since you've already distracted me, you might as well tell me what you want.
Don't let the shadows distract you. Complete your investigation and leave this place before you become a permanent resident of this field.
The shadow array gives Night Sister Kamira power and dominion over this realm. Destroy it and everyone they lured into this place will be freed.
I sometimes wonder why Sotha Sil lets these ridiculous people live here. Perhaps it's just another experiment. I suppose it doesn't really matter. No one will deny me entry. Not even Proctor Luciana.
Night Mistress … I am coming.
You need something else? I'm busy down here with … you know, experiments and such.
I already told you, I'm not coming out! Begone!
We should go back to the Brass Fortress at once. The shadows are everywhere.
Our business is concluded. Be on your way.
I can't believe we are talking to birds.  But its the only lead we have.

I thank you once more for aiding us in our time of need. May your thoughts be clear and your heart ever-oiled.\n\nHmm. I know we haven't met before, but I feel a sense of familiarity with you. Odd, how you sometimes get that feeling with strangers.
The nerve of that Elf! Clubbing people and throwing them into the sewer like garbage! These apostles better not go easy on him.
As one journey ends, another begins. I imagine there's much more to discover here in Sotha Sil's Clockwork City.
Is it just me, or did it just get much more uncomfortable down here? Best talk to Varuni before she and Luciana start really quarreling.
Who are you? Look, I don't want any trouble!
Still looking for your friend? Better hurry.
Bah! Oil those ankles and keep walking, green-heel. This one has nothing to say to you.
Look who's back. Just couldn't turn the key with those birds, eh? Don't be too hard on yourself. At least you've still got all your fingers.
We need to enter the regulation chamber quickly. I'm not sure how long the galvanic engine will last. If the guardian factotum doesn't destroy it first, that is.
Provost Varuni seems eager to speak with you. Go on, then.
Spy! Stay back, spy!\n\nThis tree belongs to the Blackfeather Court. The Duke claimed it, by law of sovereign roost! Look for shinies somewhere else! Go! Go!
That fool has no idea what he's in for. Live uncomfortably and learn, I suppose.
By the word of Seht, I am bound.\n\nGreetings, resident. All documents pertaining to your citizenship have been pressed and archived. Thank you for your interest. Go forth, and create.
What are you waiting for? Sil will take the stage any minute. Make your way to the loqutorium.

If you be foe, cast down your silly gauntlet! But I warn you—you touch this magnificent trove at your peril! I gathered these treasures for my lady love, and I would sooner die than let you take them!\n\nWhat say you, Featherless?

Do you like this place? It took me the better part of a decade to perfect it. Every stone and flower tells a story. Tales of how things were … how they ought to be.\n\nI thought about destroying it on more than one occasion. I'm glad I didn't.
Hail, crow-friend to my great Knight of Marrow! You come to parley? What boon do you seek from the Blackfeather Court?
Ah, you've returned. Excellent. Raynor and I have cobbled together a serviceable frame for the lamp—all we need now are the components I sent you to acquire. Were you successful?

Kireth and I reassembled a Dwemeric orrery with nothing but broken soul gems and spare parts … now look at me. Puzzling over a lamp.\n\nDon't worry though. We're near to finishing this thing, I know it.

Raynor and that annoying High Elf finished your lamp, but there's a problem.\n\nOn the way here, I overheard an aide complaining about some new security measures Sotha Sil put in place. Looks like the balcony is under heavy guard now.
Ah, my erstwhile companion. You look remarkably … coherent. Most mortals caught in a Daedric tempest would suffer some lasting effects. \n\nI'm impressed. Baffled, but impressed.
Was just popping up for some fresh-ish air and what do I find but the tangy smell of fresh meat. Looks like you've had some luck at the butcher's.
Now there's the look of someone on the hunt for something specific. You've come to the right place, friend. I've got a bit of everything.\n\nWhat can I get you?

Remember, you can yank a compressor out of most any verminous fabricant—assuming you don't smash it during the fight.\n\nOr you could just take one from <<1>>. It'd serve him right for cheating people.
Is that a modulated compressor? You impress Na'jhargo!\n\nlf you cannot find a use for it, this one will gladly take it off your hands.
Best nibble, if you know what's good for you.

So, you're the one Divayth tapped to be his aide in the Brass Fortress? Sorry to hear that. \n\nProvost Varuni's ancestors hail from House Telvanni, just like Lord Fyr. But honestly, they couldn't be more different.

So you're Divayth Fyr's new auxiliary, eh? Tough luck, friend. I've heard he's an insufferable bastard, but at least he's not Sotha Sil. Better to be turned into a guar than to serve the Clockwork God.
You're Lord Fyr's newest steward, huh? Could we talk later? If I don't finish this lamp inventory, Gascone will feed me to the fabricants.
Undaunted are usually the first to go charging into danger, but I'm more of a scout than a slayer. Better if you take the lead.
You know, this has only been mildly terrifying and I've enjoyed our time together. Maybe I should start taking pledges again myself.

Well met, traveler. \n\nI'm not sure what has brought you to Scalecaller Peak, but I must advise you to turn back. The creatures within this mountain have been exposed to a terrible disease, and I'm afraid there's a chance you'll become infected.

I don't regret coming here. Thanks to us, this plague has been stopped. We've saved countless lives today, my friend.\n\nStill, I can't help but wish our adventure ended under different circumstances.
Greetings. This partition governs All-Axle operations and gate controls. How can I assist you?
Is everything all right? I think that bird wants to see you.
So. We're going to fight … birds. If only my Reman dragoons could see me now. Channeling the arcane to defeat poultry.
Welcome to the Archivox, where all children of Sotha Sil may hear His divine word. What can I help you with?
You need something? I'm sort of in the middle of this theorem and …. Yup, lost it again. Damn.\n\nWell you've got my attention now. What do you want?
By the word of Seht, I am bound.\n\nWelcome to the Archivox, resident. How may I assist you?
What is it that you want?
I hope you can get through to Lector Trivura. She's remarkably reticent when she's thinking deeply on the will of the Divine Metronome. Which is often.

Please submit your questions to the deceased resident directly. All archival data related to your query will feed through the deceased resident via vocal emulation. \n\nMay Sotha Sil bless your many labors.
By some words, I wind my gears.\n\nI am in need of my integral of memory. You can find it in sector grid cube 3Z-A of the Mnemonic Planisphere.
The denizens of the Evergloam are devious! They caught me by surprise and threatened to feed me to the crows!

I hold in my head a globe. An intricate network of loops, gears, and strings. All interwoven in a delicate pattern which focuses the strength of all without tearing at the seams.\n\nWhere do you fit in this pattern?
They said our fate was inescapable, that our sequence was set and nothing could change it.\n\nIt's almost too much to hope for, but if Kamid could change his fortune, then so can I!

That display of emotion isn't indicative of the people of Slag Town. Kamid lost his mother in the last pilgrimage, and that's made him angry at the world.\n\nHe has a point, though. Dreams and prophecies can be dangerous things.
Go find another beggar to bother. I've got more important things to do than carry some apostle hopeful's sack of dirty laundry!

Did everything go all right? You didn't run into any trouble, did you? Raynor requires constant supervision, especially around ruins and other ancient places.\n\nHe's extremely smart, but he has few practical skills and he's easily distracted.
I'll apologize to Kireth, but you talk to her first. Make sure she isn't still angry. She tends to hit me when she's angry, and I'd prefer not to get bruised today.
These minions of Nocturnal, so rude they are! This one has never been treated with such disrespect—not even when I traveled among the Telvanni!
I'll meet you back in Slag Town. Then we can talk to Palbatan and find out what the old man knows about the lost treasure.

Gear Grinder is a terror. Tales of spotting the foul beast haunt the nightmares of every child in Slag Town. But if the fabricant is still there, then so is the treasure.\n\nMay the pistons of fate run smoothly for you and Kamid both.
You talk to Palbatan, tell him what we discovered. The stubborn old Dark Elf refuses to share any information with me about the lost treasure.

You did it! Thanks to you, we found the lost treasure! This proves the Prognosticator isn't an oracle, it's just a machine—and not a very good one at that!\n\nNow I can show the people of Slag Town that we're not prisoners to destiny.

I suppose I should get this over with. I just hope I can convince the people of Slag Town that the Prognosticator isn't an oracle. That we can forge our own futures, despite what statistics might indicate.
We need to talk. It involves that sequence plaque I told you about.\n\nMeet me in the Outlaws Refuge. The streets of Slag Town have many ears, but we can speak privately in there.
<Snuffler emits a low, agitated chitter at your touch. It's impossible to tell whether it enjoys or detests the attention.>

If you have come to pay your respects, I'm afraid I can no longer allow visitations. My wards have become too unpredictable for unfamiliar company.\n\nTruth told, they struggle to find comfort in the routine now as well.
I wish you the best of luck. I have faith Sotha Sil planned for everything to happen this way. And that means it will all work out in the end.
I still can't believe Orinol isn't coming home. Well, guess it's just me and Jona now.
I've been searching through pipes all morning trying to find Brassie. I thought I'd never see him again! Not, of course, that I wouldn't just purchase another one. But they aren't cheap you know!
Son of a troll, I can't believe you found our clan's sword. Never thought I'd see it again, not after Aunt Dulza vanished. Twenty years is a long time to wonder.
Have you come to be a taste tester too? This one hopes you brought an empty stomach. Best not to waste good food.
Okay, deep breaths—oh, bad idea! The smell's bringing it all back again. Really hope I can get through the meal ….
Sometimes the Eye sees treason and must cut it out before it spreads. This one is sorry you had to witness that.
Oracle Marieve doesn't appear to have suffered any permanent injuries. Of course, a visit to Oblivion can shake even the strongest minds—especially if the trip wasn't taken voluntarily.
First these Daedric aberrations and now you. What trouble has Oracle Marieve dredged up this time?

Even though I sometimes see far-away places and future events, nothing can ever be truly certain. I knew you were coming to rescue me, but that didn't alleviate my fear. I thought I was going to die in Mephala's realm.\n\nThank you.

I am one with Lord Seht's grand design. I can feel my purpose in my very core. My mind is free of the clutter of my living needs. I am no longer burdened by the weight of my decaying flesh. I am free.\n\nThank you.
Crow-friend! I am glad I found you. Just let me … catch my breath.

I have no more time for you. I have to prepare for my meeting with the Aldarch. Why he wants to meet in the Coral Forest is beyond me, but he claims he wants to show me something.\n\nWhy are you still here? Go away.

How bold of you. The nebarra dares to stand in my holy presence. Very well, bold nebarra. What can the new Aldarch of Shimmerene do for you?\n\nAnd please, try not to bore me or spray any spittle on my spotless vestments.

Another newcomer? Ink has barely dried on the Queen's decree and there are already more of you than I can count. I look forward to hearing how the Kinlady and new Aldarch plan to protect Summerset's interests.

First the Kinlady invites us to discuss the situation in Shimmerene. Then she tells us to sit here and wait. And now a damn nebarra is standing close enough for me to smell it!\n\nWell, nebarra? Speak up! Or is talking not part of your repertoire?

A newcomer, here in the Kinlady's garden? And during her latest rant on the dangers of the Queen's decree? Oh that's just grand!\n\nI really can't wait to see her expression when she finally notices your presence.
You see that, right? My eyes aren't playing tricks on me? That's a Sea Sload! They haven't been seen in Summerset since … well, it's been centuries, at least!
Dawnbreaker's gem contains a portion of Meridia's power, but on its own it isn't strong enough to dispel this barrier. We need to find the Dawnbreaker sword and make it whole once more.
Strange magic. Life-stealing pearls. Unknown sea creatures. It all relates to Sotha Sil's warning, but we still don't know what form the real threat will eventually take.
It had to be one of the lesser races. No Altmer, even a newcomer, would deface a beautiful wall like that.\n\nRazum-dar claims it's a message of some sort, but I just don't see it.
Come to admire the art, newcomer? If I find out this was your handiwork, sequestering will be the least of your problems.

Now then. I see no reason to delay Emile's exile. I will formalize his conviction today, and have him turned over to the Mages Guild shortly thereafter.\n\nThis sordid affair has caused enough pain. I'll not draw it out.

How can you condemn an innocent man to prison? He's obviously out of his mind with grief!\n\nI'd find a way to exonerate him myself if I thought anyone would listen. Damn your eyes! And the Sapiarchs!

I know this wasn't easy. Condemning an innocent man to prison makes me nauseous, but sometimes sacrifices have to be made for the greater good.\n\nAs odd as it sounds, I think your decision brought Emile some measure of peace. Thank you.
So Emile was guilty after all. Can't say I'm happy to hear it. Then again, it does feel good to put this whole mess behind us.\n\nJust don't mention my part in this to the Sapiarchs, all right?

Five-claw! You have the happy ability to know where to find Raz when Raz has need of you!\n\nGetting information out of these Peryite idiots is like squeezing milk from a stone. This is why Raz hates dealing with Daedric cults!
Raz is pleased he was able to find Sadara-do safe and uninjured. She has agreed to talk to you, so this one suggests you get to it, yes?
May Meridia's light shine upon you. Raz told me you need to contact my Prince.\n\nWith the recent attacks, however, I need to ask you what your interest in Meridia happens to be.

Poor Emile. He must have lied about murdering Haladan to protect us. The Sapiarchs would come after me if they knew I existed, and Haladan's reputation would be destroyed.\n\nPlease, take Haladan's notes to the Sapiarchs. You must prove Emile innocent!

Raz will take Sadara to a place where she will be safe from the Court of Bedlam.\n\nMeanwhile, it seems that you must journey to hidden islands and Daedric realms. This one would say he wishes he could accompany you, but we'd both know Raz was lying.
Our shrine to Meridia waits on the other side of this door. I am not sure what the Court of Bedlam left behind, so please be careful in there.

My followers murdered. My shrine desecrated. The other Princes, this so-called triad, they must answer for these insults.\n\nBut I sense a question in your mind. Speak, mortal! Ask what you will of the Prince of Light!

Thank you once again. Haladan was the wisest, kindest, most beautiful soul I've ever known. I don't know if I'll ever fully recover from this, but the knowledge that his memory lives on sets my mind at ease.
<The telescope is set to view the platform's associated constellation.>

Perhaps the Psijic sages can help me remember where I hid the Heart of Transparent Law. At least you stopped K'Tora before the Sea Sload gained that knowledge.\n\nIn the meantime, we must warn the Sapiarchs of the threat to the Crystal Tower.
I'll make my own way to Rellenthil and meet you there. I expect we should start by seeing if the town's Canonreeve has noticed anything unusual in the area.

What a fool I've been! I was worried sick about Leythen while he was out cavorting with worshipers of Mephala.\n\nI lost our daughter, too, but you don't see me abandoning my friends and family. I didn't forsake the Psijic Order!
How could the abyssal pearl disappear like that? It makes no sense.
This is Meridia's champion? He's not as impressive as I imagined.

Well, this is awkward. Here I am, Meridia's champion, covered in webs and held at the mercy of unsettling spider people. Thanks for rescuing me, though.\n\nI would have freed myself at some point. I was just working up to it, that's all.
I see Valsirenn found you. Good. I've been making preparations while the knight recovers. Since I can't remember what's on the other side of the barrier, we'll need to be ready for every contingency.

Who? Oh! Don't you know not to interrupt a sage when she's deep in concentration?\n\nI suppose the Ritemaster sent you to see how my research was coming along? I've listened to his memory over and over, and I examined every relevant tome I could find.
I'm sorry, but I don't think I'll be of much use if Glardir's summoned hordes of literary monsters. I wish you good luck, for whatever that's worth.
I just don't understand how Larydel and I could grow so far apart. Did I really lead him to believe I doubted his ability with magic? Does he really envy mine? If only he'd told me ….

I wanted to thank you again for getting me out of Mephala's realm. It wasn't anything like I originally imagined.\n\nOh, and I wanted to let you know that I was able to repair the Dawnbreaker. The sword's power should allow us to breach the barrier.

I regret hurting Rinyde, but I know now she'll find happiness. Once I explain—once we're both where we need to be—she'll understand.\n\nOh, and feel free to visit me in the Manor of Masques sometime. I'd like to stay in touch.
I've got a theory, based on our findings thus far. I don't think you're going to like it.
Did that mage really plan to unmask us? Why in Mara's name would she do such a thing? We've all worked so hard for this day!
Lorkhan's bits! Did that drab looking mage really just try to unmask me? The nerve!
I don't really understand, but … did you just save us from being unmasked? I can't believe you would sacrifice yourself like that. My friend, thank you!
Talerion will leave my boy alone now, right?
I've never seen Glardir like this. Mischievous, brassy …. I actually kind of like it! Oh, don't look at me like that.\n\nWe'll bring her back somehow. Don't worry.

So, you found our lost sheep. Well done. \n\nAs you can see, I sent for Arathel's mother. She won't speak to me of course, but she seems appreciative enough. Perhaps this will be a teachable moment for the both of them. One can hope, I suppose.
So … it's you. When you didn't return, I assumed you had abandoned your search. What are you doing here?
So, I think we're done here. Right? Right.
How did Talerion find this place? I guess it doesn't matter. I'll go quietly if I must. Just don't let him hurt the people here.
That was it? I don't feel cured at all. I feel the same. I'm confused.
The Dragon was my prize. Stolen from me now, like my friends, my peace, and my free will. Destroy Orryn and let me lie.
Ugh, thank you. Glad to be free of those aching bones. Gone stiff in my old age.\n\nMy place is in Sovngarde. Don't let these ash eaters keep me like some trophy.
Divines grant me strength, there's a grudge to be repaid. I'll do whatever I can to see our tormentor answer for what he's done.
Take a nice deep breath of non-putrid air, you deserve it. We can rest easy, and murder-free, for the time being.

You'd think as Canonreeve I'd be immune to the troublesome temper of a spoiled and rebellious child. \n\nBut what distinguished visitors I have today! A wandering sage, a well-dressed Khajiit, and you. What brings such a group to Rellenthil?
I'm going to take the longest bath. Long enough to grow gills. And spend half my weekly wage on scented oils. Whatever it takes to get the stench and feel of that place out of my skin.

Ah, you're back. Sorry if I seem surprised. Honestly, I wrote you off as dead the minute you walked through those gates. No offense.\n\nBrought something for me, eh? A key … with the Direnni seal? What exactly did you find in there?

Careful there, friend—there's a thief about.\n\nOne of these two scamps is the criminal mastermind behind a half-baked plot to steal a pie. My pie, in fact. Cut down in its crispy, gooey prime while my back was turned.
I didn't think I'd see you again after we parted ways before. I'm pleased to be wrong, for once. Lindafwe, Silurie, and I all owe you our lives.
Can't you see I am busy?
To think, this whole expedition has been a trap!
Thank you. I don't know what would have happened if you hadn't shown up.
It can't end here. There has to be something we can do to stop her.
We must warn Forte … that he's putting everyone in danger ….
Go through the temple … the southern stone. Baneaweh tendell. Those are the words. Stop this … from happening.\n\nTake my diary. It will prove … everything ….
My, my. You look like you could use gold. Care to take a job of mine? Quite simple, really. An academic needs an escort through this forest.
What? Oh, thank Malacath! I thought you were the Relicmaster!\n\nI'm not sure what brings you down here, but you couldn't have come at a better time. As you can see, I'm a little … impaired.
Come on, what do you say? We're both benefiting here, really. You get a cozy room, I get a tenant who won't ruin my reputation. It's a win-win here.

How dare you show your face? Scoundrel! Oh, yes, I know exactly what happened to my supplies. Vaerelel will be crowing about his victory for weeks, no doubt!\n\nAt least I have a villain for my next painting. You. And it will not be a pretty picture!

Finally, someone who listens to reason. Now I can keep the aurialis hidden.\n\nAnd feel free to tell whoever you can that it's gone from this hilltop, forever. Keep other artists from snooping around, like that Vaerelel fellow.
These words of power, they aren't meant for mortal eyes.\n\nAs an earl in the Court of Bedlam, believe me when I say that Leythen isn't being totally honest with you.

No High Elf wanted to do business with me until Tindoria started buying my stock. Her good word has earned me quite a bit of business.\n\nShe's a bit stuck up, but she sees the value in hard work. No matter where you come from.

It seems that Tindoria has certainly gotten what she's always wished for. After all, she must have accumulated quite the influence to have acquired this tea.\n\nIf only she put as much commitment into her art as her status, she might truly be great.

So you've chosen to be as unreasonable as your employer. Typical.\n\nWell, no matter. I have no doubt the royal court will choose to sponsor me as their next artist. I have no need for fancy paints to sway the hearts of mer.
I have a lot to make up for. More than is possible in a lifetime, but you have my oath that I will do all I can.

This escapade of yours could have been disastrous. What were you and Oriandra thinking, trusting Leythen to help us translate the ancient language?\n\nNow nothing you discovered can be trusted. We're back to square one!

You can find the Ritemaster in the Dreaming Cave.\n\nIn the meantime, I want to see how the Golden Knight's recovery is progressing. And I should probably look in on Leythen—provided I can resist the urge to kill him, that is.
One of these days we're going to meet up in a tavern and there won't be any Daedra or monsters or evil necromancers trying to destroy the world and kill us all.\n\nOne of these days ….
Urlsar's up ahead—in the eye of the storm.
Step through the portal when you're ready, but be prepared to face our most dangerous battle yet.\n\nHead for the ancient ruin and we'll meet you there.
I don't like any of this. Lost memories, deals with Daedric Princes … nothing about this feels right.\n\nAnd Iachesis. I've never seen him like this before. I actually think he might be … afraid.
Didn't the old man mention an ancient ruin? Let's keep climbing until we find it.

Before we charge into certain danger, you need to know something isn't right. I remember defeating K'Tora, but somehow the creature and its cabal have returned. And the pearl. I have a vague memory of moving it myself.\n\nI am … unsettled.
You had something else to report?
I just need a moment here alone.\n\nIronic that this came to a head in such a holy place. Maybe I can find some absolution here. Or at least some small measure of peace.
It's a good thing I followed you after I alerted the rest of the Conclave.\n\nI think I can counteract K'Tora's mind magic, but I'll need your help.
Tranquil greetings, initiate. Have you come to deliver the Augur of the Obscure? I cleared a place for it in the vault. All is prepared!
You! I remember you. Please, you have to tell me what's going on. My son never came home, and now they tell me he's ….\n\nThey won't even let me see him! What happened to my boy?

How unusual. The Ritemaster has kept me waiting for an inordinate amount of time, but instead of Iachesis, here comes the savior of the Clockwork City.\n\nThat leads me to a single conclusion—the Ritemaster has not returned from the Dreaming Cave.
Go have a look around. I doubt you'll find anything, but there's no harm in trying.
A Sea Sload. Interesting. I haven't dissected such a specimen in an exceedingly long unit of temporal measurement.
Poor bastards. They never stood a chance.

I guess I should inform the Conclave of the Eleven Forces. They'll want to appoint an interim Ritemaster until a formal election can be held.\n\nNot that it will matter once Nocturnal takes control of the Crystal Tower.
Looks like Leythen got the door open. Let's head inside.
I'm a little busy here. If it's explanations you seek, talk to Darien.

The Conclave is at its wit's end. Since the loss of the Ritemaster, they've looked to me for guidance. Nothing I've suggested has gotten us closer to reaching the Crystal Tower, though.\n\nIn the meantime, Sotha Sil has asked to see you.
I see that Erilthel made it back in one piece. Thank the Hist. The Guild might have docked my pay if she wound up dead.\n\nMore importantly, did you find the tokens of Meridia in there?
Raz feels so helpless. So much death.\n\nWe need to find a way to end this. We have to.
Do you see? What they did to me? What they are all still doing? Is a young girl's curiosity worthy of this torment?\n\nI only wish to pass on—to be free of this place. Please, help me.

My master has been livid since Nocturnal betrayed him. That's why I've been keeping my distance. Do me a favor and try not to make him any more irritated when you talk to him. I'd hate to see something bad happen to you.\n\nOh wait, no I wouldn't.
What happened? Did the threatening words do the trick or is Rigurt in even more trouble with the snooty High Elves now?
Rigurt will have his audience with the Proxy Queen, for all the good it will do him.\n\nNow go away and let us never speak of this incident again.

I appreciate your help in acquiring cultural mementos from the newcomers. I hope my letter of recommendation provides Ambassador Rigurt with the opportunity to meet the Proxy Queen.\n\nShe really is an interesting woman.
"Milk drinker. Milk drinker!" Is that really a Nord insult? How benign.\n\nAnd what do you want? Can't you see I'm trying to rehearse? I always have trouble with the accents of the lesser races.
You performed admirably. And the fact that I don't have to tell the Queen that her favorite bowl and cup were stolen, well, that's just honey butter on the sour meat pasty.
I'm ever so pleased you could arrange this meeting. Manacar has been the perfect gentlemen, and such a great model! Inspiration is just flooding through me.

Well, this isn't quite what I expected. Your friend is a curious individual. Scribbled constantly as we talked. I had no idea she wished for me to be a … model.\n\nWell, no matter. Have you the heart?

I was going to recommend that the Queen shut this place down when I give my report, but if Talomar thinks he can rebuild it into a place where the animals come first, I bet I can make the promotion stick.\n\nHe was always her favorite keeper.

I know a quick route in Alinor. I'll get Tableau back to her debut before anyone panics. It will be difficult saying goodbye again, but ….\n\nDon't worry. Soon she'll forget all about me. It's all for the best.

Thank you for helping Manacar realize the truth.\n\nFor now, I'll continue my art. Perhaps I'll lose some prestige, but I don't really mind. In fact, I'm actually looking forward to some peace for once.
Strange. I don't remember seeing you on the guest list.
I don't know how much longer I can hide out here. Give me some good news.
The time has come for me to unsheathe the quill of justice and cut an inky swath through centuries of lies.\n\nAnd probably book passage back to Daggerfall well in advance.

A new face in the court! And how pleasant and interesting it is! We do appreciate the return of our brothers and sisters to the Blessed Isle, even if our nobles count you among the other newcomers.\n\nNow then, what business brings you to the palace?
Not now, please. I really must prepare for tonight's lecture. Besides, only those with permission may enter the College of Sapiarchs. We can't have just anyone wandering around the compound.
Why do you linger, walker? If you wish to save this boy, Arathel, you must move quickly.
Don't let these crumbled husks trouble you. I needed to vent my frustrations and my loyal followers were close at hand.

I can't believe I was concerned about the welfare of my husband! To find Leythen here, threatening the Sapiarchs and leading a horde of Daedra … how could he betray the Order like that? How could he betray me?
I came to Summerset in search of a better life, but all I found was the same old life—just in a different location.
I've been trying to get a job with a clothier or tailor, but most of the High Elf shop owners want nothing to do with newcomers such as me.

This one thanks Jone and Jode for bringing me to this land of sparkle syrup and honey pudding. Well, the food and drink is different, but the sentiment is the same.\n\nGood things await us all here in Summerset!
Your departure wasn't a request. I suggest you go before we find a cage for you.

We appreciate your aid in this matter. Before you head to the Illumination Academy, perhaps you can have your friend get that … cultist … out of my compound.\n\nAs it is, it's going to take weeks to get rid of the stench of Daedra.
My Mistress Mephala remembers every slight, and so do I. Bear that in mind if you decide to keep aiding the Psijics.

Nocturnal must pay for betraying my Mistress, but the magic of the abyssal pearls appears to do more than just siphon our life energy. It obscures my connection to Mephala.\n\nThis shrine may be blocked, but I may know another way.
I understood about half of what that crazy Dark Elf told you, but it didn't sound like something that's going to make either me or Meridia very happy.
This one has seen many bizarre things working as an Eye of the Queen, but this may take the moon-sugar cake!\n\nA strange dog walked up and spoke to Raz!
Magic always makes Raz's head hurt, but this was an impressive feat! Go on, go talk to the Sapiarch.
The amount of wooden furniture in this place boggles my mind. But I have to confess, I rather like polishing and waxing it all.
As I predicted, your efforts were successful. A slight chance is all probability requires. There is no such thing as impossible odds. You are proof of that.
If you're the person that's been following me, I warn you, I'll … I'll scream!
So you return to me alone. I … the pearl? Is it destroyed?
I should have tried harder to keep them from going into those ruins.
A slap on the wrist. It'll take months, if not years, to restore my work to its original condition.\n\nYou've done me and Summerset a great disservice today.

All I wanted was for the High Elves to show a little more respect to nature, but they're just so set in their ways.\n\nWhen I get out of prison, I'm going to explore more of Summerset. I have to hope it's not all like this.
How many squatters are living out here?

A fling with a Wood Elf is one thing but … a werewolf? Unbelievable.\n\nI'm sure you understand my need for discretion. It wouldn't just be Niralin's honor on the line if word got out. Why, it would positively ruin me as well, just by association!
Just leave before you end up getting yourself killed.
That was … totally exhausting! Thank you for trusting me and for helping me break K'Tora's mind traps. I couldn't have done it without you.
Can't say I miss the smells of sea salt and hot blood, but it felt good to give those Sea Elves a right thrashing.\n\nWe best make for the mainland while their cutter is still taking on water.
We're finding more questions than answers. There has to be more. There has to be.\n\nTry the room across the hall.
He washes up here after being gone for weeks, his boat nowhere in sight, and he acts like it's just another day on the sea. Was everything all right? Did he cause you any trouble?
You seem to have a knack for battle, but make no mistake. If we hadn't lost Ludovic, me and my men would have cleared this place out.
Hey, I remember your face. I'll let you buy me another drink when this is all done. I'm sure I'm going to need it.

Sotha Sil allowed Barbas to come to Artaeum so he can lead us to the Crystal Tower. In a moment, he'll also open the way so that my Prince can attune the diamonds for us. Then we can attack Nocturnal directly.\n\nI'm actually looking forward to that.

Things will never be the same between me and Leythen again, but I think we understand each other a little better now.\n\nFunny how the approaching end of the world has a way of putting everything into perspective.

Sotha Sil personally requested our help to maintain your connection to the Dreaming Cave. I know Valsirenn wanted to go with you, but just the thought of entering a tower that's bouncing through every level of reality scares me to no end.\n\nGood luck.
Raz must return to Summerset. If you do not stop Nocturnal, this one must prepare the island for the nastiness that is sure to follow.
This is the day we've waited for, for so long. The return of a living descendant. The Saviors will be pleased that their sacrifice was not for nothing.
I think it's best you leave. Before I lose my temper and throw you off this bloody mountain.

I've learned to trust my instincts over the years. The problem this time, though, is my instinct is telling me to run far, far away.\n\nThat wouldn't be very heroic now, would it? Into the fray we go, my friend. Even if it might be for the last time.

I appreciate the help. Trust me, this is a noble cause!\n\nFirst things first—you'll need to track Lirendel down and find out how to get this nonsense started. I'd ask him myself, but the urge to punch him might be too much for me.
By the Eight, can't I go an hour without being accosted by some Orcish clod? What do you want?

Greetings, walker. How good it is to see a fellow newcomer! This one grows tired of serving these dungy High Elves. Unclawed dandies make my tail bristle!\n\nBut my words wander. What can Nahdahni do for you?
Scurry back to your Orc friend. We'll be along shortly.
Even if it's too late for him, don't leave us to the same fate. Please, find Arillas's keys and free us.

Thank the Stars you arrived. I thought my life forfeit.\n\nViscarne was ranting before you came. Burned supplies, released prisoners. A gryphon now roaming the skies, picking off Sea Elves like the rats they are. Tell me, was that your doing?
If you want to help, best talk to Kinlady Helenaere. Trust me, you don't want to ignore a High Elf. Especially not a noble one.
I must get back to work now. Every moment that my cousin remains sequestered is another moment where I must perform the work of two people. Good travels, wayfarer.

We must be nearing the pinnacle of the tower. That's why Nocturnal sent her champion to slow us down.\n\nNocturnal's earl damaged this mechanism beyond repair. Even if we had acquired the key, I'm not sure it would have opened the gate.
Come on. Leythen gave us a chance. We can't let his sacrifice be in vain.
Ugh, my feet hurt. Pacing around a bunch of pigs for who knows how long … I'm never eating pork again!
I'm just glad I didn't find a pile of mud to wallow in. These robes are impossible to clean!
Let's just forget this ever happened, all right?

Thank you for helping me win this last battle. While the Psijic Order will not be among those protecting the Crystal Tower, we will continue to observe from afar.\n\nAnd now, it's time for us to depart Summerset.
Just another voyage or two, and Renzir will be set to retire in luxury. Alongside his Nubani, of course.

Quickly, dump the shipments overboard. There are darker forces in this cave than mutinying smugglers. Nubani wishes to sail out of Karnwasten as soon as possible.\n\nAnd have no worries. She will find her way back to Renzir.

Good luck getting Sotha Sil to attend this council. He's never been particularly excited over the idea of social gatherings.\n\nIn the meantime, I have missives to send and leaders to collect. Lucky me.
The Sapiarchs recognize your bravery on our behalf in Lillandril and within the Crystal Tower.\n\nBut there is nothing you can say that will alter our thinking on this matter.

This situation sets a precedent that makes us uncomfortable. The Psijic Order tries our patience, but we will allow this council meeting to play out.\n\nRazum-dar has suggested we hear from you. So, please, talk to Larnatille and let's get on with it.
Why did Nocturnal have to kill Iachesis? Because of some damn crystal? I don't understand any of this.\n\nPlease, I need a moment to gather my thoughts.
Well, that could have gone better. I know it looks bad, but … aw, who am I kidding? It is bad!\n\nI'm sorry Nocturnal killed the old man. And took the Heart. And took my damn sword!
You got here just in time. I've never seen Valsirenn with such … murder in her eyes.
They will be here soon. We have to hurry.
Ahem. Battlereeve Tanerline requests your presence at the Royal Palace. There is a situation developing and you have come highly recommended.\n\nOr so we have been led to believe.
Talk to the Battlereeve. She's been waiting for you to return.\n\nBesides, I can hear you perfectly fine from over here.
Uh, hey. About Karnwasten. Thanks for your help back there.

Indirim and the rest of the marines retreated … down the coast. Find them and make sure the report … reaches the Battlereeve.\n\nBe careful … the geysers … and the Sea Sload B'Korgen … they're also nearby.
Just have to remember the route to Sovngarde …. It will come to me eventually—as sure as the snows of Frostfall!

I thank the Divines that you've agreed to help. This murder weighs heavy on all of us.\n\nThe victim, Halimorion, was not well-liked. Many locals may lift a glass to his passing. But the assassin, the Ghost of the Green … that's altogether different.
Thank goodness the academy has returned to normal. I don't think I'll ever fully recover from my time as a Nord prospector.
I hope there will be no more distractions. My students are weeks behind in the material!
I always love watching the fish in this pond. So peaceful.
Hey! What are you doing ruining my show? That scrib was going to make such a delicious splatting noise!\n\nWait … the Brave Little Scrib ran away? I'm confused.

The High Magistrate watches us the way a gryphon scrutinizes coral crabs at meal time. I do not wish to appear idle before her and neither should you.\n\nLet's conclude our business and be done with this.
I guess being a member of the Illumination Academy is a little better than being a pirate queen. I guess.
Once again, thank you.\n\nI don't know if Hunrand will ever recover from having his life as a pirate queen snatched away from him, but I'm much happier now!
There was one other thing I wanted to discuss with you, initiate. It will just take a moment.

I suppose it's too much for a prisoner to expect a few moments of solitude with his thoughts. Ah, well.\n\nSo what can I do for you? Has the Ritemaster sent you to interrogate me? Doesn't he trust my wife's talents in that regard?

You should make haste to Artaeum. Those books need to be returned to their master's pit. The sooner, the better.\n\nI will be here nursing these exquisite beverages if you have any questions. May the Old Ways guide your path.
Ah, another newcomer. Delightful.\n\nWhat exactly can I do for you?
Manacar never was one for idle chit chat.\n\nAnd what are you still doing here? I got a disreputable business to uphold. Don't need you ruining any more of my contracts.
Remember, I need three bottles. If I don't bring home all three, I might as well not come home at all.
You've told no one else the contents of this letter, correct?
No, please. Don't make this all have been for nothing. Corgrad needs him. It needs us.
Iachesis is in a mood. I'd watch my step around him if I were you.
Why won't these damned High Elves tell us anything? We need answers!
Do not invoke our wrath, trespasser. Go now and we may forgive your intrusion.

The embalming process has already begun. When the stone is finished we will be restored and he will be a Savior.\n\nI regret that Faidur must suffer, but his pain will be a small fraction of the sacrifice required to save Corgrad from annihilation.
Oh, just do something, I don't care what.

The Grand Maestro mentioned Daedra, but I never imagined they'd belong to one of the patrons of the Court of Bedlam.\n\nThis changes everything. Now I'm really interested in helping you translate the Ritemaster's memory.
I'm not sure how long I can maintain this link, so please hurry. I'd hate to lose Oriandra to K'Tora's mind trap!
Damn, this hurts.
Still a pretty vantage. I hope the Sea Elves don't despoil this old tree along with everything else.
I've never seen Curtaros look so serious. It's making me nervous, if I'm honest.

You must be the concerned bystander I'm hearing so much about. Both Vinafwe and Eslion claim you can prove their case, which begs all sorts of questions, but I don't have time for that, so lets cut to the heart of the matter.\n\nIs Eslion guilty?
Stay back! I can't remember who I am … or what happened to me.
Your bearing is that of an awakened artisan. Have you deconstructed a piece of jewelry, as I requested?

Y'ffre be praised, I can't believe you were able to pull that off. You're something else.\n\nAnd don't worry, Gwinolas told me about Aralem. It's a damn shame he had to die, but at least my other companions are safe.
I can't believe I was nearly pecked to death. Nothing is worth this sort of trauma.
I haven't run … that hard … in a long time.
Oh, my! A roguish adventurer. Finally!\n\nSorry about the mess. I usually keep things so neat. When things get dirty … oh, I get so flustered.

Ah, a fleshy, thick-thumbed biped! Hello!\n\nYou're an Elf, right? Or is it a man? I'm sorry, I have some difficulty telling you people apart. You're much less blue than the others. In color, I mean—not disposition. Anyway. What can I do for you?
I should be reclining on my lounge with a quarter-millennium aged port and Eustasia nestled in my bosom. But no, Durell insisted we take a stroll along the beach.
You can be rest assured that my assistants will be well looked-after. No need to do anything rash!
It seems the Sapiarch has calmed down, at least for the time being. I suppose we have you to thank for that.
I have to keep working, else I'll never become a Sapiarch. If you'll excuse me.

Strange. You certainly don't look like a prisoner, yet here you are, joining me within the cells of Moon Hunter Keep. \n\nI'd tell you to turn back, but I doubt my werewolf captors would let you just leave.
I'll make sure the Silver Dawn knows of your bravery. My order shall forever be thankful for your deeds, my friend. And myself as well.
Apologies if you expected my assistance, but I'm more of a scholar than a warrior. I'll hang back while you clear out the forest ahead.

I … I know what I must do. My father was bitten protecting me. He sacrificed an eternity of peace, all so I could live.\n\nAnd now I finally have a chance to repay him. To save him. To be free of that guilt.
It's going to be a long time before I can look at my own reflection, that's for sure.
Good to know the Orc is not completely without manners, I suppose.
Igeke's the one you made a deal with, not me. I'll happily accept Gjadil's treasure, but I won't pay you for the effort.
So? Were you able to find Gjadil's treasure?
If you've got Gjadil's treasure, it's best to inform Igeke. She's quite the brute if she doesn't get her way.
I still can't believe you were able to defeat Z'Maja. A feat not even the Welkynars could accomplish, in all their might.\n\nI'm so grateful the Stars led you to Cloudrest.
You couldn't pay me to ride that gryphon again. I don't know how the Welkynars make it look so easy!

Before you say anything, just know I got word from my mother. She sent a letter with someone smart enough to flee the city.\n\nI always knew she was a bleeding heart, but staying in that Star forsaken city? She must have grown mad.
Another newcomer in such an unwelcoming land! Surely, you feel pity for a fellow outcast?
What am I missing? What?
I don't let just anybody snuggle up to my trunk, but you've earned some rest for the both of us. Take a load off!
Who in Oblivion are you? I left explicit instructions with the manager of this establishment that I was not to be disturbed under any circumstances!
Oh dear, I'm not sure I can evacuate. This harp is awfully heavy, you know. Perhaps Welkynar Olorime would be willing to carry it for me.
Thank you for taking on my son's request. I'm afraid I hadn't even thought to contact him since the city was attacked. I've been far too busy helping the injured.
Get away, ephem. Away from me. Away from our island!
You may go no farther, citizens. Cloudrest's gates have been barred from within. \n\nAnd before you ask, I don't know anything else. We're just as much in the dark now as when we got here.
I thought my Zan'hi was mistaken, but now …. Could Mirulon be what he says he is? Be careful, walker.

From what the Loremaster tells me, the scryers are nearly halfway to locating the last four pieces of the staff. Placing another batch of Psijic Seals should give them all the information they need.\n\nAre you ready for another trip to the continent?

Well, I guess this is goodbye. I'll take good care of the Augur, you have my word.\n\nThank you … for everything. I deserve this exile, but I don't think I will ever deserve a friend like you. Take care of the Order for me, all right?
You needn't worry. Both Josajeh and the Augur will be fine.\n\nTrue, the skull may resent your choice for a while—but dissatisfied safety is better than blissful danger.
Is it …? I'm sorry. I'm so sorry! Was anyone hurt? I will never forgive myself if someone ….
Summerset's days of isolation are over. You ought to visit, someday. You'll never find a more beautiful land in all of Tamriel.
So this is the end of my fighting days? I suppose I'll have to find a new purpose in rebuilding our order. Passing on my wisdom and all of that.
My power may be gone, but my life remains. I'll continue on as I always have; in service to the Welkynar, and the goodness they represent.
It appears as though my power has been diminished with the loss of my shade. Z'Maja's power truly does continue to amaze, despite the outcome of its use.
To think that mage would taint our sacred stage with such an act. Why, I've never seen such an outrageous display of disrespect!

Honor and praise! It's nice to see you again.\n\nI've been busy in Cloudrest of course. Recruiting new riders and rebuilding. It's not an easy task, but one I'm honored to do. It's not every day you get to rebuild an ancient order.

Headed to the famed Russafeld winery, traveler? Well then, it seems I'm not the only one who'll be disappointed today.\n\nOld Halimorion's been offed by those Wood Elves. Won't be any wine tastings for a while I'd wager.
Yes? And who might you be?

Raz could get used to such a seat. Metaphorically speaking, of course. This one would prefer a throne with far more padding.\n\nBut enough of such talk. Today we celebrate your victory! From newcomer to savior of Summerset. Quite the feat, yes?
Welcome, stranger. Are you here to join the Mages Guild?
You're not part of the Mages Guild, are you? Perhaps you would like to be?
Sorry I can't be more help. Hopefully that Esterdel fellow will be able to tell you a bit more than I could.
There you are! The Ritemaster sent me to find you.\n\nHe's been scrying through his memories and believes that he discovered something significant regarding the Heart of Transparent Law.

I grieve over the loss of my mentor and friend, Iachesis, but grief isn't going to stop Nocturnal. We need to find a way to turn this Daedric tide before the waters of Oblivion overwhelm us.\n\nThankfully, Sotha Sil has returned to Artaeum.
Experimenting with time unfortunately leaves one rarely surprised. For example, I knew I would find you here.

I'm sorry it had to come to this, but nothing can stop the magic of the pearls now.\n\nMy Mistress offers a small mercy. Leave her to finish her work and she'll kill the Psijics quickly. But if you interfere, you will all suffer before you die.
Thanks, mate. I know you've got other adventures ahead, but I wanted to just take a moment and speak face to … crystal sort-of face.
Tranquil greetings. We do not see many newcomers on the island. Welcome.
Do you have a moment? A friend of mine. She's run off and I fear the worst.
It's you! I never thought I'd see you again! You probably don't remember me. Tirwin? You freed me from those Telvanni slave drivers in Vvardenfell.
Don't suppose I could declare it a wildlife preserve and leave the animals to roam freely, could I?\n\nI'm going to have my work cut out for me, getting this place back in order.
Oh, there you are. The Relicmaster has been looking all over for you.
Convince Ruliel to flee, as I do. It's madness to remain.
Hey! Hey, you … yeah, you. The one with the fancy clothes. C'mere. I'll tell you a secret!\n\nHa! You should see the look on your face!
I don't know how Battlereeve Pandermalion is still standing. Hasn't he done enough?

Narazda knows these symptoms, walker. Sometime soon, our soldier friend will be more rugged than handsome. And when he turns … he will turn on us.\n\nBut there is no time to handle this. We must make our way to Vykosa.
Tell me about the Skull of Beela-Kaar, my friend. Was it really made of gold? Is it truly an Argonian's skull?\n\nRegardless of the curse, the historical significance of such a find is monumental!

I don't want to admit it, but … Narazda's right. I'm turning into one of them.\n\nThere's still hope though. Somewhere within the keep should be ripened belladonna berries. You'll need to collect them if I'm to be cured.
You should speak to Adonatus, yes? There's no telling how long he can hold back the urge to transform.
Apologies if you expected my assistance, but I'm more of a scholar than a warrior. I'll hang back while you clear out the forest ahead.
I can't begin to tell you how proud I am of my daughter. Coming here, risking her life on my behalf … never have I known a stronger soul.\n\nMay her wisdom guide our tribe for generations to come.
A little bird told me you were on your way down here. It also mentioned that you had something that would make both of us very happy.\n\nIs it true? Were you able to acquire the elegant jacket?

You did as this one asked, but you are no longer welcome here. Your presence reminds me of my poor assistant, Argar—may his furless body rest in peace! Please go. This one must compose herself and hire a new helper before the next shipment arrives.
Welcome back, wayfarer. Was your journey successful? Have you acquired one of those beautiful eggs as I requested?
I am grateful the Hist has guided you all to me, but … is this everyone you were able to find?
Are we all that remains? This world is doomed.
This all of us? Huh. \n\nNo matter! Just more vampy faces for me to bash in …! Soon as my head stops spinning.
