The journal and letters we found prove that the Lost Legion met its doom in Tsofeer Cavern. They also reveal that my ancestor led them there in order to protect Murkmire.\n\nAnd more importantly, we used the rite of binding to trap the Wuju-Ka!
Go on, go on. Fast-fast! I'll meet you on the ship.
You heard what I said, right? Kassandra hates to be kept waiting.
I know you are disoriented, but you must try to focus. Native hunting trips, while fascinating, bring us no closer to our goal.\n\nPlease, stay the course.
Please, I've told you everything I know about the woodcut you showed me. You can let me go now, right? I did what you asked.

If you're another one of those Blackguards—and that's the way to pronounce it, not "Black Guards" like that thug insisted it was—then my answer is the same. I've deciphered as much of the woodcut as I can.\n\nNow leave me alone.

Yes, yes, I'm still here. Where could I go, what with your thugs watching me like horned owls regarding a branch full of tree slugs.\n\nSo, what Argonian antiquity do you want me to examine this time?

This Remnant business is serious, isn't it? Well, I can think of no one better to protect it from those Blackguard rascals!\n\nTalk to Kassandra. Maybe she has a plan on how to get between those thugs and the Remnant!
Rescued! That is what they say! Brave, beautiful Zadaza rescued by the new blood. Ziss'vo! Varo will never let this one hear the end of it.

I took a real beating during the fall—leg broke like a dry twig. Want some advice? Don't get old. \n\nHopefully Kirstaleth can patch it up well enough for me to walk. In the meantime, you should be looking for a way out of here. And hey … thanks.

I can't believe we all nearly died in there. Can you imagine? A child of the Green, choked to death in some dusty stone ruin?\n\nAnyway, I'm alive, and I have you to thank. If you ever need a favor, come find me.
It is nice that my betrothed does not have to be disappointed today. We will have a very pleasant bonding, I'm certain.

Was the Tsofeer Cavern as full of ancient wonders as I always imagined? No, don't tell me! I want to be surprised when Varo brings me the items later.\n\nYou should go and talk to Varo. If he authenticates your findings, he'll reward you handsomely.
I hope you see now—I do not exaggerate about the xanmeers.\n\nAre you all right? You are not wheezing or leaking blood from your ears. That is something, at least.

I hope our fortunes are better than the last time we worked together. For both our sakes.\n\nIf you wouldn't mind taking the lead. My crew will be slow with the equipment and the way forward is dangerous. These ice caves aren't uninhabited.
This tablet has lain sundered for ages, eluding everyone who sought its pieces, except me. I'm the first to see it whole in thousands of years. This is history in the making.

To reach Garlas Malatar, we'll need to traverse the crumbling fort below. I was told it was long abandoned, but I was misinformed. It seems the Imperials never left, if you can still consider the things I encountered down there Imperials.
We're clear, for now. Not that we should linger. I need to get the Wrathstone somewhere secure and secluded for proper study. I'm sure you're eager to deposit your own hard earned loot as well.
The dowry is in hand, and the Bright-Throats are none the wiser. My people's custom is met.\n\nSoon I will take my betrothed.
Can I assume that your presence here before me indicates that you found something worthwhile in Tsofeer Cavern?
I raise the spine of gratitude. Thank the Hist that you came along and agreed to save Kishi.\n\nThe swamp would be a darker place if he had been devoured by a hungry predator.
What are we waiting for? Those other suitors may sulk if they wish, but Waku-Mat is ready to bond!
Listen to Kishi and do exactly as he says. And try not to anger the raj-kaal.
Welcome back from the dreaming, beeko. The ritual is prepared. All we need now is the Remnant of Argon.\n\nI see you carry its weight with ease. You truly are a friend to the Hist. And to me.
Mewah-Jez's novices fail because they attempt to use brute force to complete the rite of passage. Listen to my words and we will succeed where they have failed.\n\nTrust me as I trust you.

Hmph. My pride spines bristle.\n\nThe Dead-Water tribe is diminished without a kaal like Jaxsik-Orrn. But I know her place is here. She will lead with strength and wisdom. Perhaps we will finally have a tribe we can trust.
Ayleids … invaders …. Do you see? Do you …?
Haxara stays then. I will help how I can, but I will also be watchful.
Well? Going to help me polish off this mead, or are you too busy for fun?

All done, are we? Let's see if Kyne has answered your call.\n\nYes, I feel her presence within the rune. The goddess has accepted your offer. Now, tell me, where is this organization of yours headed to?
Shouldn't take long to find a venom sac here in Alik'r. The beetles and scorpions out here … let's just say they're hard to miss.
It will be a long time before the tribe accepts them. Even Bright-Throats have limits to their trust. I am hopeful that we will all grow stronger from this ordeal.
Not this way! Not this way! Get to the cauldron, quick!
What are you waiting for? Light the candle! Quick!
Were you able to find the equilibrium sphere? The Soul Gem could become unstable without it and believe me, we don't want that.

See how the Goblins were hoarding this scrap? They were studying it. Given time, I'm sure they would have made some ingenious tools.\n\nOf course, it's far more important to dig up a long dead civilization than observe the birth of a new one.
Are you still looking for Haxara? She hasn't been back since you chased her off last time.
Mateem-who-is-not. At last.\n\nThe sight of you warms my scales. I feared you would not come, but I was wrong to worry. The Hist, in its wisdom, always provides.

Welcome to Lilmoth, friend! Is that a shrewd and discerning gaze I detect? I know a fellow entrepreneur when I meet one!\n\nI'm a financier, you see, and I have an exciting business proposition—if you're interested, of course.

You don't look like you require protection, sharp-tooth. You need something or is this a social call?\n\nAnd if I killed someone you knew, remember that I'm a mercenary. It wasn't personal. It was just business.
Yes? Is there something I can do for you, ojel?
So tell me, friend-partner. Was Captain Jimila impressed? Will she sell my vossa-satls in far-off lands?
I am glad you retrieved my objects. Now we are on to more pressing matters.

By Mauloch, I've got to find a better way to pass the time. I'd have left already, but there's literally nothing to do in Lilmoth but drink, sleep, and scrape mud off things.\n\nI guess watching lizards roll around is better than scrubbing boots.
Easy … easy, now. You're all right. You haven't been out long.
I honored our bargain. Friend-Famia's explorers are free.\n\nIf you seek more information, speak to Jaxsik. You two have a similar temperament, I think.

I shake my head. You think like a Bright-Throat—exposing your soft underbelly to make peace. That sort of thinking may help you in Lilmoth, but it will see you killed in the deep murk.\n\nIf you wish more words, speak to Xukas. He has many to spare.
These Argonians are crazy! Please, you can't let them kill me. I surrendered! I had nothing to do with the abduction of that lizard's people! I swear it!
You dare too much, ojel scum.
Shuxaltsei fought against tides of change longer than we can know, but in the end the old always gives way to the new. May she finally find peace in the Void.
The sacred lily … it represents the hopes and dreams of the Naga-Kur, the Dead-Water.\n\nIt has been too many seasons since the last one was presented to me. And by an outsider, no less.
I'll wait here until you're ready to leave. I give you my word.
I know this is taxing, but please, try to stay attuned to the dream-wallow. These Ayleids—I had no idea they were so savage!\n\nI only see one mural remaining. We should have our answers soon!

How did it feel to claim the sacred lily, ojel? Did your scales quiver and your spines tingle in awe and wonder?\n\nI am grateful that you helped my egg-son. And that you survived to prove my methods.

The novices I saved will need to be trained again before they can walk the Path and complete their rite of passage. And then we must start on the next season of hatchlings that come of age.\n\nOnly a moment as Ka-Deelith and already I am busy!
Thank you for this. She'd thank you too if she could. We saved one.
Surprised you're still standing. Go drool and mutter somewhere else.
I erect my quill of relief. You are back. Good.\n\nEverything is prepared. We only need to place the Remnant with Xukas, and I will begin the ritual to send the souls on their way.
Both of your companions will wish to make this sacrifice. Testament to their great wisdom and your strong example. The choice will not be easy. I leave you to it.
Xukas certainly seems excited about this deep sap. We should probably ask him why, right?
It's not that I bear ill-will toward Haxara's child, but her presence makes my spines quiver.
Why, if it isn't my gallant friend! What brings you to Murkmire? \n\nWait …. Don't tell me you decided to join the Blackguards! Don't you know they're about as rotten as they come?

I have learned much through this ordeal. \n\nIt is not enough to simply read the unmoving letters of books. I must also venture out into the world, and learn from the moving words that my people speak.
Once you have collected the items, travel back to the Xinchei-Konu. I have no doubt my pupil awaits you with bated breath.
Where are you from, Saxhleel? You reek of dryskin, even though I see your scales.\n\nScales or not, outsiders find no welcome among the Naga-Kur. Our tribe is old and set in its ways.
Greetings. Dare I hope you're here to inquire about joining the Mages Guild?
Ah, how swiftly changing fate can be. One season I am a besotted fool, both gifts and hope lost within the swamp. And now here I am, presented with that very opportunity I so desperately craved.

Have you come to learn all you can about egg-tending before you witness our bonding ritual? I'm sure Mimme would be happy to help you. I am soon to begin my watch of the nests and I wish to enjoy the peace and quiet a while longer.

You really want to talk to me? Visitors never want to talk to the egg-tenders! Did you know that we are the only tribe that bonds with other tribes? It may not seem so from the luster of our scales, but it's true!

Varona made it back safely. And Drooler, too! Thanks for going into the swamp to find them. I really appreciate your help.\n\nIn the meantime, I'm going to pamper my wife and help her forget her ordeal. Nothing but the best for Varona!
Hey, you're the Champion of Vivec! I remember you! Did Drooler find you and bring you out here? He's such a good boy!
<<<1>> appears agitated and eager to tell you something.>
You have seen my postings? Word of Xul-Motas staked across Murkmire with dagger and nail. You come for the Death-Hunts?
Ranja is here to open locks, not her mouth. Tharayya is the one to talk to.
Do not worry, Mateem—Uraz will turn up. He probably stopped to gather razor-clams for the feast. always thinking with his belly, you know?
Hurry and find Uraz. The feast is getting cold!
Well done, Mateem. But Uraz is still missing? My trouble-spine quivers.
Have you found Uraz yet? I hope nothing happened to him.

Did you not hear, Mateem? Fat Gixthi awaits!\n\nYou are not stalling, I hope? Do your scales wilt in fear? Well, too bad! I will not have my voh-vastei students curling their tails at the sight of a little wamasu! Bare your fangs!
Why do you hesitate, Mateem? Find the sap-speaker's sacred clutch. Without the blessings of the Hist, this fight will be lost.

I … I think I have to lie down for a moment. \n\nAnd after that, it's off to get the farm back in order. Let's just hope I can honor Keema-Ru's dedication. Elsewise … well, I don't want to think about the elsewise.
So the midge becomes the Rootmender. Impressive. You certainly have proven yourself a capable ku-vastei.
Many thanks, traveler. You have calmed this elder's heart.\n\nI shall await here for your return, of course. And take caution. Hackwings are dangerous creatures, and quick to strike.
Ah, my esteemed beeko! I'm sure you come with good tidings. After all, my claim is as strong as the roots of the Hist!
How fortunate for me that someone capable finally arrived.
You again. Here to tell me the Shadowscale's judgment, are you? Well, let me hear it.
The Blackguard caravan is just north of here. Shouldn't be any issues. Just keep to the edges and stay alert.

The beauty of change is undeniable. The crumbling stone of our foolish past. The sky bleeding red above a setting sun. The bloated face of a corpse as the skin begins to decay.\n\nAh, to gaze upon such wonder.
Choose your words carefully, ojel. An angry war-chief won't do us any good.
It makes no sense. No outsider should have been able to walk the Path, let alone complete it using Bhoki's archaic techniques.\n\nA trick. It must be some sort of trick.
I knew Bhoki's methods would work, I just knew it!\n\nBut let's stay focused. Take the sacred lily and we can complete your rite of passage.

I grew worried after Guhcin told me you left to hunt the Skin Taker. He seems so certain that violence is the only recourse left to us. I don't want to believe that, but with acts so heinous, what other punishment could meet the crime?
Ah! Don't kill me! Or at least make it quick! Not like the others. \n\nPlease. Not like the others ….
I've seen you. Yes, the friend of Xukas. \n\nBeware. The roads surrounding Alten Meerhleel are no longer safe. I keep watch, but I am only one.

Had Jaxsik shown mercy this could have been avoided. You sound like a Bright-Throat. I see some truth in it. Our haste cost the lives of their root-kin. Others as well. Without their forgiveness, a new battle sprouts forth.
Mmm! You have my quartet! Wonderful!
If you find the fool girl, tell her Axdred will be waiting with her knife in Orkey's bloody teeth.
A glade within the swamp, where a first love was formed. A tree it once had, but now it does not. It is gone, just as Tun-Zee is now gone.\n\nA fitting place for his memory to rest.
Ah! The Xukas-friend I hear so much about. Sun's blessings! I see you did not kick your feet clean before entering. Well, no matter. I will clean it up later.\n\nHow can I help you?
Tempers are running hot by that fire. This cold is preferable.
I no longer see the painful emptiness in Haxara's eyes, but is it better to fill the hole in a soul any way you can or live incomplete?
We'll be frozen solid by the time that barmy Breton gets us safe passage.
It's … it's freezing under here … but I think I can feel … feel my mind aligning quite nicely ….

My sorry excuse for a manservant can't even take part in a simple Argonian ritual without one disaster or another befalling him.\n\nWorse, he didn't even get a chance to tell me what happened inside the lodge before he … changed!
Find my poor associate's dead body and get the key to his strongbox. I'll wait here and make sure the renewal charm Lady Laurent is so desperate to get her hands on remains safe and sound.

You! You are the outsider who brought life to the lost village! All of Murkmire owes you a debt of gratitude.\n\nI am surprised that you speak for the loud woman, but my answer remains the same. No ojel has ever witnessed our sacred rite.
Rootmender! Thank the Hist you've arrived to save me.
Xuth! Those damn Blackguards shot me in the ankle. So much for a life as an envoy.
I wish you luck in your ritual, ojel.
An ojel at a renewal rite? I never thought I'd see the day.
I for one will not be part of any ritual of renewal that includes an outsider. The thought is much too scandalous to even contemplate!
Did I hear correctly? That dryskin is going to attend the ritual of renewal?\n\nWell, this ux suddenly got a lot more exciting!
Hunters hunted …. Hurry, beeko. There is much more to see.
Xukas and I have much to talk about. This riddle may dry my membranes, but you have my word as a Bright-Throat that we will see it solved.\n\nSafe journeys, Xukas-friend.

Greetings. I am Kassandra. I regret that it's taken me so long to make your acquaintance. Famia told me all about your heroics in the xanmeer.\n\nSpeaking of heroics, thank you for trying to find our lost explorers. Abducted by Blackguards, were they?
Find her, Mateem. Please.

We sail on the next tide, but there's still enough time to have a few drinks with an old friend.\n\nSit and regale us with tales of your latest exploits! I'm always pleased to see you healthy and alive.
Jaxsik has made her tribe proud, friend-outsider. I assume you had something to do with that. You are like a strong breeze after too many days of still air.
Jaxsik showed strength and courage in the end. She would have made a terrific warrior for the Naga-Kur.
My spines vibrate with building rage. The outsider that interrupts a warrior's training often finds a spear in their side.\n\nBegone, ojel scum!
My insides clench at the sight of you, outsider.
You helped Famia, yes-yes? Sorry I missed all the excitement. \n\nI can hardly believe that you were able to reawaken a Hist. Despite everything else, that is good-good.
I can't believe you got him to agree. Thank you, friend! It's good to see someone with a sense of justice in these swamps.

My gratitude, oh traveler. I thought he would never agree to my changes. Now I can present the story of Murkmire to my people, in a way all will enjoy.\n\nAnd have no fear. I will always respect the heart of these stories.
I will tell this bard our drum beat words, and watch in silence as she turns them into her flower songs. But such a thing? I will not enjoy.
I have nothing more to say to you. Be gone.
Famia told me all about you and how your assistance has been invaluable to her most recent expeditions. Thanks for helping my sister. Cyrodilic Collections owes you a debt, most certainly!
Finally, some justice has prevailed in this dreadful place. If I gave that lizard even one gold piece, it would be one too many!
Beeko, it's so good to see you! Xal-Sisei, it's our friend, they came to see us.
I do not mourn the lost gold as much as my lost pride. Perhaps I should reconsider my line of work ….
You'll find no Sanctuary in this swamp, brother. Murkmire is where the Dread Father takes his meals.
Do not feel pity for the Wood Elf. He had many opportunities to learn, and failed every one.
How wondrous. Now we are stuck with this kuuda for who knows how long!\n\nAt least he does not wish to play teeba-enoo. Even I have trouble remembering the rules to that game.
Don't feel too bad, friend. I can't understand the rules either.
I just can't believe it's true. Kassandra? Working with the Blackguards? I always thought she was a respectable sort. Suppose I was wrong.
Kassandra couldn't really be working with people like the Blackguards, could she? She's been a pillar of Lilmoth since before I got here!
I sense trouble in the air, though I do not know what. Whatever could be happening?
Do you feel that? The roots beneath us grow restless. I can almost hear them whispering ….
There is a threat somewhere in the swamp. I can smell it.
My egg-sister bids me to wait for this trouble to pass. I will listen to her words, though my hands itch to pick up a spear and fight that which threatens us.
If you're here for information on the Ebonheart Pact's war effort, speak to <<1>>. She's recruiting new members at their kiosk just to the south of the docks.
Look at that. A Dominion dimwit has graced me with their presence. Well, why don't you just move along? Because I certainly don't want you here.
As fun as it's been to welcome you to our humble swamp, I'm being called away on business. I'll miss these little talks. Not too much—I have a talent for finding interesting company—but still.
You overstay your welcome here. Leave, and allow my apprentice to return to his lesson.
Go ahead and light the fire.

At last, all is right with the tribe. The winds carry the lovely scents of Hist blossoms and musk-reek upon the air, and soon the chimes of nuptial huts will rattle the night away.\n\nIt's enough to make anyone let out their frills.
I see that you've collected some of the tablets! Keep up the good work. After all, I traveled all the way to Murkmire to see the Xinchei-Konu in its full glory.

So what do you think of Jaxsik and Xukas? They're the best of their tribes, and that's a fact!\n\nYou better get moving though, if you want to find the Remnant fast-fast, before those Blackguard bastards.
New blood! Zadaza thought Famia would be with you. She is unharmed, yes?

Abnur Tharn makes an excellent point. Even this small group is too large. We stand out like a shaved Alfiq.\n\nI will teleport into the palace with Tharn while you and the others use Aneshi's key to gain entry through the crypts.
Nala-do couldn't have done better, five-claw! Now finish the beast!

Hurry along and warn Abnur and the cats. I want to get a sense of what's coming our way. Reconnaissance, it's one of my fortes! That, and counting the number of Dremora that can dance on the head of a pin.\n\nIt's not as many as you might think!
A wounded Dragon is still a danger, friend walker. This one suggests you dispatch it before any more lives are lost.
This one's brother now walks the endless Sands Behind the Stars.\n\nTsazii's sorrow is only eclipsed by the hatred she feels toward the Euraxians.

Ah, five-claw, you are just in time my friend.\n\nSince you recovered the Anequina Dragonhorn from the hidden Dragonguard sanctuary, we have been attempting to figure out what to do with it. So far, its purpose eludes us.
The documents you uncovered allow me to make sense of this unfinished dictation.\n\nI believe I now know the contents of Euraxia's final order.

Surprisingly clever, those ancient Khajiiti. An old tablet, oral histories disguised as fables, and sophisticated triangulant tiles, all pointing to one location—the Halls of Colossus.\n\nThe abhorrent Three Banners War is practically over!
We need to speak quickly. I doubt I'll remain undiscovered for very long.
This one has told you all that he knows about Khunzar-ri and the demon. If you want to hear the tale of Queen Anequina and the Baandari Pedlar, come back later.
Well, let's get on with it. That old relic isn't going to collect itself.\n\nMy Irregulars will stand guard in case any more of Saulinia's Euraxians still want a fight.
May Jone and Jode shine upon you, walker.

Hello? Is someone there? I appear to be back in my head. Well, my other head. The other head. This is so confusing!\n\nAh, wait, wait. Things are becoming clearer now. Ah, yes, well there you are! So good to see you again, my friend!
Something else, traveler? This one thinks that stern old wizard wants to talk to you, yes?
Hmm. That was quick. And no Hadaz, eh?

The Halls of Colossus and a demon weapon! By Jone and Jode, no good can come from any of this.\n\nHrrm. I will help you find the item and make sure Euraxia does not attain it. But then it must be destroyed. That is the only option.
Numaia wishes she could take a break, but stalls need raking, troughs need filling …. A rancher's work is never finished.
Do not hesitate, my friend. Let us collect the Dragonhorn and be done with this place.
May your path be easy and your footsteps sure.

Vazbi has much to do. At the very least, I must find the names of the sick-scarred we left to die in Baan Dar's Litter. If any of their kin remain, they should know what happened here.\n\nI always have a moment for you, though.

The Stricken are the ghosts of my past. Of the Cradle's past. Silhu-jo hoped that time and seclusion might let them heal on their own. But that was always a fool's hope. The sickness made its way to their souls and festered there.
You'll find Vazbi arguing with some old adept. That's where I last left them.
You must leave here, now. The very air is poisonous.

Even now, Abnur Tharn searches through the documents in the royal study, seeking information concerning this final order.\n\nDespite his show of indifference, Euraxia was his half-sister. Her death is bound to affect him. I suggest you tread warily.

Have no fear. I promise to keep the cat safe. We'll meet up with you in the palace before we reach the throne room.\n\nJust watch out for any defensive spells my half-sister may have placed as you make your way through the crypts.

The hero Khunzar-ri was enamored of moon-sugar pies. He loved them! Even defeated the giant Drol by eating four-hundred-and-one in a single sitting! Or was it four-hundred-and-two? The Moon-Singers don't all agree, you see.
Interesting. A magic pendant. I wonder if Khamira would allow me to study it?\n\nAfter she's finished using it, of course.

I always heard that … introspection could be difficult. But meeting yourself … no one likes to discover that they were a tallow-catch.\n\nTry not to … hold it against me. Him and me … we're two sides of a … of a dented coin.

Go, my friend. Help Abnur Tharn determine the significance of Euraxia's final order. He searches the royal study. I must consult with Gharesh-ri about Rimmen's defenses.\n\nHrrm. I dreamed about reclaiming my father's throne for so long, but now ….
That door should lead to a passage that will take us up into Rimmen Palace.\n\nGo on. This one will be right behind you.
We need to proceed cautiously where Zumog Phoom is concerned. He's not only powerful, he's crafty. He won't be defeated as easily as his followers.
Into the sewers, five-claw! And do not mind the smell. It will wash off. Eventually.

Now, despite our daring rescue, I'm certain the magnate doesn't want a member of the Morag Tong hanging about. Though it does look like she's about to make her big announcement, doesn't it?\n\nWell, perhaps I'll stick around long enough to watch.
Where is the fiend? Let me at him! I returned as soon as I could to help you give the Betrayer a good thrashing!
I can't believe it. The founder of Hakoshae … my ancestor … he lied?
Ugh. Just once I'd like to claim an artifact without complication.
This city, Rimmen. I believe I visited this place long ago. It was newer then, not quite as large.\n\nAnd there were definitely fewer Euraxians. I'm almost certain about that.

Through this Proof, you have shown reverence. Well done.\n\nNext is the Proof of Strength. You'll need to … to …. My, I'm sorry. I'm just so tired today. There's been a lot of strange noises at night lately, and I haven't slept very well.

I admit it. Euraxia got the better of me. She enticed me with rumors of a weapon and tricked me into releasing a plague of Dragons upon the world.\n\nAs the Eight Divines are my witness, I will correct this travesty and deal with my half-sister.

Excuse my anger, walker. I am just not used to watching a horde of creatures not seen in a generation descend upon my homeland. It … disconcerts me.\n\nI know you tried to help. No, the fault lies in the Tharn family, damn their eyes.

Bright Moons shine upon you, walker! This one pursued his friend, Zargha, before you arrived. The fool chases a beast's young with a butterfly net and woe unto him when their mother follows the commotion.\n\nPlease, find Zargha before he is eaten.
You have the look of victory about you. Tell me, were you successful?
You've returned! Tell me, what item did you bring?
A safe town, a happy client, and an investigation expertly solved. And a five-claw partnership, if Mizzik does say so himself. What more could this one ask for?
Can't a fella lick himself in peace? Off with you!
Greetings. Say, aren't you the traveler who joined the Proving Festival?
The Betrayer did something to the apparatus. The Moons cannot hear my plea.
The job is done. Maybe we didn't leave the palace with everything Tasnasi promised, but this is the Stitches. If everything went as it should, none of us would be here.
Heard you slew that slab of beef, Cud. You bring me any? I really worked up an appetite on that job.

You can't rob me. Those Avernos already took me for all I've … all I had. Four bottles of cheap wine. That's all I'm worth. You can't take that either. I drank'em. It's all gone now. Everything.\n\nWhen this town hits bottom, I'll be there! Waiting.

"A friend is the only gift that brings joy when returned," or so the Baandari saying goes. Nazdar has never had much to give besides his friendship, but he can attest it is joy he feels seeing you here again.
Salutations! Mell the Musical, at your service. Are you here for a performance?
Go then, and convince Feina-Darak to speak the truth. Only that will save her.

I suppose the quality of service will have to go up now that Tasnasi's in charge, but it's a small price to pay for a leader with some panache. She's no Dashing Dasalzo, but she's got a certain charm. Any charm at all is a step up from Khasda.
Someone killed Khasda? That's a shame. He promised to show me his dungeon last time he was here … though I'm not sure he meant it how I took it. Summerset wine goes straight to my head.

This one smells meat wafting on the wind. It is not an odor he would call beefy, but he thinks it may be the trail they were following.\n\nHaduras will keep his eyes on these ones, so they may keep their eyes.
You got the Akaviri relics!\n\nDid the spirit speak to you?

I told you, did I not? First time was a warning. Now, it is a threat.\n\nYou both leave town. No more investigations, no more sticking your snouts where they don't belong. Collect your things and leave.
It was me the whole time! Are you surprised? I was surprised.
Yes? Any news of this one's Zinthia?

Ha! Come to your senses, eh? Don't worry, Sarazi won't tell anyone that you ran away. Predator Mesa is not for everyone. Now, watch a true hunter take—\n\nWait. Is that blood on your hands? Where did all this blood come from?
My hero returns with the dread Burtle in tow!\n\nSurely, the creature is under some powerful spell. Your magicks astound even me!

Five-claw, thank you for responding to my summons. Despite our many accomplishments, I cannot shake this sense of impending doom.\n\nMoons! We overthrew Euraxia, defeated the Betrayer, and even killed at least two Dragons. Why do I feel such unease?
This one has nothing more to say to you. Leave me be or I will summon the guards!
Let us speak after you have opened this cage, yes?
Go, walker! We will hold them for as long as we can!
Daedra are tricky beasts, and none are eager to be trapped inside a gem. Keep your weapon at the ready.
Did my blood-sister beg you to hunt me, walker? Has she grown too weak to do it herself?

Remember, my friend, I am not the battlemage I once was. I need to reserve what magic remains to me for when it will do the most good.\n\nConsequently, if we run into any obstacles, I'm going to leave them for you to deal with.
Gharesh-ri still breathes, but his injuries are serious. He needs a healer.\n\nIn the meantime, Zamarak knows what he must do.

Like most of Abnur Tharn's plans, it is both brilliant and daring. If it has any chance to succeed, however, we need a way to get a small force into the palace without being seen.\n\nLuckily, I may have an answer.

I'd prefer if we had another cohort or two at our disposal. Facing a Dragon is no small task, and a horde of them … well, that's just excessive.\n\nStill, the Cygnus Irregulars will stand with you. Whatever the outcome.
Bright moons, you're back! Not that I had any doubts, mind you.\n\nSo? Success? Did you find Marzula-jo's notes and memory stones?
So, Arum-Khal wasn't beyond redemption after all. That's heartening.\n\nIf a creature like the Dark Adept can rediscover the light, perhaps other lost souls can do the same.
Best hurry! You're going to miss the show!

You and Cadwell, the two of you just can't leave well enough alone.\n\nNo one was supposed to notice as I slipped out of Rimmen. Of course, very little has gone according to plan since the Wrathstone tablets set me on this path.
Zamarak cannot wait to see Khamira formally recognized as our queen. It is a proud day for Anequina, my friend.
Our brave warrior will follow your lead. Fight well and be careful. It does us no good if our recruits are harmed during your demonstration.\n\nShould you become separated, return to me.
Just one more thing, five-claw. If you are ready to receive another accolade, I have one more honor to bestow upon you.

Ah, walker, good tidings and heartfelt salutations! Dagaril-dro wonders what brings you to this serene location. This one rarely receives visitors.\n\nWait, wait. Something smells delicious, yes? Do you, perhaps, carry dusk mushrooms in your pack?

My children. Did you see them? Shando-ri never lost faith, as I did. He did not give in to fear or doubt even as the stones fell around us. Arum-Khal … my boy.\n\nBe gentle, Khenarthi. Be merciful, Azurah. My children are coming home.
It was a real pleasure watching you work, hero. I thought those Bonechime poachers would have cooked up at least one of our furry friends, for sure.\n\nThanks, mate. We owe you one.
Walker, this one remembers you from her dreams. Your face. Your voice. Two Moons guiding her through the fog.\n\nSizenza cannot repay you enough for this.
Sharp claw, Haduras is glad to see you kept your wits about you. This one thought he too would lose his mind, while keeping the priests from getting into trouble. It was like trying to herd mice.

You … you followed? Azurah be praised. My failure may not doom us after all.\n\nI hesitated, sword-wielder. Despite all the years, all the sorrows. I still thought I could save him. Now, he prepares to reconstitute himself—to escape once again.
Has that tunnel always been there?
How could Kideya have been so blind!\n\nYou and Razum will go into the tunnel, yes? Find whoever has been stealing our moon-sugar and make sure they never do so again.
Quite the investigation, yes? We infiltrated a heavily patrolled farmstead, saved three beautiful damsels, and dismantled a skooma operation.\n\nAll in all, not a bad day's work.
Thank you, thank you! Moons be praised that you have come in our hour of need, brave rhook.

Why, you certainly have a lot of eyes. And they're different colors, too. Fancy that.\n\nWould you mind untying me? Itchy, itchy, and I just can't scratch. Don't know why Saevus tied me up. He's a mean, mean mage.
Thank you, I don't know if I could have subdued Quintus without your help. He always did pick fights at the worst time.
If I may be so bold, you match the description I was given. I have a message to deliver to you. If that's all right.

Ah, there you are. Now, to business.\n\nAbout your idea for a parley with Euraxia. I sent word to Rimmen to expect our imminent arrival. I imagine my half-sister will treat us as befits my station and agree to a civilized meeting.

Thank you, wayfarer. I would fight at your side, but I fear one of those beasts poisoned me. I would only get in the way.\n\nMy ally, Morgane, carried a sending stone. If you can find her body, we can use the stone to communicate. Onsi guide you.

If we've had this conversation already, then I wanted to thank you for the useful advice. But if I haven't seen you since our talk at that mysterious gravestone, which seems much more likely, then I could really use your help.
Damn us for arriving too late! I did not expect to find our militia under assault by a horde of undead, and then the Dragon—\n\nIt tangles the tail, walker, it truly does.
I heard what the Dragon said. Perhaps my confidence was a bit misplaced. That creature was much bigger than it appeared when it flew over the camp.
Mulaamnir wanted to thank you, little morsel. Your actions helped set us free of our hated prison.\n\nNow, listen to the words I say.

Tharn and Nala-do gave me their accounts of the attack on the outpost. Dragons, undead, Euraxia's soldiers. Our foes seem as numerous as grains of sand in the desert.\n\nTharn and I have discussed options, but we have not settled on our next move yet.
Show us the way, Moon-Bishop! Step out into Khenarthi's arms and reach the stars!

Thank you for saving Ma'jha-dro's disciples. You have a courageous spirit. It will do you well, should you decide to stay in Elsweyr. And this one does hope you decide to stay. \n\nThe Khajiit need heroes like you during these dark times.

My half-sister. She's not only an embarrassment to our family name, she's the reason we're up to our shoulders in Dragons and shambling corpses! The time has come to deal with Euraxia.\n\nPermanently.
Well, that's an experience I won't be adding to my memoirs. \n\nWe'll separate here. Make it harder for Euraxia's lackeys to follow us.

So you're Abnur Tharn's bodyguard and valet? Not what I expected.\n\nI assume you want to follow your master into the queen's inner sanctum, hmm? I'll allow it. But first, I want to gauge the measure of your marrow.
Well, it looks like you've certainly recovered from your wounds. And just in time to put that Euraxian jekosiit in his place!\n\nZiss'vo, is this one grateful we found you in that wreckage.
I will happily offer you a reward if you can find my lost item.
My sources indicated that my half-brother's associate was somewhat … taller. Ah, well.\n\nNow, why in the world should I even consider negotiating with members of the losing side?
We must rebuild Star Haven. What would Elsweyr do without it?
What has happened here? Who killed the Grand Adept?
Please, do not worry about me. I am a very fast runner.
I will be vigilant, yes? I will be very, very vigilant.
Don't worry about me, rhook. Even without my bow, I still have claws.
Rajhin had a feeling you would see things his way.
Please, go on ahead. This one needs but a moment to catch her breath.
Let us hope that this mural inspires all of Elsweyr to come together, just as the sixteen kingdoms came together long ago.\n\nWe need that unity, now more than ever.
At last, the House of Histories can flourish!\n\nOur patrons will be many, our reputation fragrant. And, most importantly, the gold will start flowing in! Oh, I can already picture it.
So, you've heard the details. Still interested in lending a claw?

You must not have a fear of vampires to have wandered so close to this den of leeches. If you have quarrel with the Hollowfang clan, know I am not your enemy.\n\nIn fact, I could use some of that bravery right now.
I have lost another comrade today, but I have gained many more. It has been my honor to fight alongside you.
I confess, I didn't think our luck would hold there in the end, but Z'en was watching over us today. You too. I don't believe this plan could have been successful without you.
These are dark days for the temple, but we shall heal in time. That is another of Alkosh's gifts. Through him we learn and grow.
This is a pure house of Alkosh now. This one swears it upon her soul.

Hop in my cart when you are ready for the journey and I will take you to Priestess Shalani. Though, it would behoove me to depart with a full cart.\n\nPerhaps you'd help Natrada gather more faithful? A dozen would do, but she will take you either way.

Saviwa just woke up from his best nap in weeks! You got rid of that nagging jeek, didn't you? Did you decide to just kick his urn off a cliff?\n\nSaviwa won't tell anyone if you just decided to kick his urn off a cliff.
Jora-ri appreciates your efforts, but this is not where he belongs. We should keep moving before the cultists find other uses for my urn.
Zamarak remembers Khamira's pendant. Her mother, Queen Numara, wore it before she gave it to her daughter.\n\nThis one did not know it possessed such an enchantment, though.
Hurry to Riverhold. Find this Tharn. Meanwhile, Zamarak must go to the Desert Wind adepts. This one needs to make sure his old master knows about the Dragon threat.\n\nSafe travels, walker.

I'm just here to count my gold and catch up with an old business associate. I may have procured the tablet that Tharn is referring to, but that's where my role in this affair comes to an end.\n\nTalk to Tharn if you want to know more.
You'll want to find another place to rest your feet, stranger. The Stitches are about to burst. It won't be much longer before the whole place unravels, as it were.

Kaalgrontiid? It seems that even Mulaamnir answers to a higher authority.\n\nAs for Khamira, she continues to surprise me, though I knew she was hiding something. But what are you waiting for? Use the ballista. And try not to miss.
Tears of joy, my friend! Once Khamira arrives, this small stream will become a raging river. And Honor, he's even more emotional than me!
Pardon my intrusion, but I have another message to deliver to you. And if you don't mind my saying so, it's good to see you again.

The losses we suffered at the Defense Force outpost were devastating, but we aren't done yet. The documents you recovered from the ruins of the camp provide options and access to allies, should we need to call upon them.

Ah, five-claw. Good, good. This one saw what you did. The Dragon never stood a chance!\n\nLyrrsazhi can shower you with praise later. Right now, the war council is eager to get on with things. They await you in K'har Zhab Hall in Riverhold.
Well, not sure what a Pact rootarse is doing in Elsweyr. Don't you have some more battles to lose somewhere else?

Ugh. Whatever that witch did to her blade, it's working. This wound won't fade easily. She's robbed me of my friend and the strength to stop him myself.\n\nMuch as it galls my pride, you must go on without me. Stop Grundwulf however you can.
Thank you for saving Marthine. May Peryite bless you with a parcel of plague-soaked pillows.
I'm starting to wonder if that deranged cultist might be right about sickness consuming all of Tamriel. Maybe we really should be worshiping the Daedric Prince of Pestilence.
We could always use more supplies. Who knows how long we'll be trapped in this foul city.
Let us know if you find new supplies. We'll need them whether we make it out of the city or not.

I know you. I saw you through the Soul Shriven's eyes. You were with the fool who thinks himself the shining knight of Cyrod.\n\nIf only he knew what a monster I was. The horrors of Coldharbour pale before my heinous deeds!
Everyone says the farmhands are just leaving, but why haven't any of them said farewell? Why do they leave their possessions behind?\n\nThere's something in the sugarcane. Shazari knows it.
If you're looking for help, feel free to speak to my sister. As magnate of this town, she's the best one to answer any questions you may have.
Did you hear that Razum-dar is back in town?\n\nOh, it's been years since Majadhi saw him. And now he's back, handsomer than ever! This one didn't even think it was possible.
I remember you from Summerset! Peryite must have sent you!
Where is Khamira? I expected her to be eager to hear my proclamation.
This is my first royal coronation. I hope it isn't as long and complicated as the Imperial ceremonies I've read about.
This is it, five-claw! Now that those two are dead, nothing bars your path to the chancel.\n\nBe Alkosh's mighty retribution against the fraud in fool's gold scales!
B—begone from my temple!

The healers were able to do wonders, my friend. I almost feel like my old self again. I will secure Khamira's claim. You just stand beside her and support her. She values your presence. As do I.\n\nBut where is Khamira? I expected you to bring her in.

This brew is my own invention, if you can believe it!\n\nYou see, the Khajiit aren't typically fond of rotmeth. I think the rancid meat smell is what turns them off. That's why I added plenty of moon-sugar to my brew! It's sure to be a hit now.
So, you found our keg of rotmeth. And even decided to return it! How generous of you.
Well. This is awkward.
You were fortunate Tu'heiba was in a generous mood. Do not presume this means we are friends, outsider. Now go.
You are lucky Daibiza only chases down clawless jeeks, like your friend, Jakarn. You may wish to leave Rimmen before this one changes her mind.
You should speak to your friend. Who knows how this will turn out?
Please, walker, the key!\n\nFez'skar can barely feel his legs. Also, he really, really needs to pee!
You cut a striking figure, walker. There are—ah, you again. How goes your holy work?
Ah, five-claw. Alas, Lyrrsazhi has no message for you.\n\nFurthermore, Lyrrsazhi should point out that small talk is not this one's specialty.
Please, walker! You must bring our animals back. If we wait too long … Mara's mercy, Bizaku does not want to think of the consequences!
Ziss on those poaching shaveskins! Tamanat will not let this ranch burn!
I tried to stop them. Truly! There were just too many of them.
I'll … I'll be all right. Just rescue our animals. Please.
Do you hear that yowling? It's got to be Milksop. Let's hurry!

You just missed the festivities, walker. Nothing left. Though if you wait around for a bit, perhaps that five-claw stranger will come back.\n\nWait. You don't want to go to the hideout, do you? Qa'jahd isn't sure he's fit to steer.
We're about to head out on a trading mission heading for the glorious city of Rimmen in golden Anequina! You interested in coming, walker?
You look as good as moon-sugar. Careful, or Tajirri might lick you!

Rigurt could not have completed his diplomatic mission without your help, friend. Rigurt is externally grateful and will return the lute and drum to the Screaming Mammoths so you can go about your business.\n\nAfter Rigurt plays with them some more.
Thadarra isn't surprised that Rigurt's package arrived in Riverhold by mistake. The attached note looks like it was written by a drunken mudcrab.
Asaldak understands why you would want to approach him, but he only signs autographs at special events, and he only talks to his admirers at … actually, he never talks to his admirers.
The chest is unlocked. Anyone who's tried to open it without our permission has had their face caved in by Ghamokh. He earned the surname Skullchucker.
Unfortunately, the Screaming Mammoths are temporarily unable to perform.\n\nPlease check back again once they've had a chance to get some rest, and ponder their poor life decisions.

Lady Izza thanks you for aiding Rigurt in his—diplomacy. This one suspects that things would have gone far worse were it not for you.\n\nNow, please present the honorary collar and bell to Rigurt. He has earned it.

That was as brain-bashingly entertaining as I'd hoped! I've always said that everything is better with exploding heads.\n\nYou have to use this hammer in the Three-Banners War. I might finally be able to watch an entire battle without falling asleep.
You got rid of the wasps and you found Gordon! Hadamnargo can't tell you how happy this makes his horse.\n\nDid you run into any trouble?
You smell much better than before, walker. Did you bring something good for Sanzagh?
Hngh … ah! Still no thumbs.\n\nJust quit tempting me with cream when I can't drink it!
Have you found one of my master's treasures?\n\nHe's always interested in reclaiming what is rightfully his.
Get away! Go, fancy-face, or I bite you! Go!

I watched you go from location to location, just like the man with the pot on his head!\n\nAre you one of the soldiers intent on digging up every plot of land? Or are you simply a deviant who enjoys skulking and slinking through the wilderness?
If Dragons can be blinded with forks in our eyes, perhaps if we sink them further we can dig out the Dragon's brains as well!
Haduras says we are on a fool's errand! If we were all so blind we would need no forks at all!
"Don't touch the dead thing," Thaeduna tells me. Like I don't know how to handle a Daedric corpse!\n\nI wonder what killed it, though? Maybe it ran afoul of a Dragon?
Bahzdal has been confined in Rimmen for far too long. He needs open fields to stretch and run! Instead he is forced to walk crowded city streets.
Greetings! It is good to see another traveler. Please! Come join us for a few moments. We would love the company.

Ah, yes, another traveler not of the Khajiit. I hope you fare better than the people of Elsweyr have of late.\n\nBy chance, would you care to know more about my kind, the Alfiq? I am happy to share, if only to prevent further … misunderstandings.
I have a potential surprise for you!
Another traveler, eh? Perhaps Raiffi can provide you with knowledge that helps further your understanding of the Khajiit?
Yeah, I see you there, sizing me up. Never seen a Pahmar-raht before?\n\nOh, wait. You're going to ask me questions now, aren't you? Go ahead. Far be it for me to deny you your questions. To a point.
When Euraxia took over Rimmen, she did not wish to keep Khajiiti nobles like this one around.
Dark rumors of necromancy in Elsweyr drew me out of my home to find those who need help. Be watchful, walker.
Blast! I left the war and strife of Cyrodiil for the relative calm of Riverhold. But now Dragons? Dragons! Was I cursed as a child?
The queen has been anxious since you and the others left to deal with Zumog Phoom. She's waiting to hear what happened.\n\nI suggest you report to her immediately.
Pinumar once lived in Star Haven, a beautiful adeptorium with many wonderful adepts. But a Dragon came and attacked our home, leaving much to rebuild and no comfort to be found.
The cries of the falling Moons will haunt this one to his grave.
I have seen the Dark Elves' living gods. I assure you, they pale in comparison to true divinity!

What an amazing coincidence, meeting you here like this! How are you, my cherished friend? I haven't seen you since we put a crown on the head of that beautiful cat lady, Khamira.\n\nSpeaking of crowns, did you happen to see where I placed my hat?
Greetings, walker. You are not also going to the Abode of Ignominy, are you? As its name implies, it is a moonless place full of forgotten secrets.
Hey, you came! Did the Ruddy Fangs still have my things?
I try to be a gentle-orc and help a lady in need, and what does it get me? A lecture on Akaviri artifacts and a magical talking voice.
A pity you could not incapacitate the Dragon. No matter what the Wood Elves think, Maarselok would have been an invaluable asset for the advancement of civilization.
Hoo, glad that's over. Not sure I could have taken much more of Selene sucking the life out of me. I mean, I let her, but I was sure I was going to die during that last bout!
They can tug and tear all they like. I will not submit to Elf, Dragon, or Man!
We need to hurry and find the wounded Dragon. The tremors grow worse with every passing moment and I fear we're running out of time.
It appears you were as successful as I. Did your tomb contain anything of note?
No time like the present, yes? Let's head into the temple.
Za'ji claims you seek to save Elsweyr, yes? Tadali doesn't believe anything that comes out of that insolent cub's mouth, but you should not be judged for his failings.\n\nWhy have you come here?
You're traveling with Za'ji? Then I'm going, too. I wouldn't want him to get into any trouble now that he's an official member of the Dragonguard.
I suspect the Dragon cult seeks something more important than limestone, but what could it be?

Hinzurr found you? Good, good. I've studied the journals we discovered and the path ahead is clear. We must enter the lair of the Dragon Vahlokzin in Southern Elsweyr and retrieve the Horn of Ja'darri.
Finding Yahgrondu requires a test of skill rather than mere bravery. I am curious to see how you and your companions fare.

I think I will leave the investigation of the cultist stronghold to you and the sour old men, five-claw.\n\nI want to find out more about the situation in Pellitine from your Dragonguard companions. They are locals, yes?

I'll gather the Dragonguard as long as you and Tharn keep your heads low. Go to the island and find a way to take down its defenses. Then wait for us to arrive.\n\nNo unnecessary heroics. Not with Tharn in such a weakened state.
As an instructor at the Abbey of Blades, I cannot follow Sai into battle.\n\nI know that my student will rally warriors to his cause. He has a way of bringing out the best in others.
There is so much to accomplish and so little time to do it. I sound the call to arms and organize our forces. If we must face Laatvulon, we have to know who and what we have on our side.
You're going to help my sister save Vijari? You are a kind one, walker. Khenarthi keep the wind at your backs.

Vijari sees you clearly for the first time. He is glad to know your face before he journey's onward. Vijari will paint it for Khenarthi in the Sands Behind the Stars and beg her to repay your kindness.

The Dark Aeon. So that was the approaching darkness I sensed.\n\nNow tell all these lesser creatures to stop exuding the scents of frightened furry rodents. The smell gives me a pain behind my right eye.
My dearest friend, you must take your place alongside the rest of the Dragonguard. The ceremony cannot begin until all of those I wish to honor are accounted for.
When Anequina and Zar reached this point, we decided to celebrate behind that rock over there. Our companions were mortified, but we are Khajiit, yes? How could we help ourselves?
Are you ready, my friend? One last leap into Oblivion?\n\nWe'll finish this. Of that, I'm certain.
At last, the Horn of Ja'darri! Now we finally have a chance against this Dragon threat.
Could the Horn of Ja'darri truly be a gift from a Dragon? Vahlokzin said it was a Dragon's horn, willingly given … but for what purpose?\n\nAh, well. Perhaps I'll learn more in due course.

I doubt my father can point us directly to a recruiter, but he will know if the cult has been active in the city. Anything he can tell us will help.\n\nI'll meet you in Senchal, in front of the palace. After I take a moment to compose myself.
We need to learn more about Laatvulon's plans and this cult of his.
It sounds like Queen Khamira has made some progress. Talk to her and find out if she can get us to Dragonhold.
I'd consider it a personal favor if you find Lahini and return her to her family. I wish I had the resources to do more.
If we're to fight back against Laatvulon, we'll need more than a single Dragon. We'll need an order dedicated to eradicating this threat.\n\nThe time has come to reform the Dragonguard.
Can't you see that I'm trying to drink away my sorrows? It's an extremely delicate process, you know. Doesn't require company.
Whether writ or will or waiver, Darkhu is your savior! Tell this one, what need have you of the finest forger in all of Senchal?
Who would have thought that Senchal of all places would have customs? I'll never make my appointment at this rate!
Apologies, walker, if we've concerned—wait … you were one of the saviors of the Temple of Seven Riddles, yes? Adara'hai is glad to see you still standing tall against the darkness.
Unless you have cargo for this one to inspect, be on your way. He has no time for idle chatting.
Is he giving you trouble?

Thank you, walker. If we can find something valuable in the wreckage, Daini can use it to pay for her passage out of South Guard.\n\nI know how this looks, but I swear my brother Safik and I only want to escape this place and the jeeks who ruined it.
Safik is very glad to see you, walker. Go … cut Daini down first.
So, it's a warehouse raid now, is it? Shor's bones …. Well, you'd best get to it. Don't do anything stupid, eh? I mean, this whole raid is stupid, but you know what I mean.
Quickly, walker. Into the boat, yes?
I feared the worst, but praise Jone and Jode, Tharn still lives!
Leki's blade, Za'ji smells like a keg pulled out of a tavern fire! Please let this go well ….
Za'ji is not drunk! How dare San Sihan make such an insituation!
If the captain embarrasses me in front of Queen Khamira, I am going to bite his head off.
Look at all the people! And they turned out for us! I can hardly believe it!
If you find Lahini, please convince her to come home. We're all worried about her.
Happy hunting! Za'ji will see you back at the sanctum.
We also heard that the Dragonguard have returned—and led by Sai Sahan himself!\n\nI wonder if the Irregulars would make the cut? We've battled a Dragon or two since agreeing to Queen Khamira's terms.

Zamarak still cannot believe you are here, five-claw. Still, if this one wasn't close enough to protect the queen, Zamarak is glad that you were.\n\nNow, this one must see to the queen's luggage. She will want to look royal for what comes next, yes?
I suggest we make our way to the gardens and attend the queen's ceremony. If we're late, Aeliah's apt to use us as target practice!
Hey, if you find Lahini … tell her to come back, all right? I may be mad, but I don't want to see her get hurt.
We're off to Senchal, in Southern Elsweyr. Fancy a trip?

So you're a companion of the infamous Captain Sai Sahan. Though I suppose that title no longer means anything, given the current state of Cyrodiil.\n\nWell then. Care to share how you plan to slay this Dragon?

I heard what happened from the crew. I'm glad you were there to help recover the Pounce. I don't think Za'ji would have handled the loss of his ship very well.\n\nSpeaking of Za'ji, did he agree to sail you to the island?
That map will lead you right to the robed walker! It's a fine map. You're welcome!\n\nNow where in Oblivion is Ranza's drink?

So both Aeliah and Caska have joined your hunt, eh? Two beautiful sweetmeats, willing to fight by your side! Ah, there's no better way to leap into battle.\n\nNot that Caska needs to know this one called her a sweetmeat.
When you find the New Moon Fortress, show the guard your pendant. It will grant you entry.
It seems the little one has come aboard. Why don't you see what she has to say?
Please, do not delay. Save the others.\n\nI will hold out as long as I can, but eventually Turo will tire of hurting me. Then …. Just hurry, walker.
Under the light of the New Moon, we shall find salvation. But only if you are found worthy.
Off with you, now! You cleared the way. I'll make it out of here just fine.
This one was surprised to see Vijari up and about today. He had not left his home in many days. Perhaps he is on the mend?
Bad omens. Bad omens all around. They are drawn to this house like moths to flame.
This one has worked his paws raw plucking weevils and slugs from his precious vegetables and yet every hour he finds more. Never has he seen so many bugs trying to spoil his crop!
Hail, O warrior. \n\nBlademaster Sai Sahan requests your presence at the Abbey of Blades.
Well, that was an adventure. Of sorts. Thank you, walker. Truly, we would never have made it out of that place alive without you.
Bahzahar's stench is unmistakable. He's locked himself in this chamber. Probably has his loot nearby, too. Hopefully, that includes the bell.\n\nWe just have to figure out how to get inside.
Safik has no idea how to sail a vessel that size, but he will do his best to do his part!\n\nThey say the surest way to a sailor's heart is through the belly, yes? And no one makes soups like Safik!
We're all done here, right? I'm anxious to put South Guard far behind me. Scenery's great, but the locals stink! Present company excluded, of course.
Mother always did have a flair for the dramatic. The bell's just a little dirty, that's all.
This aeonstone absorbs and enhances magical energy?\n\nBy Leki's Blade, that sounds grim. A sizable Dragon cult capable of empowering their Dragon gods.

Portal magic. I have never been impressed by what spews forth from such puerilities.\n\nThis time, however … one smells of old power and approaching death. The other of moonlight and ancient spirits. Interesting.
Bebbia did not realize you were so famous! It seems restoring Khajiit of the Moons was just a simple errand for one such as you. This one is a little embarrassed to have troubled you.
It's no surprise Lahini ran off with someone else. Hard enough to share a drink with Kazahn, much less a bed.
Are we in?
The heart … it pounds! Or is that his own?

Well, Ja'darri has spoken. Only one hero can claim the mask, and that hero seems to be you. Which makes complete sense, of course! You have done the lion's share of these trials.\n\nI'm just glad I could help you get this far.
It couldn't be. The Red Beast?
That's the raiment of the queen of Rimmen? It seems to lack a certain … something.
I have no quarrel with you, hunter. Nor with the mortals of Elsweyr. I only came to this land to kill Laatvulon.
It would be best to speak with Nahfahlaar and see what he has in mind. I want you to do your utmost to help him.
Well. You sure know how to stay out of trouble, don't you?\n\n'Course, we'd all be dead five times over if you didn't keep sticking your nose into things.
Tadali will pray for Bright Moons, Dragonguard. You could certainly use them.
Good, you're here. Sai Sahan has been glowering even worse than Nahfahlaar since he got that letter.\n\nHe wants to speak with you. Something about a new threat.
Za'ji knew his gut was right! Only a truly great warrior could tame a Dragon.\n\nDo you suppose the creature will let us ride it? Hmm. No, no, best not to ask. This one would not want to be rude.

Our mysterious crew has departed. Those left alive to depart, that is.\n\nThey were Dragon cultists, yes? It would certainly explain their choice of garb. This Laatvulon must have an affinity for black.

I can't believe we're in a Dragonguard sanctuary.\n\nMy father would tell me stories about the order when I was little. Protectors of the emperor, slayers of Dragons, daring adventures! It was all quite exciting.
Wha-? No, no, no. Zurnash cannot talk now. Dany things to moo … many things to do, I mean. Wait … what was this one supposed to do?
Shazar has never seen such a tsunami of spew! Surely it was a sobering experience, but you've spared Moonlit Cove a similar fate.
You want to enter the arena? Convince Caska to join you. That's the only way you're getting in.

Marekki looks forward to showing Skordo all of Elsweyr. Rimmen especially.\n\nIf he marvels at an Alfiq, just imagine how he will react to a Senche-Raht! The only Khajiit gruffer and tougher than he is, yes? Ha!
Aren't you the one who faced off against the Dragon in Moongrave Fane? We could really use your help with another that threatens Elden Root!

I heard about what you did in Moongrave Fane. We could certainly use some of that fearlessness. There's a Dragon blighting the Green and I'm not so sure about Allanwen's current plan. Maybe you could make it … more feasible?

Excellent fighting out there, Dragonguard. Of course, your work isn't done. There remain plenty of Dragons for your order to slay. \n\nBut I swear to you, from here on, that the Shields of Senchal will aid you however we can.
If you come to share a meal, we do not have much. Talk to Safik, yes?
Who're you? Not one of Turo's thugs, are you? Nah. Not ugly enough.
Well met, warrior. Do you seek peace as well? Whenever I'm feeling anxious, I like to come here and meditate.
If the subject comes up, let Nahfahlaar know that he's welcome to recover in our sanctum. He's our ally and the Dragonguard takes care of its own.
I have a plan that could give me the best of both worlds, Wrothgar and Elsweyr! I just have to convince my uncle to go along with it.

You must raise the Mask of Alkosh before him. Do not think, feel. Cast doubt from your heart and ready yourself to accept Alkosh's divine will. \n\nYou must succeed where Ja'darri failed, mask-bearer. You must slay Laatvulon.
Shor's bones … did the Skald-King send you? He must know what's going on here. He must!
You … you did it. You killed Kjalnar.\n\nI should have been at your side. My blade should have struck the mortal blow.
What? Haven't you ever seen a Wood Elf before? I know I'm still learning my trade, but the armor I craft isn't half bad.\n\nFor a Wood Elf.
You walk with purpose, hunter. What hastens your steps?

I can't tell you how grateful I am for your assistance.\n\nA woman in my position can't afford to fall asleep at state dinners. And my mother … she should be resting peacefully in Aetherius, not calling out for help from beyond the grave.

Thank the Eight you're back.\n\nDid you destroy all three totems? I pray you did. I already feel the binding ward loosening. If we dispel the magics on the locket, our souls should find peace at last!
Welcome to the finest inn and tavern in Senchal. It's also the only inn and tavern in Senchal.
Perhaps I didn't make myself clear. Find Zurnash and make sure Auberic Dufont gets his token. Do that, and we can talk.

Greetings. As Selloe clumsily pointed out, I am Lady Ghisiliane. It seems I have you to thank for settling this business with Auberic Dufont.\n\nTell me, what payment do you require? And what do you have planned for your scowling, green friend there?
So, now that you know the particulars, do you wish to provide your services?
I can feel the fog lifting. Mara's mercy, what a relief.
Was that a saucy retort? From Nahfahlaar? How dare the Dragon encroach on Za'ji's forte!
We don't have time to mourn them. All these priests, their bodies left to rot.\n\nLaatvulon wants to rule a kingdom of corpses, and he's succeeding.
There you are! Captain Za'ji told us to watch for you. People want to talk to you. Important people, you understand?
Congratulations on the win, mask-bearer. Just do not brag about it, yes? I get enough of that from Za'ji.

We did it. Senchal is finally safe from Laatvulon and the Order of the New Moon.\n\nThere are other Dragons to contend with, of course. But we'll defeat those too, won't we? Just like the Dragonguard of legend.
Za'ji knew we could do it! There was never a doubt in his mind.\n\nAfter all, we are the Dragonguard, right? The scourge of Dragons far and wide!
Should all go well, you'll have the privilege of fighting at Ra'khajin's side. A great honor, I assure you.
You have given this one an important task, yes? Leave me to do it.
This one thinks we will get a much better price for the gourmet moon-sugar in Senchal than we would have in Rimmen.
You would find Vigwenn's lost ingredient bottles? Oh, thank you, stranger! I promise to make a new batch with those ingredients so that you can experience the joy of the sand-whales personally!
Thank you for bringing Tender Claw home. But tell me, did that little thief steal anything from you?
Come on now. I'm never going to get through these if you keep interrupting me. If you're feeling chatty, go bother Chizbari.
A magical plot with a mysterious and powerful ally. Hmph. Looks like this axe has a few more necks to cleave.
Looking for more tips, eh? Well I haven't got any left to give. Sorry, mate.\n\nGood luck out there, though. And mind the birds!
I'm sorry, but I can't talk right now.\n\nMy beloved J'saad should have returned from his travels days ago. With every passing moment, I fear for his safety.

My friends must be hiding around the quarry. Find them and let them know I'll be waiting at the rendezvous spot.\n\nThey're Argonians like me. You can't miss them. Look for Meetza, Falls-with-Grace, and Nasee. And please, watch out for those cultists!
Please, I didn't take any of the green stones. And … and if I did … I'll make sure to put them back!\n\nJust please, don't hurt me.
I cannot run any more. There's too many of them and my friends are gone.\n\nI … I surrender. Go ahead, cultist. Do what you may.
Be quick, be careful, and be discrete.\n\nOh, and don't worry about the Shields. They're some of my best customers.

I know I should pay, but we don't have anything left. We only have each other, and even that won't last much longer.\n\nTell the herbalist he can have my life if that's what it takes. My daughter needs the medicine.

You could have made the deliveries faster, but at least you completed them.\n\nI hope you didn't ask poor old Tildri for payment. That woman has been through enough. I've punished more than a few couriers for taking advantage of her situation.
What has Janessa done this time? Did she shred your curtains and pillows in a wild binge? If she bit anyone, I assure you she carries no diseases, other than a chronic lack of shame.

Chores! This is almost as bad as the time I woke up in some old lady's junk shop and she tried making me wear these ugly old doll clothes. She did not care for my backtalk and tossed me in the basement with a dozen other Khajiit stuffing packages.

Pirates to the south, raiding this one's galleys for gold. Cultists to the north, burning this one's villa in the name of their forsaken gods. Woe is life in Southern Elsweyr!\n\nWe seek refuge in greener pastures, walker. You should as well.

I swear, if Fabilius makes one more snarky remark about the fire I've built, I'm going to make him kiss it.\n\nThe master is the one who chose to stop here. It's not my fault that we're surrounded by wet wood and whiny valets.

The master has elected for a momentary respite from the demands of the road. It would be far more tolerable if Rezzai took the care to build a suitable fire.\n\nThe master has already suffered enough, becoming a refugee. And now, this indignity!
Well, I'm thankful for crossing paths with someone who has a sense of right and wrong. I may not find what I came here for, but at least this cheating Khajiit won't profit from my misfortune.
We've spoken enough, outsider.

Hail, O honored warrior.\n\nBlademaster Sai Sahan has need of your aid once more. A Dragon nests on a nearby island, and he believes it means to attack Senchal. He hopes to slay the beast before it can strike against the city.
I am ready, my friend. Leki guide our swords!
Leave Dancer alone. This one sleeps. No dancing.
Now you can't claim you didn't know about butchering the good bits from your kills. I don't want to see you coming back here empty handed.
We did it! We're officially members of the Order of the New Moon.\n\nCome on, we should follow the others to this ceremony. We would not want to be late on our first day.
You steer clear of Kiza. She has her troubles and needs no more.
The cart will take us to the Grinning Horker in Eastmarch. Hop aboard and we can get along.\n\nI don't want to give the coven any more of a lead than they already have.

The Nords don't tolerate Reachmen in their territory. Once you warn the guards, I'm sure High King Svargrim will dispatch his troops. The coven's threat is as good as done!\n\nBut just in case, I'll tell my fellow Ravenwatch what happened here.

My father … working with the Gray Host. How long has he been a part of this? Did he have a hand in mother's death? And what has he told them?\n\nIt's almost too much to bear … and then there's the harrowstorm. My friend, I don't know what to do.
I should have suspected, sensed something. Svargrim has taken the curse. Become a vampire. And he's working with the Gray Host.\n\nThis is bad, my friend. Very, very bad.

This … this is bad, but we'll figure it out. We have Fenn's elixir. That's something, right?\n\nSvana needed a moment after her father revealed his betrayal, but now it's time to act. Talk to her. We're just visitors here. She needs to lead.
It looks like we're on the right trail. I hope we find Rasir safe. \n\nI don't like to imagine what would happen if he went up against an afflicted on his own.
The Gray Host is more widespread than we imagined! Talk to Lyris and let's determine our next move … while we still have one to make.

I've been looking all over for you. Well, mostly I've been looking right around here, but I have been apart from my favorite seat in the Troll for the better part of this bottle.\n\nOn the good side, the wine's delicious.
I'll head back to the ship. I'm no good to anyone if I lose my toes. \n\nGlad you came along when you did. Hopefully you can help get us out of this mess.
We've already chopped up all the non-essential wood on the ship … chairs, benches, small crates.
I didn't think anyone would ever find me out here. If not for you, I'd be a frozen corpse in a few hours.
Surely the gods sent you to Western Skyrim. May Arkay grant you the strength to strike down every last one of those fiends of the Gray Host.
Speak your piece to the king and be done with it. I need to clear the hall.
Go talk to Mjolen and figure out this mess. I'm not leaving my farm until those zombies are gone. I haven't lived this long by taking stupid risks.
Audiences with the high king require formal appeal. Please remove yourself from the throne room until such a time an appeal has been granted.

It's good to see you again. I can't thank you enough for what you did. No more curse means I can be with my family again.\n\nMother and I talked. She wishes to keep what happened a secret. I'm not so sure. We will see what Father says about it.
Oh, my sweet baby girl. What will I do without you?
Ah, my savior! I apologize for running off like that, but I had to ensure my crew was safe.\n\nI'm glad you're here now. The Silver Cormorant owes you a great debt, stranger.
From everything we learned, I fear that the Icereach Coven plans to attack Western Skyrim in the near future.
Don't waste your time with me. Princess Svana wants to see you. She's waiting in her private chamber.\n\nWe can talk later, if you're so inclined.
I'll get Fenn to Solitude and sneak him into the Blue Palace. We'll meet you in Svana's chamber.\n\nWe've got a lot to discuss and not a lot of time to put a plan together, so let's not dawdle.
Thank the Eight you came along! We were next in line for the witches' ritual.\n\nPlease, I need to tell you what I saw.

Whatever Rada al-Saran and the Gray Host were planning, I think the worst is behind us as far as Western Skyrim is concerned.\n\nWith my fa—with Svargrim—dead, their grip on the holds comes to an end.
Can't you feel it? The storm's getting closer. We need to get to Svargrim and stop him.
We've got precious little time. Let's get to Svargrim and end this.
Who does Titanborn think she is, demanding to see the Skald-King?

You have done great service to Skyrim, my friend. The Skald-King is in your debt.\n\nFor now, let me enjoy the nearly complete comforts of my palace. One day, perhaps, the place will actually be finished.

Princess Svana has been waiting to speak to you. She's in her private chamber.\n\nI've tried to talk to High King Svargrim but he has been somewhat … distant, shall we say? Grief-stricken, perhaps? His dismissive attitude is beginning to annoy me.
I lost both my faith and my friends today. I don't know if I have the strength to eliminate this corruption and seal the temple, but I do know that I have to try.\n\nDo you have the relic?
I need to say the proper words before I leave him.\n\nYou should go. Keep Priest Bavian safe.
Just let me gather my wits for a moment. Then I'm headed to the tavern and never leaving.\n\nIf you see Havil, please tell him I'm sorry for running.

Our priority remains getting an audience with High King Svargrim. We need to convince him that the Icereach Coven is a threat to his kingdom and get him to help us stop them.\n\nLet's return to Solitude and present our findings to the queen.
Go, find the cure and bring it back to the Grotto.\n\nI'll take Rasir there so I can properly tend to his wounds.
I am Gerhyld, Queen of Skyrim. Allow me to welcome you on behalf of our kingdom, our city, and our hold.\n\nWho might you be?
So few of us are left. But, I'm indebted to you for those we still have. Especially my brother. \n\nHafskjar mentioned Reach witches captured Bjora. And they used some mind magic on her?
Hey, hey, hey, hey! Don't step on the dice! There a reason you're interrupting our game, hork-face?
Something took Terga last night. I was too weak to go after it … I should have saved her.
Who gave you the right to walk in here and bully my friend? Did my father send you?
After we parted ways, we needed a safe haven. Solitude can give us that much, at least. The stone walls and all the soldiers help us feel safe. No Reachmen breaching this city.
The hold is gone. We'll have to find a new home. That's fine by me as long as we're together. The Nords of Karth are survivors.
This place is … different from Karthwatch. Busier, louder. But I'm told it's safe. So at least there's that.

Remember, the Lightless Hollow is the large cavern to the east. My pack is imprisoned in a work camp on the western side.\n\nI'll work my way over there and meet you south of the camp—after my pack mates are set free.
I thought you might be one of the wolves. Are you escaping as well?
High Priest Varkour will find me! Meridia will save me! When things are darkest, her light shines the way!\n\nPlease don't eat me ….

I will mourn Skor. He was all I had in Greymoor Keep. I would never have escaped without him. \n\nBut I know he would want us to continue on. Dark Moon Grotto must remain a beacon of hope for all those who seek refuge in this darkness.

Look at you. Those resolute shoulders. That glint in your eye that says: I'm ready for action! After searching high and low, I've finally found just the person that Skyrim's premiere arts college calls out for!\n\nHow would you like to become a legend?
The only proper thing to do at a memorial service is drink to the memory of the lost.\n\nI'm not sure we have enough stock for all that.
With all due respect, Sapphire, I've no more to say.\n\nI have to prepare the next auction.
Oh look, another masked person. How dreary.\n\nIf a steak comes back up on the block, don't you outbid me! When else will I get to try Argonian? I hear they're all flavor and no fat. Hah!
Well, that was, you know … horrifying. We never could have bested a mage like that without your help. Thank you.
You risked so much to rescue me. Why would you do such a thing?
House Ravenwatch will always welcome you, friend. It lightens this one's heart to know you walk beside us.
Next stop, the surface. After this business, I'd be willing to go top-side in the middle of the day!
Yes? Perhaps you seek this one's mistress? She is busy, not to be disturbed.
Don't worry about her, she'll come to her senses. What came out of that basket there?
Oh good, you're just in time. We've hit a wall in the investigation ….\n\nHow did it go with Elle?
I'm beginning to think hiring those ghost hunters was a mistake. \n\nI thought it would make everyone feel a little safer to know we were looking into it, but it's just made everything worse.
I had a feeling it wasn't just an opportunistic thief trying to steal my cargo. What are you after?

Do you see? These are the same as the urns smuggled from Bangkorai. They didn't just shatter, they exploded. I can sense traces of magicka clinging to the shards that match the energy used in the storm ritual.\n\nThese other fragments though ….
Removing these splinters would be a lot easier if my fingers weren't numb from the cold, but I'd rather not find anymore spriggans waiting for me in the Shadowgreen.
I escaped. I never thought I would escape. I … I have to get out of here.
Hagridden may not have been a traitor, but his poor judgment cost a lot of innocent lives.
You're back and the bridge still stands. Report. Is Dragon Bridge safe now?
You and the she-giant, you did a good thing for the people of Morthal. Thank you.
My wife … she's like ice. So cold, so pale. All the warmth sucked out of her.
Will you pray with me for these poor souls? Cut down and bound for the Hall of the Dead much too soon.
You again? Didn't I warn you about putting your nose where it doesn't belong?
Damn it, the vampire and the werewolf are long gone. They called themselves Tzinghalis and Ulfra. And they had an unusual rank or title. Exarch. I wonder what that means?
I think Hingrid wants to speak with you. Go on, now.
