My mother … she told me she gave the mighty Lyris Titanborn an important task.\n\nTell me. What were you doing for my mother?
They say that Jarl Olfwenn went mad from that … that Reach magic. May she rest with her ancestors in Sovngarde. She was a fine woman, a fair jarl.
No horses for sale, but if you've got a nag we'll keep her from sinking into the swamp while you're here.
Shh. You'll scare the fish. The ones that aren't frozen anyway. Going to be a brisk snow bear plunge at this year's New Life Festival.
Oh, Ena's here! I'm glad she's safe … but I don't love the look on her face. Better go talk to her.
Don't worry about me, I'll be fine. You should talk to the captain.
Come back anytime. And bring your High Elf friend too. I'd love to hear about all your travels.
The Wolf Mother showed the vampire you seek. At a small camp. And the magic points west.\n\nWhat are you waiting for? Follow the trail and catch your quarry.
Urlvar will answer for what he's done here. I'll make sure of it.

You saw it too, right? That werewolf shed that statue like a snake sheds its skin.\n\nWas she inside that stone husk the whole time, waiting to be awakened? Or did the ritual somehow summon her into that vessel? There's a lot I still don't understand.
There's something I'd like to say, before we begin.
I was just discussing a theory with Mjolen and it seems like we're very close to turning this elixir into a true restorative.
We're all waiting for Svana and she's waiting for you. Go and talk to her.
I'm not the jarl you need to speak to. The longer you keep Svana waiting, the more anxious this crowd will get.
The Skald-King welcomed to the Blue Palace with open arms. Svargrim would be spinning in his grave, if he had one.
The people appear apprehensive of our presence here, but no one has voiced their dissent. That's reassuring.

In their own way, the people of Western Skyrim are as strong as the Nords of the east. Even after so much suffering, they still stand against the howling wind.\n\nWe shall do everything within our power to help them recover.

Za'ji will meet you there? Ah, yes! Of course. This one is your resident expert, after all.\n\nHe just did not realize that his first Dragonguard mission would take him back to Black Heights. He hasn't visited since … well, he has never visited.
They surprised us. Attacked without warning. We barely got out of there alive before they sealed the gates!

Sorry if I gave you a bit of a scare! That was closer than I'm proud to admit. But it all worked out, didn't it?\n\nThis has been a memorable conclusion to a long and storied career. Thank you for your fellowship, and your indulgence!
Oh! You startled me! \n\nWell, you certainly have the look of an adventurer about you. How would you like to chase down my idiot husband and make sure he doesn't get himself killed?
Come on then, don't lose sight of him! Pickle may be old as dirt but he's still got two legs more than you or I!
I mean it! One step closer and I'll stick you like a horker!
Now you've done it. Once you rouse Princess Svana's ire, the best you can do is grovel until her temper subsides.\n\nLook on the bright side. There are worse arses to kiss than her royal highness's.

If you're heading to Mor Khazgur to trade, don't bother. Damn mine collapsed and the whole clan's on edge.\n\nThe fact that Chief Urzikh and Overseer Thulsgreg are at each others' throats doesn't help. Typical.

If you're here to convince me to turn over the key, save your breath. It's too risky to expose the stronghold to attack. Urzikh knows this, but she's too stubborn to admit it.\n\nMazog hid the key for good reason. That's all I've got to say about it.
I'm patient, but not that patient. Don't let Mazog waste your time.\n\nEvery delay puts my people in greater danger.
The key will be on top of the watchtower. You should go quickly.
Away with you. We're much too busy for Svana's frivolous notions.
I wouldn't go toward Karthwatch, traveler. Not now, maybe never again. Nothing left there except horrors.
<Pickle pants excitedly.>

It's been many years since I lived in Wrothgar. I never thought I'd adapt to the deserts of Hammerfell when I started sailing with Mavvok and his crew, but here I am, shivering with the rest of them.\n\nDoesn't feel right.
Qasnareen, Mamdahan, Terga, Dringolir ….\n\nThat thing took 'em. Just like that. Now the Captain's gone too. It's just a matter of time before the cold takes the rest of us.
Please, find my friends!
Don't be fooled by this, outsider. We'll learn the truth of this cave-in soon enough, and Chief Urzikh will have to admit her mistake.
You talked the chief into freeing Mazog. You have my thanks. She is a dear friend and I would have hated to see her punished for trying to do good.
Narzba and Blograth were close by. Scourge thump it! I hope they're still alive.
You there! I bring a message from Lyris Titanborn.
The matriarch lays the eggs, but until a male wanders by, they're unfertilized. That one looks perfect. Good job!
Meridia's light guides you, my friend. Be careful, for the storm has covered the land with monsters instead of snow.\n\nI'll go inside and aid Priest Bavian with her ministrations.
I apologize for that display. Tell the princess … tell her it won't happen again.\n\nYou need to understand. I pledged my sword and my soul to the high king. We all did. And he betrayed us!
There's plenty of work to be found if you're willing to do it.\n\nDo we have an arrangement or not?
Private gathering. Be off.

The affliction comes suddenly with no apparent cause. I think this cursed place is driving us mad. If it weren't for the other refugees still coming to Dark Moon Grotto for aid, I would head for the surface and not look back.
You can't give up yet! Nelfthea's in danger out there! Please, you've got to bring her back to me.
You aren't one of the Reach witches? You have to help me!
You're alive! What happened? Where did that strange man go?
Stop! Stop, just … stand still a moment. Oh, it's no use. There are currently four of you, and the longer I look at them, the less I trust my stomach. \n\nTalk to my sister while I compose myself.
What are you talking to me for? Do you want to save your companions or not? \n\nGo throw the switch on the overlook! Move it, move it!
I can't tell you how exhilarating it is to have control of my limbs once more. I feel like I could run forever! Jump as high as the clouds!
Ah, good, you made it out. That's certainly enough hostile Dwemer creations for one day, I should think.\n\nI trust you still have the necessary components?

It's done. My grandfather's so-called pilgrimage … it was a tale made up to explain all of this. To keep Morokei sealed away.\n\nIf only he would have told me sooner, I could have helped. I could have saved him and Hjarnam.
That look on your face …. Tell me you found something.

The spirit-chasing fools are down in the settlement, likely setting more traps for people to trip over. The damn things covered one of my workers in paint and nearly took off his leg earlier!\n\nShor's bones, I wish my wife hadn't hired these idiots.
You must be new to Dusktown. You've still got that look.\n\nWell, get settled in. You won't be allowed topside again until you complete your contract, so you might as well get comfortable.
Go bother someone else, horker! If I don't finish this by the end of my shift, the overseer will have my hide.
Rigurt knows diplomacy is not the smoothest road, but this one was almost too bumpy, even for him! \n\nEither way, Rigurt could not have done this without your help, friend.

Now, the grim work begins. Burying the dead, repairing our homes …. Much to do. But mark my words: Kyne's Aegis will emerge from this stronger, fiercer, and more vibrant than it's ever been.\n\nI weep for the fool who tests us again!
Just say the word when you're ready. My axe is thirsty for Giant-blood!
Kyne preserve you, friend. With your help, we might have some hope of driving the vampires back. Not much, but enough.

Lady Ninetha's loyalty to her daughter is admirable. Like a mother wolf guarding her pup. But it may mean her end if we're not quick.\n\nGo to the red tree overlooking Morthal. Together we will end this curse.
I understand their fear, but I don't know how to get through to them. How are we supposed to assure them that they're safe when they're all riled up about spirits and ghosts?
I'm sorry, but Jarl Morryn has asked not to be disturbed.\n\nTruly, the jarl was ambitious to try to get both thanes to meet with her at the same time, given their history.
I don't love the idea of Mazog not getting punished. Hasn't she caused enough damage? But I trust the chief. She knows what's best.

Ah, I'm glad you've returned to Morthal. Freiwen has slowly recovered. The curse took its toll over the years. And though she claims to understand it wasn't her fault, I know she still feels the guilt.
Word of warning? Don't wander around the outskirts of Morthal if you can avoid it. Something evil stalks the hills, make no mistake.
I'm going to rummage through more of Arkasis's work before his allies catch wind of our attack. See if I can dig up more on this mystery research. If not, I've got a new lead to follow anyway.

The documents we found describe Lady Thorn's plan in significant detail. An army of darkness joining forces with the Gray Host. If we hadn't come along, she'd be unstoppable.\n\nGood thing Talfyg didn't count on you showing up.
Everything will be fine. As long as Rigurt lets me do all the talking. And — Gods. I could use a cup of ginger tea.
We haven't the strength to fight Lord Falgravn, but nothing will enter those gates behind you. On Ysgramor's head, I swear it!
Was that woman a half-giant? Like Lyris, the axe-warrior of the east? Does she have anything to do with those strange sticks we found outside of town?
As long as the Gray Host controls the temple, we're cut off from the supply of sacred oil.\n\nIt's imperative we get our hands on that oil—and quickly!
Praise the Divines for sparing Solitude. I have enough souls to mourn today.
Hello again. Master Dren isn't here right now. Believe me, I checked all the bottles!

You haven't left yet? By the Three ….\n\nYes, by all means, let's have a bit of chit-chat while I'm afflicted by this ridiculous illusion. Did you bring some tea? I'd offer you some scones and kwama spread if I wasn't, you know … a bottle!
It seems like the worst of the storm in the city above has passed. Princess Svana sent word. You're needed in Solitude.
I'm still always surprised at how many people crave my howlwater. I've never been able to develop a taste for the stuff myself, but most Orcs can't get enough of it.

Now, I will do what I always do in situations like this. Hyperbolize! With some clever prose and a few creative liberties, I can spin this into a yarn worthy of Narsis Dren.\n\nAs for you, I suppose you should return Maelmoth's journal to Deem-Vilax.
Hm. It's a bit messy in here. Not that it matters. Not that anything matters.
Perhaps I should find a bundle of flowers. You know … to make Narsis useful, for once.
That storm! It was terrifying!\n\nOh, the others are still out there. I hope they're all right.
When the storm struck, we ran for our lives. It was … unnatural. Evil.\n\nStill, I'm alive, praise Meridia.

I wanted to help the others, but Meridia's words came to me as the storm struck. "Every life bears responsibility for itself."\n\nI made sure I was responsible for my own life, just as the priests teach us.
Priest Bavian was so brave. She led us to this cave and safety. But those noises outside … what did the storm bring with it, I wonder?

I'll search the lair for more trophies. Holding my brother's ring again feels like it validates him. His life. Everyone who lost someone should feel this closure.\n\nI'll send word to Eyfja and Hautgerd. If you ever come near the farm again, stop by.
My favorite part of coming to this inn is the strangers trying to talk to me. It's great. Never gets old.\n\nWhat do you want?
This better be important. Unless you want to pick up a rake, I don't have time to jaw at strangers.
I'm surprised Chief Urzikh let Mazog off with no punishment. But at least the fighting is done, and a decision was made. A clan can only take so much.
Welcome back, Antiquarian. I trust your time with Gabrielle was illuminating?
You found my posting? Marvelous!\n\nGo speak to Verita. She'll prepare you for the trial of admission. Nothing too scary, I assure you. Good luck!
You there! The barrow is off limits. We are here to make sure nothing gets in or out, and we'll do so by any means necessary.
Really, you should think about joining the Antiquarian Circle. You have a knack for this sort of thing!

There you have it! You're a proper antiquarian now. Seems you have quite a knack for it, too!\n\nJust keep practicing with the Antiquarian's Eye and master those digging techniques. I'm confident you'll be recovering priceless relics in no time!
I'll get these miners back on their feet and back to work soon enough. Now that Mazog's punished, we can all get on with our lives.
Chief Urzikh made the right decision. Mazog deserved to be punished for her crimes, even if she had good intentions. She'll be back to work soon enough … hopefully she's learned her lesson.
I see there's no talking you out of it. Go seek your glory and try not to get stomped into the earth.
Used to be a goatherd's biggest troubles were half-chewed boots. What I'd give for those days again.
Don't worry about us, we're right behind you.
Oh, excuse me! Have you seen a mammoth with big adorable eyes stomping around anywhere? Her name is Muffins, and I'm worried sick about her!
That mead knocks you on your arse, doesn't it? Ha! It's the best!
Don't try to beat Skreg at his own games. The Circle of Champions deserves better than that.

Most disappointing. Though, I suppose it wouldn't be a mysterious place of myth if everyone knew of how to reach it.\n\nFear not! I will discover it and its secrets at some point! Thank you for your time, friend.

Many see Nords as drunken fools. With the decline of Jhunal in our pantheon and disdain for learning and curiosity, it is no wonder so many others think of us as primitive.\n\nBut I will never stop spreading the words of Jhunal. Some must hear it!
It's your funeral, friend. According to the rumors, there's something truly evil in that mine. I'd think twice if I were you.
You there, friend! You look like a traveler with impeccable taste and a truly adventurous palate. How would you like to be the first to taste my delightful skeever kabob?
I hope you can find Rasir. He's the only chance we have at reuniting everyone. If we have a cure, we don't need to live in fear any longer.
You! I've seen you with Princess Svana. You and the princess saved us! Thank you, traveler.
They say Svargrim was on the Tower of the Wolf, trying to call the storm. But you and Princess Svana stopped him, didn't you?\n\nI—I don't know how to thank you!
The rage … it's gone! I have control of my senses once more. \n\nPlease, you must save Rasir. He's our only hope!
The sagas of Skyrim are our histories. People tend to forget that simply because they're more lively than dry, old Imperial texts.
They say we're safe now. That the Gray Host has been defeated. I say don't believe them.\n\nThe gods aren't done punishing us for allowing the high king to endanger our holds.
You were there, weren't you? With Princess Svana? You're the one who killed Svargrim and stopped the harrowstorm?\n\nThank Kyne you came to Western Skyrim!
I was so worried for Rasir. Thank you for bringing him back safely!
Werewolves. I always thought they were monsters. But down here, it's hard not to pity the poor sods. The shadows are the only place they can be themselves.\n\nUntil some vampire puts them in a cage.
Did you hear? Something about werewolves in the Lightless Hollow? I came down here to earn some gold, not get caught up in the exploits of monsters!
Skor ran through here, chasing after Rasir. Some of us tried to fight him off, but he's too powerful. \n\nWe couldn't help Rasir, and now I fear we're all infected.
You did the Mor Khazgur clan a great service today. Some of us might not like the outcome, but everyone appreciates what you did. You at least gave us a chance to rebuild.
Can I help you dryskin? Or do you wish to ask me how I find the cold?
I don't envy you. The things I saw in that charnel pit will linger with me the rest of my life. I'll pray for your safe return.
Yes?

Ah, my new assistant I presume? I look forward to any valid test results you might be able to produce.\n\nErm, when you use the Dissonance Apparatus, do exercise caution. It required a significant fiscal investment to create.
Nezashul is glad to be of acquaintance to you! Tinzen tells him that you are to assist with his inquiries on behalf of the Coterie of Organized Scholars, yes?
Drat. Drat, drat, drat! I'm stumped. Until Tinzen gets me a proper research assistant I have next to nothing to go on. Might as well be sitting on my thumbs.

I'm telling them, it's true! But do they listen? I know I've got a few knots on my head the size of a pear, but I didn't imagine a giant Dwarven construct scooping up scrap to cobble onto itself! It's real!
What did Essenia do to this poor Orc? His eyes … and the scars.\n\nSee what you can learn from him. Just be gentle, all right? Look like he's suffered enough already.
I can't believe <<1>> stood up to those werewolves! I never thought she even liked me, but there she was defending our lives!
Thank you for saving us from those monsters. I'm beginning to question my fondness for living outdoors.
I don't know if I feel good about Mazog going free. Who's to say she won't do something so careless again?
Chief Urzikh should punish those disobedient miners. They bring great shame on our clan by defying our chief!
That scent … why do you smell like Edjar?
Mining will resume when the creatures have been cleared out of the caves. I hope that Chief Urzikh's mercy will help her and Mazog find a way to work together.
I'm not losing my sister to some lunatic pureblood. We push on until we find her!

You should get out of Blackreach while you still can, stranger. The mines are haunted. Our leaders may be trying to pretend nothing's wrong, but they're not fooling anyone. \n\nThis place is angry. We never should have come down here.
The interrogation is over now, right? I need to … I need to find a healer. A witch to purge whatever this is out of my blood.\n\nYou got what you wanted. Now, let me go!

I almost pity Overseer Urlvar. Sure, what he did was awful … but he's not a bad man. An idiot, maybe, but not evil. \n\nElle assures us we'll be safer now that we're prepared. But I do wonder … what else awaits us down here?
Don't sneak up on me like that! Haven't you heard what's going on down here? This place is cursed. People are jumpy.
You look like you had a rough expedition, friend. But we in the Undaunted don't sign up to sit on cushions and drink mead, do we?
Have you had a chance to review the guild listings, friend?
What? You constantly interrupt me when I'm working! Snap it out.
Huh. This reminds me of my home.
Careful not to disturb the fish, stranger. Hard enough to catch them as is, and even when I manage, they get stolen anyway! I'm sick of feeding thieves. I can barely feed my family!
Well, now. What brings you back to me? If it's for some headcheese, it won't be ready for another hour or so.
Skor … my friend. There was no way of saving him, he made sure of that. But I can't help but grieve for the man he was. Damn all of Greymoor Keep for what they did to us.
I don't mind telling you, I'm in no hurry to get back in that mine.
Keep my brother safe in there. If we lose him, we'd never get another healer in time to save either of them.
You kept my beloved Hamvir alive and gave us hope for his sister. I won't forget this kindness, traveler.
Mor Khazgur will endure, thanks to you.
We will heal from the casualties in the mine. Now that our leadership has reached an understanding, we can finally move forward.

I don't think Brun would still be alive without Old Mjolen's help. She keeps knitting his wounds back together with her magic. Then minutes later they open again.\n\nPapa told me never to trust her, but maybe he was wrong.

You there! Don't run off screaming, there's a perfectly reasonable explanation for this.\n\nIt's rather humiliating, but my soul is trapped inside this ludicrous child's toy. I need someone with a corporeal form to help return me to my body.
You have shown yourself to be a true warrior, not only at Mor Khazgur, but here, too. \n\nMy clan is eager to repay you and help these people. We know their suffering all too well.
People I know … changed into mindless creatures. Or worse. What a dismal day!
The jarl's dead, rest her soul. \n\nSome folk want to leave, but I think we should stay. Rebuild. It's the right thing to do.
Did you come to help us? Are you with the princess?\n\nWell, you're too late. The town is lost and everyone I knew and loved is dead.
What god did we anger to deserve this terrible fate? That storm … it was angry, I tell you, angry!

You mean to join the Circle? That's great! That's really … really great.\n\nSo, I'd love to indulge in introductions, but I've just had a thought, and you know how that goes. Pop in, pop out! Have to commit it to paper! So, you know … goodbye!
I'll heal up soon. I'm ready to get back to work … now that this mess is over with.
So. Looking to earn a place in the Circle, eh? Good. We could use a few sturdy scholars around here.
You know, I think Phebe looks up to you. You've become a point of inspiration for her. I know we both hope our paths cross again.
So the Ravenwatch youngling recruited others to break into this fortress of the dead? Not really what I expected, but welcome nonetheless. We'll need the diversion if she and I are to sneak in.
We'll fight beside you. I'll gather the others and bring them to Rebel's Retreat.
You can't stop what must come to pass, outsider. And neither can my sister!

That letter we found. I can't believe Verandis was a part of something as evil as the Gray Host. I guess we need to go to the secret island. And the castle, if it still exists. \n\nI won't rest until I learn the truth. The whole truth.

I need to consider what happened in the barrow, harrier. Think about what I could have done to save my sister. What I can do to save the clans that look to me to lead them.\n\nOh, is that your friend Gwendis over there? I think she's looking for you.

Ah, good. You received my message. I was almost tempted to go exploring. This is Blackreach, my friend! The legendary land beneath the land. If I had realized it existed, I would have come here long ago.\n\nNo matter. Are you still with me in this?
Come, my friend. Let's continue our search. Rada and Lady Belain can't be too far ahead of us.
I am … fading … away ….

Cogline and Indouz fled in the direction of Evermore with the Pyre Watch warrior, while Jeanard headed toward Kerbol's Hollow.\n\nPlease be careful. The wilderness can be treacherous between here and there.

You're back. Good. I've been thinking about what you learned down below. There's a story that the Ghostsong clan—my clan—knows well. The Dark Heart. My sister Nathari studied the old secrets. If anyone can glean the mind of Lady Belain, it's her.
Not many of my clan learned the scratchings, but Senan could read and write the Imperial language. He spent years in Moricar's Imperial Guard.\n\nWhat did he write down?

Thank you again for the timely rescue.\n\nI daresay, I'll regale my grandchildren with the tale of my escape and return for the rest of my days. I simply must commit it all to paper. So much history to record!
When the Imperials attacked, I resigned myself to whatever fate Tall Papa thought fitting for me. I am glad that you were part of that fate. I am not yet ready to leave the land of the living.
I do not know the nature of your mission, wayfarer, and I still have my own to uphold. But if you seek answers about the Gray Host, then may Mara bless your search.

What an exciting day! When that gorgeous Wood Elf came swooping to my rescue, I just about swooned!\n\nMind you, I didn't need to be rescued. I had it all well in hand. Even still, my rescuer was a delightful surprise. No complaints here.
The portal into the Dark Heart stands open and waiting. Let's just hope it leads where I think it does.
Well, this is it. The portal leads to Rada al-Saran. To the Darkstorm. And to the end of all this … whatever that is.
Can't say I'm looking forward to another romp in Oblivion. I've seen enough of the place for ten lifetimes. Let's make this a quick trip, all right?
I'll do all I can to keep the orrery in alignment, but I don't know how long it can sustain this. I don't believe it was designed to have this amount of power coursing through it.

Are you here about the notice? So many new faces in the city, but we could use the help. \n\nIf you need work and aren't concerned about the risks, then we should talk. As a former Imperial consul, I assure you that this is all aboveboard.
Look at this place. Still impressive, even if it's more ruined than not. \n\nThe ancient clans certainly had a sense of style.

Our enemy advances on two fronts, my friend, and we must match them move for move.\n\nRada al-Saran has activated the orrery, while Lady Belain has gone to Markarth. Worse, the Dark Heart beats stronger with every soul that flows into it.
You didn't just help me learn the truth about Verandis. You helped me save him. That's not something I'll ever forget. You have my word on that.
Can you smell them, Verandis? Prey. On the wind. We should be out hunting them, not uselessly debating in these halls of stone.

Ah, Verandis. Good. I wanted to talk to you.\n\nI never tire of looking at this creation. Tell me again, why did you abandon your stone husks? I thought you wanted your precious mortals to enjoy the everlasting life of their betters.

How good to see you, Verandis, my old friend. You look well. Our halls have felt quite empty without you.\n\nWhat do you think of our new home? Is it not, as I wrote in my letter, everything one could ask for?
If there is anything else you need during your stay, please do not hesitate to ask.

My ward and I have much to discuss. I owe her an explanation. And I need time to adjust. Returning from Coldharbour … it doesn't seem completely real.\n\nI promise, after that I will find out what the Gray Host has planned. I give you my word.
I—I don't understand. Arana—she was dead. Wasn't she? What's going on?
It may seem odd coming from a Nord, but I'm glad to see all these Reachfolk alive and well.\n\nThey seem content, but I'm sure they wouldn't mind us bringing them a few more reasons to celebrate.
Look. The Dark Heart, it's … dormant. Was that Verandis's doing, or that woman's?

<<1>> and <<2>> made it back safely! Thanks for finding them. Next time, we'll save the argument until we get back home.\n\nFor now, I'm going to snuggle up with <<2>>. She's so soft! What a good girl she is!
<<1>>! I've been looking all over for you. And it looks like you made a friend, too.\n\nDid <<1>> bring you here, stranger?
<<<1>> seems agitated. Maybe she's trying to tell you something?>
These Gray Host bastards. Under our very feet this entire time!\n\nThey're tending to the plant. They must be the ones corrupting it!
I did not think an outsider would be the one to save the Crow-Eye, but I am grateful to you. Know that you will always have a home here.
There are more problems in the Reach than Freyleth and the Lothid clan. The Ravenwatch's work never ends, it seems.
There you are. I hope whatever you were doing was important. I hate being kept waiting.\n\nSo, are you ready to go with me to the Gray Host's secret island now?
Grand. You go bash some monsters, cover yourself in guts and glory, and get yourself a piece of the loot. Easy as pie. We clear?

Ah, good. I hoped you'd turn up. You uncovered that Ard Caddach's advisor, Lady Belain, is working with the Gray Host. And that she's a vampire. To hide that from me takes great power.\n\nTell me what else you heard during her conversation with Rada.

If you hadn't arrived when you did, Gwendis and I would not have been able to power down the orrery. Thank you.\n\nBut tell me. What of Arana and Lady Belain? I could feel them … it was like a battle in the darkness.
Don't linger, harrier. All this death, it fuels the Dark Heart. Making it stronger with every passing moment. Find that keystone and stop Lady Belain. Hurry.
<This table is set up to conduct some kind of alchemical experiment, but you don't have the ingredients necessary to recreate it.>
Verandis is back. Does he look a little better to you? Why don't you talk to him and see how he's doing? I'll just wait over here.

We lost too many good Reachfolk to Lady Belain and her damn desires. I'm glad you and Arana dealt with her … ah, but I wish I'd been able to kill her myself!\n\nIs that Count Verandis over there? Aye, looks like he wants to talk to you.

I'm sorry Freyleth tricked you. I didn't know the darkcap would kill Boss Trenlor. Once the mushroom weakened him, I planned to challenge him in her stead.\n\nI was as surprised as you and Adusa when he fell back in his throne and just … died.
You think I'm foolish to keep Lady Belain close, don't you? It takes a bit of foolishness to rule this place, don't you know?\n\nYou tell this High Elf of yours. I'll see him if he wants.
<This table is set up to conduct some kind of alchemical experiment, but you don't have the ingredients necessary to recreate it.>
<This table is set up to conduct some kind of alchemical experiment, but you don't have the ingredients necessary to recreate it.>
And now Count Verandis has returned and wants to speak to you. I suppose I'll have to wait a little longer to find out what happened down there.

Did you see the expression on that bastard's face? We made him pay for all the pain and suffering he caused.\n\nAs for you, I thank you. I could use someone like you when I take Trenlor's place as leader of the clan.

Not a moment too soon. Caddach's eager to demonstrate that he's the equal of any Nord king. He hopes it will legitimize his claim as king of the Reach.\n\nHe's not wrong, but he'd look more a fool if I weren't here to keep his temper on a leash.
You and Lyris must go. While I still possess the power of the Dark Heart, I can open a gateway to the orrery. Return home.
You go on and speak to Caddach. I'll see what's so important that your friend here has to tell me in private.
Here and gone, here and gone! It's cruel to play with a girl's heart like this … but I'm glad Verandis kept his promise. Ugh, I'm having too many feelings right now!

I—I don't know what I expected when Arana said there was someone waiting to see us, but I never—I thought he was gone! I don't think there's anything left that could surprise me today.\n\nForget I said that. Better to not tempt fate.

I have no regrets. You gave me the opportunity to reckon with my past and pay penance. This journey has brought closure to the life of Count Verandis Ravenwatch. I have a fresh start.\n\nAs do we all. The kings are soon to speak. You should be there.
The ard's eager to announce our peace agreement. Don't keep him waiting any longer, his patience is already wearing thin.

Understone Keep is strikingly different from the Palace of Kings, I can say that much for it. All this Dwarven architecture is suffocating and I find the little machine noises that carry through the halls unnerving. I wouldn't get much sleep here.
Go on, my witch beckons. Just make it quick. I feel a fool standing about like this.
Well met, harrier. Too many people here for my liking, but I guess it's understandable. We've seen some dark days of late. Good to see the sun come out again.
Don't let us keep you. We'll manage to keep each other company while you take your well-deserved bows.
I couldn't help but overhear. Ard Caddach's voice, it carries.\n\nNow tell me about the leader of the witch-rebels. The name you provided. Arana, I believe you said.
Lost Valley Redoubt? A revelation? I don't know what Nathari is planning, but I don't like the sound of it.\n\nWe need to see what's going on in Lost Valley. I'll meet you there.
You wanted to talk to Arana? Well, now Arana wants to talk to you.

This is all that remains of my clan? Oh, Nathari. Your prophecy brought an ending to things, that's for certain. I should have dealt with you sooner.\n\nThe survivors will have a place with us at Rebel's Retreat, if they want it.
Go on, off with you! I don't need you staring at my misery, outsider. It's … embarrassing enough I got ambushed by the rebels.

You left already. Our business is done, outsider. Unless, that is, you actually find Bthar-Zel. I've never had the gumption to go and look for it myself.\n\nIf you do find it, come back and tell me all about next time you're in the neighborhood.
I hope Arana's all right. It's like something attacked her the moment you opened that door.
The storm tested us, as life tests us. We survived to hunt another day, and none of us will take that for granted.

Tayfaern told me about you, harrier. You wanted to talk? Well, here I am.\n\nWhat will it be? A battle? I haven't turned anyone into a goat recently, but I'm willing to try if you so much as raise your weapon.

I don't hear any clanking behind us. I think we're clear.\n\nCurse that Lady Belain! I thought if we could acquire the keystone, we could finally get the upper hand. I'm tired of snapping at the heels of the Gray Host. I want to go for the throat!
The door opened, but something happened to Arana. She mentioned something about a darkness.\n\nWe should check on her, but we also need to determine that the keystone we seek is here.
We see your true warrior nature now. It shines through your skin and bones. A glow of strength unseen in previous outsiders.\n\nYou deserve your song among the Spiritblood clan.
You thought yourself so clever, so stealthy, hiding in the shadows. But the darkness answers to me.\n\nVery well. My curiosity is piqued. What have you come to find in this forsaken barrow?

With the path ahead blocked, our only option appears to be the door above us.\n\nHowever, I sense something on the other side. I smell oil. I hear the whine of ancient gears. Proceed with caution, my friend.
I hope our paths cross again one day. It was an honor to work with you. Though next time we meet, let's make sure it's under better circumstances.
I'm almost certain I granted you an audience with the ard. Get to it before I change my mind.

I saw you go back there and start fiddling with something. Then this stern-looking fellow popped from nowhere. Do you know what he wants? Seems like he's ready for a fight.\n\nIf anything happens, I'll back you up.
I know we came this far together, and I know the debt to Lyranth is mine. But I can't lose my father.\n\nPlease, go with her. Find what she seeks. We can talk later.
You won't find a braver, more trustworthy mercenary than me, but I'm not suicidal!\n\nWhen that cat asked for help, I didn't know she was planning to walk into the leviathan's maw. So to speak.
Lyris was on her way to Markarth when last we parted ways. You were to meet her there, yes?
We are all grateful for any help you can provide to our people. Their struggle can only be alleviated by kind sorts such as yourself.
I felt the darkness inside me. Pulling me towards the pit. Down to something evil beneath the ground.
My wife, I tried to stop her. I tried to pull her back. But the shadows reached out and grabbed her. I couldn't save her.\n\nThey're all gone. Devoured. Like the stories said.

My thanks. The messages you carry are the private thoughts of many weary Imperial refugees. Please, let them remain private.\n\nBurn them at the Old Life shrine. Their authors, by the Divines, will know if they were heard in Aetherius.

More of us survived than I hoped. Maybe next time my father will heed my counsel and keep away from dark places such as Briar Rock. Better to leave your foes chasing after your steps than to stand your ground with those you can't trust.
I'm not one of those monsters! And I didn't kill this one. It was the blond giant and her companion!
Damned vampires. At least that fine Redguard and his blond giant knew how to deal with them.
Welcome, partner. I take it you got my message?
Both the words on the cave pillars and what Snow Lily said to me … I have much to consider. Much to think about.

Funny how the Lord of Destruction would choose a pixie as his champion. I guess one shouldn't judge an enemy by appearances. Huh, I suppose I learned something today as well.\n\nGet going! More of Mehrunes Dagon's creatures await.
Ancient legends, old songs … it's all up to Sai now.
You there. You match the description I was given.\n\nI have a message for you. From Lyris Titanborn.
So tell me Verandis, have you decided to accept the truth of our nature or are you still blinded by delusions of peace with our foodstuff?
Go in peace, freehand. We'll never forget your actions here.
Fynvagh says we must still go to Markarth, even after hearing what the Gray Host did to the city. I only hope the butchery is over with … I don't know how we could possibly help.

I heard what the Gray Host did at Markarth. To think the city of stone might fall—and from under their very feet. It was always the safe place in the Reach, since I was a lass.\n\nNowhere feels safe. Not in these days ….
Have you heard, stranger? The Miracle at Markarth, they're calling it—our loved ones dead from the Gray Host attack, returned to life!\n\nWe want to see it with our own eyes. Can it be true?

Well, a vateshran can't pick his audience, especially in a place like this.\n\nDon't suppose you could part with some coin for a performance of mine? My tales thrill and inform. And some coin in my pocket—a soul's got to eat. You won't regret it.
She's … not punishing me? After everything I've done? It doesn't seem possible.\n\nI will not squander this second chance. I will work with Chief Urzikh this time, not against her.
Friend! I hoped I'd bump into you another time.\n\nI have something I wanted to say to you.

Well, well. A carcass, a witchman, and an inquisitive traveler. Most auspicious.\n\nIf Namira bids humble me read the entrails for your fortune, who am I to refuse? But we must be quick — the gall is cooling quickly.

I didn't think an outsider would ever be inclined to help the likes of us, but you proved me wrong. And in doing so, you saved my home.\n\nMy gratitude may mean little to you, but you have it all the same.
What could you want? Never seen a body sit before, is that it? Or you think someone enjoying themselves means an invitation to say hello.
It was a near thing, but the handfasting is done. Now there can be peace between the Eagleseers and Six-Fords.\n\nThank you, outsider for your part in delivering this.

Well, that went smoother than I expected. It certainly took long enough, but I suppose the end result is worth it.\n\nStill, the sooner we leave this place, the better. I do not enjoy time away from my clan holdings.
Hmm. So Eslyn did allow herself to be saddled with the Six-Ford lad. They both look happier about it than I would have expected.
My business here is concluded, outsider. My clan has new allies now. That will take some getting used to.
To say I did not think this would happen would be a lie. But … I still must take time to deal with it. I think I need to be alone now, outsider.

I followed my heart and the feud is done with. Thank you for your help, outsider. This is a triumph.\n\nI only hope Drisene can forgive me. That she someday understands that a life with me would not have filled her heart as she deserves.

We did it, outsider. It's funny, all that time we spent trying to thwart this plan, only to go along with it in the end. Love is a strange force, isn't it?\n\nI only hope Madearn has no regrets. I know it wasn't easy for him to go back on his word.

It was bold of the lad to stand by his word. I can understand why he did it. Aside from kin and clan, word is all a Reachfolk can be sure is his in the tumults of life.\n\nThe chief-of-chiefs may not have gotten her peace today. But perhaps in time.
You have returned from the sacred cave. I hope you and your companions found the knowledge you sought.
First we're fighting vampires. Now we're working with them?\n\nI trust Arana, but I hope she interpreted the signs correctly.
Ah, the hunter returns once more. Hircine certainly favors you, my friend!\n\nWhat of the Symbol of Uricanbeg? Were you able to retrieve it?

Look at you. Strutting around, thinking you're tough. Sure, you may have seen a clash or two. Tricked yourself into believing you hold a warrior's spirit. But could you stand against a true Reach challenge?
It cannot be! I prayed for salvation from this place, but I never expected it to happen.
I thought I would die down here in the dark. I long to see the walls of Markarth again.
A glorious success, stranger! No one in living memory from outside the Spiritblood clan has ever completed the Rites. Our people will sing your story for the rest of time.

As we speculated, the keystone does more than open doors. Rada and Lady Belain plan to use it to restart the orrery.\n\nThe question remains … why? And what role does this Dark Heart play in their schemes?

Find Verandis. Don't let him get distracted by all the intriguing mysteries of Blackreach. Walking around in an actual legend, one he can't explore at his leisure, that's probably eating him up inside.\n\nGo on. I'll rendezvous with both of you later.
Meet Arana back at Rebel's Retreat. I'll wait here for Verandis.
You may want to speak with the Ard.
The Ard would like to speak with you.
There you are! I've been looking all over for you.\n\nVerandis wants to talk to you. You do remember we have an army of werewolves and vampires to deal with, right?

I knew Hircine smiled upon you. Keeva can discern the good from the bad, and she's been happy ever since we crossed paths.\n\nGo on. Give the sacred relic to the high shaman. It's the last thing we need to dedicate and complete this shrine.
Is what they are saying true? That the last of the Gray Host is truly dead?
Outsider … you are an inspiration. What you did for this land, its people, I can scarce fathom it.
Friend, I'm happy to see you. News of what you did for the Reach brought joy to me. And to Madearn as well.

This one is not used to being this close to the center of attention. She does not like it.\n\nGive Adusa a shadow or dark corner. Celebrations such as these tend to be too bright and noisy for my taste.
If I could walk, I'd carve out the heart of every Thornroot in this damned place.
Curse those Thornroots! They've all gone mad.
You caught me in a moment of quiet contemplation … but, please, join me.

My mistress's letter waits over there. I had to put it down. For some reason, carrying it all this way made my skin itch and my head tingle. And not in a good way.\n\nOnly you can read it, or so the Dread Lady informed me.

Well, that was an unusual adventure. Puts things in perspective. After all, nothing drives home the realization that one manservant is more than enough like an abundance of Stibbons.\n\nI shudder to think about all that goo, though.

She may have more hair than scales, but the dryskin is clever. You have not violated any of our customs, so we are not bound by strictures with you.\n\nWe may talk of the xanmeer and the curse that has befallen the shiny-headed, scaleless one.

I have a feeling you hate this sort of thing, but we need to head back to Gideon. Governor Keshu insists on throwing us a victory celebration!\n\nI wonder if there will be cake. I could really, really go for a big, gooey piece of cake!
It looks like Governor Keshu and Eveli are making plans. You better go and see what they're thinking. I want to stay here and talk to Calia for a while.

That battle was not what I expected. Things were getting out of hand for a time, what with Mehrunes Dagon stomping around, knocking down towers and crushing anything in his path.\n\nI'm glad that it's over. And I'm glad that you fought by our side.
I believe that Eveli wants a word with you, mercenary.

We have a door locked from the outside, a dead councilor, and a missing servant. Did the assassin take off with both the torn-out journal pages and the servant?\n\nAnyway, they not only murdered Abor, they probably know how to find the Ambitions now.
Now that you satisfied the Wood Elf's curiosity, it's time to satisfy mine.\n\nShow me what the cache contained, little mortal.

Is that an invitation I smell? I soaked each one in bacon grease before sending them out. Right this way then! I hope you brought your apron. Between the blood, saliva, and crying—well, you'll probably also need wading trousers down there.
My orders are to protect the councilor, and I take my orders very seriously.\n\nBear that in mind and keep your hands away from your weapons. Do that and we'll get along fine.

Perhaps my records, when combined with the documents you secured from Jirich and Sophus, will finally allow us to determine the truth of these Ambitions.\n\nI remember the scribe Beragon. He was quite competent. I'm sure he can decipher the code.
Oh, Velan! Oh, my love!\n\nWhat happened? I thought Captain Rian sent you to protect my husband?
My friend, I see you have once again come to the aid of my lady. I thank you for that. And for rescuing me.

Even now, Zenithar is teaching me. I came seeking his blessings of wealth and instead I find a life he spared from the sickness of greed.\n\nThe true Divine wealth we discovered here is that old man. I'm certain.

Spawn-worthy feelings to you, brave warrior. Not only did you rescue my tribe, but you became a storm that tore free the evil roots of the Sul-Xan here. \n\nWith this, you have saved many more innocents.
Councilor Lovidicus is ready to speak with you now. Just don't push him too hard. He's been through a terrible ordeal today.
Given what they faced, Blackwood's defenders did a remarkable job of not getting stomped into paste. Good on them.\n\nNow, I need to think about dinner. I'm famished!
I am eager to leave. I wonder how much blood is soaked into the mud that surrounds this place. \n\nThank you for getting us out of there. My scales still shudder with revulsion.
Patience dissipates. We should leave this place, there will be time for rest later.\n\nDon't mistake my tone for ingratitude, outsider. I will never forget what you did for us.

I did not know if Jela would come for us. I hoped for her sake that she would stay away, but then the winds blew you to her. We are fortunate. \n\nKeep your blood from those who wish to take it, traveler. Farewell.
Vandacia … a high priest of Mehrunes Dagon. Has he been a Daedric cultist all these years?\n\nI failed to see the signs and now the councilors, they're all dead … Faleria, Sophus, Abor, and Jirich.
I refuse to let them sacrifice the remaining Ambitions. Somehow, I'm able to read this accursed book. Just keep Vandacia busy long enough for me to figure out these rituals and incantations.
At least I helped to defeat the monster who destroyed my parents and sacrificed my brother. Vandacia won't hurt anyone else. There's some comfort in that.
All right. You talked to the fort's servants and rummaged around in our pantry. What's the verdict? Did you find the missing servant?
I must say, I came seeking one thing and discovered a much larger mystery. Why sanctify this site? For what purpose?\n\nNot knowing what the servants of Mehrunes Dagon plan feels … uncomfortable.

The deciphered document, it mentions the person who hired me. Farrul Lupus. Could he really be Emperor Leovic's steward? I guess it's possible.\n\nAnyway, I'm supposed to bring this book I recovered to him. Well, to his contact in Riften, anyway.
Mercenary. We'll be moving to retake Borderwatch soon. Or have you returned for some other reason?

All Tenarei has to do is tell Larz-Tul the truth about the Sithis-cult we found here. People have disappeared, and rumors about dark doings have reached Leyawiin. Let the criminal believe the Daughter of Sithis sacrificed Quistley.
Can you believe it? We saved Borderwatch! People here will be telling tales of our skullduggery and derring-do for … for at least a week! This might really be the birth of Lady Twilight's legend!
I've had jobs go better—much, much, much better—but all things considered, this could have gone a lot worse for us.

If you're looking for more people to free, try the fortress smithy. I saw the Painted Eyes herding a group in that direction before they chained me up.\n\nYou're—uh—certain it's safe to head to the cellars?
We'll head out soon. I've spent enough damn time in this smithy.\n\nIf you're looking for other hostages, try the stables. I could hear Otten blubbering from all the way over here.
Ah! Who's that? That's your friend? Why's he look so scary?

Captain Axius put the key in his office, but who knows if the Painted Eye ransacked it yet. I'd hurry.\n\nI hope you appreciate the renowned Teldundindo giving you the honor of being the first to enter that ruin. It's only been the work of decades.

I shouldn't have kept Phalevon's horn! Minotaurs can sense, smell, or somehow see it, even if you don't blow it. One set upon me halfway to Gideon. I threw the horn into a bush and ran.\n\nI barely escaped with my life. And many bruises!

Keshu told me to take a thinking break. It helps to take a break sometimes, you know. From thinking. So you can think better later.\n\nAnyway, how are the Ambitions doing? Have you figured out a better place to hide them?
Every stone tossed into a pond causes ripples. The stones you have thrown have caused waves.\n\nAs much as I wish to assist you, I need to think of Gideon and its safety.
What is the meaning of this intrusion? Who are you people? What do you think you're doing here?\n\nI warn you, I am favored by the Daughter of Sithis. She will avenge every injury you inflict on me!

Xynaa … she never gave me any indication that she was going to betray us. That she was involved in our creation and wanted to sacrifice us to Mehrunes Dagon.\n\nAt least the twins don't appear to be in imminent danger of exploding.
Let's go find Xynaa. I want her to show me how not to destroy myself the next time I call upon my fire.
Now that we're here, I wonder what happens next.

The power of these two Ambitions grows with every passing moment. You must hurry.\n\nThe path begins to the northwest. Look for the Obelisks of Origin, Empowerment, and Inevitability. Each will reveal a hidden truth.

Well, this is unexpected. I'd resolved to spend the rest of my life in exile, but now Tiras is singing my praises! Do you think he hit his head or something?\n\nI guess anyone can have a change of heart when they have a brush with fate like this.
Bastian isn't wrong. There's a good chance that Larz-Tul decides to make an example out of Quistley. It's not entirely about the gold—a crime boss can't afford to look weak.
I'll be sure to mention your role in my rescue, too. The debt of a Tirethi is a valuable thing—especially one who will one day become a magister!
Did you have any luck snatching some fermented mudcrab apples out of King Boar's mouth?
I knew I would be free one day. Zenithar exacts his price, but never more than what is owed. With his forgiveness, perhaps now I can earn a modest living for the twilight of my years.
You have my gratitude. I gave you my word I would not harm you or your friend, and I will keep it.\n\nBeware the Daughter of Sithis. The thing she calls her brother is a flesh atronach.
Well? Did the letter say anything important?
Ah, fancy seeing you here! \n\nI may not have those seeds, but I have been able to see their effect on Bevene. She's better than new! We could barely keep up with her on our way back to Gideon.
Oh, Farrul! I told him to forget about the past, but did he listen? No!

I really don't think there is anything more to discuss. I am certainly not going back to Leyawiin to grovel for my life in front of some lizard-faced thug. He's lucky I graced his seedy establishment with a touch of class!
I suggest you discuss your options with Eveli. For someone so recently out of her egg, she has remarkable instincts. And a good heart.
How long ago was it? When I crushed you and claimed the Ambitions for myself?\n\nIt must be rather depressing to see that all your efforts were in vain. That my victory is inevitable.
Gods he was gorgeous. I'll find someone, eventually. But I doubt they'll have a chest like that.
Pleasant days, visitors. How can this one assist you?

Commander Ortin isn't listening to what I'm saying! I don't care if the councilor doesn't want to be disturbed! My sister brought a meal to her and hasn't been seen since. \n\nIf anything has happened to Talaise ….
This one has told you everything she could think of concerning Talaise.\n\nNow, please, we are very busy. A fort runs on its stomach, you know.
Another new face in the fort? First Councilor Abor, now you and that cute Wood Elf. \n\nLook, I'd love to chat, but Talaise has wandered off and left me to handle her chores.

All right. I think I figured it out. The assassin followed Talaise down here, murdered her, and took her place so they could gain access to the watchtower. Pretty clever, but they didn't have to kill her.

And so the secret finally becomes clear. The Ambitions aren't just weapons—they are mortals, of a sort. Obviously, these two have been imbued with immense power. Power that has a distinct Daedric tinge to it.\n\nI have learned enough. For now.
Where is your lecherous friend? Just like her ancestor! Ensnaring her betters. Meddling in family affairs. Mathen should be thanking me for sparing him the pain!

I thought you were going to be the last person I ever saw, sera. Next thing I know that Wood Elf's got me choking down some fetching awful mixture and babbling about trees.\n\nSeht only knows what that's all about, but I'm grateful nonetheless.
The Shadowscales remains are destroyed, and we are triumphant. Thank you, valiant traveler. I could not have finished this task without your help.
How refreshing it is to have something to look forward to. An existence outside the walls with a beautiful woman at my side …. It is a miracle. And I have you to thank.
Follow the road. It should be safe up to the fort. You'll find Commander Axius's camp outside Borderwatch's walls.\n\nI just hope you're more help than the so-called professionals he sent in already.
Cres's story has come to a close. It's a bit of a bittersweet ending. What does it say about the nature of such creatures? Ourselves? Fate? Purpose?\n\nI'll draw inspiration from this. I'm certain.
Like I said, Annyce—or Cres—or whoever went tearing off out of town to the east. You might catch up with them if you get a move on.
Don't think she's noticed me staring. I'm too scared to take my eyes off her. Divines only know what she'll do.\n\nWhatever you and Alchemy have a mind to do, do it soon.
I do not wish to speak of what has happened here, but I will. How many more will vanish and return to haunt us if no one tries to stop it?\n\nWhat is it you wish to know, stranger?

Thank you for helping me get my brother back. I have to admit, he does have talent. But I need to get him to take up an instrument that requires fewer live animals. Our egg-mother would be devastated if he came home as a bantam guar.

The councilors should be safe, so meet me at Bloodrun Cave. We need to determine if the Dark Brotherhood is behind the murders or not. Either way, that sanctuary is a threat to Blackwood.\n\nI just hope I don't have another one of those waking visions.

Lovidicus has finally decided to act? Good! Find the Dark Brotherhood sanctuary hidden in Bloodrun Cave and end this threat once and for all.\n\nOh, and take the Wood Elf with you. I understand she's the one who warned Lovidicus in the first place.
I knew the prisoner seemed too calm given the severity of the situation. Examine the lock and see what you can determine.
Look, just leave me alone. I'm going to get enough of an earful from my mom about this.

Sailor! What are you doing wandering around? Get across that gangplank and take the fight to these damned draugr!\n\nIf you're worried about Captain Wereshark, don't be. I won't let a single one of those embalmed bastards past me.
Sithis does not require I maintain my knives, but it does make it easier to do their work.\n\nYou'll have to find your own kills, sailor. These have already been claimed.
The stores on this ship are as bare as the arse of Reinhardt No-Pants. \n\nAh, poor Reinhardt. He'd of loved to see Red Annyce give Prince Vaugr his comeuppance.

Well met, brother! If I had realized you were in the area, I would have suggested we meet for a meal at the Egg and Hammer. The chef makes a superb fungus omelet.\n\nI suppose you're chasing me because of the incident at the courthouse, hmm?
It was nice, you know? But I'm sorry this caused so much trouble.

Salvitto is definitely involved somehow. There are Waking Flame cultists all over the place!\n\nCome on, let's look around. We need to figure out where Vandacia is or at least learn the location of this event they're preparing for.
I think that's everything we're going to find. Let's take another look at the evidence and see if we can figure out what's going on here.
A ship at the Leyawiin docks? Where is Vandacia holding this event of his? And he's got a prisoner? It sounds like he found one of the Ambitions.
Let's find the tailor's shop. We're going to have to look like nobles if we want to get on that ship.

Don't stand on ceremony, my friend! Pick the outfit that brings out your most noble pretensions and I'll be glad to make whatever adjustments it needs. When I'm finished, it will fit like the most supple glove.
She is going to make a pact with me? I get another chance? Oh, thank you. You won't regret this!
Were you able to find the silk? The tailor has been watching me like a hawk ever since you headed out. I don't think he completely trusts us.
And who might you be? This vessel's been hired for a private affair.
We must be on the right ship. Everyone is dressed like they're about to have tea with Queen Ayrenn herself!
We're too late. While you were searching for the key, Vandacia arrived and called in the nobles. He started his presentation.

I'd prefer not to be sacrificed today, if it's all the same to you.\n\nFind the key that unlocks these chains. There should be a copy in Kynreeve Dezerog's chamber in the northern portion of the keep. Hurry, please!
I owe you, my friend. And Sombren always repays his debts.\n\nBut for now, I'd like to meet these other Ambitions and get some rest. This ordeal has been very tiring, to say the least.
A berth? Not a proper bed at all? That is what I get for waiting until the last moment. Believe me, Vandacia will know of my displeasure. It's not like he couldn't afford a better-equipped vessel.
How exciting! Councilor Vandacia always throws the most mesmerizing events! I can't wait to see what he has in store for us this time.
You talk to the Dark Brotherhood person. I'll keep watch for more of the cultists.
He spoke to you; I am relieved. What did he say?
Thanks for—ribbet!—helping remove that curse. I—bok! bok!—never want to lose my beautiful scales again!
I'm just going to ignore the fact that you and my sister stepped out of a tear in space and that a Dremora wants to talk to you.\n\nYes, that's exactly what I'm going to do.
Ah, glad to see you made it out safely.\n\nPlease, we can speak after you talk to Naheesh Nurwul. I know she wishes to thank you.
Gideon? That's a city, isn't it? I suppose we could go with you and the Wood Elf. I always wanted to see a city.

If you think we'll be safe in this Gideon place, then we'll go with you. I sense nothing but good intentions from the Wood Elf. Well, and a little fear, too, but that's perfectly understandable after what Destron just did.

Come, my friend! Let the fury of our combined prowess topple these lures! \n\nFear not! With my mighty sword arm, I will protect you from the fearsome creatures that prowl this xanmeer while you disable the lures.

So now I know who needs to die for this grave insult to the Dark Brotherhood. Councilor Vandacia—the high priest of the Waking Flame!\n\nBut what do you make of that journal entry? About the first Ambition and an attack on Leyawiin Castle?

The totems have fallen silent above ground. I assume you and Heem-Jas were also successful from below.\n\nThe beasts should move on now. I do not think they will trouble us anymore than they did before all this. We will all be safe.
I am glad you and Heem-Jas are alive. I have enough blood on my hands as it is.\n\nYou should speak with Naheesh Nurwul. Don't waste your breath on me.
Thank you for finding my girl. I'd never imagine she'd have gone to such lengths to get away from here.\n\nI should have listened sooner.
Any cultist tries to get the jump on us gets an arrow right between the eyes! Come on, let's move.
It would appear things have gone better than expected! That does not happen often to me.\n\nHah, it is good to have the Hist bless us for once.

It is you! Hail, crow-friend! My keen eyes recognized your ambling gait! The Duke of the Blackfeather Court requires your aid. My flock was lured here by peasant cultists. We were tricked by promises of shinies and now we are all trapped. Trapped!

So many new faces in the city! Are you here about the notice? We can use the help. \n\nIf you need work and aren't concerned about risks, then we should talk. As a representative of Leyawiin, I can assure you that this is all aboveboard.
I'm sorry, I need to think of what to say to my brother once I see him.
I need a minute to take this all in.
This one's raspy tongue will never know the pleasure of licking such divine sugar from such doughy, supple rolls again. Why? Why must Bugtail suffer so?
Welcome, traveler. Rest your weary bones and enjoy the best show anywhere in Tamriel.
Hey, keep your distance, stranger! You'll spook the fish, and I'm spooked enough for the lot of us.\n\nMy advice? Don't linger in town and head back the way you came.
Hmm … a stranger wandering through Stonewastes. Have the scavengers arrived to pick the bones of our village?\n\nIf that's why you came, well, there's not much left. We are already squeezed dry.

Your test is complete. And with barely a scale out of place. Impressive.\n\nDo you like my blades? The hilt is kagouti bone. And Meer-Ta himself enchanted them. Back when I could tolerate the withered toad.
This is some of the worst news you could have brought me, but even so, it's not all bad.

Do these runes have the same derivation? Maybe if I replace … wait … what? Who are you? Why are you interrupting me? Leave here immediately!\n\nArg … you brought that dusty blacksmith from the village. You must need something.

The Chamber of Legates appreciates your help in this matter, but this one wishes she knew why these tragedies plague us. The Elder Council's past has come back to haunt us, or so it seems to Tebeza-ko.

Secrets in government are like water splashing against the shore. Slowly, over time, they erode the foundation of society. It is the way of things.\n\nStill, despite all the tragic deaths, I appreciate that you and the Wood Elf have offered to help.

There is Meer-Ta. I don't think he has seen us yet. I guess you should interrupt him? Not the best introduction, it seems.\n\nRemember, he can be prickly. So be patient. We … I … the village needs him.

Please, I beg you. Do not just stand there waving those seeds around. My stomach already jumps into my throat like a bad frog stew.\n\nPlace the seeds under Otumi-Ra's nose to wake him. And then get rid of them.
Ugh. I could have slept for another day. Or two. But eventually get up to drink.

Impressive! Such strength! Such power! Such a stomach! I did not know they made outsiders who could stand against the might of Argonian ale.\n\nWould you like to continue? Not as part of the test, just for a wonderful time!
This is our home. We will not let someone just take it as they please.
This "army" is nothing more than a collective of hired thugs. We shall have no problem at all.
We'll clear this place out. One Wind is a force on their own. But three? They don't have a chance.

I should have come down here more often when I lived in the village. These tomes are out-of-date, certainly. But an interesting history.\n\nWell, I suppose we're in a battle and shouldn't delay. Did you find the Binding Word?
Did the Dark Elf get you wrapped up in her troubles? I don't know how you managed to make things worse, but she looks even more irate than before.\n\nSo long as the matter is settled, I don't care.

I never should have roped my baby brother into this. I knew the job seemed a little shady, so I thought having someone I could trust with me would be for the best, but I only put both our lives in danger.\n\nNever again.

That was kind of exciting! I've never been to any part of Oblivion before. A lot of it felt familiar though. Like places I've seen in my dreams lately.\n\nAnyway, thanks to everything we learned, I know exactly what needs to happen next.

The portal is over there, little mortal. You do realize how much energy it requires to keep such a passage open, don't you?\n\nNo, of course you don't. But rest assured, it will take you to a spot close to the warded annex. Now go.
Did I hear correctly? We're going to a fort? Why do I have a feeling that this story isn't going to have a happy ending?

Thanks again for what you did for my family, sera.\n\nWe all survived this trial because of you, and somehow Bevene seems healthier than ever! Whatever medicine that little Wood Elf made must have been miraculous.

Not sure my arm will ever quite be the same, but thanks to you one day I can come back and return the favor to a few of those Sul-Xan savages.\n\nI'll never forget what you've done for my family, stranger.

We're it then? Barely half of our caravan. Butchered by those monsters. Fed to that thing. I'd say it makes me sick, but I don't feel anything at all. It may not have drank my blood, but it sucked the life out of me all the same.
You're back? We're still cleaning up after the last time you were here. Has something happened?

The tricky shinies have been destroyed! But one remains! It stands in the room where those peasant cultists attempt to open their gate. A few members of the Court are still trapped there, including myself!\n\nYou must disrupt their ritual to free us.

So you did get my message? I was worried I had hired one of those incompetent couriers. You know, the ones who take your gold and then toss your letter into the dung heap? I've had to eliminate more than a few of those in my time.
There are a lot of relieved villagers here, thanks to your efforts. Well done, friend.
Thanks again for getting me out of there. Shame Mirri's brother wasn't so fortunate, but I'm sure you did all you could. A damn lot more than I managed.
Counselor Vandacia is going to have my head when he learns of this. You don't know what he's capable of!

There you are, free as a spring cricket. I hope you intend to keep your word. We'll need each other out there, of that I'm certain.\n\nThe name's Norianwe, by the way. Of Clan Direnni. Pleased to make your acquaintance.

Those who still live have a great deal to clean up. I need to find any remaining captives, but with the Sul-Xan thwarted we should not face trouble.\n\nThe Ca-Uxith shall start anew. Our Hist requested we watch this xanmeer, and this remains our task.

When the sun rose, I told my mate that I could taste toxins on the wind. He dismissed my fears. Then, this happens. I wish he were here for me to gloat.\n\nDust-on-Scales knows the xanmeer well. His guidance will be invaluable for your efforts.

My gratitude fills every pond in the marshes. Perhaps with your aid what remains of my home can be salvaged.\n\nRockgrove lies south-east of here, or you may take my cart. Speak to Im-Makka when you arrive. She can offer you the necessary guidance.

Wait, egg-friend! If you're headed to the shrine to pay homage, you might want to reconsider.\n\nNisswo Somarz and the keepers have their claws full this day. Outsiders have brought terrible trouble to the shrine!

I suppose things worked out in the end, but let me offer a word of caution. Dragging the Brotherhood into this was risky. What you do in your spare time is your business, but assassins don't like the spotlight.\n\nWe prefer lurking in the shadows.
Poor Mirri. Anyone could tell her brother meant everything to her.\n\nI should be grateful. I am grateful that you two saved me. But all I feel is guilt when I look at her.

This is a far cry from my usual leathers, but I think I kind of like it. It makes me feel elegant and ridiculous at the same time. Which is how I always imagined people felt at those fancy parties anyway.\n\nLet's head for that ship!

You were able to save me, but not Liam? Surely Mirri regrets the time she wasted sparing my hide. If our positions were juxtaposed, I know that is how I would feel.\n\nI should show her my gratitude, but my words would only salt her wounds.
As this one has told everyone who has asked, I have no idea what our destination is.\n\nThat's between the captain and the client. This one's job is to make this deck spotless!
May the Lord of Destruction grant you power, sister.

You nobles are all the same. Bother a honest sailor just trying to get his work done so we can satisfy your every whim.\n\nWell, go ask someone else to pour you wine or to fluff your pillow. I'm busy!
Huh? Oh sorry, I was checking the rigging.\n\nWe'll have the ship ready to sail momentarily. Please make yourself comfortable and enjoy the voyage!

Leyawiin has problems enough, and now the predictions of the Wood Elf archer seem to be coming true. Damn these old Imperial secrets!\n\nCouncilor Jirich has disappeared and my Ivory Brigade is spread thin as a sliver of butter on day-old bread.
The councilor thought she was being followed. Please, check the area around the eastern gate and see if you can find her. If anything happens to the councilor, I'd feel just terrible!

There's some kind of rustle-up at the keep, word is. I heard the garrison is camped out down the road.\n\nEven worse is I dropped my ring down the well. Had to send Bertio down to try and fish it out.

We made it back safely and burned our sodden silks. I still feel filthy. We're both going to need a long, hot bath after all this.\n\nBut what's more important is that we stood up to the Fang-Furls … and won.

The Fang-Furls continue to sniff around our skirts. If we don't move quickly, there won't be a Happy Averno Shipping Company left to save.\n\nDid you find the ledger my brother asked about? I'd like a look. Iulius has no head for sums.
Got a gullet that needs filling? If you're not too choosy, then look no further! These bilge grubs will settle your stomach! There's the smell of low tide in every bite!
You heard the commander. The kitchen is inside the headquarters building, right over there.
Many rains have fallen since I was in a good fight. I look forward to crushing bandit shells.
They will regret taking the life of a member of the Four Winds. I will see to it.
Thank the Eight for Fire-From-Nowhere—and for you! I never could have accomplished this without your help.\n\nI can't believe it's over. These zealots will finally know the truth!

I know you. You brought those guests to our temple. Calia and Sombren and poor Destron.\n\nEveryone in town is talking about your deeds in Blackwood. You helped stop that traitorous Vandacia and his cult. Thank you for that.

Here you stand. The stranger who drifted through the mud to save us. And to think, I assumed you were a crow come to pick our bones.\n\nWe can live in peace once again. And the legend of the Winds will continue.
Clairene is a stranger to me, of course, but part of me feels like I know her, somehow. She said I favored my—our?—father. I've always wondered about that.
I stayed away from this life for too long. Solitude is no way to spend my days.
There are a lot of relieved villagers here, thanks to your efforts. Well done, friend.
Hmph. You know, I still have studies to finish. The village might need me, but my work cannot be ignored.
Well, that's been dealt with rather handily. Time to be on my way. I have a wedding to prepare for.
Sun's greetings, beeko. Your friend's eyes seem gray with worry. What troubles you both?
Bang … bang … bang … goes my hammer. Why, yes … I am strong ….
Ah, travelers. This one looks after inventory and deliveries for the Hearty Hoarvor. If you want a room or food, talk to someone inside the inn.
I thank Y'ffre himself for bringing Lord Bastian here. His mother was a kind woman. She was so worried for him when she knew she would not be able to look after him herself.
You have other business to attend to, mercenary. I'll wait until you're done.
Captain Rian sent me to find you. Your presence is urgently required in Leyawiin Castle.

So this is what it's like being the hero everyone looks up to? Most of the stories I've read end with the hero riding off into the sunset before anyone can properly thank them. But I feel like we ought to stay for just a little while, don't you?
I can't believe Vinnus is gone. He was my everything.
The tension in the air is almost too much to bear. Either we must run, or face our deaths.
I can see the Sul-Xan out there doing terrible things. I keep expecting them to attack at any moment. I bare my fangs at the thought of falling without a fight.
The Sul-Xan can strike at any time. We must be prepared, but we have so few survivors.
Thank you for everything you've done for us. I promise we'll return once Calia learns to control her power.
We defeated the traitor Vandacia's plot and saved Blackwood. And we couldn't have accomplished any of that without the help of you and Eveli.\n\nHold your head high, friend. This day is yours.

I can't believe Councilor Vandacia betrayed us! That he was behind the murders of his fellow councilors. And that he's the leader of a damn Daedric cult!\n\nBut that's a worry for another time. Right now, Eveli Sharp-Arrow has need of you.

I truly never intended any harm to Clairene's brother. I thought I was keeping them both safe. And protecting her reputation, of course. Well, her reputation as the Countess Auzin.\n\nThere was no other choice, really.

Haven't we already had this conversation, brother? Tell your little Wood Elf friend that we are not her enemy and go find the real killers. \n\nYou know that the Dark Brotherhood doesn't play coy. If this was our doing, we would proudly admit it.
There you are! I have a message for you, mercenary.

Well, that was invigorating! Thank you for your help, I wouldn't have been able to handle all of those creatures on my own. You are a marvel across the battlefield!\n\nYou saved the day, my sprightly friend.

I suspect Bastian is overwhelmed by all this. It would not surprise me if he needs some time to accustom himself to the fact that he has a sister. \n\nA sister who is going to insist he come for holidays and visits.
I don't know if the Imperials will truly be willing to help us, especially after finding out one of our own is responsible … but it is our only option.
Good to see you, mercenary, but you're needed in Gideon.
Exciting! I was right to make the trip here! I had heard that Vandacia had found something of great interest but I didn't imagine something like this!
This is his Ambition, is it? Interesting! I thought he would be all bluster, but it looks like he's delivering.
I told everyone they'd be surprised! I knew about this, of course, but was sworn to secrecy.\n\nJust wait until you see what comes next!
Hm. What is this poor creature that Vandacia has in chains? How is this an 'Ambition?'
So it's a sacrifice, is it? Between you and I, this is not a thing I would usually be comfortable with.\n\nThis is where I've thrown my lot, though.
All this for the price of a single Dagon coin … and then they let me keep it! I will never understand the motivations of mortal creatures.

My power. I can feel it building, ready to burst. Sombren doesn't think I have much time, which is why we left without a word. I'm sorry about that.\n\nBut thank you for all you've done for us. I won't forget you.
We won't let Councilor Vandacia get away with this. He has to answer for those murders! And we can't let him and his cult get the Ambitions.\n\nCome on!

Councilor Lovidicus's suggestion is wise. If not Governor Keshu, someone in Gideon should know where to find the ojel-bak. If it's actually a place, that is.\n\nJust make sure you watch out for my sister. Eveli is good, but she's still learning.
I obviously know more about the world and my powers than these two. I look forward to learning more about them and sharing what I know.

Is there a reason you're just standing around? If you are looking for someone to chat with, I assure you, I am not the right candidate. \n\nPlease, I am very busy. If you have no news for me, do be on your way.
I look forward to speaking to this Sombren in great depth. We have so much to tell each other. So much to learn.
Is this Sombren truly like my brother and I? If so, we have a lot to discuss.
Hmph, well, I guess Red Mountain can freeze over.
I heard you were with Councilor Jirich when she … when she expired. I hope you find the cretins that killed her. They deserve whatever punishment you and the Divines can devise!
It was just as I feared. Councilor Jirich, murdered! And so close to the city gates ….\n\nWhere were the city guard or the brigadines when she needed them?

How terribly frustrating! Not only did Councilor Jirich miss our meeting today, she went and got herself killed!\n\nNow who will help me with the project we were working on? It's so very inconsiderate.

Hello again!\n\nThanks for helping me with such a difficult decision, but I think it's for the best. Right? There are so many wonderful stories yet to spin. Look around us! I'm sure there must be some steamy goings-on to discover!
Dare I ask? Is the deed done? Is my little treasure to be returned to me at last?
Greetings, adventurer. Keshu the Black Fin wishes you to attend a celebration in honor of our victory over the forces of Mehrunes Dagon. Can I tell her that you will come?
Gather the Ambitions from the Temple of Dibella in Gideon. Make sure they attend the celebration. I'll see you there.

If you can find Giovanni in Leyawiin, follow him to his meeting with Darene.\n\nAnd also, I know it's a lot to ask, but could you try to get them to abandon all this? The thieving and conspiring? It's not worth it. I just want them to be safe.
Ah, you return. \n\nI hope you did not have too much trouble. I feel as though something has shifted. Sithis has ushered in change. Tell me, did you find the Nightwielder's Tome?

I wish Liam could have been here to see this. He always looked up to me, even if he'd hate to admit it. I can just see him standing here wide-eyed and dumbfounded over the whole affair.\n\nI miss him.
Darkness curse you and the land you have traveled, mortal.\n\nWere I not otherwise occupied with that sniveling wretch of an acolyte I would tear you to shreds.
Who are you? What did you hear?
What do you want?
Greetings. I bear a message for you from the sly Tee-Wan, spymaster in service to Keshu the Black Fin.
