I trust Vos-Huruk's instincts. The two of you must be right about this. I'll admit, I tend to have a soft spot when it comes to Xocin.

I believe this is the right decision. I do not wish to see my egg-brother suffer, but we must look beyond our own needs now. For the greater good.\n\nWhen the time is right, I promise I will help him reunite with Xyria.
Welcome, welcome! Another adventurer comes seeking the wisdom of Melyn Drad, eh?\n\nWhat will it be this time? Conjuration training? Escort through the greater planes, perhaps?

As valiant as a death hopper? As sweet as honeyed mead? No, no, no, that's not right.\n\nOh, sorry! I've been trying to get this line right all day and nothing's working. Do you need something from me?

Oh, hey there. I see that you forgot about me again. No worries. Black Marsh was lovely by the way. Lots of rituals, dark magic, and more than a few things I don't understand.\n\nOh, I think I might be immortal now, so uh, thanks for that.
I knew he'd never change. All these years dead and he's only grown more bitter and jealous. Obsessed with house politics and prestige, like so many others. Stupid.
It will take a moment for me to prepare the conjuration spell. In the meantime, speak with Tee-Wan. After all, the Black Fin Legion owes you a debt of gratitude.

Destruction is a harsh end to anything, but often necessary. Ridding the world of these eggs will no doubt save lives in the long run. \n\nI hope you leave here in peace, knowing you made the right choice.
Well, outlander, at least you understand the value of doing what you're told.
I understand you turned the eggs over to someone who would see them destroyed. You've made a grave mistake.\n\nI have nothing more to say to you.
Behold! The Blackfeather Court is free! Thank you, crow-friend. You have done exceptionally well. You may have eyes of jelly, but your heart is as strong as a crow.

You're back! And you come bearing fowl! Yes, that looks to be Arelette. He can see the profound sadness in her eyes, or judgment, but either is a good sign!\n\nSuch a relief! This one was shedding most profusely from nerves.
They came from all directions. I tried …. I tried … to fight. But just too many.
Naxhosa thinks he's won. That he can take everything. But I'll show him. I'll show all of them.\n\nI just need … a nap. A quick nap ….
Satul-Sa? Is that you?\n\nI knew they couldn't kill you …. You're too strong, too brave. Please … save us.
Ojel? Did you … come to pick the remnants clean? Take what isn't nailed down?\n\nAll the same. All the same.
My home, burned to the ground. My mate, killed. I tried to fight them. I thought perhaps they would end it for me.\n\nBut no. Now I must suffer still.
I can still fight. I just … need a quick rest.
Are you here about the job? You look like the sort <<1>> would send my way. \n\nHe knew I needed someone capable.
Constant Lut-Eileel attacks have taken everything. Soon they will take the mud under my feet.\n\nI cannot stay here. When my wounds heal, I need to follow a trail to a new home.
Another outsider. Our village is under attack, outsider. If you can't help, then leave.
Careful! There are a few insect friends roaming around in the grass here, I'd rather you not step on them.\n\nDid you need something from me?

There is an aura of death about you, a quite dour and pervasive one at that. It's a good thing we found each other, I can patch you up in no time.\n\n Just need to identify the source of your spiritual malaise.
You're back. I'm surprised, thought my bad luck had driven you away. \n\nYou must be braver than I thought to ignore the tides of ill fortune.

I don't know where I'll go, but I can't stay here. Bandits destroyed my home, cut down my family, and took everything I had. How can they do this? If they were Imperial rats I'd understand. But, fellow Argonians! \n\nThere's not much left I'm afraid.

Ah. You have caught me in a moment of indecision, stranger. \n\nI set out with the idea of looking into strange rumors concerning Deepscorn Hollow. Now that I have had some time to think it over, I find that I lack the courage for the task.
Don't let that one take more than his share. I don't care if he has to go a long way to get to the treasure, he's not getting another bite!
Your advice was spot on. She loves it!

He looks just like how he did when I saved him from the clutches of that strangler vine! Well, a little cleaner of course. And with less crying and screaming. But this is how he looks best to me. My dear future husband doing what he loves.
Ah, you are one of the mercenaries working for Captain Rian and the Chamber of Legates, are you not?\n\nI have heard much about you and the young Wood Elf. Thank you for aiding our city.
Hmm. Nowhere to be seen. But all her belongings look like she was just here.\n\nYou know, a less confident Argonian might start to take this personally.
That was the last of the emanations … and the last of the Knights of the Silver Rose. I even see the items stolen from my temple within this vault. All the wrongs here have finally been set right.
Argh, my age is showing. Don't worry, I'll live. It'll take some effort to mend though.\n\nI'm glad that abomination didn't leave you too much worse for wear.

The waters that carry stories can be deceptively turbulent. It is a time of great change. Be careful that you are not swept into the current. It would be a shame to have your tales swallowed up. Then I would not get to hear them.
This battle belongs to the Black Fin, Champion. Yours awaits you in Destruction's Solace. I will look after matters here. Now go!
We'll give you as much time as we can, but I can't make any promises. The sooner you put a stop to Dagon's plan, the better.
I'm beginning to feel that perhaps you lack confidence in my work. Go on. We can deal with this little imbroglio. You're needed elsewhere.
We'll hold the line, to the last of us if we have to, so get on with your mission so it doesn't come to that!

Our enemies are blind wamasu, charging wildly without noticing the threat from behind. I expected more of a challenge. Even Naxhosa's simple brutes showed better skill at observation.\n\nWe shall enjoy the muds of Stonewastes again in no time.

I expected to encounter true threats out here. Not these hatchlings playing in the dirt. Even the magic they wield reveal their simple minds.\n\nCarry on with your efforts. I can easily manage my own defense against these kuudas.

Did you see? I was surrounded on all sides. A weaker snake would have slithered away. But I smashed each and every one of them. Incredible.\n\nI can feel a river under my scales. It roars through me and floods my mind. Let us continue!
This troublesome bargain is nearly at a close. Let's be done with it.

As I surmised, the egonymic is a more powerful version of a nymic. Perhaps only the Princes have them, since I never heard of them before.\n\nSombren has two, perhaps even three of the four. We cannot allow him to return that power to Mehrunes Dagon.
It is not a surprise, but the shock of her death still hurts. \n\nMy stupid, foolish sister. She just had to go to that meeting.

You saved Nirn from a most horrid fate. At least for the moment. \n\nDriving the Crowborne Horror farther back into the Evergloam will at least stave its ambition for now. But if it encroaches upon our realm again, I will call on you.
I don't like that look of pity he's giving me, but at least Martus doesn't look like he'll stand in my way.\n\nI hope you and I cross paths again someday. Him, not so much.
Great. Not that I had any doubts. \n\nYou and Eveli head to Fargrave. Get Madam Whim and Calia caught up. I'll meet you in Nirn once I've got my head sorted.

You've made many allies. I shouldn't be surprised.\n\nI'm sorry I can't join you in this fight. I wouldn't be much use to you without my power. And I'm not sure I want to see how this ends anyway. It will be too painful.

Fluster fume plants grow nearby. Southeast, in the caves of Camp Gushnukbur. As for the tincture of befuddlement, I believe Aurien the alchemist may have one at the outpost south of Bramblebreach.\n\nReturn here when you have acquired both.

The window of opportunity closes quickly, mortal. Both for what I still wish to learn and for you to save your world. Mehrunes Dagon has been thwarted twice, but that will only make him more dangerous next time.\n\nLet us go meet up with the Wood Elf.

Sweet Daffodil will whisk you directly to the location. Once there, you must get past the creatures that roam the place to find Lyranth's hidden lair.\n\nThe pendant will alert you when the time comes to use it. Then just follow the trail of energy.
The Isle of Joys is just off the coast here. We should be able to use this portal to get across. Let's go!
There is no time to waste, little mortal! We must stop Sombren. Go! I will follow you inside.

I'll be honest, I really didn't think we'd survive in there. Perhaps you were sent to help me through that trial. Or maybe it was just luck.\n\nBut now I think we should go our separate ways. The Ravener will be hunting us. But at least I'm not alone.
Well, little mortal? Did you recover the item that maggot stole from my coffer? Was it in one of his pockets as I suspected?

I went to a lot of trouble to acquire the relic they stole from me. With your assistance, I will get it back.\n\nRemember, use the pendant to follow the trail of residual portal magic. That should eventually lead you to the cultists.

You will tell the Dread Lady and her lovely prophet that I cooperated, won't you? Let Lyranth know she should consider the tincture to be a gift? To show how much I revere her?\n\nI hope that doesn't sound too forward of me!
You did well, little mortal. Sister Celdina and her cultists never suspected a thing. And we return richer than when we departed.
I opened a portal. It will take you to a safe location in Marbruk. I shall meet you there.
I'll meet you at the Brandfire Reformatory. I want to see this memory or lost soul or whatever it is when we find it.

Use the portal to the Burn in the nearby plaza. That will take you to the Deadlands and close to the Brandfire Reformatory. Once inside, use the amulet to summon the lingering emotional signatures from the memory fragments to lead you to Moricar.
This Sister Celdina obviously commands a level of respect in the cult.\n\nRemember, you are Devastator Rullen and I am your prisoner. Play your part and I'll do the same.
Sister Celdina is in the next chamber. She's been awaiting your arrival.
Welcome back, devastator. I look forward to hearing your full report.
Your wish is my command, devastator.
Not now, devastator. It's almost time for the next demonstration.
Away, mortal. I do not have time for the likes of you.
If Lyranth suffered any lasting injuries on your latest excursion, you will answer to me!\n\nNow go talk to my mistress. She has words for you.
That power … that man is an Ambition, isn't he? I sense something familiar about him. Or maybe I'm just imagining things.

We can't leave the Anchorite in Valkynaz Nokvroz's hands. That would be a very bad idea. He can use her blood to create devastatingly powerful Incarnates, abominations even I could not stand against.\n\nWe must assault his fortress—Ardent Hope.
A lifetime of study. All my aspirations. Yet, I end up here, in a pit.\n\nNot fitting at all. Just not fair.

I can't wait to return home. Adventures are great and all, but I don't think I want to go on another any time soon. It will be nice to see my family and tell them about Sovisa. \n\nI'm sure they'd help me think of ways to free Ordinator Nilera, too!

I had an idea, and then suddenly … the memories are overwhelming! I see other people … hear their voices. They're filling the room … yes, I've been here before ….\n\nThe amulet, it's like it's singing to me. I want to try something.
You acquired a portal key? Good. The portal may be warded against Kyn, but it has no such protections against you or the Anchorite.\n\nTalk to Lyranth. She has a plan.

Grab the daedrat and prepare yourself. The dangers of Annihilarch's Summit are enough to make even a Dremora pause.\n\nI assume we will have to deal with both Nokvroz's forces and the Order of the Waking Flame along the way.
Tell me that we will find Nokvroz at Annihilarch's Summit, master. Oh, he has so much to answer for!\n\nIf you smash him to the ground so I may reach him, I will gnaw his face off!
Let us find these mortal cultists and finish with them, master. Then we can wreak vengeance on that traitorous Nokvroz!
Lyranth the Foolkiller wishes to speak to you … although what need she sees for discussion is beyond me. We should move against Annihilarch's Summit at once. My missing Kyn may be there.
Please, not now. I need to think.
I … I didn't think Sombren was going to do something so … dramatic. You have to forgive him, he's been very … intense lately.
Tarvyn. Undermining our safety. Didn't see that possibility. Hrmph.\n\nI don't understand his thinking. Why help us? Why invite danger into his home? Mortal reasoning doesn't follow an obvious path.
Uh oh. Lyranth's using her scary voice again. You better find out what's wrong this time.

Hmm. I saw everything my mistress added to that bubbling cauldron. Funny, I'm no longer quite as envious of your role in all this as I used to be.\n\nI understand it goes down easier if you hold your nose before you swallow.
So many new faces in Fargrave! If you need work and can handle a weapon, we should talk. \n\nAs a representative of House Hexos, I assure you that this is all aboveboard.

Another stray piece of refuse has stumbled into our town, I see. At least you're not a Scamp or some other horrid creature.\n\nWell, welcome to Wretched Spire, apparent home to all of the Deadlands' castoffs. Why have you come?
If Elegian devised both the cataclysts and my mask, did I know him before my memories disappeared? And did I know about the cataclysts?\n\nIt seems I wound up with more questions than answers.

So, you figured it out. You know I killed them. Tephilaz, Vontan … even my father.\n\nBut you don't understand! How could you? The Daedra deserve their freedom! They're beings with souls, just like you and I. We should protect them. Welcome them!

My mind grows … still. Free of those awful visions. I do not know you, stranger, but I thank you. And the others I hear.\n\nThe elixir grants me only a few moments of clarity, so speak swiftly. What do you ask of me?

Do not give me that look. Paths diverge and cross all the time. It's in their natures.\n\nSombren has opened the way to Nirn for Mehrunes Dagon. If he gives the Prince his power, then Dagon will be able to merge the realms. You must go and stop them.
We should make our return to Fargrave and locate the rest of our allies, master.

We suspect the Riven Cataclyst waits through that portal, but we cannot be sure. If you find it, deal with its guardians and do what you must until I can join you.\n\nIf this is a trap, do your best to survive and then return to me in the Deadlands.
Talk later! We must get to Sister Celdina and Valkynaz Nokvroz!
You're becoming something of a celebrity, my dear. Well earned, I must say.\n\nI do hope you won't stop coming to visit. Perhaps one of these days I'll convince you to stay.

We have done well, little mortal. The cataclysts are destroyed, Sister Celdina and Nokvroz are gone, and the Anchorite has learned her identity. It will take her some time to sort through her memories, but she is safe. You have seen to that.
The citizens of Fargrave hail you as a hero, mortal. Savor your triumph. It is from moments such as these that legends are born.\n\nLet us return to Lyranth. But … not too swiftly.
Now is not the time for questions. Our enemies await us at the Riven Cataclyst. Do mortals have no sense of urgency?
Go! It's time to end this!
Word of Valkynaz Nokvroz's defeat has spread quickly. I smell Madam Whim's hand in that. So many people have turned out to hail the triumph of Arox the Mutilator!\n\nAnd you, as well, master.

I know that I said last time I was done fighting. But, honestly and truly, I think this is the last one for me. Not that I regret it! Just … oh my. I'm exhausted. And filthy.\n\nBut it's over! We did it! And I was able to help, because of you.
There are others who fought along side us that are not present. They deserve to be here as well. We would do well to find them.
There is nothing defective about my hearing, master. Or my curiosity. The Bladebearer is wrong to dismiss me with such contempt. I am Arox the Mutilator!\n\nHave I not proved myself useful, master?

There you are partner! Now that the dust has settled, I'm not really sure what to do with myself. I suppose we should probably check in with a few people. Word probably travels fast with something this big, but we can't count on that.
If you are truly our ally, mortal, you will slay Sister Celdina in a slow and painful fashion. And then destroy their abominable device—but not before you feed Valkynaz Nokvroz to the machine.

A hero's welcome? In Fargrave? How did they even know? And no one in this city cares about anything that isn't their business!\n\nUnless … this must be Madam Whim's doing. But why would she go to all that trouble? It's so unlike her.

That was incredible! I'm sure you've faced many foes in your time, friend, but nothing is more threatening than mediocre festivities.\n\nEven the minstrels were smiling! Or as much as they ever smile. Difficult to please, that bunch.

We didn't get Sister Celdina, but we stopped her ritual. Destroyed the votive runes before she could conquer Fargrave. Thanks to you.\n\nI don't think this cult is finished, though. I think they're just getting started. We need to decipher that note.

Has anyone ever told you that you have an incomparable mien? Most in this Celestial Palanquin we call Fargrave have the barest patina on their auras. But you! I know multiple buyers who would pay top price for a soul like yours.\n\nShall we trade?
Yes! Madam Whim has been spreading the news! The Anchorite did it! She stopped the Order of the Waking Flame and saved Fargrave!\n\nOh, apologies! I also heard you helped, too. Thank you for that!

Ah, there you are, little mortal. The encoded message you recovered from the bathhouse. That may be the key to determining the Waking Flame's next move and revealing the secrets I am searching for.\n\nWe must find someone who can decipher it.
It approaches. It dares speak. Will it offer the mask to compensate for such insults?

I want to protect the city as much as the next Fargravian, but marching into the Deadlands … ah, well. I suppose we all have to die sometime.\n\nExcept for Lyranth and Arox. They can't be killed. Just inconvenienced for a while.

Ah, darling! How good of you to once again grace my fine establishment. And I see that my information proved useful. You found Lyranth. Another customer, satisfied and content!\n\nNow, what can Madam Whim do for you this time?

I applaud your initiative, little mortal, but the Deadlands will test us all. Mehrunes Dagon and his ilk revel in destruction and constant warfare. Maintain your vigilance at all times.\n\nWe will meet near the keep, provided we survive the journey.
You have set Arox free! Free! Arox owes you a debt of honor, and Arox will pay it, no matter how long it takes. You have my word.\n\nBut pray tell, who do I owe this enormous debt of gratitude to?
A capable adventurer is taking on my assignment? Magician be praised! Maybe it'll finally get done this time.
Survived a lot of the Saraathu Tong's assignments I see. Good on you my friend!
I was hoping you'd be the one to take on this job! You're my favorite of the adventurers Sera Indavel contracts.\n\nSpeaking of, I assume you're here about my latest project, yes?
Kynreeve Rynkyus entrusts you with a mission of great importance. Good hunting, mortal.\n\nAnd do not forget to remove the daedrat from the kynreeve's sight.
You're the Saraathu Tong's latest success story, aren't you. The one with a record of getting jobs done well. Good to see my contract is in the right hands.
I'm glad to see the Tong realizes the importance of the matter I brought to their attention. What can I do for one of the best hirelings in our employ?
Eveli's a little nervous. That Wood Elf can stare down a Daedric Prince without blinking, but public speaking? Perish the thought. She could use your help.

Look at all these people! I wasn't expecting this. I guess it's not that surprising. You've got a habit of bringing all sorts together, don't you?\n \nI think they want a speech or something. I can't stick arrows in a speech! What do I say?

I had a feeling you would not rest until you found me, little mortal. I skirted the Wood Elf earlier, but I know better than to keep you from your goal.\n\nI assume you wish to speak with me. So. Speak.
Oh gosh, you're one of the Saraathu Tong's senior operatives and you've come to visit me? I'm just a first tier Scryer. Unless … Oh! Are you here because of that job I told Sera Indavel about?

Just between us, I'm not in favor of dealing with Daedric entities. And Aurien has become quite infatuated with both the Dread Lady and her prophet.\n\nI suggest caution, traveler. In my experience, little good ever emerges from Oblivion.
Don't worry about me. I'll find you at the base of Annihilarch's Summit
This matter does not concern you, mortal. The daedrat will be dealt with soon enough.\n\nDo not needlessly involve yourself in the Grasp's affairs unless you are ready to deal with the consequences.
You have your reward, mortal. We have no further business with one another.\n\nPlease, leave me to conduct my business. Your time alive is very short, do not waste it on useless chatter.

We're safe here from the worst of the storms and beasts. And the Grasp, I guess. I'm taking some comfort in that. \n\nBut Elisa's not getting any better. I don't know if there's anything I can do but keep the fire burning.

Wasn't sure we'd see you again. I'd already forgotten your face, but it's coming back now.\n\nIt's so cold … even sitting by this fire, I can't shake the chill from my bones. There isn't much comfort in this place, but at least I have Bakh.
The Grim Warden is the last guardian that's preventing me from leaving this prison. Don't fail me now, for both our sakes.

Word of your victory over Mehrunes Dagon spread quickly. A crowd gathered almost as soon as we arrived, and it's only grown since then. \n\nIt's only natural people would want to celebrate. This is a tremendous achievement.

My, my. So many interesting potential clients at this little gathering. Who should I speak to first, I wonder?\n\nDo not mind me, mortal. I am here at your request, I will adhere to whatever plans you have in store.
Since I left Nirn, I've seen horrible cities, savage beasts, and the saddest outcasts. But this place, it's unlike anything else.
Don't like it here. Too open. Exposed. Could be summoned at any moment. Captured.\n\nHope this magic holds as promised.
Merrunz and his putrefying swill of a cult whisper their lies into unsuspecting ears. You do a good thing. Tufeh only wishes she had the skill to help you in your fight.

L—Lord Sotha Sil! Look! I've made it back to Tamriel! I wasn't killed in the Folly, eaten by horrific monsters with far too many teeth, or lost between realms!\n\nSelveni, you're an s'wit. Stop making a ruckus. You're ruining Seht's disguise.

Many have come to witness the hero who defeated Mehrunes Dagon. Word of your success has spread far and wide, master. \n\nIf any more of these mortals attempt to pet me, I will not be responsible for what happens next.
I am unnerved. This place is said to be a fortification, but myself and the others were allowed in with only passing glances. Mortals are far too trusting.

I saw you over there talking to Noroth. Just like I watched you come into town for the first time. Nothing goes on around here without Ruldzara noticing.\n\nWant to know what happened to that Dremora dead on the ground?

Infinite thirst for prepared interest proposal. Turned advice sets vanity in mutual.\n\nMisery wisdom arises through the spirit's scream. Fragile tendrils allow connections to foregone and until now. Your efforts become necessary.
I've dragged my sorry horns halfway across the Aurbis chasing after your mortal carcass. \n\nYou're wanted. In the Deadlands. At Wretched Spire.
I only have time for those who succeed. You better not be here to bother me with your company.
Our orders are simple. We are to protect Lyranth and keep this area secure while you go on ahead. Fear not our failure, mortal.
Our Kyn are delivered from captivity. Now we must gather strength for our furious riposte. Those who dared to mistreat Bladebearers will soon learn the cost of their arrogance.
No point in hiding it now, you probably know everything.
Ah, I was told to look out for you. Apparently you've done some impressive work for the Gleaners before. \n\nVery well. I take it that you're here to deal with those lying cultists?
I've got a lot of writing to do. Figure I'll spend some more time here with the Impressario. Interesting people pass through here all the time, and she's not hard on the eyes either!
You're making a name for yourself among the Gleaners. Still, this one thinks he will hold his judgment for a while longer.
I've heard about you. The others say you're a promising addition to our ranks. I—I don't know why exactly you're talking to me. My record isn't nearly that clean.
Clearly you're an adventurer. Alright, which wound has gotten infected?\n\nOh, you're the Gleaners new gem. Are you here about my plant?
I've heard all about you. Lady Beriel says you've already completed a few of our more dangerous assignments. It's good to meet someone who's already earned her respect. \n\nWhat can I help you with?
You weren't followed by any chance, were you?
Kynreeve Rynkyus has commanded Dothaz to speak with you. While you have my gratitude, mortal, I will not contradict the kynreeve's order.\n\nSpeak to Dothaz.
Mortal. It was your kind that caged me, with the help of Valkynaz Nokvroz and his underlings. You have earned my thanks, but they have earned my fury.

And that appears to be that. Exemplary work.\n\nFrom the looks of things, our web-brained friend here planned to sell several more forgeries. Now that we've apprehended him, the flow of counterfeit artifacts should grind to a halt.

Always a pleasure to see a fellow mortal! These Daedric types …. Well, they're all a bit creepy, eh?\n\nBut look at me, babbling away. Sorry—quick tongue, you know? Comes with the profession! Here for the auction? Nothing but first-rate goods here!

Well, that's Jakarn, the letter, and the medallion all in hand. I'll admit, I thought getting out of here with all three was a long shot. Probably would have been, if you hadn't shown up when you did.\n\nI wish more of my crew pulled weight like you.

You heard what the Sea Elf captain said, yes? He let the plans be taken, but boasted of the lodestone we would not claim. There may have been something here more powerful to plunder than Za'ji anticipated.
Got nothing to say, Nirnling. Nothing you're worthy to hear.
Speak with Kynreeve Rynkyus, mortal. He has a task for you that will help us put an end to the Waking Flame.

Madam Whim once again forces me to carry messages for her preferred customers. The Dremora who orders you about, Lyranth. She and the mortals demand your presence at the House of Whims in Fargrave.\n\nNow.
Well? What are you doing standing around? \n\nOut with it. Or I'll forget that I am making my presence small in this new city.
The Bladebearers clan? I've heard of them. Their mercenaries appear in Fargrave from time to time. This isn't their keep, though. And that sword looks badly damaged. What happened here?

The Bladebearers are not affiliated with Nokvroz or his clan. Their weapon has no reason to be here, especially not discarded and so badly damaged.\n\nWe must reach Sister Celdina and Nokvroz and determine what's going on here.

This was quite the learning experience. Not what I had in mind when I embarked on this journey, but informative nonetheless. I do look forward to some less hands-on exploration of the Eleventh Force for now.
Are you attempting to mask your horrendous stench by rolling around in ash and dirt? Only a mortal would believe compounding filth with filth is somehow an improvement.

Back again? Well, Nirnling, I still offer to guide you through the Constrictions of Moath. Your body will thank you, should it endure.\n\nAnd I'm not lowering my prices just because you're a returning customer.
Well, this little development should help paint myself in a better light. Being abducted is embarrassing. Being abducted by gryphons? That's an adventure.
Again we are here, living one. Nzerru still has the Golden Panacea, should you wish to partake of a cleansing.\n\nNzerru, needless to say, highly recommends it.
So, it travels to the Shambles now, yes? It should take heed—that is a place without law or decorum. A pit for wastrels and curs.\n\nIt has been warned.

Again I greet you as the mouthpiece of Great Vruxynbu, fellow mortal. For all who enter the House of Whims, my master offers spiritual lustration—the caress of his animus is gentle and soothing to a … to a disquieted soul.
It's you! The ghost says everything is all right. Gilfrex no longer wants my tail … or any other part of me.\n\nIs—is it true?
Usually, I have to have my debtors dragged back here kicking and screaming, but here you are striding right in like you own the place.\n\nYou better have brought more than excuses with you.
Can't you see I'm distraught? My guard was attacked! Now who will protect me while I finish my business in the Shambles?
Bring me the stones that prove Rrvenk's words true. I will not ask again.

I thought we were done with you, but no. My mistress Lyranth has once again sent me far and wide to bring you an important message.\n\nShall I impart the words of the Dread Lady now, or would you rather wait until after the Dagonists destroy the world?
A quick study. Not everyone learns to embrace change, but you mortals seem more mutable than we Daedra.

Only a simple mortal could think pushing Tephilaz from his body means anything. Daedra do not die. Such arrogance.\n\nBut you watch, he will return and still insist on his pursuit of a treaty. Though, perhaps you will not live long enough to see it.

Do my eyes deceive me or are you the one who slew the Valkyn back in the City of Ash? Yes I know who you are. Dagon was not pleased with your actions. Practically everyone's heard what happened! \n\nSit by the fire. Let me bless your travels.
Go on, mistress Lyranth awaits you in the Bearer's Rest.\n\nThat encoded note you found isn't going to decipher itself, you know.
Prince Dagon has been massing power and weapons for a considerable time. When the Puissant Lord brings down the full brunt of his strength on his foes, there is nothing left of them to mourn.
I don't like the kind of gossip I hear around Fargrave lately. People are saying that Prince Dagon plans to march. On who? And for what?
I have relayed the message as commanded. The things I do to reduce my enormous amount of debt. Now go. They're waiting for you at the House of Whims!
Destruction's Solace … I never knew if the place was a city or a graveyard. And now there's an army of Daedra massing there? That can't be good.
Mehrunes Dagon's legions are on the move across the Deadlands. You'd better keep your wits about you.
I knew you were capable, mortal. But the more I speak to the individuals gathered here, the more I hear about your exploits.
Have you seen my mistress? Lyranth, the Dread Lady? I've looked everywhere. Has she … forsaken me?
So many mortals in one place. How do you all stand the overwhelming odor?

When you helped us in the Sever, I had no idea you'd go on to save all of Nirn too. We're grateful you took the time to pull our sorry hides out of trouble.\n\nDon't let us distract from your celebration. Just wanted to say thank you.

I can't believe you beat Mehrunes Dagon. I knew you were capable after you helped Bakh and I in the Sever, but I had no idea just how capable.\n\nWe came to Nirn hoping it might help me manage my symptoms. Thanks for making it a safe place to land.
You have come a long way from leading this poor lost soul to enlightenment. I've witnessed a great many phenomena as a Psijic, but never a mortal contend with a Daedra Prince as you have.
Quite the fete. And like all great celebrations, it's full of uninteresting people.\n\nPresent company excluded, of course.

Just dreadful! First, Daedra invade the sanctity of Wretched Spire, where they are not wanted. Then just now I saw one of them, Tephilaz, die in the street!\n\nI have suffered those creatures enough to know they do not just die. Someone murdered him.
The Celestial Palanquin is in alignment, traveler. Will you go to Fargrave?
The tiny, sharp-eared mortal irreparably damaged my servant. I demand restitution!
Mortals. Such delightful little scamps!
You again. Few mortals take such keen interest in the Stricture.

Ah, there you are, mortal. \n\nI serve Madam Whim, not your perky Wood Elf friend. Please keep that in mind. That being said, I shall deliver the Wood Elf's request to you. She wishes to meet with you at your earliest convenience.
You're becoming something of a celebrity, my dear. Well earned, I must say.\n\nI do hope you won't stop coming to visit. Perhaps one of these days I'll convince you to stay.

Just as the Colossus watches over Gonfalon Bay, I was supposed to keep the alliance leaders safe. I failed in that, but at least they aren't in the Ascendant Order's hands. Not yet, anyway.\n\nWhat did Captain Kaleen and the others have to say, dear?
Oh, no. It looks like Lady Arabelle's messenger has gone and had too much of the Duforts' wine. Someone ought to stop him before he removes any more of his clothing.

You. You were at the docks with Lady Arabelle. I thought the Ascendant Magus had returned. He didn't need tools to torture me. Not with his magic.\n\nThe pain, the fire. It was inside my skin! Get me out of here, please!

I'll continue scrying for the missing alliance leaders. In the meantime, you're more likely to turn up something using more direct and mundane means of investigation. \n\nI have faith in you and Lady Arabelle, though, my friend.
Place the idol here and I will invoke the rites to call forth its light.
Valessea told me what happened. I'm glad she wasn't harmed, but I fear for her friend, Quentyn.\n\nYou must help her find him. She blames herself for eluding capture while he did not.
You performed your task well when I needed your help creating an offering for Zenithar. I know you'll do well in this, too.
Well then. Here we all are. Somewhat whole, marginally hale, but decidedly alive. Do you have the scoria?
Something else, newcomer? I'd like to get back to my drink.
Good luck to you, wayfarer. Opportunity is around every corner on these isles. Even for someone like me. You just have to keep searching. \n\nNever know what the tide might bring in.
Just have to find something shiny. Then I eat.
Good luck to you, traveler.
This is a bad sign, walker. Perhaps we should move our hideout onto a vessel at sea? \n\nAt this rate, Za'ji fears the whole island will crumble beneath our feet.

As soon as I'm back in fighting form, I plan to make those Ascendant Order bastards sorry for what they did to us. And I'll help you find High King Emeric. He's too tough to die in a storm.\n\nUntil then, I'm glad Lady Arabelle has you at her side.

I have visited High Isle several times over the years. Never have I seen the ground so restless. It is alarming.\n\nCould Za'ji be right? Could the Ascendant Order be causing these tremors and eruptions?

High Isle feels so peaceful most of the time. That's why I like it here. A respite from all the chaos of the mainland.\n\nBut recently there are Hadolids and rogue knights roaming the roads. And adventurers like you. Too much excitement for me.

Hey there, good-looking! Are you the one Lady Arabelle promised to send to me? I could use the help!\n\nI'm neck deep in a secret mission that involves a beautiful missing woman. It's a mystery straight out of an Investigator Vale novel!

Even without lungs, I cherish being in this fresh air. \n\nI'm glad I put my skull in your care, pilgrim. You prayed at the sacred altars, and removed the ritual items from Lord Leobert's sphere of influence. You are honorable and dutiful.
If I'm going to be ruined, I don't have to be sober when it happens. \n\nWhen are the nobles going to do something about those damn rogue knights?
You brought the scoria? Vinilsare's instincts really are better than mine. \n\nThank you. You just changed our lives for the better. The things I have planned for these scoria!

Tarazka left a lantern at the entrance where this one saw the Ascendant Order take Jakarn's friend. You cannot miss it.\n\nBe sure not to let Jakarn die. He owes Tarazka a great deal of gold and this one intends to collect at some point.

Things took a few unexpected turns, but we delivered the medallions and the peace talks can proceed as planned. \n\nI wonder who the alliance leaders will send as their delegates? Hmm. I haven't seen Rigurt the Brash in quite some time ….
What a day! I suppose that just shows what determination can get you. When the tourney began Aurelia was in the depths of despair. I was … well. I was struggling.\n\nAnd now look at us.
This has to be the entrance to the hideout. I might have missed it if it weren't for Tarazka's lantern. \n\nCome on, let's get in there. Valessea awaits!
Thanks for talking to Tarazka. He's as cranky as ever. Anyway, the prisoner he mentioned must be the lovely Valessea. We need to rescue her. \n\nLet's get inside and find Valessea and her kidnappers!
I've been so tense and worried over mother's rash promise. I knew my Isobel would help make things right. \n\nAnd you too, of course. Thank you a thousand times!
Your actions certainly didn't go unnoticed in there. I take it everything worked out though?
I can't believe he didn't even try to rescue me himself.

You're back! I'm so glad you're all safe. I knew I could count on you and Jakarn to track down Lady Arabelle.\n\nI'm sure Jakarn will regale me with the fascinating tale of your adventure on Sword's Rest Isle … whether I ask him to or not.
Hey, I'm not the brains of this operation. I just go where Lady Arabelle points me. Speaking of which, you ought to talk to her about our next steps.\n\nI'm sure she's got some ideas.
Well, that didn't go to plan exactly, but it was an adventure nonetheless.

Well, so much for my raft. All that work collecting trash for only two trips.\n\nBut we saved Anton and that's all I really wanted. Sure, I hoped we could escape to High Isle. But this will have to do. Thank you for keeping both of us safe.

I'm not well versed in the ways of magic so forgive my skepticism … but how can you be certain the medallion is no longer dangerous?\n\nI refuse to hand the Skald-King something I'm not absolutely sure is safe.
Give me a moment and I'll help you look for the medallions. It's extremely important that we get them back. \n\nThose Ascendant Order thugs must have taken them further into the cave.

You start tracking down the medallions. Valessea and I will catch up with you in a moment.\n\nI want to make sure she's not too shaken up by all of this. I'll be her handsome shoulder to cry on. My shoulders are handsome, right?
Go ahead, good-looking. I'll make sure we weren't followed and meet you inside. Then we can track down those medallions.

I have said all I wish to on the matter. In my opinion, Lady Arabelle's investigation is all too likely to scare off the very people we're trying to catch. \n\nHer reputation as High King Emeric's troubleshooter precedes her.

You're working with that would-be investigator? I can't imagine what you think you'll find here. You should be out beating the bushes for those bandit knights. Or scouring the back alleys of Gonfalon Bay. You'll find plenty of criminals there.
All may not be lost, despite the ineptitude of House Dufort. If pirates kidnapped the royals, they'll seek a ransom rather than kill them.\n\nMost likely.

We recovered all five medallions. And we got to witness a surprise appearance by the mysterious Ascendant Champion we've been hearing so much about. Lucky us. \n\nA job well done, if I do say so myself.

I'm still not clear on all the details, but Lady Arabelle needs us back at the manor. Something about how our actions over the next few hours could determine the fate of Tamriel.\n\nYeah, sounds grim. I hope she was exaggerating.
Figured I'd better not spend too much more time hanging out in the fountain square. Lady Arabelle's got things to do. Looks like some of them involve me.\n\nBut mostly you.

Lady Arabelle is everything I said, right? Tough as a battleaxe but with a voice like an Aedra. Anyway, I'm glad you decided to stick around. There's more to do and I could use the help.\n\nTalk to Lady Arabelle and she'll give you the details.

The Commodore's ship should bear some clues about the magic that binds us. It's somewhere in the cavern but … my memory isn't all there.\n\nThere were captains among our fleet who partook in the deep druids' ritual. Their ship logs might reveal more.

Of course, of course, I had to come and see the presentations. It's good to see my fellow Oaken Order members every once in a long while. And I had some turkey leg, you know. \n\nPlus we'll get to see dear Izzy win the tourney, won't we?

There you are. I'm happy to see that everyone got back from Sword's Rest Isle safe and sound. Lady Arabelle tells me that High King Emeric got his medallion. Among other things.\n\nYou should speak with her. This is my favorite part. When we get paid!
First a pair of uncouth adventurers and now a magical projection. This is highly irregular. Highly irregular indeed!
See, what did I tell you, dear? An all-expenses-paid voyage and a brand new outfit—if a tad frayed and smelling of fish.\n\nDo put it on and let's see how you look as a prisoner.
Our great escape will be aboard a raft made of trash? I'll have to talk to Louna about the state of these accommodations.\n\nOnce we're safe, of course.
Get aboard, you wretch, before I decide to tie you to the anchor and drag you to Amenos!
Thank you, champion. You did as you said you would and claimed the shield before that necromancer stole it from its resting place.\n\nMy duty is fulfilled and I can finally rest.
Amunara's own censer? How dare you use that against her?
Well, pity about the tourney and all. I had planned to buy some new armor if I won.

Good, I'm glad I found you. Something's wrong. \n\nThe Ascendant Order attacked me! I managed to fight them off, but now I can't contact Lady Arabelle. I think she's in danger and she still doesn't know about the altered medallion she's carrying.
We found Lady Arabelle! What a relief! She looks unharmed. Happy even. Is she enjoying this?\n\nGo speak with her. We need to find out what's going on here and tell her about the medallions.
Excellent! I do so hope we'll see an efficacious outcome to today's events. And that Dame Madach is safe, of course.

The map you acquired provides a number of leads that might help us find High King Emeric, Queen Ayrenn, and Prince Irnskar.\n\nAs the line from the Investigator Vale books reads, there's always another mystery. Let's get to it, my dear.

Guess I wasn't the only one who decided to crash this party. That was the Ascendant Magus himself! He told the high and mighty of the archipelago to stay out of his way, and I think they just might. \n\nBut we won't … will we?
Commander Jourvel is expecting you, and Dame Isobel. Go on in.
Eyes as blue as bugloss … hmm, what rhymes with bugloss?
Get aboard, wretch.
Tell Lady Isobel that I hope there's no hard feelings. Sir Langley promised to take me on as his squire after he becomes a knight.
I'm starting to wonder if Isobel Veloise pulled a fast one, making out that Berjo was an excellent second. \n\nHe was rather lackadaisical. Likes books more than swords, or horses. Can you imagine?

Veslyn told me what happened. Is it true that a few of those druids were enough to cause our shipwreck? All those lives lost at sea, how much harm can they do? How many more ambushes do they have planned?\n\nMakes a person reconsider their work.
You! You saved everyone. I—look, I meant what I said in there, I'm done with piracy. \n\nMaybe I'll give working for Amenos a try? Those Mornard lugs are uptight, but they're good to their prisoners.

It pains me that we weren't able to save the archdruid. It really appears that the Allwither took control of her without her consent or knowledge.\n\nAt least we were able to restore the Evergrowth and stop the spread of corruption.

I see the look in Isobel's eyes that I have seen in other young, energetic knights. That first bloom of earned confidence.\n\nTime and experience will forge her, I'm sure. She will be a formidable knight.
We … we'll have to raise a flagon to Dame Madach. Later. Right now, the best way I can honor her is to see to this quest completed.
It's time for me to move on. I need to see the world and learn from it.\n\nI suspect Magister Irin won't be surprised. And Huldressa will probably do a cartwheel out of sheer joy.
Something you need, friend?
Oh, hello. Did I just see you speaking to that bard, Adistair?\n\nI noticed he keeps stealing glances at me. Of course, my father would never allow me to … nothing. Never mind.

You earned the appreciation of the leaders of the three alliances this day, friend. The queen of the Dominion will not forget your actions on our behalf.\n\nWe can't celebrate just yet, though. We still need to deal with the Ascendant Order.

You might as well enjoy yourself while you're here. Perhaps you can slip away once the requisite amount of socializing has been concluded. That's certainly my plan.\n\nLook into the druids. You might just discover they were behind this all along.

I am in your debt, my friend. Know that I will negotiate in good faith for a lasting peace—so long as Ayrenn and Irnskar do the same.\n\nAfter we deal with the Ascendant Order, though, I think. Those fanatics threaten all we hope to accomplish here.
A successful rescue! What sounds better—Za'ji, Deliverer of Freedom, or Captain Za'ji, Bane of Amenos?\n\nTake your time. This one is going to print up calling cards, so I want to get it right.

Thanks to you, the royals have finally reached High Isle. While the Ascendant Order has lost their prizes, they remain a threat.\n\nOnce the Ascendant Lord and his Magus learn the alliance leaders are here, they will stop at nothing to reach them.

My friend. Know that Prince Irnskar will honor the Skald-King's wishes and see these peace talks through. Provided Ayrenn or Emeric don't try to take advantage of the situation.\n\nBut as Emeric says, we should deal with the Ascendant Order first.

You go on ahead. You have other locations to investigate.\n\nI'm going to report this to the guard, for whatever good that might do. And someone should bury those recruits. Not even traitors deserve to rot in a cave.
I see you found the letter. Don't keep me in suspense, dear. Tell me what it says.
Cruel but fair. The dockmaster deserves whatever the Order has in store for him.\n\nLet's get all this information back to Lady Arabelle. I'll see you at the manor.

Not many people escape from the jungle of Amenos. I'm impressed, wayfarer! I only wish Za'ji wasn't the one to pluck you from the shore. I'll never hear the end of his boasting now.\n\nAnyway, Lady Arabelle is waiting for you out back.

What wonders you accomplished, my friend! Not only did you rescue Prince Irnskar, you managed to bring Queen Ayrenn and High King Emeric back safely.\n\nFew heroes can say they've saved a king, a queen, and a prince all in the same day.

So let me make sure I've got this right. Viralaine's been dosing our patients with Vampire blood as some sort of medical experiment? And he was ready to kill Roslenn to cover it up?\n\nYou've got proof, right?
If you enter Stonelore Grove with peace in your heart and walk the path of the True Way, then you are welcome here, stranger.
It appears that you and Druid Audrine did well in the Undergrove. \n\nThe nature spirit wants to have a final word with you, adventurer. Go on. I'm eager to hear what it has to say.
Well, that was an experience I'll never forget. No matter how hard I try.\n\nChyrisnia and Sergeant Brusic told me what happened from the beginning. If you ever need anything, House Mornard owes you.

Hey! Patients can't go this far … wait, you're not from the manor.\n\nSorry for the stern-healer voice. We have a crisis at Steadfast Manor, and I'm frustrated. A mysterious affliction is weakening our patients. We're powerless against it.
I can't believe she's gone.

I'll stay with Ryvana until the lingering magic has been purged. My more traditional, Guild-scholared dispelling techniques might be helpful here.\n\nWhen I'm done, we'll meet back up at the manor. Hopefully Lady Arabelle can put the pieces together.

With Valessea's assistance, we will have this disturbance cleared in no time. Thank you for helping us to ferret out its source.\n\nI hope what we learned will help you stop the villains who threaten our isle.
It's over. The phylactery is destroyed, and I am a knight.\n\nWhat a thrilling adventure.
Good gathering, stranger. I do not recognize you, but I know Druid Audrine very well. What may I do for you this day?
I have nothing more to say to you. But you might ask that ox-brained soldier Armin Demalle what is to become of all the patients who have been in my care.\n\nI doubt he considered that.
What? I was hungry!\n\nLady Arabelle and Lord Bacaro are in the other room. You should go talk to them.
Well, that was the most fun I've had in years! I just wish … I wish Donel and Watkins were here to see it.
Well, that was exhilarating, right?\n\nFinally, my ship is back where it belongs. In the hands of her loving captain. And we have you and this strange hermit to thank!
The way you handled those pirates was impressive … but the way I handled the bow? That was masterful!
Newcomer? Well, you aren't the only one looking for a fresh start on High Isle. Wait your turn. The Ascendant Magus will summon us soon.
What are you waiting for? Move along!
You are a true friend in need. Did the innkeeper give you my official scepter of office?
You'd better give that scepter back to your friend Rigurt. Maybe tie it to him this time so that he doesn't lose it again.\n\nI'd rather not deal with this a second time.

We have two reports that indicate our missing royals may have washed ashore on Amenos—the dockmaster, who told you the Order has moved their search from the Shallows to there, and Tsuzo's crew member, who saw Prince Irnskar swept in that direction.
Do you have that silly scepter? Good. Give it to Rigurt, please. And see if you can convince him to never bring this up again.
You've got Rigurt's scepter of office? Please give it to him. Before he thinks of some other way to show his appreciation for the cultures of other lands.
If we don't manage to quell the Hadolid invasion, I'm going to have to abandon the mine. \n\nHouse Mornard will not be pleased.
I think your friend the soldier wants to speak with you. He looks like he's got something on his mind.
Islinne was responsible for maintaining my vessel. She can be trusted.\n\nTalk to her while I tend to her injuries.
Captain Tsuzo and I will be all right. You go help Prince Irnskar.
You should talk to Armin. I know he wants to thank you for your help.\n\nFor that matter, so do I.
We did it! Once the prisoners and sentries recover, they'll be able to return to work. Without having to worry about being attacked too!
Oh, I feel strange. That was quite unpleasant. \n\nThank you for saving me. I know I'm nothing to gawk at, but I'd prefer to look like this instead of a guar.
I didn't hear what Damard said to Steward Hercian. But I'm sure Hercian left the letter my brother gave him somewhere in the cabin. Search for it if you like. I have nothing to hide.
We determined that Count Damard is the Ascendant Magus. And we discovered his plan to attack All Flags Islet.\n\nAs you can see, I need your help, my friend. The alliance leaders are in grave danger.

You're a new face! Must be here about the notice, am I right? Course I'm right! If you need work and aren't too concerned about the risks, then we should talk. \n\nI assure you, I'm a fully sanctioned representative of the Gonfalon Bay authorities.

Don't worry, Ember isn't in any trouble. While I am not pleased about my traumatized cook, I must concede that everything is back in order and the consequences of Ember's magic weren't dire.\n\nStill, I must consider what to do now.
The Hadolids … nothing stops them or slows them down. The mine should've been abandoned the moment people started to go missing. \n\nIt's a coffin in there!
I don't know who you are, but take Meryline out of here before the Hadolids come back. I've protected her for years, I'd hate to drag her into death with me.

I spent my entire life keeping Meryline out of harm's way! Did it matter? No! Here she is, deep within a mine filled with horrible creatures who've already killed my best sentries. This is a disaster. \n\nHow did you manage to find me?

I appreciate this, stranger. Find my beloved Valentyn before something even more terrible than getting tossed in the stockade happens to him. I'll wait out here and pray for both of you to safely return.

Now that what's done is done, it's hard to fathom that Hadolids invaded my mine. Nothing like this happened under my predecessor's watch. There are strange things afoot on Amenos. Good thing I only have to worry about the mine, eh?

We're done, citizen. Keep talking and I won't be able to ignore you. But if you lose your outfit, look around the stockade. The trusties stash spare clothes in the most unusual places.\n\nNow let me finish my shift so I can go and enjoy this wine.
Go on, little mouse. I told you everything I know.

Marcelle is angry with me, but she'll get over it. These competitions keep our blood hot, if you catch my meaning. While she finds another way out of the jungle, we slip away on the next ship departing Amenos Station. \n\nNow about my gem ….

You have already done so much for the archipelago, I hesitate to ask for more. But while the threat of the Ascendant Lord still looms, Lord Bacaro will be reluctant to move forward with the peace talks. The safety of the leaders is paramount.
I'm still not entirely sure I believe <<1>>'s story, but I've got nothing more to say on this matter. Get him out of my sight before I change my mind.

The remaining Dreadsails are sure to put up a fight, but without their Fleet Queen I favor our chances. Even before you struck her down their maneuvers weren't so deft as they have been in recent battles.\n\nSurely another trick she was behind.
Let me have a look at you, marine. Hmm … yes, you'll make a fine addition to the assault force.\n\nWe only have time to land a few of you, so every fighter we send will have to count for ten.
I have you logged and accounted for. Are you ready to begin your mission?
You can use the dinghy there to ferry your party to the flotilla's flagship, the Lofte Empyrean.\n\nReport to Purser Ashcroft and she'll see that you're accounted for.
I think this next part's up to you and Lady Arabelle. But don't worry—we'll keep the Ascendant Order busy out here.

I hate to do it, but we must leave the skirmish outside the walls to our valiant captains. You and I need to see how matters stand inside All Flags Castle.\n\nRemember, finding the alliance leaders is your priority.
I'll help Lady Arabelle handle this. Go find Queen Ayrenn and the others.

So many people! And most of them are actually talking about you instead of me. That's sort of strange, but rather refreshing!\n\nI think I understand what Lord Bacaro hoped to accomplish. We can be in the same room and not attempt to kill each other.
I'm impressed that Lady Arabelle managed to arrange all this in such a short time. It might not be the setting Lord Bacaro originally intended, but it works well enough for a party.
I need to get off my uncomfortable throne and meet challenges with steel in my hand more often. Still, it's nice to be around people who aren't actively trying to kill me.

You know, maybe I will stick around just a little bit longer. No sense missing a good party. And Valessea would be devastated if I didn't save at least one dance for her.\n\nBut right after that, I'm out of here. As soon as I sample the buffet.
Za'ji will cheer you on from afar! He is very good at emotional support.
Now this looks like a fight! Go on ahead if you need to—I'll find a way to keep myself busy out here.

Excellent! I see all three of our royal guests are in attendance. And Lady Arabelle has worked her usual magic to create a suitable setting for the occasion.\n\nThat woman's competence is positively uncanny.

I can't believe we saved Song and destroyed the Emerald Eye's creepy relic! I was worried there for a moment, but I should have known better. There's nothing you can't do.\n\nThank you, thank you, thank you! How many times am I allowed to say it?

This one hopes you find Jhaka. His life cannot have been a happy one if Sadrith Mora is where he ended up. If he is there, I pray you rescue him.\n\nAnd as a friend of Ember's, know that fresh pastry will always be waiting for you at my cart.
If the owner or his wife ask, tell them I was enthusiastic in serving you.
No bracelet, no information. Simple enough, even for you, isn't it?
The Aldmeri Dominion owe you a debt, friend. And Lady Arabelle, as well.\n\nLet her know that the Ascendant Magus is defeated and the danger has passed. For now.

We will sing of your courage in the halls of the Skald-King, my friend! And in all the cities of the Ebonheart Pact as well!\n\nThank you. And Lady Arabelle, too. I think things would not have turned out so well without your intervention.

Lady Arabelle chose well when she recruited you to help. We never would have defeated the Ascendant Magus without your skill and bravery.\n\nYou have the gratitude of the most beloved ruler in all of Tamriel—me!

Nothing about this peace conference has gone as planned, but the Ascendant Order might have given us something we didn't have before—a reason for the alliance leaders to cooperate.\n\nCan I ask one more favor of you, dear?

Thank you again for rescuing this one. You have a good heart. Jhaka can tell. And Ember would not be with you if she did not fully trust you.\n\nHer trust is a hard thing to earn. You are quite special indeed, and this one is thankful for you.

It is good to see you again, cherished friend. Because of you and Ember, this one has been allowed to rest and recover here in Marbruk. Jhaka feels strong once more. \n\nThis one assumes you are here about the information about the mercenaries?
To see Silverslip's wry smile again, Song's soft face, and of course Ember's eyes, alight with mischief and joy as ever—Jhaka's heart is very full.

Don't worry, I'm keeping a close eye on Song. If she wavers for even a moment, I'll catch her. I'm surprised she's still on her feet.\n\nShe always was tough. I'm not surprised that's changed. And she's just as pretty as I remember, too.

I'll be damned! That's some powerful stuff! I feel like I cleared out ten years' worth of crud! My mind's sharper than it's ever been. You got any more of that? Could come in handy.\n\nWhat was it you wanted to talk to me about again?

Ah, I had a feeling my letter would somehow make its way back to you and your friend. I am Izbadd. I apologize for the deception, but I am not actually a merchant. \n\nKing Fahara'jad's goals happen to align with yours. What say you to a partnership?
Please, I need just a moment to collect my thoughts. So much has happened. I need to think of what to say to Ember and to the others.

I've already said too much. I've put myself at great risk today by telling you all this, but … I love my niece. \n\nGo to the Emerald Eye's camp. Perhaps you will find something there that will tell you where they're keeping Song.
You know, not everyone would be so patient watching a new friend muddle her way through feeling and relationships.\n\nI got pretty lucky finding a friend like you.
Aurelia and I are already making plans. Perhaps we'll see you and Isobel at some distant port on the far side of the world. Who knows?
I feel terribly that he made off with Isobel's ring.\n\nGood luck finding it! I hope he's not too much trouble for you two.

I've got a lot of work to get through here. But tonight I'm going to enjoy a nice cool ale at the Mermaid. Maybe finally work up the nerve to talk to Witalia. Maybe ask her what she thinks of my tattoos? Heh heh.
I was beginning to associate seeing you with bad news. I hope we've broken that streak now.
I had a feeling that mixture was off. Still, a spider's not bad right? \n\nHe'll remain a spider for quite a while. More than long enough for Julles and I to decide where to release him.
We will soon be overrun by more of the Order's forces. We must enter Memorial Hall.
Did that really happen? Did I have the spirit of some ancient All Flags Navy captain residing inside my head? My memory is all a jumble.
Oh, thank you, my friend! I never would have been able to save Lady Laurent without your help.
Back so soon? Are you done with the task Zenithar asked of you?
You don't like me, but you don't win all the time. So let's square things up.
Ugh, I'll be hacking that foul water from my lungs for weeks to come.
The bloodmage will have his reckoning. By my sword, I will see his end!

I am quite impressed with Galedra's alchemical technique! Heh, I thought it was mostly good for potions and such. But that clever woman uses alchemy as a weapon.\n\nI do believe the three of us may go into business together!
You don't like me, but you don't win all the time. So let's square things up.

Friends of Aurelia Jourvel, right? Heh. Yah got me, yah got me. Kiv Lindres, at your service. Your seething knight buddy must be Isobel. \n\nShe wants her ring back, I don't wanna be killed. We've got no problems here.
This is all so confusing! My love, his jealous brother, you. People in other people's bodies. Forgetting the slightest details ….\n\nSay you'll break this dreadful curse, please!
Good of you and Isobel to come. Let me be brief. \n\nRather than being sobered by her misadventure on Stros M'Kai, Aurelia has set off on some kind of quest. I'm concerned for her safety.
Can't ask much more than an honest day's work, can you? \n\nA few coins to keep a roof over my head and food in my stomach is all I need.
Oh, it's Isobel's friend. Hullo friend, hullo Isobel. \n\nIf you're looking for her, Aurelia is Gonfalon Bay … I mean, very much gone away.
Halz is a sneaky bastard. He stole that wine out from under my tusks when we was playing cards one night. \n\nIf I don't get the stuff back, it's going to cost me a month's pay! Damn it.
Leave this one alone. Poor Halz and his aching back.
No one survives the jungle. Not Rassa, and certainly not new meat like you.

Do you remember how angry I was when mother promised my hand in marriage? And just think. If that hadn't happened, Isobel would never have met you. \n\nAnd I'd have never met Marso! I suppose the Divines really do work in mysterious ways.
Thank you … for helping Rayan.
You saved us, walker. As strong as Caska is, that jungle was stronger. I wouldn't have lasted much longer without your help.\n\nIf you need my claws, you only need to ask.
I'm sorry I missed Lady Arabelle. I so wanted to catch up. She always has such fascinating stories to tell.
Do try to make sure Isobel remembers to have fun. She's always been such a serious person, even when she was young.\n\nShe used to salute us with her little wooden sword. So cute!
I'd bet a handsome coin or two that the theft of the ring was somehow related Aurelia.\n\nThose two were thick as thieves growing up, but Aurelia can be um. Careless sometimes.
I'm so proud of Isobel. Watching her grow up, I knew she'd be something special one day.\n\nBut to think she's achieved so much, with you at her side. Tremendous.
Ah, I say! Hullo! You must be Miss Aurelia's friends from home. I hope you can help her friend. They've become very dear to my husband and I.
Ah, you are a sight for sore eyes. I was worried Aurelia might try to save me on her own!
A daring rescue, a clean escape. Well done, my friend! I can't wait to tell Queen Maraya all about it.

Hello again, traveler. Have you studied the teachings of Zenithar since last we spoke?\n\nMy questions may change, but the reward for answering correctly is still the same. So, would you like to test your mind once more?
Y'ffre's bones, I've never seen Sorinne so focused. I think we might just have a chance!

Eager to begin the next tournament? Then I have good news! The Roister's Club just sent word that our new opponents will arrive soon!\n\nWe have time, though. I imagine they are in no hurry to face defeat at the hands of our chapter's newest prodigy.

Nice work out there. I hear you saved that runty Brahgas. More importantly, you saved my job! Mauloch knows Teliv wouldn't have kept an Orc on the payroll.\n\nLet's get you a drink. And don't tell Sorinne, but just this once you can dance on the bar.

Hey there! You left so suddenly after your introduction, we thought Razhamad scared you off. I mean, everyone reacts differently after their first game of Tribute, but I've never seen someone just … flee.\n\nIt's fine, really. I'm glad I found you!
Kishka has a fine reward for you, walker! Of course, you could earn an even sleeker prize if you win one more match …. The choice is yours, yes?
We're doing things my way this time. Win or lose, Raenobi will never forget what happens here today.

Ah, there's my new favorite Roister!\n\nI guess if you've spoken to Sorinne and Kishka and gotten their sage advice, it's down to me to provide the final part of the chapter's introductions and provide one last little acorn of wisdom.

This is terrible, just terrible! I've been dispossessed of property my family has owned for generations, and no one seems able to punish the druids responsible!  \n\nPlease tell me you've been hired to take care of my Eldertide troubles?

Well, well, well. Razhamad's proxy, like swamp gas, rises to the top!\n\nI must admit some surprise. I never thought you'd make it past Daggerfall. But, so much the better! I always revel in destroying new opponents. My strategies are flawless!
How … how did Varnauld's strategy not work? My calculations were perfect! Damn it all!
So, you managed to beat my associate? Well, the winning ends here, beef-wit! The Wayrest Chapter cannot be defeated!

I sense that you carry the cleansing water I gave to Parisse Plouff. Go with care, hero.\n\nAny soulrazer knight is a fearsome foe, but the Sable Knight is one of the first and most powerful of its kind. I will pray for you.

What brings you to our tourney grounds here at Castle Navire? \n\nNever mind that. Have you heard the latest? The Knight Commander has offered her daughter's hand in marriage to the Sapphire Tourney winner! Everyone's aghast!
If you want the latest scandal or gossip, you can talk to Remard. \n\nMe? I never gossip.

So many knights have fallen in battle over the years. I can't count the number of compatriots I've lost in my time in the Order of the Albatross.\n\nThat's why I come to the temple. To remember them and honor their deeds.
I see we meet again. I wonder if your fortunes have changed. Mine have not. This road is as empty as always.
Sorry, mainlander. I'm not guiding any more hunters into High Isle's wilderness until I know there isn't a murderous horned monster stalking me while I'm stalking game.
I can't believe we made it out of there! Those druids were going to come for me next, I'm sure of it.
I don't rightly understand what happened, but Chyrisnia here says you kept us living. Something like that's worth a good and proper drink if you ask me.
Poor travelers lost and all alone? Whatever will you do? Good thing me and my friends found you when we did. Isn't it?

I understand we have you to thank for High King Emeric's safety. And for the other leaders, of course.\n\nI am appalled by the part Damard played in this plot. I promise you, House Dufort will do everything in our power to set right his wrongful deeds.

After so many challenges and setbacks, it's hard to believe all the delegates are finally together in this chamber. Except Quentyn Guerot, of course. I can't support the choice he made, but I hope he is at peace now.
I'm in the same room as High King Emeric, Queen Ayrenn, and Prince Irnskar! \n\nI'm trying to stay calm but I'm not doing a great job.
Oh, prisoner. Why did you choose my gate? I'd rather not have to deal with you right now, so just head back into the stockade. all right.
I'd rather meet the rest of the enemy on a field of our choosing. Let's make our stand in Memorial Hall.
You mind? I'm a little busy at the moment.
A new trusty? The jailers never tell me anything.
I'm on a break. Contemplating the Dark Elf there, at the boats. One day I'll kill him, I think.

For a small island dedicated to the pleasures of wealthy nobles, the library here at the guildhall is surprisingly well stocked. It especially has the volumes I need to help me with my research.\n\nIf you'll excuse me, I must get back to it.
It hurts. My leg!
Those monsters are lucky that rock fell on my shoulder. I was gonna give them a piece of my mind!

I thought Master Healer Viralaine was clear to Armin. No outsiders should come on these grounds! Certainly not inside the manor.\n\nYou see this man? We don't know what's caused his condition. But it seems all our patients share this affliction.

I don't know much more about this affliction. If you can find Mender Roslenn, she's the one to ask.\n\nSorry to say it, but talking to you has taken the wind out of me. Without sleep I just can't seem to focus.

Milagi can only do so much to remain calm. He needs Mender Roslenn here for her knowledge of alchemy. Perhaps she will finish the cure she spoke of.\n\nIf you happen to see her, please ask her to visit this one right away.

You're back! Were my directions helpful? Did you manage to find everything?\n\nPlease say yes—I've listened to Hilgrim belch, groan, and try to convince himself he's not the one who got us into this mess for long enough, I should think.
Darkness. Swallowing darkness. Clicking claws. Everywhere.
Most people come here for the ale. But they brew a fine tea here as well!

House Dufort and High Isle are more or less synonymous. The nobles of the house really care for the island and its citizens.\n\nYes, I happen to be a page in service to the house. That doesn't make my statements any less true.

It is a great city, is it not? But my heart is heavy for those people who never venture outside these walls. Neither Man nor Mer are meant to separate themselves from the natural world.\n\nHow can I help you?
The Ascendant Magus seeks to shake the castle apart. We should go out there and face him.\n\nWhatever happens after we leave this hall, know that I'm proud to draw sword by your side. For High Isle!
Well, well, well. If it isn't the triumphant tourney winner Isobel Veloise. And her second.\n\nHave you come back to Castle Navire to flaunt your incredible luck?
I tried to get the others to wait until you arrived to begin the revels, but it is not in the Gonfalon Chapter's nature to delay a celebration!\n\nSorinne and the others are so proud of you. As am I.

The Society of the Steadfast does much good work, both here in the archipelago and back on the mainland. I, for example, am an advocate. Currently, I am involved in a long-term project to make conditions on Amenos better for the prisoners there.
Who—who are you? Sorry, I'm just a little jumpy. It can happen after you've been through the sort of ordeal I've been through.

So, Sorinne's new, boring friend comes to face Raenobi, yes? This is good. Once this one scratches your dungy strategies to pieces, Sorinne will learn what a fool she has been.\n\nShe will come crawling back to Raenobi soon enough.
Hmm. If they have the properties they're purported to possess, then the enhancement of the olfactory senses must—ah, sorry. Hello there. I'm afraid I was lost in my thoughts. \n\nMay I help you?
You … you beat me? Well, bully for you.
What? How did you do that? How many cards did you play? Wait, how many cards did I—?\n\nZ'en's price my head hurts. Just get out of here. Leave me alone.
Ascendant Order forces surround the castle. We will do what we can to hinder them out here, but I do not know what you will find inside.\n\nI fear the worst, though.

I'm Levus Cavus of the Fighters Guild, currently serving as an agent of the three alliances. I work as a go-between while they conduct some related business here in the archipelago.\n\nI'd do my job better if they told me what that business was.
Queen Ayrenn ran down to the museum below to deal with the creatures crawling up out of the floor. Please, you must go help her. I think she's alone down there.
Again the spirit of the grove manifests, and again it decides to speak through Druid Audrine instead of me. I guess I need to commune more with nature. Get my circles back in alignment, as it were.

I deplore violence. It goes against everything I stand for. Everything I've built. But only a fool can't admit that sometimes you must do whatever is necessary to stop evil.\n\nI will gather what forces I can and get them to All Flags Islet.
Into the stockade, dog! I won't tell you again.

The Mages Guild has finally granted my request to study druidic magic, but some of the druids are being quite problematic.\n\nThose of the Stonelore Circle are friendly enough, but they reveal precious little. And the Eldertide are downright hostile!
Thinking about getting some ale. Should be some vendor around here.
Ah, I see that Druid Audrine has brought us a visitor. What can I do for you today, traveler?
Sorry I started the revels a tad early. Once we knew Brahgas was safe, I might have let it slip that you won.\n\nGuess that means you have some catching up to do. Grab a drink and get to dancing!
Go on and speak to Razhamad upstairs. This is your moment, chum. I'll not take away from it anymore than I already have.\n\nWe can always chat later.
I can't believe Razhamad would put all of this on a player like you. That gaming hall is as good as ours.
It will take some time for Brahgas to learn his place, but don't worry— we are very diligent teachers.

Greetings, sera. I apologize for Brahgas's atrocious manners. We haven't had time to train him properly yet.\n\nNow then. The final match. You appear to have Razhamad's complete confidence—he wouldn't have made this foolish bet otherwise.
Oh hello, how are you? Have you come to participate or are you a valued spectator? \n\nEither way, welcome and welcome again!
There's some excellent food, salacious drink, and damned attractive men around here. \n\nTourneys are a fun time. I must say.
A battle at All Flags Castle? Who could have believed it? Nothing's happened there for hundreds years … until these Tamsfolk brought their troubles here. At least it's settled now.
Whatever the Ascendant Order was hoping to win at All Flags, it's dashed upon the rocks now. Serves them right. Maybe these storms are finally blowing past us.
You were successful, weren't you? Good! I was beginning to worry … I nearly sobered up while you were gone. The horror!\n\nQuickly, give the ingredients to Genalda!
I was just looking for rings, honest! No one was going to miss them and the dead can't use them, but then there was this voice. And the skull….

What's this? Were you distracted by my glory? Do you not recognize the hero standing in front of you? My deeds may be humble, but my name lives on in song. Believe me. And now my squire and I are on our way to give the bards more to sing about!
I'm sorry, but Roister's Club regulations demand you rise in rank before we play. Good luck out there.
I can't accept your challenge, friend. Not at your present rank. I'm sorry.
I'm afraid you need a few more notches in your belt before you can face me. Raise your rank a bit, then we'll talk.
I'd love to play you, but your rank's still a bit too low. Come back when you've earned your laurels.
Not yet, pup. Put in the work. Get your rank up. Then, we can talk.
You've got a lot of work to do before you take me on, pup. Come back when your rank's improved.
You still have much to learn, wayfarer. Rise in the club rankings, then return.
There would be no honor in defeating you now. Rise in rank, then we will have a fair contest.
Oh no, darling. You'll need a far higher rank to take me on.
Do you honestly think you can keep pace with me? You should find someone of comparable skill, darling
Mmm, nope. Sorry. You need to up that rank a bit, mate.
Sorry, mate. Looks like you need a bit more time in the oven. Go find some players at your rank.
Play someone at your rank? Not a chance.
What, you want to face me in a Tribute match? You're getting ahead of yourself. Rank up. Then I'll consider it.
Sorry, walker. You have more work to do to reach this one's rank, yes?
This one would gladly play you … if you had the proper rank.
Your rank is still a tiny seed, beeko. Return to me when it becomes a tree.
Hatchlings must learn to walk before they can swim. Grow your rank, then return.
Sorry, friend. Need a higher rank than that to take me on!
Think you can take down this old bear, eh? Get your rank up, then we'll talk.

If you're looking to rob us, we only have crumbs. \n\nMy knight master was supposed to keep track of our supplies, but I think his vanity is rotting his brain. I just need to find him some sort of adventure so we can go back in triumph.

Come closer. I cannot see, but I would still get a sense of you.\n\nAh yes, the creak of armor—the smell of oil on whetstone. You're a traveler. A warrior. And also a card player, I think. Tales of Tribute, yes? Praise Akatosh.

Ah, one of Verandis's friends. Or just a weary traveler seeking refuge, maybe?\n\nDon't worry. I won't eat you. The Count's particular about the menu here in Castle Ravenwatch. I do have a thirst for competition, though. Do you play Tales of Tribute?

Ha! I cracked it! This smaller pawn serves as a tomb marker. It's just a simple matter of—wait. Who are you?\n\nI'm trying to reassemble an ancient Yokudan parlor game, and you're standing in my light! What is it you want, exactly?
Meryline? She's here? Overseer Barthel really isn't gonna like that.
I don't want to die!
Try not to make too much noise. It attracts the Hadolids.

I've always enjoyed playing Tribute by the candlelight. The whispers of a deck shuffle on crisp linen tablecloths. Quiet. Elegant. Not some drunken spectacle for cheap thrills and glory.\n\nTribute is meant to be intimate. A game for two and two alone.
I was gonna give him to the town guard. But Julles and Galedra have come up with way better ideas. \n\nHehe. Be fun to see how this turns out.
A great day, friend. Despite the Ascendant Order's every effort, the delegates to Lord Bacaro's conference survived and are still willing to talk peace.\n\nYou and Lady Arabelle made this possible.
