A few days ago I was sitting in a dank crypt, wondering when the Ascendant Order was going to slit my throat and feed me to the slaughterfish. \n\nDidn't see anything like this in my future, that's for certain.
Finally, Queen Ayrenn is where she belongs! Za'ji is content. \n\nZa'ji could be content to gaze upon Queen Ayrenn all day, in fact.
I owe you my thanks, walker. I found all the Ascendant Order knights I could hope for during that fight on All Flags Islet. I can finally say my crewmates from the Perfect Pounce have been avenged.

Are you surprised to see a simple sea captain like me in the company of aristocracy? It seems my service to the Dominion lifted the Prowler's name to Queen Ayrenn's ears.\n\nGo speak to Lady Arabelle. We'll catch up after.

Your assistance at Stonelore Grove wasn't an isolated incident, it seems. You have a knack for getting other people out of trouble, my friend. And the notables in this chamber … an impressive collection!\n\nI am honored that you also helped me.

Do you see that house above us? Mandrake Manor, just like that place in the Investigator Vale story. People have been coming and going from there all day.\n\nA suspicious person might wonder what's going on.
You rescued the alliance leaders? I thought you were amazing when you helped me in Brokerock Mine. But, friend, you're incredible!
The alliance leaders live up to their reputations, good and bad. \n\nI can't say I ever expected to share a room with them. But then, I suppose I have you to thank for that.
The turnout for this is incredible. Look at all these lives you've touched. Draigh, I knew you were a hero, but ….
Just look at all these fine people committing diplomacy together! And they say it is all because of you, my bestest friend!\n\nYou must tell Rigurt how you did it sometime.

It seems you've been busy, my friend. Not only did you assist Stibbons and I with that unfortunate business on All Flags Islet, but it appears you aided all these notables as well.\n\nPerhaps I could hire you on full time? No? Ah, just as well.

Thank you again for freeing Lady Laurent from the clutches of that lascivious sea captain. It mortified me to think of him stomping around inside m'lady's perfectly coiffed head.\n\nAnd, truth be told, I was a bit envious, too. No, forget I said that!

There you are! Everyone's talking about how great you and Lady Arabelle are and all the great stuff you did! Everything you did at Tor Draioch must seem small in comparison.\n\nI've been bragging about knowing you, I hope that's all right.

The meeting of the delegates is the closest we've come to peace. I don't understand the motivations of anyone who tries to stop it.\n\nFortunately, they have you here to protect them. I believe Lady Arabelle wishes to talk about that very thing.
What are you still doing here? You want to carry my groceries?\n\nGet back to Gonfalon Bay!

Ah, there you are! I wasn't sure where to start looking for you. Looks like I got lucky!  \n\nIt's a miracle, chum. Truly. Razhamad just said, "Brahgas, go find everyone, let them know the tournament is about to begin." How's that for directions?
Hey! I was waiting for you or Sorinne to show up. I already won my match—figured I'd cheer you on.\n\nJust be careful with this Malilen, yeah? She's a quick thinker. Almost got me a couple of times.
Hey there, friend! You go first, all right? I've got to make sure I'm composed when I battle Lentondil.\n\nI won't lose this tournament. I've come too far.

Surprised to see me? This is the final tournament, my friend. I had to see it for myself!\n\nJust remain focused. Use what you've learned over these past weeks. This match will be difficult, but you can win. I know it.
Quite a fancy to-do here at the castle. It's rare I would bother with such a thing. \n\nI do like the taffy they sell at the booths, though.

Did you see that ridiculous Breton running around collecting trash? Called herself Louna Jolvanne. She's building a raft to take her to Whalefall.\n\nIn all my years as a prisoner on Amenos, I've never seen someone get away. She'll get torn apart.

Steer clear of Tor Draioch, stranger! Those strange motes are everywhere! I saw one of them turn a cow into a person! \n\nI'm getting out of here before one of them gets me! I'm not spending the rest of my days as a farm animal.
No, I refuse to allow an unskilled laborer to mar my beautiful craftsmanship! As master builder of this monument, I absolutely forbid you from adding my brother's name to that plaque!

The archdruid has returned to the Undergrove. Even now, the Allwither compels her to speed up the spread of corruption so it can consume us. In our weakened state, we cannot stop the Allwither from becoming the prominent spirit of the grove.
It is done, hunter. I am not accustomed to working alongside a partner. But you have my thanks.\n\nAt last, the souls stolen by the Pale Worm can rest in peace.
You won two victories, yes? Well played, walker!\n\nAre you sure you do not wish to win just one more match, though? You can earn a greater reward if you do. The choice is yours, of course.

I like to think I'm not easily fooled. But not in a thousand years would I have guessed that Lord Bacaro was the secret leader of the Ascendant Order. No one argued more eloquently for a lasting peace than he did.

Lord Bacaro a villain? Rogue knights collaborating with druids? And what was that about Sea Elves? This visit to the archipelago has been one surprise after another. I owe you a lot, friend. \n\nYou saved my life and you saved my realm.
There you are! And the hero of the day—again! \n\nI knew we weren't done with the Ascendant Order after the assault on All Flags Islet. But I never imagined it was Lord Bacaro who betrayed us.
Wish I could tell you I had a funny feeling about Lord Bacaro, but I'd be lying if I did. Glad you figured it all out before he made a real mess of things.

If I don't cleanse the corrupted Spirit of Stone before it reforms, it will just go on another rampage.\n\nI'll take care of this. Hurry after Archdruid Devyric. Or that path-traitor's going to do this to the next spirit too.

There will be an investigation! I'll make sure of it. \n\nThis enclave will be restored, as much as it can. It'll be difficult. They've lost so many … but stone is eternal, it doesn't give up. No matter how much work it takes.

Laurel will enjoy this. A member of the Druid King's crew wrote it. There's a description of a meeting between the Druid King and the wyrd just before he left Glenumbra.\n\nThey stopped to investigate this Dwarven machine. But something turned ….
You know, I'm quite optimistic about our prospects! Your thoughts on our local delicacies and the best spots to visit around the islands should draw tourists from all across the mainland.
Spirit! Attacked by the Firesong Druids. I know they follow a different path to the True Way, but this? This can't be the path Y'ffre wants.

Like I was telling Dhulef, I want to take Frii to Galen. An island in the Systres Archipelago. They should be with the Stonelore Druids. If anyone can help them find their purpose and keep them safe, it's us.

Portals are fast, but not necessarily linear. We arrived first and were able to give Wyress Matilde the news—both the bad and the good. The Glenmoril haven't kicked us out yet, so I think they believed our story.\n\nWhy don't you talk with Laurel?
Did you find anything? Do you know where they took Wyress Tola? Please, discuss among yourselves if you must, but I ask that you hurry.

Go to Bangkorai. Speak with Wyress Sorcha of the Glenmoril Wyrd. Tell her I sent you. They have a camp just southeast of the city of Evermore.\n\nArchdruid Michiel has already departed, so every moment you delay brings him one step closer to his goal.

The mage and the druid explained what happened. Thank you for trying to save Wyress Sorcha. At least you made that vile archdruid pay. I still don't fully understand the difference between those druids and yours, but I recognize the good in her.
Softer, pulled from the soil, breathing deep. Druid. Druid Laurel. Frii. I am the nourisher of the seeds. Find purpose. Together.
It's done, five-claw. Roneiia could not have survived the cave-in. And the Aquilarios Bequest is buried for good.\n\nRaz could use a break.
Coming right up! I'll bring out a few raw onions for after. Really the only thing that drives away the smell.
Finally! I'll get that authentic seedy tavern experience I've been waiting for! \n\nI've even practiced a bit of braggadocio for just such an occasion!
Finally, a chance to display my immense talent! Thank you, traveler!
Roneiia … Redblade. Whatever she calls herself, she must be here somewhere.

Your job performance was spotless. Must have been my inspirational supervisory skills.\n\nOnce the lava recedes, I can complete my contract and get paid. Then my employer can get paid. Then her employer gets paid. A very sensible system.

Find the alliance leaders at Gonfalon Palace and convince them to wait just a little longer.\n\nAfter that, look for Lord Bacaro at the city's western docks. He's been there for days, overseeing the Society of the Steadfast's relief efforts for Galen.

Five-claw, Lady Arabelle needs you at Mandrake Manor. Ever since you discovered the truth about that lying skeever, Lord Bacaro, Za'ji has been waiting for the chance to move against him.\n\nIt's time to end the threat of the Ascendant Lord, yes?
Talk to the Sea Elf. See if you can get any more details about this attack on Vastyr or the Stonelore seed.

As far as I know, we have nothing to discuss, mercenary. You've been paid for your efforts thus far, and I am not inclined to repeat praise.\n\nMy son, however, does wish to discuss something with you. Talk to him.

Well, my plan almost worked. And you did your part. Even rescued the lordling and the druid, I see.\n\nSealord Nalos may have escaped my blade again, but I got my crew members back. Better than a leak in the hold, I suppose.
Go on, mate. Sir Stefan has been waiting to talk to you.

Archdruid Rahval is right. I must protect Frii. But this is all my fault. If I hadn't rushed ahead to confront Orlaith, Stefan wouldn't have been captured.\n\nI couldn't bear it if Stefan comes to harm because of me.

Laurel blames herself for Stefan's capture. He is dear to her. And to me. I tutored them both when they were young.\n\nThank you again for defending us at the Draoife. I just wish we'd been able to save all the archdruids and not just Ellic and I.
Niraya tells me you saved her from the Dreadsails at Castle Tonnere. And that you recovered the sacred seed of our circle. Is this true?
Ah, there you are. Count Mornard asked me to find you. He requests your presence at Mornard Castle.
I wish I could have been there with you when you took down Bacaro. I really wanted to rip into him and see what a traitor tastes like. Maybe next time, yes?

Ah, the Defender of the Three Thrones and the Savior of the Systres! I'm afraid you've caught me at a bad time. The Society of the Steadfast is needed in Vastyr and my ship is ready to depart. I decided to oversee the relief efforts personally.
Everyone else has gone ahead to Mornard Castle. Lady Arabelle asked Za'ji to wait and send you there as soon as this one saw you. I think she has something to give you, five-claw.

Everything is still exactly where I left it. Examine the note and bottle carefully. See if you can trace them back to their origin. And talk to Ryvana. She's been working to identify the poison and figure out an antidote.\n\nMy life is in your hands.

I'm not sure I can think of too many mainlanders who would have gone out of their way to help the archipelago, not to mention the druids, through these difficult times.\n\nThank you for everything, my friend.
Welcome to Ashcroft's Fine Goods and Imports! I am Philian Ashcroft, proprietor and expert on all things luxurious and exquisite. What might I help you with today?
You weren't sent by Duchess Elea to sign for my delivery, were you? All right, I'll just continue to stand around here and wait for her grace to get around to me I suppose.

So Lord Bacaro—the Ascendant Lord—believes he's descended from the last Druid King through his mother's bloodline. He wants to become the Druid King and reestablish the Ivy Throne.\n\nThat's why he went to Galen. He needs the Druid King's regalia!
Reading is not Raz's favorite part of the job, but so it goes. You take some of these documents, Raz will read the others.

Those who commit themselves to the Elsweyr Defense Force are a rare breed.\n\nWe are no heroes. Just those that have the heart to stand between the people of Tamriel and one of the most destructive creatures to ever touch its skies.
It is with some sorrow that I must inform you this table is now closed.\n\nYou're more than welcome to partake from the complimentary amenities of this establishment. Such as the buffet.

The Firesong took captives during the attack on Vastyr. And they have Druid Laurel. I must protect my people, but I can't trade one life for another. Even many others.\n\nUnless … yes. We give Archdruid Orlaith exactly what she demanded.

The island is at peace, the druids have ended their fighting. Now I need to take up my father's title and become Count Mornard, Steward of Galen.\n\nStill, there are wounds to heal. Things to tear down. Things that we must build anew.
Friends outside my own kind … that's not something Maormer do. But it's refreshing to stand among … allies.\n\nBah. Don't worry. I plan to be on my way before I wear out my welcome.
I understand the pattern of what occurred. Druid Laurel was scouting. Came upon these Firesong Druids. They fought. She was overpowered. Taken away.\n\nThe leaves tremble for her. So do I.
Be careful. There are more Firesong Druids here than I expected. Archdruid Orlaith must be planning something big to bring this many of her circle from Y'ffelon.

I can't in good conscience start the peace talks while the Ascendant Lord—the man I knew as Lord Bacaro—is out there doing who knows what.\n\nI'm afraid I need your help again, my friend. We must keep the Druid King's regalia out of Bacaro's hands.
Hail, my Defense Force comrade. \n\nYour presence surely means no rest for the Dragons flying the skies today.

I'm sorry we couldn't figure another way to get out of this. Frii shouldn't have had to sacrifice themselves to save the rest of us.\n\nI'm just glad you stopped Bacaro. Now maybe we can finally start to rebuild Galen.
They stole the crown, right out of my own castle! How is this possible?\n\nYou said Lord Bacaro is behind this? I think you better tell me what you know.

I have arms and legs again! And feet! Oh, how I missed my fingers and toes!\n\nBut what about Joslin? She was standing right over there, where that tree is, but now she's gone. I don't understand. Is the curse over?
What did you do! I told you to choose Octin! How could you make him stay like that? He's too smart and funny to spend the rest of his life as a signal flare!

Lady Arabelle said she could spare you and I appreciate the help.\n\nBefore Frii was taken by Lord Bacaro, they gave me something. Told me what to do with it if they didn't return. I thought Frii was just being cautious, but I think they knew.
Oh blight! Lady Arabelle triggered one of the ruins old defenses. If she steps off that pressure plate, something very unpleasant will happen. To all of us.

There you are. I decided to see for myself if Archdruid Rahval and his druids were coming to help defend the city. And I wanted to find you.\n\nI made contact with Captain Siravaen. She agreed to aid Vastyr, but only if she can recover her ship.
I got everyone back to the ship before the volcano fully erupted, but even so I'm surprised we're all still alive. Care to enlighten us about what happened inside Mount Firesong, dear?

I'll hand this off and make sure they know to keep the cloth on. After that, it's the client's problem, not mine.\n\nIf we come across a bunch of druids who are all over each other, you can bet they messed with this thing again.

I can hardly believe my eyes. My Gwenaelle, as radiant as the day I first set eyes upon her. I thought I lost her.\n\nBut … the Chronicle. The Spirit of the Path. What a terrible price to pay to set things right.
I didn't expect to leave that ruined castle alive. Thank you, mainlander. \n\nPlease, give the sacred seed to Archdruid Ellic. Tell him I almost failed him, but I didn't … thanks to you.
You two whispered for quite a while. A man could become jealous, if he didn't know better. But the look in her eyes tells me all I need. She's totally captivated by my charms.

Another successful job for me. I always knew I had natural talent. Even with the risks to my life that I endured.\n\nI think Quen wants to talk to you. She keeps eyeing me and scowling. What do you think that's about?
That's a whale of a story, mercenary. But I think I prefer having you with me than against me.\n\nSo, at least for now, you have the respect of the Gilded Blades and their captain.
Sir Stefan still wants to talk to you, druid-kin. And I have a few last preparations to make before we're ready to head to the city.
Stefan still wants to talk to you, friend. You better see what he came all this way to say.
Those druids are doing something to Frii. We need to save them!
You have the seeds … good. Now go to the center of the chamber. Find the mote of light. We must summon Urdiir.
Tell Druid Laurel that I will miss her, friend. I will miss you all.

Druid Laurel will tell you what she needs. Just don't dawdle. Finish things here then meet me on High Isle. We've had the alliance leaders waiting quite long enough, and I have to make some arrangements with the Society of the Steadfast.

Oh, hello there. Aren't you a tasty looking treat. Please, ignore Laniwys. His jealousy won't interfere with you and I.\n\nGive us the key over there and maybe all four of us could go somewhere private? We don't deserve this treatment anyway.

Tell your … extremely handsome friend that Ellorien is taken. Not that she'd be interested in the likes of him anyway.\n\nThere is something about him, though. And you're very gorgeous. Maybe you'd both like to stay awhile?
I've seen magic like this in old druid ruins before. We need to turn both stones to dissipate the ward and open the door.

Druid Laurel and I will help the other Stonelore. Slow steps, crunching over leaves, slipping through mud—they still come, and we will be here for them. Then, Vastyr will open like a flower for them, and close them inside, thorns protruding.
Now this is the pirate's life I've always wanted. Freedom, drinks in good company, and clear horizons!\n\nAnd I suppose you have my plunder?

Count Stefan and Lady Arabelle can't stop singing your praises, adventurer. And if it weren't for you, I understand we'd all be buried under an avalanche of lava. That would have been … unfortunate. Thank you.
I'm sorry I missed the biggest battle of the season. My claws could have earned me purses from those distraught nobles. Ill fortune to Yves and this debt!
What a delectable morsel you are. You must be new to Galen. I'm certain I'd remember a face like yours.

The Society of the Steadfast will continue to sponsor the peace talks and take care of all the expenses. Lord Bacaro set up a trust many years ago, making the society self-sufficient.\n\nI assure you, nothing else untoward will take place.

You have my thanks, traveler! Y'ffre guide your safe return.\n\nYou know, if I were the Druid King, I'd have started with a much simpler combination of animals. Like a guar and an ornaug. Guarnog? Hmm. That's pretty good.
Well, sellsword, can House Mornard count on you to safeguard the island?

I know Joslin is angry. She really wanted us to save her cousin, but you made the right choice. As much as I adore the Green, she would have made a very bad tree.\n\nI'll do what I can, but I don't sense Octin's mind inside the light anymore.
The Firesong Druids … I remember them … threatening me. They killed Eldertide! Why?\n\nI need … to rest … to think about what happened. I just know, somehow, that I have you to thank for my life.

Mohair is really excited. He kept running to each of the berry plants and back to me. I'm pretty sure there are more brambles in his fur than I've ever seen before.\n\nYou've made this little Faun very happy. And the herd, too, I suspect!

Once you collect enough radiant cores, bring them here! Filimor Vette can tell you all about them. You can find him around the stable near the north gate of Vastyr.\n\nHopefully the cores aren't hot. Or dirty. Hmm … you might want gloves!

I heard someone went and wallpapered Llanshara with handbills. Must have been you.\n\nI'll admit it, I'm impressed. Now we just wait and see if there's a Sea Elf who would really take up Lady Juline on her offer.
Count Stefan has been waiting forever to get a word with you. We can talk later, dear. For now, go indulge the count.
Well, I'll be. I heard that you came back to town with a bag full of critters for Juline. And nary a bite mark on you, too! You made out better than I did.\n\nHope she paid you well for your trouble.
Finally, we get a moment to ourselves. I did want to speak with you before Lady Arabelle gets on with the important business.
It seems we got here in time. Those bloody reavers weren't able to lay a hand on Archdruid Ellic—he doesn't look hurt. \n\nGo and speak with him. I'll make sure no others try us.
Thank you. My strength almost left me at the end.\n\nBut I … I failed. I wasn't able to stop them from taking our sacred seed. It's gone.

You know, this is my first visit to this islet. It was closed off and abandoned for so long. I'm glad to see the efforts they've done to renovate it and make it presentable.\n\nDon't mind me. I ramble when I get nervous.
Za'ji and Caska have arrived! The party may now begin!\n\nOh. Right. Za'ji supposes they should finish the peace talks first. Then the party!
Five-claw! Isn't this exciting? Oh, Lady Arabelle said to send you into Memorial Hall as soon as you arrived. She definitely wants to talk to you.
I don't suppose you came all this way just to get a drink with me?
I was sure I was going to die on Y'ffelon. I'm still trying to sort out what happened. What it all means. Why, the—oh, that can wait for later.\n\nIt looks like Stefan wants to talk to you.
The season of darkness and wrath ends. What comes next? Hopefully a season of warm sun and gentle rain.\n\nWe have all shared counsel. Friend-Stefan wants your counsel, too.

Dozens of people lie dead in the cathedral's rubble … including my father. I know I must carry on. Yet Archdruid Orlaith, she also took my mentor. The person I counted on my whole life. She murdered Rahval.\n\nWe must end Orlaith's madness. Somehow.

Glad I caught you, sailor. Sir Stefan has some pretty urgent business to discuss with you. I caught him just on his way out of the city. He was hoping to meet up with you, but I suppose if you're here, it means you didn't cross paths.

Well, you won the day. The city is safe. Doesn't feel much like a victory though, does it? Did you talk to the lordling? I doubt he's faring well. Death always cuts the softest ones deepest. \n\nI'll try not to celebrate Nalos's demise too loudly.

Be gentle when you speak with him. Stefan is a strong man and I have no doubt he will make a great leader for Galen. But right now, he is also a boy who has lost two of the most important people in his life.\n\nHelp him get through this, my friend.

I'm glad to see you and Stefan. We could use your strength.\n\nMy knights and the druids have been holding their own, but the Sea Elves. They arrived in such numbers! I need you to find the archdruids. I think the Dreadsails are hunting them!

One … two … three … oh, sorry, I didn't see you there! I was merely counting the time between the tremors of this island. Subtle, yes, but present if you have the sense for it.\n\nIs there anything I can help you with?

I fear the Druid King is making a mistake. These symbols are gifts from Y'ffre. For centuries, our kings have worn them with wisdom and mercy. I begged Kasorayn not to take them from those who come after us.\n\nBut he insists.

You are home. I am … now. But, I am also fighting the beast. And I am wandering the fields as a child. Ah. I see.\n\nThe temporal distortion—the knot—had wrapped around an artifact. Cutting the knot exposed its energies. Made me multichronal.
Are you the one they hired to save my son? Find him, please! I beg you. Nobody else will help me besides the druids.
I heard that Juline got those kingsblood blossoms she was hoping for. Your doing, I assume? I'm sure the plants are none too happy, but I for one am glad you made it out in one piece!
You didn't step on a beetle coming up those steps, did you? No? Damn. I could have used one for this poultice I'm making.
You must be the mercenary Gastoc hired. Good.\n\nI'm sure we druid initiates aren't supposed to say things like this, but make sure that beast suffers!
Lady Juline told me about your work in Y'ffre's Path. A job well done, adventurer! I'm not too embarrassed to admit you have rekindled my warrior's spirit today. No small task, mind you.
You. There when blood soaked the leaves, when eyes opened and roots awoke. Defender. \n\nYou feel it, yes? Unrest in the soil. Wrongness.
Lady Juline sent word that you returned with the radiant cores. Top-notch work! I'll study them once they've cooled down a little. Don't need to burn a hole through my workbench.
Druids attacked! Why spill blood on holy ground? Afraid, confused! Actions come as waves crashing against the shore.
Ho, sailor! You're harder to pin down than a sail in a windstorm. Sir Stefan wants to see you.

The Society of the Steadfast is a philanthropic organization. What few knights I have are purely for the defense of our pavilions. Our assistance to Galen is as relief, nothing more.\n\nIt's good to see that Sir Stefan has confidence in you, though.

I knew you were no ordinary adventurer the moment you arrived in Vastyr. If there's ever anything the Society of the Steadfast can do for you, you only need to ask.\n\nNow go on. Talk to Sir Stefan. Or should I say Count Stefan? He's waiting for you.
Imperials never do well with isolation, do they? She'll tire of hiding before long.

Well, that's done! What's next for us, I wonder. I do like it here on Galen. And I enjoy spending time with Laurel and Stefan. But I'm an adventurer at heart. The sea calls to me.\n\nPerhaps we'll cross paths again, mate. Stranger things have happened.

I'm not sure why the lordling invited me to this, and I'm not sure why I decided to come. I suppose it's interesting to see how the various alliances negotiate. It appears to be a lot less bloody than the functions I've attended in Pyandonea.

Lady Arabelle insisted I stay close, but I'm really not all that comfortable inside structures such as this. I prefer more humble dwellings or simply the open fields. \n\nAnyway, she really wants to talk to you.

What an inspiration you are! So productive and efficient. Watching your promotion from lowly guard to a mineral surveyor to savior of the isles gives me hope.\n\nIt also makes me a bit jealous. I worked so hard. I hope my efforts pay off financially.
So you really are a hero? I'm glad you didn't turn Joslin and me in to the authorities for our little … ah, procurement enterprise.\n\nBut hey, thanks for what you did for us. I won't forget it.
Well look at you, the hero of the archipelago! Mind if I tell some of these nobles that I know you? Maybe they know someone who can help me change Octin back to how he's supposed to be.

All these lords and ladies! Usually I stay out of sight around these types. I'm not sure how to act while mingling with them.\n\nIt's worth it to celebrate you, partner. You always seem to show up just with you're needed.

I suppose I should offer my congratulations. Not only did you help Quen and me, but I understand you calmed the volcano. Nicely done! Maybe next you could do something about mudcrabs. I really despise the shells and those weird eye stalks.
I should have known you had a hand in all of this, outsider. You seem to have a knack for making hopeless situations turn out for the better.
That Druid Laurel of the Stonelore Circle, she's trying to get us all to work together. I suppose these peace talks are giving us all ideas.
The wind vortex will take us higher, away from the rising lava.
Welcome, my friend! As happy as I am to see you, I didn't expect a return visit quite this soon.\n\nTell me, what brings you back to Vastyr?

My Unu is safe and well, thanks to you. I almost wish they had gotten their grubby hands on him, Unu would have left some nasty burns to mark this discretion. \n\nI'm the only one he doesn't spit flames at, you see. What a sight that would've been.

Just in time, my friend! This nose of mine has yet to lead me astray, and I could smell those peppers and that smoldering cut of meat drifting in on the wind.\n\nDid you manage to get the brandy, too?

Feels good getting to run through a few of those bastards. We've been cooped up for too long. \n\nYou might want to talk to the captain. Looks like she's waiting for you. She doesn't like to be kept waiting.
We meet again, shark-bait. Guess I should thank you for helping the captain get us out of this scrape.\n\nEh. Why don't you just go talk to her?
I'm sorry, if you're looking for a bottle of my Vastyr Brandy you'll just have to be on your way. It is highly sought after, and I don't sell to just anyone.

My heart feels lighter knowing Frelene will know my fate. I know her heart will ache, but I hope having my ring will help. \n\nI appreciate you doing this, my friend. A peace is settling over me, knowing that this is in your capable hands now.

I'm sorry, I suppose I'm still in shock. I've known Jocien was gone for some time … but you spoke with his ghost!\n\nAnd he wanted me to have his ring, after all this time. Romantic, isn't it? He was always like that.
Be careful. We certainly don't want to let the Firesong catch us sniffing around their stronghold. Archdruid Orlaith must have gathered her circle for a reason. But what's she planning?

Stefan doesn't take kindly to threats. Must be the Mornard in him. I'd say he means to do something about Archdruid Orlaith sooner rather than later. Go on, talk to him. I'm curious what he has in mind.
I would like to observe this gathering of leaders for the Eldertide. If nothing else, I will tell everyone there what you did for my circle.
I know the Firesong have not earned a place at the talks. But I will come, if you will have me. I must bear witness for the rest of my circle. And offer to make amends if I can.

I'm sorry I missed that last battle. At least Archdruid Orlaith is no longer a threat. Good work on that, mate.\n\nSir Stefan wants to talk to you about the druid regalia. Laurel wants to keep them separated until a new Draoife can be formed.

Hero of the Systres! We're still making repairs after that unfortunate incident at the last banquet, but Duchess Elea said to direct you to the knight commander's office in the knight's wing were you to return.\n\nI'm sure she'll be happy to see you.
Lord Bacaro betrayed us. He took the Druid King's staff! Please, speak to Druid Laurel. She needs your help.
Druid-kin, if only you had gotten here sooner. But the river flows on and day gives way to night.\n\nDruid Laurel will tell you what happened.
Captain wants to talk to you. Let me catch my breath … I haven't run that hard in a long while!
What is Count Mornard thinking? We have some of the best knights in the archipelago. We don't need the help of those strange druids.

More druids in the city? Oh, they say they're here to help defend the wall, but all I see are more mouths to feed. And you know who's paying to feed them? We are! I may just withhold my taxes this season.
Druids attacking druids, what's this island coming to? Poor Galphen is beside himself.
The Dream of Kasorayn has long been a subject of debate among the druid circles, but to go to war over a prophecy? That's madness!

The Firesong Druids have gone insane. They truly want to wipe all of us from the archipelago. We need to work together, city folk and druids alike, to stop Archdruid Orlaith before things get really out of hand.

Now we are both connected by our agreements with the Prince of Fate. Next comes the harder task. Saving Apocrypha and thereby preserving Nirn.\n\nThese Dusksabers from the Telvanni Peninsula. Without any other information, I suggest we start there.
Glad you're still on your feet. So many others are buried in the rubble of the Cathedral District.\n\nListen, Sir Stefan sent me to find you. He needs to see you up at the castle.
What? Discovered already? Zilipif, you watched the door, yes? How could we be discovered? Unless ….\n\nYou aren't one of Valinna's new scribes, are you?

This place is magnificent, is it not? Being underground, the air is the perfect temperature and quality to preserve our records. \n\nBut all of that will mean nothing if Valinna has her way. We must recover the staff from the Deadlands.

As soon as I learned of more threats against the faithful, I came as quickly as I could. Unfortunately, I arrived too late to save Naraheida.\n\nI'm glad you're here, though. I wanted to tell you what I uncovered concerning the traitor, Leramil.
Walk in the ever-vigilant gaze of the Golden Eye, chosen.

I foresaw that you were the one mortal in all of Nirn to aid us. I also saw you die at the traitor's hands. Many, many times.\n\nI am pleased with this version of events. That the traitor Dralys has fallen and the glyphics are secure. Very pleased.

Sailenmora remains ever the same. And yet everything has changed for me.\n\nI thought I knew everything about the Lark of Rosgard, but I didn't. I tried to stop one crisis of faith and ended up with my own.
Look around, friend. All these people are here because of you. I don't know what we would have done without you.

You'll find the entrance to Kemel-Ze here. It may be difficult to spot, but the elevator should take you straight into the Magician's laboratory.\n\nNilphas Drethan will be there somewhere, find him and rid the holy site of the Painted Eye.
This one has nothing left to tell you, walker.
This one and his kin shall make haste from here. We are not welcome in Telvanni lands.\n\nMay your feet find warm sands, walker.

Thank you again for your service. I would say that we are in your debt, but this is what Rilasi hired you for, is it not?\n\nI did want to ask you something. I noticed that the talisman appears a little … different.

I don't know how that sergeant knew about my involvement. I hoped having you free them would rid me of this inconvenience. \n\nStill, despite this unfortunate turn of events, I ended Luaffyn and you followed directions well.

I'm required to inform you that as a contractor for the Kwama Consortium you are held to the highest standards of conduct. But on a personal note, thank you. \n\nNow, we'll need to inspect the pens, speak with the overseer, and take note of the queen.
Error. Critical Components Missing.\n\nCritical Component Location: West Wing.
What happened here? Did you do this? \n\nI knew Rilasi was desperate to get me, but I never thought she'd order something like this.

No one goes to Sailenmora anymore, and now I can see why! Getting badgered by priests and Buoyant Armigers isn't worth seeing the one impressive relic they keep at the shrine.\n\nIs that where you're headed?

I assume that fool Thoryn sent you? Well, your presence isn't required. I am a Clockwork Apostle, and I have the situation here well in hand. If you'd be so kind as to vacate the premises, you can reassure Thoryn that he has no need to worry.
No need to tell us of your exploits, mortal. We can hear. Though still faint, the hum of knowledge steadies. The threat has passed. \n\nBefore we conclude, return the relics you secured.
I have been conversing with Curate Gadayn. I find him … interesting. But now we must return to the business at hand. The fates of two worlds depend on what we do next, proxy.\n\nShall we proceed?
Sign the contract, mortal. I offer to bind myself as a surety to you. A promise that in acting as my proxy, you do no harm to this world of yours.

I'll clean up my mess here once my strength returns. Then, I can teleport to Fargrave. No need to concern yourself further about me, mortal.\n\nYou're a capable sort though. Maybe you'd be interested in joining my show? Hmm, perhaps not.
I told Abbot Ilvel all about Blightcrown and the plot to steal the Fulcrum Obscura. And I told him everything you did for us. He wants to talk to you.\n\nBut not too long. He needs to rest.
You again? And without that good for nothing, lazy Randas in tow.\n\nI told you before, I don't have any time to waste on nonsense today.
I can't leave these two to fend for themselves. These kwama are vicious, and whoever those cultists are, they certainly aren't friendly.
Without Ulfengar, me and Barluk would have never made it out of there. Whatever he chooses to do, I've got his back.
The overseer might be right. Hard to forgive the Consortium for leaving us here. But I'd do it all again if it meant I could protect my chitinous little rascals.

Some will feel relief. Some will despair. Understand that our kind rarely get an opportunity to choose their own fate. A rare moment like this can overwhelm us.\n\nIn any case, we will get to decide for ourselves.
Greetings, friend! It's good to see you!
Greetings, my friend. It is nice to actually have a chance to introduce myself. That other form was, well, a bit limiting in terms of communicating effectively.\n\nI'm Vorm, and I am in your debt.

Evening, friend! Or morning. Hard to tell in these Daedric realms! You've just stumbled upon the oddest family reunion this side of Fargrave. I'm Ysgild and this annoying tome is my brother, Vorm!\n\nAs you can see, we're in a bit of a conundrum.

The researcher taps into currents of fate that aren't hers to access. And look what it does to her.\n\nLeramil has been performing stunts such as this for more than a century. I'm surprised she's still somewhat sane.
Poor Leramil! That seemed to take a lot out of her. You should check on her, my friend.

You did it! You ended the cycle! I'm slowly starting to remember everything. And yes, that includes all my deaths. But best not to dwell on that now. Thank you for everything you have done for me—er, for us!
You should speak with Meenai-Shai. He's very energetic for someone who was just released from an endless cycle of deaths.

Young Gadayn told me of your mission for the Prince of Fate. A strange and perilous ally … but I thank you for saving the Necropolis. We owe you our lives.\n\nWhat happened in the catacombs? Did you find the imposter who called himself Prelate Faram?
You can go explore all you want, but I'm just a librarian. I'm keeping my distance.
Hermaeus Mora and the Rectory Corporea owe you a debt, adventurer. One we will never forget to repay.
Ah, the curious Watchling has returned. I think she wants to talk to you.

Meln the Mouthless let down his guard and paid the ultimate price. His body has remained here, forgotten and undisturbed for decades because he preferred solitude above all else. Now Master Shelreni has both Meln's spirit and his Black Book.
Apocrypha is no longer safe! Can't you feel it, stranger?
I expected to have Tel Rendys all to myself today. And you're certainly not one of Captain Zenfis's vampire mercenaries. So who are you and why have you come to this tower?

We cannot argue with the facts before us. Remnants struck down by the Dreamcarvers now wake. We can hear each other once again.\n\nLord Mora sent us a test. Only he can know our fate and we should not try to divine it. Our task is service and faith.
I no longer feel the Great Eye's presence! What could have happened to him?
So many of the ciphers have fallen ill. Even the Daedra seem susceptible to this terrible plague!
Do you smell that foul odor in the air? It's a corruption unlike anything I've experienced before as a Cipher of the Eye.
Why do the Great Eye's Daedric servants attack us? Have we done something to displease Hermaeus Mora?

The ritual worked, proxy. We located the entrance to the Infinite Panopticon—at least, until it moves again.\n\nLet us head inside and try to stop the Hidden Kindred from locating the secret they seek.
All right, so you figured it out. Maybe Master Shelreni will give you a bonus.\n\nI still don't trust anything in here. You go and touch the sword. I'll stand by and wait to see what happens.
Two cairns activated, one more to go.
Feast your eyes. Is it not magnificent? Shelves and books grow musty, but the items in here will never age or turn to dust.
We were too late.\n\nI thought something might come back to me, seeing Reynila. She knew me. And now she's just gone.
The gem is right over there. Take it and leave this place. I'll literally go wherever you take me, as long as it isn't here.\n\nI have no desire to be here when Shelreni returns.
This hall seems grander than the other locations we passed through. Proceed with caution, proxy.

I was beginning to fear the worst. Tell me, did you destroy the corrupted scrolls? And did you find Cipher Sabinius? I can't believe any cipher would willingly take part in a plot to wreck the work of Quires Wind.
If you have further business with me, get right to it. If you don't, you're blocking my view.

I see you found the papers and placed them on the correct desk. And my paws are clean in this matter. Thank you.\n\nNow it's just a matter of waiting for Mouth Delvi to resign. Then I can swoop in and claim the position.
Understand, mortal. I wish no harm to befall anyone. But I will have what was taken restored. It is my eternal undertaking.
Interested in a game of dice, my dear? Or perhaps you want to buy me a drink?
Are you here to try Cortin's Cordial, the new improved formula with half the bitterness and twice the benefits?\n\nOne sip will get you hooked! Guaranteed!

Hmm. It's not a good idea to look at your own fate. I wonder why my master is so fond of that particular one?\n\nSpeaking of fate, you certainly helped me salvage my own! To think I came this close to being tossed into the nemesis looms!
Excellent work, meddler! We even managed to avoid creating a realm-tearing temporal anomaly. Those are a nasty sight, I assure you.
Use the portal and return to Leramil. I wish to be alone with my memory.

What you described. How could Torvesard change a memory of Hermaeus Mora? How could he alter what happened so long ago? Such a power should not exist.\n\nThis sensation. Bafflement. I do not care for it.
I wasn't expecting you to be the ones to rescue us. My claws were just starting to wear through my bonds. Still, you have my thanks.
All claws and scales intact. Fresh air and real light, that's what's needed now.
That Dark Elf's arrogance is a scythe on my good mood. Still, we are free now.
After you. My portals are perfectly safe. Usually.

Aww. Look at that Infernium, it's just trying to protect the sarcophagus. Or maybe it's trying to break the sarcophagus?\n\nEither way, it'll probably try to bite us if we get closer. It might even try to bite us if we don't.

Thank the Eight you came along. I had no idea how I would do this on my own. I know Sathile would just throw me out again, but Nathyn is my whole world. I can't possibly leave Tel Dreloth without him.\n\nThe first step is finding that key.
Mother … I've never seen her like this before.
You should speak to my son.

Meln and Gadayn have more experience with the dead than I. I shall review my volumes on Daedric Princes and the fundamentals of Oblivion. You never know when a seemingly irrelevant detail may prove useful.\n\nReturn here after you finish at Tel Baro.

Oh, the heights I have fallen from! Forced to work alongside mortals and the spirits of mortals! As for the curate's plan, I can't see if this course of action will untangle the threads of fate or not. So my professional advice is … sure, whatever.

I was still in the access corridor when Master Shelreni unleashed her attack. By the time I reached you, you were unconscious and Shelreni was gone.\n\nI think Magister Gothren can explain all this better. He wants to talk to you.

Magister Gothren and I go way back. He was a pompous arse then and it seems nothing much has changed. Still, he is in charge here.\n\nWhen you talk to him, remember that you represent me. It will add power to your words.
Rest. I need rest.
Oh, good, you stopped. No time for details. People eager to see me dead will come over that hill at any moment.\n\nSo, want to earn some easy gold?
Are you … are you real? Not another one of those awful dreams? And you look undisturbed. Don't you hear the terrible whispers?
It's really done, then? Sharp and Dimik-ei, both alive and well. Reynila would be glad to see it.
The journey towards my ascension was made a little easier today. Despite the hordes of Daedra and the smell of burning fungus, I'd say this went remarkably well.
Remember, warn Garalo Givyn about the prism. About the ….\n\nOh, who might you be? Ah, my assistant, of course! Come, come, let us explore the folds of time. Nothing but wonder awaits you!
Another job done. Despite all the running around, it always ends the same. I quite like the simplicity, to be frank.\n\nBe sure to look me up again, hero. Always a pleasure.
The world is darker without Reynila. I don't know what we're going to do without her.
A new servant? I suggest you dress more appropriately for the position. The masters are strict about decorum.\n\nNow, what do you want?

So, you have the boon. Which means the secret had value. Madam Whim believes what she said.\n\nYou helped lowly Hezehk. Reminded me of my purpose. Even though relying on a mortal embarrasses me! But, I'll give you something of mine with great value.
I was worried maybe I'd feel hollow after delivering Sondivel from this world. But I don't.\n\nInstead, there's this … lightness. I wonder if Dimik-ei and the others feel it, too.
Glad I didn't have to see Sondivel again. Always awkward to run into the boss of a job you ran out on!

I met this Imperial at the Sober Nord. He'd come all the way from the Telvanni Peninsula to sell some tonic of his.\n\nI really shouldn't have let him drag me outside the city to show me the power of his miracle elixir. But we'd been drinking, you see.

Thank you for your work in closing this matter. I saw Naryu and you whispering in the corner. Are there things you're not telling us? Ah, well. I'm sure everything important will come to light in due time.

Word travels fast in Ald Isra, outsider. I heard you work with the dark lady. Last time she came through, I had to clean up three bodies. If she sent you to ask for my help again, the answer is, politely, no.\n\nI do not want her to be angry with me.
I told him it was a bad idea. Zavaal. Said he underestimated them.\n\nAh, damn, this stings.
I haven't felt this terrible in a long, long time.
This one's father may not be bothered by the treatment of these mercenaries. But Urishabi cannot say the same.
I'm all right. Sharp looks like he wants to talk to you.

The hero who saved Summerset, I knew you'd be the one I'd speak to here.\n\nIt's not often that one bound by mortality comes to my attention more than once. Most, like Nilphas Drethan are wisps of smoke in the fires of time.
Talk to my employer, stranger. Master Shelreni is not known for her patience.

Ah good. Researcher An'Xeh said he would find someone to help Warlock Vanton.\n\nThis one is not sure how well informed you are, but we face a problem that we cannot solve ourselves. We're too vulnerable.
We'll do what we can out here. Once you step through that portal, don't lose yourself in Vanton's nightmare. I don't know what we'll do if you fail.

Talk to Scholar Arlance when you arrive at the tower. He's watching over Warlock Vanton with the rest of the mages. I only left to find help when we figured out what Vaermina's Daedra planned.\n\nThe portal is right there. Quickly now!

What can this simple healer do for you? Either of you.\n\nAnd I do mean simple healer. I am not an expert of healing magic, but I am good with herbs. And offering advice. You'd be surprised at how just listening to someone helps them feel better.
The Masters Conclave is in session. All other business is on hold. Come back later.
The Morag Tong's assistant? You certainly get around. While I appreciate what you did for the assembly, this is a matter for the masters and the magister. You really shouldn't be in here.

While I mourn the loss of a valued servant, I am glad that you eliminated the spy that was stalking these halls. I was hoping to finally get on with this conclave when you and Meln showed up, though.\n\nWhy is it that magisters complicate everything?
First Magister Gothren arrives to take the reins of our conclave, and now the spirit of Magister Meln? I knew gathering the local masters all in one place was a bad idea ….
Meln is dead? I knew it! Master Foves owes me two hundred gold!
You! You must warn the other masters! I can no longer stand by and do nothing while Master Shelreni continues along this dark path.\n\nHer actions threaten the entire peninsula!
I think we need to stop that monster and rescue Master Marena.
You should see the reams of parchment I've scribed about our adventures together. Endless research opportunities.\n\nYou do still want to continue our collaboration … right, cohort?
A treat to see you. This one's just cranky because he's losing to me, yet again.
Those druids are doing something to Frii. We need to save them!

Incredible. Somehow my experiment seems to have created a new, previously unseen mystic phenomenon. One frayed fate consumed the other, by means and for reasons unknown.\n\nI'd be even happier if it didn't want me dead. Hah!
I hope you're happy. It's going to take hours to clean this up.
Extra toes? No walls and ears dry. No runny-nose brain soup either. I'll say success. \n\nFree. No walls or home. Just feet to talk and eyes to read. No toad am I.
I'm restored! Herm'us Mora is bountiful. But at what price?
I think I'll stay with Leramil. See if I can be of any help with her research.\n\nYou tend to get into fights, and that's not something I'm very good at.

The Great Eye trusts you, mortal. I suppose that means I must, too. Which indicates I'm probably going to regret everything that happens next.\n\nGo talk to Leramil. She has that look on her face again.

Despite her protestations, Master Shelreni will talk to you. Wizards like her are proud. They enjoy the sound of their own voices too much to be silenced by the grave. \n\nI should know. I was just like her when I was alive.
The main entrance was definitely sealed by a powerful mage. We won't get in that way. Well, since we're here, we might as well look around.
I would have led House Telvanni to new heights. Instead, I lost everything. All my work, unfinished. My legacy in ruins.\n\nThis is your fault, outsider. You and those duplicitous Daedric Princes!

Morian really is a singular creature. He's so much more special than me or any of the other ciphers just by the nature of what he's done and what he knows.\n\nPlease help him escape the gallery—he's too special to rot in here.

I was not sure if that would work, proxy. It … weakened me. It will be up to you to safeguard us against whatever awaits inside. Like Scruut, I feel the agony rippling through the very fabric of Apocrypha. How that will manifest, I hazard to guess.
Vaermina has a guardian. Looks pretty tough. Much too tough for my fragile tentacles and soft, squishy eyes. I'll leave this mostly to you, mortal.
I shook off the worst effects of Vaermina's corrupting presence, but not soon enough. \n\nThe intruders have fled, but the Vault of the Glyphic. You must determine if the secret remains secure.
Azandar al-Cybiades, back in my life. No doubt you're the new assistant? \n\nTottering along after him like he's got all the answers? What's made you desperate enough to come talk to me?
Your bearing speaks well of you. I've come to the City of Tombs in search of the brave. The Tribunal Temple has need of you.

Oh, thank the Eight! You stopped!\n\nI've had people pass by without even a glance my way. Suppose they must think I'm bait for some sort of trap with clothes as nice as this. Really, I just need an urgent favor.
Stranger? What business do you have with me? I am trying to tend my aunt's funeral pyre.

Scruut can tell you all about the process for inscribing her records in the Chronicle of Apocrypha. You should talk with her.\n\nMeanwhile, I shall discuss arrangements for returning to Necrom with Curate Gadayn.
Oathman Balver Bemis. I like the sound of that, don't you? If you need any favors from House Telvanni, well, ask Spellwright Varsva. But I can guarantee you, I'll put in a good word for you.
I suppose some gesture of appreciation is in order. Here, have some coin. I hope that will cover the costs of dealing with this fool, even if you did help him in his scheme.
Saw you talking with Retainer Balver. He's up to something. Perhaps old Edril can help you find out, eh? For the proper price.
I've no real care for what happens next. Llaro needs to find a new retainer.

Did I hear Leramil correctly? We can soon return to Necrom? That would be splendid! I can't wait to put the Fulcrum Obscura back in its proper resting place in the Necropolis.\n\nStill, if we're almost finished … I might not see Leramil again.

Apocrypha may require more paperwork than all the Great Houses of Morrowind combined! Talk to Scruut and find out what's involved in updating this Chronicle of Apocrypha. It sounds either very important or exceedingly boring.
Your master beckons, mortal.\n\nTell him I have no wish to continue the assault on his realm. In fact, I wish to end it.

My role has always been to observe and repair the lines of fate. Never to unduly influence them, no matter how sorely I'm tempted.\n\nSo, while I was waiting, it was just a nervous habit that I haphazardly started checking the nearby lines of fate.
Pardon my impertinence. Now I see that you bear the mark of Hermaeus Mora and travel with one of the Great Eye's Watchlings.\n\nHave you come to aid us, stranger?

The Great Eye turned to you to untangle the threads of fate, so get to it. Leramil waits for you in the Necrom ruin that once served as a repository for mortal books. \n\nImagine, a place where mortals go to purchase books—with gold! How barbaric!
Peryite's plague-dog defeated, Vaermina expelled. You did well, mortal. Fate chose wisely when it selected you to aid me.
You return. Did you find Cipher Akacirn, and put a stop to this madness with the Numinous Rite?
Another mortal seeking my wisdom? What have I done to earn this tiresome privilege?\n\nCome now, get to the point. You have already distracted me from my work. I might as well know why.
Tem sees you, mortal. Adventures, triumphs, that have happened. Or may happen. Or may never happen.\n\nSpeak, and Tem will tell you what you wish to know.
Ah, another wanderer, fearless of these dangerous times. But perhaps well-protected against fear.

Look, I don't want any trouble. Federo is a good enough sort. He wouldn't mind that I've holed up here for so long, honest! \n\nBecause, er … we were engaged. To be married. As you can see, losing him has made me take to drinking. Oh, how I miss him!

You found the gate! Now the real battle begins.\n\nA fearsome Herald has taken control of Bastion Nymic, subverting its defenses. The Golden Eye needs you to destroy this powerful adversary. But the Herald is protected by a barrier.

Tremble at the sight of my greatness! I am the avatar of a dark power beyond your shallow comprehension!\n\nDoes my presence not turn your joints to stone?! Do you not quake in your boots! Do I not terrify you?
Your record has been successfully inscribed into the Chronicle. Go on, now. Curate Gadayn's waiting to talk to you.

The abbot insisted on the immediate return of the relic, friend. Sorry you missed that part of the ceremony. But now he wants me to give a speech?\n\nI'd rather go back to Apocrypha with you and face a horde of corrupted lurkers!
As long as Torvesard seeks the final glyphic, our contract remains binding. Your work is not yet done, chosen of fate.

Magister Goreth referred to you as the mouth of the mouthless. I suppose that fits. Look, I've never been very good at this, but I wanted to thank you.\n\nIn life, I was a secluded old wizard who cared nothing for anything but magic and my own studies.

When I heard about this gathering, I knew I had to be here. You allowed me to learn from my mistakes and set things right.\n\nAnd with you as an inspiration, I'm facing the challenge of taking on the Lark of Rosgard with renewed vigor.
Since we seem to have a moment, tell me what occurred at the Prismatic Iris Shore.

Thank you for what you did for us here, traveler. Our honored dead are at peace again. Gadayn, however, is not. I fear I surprised him when I called on him to speak.\n\nWould you talk with Gadayn and set him at ease?
The Cenotaph firmly remains in Remnant control, thanks to you. Our group is stronger than ever.

Apocrypha's pain is like salt in my orb sockets, mortal! Whatever happened, I have no doubt it was your fault. So, you must fix it. Make it so I can hear the soothing adjurations of the Great Eye once more!
A Masters Conclave at Ald Isra? That hardly ever happens.
These Telvanni masters are so high above my station that I just refuse to think about them. They can deal with their problems, and leave me to mine.

Don't tell this hireling, I just need to keep him busy while I deal with other more important matters. With the gathering of the Telvanni Magisters, I've enough trouble to deal with without him tailing me.

Can anyone really blame me for worrying about the gathering of the Telvanni Magisters? I mean— seems like something important is going on, and I'm not supposed to worry about it and just do my job. How am I supposed to fix this book?
It comes to a close, but will this be the end? The omens are never precise.
Though the danger wanes, more lurks yet still. My spines sense the presence.
You haven't seen a book lying around anywhere nearby, have you?
Entry to the Masters Conclave requires special dispensation, outsider. Speak to Sentry Valyne if you seek admittance.
I wish I could be in the chamber when my master delivers her speech. I wrote it, don't you know?

Your resistance is thrilling, Sharp. Keep it up. I need to know where my weaknesses lie.\n\nBut we both know you understand exactly what I want you to do. It's only a matter of time before you give in.

The mouth of the mouthless. I suppose you want me to say that you and Meln were right. That I should have taken Shelreni's threat more seriously.\n\nWell, let's pretend I said that and move on to what needs to happen next.
By my horns and by my blood, my Prince will be restored.
Careful. Work with too much efficiency and Harn will find some excuse to keep you coming back.
Get moving, merc.
Go on, then. It's your turn to plea for Harn's mercy.

The Morag Tong agent has returned and the tower is in an uproar. Zemzo does not like all this drama.\n\nStill, this one will stand his ground and report everything back to Master Thilse as accurately as possible.
Well, I guess that ties up your part in all this. You better hope you chose correctly. I would hate to have lost a fine servant for nothing.
How dare that wretched assassin speak to Master Foves that way! He could snap his fingers and she would dissolve, yet she treats him like he's a knee-high whelp.
And I thought I had it tough. You fought to save all of reality!
I don't mean to burden you with my troubles, stranger, but something dreadful is happening in Alavelis. I'm lucky I escaped when I did.

Azandar seems to have mellowed, somewhat. He's been here a few moments and he's hardly insulted anyone.\n\nThat rubric he made … it's probably tucked away in an old chest or barrel. We rarely throw away anything around here.

This is unheard of! We traveled a long way to visit our ancestors in the Necropolis. But the Keepers of the Dead refused to let us in. They turned us away!\n\nOur ancestors will become angry and curse us! They'll curse the entire peninsula!
I can't believe they won't let us enter the Necropolis! They've never closed the catacombs before. How can we honor our ancestors if we can't visit them in the Necropolis?
We traveled for days to make this pilgrimage. Days! And they had the audacity to send us away? It's disrespectful to us and our ancestors! The Temple will hear of this!
I look forward to his no doubt heartfelt, impassioned words.
Please don't distract me. The masters take a dim view of servants that shirk their duties.

Incredible. It's just like the High Elf said. She described you down to your footwear. And she even knew exactly when you'd pass by this exact spot.\n\nI have a message for you, serjo. From Leramil the Wise.

Surprised to see me? I'll admit that deciphering Dreynis's notes have proved to be quite the ordeal. A surprising number of sleepless nights, but I wouldn't have missed this for the world. Not when there are so many important people in attendance.
It seems Dreynis suspects my motives already. Why don't you speak with him? Sound him out, if you will?

I was booking passage to leave the peninsula when I heard about a gathering at the Necropolis. Glad I could make it!\n\nIt's lovely to see you again. And Nathyn's here, too! In his own way. Did you see?
It's you! Hello! I'm still getting the hang of this magic and I have no idea if it's working.\n\nCan you and Dacia hear me? Am I coming through?

To think you stopped to help the survivors of Anchre Egg Mine when you had all this, this … adventuring doesn't even do it justice, does it? \n\nI won't forget you. Even after I leave the peninsula behind, I'll remember you.

Congratulations, friend. Malsa and Barluk would've been here, but they're spending their last few days on the peninsula drunk and singing your praises. You made a real difference here. I hope you know that.
For a mortal to help so much, we find it encouraging. Perhaps we cannot understand our fates at first glance. Fighting against the odds could be part of the calculation.
This one could not resist coming when he heard you were to be part of this celebration.\n\nIt is good to see that fortune smiles upon you and your deeds!

About time the Necropolis reopened. This city hasn't been the same since they closed the catacombs … but you know all about that.\n\nYou should head to the Necropolis. I'm sure the abbot wants to thank you personally.

Why, it's you! I must admit, I was satisfied to hear that Master Shelreni Baro had met her end at the hands of her own allies. It was … fitting. \n\nMany interesting people are gathering at the Necrom Necropolis. You will be there, yes?
While we may have failed to unlock the secrets of the tome, I can't help but feel I've learned a valuable lesson. Had you not been here, my daughters may have lost their father as well.

I hope this doesn't paint me in a poor light, adventurer, but there's still the matter of the scattered pages. Father will recover soon and Tralise, well, I'll do what I can. But, my mind can't help but wander.
Is that you, outlander? I can't see anything. I can feel the curse's absence, though. Like a great weight has been lifted. It seems the ritual worked precisely as intended.

The tides of fate swirl around you with glorious fury, proxy. The future of at least two worlds hangs in the balance. You have a talent for changing destiny. It has been noticed.\n\nHence, I bring you an offer from the One Who Knows.

This is very odd. I've heard troubling rumors lately about the scriptorium of Quires Wind. Something about the Daedra and the mortals there acting strangely. But now I hear nothing at all.\n\nI'm worried.

Proxy, there are two other tasks we must accomplish while we attempt to locate Torvesard and the stolen glyphic. One concerns updating the records of Apocrypha. The other requires us to return to Necrom and rectify the original anomaly of fate.

What? I was resting! Besides, you got along fine without me. I'm awake and materialized now because I never could resist a good celebration—that includes not a single other Telvanni who is out to get me.

I was sorely tempted to inscribe these events in the Chronicle of Apocrypha, but then the Great Eye reminded me that reality must forget what happened here—again.\n\nIt makes my tentacles shudder, but that's the way it has to be.

Leramil sent for me and I got here as soon as I could. I'm glad I heard the story of what you did. And I'm glad to share this celebration with you. I just wish I could remember everything come tomorrow. An experience such as this should be cherished.
You've been inscribed in the Chronicle of Apocrypha! I knew you were special, but not to this extent.

So long as Tho'at Replicanum exists within the Infinite Archive, it'll never be quiet.\n\nYou could return here and collect your dues after fighting the first Replicanum, but don't let that stop you from fighting her more.
Can we get on with this? Hear whatever the High Elf has to say before her brains start leaking out her ears. That happens when you gaze too long into the annals of Apocrypha, you know.

Bravo, outlander. A rising tide lifts all boats, and all that. Do be sure to bring us any more pages you find. Countless only scratches the surface of the number of lost pages and your assistance will surely usher in a new era for this family.

I can trace the lines of destiny, from insignificant happenings to cataclysmic disasters. But what am I sent to do? Find the chosen of fate and deliver another meaningless message.\n\nWell, it does concern the end of reality, but still.

Master Malkhest seemed rather urgent about finding help. I can tell when mortals become worried. They make a bit of a face. I don't dislike mortal faces, with their noses and mouths. \n\nUh, would you like the reward Master Malkhest left for you?

I don't know what your plan is, but you may not want to be alone when you go in there. The archive isn't as friendly as it used to be.\n\nOh, you'll have to take a portal too. This space right here isn't big enough to hold the infinite.
You're back! Do you have the supplies? Can I make my translation? Will I finally be done with this project?

To think that masked brigand was Amaurel Verdulis. How many seasons we spent planning this marriage! If I may be vulnerable for just a moment? I had grown quite excited. Not for the business of it all, the coin, but to be held.

A proper introduction, then. I am Amaurel Verdulis, Grander's bride to be. You can tell him it was me. I'm certain my betrayal will make for quite the waterworks. I harbor no ill will toward the man, only what he represents. This contract.
Selling just a few bottles of Blue Aedral goes a long way to keeping our winery open and our workers employed. Speaking of … can I have the wine you recovered?
Found that valuable wine, eh? All of it? I mean, I hope you found all of it.

I am relieved to observe the perpetuation of the macrocosm—bah. Our reality has not unraveled yet. For now, we must wait and watch.\n\nEventually I shall notice Torvesard's passing in the threads of fate. Then I shall send for you, proxy.

Leramil the Wise sent me to find you, proxy. Hermaeus Mora summons you once more to his service, in accordance with the contract you signed in Necrom.\n\nThe realm of Apocrypha is under threat again. And with it, our own as well.
Gather the relics, proxy. Then I shall open a portal to the realm of the One Who Knows.
I may have more appendages than you, but I'm not a pack bearer. Leramil specifically told you to take the relics, so get to it!
By the looks of it, you gave Orissa bad news. This one will mind his own business, but perhaps you should talk to her.

Oh good! I was starting to worry those necromancers got the better of you. Or that you fell in with their ranks! Hah. Just kidding. Who would be tempted to fall in with a group like that? Ridiculous.\n\nDid you happen to retrieve those shards?

A good officer gives credit where credit is due. You did good here, comrade. Rustwall won't be ready to host any visiting dignitaries for a while, but we learned the fate of my cohort and stopped an invasion.\n\nNot bad for a day's work.

That was the last of the Recollection. Now the Oathsworn can rebuild. It will be difficult, especially without Axeborn Khurga, but that's just the way it goes sometimes. Dulzush and Garm will get the pit straightened out in no time.
These ruins sound dangerous. We should be prepared for trouble, friend.
It's hard to believe Curate Gadayn is gone. We knew those tears in reality were dangerous, but to lose one of our own ….

Ah, interesting. Old Ri'jhaad is an expert concerning those days. Strife consumed all of Elsweyr when the cult of Riddle'thar spread like a storm across the sands.\n\nOne could say Boethra died in that time.
If you think you're ready, then off you go. The Legion has work ready for those willing to do the job.
Well? Finish your report, mercenary. The signal fires in Varen's Watch. Are all four of them ignited?

We wrecked Lord Gallio Valente's operation and his coven is broken. I'll stick around to help Ursilia destroy the tainted vines and any remaining samples of Vesper Valente. Then it's on to my next adventure, I suppose.\n\nJust like you, my friend.

You've returned! And in much the same way that you left, stepping through a mysterious portal. You must have an interesting story to tell … but it looks like your friend wants to speak with you.\n\nGo on. I'll wait.
The wounds are painful, but this one thinks they are mostly superficial. Dro'vir will be all right. You should head inside and join the party.

If you're here to complain about that pamphlet I posted about the jungle growth blazing through the countryside, I'm not overreacting. You just aren't seeing the danger it poses to everyone working outside of Skingrad.

It seems the cook knows more than he is willing to let on. How very curious. Mizzik will have to make note of this. At least this confirms that the residents of the estate are keeping their secrets close to their chests.
I can't believe Betu was so brave. Chasing down Pelena like that. I've never seen him so singularly focused.
Next, we have to figure out what our precious Lady Sowerra is doing.

Mizzik's snout wrinkles at the stench of both fresh and old death. Betu led us to the memorial of the lost Uriel Weatherleah and now we find the cook, freshly poisoned. Let this one see the confession letter.
Do you feel it? Like thousands of aggravating daedmites crawling across my tentacles. There is definitely something not right here in Apocrypha.\n\nHurry up and use the Skein!

The plan Scruut has brought us sounds tenuous, but we must put our faith in the One Who Knows. \n\nEven with Ithelia gone, the tears ripped in the fabric of reality shall continue to spread. Like pulling on a loose thread until your tunic unravels.
Good. The portal still exists, even after all this time. Lead the way, proxy.
No invitation, no admittance.

I assume that explosion that rocked the vineyard was your doing? You and Fennorian, I suppose. I'll take it that you accomplished what I asked? \n\nNever mind. Speak to Fennorian. I have a business to set right.
You there! I am bored and my hounds are hungry.\n\nWill the auction start soon? Or must we continue this Colovian dance of manners and pleasantries while my gold sits unspent?
I'd offer you a glass, but your friend just took the last one! I wasn't expecting that. None of the other guests I've served this evening even tried it. Only their attendants and servants.

Ah, welcome. I'm Lord Gallio Valente, the humble proprietor of Valente Vineyards and Winery.\n\nYou, however, have me at a disadvantage. I do not believe we've met. Which of my acquaintances decided to bring you along as their guest today?

Fate's chosen? How presumptuous a title Hermaeus Mora has bestowed upon you.\n\nThe Prince of Fate is using you, mortal. Long ago, he and his allies inflicted a terrible wrong on my Prince. Now he hopes you can stop me from undoing that damage.
This is Grahtwood? Why, these trees are almost as big as the mushrooms back home!\n\nFor what it's worth, I don't see any signs of reality unraveling. I'll take that as a good sign.

Ah. Judging by your quickened step and thoughtful expression, I'd say you found something useful in our library … and you are not quite sure what to make of it.\n\nAnswers are often more complicated than we hope.
Curious. I sense a powerful arcane aura surrounding you. You carry something rarely seen on this mortal plane. It reeks of the black arts of Oblivion.\n\nWondrous. May I see it?

You did it! That strange woman has left and taken the shadows with her!\n\nTime to start running a regular inn again. Maybe I'll add the Sage's Dream to the menu. Provided I can get some more of those ingredients!
From the sound of the bell, I assume your mission was successful, soldier. Were you able to recover the cohort's payroll as well? And where's Legionary Calvo?

The estate feels hollow now without her. And apologies for my appearance. Needed some liquid courage to walk the halls of this corpse. I hope you find who did this. She did not deserve what happened to her.
Nice work, dealing with that thief. I probably could have chased her down myself, but you should have heard the way Grander was yowling. Like a pup with a thorn between his paws.
I'm sorry, I didn't see you and the investigator there. This search for the will is rattling my nerves! Please let us know at once when you find it.

Losing my late mother's will has got everyone on edge. Hopefully it turns up soon and we can have this uncomfortable business taken care of. Then we can discuss more lighthearted matters such as a celebration of my return.

You can find Mizzik just down the road, searching the Weatherleah Estate for Betu. He has quite a distinct look, you can't miss him. Khajiit wearing a broad brimmed hat and big heavy boots. Quite the flair for the dramatic if you ask me.
I knew you showed promise, but to make it this far without taking the Oath? I'm impressed.

My very nature makes returning me to prison a temporary reprieve at best. My power will always find a way back to me. And with it, the threat of the madness that overcomes me and can unravel reality.\n\nMortal, talk with me more about change.

I'll continue to do all I can for Leftwheal. The fact that I have a second chance is thanks to you. Your aid went a long way to ensure we have a future to look forward to. Once we've dealt with all the remaining cultists of course.

Speak with Beragon. See if he has a thought about our next steps.\n\nIthelia's presence untethers all consequences. It makes it nearly impossible for me to perceive the threads of fate, let alone determine which threads to follow.
Just ring the bell in the proper sequence and that will alert the rest of the Legion.

I can't believe we found a corrupted seed at Ostumir. That the Recollection somehow caused the new forest to overgrow West Weald. Or that my friend Sorilen was involved.\n\nLeramil wants to talk to you, but I'd like to hear what else you discovered.
We found her, proxy. Ithelia, the Prince of Paths.\n\nApproach her carefully. She may appear in the guise of a mortal, but she is the very incarnation of the Daedric power that permeates this place.
I do not recognize you, yet you seem familiar. Almost like this shrine … I know I should remember it, but I do not.\n\nTell me, what is this place? Why am I drawn here?
Thank you for helping us. Please tell me you're also here to stop Lord Valente.
Speak, fate's chosen. You were deep in conversation with the Prince of Paths. What do your mortal eyes see that elude my Daedric senses?
You succeeded where I failed. I can't believe I've never seen someone of your skill before. I owe you. Which is something I rarely say. Bazrag was lucky to find you.
Please, my friend. Talk to Tham. I need to compose myself before I can comfort him.

That was one of the most entertaining series of fights I had the opportunity to watch in a long time. \n\nBecause of your actions, my promise to Hermaeus Mora is fulfilled. The Echonir is safe thanks to you.

You're here, too? I wondered why Malacath told me to find this mage and tell her about the old staff stolen from the Oathsworn Pit. Now I understand. He means for you to punish whoever sent the Recollection to enlist our lodges.

You are one of the more interesting mortals I've run across in the last century or two. First you help me chase the Blind Path out of Maelstrom, and now you turn up here?\n\nClearly, the Echonir was more important than I thought.

I see you found your way to this Beragon person, too, comrade. We started to compare notes about the Recollection, but then he insisted we wait for you.\n\nSo, go talk to him. I need to know what's going on.

Our journey has reached a suitable conclusion, friend. A long rest is in order for all of us. Perhaps I can convince Curate Gadayn to join me in exploring Apocrypha. I would … like that.\n\nAs for you and me, thank you for everything.

I bring another message from my tribune, mercenary. You may wonder why an experienced and capable legionary such as myself is still relaying messages. Believe me, the question nags at me, too. Perhaps I'm being punished for some unintended offense?

See how the map shifted and those marks appeared? I'm pretty sure they indicate places where the Staff of Many Paths has been used recently. A lingering aura of sorts, maybe.\n\nI think we need to investigate these sites.
You can find Baroness Eliana Cossa just inside the town walls. The entrance to Leftwheal is just north of Feldagard Keep. Let her know Grimmer sent you.

An ancient quarrel between Daedric Princes is beyond me, friend. But it's clear Mora attempted to reason with Ithelia. She willfully ignored his warning. And was too strong for him to overpower without help.
Apocrypha is saved, reality preserved, and the threads of fate are untangled—thanks to you. \n\nI never imagined mortals could be so … capable.

It was an honor to work by your side, my friend. Thank you for helping me stop the Recollection and save West Weald—and everything else we wound up saving in the process!\n\nI'm just glad I got to throw this little celebration before you departed.
Not sure how a location in the Weald gets us to Oblivion, but I'd like to hear if Leramil can tell us anything about the place.

A Colovian soldier can't just stroll into our town and throw around accusations! If not for Beragon …. He may not be part of our settlement, but his good works are known to us.\n\nWell, what is it? What did you bring to show me?

Go on, I'll be right behind you. \n\nYou know, I'm kind of eager to see a legendary Ayleid stronghold no one else has set foot inside in centuries. If not for all the enemies who might be waiting inside to slaughter us, this might be sort of exciting.
Greetings, stranger. All are welcome in Vashabar. But tell me, who enters my humble abode with Beragon, the hero of Ninglenirre Pass? And what was that about a danger to our unassuming town?
