That report we found about Feldagard Keep concerns me. If the Shardborn capture the fortress, they'll control the Colovian Hills. I have to make sure that doesn't happen.\n\nFind me there if you have time, comrade. I'm sure I will need your help.
I'll be all right. Go stop King Nantharion!
There's Beragon! Come on, comrade—we can't let him confront Ithelia and her servants all by himself. We need to hurry!

I wasn't sure what I expected the Skein to show us, but I assumed it would be … not that?\n\nI think that marks a spot near the old ruin of Wendir. Maybe Leramil can shed some more light on what this means.

My alchemist shop is close by. Feel free to make use of anything in there. I don't know of any potions that harm vampires, but much of my stock is explosive … when mixed correctly.\n\nAnd if you find Grivier, please send him back to us.
Please! You can't leave me like this! Not like a boar trussed up for slaughter! I need to get back to my family!

That was close! But at least we destroyed the seed and this Recollection fortress.\n\nBut … I hoped things would turn out differently for Greenspeaker Sorilen. I wish I knew what drove her into the arms of the Recollection and their mad leaders.

I took my oath a few weeks ago. Black-Glove Garm barely knows my name. I may have pledged myself to Malacath, but I don't want to die for him. When Garm told me to run, I did!\n\nI didn't do anything wrong.
Once I have secured the ritual items, I will be able to put this whole thing behind me. Let this be a lesson, friend. Necromancy is a dark, volatile business. And it stinks, too.
I stashed the key inside the old statue in the garden. Don't worry. I'll draw you a map.\n\nJust be careful wandering in the garden. We've had an infestation of odd bugs recently. Odd and dangerous.
Hail, mercenary. Tribune Alea ordered me to find you right away. You won a battle in the ruins under Vashabar, but Beragon thinks the war for West Weald isn't over yet. They still need your help.
I have not observed Abolisher up close, but I know it is a blade sharp enough to cut a door between the realms. Let us put that to the test here, proxy.
I wouldn't go into Faro's Cavern, stranger. That … tear … it's terrible! The light … the sound ….\n\nAnd if you get too close … you fall into the nothingness!
Is that it? Do we have what we need now to … how did Leramil put it? Save all of existence?\n\nI can hardly comprehend the threat we're facing, comrade.

I heard you agree to help the Wood Elf find more survivors. Do your best to find everyone you can, please. Those are our neighbors and friends trapped down there.\n\nI'll tend to any wounded up here. Don't worry, I won't leave anyone behind.

Despite how I feel right now, you and I did some real good in Ostumir. And we kept this weird seed out of the hands of the Recollection. So, wins all around, I say.\n\nIf you're ever in Skingrad, come visit me at my townhouse.
It looks like we found a place where we can use Abolisher. Go ahead and give it a try—anywhere it takes us has got to be better than here.
The symbols the Lamp of Clarity revealed above the mirrors are the same as the ones that appear in the portal archway. There is certainly a connection.
Back out of the stew pot and into the fire. We won't let Ithelia get away this time. Let's get those relics and head out.

Do you feel it? The power of the Ayleids pervades this place. Millennia separate us from the Heartland High Elves, but I can feel their legacy flowing through my blood.\n \nIt pains me to see their glory buried in these ruins.

Allow me to advise. Read the epitaph very clearly. The wine we found earlier leads me to believe this place hosted a gathering of the Five Loyal Retainers. A final toast, perhaps, using the finest drink.
Delightful to see you remain in one piece. Some of my dear Narsis's collaborators do not survive the experience. Tell me, how did you fare?
The Loom, I see the threads all around it. It consists of portals within portals, all connected to the Many Paths. You can destroy it with Abolisher, proxy!
This sounds serious. Let's get the relics, friend. There's no time to waste.

Hermaeus Mora chose his proxy correctly. Saving reality from inside a simple inn is an impressive feat.\n\nThe Lamp of Clarity will help us against Ithelia. I would like to bring it to Beragon's townhouse in Skingrad to study. May I have it?

We walked the Many Paths together and learned much, mortal. Yet, I still cannot control my power or clear the storm from my mind. Every path collides in this place.\n\nIf you have a Sage's Dream, please place it on the table. I wish to calm the chaos.
I think Master Grander wishes to speak to you. He's a patient man, but it would be rude to keep him waiting.
My master wishes to speak to you again. I can see why. Fa-Nuit-Hen delights in combat the most, but even I found myself enjoying that.

I can't believe I allowed myself to get captured by this bunch. If my fellow legionaries hear about this ….\n\nBut tell me, did you stop the mercenaries from polluting the reservoir with the remaining elixir?

Be careful, deputy. If Constable Yabren's right, whoever's behind all this didn't hesitate to remove the healer and Yabren's father when they got too close to the truth.\n\nWatch yourself at Carvain Manor and Raxalee Tower.
I knew this was a bad idea. Why did I ever let that alchemist talk me into this?
The constable has no idea who she's dealing with!

A good officer gives credit where credit is due. You did good, comrade. Feldagard Keep needs to rebuild and do some cleanup, but we repelled an invasion and gained a valuable tool.\n\nNot bad for a day's work. If only I could shake this feeling ….

The permutations of fate created a high probability that you … ah. I would like to talk about the relics I heard you describe to Beragon.\n\nThe Lamp of Clarity and Abolisher are two of the relics once used to defeat and imprison Ithelia.
Why do you delay? Enter the portal, chosen of fate. Torvesard is one of the Unseen. I cannot perceive his movements. If you do not find him, he will not be found.

As safe as can be expected. We are a military installation, after all. We'll wipe out the remaining Daedra, then begin rebuilding the keep.\n\nI expect Tribune Alea will want a final word or two with you before you go.
Damn. I honestly don't remember the last time I felt this good. I'm already planning details in my head. This will be so much fun!
She's already making plans, I can tell. I just hope we can enjoy the moment.
I'm so proud of those two. Thank you, traveler.
My daughter, marrying Minth's son. I've been fighting this for so long, like trying to deal with pests in a grove. \n\nPerhaps it's time I thought about this a different way.
When the day started, I had no idea it would end like this. My son, marrying Nedolir's daughter. The Dawnway and the Green Pact … ancestors give me strength.
This camp is lost and my companions are dead. Wildburn will cover any trace of their existence. And the evidence of the Recollection's crimes.
That was beautiful. Let's get drunk on Ciiril's best and dance until dawn. Praise the ancestors!
A beautiful ceremony. Like a … oh, a metaphor escapes me. It was so nice.
An exquisite execution of the rite. The ancients of Valenwood would be proud.
Ah, my friend!  Would you believe it, you are speaking to the new Jester of Skingrad! Count Calantius was delighted by my performance. Or maybe amused is a better word. Hard to read him, really.

Your skill at pie throwing is quite excellent, my friend! And it was only a matter of time before those so-called bakers' false claims came back to hit them in the face. \n\nWere you also able to recover my sugar and father's flour blend?
I really worked up a sweat saving Hyacinth! That was so exciting. And you? You were amazing!\n\nHey, maybe we should make a habit out of this.
Oh no, what happened to Calvo? And who's ringing the bell? But why are you talking to me? Go report to the captain!
I knew it! Calvo went and got himself killed, didn't he? Well, don't just stand there. Go tell the captain!
You're back, but where's Calvo? Is he …?\n\nNo, don't tell me. Report to the captain, first.
Perhaps I should read up on necromancy more first. Legends say the Ayleids had huge labor forces of undead, but nothing about their spellcasting abilities.
Greetings, wanderer. Do you hear the wisps? I do. They bear fortunes and portents of things to come. If you cannot hear them, I'd be happy to share what they say about you.
You have my thanks. The shame I would feel had I left the others behind ….
I need a moment to clear my lungs, but I'll make my way to safety shortly, I promise.
It took us years to build this city and now it's all gone up in flames. What a nightmare.
Thank you for coming to our aid, traveler. You're a light in the dark.
All is in readiness, walker. Do as Zerith said and ignite the two braziers.

The songs of these Twilight Cantors can stop souls from falling to the Bent Dance?\n\nIn my time, we had no such songs. I am glad to see it! Yet this means they are at greatest risk of being hunted by that Rajaska-z'har.
I'm very eager to get moving. West Weald wine accompanies cosmic theories the best!
So do you now have a good grasp on the complexity of this paradox?

Your time with us was brief, but impactful. For whatever it is worth, I think fondly of our time together. Well done.\n\nIf Tanlorin continues to travel at your side, I wish you the best. Just. Please ensure they stay well. They are … unique.
Hmm. Something … something … I'm sure I'm forgetting something ….\n\nNo matter. I think Curate Gadayn wishes to speak with you, comrade.
I can't believe we did it! We saved Apocrypha and West Weald! If you told me we'd do anything like this back at the necropolis, I would have asked how much sujamma you had to drink.
I really am quite busy. Tell Constable Yabren that I'm sorry for her loss. I'm sorry for everybody's losses.

This so-called fatigue fever. I wouldn't be surprised if it were nothing more than an excuse used by lazy workers to avoid hard labor.\n\nNone of my best ranch hands have gotten ill. At least, not yet.

Azura's Lamp is not a friend to Ithelia, pathwalker. All the relics work to subdue us. If it helps make a Sage's Dream, it is not to empower my reflection.\n\nNo matter. My fate here is sealed so what do I care. Take your harkfruit and leave me.
I have to return to the field, but I'll keep in touch with the Gardener. The moment we know more about this traitor, I'll be at your side and ready to strike.

Traveler, we hoped to see you here.\n\nI'm told you killed King Nantharion beneath Vashabar's very roots. I know he had to be stopped, yet the tragedy will haunt me. He started with a great vision before he wandered onto dark paths.

Tribune Alea has spoken at length about you and enthralled me with tales of your exploits on behalf of West Weald. And to think you're not even a native of Skingrad or Vashabar! I hope it isn't too late for us to learn something from your example.
You and Nahlia certainly had your work cut out for you. Well done!\n\nAnd now, with all the cataloging and reporting to superiors, I suppose I'll have my work cut out for me.
I have no idea how I'm going to explain this to the head of my order. This will be a long and entertaining conversation.\n\nIn the meantime, you have a feathered scholar to speak with.
Clen and I were just talking about you! If you hadn't come to the village, we would never have gone through the rite. \n\nAnd now look at us. Assisting the greenspeaker with negotiations!

Your Ithelia, does she not sense it? The Ithelia of this path, my Prince, has lost herself. She has become the monster that Hermaeus Mora foresaw. If she cannot regain control, this reality is finished.\n\nWhy does a mortal walk beside an Ithelia?
Watch your step on the other side of that door, there's raw magic aplenty. I also have a personal code about seeing our adventurer-consultants being torn apart.
I feel … cold. My skin … it's pale. Please, tell me this isn't happening.\n\nTell me I'm not becoming … one of them.

Feldagard Keep still stands, thanks to you. I'd like to find a way to remove the taint those Recollection dogs left in the barracks. Daedric magic is foul, and the stink of Mirrormoor is fouler still.

I offered Beragon the use of my more … spacious accommodations for the celebration, but he felt more comfortable hosting it himself. I suppose he prefers this quaint setting to a ballroom.\n\nNo matter. Ithelia is thwarted and West Weald is safe.

The rot has been culled from Vashabar thanks to you. I only hope that Nantharion's mad plan was due to the influence of this forgotten Daedric Prince, Ithelia, and not the philosophy of the Dawnway.\n\nVashabar has enough problems remaining as it is.

Hello, walker. One needs not be as perceptive as Mizzik Thunderboots to see all the good you have done for West Weald. \n\nBut this one is curious about the Recollection … the group's origins sound like a mystery Mizzik should pursue next.

Ah, my friend! I've been hearing about your exploits beyond what we did at Valente Vineyards. You banished a forgotten Daedric Prince? How fascinating!\n\nThe arcanist also mentioned something about preserving reality, but I assume that was hyperbole.

Look at you, the hero of West Weald! I had no idea I was asking a genuine hero for help back in Sutch.\n\nThis food, though? It has no taste! Colovians have no sense of flavor and spices. Makes me long for the cook fires of Alik'r.

I'll be honest, I'm not entirely sure if I should even be here … but I wanted to show my support for everything you did for Maerenah. And me. And, apparently, all of West Weald!\n\nWe're a long way from Sutch, eh?

Did Nivan send you to haggle in his stead? Tell him he should not have bothered. He's out of his mind if he thinks this one will sell him shields at half their worth. \n\nChirrabi cannot eat word of mouth, thank you very much.

News has begun spreading through the city. That mercenary the Legion hired, the one working with Tribune Alea. I heard he took down that false Wood Elf king, Nantharion.\n\nEven his own people are cheering about his death, or so I've heard.
Recollection? Bah! A Wood Elf is a Wood Elf! If their king is a bad guy, how can we trust anyone from Vashabar?
Did you see that? The displays of aggression just disappeared. They're calming down. I don't know if they'll attack either of us on sight anymore. \n\nThis is impossibly exciting!
A new day dawns, Scribing returned to the world. I'm trying not to get feathers everywhere in my excitement.
With the king dead, Vashabar needs strong leadership to guide us through the coming storm. I can think of no one more suited than Greenspeaker Darolith.
I don't believe it. King Nantharion is a good man. These malicious rumors must be the work of the Colovians. They'll do anything to be rid of us!
That damned Nantharion got what he deserved! Good riddance to dead birch wood, I say!
The signal fires … they're lit! Looks like Legionary Thania came through! But if you need something, you should talk to the captain.
Let me guess. You're here to help Votary Nahlia. She wants an outsider's perspective.\n\nI'm not sure why, but I guess it's good that you're here.

The Indrik's power has been unlocked. Splendid! Ulfsild would have been so very proud of you.\n\nYou should inform the Knight of your recent adventures. She's only just returned with a handful of assistants.
You are Constable Yabren's deputy, yes? Thank you for revealing the truth behind fatigue fever. Perhaps now the town and its workers can both truly prosper.
You are the deputy? The outsider who helped Constable Yabren bring justice to Ontus? Whatever she paid you, it wasn't enough for saving us from fatigue fever.

Bog … erm. Tanlorin is a rare and exceptional individual. And, from what I've seen, you both have that in common. \n\nI can't imagine the toll this has taken on them. But I take solace in knowing they have you by their side. Thank you.
You'd think with all the flowers I wouldn't be able to smell the Gardener's perfume.\n\nAnyway. We'll figure this out. I find careful thought solves most any problem.

The power of my domain flows into the altar once more. My old friend would be at peace with what has come to pass.\n\nGo, continue to walk the path. Seek the other Luminaries and learn what you can from them as well.

Good, you got out. I worried for a moment that those Recollection bastards caught up with you. Or, worse, those horrid Daedra.\n\nYou should talk to Tribune Alea. Losing all those people weighs on her. I know the feeling.
I feel quite honored, adventurer. To be present for the restoration of a lost history.\n\nAnd thanks to you and Nahlia, so many more will learn about Ulfsild's legacy.

I'm not above admitting when I see a good job well done. It's not how I would have done things, but … maybe that's why Nahlia chose you to go through that portal and not me.\n\nGood of you not to gloat about it, either.

Hopefully the Dragon will give us a break from riddle-hunting. Not that I wouldn't mind another chance to prove myself! \n\nBut we've got other trees to mind, and her puzzles seem designed to distract.

Not sure what I'll do next, now that the Garland Ring is no more. I was thinking I might head to West Weald. There's rumors of my people up to something over there. \n\nCuriosity always seems to get me in trouble.
It doesn't matter how you found us. You two, every one in that pathetic little club of yours. You're dead. You're all dead.
So much as blink wrong, mortal, and I shall end you.

Pim always talked about how dangerous entering a Goblin's camp was. I was trying to stay away from the Goblins, but I guess I should have been looking to stay away from the traps instead. \n\nYou found a knife? Can I see it?
See if there's a focal point anywhere. I'll start digging through these books. Only a couple hundred to go through, right?
I know you have been helping Tribune Alea. I'm in no shape to charge in there after her, but maybe you can go assist her.

Back when we were in the Legion, we used to say any battle you walked away from was a victory. You'd be alive to fight again. I always felt that was a coward's boast. But after all this, I see the truth in it.
What happened in the cellars was tragic. But I trust the Divines will guide Marcan Caelum's soul to the peace he was denied in life. Just as they guided us through our actions to save Valenia today.
I'm glad Val's alive and kicking, but that wound's going to give her trouble the rest of her days. She deserves better than that. I need to go to Black Marsh.
You're back! How's Marcien? Did you find them?
Sorry, friend. Can't talk much. But … thank you for saving my life. I won't waste this second chance you've given me. Not for all the gold on the Gold Road.
Again, you have my thanks. Hopefully we will meet again—preferably in a dark and terrifying cave. Full of scary fish. I am much better at fighting fish. Trust me.

The arcane knot is secure and Xoryn won't be able to reconstitute himself for a while. Keshargo will remember how useful it is to have skilled warriors around, especially on important expeditions like this one.

Right. Now I could explain everything, but you should really speak to Keshargo. He is supposedly in charge of this mess of an expedition.\n\nI hope he sends you after Xoryn. If that battle broke my null arca, I'm going to be upset.

If you have any friends, you might want to ask them to join you. I don't know if the expedition is still under attack or what is happening. It could be exceedingly dangerous. \n\nThe portal is there, whenever you're ready.
We'll fight you if we have to. No damn vampires are going to make a meal out of me or my mother!

No matter how many times you lose a squadron, it never gets any easier. \n\nNo need to stick around, mercenary. I'll be ready to head out myself in another few moments. I plan to personally lead the patrol that goes hunting for that traitor, Ulrath.

Not that I owe you an explanation, but everything I said is true. I wrote it all down. My report to the Legion. I doubt the captain will pass it along, but at least my conscience is clear.\n\nAs for me, tell her I died. Or I'm a deserter. I don't care.
I suppose we'll have an old fashioned handfast, won't we? A Greenspeaker's wedding. So many traditions to uphold, there.
On the path to ally with the Dragon you must choose your words carefully.\n\nIf she asks if you are my inheritor, do not agree or disagree. Insist upon taking her trial.
Mercenary, I have more orders from Tribune Alea.
Yes, yes. This one can't afford to settle with Shan-Ra, so he takes his business elsewhere.\n\nJode's Chariot. What a joke.
Why must these stall-keepers take theft as a personal slight? Your wares are good. It is a compliment!
Walker, you are interrupting a very serious nap. Please move on so that I might rest.
If we are through, then this one would like to return to her meal before it gets cold.

Now this is a celebration that's more to my liking. Plus, it's good business to get to know some of the other movers and shakers of the Weald. Perhaps I'll even get to make conversation with the count. I'm sure he'll find me captivating!

When I heard about this party, I decided to make my way to the city and offer my regards, too.\n\nNice to see all the folks you helped here. I guess helping my little inn was only one step in what sounds like an epic adventure!

Tribune Alea ordered me to attend your party! Messenger, party-goer … it's degrading! Well, now that we're done with your heroics, maybe I can get back to being a soldier again. Wouldn't that be nice!\n\nWe are sure we won, right?

It seems we have you and your friend to thank for our salvation. Who are … wait. \n\nYou are that person. The incident with Razum-dar. The Psijic Order and the Crystal Tower. Well, that explains some things.
Well? More tricks? Or did you find the real Fable of the Netch?
Your tactics were unconventional. Even devious. I loved every moment of our conversations. \n\nMake clever use of my power, mortal. For Ulfsild's sake, if nothing else.

Don't worry about me, traveler. I can handle myself now that I'm not tangled in my net. \n\nGo let Sariyaah know I'm safe. I'll catch up with you shortly. And when you see her, maybe leave out the part about the guzzards.
Fascinating how the Netch has adapted to our presence here.
Our adventure with the Netch is behind us, my friend. I'll be … digesting some of that for a while I think. \n\nJust let me know if I can be helpful.

As my power flows through the altar, reach your tendrils out into the world, Not-Ulfsild. You never know where scribing will take you next.\n\nAnd of course, if you're lucky, we'll see each other again soon.
He can hear me, he knows I'm here. My father doesn't have to pass from this world alone.\n\nI'm so overwhelmed. I don't know how to thank you. What did you do?
I don't know how to express my gratitude. If he wasn't able to reconcile with his father, I know my Elic would have carried that sorrow with him for the rest of his days.
Elic is here. If my last breath was an apology to him, it would have been worth it. But I have a few more left in me. And ears to listen.\n\nThank you, stranger, for guiding my spirit back to my boy.
The Fox was able to leave the Gryphon's side at any time, but I wonder how much he did. You've done a kind deed today.
These constructs are so powerful, you can practically see the magicka radiating off of them. Eye-opening, incredible. \n\nJust like my time with you, my friend.
I name you ally of Skingrad, traveler. You will always be welcome in our fair city.
You…you found him! Great work!
Eifa … she is so beautiful! I wonder what she wants to tell you, walker.
No darkness in me. I'm too clean!
Be wary, traveler. The swill they pour here works better as a boot cleaner than as a way to slake your thirst.\n\nThis one swears, no cat north of Tenmar seems able to make a decent drink.
Unless you can spare some coin, I think we have nothing more to discuss.
Eifa wants to tell you something, friend of Zerith-var. Talk to her before she departs for Azurah's Crossing.

I understood my other facets. None of them were perfect, but I recognized them as part of myself. \n\nThis one is different though. I've been suppressing her for a long time. I don't want to take her back.
You know, I always wanted to be buried with a crown of flowers.
You did so good! Congratulations! Any time you're up for stealing more stuff from Daedric Princes, just let me know. \n\nJust don't tell the Gryphon all right?
Don't be long, I'm thirsty!
Take the sigil, mortal. The Fox has been known to claim shimmering objects left out in the open. Best not to tempt him.
Don't talk to me until you're better looking.
Please make yourself comfortable, traveler. There's plenty of ale to go around.

Did you feel it, traveler? The ground shook so hard that what remained of our poor village crumbled around me. I can still hear my neighbor's cry as the roof fell on her.\n\nI'm sorry. It's just all too much.
Well, at least you got a confession out of her.
She's a monster, she has no remorse at all!
It seems like just yesterday I was getting bored and a little bitter patrolling ruins and making portals. Now I'm not sure I'll ever be bored again!\n\nAnd all because of our adventures together.

What lies always ahead of you though you will never see it? What is always coming but never arrives?\n\nExistence itself is a mystery, an unmapped territory spread out before you. Will you take a vow to explore it?

Kindness is like the first snow of winter. Get enough of it all at once, and soon it starts to stick.\n\nWhen I pass from this world, I'll never look back and wish I'd been less charitable. Will you vow the same?

Relationships do not lose their worth when they end. You can carry someone with you in other ways.\n\nBut while it lasts there's such joy in loyalty to one's friends. How will you vow to respect them?
You have it, my sigil. Well done, inheritor. Amplify the altar, and bring this journey to an end.
Friend, Leramil sent me to locate you. She's quite certain that we're not done with the problems of Oblivion and the destruction of reality quite yet.
It is over. At last. Talbira smiles to see her brightest student travel to the Sands Behind the Stars.\n\nZerith looks as though he wishes to speak with you, walker. Go to him.
Talk to the Crow, my friend. I have to find out how this turns out!
We need to get across quick as we can. If your Ulfsild-lens-sight-thing runs out we might get stuck. \n\nAnd that would be bad!
Speak with the baroness, I'm still trying to recover from my wounds and our little conversations are tiring.
You've done us a great service helping more civilians escape the chaos. I'll admit that my bow is of little use against smog and flames.
Hold on a moment, I'm just catching my breath. I've healed more wounds today than I have all year.
Is it safe inside yet? No? I cannot rest until I know my family is out safe.
Halt. We're practically at war here. You can't just wander into our camp unannounced! Go! Talk to the captain this instant!
You help them? Traitor! You aren't worthy of our great heritage.

A moment, traveler. A detachment of legionaries should be roaming the grounds of Rustwall. We came to meet them, but we can't find a soul. No legionaries, no servants. Not even a gardener.\n\nI'm at a loss as to what has become of them.

Hurry, mortal. Go to Beragon's. Talk to Leramil. If we're going to preserve reality, we have to do it quickly. Soon there won't be anyplace to keep our stuff. Or us. Or anything.\n\nNothing frightens an immortal more than the threat of nonexistence.
Keshargo needs water, but where is this one supposed to find it? There is nothing but sand and rock here. We used all the clean water we had putting out the tent fires.
I'm getting Keshargo's personal attention, he must be worried about me. \n\nI don't remember what happened after that Dremora showed up. It feels like he won the fight though.
I should have seen that Dremora before the fight broke out. And instead of helping, I'm resting with the wounded. \n\nI'm sure my wounds hurt worse than my battered pride, but it's a close call.
I need to keep busy. To keep my mind off… this.
Found this axe in a crate. If Xoryn comes back, I'll be ready.
This is our chance! Use Abolisher to destroy the Loom before Ithelia weaves us all out of existence!
What are you waiting for? Use Abolisher to destroy the Loom!
The Loom, I see the threads all around it. It consists of portals within portals, all connected to the Many Paths. You can destroy it with Abolisher, proxy!
And all this time it was a children's book that would guide my way. There is one more location I must go to meditate on.\n\nThe riddle is so close. I just need a little more time.
Oh dear. I can see that Orissa's temper is brewing. I'll just mind my own business, shall I?
Brynmir seems upset. Why? Do those odd wandering people bother him? Just leave them alone.\n\nMaybe they want a drink. Has he tried that?
Can I see them? Yes. Did I notice the sky as I walked in? Yes. Am I concerned that something horrible could happen here? Yes.\n\nDo I want to talk to you about it? No.
Keep playing. Just keep playing. They won't hurt you unless you stop the music.\n\nI don't know why I believe that. But I haven't stopped for a moment and I'm still safe.
I visit the inn to do some reading and sometimes to work on my novel. Usually it's filled with people drinking and making noise.\n\nNow with the other customers scared off, it's perfect for me.
How does Brynmir expect me to get work done with these odd happenings going on? I can't clean now! I'm just too scared. Yeah, that's it. Too scared to do my work.\n\nThat's a good excuse, right?
You're the new deputy that's been running around town asking questions. I'm not inclined to appreciate such activity. Bear that in mind as you conduct your business with the baron.
Lady Raxalee is very busy. If you must talk to her, be succinct, be direct, and be polite. Then leave as soon as she dismisses you.
Follow the commander's orders. He's gotten us out of worse situations than this.
I owe you my life. I've seen what Daedra do to their enemies. But your skill with the ballista kept me alive. Thank you.

I can't thank you enough for saving me from those Daedra. When they came rushing down the hill, I thought I was a dead man. Then a ballista bolt landed right on top of them. Your targeting was impeccable!
I hope you find more of my neighbors out there. We should never have come back to Ostumir. Rebuilding in all this jungle? Feh. Too much work.\n\nAnyway, I'll stay here and help watch over the camp.
Gods, my leg hurts. Beragon carried me here, but some of my family is still in there. Please, find them.
Careful, stranger. Reeve Nardarmor is throwing his weight around. The Skywatch Guard barged right into the guildhall and arrested a mage!
That ballista has great range. When it's working, that is.
I've served under Commander Merian for ten years. He's tough on us, but I know he cares. The stronger we are, the more we can handle.
I never wanted to join the Imperial Legion. My father forced me. Now look! I'm about to die from a Daedric blade.\n\nSome people see honor in dying from combat. I just see death!
No one will get past the gate. That I can promise. That barricade is strong and my blade is sharp.\n\nYou just do whatever the commander orders and we'll do the same.
I helped build that barricade, so you know it's strong. And if they knock it down again, I'll put it back even stronger. I can do this all day.

Not to get all mushy, but we make a good team. Since I met you, I've felt more in touch with who I am. I never realized how much I used to hold myself back. Why? Insecurity, maybe. But with you, that all fades away.\n\nWe'll figure this out. Together.
Thanks for picking me up off the floor, friend. This has been … well. A terrible day.

I heard. The Ring becomes a part of the Proxy Queen's court, huh?\n\nThe Proxy Queen is no Ceythalmor, but royalty have their own particular ideas of what constitutes justice. I think … I think I say, no thank you.

Wisteria is the traitor. It feels impossible and inevitable at the same time. Was anything she ever said to me real? Or was it all just part of her plan? Whatever that is.\n\nSorry. I'll try to stay positive. Just a lot to take in.
Be careful, Lord Hollowjack is very powerful. I'd join you, but my fears would just strengthen him.
The flames! They no longer consume me! Just before they disappeared, I saw you in the middle of them. \n\nWhat happened?
The voices! They're gone! I saw my ancestors. Lord Hollowjack and you, as well. What did you do?

I was fortunate that you were at my side when we faced the fallen Cantor Izalgo. \n\nAnd Azurah has blessed us by allowing us to acquire Moon-Singer Talbira's song. At least, we will have it after Krin'ze practices it.
Let us reach the end of this tale, tamiit. The story was longer than I expected, but we have reached its end.

Now you know the secret, the guilt, that has filled my heart with darkness for so long.\n\nIf we are to stop Ravith-morna from forever blocking the paths to Azurah's Crossing, I must earn back Cantor Krin'ze's trust. And yours as well, tamiit.

My wounds keep me from going further. I am not as young as I once was.\n\nSpare no more thoughts on my behalf. The people of Elsweyr will be in dire need without my fellow Twilight Cantors. Save them, please.
Ka'iir, stranger. The road beckons you. See yourself down it, swiftly.
The blood … it's gone. I saw the dead. And Lord Hollowjack. And you. You cleansed my axe, and with it, me.

I'm thankful your timing is more punctual than mine. But I've nearly finished a chapter that covers the Ayleid Diaspora, which is probably how the remnants became so scattered. Tell me, have you found any yet?
The Inquisitors of the Torval Curiata will find you, outsider. You and your necromancer.\n\nStay away from the Twilight Cantors or else.

I knew that name sounded familiar. Caecilius was Cato's son and heir. He must have died on the battlefield. \n\nIf his death pushed Cato to this cause, then that's what Cato's doing too. Using these soldiers to turn the nobility against the war.
I'm not certain I believe what I just saw. Did the specter of Cato's son appear to you, too?

I created that clarity spell I used in the fight when my vision faded. Knowing I could bolster my sight helped me feel confident as I grew used to the darkness.\n\nThe monastery awaits. You might want to heal your hurts while you can.
The sounds of fighting stopped. Is it over? Did you defeat Orpheon the Tactician? Is the Elder Scroll safe at last? \n\nI need to hear it from you.

Izalgo. My poor friend. May his voice join the chorus of our brothers and sisters in the Sands Behind the Stars.\n\nIn a way, his disappearance led us to Moon-Singer Talbira. Oh, I wish he was still here. I have so much I want to tell him.
<The scamp points to small hand-written sign nearby. Caal: Assistant Chronicler, Familiar to Firandil, Merchant.>
Sorry, I don't feel like talking right now.
Unhand me! I am Cato Albus. I am the arbiter of justice and peace!\n\nCaecilius's dream requires that I am free to destroy the alliances from within. You cannot stop Caecilius's dream!
You don't look like an Inquisitor. And your friend only looks somewhat like a dark spirit.\n\nWait, you're the ones from the Vile Manse! Are you here to help us again?
Your scents are unknown to me. But I know your descriptions. The Inquisitors who rallied us here complained of you often.\n\nBut they are dead now. I hope you come to us bearing good news?
This one prays you are flesh and not a desperate imagining. We are lost! Doomed!
Solstice? Never heard of it. Sounds nice and peaceful, though. I'm betting it's anything but.\n\nWell, if that's where the worms are hiding, then that's where we need to go.
What? Why? I told you everything I know! I suppose I deserve this, but I don't want to die!

So much intrigue over a small coffer. Lady Lirinisse spent a small fortune to ensure there was no record. And of course, there's the matter of her death, so soon after this account was established. \n\nVery curious.
I can see by the looks on the faces of the ambassadors that Vanus's word have shaken them. Good. Perhaps now they'll set aside their differences and agree to work together to stop the Worm Cult.
While you search the eastern path, I'll take the western door. This base is large, we need to cover as much ground as possible.\n\nHold on to Skordo's blade. He'll grumble if we lose it.
This Worm Cult doesn't scare me. I plan to get revenge for Guildmaster Merric at any cost.
Into the lion's den, as they say.
Orpheon's dead, but so is Mentor Huzbedad. Both seem like a dream, or a nightmare.\n\nYour actions kept my people from dying in vain. That will be a comfort in the days to follow.
Though Khafdeed's words were rash, they were right. We will talk later, if you still wish. But I must discuss something with Khafdeed alone.
I know better than to doubt the words of Vanus Galerion. I will do what I can to assist the guilds in this endeavor.

See the love Azurah has for her children, tamiit. Those most in need of saving are never turned away from her embrace for good. Shando-ri and Arum-Khal both learned that. I am reminded of this lesson, too.\n\nThank you for seeing this through with me.
I have standing orders to take the words of the great mage Vanus Galerion with utmost seriousness. I'll do what I can to get you the support of the Covenant.
Solstice? Never heard of it. But the words of Vanus Galerion give weight to your message. I will make sure the Pact provides its support.
Looking around, it is difficult to see how we will rebuild and recover. But a well is not dug without preparation. We will persevere. We have to.
The siege started so quickly. I don't want to credit a bird for its talons, but this deserter army is well trained in warfare.
We couldn't make it to a place to hide. If the Gods are willing, we can stay here undetected until it's over. \n\nPlease don't call too much attention to us.
The flamedancer burns everything in her path. Don't get in her way!
Breathing hurts, but the pain lets me know I'm still alive.
We thought it would be safer down here, but Orpheon's army found us before we could escape.

You're not the usual serving wench. Where's the tonic I requested? I need something to settle my nerves.\n\nOh, what else can befall me today? One more interruption and I'll never make it to Shornhelm on time.

We heard that Guildmaster Merric had died and that Prince Azah was taking control for the interim, but no one told us Skordo was coming here.\n\nThen he opened a portal and a Worm Cult horde swarmed out. That's when I knew—that wasn't Skordo.
I fought the Worm Cult during the Planemeld. They're all monsters, even the ones who look like people.\n\nSeeing them again is a nightmare.
If you're here to speak to Magister Andrelo, please state your business and go. She's still recovering from that terrible incident.

Between your efforts and Vanus's message, the alliance ambassadors finally seem willing to throw us their support. And from what Vanus told us, I suspect we'll need it.\n\nA rescue must wait. The threat hiding on Solstice is our first priority.
Who would have guessed that Julien and I would end up together? When he spoke those words, I understood what love truly is.
Maybe my time in the army will help me sort things out.
I can protect myself. Let's just leave this wretched place.
The Duke has returned, thanks to your timely intervention. \n\nHe wants to see you inside.
Are they here? Are Faolchu's cursed offspring here in Aldcroft?
Please. Please hurry. I'm afraid. What if it's too late?
What have I done? What have I done? I thought I could kill the bastard, but instead he … he turned me into a … a monster!

Thank you for aiding in our cause. When you find knights in the keep who would stand up for what's right, send them to me out here. \n\nWe will make preparations to storm the keep and stop Sir Croix and this rash attack.
Testing greeting text for problems.
I'm still getting the hang of this feeding thing. But don't worry. We only feed on willing vassals or evil villains. And we never feed to excess—except maybe on the evil villains.
They are going to release me, aren't they? Has Olivier really not come forward? \n\nHe will. I know he will.
Forgive me for my earlier outburst. I must have made quite a fool of myself.\n\nPlease, forget everything I told you.
You poured the packets into the braziers and nothing happened? That's it then. We have no choice but to surrender.\n\nGo tell the king. I'll be down here. Praying that he sees reason.
You return, and sooner than S'rashi expected! \n\nYou have S'rashi's gold? Please say you have S'rashi's gold.
You can come and go as you like.\n\nThough you're a fool if you don't just go.
You've got a free pass to go in or out. \n\nIf I were you, I'd pick out.
Oh, praise the Eight it's you! Quick! Untie me!
What in Oblivion's name happened in there? Heloise ran right past me, crying her eyes out. \n\nWell, don't just stand there! Get after her! She's not safe out there on her own.

Use the torch and burn poor Gennove's body. If bloodfiends are really involved, we can't take any chances.\n\nBut make sure you collect his ashes. It wasn't his fault he died like that. He deserves to be buried in hallowed ground.
Sir Edmund will stay on as leader of the Knights of the Flame. He is a good man, and loyal. Though I fear I will never trust anyone fully again.
Preparing the entire order to go to war isn't easy. This is going to take some time.
I hear King Fahara'jad's been plotting to take over Alcaire for years.
Have you come to pay your respects? That's very kind of you.\n\nMathias was such … he was good to me. Better than I deserved, I think.
Get back to the fight, Lieutenant! We will win this day, one way or another.
Stupid horse. Does not even know how to do what he is told. I have a good mind just to feed the stupid thing to the dogs.
We caught them by surprise and I think we have the upper hand. \n\nI've been wounded, though. I don't think I'd be of any more use in the battle.
The keep, the Redguards, the duchess… all of this caused by Sir Hughes's madness. \n\nSo many have died.
Hunt down the Band of The Three and their risen minions. \n\nDefeat them and their souls will be bound to my holy blade. Then we can destroy them.
Akatosh bless you and yours, traveller!
Do you know what that armorer is charging for greaves these days? It's scandalous!
I can talk about my son all day long if you like. I do love him so. I just hope he eventually straightens himself out.
More than what I have said, I do not know. If the curse can be reversed, so relieved I would be.
Denthis once wanted a spell to make people taller and heavier. He said it would give us "parity" in dealing with the Nords. \n\nHe's an idiot. A thieving idiot.
Let me know how it ends.

As soon as I saw you, I had a good feeling. 

We can do this. We just have to watch out for the slavers' leader, Ma'jhad Kha. Avoid him at all costs. The fires should keep him busy though.

If you got questions, ask. Otherwise, good luck.
Whatever Murk-Watcher has asked you to do, this one hopes you keep her best interest in mind.
I feel like a new man already, friend. Sooner we hit the road the better, far as I'm concerned. \n\nDro-Dara says he's just about ready. Now we just need to round up Murk-Watcher. I hope she'll come.
I am prepared to complete the incantation. Then we will get vengeance against the bandits. Will you join me?
Thank you for your help. This is going to be perfect now. Perfect. \n\nI don't know whether I'm happy or sad, or both, but I feel better.
Someone tell General Godrun to hurry up and give us our orders! If there's to be another battle, let's get on with it!
Something is wrong. These ruins are centuries old, yet power still stirs here.\n\nIt's pulling at my very soul.
We put our lives into your hands. Bring that cavern down on their heads!
You're a credit to your race, soldier. \n\nIf you can collapse that cavern, Clan Murtag will be in your debt, and we pay our debts.
Thanks for taking care of those zombies!  Now I can head back back to town.  I'll let Captain Yarborough know you helped out here.

Welcome to Shinji's Scarp. Once a quaint village—now a warzone.

Grandmaster Durak told us to be on the lookout for you. He's expecting you, so come on into the camp. 

Keep your weapon handy though. Don't forget there's a battle going on.
These are sacred grounds. My sacred grounds. They are not meant for the living. \n\nAre you the one who disturbs our rest?
You truly are a divine gift from Azura. Right when I asked for it, too. I'll never doubt the power of prayer again.

Sorick admitted it, and he's paying … reparations? He should be paying with his life! At least he's leaving. You know how nobles are. They'll never convict him.\n\nYou've saved us and our homes. We are grateful.
Baron Sorick's men were here. They killed my husband!\n\nPlease, I … I won't say a word about the eggs. I swear! I won't tell anyone!
I'd go with you, but I can't disobey Master Altien.\n\nPlease take the scroll to him.
I can see that many of the smaller fires have been extinguished. Thank you for volunteering to help us.
It's only right that you should be the one to return the Dream Shard to its place with Azura.\n\nWe would be honored if you would place the shard upon the statue.
I knew you'd do it. Abbot Durak is awake!
Ahh! The smell of fresh Goblin blood is like perfume to me. \n\nI knew I could count on you.
You've got to help me. Those Goblins will eat me!
That totem's got to come down from the tower, or we'll never be rid of these Goblins.\n\nBlast you, Rama! I'll have your hide for this.
How fares the task? Do you have it yet?\n\nPerhaps you need to take a more forceful approach. My patience is wearing thin.
I've used the same poultice on myself that you used on the other wardens. I should be fine. \n\nSeriously, don't worry. Go on now.
I asked Abbot Durak to go downstairs because I wanted to speak with you for a few moments alone.\n\nTell me something. Do you recall everything that happened in the dream?
I don't know what else you want from me. Leave me alone!
Walk softly, please. I had one too many last night at the Cloudy Dregs.\n\nYou tromping across the deck sounds like someone hammering a two-handed mace against the side of my head.
The focusing crystals are in place and we have the oil. \n\nGo ahead and relight the signal fire. The honor's all yours.

Go do your thing, friend. Watch out for Ma'jhad Kha though. \n\nCaptain Angarthal was just one of his lieutenants. A brute, really. This Ma'jhad Kha is a spectre from seafarer ghost stories—a dark legend that I didn't even believe until now.

Please. You must get us out of here. There's a key somewhere. 

Look for the first mate—she may be somewhere outside the slavers' camp.

Please help us.
Did you poison the slavers' wine?
When Sir Hughes comes back, I hope we'll be able to eliminate the bandits altogether. \n\nGetting our tabards back was a good start though.
So many tribes gone from High Rock—the Ratfarmers, the Throatcutters, even the famous Disembowelers. The Stonechewers are really the last of the breed.
Hurry up! Please! Do whatever you have to do! Just get me out of here!
Whatever she did to me … it really hurt. I thought she would kill us both! I don't know how you did that, but thank you.\n\nDo you have the Water Stone?
The Knights of the Flame will need years to recover from this.
Thanks again for your efforts. With no crew, I'll have to leave this place, but at least the major threat is gone for others should they want to retake the mine.
Destroy anything and anyone you find on that island.\n\nThen make them pay for what they've done to the spriggans.

Now that you're here, we can get on with it. Gabrielle is joining us from the Mages Guild and Darien from the Fighters Guild. I suppose you want to discuss strategy with them. \n\nWhen you're ready, just ask Gabrielle to open the portal.
The wind whispers to me tales of distant places, of verdant glades dappled with sunlight. Where is this beauty, this wonder? Why can't I go there?\n\nWhat is this strange being standing before me?
They ready themselves for battle. We will hold the palace while you take out the Imperial within.\n\nWe must all move quickly.
Might I sing you a song, my lady? Can I tell you a tale? \n\nWe could take a private room. I've been told I have a silver tongue.
Shall I dance for you, my lord? I've studied under many masters of the art. \n\nI'm sure I could hold your attention for hours.
Do you have the poison?
Mara bless you for helping these people. They don't have anyone else to turn to.\n\nJust don't get yourself killed, all right?
Jahi and <<1>> will adjust to life in the city quickly. And the sooner I find a buyer, the sooner we can put this all behind us.

General Thoda is a trusted advisor and a good friend. He has heard the rumors about the Withered Hand, and he can help us.\n\nTell no one else though. People remember Suturah, and hearing his sons have returned could cause a panic.
To know the prince lives is a great relief. I never would have forgiven myself were he harmed.

I am tempted to apologize for you getting caught up in all this, but something tells me the hand of fate brought you here. \n\nBesides, if we can't stop them from stealing the Ansei Wards, none of us will be safe.
For centuries, amateurs like yourself have tried to release me. Fools! All of you!\n\nYou'd have a better chance of becoming the next emperor.

Isn't it pleasant up here? It's far above the dust of the streets, the air is cooler … between you and me, I think that's why mages build towers. Smart, huh?\n\nSo, did you come up here for the atmosphere or do you have business with the guild?
I do not know where the other Ansei Wards have been taken, but Tu'whacca tells me that you must go east, my friend.\n\nHe says that is the next step on your journey.
Don't even think about it! If you try to pick me up and give me a kiss, I'll bite your nose off!\n\nI may look like a monkey, but I'm not a monkey, and I'm done being treated this way!
Make those deliveries and Unishi will undo what has been done.

I'll mark the graves' locations on your map. I'd go with you, but I have to watch and ensure they don't slip by.\n\nThere are other Ash'abah who can join you, though. You want one skilled in swordplay, or one who's adept at restoration magic?
I never should've listened to <<1>>. Look at all the trouble he's caused!

I hope the prince has learned more. I believe the Withered Hand has brought one of the Ansei Wards here, and that does not bode well.\n\nYou were at Tu'whacca's Throne, were you not? So you know that as well as anyone.
You must go quickly. I … am fading much faster than I expected. My fate, and the fate of all Alik'r I fear … is in your hands.
The first dose is always the hardest. See how peaceful his face is now?\n\nYour Orc female should find her way out of the mine. I would follow her, unless you've changed your mind about staying.
If you want to discover what <<1>>'s favorite student gave him, you must speak with the servants of <<2>>.
I called an arbiter here to decide my fate, but she wished to speak to you first.\n\nWhatever she decides, I will submit to. It is the only justice I can give to the ones I've wronged.
Completed the rite, have you? The students usually look more taxed when they come down from the tower. Perhaps I've underestimated you.
I've had enough of your accusations, outsider! I'll hear nothing more until I speak with <<1>>.
You thought as the disciple did, though I am sure she is conflicted.

I have witnessed many dark crimes in my time as Justice, but they pale in comparison to this.\n\nTo think our own Magistrate would make a deal with the Withered Hand. What could she possibly hope to gain from such a thing?
It worked! Let us head back at Telenger's camp so we can bring him the good news!\n\n...I hope that Meliara does not try to take credit for our achievements.
Cursed, I tell you. These lands are cursed. The desert belongs to the dead.\n\nRuptga sent the beetles as a sign. They'll just keep coming, more and more beetles … until we leave.

Ironically, it was in our fight against the hideous Goblins that we came to love the desert and its simple beauty.\n\nNow you must face the proud Orc warriors of ancient Orsinium. The fight for the Orc city proved to be one of our greatest trials.

So now you know my dark secret. It must be horrifying—I haven't been able to bring myself to go down there since this began. I just gave Fakimal a key ….\n\nDo you understand though? Do you realize why this is necessary?
I see her now! And that Daedra has her in its grasp! We must save her!
Great work! Now we have jewels for the ransom and puffball caps for the sleep potion.\n\nIt's time to execute my plan. They'll never release Miranda alive unless we have leverage on them.
I'm back with reinforcements, but I was too late to save the commander, Daedra take it.\n\nBefore he died, he said he'd sent you on a mission. I hope you succeeded.
To think that Serge's plan almost worked. Without you … I won't forget what you've done.
Lady Miranda's in the manor house, probably upstairs. Give her the antidote before it's too late!
I don't care what he thinks is right. \n\nThere must be another way to get that Daedra out of him.
We're under attack!
Please—get me out of this! I can pay you, I swear!
I saw Baron Sorick's men taking eggs back to the pools. \n\nThank Mara! I hope that's the end of it.
Did you see his face? I fear the cultist awoke and … suffered. \n\nWell. It is over. Now for the Daedra.
If you decide to go after the Grinder, just don't let him get the drop on you.\n\nThat would be the last mistake you'd ever make. Good luck out there.
What a day.
I'm relieved you were able to help the Vannes. I'll be heading back to Pariah Abbey now.\n\nYou should stop by some time. I'll tell you everything you ever wanted to know about the Spirit Wardens.
There's a friendly face. After being surrounded by Supernal Dreamers for so long, it's refreshing.\n\nThe more I get to know these people, the more I despise them.

Thank you. I was beginning to lose faith. So many selfish people just walk by, abandoning me and my sister to fate.\n\nIf you can just convince her to leave the house, then she and I can get out of here and go back to Camlorn.
Well, at least you're still alive. \n\nDid you manage to find any evidence that will help exonerate Hosni?
Hmm. You know, the sword doesn't feel especially magical. \n\nNonetheless, this is what I was sent here to reclaim, and you have aided me in this cause. The Mages Guild thanks you.

The lines on my face tell a sad story: the tale of a woman whose youth was stolen by circumstance.\n\nI was widowed even before I flowered. I did what I thought was right. I assumed the burden of leadership, but I paid for that choice. I paid dearly.
Now the trainees complain when I demonstrate thrusts to the head. Can't please anyone now a days.
You killed Galthis's minions? We mustn't get our hopes up, though. Not until Galthis himself is dead.

Did you pass through Crestshade by any chance? Do you know what's happening there?\n\nMy wife, the mayor of Crestshade, made me lead this group away when the fiends attacked. I keep hoping she'll walk into camp any moment now.
The Covenant thanks you for joining the war effort! With talented crafters like yourself at our back, there's no challenge we can't overcome. \n\nAkatosh bless your wares, friend.
Go away! So far, all the crazy people and monsters have just ignored this house. If you keep knocking they'll come and kill you!\n\nAnd then they'll break down the door and kill me!
I suppose I should be happy if the countess has finally chosen a husband.\n\nPerhaps it's time for me to move on.
Perhaps our reunion can bring peace to this place. I sense that something has changed.
Slowly, by divine grace, my powers return. \n\nSoon I shall once again be ready to contend with Molag Bal's monstrosities.

Damned foreigners. We've had nothing but trouble ever since the duke married King Fahara'jad's daughter.\n\nAnd now they bring an army to our doorstep and expect the Knights of the Flame to just stand aside?
How goes the search? Have you discovered anything yet?
I can't believe my suspicions were so far from the truth. The assassin being a Breton only makes this situation more volatile.\n\nPlease, tell Sir Hughes and ask him to resolve this matter swiftly.
I wouldn't go up there, if I were you.\n\nThe entire farm's been burned down. Scamps are everywhere, and Mister Nurin, he's gone missing!
I never imagined that getting locked in the stocks could be this painful.\n\nI hope you haven't forgotten about me.
It's about time. I assume the duke sent you? I am his personal messenger, you know.\n\nWell, what are you waiting for? Untie me!
As I said, I appreciate your help before, but in this situation, I can't afford to have someone questioning my authority.\n\nPlease. Just leave town. Easier for all of us.
Haha! My spirit soars to see you return in one piece. And you found the ledger, Ruptga bless you.\n\nPlease, take it to this constable and prove that we are friends and in need of assistance.
If you can just take care of those portals, I'm sure the rest of the Scamps will wander off eventually.
Turns out that almost everyone in town thinks Pascal has been acting strange—even the guards.\n\nDid you find anything that explains his behavior?
If you find Lucas, I'll be eternally grateful. He's just an innocent boy.\n\nIn a minute, I'll have to go get dinner ready, but I'm going to keep his plate warm.
My mother may have gone totally insane, but it's all right. My dad's here, and we're still a family.

Gods strike you! Couldn't you have just waited five more minutes?

The slavers outside the tent were talking about where their base of operations is … then they got interrupted. I'm guessing they saw you.

My mom sent you, didn't she?
I don't understand. Sir Hughes served me for so many years. Loyally. Faithfully. \n\nWhy would he murder my wife?
Lucas. Lucas. Lucas. That's all she talks about. \n\nMargot's worried sick about the boy. At this point, you'd think she'd have gotten over it.
Well, that didn't work. Time to come up with a new plan … again.
You are either suicidal or simply very stupid to barge in here without my permission. I will waste no further time with you. Be gone!
Listen to this braggart. Claims he could drop us all with a hand behind his back. The nerve.\n\nAnd King Fahara'jad claims these warriors are here in a diplomatic capacity? Preposterous!
You know what I'd love to do? I'd love to lay waste to every last one of these poxy clowns, but the constable says we're to just guard the door.\n\nAt least I'll get to watch them starve.
Soon, my husband and I will travel to Wayrest to get away from these gossipy provincial villagers.
You spoke with General Thoda? Please tell us, tell the Duchess what he said.
I will return home and speak with King Fahara'jad. I hope we can now focus on the loss of the one we loved rather than the crime that took her life. \n\nTime heals all wounds, or so they say.

Nothing about this has been easy, and it will be hard to look back on these events with anything other than sadness.\n\nI am glad you came along, though. Without you, we might not be able to look back on these days at all.
Trouble and trouble has come to Fell's Run. I hope you aren't bringing more, stranger.
Move along. The general is not entertaining guests right now.
<<1>> is the only champion left.\n\nWatch it: he's not called the Scourge of the Arena for nothing.
I can hardly believe it. <<1>> killed, and here I am speaking to the one who did it.\n\nI hated that Orc. If I could watch him die again, I would.
Revenge is sweet.\n\nIf only it could have been me out there. I'd have torn that beast's legs off one at a time.
You're back. What happened?
You did well. Roy couldn't have handled things any better.
Welcome back! Do you need more flowers?
Welcome to my shop. How may I help you?
Have you and Grenna found out anything new?
Save the villagers first, then we can talk.
Good luck in your travels. I expect to hear more great things of you in the very near future.
Not more pig trouble, I hope.
Please don't let Glutton become bacon. He's much too young to be eaten.
They were hiding here among us, weren't they? I thought as much. \n\nI hate missing out on killing werewolves, but I had, well, something else I had to keep an eye on.
The Red Rooks are done here. We'll be able to clear the rest of them out.
Traveler, there's trouble ahead. Bandits. You should turn back. We can't guarantee your safety.
Who goes there? Identify yourself.

Get everyone back here and we can keep them safe. For a while. In the meantime, we'll work on what to do next.\n\nAnd make sure you put those fires out. This building won't provide much protection if it burns to the ground.
Faolchu's hairy … Of all things!
I understand that saving my husband was just the latest in a series of heroic acts to save Stormhaven.\n\nThis was a threat to the Daggerfall Covenant as a whole, so Alik'r thanks you as well.
Thanks again for helping out with our training program.

He killed them, didn't he? By Stendarr, that's one more score we need to settle with Faolchu. \n\nIt's my fault. I should have acted sooner. I shouldn't have waited for proof that the Duke had been cursed.
Haven't seen that Fausta woman around have you? Oh, never mind. I'll find her later.
Please hurry. There's no telling what they plan to do with the captive women.\n\nThis is all my fault. I wish we'd never left Camlorn.
A spirit spoke to you? You need to continue this line of investigation and see where it leads.
Wonder why Lord Diel is so interested in keeping these things alive? What can you learn when a damn harpy is trying to peck your eyes out?
I'll never regret this decision. I will do my best to find happiness with my family, as my father wished.
I'm not sure I completely understand what's going on here. There is a harpy menace—isn't there?
You found Guy. I hope you can save the others, too.
Your actions have changed the balance of power in the bog.\n\nMother Murk's power wanes. Now the bog belongs to the wyrd.
That is the Gem of Westtry's Torment. How you acquired it, I don't want to know.  \n\nBut quickly, use it to free the villagers from this terrible curse.
Hawthorn shrubs grow throughout the village. Just pluck a few berries and get them to Muriel at the apothecary shop.
Don't worry about me, Captain. You've got a town to defend. I'll tend to any wounded who find their way here.
Captain Rosalind? I'm sorry. I couldn't hold them off.
Well, we're still alive.\n\nBut it's only a matter of time, of course. Even if we escape the hags, there's still the werewolves.
Aha! Perfect! Say though, you didn't happen to pick up a few giant's toes while you were at the bazaar, did you?
This should be interesting.
Best of luck, my brave friend.
Knock those hags' heads together!
It seems we've created a ripple in time itself. \n\nSomeone needs to go and find out what our spell actually accomplished.
Go, find Alana. We'll deal with Faolchu, once and for all.
Parmion will want to see these orders immediately. \n\nHe's in our camp to the east, in case you forgot that as well.
For a second, I thought I heard <<1>>. I must be losing my mind.
My sisters return to camp. Speak with the guardian.
You return. My brother and sister monarchs await word of your success.
The tower in the north courtyard contains the gate works. Get in there and lock it down. \n\nIf you stop more werewolves from coming in, we should be able to deal with the ones that are already here.
You return? I cannot believe … do you have the relics?
What a fantastic plan, I must say! So much excitement!
That was terrifying! A tad thrilling, too. But terrifying!
Stendarr bless you.
Thanks for helping the Duke. I'm glad I don't have to have his death on my conscience.
Take the path down to the beach. \n\nI'm too weak to walk, so I'll use my magic and meet you there.
General Gautier's troops are to the east, in the siege camp. \n\nThe wolves are on the offensive, so watch yourself.
Let Gautier know we're safe. I've got to get the wounded to the healers.
Go. We have nothing more to say.
I'll protect the portal and keep the Bloodthorn at bay. You go rescue my father.
We're committed to aiding the Lion Guard, so do as the General suggests.\n\nIt's not like we have a better option at the moment.

Thank you for helping us, wayfarer. \n\nI know my father explained everything, but I would add a desperate plea. Please do not just accept Enneh's word. Look elsewhere in the town. Whatever it takes to find Casnar and bring him here.
You know, I think we might actually have a chance of pulling this off.\n\nWell … if you can actually convince Uncle Thakh to let me out …. Hmm. Maybe we don't have a chance after all.
Welcome to Bergama, wayfarer! We have the finest musical instruments in Hammerfell!\n\nI am just closing up shop now, but if you want a harp, a lute, or even a drum, come back another time.
Try your hand at my gaming tables. We've got cards, dice, and good company. \n\nStay as long as you want. You might win big. No guarantees, of course.
And here we are, at the inn, all safe and sound. More or less. \n\nWe saw the light and followed you inside.
You placed my stone well. I should be protected this close to the tree.

Finally! Someone who's not afraid to do the dirty work. Someone to clean up my docks! I watched you from the window until I heard those necromancers downstairs. \n\nBut I thought Maujad was coming here too—did you see him?
We just watched boats filled with Bloodthorn cultists sail away from the docks. What happened down there?
Your advances are sweet, walker. \n\nMaybe we will cross paths again in the next life and things will be different.
Darien talks of nothing but wine and women, but behind his bluster he's a better tactician than his father. \n\nThough that's not saying much.
Will someone just let me know whether or not we're going to get paid for this? I could really use the gold.

I'm sure that you realize that with the Reachmen bearing down on us, I have a great many matters to attend to.\n\nI absolutely do not wish to be rude, but I must be going. Come back another time and I will endeavor to answer all your questions.
Good day to you. Have you come at the summons of her ladyship?
Ah, you're back. And in a timely manner. Did you find the crown?
I trust General Gautier. Follow his orders and the city will be ours again.
Get into that tower and lock that gate. We'll be right behind you.
Go and find that bothersome noble. She's not far, just down the passageway.

Don't worry. I'll take the priest to Prince Adrien. \n\nHopefully, the prince has regained enough strength to walk to the church. I don't think I can carry him in full plate, and I'm betting our friendly priest here won't be much help.
Please, don't hurt me! I don't want to die!\n\nWait, you're not the creature that attacked my father. You're not even one of the Montclairs.
Though I hate the undead, I can't help but pity the men and women they once were. \n\nTu'whacca, guide me!
No! No, please! Leave me alone! I haven't done anything.
I don't remember inviting you aboard. Make your business quick, or you'll be picking seaweed out of your teeth.

The captain headed in the direction of the inn. You should be able to catch up. Find out what she's up to and then take all this to the queen.\n\nIf this prompts her into action, it might just be worth it. She would make a wonderful ruler, you know.
You certainly made short work of those Elves. There seem to be few odd skeletons down here, no problem for you, I'm sure.\n\nNow, I assume you found the old tome in my camp?
The stone rules the flesh, here as everywhere. Flesh must always yield to stone.
You are a noble spirit and a brave soul, my friend. \n\nYou've done me a good turn here, and by exposing Stibbons' uselessness, you've done Lady Laurent a favor too.
Evoker Valinwe can be found in Aldcroft, to the east of here.
It's good to see the Duke back in Camlorn. This is where he belongs.
He wandered as a vulture circles its prey. But he truly has no sense of direction, and thus managed to wander farther away with each passing moment.\n\nWe must find him.
A familiar scent surrounds you. Did the Sentinel send you? What do you hold?

That certainly wasn't my finest hour, but I thought … I thought it was Arkay. I thought he was giving me a second chance.\n\nThere's nothing more foul than this creature's deception. It must've hailed from the depths of Oblivion itself!

I've known Stenwick since I was a child. Just because we didn't agree on many things, doesn't mean his burial tradition should be ignored.\n\nI'd hoped for a change with his death, but it seems the princess will continue the Sentinel's work. A shame.

The <<1>> should make itself known to you. You'll have to keep your eyes open for a sign.\n\nOf course, there's other, less subtle ways of getting its attention. They say the forest feels the death of every creature.
Where are the rest of the reinforcements? Are you all they sent?
You're not from the Reach, are you? Sometimes, it's hard to tell.
<Medya's torso is covered in old and faded Reachman tattoos which were previously obscured by her humble peasant's attire.>
I can't believe it. You gave the tools to Tamien? How could you?\n\nNow I'll never get back to Lady Laurent's good graces!
Stenwick only asked for wyrd's blessing to be kind, but they don't seem ready to help him, do they?
This beautiful woman from the Mages Guild just arrived. Says she knows you! You can introduce me later.\n\nI was right about the amulets, though, wasn't I?
The rescued miners are singing your praises. Well done!
The king will be grateful for what we've done here. Some of Angof's minions are still running loose, but it's nothing we can't handle.\n\nMaybe things will finally return to normal now.
All Crosswych is talking about you. \n\nThe Red Rooks are on the run. If they try to stop, we'll chase them right out of town.
What answers the call is the Hunger.
Get to Lainlyn, comrade. <<1>> will fill you in on the details when you get there.
Report! \n\nHave you stopped the Withered Hand from recruiting the Saltwalker Company?
Well, we've been through quite a bit together, haven't we? \n\nI think I like you. You're fun! Stop by and visit if you're ever in the neighborhood!

Hm. I suppose that answers the question. Our fates are no more fixed than the wind that blows across these dunes.\n\nUnless … do you think maybe that was not the right wind storm? Do you believe that maybe there is another … just about to appear?

I'm sorry I wasn't there when you killed Angof. I needed to get the others back here safety. I think they'll recover. Now if only Darien would stop distracting me with his chatter.\n\nAnyway, you really are something.
Given how many of us were hurt at the garrison, prisoners aren't high on the priority list.\n\nI hope we can get his wounds treated quickly.
Always remember the lesson you've learned here today, friend. Fate does not control those who are willing to step to the fore. Set your hand against fortune, and you will see your wishes fulfilled.
Medya needed to die for all that she's done here.\n\nThe people of Evermore need not hear whatever lies she would use to defend herself at a trial.
We must hurry, before Kerbol does anything more to hurt my husband!

He speaks the truth. I've bound everyone here to this village, but by doing so, freed them from the curse of lycanthropy. They all chose it willingly.\n\nThink what you want of it, but each of our sacrifices is for the greater good.
My commander will hear of your exploits, I promise you.
Is that … is that blood all mine? All of it? I don't think that's good.\n\nIf I die, I swear by Malacath that I'll come back for you.
Now that you've picked a lizard, you can enter it in a race. Put your lizard in a starting cage when you're ready, and let's watch that baby fly!
I'm certainly glad you came to Crosswych. People wanted to fight back, but they just needed some encouragement.
You have a triumphant look about you. Spit it out, have you the key or not?
<The dog pants happily.>
If you plan to enter your lizard in a race, you'll need to put it in a starting cage.
It hurts … it hurts! Go … away!

In addition to the public praise, I must add my own private words of appreciation, wayfarer.\n\nYou not only saved the kingdom, you also saved its king. My reign would have been buried in the sands had you not intervened. Thank you.

They don't suspect, do they? Surprise! Surprise on the dancers. Surprise on Madame Lurue. \n\nHer black book is in her sanctuary, beyond the dancers. Stop them all! End of the dance. It's time to go home.
I think my luck's about to change for the better … oh yes.
Destroy the relics! They keep me trapped here.
No one died today. It's all because of your help.\n\nMay Tava lend speed your steps, traveler.
Your actions today have saved lives, wayfarer. You should be proud.\n\nRemember that as you bed down tonight.
Now that you have the goods, take them to Ildani, and then to the buyers. \n\nDon't worry. We'll be watching. If anything goes wrong, we'll have your back.
My son is safe and my family has been restored to me.\n\nYou are truly a gift from merciful Stendarr.
Without your help, I would have been a meal for the jackals.
I hardly see why you deserved payment at all. Still, you are one of the few who actually bothered to return to let me know.
I'm glad we won't be seeing any overgrown alligators in these parts anytime soon.
<The captain lies writhing on the ground. Nightmare fire streams from braziers to his struggling form.>
Speak to Lorelia and listen to her wisdom.
This is the entrance to her lair. I'm sure of it. \n\nI don't see her in there, so I think it's safe to go in and search for the stolen relics.
Go away before the guards catch us!
I look forward to doing business with you in the future!
Thanks to the Baandari, I can maintain a pretty decent lifestyle.
You know, we're supposed to be keeping this relationship subtle.
Hurry! You need to switch the orders before they start to move out for Volenfell. \n\nThey could strike camp suddenly. You never know with armies … it's always hurry up and wait.
I'd check the Mages Guild in Daggerfall if I were you. They must have a scroll or a tome that will tell us how to speak with the spirits of the dead.
Praise the Golden Eye! That foul creature could be here any moment, and I wouldn't have wanted to face her without you.\n\nWhatever happens, we can't let her get to the shrine! Are you ready?

So you are the one the tides of fate carried here to stop this transgression?\n\nI had watched this pathetic spirit's attempt to avoid her fate with some amusement … but I knew it would eventually have to come to an end.
Our captive convinced you to help him, didn't he? \n\nHe's sending you into a trap, mark my words.

Look for the Bloodthorn envoy in the central part of the ruins.\n\nBe careful though. Once he falls, disguise or not, they'll come after you with everything they have. Only your wits and your weapons will get you out of there in one piece.
Now we have to extinguish the signal fires.
We'll make sure the Dominion are stopped here.
Have you dealt with Leonce yet? As long as he lives, we'll never be able to overcome the Fell's Brigade.
You don't look like one of those vampires or bloodfiends, so I guess you're welcome. This is Camp Tamrith. We're sheltering the refugees from Crestshade and the surrounding countryside here.
Save Captain Janeve!
Mother is hungry, but it makes me a little sick to watch her eat.\n\nAre you looking for the Captain? They dragged her into the cave. The Bad One is going to do terrible things to her.
We lost too many good soldiers today. But the four of us survive thanks to you.\n\nThe rest of the Lion Guard will hear of your exploits today, friend.
And here is the savior of my people, my city, and me! We are all in your debt, friend.
I'm glad we won't be seeing any overgrown alligators in these parts anytime soon.
We're dealing with the harpies as fast as we can, I assure you. Now please, address any specific complaints to one of the guardsmen.

Nuwarrah's family has alway been a thorn in my side. Now that I helped save the city, she'll probably host a feast in honor of the deed.\n\nThat could mar my reputation with the Thieves Guild. The woman is impossible.
State your business, traveler. Fell's Run has enough trouble. We really don't need any more.
Orcs are parasites, sucking the very marrow from our town. They are fur-fleas, getting fat and bloated on the blood of our people. The time has come to end the infestation once and for all!

Did you hear what that son of a troll said about us? It's slander, I tell you! Slander!\n\nLeonce is just trying to divert attention from his own guilt. If our cowardly constable won't do something about this, we will!
I think it's best if we go our separate ways. Though you helped considerably, I can't take that risk again.
May the gods grant you luck against the Imperials. Many more are on our side that it appears.
Thanks to you, we've finally got this town back under control.
It's not safe to speak so openly. The sand carries whispers wherever it goes.
What are you doing in my home? Did Quatrius send you?\n\nI've done everything he's asked! I won't suffer any more humiliation at his hands!
Nasir sells no goods, only information. More dangerous, more profitable.
Luck to you. I'll see if we can hold this line in case you return … I mean, until you return.

Grandmaster Tanval says that if the Covenant gets the heart, it could let them raise a Brother of Strife against us. That thing could wipe out Ebonheart.\n\nWhatever it costs, we've got to keep that weapon out of their hands.
My eggs must twine with the coral, if it's to join us against the Covenant.
Well, get going. The grandmaster needs to act now.
Did you recover the relic?
You have the <<z:1>>?
A living soul? It has been so long. To walk the river again, it is so strange. And so sad.
I don't understand Furon's plan, but you shouldn't keep him and that clever brother of his waiting.
Still no news? Work quickly before his crimes are discovered. I will not let my brother ruin our house!
Are you looking for <<1>>? He's on the far side of town from here.\n\nLook for the temple.
The coral child lives, and will protect us from the Daggerfall Covenant. We are once again fruit of the same tree.
The hatchling has been found, unhurt. This is good. \n\nGirvas speaks like an angry wind. Perhaps you should calm his blustering.
Oh, great. This is all I need.
Traveler you … you found my daughter. In the midst of all this, you found my Morvani.
Use this medicine on the injured. If they complain it is Argonian-made, ignore them.\n\nWhen you are done, find <<1>>. He is near the center of town.
F'lah, you'll find the flasks of blinding light upstairs. Use them to reveal the assassin infiltrators. Put an end to their plans.
Activate the first four plates in these tunnels and meet me in the last chamber. Go well, and go quietly.
We need to get that thing under guard, and fast. Get it to Holgunn back at camp. There's a quick exit to the west. Look for the vines.
