Good. You made it! Thank you for rallying these brave men and women. We stand a chance now!
You don't belong here.
Remember, get arms caches and bring to Khajiit out by the shoreline. He will have your money waiting for you.
Shame about Captain Helane. I hear even a touch of that poison gives you the runs for years, though. That'll keep me grinning.

The sergeant said Velyn Harbor would have fallen without you. Honor to meet you—I'm the Green Lady. The, uh, the new one.\n\nI could use your help. The Drublog clan usually side with my people in times of war. We need to learn what changed.
Have you spoken to my father? We must hurry, with or without his blessing.
<<1>> told me she'd wait for the right champion at the upper arena's gates.\n\nGo and do what you must.
I'm surprised House Dres managed to do anything with the Ordinators on high alert. Not much gets past them, even when they're not looking for trouble.
Did you get it? I'm going to need that wine if this ruse is going to work.
I watched you fight. Impressive.
Soon. Soon you too will know of my greatness.
Tell Daljari you bested some brawlers. Then come back here so I can knock you around.
Once again, you return safely from the dream, bringing one of Vaermina's victims back with you.\n\nGeneral Godrun seems to be feeling himself again.
Your technique is good but that is rarely good enough.
Bthzark is on the north side of the island. Neramo should be poking around the ruins.
Tell Daljari you're ready for a real fight.
I didn't expect to get help so quickly. Remind me to thank Kaleen when we're done here.
Where do you think I found my husband? Hiding! Hiding in a tree stump!
I'm going to stick around and see what I can salvage here. Pity about poor Raston, though.
Follow the rules. Talk to Daljari and then we can fight.
You should give the bucket to Jill.
What do you want?
Follow the road to the mine. I'll be right there.
You desecrate a few old graves, and already the Bretons are back to complain.\n\nNice work dealing with the cult. Warchief Tazgol will be pleased.
If the Maulborn figured out a way to reactivate these wards, they have more powerful allies than we thought. \n\nNow be careful and get your shapely butt moving.
My friend! As you can see, my lovely wife Liane found me. I mean, I found her! We found each other!\n\nPlease give me good news. Please.
Let me do the talking, won't you?
I'll have this guillotine down and burned before the day's over. You have my word.
Please … you have to help. They're trapped. There's no help coming, and they don't know it.
Get out of my house! Put on a shirt and get back to the arena, whelp!
Thank you for helping <<1>> find me.
Thank you for sparing my cousin. \n\nEspecially since I'm sure he doesn't deserve it. The old rascal.
I'll be sure to credit you when I present my findings to the Mages Guild. Thank you again!
Hurry! If the guards catch you, they'll have your head on a pike!
I hope you made the right choice. It is done. Other matters concern us now.
We've got a crew to rival the legends! Time to make some money, don't you agree?
I am done talking. Make the right decision!
Now, put it over your head and get out of my sight.
Well, look who's come to pay a visit!
The man is a pig. But then, aren't they all?
By the Empyrean Light. The Worm Cult brought his spirit back, didn't they? And you led him here.

I feel … free. It's as though a burden has been lifted from me, a burden I didn't know I carried.\n\nWhatever you did, it feels … right. When my memory returns, I'll find you and thank you properly for this.
Another day, another whipping. This job just gets better and better.
Endarwe has to know more. Talk to him again.
Shuzura knows how I feel about her. Just make sure to rub it in. Heh.
Khali … damn it. So strong, so forceful. So stupid when it comes to things like this. \n\nI suppose there's nothing else for it. We have to make for Dune.
You're a gift from the Stars. Once you're into the tunnels, Telenger should be easy to find. Do whatever it takes to get that old fool out of there.
Shazah … damn it. Why did she force me into this? \n\nI suppose there's nothing else for it. We have to make for Dune.
I should warn you, Gloo is a little … odd. But she's a damned genius when it comes to alchemy.
Good timing. We need to get some information out of our friend here. She seems pretty dense.\n\nI was just telling her how delicious I find silent tongues.
You're going to do great! Just, whatever you do, don't … err. \n\nYou know what? I forget. Probably wasn't important. Meet me at my workshop, northwest edge of the village, when you're done.
I wanted to pick up something nice for Captain Kaleen. Something to surprise her, like a new mug. But all this stuff is so expensive!
If the Countess is truly sick, I am more than a little bit concerned. \n\nI would not wish to remain in this village if she was not in charge.
We have sailed often to Betnikh these last years. Chief Tazgol is a gracious host. In many ways, this is my second home.
If it's true that the Countess is… well, no longer able to manage her estate… I hope it's Sir Brice who takes over.
You will always find a warm welcome aboard our ship, for as long as Captain Kaleen's in charge.
You journey into danger. Choose your steps carefully.
Bah, the dull claws on you. Do you have any idea how many coins you're leaving on the table?
Thank you. You have made a wise decision. The Bright Moons will sing your name for this.
Kalari will be all right, you will see. Just needs some time to deal with what has happened.\n\nGo, speak to Shuzura. She will want to hear from you.
You haven't finished serving everyone at the bar yet!
He came stalking back here, mad as a wet Khajiit. You'd better talk to him.
You smell like burnt corn. Is it done?
My, my. So the Arbordawn cult has been spun into Mephala's web. Fascinating. Worrying, to be sure! But fascinating.
Fivefold venerations upon you, traveler. What brings you to the Falinesti Autumn site?
Welcome to the Falinesti Autumn site. I'm with the team Telenger has brought. What brings you this way?
Welcome to the Falinesti Autumn site. Ghadar is working with the famed Artificer Telenger to study the site.
Don't worry. Tazia will not be moving. She has no interest in any kind of heroics.

That map—it marks the location of our treasures! Listen, I don't know how you got it, and I can't stop you from looking for those relics with these necromancers around, but if you find them, bring them to me.\n\nI'll make it worth your while.
Did you do it? Did you kill the Goblin king?
There's more to this plot than simply spreading chaos across the land. I won't rest until we uncover the truth behind this assassination attempt.
This is it! Either we break them or they break us!\n\nWhere is everyone? It's going to take more than just me!
Well? What did you find? Did he leave behind some papers, something to show what's going on in Shuzura's town?
I know we have just met, but you must listen to me. You must decide, do your duty. Destroy the circlet.
What are you still doing here? Shuzura will be wanting you there now, not when you feel like it.
Still waiting to hear why I need you.
You again? What's it this time?
Keep your eyes peeled. This place is crawling with surprises.
I honor you for bringing news of my brother's death. Now I know his fate, sad as it was.
Ha! I didn't think I'd ever find you. You move around.
What were you doing in the mine? And did you see a scummy Breton up there?
I'll take the Baron back to town with me. The magistrate will know what to do with him.
Ah! Thank Alkosh you found her! We've lost enough soldiers today without adding our best scout to their ranks. \n\nWith luck, the two of you will find more, yes?
What a day.
If you choose to destroy the relic, then you've turned your back on me and the Covenant. Make the right choice.
Did it go well? Do you have the samples?
Raz could not help but overhear. It is a terrible thing, to tell a person her father is gone.
He's badly hurt. I'll see if I can get him bandaged up.
Head to Moriseli, the Ayleid ruin to the north. Shaman Azlakha is already out there, and she may need help.
Chief Tazgol took the army to Carzog's Demise. Hurry if you want to actually kill any cultists.

To think that my brother was afflicted by something similar to Sir Hughes … that's frightening indeed. \n\nI thank you for helping him. I still hope we're able to bring Sir Hughes to justice for what happened to my sweet Lakana.
What're you waiting for? Let's get rid of that pest!
I can't make Goblin's Delight without sugar leaf. Get it and I'll make you a treat you will never forget. Zich loves it!
You! How much more blood do you want?
Spare your blade, Orc. We have yielded to you.
Looks like you found his family. Maybe he isn't as full of Elf dung as I thought.
It's time. The people of Crosswych have taken up arms and are ready to retake their town.\n\nBut first, <<1>> must die.
We need this shore cleared to advance. Get these lamias off my beach!
My mistake cost my family their home and my people their lives. In my anguish, I sought to redeem myself.
I had my unit scale the sheer cliff behind us, and there was much complaining. The young are weak.\n\nYou, however, handled that Conduit Stone very well.
So the duchess got killed by one of those high-and-mighty knights?\n\nFolks like me, we liked her—and now she's gone. I hope those knights get what's coming to them.
The ritual tore the veil between Nirn and Oblivion, allowing Mannimarco to begin stealing the souls his master needed to power the Dark Anchors and initiate the Planemeld.
The holy waters of Do'Krin have kept the Claw safe for years. I pray they keep you safe as well.
Why did you invade our island? We had no quarrel with you!
The thought of the dead walking around is unsettling at best. Soon they'll be shambling into Cropsford!
As soon as I know there's nothing in here, we can go. I have a feeling though. Keep looking around.
The spirits have vanished! Their valiant souls rest once again. Quickly tell me what you found below; we have much to discuss.
I need to get these goods shipped to Daggerfall right away. So please, just leave me alone. \n\nNo offense, but our business is finished and I want nothing more to do with you.
Yes?
Lord Diel is a miserable piece of work. I just hope my brother knows what he's doing.
I've got no love for the Covenant, but it is good to see a few more Orc faces in town.
I think the constable did the right thing. There's something shady about that knight. I've been watching her.

Indaenir's a real piece of work, isn't he? I always thought he was half-mad. They say he has "the Green" in his blood, but most things that man does, I just don't understand. \n\nRecently though, I've realized just how fortunate we are to have him.

The incessant clamor of the undead at the gate finally stops, and you come through the gate—it is a relief to finally see someone new from among the living.\n\nIs Akkhuz-ri correct in thinking you have come to our aid?
Glad that's done. The pleading of the condemned is almost too much to bear. One way or another, they are returned to the Forest.
I'm just going to assume at this point that S'rashi's giving me a break. True or not, that's what I'm going with. \n\nMeans I can head back to the ship …. Well, maybe just one more drink first.
That was unexpected.
First time an outsider's ever beaten me.
That banner has no place in Vlastarus. You know what you need to do.
You have taken many steps along the Path already, Hallowed. Jone and Jode have shown me … just a few more to go.
You made it! I wasn't sure if you would. I haven't had a drink in days, but if you've got the ingredients I need, it's time to celebrate!
Why isn't … why isn't he breathing? \n\nOh gods, we're too late.
This guar gives its life so we may have meat. Now, I give you my time. Why?
When I leave this place, I will need all my strength. I thank you for my life.
Did you get my lute from <<1>>?
Stretch your tail here in peace.\n\nWhat brings you to the Hatching Pools?
Been to Crosswych, eh? We'll have the Red Rooks on the run soon enough.
What took you so long?
I'd never seen Sai's proving grounds before. It must have been a serene place before the attack.
I suspect that Vardan died when the portal closed. The body cannot survive without the soul.
You have a container, good. Are you ready for what's next?
This place is pretty impressive.
I need you to listen to me.
This thing must be destroyed!
Don't mind Marius. He was ordered here to look after the interests of the Empire. But really, all he cares for is his own advancement.
Quickly, Hallowed. Close the portal! Sealing it should draw the beasts back to Oblivion.
More wounded arrive by the hour. I hope you have good news for me.
Use the visions as guides, not shackles. Your fate is yours to determine.
Hmph. You've impressed even me. The Dominion owes you yet another debt.
Leave me alone.

You're looking for Sir Hughes, aren't you? Get in line. We've been waiting for him to come and clarify our orders for days. \n\nHe returned all right. But mumbling incoherently. Know what that means? Just more confusion. I think Hughes has lost it.
I wonder what's taking Jakarn so long? I wouldn't keep a girl like me waiting.
Curse Jakarn! How does he slip about so easily? I turn my back for one moment and he's gone.\n\nHe's probably off with those slatterns from Stros M'Kai. If I find any of them, it won't be pretty.
You have no idea how long I've waited to taste a good Orcish brew! That swill the Redguards call beer has less kick than a mudcrab.\n\nNow, if only Lambur would join me.
At last, I find myself looking forward to my future.
The Bright Moons smile down upon us, traveler. The Claw is safe.
You have returned! Bright Moons be praised! Do you … do you have the relics?
I respect the captain, but I won't set foot on an island full of Orcs.
Well, I'm considering waiting til we get out to sea, then throwing you over. I can barely stand the sight of you.

I lost my best daggers when the Maiden's Breath ran aground. I'm going to pick up something new, but the question is what?\n\nDo I need a new dagger or a trusty mace? Depends on what we're killing, I suppose.
I don't trust these Orcs. Their chief refuses to join the Covenant. No idea why.
I'm … I'm the Mane! Hallowed, we survived!
Hallowed, thank you for dispatching that treacherous Urcelmo. I … have to admit, I'm going to make jokes at his expense for years off this.
Sholg says you talked Lokra out of her wild ideas. You honor our clan. She will be an asset to her people.
Point me at what you'd like slain.
What is it? You want me to stab something?

We've been through quite a bit together, haven't we?\n\nIf you ever pass this way again, feel free to stop by and visit. I can think of a few other rituals that you can help me with, if you're interested.
Hunal's commentary on your progress has been … most interesting, Hallowed. I hope seeing me alive and well is not too distressing.
I'm sorry, Hallowed. The words of the Moon-Bishop have affected me greatly. The thought of my people gone feral, my Silvenar dead ….
Hunal tells me you've already progressed well along the path. You continue to impress me, Hallowed.
Oh the agony! The affront to our faith and our people!
They have some interesting brews here, don't you think?
The Covenant moved in when they took Drakelowe. As long as they don't make me work, we'll get along.
Too close! They nearly had us that time. The wards will keep the Daedra bound, for now, but I'm still not sure how they managed to break them. We need to investigate Ilmyris.
You have my gratitude. That is no small thing. Zadala always remembers her debts.
The Woodland Man is not wood or land or a man.
Orthenir's soul seals the binding, but without a caretaker the Daedra flee. It is temporary. The mountain is worn away and the tides rise and fall with the same inevitability.
We can get to the Imperial underground through an old guardtower. Raz thinks it's … to the southwest? Yes. Let's go!
Quick work. Word spreads that I have a new collector. I've already gotten back some of the coin I was owed.
What are you doing standing around here? You have your mission. Do not miss the meeting!
Well done. You've made quite a name for yourself among the Shadowscales. \n\nSoon, our services will be required elsewhere. We may need you again in the future.
Don't bother coming back here until you've run off the Orcs. I've got important business to attend to. Heh.
Hurry! Head into the tunnel and find our leader. She'll explain the plan to you.
It is time for you to go. Leave my body here, where it cannot be bothered again.\n\nYou have done more than I could have hoped for. Thank you.
Ahh, a traveler. Coming from Dune, sent by the Moon-Bishop, if she had to guess. This one is pleased to see you.
My scales are falling out.
What a day.
The Stormfist thugs captured me. I'm done for!
Beginner's luck. You still need to win three duels.
If the plague of necromancy has truly returned, I fear the future may bring many dark days.\n\nSomeone will need to come forward to fight the risen dead.
So there you have it. My true form revealed.
Ha! You should've seen Garnikh's face when you won that duel!
Oh, no.\n\nCheck his body. There must be something to tell us who did this.
Good fight. Garnikh's bitten off more than he can chew this time.
So, I'm next?
Good Thane Harvald here has let me in on your recent accomplishments.\n\nYou certainly are disrupting Fildgor's plans here at Fort Amol.
I hope you realize what you've gotten yourself into. Once you're in Fahara'jad's inner circle, you'll never get a moment's rest. \n\nI know this from personal experience.
So, you convinced Lokra to remain. Good. It may not be what she wanted, but it's best for our clan.
Lokra never really had a choice. I'm glad you helped her see that.\n\nWithout her clan, she is lessened. And without her, so are we.
Did you manage to fill up the supply cache?

Of all the ports in Tamriel, why this one? I sailed all the way across the Iliac Bay and I need a glass of grog!\n\nI've shared a drink with some unsavory characters, but I draw the line at zombies. I think I'll stay off the docks for now.
We're here. In Daggerfall. Now get off my boat.
The Fangs of Sithis are the property of the Night Mother. We will return them to our enclave and protect them until they are needed.
Thanks for getting those supplies. Quite a few of us have been in need of a good patching up.
I can't believe we survived that! You made the right choice, I think. Anything else would have been disaster.
Rid-Thar will tell you what he can. But know that this choice is yours. You must choose with your heart, and your mind, and your soul.
Look for the truth behind the appearances in her memory. She is a very special young lady.
I trust you, traveler. I know you've made the right decision.
You should find enough uniforms to disguise all of the prisoners in that crate over there.
Tand thought he was going to be sold! This one thanks you for your help!
His life mate <<1>> warned him of the dangers here, but <<2>> did not listen. The son of Muzag is as stubborn as he is naive.
<<1>> attracts trouble like fleas. He'll get his claws clipped one day, I swear.
I almost lost hope! You will always be remembered by this family!
Thunderbug bellies and hive seeds make a fire guardian. Hive seeds and dew bugs make a wooden guardian. Thunderbug bellies and dew bugs, a water guardian.\n\nIt's up to you.

You released him—I think that was the right thing to do. \n\nI'm glad to know that at least some of the spirits here will be able to rest, though I am sorry for the villagers who remain trapped in the Shadow Wood.
Do not hesitate. This is the only way the Keeper oath is fulfilled and Tamriel remains safe.
Patience, my friend. The race is about to begin!
Please … help me.
Let us not dawdle in this vile place. Find me in the Hollow City and speak to me there.
Rumors say that the people of Zuuk were wiped out by a flu years ago.
All this standing around is bad for my knees.

It seems the Prince of Murder has already disrupted your plan. Where is your army? Surely not even you can hope to take on a Daedric Prince by yourself.\n\nYou need an army. And you need a safe haven to discuss strategy and gather your forces.
Will the Champion of <<1>> also prove to be the champion of spikeball?
Keep moving. I'm right behind you!
Well, don't dally about here, you've got a princess to rescue. It was a princess, wasn't it?
Disaster looms with the Elder Scroll of Altadoon in the hands of our enemies. It must be recovered!

You see? It's clear that Asteril has been dead for some time, so she cannot have been the one you saw in the Imperial tunnels!\n\nI told you—say what you will about the Thalmor—but we do not have traitors in our midst.

If you haven't seen it yourself, Dominion forces are all over <<A:1>>. They kill anyone who tries to leave.\n\nThe only good news is they've left the eggs unharmed. We could use your help in learning why.
I guess you aren't an illusion, after all. Skordo also vouched for your existence. He doesn't vouch for anything, so you must have really impressed him.
Ezreba prays for forgiveness.
Damned cultists. Tried to melt our minds and left a giant mess to clean up. Damned inconsiderate.
Was that a vision of Lady Estre? Is there no end to the strange magic of this place?
Do what you must, outsider. Do what you must.
I'm trying to eavesdrop on the conversation, if you don't mind.
The fight is about to begin! May Riddle'Thar bring you luck!
I wish I'd had a chance to talk to that Dunmer before he sped off. What could he know about this?
Finished with your little chat?\n\nI shall relieve him of his head now and rid us of his insufferable mewling.
You must have mercy! The Dark Elf won't listen, but you will, won't you? \n\nWe were different! I didn't want this!
<The statue holds the Gem of Preservation.>
Stay alert.
Sadly, they weren't much of a challenge. What's a girl gotta do for a challenge these days?
<The statue holds the Gem of Preservation.>
<The statue holds the Gem of Preservation.>
Your legend grows. Bring this information to our warchief.
Orc! You will pay for this.
So, not overcome by poisonous fumes or fallen into lava yet?
You've done it! Tell Yzzgol what you've learned. Let's end this.
When you're prepared to travel, we leave for Rictus.
I know it will be hard for the community to accept her, but I think this is for the best. She deserves a chance to rejoin the village.
<<1>> pulled me out of the water. Owed him my life.\n\nNot too late to pay him back.

Thanks to you, my squad has safe passage to <<1>>.\n\n<<2>> offered to make us part of the Prowler's crew. Don't know if I'll have a choice once the fleet puts itself back to together, but it's better than sitting around and counting sand.
May Y'ffre look after <<1>>. The gods know, nothing will protect his killer once the sergeant learns their names.\n\nYou go warn that ship. We'll prepare our friend for what awaits us all.
Before the next sun sets, my blade will find a home in the heart of <<1>>'s killer. May the fates guide me to avenge him.
Bright moons, traveler. Merani is grateful she has the chance to improve her aim!
You're the talk of the town. Why don't you come over here and let me thank you?
That foul creature. I expect her to lead the Shadowed Path into Vlastarus any minute now!
Forgive me. You did so much to help a stranger. I won't forget.\n\nI can open a portal to the temple courtyard, if you wish.
Please don't think me ungracious. Without your aid, I'd still be under <<1>>'s influence. I won't forget.\n\nI can open a portal to the temple courtyard, if you wish.
If only the bandits would leave us alone, we might have a chance.
Sea Vipers are all over the beach, but the lookout spotted a bunch of them on that island nearby. I don't know what they're up to, but it can't be good.
Stop interrupting, Dark Elf!\n\nExcuse me, please. What else can Zur assist you with?
The summoner's array still remains. Destroying it should put an end to their assault on Mistral.
I could get used to traveling around with you. It's never dull, I'll give you that.

I will never forgive you for what you did. That relic is going to cause horrible suffering in the world.\n\nI'm leaving this ship, leaving Kaleen. Perhaps I'll go out on my own. Whatever happens, stay out of my way.

I will be blunt. You were a fool to trust a relic that powerful to these Bretons. If they do not use it for evil, they will harm themselves through their ignorance.\n\nI believe I am done with both you and Captain Kaleen.

When the elves attack our shores and hundreds of our soldiers die, I want you to remember the choice you made. If you had kept that relic, we could have saved those soldiers.\n\nYou made the wrong choice.
Your decision at Carzog's Demise will affect this world greatly, for good or for ill. Kasan fears the relic will bring more destruction than good. Even so, it was your decision.\n\nTravel safely.

Well, after all the years it's taken me to find this place, I certainly did not expect to see someone else down here. \n\nWere you searching for it as well? Or do you even realize that this is the final resting place of Sabasad the Shield?
Can't you see I'm reading here? Please, leave me in peace.
What is it you want? Wait, what are you holding? Is that … no! He must have sent you. Please, I need more time.
Be cautious! There are some here not friendly to Pact soldiers.
Ears that large and you still don't listen? Perhaps you need a few alterations.\n\nThere was a time when the sound of <<1>>'s voice commanded the terror of thousands.
Welcome back to the Guild Hall! How goes the search?
Watch yourself! This isn't a safe place for soldiers of the Covenant.
Seeing my comrades again gives me hope. We'll guard the outpost while you finish this.
Choose carefully. I don't want that … thing in our village any more.
I applaud your bravery in coming here, but sharp swords will seek your life if you stay.
The spring in your step! Did you know a sense of accomplishment can alter one's stride? You learn to notice it in others.
You are with the Khajiit, outsider. I know this. Go. Talk to your friend.
The Mane still lives. I trust you have a good reason for this, my friend?
The light of the moon will purge the darkness from the heart of Arenthia.
They think I've no authority here. How wrong they are! \n\nI am here under the personal authority of <<A:1>>, and when he hears of this debacle, heads will roll. Mark my words!
If the Sea Vipers call up a hurricane, the Prowler won't ever make it out to sea.
I don't know how much the Maormer are willing to listen to reason. But I must try, for the sake of <<1>>.
Please, bring <<1>> to justice.
Happy just for the chance to do something normal. Relaxed. Thank the Green for you.

Ah, the errant deputy.\n\nI was just informing Headwoman <<1>> of her apothecary's connections to the High Elves of Summerset Isle. Once the torture begins, we'll learn why the Dominion killed their own diplomat.
Get what you need. I'll get what I need in a moment.

Z'en's price! We don't deserve this. We've done nothing wrong. I'm beginning to think our clan's just cursed.\n\nDriven from our home, then we find a new place to settle, only to have the very earth itself rise up against us …? It's not fair.
Balag hears that you are doing well in the arena. You don't look so tough as you must be.
Congratulations. As insipid as those hopefuls undoubtedly were, you surprised me. I didn't think you stood a chance.
I suppose you're feeling pretty cocky about now. Don't let it go to your head. The qualifying rounds are child's play. \n\nAre you ready to take on a real challenger?

Welcome back, my lovely! Zara wondered when you would return. She missed you terribly. \n\nThe other contenders should thank Jone and Jode that championships are not won by physical attraction. Your sleekness would best them all.
Mysterious Stranger, you are truly the Grand Champion! You should consider accepting a position as the trainer here. You could have your choice of divisions!
You're doing the right thing. Go destroy that bastard so my people can live here in peace.

Few have emerged from the forest who were not fleeing in terror. I can only imagine how dark it must be. \n\nAll the same, this is no safe haven. Driladan Pass is overrun with skeletons led by the undead form of Prince Naemon himself.
The seals … unlock the seals … and I can … break free ….
The scribs kept away from that fetching tree trunk. They don't seem to care for it. If you help it do what it needs to do, I have no doubt they'll find their way back to shore.
This isn't a good time for a chat, stranger. Though if you have good news, that would be a welcome change.
Yes?
You got what you wanted. Off with you.
I can feel the spirit's frustration. It wants to help the Great Tree, but something prevents it.
Thank you once again for what you did. Let's not speak of the details. Thorinor has worried enough as it is. You brought us back together, and that's all that matters to us.

You have now witnessed the first sacrifice, and you know that true honor need not be named.\n \nYou are now one of us. You are Ash'abah. We will recognize you as our sister and together, we will uphold the sacred duty of our tribe.
Do not be afraid. The Wood Elves have only themselves to blame.\n\nWe shall never cower in the shadows again.
Oh! You startled me!
The passage to the tower is to the northwest. Go on. And good luck in there!
<<1>> cooks the filthy skooma in his lair. Let's put an end to him.
Who are you?
You'll have to go on alone. Find the Engine. Destroy it.\n\nSurveying these ruins will have to wait.
I want to heal the Great Tree, but I'm just a farmer. If something is keeping that spirit from mending the roots, there's nothing I could do to help.
You are one of us now. Welcome to the tribe. \n\nTrue honor need not be named.
Good day to you, and welcome! I hope you didn't have too much trouble with the locals on your way in. Feel free to look over my sundries. Just let me know if you find something you fancy.
Welcome back to the Guildhall. There is much knowledge buried beneath the sands of Alik'r. Have you found any to share?
Please … there is not much time. \n\nFirst, you must decide … are you willing to join us, to become … an Ash'abah?
What foul magic is this? This … is this the Shadow Wood? \n\nIt is. This is what the Shade seeks—to transform Valenwood into … this. A realm of darkness and evil. It's inconceivable!
Welcome to the Sentinel Fighters Guildhall. You look like the capable sort. Interested in signing up?
Today truly is the worst of my life.\n\nDamned Netches.

Collect the gate key from the coffer to the north and destroy the three crystals to bring down the barrier. There's one crystal in each tower.\n\nMeet me near the Hall of Judgment's entrance when you're done. I'll continue scouting until then.
Help me, please! I got caught in this bubble of force, or whatever you call it. Get me out!
I found a note in one of the desks talking about this hatch back here. Guess what's down there?
Sorry, the lodge is off-limits to anyone not part of the Pact delegation. You'll have to move on.
I just need a mug.
Ah, mortal! You are a curious creature.
You've done it. The tomes are gone! I can't hear them anymore.

Who are you? You don't belong in here. Wait, maybe you can help me?\n\nI ran away from home with one of the bandits, but I've since learned that he was a jerk. He lost my ring in a game of dice and killed my father when he came looking for me.
Quickly. We don't have much time.
Nice to be out of that ogrim trash pit. \n\nI'm ready to take on Molag Bal himself now!
Such a pity! The Mourning Stone's secrets would've brought me to the Queen's attention. Once again, <<1>>'s plans stand in my path to glory.
Don't! Oh—I'm sorry, I wasn't expecting—I mean, I am really glad you're not a Daedra.
Good luck out there. This one will stay here for a moment. Relax, so that no one says we do not fit in.
You do not have horns. This is a bright moon indeed.
This one wishes you hadn't destroyed the books, but the shrine may yet reveal its secrets.\n\nFirst is first! Determine how to rekindle the flame.
Carry on, soldier.
If the inspectors see these rats, we're ruined!
Whoops! I'm sorry. I didn't see you there. I almost ran right into you. I guess I'm a little distracted. Anyhow, I hope you'll forgive me.
Beg your pardon! This is a private residence. Where are my guards?

Z'en's sweet mercy! We did it! The serpent's bound again! \n\nFirst off, I have to say I'm sorry to the gods for ever doubting them. Second, I promise I will never say that guard duty is beneath my abilities again. Never!
Please return quickly with the tools. If I can't trade them for medicine, this one's father will die.
Want to buy a carpet? How about three? They aren't good for much else.\n\nYes, <<1>>, even you!
This one hopes the people may be forgiving. Akkhuz-ri can't expect a warm welcome.
Thank you! This one thought we were done for after <<1>> sentenced us to death.\n\nHow do we get out of the Hall of Judgment? They're not going to let us simply walk out of here.
You've got to let us out!
You've got to help us!
This one will get Kargand the help he needs.
Did Marcella send you? Please! Get me out of here.
Please! You've got to help me get out of here! Those crocodiles look hungry.
Peace be upon you, wayfarer. I am relieved to see a survivor from the docks. The news we have received is grave indeed.
I shall return to the council. We have many plans to put in place—both to assist you in your cause and to prepare for our return to Valenwood.\n\nGood luck, outsider. And thank you.
If this place remains open, as has yet to be determined, the Clan Mother should hire you in a more legitimate capacity.
You are thrice lucky, but you will never best Ishalga!
All right, you've had enough time. Where's the skooma?
Thank you. S'rendarr himself would commend your actions.\n\nGive me the skooma so I can destroy it. I want to finish what I started.
The troops have secured the Chasm. Thanks!
We will stay here to protect the priestess from the bandits, in case you drive any of them out.
I'm terribly worried about my comrades. Especially my brother Veranus. Mother would never forgive me if I returned to Bravil without him.
Mara bless you, child. Did one of my temple guards send you this way?

Ah, it is my most pleasant and clever friend. Zur is happy to see you again!\n\nThis Hollow City, it is nice, yes? Gadris would have liked this place. I learned much from our time together. Zur keeps better notes, now. Very neat. Less doodles.

It is nice to see you again, friend. I find the accommodations in this city to be most pleasing.\n\nI can't help but imagine that Zur would have taken great delight in this place. I think of him often.
We must be ever vigilant. Daedra can be as devious as dark clouds on a sunny day.
You've got to destroy all four of the focus crystals in order for us to open the portal.
Sorry I missed the fight with Molag Grunda. I got distracted by a veritable flood of Dremora. I was up to my ankles in Winged Twilights and was having a grand old time!
Go on in, don't keep the Captain waiting.
Go, walker. Repair and learn.
Bright moons. Jone and Jode shine down on us, even now.
We're almost done. Just destroy those totems.
Thank you, Hallowed. You've filled your role admirably, as hundreds of Moon Hallowed have done before you. You have the thanks of all who praise the Bright Moons.

Only the dead and the desperate end up in this part of the desert. You appear to be neither, so you must be a very brave soul. \n\nDo you intend to enter the cursed grounds, the Tears of the Dishonored?
So, we meet in person at long last. You looked taller in your projection.
I erect the spine of caution. Adalmor is not the most patient of Nords. Perhaps there are no patient Nords.
Go on—repair one of those siege weapons.
Just stick with the training, soldier.
The time has come to perform the ritual and destroy the Harvest Heart. My children yearn to be free!
I'm sorry. I don't have you signed up for a fight at the moment.
I'm sorry. I don't have you signed up for a fight at the moment.
I'm sorry. I don't have you signed up for a fight at the moment.
I'm sorry. I don't have you signed up for a fight at the moment.
I'm sorry. I don't have you signed up for a fight at the moment.
I'm sorry. I don't have you signed up for a fight at the moment.
I'm sorry. I don't have you signed up for a fight at the moment.
I'm sorry. I don't have you signed up for a fight at the moment.
What … what are you? Are you real?
Hm?
You heard Father, yes? We must pray at the lunar shrines to learn more of his … my past. Let's do it.
Mother said we should pray at the shrines, see more of her past. Come, Hallowed. Let's do it.
We have accomplished great things this day, my faithful friend!
I'm so glad you could come! My parents will be back tonight, and I was afraid I'd have to face them alone again.
This is my test. If I can take the life of this girl, it means that I'm willing to make the necessary sacrifices.
Gifted with a rare and powerful ability, Aranias tried in vain to win her parents' affection.
Peace be upon you, comrade. Good to see you at my little meeting.
By the Divines, it's good to see you here.
You look formidable, comrade. Perhaps one day you'd care to spar with Ra'zaym, yes?
Ahh, so nice to be holding this meeting in Skyrim. Perhaps later we can go for a run out to one of the dragonshrine ruins! Always a good fight, draugr.
You must be the one Merric and Aelif have been talking about. Finally we get some movement around here.
What news do you have?
Our customs and our traditions … these are the things that sustain us in this foul land.
I toil and sweat, but this foul land provides few bounties.
I often deal with the unknown in my role as a go-between and agreement broker.

I am most grateful for your help. Casnar's brother, Enneh, will be at his market stall. The wedding offended him so greatly, he had refused to attend.\n\nWhether he knows what happened to Casnar or not, let us hope we can soon put the matter to rest.
Congratulations. The path is over. The moons shine their light upon you once again.
None have entered the vault save you and the vicereeve. I have confirmed it.
You again? You seem to make a habit of showing up just when things are getting properly twisted.
This one will never complain about a job again.
We were lucky to make it back here alive. Those Dawnmead are … they're monsters. Thank you for getting the relics back here.
Somebody here must know why <<1>> has gone bad. Ask around. Discreetly.
Be mindful of your step. This forest has been most unkind to guests.
I really appreciate you helping me out with this wolf situation.
I can't believe they're dead. Glad … glad you could bring the relics back, traveler. Make their sacrifice worth something.
The pillars seal the gateway. Unlock them with the keys.
Use the keys on the pillars and we'll be on our way to Moonhenge. Well, this Moonhenge. Confusing, isn't it?
Those bastards killed Patraud, for little more than stepping into the clearing. I'll be sure to return the favor to these Bosmer savages.
When inspecting all the claws of this plan, this one is not so sure it will work.
We'll find out what we need to know.
I'd be lying if I said I liked Patraud much. The Apprentice never knew when to shut his mouth, but he didn't deserve to die like that.
That Bosmer we … captured mentioned a matriarch named Selene.
By the Egg, those Bosmer were vicious. I won't forget Patraud's sacrifice.\n\nLet's hope there's research worth doing in this forest.
Told you I'd make it back, didn't I? Not going to let something like a little gutwound stop me. No way.
Honor and praise, my friend. Do you have the Staff of Magnus?
I'm sorry. Only Forebears are allowed in today. We do welcome guests on some occasions, so I hope you will return at another time.
I know you are a guest in our city, wayfarer, so I will forgive your ignorance, but the fellowship hall is open to Crowns only.
Accompany Evoker Ahainar-jo. He will attempt to contact the Bosmer again. Perhaps they will tell us how to contact the spirit of this forest.
Greetings, Crown. \n\nBy Stendarr's grace we have summoned the strength to forgive you for your trespasses. I hope you will afford us the same courtesy.
Don't you have your own dead to tend to in the Crown quarter? \n\nLeave us to our grief and we shall do the same for you.
You have our condolences, Forebear. We have asked Tu'whacca to take up your dead. No Redguard should face such defilement.
Thank you. You have no idea what it means for me to see Lorwen alive. And our project fulfilled. You've saved us.
May Ruptga's blessings fall upon the wayfarer who uncovered the truth about our inglorious Magistrate. Crown justice prevails once again.
Greetings, sera. Distrust runs deep here in the Alik'r, but you are most welcome in our Guildhall.
I thank you. If you are braving the cellars further, I would ask again for your help. On behalf of all my people.
What foulness is afoot now? The dead have risen? I thought Alasan was purposefully not raising them!\n\nWere we too late? Has Alasan transformed himself into a lich?
I really miss my lute, F'lah.
Hunal has been giving us a running commentary of how it's going in there. Truly, your vision showed me falling to Urcelmo's blade? Raz thinks Jone and Jode do not know him very well.
I can't work under these conditions! I'm not built for war!
Remember, the beacon at the lighthouse will be our signal to move in. Light it once you've completed your task. We will descend upon the Maormer at that moment and crush them.
Leave me alone. Let me die here.
Thanks to you, my soul is back where it belongs.
Freedom is a wonderful thing. And I'm sure that dear Lady Laurent has missed me terribly. She really is lost when I'm not around to help her.
You work quickly and efficiently, young one. I appreciate that. \n\nDid you recover all the ship designs?
I prayed Tu'whacca would guide you.\n\nDid you find Zariya? I heard fighting amongst the dead … is she all right?
Don't tell anyone, but I've started sleeping under the desk. The streets are too dangerous at night.
I've a great deal of work to do, so please excuse me. \n\nI need keep busy. Keeps my mind off things.
Greetings, wayfarer. I'd ask you to report any rumors you might hear concerning disappearances to Justice Istah.
These disappearances have the Justice on blade's edge. Seek him out if you have any information to impart.
Hers is a sad story.

Ruptga's blessings upon you and your house, wayfarer. \n\nI apologize for the poor state of our streets. The recent unpleasantness in the wastes has brought an influx of Forebears from the west—and you know how they are.
Fahara'jad's appointee is as useless as a sundial in a sand storm. \n\nIf this is the best our Forebear king can send, he should abdicate.
You must be the person who rescued all these people. We were part of Vanus Galerion's group before … well, before everything fell apart.\n\nWe appreciate everything you've done for us.
Got me new bones yet?
My mother banished me to this Crown-infested hamlet with its absurd bumpkin nobility to "cool my blood." \n\nIt leads me to wonder if she already knew people were being kidnapped here.
I've not seen my son for some time. At first I thought he'd debauched himself into another stupor, but now … now I bear a father's worry.
You missed all the fun.
You have to get out of here before my babies find you. They'll tear you apart! This has never happened to me before. So many people are dead!
This hall is full of secrets. If you will hear advice, then hearken—leave Bergama now before you are caught in the jackal's snare.
If rumor is to be believed, a great many of the disappearances occurred near the gambling hall. I've been giving it a wide berth.
Hmm. You looking for a skull thumping? Keep walking, stranger.
You have returned. Did you ignore the instructions of the Champions as well? Raz hears that is something you do.
Let these petty man-thieves come for me. By Tava's red feathers, we will see this nonsense ended with a flick of my blade.

I knew we could count on you. You have never disappointed me. But there is so much left to do if we are going to win this war.\n\nStill, with you leading the charge, we have an excellent chance to end the Planemeld and save our world.

My friend! It's good to see you again. I'm thrilled I could persuade Urcelmo to trek out here. We need to support Akkhuz-ri and the Champions. This is a vulnerable moment for our fragile new Dominion.
Hey … hey. You wanna walk me home? I heard there are nasty folk out there, y'know? Dangerous! \n\nWhy's your face so fuzzy?
Hallowed. I hope you and these Champions won't take long. I worry about Her Majesty's security this far from Auridon.
I know that scent. Green keep you, my friend. The Silvenar and I are well pleased that we could be here to support the Khajiiti people.
My friend! Isn't this amazing? It's my first time on the borderlands of Valenwood. And my first time in a Khajiiti temple! I'm honored to be here today.

It's a shame about all these people going missing, but I tell you, it's great for business. Samhudah's paying me to stand here and make sure no one shady gets in. That's it. \n\nEasiest money I've ever made.
I hope to save enough gold to make the journey to Sentinel, but it's hard to come by in this stingy Crown village. They cling to their wealth like a goat kid to its nanny's teat.
I have something for you to do.
Ah, well met! Very well met, indeed! Allow me to welcome you to The Winking Jackal! If you should need anything, feel free to call out. \n\nOr, you know, throw something. That seems customary here.
The decision is yours alone, though you know what I believe is the best course to take.
Business has slowed to a tortoise's crawl since the disappearances started. \n\nMany of the missing were patrons of ours … friends, even. If you ask my opinion, this smells like Crown mischief.

Fair winds. Have you come to escape the sour looks as well?\n\nAs soon as people began to disappear, the guards went looking for the foreigners. I've taken refuge here to avoid harrassment. It's not all bad though—I'm a fair hand at dice.
Deliver the mixture quickly. If the vampirism progresses too far, curing it becomes a far more difficult endeavor.
We'll both be happier with that altar smashed. You'll see!

All stories go on, even when your part is complete. There was a reckoning for Aranias and for the Wilderking himself, as you well know.\n\nNow, go where your story takes you. I will try not to interrupt it again.
Now remove the heart and there may be a chance we can grow a new one.
My friend! They hit me over the head and dragged me in here. Is Alanya safe?

If Andur kills me before I pass the mantle to Aranias, there will be no caretaker of the Valenwood. \n\nThe forest would become a voracious monster. It would turn against the Bosmer and ultimately bring about its own destruction. You must stop him.
The bundle of roots will pull you into the ground and let you pass under the fire.
If you don't mind, I still have recruits to drill.
Please, go let Pircalmo know what's happened. I'll untie Alanya. We've made such a mistake.
You don't look like one of Gudarz's bruisers. What do you need?
Ranneth untied me? That means Pircalmo is safe, right? He did nothing wrong?
Take out <<1>> and his lackeys will take to the hills. Spineless bastards.
Pardon me, I have to go on sentry duty.\n\n…Which is a relief, with all these new low-lifes in camp.
A woman named Aranias endangers the whole of the Court of the Wilderking, you must stop her.
I have guarded this square long and long, wayfarer. Even so, I do not know what the Forebears might do about these disappearances. Best that a Crown abide here and keep watch.
Welcome to the Manor of Revelry. Let me know if you see anything you like.
Help me clear a path so we can get <<1>> out of here safely.
Look at you! Nothing but skin and bones! We really need to fatten you up before you wither away to nothing.
The manor is everything you hoped for, isn't it? But look at you! You could really use a bath.
<<1>> is kind of clumsy. He tripped and stumbled six times on the way down here. It's a wonder we weren't spotted.
I don't think I like you. And I don't think my friends will like you, either. \n\nBetter think about moving on.
I'm a Nord—which means I'm moody, and prone to violence. Don't provoke me.

You must decide which companion to take on the initial assault. You need to travel light and move quickly, for speed is essential.\n\nEach of these soldiers has worked with you before. You know what each of them can do and who will serve you best.
Once you select the companion that will aid you in the initial offensive, let me know.\n\nAs soon as you're ready, we'll begin our assault.
The Fighters Guild came to Coldharbour for this express purpose—to stop the Planemeld and save our world. \n\nNo matter how many of us fall this day, we shall not fail!
Go on, close that portal. The honor's all yours.\n\nI'll make sure nothing sneaks up on us in the meantime.

Win or lose, it's been an honor to fight alongside you.\n\nThat said, let's do our best to win this thing, all right? I'm not sincere very often, and I'd hate to have wasted it just before I die in battle.
The Champions are in good hands with you, Hallowed. Good luck on your path.
The expression upon your face tells me that the time has come. The final assault is about to begin, isn't it?
The final adventure begins, yes? May the many Moons bless this foolhardy endeavor!

I enjoy a challenge as well as the next mage, but this might be a little much, even for me.\n\nStill, I'll do whatever I can to make sure our world isn't completely destroyed. While I grew up on the Shivering Isles, I now call Nirn my home.
Please, you have to hold on. We … we can't lose any more of our companions. There's been too many deaths already.

When I left the forest, I thought I was going to be alone in a new world. But everyone here … it feels like I'm with family again.\n\nYou're all stuck with me now. I'm not leaving until we finish this.
No longer will we hide in the darkness. No longer will we fear those who would hunt us.\n\nToday, we become the hunters.

So now we just need to find the other two wards. My apprentice Shiri is traveling with Prince Azah, trying to find answers, but they need my research.\n\nLet me work. I will ensure you are notified when we know more.
Hurry! If you take too long, these bandits will kill me.
You! There you are! The scholar Zohreh said I might find you here. \n\nYou must make great haste. Prince Azah is in need of your assistance.
Looking for something? A set of keys, perhaps?
You did it! The portal is ours now!\n\n<<1>> and <<2>> have already led troops through to the other side.
Here in Willowgrove, we pride ourselves on two things—our honey-mead and not being stung by bees.
You look like you're at loose ends. Interested in making some money?
I can't believe you beat me. You! A cheat and a swindler, in league with that false matchmaker!
Sorry, I'm a bit busy right now. Have you had a chance to try our honeymead?
If you're not going to deliver those to Zan, I'll give them to someone else.
My soldiers stir from their feral state. I can only assume the corruption has receded, and Naemon is again put to rest.
We will find Sai Sahan. Your vagabond emperor and I will find a path to the Halls of Torment.
Come. I need to speak with Queen Ayrenn. I expect she'll want to speak with you as well.
My men are itching to soak the sand with Imperial blood. We're just waiting on you.
I hear Zara will be picking fighters for the next division round soon. Maybe I should go flirt with her.

My scouts reported sounds of battle along the beaches. This forces my hand. If I can't explain this immediately, my superiors will hear about this and assume the worst.\n\nI need you to tell me what's going on in <<c:1>>.
Be on your guard wayfarer. There are more dangerous things in Bergama than discontented Redguards.
The Withered Hand rallies more dead to its banner with each passing day, and still these fools feud. Crowns and Forebears taste the same to vultures.

Tava's red feathers! Do I dare to believe my eyes? I have been watching that door for so many days … I had ceased to hope.\n\nTell me—did the king send his army? These Imperials could launch a full invasion if they are not stopped.

Whoever you are, I rejoice that you have come to my rescue. The Imperials have kept me locked in here.\n\nI deemed it likely that they would seize control of all Alik'r, and there would be nowhere to flee to.
This Khajiit's magic has no equal. Save your dignity and quit now. This one will be Sorcerer Division Champion.
You've seen for yourself. <<1>>'s influence is gone from this tribe.
Welcome. What brings you to <<c:1>>?
I've seen better.\n\nGo on then, ask what you will.
Do not tell Meridia, but Mezha-dro should have joined Fighters Guild. At least then fighting all these Dremora would pay something.
My axe and pack are outside. Take them with my gratitude. I must do this alone.
The harpies are congregated around this building. Looks like the mercenaries took something every bit as valuable as the harpies' eggs.
By Jone and Jode, I wasn't sure we'd make it out of that one, but you never cease to impress. Things are always exciting when you're around, it seems.
Let's go. My axe won't find a Sea Viper spine on its own.
Lead the way. We'll learn what the Sea Vipers plan soon enough.
We did it. I can't believe I'm here. My master, Rurelion, would be proud of me, I'm sure of it. \n\nCome on, it's time to kill Molag Grunda. We can do this!
Tu'whacca has taken the Chief. So passes Marimah—water into sand. May the Divines bless his passage.

It wasn't easy, but we did it. We stopped the blight from spreading, defeated Naemon's servant, and we still have the heart we can use to grow a replacement for the Eldest.\n\nAll things considered, this went as well as I could have hoped.
If I only could get to my feet, draw my weapons …. \n\nBy Onsi's bright blade, I would die in combat—not like this.
Tu'whacca, I cannot heed your summons—not yet. Just a few days more and I will cleave that Withered Hand in two.
This poison strikes like a scorpion … just below the ribs.
Slain by a cup of water … Onsi, forgive me.
Many here are beyond our help. All we can do is ease their passing. Water into sand, wayfarer … water into sand.
Zeht's tears. Our dead, our sacred water—we've nothing left to revere that hasn't been polluted by these Withered Hand dogs.
Our tribe is beset by sickness. Is this the end of the Ash'abah?
I feel like I can see forever here. Not seeing what I want to though.
I beg your pardon, O wayfarer, but I must hold to my work. Many and many of my tribe-folk require attention.
The Chasm is ours. We'll protect the portal while you push on ahead.
Killing Dremora is thirsty work. I need a mead!
I think … I think I just narrowly missed Tu'whacca's summons, brother. I credit my mother. She had a stomach like an iron kettle.
Tava curse these twisted legs! I almost reached him in time. \n\nI wasn't fast enough.
If my brother is taken from me, by Onsi's bright blade, I will visit a blood-storm upon the Withered Hand such as the world has never seen.
That's it! Welcome to the Undaunted. Now go make ol' Mordra proud.
And so, the little mortal, once more into the breach!\n\nI believe the Ayleid King wants you to find a hidden key. Hurry! I think your friends have already made it into the sealed hall.
Well, so far the vampires have remained true to their word. They allowed us to pass through the Orchard without any resistence.\n\nI wonder how long our good fortune will last?

With your help, we will launch a two-pronged attack into the citadel. It starts with the abandoned Fighters Guild hall within the city.\n\nWhile the fighters use the secret tunnel to reach the hall, you need to find the key to deactivate the wards.
What are you doing, sneaking up on a woman in my condition?

Hey, I know you. Indaenir mentioned you. You've come along at just the right time—or I guess it's the wrong time. The forest that way is blighted. Indaenir's looking into it. I'm not supposed to let anyone through, but I can make an exception.
Ah, my friend! So good to see you again! Now that my head has cleared, the writing has been going very well. How went the relic hunting?
I'm hoping to compete in the Summoner Division. I finally learned to conjure wolves. Only took me three months of training—and three lost fingers.
Don't worry about my safety. I'll be perfectly fine.
I would like to speak with you, but I must finish reading this first.

Everything is so … very different. It's like I'm no longer a single physical form, but my being is spread out across the forest.\n\nAranias is slipping away. You are my friend though, whoever I become. Will you stay for just a moment?
Wonderful! Thought I'd be yapping here for eternity. Blasted Wormies only have eyes for the empty ones.\n\nVery well, tie me to your belt and we can get started. No time to lose!

You'll find Ugorz in the Orc stronghold to the east, and Zirani in the Khajiit village in the west. Both were once-flourishing townships—but no longer. They'll need help to escape.\n\nI'll meet you all at the Overseer's overlook.
Please, go away! If the Taskmaster knows we've talked, he'll be furious.

I can't tell if you're crazy or daft, but you have my thanks.\n\nIf you can stop the Daedra at the other fronts, we should be able to hold here. I won't blame you if you fail or flee—we're prepared to defend our homes either way.
This one knows you mean well even as you keep pestering her. You must, to risk your life to come here.\n\nBut she has already told you. This one refuses to leave. Taskmaster is watching.
I'll wait right here, and hope no one notices their things are missing. You do this, and you can just take the damned thing.
You-you are here? Thank the gods! We need you!\n\nThe third Ansei Ward is here. That girl Shiri—the scholar's apprentice—she is a necromancer and she has come to the necropolis. We have to stop her!
Do not linger here.\n\nThe living who wander in my realm tend to become … lost.
Welcome, stranger. I'm on the hunt, but you're not my quarry.

With Vanus and the Mages Guild to aid you, you've gained a strong advantage in this fight.\n\nDo not underestimate the power of Vanus Galerion. He's accomplished many great things during his lifetime.
Have you spoken to Malesse?
You didn't hear anything, got it? Certainly not that I'd like to be his night blossom. Or anyone's! Especially not his! You didn't hear that!
My apologies, but I can't chat. Tholbor's given me an arm's length of tasks to do, including his filthy laundry. Horrible man, honestly.
My apologies. I'm all out of sorts. Malarel has a thousand tasks for me, and her idea of motivation is a lightning bolt to the forehead. I understand I'm the third assistant she's had in a month!
I'm the stage manager for the Swordmaster Division. If you hurry, you can make the next round of qualifiers. Credentials, please?
A moment.
Excuse me.
Raz wishes he could help. Naemon would not last long.
A moment. I want to watch this.
Pardon. This seems an important moment.
In a moment. Shazah would like to see this.
In a moment.
Sorry. I'd like to see this.
Not only did I witness the choosing of the Silvenar, I also got to see the Heart of Valenwood. It's really been quite an extraordinary day.
Don't interrupt.
This looks important.
We've been away from the central barrier long enough. Gilraen and the others will need my healing. Let's hope they're not dead.
By the Green Pact those Daedra were powerful! \n\nI fear what Gilraen and the others are facing at the central barrier. Perhaps we should return to help.
Honor and faith are due all, but you who have come from afar … your contribution is matched in measure only by the length of your journey.\n\nThank you.
We have to keep the Sea Vipers out of <<1>>. We must hurry.
If not for your little challenge gambit I'd have killed you by now. Get on with the fight before I change my mind.
My sword-arm hangs loose in the socket like a sagging palm frond. If you have come here to train, I suggest you find a lighter sword.
I thought we were safe here. Hidden from the enemy. The God of Schemes grows more powerful by the day!
I'll just stay here for a while longer. I should whisper a prayer to Y'ffre for my fallen brothers. \n\nThank you once again.
You're a strong one, aren't you? Khuzi likes the strong ones.

You retrieved Ansei Maja's Ward? Tava smiles upon us! You should hold onto it this time, just in case.\n\nYou need to get the other ward, as well. The one Throne Keeper Farvad was carrying. Go on! I'll find you later.
What have I done? What have I done? I have struck down one of our ancestors!\n\nI have betrayed my vows, my people, my god. Tu'whacca! How could you allow me to do this?
You can talk to them. The fine people inside, where the skies can't be seen. Go on, they're near.\n\nThey're all near. Above. Below. Who'll protect us from them?
We'll hold them off! Close the rifts! Go!
I've never seen anyone fight like that.\n\nI mean, you should go.
Anyone could defeat you, with enough training.
Luck is not victory. Watch your back.
Winning one battle doesn't make you a true warrior.
I'm relieved to be out of the Tower of Lies, but I'd be lying if I said I didn't want to be out of this damned place altogether.
We're far from the familiar sights of Stonefalls. But these perils we face—they're epic! They will sing songs of our glory long after we're gone.
You're looking for a High Elf woman? Yes, I saw one pass this way. Right into that strange cave. The one with the village that just appeared out of nowhere!

I stepped out for a moment, dispatched a dozen Dremora, then popped back in. Just wanted to make sure I had the opportunity to see you off.\n\nWell, off with you, then! So long! Toodle-oo! Don't forget to write! Ta-ta! Cheerio!
Have you found <<1>>? They can't have taken her far from here!
The trail of the Senche begins at the bones of my fellow Hound. I barely escaped with my life, and his life escaped with his bones bared.
Did you find her? Please tell me you did … or at least, that you didn't lose the flute. It's the only memory of her I have.
I've always loved this part of the Chasm. So majestic. Takes your breath away, doesn't it? On occasion, quite permanently.
You really do need to go now. The tribe will return from raiding the Wood Orcs to check on me, and I don't want any bloodshed.
Nielas is back! Thank you! What of the others?
I'm safe. I'm safe. They can't hurt me here.
Go to the circle. I will draw Gorzesh out of his lair and lead him to you.

Good, I can't imagine the source of what's going on over there. Plus Girin went to scout the area. Don't let him flirt with you too much. He's more interested in his own … interests sometimes then the problem at hand.
Thank the gods the ship's stopped moving. I don't know if I can bear going to sea again.
Now that the Fighters Guild and Mages Guild have finally set up shop, maybe this place can return to some semblance of normal.
Fighters and mages can be a little rowdy, but I'd rather have the customers than the quiet any day!
I'm not sure who drinks more—the mages or the fighters!
Where did all these fighters and mages come from? They're eating me out of house and home!
No matter how far from home we might be, the Mages Guild always provides for its members.
I hate this so-called existence.
Welcome back to the Guildhall.\n\nThe sands of the Alik'r hide all manner of wonders. Have you found any to share with us?
I saw you eyeing my fire. It isn't very warm, but it's all we've got. Go find your own fire, stranger.
I wish we could take longer breaks, but the work never ends.
Escape? That's easy. \n\nWaiting for the right time to make your move? That's where the difficulty comes in.
Don't run off like that again, Alexis. You know that I worry so!
The Pact may still be active in the area. We will continue our patrol, for we must be ever vigilant.
You return. And with the gold, yes?
Go on then. I have nothing more to say about it. Run back to your kittens!
I can't believe he just blew my cover. Please tell me you have good news?
We'll settle down here in Longhaven until we've fully rested up. Then maybe we'll hit those Argonians back and make them sorry they ever crossed us.
A contest? Grand! Go quickly, before the guards I tipped off arrive. It'd be a shame if they mistake you for the Artisan.
Good luck with that Darius fellow at the Mages Guild. And, of course, let me know if I can get you something.
I'm sorry to bother, but have you seen a mer named Rollin? He was supposed to meet me here. But he's late. Very, very late.
Let's see what Manthir has to say. Oh, I'm so excited!
These should fetch some good coin here in Woodhearth. Thanks again.
Like I said, I'll send troops to the necropolis as soon as I can spare them. \n\nUntil then, may the gods be with you and Prince Azah both.
A pity you could not do more for us, but I'm sure you have your reasons.
All right, a deal is a deal. You won't see me again.
Welcome to our sleepy little town of Willowgrove, traveler. We make the finest golden honey-mead—rare and delicate on the tongue. Well, we do when things aren't all aflutter.
This one is so proud of Yenadar. To give himself so that others might live. Thank you for being honest with me. I know he would have wanted me to know the truth.
Red Mountain Ash, how Thalara longs for it. Seek the tuffs around Lake Rumare. Gather ash for Thalara, and rewards will be yours!\n\nBeware of other seekers. They will steal what you've gathered.
My guards … all dead ….
Curse that Molag Bal!
This is all they send to kill me? Truly?
Get out of my face, milk-drinker.\n\nI don't need a blood-spitting child like you in my way, I've got winners to bet on.

Greetings, sera. I am a long way from home, but Boethiah has guided my hand to this place. And I know—in time—I will find myself standing atop a pile of the dead, glory backing my hand.\n\nWhen I win my chance to fight, that is.
Gutter trash. Wait your turn, like the rest of us.\n\nI haven't put this much thought and sweat into this filthy arena to have a cretin like you butt in front of me.
Ah, another sorcerer, I think.\n\nWill it be you or I who sees the champion's seat first, I wonder? How could one know of such a thing?

Oh, hello. I'm not entirely sure how I found my way here, but I think I can earn some coin to find my way back to Wayrest.\n\nIt's been quite a trip, I can tell you that! Good luck, if you're fighting!
Unless you're betting, step aside. This one has no time for peasants and idle thinkers.\n\nBe ready with your coin if you step in front of this one, yes?
Yes? What's the problem?
Here—try your luck with the lizards.
After a hard day's drinking everyone gets hungry, right? Pass me a few coins, and I'll fill your belly.
I've heard Hadran is dead.\n\nThugs like him get what they get, I suppose. Makes no difference to me.
You are truly kind to have taken such time to seek me out and return my great-grandmother's recorder.
I take what time I can to study. I never knew warriors had so much to read.
The slime Hadran's been slain, I hear.\n\nGood thing. Perhaps I'll finally be able to leave this muckhole.
Seems like people are starting to leave. I guess I'd better start packing my casks away, but I'll hold off to whet thirsts until more people have left.\n\nSpeaking of - want anything?
Come closer, Khajiit, and listen well.\n\nBare your claws to this arena and shed much blood. Come and come to win. Do it for Khajiiti. Do it for Jone and Jode.
Have a little chat with your beggar friend, then you and I need to talk.
I see noises … have you seen them? They glow pink and sharpen swords in the moonlight with a caterpillar with fangs.
Are you a pilgrim? The throne is not safe for you today.
You are always welcome here, warrior.
<<1>> knew you would solve Khenarthi's Roost's problems! This one thinks we will see much more of each other in the future. Safe travels, my friend. Say hello to Watch Captain Astanya for me.

I am glad Pelidil's threat is ended, but the Staff of Magnus is still missing. For now, I have another task for you.\n\nUndead rise in the north. Bodring and his Vinedusk hold the line. Meet him at Marbruk's north gate and aid him however you can.
I don't know how you found us, but we need your help. The forest has turned against our village, and we've been forced to take refuge in this cave.
You don't understand what you're doing!
It's not surprising that the Khajiit had no respect for our sacred Pact. What else do you expect of an outsider? No offense.

Come to me when you have collected the testimony, physical evidence, and magical omen needed to prove the guilt of the accused. \n\nWe are eager to put this matter behind us and make peace with the forest.

This is the Thalmor Headquarters, our base for operations in the region.\n\nThe locals have voiced some issues with our presence, but they recognize the necessity in the face of the Dominion's current troubles. At least, they had best do so.

I take it you ran into Lady Meridia? Lovely woman. Charming. We get on famously! \n\nWhile you lot were having yourselves an epic row, I gave her a shout. Asked if she'd be willing to help us out if things went badly.
I can't believe Calastil would stoop so low as to steal my heraldic cane just to score a few favors with the queen in my absence!
Can you believe Laurosse stole my husband's dog Pluck? He may have inferior blood, but that's no excuse for such cruelty!
Earrastel's a pretentious oaf, but stealing my wedding gift just to satisfy his vanity? Unforgivable!
The second stage is the most important. What use is magical inquiry if it cannot foster relationships?
I'm … I'm the Mane! Hallowed, we survived!
She's going to love this!

Red Mountain Ash is what I need. And you're just the sort who can bring it to me. Harvest it from the tuff around Lake Rumare.\n\nIf you see anyone else harvesting ash, steal theirs before they steal yours!

Good journey to you, warrior. I thank the Divines for sending you to me. Hasten to Lake Rumare and gather Red Mountain Ash. Return as soon as you can.\n\nBeware others who also seek the ash. Slay them to ease your task.
Keep those marauders off my ship!
No passing through <<c:1>>, citizen. If you want to gawk at Argonians, you'll have to do it elsewhere.
Halt, citizen. By order of the Thalmor Inner Council, all contact with the Argonians in <<c:1>> is restricted until further notice.
Was your hunt successful?
Track the troll carefully. The thing is quick and powerful, and it won't hesitate to snap you in two.
Another pilgrim? The Bone Barrow's full of them these days. If I could get anything done, I might be glad for company!
<<1>> wants to thank you for rescuing <<2>> and the rest of the crew. Best go see her before you leave!
Please present your findings to the Treethane, advocate.
Not only did I lose Erinel, my neighbors openly despise me for daring to court a Bosmer. Why, Quertasse paid someone to steal my censer!
Please take whatever you've found to Treethane Rolon, advocate. Everyone wants to be done with this terrible business as soon as possible.
Look for signs of where the wasp landed. A keen sense of observation is the hunter's best weapon.
It's been a few days. The vision alters time. You never really get used to it.
So, you've returned. Tell me, what did you see? Did you speak to Brackenleaf?
There are hundreds of places in Wayrest for a noble to loaf about, but he chooses the sewers.\n\nI bet all that privilege fosters eccentricity, after a time.
We need to find Master Pellingare—no telling what could happen to him down here.\n\nNot the brightest noble.
I can't argue with anything he's said.\n\nI won't stop him.
Good luck with your trial. I like you. I rather hope you survive.
<A deep rumbling reverberates from within the tree, like the sound of snoring.>
A heated battle. I haven't felt its like in ages. With luck, the invaders will crawl away from this place and leave us to our slumber.
I'd keep moving if I was in your boots. This isn't a friendly place. Not at all.\n\nYou'll want to follow the bridge. Best of luck and all that. Cheers!

That was … different. After we took down that titan and the Valkynaz, all those Dremora appeared.\n\nI think your Dremora friend is establishing her dominance. She threw Cadwell and I out, which was kind of rude, but what can you do?
There has to be a bottom. These rocks need to be anchored to something, don't they?\n\nBest stand back, though. I don't think either of us wants to find out what's down there that badly.
This is incredible! I feel the life of <<A:1>> flow within me! Have you seen my wife? Where's <<2>>? Why hasn't she come to congratulate me?
I'm sorry this puts you in an awkward spot. Truly, Y'ffre and the Wilderking brought you to us in our hour of need.
Quick, close that door! That's a dreadful draft!\n\nIn the meantime, I'll make sure none of the Dark Lord's minions creeps up on you.
I was afraid something like this was going to happen. Poor Nadafa! She loved to go walking in the dead of night. She said it helped her sleep ….
It appears we have come full circle, Vestige.
Lord Varen is waiting for you.
My lord Varen has more to say to you.
You'd better speak to Varen. I think we've given them all something to think about.

I simply cannot believe this is happening. Our father, you …. \n\nPerhaps it is better that you are going. My courage might fail me in the face of such a task. Whatever tradition may say, there is no dishonor in what you are doing, Sameer.

This is too much! Do I look like some kind of powerful sorceress to you? \n\nNo. I'm just an apprentice. I can't take on an army of Baron Montclair's thugs! I mean, I want to advance within the Mages Guild, but they ask the impossible!

Honor to you, Sera. Welcome to the Guildhall. I realize that our presence here in the temple is unconventional, but I'm afraid that our former hall was razed just recently. One does what one must, yes?\n\nWhat can I do for you?
Watch the little adepts play at sorcery. This one thinks they will make good members of the Mages Guild one day.
There is no time to waste. The Elder Scroll of Ghartok must be returned to us!
You are too late, Sameer. Your father is dead.\n\nEven worse, some Elven necromancer …. He turned your father into an abomination!
My father's blade. It's strange to see it again after so many years. I will use it to strike down our enemies, in his name.
It's not as it seems! I love Almur with all of my being. Why would I do anything to hurt the ones he loves?
I don't know who you are, but if you seek the one responsible for the johads, you do so backwards.\n\nCome. Jahi should hear this as well. I'm tired of secrets.
Welcome to the hall! What can I do for you?
Just when I think I've read all the books we have here, someone brings in another ancient tome.\n\nIt seems I'll be reading and categorizing for the rest of my days.
I felt every blow as if you were hitting me, but the creature's death has put an end to the pain. Praise the Eight that our tormented flesh has been put to rest!
This one heard your words with Nabira. She spoke the truth. Zaddo can tell you where next you should go. Where the paths of moonlight lead you.
Ahh, yes. The Bright Moons spoke of you to Saifa last night. She sees their light in your eyes, even now.
Get yourself gone. The situation in Arenthia can only get worse.
Good day to be alive, isn't it? Everything's just as I remember it! Always gratifying, that is.
You've been gone awhile.
You've been gone awhile.
You've been gone awhile.
All honor and glory to the brave Covenant warriors who returned the Elder Scroll of Ni-Mohk to us!
If <<Az:1>> can control <<Ac:2>>, perhaps the shades will settle down. Then we can get back to excavating <<Ac:3>>.
Keep an eye on Tharn. Remember, he's a politician. That means he knows nothing, but thinks he knows everything. \n\nJust bring Sai back in one piece, all right?
The Mages Guild has no record of shades haunting this location. Where did they come from, and what do they want?
You're going to take the she-troll? She has all the subtlety of a stampeding mammoth in a pottery shop! Good luck. You're certainly going to need it.
Time has not mended their mistrust. No good can come from taking both Abnur and Lyris with you. You must choose one, and only one.
You did it. You did it! I'm free, I'm finally free!\n\nThank you, thank you!
It's truly terrible what has come upon the village, but I promise I'm not the one responsible. It's my duty as Spinner to teach the children about the Green Pact. I would never violate it.
I wasn't sure if an outsider would be found guilty of violating the Green Pact, but I guess it was Aranak who cut the flower.

My friend, I am sorry you had to be the one to end Lleraya's troubled existence. It was unfortunate, but necessary.\n\nAnd now if we are to save Rivenspire, we must engage in another unfortunate act. The time to deal with Baron Montclair is upon us.
Despite my myriad talents, I must maintain a supply train in this backwoods marsh.\n\nWe have excess stores. Feel free to peruse them, if you like.
Sorry, not doing any business today.
I won't beg, but I implore you to restore my son. I have waited so long for this moment.
The Khajiit are a marvelous people. I am blessed by this opportunity to enjoy their company.

Do you think Molag Bal actually reads this stuff? Er, sorry. Trying to help my brother find something useful here. But look at all these books!\n\nI always wondered what a Daedric Prince read at bedtime. Some of this stuff is pretty disturbing!
How could a spinner violate the Green Pact? Madness.\n\nOh. If you're hungry, the meat was untouched. So we can trade, if you want.

Things will be strange until we have a new spinner. I don't like how that feels, especially after such a potent violation of the Pact.\n\nBut it's good to be able to go back to business. If you want to trade, ask.
And so it ends. I pray that it has, at any rate.
You're not going to get all weepy with me, are you? I mean, I've got that stoic reputation to maintain ….
Honor and faith to you always, my friend. My part in this is over.
Yes, this will be close enough, I think. Are you prepared?
Eranas, really? I can hardly believe it. He was a good man. Well, he had his reasons, I guess. We all have our reasons.
You will not be sorry, my friend. I assure you that my days of aiding man-eating serpents are over!

Eranas was just a scapegoat, to distract us from their real intentions. Did you see what pattern his sigil made when it was destroyed? Ancient Ayleidoon for "thorn," which is what the spinner was. A thorn in their side, so they plucked him out.
Amazing. The person in the village most in tune with the Green Pact somehow violated it.\n\nLike that never happens.
My priestess, returned to me at last. Long did she suffer in the clutches of Molag Bal, yet you have brought her to me.
A pretty stone, yes? But it will remain dull as an old torture puppet until you've filled it with Daedric souls.
While you were gone, we had a few visitors. Nothing Adusa couldn't handle, of course. But we shouldn't linger in this place much longer.
Even with Shaman Bogham curing me, I feel like goat dung.
I should not have had all that garbage dung water … I should have listened to Gluth.
