Malacath's teat, my guts are still on fire. This was spider venom? Was it as big as a house?
That was even worse than the time I ate rotten kagouti stomach.\n\nWhich was as bad as it sounds.
Razum-dar sent me here to await your arrival. He wants you to join him as quickly as possible.\n\nIt seems Vicereeve Pelidil came this way after stealing the Staff of Magnus.
I owe you my life. My Lord calls you Vestige? A strange name. Is it true your soul was taken from you?
Now where did that greedy little captain run off to? I'm ready to hit the waves!
You actually found other townsfolk? And you brought them back here? Remarkable!
Not a bad location to make a stand, it's far from perfect though.
You've done well, my friend. The Mortuum Vivicus is destroyed.
This is no place for idle travelers. Turn back.
My head … make the pain stop! Please, do whatever you must to make it stop!
I knew I should have done a few more deep knee bends before we rushed into battle.\n\nGo on, go on. Don't let me slow you down. You still have a world to save, you know.
Great gifts often appear as a surprise, but sometimes, the surprise should be spoiled.
Who are you? Can't you see I'm having a drink with my friend here …? \n\nMight as well embrace the crows; they're here to stay. If anyone goes, it'll be us, not them.
Divines be praised, you came back. Can we get going, please?
I didn't think anything short of my death would sate Gargak's bloodlust. We may still end up at each other's throats one day, but for the time being we can enjoy a little peace. We owe you much.
You obviously aren't a frightened refugee. Welcome to Camp Tamrith, a little slice of home in a hostile wilderness. It isn't much, but it's better than nothing.
I hate this, but there's no other way. By the Light, my sister must die with honor before the evil completely overwhelms her.\n\nOh, Arkay, grant me the strength to do what must be done.
<<1>> is currently off-limits. You'll need to keep back, for your own safety.
Last I saw <<1>>, she was taking shelter in one of the tents.\n\nI could do without this damnable rain. It's been storming since we arrived, and it shows no sign of letting up.
I can't bear the sight of him.
Wait. Did you hear that? It's the sound of you not killing each other! It is the most boring of sounds. Beyond mudcrabs mating underwater. More of a "clump … clack … clump … clump."
What a terrible shame, losing <<1>>. Even if she was kind of mean to me. At least Reezal-Jul won't be stirring up any more trouble.\n\nNow all we have to do is take care of Lleraya and Montclair.
It is done. The Amulet of Kings is ours once again.

The time has come for us to enter the catacombs of Sancre Tor. Do not underestimate the dangers that await us. \n\nIn ages past, Sancre Tor was a place of light, but I fear that is no longer the case. We must be prepared for anything.
I know we don't stand a chance against Molag Bal unless we recover the Amulet of Kings, but I'm still uneasy about this. That damned thing has been nothing but trouble from the beginning.
I'm not one to hope any creature suffers, but with <<1>> I'll make an exception. She can spend eternity in <<Az:2>>, for all I care.
Sebazi hopes to hear you've killed your quota of Gray Vipers.
Rumors swirl that the Gray Vipers have suffered losses of late. May we thank you for this?
Back again, eh? Now, which contract did I give you?
We must find Sai Sahan. Everything depends on that.
My estates, my titles, my own life—it's all forfeit now. All in the name of preserving the Empire.\n\nI swear by all the gods, Mannimarco will pay dearly for this.
I thought you had left me! Please don't do that again!
Lyris is safe, and whole once more. You have done well, but there is still much to do.
My brother's wife can't take much more of this. And truth be told, neither can I.
This place stinks of dust and death. Let's finish this and get out of here.
Do you really think this is a good time to stop and chat? The Redguard needs your help.
Sorion is very much aware of the depths of his talent. That can rub some people the wrong way. I do hope he hasn't landed in trouble he can neither sing nor play his way out of.
Beware, these roads aren't safe.
Careful there, traveler! These roads aren't safe. Bandits about.
What's wrong? You look like you've seen a wraith. \n\nTharn's been gone for hours. I think he's up to something.
An unexpected visit! What brings you back, Vestige?
Welcome to the chasm my friend. We're nearly there.
So, <<1>> is dead, eh? Well, that's a bit of good news, I suppose.

Hmmph! I can't believe the king's being so over-cautious. I asked to borrow one of the Ansei Wards for a few days to study it, and he flatly refused! \n\nI'm still glad you got them back, of course … we make a pretty good team, I think.
Please excuse me. The stablemaster already rebuked me for neglecting my duties once. I would not wish him to do so again.
Etienne … I'm sorry I failed you.
Where is Etienne? He should be back by now. Where could he be?
I'm nearly out of supplies, treating all these wounded guards. \n\nIf you have something to ask, be quick about it.
Stay back - I don't want to be coughing blood on you.\n\nThis whole mess … It could've been avoided, somehow. We weren't ready. We couldn't have been.
Let me know if you see movement, friend. I've gathered the other archers' arrows … it's just a matter of putting them in the witchmen.
Let them come! We're as ready for them now as we ever will be.\n\nI have all of Malacath's strength behind my axes - none of these toothless savages will topple me, now or ever!
I've killed a fair few of them today, but they just keep coming.\n\nFine by me. My arms aren't tired yet.
That's my home. Over there, the one on fire.
How could this have happened? This is our home! Evermore is just across the lake, and this is all we get?
Imagine, all these crates lying around and no guards in site. It's a real shame.
Don't worry. I'll make sure no dead men make off with this unattended cargo.
Shoo! Away with you! Stay out of my garden!
I hope you've not come looking for the queen. She's left all matters of state to Duke Renchant. I heard Her Majesty's tending to the indigent masses at the chapel.

She brought the book here. I followed, but it's a witches' coven—dozens of them—trying to use the book for some evil ritual. \n\nI'm just a novice. I should return to the guildhall in Hallin's Stand. If I'm not here when you return, meet me there.
Brave meeting. Mind your tongue in this place. Too many ears and not enough brains.
Forgive me for stating the obvious, but you're alive!\n\nWe heard some terrible noises in the caves below. What happened?
Amazing powers, you say? Well, I can't wait to test your theory and see what happens!

The ritual is prepared. Wyress Rashan assured me that you'd have the heart.\n\nAssuming you do, tell Rashan, and we can get on with it. We don't want the forest to suffer a moment longer than it has to.
Well … I expect you won't be returning any time soon to enjoy my sisters' hospitality, and I can guarantee we won't run into each other on some city street ….\n\nSo I guess this is goodbye then.
Good luck in locating <<1>>. I'm sorry I couldn't be of more help.
Such a shame about King Eamond and his son. Both of them were so dashing. Renchant is a very poor substitute.

I tell you, things grow darker here by the damn hour! \n\nReachmen are right down there! Came in by boat, took the lighthouse, and now they're crawling up in the woods to assess our defenses. And our orders are to just sit here and watch!
Must be nice to be able to travel between this realm and the physical realm. I'm stuck here. Yes. I'm stuck here.
Welcome back to the guildhall, my friend. \n\nThe history of Bangkorai is rich in lurid and bloody events. Have you brought us any regional books or journals?

Aha! I thought we were in for a bit of easy coin with this job until the queen said you were coming along. Now I know to expect danger.\n\nBring it on though. If the plan goes awry, that just means we get extra hazard pay.

Surprised to see me? Sounds like I already missed some interesting experiences. A Hagraven controlling crows? I want to see that!\n\nThis business has potential too. Of course, our part only comes into play if there's trouble. Let's hope there isn't.
The sky is beautiful! A little different to what I remember.\n\nBut the Walking City. I must find it, so I may finally return home.
We don't take kindly to strangers.
I would rather not speak to someone I don't know.
Glad to see new faces in the village. It gets lonesome seeing the same people, day in and day out.\n\nIf Kerbol doesn't mind, maybe you can stay a bit longer.
Head right up those steps to leave the village.
Well fought! Sai Sahan travels with worthy companions.
Go now, before the Goblins find you.
Do you mind? I'm trying to have a quiet moment to myself here.
Reynelle was a kindly one—she entered these Vaults with us, and I'd like her to leave with us, if the Mad Architect hasn't scattered her soul across Oblivion.
Now! The heart!
So, we're to stumble blindly into the catacombs beneath a crumbling ruin abandoned for an age? Lovely. That bearded idiot swordmaster will lead us straight into a trap, no doubt.
The wyrd expect an alliance now after they murder my daughter in cold blood? They're lucky I don't have them all killed here and now!
I can't wait until this war is over. After this, I'm due for a vacation.
I'm in your debt for finding me. Elgenie says I'm going to be fine. I think Abir was more relieved than I was.
I'm not sure what you're hoping for with the girl, but I can tell you, she won't leave this ruin.
The captain will soon realize the right decision was made.
So those abominations the Dark Witnesses are herding about were once people like you and me. You should speak to Delphique. She may have something to say on this.
Perfect! One of Elgenie's, I bet. This will do nicely.
Happy to hear that <<1>> has been destroyed, but it's a terrible sad thing, what happened to Crestshade and Camp Tamrith.
Already the woods are defiled by habitation such as this. We can never recover.

Think of the glory! It'll be just like Ranser's War! We'll rescue Rivenspire and the women will swoon. It'll be great! You'll see. \n\nGo on to Shornhelm's chapel and tell Countess Tamrith I recruited you to the cause. I'll be along as soon as I can.

Well, that went better than expected! Not one breach of our perimeter! Guess those Baandari are good at something more than just swindling … ah, I shouldn't have said that. \n\nThe Knights of Saint Pelin are indebted to those cats. To you, too.
You have shown me more kindess than I deserve. I shall spend my remaining days attempting to atone and truly honor my son's memory.

Hmm. Well, there is a thing about the poultices. We do not have them just yet. \n\nThe good news is that I had foreseen the need for them, so I sent our herbalists out to gather what they needed. But … they haven't returned yet.
Tell the most honorable guard how you heroically drew your weapon before chasing after that mangy cur!
Ah, you must be <<1>>'s agent.
We dislodged House Montclair from its nest. The upper city is ours and Shornhelm is free.

I can't believe that Baron Montclair would order the brazen kidnapping of Shornhelm nobles. Even if it was his general, this Reezal-Jul, who carried it out, Montclair is at the root of it. I am shocked.
<<1>> has accepted you, then? Good. We need all the help we can muster.
If they don't stop yelling at each other, I may just have to grab a switch and tan some hides. That'll give them something to cry about!
Deepswimmer doesn't fear alligators, but he fears trolls!\n\nThanks for saving this one's hide!
<<1>> sent you? She thinks, perhaps, you can do work for us? Who are you to know so little, yet offer so much?

Remarkable! What a strange sensation of new recollections and old. I believe that Reezal-Jul somehow removed those moments from my memory. But you were able to restore them.\n\nAnd now you understand what we are facing.

I know we're having problems, but I'm certain that Constable Agazu can handle it. Why the mayor allowed the militia to mobilize is beyond me.\n\nIt's like we're under martial law. And they closed the inn! What happens when I want a drink? What?

Are you as hungry as I am? I'm completely famished. The thrill of battle does that, you know. And flirting with death makes food taste so much better too.\n\nWe'll have to have a feast later. Yes, when the garrison's cleaned up.
Ah, sweet-bringer! Thank you for your kindness! You have saved me from many sleepless nights!
You look like someone who appreciates the finer things in life. I'm afraid that's in short supply right now.
Friend, you. Grateful.
Hey thanks again for all that stuff! It'll really help, you know?
Won't forget your service. Means a lot.
So much pain, it's … it's too much.
If only we had the full force of the Mages Guild behind us. These Reachmen wouldn't last long.
Walker … we may never be able to repay you for what you have done, but thank you.\n\nMay you dance with Jone and Jode until the end of days!

Have you heard the story of the shipwrecked Argonian? He swam from Summerset to Bal Foyen in under an hour. When the messenger arrived with word of the shipwreck, he was warm in bed with a flagon of mead.
Thank you again for finding my lost Puddles. I'd be so lonely without her.
Can't believe it's come to this. I should be leading my clan out of the Strid right now.

These animated bones—why do they seek to keep us from the relic? Are they the lingering remains of the Ayleids who once dwelled here, do you think?\n\nWell, they won't stop me. No matter what their reasons are, my cause is greater.
My dear friend, Verandis. I'm glad you're here. You've always been so good to our family.\n\nI … I never really thanked you for that.
Who invited you into our camp?
I'm going to do one last perimeter sweep and hold the north gate. Don't worry, if anything gets past us, I'll be there to help you.
What brings you into our midst?

Needless to say, this behavior is more than a little disquieting. Short temper is not one of Arkay's blessings.\n\nI will reserve judgment for the time being, but if he is corrupted … well, let's see what unfolds.
Oh, hello again. I'm still waiting on a few more signatures before I can head back to Valenwood. But maybe they'd take some books instead. What've you got?
My fool of a husband can sell apples. I see an opportunity that'll make me rich!
Are you all right? Crazy Eye saw you fall! She was worried you might not get back up!
<<1>> said you're headed off to kill more bandits. Keep good count, all right? I bet him it would be less than a dozen.
Dark anchors here, now? The Daedric Prince Molag Bal is surely making his presence known in Bangkorai.
I'll always treasure Dame Marcelle's sword. Perhaps it will encourage me to take up a life of honor and adventure.

Of course, the Fangs! It all makes sense now. Blessed Almalexia had a vision that the Prince of Schemes had sunk his teeth into the ground at Gil-Var-Delle.\n\nThe fangs she saw in her vision must be the devices Meva described.
Greetings, guild-brother. How may I help you?
Fight now, talk later.
<This bottle seems out of place, balanced on a dagger. Something seems to be inside.>
Good luck out there. The Blacksap are a violent bunch.
You did well, my friend. Adusa would fight at your side any time.
You should get back to <<1>> as soon as possible. He'll want to hear what we found.
I do not seek to offend you, but … you look like trouble—the kind of trouble we do not need in Fell's Run right now.\n\nI would suggest you simply leave town. There is nothing for you here.
You can always look, dearie, but don't touch. I'm a barmaid, not a trollop.
What do you say? You interested in having a bit of a laugh?
I suppose a public trial is for the best. If anyone learns we're holding <<1>> and his sons, it might rally support for another rebellion.\n\nAt least with a trial, there's an end to this conflict.
Can I ask your help? My husband and our dog are missing. I can see the red eyes of the undead from here. I'm worried … we're both capable with a blade, but he's no match for the undead.
<<<1>> makes a sad sound as he looks to the north.>
Find my knights and bring back Arkay's relics. They are our only hope now against the dead tide.

That's the first time I've seen Queen Arzhela in the castle in days! \n\nThe people love her so much. I hope she returns to the throne—it would be so good for the economy … assuming we don't get slaughtered by the Reachmen, of course.
Take as much time as you like, my friend. \n\nIt's only the High King and the entire kingdom of Rivenspire waiting.
Burying corpses once they begin to stink is one thing, but when they've been in a damp cave for days? It's like eating hot stew on a summer day. No one likes that.
I'm glad my sons are alive and safe. I just wish they would stop bickering.
I respect the High King's decision, but I can't hold my tongue—I have serious doubts about Queen Eselde's ability to rule.\n\nI hope she proves me wrong, or all of Rivenspire will pay the price.
I respect your decision, and that of the High King, of course. I will do all I can to support King Alard.\n\nI do worry about his militaristic tendencies, though.
And so the Infinium becomes mine again. As it always does.\n\nYou performed well against Graccus.
I almost feel sorry for young Dorell. Almost. But I learned long ago, if you're going to drink to excess, you have to face the consequences.
You've returned. What have you found?
I heard you and the Prophet talking about Abnur Tharn.
Nice work, "Hallowed." I hope your visions weren't too frightening.
Balance will be restored before too long, I think! With laurels, wine, and crushed velvet lining, yes?
Have you secured a meeting with <<1>>?
I'm not selling anything, friend. You'll have to go inside and talk to Sabir.\n\nMy part in this business is in acquiring the items we sell and managing relations with our partners.
<<<1>> makes a sad sound each time he looks toward the north.>

My husband, <<1>>, went for a walk yesterday morning. Said he wanted to get away from the squabbling at Elden Root. He hasn't come back!\n\nI went looking for him this morning with our dog, and now my dog has wandered off!
What a pleasant surprise, to see an acquaintance from Glenumbra. Good to see you still have your health.\n\nIt's such a shame, isn't it, that our looks are always the first to go.
Hallowed. Strange to refer to you by that title after everything else you've done for the Dominion. But then, I suppose this was ordained in the moonlight, yes?
This one is humbled to stand before the Moon Hallowed. You have done so much for Akkhuz-ri's people … more than he has done in some time, he thinks.
Who are you? You don't look like a skeever.
I signed on with the Shornhelm Guard because Baron Dorell is a man of action. He's someone who gets things done.
Well, now that we're a big happy family, you should have <<1>> go over the plan so you know what to expect. It's going to be brutal. I can't wait.
I'll do my part, just get into position and do yours.
If it wasn't for you, <<1>> would have been a meal for a spider.

I take <<1>> at her word, and I'm sure there's a good reason for the delay. But it looks bad when she can't construct a simple building for the people she's sworn to lead.\n\nI do hope <<2>> can clear things up.

<<1>>'s betrayal could not have been more absolute. She knew the details of the ratification ceremony, which puts <<2>> at risk.\n\nIt's my sister's own fault. She thought to appease <<c:3>> and the Mane by agreeing to this foolish process.
Don't think to start any trouble. None of us are in a forgiving mood.
Firaelion's a little shaken, but he'll be okay. I won't let him out of my sight again for a long time, you can be sure of that.
Your victory will be remembered. We could feel the death of Brinarch through the earth beneath our feet. Even the insects will not mourn him.
You did it. And Wyress Nyronie's sacrifice pays off. Now we only need to contact our other sisters and drive out the remaining Reachmen.
I'll do what needs to be done.
I look forward to your final show of prowess.
Did you use all of them? I do hope you paid close attention to their effects.
I brought <<1>> into custody. Of course, we can't question her without special permission from the Thalmor Inner Council.\n\nPolitics.
Apologies, I'm a little overtaxed in here. Not much time to talk, I'm sure you understand.
The Prowler is ready to sail when you are.

I should warn you. Ravenwatch Castle is as strange as the man who owns it. His family is very old, and they have … strange traditions.\n\nDon't worry, though. I have no doubt about the fact that he is on our side. You may rely on anything he says.
There's no use for anger. I can't say I'm happy to be here, but at least we're alive.\n\nAt least I know my father is still alive.
As soon as Marien is rested, we're going to head for Shornhelm. Try to put this all behind us.
I heard you talking to Lothson. Don't worry, I'll be fine. The big galoot has it in his head I'm some fragile thing. But … it would be nice to have the necklace back.
I don't know you, and I don't care to know you.
You actually got the bow? Incredible. Did <<1>> give you much trouble?
This is it. The monster's lair. But no sign of Zungarg. This is … discomfiting. Keep your guard up.
Mayla and I are going to stay here a little longer. You don't have to worry about us. We'll be all right.
None of this feels real, but your help has made it easier for my brother and I. Jowan's trying so hard to be strong for me. I guess I need to do the same for him.

Today is a fortuitous day indeed for Rivenspire, though I fear other kingdoms within the Covenant may not be so lucky.\n\nI know that my husband considers you to be his champion, but I wonder if you might be willing to assist his queen as well.
Tread carefully, Vestige. Mannimarco's agents are everywhere. The King of Worms will not be pleased that you stole his prize captive from the Halls of Torment.
Get away from me. You're lower than the Vinedusk.
I have a bad feeling this isn't going to turn out well—for me.
I've half a mind to go after Nedras. What in Tamriel possessed him to leave me like this?
Once I publish my research, you will be able to read all about my findings. I'll be sure to acknowledge your contribution!
Damn him. Damn that stupid old mule. To think I'll never see him again, to give him a swift kick in the rear.
This one is so proud of Yenadar. To give himself so that others might live. Thank you for being honest with me, traveler. I know he would have wanted me to know the truth.

Ah, it is good to see you, my generous friend. I came here to pray to Mara for forgiveness for my past, and it was like the clouds parted and the sun shined on my soul.\n\nI have decided to stay and devote my life to Mara. It is a better life.

We'll finish patching up these farmers and then send them south, toward Fell's Run, at the first opportunity.\n\nMeanwhile, go find Darien. And if he's lollygagging with some lonely farm girl instead of working, punch him in the head for me.
I think I heard a troll up near the <<1>>, so I picked up my gear and returned to the city. I don't know about you, but I wasn't eager to tangle with a troll!
During their raid the Imperial Legionaries left our pavilion alone. I guess they're not all idiots.
This region has an incredibly rich history. I'm sure there are vast repositories of lore hidden in these hills and valleys … if you know where to look, of course.
Cursed Imperials. Shooting arrows at us from behind rocks and trees… cowards all, I say.
Take the taciturn <<1>> with you, will you? I don't want to feel her slicing me to ribbons with anything but her eyes. Not until everyone's free.
Thank you for retrieving our goods, friend. At least the wounded won't go hungry now.
Do you feel the power? Can you taste it?
Thanks for your assistance with the Imperials. Now we have to deal with bandits of a different kind. These Baandari plan to gouge us, I have no doubt.
Bested by twig-boned Imperials on our own ground …. \n\nShameful.
Well, that was demoralizing, wasn't it? \n\n"Your death matters little, Emeric." I can't believe she said that! I don't know though. Is it true?

We'll remain here to secure the area. Once Dominion reinforcements arrive, we'll figure out how the Covenant was able to conjure that portal to begin with. \n\nAnd if they try again, we'll have a host of armored soldiers waiting on the other side.
I hope <<1>> is ready for <<c:2>> … assuming it's ready for her, of course!
She's a braver woman than I!
The mine may be lost, but with these notes I can at least continue my research. Thank you.
Face the consequences. The rest of Adeena's family is in Sentinel.
Do you feel that? It feels like another presence just entered the ruins.
It's strange to think that Najan and I will never speak again, but he deserves it. He deserves worse.
Participating in this ceremony means you accept the blessing of Mother Lamae. Will you proceed?
We lie about like whipped dogs. Ufa drags his feet, waiting for aid. Can he not see that none comes?
Hallin's Stand is a fine city. Lots of good stone work and deep bones. It should always be free.

The real mystery is what's a woman like that wanting to do in a place like this? \n\nShe has a prisoner, but the Chamber of Passage is not a place for holding someone, it's a place for sending someone on!

I would take back what I did if I could. I just … I didn't know things would turn out this way.\n\nI thought that, for Dutheil, it would simply be a matter of finding new work. I didn't intend to destroy his life. His mind.
You have all the tools you need to save <<1>> with you. That greedy and cowardly man has few defenses.
I just want to see my mother and father again!
We slipped the farmers out and sent them south with a few soldiers. Now I'm ready to break a few Montclair heads!
Mind the furs. It takes hours to comb out the snarls.
Lovely day for a drink, wouldn't you say?
We follow the Green Pact in this home. Respect this, and we'll do the same for you.
My father thinks he's the alchemist in the family, but mother always said I'd surpass his skills.
The new treethane is a joke!
You should go. I'm not playing this lute for you.
I know you, brother. You're one of us, even if you don't know it yet. Hircine calls you. His song is in your blood.
What happened to you? It looked like you were in a daze for a few moments.
Leave me. There's nothing you can do.
I may have little time left before the Imperials find me. Let me pray in peace.
Your kin live among the mortals. They may be wearing rags or crowns. They may hide within or rise above the masses.\n\nFind them. They await.
The Baron was just filling us in on what was written in his son's journal. Spell or no, Ellic has a lot to answer for.\n\nIf he's even still alive.

Thank you. Take this vial and fill it with the waters from this basin. The water must be taken by the one who carries it. With that done, make for the falls that feed into Gil-Var-Delle and pour the water at each crest. Nature will do the rest.
Oh, I know you! You must be the one her beautiful ladyship has been expecting!
Would you look at that line? We're drawing more people than in <<1>>!
You look pale, my child.
I was wondering when you were going to show up.\n\nWant a bite?
Did you pick up the crate? I'm certain that <<1>> in <<2>> will assist you if you ask nicely. \n\nWell, I'm not certain of it … but it's worth a try.
Welcome to <<1>>. I'm rather busy today, but I'm sure another merchant can assist you.
Do you have them? You have them, don't you?\n\nOh, I shouldn't get my hopes up. They fell in the sea, didn't they? I knew it, I have the worst luck.
Look at them, limbs so sluggish and carapaces dreadfully dull. When you've raised the shalks since they were pupae, it gnaws at your heart to see them so listless.
You didn't drop a single one, I'm impressed! Come to think of it, I have been needing an apprentice ….
Oh, Edouard, you foolish man. Now look what you've done.
Have you found anything I could use? I've told our guests I'm still preparing, but they're eager to hear my stories.
This High Elf thinks that his people rule over me. The Wood Elves follow King Camoran, not some High Elf Queen! Am I right?
This Wood Elf doesn't realize he would be dead without Queen Ayrenn and the Altmer.\n\nSuch disrespect. We risk life and limb to save them and they thank us with accusations and insults!
Now, where did I leave that scroll?\n\nYou'll have to excuse me. Just doing a bit of housekeeping.
I overheard what <<1>> intends to do in order to pad out his research journal, and if I wasn't still sickened from this poisonous spider bite I surely would be now.
The wine's just over there, in the alcove.
All the Children of Yokuda are dead or gone. We did it!
I'm glad that you've learned to come to me when you are seeking knowledge!\n\nIn this case however, you will have to look elsewhere first. Say … away from me.
They're so cute together.

Oh—a visitor. Greetings. We don't get many walk-ins these days. "Curfew and regulations" from what I hear. \n\nCouldn't have been easy getting past all those Imperials. Maybe you should think about membership in the Fighters Guild.
Wouldn't trust Ludippe with my coin purse, but his eyes are good enough. Let's have a look inside, shall we?

Is that? Yes! I can tell by the runes. The slight alterations in the design and structure is unique to the Valenwood Ayleids. I would be greatly interested in reassembling and studying this tablet if you are willing to part with it.
If that gold is getting too heavy, I'd be happy to carry some of it for you.
Is he breathing? Tell me he lives.
Dammit! That's Kaleen. See to her. I'll keep watch.
Welcome to the guildhall, friend. Found any interesting books or scrolls? Please just place them on the desk. \n\nWe had a grimoire come in yesterday with troll fat all over it … so … safety first.
Ah, that's better!

Tell this High Elf she's being ridiculous. Yes, moon-sugar is used to make skooma, but Khajiit use it as a spice! It's a facet of Khajiiti cultural cuisine!\n\nMoon-sugar shouldn't be regulated because some people use it for the wrong reasons!

Set this Khajiit straight! Moon-sugar has important cultural significance to the Khajiiti, but some people … use moon-sugar to make the drug skooma.\n\nMaking moon-sugar illegal hinders skooma vendors—and that's a good thing.
Thank you. Take this ice rune. Captain Gemelle gave it to me to freeze the webs trapping the others. It should make them brittle enough for our soldiers to break free.
<Scouting mission notices and reports are posted to this board.>
I thought for a minute he would start making sense now … but I was wrong.
This one can't believe we have to go all the way back to <<1>>. The last time we were in Arenthia, <<2>> hitched a ride on a cargo ship and ended up in Senchal!
This one must escape!\n\nYou have seen them, yes? The vampire skeevers?
Why?
No, I'm all right.\n\nYou saved <<1>>'s life by killing her brother. You should probably speak with her on the matter.

Pardon me, walker, do you have a moment to help out my lunatic boss?

This Khajiit thinks he can walk into this forest and kill and maim at his leisure.\n\nHe may not follow the Green Pact, but I do, and I'll have him learn respect for the flowers and the trees before this day is done!
You, there! Do you scout for the Imperial invaders? Is that why you pass this way?
Take this ice rune. It should make the webs brittle enough for my soldiers to break free. Good luck.
Hm. For some reason, looking at you makes me want to vomit. My emotions just feel like they're going to burst out and run away again.\n\nOverall though, I am feeling a little lighter on my feet.
Really, I hate constant interruptions. If it weren't for my friend <<1>>, I'd never have come to visit.
These people will never forget what you've done for them. And neither will I.
Speak with <<1>> here, or move along. I have no time for you.
What a damn joke. I knew I shouldn't have moved away from the sea.
I used to find comfort in the desert winds, but now I only hear voices.
Nothing left but the clothes on our backs. I'll never forgive the Imperials for what they've done to us.
This is terrible! I've lost everything and that smuggler doesn't even care!
<<1>>'s wounds are too great … he cannot dry up like a puddle on the desert sands. \n\nHe deserves to meet death like the mighty warrior he is.
Hello there! I'm so glad you came by!\n\nI think I'm about to make a new friend, and you know what that means?

Do you see how grey it is here? Everything is grey. Just like my life. \n\nOne long chain of miserable, lonely days … each one worse than the day before it. Do you know why it is that I even bother to get out of bed?
If you find Sir Dubroc, tell him that unless he's making progress against the Reachmen, he needs to get his buttocks back down here.

I hope you're getting more insight into this than me. Every time I think I have it all sorted out, I realize something doesn't make sense.\n\nDo you think you know what each of the Raiders' names and professions were?
Never thought I'd see the day. And here Tholor and I were thinking of taking on apprentices of our own! Haha! Could you imagine?\n\nThanks, wayfarer. You're certainly a force to be reckoned with.
Soon I will be thirsty again. Then I will come find you.
I don't care who you are, if you can't carry my luggage you're useless to me!

May the Hand of Auri-El guide us to greater peace than exists in this moment.\n\nNo house or kinship should suffer undue strife from within, and that is exactly what the Dominion is encountering now. Troubling.
Getting the leaders to cooperate will be no small task. I hope you're up for it.
Isn't it exciting? The Mage Guild actually asked us to come with them on this mission! It seems our hard work is finally paying off.
We shouldn't speak, I could get in trouble. <<1>> can explain, I'm certain of it.
The soldiers don't want us speaking with outsiders. <<1>> can explain. She's by the northern barricade around <<Ac:2>>.
According to my calculations, the chances that the leaders of the three alliances can reach any kind of agreement is seven-hundred-and-fifty-six-thousand to one.
Guard duty on a tropical island? Sure, why not?
I hope this invasion goes smoothly. I've got more than enough scars for one lifetime!
Use the repair kit first, then go talk to Aurorelle.
I remember you! You're the reason my master back in Stonefalls almost ate me for dinner! Thank the Divines I was able to hide in that chicken coop.
I pray these talks go smoothly. We need to learn to work together.
Be respectful in the Queen's presence. I'll be keeping an eye on you.
Keep your steel sheathed in the presence of the High King, or you'll answer to me.
Ever get that feeling you've walked into a place you don't belong? No? Think about it ….\n\nI'm saying you don't belong here.

Fascinating, isn't it? To think that such a tiny rock could hold so much power. Can you feel it? It's like it's calling to me. Like the moons call to the tides.\n\nImagine what the relic it came from could do!
What're you looking at? The song's over.
Do I come and bother you while you're eating? No? Think about that while you turn around and walk away.
I brought enough food for an army but without the performers bringing in the crowds I'm worried it's all going to spoil.
Hey there, milksop. You stared an ancient, unfathomable evil in the eye, causing you to question your sanity, mortality, and very concept of the self yet?
I love every one of the stories Noryon tells, but I hear the Magic Act is beyond belief, so I'm going to keep checking back until they start.
My friend, this table is for the worthy, the bold.\n\nAnd this one thinks you don't look like either.
Pray pardon me, I wish to keep company with my friends here. Perhaps we could speak another time.
You must be ….\n\nYou must be … you must be … incredibly stupid to come talk to me.
Huh?
Move along. It's been a while since I stabbed anything, and I'm getting itchy.
Step away … step away, you … fool!\n\nOr I'll make sure no one will ever remember your name! Because all they'll see is a fool who's been … beaten into the ground.
Do you hear it? Sithis calls for you. Tempt me and I'll take you to him.
Go away. I've got nothing for you. This table's for the Undaunted. What counts as Undaunted in these parts, anyway.
Are you Undaunted? No. Get out of here … uh … daunted.
I don't care to converse with strangers.
I don't speak with outsiders.
The Empress of Bone does not wish to speak with you.
Scamper along now little one. Felvyn's a fool, but he's an Undaunted. Good for a story, at least.
I only need one good eye to send you to your grave mongrel. Best you be off. This table's for Undaunted only.
Looking for any work not related to carnivals. Let me know if you have any leads.
What sort of mischief have you been up to now? No, don't tell me. I'm keen to guess! \n\nUm … is it larger than a breadbasket?

I sell adventuring supplies, kit, and the like.\n\nI'm open for business, but I'm warning you—try to steal from me and I'll knock your teeth out. I've got a necklace I'm working on, and I can always use more teeth.

I, Boeuf Sterone, have no fear of thieves. For first and foremost, thieves do not steal food if it's poisoned!\n\nMy food is not poisoned, trust me. It's a trick to ward off the thieves, yes? Anything you buy from Boeuf Sterone is safe to eat.
Well, that's something, at least. Now we can get this ceremony business out of the way. This rabble will learn what a true ruler looks like.
Huh, who are you?
You should speak with Glaras if you wish to join the Briars. Otherwise, I have nothing to say to you.
I understand you attacked Fort Greenwall? Word travels fast in Riften, and I am eager to hear of your exploits.
Thank you once again for seeing my brother safely back to the village. He may cause my hair to fall out before I've seen a thirtieth winter, but I don't know what I'd do without him.
You've made Ivarstead safer for all, and for that you'll always find welcome here.
You're back. What happened? Did you stick something long and sharp through that crazy lizard's blackened heart?

How long does it take to count our pay? Go talk to their elder. We deserve some compen … compla … gold for all the trouble we've caused.\n\nBeen through! All the trouble we've been through! None of it in the contract, either.
Never much time to chat, it seems. <<1>> wants to know how well we've fulfilled our contract, and you're the only neutral person around.\n\nI hope you can give a good report of our work.
They speak in circles, like city-people do. What do they mean? And why do they smell so much like the harpies?
You can't leave us out to dry. We're good, mostly honest fellows. Trying to make a living. You're not so different than us when it comes down to it.
You know how hard we worked for them, right? Toughest job we've ever had.
I don't see Althen. If you have questions, that's fine, but at this point, I'm counting on you.\n\nYou don't want to disappoint the Ring of Daggers, do you?

Damn bastard Gavendien! Did it all for the jewels, and got away with it, too!\n\nHe got me good. I'll survive, but he cut Lauravieve's throat. He didn't have to! He just did it to prove a point. I thought I could be cruel, but he is a monster!
We did everything they told us to, but somehow we still failed. How will I ever make this right?
They were using my mill, the bastards! And look what they did to the poor jeweler!
I'm sorry, but the jewelry shop is closed for today.
No, no. I'm not going anywhere. I'm going to stay right here. Yes. Right here.

Praise the Eight! Did you kick that stupid thug's teeth in? I don't know what was worse—being held hostage or smelling that ruffian's breath!\n\nWhat about the robbery, though? Did you stop them or did they get away with the jewels?
I can't wait to see my father again. I hope he's all right.
Why? Why would they kill her? She was cooperating! She gave them the jewels!
I'm yours to do with as you will. Whatever you decide, I will go along. My fate is in your hands.
Don't feel bad. I knew Julien was a hopeless case. A man who's sick in love is a sad man indeed. \n\nI feel sorry for him, really. Enlisting would have probably helped set him straight.
Remarkable. It appears to be an intact volume of Ayleid lore. If it's real, then this is what we came here to ….\n\nNo. This can't be correct.
Nice of you to finally join us. Those damn Montclairs have locked me out of my own city!\n\nIf any of my people have been hurt, I'll kill Montclair and his daughter with my bare hands.
Qariar is the Blademaster of House Dorell. He's a good man. See what he has to say about all this.
You can reach the Pass by traveling west along the northern coast. And when we get there, I intend to make Montclair pay for the damage and sorrow he has brought to Rivenspire.

It seems that some of my loyal subjects have become dissatisfied with my leadership. Think that I have been blinded by the Light that shines so brightly around me.\n\nWell, to Oblivion with them! To Oblivion with him! I don't have time for this now.
If we don't get Gwendis out of there soon, those restraints will break and she'll feed on the nobles.
Without <<1>>, we will be hard pressed for help, but we'll get on, somehow.\n\nThank you again, my friend. For everything.
How wonderful it is, to have everyone safe at home! We owe you everything, my friend. I do hope you'll visit. We could go to the windmill and you can tell me all your stories!
Thanks again, friend. We never would have made it out of there without you.
Destroy the <<1>>. It's … it's the only way to make sure this never happens again.
I'll be more understanding with <<1>>. I promise. With Federic leaving … mind you, I still don't approve. But she is a good lass. She doesn't deserve what I did to her.
I knew it! You lost your spine, didn't you?\n\nThat's fine. I'll be here a bit longer if you get it back. Otherwise, goodbye to you and your stupid Shornhelm Guard.
You're right, again. They do.
I must tell you the rules before you ready yourself for the race.
There is no way I'm sticking around here to shovel horse dung for the rest of my life.\n\nI got big dreams, and I got the skills to make them happen.
I'm glad that my daughter's happy, but I'm not sure I can ever trust Dulkhi. Not after what happened.
Hmm. You know, that's the first time I've seen Countess Tamrith in her full armor. She looks so very … yummy.\n\nI mean regal! That's what I meant!
He's really gone, isn't he? The mighty Verandis.\n\nI hate this! I really hate it!
Well done! I'll follow in a moment. I find this room strangely calming and I want to look around.
What is your decision? We need your help.
Did I see the flutter of butterfly wings? It must have been a trick of the light.

Oh look. You're that nosy, fobbing arse who talked me into joining the Shornhelm Guard, aren't you?\n\nTalk about a nightmare. All that marching … I actually prefer to be here in the stocks, and it's clearly where I belong.

Hey there. You the one Queen Maraya bought passage for to Sentinel? All right.\n\nI'm just glad you didn't bring along a chest full of luggage. We got to row out to the Posset in this little dinghy here. Real glamorous, eh?

My friend from Hoarfrost! These two wouldn't be here if not for you. You should be proud.
Julien and Shuga have turned out to be great soldiers.

Martin couldn't cut it, though. Abandoned his post one night. I hear he's back in the stocks again.

I'm really enjoying the soldier's life. The thrill of battle, the rush of victory—these are real feelings.\n\nI'm thinking about staying in the Guard. Mad as it may be, now that I know Guendeline's waiting for me, I don't really like her any more.
Strange times, my friend, strange times indeed. And you know what strange times call for? A drink!

I'm not the seer my grandmother was. She didn't need to hear any gossip. Oh, no! She knew long before anyone else what trouble I'd be in. How I miss her!\n\nTell me what happened; the bones are unclear.
Doom has come to Craglorn! The stars have vanished from the sky! \n\nWill no one listen? Will no one help?

Thanks again for everything you've done. I'll take some time with the amulet to see if it could be of further use to us.\n\nIf you're looking for other ways to aid us, Hara might have some suggestions on where to go.
Glory has no patience for the idle. Go prove your worth against the Reachmen in Shor's Stone.
I'm just going to sit right here until all this nonsense between the nobles blows over.
Montclair is responsible for all this madness? Hard to believe. He was always kind to me.
The city is safe now, and do you know why? Because Baron Dorell took charge and showed Montclair's lackeys the business side of his boot!
The Light shines on Shornhelm and the Countess! Thanks to them, the city is safe again and Montclair is on the run.
They say the city is safe now, but how can they be sure? Baron Montclair's followers could be all around us, waiting for another opportunity to rise up and strike!
They say it wasn't really the Baron who attacked us. It was some kind of mad Argonian. I never did trust those overgrown lizards!
Welcome back to the Hall! How goes the search?
I suppose I'm lucky I made it out alive, but by the Three I'm glad you came along.\n\nIf I'd failed here, I think my captain would've had my head.
Good, good. I think I'll have a sit down out here. The wind seems very gooey, doesn't it? Very squishy. Ugh.
Don't worry about me. I'll be waiting here with these rented guar, my carts, and the stench of decomposing guards. No rush.
Soldier, report. What brings you to Ash Mountain? Did Holgunn send you?
Damn those Covenant bastards! It seems like they're fighting us at every turn.

When I was a kid back home in Riften, we'd kill any mudcrab we saw. Ensured they didn't get out of control.\n\nThat's how I feel about these Covenant soldiers. If we don't kill them all, they'll just keep coming.
I left the mines to breathe fresh air and swing my blade for the Pact. Then I get posted to this place. I think I'd rather go back to the mines. Hah!
Three guide your blade, soldier. Get out there and make us proud!

Thanks. Not many willing to help these days, especially a dusty Ashlander like me.\n\nWe'd planned to rest up at the Davenas' farm near Kragenmoor before passing through the Deshaan gate. He should know it.
I am so doomed.\n\nAnd it feels like there are a dozen horses dancing the Wood Elf frolic directly behind my left eye.
Is there something I can do for you? I really am rather busy at the moment.
That was considerably faster than I expected, thanks to your assistance.
Thank you for helping Priest Marnest. I feel better with you accompanying him. You never know if there are any more of those damn vampires hiding nearby.
Don't ask me why we're here. I have no idea. Someone seemed to think we needed to be here to keep Stormhaven safe.\n\nI haven't seen the rest of the kingdom, but this part's as dull as dirt.
Get out there and find the last of them. Northpoint won't rest easy as long as a single one of Lleraya's vampires remains within its walls.
I don't know how much more of this I can bear. \n\nWaiting for the general to call us back to the fight against the Ironhand Ogres—it's gnawing right through my nerves.
Bad time to visit the city, traveler. Might want to move along.
Hurry, hurry! I'll meet you outside!

Well, hello there! I certainly hope you've found something worthwhile to read in your travels. The selection here has been rather slim. I've resorted to reading cook books! \n\nOn the plus side, the dinners I've made taste much better.

My Lord Vivec, I bear the most grievous news. Belronen Telvanni challenged me to a duel of blood. I regret to say I won.\n\nIt was a small cut upon the arm, enough to settle the matter. But he fell dead!
You must go to Bramblebreach. There is nothing more to say.
You have my thanks, traveler. And the thanks of every guard in Skywatch.
Hey there. Saw the carts, eh? Sorry, nobody out here but the help. The Queen herself is still in Vulkhel Guard.
My brother—the plague boils his blood and ravages his body. I fear he doesn't have much time, but he wants to talk to you.
It's terrible. My book's gone. Years of my life wasted!

Oh, look at me! I'm a terrible mess! You really must excuse my dreadful appearance. I haven't been feeling very well lately.\n\nBy the way, you haven't seen Nostrum Breva, have you? She promised to bring me more of the Maulborn curative.
Do you hear that? It tastes like yellow ….
We're a family again thanks to you!

It is good to see a friendly face. Greenshade is a far more exciting place than Raz expected.\n\nHe hears now that the Staff of Magnus has been stolen? As if these rebellious Bosmer rebels were not trouble enough!
Don't come near me! Are you real?
You're not a daedra. What's going on?
You are a miracle worker. Without your help many people would still be in the clutches of the daedra.
You've done the fallen warriors proud. We completed our mission. That's got to stand for something.
Please. Stop the Maulborn and destroy their ability to make more of this damn plague.\n\nJust be careful. The chamber ahead is crawling with an army of plague husks.
You are a miracle worker. Without your help many people would be dead or dying.
How very strange? What in the name of Oblivion were the Maulborn thinking when they mixed these toxic ingredients together?\n\nOh, are you back again?
The Eight guide your hand, traveler. You may be the only one who can restore this holy site.
Though I have no sense of sentiment, I am able to understand that her intentions are natural and even have merit.\n\nNonetheless, there are larger matters at stake here. This is the way it must be.
Stendarr guide your hand. You may be the only one who can restore this holy site.
Welcome to the Guildhall, knowledge-seeker. What brings you here today?
Please, hurry! I know you can do this. I have faith in you!
I can't leave the tree! Erunor and I must stay here as its last defense! Go, help the villagers below!
You did it? Well done! I never doubted you for an instant.\n\nNow, let me have the mixture, if you please.
If I were a few years younger and my hands were still steady, I'd do this for you. But I'm not and they aren't, so you're just going to have to go over to the alchemy table and get this done.
I hope Nilyne can put those healing herbs to good use.
I love listening to the sounds out here. It's rather peaceful, don't you think?
Three keep you, traveler. Welcome to the Davon's Watch Guildhall. What brings you to our doorstep?

Do you know how much gold I've spent to get my wife here? And now the Maulborn have stopped providing their curative?\n\nI'd trade my entire estate if it meant the plague would release its hold on my wife.
Hello again, my slick-scaled friend. Have you been to the Armature yet? And did I ever tell you about Emberflint?
Mimic the water and flow and we will have no cause to inflict angry pain upon each other.\n\nThe Maulborn discarded these crates, so now they belong to us.
Those damn Maulborn stink flies! They refuse to give us the curative, just because they call us lizards and look down upon us.\n\nSo we'll take the curative. As soon as we can find any.
We were hoping to find something good in these crates, but the Maulborn don't seem to throw away anything valuable.\n\nTake whatever you want. Especially cheese. I hate cheese.
You're so lucky! Verandis never let's me go on dream-walks with him.
Traveler. How goes your survey of Zabamat? Have you found Hightide Hollow, as yet?
Don't mind my good-for-nothing egg-siblings. They're young, bored, and stupid.\n\nRest assured, I shall continue to remain open throughout this time of crisis.
Why'd we ever come to this island? It's so out of the way. At least <<1>> promised us extra pay for this.

Life is so precious, and so fleeting. Don't let it pass you by. Take time to feel the caress of the wind and listen to the way it carries the sound of your true love's name.\n\nMirilir … I never did hear anything so sweet and so dear.
I'm rather fond of Estre. High Kinlady Estre, that is. So noble, just, and Altmer through and through. She'll keep us strong.
Who knew that so many afflicted would flock to the Serk! All these people. They're so … sick.
Welcome to Shrouded Hollow! Will you be sojourning with us? Or are you simply a visitor?
These are dark times, and the Star-Gazers are a shadow of who we once were. But our role remains more important than ever.
Always work to do! Keeps one very busy, yes?
The Sword-Disciples are still in thrall to the Serpent. Anything you can do to put them to rest would ease my mind.
If you would receive knowledge, you must give knowledge in return. \n\nWhat have you brought me, Seeker?
I will seek out these monks once I make sure everything here is all right.\n\nI will see you soon.

What happened to you out there? You look horrible. Think of the legendary scars you'll get from those wounds!\n\nYou'd better head back out, or I'll beat you to the center of that Citadel. Soon as Roaring Ramavel and the others get here.
Hermaeus Mora's shrine is in the deepest part of the archive. I have an unusual relic from the Dragontail mountains to trade for the knowledge of the Celestials. I hope it's enough.
Greetings! I am Vanus Galerion, head of the Mages Guild. I have need of your assistance.
In time, the body you and Valaste have formed for me will fade. But with this charm, you'll never forget our trials together. The decision you made. I take comfort in that.\n\nAre you ready?
The court has heard tale of your deeds at the Sentinel Docks, wayfarer. Perhaps you have some advice to offer our great king in this time of need.

Here is a person who looks noble and respectable. Yes. Razum-dar thinks you would be perfect to act as Queen Ayrenn's envoy.\n\nIt is a very dignified task. You should be honored that this one even asks.

Get down and be quiet. We don't want to give our position away.\n\nWe're keeping an eye on these Red Rook bastards. They're not the simple bandits they pretend to be, that's for sure. If you want to help, go talk to <<1>>.

When I was young, I studied all the tumultuous times and the heroic deeds from the first era and I always wished I had lived back then instead.\n\nRecent events have made this era more interesting though. I realize now—these times are good too.
I wish you the best in there. If one Nereid caused all of this, the power she wields will be frightening.
I can't believe it. So many dead. Our whole city in ruins. All because of those damned mages.\n\nPlease, you have to help us.

Arch-Mage Yamanu-ko is in this tower. We call it the Apex Tower. The arch-mages of Elinhir have occupied it for centuries.\n\nIt was our duty to protect the city. Instead, we leave a legacy of destruction.
Hurry. We need to channel the elemental infusions so that we can force an opening into the staff.
That was sickening. I had to get rid of it. He just left … the body here. By the Light of Aetherius—what was he doing with it?\n\nLet's get out of here. We have a ritual site to find.
Go on! Hara waits upstairs.
I thank you, my friend. From the bottom of my soul, I thank you. I don't care where we go, or what we do. What you've given back to me is priceless.

Many believe the Nedes were barely more than barbarians, but ruins like this prove otherwise. Don't underestimate their cleverness. Look for a pattern if you can, and consider the possibility that the lock was designed to be impossible to open alone.
Strike the Lost One down. It is the only way to end this.
The Lost One waits below. Do not delay.
Why would <<1>> bring the Iron Wheel to our doorstep?\n\n<<2>> hopes he falls into a hole. A very deep hole. Filled with vipers!
Once the Lost One falls, we will become the Mage once more. Do not delay.
There is no more time for us. You must not delay.

You're so desperate to live on, short as your lifespan is. I'd be impressed if it weren't so futile.\n\nOnly the Warden remains. You could turn and run now, if you'd like. After all you've seen. But I think you'll push on. Go! Slay him! Or die trying.
And who might you be? I suppose you're wanting to go into the Archive? Great. Another raiding party.\n\nWhere in Oblivion did Brulo get to?
So it was true, then. Those crazy High Elves really were the Celestial Mage? Unbelievable!
Another visitor?\n\nAt least you seem less offensive than that Orc over there. Slightly. Avoid the upper floors. That's where the Learned One dwells.
Again you accomplish the unfeasible. Even in our mortal forms, we each could challenge armies. Mortal potential is staggering.
I have no time for idle chatter. It is most unfortunate the Learned One broke the seal.\n\nDistractions from rabble like you are precisely why we locked ourselves away in the first place.
So many distractions of late. The Learned One does not wish to be disturbed. You would do well to stay away from the upper floors.
This one said going by an ancient, cursed Yokudan fortress in arid mountains was a bad idea.\n\nBut nobody listens to Khajiit—because all they do is sit around eating moon-sugar all day, yes?

Don't mind me, just fixing our wagon. It's not built for this sort of terrain, but it's not as bad as Sallunas makes it sound.\n\nWe came out here to be the first merchants on the scene, but the disappearances have been bad for business.
I've always wanted to study the Citadel of Hel Ra up close. None have been inside since the First Era.\n\nBut many of my fellow Redguard who entered have not been seen again.
Move on, then. Nothing to see here, is there?
One good turn deserves another. What do you need?
I owe you much, my friend. One day, your kindness shall be repaid.
The inspector checked my cargo already. There were no problems!
Let me know when you are ready, and the race will begin.
Do not worry about me. It is nothing. This one simply climbed a tree and could not get down without falling. Very embarrassing.
They say this is an easy course. I'll probably fail. Again.

Satakal's coils surround you, friend. My remaining acolytes are much more attentive, and the Scaled Court no longer seeks to steal what is mine. We have shown the power of the one true serpent, and those who reject him suffer his fangs. \n\nThank you.
You should not be here, walker. The moons have told Thalinfar so.
Have you rescued our guards yet? Please, get back out there and try to find them.
Have … have you done it, Milksop?\n\nDid you put that spirit down?
You're actually going in there, aren't you? Do you have a death wish?\n\nThe Celestial Serpent himself leads the Scaled Court in these caverns!

I overheard your talk with the Khajiit. I can't believe he convinced you to enter these caverns. We've been trying to get him to leave.\n\nThe Celestial Serpent stalks these caves, and he has plans for Craglorn. For all of Tamriel.
How … how have you returned? The master should have … what have you done? What have you done to the master?
Lashburr can't wait to see Agganor's mounted helm! Not a head covering fit for an Iron Orc, but good to befoul.\n\nBut Lashburr has said too much. Walk away, little goat. Walk away.
Why is the Pact here? Have my friends all died? Hurry and free me, if that's why you've come.
Heard you speaking to Turuk. If you're going into those caves, you're going to need equipment.\n\nJust so happens I have some to part with. What do you say? Give me your money.

Did I hear that right? You're going into those caverns?\n\nWe're in no shape to do it, so you might as well. But you'll need some potent soul gems to take those cultists on. Lucky for you, I have a few lying around.
Oosh and I will be discussing this at length. There's definitely something more than the Listener wanting to enforce the tenets going on here.

It must have been gruesome work, but thanks again for dealing with the Scaled Court in Skyreach Hold. I'm sure you saved many lives.\n\nI only hope the Scaled Court doesn't return to try again. That would be disastrous.
You've got to help me! By the Eight—the pain!

So that's how he did it! He was imbuing the trolls with pure nirncrux! Fusing the armor and the runes into a powerful whole!\n\nI wonder what would happen if one of the mortal races was subjected to the process?
You are a shining light in the darkness, friend. Yes. You definitely have a divine glow about you. \n\nI trust you were able to recover some of the statue fragments?
You're finally here. So is the Celestial Serpent—you'll find him through those doors.\n\nBe careful.
None of these deaths would have been necessary if the Serpent hadn't lied to me.

Blessings of the Divines upon you. I will not forget the selfless aid you have given today—and at no small risk to yourself. \n\nShould the time come when that dread creature stirs again, we will be ready. Until then, safe journey to you.
Not now! I want to watch this.
I sense Cassipia's presence, but I do not see her. Be on your guard.

I'm impressed. You demonstrated a willingness to risk everything for the sake of others. You even helped someone you once called an enemy.\n\nMaybe this world isn't as irredeemable as I imagined. Thank you for helping me correct this terrible mistake.
The old Elf didn't give you too much trouble, did he? You'd never live it down.
You have returned, with no obvious bodily harm. I commend you. The Crypt has been quieted?
You are looking for those Legion Zero saboteurs, yes? Or did you already find them? \n\nTell Shaghila their blood now mixes with that nasty sewer water.
You here for crafting certification? Don't worry, there's no cost involved—your alliance covers all my fees.\n\nOnce you're certified, they'll let you fulfill the crafting writs. Everyone wins!

I have the faintest sense that the Warrior is nearby, but I can't see his face or hear his voice. What's happening to me?\n\nWill my skills disappear along with my memories? Has the Warrior truly abandoned me? Bah! Leave me to my grief!

I knew I could count on you. I last saw Titus in the north, searching for his wife's grave.\n\nAs his mind slips away, he fights to hold onto it. It pains him to accept that all he knew is dead and gone, yet he strives to keep the memories alive.

You're here for crafting certification, yes? Fear not, your alliance covers my considerable fees.\n\nIf you can prove your basic competence, I'll certify you so you may fulfill crafting writs.
Zantan has been inspired by your five-clawed nature! Your very presence gives him strength! So go! The Wood Elves will need you again before this ordeal is over!
I'm going to be all right. I'm sure the others are in dire straits.

<You notice a prominent handbill on the requisition board.>\n\n"The people of the Systres Isles bid you welcome! Masters of the craft await you in <<1>>! New crafters shall be trained! Accomplished crafters will be certified! All at no cost to you!"
"All members of the Ebonheart Pact! Master crafters await you in <<1>>. They offer free training for those new to a craft, and free certification for accomplished crafters!"
I think I'm going to be fine. The others will need you. I didn't think it would be like this. None of us did.
Go! I've seen what you can do.\n\nIf someone has a fighting chance against the Valkyn, it's you! You wanted a way out? Slay him, and you'll get one!
Go! You'll do more good clearing the path for me.\n\nI'll be back to cutting in a moment. Just like weeding my garden.

Brittgerd is finished with the Undaunted. With Hogondar. She will have trouble forgetting this trip to Oblivion. Perhaps I will join her—find a quiet corner of Skyrim and become a farmer.\n\nHa! She wishes! Undaunted! Undaunted! I am Undaunted!
I will be fine in a moment. Hogondar can fall on his sword if he gets bored.
Go! Sobabe promises to hurry. It is in her best interest.
I erect the spine of ….\n\nI erect … I don't feel so good.
I'm good. Give me a moment, and I'll be right along.\n\nNo, really. Stop staring.
I'll be all right.\n\nHaven't had this much fun since I fought in the war.
Is there something I can do for you, Undaunted?
Glirion's a good sort. Just … not too friendly. Doesn't show any emotions, really. Is bloodthirst an emotion? Never mind.

Stay back, you! I'll bring the full fury of Julianos down on your head if you …. Oh wait, you're not one of them! I'm sorry, just a bit jumpy, and my eyes aren't what they were.\n\nWhat brings you all the way up here?

You see me not at my best, wayfarer. I just needed a rest. My friends and I were discovered by these creatures. The Daedra are everywhere down here.\n\nI've taken shelter here, but I don't know how long this respite will last.
This power core contains an enormous amount of energy. Think of the applications it can be used for! My mind literally reels at the possibilities!

I'd take off if I were you. Raynor's going to build something that turns these Dwarven constructs into his personal army. Or, more likely, there's going to be a massive ka-boom.\n\nBut thanks for the help all the same!

By Trinimac's angry nose, where do you people keep coming from?\n\nDid you see those harpies haul my soldiers away? This is a siege, not a tent show! People are dying out here! If we don't deal with those nests soon, the camp will be overrun.

Those fools in Watcher's Hold just refuse to give up! When the Lionguard arrives, we'll finish them off. But in the meantime, you need to keep them from heaping any more dishonor on High-King Emeric and the Covenant.
Arushna has been kind enough to capture a wild durzog for me to tame.\n\nDid you find the whistle?

Go on now. Hurry, hurry. Retrieve the potion and the wing bone. Oh, and the egg, of course. Mustn't forget the egg!\n\nI'll be upstairs, researching the ritual. We'll conduct it up there when you return.
I suppose it's good to have <<1>> back. Even creepy Elves are better company than those creatures.
The fool thinks he can tame a durzog. He can do what he likes, as long as he pays me.
You've returned! Did you find anything of interest?

What a waste of a perfectly good opportunity! Oh, very well, I'll defer to your expertise in diplomatic matters. I guess remaining alive is reward enough.\n\nI heard about a nearby Ayleid ruin. I think we'll head there and explore. Farewell, friend.

So our ambassador finally found you? Took her damn time. But you're here now and that's what counts. \n\nWelcome to Orsinium. Amazing how fast we rebuilt the place, isn't it? Orsimer can do anything when we work together.
You were saying something about the stolen supplies?
We need to find a way inside the fort. Talk to Chief Urgdosh. They're working on a plan to get into Frostbreak Fortress.
He got half my workers killed, and now he insults us as well?\n\nThe Elf's blood price is steep and he's going to pay it very slowly.
The Order of the Silver Dawn will survive. We will one day rid the world of these murderous werewolves.\n\nOn this, you have my word.
It's not fair! We had them! We were almost through! The damn birds! I hate them!\n\nLook at those vultures! They're just sitting out there, picking at the bones of my warriors!
What did I tell you? Easy as echatere pudding and baked horker pie!\n\nThanks to your efforts, we should be able to wrap up the siege in record time now!
Can you believe it? A female chieftain! We'll be the laughingstock of Wrothgar! I've known Ushruka since she was a babe. Fine woman, but she won't last long with everyone scrambling for her head.

Good day, friend. Or is it evening? So hard to tell down here. Hm. Even in this dim light, your face looks familiar. Yes. Stormhaven. You were the one with the Stonechewers' totem.\n\nAnd now you're here killing Riekr. Is this really necessary though?
Perhaps <<1>> is right about the changes in Orsinium. Time will tell whether she is an exception, or the first of many.

I'm sorry. Do you need something? If not, go bother someone else. \n\nIf I don't finish all these texts within the week, my master will send me out into the field where I'll probably get killed. I prefer the books.
Another outsider, here to perform tricks for the false king?\n\nBah, go back to Kurog and leave a real clan chief in peace.
Zhasim is stubborn, especially where that cat is concerned. He's smart though, so I know he'll be along soon.
Murukh's probably the strongest in our party. He took the uninjured hunters and went after the Riekr. I think they headed toward the cave in the cliffside.
If that damned Moth Priest doesn't get moving soon, I'll move through her.\n\nGet going. Maybe she'll follow. We need to retake the throne room, first and foremost.

I'm one of the mighty King Kurog's shield-wives. I'm his protector, his confidant, his lover.\n\nIf you do anything to betray my husband, I will separate the limbs from your body and toss the entire mess to the harpies.
This one is confused. I thought we were going to the Orc city. Where are all the buildings? This is the worst city this one has ever visited!

I pray to Trinimac that the chiefs will learn from this experience, but I fear that their stubbornness won't be set aside so easily.\n\nBut I wanted to thank you. You helped my son and I appreciate that. Go in peace until he needs you again.
I know you. You're one of those outsiders that Kurog brought to our land.\n\nI heard you've done some amazing feats, but I'd rather you didn't linger in my stronghold.
The next time I see you, I'll be chief. And a good chief remembers her allies.\n\nHuh. "Her allies." This is almost real.
Messy, but necessary. He waved that thing around enough that anyone in Shatul will recognize it. A very distinctive tattoo.\n\nLet's head back to the chief's tent.
That's the <<z:1>>. Grab it so we can get back.
Reality is bends around us. Local Mundus is in flux. \n\nThe pinnacle of White-Gold Tower is straight ahead, through that portal. That's where you'll find Clivia.
I took one bad scratch to the face and now look at me—stuck here handing out rewards to other soldiers.\n\nLet me guess—you want a reward for something?
Don't ever volunteer for quartermaster duties. In fact, don't ever volunteer for anything in this army. That's the best advice you'll get all day.\n\nSo, how can I help you?
<A new bounty notice has been posted to the Hunting Board.>
Is it done? Did you manage to disrupt the ritual once again?
Aishah is happy to see you again, walker. You have been busy, yes?\n\nYou rescued the people as this one asked?

Come stretch your tail by my fire, fellow Lukiul. As the stones of this city grow colder, we must rely on each other if we are to survive.\n\nYou've been outside. Tell me, have the chains already pulled us into Coldharbour?
Thank you so much for agreeing to help. Oh, I hope they're all right.
This one is relaxing. Can you not see this? Please, just go away.
Astia is anxious to study that blood. Have you retrieved it?

I'm sorry if I look disappointed. When you came in, I thought you were someone else.\n\nI'm terribly worried about my house-servant, Gryna. My husband passed away years ago, and we never had children, so she's all I have left.

<You notice a prominent handbill on the requisition board.>\n\n"The people of the Systres Isles bid you welcome! Masters of the craft await you in <<1>>! New crafters shall be trained! Accomplished crafters will be certified! All at no cost to you!"
I have no idea how you got this far, but go no farther. Soon, we battle to retake the Palace in the name of the Empress Regent.
Stand where we can see you.
This is no place for dawdling. Move along. Preferably back the way you came.
Quickly, take the side tunnel to return to the entrance!
Don't you have Daedra to slay? I have nothing to say to enemies of the Pact.
Ew! You've got bits of that barrel-belly's fleshiness all over you. That makes even the Rat's stomach turn, and he eats in the sewers.\n\nSo you killed this barrel-belly yourself?
You are the one sent by the sewer-dwelling Ebonheart Pact, yes? Why you choose to live in a stinking dung-hole is beyond me. \n\nBut Ezudash digresses! Let's discuss these anchors, yes?

General Aklash sent you? All right. Let me make one thing clear then. I owe no loyalty to the Covenant. My duty is to the Fighters Guild. \n\nI will avail you of my knowledge of the anchors … but only so that we can save the city.

Well, I guess you've gone and proven skeevers can fly … I hate to say it, but if I was a gambling woman, I'd have bet against you.\n\nWhen I heard that horn, I nearly soiled myself. I didn't, of course, but I was pretty surprised.
That was quite a feat you pulled off out there. To be honest, I'm humbled that you went to such lengths on my behalf.
Back again. Had some more time to think about joining the Enforcers? You won't regret it. It's the one way you can get paid to start a tavern brawl.
I'd encourage you to mend your ways outlaw. Your crimes are well-known here and will not be tolerated. But there is still hope, you can cast aside wickedness and take up the mantle of the Enforcers.

You'll check on Narsis Dren? Thank you! My clan has an aversion to disturbing the dead—especially the dead of different races.\n\nThe barrow's at the top of the hill. The Dark Elf said he'd send word, but we haven't heard anything since he left.
You really do have a knack for adventuring! Are you ready to look upon the grandeur of a Dragon priest's tomb?

Trade these Nord delicacies for the finest ale and cheese in Wrothgar. Rigurt and his jade princess will feast until we are too full to escape our love!\n\nAnd find out what poems or perfumes are used in Orc wooing rituals. Rigurt might need the help.
Have you come for my cheese? That seems to be the only thing anyone ever wants to talk to me about these days.
This land rises fierce and sharp, swept cold by a fierce wind. It reminds me of the desert at night, back home.
You make more noise than a mountain bear in heat! I heard you coming from an arrow's flight away and I smelled you from two!\n\nIs there something I can do for you?
Welcome back. Let me guess. From that look on your face, Narsis Dren wasn't completely honest with us when I hired him.
I think it's time for the great Narsis Dren to shake the dust of this village from his boots.\n\nAdventure awaits, and Narsis Dren always answers the call!
Stibbons always finds a way to turn the simplest task into an ordeal. I don't know why I continue to employ the man.

I must say, I'm relieved that you volunteered to ascend to the summit. I was certain my lady was going to make me do it.\n\nNow I might actually get off this mountain without getting frozen into a block of ice!
How embarrassing. To be fair, "zugka" and "zugra" are rather close, but I guess there's a big difference between a "kiss" and a "curse."
I'm better at research than actual field work. I heard they're establishing a museum in Orsinium. Perhaps I'll go work there. I know they'll appreciate my skills more than Dren ever did!
Glad to see you made it out of there without twisting your ankle or anything. But I don't see our contract target.\n\nYou weren't able to find Khoruzoth, I take it?
See that cave? That's an old smuggler's hole. I'd bet my last gold piece that Captain Henrisa is in there. Maybe even the ambassador.
Once Captain Henrisa left the camp, I couldn't convince his lordship to remain behind. So I followed along to try to keep him safe.
Skordo found something? Oh, I hope he found Lady Sovelle. And I hope she's all right.

Thanks for solving the mystery, but I can't believe you left my son in Thukhozod's forsaken sanctum.\n\nMaybe I can hire Meram and Bardun to fetch his body and bring him back here. An Orc shouldn't have to spend eternity in the company of the dead.

Oh, next time I decide to go on an adventure, just remind me not to leave Camlorn!\n\nI have a deep and abiding fear of anything with feathers. Especially if they're bigger than I am and want to eat me!
Do you see how my clan looks at the forge-hammer? The fire in their eyes! They'll rebuild Orsinium by themselves, if they have to.

The Orcs will negotiate with me. There's still time to salvage my mission and make sure Ethian's father lives to regret what he set in motion.\n\nBut thank you. Without your timely assistance, more innocents would have been lost.
Well … that was … amazing!\n\nWe get to do that again, right?
I recognize that Orc standing beside you. That's King Kurog!\n\nI'm honored that you and the king came to find me. I just wish you had gotten here sooner, before the rest of my squad was lost.

We opened Orsinium to the best and brightest—crafters, farmers, scholars. Anyone who can help bring my vision to life. I leave the details to my wives and mother. But you attracted my attention.\n\nWhich brings us to the big question.
Back away, citizen! We have enough to deal with as it is.\n\nMy soldiers can't do their job with all you civilians getting under foot.

I don't know how to thank you. These fanatics, they beat us, threatened us. They told us that they were going to kill us as soon as the king or his soldiers showed up.\n\nBut you got in without alerting them. You saved us. The others though ….
My beloved must be beside himself! To think these cowards would attack innocents at prayer.\n\nIf King Kurog demands it, I would comfort my beloved with the blood of these fanatics.
Damn Malacath fanatics! To attack a sacred temple! It's … unthinkable!

You're alive! Finally something good comes out of this debacle. Too many priests died because of those fanatics. We removed their bodies, but if word of this gets out ….\n\nI need to know—did you find High Priestess Solgra? Is she safe?

I knew I liked you the moment I saw you!\n\nChief Bazrag is big and mean and looks like he can fight, but there were an awful lot of marauders. Ice-Heart's Winterborn won't stop until Bazrag and all the Orc peasants are dead. You better hurry!
My head feels like a harpy got inside it and won't stop flapping its wings. Just tell Avreg to get back to camp. He'll make sure his brother is safe, like he always does.
Please, you need to check the coffer. My hands are shaking too much.
<The body of <<1>>. His hand appears to clutch at a journal of some kind.>
The pyre—it must burn!
The great pyre burns. Its ashes will smolder for years.\n\nYou did this, despite all arrayed against you.
Go. The shrine awaits you in the stronghold keep.
Running off to <<1>> is why <<2>>'s still unwed. Finding glory in old relics instead of at the king's side? He'd have chosen her if she wasn't so headstrong. Pah!

If you have a letter from the Forge-Mother, then you've come to the right place. And we don't even care that you're one of those Nord-loving, lizard-liking, preening like a Dark Elf, card-carrying members of the Ebonheart Pact.\n\nNo offense.
I heard you say you're going to help us. Malacath smiles upon your bravery, stranger.
Ah, my friend and ally has returned! Let's talk.\n\nI heard what you did at the temple. Your efforts no doubt saved countless lives. It pains me to learn that Chief Bazrag was involved, though.
You again.\n\nWell, if you're here to help, then talk to my king. His new idea sounds reckless to me, but my husband has survived reckless more than once since I've been at his side.
Ah, welcome back, friend of my beloved and ally to the king!\n\nI'm glad that my beloved has someone as noble and trustworthy as you at his side. It does my heart good to see him make a new friend.
