Relax. Enjoy yourself. You earned a good rest.\n\nI'm sure I'll have something else for you to do before the Great Moot commences. In the meantime, go and mingle or something.

While you retrieve The Rat's message, I'll coordinate with Father Egnatius and Captain Caudex to chart out our next move.\n\nBy the time you return, we should have a plan in place. I can't guarantee it will be a good one.
I can make it out on my own. Just let me rest for another moment and then I'll get moving.
Isn't my sister the greatest! I learned so many important lessons during this hunting expedition.

You can get a rope over by the forge. I'll wait here. Less chance of getting spotted if only one of us goes traipsing around the stronghold.\n\nJust between us, I'd rather climb down than jump into a deep, dark hole, wouldn't you?
I wonder how many unfortunate souls have given in to these demented Vosh Rakh?
The sooner we get out of here, the sooner I can report these mad cultists to the authorities.

That stupid sphere rolled right up to my stupid brother like nothing happened!\n\nIt's like it thinks it's his damned pet or something! A dangerous, demented pet made out of metal and gears, but a pet all the same!
Did you … what happened? I thought I was someplace else for a moment. Someone else … a Breton knight?

I'm sure that one more use of the rod with drain the sphere and rectify its frenzied behavior. Then I'll be able to safely repair it.\n\nI'm certain everything will work out fine. Well, mostly certain. Anyway, go find that sphere!
Memories imparted through water? I know of a similar technique involving stone.\n\nSo much to take in. My head is still swimming!
Welcome to the spike room. I'd brag about the craftsmanship if we weren't trapped down here.\n\nSee those valves on the wall? I need you to turn all three of them. Just watch out for the spikes.
I refuse to leave one prison just to enter another. If you plan to take me to Kurog, forget about it.\n\nI'd rather die here, with my clan, than have to see Kurog's gloating face again.
I'm glad to see that most of the others made it. Now all we have to do is make it the rest of the way out of these ruins.
Malacath's bloody bones! What is that thing and why is it attacking us?
Funny, when I was stuck behind that fire, all I could think about was getting back to Shornhelm with Raza.\n\nBut now I think I want to stay in Orsinium and really learn about my heritage.
Chief.\n\nUh, is there anything you need? I can get the echatere back in their pens … or out of their pens. Whatever you need.
We'll resolve this outside of Shatul. I'll pay no blood price.
I think it best if <<1>> and I stay with Shatul. We still have much to offer the clan.\n\nI hope she agrees with me.
I'll be fine. Go, face the Beast of the Reach—before she escapes!
Who would have thought that Solgra would help me? After all I said about her?\n\nWell, I was wrong. Even if she does worship a false god, she still cares about the people. I can respect that.
I know you have questions, and you're probably just as angry with me as Eveli. But please, hear me out, I beg you.\n\nThere are deadly plots unfolding and we're all in terrible danger.
High Priestess Solgra wants to talk to you. Better not keep the lying liar who lies waiting.
I didn't expect Wrothgar to be so harsh. Next time I won't be so eager to find a partner.
Frozen durzog liver pairs surprisingly well with mead.
I don't know why I'm here exactly. I'm just an innkeeper's daughter.\n\nStill, it's kind of nice to be rubbing elbows with all these celebrities. I just hope they don't expect me to say a few words.
You did it! I don't know how you did it, but I'm eternally grateful for what you've done!
Keep away from the Khajiit. If I see you pass her anything, you'll end up in your own cell.
What to do, what to do? Chief Bazrag and Eveli are in danger, but there's also the moot.
You look familiar. But I don't really care. Now get out of my way.
Take your time to study the scrolls and choose carefully. Only one blessing per overseer, you know.
You've returned. How surprising.\n\nAre you ready to make a deal?
No, I have no idea what it means. Hey, I'm just the messenger!
I lost a wager there by putting my money on the Lamia Queen. She's never failed before. \n\nIt might be time to start betting on you, instead.
You did great back there. I have to say, I'm impressed!\n\nJust give me a moment to catch my breath. It might be an illusion, but I'm sweating like an Orc under here.
I know what you want me to do. I'll warn Bazrag and Solgra. Now leave me alone, all right? I don't want to look at you right now.

Good, good! You've done such a fantastic job filling these walls. The House of Orsimer Glories is finally worthy of its name!\n\nThere's just one final piece … if you don't mind braving the wilderness.

I should have known that hiding folks in our inn would eventually bite us in the arse. This is ridiculous, though. They sent an entire squad of soldiers to lock down one inn!\n\nYou'd think we were the damn Winterborn or something!
Away with you! The Rat has nothing to say to you.
That was more of an adventure than I was expecting. I hope the rest of my journey doesn't turn out to be so eventful.
Get to the temple and help Eveli and Solgra. Then find the way into the moot.
I hope you had better luck than we did. All of the chief's contacts have disappeared faster than rabbit meatballs at a Nord banquet!
Champion of Orsinium, it is an honor to meet you. May I bestow upon you Trinimac's blessing?
I'll watch over Eveli. You go and see what Chief Bazrag wants to talk about.
Is … is that you? Oh yeah, that's you. I'd recognize those footfalls anywhere.
The final battle approaches like dusk before the dark. We either stop Kurog now or we die trying.\n\nStrike often and strike true, my friend. And make every strike count!
This isn't a good time to visit the temple. We have a bit of a situation.\n\nI humbly suggest that you come back later.
You have no business asking for <<Cz:1>> if you can't display a basic understanding of her legend.
Greetings, friend. I have a request on behalf of the mighty King Kurog!
Fine. Talk to the liar. But be careful. His words fall like nectar from a tree.\n\nI thought he liked me, but he only had eyes for the gold around my neck.
Did you find <<A:1>>? Do you have it with you?
Tell me, my good friend, were you successful? Did you find my pendant among the wreckage?
You bear the <<1>>. I knew, because as soon as I saw you, Malacath whispered that I should kill you where you stand.\n\nClearly a sign.
Our conquest of the Imperial City is underway, soldier. Are you prepared to do your part?
Our conquest of the Imperial City is underway, soldier. Are you prepared to do your part?
There is grim work to do, soldier. Get to it.
So. You're making a stupid face. I'm assuming you have questions?\n\nSorry. It's not a stupid face. It's just—never mind. I have … difficulties.

Meet me in the rectory when you're finished—it should be safe there.\n\nNow stay low. You don't want to be strung up like the rest of these dolts. We're just going to find Egnatius and get out of here, right? We're agreed …? Just nod.
Once you've placed the auricular geodes, meet me at the base.
Champion of Orsinium, it is an honor to meet you. Would you like to receive Malacath's blessing now?
I'll get this lot out of the city, but they won't have much. A few blankets, a crust of bread …. From what I hear, Cyrodiil isn't kind to refugees. I can only hope, I guess.
I have a feeling we'll be seeing each other again, soon. This war is far from over.\n\nUntil then, watch your back, soldier.

Ah, the handsome Rigurt has chosen you to be his champion? I approve. What a rare and prestigious honor, to be selected to participate in the sacred rites of Orc love!\n\nSo tell me, what would you like to know?
Appreciate your help. Grandfather deserves a tidy cairn.\n\nCareful. Most folks who go into <<1>> don't come back.

Ah, you're just in time. We finished clearing out the Vosh Rakh and the remaining chiefs are waiting for me to address them.\n\nBut, word of Kurog's death is spreading through the city like wildfire. I don't know how the people will react to the news.
There you are. I was beginning to think you'd been caught.
You've done well. I think, on behalf of my master here, I may begin to be cautiously optimistic.
This one thanks you for preserving what little we have left. Our methods are … unconventional. But in the fullness of time, people will see if was for the best.
Thank the Eight, you've made it. Barely got past the Daedra myself, but this place seems safe enough for now.
So. You're making a stupid face. I'm assuming you have questions?\n\nSorry. It's not a stupid face. It's just—never mind. I have … difficulties.

That was a beautiful ceremony. So respectful and yet also inspiring. I particularly liked the fire. It was so … fiery!\n\nAnd I'm glad they made Bazrag the king. I think he'll do a fine job for his people.
Eveli woke up and wanted to come here straight away.\n\nIt's good to see her up and around. She'll be her old self in no time.
May Trinimac watch over all those who have fallen and guide them to their next reward.
He turned me into a messenger when I first arrived, but I never suspected the king was a villain.\n\nI guess no one is above greed and corruption.
I have never attended a funeral before. Things like this, they don't happen where I come from.
Kurog was always headstrong, confident. But these things I've heard he did? That's not the Kurog I knew. Not the mercenary I fought beside and trusted my life to.\n\nIt just doesn't make any sense.
Never liked funerals, never will.
So. You're making a stupid face. I'm assuming you have questions?\n\nSorry. It's not a stupid face. It's just—never mind. I have … difficulties.
Our conquest of the Imperial City is underway, walker. You prepared to do your part, yes?
Our conquest of the Imperial City is underway, soldier. Are you prepared to do your part for queen and kin?
Our conquest of the Imperial City is underway, soldier. Are you prepared to do your part for the Covenant?
Our conquest of the Imperial City is underway, soldier. Are you prepared to do your part for the Covenant?
Kurog's favorite ale will be at the keep on time. Don't worry about that.
Thank you for gathering everyone. It's important that they're all here to see what happens next.
Please hurry and find my friends. I fear that none of us will survive long on our own in this forsaken wilderness.
Keep your head down and your voice low. We don't want to attract any attention.

This is not the most … ideal location for preserving ancient documents. A bit too much moisture and low breeding. But it's far better than the belly of a Daedroth.\n\nI will see to it that these records are cared for until we retake the city.
There's an ogre den in a nearby cave called "<<1>>." Grab anything ogre-created which has a natural look, feel, or smell.\n\nBring it all to the House of Orsimer Glories and I'll assemble my artwork!
Didn't think I'd miss the smell of ash and burning pitch, but … yeah. Smells like an Ogrim's loincloth down here.
I'm headed topside again soon. Too many of you provincials up there, running around spooking my quarry. No offense.
I told Chief Gloorot that this was a cursed location, but he wouldn't listen. No one ever listens to old Shab.\n\nSay, what clan are you from? I don't recognize you.

Any one of these cultists could be carrying the Daedric Brand or a key to the chapel. So … happy hunting?\n\nI have to track down a lead of my own. Once you've branded a skeleton and heard what it has to say, meet me in the Undertaker's Office.
I have no idea what direction I should go and I'm freezing out here.
Sailors should be out at sea, not skulking around in the ice and snow with absolutely no idea where they're going.
The rabble outside? I take it that their demise was your doing?\n\nWe were forced to take shelter, but we can't complete our mission from inside this blasted tower.
Don't worry. I won't let anything happen to the alchemist. I promise.

Weren't you just in the Arena District? You should go back. It's easier to get work done when the games are on. It's an excellent distraction. So, yes. Go make some trouble. \n\nI might have something for you here later on.
I knew that Elf was up to no good. I just knew it!
I hope Master Dren gets back soon. He hates it when his dinner gets cold.
Don't hesitate to break those machines to pieces. This Dwarven garbage is nothing but trouble.\n\nMake sure to speak to Birkhu when you're done. He's anxious to close the book on this.
Back again, eh? Well, the task remains the same. Cut the hides off those werewolves hiding in Argent Mine and slay their leader. I'll be here with your payment when it's done.
Why do you linger? <<1>>'s assassins already advance upon the duel.\n\nWarn them. Hurry!
I would thank your master for the stew. It is quite delicious.
We're not going to let those metal monstrosities anywhere near our stronghold!
I can't believe I trusted that little skeever! I guess my mother was right when she told me not to get involved with a tuskless High Elf.
You there … we need help. Our caravan … they came out of nowhere. Attacked us, stole our cargo.\n\nThe Orcs need those supplies!
These people and their Dwarf-junk … honestly. Just leave the damned things where they are, am I right?
So you're the one seeking out my eggs? Excellent! I know I can count on you to get the job done right.\n\nJust be careful bringing them back. Eggs don't travel well.
Well, I can't say I'm surprised to see you back again! Even a death-trap like Zthenganaz proved no danger to you!\n\nDid you get the data I need?
Did you see all those skeletons? Weren't they frightening, with their bones and their skin all missing and everything? I hate those things!
So, you're going back into the Kennel for me? Good, good. Just make sure you don't end up as durzog food yourself.
I am glad to see you've taken up our cause once again, my friend. There are still many souls struggling under Thukhozod's heel. I know that you will do what's necessary to save them.
You're back? Good. I've got a whole mess of growling bellies waiting to be fed. Get out there and get hunting!
So, ready for another journey into the frontier? I've heard that some more of those brutish ogres were sighted doing … well, ghastly things with my book. That will not do.
The corruption stirs once again. Actually, that may be indigestion. One moment …. No, I was right, the corruption has returned. You must cleanse it before it has a chance to spread!
Dark clouds swirl overhead once more. I sense that Zandadunoz has returned. Are you prepared to send him back to Oblivion?
I knew Wrothgar was dangerous, but giant metal men, too? It is too much!
I'm afraid those Riekr are at it again. You ready to teach them another lesson in manners?

It's good to see you again, though we seem destined to always meet during troubled times. First the frozen peasants, and now this difficulty with the Vosh Rakh.\n\nI try to remain optimistic, but sometimes I just want to scream.

Eveli's plan puts you and I into the thick of things. Fine by me! I wanted to see if everything our Wood Elf says about you is true.\n\nSpeaking of which, Eveli wants to talk to you before we go inside.
Can't do business with you. Not until you speak with Ralen Veri.
Want to do business? You should see Ralen Veri. Rules are rules!

Ah, my favorite problem-handler has returned! Have you come to see what you accomplished? Thanks to you, the clan chiefs have gathered to hear what I have to say.\n\nThis is going to be a moot that all of Wrothgar won't soon forget!
With every day, more and more of the city nears completion. But these rumors of traitors and assassins—I fear for the safety of my workers!

I had heard that the city was coming along nicely, but I must say, I'm truly impressed.\n\nIf Kurog's goal was to capture his essence in stone, then Orsinium is a perfect testament to his cold and heartless arrogance.
Is something wrong? What were you and Kurog whispering about over there?\n\nOh, never mind. I really don't care. I just want to find something strong to drink.
You look like I feel. I take it you're as thrilled to be here as I am.\n\nDon't worry. I expect that this will all be over soon.
Not that it's any of my business, but I hope the news you brought doesn't affect the moot. I'm really looking forward to hearing what Kurog has to say.
My husband cared about Kurog in his own way. I know he shouldn't feel this way, but he's disappointed that events forced you to slay the Orc who would be king.

These little Dwemer constructs are particularly loyal and affectionate. Sometimes I almost forget that they are only machines.\n\nWe're going to explore these ruins as soon as I finish making a few simple adjustments to account for all the undead.
Hide, quickly!
Welcome home, Assassin. I know what occurred but I want to hear it from your lips. Say the words and say them loud.

My sister appears to be safe and sound. She's surprisingly calm, even if she's still mad about what I did to her friend. That's better than I expected.\n\nThank you for your help. I couldn't have exposed Grand Chanter Surus's corruption without you.
"Thieves should always travel separately." Advice from <<1>>—good advice.
You're back and alive! That's better than most folk who I've tried this with before.

Wise of you to do what <<1>> says. I find it best not to rub her the wrong way. Like petting a ball made of lemon-soaked razors.\n\nNothing, <<1>>! We were not speaking of you, I assure you! Oh … I think she heard me.
<<1>> told me you went into the Iron Wheel's headquarters by yourself.\n\nWhat in Oblivion were you thinking?

The first part of the lesson is complete. I need a few moments to consider how best to apply the second part.\n\nOf course, Anais and her agents may find me before that. I suppose that's the risk all good teachers must face.
Be warned, the disguise won't do you any good within the Iron Wheel's headquarters.
New-Brother! Welcome! Welcome! If there's anything you need, anything at all, you come to me, yes?
Didn't think I'd stay in that bed forever, did you New-blade? As soon as I'm back to full strength, we'll see who's the better assassin!

I almost bit my tongue trying not to laugh! Qamar doesn't so much strut as slosh about like a half-filled waterskin.\n\nHe's completely oblivious to the misfortune that just visited him. It's too much!
Private game. Go beg somewhere else.
Not now! I'm winning!
You don't belong here, and you absolutely shouldn't be speaking with me.

Curious. I vowed never to return to this place, but now I have an uncontrollable urge to linger for a few moments longer.\n\nYou go ahead. Shazara-Ta will see you safely back to the Gold Coast. Let's meet in Kvatch, in front of Akatosh's Cathedral.
Astara was looking for you, Initiate. Sounds like she has a special job for you. \n\nAmbitious, aren't you? Hasn't taken you long to catch the Matron's eye.
You took your time. I was starting to get worried.\n\nBut tell me, were you successful? Have you secured gainful employment for Kireth and myself?
You're back. Did you have any luck? Did you find anyone who's willing to hire us?\n\nWait, don't tell me. I need a moment to compose myself. Tell Raynor how things turned out while I have a sit down.
Did you have any luck? Were you able to gather a blossom from a wyrd flower?

What a disaster! That bard gets in one scrap with a Dark Elf and suddenly he can't play tonight's show. She strained his finger? What does that even mean?\n\nSorry, I'm rambling. The crowd gets rowdy when there's no music to listen to while they drink.
We'll set sail soon—as soon as the tavern runs out of this tasty brew!

The sea wants this one to starve to death, that's how stingy it is! All those tasty fish and it refuses to share unless I stress and strain and twice on Sundas!\n\nLife is a terrible joke and Shantin is the punch line.
Customers should check in with the banker downstairs. I'm quite busy balancing the accounts right now.

The ingot thieves use an old smuggler's dock along the coast east of Anvil.\n\nThey won't part with the ingots willingly, but if you retrieve them, I'll let Raynor work on our forge and compensate him accordingly.
I have good news, my friend! <<1>> and the Iron Wheel will soon depart Hew's Bane.\n\nAnd the bad news … <<2>> will be sent to Taneth, where she will stand trial for raiding <<c:3>>.
I've never met <<1>> before. Far as I'm concerned, I never want to see him again.
Silver-Claw is fidgety as a … well, as a cat. On hot sand. With a knot tied in his tail.\n\nHe's got some information and he's anxious to share it with you.
I'd planned to go to Abah's Landing after this job. If he's willing to take us there, I say we should go.
I'll see you at <<c:1>>. I have a few things to discuss with <<2>>.
I have no quarrel with you. My dowry is safely returned to <<c:1>>, as are the remains of my ancestor. Those responsible are in custody.\n\nYet I am not entirely satisfied with the outcome.
I can't imagine we'll ever speak again, but I wish you luck in your many endeavors.
Could've lived my entire life without running through a spider pit.\n\nBut we made it through. You'll make a real impression in Abah's Landing.

Until I spent time in a cell, I didn't realize how much this place had grown on me. It's good to be back.\n\nBut it's better to have robbed the Iron Wheel of their dignity, our guildmates, and a dockload of ill-gotten goods.
I'm so sorry to hear of what happened. I will give what aid I can—I promise you.
I've never seen <<1>> this happy. And we do have need of a good forger.\n\nIf he helps us get <<2>> in hand, I'll make him an honorary member.
If I had it my way, we'd go in over the palace walls. Watch for <<1>> from the rooftops.
I'll wear whatever finery I recovered from my home. I don't care what <<1>> says, I refuse to set foot in the Diamond Thimble.
Your date made it back before you. Informed us of what happened at the wedding. \n\nDon't blame yourself. <<1>> told you to leave.
What are you still doing here? Get lost. If you're lucky, I'll have more work for you tomorrow.
Do avoid staining your outfit. I recommend keeping to white wine.
My father, dead? Before that, together with <<1>>?\n\nPlease, see what she has to say. I need a moment to think.
You'll get no help from me. Begone. I will finish my drink in peace.\n\nAnd stay away from my things.
This is more exhilarating and terrifying than I imagined. But we should find a way out, yes?
I want to take everything in this room, but there's little time.\n\nPerhaps a hatpin. Nobody misses a hatpin.
<<1>> always had an escape plan. There must be another way out of this room.
Check everywhere. <<1>> loved his escape routes. He'd never let himself be trapped—not even in his own home.
Go ahead, tell her. You saw yourself what <<1>> did.\n\nAnd I don't think she'll take me seriously in this outfit.
You've got that look in your eye. That look of absolute boredom. If you want something to do, I could direct you to some dishonest work.\n\nIf that sort of thing interests you.
My father died to protect <<1>> from the Iron Wheel. If it was his last wish, I should honor it.

Have you met my cousin, <<1>>? Said not to embarrass her in this little backwater of a town. Very well, I told her, I'll keep my mouth shut by filling it with wine.\n\nDid I mention she's my cousin? I don't recall.
I deserve such cruelty.
What now? I thought I asked you to leave.
"There's gristle in the camel milk," she says. Of course there's gristle! Who wants milk you can't chew?\n\nNo job is worth this. "The resplendent <<1>> shan't require your attendance." Bah!
Ah, a friendly face. Good of you to join me on my unexpected jog.\n\nAnd I agree, this isn't my color.
Everyone's accounted for. Did you have any trouble?
Almost to the treasure vaults. We can do this.
Is it strange that I don't want to find anything? I don't want to believe <<1>> abandoned us. Even though it's probably true.\n\nWe should look around.
A vampire lord has been vanquished, but always another appears to take her place. That is the way of things.\n\nWhen evil again steps from the shadows, my blade shall be ready to greet it.

This one recognized you as a warrior of distinction! We should split up, yes? Explore separately and locate the Captain and the stolen items.\n\nIf you find the Captain before I do, please give her Raz's utmost regards. Preferably, right in the heart.
Find <<1>> in <<c:2>>. And hurry—the wedding is very soon.
Like shadows, my friend. We need to get in and out of the mansion without causing too much mayhem and without being seen. Agreed?
Last I heard, the Desert Falcon was in Rivenspire—some tavern in Shornhelm.\n\nSee what you can learn. If any trails lead to <<1>>, follow them.
I never believe a thing <<1>> says, yet she stands by your competence.\n\nYou're here, sooner than expected. I suppose she can be right … on occasion.
I knew my time here wouldn't last. I hoped it would take longer, though.\n\n<<1>> wanted to make sure I was truly dead, yes? I taught her too well.
Last I saw <<1>>, she was pacing about in <<c:2>>. Going to put a furrow in the floor if she isn't careful.
Bellulor's the name, gossip and rumor is the game.
The tomb must be sealed again or Hew's legacy—such that it is—will be destroyed.
This hot desert sun feels so good upon my flesh! Not like the pitiful sun we have in Skyrim!

Do you expect me to thank you for … that came out wrong. I … appreciate your … assistance in this matter.\n\nIf you find out anything at the merchant enclave outside the gates, maybe it will lead you to the author of that letter.
Does the secret passage require a pass phrase or a special key? It's been a long time since I traveled through a secret passage.
Cooperating with you worked out so much better than I had planned. Now pull up a chair and have a drink. You deserve it.\n\nBesides, I hate to drink alone.
My lady made an amulet like that from one of my scales, too.
The door … what is it about the door?
Leave me be. I have to keep my hand on a panel.
We'll search the room. If there's anything to be found, we'll find it.\n\nUnless we find gargoyles. I hate gargoyles. Even more than spiders.
Left your picks on the bedstand this morning? Best hurry, if you're ready now.
I see you but I don't see Narahni's son. I suppose this task was more than you could handle. Why am I not surprised?
Please find my son, Tashmin. He has made mistakes, but he hasn't done anything that warrants the shackles of slavery.\n\nThis one will wait here and keep Velsa from worrying so.
Your words rekindled the memories this one thought were long gone. So I decided to come to Abah's Landing sooner rather than later.
I've got nothing else to say to you until you bring me that ledger page.
Ah, Velsa tells me you were the one who freed Fa'ren-dar from Cosh's leash.
On the one hand, I'm grateful that Anais doesn't appear any worse for the wear.\n\nOn the other hand, I hoped to see some evidence by now that she had learned her lesson.
You're Walks-Softly's idiot associate. Don't think I haven't memorized your face!
I have very little interest in chatter.

Met a sea captain today with dreadful luck. Lost his favorite spyglass, and his whole crew! Maormer slavers got the drop on them in Thrall Cove. I don't usually handle missing persons, but see about any crew if you find them. I abhor slavery.
I would love to see your collection, but not a single coin moves without Ralen Veri's say so.
Speak to Ralen Veri. Then this one may deal with you.
Go on, Assassin. We both have things we need to do.
Kor and Hildegard mean well, but they're worse than a couple of mother hens.\n\nYou're alive. Does that mean the Grand Sermonizer is no longer with us?
It seems you have me at a disadvantage. But you don't have to be afraid of me. Put away your weapons and I'll help you in whatever way I can.

So many Divines, so many rituals. But I've come for the main event, as it were. I have a particular fondness for Dibella. Must be her connection to beauty and love.\n\nAnd erotic instruction. I could use a few new techniques in that regard.
I appreciate your help, but I think you were too hard on Hilde. She knows she was tricked by that religious fool. She won't let it happen again.
When you're ready to go back to Anvil, just say the word.
Why would the Chanter tell me to leave if it wasn't true? If I wasn't a danger to the Brotherhood? You don't know how ferocious the wolf can be! He promised that Akatosh would help me!
Should you finally cleanse Exulus's evil from Hrota Cave, Arkay will look kindly upon your deeds. \n\nAnd the material reward is valuable, too, you understand.
Hey, quit poking around! I've got work to do and so do you. What more could you want from me?
I probably don't need to tell a professional to be careful. But … do be careful, all right?
Well, you look interesting. I'm quite certain I don't remember seeing you around the castle before. Even so, I do hope there's a good reason for this interruption.

I assume you have a reason for approaching me while I'm working. What is it? Are you trying to get me noticed?\n\nWait a moment. Did you run into a problem with the Governor's contract? Did something go wrong?
You want tickets, talk to the front counter. You want a refund, go jump in the sea. All sales are final.
It looks much worse than it is, I am sure.
Why risk the law undoing all your hard work, when you have this one here to serve?
Never liked camels. Bumpy, ill-tempered, and it takes days to get all the fur from the armor seams.

Losing <<1>> was a swift kick to the tail. But from what our people have observed, the Iron Wheel is preparing to return to Taneth. Sweet and bitter at the same time.\n\nOh. "Bittersweet." Now I understand.
There was nothing I could do. <<1>> chose to confront <<2>>.\n\nBut I feel as though I should have done something.
I warned her. You heard me warn her. But did Zeira listen? Of course not! She never listened to anything I told her.
I wouldn't want to be the guildmaster. They don't seem to last very long.

Repairs to the Rowdy Guar are coming along nicely. The captain even complimented the way I placed the new planks. She said she's never seen anyone lay boards the way I do. Once my dungeon-delving days are behind me, maybe carpentry can pay the bills.

Just between us, the bank's ledgers are a total mess. Poorly organized, missing entries, handwriting I can't decipher—it makes me itchy just thinking about it!\n\nIt's good you convinced them to hire me. I'll have these accounts balanced in no time!
That was a harrowing fight, I am sure. I only wish I could have been here.
May the power of Akatosh surround you in these troubling times.
Move along. The castle has been closed by command of the Count of Kvatch and the Order of the Hour.
I have the gold required for payment, but I wanted to offer you something more. I can tell you who's been murdering your assassins.

Word of advice. Urges aside, the Dark Brotherhood prefers to keep a low profile. Just remember—kill an innocent, get noticed.\n\nMy sources say they're recruiting in Anvil, on the Gold Coast. I'll be at the docks there if you want to talk some more.
Go and look at the Litany of Blood. If you see nothing, then you aren't the one I supposed you to be.

It's like this whenever I arrive in a new city. Everyone wants one of my cakes. That's why they call me the Wizard of Whisking, you know.\n\nI wonder if anyone here received one of my rare cake vouchers? Those lucky netches are in for a special treat!

You could have left Zeira and kept the guild for yourself. I guess, you and her are cut from a different cloth than old Nick.\n\nSuits me fine. I'm still cleaning up the mess the last power grab made of our books.
Welcome to the guildhall, friend. Found any interesting books or scrolls? Please just place them on the desk.
Better get moving, Assassin. And in case I don't see you again, it's been a pleasure and an honor to watch you work.

Fortunata's death bodes well for the future of the Gold Coast, but our problems remain. I need to consult with the Speaker and determine how best to collect the rest of what Count Carolus owes us.\n\nIn the meantime, I'll leave you to your contracts.

An unexpected turn on your last mission. I admit, I would not have expected Count Carolus to have the will to perform the Black Sacrament. And now he owes us information as well as gold. Very interesting. We can always use both.
I'll wrap things up and get out of here. I know just the place to hide.\n\nThanks for dealing with this. You're an honest to goodness hero!
I told you to leave me alone!

Raz is thinking this spy business might not work out for the lady Elf. At the first sign of trouble, she lights herself on fire, screams at the top of her lungs, and runs in circles. \n\nRaz does not remember that technique in the handbook.

According to the notes we found, every one of the targets is a guilty liar. Except for the reference to the handsome Khajiit. That observation was extremely astute.\n\nWe still don't know who the messages were left for. Let's try to figure it out.
I bid you welcome to Kvatch, citizen. Obey our laws and respect our traditions, and we will do the same in return for you.

Razum-dar is the only reason you're still alive, Brotherhood fool. Why did I receive that pastry? Do you know how hard it is to look this good? Eat one sweetroll and I'd never fit into all this leather!\n\nIf the Brotherhood is involved, I'll ….

Raz's Wood Elf apprentice has disappeared. I've tried to reassure the cat, but my guess is that the Sweetroll Killer has started making his move.\n\nIf we're going to put a stop to this, we're going to have to move quickly.

Why did Raz give Elf apprentice a weapon? Now she's missing and the sharp blade was just lying on the floor. Naryu thinks she ran away, but Raz knows better.\n\nWhoever has Yarmia, Raz will find them. And then they will experience so much pain.

Damn the Sweetroll Killer! We were only able to get a few of his targets to safety and it's only a matter of time before he finds the rest of us.\n\nI'm beginning to really dislike this soothsaying maniac and his menacing morsels.

Raz must sadly report that we could not find all of the killer's targets. Just the ones you see here in the hostel.\n\nThe killer has struck, Raz feels it in his paws. I just hope we can keep the others safe.
Go on. Speak to your companions. I'm sure they're eager to give you their opinion.
Raz knows the risks. But letting people die when we can save them? That is not who Raz is, and Raz does not think that is who you are, either.
I can't believe you're even considering this. Did you hear how crazy she sounded?
Oh, hello. Did you need a book? There certainly are an awful lot of them, aren't there? It's a wonder anyone finds anything in this guild.
We can't talk unless Ralen Veri gives you the nod. He's around here somewhere.
Raz doesn't think he'll ever look at a sweetroll the same way again.\n\nThat makes Raz a very sad cat.

Just one kiss to a customer! But I promise something even better the next time we meet.\n\nNow if you don't mind, I don't want you to see me eat this sweetroll. And don't judge me! After everything that happened, I deserve a tasty treat!
We can'd do business unless Ralen Veri says you're worth knowing.
You stink like death, strange one. Just what are you? No, better not to tell me. If the Shadowscale trusts you, then so will I. For now.

I know you can handle yourself, but I have a feeling that the Black Dragon is leading you right where she wants you. She's treating you as easy prey.\n\nShow her that's a mistake. Find her and send her to the Void.

Artorius has turned the guardians of the Cathedral into his personal army. He already dares much, so why not threaten our home?\n\nWe need to determine our next move carefully, Assassin. The fate of the Sanctuary hangs in the balance.
You're going after the Black Dragon, aren't you? I thought I'd be worried, but I just feel … excited. You're going to end it, I just know it. You're going to make her pay.

Nothing about you says "risk" or "challenge" … especially not "punch a troll in the face while wearing a crown made from your own trousers."\n\nIf you care to prove me wrong, I can introduce you to my two best friends—gold and bragging rights.
I appreciate the help. Just keep a firm grip on those weapons, all right? Whoever or whatever killed these Shadowscales is sure to be lurking in the Cradle somewhere.
The reaper returns with the harvest!
What is your decision? We need your help.
Stay safe out there. Lots of things that want to kill you.

Thanks again for everything you've done. I'll take some time with the amulet to see if it could be of further use to us.\n\nIf you're looking for other ways to aid us, Hara might have some suggestions on where to go.
Hello. I understand you've been helping Hara study the Celestials. We're truly grateful for your aid.
It's about time! We sent a runner to Belkarth days ago!\n\nWait—you're not the reinforcements we requested, are you? Damn it.
These are dark times, and the Star-Gazers are a shadow of who we once were. But our role remains more important than ever.
The Sword-Disciples are still in thrall to the Serpent. Anything you can do to put them to rest would ease my mind.
I've heard there are atronachs tearing the land apart to the east. Rare ones, even. Unseen for centuries. I wish I could see for myself!
If you would receive knowledge, you must give knowledge in return. \n\nWhat have you brought me, Seeker?
Hermaeus Mora's shrine is in the deepest part of the archive. I have an unusual relic from the Dragontail mountains to trade for the knowledge of the Celestials. I hope it's enough.
I wish you the best in there. If one Nereid caused all of this, the power she wields will be frightening.
I hear you defeated Yamanu-ko and her apprentices. \n\nIt will take a long while for the city to get back to normal, but at least it's our city once more.

Arch-Mage Yamanu-ko is in this tower. We call it the Apex Tower. The arch-mages of Elinhir have occupied it for centuries.\n\nIt was our duty to protect the city. Instead, we leave a legacy of destruction.
Hurry. We need to channel the elemental infusions so that we can force an opening into the staff.

I thought I heard the tell-tale sounds of the living outside these doors.\n\nBe warned: the once-refreshing waters of this place run rancid with an unholy magic—a curse that grants great strength and unnatural long life, but for a price.
Go on! Hara waits upstairs.

That flesh abomination killed thousands of Yokudans as they assaulted this place. That you took it down so easily—could Zal'ik's magic be weakening?\n\nIn any case, the cloud of poison has begun to move.
My dear friend, what did you get into? This is worse than moon-sugar withdrawls.

Many believe the Nedes were barely more than barbarians, but ruins like this prove otherwise. Don't underestimate their cleverness. Look for a pattern if you can, and consider the possibility that the lock was designed to be impossible to open alone.
Strike the Lost One down. It is the only way to end this.
The Lost One waits below. Do not delay.
They're out there! Those creatures in the water! I was at the water's edge and I saw them, looking up at me from beneath the surface. Hollow, pale eyes. \n\nWe have to get out of here!
Keep an eye on those tentacle worshipers by the staircase. This one would have gutted them already had Sali'ma not intervened.
Once the Lost One falls, we will become the Mage once more. Do not delay.
There is no more time for us. You must not delay.
So it was true, then. Those crazy High Elves really were the Celestial Mage? Unbelievable!
<A blackened gem rests at the center of the orrery. Small Dwarven runes are carved across the surface of the gem.>
It's bad enough that the Celestial Warrior and Mage have been turned against us. \n\nBut what of the Thief? The legend is of the Guardians three. I wonder what happened to her?
You're making a name for yourself around here already! Good, good. Frail, old scholars like myself must rely on people of action, especially in such difficult times.

Satakal's coils surround you, friend. My remaining acolytes are much more attentive, and the Scaled Court no longer seeks to steal what is mine. We have shown the power of the one true serpent, and those who reject him suffer his fangs. \n\nThank you.
Have you rescued our guards yet? Please, get back out there and try to find them.
Lashburr can't wait to see Agganor's mounted helm! Not a head covering fit for an Iron Orc, but good to befoul.\n\nBut Lashburr has said too much. Walk away, little goat. Walk away.

It must have been gruesome work, but thanks again for dealing with the Scaled Court in Skyreach Hold. I'm sure you saved many lives.\n\nI only hope the Scaled Court doesn't return to try again. That would be disastrous.
I'm embarrassed to say it, but you did what we couldn't. For that, you have my gratitude.
I can't believe they ate our friends. What kind of monsters would do something like that? I mean, other than Iron Orcs and trolls, that is.
Better to know what happened than never know for sure, right? That's what Camaarie always said.\n\nI miss her so much.

As soon as I heal up, I'm going back out there. We've got a score to settle and I need to chop up a few dozen Iron Orcs.\n\nBut thanks for taking care of the Butcher. I'm pretty sure he'd have killed me without working up a sweat.

So that's how he did it! He was imbuing the trolls with pure nirncrux! Fusing the armor and the runes into a powerful whole!\n\nI wonder what would happen if one of the mortal races was subjected to the process?
None of these deaths would have been necessary if the Serpent hadn't lied to me.

Blessings of the Divines upon you. I will not forget the selfless aid you have given today—and at no small risk to yourself. \n\nShould the time come when that dread creature stirs again, we will be ready. Until then, safe journey to you.
Not now! I want to watch this.
I sense Cassipia's presence, but I do not see her. Be on your guard.

I'm impressed. You demonstrated a willingness to risk everything for the sake of others. You even helped someone you once called an enemy.\n\nMaybe this world isn't as irredeemable as I imagined. Thank you for helping me correct this terrible mistake.

I have the faintest sense that the Warrior is nearby, but I can't see his face or hear his voice. What's happening to me?\n\nWill my skills disappear along with my memories? Has the Warrior truly abandoned me? Bah! Leave me to my grief!

I knew I could count on you. I last saw Titus in the north, searching for his wife's grave.\n\nAs his mind slips away, he fights to hold onto it. It pains him to accept that all he knew is dead and gone, yet he strives to keep the memories alive.
If only my parents were here …. Do you see mother? There's nothing your Sun-in-Shadow cannot achieve!
Oh, excellent. Another clumsy adventurer bumbles into my home. I really must put a hex on that lift ….\n\nHave you come to rob me? That would go very poorly for you.

Lord Vivec protect me! That was Azura, the Queen of the Night Sky! And you—she spoke directly to you, outlander!\n\nI'm surprised the Daedric Prince would risk Lord Vivec's wrath to proclaim a prophecy, but she did say you were here to aid us.
Impressive! You're just what I need to pull my plan together.\n\nMost of the slavers are currently out on a raid. That means it's the perfect opportunity for us to make our escape.
Welcome back! Did you enjoy your journey to the island of Betnikh?
Please, do what Naryu asks. The hist sent her to save us from this terrible place. I can feel it in my scales!
I should move on. I have other overseers to frustrate.

The Order of the Eye could use your assistance. Daedric relics, cursed by Sheogorath, have begun to appear throughout the lands. Do you dare defy the Mad God and recover one such relic?\n\nIf you aren't too busy, of course.

Foreman Nox is somewhere in Balmora. Should be simple enough to pluck the key from his pockets. Or, if you prefer burglary, you could take my brother's key from the desk in his study. Our manor is just up the hill, to the west of town.

I don't think we've met, comrade. I handle all special contracts involving the Worm Cult. Dark Anchors are everybody's problem, no matter your political leanings.\n\nI have an available contract, if you'd like a taste of real Fighters Guild work.
By Shor's shiny arse, if you aren't a robber and you don't work for the witch, then you have to help me! I can't move so much as a muscle and my nose itches like a flea-bitten dog!
Approach the chests when you are ready to pick their locks.\n\nYou must be quick as Rajhin! This one shall judge your efforts.
Hmph. It's you. You made yourself perfectly clear the first time. There's nothing you can say that'll stop me from being with Tirwin.
Pardon the mess, my slaves require another lesson concerning their work ethic. And their no-good overseer as well. \n\nI suppose I'll have to wield the lash myself today.
Praise Vivec! You certainly look more competent than that half-naked Nord with a thirst for foul mead.
I won't marry Llonas, not for anything.\n\nPlease, just bring me my Servitude Obligation so I never have to see his face again.
There is no shame in failing to light the fires. It reveals just how fast Zoreh had to move.
May your grace be noted by Mara herself. Your donation shall help feed the orphans.\n\nYou are of course welcome to cull the wildlife, should you desire to aid us further.

I'll stay with Lord Vivec. Do what I can to help him and alleviate his suffering.\n\nSome might consider it heresy to seek assistance from a Daedric Prince, but if it restores Lord Vivec then it can't be too wrong.
So many fish to scale, such wonderful smells. None shall go hungry tonight.

You've proven yourself willing to help those in need, even without the promise of compensation. I hesitate to ask more of you, but just between us, I can see that these events have shaken Mistress Dratha. She could use your help.
Good, you're back. I'm almost out of meat. What did you bring?

Good on you for doing this, mate. Khartag's an idiot, but he doesn't deserve what the Camonna Tong will do to him.\n\nLike I said, he went in with some slaves. Mabkir, Jaree-Eeto, and Wih-Waska. You should drag them out too.

There you are! I'm glad you're back. I just had a fruitful conversation with our friend Arith. Seems that I'm not the only one Ralasa's holding back.\n\nI think it might be time for a less conventional strategy.
Go on then. Stop Nerandas and find a sample of that toxin! I'll make my way out of here while you're providing a distraction.
I will follow you soon, friend. I just need to make sure that Sun-in-Shadow remains safe.
Do hurry to the ruin. Vivec only knows what mischief that boy's fallen into.
A visitor? Oh, I envy you, sera. I've not seen a city in months! All this peace and quiet is driving me mad.
Sweet Almalexia, another explorer, not a daedra

Ah. True to your word. I knew I could trust you. \n\nI led the Iron Hounds on a merry chase, but I doubt they'll stay scattered for long. What of your search? Did you find any evidence of Hlaren's corruption?
There you are! Any luck finding the lichen? We'll need to be quick if we want full potency.
Did you just …? Is Overseer Torvayn really dead?
I saw you strike down Overseer Torvayn. Well fought, friend. If ever an Elf had it coming, it was Torvayn.
Farwen does not stand with you, yet her ward is active. Is this yet another secret of her faith?
These Ashlanders are fools. Stuck in their primitive fictions. Galgalah and his curse are supposed to scare me? Hah!\n\nWait, who are you? Why are you speaking to me?
Ha! Well, I'll be a skeever's drunk auntie! Did you really cut down Overseer Torvayn? Certainly won't miss that horse's arse.
Oh, a Khajiit! And a furry one too. How … delightful.\n\nI suppose you've come for a consultation. What is it? Unsightly tail warts? Poor eyesight? a dull coat, perhaps?

Well done. Hm. I envy your youth. I might have found some way to rob or deceive a weakened benefactor, but not you. It's just on to the next adventure.\n\nVibrance and integrity. What a curious combination.

We caught these three trying to slip away. Should have seen their faces!\n\nIt's a big risk arresting Suran's most powerful landowners. I'm hoping you've got the evidence to make it worthwhile. Where's Marshal Hlaren?
Was there something you didn't understand?\n\nMake for the shrines of Molag Bal. Retrieve the Stones of Cold Fire, one each from the seven shrines. Do this, and we just may save Dratha's life.
I do hope Constable Mirel is all right. He's a reliable customer and I do appreciate reliability.\n\nStill, he never could handle his sword. Unfortunate business.
Move along, now. Wouldn't want anyone to arrest you.

It's good to see you again, my friend.

Forgive me for not rising to greet you. It is a beautiful day in Suran, and I believe I'll sit for a bit longer. A few months, perhaps?

I jest, of course. Today's victory was worth a few broken bones.

Hmm. You look familiar. Let me think. The cave full of nereids? The incident with Morella the Cruel and the Mephala cultists? No, no. I remember. The draugr incident! We helped the Orcs out of a jam, as I recall.\n\nWhat brings you down here, friend?
Good luck with your dung-pile sing-along. If you develop some common sense, I'll be here.
I don't know what we would have done without you. To Sovngarde with House Redoran! We'll make this mine the envy of Vvardenfell without their help.

Thank you for rushing to my aid, stranger. Fortunately, the Scarlet Judge had it well in hand. I'd hate it if you were injured on my account.\n\nYou should take a moment to speak to the Judge. You probably have a lot in common.
I'm certain the Scarlet Judge can handle things from here. Please, accept our gratitude.

I wonder what other delicacies the Dark Elves make? You'd think that after all these years at the side of the great Narsis Dren I would know more about his culture. I suppose he's more interested in the ancient past than in talking about the present.

You'll check on Narsis? How sweet! I will make certain you get a mention in his next book.\n\nI suppose he just lost track of time studying an intriguing relic or some such, but I'll feel so much better if you go into Dreloth and see if he's all right.

As a god weakens, so too does his city suffer. I know my people grow fearful. Even the Archcanon is distressed. But the energy that remains to me holds the moonlet in the sky—at least for now.\n\nSo, what news does my eyes and ears bring to me?
Don't crowd me. You can admire the view from afar.

We need to stop Chodala, and to do that, we need to find a way to overcome the device he's wielding.\n\nFind Barilzar and make sure that crazy mage provides you with something we can use to save Lord Vivec.

I see you've got the Blessing Stone. Look, I appreciate that you were able to aid my workers. And I understand that Lord Vivec has need of the stone. But I won't feel comfortable starting construction again until it's back in place.
What a stroke of luck! You're a warrior, yes? Of course you are. I need your help, sera. All is not well in Matus-Akin.
Your stench is proof enough of your deeds. Was this Ruddy Man a worthy foe?
If this Ashlander is a friend of yours, do the friendly thing and tell him to go away.
You are kind to check up on Halinjirr, but this one is fine. Again, thank you.
So you've agreed to help Halinjirr destroy his crop? I'm not sure whether to be heartbroken or elated. Just be safe, all right? This task is more important than you know.
I think you've seen all that Seyda Neen has to offer, outlander. I suggest you go and visit another of our fine cities.
You shouldn't have any difficulty finding the egg-heaps. Just look for giant piles of hardened mud and feces. Did I mention that feces would be involved? No? Well, there will be feces. Loads of it.
You look thirsty! Find a seat and I'll be around shortly to take your order.
Be careful in there. I'd hate to see you turned into a guar or something by those vile cultists!

How nice! You made it! I appreciate someone who knows how to keep an appointment and follow directions!\n\nAlmost as much as I appreciate Narsis Dren! He is inside now, probably discovering something remarkable again!

As a famous author and explorer, I constantly receive invitations to events such as this. Normally, I send my regrets, but Lord Vivec and I go way back. It would have been rude not to attend.\n\nBesides, it will make a good afterword for my book.

Interesting. Summoned by a Daedric Prince and her mortal mouthpiece. I was right in the middle of a crucial experiment, but I suppose I can spare a few clicks of the cogs for Azura and my erstwhile assistant.\n\nSo, did you break the tonal inverter?

I knew something was wrong as soon as I approached the palace! I could feel it in my bones.\n\nI was on my way here when Azura showed me a vision. I saw Sunna'rah, killing Vivec. Even without Chodala, that damn staff is dangerous!
Don't hurt me! Please!
Honestly. You brought the formula back only to destroy it in front of my eyes?
You're back. Just in time, too. The Ashlanders' mood has soured since you set out. I'm not sure how much longer I can linger here.\n\nTell me, did you find anything in the tomb?

If you seek further guidance, or wish to know more about the significance of these offerings, you should speak with members of each tribe. Approach them with the same respect you have shown me and you will not be treated unfairly.
Sadly, I see nothing else of interest. We should leave these ruins, assistant.

You made it! Lord Thanlen ushered us out of the camps so fast we almost didn't get supplies. Bastard threatened to pull our contract if we didn't hurry up.\n\nLuckily, this case seems fairly standard—just some mad spirits we need to put to rest.
Empty-handed again. At least we're alive.

You surprise me, outsider. All here assembled say you are both brave and courteous. A hero worthy of praise. Yet I still sense a hidden motive.\n\nYou showed us respect, so I will do the same by asking you directly—what really brings you to Ald'ruhn?
Kyne be praised, I wasn't sure I'd see the end of these cursed wilds!\n\nPlease, you have to help the others! These beasts torched our homes and dragged us to this place to slave and die.

It feels strange to talk to an outlander in such a sacred place, but the Queen of the Night Sky insists. I need to render judgment on an important claim, and she says you can help me reach the correct decision.
Falkreath endures another day. We'll honor your deeds here for years to come. You are always welcome in this hold.
Were you confused as to your purpose in this endeavor?\n\nStop that incessant machine's prattling.
Llayne will be glad to have your help. Most citizens support her effort to get rid of Savarak, but it's just too dangerous for common folk to speak up.
Your ambitious Argonian friend is actually quite clever. Pity I'll have to pay her now, for any work she does, but she is quite thorough and careful, when helping with magic tasks.

You look like the traveling sort. In your excursions, have you perchance come upon a young Dark Elf named Veya?\n\nShe went missing a couple of weeks ago and her father desperately seeks any information regarding her whereabouts.
I'm surprised to see you back here, but I'm also relieved. Does this mean you have news about my daughter? Is she safe? Is she ready to come home?
This one has said everything he's going to say. Now leave Renaku alone!
Be wary. I saw shapes in the ash. Robed figures. \n\nThat's not the blood loss talking … I don't think.
Not now, outlander. If you need some sort of assistance, go find one of the House Guard.

It's done? Thank you, sera. Not many people would take a life for their friends. At least I hope we're friends. The House … it makes it difficult to tell sometimes.\n\nArith and I spoke just moments ago. Things should move quickly.
A vacation! I don't think Shiralas has taken time off since we got married!\n\nI hear Seyda Neen is beautiful this time of year. Maybe we can take a cruise up the coast ….
Why are you still here, bothering me, n'wah?
This one heard you arguing with that foul-mouthed Dark Elf. Kizmar can help.
Ugh. What's that I smell? Grease and kwama dung? Let's make this quick, n'wah. I won't have you soiling my rugs any longer than necessary.\n\nThe prism. Do you have it?
Tell me you're here about my request. I can't afford to waste another minute.
I hate the city. So much damned noise! How am I supposed to get any writing done with people like you coming and going at all hours?
If you need food or drink, this one can summon a server. Otherwise, Zashanti has a floor to sweep.
No time to talk. Waiting for someone. You know how it is.\n\nJust be careful out there. I haven't seen Red Mountain this active in a long, long time.
I've no time for idle chit-chat. Be about your business.
I thought I made it clear that I have no interest in speaking to beasts. Now, tuck your tail and leave me be.

Remarkable! No ordinator or armiger could have done any better! You uncovered a Daedric spy in our midst, brought a Living God back from the brink of death, and saved all of Vvardenfell.\n\nWell done, my friend!
I sense you know of our plight. Have you come here to help my tribe?
I had that situation under control. Just needed them to make the first hostile move.\n\nStill, I cleaned enough blood off my axes for one day, so thanks for lending a hand.
I thank you for your aid. Fewer than ever are willing to aid their elders in these troubled times, though I suppose the distance with my children is my fault, not theirs.
Don't waste time. Do whatever it is Gothren wants you to do. Please!
If only I'd come sooner ….
Are you here about our little … pest problem?
You must be here about the job notice I posted. Wonderful! I really can't afford to lose more specimens.
I said I'll be along soon! You needn't hover over me.
Have we met before? No matter. I believe you're here about the job I posted.
Are you here about the job I posted? I doubt you'll want to go through with it once you hear the details.
You retrieved the journal, yes? Give it to me.
You're back already? What are you doing out here? We'll never get the crystal … er, prism out without those parts!\n\nOtheri could be back any minute. You've got to hurry!

You're obviously not one of the Malacath cultists, so I have one question—why the tusk are you following me and why shouldn't I just kill you and be done with it?\n\nYes, that was two questions. And an Orc curse. And a threat. It's been a long day.
Did I mention how much I hate being a messenger? Makes me wish I had a writ so I could kill something.\n\nAnyway, Naryu wants to talk to you. Said you'd know what it was all about.
Go on. Let's see what message Ulran left for us to find.
Someone attacked the governor. This guard will live. Did you find anything important on Firemoth Island?
If there's nothing else, some of us have guard duty to get back to. Wouldn't want anyone to steal the lighthouse's signal fire again.
Would you be so kind as to move along? You're disrupting the current.
Ah, our special customer! Is there something I can do for you?
I … I can't believe what just happened. That filthy Elf was going to kill me! A Telvanni mage!\n\nAnd Eoki sought to drag me off like a prisoner! How could he do such a thing? Has he lost his mind?

You honor the Urshilaku with your enthusiasm, but we need time to study and preserve the last relics you brought us.\n\nFeel free to rest in our camp for as long as you like. On the morrow, we'll find another shrine to explore.
Study the gap in the model and go to that location in Vvardenfell. If the lost Library of Andule still exists, that's where we'll find it!
What are you waiting for? I want to hear what my brother had to say.

You're free to do as you wish, but I suggest you let us finish this. Once the Warclaws catch the scent of their prey, they become rather singleminded. I'd hate to have to report your injury or death to Councilor Eris.

If you'll excuse me, I need some time to consider everything you told me.\n\nOnce I determine the best way to proceed, I'll contact you. In the meantime, make sure Veya stays away from Balmora and House Redoran.
See if you can find anything else and then let's get out of here. I've got a legal writ. You? Not so much.
Back again? Took your sweet time. You didn't learn anything, did you? Not that it matters. Ulran's dead and nothing can change that.
Oh! You are that daring matchmaker who put a smile on Jorunn's face!\n\nPerfect, I have need of a merry-maker!
Rejoice, champion. You speak now to Azura, Queen of Dusk and Dawn.
His meatiness Skald-King Jorunn recognizes your flashiness from his visit to Daggerfall. \n\nWhat other tricks do you have up your skeeves, this one wonders?

You carry an Ashen Fern, as did the hunters of old. It is a traditional offering for the First Ashkhan, who taught us how to use it to mask our scent. \n\nPlace it on the cairn if you have come to pay your respects.
Why do you linger, mortal?\n\nGo forth and destroy any Daedra you find. By the time you return with their essence, Rhea will know where to find my captured oracles.
What is that you carry? A jeweled cuttle? A worthy offering, to be sure. Place it before the cairn.
Guar bones? Most outsiders would honor Lammak with useless baubles and incense. Your gift shows wisdom. Place it before the cairn.
Truly? You threaten us with a broken weapon? Very well, outlander! Time to … wait. This is an exile's weapon? A gift?\n\nPlace it near the cairn. Slowly.
Oh! This is not a good time for a chat. Excuse me.
You must be the celebrant Ayrenn was going on about. I could certainly use some of your acclaimed good cheer.
The soldiers have to be in here. I just hope the cultists haven't killed them all yet.
I'm not sure what you and Veya are doing here, but let us out. Then we can return Veya to her father. Councilor Eris has been terribly worried since she disappeared.

The Mother Soul, talking through me! Even after the tragedy of my brother, I am blessed. But time is running out for Vivec, for Vvardenfell.\n\nYou must follow Barilzar and stop Barbas. Meanwhile, Azura has other work for me to do.

What an absolute mess! I knew an apprentice was going to be difficult, but this is ridiculous.\n\nStill, I don't want to see Veya get hurt. Let's find her before we both wind up with our names on a writ.
Seems like business is good around here. I wonder if I can get Dridyn to cut a good deal.
I'm not sure about this. It's a generous offer, but those are some big secrets to sweep under a rug.\n\nBesides, Veya isn't dead. At least not yet. She's still breathing.
The deputy governor awaits you in the governor's office. I'd hurry up. Neither of them appeared to be in a good mood.
Master Eraven is away on business. Has been for some time, in fact. I know a prowler when I see one. What do you want?

I'm going to miss having Veya around. I was kind of getting used to having an apprentice. Oh well. And I think I'm going to miss you too, hero. I hope we can do this again sometime. Well, not this exactly.\n\nYou know what I mean.
I come here to rest and repair my gear, not chit-chat with Outlanders.
You're our hired infiltrator? I suppose you'll have to do. It's good you decided to talk. The Camonna Tong aren't a group you want to tussle with before gathering your information.
Are you the "miss-informant" sent by the Temple? The more we wait, the closer those bandits get to succeeding.
Oh dear, I do hope you've come about my request. It would be awful if those kwama spread across Vvardenfell!
Now this is intriguing! Someone set up a little workshop in these ruins.
Keep away from me! I won't let you turn me over to the spiders! No, no, I'm not going to dance for those … things!
This will have to wait, sera. I need a nap. These meetings exhaust me.

Lady Laurent's tea was actually quite delicious, but the thought of listening to that spider and walking into a mysterious ruin just scares the pudding out of me!\n\nStill, if that's what my lady thinks is best ….
This is more nerve-racking than I anticipated! Which scroll do you recommend to counter this argument?
I don't suppose you'd put in a good word for me with Master Fyr, would you?
It's beyond belief that the Temple keeps me waiting. Don't they realize that it's a courtesy that I'm here?

That's the atelier behind me. Not only is this the workshop where Sotha Sil experimented with divine energy, it also houses one of the reservoirs that can be used to power the entire city—a reservoir currently filled with Vivec's energy.
Farwen … dead.\n\nShe was a little crazy with all her theories about old gods and whatnot, but I hope she's walking among them now.
The word shall go out to all the people of Vvardenfell. We shall gather at my statue on the central canton.\n\nJoin us once you've retrieved the Archcanon's Signet.
No. I won't listen. I won't listen! Leave me alone, spiders!
You look well-traveled, friend. Are you, by chance, going to Sadrith Mora? I can make it worth your while!

So my daughter did go to Naryu. I'm not surprised, and I suppose it's better than the alternative. Naryu won't let anything happen to Veya. I know that much to be true.\n\nThank you, outlander, for accomplishing more than Brivan and his soldiers.
Another adventurer looking for work?
We must adapt if we are to survive. Why can't the others see it?
A boost of energy from a Blessing Stone … how ingenious! The danger hasn't passed, but you've bought us … a little time.
The councilor has his priorities all out of sorts. The real threat lies to the south!
<<1>> can sound a bit overzealous in her sermons, but those who listen are inspired without fail.\n\nAre you also looking to receive the Blessing of the Whitestrake?
When my father was a constable, he was respected. Now marshals run roughshod over us and vigilantes make laughing stocks of us all!
I'm finally at ease now that we're free of the marshal's tyranny.
The Old Gods show us their favor by marking out where the wards should be placed with a holy glow.\n\nWe must heed them. Quickly. Possession spirits are not to be trifled with.
Don't let Gascone wriggle out of this. He has a duty and an obligation. As do I.
We should get going. Kyne knows how long I've got before my shadow comes calling for blood.
Why are you still standing here? Adeber's in danger!
Did you not hear me, shadow-weaver? My sister is coming, and when she gets here, she will make a meal of you!
Greetings, egg-kin. What can I do for a fellow child of the root? Do you have a crime to report?
We employ the most powerful scrying device in Tamriel, and all it yields is more questions. Hmm. A perfect metaphor for the scholarly life, I suppose.
What are you waiting for? Every moment we delay tempts death to snatch me away!
Is it him? Is that really my Bolin, or just what's left? Will he hate me? Will he even recognize me?\n\nI—I can't. I can't do this. I can't face him.
I will ask after your friend. In the meantime, I hope you will honor our arrangement.
Great work with that flash stone! Just milling up a new batch of powder now. Got plenty of pipes to cut by week's end. Thanks again.
I got to work on those air filters as soon as you returned. No more hacking up black phlegm … for now at least. Thanks.

There's my favorite forester! Keep this up, and Razgurug's liable to make you an honorary citizen of Slag Town! Wouldn't that be something?\n\nIf he does, you should probably keep it to yourself. We never get invited to parties.
Many thanks for that runic residue. Sturdy shoes do wonders for weary feet.\n\nOne day, we'll use these shoes to stamp out the Apostles and their unjust policies! Just you wait!
Thanks again for the satchels. Can't afford another rust-jaw outbreak. You're a true friend.
Evoker Tadari told me what you accomplished in the Shadow Cleft. You have my thanks.
Seht. Sotha Sil. Is he…?

Ah, you again. I suppose I should thank you for sparing me, for all the good it will do. That lumbering pile of scrap, Luciana, means to lock me in deep storage, I know it!\n\nJust leave me to my hand-wringing, all right?
I knew that slag-addled piece of garbage, Gascone, would turn on us eventually. We should have dealt with this decades ago.
There's nothing to be done for these poor apprentices. The inductor has drained every drop of life from their bodies.\n\nBut what of Lector Naril? He cloaks his evil in good intentions.
Is there something else I can do for you? You won't find Sherizar by standing here and talking to me.
Keep close to Snuffler. But not too close, you know? He spooks easily. And when he spooks, someone typically gets stabbed. Just a friendly warning. Good luck!
Not now. I'm in the middle of a delicate experiment.
Please leave me be. This is a crucial stage of my experiment and I simply must concentrate.
Luciana clearly hasn't lost her charming demeanor. Predictable.

The Mnemonic Planisphere welcomes you, traveler. Due to the recent attack, we are not holding memory viewings. You'll have to return at another time.\n\nHow strange. I feel a sense of gratitude towards you, though I'm not sure why.
I think we're done here, don't you? Let's get back to the surface. I'm sure Raynor's paced a hole in Varuni's floor by now.
Well done, assistant! One quick trip to the clockwork registrar and we'll be full citizens of the Brass Fortress.

Kireth looks no worse for the wear. You have my thanks. I do hope she took a thorough survey while she was down there. Just think of the discoveries to be made!\n\nBut I'm getting ahead of myself. Let's settle this miserable affair first.
Spare a few coins? I've had nothing to eat but wire and dirt. Have mercy ….
My wife gave me that canteen, you know. Lucky for you, I hate my wife.

I can't believe we were actually able to do it! The Halls of Regulation are up and running again. Our repairs won't hold forever, but I should be able to maintain function in the meanwhile.\n\nI don't think it's too much to say that I'm truly a genius.

What are you still doing down here? Varuni gave you her sponsorship, correct? You should go speak to the Clockwork Registrar. As much as it pains me to congratulate a friend of Divayth Fyr … congratulations.
Well? Do you have our shinies? Speak, spy!
Try to keep this inquiry quiet, all right? In the Clockwork City, even a small creak in the gears can draw curious eyes.
By the word, I wind the gears.\n\nPlease state your business or depart.

I convinced Sotha Sil that the congress requires yet another lecture on the sanctity of clockwork automata. He eagerly agreed. Seemed almost giddy about it. It was … unsettling.\n\nIs all in readiness?

We will speak in time. First, find Divayth Fyr. I wish for both of you to meet me at the Elegiac Replication—a memorial south of here.\n\nOur discussion should be away from prying eyes and ears … even those of my own people.

Victory! We picked the bones clean and plundered the Exarch's hoard. A proud day for the Blackfeather Court!\n\nNow, the Queen of Chaff sent an emissary requesting a parley. I have a plan to scare her off for good, but I need your help.
I'll fetch young Raynor while you collect the parts we need. Not that I need his help! Obviously.\n\nMake that last part clear to Lord Fyr if you don't mind.
Another trip into the Fundament? I would accompany you if not for Kireth. I think she needs a break from fabricant-infested sewers.
Taking Neramo down into the Fundament, eh? Keep a close eye on him. You and I both know how dangerous that place can be.

I never would have been able to concoct any of these wonderful dishes without you, and you've clearly got an appreciation for food, so I've conjured up a unique recipe to help you through your time in Clockwork City.\n\nI hope you enjoy it.

If you're looking to barter, you're out of luck.\n\nI traded most of my salvage to <<1>> for firepot oil. Turns out, it's not firepot oil at all. He just skimmed residue off one of the water tanks and dyed it with boot polish. He swindled me!
Na'jhargo will not stand for slander. Duldresi needs to learn to do business rather than blaming me for her mistakes.\n\nNow, do you wish to barter in good faith? If not, off with you!
Bren says those fabricants are tender, but so's a peach until you hit the pit.
Good to see a fellow Undaunted. Normally I'd say "wait your turn," but these necromancers are up to something big.
You're quite skilled at delving. The Undaunted would be lucky to have you, if you're going to make a habit of it.

I would have done it all again, even knowing it would end like this. I'm so proud to have fought by your side. I just wish that I could share this tale, share all that we've been through. \n\nStill, I count myself lucky to have you as a friend.
I have deactivated the gate. Please proceed to the throne room.
You look haggard. What happened in there?
A Motionless Guardian. Hope you remembered to stretch.
Go to Amili. Perhaps you will help her find the answer she seeks.
We've finally done it! We gathered all the parts the Precursor needs to fully regain functionality. Oh, what a gleaming day for innovation.
May my labors please the Clockwork God.\n\nWelcome back, resident. Your permissions remain active. What do you require?
Is there anything else I can help you with, apostle?
You have my gratitude. I won't forget what you did for me.\n\nAnd if I happen to get caught by those creatures again on my next foray into the Shadow Cleft, perhaps you can do it again?
Please, unless you have gold to spare or something other than paste to eat, just leave me alone.

What I said to Raynor was pretty harsh, but he can be so infuriating!\n\nLook, he might be a brilliant artificer. Unfortunately, he's a terrible dungeon delver. Without me, he's going to get lost or hurt. Just don't mention me when you see him.

So much information to parse and consider! Then we need to decide what to do with it all!\n\nA scholarly paper? A series of lectures held at Mages Guildhalls across Tamriel? A request for funding for further research from the University of Gwylim?

That Shadow Cleft portal is the first indication this one has had that there may be a way to escape this mechanical monstrosity.\n\nAs soon as Tadari recovers from her last ordeal, she will go back in there and figure out its secrets.
Well met!\n\nCan you believe it? Both of us, helping the apostles make Clockwork City a better place. I couldn't have asked for anything better.

Interesting. The Prognosticator doesn't have a prophecy for you. More proof that it uses what it knows to make calculated guesses.\n\nBut it predicted doom and gloom for me. Now I can change my future and show everyone that our fate isn't fixed.

When I asked you to help Kamid, this wasn't exactly what I had in mind.\n\nI want to see our people abandon the reckless pilgrimage to the Grand Prognosticator, but going after the treasure is just as dangerous—maybe even more so!
That creature—it's even worse than Palbatan told us! Look, I appreciate all the help, but I don't want to see you die on my behalf.\n\nAre you sure you can deal with that beast?

I've called a few people together so I can tell them what we've done. Hopefully, word will then spread throughout Slag Town and all of the Brass Fortress.\n\nPalbatan and I talked about my mother. We don't think she sought a prediction from the oracle.

Kamid changed his fortune, thanks to you. And not just that, he'll show us all that we shouldn't limit ourselves to the enigmatic ramblings of an out-dated machine.\n\nThis is better than I had hoped!
Such sounds of pain, anger, and suffering. I'm glad that they have finally fallen silent.
If you're looking for a handout, keep looking. I have a hard enough time keeping this mangy dog fed.
I'm warning you, don't even think you can hassle me just because I'm an apostle—.\n\nWait a minute. Where did you find that brassilisk?
Well met, traveler! What brings you out to Fell's Run?
That sickly sweet smell, it reminds Tubabi of Skooma … not that this one would know anything about that.

I don't think I've ever seen Brengolin heave up his own makings. Wonder if its because he's only tasting a tiny bit, or maybe being raised here gave him brass guts.\n\nOh no. Maybe he's really a fabricant!
Did the pretty Psijic say … Sea Sload? No, Raz must have heard wrong. That could not have been what she said.
Not that I was overly concerned, but I see you were able to retrieve the Oracle. Care to tell me what happened?
Now just … destroy the … center fulcrum ….
I look at my former self and see only a cocoon from which I have emerged.
I'm sorry, cerum, but I have no time for petitions or solicitations today. I have important work to get back to. Perhaps you can talk to my cousin. She's the canonreeve of our fair city.
That young woman was certainly in a hurry. And what was that about Nedoril and an attack?

The answer to where I hid the Heart of Transparent Law resides in the Dreaming Cave. Or, more precisely, through the portal I opened and once traversed. Therein lies the problem.\n\nIt's best if I showed you. Meet me in the cave beneath this tower.

What a rare honor Valsirenn bestowed upon you. Only a select few not of our order have ever walked upon this sacred island.\n\nVal tells me your aid was indispensable in uncovering the false Aldarch's plot on Summerset.
Away, newcomer! This is official business of the Divine Prosecution. Defacing Altmer property is a capital offense!

This business with Haladan disturbs me greatly.\n\nWhile I'm loathe to admit it, the Sapiarchs are not without fault here. We will endeavor to keep a closer eye on our younger members from now on. I encourage the Mages Guild to do the same.

I know Calawende plans to make Emile's imprisonment as pleasant as possible, but it's still prison. Emile has so much more to offer the world!\n\nWhat's more important—a good man's life or a dead mer's reputation? Hardly seems like a choice to me.

I trusted you to investigate this matter, and I've made my recommendation. Truthfully, I am too close to both Emile and the Mages Guild to approach this choice objectively.\n\nUltimately, I leave the decision in your hands. I do not envy you.
If you found something at that cave, just keep it to yourself. Less I know, the better. No offense, but I may be in too deep already.\n\nEven so, I hope you find the truth.
Emile? Is that you? Where is Haladan? Is he all right?
Such a tragedy. Raz hopes these wounds don't scar Sadara too badly. She has such a kind and gentle soul.

There's nothing to consider. Even if I didn't kill Haladan, the vampirism was my idea! He never would have agreed to it if I hadn't pushed him!\n\nHaladan meant more to me than you'll ever know. His memory is all I have left. Don't ruin it. Please.
K'Tora compelled me to steal the Heart of Transparent Law from the Crystal Tower and hide it … somewhere. I must remember where I hid it before Summerset falls.
I suppose I'll be off to Rellenthil. You, too, I imagine.\n\nIn the meantime, I believe the Ritemaster wishes to speak to you.
This is terrible! The Ritemaster and the Conclave of the Eleven Forces were hoping to learn more from the abyssal pearl, but then the pearl vanished!
The Golden Knight! We need to get him down from there!
