Well, this is awkward. You're probably wondering how your old friend Darien became Meridia's champion and got stuck in all this sticky webbing. It's a funny story, really.\n\nProbably better if I wait to tell it until after we escape from this realm.
Once the Dawnbreaker has been restored, we can see what waits on the other side of that barrier.
She vanished! Of all the luck! Where did she go?

Come to gloat over my misfortune? Or does Alchemy simply want to make sure I leave town?\n\nNo matter. Neither of you need worry about me any longer. My brother wants nothing to do with me, and I'll respect that. I depart for Lillandril today.
Please find Rinyde so that I can tell her everything. I'll explain why we must part, and ensure she follows her dream. Just as I must follow mine.

These animals aren't native to this cavern. They were brought here, but why?\n\nI've heard of sentimental necromancers reanimating pets and loved ones, but this seems more like a display … or a study.
Back to practicing, my friend! Never enough time to practice when so much is at stake.
Now now, off you go. We'll have plenty of time to conspire in the days ahead. And if you want to ask me any more questions, gorgeous, you'll have to get a few more drinks in me first!
Your rhythm could use refinement, but I salute your determination. May the best performer join the House of Reveries and become a great name!\n\nAnd now, to my question. Who trained you?
Damn that toad, Talerion! Don't let him take my boy!
So? Can you guess who I am?

Funny. I thought you were in a rush.\n\nYou can linger here as long as you like. Just don't bring any of that kinlord hypocrisy with you. I live down here for a reason, you know. Oh, and leave the rats be. They're particular about company.
In you go.\n\nJust have a care where you step. If the rumors are true, the Mother of Rats doesn't care for outsiders stepping on her little scurrying servants.
I know it doesn't look like it, but I'm working. So … jog on.
What's the hold up? We need to get back to Mother's Den before Mirulon's thugs run us through!
Have you come for another look at nameless sorrow? Look, then ….

Thanks for stopping that Daedra-loving looney from sucking out my soul. You took a big risk sticking your neck out for us … but what are recent acquaintances for, right?\n\nGuess I owe Lin too. Not going to live that down.
What are you waiting for? Get in there!

So you're really going to look into this, yes? Y'ffre's bones, if you adventurers aren't a peculiar bunch.\n\nI've got no orders to keep you out. Not many grave robbers dumb enough to loot this place. No offense. Anyway … it's been nice knowing you?
Ugh … my brain feels like it's been pushed through a sausage maker.

I'll try to think of an apology for Silurie. It's been some time since I've chased danger like this. Of course, it's also been some time since I've seen my own blood, so—ups and downs.\n\nGo on now. I'm not getting less wounded.
Thank you for saving me, friend. Ugh. I think I've had my fill of drama for a while. Time to curl up with a nice, boring cookbook.
We finally made it to the temple! Oh, I just can't wait to see what secrets are inside.
What is she still doing here?
Am I really in Aetherius? I didn't know they let your kind in here.

What luck! To find a fellow troublemaker on this stiff-necked isle.\n\nThere should be pedestals scattered throughout the ruin that will cause the Eye to activate. I'll contact you through aural projection to walk you through it.

Hope the room is to your liking. With your reputation, I'm sure you shouldn't have any trouble with the neighbors. If you do, remember, death threats are not the way to go. Had a spot of trouble when my last tenant started sending those out.

I understand that complications arose, and I thank you for overcoming them. But I simply must have those ingredients! My muse is gnashing at the bit just thinking about the masterpiece I shall create!

I don't care if you create a masterpiece with that bloom. It will never replace the natural beauty that's been lost here today.\n\nFirst that Vaerelel fellow, now you. Will I ever not be plagued by greedy artists?

I never expected to see you again, but you shouldn't have come here. These words of power, they aren't meant for mortal eyes.\n\nI'm an earl in the Court of Bedlam now. So believe me when I say that Leythen isn't being totally honest with you.
I trust your search was as fruitless as mine.
If you've come to rob me, I'm afraid I have little of value. I can help if you've a high fever or nervous stomach, but I have no need for gold these days.

Always a pleasure to do business with those who recognize true talent. If you see Tindoria, tell her I really do wish to send an invitation for dinner one of these days. It's only fair she gets to see the inside of the palace.
The moment of truth. I will accept whatever you choose to tell Farwenya.
The Ritemaster sent me to find you. He said he's recovered another memory.
There wasn't a shred of hesitation in Tenerive's eyes. He went to his grave hating me with every fiber of his being.

With every step along this path, my memory grew clearer. This portal, it leads to where I had my fateful meeting with Nocturnal. Where she offered to aid me in my struggle against the Sea Sload K'Tora.
Talk to the Ritemaster. Find out if he knows what we should do next.
I feel one of those momentous occasions coming on. You know, the ones where we do something amazing and save the day, or we die horribly in a blaze of glory. Yeah, one of those.
You've accused a decorated officer of treason. I sincerely hope you have some sort of proof to back up your claim.
Don't … don't worry about me. Find Soravil …. Go!
Ah. The Augur. Excellent! Place it inside, please. I assure you, it will be quite safe here.
I've said enough already. If you're finished here, please, just leave us in peace. And if you see my boy, tell him to come home.

How unusual. The Psijics know better than to disturb me in my private study. And the Ritemaster has kept me waiting for an inordinate amount of time.\n\nThat leads me to a single conclusion—the Ritemaster has not returned from the Dreaming Cave.
I was too slow. Damned Mer slipped right past me. Tall for a Wood Elf, and quick as a spooked hare.\n\nSo it really is the chief's son ….

I'm sorry to ask this of you, but we must give Ila and Lodiss a chance to come up from those broken stairs. You'll need to defeat the creatures that are guarding the temple's entrance.\n\nGood luck, my friend. Stay vigilant.
This doesn't make any sense! What happened to the Ritemaster?
Trust me. Just talk to Leythen and let him explain what he's thinking. He's actually not that bad a person … for an evil, power-hungry cultist, that is.

If you want to return me to Artaeum, I won't resist you.\n\nBut first, I need to find out if the rest of Mephala's followers are safe. Let me learn their fate and then I'll submit myself to your mercy.

Making alliances with the very same Princes who tried so hard to kill us? Oh how far the order has fallen since the death of Ritemaster Iachesis.\n\nBut I fear the deals will prove worthless without a way to attune the Resolute Diamonds.
I suppose I could answer some questions. Long as they're quick. I don't suspect Erilthel will make it out alive, but there's no use prolonging the news.

Raz was nearby when he heard that the Sapiarchs were up to something at the Crystal Tower. This one didn't expect the tower to start glowing. I hope this is the work of the Psijics, yes?\n\nNo. This is something worse. Raz feels it in his paws.
I can say no more. Grief's noose tightens around my throat. Find the Crimson Seal. Listen for my mournful song. I can say no more ….

Vile told me to find the mortal flea that continues to pester him and deliver a message. He's terrible with mortal names, but I immediately thought of you. Glad to see that my intuition's as sharp as ever!\n\nOh, yeah. I've got a message for you.
Go ahead. Tell Courtier Vindilween we know about the dinner party. That should get a meeting with the Proxy Queen faster than a torchbug diving for the spilled mead!
Back again? You and that Nord are worse than a plague of fellrunners in a field of swamp nettles.\n\nWhat do you want this time?

Something else? We can discuss the letter of recommendation for Ambassador Rigurt after you have acquired the mementos of cultural significance from the newcomers Urjurra, Ondare, and Grayscale.\n\nI shall await your quick return.

Thanks to Ambassador Rigurt, I feel like a proper Nord battle maiden now! I suppose I smell like one, too. Isn't it exciting?\n\nTake the tickets and use them well. I expect it will be my best performance ever!
I see you haven't had any better luck tracking down those bandits than the Divine Prosecution. Well, if you want that writ, you'll just have to try a little harder.

Thank you for accepting my offer. I'd travel to the hulkynd myself, but the wilderness is no place for an artist. Besides, they may be more willing to talk to a newcomer such as yourself. The hulkynd are well known for being distrustful.

We have a deal. You'll collect the heart, and I'll meet with Tableau.\n\nCur will lead you straight to the indrik. I've already given her the scent, so it's as simple as following behind. And then killing the beast, of course.
I don't think the Queen will mind Talomar taking Lotus away from this place. She couldn't have a better caretaker.

I know Tableau will regret giving up her life as an artist, especially for one such as myself. I couldn't bare it if she ended up hating me for it.\n\nLet me end it now, before she makes this mistake.
Come on, just a little more prodding. I'm sure Manacar wishes to stay by my side. You just have to help him see reason.
What are you? Some sort of saint sent to deliver me from digging through Malooc's squalor? \n\nWell, two searchers are better than one. Meet me back here when you've found something.
There's not much time left before I present to the Illumination Academy. I have my work cut out for me ….

We grow accustomed to the influx of visitors to our Blessed Isle, though your increasing numbers remain a source of concern to our nobles. We, however, find the many non-Altmer faces to be … interesting.\n\nWhat business brings you to the palace?

The College of Sapiarchs is extremely grateful for your help with that terrible invasion business. And for saving Sapiarch Larnatille. I'm not sure what we'd do without her!\n\nAnyway, feel free to use the portal dais whenever you want.
There's more to this than a simple Daedric incursion. I felt a strange sensation when we arrived. A sense of urgency.\n\nWe need to hurry and find the trapped Sapiarchs.
The Royal Menagerie is closed to the public at the moment. What are you doing here?
You and your companion arrived in the proverbial nick of time. Now if you wouldn't mind, who in Oblivion are you and how did you know the College of Sapiarchs was under assault?
You there! Tell my darling wife to release me and I'll ask Mephala to kill you quickly when the new age dawns.
I never trusted Nocturnal's earl. A Dark Elf, in the Court of Bedlam? It was unprecedented!\n\nHer daggers are as sharp as her temper, so we must tread carefully here.
Look what they did to Dawnbreaker! It's all dark and gloomy now! It was a weapon of pure light and they corrupted it!
Those appear to be the correct volumes. Now let's find the podiums we need to set them upon.

Heed Mephala's advice and keep your companions close to the diamond. Without it, you would be lost in the darkness between realities.\n\nNow, recover the Heart and restore Transparent Law. Just remember, you must find a relic imbued with divine energy.

What, are you here to kill me? Might as well. There's no honor left for me now. Not after I decided to send my squad off to certain death. \n\nI've failed them as their captain. I've failed all of Summerset.
Sorry, stranger. My friend can't see too well anymore. She mistook you for someone we've been looking for. Things have been rough, lately.
Once Eslion is gone, I'll finally be able to begin the long process of restoring the beauty of these lands.
I'll be so glad to have this mess behind me. My brother's going to get a real kick out of it. Right in the backside, if I can help it.
For a place with such a terrible reputation, this estate certainly gets a lot of trespassers.\n\nYou're not another layabout squatting on my land, are you?

What a positively pointless reason for Niralin to die. If only she'd been reasonable.\n\nI'll make sure her family receives her ring, though I don't believe I'll be sharing the full details of this escapade. No need to grieve them further.
Don't worry about me. The pack won't attack one of their own. I just don't want to rouse suspicion by being seen together. Best if I sneak out alone.\n\nI'll meet you in Shimmerene.
Find the Redguard named Miriya. I sense her somewhere deep within the ruins.
All this crouching is damnation on my back, but I've seen everything I need to know what the enemy's up to. How fares the search? Any sign of Cartorrel?
Can't say I care for the naturalized aesthetic. Keep your eyes out for anything that may have survived the elements.

The fleet set off west. Wasten Coraldale is an island engulfed by coral reefs, but you can reach it safely in that sailboat.\n\nI'd go with you, but I'm afraid I don't share my father's comfort with open water.
Taking down that giant was impressive, I'll admit. Just don't get too cocky on me. I already get more than enough sass from Lodiss.
Huh? Need something?

Even after being gone so long, I could never forget this place. I can still hear the sounds of my little girl's laugh as she climbed this tree, giggling and shouting at Val and I to watch her.\n\nIt's a memory I'll forever cherish.
I wish the Ritemaster were still with us. I'd feel better if he were here to help with this fight.
Razum-dar sent word that he needed to talk to you, so I took it upon myself to bring him to Artaeum.\n\nI assumed you'd want to speak to him before you go off to assault the Crystal Tower.
Your companion wishes to speak. We will wait.
I think I'll go visit my sister and niece. It's about time I reconnected with what little family I have left.\n\nBut first I'll bring Ludovic's body to his family. Try to make amends.

I'm going to finish my ale before I head to the Dreaming Cave. I mean, it could be my last drink. Even if this tastes terrible, it's still alcohol. \n\nOn second thought, maybe I'll just have some water.
Back so soon? He blew you off, didn't he? What I wouldn't give to knock that smug grin off his face ….
I heard your ridiculous challenge. We'll be along presently.
A thousand apologies, walker, but this one has much to do! You will come back again later, yes?
So, ready to watch Lirendel skewer your friend?\n\nHmm. Skewer may be too harsh a word. We're only fighting to first blood, of course. But then again, accidents do happen ….
We aren't free yet. We have to get out of here before those cave vermin come scurrying after us.

Khavid and I shall head to the merchant's district. I need to investigate the area and see where the Maormer may be holding Sunhold's nobles prisoner.\n\nMeet me there when you've completed your tasks, and we'll assess the situation.

Get into Sunhold, not even a month on the job, and what happens? Stinking sea snakes invade the place. I'm pretty sure I'm the only one in my patrol who made it out alive.\n\nAnd now I'm playing nursemaid to a Kinlady. What a day.
A newcomer? In the warehouse district? Unusual, but how can I help you today, my friend?
This portion of the tower seems more damaged than the previous sections we climbed through. Let's look around and see if we can find a way out of this library.
Why is Leythen all dark and glowy? He didn't stay close to the anchor, did he?
Go and tell Oriandra of my plan. She'll know which parties to contact.\n\nI'd also like to ask Sotha Sil to join us. His support would be extremely helpful to our cause.
This was to be our last trip, you know. Then this one could retire with Nubani in peace. His days at sea were to finally come to an end.\n\nMadja has ruined everything for us.
Did Renzir send you? Nubani hopes he cared to mention his wife alongside his goods.
Finally, you arrived.\n\nWe were able to gather everyone together, but they've already started the meeting. Valsirenn tried to make them wait, but the Sapiarchs demanded to know what was happening.
Have no worries, I'm a Mer of my word. I'll begin preparations at once to decide on appropriate allies for the Crystal Tower's defenses. \n\nIt may not be a one day affair, but it shall be done.
We thank you for the aid you provided to our green and pleasant land. Newcomer, you have shown us that sometimes change is for the best.
First my husband betrays us. Then my friend and mentor dies at the hands of a Daedric Prince. This situation gets worse and worse with every passing moment.
I hate this! I was supposed to save everybody. That's what Meridia sent me here to do. I am not used to failing so spectacularly. Not used to it at all.
We must leave this cursed place.

Miriya took the marines and went south to investigate rumors of a Sea Sload near Alinor. If the vile slugs have developed a magic powerful enough to sink Summerset, then my friend may be in over her head.\n\nYou must go and help her.
Got any Orsinium ale in your pack? Wine? Maybe some mead? I'm kind of parched.
Tell me you are real, my friend, and not another mind trick sent by the vile slugs to deceive me.

And just like that, Auri-El provides.\n\nGreetings, ceruval. I am Chief Jurisreeve Tarnamir of the Divine Prosecution … or at least I was, in the long ago. I know this is unorthodox, but perhaps you'd be interested in helping us?
What the—? How did I get up here?
So good to see a fellow Altmer step forward in our time of need. You are here about the contract work, I presume?
Avast! Why do you pester me like this nosy wench? I've no use for lubber-pies!
You lay yet more burdens on an already burdened brow? I stole no pies. Now off with you, before I cast you into the dungeon!
The time has come, initiate. We must gather the final fragments of the Staff of Towers.
Please excuse me, but I'm busy at the moment. Studying this … enchanting beverage requires my strict attention.

I believe we toured the southern, northern, and central arbors. Yes, that sounds right. There should be three bottles, all with the Russafeld seal.\n\nNow, you go do that. I'm going to lie down. For just a minute.
Thank you for understanding. Hopefully I can put this whole affair behind me soon.

According to those notes, the writing is carved into a massive stone. I doubt you'd be able to carry it back here.\n\nAll right, you've piqued my interest. Use this rune when you reach Ebon Stadmont and I'll be able to see what you see.
I can feel the powerful magic that permeates this place. I sense a Daedric influence, but something that's far older than my Prince Mephala.
Miriya. She's a remarkable young woman. One of the best sword fighters I've ever seen. Please find her and free her from the mind trap.
Stranger! Don't anger the salamanders! They're the only thing keeping those Sea Elves from wandering too close.\n\nWhat are you doing out here? I've never seen you before.

Ah …! Sacred Ascendants take me home! I thought you were a Sea Elf!\n\nOne moment, I was just dipping my toes in the shallows having a pleasant day. The next, there's a murderous corsair or hungry reef viper around every corner. We're trapped!

It seems like you are caught in the middle of this whole affair. If you wish to mediate this disagreement between Vinafwe and Eslion, by all means. There are more pressing matters I need to attend to.
I look forward to hunting down the Sea Sload and introducing the foul creatures to the sharp edge of my blade!
At times, appreciating your craft requires dismantling it. Take the ring, or any other piece of jewelry, to a jewelry crafting station and deconstruct it.
We'll head to Cloudrest, soon as my companions have time to rest. I think we've got our bearings now.
This is the last time I try to pull off one of Miranrel's hair brained schemes.
I really need to start exercising more. Though you would think someone in my line of work would be used to running by now.
Oh … leaving so soon? I thought perhaps you'd like to loosen those muscles before battle, you know? I'm sure I can help you with that.
Ugh, what a disaster. It will take weeks to get the mats out of her coat.
Your patronage of my research shows exemplary moral character. You have my thanks.
Sorry, but I don't have time to chat. At least not while the Sapiarch is watching me like a hawk.

If you are to join me on this hunt, then I may just have a chance.\n\nWe'll need to take that portal down to the Hunting Grounds proper. There we can begin our search for Tarcyr … and hopefully not die along the way.
Well. I'm glad that you talked the Elf down. Because I would've used my fist to do the same job.
I am glad to know my horse is safe. Thank you for finding her.

Seems Igeke roped you in on this little adventure too. Just great.\n\nYou know, I always wanted siblings growing up. But if this is what my cousins turned out to be like? Glad I was spared the experience.

You walk in here on three skeevers arguing over a dead body, and decide you want to chat with one of them? You either got some kind of guts or you're some kind of stupid.\n\nEither way, maybe you can help.

So you've decided to join our little escapade? Well, I'd watch my back if I were you. Never know when a dagger will end up in it!\n\nBut have no fear. I'm certain I'll crack this little mystery wide open.

If you're willing to fight, so am I. \n\nZ'Maja lies within the Aerie, just beyond the gate. If we strike against the Sea Sload first, she'll summon the shadow warriors to her side. It'll be an easier battle if we take the replicas out first.

I know a few merchants headed to the city. I'm sure they'd be amenable if you ask for a ride in their cart.\n\nAnd remember, gather as many allies as you can before heading out. If Z'Maja has attacked Cloudrest, you'll need the aid.
It's time I spent some time looking over the immigration records. There may be something in her past that provides a motive for her strange vendetta.
You know what, fine! Let him take me in! I can sleep in a bed for once!
I can't leave until everyone has evacuated. Far too many are injured from the Sea Sload's attack, and I'm one of the few healers left within the city.
So. Are you ready to take your next step, initiate?
Nothing else to prepare, I guess. Time to bid this island farwell.
The time has come.\n\nRest easy. I am certain that both Josajeh and the Augur will be fine. No—they will do better than that. They will thrive.
How fortunate, that you were the only one caught in that mage's spell. I suspect there's more to this tale than meets the eye.
Raz had many plans for what he would do once Summerset was safe. Fine drink, fine food, a chance to relax.\n\nInstead he must deal with the petty squabbles of High Elves. Nothing ever changes.
I've spent so many years here, with such terrible things happening right under my nose. Maybe it is time for me to move on.
I can't believe Battlereeve Pandermalion went back in there. He sacrificed himself to save us all. I'm honored to have known him.
<A notice for a Conquest mission has been posted to the board.>
<A notice for a Conquest mission has been posted to the board.>
<Conquest mission notices and reports are posted to this board.>
Our soldier friend is not looking so good. Well, he is always looking good, of course. But still, Narazda worries that he may be ….\n\nBest not to dwell. You must focus now on defeating Moon-Caller.
Welcome back, my friend. Were you and Jee-Lar successful? Were you able to stop Margus? And what of the cursed skull? Did you see it?\n\nTell me, is the threat to Murkmire behind us now?

You must defeat Mylenne Moon-Caller if we're to move on. From what Narazda has told me, she'll likely be in the bailey, right up ahead.\n\nBe careful. That cur killed many of my companions during our initial attack.
He did not have to die. Narazda could have taught him to control it. We of the moons … we are not all like Vykosa and her ilk.
We need to keep moving, before the other hunters find that indrik.
I knew you'd be back. That is my business, after all.\n\nWere you able to acquire that elegant jacket I asked you to obtain?
Was your search successful? Were you able to find my assistant, Argar?
You're back? And how can this humble smuggler help you this time?

You are not one of her thralls? No, you do not smell like them.\n\nQuickly, you must help me! I only barely escaped her clutches, but my root-sisters and brothers were not so lucky. Every moment we delay will be measured in innocent blood.

Find the Wuju-Ka Guardian and slay it. That should weaken the source of the voriplasm long enough for me to complete the rite of binding. Then meet me at the top of the stairs.\n\nMay your branches bend but never break, my friend.

Good, good, you're here! It looks like Margus has already departed for the island, but the Blackguards are preparing to send back-up.\n\nWe need to sneak onto the expedition ship and use it to take us to Norg-Tzel.
Hey, scaleless one. I have a message for you. From Kassandra. She wants to see you in her office in Lilmoth right away.
Can you hear me? This is just …. Please, if you can hear me, make your way toward the light, or the vortex, or whatever it is you're supposed to examine.
You've given me a lot to think about. You should discuss all of this with Kassandra.
Off you go, new blood. Zadaza can only play messenger for so long, yes? This one goes too long without a decent nap.
Take care of Famia, would you? I sometimes get the feeling she doesn't really grasp the danger here.
I'll be all right. I just need to catch my breath.\n\nHurry on and find Varo. I don't want to think about what might happen to him!
Hello again. You have been enjoying a good wallow, yes? The mud here is smooth and moist.

You found something in the cavern? Sealed scrolls, I presume? Maybe a cypher ring? No, don't tell me! Famia insists we follow proper procedure.\n\nTake the items to Varo. He'll confirm their authenticity and render payment before he brings them to me.

Walk softly in the xanmeer, beeko. Our ancestors took great pains to make those places … unpleasant.\n\nHopefully I will see you and friend-Famia back in Lilmoth before long. With all your limbs intact.
You take the lead. My crew will be slow with all of this equipment and the way forward is dangerous. These ice caves aren't uninhabited.
The Dwemer took extraordinary measures to keep this from the Ayleids. The question is: why?
This is not where I imagined we'd cross paths again. It seems we've both come a long way from Volenfell, but are we after the same thing?
This tablet has lain sundered for ages, eluding everyone who sought its pieces, except me. I'm the first to see it whole in thousands of years. This is history in the making.
The brewer tells me I drank all the celebration phlegmwine. Now he asks coin for more. I would thunk his head in if this was not a bonding.\n\nFind my dowry so I can leave this place.
So, about that armor. Did you recover any from Tsofeer Cavern?

You may have scales, but you aren't one of the Naga-Kur. Remember that or trouble will find you.\n\nLook for Kishi's father, Bhoki. Tell him you want to help. Just be mindful of Mewah-Jez. Spines and scales don't make you one of the Dead-Water, ojel.
You have not succumbed to the swamp's poison lips. Was the pizzle jutting out from the short grass as I described?
Do not linger like the sickly guar that waits for the crocodile to eat it. Hurry and do the thing we spoke about.

Strange. I feel as though I am walking through a dream, one I have had many times before. Each time I am called to lead, and each time I die. \n\nI must think on this and try to hear more clearly what the Hist is telling me.

We must return to my village and go to the war-chief's pavilion. Only Raj-Kaal Seelan can grant an outsider permission to walk the Path of the Lily.\n\nJust choose your words carefully. The war-chief's ego bruises easily and he's quick to anger.
You have Etra's grave-stake? I am … impressed, ojel. Show this stake to Jaxsik-Orrn. She will read its story.
Dream well and fight well. We will be here when you wake.

I know it was a difficult decision, but you have done the right thing. Her selfish desires jeopardized the well-being of the entire tribe, and her staying here would do so again. This was the only way.
Hey there! Come to salt some buy …. er, buy some salt?
You'll find some lovely vistas just east of Windhelm. That's where I generally go when I want to get Kyne's attention.\n\nNow, be off with you. Don't want to keep the great goddess waiting, do we?
Is that … yeah, those are venom sacs all right. What a mess! You should take them to the skink nesting ground, quick. Don't want those things to dry up on you.
Haxara is stronger than she gives herself credit for, and for that child she will be stronger still. There is time, yet, to make a good life.
Go on. Drink up! Might want to hold your nose though. Friendly tip.
Oh, why the sour face? It's just a bit of fun!\n\nAnyway, that candle's pretty remarkable, right?
We won't be able to direct the Soul Gem's power without functional shock conveyors. They're common Dwemer technology, but we'll need the most pristine you can find for what I'm planning.
I knew it! I knew it was going to be for nothing. Tharayya's grasping at straws now. This is a wild goose chase.
What did you say to her? You just doubled my work load.
I wish you luck in your negotiations with Captain Jimila. \n\nPlease do not let any harm come to the vossa-satl. The deaths of all those tiny croakers would dry my scales something terribly.
Success? Do not let my lack of dancing and cheering fool you—I am very impressed. I did not think you would secure the clues we need so quickly.\n\nHow did you fare in there?
Teeba-enoo! More like teeba-e … stupid! This game's a joke! No tusk-jabs, no eye gouges! Just a bunch of rolling around and tail swinging!
Please … get Xukas and Jaxsik-Orrn, quickly. I'm only supposed to hold this for a little while. Only a little while.
You made the right decision, beeko. Thank you.\n\nSo, the ojels have learned about the Remnant of Argon. That is … frustrating.

I sigh with satisfaction. You understand the truth, ojel. A predator who spares wounded prey shows weakness. Weakness invites challenge. The Dead-Water tribe brooks no challengers.\n\nYou were useful today. Should we meet again, I will not kill you.
Begone, ojel scum! The business of the Naga-Kur is no concern of yours.\n\nLeave this place before I set my warriors upon you!

I confide a secret truth. The only reason I break tradition and allow you to walk the Path is because I know that Bhoki and his egg-son are correct. My tribe is dying.\n\nListen to Kishi and show my people that there is a better way. Now go.
Don't hurt me! I'll do whatever you say!

You're back! I … I'm getting a taste of the smoke too. Enough to see shapes—hear whispers. The Argonians you spoke to seem unlike any I've met here in Murkmire. Not Bright-Throat or Dead-Water, but a different tribe entirely!\n\nThere must be more!

Few Naga live to be as old as Bhoki. Most of our warriors die early, but not my egg-sire! He has used his wits and strength to overcome every challenge.\n\nHis lessons helped me guide you through the Path of the Lily.
You know it's not true, what Iskenaaz is saying about her. You know it. He's a coward.\n\nShe needs the Hist. It can help her.
Well, now. Looks like someone put you through a night at the alehouse in the span of a minute. Try not to choke on your own vomit before finding the Remnant.
I speak with joy and sadness. Farewell, sword-kin. Watch over Xukas for me. We will meet again, I think. Farther down the river.
The winds shift and the deciding season is upon us, Rootmender. Who will lead our tribe out of the Remnant?
We should try to reassemble the party, right? We have the sap and the blossoms—all we need now is a place to conduct the ritual.
I'll just stay out here until things settle down. If anyone asks, I'm hard at work, gathering plants for the ceremony.
You know, you don't really strike me as a member of the Blackguards. More like a hero type, in my opinion. A hero who would be only too keen on helping a poor lass in need.

I erect the spine of thanks! You'll find the first tablet in the belly of the miregaunt that lurks near the infamous Blackrose Prison.\n\nFeel free to take the book of riddles to help in your search. It does me no good.
The needed change is not always wanted, ojel. But it is always needed.
I will present these gifts to Kud-Nakal when the next bonding ritual is announced. I simply must tweak my poem, perhaps refine my carving, and all shall be ready.
I've had a long watch. I'd like to get some rest.

Hey, I know you! You borrowed a Blessing Stone from my construction site in Vivec City! And stopped the moonlet from falling out of the sky!\n\nNow I feel kind of embarrassed. My current problem isn't anywhere near as important as saving a Living God.
<<1>>! Thank the Three! I wondered where you ran off to. Did Drooler bring you to me, stranger? He's such a good boy!
<<<1>> makes a sad sound as he looks to the north.>
This one thinks the little metal rat would make a good toy for her Senche-cousin's cub. Perhaps she will take one as part of her payment.

By the Hist, did you see that? They just touched and … exploded!\n\nI-I suppose I can't be too surprised. I was the one who suggested we go to a Shadowscale in the first place. Though this is not the resolution I had in mind.
In the name of Sithis, I have brought about the needed change. That which hindered has been removed. That which must be, shall be.
I see you have returned empty handed. Were you unable to find the box I seek?
Good luck getting Paheiza to even bother attending. Or even speaking her case coherently, for that matter.
Good luck getting Nurhei to agree to come. He hasn't deigned to speak to me once since Keema-Ru died. Just uses Chuxu to relay messages.
So you've returned. Have you the hunting bow?
Have you come with the crumbling stones of our folly?
Talk to your mentor, ojel scum. The sooner you step upon the Path, the sooner you die.
The final challenge will be the most difficult one yet. Prepare yourself, friend-outsider.

Don't blame your mercy for what happened. You gave this woman a chance to lead a better life, she chose to squander that. It seems that sometimes vengeance can't be appeased.\n\nMust we be forced to use violence to prevent greater violence?
You're a long way from home, ojel. Best tread carefully if you wish to return to it.
You return. There has been no news of the Skin Taker. \n\nWhat of your hunt?

I borrowed a frog net from my friend in Lilmoth. I'm certain it'll work for catching swamp jellies as well! There are four varieties of jellies around here, so one of each color should do.\n\nI'll wait here and concentrate on appetizing thoughts.
Orkey's bumpy arse it hurts!\n\nYou—yeah, you! Do me a mercy an' slit my throat. I can't take anymore of this.
What hope have I, what song have I? A grave-stake I have not. It was taken by pale hands, away into the swamp. It is lost, just like my egg-brother's honorable end.
I fear the suitor-thief has set you on a fool's errand, beek-ojel, but I'll trust you know better than I what is needed.
If they expect me to go back for our supplies by myself, forget it.
Toteik! Your warmth is not from the sun, beek-ojel. Tell Tree-Minder Pavu that Tseedasi will be home soon with supplies.\n\nLick the tree on my behalf.
I've never seen anything like that little rat. Didn't know anyone but the Dwarves made things like that. Might have to visit this Clockwork City when this is all done.
There must be a snake den around here someplace.\n\nI wonder what snake venom tastes like? I can't imagine it will be very pleasant.
Make sure Stibbons aligns his bodily fluids just as the Argonian described. I want him to be totally ready for the renewal ritual.
Keep your voice low or you'll awaken every skeleton in the grove!\n\nWhat are you doing down here, by the way?

I heard that you made an impression on both the Bright-Throats and the Dead-Water tribes. You have my respect.\n\nBut that does not alter the fact that outsiders have never participated in our sacred rite—no matter how forcefully they demand it.
Despite all that's happened, I still wish to offer my services as envoy. Though, hopefully I'll be able to have a few guards accompany me next time.
I thought becoming an envoy would be an exciting line of work, but that was all too much. It's back to the farm for me.
All things crumble, all things break. And so too do all things grow again.
All is prepared, beeko. Just breathe in the smoke, and the wallow will begin.

Xukas! My little listener! As mud is my mother, how many secrets have passed me by that he might have heard? \n\nHe has the soul of a chime-maker. I knew it. One day, he will find his way to the wind and music. If not in this life, then in the next.
Greetings. I assume you are looking for Famia? She's just downstairs.
Mateem! I cannot find Honei anywhere! I shout my throat dry, but she does not come!

It sounds like … well, a bunch of croaking frogs to me. But I suppose Argonians might find the noise to be soothing.\n\nWe'll see how it sells and then decide whether or not to expand our arrangement.
This bag of scales picks my coin purse off the ground, and suddenly it's his? I've never heard of such a ridiculous thing!\n\nBah. Just my luck I run afoul of a Root-House lizard.
Hail, oh traveler. What is it that you wish of me?
My tail whips from side to side, and yet you wish speak? Speak then.
Hmm? Do you have something to say, egg-sibling?
I simply cannot believe this lizard swindled me like this. I was promised a wondrous tour! Wondrous! And so far all I've gotten is bugs in my hair and my shoes drenched in swamp water.
I knew this was a bad idea, the moment I laid eyes on this dryskin. Why would she even come to Murkmire if she expects such things?
You'll find no Sanctuary in this swamp, sister. Murkmire is where the Dread Father takes his meals.
I could waste seasons with this kuuda, and still he would never learn the ways of teeba-hatsei.
I could be spending this time practicing. Instead, I am forced to help explain such simple rules to this ojel.
I can't do it. Just can't wrap my head around how this silly game is played. I might as well give up now.
Every time I go on on an expedition, I always find plenty of angry natives, raging creatures, and deadly traps … but still no treasure. My luck seems to be as rotten as a gas blossom.
Wait a minute. You're Cyrodilic Collection's new hire, aren't you? I heard you sank Tsona-Geeva! What a way to make your Lilmoth debut.
Our Hist speaks to us through the many chimes hanging throughout the village. I wonder what the Remnant Chime will tell us?
Were you not the one who brought the Remnant Chime back to our village? If so, you have my thanks.
So you are the one who fought alongside Jaxsik-Orrn?\n\nFrom what she speaks, you fight with the strength of a Dead-Water warrior. Your bones will make mighty weapons.
You have fought alongside Jaxsik-Orrn. I grind my teeth in envy.
Why hello, you Covenant s'wit. Taking in the scenery, are we? Well do it quickly. Murkmire is no place for a member of your alliance.
Take the place of honor, and ring the Bonding-Chime to begin the ceremony.
I travel all the way to Murkmire to see the wonders of the Xinchei-Konu, only to find all of its tablets have gone missing! What an utter shame.
Both Famia and Kassandra are impressed with you! From everything I've seen and heard, Cyrodilic Collections could use a few more explorers just like you.\n\nKeep up the good work!
Famia may not know how to save her hide, but she knows much about the ebb and flow of Murkmire. You should find her quickly.
I remember Aneshi. He and his wife served my parents well.\n\nTell him that I am alive and I plan to take back our kingdom. He will provide the information we need, of that I am certain.
Did this one hear Khamira's words correctly? A member of the royal family still lives? That must wait until later. Provided there is a later.\n\nHurry, five-claw! Do as Khamira ordered.
Why are we all standing around out in the open? That's a terrible way to sneak up on someone. Believe me, I've tried!
Zamarak knew he recognized Khamira. But we can talk later. Now, you must do as Queen Khamira asked.
This one's son plans to join the militia. Tsazii would rather keep him safe, but children never appreciate the advice of their elders, yes?

Euraxia hoped to appease the Dragons by assassinating the last Dragonguard of Elsweyr. He died, but at least you acquired the Anequina Dragonhorn and avenged his death.\n\nNow if we only knew what to do with the damn thing!

This study contains documents from when the Khajiit ruled Rimmen, as well as papers that cover the span of Euraxia's rule. So many, many papers. She was a prolific writer, I'll give her that.\n\nAt least she didn't destroy her files before she died.

With your assistance, we gathered the three triangulants that allowed me to decipher the map formed by the Wrathstone tablet.\n\nI now know that the demon weapon resides in the Halls of Colossus, along the southern coast of Elsweyr.

Try not to alert the entire garrison to our presence. And keep an eye out for Captain Saulinia or anything related to Euraxia's final order. We need to determine where the assassination squad plans to strike if we're going to save the Dragonguard.
This one recognizes a lover of stories when he sees one. Care to hear another tale?
Ah, there you are. We came as soon as we could. Were you able to stop Captain Saulinia and her assassins?
Mizbina hopes that you and your friend enjoyed the story. Is there anything else that this one can do for you?

I found a set of round, orb-like objects sitting on a forgotten shelf here in the palace. They're the perfect shape for juggling! Turns out I'm good at juggling. Who knew?\n\nAnd I find it strangely soothing, after all that mayhem and fisticuffs.
Satarri is new to the art of storytelling, so forgive her if she isn't as interesting as she should be. She will improve, of this she is sure.
Hadaz was an idiot, rhook. But he was Mara'dahni's idiot, right? Please, make his death worth something. Kick these Merrunz worshipers in the tail!
You should enter the ruin and wait for Abnur Tharn to arrive. Then convince him that this ancient weapon must be destroyed.\n\nI will be nearby. In the shadows. Watching.
There is Numaia's favorite ranch hand! When Milksop and sneaky Marmalade returned, this one knew you would not be far behind.
That is Prefect Calo. Abnur Tharn brought him to Rimmen to meet with Queen Khamira.\n\nWhy is he here, Zamarak wonders?

Through my egg-mother's research, I had hoped to bridge the gap between our people. Prove that Argonians are not the cold-blooded monsters so many see us as.\n\nBut by sharing what happened to Cicatrice … that may only strengthen their hate.
Vazbi should start preparing for her trip and saying her farewells. I will always have time for you, though.
There is a cavern deep within the Litter. If memory serves, it ascends to the Baan Dar Gate. We will find the aqueduct blockage and Vazbi there.\n\nCome. We must hurry.
Please, find my companions quickly. I fear they will not last much longer.

Khamira has stepped into her role with grace and purpose. Her parents would have been so proud of her.\n\nStill, our forces have been depleted and no additional help is forthcoming. We are on our own and the Dragons remain a constant danger.

Ordering me around like I'm one of her subjects. The very idea!\n\nBut we do need to split up. I sense defensive spells in place that will be triggered if a group of our size moves around beneath the palace.

Thank you, walker, for bringing Queen Khamira to this humble shrine. It gladdens this one's heart to see her all grown and stepping forward to fulfill her destiny.\n\nBy Jone and Jode, her people need her.
The Dragons are definitely anxious about something. No sign of the Betrayer, though.\n\nGo inside and help Khamira, but do it quickly. We're too exposed out here for my liking.
Who's there? Speak up! I'm about to teach these rapscallions a valuable lesson. And yes, I plan to make it hurt!

When I was a little girl, I played in this room. I pretended that Jone and Jode spoke to me over there, beneath the statues.\n\nAfter Euraxia's coup, I dreamed of this moment, when I could reclaim my father's empty throne.
They took his body! They desecrated the king's grave!\n\nAnd from the looks of it, the queen's and Khamira's siblings as well.
Now, I'm no mage, but a Soul Shriven leaping through a portal? That's just not a natural occurrence.

A queen should not rush into danger! It is unseemly! This one should be at her side to keep her safe.\n\nNala-do will follow orders, though. We must make our way through the crypts and into the palace before Khamira gets into too much trouble, yes?
It seems my investigation has come to an end. The rumor was false, my family name is cleared, and no one even needed to be executed.\n\nA happy ending all around, wouldn't you say?

The cat captain, she sacrificed herself … for me. I … I don't know what to say.\n\nWe need to hurry, my friend. Zumog Phoom is almost finished, and I'm starting to find this whole looking-through-two-sets-of-eyes thing to be quite disorienting.
Please, just do whatever this spirit says. I don't want to die here!
I don't suppose this was the woman that voice from before was going on about.

We helped the cat-folk save Riverhold! I defended the bridge, you know. Gave us a tactical advantage.\n\nFor a moment, I heard Zumog Phoom's dreadful call. Almost deserted my post and went to join him before the sound abruptly went silent.

Return to me when you've completed your task.\n\nOh, and feel free to ask any questions you may have. This is Hakoshae's first Proving Festival in over a century, after all. I'm sure you're just as curious as everyone else.

That could have turned out better. At least we stopped my half-sister from seizing control of the imprisoned Dragons. That's something, I suppose.\n\nOf course, this delays my plan to end the Three Banners War, blast it all.

Everything Gharesh-ri sent me to prevent has occurred. I knew going to the Halls of Colossus was a mistake. Now Dragons are loose in Elsweyr!\n\nAt least we stopped Euraxia's soldier. I suppose that counts for something.
Make sure to keep your senses about you. Senche-lions aren't beasts to take lightly.
Best of luck, dear. And if you have any questions, feel free to ask.

A family reunited, a smuggling ring destroyed, and the gratitude of all of Riverhold. Not a bad start to a partnership, yes?\n\nMizzik was even able to secure a hefty bonus, thanks to the generosity of Captain Kahiri.
The Proving Festival has certainly made my job easier. With so many of the town's residents worrying about their ancestors, everyone's been on their best behavior.
We are about to enter the place where the Betrayer faced his greatest failure. Where he died at the hands of the remaining heroes and Moon-Priests.\n\nWe must make sure history repeats itself.

This one regrets getting you caught up in her affairs, but she is glad to have crossed your path. Things would have gone very differently had you not come back for her.\n\nMoons willing, we meet again, eh? Work another job. One with a better payout.
Well, we didn't get into the vault. Normally, I'd call the job a wash, but it seems like Tasnasi owns the vault now, so I guess you could say the job was a success.\n\nFunny how things work out.
There you are! Vole managed to swipe a bottle of Oleander Reserve from the Avernos. It was delicious.\n\nThere's, uh, something else to drink around here, I'm sure.

"To defer celebration without necessity is perhaps the most grievous sin." Hokae the Festive knew the truth when he spoke it. With so many uncertainties in life, we should celebrate when we have reason! And what better reason have we than this?
Mell the Musical is always ready to perform!

Feina-Darak has called my spirit to judge her. By her quill my name was written, by her hands the paper lotus placed. And so I have come to punish her wickedness.\n\nAnd yet you try to stop me. Who are you to deny me my revenge?
Unless you've come back bearing massage oils and nimble fingers I am not really interested.
Something has upset my dear brother. I'll get to the very bottom of it … later.
If this one must talk in circles with lunatics much longer, he too will go mad!\n\nDid you find any offending forks at the campground?

Kiseravi knew that she would meet someone brave enough to enter the tomb, strong enough to pass the spirit's test, and wise enough to accept her protection and never question her voice.\n\nKiseravi knew because the spirit told her.

I must admit, you and Thunderboots make quite the charming pair. And watching you both play at being investigator? Why, it's been sleek entertainment, truly.\n\nBut now … now you tread upon sands that are best left undisturbed.
May Bright Moons watch over you.
Sarazi must get back to training. You may have beaten me in our hunting competition, but no one will match my raw physique!
This one is humbled by your generosity, walker. She will see you fully compensated for the danger of this task!

We have accomplished much, my friend. We overthrew the tyrant, Euraxia Tharn. Defeated Zumog Phoom and the Betrayer. Even killed at least two Dragons and made the Moons move in the sky.\n\nIf only I could shake this sense of impending doom.
Good luck with this dog, walker. Jahlar has heard many unsettling things about such animals, so be careful, yes?
Mazdurr is grateful for such a rescue. Were you able to find his amulet as well?
Yushiha has come to return her debt to you. Zumog Phoom is dead, but those he served still seek to ruin all we hold dear.\n\nWhat strength there is in my blood is yours to command.
When I awoke this morning, traveling to the Plane of Jode wasn't on my agenda.
We are done here. Let us continue on to the Moon Gate and Queen Khamira.
Hear what Abnur Tharn has to say, then return to me.\n\nHurry, five-claw. We have much to do and little time to waste.

The quiet moments between battles. I like to spend the time catching up on my reading.\n\nHistory, military strategy, recipe books. My secret pleasure is a good mystery, though, and the new Investigator Vale is a real page turner!
I wonder how long after death you can perform these rituals. Do you think they would work on something smaller, like a mosquito? So many questions!
Hurry to the ritual circle, my friend. We haven't much time before Arum-Khal's realm fully collapses.
Zamarak is glad to see Rimmen free once more. The cost was dear, but it was worth it.
Welcome, walker. You have come to show our warriors how to fight, yes?
Courageous five-claw, I will make sure your deeds are sung by my people. They will be told from one generation to the next.\n\nAs Khunzar-ri passed into legend, so too will you.
I had almost lost hope for dear Shando-ri. Your witch shows great kindness in trying to save him once more.\n\nDo not fear, child. This will work. It must.
Just … have to catch my breath. Be with you in a moment, eh?
Keep steady, sword-wielder. As Lorkhaj taught, look into the darkness of the void without fear in your heart, and it will come to fear you instead.
Rakhzargo has never seen that tapestry before.
Kideya will admit, that tapestry is rather suspicious. Best if you investigate, yes?
A skooma ring operated by a Daedra-summoning mage! This one thinks we need to put an end to this—and Raz isn't even wearing his fancy leathers.
Please, be quick. J'dathal fears his daughters are in grave danger!
Dealing with Quintus always takes a lot out of me, just never so literally.

A parley with Euraxia is a capital idea! I'll send word to Rimmen to expect us. I imagine my half-sister will treat us as befits my station and agree to the meeting.\n\nAttend to any other matters if you must, then see me when you're ready to leave.
I think I'll just sit here for a bit longer. I'd say we earned a sit-down, eh comrade?
I noticed a Khajiiti settlement nearby. Riverhold, if I recall. The last time I visited the place, it was barely two buildings and a creek!\n\nI'll meet you and Abnur there after I finish up here.
Not now, walker! I have wounded to tend to. Talk to Tharn and let me work.

We tracked the Dragon to these mountains. If a necromancer also hides here, we can eliminate two enemies with a single arrow! Such a victory will boost the militia's morale, of that I am sure.\n\nLet the hunt begin!

When Abnur Tharn spoke of a hero of renown, I had no idea he was referring to you. It's so good to see you again, though I wish the circumstances were not so dire.\n\nWell, you helped the Mane before. I have no doubt you will do so again.

This one fears the Dragon that attacked you was only the beginning, traveler. Dark Moons loom on Elsweyr's horizon, of that Ma'jha-dro has little doubt.\n\nBut enough talk. We came here to spar, did we not?
I have preparations to make before we launch our assault on the palace.\n\nSpeak to Lord Gharesh-ri. He thinks he knows a way we can slip inside without immediately alerting Euraxia's guards.

All sorts of vermin wander the sewers, including Euraxian soldiers. So I recommend vigilance. In my current state, the only assistance I can provide is advice. Here it is.\n\nAvoid what you can, dispatch what you can't, and watch where you step.
Izjadi will look after her fellow adepts, don't you fear. Though this one knows it will not be easy to return Star Haven to its former glory.
Can I help you with something?
You do not look like one of the Usurper Queen's soldiers! Who are you and what are you doing down here?
By the Moons, you have to help me! A monster attacked our farm. My father ran, but I do not know what became of him.
Have you seen my father, J'dathal? I've been searching for him, but I wasn't able to make it very far.

These beasts should thank the Moons that they found me without my bow. I'd make quick work of them if I had it on hand!\n\nHave you seen my father, by chance? He's a kind man, but not very quick. I fear he may have come to harm.

The feisty Khajiit is right, you know. The Rithana-di-Renada does have a song to sing.\n\nAn awful shame that the jewel is still missing, yes? The Singing Crystal it was called. Rajhin remembers how beautifully it glowed the night he stole it.

The Song of Kingdoms. I didn't know it would be quite so … beautiful. And thanks to you, all of Elsweyr will be able to hear it. Perhaps even inspired by it, yes? \n\nNow, more than ever, we need to spread hope.
I should have never doubted my brilliant sister. This Song of Kingdoms, it is simply wonderful. And wonderfully popular too, by the look of things!
Don't forget to check back regularly, walker. That retainer won't fill your belly for long!

I can see you aren't kin to the leeches in this ruin, so I offer you this warning. I am here to tear the Hollowfang clan down to its foundation. If you seek to join in their madness, I will end you just the same.
Don't worry about me. You're holding up? We've come out ahead on this gamble twice now. Third time's a charm?
The Dragon is tearing the wound asunder! You must stop him!
Do not shy away from the Divine. You've come so far already, just to turn away. You may not feel worthy, but now is your chance to prove yourself deserving of Alkosh's grace.
Aha! More faithful heed the call! You wish to go to Sunspire Temple and pray before Divine Alkosh yourself? Natrada will take you.
Saviwa is grateful to you for helping his ancestor's spirit find peace. Saviwa would be even more grateful to you if you helped him get a jug of plum brandy.
Gather Jora-ri's urn and we will find the proper tomb together. Bright Moons will show us the way.
Zamarak will assist Tharn against the Dragons. In the meantime, you should go inside. Queen Khamira is waiting for you.
The Grand Adept wishes to thank you for all you have done, walker. It would be unwise to ignore such a summons.

Well, look who it is! Didn't get enough of my company back in the ruins, hmm?\n\nBy the look on Abnur Tharn's face, however, I suppose you're here to see him instead of me. Go ahead. Best not to keep the emperor's battlemage waiting.
Find Khamira outside and see what she requires. Euraxian soldiers will soon reach Riverhold. When that happens, all Oblivion will break loose.

Abnur's received a new quest from the Mane. As soon as we finish here, I'll join him. Quests are my specialty! \n\nOh, fiddlesticks! I just remembered. Queen Khamira asked me to be her King's Claw. I guess Abnur will have to soldier on without me.
Ah, excuse me. If I may be so bold, you match the description I was given. I have a message for you, if you're willing to accept it.
This one doesn't know you, but at least you aren't a walking corpse.\n\nThis one must ask, why are you here?

This one's been studying the great Tharn. Such presence he has! Confident, strong, loquacious. Words flow like honey pudding from his mouth. Makes Lyrrsazhi's nose wet just to think about it.\n\nHe often smells rather acrid, though. Pity.
What's that smell? Oh, I see: a Covenant drag-heel has decided to grace Rimmen with their presence.
You truly are a blessing from Peryite. The first one that didn't make me itch.
Did you find food, water, and healing supplies?
I thought we were the only ones still alive in this rotten city.
Why would you come to Orcrest when everyone here is dead or dying?
Did Peryite send you?

Before you return to Khamira's side, this one requests an additional favor.\n\nThe Mane gave Cashia a sealed letter for Abnur Tharn, but he refuses to see me. I understand that you and he share a special bond. Perhaps you could deliver the letter?
I'll send a copy of my report to Queen Khamira shortly. A modern account of a battle with Dragons—just think how this will be able to improve our training regimens and strategies moving forward!
They may not be gods, but to slay a Dragon is no mean feat! Maybe you truly are blessed by Alkosh. Did he guide you here to cast down these pretenders?
Do you not fear the Way of Jone because it does not scorch the darkness of your souls? It will not protect you from the claws of the righteous.

I'll make sure the Moon-Singers tell the tale of the soldiers who defended the Moon Gate—Khajiiti and Imperial alike.\n\nFor now, though, talk to Zamarak and Calo. Let them tell you what happened in their own words.
Seems like I have quite a bit of work ahead of me.\n\nStill, Imperial City wasn't built in a day! I just need to tweak the recipe a bit and try again.
We are setting up shop, rhook. Feel free to check back later.
I'll be along soon. Promise.
Still alive, eh? More than Ak'an expected. Perhaps you aren't as flimsy as you look.
So, we meet again, walker. I see you, but not your friends. Where are Jakarn and that mangy idiot, Fez'skar?
There you are! Did you find the key? Fez'skar's fur falls out from all this stress!
Start your pilgrimage here, with the ledger from the Goiter's Gulp. An idol from Rimmen would make a nice addition to this temple. Ah, and fine silks from the merchants at the Valenwood Gate. Yes!

This one hears the danger has passed. Mostly. A few Dragons remain in the wild, and the occasional Euraxian leaps from the shadows, but Rimmen is free and the Usurper Queen is dead.\n\nLyrrsazhi thinks you had something to do with all that, yes?
She did it!\n\nGo pick up the key, eh? We'll find Milksop behind this door. I know it!
Eh? Can't you just let Qa'jahd enjoy himself?
The great city of Rimmen in the Khajiiti land of Elsweyr is a wondrous place to conduct business. You should visit some day, walker.
Lady Izza is eager to use her influence to bring peace between the Nords and Khajiit, isn't she?\n\nNothing solves problems better than a traditional Nord love ballad. Except for mead.
This one paid good gold for Rigurt's package. More than it is worth, judging by the smell.\n\nYou will give Thadarra what she is owed, yes?
Could you please stop stomping around like that? My head is pounding enough as it is.\n\nShor's Bones, we never should have eaten those sugar cakes.
Lady Izza is going to pretend that Ambassador Rigurt did not just confuse her with a house cat.
What are you doing up here? Go teach those gibbering idiots about Volendrung's ultimate power! Not that they'll remember after their brains are bashed out.
Thanks for your help getting rid of the wasps in the fields and finding my lost guar.\n\nIf Hadamnargo's horse wasn't so sad and knew how to talk, he would thank you, too.
Bring back game from the traps in the hills west of here. Longer you take, the better this lizard looks.
You again. Toys that get in my way wind up back in the box. Is it time to pack you up?
A beautiful day for a stroll in the Scar, heh?\n\nAs long as a Dragon doesn't swoop out of the sky and eat you. That would certainly ruin an otherwise nice excursion.
Stink! You stink like oil! Get, or I bite you! Bite, bite!
You have heard that the Khajiit love naps, yes? So does M'aiq. Though maybe M'aiq is napping now and this conversation is but a dream?
The Betrayer did terrible things to the Khajiit of old. Zumog Phoom must not be allowed to return that monster to life.\n\nDo whatever you must, walker. Whatever you must.
You may join the prayerful in the courtyard when you are ready to witness the Divine for yourself.\n\nOr you may pray with us here, if you are not yet ready to see.
I seemed to have jigged when I reached Solitude when I should have jagged. Well, anyway, here I am!\n\nNow, did you summon me or did I send for you?

You'd do that? It's a backpack, Imperial legion make. It was my husband's. It's just some personal items. Things he had before … before there were damn Dragons!\n\nSorry. I'm tired and hungry. I should go. Find me at the inn in Riverhold. And thanks.
If Selene devoted half the effort she wastes tugging at my control to fighting Maarselok we would not be chasing him through his overripe garden.
So, we've earned a breather, right …?\n\nProbably don't want to breathe too deep here anyway.
I've had enough of this cat and mouse game. I'll tear him from the sky. Let nothing interfere with me.
This tapestry continues the legend of the Dark Aeon. I suppose it would be more accurate to call it a prophecy.
Once you determine the nature of the three glyphs, you can use that knowledge to reveal the entrance to the tomb.\n\nFeel free to consult my notes. They should help if you run into any problems.

Za'ji will meet you there? Ah, yes! Of course. This one is your resident expert, after all.\n\nHe just did not realize that his first Dragonguard mission would take him back to Black Heights. He hasn't visited since … well, he has never visited.
Place the bell back on its hook so this one can assess it.
Well, this certainly complicates things. Let's hope the Clan Mother will still agree to our request.
This must be the entrance to the mine. We should head inside and see if we can find Yahgrondu.

The journals we discovered in the Dragonguard sanctuaries point to one obvious conclusion. The Horn of Ja'darri exists, but was stolen by the Dragon Vahlokzin.\n\nWe must enter the Dragon's lair in Southern Elsweyr and retrieve the horn.
With Yahgrondu's death, our chances of defeating Laatvulon diminish.\n\nWe must act cautiously. We are one Dragon and a few mortals against a host of enemies. We must plan accordingly.

I traveled to Southern Elsweyr not just to finish this business with the Dragons. The Khajiit of Pellitine have been on their own for too long. The time has come to welcome them back into the Confederacy.
Be careful. Magic is a tricky business, especially in Tharn's hands.
It is good to see you hale and whole, warrior. But … where is Sai? Did something happen?
I never thought I would live to see Dragon wings cloud the sky once more. We must end this infestation before it spreads.
Oh, Vijari, this one can't see your precious face. He—he isn't a Lost Cat yet, right? Adara'hai can save him. She will save him.
Vijari … Vijari can play inside. He can … he can paint like papa. Vijari doesn't mind.

Ah, good. Zamarak brought my luggage. I should wear my royal regalia and appear official for the ceremony to honor the Dragonguard.\n\nNow, go and speak to General Renmus, my friend. Then join me in the gardens behind the palace for the ceremony.

Every kra'jun requires specific heroes to fill its ranks. Azurah shook the Sand Behind the Stars to give yours just the right collection of protectors, warriors, and ne'er-do-wells.\n\nMine was a kra'jun for the ages. Yours is perfect for today.
You worry more than … a Nord nurse maid ….\n\nTo the center of the island. It's time to end this.
What are you waiting for? Grab the Dragonhorn before Vahlokzin arrives!
Now that we have the Horn of Ja'darri, our true work begins.\n\nAs the saying goes, strike when the opportunity appears or stand by and do nothing. I can never do nothing.
That was Buzinda, a local baker. I wonder why she came to see my father.

If we can't outmatch our enemies, we must outwit them.\n\nI want you to infiltrate the cult. Learn where their base of operations is located, how large a force they command. And, most importantly, what they plan to do next.
Has Queen Khamira solved our transportation issue? The Dragonguard is eager to at long last take the battle to Kaalgrontiid.
In the end, our mission was successful. We secured passage to this island, found the Dragon who nested here, and ensured Senchal's safety.\n\nIt just didn't go as I expected.

Apologies, walker, if we've concerned you. Ka'ishka's husband has been ill for a very long time and this one fears it has frayed her nerves to breaking. Adara'hai knew she needed help from her letter, but this one didn't think she meant an exorcism.
I think you'll find our new friend far more cooperative now.
Daini will get out of this place soon enough, walker. Guaranteed.

So, it is off to Papa's old warehouse. You will be careful, yes? In and out, like a serpent's fangs.\n\nAnd do not let this one's sister wander, all right? That place is full of old ghosts. Bad memories. Moons protect you, walker.
Go on and speak with her. But mark me, if she doesn't bring me something soon, I'm off on the next tide.
Ah, you are back. And with all your limbs. Good. Good.\n\nWhat did you find in the wreckage? Please tell Daini you found something more than splintered crates and giant murder-chickens.
We destroyed the focal points and cut off the flow of energy, but were we in time to stop Kaalgrontiid's ascension?\n\nMoons, I wish Tharn were here! We should hurry and find that damn Dragon.
Queen Khamira impressed me, my friend. It isn't every ruler who readily puts themselves in harm's way for the sake of their people. Tamriel could use a dozen more like her.

A Khajiit queen has summoned the Dragonguard to Senchal? She must want to reward Za'ji for his heroic actions! Oh, and the rest of you, too.\n\nZa'ji must break out the good plum brandy. Not those cheap bottles Caska loves so much.
If we're to appear before the queen, then I need a bath. If you'll excuse me ….
I wonder why the queen has asked all of us to come to Senchal? I hope we're not in trouble!
Caska spoke with this one. Let her know that Lahini is ….\n\nWhy? Why did she have to die? Why did they need to take the life of such a young, innocent woman? Our poor, poor Lahini.
Walker! Tell Aeliah to relax a little, yes? This one completed his last mission perfectly. He deserves a pint or two.\n\nZa'ji heard about Yahgrondu's death. Tough break, yes?
Well, look who it is! My spies informed me you were in the area, but I wasn't sure our paths would cross again.
This one thanks the Moons that you and Queen Khamira both appear safe and well.\n\nZamarak's tail turned gray when he realized he had lost his charge before we had even departed from Rimmen!
Ah, it's you. I understand we have you to thank for stopping the Dragon and getting rid of the floating island? Thank you.\n\nBut what brings you to my office at this particular point in time?
First a broken heart, now this? Show a walker some pity here.
Loading up for a journey to Senchal, friend. Climb aboard if you wish!

Hello! I'm Aeliah Renmus. General Renmus's daughter. I couldn't speak freely in front of my father, but I might know someone who can help you get to that island.\n\nBut tell me. Do you truly believe you can slay a Dragon?
Hey, walker! You see my drink? Oh, wait.

There is no day like today for adventure! And you have a Dragon to slay, yes?\n\nTalk to the bearded one first, though. He seems like the strategy type and will probably want to discuss many, many boring things with you.
Can't you see I'm busy? Go away.
You heard the captain. Let's sail for Senchal!
Blademaster Kasura has requested that I guide you to the Valley of Blades. We can depart whenever you're ready.
Thank you again, walker. Perhaps we will meet again, far, far from here!

See that alcove up ahead? It was Za'ji's secret spot when the cove contained less Bahzahar! That's where you'll find the key. \n\nHmm, the ladder this one used is missing. If only we had … wait! Za'ji has something that will help!
Za'ji, ah … Za'ji will own up to that one. He messed up.\n\nMother never did like it when I interrupted her. This one doubts she will be eager to help us now.
If you discover the location of this mask, don't hesitate. I trust you to follow up on any leads you might find.
Why do you hesitate, mask-bearer? The portal awaits. I thought you were intent on solving riddles such as this?
There it is. Khajiit of the Moons. It's been many years since Bebbia last saw it.
Did we set sail? If not, this one … might need to slow down.
I'll meet you at the fortress entrance. And before you ask, no. You cannot ride me there.
Ka'ishka, is that you? What is that song? It calms Vijari's heart. The voice this one knows, but it's so dark.

I think I understand. You need to push the sliding stones onto platforms to open the gates. Once a gate opens, another sliding stone will be free to push.\n\nEventually, you should unlock the sliding stone that opens the door forward.
The Clan Mother must be in the temple! Please, you must see if she has come to harm.

From what Bebbia has said, the techniques used to make Khajiit of the Moons has been lost to time. Infantile as my understanding of them is, I may be the only person in Tamriel with the knowledge to replicate this technique. Not bad for a tailor, eh?
I am Nahfahlaar, I do not fear you, hunter. If you seek a battle, understand that it will be to the death.\n\nI would rather talk, though. Where did you get my horn?

Nahfahlaar and I have come to an agreement. We'll work together to defeat Laatvulon, but only that. After our battle is won, Nahfahlaar will peacefully depart from these lands.\n\nNow, what did Za'ji say to my proposal?
Good luck out there, pal. Dragons, outlaws, big hungry cats …. Elsweyr can get pretty rough.
Khenarthi calls to you with gentle winds. She can guide you, but never carry you. With cunning, with speed, you must find your own way.\n\nDo you accept Khenarthi's blessing?
There is no time to chat! Go to the sanctum and speak with Sai Sahan.
That Dragon took one look at you and just gave up! You must be some sort of five-claw.
So we have decided to befriend the Dragon now? Well, better than a fiery death.
I'm glad that Senchal is safe, but … making an alliance with a Dragon? I'm not so sure about that.
Ah, stranger! You're sodden to your skivvies! Have you supped on the shrine's waters?
Caska the Unconquered, back in the fight! This one may need to end his shift early.
Friend Skordo has a traveling companion now, whether he realizes it or not.\n\nMarekki is very difficult to dislodge, walker. Just look at these claws!
I pity Elsweyr, but Valenwood has a Dragon problem of its own. The Dragon, Maarselok, is blighting land and threatening the Green.
You look like you could give a Daedric Prince pause. Like your chances against a Dragon? Maarselok is corrupting the Green and we're grasping at straws.

Searching for Nahfahlaar may be a fool's errand, you understand. We don't even know if he's still alive.\n\nNo matter. My reluctance to aid you has done little good so far. I'll lead the others while you and Sai Sahan search.
I heard you talking, walker. You mean to steal from Turo? Again?\n\nDaini does not understand. You can only yank a senche-panther's tail so many times before it turns and gobbles you up.
Daini helping you escape, too? Nah. Other way around, I wager. Thanks.\n\nDaini takes good care of us, so you take good care of her, all right?
At long last, we defeated the Black Beast. \n\nToday we finished a battle the Dragonguard began centuries ago. A fitting start to our own order, I must say.
Look at that! I actually negotiated a profitable contract for my uncle!\n\nBut what of you, my friend? Were you able to secure the last of the stolen moon-sugar?
I wish I could do more, wayfarer. Truly. But I know that you will wreak the vengeance my brothers and sisters deserve. May Onsi guide your blade.
So strange that dreams can bring people and places together …

I apologize for the state of my comrades. Despite their appearance, all of those shambling corpses served the Empire nobly and well. Brilliant tacticians, wise scholars … good friends.\n\nI try not to think about what Honoria and I put them through.
Mara's mercy. More distractions.\n\nI'm a little busy. So, unless you have a message from my mistress or a ferocious beast to sell, you should just be on your way.

A fellow High Elf. How refreshing. I am Lady Ghisiliane. It seems I have you to thank for settling this business with Auberic Dufont.\n\nTell me, what payment do you require? And what do you have planned for your scowling, green friend there?
Do be careful out there, hmm? Dragons! Can you believe it?
Do not be a stranger, rhook. Southern Elsweyr never stays quiet for long. A new day means new adventures.\n\nMoons guide you!
I think I'll rest here a moment before I head back to Senchal. It's the first rest I've had in weeks.\n\nIt really is something, isn't it?
What are you waiting for? Go, go!
We'll keep watch. Find the Clan Mother, quickly!

I've been fighting all my life. For gold, for glory, for sheer enjoyment. But now I fight for something greater. Now I fight for my people and my home.\n\nIf I die today, it shall be with blood on my fangs and fury in my claws.
This is it, isn't it? Our final battle against the Order of the New Moon. A chance to see if our Dragonguard can live up to the name.\n\nLet's just make it out of this alive. All of us.
Our final battle, is it? How fortunate for you to have Za'ji by your side.
Congratulations, acolyte. The Order of the New Moon welcomes you into its fold.\n\nYou have come at a fortuitous time. Ra'khajin prepares to lead an attack on Pridehome. You shall join him.
What do you want?

Maezi smells the distinctive aroma of Hizhikar's gourmet moon-sugar. You found the two portions! Well done, walker!\n\nUnfortunately, we have not found the third portion as of yet, but we are still looking.
If you ever find yourself in Skyrim, look me up. I promise to save enough of my concoction to share with you next time!\n\nAt least, I promise to try!
If you ever find yourself in need of some dishonest work, come find Kishima. She is certain she will need a new partner shortly, yes?
Yeah? Can't you see I'm reading? Trying to read. What letter does that look like to you?

Sacking the Icereach Coven's stronghold here is a good start, but I've already heard tales of related sisterhoods springing up on the mainland. If they've really made some powerful friends in Skyrim, we need to root them out. Quickly.
I must ask. When you found J'saad's body and this stone … did the stone speak to you?\n\nIt sounds strange, but what if J'saad wasn't crazy? What if the stone really did tell him things?

While we weren't able to get any of that aeonstone, we learned a valuable lesson. Never cross paths with crazed cultists!\n\nI suppose we should make plans to head back to Murkmire. Thanks again for finding my friends.

My friend … dead. That could have been me, you know.\n\nWell, at least I got a small chunk of that green stone. Just don't tell the others. I plan to make something special when we get back to the jewelry shop. In Falls' memory, you understand?
I almost had one of those strange green stones in my hand. I could almost feel it!\n\nAh, well. Maybe next time.

Do I know you? If not, I suggest you move along before I summon the guards.\n\nThere are many vendors in Senchal who can assist you with your purchase, albeit their product is infinitely inferior to mine.
Everything in Elsweyr wants us dead. Smugglers, pirates, Dragons. Now even our own bodies try to kill us.\n\nI only wish it was me instead of my poor Ania.
I hear you completed the deliveries quickly and while the product was still potent. Well done.
Juisa thanks you for dragging her deadbeat sister home. She will ensure she stays out of trouble for as long as she can. Next time this happens, Juisa will tie her to the broom and use her as a mop.
This is what I get for trusting a Khajiit. He guides me to the middle of gods know where, and expects me to pay? For what? A tour of the wilderness? He should be paying me for my wasted time!
Thank the Moons for delivering someone who looks like they might have a lick of sense.

Honor and faith, warrior! \n\nBlademaster Sai Sahan requests your presence. A Dragon nests on a nearby island, and he believes it will attack Senchal. He requires your aid to slay the beast before it can strike against the city.
Tharn is still with us! By Leki's blade, that improves our chances a thousandfold!
It's not story time. I'm not going to read it to you. If you can't read it yourself, go bother Dirge about it.

Thank you for helping Lahini see reason, five-claw!\n\nAll this time, she thought her family resented her. But it is not true! They see Lahini's worth. And, bit by bit, this one is beginning to see her worth, too.
Anything else I need to know before we head to Eastmarch?

The Icereach Coven's presence in Western Skyrim is troubling. After you gather yourself, go to Solitude. It's the capital city. Tell the authorities what we saw.\n\nSomeone needs to warn them about the storms.
I thought he was grieving, but it was all a ruse. My father, high king of Western Skyrim, in league with the Gray Host!\n\nPlease, talk to Lyris. I need to consider what happens next.
I'm not comfortable in such surroundings, but I'll endure. We need to convince the high king that the elixir works. And then we have to make a lot of it, and quickly!

Svargrim's a bastard, but King Jorunn believed he had the best interest of his people at heart. Obviously, something changed.\n\nAnd with Solitude targeted for a massive harrowstorm, things have gotten more complicated.
No sign of Rasir himself, but his journal should at least give us a clue as to where he went. \n\nWhat does it say?
I can't wait to hear what Lyris has planned for these bastards. Go ahead and put the map on the table.
