I've been standing out here for the better part of … three-fourths of the contents of this mug. Don't you know it's rude to keep people waiting?
It's nice to be warm and have a full belly. It'll be some time before I'm ready to leave the comfort of a fire.
We're so cold … none of us are well enough to hunt. If you could get us some meat, it might help us last a few more days. \n\nHopefully this storm breaks soon.

I hate that the bodies of those we lost won't be committed to the sea. But I know they would want us to carry on, know that we have a fighting chance. \n\nThank you, wayfarer. This ship and crew owe you their lives.
I pray that cool heads prevail. Hot blood and rash action will not benefit anyone.
You try my patience. Take the princess and leave here immediately.
What are you doing in my house? \n\nFirst all my workers rot away into monsters because of frozen skeleton wolves, and now strangers are traipsing about my home.

My skin … it's no longer blue. And … my heart! I can feel it beating again! By all the gods, I'm alive! \n\nWhatever you and Mjolen cast on me, it broke the curse. I feel heat course through my veins for the first time in years.
One moment my Dapper was here, inside my vest, snug as a bug. The next she was cold and lifeless.\n\nShe was my best and only friend. What will I do now that she's gone?
The Divines smiled on us when they sent you our way. We would have been lost to the ice were it not for you.

Svargrim and the people of Western Skyrim can be real pains in the arse, but they're still Nords. Despite the differences between their holds and ours, we won't abandon them to the coven's conspiracy.
Do not worry. I'll provide good counsel to the high king. It's obvious to me that we need to take the Reach threat seriously. By the time I'm done with him, Svargrim will see that, too.

We set out to find Fenn and bring him back to Solitude. Along the way, we learned more about our true enemy, killed one of their leaders, and acquired some valuable intelligence.\n\nThat's a victory in my book.

I can't believe we did it. We stopped a harrowstorm and saved my city. And we killed my father, who was mad with power and betrayed us all.\n\nNow I must get back to work. Someone has to step up and take command. The people need a leader.
Those harrowfiends … stacked up like war hounds before being set loose on their prey.\n\nSuch close quarters is driving them into a frenzy. Let's hope that pen holds.
I can't believe those harrowfiend creatures were once regular people. It's horrific what's happened to them.
No time, no time. Off with you.
You have given me much to consider. If these Reach witches really do plan to attack Haafingar, I need to inform Svargrim at once.\n\nI fear that this plot against Skyrim is only the beginning.
I still need to finish studying the Icereach Coven Medallion. If I can ascertain the enchantments used to protect its wearer from the harrowstorms, that will give us something to go on.
How fragile my faith when I can depend more on help from a stranger than from my god.
Just this morning, we were debating the mysteries of the Colored Rooms. Now … now he's gone.\n\nHe attacked me. He tried to devour me. I had no choice but to kill him. To kill a cherished student.
Are you mad? Don't step foot anywhere near that farm. Those … bone wolves will rip you apart limb from limb! They turned everyone there into zombies.
Finish any other business you have in Solitude, then meet me at the Blue Palace so we can report to Queen Gerhyld.

Skor found us. I did my best to fight him off, but he was too strong. The affliction transformed him. It took everything in me to just stall him.\n\nI told Rasir to run, but Skor went after him. Please, you have to save Rasir! He must survive!

I'm lucky you came along. No matter what you find in the barrow, I need to know. Tell any survivors you see to meet me here.\n\nHafskjar's the only family I have left. If I've lost him too, well …. Just hurry back safely.
Private game. Get lost.

I know you can't stick around. Don't worry. I'll protect Bjora and the others with my life. No more hiding.\n\nIt gives me courage knowing people like you are out there defending folks against these evils. Maybe we have a chance.

I knew I could trust you to find Bjora. My daughter means everything to me. Thank you.\n\nShe didn't want to talk about it, but she looks … changed. Haunted. It will take some time to recover from this.

Don't worry about me. I'm back with my family now. I know they'll keep me safe.\n\nPlease, be careful if you venture towards Markarth. If the visions I was shown are true, I fear horrors are gathering there.

My pack mates are in a work camp on the Lightless Hollow's west side. That's the big cavern to the east. You need that key to unlock the special chains that bind them.\n\nI'll meet you south of the work camp after you set them free.
Hmm, I expected to see a drunken souse named Dorbin walk through that door. Not this incredible specimen before me. Tell me, what became of the man I hired?
Take good care of the princess. Jarl. Svana. Whoever she is now.\n\nIf you need me, I'll be deep in a bottle.
I trust you found what you wanted, Sapphire.
Eh? What's that? Oh? No, but more wine, please.\n\nFive thousand! Oh, wait—has the auction started? Oh, dash it all … seven thousand!
Ready yourself. I've encountered more than my fair share of evils. Please believe me when I tell you that whatever Kjalnar Tombskald found down here dwarfs them all.

My flask! Thank you, my friend.\n\nRada al-Saran is the one they call the Ashen Lord … leader of the Gray Host. He and Tzinghalis often went into the nearby sanctum to talk. I heard a few words … map, plan … but I couldn't make out the rest.
Many innocents have been saved and Lady Essenia will no longer plague these lands. All thanks to you, walker.
Greymoor Keep. What a nightmare.\n\nPlenty of my adventures would make decent bard songs, but this is one I'd just as soon forget.
Right, let's move. Every second we waste is one we could be using to our advantage.
I think Elle is talking with some of the miners outside the mine.\n\nIf you could tell her that we finished setting up the traps, I'm sure she'd be delighted!
Get a move on and find something. I don't care if it's ghosts or spiders, I just want answers.\n\nIf Captain Ageran was last seen at the mining offices, there has to be some kind of lead there.
Would you mind asking that remarkably large woman to lower her rather large axe, please? Assure her that I'm harmless … mostly.
Things seem to have stopped shaking, so I'm making better progress extracting the splinters from my gut. I take it the pyres have been put out?
My family will never believe the traitor-jarl was wrongly condemned.
It's good to see you, my friend. I feared the worst when the Reachmen started pouring out of the cave. \n\nSince you're here and the bridge is still standing, I assume your mission was a success?
Have you investigated the barrow as you promised? What news of our soldiers?\n\nInform the jarl immediately or get back out there and get it done.
Fenn can lead us to that coven witch. Come on.
Thank you for rescuing my Ulang. And I assume you defused the explosives, seeing as our bridge is still standing.\n\nBut you should report to Captain Hingrid. She hates to be kept waiting.
Don't you worry. The moment a Reachman comes out of that cave, they'll get an arrow through the eye!
You don't look like these tusking Reach bastards. I assume that means you're here to rescue me.
You have the enchanted medallion. Make good use of it.\n\nFennorian and I must return to our work. The answers he seeks about the witch's ritual will not come as easily as yours.

I hope our two ghost hunters won't judge me too harshly for being a thorn in their side. Without them looking into this, Urlvar would never have been exposed. I gave them a hard time, but they never gave up on Dusktown.\n\nI owe them.
I'll find Lyris and we'll be right behind you.\n\nRemember, Kagnthamz is southeast of Dusktown.
I'll feel a lot better delivering a speech about healing and hope knowing that we're on the road to recovery. What did Fenn have to say about the elixir?

The swordthane gathered people in the Hall of the Dead. Go check on them while I pull myself together. This whole ordeal has been a lot more strenuous than I'm accustomed to.\n\nThen I'll get to work on the elixir and a cure for the harrowed.
I should remain with the Skald-King. I trust you can handle Svana's request without me.
So we're to bow our heads with the Skald-King? Perhaps the poet's prepared a dirge.
Clasping arms with easterners. There's been enough death for one day.
I was not expecting Princess Svana to be so commanding. I'd heard—well, I'm glad that not all the rumors I've heard about the state of Solitude are true.
A proper Haafingar dirge for Svargrim? I haven't attended one of those since I snuck into Solitude as a young man.\n\nNot the most auspicious start to Svana's rule, but it will teach her wisdom.
The walls are strong. There's nothing to fear.

Now, I take on the most challenging adventure of all. Marriage, full time.\n\nI got damned lucky with Telline. She's better to me than I deserve. I'm going to spend the rest of my life making it up to her.

That man infuriates me so much I could incinerate him with a fire summoning, then dump his ashes into a resurrection pot just so I could do it again! \n\nI married the damn fool, so I suppose I have no one to blame but myself.
Check the body. I'll make sure nothing catches us unaware.

Whoa, hold on there, stranger. Might want to reconsider entering Mor Khazgur. Damn mine collapsed and the whole clan's on edge.\n\nThe fact that Chief Urzikh and Overseer Thulsgreg are at each others' throats doesn't help. Typical.
She gave you the key, did she? I hope she's not wrong in trusting you.\n\nGo on then. Give the chief what she's been waiting for.
Go on and talk to Overseer Thulsgreg. \n\nI threw his wife in a cage, but even that didn't make him see reason. Maybe you'll have more luck.
So, you're back. Did you do what I asked?
<Pickle looks nervous.>
Everyone made it out except for the three down here. Any luck finding them?\n\nFind any proof of the chief's carelessness?
I never thought I'd be so happy to see the sky again.\n\nI don't even care what happens now. Just glad I have my life.
Just one more boulder and we're out of here. Go on!
The Skald-King's agent can be found in the city, at the Fighters Guild.\n\nI wouldn't keep her waiting too long if I were you.
A pen? Do these underground humanoids keep the chaurus like cattle? Let's keep going.
Priest Bavian gathered everyone she could, but it was madness. You'll find her in the nearby cave, tending to the injured.

<<1>>'s scholars should have simple jobs fit for an adventurous individual; however, you won't want to go it alone on orders from <<2>>'s militia. Their duties are far too dangerous for one person.\n\nHelp both with their tasks and we can all get paid.

Local sources have mostly been consumed, but the bushes along the Frozen Coast should be remote enough to remain untouched.\n\nOh, and if you have any additional questions as to the nature of my study, please don't hesitate to ask!
Where is she? Where's my Nelfthea?
You go on ahead, I'll cover you. If we have to fight, better I have the element of surprise.
I must say, your punctuality speaks well of you. They assured me you would not be here for some time, and yet, here you are. It's good to see you!
Hah! There you are. Did you find the parts we need? Time is of the essence!

You did it! \n\nOh, it feels so good to be back in my body! Flesh and blood! A beating heart! It would truly have been a shame to keep all of this beauty locked away in a silly doll for eternity. I owe you a great debt.
Can you imagine how this place must have looked in its prime? \n\nI can almost see it now … the hiss of steam, the singing of metal, the hum of the power cores. It must have been a sight.
Let us speak again once we've escaped this place. I long to see the sky again.
Curse him! We'll never be able to catch him like this!\n\nHow do we apprehend a man who can vanish into thin air right before our eyes?
Now that Thane Hraldi and Thane Svyne have agreed to meet, we should return to Jarl Morryn's hunting lodge.\n\nGo on, friend. Rigurt will meet you there.

I wish we could follow you, but against a foe like Lord Falgravn, we would only get in the way. \n\nIt feels like cowardice, but I'm old enough to know the difference between a fool's death and a death worth dying. Nonetheless, forgive me.
You must be one of the recruits from the mainland. Did Tyrvera send you?
You look sturdy enough. Vampires and Sea Giants have invaded the island of Kyne's Aegis. We need all the willing warriors we can find to repel the attack!

Your return may be too late. Lady Ninetha ran off to meet Freiwen at the tree she described. She wanted to be with her before the end. If we don't act quickly, she will die. \n\nWere you successful in obtaining the memories?
Are you investigating this now as well? We already have too many people involved as it is.
At first, I didn't believe Rigurt was an ambassador. He's not exactly what you'd expect.
Chief Urzikh wouldn't put us in harm's way without cause. There has to be some kind of explanation.
I have my daughter back! How can I ever repay any of you? Please, if you are ever in Morthal again, come see me. There will always be a warm fire waiting for you.
Dark forces all around us these days. Have you noticed? Nowhere to hide from it.
That's that then. Had enough excitement for one day?

An undead army shattered, an evil Vampire Lord destroyed, and a monstrous I-don't-know-what banished back to Oblivion. You do incredible work.\n\nSeriously, I don't know what might have happened if you weren't here. Thanks.

Well, well. Rigurt the Brash's surprisingly comely friend! I don't have any unopened bottles left, but you could probably fill a flagon if you're willing to mix a few of the vintages. \n\nSo? Get drinking! There isn't anything else to do, is there?
Save some vampires for me, eh? My axe is thirsty!
Creatures of ice and snow, bah! Give me something of substance to hit, like a giant or a Reach barbarian!
I knew there was something wrong, but this? How could Svargrim throw in with the Gray Host? It's brazen, even for him.
This is bad. It's Karthwatch all over again ….
You did it! Just keep Master Dren's attention over there, all right? Want to let him cool down a bit before I tell him we're out of biscuits.

My assistant, Borfree, has my journal. Find it, read my notes, and acquire the incantation. Also, tell him to come get me. Someone nearly took a swig of me!\n\nOh, I suppose introductions are in order. I am Narsis Dren—famed historian, etcetera.
So much of what happens next rests on Fennorian's shoulders. I hope the pressure doesn't get to him. He's such a sensitive soul.
You're here for my howlwater, aren't you? How in the Twelve Strongholds does everyone know when the latest batch is ready? It's ridiculous!
One last riddle, assistant! One final test! Then I … we, will reap the rewards!\n\nSo, tell me. What did Maelmoth's tome reveal?
I'll venture to Jarl Morryn's cabin shortly. I believe I need to be alone for a moment.
You are here to return Maelmoth's journal, I assume?\n\nIt does my heart good to know that not everyone in Solitude is as careless and irresponsible as that Narsis Dren.
How could Meridia allow such corruption? Why wouldn't the Lady of Life and Light protect us from such darkness?
Talk to Priest Bavian. Can't you see I'm in pain?
By the gods, I never ran so fast in my life.\n\nI should have helped the others, but all I could think about was getting away from that evil storm.
So much blood, so much pain. And on Meridia's holy ground. How could this have happened here?
It's over. At last, after so many years, it's over.
Not looking for new friends. Best move along before I make things unpleasant.
Plan to pick up a rake and help me? No? Then off you go.
We almost died because of this alchemy! These methods cannot be trusted!
Speak with me again once Gabrielle's taught you the basics.\n\nI know I can come across as … chilly. But truthfully, I'm anxious to get you into the field.
So far so good, eh? You're making fine progress. You'll be a member of the Circle soon enough.
Stay clear of the barrow. There's sorcery at work down there.

Now, I need to get up the nerve to report my findings. Part of that includes telling Gabrielle that I went against her wishes. Hopefully she'll go easy on me.\n\nThank you for listening, and for all your help.

Time to get your hands dirty! The Eye can show you where to find an antiquity, but digging it up is more of a do it yourself affair.\n\nJust take your time. Rushing the excavation can destabilize the site, and that wouldn't do at all!
Things will go back to normal now that this is all over with. I'm glad the chief spared Mazog.
I trust my chief. If letting Mazog off without punishment is truly the best course of action, I won't argue. Chief Urzikh knows what she's doing.
Not now. Just let me drown my sorrows in peace.
Is this the friend you were talking about? Does this mean we're getting out of here?
It's a wonderful day for a drink, isn't it, friend? The more the merrier. What say you join us in tossing back a mug like a true Nord?
Even if I never fight again, I can die happy knowing I outlived Skreg the Undefeatable.

Ah, hello, fellow traveler! Do you have a moment to speak? I was hoping to trouble you for some directions.\n\nHave you ever been to Blackreach? Some say it's just a legend, but I believe it to be a real place, one ripe for the taking!

I'm certain you'll find that book a worthwhile read! Once we gather the funds to open the Temple of Jhunal again, I look forward to seeing you at our services!\n\nNever let it be said that the Nords of Skyrim are not lore seekers as well.
What has happened to our city? Our kingdom? Has the high king truly abandoned us?
Everyone's talking about what happened in the palace. Is High King Svargrim really trying to destroy the kingdom?
I need a moment to catch my breath.
Things like the Shademother make me hope that my next subject for research turns out to be pure fiction.
Oh, dark days are upon us! The Gray Host, an army raised from the dead!\n\nHow will we survive such horrors? How?
I never met Jarl Olfwenn, but I've visited Karthwatch on occasion. It was a beautiful town. I hope its people rest easy.
Forcing our friends out was wrong, but we feared for our lives. I will regret it for the rest of my life.

I swear, people come down here and go crazy. First those witches start planting weird sticks in the ground, then everyone goes running into the Dwarven ruins near town. If there's a quicker way to die, I don't know it.
Another new recruit? Well, welcome to Dusktown!\n\nJust keep your head down, work hard, and you'll do fine. And if anyone mentions vampires, just smile and nod. Smile and nod.
Thank you for saving Rasir. Our people need him now more than ever.
You are doing the Divines work. Deliver their light to deepest reaches of this world.
Maybe I'll head back down to those ruins once you've stopped that mechanical terror. There are bound to be some less dangerous discoveries to be made.
Let's try to keep things quiet, all right?\n\nKeep an eye out for anything or anyone who might get us into the keep. I'll do the same.
Sure our chief has some strange ideas, but who am I to question them? The clan must remain unified to survive.\n\nMor Khazgur needs a change. We can't keep struggling like this.
I wouldn't travel any deeper into the Hollow, stranger. It's dangerous in there.
So there's a pass phrase. "We Shall Rise Again". What does that even mean? Adusa always handles the riddles. Ugh. How's that for irony?\n\nLet's look around. The answer's here somewhere.
Welcome to Dusktown, traveler. Enjoy your stay, and try not to stray too far into the dark.
Well, go on then! Read through the guild listings. You may find something that strikes your interest, no?
If you're going to tell me someone else is dead, you better make it worth my time.
Yes, yes, I'll be there. Just, by the Gods, give me a bit to collect myself.
You almost forgot your reward!
We don't have anything else to discuss, right? I need to focus on the curing, or that's two days of work for nothing.
Go on, I'll catch up.

I heard you and my brother talking. Thank you for agreeing to accompany him into that terrible place. I was afraid I was going to lose both of my beloved siblings.\n\nBut with your help, I think Hamvir will be safe and Hedrynne will be cured.
Good traveler, would you happen to be heading in the direction of the Chillwind Depths?
Before Brun passed out, he raved about seeing wolves made of bone and ghosts in the snow. He won't stop shivering. Gods, I hope Ninetha can help him.
This is humiliating, but … my soul is trapped inside this ludicrous child's toy. I need someone with a corporeal form to help return me to my body. Interested?
Mind yourself in here and out there. A storm destroyed our town, but I'll be damned if I let anyone cause more mischief for these survivors.
Please, leave me alone. I … I have nothing to say.
My neighbor, Trubin … he attacked me! Like a ravenous beast he was!
Saarthal …. I mean, something had to be there, right? Clearly. But what? Atmoran relics? No, no, no, no. Too obvious.\n\nOh, I'm sorry, can I help you?
I don't know how we'll recover from this. I worry for the future of our clan.
Welcome to the Gwylim Annex. Try not to trip over the egos.

Another case solved. Though we weren't dealing in spirits today, I have no doubt you'd make a fine ghost hunter. You have a natural talent for investigation. \n\nElle has my sympathy. It is not easy to condemn someone you love.
Did Gwendis bring in reinforcements without telling me?\n\nI've told the young one time and again—her suspicion is unnecessary. I swear I only wish to help. Maybe you can talk some sense into her.
I knew Nathari's ideas were folly, but this? With her own hand, she gave her kin to the darkness.\n\nShe would have killed all of us if you and Arana hadn't arrived.
I think I'm as ready as I'll ever be. Delaying the inevitable won't help anyone. And it won't get me the answers I need.\n\nCome on, let's go see what's on this secret island.

The news that Lady Belain was invoking the Prophecy of the Dark Heart. I never expected it to lead to the decimation of my old clan at the hands of my sister!\n\nStill, I can't help feeling that this was a rehearsal for something even more terrible.

This must be Blackreach. I've read the legends, but I never thought it was real. The stories hardly do it justice. Perhaps one day I'll have an opportunity to explore it more fully. For now, we have work to do.\n\nAre you still with me, my friend?

Such anguish, such pain. Souls trapped in Molag Bal's realm wither over the centuries, but this Dark Heart. It stripped that creature of its vitality almost instantly.\n\nI wish it had told us more and could have been more coherent.

Oh, I'm sorry. Are you here for a tour? I'm afraid they've all been suspended until this mess with the Imperial army is resolved. \n\nIf I could offer a suggestion? Turn around and head for the safety of Evermore's walls.

The story of the Dark Heart … the Ghostsong clan knows it well. My clan. Once.\n\nI need to speak with my sister, Nathari. She studied the old secrets. Knows about prophecies both ill and fair. If anyone can glean the mind of Lady Belain, it's her.

Another old friend lost to Nathari's madness. That's Senan, a werewolf with many winters. He was a fierce warrior in his youth and a wise mentor in his later years.\n\nThat sheet of parchment, does it contain words you can read?
I'll find Scholar Diel's camp straightaway. I'm in your debt. If I can do anything to aid you, all you have to do is ask.
I will go to Scholar Diel's camp now. We are most fortunate you came to our aid.

I came to Bangkorai Garrison seeking recruits for the Pyre Watch. HoonDing help us, I did not expect those villains to arrive and send innocent people fleeing for shelter.\n \nI am grateful you saved the scholars. Now, what can I do for you in return?
When you're ready, activate the mechanisms on each of those platforms in sequence. This process should be less risky than what we attempted earlier. I believe.
Don't look at me, you were the one working all the contraptions before. If you're worried, I'm sure Verandis knows what to do.
Fire up that rotten contraption. I'll be right behind you.
Well, the Darkstorm isn't going to stop itself. Let's see about getting this portal open, shall we?
Remember, <<1>> for jobs you can handle on your own, and <<2>> or <<3>> for jobs that require groups to deal with.\n\nFor every task you complete, you will be paid for your efforts.
Talk to Verandis before we start poking around that castle. Place looks creepy.

I now understand the what of our enemy's plan, if not the why of it. Rada had centuries to set this in motion, yet I don't see how the orrery can free the Gray Host.\n\nAs for Lady Belain … the Dark Heart beats again. Her Nighthollow are reborn.

I couldn't have gotten through all this without your help. If not for you, I might never have learned the truth about Count Verandis and his connection to the Gray Host. How he tried to forge a peace with mortals, even way back then.

It is good to see you, Exarch Verandis. Lord Rada al-Saran will be pleased you accepted his invitation. You have been terribly missed.\n\nExarchs Ulfra and Tzinghalis asked me to send you to them as soon as you arrived. They wish to speak with you.

My ward and I have much to discuss. I should not have kept this secret for so long. Given the circumstances, Gwendis deserves to know the truth.\n\nI promise, after that I will find out what the Gray Host has planned. I give you my word.
Good. Make it quick. Rada al-Saran's preparing to summon his Darkstorm even as we speak.
It's still hard to believe this is real. Verandis returned all these souls to Markarth.
Where are they?\n\nOh hello! I don't suppose you've seen a big dumb Nord and a beautifully soft bunny around here, have you?

Me and <<1>> decided this isn't really the place for a shouting match. We promised to keep our tempers in check, at least until we get back home. And <<2>> approves!\n\nAnyway, thanks again for your help.
<<<1>> thumps her foot once and stares at the next hill.>

Can you smell it? Something foul and acrid. There's something sinister down here. We must be on the right track. \n\nThe source of the contaminated root has to be down here somewhere. Let's scout farther ahead.
Apprentice Fialyn believes the spirits sent you to aid us, outsider, and who am I to disagree?\n\nTalk to her and she will give you a gift. To thank you for saving our village.
Be careful, five-claw. Adusa has rarely walked into a room full of hostile vampires without something going terribly wrong.
You must be here about our notice. Well, scamp, you either want to join the Undaunted or you need instructions on how to wipe your arse.\n\nSo, which is it? You here for the plunder?

Your investigations uncovered that Ard Caddach's advisor, Lady Belain, is working with the Gray Host. And that she's a vampire. To hide that from me takes great power.\n\nTell me exactly what you heard during Rada al-Saran's conversation with her.
Use the keystone, my friend. It's finally time for me to confront Rada al-Saran.
I wanted to finish this, but Belain … she's too strong. And the Gray Host …. I tried to return to Markarth … but got turned around.

<This table is set up to conduct some kind of alchemical experiment. It might be possible to reproduce the results with the right ingredients. A skilled alchemist might even be able to improve upon it.>
You should talk to Caddach. He's been pacing like a caged senche cat since I got back, demanding answers.\n\nI probably could have told him what happened, but I didn't want to.

We did as you said, rover. We defended the city and kept our people safe. Then, all of a sudden, the Gray Host turned and fled. And I barely got to kill a dozen or so of the bastards myself!\n\nDo I have you to thank for this unexpected turn of events?

Freyleth lied to me. To all of us. Still, we accomplished what I set out to do. We freed the Lothid clan from that monster, Boss Trenlor.\n\nWhatever happens next is up to them. It's time for me to walk a different path.

The outsider returns. But are you a true warrior or a parasite like these damned leeches?\n\nDid you do as Lady Belain asked? Did you deal with Arana? Tell me you have her head in your pack. I've got a pike on the walls waiting to be decorated.

<This table is set up to conduct some kind of alchemical experiment. It might be possible to reproduce the results with the right ingredients. A skilled alchemist might even be able to improve upon it.>

<This table is set up to conduct some kind of alchemical experiment. It might be possible to reproduce the results with the right ingredients. A skilled alchemist might even be able to improve upon it.>

The Gray Host broke and scattered to the four winds, harrier. You and Arana's doing, I suppose?\n\nYou can tell me all about it later. Caddach wants to hear your tale. He does seem to think he's in charge around here, after all.
This is going to work perfectly. I can taste it! You look just like any other servant. Trenlor will never suspect a thing.\n\nJust drop the mushroom in his chalice and offer him a drink!

Now, Caddach's eager to get this under way. If it were anyone else keeping him waiting … well, it's not just anyone else keeping him waiting. So he'll bide.\n\nEnjoy the moment, harrier. You only live once. Well, some do, in any respect.

Ahem. Sai and I were just talking about the Ashen Lord. And, well, a few other topics came up. Nothing that bears mentioning. Of course that bears mentioning, Sai. \n\nLook, partner, you understand, right?

Don't think it's just Verandis I expect to visit. It'd be nice bumping into you somewhere other than a moldy cavern once in a while.\n\nCastle Ravenwatch is always open to you. It's not like we have a shortage of guest rooms.
Your vote of confidence is always encouraging.\n\nGwendis could use some of that as well, I think. Have a word with her, won't you?
It seems I spoke too soon when I bade you a final farewell. I'm glad to have the opportunity to see you again, my friend. None of this would have been possible without you.
We've reminisced enough, there are more pressing matters that require your attention. Like Ard Caddach's dwindling patience. \n\nWe'll catch up later—in fact, I demand it.

Trust takes time to build, but we must start somewhere. I couldn't have done it without Svana—Jarl Svana. Watching her put aside past differences between Eastern and Western Skyrim for the sake of her people has made quite an impression on me.

Feh, adventurers. Come and go as you please. Keep three kings and a jarl biding on their thumbs in a crowded hall. Suppose you've earned that right, rover!\n\nNear everybody in this room wouldn't be here if it wasn't for you.
Good to see you alive and well. It's good to see everyone alive and well! I don't know to what gods we should be giving our thanks, but I wager we all owe you a good portion.
Thank you again for agreeing to help Lyris and I with our little problem. It seems there is always trouble that needs fixing, but it's good to find a moment for celebration now and again.
If the sentry allowed you to enter the throne room, you must have news to share with Ard Caddach. So why are you talking to me? Making the ard wait is … unwise.
I knew we'd find Bradan here at this time of day. Introduce yourself. Talk to him. He won't help if he doesn't get a sense of you and your purpose.
The stockpiles were spotted to the east and south. If you can find out what the Gray Host is using them for, then we'll owe you a favor. And true Reachfolk never renege on a favor.
Nathari has forced my hand. If any Ghostsongs are to survive the day, she must be stopped.\n\nForgive me, sister. I never should have left.
We're closed—oh, it's you. Was it there? Was there a new package with my name scrawled on it?

Damn that Lady Belain! She slipped away like a snake through a crack in the wall.\n\nAh well. We'll catch her soon enough. Right now, you should be working on getting us into Bthar-Zel. Go on. Find the door.
With your help, the wards are back in place and the spirits smile on Karthwasten once more.\n\nThank you, my friend.
Lady Belain poisons Caddach with fancy words and visions of a Reach kingdom. He needs to see through her lies.

That was a proper Reach victory! Remember that beating in your chest, harrier, and the sweat on your brow. No metal beast—big or small—knows what victory feels like. That's how we win. That's how we always win.\n\nCome on. Let's get out of here.
As soon as we lost Lady Belain's trail, we decided to instead pick up yours.\n\nAnd I see you've had some success. If the entrance to Bthar-Zel is here, I'm certain we can find it.
You cleared all three wings and defeated the fiercest spirits my sister can bind. Many Spiritblood have died attempting what you accomplished today.\n\nYou have more to do, though.
I propose a simple arrangement. A truth for a truth. Ask a question. I will answer honestly, then I will ask a question in turn.\n\nA fair compromise, don't you agree?

The few Dwarven ruins I've visited were cramped and industrial affairs. Whatever scholars walked these halls must have been among the elite.\n\nLet us explore this place and see if we can find Rada and Lady Belain. They must be deeper inside.

I never expected Master Pythis to betray the Order. He was one of the best. If we hadn't intervened when we did, what kind of chaos would he have wrought?\n\nBut, at least the device is secure now. The Psijics will ensure it stays that way.
You again? You dare to disgrace Understone Keep with your presence, outsider? That takes guts, I'll give you that.\n\nWhat's your business in the ard's keep?

The more I look through this book, the more uneasy I feel. Something about it … I don't know. I wish I could understand these symbols.\n\nI know I have a job to do, but a little voice in my head says I should leave it here.
She may be bossy, but it's a relief to have Lyranth back. With her powers we can make our way to that ritual and stop it. Hopefully saving everyone we can along the way.\n\nEspecially my father.
Welcome, stranger. Have you come to assist with the Imperial Resettlement Project? If you have an Imperial charity writ, I can accept your contributions here.

Fortune upon your travels. I hope you receive what you need from the Old Life ceremony, whether it be joy, or closure, or something in between.\n\nBefore you leave … may I ask a favor of you, purely at your own convenience?
The Reach is better off without those Hagravens making free folk into briarheart slaves. You've done a great service to all the clans by burning their briarheart tree.
Lyris and I must discuss what you helped us learn here today. We'll meet you outside in a moment.
The steam, the heat—this is the Brimstone Den, all right. Mehrunes Dagon truly enjoys his lava.\n\nProbably best to get going as soon as possible. The fumes can't be good for you.
We need a moment alone, partner. Wait for us outside, please.
It's good to see that tree burn, after all the pain it caused my people. Give me a moment to enjoy this, friend.\n\nOh, and I think Medone wants to speak with you.

Gods take me, my insides are boiling. I've put nothing but leaves in my belly for too long.\n\nFynvagh needs to let us make camp. Why rush to shelter in Markarth if we're on death's door when we get there?!
My sons and I have walked for what feels like days, now. We must bide here for a bit—on account of my old bones, and Drisoal's weak spirit. A shame to our clan, that one.

You heard of what happened at Markarth? The Gray Host attacked the city from below! \n\nWe planned to take refuge in the city of stone on Ard Caddach's word, for safety. Now we head there to see if our loved ones are among the dead.
I've traveled all across the Reach, seen clans of all types and beasts beyond description. My tales deserve every coin they earn.
If you know the truth, just get it over with. I don't expect your sympathy or understanding.\n\nWhat happened was an accident. I don't know what more to say than that.
I have to think about what to put in this report. What can we learn to stop the next band of vampire recruits from joining up with the Gray Host? Assuming I get another chance ….
I'm not sure the spirits sent you, but you helped us nevertheless.\n\nI suppose I owe you an apology. And my thanks.
I expected better of you, outsider. This is what I get for involving you in the business of the clans.\n\nDamn you. You've doomed these clans.

I knew Eslyn might prickle at the idea of the handfasting, but to go through all of this only to accomplish nothing? Foolish. And I've lost face in front of both the chief-of-chiefs and Vateshran Barth.
I'm bound to follow my chief, so I followed when he left. But … I keep thinking of the vateshran's story. I wonder why the elders won't share it with the rest of the clan?
My son has brought shame to our clan. Had the chief-of-chiefs not been watching, that would have ended quite differently.
I don't think I entirely understand what just happened. The handfasting is off? Madearn kept his promise to me?\n\nI fear what this means for my clan, but I won't deny that I'm relieved.

I'm sorry for my father, outsider. He's too stubborn to listen.\n\nBut he won't be chief forever. Just because we didn't end the feud today doesn't mean we won't end it in the future. Eslyn and I made a connection today. That's no small thing.

Well, we tried. The feud won't end today, but at least I'm not being leashed into a marriage and Madearn won't have to break his word. \n\nThis is not a failure, only a setback. Madearn and I will spread the tale to our clans, I swear it.

Peace between the Eagleseers and Six-Fords at last. I know it's not what these two originally intended, but given the way they look at each other, it seems fitting.\n\nI feel for the lass Madearn was to marry, but Reachfolk are hardy. She'll be fine.
The cave will reveal what it knows … if you prove worthy.\n\nGo on. I will speak to the Titanborn if that is her desire.
Arana's ready for you.\n\nRemember, thinblood, you'll be in the presence of our sacred spirits, so be respectful.

I hope Apprentice Orla still lives. Hircine tests our limits, but he is never needlessly cruel.\n\nGood hunting, wanderer. Find Orla and the Symbol of Uricanbeg at Lost Valley Redoubt, and then this shrine will be complete. Let us prove we are worthy.
All these strangers lurking around the Reach. They bring chaos into our home! \n\nNone of these dogs would stand tall in a fight against true Reach warriors.
Ardanir has offered us a place among … what did he call them? The Wayward Guardians. \n\nDefenders of the Reach, he said. Yes. Perhaps in this way I can atone.
My clan may have forgotten me, but it seems these Wayward Guardians believe my life still has value.\n\nThank you, stranger. I won't waste this opportunity.

By even agreeing to perform the Vateshran's Rites, you show more courage than other outsiders. The Reach crawls with those who don't belong here these days. But only you show us this respect.\n\nLet's hope you survive.
What an incredible place we discovered. A pity it contains such horrors.
So, you're working with the Ard?
The Ard knows more than he leads on.
You look about the way Verandis described you. The count would like to see you, if you aren't too busy. We do have an army of vampires and werewolves to put a stop to.

Hircine demands we hunt to survive, but he doesn't demand we do it alone. I'm grateful the high shaman sent you to help.\n\nFind the Symbol of Uricanbeg at the old tower on the rise. But beware of the minotaur. It's a mighty hunter in its own right.
Outsider, your face is a welcome sight.\n\nI haven't seen this many happy faces since we were last at Hroldan Ring. Eslyn and I were just remarking on it as we were … catching up.
I'm glad I got a chance to speak with you. After hearing all you've done, seeing you once more put a smile on my face. It's given me hope.

Adusa heard that Verandis had been imprisoned in the Void, but he's here!\n\nForgive me. This one is glad to see you, five-claw. Your help at Reachwind Depths was much appreciated. Without your assistance, Kathad would still be in the Deep Tombs.

Hear ye and be inspired! I have heard the word of the Dread Lady and those words have led me to you.\n\nI bring you greetings and a message from my lovely and powerful mistress. Prepare to be enlightened!

We need to get Stibbons away from Rectavius and cut off the source of the duplicates. Then we need to destroy the voriplasm that contains the sorcerer's essence. That should break the curse.\n\nI expect we'll find them both beyond the main doors.
Dryskin, know that this shrine is sacred to Sithis and the primordial chaos. Mind yourself, for we have had enough trouble with visiting outsiders this day.

I can't believe we did it! We saved Blackwood! My brother Beragon has got to be impressed. Oh, he won't show it, but I'll know it!\n\nOh, everyone is starting to head out. Keshu back to Gideon, Rian to Leyawiin, and the Ambitions back to the temple.
Calia is having a hard time with the idea that she survived and Destron did not. If you could speak to her … well, it might do some good. I have no gift for words of comfort.
Portals, just as we feared. At least they can't transport overwhelming forces in that manner.\n\nGo check on the guardhouse. Make sure Eveli and the Ambitions are secure.

The people of the Blackwood owe you their gratitude, mercenary. You and Eveli both.\n\nIf not for your courage, Vandacia and his Waking Flame cult would have unleashed unthinkable destruction. The losses would have been devastating.

Damn it! Too late again! How is the Dark Brotherhood always one step ahead of us? And where's the servant who brought her meal? We've got a real locked-door mystery here.\n\nLet's look around and try to figure out what happened.

The Wood Elf appears to be agitated. Or is that how she portrays excitement? Nevertheless, go on and show her what you discovered first. I wouldn't want her to explode from the anticipation.\n\nI saw that happen once with a Daedroth. Made quite a mess.
By the powers vested in me, I dub thee Jester King Emeric's Champion of Charcuterie!\n\nNow get in there are carve yourself a rasher!

I'm glad you were able to reach Councilor Vandacia before anything untoward befell him. I'm still trying to comprehend the murders of the others.\n\nBut don't let me detain you. Lovidicus is anxious to get your perspective on the Dark Brotherhood.
My husband and our dog Chaero should be close by. I'm certain he's all right, but I appreciate Captain Rian sending someone to check on him.
Thank you, kind friend, for assisting my lady. If any harm had befallen her, I'd be devastated to no end.
You have been a great boon to the Resolutions of Zenithar. I could not have found the Golden Anvil without you, let alone save it from its ignominious fate.
We should not remain here. The breeze still stinks of death. \n\nLet us speak outside.
Thank the gods Councilor Lovidicus and the legates survived the attack. Even Countess Caro was able to slip away unharmed.\n\nWe were lucky. The casualty count could have been much higher.

Now I can add facing down a Daedric Prince to my already impressive list of accomplishments. Food connoisseur, master assassin, consummate vossa-satl player, and now this.\n\nI suppose I should thank you for getting me mixed up in this.
A moment please. Talk to the scribe while I catch my breath.
I'm still alive. I can't believe I survived all that but Destron didn't. It's not fair. None of this is.\n\nI don't know what I'm supposed to do now.
When you find the missing servant, let me know. In the meantime, I have a few brigadines sweeping the grounds for any sign of the assassin, but my guess is they are long gone.
Zaudrus's ritual failed. It appears he wished to consecrate this site with the blood of mortals. But for what purpose?\n\nThe answers lie with the Baron himself.
Well? What did the scroll say? Do we finally know the emperor's secret?
If there's a chance we can repay what you've done for us, my garrison is at your disposal. You have my word.

Once we get Quistley out of here, I'm done. I've paid my debt to his family three times over.\n\nAll right, I think I know how to sort this out. If Tenarei is prepared to listen, that is. I'm willing to overlook the knock on the head to settle this.
Right. I suppose this is the last time we'll see one another until we get to the other side of all this. Keep an eye on Seeks, won't you? And try not to have too much of a daring escapade without me.
I hope you've got ideas, because this is way outside my area of expertise!

When I heard these Painted Eyes talking about their demands, I thought we were doomed—maybe a little flattered that they thought we were worth that much—but doomed nonetheless.\n\nAnyway, these so-called revolutionaries are a chatty bunch.
Those were good chains you broke. I should know, I made them. But better broken than binding me.\n\nI don't hear a battle going on—so, I'm guessing you didn't come with a battalion at your back.
I'll do whatever you say. Just get me out of here!
Finally, someone besides these Painted Eyes. They threatened to break my left thumb if I didn't tell them what they wanted. That's my writing thumb!
I hope to see you again sometime. Although I must confess … now that I've finally found evidence supporting the legend of Phalevon, I'm not really sure what I'm supposed to do next.

While you talk to the Ambitions and figure out a new place to hide them, I'll work with Governor Keshu's people. Try to get a better handle on this threat her spymaster has detected.\n\nIf Vandacia is nearby, I'll flush him out.

Eveli tells me your mission went well, mercenary. That you recovered a third Ambition. Another dryskin male.\n\nThe Temple of Dibella has never had so many prestigious guests before. I will owe the priests for this favor.
I'll be ready in a moment. In the meantime, examine that book I found as I made my way through the cellar. It explains a lot.
Vandacia is going to win. We saw ourselves. He was drawing power from us. Like sipping wine from a chalice.
We learned about our origin and we saw one possible, awful future. Now we're ready to finally gain control of our powers.\n\nLet's go see Xynaa now.
I greet you, mortal. As with Sombren, I shall do all that I can to aid the twins.\n\nBut first, they must survive the Ashen Forest. They must walk the Path of the Obelisks.
Well, this is … unexpected. I thought for sure he'd try to strangle me or something.\n\nLet's make our way back to the surface.
I'm not proud of what I've done to work off my own debts. I'm loath to admit it, but nothing good happens if I drag Quistley back to Larz-Tul.
You! I owe you such an apology. I could see everything you and Revus did. No one … no one has ever looked out for me before. Thank you!

All the fermented mudcrab apples you could ever want are in the baskets around the arena. Of course, you'll need this ticket to get in, and you'll have to get to them before King Boar, and you most definitely don't want to let him gulp too many down.
It's good to feel the sun through more than a crack in the roof. I could savor it for hours, but Zenithar would think me indolent.
Perhaps, before you rush off, you might unlock this cell? A favor in return for my showing you the switch?\n\nLet me again assure you, I am in control of my urges. I shall not harm you.
The courier's waiting right over there. Talk to them and find out what they've brought us.
Shame I didn't have a longer chat with that Hist, but we've probably overstayed our welcome as it is. Even with their creeper dead, there no telling what those crazy Sul-Xan will do next.

Go to our house and talk to Farrul. He'll explain everything. Or, at least as much as he's able. I'll be along shortly.\n\nJust remember to knock two times and only two times. That's our code. Farrul won't respond unless he hears exactly two knocks.
Leave me alone. Can't you see that I'm in mourning?
You did well to bring these twins to Gideon. I will make sure that they are well protected.\n\nIs it true, though? What Eveli told me? These are the Ambitions you sought?
Hey! So nice to see you! Come talk awhile!\n\nMathen and I are just, well, trying to get to know each other better!
First Councilor Abor and now more new faces? Where we will put all you people, this one has no idea.
Fort Blueblood? It's a fine place to work, I suppose. The brigadines mostly treat us well. At least, they treat us as well as any servants get treated.

The servants come to the kitchen to mutter and gossip. This one will not have it. Misaba asks that you do not distract them overly long, as they are already naturally lazy.\n\nWhat is it that you need?
I should probably get back to work. Come back when I'm off duty and I'll show you around the fort.
Someone's going to pay for this, I promise you that! But if Talaise died down here, who delivered the councilor's meal to the watchtower?\n\nHey, look. There's a sheet of paper lying next to her.

I attempted to open a portal that would take us out of this Daedric structure, but instead it dropped us here. Before I could try again, the cultists confronted us. And then ….\n\nWell, you saw what happened. I suggest you ask Destron to explain.
Did you find my dear Mathen? Can't I trust you to locate a simple cottage?
Whoever you are, please … help. They have my family.
Let us not waste time.\n\nWe need to destroy the skull of the fallen Shadowscale in order to ensure their spirit is fully released from Tumma-Maxath's grasp.
It seems Lady Yisara has made her decision. I see color in her cheeks. This bodes well, I think.
Scout Iscaria, Ivory Brigade Borderwatch garrison. We're in desperate need of help.
I'd always planned to take on an apprentice, but I'll admit, Cres is not quite what I had in mind.
Have you seen Annyce? She ran off. I knew I shouldn't have let Heseph watch her alone!
I want to believe that this is really Annyce, but … just keep seeing my sister when I look at her.\n\nPlease, you need to put an end to this. Can't live life looking over my shoulder like this.
Ah! Careful! You—you might have scared the mare. Who are you? What do you want?
Shhh. I want to hear my brother sing!

All right, you heard Lovidicus. Time to get back to work. While the councilors remain here and wait for the scribe to show up, we need to determine what your Dark Brotherhood friends are actually up to.\n\nShow me that letter you found in Gideon.

You understand this better than anyone. You found the letter. You saw the murders firsthand. You must convince Lovidicus of the seriousness of the Dark Brotherhood threat.\n\nOtherwise, the next councilor to die will be on your head.

Why is this the first I am hearing of a threat against the former members of the Elder Council? I should have been alerted to this the moment it came to light.\n\nThe Chamber of Legates and the Ivory Brigade are usually quicker to share information.
What's the big deal? This is the seventh time I tried running away in three years. Why are they all gawping at me like they're afraid to blink?

Ha! Think you can sail with me, wee one? I've felled Giants like trees! I've slapped a Dragon around until it got down and licked my hand! I've kicked Molag Bal in the arse, once, and he begged me to do it again!\n\nAnswer me this: why do we sail?

The high seas run deeper than any river, filled with the blood of enemies. A challenge awaits you, sailor. Are you prepared to give our journey your all, or will you wilt like a mushroom in summer?\n\nTell me! Speak true! Why do we sail?

So you've impressed the big bear and the hard turtle? So what? I walk in the shadow and sleep in the trees! I drink snake venom and piss honeyed mead! I'm the baddest, sharpest, meanest pirate on the high seas, but I don't sail alone.\n\nWhy?
Do you make it a habit to read other people's mail? That letter is personal and private, full of sensitive information.
I missed her. Even in the dream. It was easy to get lost in the adventure at first, but I think it would have been harder and harder to ignore feeling homesick. Knowing I couldn't go back.
Let's look around.
Was that Elam I saw outside? Never mind. Tell me later.\n\nI assume we're supposed to find something important in here? Let's look around.
There he is! No place else to run to. Talk to Salvitto and find out where this event is taking place.
Ah, you've returned. Were you able to acquire the silk I requested, or would you like to conclude our transaction in some other manner?
Oh … I see it in your tiny eyes. You're going to send me back. I made too much of a mess of this. I guess I wasn't meant for mortal life.
How do you choose? They all look so … impractical. Pretty, too. But not something I'd want to trek through the wilderness in.

Everybody was looking at me on the way here! You'd think they never saw a fancy-arsed woman with a bow before!\n\nAnd this dead stump! She won't let me aboard until she sees the invitation and the coin Salvitto gave you.
I'll stand guard. Just find that key and get back here as soon as you can.

Those cultists that attacked the Dark Brotherhood. That's the Order of the Waking Flame! They're those Mehrunes Dagon fanatics that attacked me when I first tried to learn about Leovic's secret.\n\nWe have to figure out how all this connects.

I am sure our combined heroism will save my tribe from this plight. \n\nThe Imperial lieutenant is just ahead. While you speak with him, I will head to the northern swamps to continue investigating. Meet me there when you are finished.

An interesting document. I'm not sure what these Ambitions that Emperor Leovic mentions might be, but it appears he shared the secret with his personal steward, Farrul Lupus.\n\nI hope I don't have to tell you how dangerous Longhouse secrets can be.
Naheesh Nurwul has a plan that will take all of us. Speak to her, she can explain it to you in better detail.
It appears that the Wood Elf wants to speak to you.\n\nGo on, but when you're finished, I think we should leave this place.
Those people … they wanted to take us away!
There might be hope yet! Speak with Naheesh Nurwul, it looks like she found help after all.
This looks interesting. Plus, in my experience, any room you make it this difficult to get to has to contain something important.\n\nI suggest you look around.

Such fun, don't you think? There's nothing better than the feeling of having just pulled off an amazing prank. Doesn't it flood your whole body?\n\nI hope you had as much fun carrying it out as I do hearing about it.
We must put our differences aside to overcome this challenge. I hope fighting together is a path toward making amends.\n\nGo to Xal Irasotl, use the ward to open the door. We will meet you there.
Imperials? They came to help?
You'd better get back to the Happy Crow and deal with that freeloader. We'll be fine now. Now that we're back together.

Come on, we need to get inside. Councilors Lovidicus and Faleria and the legates might still be alive. If there's a chance we can save them, we have to try! \n\nAnd Vandacia. That must have been what that vision I had was trying to warn me about.

The tribe will be telling stories of this for many years to come, I am sure! The mighty Heem-Jas, with his faithful partner, slashing through horrors in the darkness of ancient ruins without a shred of fear! \n\nThank you for your help, friend.

Hail! Come closer. You stand before a projection of the Duke of the Blackfeather Court. A grievous injustice has been done here and I must implore you for aid. Implore! \n\nMy flock has been tricked! Lured here with foul magic and promises of shinies!
Remember, see <<1>> for jobs you can handle on your own, or <<2>> for jobs that require groups of heroes.\n\nYou will be paid handsomely for every task you complete.
How could you do this? How could you wake me? Cres said I would live in that dream forever!
Where are we? Some kind of tomb? Where's my treasure? Last I remember I was in my treasure room.
So delicious. So moist, and rich, and warm. So much frosting. This one can just barely still taste them.
Fish aren't biting. Seems to be the story of my life.

Hello, stranger. I wish I could offer hospitality, or even some sap from our Hist. But, hmm, perhaps you have lucky timing.\n\nYou can see that our village has crashed upon some rough rocks. We won't survive much longer without a strong hand to aid us.
My daggers represent a life I thought I left behind.\n\nIf you are serious about my help, find them. Bring them back, and I will become the Sudden Gust once more.
I wonder if the Temple of Mara would marry us posthumously? It was his dying wish after all. Maybe I should employ a priest of Arkay for the ceremony, so he can pass on without regrets?
You have no business being here. Leave.

I find the elder councilors to be overly enamored of their own voices, but this one still appreciates their wisdom.\n\nTalk to Lovidicus. He refuses to make a decision until he hears from you about events in Gideon.

Vandacia says the Dark Brotherhood plans to kill us all! Murder us in our sleep! Cut us down in the streets of Leyawiin and Gideon! Can the brigadines even protect us from such a threat?\n\nApologies for my hysterics. You should talk to Lovidicus.

Meer-Ta is a master of arcane arts. I have never met him, but I have heard that he can be kind of a brute to deal with.\n\nYou did an excellent job with Elossi, though. No doubt you will convince him as well.
Kaoc! I can already smell them on you. I do not even need to ask.\n\nPut them right up to Otumi-Ra's nose. Let him get a big old whiff. Hopefully that snaps him right out.
Go on, ojel. Drink your fill with courage! I shall match you drink for drink. If you succeed, then I join your quest with joy in my heart.\n\nIf you fail, well, hopefully there's a doctor nearby.

These beasts passing as Argonians stumbled into some powerful magic here. And of course, their only thought is thievery. Gah!\n\nGo, find the Binding Word. Bring it here so we can undo the only clever thing these creatures have managed.
I suppose you helped the Dark Elf rescue her associates? You'll hear no complaint from me. I can report the matter closed and get back to a worthwhile patrol.

We did it! My little brother is safe and that backstabbing viper, Xigira's plans are in shambles. I almost wish I could see what Dagon does to her for her failure, but my imagination's probably better than his anyway.
The Daedra lady wants to talk to you. Go on. I'm still trying to wrap my vines around everything that happened.

Say thank you, little mortal. I have read the ensorcelled scroll and I know where we need to go next on our quest to learn Leovic's secret.\n\nUnless, that is, you and the Elf discovered something in the coded documents?
I hate all this waiting around for something to happen! Especially when I know our time is short. We have control of our power for the moment, but Sombren assures us that it won't last.

I feared the worst when no one was here waiting for us. There were almost half a dozen that tried to escape. I prayed that they'd make it to freedom. I prayed and prayed. The Three must have heard us, even out here.
Look what they did to her. To my mother! They nearly killed her. Killed all of us!\n\nThey won't get away with it. It may not be now, but one day I'll make these fetchers pay for what they did to us.
I want to quit this wretched place, but after all that digging I need a moment to catch my breath.

You see now, the great shinies that tricked the Court into this miserable place? But they only show lies. Lies! When one crow looks upon it, they see a likeness that copies their every move! These are no treasures! Just tricks!
Away with you. I'm trying to blend here.
Thanks mightily for getting me out of there. I don't know how much longer I could've lasted.
Choose any weapon that strikes your fancy. I can't speak to their quality, but they seem sturdy enough to dispatch a beast or two.

You have fulfilled my request. Bahsei is dead. But with bare abdomen and bowed head, I beg one more task of you.\n\nWhile this gate stays open, Xalvakka still threatens this land. Dispatch the creature and close this portal. Only then are we safe.

The news that Malosza made it to safety strengthens my spine, ojel. Though I still feel surprised he did not send a more familiar face.\n\nPerhaps this is how it should be. A stranger coming from the marsh to preserve our home. Yes, this feels correct.

I open my claws in humility, wanderer. Please, stay to hear my story.\n\nHave you heard of the Sul-Xan tribe? Vicious and unrelenting, they wander through the swamps attacking any they find. Now they've fallen upon my home in Rockgrove.

Hail, dryskin. Not sure where your feet are taking you, but if it's to the shrine down the road, I suggest you reconsider.\n\nNisswo Somarz has had more than enough trouble with outsiders for one day.
I'm going to take it slow, but I should be all right getting away now that you and Mirri are here causing a commotion.\n\nI hope you're able to save the others.
Thanks to you, there will be something left for the Hist when my time finally comes … but I did not expect the Dark Elf to stick her neck out for me.

Here. Let me update your map. These are places Jirich visits during her daily routine. If something befell her, it happened somewhere along this path.\n\nMeanwhile, I have Eveli Sharp-Arrow checking locations in the city. She was very eager to help.
Poor Councilor Jirich! What happened to her, it's so awful!\n\nI was the last one to talk to her. I should have gone with her. I should have been there when it happened!

I'm sorry my brother gave you the less glamorous tasks of this operation while we sit here writing titillating prose. \n\nBut I promise, we will be especially scathing. My brother and I will give Pungent Adder a tongue-lashing he won't soon forget!

Ah, you're going to help us? Lovely. \n\nI trust Iulius mentioned that we would pay you for your services. We may be in a tight spot currently, but rest assured, if you succeed in this, you will reap the full benefits of our appreciation.
Don't tell me what you found in the watchtower. I'm just a simple brigadine.\n\nIf you have something to report, tell it to the commander.

I hope Granna Cerise can find some rest now. Let's head back to Gideon and clear her name. Keshu's mage and researcher is named Fire-From-Nowhere. Hopefully, he'll listen.\n\nRolaine was a murderous necromancer, and now all Blackwood will know!

I have so many questions, and no idea how to begin. Maybe … maybe you could speak to Clairene first? I feel like I could use a little more help. A word of introduction, I guess.\n\nBut let's make sure we're somewhere safe first.

I thought I'd wait out here, out of sight from the scoundrels who hide in that old tower. \n\nI just … I really need that ring back. I'm supposed to present it to my betrothed at a gathering tonight. Do you have it?
My stomach … burns. But the floor … so cool ….
Inventory and deliveries do not get sorted by themselves. This one is rather busy.

If you've been sent by the innkeeper, I will say it again: I did not steal anything. Nellor loses track of things and blames others. So you and your friend can—\n\nWait. Who are you? Why is he looking at me like that?
Captain Rian Liore. That's who you're looking for. If you're interested in helping Leyawiin, speak to him. He should still be outside the city gates.

Poor Calia. I hope Sombren's right and he can help her. But taking refuge in the Deadlands? That's like the sausage leaping out of the pan because it thinks the fire will be safer.\n\nAs for me, I never want to visit the Deadlands again.
I'll look into this strange stone immediately. It'll give me something to focus on with everything that's just … happened.

Eveli is waiting for you in Leyawiin Castle. She wants to discuss plans before the two of you set out to investigate the Dark Brotherhood sanctuary.\n\nI'd find her soon. I get the distinct impression that she isn't the most patient sort.
This isn't a very good time, stranger. Be on your way, unless you bring some new tidings about my wife.

Haven't we had this conversation already? The Dark Brotherhood didn't murder those councilors. I have no quarrel with you, and you none with me.\n\nNow turn around and leave before you force me to do something you'll definitely regret.
I'll continue to oversee the Ivory Brigade and make sure Leyawiin is protected. If we hear word of Vandacia or his cult, I'll send word immediately.
I'm not as young as I once was, but I must admit, I feel invigorated by all this! Being around you has roused my blood! \n\nI could not have done any of this without your help.

I don't know what to say! This has been such a day. First caught by slavers, then rescued by two brave heroes, and then learning one of them was a brother whom I thought dead.\n\nDo give me a moment. I'm quite undone!

Speak to Naheesh Nurwul. Tell her what we've learned about the totems. It will not be easy for her to hear that it was one of our own that caused all this, but she needs to know. She will know what to do next.
You can find Governor Keshu in her mansion in Gideon. I believe Eveli is already there.\n\nConsider this matter to be of the utmost importance, mercenary.

Let Councilor Lovidicus know what I deciphered from the coded document. That the vault that protects them is hidden in the ojel-bak.\n\nI wish I had been able to finish translating all the documents before Vandacia stole them.
Stare at me overly long, stranger, and it will not end well for you. \n\nIf you have business with me, speak quickly. I have neither patience nor time for fools.
Damn ancestors. If they want to make such a big deal of us paying our respects, they could put more effort into paying them back.
I'm Councilor Jirich's aide. She would have informed me of any schedule changes. It's not like her to simply disappear without a word.
Councilor Jirich is missing and the Ivory Brigade makes promises it can't keep. Something terrible has happened to her, I can feel it in my bones.
Councilor Jirich never showed up today. It's not like her to miss a scheduled meeting with a noble of high standing. I am very put out!

My inkwell is currently in the possession of a banker here, the result of an ill-advised card game. They seem to enjoy lording their victory over me, so they refuse to part with it at any price.\n\nI want it returned. I don't care how.
Make haste to the governor's mansion in Gideon and speak with Keshu the Black Fin. Our enemies will not wait for us to complete our preparations before they attack.
Mercenary, I have one more mission to send you on.
Did you recover the Shade Sickle? You did! Return it to my lady at once!

I would retrieve the tome myself, but I fear the Sul-Xan who inhabit Xi-Tsei and killed Nesh-Tei will try to disturb his remains. I must stay here and guard them.\n\nStrike the Sul-Xan down if they threaten you. Claim the tome and return.
Another mortal? Have you come to the Shrine of Nocturnal to grovel at my feet like that worthless acolyte, or will you betray my hospitality as well?

When we were growing up back in Seekhat-Xol, I would have never thought that someday my egg-brother would fall in love with a demon. Funny how things work out.\n\nLet's give them some time. They've got years of catching up to do.

I hope this won't come back to bite us in the tails. Still, I hold no grudge. Xyria is important to Xocin. As long as she is with us, I will help keep her safe.\n\nAnd if she turns on us, well … I'll send her back into the fire myself.

Remember me? Listen, about the last time we spoke, I ran off and you promised to come rescue me.\n\nOh, don't worry about it! I got a little mauled, but I understand. You were busy saving the world. I get it!
Do you really have it? The puzzle box? Truthfully, I barely remember what it looks like.

Xyria is a powerful ally and friend, and yet an outcast Dremora will almost certainly draw some measure of unwanted attention towards the Black Fin Legion and Gideon. It is a difficult decision.\n\nSpeak with Tee-Wan and Vos-Huruk. We must decide soon.
You return. Did you have any luck in Arpenia? You do not look any worse for wear, which is a comfort.\n\nDo you have the eggs?

Onimiril was the Mer who wronged me. A guild mage of Vulkhel Guard. A silver-tongued liar who cheated me out of my dearest possession and my life.\n\nReturn what's mine. Bring me the puzzle box and Irenni's failings will be forgiven.
You're back! Do you have the eggs from Arpenia?
They seek to force the Court to do their will. But we fly where we please. Where we please!

This one fears Arelette will be tempted by the grains near the Salted Wings Tavern and wind up someone's dinner! Please find her quickly. She had lustrous blue-green feathers. Takaano is certain she will stand out, for better or worse!
Lost souls flutter all around us, looking for a refuge. Best not to give them one.

Wouldn't get too close if I were you, friend. Apparently my run of bad luck is contagious. No one wants to come near me until this dark cloud is lifted.\n\nA lot of rubbish, I say. My luck will turn. Sooner or later.
The Stonewastes' my tribe's home for an eternity. To see it ruined like this, and so viciously … just unbearable.

These cheeky creatures think I can't tell them apart, but I know who's eaten. Can't let one of them hog all the food, not when they're so excited about the treasure they've stuck in that new hiding place of theirs.
That seemed to go well. Maybe. I can't tell. I'm terrible at reading her.
I can see that he tried, but that is decidedly too much. Perhaps I can ask the artist to refine some of the colors and remove some of the more ruffly bits.
Must the Chamber of Legates hold their meeting in my audience hall? I can barely hear myself think with all the commotion!
Elossi can act a little shy sometimes. She does not like much attention in her direction. Usually she sticks to the shadows.
I thought it might have been simple avarice that led to the corruption of the Knights of the Silver Rose, the truth is so much worse.

We are drawing close to something of immense power. I have no doubt it's this Cataclyst we've learned about. Now isn't the time or place for squabbling. We need to focus on finishing the mission and getting out of here alive.

Hmm? Ah yes, it is you. I was expecting you. You are perfect for this task, for I sense you already have many stories in your soul. But you desire more. You have followed the river to me, haven't you? Where the water that carries such stories flows.
I have fought many battles, friend. In some I recognized victory before the first blow was struck. In others I saw no hope of winning until the last enemy fell.\n\nToday was one of the latter.

By the Eight, that was close!\n\nAs a small favor to me, the next time you ask for my help, try to make sure we're not fighting creatures from Oblivion. I'd much rather deal with bandits or even a mundane monster or two.
There you are! I frankly did not expect to meet you again in this life. There were some bad moments when I found myself wondering how I would extricate myself when everyone else was dead.
I keep telling myself I'm getting too old for war, but I keep coming out the other side. I don't think I'll outdo the battle we had today though. Maybe I should retire on a high note.

Once more, you lead the Winds of Stonewastes to victory. Otumi-Ra's scales glimmer with life now, instead of a dull gray from drink. Even spiky Meer-Ta seems a little softer.\n\nMay your teeth stay sharp, and the breeze carry you well.

Truly impressive work for an ojel like yourself. And an even more impressive effort from myself if you noticed. I suspect even the dryskin bards shall chirp their songs about me about this day.\n\nNow I must be off. My studies can no longer wait.

I have not felt so strong in many, many seasons. Not since the day I hatched and crushed the head of an alit preying on my nest-kin have I felt so hardy.\n\nWe once again owe you a debt. When you wish it, come drink with me until we go blind!
Treasures abound, and still no sign of what we seek. I'll search every corner of this fortress before I leave without what was promised to me.
Allow the Anchorite to observe the relic. With any luck, she will be able to discover what secrets it holds.
Did you find Pibiha? Where is she? Is she all right?
The Crowborne Horror ebbs back. The darkness slinks away like a shadow scorned by the sun. \n\nYou were successful. I suppose congratulations are in order.
That smug bastard deserves worse than death for all the pain and suffering he's caused in his life.
You should speak with Eveli. She's practically bouncing.

When Vandacia killed Destron, he said he took my brother's power and gave it to Mehrunes Dagon. But I don't think he got all of it. Sombren was more powerful during our wanderings. I assumed it was the book, but now I think he got Destron's egonymic.

We got lucky, little mortal. The letter we found indicated that Sister Celdina wanted the portal key brought to her after the cultists recovered it. For whatever reason, that didn't happen.\n\nPerhaps they were waiting for Devastator Rullen to return.

We stopped the Waking Flame's threat to Blackwood and saved Fargrave from the Incarnates, but many questions remain unanswered. Mehrunes Dagon is still a threat to your world, mortal, and there are things I still wish to learn. Will you aid me again?

Ah, adventurer, this is your lucky day. Where once the Dread Lady sent my pitiful brother to convey her words to you, this time Lyranth has sent her true prophet. Me.\n\nI bear a message from my lovely and powerful mistress. Listen and be enlightened.
If I were the Anchorite, I'd want answers, too. I still have a bad feeling about this, though. Something about Sombren was off. I don't remember him being so quick to anger back in Blackwood.
Into the portal! We must get back to Annihilarch's Summit before Sombren overcomes Calia and the Anchorite.

We … survived. From the moment we came into the Deadlands, I assumed this was a suicide mission. If you hadn't come along it likely would've been.\n\nNever thought for a moment we'd find a helpful face in Mehrunes Dagon's realm.

The maggot distracted me. Allowed the other to plunge the enchanted blade into me. At least I delivered a mortal wound before the incapacitation took hold.\n\nSearch his corpse. Maybe the item he stole from my coffer is secreted in one of his pockets.
Go, into the portal. Let's be done with this place.
The relic is close. I can sense it. Search everywhere until you find it.
I think I'm going to be sick. Everything is spinning.

The Anchorite's memories are too scattered, unfocused. She has not yet come to grips with the fact that these newly restored memories belong to her.\n\nLet me see the memory vessel. Perhaps we were able to gather something useful after all.
I have nothing to say to you, Dagonist dog.
Once again, the Dread Lady commands me to deliver a message to her chosen mortal. Hear my words and let your heart be filled with awe and wonder.

The souls of the Longhouse Emperors! We found them!\n\nLook, spending decades encased in a chunk of metal can't have been good for their minds, but we need to learn why Mehrunes Dagon is interested in me. I'll let you do the talking.

The Anchorite's ties to the Order of the Waking Flame run even deeper than I suspected. The cataclysts were built to respond to the blood that runs through her veins.\n\nWhat else did you learn in Deadlight?

Ordinator Nilera was so brave, I wish I was more like her. But I—I'm not cut out for all this danger. \n\nI'll let the other Living Gods know what happened here. Maybe they can think of a way to free Sovisa?

Is this a shrine to Mehrunes Dagon? I feel like I've been here before. I recognize it from one of the memory fragments … the visions … I've been having.\n\nAnd my amulet. It's warm all of a sudden. Like it's drawn to the altar. How strange.

Go. The longer we delay, the more cultists escape our grasp—or fall prey to Valkynaz Nokvroz's forces. We are not the only ones hunting the Waking Flame in the Deadlands.\n\nGood luck, mortal. We will meet you once we locate the hidden portal.

Look at us, little mortal. Forced to accept the word of a blind, old seer, imprisoned and driven mad in Mehrunes Dagon's Blood Pit.\n\nIf Elegian is to be believed, we'll find Sister Celdina and the Riven Cataclyst at the summit.
I will not rest until I find out how Nokvroz did this to me. What trickery did he employ? And how can it be undone? Crushing him beneath my talons will be much easier when I am my proper size again.
The mortal cultists run like scared Banekin. I can smell their fear on the wind.\n\nFinish them swiftly, master, so that we may turn our attention to Nokvroz and destroy him for his treachery!

I do not know what Lyranth hoped to learn from the cataclyst, but I could feel the heat of her anger from over here. This Deadlight is also a mystery, but my Bladebearers will tear the Deadlands apart until they find Sister Celdina. You have my word.
I fear we're running out of time.

Waking Flame. Dagon cult. Digging their way into the town. Must be the tip of the spear. They threaten my protection. My freedom. And, I guess, the lives of your mortals.\n\nGo clear them out. Perhaps something there will explain their actions.
Go ahead. Try the ring in that lock. Someone went to a lot of trouble to protect that chest. It must contain something important.

You dropped the items in the cauldron. What a spectacular accomplishment.\n\nSo why are you talking to me? I'm just the Dread Lady's humble and devoted prophet. She wants to speak to you, her chosen mortal.

Luna Beriel has jobs that you can handle on your own and Vaveli Indavel trades in tasks that require groups of adventurers. \n\nRegardless of which job you take, I guarantee you'll be paid well for your work. That's a House Hexos promise.

Delightful. Another wanderer enters town seeking refuge. We just keep growing! I have no idea how we will sustain all you people.\n\nWait, are you with this Daedra? You should speak to him then. Tell him to leave. I want nothing to do with him.

I can't stop thinking about Elegian. Why did he give me this amulet? And why did he create my mask?\n\nDamn it! All these questions! And they need to wait until we finish our business at Annihilarch's Summit. Save Fargrave, then worry about myself.
Vontan? Never heard of anyone by that name. I hope my father isn't sending you on a fool's errand.\n\nJust be careful in the Fleapits. It's not the most hospitable part of Wretched Spire.
Forests burn across all of Nirn. Icy doom makes the world a tomb. No one knows. No one sees, but me!

I was barely able to get a hold of you before the spell dispersed you along with the others.\n\nI was a fool to think we could challenge a Daedric Prince! Mehrunes Dagon is one step ahead of us and we've already lost.
Mehrunes Dagon is defeated, master. The Deadlands is the plane of change, of revolution! What will become of it while its Prince suffers defeat?
