Tell me again, mortal. What, exactly, did Elegian say to you when you asked about the Riven Cataclyst?
We have no clue as to how close Sister Celdina is to creating another Incarnate, let alone an entire army of them. Let's find the Riven Cataclyst and see what's going on here.

Do survive, mortal. The House of Whims would be far less interesting without you to grace it with your presence.\n\nAnd bring the Anchorite back with you. Don't tell her I said this, but Fargrave needs her unselfish compassion.

All has turned out to my satisfaction. I learned what I needed to and you eliminated the threat of Incarnates laying waste to Fargrave and the mortal world. \n\nAnd with Sister Celdina and Valkynaz Nokvroz gone, none remain to build new cataclysts.
Enough talk. It is time to put an end to Valkynaz Nokvroz and these accursed cataclyst devices.\n\nFight well, mortal. Let them see your might!
It was a simple matter to follow your path, mortal. Let us find the cataclyst and end this.
We have to stop Dagon. There's still a chance, let's go!
Master! Something must be done, quickly! If I possessed my true form I could destroy them all!

Without a doubt, I'm grateful for what you showed me back in that cursed mine. I already took out … ten, I think? Much better than what I could have done before you came.\n\nNot saying that I'm glad my family and friends were captured, you understand
The battle against Mehrunes Dagon will surely be celebrated as the greatest triumph Clan Bladebearer has ever taken part in.
Let me examine that metal rod for you, master. It smells of power. And secrets.

Now that the dust has settled, I'm not really sure what to do with myself. I suppose we should probably check in with a few people. Word probably travels fast with something this big, but we can't count on that.

Bladebearers do not bother with mortals. Even those at Wretched Spire we barely tolerate. But if Rynkyus commands it, I will treat you as an ally.\n\nThis device they call the cataclyst, it is an abomination.
These soused jesters are a few drinks short of being properly drunk.  They're the perfect revelry fodder. \n\nStep lively now and ring the bell. Chime us all into gaiety!

I don't know what I expected, but it wasn't that. Finding the leader of the cult, watching as she almost completed a deadly ritual, and then allowing her to escape. I never fail like that.\n\nAnd all we have for our trouble is a coded message.
I do so enjoy dealing with mortals. Despite their short, meaningless lives, they can be quite fascinating.

Well, the end of the world is certainly taking longer than I expected. The Anchorite and you, no doubt?\n\nI've heard some talk about the Anchorite. What's going on? No, don't tell me. I'd rather not get involved.

We have unfinished business, mortal. The encoded message you recovered from the bathhouse. That may be the key to determining the Waking Flame's next move and revealing the secrets I am searching for.\n\nWe must find someone who can decipher it.
It seems to want our attention. Go. We have no time to waste on lesser creatures.

I'm still coming to grips with the fact that you're getting vital information from a talking daedrat, so don't look at me. Find out what else the encoded note said. And maybe Lyranth knows something about Burning Gyre Keep.
Back again? Why is it that mortals can't seem to get enough of what Madam Whim has to offer?\n\nMy establishment and its many wonders are always available … for the right price.
If what the daedrat says is accurate, then the danger to Fargrave is far from over. The forces of Burning Gyre Keep stand as some of the most fearsome of Mehrunes Dagon's warriors.
Arox the Mutilator is a daedrat of his word! At least, currently. \n\nRelease me and I will do anything in my power to aid your cause. You do have a cause that needs aiding, don't you?
You're that recent hireling. Good to see you! Adventurers don't usually come back after taking on a job for the Saraathu Tong.
You don't seem like a customer. Oh! Are you the experienced individual that's been hired to help me with my … issue? Let's take a look at you. \n\nWhew! The Tong only goes in for the best, I see.

You seem familiar, but I don't recall your face from the Bazaar which must mean—ah! You're the hireling who's contracting with the Saraathu Tong right? Good to see you again!\n\nNow, which of my many projects have you been assigned to this time?

The kynreeve commanded us to track the mortals of the Waking Flame. You have put them on their heels with your efforts. Impressive, mortal.\n\nSpeak with Rynkyus. He has orders for you, as I have mine.
You must be … ah yes, the new hireling. Think you're up to the job?

It's my business to know everything that goes on with the Saraathu Tong, so I know that you're one of the recent hirelings. Impressive record so far. Very well, which contract did you accept this time?

Good, you're here. I was afraid this crowd would turn ravenous if they had to wait any longer.\n\nDon't be alarmed. Looks like everyone's in a good mood. Though, I think there's a few more people here than expected.
The Anchorite already went ahead to Leyawiin with Calia, Madam Whim, and some of the others.\n\nI'll meet you there.
I must do this, little mortal. Do not attempt to stop me.
I know you. You're the hireling adventurer who's been running jobs for the Saraathu Tong.\n\nHave you gotten assigned to my job?
I will be going to Annihilarch Summit, of course. I know where it is, roughly though I have never gone up it.
It is the duty of the Grasp to interpret the Stricture and make sure it is adhered to. It is a heavy responsibility.
Mortal, you're back. The criminals turned themselves in to me. They tell me you found them and encouraged them to return to Fargrave. You have done well.\n\nWhat of the stolen Redmaiden?

The Grasp-Kyn seems happy that we turned ourselves in at least.\n\nElisa told me you gave her the Redmaiden. There's no way I can possibly thank you. She already looks better. I'll do whatever it takes to make sure she stays that way … free or not.

The Grasp may keep me and Bakh in chains, but what you did for me … it means I have time. It's the most precious gift of all.\n\nWith it, maybe Bakh and I can figure out some other way to stop the Drain, even while serving our time. So, thank you.
The Grim Warden's guardian stone is reconnected. When you're ready, I'll prepare the stone so you can summon it.

Madam Whim and I will meet you in Leyawiin. I hope you get the chance to speak with Lyranth before then. I still can hardly believe she has the power of the Ambitions now.\n\nWhy would she take them from the Anchorite? I thought she was our ally.

I do not know if you will find Lyranth, but you may as well try. I sent my faithful servant Hezehk to investigate the disturbances, though I doubt the fool has found much.\n\nRegardless, Calia and I will meet you and your other allies in Leyawiin.
Master! It warms my tail to see you.
Mortal. I have grown accustomed to your presence. It is a strange thing, but not entirely unwelcome.
People often tell me that I talk too much. They look at it all wrong. What else is left except for decent conversation?
Residence certainly elsewhere bringing him down. In power match on truth, not natural dissolution. Delightful songs of Oblivion's rest.

That's that. Another century off my debt! \n\nBe on your way, mortal. To the House of Whims! I heard your friends talking about the Bladebearers clan. And something called a Riven Cataclyst. Hezehk's not supposed to listen, but you all talk so loud!

You have the location of the portal from Skoedal? What are you doing in Fargrave then?\n\nI don't have the time to congratulate you for finishing a third of a task and Madam Whim does not pay for half measures.
This is no time for idle talk, mortal. Our clan's enemies seek to escape our vengeance. Speak to Lyranth. Perhaps she knows where they have gone to hide.
I do not command here. Why does the mortal continue to pester me?
Something else I can help with?
I don't recognize you, so you can't be a customer. Oh! Is someone finally going to do something about those kyncursed cult pamphlets moving through Fargrave?

Ah, you're back! Excellent! And no worse for the wear, I see. I'm not surprised.\n\nSo? Tell me, how did your adventures in Vvardenfell, Summerset, and such treat you? You've got plenty of tales to tell, I'm sure!
You don't seem like someone Airlur has met in the taverns before. He does not find your eyes appealing.  \n\nAh, you are here about the job Airlur told the fierce Luna about.
Oh! Are you new to Fargrave or the Gleaners? It doesn't matter, you've probably never messed up as badly as I have. Maybe we can help each other.
You don't seem to be suffering from any malaise, body or mind. Why are you here adventurer?
Ah. You're the brave new hire who's just accepted the assignment I gave to our Lady Beriel. I expect you have questions.
You don't have the shifty eyes of most Gleaners. What do you want?
Once my Kyn and I have regained our strength, we will see to a reckoning with Valkynaz Nokvroz. His actions warrant prolonged suffering.
I am heartened to see my fellow Kyn free of chains and cages. But many more were fed to the barbarous device, the Riven Cataclyst. This must not be allowed to stand.
We're finished with this filthy spider-nest. Meet me outside.
You're still here? Look—from one mortal to another—I'd love to help. But my hands are tied!

This cinches it. This Varallion is the same one who was working for the Veiled Heritance. Guess he found himself a new outfit.\n\nNo sign of the medallion, but these papers are probably worth something to the right buyer.
All these papers … yes, look. This was the master shipbuilder's office! The plans Za'ji sought were surely here. The Sea Elves must have come for them as well!
What? Found what you wanted. Ebony Blade's right there. Go on. Look.
I told the mistress I would deliver her message, so I have. That's all I was instructed to do.
I might be waiting for others of my kind to reform before going out into the planes once again, but do not mistake me for a coward. What do you want, child?

From here, it just looks like a pile of discarded Daedric junk to me. Lyranth's eyes must be as sharp as a gryphon's.\n\nJust watch out for lava crabs. The Deadlands are crawling with them and that's exactly the sort of place they like to hide.
That sword. It bears the mark of the Bladebearer clan. And that clan has no connection to this fortress.\n\nGo ahead, little mortal. See what you can make of it.

Ah, at last. I'm whole again! I can't begin to describe how unpleasant it is to be strewn across the cosmos. \n\nI think my sense of touch was underwater half the time. And my teeth feel like I've been sleeping with my mouth open.

I told you what you could do with yourself, rancid boil. It's impossible to fish with you weeping your stink-juice like a slobbering Scamp.\n\nI'm tempted to kill you, but I fear it would somehow make the stench worse.

If you want my attention it comes at a price.\n\nI offer patrons of the House of Whims the Constrictions of Moath. Know that mortals have difficulty enduring this act. But those that do survive hold no regret.
Damn, they broke the seal on it! I'm sure to hear about that later.

Aha. Nzerru always attracts them, does he not? The curious. The irrepressible pryers. You wish to know what Nzerru can offer you in this house of Madam Whim's, yes? \n\nNzerru has the tonic, living one. My Golden Panacea, to make your insides shine.
Prices are fixed and all sales are final. Cheats and hagglers do business at their peril.

I welcome you, fellow mortal, as the mouthpiece of Great Vruxynbu. For patrons of the House of Whims, my master offers a spiritual lustration. Know that … know that his gentle manner and bearing will elevate your mind and soul to untold heights.

Gilfrex rules the Fleapit District, feeding on desperation and despair. Shiro-dar suspects he is not so important for a Daedra, but among the dregs of Wretched Spire he is a king!\n\nThis one should not linger in the Fleapits. He will hide outside.
You'd better hurry if you plan to get the Slave Choker from False Martyrs' Folly before I find that Scamp-livered cat. And take my due.
What, maggot?

Once again, my mistress, the Dread Lady, Lyranth the Dremora, deigns to share her infinite wisdom with a chosen mortal.\n\nWhy she continues to choose you, I have no idea. No matter, are you prepared to hear the words of the Dread Lady?
I have been expecting you two. Your friend is ever-present here. Everywhere and nowhere. Too used to order, and now drowning in chaos.
Seems like a joke that the one place where I can hide from Dagon's eye is filled with mortals.

I'll not ask why you're wandering this cursed place, but I'd urge you to leave. The Deadlands are hospitable to no one.\n\nIf your mission keeps you within this realm like mine does, then I'll gladly share what I can—be it my fire or a blessing.
Ardent Hope, site of Mehrunes Dagon's great war machines and armies, was stormed? And the great valkynaz was killed? How could such a thing come to pass?
I think every Daedra in Fargrave is looking at mortals with a bit more respect now. They've seen even the most humble folk can stand up to the likes of Mehrunes Dagon.
This is the truest torment. To spend eternity trying to catch up to you. \n\nDo all mortals move from place to place as much as you do?
The last time one of our scavengers went near Ardent Hope, Valkynaz Nokvroz had a cloak made from her hide. I hope that bastard suffered before dying.
The Deadlands are never really still, but … things almost seem calm, for the moment. Maybe my mind is playing tricks on me.
This almost feels like Fargrave. I've never seen Nirn so full of Daedra.
This is quite a gathering. I haven't seen this many Daedra and mortals together since we left Fargrave.
We can't leave to wander about the Deadlands. And staying means misery. How did I manage to get stuck within Wretched Spire? Will I live out my life like this?
The planes of Oblivion await, mortal. My portal can take you to them.
This short-horned swindler means to play me for a fool. As if I cannot tell the difference between a dead mortal and a living one.
I knew the Grasp would rule in my favor. Who wants a living mortal anyway?
None dare speak against the rulings of the Stricture. Its power in Fargrave is absolute.
Madam Whim has me traipsing all over Fargrave to deal with such menial tasks. As much as I detest it, I must get back to them.

I do so adore a conquering hero, my darling! Do you like the welcome I prepared? It was the best I could do on short notice.\n\nLyranth awaits you upstairs, but know that I plan to show you all of the House of Whims pleasures. Later. No charge.

I adore this view. Isn't the Colossus a wondrous sight?\n\nStill, gazing upon it does nothing to quell my anxiety. Somehow, the Ascendant Order learned not only about our secret peace talks, but that the alliance leaders were going to attend.

A pity. This would have been a truly grand occasion under better circumstances. I suppose we must make do.\n\nConduct your investigation with discretion, please. You do not want any of these nobles to mark you as an enemy.
Can't say that I see much point in asking around High Isle. I'm no investigator, but isn't this the one place that we know Lady Arabelle's ships aren't?
Speak with Lady Arabelle, friend. Tell her what the captains revealed to you. I'm sure she can image a way forward.

Bless you, traveler! Please understand: To my order, this is more than just a lighthouse. This beacon spreads Kynareth's blessing across both land and sea. But only with the idol in place, so it must be returned.

I warned them that the rogue knights were dangerous, but they insisted on going to investigate. And Valessea assured me that she and Quentyn could take care of themselves.\n\nI hope you find them well and unharmed.

I see you spoke to Fasaria. \n\nUnfortunately, I don't think I'll be able to properly pray to Zenithar for you. My mind is cluttered with the tasks of my day. But the altar is right there. Fasaria might be able to pray on your behalf.
You have all the scoria we've come across? Good. \n\nLook, you talk to my wife, see how she's doing. I need to think about the best way to get her out of here.
Leave me to my drink, citizen.
You will find Queen Ayrenn, won't you, walker? And Za'ji's friend Caska, too?\n\nZa'ji could not live with himself if anything happened to either one of them!

I'll do whatever I can to help you and Lady Arabelle recover High King Emeric and the others. Especially if it involves beating Dockmaster Arnauld senseless while he's floundering ashore, half-drowned in the surf.
The mud flows where it will, my friend. As soon as I recover my strength, I will help in any way I can.\n\nI know that Prince Irnskar is still out there somewhere. We just need to find him.

I must say, and I don't usually speak ill of anyone except goats, but those Hadolids were awful. Didn't even bother to explain themselves.\n\nI'm thankful you came along to help. And Privette tells me she appreciates you as well.

We meet again! I know our time apart must have been as difficult for you as it was for me. \n\nNow that we're together, I've got a secret mission for you complete with my missing lady-love and a tantalizing mystery. What do you say, care to assist?

With your knees and my knowledge, the altars will relinquish the items we seek. Find them in the chapel, the living quarters, the statuary, and the catacombs.\n\nPut me in your pack. Together, we'll ensure Lord Leobert's plan is never realized.
Is it true, stranger? You've already collected all the scoria?

Don't worry about me, dear. Emeric and I go way back. I know all the ways to calm him down after a long and grueling battle. I have a knack for that sort of thing.\n\nI promise not to take too long. I'll meet you back at my camp in Vvardenfell shortly.
I wonder what she wants to talk about? She doesn't seem upset, at least. That's an improvement.
The Ascendant Order must have a hideout in here somewhere. Tarazka said he left a lantern at the entrance, right? \n\nLet's look around for any signs of Valessea.

Thanks for talking to Tarazka. He's as cranky as ever. Anyway, that prisoner he mentioned must be the lovely Valessea. We need to rescue her. \n\nCome on, let's get inside and find Valessea and her kidnappers!
I can tell she's trying to hide it, but I think mother's happy how things turned out. \n\nAnd it's all thanks to you and Isobel!

The three things to lookout for are enemy messages to collect, allied documents to destroy, and Nari to bring to safety. You'll find all of them either among the wreckage on the shoals or among the Sea Elves.\n\nTake my skiff to get there.
Get me out of here! Please! Those Sea Elves are trying to break me—force me to decode documents to help them attack alliance ships. I can't take much more ….

You're wasting time, my friend. Jakarn may not be the sharpest thorn on the bush, but he knows how to make a delivery.\n\nMy portal will take you to Windhelm. Get to the Palace of Kings and use the dispelling powder. That will make the medallions safe.

Don't look at me. I'm the beauty here, not the brains. Go talk to Lady Arabelle. She's always got more plans and theories than you can shake a wet horker at.\n\nWhat does that even mean? It sounded good before I said it, but now I'm not so sure.
Breaking that curse doesn't seem to be sitting well with the stone here. Let's get out of here before we get buried with the rest of the dead!

That rascal Anton survived somehow! Barely. If we found him dead, I would've killed everyone on this island. Well, I would've paid you to do it.\n\nLet's get out of this horrid place and back onto the raft.

Go on. Do whatever you need to do to make that medallion safe. I can't believe I was about to hand something dangerous to my liege lord. It's my job to protect him. I dread to think what might have happened if you showed up a few moments later.

I didn't think anyone would find me in here. Least of all Jakarn. But I am thankful to you both.\n\nThe invitation medallions! Jakarn was supposed to pick them up for Lady Arabelle, but the Ascendant Order stole them. We have to get them back!
We found Valessea! And isn't she as radiant as I described her?\n\nGo ahead and talk with her. She might swoon at the sight of my bulging muscles and we don't have time for that.

Welcome to Castle Navire. You're Lady Arabelle's assistant, yes? Then you know these festivities are only for appearance's sake. Our guests of honor have yet to be found.\n\nRest assured, I intend to bring the radicals behind this plot to justice.
The duchess has many guests to attend to. It would be rude to monopolize her attention.\n\nHave some wine. Introduce yourself to some of the other guests. Go on. Mingle.

I don't believe we've met. Jonne Mornard—a pleasure. My family is in shipping. We import goods from the mainland and send wares from the archipelago to markets in Tamriel.\n\nYou're the investigator working with Lady Arabelle, aren't you?
Hopefully Valessea's shell will make finding the medallions a piece of cake. Go ahead, try using it.
I'll meet you back at Mandrake Manor. Should be there before Lady Arabelle finishes briefing you.
Three royals and a very large cat. Not a bad rescue, good-looking, not bad at all.

I told Lady Arabelle all about you. I gave her the quick version of everything we learned, but she wants to hear your version. I don't think she completely trusts me.\n\nGo ahead. Just keep quiet about the author thing. I never said a word.

I never expected to speak with the living again, let alone one of my own flesh and blood. How many generations removed, I wonder? How long have I been trapped in this watery grave? Centuries, I'm sure, but there's no sense of time down here.
Back so soon? You didn't drop the staff down the well, did you?
Seems like our work here is done. \n\nI'll meet you and Lady Arabelle back at camp. Then we can properly celebrate our victory.

How dare you deliver a dangerous relic to the Queen Ayrenn's court! If you have a way to rectify this situation, I demand you do so immediately!\n\nI wonder, could this be connected to the other recent attempts on the queen's life?

Captain Basrush is a very close friend. Tell her I'd like her to take you to Amenos. As a prisoner. You're less likely to attract attention that way.\n\nTell her she'll receive a full purse of gold. And an evening in my company when this is all over.

Having a brave protector by my side feels so much better than going alone. But they'll notice I'm gone soon. So we should be on our way.\n\nI don't doubt someone powerful like you could take them all on. But watching that violence would upset me.

You need disguises because you want to travel aboard a prison ship. And because you want to avoid notice when we reach Amenos.\n\nSo, disguises. You'll look like just two more poor bastards bound for the prison island, guaranteed.
After you, champion.

The opinions of some ghost knight means nothing to Amunara. This one didn't come so far and spend all her gold on mercenaries not to get that shield.\n\nBy all means, go through the trials if you want. Just stay out of Amunara's way.
My thanks for the discretion you and Dame Isobel have shown, not mentioning the … ah.\n\nThe events in the catacombs.
These peace talks must come to pass. I fear that if they're halted, the war will continue indefinitely.\n\nWe must do everything in our power to ensure they take place as planned.
We need to find Lady Arabelle first. Hopefully she knows where High King Emeric is. Let's watch out for the Ascendant Champion, too. I have a feeling we might finally get introduced.

Was it too much to hope that one of High Isle's nobles would openly admit their guilt? Ah, well. At least we can rule out Duchess Elea. Her notes make it clear she was caught off-guard by the attack on the delegates' ships. And this map. Interesting.

Trust me! It'll work! We just need to buy you enough time to get into the lower castle without the guards noticing. Once you're inside, the rest will be up to you.\n\nRemember, the song I want you to request is Stagger and Sway. It's a classic!
I'm quite sure our striving Nord poet can help you. I am actually quite busy.
I saw you talking to her. Isn't her voice beautiful? Like a gentle brook burbling through a forest glade. Ahem. Sorry. \n\nDid you give her the note? How did she react?
So you're Lady Isobel's new second. Huh. Didn't think she'd replace me that quickly.

Hadn't you better run off to the Knight Commander? She probably wants to lecture you both in private. \n\nImagine turning down the chance to be legally wedded to such a well-connected and wealthy heir. Hmph.

The Coral Cliffs aren't an area anyone wants to be lost in. Strange noises thereabouts. Makes me shudder. \n\nYou find my fellow sentry and those prisoners of ours. Get them out of there safely. I need to rest my hurts before we move on from here.

I'm getting out of here. Everyone else—everyone still alive— is through the caves at the bottom of that hill. They're caged up. But if you really want to help us, you'll destroy the corrupted coral. Make it so the druids' plan never works!

It's disappointing that the archdruid tried to renew the wards on her own and allowed the Allwither to take control of her.\n\nAt least we were able to restore the Evergrowth and stop the spread of corruption.
I'm not sure who is happier with today's events, Aurelia or Isobel. \n\nI think our new knight is anxious to speak to you.
Oh no! Dame Madach ….

I thought Magister Irin would be as mad as a wet Dragon. But he looks amused. It's probably because he's wanted to turn Huldressa into a guar at some point, he just won't admit it. And the fact that we fixed it all before he got here helped.

It's an honor to be invited to one of Duchess Elea's parties. I've heard she only allows members of her own family into the castle. Most people never set foot inside the walls, let alone rub shoulders with the highest nobility of High Isle!

As depressing as it sounds, that's the most fun I've had in months. \n\nTo be honest. I wasn't sure the ritual would work. If it hadn't, let's assume Za'ji could have navigated through the storm and reached us anyway. Yeah, let's go with that.

Such a waste. I have little patience for the vanity of our noble houses on the best of days. Right now? I'm sure we all have better things we could be doing.\n\nI suspect you agree. You're the one assisting Lord Bacaro and Lady Arabelle, aren't you?
A daring rescue, a clean escape. Well done, my friend! I can't wait to tell Queen Maraya all about it.

Za'ji's ship was closest when the signal flare ignited. Do you like it? I call it the Perfect Pounce II!\n\nAnyway, Za'ji is supposed to get you back to Mandrake Manor as quick as he can. Just give the order and we'll leave these dreadful shores.

Good work finding the alliance leaders and getting them off Amenos safely. I'm quite proud of you, my dear.\n\nLord Bacaro and I will spirit them to a more secure location shortly. Then we can turn our attention back to the Ascendant Order.

The Ascendant Magus and his lord are cowards. Neither would stand and fight! They call themselves knights? Hardly.\n\nAt least we heard their plans. A meeting on High Isle, we heard the Ascendant Lord say.

Lady Arabelle was right, damn it. We do have a rat in our company. Now I owe her a bottle of Tamika's Dark Rum.\n\nSomeone gave our plans to the Ascendant Order, and they somehow used lodestones to track us and target us with that storm.

I listened carefully while you questioned Duchess Elea. I do not believe she said anything that was untrue.\n\nLet's see if we can find the letter Count Damard gave to the steward. I'd like to have a look at that.
Nicely done. We got what we needed and the dockmaster gets what he deserves.\n\nI'll take another look around. We'll meet back at the manor after you check the other sites.
Make those Ascendant Order dogs pay for what they did to my ship.
Islinne will be fine, thanks to you. The menders are seeing to her now.\n\nIn the meantime, I stand ready to help once more. You have my word.
You should talk to <<1>>. I'd like to hear him try to weasel out of this.
I'm trusting a capricious nature spirit. Wonderful. Well, talk to Audrine and get moving. Warrane and I will try to buy you some time by cleansing as much of the corruption as we can.
Please, hurry and open the lock. Who knows when the druids will come back.
Can you imagine if we finally realized the goal of Steadfast Manor? People from all over Tamriel coming together in peace. Recognition of a shared life. It would be like a dream.

I'll stay with Ryvana until the lingering effects of the ritual have been purged. My more traditional, Guild-scholared dispelling techniques might be helpful here.\n\nI hope the other locations on the map will provide more complete answers.
An outsider made use of this place of power, I'm sure of it. It would require great arcane knowledge to forcefully bind the elements to their will, even if it didn't work exactly as they planned.
I shall return Dame Madach's body to our order. After I take a moment to rest, of course.
Good gathering, traveler. The grove welcomes all. Feel free to wander about and enjoy its many offerings.
Oh? I suppose you're here to fling more baseless accusations at me, too! Who are you to speak against me? What do you know of the work I do here?
Are we done here? I'm starving!\n\nI'll meet you back at Mandrake Manor. Lady Arabelle always has something tasty in her pantry.
Ha ha! Look at those scaly rascals run!
Get us out of here, quick!
We should get a move on before these pirates realize what's going on.

My bestest friend! Thanks to your help, I can commit diplomacy again. Everyone here will know that they have been diplomacized by Rigurt the Brash!\n\nBut I still have no idea how things got so out of hand. Everyone was so upset!
I think your friend Rigurt wants to talk to you. Remind him to make sure he pays for his expensive dinner and endless rounds of drinks next time. \n\nNormally I don't have to mention that part.
Another one of my favorite associates, back safe and sound. And were you successful? Did Captain Tsuzo find anything important at the Shoals?
I am positively mortified. In all my years of diplomatic work I have never been involved in such a scene.\n\nI would be in your debt if you could convince Rigurt to never bring this up again.

I have one more favor to ask, friend. Could we try to keep this whole business just between us? \n\nI'm kind of new at this, you see. I was just appointed to the Covenant's delegation, and I'm worried they'll send me home if I foul it up.
Talk to <<1>>. I want to hear what he has to say for himself. And I would like to think that some small part of him regrets what he's done.

When I got to the Shoals and saw all those Sea Elf pirates and Hadolids, I quickly sent a message to Lady Arabelle requesting assistance. But I was able to sneak over here, and that is when I spotted her.\n\nThe sea has returned her back to me!
I didn't think anyone would come for me. But if you're with the captain … please. It's Prince Irnskar, we have to help him. \n\nI'd be dead if it wasn't for the prince.
You should talk to <<1>>. I'd like to hear an admission of guilt from his own mouth.
You heard what father said? He thinks I'm capable! He might let me go on more adventures! I'll be able to help people!\n\nTalk to him please. I want to hear what else he has to say about me.
Oh, thank you! You arrived just in time. My steward locked me in my own cabin! The nerve!\n\nI thought he was surely going to take me away, never to be found.

Count Damard, or should I call him the Magus? He thinks I'm dead beneath Castle Navire, that Duchess Elea is locked aboard the Silver Swan, and that his victory is assured. But thanks to you, he's wrong about everything. We're not finished yet, dear.

Remember, Wayllod provides jobs you can handle on your own, while Parisse and Druid Peeska deal in work that requires a group to complete safely.\n\nYou'll be paid handsomely for every task you complete—I guarantee it!

So, you were witness to the events here. And as I understand it, you had a hand in bringing them to an end. For that, I thank you. \n\nBut if you'll indulge me, I do have a few lingering questions. What in the world happened?
Be careful down here, the mine's not a friendly place for those who don't know it. And that's on days when it's not filled with flyblown monsters from the depths.
I—please make sure my daughter survives this. I can never seem to curb her rebellious streaks.\n\nMeryline. She's all I have. Protect her. I beg you.

Here, I'll mark a location on your map. There's a spot out in the jungle where we can meet. I'll have us a way off this cursed island by the time you collect Valentyn and get there.\n\nJust give Jailer Omdil the wine, get inside, and find my husband.
You're not supposed to be on this side of the stockade fence, prisoner. Get back inside or they'll be consequences.
Well, were you able to slip one of the jailer's valuables into Yvara's bedroll?
We can beat Marcelle and her minions to the extraction point if we hurry, I'm sure of it!

I knew it the moment I saw you, dear. This one has spirit. This one has the heart of a hero. Not too unlike what Emeric saw when he first looked at me.\n\nYou know I appreciate all you've done, my friend. You can call on me for help whenever you need.
Did you find <<1>>? More importantly, did you bring back any proof that he's dealing in skooma?\n\nSomeone has to go to prison today. I'd rather take him than your friend here.
There's nothing left to do here but clean up the mess. Leave that to the Dufort navy, you're due some shore leave after this assault.
Mission successful, marine. You've done our flotilla proud.\n\nDon't turn away an ale when we get back to port. You deserve every one.

Head up the Lofte Empyrean's gangway then, and watch your step. Taking a tumble from the flagship is quite a drop. \n\nReport to Purser Ashcroft on the lower decks and she'll see that you're accounted for.
Well done, friend! We sail for All Flags Islet on your order. With a little luck, the Ascendant Magus will assume we're bringing expected reinforcements to join his attack.

I wanted to get the alliance leaders safely behind the wards in Memorial Hall. Or perhaps even spirit them away on the ship, but I doubt we'd succeed at that trick a second time. \n\nYou need to find the leaders and get them to Memorial Hall.
This isn't really my bailiwick. I don't fight wars—I'm a thief!\n\nBut I said I'd help and I will. You can count on me.

Most of the belongings I brought along were lost when the Perfect Pounce sank into the sea. I wonder if I can find any suitable attire on this island. Breton tastes leave something to be desired.\n\nWhat am I thinking? This outfit is perfectly fine!

Wait until the Skald-King hears what he missed! Raging storms, a deadly jungle, a battle against near-hopeless odds at an ancient castle! My father is going to kick himself! Well, maybe not about the storms. He gets sick at sea.

It seems I'll need to pay more attention to the Systres Archipelago in the future. My negligence allowed treason to fester and bloom unchecked. That changes now.\n\nBut enough grim talk. We must celebrate! I will see you at Lord Bacaro's gathering.

Lord Bacaro may have proclaimed that this was a celebration for the alliance leaders, but everyone came out to see the hero who saved All Flags Castle. I'm impressed how fast the word got around—even if I may have had something to do with that!
Za'ji wishes more of the Perfect Pounce crew was here to see this. But he and Caska will do what we can to honor our lost shipmates.\n\nWe are ready for All Flags when you are, five-claw.
What are we waiting for? Let's sail before the Ascendant Order starts wondering why their ship's taking so long to show up.

How often does someone get to save three realms in the same day? Your actions are an inspiration! I wonder, though. Did the Ascendant Magus inadvertently help us by attacking the royals? We shall see.\n\nGo. Tell Arabelle. She'll make the arrangements.

For the first time in years, I feel like I can take a breath. I don't really know what to do. There's so much I want to say to my friends, so much I want to tell them. \n\nThey've all been through so much, and so have I, I suppose. Hmm.

This one does not know your face, but Ember …  it is a joy for these old eyes to see her well, even if she is still a bit jumpy. She watches the area just as she did when she was a child. Always uneasy. \n\nAre you her friend?
Don't forget to try the jellied scrib in pastry for a starter. It's full of … jelly.
Ah, you again. I'd nearly forgotten about you. Do I dare hope you procured the bracelet I asked for?
We defeated the Ascendant Magus and drove his knights back into hiding. But the so-called Ascendant Lord is still out there. Somewhere.
I think it's safe to say this diplomatic mission turned out differently from what my father anticipated.
To think, these Ascendant Order malcontents were operating in my kingdom! I fear we haven't heard the last of them. Or of their Ascendant Lord.

I admit, I feared all was lost as more of those rogue knights pressed onto shore. Then the castle's siege weapons unloaded on their ships, and the dark storm suddenly abated.\n\nTell me. What actually happened in Memorial Hall?

Ah, the fresh air already makes this one feel better. I am in your debt.\n\nAnd Ember … how clever she was to track me down. She was always so smart. I used to love the way her eyes all but burned in her skull when she was trying to solve a problem.
Marbruk is peaceful. This one likes it here very much. \n\nIt is strange to be free, to not be beholden to anyone or anything. Jhaka appreciates this new life you have made possible.

This one believes Ember wishes to speak with you. Likely, she wants to thank you for helping bring us all together. Jhaka wants to thank you as well, but there are no words that properly convey his gratitude.

I'm not looking forward to telling Song about what really happened that day. But she needs to know. I want to tell her the truth. \n\nYou should talk to Ember. She looks like she's getting ready to hug you or something, watch out.
Eh? What do you and your blurry friends want now?
The Emerald Eye has been a thorn in King Fahara'jad's side for a long while now. I do hope that you are the key to solving that age old problem. \n\nNow be off with you. There is work to be done.

My treacherous family will fall to ruin and I am … free. My friends are alive and the future blooms like a flower before me. \n\nPlease, discuss what you need to with Ember while I collect myself. She must wish to speak with you.

I knew who you were as soon as I laid eyes on Ember. Mahtelah, er, Song, described her perfectly in her stories. Apologies for the secrecy, but if you know anything about the Emerald Eye, you understand the necessity. \n\nHow much do you know already?
Stendarr's got to be smiling on us. My family's coin and reputation are safe.\n\nAurelia and Marso are in love. Draigh, I think even the Knight Commander's mood has thawed a bit.
Isobel's parents were exceptionally kind. It's a point of pride I get to sail for them.\n\nBut don't worry about us. Go speak with Isobel. It looks like she has something to say.

Kiv was quite courteous, right up until he robbed me. Oh, I very much hope you can find Isobel's ring.\n\nAfter he fled the inn, perhaps he dropped some more of his … booty? Maybe you could track him that way.

Be careful around Shipwreck Shoals. It's more dangerous to boats than people, but I hear hadolids come to pick over the wrecks for fresh, uh, meat.\n\nHopefully that map will make quick work of claiming the Scourge's bounty.
That fetching … gah. Kiv will just seduce a guard and slip out of town if we turn him in. \n\nI have a better idea.

Ascendant Order ships in the loch, rogue knights and their druid allies inside the castle. They may have the numbers, but I say let them come!\n\nTogether we will make them pay dearly for their victory!
When you and Stibbons are done chatting, remind him that I have a task for my manservant.
Did it work? Did we break the curse? Lady Laurent sounds like her old self, but ….\n\nYou talk to her. I couldn't take it if that foul captain's voice came out of her perfect mouth again.

Hard at work, I see. Good. Well done. Zenithar might want more from you, but he's still watching what you do with a keen eye. I believe you can better yourself and the realm before this day is done. \n\nGo on. Make Zenithar proud.
Walk off, pal. No time for useless chatter.
I smell old parchment and paper here, more than just the moldy stuff we've seen so far. Some of those plans might have really been safely stored here. Until the Sea Elves took them.

Galedra and I have rather different perspectives on punishing Kiv, but we agree he must face some measure of justice.\n\nIf we just turn him over the guards, I suspect he'll charm his way out of jail. The same way he charmed me out of … nevermind.
Walk off, pal. No time for useless chatter.
I knew this curse was all Tobin's fault! That little monster was always jealous of my captain and the love we shared.
Aye, what can I do for you? You looking to book a cargo ship?
Ooo. Unless you can cure this one's aching back, Halz is not feeling like talking.
Hmm. Izzy has that expression on her face. She has something to say. \n\nShe always gets a little ruffled, where emotions, especially happy ones, come into play.
Thank you, walker. It's good to feel my claws on the deck of a ship again. And it's good to be back with Za'ji.\n\nThat lazy Khajiit is lost without me.
Such a pleasure to finally meet you. Miriette Veloise. We travel a lot and it's been hard to get Bella back here for dinner.
I was sad not to be at the Tourney! Not every day a father gets to see his daughter elevated to her full knighthood. Hah!\n\nShe wrote us with all the details, and said that you were a big help.

I was a bit surprised, when they asked for my blessing. But … Aurelia has grown so much. And we've had such lovely conversations in our letters. \n\nI just made them promise to visit the castle as often as they can.
Ah, good day to you. Welcome to Fell's Run. A tiny little hamlet with great big problems. Haha.
A ship! Let's get off this miserable rock.

Zenithar keep the working days of your life long and your purse filled, my friend.\n\nIf you'd like to try your hand, I have some questions about the Provider of Our Ease for you. I can promise a worthy reward should you provide the correct answers.
And here we are. Time to rub defeat into Raenobi's expertly-coiffed ….\n\nHang on. Is it me, or are all of Gonfalon's opponents well-groomed? Or, maybe we're just scruffier than everyone else ….

Roister's Guild leadership is still organizing the next tournament. Your eagerness does you credit, but a brief respite will do you well. Keep your skills sharp and try to acquire some new cards and decks.\n\nOh, and don't forget to revel!

Advanced rank now, eh? You've come a long way since you first showed up. Must be earning heaps of gold!\n\nDon't forget to drop a few of those shiny coins in old Gelekh's purse. The drinks are swill, sure, but it's the company you're paying for!
You are going to have such a grand time. I can still remember my first win. Such a thrill!\n\nI'm actually on my way back to Gonfalon Bay myself, so I'll see you there!
So, you come to collect your reward, yes? Are you sure you don't want to try to earn something even sweeter? Even if you lose, you still win!\n\nIt is up to you, though! Kishka does not care.
Don't worry about me. Don't pay me any mind. Just wipe the floor with her, friend.
Go out and win some games, my friend! It really is true that experience is the greatest teacher, especially when it comes to Tribute.\n\nI'll be rooting for you the entire way.
Well met, adventurer. If you're here to put a stop to those crazed Eldertide Druids plundering my land, you have my earnest wishes for your success.
I expect this will be the last time we speak. The odds of you beating dear Fabermund in Daggerfall are comically slim. He's learned from the best. Me.

So, you really think you have what it takes to challenge the Wayrest chapter? According to my calculations, your chances are roughly zero. But who am I to refuse a match?\n\nThe tournament starts now!
I knew that pompous little weasel was feeding me bad Tribute strategies!\n\nBah! Be off! I've got some drinking to do.
Don't forget to cleanse the area when you destroy the Sable Knight. Otherwise the necromantic energy may seep back into its discarded armor and renew its curse.
I see the wind brings us together like two fallen leaves on this empty road.
No hunter on High Isle will be safe until you kill Glemyos Wildhorn. It's a hard thing to do, but it must be done.
No hope. They're gonna kill us. It's only a matter of time.
My head. Got it right smacked up. The ship. Sunigil. So much light.
My noble rescuer! I am pleased to see you again. When I heard about the terrible things my brother did at All Flags Castle, I feared the worst for the alliance leaders. And for you, too, of course.
Look around, friend. All these people are here because of you. I don't know what we would have done without you.
Draigh, look at all these people. And they're all here because of you!

Nothing to see here, citizen. Get back on whatever scow delivered you to these damned shores and sail back to High Isle. This isn't the place for tourists or bored nobles with nothing better to do, mark my words.
Go! The stairs to the south lead down to the dock. I'll take out as many of these Ascendant Order knights as I can!
Funny, I haven't heard about any new trusties lately. I'm watching you, stranger.
You don't look like a prisoner. You probably shouldn't be in here, friend.
Meryline's back on Amenos? Well, I'm glad Overseer Barthel sent for her. We need all the help we can get.

I need Brokerock, all right? Out there, the Green Serpents have their lackies looking to do me in. End me, you hear? Even if this place closes, they won't get me to leave. Overseer Barthel and his sentries can try all they want, but I'll not go.

I'm sorry, but I can't talk any longer. I do wish to help any way I can, but the patients need me. Especially in Roslenn's absence.\n\nGood luck in your search for the affliction's cause. And alert me if you start feeling strange!

I was told they weren't taking new patients, not until they figure out what's going on. Still, welcome to Steadfast Manor.\n\nI'd offer a tour, but I don't quite feel up to it. Haven't slept in days. I can barely stand up straight.

Such a calming vista, yes? The sound of waves lapping at the shore always used to bring Milagi peace.\n\nBut now Milagi feels like he may jump out of his fur. Fear ripples through Milagi as if he faces battle again.

Here, these spots should have the ingredients I mentioned. If you can gather them and bring them back, I can whip up a drink that's sure to make all the mainlanders empty out their pockets! \n\nSo long as I can keep Hilgrim away from it.
Loshu-Jat never expected working at Brokerock to be like this. Nothing good ever happens in the darkness under rock. Loshu-Jat knew this. Loshu-Jat should have listened.
Be certain to take good care of those eggs when you find them. Understanding how the Serpent Caller is attempting to alter them may help us undo the harm she's caused.

This is where we were supposed to set aside our differences and discuss the possibility of peace. Instead, here we are hiding behind wards so that crazed assassins can't kill us.\n\nNot what I expected when I agreed to Lord Bacaro's invitation.
Unless you have word of a fair damsel to rescue or a fell beast slay, you need not waste my time. \n\nI've got to tend to my weapons and strengthen my core. As any true knight would do!
Don't hold back. Use everything you've learned to crush Teliv.\n\nOnce you win, we'll host the grandest celebration that Gonfalon Bay has ever seen!
Please, free my companions from the Executioner and the Harrower. No one deserves to suffer that fate.
Bah! You fumble about like a ja'khajiit! There is no backing out now, walker. Sit and play!
Do be careful handling those glands. I need them intact and in pristine condition, or they'll be of no use in my research.
Welcome, welcome, welcome. I was beginning to worry you wouldn't show. Not that anyone could blame you.\n\nAre you ready to begin?
There you are! Show me your cards, Gonfalon. Come on and show me!\n\nDon't drag this out. I've got things to do.
The winds are at our back again, friend—Nereid's Song is ours! Soon we will see what awaits us at All Flags Islet.
I gathered what help I could and mounted a defense, but the Ascendant Order's attack came so quickly. We had no time to prepare.

Unbinding the bound nature spirit? If this doesn't work, we could be facing an all-consuming corruption or a total breakdown of the laws of nature. Y'ffre preserve us!\n\nWell, go be a hero. You and Audrine both. We'll help as we can from up here.
While our delegates recover from their harrowing escape, I'll revisit our arrangements for the peace conference. The problem of the Ascendant Order I leave to you and Lady Arabelle.\n\nGood hunting!
Move along, citizen. No decent person has any business at the stockade.
Aren't you supposed to be meeting with the Knight Commander?\n\nShe's amazing, isn't she? Inspires me to one day stand on the stage myself!
Good gathering, traveler. Have you come to see the wonders of our grove? Feel free. All are welcome here.
Teliv thinks he's untouchable, but he has no idea what's coming for him. You're one of the best players I've ever seen.\n\nWe're getting Brahgas back. I believe it. You should too.

My friend, it has been a genuine pleasure. Except for that whole almost being sold into slavery bit.\n\nI suppose it does add a layer of suspense to the tale, though. All the best stories include some fool up to his ear-tips in trouble, right?
You may have bested me, but Teliv will vivisect you!\n\nGet out of my sight!

Hmm. Well played. I'd almost forgotten the bitter taste of defeat. I suppose I should thank you for this lesson in humility.\n\nOf course, you may face a similar lesson in Stormhold. Go on and face your next—and likely last—opponent.

I certainly didn't expect Brahgas to make it this far, but as I said, I never underestimate my opponents.\n\nWatching the two of you play should be quite the treat. Please, take a seat. I promise, I won't make a peep.
Wonder why the knight commander wants to speak to you and Dame Isobel?\n\nI do hope she's not annoyed that Isobel thought to free her friend from that ridiculous promise.
These faceless knights—the Ascended ones, or whatever they're called—are giving the Systres a bad name, if you ask me. Someone needs to do something about them.
Who cares about peace talks and outlaw knights right now? None of it's going to make any difference to the likes of me.\n\nI'm worried about Mount Firesong. And monsters coming up out of the ground!

The last batch of our newest drink was groundbreaking. Guaranteed to be a hit! We're not totally sure who drank the entire stock, but it's been suggested—hic—that it might have been me.\n\nBut now you're here! Thanks for agreeing to help.
So many crypts. Buried bodies. Knights and nobility. Even merchants with all their grave goods. The dead are all around us!
There are many ways to honor the True Way. This one believes quite sincerely in communion and prayer.
This ain't at all what I thought today was like, but it's uh … kinda entertaining, actually.
I did not expect to survive the wreck of Kamal's Bane. Nor did I expect to survive the Ascendant Order's dungeons, or the fight at All Flags Castle. Yet here I am. Thanks to you.
I'm not really comfortable rubbing elbows with nobles and kings in fancy palaces. I've spent a fair amount of my career trying to avoid royal attention, to be honest.
This is more like it! Good food, plenty of drinks, elegant company. Just what Za'ji hoped for when he set sail for Gonfalon Bay.
Strange. I expected palaces and parties when we set out for the Systres. Then we got shipwrecks and desperate battles against the Ascendant Order.\n\nNow we're back to palaces and parties again.
It seems the Prowler frequently catches winds that take us into trouble. Fortunately for me, I enjoy trouble.
So this is how the nobles of High Isle celebrate? Interesting. I've never been to one of these events before.
Father would never allow me to be here. Good thing I left him back at Brokerock Mine then, isn't it?
Ah, I had hoped to see you before the politics begin. You're quite impressive, you know that? \n\nAlmost … almost … up to my standards.
Good to see you again. Is … is the hat on straight? I'm still getting used to it.
You are here, too? Rigurt thought this was special meeting for diplomats. Although no one remembered to tell me about it. I just followed everyone else.
These sorts of events always captivate me, but I feel sorry for my poor manservant. Stibbons is more comfortable offering drinks and snacks than accepting them.
So many rich and powerful personages … I hate it when Lady Laurent makes me attend to her at such functions! The actual waitstaff gets annoyed when an unfamiliar manservant handles their dinnerware.
Do you ever get tired of being amazing? It seems like a lot of pressure! \n\nBut I'm glad to know I'm not the only one who thinks so. Go on, get out there!
Living as a vampire—or even vampire adjacent—would have felt impossible. Those creatures must take to thrive. Life, souls, safety—they steal everything.\n\nI only want to give to the world.

Ha! Just look at him—thrashing about like a fish on a hook. Almost makes you feel bad for him. Almost.\n\nYou should head back to the club. Sorinne and I will meet you there soon. Right after we thump this weepy sod.
Even on the verge of tears … I still want to punch him.
Knight Commander Jourvel is no different from any other mother, really. \n\nAlways worrying about her little chick.
I have wandered everywhere on this island. Seen every leaf. Touched every blade of grass. No one knows it better than I do.
I'm not going anywhere near that place. I'm too old to go looking for excitement and too young to risk my life carelessly. Go to Tor Draioch if you wish, but don't say I didn't warn you.
I forbid you from adding my accursed brother's name to that memorial plaque. I'm the master builder and I absolutely forbid it!
We are the Evergrowth. The one you sought, she carries the taint of our corruption. We remember her from the Undergrove. She performed the ritual that released this blight upon the land.
Niras is dead. The Pale Worm is ash. And my quest here is at an end.

So, you return to Marunji instead of pursuing another victory? Hmm.\n\nIf you wish to settle for a lesser prize, walker, that is your choice. Just remember, you can earn greater rewards if you win more matches!
Do you bring news, my friend? Is Lord Bacaro ready to summon us so we can finally engage in the discussions of peace?

I used to enjoy my visits to the archipelago. It was a welcome change from the hustle and bustle of my court. But because of the Ascendant Order, I'm practically a prisoner in here! \n\nBut tell me, what have you been up to?

They've separated us, have us under constant guard. I feel like a prisoner! And all because Lord Bacaro wants to maintain the sanctity of his peace talks. But I want to hear your news. Where have you been, my friend?

Don't say I didn't warn you. Save the day once and everyone expects you to do it again. But save the day twice? You'll never know a moment's peace.\n\nDon't worry. I won't get in your way. I'm officially out of the hero business—for real this time!

Why is Archdruid Devyric doing this? Is that flaming blight trying to cleave the Circles apart? He said he's after the Stonelore seed … but why?\n\nHe's heading toward the Dais of Stonesight, that's where I'll meet you. Druid Lyam needs my help.

Each of the druid circles has their own seed, why would the Firesongs kill for ours? \n\nIt doesn't matter, Archdruid Devyric will never get his rotting hands on the Stonelore seed now. I just hope the Eldertide's seed is safe too.
I'll hold the portal, but this is unstable magic I'm wielding. Once outside, hurry to the central core.\n\nI'll follow along once you make it to the other side. Look for another portal like this one.

Ah … my dauntless assistant returns! You look like you've been from one end of archipelago to the other … which is pretty much true, I suppose. \n\nSo, tell me, what did you think of the local cuisine? Which dishes did you sample?
That bear, it could have killed me with one swipe!

Use Dhulef's portal and meet us back at the Glenmoril Wyrd camp. We'll explain what happened and then figure out what to do with Frii.\n\nWe couldn't save Wyress Sorcha, but hopefully us stopping Archdruid Michiel will make things right with the wyrds.

We'll see you at the Glenmoril camp, sailor. Go ahead and use the portal. Take a bit out of me, but it's faster than walking.\n\nI've got a lot of questions for Frii. Not sure if they'll be able to answer them, but I can't wait to ask them!

Please, if you really mean to help, find Wyress Tola! Archdruid Michiel, there's a darkness in his eyes. I fear he'll hurt her once he gets what he wants. \n\nMaybe something in the Firesong camps will lead you to them. Please, hurry!

Thank you for coming to rescue me from that druid villain. Your arrival undoubtedly saved my life. But you were too late to stop the archdruid from completing his ritual. \n\nI think this is all related to the stories your friend Dhulef asked me about.

The Glenmoril Wyrds know this ancient spirit only through stories and legends. It sleeps in a ritual site hidden within the Sunken Road.\n\nPlease, find the site and save Wyress Sorcha. The archdruid … he seemed to enjoy hurting us.
Awake? Sap flowing, roots stirring … you! You dug me up! I was … asleep. Seasons and seasons. Plucked like a flower from the dream of the Green. A promise whispered in petals. Needed.

Distract the thugs and Raz will slip away. Then meet this one outside near the tavern. Raz is reminded of that time in Velyn Harbor. \n\nA bar, a pair of nasty thugs, and nowhere to go but out a window. Raz was picking glass out of his fur for days!
You look hungry, sandpiper. We have the finest kitchen in the city. Well, the finest kitchen on the block. Well, we've got a kitchen.\n\nAnyway, why not try some traditional archipelago fare?

I say, as far as seedy establishments go, this one is at the very top! The absolute nadir. \n\nNigh-toxic potables, deplorable clientele, sagging architecture … it has nearly everything I'm seeking. Very nearly.
Care for a bit of musical accompaniment with your drink? You could be enjoying that tasty brew while listening to a self-taught savant!\n\nNot that these swine know what they're missing.
Time is not on our side, five-claw. Let's find Redblade.

As someone who breaks rocks for a living, you've done amazing work on these crystals. One hit and they break into pieces!\n\nI think standing near all this lava has made me a bit dizzy. Let's hurry and find that last one.

While you head to Galen to secure Count Stefan's cooperation, I'll work with Lord Bacaro to get the peace talks underway. And I'll continue to watch for signs of the Ascendant Lord. By the time you return, perhaps I'll have uncovered something.

Come to think of it, this must be about the peace talks. Queen Ayrenn and the other leaders are quite annoyed that the talks haven't started yet.\n\nHurry, friend. Go to Mandrake Manor. And tell Lady Arabelle that Za'ji sent you, just like she asked.
We should return to Vastyr immediately, friend. If Sealord Nalos plans to bring the Dreadsail fleet against the city, we must get ready to welcome him.

If you seek more praise, you will find that I am not very generous. I've already thanked you and paid you for your part in saving my son.\n\nNow, speak to Stefan. He has something he wishes to discuss with you.

I had Sealord Nalos at the point of my blade. Then a wall of bodyguards rushed between us, damn their sails! That's twice now the maggot-ridden eel has escaped me.\n\nI'm done with this dank old druid shrine. Let's speak outside.
There you are! Sir Stefan is back, safe and sound. If you've got the Eldertide seed, take it to Archdruid Ellic in the Vine District. Then come back up to the castle—you aren't done yet.
Orlaith was going to take me, but Stefan intervened. He put himself in danger to save me and protect my circle.\n\nWe need to tell Count Mornard what happened. And then we have to help Stefan!

Archdruid Orlaith never planned to discuss peace this day. She let the Draoife gather so that she could eliminate us with one swift blow. Treachery indeed.\n\nWar has come to Galen, whether we wanted it or not.

I am trusting you, outsider. Rescue Druid Niraya and keep the sacred seed away from Archdruid Orlaith. Accomplish this and the Eldertide Circle will not forget it.\n\nRemember, Castle Tonnere, on the northwest coast.

I'll see these druids back to their village. You should return to Vastyr and report to Sir Stefan. He needs to know what happened here.\n\nHe should be back in Castle Mornard by now. You'll find him there.
I was certain we were all doomed when the volcano exploded. But no, we're all still alive. I suppose we have you to thank for that, five-claw?
I cannot thank you enough for your efforts on behalf of the archipelago. The Society of the Steadfast's vision of peace for all of Tamriel seems ever closer to becoming a reality.
Za'ji could get used to this hero business. If only it paid better. Ah, well.\n\nWhen you're done talking to everybody, let Za'ji know and we'll sail back to Vastyr.
I want to hear all about your conversations with the alliance leaders and Lord Bacaro, dear. But I think we need to deal with the situation I find myself in first, if that's all right with you.

What a season this has been, my friend. The Ascendant Order, rogue druids, a false druid king, and an ancient nature spirit … all because of a prophecy most of my people barely remember.\n\nI'm just glad you were here to help set things right.
Welcome to my little corner of Bayside Artisans. Here at Ashcroft's Fine Goods and Imports, the customer's satisfaction is our primary concern. How can I help you today?
Examine the carvings, friend. Then I'll tell you what I think they mean.
Things have taken a turn, five-claw. Of all the places this search could have led us, Raz did not think it would be to a dead Eye of the Queen. \n\nNot to Roneiia.

Not only did you complete the trials, but you also chose to pit yourself against even greater challenges and emerged victorious.\n\nQuite impressive. That kind of initiative is something the Elsweyr Defense Force can benefit from.
Salutations, newcomer. We're playing Tales of Tribute at this table.\n\nI see you have a stake. Are you interested in a game?

Archdruid Orlaith has the sacred seeds, some of my people … and Laurel now, too. If we don't turn over Frii, the Sower, she'll use the blood of innocents to secure her claim to the Ivy Throne.\n\nTell me you found something we can use, friend.

You continue to amaze me, friend. Your efforts on Y'ffelon went beyond the call of a mere mercenary. Thank you.\n\nWhile the druid circles choose new leaders and the Firesong regain our trust, it's better that we separate the regalia for now.
Shouldn't you be off rescuing those poor townsfolk or something? I think you'll find them somewhere along the beach to the east.
Druid Laurel's staff. I know it well. Hold it for her, please. I do not think she meant to leave it here unattended.
Ivyhame? I know that place. It's to the east, on the most-eastern tip of the island.\n\nFrii and I will meet you there, friend. Go with Y'ffre.

Looking back, I should have suspected something. All the delays in getting the peace talks underway. How the enemy always seemed to know what we were up to. I suppose Lord Bacaro was always just a little too good to be true.

To succeed in all three trials is rare. To champion the additional challenges is just unheard of!\n\nTruly, the Dragons of Elsweyr stand no chance against someone like you. I'm sure Captain Samara will be pleased.
Tell Lady Arabelle your story first, my friend. I can wait to hear the details.
I locked the crown in a case hidden behind one of the bookshelves. With any luck, they didn't find it before my knights drove them off. Let's look around.
Hi! Good to see you again! Why does Joslin look so glum?\n\nOh, wait a moment. I remember. The ritual. Something went wrong, didn't it? I knew we wouldn't get out of this that easily.
What did the druid say? Only one of us can be saved? Why is this happening to us? We were just trying to earn a living!
I can't thank you enough for all your help, friend. Remember that the Stonelore Circle owes you a great debt. Hopefully, one day we can repay it.
How did Lord Bacaro know this passage was here, I wonder.

Now to the reason I came here to find you. I made contact with Captain Siravaen. She agreed to help defend Vastyr, but only if she can recover her ship from the Dreadsails.\n\nWe'll have to hurry. I fear the Sea Elves and the Firesong will strike soon.

Well, here we are, right in the middle of a story that might be too outrageous for even Investigator Vale to tackle. Luckily, we have you.\n\nI still can't truly believe it. Bacaro, the Ascendant Lord. Let's get aboard the skiff and go, dear.

You know, we just left Veshin there in the sand. I feel a little bad for him. He's a bit arrogant, but in an attractive way. And he has such nice hair.\n\nPerhaps I'll go find him. Just make sure that he's all right.
That blast. It hurts. My chest burns. \n\nDo what you must. Help me.
Sea Elves never talk. They just plunder and kill. Why does this one want to confer with you? I recommend caution. It could be some sort of ruse.
Ah, this sweet lady. I wonder what secrets she has planned. Will she whisper her desire for me into your ear? I must know!\n\nNo, I can wait. Anticipation makes the revelation more delicious.

This is the kind of job that makes me happy I joined the Thieves Guild. Adventure, danger, and some romance. I even survived a threat to my very life.\n\nIt seems Quen wants to discuss some business with you. Never keep a lady waiting, I say.
You're here and the volcano has calmed down. I suspect that means you also dealt with this Lord Bacaro that everyone has been so concerned about? Good.
Talk to Sir Stefan and find out what brings him here. He should be back in Vastyr, waiting for us and shoring up his defenses.
Stefan? What's he doing here? Talk to him, friend. Find out what made him risk leaving the city to come all the way out here.
A vine-covered cave can only mean one thing, dear. That's our way into the mountain!
Thank you, my old friend. Take the seeds … go to the center of the chamber. Touch the mote of light ….

You're really making a habit out of saving the archipelago. And of aiding me. Thanks to you, we revealed Lord Bacaro as a traitor, saved the islands from an erupting volcano, and ended the threat of the false Druid King.\n\nWell done, my dear!
I wish they'd just leave us alone. For a bunch of pirates, they sure do love to control everything.
You shouldn't be here, outsider. The other Dreadsails will gut you if they find you.\n\nBut since you'are here, why not stay awhile, gorgeous?

I think Frii set that ward. They must be somewhere beyond that door. At least the Firesong haven't been able to get past it yet.\n\nLet's look around and hope we're smarter than they are. Or at least a little luckier.
Nervous, trembling leaves. Armor that shimmers, but can it protect? You must speak with the druid in armor. Go now. The trees whisper. Urgent, urgent.
I got you that drink, friend. Grab your mug and let's toast!
Lord Bacaro, the Ascendant Lord. You know, I never really trusted that man. He was too … charitable.\n\nAnyway, congratulations on solving the mystery and saving the archipelago. You have my thanks.
Did Yves send you? No. \n\nI swear it feels like he's refusing to call for my claws in order to keep my debt longer.

I'm as surprised and appalled by the revelations as you and Lady Arabelle. I believed in Lord Bacaro, trusted him. He betrayed us all.\n\nI swear to you, the Society of the Steadfast played no part in his grand schemes.

Nuzdef, one of the wounded initiates, is nearby. Speak to him before you go if you'd like his account of what happened. Maybe it will help you in facing the chimera. \n\nHe fared better than the others … but think twice before telling him that.
Hmm. By the looks of you, I imagine you're here about the handbills posted around the city. Does that mean you're up for the dangerous work House Mornard is offering?

A hard decision to make, but the right one, I believe. I just wish there had been a way to restore both of them.\n\nYou should talk to Joslin, friend. She should be relieved to no longer be a tree, but she lost her cousin this day.
What happened? Everything is so … unclear.
We planted all the seeds I brought with me. Let's leave and let the Fauns find the berries on their own. I learned long ago that they like to discover food for themselves.

A handful of sketches, how hard can that be? Just ask Urtisa Drolnor about Embervine if you need to know more. I think I saw her at the fountain outside the cathedral's gate.\n\nOh, if only I could go! People say I have an eye for beauty.

Look, if it's all the same to you just leave me be. I got cargo sinking off the coast, a crew that needs to get paid, and a ship that can hardly float.\n\nI don't need a tiresome mainlander pestering me on top of all that.
Go ahead and speak with the alliance leaders. They're waiting for you downstairs.
Look, friend, I just want to finish my drink in peace and plan my escape from this gods-forsaken island.\n\nPlease, leave me be before you attract any unwanted attention.

I heard what Lady Arabelle told you. Well, you can't keep the leaders of the three alliances waiting. That's a capital offense, I believe. Go on downstairs and present yourself. We can catch up later.
Archdruid Ellic! We have to help him!
Please, don't let them take me!

And just between us, the talks with the druid circles aren't going too badly. I just lose patience sometimes. I want everything to happen right now, but flowers blossom when they're ready, am I right?
Za'ji and Caska will leave for the islet at once! And we'll bring along a few of the Pounce's crew. A little extra muscle never hurts, yes?
Invited to the peace talks? I suppose that means we're important now. Moons help us all.
Portal travel is perfectly safe. And Dhulef is a good mage. Go on. I'll see you in Vastyr.

Urdiir the Guardian is awake, but the danger is past. We should depart before the great spirit turns its attention to us. We are intruders here, too, after all.\n\nLet us return to Vastyr and finish our talk there.

We will mourn those we lost this day, but we must take heart and remember that we fought back against an overwhelming enemy and prevailed.\n\nThe Dreadsails are leaderless. The Firesong have retreated. And we're still alive to oppose them!
Go. There might be someone left alive under all that rubble.

Horrible. So much death, so much suffering. Young Stefan lost two fathers today, and the city lost even more. I keep asking myself why I survived when so many others perished?\n\nBut I wanted to talk to you before you go in to see Sir Stefan.
How intriguing. Even now you can feel the subtle vibrations shaking this island. So very much like Vvardenfell. Fascinating.\n\nI wonder, can you feel the island's movement?
King Kasorayn needs you, Aiven. I will tend to this.
The knot is untangling. The threads are once again taut and clear.\n\nI have spent all my abilities. All there's left is returning home.
Have you seen a wandering Breton, by chance? A hireling? Gods, I fear the worst has happened. My boy!
Greetings, friend. May the sun always find your path.
Do try not to knock anything over. I'm due to restock my supplies, and these subjects are all I have left.
Do I look like I can carry on a conversation right now?
If you're going out into the wilderness make sure you keep your blade sharp and your boots laced. Galen holds plenty of surprises for the casual traveler and none should be taken lightly.
Friend of Laurel. I am Frii, keeper, nourisher, sower. Song of the Green. The king spoke, Frii became. Dream given form. Made real.\n\nAwakened too early … unrest in the soil. Something is wrong.
Unless you have pressing business, I advise you to move along. While we stand here talking, the jungle and the waves are tearing down our walls.
Protected but afraid. Safe yet unsure. The story goes round and round.
Clear skies, mate! Our paths will cross again before you know it.

Young Sir Stefan is over there with his father, Count Mornard. They will readily accept any assistance you're willing to offer.\n\nNow if you'll excuse me, the Society of the Steadfast's work is never done.

Once again you have saved the day, my friend. Evil druids, rogue knights, marauding pirates—you dealt with them all.\n\nNow go on. Talk to Sir Stefan. Or should I say Count Stefan? Either way, I'm curious to hear what's on his mind.
That Khajiit has to be close. He can't have made it off Galen already.

Hello, mate! I understand that what's about to happen here is in no small part because of you.\n\nDon't mind me. I'm just an observer. The Mages Guild rightly sent Valessea to represent our interests here.
What brings you back here so soon, friend? Not another danger to the archipelago, I hope.

Despite all the troubles, I'm glad I visited the Systres. Who would have thought such a few small isles would become a hub of commerce?\n\nWith the volcano calmed, there should be much more work for me now.
You helped everyone here and saved the archipelago? And you still had time to help Joslin and me? Thank you!
This is a lot of fancy-dressed nobles. Hope my dirt-stained boots don't draw too much attention.

Sailing to the Systres isles wasn't my favorite experience. The ships rocking and the splashing water—well, let's say my lunch returned to the sea.\n\nBut I'm glad I came. Galen's beauty is worth the trip.
Quite the hero you turned out to be! Saving the Systres and without my help. Well, we'll just tell everyone you learned from the best. Me!
First the Chronicle and now this Frii? Are we to lose more nature spirits? No, surely not. Y'ffre cannot be that displeased with us.
So many people are here, outsiders and druids alike. It … feels good to be among so many new faces.
The spirit of the mountain created an avatar to defend itself and the false king. Interesting.\n\nYou must defeat it to get to Lord Bacaro.
House Mornard stands ready to provide whatever assistance Lady Arabelle requires. You have my word.
Before you ask, I would not advise trying to pet my Unu. He can be a little bitey when he's hungry.

Good to know you can stand the heat! The vulk'esh meat and reaper peppers can be found in the wilds of northern Galen. Try buying some Vastyr brandy over at the Jaded Ornaug Tavern.\n\nThen hurry back. I'll save you the first scrumptious bite!
None of this makes sense to me. I hope Captain Siravaen knows what she's doing.
You look ready to turn your blade on us the moment you don't think you need the Gilded Blades anymore. Fine. I'll just kill you then.
I haven't the time to speak just now. I await a meeting with some important clientele. \n\nMy delicious brandy will soon be the stuff of legend in every manor house and castle from here to Wayrest.
You can see me! And you're not running scared either. \n\nApologies … so many walk these beaches without ever noticing me. This is an unexpected gift. Perhaps this is fate, and you can help.
Oh, I'm sorry. I didn't notice you there. I get lost sometimes, looking out toward the sea ….\n\nWhere are my manners? Is there something I can help you with?
Frii and I will meet you at Ivyhame, friend. Go with Y'ffre.

We can't ignore the Firesong threat against the captives they took from Vastyr. Archdruid Orlaith is so caught up in her mad vision, there's nothing she wouldn't do. Ask Sir Stefan how he wants to play this.
I understand what Laurel is trying to do here. I even hope it works. Still, there are those among my circle who are not ready to let go of their anger with the Firesong.
Many of us knew Archdruid Orlaith was leading our circle down a dark path, and we did nothing. I would understand if the Stonelore and the Eldertide never trusted the Firesong Circle again.
My magic won't last forever, mate. Step into the portal. It will take you directly to Vastyr.
I'll be the first to admit that I never liked Count Mornard. But his son? He's so young and his head is filled with all that druid nonsense. I see bad days ahead for Vastyr. Bad days indeed.

It is a shame about our beautiful cathedral. And poor Count Mornard, of course. I do hope young Stefan can live up to the challenge. It's not like we have anyone else to turn to. \n\nUnless … what do you think of Duchess Elea?
I've heard of your heroics on behalf of Sir Stefan and House Mornard. We could use more people like you. Our knights are stretched pretty thin right now.

Fayda means well, but if the druids are coming to help defend the city, I must also do my part. I may not be a trained knight like she is, but I've learned a thing or two roaming about the wilderness. Tell her I don't require protection.
Your heroics precede you, friend. Count Stefan has nothing but praise for your actions on behalf of the entire archipelago. For that, you also have my thanks.

The contract is a standard agreement that protects both parties. I have profited from the benefits of such a contract for more than a century. Signing it will ensure that Mora cannot do anything to knowingly harm you or Nirn.\n\nSign it, proxy.
I've sailed some stormy waters in my time. But today is about the worst I have ever been caught up in. Count Mornard was a hard man to like, but he didn't deserve what he got.

Oh! Ah … Hello.\n\nDon't mind the Watcher, they're friendly. Zilipif has been with this one since he started in the Scribes of Mora. Now, when Keshargo seeks to take the scribes back from Valinna, Zilipif wouldn't think of leaving his side.

Riftmaster Naqri will not let us through the gates. He's always been loyal to Valinna.\n\nBeyond the next corridor is the Deadlands Rift. It should remain stable for a little while longer. Defeat Naqri and we'll be on our way.

Hurry, friend. You can't assist the Great Eye without the Emerald Glyphic. Take it and depart before more of these mercenaries arrive.\n\nJust … be cautious of Leramil. Her thirst for knowledge doesn't preclude her from being the threat foreseen.
Never have the threads of fate become so twisted between Apocrypha and Nirn.
The Lark got away, but the remaining Khajiit are safe, right? Then it's a victory in my book.\n\nDid you … recover anything else for me?

You. You saved the Clockwork City. As a friend to the Living Gods, help me. \n\nKemel-Ze—Sotha Sil's sacred underground laboratory is under attack. It hasn't been disturbed since Sotha Sil studied with the Dwarves there. Please. Before it's overrun!
