You are still standing here? This one is concerned you do not know what is good for you.
You are clever as the Pariah, walker.\n\nThis one wishes you luck and safe travels in every endeavor. May our roads meet again, friend of the Baandari.
I do think this attempted theft might actually encourage more Telvanni to visit our humble shrine!\n\nOne can hope, anyway.
With you providing a distraction, this writ just got significantly easier. Camonnaruhn is just ahead. Are you ready to see what traitorous cretins like Luaffyn Romavel and the Camonna Tong can do?
By the Green this is ghastly. I can't even begin to surmise the damage.
Scanning Component Location: Components Nearby. \n\nInsert Into Palmar Shelf.
Sorry, can't talk—I've got somewhere I need to be.\n\nAnd if anyone asks, you didn't see me.
The reputation of this place far exceeds its actual grandeur, I'll say.

This is a visually recorded journal—one of Seht's inventions that was too flawed to bring to the Clockwork City.\n\nI wonder what the issue with this one is? No matter, the only way to understand is to study. I'll keep a record of my time here.

Take this rune. It will draw you to our most powerful relics. As you find Dremnaken portals, use the rune to collapse them. Once completed, reset the ward at the peak.\n\nNow go, agent of fate. Ascend the Apogee. We shall await your return.

I perceive the outline of our adversaries' plan. They require a key to reach a dream which only Hermaeus Mora remembers. And a rite that involves a Black Book. Someone knows a great deal about Apocrypha and this conspiracy of secrets, but who?

The three glyphics before you contain the concepts necessary to create a contract to bind us. I submit to this as a promise of cooperation. You may serve as my proxy without fear of harming your own interests.\n\nNow take the glyphics. Combine them.

Well, there they go. My creatures are off to Fargrave and I'll follow soon behind them. Plokun's Inquisitive Menagerie will perform as planned, thanks to you.\n\nPerhaps I underestimated the capabilities of mortals.

Take the key from the desk and head to the catacombs. The door is through the chapel and to the north. I'll stay with Abbot Ilvel. Do what I can until he recovers.\n\nJust be careful. We know Blightcrown didn't arrive at the Necropolis by himself.

Port Agent Randas likes to fish at a little cove south of the city. Even when he's supposed to be working. Tell him to get his arse back here and I'll let you look around the Stormwing.\n\nJust be careful. The wildlife along the coast can be dangerous.

If Cindieth had wandered in here alone and gotten herself killed, how long before the Consortium sent another to find us? A day? A week?\n\nWe're lucky someone of your mettle was nearby. You have my thanks, friend. Truly.
If it isn't the savior of Anchre themselves! I knew we'd see one another again around Necrom. This city could use someone of your talents!
Well well, not often do you get to see a hero in the flesh! How are you?
We feel more certain than ever about our task. Our clan will gather and discuss how to prioritize. The Cenotaph of the Remnants will become the sword and shield of Hermaeus Mora once again.
This man is a friend of yours, no? He feels … quite familiar.

That's the lot of them, right? I imagine Vorm would prefer the safe expanses of the Endless Library to perform whatever magic he needs to do rather than this frankly overcrowded study.\n\nWe'll meet you outside when you're done in here!
Tapping into the ancient cairns of Apocrypha, what could possibly go wrong? Well, other than everything?\n\nProceed with caution, mortal.
If you did indeed find something, my friend, please share it with Leramil.

The Empyrean Ascent. This is where prophecies that foretell the changing of regimes and dynasties are stored. Powerful knowledge to be sure. Even a single page would allow someone to sway the currents of the realm's politics in their favor.

Perhaps now I understand why Mora's trap made me a passive observer. After all, if a cultist of Peryite was able to make his way into the Divinatory Forums on my watch … then what good was I as an overseer?

Look after Gadayn, adventurer. He's young and he has seen little of the world. He'll need you to guide and teach him.\n\nI have a feeling that the schemes of Daedric Princes will take you both farther than we can imagine.
Ah, fresh air. Better, yes?\n\nAccording to my instruments, you made it out of the Chorus with nary a scratch on your psyche. How are your memories? Any confusion? Dizziness? No? Good!
Looks like Leramil's spell worked. Take what it dredged up before it slips back into the stack.
Take a look around, proxy. Meln the Mouthless mentioned a letter, as well as his own mortal remains. Let us hope we find something to point us in the right direction.
Traveler, I can sense the Great Eye's blessing upon you! You must tell me what it feels like to bask in the Prince of Knowledge's unwavering gaze.
I will obtain Tel Rendys's secrets. It's just a matter of time.
We can understand resistance to giving up. A fighting spirit infuses the Remnants to their core.\n\nBut we see a difference between struggling against the odds and denying your fate.
Apologies, traveler. I am very busy right now. There's never a moment's rest for a Cipher of the Eye.
Traveler, I sense the unflinching gaze of the Great Eye upon you. I hope you find what you seek in our bountiful collections.
I've been a Cipher for more years than I care to count. But I remember the day the Lord of Secrets invited me to tend his Endless Library. Proudest day of my life.
Welcome to Cipher's Midden, traveler. Enjoy the hospitality of our settlement and feel free to peruse the many tomes in our collection.
Go to the northwest region of the Chroma Incognito and see what you can find, proxy. I shall catch up with you in due course.
I think the lens is just part of the trap. Probably doesn't do a damn thing.\n\nThe mad old mage probably thought it would be funny to send intruders around in circles trying to figure it out.
The cairn is glowing, just as Leramil said. Let's find the others and finish this.
Hmm. You don't look like one of those useless scribes.
Reynila knew me. I don't remember her at all. \n\nJust give me a moment. This is a lot to happen so suddenly.

I see you were able to follow the clues I left in my tower, but you took your sweet time. I can't defy Shelreni much longer. If we're going to get out of here and keep me from complying with that lying murderer, you must do exactly as I say.
The Fulcrum Obscura passed through this door. It is definitely leading Blightcrown and Torvesard somewhere. Let us follow while the Eye of Mora is still distracted.
The corrupted scrolls are inside Quires Wind. I need you to destroy them. And find Cipher Sabinius, if you can. There must be an explanation for how those scrolls came to be here.
Brelynn and Cortin shouldn't give you any trouble. And if they bother you with questions, just remember not to give them anything for free.
You have the papers? Good. Now take them to Mouth Delvi's desk over in the south alcove and leave them there. Discreetly!
Move along, dear. We don't know each other, and I don't care to change that.

Come back soon to try Cortin's Cordial! My new and improved formula has half the bitterness and twice the benefits!\n\nOne sip will get you hooked! Guaranteed! I just need to let this batch finish brewing.
Keep your eye on that strange mortal. He already charmed me into throwing away my master's favorite glyphic once today!
You really do make an invaluable field assistant, meddler. Even your Watchling friend here played his part expertly. Now please, the glyphic. I can't stand to wait any longer.

Torvesard chased a fragment of a dream across Apocrypha, beginning the process of restoring a memory that can destroy reality.\n\nAs Hermaeus Mora told you, the threads of fate have frayed, but they have not yet snapped.
Glyphics endure for eternity. I've never heard of any erasing themselves before. Very strange. Do you understand the text that remained, mortal? I found the words very disturbing.
Where's Keshargo? He said he'd meet us here. You don't think anything's happened to him, do you?\n\nWe should go find him. Valinna said any intruder should be killed on the spot.
Right. Walk with purpose, don't make eye contact, and no one should pay us mind.\n\nMistress Dreloth's chambers are at the top of this tower. The key is there.

Dacia … join me on this side of the ward? But she'd be afflicted forever. Or until we find a cure.\n\nWe always talked of leaving Tel Dreloth and traveling Tamriel together. Could she really be happy staying here? With me?

I'd kept this secret from Nathyn his whole life—that he might not grow up knowing he was a monster of my own making. That he might keep his will to live while I sought a cure.\n\nAfter all, I gave him the Knahaten Flu and cured him of that, too.

Fortunately, we have two conduits to spirits not yet bound for Aetherius at our disposal. Magister Meln and Curate Gadayn.\n\nSpeak to Meln first. He obviously knows what happens when a Telvanni mage dies.
The corpse-keeper is eager to tell you what he discovered. Oblivion forbid that I ruin his surprise. You should speak with him.
It sounds like the conclave has started. Did you find Master Shelreni?

What could Shelreni be thinking? She's obviously counting on the support of two Daedric Princes, but does she really expect them to magically elevate her to the rank of magister?\n\nLet's get to Tel Huulen in Ald Isra and see if the cloak works.
A sheaf of parchment in the right hands can mean the difference between life and death. Doubly so in Morrowind.
Thank Azura you made it. But I think Sharp wishes to speak with you.
You've been quite helpful. Perhaps I'll contract for your services again someday.
It seems you've succeeded where all my previous visitors failed. Most of them fled at the sight of the Daedra, but not you. That's impressive.

With that, the writ is complete. I'm still curious why Guitot decided to betray his master, but I suppose that doesn't really matter at this point.\n\nIn a place like this, you don't always need a reason for betrayal.

Reynila …. She can't be gone. She fought so hard to protect me. What am I going to do?\n\nWe were supposed to have help. I thought maybe you and Sharp—but I can see it in his eyes. He doesn't remember me, does he? He doesn't remember anything.
I spend all my time cleaning the floor to make it shine. Naturally, as soon as I finish, someone tracks mud all over it.
We came all this way and you still haven't collected Whim's new boon? Go! Pick it up! Hezehk tires of all this.
All that time I spent worrying that I was going to be someone else when I got my memories back ….\n\nWell, I guess it's safe to say I don't need to worry about that anymore.
Sharp looks like he wants a word with you.
I see the Morag Tong was able to close out the writ. We thank you for your work. I doubt Guitot had the courage or intelligence to do this on his own. I wonder which of my rivals was helping him.
The Telvanni tell people that we should feel grateful to work for them. Two meals and a straw bed just aren't enough.
Just leave me be. I have nothing for you.
Greetings to you walker!
Touch the tyranite calx when you're ready to start.
Hello, mortal. I am a memory gestalt facsimile. Sotha Sil in all but flesh.\n\nI see Nilphas Drethan's bid for control over the Probabilis is over. Good. He lacked the capacity to understand it.
You look like a fellow soldier of fortune. I have no quarrel with you … at least until my employer tells me otherwise. Mind your manners, sellsword.

Dark skies loom overhead, but fortune smiles on us. You are just in time to be of great assistance to the Mages Guild. \n\nDo you see Warlock Vanton there on the bed? He fights a terrible battle. A battle we must help him win.

It's time to go. Speak to Wizard Twelvane. She'll tell you how to enter Vanton's mind.\n\nYou'll need more than bravery in there. I hope you're skilled enough to meet whatever nightmare Ansuul has created from Vanton's dreams.

We don't like to discriminate against the more bookish members of our guild. In fact, we tend to encourage them. But we need an adventurer, not a librarian.\n\nThe guild has need of you. It will be dangerous, but we can compensate you.
Ohrijha is a purveyor of useful tonics and tinctures. If you are bleeding from a wound, however, you want to one who can stitch you up. This one does not care for needles. Or blood.
The rest of Tel Huulen is restricted, outsider. If you have business here, conduct it in this chamber.
The Morag Tong's assistant? You certainly get around. While I appreciate what you did for the assembly … for me … this is a matter for the masters and the magister. You really shouldn't be in here.
I have nothing to say to you, outsider. Not only did you cost me the life of a valued servant, you set back my plans in the assembly. I will not soon forget such insults.
You must heed my warning. Lives are at risk!
Not now! We should watch what's happening!

Destructive doppelganger dealt with? Yes. Threat to the populace of Skywatch contained? Yes. \n\nDecade-long research project and irreplaceable relic destroyed? Sadly, yes. I suppose it's been a good day's work.
I've no matters with any strangers unless they're aiming to buy me a pint.
A vine-covered cave can only mean one thing, dear. That's our way into the mountain!

Much to think on, much to do. Some kind of fate binding. Go on the offense? Or are runic bulwarks the better choice? \n\nBest to review Martina's research … and of course there's still the Key to consider. Blast!
Some of my cohorts dislike the work of the expungatory, but I find it quite soothing. Especially after the rigors of field work.
The kettle's broken but the tea cup holds. Let's do that again!\n\nThrough the door, before someone steals it.
You made the right choice. I'll remain here to carry out what role Herm'us Mora's chosen for me. Fear not, I'm at peace knowing that my son will carry on.
One moment we were trying to follow you into that big eye, the next Leramil and I were back here in Cipher's Midden. I'm not particularly fond of these rapid changes in scenery.
I wandered a memory of the Great Eye. Floated through the chambers of the Mythos. Do you think Hermaeus Mora will send me to an expungatorium? I would really hate that.
Do you see it? The telltale sign of a spiritual presence? Go take a closer look.
Spirits can be unpredictable and dangerous. Especially the spirits of recently deceased Telvanni masters.
They used me! They held out the promise of power and I snatched at it like a foolish child!\n\nDeath will not stop me. I'll find a way ….
Hmm. You aren't a Dreamcarver. What's your purpose here? Are you threatening Morian?
Let us meet at the location where we first entered the Infinite Panopticon. While the entrance never appears in the same place twice, I have an idea that might just turn this to our favor.
Vaermina isn't just seeking a lost memory—she wants to punish the Great Eye! We need to stop her, mortal!
It cannot be avoided. Fate's chosen must make sure the glyphic is secure and the memory intact. We shall talk again when you are done.
Let's make this quick. I'm contemplating deep mysteries here and you're going to make me lose my train of thought.
May the Three guide your path.
Torvesard has the second glyphic and is invisible to the One Who Knows. Our task is clear, proxy. We must find Torvesard and recover the glyphic before he can break the seals.
Let me explain! The ingredients were faulty! I got the dosage wrong! Yes, I'm certain there's a way out of this!
Do you need something? I don't have time to waste with someone below my station. I've important House Telvanni affairs to see to, and my head is aching.
What you want, s'wit?
Well, you've made yourself useful in some small way. But I've no time to dally.
I don't like the looks on your and Meln's faces. Something went wrong, didn't it? There's still some terrible danger that needs to be dealt with?\n\nWell, don't tell me about it! Talk to Leramil!
Glad I was able to help back there. But sorry Torvesard got away. \n\nGo on, talk to Leramil. I'm sure we're not finished yet. At least, reality still seems to be stable. For the moment.
Do as Leramil says, mortal. Bringing these disparate threads into alignment is no easy task!

My many ocular orbs appreciate what you did in the Mythos. That foul corruption was worse than forgetting to blink during a firestorm in the Deadlands.\n\nBut I really wanted to see you beat Vaermina with a stick. Sorry I missed that.
The way into the Mythos stands before you. Take your allies and go.
Did you find any clues to Akacirn's whereabouts in Quires Wind? It's often futile to seek justice from Apocrypha, but three dead ciphers demand an answer. Find him, traveler—wherever the trail leads.
Be on your way, mortal. You may be of some passing interest to Hermaeus Mora, but I have other matters on my mind.
I'm not stealing anything! I'm just borrowing the place for a bit.

I'll mark your map with the location of the Glasscrags gate, as well as where the Seekers flock.\n\nMora's foes control these Seekers. Find them, kill them, and take their ichor. Once you collect enough, you can open the gate and enter the Bastion.

Hello, mortal. The Great Eye told me what happened. Even though things didn't go exactly the way we hoped, we're all still here. That means reality is stable, for now.\n\nI'm as surprised as you, but existence is resilient. At least for another day.
I must consider the best parts of the Necropolis to show to Leramil. She wants to see everything!\n\nWe'll meet you in Necrom, friend. At the Necropolis.
There's something not quite right over to the west. Use my ghost sight to investigate.
Give Gadayn some assurance, proxy. Then come back and speak with me when you are done.

Well done. I half-expected my young curate to flee the hall rather than speak to this assembly. But he did a magnificent job!\n\nThank you again for helping Gadayn recover the Fulcrum Obscura. The Necropolis wouldn't be the same without it.
Some day fate will look kindly upon me. Not today, apparently, but eventually.
Wouldn't mind shoving this s'wit through a portal to Oblivion. Ahem. Don't tell him I said that.
A portal to Apocrypha. Can't say I'm not intrigued by the idea of going to a plane of Oblivion but why can't it be somewhere more uplifting. I'm certain Azura's realm might be more inviting.
Apocrypha! Feh, I can't imagine the magisters haven't already accounted for such things. What troubles me is ensuring that this hireling stays out of my hair.
A portal between Mundus and Apocrypha? That's a terrifying thought. Perhaps slightly less terrifying than the thought of being shoved through it by Spellwright Moran.
The fate of fates is imperiled by forces that even the all-seeing eye cannot see and yet we remain steadfast in our duty.
The waxing of power amasses as those who seek to pry convene around you.
I have no time for outsiders. Away with you.
You'll never get away from me, you know.
Didn't I make myself clear? Remove yourself from this chamber or I will have you removed, mouth of the mouthless.
This should teach Brelynn and Menredius a lesson. Don't get too comfortable until you've paid off your debts.
Cortin deserves a beating more than some flower.
Don't talk to me. I'm in enough trouble already.
Zemzo does not believe it wise to anger a renowned assassin. Not even a Telvanni master should be so disrespectful.
It takes so long to find someone you can trust. Raise them up, teach them how best to serve you. So much time invested. Then, they go and do this.\n\nThank you, I guess. Now, please, leave me be.
The easiest part of my day comes while Master Foves enjoys his first meal. He insists that I leave him alone while he eats his kwama eggs. That's when I enjoy a nice book.
Azandar al-Cybiades back at Shad Astula. ALMSIVI's arse, I never thought I'd see the day.\n\nPray tell me, attractive stranger, what in Aetherius could he possibly want?

Odd. The estate here isn't as illustrious as I was led to believe. And do you smell that? There's a strange stench in the air here. Like something is burning?\n\nLet's get moving and look for Dreynis.

I was a fool to think we'd outsmarted the Prince of Knowledge. And it seems dear Tralise has paid the price of my hubris. Please, speak with my daughter Tralise.\n\nI must speak with my Mouth. There's much to be done.

I wouldn't have thought I'd ever rely on the kindness of a stranger. While this may not have been the showcase we intended, I assure you our family is still destined for great things.\n\nTrust that I will see to that.
Place the phylactery within the ritual circle. Once it is in place we'll be able to siphon and distribute the curse binding my father.
For the first time in all my dealings with the One Who Knows, there is a portion of this plight that the Prince cannot see.\n\nYou do not know how much that notion troubles me, proxy.

Another Tho'at Replicanum gone. I shouldn't be impressed, but I am.\n\nThere are more versions of Tho'at roaming the Infinite Archive. I'd understand if you want to keep hunting them, but I do have your payment.

Shelreni Baro was ambitious to a fault when I mentored her. Now she's in league with two Daedric Princes and a clan of Dremora? I knew she was reckless, but deals with Princes always end badly.\n\nOh, probably not for you. You should be fine.

And with that, I think we're done for today. After all, you might change your mind after you've had to deal with one sister or the other for much longer.\n\nLord, Mother, and Wizard, I know I do from time to time.

Helping us with the maligraphies are you? You know that they're not here, right? Good, good. It'd be really embarrassing if you were confused.\n\nOh, and you should bring another mortal with you. You'll need the help.

Let's see. Limbs, mouth, clothes … yes you're a mortal. One moment, he had me remember something. Ahem.\n\nBrave adventurer, the Infinite Archive requires your aid. Reality warps in its halls and I, Master Malkhest, cannot defend them alone.

So many hiding places in the archive. Too much chaos. Even Master Malkhest doesn't know where everything is. If only the filers were better!\n\nSorry, it's just so overwhelming. I'm sure you'll find everything. Then I can finish my translation.

You're back! And with my dowry in tow! This is still plenty to impress the Verdulis's eldest daughter and secure her hand. I could kiss you, adventurer! Though, I suppose I should save that for my bride-to-be.
I know the tharriker are intimidating beasts, but if you're gentle, they'll respond in kind. Usually.
Apologies for dashing off like that. Those horrible crystaljacks were really starting to unnerve me. Besides, I wanted to get Lazen to safety. \n\nNow, what was in that note you grabbed?
Don't know what Orissa expects to find. The bastards are likely gone by now. Nothing but a waste of time to search that cave.
Let us go, proxy. There is nothing more we can do here.

Greetings, champion!\n\nLeramil the Wise sent me to find you on behalf of Hermaeus Mora, the Daedric Prince of Fate and Forbidden Knowledge. Disaster looms over both his realm and ours. Only you can meet this threat.

It's been so long since I fought anyone, let alone had the duel feel so invigorating. \n\nHmm. I don't recognize you. You must be new. For someone so untried to fight against someone so renowned … well, I am impressed.

Ithelia has become the threat that Hermaeus Mora foresaw, racing to Apocrypha to take the realm as her own. And with each passing moment, reality breaks down a little more.\n\nTime grows ever shorter, proxy.
Reality is falling apart around us and you want to chat? Well, then go talk to Leramil and let's figure out where we can find Prince Ithelia!
Orissa would like to speak to you. She is over there with dear old Lazen.
Yeah, I wasn't paying attention to the pattern either. \n\nJust activate the alarum again and watch the pattern. Then replicate the pattern to release the shard.

A good officer gives credit where credit is due. You did good here, comrade. Rustwall won't be ready to host Count Calantius and his guests for a while, but we learned the fate of my cohort and stopped an invasion.\n\nNot bad for a day's work.

So, the Recollection think their poison is strong? I've inhaled worse concoctions from our wise woman.\n\nThe Staff of Many Paths though, maybe it dropped. I have to find it. Those Wood Elves can't take that, too.
Uh, I always feel unclean after traveling through a portal from Oblivion. But enough of my problems, go talk to Scruut.
You really did it? You created a new Daedric relic? That's not something that happens every day.
Use the relic. Let us see what it reveals.
Ah, are you here about the job postings? West Weald's Legion could use some capable hands.
If you're on of those Recollection bastards, you have a lot to answer for. Tell me why we shouldn't just run you through, Wood Elf.

That was excellent work, friend. We destroyed Lord Gallio's laboratory and managed to rescue the workers he experimented on.\n\nThere might be some ramifications over any remaining Vesper Valente, but it won't become the sweeping problem I feared.
I think your High Elf friend would like to have a word with you. Continue your hunt, traveler. I'll continue mine.
This is no place to wander aimlessly, traveler. The foul beasts are vicious and hungry for blood!
Oh, uh, I'm all right. My knees just don't seem to want to work. There's so much to do. I have to tell our parents. \n\nOh gods, I have to tell our parents.
Be wary. That man is Edric, the estate's cook, and he seems on edge. One should always worry when the help looks nervous.
Where is Betu going off to now?
I could use your help planning our debut. If you're willing, of course!
Let us examine the scene. Hopefully something here can explain what befell Edric.
I have a bad feeling, mortal. True, I have a bad feeling about most things, but this is different. Badder. More bad.
Another task, another danger to deal with. It never ends, does it, proxy?\n\nGo on. Talk to Scruut and see what else the One Who Knows requires of us.

That memory showed us priests of Mephala, persecuted by servants of the Tribunal. But I do not know anything about a skein, or why such a thing might be of interest to Torvesard.\n\nActivate the gate. If there are answers, they are through there.
I'm not sure I want to drink anything else offered to me by a vampire, but I suppose Fennorian can be trusted. With this matter at least.
Valente certainly loves his games, but his offer was too good to ignore.
The auction will begin shortly.
I have no quarrel with you, mortal. I only seek to restore my Prince.
I guess we're done here, right? I know I'll feel a lot better about things once we're back in our own world.
Have you visited the library yet? If an answer to your questions is to be found, you will likely find it there.
Few travelers come to Holamayan. You must have walked a strange road indeed to arrive at our doorstep.
What are you waiting for? Give her the drink already!

Legionary Calvo can get you into the fort through a side passage and guide you inside.\n\nYou need to find the communique that contains the current chime sequence, the key to the bell tower, and then grab our payroll before those deserters find it.

Betu has always been the incorrigible sort. Best not to let him walk all over you. \n\nApologies. I should introduce myself. My name is Edric Brussiner. I was Lady Weatherleah's cook. A terrible thing, her death. Beyond compare.
Thank Malacath you're back. Grander's pitiful whimpering was beginning to drive me mad. Go talk to him. And if he say's he hasn't been crying, he's lying.
Everything was going fine until that idiot Theophan came bumbling back into my life.

I didn't realize Mizzik had an assistant! A pleasure to meet you. I hope, despite the circumstances, you will find time to enjoy the estate grounds. It's beautiful this time of year. A small blessing while we grieve.
Excuse my shouting, traveler. You wouldn't happen to have seen a dog running around? Large, fluffy, carrying a very important, estate-defining scroll in his mouth?
Let me get a good look at you. Hmm.\n\nYou show promise. If you want to join the Oathsworn, there are spots open in the Lodge of the Fist. Maybe even the Lodge of the Axe given that fight.
Hermaeus Mora, the One Who Knows. For all his knowledge and foresight, his solution remains the same. To repeat our cycle. Such is the nature of the Daedra, mortal.\n\nLet us proceed.

You've returned! I'm already getting reports of the tide of beasts waning and we're tending to the townsfolk you helped. Thank you.\n\nNow tell me, what of the Recollection? Were you able to stop their rituals?

Encountering a material conformation of … that is, I thought it would take longer for us to find and confront Ithelia in person.\n\nWe determined that my suspicions about the frayed fates proved correct. Each location had a connection to Ithelia.

All right, we have the payroll, the chime sequence, and the tower key. We need to reach the top of the bell tower on the west side of the fort and sound the bell chimes in the proper order.\n\nWe made it this far. I can keep going if you can.
I gave up adventuring because I was more skilled with quill and parchment than I was with sword and bow. But I'm ready to help however I can.
The Daedric power I sensed earlier is even stronger here. The Daedric shrine is near.

Ithelia speaks true. Imprisonment is not a permanent solution, as we have so recently experienced. And she is right. I made you fate's chosen for exactly this moment. To provide us with a different perspective.\n\nGo ahead. Speak with Ithelia.
My extensive training kept me alive. I wish others had that luck.
My sword tasted Balandrus's blood and we ended the Terror. Let's head outside and find Tham.
The Blind is after the Echonir? Why?

It is good to see you again, friend. Still, I have no liking for any of this. I have troubles enough in Wrothgar without new enemies ready to spill blood over old relics.\n\nI didn't even know there was a staff worth stealing in Oathsworn Pit.

Why, it's my favorite challenger! I shouldn't be surprised. Hermaeus Mora fancies himself the Gardener of Men. He, too, recognizes talent.\n\nI admit, I never gave the Echonir a second look. Perhaps it was more important than I thought.
Whoever's behind these attacks on West Weald—Daedra, Wood Elf, or Recollection fanatic—I mean to make them answer for what they've done. This land is my home, and I'll fight to protect it.

I knew you were special the moment I met you, proxy. No, you are proxy no more. You are just … my friend. We stopped Vaermina and Peryite, defeated Torvesard, saved Necrom and West Weald. But I feel there was something else. Something important.
Any raw recruit can carry messages. I'm an experienced legionary! I should be out there, fighting for the glory of count and country!

If I'm right, Nantharion is planning to set off a massive wildburn, enough to destroy Skingrad and cover the entire Weald in forest!\n\nTake a look at the Skein and you'll see the sites I'm referring to. I think they can lead us to Nantharion.
It's just like we saw at Hoperoot—the Echonir has something to show us. Go on, friend. Let's see what it reveals!
What just happened? I heard my master's voice, and then … something went away. It's right there, on the tip of my tentacle … and now it's gone!\n\nHey, how did Gadayn get back here?
Strange … I feel like I just awakened from a deep sleep and the fragments of a dream are fading like mist off the morning dew.\n\nBut is that Gadayn? I thought for sure we had lost him!
A map that shows you exactly where to find Ithelia's power? That sounds remarkably useful. Who came up with that, I wonder.\n\nGo ahead and try it, comrade. I want to see how this Skein thing works.
I thought Dawnwood was a blessing, a sign from the Green. Now … I'm not so sure.

The Skein was right—Ithelia used her power here. There was no doorway into these ruins before this one suddenly appeared. According to this legionary, Tribune Alea witnessed the whole thing and went charging in after them!

The people of Vashabar wish only to live in Dawnwood in peace. We are not invaders. We do not seek to displace the Colovians. But the Green has given us this forest and we mean to make full use of that blessed gift.
Nantharion got away, damn it. Shardmarshal Vargas, too. At least we stopped them from using this wildburn seed at Skingrad.\n\nTalk to Beragon, will you? I'm afraid he's taking this pretty hard.
Go on ahead. I'll catch up to you and Tribune Alea just as soon as I see to these injured legionaries.
Nantharion and Ithelia are at the well, and Beragon is going after them! We need to get in there and help him, comrade. Use Abolisher and open a portal!
Take a look at the Skein of Secrets. If Ithelia returned to Mirrormoor—wherever that is—then perhaps the Skein can show us how to follow her.\n\nIt's worth a try, anyway.

An ominous letter and a map with notes in code? I have some experience with that sort of thing from my days as an Imperial scribe. Pack those up and take them with you, friend. I'll see if I can puzzle out the code later.
Arkay smiles upon you, friend. Your assistance in stopping the ritual has finally put the spirits of Nonungalo to rest. You saved both the living and the dead of West Weald today.

I'm glad to see Tribune Alea, but she certainly took her sweet time! We've had all sorts of problems here!\n\nDid you bring reinforcements? Captain Leronus sent the remaining legionaries and staff into the catacombs. Then he was going to call for help.

One of these days, Tribune Alea is going to realize she's wasting me on messenger duty. I'm strong, I'm fearless, and my sword arm strikes true!\n\nI should be back in the thick of battle, not passing messages back and forth.
Proceed to Wendir, the spot marked on the Skein of Secrets. I shall meet you there and together we will discover what the Skein wants us to know.
A Daedric ritual? That's not something I get to see every day.
Mother demanded we return for the family jewels. Priceless heirlooms, she kept insisting. I begged her to let them go.\n\nWe should never have come back here.

Sorilen joined the Recollection. The group I'm actively trying to stop. Cracked acorns, that hurts!\n\nIt seems they want to take back land that once belonged to the Ayleids. If that's why they built an army, they're more dangerous than I thought.
I was afraid we'd lost Tribune Alea forever. I'm glad she had the sense to find these mirrors and wait for help!\n\nGo on, friend. The sooner we're out of this place, the better.

I believe the mirrors are a lock or activation method of some kind. They might awaken the dormant portal, if we can but determine the correct order in which to activate them.\n\nTouch them, and we will see if anything changes.

I've fought in enough battles to appreciate the chance to savor a victory, even when I know there's going to be another fight tomorrow. Enjoy this while you can, comrade. There's unfinished business ahead of us.

Beragon's an old friend. He'll appreciate my discovery. I hope you do, as well.\n\nThe ruins are to the southeast of the village. Meet me outside the entrance when you finish helping survivors. I can't wait for Beragon to see what I found.
This place is in a disarray. Do you think you … I mean we, could excavate one of these tiles? No, no, Narsis Dren does not loot. Let me instead commit them to my notes here.
My dear Narsis is always overflowing with tales of his discoveries, I find myself impatient waiting to hear about them.
Shardmarshal Vargas hopes to delay us long enough for Ithelia to finish her work with the Loom. We must defeat Vargas as quickly as we can!
What is that thing? Never mind, it wants to talk to you. Go find out what it means by we're all doomed.

This threat to reality is over because of your actions. Very unexpected that such danger would appear in a simple inn.\n\nI would like to examine the Lamp of Clarity further. It may help in our future efforts to locate Ithelia. May I have it?
If you have the ingredient we came for, then we need to go. Now.
I hope you have good news for Master Grander. This whole ordeal has had such a profound and distressing effect on the young lord.

You didn't stop the Blind here. But, my master isn't displeased.\n\nStill, you'll need to contend with the Blind in the Skyvault now. The amount of damage she could cause there is almost not worth thinking about.
Hurry! Untie my bonds before they notice you!
Deputy, I have a message for you from Constable Yabren.
I believe our interaction has concluded. Take your suspicions and go bother someone else.
I do hope you'll tell Constable Yabren that Carvain Ranch has nothing to hide.

Mirrormoor and Shardborn. Two words I never knew existed before all this. We should tell Beragon and Leramil what happened here. I expect one of them can tell us more about Abolisher. I'm headed to Skingrad. May I take the blade for them to examine?
Tell Beragon about your recent investigations, proxy. I confess I am curious as to what he makes of your report on the events at the Outcast Inn.\n\nAfterward, we must take counsel together.

Torvesard proves surprisingly resourceful. I created this gate to admit none but the mortal vessels of my allies to Apocrypha. Yet the relic of Boethiah he carries deceived my defenses.\n\nA clever ploy.
The battle out here appears to be over except for a few straggling Daedra. Are we in the clear? What did you find in the barracks? And how did you wind up emerging from a portal?
This hardly feels real. They rutting stand with us! Singer be praised!
Don't usually get overly emotional. But I'm … hmm. Why don't you talk to Laeni for a moment?
You talk to the happy couple. I'm going to try to get the village pleasantly tipsy.
I can't believe it's come to this. Are we just old fools in the eyes of the village?
It may be the jagga talking, but I think I'm beginning to see sense in what they're saying.
I failed my companions. When they needed me, I wasn't here. The Recollection has much to answer for. And so do I.
Look at them up there. I think I'm going to cry.
The garden of my heart is bursting with love. I can't believe it.
Singer be praised. To see the rite enacted after all these years.

Take these flinging pies and throw them at Chef Zee-Ram and Chef Banelle. That will teach them! Then grab the ingredients they stole—my father's special flour blend and my mix of essential sugars.\n\nI'll reward you well for helping me, traveler.

We did it! We defeated the Ceythalmor and saved Hyacinth. Side by side, what a feeling! I knew you were special. Not everyone would drop everything to assist a stranger.\n\nYou know, you'd make a great addition to the Garland Ring.
If I hadn't been injured, I'd go back in there with you and Calvo. As it is, I'd just slow you down.
Good luck in there. Well, maybe Calvo needs it more than you. Divines know he's no hero.
Please keep an eye on Calvo. He's scared out of his wits, but he's determined to go back in there anyway. I suppose that's what it means to be a legionary, but I don't think I could do it.
Step back, stranger! I am about to perform a miraculous feat of mighty spellcraft!
A tragic day for those who call Leftwheal home.
This level of destruction and twisted magics. What could have done this?
Please, I need a moment to catch my breath. This is all too much.
What were those things? I've never seen anything like them before.

Once we are through mourning, I will have plenty to say to High Cantor Viti. Sending those Inquisitors after you! If I had known she would betray my trust so, I would have told her nothing.\n\nWish me luck that I can make her see reason, walker.
Let us leave this place. I am used to walking in darkness, but I have no wish to linger.
The Molag Bal Paradox is a classic. I wanted to dig into it because I know Isayas doesn't like talking about Daedra, but I also think it's a good one to pass the time.
Speak to Agmund and hear his argument. I'll share mine. Then give us an outsider's perspective.

Interesting fact. These flowers bloom across the Dominion. From Summerset to the deserts of Elsweyr. In a way, they represent the great beauty this part of the world shares in common. United.\n\nAh, well. Into the fire with them.

Don't look so surprised, comrade! The people of the Weald know how to throw a celebration!\n\nWe did good work, but I can't imagine what would have happened without your involvement. So allow us to sing your praises. You deserve it!
The last thing I remember, friend, we were exploring an Ayleid ruin, looking for … something. To stop … hmm. The more I try to remember, the less I can recall.\n\nWhat happened to me, my friend?

No, you do not belong here. But a reflection of the Prince of Paths travels with you. Have you come to revel at my defeat? To watch Hermaeus Mora imprison me? How shameful that I attract a mocking audience.\n\nGet on with your gloating then.
Remember what I said. I know you and Tanlorin won't rest until you figure this all out. Until you determine which of our flowers is really a weed. Good luck out there.

Greetings, friend of Beragon. I have to say I don't care much for houses made from cut wood and shaped stone. Beragon has been too long away from the forest, if you ask me. \n\nAnyway, he's expecting you. You'll find him in the nearby room.

Your exploits precede you, hero. Impressive tales! And I understand we owe you a great deal.\n\nBeragon is waiting for you in the other room. Come back once you finish with our gracious host. I would like to speak with you.
I saw everyone gathered, so I assumed there must be something going on!
I've never seen anything like this place. Once the adepts get wind of what's down here, they'll be lining up to begin their studies.

I found your conversation with my Prince very interesting. A mortal walking the Many Paths? And in service of the Fatechanger? I must respect that.\n\nI hope you find what you need to help your Ithelia. Maybe you'll succeed where I have failed.

I need to figure out what to do next. Do I learn to live with this curse or find a way to cure it, like Maer did? And what about the town? Do we abandon Sutch or try to rebuild?\n\nToo many questions and not enough answers. At least Maerenah's back.

Chirrabi is in need of more brass and nickel for inlays. This one's usual supplier is still angry with her for a late night of tribute gambling.\n\nMaybe Chirrabi should have been more honest about how good she is.
Have you heard? The Vashabar ruler, King Nantharion, he's the leader of the Recollection!
It's the damn Wood Elves, mark my word! Why else would they settle on this side of the Strid?
Thank the Eight! \n\nHand me the totems. The sooner I can return them to the Goblins, the sooner this mess is over.
There is much to be done. But it will be good to flex my feathers again.
Don't believe these nasty rumors about King Nantharion. All we have to go on is the word of some city-dwelling Wood Elf and some mercenary from who knows where!
Dawnwood's sudden appearance is proof that we were meant to settle this new forest. Vashabar is only the beginning. Soon we'll have settlements throughout Dawnwood … and maybe even beyond!
I knew Nantharion was too good to be true! The bastard! The rot-infested, fungus filled, mite eating root poker!
Cowards … shooting arrows from a distance. A true warrior faces their opponent up close so they can look them in the eye!
I can sense the power of the Indrik within you. You are one step closer to unlocking the potential of the Scribing altar.
So many deaths here in Ontus. So much illness. And did you hear about the Wood Elf cultists? Their leader is a king of some sort!

A passing traveler says the Wood Elves in the new forest are evil. That their king leads a violent cult that seeks to turn the entire Weald into jungle.\n\nIf this is true, I'm ashamed to call myself Bosmer.
Please, the flowers. It's time we bring an end to this chapter of the Garland Ring.

Never fear. I can tolerate the old man long enough to figure out who betrayed us. I'll gather my notes and consult with the Gardener and Hyacinth.\n\nWe'll discover the identity of this traitor. You can count on it.
With the sigil in hand, you need merely return to the altar. You will see, you will feel its power unfold. And know that you have taken another step on the path of Scribing.

Go east and you'll find where the Daedra dug up from below. Drop down and keep going east. You'll know the portal when you see it. Break those anchors and I bet the portal closes.\n\nI'll try and lead the Recollection away and then find you down there.
You're back! And with some success, I hope? What happens when you fully restore the altar?
Color me intrigued. Just what have you and Nahlia been up to while you've been gone?
I'm just grateful I got a chance to help you out. Seeing this ancient library come to life around us?\n\nIt's so different than my normal work. And far more fulfilling.
Good to see that many, uh, flowers, in one place. That Gardener, he's an odd old man. Maybe when the Altmer get on in years they get more and more whimisical? \n\nEr, don't tell anyone I said that.
I recognize Pim, but who are you? Are you one of those hunters? No, I don't think so. Pim wouldn't stand within ten feet of you.\n\nIt doesn't matter. Can I see that knife now?
Listen, I climbed plenty of trees back home, and I'm nothing if not committed. Let's not talk about it.\n\nDid you find Ulfsild's notes?
Thank you for helping me save those I could. Any life lost is my own doing. Valenia … Naku … the rest of the Scarlets.\n\nI have to take responsibility for who I used to be.

Valenia's family will want her body back. I believe Hooke plans to take her to Marbruk. I'll go too, and say a few words when we lay her to rest there.\n\nAnd that may be the last time I speak to the Divines.
I'm worried about Hooke. Him and Val, they were always close. Even all the way back when we were legionaries in good standing.\n\nGods, what a mess.
Marcien's been helping me settle in since I arrived. It doesn't feel right without them here.\n\nWho knows what trouble they might have run into? I hate thinking about it. Please, find them for me.

I can't believe I'm here. I was only out of sight of Fallen-Knives and Big Urm for a moment when Caelum grabbed me and dragged me into a hole. The tunnels were dark, but he knew his way.\n\nI was sure I was done for. Then you and Hooke showed up.
That was a harrowing fight, I am sure. I only wish I could have been here.

Well done getting the arcane knot out of there before things could go poorly. Good timing is either a matter of skill or luck. But Keshargo thinks you have the former. \n\nStill, he'll breathe easier knowing the knot is stabilized.
Valaria sent you, right?\n\nWhy did she tell you to talk to me? It must have been for something interesting. She knows how I feel about inane interruptions.

You stopped! Good. I need help. Well, my expedition needs help. \n\nWe were trying to recover an artifact from the Lucent Citadel, but we were attacked. I don't know who else survived. I just ran through a portal and wound up here.
Ulrath deserted the Legion? Did I hear that right?
Careful. I've lost a lot of comrades today, so I'm not in a trusting mood. Who are you and what do you want?
Their technique was a bit sloppy, but it's good to have seen a rite like that used again. How nice.
Mercenary, Tribune Alea requests your presence. Immediately, if not sooner, I might add.
Inisez knows what you are thinking. You see an old cat without two coins to rub together. \n\nAnd you'd be right.
A word of advice. If your friend is carrying valuables, he should keep a claw closer to his belt-strap. Unless those strange eyes of his also see out the back of his head.
It seems we have you and your friend to thank for our salvation. \n\nAlthough, and we hope this isn't rude. But who in Oblivion are you ?
If you're looking for inspiration, search the many libraries within the Scholarium. \n\nSomewhere Ulfsild must have left behind notes about how she approached the Dragon's task.
I have been sitting here mulling what morsel you might lay at my feet, mortal. \n\nI honestly hope I am not disappointed. Out with it. What is your riddle?
I can't imagine a more embarrassing way to die than being trapped in my own net, pecked to death by guzzards. I didn't think anyone would find me out here. What brings you to these parts?
The ink does not yet flow. I assume you are still working to complete the Netch's trial?
Creating portals from afar like that really pushed my understanding of portal magic, and what I thought I knew.\n\nI get the feeling that was part of the point? The Netch certainly is tricksy.
Did you come to see who I'm going to trick next? My tendrils are already in motion, already reaching out.
I'm tempted to follow you into those portals, but I need to stay with my father.
Do what you must. I'll watch over my husband and make sure he doesn't go running after you.

My final venture as a man of the sword.\n\nI resigned my station and took to mercenary work. I had tracked a bounty to these ruins, filled with traps and monsters. I was lost. Injured. I fell and my torch went out. I was alone. So alone.
Your dedication to restoring the Scholarium fills me with pride. \n\nThe Gryphon is a … complicated figure. I hope he treats you well.
Look at these constructs! The Archmagister himself will be jealous, if we can ever get him down here. Hah!
You performed a great service for West Weald today, traveler! Without Sir Svendalmor of the Burnt-Biscuits at my side, Skingrad would fall apart!
What have you found?
Zerith's ritual, it was so beautiful! And I can still feel his words, resonating with Moon-Singer Talbira's song.\n\nI have much to think about, walker.

Eifa. It is really her. Radiant. Healed. Forgiven. Zerith-var is … remarkable!\n\nThis one apologizes for acting as she did against you. Viti thought all cats that fell to the Bent Dance were lost forever. That is all this one has ever known.
This is awful. She's not just my vanity, she's my rage.
If only I had the energy to drown myself. I can't even do that.
The altar won't do … you know, more altar things, unless you go imbue the Gryphon's power into the altar.\n\nThat's outside. In the main hall. Go!
Well, hello there, gorgeous. You fancy a drink?
The ritual is complete. The Scholarium is safe. And you are a shield for Ulfsild's legacy, just as much as I am.
I thought perhaps we could finally return home. But not anymore. Ostumir is cursed.
Don't make me regret this.
I don't care who you are, I demand justice for my wife!
You know what? I think maybe, just maybe, my parents might be impressed with me next time I go home to visit.
I hope I … I hope Ulfsild left something of herself behind, where you're going.
The darkness that Zerith held fast to … I feel it fading. Like night giving way to the light of dawn.
I think this is it, my friend. Get ready. Who knows what the Crow has in store for you.
It's you! Hi! It's me! When the Gryphon told me you'd entered the Crow's wing I knew you needed me. \n\nAfter all, Ulfsild told me you would! I'm supposed to help you get past this next bit.
Watch your back in there. Those creatures are faster than they look.
You've come to support us? Very well. Go on through the front gates and may the Divines be with you.
I overheard you talking with the baroness. Be careful in there. I appreciate what you're doing, but we won't be able to save you if things get worse.
You're going in there yourself? For the sake of all we've lost, I pray this city must not lose more.
Damn Wood Elf won't tell us a thing! If the captain let's me, I can make her talk!
Strange times here in the Weald. Makes me glad that I'm part of the Legion. I can't imagine trying to deal with these headaches on my own.
Come on, friend! Ithelia is already in the Loom. We must get past Shardmarshal Vargas before it's too late!
Attack, comrade! We can defeat the shardmarshal together!
Shardmarshal Vargas hopes to delay us long enough for Ithelia to finish her work with the Loom. We must defeat Vargas as quickly as we can!
You probably want to speak to Orissa. The sooner you settle your business, the sooner we can put this buzzing nightmare behind us.
The innkeeper still serves ale and the fire's still warm. That's what matters.
People come to an inn for privacy, not to meet people!
Everything is fine when you have a lute!
Finally, some peace and quiet around here.
The Innkeeper has me busting my bones cleaning this place up!
These are the offices of the Carvain Ranch, not a public house or waystation. If you have business here, get on with it. If you don't get out.
If you have business here, get to it. Just be aware—I'm watching you.
Those Daedra came out of nowhere!

I just curled up under a tree for a nap when the quake hit. I slept through most of it until I heard the screaming. That's when Beragon pulled me to my feet. Good thing, too. A huge branch fell right where I had been sleeping just a moment before.
I'm pretty sure my leg is broken. Beragon pulled me out from under a rock. He's a good sort, for a Wood Elf. Maybe you can help him.

Things have gotten strange in Skywatch recently. I heard bizarre noises from beyond the barrier in the ruins. And there have been suspicious types hanging out by the frog races. Mark my words, something terrible is brewing.
Feldagard Keep won't fall to these Daedra!
The Legion never backs down from a fight.
Why are Daedra attacking us? What did we do to them?
If I see a Daedra, I'll run it through!
When the Daedra first breached the wall, I thought we were done for.
A traitor in our midst? Someone I trust working against us? I'm not sure what to think.\n\nIt's all too much, my friend. I feel … lost.
I feel hollow. Like she took a part of me with her. In a way, I suppose she did. \n\nWhat am I going to do? Wisteria taught me everything I know.
Oleander. Snapdragon. Gladiolus. Even you, Wisteria. I'll never forget you. Any of you.
I bet you didn't expect all this excitement after you got me out of that trap. I'm so glad it was you. \n\nI swear, I was this close to calling over a deer to try to lick me out of that ice.
This doesn't make sense. You radiate the primal fear of Detritus, but it hasn't driven you mad?\n\nWait, what happened with the Haunted?
The flames are growing! If they touch me, I'll die! You'll see!
Leave me. I've failed everyone. I must prepare myself to meet my ancestors.
The spirit of Moon-Singer Talbira, reborn into Cantor Krin'ze? Returned to this plane just as I was? As Ravith-morna was?\n\nAzurah's purpose for me becomes more clear. And yet more fraught as well.

It is finished. The Rajaska stalk the face of Nirni no more.\n\nIn my last moments connected to Ravith, I felt her relief. The door between us closed forever, but there was no fear. Not like before. The ties that bound us, we were both ready to let go.

My great misdeed, finally pulled from the shadow and cast into the light of day. Moon-Singer Talbira, my friend, my partner. She asked me to strike down Ravith-morna. But I had not the strength to do it.\n\nSo I turned my blade on Talbira instead.
Azurah heard my prayers and sent you here, thank the moons!\n\nTwilight Cantors from every corner of Elsweyr are holding off dark spirits as best they can. We can definitely use your help.
He said I'll never be clean. The blood covers me, seeps down my throat until I choke. In Detritus, he showed me the truth of what I'll become. Why won't the blood come off?
Oh, good to see you, friend! I mean it when I say I haven't put my quill down ever since you brought me that bundle of remnants! Speaking of, I think I might be ready for another one.
This trouble, it is all the outsider and the necromancer's fault! Leave us!

I don't like being watched, magically or not. The Albuses know we're here by now, but who ever is behind this is learning about us. They're getting an unfair advantage. \n\nStill, there's only one way to go. After you.
He can use the death of his son as an excuse, but plenty of parents feel grief. None of them kidnap and kill other people's sons and daughters!
If I could fight, I'd show that tracker what eternal darkness looks like. Sometimes I wish I had my vision!\n\nWell, I'm not going to stand idly while you fight. Garvin won't escape us.
You did it? It's over?\n\nIt's hard to feel excited knowing what this victory cost. But still, we are grateful. I hope that you know that.
Moon-Singer Talbira, I saw her spirit and then ….\n\nThe pain. I did not imagine it, did I? Her spirit … collided with mine?
< The scamp glances up from arranging her wares before returning to her work.>
Is this how you treat your betters? The ones who will shape the future and bring it to pass? Without me the alliances will be unpunished. \n\nWe will have justice in Cyrodiil!
I can lead this group to safety. May the Mother of Twilight guide your path, walker.
Once these two have readied themselves, we'll make for safety. My thanks to you, walker.
This one must collect herself so we may flee to safety. Thank you, five-claw, for your help.
I knew Vanus would find a way to crash the party. He just loves being the center of attention!

Order of the Black Worm. Sounds powerful, right? I thought belonging to the group would make me strong. Now, look at me.\n\nI plan to disappear. Go somewhere no one will never find me. I'm done with necromancy, Daedra, war—all of it!

Let me guess. You and your sweaty, tattooed friend are here regarding a locked coffer in our care?\n\nIt's not often our clients include detailed descriptions of their beneficiaries. And I must admit, she was spot on.
Go on. He wants to talk to you.

It's Skordo's blade, all right. I'd know his tough, stubborn aura anywhere, and the sword reeks of it.\n\nHe wouldn't have parted with his weapon. Not unless he had no choice. Our task now shifts from gathering information to rescuing Skordo the Knife.
Skordo said there's a Worm Cult base somewhere around here. I'm ready to fight as soon as we find a way in.
If there's a Worm Cult nest here, we will find it. This one never gives up.

I don't understand why the gryphons would just fly away. Unfortunately, there's no time to ponder. Perhaps the gryphons longed for the sky. \n\nThe main gate is gone, but we can still journey to the upper monastery.
That's the great Vanus Galerion? I thought that he'd be taller.

Shando-ri really believes Arum-Khal is beyond his reach? Hrrm. \n\nI have my doubts that an implement of Azurah can be used to destroy the spirits of her children. Use the Moonlight Blade as your are instructed. Azurah will not lead us astray.
An arcane projection? Vanus Galerion truly is a powerful mage!
Vanus Galerion? I thought you said he had been captured? Well, let's hear what he has to say.
My home is burning. My family is injured or dead. Everything I know is in ruins. Forgive me if I don't have the concentration to show manners.
So many dead in our streets. We don't have the space to send them to the Far Shores properly. \n\nThis sadness is stronger than the tide.
Whatever loss or pain Orpheon's army of deserters suffered, it was not enough. They should be punished by all the ills the world has on offer.
Orpheon and his army never learned restraint. This is not how you win allies or friends.
I don't know how they found us. We stayed hidden for so long. Only the Moth Priests knew where we were and what we protected. I hope they're not compromised.
I normally pride myself on punctuality. No excuses for lateness is my motto. How hypocritical of me to show up late to the Mages Guild meeting.
Who knew the Worm Cult still existed?
Never would have believed we'd be attacked here in the Earth Forge. And by the Worm Cult no less!
Vanus still lives? Excellent news indeed! Talk to him and let us see what message he conveys.
That was so insulting. Julien is clearly not suitable material for a woman of my station.
It seems I am doomed to admire Guen from afar. \n\nPerhaps after a few years of experience in the High King's army, she will reconsider and give me a chance.
I'm glad the matter we discussed has been, er, dealt with. \n\nRest assured, the Duke of Camlorn does not forget his friends.
At least now we know what we're facing. \n\nMeanwhile, Gloria has discovered something important about how Faolchu came to power.

This whole thing was like some terrible nightmare. It reminds me of the day I lost my husband so many years ago.\n\nI don't know if you can understand. I've moved on, but sometimes, I still feel a little lonely.

As much as I want to rush out and put <<1>>'s head on a pike, I have a responsibility to these people.\n\nJonah is a strange one, but I doubt he can fend for himself, let alone protect his mother. I hope you can find them quickly.

I dread the prospect of having to do battle with my fellow knights. \n\nNonetheless, it must be done. I've ordered the knights who have joined our cause to take up strategic positions around the keep.
Verandis trusts you. Hopefully, you now see that not all vampires are evil.

If you've come to poke fun at the prisoner, you'd better think twice. I'll be out of these stocks soon, and then you'll have to watch your back.\n\nThey may not have enough evidence to hold me, but that doesn't mean I'm not a dangerous criminal.
Did you see her? Wearing the necklace I made? Well, I hope you're happy. This is all your fault.\n\nNow go away and let me work in peace.
Go as fast as you can, Lieutenant. Until we've tried this, the king won't even talk about surrender.\n\nWe have to get him to come around before it's too late.

Oh no! It's you. Have you come from Hosni? Please. Please have mercy.  \n\nS'rashi promises to have Hosni's gold soon, but S'rashi cannot get Hosni's gold if he's dead. Tell S'rashi you've not come to kill him.
You. You're to go right in.
If I see you, I'm supposed to send you in. So I'm sending you in.
Whoever did this to Mathias needs to pay. Hope you figure out who it was. I bet it was that creepy Altmer, Yarelion. \n\nI suppose it could have been any of the suitors though.
Go on into the tower and talk to the Hinaults. Reassure them. They're both pretty shaken up.\n\nBut if Heloise doesn't return soon, I may need to send you out to find her.
I'm not sure I can stand much more of this. The bodies … the blood ….\n\nI wanted to save this family, but look what happened. It feels like everything has suddenly gone wrong.

If I could trade my life to bring back my dear Lakana, I would. Moving on will not be easy, but I must honor her sacrifice by doing all that I can to protect the Covenant.\n\nI will speak with King Fahara'jad. Perhaps we can come together in mourning.
If Alcaire is truly threatened, regardless of where it comes from, I will defend it to the death.
If Alcaire falls, what's next, Wayrest? If these Redguards mean to invade, we have to stop them here.

If you don't mind, please apologize to Mathias for me as well. Tell him I would have him and all the other servants return if they're willing. \n\nNo more suitors though. I'm done pretending. I have no intention of marrying again—certainly not now.

Killing my fellow knights to restore order was hard enough, but this matter with Sir Hughes is unthinkable.\n\nHe's down in the infirmary. I'm told he was raving about killing the duchess before he fell unconscious. I-I don't know what to do.
You have bathed my sword in vengeance.\n\nTake it now down to the fissure. Destroy the evil Fallen Three.
I read stories to all the children in the village here once every week.\n\nYou're always welcome to join us, dear. One is never too old to be a child again.
"Arkay's Beard" or "Eyes of Akatosh?" Hmm. Arkay sounds right, but Akatosh would be more sensible.
So he didn't turn into a chicken? Too bad.
Don't be shy. Go light those fires!\n\nThis is going to be fun.
It was a boon from Baan Dar that you happened along. \n\nWas it Janne who asked you to help Dro-Dara and the others?
Now there's a sight for some sore old eyes. I missed this stuff.\n\nYou've done me a great favor by getting it back.
I am safe here. The bandits fear the crocodiles—and wisely so.
My wife, Breloth, is dead. Mara take her soul. \n\nShe was the only good thing I ever knew in this world, and now I can't even give her a decent burial.
Steel and stone! Welcome to the Scarp! \n\nWe could use your help on the battlefield. Would you join us in the fight for glory?

You shattered the gems? I wish I could say I've been as successful. The temple entrance is sealed by magic.\n\nWe must find a way in here. There's something in there. Something is calling me. You must think I'm crazy!
It's just those three support beams. Be prepared to run though. That place will come down fast.\n\nI'll be here, hoping the ogres don't see me.
We're ready and waiting to move up to that tower. Are you going help us or not?
Welcome to Shinji's Scarp. \n\nOnce a quiet little village at the foot of the mountains—now the front line in the battle with the Ironhand Ogres.
Somehow I sense that getting rid of the sword will bring us rest. \n\nI pray that it is so.

Now that's incredible! Azura sent you, didn't she?

Here I am, down on my knees, begging Azura for help, and you walk up. If that's not divine intervention, I don't know what is.

You are going to help me, right?
Thank you again for freeing my husband. \n\nDreughside's already returning to normal.
Before we return to the abbey, Hakam and I need to figure out which crops have survived.
I don't understand how this could be happening … we have no feud with the Midnight Union!\n\nWhy would they suddenly attack the Abbey? It doesn't make any sense.
Without you, I'd still be trapped in that dream.\n\nNow we must work together to stop this threat to Stormhaven.
You saved Abbot Durak. You recovered the Dream Shard. \n\nThere are no words.
Goblins must die. All of them.
How fares the task?\n\nIf my father resists, you may press the issue. Pain is a wonderful motivator, and really, I've been very patient.

Don't be a stranger now, my friend. We need more people like you hanging about here in the castle. It makes the place more interesting. \n\nThough I suppose if you hung about here, you'd be pretty boring, wouldn't you? Safe travels, then.
You won't get another coin from me. Off with you now!
You have the focusing crystals? Great! Place them in their fixtures and we can relight the signal fire.

Talk about perfect timing. Elvira's got a damn good plan, and now that you're here, we might actually pull it off.\n\nFight like you did at the lighthouse and we'll have the rest of the crew free in no time.
Each night as I fall asleep I will think of what you did and the sounds they will make as they choke to death on poisoned wine.
You there! If you respect the name of the Knights of the Flame then I would ask your assistance.\n\nBandits are masquerading as members of our order and then robbing people blind!
If only more people were aware of the Goblins' rich cultural heritage, perhaps they wouldn't be so persecuted.\n\nPlus, the females are kind of cute. In a way.
They've tied me up! I think they're going to give me to some Daedra!

Traitor! I can't believe I thought you would help us. It is clear that you've given over to the same greed and brutality as those Primeval Seekers. \n\nBut why would you dare enter my personal chambers?
It is done. The last spriggan is dead. It is good that we eased her passing ….\n\nNow, though, she must be avenged. She, and all her sisters.
Between you and me, I'm incredibly relieved that Emeric's here, but it took him so long, I don't know whether to kiss him or slap him.
<<1>> will help, for the good of us all.\n\nBut I understand her fear. We must be cautious on her watch. If anyone suspected her involvement, that would mean her end.
May I get you a drink, my lord? Perhaps a tune on the lute? \n\nI've been told my fingers are quite gifted.

The talk of men grates upon my ears. Always comparing swords. One-hand grip, two-handed grip … it's all the same to me.\n\nNow if you could show me a beautifully filigreed sheath, that would be a different matter entirely.
What is your decision? We must proceed—one way or another.
I heard everything, and I saw Baron Sorick flee. \n\nIt isn't right. I'm going to make sure the baron lives to stand trial.
I know selling the johads makes the most sense for us.\n\nMy family did not trust my decisions, and so neither did I. But now, I see events clearly. My sister and I will find our happiness elsewhere.

Welcome to Sentinel, wayfarer. If you've come about the docks, rest assured, I already know. \n\nI regret that you visit during such times, but perhaps your arrival is fortuitous. Perhaps the gods guided you here to help us fight the Withered Hand.
Roheebah seems to be feeling better already. At least we have that to be thankful for.

Finally my father stops chasing the mirage! I advised him to listen to Ash'abah weeks ago, but better late than never, yes? Please, speak with Marimah, while I reach out to my Ash'abah contacts. \n\nWe will find a way to stop the Withered Hand.
Before you speak, stranger, know this: for centuries, a spell has bound me. Many have tried to free me and failed. \n\nThis prison has no lock or bonds to break.

Hey—I know you! We broke into Cath Bedraud together, killed that crazy old necromancer, Angrad, er … Angolf …. What was his name again?\n\nI guess it doesn't matter now that he's dead. Ha! Good to see you!
I am very proud. Tu'whacca says that you smote this Uwafa mightily! \n\nYou recovered the Ward of Ansei Radan as well! The Temple is restored, and Alik'r is safer! Tu'whacca is pleased.
Unishi's business in Sentinel is done. Time for this one to move on, she thinks.

There are many heroes buried here, to be sure, but these three are the ones Ash'abah scholars are most concerned about. \n\nThey were extremely powerful in life, and scholars fear they could be extremely dangerous in death.
Tu'whacca give me strength! These mine doors must not open ever again. I'll be a poor man, but at least no more souls will fall into this deathtrap!
Whatever they are planning, they must be stopped. That much is certain.

After so many centuries, it is a wonder I can still be surprised. I could not abide the necromancer corrupting my ward, but I was powerless to stop him. \n\nYour actions have shattered the blade—but you made the right choice. You have my gratitude.

True love! Ah, it warms my silent heart. They will be happy for the rest of their mortal lives.\n\nAnd do not worry. It will be a full and healthy lifetime in my nest. Such prizes like these are not to be wasted!

Greetings to you, student. What knowledge do you seek? A strategy to slay your opponents? The strength to protect your allies? The power to split a kingdom in two?\n\nThese things you may do, and have done already. But these are not the arts I teach.
Had the choice been mine … but no, it is done. Speak to me no more.
Excellent! <<1>> will be eager to speak with you.
Even with your experience, until you have spoken to <<1>>, no master of blades will teach you.\n\nIt is our tradition. You will find we hold many such traditions here.
You thought as the disciple did, though it appears the old master does not appreciate her freedom.
Sharing the evidence you discovered at Fakimal's house, I was able to convince the other bailiffs to release me from the stocks. \n\nTell me though, what did you learn at the Magistrate's house?

Let me know when you are ready to go. We will need to find the various points of power in the area.\n\nI will accompany you and aid as best I can through this projection. If something should happen, I will meet you back here.

The swords of Yokuda were not often sheathed. Our long siege of Orsinium taught us the value of patience.\n\nNow you must face the forces of the Breton King Joile—a treacherous asp whose lust for power led to broken alliances and countless sorrows.

I welcome you to Bergama, wayfarer. I hope you brought your gold. Our markets have goods of the finest quality, things you can find nowhere else.\n\nRegardless of any rumors, I assure you the city is safe. So stay as long as you like.
I've stayed still, trying not to attract attention from these spiders.\n\nWe can't leave without <<1>>. She may be trapped too. I'll fight my fear to rescue her! With … your help.
Now that we have the jewels to ransom and puffball caps for the sleep potion, we can execute my plan.
Is it done? Has the totem been returned to the Goblins?
Quick! Lady Miranda's in the manor house. Get the antidote to her before it's too late.
How could you do that? How could you kill him?\n\nJust go. Go kill that Daedra. That was his last wish.
Thank you for not leaving me with this mob. I wouldn't have lasted long.
Baron Sorick is going to regret what he did to us. \n\nWe'll make certain of that.
And so it ends. \n\nI believe I will use you as an example in a parable, to explain true courage to novices. Yes, I believe I will.
You're new to Wayrest. Welcome. Even if you're just passing through, your safety's important to us.\n\nIf you have any troubles, you just let me know and I'll take care of it.
It's good that you've come along, friend. The Vanne family is in dire need of aid.\n\nIf you could untie me, we could have a more civil conversation?
Don't worry about me, I'll be fine. Just close those conjuration boxes. \n\nI'll be waiting for you at Tabakah's camp.

Praise Akatosh! You'd be amazed how many people just walk by a fellow in dire circumstances.\n\nMy sister and I were visiting our aunt's farm when the whole place went to Oblivion in an oat basket! Crazy cultists and Daedra are killing everyone!
Follow the path down to their camp by the dock. \n\nThe Supernals arrived by boat—search there first.
Is that it? Is that the sword?\n\nDid you get it reforged?
You can learn so much about a person by simply studying their face.\n\nThe same is true of yourself. I can see now so many things I've refused to acknowledge about myself.
I hear you are that crazy runecrafter's novice. \n\nJust you keep her away from me, do you hear?

What in Oblivion just happened? Something changed. It's going to be bad, isn't it? It always is. I don't know why I bother asking.\n\nStill. I seem to remember you, but … this is just another trick, isn't it?

Now that you have a king's writ you should study your profession under your new master. It will be hard, no doubt about it. Stick to it and you might mean the difference between success and defeat in Cyrodiil!
Go away! There's no one in here!
Pardon me, but have you seen the countess? \n\nShe's usually bustling all over the town, but I haven't seen her in days. Perhaps someone should check on her.
I trust you've earned the duchess's confidence by now. That's good.\n\nHave you been able to learn why she was conspiring with her father?
I hope Dame Falhut was acting alone in this. \n\nIf there is a wider conspiracy, I fear for what that might mean for our future.

I certainly hope I'm not asking too much of you. I am, of course, in your debt. 

I just can't ignore the fact that you might be able to set matters straight up there at the castle. 

Wherever you go, I wish you safe travels.
So Dame Dabienne isn't the only one working with the slavers?\n\nThis doesn't make any sense.
The captain still refuses to leave?\n\nAll right then, we'll do this the hard way. I'll call together the rest of the guard.
The hatch is unbarred, and you may go belowdecks. The ledger is on my desk.\n\nI'm uncertain how many slavers we trapped down there, but be prepared. They will not be happy to see you.

To think I shared a bed with that woman and she nearly killed me … I suppose she may have been under the influence of that crazy cultist, Sentulus.\n\nThat reminds me. I hate to ask anything else of you, but I think there may still be some danger.
Pascal's home isn't usually locked. You should be able to go right in.
Still no sign of my son?\n\nWhat if … oh, I can't even think about it.
You are an unnaturally incredible hero among heroes. You saved my dad!\n\nI feel like I should be sad because of my mother, but I just can't help it. I'm so so so happy. Thanks to you.

What are you doing? Can't you see that I'm spying on the slavers?

I think they're planning another attack on the village, but I need to know their strategy.

Go on now. I don't want to be rescued.
So Lucas just up and wandered off again? Boy's head is as thick as stone. If he went and got himself captured by those slavers ….\n\nI hate to say it, but I told him so.
Whatever you do, don't hesitate. \n\nIf you get out there and start doubting yourself, we'll be scraping you off the bottom of a rock.
These bootless louts have climbed into their own crypt.\n\nThere's no way out of this warehouse except through me, and that's not going to happen.
Back so soon? Had second thoughts?\n\nMaybe you're smarter than you look.
Would you care for some refreshment before the next fight?\n\nAt Hammerdeath, we sate all sorts of appetites.
I see Count Hosni's taken notice of you.\n\nYou look like you could show us a trick or two in the arena.
Lerineaux's manor is a short walk from here.
There's no time to waste. The life of our King is at stake!
That ward will buy us some time. Now we have to figure out what to do next.
I know this looks like a terrible way to earn a living, but it has its own rewards.
I'm not sure I thanked you properly for your help against those Bloodthorns. \n\nWhen all this werewolf trouble has ended, remind me again and I'm sure I'll think of some way to reward you.
I assumed that horn was a signal when I saw the nobles run out. Good thinking.

Look for the roots of the Wyrd around the mill.\n\nRemember that those creatures must give up their lives near the roots or the roots won't absorb their life essences. Any creature you kill away from a root is a life extinguished for no reason.
The Duke was infected? I was afraid of that, but I hoped I was wrong. \n\nI've been keeping an eye on him in case … the change came over him.

I was deeply saddened to hear of my sister's death. In Alik'r, her murderer would have been put to the sword immediately.\n\nI wonder, though, if the custom here is more civilized. If the man was insane, perhaps he does not deserve to die.
So the Duke of Camlorn is dead. \n\nRestoring his city won't be easy now.
Hmm, you're here. Don't see that Gloria woman with you, though. I suppose she had other business to attend to.
My sister and the other women made it here. Everyone's a bit rattled and tired, but otherwise they don't seem hurt.

The generals of the Alessian army played a vital part in the Battle of the Glenumbra Moors. Their weapons, if still intact, would suffice, I think.\n\nIf you manage to get your hands on the weapons, find Sarvith. He knows what to do from there.
Try not to judge the Daggers on what you've seen so far. We're a good group and we mean well.\n\nNow, enough talking. Let's go hit something!
Everything's happened so quickly. Father … the johads … I can hardly take it in!
When Gelvin gets like this, it makes the rest of us extremely nervous.
We're not warriors. We're just simple townsfolk. We're lucky you came along.
The balance has shifted. The shadows and darkness of Mother Murk fade away. The power of the wyrd rises.\n\nThanks to you.
A great peace has fallen on Westtry.\n\nIf only my heart could feel the same.
