Who's there? Stay back. Wait. Is that you, Captain Rosalind?
It's all right, Captain. I'll rally the guards and we'll make a stand at the inn. \n\nSee to Leon.
What are you doing standing around here? You think I broke the seals just for fun …? Well, it was fun, but I broke them so that you could go in.\n\nSo go in!

If we are too late, the implications are unthinkable … for all of Alik'r.\n\nI've prayed to Tu'whacca, Stendarr, and even Akatosh. Though I do not hold them sacred, I will pray to the Yokudan gods as well. Just in case.
I'd wish you luck, but I don't have any to spare.
Knock the stuffing out of those hags.
Julianos's little teapot! We did it!\n\nI think.
My best knight will meet you inside. We'll save Alana, don't you worry. \n\nGood luck, Captain.
I know you wanted to go after Faolchu, but you'll see plenty of action defending the camp.
Strange. I came out here for something, but now I can't remember what. Whatever it was, it's not worth going through those spiders!\n\nWhy are you looking at me like that?
That poor spriggan spirit is finally free. It is a lurcher no more. \n\nThrough its blood, we have cleansed this site. Everything is ready.
Have we your leave to depart?
The camp is ours again. I've never seen anyone fight like you. It was … inspirational.\n\nDid you reach General Mandin?

If you can restore our relics, perhaps my faith will return, and we can restore the temple.\n\nThere are three relics missing—they represent body, mind, and spirit—the Sword of Shabnam, Majeel's Scroll, and the Lamp of the Satakalaam.
We'll wait for your signal and then make our way out. What fun!
Please excuse my husband. He gets so enthusiastic.
I hope Wizard Benele knows what she's doing.
This is it. All our work has led to this.
I'm sick of the stench of fur and blood. I want this to be over.
Alinon knows what to do with those ingredients. And he knows what to do with the blood you're going to collect.\n\nGo quickly, before it's too late!
Make your way to the house the Bloodthorn have been using. I'll collect some things and meet you there.
We lost more troops in that charge than I expected.\n\nThe courtyard is ours, but if we don't push forward we'll be overrun again.

I am so happy, I could walk on water. I hear that is how they say it in Sentinel. Casnar and I have talked about moving there, you know. \n\nWhether here or there, we are going to name our first child after you.
I have to admit, when Uncle Thakh's thugs came to the door, I thought they were going to kill me.\n\nOne thing I know—we will certainly be able to look back at our wedding day and laugh.
Ah, the lovely clank of armor. Well done. When we get out of here, the first drink's on me. \n\nNow, I have some good news and some bad news.
Not here. Place my stone near the entrance to the Wyrd Tree.
Bloodthorn cultists made a mad dash up the road. We cut down a number of them. They clearly weren't expecting to run into us.\n\nI assume you had something to do with that?
Good to see you looking healthy and light on your feet, walker. Did your deliveries go smoothly?\n\nIldani takes your presence here as a good sign.
Find a way to get into the inn so I can make the antidote. \n\nMy cure may be the only way to truly save this city.
I just want to build traps and gadgets. But if the Daggers fold up, I don't know what I'll do to make a living.

You're welcome to Evermore, stranger. You look like someone who's seen your share of battle, and in a time like this, that makes you a valuable commodity.\n\nYou should speak with Guard Captain Hjurrun. He could use your help.
You made it. Well done.\n\nDid you get the crown?
My beautiful city. \n\nAh, you miserable beasts. By Stendarr, I won't tolerate this abomination.
You see what's happened to Camlorn?\n\nIf not for you, that would have been the fate of Aldcroft.
You've come to the tomb for treasure, of course. Everyone does.

I'm out of my depth here. If it comes to blows, I can't raise my sword against Prince Adrien, but I can't stand by and watch him strike down an unarmed priest either!\n\nThis is starting to look like not such a miracle after all.

You just missed it. The ship's captain left the ship and headed toward that alley to the south. She looked like she was in a hurry.\n\nWhat did you find though? Anything that reveals more about their plans?
Arrogant Elves! They have so much faith in that seal they put on the main door, they don't even have anyone guarding the portal!\n\nI'm not complaining though. Are you ready to do this?
I just keep asking myself, why in Oblivion would you help Stibbons?\n\nI have to believe that you were motivated by some deluded sense of pity. I feel sorry … for both of you.
I can't believe all you brought me was a dusty old book.

I didn't know Gloria was involved in all this. She does make wading through werewolves look pretty good, though, don't you think?\n\nMaybe she and I can get together later. Share a bottle of wine. Find a quiet corner where we can … compare notes.
Truly the gods smile upon me to return you to my path. This is the second time that you have rendered your aid to me.
You … don't I know you? It's so dark in here, and I'm simply too tired to think.\n\nAlas, the world might be denied my brilliance!
He'll be at the standing stones by Viridian Lake. His power is strongest there.\n\nLook for the broken statue. It overlooks the altar where he works.
You know, an army of undead can't even be killed …. We're going to be unstoppable!
The roots run deep through the wood. We hear all that transpires within it, whether for good or ill.
Ah, I was hoping you'd return before … I couldn't speak to you one last time.\n\nIt's good Elara's not with you. I'd hate for her to see me in such a state.
<Medya's death, much like Sir Etienne's, seems to have been quick.>
I can't wait to take these to Lady Laurent. She's going to be so pleased with me.\n\nI am heavily in your debt, and I won't forget it.
The wyrd have stalled long enough. Stenwick isn't healthy, and we must do what he asked before it's too late.\n\nGo to him, tell him what we've done. I'm short of breath and must save my strength.
Well, now, wasn't that fun? I'd fight alongside you anytime.
How many innocent people died in those mines? The Red Rooks must pay!
When you find my soldiers, tell them to get back here as quickly as possible. \n\nWe need to regroup for when an opportunity to strike presents itself.
Finally, someone stood up to those bandits. The townsfolk you saved are all determined to fight the Red Rooks now. \n\nThe resistance grows, my friend.
The Pearl is the Way and the Guide.\n\nIt is the light to the Far Shores and back again, as they are placed by Tall Papa's hand.
You've talked to <<1>> in Lainlyn? Then what are you doing here? \n\nWe can't risk an alliance between the Withered Hand and those mercenaries.
Report! \n\nHave you stopped the Withered Hand from recruiting the Saltwalker Company?
That takes care of the mist, but who knows for how long? Let's not waste this opportunity.\n\nThe time to strike at Angof has arrived.
Go! Run! Why are you talking to me?\n\nFate does not sit idly by, and neither should you.
Maybe I'll go back out on the road. Darien and I used to get ourselves into a lot of trouble. I've sort of missed it.
I'll make sure he gets all the food and ale he wants.\n\nI hope he can get over his distaste for warm ale, though. We're on the edge of the desert, for Julianos' sake!
I can't stand to speak to her. Make sure she understands what's going to happen.
What will happen to Draven now? I don't understand any of this.
You can speak to him now. I'm not … feeling very well all of a sudden.
Don't take this the wrong way, because it's nice to see a friendly face, but what in Sheor's name are you doing down here?
Coward. You enjoyed that, didn't you? You like hurting things?\n\nYou're no better than the average Imperial noble.
Sit back and enjoy the race!\n\nIf you picked me a winner, I'll give you a good price for it.
Looks like things are finally happening. We're going to take the town back.
What?
<The dog motions to follow.>
Did you enter you lizard? Let's watch the race. I hope it's a close one!

One cannot be a great ruler without first being an impeccable judge of character. You walked into my palace a stranger, but I trusted you immediately.\n\nYou have proven that my faith was well-placed.
Shh! You'll scare the beetles away.
Please. Go quickly. It would be terrible if the mine collapsed and we did not at least discover my partner's fate.
I can feel the grip of those accursed anchors releasing. After all this time, I am free!

Please, wayfarer. I need your help. I was hired to guard a caravan out of Bergama, a family moving to Bangkorai.\n\nI am ashamed to confess it, but I failed to honor the contract. I abandoned them—all of them—down at the oasis.

Please, wayfarer. I need your help. I was hired to guard a caravan out of Bergama, a family moving to Bangkorai.\n\nI am ashamed to confess it, but I failed to honor the contract. I abandoned them—all of them—down at the oasis.
Nice work, deputy! We have everything we need to satisfy statute three. \n\nThat means Ildani is in deep desert without any water.
Without your help, I would have been meat for the jackals.
Excellent work! We can examine this at our leisure once we're back in Cyrodiil.\n\nHmm. Do you hear something? I thought I heard something.

There you are! Lorelia was starting to worry. She said those cultists were trying to mislead you again. She worried that you would turn against us.\n\nI knew it was all right though. Why would you possibly oppose Lorelia?
Watch your back out there.
Maybe once I've completed my apprenticeship, I'll be able to walk that straight and narrow path my father always preached about. Maybe.
I'm sorry, my friend, but my services are by appointment only.
Fast and effective! Onsi has blessed me with a capable ally in my time of need.\n\nNow let's take a look at what you've found, and we'll learn if fortune continues to favor us today.
Go on. Burn the disciples' food and I'll slip by. Catch up when you can.
Do you dare to ask more of me?
Well, seems like the captive convinced you to help him. \n\nI'll be interested to see what you find out.
Is it done? Is the envoy dead?\n\nThen let me out of here so I can go rescue my family!
I heard you doused the signal fires and stopped the Dominion attack. \n\nSounds like a fine day of work. A fine day of work, indeed!

The mayor and I will muster my bailiffs and tell everyone what happened. We'll prepare for a fight, but I don't think it will come to that.\n\nOnce you deal with Leonce, the militia should disband. We'll sort out the guilty after that.
My fault. It was my fault, but I didn't mean it. Oh, Mother is sad now, very sad. \n\nI hate <<1>>. I hate him! But … I kind of want to join him. And that's bad. Very bad!
You there! You're not some Daedric illusion, are you? I need help!
Hallin's Stand will forever be a home to you.

I haven't seen as many harpies swarming the skies, which makes me think the threat may be over.\n\nI'd rather hear it from my own people, but the only ones I talk to are those who've got something to complain about.
Reminds me of my younger years.\n\nWe've left Seius for you. Once he's dead, this all ends.
I hope you're not one of those gullible people. Susceptible to angry lies and wild accusations. Leonce has let the power go to his pointed, little head. It's disgraceful!
I can't believe my eyes!
Once we have the rest armed, we will be closer to the numbers we need.
It's only a matter of time before <<1>> is ours again.
Thank you for your discretion. I'm rather concerned about what's going on in Hallin's Stand, but it's not a good idea to say so in public.\n\nYou see, it's my husband ….
Leave me to my shame. There is nothing you can do.
The Covenant is falling back. They're squirming like scared kwama grubs.\n\nNice work. May the Tribunal requite you, as you deserve.
Troll's blood! Do you need an invitation? Speak to Tanval.
Go to the west gate and help <<1>>. Garyn can show the way.
Bring the <<1>>. I need it for what we must do.\n\nTrees will grow where we rest, and balance will be restored.
It's a good plan. Can't say I like ghosts anyway.
Fool that I was! I can only imagine what Giron is up to. You should find out.
Shalk are all over the town. Collect their chitin and bring it to <<1>>.
Until Girvas finds his daughter, there will be no trust. Look for her to the west.\n\nPerhaps the wind that blows is pushing us to what must be.
Whatever you're going to do, just do it.
<<1>> is not with you. You must find her.
You are not of Senie. Your scales bear stains of soot, and you smell of smoke and flame.\n\nWhat brings you here?
Have you found Ahknara? B'vek, I wish I could see the look on her face when she meets you in combat for the first time.
Through that door to the south, you'll find Ahknara.\n\nSee that she is fed to the land.
Shalk are all over town. Collect their chitin and bring it to <<1>>.
Ah, look at the dancing flames. \n\nDid you get them all?
You can see me, outsider!\n\nI beg you, help me.
Captain? Captain Hjolm?
My nix-hounds are nervous. They smell the Orcs in the pass.
Once you've got the chitin, look for <<1>> in the temple.
This might not be the place for you. We're looking for fresh recruits here. \n\nYou look more like a seasoned veteran. I'd suggest you seek out the battlemaster instead.
I see the vision has left you, student.
Speak to Giron and take care of anything he asks you to do.\n\nI'll lock down Narsis. The Maulborn won't get near my people.
She's not with you? Muck water! She's gone off to do something brave, hasn't she?
Merely mark the door with the branch.\n\nYou need not be a sorcerer, for the Hist has its own magic, even when far removed from the roots.
Help <<1>> with whatever she needs to prepare the ritual.\n\nOur lives, and perhaps the future of our people, rely on seeing this through, no matter what the cost.
<<1>> has begun preparing for the ritual. The blood on your hands will be put to good use.
The matriarch is poisoned? She's a stern woman, and I must confess I dislike her. But she's also honorable and strong.\n\nPoison is no way for a Dunmer lady to die.
You make it look easy. At least, what I saw when I wasn't hiding and squealing like a hatchling.\n\nI know I'm not brave. But did you hear his voice? Mavos has returned.
<<1>> was out searching for Bjorick when the Goblins attacked the hall.\n\nFind my sons, stranger. And find them alive.

Troll's blood! You've saved my life and the lives of my kind. I'll ask for your help one more time, if you'll let me.\n\nI crave revenge. We must make the Goblin Warlord and his spider queen pay for what they've done.
Gods! I haven't been hit like that since the war. Witch must have put a hex on the Tear. \n\nDid you see that? Threw me clear across the room!
Check the cocoons for signs of <<1>> or <<2>>.\n\nThere are more spider cocoons near the beach east of the manor house.

I can't perform the ritual without my implements. I don't even have hands to pick them up! That's annoying.\n\nEast and west tombs, candle and skull. And whatever you do, don't … um, do something. You know. That thing.
I … can't hold him … much longer. Use the altar now!
Lord, Mother, and Wizard! Saalu has been poisoned?\n\nDo what you can. Please. That's not a death a Dunmer lady should suffer.
Welcome to the Dusklight Inn. You can stay for as long as you like. We've got plenty of room.
Get that cursed thing off the door. Then we'll see what Serien thinks of my axe.
Well met! I'm on duty, friend. Speak with <<1>> straight away.
Like eels through seagrass, we're inside. Well done! As we speak, my troops are attacking the fort's main yard.
I'm surprised that a man could see the Ghost Snake and live.
My vision was clear. Your actions will affect our future. Perhaps in ways we cannot yet see.
The constable and I are taking bets on how long before Martin annoys an officer and winds up back in the stocks.\n\nI really do wish him the best, but my gold's on two weeks.
Try the tombs to the west. \n\nI know he's here somewhere. I can feel his spirit.
Is that what I think it is? Don't draw attention to yourself.\n\nI'll take those and get them to the others.
Investigate the shack near the docks. That's where Rhavil went.
You have the meat and the reeds? Good.\n\nOur Hist is on a small island north of this hut. Spread the fertilizer you've gathered around its roots.
A totem, eh? My lovely Merarii, innovating again.\n\nSave who you can. I'll do what I can when they get here.
Flea-bitten, mangy Khajiit!\n\nThose opportunistic, vile, simpering creatures are unworthy of the lives they possess!
I knew you'd help us. I just knew it!\n\nI'm going to see my egg-sister very soon.
Find <<1>>. He's a blacksmith. Tell him I sent you. \n\nBest of luck to you, outsider.
If you ever need anything, don't hesitate to ask. If it's within my power, I'll try to help.\n\nI'll make sure things get cleaned up around here.
Your involvement in all this is quite … unexpected. I will be watching you, outsider.

You want us to help drive off the Daggers, you better prove the rest of the Pact can fight like a Nord.\n\nGet yourself a drink, grab a weapon—or a poncy spell, if that's your preference—and duel three of my soldiers.
Now go. Take this knowledge and defeat Balreth.\n\nKill him this time!
I hear Dark Elves are milk drinkers. Too bad. I bet a good mead would loosen your back ends enough for you to pull the sticks out of them.
Hurry, do what <<1>> asked!
You're back! Is everything all right at the mine now?
I still can't believe what Edrasa did. Foolish, thoughtless woman. \n\nI'll send her away as soon as things settle down. I don't want anyone to learn what she did, but I need time to get over this.

The shrines are outside the city—north, southeast, and southwest.\n\nVivec's shrine is across the river to the southwest of Ebonheart. Almalexia's is to the southeast. The shrine to Sotha Sil is on an island north of the Argonian quarter.
Move along. There's nothing to see here.
Good. Everyone is out. \n\nOh, wait. That Vanguard who was with Tanval … you should probably free her as well. She's atop a tower.
Return to the hidden chamber. \n\nDispel whatever remains of Tanval Indoril's ritual.
Whatever you seek here, strange one, now is not the time. \n\nThe reliquary has been violated. My spirit demands vengeance.
You aren't the one who tampered with the reliquary. \n\nI need seek no redress from you. You may go. Or do you have another purpose here?
By Ayem—you've run through a gauntlet of plague and death, yet you aren't sick. How?
Find the rest of the scouting party. I'll report what I've learned to Diiril.
The Woozle, the Woozle. I must have it! Please, hand it over now.
You—you look like you can handle yourself. You have to help me!\n\nThe other guards went after the raiders, but one of those Dwarven things wounded me.
You've returned! Did you recover the <<z:1>>?
I heard <<1>> asked you to investigate the murders.\n\nI hope you find something.
If my instincts are right, we'll be digging up a hornet's nest when we get to <<1>>.
I saw a Khajiit run out the door. What's going on?

Have no fear. The offering was intended to pique the Daedric Prince's interest. It worked, perhaps better than expected.\n\nThe curse upon you is temporary in nature. Make sure you find the <<z:1>> before Clavicus Vile loses interest.
I will always be in your debt for freeing my son.
That tomb complex will be well defended. Take care.
You've slain three minions of the Worm Cult.\n\nDo you think that's all it takes?
This plantation will be rebuilt and repopulated with many cat-man slaves.\n\nAnd I will work every one of them to death in memory of my Tiril.
Why do you stand here? You should run!
I've waited for you. You've undertaken the Trial of the Heart.
Another pilgrim? So few today, beyond yourself and that Dominion soldier. Are you ready for the Trial of the Fang?
I pray the Hist amber is lost to the ages. <<1>> must not control Hissmir's lost power.
You could easily rise in the ranks here. I can sense it.\n\nBut I have nothing left to teach you. You should journey to Wayrest if you want to improve your crafting skills.
So, any luck? Did you find the raiders' leader?
I still have my eye on you, even if the Farseer considers you a friend of the clan.
Ra-shadda will tell the moons about you, so they will always watch over and guide you.
It's so good to see everyone free again … I mean almost everyone.
Thanks for getting me out of that cage—but you could have backed me up, you know.
Tribunal's blessings. Watch yourself here in Tal'Deic. Discipline isn't what it used to be, but that doesn't mean you can start trouble.
She's not letting me out? What, am I to wait here while you do her little errands?\n\nShe's probably laughing at me from her decrepit little boat wreck. Never try to negotiate with criminals.
These are troubled times. But all times have trouble of one sort or another, yes?
And what do you bring me? It better be something of worth. I don't pay layabouts for rotten fruit. \n\nThat's bad for my reputation, but it's worse for the layabouts. I'm sure you understand.
Something is influencing the General. We need to find out what's wrong with him.
Leave me. I prefer to spend the hours before my death alone.
What can I do for you?

I'm grateful for your aid, outlander.\n\nThe crates and potions are scattered throughout the camps to the southeast. Collect them and bring them to my farseer inside the Tribunal Temple. Her name is Tirinaat.

A little messy, but sometimes you have to take the low road, right?\n\nOne of your vicecanons is waiting for you. I'll let them stay as long as you're vouching for their behavior. This is still my town, understand?
I hope you've learned something.
Don't mistake my attitude. Naldyn was a thug, but he was my brother. \n\nI don't care who he harassed. He didn't deserve to die.
You say you can help? Prove it.\n\nI won't believe you until I see some results.
Aren't the wasps just adorable?\n\nBe careful not to get stung. The venom is very painful. Oh, and so are the foot-long stingers.
Please hurry to Gethis. None of this makes any sense.
A bound spirit. So beautiful.
I can't remember anything, though the cloud over my mind is gone. Now my memories lie in deep pools, inaccessible to me unless they bubble to the surface.
You, there! Did Maera send you? \n\nI discovered this resonating thing on one of the smashed constructs. I think these resonators are how that Dres rod controlled them.
<<1>> is a boisterous, loud man. If he isn't found soon, the peace and quiet in Stormhold will betray his absence.
Spare our misguided warriors, if you can. I assure you, if you use the artifact I gave you, they'll stop and leave you in peace.\n\nMay the wind be in the eyes of your foes.
Vivec bless your steps, recruit. Thanks for joining the war effort! With talented crafters in the Halls, there's no challenge we can't overcome.
We've waited far too long.\n\nThe people have a right to be upset, and now <<1>> has paid the price.
We'll hold the line here, ensure that the Ashlands are safe. All of Stonefalls is relying on you, my friend.
Repeat the past. Summon the guardians.\n\nWe must see this is done.
A sad event, but as I feared. Not all trees are strong. \n\nHopefully, this <<1>> has taken her last victim for a few generations, at least.
You. My wife asked me not to allow anyone—especially you—into our sanctuary. It was heartless of you to put such fear in her.\n\nLeave.
Quickly, soldier. Speak with Turoni. We have little time left, and my brother grows angrier by the moment.
My orders are to summon up <<1>> for you. \n\nThese Daedra take the heart right out of me. I'll be in the rear, watching your back.
Honor to you, soldier. I have been given my instructions. I am to summon the beast known as <<1>>. \n\nI summon it, you kill it, and you gather its essence. This should be easy ….
Honor to you, soldier. I'll take the bloody offerings and ready them for the ritual.\n\nAre you prepared for the next step?
I can't thank you enough for helping my son. Hopefully he has learned a lesson.
Oh my lovely lovely crystals…
Be safe up there. If even our Lady cannot tend to the fates of this Vox, you should be wary.
My orders are to help you.
I heard what happened with the chieftain. Don't blame yourself.\n\nWait, are you blaming yourself? You forget how to read faces when you haven't had a face in decades.
Remember, it is illegal to enter Mournhold without registering at the city center. You do not want to get fined for noncompliance, citizen.
Word of the plague in the west has reached Mournhold. We were told to watch for someone matching your description. It's good to have you in the city.
I sense the Temple is free of the Daedric incursion. We are well pleased.\n\nWhile you fought for my glory, I learned more about our foes.
I heard <<1>>  tasked you with investigating the murders.\n\nYeah, well … good luck.
I was told <<1>> asked you to investigate the murders.\n\nMay you find the secrets hidden in deep waters.
We've been expecting you.
By the smell, I can tell you've gathered the ingredients she wanted. Don't linger here on my account.
Always a pleasure to speak with another knowledge-seeker. Guildmaster Vanus will be pleased!
Well met. I'm just waiting for Johraine to give me the word. Then I can get us out of here.
I have to dig. I have to bury myself to make it stop! The voice! The voice just won't shut up!
Quiet! Don't talk. I have to listen. I have to get back to the dream.
You're not real. You can't be! Get out of here. I have no time for illusions. I'm supposed to be dreaming.

We need the Stone complete to contain the Daedra, finish the Goblins—you have my thanks. I hope you fathom what you offer.\n\nIt seems Sir Edgard and his squad have returned—they found one stone piece, but there are others.
<<1>> is very important to me. After all, he sewed the receipts for last year's profits inside his vest!
Good work rescuing those travelers. What those necromancers would've done to them ….
Meejapa mentioned that you fought a monstrous Orc.
Kill them. Make the ash safe again. \n\nI must find that insect, the lieutenant. When I catch him, I'll pluck his wings and watch him dance on his back.
We're in grave peril.
Hah, I can tell we'll be drawing blades together soon enough.\n\nNow, what can I tell you?

Good luck. Beware their blades. Even the inexperienced members of the Vanguard are deft swordsmen.\n\nOnce you've found what we're looking for, get back here and report to Denu. She'll know what to do.
Three of the merchants I worked for wore the keys on chains around their necks. They were the first to fall when the Maulborn attacked, but I don't think their bodies were searched very thoroughly.
Look what the Vanguard did. They confiscated my guar pen to hold their supplies. They scattered my poor guar and laughed. \n\nI'm too scared to go looking for them. What will I do now?
One moment, soldier. This takes concentration.
You found it! Take it to <<1>>. She should still be resting nearby.

You've done excellent work. Our agents are in place; all that's left is to set fire to the river.\n\nOnce the river is ablaze, we'll strike hard from the shadows and take back Murkwater. Are you ready?
I hope <<1>> told you the plan.
Good to see you made it. I told <<1>> about you, and she's eager to meet you.
Have you found out anything about the keystone yet? Why are you out here?
To take out the supports, you need a pickaxe. \n\nYou'll find some tools in the monks' quarters, just to the east.
Namira, I revere thee! Namira, I serve thee!
Turn back, wanderer. The oasis isn't safe. Look what that creature did to my goat!\n\nI tell you, the gods look down and say, "Hram, you deserve a life of annoyance and inconvenience!"

Our attack was a disaster. The other vicecanons agreed to keep our forces together. Should've known they'd peel off the moment I turned my back.\n\nIf they weren't keeping Stormhold from tearing itself apart, I'd let them boil in a fish kettle.

<<1>> informed us you had entered the ruins to pursue <<2>>'s imposter. Whatever you did in the ruins caused a lot of panic amongst the Dominion.\n\nWe chose our moment and pushed out of the cave. <<3>> was wounded in the process, but she'll survive.
<<1>> is one of our finest scouts. Seeing him alive is sunlight in the afternoon.
Hold. The name's Ragara, and this job site belongs to my band.
Good thing you didn't release the Dremora. We'd both be ribbons in her hair.\n\nBehind her there's a door to what <<1>> called the "Vault." They have Hist sap in there, stored in giant vats.
If that harlot Tevynni steals my deal, she'll regret it.
Do you desire an exquisite torment? No? Then go, before I change my mind.
A word with you before we enter the portal.
Find a way to kill <<1>> and I'll reward you handsomely.
Excellent work with the Stonefalls dead drops. I'll let you know when any more contracts become available.
My brother arrived at the inn. Do I have you to thank for this?
My mother and brother are safe, and I have you to thank. Praise the Three they survived.
Some advice, outsider. You want to fill the bowl with <<1>>'s blood.
Sithis will decide your fate, outsider.
Enough about my problems. I'm just glad you're here.
Thanks for saving me back there. Whatever you did, <<1>> wasn't pleased, not at all.\n\nDid you recover the keystone?
What did <<1>> promise you in exchange for the supplies? There had to be something.
Tall Papa and I owe you one, my new friend. But I need to ask another favor. If I can.
What of <<A:1>>? Have you learned what the Dominion wants with it?
Mavos, did you speak with him?
The tree-minders will know what to do. Go, now!
Whose truth is truth, I wonder? May Sithis reveal his champion.
I don't want to spend any more time down here than is necessary. We should keep moving.
You honor Saint Veloth by your actions.
Good to see you again, friend. The Goblinization matrix could have been amazing, if my brother hadn't ruined everything. \n\nOf course, you know that. You've already seen my genius in action!
Strange meeting you out here in the wilds. After Davon's Watch, I hadn't expected to see you again.\n\nIf I might say it, another … minor issue has arisen.

If you wish to help, you should wear the clothing from that chest. The Dominon will see another assistant and leave you be.\n\nBut you haven't spent much time around <<A:1>>, so their tigers may pick out your scent. Do what you can to avoid them.
The keepers will remember you for what you've done. The Hist will remember you.
Fewer of my fellow spirits haunt the hamlet. Did it work?
Outside the sanctuary of the shrine, you will find the true forms of the Shadowscales revealed to you.\n\nUse your newfound sight, and remove this cancer from our midst.
The Dwarves were quite creative! For such a godless race. Perhaps those stands could help us get past the doors?
Why do you pollute our swamp with your presence?
I hear there's profits in Ebonheart.
The savior of Davon's Watch, and the Virak siege-breaker!\n\nThank Vivec you're here. Kragenmoor has been taken.
<<1>> is near the top of the hill.\n\nHe's got some kind of bodyguard with him.
Well, you saved my miners, but I still don't see the Goblin totem.\n\nThe gold I'll reward you with doesn't multiply the longer you take, so you should hurry on.
Welcome back to the arms of the guild, comrade.
This one greets your return, comrade.
What are you doing back here? Jurni needs those supplies at the tower in the prison's western sector.
I'm not harboring any wild beasts nearby, as I'm sure you can see.
I can hear the Night Mother's voice! If she only speaks to the leader, then ….
I'll stay here and try to figure out how this thing works.
May good fortune stalk your steps, comrade.

The seed is planted. The dreugh are frenzied by the Dominion scent. \n\nSaervild must be stopped, and the relics returned. The wind tells me that they are near Mudshallow Cave, in the Dominion camp. Make haste!
If your Nord friends send some troops our way, I'm sure we can dig up more artifacts for them.
What's going on? Shadowscales, here? No—they can't be!
Is that really Sithis? That's amazing … oh, wait, this is bad, isn't it?
Back so soon, comrade?
Always good working with a guildmate. May Stendarr watch your back.
Master of Apocrypha, I beseech you. Send us a weapon to wield against these invaders.\n\nOh, hello!
<<1>> is pleased to have you at her side.
Good luck at the court. I'm going to poke around a bit more, then head back to the portal.
There you are. I feared you'd been kidnapped by forces from beyond.
Whatever you plan on doing, you have my full support. Just know that.
I'll make sure no one follows you. \n\nI'm tired of sitting on my hands. Time for some action.
Pleasure working with you. May Almalexia guide your steps, and may Vivec guard your coin purse.
I would entrust this task to no one else, comrade. You go with the weight of the guild on your shoulders.
Use the bellows to stoke the flame just a bit. Use the valve to fire it yet more. And for a truly fearsome blaze, pour fire salts on the coals.
It will be a while before Feyne accepts my choice.
Tree-Minders know many cures, for those who seek treatment.
Aelif will see you soon. She has business to attend to. Suspicions to investigate. We shall see.
I'm sorry, but I don't have time for outsiders.\n\nUnless you care to join the Fighters Guild. I'm sure the steward is around here somewhere.
We bargained in good faith! All fair and square! You can't have him.
Thank you again for your time on the river. One day, I hope to soothe my scales in the mud of laughter.
Pay the toll or pay the price. Something, something … rhymes with rice. Yes. Almost got it.\n\nI'm not good at warning rhymes yet. Don't look at me like that!
Adept, new recruits to the Guild rarely impress me anymore … but you've already proven yourself to me. Good luck in Sheogorath's realm.
I can sense … yes. The aura around you glows with good fortune. You will be the one to help me complete my final task.
I'm so glad we've had this time together. One must usually go to a public execution for conversation of this caliber.
You! Knave tells me you choose toll of flesh. True? True?
An outsider! You walk and talk, so no good for eating. Still, an intruder. You must pay the toll.
This has gone wonderfully. "A simple overseer job," she said. "Just like the old days." Why did I ever leave Kragenmoor? \n\nMany thanks to you for your help.
Quickly! How did it go? Was there a strong color change? Perhaps a strong smell?
I … I don't feel so good.
I had no idea I was in Vaermina's thrall. She'll never touch my mind again, my friend.
The lute's probably back where Engling did her performance, down to the south. I'll be just on the next island over. Standing upright.
Sage Tirora answered your call, Shor bless her.
You're needed beneath the loam. The stone of Shor calls out in pain. Can you hear it?
Remember, <<1>> is in the shack to the southwest. Did you need something else?
My crystal tells me you have done my terrible deed.
I'll bet you couldn't find my bongos. In fact, I wager you mocked me by accepting my task.
There is still more to do.
I saw some Dreamers packing up and fleeing.\n\nHave you done the deed?
Have you killed the Twilight Boss?
I tremble in anticipation.
What do you want?
<cough> I don't have long. Is he dead?
I'm happy to see you, but please keep your voice down.
I can't stay here!

Thank you for getting me out of that mine. My husband and I are indebted to you. Once things calm down here, I'll get you that mead I promised.\n\nAnd it'll be good stuff from Hodmar's private stock, assuming the Goblins haven't stolen it.
If you hurry, you may be able to take <<1>> by surprise. Any advantage we can get at this point is worth it.
There's only one more trial. We'll let you know once we're finished delving through Sheogorath's madness.
And the cycle of pain continues. I hope you're proud of your part in this tragedy.
How can I assist the hero of <<1>>?
My brother and I came here together to join the Companions, and I'll be damned if we're not leaving here together, but he's caught in the mine. Please, look for <<1>>, you must save him.
I can't believe you actually sided with that coward.\n\nGo die in a hole, Goblin-lover. The Pact doesn't need any more snowbacks like you.
Stral is all that remains. His time on the river must come to an end.
Be careful, now. No telling what these creatures are capable of.

They're everywhere! I don't know where they came from. I didn't see them until I grabbed a bucket to douse the flames, and then it attacked me. A Daedra!\n\nMy fortunes have never looked less pleasing.
We now pause for a brief intermission. Would you like some cheese?
Did you find them? Did you find the Eyes? Let's get this door open!
You've saved us all, but the giants are gathering on the hill. The Worm Cult must have angered them. I just hope there isn't a stampede.
They keep trophies every time they kill an invader. That drum in the treasure pile should get the chieftain's attention.
I can't believe Dad brought down that mammoth. He's like Ysgramor!
You can do it! You're the champion of Treva's Farm!
Valaste awaits you at the Guildhall in Vulkhel Guard, along the southern coast of Auridon.
I don't understand. What's happened?
Well. Glad to see someone who can get things done. Good work.
I wish we'd never come here, but <<1>> insisted we'd find a way to fit in.
I hear a fool speaking. I choose not to listen.
You dishonor the Pact with your actions. We cannot forget the past if we keep repeating it.
So … what did you think? What was your favorite part? \n\nNo, don't answer that. I can see by the look on your face how happy you are!
I need to get the wounded back to the tower. Gut the bastards and climb their corpses to the signal fire.
It's done. My students return to the Hist.
Follow the trail I left when I made my escape. You'll know his lair by the bones, blood, and smell.\n\nTempt him with some game, and I bet you'll get his attention.
Orkey's Hollow is north of the village. Send everyone you find back here. Good luck.
Praise Sithis! A traveler! Please, the poison's chill is getting to me. I don't know if I'm going to make it.
I hope you have better luck at the shrine than I did. Watch yourself in there!
Thank you for your help. I never dreamed we'd leave this place alive.
It's strange, but knowing he's a peace brings a smile to my face. Ulrich was a hero to the end. We'll never forget him.
If you can stop to chat, your business must not be all that important.
Get that switch on the far wall, friend.
Thank Kyne! You have it!
Uhh … Xarxes give me strength. I'm all right adept. I just didn't realize how tired I am.
They haven't crawled inside, have they? Do you see them anywhere? Are they looking out of my eyes?
<<<1>> wags his tail happily.>
You did all right. Not as good as me, but still good.
Grab some gear from our friend here. His kit will help you slip into the mine unnoticed.
Damn me for a fool! Why did I trust that madman?
Comrade. Bright Moons, Aelif is glad to see you again. She would trust no one else for the task before us today.
Thank Stendarr! Safely back in Tamriel. \n\nNow, we just have to face the council.
Greetings, Vestige. Sai is recovering well enough, though he hides a great pain in his heart. His confinement has shaken him more than he dares admit.
Alive and kicking, I see. As for me, I feel a decade younger. Can you see the healthy shimmer to my scales?\n\nYou no doubt have questions. Please, ask. It's the least I can do after your help.
Close the portals around <<1>> before the Covenant can gain a foothold.
<<1>> is back. I raised him by hand. He's more Argonian than most Argonians I know!
The Covenant is everywhere.
Please. My scales are slick. Don't send me to Sithis.
You don't wear the lion crest. Please, help.
Everywhere I see, these cowards put us to their blades. Dryskinned wretches.
Jofnir continues to aid us, even in death! I'll be right behind you, comrade.
You did it! The traitor is dead, and Molag Bal's hold on Tamriel is weakened. \n\nYou are wise, comrade. Wise, and strong.
Remember, it's the appleblossom honey. That's what I need to make the next batch of mead.
You must stop Skorvild from carrying out his mad plan. Eating giants is just so … unappetizing!\n\nYou'll probably find him up in the old manor house. He's been spending a lot of time there lately.
Kazok's ugly head on a pike! I can't think of a better way to tell people that Voljar's Meadery makes mead fit for the toughest Nords.
The giant's leader usually prowls the hill overlooking the village.
Please tell me you've accomplished your mission.
A moment, please. No one else will listen. \n\nI have an idea that could help turn the tide against the Covenant.
Go on. Take a drink. It won't kill you.
I don't know what you did, but my soldiers and I are alive! Thanks.
Did you make it through? The passage leads directly to the signal fires.
Let Droi rest. I'll watch over him until the Kyne's Breath does its work.
Hmm?
I must tend to the wounded.
Comrade, I must speak with you about an urgent matter!
The Skald-King is in danger! We must warn King Jorunn. The Stormfist clan has gone to the Hall of Trials, and I fear the worst.
You're back at last. Were you successful?
What happened to you? You were doing so well. Why'd you stop running?
What right do you think you have to speak to me?  I have no use for you.
Good security is in the details, my friend. Keep an eye out for anything unusual.
So what have you learned?
Why you look so proud, what did you find out?
So what'd you find out?

Welcome to Windhelm! You're just in time for the celebration. \n\nIf you don't mind me saying so, you look pretty capable and good in a fight. Just the sort of individual that Thane Mera is looking for.
I feel a thousand years young. Your tale captivated every one of us.\n\nI do hope <<1>> will tell another one soon!
I can't believe my ears. <<AC:1>> is restored! Praise the Silvenar's champion!
Please, be careful in the forest. Villagers return with tales of werewolves and Houndsmen prowling near town.
Your work here is done, Arrow. But know that you will always have a place of honor in the Skald-King's court.
Thank you for saving Spinner Indinael's spirit from the Worm Cult. If she'd remained a lich, we'd all be doomed.
You must go quickly. My hold on this world grows weaker with every passing moment.
You've saved the Spinner! Now, she can join the other spirits in eternal slumber. Thank you!
Well done. As a final step, you must scatter dirt on the fire.
Well. You got his attention. I can feel his energies shifting. He's angry.
Fascinating. The roots do not consume you. That may prove useful.
What news? Have you found my daughter?
I really enjoy these impromptu celebrations!
I need to figure out what happened here. My friends deserve answers.

You saved the lives of the hunters. You ruined their clothes, but you saved their lives.\n\nMy father will be upset when his slaves fail to locate new prey. He'll become curious. Then we'll catch him off-guard.
You gave the orb to my sister? \n\nI hope you had a good reason.
I can't believe all this happened. Because of a thief and an enchanted lute.
Thanks for coming to get me.

You follow me to my home? I should bite your feet off, and see how well you run!\n\nThe Hound is my consort. He has shown me the way of the wilds, and we rule over the forest, together. I need nothing from you!
With your help, I just know we're going to succeed!
Goat stew! You have to use a spoon or a fork to eat it. What kind of meal is that?
Remember, after you get the goat to follow you, lead it back here to me.

We're fortunate no one has perished, but I fear my Keepers have grown desperate and cowardly. Did you hear Voranil's remark? Use Daedric power? Sacrilegious.\n\nWe need to get Rilis back in his prison before my Keepers do something they'll regret.
Holed up in a cave. Good to hear she's still up and kicking!
Greetings in his name. I've never been to Orsinium but I hear it's … nice. We're always pleased to have new faces join us.

Ah, the smell of fresh blood. It's intoxicating. I only wish I had been the one to drain the life from their bodies.\n\nBut this is not about me. This is about sending a message. And Valeric has heard it, loud and clear.
I can't believe I slept through the whole thing.
Things are quiet here. For now.
I'm afraid this is only the beginning. I burn with eagerness to eradicate our enemies.
The Ternion Monks have helped you and the Skald-King. Maybe now people will understand that we are not the monsters they thought us to be.
I'm sure we'll run into each other again. Maybe even when we have a show to perform!
Don't get yourself killed, now!
Come no closer until you've stated your business.
That was no trick. That was Sai Sahan!
It's always good to see you, brave one.
I'm sure Irnskar has other errands for you to run.
Lucky shot from one of those Sea Vipers. Looks like I'll have to postpone those dancing lessons.\n\nDid you find the sky-key?
King Jorunn stirs in agony before he calms and grows still. These waves repeat, even as you enter his dreams.\n\nHis life continues to slip away. What did you discover?
Once you rescue the Silvenar, you'll need a warrior's help to get him out of Jathsogur. All the advice I can give you won't make up for a strong sword at your side.
One more wounded warrior won't make a difference. Good advice is what you need on the road out of Jathsogur. Sacrifice me and Sariel can help you after you save the Silvenar.
Free of this accursed tomb and those thrice-damned cultists! I owe you a debt. Perhaps someday I'll repay it.

There are few who can claim to have fought against the Worm Cult and survived, let alone prevailed. \n\nI wonder if you might be convinced to strike another blow against them. The Skald-King could use someone like you at Honrich Tower.
We've got trouble here. The Reachmen have taken over the Northwind Mine up ahead.
Did I hear that right? The hero of Eastmarch? Well met, and good to have you with us!
Were you sent to rescue us?
The Stormfists were panicked by the raging fires. We cut through their ranks as quickly as we could, but I'm afraid we were too late.\n\nTell me … my sister …?

It's good to finally see you with my own eyes. Thank you for rescuing me, but our trials are not over.\n\nThe binding stones affected my connection to the Bosmer. I must get back everything they took from me.
Spinners don't usually write their tales down. I guess since this valley's been fought over many times, they wanted to keep their tales from fading. We're lucky these journals exist!
Help Firras find the end of his tale. Not with wind and rain, but with pain and death!
The brewery's up the hill. Follow your nose, you can't miss the smell of fermenting rotmeth.\n\nI'll stay here and tend to <<1>>.
Thallik is just down the hall. Hakra and I have your back.
The spirits of Ysgramor's companions will ride with you against the Worms!\n\nTalk to Valdur before you go. And Kyne's speed, my friend!
I'm glad you're the one who brings us the Handfast, after all you've done.
Over here, friend. How did you fare?
The Silvenar believes you are a friend. Frankly, I think you're a blessed hero.\n\nY'ffre knows we need one now.
I am so relieved that Jomund is safe. Thank you for helping.
At long last! Long live the Silvenar and the Green Lady!
A simple ceremony starts the Bosmers' most important relationship.
Be careful. Something's not right, here.
The Green Lady and the Silvenar will always be in your debt. As will the spinners of this city.
I'll meet up with the rest of the crew once my tasks are complete.
We caught this Maormer exiting the hold, likely off to warn his masters. With a bit of coaxing, he gave us the information we need.
You'll probably find Lord Vurlop in the inn. Like most Nords, he enjoys his mead. And I understand that nobles can get particularly thirsty when the King is in town.
I've had enough of this pit of Oblivion. Going home.

The Prince and his hot temper! He decided to hold his own meeting while the King and the Pact ambassadors meet at the keep.\n\nHe managed to insult both the Dark Elves and the Argonians with his posturing and boastfulness!
This is your chance. Prove your legacy.
If you're going to wander the city, might as well start on the east side of town. The homeless there tend to complain louder than the others.
It's like a veil's been removed from my eyes. No, from all my senses!\n\nEver since becoming the Green Lady, I've felt the power of the Bosmer, but now I sense their spirit as well.
I can't wait to hear the bard sing. I wonder if he gives private performances?
You win, outsider. We'll return to the surface.
The King's Arrow! Well met.
Just go. I'll be fine.
Sai Sahan is back with you. I've lived up to my part of the deal—I trust that the rest of you will do the same.
I need to get an idea of how much damage they've done.
What a mess. We'll be eating omelets tonight, I can tell you.
I think I figured out why cats like us so much.\n\nIt's because we are so beautiful. And we smell good.

Do you know what that s'wit had me fetch while you were gone? Food from the other tent! As if walking ten feet would kill him.\n\nI got the food, though. Added a special berry, too. His stomach will appreciate it.
Under the table, just there! Did you see that? It was a Worm Cultist!
You're giving me an odd look, stranger. I'm not sure I like it. Didn't I tell you to move on? Must I have you escorted out of my Thane's keep?
I don't trust you. Hallfrida looks disgusted. No doubt you've done something.
I overheard your conversation with the thane. Let me know immediately if her advisors find anything.
Good, good. Need to hold the line here. Can't let the Captain down, yeah?
Thank you.\n\nOh, and when you meet whoever's responsible for this … twist the knife a little? Just for me.
Help Imiril. Rilis has a twisted fascination with her.\n\nI'd wager she's alive, though I doubt she's enjoying herself.
The Three smile on me today. My silk sits again in my stores, and Turil must wallow in his misery.
You gave away my silk to that … that netch. Does it bring you joy to steal from an old Dark Elf?
Thorulf's room is on the first floor of the manor, on the eastern side. Sirkidur has a skeleton key, but I'm not sure how to get it from her.
Thanks for meeting me here. Please stay until I'm officially a sage. It means a lot to me.
<<1>> is with you? Can I see her?
You don't look infected. I guess you're all right.
Well, at least they're all accounted for. No more dares for me.
You! Thank Kyne. You want to do something about these ropes?
Thank Kyne! A familiar face. How did you know to come here, my friend?
I hope you're up to the task. Some of my best warriors have fallen attempting to push out those cultists.
I'm going to make it. I am! I'll live to see Riften and hoist a pint. Thank you, my friend.
<<1>> won't be safe until Treehenge is secure.
Do what you must to save <<1>>.
Why must the Worm Cult meddle in Bosmer affairs?
I'm getting stronger every minute. I wonder what my sprout will look like?
Do not linger here. Danger threatens elsewhere.
A new face? What brings you to this godsforsaken place?
I'm sure with a little coaxing <<1>> will get the job done. He's far from the best performer on the island. But at least he's awake.
I need to get my daggers.
I hope you can help Merric at-Aswala with whatever it is he needs.
Go, investigate Betar-Nes's home. I don't trust these locals to do a thorough search. You, I can trust.
I hope the Worm Cult has been shattered. But I fear they are just the foot of the mountain.
Hero, huh? Good luck in the mines. The Reach are bloody-minded bastards.
Place the <<mz:1>> in the final two sconces so we can enter the shrine.
I have great news for you, Adept!
I am the Watcher at the Bridge. I guard the border between this world and Sovngarde.
Listen! This is marvelous!\n\nDown this ramp lies the hollow chamber in which our story can be lured from skin to flesh!
Well, that was easy, eh? It gets harder from here.
Like a spring torrent, our troops will pour through the pass you've opened.
The braziers I've prepared will harness the power of the shards of Wuuthrad. Gather all that you can.\n\nWhen I give the word, activate the brazier to unleash the power of each shard.
You have to get out of here!
You've done it! By the gods, the lieutenant would be proud.\n\nWe've killed or rounded up most of the Ra Gada invaders. The militia won't have a problem with them anymore!

The mercenaries of the Gold Coast drink our wine and eat our food. They are waiting. For what, we must find out.\n\nI've heard of a courier's arrival within the hour. I need his message before it gets into the hands of the Gold Coast.
I'll do whatever the lieutenant says, so long as Velyn Harbor is saved.
Our worst nightmare has come to life. Sinmur has returned. The ancient enemy of the Companions must be faced once more.
Have you ever thought of becoming a brewer's assistant? We could go after even more unusual ingredients.
Don't bother … with a whole tree. Just gather kindling. Plenty of branches down.
Best-case scenario? They've found the Mora. I don't want to think about the worst-case. Too many variables.
Be careful.
I've never seen the <<1>> look like this before. It's wonderful!
What the …? What just happened?
Someone finally shut that lizard up. Great work out there, and some mighty fine shooting.
The Maormer around the lighthouse should have a rune that opens the barrier on the lighthouse's front door. Shake a few of those beach lizards down. I'm sure the rune will fall out.
You made it, and in one piece too. I thought my leg was going to give out crossing the water.\n\nBut enough of that. Did you locate my things?
You should find the Black Dagger camp west of here. Please recover our claw!
Go carefully on the roads, my friend. You're a valuable resource to the Dominion. \n\nAnd me, of course.
You've returned. And with the spell-lattice?
Another blade for the fight, eh? Are there lots more behind you?
<<1>> has a keen mind and a good heart. She's the key to freeing Ezduiin.
Thank the Earth Bones you're here!
Oh good. She made it to the entrance of the tombs. Fantastic.
You need to speak with my Sister of Floods.
Good to see her on her feet. She's got a will of iron, our captain.
They're stealing … my memories!
What fascinating artifacts these stones are. I wonder where they came from?
<<1>> asked me to thank you for gathering all the shards. He brought them into the ruins for the final battle.
Thank The Eight! Quickly! Untie us!
The fighting has been difficult, my friend. It's good to see you still alive.
The Veiled Heritance is behind this madness, I'm sure of it!
Kyne speed you—and if you run into any Worm Cultists, squash a few for me!
The spirits won't be appeased without a sacrifice of some kind.\n\nI don't believe they'll want a life for a life, but one must never be too careful.
You're on your way to the dig site? The supplies Telenger's been screaming about, no doubt.
If you can get Yiri to come back to me … well, you'll be my hero today.
You made it! Thank you for saving the other minstrels!\n\nIf only we had our instruments ….
I don't know if we're ready to play yet. We should go back to the camp and practice.
Buzul won't ruin the performance by limping. Drummers don't need to move much.
Ni-po-tu-la-hee! Ni-po-tu-la-hee!\n\nExcuse me, you're interrupting my practice.
What was all the muttering about? Go on, clear out. I've got work to do.
This isn't over yet. Remain vigilant, my friend.
Rotmeth for everyone! That is, as many of the guests as can stomach it.
Haven't the Draugr killed you yet?
Come to see how I'm doing? Don't worry—I'll recover. Really, I'm just happy to have cleaned up a bit.
Once you lead us to the top of <<1>>, the battle against <<2>> can begin!
We're counting on you to clear the route to the top of the mountain.
You returned! I kiss the two moons in thanks!\n\nThe mercenaries await. The merchants arranged a strange bargain for them.
Clear a path for the troops! We must deal with <<1>>.
I hope Urcelmo's plan is successful. Those Daedra frighten me.
Whatever you plan on doing, I hope you do it quickly. We can't hold here for long.
Now for the portals.
Now we take down the portals! Take them all down.
Welcome to Lord Sanguine's celebration, mortal. My lord requires you to perform a simple task. But have no fear, it will benefit us both.
Since your impressive feat in Vulkhel Guard, you're all the Queen can talk about.
The Pellingares are one of the most esteemed families in Wayrest. Or, they were, before today. They've a long history of lawmakers and politicians in their line. Such a waste.
Beat a champion and you become a champion.
Hah! I won five coins betting on you. Thanks!
Good luck out there! You'll need it.
What was that line again?
What can I pour you?
Some of the guards are willing to help us, but they need an excuse. If you search Bar-Neeus's stall, you might find illegal wares. My family would be in your debt.
I assure you. I have plenty of names. I just can't say most of them in polite company.
Ah, you again. You look terrible. Something wrong?
Everything's going to be fine. We're just very worried about the poor victims in the mine.\n\nDoes everyone have their salve?
Truly Kyne guided your steps. An achievement to be proud of!
My friend. It is good to see you again. You are welcome anytime.
Well, what do you say? What was the answer to my first riddle?
Almost wish I could take the trials myself. It's been too many years.
The gates are closed. And Tamriel is just a little bit safer.\n\nWhat do you say we put an end to Estre?
What am I going to do? They've been taken!
Listen to me, please! They've all been taken—Adelsar, Hara-Na, Varryn, even Captain Viveka. I can't go back there!
Gullveig would have sacrificed me as well, if not for your help.
She's encamped just outside of town. With her followers. Put them all down, for the good of the Pact.
You've too kind. I wouldn't dare go back to the Mages Guild without one of his books.\n\nMaybe two. With an autograph, please.
Thank you. I heard what you said and—thank you.
Haven't seen you around here before. Probably want to make yourself scarce. Town's got a plague. Bad one.
If you're here to help, speak to Sinien.
Did Urcelmo send you? It's about time they found someone.
Here to help? You'll want to speak to Sinien.
Leave me be.
Finish her. Show no mercy!
You were saying something? About not being here?
Go on. Go have a drink and sing for us.
Eh. I've seen better. But good enough for now.
Sorry friend. This area's off limits.
Don't listen to what that traitor said. Tell the Canonreeve!
What? What just happened?
Dirty work out there. Glad we have you on our side.
Did you strike a bargain with Deros and his crew? Did they rise to the bait?
Causing trouble, you dingy dung herder? Don't think you can scare me off so easily.\n\nI won't leave till that Redguard hands over what's due.
I've done all I can with Jorald's wound. I think he's going to be fine.\n\nWe'll set out to the Withered Tree soon. If you go to Riften, be sure to see Uncle Wilrek.
Find that cave yet? That's our only clue at this point.
Good luck, traveler. Stay well.
Stay well. You don't want what these folks have.
Those cultists were nasty pieces of work. Sure glad Harnald sent you along to help out!
That dragonshrine's always attracted a bad crowd. We'll keep a closer eye on it from now on.
The Peaks' scavengers will feast well tonight!
Kill that Daedroth, or we can't save the Walking City!
Tell me what you found.
Welcome. We're sending all newcomers to check in with Watch Captain Astanya. \n\nShe's on the docks. Southeast end of the city.
Welcome to Vulkhel Guard. All newcomers must check in with Watch Captain Astanya. You'll find her at the docks on the southeast end of the city.
Who are you, really? Are you here to save us?
Well? Did you find the plans?
Cadwell's a legend among the Soul Shriven. In Tamriel he was mocked and dismissed. Here, he's respected. \n\nHe's an odd duck, no question, but he knows all the secret paths of Coldharbour.
See what I have seen, traveler. See what the Divines have to show you.
Ssk! We are being overrun by a plague of dead giants, a curse of the Worm Cultists.
So much to do, so much to do. Excuse me, please. Can't let her down.
Good work.
Our friend here was too noisy. Had to have some fun with him. What did the Canonreeve's home yield?
Well? What's your answer? I hope the bodyguards aren't throwing you off. I know they're a little much.
You're quite the clever one. Well done.
Razum-dar wants to say that went pretty well. Then he remembers Fistalle, and her parents.
To allow <<1>> to come to harm would curse this village with the Green Lady's wrath. Please, do what you can to help find her.
At this point some of them will just get clapped in irons when they get back. Every minute slumming around in Vulkhel Guard is three gold off their pay!\n\nSome of them owe me money now!
Maormer back in the seas around Auridon. No thank you.
I suppose I really should be going now. It's just, Erronfaire's never treated me quite as nicely as spiced rum. And I like to keep myself among friends, if you know what I mean.
Fasarel and the others you've saved give you their thanks, stranger. I'll buy you a round when next we ….\n\nSheor take me. What is that stone you carry?
What? What is it? My guts, still roiling. Damn the sea, and that captain!
Please return as soon as you find <<1>>!
Raz must admit. Even he did not think we'd be seeing each other again so soon. How are you, my friend?
Please don't tell Harnald how much you did here. He'll never give me another mission if you do!
New in town, eh? If you're looking to get your feet wet, I have some work needs doing.
Go on ahead. I'll report to Two-Blades as soon as I'm able. Thank you again, my friend.
Please hurry, there isn't much time.
I'll return to Two-Blades when I can. Go on ahead. There may be more lives to save.
Please, master! Mercy on this poor wretch!
That creepy advisor from Mournhold says my father's missing. How is that possible? He's the House Councilor!
Quickly, go fetch Odvild. The poor woman is devastated. This will certainly lift her spirits.
Oh, fair day. Fair day to you. You're here with supplies for Telenger, I expect.\n\nPlease don't tell him I was sitting down on the job.
I know Cracktooth will come for me. I'm so helpless! What will I do?
Sorry, but I'm very busy. Please go see Breca at Fallowstone.
I think me and my boy can handle the rest of the chores. \n\nTruth to tell, I don't think you're cut out for farm work.
Thank Auri-El, a friendly face. You're Raz's cohort, aren't you?
I think the tomb is somewhere within these ice caves.
This is the best party I've been to all night!
Ysmir's beard, it's good to see a friendly face! I never thought I'd find my way out of here.
Ah, good. I was tired of only seeing dead people.
Eshaba has just about anything you could want. So. What can she get you?

The King and his parties. Today, three sloppy drunkards wandered into the crypts and haven't been heard from since. \n\nI'll wager a week's pay they'll unleash something unspeakable down here, and I'll get blamed. They always blame the priest.
Kill the matriarch and this all ends.
Could it be I made the wrong decision?
I can't believe you agreed with him!
Go, go! Let's get out of here.
So … it is the end. There's no saving myself after all.\n\nMy mother will never forgive me, but I don't regret saving our village. Perhaps I can save her as well.
We'll see that reinforcements reach Firsthold right away. You have the thanks of the Eagles, traveler.
I can hardly believe it—Estre, the Veiled Queen.
Good luck with that blade, my friend. Those Heritance bastards are yours.
I don't have words. Thank you so much for finding Ilara. What news of Tanion?
Hmm? Have you had a chance to look around yet?
It's about time. You're heavier than you look.
Greetings, citizen! I seem to have suffered a temporary setback. I require your assistance.
Please let me know if you find Recruit Gorak. He may be a little overzealous, but he means well. \n\nI think.

We should move on. The design of this altar … it points to the existence of others. There may be more ahead, waiting to be disassembled, and there are still Wood Orcs standing in our way.\n\nGo on ahead. We'll come to you when you find another altar.

Divines be praised, a friendly face! I've been hiding out here since the Covenant ambushed my team. They took three prisoners. \n\nI tracked them to a nearby camp. I'd rescue them myself, but there's a slight wrinkle ….
Finally, someone with a backbone.
Don't kill me! I'm just a soldier following orders!
They're going to throw me out of the Lion Guard now for sure.
Did Thragof send you? I don't know if we'd have lasted another night out in this cold!
Nurad knows nothing, sees nothing. Leave him be.
Remember: spellcasting all in the timing.
Here for the Trial of Endurance? This is a race around the island, mind. Not a casual stroll. Think you can handle it?
Start by looking for my runner, Lorumel. She might have learned something. \n\nWe'll be right behind you, soon as more blades show up. Good luck.
Thank Stendarr, a rescuer! You must help me! They're insane!
There is still much for you to learn.
She's just so glad to be out of that horrid place. Thank you. Thank you for what you did for Ilara.
You guessed the old man's riddles and ran a little race. Good for you. Ready for a real challenge?
Thank you for freeing me. It wasn't the choice I would have made, but I appreciate being able to see my son once more.\n\nI'll do everything I can to make this right.
If you go into the mines, please find my husband Len. I'm terribly worried about him.
I'm going to hurt you very badly.
I heard Dame Clarique let the bandit go into the village. She told us to keep a close watch on anything happening over there.\n\nI trust the Dame, but I hope we don't regret this.
The captain might've lost more than just his sight, but he's still a pirate at heart.
Senche-tigers often lie in the small cave near the falls. I often wonder what stories they tell their cubs.
Citizen.
Get that thing activated. Burn those boats. Save the town.
I had a feeling the truth would be bad. \n\nIt's a good thing Urcelmo took a small force with him on ahead. I'd hate for the Queen to have reached the city first. But Rilis. We'll need to warn him.
What a creepy place! I can feel something tugging at my mind.\n\nFind my brother and the scholars. And hurry! The spell might adapt and eventually trap us in here, too.
I try so hard to resist, but sometimes it's too much. It was easier when Gamirth was here to help me.

As I feared, we arrived in different locations. I am in a city of industry, where men speak of intrigues and plots beneath layers of innuendo and pleasantry.\n\nIt matters not. You have awakened once again and we must set you on your path.

The members of the Mages Guild compete in the battlegrounds, working with the sides that chose them. You have been granted the rare opportunity to choose your own side, which you must do soon if you wish to aid your friends.\n\nNow, make your decision.
Did Nelhilda tell you the plan? Did she make something to help us. Oh, tell me that this doomed celebration is finally coming to an end!
Oh dear. What is your type doing here? You smell awful. Truly awful. Get away from me, please.
Let's get back to it.
My poor father. Damn the Daedra!
I have a plan, but I need a crew. Congratulations. You're it. This will go much easier if you follow my orders and agree to do it my way.
I can't leave. I can't leave without it!
Look at it. Such terrible beauty.
People need to know about what's happening in the Serk!

I take it that you are the one who read my note? The spells I placed upon it alerted me that non-Daedra eyes examined the writing.\n\nI do hope that you are a member of the force from Tamriel. If so, I have something to show you.
My husband. I can't find my husband anywhere!
If you can, find my patrol first. They're directly east of here. Somewhere.
Can't a woman drink her mead in peace?
That silly, stupid boy. He's going to get himself killed in there.
Still a bit unsure about what has happened to us, to our little village. But perhaps I'll write a ballad about it one day.
You've chosen to side with us?\n\nIt was the right decision to make from a list with no good answer. Speak to Angof. You'll see.
Perhaps there is a way to use Thallik's offer of power to our advantage. This one will have to think about this a little more.
Thanks for getting me out of that library. I always tell Kireth to be careful and what happens? I'm the one who gets into trouble!\n\nMy sister's never going to let me hear the end of this.
I will find this city you speak of and seek you there. Just make sure you remember our agreement.

What an annoying development! The Observer changed the rules! On me!\n\nMy champion won, so I should be free. Instead, I'm in a cage, waiting for you to make a decision. Clearly, I am the logical choice. Select me and let's be done with this.

Lady Estre appeared. She said I should trust her. That I'd get out of here.\n\nI … I don't know what to believe, but her words comforted me, at least. That's something. I think I'll stick with her for now.
There you are. I was wondering when you were going to show up and rescue us.\n\nThe Observer has been so rude. And now he's put me in this cage! What shall I do in here all by myself?
I prayed to the Eight that more help would arrive. And here you are.
Your decision will allow the Hist tree to die with grace and dignity. Please, make An-Jeen-Sakka understand why you chose this path for us.
Don't bother my patrons. They're drinking.
Stay down and keep quiet. You'll reveal my position.
The berries I gave you should lure <<1>> to you, if she's still alive.\n\nPlease get her before the crocs do!
Good luck with <<1>>. He's a stubborn old Nord.
I hope <<1>> acts quickly. I could do with a good night's rest.
The runner's name is Lorumel. Seek her out. We'll be right behind you, soon as more blades show up. \n\nGood luck.
You did it, and just in time! The pirates outside the fort didn't notice our arrival.
An attack on the lighthouse? But why? That doesn't make any sense.\n\nLet me take a look at these plans.
I've begun to distribute the antidote. It will take time, but my people will heal.
Well done, my friend! <<1>> brought me what you found.
I … I don't know how to thank you. And I'm so sorry I insulted you. \n\nTruly, I'll never forget your kindness!
Thank you again for returning <<1>>. I've run into some unsavory types that would have … taken advantage of the situation.
My husband awaits you.\n\nHave no fear, I spoke on his behalf. He won't blame you for the death of his brother.
By Y'ffre's hairy feet, you outsiders just keep showing up!
I'm still not totally clear on what's going on, but I'll help Captain Eilram rally our troops.
Fires of Oblivion! These motherless slavers have captured my entire crew!\n\nI'm not one to shy away from a fight, but I think I may be in over my head.
I thought running an inn would be safer than sailing a merchant scow. And yet, pirates. Always pirates.
My contact has access to the Mages Guild. If you're not too late, you should find him inside.\n\nHe has a good nose for what you carry. If you don't find him, he'll find you.
Oh, hello. Who might you be? You have a familiar air about you, but I cannot place the face.
You said you'd bring proof of the mine's worth. You should get moving.
There's little time to stop <<1>>. With <<Ac:2>>, she could control everyone in <<3>>.
Just put your frog in the basket on the end there and they'll be entered in the next race.\n\nDon't forget to feed them, now!
The feral beasts ruined everything. I don't know how the Bosmer survive out in the wilderness like this. \n\nLike living in a war without purpose. Savages.
Too busy. Too busy tending Hopper to talk.
Just scoping out the competition. These amphibian idiots are no match for my Snooks.
What? You have no business with me. Begone!
Hey there, do you have a moment?
Been waiting for you. The boss sent me. Need to deal with this Heritance situation, now that you've put Estre in the ground.
This weapon won't forge itself, stranger. I don't have time for idle chatter.
Ah, the hero. What do you want?
I'll be fine. You take care of those bandits!
I don't know how long I'd have waited in that garden if you hadn't come along.
You found <<1>>. Splendid! Simply splendid.
<<1>> is impressed by Pact-soldier's talent and mercy. Now use the keystone to break through <<2>>'s defenses!
Don't get caught tainting their food; they won't appreciate it.
You can trust Count Hosni, you know. \n\nEspecially if you're one of his special friends.
Thank the Egg. You made it out too. I think Dracien's gone.

Bakkhara refuses to deal directly with the Orcs.\n\nWe should finish them and sort out the mess later. But she fears how the Thalmor will react if the Mages Guild raised a hand against the Canonreeve. Even if that Canonreeve is acting on her own.
I came here for the gold, but I can't stand here and not bask a little in the history.\n\nI've often wondered if the Dwemer ever expected they wouldn't be here today.
Search for the source of the failure. Use the control rod to spur the spider to act. It will do the rest!
Where's <<1>>? Have you seen my wife? You check inside the ship, and I'll sweep the beaches.\n\nIf he hurt her, I'll raise him from the dead so I can kill him again!
Dead archers are much less effective than live ones. Keep that in mind.
Shalidor found you! Good to see you again. I've deciphered the spell inside the book. Are you prepared for Sheogorath's first test?
An interesting task indeed.
I see the show does not always go on.
Nelanya and the Goblins taken care of in a single stroke. I've found quite the boon in you.\n\nWe'll handle things from here. You have my thanks.
Have we met? The two of you look familiar.\n\nNo, I'm fine, I can focus. I'll help the captain stick a cutlass in <<1>>'s throat. Both of them, if I have to.
Don't worry, dearie. Just hop back there and give them what they want. You'll get the hang of it.
Told you chief would say yes! No hurt Byz!
Thank the Green, reinforcements! Where are you coming from?
Try not to make too much of a mess.
Come on. Let's go find my sister. Leave Shazah alone too long and you'll find her curled up in a corner with a book.
Help me, please! They've stolen my Iriana.
I think I'll stay out here a while longer, since this is as close to him as I'll ever get.
I do beg your pardon, but would you happen to be amongst the living? Everything is so hazy.\n\nOh, I'm talking to another corpse, aren't I? Damn my ghostly eyes!
Quickly, my new friend. Speak to Khali. We're in agreement. The signs are all there. You may yourself have an important role to play in the Two-Moons Dance.
Throw that switch, please.
Great. A fan.\n\nI need you to keep quiet!
I fear Sir Hughes may already be too far gone. May the Eight watch over his soul.
Mother said this would happen. I can't do anything right.
Chief Tazgol is leading the Orcs toward Carzog's. He's determined to wipe the Bloodthorn Cult off Betnikh.
Ugh. Whatever she was doing felt like a giant hand crushing my skull! I could not have lasted much longer.
Here he comes. He has no idea, does he?
This is so exciting!
Not a bad look for you! The Drublog down by the waterfront won't notice a thing.\n\nYou'd better get moving while the magic's fresh.
The festival is so much fun!
You've brought the parts?
How's the wine downstairs? Did you find the special blend?
If we don't get those civilians out, they'll be sitting ducks for the Drublog.\n\nI've heard this particular Wood Orc clan likes nothing better than to torment the helpless.
Khajiit is flattered the Goblins would try to eat him.\n\nThanks.
My crew's safe and only a little bit tortured. I call that a win!
Looks like those four totems hold <<c:1>> captive. If my father told the truth, what you carry can disrupt them.\n\nI'll protect you any way I can, but I won't raise a hand against my own clan.
The future of the Drublog is uncertain. As my daughter always said, I must learn to think for myself.
I hoped we could duel.
Behold! You stand before the great one.
It's time to see how tough you really are.
You've done this before. Touching him should draw you into the dream.
There are no lies on the battlefield. Shall we find your truth?
Look for the entrance to Bloody Bhosek's dungeon beneath the palace. And watch your step.
If I smack you around too much, feel free to cry. I love it when they cry.
Now, answer my question. What are you doing here?
Do you think I'm an idiot? I just watched you give that moron his pouch of moon-sugar candy!
You're ready now? Wait. There's a giant over there!
Go kill the werewolf and get the bucket for Jill.
I really need that bucket.
Be careful, good-looking.
Do me a favor and keep the lucky pouch between you and me … yes?
Greetings, Champion.
I can't wait to tell my uncle I met you. Count At-Tura speaks very highly of you. \n\nGood luck in Gavaudon. Kill an ogre for Captain Ernele while you're out there!
Rama's family, so I'm sure you'll understand if I don't cooperate with his execution. \n\nJust, please—make it quick.
It's not over yet. Please, you have to win! They mean to feed me to these monstrosities!
What did you decide to do with the relic?
Thanks to you, we've actually got a chance to pull this off.
Destroy the relic, now! Didn't you hear the screams, as those things consumed the souls of my people?
It's in the box. You open it by moving the lid. You know, with your hands.
So you know about Nanwen.
Fancy a tune while you scrub the floors?
Ah my friend, come in and relax.
Khali … why? Damn that Javad Tharn to Oblivion!
I'm very glad you're in there keeping him out of trouble. I swear, sometimes I feel more a nursemaid than a scholar. Hah!
Go … Hallowed. Get her out of here.
Looks like the plan was a success. And Gloo said you helped to evacuate some of the villagers?
Go ahead. Light the crates. She'll talk.
Hey, there you are! I remembered what you weren't supposed to do. \n\nBut you still have both your hands, so obviously you didn't do it!
I knew Captain Kaleen would get another crew together! When she wants something, she gets it!
Again, sailors flock to the Spearhead. For this, Kasan is thankful.
The withered stalk flowers again. It is good to see you, alive and well.
We must stop the cultists before their efforts bear fruit, to the ruin of us all.
Ahh, good choice, partner. Your cunning has made us a lot of coin.
You would desecrate our relics for the sake of coin. You sicken me.
Milk Eyes is a kind old man. You will see. If he says there are rats, I'm sure there are rats. Be sure to tell him I say "bright moons."
Have you delivered the <<1>>s to the bar?
You've returned. What happened? Where is the Queen's agent?
Offerings to the gods are best made in a timely manner. Please hurry.
Be very careful how you speak to her, assistant. We're in her web. We need to tread lightly.
Keep your voice down. Tazia has no interest in slavery today, thank you.
What a rotten day.\n\nThe entire Merethic Society collection is stored in these ruins. And the Worm Cult gets to have their way with it all.
I just need to gather my strength and hobble back to town. Get that Goblin king and bring me his crown, if you can!
