It would seem that the Captain's concern for me was well founded.\n\nYou saved me from this assassin's blade, as well as from my own foolishness this day.
You have my thanks just for seeking that Rakhad. Shuzura thought him a noble Khajiit. But instead he is a snake in the grass.
Well done, very well done. Now take the circlet … and get ready.
This one hopes you can help Milk Eyes with his rat problem. Ezzag wants to find more than his old bones next time he goes for cards.
And what might you want?
I know I was bound for Daggerfall when my ship was attacked. I need to find a way there.
Can't hardly keep my eyes open. I hope I don't bleed out before I can get back to <<1>>.\n\nDid you find the plant?
If the Pact leaves us alone, they are welcome to Drakelowe Keep.
What's all this, then?
Seems we've you to thank for <<1>> and the lieutenant's return.\n\nJone and Jode shall dance with you, wherever you may roam!
If you choose to destroy the relic, then you've turned your back on me and the Covenant.
Thank you for your service. By the time you're done gathering those samples, I'll be back up in the camp. Look for me there.
Good day. This one is on royal business. If you will excuse …
You're back! I knew you'd make it.
This was part of a larger plan. I'm sure of it!
You're the one who discovered what the Bloodthorn are planning?\n\nI'm impressed. Now go help kill them.

When I heard my brother had fallen ill, I was extremely concerned. We've had troubles in Alcaire, but nothing this bad.

All the same, I'm glad to hear he's all right, and I understand I have you to thank for it.

Thank you.
Judging by that sickening smell, you got some of Zich's food.
Stay away from me, you foul beast.
Do you always fall for such sob stories?\n\nWell, I think it's a fool's errand, but be careful out there.
You've done well, but I need you to talk to <<1>> about getting more of the people on our side.
This is a disaster. The bastards were prepared for us.
I was a fool, an arrogant, overconfident fool. I should have listened to them all.
We're preparing to climb to the summit. Destroy the other Conduit Stones and meet us there.
Those damn Redguards! Showed up and made me move from the warm spot I had by the river!\n\nI may be poor, but a little respect would be nice.
These were the Five Companions, who set out from the Imperial City on an epic quest to recover the lost Amulet of Kings.
All of us feel the light of the Bright Moons on our faces with the Hallowed walking the halls of Do'Krin.
If I get turned into an undead monster, feel free to crush my skull. Seriously. I never want to be like that.
Tell me what you found.

Honor to you. Three keystones must be activated to unseal the entrance to the inner ruins of Moriseli. You'll find them ahead. \n\nBe cautious. The air reeks of foul necromancy. Powerful magic taints the very ground.
What's my brother talking about? How did he fail us? You need to talk some sense into him!

I wish this victory didn't feel so hollow. Other than keeping the undead at bay, it seems there's little we can do to battle this darkness.\n\nWe are here to support you and Indaenir though, if you need us. Are you going to rejoin him now?
I trust you will make wise decisions.

Hey friend. Care to have a drink? \n\nYou'll have to buy though. I'm flat broke. Can't even pay my debts. Have to go upstairs and tell S'rashi I don't have his money …. You think he'll have me killed?
Your defeat will honor the Seamount clan.
Come to try your luck with me?
I see Talmo's Aldmeri banner. I hoped you would destroy it.
The Bright Moons will guard your path!
If you do the hunting, I'll do the cooking. I promise you won't regret helping me beat <<1>>!
There's something moving in there. Help me get it open.
What a fortunitious event, meeting you here! I hope your hunting went well.
When I recover completely, I'll leave this place and start over.
I don't know what I'll do without that lute. I've been a musician since childhood.
Troubled times in Glenumbra, it seems. All I hear is bad news no matter where I turn.\n\nBut the worst, as far as I'm concerned, is poor Crosswych.
You're not considering keeping that thing, are you? It'd take all the fun out of war.
An intriguing place, the Valley of Blades. It'll be a treat to see where Sai Sahan trained as a boy.
This is a great moment! You will assist me in the study of this object, won't you?
Do you have the poison gas? Quickly now, give it to me.
First you appear out of nowhere, and now this! What are you anyway?
We'll hold here. Keep moving.
Continue on your path. We have your back.
We should get started with the clean-up as soon as possible.
The destructive act unleashes their corporeal form, yes? Untethers them from Nirn. The attunement Esan has put on the Fang draws forth power from that tether, harnesses it for our needs.
I really need those mushrooms. Five should do for now.
I meet you at last. I saw you defeat the scheming Redguard who rules Stros M'Kai. I see great events swirling about you.
So the fighting's over? I guess that means everything's back to normal now, right?\n\nNot for me.
I didn't expect an outsider to be of any help. I am indebted to you.
You have done it. All that remains is to claim the Claw.
You are a bright moon in Felari's sky. Thank you. You can find Nethrin recovering in the tavern. He's beside himself with worry.
Welcome aboard. I have interesting news. <<1>> has asked us for a favor. He has another problem he'd like us to resolve.
We … we did it. We walked the path and lived. I'm … I'm going to be the Mane. And my sister is dead.
The Dominion has never known a greater hero. And I am proud to call you a friend.
Your bravery astonishes me, Hallowed. To my ears this Path you walk sounds like some kind of nightmare.
Our thoughts are with you, Hallowed. May the Green guide your steps.
The hopes of my people go with you, Hallowed.
The wardstones surround the grove. They are powered by magicka.
Traveler! A moment if you please. I'm an … associate of Cariel's. Would you have a moment to assist me? My horse startled as we crossed the bridge, and I lost some important cargo over the side.
Three servants reunited to their master. Only one remains.
Well … that hurt ….
Move on down the river, friend. I'm mulling my next wager. There is much profit to be made at the arena!

If what Razum-dar says is true, the city of Woodhearth owes you a debt. Of course, if the city's attacked and destroyed, that won't be worth much. Maybe we can prevent that.\n\nThe cat said you found orders from Vicereeve Pelidil. Can I see them?
If you're leaving soon, I'd like to ask a favor of you.
If you are fortunate enough to actually speak to the Wilderking, I suggest you keep the conversation to yourself.\n\nOtherwise, people might think your brain's turned to peat moss.
I'm glad you're here. We were worried we'd missed our opportunity. The other scouts report that Fildgor's flank is undefended.
May the light of the Bright Moons wash you in their purity. May you bathe in moonlight, and let it suffuse your soul.
Who's there? I didn't kill your Dominion friends. I warned them, but they didn't listen.
Beat three of my hunters in duels and my axe is yours.

I wonder if you know how completely we are in your debt? Alik'r warriors fear no evil, but they will not fight the undead.\n\nIt may be a superstition, but it has been tradition for centuries. I could not have convinced my guards to break it today.
By the Eight, you've got one of the skulls! And you don't appear to have fallen under the spell …. \n\nLet me see it. Please!
His hunters? Ha! The Hunt-Wife better not hear him talking like that!
Something's wrong. He smells … very dead.
Not another one. Where does Garnikh find you suckers?
Yeah? I don't have all day.
We should head up to the gates to the keep. It won't hurt to check in on the King, though I doubt anyone without a key could get past those gates.

My hope is that Prince Azah might have a lead on where Uwafa and Alasan have set up their headquarters, or better yet, what they're planning next.\n\nRegardless, these are things we should discuss at the palace.
Those supply caches are the runners' only chance to reach help. We must get them stocked!
I know that many aren't happy you kept the relic, but you made the right decision.\n\nIf you're ever in trouble, you can call on my blade. I hope we get the chance to sail together again, my friend.
Move along. Don't you have somewhere to be?
Sithis? Here? That can't be ….
Hallowed, I can see the light of the Dance reflected in your eyes. Jone and Jode smile down upon you now. They are with you, at this difficult hour. You must choose.

As you've just seen, the young girl—Aranias—is associated with the Veiled Heritance. Until I know more about her, I hesitate to call her an enemy.\n\nI will have more insight soon though. Even now, Aranias is on her way to my throne.
I heard what she said. She's a good friend, Bowenas. Must be very hard for her.
What I propose is simple. A kind of limited partnership. Kill <<1>> and walk out of here with that boy Tand.
My life mate must have been sick with worry. I never thought I would see Sind again. This one doesn't deserve him.
This one begs your indulgence. He wonders if you have seen a flaxon-furred Khajiit with a braided mane in your travels?
Well met, friend. I don't suppose you have seen a male Khajiit wandering about? He has mane-braids like mine, and a foolish tendency to gamble until his pockets are empty.
I can see the benevolence of S'rendarr in your eyes. Thank you.
Let's see how tough your guardian is. Go to the stumps to pit your guardian against the others. You can use the stone to heals yours if you like.

So you commanded the general to turn around and fight on our behalf instead?\n\nI feel sorry for the spirits of his soldiers that they remain bound here, but at least you were able to free the villagers from the Shadow Wood.
You've returned! \n\nI hope you have fared better in your travels than I. For a moment I imagined you were a Daedric illusion. Rilis and his Daedric thrall have been a menace to me.
The hero of the caravan returns! Are you in for the next race? We have many fine and juicy lizards!
Ah, freedom at long last! My calculations suggested that you had a slightly better chance to fail rather than to succeed. I suspect, though, that you often beat the odds. Thank you.
Ah, look around you. See how the people brighten the streets with their very presence! It is good to have this place inhabited once again.
Admit it. You cannot resist the lure of the spikeball!
Find out what he wants. We need to get out of here!
There you are! Quick as you please. There's even time for tea.
With the Elder Scroll of Mnem in our hands once again, the Dominion is greatly strengthened.
Go. Go and find whoever did this to her. They must pay.
I hope that helmet does the trick. If that doesn't put her in a more reasonable state of mind, we may have to turn to a more forceful solution.
Ezreba awaits judgment. This one is ready to face the consequences of her actions. She hopes that mercy remains in the hearts of her neighbors.
I was very proud of this meal, too. Damned cultists.
Dancing elves, forest spirit kings … these people are pulling on the tail in more ways than one.\n\nYou can stay if you want to, but Hazazi thinks it is time for him to return to Marbruk.
You have better things to do than spend time talking to me, outsider.
Is that Captain Arakh's helmet? Well, return it to her already! She's about to rush us!
Our hero honors this humble arena! These troll fights are nothing compared to your fearsome battle with the great <<1>>. This one has already heard several tavern songs about it.
With the mist no longer claiming our hunters, Longhaven will thrive again, thanks to you. \n\nMake yourself at home! Doralin makes an excellent brew if you've the stomach for it.
<It appears that a gem would fit within the face of this statue.>

Well aren't you the bold one? Running around this part of the forest, you've got to be either fearless or just plain foolhardy.\n\nHaven't you seen the undead? I'm a Vinedusk Ranger and I'm not even sure I'm safe here.
<It appears that a gem would fit into the face of this statue.>
<It appears that a gem would fit into the face of this statue.>
The sight of their kinsmen's blood on your axe ought to loosen our prisoners' tongues.
Begone, pig child.
Even if the rest of the townsfolk don't want to think about it, having atronachs roaming about is bad news.
We've gathered the prisoners' belongings. A quick search may give you clues to what they know.\n\nMake these Bretons talk, Targoth, or the blood of your people is on your head.
It's hard to think of life in Greenhill without her, but I agree. The villagers cannot live with a traitor in their midst.
Been thinking. If I were bigger, waves would've smashed me even harder. Punctured lung, cracked skull?\n\nNever thought being this short would come in handy.
We'll make sure the Sea Vipers don't attack the Prowler. Make them suffer.
Gods be with you.
Lots of snakes out here. Watch your ankles.
You do see that I have a bow, don't you?
Back off. I don't have any interest in speaking to your kind.
I won't be able to sleep until that Dremora is dead.
It's done, isn't it? <<1>> is sealed inside with that monster.
We've restored the Mourning Stone. But if you're here, then <<1>> is lost to that monster.
The Sea Vipers are prowling around the beach, stealing our supplies. Do you know how hard we worked to liberate those crates from Covenant sloops?\n\nStinking fish-Elves.
This is rather disconcerting. I don't believe I've ever had a conversation with a monkey before.

I know going against Kaleen was a hard thing. It was for me as well. We have more history together than you can imagine.\n\nEven so, I'm leaving. It's time to start my own crew, sail my own ship. You, my friend, would be welcome with us anytime.

I wish I could have retrieved that Ayleid relic for study, but you were wise to destroy it rather than place it in Breton hands.\n\nI realize Kaleen disagrees with your decision, but never doubt it was the right one.

I know the others have doubts, but that's their problem.\n\nIf Captain Kaleen believes the power of that relic can be used for good, I do too. You did the right thing! When I see my brothers again, I'll tell them what you did for them.

By destroying the relic, you have saved the world from a great evil. Kasan's apprentice does not agree, but she has lost her way. This one can only hope she one day returns to the true path.\n\nGo safely, friend.
Don't hurt me. You can have the coin I've earned so far. For my debt.
You made it past the undead outside Marbruk? Either that, or I lost more blood than I thought.
My favorite traveler! The forest keep and protect you on your path.

Killing <<c:1>> was foolish. <<A:2>> and <<c:1>> shared a lifebond. She has little time to avenge him before she too will die, and <<c:2>> is a most dangerous creature.\n\nBut then, you have that spring in your stride again. What have you learned?
You recovered our eggs! How wonderful! My people will be most grateful to you for this.
Good luck in there. Hopefully, the Stonefire haven't been able to finish their ritual.
Bright moons guide you and watch over the Mane in his darkest hour.
I warned them. Warned them! But why would I know anything about Maormer treachery?\n\nMaybe now they'll listen to reason. It only takes a murder, right?
You heard <<1>>'s story. If the Sea Vipers call up another hurricane before the tide rises, the Prowler will be smashed to pieces.

Your pardon, friend. The Dominion's arrival on <<1>> has upset the locals. It falls on me to smooth the waters.\n\nPlease, help yourself to food or drink. I'm happy to speak with you once this matter is settled.
Even our worst enemies deserve respect. I admit, I'm glad to be proven wrong about Dominion justice.
Never thought I'd be so grateful to be cleaning the house. Hah.
I have some questions for this pompous lackwit of a vicereeve. Do let me know if you find any leads, won't you?
Stop her so I can kill her!

Balag welcomes you! If you are cunning of mind and fierce of spirit, Thizzrini Arena is the place to prove these things! \n\nAlso, Balag is running short of competitors. It is the downside to running fights to the death.
You again? Don't tell me you were serious about competing in the Sorcerer Division Championship. You'll be eaten alive!
You're a strong one, aren't you? Are you ready for a real challenge?
You still breathe, and your lovely face is intact. Zara is very pleased. And yet, she is also sad.
"Mysterious Stranger." I like the sound of that. Fight well and you could be the arena's next star!

I've never met the Wilderking, but I'm sure he wouldn't have created a bunch of monsters to indiscriminately kill innocent Bosmer. \n\nEither way, my people have sacrificed enough already. We're staying here, even if that means we do so as corpses.
Ah, the pain! It's exquisite! But this has to end.\n\nThe Great Mage must be made whole again so we can finish our mission!
Been a kwama master for over a decade. I'm not afraid to admit when I'm up to my neck in droppings, and I sure could use a hand getting out.
Have you seen <<1>>? He's missing.
Get off my ship before I throw you off.
<<1>> depends on the Great Tree, yet it sickens before my eyes. Our fates are like leaves in its branches.

You have now witnessed the first sacrifice, and you know that true honor need not be named.\n \nYou are now one of us. You are Ash'abah. We will recognize you as our brother and together, we will uphold the sacred duty of our tribe.
Come, let us see how the Wood Elves' council fared against my children.
What did my father say? Did you convince them?
Now is the time to strike. <<1>> must die for his crimes.
This is a dreadful place. Kargand appreciates your assistance.
We have to find the Engine. If we disable it, the ruins will be safe to explore.
This is horrible. The spirit wasn't any help. The Great Tree can't last much longer against the vapor!
Marimah says you are to become an Ash'abah, so I welcome you to our tribe.\n\nTrue honor need not be named.

Have you come to look over our books concerning the undead? Word has reached us that a blight has emerged from the waters surrounding the docks. I'm afraid our library doesn't contain any relevant literature, but please look over my other goods.
You are welcome to our camp. \n\nWe are usually generous hosts, but … under the circumstances, I hope you understand.
Hail and welcome, comrade. How goes the fight?
What did I ever do to that Netch?

The trial is over. <<1>> found my companions guilty and sentenced them to death. They were taken to the cells below the hall while preparations are made for the execution.\n\nI'm working on a distraction to cover our escape. Did you find the key?
He's got to be hiding it around here somewhere. I can smell it. Keep looking.
Oblivion's sake, another clueless jackass. I'm hung over and bored. What?
I find your antics to be quite enticing, little mortal!
The flame is lit! Before I fade forever, you must burn the tomes!
Damnable Daedric rituals. Just wait until I'm free.
You rescued me from a fate worse than death. I owe you, friend.
Marvelous, isn't it? We'll have to construct a special room for <<Ac:1>> when we bring it back to the Mages Guild.\n\nI'm sorry, did you need something?
They did not cover this in training.
We need your face to become familiar so your presence won't be questioned. Come, stay by my side.
Azsu will remember this. Oh, yes.
Ah, well. <<1>> bears no grudge, and wishes you luck in your endeavors.\n\nProvided they involve no more burning of books.
At ease, soldier. Fresh from the wreck? You've got a faraway look about you.\n\nIf you feel unwell, I'd suggest visiting <<1>>.
Clever, luring <<cm:1>> out of their mounds like that. A scheme worthy of Baan Dar, himself!\n\nThey're all gone, then?
Quick! Kill him!
Father burned in the fire, my brother missing … S'rendarr, show mercy!
This one found a sugar-rat you roasted. It was dipped in <<cm:1>> egg yolk. How was <<2>> to resist?\n\nSo delicious! But … so sleepy ….
Bright moons, you have saved Akkhuz-ri. Drove out the evil that was corrupting his soul. Thanks to you, Akkhuz-ri is free.
Hurry! Find the key and let us out of these damn cages, yes?
I never expected to have to do battle with Daedra! I rather enjoyed myself!
That was too close for comfort! I'm a conjurer, not a battle mage!\n\nAnyway, thanks for getting us out of those cages. I appreciate it.
This one must gather the strength to end Kargand's corruption.
You have given us much to consider, outsider. Please return to the Moonless Walk. We shall come to you after a decision has been reached.
You think the others were a challenge? Wait until you face Ishalga in the arena!
I asked around. Nobody from the shipwreck remembers seeing you before <<1>>.\n\nNo more lies! You're running skooma, aren't you?
Please, my family has seen enough pain today. Do what is right.
There's too many of the foul beasts! We can't get close to those focus stones.
Well done.
Good day, traveler. Mind yourself around these parts.
The Goddess watch over and keep you in your search. You seek four of Mara's treasures: a circlet, a dagger, a phylactery, and … of course … the chalice.
Damned Dremora are defending those stones. Already took out a few of our people. They'll pay for that! I promise you!
You must be the latest of Captain Balrook's playthings. You're certainly his type.
There is nothing like practice for perfecting one's skills, yes?
This one is at one with Jone and Jode.
It's too late to change our minds now. Destroy those binding totems and leave us to our work!
You've done it, Hallowed. The Champions have stepped onto their new path. And all that remains is to conclude the ritual.
Quickly, now! Your lives are on the line, too, you know.
Please. I honor your commitment to the Pact, but I have no more time for chat.
If you're done here, time to move along, warrior.
Now we must return to the Harvest Heart. There is one more thing to do before we can destroy Molag Bal's vile monstrosity.
Khali … she does not look so well. What happened in there?
Shazah doesn't look like her usual upbeat self. Is she all right?
I never expected that reversing the conduits would cause that poor creature to explode. Ah, well. Live and learn.\n\nThis door leads to the Great Mooring. We're almost there!
They can't do this! We've got to get rid of them!
I wonder if they will notice if I wrap this tree around myself and hide.
Have a seat by the fire and let me know when you're ready to hear the story. Remember, ask nicely.
What I wouldn't give to be having this meeting in Skyrim. It's hot as Dragon's breath in here.
If anyone can get to the bottom of this, it's you and Aelif. She's gone up to the roof of the Hall to get some air. Stendarr guard your steps, my friend.
I cannot believe we are still standing here! \n\nPlease, talk to Enneh and then let me know what he says. If he doesn't know where Casnar is, then we can call the wedding off!
This path is over, but the journey never ends. May the moons shine brightly on you in the future.
By the shining trees of Aldmeris. We have been burgled, but how?
Shh. Keep one good ear to the ground, always.
Hazazi never thought he would miss the dancing Bosmer.
Oh! Ah … greetings, traveler. What can I do for you?
What have you learned of my old friend, <<1>>?
Thank the gods you're here!
By the forest itself, I'm saved! Thank you. Did Nethrin send you?
The portal. It's unsealed? Praise the Divines. And Galandir? Is he all right?
Looks like we only meet in horrible places! Did you bring the hundred blades this time?\n\nNo matter. You didn't need them in Firsthold.
I've seen no sign of a forest spirit so far, ancient or otherwise. But there is, indeed, a powerful aura about this place.

I wasn't expecting open war out here, but that's what that was. Patraud never had a chance.\n\nI don't know what the Warlock has gotten us into, but I'll die fighting if I have to. I'm Redguard before I'm a Mage.
Warlock Carindon may trust you, but that doesn't mean I do. I've no desire to have my fate dictated by the likes of you.
This is difficult to behold, but if it saves another mage from harm, then I'll abide it.
The price of knowledge is always high, but I don't like the feel of this place. Mayhem awaits us, I think.
Don't worry, I'm not dead yet. Go on. I'll see you around.

This continued aggression from the Bosmer is distressing. With two mages lost already, we'll need to be careful. My fallen colleagues will not be forgotten.\n\nNo doubt our elusive forest spirit is nearby.
How dare you enter our gathering hall, you Crown dog! Go back to your own kennel for jackals!
You have a senche-tiger's heart coming here, Crown. But the bravery of a beast is rooted in folly. Leave now.
Forebear dog! Do not sully our carpets with your faithless heels. Leave now.
I'll … I'll see you back in Rawl'kha. Go … go now. Save Lorwen!
Welcome—it's good to have you come with us. You will not find that cup of fellowship in that Forebear Magistrate's hall.
Those are the items I seek! Give them to me, and I will learn their place in the story of my people.

I believe we must first destroy the focuses. Alasan's minions have been piling the dead around them so they can channel energy for the ritual.\n\nDestroy the focuses. Then go to the lighthouse and find a way to disrupt Alasan's ritual.
Ah good … you're here. Razum-dar was afraid he would have to bleed to death by himself.

Send another score and I will smite them just the same! I could cut down Sea Vipers all day long!\n\nWell done, my friend! We'll have the sanctuary back under control quickly now, but we can't stop here. The battle's only just begun!
My soul! They've taken my soul!

I'm glad there are a few of us left who know the meaning of courage and loyalty! You'd make High King Emeric proud.\n\nLook on the decks of the three ships. The designs should be there … unless they've already been stolen!
Her body must be consecrated, or the gods will know her not.
Have a seat by the fire and let me know when you're ready to hear the story. Remember, ask nicely.
Hurry up. I ain't getting any younger.
You have returned! This one hopes the visions were not too intense. Raz has heard stories.
It's good to finally meet you. I'm very happy we could be here to support Akkhuz-ri and the Champions. This is a vulnerable moment for our fragile new Dominion.
Good luck in there.
I have heard of your valor, though we have not met before. My Silvenar and I are well pleased that we could be here to support the Khajiiti people.
Green keep you. This is my first time on the borderlands of Valenwood. And my first time in a Khajiiti temple! I'm honored to be here today.
Some things are best left undisturbed.
Hey there mortal! How you doing?
The story now approaches its conclusion. There will be a reckoning for Aranias and for the Wilderking himself.\n\nYou must hasten to Greenheart, for you still have a key role to play.

If the Eldest has been corrupted, then everything in this area—every plant, every creature, and every person will soon become corrupted as well.\n\nI can't imagine how this blight can so easily penetrate the forest's protections.
Nnnn! It's … just barely holding together!
Quickly. Aranias waivers. She knows now why she was guided here—not to destroy the Valenwood, but to save it.\n\nShe wants to change course, but she's afraid. She's afraid to stand up to Andur.

It's you …? From Silatar? My … my friend. Thank the Eight! You were right about the Veiled Heritance. I'm sure now. \n\nThey used me as bait to trick the Wilderking, and now Andur's going to kill him. I can't let that happen. I have to stop Andur.
I saw you talking to <<1>>. I hope he's finally going to do something about these ruffians and thieves.
You've returned! Don't try to interfere. Pircalmo brought this on himself. Atronachs! In our wood!
I don't know what <<1>> plans to do about these bandits, but I hope he does it soon.
What's going on? Where's Pircalmo? Where's my husband?
Another damned bandit? Oblivion take you, I have no more supplies to give you, filth.
You look weary. Perhaps you'd care to stop here and rest? We have much to offer.
My dueling lessons have finally paid off. We made it down here with almost no trouble. Well, <<1>> helped a little.\n\nDid you find Lady Laurent's jewels?
You look so tense! You need to relax. Please, enjoy our hospitality and let all your worries slip away.
Did it work? Yes, I can see it in your eyes! Now you can see things as they really are.
I'm half a heartbeat from throwing you out of this camp.
What?

After you receive your briefings from Hahnin and Gabrielle, select a soldier to accompany you on your mission. Choose carefully, for our plan hinges on you opening the way into the Labyrinth.\n\nThis is our last strike. Make it count.

I have seen more than my fair share of years. Many more. But in all that time, I've never contemplated something as foolhardy as this.\n\nWe're about to face a Daedric Prince for the fate of our world, and I couldn't be more proud of all of you.
What are you waiting for? Kill that horrible creature already!
Welcome, Moon Hallowed. Welcome to your first steps along the path.

I'm a brilliant artificer and a genius when it comes to Dwemer constructs. But I have to tell you, being surrounded by all these remarkable men and women .… It's kind of humbling.\n\nI hope I live long enough to record this in my posterity journal.
This one cannot wait to see what's inside the stronghold of the Daedric Prince!\n\nBut Zur wishes that Gadris was here to share this auspicious occasion.

I imagined that this was going to be a grand adventure, but I never pictured the horror of all this.\n\nSo many of our friends and companions have died, and this damn vortex still threatens our world. I think it's time we shut it down. Permanently.

I see you there, but you must wait. A scholar's work is seldom urgent, but I have a request from the king himself. It seems the Ansei Wards have been misplaced! \n\nWait, I should not have …. Um, just forget I said that.
Hurry! If you take too long, these Ungodly might decide to kill me. Find those keys!
I'm afraid you'll have to pardon me. I'm here on royal business.
Don't talk to me. I have problems. Big problems.\n\nYou wouldn't understand.
We did it. It was an honor to fight beside you once again. We've certainly come a long way from the Temple of the Mourning Springs, don't you think?
How much gold did you take from my daughter's dowry? How full are your pockets, you snake?
Indaenir believes he can enter unharmed. And you as well. I pray he's right.
At last! Sai Sahan has been taken to the Halls of Torment!
Could it be true? Me. The Silvenar?

Now here's one who I know is loyal to the king! It's good to see you again, my friend.\n\nYou're going to find this hard to believe, but the damned Imperials are here! They've seized control of the city—for the moment, at least.
I'll be with you in a moment.
You're back! You stopped <<1>>, then?\n\nOh, no. <<2>> didn't survive, did she?
You keep returning like some kind of scale-rot. Leave me be, outsider.
Praise Meridia! This one was worried he'd never find another living soul in this horrible place.
She is wounded! Did you hurt her?
We have to find out what they're doing.
We've got some repairs to do on the Prowler, but maybe we'll sail together again soon. Until then, stay safe.
We should check the houses, or secluded areas with good visibility of the quay.
Survivors of the Sea Viper attack will likely have hidden. Perhaps the buildings around <<1>>?

I knew we could do it! We're practically on Molag Bal's doorstep now!\n\nMolag Grunda is no more. At least for now. Daedra don't really die, if my studies are correct. But at lease she's out of our way for now.
Tu'whacca has taken the Chief beyond the dunes. So passes Marimah—water into sand. May all the Divines bless his passage.

We mustn't dally. Naemon's Shade and his servants clearly have larger, darker designs. \n\nWe should spread out and search for signs of their corruption and do our best to stamp it out wherever we can.
I think … I think I just narrowly missed Tu'whacca's summons, sister. I credit my mother. She had a stomach like an iron kettle.
Still alive, are you? And all your limbs intact? Maybe you should spend more time adventuring and less time at the tavern. Ha!
The old Fighters Guild Hall. It's near the main gate. Go!
We were able to overcome the vampiric snare of the Orchard. I expect we'll handle the Reaver Citadel with equal aplomb.
We have come so far, but we have leagues to go before this business is concluded.\n\nWe must push forward! We must find a way through the walls of the fortified city that looms ahead of us.
As I was saying, there's a blight here. I'd highly advise staying away.

Thank you, traveler. The barkeep in the Waxing Crescent Inn … I think his name was Duzal-ja? He has one of them, and can probably tell you where to look for the others. We have to get the relics back before Meldil makes an appearance.

Phenomenal. I knew proximity was the key! And look at you, not even a hint of electrocution.\n\nYou have the principle. Now, to apply it to the other <<m:1>> before … well, best not to worry you about that.
I know why you originally came here—to ask for the Wilderking's allegiance to the Aldmeri Dominion—to know the Valenwood was on your side.\n\nWould you still make such a request to me now?
I can't believe <<1>> let me stay like this. Come, let's help the old bones drive back the new!
We're almost free! Only one task remains.\n\nYou must die.
I already told you—I'm not going anywhere!\n\nThe Taskmasters in this place … they can inflict pain that should kill—but doesn't. I will not risk getting strung up by them! Not even to escape!
I didn't think we'd survive this day. Many have died, but some live.\n\nThank you for fighting on our behalf.
You've returned, and this one heard fighting.\n\nCould … Taskmaster be dead?
The Eight take this thing! Everyone's going to think I'm a thief. An incompetent thief!
Auri-El watch over you. Maybe just tell Malesse my Tacia is adopted? And that I don't want her to feel unwelcome here? I don't know. I don't understand that woman.
Welcome, welcome. We have … lots of interesting people here. Like the merchant, Sarolion. He's certainly got a story or two.
I'm the operations manager for the Summoner Division. I assume you've earned your credentials?
Drauginor's the name. Business manager for the Sorcerer Division. Credentials, please.
Zara's tasked me with picking flowers, believe that? I'm a swordsman, not a flower girl! \n\nDamn my tongue, I can't say no to that girl. It's that purr of hers. Damned distracting.
I see you were successful.
We all saw the corruption draw back. It's such a relief.
This one is relieved to see such estimable help arrive. Raz has already volunteered to enter Hectahame himself, but the queen has forbidden it.
Quite an amazing scene to witness.

It's good to see Akkhuz-ri made it out safe and sound. Gharesh-ri tried to warn him of the danger, but he doesn't always listen. He sometimes forgets he's a spiritual leader and not a hardened warrior.
Shazah has never witnessed such a scene. Kauzanabi-jo thought this experience dangerous, but the history this one has learned. Shazah's sister may disagree, but the trip was well worth it.
Khali wanted to be there, but Lord Gharesh-ri and Kauzanabi-jo wouldn't have it. How does one expand her horizons if no one allows Khali to test her skills?
To be trapped outside these walls while the Veiled Heritance destroys more lives.
It's amazing. I can't believe I witnessed the choosing of the Silvenar!
You've proven yourself a valuable member of the Aldmeri Dominion.
Thank the Eight you returned.
I see Elolir is with you. Keep him safe. He's a decent shot, but he's a fool.
Take those Daedra apart. We'll make sure the barricade stays up.\n\nAnd take care of Laeneval, will you? She's the last healer we have.
You have accomplished a heroic feat today, but there is more to be done.
I suggest we search for survivors. In these situations most people will try to stay hidden. Perhaps the buildings will yield results.
Back, are you? It's your funeral. \n\nI knew you couldn't be trusted. Now I get to take it out of your hide.
Caldien ….
I'll say a prayer to Y'ffre for my fallen brothers. I hope they'll forgive me for my corwardice. \n\nThank you once again, traveler.

Mara's grace! The humiliation of being rescued twice … it makes me doubt all the training I received as heir to the throne.\n\nYou must retrieve the wards and quickly. If my father hears I had one and lost it, he'd pack me off to the Fighters Guild!
They'll come for me soon, and who'll miss me? No one but the rats, I tell you. No one but the rats.\n\nThey'll come for you too, if you're not careful.
So? Did you convince them? Oh, don't tell me! Talk to Vanus!
You shouldn't be here, traveler.
Is this your land? No? Then leave.
On your way, outsider. You'll never belong here.
Fish aren't for sale. Go catch your own.
The fortress up ahead, they call it the Reaver Citadel. If the Daedra were going for imposing, they damned well succeeded.
My old chum. My bosom companion. My comrade in arms. How long has it been? I've missed you, terribly!\n\nBy the way, what took you so long? The King is upstairs. He wants to speak to you.
You return. What have you experienced since last we met?
I'm worried sick about Erinel. I can only pray that whoever hired her kidnappers only wishes to stop the wedding and not worse!
Shall we go and have a proper visit? I'm sure Grunda's prepared something lovely, just for the occasion.
My old life is over. I'll miss Laurosse, but these are my people now. I can't just abandon them.
I wish I hadn't run. I'm not a fighter, not like Halalin and Nielas.
You? Who are you?
Still alive. Good.

Hectahame. Lovely isn't it? Especially with its moat of undead and eerily corrupted trees. As much as I know you want to take a peek inside, as long as those wards are up, no one is going anywhere near it.
Has the storm stopped? I don't think I've ever been this sick.
That is all for now. If we have need of you in the future, do not doubt this one will find you.
I'm quite busy at the moment, sorry. I'll be lucky if this haul allows me to keep myself fed, much less pay off my debts. Please leave me to my work.
Did you find out who the Artisan is?
I, Nidras, the Artisan, acknowledge that you rightfully stole my letters, and in exchange for their return, I'll tell you their story.
Hello, hello! This one has tasty foods for the hungry. What can Duzal get you?
Excuse me, sorry. I'm waiting for someone here. Someone who's trying my very last nerve.
Thank you for helping Manthir see how much he loves me. You are the best!

There's more to be done, though. Always is, isn't there?\n\nPrince Azah's here. He says they've tracked down the third Ansei Ward, and he wants you to join him as soon as possible at the Motalion Necropolis.
I am certain things will return to normal again soon, and these spiders will leave us.\n\nThey will leave, won't they?
You should've taken the gold.
Yenadar, gone to preach in a High Elf city. Kala is beside herself. Thank you for telling her. This one must arrange passage to the port of Haven at once!
Leave me. I have much to consider.
Apologies, but I must speak to my troops.
Give me a moment to cool down. Talking to those two makes my blood boil.
Don't bring any trouble to <<1>>.
Is there any reason you've chosen to interrupt my thoughts?\n\nIf so, make it quick. If not, begone.
Valencia wants me to keep playing. So I will. I'll make her proud.
Remove yourself from my presence. You've the stink of this place about you.\n\nI already can't stand to be here. I don't need … you people clinging to me.
Join the games or join the revelry, sooner or later you'll be back here with a thirst! I just know it. \n\nWhy not load up now?

The walker is five-clawed after all. Five-clawed, sleek, and fragrant indeed. What will you do, blood-scarred victor? Become drunk and fat?\n\nThis one hopes not. This one would see you hunt this arena ever more fiercely. It was … an inspiring sight.
This one … feels odd.

So the Veiled Heritance have emerged again in Woodhearth. I see Pelidil and his treachery at the center of this, and once again, you have thwarted his plot. Well done.\n\nNever mind how this news came to me. My ears now spread throughout Greenshade.
We will never forget how you helped bring peace back to our village.
Please, it wasn't me. How could it be me? I'm a Khajiit. Only Wood Elves can break the Green Pact!
Please take the convicted to judgment, advocate. The wound cannot heal until the burr is removed.
Oh! Hello there. Surprised to see me? So am I, so am I. I do get around, don't I? Haven't the foggiest idea how I do that, quite honestly.
Excellent. Well done. A fantastic experiment, if I do say so myself.
We … we did it. We walked the path and lived. I'm … I'm going to be the Mane. And my sister is dead.
Khalima's life would be unbearable without us.
Get down there and man those ballistae, or that serpent will sink us for sure!
<<1>> has you running all over <<c:2>>. Better you than me.
I heard <<1>> allowed you inside <<c:2>>. Stay on your toes, citizen.
Don't stamp all over the mammoth's tracks! And stand downwind!
Damn troll. Got away again. Impossible to kill. You really got yourself in it this time Ledronor.
The Worm Cultists haven't bothered me in some time. I suppose I have you to thank.\n\nWait, what happened to <<1>>?

The captain's concerned about <<1>>. She should be! But I spend a lot of time in the crow's nest, so I always try to know what's ahead of me.\n\nI last saw <<2>> and <<3>> near <<Az:4>>. They may know more about <<5>>'s plans. Neither are mutineers.

So Spinner Eranas was guilty after all. Don't think I'm happy to be proved right. The Spinner's job is to uphold our traditions and pass on our culture to the young. For him to violate the Green Pact … it will take our clan a long time to recover.
The local Altmer still disapprove of our marriage. Quertasse paid someone to steal my censer out of spite. I'm just glad I have Erinel.
I knew it. Gathiel always considered herself above our traditions. A poor match for a Spinner. She deserves what she gets for bringing doom to our village.
Stupid wasp. It keeps getting away from me!
Glaras has been one of Brackenleaf's Briars longer than any of us. She meditates in her tree home, among the trophies of past hunts.

Don't be alarmed if the world around you seems to change. It's a property of the Falinesti Peeper to reveal the true nature of the forest.\n\nBut be careful, the true nature of the forest can be deadly.
By the Divines, look at these poor souls. I'll bet they were in line to become undead.\n\nYou and Yahyif go on ahead, find the Master. I'll see if I can get these people some help.
Gedric knows what he's doing. We should press on for Pellingare.
This is the second time I've lost them.

Oh ho. Now, you have seen how the roles of hunter and hunted are interchangeable. You have stalked your prey and confronted your predator.\n\nYou are almost ready to become a Briar. One last trial remains.
Things are really moving fast now. Further on and further in. \n\nI'm ready. A little scared. But ready.

I see the time has come. We must climb this Endless Stair and pray we can stop the Planemeld.\n\nI hope this ends better than my soul-meld fiasco. I'd hate for either Nirn or Coldharbour to survive only to see the other destroyed. Just like poor Zur.

This is truly an honor for me! I don't know what to say. I hope  <<1>> got to hear the news!\n\nPlease help protect the village now. I'm no longer allowed to leave <<A:2>> while I learn from the old caretaker.
Their main camp is south of this cavern. They've been pouring in that way! Go!
I hate to be the one to say it, but that poor, lovely creature has to die. It's the only way she'll listen to reason.
How could Nadafa do this to me? And with a monster, no less! Oh, this is such terrible news!
Tharn has requested to speak with you.
The vein in Tharn's forehead looks like it's about to pop. You better see what he wants.
Tharn would like to hiss in your ear. Beware that snake's venom.

Getting all chummy with Titanborn? I enjoy the company of clever, well informed people. You really should try it some time.\n\nSo, you felled the great Mannimarco. Well played. You've done the Empire a great service.

Fate has dealt us a cruel hand, my brother. I agree with you. Father would not want us to flee our home, but do we dishonor ourselves?\n\nTo kill him would mean exile, but … I am willing to do this if you command.
It's a pleasure to speak with another knowledge-seeker. Guildmaster Vanus will be pleased!
The Elder Scroll of Chim has returned. This blasphemy must not be allowed again!

Sameer, I beseech you. Let us be gone from this dark place. You must not harm your father's corpse, even in self-defense.\n\nIf you choose to do this, I cannot stand up for you. You will forfeit your title, and you will be exiled!
I can feel the presence of my ancestors whenever I come here. I am burdened with a great responsibility to honor their sacrifice and uphold their legacy.
Please don't disturb <<1>>. He needs to rest, especially after all that's happened here.
Excellent! I know we'll all be drawing blades together soon enough.\n\nNow, what can I tell you?

Crestshade was such a quiet town, until that terrible Reezal-Jul arrived.\n\nPlease, if you haven't already found them, seek out Tharlas and Jonne. Find our personal items. Then maybe we can end this nightmare.
Jone and Jode look down upon us. Bask in that light, that your soul might join them on the path. Zaddo can tell you where you next should go. Where the paths of moonlight lead you.
The moons speak to Saifa. They tell her of your journey.
Traveler. I've got some information here you might find interesting. Someone of your prowess should be able to make a difference.
These shrines are sacred, please show some respect.
If you're looking to join the Briars you should speak with Glaras. Just head up to the top of the tree, you'll find her there.
<<1>> is pacing around again, playing his flute. How can anyone like an instrument that makes such a high pitched sound?
The Elder Scroll of Ni-Mohk must be recovered. It cannot remain in enemy hands!

That <<z:1>> is the only thing of note we've found. There's no end of trouble since we pulled it from the ruin.\n\nIt's not dangerous, not directly. What I mean to say is that holding it won't rot your hand off. At least, not immediately.
I heard about this place when I was a prisoner in Coldharbour. It's a living nightmare. Be ready for anything.
I heard stories about this foul place during my time in Coldharbour. Chilling. I might have become a permanent resident, were it not for your timely rescue.
The portal will deliver you into the Halls of Torment. Find Sai Sahan and bring him out. He is our last, best hope if we are to locate the Amulet of Kings.
No … please, you can't make me be a monster again!
I was foolish. I tried to convince myself that I was keeping the Pact, that my actions wouldn't catch up with me.\n\nI'm sorry. At least Gathiel lives.
Don't you understand? I was dying! That plant was my salvation. You would've done the same!

Poor Lleraya. I had hoped to find a way to bring her back from the brink of madness, but it was not meant to be.\n\nI will not be blinded by sentiment when it comes to Baron Montclair. No. To save Rivenspire, we have only one course left before us.
Again, you trouble me at a critical juncture? What must I do to hasten your departure?

My brother and I might be a bit out of our league, but we'll find a way to help.\n\nWe've explored enough Dwarven ruins and dungeons to fill a hundred lore books. How much different could Molag Bal's Labyrinth be?

I can't imagine what Eranas will do. He spent so much time caring for Gathiel, you know? But, the Green Pact is appeased and we can go back to our lives. Thank you for that.\n\nIf you're hungry, the meat was untouched! So we could trade, if you like.
I can't believe Gathiel did that. She knew that it would violate the Green Pact. She knew there would be consequences.
The time for words is over. Go, now!
Don't stop now! We'll take care of things here.
No time for words now! Get moving!
The time is at hand. Stop second-guessing yourself, stop questioning your resolve, just stand up and do it. You're ready.
It kills to know Gathiel's gone. And poor Eranas. I can't imagine what he's going through—to nearly lose her to that illness, and then this happens.
So Gathiel's gone, I see. I see ….\n\nYou know what this means, don't you? The torchbugs. They're listening to us through the torchbugs.
Huh. Well, I guess she was sick anyway. One of those situations where the forest reclaims its own, I suppose.
<A quiet stillness hangs over the shrine, but you feel a sense of anticipation.>
You won't escape! You'll die in here, like the others!
So? Where are the other survivors? Adusa doesn't see them, so that means you need to get back to the looking, yes?
You should leave before the curse gets you too.
I feel horrible. My mouth tastes like ash and dirt.
Ugh, kill me. Just end it all.
I've never felt this bad. Never.
We will meet with Kasura as soon as I am well enough to travel.

Z'en's price! I knew if I banged on this door long enough someone would come.\n\nNever dreamed it'd be another Tree-Sapper, though. I'd ask how you ended up here, but I got more pressing matters. Can you spring me before the trolls come back?
I'm not sure how we managed to survive. It was so horrible. But since we're still alive, maybe there's some hope left in Moira after all. Maybe there are others out there.
You came back? All right, let's try that again.
This great time of unrest within the Guild is at an end. You've done very well, comrade.
I hear things, deep inside my mind. Voices. Sounds. I don't want to listen! Make it stop!
Are you sure this place is safe? And who's the strange Khajiit lady? Oh, I feel faint!
Janeve … my sister …. Reezal-Jul afflicted her with his blood-curse. She's becoming a … a vampire.\n\nVampires are evil. Totally, utterly evil. But by Arkay, this is my sister!
Turn back, citizen. <<1>> is … I don't know what to call it, exactly.

I don't remember how I came to be here in this cell. When I woke you were just standing there, foaming at the mouth.\n\nCount yourself lucky that <<1>> had no desire to treat you like a puppet. Unlike myself.
I can never decide between Choice and Free Will. Which will triumph in the end? But why not settle the matter for me?\n\nOr you could yank a lever, but that's hardly fun for either of us.
I'm sorry I missed being able to shove my blade deep into <<1>>. I was kind of looking forward to that.\n\nI'll make sure Captain Janeve gets the same training I received. It's the least I can do.
Rest easy, Vestige. We've come a long way, but there is more yet before us. Molag Bal must be thwarted. The Planemeld must be stopped.
Honor and faith to you, my friend. Kasura sends her regards. She is recovering quickly, and reconstruction on the Abbey of Blades has already begun.
I'm right behind you. Let's go get that amulet!
Place the stone on <<1>>'s forehead. Every second that beast is free is one she might use to escape!
The Empire collapses and the Gray Vipers flourish. The first is beyond our ability to fix, but we can do much about the second.
You have accepted a contract. The guild expects you to fulfill it.
Personally, I like to crush bandits' skulls with a warhammer. However you do it, kill as many of them as you can.
You are angry. It is to be expected.
Well, that was a deeply unpleasant experience.
Now that I'm safe, I'd prefer to keep it that way. If it isn't too much trouble, could we please hurry up and get out of here?
It is good to see you again. And I do see you, in my own way. You are a wound in time, a tear in reality that shouldn't exist and cannot long endure.
We're going to try to put this behind us. To start over. But we'll never forget the friends and family we lost. Never.
Sometimes it feels like these cultists really are worms. When you slice them to pieces, you just wind up with more of them!
Mannimarco is aware of our presence. We need to find the ring and leave this place.
He promised me again and again. And, fool that I am, I believed him—again and again.\n\nI will never meet another like him. Perhaps it is better that way.
Welcome back, my friend.
I'm pleased that you are still willing to work with me, Vestige. I hope to make amends for my part in all this.
You tear away the Architect's legion like weeds.\n\nThe Harvester that possesses my soul waits just across this bridge.
I think I heard something! If those monsters return, I'll give them what for!
Please, leave me some room to treat the injured here.\n\nNot to be rude - bad circumstances for a chat, that's all.

A Breton—what was I thinking? I should've known a pretty little Breton lady wasn't interested in me!\n\nIt was just that we had so much in common. She was quiet, she wanted to be a mage … but it was all a lie! Now I'll be kicked out of the Guild!
I wish I could join you, but … with all those frost trolls, I'd only hold you back.\n\nYou be careful in that cave, would you?
So the Emerald Chalice turns ordinary people into green Goblins? Remarkable!

Rashan will show you how you can be of assistance.\n\nDo not be mistaken though, outsider. If you take any action to harm what little nature remains uncorrupted here, she will go straight for your throat.

Who would have guessed it would be an outsider who would show up and kill Uela?\n\nI doubt this means we'll start inviting families from Evermore out to visit, but maybe, just maybe, we can be a little more friendly.
You travel with <<1>>? He has proven himself a friend to the Falinesti Faithful.\n\nThere are questions written upon your faces. What is it you seek?

Pox on it! I would've given my axe to have been there when you gave that head to Captain Hjurrun! \n\nI heard his jaw just about hit the ground. You've given me a good laugh, friend, and a little bit of hope too.

Ah, the queen's champion! Honor to meet you. Means we're that much closer to getting paid. That's good, because I didn't come to Evermore for the women.\n\nAre you ready then? As long as you're good with the plan, this thing's going to be a breeze.

Hi there. Queen Arzhela told me about all you did for the city. Sounds like they should be building a statue.\n\nAnyways, compared to what you've already dealt with, this should be a cinch. Really, our part only comes into play if there's a problem.
He took the Walking City? He took my home?\n\nOr is this another of his lies?
The crypt is to the east, at the top of the stair. Come.
What? Follow me. We'll talk when we reach the … gah … safe spot.
All that's left is to face the Architect. He's defended and he's powerful, but he can be defeated ….\n\nYou've made miracles happen today, my friend.
Speak to Rashan.

I must admit, I'm not comfortable with this little jaunt. Sancre Tor is in the mountains of Colovia, and Colovians are the worst kind of Imperials—backwards mountain men without any sense of decorum. At least Varen will feel right at home.
This is absurd!
I barely made it out of there alive. Those things. They're like nothing I've ever seen.
Another one? Curious. What do you want?
I did what needed to be done. Isabeth knew this. Let's hope her father can open his eyes.
This is Denille's last hope. If this fails, the worst is inevitable.
For the love of Mara, I didn't think I'd see the end of this day. Did Captain Gaercroft, my father, send you?
We couldn't stop those monsters. I fear that soon all of Rivenspire may be lost!
So this trip turned out to be far shorter and far more fortuitous than I expected.\n\nThat's assuming you're up to the challenge, of course.
I guess it's a good thing we gave the bows to Baandari after all.
I deserve to suffer. All those lives ruined because of my petty need for vengeance. I deserve worse. Leave me be.
You convinced Knight Commander Cheryline to give up the bows? If I had asked her, she wouldn't even have spared me a wooden dagger. \n\nShe must really like you!
You saw the thief, yes? Or smelled him, perhaps? He was quite filthy. This one will be scrubbing the stench of him out of his clothes for a week, at least!
I'm sorry we can't chat for long. I'm waiting for someone.
The information you have obtained for us is invaluable.\n\nGo. Do what you must. And be certain that we will do the same.
The Fevered Mews … I haven't thought about that place since I was a child.
Quite the haul for your first day. You don't do anything half way, do you?
Well, all's well that end's well, right? Except for the real mystery—who in Northpoint was pulling Leonce's strings? And why?\n\nI don't think I'll sleep well until that gets resolved.

Speak of Sheogorath! You've caused quite a stir! Merchants speak of a black wind robbing them blind! Your open hand is blessed on every street corner!\n\nIf you were looking to make an impression, you have!
I remember now. The translation—we misinterpreted it. We assumed the Crag housed a powerful healing artifact. But we were wrong.\n\nThe hillside community, though. Why didn't I ever look into that?

When you went below into the crypts this foul icy fog rolled in. The earth shook and those Dolmen emerged from the ground beneath our feet. \n\nWe retreated here to await your return, the rest you can clearly see.
Hungry … so hungry. A sweetcake would be nice. Candied mammoth tail swimming in sparkle-syrup. Honeyfly bisque over a comb the size of my head … oh, I can almost taste it!
You look like someone who cares about the health of a community. We need more people like you in these troubled times.
Smells good. Maybe, if I wait, they share.
Back of the line, bug nose! I was here first!

There was a time this place was nothin' but a game trail, if you believe it. Blacksaps used to ambush old coins not familiar with the Valenwood.\n\nThat's where I came in. Know these woods like the back of my hand. Blacksaps never saw us comin'.
If we can't get the information we need, we may be better off barricading Evermore completely and preparing for siege.\n\nIf you can help, please speak with Captain Gaercroft. We need it.
He sleeps now, thank S'rendarr.

You're such a good person! I know that Puddles will be home in no time now that you're out there looking for her.\n\nI could see it in her eyes when we arrived. Puddles really wanted to go out and explore this new city. She's very curious, you know.
This place, it speaks to me. It whispers in my ear, sings into my soul. It runs through my blood like cold fire. \n\nBut none of that matters. When we save Leila, it will all be worth it.
Don't mind Wylon. He's just angry that the shard's effects faded away. He knows you didn't mean for this to happen to me, Verandis.
Looks like you've made your introductions. Time to get to work.
We should honor who the prince was in his life, not the abomination he became in death.\n\nI will leave you to your mourning.
Ah! If it isn't the five-clawed walker who saved our herbalists! Crazy Eye is very impressed!\n\nAre you here to help me fight these dungy Imperial dogs?
Hello, bloodkith! Heard you gutted some bandits in the attack.

You're going to the crypt, aren't you? If those churlish rats have raised Eamond, you strike him down. Don't hesitate. \n\nI loved my husband, but I'd rather see him burned than in that … state. Whatever happens, just make sure I don't see him.
We have enough trouble around here without the noble houses bickering among themselves.
This is no time for idle talk. We need to destroy the Fangs of Chaos to weaken the Dark Anchor!
Greetings, guild-sister. How may I help you?
Ah, my friend! Your return, it is well timed.\n\nFor some reason, Montclair's forces have attacked the castle. This one can't imagine why they would do such a thing.
Say the word and I'll open a portal to <<1>>. Once you pass through, it will seal behind you.\n\nIf you have anything to do before you leave, now is the time.

I do not understand why this inn is so popular with travelers. The beds are like rocks and the mead tastes like the sweat of a dog.\n\nI will not spend one night more here than is absolutely necessary.

Gold. Some people believe we're too obsessed with it, that it controls everything. But I think that's actually a good thing. \n\nHow else do we create a standard for the value of social and cultural exchange? Gold is the best way. It really is.
<<1>> and his sons rose against the rightful king of the Valenwood. This prison may not be the perfect solution, but it suits them better than a quick death.
<<<1>> wags his tail happily.>
Dark days are upon us, friend. Arkay's foes spread like wildfire. Only his holy relics can save us now.
Hail, traveler! Welcome to Evermore—Bangkorai's jewel of joy and plenty!
I'm surprised you made it. The Houses informed me of what took place in the Doomcrag. Most soldiers would have perished inside of there.\n\nYet here you stand. Commendable and respectable.
I've said all I'm going to say. We both know this isn't true justice. If your Dominion means what it says, you will give my family a public trial.
My patience wears thin. If this crisis has taught us anything, it's that a nation needs a single ruler. I just hope the High King sees that as well.
The time has come to crown a ruler of Rivenspire. The Light shines on us all, but a nation needs a single leader to look up to.
You draw ever closer. Graccus holds my book, the Oghma Infinium, in the ruins below.
Tough family, huh? Not sure it was his fault, exactly, but I've been known to do some crazy things for a woman.\n\nNever anything like this, though. I do have limits, you know.
Lyris has more to tell you, Vestige. Speak with her.
I've dealt with these Worm Cultists before. They use the darkest magic, and they don't fight fair. Be careful.
Good to see you again, my friend. Kazirra asked me to send her regards. Actually, she said something about the moons. You know how it goes.
What is the matter? You left before we could finish!
I'm sorry you had to witness that. I knew <<1>>'s citizens were zealous about the Green Pact, but sometimes they go hunting for trouble.
If you're looking to buy something, go inside and speak to Sabir. I'm sure he has what you need.
<<<1>> wags his tail happily.>
You're the last person I'd expected to see in this backwood. Or, at the least, it would be a wood if there were more trees.
Hallowed. It is good to finally put a face to all the tales I've heard.
Take care inside, Hallowed. This one remembers his cleansing. Many things from the past came to the fore, many old wounds re-opened. Stay close to the Champions, and keep them safe.
May Arkay's light guide you on your journey.
Hurry up and move into position. I'm getting antsy for some vampire slaying.
What are you doing? Go activate the blood fountain already.
I don't guess you've seen my friend, Garth, around, have you? Middling height, anxious-looking fellow, with a bit of a beer gut?
You've returned. What have you learned of the Khajiit Embassy?

I heard what you said to the king. <<1>>, a traitor; my wife's killer, a loyal servant; and I, <<2>>'s representative in <<3>>, required to thank you for your efforts.\n\nVery well. I'll provide no reason to question my duty to the Dominion.
My friend <<1>> has gone missing, and I'm worried he got himself into trouble inside the cave to the north.
Good luck in your battle. We will be with you in thought and spirit.
So, you're to kill Brinarch? Good. Tamriel will be better for it.
We're very close now, thanks to you.
My hunter. The scent of your success surrounds you.
Daedra take it! Gargoyle spit, and on my best breeches. Now let's see ….\n\nReally, this is quite revolting.
You're confident, I'll give you that. Strode right up to the king.
Meet us in Vulkhel Guard. We'll head there right away.\n\nAs soon as we finish our drinks.

I've received word that Northpoint has been liberated and we march now to face Montclair himself in the Doomcrag.\n\nI know that between you and Verandis we can stop the baron's evil plan before it spreads any further. Gods be with you, my friend.

Every night since the massacre, I've dreamt of the horrors the Jade Butcher brought to <<1>>. It seems fitting to meet the one who brought her to justice on the very spot she slew the Blacksap.\n\nI wonder, will I have nightmares of you?
Our farm … everything we owned. It's all gone.
All this time on the road … it's been hard. Makes me wish I had better boots, you know?
Thanks again. Now I can give the treethane his bow back. I'm a free Elf!\n\nTake care of yourself out there. <<1>> is a dangerous place, as <<2>> discovered.
Damn it. What went wrong? The vampire lord should have appeared by now. \n\nWhere are Zungarg and Agalir?
What happened to our family is terrible, but as the bards say, life goes on.\n\nMy sister and I came up here to … well, to give them a proper burial.
Why? Why did they have to leave us?
I think that Countess Tamrith and Baron Dorell both could be excellent rulers. The important thing is that we crown someone. And today must be the day.
Fear not, Vestige. When Sai Sahan and the others return, we will slip into the shadow of Sancre Tor and retrieve the Amulet of Kings.
Are you with the Vinedusk Rangers? The Justiciars? The Fighters Guild?\n\nIt doesn't matter. I know why you're here.
I don't understand …. How can I cook dinner now?
My brother … my Nedras. All this gold ….
I'll be better off without him. Yes. Now that I know he's not coming back, I can move on with my life. Better off without that stupid mule!
Yenadar, gone to preach in a High Elf city. Kala is beside herself. Thank you for telling her, traveler. This one must arrange passage to the port of Haven at once!
Please do not strike me. I am not with the Bitterhand. I am as a tree buried beneath the ground, stuck in darkness and doomed to die.\n\nI am not even a bandit … any more.

Well, kiss a troll and call me pumpkin! I know you! From Shornhelm! Did Baron Dorell send you?\n\nI was the Orc. In the cage. Not my most shining moment, but it's not like I'm a noble or anything. No matter. I'm just glad you're here.
Fortunately, I'm on the stealthy side. That's not Snaruga's way, though.\n\nThe old girl gave the Imperials too many black eyes. They dare not trust her with a pick!
No one seems to be asking where these Imperials are coming from. We're a long way from Cyrodiil. Something is amiss here.
Don't drag your feet. The slow hunter never catches his prey, and I can't keep this gateway open forever.
These Imperial dogs are vicious but smart. They know they can't beat us in a direct confrontation, so they starve us out. I'd like to compliment their commander before killing him.
It's good that you're here, my friend, though I'm afraid I may be dying ….
Imagine! The chance to see <<c:1>> operate.\n\nConservator <<2>> is preparing <<3>> as we speak.
<<1>> knew the dangers. What hubris, to do such a thing.
I've ruined everything ….
Good luck ….
Have you seen my husband, Najan? We should go to him.
Touch the symbol of Arkay. Profane the Forsaker.
Nothing to see here. Move along.

Heroes, gods, Imperials … who's in charge here? You. You've earned the blessings of the heroes, but blessings will only get you through the door.\n\nAre you really ready for what lies on the other side?
I must seek my fortune. And you must go elsewhere to seek yours.
You know, there were rumors that Ranser was betrayed by his chief military advisor, General Dathieu.\n\nIf Ranser was decapitated, that might suggest the rumors were true. How can we be sure, though?
Your kin live among the mortals. They may be wearing rags or crowns. They may hide within or rise above the masses.\n\nAs your Bloodspeaker found you, you must find them. They await.
Go on. Go find the rest of our assault team. I'll have this place all cozy like in no time!

The falls you seek are southwest of here, overlooking Gil-Var-Delle. Simply let some of the water from the vial fall at each crest, and the flow will carry it across Gil-Var-Delle so that the earth may drink and be cleansed.
Even with a single performer back on the job, I see smiling faces. I think we're starting to draw a crowd!\n\nWhatever you've been doing, keep doing it!
May Arkay drive back the darkness, forever more.
Oh! You took the shipment to <<1>>? And you don't smell like fungus and rotten meat … good work.
Any luck with the supplies? They should still be in <<1>>.
My you smell lovely … delightful. How delightful.
As soon as he gets home, I'm going to give my husband a piece of my mind. Edouard will be lucky if I don't throw him out after all this trouble.
I apologive profusely for the burden that escorting <<1>> surely inflicted upon you.\n\nI will safeguard him from here, so that he takes nothing of this place with him aside from stories.
I owe Ufa a favor, not you. Be on your way to do what you must. I'm sure I'll see you later at The Drowsy Owl Inn.
You saved her. Thank you. I don't know what I'd … never mind.

Ah yes, I recall you from before. You failed to find the relic I was hunting in the Alik'r. At least you didn't fail to find <<1>>.\n\nI don't suppose you'd be willing to help me find something else, just to prove you're not entirely inept?
An abandoned house. Lovely. One day, my dear, you'll need to take me somewhere nice.\n\nWell, let's go investigate.
That's an interesting story. If Naruk had Kaleen under duress, wouldn't she alert the guard? Now I'm curious.
Thank you. A find like this is incredibly rare. It could greatly advance our understanding of the Valenwood Ayleids and their unique dialect. I must begin translating immediately!
No. Don't tell me he's dead. He can't be.
Is that your friend? See to her. I'll watch your back.
I think I'm ready to swing a sword again.
Please. I need your help.

Can you believe this? The fool's turned himself into iron!\n\nIt's like a practical joke. I keep expecting my boss to step out from behind a rock and just tell me he wanted to see how I'd react. I'd carry the bastard if he wasn't so damn heavy.
Good meeting, walker! Do you have a moment? My business partner is in trouble and this one could use some aid.
Fascinating! And a bit intimidating.\n\nBut I suppose you could say that about much of Ayleid construction.
This is wonderful. After all these years … it's going to work, I know it.
<The Bounty board has a place for me to post my report.>
<The Bounty board has a place for me to post my report.>
<The Bounty board has a place for me to post my report.>
It is no small feat to take on an Imperial cohort. Mauloch must approve.
Wait! Please, stay your blade and listen.
Hello there. I suggest you don't try to pick me up. You'll only injure your back.\n\nDon't ask for any long-winded explanations either. It's tiring to talk when you're made of iron.
The tension between the locals and the Imperials makes it difficult to concentrate.
Hold it. You're not working for the Imperials are you?
<<1>> believes we Covenant troops require a symbol to rally behind, but he is mistaken. \n\nThe Old Tower is occupied by an Imperial Cohort. No stolen hat will change those odds.
I do not know if <<1>> will last much longer. \n\nBring him this thing he yearns for, that he may feel victory in his hands once more before embracing a warrior's death.

Halt there. Bangkorai Garrison is on lockdown since the death of King Eamond. Only Knights of Saint Pelin and members of the royal family are allowed in.\n\nAlso, if you were planning on going to Evermore, you might want to reconsider that.

It sounds archaic, but the Blacklight Raiders were well-rounded—warrior, cleric, thief, and mage.\n\nThe mage wrote a letter to one of the others telling how to open the lockbox. Between the letter and the gravestones, I hope we can solve it.
Any luck?
The Lady says you are one of the Undaunted. Welcome. Newcomers buy drinks.
The soldiers said I could fish for a while longer. You can ask them, they'll tell you I'm allowed here.
A soldier already told me to return to <<Ac:1>>. But let me fish a little longer, all right? I'll head back shortly.
All done, warrior?
Well met, friend. I've heard a lot about you!
This is hopeless! Baron Montclair forces me to mix concoctions that I know won't do any good.\n\nIf he'd just listen to me, I could show him exactly how to heal his wife and end her suffering.
Well scamp, you don't look any worse for wear. Maybe you should put the ale down every once in a while and pick up a sword. Hah!
How are you doing, milksop? Kill any big scary monsters this week?
They say it may take weeks for the performers to start their shows back up, but I am worried if I leave I'll miss it.
Off you go, then. Ta!
Ah, our magnanimous prince. Such a kind and noble ruler, don't you agree?

Fine, I stand corrected. You weren't just trying to trick me.\n\nYou've got my thanks, for whatever that's worth. Now that <<1>> is dead, the rest of us should be able to hold out until reinforcements arrive.
Your drunken exploits gave the bards much to work with. I think your battle with the giant will make a fine song. Still, I am sorry for this inconvenience.
Hurry, friend! Who knows what that mad Argonian is planning to do to poor Janeve.
Have you talked to Bumnog yet? He's got something important to tell you. About, you know, things.
Get after them. Make sure the harpies don't kill them before they've washed that stench off!
We will escort these men to our border. They are not as skilled as we were led to believe, and I'll be sure to let this be known.
Before you go in, I need to talk to you.
Can you talk to Bumnog? He's got something he really, really needs to say to you.
Ah. I almost feel sorry for him. Almost.
You better hurry. We need to get those hostages free as fast as possible.\n\nMeet me back in the center of town after you've taken care of things.

Welcome to Fell's Run. Normally we'd welcome you with open arms and throw a feast, but not this year.\n\nWe had a terrible harvest, and times are hard. Might be better if you moved on and spent the night in Northpoint. Come back next year.
What in Oblivion do you want? \n\nUnless you can haul it yourself, don't tell me you have a load of grain that needs to be ground at the mill. The constable's deputy just confiscated my damn wagon.
So we're going to live? I thought those men were going to kill us!

So here we are. The moment of truth. I can now look upon the face of the one who will be my judge. \n\nI hope you understand that I am in no way trying to deny my past wrongdoings, nor would I argue that those acts should be forgiven.

Oh, well. It was worth a try. I knew she was something of a long shot, with an attitude like that.\n\nI'd probably have been forced to beat her down every other day just to keep her in line. Maybe it's better that she won't enlist.
You have done well, my friend. You have a singular knack for shredding Lleraya's illusions.\n\nCome. Let's find out if the way ahead is truly clear.
Talk to Skordo. He has a plan. It's a bit crude, but it just might work.\n\nAt least, it has the advantage of being remarkably simple and easy to remember. I appreciate that in a plan.
I see plenty of Montclair's monsters, but no survivors. Let's keep looking.
It has been a grueling day. Restock and rest. We'll begin the march to the Doomcrag when you're ready.
Some of my soldiers seem to be having second thoughts about our grand purpose. About the faith that guides us through the darkness.\n\nI really don't have time for such distractions right now!
We need to find the others before it's too late. Lead the way upstairs, but stay alert.
We are lucky you came along when you did. Had you been but a moment later … I hate to think what might have happened.
It's so strange to have Federic return after all this time only to leave again. But I think I'm done being lonely. <<1>> has been wonderful to me. It's time I gave her a chance.
And everything goes back to the way it was … I don't know how I feel about that.
My wife, is she …?
Whatever will become of our dearest Arlie, now? With <<1>> and Federic leaving, it's as though the light has gone out of her eyes.\n\nPerhaps I can find someone in <<2>> to keep her company.
I've decided to make this a personal challenge. I'm going to turn things around for the Shornhelm Guard. They'll be the most feared outfit in all the Covenant by next year. You can bet on it!
Thank you for walking with me Adept. I know what I need to do, now. I just need a few more minutes outside before I return to complete the work on the volume you found.
Kynareth's blessing be upon you.\n\nHave you come to put yourself to the challenge, and ride in the race?
My daughter may not be happy, but she learned a valuable lesson.
You can't have your ballom pudding and eat it, too. I hope our new ruler realizes that. Gods know, I do.
What happened? Where's Verandis?
I didn't have time to explore when we were here last. It's far larger than I realized.\n\nWho knows what treasures may rest within these ruins? The Ayleids have always been such a mystery.
Speak quickly. I am very busy and our Order is stretched to the breaking point.
I can use the root words embedded in the text to make rough translations.
Good day to be out on the sea, isn't it? So why am I standing around here on the docks you might ask …? That's good damn question. \n\nAsk Captain Marck.

It's good to see you here. It's long overdue for Rivenspire to get a new ruler! \n\nAs you can see, Julien and Shuga are here. They've surprised even me with their valor in battle. Sadly, we lost Martin. He went down fighting, though. That's something.
The burnt bones foretold death, and death came. They also showed me things which confused me. Hidden things, secret things. And the arrival of someone who can help.\n\nWhat news do you bring?
Excuse me. Hara says you've joined our number.\n\nThat's very exciting, because I believe I've discovered something that can help us understand who or what the Celestials really are.
Why don't they simply put Baron Dorell in charge and be done with it. He's obviously the one who should be running things around here.
Ever since Countess Tamrith returned to the city, I've felt much better about our chances. She's her father's daughter, that's for sure!
It seems our troubles never end. First, the mad king sends us to war against Wayrest. And now the nobles who are supposed to protect us are fighting against each other.\n\nWill it never end?
Are we safe here in the lower city? Will Baron Montclair's forces attack us down here? I can't stand all this waiting!
A friendly face! Good, good. This day may not be a complete failure.
Ah! Oh! Oh … you're … not who I thought you were.\n\nI'd clear out, stranger. Spiders in this cave. Lots and lots of spiders!
Stars above, finally someone with a bit of sense to them. Please, traveler. Help out a fair trader, aye?
These Covenant soldiers are prickly sons of bitches. But we'll hold them back.\n\nI'm sure of it.
I remember when I'd hunt here for days and not see a soul. The war was on, and people stayed behind walls or stuck to roads. Those days are behind us.
Shoes? Shoes are for lesser men! My manly toes need to breathe! It's a medicinal fact.
Use the torch to burn the dead. I'll follow behind you and perform the ritual of sanctification.
