Priest Marnest is surprisingly more helpful than I anticipated. Comforting the refugees, performing blessings and rituals, cooking and cleaning. He even tells a pretty good story.
Ah, it's good to see you again, friend. And what can I do for the hero of Northpoint?
You have the gratitude of Sen Dres, my new friend. I'd raise a goblet of wine with you, if there was time. But there isn't.

You have come deep into Valenwood. There is nothing for you here. One such as you is needed to the north, though.\n\nThe Wood Orcs encroach on the forest. They trample the grass. They chop down trees. They must be stopped.
Good luck, traveler. May you succeed in your service to Her Majesty.
Hey there, traveler. Go well on your journey.
I'm going to stay here with my brother. See what you can find in the chambers we passed through.
Keep your distance. No need to contract the plague on my account.
I can't find them anywhere!
It's horrible they're capturing people all over the city!
They're all dead. I'm sure of it. Now how can I possibly complete our mission?
The Llodos plague … I have no idea why, but it's clear to me that the Maulborn curative is actually the source of the disease.\n\nWhatever they're planning, you have to stop them.
It's horrible there are injured people all over the city!
Were you able to acquire any samples of the Maulborn curative? I'm really curious to see what the elixir is made of.
Thank the Eight! Please, you have to help us. We can't keep them contained much longer!

I must emphasize to both you and these Bosmer that we did not desire this duty, nor do we take any joy in it, but we cannot act against our directives.\n\nThe only way one might circumvent this is to destroy us, and that would be very difficult to do.
Auri-El preserve me! A friendly face! Please, you have to help us. We can't keep them contained much longer!
Always good to speak with another knowledge-seeker. Guildmaster Vanus will be pleased!
I knew you'd find everything Nilyne needed! Please, talk to the alchemist and give her the additives she's been waiting for.
Erunor will make an excellent caretaker. He's always been a stickler for details. I remember when he was just a lad, before the village left last time.\n\nOr maybe that was his older brother? Hmm.
Haven't you ever made a potion before? My notes are by the table. I need to care for my patient now, but my notes should be able to guide you through the process.
Once again, you show up just when you're needed most. Nilyne has been waiting patiently for you. Well, mostly patiently.\n\nPlease, talk to her and let her know what you were able to find.
I'd welcome you to the Brooding Elf Inn, but I'm not in a very friendly mood. Between the plague and the Maulborn, I'm at my wit's end.\n\nStill, if there's something I can get you, feel free to ask.
Good, good. I know we'll be drawing blades together soon enough.\n\nNow, what can I tell you?
Good luck exploring the caves of Daen Seeth. The Ashlands is an exciting place for travelers and adventurers. \n\nMe? I'll just stay here in my nice, cozy tavern. Mmm … Bile Beer.
It's good to know there are travelers such as yourself out there. Keeping the Ashlands safe from … subhumanoids. Hmph.

You are generous to humor two silly old men, but those seeds would mean so much to us. When we were young, we used to sneak away from the clan and come here to be together.\n\nLying here among the Nereid's Smile, it seemed like we had forever.
I am the answer to all questions and the question behind every answer.\n\nNo need to introduce yourself. Your name is already recorded in my realm of Apocrypha.
If you ever need assistance, you need only to ask.\n\nI owe you the largest of favors. As do my people.
Those are some formidable wounds. I haven't seen lacerations like that since Fungal Grotto!\n\nAt least you're alive. Get back in there, already.
Now that we're inside the temple, there's something I must tell you.\n\nThe Seeker's Archive holds vast reserves of secret knowledge, but I didn't tell you the reason for this.

Shor's bones, I can't thank you enough. In time, the body you and Valaste have formed for me will fade. But with this charm, you'll never forget our trials together. I take comfort in that.\n\nAre you ready?
Tu'whacca smiles upon you this day, wayfarer, for you are not caught in the calamity at the main docks.\n\nBy any chance do you have experience dealing with the dead?
Can you believe it? These people … our people who drank the water … they're starting to return. They seem to be in their right minds again!

Before we can stop Yamanu-ko, you need to bring down the wards protecting the Apex Tower.\n\nYamanu-ko's apprentices set the wards in the other mage towers. Disable those wards, and I'll meet you at the Apex Tower.
Be warned, the concentrated energy in the shards has caused unpredictable elemental storms. \n\nYou'd be wise to avoid them while you harvest the elemental infusions.

All these years. He kept the body. It's been so long, and the torture of my soul so recent … I had forgotten.\n\nIt was a single stab through the chest with a blade so sharp it pierced my ward. Possibly with the Daedric blade he now wields.

Oh, good. You're here. I'm worried about Hara. She's clearly tired, but she refuses to rest. She's going to make herself ill!\n\nSpeaking of which, she wants to see you as soon as you can manage. It sounded urgent.
According to everything I've read, breaking that Sigil Stone up ahead will bring us, and everyone who came through that Gate, back to Whisper Grove.
Hara hasn't been herself lately. It has me ill at ease.\n\nI know Nazdura was concerned about Hara's well-being. Maybe she can help make sense of this.
We have much to discuss with Hara of the Star-Gazers. Make haste and find our other selves. We will meet you at the winery when you have completed the task.
Find the other aspects quickly.\n\nIf the Serpent catches their scent, he will stop at nothing to claim them.
This one shall lodge a formal complaint! What right has the Iron Wheel to march in here and smash our merchandise? Thugs … thugs and hooligans!

Your will to survive is impressive. With the Sculptor gone and none to command the prison's flesh constructs, the Warden's sword is broken.\n\nThere are wretched mortals in cells up ahead. Free them if you must, but you face the Gravelight Sentry next.

Be careful if you're going upstairs. These mages are running experiments, and I met several of them a couple floors up who didn't take kindly to visitors.\n\nIf I had more allies I'd have given them Mauloch's fury. If only Brulo would get here.

You were at the observatory earlier, weren't you? I thought I saw you talking to Hara.\n\nAre you going to visit the tavern? If so, watch out for two lunatic High Elves. I don't know if they're dangerous, but you can never tell.

I suppose we're allowing just anybody to enter the Archive now. The Learned One brought many gifts with her when she entered, but she undid our seal on the Archive, and I'm beginning to wonder about the drawbacks.\n\nDo try to avoid the upper floors.
Aye?
Good work. Talk to my assistant Talaya, so she can record your time.
Yes, yes. You'll do nicely.\n\nI have a task for someone with your abilities. A dangerous task, but very profitable.
May the Moons watch over you and always guide your steps.
We'll calm the water here for a while longer and mend what wounds we can. Return after you've found my missing guards and I'll pay you for your trouble.
You did it, Milksop! Speak to Atildel. She has something for you from all of us.\n\nGo on! You'll love it!
It's … it's you! I'm not sure what to say. I honestly didn't expect you'd be back.\n\nGlad you're alive. What happened down there?
You defeated the Serpent? How? We weren't certain he could be harmed.\n\nThis bears investigation.

Outsiders! Sniffing around our valley like hungry little goats. But this is Osh Ornim land, little goat. Iron Orc land!\n\nAway, little goat, or Lashburr will use its bones to pick our—argh! Flint and blood, don't make me yell. It hurts too much.
You're back! And you have this Skooma-drinking grin on your face. Beat those cultists, did you? It's awfully Undaunted of you. You should celebrate. Buy something.\n\nNo, really. Give me your money.
You're back!\n\nI'm not disappointed. Just surprised.
I doubt the Listener spoke to the Keeper before making this decision. It'll be interesting to see what happens when he returns.

You there! You can't go any farther. It's the Scaled Court. They've taken over the ruined city. They're tearing apart Skyreach Hold in their search for more nirncrux.\n\nUnless, of course, you've come to stop them. Could I really be that fortunate?
Well, there certainly are a lot of Orcs and trolls in here. Exarch Braadoth is the chief, after all.\n\nAm I babbling? I think I'm babbling. I'll try to hold it together so we can finish the mission.

It is my belief that Molag Bal's minions committed a great sacrilege in defacing those statues. Even for a Daedric Prince, that is simply too far.\n\nThe gods would see him humbled, and they will strengthen our sword-arms accordingly.
Finally, the Serpent defeated. He killed so many of the others, wrought such destruction on this region … I didn't think I would live to see it happen.
Free the prisoners. There's no need for any more of them to die in these foul spawning pools.

Beware. A great darkness infests the catacombs below and its dead no longer slumber.\n\nI hoped to consecrate the tombs, but the danger is greater than I imagined. Something calls to the dead. It drives them into a frenzy.
Set the six pedestals ablaze. Once the fires burn, the Thief can finish the ritual.
The triggers will summon a bridge of Aetherial energy. It can only be activated in the presence of Celestial power. That means Cassipia is close to achieving her goals.

Your name is spoken of with a mixture of fear and respect among the Scaled Court. I know what you have accomplished against my former comrades. Now I need your help to undo what those fools have done.
How'd that big bastard taste? Never had dreugh in butter sauce before. Was he gamey, or tender like his little cousins? Hah!
Soaked to the bone, yet still breathing. Have you left the lamia cold and dead?
The Legion Zero soldiers are more dangerous than they look. This one thinks they have been ensorcelled by Molag Bal. \n\nSo you be careful. Shaghila wants the saboteurs dead, not you.

You here to learn a craft? Don't worry, there's no cost involved—your alliance pays me to teach the basics.\n\nOh, and you'll earn certification as part of the training. Then you can fulfill crafting writs. It's a great deal!

Now is not the time, my friend. I mean you no ill will, but if you don't leave me to my thoughts I will draw steel against you.\n\nI came here to remember her. I have to remember her. I've lost everything else. I can't lose her as well.
Mortal, this Celestial Guardian has one more obligation for you to fulfill.
I'm authorized to train and certify provisioners, alchemists, and enchanters. If this interests you, we should begin immediately.

<You notice a prominent handbill on the requisition board.>\n\n"The Jarl of Solitude bids you welcome! Masters of the craft await you in <<1>>! New crafters shall be trained! Accomplished crafters will be certified! All at no cost to you!"
"ALL CRAFTERS, take heed! Master crafters currently offer free training for those new to a craft, and free certification for accomplished crafters!"

It's you! How many mercenaries did my husband feed into that Gate? No one was supposed to follow me here. Not my husband—not you.\n\nBut perhaps I can use your strength to my advantage. Go on ahead. It's the only way out.
I will wait. But I will not wait long before I start shouting again.
Welcome to the enclave. Speak to Maj al-Ragath if you have come about the pledge.
You made us proud today.
Well, this is fortuitous. You'll never believe what my sister Kireth has gotten herself into this time.\n\nI swear, she does these things just to vex me.
Well, this is a strange place to see a familiar face, but it's a pleasant surprise as well!\n\nDid you fall down that hole, too?

Great work in there! You, the Wood Elf, and the alchemist really came through for us!\n\nBut no time to talk now. I have to start planning the final assault. I tell you, when we capture the main keep—that's going to be a glorious moment!
Once my scouts return from the coast, I leave this Eight-forsaken place and return to Hammerfell. Hopefully a few weeks in the Alik'r will thaw out these old bones.
I don't suppose you'd like to buy this whistle back from me? It's … you know … impeccably made. Only a little dented! \n\nRight, I thought not.
Hmm. I smell something intriguing. Something … interesting ….\n\nWait. No. Don't tell me. It smells like … it smells like … a dead bird?
Watch out for those creatures inside. They're faster than they look.\n\nIf you see <<1>>, tell him to come back before he gets himself killed.

Look for anything surgical in nature, or conducive to the manipulation of souls. Skull lathes, counter-rotating bone scalpels, odd gems … that sort of thing.\n\nOf course, any notes you find would be invaluable.
She's being irrational, but I'd rather not press the issue if it's all the same to you. Orcs have a tendency to fly off the handle at the least provocation. \n\nPlease, talk some sense into her.
Is this one of the outsiders who responded to my invitation?
Ah, another traveler arrives in our grand city! Welcome, welcome!\n\nAre you one of the chosen? Do you bear the letter from the Forge-Mother?
That was invigorating! Nothing gets the blood pumping like killing a damned Reachmen ice wizard!
As soon as our scouts sent word that people were emerging from the quarry, I hurried down to see what was happening.\n\nSo, where's that damned Elf and what did he do?
Careful, friend. Argent Mine has been overrun. I barely made it out alive.
Everything proceeds exactly according to plan. Exactly. We are slowly pushing our way up the hill. \n\nWe'll take the fortress in no time at all. No time at all, I tell you!
Don't rest on your crest. The other trials won't try themselves. I'm getting better at these jokes, huh?\n\nRight. I'll be rooting for you.

Good day, friend. Or is it evening? So hard to tell down here.\n\nIf you're expecting me to thank you for killing my captors, you're setting yourself up for disappointment. I don't know why you people won't leave the Riekr to live here in peace.
Interesting times ahead.
First that damn Elf and now you? Can't a wounded chief have some time alone to rest and recuperate?

Thanks for the help, friend. And I really appreciate that you helped my brother. He always wondered how he ended up as an Orc. \n\nMaybe we'll go and explore the Khajiit lands some day. Think of it! Two brothers on an adventure! What could be better?
I need to do something nice for my sister and the other hunters.\n\nI know! We'll stop in the new city for some drinks before we head back to our clan.
What are you? Some kind of vagabond? I have nothing to say to you.
Look, outsider, I have enough trouble right now. I don't need you bringing any more to my stronghold.
Hmm. You looked different from inside <<1>>'s helmet.
Some trackers can spot a snapped twig. I'm lucky to notice a broken tree.
Find the truffle patch and give me a whistle. I'll send <<1>> your way.

It's time for you to face Clivia Tharn. I don't know what stake she has in this, but it can't be in the Empire's interest.\n\nYou'll find her through the portal ahead, at the top of White-Gold Tower. Divines go with you. And my cat.
Hmm. You're pretty clean for someone who's been slogging through the sewers. I'd at least expect to see a little blood on your gauntlets ….\n\nWho'd you kill, anyways?
If you find any good mead out there, bring some back for me. I miss mead.\n\nDid you want something?

Well then, what are you waiting for? Go on. I'd offer you a blessing, but at this point, I don't think the gods even care.\n\nIf you really want a blessing, ask Valerianus over there. His faith certainly isn't wavering.
Remember—find citizens, turn to torchbugs, return to Aishah, collect reward. What could be easier?

Come warm yourself by my fire, stranger. As the stones of this city grow colder, we must rely on each other if we are to survive.\n\nYou've been outside. Tell me, have the chains already pulled us all into Coldharbour?
You found them all! Mara's heart, I thought I'd never see them again, but here they all are!\n\nThank you!
I know that this is a crucial mission. Just … just make it quick, all right?

<You notice a prominent handbill on the requisition board.>\n\n"The Jarl of Solitude bids you welcome! Masters of the craft await you in <<1>>! New crafters shall be trained! Accomplished crafters will be certified! All at no cost to you!"
Go on ahead. I'll report to Sternis as soon as I'm able. Thank you again, my friend.
Get down, fool. Enemies of the Pact are everywhere. If you want to make yourself useful, speak to General Hal-Rei in the sewer.
If the Rat were you, he would try not to let the fleshy mess get too close. \n\nWhat if that condition is contagious?

You remember what you need to do, yes? If you go there and your alliance controls the district, it is easy. Just blow the horn. This one will send a runner to your silly boot-skin general. \n\nIf not, capture the district and then blow the horn.

I care not for the Covenant's ambitions, but I pray Onsi will guide your hand and that you will save us from the clutches of Coldharbour. \n\nIf you find the district is already under control, blow the horn to let me know. That would be very lucky.

Whatever's going on in the Temple, it can't be good. I'm glad it's you and not me going. \n\nNormally, I'd say that's a suicide mission, but after what you did here … I don't know, maybe I'll put my gold on you pulling it off. Maybe.
Go see Ralen Veri. He'll set you up with our … organization. Then we can do business.
Psst! Hey you!
Hmm. You don't look like an outlaw, but you look like outlaw material.\n\nGo see Ralen Veri, if you want to make some extra coin.
Psst! Over here!
Yes, yes, you'll probably do fine. Go see Ralen Veri. He'll tell you what we're all about.
Want to be a part of our rather lucrative operation? Of course you do! Ralen Veri will tell you all about it.
I'm not sure what he sees in you, but Ralen Veri was quite adamant. He wants to offer you a place in our organization. As hard as that might be to believe.
This one shall tell you a lucrative secret … Ralen Veri. He'll make you an offer you shouldn't refuse.
I have two words for you, lover, so pay close attention: Ralen Veri. He'll treat your purse quite well.
Sorry, can't help. Talk to Ralen Veri. Let him decide if you're outlaw material.
You there. Yes, you!
This one isn't allowed to speak with you. Find Ralen Veri. Let him decide if you belong in our organization.
You there! Come here!
I only deal with members of … an exclusive club. If you want to know more, talk to Ralen Veri.
Psst! This one has searched all over for you.
You didn't hear it from me, but Ralen Veri can set you up. He's connected to all kinds of tempting opportunities.
Fresh meat, eh? Think you can beat me?\n\nHeh! Just kidding. We haven't made anyone duel to join the Enforcers in years. Those were the days.
We're just a peaceful village, far from the turmoil of Orsinium and its newfangled ways. Surely an Orc like you can understand that.
We're almost there! You can do it! I have the utmost faith in you!

Rigurt thought he was in love with the beautiful Lazdutha. You can imagine my wonderment when Rulfala expressed her feelings for me. That must have been some powerful cheese!\n\nBut Rigurt isn't certain he wants to get married. That's so … permanent!
If you've come for my cheese, you'll have to bide your time. The perfect wheel of cheese must age slowly, delicately.\n\nThe process can't be rushed.
You really need to work on your stealth. All that noise is going to scare away the game I'm tracking.
Never trust a Dark Elf who carries copies his own books, that's what I say.
I've done as you asked and made a generous contribution to Mazgroth's village.\n\nI hope you're happy.

Stibbons always finds a way to turn the simplest task into an ordeal. I don't know why I let him accompany me on my adventures.\n\nBut what about you? I can't believe you agreed with Kharsthun instead of me!
You should talk to Lady Laurent. She has that gleam in her eye. You know, the one that usually results in some catastrophe befalling her faithful man-servant—me.
How embarrassing! But to be fair, it looked like a "k" and not an "r."
Just be careful in there. Those ruins can be dangerous—even when you're as experienced as Bardun over there.
Go after his lordship and make sure he doesn't get himself killed. That would upset the ambassador, though I don't know what she sees in the rat-faced milksop.
You … you don't look familiar. Which of the ships were you sailing on when … when we hit the ice?
I promise you, I never meant for any of this to happen.\n\nSovelle must be all right. She simply has to be.
The news of the blood-forge brings strife, but … I will not allow us to look away. It is not in our nature.

Do me a favor and don't let any of those filthy harpies get too close. I'd hate to get carried off because I was busy concentrating on making this ridiculously easy strike.\n\nSpeaking of which, let me know when you want me to loose my arrow.

I'm going to assume that since you are neither trying to rip out my heart nor consume my flesh that you're from the king's camp?\n\nI wish you had arrived earlier, before the other soldiers were killed.

Try the ice-berry ale. It's delicious!\n\nI love this place! Back at the keep, I'm always being pulled in a dozen directions. Fighting over here, debating over there. Gives me a headache! But here? Here I can just eat and drink until I pass out.
I'm glad to see you and the priest alive. I believe things may have played out very differently if you hadn't agreed to my plan.\n\nBut what of the high priestess? Is Solgra all right?
My head! It hurts like a skinned horker! One of those Riekr hit me. With a damn rock!
Zayshara must've kept hoping her son … that I … would return ….\n\nNo crying! Orcs don't cry. Look, I think there's a moon on that vase.
<There is no response.>

Outsider, you honor Malacath with your actions. I serve the Furious One as well, and as his instrument of vengeance, I swear that the death of the archivists will not go unanswered.\n\nYou, however, have a different purpose in all this, I think.
I pray <<1>> returns safe and sound.\n\nMaybe with some new battle scars … the kind a chief would notice.

If you have a letter from the Forge-Mother, then you've come to the right place. And we don't even care that you're one of those Khajiit-loving, Bosmer-liking, preening like a High Elf, card-carrying members of the Aldmeri Dominion.\n\nNo offense.
Did Orgotha say something about drinks?

I heard what you did at the temple. Your efforts no doubt saved countless lives. I would have been a bit more spectacular in my actions, but I am the king after all.\n\nThe news troubles me, however. It pains me to hear that Chief Bazrag was involved.
You're back—good. I just finished looking through some of this correspondence and …. Wait, what's that? A scroll? It looks ancient. Where did you find it?
Don't know who you are, but at least you're not a short, hostile Riekr.
Did you learn anything about the prison? I gathered some interesting information, but nothing that helps us at this exact moment.
Our captors and tormentors are dead. Good riddance, I say. Now let's find a way out of this terrible place.
Our tormentors and captors are dead. Good riddance, I say! Now, let's find a way out of here.
Please, find that sphere! I don't want to see anyone else get hurt.
I'm in the same room as <<1>>. And <<2>>, it seems.\n\nThere must be an explanation.
How disappointing! The stupid sphere got away!\n\nWell, at least it didn't explode. I guess that's something.
<<1>>'s body … it's not displayed as I'd expect it to be.\n\nCould it be that he was not Redguard? There are theories, of course … could this be confirmation?
Thanks, but what should I do now? I'm not really good at making difficult decisions.
I can't thank you enough for helping us.
You're the one who helped <<1>> find the <<z:2>>. Everyone calls him lazy, but they just don't know how to motivate him.
I sense that Rogzesh has not seen the error of her ways.
You don't understand the evidence. <<1>> is a follower of Boethiah. She killed <<2>>!\n\nSomeone should make her suffer.
<<1>> killed them both. She dishonored their duel—dishonored the truce.
<<1>> will head to the Greedy Gut. Meet her there, yes?

The <<z:1>> features in this dish, so bring me a bundle. Also some <<mz:2>>, and a decent amount of <<z:3>>.\n\nAs for the <<z:4>>, I want you to take it from <<5>>'s shoulders. Bastard ate my shipment of coffee beans.

Damn moot! First the king invites outsiders and now this! It's no wonder we don't have any rooms left to rent!\n\nPlenty to eat and drink downstairs, though, so feel free to go and bother the bartender.
Thank you so much for helping me! With your help, I just know that Shalda and I will be back together in no time.
Stay away from the bars—the Khajiit's claws aren't filed down. If you lose an eye, it's your own fault.
You're a pleasant scent in a dank swamp! What happened in there? The mood around here became very tense all of a sudden.\n\nWait, where's Talviah?
Why am I constantly interrupted? Can't an old woman just walk around in peace?
Yes, you wish to buy me a drink. No, you aren't entitled to waste my time.\n\nNow. Fetch me a mulled claret.

I thought that was you when I saw you enter the keep. You were in there so long, though. I was beginning to think you'd never come back out.\n\nIt's scary, isn't it? Malacath this and Trinimac that. And all that talk about traitors in the court ….
That giant clockwork spider made a terrible pet, so I put it on arena duty. I won't do that again. \n\nLive and learn, eh?
I don't think this is just some routine meeting. What in Akatosh's name are they talking about? A trial? Trinimac's blessing?\n\nSounds kind of dangerous to me.
Flies and I will sneak out of here and go warn Chief Bazrag. We'll see you back in the city!

<<1>> was the largest bear ever seen in Wrothgar. Legends say that by taming the great beast, <<2>> bent all the bears of the land to his will.\n\nWhether true or not, he was all but invincible on <<1>>'s back.
How infuriating! I don't even like the place that much, but I'll be damned if I let them toss me out of my own inn!\n\nThe closer the city gets to completion, the worse things get for us common folk.
I think it's time to get out of here now. Who knows when the rest of the cult will come looking for us?

I had a feeling I'd find you here. Kurog sealed the route to the moot, didn't he?\n\nDamn it! Most of my contacts have gone deep into hiding and we're no closer to saving the chiefs than we were when I scraped you up off the floor of the keep!
I'll make sure Chief Bazrag gets out of here safely. Don't worry, you can count on me!\n\nBut I can't believe what you said about the king. That's some rotten acorns, that's for sure.
I've done what I can to heal Eveli's wounds and ease her pain. The rest is up to her.\n\nShe's been asking for you. Seeing you will do her a world of good.
Are you as mad about what happened as I am?\n\nWe need to use that outrage to bring Kurog down. If we can get to the moot, he's going to throw everything he has at us to slow us down.
<<1>>'s tomb was to remain buried under ice until a true hero of Wrothgar walked the land. Now you disturb the dust in her resting place.\n\nWhy are you here?
Did that skeever Youss ask you to find a pendant?
Find me once you have <<A:1>>. And you'd best not touch it to your bare flesh.\n\nNo reason.

Welcome and welcome, my good friend! Before we get down to business, it seems that Azeeda would like to talk to you.\n\nFind out what she wants, but don't listen to a word she says. I think the trauma we endured has addled her senses.
Malacath whispered to me, as soon as I saw you. I felt the urge to kill you where you stand.\n\nClearly a sign. Of what, I wonder?
You didn't come to pray, did you? The Temple District is no place for pilgrims—not anymore.\n\nI'm sorry if I seem distracted. I lost something.
Good work. In time, we shall know all the Worm Cult's plans. We'll hit them where it hurts.
Back again? I thought I was the dumb one.
That was some damn fine soldiering out there. Nothing I didn't expect, but it's refreshing to have something go right.
When Ambassador Rigurt and I are married, we're going to have loads of sweet Orc babies!
My grandfather's cairn. He wanted it out in the field, open to the sky. He loved this land.\n\nWish his helm had been recovered. Feels incomplete.
This last favor is of a more personal nature.\n\nI want to give Kurog a proper funeral, to honor him for the warrior and leader he was and not the crazed despot he turned out to be.
You'd better get moving. The more time you take, the more time there is for things to go wrong.
I'm beginning to think you might actually triumph in all our arenas. That would be splendid! \n\nThough then we'd have to restock all the non-Daedric monsters. Bother.
Hello again, my friend. I fear that the wards you cast on our consecrated oil have begun to weaken. Will you aid us once more?
The high priestess … she looks so peaceful now. I think she'd appreciate all this attention.

I'm glad you're here.\n\nEveli has entered a deep sleep. I don't know when or if she'll come out of it. But I'll stay at her side, no matter how long it takes. I just hope that Trinimac hears my prayers.

The temple has never been more full of joy and life! Thank you for saving the high priestess!\n\nBut where are my manners. Your Elf friend. She's still fighting to survive the wounds inflicted upon her. May Trinimac watch over her and make her well.

I'm glad you're here. Saves me the trouble of finding you. Before I return to the Summerset Isles, I wanted to thank you for not killing me back at the Vosh Rakh temple.\n\nI appreciate that. I think I would have found death to be very boring.

I hope you're not here to take me on another adventure. I'm done with this wretched place. With you, the king, everyone.\n\nI … I apologize. Talviah's death hit me harder than I realized. I know you did what was needed. Eveli told me as much.
Tusk off! I've got no time for beggars or dishonest traders and I'm in the mood to throw someone into the river. So walk away before we find out if you can swim.

Are you a sight for sore eyes! What brings you to the arse end of Malacath's wasteland?\n\nNo, you don't have to answer that. I can guess why you're here. This is just the kind of place that attracts people like you. You can't help yourself.

No sad faces. Not in here. This was Kurog's happy place, and that's how it's going to stay!\n\nTo Kurog! To Orsinium! May the city always remember the kind and gentle king who cared for his people. Everything else … that was his mother's fault.

Your name will never be forgotten by the Orsimer. We will talk of your deeds for generations to come!\n\nNow, we'll find a way for the clans to work together. To fulfill Kurog's original dream of a united and strong people. Orsinium will stand forever!

Please, our hearts and limbs sag with sorrow and fatigue. Perhaps you could ease our minds. We are searching for our friend and partner, one <<1>> of Daggerfall.\n\nHave you, by chance, seen her on your travels?
Please, we are but poor merchants from the city of Daggerfall. We've lost our goods and our friend. If you really have business with us, talk to <<1>>.
The records you found before were invaluable, but incomplete. Through no fault of yours, of course!\n\nAre you … quite busy at the moment?
You would think the great artisans of Morkul might appreciate a fellow artist. You would be wrong!
Look who's back! The Legion's got more ballistae, ready to move up when they wear the old ones out.\n\nYou ready to stick another thumb in Molag Bal's eye?
Ha! I knew you'd be back. Is it the money or the thrills? Bit of both for me. But enough small talk. You ready to get to work?
I told Chief Gloorot that this was a cursed location, but he wouldn't listen. No one ever listens to old Shab.
What are you doing up here? Go place the kindlepitch. Honestly, these cultists were not eager to give the place up. I'm sure more are on the way. \n\nSo, yes … urgency.
I think the alchemist found something. As much as I like the attention, you'll probably learn more if you talk to him.
What are you doing here? I thought you were busy branding skeletons and killing Worm Cultists.\n\nThere's work to do here, but it will keep. Get back to the Memorial District.
I'm not sure what you did down there, but I'm glad to see that Bolgar and Shabon are alive and well.\n\nToo bad Mulur didn't make it, though.

You're looking for Master Dren? That's kind of you! I really can't abide spiders. I have a condition, I think. The barrow's entrance is over there. Master Dren said he would be right back, but he's been gone so long. It's not like him to miss dinner!
It's done, yes? That machine is destroyed? Hope you didn't break a blade on that thing. Ugh. Dwarves.\n\nBirkhu's been asking after you. You should settle accounts with him before he passes out.
So you're <<1>>'s hatchet hand? Excellent!\n\nYou seem like the dangerous sort. I expect you'll have no trouble with a few stray werewolves and their flea-bitten leader.
Go on, then—kill me. At least I took a few of you traitorous bastards down before the end.
I shall not speak while your master awaits. I refuse to give him any excuse.
I was able to slip right past those metal monstrosities! I guess my old skills aren't as stale as I thought they were.\n\nAnd my daughter made it out, too. Thank you!

Looks like all that training my mother forced upon me paid off! I was like a breeze blowing through the ruins, like a whisper in the night. I was, if I say so myself, magnificent!\n\nYou should talk to the forge-wife. I'll just wait here for Neramo.

Hrm. You've got a little axle-grease on your face, pal. A few close calls in Zthenganaz, huh? Well, Raynor will be glad to see you. We've already settled accounts. If you want your cut, you'll have to talk to him.
Thanks again for collecting these eggs for me. I've already got a handful of potential buyers. They're very odd people—but also very wealthy!

Ah, there you are! You'll be on your way to Zthenganaz soon, yes? I'm sorry if I seem impatient. I'm just anxious to begin these new experiments in earnest. The last one was … explosive.\n\nDon't look at me like that. You aren't my sister!
Argh! Ever twist your ankle so bad that you want to cut it off your own leg? Well, I certainly don't recommend it!
That old tusker Guruzug sent you, right? Just to be clear, you might lose a few fingers on this one. Nikolvara has wound her durzogs up tight. They're liable to bite anything that moves.
All those spirits, trapped by <<1>> … deprived of life and glory. It's a tragedy—one we would see remedied.

If you can scrounge up enough <<1>> to feed the workers of Orsinium for the next week, you'll have my thanks.\n\nIf you kill those poachers, though? If you kill those poachers, you'll have my respect.

So you're the gallant adventurer who means to recover my books, hmm?\n\nWell, you won't find any of my missing pages in this inn … such as it is. There's barely enough erudition to fill a teacup in here. You should look outdoors.
Corruption weakens the wild, which weakens us all. These crude structures we build today were in ruins before and will be ruins after.\n\nThe wild remains. Cleansed or corrupt, that is up to you.
The Worm Cult threatens to sweep over Wrothgar like an ill wind, bearing horror, disease, and death.\n\nYou must face the storm and call down the thunder.
This one needs more drink. Much more.

So you're the Riekr hunter? Good. If you can save even a few of the captured travelers and punish the Riekr for what they've done, you'll be doing me a favor. Reputation is everything in the caravan business, and mine has taken a significant hit.

Look who it is! You made all this possible, my friend. You brought all the chiefs together.\n\nI needed to step away and have a moment to myself. All this excitement! But I promise you, this will be a moot the Orsimer won't soon forget!
Just look at how our city progresses! And now that the Winterborn warlord is dead, I expect we'll have few problems from here on in.
I rarely leave my own clan lands, but this moot intrigues me.\n\nI just hope Kurog's speech doesn't delay the feast we were promised. I love a good roast mammoth!

I'm here, as promised. I just hope this doesn't turn out to be another one of Kurog's time wasters.\n\nIt is nice to see what they've done with our stone, though. Rock from Graystone Quarry, it's the finest in the land!
I don't have a lot of patience for Kurog's games. The sooner he says his peace, the sooner I can return to my own stronghold.
Unlike some of my fellow chiefs, I'm willing to listen to what Kurog has to say.\n\nWords of wisdom can come from the most unexpected places.
I'll see you at the funeral. I have a few preparations of my own to attend to before I return to the keep.
This one senses, profoundly, that your travels are many and vast. Surely such travels have brought you many riches?
I'll keep watch. Find the ledger, then we can leave.

Meet Tanek in Kvatch. He should have had plenty of time to find a way past Artorius's defenses so that you can enter the Cathedral.\n\nOther members of your family will join you once the way has been opened.

I appreciate you not slaughtering everyone in there. A holy bloodbath wouldn't have served us any better than you getting your head chopped off.\n\nUnfortunately, Josseline is as slippery as I am. She snuck away before we had a chance to talk.
I told you about our failed heist—the one that led the Iron Wheel to Abah's Landing.\n\nSomeone pointed them in our direction. It's time we found out exactly who it was.

Remember, you only have a limited amount of time to grab what you can before it gets too dangerous. Don't dally and don't be seen.\n\nBut… if you're feeling cocky and want to earn more coin, I've heard there are hidden passages in these tunnels.

Are you some sort of … freelance gardener? The first I have met! A most effective entrance.\n\nEr … can you not feel <<1>>'s glare upon you? Oh, it is upon me! I … ahem … perhaps you should speak with her.
I sent <<1>> to her own task. <<2>>, too. Didn't even second-guess me.\n\nShe must be up to something.
Our meeting with Anais didn't go anything like I had imagined. She has changed. Or perhaps I'm the one who changed.\n\nLearning your own truth can be so confusing.
Hold still. Your attire is … that isn't a bloodstain, is it?
I look forward to working with you again, Silencer. Perhaps we could share a murder spree sometime soon, yes?

I'm pretty sure we're done here, New-blade. There must be some other Brother you can bother. Or maybe Elam? He probably has a contract for you by now.\n\nBit of advice—old Elam can be a grouch, but he loves it when initiates give him a hard time.
My friend, you've arrived at a bad time. I'm playing host to the king of skeevers and he hasn't the sense to know that he's outstayed his welcome.
It's been a poor day so far, but the wind's changing. I can feel it!

Well, wasn't that revealing! I might have to find other uses for these wonderful fumes!\n\nIt appears that not only did Lyra complete the purification of our old Sanctuary as she was commanded, but she also took on another contract when she was done.
Look at those two. You wouldn't know them for assassins of the Dark Brotherhood just by looking at them, that's for sure. \n\nThanks for making sure this ended well.

Ah, finally a turn of good fortune! You have a knack for arriving at just the right moment. You'll have no problem convincing these clods to hire us forthwith.\n\nHonestly, I'm extremely overqualified, but I'll take whatever employment you can secure.

I usually see the tomb as half full, but even I was about to give up hope. Getting doors slammed in your face certainly took the air out of my sails!\n\nWith your help, we can raise the gold we need to leave this wretched city and get to Sentinel.
For some reason, the wyrd flower only grows in Ayleid ruins. The nearest one is Garlas Malatar.\n\nGet me a blossom from that flower and the saucy Dark Elf can work here as long as she likes.
Anvil's not as sophisticated and civilized as it used to be, and I for one like it this way!
So many nets, so many fish, so little time. This one's life is a tale of excess and woe.
Sorry. Between my brother's problems with the forge and that load of ingots that the puny Dark Elf dropped on the docks, I am way too busy to talk right now.
You should discuss the matter with your guild. It is not entirely my business.\n\nAlthough I will stand over here and pretend it is. So exciting, what you all do!

Scouting successful. The Iron Wheel doesn't send patrols beyond the walls anymore. They're too busy preparing to leave.\n\nAnd there's some sort of commotion at the main gate. Seems they've pulled a few soldiers there to deal with it.
All right. I'll admit it. You may … provisionally, mind you … be somewhat competent.\n\nBut don't let it go to your head.

Did you find <<1>>? I'll keep watch, and thump my tail on the deck if I spot the Iron Wheel.\n\nThree means "too many." Two means "you can handle them." One means "I was clumsy and accidentally thumped my tail on the deck." It happens.
Didn't realize there were two of you. Next time the Iron Wheel springs a trap, I'll bring another uniform.
I almost said something pithy like, "You're late!" or "About time."\n\nBut really, I'm glad to see every one of you. Even <<1>>.
So much to do before the wedding begins! I shall meet you when I am ready.
You'll do fine in the palace. I have every confidence in you, partner.
We'll await your return from the palace.\n\nAnd if you don't, we'll split your earnings amongst us.
Do you dance? I don't, at least not in public. I only have one tail, and I grew tired of people dancing upon it.
Stop right there, you despicable pirate! Take one more step and I'll gut you, belly to nose.
I have no idea what we're going to find inside. After <<1>>, I keep thinking the Iron Wheel is around every corner.\n\nThere I go, jumping at shadows. Are you ready?
You are the last person I expected to see. Did you come to gloat? To tell me my search for <<1>> will end in failure?\n\nAnd how did you learn I was the Desert Falcon?
<<1>> is the one you must convince, not me!
Those paintings … don't they seem a bit off? If <<1>> is an art lover, his presentation seems rather strange.
If you hope to convince anyone of anything, you must first listen to what they want. Go, and listen.
<<1>> is a noble—a true noble, not one of the fops from the garden. She will weigh your words carefully, so treat her with respect.
We must reach <<1>> before the wedding begins. Thieves should always travel separately.\n\n<<2>> always said that. Saying it now makes me sick.
I can barely stand to look at her.
I did not expect such mercy.
Murderer.
Do the ashes reveal Shinji's Truth?
Leave. This cave poses a danger to those with weak wills.
The corrupt captain is dead, but some of her ill-gotten goods remain to be found, yes? We should be doing that.
Did <<1>> speak with you about the wedding?
Ready to help me with that personal matter? This is the family mansion of my old friend, <<1>>. Just as big and opulent as the last time I was here.
Last I heard, the Desert Falcon was in Greenshade—some tavern in Marbruk.\n\nSee what you can learn. If any trails lead to <<1>>, follow them.
You hear about the wedding?
What you have done has saved Hew's Bane from a terrible fate. Just do me one more favor and never speak of what happened. Prince Hew's secret shame should remain just that—a secret. Thank you.
No one in the guild knows I hail from House Dres. Keep it to yourself, and don't you dare tell <<1>>.\n\nThe letter is over there, if you wish to examine it.
Time flows so differently for a Khajiit and a Dark Elf. I am old now, but Velsa ….\n\nNo matter. This one will be glad to see her friend again.

That went surprisingly well. It's amazing what can be accomplished when trusted associates collaborate to get a job done.\n\nHouse Hlaalu won't recover the gold he embezzled, but at least Dathus won't be tearing down any more orphanages.
I don't want to talk to you any more!\n\nNow get off the floor, please. I really need to deal with those spots before my lady returns.
For once, I'd like to travel to a remote location and not find the Iron Wheel.
Don't look at me, I hate puzzles. Once someone knows the answer, everyone knows the answer.\n\nEveryone but us.
There's something strange about the fires. Do they hold some clue?
Well done, boss. You're living up to your reputation. I'll get these sold in the flick of a tail and have your take at <<c:1>> once the guild clears it. Don't forget to collect or it might grow legs.
If my family hurts Narahni's son, I'll make them regret they ever sired me, damn their eyes!\n\nFind Tashmin. Make sure he's safe. Do this, and the favor you owe shall be paid in full.
This one left the letter in the other chamber. Faradan explains things so much better than I ever could.
Tashmin thanks you but continues to wonder why you bothered? You want something, yes?\n\nExplain quickly, because this city no longer feels safe to me.
That skeever Celwen send you? Tell her I don't have the gold yet. I'm working on it.
Those letters will keep the Velmonts from tearing Abah's Landing apart looking for Anais. Meanwhile, I have other matters to attend to. I'll see you back at the Den.
I see now why Walks-Softly wasn't so keen on the whole slavery thing. But I'm still not sure I forgive him for leaving me twice in the same lifetime.

An elderly noblewoman was robbed recently, but the only piece she cares about getting back is an old engagement ring from her youth. She'd hired a man to track the burglars, but he only got as far as Sep's Gullet. See if you can do better.
Astara just gave you my mission, didn't she? Well, I can't say I'm surprised.
I was wondering how long it would take you to get here. Didn't Astara instill you with a sense of urgency about this mission? She must be getting tender-hearted after all these years.

I'm always fascinated when I visit a new city and find a place of worship. Did you know that the first structure built in any new settlement is usually a temple of some sort?\n\nI wonder what that says about us as a people?
Thank you for saying such kind things to Hilde. I know she's taken your words to heart.\n\nYou did good, Initiate. I'm glad you're one of us now.
Go and find that pretty little Nord with the flower in her hair. I'll stay here and guard the horse and wagon.
I did not mean to cause so much trouble. I never meant to put you or Kor in harm's way.
Often I wonder, why has every warrior I sent into that cave failed to accomplish Arkay's will? It's baffling.\n\nI'm sorry, can I help you with something?
Yes, what? Sorry, I've got shipments to attend to. Your business?
All that work and not a thing to show for it ….\n\nOh, I'm sorry, did you need something?
I'm quite certain that you are a little person. I don't talk to little people. They're just so … unimportant.\n\nI have assistants to deal with that. Go find one of them if you need something.

I didn't think I'd ever see the guild bustling again. The other day I bumped into a Wood Elf—never seen him before then. He called me guildmaster and saluted.\n\nI did check my pockets afterwards. We are thieves, after all.
I thought I wore more faces than <<1>>—it seems he fooled us all.\n\nIt's an expression. I don't actually wear faces. That's a rumor <<2>> doesn't need to start.
I heard all the old stories of <<1>> from <<2>> and <<3>>. Were they all lies?\n\nDo you think he decided betrayed his old guildmates all along, or did it happen slowly?
You know what happened to the last new recruit to ask me a foolish question? No?\n\nNeither does anyone else. I'd hate for you to solve the mystery, so do yourself a favor and go bother someone else.
Sometimes I wonder what it would be like to be a member of this fine and upstanding crew.\n\nThen I think, "hunted by the Iron Wheel and forced to live in a cistern."
This place is nice, but it's not a home. It feels like I'm hiding down here. People like us, we need powerful friends if we're going to make it in this world.
The Listener said you would come to me.

I hope you like the cake. Maybe we'll meet again some time. My bakery barge travels all around the world, you know. That's how we'll end this war of the alliances, mark my words. Cake has a way of bringing people together.
Keeping your mind off things with work? Just don't let it distract you on the job or we might need another acting guildmaster.
There's something happening at the Sanctuary. That old crow, the Speaker, he asked for you specifically.

The Speaker brought me news of your success in Kvatch. And of the events that followed.\n\nI must admit, I didn't expect you to return from Fortunata's den of pirates and brigands. Does this mean the Pirate Queen has been dethroned?
I don't know who Fortunata wants dead, but an educated guess isn't difficult. According to my notes, relations between Anvil and Kvatch have been strained, if not outright hostile, of late.
Are you talking to me?
So this is the point where we decipher the code and track down the messages, yes?\n\nIf Raz has any ideas, he will gladly share them with you.
Damn the Sweetroll Killer! All of the targets we knew about have vanished. All except me, that is.\n\nI'm beginning to really dislike this soothsaying maniac who makes his own predictions come true.
Raz must sadly report that we couldn't find any of the killer's targets. They all vanished. Poof!\n\nThe killer has struck, Raz feels it in his paws. Now I want to find the killer and end this.
I knew you'd find me. The fates told me so. But the climax isn't certain. There are many paths before us.
Raz heard the nonsense that spilled out of the killer's mouth. Why are we even considering bargaining with this crazy Dark Elf?
There's nothing to consider. The crazy Dark Elf has to die.

Sounds like you and Venom had quite the adventure. So the Black Dragon was one of us, huh? Makes a certain amount of sense, given how she's been able to take us down so easily.\n\nDamn it! All the more reason to gut her like a swine.
The Black Dragon killed Green-Venom-Tongue, didn't she? Damn her to Oblivion's darkest realm and damn me for sending another Brother to his death!\n\nBut what else? Tell me the rest, Assassin.

I'm glad you accompanied Green-Venom-Tongue, and even happier that he trusted you enough to ask. He's always been distant with everyone here, but there's something about you. You inspire trust and confidence.\n\nI like that.

Here to explore the Cradle? Well, watch your step.\n\nMy mentor, Tsatva-Lan, is missing. Abducted by the Silken Ring no doubt. If you're offering aid, I won't turn it down. I've only got two blades, and this place is packed with spider-worshipers.
A fine feast, fit for kings and tyrants alike!\n\nAre you not eager to taste, dear reaper?
Speak quickly. I am very busy and our Order is stretched to the breaking point.
Excuse me. Hara says you've joined our number.\n\nThat's very exciting, because I believe I've discovered something that can help us understand who or what the Celestials really are.

It's good to have another new face around here. I'm just a student that came to study with the Star-Gazers. I never expected I'd see an event like this! It's terrifying, but it could mean a chance to learn so much more about the Celestials.
The library is grand, isn't it? Not as grand as it once was, I suppose. But the years are long and the past has no greater enemy than the present moment.
Now that we're inside the temple, there's something I must tell you.\n\nThe Seeker's Archive holds vast reserves of secret knowledge, but I didn't tell you the reason for this.
Can you believe it? These people … our people who drank the water … they're starting to return. They seem to be in their right minds again!

Before we can stop Yamanu-ko, you need to bring down the wards protecting the Apex Tower.\n\nYamanu-ko's apprentices set the wards in the other mage towers. Disable those wards, and I'll meet you at the Apex Tower.
Be warned, the concentrated energy in the shards has caused unpredictable elemental storms. \n\nYou'd be wise to avoid them while you harvest the elemental infusions.

Oh, good. You're here. I'm worried about Hara. She's clearly tired, but she refuses to rest. She's going to make herself ill!\n\nSpeaking of which, she wants to see you as soon as you can manage. It sounded urgent.
Hara hasn't been herself lately. It has me ill at ease.\n\nI know Nazdura was concerned about Hara's well-being. Maybe she can help make sense of this.
We have much to discuss with Hara of the Star-Gazers. Make haste and find our other selves. We will meet you at the winery when you have completed the task.
Find the other aspects quickly.\n\nIf the Serpent catches their scent, he will stop at nothing to claim them.

You were at the observatory earlier, weren't you? I thought I saw you talking to Hara.\n\nAre you going to visit the tavern? If so, watch out for two lunatic High Elves. I don't know if they're dangerous, but you can never tell.

You are very welcome among our order, my new friend. It's a frightening time and we could use allies like you. Feel free to get to know the other Star-Gazers here. I'm sure some of them could use your help.
Yes, yes. You'll do nicely.\n\nI have a task for someone with your abilities. A dangerous task, but very profitable.
We'll calm the water here for a while longer and mend what wounds we can. Return after you've found my missing guards and I'll pay you for your trouble.

Outsiders! Sniffing around our valley like hungry little goats. But this is Osh Ornim land, little goat. Iron Orc land!\n\nAway, little goat, or Lashburr will use its bones to pick our—argh! Flint and blood, don't make me yell. It hurts too much.

You there! You can't go any farther. It's the Scaled Court. They've taken over the ruined city. They're tearing apart Skyreach Hold in their search for more nirncrux.\n\nUnless, of course, you've come to stop them. Could I really be that fortunate?
What a disaster! They came out of nowhere, the Iron Orc bastards!\n\nYou should talk to our caravan master, Scattered-Leaves. I'm too rattled to even think straight right now.
I'm still alive! Thank Tall Papa! And all of my limbs are still attached!

Damn, stinking Iron Orcs! They dragged away poor Camaarie! Ran me through and took her while I was bleeding!\n\nLook, you need to find her. And the others, too. Talk to Scattered-Leaves. He's the caravan master and I'm sure he'll give you a reward.
My matron used to say I had some Iron Orc blood running through my veins. I guess they wanted it back.
Well, there certainly are a lot of Orcs and trolls in here. Exarch Braadoth is the chief, after all.\n\nAm I babbling? I think I'm babbling. I'll try to hold it together so we can finish the mission.
Free the prisoners. There's no need for any more of them to die in these foul spawning pools.

Beware. A great darkness infests the catacombs below and its dead no longer slumber.\n\nI hoped to consecrate the tombs, but the danger is greater than I imagined. Something calls to the dead. It drives them into a frenzy.
Set the six pedestals ablaze. Once the fires burn, the Thief can finish the ritual.
The triggers will summon a bridge of Aetherial energy. It can only be activated in the presence of Celestial power. That means Cassipia is close to achieving her goals.

Your name is spoken of with a mixture of fear and respect among the Scaled Court. I know what you have accomplished against my former comrades. Now I need your help to undo what those fools have done.

Now is not the time, my friend. I mean you no ill will, but if you don't leave me to my thoughts I will draw steel against you.\n\nI came here to remember her. I have to remember her. I've lost everything else. I can't lose her as well.
Mortal, this Celestial Guardian has one more obligation for you to fulfill.
I've imagined this moment since I was a hatchling. I knew I'd be free eventually, but now that the moment's here … I just hope I don't embarrass myself.
Who, or what, are you?

Forgive me, outlander, but I have enough to deal with.\n\nI'm just a simple Tribunal priest, and the trouble at the ancestral tomb was too much for even our Buoyant Armiger to deal with. I have failed Lord Vivec and left a colleague alone at the tomb.
See, easy as charming a bull netch with a tasty nix-ox!\n\nI think I might hold onto these for later, if you don't have any objections.
You have the smell of soot about you! Did you just return from Ebonheart?
Captured by slavers, what a predicament! But at least we're still alive.\n\nGo on, now. Naryu wants to talk to you.

Hist bless you, my friend. Sun-in-Shadow's tail quivers with joy and her heart leaps over the moons. I have never seen her so happy.\n\nAt last, she can roam free and read her books in peace. I erect the spine of gratitude.

So I was right? You're a sword for hire? Excellent! My name is Malur Rethan of House Hlaalu, and I have a proposition for you. I need someone to investigate what's going on in the Vassir-Didanat ebony mine.
The Fighters Guild can't show the Worm Cult any mercy. We need to root them out, destroy their Daedra, and destroy any Dark Anchors we find.
I feel like I spent an evening drinking with the heroes of Sovngarde—and then they danced on my head.
A valiant attempt, but Rajhin frowns upon your beetle's pace. Well, this one frowns on behalf of Rajhin.
You're back! Did Nixxie pull through? Do you have the red star shells?

I thought it might be interesting to hire an escort and walk to Vivec City. Pick up some different ingredients, see the land. Next time, I'm taking a strider.\n\nWhile you find the Goblins and recover my possessions, I'll go check on Stromgruf.
Who are you? These are Givyn lands, you know. Take any star shells from this beach and you'll have them to reckon with.
You are unfamiliar, but not unwelcome. What brings you to Bergama?
Another on the War Orphan's Sojourn? Though Stendarr provides for all lost children, we will not turn away donations for our charges.
The Blessing Stone has helped, but Lord Vivec remains in a precarious state. You should talk to him and determine what else we can do.
You're back! My Mistress and I feared the worst. Is it over? Is Savarak slain?
Everything you need is on Betnikh. Show me you hunt for hearth and clan, and you're welcome to join the Stonetooth Bash.
Hope you're not looking for passage off the island. The crew's on shore leave, see? The permanent kind. Probably tripped over a few of them on the way in. Poor bastards.
I do hope Magister Firuth didn't give you too much trouble. He's … an acquired taste.
Back, you imp-faced brute! I have moldy bread and I'm not afraid to use it!\n\nWait … I've seen you before.
Your presence warms my scales, egg-friend.\n\nOur companions in the mine know we are coming. We equipped ourselves as best we could. Now, we strike.

Ah, another adventurer. If you've come looking for saltrice, you'll have better luck in the market. Slim harvest, you know, and we're a bit shorthanded at the moment.\n\nMy son, Seythen, has gone missing, you see. You haven't run into him have you?
I thought exploring on my own would be exciting, but it's a bit lonely.
The plantations are crawling with Iron Hound mercenaries. I'll draw them away as best I can, but do hurry. They won't leave their posts for long.

Current events have left the Temple in need of additional resources. The requests I handle are citizens whose interests best align with the goals of the Temple. You'll work with these individuals to help better Vvardenfell. Are you interested?

Citizens hand in their request, I tell you what I know, and you take care of it. The person with the problem is usually more than willing to talk your ear off about it. The more people you can convince to help you with the job, the better.
I can't wait to embarrass that pompous goldenrod.
You're going to get me in trouble with Overseer Torvayn. He'll kill me if he catches me talking to you. Please, just go!
I'll not suffer another lashing from Overseer Torvayn. He may well kill me the next time. Off with you.
We will rescue our friend and complete the job of exterminating these spirits.\n\nThe hateful dead cannot serve the bonds of true camaraderie and honor!
Run along now. \n\nYou do want to catch up to your companions, don't you?
Bah! I've got enough stripes on my back. Torvayn's just itching to toss me in a shallow grave. You bury a hatchet in his face, then we can talk.
Yes? I suppose you've come for a consultation. What is it? Unsightly warts? Poor eyesight? Flat feet, perhaps?
I am not impatient, but neither do I wish to maintain this gateway forever. Hurry now, face Xykenaz and bring him down. Do this for me and you will be rewarded as I have promised.

Best keep your eyes peeled in that mine. Inanius kwama are always ornery. Hlaren probably left some Iron Hounds to watch for intruders, too.\n\nI hate to say it, but Hlaren probably won't come quietly. If you need to put her down by force, so be it.
I'm going to give you the benefit of the doubt and assume you have a very, very good reason for barging into my tower.

You're new in town, aren't you? Yes, I'd recognize your face otherwise.\n\nWhat brings you to Suran? Here to tour our idyllic plantations? Sample our Redoran wines? Or are you looking for something more … stimulating?
Bah! I'm drinking here. Bugger off, f'lah.
Don't worry about me, friend. It will take more than a few broken bones to make me talk. You'll capture Hlaren yet, I know it.

Can you smell it? The dust of ancient Elves permeates the very air of this old tomb.\n\nOoh, that's a good phrase. I must remember it for my next book! But tell me, what brings you to this lonely place?
How did all these miners get here? Are you… are you responsible for this?

Revus lives just north of here. You'll see a tangle of old rope-bridges and rocks. Kyne only knows what that wizard does out there.\n\nMake sure you really lay into him, eh? I'd do it myself, but I've got to take care of this lot.
Those damned ruffians! If the Scarlet Judge hadn't arrived, I fear those bandits would have been the end of me.\n\nI appreciate your efforts as well. Thank you, stranger.
Thank you! Please hurry. I'll follow … as soon as I catch my breath.
Did you know that the Dark Elves make jelly out of scribs? You'd think bug jelly would taste awful, but spread it on bread and it's divine!

One moment … let me finish this thought …. Hmm, what's this word? I wish my dear Narsis would return so I could ask. His handwriting is atrocious!\n\nAh, well, I'll just write "inky-black darkness." That sounds like the tomb he described to me!

The wary warrior weakens and withers, despite his dashing exuberance of expression.\n\nDo as the Archcanon directs while I conserve my remaining energy and do what I can to stave off this attack—if attack it truly is.

Lord Vivec must conserve his remaining energy, so we need to solve this problem on our own.\n\nIt all comes back to Chodala. That damned Ashlander's draining the Warrior-Poet's power! We need to stop him and get that damn staff!
It looks like you cleared a path through the debris and rescued my trapped workers. Thanks for that.\n\nFeel free to take the Blessing Stone. We'll begin making repairs to the damaged areas shortly.

I hate that it's come to this, but Drovos forced my hand.\n\nKwama husbandry is a delicate science. Introducing a belligerent expansionist breed like this? It's madness, pure and simple. We can't take the risk.
Your Armiger waits for answers. Tell her we are no threat.
Just when I think my day can't get any worse, in come the Ashlanders.\n\nWatch yourself around their ilk.
Ah, you are back! You were successful, yes? Where is Falura? We should be moving on soon.
What can this poor and benighted farmhand do for you, friend?
Not now, citizen. I'm up to my armpits in problems today.

Excellent work finding those egg-heaps. Really, first rate.\n\nNow comes the real challenge. The mud-slurry encasing the eggs is hard as obsidian. There's really no way to tell which heap contains the royal egg until we crack open the casing.
You shouldn't be here! Didn't you read the House Redoran proclamation? I wouldn't be here myself, but some of my miners are still in there!
I see you found your way. It's nice that you want to help my Narsis, but he doesn't really require another assistant. I'm quite capable of taking care of his many … wants and desires.

Oh, it's you. Well, I suppose any friend of Lord Vivec's can be forgiven for inadvertently pushing a famous author and explorer into a dank, dark well.\n\nJust understand that I will not be mentioning you in my next book.

With more time, I could have improved the design. Made it smaller, more portable. But the inverter should work perfectly, provided you find someone to help you.\n\nMake sure you read the instructions. When you don't read, things go horribly wrong.
I need to take care of my brother's remains. You should gather up Sunna'rah and return to Vivec City. I'll meet you there.\n\nNow, please. I need to handle this myself.
And here I thought you were just going to leave without collecting your reward. That makes a person like me nervous.
We're near to solving this mystery, I know it!
What's that? Perfume and incense? You have the stink of the Great Houses on you, oathman. What brings a House Dunmer like you to Ald'ruhn?
The Dwemer hid a number of treasures down here. I wonder what other clues investigation may yield?

Well, at least the ward is keeping the spirits out for now. Which is good considering we're nothing more than vessels to them. I'm not ready to give up my body just yet. Still some good years in this one!\n\nBut where's Farwen? She must be with you.
Let's have a look around. Maybe we'll finally find something valuable.
These Reach-fiends won't take my hold, so long as I still draw breath.
Keep your wits around Savarak. He's slippery as a slaughterfish and twice as deadly.
Do I know you? No? Go away.
Captain Brivan oversees the House's attempt to locate my daughter. You should speak to him and see what his investigation has already turned up.
Didn't expect anyone else out this far … you another relic hunter? The last find didn't cause enough harm? Needed another go?
Mind your manners around Magister Gothren. I hear he's … unpleasant.
You got nix-spit in your ears? Tel Aruhn's closed. Jog off, ya fetching nchow.
I promise retribution and still you dawdle? We have nothing to discuss until you deliver Otheri's notes.
I don't have time to talk right now. I'm having a bit of a crisis at the moment.
Bit busy. Can't talk. Ta-ta.
Come to have words with me, have you? Well, lets get it over with. I have things to do.
My time … draws to a close ….\n\nWere you … successful? Can you restore … my energy?
Greetings, outlander. There are far more of you here than I expected.
I'm in need of a strong set of legs, traveler, and you look like one capable of protecting yourself. Will you aid an old Mer in one last task?
Do you see what he has done to me? This is an outrage. I am a free Telvanni!\n\nGo, speak to Magister Gothren. Demand he free me at once!
I'll head home as soon as I can get approval from the stablemaster. Thank you for everything you've done.
A word of advice. Never go into the egg mining business.
Do you know if a nix-ox hibernates? No, what am I saying, that won't fix anything.
I believe I made my wishes clear.
Are you here about my request? We have to fix this, before it's too late.
I won't go back! She can't make me go back! Can she? Oh no.
Well that could have gone worse.\n\nUgh. Channeling spells always gives me dry mouth. Isn't that weird?
Ha! I knew you weren't interested in kwama caves. One of those blackhearted magisters sent you to filch this thing, am I right?
What? Even assassins need to eat. Stop staring at me like that!

Veya shouldn't have had to see this.\n\nEven I'm finding it hard to believe that the mercenaries would slaughter these Ashlanders for no reason—not to mention the son of a House Councilor. It doesn't make any sense.
I'll remain with the boats. Rescue the slavers' prisoners and look for evidence that ties <<1>> to this sordid operation.
Halt! No one's allowed up here!

Hello again! I wanted to tell you how much I love Mournhold. It's so much more friendly than Seyda Neen.\n\nWhen I asked the Ordinators if they wanted my help, they just looked at me funny. I suppose that's all just part of the secrecy.

Eoki berated me because the Zalkin-Sul cave-in killed some miners.\n\nYou stole the prism to save us from Magister Gothren. I suffered humiliation in a cage while you did what was necessary. Is that so wrong?
Greetings, outlander. There's more history to preserve, if you want to help our tribe again.
Our miniature model is nearly complete, my friend! All that remains is a single component—and that's the key to everything!

Ulran's not supposed to be dead. That wasn't the way this was supposed to end! What am I going to do now? Damn Ulran for leaving me that damn message! And damn him for dying on me!\n\nGods, I miss my brother.

Ah, the councilor's lackey. I understand you've made significant progress in your search for Veya. As a matter of fact, so have we.\n\nThis whole ordeal will be over soon and then you can be on your way, outlander.

As much as I'd like to help, I'm here on official business. I can kill the Councilor, but torture is right out. Rules can be so constricting!\n\nI'll leave it to you to get the information out of her. Just don't get taken in by her … alluring assets.

I appreciate you agreeing to see what you can learn at Arenim Manor. My father used to say it was used by councilors as a retreat, but Mother always told me it was where they conducted business that required a certain degree of privacy.
My champion of cheer returns! \n\nHave you vanquished the stubborn seriousness in my land?
You have the gifts! Good. If you find the deepest part of the ruin, I'm certain Dyzera will show herself.
Ho! You have brought Jorunn his bride-to-be! Or does this one's eyes sieve him? He is very toxicated.
Careful where you step, outlander. This land drank the blood of Ahemmusa heroes. I would not want it to drink yours as well.

Rejoice, mortal. You stand in the presence of beauty and terror, between pale light and long shadows. I am Azura, Queen of Dawn and Dusk.\n\nYou served me before—cleansing my shrine near the Weeping Giant. Now, the time has come to serve me again.
If you insist on lingering here, bare your palms. The Zainab do not suffer guests who hide their hands.
If you come to pay your respects to the First Ashkhan, do so quickly and move on. The Urshilaku's patience is not without limits.
You've strayed into the wrong camp, n'wah. The Erabenimsun greet outlanders with steel, not pleasantries. Pay respect, leave, or die.
Thwarted by my own queen in front of the other royalty. I can't be the laughing stock in my own kingdom!

We've got to get inside the stronghold. The Three only know what the cultists have planned for my brother's soldiers.\n\nUlran wouldn't want them to wind up sacrificed for the glory of a crazed Daedric Prince.

So Vivec deigns to ask for help? I foresaw such an event, but scarcely believed it.\n\nListen well, for if you continue to perform flawlessly, we might yet thwart the efforts of Clavicus Vile and his hound, Barbas.
I leave you and Veya alone for a couple of hours and everything goes to Oblivion in an ore cart! \n\nWhy did Veya leave the safe-house? And why is House Redoran tearing the city apart to find her?
She wants to talk to you, hero, not me. Best not keep the High Councilor waiting.
Unusual for the governor to omit items from the official record, but I'm just her clerk.\n\nYou'd better head inside and talk to the governor now.
Ashur did an outstanding job. For an assassin, he's got a gift for the healing arts.\n\nVeya's going to live. Now I just have to convince her to listen to me this time.
The good thing about Worm Cultists is that they provide me with plenty of stinking Daedra to send back to Oblivion.
You with the Temple? It feels like I've been on that s'wit's waiting list forever. Tell Traylan I still need someone to help us with this job.
Are you working with the Temple? Tell Omoril that we need someone for this moon-sugar operation. Now.
Do you work with Traylan? Could you please tell him to look over my request again. The problems in that egg mine simply must be addressed!

That's one of the spiders? You don't expect me to touch it, do you?\n\nI wonder why it hasn't controlled us? Too far from the ruins? Maybe it targets specific individuals? Well, release the spider and let's see if the tea keeps Stibbons from fainting.
I don't want to go back. No, no, I can't go back. You can't make me go back!
Lady Laurent and I shall remain at the camp until you return. I think I've had more than enough adventure for one day.
Chodala puts forth his great strength as proof of his claim.\n\nGive me the scroll that discounts such a trait for the Nerevarine.
You I don't recognize. If you've come to see Master Fyr, he's preoccupied. Indefinitely.

Interesting … sounds like the master isn't completely happy with his dog ….\n\nThis engineering junction contains some of Sotha Sil's more powerful fabricants. They'll take care of the skaafin, but they might also try and deal with us.

We were wondering when you were going to arrive! I told the others to wait until you got here before we began celebrating, but Sharz found the drinks and one thing led to another and well … I'm glad that you're here now!

You have done much for Vvardenfell and its Warrior-Poet. But as was written in my book of inspirations, "Do not think the battle ends when the enemy dies. The hearts and minds of the people must also be won."\n\nI must ask you for one more service.
Mustn't … listen. The spiders … have to block out the spiders.
If you learned anything relating to the whereabouts of my daughter, please talk to my husband. He's been anxiously awaiting your return.
If you aren't here to work, I'm not here to talk.
Baar Dau … must keep Baar Dau … above us ….

It's Pelinal's Midyear Massacre, celebrated by Imperials since—well—since the fall of the Ayleids! \n\nWe remember the Whitestrake's slaughter of elves at Heldon Bridge, the key to capturing the Imperial City. Before it was Imperial, mind you.
Be careful, outlander. The new marshal needs little reason to put us in chains.
Classic Gascone. Fleeing to his chambers when things go poorly.\n\nI'm sure that news of Lord Seht's condition has already made it to the streets. We have to move quickly to prevent a panic.
I can't let you wade into this business alone. I'm coming with you. End of discussion.
Ah, greetings, Adept! Everyone recognizes the guild associate who matched wits with the Mad God. What can I do for you?
Stay back. Back! I will not die like the others!
Greetings, cat-kin. What can I do for you? Do you have a crime to report?
If what you say is true, I am relieved. A pity that so many had to die for an artifact that was already made safe. There must be more to this than we know.

Terari has been gone a very long time, but her ill-fated experiment created a persistent disorder in the grand schema. Its motions are chaotic, but not entirely unpredictable. Following it may provide some clue to her whereabouts.

Remove the black soul gem from his factotum body and return it to me. He'll resist you, and as that machine Bolin is extremely dangerous. He nearly killed me during his last episode.\n\nIn the meantime, I'll contact Sovor, but no promises.
I hear <<1>> asked you to help us skim <<z:2>> out of Sotha Sil's waters. I thank you for your assistance.\n \nDo you have any questions?
Hey, you're new here, right? I'd ask your name, but I can't hear a thing. I'm Duldrar. Welcome to Slag Town!
Better keep those feet spring-loaded, friend, or you'll wind up down here like the rest of us. You don't want that. Trust me.
Watch your step, friend. That liquid all over the floor? Not all of it's oil.
Welcome to Slag Town. Have a care how you speak to the people here. They may look humble and beggarly, but they're stronger than they look.
Wow, look at you. An adventurer, eh? I don't know what brings you to Slag Town, but heroes are always welcome!
I thought for sure that Khajiit from the Mages Guild could take care of herself. Now she's disappeared into the Shadow Cleft and taken one of our rare and valuable perception tabulators with her!
You arrived just in time. I don't know how much more of Divayth and Varuni's bickering I could take.
He's mad. And obviously dangerous. Please be careful!\n\nIn the meantime, I'll examine the inductor and see if I can determine how it actually works.
My new apprentice, Sherizar. Where did she disappear to? Oh, she's off to a bad start. A very bad start.
You should speak to Luciana … mostly because I don't care to.
I've made my choice. Will you stand with me? The Astronomer isn't the most fearsome creature I've met today, but I'd rather not oppose him alone.
We have to be close. Keep a keen eye, all right?

You should hurry. Knowing Kireth, and I sort of do, she's probably done something imprudent. You'll find her southwest of here.\n\nIn the meantime, I'll keep examining these records. Farewell, assistant.
I'll get the others. You hurry off to Slag Town!
I pity the factotum that has to clean His holy likeness up there. I've never seen so many droppings in one place.
Now, we don't have time for dawdling. The vapor manifold still needs to be fixed after all.\n\nWe just need to find a ventilation gear.
More questions? Speak crow-friend. Speak!
Greeting, auxiliary. Is your friend correct? Did you bring an offering?

Kireth's logic is sound—keep those guards alive and position the lamp, just as we planned.\n\nYou must move swiftly. Once I convince the others to call an assembly, we won't have much time. The Congress of Calibration is nothing if not prompt.
Strange. I spent lifetimes here in the world of tangible-forms, but each time I emerge from the throne, it's like I'm seeing it for the first time.\n\nBroken, impoverished … beautiful.
We have preparations to make, crow-friend! Into the Incarnatorium! Go!
Compressors, filaments, housings, modulators …. Yes, I think I understand what these discarded lights have in common!
Have you ever seen so much machinery in one place? I could spend years here and barely scratch the surface!
Ugh. I don't think I'm ever going to get this fabricant blood off my boots. I love automata, but automata with fleshy bits? No thanks.

You really are the best! Bratheru keeps his fresh meat in an airtight trunk at his stables until he's ready to either cook it or preserve it. \n\nMaybe just nick a little? He does well for himself. Probably won't even miss it.
