Bright moons! A fellow child of the khaj! Welcome! Welcome! Na'jhargo is always glad to see a whiskered face in this silly metal city.\n\nIf you search for salvage, you have come to the right place. What can this one get you?
Bren looks pretty pleased with the stuff we made him. Guess it was good for something, at least.
Normally I tell random delvers: "this is an Undaunted claim, shove off." But these necromancers are up to something big. No time for pledges now.

I'll write about it all, everything that we've gone through. The battles, the hardships, the … losses. Everyone shall know of what transpired here, and of your brave heroics.\n\nI can finally write my grand thesis, and I have you to thank.
Environmental irregularities detected ahead. Point of origin: Oblivion. Daedric Prince Nocturnal threat level elevated to high.
Well done slaying Gascone. Sometimes justice requires a heart of brass. Varuni will learn that eventually. Perhaps sooner than she'd like.
We're done, right? Where's the key?
My apprentice wishes to speak to you.

Remember, the parts are most likely in the Clockwork City or in Dwemer ruins in Tamriel. \n\nI've heard of corrupted memory crystals firing at random, so you may want to return occasionally to see if the Precursor knows anything new.
I speak the will of the Divine Metronome.\n\nPlease locate a tok-plug to hear deceased resident, Gascone Duscant's, archival data.
Sorry you had to hear that. Our family feuds aren't usually so dramatic.\n\nRaynor always requires a delicate touch, but he's never stormed off before. He hates being on his own.
What a magnificent monolith! I wonder if the workings extend into the subterranean levels below us. Maybe that's where the true functioning takes place.

I see you've brought back an animo core. It works, I assume? Good job!\n\nWhile you were gone, I figured out where to install the core. There's a cavity in the machine that looks to be about the right size. I think it goes in there.
You do your part and I promise to do mine. And don't worry. If we find the treasure, you'll get a share.

I've called a few people together so I can tell them what we've done. Hopefully, word will then spread throughout Slag Town and all of the Brass Fortress.\n\nI couldn't have done this without your help, my friend.

It is no longer a matter of if the Saints will lose control, only a matter of when. The threat they pose is too great a risk. The black soul gems powering their bodies must be removed, by any means necessary.
If you're looking for the inn, it's right downstairs. Keep moving.
With all the troubles in Rivenspire, it's always good to know I can come to the Run for a stiff drink.
This one suspects Maurice is up to no good again. His schemes are entertaining, at least, if not well thought out.
You got more of that root juice Maurice had his hands on? That stuff's pretty good if you don't mind black teeth for a week. Know I don't.

Raz's investigations have brought him to Rellenthil. When this one noticed your Psijic friend slip into town, Raz figured you'd be along soon.\n\nSo, what did you discover on Artaeum, the island that isn't here anymore? Ow. That made Raz's head hurt!
That sounded … not good. You really should make haste and get to Bewan. The Oracle has need of you.
Please … hurry ….\n\nAs soon as the portal … reaches maximum expansion … the dark princes will come ….

No, I refuse to deal with one of the Queen's guests—especially not in my own home! How did you get in here, by the way? No, never mind that. Since you found your way in, I assume you can find your way back out.\n\nBefore I call the guards.
The Canonreeve's son certainly seems agitated about something. I wonder where he ran off to in such a state?\n\nWell, I suppose we should go and take a look at this sinkhole the Canonreeve mentioned.

Ah, good. Oriandra got my message to you.\n\nI've been scrying through my memories, trying to find the missing events that will remind me where I hid the Heart of Transparent Law. I believe my efforts have revealed something significant.
It's a scribble on a wall! This is so beneath my duties as a Divine Prosecution bailiff.

Your honesty does you credit. I know that damning a fellow outsider must be difficult for you, but the truth often demands a heart of diamond—rigid and razor sharp.\n\nPerhaps now we can finally get back to business as usual.

By Magnus! If what you say is true, Emile's innocent!\n\nYou seem hesitant. Don't get bogged down in the details of his experiments. The important thing is that he didn't murder Haladan. You have to take this to the Sapiarchs!

Poor Emile. He meant well, but these are shocking revelations. I never thought he'd be so reckless.\n\nCreating a potion to deliberately infect someone with vampirism? By the Eight. If this gets out the Sapiarchs may never trust us again.
I wish I could do more to help, but it's Sapiarch gold that keeps food on the table, you understand?\n\nIf you have other questions, ask. But let's keep this between us, all right?
You again? I told you, I don't want to talk about this. I'm guilty!

I owe you a debt of gratitude, friend of Valsirenn. What the two of you did to help me, that was a step beyond. Thank you.\n\nAnd it seems you accomplished what I failed to do. You ended the threat of K'Tora.
We can only take the ritual so far without the elixir the Ritemaster requested. Oriandra knows where to find it. Just go and ask her before the matrix of augural energy reaches a critical level.
Yes, that's the elixir. Now take it to the Ritemaster. There's no time to waste.
We just need to push on and find the Golden Knight. The faster we can get out of here, the better.\n\nIf I never see a giant spider again, it will be too soon.
You and Valsirenn entered Mephala's realm and rescued Meridia's Golden Knight. I couldn't ask for more, my friend.\n\nI assume Darien believes he can repair the Dawnbreaker?
There you are! Glardir's gotten far less cheerful, and the book shifted again. I think things are coming to a head!

You. I want to blame you for this, but—you were right. I was foolish.\n\nI never meant for anyone to get hurt. All those poor performers—did I really destroy their chance to join the House of Reveries? I hope not. I hope they can still join.
Once Rinyde has departed for Lillandril, once I'm certain she won't give up her dream for mine, I'll write her a letter explaining everything.\n\nI know she'll forgive me. Eventually.
The way is open, thanks to you. Keep clearing a path. I'm going to poke around and see if the recently deceased left anything of interest.

That was impressive! You've got quite the talent for juggling. Never could I do that myself. Tried it once and nearly sliced off a finger!\n\nNow, to the questions. I'll start. Tell me, my deft-fingered friend—where did you grow up?

You've got a great voice. I almost worry you might have oversold me.\n\nNow, to the game. Maybe it's the alcohol talking, but you're a fine looking one, aren't you? Got someone special waiting at home? Tell me, I'm curious.
It's now your turn to ask me a question. What do you wish to know?

You have a perfect heart, newcomer. None of my neighbors would lift a finger to help me!\n\nThe guards placed Arathel in a cell beneath the kinlady's manor. I'm told the Justiciar of Remand is there now—a Mer named Talerion. He must know something.
This isn't right! I'm brave! I'm brave and fearless and … what happened to me? Where am I?\n\nMara help me, were we up on the walls?

Well, well … you made it. You'll forgive me if I don't stand to greet you. I have a thing about social niceties.\n\nMy spies told me you were coming, but neglected to say why. You're a recent arrival to the isle, yes? I'm intrigued. What brings you?
Ah, it's you again. Any luck following that crude map? My officers seem incapable of seeing this through.
Best talk to Mother. She'll sort this all out, no question.
Thank you so much for dealing with Talerion, cerum. I think the Mother of Rats wants to talk to you.
Please, my lady … spare a coin for a wretched beggar?

You must have clenched pretty hard to sell those forged papers to the likes of Lin. Relax, before you sprain something. \n\nNow all we have to do is find and kill a murderous Daedra that's evaded capture for weeks. Easy, right?
This is really, really unpleasant. Bathing in leeches unpleasant. Please hurry.

Hm, a traveler? Don't see many wanderers out here near the acropolis.\n\nBest give it a wide berth. There's a curse on this place. I didn't believe it at first, but once you hear that ghostly shriek … it'll make you a believer. Trust me.
So, finished reading about my heroic exploits? Impressive, yes?
Well, I think we might be on the right track. Ow.
You! Oh, I've had just about enough of you! My story was perfect. Perfect! And now you've muddled it up. I won't have it! Not anymore!
This stone should lead us back to our natural time. All you need to do is keep that destination clearly in your mind. I'll follow right behind you.
You can save Lotus. I believe that with every fiber of my being. Bring her back safe.
Am I in Aetherius? You don't look like my ancestors. Are you gods?

Welcome back, partner! By Malacath, what a discovery! We learned about the history of the vault, the Worm King's relationship with Vanus Galerion, and you even destroyed one of Mannimarco's vile experiments!\n\nNot bad for a day's work!

You have a look about you. Some sort of quality that's rare to find. And trust me, I'm never wrong about these sort of things. Can I interest you in a room at the local inn?\n\nActually, wait. That came out wrong.
At last you return, and with my reagents. Come, I simply must see them. My genius is like a stallion waiting to be set free!
Were I a warrior, I'd cut you down where you stand. You've made a stupid, selfish decision here today. I hope you can at least feel guilt over what you're about to do.

I wasn't sure how I'd feel if I saw you or Naryu again. Balmora seems like a lifetime ago, and I'm a new person since committing myself to Nocturnal's service.\n\nI wish you weren't involved in this matter.
Go on, check all around my farm. You won't find anything useful, trust me! Tindoria is far too clever for her own good. What does that leaf-eater care about us little people? Nothing, not a thing!
You know, I didn't choose a life of seclusion in order to chat with strangers. If you have no business with me, best be off.
Oh, but what a crime it would be to waste such beautiful paint on mediocre work. Come, be reasonable. Those supplies would do far better in my talented hands.
I don't expect you to keep my secret, but I'd rather pay my penance through action, not rotting in a cell. It's selfish, but it's all I have left.
The Ritemaster requested my presence in the Dreaming Cave. It looks like I'll be joining you on this expedition.
Do what you have to do. I'll not shed any tears for these back-biting sea snakes.
My memories … it's like a rush of water, all jumbled and confused.\n\nYou keep clearing the path while I try to organize and make sense of my thoughts.
We need to keep going. I don't like where everything is leading, but we need to see this through.
I hope the old man remembers something or we climbed all this way for a whole lot of nothing.
When Pandermalion's soldiers told me he'd returned to the keep with a passerby, I thought he'd lost his mind. What were you thinking?

Soravil. Is he …? He is. It's done then, isn't it? I knew he wouldn't come quietly.\n\nIn the end, I bear the blame. A killer right beside me and I didn't see it until more lives were lost. I'm glad you were here, admanen.
Now that you're all set for the journey, feel free to ask me any questions you'd like. I've never been one to ignore a healthy curiosity.
See? Nothing to find. Please, if you see my boy, tell him to come home.
I bought us as much time as I could. I hope you found something useful.
I just don't understand. These gargoyles were merely statues when I came here before.

Grief does us no good unless we use it to focus our commitment. We need to rally our forces. It's time to turn this Daedric tide before the waters of Oblivion overwhelm us.\n\nThankfully, Sotha Sil returned while you traveled the Dreaming Cave.
Now don't get mad, but there's a perfectly good explanation why Leythen and I busted out of Artaeum and came to this charming little hideaway.

Rushing a spell as complex as the Sapiarch ritual will not end well. I researched the diamond keys to find out how they work, and the magic isn't stable.\n\nMark my words. It can't be accelerated without dire consequences.

We've failed. The Conclave, despite its best efforts, wasn't able to attune the Resolute Diamonds. We can't use the diamond keys to enter the Crystal Tower.\n\nBut what about you? Were you able to track down Darien and the traitor Leythen?

The Thieves Guild send you? Hmph. Wouldn't go any deeper if I were you. Darkness crawls along the walls of Eton Nir. Only thing you'll find here is an ugly death.\n\nThat, and the corpse of my former apprentice. Most likely.
A Keeper? No … no an intruder. Did you not hear the shrieks? The groaning admonitions? This is a cruel and sour place, outsider. Your beating heart mocks the dead.

Wasn't that fun! Exercise is good for the digestion, after all.\n\nBesides, I find that people look at me strangely whenever I start chatting in public. Oh yeah, I'm supposed to tell you that my master wants to have words with you.

Rigurt is so disappointed! How can I negotiate peace if I can't even get an audience with the High Elf Proxy Queen? What a terrible predicament this has turned out to be!\n\nDo you have any brilliant ideas, my friend?

Accept your appointment and be thankful I got you on the Proxy Queen's docket at all. She's extremely busy, considering she has to stand in for Queen Ayrenn during every meeting, ceremony, and public event.
Sorry, sorry. No time to chat. The newcomers have been flowing into Summerset at an unbelievable pace since the Queen proclaimed the island was open. I'm much too busy for a social visit.

"Hark! What Maormer magic is this that makes water burn and clouds drip serpents from the sky?"\n\nJust a taste. For the full performance, you must come and see my evening show. I promise, there won't be a dry eye in the house!
Honor upon you, traveler. If the Divine Prosecution can be of assistance, don't hesitate to request our aid.

I finally decide to pursue true art, to move beyond painting backdrops for someone else's stage, and what models do I find? Polished! Unblemished! All around boringly beautiful.\n\nI need someone who will give my work meaning. A depth of morality.
Would you care to explain why you're tracking me?
You found something important, didn't you? I could read it on your face from across the room.\n\nWhat's in those papers?
I'd rather not cause any more disturbance for this debut than Tableau already has. Come, let's move along.
Please, you have to understand. I'd rather risk it all and stay with a mer who truly appreciates me, rather then go back to how things were.

What are you? Some sort of saint sent to deliver me from digging through Malooc's squalor? \n\nWell, two searchers are better than one. We'll meet near the eastern exit of the Coral-Splitter Caves. Not too far from safety. Watch yourself.
Oh gods, this is terrible! This adventure truly is a tragedy!\n\nI can't use any of this!
Another newcomer. Very well, you have seen and spoken to the Proxy Queen of Alinor. Now be on your way.

The College of Sapiarchs isn't open to the public. We don't just let anyone wander around in its academic splendor.\n\nNow if you'll excuse me, I have a lot of reading to get through before the next lecture.

I've checked over Lillandril from top to bottom and there's no sign of the Court of Bedlam. I can't get the portal master to let me go to the College compound, though.\n\nHave you brought permission from the Proxy Queen?
I know you consider my people to be nothing more than crazed cultists, but they didn't deserve this fate.

I want to trust Leythen, but even I have to admit that this doesn't look good. Let's try to catch up with them before something even more terrible happens down here.\n\nI'd hate to think I set Leythen free just so he could betray us.
The Sapiarch's letter. She's hidden a coded message in the words. Raz has seen this done before.
This is the moment of truth. Once we begin, nothing can stop the rush to the grand conclusion. Make sure you have everything you need before I activate the Dreaming Cave.
You must move quickly. The pearl is with Justiciar Avanaire, somewhere in Tor-Hame-Khard. Once you find it, destroy the cursed thing. \n\nEven if you have to go through Avanaire to do it.

You're a kind soul. Be careful, we've lost a lot of kind souls of late.\n\nThat pushy noble, Faidur, might know something about that. He arrived not long ago claiming to own the place. Certainly acts the part.
You know he is guilty of these crimes, and yet you intend to speak on his behalf? You arrivers really are a blight on our society.\n\nGo on, I have nothing else to say to you.

I did meddle a bit, but I didn't mean any harm by it. Surely tossing me in jail's blowing the whole thing out of proportion, right? Promise I'll never do it again. I'll even transplant my additions someplace where they'll be appreciated!

I don't mind having some company in this endeavor. Most people are barely willing to speak of this place above a whisper, let alone offer any help.\n\nLet's try to find a way inside the sunken ruins, shall we?
Well? Were you able to find Niralin? Or at least, whatever those werewolves left of her.

You smell like one of them, but … different. You're a werewolf, but not of this pack. I'm not sure how I know that, but I just do. \n\nYou need to leave now. It's far too dangerous here. They've already killed Brengas, and … it's too late for me.
I sense Grog in the northern section of the ruins. I'll get Cainar to help me with the link as soon as he recovers from his ordeal.

Best we split up. Unless my creaking knees give me away, I ought to be able to handle some scouting while you're searching for survivors.\n\nWe'll rendezvous at the old lovers' tree, near the reef on the eastern shore. My friends will know the one.
I wonder whose chambers these were. What was their life like before they abandoned it, and why?
Thank you for heeding my call, newcomer. I don't suppose your passage to Summerset brought you past Wasten Coraldale?
By the Eight, I'll be glad when this cult is wiped clean from the face of Nirn.
Can't you see I have a job to do? Wouldn't want to keep the corpses waiting.
Give us another moment, then we'll join you in the Dreaming Cave.

Valsirenn is waiting for you in Ceporah Tower. She's concerned about the whereabouts of the Golden Knight and Leythen. Not to mention the whole remake reality thing that Nocturnal has planned. That really has her on edge.
I'd start with this Altmer dueling foil. Probably some flimsy toothpick of a blade. Typical.\n\nCheck around town. I'm sure you can find someone willing to part with theirs.
If you are here to help that pig-faced brute challenge me, speak to my second, Fandilol.
He just …. But the rules state …!\n\nLook, I won't tell anyone about this if you won't. I'll say … I don't know, Lirendel fell from his horse. Yes, that's it! Just keep that Orc away from me!
Shor's bones, this is the foulest of Elf magics!

As kinlady of Sunhold, I implore you to hear my plea.\n\nMy city has been overrun by the Maormer, and Admiral Viscarne declares only my death will stop this attack. He hates my family and demands my head, but I know surrender will not save my people.
Barra, ceruval. How can a humble merchant help so exalted a personage on this fine and fine day?
A ballista? That's certainly more in the knight's area of expertise than in mine.
Talk to Leythen. I'm not a locksmith!
After all those voices singing your praises, I'd be silly not to have you talk to the Sapiarch one more time.\n\nGo ahead. See if you can convince her.

If Renzir sells his ship, he'd have no means to continue work. What life could he make for Nubani, here where none desire the Khajiit?\n\nDoes my love wish us destitute? Is her hate of Renzir so great?
The Sapiarchs aren't capable of protecting the Crystal Tower alone, but they're just too stubborn to admit it. It's up to you to convince them.
I had almost forgotten what kindness looks like. Thank you.
Good to see you survived the perils of Karnwasten, my friend. But where's Grog? I expected him to return with you.
Thanks for making sure I got back to Cainar. We'll tell the Battlereeve what we know, but you've got to find Miriya.
Whoever you are … if you aren't an illusion … you need to take word to Alinor. Tell Battlereeve Tanerline—
You aren't a Kwama, but I'd watch you fall just the same. Not having wings must be just awful!

Ah, another ephem. Ever since the Queen's decree, I can't take three steps without bumping into someone who lacks even a drop of Altmer blood. No offense intended, of course.\n\nShall I presume you're here about the contract work?
Tranquil greetings, initiate.\n\nIt seems your efforts in the swamp proved fruitful. Just a short time ago, our scryers located the remaining fragments of the Staff of Towers.
Let's just keep this little mishap between us. Don't need word getting to my father. Again.
I'm not in the mood for conversation. Go chat up another stranger.

By the Spinner's holy webs, when did I become an insufferable arse? Valsirenn didn't deserve that. Ealdaawe was her daughter, too.\n\nWhy am I talking to you about this? I know it isn't because I like you, because I really don't.
My drunk friend and companion, Grog, is still out there. Oriandra assured me that you'd find him and return him to us safely.
The Wood Elf is only being detained until we get to the bottom of this matter. You may speak to him, but he's not leaving our custody until I see fit to release him.
I look forward to hunting down K'Tora and introducing the foul creature to the sharp edge of my blade—whatever it turns out to be!
Well? Do you have a ring to show me?

Whoa—hey! What are you doing in this neck of the woods?\n\nNot that you don't have a right to be here, that is! It's just, well, a gryphon nesting ground doesn't tend to be the best place for a stroll.

Newcomer, I have been on my feet for nearly an hour and I have just about had enough of it. Be so kind as to retrieve my absentee husband and my dear Eustasia, so I might be finished with this so-called leisure stroll.
Hmm. You were the one who stopped the attack on the College, if memory serves. While your past courage is admirable, your current timing is not.
We'll need to take that portal down to the Hunting Grounds proper. There we can begin our search for Tarcyr. We'll need the indrik's heart if we're ever to win Hircine's boon.
Move along, there's nothing to see here. Just a petty squabble among us Nord types.

Now, I know what you're probably thinking. "Look at these squabbling fools. Why don't I just take the treasure myself?"\n\nTough luck, that. The only thing that will crack the chest open is the blood of Gjadil's descendent. Thus, you'll need one of us.
Enter a mysterious stranger to our little circle of mystery. Mind the cadaver. Or, should I say, the cada-Var!\n\nForgive a thespian his morbid humor.

You've picked a grim day to visit Cloudrest, traveler.\n\nThe city has been besieged by the Sea Sload Z'Maja, a sorceress who commands darkness itself. Most have already evacuated. I'd turn back now, if I were you.
You have the look of a traveler. Tell me, have you heard news of Cloudrest? The city within the mountains of Eton Nir?\n\nMy mother is there, and I feel she may be in danger.
It's the end of the road for this vagrant. She's really slipped up this time.
What's it going to take for a girl to get some shut eye around here?
I'm not sure what's brought you to Cloudrest, but I have to recommend you turn back. The city is far too dangerous to enter. I'm busy enough as it is without more souls getting injured.
There you are. I was wondering when you'd return.\n\nDid all go well in Valenwood?
I think I'll stay here just a few moments longer. I never knew how difficult it would be to say goodbye ….
You should speak to Josajeh before she leaves. You may not get another opportunity.

Raz has much to do after this. Reports to write, missives to send. Perhaps he will go visit his family, once all is done. It has been far too long since he has seen them.\n\nBut first, Raz shall drink some very expensive wine.
It's going to take a lot of work to restore the Royal Menagerie to anything close to its former glory. Am I really the best choice for this?
I've done all that I can for the wounded. But if that storm gets any worse I'm not sure it will matter.
Narazda said she would help, yes? \n\nThis one shall watch over you as you fight that creature. Heed her words, walker. They may be the only reason you survive.

While you and Jee-Lar go after the Blackguards' expedition ship, I'll write to my sister and let her know what we've been facing.\n\nIf Margus Derius manages to acquire the skull despite our best efforts, at least I'll have warned my sister.
Looks like you can take care of yourself. Good. Because this is far from over.\n\nNow, you'll head to the gardens next. Remember, I need you to keep a look out for any wolfsbane flowers you may find.

Well, Narazda certainly didn't expect our handsome soldier to throw a parade in her honor, but … a thank you would have been nice.\n\nStill, this one is used to such treatment by now. Not many are kind to us children of the moons.
My father has given us an invaluable gift. \n\nThat light should seek out Tarcyr. I suggest you follow it closely as you travel through the Wispwood.

If you're looking for information, then you've come to the right place! I am the most knowledgeable broker in the refuge.\n\nOn the other hand, if you work for the town guard, I have no idea what we're talking about.
You again? Either tell me you have located my assistant or leave me to my work.

A thousand greetings, wayfarer. This is no place for casual visitors. You have wandered into a nest of vipers.\n\nBut have no fear. Eshundir will take care of you. Come closer and let us conduct business.

The priestess holds them in the Teeth of Sithis. Use the tunnel beneath the waterfall to reach the xanmeers on the ridge above. \n\nWe will regroup at the top of the western xanmeer once you've found the others.

From what we learned, my ancestor only pretended to help the Legion. He led them here to save Murkmire. When the Legionnaires sealed the cave, they interrupted the cycle. No one has come to bind the Wuju-Ka in centuries.\n\nI guess it's up to us.
Was Concordia able to reconstruct the map? Let me see!\n\nAll right. I'll meet you down south and we'll find the expedition ship together.
Kassandra seemed eager to talk. I don't think you should keep her waiting.
I understand you might be feeling some anxiety about proceeding with this ritual, but the time for second-guessing has passed. Please, do as Xukas and Jaxsik-Orrn say.
You're back! Fabulous!\n\nSome of my missing friends already tracked me down, telling tales of a daring, fiery rescue. Marvelous! What happened out there?
Ah, walker. This meeting is fortuitous, yes? Our mutual friend, Famia, is looking for you. I warn you—she twitches like a sugar-sick kitten.

Hmm. Good to see a recruit with a few notches in their shield. Still don't want to know your name, though. No point in getting attached until you've survived your first hunt.\n\nAttachments slow you down. And in Murkmire, you keep up or you die.
Can you even imagine the treasures we'll find? Let's hurry inside!
Your interest is misguided. Turn your eyes elsewhere.
I see no reason why I would not join the bonding ritual, but I do not have my betrothed's seed-doll. It is pointless to dwell on what's lost.
Waiting is the hardest part, don't you agree? Of course you do. Which is why I won't force you to wait a moment longer. Well, no longer than necessary.\n\nSo, how can I help you today?

Greetings, beeko, and welcome to Murkmire. My name is Xukas. I am wondering, who are you?\n\nForgive the rushed introduction. I find that trading names and intentions makes for calmer waters. We understand each other, I think.
Glad to see you received my invitation. Your timing is perfect. I need you to clear an obstacle for me.
The Dwemer took extraordinary pains to seal the Wrathstone away. The question is: why?
I thought for sure I'd covered my tracks well enough to avoid any run-ins with Quintus's friends, or enemies. Who are you? What did he tell you?

I've barely had a moment to examine the Wrathstone in any detail, but it's obvious that this tablet is incomplete. I'll need to reexamine my research, see if there's something I overlooked that will indicate where the other half may be located.
The Wasseek goods-keeper took my dowry to the storehouse for keeping-safe. Go find it.
You're back. I suppose I need to ask. Were you able to place the sacred candles in Tsofeer Cavern?

Find Kishi's father Bhoki. Tell him you want to help. He will know how to best utilize an outsider in this matter.\n\nBe mindful of Mewah-Jez, though. She seized Kishi because he interfered. My spines quiver just imagining her reaction to an outsider.

There is a rare plant—the Leviathan Pizzle. It is the key ingredient to the elixir. Find one and I will join the bonding ritual.\n\nI should warn you—it resembles many toxic mud-blossoms. This sketch should help you avoid them.

Find Kishi. He plans to show our war-chief that there is a better way to train the novices.\n\nIn the back room, take the fire stones. Use them to find my egg-son's hidden camp in the swamp. Then help him carry out his plan.

Ah, beeko. I guess this is goodbye. This was fun, right? A little terrifying, but with the Hist's blessing, all ends well.\n\nPlease, take care of friend-Famia, and Jaxsik. They are precious to me—just as you are. Farewell, my friend.
Bhoki's fire stones? I suppose he told you how to find my camp?\n\nI stare in wonder. Though I appreciate the aid you provided, I must ask why the outsider is here.
The dead hiss your name, ojel. I hear it bubble up from the shallows. Here in the deep murk, you earn their favor or you join them.
Keep your claws sharp, ojel.
Please, you have seen the horrors that Ree-Nakal wrought. She soaked that corruption into the very essence of her creations. We cannot allow her poisons to seep into our roots. I beg you.
Go on! Drink up, friend!
You've gotten your prediction, as promised. Now get going. All your shouting is ruining my peace and quiet.
You catch that skink yet? Remember, grab it with two hands! He's slipperier than a greased guar.
Do not dwell on what has transpired. We cannot change the past, but we can guide the course of our future. The Hist will always steer us true.
You're Jee-Lar's partner, right? Said he'd send somebody with guts, and that about sizes you up. Hope he's right.\n\nDid you bring the stuff I need?
Safe travels, sera. And make sure you wash out your bag! That ash basil smell isn't going away anytime soon. Believe me.
You really think Tharayya is going to get that enormous pile of junk working with a few of these tiny parts?\n\nIf we just massacred all these Goblins for nothing … I don't even know what I'll do.
Stop it. I have work to do. You want to snoop around, fine, but stay out of my way.

Our little friends are happy, I am happy, and Captain Jimila will be happy very soon. Oh, sun-filled day!\n\nRemember, when the Captain asks you who created this masterpiece, shout my name with great enthusiasm. Nesh-Deeka, the pride of Lilmoth!

I should tell you—the Dragonstar dryskins are not overfond of uninvited guests. If they see you, they will probably shout, or ring bells, or run in silly circles. So be cautious.\n\nAnd please try not to kill anyone. It always leads to headaches.
If you're looking for a good show, you're in the wrong place. This game makes no tusking sense.
The Remnant. I see now. It contains all the souls … all the souls of the ancient tribe. Their name was … the Root-Whisper tribe. Yes. Yes, that's it.\n\nI know what we have to do.

So the Blackguards seek the Remnant. That is … unwelcome news. Even so, killing a single bound prisoner will save no lives. Friend-Jaxsik thinks it is justice. It is not.\n\nRelease the Blackguard. Spare this one life, and we may save many more.

This savage lies as easily as it breathes. Look at its eyes—the sweat on its brow. It stinks of deceit and cowardice. Now it speaks of the Remnant of Argon? It must die.\n\nThis ojel is a liar and the spawn of liars. Now, Tsojei and I will kill it.
Bhoki says the Naga-Kur are doomed. Kishi claims our war-teacher is to blame. What do you say, outsider? Why have you come to the village of the Dead-Water?
I'm just the hired help! Don't hurt me!

Hmm. Dilated pupils, ragged breath …. Tell me, do you see anything strange? Anything about the Remnant?\n\nWow, you're really out there, aren't you? On review, maybe I should save these questions for later.
I'll take her home. I can care for her there. Being part of the tribe will help her.
We better find this thing soon. Getting a little tired of chasing you around. For now.
I stand ready to guide these souls. Choose wisely, sword-kin.

Rootmender. After all this time … it warms my scales to see you again.\n\nI sensed a twisted soul trying to claim our power. Had she succeeded, many would have suffered. Thank you for stopping her. Now all that remains is to set us free.
I never thought I'd see Jaxsik-Orrn so enthusiastic about … flowers. Maybe they're poisonous, or give you enhanced strength or something? You should talk to her.
Come for the bonding ritual? You don't bear the trappings of any of the local tribes. Doesn't matter either way, you're early. Now might not be the best time to partake in Bright-Throat hospitality.

I'm so glad you've agreed to help me!\n\nNow, the Blackrose Prison gauntlet is no laughing matter. You'll be forced to fight against all sorts of enemies, one after another. So make sure you're well prepared!
If you have the tablet, feel free to place it back into the Xinchei-Konu.
Walk well, traveler. May the ground be sturdy beneath your feet.

You there, are you familiar with the local terrain? If so, I could use your help.\n\nMy wife and I, we came to this godsforsaken land to get away from the clamor of Vivec City. But I fear my poor Varona may have gotten into a spot of trouble.
<<<1>> coos happily.>
Ranja's method of opening doors is not so dramatic as this, but she thinks it's more elegant.

I have an uneasy feeling about this ceremony.\n\nStill, it would be unwise to ignore Sulahkeesh's judgment at this point. Especially given that I'm the one who sought out such a judgment in the first place.
And so the farm now belongs to one who is worthy of it.\n\nI'd much rather pass such judgment with my own hands, of course. But at my age, this is the best I can manage.

When your task is complete, meet me in the Bright-Throat Village.\n\nIt pains me to ask so much from you, but please know that the branch you seek holds great importance to me. I don't know what I would do if it was lost.
If you do not believe me about Paheiza, merely speak to her yourself. I'm sure she's already well into her cups, as they say.
Just leave me to my grief. And tell Chuxu I have a few choice words for him, when this is all over.
The box itself is likely to break apart any moment now, so I'd not bother to take it. The branch within, however, should hold up well to travel.
Quickly then! Go collect that which is needed.

You have done exceptionally well, friend-outsider! I think we may actually succeed and reach the sacred lily!\n\nOverconfidence can fell even the mightiest warrior, though. The final challenge awaits us. Do not let your guard down.
I'm glad to see you unharmed. The Dead-Water said you had passed through here in your search for the Skin Taker. I was beginning to worry.
You return. There has been no new sightings of the Skin Taker since we last spoke.\n\nThough this Bright-Throat woman arrived. She was asking for you.
Mmm! Greet—arhgle! Ack ….
Be careful with that grave-stake, traveler. It took Tun-Zee many years to carve it.
I see the glimmer and shine of victory in your eyes. You must have located the hidden dowry!\n\nI am glad for you, and lift my broom to your success.
Imagine what this monstrosity must have been capable of when it was fully functional. Horrifying.
Many grateful thanks to you. You need only tell Tree-Minder Pavu that Tseedasi will be home in a day or so with supplies.\n\nMay the mud remain firm under your feet.
Oh, Landal's in for it now ….

The Hist has awakened from its long slumber, and Root-Whisper Village lives once more. Many have traveled to join us, and many more will come.\n\nBut this is both blessing and curse, for as our numbers grow our supplies dwindle.
Could you deal with that rather large insect? My blood needs to be aligned, not siphoned completely from my body!
Will you please talk to that Argonian and clear up this matter? I detest these kinds of delays with a passion.
Keep your voice low. There are dangers nearby.

You are the outsider bending the reeds in Lilmoth? The one who destroyed a xanmeer? I imagined you would be taller.\n\nStill, there is nothing you can say to change my mind. Not even for the loud dryskin who thinks the sun shines just for her.
We … we are being guided to something. I feel it in my frills.
I feel the first breeze … now, the silence before the exhale. Now, focus on the prayer-stone! Summon the Hist's wisdom!
You walk up to the great Captain Jimila with pride and purpose. Do you seek passage on my ship or does some other business put that spring in your step, hmm?
Hmm? Do you have something to say, ojel?
A wise wanderer would have walked the other way. Are you lost, friend?
New in Lilmoth? Don't worry, it's not as bad as it first seems. Just mind where you step, yeah? Never know when you'll end up buried up to your knees in mud.
If you've found any good expedition spots, it's best to keep them a secret. Otherwise they'll be picked over before you've time to blink.
I still can't believe Xukas charged into battle like that. Against the Blackguards, no less! If I didn't know better, I would say that Dead-Water warrior was influencing him ….
Murkmire has always been dangerous to traverse, but the Blackguards have increased that danger greatly. I am glad someone has taken them to task.
Those who bring trouble into our village do not often leave. This is because we kill them, of course.
My brow furrows at your arrival. Complete your task, and be gone from my village.
The light is gone and darkness clings. Yet it is only in the dark that we may see the void which is Sithis.
Nisswo Kahei may be wise, but she can be a real kuuda sometimes. How are we to fend off anything if she refuses to let me light a fire?
Everyone is assembled, except for the suitors. What is the word, beek-ojel? Must I call off the bonding ritual and bring shame upon our tribe?
The Xinchei-Konu is a marvel of ancient Argonian craftsmanship. If only they had continued to create such structures to this day.
Good to see you again! I'm so glad you decided to come to Murkmire, I really am! We could use your help, and that's a fact!
Ziss'vo, new blood! Zadaza thinks you look like a skooma-sick senche rolled over!\n\nBut since you are here, perhaps you can help.
As much as it galls me to admit, I agree with Tharn. The time has come for the true queen of Anequina to vanquish the Usurper Queen.\n\nShe defiles my family's throne with her heinous presence.

Cadwell plans to place traps on the main road into Riverhold. With Jone and Jode's luck, his devices will work as intended and not harm either him or you. With Jone and Jode's luck.\n\nStay fragrant, five-claw!
I have enough trouble seeing through my own eyes, let alone someone else's. I hope this doesn't become a regular occurrence.

This temple holds a secret only the adepts and Moon-Priests who studied here know. Luckily, Zamarak falls into one of those categories.\n\nThe Prayer of the Purifying Moons can activate moon pillars around the city to disrupt the necromancer's spell.
Who are you to burst into our home without permission? Wait, this one recognizes the brawny adept standing behind you.\n\nWhat do you want with Tsazii and her family?
Agreeing to an alliance with Imperials! At least it appears this Prefect Calo assisted you.\n\nTell me what happened out there, five-claw. I want to hear it from you.
When you look at the world as lines on a map, it all seems so small and insignificant.\n\nI was trying to determine the meaning of this document, but so far the secret eludes me.
Yes, yes. I see what you did. Would you like a sweet biscuit? Collect the tile and let's be on our way.

Prefect Calo commands a full complement of soldiers, mostly seasoned Imperials and not the Nibenese mercenaries that make up Euraxia's main forces.\n\nIt's probable that Saulinia and her assassination squad is here as well, so I advise caution.
You said the Dragonguard gave you a key to the door? Well, open it and let's see what's inside!

There you are! Things seemed quieter, so Mara'dahni came to take a look around. Maybe snatch up Hadaz's body, right?\n\nDid you settle this business with the cultists? You look a little singed, so I'm thinking yes?
Please, a moment of your time. I need to speak to you about Abnur Tharn.

My best ranch hand, Elhalem, will accompany you. He has sharp eyes and knows the Prowl better than most.\n\nI hope we are not too late. If something happens to this one's sweet boy, Milksop …. Oh, Numaia would never forgive herself.
The Dragonguard is gone. We need to enter the sanctuary and find this Dragonhorn he speaks of. It may be the answer we seek.
It does my heart good to see you unharmed. I trust the Nereid suffers no longer?
Moons blessings, walker. Forgive Vazbi. She just thinks of Silhu-jo. And her future.
Silhu-jo saw everything. We must save Vazbi, quickly! Please!

Help Abnur Tharn track down this mysterious final order that the Usurper Queen issued before you killed her.\n\nMeanwhile, I will work with Khamira to learn more about the Moon Gate that the Dragons seek.

Captain Nala-do's waiting for you near the siege weapons. Work with her to put them out of commission.\n\nOnce we see the weapons go up in flames, we'll head out and rendezvous with you at the sewer entrance.

Old Aneshi doesn't get many visitors, friend. Few find much comfort in the ancient tales of Khunzar-ri during these trying times.\n\nWait. Aneshi recognizes your friend! She is grown now, more serious, but this one knows Princess Khamira, by Jode!
Travel never used to take this much out of me. Ah, well.\n\nNow that you're here, we can begin our investigation of the crypt.

I was never supposed to inherit the throne. My older brother should have this honor, this responsibility. But Euraxia murdered him along with my parents. So now there is only me.\n\nWhat say you, five-claw? Will you stand with me against the Dragons?
Desecration and blasphemy! Someone has opened the resting place of King Hemakar and the royal family!
So that's a Soul Shriven? I've heard of such creatures, of course, but I never expected to see one. Especially not among the leaders of the Khajiiti resistance.
Five-claw, good, good! We have work to do.\n\nAre you ready to disable the siege weapons and wreak some more havoc?
Keep your wits about you. After all, you're no use to this investigation dead.
I have to admit to a pang of jealousy. Being able to turn incorporeal has always been a dream of mine.\n\nNever wanted to be quite that dead, though.
Let me know if you have any other questions. I realize that Hakoshae can be quite the curiosity for travelers such as yourself.
The orb is sustaining the Aurorans! You have to find a way to destroy it or they'll be unstoppable.

Zumog Phoom has been collecting my original body parts. He tried to steal my essence and stick it back in my old noggin. I think … I think he's trying to put me back together!\n\nWell, not me. The other me. The Betrayer.
Oh, you're that traveler I saw earlier. Do you need something?

My half-sister has stooped to employing necromancers. How distasteful. No matter. We need to open this door and deal with Captain Calsivius and his soldiers.\n\nInteresting. What's with all the Dragon imagery, I wonder?
Euraxia's soldiers were here long enough to turn some of the hall's own defenses against us.\n\nWe need to be on our guard, walker.
Hmm? What can I do for you, traveler?
Why, if it isn't our town's mysterious stranger! Magnate Feina-Darak told me all about your participation. Have you completed the first two Proofs?
Mizzik just needs to collect our reward from Ishu. And perhaps Captain Kahiri will be feeling generous as well, yes?\n\nFeel free to head to the Banished Regrets. This one will meet you there.

The ancient memories become clearer in my mind with every passing moment. We follow the same path as the heroes of legend. Khunzar-ri, Anequina, the Betrayer, they all walked these steps to reach Jode's Core.

My friend! No, more than that. Family. \n\nKhasda's deeds have been made known to the Stitches. Tasnasi's name is cleared. For now, at least, there is something to drink to. Or, in Sereyne's case, something else to drink to.
Khasda's dead, huh? Couldn't have happened to a nicer person.\n\nWell, we may not have gotten the vault that Tasnasi promised, but it's a nice consolation prize to know Khasda's throne is empty.
How many of those Averno brothers are there? It's like there's a couple more every time I look over. I swear they're multiplying!

"Do not mistake a righted wrong for an undone wrong," I believe is the mantra of Goutfang master Jun-ri. Nazdar is glad to know Tasnasi's name is restored, but perhaps gladder to know she faced this tragedy and overcame it.
Going to bring the little mage back her bauble, then? May as well chuck it in the canyon. At least that way it won't be covered in regurgitated fur.
Don't feel the need to rush out so soon. I rarely have the chance to make new acquaintances. \n\nEspecially with Iulius breathing down my neck day and night. Not that I always mind it.

Please, you go ahead to the temple. Find our Moon-Bishop, keep her from spreading any more of this madness!\n\nHaduras will meet you there. Once he leads these ones to safety without them straying toward any other foolishness.
Did the spirit send you to help Kiseravi? What did she say?
Ishu hopes you can find his Zinthia soon. All of us miss her.
You have something to say, dull claws? Let's make it quick. You don't get muscles like these by standing around, chewing the fat with outsiders!
A hundred apologies, walker, but the show is postponed for now. If you purchased a ticket, this one will gladly refund your gold.

I need to deal with the Mane's envoy, but our forces remain unaccounted for. I cannot help worrying about Gharesh-ri and our soldiers. Even Prefect Calo and his Irregulars. \n\nThey all fought bravely. I hope they survived the battle at the Moon Gate.
Yes, it is delicious. No, this one is not in a sharing mood. Go find your own food!
And so Mazdurr is once again saved by the intervention of Azurah.\n\nThrough your actions, of course.
It's good to know that my Clan Mother was not the only vampire to understand that our relationship with the living is a tenuous one.\n\nDo not let the bloodlust convince you otherwise.
Do not let your steps falter. Nord crypts contain many traps and are often protected by the dead who rest within them.

The moons have aligned and the gate has opened! Khamira definitely gained something at the temple, but she hasn't figured out how to control it.\n\nYou were with her. Talk to her. See if she can close that aperture before it's too late!
We need to deal with that breach before the Euraxians overwhelm us.
The war council has much to discuss. Finish your business with Abnur Tharn so we can decide our next course of action.
Who are you? Did Caldathir send you? Well, don't even try to stop me!

You return, victorious! What a relief. From this side of the portal, I could only see white flames slashing through the shadows. Even so, I'm confident you sundered Arum-Khal's spirit.\n\nI am sorry about Shando-ri. I just couldn't reach far enough.
Zamarak is happy to see you, friend. After the Dragons entered the Moon Gate and you followed, this one worried that all was lost. But then the Moons parted and suddenly everything seemed all right.
Go on, my friend. Enter the throne room and wait for me. I need another moment to compose myself, but I will be along shortly.

The sword-wielder returns. Azurah be praised.\n\nIn my younger years, we would honor your victory with song and garlands of sugarcane. Mazza-Mirri is too old to sing now, but she honors you all the same.
Just follow the cliffs east, and listen for the snorting, barking, and roaring.\n\nGot lots of loud beasts on the ranch. Makes it difficult to miss. Trust me.
The power of the Moonlight Blade should dissolve the wards and allow us to enter the temple. Harness that power, and we can proceed.
Rakhzargo usually isn't allowed in the cellar. The moon-sugar is too tasty to resist.
Kideya won't have you two mucking about her stores, you hear? There is enough to do with so many farmhands missing.\n\nWhat are you even doing down here?
We should talk to this woman. See what she knows and ask her why she's all tied up, yes?
Please, please! J'dathal begs. You must rescue his three daughters from that horrid beast! They should just be west of here, up the path. \n\nYou must find them before that monster does.
If my half-sister wasn't so obstinate, I might just suggest a diplomatic solution.
Ah, another member of the Fighters Guild. A bit of good fortune, at last.\n\nI need a steady sword-arm to handle business in this doomvault. Pay's good. Are you willing to help a brother in arms?

Were the words the same for you? Sometimes written language likes to confuse me. Words change and switch places. Very annoying.\n\nAnyway, the gravestone mentions the Betrayer. Sounds like a dastardly chap. I wonder if I ever met him?

Hrrm. I suppose it is good to see you again, walker. Someone must help Tharn clean up the mess he created at the Halls of Colossus. Come to think of it, you share some of the blame, yes?\n\nAh, do not mind me. Rampaging Dragons put me in a foul mood.
I did not expect to see you in this desolate place, walker. Did Captain Nala-do send you? Or have you come to join us as we hunt the Dragon that killed so many of our warriors?

You're the adventurer who helped Abnur Tharn and Khamira at the Halls of Colossus? The battlemage has been waiting for you.\n\nBut where are my manners? Welcome to Riverhold and the province Anequina. I am the Speaker of the Mane.

Greetings. This one is Ma'jha-dro, Grand Adept of Star Haven.\n\nHe is glad to see you in good health, traveler. It is not every day that one survives a Dragon attack. Bright Moons must have blessed your path.
My half-sister continues to be an embarrassment to our family name. The time has come to deal with Euraxia.\n\nPermanently.

I recommend vigilance. Old sewers attract all sorts of vermin. Plus, it won't be long before Euraxian soldiers come looking for us.\n\nAll I can offer at this moment is advice. So, avoid what you can, dispatch what you can't, and watch where you step.
You have my gratitude.
Many greetings, walker! Please, make yourself at home. We Baandari take great pride in our hospitality.
You? Zamarak cannot believe that you have joined the Usurper Queen.
A trickster, a hero, and an ancient mural; just the recipe for a grand adventure, no? Ah, but this one is most excited to see it unfold.
Go on! You should have the honor of completing the Rithana-di-Renada. After all, it was you who restored it.
You have the singing crystal, thank Jone and Jode! I was afraid you would fail and invite Rajhin's wrath upon us all.
Greetings, walker. If you are looking for work, there is more than enough to go around! Just speak with my friends here—Ri'hirr, Nisuzi, and Battlereeve Tanerline.
It's taking a lot out of her. I can feel it. Selene's going to need a lot from all of us before this battle is done.
He has called his faithful to his temple and you have answered! Once you lay your eyes upon divinity everything will become clear.\n\nThis way! Come join in our worship and praise Alkosh's return!
May Alkosh grace you with long life and a clear path.

Saviwa wishes he had his ancestor's treasure. He could have thrown his best party in ages. There would have been nice wine, lots of ladies, weird smoothskins juggling sharp objects ….\n\nAh. It would have been good times, my friend. Very good times.
This is much closer to Jora-ri's resting place, but not quite right. We will know we are there when we find the shining guards.
This one will enjoy putting a stop to the necromancer, Zumog Phoom.
Zamarak does not wish to remain in Star Haven if that Dragon decides to return. Let us keep moving.
As flattered as I am by the attention, I'm pretty sure you're here to talk to the great Abnur Tharn.\n\nSince I'm done with the old wizard, he's all yours.

Dragons, necromancers, multiple Cadwells, and now Euraxian soldiers marching on Riverhold. I ask you, could this day get any worse?\n\nYour skills, such as they are, may be of use. There's much to do and not a lot of time available.
Talk some sense into him! Abnur can't just slink away like a thief in the night. It's undignified! Not to mention rude. I don't know what goes on in that otherwise brilliant mind of his!
You look like you could be handy against Dragons. Let's talk.
Ah, five-claw, good, good.\n\nThis one brings another message from the great and powerful Tharn.
Are you sure you don't want to become a follower of Peryite?\n\nOh well. I suppose some people like bathing and covering their orifices when they sneeze.
Unlock the cage if you must. Just remember that he's your responsibility.
It's fine to gather supplies for the survivors, but focus on finding accounts of the flu outbreak. That's how we'll prove Peryite was responsible.

This one never expected to set foot in the capital of Anequina again. She hoped the militia would succeed but she didn't believe they stood a chance against the Usurper Queen.\n\nCashia understands you played a significant role in these events, yes?

Hmm? Oh, it's you. Good to see you're still among the living. I suppose you had a hand in getting the moons to finally pull apart?\n\nHang on, I need to finish my report. I find that it's best to write it all down while it's still fresh in my mind.
Thank you, five-claw! Azin-jo may be blind to the truth, but I'm glad you saw through the false god.
Walk the Way of Jode and bathe in his holy light. He will burn away the darkness in your hearts until no wickedness remains!

It's good to see you, five-claw. We only just returned and I have yet to report to the queen. Khamira is all right, isn't she? We saw the Moons move and the eclipse end, but we haven't heard what happened after you entered the Moon Gate.
Don't have much time to talk, I'm afraid. Lots to do!
Oh yeah, I can make that. Definitely.
Tu'heiba gave you what you seek, yes? Be off.
Do not forget my warning. This Jewel of Baan Dar carries a power none of us understand. Be careful what you wish for, yes?

Find the key to free the chain. Pull the chain to free Fez'skar. This is simple, yes?\n\nPlease hurry. Fez wants to live! Or at least use a decent privvy before he dies. The Ruddy Fangs didn't even give me a bucket!

You cut a striking figure, walker. There are many dangers to such an enviable personage in the Stitches. All of Elsweyr, in fact, if you cast a shadow long enough.\n\nHear this one and he will tell you how to grease the right palms to pass unmolested.
Ah, five-claw, just the one Lyrrsazhi was looking for.\n\nQueen Khamira requests you come to the Rimmen Palace immediately. She has need of you.
I'd bet my last cup of jagga that the key to this door is clipped to that drunk guard's belt. Send Marmalade up there to have a look.
Rigurt was surprised by the true Lady Izza, but thankfully he's known for thinking quick with his feets.\n\nKeep her busy while Rigurt gathers his diplomatic thoughts.
Congratulations on finding the finest cloth merchant in all of Riverhold. Thadarra can see that you are in desperate need of a renovation.
Why am I not laughing at a mountain of dead gibberers? Get to work, mortal! Hammer those idiots!

This is the life, yes? The sun beating on your shirtless fur. The sweet smell of moon-sugar cane wafting through your whiskers. It doesn't get any better than this, walker.\n\nEverything would be perfect if it weren't for those meddling pests.
Did you come to share this lizard with Sanzagh? You can have the neck. Maybe a hind leg if you're lucky.
Wait your turn, plaything. There'll be plenty of time for me to chase you around this little maze after I've finished my snack. All these games work up an appetite!
Tail! Where is Eljhan's—? There it is! Stupid tail! Stupid!
Cadwell may have given Zumog Phoom exactly what he wanted. Talk to Abnur Tharn and figure out how we are going to salvage this situation, walker.
Stay low in the grass. We've got Ruddy Fangs up on the hillside, and probably more down on the other side of the cliff.
Playing right into the Dragon's hand. I expected more from Selene, but her baser instincts drive her. She may seem like a Mer, but that is a facade to draw you in to her web. Don't forget that.

Y'ffre's bones, I'm feeling green as the Green. Like I killed a bottle of overripe rotmeth last night. Selene's not looking too good either. Even Carindon looks sour. Then again, he always does.\n\nHope it's not the blight setting in ….
This horrid blight. Why? Dragon's aren't of this world. No natural creature would twist the land this way.\n\nWe have to kill Maarselok. We must.
I'm not sure we stopped the ritual in time. There's a … disturbance in the air. Something's about to happen.\n\nCome on. Let's find the source of the island's defenses while we still can.
Find the three glyphs in Tanzelwil. Let me mark their locations on your map, along with where I think the hidden tomb lies.\n\nI prepared notes as well. Feel free to take them with you.
Za'ji didn't think she would be this mad. It was just one measly bell, after all! And perhaps a few tiny trinkets ….
Tadali was worried about this.\n\nOur sacred bells must be cleansed every Moon cycle, but the one you returned has been away for many years. We need to perform a purification ritual.

I can't believe Za'ji would steal a bell from his own people! I knew he was a smuggler, but I thought he had a sense of honor.\n\nYou go and find the bell. I'll try to smooth things over with Clan Mother Tadali in the meantime.
This doesn't sound good. We need to get down there and try to protect Yahgrondu!

When you brought the Dragonguard sanctuary maps to me, I had no idea what we would find. Hunting techniques, perhaps. Maybe a weapon or two.\n\nBut the promise of a Dragonhorn! That's more than I dreamed possible after all this time.
The Dragonguard and I have agreed to an alliance. To defeat Laatvulon, we have joined forces.\n\nNeither of us much likes the idea, but allowances must be made.
Our way to the island was just here! Talk to Tharn and get the old mage to open it while there's still time.
May Tava watch over you on this journey, warrior. And may you and Sai return to us alive and well.
Ka'ishka is so grateful to see Vijari's eyes again. No matter how frail he becomes, his eyes are always full of life.\n\nYou are all so strong.
This is as pure an expression of anguish and sorrow as this one has ever seen.\n\nNow that Vijari sees it for what it is, it pains him to blot out his father's final work.
Ah, five-claw, you arrive in the nick of time. While I deal with my royal protectors, I have an important task for you.

The Jonelight Path. Magnificent, yes? It was here that the most legendary Khajiit learned to cross vast distances in a short amount of time.\n\nThe quickest way to reach the unreachable. Dangerous without an experienced guide. Luckily, you have Zar!
I had a feeling that you were behind the disruption of the other focal points. Figured I'd help … by taking out this last one.
Notice the pulleys. They should help us lower the drawbridge. Unfortunately, I'm not sure which combination of settings will open the way.\n\nSee if you can find anything that could assist us.
Poor Buzinda. I can't imagine how upset she must be right now.\n\nIf we do infiltrate the cult, we should find Lahini and convince her to leave. Or force her to if she won't listen to reason.
When you've learned all you can about the Dragon cult, return to the sanctum and report your findings.
Take the claw to Queen Khamira. Hopefully, it will provide her with the insight she needs to find us a path to Dragonhold.
Well, I certainly didn't factor this into my plans.\n\nThe Dragonguard were very clear about their dealings with Dragons—hunt them, slay them, use their parts. Yet this one shares our goals.

We must head to the Wall of Life and find Vijari. A path leads up to it from the rear of the village.\n\nIf there are dro-m'Athra to be found Adara'hai will need you to defend her while she banishes them. She prays Vijari will not be among them.
You should listen to Ranza, walker. He seems to know something.
You should speak with this one's sister quickly. Safik fears we may not have much time left here.
Orkey's marbles, these cats are driving me mad. You here to help? Well, get to it! I've got schedules to keep, you know?

You found the place! And Safik is well? Good. Let this one guess, Sormund blusters like a Pahmar squall. Pay him no mind. He is like a harbor mutt, yes? Bark, bark, bark, but no teeth.\n\nNow, we have work to do—that is, if you still mean to help?
Our actions … I remember them, five-claw. Anequina and her kra'jun did something similar when they dealt with Kaalgrontiid long ago.\n\nHow … interesting ….
I heard the wings. Nahfahlaar has left us? Probably for the best, all things considered.\n\nWere you able to get him to tell you what happened on Dragonhold before the island totally broke apart?
Za'ji still thinks a celebration is in order. Perhaps this one will mention it to the lady queen from Anequina. She must have enough gold to throw a proper party.
The wind's at our backs now and our sails are full. Time to see where it carries us!
You know, I really do like being a part of all this. Aeliah of the Dragonguard. I'm going to make you and Sai proud!

Thank you, friend! Because of your actions, Lahini has been returned to us. Buzinda cannot imagine what would have happened if her daughter stayed with that awful cult.\n\nFrom now on, this one will make sure Lahini knows how much she means to us.
You did it again, Champion of Anequina! I'm almost tempted to abandon my post and follow you around. See what kind of adventure you get into next time.\n\nAlmost.

Zamarak suspects we will be making many journeys between Rimmen and Senchal. Queen Khamira isn't fond of simply sitting upon her throne day in and day out.\n\nIt is good that Zamarak never stopped his training.
Impressive portal magic … for a Khajiit.\n\nYou should probably get moving, though. Queen Khamira doesn't look like she can maintain the passage much longer.
Lahini came here with a jekosiit in dark robes. She begged me to come with her and join something called the Order of the New Moon.\n\nI told her to get lost and they both walked out.
I'm sorry my father wasn't able to agree to your request. Hopefully you'll find another ship to sail you.

Once again, the Perfect Pounce sails under Za'ji's tender touch.\n\nShe is an impressive vessel, yes? Sleeker than a greased Alfiq and twice as fast! Swift enough to dodge any Dragonfire that comes our way, this one assures you.
Make sure you keep up, walker.
If you have any questions about your task, Blademaster Kasura would be the one to answer them. I am simply her humble student.

Remember, look for a lock box. That's where young Za'ji stored his most precious items. Well, before he acquired the Perfect Pounce.\n\nZa'ji will keep watch from down here. We only have one grappling bow, yes?

Did you see that? Whenever the bells chimed a certain way, a lantern would glow. \n\nNow that this one thinks about it, aren't those lanterns on the larger bells as well? Perhaps there's a connection.
Let's hope Nahfahlaar proves cooperative. Without his guidance, we'll never be able to recover this mask.

The bearded one speaks as though I am not perched within striking distance and can hear every syllable he utters. \n\nI might find his hubris amusing in a different light. But the light that remains fades as darkness comes.
Do'mazir is as stubborn as he is smug. You talk to him.

Each time we ignite the shrine's brazier, dark spirits are summoned. If we're able to defeat all those spirits, the shrine's lanterns light up.\n\nI'm willing to bet we'll need to light all four shrines in order to move forward.
To think that Ra'khajin would be the one behind this attack. It chills this one to the very bone.
I got a lot to learn about Elsweyr. Little talking cats, big talking cats, Dragons, Moon magic …. Glad I've got a guide like Marekki.

You will find a bell stand by the statue, much like the one in our temple's courtyard. After so many years of neglect, Tadali is sure the bells are heavily tarnished.\n\nYou should cleanse them before this one arrives.
Thank the Moons this one found you.\n\nYou need to head back to the sanctum. Sai Sahan wants to attack the Order of the New Moon. Something about Ra'khajin kicking the bucket and a divine mask.

S'rendarr sends me a saint! To sanctify the shoal you must seek the sacred shrines inside Moonlit Cove and sip from their source. Swallowing the sacramental waters will suffuse you with their sanctity, and the skooma.\n\nThen we send it out to sea!
This is a private event, walker. Move along.
Go talk to Skordo, yes? Tajahir's passing weighs heavier on him than he lets on.
Despite my rank, I defer to Captain Sai Sahan in this battle. You should speak to him about our next step.

Ah, walker! Thank the Moons! You will never believe what horrible things these slavers said they would do to poor Malahbu! You are a true friend, walker. A true friend!\n\nNow, you will help this one escape, yes?
Daini's friend, but no Daini. She all right? Y'ffre's bones, if that skeever Turo did anything to her, so help me …. Get me out of here and we'll find her together!
Do as Nahfahlaar says. Raise the Mask of Alkosh before him.
If you can recover the last of the gourmet moon-sugar, I have a plan that I think will impress my uncle and show him I am good for the family business.
I shudder to think what my ancestors would say if they saw this desecration. Ruptga forgive us.
Please, my friend, don't delay. The peace of Aetherius is so very close!
Why do you linger? You got what you wanted. Be off!

Moons' greetings, rhook! If you seek a job, you have come to the right place.\n\nTsaraba's friends here—Guybert and Bruccius—have pockets full of work requests just waiting for a brave hero to complete them. That hero could be you, yes?
I just need some rest. Thank you for helping me.\n\nPerhaps I can find a place to lie down. Just a moment's rest is all I need.
Maybe mother holds the quill in her mouth? Ha! Can you imagine that?

You'll find Za'ji farther ahead. He heard some bells and went running off.\n\nQuite bold of him. He may have a big mouth, but he's never been one for a direct fight. Has our little captain finally found his courage?
We're with you, no matter what comes next. That's what it means to be Dragonguard, yes?
Why didn't Nahfahlaar wait for us? We could have helped him!

Seems like Nahfahlaar is being chased straight to Doomstone Keep. It's a creepy old ruin, abandoned for centuries. The locals say it's haunted.\n\nActually, that sounds like a fairly decent Dragon lair, doesn't it?
This one is cleaning. You may help clean, or you may stop bothering this one.

Despite all that occurred, Maezi is glad she is on this run. Zhasim has much to learn about being a merchant, but he is very … interesting. This one is happy that the smugglers did not injure him too badly.
Ha! They said my concoction wouldn't work in Elsweyr, but Vigwenn proves the doubters wrong yet again!
This one suggests you step carefully, walker. Senchal is full of thieves and scoundrels, yes?
Guess the captain got the Pounce back. He always does. Not the first time he's lost it, you know.

Sorry you had to face that creature alone. That witch, Maefyn's, been locking doors, conjuring illusions, and turning rooms upside-down since we arrived. Luckily, I've got a strong stomach and a lot of patience.\n\nWell, maybe not a lot of patience.
J'saad … where did you go?\n\nOh, I'm sorry. My beloved was supposed to be back days ago, but so far I haven't heard a word. Please, don't mind me. I just need to watch for my beloved's return.

Thank the Hist someone arrived. You're not with the crazed cult out there, are you? \n\nNo, if you were you would have summoned the others by now. Please, help me. I've been trapped here for hours with no chance of escape.
Recreational or remedy? I prefer the latter but the former pays the bills.\n\nRegardless, I'll continue to deliver the product until the pain ends or my more aggressive suppliers catch on.
Juisa finally has some peace and quiet to catch up on her chores.
Another outsider. Are you here to cheat me, too?
We've dealt with more than enough of those Dark Aeon spirits. I want to see what happens when I sound my horn at Kaalgrontiid's black heart!
Found the Dragon spit I asked for? If not you could always get swallowed and we'll wring you out when you slosh back.
May the New Moon guide our path forward.
All right, the cart's ready. Now tell me what else you found out down in the Ratway.

The Icereach Coven's presence in Western Skyrim concerns me, but we need to keep moving. The path down is through those doors. Outside, I'll point you toward Solitude.\n\nGo to the city and warn them. Whatever the coven has planned, it didn't end here.
He's my father, but he never listens to a word I say.\n\nMaybe you can get through to him. You have to try.
You go on ahead. I'll make sure Lyris gets back to Solitude.
Svargrim has the manners of a rabid horker. How do his people stand him?
We need to get to the cavern quickly and see if Rasir is there.

Talk to Fenn. If he has any bright ideas, I'd love to hear them.\n\nMagister Fridelja has been studying the Icereach Coven medallion, but she hasn't had a lot of success. She seems even less confident about reproducing their protective enchantment now.
If you're going to make Svana talk to her father, at least have the decency to buy her a few rounds first. No one should have to stand before the old wolf in a sober state.
Just … need to warm up a moment. It's cold. It's so horribly cold.

Blade's edge, this is incredible! This meat will see us through the next few days. Longer, if we're careful. Thank you, friend.\n\nNow that we're not in danger of starving, we need to find our missing crew members.
You've done a great thing already, friend. I'm glad to see the crew looking better.\n\nBut there are still more missing, and I can't carry on without knowing their fate.
My child, it is a grace to see you alive and well. I've heard that we have been delivered from our troubles. Gods be praised.
Shor's cold nose! Take what you came for and be done with it already!

Farming life is hard this far north. Not much grows in the frozen ground. And we never know when Reachmen will decide they want to burn our crops.\n\nBut I've never done anything else. I'll raise these crops until I die.
Seeing Morthal once more provides some comfort. I only wish I could say goodbye to my parents. I feel better knowing that you'll deliver that my message with that locket.
When the last of my blood thaws, I'll start chipping away at the ice myself. I'm sure the Cormorant is as eager to be free as her crew is.
I have a feeling we're not done with the Icereach Coven just yet, but at least the Skald-King is safe.\n\nGo on. He wants to talk to you.
Thank you for dealing with that trouble in the barrow. Morthal appreciates your service.
Turn this place upside down. We need to find out exactly what the Gray Host has planned.
It's done. We killed my father and ended the harrowstorm. The city still stands. Skyrim still stands.\n\nAlthough the Tower of the Wolf may have been damaged beyond repair.
Go! If the storm gets any stronger, there will be no stopping it! Lyris and I will take care of things down here.
What are you waiting for? An invitation? Get moving and find a way to stop that storm.\n\nFenn and I will defend the gate from the harrowfiends. You have my word.
Held captive in my own dungeon! If word gets out, I would be laughed off my rebuilt throne—and rightly so!\n\nOn to business. I heard Lyris's report. Now tell me, what did you uncover?
I am neither jarl nor thane, but Svana asked me to come to Solitude to help petition the high king.\n\nHe may not listen to me, but I'll do what I can to aid the princess.
How could Meridia allow High Priest Varkour to become so … corrupted? Has she lost all power? Or worse, is she as heartless as the other Daedric Princes?\n\nRegardless, you must retrieve the relic!
Nowhere in these lands are safe. I've traveled all over and no matter where I go, there's always trouble.
If there's anything else we need to discuss, let's get it out of the way now, before we return to Solitude.
Please, hurry! Rasir is the only hope my pack has.
You'll want to turn back from this damned town, wanderer. Those savage Reachmen finally got what they wanted. Karthwatch is gone. And all that's left are husks of a once proud people.
I was honored to fight by your side. I've never thought of myself as a strong man, but you helped me do what was necessary. I'll give my life to protect Bjora and the others. Count on it.

There's an old hunter's path down the mountain that will lead us safely beyond Karthwatch. It's overgrown enough to hide the villagers from enemy eyes. \n\nGo find Bjora. I don't care where she came from — she's my daughter.

Thank you for finding me. You and Hafskjar pulled me out of a nightmare. I keep seeing the face of that horrific fanged man. But, I'm safe now.\n\nI want to get far from this place. These people are all I have left. We need to stay safe.
You don't listen too well, do you?\n\nAll right. Talk fast and tell me why I shouldn't rip out your throat.

Now, naturally you can't walk into a secret auction without the proper attire. Especially not the Sapphire Society's. Their events are outré and rare. Mind-boggling and taboo fare. No serfs at their affair! \n\nSorry, I can't help myself.
Svana hasn't come down from the walls since you finished that nasty business at the Tower of the Wolf.
You again. Well, make it quick before the next auction starts. \n\nAnd did you tell someone to clean up this wine?

I wish I could explore these ruins under happier circumstances. Of course, under happier circumstances, the Pyre Watch sentinels would still be alive, and they'd kill me before I could enter. It's a pickle.
You should have left me … go warn Solitude ….

Ah, the hero of Rivenspire. It is good to see you again. You helped this one's sister, yes? You have the thanks of House Ravenwatch, walker. We have little to offer, but our memory is very long.\n\nNow, you killed that monster Essenia, yes?
Let's search these halls and see if we can find out what Lady Essenia is doing here.
You'll have to forgive Phebe. She's still young … and for all her scholarly knowledge, she's prone to startling at the slightest provocation.\n\nDid you find anything worthwhile?
Go ahead and unlock the door! The sooner we solve this mystery, the better.
If you're done assisting Bavian, we should gather my equipment and begin studying that alchemical residue.\n\nOtherwise, I'll keep a low profile and wait for you here.
I should get back to the old wise woman who got me into this mess. She probably has some sort of natural Nord remedy for intestinal bark.
I can't believe I'm still alive. That place will haunt my nightmares long after my damned ancestor's ghost gives me rest.\n\nMay I have him, please?
Have you defused the explosives yet? If not, get back in there and get the job done!\n\nWe'll make sure none of those Reach bastards slip past us.
A number of good soldiers disappeared at the barrow. Find out what happened to them and you will have done a great service for our hold.
Fenn said to meet him on the far side of town. You lead the way.
You need to get back in there and finish what you started. Dragon Bridge is counting on you!
I'm afraid I have little to offer, traveler. There … there's been a terrible disaster in Karthwatch. \n\nI'd suggest you keep walking. Karthald is cursed and probably unsafe.
Are they coming out? I'm ready to loose some arrows!
You'd think the Reachmen took my arm clean off rather than just grazed it with the way Ena frets. She's a good woman. Thanks for making sure I got to see her again.
Mother Wolf smiles upon you. She has seen fit to join your pack and aid you in your hunt.

Well done, my friend! Before the witch could even begin her ritual, I saw the magicka disappear like the flame of a snuffed candle.\n\nThe witch and the vampire assassin fled to Kagnthamz, a Dwarven ruin. We can deal with them in there.

Fenn is with Old Mjolen at the Mages Guild. When you're finished with him, join me in the courtyard of the Blue Palace. I'm going to hold a moment of remembrance for this city. We all need a moment to mourn what we lost.

The elixir is my next priority, of course. As long as the harrowstorms are still a threat, we need a defense against them.\n\nAfter that, I want to examine the records we took from Greymoor Keep. I still think there's a cure for the harrowed in there.
Now we're finally getting somewhere. Help Svana clean up this mess as best you can.
The moment of truth. Let's see how Svana handles herself with the Skald-King.
Maybe we are being foolish. We've been seeing enemies around every corner for so long we don't know what an ally looks like anymore.
I haven't seen Princess Svana since we were children. She's … changed much, since those days.
Did the princess say something about an elixir? Windhelm will provide whatever resources are necessary to produce as much of an elixir as possible.

Thank you. Viggol may be an old fool, but he's my old fool. And Gods damn it, I don't know what I'd do without him. \n\nYou'll find him in the mine. He can't have gone far. I was giving him an earful just a few minutes ago.
A blade made of chitin … how odd. I've never seen anything quite like it. The craftsmanship is unusual, too.
Go on and speak with Mazog. She'll help you see the wisdom here. \n\nCheck the storeroom under the longhouse.
You see? Harmless.\n\nCome on. We still haven't found Mugha, or some of the other miners. Let's move.
Gather up all the meat in the traps, and I'll tell you where the key is.
<Pickle looks determined. He wags his tail.>
Regardless what happened with Mazog, or my feelings about Chief Urzikh, Mugha is kin … and a friend.\n\nI'll get him to safety. You just need to clear a path.
