Steel and stone, am I glad to see you! I thought we were done for.\n\nListen, there are still miners that need help. They're trapped behind a tunnel collapse down below. I tried to dig them out, but those creatures started gathering. I had to run!
You cleaned out those monsters, right? Don't worry about me. I'll just catch my breath and head down.\n\nGo on and find the others.
You there! I bring an urgent message from the Skald-King.
The mushroom plays an important role in the chaurus's diet. With it, we're one step closer to creating an antidote for my sister. Let's keep looking.
Oh, thank Meridia! The priests and pilgrims of Kilkreath Temple, we need assistance. A great and terrible storm struck, and so many of us were lost.
This shortage of workers plays havoc with my ledger. Would you by chance be interested in a job?
Do you know what happened to my Nel? Did those rotten Frostbite bastards turn on her, too?

Raynor wants you to clear a path? Ugh. I suppose I don't have much of a choice. Once Raynor sets his mind to something, he doesn't make a habit of changing it. \n\nI guess I'll make sure he doesn't fall into a hole or something while you go on ahead.
You best go check on whatever, or whoever that is up there. Be careful.
You need to repair the machine! Need I reiterate that time is something we do not have? Hurry!

The Dragon Cult's lair, Dragonhome, is farther inside the cave, as is the altar where you'll place my belongings. You'll need to put me inside your pack so I can direct you and offer guidance. \n\nDon't make a fuss of it.
It boggles the mind how such tiny nodes could power a ruin as large as this.\n\nEvery time I think I've reached my capacity for surprise, Dwemer technology astounds me once again!
There's someone down there! We must seal the tomb, come on!
There has to be something in Overseer Urlvar's office. Either steal his key while he's not looking, or pick the lock.
Rigurt needs to taste this boar for himself. Nothing better than fresh Hagraven squeezings!
Fight on, my friend. We will follow soon, I swear it.

Fill the locket with Freiwen's memories. You won't need much as it holds a great deal of her energy already. Seek them out at places she frequented, like by the water or her house.\n\nReturn to me when it is done.
This entire charade is ridiculous. No one will listen to a word you say.
By Mauloch, I've never seen anything like these creatures! Horrible scuttling things and tiny, shriveled monsters.\n\nThere's not enough iron in ten strongholds to fight off beasts like that!
You did it! I can't believe it. You brought my Freiwen back to me. Thank you. \n\nI have so many questions for her. And the Jarl, he still doesn't even know! We must … phew… please give me a moment.

Arkasis seems to be working from someone else's theories. Old theories. I've seen draugr with younger looking skin than this parchment, but this handwriting seems familiar to me. Where have I seen this before?

These documents are a treasure trove. Papers that go back into the First Era. All of them detailing parts of the Gray Host's history.\n\nLady Thorn's connection to the Host are deeper than I realized.
I hope we survive this, if only so I can tell my daughter the tale. The time I saw warriors fell a Sea Giant! Ha! What a story.
Something is off about all this. Svargrim has always been stubborn, but now …?
How can this be? The high king, sacrificing his own people … it's so hard to believe!

You're back! Thank Kyne. Master's been muttering like my great aunt Hjolren. She hit her head on a stone, see? Now she says all kinds of terrible things—just low enough that you can't hear it.\n\nYou don't think my master hit his head, do you?
Borfree, is that you? Listen closely, you insufferable clod! I need you to find my notes and—\n\nWait. You're not Borfree. I can tell from the lack of heavy breathing and sniffles. Who are you?

Things are coming to a head and they need you in the Blue Palace! You heard about High King Svargrim, right? What am I saying, you were there! Of course, you were there!\n\nBut Princess Svana, she wants all her allies around her for this.
What do you want? Can't you see I'm not interested? Go bother someone else.
Quickly, assistant! Open the door!
Please leave me if you still have business with Thane Svyne. I think I need to be alone for a while.
You've brought Maelmoth's journal back? Good.\n\nI assume that the mad mage's ramblings did not lead you and your greedy Dark Elf friend to any fabled treasures.
Was it in there? Were you able to kill it? What happened in there?

Now then, we should begin your education in earnest.\n\nI suggest you speak with Gabrielle Benele. I can provide some scholarly advice, but when it comes to using the Antiquarian's Eye itself, you'll find no better teacher than Gabrielle.
Have a care around Verita, friend. She's in a foul temper. Slept poorly, I imagine.\n\nGiven the state of the beds here in Skyrim, I can certainly empathize.
How would you proceed, if you were me? Should I tell Gabrielle I'm confident in my theory, even if it gets proven wrong later? Or should I only say what I did and leave it for others to decide?

Don't fret. I mean, sure, it's not as if we're learning to boil rice down here. But someone with your innate talents should take to the process quite well. And like most things, you'll only improve with practice!
This is a mess. Over half our workers are wounded. And where is our chief? Bickering over who's to blame, no doubt.
We're being worked to the bone. This is how accidents happen. \n\nChief Urzikh says we have to work hard to survive now, but what kind of life is this?
I should have tried to kill that Sea Giant the moment I laid eyes on it.
What was that? You don't think those creatures got to him, do you?\n\nWe can't stick around to find out. We need to move!
A lifetime of fighting is finally catching up with me.

Have you heard tale of Jhunal, friend? The Imperials call him Julianos and claim him as one of the Divines, but few remember his true origin here, in the snowy lands of Skyrim.\n\nCan I interest you in a book on the god of knowledge and wisdom?
The Jarl of Morthal is a tough old goat. At least we can count on him to give the high king a kick in the arse.
Karthwatch has fallen? That can't be true. They were the shield of the kingdom!\n\nIf these storms could destroy Karthwatch … what about us?
The history of Skyrim is a perilous one. Never forget that.
You! I saw you enter the barrow with Lyris Titanborn! Morthal owes you a debt, friend.

Jarl Reddharn doesn't abide threats against his people. Svargrim may be High King of Western Skyrim, but I know who I can count on when things get bad.\n\nIf these storms come for Morthal, the jarl will act.
Thank you for everything. The people of Dark Moon Grotto will never forget what you've done for us. \n\nWe will rebuild. And we won't let what happened to us at Greymoor Keep continue to haunt us.
Arkay, preserve us from the terrible fate lurking below us.
Ugh, my head is still swimming from that fall. Don't know if I need an alchemist or a brewer.

You're a lifesaver! Literally, if all goes well.\n\nFirst, we need to find a way into the keep. Greymoor elites and their death hounds guard the main gate. No use trying a frontal assault. We've got to find another route. A postern door or something.
We could ask this lot for a clue. You know, if they weren't catatonic thralls.\n\nHave a look around. We're missing something. I can feel it.
Have you seen the note? If you seek companions for your adventuring, look no further! This one can help with that!
You again? What, you fancy me or something?
Make sure Hraldi gets his arse in that lodge. I'll pull myself together in the meantime.

A sad day when a man has his livelihood stolen. \n\nI went home yesterday with a full catch and just like before, it got stolen right out from under my nose! Every night's the same. Doesn't matter how much I get, it's always gone come morning.
A watched sausage never dries, so my father said. I suppose talking to some stranger is as worthwhile a way to pass the time as any. \n\nWhat do you want with the likes of me?
Speak with Tranya. She needs to know what happened.
You kept my brother safe and made it possible to heal my sister.\n\nYou have my thanks, traveler.
Father used to tell stories about the monsters that hide in the woods. Spooks and demons that attack at night and eat you alive. That's why I never leave Morthal. It's nice and safe here.
Take my advice and stay clear of Karthwatch, friend. A devastating storm blew through … and it brought with it monsters! Truly it did!
I doubt the Lady has seen this many guests at her home in centuries. She may be … hungry for company. You'll need what I know to stay alive.
I had business here in Hroldan Ring, but now I need to get to Lost Valley. The rest of the Ghostsong clan will be waiting for me.
Go wait for me by the cart. I promise I'll join you soon. I need to take a look around. Consider everything we learned.\n\nWe'll travel to that island and see what's in the castle soon enough.

My friend. I thought I could catch Rada and Lady Belain. Convince him to ….\n\nAnyway, I'm sorry I failed us. They acquired the keystone and escaped across the river. Toward that Dwarven structure in the distance.
Quickly, my friend. Speak to the shade. There's no telling how long it will persist.

I wondered if you were going to return, harrier. The worms and ghosts wouldn't stop whispering to me. Talking about dark doings and stirring evil, but they were deadly silent about you.\n\nDid you catch up to Lady Belain?

I can't believe that Bradan and all the members of the clan would go along with this willingly. We need to find them.\n\nAnd if any of the Ghostsongs try to stop us … well, they seem to be willing to die anyway. More's the pity.
You're the first thing I've seen that isn't an undead monstrosity. Lovely. Are you with the garrison? Please tell me you're here to rescue me.
You don't look like a refugee. Are you a soldier come from the garrison? What news of the Imperial attack?

I am sorry I cannot be more help to you. All the fighting and running has worn me out.\n\nOnce we are free of this place, you have my word that I will do anything you ask. Upon Leki's blade, I swear it.

Rada has started the ritual in his sanctuary realm. I can feel the pull in the darkness. Soon, the Darkstorm will consume the energy in the Dark Heart. Then more people of the Reach will die to feed the Heart and power this apocalyptic storm.
Y'ffre's barky backside! He was right there! Can we go after him? \nVerandis must know how to do that. Talk to him!
If Rada al-Saran thinks I won't follow him to Oblivion to end his miserable life, he's got another think coming.
I can't tell if Rada al-Saran is playing with Count Verandis's emotions or is totally serious with these offers.\n\nPlease, see how my father fares.

I may be an Imperial, but I've served the city of Markarth since the days of the Longhouse Emperors. I've grown to love this land and its people.\n\nThat's why I agreed to stay on and assist Ard Caddach. Good administrators are hard to find, after all.
Nighthollow Keep is down in Blackreach, east of the Library of Arkthzand.\n\nVerandis is there. He's waiting for you before he continues his search for the Dark Heart.
Let's get out of here, my friend. I'd rather talk away from this source of darkness.

I started out seeking information about the Gray Host only to discover that my mentor had a hand in their creation.\n\nAs angry as that made me, I was comforted to know Verandis opposed their war. And now he's back. I … I don't know what to think.

You have no idea what torments I suffered in Coldharbour. I appreciate the efforts you and Gwendis went through to rescue me.\n\nFinish your business with my ward. I … I need a few moments to collect myself.
You need to get to the orrery chamber in the Library of Arkthzand. Verandis is about to go after Rada al-Saran, and we can't let him do that alone.
That magnificent bastard really did it. He brought them back.
<<<1>> wrinkles her little bunny nose. It's adorable.>
Something went wrong. I've never seen the ritual pyre flare like that.\n\nGo check on Shaman Ulvoch. Make sure he's all right.

The ritual was a success and the Karthwasten wards have been restored. Once again, the spirits and the Crow-Eye clan are in alignment. We owe you a great debt. \n\nSpeak with Apprentice Fialyn. She shall reward you for the help you provided this day.
Adusa supposes that outfit will work. Provided Boss Trenlor and his court are suitably intoxicated by the time you walk in.
It's the scamp! Welcome back, scamp!\n\nYou ready to give it another go for some more of our sweet plunder?

I've been watching, but Lady Belain hasn't returned to Understone Keep yet. I wonder how the ard plans to deal with her.\n\nSpeaking of Ard Caddach, will he meet with me now? Will he help us stop Rada al-Saran and the Gray Host?
Try as I might, I haven't been able to penetrate the wards on the door into the orrery. The Dwarven magic is too powerful. Without a keystone of our own, we'll never get inside.
I want to check on Verandis one last time before I return to Markarth. All this talk of a connection to the Dark Heart …. I don't like the sound of that.\n\nBut you did good, today. Real good.

Watch your step in Nchuand-Zel. From what we could tell, the Gray Host was gathering there for days before the attack. Even without the vampires and werewolves, there are old traps and metal monsters to contend with.\n\nDwarves never did like company.

Once you reach Boss Trenlor's court, remember to act like you belong there. If they think you're just one of the servants, most of the vampires will ignore you.\n\nWe'll join you once Boss Trenlor is weakened by the darkcap.
The outsider returns! Give me a moment to finish what I'm doing, then you can tell me about your hunt.
Stay sharp and keep alert on your way to Understone Keep. The Gray Host could attack again at any moment.

Quickly, my darling, put those clothes on.\n\nThe sooner you give Trenlor the darkcap mushroom, the sooner we can save the Lothid clan. Then Kathad can decide if he wants to go with Adusa. Or stay with me.
There's an out of the way chamber in the rear of the keep where you can meet.\n\nNow, I should find the ard and make sure he thinks before he speaks.

Didn't expect you'd find me here. Thought this spot was a little more private.\n\nThis is Sai Sahan. He's … a friend. A close friend. We used to travel together with Emperor Varen, before things went horns up.
Welcome to the Ravenwatch. I suppose that makes me your superior now. I'll try not to let it go to my head.\n\nI actually have your first assignment, if you're ready.
You seem more comfortable standing among kings and jarls than I do. Then again, you always did. It's good to see you again.

Thank the gods we have better matters to attend to than the deployment of troops and suspicions of treachery. For a man called Despot, the ard is in an agreeable mood.\n\nBut that's not your concern. It's good to see you once more.

I've need of a counselor. In spite of her treachery, Lady Belain was a canny advisor. I need that again now, more than ever.\n\nTell the witch, Arana, that I will offer her my ear if she will share her wisdom. I hear she's recently arrived to my keep.
My friend! It is good to see you triumphing over evil yet again! And you have taken good care of snow—our dear Lyris while I was gone as well. I am in your debt.
I am an advisor to the throne of Markarth and a confidant of Ard Caddach.\n\nYou … are not.

This is horrible. Nathari has convinced herself that she's doing the will of the Spirit Queen—and she persuaded at least some of the clan to go along with this madness.\n\nWe have to find a way to stop her!
These hills belong to the Reachfolk, rover. Turn around and go back the way you came, or I'll have your nose for a trophy!

My former sisters draw strength from the darkness gathering below. It's changing them. These powers of shadow are like nothing I've ever seen before. \n\nAnd each sacrifice makes them stronger. We need to catch Nathari and end this.
A bargain's a bargain, outsider. Go pick up my package, give it to me, and the map to Bthar-Zel is yours.\n\nYou have my word.

Find that keystone. I don't know what it's for, but if Rada al-Saran wants it, then we need to make sure to keep it away from him.\n\nVerandis and I will catch up with you after we track down Lady Belain.

The ritual, it worked! The last remnants of the storm seem to be cleared away … the worst of it is finally behind us. And thanks to you, we have our natural defenses in place again. \n\nKarthwasten is safe again.
We can't go after them with that mechanical monstrosity in our way!\n\nCome on, harrier! Hircine will guide our strikes!
Keep Arana safe, my friend. Without her, I'm not sure the rebels will honor our new agreement.

This door leads to the Choosing. Once inside, decide on the first path to take. The Rites continue until you destroy all creatures within.\n\nA rare offer of caution—the Hollows behave strangely in recent days. Stay wary.

This place … I had no idea! I knew the Dwarves created some magnificent structures, but this is amazing.\n\nAnd look, more of those void portals in the higher portions of this … the only word that comes to mind is … cathedral.
That was closer than I would have liked. We're lucky <<1>> found us just in time. I was on the verge of losing control of the relic.\n\nI don't even want to think about what might have happened!
Go east and sniff out the rebels, outsider. Maybe that will get you your meeting with the ard.\n\nNow I need to return to Understone Keep and report to Ard Caddach.

This is definitely the book I'm supposed to bring to Farrul Lupus. It looks exactly the way it was described. But, it doesn't have any words in it. Just these strange symbols ….\n\nWe have it now and that's what matters. A job well-done.
No sign of Lyranth down there. And I can't tell if my father is among the captives. We must get down there fast.
You found the shrine? Such good fortune! Now, all you need to do is light a candle, write your message, and then burn it with the flame. \n\nAt your own pace, traveler.

Thank you. Reachfolk are no strangers to feuds, but what the Thornroot clan did here was a mockery of our traditions. Strange that the punishment for their treachery came at the hands of an outlander.
This song … is this what Red Eagle shared with Rada al-Saran? What allowed him to reclaim his Shehai?\n\nI must ponder this.

Such skill! The speed, the grace. That dumb minotaur didn't stand a chance against you. One key lesson I learned while still alive—size doesn't always determine a battle.\n\nWhenever you feel rested, head back through the portal to the Choosing.
I think I understand. I think I know the meaning of this ancient song.
The Hagravens will regret what they did here. I'll see to that, I promise you.

Only a fool would allow strangers to approach in times like these. You'll find a knife in your gullet should you try anything.\n\nWe head for Markarth. You ought do the same. Dark things surround us and only stone walls might hold them back.
Get on with it. There is no need to prolong this.
What a relief to run into a familiar face out here, especially after everything that happened to me today.

It worked. I can hardly believe it. The fact that an outsider helped save our home is something that will take some getting used to … but thank you. Karthwasten would have been lost without you. \n\nI should not have judged you so harshly.

After everything I did to bring these clans here today, to help them end their bloodshed, you're just going to toss it aside?\n\nSpirits take me, this story of yours won't work! But now … it's all we have left. You've doomed these clans, outsider.
I saw the chief-of-chiefs' temper rise, but she's calm, now.\n\nI don't know how you figure into these happenings, outsider, but I don't like it. This is clan business. You shouldn't be involved.
Just when things were starting to get interesting between you and the chief-of-chiefs, you calmed her down. Whatever it is you're up to, outsider, remember the Eagleseers are watching.
Something has gone wrong. I can sense it. This must be your doing, outsider. I knew it was a mistake to involve you in our affairs.
I can see it on the chief-of-chiefs' face. The handfasting's nearly done, isn't it? Oh, cruel spirits! This is more than I can endure.

Perhaps you're right. Drisene will have a better life if she's allowed to follow her heart. It's not fair to stay with her just because of a promise I made ages ago … she deserves more than that. \n\nI'll do it, outsider. Even if it may hurt her.
Let's get to the end of this, then. For good or ill.
Eslyn and Madearn will have to return to their clan holdings soon. You may wish to say your farewells before then.
You seek knowledge, outsider, and I have told you all I can. The rest awaits you in the cave beneath this redoubt … if you and your friends are worthy enough to find it.
You heard Arana. We need to perform that ritual. Gather the components and return as quick as you can.

With your help, the hubris that clouded my sight has lifted. It is not by coincidence that these sacred relics were hindered in their journey to this humble shrine. The Hunt-Father tests us.\n\nHe tests me and my apprentices. And he tests you.

Our people prepare their entire lives for this day. If they survive, they become full members of the clan. Failure, of course, means death.\n\nAre you certain of your desire to take the Vateshran's Rites?
If you'd excuse me, I have work to do.
We've seen quite a few outsiders in here lately.
If you planned to harm me, the jaws of my wolf would already be around your throat. I guess that means you aren't an enemy.\n\nSo, what are you doing out here, wanderer?
Five-claw, it … Adusa heard that Verandis had been imprisoned in the Void. But he's here!\n\nForgive me. I'm glad to see you. It has been too long since our paths crossed.

Whatever you and the duplicates did, it worked. The main doors unlocked with an audible click.\n\nBefore we rush in and attempt to deal with the sorcerer, we should discuss our options. I discovered something unsettling in the ancient carvings.

I erect the spine of greeting, egg-friend. But I must also unfurl the flange of warning. Our humble shrine to Sithis has been thrown into upheaval by the dryskin outsider and her manservant.\n\nI suggest caution lest you get drawn into their mess.

Governor Keshu made the right call bringing the Ambitions here. Can you imagine what would have happened to Gideon if Mehrunes Dagon appeared over the Egg and Hammer?\n\nWe didn't just save Sombren and Calia. We saved Gideon! Maybe all of Blackwood!
I've been alone my entire life. First in my vault, then in my wanderings. I finally found a real family, and I let one of them get taken from me.\n\nI promise you, I won't allow that to happen again.

General Keshu will command the Black Fin Legion out here. I'm heading inside to oversee the brigadines on the battlements.\n\nI understand that your role is to protect the Ambitions and serve as the last line of defense. Strike true, mercenary!
Victory is ours, mercenary, thanks to you.\n\nI think you should talk to Sombren and Calia. Then we can discuss what has happened.
A missing servant? I wonder what that's all about?\n\nWell, let's head into the watchtower and talk to Councilor Abor. Hopefully it won't take a lot to convince her to return to Leyawiin with us.

That ward was more powerful than anything we encountered before. The amulet alone couldn't penetrate it. How in Oblivion did the Wood Elf accomplish that?\n\nNo matter. See what the cache contains and then we can talk further.

Come to watch the finest display of porcine pugilism to ever grace the realm? Or perhaps you hope to bring home the bacon yourself? You'll need an invitation from one of the Jester Court first, of course. Why not see if you can win their favor?
I still can't believe this is happening. It seems our past has come back to haunt us in ways we could have never imagined.\n\nI'll head to Leyawiin. I pray we'll all be safe there.
Are you here to speak with Councilor Sophus? I'm afraid my husband has taken our dog for a walk.\n\nIs there something I could help you with, perhaps?

For what it's worth, I believe Gavos speaks the truth. I can see great care has been taken for this anvil, in spite of the toll of years and the corruption of the abbey.\n\nZenithar has not fully abandoned this house.
There, the Idol of Xulunaht! We must destroy it, hurry!
The Waking Flame cultists created a distraction. And like raw recruits, both Eveli and I fell for it.\n\nAs soon as we left the castle, they swarmed the place and barricaded themselves inside!
Don't mind me. I'm just going to slip away when no one's looking.

Be careful, but do whatever you deem necessary to find out the truth of the Dark Brotherhood's presence in Blackwood.\n\nThe councilors and I will wait here in the castle for the scribe to arrive. Hopefully, we'll have information when you return.
I can't believe it. He killed my brother. He killed Destron!\n\nListen, sacrifice me. Let Sombren take my energy. Then you can kill Vandacia and save the fort.

I'm leaving this to you. My brigadines are soldiers, not investigators. Besides, I'd rather not send the entire fort into a panic.\n\nTalk to the other servants. See what they can tell you about Talaise and her actions today.
What an absolute nuisance this Baron Zaudrus has become. How dare they try to imprison me! And worst of all, forcing me to rely on you—a mortal!\n\nHe shall pay for this indignity.
Go on, you read it. I'm too nervous. Written words become all blurry and jumbled when I get nervous.

I've got a camp full of liberated hostages, and my scouts tell me there's a significant drop in Painted Eye activity within the fortress.\n\nBut I want to hear it from someone who's seen things firsthand. What's the situation in Borderwatch?
This is a new low, even for Quistley. In love with a murderous cult leader? He has the self-preservation instincts of warm bread. \n\nI don't think I can keep running after him. It's exhausting.
Ah, don't mind Seeks, it's just his way of showing affection!\n\nHe may not want to admit it, but he likes having me around. You'll see.
I may not give a fig for all this sorcery, but if the Painted Eye do then we'd better start mucking it up!
If you're here, have the Painted Eye gone? Are we safe?
I must remember that the Horn of Magnificence is only one part of Phalevon's legacy. In this case, discretion is the better part of valor. I suspect my ancestor never quite grasped that lesson.

I just finished telling Governor Keshu all about how we found the third Ambition. Listening to myself, I'm not sure how we accomplished that. Good thing Lyranth was there.\n\nOh, Keshu wants to talk to you about something.

The skull is in the treasure chamber. You can get there through the east door. Retrieve it and meet me at the door in the north.\n\nWhen you find me, I'll be in a meditative state. Present the skull and I'll do the rest.

Our parents went along with this madness. They allowed themselves to be sacrificed to empower Vandacia's ritual. To imbue us with Dagon's power.\n\nBut for what purpose? He said something about ripen and grow.
I didn't think that was how my story was going to end. I really thought we were going to win.

Interesting. I didn't expect to hear from Sombren again after he left despite my advice. But to find him in the presence of a powerful mortal and two other Ambitions ….\n\nBut where are my manners? Greetings, mortal. I am Xynaa.
If it's any consolation, most magisters aren't certain of a hypothesis until they test it. Our test just happens to have the potential for cataclysmic results.

Bastian doesn't seem very fond of Quistley. I can't imagine why. \n\nWe compared notes while you were talking with that simpering idiot. Bastian said he might have an idea that would solve things for both of us.

I suppose that even a blind vvardvark finds a grub every now and then.\n\nI would measure your expectations, however. Even with the source of the interference destroyed, Revus's experiment remains critically flawed.

Ah hah! Jad'zirri knew you would be back for more! One taste of her special cider is all it takes to have patrons begging like sugar-tooths! Er, this one assures you skooma is not in her recipe.\n\nWould you care to earn more of Jad'zirri's cider?

Your friend seems shocked to see me. How long has it been, I wonder? Many, many years, but I can only count them by feeling the lines on my face.\n\nIf the priest of Zenithar has come to pass judgment or absolution, please let him do so quickly.
Give Lalais my regards when you see her. I would want the Daughter of Sithis to know that I've been thinking of her.

Ah, I see my message reached you. While Governor Keshu takes care of Destron and Calia, we need to determine our next move.\n\nOh, I almost forgot! A courier arrived a short time ago. They're waiting to deliver a message to us.

Whew, all of this doesn't sit well with my special mixture. Got my head spinning like a maple seed. Would love nothing more than to sleep it off right about now, but I reckon here's not the place for a lie down.
Yes? Is there something I can help you with?

You've spoiled everything! You and that lumbering oaf my father insists on sending to make my life miserable. And whoever that Dark Elf is, barging in and ruining my life!\n\nWho do you people think you are?

Ojel-bak, the pit of the outsider. It's a natural formation located south of Stonewastes. Just proceed carefully, as it lies in the heart of Sul-Xan territory.\n\nI suggest you meet Eveli on the outskirts of their territory and go from there.
Tava's feathers, this is so exciting! Who else in the world has a ghostly beau to talk to? Other than crazy spinsters, I mean.\n\nWhat an adventure!
Let's go around the building and find the door to the pantry. Maybe something down there will suggest what happened to Talaise.
From the tremor in the Wood Elf's voice, I suspect the Waking Flame cultists have arrived.\n\nGo, help your friend. I shall see to the safety of the twins.

You … you can see me? It matters little. The miseries of Castle Giovesse bind me here—bind all of us here.\n\nWe are cursed! Our gardens wither. Our once great walls crumble. And my gentle son feels nothing but heartache.
Forget me, just save the others. Those Argonians are working them to death.
We successfully destroyed almost all of the remains, but the Shadowscale with the missing skull is cause for concern. \n\nI believe those remains once belonged to Ajum-Shei.
It seems Lady Yisara's made her decision. I sense that my time here nears its end.
This won't harm Cres, but I can't help but feel like I'm snuffing them out.
It was a fool thing of her to run off like she did at a time like this. Her mother needs to watch her like a hawk even if there's nothing wrong with her.

Cylle lead me to our old swimming hole. Hadn't been there in decades. She dove right in, like we did as kids … I—I looked away before she struck the water. She hit hard. When I screwed up the courage to look, just inky black water. She was gone.
Leave me to my horses, stranger. They're the only company I trust these days.
Pour some water on him so he starts singing. This has to work.

All right, you heard Lovidicus. Time to get back to work. While the councilors stay safe in Leyawiin Castle and wait for the scribe to arrive, we need to find out what the Dark Brotherhood is actually up to.\n\nShow me that letter you found in Gideon.
Councilor Lovidicus fails to see the threat right in front of us! The Dark Brotherhood must be rooted out like weeds in a garden before it's too late!\n\nTalk to him and make him see reason.
I am Keshu, called the Black Fin. I have the honor of serving as governor of Gideon. If there's anything you need, please let me know.
I have no intention of being dragged back to that prissy councilor and his angry little beard.
All right, so we're awake. Dreams shattered. A life of brooms and boredom ahead. Happy now?
So what shall it be? How would you like to conclude our transaction? Will you be paying in gold or would you rather make the trade?
Please don't send me back. I promise not to be a bother to anyone ever again. Ever ever.

That's Percius Loche, one of the tailors working at this shop. He's kind of haughty, but he seems to know his stuff. You should do the talking, though. I've never worn clothes like this in all of my life!
Tell me the truth. Do I look ridiculous? No. Never mind. Let's just get on with this.

You talk to this Sombren person. Find out why Vandacia has him chained up like that. Oh, and ask him if he's an Ambition!\n\nI'll keep my arrows aimed at the door in case any of those guards come by to check on him.
The creepy black door … it talked to you? I find that both frightening and fascinating at the same time.\n\nAll right, let's go see what's on the other side.

Oh, it's you! You come at a perfect time, my friend! Care to team up again for another bout of heroics?\n\nI need your help avoiding a conflict. Tensions between my tribe and the Imperials who set up camp nearby are close to a breaking point.
I left the deciphered document right over there. Just try not to let my sister get into too much trouble, all right?
I'll go talk to my commander. Once we put an end to this threat, then we can turn our attention to improving this relationship between our people.
They wanted to take us away. Me and my sister. I … I couldn't let them do that.
Your friend sounds like she's in trouble. You should go to her.
After all the blame he placed on the Imperials, Olik is the one behind this? \n\nPlease, talk to him. I cannot bring myself to. I need a moment.
Looks like the portal sent us to another part of the Ayleid ruins. Let's see what's in this section.
You have a satisfied air about you. The aura of a successful prankster!\n\nTell me everything.

I am full of sap and fury at the actions of my tribe. Whoever did this will answer for this mistake.\n\nPlease, see if you can convince the Imperials to help us bring an end to this. Speak to the lieutenant, see what he thinks.

I cannot disable the lures, no matter how hard I try! My touch causes them to fade, yet they return within seconds. When I take my axe to the stone, my blade only dulls.\n\nI blamed the Imperials for our missing people. I was a fool.
Well, whatever the case. You needn't worry about Annyce for now.\n\nThank you for caring and good luck with getting to the bottom of all this nonsense.

Oh, thank Y'ffre you're back! Captain Rian and I … they tricked us! Lured us out of the castle.\n\nNow the place is locked down and I don't know if any of the councilors are still alive. I've mucked this up real good.
They seek to force the Duke to do their will. But he will not!
There's never enough time in the day for everything you need to get done.
This can't be happening. I can't be back here. This has to be a bad dream!
Where am I? Where's my gold? It was right here ….
There are no sweetrolls here. Why are there no sweetrolls?

Hey there, ojel. A strange moment to wander into the Stonewastes, I have to say. But, hmm, perhaps you have lucky timing.\n\nYou can see that our village has crashed upon some rough rocks. We won't survive much longer without a strong hand to aid us.

An outsider entering my home unbidden seeks death. You only live because the annoying blacksmith who joins you is familiar to me. But this pause is a temporary state.\n\nSpeak, then. What is so urgent that you would break into my home?
I'm not in the mood for conversation. Go chat up another stranger.

Leyawiin and its citizens are in danger, and Lovidicus is only telling the Chamber of Legates about this now?\n\nThis one knew we weren't done with Leovic and the Longhouse Emperors. She just knew it.
To keep a situation like this a secret from his fellow legates … what was Lovidicus thinking? And now Councilor Jirich is dead?\n\nWhen the river rises, everyone gets wet I'm afraid.
Those are Elossi's famous twin daggers. She claims they possess all of the speed and venom of a striking viper. Deadly in her hands.\n\nLet us get those back to her quickly.
Did you find the seeds? They are small and the plants glow slightly. You can find them to the east. Just follow your nose.

All right, my newest friend. By joining me you choose to engage in the challenge of my choice! Only through completing this test of your endurance and stamina shall I know your worth as a warrior.\n\nDo you believe yourself prepared?

Perhaps you are surprised to see me here ahead of you? Meer-Ta has many secret abilities that baffle the unlearned. But, you reached this far on your own, so I am impressed.\n\nI would ask your assistance in my attempts to clean out our guests.
I won't stand in the way if you wish to help her. It'll get her off my back at the least.

Damn Xigira! Damn her fetching soul to the blackest pits of Oblivion!\n\nI hope Dagon rakes her over hot coals for eternity for failing to accomplish whatever it was she was trying to do here. It's my only consolation.
That's it? No talking? No explanations? Just go home, little mortals?\n\nFine! Come on, let's get out of here.
I should have gone with her. She didn't want to risk it. She told me to look after our son until help came. \n\nOh, Bevene, I did that much …! I'm sorry.

I can't believe it. She seemed invincible through all this. If it weren't for my mother, we never would have lasted this long.\n\nI should have been stronger! I should have fetching killed these monsters before they laid a hand on my mother.
Hurry, hurry! My talons may be sharp and fearsome, but even they are not strong enough to break these mirrors. I need your strength, crow-friend. \n\nLet us take wing! The Court needs our help!
That was … horrible. Felt like my soul was getting torn out of me, little by little.
No use letting that weapon rattle around in your pack. Equip it, then I'll help you work out the cobwebs.
The tempest of light we saw above the xanmeer—it grows stronger with every soul taken from my kin.\n\nLet us hope we are not too late to stop the arrival of this Xalvakka.
Hmm. While I may avert my claws in greetings, I promise they still are sharp. \n\nCome, ojel. Speak. How did you arrive here? Especially at such a time as this.
For all the monsters and beasts that roam that swamps, I never expected my own kind would make me fear for my life.
Normally I love new experiences. It's why I got into exploring. Not that one. Never, ever again.
You've found the ledger, I take it? How exciting. \n\nYou should let Scipion take a look at it. He's always been better with numbers than myself.

Come to Leyawiin, Iulius said. We'll make a killing, he said. Now here we are, sharing a bed in a louse-ridden hovel, having to pawn my finest silks to pay rent! \n\nForgive the outburst. Perhaps I'm being too hard on my brother.
Commander Ortin gave you permission to enter the watchtower? All right, if he says so. Go on in.

If you don't mind, I'd like to have a moment alone with Granna Cerise. I don't know if she can understand me, but I figure I should pay my respects.\n\nI'll catch up with you on the way back to Gideon.

I know Bastian and I haven't always gotten along, but I don't want to jeopardize this arrangement. My bride-to-be is from a very good family. \n\nI'm turning over a new leaf—I swear it. I won't need Bastian's help in the future.
I thought Otumi-Ra's hut would be a little more lively. I don't see why he brought you in here. Let us find out what he plans for us.
I may not be as spry as I once was. But I am still good with a bow and I know this part of the Grahtwood better than most. I can look out for myself if I need to.

You look like you've got your wits about you. Care to make a bit of extra gold working for Leyawiin's Ivory Brigade?\n\nI've been asked by my captain to find someone who can handle themselves. We need help with a delicate situation.
All right, we found them. But why's Sombren holding the Mysterium Whatchamacallit? He shouldn't be fooling around with that thing!\n\nYou talk to them, I'll keep watch, just in case.
Researchers shouldn't take their responsibilities so seriously. I'm getting a headache from deciphering all these codes.
Mercenary, you are to report to Leyawiin Castle at once!
When I figure out who's been impersonating the Dark Brotherhood, I'm going to give them a very stern lecture. With my dagger.
Let's get somewhere a bit safer before we speak again. We've contained it for the time being but even still, I'd rather we get some place cooler before we chat. Come, let's leave this place.

I am Countess Clairene Auzin. I had hoped that my husband's troops would rescue me from that awful mine, but I don't recognize you. No matter—you have my deepest gratitude, strangers.\n\nHow did you know where to find me?
Mercenary! I was hoping I'd find you here. It seems they require your presence in Gideon.

I may stick around Blackwood for awhile. Councilor Lovidicus offered me a job and it might be nice to have a steady income for a change.\n\nFreelance scribes don't make as much as you might suppose. It's a cutthroat business.
Go on and talk to my grandfather, if you like. Maybe he'll actually show you some gratitude. I've got nothing to say to him.
Do I know you? I don't believe I do.
Well met, adventurer. I carry a message for you from the Black Fin.

So, any chance I could talk you into enlisting in the Ivory Brigade? No? I didn't think so.\n\nI want to thank you for helping us with all this. I hate to imagine what would have become of Blackwood if not for you and Eveli. I'm in your debt.
So? Did you just return the Shade Sickle? Is my lady appeased?
I whispered a prayer to the Shadow of Atakota and now you stand before me. An agent of change who appears in my hour of need.\n\nYes, this will do. I have a task for you.
It will be good to see Xocin and Xyria reunited. And I look forward to picking her brain in regards to whatever Dagon's forces have in store for us.
Of course Xocin still wants to summon her, I should have known.\n\nBut we must consider our course carefully. Having a Dremora in our midst could affect far more than just our own family.

It's you! It's actually you! My friends said you were a story—a myth. But here you are!\n\nIt is you, right? The hero of Tamriel! The slayer from the legends! It has to be. You look just like the paintings!

Well, this little misadventure wasn't a total wash. I did finally get to meet you. Don't be a stranger now. I'll expect Mirri to bring you by for tea and biscuits. Her father has a source for the best scrib jelly in Mournhold.
I owe you a debt of gratitude, my newfound friend. Not only for pulling me out of that vault, but for being willing to help me recharge the stone.\n\nI won't soon forget it.
Azura be with you, traveler. If you have business with me, I ask that you make it quick. I have many things on my mind.
My daughter leaves me to rot for decades and this is how I'm greeted? Roused from a neglected grave by a stranger who happens to share my blood and a filthy n'wah?
Oh, hello. Can I help you with something?\n\nI very much doubt you came all the way back here just to speak with little old me.
Oh, Takaano will get in trouble. Now that Caelia is keeping an eye on things ….
It's all coming together quite nicely, I think. All that's missing from the picture is Sevilo. I can't wait to see his outfit for our portrait! He told me he picked it especially for today.

Welcome to Leyawiin, citizen. Our city is a jewel on Topal Bay, safe from the ravages of that insane war. Thanks to the Ivory Brigade and Captain Rian's brigadines, we are totally secure.\n\nNow, please, go about your business and have a nice day.
By Azura's grace we'll cleanse Red Petal Bastion of this spiritual rot. If you lead us to the other wells of this corruption I'm certain she will draw the poison out of this world.
Despite what Lucilla might think, I had no foreknowledge of what—or who—we'd find here. The Dread Cellar was abandoned a long time ago, and I left it behind long before that.

Ah, your walk, your essence, your spirit! You strike me as one with many stories within you. But you also thirst for more. You are a leaf that welcomes the rain. A river that will never be full. \n\nAm I correct? Do you hear the water?
Twice now you have saved the people of Blackwood—and perhaps all of Tamriel—from the devastation of Mehrunes Dagon.\n\nForgive me if I say that I hope we do not meet this way again.
This day belongs to you, friend. I can't imagine how we would have stopped Vandacia or Mehrunes Dagon without your help.
Once again, I believe my work here is done. But if it turns out that Mehrunes Dagon needs yet another sharp lesson, I hope you'll think of me.
Enjoy your accolades and parades while you can. Take it from an old soldier: there's always another battle ahead.

Your legend within these lands grows, and it is well deserved. I hope you have no plans for moving on from here unnoticed. Believe me when I say that the more people speak of you, the harder blending in becomes.

I once read in a First Era tome that even the smallest flea might inspire the tallest Hist. You have inspired me in much the same way.\n\nI do not offer gratitude all that often, as you may know. But … the other Winds ask that I say thank you.

Strength! Vigor! Firm, hardy skin! How could a single person contain so many gifts? And yet, here you stand my raj-beeko.\n\nFrom the muds below my hut, to the heights of this moment. A legend grows before my eyes.
It seems Azura deigns to assist us. I suppose Weylin isn't completely useless after all.\n\nContinue driving the knights back and we'll clean up after you.

Our best hope lies in the Anchorite now. Show her the Daedric relic you recovered from her vault. Let her study it and extract its secrets. Perhaps some of her memories will become clear when she examines it.
Please find out what happened to Pibiha. Who knows what those unclawed cultists are doing to her.

Go, go! The Crowborne Horror must be defeated, child!\n\nWe have taken a great risk by pulling it closer to our realm! If you don't enter the portal and defeat the creature soon, we will all suffer the consequences.
The thought that Martus will just get away with all he's done doesn't sit right with me, but taking his life wouldn't make me any better.

My powers are gone. I'm honestly relieved. Having all of the Ambitions' abilities inside me at once made it feel like my head was going to split. \n\nI doubt Lyranth took them for my benefit, however.

Oh no. Without my power, I no longer possess my piece of the egonymic. Is that why I feel so … empty?\n\nThat means Sombren has two parts of the egonymic now. He might even have Destron's. Is that how he summoned his spirit to fight you?
Questions about the Order of the Waking Flame still linger, little mortal. And the danger posed to your plane of existence hasn't abated.\n\nWe can still help each other, if you are willing.

I have always been fond of Fargrave. One can find such interesting things here. I am rather pleased that you did not allow it to be razed to the ground by Mehrunes Dagon's hordes.\n\nAnd I do find all that talk about conquest and destruction so boring.

Ah, adventurer. The Dread Lady has told me about your exploits at her side. Lyranth considers you to be quite competent, for a mortal.\n\nNow hear the words of her prophet and be enthralled. I bear a message from my lovely and powerful mistress.
I'll meet you at the Isle of Joys, we can explore it together. I'm sure we'll find whatever it was Emperor Moricar was talking about there.
That fool Ambition! He will ruin everything!\n\nYou both need to come with me. Sombren has turned to Mehrunes Dagon, and he plans to take Calia and the Anchorite with him. We must stop him!
I'll be right behind you, I promise. I just want one last look around. This place … home of the beast who killed everyone I know. I want to remember what I hate.

I might have been incapacitated, but that didn't hinder my senses. I knew I saw the wounded cultist near my coffer from the corner of my eye.\n\nFind him and recover what was stolen from me, little mortal. I will follow when I can.
I cannot open a portal this close to the cataclyst. The energy it throws off is … not conducive to my magic.\n\nLet's keep moving, little mortal.
I expected Dagon's bootlickers to have grander accommodations than a simple cave. Look around and find my relic, mortal.

I know I agreed to take part in this ritual, but now I'm not so sure. Since my memories all came flooding back to me, I haven't been able to make sense of a fraction of them.\n\nI'm not sure what Madam Whim will find, or if it will actually help.

Lyranth asked me to help the Anchorite sort out her restored memories, so I devised this ritual. Take the memory vessel and we will begin.\n\nThis is a delicate process and I make no promises. We may learn what Lyranth wants, or we may not.
This obscure corner of Oblivion is known only as Fargrave. I certainly didn't expect the portal key to lead us here.
Why are you still here? The Dread Lady is done with you for now and she needs her rest.\n\nIf she requires your assistance in the future, I'm sure she'll find a way to get a message to you. Now go.
I think we need to ignite the furnace to melt down that slag. Hopefully, that will release whoever is trapped inside—whether it's really Emperor Moricar or not.

Valkynaz Nokvroz and an entire cohort of Dremora attacked the portal to Deadlight. They overwhelmed and eventually shattered the ward. Rynkyus and I were forced to retreat.\n\nIt seems I retrieved you just in time. Wait, where is the Anchorite?

All right Selveni. Now you just have find a way off this plane. With its lightning strikes, monsters, and murderous, blood-thirsty Daedra.\n\nNo. Be positive. You saved two spirits from the heart of the Deadlands. You're a hero.
Let's keep going. I don't want to give Sister Celdina another chance to slip away from us.
Where is Lyranth, mortal? As you heard, the Bladebearers have found Sister Celdina and her cultists. The Waking Flame has nowhere left to run.

You continue to impress me, mortal. You confronted Nokvroz's churls, survived the Blood Pits, uncovered the secret of the Anchorite's mask, and determined the location of the Riven Cataclyst.\n\nEven Rynkyus is impressed, which is noteworthy indeed.
Finish this business with the mortal cultists and their device swiftly, master. Then you can help me visit the torments of a thousand shattered souls upon Nokvroz for his treachery and impudence!
Did I happen to mention that this isn't my true form? When I return to my greatness, you will have to travel in my pack, master!
Some of my missing Kyn have been recovered, thanks to you. A sensation of gratitude, directed at a mortal. How unusual.\n\nYou should tell Lyranth what happened at Fort Grief.

Faven planned to attack Daedra. Attempt to push us out. And it would have failed. The mortals don't have the numbers, the strength. And we would just keep coming.\n\nWon't happen now. But we needed him to remove the Waking Flame. No leadership now.
So Sombren and Calia came here at some point, after they left us and went to the Deadlands? I wonder what they were looking for.\n\nSo, anything good in Sombren's diary?
You have the components my mistress sent you for? Then add them to the cauldron.\n\nQuickly! Never make the Dread Lady wait when she demands satisfaction.
Fargrave connects to multiple planes of existence, but that just means more work for me. I'll never get everything done.

I did not ask to get tossed here like old gnawed on chicken bones. But I have done the best I can considering the circumstances. \n\nWretched Spire requires my leadership. Else it descends into lawless chaos like the storms that surround it.
Back to Fargrave? Good. I could use a familiar place right about now. I'll meet you at Madam Whim's.
My father will speak with you, but don't expect him to cooperate. He can be quite stuck in his ways.
No, no. The knowing is worse. Don't make me stare into the fire. The pyre. Dagon's desire.\n\nLook away! Look away!

Speak to your allies if you wish, but do not dally. Sombren grows closer to Mehrunes Dagon with each moment that passes.\n\nWhen you are ready to go to Destruction's Solace, we will move on your word.
Hurry, master! Do not stop on my account! You must prevent Sombren from giving his power to Mehrunes Dagon!

Unlike others of my ilk, I have no particular interest in open battle. I leave the assault on the summit to you and Rynkyus. The Anchorite, the Bladebearer rearguard, and I will catch up once you locate the Riven Cataclyst.

How many Daedra does it take to create these new Incarnates? Do the cultists try again and again until they find one that can withstand the transformation?\n\nIt's strange, but I think I actually feel pity for the Dremora.

In the likely event that Valkynaz Nokvroz captures you, I hope you'll have the discretion not to mention my involvement in this scheme.\n\nOh, and don't forget Arox. He would be crushed if you left him behind.
To the volcano, go! I cannot suppress Arox's curse for long.

Good hunting, mortal. My Bladebearers and I will draw the ire of Nokvroz's army while you infiltrate the keep.\n\nIt is a great opportunity to prove the might of my clan. Today we repay Mehrunes Dagon's servants with pain and sorrow!

I will lead my scouts back to the portal. Make sure they return to the Deadlands safely. Then I will meet you in this citadel Dothaz spoke of.\n\nThere must be a reckoning for what they have done to my Kyn. It is the Bladebearers' way.
You have to find Sombren! He can't give his power over to Mehrunes Dagon!

Lyranth is correct, master. Before I was cursed with the form you see before you, I commanded Ardent Hope. I know its many rooms and passages as well as I know the back of my tail!\n\nAnd you will need me when you confront the traitorous Nokvroz.
Do not fret over the Dremora's deception. It is her nature to be selfish. The battle here is done. Let us return to the Deadlands.
What is that scent? It is faint, fading now. The echo of a spell long expired, I think. Quick, master, search the cave!

You did it! You banished Mehrunes Dagon and saved Tamriel!\n\nHow does it feel? Being a big hero and all that? None of this would have been possible without you, you know. You were right there from the very beginning.
Pure luck spared me from the infernal device. And your timely arrival. I am … grateful … mortal.

See for yourself, my friend! The stage is set. The oblivious inebriates are gathered in befuddled groups. And the minstrels are so warmed up they're practically cooked. \n\nThe time has come for merriment!
We can meet up at the Bearer's Rest. It's the largest inn in Fargrave. Because of the crowds, we can talk safely there without fear of being overheard.

I'm done with the order! Let Sister Celdina send her Dagonists after me. What does it matter? She's going to destroy Fargrave anyway. If we're all going to die, the Bearer's Rest is as good a place as any to face the end.

An unusual city, Fargrave. They say those huge skeletons are all that remains of the beings that once carried it from place to place. This inn is named after them, I believe.\n\nBut why are you speaking to me? Ask the Anchorite about a codebreaker.
We can talk once we get out of this house of horrors and return to the House of Whims. I didn't really appreciate being put on display in this insane museum.
This door must lead to the Collector's galleries. While Gazmod gazes upon the Anchorite's mask, let us step inside and locate the Arox of which the Collector spoke.
Few things that walk the Deadlands can hear the name of Arox the Mutilator and not soil themselves!
An adventurer? Talking to me? \n\nPlease tell me you're here about a job and not because Vaveli didn't have the funds to pay you.
Oh, a new adventurer in the Tong's house? What can I do for you?
Oh! Did the Saraathu Tong hire you? Excellent! \n\nLet's talk. Which of my projects did you get hired to help with?
Good hunting, mortal.
Another new hireling? Do you know what you're getting into? The last group didn't respect their enemy. I ended up having to cure thirteen different time sensitive poisons.
I don't think we've been introduced, but you walked towards me with a lot of intention. It's very presumptuous of you. Are you on Saraathu Tong Business?
I'll meet you and the others in Nirn at the place you specified. Leyawiin, was it? \n\nWe'll talk later.
I looked everywhere and talked to everyone I could find. I even gave someone one of my arrows, and then he ran off with it! Ugh, this place!\n\nDid you find Lyranth? I'm at the end of my branch here.
Whoever you are, now's not a good time. I'm expecting a visit from an agent about a job I posted. \n\nUnless that's you. Please tell me that's you.
I cannot stop thinking about Blind Elegian. Why, and when, did I give him this amulet?
Mortal, you return. But I do not see my quarry with you. Explain.
I've never known the Grasp to be lenient, but if there's any justice, they'll acknowledge we turned ourselves in and get Elisa the Redmaiden she needs. She's looking worse by the minute.

After everything we went through, losing Minwileth, running through the Sever … to just end up back here. It's almost laughable.\n\nBakh says this isn't my fault, but he's wrong. We never should have come to Fargrave.
With the last arcane matrix restored, you just need to connect it to the remaining guardian stone. We're so close.

Eveli gave us a condensed version of what happened. I'm so glad to see you both safe and sound. You thwarted a plot that began before I was born. Now I am bound to no one, nothing.\n\nIt's almost bittersweet.

The small Wood Elf has an oversized persona. Rather like a Banekin, I suppose. \n\nShe informed me of the rendezvous in Leyawiin. Calia and I will be sure to attend. There is something I'd like to bring to your attention first.
Look at what poor Hezehk has been reduced to. Delivering messages to the likes of you.
I don't have time for dawdlers. Get the location of the portal from Skoedal and retrieve Uxark's hidden treasure.
Kynreeve Rynkyus is one of our clan's finest blades, mortal. Do not step between his edge and our foes.
Your path lies through the portal. Find our Kyn or do not return.
Did you see what happened here?
Maybe I worry too much, but I do not trust any cult that would advertise their group on paper. Paper is for printing truth, not spewing filth.
I travel around quite a bit, but always make my way back to the Impresario's camp eventually. If you're looking for me, that's where you'll find me.\n\nY'ffre protect you, mate!
You're not good looking enough to talk to Airlur. Freshen up and try your luck next time.
What sort of thief has to leave something behind because they didn't bring a bag? \n\nOh, don't worry, I didn't take anything from you or from Fargrave. Please don't report me!
There are so many new maladies to come to grips with here. I thought I'd be doing good in Fargrave, but it feels as though I'm barely making an impact. \n\nAre you ill as well?
Out of everywhere I've traveled, the best and most unique items are always here in Fargrave. It's inspiring, honestly.
Hey, don't talk to me! I'm in hiding!
Quickly! Use the sundial!
Top goods at rock bottom prices!
Good work with Sarydil. If you'd taken much longer, this idiot probably would have gotten himself skewered trying to play hero.\n\nStart searching for Varallion. I'll keep Jakarn on a short leash.
How did these scaly Elves learn of Za'ji's treasure? Surely he wasn't followed.\n\nNo matter! So long as we snatch up the designs and be on our way such details are moot.
This is it. Signal line never lies. Even if you want it to.\n\nYour fake came from in there. Guaranteed. Go see, yeah?
No mortal is worth my time. Come talk to me when you've survived a millennium.
My forays into the Deadlands tend to be short. And I usually avoid places like this. So let's be quick, figure out what's going on, and get back to Fargrave as fast as possible.
This may be where Sister Celdina fled to after we disrupted her ritual at the Shambles' bathhouse.\n\nStay alert and be watchful, little mortal.
It—it didn't work … I can't keep that up. I'd hazard to say the results were the opposite of progress.

Your odor precedes you, leaky skinbag. At least I could tune out the apparition, but your sweaty, reeking body would test even Lord Dagon's endurance.\n\nWell, go on, before your overwhelming miasma seeps into everything and drives away the fish.
I can always count on you when I'm in a bind. Good to see you again.
Call off your attack ghost! Shiro-dar knows when he is caught, but have mercy! No matter the size of this one's debt, Gilfrex gets nothing if Shiro-dar dies!
You're not one of my debtors … yet. But everyone in Wretched Spire needs something, and I provide. So what can I do for you, poor mortal?

Yes, you're the one. I'm certain of it. The Dread Lady was quite specific, though her description made you sound more imposing.\n\nNo matter. I bring you a message from my mistress, Lyranth the Dremora!
The swords carried by Clan Bladebearer are exquisitely sharp. Whatever fools sought to subdue them will learn that soon, to their sorrow.
This Bladebearer clan apparently carries a great deal of influence with the Daedra in Fargrave. I suppose I'll have to buy someone a drink if I want to hear the whole story.
Why do you wait? You're required at the House of Whims!
The Waking Flame cultists make bedfellows with Mehrunes Dagon and his legions, and then they're surprised when they wake up with a knife at their throat? They get no sympathy from me.
Any Waking Flame cultist that turns up on our doorstep looking to hide from the Daedra is out of luck. I can promise all they'll get is a bellyful of arrows.
More payment? I shouldn't have even bothered fetching this mortal.
The Stricture provides the means to resolve all conflicts. I shall interpret its intent.

Tell me the rumors aren't true, my dearest. Tell me the Anchorite is safe and sound and not in the hands of that vile Valkynaz Nokvroz.\n\nNo, I can see it in your eyes. Then promise me you will retrieve her. Fargrave needs its darling of the alleys.

Go on inside, my dear. Talk to Captain Kaleen and get her to tell you what happened to her ship and the ships of the other captains.\n\nI need time to review what else we discovered. Then we can start putting the pieces of this puzzle together.

Duchess Elea of House Dufort is hosting the banquet. She's decided to go ahead and throw the party, even though our guests of honor are still missing.\n\nGo to Castle Navire's courtyard. Introduce yourself when you arrive. Be discreet, please.
I'm a dockmaster, not a bloody mage. What does the lady expect me to do if her ships never made it to the docks in the first place?

Lady Arabelle explained that Guild General Quentyn chose to join the Ascendant Order. I knew he carried pain in his heart for the people he lost, but I never imagined his pain could lead him into such folly.
Oh! A traveler. I thought those vile knights had returned.\n\nForgive me. I must continue praying for the return of our idol. Without it, this tower's light will remain dark.
Greetings, traveler. Is there something I can do for you? Do you need a poultice, or perhaps an herbal tea?

I thank you for taking time from your own labors to complete this in the name of Zenithar and collaboration. \n\nGo in peace and with my thanks. For it is a singular individual who would stop to help an aging priest on the festival of his lord.

When I get Tarrinore out of here, we are going to have a talk about her hare-brained schemes.\n\nWould you see what she has to say for herself? I need to think about how I'm going to get her out of here.

Za'ji has decided. No more drinking until Queen Ayrenn is safely back in his arms! Er, maybe that was a dream. Never mind. But Za'ji wants the queen and Caska to be safe.\n\nHe will help you and Lady Arabelle foil these villains and rescue the queen!

Funny. First time we met, you were the one fished out of the water. Now look at us.\n\nI owe you a great debt. And I owe Dockmaster Arnauld a debt of a different kind. I visit High Isle often and I thought he was a friend. Bah!
If there is any way I can help with your investigation, I am at your disposal. I want to find Prince Irnskar as much as Lady Arabelle. More, even.
Privette's alive! What a relief! All those bones really had me worried. \n\nPlease get her out of that cage. The Hadolids might get angry when they notice what we're doing.

Hey there, good-looking. It's been a long time, hasn't it? I've missed our adventures, and I'm sure the feeling is mutual.\n\nLucky for you, I have one. It involves a secret mission, my missing lady-love and a mystery. What do you say? Want in?

You appear as if you expected to find me. I wonder, do you know where you stand?\n\nThat was the home of the long gone Knights of Death's Valor. Lord Leobert turned on his oath and cursed us with undeath.

If I knew someone like you would actually pass our way, I might've reconsidered coming in here alone, eh?\n\nThen again, maybe not. Our life isn't what I promised Vinilsare. I'm going to change that, no matter the danger.

Well! Nothing warms the blood like a bit of a scuffle, wouldn't you say? That mage underestimated me, the poor dear.\n\nIt's over now, at least. All that's left is to deal with this medallion and get it to High King Emeric.
I couldn't have done this without you. \n\nLet's see what the commander has to say, before I thank you myself.
I trust you can handle yourself in a fight, yes? Come on, we need to hurry. If Valessea is somewhere inside this gods-awful place, I want to find her before the skeevers do.

Why don't you talk to Tarazka? He's still cross with me over a little incident involving a card game and a circlet. Maybe he'll be more receptive to a third party. See what he knows about Valessea and where she might be.
Mother wants to speak to you first. She never likes to be kept waiting.

No, you don't know me, but I do know you. Keeping an eye on notable people while going unnoticed is sort of my expertise.\n\nThe only reason we're speaking is because I'm in something of a predicament.
Ugh … ow ….
Take the pouch of dispelling powder. Then give me a moment and I'll open a portal to send you to Windhelm. Please go quickly. Jakarn may have already delivered his first medallion.

You know, the crypts didn't seem to be the Ascendant Order's main base of operations. I say the next step is to find out who they are under those helms and where they're hiding. But I'm not in charge here.\n\nBetter talk to Lady Arabelle, I guess.
The late Captain Maul here is looking a lot better, for a ghost. Whatever you did must have broken the curse!

All the stuff Anton left behind makes me think he got into serious trouble. But we haven't found his body anywhere. That's some relief.\n\nIf we keep moving toward the stage that welcome sign mentioned, we might find him.
Oh, I recognize you. You're the hero of Windhelm!\n\nThane Mera speaks about you a great deal. What brings you back to these parts, friend?

Jakarn offered to escort me to Lady Arabelle. I'll try not to turn him into a mudcrab along the way. I'll tell Lady Arabelle what happened while you retrieve the medallions. Remember, the scroll said there were boats nearby to take you to the grotto.

I'll make sure Valessea gets back to the camp safely. I'm sure she'll feel much better with me at her side, most people do. I have a … calming presence. \n\nI'll meet you at Sareloth Grotto soon! We'll retrieve the medallions together.
I believe I have discussed all the business I care to for the moment. This is supposed to be a festive occasion. Please, mingle with the other guests. Enjoy yourself.

I'm not really sure why Elea Dufort insisted on going ahead with this affair. The guests of honor are likely dead or being held for ransom. \n\nI suppose if she had her way, she'd blame House Mornard for this debacle. She usually does.

We need to find the five medallions. The enchanted shell Valessea gave you should let you know when to use it. Maybe it tingles when a medallion is close?\n\nBut keep your guard up. If the Ascendant Order is here, we may have to get rough with them.
Hey there! Lady Arabelle sent me to find you. She wants to talk about everything that happened on Amenos.\n\nShe's waiting for you in the courtyard behind Mandrake Manor.

Try not to let anything in the scary jungle kill you. Just head north, go through the gate, and head north some more. I hear there's a Green Serpent camp out that way.\n\nHey, you got this! I mean, you probably got this. If anyone's got this, it's you.
Make yourself at home, good-looking. Since Lady Arabelle told you more about the secret mission than she ever told me, that makes you an official member of the team!
So the Commodore had the other captains take his idols for safekeeping. They're likely to be all around this cave then. I'm sure that tomb he kept close to himself.
Off you go, then. And be careful where you point that thing. \n\nThat staff's like me. It might be old, but it can still zap the ears off a rabbit if you aren't careful.
The Ascendant Champion didn't stand a chance! You were amazing! And slightly terrifying, truth be told.\n\nGo ahead and speak with Lady Arabelle. I'll make sure she's not injured.

Another adventurer sent by the Society of the Steadfast? They used to hire a better class of messenger, as I recall.\n\nSpeak with that uncouth ruffian if you must. I want to take a closer look at this medallion.

We must hold out hope that Emeric and the others are still alive. Without them, any chance for peace is lost.\n\nBesides, I'm rather fond of the high king. We've had many a laugh and adventures, Emeric and I.

It seems that my dear friend Louna brought me a savior. And I can see why! Someone that's as brave and strong as you makes the perfect choice.\n\nThose hunters might return at any moment. Please, kindly unbind me so we can flee.

Good health to you, wayfarer. I'm the captain of the Shackled Guar. Now tell me. What grand adventure has Lady Arabelle drafted you into and what does it have to do with me? \n\nTalk fast, mainlander. I sail for Amenos on the tide.

Although the necromancer has proven herself unworthy, I cannot yet allow you to pass. One more Test of Worth awaits you, a surprise to ensure you remember your lessons here.\n\nAre you ready for the Test of Virtue?

Another mercenary? Running a bit late, aren't you? This one has all the help she needs. They will already cost more than she budgeted for.\n\nYou do appear quite exceptional, though. Perhaps Amunara could swap out one of the others for you.

I'm astonished that Isobel decided not to take advantage of the Knight Commander's promise.\n\nIt's only a rumor of course, but some seemed to think that Dame Isobel rather fancied Lady Aurelia. More than just friends, don't you know?

We have more problems than we realized. Not only is Lady Arabelle certainly in danger, but now High King Emeric is as well.\n\nThe Ascendant Order have really taken to villainy, haven't they? Come on, we need to get inside.

Oh, good, you're all right. It seems our adversaries decided to send a message to all those in attendance—submit or die. A classic.\n\nDid you uncover anything useful before the Ascendant Magus made his entrance?

Didn't think I'd miss this little soiree, did you? \n\nListen, I have it on good authority—from a very accommodating chambermaid, in fact—that the duchess has been looking into the Ascendant Order on her own. Well, I've got a plan.
Our transaction was completed satisfactorily. It does not require further conversation, surely. I'm a rather busy woman.
Remember, you must be discreet. It would be scandalous if she were to be seen taking secret missives from secret lovers. \n\nScandal!
I'm honestly not sure if I am cut out for the life of a knight.

Well. I suppose luck was on your side today. \n\nI must say though, you and Lady … Dame Isobel were a bit sly at the Oldstone Woods. Not sure I'd call sneaking around and finding another entrance knightly behavior.

Our ship was attacked, by coral I think. It just… It just grew out of the waves and—I don't know what happened to the other sentry, Veslyn, or the Sea Elf prisoners we were transporting.\n\nI woke up alone on the beach.

I've got to get out of here! Why didn't I just drown in that shipwreck?\n\nThey turned them into coral. Sunigil—those Eldertide bastards turned him into this … glow. Then they fed the glow to the coral.
You and this druid have our thanks, mortal. You trusted us, and now the balance of nature has been restored.
I've known Isobel … Dame Isobel for many years. It was encouraging to see her push herself like this. \n\nI believe your able assistance may have also played a part?
We're entering Bloodmage Cassel's seat of power. Be wary, many a knight has met their end here.

It's probably for the best that Magister Irin speaks with you first. We fixed everything, but I still have a feeling he's going to skin me alive.\n\nI did learn a lot from this experience though. That's positive right? Put in a good word for me?
Get on the ship now, my friend.
A splendid gathering of grand people with small ambitions. Most come to such events simply to see who dressed the best. Or to catch sight of anything vaguely scandalous.
Excellent work, rescuing the Prince. The Skald-King and his son can be … well. Insufferable. \n\nBut these talks deserve a real chance. And you've given that to us.

Lady Arabelle wants us to be ready. We're going to Amenos to rescue Queen Ayrenn. And Caska, too, Za'ji hopes. This one's fur sheds with worry at the thought of his friend and first mate lost on that prison island.
Investigator Vale smiled wickedly. "You mentioned a hot springs, Lord Vance?\n\nOh, hello, dear. I was just … going over our notes. Did you need something?
Let's move! I want to get off this wretched island.
Let's keep going. A moving vessel makes a harder target.

Count Damard isn't here. But as we feared, he was planning to remove Duchess Elea from the picture. Talk to her. She may have seen or heard something that will help us. \n\nI'll be listening. And if she lies to you, I'll know.
Well, you're more merciful than I would have been. I'll look around a bit more, see if we missed anything.\n\nI'll see you back at the manor after you check the other sites.
I can't believe that mender fell for the old closed-for-cleaning line. Well, did you find anything?

Y'ffre's bones! The spirit of the grove is talking to us! This is … this is quite unprecedented!\n\nYou seem to have a rapport with the spirit, adventurer. See what it offers and find out what considerations it expects from us in return.

Thank the Eight you're not one of those druids. Hurry, get us out of here. The druids, they're using us to feed their coral. The screams—I don't want any more of us to suffer that pain.  \n\nPlease. Please get this door open!
An enchanted lodestone, a cracked staff, and a smoking fissure. \n\nAll left behind in a place once used by the ancient druids of the island. Curious.

This is an old druid ritual circle, but it hasn't been used in quite some time. I didn't even realize it was here.\n\nSomeone performed magic here recently, though, but it is not the magic of nature. Not exactly, anyway.
I'm not sure if I'm worthy of the title, but I will do all that I can to bring honor to the Order of the Albatross. \n\nIt's what Dame Madach would have wanted, after all.
Good day, stranger. Did I just see you speaking with my friend Armin? He is one of our most noteworthy successes at Steadfast Manor, or so I believe.\n\nHow can I help you?
I'll make sure Duchess Elea isn't stashed away aboard one of these ships here at the dock. You'd better go check the Silver Swan.\n\nOne or the other of us gets to rescue a duchess today. Not bad.
This is a plan! It is definitely a plan!
Ah, I found you! Thank Jode …. Sorry. We don't normally run this much at sea.\n\nBut we have a problem.
This plan is crazy. Like, Skooma Cat crazy.\n\nWhy do we never have anything good to drink when Captain Jimila makes us do things like this?

A good day for diplomacy, yes? Nobody died or went to prison, and the innkeeper was paid in the end. Now, would you talk to <<1>> about my scepter of office?\n\nI think she is still a little mad at me.
I admit it, I didn't expect to see you again. But your three friends finally came back to pay their bill. They even added a little extra for all the trouble.
The shoals are a graveyard, the final rest for vessels that met an unfortunate end in the straits between High Isle and Amenos.\n\nGo and help Captain Tsuzo, dear. He made it sound quite urgent.
I think this sorry affair is all settled, but you should talk to <<1>>. I would like to know that she's willing to put last night behind us. \n\nUgh. I can't believe I drank rotmeth.
You should talk to <<1>> and make sure we can put this whole event behind us.\n\nI can't believe I got arrested.
The idea that the monster who tormented me over these last few months presents himself to the world as a healer is … infuriating. I am ready to face Viralaine when you are.
We should go back to Steadfast Manor. I'm anxious to have some words with Master Healer Viralaine. And make him explain exactly what he thought he was doing with those poor souls in our care.
Those crystals will carry my calming song down to the Hadolids in the bottom of the mine.\n\nNow we just need to find where the Hadolids are coming from and see if we can keep them out.

The letters you found make it clear the Ascendant Order is preparing to launch a major naval attack on All Flags Islet. We must inform Lord Bacaro about this threat.\n\nI'll collect Jakarn and meet you back at Mandrake Manor.
There's never enough time in the day for everything I need to get done.

You … you're actually stopping to help? Everyone else ignored me or looked at me as though I were insane.\n\nMy husband and I, we were here at Amenos Station on business. Then the jailers grabbed poor Valentyn and dragged him away!
Unless you want to become a permanent resident of the prison stockade, just move along, citizen. I'm tired, I'm thirsty, and I'm not in the mood for gadabouts from High Isle today.

You get something? Let me see. Yeah, yeah. This will do nicely. Now go slip it into Yvara's bedroll.\n\nRemember, she's got eyes like a hawk. You might want to cause a distraction before you approach her stuff.
Up the ladder, my friend! And don't drop that gem, not after all we've been through to acquire it.

I see you convinced our royal guests to come to our little gathering. Well done, dear!\n\nNow for the tricky part—persuading them to stay for Lord Bacaro's talks. After so many perils, I suppose I couldn't blame them if they decided to leave.
Bring me proof that <<1>> is a skooma dealer. He must be hiding his contraband somewhere close by. All you need to do is trail him to his cache.\n\nHelp me catch a big fish, and I'll let <<2>> go.
<<1>> is right over there. He'll be able to tell you anything you need to know before we make landfall. Don't keep him waiting.
Seeking a commission with the honorable House Dufort? We need able hands to rid the Systres of a menace we've endured for too long.
