We'll wait for you to draw the knights' attention, then we'll seize the ship. \n\nGo on. We're right behind you.
We won't know what we're dealing with until we reach All Flags Islet, but I trust Captain Kaleen to guide us past the Ascendant Order's forces. Let her know we're ready to get underway.

This seemed like a great idea until we sailed into the middle of a battle. And it looks like the enemy has druids, too! Ah well, might as well make the Ascendant Order sorry they let us in.\n\nGo on, good-looking. I've got your back.
I've always loved the sea. Comes from growing up on Summerset, I suppose. \n\nBut what can I do for you, my friend? Don't tell me there are more rogue knights threatening High Isle.
After the battles we endured, I was hoping to find a celebration. Unfortunately, this inn is as dead as the elk served at the Skald-King's table.\n\nHave you come to drink with me perhaps, my friend?

Have I thanked you yet for all you've done? Not just for the alliances and Lady Arabelle, but for me personally? No? Well, thank you, my friend. I don't know many people who could have beaten the Ascendant Magus.\n\nBut what brings you to the temple?

Well, don't just stand there. Lady Arabelle is waiting at Mandrake Manor. Me? I'm going to find a nice strong drink and try to forget about this debt I owe. And that I actually agreed to go fight an army alongside that feisty old lady!
Za'ji loves stealing ships! All aboard!
Heh. I don't mind engaging in a little piracy for a good cause. Let's take the ship!

I've been sending messengers throughout the countryside, but so far I've only managed to gather a handful of knights. I was about to send them the order to head out, when I saw you approaching.\n\nDoes this mean you have news from Lady Arabelle?

We did it! That was intense! I'm glad Jhaka and Silverslip held off, probably safer that way for everyone. Now … we just breathe.\n\nSong looks exhausted, but I think she's all right. She's probably a bit overwhelmed right now. Could you talk to her?
This one has never had the heart to leave Skywatch. Perhaps the memories here are not always sweet, but they are plentiful.
The food here is greasy and the portions small. Just pretend I raved about it if you are asked.

I want that bracelet by any means necessary. But see that you don't get caught. I shall, of course, deny any knowledge of you, your friend and this conversation, should you be accosted. \n\nNow go. Shoo.
Hello, dear. Do you prefer maniacal despot or raving figcake as an adjective when describing the Ascendant Magus?
Jhaka is fine. Jhaka can keep up. It will be good to breathe fresh air again.\n\nLead on, friend of Ember. This one will follow you to the exit of this horrid place.

Apologies for our late arrival. Silverslip assured this one that you and Ember could rescue Song without our help.\n\nIt is a joy to see her alive. She has endured such horrors, and yet she still stands. Her strength is resplendent.

Sorry we weren't much help. Jhaka's still not up to full strength and I figured you and Ember had it covered anyway.\n\nI can't believe Song is here, and she's safe. I hope she doesn't recoil from me. Or hate me.

What are you still doing here? If you're not gonna join me for a drink, then take your sorry hides out of here! \n\nI'm too drunk and too happy and too … did I already say drunk? I don't wanna answer your questions.

I was so close to losing all hope. Then to see Ember again, my long lost sister, at my greatest hour of need, and now my friends … truly Tall Papa has me in his gaze.\n\nAnd with that evil relic destroyed, I am free. Freer than ever before.
Unless you're here to bring me another drink, get out of my face.
Looks like everyone's here. Let's see what Aurelia has to say.
I'm very glad you could join us. Aurelia has been quite eagerly awaiting your arrival.
I remember you! You helped Isobel during the Sapphire Tourney. \n\nOh, you do seem to catch me at my worst, I must say.

I finally have every piece of the Scourge of Sentinel's map, but everyone I sent to collect them died. Except you. I guess that means you're the only one who's capable of finishing the job. Interested in a partnership?
We're not gonna let Kiv hurt another soul.
Fight first! We can talk later!
Don't just stand there! Go and carve this oafish captain's name into the memorial so we can end this curse. I much prefer it when my head is only occupied by me!
Oh, do be sure to spell his name correctly. R-E-N-W-I-C.\n\nWho knows what could happen if we misspelled that body-thief's name.

Offer a prayer to Zenithar at that altar. Or, if that goes against your beliefs, I can petition Zenithar on your behalf. \n\nAll that's left to do is dedicate one of your day's labors to the God of Work and Commerce.
We've tangled with Sea Elves a few times. Nasty bastards. Show no mercy. They certainly won't.
Very well done. And he's still quite handsome. Once you've gotten what you need, Galedra and I will enact … the plan.
Baron-Admiral! You honor me, sir, but you should talk to my captain.
My friend! May I count you as my friend? You're very dear to Isobel, and she's very dear to me so … ahem.\n\nI'm very glad you both could make it.
Time to go, walker!
Isobel writes us, tells us all about her travels with you. She says she's learning so much!
Nice to put a face to the name at last. Delven Veloise, great to meet you. Isobel speaks very highly of you.
I'm so glad you came. Aurelia has been talking about your heroism nonstop.
Give Suungir to the prince. We'll need him fighting by our side.
That's her! That's the Khajiit that upset Sorinne!\n\nOh, we'll make her pay!
Ah, another victorious player returns home! Truly, I could hear Varnauld weeping from all the way across the Abecean.\n\nWell done, my friend!

You're the first one to come back. Razhamad's waiting for you, fretting like a mother echatere.\n\nPersonally, I knew you'd make short work of those Elden Root runts. Don't tell Brahgas I said that, though.
Hey there! You've got a hungry look. The eye of a real competitor—I can see it!\n\nWell, my friend, Tales of Tribute is the game for you.
You are here for your reward, yes?\n\nThis prize is yours!
Well played! That face Raenobi makes she when she knows she's beaten? It's like a breath of fresh sea air. And I mean to see it again when I beat her!

That wine-addled Razhamad doesn't even dare to meet us? You must be his proxy. Well, take a long look, you hay-born buffoon. This is what real talent looks like!\n\nNow, give me your name so I can scribble it carelessly in my ledger of doomed rivals!
You may as well give up now. I've pulled out the abacus and done the maths. A victory for Gonfalon is statistically impossible!
Varnauld's strategies are strong as the walls of Wayrest! You witless fishmongers are in for a beating.
You have a good heart. The few travelers who walk down this road pretend not to notice my muddy scales.
The shipwreck. Everything after it seems like a bad dream.
My head. It don't feel right.
I don't know how you got here, but I'm glad to see you! That ship approaching the pier is full of Ascendant Order reinforcements. We need to do something!
How did you—you're not a prisoner! Get lost before I inform the jailers!
Can you imagine a more beautiful place to serve during this war? I wish I had more time to enjoy the view. But the patients keep me so very busy.
Being here in this beautiful place should bring me peace. But I still remember the things I did on the battlefield.
This one saw many horrors on the field of battle. And committed some as well. Milagi does not wish to face such a scene ever again.

Ah, hello there. Say, you look like the type who could go traipsing around dangerous areas in search of rare ingredients. Could I interest you in a job? There's coin in it for you, and the knowledge that you'd be bringing joy to many in Gonfalon Bay.
The door to Memorial Hall stands on the south wall. We will make our stand there.

Sorinne says you know the details of my agreement to save Brahgas. I am sorry, my friend. I did not mean to place so heavy a burden on one of my best students. The championship should be your only concern.\n\nHowever this unfolds, the choice was mine.
So, Sorinne really has shaved her tail. Kra! My fun-loving sugarsnap, ruined!\n\nLooks like Raenobi will have to remind her who she is the hard way.
You don't have a snowball's chance in Hammerfell. Nobody plays like the Elden Root Chapter!
Raenobi gives us everything we need to succeed. I see things so clearly with her guidance … and her enhancements.\n\nYou'll see soon enough.
Board the vessel, my friend!
The Ascendant Order will not stop until the alliance leaders are dead.

The spirit of the grove, communicating with us directly? And through an inexperienced druid instead of a seasoned elder such as myself? How insulting!\n\nWell, don't keep the spirit waiting. Talk to it and see what it wants.
What a service you have done for all of Tamriel. You rescued the alliance leaders and secured the future of these peace talks. Lady Arabelle chose well when she selected you.
Figured I'd come see who won this fancypants affair. Your partner did well for herself. \n\nAlmost as good as one of the women warriors in my clan!
You've got this. I know you do. Just try to think of it like any other game. Just … against one of the strongest Tribute opponents you've ever faced.\n\nI … I'm not helping am I?
Take this bastard down, chum. I believe in you!
Greetings, Gonfalon. That Sorinne was a pleasant enough appetizer, but you, sera, are the main course.\n\nAre you ready to begin?
So, I face the prodigy first, eh? Excellent. I imagine that if I can beat you, the other two matches will be a snap!\n\nCome on, then. Show me what you've got.

The Gonfalon Chapter's redeemer, in the flesh. I've looked forward to meeting you. The novice who blossomed into a contender within the span of a single tournament season. Quite the feat.\n\nNow, I assume you know the rules of the final tournament?
Winning the tourney was always a long shot, a chance to bet big and win big.\n\nIn truth, I'm damned glad to see Dame Isobel walk away with the honors. Well done.
Three mainland royals in Gonfalon Bay now. Could Lord Bacaro's peace talks finally be happening?
Trouble on Amenos, Perditte says. Feh. There's always trouble on Amenos. I wouldn't set foot there for a purse full of coin.
Ugh, my head. Every time I move, it feels like someone's putting my skull through a grindstone. \n\nWhat happened last night?
You're not gonna kill him, right? I don't wanna deal with the guard.
You've played good games so far, friend. Now it's time to shove defeat into Varnauld Broch's expertly-coiffed beard. That's the Gonfalon Bay spirit!

Well, you made a meal of her, didn't you? Couldn't have happened to a nicer person, right? Ha!\n\nBut enough about the tragic fall of Cecile Nevim. You've got a tournament to win! Time to make your way to Wayrest and crush that blowhard, Varnauld!
Oh hello. Who are you here with? \n\nI'm old friends with the knight commander.
Stay vigilant. The Worm's transformation has made him horrifically powerful.

You have matches to win, walker. The only thing you will find here is big sister Kishka, refusing to admit she stole Marunji's jar of sugared violets from the larder.\n\nJust look at her! She is like the terror bird who swallowed the senche, yes?

After the Ascendant Magus attacked All Flags Islet, I hoped we were done with sinister plots and masked villains. I knew the Ascendant Lord was still on the loose, but I never imagined it would end like this.

When I boarded Captain Kaleen's ship in Wayrest, I never imagined the voyage would lead me to this place, this moment. We've had an adventure, my friend. No denying that! Dark and dangerous at times, but I'd do it again in a heartbeat.
It sounds like you were involved in a great battle on Y'ffelon. I'm sorry I missed it.
There's no need for this violence. All druids are welcome to come here and commune with the spirits!

The Stonelore seed is safe … but, what did Archdruid Devyric want with it?\n\nI'll look into that mystery when I've recovered from … all of this. For now, I'm just grateful his plan failed. Thank you for stopping him.

I joined my first pirate crew at such a young age that I can't remember anything before it. I spent most of my life on the water. Never saw it this way, though.\n\nI thought I knew the sea. But it holds more beauty than I ever imagined.

If you're brave enough to sample those delicacies, you'll have no problem scouting the locations I came up with for you. I've only visited a couple of the nearby ones in person.\n\nThe sites over on Amenos are a little too … exciting.

We actually did it. We learned why the Druid King met with the wyrds before leaving High Rock. It was to summon this nature spirit. But as to their purpose, that remains a mystery.\n\nPerhaps the Stonelore elders can help me figure it out.

Fascinating. The spirit seems to want to communicate with us, it just can't do so efficiently. Still, at least you slew that duneripper Michiel. Now we have time to work out the knots of this whole thing.\n\nTalk to Druid Laurel, see what her plan is.
First those druids arrived in force. Called themselves the Firesong. And now you show up, with the mage who spoke to Wyress Tola and another druid. Are you here to attack us, too?
The wyrds keep our history as oral stories, tales of seasons long past. A few involving the Druid King have been passed down, but I know only the barest details. I am sorry I cannot tell you more.

You travel with a druid, stranger. The last druids that entered our camp were quick to violence and stole one of our sisters away. They said they needed her to open a path.\n\nI don't wish to see any more blood spilled, but if you're with them ….
Loud and bright. Blood and soil. Awake! Awake! The season of purpose approaches, yes it does!
Who knows, perhaps Raz will meet a nice druid boy while he is here. This one likes plants as much as the next Khajiit.\n\nGalen really is quite beautiful, yes?
Take a seat, anywhere you like! Kitchen's open and everything on the menu is available. Except sprintfish. We just ran out.

This certainly is a tavern, isn't it? The ale has mites in it. The floor's sticking to my boot-bottoms. And there's someone living in the outhouse. Hah! You don't get this experience on Auridon!\n\nIf only there was a little more action, though ….
What's a flagon of ale without a bit of music, eh?
Raz will see you inside. Keep a keen eye open. With this one's disguise, you will have a hard time recognizing Raz.
Two crystals smashed to pieces. I don't want to get my hopes up, but we haven't died yet.\n\nLet's take care of the last two so I don't have to worry about drowning in a rising pool of lava.

I'm glad Za'ji found you. Sometimes he actually manages to surprise me.\n\nYou've already done so much, I hesitate to ask … but Lord Bacaro is reluctant to move forward with the peace talks while the Ascendant Order remains a threat.
Thank the moons! Za'ji was worried you left with the tide.\n\nLady Arabelle sent this one with urgent news.
Well fought, friend. Retrieve the seed and we'll take it to Vastyr. The druids in the Vine District can protect it until we find Archdruid Ellic.
You were as good as your word, mercenary. None of my knights could have done better. Thank you for rescuing my son.\n\nHe wants to speak with you, by the way.

If you're heading for the dungeons, I'll scale the walls while you're clattering around downstairs. Once I free my crewmates, I'll see if I can find that sea-snake, Nalos.\n\nYou know, this might actually work.
Find Sir Stefan and bring him back. Preferably in one piece. I've always liked that lad.

The Draoife will begin soon. Three archdruids from each circle meet in a dell within the hills across the valley, just to the south of here. We should make our way there. I don't want to miss anything.
This is a sacred place! What madness grips the Firesong?\n\nI am unharmed, stranger. Please, go after Laurel. In her anger she pursued Orlaith farther into the dell. And Stefan ran after her.

First Tuinh, then Draoife Dell. My circle takes pride in protecting what we love. War has come to Galen, but we have few warriors left to fight it.\n\nHow could Archdruid Orlaith side with those pirates against her own people?
I'll see these druids back to their village. You should head down the coast to Windwrack Fort. I've heard rumors of more Dreadsails activity there.
I don't know a lot about druids and spirits, but I do know how to fight. I'll be with you every step of the way, five-claw. You can count on me.
Did the mountain spit you out? Is that how you got back here? Is that even possible?\n\nOh, if only Za'ji knew more about the workings of volcanoes!
You don't know how much your help means to me, dear. Especially now, I need someone I can count on.
My particular skills lean more toward healing than battle, but I'll do whatever I can to help you stop Lord Bacaro.
What's the connection here? Why does the Ascendant Order care about this place? And why does Lord Bacaro have a suit of the Ascendant Lord's armor?
Keep your head down and let's see what we can learn.
You've returned. This one assumes you have completed the trials and proven yourself worthy of belonging to the Elsweyr Defense Force.\n\nShow Samara what you have.

Salutations. I regret to inform you that table games are reserved for persons in good standing, those with sufficient chips to play. \n\nYou, it appears, do not have the chips necessary for an opening stake. And so I must ask you to take your leave.

Damn Orlaith and her Firesong! They took townsfolk prisoner before they fled, but we weren't sure why. Now we know. She plans to use them as sacrifices, damn her eyes!\n\nWait. Where are Laurel and Frii? Didn't you bring them back with you?
Dhulef has impeccable timing, don't you agree? Let's use his portal and return to Vastyr. I think we still have much to discuss.
See? Y'ffelon, just as I promised. We'll wait here for any captives you manage to free. Now, you should go talk with the lordling. The next part is up to the two of you.
Druid Laurel studies the old lore. Young, yet wise. We must tell her what we learned from the elder's memory.\n\nLet us try this passage. I sense gentle wind and open sky beyond.

I knew this had to do with the prophecy, the Dream of Kasorayn, but for anyone to proclaim themselves the Druid King—even an archdruid—it's just unheard of. That isn't how it's supposed to work.\n\nTalk to Frii. See if they still sense the seeds.

Ugh, couldn't you have added a touch of cinnamon or honey to this Ryvana? No matter. I assume I will be hale and hearty again before long.\n\nNow enough with the suspense. Tell me what you uncovered, dear.
You completed the three trials, didn't you? Most impressive.\n\nYou should report your success to Captain Samara. She'll be happy to hear we have a new stalwart member in our ranks.

We arrived before your ship and took the lead. Lady Arabelle wanted us to clear a path, and we've done what we can.\n\nWe ran into a large contingent of Ascendant knights. Siravaen and the Gilded Blades chased them back to the main entrance.
Keep moving. I'm right behind you.
I have a feeling I'm still missing something …. Let's see. Yup, still no legs or feet. That's disappointing.\n\nHey, could you talk to Druid Fenas and ask him what in Oblivion went wrong? Thanks!
You finished the ritual, didn't you? Then why am I still covered in bark?\n\nMy feet, they're … taking root! Please, talk to Druid Fenas. I don't want to spend the rest of my life as a tree!
I'm glad you were with Frii inside the mountain, my friend. I'll never forget what they did to save us all.
Why is Lady Arabelle just standing there? We should check on her.
Archdruid Rahval has the Stonelore seed and druids are streaming into the village. I assume you had a part in all that, my friend?

A volcano spirit? I don't like the sound of that. Go rouse Count Stefan and we'll meet you at the Vastyr docks. With Ascendant knights and Firesong allies aiding Lord Bacaro, we'll need House Mornard's forces if we're going to storm Y'ffelon.
Working together again was truly a pleasure. Zeira will appreciate that you saved my hide. Again.\n\nWe do have just one bit of business to finish, though. Could I have the relic?
You have to talk to the Chronicle. It's angry with druids, all druids, because of what the Firesong have done.\n\nConvince it, outsider. For Gwenaelle. For all of us.
We should go, mainlander. The passage to the north leads back to the shore.\n\nThe Dreadsails will regret the day they made the Eldertide Circle their enemies, this I swear.

Oh, wonderful. A third to join our little get together. This has turned out to be quite a delightful day. While I truly have eyes for this fine lady, a little extra spice never hurts.\n\nCome, sit. We're just beginning to relax.
Why would Neri trick me like that? She said to follow her to a secluded spot for more fun. Then Minahel grabbed me.\n\nAt least I showed you where they kept the relic. We really make a great team.

I assumed these Ascendant Order knights were going to provide a challenge, but they ran the moment we began to cut them down.\n\nThey did mention the Ascendant Lord, though. He's definitely inside the mountain.

Our brothers and sisters have arrived, summoned by the beacon. We're just about ready to make the trip to Vastyr. We will help defend the walls, and in turn, the walls will defend our injured.\n\nNow, Frii tells me you carry our sacred seed?
Looks like Archdruid Rahval is just about ready to head out. There hasn't been an army of druids like this in many, many seasons.\n\nGo on. Give him the sacred seed.

What strange allies this situation has foisted upon us. I never expected to work so closely with Sea Elves, but I can't find fault with Captain Siravaen's results.\n\nLet's find a way into the mountain, dear.

The followers of the Allwither … more insidious than I thought. A poisoned blade in the hand of a trusted friend. \n\nThis proves I was right. Crown, staff, gauntlet. They must return to the Green. You must help me, Aiven.
We did well, dear, but the work isn't finished yet. I could use a hand if you're still so inclined.
Frii … crowning a new Druid King? The Dream of Kasorayn says "When mountain shakes and Sower wakes, the throne shall bloom again." \n\nCome on, we need to find Frii. I have so many questions.
Urgent whispering. Metal skin. Waits. Waits
Well met, friend! Grab a mug and let's have a toast before we finish our business!

Someone has gone to a lot of trouble to try to remove both myself and Lady Arabelle from the table while also focusing the blame for this all on me.\n\nSpeak to this courier and get some answers—or I will.

Take this key. It will open the door to the cellars. Just follow the path to the north, toward the dock. \n\nIf the Ascendant Order is stealing from the Society of the Steadfast, we need to know how and why.
Fix the shrines up as best you can, would you? We'll send some Stonelore initiates that way later to make sure they're properly communing with the earthen spirits again.

Whether it's dealing with Sea Elf raids, butting heads with the Duforts, or just keeping the jungle at bay, the wilds of Galen are full of dangers. This, of course, means there's never a shortage of ways to make coin.

A hard decision to make, but the right one, I believe. I just wish there had been a way to restore both of them.\n\nYou should talk to Octin, friend. His form is returned to him, but he lost his cousin this day.
Nearly there, just need to plant one more seed and then your part in this is done.

I'm sure Meshden can tell you more about Fauns' Thicket. You can find him in the Jaded Ornaug Tavern. Anyway, he said he always found critters near wispleaf blooms.\n\nOooo! Perhaps placing these lures near the flowers will attract some little friends?
I see everyone has arrived. Well done, dear. And I did my part, as well. The alliance leaders are already downstairs.
It's rude to ignore a lady when she clearly wants to talk to you. Come see me after you and Lady Arabelle conclude your business.
We need to find Archdruid Ellic. If he went through the old tunnels, hopefully the damned sea-wolves haven't gotten to him or the seed yet. \n\nLet's go. Vastyr won't fall, not this day!

Blight and damnation, trying to get the druid circles to agree on anything is like trying to herd Fauns!\n\nBut you're not here to deal with my problems. Not this time. What can I do for you, my friend?
Always a pleasure, five-claw, but you also tend to bring trouble to Za'ji—and more work!\n\nSo, what is it this time? A Peryite cult? Vampire armies from deep underground? What?
You're just in time, five-claw. We were about to head out to the Pounce. Za'ji wants her ready to sail at a moment's notice.

I don't believe it. Archdruid Orlaith did it. She made Kasorayn's Dream come true. The crown, staff, and gauntlet are returned to us. But I don't think it happened in the way anyone foresaw.\n\nYou better talk to Frii.
My purpose was to regrow the seeds. To help crown, staff, and gauntlet blossom once again. But it is not for me to wield them.

So much death and destruction this day. I can't believe my father and Archdruid Rahval are gone. Two men who shaped me … snuffed out like two candles in a strong wind.\n\nAnd now Archdruid Orlaith has all three seeds. By the Green, what are we to do?
That felt damned good! But celebrating can come later. Let's keep going. Something's happening up ahead.
Do as Sir Stefan asks. I'll make sure he finds his way back to the castle.\n\nAt least the Dreadsails have broken off their attack. Vastyr might survive this, after all.
Are you well, Aiven? You seem ill at ease.

I pushed myself so hard to unravel the knot. But still … I couldn't do it. Maybe I'm too weak, I don't have the will.\n\nPlease, track down the distortion again. I'm exhausted, but I can try one more time.
Well, if it isn't Lady Arabelle's talented assistant. I might have guessed that Galen's troubles would draw you here. What can I do for you, my friend?

Tales of your battle with Archdruid Orlaith are spreading across the archipelago. All who died in the siege of Vastyr can rest a little easier now. I will not forget what you've done. Nor will Sir Stefan, I'm sure. He wants to speak with you.

Now the discussions to resolve seasons of conflict begin. This is an important moment, friend. And you made it happen. Even if the peace talks fail, good things will come of this. They must.\n\nAnd know that you always have a place with the Stonelore.

Lord Bacaro wields the Druid King's regalia with such force. I could not resist his commands. He forced me to awaken the mountain's spirit. But he is not the true Druid King. Not until the three circles become one and proclaim him as such.

Is this smoke in my eyes, or have my prayers been answered? I'm a bit of a culinary adventurer. But you look like you explore more … dangerous haunts. Am I right?\n\nHow would you like to assist me with my newest expedition in the realm of flavor?
Huh. We usually fight people like you. I guess it makes sense to the captain, though. Maybe you should talk to her.
You're not worth my time, shark-bait. But the captain thinks well of you for some reason. Talk to her, not me.
Don't mind me, dear. Just admiring the sea.

Firesong are as thick as quills on a porcupine around Ivyhame. And I don't like the idea of bringing Frii any closer to Archdruid Orlaith. Still, it might work.\n\nI suppose you should ask Frii. They're somewhere nearby.
Go on, tell Sir Stefan what you learned at Ivyhame. When the ship is sinking, any port will do.

You and Count Stefan have given the Eldertide much to consider. We always guarded these islands against outsiders. Pirates, yes. But also nobles, settlers, and townsfolk.\n\nNow I see we may find friends where once we saw enemies.

My circle lost its way under Archdruid Orlaith. Some of us knew it, but we had gone too far. All we could do was fight on and hope that Orlaith's victory would be worth the price. \n\nI … regret the things we did and promise to make up for it.
I'll make sure these good folk get to the Mad Maiden. Head for the temple—Archdruid Orlaith has been inside with Frii a lot longer than I'd like.

Perhaps I was somewhat unfair to the young Count Mornard. Now, I'm not saying I was totally wrong, mind you. But Stefan at least seems to have a vision. That's more than I could ever say about his father, gods rest his soul.
Have you heard the rumors? That Ascendant Order knights have been seen on Galen?\n\nWhy can't those rogues go back to High Isle? Haven't we had enough trouble for one season?
Thanks for rescuing me and the other captives from Y'ffelon. I thought I'd never see Galphen again! Well, I mean Galen. That's what I meant. Must have been a slip of the tongue.

Dame Fayda went to defend the cathedral when the Sea Elves attacked. Other knights have come back since the fighting ended, yet I've seen no signs of Fayda.\n\nShe's all right, isn't she? She has to be!
Keeping a Daedric Prince waiting is ill-advised, proxy. I am all right. Go and present yourself to the One Who Knows.
How did the Scribes manage to be swayed so far? Their so-called dedication to Hermorah is a farce. An embarrassment. A perversion of our post.

This hall leads to where the rifts form. Many scribes are lost to the unstable nature of the rifts, but the ones who return often begin to recognize the patterns.\n\nThis section will be guarded against what horrors may emerge from the rifts.

The Great Eye sent us visions. Told us to protect the Emerald Glyphic until his chosen agent arrived to claim it. But our order doesn't have many warriors. These vampires overwhelmed my fellow believers before we could marshal a proper defense.
You didn't lose the talisman, did you? By the Tribunal, tell me nothing happened to it on your way back from the outpost ruins.
You. Yes, you must help me. Kemel-Ze—sacred site of the Tribunal—is under attack. The secret underground laboratory of Sotha Sil himself has been invaded. Overrun!
What is it you want? Your nose is too close to my face.
This one's tongue wishes to express disappointment. But this one's heart can hold no anger while his family lives to walk another day.

You have my deepest gratitude for your helping Rilasi.\n\nI plan to note your name in my personal records so all the high priests who come after me will know who reunited us with our most sacred relic.
Oh. It's you. Come to tussle with the ne'er-do-wells of the Telvanni Peninsula? Hmm. Actually. I could use a distraction. This is for official business, you should remember how compensation works.
I met Fomesa during an inspection just a few seasons ago. She was a hard worker. Terrible sight—seeing her like that.

The Mnemonic Fragments house Lord Seht's insights, and preserve them within the system of Kemel-Ze so they cannot be forgotten.\n\nI located the largest fragments, which can also restore my connection to this laboratory. Hurry, please.
A visually recorded journal? I wonder why this was not brought to the Clockwork City?\n\nWhatever the reason, Thoryn doesn't know of this journal's existence. I'll use it to secure my revelations.

Curious. You emanate a familiar pattern. A tone which resonates with ours. Yet, you are mortal.\n\nPerhaps our sanctum's pain drew you here. Creatures overrun the Apogee of the Tormenting Eye, driven only to devour.

Three labors were set before you, proxy. Now Vaermina, Peryite, and Master Shelreni stand revealed as our foes.\n\nI have been speaking with Curate Gadayn. I find him … intriguing. But I wish to hear it from you. What did you find in Necrom Abbey?

Leramil has done well and brought fate's chosen into my unrelenting gaze. All other outcomes are now excluded. From this moment, fate's ever-branching tree begins to grow again. And with it, new possibilities emerge.

A fine job, mortal. With my creatures returned safely and back under control, I can head to Fargrave as originally planned.\n\nUnfortunately, I still require your help. My portal spell should work, but it may be unpredictable.

How insidious! Blightcrown made the Keepers of the Dead sick so he could question them in their fevered state.\n\nAnd all so he could find some old relic hidden in the Necropolis? Why go to all the trouble?
Not now, stranger. My assistant never showed up for work today and I've got my hands full directing cargo bound for both land and sea.
Hey there, friend! Don't mind me. I'm just planning details on how to clear the mine with the good captain here. A lot of work still ahead of us!
Hey there, hero! It's nice to see you again before we set out! Who knows where we'll end up!
Look who it is, and right before we set out! It's good to see again, friend.

As far back as we can recall, the Remnants believed we directly served Hermaeus Mora. Our connection to him drove us to defend his will.\n\nPerhaps that was a lie? The pact was nothing. A shattered plane with a rotting book.
Would this have gone differently … had I never requested your aid? I'm sorry. Leave me to my thoughts, and to my memories.
It seems legible enough, if a little wet still. Would be a shame if you don't take it after my brother's hard work!

Go ahead, mortal. Consult with Leramil. She has a talent for determining what the Great Eye truly demands of his chosen.\n\nThe rest of us? The bitter truth is, we're just grains of sand waiting to be washed away by the rain of destiny.

Leramil had the hardest time extracting anything useful out of these stacks. And every time she found something promising, it crumbled to dust or burned to ash.\n\nAnyway, she's in her study. You should go in and let her know if you fared any better.

Here I was bemoaning the task of returning these books and it was only the one. I must look like a lazy fool. Still, I appreciate your company. And how grand it must be for you to see the Sidereal Cloisters in all its glory.
This is it, Traveler. The moment before Hermaeus Mora's trap was triggered.
I'm not sure what would have happened if Gadayn hadn't recruited your help, friend. Thank you for saving the Necropolis.

The Daggerfall Devil? Watcher spare us!\n\nOn the one claw, it makes sense that a serial killer in the chorus would be the cause of our troubles. On the other, there a serial killer in the Chorus. And it appears that he wants out.

They call this a library? I see no rhyme or reason to the cipher's organization, and this is a terrible way to treat books. I understand now why Leramil must employ spells to conduct her research here.

The threads of fate here are tied to three things—Master Shelreni, Meln the Mouthless, and the Black Book.\n\nThat was the connection to Apocrypha I sensed here. Black Books are creations of Hermaeus Mora and his realm.

Any effort you provide puts us in your debt. The Cenotaph lies in the north. Just outside, you will find a group of surviving Remnants. Look for Tyss.\n\nStay cautious, mortal. The Dreamcarvers attack your mind long before they reach your flesh.

Curate Gadayn's concern is appreciated but unwarranted, proxy. I have been sifting through Apocrypha's secrets long enough to know my limits. And the ritual performed just as I hoped it would.\n\nStill, I could use a moment … to regain my strength.

Careful there, stranger. Whatever Three-cursed spell-trap the old magister placed on that door kills vampires like us rather efficiently. But I don't recognize you. You're not a Dusksaber.\n\nDid Master Shelreni send you to help us?

What a kind gesture. Leramil … she's special, isn't she, my friend?\n\nWell, I have Leramil's charm and I have the piece of the Fulcrum Obscura. I suppose I'm as ready as I'll ever be to traipse across a realm of Oblivion.
That thing she called me. Kaj-kujei. I'm her brother? Why do I know what that means?\n\nSee if you can help Reynila. I need to think.

If there's one thing I learned in death, it's how foolish the living can be. I know all that passes in my home, intruder. I heard your bargain with that so-called master, Shelreni Baro.\n\nYou have given my murderer access to my tower.

The Fulcrum Obscura passed through this chamber. Therefore, Torvesard and Blightcrown found a way to distract the Guardian Gaze. We must do the same. If the eye's gaze falls upon us, pain and disorientation will be the least of our concerns.

You'll find the corrupted scrolls hidden within Quires Wind. Sabinius is in there too. We can't leave him with any scrolls, blank or corrupt.\n\nAnd watch out for Cipher Gelon. He's a clever alchemist, but I saw the Hush take him. He's dangerous.
Your face isn't familiar to me, but I'd know that look anywhere. You want something from me. Information, probably. \n\nWell? What is it you're looking for?

The papers contain sensitive information. Letters found by a valet in my employ.\n\nThe servants quarters are in a small tower to the north. The papers are stashed on the upper floor. Bring them back and leave them on Mouth Delvi's desk. Simple, yes?
It worked! I may survive this after all. Quickly, take the restored glyphic!
This isn't exactly easy. Take the restored glyphic while you can!
When the opportunity to enter a place of forbidden knowledge was snatched from me, the frustration was nearly overwhelming. Ah, well.\n\nTell me what you saw inside the memory, proxy.
Ah. The glyphic holds memories of three books. The invaders breached Apocrypha to learn what's recorded here. You should examine the tomes, mortal.

Keshargo told Valinna that he hid the Itinerant Staff in the Spiral Skein, but I have it in my hands. \n\nValinna wasn't lying when she said she'd kill him. We have to catch up to them without Zilipif's guidance.
All right, we have the key!\n\nThis is going better than I thought it would. And it's strange—everything looks so different in here without the wards. It all feels so empty.

I don't want to be alone again. I want nothing more than for Dacia to stay with me. If we can't walk the world together, at least we'd never have to be apart.\n\nBut I love her. Deeply, truly, I do. Which is why I know I cannot ask her to stay.

If Dacia is willing, I can safely inoculate her with the same spores I used on Nathyn. \n\nShe will share his affliction and his confinement. But they will be together, and she will want for nothing, except perhaps her freedom.

Both Scruut and I felt the tides of fate churn and boil. Worse, neither of us has been able to commune with Hermaeus Mora since the Black Book's rite was completed at Vaermina's shrine.\n\nAnd you say you saw Shelreni's body walk into Apocrypha?
Some days fate dumps viscera from the Void on you, and other days something large and powerful sticks its finger in your eyes. That's existence for you.
Go on and take a look. I'll stand watch out here in case Magister Gothren sends someone to expel us.

Not a bad bit of work. You follow directions well. And the cloak looks perfectly dashing. Dashing, I say!\n\nNow let's head to Ald Isra and meet up with Curate Gadayn. He should have gotten you access to the conclave by now.
I'm relieved to see you both. I suppose the Starflower didn't give you too much trouble?\n\nWhat did you discover at her hideout?

I'll be able to study the prism in more detail once I get it back to my study. I wonder what magical tests I should subject it to first? Or perhaps I'll return and capture a few of these warring Daedra for experimentation.
No! Begone! You were never welcome here.

Now that Sulis knows what Foves was up to, the backstabbing and plotting will intensify. I suppose that's life in House Telvanni, though.\n\nAnyway, I'm glad Folsi decided to involve you in all this, hero.
Please, see if you can help Reynila.

After crossing all of Oblivion, trudging through Apocrypha, getting kicked, then needing to rely on a mortal, this better be worth it. I'd say two thousand years off my debt.\n\nGo ahead and deposit the secret before we lose it again.
It's over. I don't have to spare a thought for him ever again.\n\nCome on. Let's go meet our friends in Narsis.
Good luck in the Forgotten Crypts. Make it out alive, will you?
Thank you for your warning. I can use this to put Foves in his place. And take full control of our secret project. Yes, the possibilities are endless!
So nice of those cultists to share with you.\n\nAfter this, we can destroy what you found and let the pieces sink in the swamp. Let's just hope we can actually follow Reynila's guidance on this.
You want to talk again? \n\nVery well, since you protected my laboratory I'll allow it.

As Twelvane thought, Ansuul's presence is missing here too. That's a good thing. It means she's gone from Vanton's mind.\n\nYou've done the Mages Guild proud. You proved your strength and fortitude in the most extreme circumstances. Thank you.
Ah, just in time. I was beginning to wonder if An'Xeh would find anyone willing to help us. \n\nYou are here to help us, are you not?
This doesn't entirely break precedent, but it is unusual. I've been sent to find assistance outside the Mages Guild.\n\nCan you help us? We will reward you for the danger you face.
So, the mouthless finally appointed a mouth. And all it took was for him to shuffle off this mortal coil. \n\nI guess you can teach a dead magister a new trick.
We were just about to finally get on with the conclave when you and Meln appeared. Why do magisters complicate even the simplest of proceedings?
I'm not sure what's still happening, but that awful book looks ominous. Maybe if you close it, that will interrupt the flow of energy?
I know this must seem a bad joke … but it is not. If you do not dispose of the key in a place I cannot find it, it could prove too great a temptation.\n\nCast the Fateweaver Key into the depths.

What strange allies this situation has foisted upon us. I never expected to work so closely with Sea Elves, but I can't find fault with Captain Siravaen's results.\n\nLet's keep looking for a way into the mountain, dear.
What we just witnessed … hmm. Distressing. Horrid. Disconcerting. Apologies, cohort, I'm free-associating to deal with my emotions.
So close to a new Known Thing. I told you that the last one made my ears bleed, right? I wonder what I'll learn this time. Maybe I'll grow a stately tail!
I can't believe you'd allow him to do such a thing. Am I to live as a proud father whose son doesn't know who I am?

I hate the idea of abandoning you and Scruut, but Leramil needs time to recover. I'll stay with her. Get her back to Ciphers Midden. You and Scruut go on ahead.\n\nMay the ancestors guide you, my friend.
While Leramil's display was indeed impressive, she continues to abuse forces that were not meant to be wielded by mere mortals. One day, that will be her undoing.
Well, get moving! I can't get to Tel Baro without you, and that's the most likely place to find Shelreni's spirit.
They tried to get me to talk about the forbidden exhibits. But the Lord of Fate deals in secrets, I wouldn't give any away for nothing.
Scruut returned from Apocrypha with disheartening news, while my efforts at research have been marginally effective at best.\n\nTell me you have something better to report, proxy.

The Mythos is a forbidden place, deep beneath the Ichor Sea. This is where the Great Eye conceived Apocrypha. Where he whispered the first secret, imagined the first inkling of knowledge.\n\nWe're so not worthy to be here, even if it is just a memory.
What happened after you entered the portal, proxy? Scruut tells us the One Who Knows has reconnected with his realm, but beyond that we are in the dark.
It feels as though a great weight has been lifted from my chest.
These blasted headaches, why haven't I found a better apothecary?
The poisoning of an oathman is generally frowned upon … unless, of course, it is executed flawlessly. This was far from flawless.

You ended that disgusting Blightcrown and I recovered the other half of the Fulcrum Obscura. Now you must face Vaermina. She's still wearing Master Shelreni's body, right?\n\nGood luck, my friend. I'll watch over Leramil and Scruut until you return.

I'll never understand why I waited until I was dead to face a Daedric Prince. Oh, I know—because it's the stupidest thing I've ever done!\n\nBut have no fear. I'll go with you. I've stood beside you this long. What's one more epic battle?

Mortals manipulating the very strands of fate. How unlike Hermaeus Mora to put such power in your hands. He must be truly desperate to keep us in the dark concerning the crimes he perpetrated so long ago.

Leramil and I used every resource at our disposal to find Vaermina. This portal should get you close, but maybe not too close.\n\nA word of caution, mortal. The Dreamweaver is a nasty Prince. She'll scramble your mind before she destroys your body.

The corruption wreaks havoc with my realm, chosen. Any relief I experienced after breaking free of Vaermina's dream has left me. My connection to Apocrypha grows ever more tenuous and the vile poison debilitates me. \n\nThe Great Eye … is blind.

Akacirn's dwelling is a secret room in Quires Wind. Look for his mark on the platforms within the scriptorium. Let's hope something there hints at his current whereabouts. Otherwise, I'm not sure where in Apocrypha he might be hiding.

I'll mark your map with the location of the Fungal Downs gate, as well as where the Seekers flock.\n\nMora's foes control these Seekers. Find them, kill them, and take their ichor. Once you collect enough, you can open the gate and enter the Bastion.
I do want to get on with this, but Meln requested that you speak with him first. So I'll just wait here and twiddle my tentacles … as usual.

The time has come for me to return to Necrom and complete my mission for the abbey. When I present the Fulcrum Obscura to the abbot, I'd like you to be at my side. Um, our side. Leramil wants to come, too.\n\nIsn't that … nice?
It's good to get out of that soul gem and stretch for a while. Metaphorically speaking.

After we help Gadayn return the Fulcrum Obscura, I want to hear all about what happened with the second glyphic and Torvesard, proxy.\n\nI sense this is not yet over, as you still bear the mark of fate's chosen.
It's a grand day. The indignities Blightcrown inflicted upon our honored dead are finally set right.
Commotion at the Necropolis? I wonder what's going on over there.
All this talk of something going on at the Necropolis has me wondering if I should take a look. Perhaps they'll allow me a quick visit.
This hireling is so concerned with the goings on at Necrom that he neglected his duty. I've had people imprisoned for lighter offenses!
Spellwright Moran says I shouldn't worry about the goings on over at Necrom, but I have to believe there's something greater going on. But it's not my station to worry about it.
Our land is ridden, plagued, and infested. I sense your determination to rid us of that and applaud you for your valiant, if not foolish, efforts.
A scent surrounds you, a taste of the nightmares distilled. You are dealing with such things that those of us here choose not to, or are bound by duty to not interfere.

I recognize you. From that incident with the ambitious lizard. And now you stand before me, representing one of my most annoying colleagues.\n\nWell, get on with it. What's so important that Magister Meln dares interrupt these closed proceedings?
A word of advice. Harn's a busy man. Don't waste his time or he'll take it out of your hide.
Keep it quick, merc.
Zemzo feels grateful to have a position among the Telvanni. Father once said that this one would die poor on the side of the road. But now look at Zemzo! Soon to be a hireling … and then a mouth!

I see that you and the assassin have both returned. I assume that means she'll soon conclude her business and Tel Huulen will be safe again. Well, safer, anyway.\n\nI look forward to hearing her report.
You need something? Archmage's correspondence doesn't answer itself, you know.
Do leave me be. Once I get a hold of all the knowledge this island keeps hidden, no magister would dare deny me an audience.

Traveler, have you ever stood on the precipice of discovery? An arm's length away from changing Tamriel's history? I would think not, but now is your chance. My daughters and I are on the cusp of glory and we'll have you as our witness.
I'm a little preoccupied, traveler. Speak with my sister while I maintain the ritual.
Venture into Apocrypha and retrieve the phylactery. It should be kept somewhere within Bastion Nymic. My sister and I will stay here and prepare the ritual to free my father from this curse.

There's no time for pleasantries or interrogations. Tho'at Replicanum is summoning maligraphies, creatures of ink. \n\nThe Infinite Archive is filled with books and therefore, ink. You can see how this is suboptimal, right?

This Altmer, Leramil. She seems a few Kwama short of a clutch, if you catch my meaning. I've seen it happen to many who dared to peruse the secrets of Apocrypha.\n\nAs for the young curate, I'd say he's smitten with the lady. Mark my words.
It may surprise you to hear that the pages expelled by the curse number in the … well, there are a great many pages. Plenty to keep an adventurer like you busy, I assure you.
You get attacked by so many maligraphies and still stay on the floor. I would've just flown away, but not you. \n\nYou're something special, even if you don't file anything.
Centuries of peace and quiet, disrupted by a mortal. How appropriate.
Who are you? \n\nWait, you're that adventurer I sent to help me … do something. What was it again?

It took years to negotiate a fair dowry for the Verdulis family's eldest daughter. To come this close to a life of leisure only for some flea-infested scoundrel to dash my dreams?\n\nPlease, search Fyrelight for my dowry, I beg of you.

Truly a tireless companion, I'm so happy we found him safe and sound. Though, I suspect, if anyone did try to hurt him, they're likely tending to a nasty bite wound as we speak.\n\nLazen should be able to lead us to the rest of my missing wine.
Do I look like I'm in a talking mood? Leave me to tend to my wounds.

Prince Ithelia has escaped her prison, yet reality persists. And Torvesard understood events no better than we do.\n\nAs I have seen time and time again, the machinations of Oblivion are far beyond mortal comprehension.
The threads of fate have never appeared so tangled … so frayed. May the Golden Eye guide you quickly, champion. I fear that time is not on our side.

Despite the loss of Curate Gadayn, you recovered a fragment filled with the essence of Mirrormoor and we successfully created a new relic—the Mirror of Truth.\n\nA time to mourn shall come later, provided we stop Ithelia and reality survives.
The Mirror of Truth? As good a name as any, I suppose.\n\nWith this relic, maybe we can convince Ithelia to abandon her plan. Maybe.
Keep a close eye on Orissa. She is a brave lady but very headstrong.

Necromancers passed this by, huh? Even with all of them working together, they probably can't figure out how to release the shards.\n\nThat won't be a problem for us. Not with that Aetherial alarum I gave you. You still have it, right?

My cohort, almost completely destroyed. The Rustwall staff, almost all dead. Even Shardmarshal Vargas managed to escape us again. While we closed the portal and saved Skingrad, it feels like we failed, comrade.
Malacath's bloody sword-arm! If we hadn't already killed that construct, I would tear its roots apart with my hands.\n\nGo. I need a moment to wrestle my anger.
Back to Tamriel? Thank the ancestors! As much as I enjoy traveling with Leramil … and you, too, friend … I think I've had my fill of Oblivion planes.
Despite all that happened, I'm curious to see how this ritual plays out.
Hrm. Yes. Though the twins remain silent, their light shines upon the path … for those who know how to see it. Old Ri'jhaad understands now why the Tidewatcher told him to meet you here.
Greetings, citizen. Are you here about the job postings? No? Well then, carry on.
You there! The Imperial Legion of West Weald has need of your services. There are problems throughout the region and not enough legionaries to deal with them.\n\nWould you be available to hire?

Julianos help me, this is a logistical nightmare! Please tell me you're here to help. I've been putting out fires across West Weald nonstop and our forces are wearing thin.\n\nI'll gladly put you to work if you're interested.
The signal fires. That was you? Wait, that scroll …. I gave those orders to a legionary. \n\nWho are you and what happened to my legionary?
Let's get out of here before the vats explode! I'll meet you outside!

A strange vision! They were worried about the Ayleids, but there haven't been Ayleids here in centuries upon centuries.\n\nSpeaking of strange, it looks like we've gained a new companion. I assume you know that High Elf?
Rapid new foliage growth is dangerous! I suppose everyone is trying to be generous and welcoming to the Wood Elves, but guests don't destroy the crops or land. It's an outrage!
Grab the will before the dog runs off with it again!
Thank you, friend! I couldn't bear to think of what would happen if we hadn't treated Betu in time.
Oh! Sorry. Probably not the best idea to sneak up on someone juggling knives. Especially sneaking up on one rehearsing for their debut performance in Skingrad!
It seems once again Betu wants us to traipse around the estate grounds. Be sure to pocket that key. It may prove to be useful.

It appears we have done it, proxy. Ithelia is no longer a threat to our reality. Your solution was not what I expected, and even Hermaeus Mora was surprised. But I suppose that was why he selected you as fate's chosen in the first place.
This nebulous manifestation appears to be a condensation of—ah. Never mind. The wisp is an ancient memory. The presence of the Echonir renders it accessible to us. Please examine it, proxy.
I believe you and I have spoken enough. Tell Fennorian what you discovered and make sure he deals with my husband.\n\nRemind him that he owes me.
This is all quite beyond me. You'd better talk to Leramil—she'll know what to do. I hope.

Your companions went on ahead to the library. Our collection preserves many strange and ancient tomes. Perhaps one of them will serve to guide you along your way.\n\nYou will find it just down the eastern stairs.
Are you sure you never made a Sage's Dream before? That wasn't an easy process. But it smells wonderful. That must be some drink!
No sign of reinforcements yet. I hope Calvo can hold out a bit longer.
You are working with the investigator, I see. Don't believe a word that family says. Vultures, all of them!
I was hired to deal with road thieves and pickpockets. I'm no beast tamer, although after this I may try to pick the skill up. It was awfully impressive. I'll leave the cave delving to you, stranger.
I've committed no wrong! That man was an imposter. If I hadn't gotten him first, then he would've killed me. I spit on Theophan Pictor's name for masquerading as my dear Uriel.
I think the evidence speaks for itself. My mother's death was the work of a disturbed man who later killed himself when his guilt got the better of him.
Don't worry. I'll take care of all the remaining paperwork and help get Otho, and Betu, on their feet. Thank you for everything you've done today. I hope my dear aunt can rest easy now.
We're all warriors here, but attacking the pit is unforgivable.

That mirror … it showed me the truth. I have become the monster that Mora predicted. And I remember. I saw it, too. As Mora sealed my prison all those eons ago, I realized at the end … he was right.\n\nI am the Last Tomorrow.

Thank you for the aid, traveler. Return to me when you've stopped their rituals and freed who you can. The sooner we save everyone and put a stop to the Recollection the better. I just wish I had done more to prevent this.
Beragon has graciously offered us the use of his townhouse as a base from which to conduct our investigations. Speak with him, please. I know he is curious about what you discovered.
Remember, we need to find the communique with the proper chime sequence, the key to the bell tower, and the cohort payroll.\n\nJust keep an eye out for those bandits. And the bears.
It seems my sources were not mistaken about the maze in Elenglynn … or the deadly traps. We must find our way to the chamber at the heart of the maze and see where it leads us next.
Balandrus and his lieutenants know we're coming. And they've got Tham. Our best option is to strike fast and strike hard!

Old relics, new enemies … I have no liking for any of this. Malacath instructed me to find this strange mage and tell her about the staff stolen from the Oathsworn Pit. I have done so. My part in this is done.

Someone went to great lengths to examine the Echonir. Strange—I never gave that dusty old relic a second look. Clearly it was more important than I thought.\n\nA problem for Hermaeus Mora and Leramil now, I suppose.
I know there is a price, but my gratitude knows no bounds! Gadayn is returned!\n\nPlease, proxy. Speak to him. Determine that he is all right.

After my initial examination of the Skein of Secrets, I still don't know what to make of it. It's a map, but the image is constantly changing. I think it reacts to whatever the viewer is looking for.\n\nI wasn't having much luck, then I had an idea.

It's hard to believe that slip of cloth is a Daedric artifact. But then again, Mephala is said to be one of the more subtle Daedric Princes. We better take it and go before the Recollection realizes we're down here.
Take the portal when you're ready, mortal. Hermaeus Mora awaits you.
Speak with Leramil. I'll wait for my speech after that.
With Nantharion dead and Ithelia back in her own realm, the Recollection have scattered. Still, I'm worried about Shardmarshal Vargas and her Prince. We didn't beat them. They just … left.
Time isn't on our side, friend. The Skein of Secrets indicates that King Nantharion—and likely Ithelia, too—are already in Vashabar. If we don't stop them now, we might not get another chance.
This way, comrade! Hurry!

Don't worry about me. I picked up some healing skills over the years. I'll do what I can for the wounded legionaries, then find a way to catch up with you.\n\nAnd Abolisher will work. Remember how you used it at Niryastare!
I'm getting entirely too comfortable with stepping through magical portals. It's just not natural.\n\nWell, no point in stopping now. Let's press on.

The legionary found you? Good.\n\nI was reviewing recent reports from the tribune's scouts just before you came in. The Recollection's on the run, but the Mirrormoor incursions continue unabated. Shardmarshal Vargas isn't done with us yet.

King Nantharion hardly knows us. If the Recollection spy—or spies—around him are people he's known for some time, it might not be easy to convince him he's in danger. Wait for us before you try to storm the place, friend.
Arkay knows what horrors the undead may unleash if they complete the ritual. We must stop it!
Day after day, I toil to make this place perfect for Count Calantius. Now these invaders appear and tear it all up!

Fascinating. Wendir is another Ayleid ruin, but the Skein of Secrets offers no explanation beyond a mark on a map. A subtle tool indeed, worthy of the Lady of Whispers.\n\nI am curious, proxy. What exactly did you see when you looked at the Skein?
I don't know Leramil well, but the loss of the curate has hit her hard. You should talk to Scruut and find out what we're supposed to do with the fragment we recovered.
We should have stayed away after Ostumir was overtaken by the forest, but we refused to leave well enough alone.

Sorilen talked about the Recollection's desire to take back Ayleid land. But based on their behavior so far, I don't think it'll be peaceful.\n\nWere you able to grab that wildburn seed from the ruins?
Is that what I looked like when you found me? How strange! Hurry—use the Lamp and get our friend out of there!

I almost feel sorry for Ithelia's scions. To exist for millennia, tormented by the sense they were missing something, and could not find their purpose.\n\nThe Loom of the Untraveled Road. That must be the loom Ithelia spoke of in Miscarcand.

We shared some strange adventures. I never imagined I'd find myself wandering a forgotten plane of Oblivion. Or erased from reality, for that matter. But we finally beat Vargas and her Shardborn.\n\nI'd fight by your side any time, comrade.

I had no idea the ground would shake so violently when I asked Beragon to meet me here. Nature is nothing if not unpredictable.\n\nI also didn't expect him to bring a guest. So, who are you, friend of Beragon?
Aren't you glad you joined this endeavor? Clearly, Wendir has its secrets. Fascinating! This looks like another puzzle. I'm sure I can be of help here, but go on, take a look.
Have you found him? It would set my heart at ease to know he's safe. My dear Narsis is too kind, trusting the Recollection. For all I know, they may have locked him in a sarcophagus or something.
We must get below and attempt to stop the Loom from reweaving history. I do not think we can do much against Ithelia directly, but perhaps we can find a way to damage or destroy the Loom.

Thanks to you, things can begin to return to normal in West Weald. I know Ithelia and Torvesard are still out there, but we can worry about that later, right?\n\nFor now, I just want to sleep for a week!
I sense the knot in the threads of fate has untangled, proxy. This threat to our reality has passed. Should I assume you are responsible? Tell me what occurred within the Outcast Inn.
I sense this realm will not last much longer. The binds of reality have begun to fray.\n\nHurry, mortal. Gather the lute berries and I will open a way out of this place.
You're going to find Master Grander's stolen goods? Wonderful! If you make quick work of it, I should be able to have his evening clothes properly pressed in time for dinner in Skingrad.
If they left a key sitting out in the open, who are we to ignore it? Take the key, deputy, and see if it unlocks any of the drawers in that desk.

Welcome to the Stonechip Tavern and Gambling Den, stranger. Looking for work in Ontus? Or did you come to our fine establishment because you heard we host the best games of chance this side of the Strid?
If you're looking for work, please talk to Quarry Boss Laurina. I have more important things to do than deal with common laborers.
The Carvain Ranch does not sell to individual buyers. This is not a general store. Might I suggest the markets in Skingrad? Or perhaps you can purchase a meal at the Stonechip Tavern?

Mirrormoor and Shardborn. Two words I never knew existed before all this. I have a lot of questions and not a lot of answers.\n\nI'd like to take Abolisher to Skingrad to have it examined by an expert I know. Is that all right with you, comrade?
The tangled threads of fate I sense around the Outcast Inn fill me with dread. Something dangerous and momentous is happening.\n\nI will meet you there, proxy.
Follow Tribune Alea into the barracks! Find out where the Daedra are coming from. Go!
Almost time. Damn. Arse. Rut it all.
I'm ready to do this. Nervous, but ready.
My brother looks furious. Good! I can't wait to see what happens.
You again. My sister's co-conspirator. Well, spit it out! Tell me what's going on here.
I'm not sure why we're all gathered here, but it must be for something important.
I'm on the edge of my blade here. If they can pull this off, we're having so many drinks tonight!
The pollen bats of my heart are swarming with joy. To think Laeni and Clendagal might be able to stay!
I see our conversation has borne fruit. Well done.

Those sneaky, envious, sorry excuses for bakers …. Father warned me to be wary, but for them to swarm like vultures right after he set sail? \n\nOh, sorry. It's just that my father is counting on me and everything has gone wrong.
Hyacinth means the world to me and I want to thank you properly, but he wants to speak to you first.
I can't go back in there. I'm hurt! One of the bastards must have grazed me as we made our retreat. When you talk to the captain, tell him I'm grievously wounded!
I'm not sure who you are or what you want, but you should probably speak to the captain.
Did the Legion send you? You should talk to the captain.
Thanks to you and Zerith-var, these cantors are safe now. I am so glad I sent you to investigate that fallen star!
We must defeat the turned cantor to cleanse her soul. Quickly, my friend!
I think I know where we are. This road matches this squiggly line.
It doesn't matter if he figures out the way. Discussing the Paradox will distract us until we're lost again. I'm afraid we're like that.
To say I am impressed would be an understatement. Since the beginning, you have proven yourself time and time again.\n\nEnough pleasantries. The Gardener would like a word.
All the relics are secured and activated. Hopefully this puts this business behind us, comrade. Let's head back to Beragon's townhouse.
My patience with you has reached its end, pathwalker. Soon, Mora's forces will storm this place and imprison me for an eternity. I suggest you not be here when they arrive.
Look, with all this talk about betrayals and traitors and everything, I … well, I'm worried about Tanlorin.
You saved Dawnwood from suffering, war, and ruin. The tree-sap people thank you.

I hope this is the start of something momentous. For the first time, I truly believe there can be trust, even friendship, between Skingrad and Vashabar. I would like to think Greenspeaker Darolith feels the same.
That unmarked wing is unlocked, is it? How exciting! I'm eager to hear what sort of trial awaits you on the other side.
I've been a knight in the Order for years, traveler, and I've never heard of anything like this. \n\nA lost art of shaping magic, an ancient library, and these Luminaries. This is incredible!

I serve the Prince of the Many Paths, and so I abide by her will. But I cannot understand allowing you and that other Ithelia to remain here. Not now, when the end is so near.\n\nSpeak to her as she wishes and go. We have urgent business to attend to.
A forest springs out of nowhere and covers a third of the Weald and no one does anything? What's the Legion waiting for? An all-out attack on the city?
I've never seen Goblins so agitated. I hope it's not too late to return the totems to them. I'd hate to have to write up this incident as a tragedy, not if it can be stopped.

It's done. The altar is quiet and for the first time in centuries, Scribing has returned to Tamriel. \n\nIt's clear Ulfsild did not send you. But I believe she would be quite proud of you just the same.
Dawnwood is magnificent, but what do you make of the devastated region along the border? The greenspeakers have been studying it, but so far they have no answers.

Have you seen the devastation at Dawnwood's borders? It's just awful. I know it isn't anyone's fault, but I can't help but wonder how the Colovians feel. \n\nAll we wanted was to nurture lands they've forgotten.

Just remember, you can always reference the Fable of the Indrik from your bag. Ulfsild's annotations will guide you on your journey. \n\nFind the wards, obtain the fragments. And soon you shall meet your first Luminary of Magic.
We came to West Weald for a new beginning, but there hasn't been much call for my talents. I'm a painter by trade, but the only work I can find here is at the Carvain Ranch.
We came here to start over, but Azemad labors on the ranch while I am forced to work in the quarry. They work us so hard, it is no wonder people are getting sick.

Without you and Tanlorin, my niece would be dead right now. I, ahem. I hope you believe me when I say how much your efforts mean to me. Thank you.\n\nAs for my relationship with the Proxy Queen, well. I hope I can rely on your discretion.
As much as I'd love to shower you and Bogcup with praise for saving me, there's no time. The Garland Ring must face the facts—we've been compromised! My arrest is proof of that.
My power is yours to wield, mortal. Merely take the sigil and bring it to the altar. It will remember what to do.

Hate to bring bad news to the tribune, but I'm the only member of the cohort left. Those Recollection zealots killed legionaries guarding the estate until we sent whoever remained down here.\n\nThat's when we walked right into the Daedra's clutches.
You've nearly restored that altar, haven't you? I'm impressed.\n\nWe ought to get things cleaned up around here before more of the guild comes in.

If we let more of the guild down here, I could catalog and analyze the tomes in earnest. My true passion! Instead of setting wards or cleaning cobwebs all day.\n\nI know that's not something you'll make a decision about. I just wanted to complain.

Did you pass the trial? That look on your face. The riddle did the trick! Congratulations! \n\nYou can never be certain things will turn out in your favor where Dragons are concerned. Even if she's not a traditional Dragon.
Just… you know, be careful. I'm not sure what's going on in Southpoint, but the Thalmor didn't seem bothered by it.

Ow. I'm normally so good at conversations, but this blasted trap on my leg is really getting in the way. \n\nWould you mind releasing it? I don't think I'll be able to form any more cohesive thoughts with it on like this.
There are some inscriptions here that Llaren's always wanted to study. I'll take a few rubbings for him. Might make for a nice surprise. Go on! I'll catch up.

This … this can't be real. It's some terrible dream. It must be! I'll take off this eye patch and wake up, bruised and beaten by the Legion in some alley. Please, let it be that!\n\nOh, gods. Valenia's gone.

Poor Valenia, taken in answer for our gravest mistake. She was just telling me of her family. A family she hoped to finally mend after so many years apart.\n\nI … I need a moment with my thoughts, friend.
What have I done? Oh, gods, Valenia! What cursed drink made me split us up! We walked right into Marcan Caelum's trap.\n\nLeave me be. Please!

Thank you for bringing all these precious creatures back to me. Still, I wonder about Marcien. It's not like them to be gone this long. \n\nI would check on them myself, but I can't leave my pets behind. They need me here.

Ah … I'm sorry. Everything hurts at the moment. Thank you for saving me, friend. Arm or no arm, I have my life, and I'm grateful for it.\n\nAlthough I don't think I'll be teaching Noraine archery, after all.

Well done getting the arcane knot out of there before things could go poorly. Good timing is either a matter of skill or luck, but Keshargo thinks you have the former. \n\nStill, he'll breathe easier knowing the knot is stabilized.
You haven't attacked, so I'll give you one chance to answer my question. Are you one of Xoryn's or are you here to help?
I made it out. I'm alive! I hope everyone else is all right.
Ulrath is dead … they're all dead. Did I hear that right?
So many good legionaries died for all the wrong reasons.
I see the knowledge of the Wilderhall has proven useful. That's pleasant.
I admit, this is all above my head. What do I know about magical disasters, Daedric invasions, or secret conspiracies? Give me problems I can solve with a sharp sword and I'd be much happier!
That look on your face. The Dragon gave you her trial, didn't she? She asked you to craft a riddle she can't solve.
Hmm, do you have a notion of what to do? Where to go? With your allies at your side, craft a riddle that will confound my thinking.\n\nI know you have it in you.
I hope nothing else has been tampered with. There's already so much wrong in the Scholarium. So much that didn't stand the test of time.
Thank you. It means a lot that we could help Elic find some … closure. I'm not sure he would have ever forgiven himself, if we hadn't been there today.
Go on. Take my sigil Not-Ulfsild! Before I decide there are new and better games to play.
You work with Nahlia? Are you with the Mages Guild? Maybe there's something you can do to help my father?
You're a friend of Nahlia's? Are you with the Mages Guild, too?\n\nThey've been overworking her for far too long. If you can't help Elic's father, maybe you could help with that.
It was here at Borderwatch that I was given command so many years ago. I sent for my son, urging him to enlist. We would defend these walls together.\n\nAnd he arrived, only to hand in his blade.
The Netch and the Dragon may be more outspoken. The Indrik more powerful. But I believe the Gryphon and the Fox were part of the Scholarium's heart. \n\nGood to see that heart beating again.
A fascinating creature, the Gryphon. The more I read, the more I hear from the Fox, the more it seems almost … sad. \n\nLike a character from the pages of the fables themselves.
Welcome, traveler. I'm Calantius, Count of Skingrad, Lord of West Weald, and so on, and so on.\n\nI hope you have time to enjoy all that our fair city and the surrounding countryside have to offer!
Let's discuss what you've found.
Viti had a sister? I had no idea. I hope you and Zerith can help guide her to Azurah's Crossing, walker.

Do not discount your own role in this, friend of Zerith-var. He takes his guidance from you.\n\nThis one is sorry for her part in your troubles. Viti's rejection of Zerith's necromancy … Viti was reminded of poor Eifa. An explanation, but no excuse.
Please, speak with my vanity. I know she can be unpleasant, but we need to find out what happened here.
What are you waiting for? Take that shiny, shiny sigil. You've earned it!

I sense you return with treasures of fire, ink, and shadow. Though, to be fair, the Fox spoiled the surprise. He was quite giddy upon his return.\n\nWell done. These stolen magics will allow me to secure the Scholarium.
Look, I'm sure your friend has a reasonable explanation for everything. But you can't blame Elelorn for thinking she bears a striking resemblance to one of our prisoners.
Do you know this criminal? She's nothing but trouble!
I still can't believe it. We're Ulfsild's legacy. You, me. And if I have anything to say about it, anyone that wants to learn the art of Scribing.

I was Ulfsild, it's true. But after all these years, I much prefer my feathers.\n\nOnly two things remain. Who will tend to the Scholarium? And the location of the final sigil, the last bit of power needed to amplify the altar.
You and Zerith must weaken Ravith-morna. I will save my voice until the time comes to sing Moon-Singer Talbira's song!
I'm still trying to get my stomach under control. Let's keep moving forward. With lots of nice, visible rock under our feet.
Are you our promised reinforcements? Not the most impressive sight I've ever seen, but if you'll raise a blade in our defense then you've got my respect.
Speak to the baroness, I must keep my eyes trained on our attackers.
I can assure you, there is no matter more urgent than the injuries I am tending to.
Please, leave me. There is no placating the heartbreak I feel.
Don't worry, I will do my very very best to ensure I have what you're looking for. I take my role as Chronicler for this expedition quite seriously!
Incredible! This must be the very heart of Ithelia's domain. Do you think we're the first mortals to ever see this place? We might definitely be the last, too. We'd better get down there.
I know nothing about Daedric machines or magic looms, but our enemies are down there. And whatever they're planning, it can't be good for West Weald. We need to put a stop to this, comrade.
Trust in fate, proxy. Choice and circumstance brought us to this moment. Now we must see it through.
Oh my fragile heart! Orissa's going back in there? Didn't she see the size of those terrible bugs?
Ostumir was never a metropolis, but it was our home.
Family comes first. That's what I always said. We built a nice home here. But now everything is ruined.
A traitor in the Garland Ring! That's not possible! Is it?\n\nYou should talk to Wisteria. I'd love it if the two of you got to know each other better. Heh. It might help dull the dread?
I thought I could handle this. Please, talk to her. Make her explain herself.\n\nI don't understand any of this.

Everyone else got such nice code names. Hyacinth, Oleander, Snapdragon? Come on, Bogcup? It never felt like me. \n\nBut, I guess, I am kind of a flower that blossoms in harsh environments. Heh. What a strange old man.

Wisteria betrayed us and for what? A Ceythalmor plan we know nothing about? I've been struggling to think of something, anything that could help us end this threat. Give us a direction.\n\nSo, imagine my surprise when I got a letter from a ghost.

There are three Haunted who need your help. I'll mark where to find them on your map. They're in this world, but their spirits are tormented in Detritus. This amulet will allow you to journey there to help them, and let me communicate with you, too.
F-fire, everywhere! It's going to burn us all, burn everything up! He showed me! \n\nI can't leave. I'll burn!
P-please forgive me. I'll try harder next time. I promise! I'll wash away the shame, I will pay any cost, no matter the sacrifice. Even if it kills me.
Cantor Krin'ze is driven by purpose, tamiit. Let us accommodate her idea. And, above all, keep her safe from harm.
Ravith has gone to bask in Azurah's embrace. To a warmth denied her for all the centuries she spent in darkness.\n\nLet us leave this place, tamiit. Nirni awaits our return.
There is much we should discuss, tamiit. Much I must … confess. But not here.\n\nLet us leave this place. I promise I will answer any questions you have. Just … not here.
Grr … why won't it come off? I have to wash it away, wash it all away. It won't be long until I drown in it!

The rotmeth's on me once we're published. \n\nThose remnants might have ended up in forgotten chests or monster remains. I wouldn't even be surprised if you had to resort to thievery. But imprisonment might only tighten our schedule, so be careful.
Begone. If you wish to throw your life away, Viti will not stop you.

I refuse to leave these prisoners to their fate. This could be their only chance to leave these foul cells. No one will come to aid them should we fail and I can't abide that. \n\nYou go on ahead. I'll see what I can do about opening these doors.
Daedric worship and dark magic rituals, I can understand. But the air here doesn't stink of Oblivion or anything more sinister than blood. It's unsettling in ways I did not anticipate.

We don't have much time. Mentor Huzbedad will do his best to get to the Elder Scroll before Orpheon, but he's just one Hel Netu monk.\n\nThere's a path underground that leads into the middle of the monastery. Khafdeed and I will follow.
This is a holy place. Can you not feel it, walker?
I was so frightened! The drums were relentless! But Krin'ze's song! She pulled us out of the darkness!
Krin'ze's song, it banished the darkness! I feel so much better!
Vanus always did have more tricks up his sleeve than a skeever has fleas. Take a look at the staff and figure out what's going on.
I'm pragmatic. Relieving this pain is worth what I have to tell you.\n\nDo you have the mistscrub leaves?
This isn't my doing. Vanus's staff seems to have a mind of its own. Take a closer look.
Something overwhelmed Skordo and his comrades, but I don't see the great Orc's body. I fear Skordo has been captured. Grab his sword and let's examine it.
Can't say I like Rivenspire. I plan to move somewhere less gloomy once I finish this stint with the Fighters Guild.
