This one mourns all the losses our guild has dealt with lately.
You did well against Garvin. I hope all of Orpheon's inner circle fall that easily. \n\nThe tunnels were survivorless, but Sister Chana healed the monks we found earlier. They live, thanks to you.
Is this some Mages Guild trick meant to sway us? Well, do as Gabrielle suggests. I want to see what happens.

Heed Vastarie and Shando-ri, tamiit. But trust that those connected to Azurah cannot be content with destroying the soul of another as the only course of action.\n\nAzurah's gaze is upon us now. Perhaps we may find some way yet to save Arum-Khal.
Is the staff dangerous? Perhaps I'll just stand back here.
These theatrics are delaying any hope of an agreement. Please get on with it.
The staff is reacting to you. That's a good sign, don't you think? Anyway, do as Gabrielle says and see what occurs.
You know what? I'm honestly surprised. I just didn't think Julien had it in him.\n\nBut this necklace … I've never seen the like. Now I know. This is what love feels like.
I feel much better about leaving now. In fact, I feel proud.
What is it? I'm afraid we've got a bit of an emergency at the moment.
Gloria suspects Faolchu's agents are here among us, even now.
Wait! What about Rozenn! Was that real, or was it just a dream?\n\nWhere is she? Do you know? I think it was real. You! You have to help me!
You look like you can defend yourself. Welcome to Camp Tamrith.

If you've come to Firebrand Keep to petition for help from the Knights of the Flame, I'm afraid you'll be disappointed. \n\nOur leader, Sir Hughes, seems to have gone mad, and the knights are divided over whether or not to follow his last order.
If you can spare a few moments, my master would like to have a word with you.
Thank you for your help.\n\nJulien is easily distracted, but I love him all the same.

Lieutenant! Where in Oblivion have you been? Those damn sleep scrolls were useless against the brutes! The Orcs breached the walls, and we're down to just a few dozen men, including the King's Guard. \n\nI'm afraid it may be time to surrender.

S'rashi has marked where you can find these debtors on the map. Start with the gambler, Louis Ervine. \n\nErvine owes S'rashi the most money. S'rashi needs money from the others too, but search for them after Ervine.
Go on inside.\n\nHer Ladyship wouldn't want you to miss any of the "fun."
Go on inside.\n\nHer Ladyship's been missing you.
No. This can't be happening. \n\nNot Mathias. He wouldn't have stomped on a diseased rat, let alone hurt a person ….
There you are! Have you seen Heloise? Some of the Hinaults have arrived, but I haven't seen Heloise since she ran off with her healing kit.
One thing you can always count on after a battle—lots of extra weapons.\n\nI saw some of the soldiers tossing weapons into the barn. You should be able to find everything Gennove asked for in there.
This is not a good time for the Knights of the Flame to be divided.
I never thought I'd see the day when Firebrand Keep was divided. These are dark times indeed.
Did you find Mathias? I hope he hasn't left town or anything.\n\nIt would … break my heart if I lost him as a manservant.

I hope you don't travel to Alcaire Castle only to find it under siege. If that is the case, I have made a grave mistake.\n\nLook for Dame Falhut though. Hopefully, the Redguards have simply come here in a diplomatic capacity.
Soon, I will rest. Soon, I will find peace.
A chicken, you say? I guess it wasn't Akatosh after all.
A chicken! Well, I'll get Valdam to undo it. Eventually.
Now that we got the crew out safely, next order of business is to get back to sea.\n\nI'm betting we'll have better luck finding a ship in Wayrest than back in that little village.
Thank you for helping <<1>>, but it's Murk-Watcher that worries Dro-Dara now.\n\nTime seems to have softened Murk-Watcher's mind. She often is being very confused and very stubborn.

Ah, the young adventurer again. You remind me of the old days. So many stories I could tell, but you'll want to be leaving, of course. \n\nWell, we might be heading out too. Janne might be right about a curse here. Speaking of Janne, have you seen her?
This life is not the one for me. Star-crossed should be my name.

I'm sure there are souls in those gems. Even now, I can hear them.\n\nI don't know why they're being held. I don't know what end it serves, but it's not right. They're in torment. Please, you must aid them.
Finish what we started. If I die, I want to die knowing we got rid of the ogres. \n\nIf I live … well, I'm not gonna live long with all these ogres around anyways.
The ogres' leader is called 'Skull Crusher'. He's big, he's mean, and he's nasty, but you can take him.\n\nI would send soldiers to help you, but another battle is brewing, and they have to prepare.
May the Eight bless you for helping us. \n\nPlease, find my Arcady.

I appreciate your assistance, but I would not want you to think of the Spirit Wardens as helpless.\n\nWe are a capable lot, but to be attacked out of nowhere like this, and by the Midnight Union … we were just caught off guard.
Seek out the King in Wayrest and give him the news. He must know as soon as possible.
I imagine Abbot Durak has a plan to recover the Dream Shard. And I'll wager you're involved.
You look pretty dangerous. Consider yourself drafted. \n\nThere are Goblins here that need killing.
See that you succeed. My beloved doesn't like failure, and insists that I punish it. \n\nSeverely.

Speaking to you now as a friend, and as your king, I wonder if I might prevail upon you to assist me with some other matters.\n\nOne that is a matter of state, and another that is of a more … personal nature.
What!? Can't you let a man enjoy a moment's rest? \n\nOr does King Emeric need this bench right now?

I don't think the slavers knew what to do with the focusing crystals. Those may be close by. But the oil—they probably took that on board their ship.\n\nIf you can recover the supplies, I'll be ready to relight the fire. Godspeed to you, my friend.
What are you doing here? Only Apostle Marian is permitted in my sanctum. \n\nWhere is she? Didn't you give her the Water Stone?
Thank you. Now, with nature's blessing, our little friend will survive the Reachmen invasion. \n\nBut as for her sisters … the only thing left is to avenge them.
Praise the Eight! I can't tell you how delighted I am to see you. First, the Reachmen advance stopped, then the crows flew away, and now … you're back.\n\nI have a feeling you bring good tidings.
Get the key off his body. That's all he's good for now. And don't worry, he won't remember a thing when he wakes. If he wakes.
Use that scroll on a dreaming cultist. Bind him to your will and lead him back here!\n\nQuickly now! I can't contain this thing much longer.
Dreughside's returning to normal. We'll cordon off the dreugh and let the guards sort things out.\n\nGuess your work here's done.
Though she does not want these johads, Jahi has always been a better administrator than our father ever was. It will be an honor to learn from her.
If the Withered Hand is planning something else, I hope we discover what it is quickly. Preferably before they are able to carry it out.
I regret that my father did not heed the warnings of the Ash'abah before, but I am truly grateful that you appeared to help set matters straight.\n\nSometimes one person can make all the difference.
Isn't it pleasant up here? It's far above the dust of the streets, the air is cooler …. Between you and me, I think that's why mages build towers. Smart, huh?
Go now and light the final brazier. \n\nDo not fear the power of Tu'whacca. You and I, we are his champions in this.
What is your dream? You want to be stronger? Smarter? Faster? \n\nFor the right price, Unishi will make your dreams come true!
True honor need not be named, my friend, but I'll sure as Oblivion remember your heroics.

I cannot tell you how relieved I am to hear that the Ansei Ward is safe. I will summon other Ash'abah to come here and help clean out the rest of these Ra-Netu.\n\nYou—you must go after the third Ansei Ward.
Go on now. The blade is restored and I must rest. Take it to someone you trust to keep it safe.
The way is open to you and your Redguard friend. Once inside, you may not want to leave.\n\nI welcome you. You may stay as long as you desire. Longer, even.
You have heard my stories. I have no more for you today.\n\nNow you must learn from the other masters. <<1>> awaits you at the dueling arena.
Exiled! My torment shall be without end. I know Raifa considers this merciful, but it is not.\n\nI do not blame you, either. Not now, at any rate.
I still can't quite believe what's happened. I'm not sure how I will explain it to the younger students.\n\nNo matter. Leki's Blade needs a strong leader. This duty falls to me.
And so it comes to an end, with all of us gathered together at the last.\n\nThe student. The disciples. The master. And an arbiter!
Justice sometimes wears a mask. Kindness, revenge, duty. Fate.\n\nWhat mask did my choice wear this day? Only time will tell.
If the Magistrate was somehow involved in this, she must be brought to justice!
We are looking for large gazebo structures with orbs inside. Disrupting the orbs is our goal here.

Joile's betrayal taught us yet another virtue: caution—wariness. We remain slow to trust, but loyal beyond measure. \n\nYou have reached the summit! The Make-Way God, sees much at this height. Have you learned the greatest lesson of this place?
Go on. I will not suffer the humliation of being arrested. I will turn myself in.
I did not see you in this garden before, wayfayer. Be welcome!\n\nI await my beloved. Roses are her favorite. Their scent reminds me of her ….
Help us bring Rama to justice. He's responsible for this slaughter.
You're both crazy. Killing Master Muzgu—there must be another way!
Please. Show mercy. You can't leave me here with these savages.
The dreugh attacked in the night, but we got some of them! The boys are ripping apart their bodies. \n\nIf we catch any more, we're cooking them alive. They'll pay for this!
I wish there was another way, but if this allows me to rejoin my brother, so be it.
The towers. Were you able to close the conjuration boxes in the towers?
If what you say about the Dream Shard is true, Adima must be allied with the Supernal Dreamers.\n\nThat makes poor Hosni nothing but a pawn in all this.
Where's the sword? What happened?
I hear there's been real trouble over in Camlorn. Something about werewolves.

Well met, traveler. The Aldmeri Dominion and the Ebonheart Pact are marching on the Imperial City. We are mobilized, but our supply lines are stretched dangerously thin.\n\nWill you restore the balance and aid the war effort?

<<1>> lives in the house just north of the inn. For now, I just need you to go there and make sure she's not about to engage in any more rash behavior. \n\nI'll get my men and meet you there shortly to take her into custody.

The villagers may not realize it, but you saved this town from crumbling into chaos.\n\nI mentioned before that I came from Alcaire Castle. The situation there is critical, and I think you might be able to make a difference.
So Dame Dabienne wasn't working with the slavers after all.\n\nThat's a relief.

I've been constable here at Koeglin Village for more than a decade. I haven't let the town down so far, and I don't mean to do so today.\n\nThat ship is a threat. I'll see it gone even if I have to sink it myself.

In all my years sailing these seas, I have never received such ill treatment in a friendly port. 

My men lie here bleeding on deck, and we are refused aid.

This man they call constable is a son of a dog … or did he change his mind?
I just can't believe my Rosalie would … it's just unthinkable.\n\nI owe you for my life, and for my daughter's welfare. Though she wants to thank you herself.

If Constable Pascal sent you here with orders to open the forge, you can just turn around and head right back out the door.\n\nThat man has no right to order me around, and I'm not about to issue weapons for his witch hunt.
My poor little baby … all alone out there ….\n\nIf you're leaving the village, if you could please look out for my son. With these slavers about, I'm afraid something terrible has happened.
Please. Please hurry! I have a feeling something terrible is going to happen! \n\nShe wouldn't hurt my father, would she?
I don't understand what happened to the general, but I will say he just hasn't been himself lately.\n\nIf there's anything I can do to help him, please let me know.
Well, I guess you're Hammerdeath Arena's new champion.\n\nJust goes to show, you shouldn't judge by appearances.
Back so soon. Good. Learn anything?
Do you have anything to report?
Help Wyress Jehanne, please.
We're ready for the nobles. You're giving them a signal, right?
My sisters and I should be able to open a path to safety, but we'll need your help again to make this work.
My father and I were both deeply saddened to hear of my sister's death. \n\nI understand you made the call to execute her murderer. You made the right choice, and I thank you for it.
I'm sure Faolchu would call mercy a weakness. But I think it shows strength of character. \n\nWe're going to need such strength in the days ahead.
You can find Sibellec in the northern wyrd camp. Just follow the road across the bridges.
You'll find Sarvith in the tent behind me. \n\nAnd please remind Sarvith to be careful. He's brilliant, but he doesn't always pay as much attention to detail as he should.

What are we still standing around for? Let's go find the Daggers and get this job done.\n\nWith the gold that Lord Diel pays us, we can set up a shop within the city and buy proper uniforms and everything.
Search the house. As <<1>> says. If you find nothing, I must assume Ohama's lying and throw her and my fool brother out.\n\nThat is, if he ever shows up again, the lazy slug.
My brother and I will pack up here and follow behind you.\n\nAny harpies you catch in the throwing snare, we'll be sure to haul in and get back to camp.
You have returned. And you are victorious. Just as I have foreseen it.
Please finish this. Retrieve the sword from the chapel and take it to the burial vault where Rosalind died.\n\nDo what I cannot and face my poor wife's shade.
We're safe for the moment, Captain. Go find your husband.

Fried fire salts! This is way worse than I realized. \n\nThe Withered Hand, eh? When I get back to the tower, I'll see if I have anything on them … it'll be useful when you come ask for my help again, which I'm sure you will.
I pray that we are not too late to stop the Withered Hand, and with the same breath, I thank the gods for guiding you here.\n\nTu'whacca watch over you, wayfarer.
Good to see you again. We owe you a great deal, you know.
Well done. When we get back to town, I'll raise a tankard in your name.
I've heard a lot of greetings, but that one's new to me.
I'm afraid there isn't much time. \n\nWe expect Faolchu to launch a full-scale assault at any moment.
You're back! Tell me, what did you see?
I think one of those spiders bit me. I feel a little woozy.\n\n<<1>> … sounds familiar but I can't put my finger on it.
Meet us at the ritual site. And don't forget the lurcher.
It is well, but there is more to do. We cannot rest just yet.
You did it. You killed Faolchu.

I have realized what I must do. \n\nI will build a shrine to honor my fellow priests that were slain here … it will be an everlasting testament to their sacrifice and to the temple's ability to persevere.
Wonderful! We'll slip past their very noses. Just like in the stories!
Risking danger just to recover trinkets for me. Our family will always remember this.
We are in your debt, friend. I hope you made Angof suffer before you finished him!
You made it. No zombie bites or anything.
Camlorn is free! It may take a while, but we're going to recover from Faolchu's vile touch.
These cursed werewolves. I just …. \n\nHow in Oblivion did you get in here?
Father's at peace now. I need a change of scenery, so I'm going to Stormhaven.\n\nMaybe I'll see you there one of these days.
Please. Go away! There is … nothing you can say that will console me.\n\nMy sweet Casnar is either dead, or he's decided he doesn't love me! I-I don't know which is worse!
Must be nice. Being able to just walk out of here and do whatever you want.
We'll need all the armor and weapons you can find. \n\nJust think how grateful some of these sweet young citizens will be.
Activate the stones in the four huts. My sisters need a safe place to work.
We established a perimeter around the village. Nothing that comes this way will get past us.\n\nBut we can't cover the docks. I don't have enough soldiers for that.
Unfamiliar with Sentinel?\n\nThe inn is just east of here. The smithy is on the far east side. The alchemist is in the market, just south of the inn.
The cure won't work unless the werewolves are weakened first. \n\nRemember. Weaken them, then use the antidote. Send anyone who's cured back here.

You're going to help us, eh?\n\nI could have figured this out, you know. If I could find a way to weigh the harpy down so it'd trigger the trap … you know what? It's probably better that you take care of this.
Collect the keys and bring Anton's jeweled crown to me. I'll reward you handsomely. \n\nEven better, I'll mention you in my next book.
You took back my city.\n\nWe will rebuild and Camlorn will rise again. Thank you for everything you've done.
Ha! Now you're just showing off. \n\nBut I'm glad to see you alive and well. Darien, too. Tamriel would be a poorer place without the two of you in it.
I tried to stop him, but it was all I could do just to keep him from killing Father Quiston!\n\nDamn it all! What are we going to do now?
I think perhaps I had our assignments wrong. I should've checked the stocks and sent you to check the ship.
Come now, I don't expect that switch is just going to throw itself. \n\nIf you get the switch, I'll go on into the chamber. Then you can just meet me inside.
I watched you rummaging around out there in the ruins. If you had been in trouble, I would've had your back, just so you know.\n\nI'm guessing you've gathered all the tools by now?
You again! Truly, the gods continue to blight my path with your affliction.\n\nI expect <<1>> enlisted you to facilitate my return. You are so very good at returning things to him, are you not?

What's the point of hiring a guide if all he's going to do is abandon you at the first sign of difficulty?\n\nNot that you could possibly understand. Consider that a hypothetical … rhetorical question.
Go, do as the girl bids. We will wait for the Sentinel's strength to wane. And wane it will.
Whatever was in the royal crypt, at least it doesn't appear to have been lethal.\n\nTell me though—did you learn anything? Any explanation for my unexpected return to life?

The wyrd and I have always had a tenuous relationship. But saving Elara was something I needed to do, regardless of their objections.\n\nIt will make this process harder than it needs to be, but I still have some spirit in me yet!
You killed him! How could you?\n\nWhat gives you the right to come here and contest our ways?
Well, I think I've gathered up all Lady Laurent's personal effects from the camp.\n\nI just need those tools from out in the ruins. I don't suppose you beat Tamien to them, did you?
We have to find the <<1>>. If Stenwick needs a spriggan bud, then I'll do anything to get it for him.
Count on me to get the knights out of here. You just protect Gabrielle. \n\nIf this mad plan actually works, I'll see you inside the crypt.
We need the support of the town council. Without them, the rest of the townsfolk will be too afraid to fight back.
Wizard Benele said you'd gotten inside and were hunting Angof. \n\nWe wanted to help, but I hope we haven't done more harm than good.
Did you meet with Tamien Sellan? He's got the right idea. \n\nTime to take back this town.
The serpent must feast.
Around here, we're working hard to put an end to the Withered Hand. A wealthy benefactor is paying the guild to kill that scum on sight. \n\nInterested in a contract?

What do you want? The Withered Hand is massing to finish what they started. If we don't prepare, they'll kill everyone in town! \n\nUnless this is urgent, <<1>>, I must get back to prepping the guildhall's defenses.
Go on. Through the portal with you.\n\nThere's no time to waste.
I have much to ponder now. Do you have further questions of me, my friend?
So it sounds like we can untie him, right?
I'm sorry, I need a moment to gather my thoughts.\n\nSo much senseless tragedy. And now they will be looking to me for guidance. I need to prepare myself.
If Kerbol harms a hair on Draven's head, I'll never forgive myself.
Such a waste. I'd hoped Draven would listen to reason before it came to this.
What do you want to know?
You sure found me a fast lizard! \n\nDid you hear the crowd? They loved it!
By Zenithar, it worked!\n\nAfter what you did, every able-bodied citizen is talking to Tamien Sellan. They all want to join the resistance.
What are you, lost? It's over there, in the other big tent just up the way!\n\nDon't tell me you're as useless as <<1>>.
<The dog motions to the mound of sand.>
Was your lizard the fast one?\n\nI've never seen a lizard move that quickly!
Do not delay, wayfarer. The people of the Alik'r have been living in terror, and this is how we put their fears to rest.\n\nI would not want them to suffer this anxiety any longer than is necessary.
The mine! It is collapsing! I left the—my partner down there! \n\nI beseech you to help me in this!
I wonder what awaits me?
Remember. If you see anything suspicious, let me know.
I sometimes wonder whether <<1>>'s found the sword already and hasn't told me.\n\nNo, he hasn't the wit to keep such a treasure secret.

Lorelia promises she will reward you generously for your assistance. \n\nThe Primeval Seekers are holding our disciples across this water and down in the east side of the ruins. Please, free them as soon as you can.
See you again soon, I hope.
Sometimes I wonder if it's worth the risk.

Imperials and beetles both have surly dispositions and sharp implements, but you must persevere.\n\nThe future of <<1>> may rest on your shoulders! Once I catch my breath, I'll meet you at the ruins below the Craglorn gate.
Our first concern must be ensuring that the Nereid does not acquire the capability to create a Water Stone.\n\nOnce she gets enough memory essences, there will be little we can do to stop her.
I'll admit, I'm starting to believe his story. At least he really does have a wife and daughter.
It's so cold out here. I hope they let me go soon. I need to find my family.\n\nAnd I could sure use a shirt and a pair of pants.
If not for you, this place would have been overrun by Dominion forces by now. \n\nWell done, friend, well done.
So, did you find anything incriminating inside the inn?
Mother is sad. Very, very sad.
They must pay for what they've done to our town.
You! You are the responsible one! I told her not to trust those creatures, and now look what's happened!

I'll do as the constable says and work to settle our differences, but Leonce's connection with Northpoint concerns me. And I'm worried about the Orcs he sent there. There's no telling what foul purpose they are being put to.
Seems you've poked a hornet's nest. I hope whatever you did was worth it.
What do you want? Can't you see I'm doing my work? Or are you harassing me because I don't bow my head to the ground before the Imperials?
Tall Papa watch over you.
I heard everything! They have my Hazzi? Those Imperial dogs best not touch a hair on her head!\n\nWhy didn't Dhakir tell me? We must shoulder such burdens together!
Burn the ballistae outside the west gate. That should keep them occupied for a while.\n\nMeet Holgunn when you're finished.
You sacrificed power to give the dead peace. This was not an easy choice.\n\nYour kindness means there's hope. I think it's up to me and my assistants to give back.
I need a solution. Stabbing spirits gets us nowhere. Any ideas?
Make sure my brother doesn't ruin the reputation of House Rii.
I hope Soft-Scale's balm worked. \n\nNow if these milk drinkers can actually stop squabbling, that will be magic.
My servants say <<1>> is still in the ruins southwest of here. See if she has anything to do with <<2>>'s disappearance.
Shalk wander the streets. That makes them easier to find, but harder to kill. \n\nIf we aid his people, Girvas must admit we do not intend to kill and eat them.
His soldiers are dead! \n\nHead down the trapdoor in the tower to look for Strikes-from-Shadows. That old fetcher would never fall to the likes of those Covenant scum.
Cracking through the husk of a fallen legend, your own tale will begin to grow tall and strong.
I hope Soft-Scale's balm worked. \n\nNow if only the Dunmer and Argonians worked together. There's too much to do here.
What are you waiting for? You've got arson to commit!
Bring those plans to Captain Llaari. She's at the command post, the largest building in the fort. \n\nI'll warn the troops and get them formed up into squads. We've got to watch out for each other.
I hope Soft-Scale's balm worked.\n\nIf you could get these Dunmer and Argonians to trust each other, I'd buy you a flagon of mead, if this place had any.
Go. The vision of the past awaits.
This news is very disturbing. I'm at a loss.\n\nPeople disappear into thin air and someone brought a plague into Narsis? That terrifies me. How could they even accomplish this without our notice?
You're alone … You don't need to tell me. She's off doing something foolish, of course.
Have you rescued the villagers captured by the Khajiit?
The sorcerer is right. Slaughtering these Nedes and harvesting their hearts is the only way to set the stage for our victory.
This is justice, that the blood of fallen Nedes will open the way for their defeat.\n\nGo, soldier! Kill the troops and slay Ornskar. Then report at the ritual altar.
You found the brothers? Good. Now for the matriarch. She must be hiding.\n\nI'd try that cave on the western edge of the sulfur pools.
Defend the statue!
How fares my son? How is <<1>>?

Without your help, I'd never have defeated the Goblin chief and his spider queen. I'm going to collect the Gob's head as a trophy for my father.\n\nHead back to the manor house and give my father the good news. I'll meet you when I'm done.
The Goblins have taken <<1>> into the cave near the beach. You've got to save him!
Ah. You have the skull and candle. You want me to be impressed? You can gather small objects. Good for you.\n\nNow stand back while I perform the ritual.
Now go. Take this knowledge and defeat Balreth.\n\nKill him this time!

My sons have returned. I'm in your debt, but my wife and daughter are still missing.\n\nMy boys told me my wife and daughter fled to a cave nearby. That must be the one on the western edge of the pools.
In you go. We're right behind you.
Go into the fort and unbar the gates, my friend. The might of the Pact is going to wash over these invaders like a wave.
Tread carefully upon the Coiled Path.
A decision must be made. Our fate depends upon it.
I always remind people. If you decide to talk to a prisoner in the stocks, never trust a word they say.\n\nCriminals will say anything to convince you that they're innocent.
It's good to see you again! I do not like being here alone.
One of our people will find you when we're about to begin the assault. Do what you need to do. Then meet us at the kinhouse.
Shouldn't you be following Rhavil?

If you wish to aid us, gather the items I requested. Ashreeds grow in the tidepools in our quarter, and mudcrabs thrive on the shores nearby.\n\nGather some of each and present them at the roots of our Hist.
A totem? My wife has always been creative. \n\nSave who you can. I'll take over treatment when they get here.
What a fool I am!\n\nI led a bunch of untrained townfolk into a battle they couldn't win. They're all dead, but it's my fault.

You need to find the missing villagers and get them to safety before Madras leads this group to its doom.\n\nI'll find out where Madras thinks they are. But first, you have to help me slow Madras down.
Naryu informed me that you found a note at the Maulborn camp. That might be a link to the creator of the Llodos plague.\n\nThis drastically changes our stance on the situation here.
Well, well! Aren't you a fancy lass? \n\nWhat do you want, Elf? Come to complain about the Daggers? Go hide behind your mother's skirt, not the Nords.
Ah, good! Another apprentice! I thought you all were dead.\n\nWhy are you just standing there? Summon the guardians at once!
Quickly, take those things to <<1>>!\n\nWith a little luck, we can beat this curse!
My husband needs those potions. They're the only thing that will counteract the fumes in the mine.
I wish I knew why someone would be so malicious. I'll continue investigating.\n\nThe kwama should return to normal in a few days, thanks to you.
Be off, outsider.
Such courage. Keep in mind, these people are terrified. Talk to them or use the totem, but get them moving.
The way is open.\n\nGo. End this.
Let's learn what we can about this plague and then get out of here.\n\nWe'll be right behind you.
What happened in there? Where's Diiril?\n\nHe's gone, isn't he?
Heh. I won't tell if you won't tell. Hand over the Sleezle so I can set it aside.

How is this possible? You didn't bargain with Clavicus Vile, did you?\n\nOne moment, the curse upon you isn't permanent. This is wonderful, for both of us! Quickly, retrieve the <<z:1>> before it wears off!
A new face? You'll need to speak with <<1>>.\n\nIt's for your own safety, I assure you.
You'll likely find <<1>> at home. <<2>> works at the smithy.\n\nAs for <<3>>, try the Mages Guild. Hold your nose when talking to that one.
Well? What did you see? Speak, curse you!
The Worm Cult nearly unlocked the secrets of the <<z:1>>. If they could get their hands on it, so could anyone else.\n\nThis torment will never end, unless you're the one to end it.
My son is free and my hands are unbound. Now the Vanguard will learn the price of threatening House Dres.
The look on your face … you've discovered where the grandmaster's son is being held?
Ha! Welcome to the invulnerable fellowship! Wait, your blessing doesn't feel … permanent.\n\nAh, well! Enjoy it while it lasts.
Ra-shadda asked to be forgiven. The beast blathered about understanding and change.\n\nThe animal responsible for the death of my Tiril dared to address me!
You conquered the Trial of the Mind. Faster than <<1>>, might I add. Perhaps he's not suited to feats of intelligence.
All may attempt the trials, but only the Hist knows who will pass and who will fail.
Complete the Trial of the Fang and you can commune with the Hist.\n\nDrink the root rot poison to begin your trial. While under its effects, challenge an opponent!
The look in your eyes. You've communed with the Hist, I see.\n\nYou and the Dominion captain make two outsiders in one day. A portent if there ever was one.
Ah, you're back. What do you say?
Find that Dres coward for me and I'll be in your debt.
The merchant serves the Ghost Snake now. I think you chose well.
Go. Speak with those who are still alive. Then focus the totem, and be ready to fight.\n\nEnd the sorrow of Sathram.
You found that as fast as a nix-hound on the hunt. \n\nThe gel disrupts Fatestealer's stones. That should free my egg-kin from the Daedra's clutches.
You're back! Did you get the key and the book?
It seems your Dark Elf friend was correct. Alten Corimont aided the Dominion without my permission. This displeases me.
How goes your investigation? Any luck?
Captain Doronil, at your service.
Mind your step in my training yard, outsider.
Do you come bearing a sword, or are your palms open to the sky?
Please, find out who did this to Eroni.
Sayne sent you, didn't she? Of course she did. Can't let me mourn my brother in peace and quiet when she can send someone to check on me every half hour.
What could you possibly want?\n\nHave you come to gloat? Are you here to laugh at my expense?
You startled me! I thought you were a Khajiiti pirate.
<<1>> sent me. It's about his wife, Eroni.
That pendant is our best work. Look after it.

Forgive me. The Dominion's torture ripped my thoughts away from myself. I tried to tell you before, but it was like speaking with a mind full of sap.\n\nThe keystone is sealed in the Temple of Sul. I'll do all I can to help you retrieve it.
When I said <<1>> was indisposed, I spoke half the truth. He's missing, and I fear it's the work of our killer.\n\nThis is why <<2>> and I request your utmost discretion in recovering <<1>> to us.
I am glad Brethis understands the wise woman's good intentions. \n\nNow if only everyone would see as they do. We've been fighting with the housemen for centuries. I suppose fear is to be expected.
Honor to you and your house, traveler. Have you come to join the war effort?
If you're helping <<1>>, please see <<2>>.
Good luck at Othrenis, my friend. The dead do not always rest easily.
Enter <<1>> and find Balreth. Garyn will be right behind you. Meanwhile, the troops and I will hold the portal. \n\nGood luck.
Were you successful? I came to help, but there was a ward on the door. I couldn't get past it.
I know I have no chance against you in a fight. If you must barge into my home, then do so! That will only prove you wrong.\n\nThis isn't the last you've seen of me.
I know it must be done, but I think it's barbaric. Killing soldiers as they attack you, that's war. \n\nMurdering men and culling out their hearts … well, it's cowardly.
I'm preparing for a special ritual, soldier. I can't leave this place.\n\nIf you're looking for someone in charge, speak to the sorcerer at the ritual altar.
I'm maintaining my position for an important assignment, soldier.\n\nIf you need more information, speak to the sorcerer at the ritual altar.
We haven't much time, soldier. Those savages could break our lines at any moment.
We're going to hold out here until told otherwise.\n\nWe'll need to ensure none of Vox's minions decide to try and leave the area without us noticing.
Help Holgunn deal with the troops outside the west gate. Buy my father some time.
<<1>> told me to expect you, but …. Wait, something's off. Beyond your flesh and blood, I mean.\n\nZ'en's blessings! The curse upon you is temporary. You can safely recover the <<z:2>>!
And one more thing. The Sacred Lady wishes to speak with you. Personally. She awaits your presence. Please, head to the Temple at once.
Wait, you're the hero of Stonefalls! Please, be welcome here in the city. We've been told to watch for you.
Enter my temple and banish these Daedric invaders, my child.
Ho, there! Newcomers must talk to <<1>>.
Newcomer, please obey and report to <<1>>.
Find a way to kill <<1>> and I'll reward you handsomely.
What are you doing out here? You'd best get back to Walks-in-Ash in the ruins beneath the fort.
Welcome back adept! How goes the quest for knowledge?

We need the Stone complete to contain the Daedra, finish the Goblins—you have my thanks. I hope you fathom what you offer.\n\nSir Edgard, my second in command, and his squad already have one piece. They've gone looking for more, but haven't returned.
<<1>> and I need to catch our breath before we move on to Mud Tree.
If only we could deprive those necromancers of more of their servants ….
Brave traveler, I extend the spine of welcome to you. What brings you to our little village?
Merciful Healing Mother! What is that dreadful noise?
Welcome back. What's the news from the field?
Kaasha's just outside, selling her wares near the manor wall.\n\nOnce you've found what we're looking for, get back here and report to Denu. She'll know what to do.
Watch yourself out there. Those creatures … it's hard to believe they were once like us.
All right, the ward is down. That was harder than I thought.\n\nWe're right behind you. Get in there!
My scavengers and I appreciate your help. I don't know what's going on with the bog beasts, but at least we can protect ourselves now.
Collect the fire salts and kill the invasion's leaders. They'll be thrown into disarray.\n\nOnce we set fire to the river, the attack will begin.
Nice to see you made it in one piece.
Friend or foe? Speak up. I may be a prisoner, but I won't be toyed with.
Be careful with that Kothringi. From what I've seen, he seems a bit unstable.\n\nThat's if he's really a Kothringi. He'd be the last of his kind.
You must get to our Hist tree right away. Dig up that relic and take it to the ritual site. Use it to stop Namira from corrupting Xal Ithix!
This <<1>> is unknown to me. If it originated in Shadowfen, perhaps an Argonian would know more.
Why did that fool Nord insist we all come together? The ale's finally rotted his last bit of sense.
Get out of here while the portal holds. I'll go after the prisoners and make sure they leave safely.

What to do with you, what to do? Far too entertaining to slaughter, yet I can't let another Daedra get their hooks inside you. Besides, I assure you mine are the rustiest.\n\nPositively maddening, you are. If I end you now, we'll be together. Forever.
Has the target met an untimely end?
My mother found her way to the inn. Did you help her get here?
My brother arrived in the inn. Do I have you to thank for this?
You step firmly on the path I feel beneath my own feet. Could it be she finally answers our cries?\n\nI am the Speaker, outsider. Of what shall we speak?
In doubting you, I doubted the Night Mother. I called you a heretic. What does this make me?
Do you have it? Did you find the keystone?
It's been quite some time since I saw a new face. Why are you here?
Thank the sands! How about untying me? They've had me down here for a week.
Why do you delay? Seize the coal in your grasp.
By Satakal, you scared me! I've been dodging ferals for hours. I thought they had finally found me.\n\nWho are you?
It will take time to deal with the Daedra that came through before you closed the portals. We'll be busy for a while, it seems.

You again? Vivec knows how much I suffered as a chicken. And with the master's constant threats to eat me … well, lesson learned.\n\nOh, and I learned Andoren can't be trusted. Now about my brother ….
Strange meeting you out here in the wilds. I never did eat my apprentice, though now I somewhat wish I had.
Your clothes may fool the Dominion, but the egg-scent doesn't cling to your body as it does ours. Stay away from their tigers.
Thank you. Those people are savages. I hear they eat their own dead.\n\nI'll return to <<1>> shortly.
Xuth! No! The heat, the stench, the flames ….

Without a leader, the Shadowscales shall wither. <<1>> and <<2>> each suit my needs, but each will fracture in their own way.\n\nUse your judgment, supplicant. Tell the Night Mother what she fails to see in their hearts.
We must find the tome and crystal. \n\nA weapon against Molag Bal's minions, within our grasp!
So <<1>> is well? That's good news, but I know he won't leave the mine until everything's settled.
Good. A totem and miners.\n\nNow find Thragnar, my overseer. He'll tell you how to get the Goblins back under control with that thing … assuming he's not dead.
The longer we're trapped, the greater the chance we'll turn feral … or be eaten by them.
I submit to the will of the Night Mother.
Tell Sees-All-Colors what happened here. Then come find me and Merric.
The winds have changed. The stormclouds part. You have the relics, yes? I can sense them.
You survived! Truly the Hist guides you.\n\nBut did you succeed?
She wants the Fang? I say, give it to her! If it does to her what it did to me ….\n\nWait, maybe that isn't such a good idea.
You are the sun on my scales, comrade. You've returned Merric to us.
She almost had me. Thank you, comrade.
If it is not one thing, it is another.
Chilling. Look at this place. It was deliberately set on fire.
The lens compells the students to join the Maulborn. You must destroy it!
I'm going to stay up here until you clear things out a bit. They're just illusions, so you'll be safe, right? \n\nOh, please be careful.
Ah, my business partner. I've located another rare and valuable vintage here in Ebonheart.\n\nAre you willing to acquire it for me?
This is terrible, my friend. Ostarand was on the verge of destroying the Vivicus and … nothing.
Excellent work, oh my comrade! Together, there is nothing we cannot do.
My wife's happiness means everything to me.
<<1>> and <<2>> are outside their home. Please get him to stay.
This one is excited to see you. You will be a great help to Aelif … and the guild, too!
Intruder! Halt! Halt! Intruder!
Good luck, adept. You carry the Guild's blessing with you on your journey.
My task at court is properly distributing the flesh of the fallen to the citizens of Crow's Wood.\n\nYou are not a citizen. No flesh for you.
Remember, you want to drink it in the open. Otherwise, the experience might overwhelm you.\n\nActually, it might still overwhelm you, but there you go.
Hey again! Did you get the lute? Don't worry about me. The slug of brandy in my gut will keep me going.
We've taken the first step. There's still work to do here, clearing out the last of the Reachmen. But for you I have another task.
Channel the magicka into the effigies. That should lower the shield that blocks the mine entrance.
I am the Lord of Death Crystals. Question not my power.
Crime has been detected; justice must be done.
Have you found all the crystal shards?
Did you really not kill Remelie? Even when I had asked you to?
Thank you for finding those shards. Now the Supernal Dreamers will have no way to open their Daedric gates. However, as long as thier leader is alive they won't stop.
Now everything is done.
I see the Dreamers have fled. Has Remelie been slain?
<cough> I die in pain, but I have saved the world
Quiet! Get down!
<<1>> must be stopped. Are you ready to put an end to his plans, my friend?
Damn the Mad God and his nonsense book!
<<1>> asked us to watch the southerly approach. The Dominion seemed determined to get to <<2>>, no matter the cost. The vicecanon took it upon herself to find out why.
It is not coincidence that the river's current has led you here.
The doorway into the ruins is now unlocked. Let's move!
The more you talk, the less I am entertained. Get on with it.
This is incredible! I'm surprised the Khajiit didn't ask me to translate this text. \n\nIt's not encrusted in gold or gems, so they may not have recognized its value.
I just got him back. Don't want to lose him again, dammit!
Ysmir's beard! You've done it.
My da and sis are still alive because of you. Kyne bless your steps, traveler.
My old grandad would be so proud to see someone protecting his stead. Thank you.
Valaste awaits you at the Guildhall in Davon's Watch, along the eastern coast of Stonefalls.
Please, you have to help me. He's going to take everything we own if I don't give him those relics!
Whatever you do, don't just stand there. I'm busy, and there's plenty of work to be done.\n\nWe're going to move these people soon. Come find me in town if you pitch in.
If Ja-Reet's happy, I'll make the best of it.
<<1>> is a stubborn fool. He won't come home until he sees this through.\n\nI don't know whether to be proud of him. Maybe he should just leave things alone.
I'm glad to know my egg-brother's well, but I suspect he won't leave the mine until he sees his mistakes erased. \n\nHis heart has always been bigger than his head.

It's been so long since we had guests. You would have loved my old uncle Leo, back in the day.\n\nCharming dinner conversation, when he wasn't bringing up old girlfriends. Literally. Regurgitating them. Nasty habit.
Reach dogs will think twice before crossing blades with me again.
Months ago, I taught my students this very ritual. Now I must use it upon them.
Curse that Deathclaw! Ate my foot.\n\nI had to use my boot and some leather as a tourniquet. Damn it!
Hozzin's Folly is west of the village. Send everyone you find back here. Good luck.
Something has to be done about these undead.
I bet Ulrich is giving these necromancers a sound thrashing.
So many dead because of me. I don't know if I'll be able to live with myself after this.
The wand! It's all because of the wand. Pick it up!

Just the person I wanted to see. I've puzzled out the hints from that last book … and I'm afraid the news isn't good. Your next trial is in a particularly nasty part of the Shivering Isles. A place called the Chateau of the Ravenous Rodent.
Three little ducklings all in a row. Red bill, green bill, yellow bill too!
While you handle Vantir, I'll see about freeing the others on my way.
Orc-loving Covenant cowards.
Adept, you cannot listen to this offer. This is the exact same offer Sheogorath made me when I first lost Eyevea!
She intimidates me as well, comrade. Do not worry. I'm sure Hakruba will treat us fairly.\n\nStendarr make me truthful.
With the information you and Abnur recovered from the ruin, we should be able to locate the proper pathways to the Halls of Torment. Sai Sahan need not suffer much longer.
Did you feel the Hist slip inside your mind? Such strangeness within my head … thoughts I didn't think myself.\n\nListen to me, going on like I'm freshly hatched. And they call me a hero of the Pact!
Close the master portal, or they'll get a foothold in the fort.
<<1>>, I can't believe you were the second one back.
Please, make them stop!
I'm no blademaster. What do they want of me?
We'll all be ground into the dirt we tend. Please!
I curse the word "Dagger." I'd show these dryskins, had I one of my own.
You must stop Aelif before it's too late!
Have lots of ideas for new flavors of mead. I just need to find more suppliers of spices and herbs.
Did you find Skorvild? Are you the one who rescued the villagers?
Well, look who's finally up and about!
We'll return to Windhelm as soon as Droi and … well, all of us have recovered.\n\nWhen we see you in the city, we'll buy you a drink!
Here's the entrance. This will take you right to the signal fires.
Comrade, I have an urgent message for you.
The guards found more caches of weapons hidden around the city, but nothing else. I hope you had better luck.
Nornalhorst is south of Vlastarus. Any items you can recover will be greatly appreciated.
The other racers are waiting. Light the signal flare and start the race!
What do you want? Why aren't you getting on with your task?
Back so soon? I guess maybe I was seeing things, but I could swear that <<1>> was still walking around, but I'm sure you have a real good reason for bothering me, don't you?
Why don't you ever want to just get to work on these things? Why do you always come back to bother me?
It's changing! The story is changing again!
I appreciate all you have done, both for my family and for the Ebonheart Pact.
The Worm Cult can dig in the mire all they want! Ouze is protected from their necromancy, thanks to you.
Cleverly hidden in plain sight. That totem is one of the most powerful relics in my possession. It will keep the Worm Cult from mastering the Oathbreakers.\n\nBut first, you must prepare.
It'll be fun to watch the Worm Cult deal with angry spirits, now that they can't control them!
Just a handful of dirt should do it.
Head through the portal and complete the ritual. I'll stay below and burn more of the roots.
I left <<1>> in the village. She said she'd be praying to Z'en in the meantime, the dear girl.\n\nPlease do what you can to help her. I'll wait in the valley, near the Drublog's home.
I will set Scales free as soon as she calms down. I don't want her to pose a threat to herself or my people.
This orb will be put to good use, I assure you. Kireth rarely sees the need for proper recognition, but once she has it she'll appreciate it.\n\nShe'll come around.
How could you do this to me?
We made it! Now all we have to do is find the key.\n\nRemember, I'll dig. You fight off the monsters.
Just smell that. Sizzling red meat. Real Nord food!
I'd love to travel to Alik'r and try their exotic spices.

Imiril guards the area closest to Rilis' prison, a large binding stone that serves as his cage.\n\nThe hate that Imiril has for Rilis and the … twisted fascination he has for her is a volatile combination. I'm concerned at what he might do.
If Jardirr lives, she'll be up for a commendation. If she dies, I'll box her ears in Sovngarde!
Greetings in his name. We're always pleased to have new faces join us.
Take one of my bloodfiends and kill the hunters before my son can gain their trust.\n\nAnd let this be a sample of the power I can give you.
It's good to have this time to prepare. If only I could say the same before every battle.
Beware the lurchers. Their hearts do not beat with blood. They beat with hate.
Why have you returned from the ritual grounds so soon? Has the Skald-King succumbed to the Daedric poison? If not, you should get back up there and stand vigil for your king.
The eyes are <<1>>'s favorite food. We keep some around for when he gets cranky.\n\nHe'll smell them from here, I'm sure of it.
Going, are you? You should come to our next show. I'm going to juggle swords for a change!
Let's not waste time. We must kill the bastard who took my wife.
I almost feel like myself again!
I shall attend the Prince's council. Perhaps I'll see you there.
It's important that we get to Skuldafn as soon as possible.
Search the tents around the ruins. Let's meet at the ruins' entry, straight back from the stone steps.
King Jorunn's breathing slows. I don't know if this is due to your actions or if he slips closer to death. \n\nDid you learn anything new?
I understand what needs to be done. Read the book. One of us must die to save the Silvenar. Frankly, that's a lower price than I expected.
According to Sariel, that book says the price of saving the Silvenar is one of our lives. Good! We should pay for our failure.

You have restored tranquility here, and I hesitate to ask more, but I have no choice.\n\nAnother of Ysgramor's companions—Valdur—he was entombed not far from here in Taarengrav. It is likely the Worm Cult seeks to enslave his spirit as well.
We're defending this town to the last warrior. If you're here to help, talk to Vigrod or Ree-Zish.
I am <<c:1>>, the spiritual advisor to the Bosmer people. I have been captured by Wood Orcs from <<2>>. I could use your help, if you are able to provide it.
You've done more for me than I could've expected from a stranger. Please, don't wait for us. We'll be fine until we reach the town.
If only we could learn from the past. If the chief read these journals, she'd see our path's end!
Hurry, my bellicose ally! Take thunder and pain to our enemies! Illuminate their path to Coldharbour with lightning!
<<1>> is my brother. He's one of the brewers.\n\nWhat's wrong, <<1>>?
It has been an honor to assist your efforts. You are proof that the legacy of the Five Hundred lives on.\n\nSomeday, I will see you in Sovngarde. Until then, may the gods be with you.
We must stop Wormfather. To battle!
You beat the guardian! He'll return soon enough, so we should be quick.\n\nI can't maintain this projection long, however, or I'll be noticed.
I know we can turn things around here.
The spinners' bonds are broken! The future unfolds before us.\n\nQuickly, the Silvenar awaits! Do not worry about me. My tale continues to unfold.
We must keep moving. The sooner we find Garil, the better.
The Silvenar and the Green Lady will join, as they always have. Our tale's never changed, though some played roles most unexpected.

Listen, let's say I believe you. Let's say there are Stormfist agents impersonating people in Fort Amol.\n\nEven if all of this is true, we can't start a panic. The leaders of the Pact are here, for Kyne's sake!

With the Pact working together again, we should be able to sniff out Fildgor's spies easily enough.\n\nNow my only concern is for the King. He's surrounded himself with our strongest warriors, but the element of surprise gives Fildgor an advantage.
Thallik is dead. Long live Sinmur, eh?
I appreciate your … understanding in this manner. Our very lives are at stake.
Greetings!
The cultists. They came out of nowhere. Aera. She was leading them! She demanded I join the cult. \n\nSurprised … surprised her.
Hello again, Vestige. I'm afraid I'm quite busy puzzling out the particulars of what we discovered in the ruin. Varen and I should have a lead soon.
Sorry, I'm busy. Don't have time to be bothered.
Search around for any clues that might help us unlock those doors.\n\nI'll look around down here and make sure that none of Dhalen's thugs get inside.
Is there some reason you're still here?
I tried to raise my granddaughter well, but she's always defying Thorulf.
Have you found anything?
Good to meet you! You fought beside the Centurion at Shor's, yeah? Amazing!
What luck! You helped avenge my beloved Silvenar in <<1>>.\n\nTell me, would you lend your striking arm to my cause once more?
Imiril will live, but I need you to give me space.
Well, I've lost almost my entire shipment. But Turil doesn't even have this! His misery is like sweet nectar to me.
This was all you could get, eh? Well, you did risk your life. And Enthis is miserable. Hah!
I can't hope to replace Tirora. But I'll do my best to honor her memory.
Give me a moment. I'll be right behind you.
Where could they be? Why haven't they returned?
Well? You going to just stand there?
Thank Kyne you're here! Wait, you are here to help, aren't you?
With Valdur on our side once again, who will stand against us? Any time you need it, my blade is yours.
Just let me die in peace. The damn Worms have done me in.
You've done us all a good turn, stranger.
Your actions won't be forgotten, so long as our roots touch earth.
You have done the whole of Valenwood a great service.
My lord, before you go. There is one other thing.
You think, with all that sleep, I'd be rested. And yet, I'm totally exhausted. Damned Daedric magic.
While you were gone, Thorulf made a proposal. I told him what he could do with himself. Disgusting man!\n\nWhat news?
He's called a gathering of the Council of Province Generals in Sentinel. You should find him at the Hall there.
Now is the time. The Worm Cult dies here!
Hey. Here to join the fight? Talk to Vigrod.
The door should be unlocked.\n\nGet to the sanctum and stop the ritual. I'll seal the door behind you to make sure nothing interferes from this side.
You'll find the Mistress of Incunabula in the deserts of Alik'r, at the Guildhall in Sentinel. Good luck, Adept.
Don't worry. The words won't attach to your flesh. Probably.\n\nNo matter, don't worry. Just head down the ramp and annoint the wall hangings with the blood. Everything will work out wonderfully!
<<1>> will be our greatest challenge. You might not survive it.
<<1>> is a blight upon the land. Our task will not be easy.
If ever you meet <<1>>, I suggest you run.
That Ra Gada captain must die! Don't give up!
Most unfortunate that one had to die. Still, it's better one of their number falls than one of ours.\n\nYou have the letter, yes?
The lieutenant died for Velyn Harbor. The sergeant taught us to fight for ourselves.\n\nMaybe it's time we stepped up and helped out more.
That tomb down there. I don't … don't waste time talking to me. Get down there and find out what they're up to.
Ah, at last. You must be here with my supplies. Just put the ink and delicate items in the tent here. You can begin unloading the bulk goods with my assistants.
May the Stars guide you, my friend.
I'm sure if <<1>>'s stories came true, I would also be a bit strange.
Let me know when you're ready. Vurila will start counting.
Do not waste my time.
You have the necessary ingredients to make Tildur's fireflask? Excellent. \n\nI've been watching the Maormer come and go from the lighthouse, and discovered how they get past the ward on the door.
My tools should all still be in the residential district. The Drublog wouldn't know what to do wtih them.
Lucius isn't with you. Tell me you didn't find him yet.
My friend returns. Are the rituals completed? Are the priestesses safe?
Good luck, traveler. The lattice may be the last hope for the fallen.
We must see to it that no more monsters invade our world from yours.
We came here to honor our ancestors, and now they seem bloody well determined to kill us!
<<1>> said you'd meet me here.
Only one stone remains. Quickly now!
What happened inside? Is Jorunn safe?
I need you to head to Riften as soon as possible. We can't let <<1>> run unchecked in the Smokefrost Peaks.
We'll be waiting in the barn down the road. Good luck in there.

All this standing around is driving me mad. I wouldn't presume to question the king's orders, but I'm ready to get this battle started.\n\nWell, if you're as anxious as I am to squash some Worms, I could use your help.
Fascinating. You see them, don't you?\n\nThis will make a marvelous addition to my studies.
Poor thing. When my brother was killed, her mind just snapped. Keeps babbling about the water.
I know the other musicians and our instruments are in this ravine, somewhere.\n\nPlease find them! I'll try to reach our camp. Find them and meet me there!
My Dadazi's safe. That's all that matters to me.
You fight the Houndsmen; I'll get back to the camp. I won't give up performing that easily!
My goodness, it's you! Bedraggled, but mostly intact, I see.
The Queen's safety is my primary concern. Everything else is just bookkeeping.
How great to be a part of this!
The Worm Cult is finished here. With <<1>> dead, their threat to the Rift is over.
I hope I never hear the words "Worm Cult" ever again.
I saw three satisfied mercenaries leave here. Things went well, then?
Thanks to you, the Worm Cult has been defeated and <<1>> has been returned to the grave.
I pray you found them. We need all the help we can get.
I pray you found Urcelmo. The Eight know we need all the help we can get.
Excellent work. With the wards down, we can focus on these portals.
Excellent! We couldn't have done it without you.
Your Queen has need of you.
Well done.
Well fought, and well earned!
Well fought! Well fought indeed!
Plant this among Bar-Neeus's wares. And speak only to Bronorr at the Fighters Guild when it's done.
Still around? I'd have thought you'd have moved on by now.
Salloweed's pretty potent stuff. Gathering it should be safe enough. As long as you don't eat it, you'll be fine. I think.
Ho there, friend! Welcome to my little shrine to Kyne.\n\nI can sense a force, a spirit, radiating from you. You're here to take the Trial, right?
One down, and you look confident about the second riddle. What's the answer?
Raz cannot say what you will find in the lands beyond. \n\nHe doubts what you find will be friendly.
The lich is dead and my troopers are freed. Time to move on.\n\nI'm going to take the shard to Jorunn at Trolhetta. I hope to see you there.
How can I … oh! It's you!
I practically worshiped that Nord! The very thought of being alone with him  … hearing his sonnets by moonlight ….\n\nTell him I know where he can go shelve his other book.
Listen, you can't tell the canonreeve. She'll kill me.\n\nI'm not—I'm not joking. She'll have me put to a blade.
Please. My sons. What's happened?
You owe me a song.
Do I look like I want to talk to you?
Hendil's not expecting visitors. So I'm going to guess you're here to talk to good old Taniril?
I heard … I heard the battle. Impressive.\n\nI assume you won?
<The statue looks very lifelike.>
I suppose it makes sense. At their core the Reachmen and the Worms both venerate the Daedra. \n\nJust never figured they'd do anything like this ….
What's <<1>> waiting for? I can smell the tide turning.\n\nWhoever said the Broken Coast bastards were competent sailors must have taken a knock to the head.
The treasure turned out to be garbage. What a waste of time.
Rilyn told me you found the bandits who did this. Thank you.
What a mess this is. Bandits, you think? Or maybe Covenant raiders?
Hold up there, traveler. I'd head back the way you came if I were you.
Careful. Not safe in this part of Auridon. You walk the road in Phaer at your own risk.
About time Harnald sent someone. I need help here!
The Smokefrost Peaks should be a lot safer, thanks to you.
Did Harnald send you to help? About time he sent someone.
Darling! Can you hear me? I'll save you!\n\nIt's working! I can feel it! The portal opens!
Living up to expectations, I hope? Eminwe and Norion are important members of the court. Wouldn't want them annoyed with you.
What do you want from us? Who do you serve?
Are you still here? I could swear I set you a task.
This place stinks of death and decay.
This way, this way.
Our waters run dry and I despair. We cannot hold back the giants much longer.
Get in there!
We're close, my friend. We will act soon. Trust Razum-dar.
Well? What did my protectors find?
The Canonreeve is inside, near the forge. She is trapped.
Welcome to <<1>>.
Such a worthless crew. I'll find more reliable rats in Velyn's worst bars!
Yes? Speak, and make it quick. This one is short on time.
She just stirs my ire. It can't be helped. One day, I meant to respond with "Yes, ma'am" but all that came out was "die to a pox, you filthy witch."\n\nYou can see my problem.

You must have a death wish. Very well, that's madness I can use. What to handle first ….\n\nI need to know how the Spider Cult is indoctrinating their victims. If you can free my captured Guildmates up ahead, they may be able to share some insight.
Please, just leave me be.
Will you do something else for us? You've already done so much!
Ahh. Razum-dar's new friend is awake. How do you feel, new friend?
Don't just stand there. Are you going to help?
That was certainly a grim situation.
I thought today would be my last. You have my thanks.\n\nWho … who are you?
I'll be fine. Keep moving. \n\nWe'll need as many warriors as we can get before this day is done.
Bring my father home, outsider. And the rest of the villagers, as well.
Tell me, brave adventurer! Is Greatclaw truly dead?
Thank you for helping Ankur earlier. He does tend to attract trouble.
Are you ready to face Lodorr?
I am so tired of tunnels.
To get to the matriarch, enrage her with the heads of her sisters.
This is now official First Auridon Marine business. Your help is no longer required.
Please, you must do something. Father will listen to you.
Nice, nice. Now we just need to find those notes.
Heartblood? No, I can't. I couldn't do that!
Ahem. That's right. As I was saying, your message arrived. They're awaiting you up at the manse.
Speak quickly, please. This could be very bad for both of us.
This one is surprised you have returned so soon. Have you made contact with the Heritance?
May the Green guard your steps.
Sorry, but we're not hiring any more instructors at the moment.
Go. Prove your worth.
Greetings, citizen! I seem to have suffered a temporary setback. I could use a bit of help.
What has that fool Orc gotten himself into now?
Off with you now. Eliminate the Wood Orcs. We will follow shortly to see what the Canonreeve is up to.
Always happy to see a friendly face.
It's about time someone came after us. What are you waiting for? Set me free!
They came out of nowhere. Swarmed us.
You're a welcome sight. My toes are close to frostbitten!
Good work. The crystal?
Don't you have somewhere else to be?
Soldier, we ….\n\nWait, you're no scout. Identify yourself.
Help me! They're after me!
You have chosen wisely. Are you ready for another question?
Ilara. She just wants this nightmare to end.
Don't waste my time.
Yeah, yeah, you won. Who cares.
You've fought well here, champion.
If you haven't talked to Dame Clarique or that bandit yet, you really ought to.\n\nI think there's something else going on here and it has me a bit concerned.
Don't you dare break the captain's heart. You don't understand what he's been through. No one does.
Here we are. This is where the current Green Lady saved her friend as a young girl.\n\nShall I start the blessing?
My new friend! You live. I was hoping. As you can see, we received reinforcements. The Dremora have been dispatched?
You're back, but I don't see Raynor. What's going on?
Look what my father's selfishness has cost us! How could he have been so foolish?

As I feared, we arrived in different locations. I am in a city near the sea, in a land of eternal spring. The air smells of the ocean and of markets and gardens.\n\nIt matters not. You have awakened once again and we must set you on your path.
You have chosen a side. Now understand that only one contestant can win this game.\n\nAnd, as always, I can change the rules without warning in order to keep the contest exciting.
My Nelhilda would thank you if she could. \n\nOh, this is all my fault! I was just trying to save my failing business. Now look at us. These people used to respect me. I used to help them.
I told the last person. I won't leave here without my father!
I suppose you want to know what the plan is, then?
I need to practice my dueling technique. I hope it comes back to me. I used to be quite good.
Keep him safe down there, please. The Rilis line is strewn with hard hearts and cruel men.
I know you helped all of the mages before you chose a side, but such generosity could return to harm you.\n\nBe careful out there.
The scent of death lingers about you.\n\nThis one supposes you found a way to harness the true power of the rune, yes?
<Raynor Vanos ignores you.>
We will find this city you speak of. With Juline at my side, the journey will be easier.

I knew you would choose me! But do not think that this puts me in your debt. I've decided to help you because Molag Bal deserted me. Now I only want to get off this miserable plane.\n\nWe may be allies now, but we aren't friends.

Ah, there you are. Estre sent me to find you.\n\nShe said the Observer was changing the rules. She sent me away just as our cruel gamemaster appeared. He seemed very angry, but I also got the impression that he was … excited. What did you do?
See? That wasn't so hard. There's always a way to get everything you want. Believe me, that's a philosophy I live by.\n\nNow that we're free, where do we go from here?
I'm not going back in there.
The scholars shall be at your side when we are needed most. Good luck, outsider.
Join in, relax. It's just mead. Laughter and good times are always on tap here at the Everfull Flagon.
Remember—Imperials bleed just as easily as any other men.
My head is full of cobwebs. I can't remember which guar had the ruby.\n\nPlease, search all of them. The Hist will guide you, I know it!
I know I'm going to regret listening to you. Just another day in the life of <<1>>, the madman's apprentice.
Thank you for helping my research. The amulet may need a few modifications. Otherwise, a successful test!
Oh, thank Mara. You're with the reinforcements, right?
I'll give <<1>> your message. See you inside the fort!
I heard someone was down there teaching the slavers a lesson. I'm guessing you're that someone. \n\nAny signs they're planning something else?
Glad to have your help. Everyone else is too busy, sick, or superstitious to help me stop the poison.
Their streets are thick with Jackdaws. They're celebrating, so they aren't too alert … but if they see you, they'll sober up fast.
She's going to let me go, just like that?
I've nothing else to say to you. You're no better than a common thief. Perhaps you'd like my skiff as well, just to sink it into the swamp?
It will take time to fully recover from both the attacks and the betrayals, but in time we shall be stronger than ever. And we have you to thank for giving us the opportunity to do so.
Did you get the bark? We don't have much time left.
I can't wait to shake the dust of this place off my shoulders.

I stashed the goods around the square, but pirates have a nose for hidden treasures. Look for my stashes, or pirates with sticky fingers.\n\nAnd I mean that … <<z:1>>, <<z:2>>, and <<z:3>> don't wash off. Bring them to my contact in the Mages Guild.
Ah, a friendly face … but now isn't the time for idle chatting. I've got a little business to take care of. Can I see you later, perhaps at the inn?
Have you brought me proof? What did <<1>> say?
You! I hadn't thought you'd make it out alive. <<1>> must have been formidable alone … with <<Ac:2>> in her hands, I can hardly imagine.\n\nYou do have it, don't you?
Just talk to one of the racers here. Grab a frog and you'll be good to go.
Been waiting for you. The boss sent me. Need to deal with this Heritance situation, now that we know Estre's turned.
The sound of a hammer on iron is a beautiful thing to hear, whether in battle or at the forge.\n\nBut our mine produces tin. Can't keep a good rhythm with tin.
Gargak holds the answers you seek. Please, listen to him.
My stomach hurts. I hope it isn't the curse.
The Heart … it's good you found it, but the cost ….
How could anyone willingly leave this room? So many books! And to think, more secrets locked just beyond our grasp.
<<1>> knew you could do it. Pact-soldier is talented and merciful!\n\nThe door's seal will fade. <<2>> will not expect this. No, not at all.
Glad to see you made it back. The troopers you freed ran in just a bit ago. They were pretty happy to be among friends.
There's a lot of blood on your hands, isn't there? A lot of blood.\n\nI like that.
I'll get topside and alert the Mages Guild as soon as I catch my breath. Xuth, something awful is coming ….
The Eye was within my grasp. Months of planning wiped out in seconds. How could this happen?
Excellent work. Bthzark breathes again!\n\nNow for a personal project. How would you like to earn a little more coin?
Now's the chance! Slip past the mutineers and put some holes in <<1>>!\n\nGo, save my wife from that backstabbing piece of squid jerky!
There's no one so superstitious as a soldier on the eve of battle.
Welcome, Adept. I've deciphered the spell inside the book. Are you prepared for Sheogorath's first test?
I'll journey through with you, but I'm not sure how long I'll be able to stay within the Isles. If Sheogorath is there, he may not be pleased to see me.
It is not wise to keep my lord waiting. His lucidity is as fleeting as my smile.
Messy business, this is; never seems to be a job where there aren't bodies stacked high, these days. You're back, so may I assume Nelanya is one of them?
Hmm, what? Oh, I … I'm not asleep! I told the captain I wouldn't sleep. I'm staying awake. That's right! Staying awake.
Mmm, those chickens smell delicious, dearie.
Elf not hurt Byz, but he threaten to.\n\nWhy people always threaten to hurt Byz?
Your business lies with Lord Sheogorath.
Nice work, very nice. Always good to see Shazah out from behind her books.
She wouldn't know an epic poem from a lunar chant, but Khali certainly is good with a blade. Well done.
Look at it go!
Be careful where you tread. Contrary to most children's tales the Dwemer were not kindly creatures.\n\nIt's likely there's mechanical traps and construct warriors lying in wait.
May the Eight bless you and watch over you.
It will take time to find buyers for everything, but I expect quite the haul, yes?
I see. There really is no other way, is there?
Look, Haskill! Forky's back! It's so nice to see him again!\n\nOh. And good to see you too, mortal. I guess.
The Hound. He has gone too far!\n\nIf what he said was true, the Silvenar—my Silvenar—is gone!
Baan Dar's grace upon you, traveler! I'll be waiting for you in the Bosmer camp when you get back up here.
Quick, head downstairs and slip the poison into a wine bottle. One of the green ones with the House Dres sigil. I noticed some loose bottles on top of the crates in the cellar.
<The lieutenant is dead.>
Jilan-dar is glad to see a not-green face!
I've known <<c:1>> for a long time, but she is not a Drublog, as my uncle constantly reminds me.
All this is my fault. My flesh and blood, dead. Because I wouldn't listen.\n\nBut, that's not your concern. Will you go after the Silvenar next?
Wonderful fight.
It's not often I meet someone as amazing as myself.
You've impressed me. That don't happen often.

It's good you're here. The general says the battle does not go as well as he hoped. I told him you could help.\n\nI've had little time to search for the Omen. Did you learn anything in Wayrest? Anything about nightmares in Gavaudon?
Carelessness can poison any victory.
Saintsport is south of here, across the bay. Mind the Sea Drakes. They'll tear your head off as soon as they look at you.
You got some lucky hits.
Thank you for not giving him the pouch of moon-sugar candy. That stuff got us into this mess in the first place.\n\nPlease, can I have it? I'm going to end this once and for all.
Your dueling performance was acceptable. Just barely.
You're on the quest!
You're on the quest!
Thanks for breaking me out back there.\n\nListen, while you're in a heroic mood, want to help me get something I left with the Goblins?
I cannot wait to leave this place. Too many eyes in the trees, in the grass, and even in the water.
You look like the strong sort. Care to help out an enterprising Dunmer, like myself?

Don't worry. We're not erecting a guillotine to start executing citizens willy-nilly.\n\nIt's just a deterrent. The Supernal Dreamers are trying to recruit people all over Stormhaven. This might remind them why joining would be a bad idea.
My poor cousin. Always going on about Goblins. Goblins did this, Goblins did that—I knew it would end badly.
Thank the Tribunal that's over. Please cut me free.
What did you decide about the relic?
I'm impressed. You smuggled Jakarn out from under Bhosek's nose. He's a charmer, isn't he?
No time to waste. Find that relic!
Go away.
What's that in your hand there?
<<1>> will probably be wanting to boss you around some more. Best go make her happy, I suppose.
Go … Hallowed. Get her out of here.
Thank Auri-El, a competent soul! Good to see you again. You'd think that I'd be used to working with him, but ….
<<1>> will pay for what he's done to my sister! I swear it!
We're grateful for your help. Our families know the risk of living with us. I've warned them about this situation before, but some soldiers don't understand the price of combat.
Ready for the fun part?
I think they soiled themselves when they saw me. It's hard to differentiate that smell from their natural musk.
You just wait. Captain Kaleen will have us back on the high seas in no time.
If you seek passage, know that this ship has no crew. Our captain is ashore, recruiting.
A hive of ants is no less busy … or determined … than our captain. I am honored to serve upon this ship.
Hello again, partner! Don't worry about what this little priest said. Hand over the goods.
Do not listen to him. He is a thief!
Uncle Ezzag will be grateful for the help, even if he does not show it.\n\nIf he is surly, please do not fault him. He is really a good man at heart.
How's it going with the chickens?
Bright moons guide your path. Keep your eyes open for Raz, too. No doubt he's found some valuable information, as well.
I hope you found the seeds. Without them, a lot of people will be hungry soon.
There it is! Beautiful isn't it? In its own way.
Bright moons light your path, my new friend! Clan Mother manages town business from her office at home. \n\nYou cannot miss it, the largest building in town.
Goblins. They're gonna kill us all!
Shuzura has heard you have been all over town, yes? Tazia has told this one of your exploits, your work. A great help to S'ren-ja you have been.
Raz feels he should say … ahem. He should say his farewells. Do not worry, my friend. This one will not hold his death against you.
Kalari is a sweet girl, and my brother loved her so … hmmph. Help her, if you can.
I'm looking forward to getting back to the open seas.
The items you returned are bringing back my memory. Drinking less is helping too.\n\nI'll see you at the docks when you're ready to leave Stros M'Kai.
<<1>>? What've you done to him? Brother, we're getting out of here! <<1>>!
Until the Pact controls Drakelowe Keep, it is not safe for you in Cropsford.
The relic, ours at last! For the Covenant!
Pilgrim, be careful down here. My brethren are not themselves. Perhaps you should return to our camp? It's much safer there.
We threw them back, that's all I know. You want to know more, talk to Lambur or Chief Tazgol.
Please hurry. I feel like I need a bath every time I spot that little beast.
Good job breaking up the Red Rook-Bloodthorn alliance. That should make things a little easier for those of us out here in the field.
We're so close. If you can finish Sternis Gelves, the Red Rooks will scatter to the hills.\n\nAnd then, maybe the souls of those lost in Eagle's Brook will rest easier.
You have returned my people to their rest. I wish to repay you, but I have only information to give.
We had to ascend the cliff behind you and still beat you here. Try to keep up.\n\nThough the scouts say you handled the second Stone quite well.
The prophecies of the Elder Scrolls are a fluid, living thing. They are not fixed. At many points throughout history, the actions of heroic mortals have rewritten them.
All of us feel much better knowing a brave traveler seeks the Claw.
The Bloody Hand is just a small tribe, fortunately. I fear that Goblins will someday band together and wipe out Cropsford. I hope that day is far in the future.
I don't like this at all, you understand?\n\nI'm doing this for the Daggers and their families. That's all.
Chief Tazgol must know of your discoveries before he marches on Carzog's Demise. We have ignored the Bloodthorn threat for too long. It may already be too late.
Find my brother and get him to return that egg before he winds up getting hurt. Or worse.
You're making good progress. We've pushed forward this far due to your help. It won't be long before we can retake the rest of the area.

I suspected something like this. It explains what we've seen. The Shade of Naemon does not seek destruction—it seeks transformation. We need to close these shadow rifts quickly. \n\nFirst though, I promised their souls release.
What is it? Speak up or move on.
Staring is a good way to lose your eyes.
You smell of ashes. Does that mean you burned Talmo's banner?
Hallowed … you have come, as Hunal saw reflected on the moons last night, yes?\nThe city of Dune shall be made whole in your passing, and our people will praise your name for years to come.
Don't interrupt me! It's your fault I have to do this, so I'd just as soon get it over with!
She's been hit with an arrow. You remove the arrow while I hold her down. She might swing at you.
I'm certain the cook bambedazzled me! But a bet's a bet.
How will I ever get it back? I cannot live without my lute!
Oh look, more gloom and death.
We have to find Sai Sahan. He knows where the Amulet of Kings is, and he doesn't deserve to suffer at the hands of that sniveling, knife-eared, puddle of troll piss.
The Orcs are being routed by a spirit army. The Bloodthorns have tapped into a power I've never seen before.
Speak of the poison to no one.
Never been in ruins this old before. Bet there's some good stuff just lying around, free for the taking.
That relic … such power. I can feel it from here.
I can't believe you gave Marius the poison.
Good to meet you. This one is honored to be working alongside the Champion. Our next Mane!
Several survivors made it here while you were gone. All said you rescued them.
So it's really come to this? Knights of the Flame killing each other? I agree with Sir Edmund, but I'm not willing to go that far.
Act quickly, decisively. The Claw is so close.
Good luck to you, traveler. This one can feel the Bright Moons whisper to her. She feels you will succeed.
