Some weren't happy with your decision to keep the relic, but I whole-heartedly support you.
She led us here … Khali led us to the threshold. Hallowed, I … I've never been afraid like this before. But I don't know if I can do it. I don't know if I can take the last step.
Dune is clear, the city is safe. The Lunar Champion is here. Are you ready to help her walk the Two Moons Path?
I hope this Path you have to walk will not be troubled by the darkness plaguing Dune.
Destruction. Devastation. Our Dominion does not deserve this treatment.
Kazargi is in there. Watch over her. She is very dear to me, young though she is.
Please don't bother me. This warding spell is quite complex, and if I don't finish it soon, there will be nothing to stop the impending invasion.
If you are able to, bring Asteril back here if you catch her. This one would very much like to ask her some questions himself.

From what you discovered, it's unquestionable at this point—the Veiled Heritance is planning something here, something even worse than killing the queen.\n\nI just hope it's not too late for us to stop them.
You and the keystone are now one. Its power resides within you.

I hope I haven't given you a sense of false hope though. Bosmer 'round here petition the Wilderking for an audience all the time, and he rarely responds.\n\nMore than likely, you're simply wasting your time.
This entrance is blocked. I sent soldiers inside to try to clear it.
Get back on your boat. You're not welcome here.

Whoa! Where in Oblivion did you come from? The boat? Did you just dodge past all those walking dead?\n\nIf you told me you killed a few of them, I wouldn't blame you. I might even thank you. Anything would help right now.
You made it. Excellent! Now that we're inside, there's something you should know about me.
Garnikh is a troll when he's injured.
Who knows how long <<1>>'s imposter fooled us all.
This isn't the best place for outlanders. Best move along.

I just hope the Ash'abah are prepared for this.\n\nRegardless, I will discreetly begin looking through the ranks for any soldiers who might be willing to do what's necessary. That way, at least we have someone.
I hope that's the magister's blood I see on your clothes.
Soon we'll be off again. I'll miss those who are leaving, but it's their choice.
The Shadowscales want the Fangs of Sithis. There are so many of them!\n\nBut they're dangerous. The Fangs in the hands of assassins? I can't imagine anything worse.
The portal will return you to the surface. Dar-m'Athra still lurk within the temple, but their presence will fade in time.

Like the branches of a Graht Oak, I believe that Aranias' destiny, my destiny, and your destiny are all intertwined. \n\nI cannot yet see how these events will play out, but I do know that like Aranias, you must come deeper into the forest.
Ahh, it's good to have a cool ale in my hand again. Such a bad day!
Easy, now. Don't kill the only ally you have in this camp. I just want to talk.
Foolish <<1>>. Will I ever see him again?
I've never seen a guardian fight like that! Incredible! You really know how to choose a champion!

You released him—I think that was the right thing to do. \n\nSince you already freed the villagers' spirits from the Shadow Wood, that means all the spirits here can now be at rest. We've done a good thing here.
And who in Oblivion are you? Some Daedric illusion?
You have more bothersome questions? Dulan has more races to announce. Go away, before this one loses his patience and tells <<1>> of your meddling.

Enter this Lightless Oubliette. Draw upon the Light of Meridia to protect you. It can disrupt the darkness that shall seek to slow you down.\n\nThen move the crystals to gain access to my prison. This strategy shall succeed. I am certain of it!
If you want to make any final preparations or rescue any others, I recommend you take care of those tasks before you enter the cathedral.
You fly like the wind and hurl like a giant! If you would consider a career in spikeball, this one would be pleased to be your manager.
Look, there he is! I'll follow your lead.
High steps! Come on!
The Elder Scroll of Mnem was entrusted to the Dominion's care. We have failed the gods if we do not bring it back. Help us recover it!
The treethane may be correct in her suspicion that there is a spy in our midst, but I can assure you with all that he or she is not from within the ranks of the Thalmor.
A Dremora wants to help us? It has to be another trick. Be careful of that one.
Ezreba prays for forgiveness. She hopes the light of Jone and Jode will absolve her.
Thank you. And thank you for saving my Ganny. I don't … I don't know what I'd do without her.
The outsider has returned.
This place sure got to Captain Arakh. I've never seen anyone so paranoid before.
Khaba is done with your questions. Move along now. Your pestering makes her back arch.
Targoth! With you here, I know the Bretons on the surface have been overrun. Good.
So, did you put Minwe down?
Targoth! The Breton King has sealed himself deeper in the ruin. He is preparing some foul spell!
It's amazing to think Ezreba was involved in all this. She's such a part of this community.
Never crack your ribs. Like someone stabs your lungs with needles.\n\nFrom inside your lungs.

Damn it! As much as I want to slaughter those Sea Viper bastards, they'll swarm over this ship the moment we leave for that island.\n\nWe'll keep this ship safe. Go, avenge <<1>>. Kill every last one of them.
Don't worry about me. I'll find my way soon enough. The gods wouldn't see me through a hurricane to end my life here.
Fate wasn't kind to us. I've never seen a hurricane pick up so fast.
Other towns have rats or squirrels or cats. We've got bears.
Give me a moment to prepare myself. Go on ahead, I'll be right behind you.
Give me a moment to collect myself. I'll be right behind you.
The Prowler's down two sailors because of those fish-Elves.\n\nWould've been three, if it weren't for <<1>>'s nimble feet. She can climb rigging like she's running to the top.
Gadris is upset because we had to hide behind some rocks. Undignified, he said. Well, Zur says that being eaten by a deformed creature is even more undignified.
I wished no ill upon the man, but if the Divines will my freedom in such a way, I will not question them.
Greenhill has survived. Thank you. I'm certain we'd all be in their icy grip if it hadn't been for you.
Best not to mention our methods. It will only bring questions and hard feelings, yes?

My people rejoice! Most consider us monsters, but you helped us. We will never forget your generosity and compassion. My egg sisters will live! And life, even in this wretched place, is precious. Thank you!
My friend, I trust you to see this done. Go well.
Speak to Cariel, my new friend. She'll be taking charge from here. I have to see to the wounded and begin the monumental task of returning Arenthia to rights.
Lorkhan take them all! Why does <<c:1>> negotiate with these filthy Maormer?
Be gentle when you speak with <<1>>. She has been through much, and fears for her friends.
What's done is done. I pray future dealings with the Dominion won't end in bloodshed.
The pain was unbearable. Like something tried to crack my skull open!
This apothecary must have had a hand in the murder. I'll get it out of him, one way or another.
Out of my way!
Perhaps I'll see you in the ring. Doubtful, but I suppose anything's possible.
Don't flinch, and don't let them see you sweat.
Zara wishes you luck. You are going to need it.
Congratulations, Mysterious Stranger. You are the Sorcerer Division Champion!

Apparently, he wants to talk to you now. Some insanity about the health of the forest and his directives. \n\nI respect the Green Pact as much as the next Bosmer, but what he's talking about is something else entirely. Don't listen to him.
Did you … did you succeed?
If anyone pays you to haul kwama eggs during a hurricane, spit in their eye.\n\nBy the gods, the mess! The yelling, the smell … and that was just the sailors.
Search <<1>>. There must be some sign of <<2>>.
Welcome back. You were gone for longer than I expected.\n\nI trust you walked beside Prince Haqmir of Yath and experienced the events that led to his exile?
Now it's time to bring down their champion. She should be in one of the larger caves.\n\nWe bring her head back and my people will have to see you.
It is done. <<1>> is finally dead.\n\nWe should leave this place before his puppets come calling.
It was a mistake to remove this one from his home in the shadow realm.\n\nThis one will tear a hole in you and drink its fill.
I don't believe it! This is Rkugamz! The abandoned city!
You are not welcome here, outsider. You may visit our camp, but do not tarry near the chief's tent.
Talia … Talia? Is that you? I-I'm … so dizzy ….
If I never see another Dwemer construct, I'll die happy.
My captured companions are locked in the cells beneath the Hall of Judgment. The door to the holding cells is across the way.
Get into the drinking tents and set some fires. Kill anyone that tries to stop you.\n\nCause enough commotion and Ren'dro's men will come running. Then make for the compound.
No entry without permission. Get out of here.
You do realize that more watchers will replace these creatures. Killing them is a futile gesture. \n\nStill, far be it for me to curtail your enjoyment.
Don't listen to this fool's words. The forbidden tomes must be destroyed. Place them in the shrine's flame, quickly!
If we don't close the portal from the other side, the Daedra will find a way to re-open it.
I must consider <<Ac:1>>'s possibilities. First, to determine if the water is indeed infinite.\n\nEr, do you mind? I must focus on my work.
Welcome to <<1>>, friend. The hurricane must have been very disorienting. So many injured, confused … keep your voice down. Try not to draw attention.
You have the books? Then luck truly favors my path!\n\nDo not listen to the lying spirit. This knowledge should be preserved by one who knows how. By this I mean, <<1>> knows.
The rats are gone. If his conscience allows it, our inspector lets us continue our way of life. All is well.

You know at first, this wild magic and the seals here seemed completely incomprehensible, but I think I understand how it works now.\n\nIn fact, I think I'll poke around here for a little bit before I leave.
Well, what are you waiting for? Open the rest of the cages, if you please.

It took a bit of work, but we finally stabilized the portals. Our people aren't getting scattered hither and yon every time they travel to Coldharbour any more.\n\nAt least, not as long as they're traveling to the Hollow City.
The city is coming along nicely, don't you think? I'm not sure if we would have made it this far if not for your help.\n\nThank you.
We've made it but I fear for my brother. I think the Daedric fire burned him more fiercely than it did me.
You are a competitor? Ishalga thought you came to the arena to pick up the rubbish!
I saw you scurrying around this plantation. I know you're running skooma.\n\nTell me who you work for, or you'll end up in a cell!
My father is dead, and now this Dominion outsider wants to throw me in prison!\n\nThey say they found evidence of skooma in the storehouses, but that's impossible!
We await our companions who have gone inside the ruin. \n\nIf you wish to know more, speak to the priestess.
Mara bless you, child. Tread with care. We're from the Chapel in Bravil, north over the border. A gang of bandits broke in and stole our holiest relics. It's not safe here.
This is <<1>>'s lodge. You can't enter without permission.
Try the weapons, walker!
Bright moons and sharp claws, thank you!
Nice work out there. Now that we've prepared all of the spell components, I can finish performing the ritual.\n\nThe threat these vampires pose will soon be over.
Everyone has gathered for the ceremony, and now with your arrival we are ready to begin.
Even if it was a simple spell, it's a simple spell well done.
Yes? What is it?
Know that you have made an enemy this day, mortal. I will stop you. The Elf's ritual shall not succeed!
Those men and women worked with my father. <<1>> used to cook for us. She'd even stew vegetables, when we asked nicely.
My blade has tasted the blood of my mother's killer. I should feel happy, righteous … but I don't feel anything.
I see you found additional help. Not that we need it, but a little extra protection can't hurt.
Aranias must not meet the Veiled Heritance alone, if we're to help her.\n\nGo to the lighthouse, and thereafter to the manor to watch her past. By then, she'll be waiting for you in the garden.
If anyone can get to the bottom of this, it's you and Aelif. She went for a walk to get some air. I think you'll find her near the docks. Stendarr guard your steps, my friend.
How much longer must we pretend? My daughter wails in disappointment and our two families verge on coming to blows!\n\nThere is nothing to be done for it! The groom is not coming!

This future only exists if the Lunar Champion is not successful on her path. She is the hope of the Dominion to come, and you are the hope for her. There is one last step along the path, if you are ready to conclude your journey.
Here is the Staff of Magnus. As you can see, we have kept it quite well protected.
Don't worry, we'll be fine. We'll pack up with the Mercs, and get out of here as soon as we can.
It is not an easy task I ask of you, I understand. Take your time, but know the fate of the Militia rides on your shoulders.
Don't worry about me, I'll get gone as soon as the coast is clear!
So is saving people from terrible situations a hobby of yours?
I decided that I liked my hair just the way it is.
I have spells to prepare. If you must speak, you should do so with Warlock Carindon.
The Mages here are doing important work. Warlock Carindon keeps us on a taxing schedule.
I'm busy.
I won't forgive those Bosmer for what they did to Patraud. An Altmer would never ….\n\nThis is unforgiveable.
Long way from the Mages Guild.\n\nWarlock Carindon speaks for us. You should see him if you have an issue.
Fancy meeting you here. Don't suppose my uncle sent you, did he?
Explore the forest. The mages and I will see to this prisoner.
Fair winds and blessings, wayfarer. \n\nWar may come between Crown and Forebearer eventually, but thanks to you it shall not start in Bergama.
What you've done doesn't change anything, wayfarer. These Crown dogs will always gnaw at their lead. One day the leash will snap, and we Forebears will be waiting.
By Tava's red feathers, how wrong we were. Bergama might have sunk into the sand sea of open war had you not taken things in hand.
Thank the Green I found you!
Tu'whacca's breath, how close we came to disaster! The Withered Hand shall be severed at the wrist for this blasphemy.
Find the relics of my people. I would add their stories to the tale.
Whatever Alasan is doing, you must stop him. \n\nI fear that if he succeeds in this endeavor, the future of all Alik'r is in jeopardy.
Congratulations, Hallowed. This one is not very spiritual … but even a fool knows we need a shield against the darkness. Especially when you cheat death.
Quickly, to the Prowler! Catch the Vicereeve!\n\nDismissed!

Finally, someone who's not running the other direction! \n\nI had no idea I was rubbing elbows with so many feckless cowards! A few necromancers show up and everyone jumps ship, literally! To just up and abandon this project—they should be ashamed!
My brave Zariya … I will see her exonerated, and then she will rest among our people, where she belongs.
You certainly took your time about things. Not your fault, I understand, not your fault! We may yet get this right!
Ah, the one who did not listen to Raz. He would say it is good to see you again, but this one is still sulking.
I'd stand by your side in there if I could, Hallowed. Good luck.
The Wood Elves of Valenwood stand behind you on this sacred journey, Hallowed.
This is fascinating. I can't wait to see what happens next.
This is not the decision I thought you would make.
We must get to the Eldest Den. There might still be time to save it.
Nnnnn! Please … hurry! I can't hold this spell forever!

It's good you're here. With earth magic and fire, Aranias and Andur force their way towards my throne, leaving chaos in their wake.\n\nI've lost control of my guardians. My power fades. I've always wondered what death would be like. Soon, I will know.

I was a fool to trust the Veiled Heritance. They just used me as bait to trick the Wilderking into letting his guard down.\n\nAs soon as Andur realized I was having doubts, he just cast me aside. It's clear to me now—I have to stop him.
Whatever you and <<1>> are up to, it can't be good for Gudarz. \n\nI wish you luck.
I hope there was something helpful in the tent. I'm starting to worry about how the other villagers will react to these continued delays.
I'm delighted those ruffians finally got their comeuppance. It was about time.
This really is the most delightful brew. Being a pact-hostage is turning out to be very pleasant, really!
Collect my lady's lost jewels and meet us at the secret cave entrance.
Enter the manor and find Stibbons! You've got to hurry before it's too late!
Gudarz is the man you want to talk to. He's got a sweet scheme cooked up for us, once we get rid of the old militia leaders.
I hear the old soldiers are about to give up hope and leave.\n\nCan't come too soon for me.
Our forces have gathered and are ready to move. We need to find the planar vortex and end the Planemeld once and for all.

This all seems familiar. I don't like it. I shouldn't know what a Daedric Prince's lair looks like! How can I recognize this place?\n\nBut don't worry. I'm not going to turn into an atronach or anything. I don't think.
Welcome to the temple at Rawl'kha, Moon Hallowed.
I can't imagine we have too much farther to go. We just need to cross this region and we'll find the planar vortex in no time.
You're still alive? Quick, get me out of here!
Morwha's bosom, I'm glad to be out of that place. I want to see the lights of Sentinel!\n\n<<1>> and I will make a great team. This is the kind of matchmaking for me.
An impressive dowry, don't you agree? Worthy of my precious daughter.\n\n<<1>> advised me to place it in a chest at the base of our entry tunnel. I've sent a guard to keep watch over it.
Damn these gates. Damn the corruption. I should be in there, not Indaenir.\n\nHe said you'll be able to pass through. Help him. Stop Naemon.
Finally. I thought perhaps you'd gotten lost. \n\nWe must be cautious down here.
A moment. This will take all my concentration.
Hold up. Imperial forces have seized control of Satakalaam. \n\nI'd stay away, unless of course, you want to volunteer and help King Fahara'jad's army take the city back from these bastards.
Did you talk to the villagers?
Good luck, friend. But with <<1>> by your side, you shouldn't have much trouble.
Have you found Pariel? Please, don't stop looking.

Be at ease. The mercenaries dare not enter my home uninvited.\n\nI watched you long before you spoke to my father, <<1>>. You spoke to people in town, and listened to their answers. Are you actually interested in helping?
There has to be a way into those tunnels.\n\nI've fought enough smugglers to know how they think. We should search the buildings near the cliffs.
This cave seems rather important to <<1>>. Perhaps there's another entrance near the cliff walls?
The Chasm is secured, we have control of the portals and the gatehouse. We couldn't have done this without you. Thanks!
The Chief is gravely ill. I fear Tu'whacca may claim him soon.
May the Green bring our paths together once more, friend.
I took only a sip before they stopped me. Empty your water skin and move on, O wayfarer. It is not safe here.
What do you want, ugly?

Scurry off, little mortal, but heed my words.\n\nControlling the Citadel, while useful, is not enough. Not for where you must ultimately go. But we shall talk more of this later, provided you survive.
The Reaver Citadel. It's all that stands between us and the portal to the planar vortex. \n\nIf King Dynar doesn't give the order to attack soon, I may just have to do this without him.
No one's allowed in Verrant Morass right now. The Vinedusk Rangers are investigating a strange blight.
Don't worry, I'm working up to writing those papers. I work best when I'm under pressure. You'll see!
Go ahead, try the lodestone on the <<m:1>>. I'm certain you'll be fine.\n\nNearly certain. Sixty percent certain! Conservatively.
If it weren't for you, I'd be well and truly buried right now. You're a real friend.
Please don't make this more difficult than it has to be. The only way for our spirits to reach Tamriel again is for you to die.
You humble me with your courage. Thanks to you, the other strongholds may learn what happened here.
We can speak later. Help us defend the barrier!
Khajiit is nervous. This one has never returned from the dead before.
What can I get for you? I have goods from the March and into Valenwood!
Sorry, but I can't chat. Tholbor's given me an arm's length of tasks to do, including his filthy laundry. Horrible man, honestly.
Sorry, I'm all out of sorts. Malarel has a thousand tasks for me, and her idea of motivation is a lightning bolt to the forehead. I understand I'm the third assistant she's had in a month!
The Eight watch over you. We lost a lot of good soldiers to the corruption. I pray Indaenir is right about you.
Be careful in there. No one can say what may lie within. I hope Indaenir is safe.
Hurry. We must inform the Queen.

While at first we thought only the Bosmer may be affected, we quickly realized the minds of others were in jeopardy as well. \n\nIndaenir said there is something special about you. We pray he is right.
Shazah worries for the people here. Mane Akkhuz-ri brought us to learn and assist, but sadly, there was nothing to be done.
Khali is but a student of the Mane, but this one longs to be inside and undo this corruption.
There's no end to the depravity of the Veiled Heritance.
It's a little bit like watching a fairy tale come true.
Auri-El watch over you. The queen, the mane, and Indaenir have all chosen to put their faith in you. I hope they are right.
This isn't the place for Khali and Shazah. So close to this corruption when they should be learning of their future roles.
You certainly fight like you've done this before.\n\nWe have one more front to clear, and then we'll be free to help the others at the central barrier.
Laeneval will not be forgotten. Let's make sure her death is not in vain.\n\nMy bow is yours, if you need it.
To all things, there is a beginning and an end. Remember this.
There must be another way into the caves. Perhaps there's a passage near the cliff walls?
Any luck? Or are they still at an impasse?

Tava damn me for a fool! I can't believe I let you find me like this again! Once was humiliating enough!\n\nThere's no time for recriminations, though. The Withered Hand has stolen back the Ansei Wards we recovered! They have all three again!
Speak to them. Make them see reason!

Imagine, a fortress full of Dremora! We'll have a jolly good time storming these walls!\n\nI wonder if we shouldn't have dismissed the Dremora lass so quickly, though. When they go out of their way to talk, I find it's usually a good idea to listen.
You have the look of a hunter about you. But the Senche demands that you act the part.
Remember, just play the flute and you'll hear an echo from Erinel's counterpart. Please save my betrothed!
Maybe next time Grunda will serve a proper tea when guests arrive. I mean, really! The social graces are simply beyond some people.
Who are you? What are you doing here? You need to get out before the others return from their raid!
So much blood. The cries. I can still hear them. Oh Divines, so much pain.
I will see to the Hunt-Wife and the torturer. You must see to the son and the Hearth-Wife.\n\nMake them scream.

That, my friend, is the question of the day! We wish we knew, but we're no experts on evil wards and such. Well, at least not those of us here.\n\nHowever, seeing as how whatever business you had here will need to wait, we could use your help.
Everyone in Marbruk is jumpy over the recent thefts. The Artisan is a crafty one.
If you need banking services, my master Talqua can assist you downstairs.
You come to me with an empty belly, yes? Let Duzal fix you something.
It's an honor to have had you fighting on our side. I know the king will want to recognize you as well … when the time is right.\n\nUntil then, I wish you great luck and clear roads.
We must remain vigilant. I don't know what's gone wrong, but it's clear that something has upset the boss, <<1>>.\n\nJust a guess, but I bet it's all these spiders.
It's really for the best.
This one welcomes you to her home. She is sorry, Kala is in no mood to chat. Her brother has been gone for many days now.
Not now.
Please don't interrupt us.
Excuse me, we're in a meeting.
Oh, hello there. Sorry, was the music bothering you?

Ah, not here to bet, then. Good. Good!\n\nThis one wishes to see you hurting, but more, to see those you fight dying. There is no victory without pain, walker. No spotless wins. Remember that and shed much blood.

Scouts bring rumors of a new power in the land. A Wilderqueen, a woman who can change the land beneath our feet. I also hear she served the Veiled Heritance—until you turned her.\n\nThank you. Even if she isn't with us, she's also not against us.
If you are looking for evidence, I'd suggest looking around in town. When the forest turned against us, there was no time for anyone to collect their belongings—or cover their tracks.
You are just as bad as them. You are only doing this because I'm an outsider, a Khajiit.
You did the right thing, advocate. <<1>> was a blight on our community, and you see how we've blossomed without his presence.

So, going toe-to-toe with the big bad then, are you? Smashing! Good luck to you! \n\nThis whole Planemeld thing seems like a nasty business. I prefer my Coldharbour with a bit less Tamriel in it, thank you very much!
Yes?
She led us here … Shazah led us to the threshold. Hallowed … I've never been afraid like this before. But I don't know if I can do it. I don't know if I can take the last step.
She says she wants to kill us, but she doesn't mean it. She says that out of love.
Man the ballistae! Stop that thing before it rams us again!
Look out for evidence of the mammoth's path, and good luck!
Be careful. The oldest bones in the Barrowbough can be a bit … well, moody isn't exactly the word. But yes, moody.

So the Spinner was innocent after all? I don't know how I could've been so mistaken, but honestly, I'm relieved.\n\nThe Spinner's role is a vital one. If he'd betrayed us, it would have injured us twice over.
I still think Gathiel must have had some part of this, but I guess the evidence speaks.
So, you've heard the masters speak. Snake, Tiger, Wolf—these are the spirits of the hunt. Each Briar embraces the qualities of one of these spirits.\n\nAre you still interested in joining the Briars?
Get out of my way. I'm going to kill Pellingare myself. All you have to do is look the other way.
Something's wrong. I've never known Pellingare to run from help. We need to follow him.
It won't matter, you know, if the courts spare me. I'll just find another way to end it.\n\nI admire your compassion. Perhaps one day your children will turn out better than mine.
Don't think I'm not watching you, just because my eyes are closed. I may be old and tired, but I am not unaware.

It feels good to be whole and strong again. You shall see my true power now that I've recovered from the soul-meld.\n\nI do miss Zur, though. He'd be beside himself at the thought of exploring a Daedric Prince's stronghold.
Ah, another visitor! You've arrived at an auspicious time for our village.\n\nI am Erunor of Shrouded Hollow.
Praise the Wilderking, you're alive! I knew he would save us!
I love what the Dark Prince has done with this place. Quite lovely. Shame we have to march an army through here. Soldiers rarely take care to watch where they step.
Oh, hello. I thought that maybe you were my wife. I got back from my job at the cemetery, but she wasn't here.
Lyris desires to speak with you.
It's been a long road, hasn't it? My father used to say that if you avoid all of life's abrasions, you'll never be polished enough to shine. We must be pretty damned shiny by now.
Lyris wishes to speak with you.
Titanborn wants you first. She's even more annoying when she gets impatient.
Blood and faith, Sameer! What has befallen here? \n\nQuickly! We must find father! Ask the vizier where he is.

Honor to you, Sera. Welcome to the Mages Guild Hall. I realize that our presence here in the temple is unconventional, but I'm afraid that our former hall was razed just recently. One does what one must, yes?\n\nHave you come seeking membership?
The Elder Scroll of Chim must return to the Pact. Help us recover it!
The ring, and my father's sword, lie at the back of the crypt. We must hurry.
Comrade! It is good to see you.
I'm sure I lost my Badge of Office at the tower. You must find it for me!
It is you! A pleasure. May the light of the Bright Moons bless and keep you. Why are you here?
Sorry, a little busy keeping an eye on our friends out there. Cariel will set you straight.
The guardians of the Elder Scroll of Alma Ruma must not allow the enemy to steal it ever again!
I appreciate what you did for the acolytes. They weren't prepared for any of this.\n\nI'm relieved <<1>> is safe, but don't tell him I said that.
There's Sai! But why is he being tormented by a shade of Abnur Tharn?

I must say, my doppelganger is remarkably handsome. Nevertheless, we should probably destroy it. Imagine the trouble it could cause if it were let loose in Tamriel! \n\nI know, I know … we're here to save the Redguard.
Sai Sahan lives! You've outdone yourself, Vestige.
I—it hurts ….
No. Not Gathiel. Oh, Gathiel, how could you have done this?
This isn't real. This is all a bad dream.
Who are you? Why have you invaded my home?

What can you tell us? It wasn't the Spinner, right? I mean, it couldn't have been. Could it?\n\nAlso, you'd tell me if the meat was all gone, or if the creatures had left their filth everywhere, right? Since we're friends and all.
Please, tell me you found something conclusive. Something that will sort this out so we can get back to our lives!\n\nThe village can never return to normal unless justice is served, you understand?

Remember Vestige, we fight for our people. We fight for Tamriel. Evil might be kept at bay for a time, but it can never be completely eradicated. What is important is that we resist it; that we fight on, and keep fighting.

We've had some crazy adventures, haven't we? But adventures are what you call them when everybody comes back alive, so maybe they've come to an end. \n\nI don't regret any of it, though. Not for a moment.
I see that look in your eye, Vestige, and I wonder—am I to be the one? Know that I would consider it a great honor. It would be a fine death.
We'll never be ready, so I suppose that means we're as ready as we'll ever be.
You are a Pact Advocate and I trust your judgment. I only ask that you weigh the evidence carefully. Whatever you decide, our village will never be the same.

You're investigating things? Good. Leave no stone unturned, and remember … the construction of Woodhearth in Greenshade, the founding of the Daggerfall Covenant, and the invention of the steel-toed shoe are all part of their plan.
So let's see whatever it is you found. As long as we get it over with, right?
<The shrine is quiet, empty of whatever power flowed through it.>
It doesn't matter what you do to me. You'll be dead, or trapped for a thousand years!

Mortals! Show a little concern and this is the thanks you get! And where is the constable? Why isn't he here? But that is a mystery for another time.\n\nThe survivors are our priority. Still, these vampires … they are most unusual.
My wounds are superficial. They will heal in time. But the debt I owe you will never be erased. I am honored to call you friend.
Z'en's price! I knew if I banged on this door long enough, someone would come.\n\nLook, I really need a helping hand here. Can you spring me out before the trolls come back?
Moira's Hope may be lost, but we'll survive. And we'll remember what you did for us today, my friend. You can count on that.
The sooner we get to the barn, the better. Then we can figure out how to take back the town!
Did I get hurt? I smell blood ….
Please, let's keep moving. I don't like being in the open like this.
I hope the soldiers were able to give you some indication as to the whereabouts of my sister.\n\nWe could certainly use her around here. She's always so calm under pressure. Please, find her for me.
I don't have the numbers to retake <<1>>. One platoon is all I'd need.
You have the scroll. Now, we can enter the cathedral and give the mayor a bigger shock than the man in the tower!
Oh, you can't seem to catch a break, can you? Chin up, just like the bridge! Adversity is the brother-in-law of propensity! As they say.
You did it, didn't you? I can sense it. Reezal-Jul is dead.\n\nToo bad. I wanted to be the one to end that crazy lizard's twisted existence.
We've no time to waste. Go to Sancre Tor with Sai and the others. Bring back the Amulet of Kings!
Steel yourself and enter the portal. We will follow.
The portal's open. Let's go!
The sigil geode! Do you still have it?
Shadowed Path cultists should burn in Oblivion. Have you fulfilled this contract?
You return to me alive and well. I trust the Shadowed Path has suffered at your hands.
I sent you out after those cultists, didn't I? How did things go?
You are back! I felt the shroud of the King of Worms descend over you, and I feared the worst.
Come on! Let's have at it!\n\nI'd rather die fighting than get turned into one of your pitiful creatures!
Tread carefully in Molag Bal's realm. You are important. The Scrolls have so named you.
My sister-in-law just lost her husband, my brother. We're both really shaken up, but I have to stay strong for her. I just wish she'd say something. She hasn't said a word since it happened.
I'm looking forward to this. I'm curious to see where Sai Sahan trained in his youth.
Lead on. Let's get the ring and be done with this place.
Excuse me, I hate to bother you, but are you from this area? Could you help me find my husband? He went off again, and I … I don't know what to do.
You could be the key to my escape.
I'm sorry, it's … I'll be useless, with all those frost trolls about. I hope you understand.\n\nYou be careful in those caves, would you?
You've returned! Smashing! Were you able to recover the Emerald Chalice?
Pray you are successful.
Are you waiting for the seasons to change again? Throw the hag's heart into the circle!
Guards at the other gates must've been slacking. I heard rumors that there are Imperial spies in the city. \n\nIf you see any, send them this way. We'll give them the Strastnoc treatment Ha!
Please, don't make me wait any longer. I must leave this horrible place.
The Ring of Stendarr's Mercy is at the back of the crypt. With it lies the greatsword that belonged to Sai Sahan's father.
Don't … ack … tell her. Make her pay.
Good luck in this final battle, my friend. You've proven formidable, but the Architect wields Daedric power.
So the rumor is true. We allowed an outsider to help us. Certainly not my judgment, but for the sake of my sisters … I wish you well.
Another portal leading us to an almost certain death? Oh, please. By all means, do lead the way!
Thank you. I'd send Abir back out, but he's wounded, and no use to us in his condition.
Foul Reachmen.
Gaercroft would risk all for the safety of his doomed daugther. Do walls make your kind blind to reason?
I keep thinking how that could have been me.

Smashing! I was actually about to hike all the way to Wayrest to ask for aid, but I think I've already found what we need right here!\n\nSo what do you say, want to save an old friend from having to walk halfway across Tamriel?
Fobbing Imperials! I figured we had at least another day or two before they'd be back!\n\nThe poultices helped, but there's not a knight here who's ready for battle.
If you are looking for custom jewelry, you should know I'm retired.

Greetings. Normally I would take pride in telling you that I am the most worldly Baandari merchant in all Tamriel.\n\nI would present you with a lavish display of the amazing variety of goods I have to offer, but I cannot do that today.
Thank you for playing along.\n\nYou see, <<1>>? This is what true friendship is! Not standing like a drooling statue as your only friend is hauled away like so many sacks of grain!
You made it out of Anahbi's Tomb? Unbelievable. I'm beginning to think I was worried about the wrong thief earlier. Clearly you are a person of surprising talents.
What news do you bring from the upper city? Have the traitors been dealt with?
The way to the upper city is through the gate next to this chapel.\n\nAfter you deal with the traitors and find something that explains Baron Montclair's actions, please come directly back to us.
If you have no business with the Hollow Moon, please move along.
Things have gotten so noisy around here lately. All that arguing … all that yelling.\n\nOrcs this, Bretons that! If you ask me, they just like the sounds of their own voices.
Ah, the noble hero! Merchants and peasants from here to the Strid sing songs of your overflowing pockets! Keep it up and tales of your generosity may surpass S'rendarr's, I have no doubt.
These missing moments from my memory … they concern me greatly.\n\nYou must talk to everyone. Discover the things that I have somehow forgotten.
We're coming right behind you. I promise. But you better clear the path. \n\nI needn't remind you that you don't want my death on your head. It would haunt you for the rest of your days.
You look like someone who appreciates a strong leader. I'm sure you agree, the High King has certainly made the right choice for the ruler of Shornhelm.
Puddles! Come to mama, you stupid, stupid creature!
If you won't help her, I'll find another way. I have to.\n\nI won't lose Leila, Verandis. I can't!
You made it, excellent!
You're going to cleanse the mausoleums? Arkay be with you, my friend.\n\nIf this does not succeed, I'm afraid we have little recourse.
Crazy Eye looks at you and sees one sleek piece of sweetmeat. She wishes Baandari were sticking around here a little longer.
Here to kill some bandits? No? All right.
We still haven't checked the crypt. There's no telling what these twisted bastards are doing down there.
Without the Fangs, the Anchor is vulnerable. Let us fling these vile creatures from our world!
To find Rasaba and the list, head due south from the manor. Follow the river and you should see them camped between Silverhoof Vale and Camp Tamrith.

It took you approximately fifteen more seconds to transfer to this location. The portal I created to come here took five seconds.\n\nEither my calculations are wrong, or the Planemeld is causing disruptions in the flow of magicka!
The Blacksap are leaderless and their attack was blunted, thanks to your quick work. <<1>> will heal in time.
Arkay's blessing on you, traveler.
You realize that since I made this decision based on your recommendation, that if ever there's a rebellion in Rivenspire … well, you'll at least have to help me clean it up.
Come to mock the rightful king of the Wood Elves? Go on then, have your fun.
I've explored a few Ayleid ruins in my time. Dangerous places. But you know me. I love dangerous places.
Good, good. You are safe. Good fortune did not abandon us entirely.
My father taught me this song. Pretty, isn't it? I guess I'm feeling a little homesick.
I'm cheering you on out here, Hallowed.
A pleasure to do business with you, my friend. A pleasure to be in business!
You should go. The more we're seen together, the less the Blacksap will believe you're one of theirs.
Ah, another visitor. You should probably speak to my lady. You can find her over by the cave entrance.\n\nAs usual, she could use a bit of assistance.
The people of Elsweyr are behind you, Hallowed. May the Bright Moons be with you.
What are you doing? Go activate the blood fountain!

Oh good, you have a letter for me. Never tire of the things.\n\nYou're certainly missing the meek spinelessness of a Dominion courier. You know the letter's contents, don't you? Why not tell me, and spare my eyes the strain?
I heard what you told the king. <<1>>, a traitor? Disgraceful. Makes the rest of us look bad.\n\nBut the Dominion owes you its thanks. As <<2>>'s representative in <<3>>, the duty falls to me.
What happened? Has Hircine asked something of you?
You've returned. We feared the worst.
Curse these Reachmen. They've been a thorn in our side for too long. I should have seen them coming.
So you've succeeded. Impressive. Few best the aspects.
Arkay's beard! Could anything be more disgusting than this gargoyle's tongue? \n\nOne must make the best of it, I suppose. Now, how to prepare the antidote?
It's good to see you, friend. You will always have a place aboard the Prowler.

Terrible news. The city of Northpoint has fallen—either to Montclair's forces or some other darkness he and his minions have conjured up.\n\nNorthpoint is Baron Dorell's stronghold, so I know he is there, but I am certain he could use your help.
I know you're working for those Vinedusk cowards. I knew the moment you arrived in <<1>>.\n\nBut you wished to speak with me. Why?
I don't see him, but he may be around here somewhere. You should go check the east gate for <<1>> and I'll meet you there shortly..

It is a relief to know that the city is safe. If time allows, I will go out into the streets and try to help the people rebuild. \n\nIt is the least I can do. And to be honest, I can make more of a difference out there than in here.
I do hope you found that blasted cup. Lady Laurent has been quite impossible while you were gone.
I can't believe it. What Nedras did for me. He was always looking out for me ….
I'm sorry, I'm waiting for someone. Would you leave me to my thoughts, please?
This one welcomes you to her home. She is sorry, Kala is in no mood to chat. Her brother has been gone for many days now.
So Montclair is at the Doomcrag? Perfect. I always wanted to assault a haunted pinnacle high in the mountains.
I heard someone say hearth-husband. Not me. No, please, no.
You have the stink of something unnatural on you. Something wrong. It'll take something extra to initiate you into our brotherhood.

I was wondering when you'd wander up! I knew you wouldn't let me get all the glory.\n\nOf course, I wouldn't have wanted to take any action until you were with us regardless, but I like to pretend. Anyhow, how in Oblivion are you?

You have done what has not been done in centuries! All the parts of the Orrery have been placed within the chamber, and <<1>> awaits us below!\n\nI must admit to being more than a little excited. I've never seen the Orrery operational.
Leave me be. This is much more complicated than it looks.
Adeena …. By the Eight, what have I done? I never meant for this to happen.
Onsi's blade. It released me? It let me go.
Did you kill that thing?
Touch the symbol of Molag Bal. Profane the Defiler, the King of Corruption.

Look! Another live one! Oh, sorry. I should speak more quietly. Don't want to disturb the dead … or the Daedra crawling all over this place.\n\nI find them very distasteful. Not right for this place. Not right at all.

I knew if I came out here and hung about long enough, someone would eventually happen by to help!\n\nIf I can be the one to determine what happened in King Ranser's final moments, scholars will speak my name with reverence for generations!
This place is perfect! No bodies. No backdoor. Plenty of room. It's a veritable mansion!\n\nWe'll gather here and use it as a shelter for any people we rescue along the way.

My thanks for your selfless aid, friend. And not only that, it seems you have sown a seed of faith in my brash son. Together, we will continue nurturing the lifegiving waters of the vale until the darkness there is but another story of old.
We're almost there! The locals spreading the word. We just need our last performer ready to go and we'll be a carnival again.
My trusty courier! Did you have an exciting trip?
First, you enter uninvited, then you start rifling through my cabinets? What is this? Some kind of sick joke?\n\nWait, I've never seen that book. What is it?
Ever are you a servant of <<1>>'s whims. Have you no pride?
Do what you will.
I feel so much better having you here. I'll stay here in case she comes back. You be careful out there!
You! I knew I recognized you from before. You retrieved that relic for me, from the site in the Alik'r. Splendid.\n\nI don't suppose you'd be willing to help me on another grand adventure?
Kaleen must have a plan, but it may not be a good one. Either she's playing Naruk, or he's playing her.\n\nGuess we'll find out, won't we?
Since you know Kaleen, you should do the asking around. I'll see to it no one stabs you.
Thrug and Larzgug are just as implicit in this as Osgrikh. It's fitting that they die to satisfy my husband's honor.\n\nI think they'll appreciate it. Just like a blood price back in the stronghold.
Help me walk out of here, and then we'll deal with Naruk.
It's easier to show you than to try to explain. Let's keep moving.
<<1>> says you're to thank for ensuring the ratification ceremony will happen without delay.
How exciting! <<1>> has done nothing but spin for generations. To think, I'll be the king who sees it work again.
<A notice for a bounty mission has been posted to the board.>
<A notice for a bounty mission has been posted to the board.>
<A notice for a bounty mission has been posted to the board.>
You know, you'd think being made of iron would be unpleasant, but it's actually rather relaxing.\n\nOr maybe that's just because I have no emotions.
Leave me be. I have more pressing concerns right now.
Seeking to reclaim <<1>> at this point is futile.
I don't suppose you're here to pay your respects to the Blacklight Raiders, are you?
It's such a fine day for fishing. I'll be out here a little longer, and then I'll return home.
Such a fine day for fishing. I'll be out here a while longer, and then I'll return home. I promise.
Go ahead, try out the weapons. That's what they're here for.
Ah, Count Verandis. So good to see your striking visage again.
By the Divines, the ale servers in this place get uglier by the day.
Greetings, milksop. You must be lost. This is where Undaunted drink, not milksops. Now go away, milksop. This one does not want to catch your milksoppiness.
Will you have another go, then? Just one alliance left, you know!
You have business with the prince? Make it quick. I'll not have his time squandered on trivialties.
It pains me to stay here as Riften is threatened, but I am sworn to protect my thane no matter the cost.
This? It's merely a flesh wound! Think nothing of it.\n\nI'm worried about <<1>>, though.
I wonder if Armel's trussed up like I was? Really, it's a good thing you came along when you did.
I've got to figure out what I'm going to do next. Gelvin and his sister are going to kill me for screwing this up.
There will be a feast later to celebrate the work of these fine men! We must show our appreciation for their hard work on our behalf.

Once you find those trap wizards, get them back here on the double.\n\nWe've got to let the elder know how we're doing. She's been waiting on our progress report. And between you and me, I think she's getting a little impatient.
Who knows when we'll get another job now?

I know you. Daggerfall. That mad plan to take on Molag Bal. Crazy.\n\nLet me ask you, though. If someone committed a heinous crime—slaughtering innocent people and such—could they ever be forgiven, or should they suffer for the rest of their lives?
Now that my skull's stopped pounding, I'm ready to crack someone else's. Did you find anything in that Redguard's room?\n\nDo we know where they're holding the hostages?
As I suggested, wonderful as Fell's Run is, you should probably keep moving and spend the night in Northpoint. They have a very cozy inn there. \n\nYes, and come back and visit us another time.
By Mauloch, if you don't get out of my face, I'll grind you into the dirt.

You're back? Thank the gods! The walls of this crypt are closing in on me now. Ever since I realized I might die in here. Funny how the mind does that.\n\nDid you find my pack though? Did you find the letter?

You've certainly done your due diligence. I really appreciate the efforts, but I had a feeling it wouldn't work.\n\nSome people just have no sense of duty, and I guess Martin falls into that category.
Look how the rubble blocks the front of the door. I don't think we can get through this way.

Ah, finally, reinforcements! Have you heard? Montclair has sealed the gates and taken control of Northpoint. He's locked me out of my own city!\n\nIf you're here to help, I won't be offended in the least.
We can discuss whatever you like. Politics. The weather. Anything at all. But after we finish this mission.

What a clever device! When you pressed the tiles in the correct order, the barriers disappeared.\n\nThere appear to be two exits from this chamber. I imagine they both lead to the same place. Go ahead. I want to look around a bit before I join you.
I never should have brought everyone here. I should have handled this on my own.\n\nYou're in danger as well. Montclair will eventually try to use you against me.
My friend, you are truly a hero worthy of song. I can't begin to express the depth of my thanks. You've done so much for me already … might I ask your advice?
Ah, our savior! Thank you again, for everything you've done.
It's good to be back. I never imagined such a horrible place existed.
Daedra everywhere! Took … took my wife! My daughter!
Thank you for saving us. To think I … I nearly killed us all.

Damn trash! That's all it is! Let it be known that Jerine's Ironworks sells nothing but dung. They call them swords, but you can't get an edge on one of these blades to save your life.\n\nEven the Shornhelm Guards got better steel than this!
Adept, thank you so much for coming. I have a request, one I hope you will honor.
Don't mind Verandis. He can get this way sometimes. Especially when the stakes are so high. But I'm sure he has his reasons.
I knew you would find the chamber and open the portal.

It appears that the Serpent has gathered the bulk of his forces in the mountainous region to the north and sealed himself within.\n\nSo much the better. That gives us a chance to learn what we can about this threat and plan a defense.
I can use the Lorkrata text to help translate the Ayleid words carved upon the pedestals. Why don't you examine the statue by the barrier? It has an important air about it.
Too much is hidden. The burnt bones tell much, but even they are sometimes quiet. Perhaps I'm not skilled enough yet.
I hope you can help us. Please, speak to Hara.
Whoa, there, friend. What business do you have here?
Stupid lighthouse. Stupid bandits. Stupid Hagraven!\n\nWhy's everything spinning?
I'm going to stay here and help in whatever way I can.\n\nThank you again for your timely assistance.

Good to see you again, friend! Believe it or not, your presence actually makes us feel better. And I know that I feel safer with you around.\n\nI hate to ask, but I have another task that could use your help.
What happened to the House Councilor is unforgivable. I hope you made those responsible pay for what they've done.
I hear the missing villagers have been found. Thank the Three at least some of them survived.
You know, I don't think Varon Davel is who he claims to be. But at least he took charge after the councilor disappeared.
Green keep you. I think my friend Tendil may have need of your services. Speak with him, if you would.
We should never have trusted the Maulborn. It seems like the curative isn't really a curative at all. It might even be the source of the Llodos plague!
The Maulborn are behind this somehow, I know it. Please, find more evidence that ties the Maulborn to this plague.
Just watch your step in there. I don't trust these Maulborn or their good intentions.

Perhaps you can be more reasonable than this Bosmer. \n\nThese grounds are forbidden. Allowing them to settle here would threaten the health of the Valenwood. If they do not leave, we will purge them with the forest like a destructive rot.
Welcome, fellow member! It truly is an age of discovery we're in. Look at the marvels we're unlocking on a daily basis.
Please do as Nilyne asks. I don't think he has a lot of time left.\n\nI'd go with you, but I need to stay here. Just in case.
Hush, child! We're busy!
Where did you go to get those ingredients? Windhelm?\n\nNo matter. You're here now. Were you able to acquire everything on my list?
Nilyne's got more talent than she gives herself credit for. Maybe when this is all over she'll finally realize that.\n\nAnd then maybe she'll forgive herself for what happened to that guar.
Remember, comrade: keep your blade clean. A sharp, rust-free blade will save your life. Even if everyone else has abandoned you.

Memories of youth are the treasures of old age. Savor them … and those who share them. They'll fade, but they're as sweet as Sun's Dusk Ale while they last.\n\nTongues of Xarxes! I sound like a pedantic old fool, don't I? Forgive me.
We have nothing else to discuss at this time, Seeker. Go about your business.
I will meet you at the camp of the Ternion Monks, my friend.
You're alive! But you don't look so good.\n\nWhat's your fighting style? Ramming your enemies with your face? Get back out there!
You did it! With the beams activated, we should be able to enter the temple now.
Adept. You've done so much … I thought you were the Guild's future. But I cannot ignore the choice you made concerning Valaste's fate. I would give you a gift. A gift, and a warning.
We're going to get these people patched up before we worry about anything else.\n\nAt least we can rest for the time being knowing things are taken care of.
I haven't seen you before. Who are you? How did you get in here? \n\nI warn you, if you intend to harm these people, you will have to answer to me.

When the staff hit, pieces broke off into elemental shards.\n\nTake these focusing crystals. Each one can absorb one type of elemental infusion from a shard. Bring one infusion of each type to me and I'll combine them to open a portal into the staff.

The students and I thought we could defeat Nerien'eth when he returned. We were wrong.\n\nBut even a lich as powerful as he's become can be beaten if we destroy his body. We just need to find him. Let's check his study up ahead. I'll meet you there.
Hara seems very pleased with you. She's become more hopeful since you arrived. I can tell. Is there anything I can help you with?
Once both ritual sites on either side are disabled, we'll be able to make it across. Or so Gilraen tells me.\n\nSplit up if you have to.
We have to locate the other aspects before the Serpent does, or the Scaled One will be impossible to overcome.

There. The other aspects, our other selves, have come into view. We must reach them before the Serpent locates them.\n\nOnly once we're whole will we have the strength to face the Lost One and break the Serpent's will.

I'll lead you to the prisoners if you'll assist me in my day's butchering. Information has a price, little mortal.\n\nHead inside, slay the Overfiend, and anything else that bars our way to the inner halls. Then we'll talk.
You're alive! But you look like you clobbered a rock with your face.\n\nThe Undaunted eat rocks for breakfast. Get back up there and collect your teeth!
My friend. I am Ahmat of the Black Horse Couriers. My assistant Talaya and I have prepared a riding challenge—a winding course across dangerous terrain—and a prize for the fastest rider.
We won't forget our lost companions or what you did to help us.\n\nIf you ever find yourself in deep mud, know that Scattered-Leaves owes you a debt, my friend.

Turuk was going to dare you to do it. You think like an Undaunted! Or you're crazy. Either fits.\n\nThat spirit—the Gazers called it a "Celestial Serpent"—will wreak havoc if it ever escapes these caverns. You cannot allow that to happen!
Quiet.Now's not the time.
Braadoth's throne room is way at the back of this complex. The faster we get there, the faster we can finish this business, right?

I sense a lightness in the air … as if some of the darkness has been dispelled. I can't be sure though, is it because the priests lit another torch, or was it you?\n\nDid you destroy Molag Bal's evil shrines?
You must fight with the Empyrean Light behind you! The Serpent flung our warriors aside like toys!
Once we destroy the progenitor and free the prisoners, the Scaled Court won't be able to create more of the mantikoras.
Follow the river to the right. It flows directly past the entrance to the Sanctum.
Quickly. Meet me at Loth'na Caverns. We must stop Regent Cassipia before it's too late.
You're back! All finished knocking some sense into those loony spider worshipers?
You return … paler than you left. Is that soot or fear on your countenance?
You return, but I see none of the scouts with you. Does this mean they are all dead?
I've seen everything I need to see. You're a fine woodworker with a steady hand.
What can this humble master of the craft provide?

<You notice a prominent handbill on the requisition board.>\n\n"Queen Ayrenn bids you welcome! Masters of the craft await you in <<1>>! New crafters shall be trained! Accomplished crafters will be certified! All at no cost to you!"

Did my idiot husband bring you here? I gave everything so he'd be safe. How many people was he going to feed into that gate? It's fortunate you can hold your own.\n\nPerhaps I can use your strength to my advantage. Go on ahead—it's the only way out
I can see you are not Undaunted. Don't waste your limited time on Nirn standing where you're not wanted.
Welcome to the Undaunted enclave!
Stay back, fiend! One step closer and I'll weave a spell that will … it will … Just stay back, all right?
Stay back! I'll—oh, you're not one of them. By Tava's red feathers, these Daedra are everywhere, and I'm in no condition to fight.
Oh Kireth, what have you gotten yourself into this time?

Oh, hi. Did you fall through that hole in the ceiling, too?\n\nNot that I'm complaining, mind you. Look at this ancient apparatus. I've seen cleaner things in an Orc's bath house, but it's really interesting, don't you think?
I imagined Wrothgar would be like the desert at night, but I could not have imagined a cold such as this.
I'm headed to Bolgol Farm to warm up. It's not far. Just over the hill. After you test the whistle, you can find me there. Good luck!

Well, now that we're done with this curse business, I have a very important social engagement to prepare for.\n\nBut whose turn is it tonight? Is it Nednor? Maybe Telarnel? Ah, well. I'm sure one of them will be happy to see me!
I told them not to go in, but did they listen to me? No. Now they're dead.\n\nDon't go in. You'll end up dead, just like them.

You, there. If you're exploring the ruin, perhaps you could assist me.\n\nI find these unfortunate creatures quite fascinating, and would pay for evidence as to what brought them to their current state.
Go tell the forge-wife that the quarry is once again safe to work in. I'm sure that will make her happy.
Welcome to Orsinium.
Forge-Mother Alga would like to talk to you, my friend. Remember that your actions have not gone unnoticed.

I can see why my mother was so insistent about you. You're pretty good in a fight.\n\nI was going to do this by myself, but I'm damn glad I waited for you. I'd be a fool to challenge Ice-Heart without you.
Who are you and what were you doing in our quarry? And most importantly, where's that damned Elf and what did he do?
That echatere almost ran me over! You got the distance, but I'd work on your control.\n\nStill, that's loads better than I expected of an outsider.
You alone emerge from the Bloody Knoll. Did you pray to Malacath for your victory?
Kharza tells me you restored the quarry. For that, you have my thanks.

Thanks for helping my brother. He's always been curious about his past and hoped to meet some Khajiit one day. \n\nNow that this is over, maybe we'll go to Orsinium and see if we can make that happen.
Ever met a Riekr? I hate those sneaky little bastards ….
Are you the one she's waiting for? I suppose I shouldn't be surprised.\n\nYou both look like vagrants.
I have a few words to say to <<1>>'s mother. I'll meet you where <<2>>'s tracks begin.\n\nDon't know why we call him that … he carries a club.
<<1>> is fast asleep. Give him a good kick to wake him.
The portal ahead will take you to the Tower's top, to Clivia and the Dark Anchor. You must face her before she completes her work!
We need to put some floor mats down, with you soldiers tracking in filth from the sewers all the time. I'll talk to General Nedras about it.\n\nYou have something to tell me?
Any particular reason you're bothering me?
Mere weeks ago, this was the most beautiful district in the city. \n\nNow, it is nothing more than a carnival of terror and destruction. And soon, there will be nothing left for them to destroy.

I feel like a helpless little girl … completely lost and can't find my way home. \n\nThey're all dead. My mother, my father, my little brother, my two big sisters, my great aunt, my baby niece, my six cousins, our dog, and even the neighbor.

Hm. Interesting. You are peculiar, aren't you? Something faintly Daedric about you, yet you appear to be a creature of the Mundus, like myself. \n\nPerhaps even somewhat intelligent? Tell me, are you familiar with the Xivkyn?
Well, you look no worse for the wear. Are you feeling all right? Maybe I can use you.
Keep walking, friend. I'm down to three hide sites, and I'm not about to give up another.
Have you planted all the coins?

<You notice a prominent handbill on the requisition board.>\n\n"The crafters of Leyawiin bids you welcome! Masters of the craft await you in <<1>>! New crafters shall be trained! Accomplished crafters will be certified! All at no cost to you!"
That was certainly a grim situation.

The Rat's ears are keen. They have heard the bleating of the grateful little lambs. \n\nIn fact, the Rat thinks there was a little too much bleating. Perhaps you have saved too many. There may be an overpopulation issue now.

Victory for the Pact, yes? Ha! You stupid red-shirts with your flags, and salutes, and marching …. Ah, do not look so offended! Ezudash thinks that everyone is stupid!\n\nThis one has sent word to your general. I'm sure she will be pleased.

Well done, wayfarer. Perhaps I have judged the Covenant too harshly. \n\nNow that the district is under Covenant control, is it safe to assume your forces will try to prevent the Daedra from reclaiming it?
Want to make some fast gold? Talk to Ralen Veri. He'll get you in on the real action.
Let me tell you of a wonderful opportunity. Better yet, let me send you to Ralen Veri. He can lead you to piles of money. Piles!
You enjoy the finer things in life, I can tell. Go see Ralen Veri about a certain opportunity. He'll take a liking to you, I'm certain.
You seem like a good sort. Certainly not an Enforcer, or anything. Ralen Veri will want to talk to you about … business. You should find him.
Want to hear a secret? This one belongs to a rather lucrative organization. Lots of benefits, if you catch my meaning. Talk to Ralen Veri, yes?

Stop right there, outlaw. Don't get me wrong, I understand the criminal impulse as well as the next guy. It's just if you come any closer, I'm going to have to pound you.\n\nUnless … you're interested in joining the Enforcers?
Stay back. This building is off-limits at this time.
We don't want any trouble, stranger. We're a peaceful village, far from the turmoil of Orsinium and its newfangled ways.
I must admit, I usually wind up solving these things through a lot of trial and error.

Most excellent to be seeing you again, my bestest friend! It is I, Rigurt the Brash! But you can call me "Ambassador" now.\n\nThe Ebonheart Pact sent me to extend a branch of peace to glorious, brave, and beautiful Orcish peoples!
It seems that the famous adventurer found something worthwhile in the barrow. He even waived his fee for helping us.
Our association is at an end, my untrustworthy apprentice.\n\nYou broke the first rule of good storytelling—you told the truth.
I don't know what's gotten into Kharsthun. Why would anyone want to climb all the way up to the shrine to see an ancient relic when there's a perfectly quaint museum down in Orsinium?
Ogres! Even the dead ones make my knees shake with uncontrollable fright!\n\nDo m'lady a favor and get rid of the foul creatures before one of them decides that chilled Stibbons is an ogre delicacy.
I'm glad you recovered the Armlet of Torug. But before you decide what to do with the relic, you need to hear what I have to say.
Ah, another ancient barrow, another two-and-a-half gold pieces from my employer, Narsis Dren!\n\nBut you don't want to listen to my problems. Have a nice day.

It was a real pleasure working with you—especially since you weren't afraid of a legend and a few dozen skeletons!\n\nIf you ever want a partner, I'm sure I could think of something to do with Bardun. Next time you're in Orsinium, look me up!
Why don't you talk to Lord Ethian. I make the little skeever nervous. More nervous, actually. He's always kind of twitchy.

What a tale I'll have to tell when I return to Northpoint. If I return to Northpoint. I might remain in Orsinium for a time. Help Lady Sovelle in her work there. It might be nice to have some solid ground under my feet for a while.
Sovelle, she's not here. And I think maybe that mage tried to kill me! Well, maybe he was trying to kill you.
We need to make peace with our ancestors. I'm sure I'll convince them.
Gusting winds. Flying birds trying to eat us. Fire everywhere. But that up there? That's a stationary target that needs an arrow in it.\n\nJust tell me when you want me to make the strike.

I love this place! The barkeep stocks all my favorite drinks and serves the most delicious snacks. She even renamed the place in honor of her favorite customer—me!\n\nAnd it's the only place I can go to get away from my wives and mother for awhile.
Thank you for your assistance in this matter, outsider.\n\nMy son or I will contact you when we again require your services.
I hope you can find the others. I also hope I stop seeing double soon.
I think that's another one of my mother's notes. You look at it, all right?
Children. Never have them!

If you have a letter from the Forge-Mother, then you've come to the right place. Just be aware, this isn't official Daggerfall business. Wrothgar is open to anyone who genuinely wants to help us build the city of Orsinium.\n\nOr so I've been told.
I think the bleeding may have stopped, but everything is still spinning.
You freed Egnatius, yes? I'd hate to think I was coursed down like a hare for nothing.
That was an experience I don't want to have again. Thanks for lending a hand, stranger.

If you discover anything useful, meet me behind the great hall.\n\nAnd try not to raise any alarms. The longer we can keep the Vosh Rakh from discovering our presence, the less likely they are to start slaughtering any prisoners.
The best way to hamper these fanatics is to eliminate the one who leads this den of deluded recruiters. We should kill Azhnura the Proselytizer.
If you really want to throw water on their fire, we should eliminate the one who leads this den of deluded cultists. We should kill Azhnura the Proselytizer.
We followed after you as fast as we could! What happened to the sphere? And what's with all these fires? Was anyone hurt?\n\nOh, Mother Morrowind, what have we done?
I knew this would happen! It's all gone so wrong.
When you catch up to the Dwarven sphere, just use the lightning prod to siphon off some of its excess energy. That should calm it down.
Did you find the burial urns?
I hope that Proselytizer person is dead. She said that I would come to Trinimac by fire or by ice. She also said I was as thick as a tree trunk, which isn't very nice.
I'm shaking, but that was kind of exciting!
Dark times ahead for Shatul. I can't contend for chief—it will take me away from the echatere.
Talk some sense into <<1>>. I can forgive her lashing out in grief, but <<2>> was my husband as well.\n\nIf she accuses me of his murder … to my face? I'll have to answer that.
Chief Ogzor was strong and fair. He was a good chief … a good husband. How could he have died this way?\n\nIt seems so … small. Unworthy of the man he was.
The Order of Diagna shall fight beside my Knights of the Dragon. Truly, a good day. Wouldn't you agree … Tamahl, was it? Am I saying that correctly?
This is so much better than a cell. <<1>> thought her fur would never recover! Thank you for pitying this one's predicament.
Interesting taste, but nobody will eat a dish that smells like old greaves.
I don't think you should be here. I don't want any more trouble. I heard the king was dead and I'm sure you had something to do with it, so leave us out of it.
If you're ever in Orsinium, come find Shalda and me. We really want to buy you a drink for what you did for us. It's the least we can do.
I'll help Talviah and Eveli acquire a disguise, but I'm not good at pretending to be something I'm not. I hope that doesn't cause a problem or anything.
You are neither a glass of wine nor a warm bath.\n\nGood day.
You know, I thought those giants would give you a harder time. But I tend to overestimate the tall. \n\nTutor, make a note: need more giants.
Go on ahead. I'm going to read these scrolls and choose a blessing before we start this trial.
There you are! I was beginning to get worried about you. We've found out some …. \n\nWhere's Talviah?

It's so nice to have a little help around here. Thanks for finding that historic treasure and setting it on its display.\n\nBut this is only the beginning! The wilds of Wrothgar are brimming with all sorts of important antiquities.
Have you ever heard of these Vosh Rakh maniacs before? I certainly haven't.
Get moving! The throne room is upstairs, remember?\n\nOnce Eveli and I get out of here, we'll try to rally some additional help. You can find us outside if you run into any problems.
About time you showed up!\n\nHey, where's Owayine? No, don't tell me. I already know.
Be careful with that one, stranger. Youss is the proverbial serpent in lamb's clothing.
The hagravens read enough entrails to know <<A:1>> is within the catacombs. Once you find it, we can be rid of it.\n\nIt's for the good of the tribe, even if they won't see it that way.
Welcome back, friend! I can't wait to hear what news you bring!
Scholars uncovered the catacombs at what they call "Honor's Rest." Once inside, seek the <<1>>. Return it swiftly when you find it.
Care to spy on the Worm Cult once more? My auricular geodes were quite a success, and my superiors requested your expertise.

Quite a view, eh? I used to come here to watch the games with my brother. Never thought that we'd become the entertainment.\n\nSorry. The name's Valga, and I'm fighting to save as many of these people as I can. How about you?

Our weak points are blocked doors on the north, west, and south sides. Zel's scouting for attacks, so if he thinks the Daedra are going to hit a door, he'll mark it with a sigil.\n\nLook for that sigil and wait. Zel will update you whenever he can.

You probably want to talk to the ambassador. I'm just an aide, no one important.\n\nNot like Ambassador Rigurt! If it were up to me, his name would be "the Handsome" instead of "the Brash." His muscles are definitely all in the right places!
Keep your distance! I'm sorry. I don't know how much longer I'll have control.
I haven't seen the demiprince so pleased in quite some time! \n\nYou've really given him hope that he might be able to reconstitute his missing barons.
Greetings, my friend. Forgive me, I do not mean to ambush you. Ha! As if someone as old and frail as I could ever hope to take you by surprise.\n\nCould you spare a moment for a priestess in need?
The high priestess used to study here. Read her books. Write her sermons.\n\nNow she's gone, and it feels like I've got a hole the size of Elden Root right in the middle of my chest.
Go on. Go attend the funeral. I'll stay here and keep watch over our brave, little friend.

I'm going to miss this place. The temple has become a more somber place since the death of the high priestess. Solgra was a good woman. She cared about our people and hoped to spread Trinimac's word.\n\nI know she also considered you to be her friend.

I assume this funeral thing isn't really a trap, is it? I'd hate to show up in my finest outfit just to have someone try to kill me again.\n\nToo soon? I know, I know. I shouldn't make jokes at a time like this, but it helps keep my mood light.
I really don't want to talk to you any more right now.\n\nI'll consider the chief's invitation. You'll either see me at the funeral, or you won't.
By all the snot in Malacath's right nostril, I never thought I'd be returning to attend a royal funeral.\n\nMaybe if I had been here, I could have talked some sense into Kurog's rock-hard head.
I hope Bizra hasn't been giving you a hard time. She can't help it. She has the personality of an ornery echatere—and that's her on good days!
I can't believe Kurog's actually dead. He was just at the tavern yesterday, eating and drinking. Carrying on like he didn't have a care in the world.\n\nI miss the big horker already.

The loss of a third of our partnership hits like a heavy blow and the devastation darkens my soul.\n\nI do not know if I can continue with this enterprise. But it was Jaeloreh's dream, and I'll do my best to bring honor to her memory.

I am sorry for <<1>>'s loss. I cannot replace her in <<2>>'s eyes, but thanks to you our business and livelihood can continue.\n\nWe'll mourn, and then we'll make our way to Orsinium. I hope you visit our shop one day.
These brutes are destroying everything! Millennia of scrupulous record keeping—up in smoke! If I were a younger mer, well I'd … and I'd …. Ugh!

They're industrious, I'll give 'em that. Take a look at all those siege engines. Even took the time to chisel 'ole Boney-Bal's face onto them! Pity we've got to burn 'em down.\n\nYou are going to help me burn them down, right?
Huh. This city gets busier by the day. Name's Brihana. You here to hunt? I can give you some pointers if you like.
I've been watching them turn over graves … the Worm Cult, I mean. It's an ugly business, isn't it? I used to come here to clear my head. It was quiet—peaceful. Now it's full of these idiots. Shame.

You look lost. You're supposed to be in the Elven Gardens looking for my contact, Regilus, remember? You are far from the Elven Gardens.\n\nThere's work to do here, but it can wait. Let's sort out this business with Regilus first, all right?
Find the hunt-wife and her daughter. And kill as many of those … things … as you can.\n\nBut the Elf? Save the Elf for me.

Master Dren told me to wait here. So I'm going to wait. Right here. \n\nUnless I see a spider. Because then I will run away. Maybe down to that village. Mazgroth looks like she could kill a giant spider without too much trouble.
These cultists must be taught that Wrothgar is off limits. Once you've crushed their operation, check in with Lilyameh. Her order will reward you for the effort.
Great work with those werewolf pelts. They're selling like ice in the Alik'r!\n\nDo me a favor and don't stray too far. I'll need more of those skins before long, and you're someone I can trust.

Hurry, please. I trained Shabon well, but this isn't a mammoth hunt. Those machines don't behave like natural beasts, not in the least.\n\nMeanwhile, I'll make my way back to the surface. I think I can avoid those things if I'm careful.

I was going to wait for the High Elf, but now that you're here I think I'll try to find my way out of this damn ruin.\n\nI may not be able to fight hostile constructs, but I know how to move stealthy when I have to.

Be careful around those durzogs. One of my mates thought he could train one as a watchdog. Got ornery one day and snapped his hand off like an apple on the branch. \n\nIt's a shame too. He was a damn fine lute player. My friend, I mean. Not the durzog.
I'd heard there were some exotic egg delicacies available here in the Morkul Clanhold, but I have been very disappointed so far.

Thanks for helping us out after I went and hurt my ankle. I have a real aversion to walking skeletons. Must be a cultural thing.\n\nAnyway, if you ever need a partner, I'm not opposed to dropping Meram in a ditch and hooking up with you.
I sometimes pray to Malacath for strength—but Malacath cannot give it. He only issues the challenge. The challenge to claim strength for ourselves.
I've had a rough day, outlander. Let me drink in peace, all right?
Please, no autographs. I'm quite busy writing another valuable treatise.\n\nHmm, well, I suppose my autograph would be important, too. Still, I am otherwise occupied.

The bread is delicious, no question. But real sustenance can only be found in the forest. When I consume the forest's bounty, I take in the wild.\n\nYou don't want to be here when the wild comes out, though. Trust me.
The future of Wrothgar is uncertain. I see dark clouds on the horizon. Do you hear the thunder?
Doesn't matter how great your city is if no one can get there. These roads are treacherous, friend. Be wary.
You're the one who aided the caravan? Thank you! The additional workers that just arrived have already helped get us back on schedule.

I'm glad to see that life still courses through your body. I'd be extremely out of sorts if you turned up dead.\n\nAnd I heard what happened. You have my thanks for keeping Chief Bazrag safe. I'd be even more upset if my husband had died.
This one has a strong feeling you have been many places, many places indeed. Is there much wealth in your travels?
Hmph. A fool braying orders to lackeys.

The Black Hand has studied the situation and we have devised a strategy for dealing with the Order of the Hour. \n\nWe will strike first, attacking from the shadows and winnowing their numbers while you stalk our true enemy—Primate Artorius.

Just like old times! After this, first drink's on me!\n\nNow go and spread Boethiah's word to the cult's initiates. Once they detain you, we'll show my sister exactly how Surus treats those who disagree with him. Just don't disappear along the way.
You reconsider my offer? The Thieves Guild needs people with your kind of talent.\n\nAlso, the desire to live in a cistern. It's not much to look at, but <<c:1>> serves us well.
Huh, what do you want?
There you are! Remember <<1>>'s friend, <<2>>? He is quite grateful you recovered his ledger.\n\nSeems he kept his ears open for word of that merchant lord, "<<3>>."

I'll go by and check on Anais in a few days. Make sure the pirates lived up to their part of the arrangement. If she learned her lesson, that's great. If not, well, I'm sure I'll think of something else that will do the trick!

So you're the new recruit, huh? No, don't tell me your name. I'll just call you New-blade. It's easier to remember and it's not like I'm going to know you for very long.\n\nYes, New-blade. That's so much better.
