I don't know precisely where Qamar hides his gold, but I do know the lazy oaf uses a few trusted lackeys to deliver deposits when he can't be bothered. They often dice on the docks.\n\nIf you're convincing, I'm sure they'll reveal the location to you.
Let's approach the shrine and see what there is to see.
I hope you find her. Foolish girl, running off now of all times. \n\nJust bring her back.

Ah, finally a turn of good fortune! I imagine you'll have no problem convincing these ignorant clods to hire us forthwith.\n\nHonestly, I'm overqualified for most of the work available here, but I'll do whatever is necessary to get us to Sentinel.
I usually see the tomb as half full, but even I was about to give up hope before you showed up.\n\nIf you can help us raise the gold we need to leave this wretched city, we'd really appreciate it!
Welcome to the finest tavern on the Gold Coast! We know how to show a visitor a good time, you can bet your boat on that!
My brother's forge may have seen better days, but he's still the best blacksmith on the Gold Coast. If you need something, you should talk to him.
I know it won't be easy to recover <<1>>, but I'm ready for this. Just say the word.
I'll enjoy holding this over <<1>>'s head for the rest of her life.

That didn't go as smoothly as I'd hoped. I suppose that's the point of being a thief, isn't it? I'm just glad we're alive and free.\n\nUnless the Iron Wheel finds us. We should be going, shouldn't we? Let's get going.

<<1>> is around here somewhere, and <<2>> must still be scouting. I'll keep watch.\n\nOh, and the sailors are no trouble … it seems the Iron Wheel is slow to pay its debts, so they're happy to look the other way.
Unless you enjoy spending time in prison cells, we should really get moving.
We need to keep moving. We'll talk back at <<c:1>>.
Did you get the invitation? Whose did you acquire? No, don't tell me, I want to see it with my own eyes.
So who are you going to bring with you to the palace? I hope you say <<1>> … I'd love to see her bedecked in finery.
Yes?\n\nWhy are you looking at me like that?
No fine wine for me? No matter. I'll open the cask <<1>> stole from the docks.

Meet me by <<1>>'s mansion when you're ready.\n\nI'm not religious, but I said a prayer to Auri-El this morning. If we find nothing, I have no idea what to do next. This is the only trail leading anywhere near my father.
<<1>> wore the name "<<2>>" like one of <<3>>'s outfits? I don't know what this means, but it can't be good.
Don't look at me. I have no idea what to tell her.
Why would <<1>> do this?
I can't even say, "<<1>> should have seen this coming." I didn't see this coming.\n\nRetirement did me no favors.
Quickly, inside! We have no time to waste!
I'll meet you when you're ready. It's near <<1>>, so we should travel separately. Best not to draw the Iron Wheel's attention.

Please, I never meant to harm anyone! The mercenaries who protect my home … they overheard <<1>> and I speak of treasure.\n\nI promised them a share, and the rest I planned to give to <<1>>. You must believe me!
Why are you still here? Leave, before I call the Guard.
Be careful with those ashes. I'd rather not walk Malooc's Path a third time.
A face I did not expect to see. Not here, at any rate. This place is far from Longhaven, but just as dangerous.
This one truly appreciates all the help you provided. May your claws stay sharp and your fur never tangle, my friend!
You'll find <<1>> in <<c:2>>. She's … a bit withdrawn.\n\nNot my business, but I figured you should know.
Last I heard, the Desert Falcon was in Shadowfen—some tavern in Stormhold.\n\nSee what you can learn. If any trails lead to <<1>>, follow them.
You know where to find <<1>>. Always staring at papers in <<c:2>>, she is.
These are troubling times. When we forget the past, it has a disturbing tendency to rear up behind us and bite us in the arse.
Took your time, didn't you?\n\nBut you're here.
Your face … this one doesn't recognize it. Are you looking for a piece of pie?
I'll wait here while you sneak into the room upstairs. Just open the secret passage and I'll take care of the rest.
You're ruining the carpet! Lady Anais will make me scrub it all over again when she sees those boot prints!
Camels are cantankerous, smell quite poorly, and are too phlegmy for polite company.\n\nJust like my old professor of rhetoric.
See how the Iron Wheel litters their camp with traps?\n\nOr perhaps you don't. Try not to die out there.

I would avoid engaging the Iron Wheel at all costs. Perhaps find some other way to slip into the tomb.\n\nBut you are not I, and the world is better for it. For instance, I could never make those pants work.
Not every job goes according to plan, but that does not mean we need to run off with our tails between our legs. You got the goods, <<1>> will sniff out another buyer soon enough!
So that's what upset Narahni. I didn't know she had a son, but there's so much we still have to catch up on.\n\nI hope you can help set her mind at ease. I hate to see her in such a state.

Oh, you are a pot of treacle tea on a dreary day, my friend! Thank you for coming.\n\nFaradan, back at the inn, sent this one news that has filled my heart with sorrow. Perhaps you can help this old woman again, if you have the time.
You got the writ? Well, then, set me free!
That skeever Menant send you? Tell him I don't have the gold yet. I'm working on it.
Thanks for your patience with all of that. I hope I sounded convincing!

When Walks-Softly decided to save me from the pirates, he gave me a lot to think about. I'm not ready to shut down the family business just yet, but I see the value of a little compassion every now and then.
An old sailor is mourning the loss of his favorite wooden pipe during a scuffle with some pirates. If you track it down, he's offering a surprisingly good sum for its return.
I'm not in the mood, Assassin. Besides, I think the Matron wants to see you.
Don't worry about me. I just need to sleep right now.
Let's get back to Anvil. I'm done with this place.

Sorry I gave you the run-around, but I was just trying to protect my passenger. Those Silver Dawn ruffians came around asking about her right before you did. I didn't say a word to them, either.\n\nJust let me know when you're ready to go to Skyrim.

I won't run off again. I promise. My place is with my family. No matter what happens.\n\nStill, I hate that the Chanter tricked me. I'm going to follow Kor's suggestion and stick a fork in the old fool. Or in this case, a very sharp knife.
Arkay watch over you, child.
There are so many antiques in this market, each rich with history. Yet the buyers and sellers seem oblivious to the true value of these precious items.
<<1>> stole my bed. Actually, I can't remember when I last slept in it. I suppose it's hers by right.\n\nBut stealing the guildmaster's bed doesn't make her the guildmaster.

Twice, you've been within spitting distance of <<1>>. Perhaps you can answer a burning question.\n\nDoes he wax his scalp? He seems like the type to wax his scalp. No, don't answer, I'll find out for myself.

I never wanted to see the Iron Wheel again, and there you go, traipsing right through their headquarters.\n\nDid you pour honey on the chief inspector's bed pillows? We used to do that at the academy. To people we didn't like, of course.
Those Iron Wheel bastards! I've got half a mind to go out and poison one of their drinking wells!\n\nBut no, the "guildmaster" would frown upon such an action.
Someday I'll be a merchant lord, I promise you that! But I'll be a good merchant lord. Not like those clawless gold hoarders that won't give me the time of day.
I envy you, Sister.\n\nFew get to prove their devotion to the Night Mother and the Dread Father in so dramatic a fashion.

Sorry. As much as I like to chat with my adoring public, I have to keep working or I'll never finish these cakes on time. Everyone has an occasion that's special, you know.\n\nNow if you happen to have a cake voucher, well, then we could talk.
Acting guildmaster. You are moving up. Don't think you get free privileges with the guild funds though.
The Black Hand has decreed that we move against the Black Dragon, Assassin. Finally.\n\nAstara will tell you more when you return to the Sanctuary.

Go and see what the Pirate Queen has to say, Initiate. At the very least, it should be amusing to let her think she can order us around the way she does her Red Sails lackeys.\n\nI look forward to hearing all about it after the deed is done.
First Tanek, now small Hildegard. I suppose if you were in league with the Black Dragon you would not have saved them. \n\nInteresting. Let me jot that down.
The messengers are definitely up to something. Hiding notes throughout the city. Raz supposes a hedge maze is a perfect place for such things. Probably hidden beneath some sort of marker, yes?
Raz does not like it, but we don't have a choice. We need to let the killer walk out of here.
Don't let her talk her way out of this. Only one of us is leaving this building alive, and it isn't Louna.

Don't blame yourself for what happened to Mirabelle. Her grief drove her into a blind rage. It made her reckless. We can't let ourselves fall into the same trap, no matter how we feel. Stay focused and keep moving forward.
Word has come back from the Black Hand. It's time to do to Lyra Viria what she did to her Brothers and Sisters. It's time for the Black Dragon to die.
Mirabelle … But she was so strong. So … Mirabelle.\n\nI hope she finds Cimbar in the Void.
Hmm? Nothing for you right now. Come back tomorrow.
Hold it! Who are you?

It appears that the Serpent has gathered the bulk of his forces in the mountainous region to the north and sealed himself within.\n\nSo much the better. That gives us a chance to learn what we can about this threat and plan a defense.
I hope you can help us. Please, speak to Hara.
If you haven't spoken to Hara yet, please do. She's gathering allies in our fight against the Celestial Serpent.
I am the answer to all questions and the question behind every answer.\n\nNo need to introduce yourself. Your name is already recorded in my realm of Apocrypha.
You did it! With the beams activated, we should be able to enter the temple now.
We're going to get these people patched up before we worry about anything else.\n\nAt least we can rest for the time being knowing things are taken care of.
I haven't seen you before. Who are you? How did you get in here? \n\nI warn you, if you intend to harm these people, you will have to answer to me.

When the staff hit, pieces broke off into elemental shards.\n\nTake these focusing crystals. Each one can absorb one type of elemental infusion from a shard. Bring one infusion of each type to me and I'll combine them to open a portal into the staff.
Hara seems very pleased with you. She's become more hopeful since you arrived. I can tell. Is there anything I can help you with?
We have to locate the other aspects before the Serpent does, or the Scaled One will be impossible to overcome.

There. The other aspects, our other selves, have come into view. We must reach them before the Serpent locates them.\n\nOnly once we're whole will we have the strength to face the Lost One and break the Serpent's will.
We won't forget our lost companions or what you did to help us.\n\nIf you ever find yourself in deep mud, know that Scattered-Leaves owes you a debt, my friend.
Braadoth's throne room is way at the back of this complex. The faster we get there, the faster we can finish this business, right?
Once we destroy the progenitor and free the prisoners, the Scaled Court won't be able to create more of the mantikoras.

The Thief waits for us in the Sanctum of Farsight. That's where she must perform the ritual to locate the source of the magical disturbance.\n\nGo through the door to the left, then follow the river to the right. The Sanctum waits at the river's end.
Quickly. Meet me at Loth'na Caverns. We must stop Regent Cassipia before it's too late.
Do be careful in Zaintiraris. The Mad God put his fingerprints all over that place. I … we've got a lot riding on you.

You never cease to surprise me, hero. You have a habit of turning up whenever I could use a bit of assistance.\n\nAnd speaking of assistance, while I might enjoy taking advantage of the situation, what say I remove those bindings for you.
How was your trip to Shadowfen? Catch anything good?

Mind your step. I would not want you to step on this random patch of grass. I jest, of course. The Telvanni force me to work, but I make sure it brings them no pleasure.\n\nI see you wear no shackles. Do you seek work? I know someone who needs help.
This one welcomes you to the Trial of Five-Clawed Guile! Celebrate the New Life and pay your respects to Rajhin, all at once!
Well, did you speak to my mother? What'd she say? Knowing her, it's something incredibly unreasonable.
Give my regards to <<1>>. It has been far too long since I visited Eastmarch.
Auri-El watch over you.
Oh, thank the Three! Lord Vivec looks better already. Of course, the Blessing Stone is only a temporary measure. We still need to determine what to do about Barbas and the stolen energy.

I'm going to check on Menwendel's progress. I believe in you, but nothing can be left to chance. Vehk willing, Mistress Dratha will make a full recovery.\n\nWith her health restored, those Hlaalu bastards won't dare make another play for Tel Mora.
Who are you? Why are you wasting my time?
Ha! I recognize that swagger. Firuth agreed to my demands, didn't he?
Leaving Sun-in-Shadow drives a spine through my heart, but she thinks herself free already. I wish she could see that she bears heavier chains than I do.
Greetings, serjo. What brings you to these parts?
Keep your weapons sheathed, citizen. The situation is well in hand, I assure you.
Do I look like someone who has time to chat? Because I assure you, I do not.
The jobs I hand out aren't easy, but they are well rewarded.
Be careful out there. All manner of beasts linger around those mushrooms.
Please, I'm working as fast as I can! I can't work if you hurt me!
Stay your lash, slaver. I work. Whipping me will not motivate me further.

Greetings fellow traveler of … whatever town we're in!\n\nSpeak to me as a friend, for that is what we shall become! That is unless you have darkness in your heart. Then we will part as the greatest of enemies. For I only mingle with those pure!
While I admit this little sphere is impressive, I feel we're just wasting time. The ghosts are out there!
What? I'm working here.
Back again? Honestly, I've got important work to do. Real healing, unlike that alchemical quackery. Now, off with you!
The portal will lead you to Xykenaz's chamber. Keep your wits, child. There's more to this creature than meets the eye.
You're back. Did you find Melar? Were you able to get him out?

Ah, my friend. I see Constable Gretga found you. Please, forgive me if I don't stand up. The marshal's henchmen broke my knees as soon as I arrived.\n\nIt is good to meet you, face to face. I wish it was under better circumstances.

We're paying some bard to sing to dung-piles now? To soothe the royal egg with the power of music? Are you all deranged? This sounds like something out of a children's story!\n\nHow is Lathdar falling for this? It's clearly part of Revus's evil plan.
Please tell me you have good news. I don't think I've got the stamina for another disaster.\n\nWhat did Revus say? Can he help us or not?
Please, help. You must help!

When a god knows loss, mortals suffer. As is often the case, dark thoughts form the most poignant phrases.\n\nI must concentrate lest the moonlet plunge or some other disaster befalls us. Talk to the Archcanon. See how he thinks we should proceed.

You're back! It's Lord Vivec! He just … he just collapsed! The more he weakens, the closer the moonlet slides toward the city and the more Red Mountain churns with fire and ash!\n\nI hope you brought good news. Vivec knows we could use some!
Clear the passage and rescue my workers and you can borrow the Blessing Stone. Just let Lord Vivec know that we'll need it back to finish building this part of his city.
You have proven yourself capable, for an outlander. Avenge our lost warriors.
Be careful in there. We'll keep an eye on this Ashlander.
You are a true hero, walker. A brave and noble warrior! Falura and I are forever in your debt!

Now to get some townspeople to go retrieve those eggs with some carts.\n\nI hope you cleared a decent enough path for them to get through unharmed. Getting more Gnisis people injured would look very bad on my part.
I don't know if I should wait here or go get the House Guard, but I hate to abandon my miners to those horrible cultists!\n\nWhatever you do, don't go into the Shulk Ore Mine!

It may seem like Narsis's books write themselves, but he uses dedicated assistants such as myself to get all the words down on paper.\n\nIt is a very important task! And I love that Narsis trusts me to know his own mind.
My translation was nearly perfect, so how could this be? Where are the relics? The treasure? There's nothing here but some busted old crates and a decrepit old well!

Do you like it, my latest creation? I call it the tonal inverter! Did I mention that already? No matter, it should counteract Sotha Sil's modified staff, at least momentarily.\n\nI assume you know how to use this, correct?
That was … harder than I expected.\n\nChodala was so angry … so full of rage. Not like himself at all. Still, I can't believe I helped kill my own brother ….
Quietly now. Is it finished?
That was some first-rate diplomacy. You're practically a Clanfriend already!\n\nI saw you speaking to the Wise Woman. What did she say?
Hmm. Your footsteps are as loud as a kagouti's. What is it you want, outlander?
Hurry, assistant. The prism must be somewhere ahead.

When you kill spirits in this realm, they never truly die. They simply lose the energy that allows them to manifest.\n\nSometimes though, when a spirit is powerful enough, it'll leave a part of that energy behind. That's what we're looking for.
Well, that was one experience I never want to repeat. Let's keep moving.

You mean to spend some time in Vos? I wouldn't linger if I were you.\n\nYou don't have scales or fur, so you should be safe for a time. But if Savarak and his lackeys smell a whiff of danger on you, they'll put a knife in your back by suppertime.
Yes? Is there something I can do for you, outlander?

Didn't expect to see anyone else out this far. Not a relic hunter, I hope. Caused enough trouble already.\n\nTythis Nirith. I'm not … not here, officially. Came seeking my sister, but that didn't go as planned.
Sorry, I grew tired of waiting. I received more than a few sideward glances on my way over. What happened in there?
Ah, the murderer appears. I should thank you for saving me the trouble of hunting you down. Watching you peasants struggle against the inevitable is exhausting.

Weakness has no place in Vvardenfell. Constantly test yourself and harden your resolve or this land will devour you. We stay sharp by hunting deadly beasts and claiming trophies from each kill. \n\nI wonder, are you up to such a challenge?
Back again? Father hasn't been an undue burden to you, I hope.
Oh, you've returned to bother me again.
I've left the tower, yet I keep having the same dreams.
Yes, well. I came to warn Sun-in-Shadow, but it seems I arrived too late. I guess I should warn you too.\n\nMy most benevolent master, Muthsera Gothren is … disgruntled.
You need something else? Just call it out, bear cub.
I'll make sure Veya stays out of trouble. Just find whatever you can so we can get out of here before the Warclaws notice us.
Back again? So tell me, you didn't do anything unlawful now, did you?
Move along.
Welcome to our shop. Feel free to look around.
Well, this is a coincidence. I came for a bottle of dry white. What brought you here? Have you spoken to Eoki yet?

Enter and be welcome, outlander. I wonder, however. Are you willing to prove your friendship?\n\nDaedric shrines, remnants of a better time, dot the land. We seek to preserve the memory of these places. Aid me and gain the favor of the Urshilaku tribe.
The model of Vvardenfell progresses nicely, but we still have a long way to go to fill in all the notable landmarks and uncover the location of the lost Library of Andule.
They killed my brother! I can't … I can't talk to you right now.

According to my sources, the councilor's expecting her contact from House Dres to arrive shortly.\n\nI think this is the first time they're meeting in person, so maybe you can use that to get close to her.

Did Ashur send you to check up on me? I swear, the next person that treats me like a child is going to find my dagger in their stomach!\n\nGods, I'm not mad at you. I'm just annoyed at everybody right now!
I want you to have those grumps in stitches, one way or another!

Just be careful, all right? This place seethes with Daedric energy. I see … golden horns, suspended from gossamer strands. All covered in blood.\n\nI fear I'll see much worse before this adventure ends.
This one's overlarge heart tramples in anticipations of seeing his bride-to-be!
You stray far from the House-path, outlander. Stray any further and the Ahemmusa tribe will have your head.
Rejoice, mortal. You stand in the presence of beauty and terror, between pale light and long shadows. I am Azura, Queen of Dawn and Dusk.\n\nI have a task for you.
You walk among the Zainab as a child walks among hungers. If you value your hide, move on.
Bow your head, outlander. You may not see the dead, but the dead see you—as do I.
You dare to stand before the First Ashkhan, outlander? Move on, or pay the price in blood!
I thought I heard the raucous cheers and playful pops of my handiwork echoing throughout the city.\n\nTell me it was more than my imagination!
We need to find those soldiers. I won't let this chance get away from us.

Excellent work! Now that you have an idea of what we do here, I can offer you more specific challenges. The Circle of Champions is always looking to sponsor players who keep competition fierce. \n\nComplete a challenge and return for your reward.

I may not consider him to be a true deity, but Vivec doesn't seem to be an entirely bad sort.\n\nI'll be heading back to my tribe soon. I'm glad we got a chance to see each other again before I take my leave.
No more time to talk. Let's go stop Veya.
As far as the official record is concerned, you don't exist. So forgive me if I don't engage in conversation. I'm extremely busy at the moment.

Veya needs her rest. I don't want any of Ashur's stitches to split open before she's had a chance to fully heal.\n\nIf you want a last word with Veya, we'll be in Vivec City for a bit before her ship sets sail.

Do be quick about your task. I'm eager to uncover the secret of these ruins.\n\nI shall remain behind to prepare my man-servant. It will take a deft touch to convince him to drink the tea and face his fear head on.
You shouldn't be talking to me. Lady Laurent requires your undivided attention.

I disabled most of the defenses in this section, but Sotha Sil installed numerous safeguards. I advise caution, just in case.\n\nBarbas is ahead of us, but I know many paths through the city. We're just like the fox that chased the hound!
Farwen's safe, Galgalah's banished, and even our contract's fulfilled. \n\nYou certainly know how to snatch victory from the jaws of defeat, friend!

The Warrior-Poet shall write of your deeds in story and song, my friend. You will be remembered for your service to Vvardenfell.\n\nNow go, see the wonders of our great land. There are others who need your help, of that I am certain.

I couldn't help overhearing your conversation with my husband. We share the same office, after all. Thank you for agreeing to look for our daughter.\n\nBut know that Veya is headstrong. I say this from experience. I am her mother, after all.
Must … maintain … concentration.
Though Pelinal is seen as a controversial figure by some, none can dispute the mark he left on our land and culture. \n\nAnd so we cry: hail the Whitestrake!
The factotums reported a strange energy signature in Gascone's rectory. Did you find anything odd in there?
Are you really going to climb aboard this death trap? Just hold a moment and think it through.
You look a bit lost, friend. Can I help you find a book?
Greetings, dryskin. What can I do for you? Do you have a crime to report?
It buoys my spirit to know that you're looking into this business. I would not have chosen Divayth Fyr as your companion, but desperate times make for uncomfortable alliances.

It's wondrous, isn't it? Elegant, meticulous, timeless. I once took joy in studying the perfection of this realm, but now every revolution of the Great Gear only tightens the vice in my chest.\n\nTell me, are you here to unravel Lord Seht's mysteries?
Who are you? Give me one good reason why I shouldn't reduce you to dust where you stand.
You look restless, gear-walker. If you seek work, you should talk to <<1>>. The people of Slag Town always welcome a helping hand.

Looking to help us Tarnished in Slag Town? We have a mighty need for some supplies. You'll get payment, of course, but we're looking for a tough sort who doesn't mind traveling to some rather nasty locales.
Novice Oscard told me what you did. Thank you!
We won't get any farther than this with the bridge out of alignment. Go activate those core pumps, then I can override the bridge control manually.

This is the lector's simulated sunlight inductor. And just as we read in his notes, he's using the life force of the most recent apprentices to power the device.\n\nSotha Sil would never approve of this. Never in a million clicks of the Great Gear.

I always share a few words of advice with the hopefuls that weren't selected before I take the new apprentice under my wing. \n\nThe Everwound Wellspring provides excellent opportunities for the novice apostles.

Follow this road to the Brass Fortress. When you see the wayshrine, veer north … or what passes for north here.\n\nIf you have other business to attend to, I'll not stop you. Just meet me at the gates to the fortress when you're ready to proceed.
Would you stay with me in my final moments? I mean, I won't remember I suppose. But I'd rather not do it alone.
Lankin's clever, but he can't hold out much longer. We've got to find him.

All right, let me see what you found. Yes, I believe these recordings correspond to the dates of the disappearances.\n\nThere's something more. Look here. The last person to access the records was a BAL-167. Hmph. Circumstantial at best.
There you are! Neramo said you'd be around here somewhere. Have you seen Kireth? Is she with you?
Now, we don't have time for dawdling. The distillation initiator still needs to be fixed after all.\n\nWe just need to find a cleansing crystal.
Why do you linger, Featherless? Fetch our treasure or begone! Begone!
Seems young Kireth brings ill news. Speak with her.
A noble, if short-sighted, choice to save Luciana. But then, the long view brings its own perils.\n\nWhere will she go from here? Perhaps you can help her decide.
The Queen of Chaff will arrive shortly. We must stun her with my magnificence! Are you ready?
Lead the way, assistant … er, valued peer. Once we have a thorough understanding of the parts, I'll have the lamp assembled in no time.
Hello again, friend! Interest you in a rust crumble cake? It's not so bad—once you get past the taste. Texture's nice.
If you search for salvage, you have come to the right place, walker. Na'jhargo received a fresh shipment of cranks and cogs just days ago!\n\nWhat can this one get you?
Promise you'll keep this between us? I like Bren too much to break his heart. He tries so hard to keep us in good spirits.

I just cannot believe what fortune the Eight have blessed me with today!\n\nI'll make it my life's work to share with others what transpired here today. All shall know that it was you who bravely defeated Zaan the Scalecaller and saved Tamriel.
Beginning entity analysis. Error. Entity exists outside known possipoints. Transitioning to general reception array.\n\nHello.
Sounds like the Duke is waiting. Let's get this over with.

You must use the calibration guide to show the stars their place in the sky, before the cultists gather them once more. Still, I will answer your questions. Curiosity is warranted, given the circumstances.
Astounding! The first factotum Sotha Sil created.\n\nWe simply must complete construction now. The more memory it recalls, the further my research can develop. Council seat, here I come!
By Seht's will, I am bound.\n\nGreetings, resident. What do you require?

Well, now that that's all over and done with, we can get back to the exciting stuff! I can't wait to crawl around in some of these clockwork contraptions.\n\nAnyway, thanks for helping Raynor. I really do worry about him, you know.
I wonder how the lubricant winds up in the Vale? Every time I answer one question, three more appear to take its place!
Hello my friend! It's so good to see you again. I wish I had more time to talk, but my current tasks have me very busy. Us initiates never seem to have a moment to spare!
I can no longer guarantee your safety in this place. Please offer your prayers to the Saints from afar.
Come and go. Come and go. Brengolin has you flitting about like the dovah-flies. \n\nThis one must brace for what's to come, she thinks.
What's Maurice stepping so light around Brengolin for? He afraid of getting called on for the next experiment? You can tell him it's his turn!

Stay alert, five-claw. Raz has heard Psijics turn people into chickens and make them explode. To die covered in feathers instead of fur, such a horrible demise.\n\nIn the meantime, Raz will send Avinisse home until the Proxy Queen renders judgment.

Go on. The projection isn't going to talk to itself.\n\nAnd really, I'm basically blazing with magical energy. I fear that if I get too close, I'll overwhelm Marieve's simple spell and this opportunity to communicate will be lost.
Time is short … the dark princes have almost achieved their goal … you must help me ….
My social standing is ruined. Just … ruined.
I'll let you handle the Canonreeve. I'm a bit out of practice in dealing with the niceties of Summerset society. I wouldn't want to inadvertently cause insult.

While you were gone, I have been scrying through my own memories, trying to find the missing events that will remind me where I hid the Heart of Transparent Law.\n\nI believe I have discovered something significant.

You have new evidence to present? Very well. I trust your investigation was thorough and unbiased? Or rather, as thorough and unbiased as an itinerant newcomer can manage.\n\nWhat new evidence do you wish to enter into the official record?
You're back! Did you find any evidence that might exonerate Emile? You must have found something.
What did Guard Milerond have to say? Were you able to discover anything that might shed light on Haladan's murder?
Welcome to Lillandril. Just off the boat? Lots of sailors coming and going. Just don't forget to submit your shipping manifests to the harbormaster.\n\nUnless there's something else you need?
I don't want your help. I don't need it. Go away! Leave this matter to the authorities!
The scrying pool revealed that yaghra have invaded our island. They must have somehow used the abyssal pearl to open a pathway.\n\nWe need to get down to the beach and repel the invaders.

I'm pleased you found your way to our little island. And no significant side effects? Splendid! Sometimes the attuning process causes … issues. Nothing to be overly concerned about, though.\n\nWhen you're ready, the Ritemaster wants to speak to you.
I was examining the vial of amplification elixir myself just a short time ago. It should be right over there.
I couldn't breathe! As usual, you found me just in the nick of time.\n\nThe beast that captured me. I've never seen anything like it!

While the Golden Knight recovers, we must make preparations for breaching the Daedric barrier. Since I can't remember where that particular pathway goes, we'll have to be ready for any contingency.\n\nI also need to tell you about another memory.
See what I mean? I thought this enchantment was a bit of foolishness, but there's no frivolity in those words. I think the book means to hurt us!

It's now clear Larydel has lost his way. He has been consumed by this fantasy of becoming a thespian.\n\nNo matter. We shall solve this at the auditions. Once I reveal Larydel with magic, he'll have to leave the troupe.

I've made so many mistakes. What do I do? Should I tell Rinyde who I am, and ask her to forgive me for lying? Or should I let her depart and ensure she finds her dreams, even though she may hate me forever?\n\nI only want her to be happy.
All right, go ahead. Ask me anything!
Now it's my turn for a boast! What would you like to know about the spectacular Clever?

You must know we are competing for the same post. Let me be clear, then, in stating that I do not intend to fail my audition. I will join the House of Reveries. It is my destiny!\n\nStill, collaboration never hurts. Care to play the game?
An adventurer? Praise you, Mara, for hearing my prayers!\n\nPlease, newcomer—I'm desperate for help. My son, Arathel, has gone missing. No one will tell me what happened to him!
Hello! Come to join in my adventures? Or maybe you mean to scold me like the mean old workers. I hope not.\n\nI could use a new playmate! Torchbug's fun, but a little strange.
I would appreciate it if you kept this matter to yourself. If word got out that our procedures are imperfect, well … that would be a very inauspicious day. For everyone.
Better get rid of that Talerion quick. My knife-hand's getting twitchy.

Agh! Don't hurt me! Wait. You're not one of them, are you? Sorry. As soon as I saw an opening, I took off running. I didn't even see that drop!\n\nHonestly, I'm lucky to be alive … for the moment, at least. My mother is going to kill me.
Please, my lord … spare a coin for a wretched beggar?

All right, royal inspector. Off you go. Just talk like you've never interacted with an actual person at any point in your life.\n\nWe'll put a stop to these killings and maybe not even get arrested. Fun, right?
Any luck with those wards? Just keep at it. If there's one thing I know about cultists, it's that worshiping dark powers makes them pretty dim. It can't be that complicated.
Have you figured it out yet? The answer is as plain as the nose on your face!
Two arrests in one day. This is going to reflect well on my next report.
All right, that's enough! You were amusing at first, but now you're just a nuisance. This isn't how the story goes!

A House of Reveries expedition I've never heard of. Grand Maestro Forte rebuffing his proper title. \n\nAnd the temple room, where we found Fletch? It looked the same as the room we first entered, but there wasn't a cobweb or broken pew in sight.

She poisoned all these animals—she almost poisoned Lotus! And for what?\n\nIt's true that I've never seen an animal moved to the inner paddocks that's returned to outer enclosures, but she's suggesting what? That the Conservator is culling the herd?
Yes, our heroine should just be outside, if I remember correctly. After so many times around though, I tend to lose track.\n\nWell, no need to get into all of that.
I'll meet you outside when you've finished.
Finally, the courier! I expected you hours ago. You must acquire my materials at once. And don't think I'll compensate you for the rush, given you're the one who was late.
You just can't take the last aurialis, please! If you uproot it now, it will never spread its seeds. This might be the last chance the species has.
Hey there, careful where you step! My livestock is having their dinner, and I won't have some bumbler stomping all over them. I've got enough trouble with their mating woes.

You know, I've heard quite a bit about your little venture to acquire Tindoria's supplies for her latest sketch, and I must say I'm impressed. You've certainly proven capable.\n\nI have a proposition for you. Sell those supplies to me instead.
This is where we part ways, friend. I wish I'd known more people like you in my life. Things might have been different if I had.
Is it just the two of you? I suppose it'd have to be. No one from his garrison would volunteer to help a Maormer.\n\nYou know the truth then? About us?
The crows … their words stir the echoes in my mind.
The crows … they implied that the Ritemaster accepted an offer from Nocturnal. Could such a thing be true?
Why are the realms of Daedric Princes always so ominous and evil looking? You'd think they'd get bored with all the forlornness and tribulation.
Where is Battlereeve Pandermalion? His soldiers said he returned to Sea Keep with a passerby. One that matches your description. What is going on?
You're sticking by my side? Even after I used that death-memory ritual? I appreciate that, admanen. Truly.\n\nI suppose I owe you a bit of an explanation.
Looks like you've got everything you need to start your search!
Who are you? Are you with the Divine Prosecution? My husband warned me you might come poking around.
I suppose I'll stay here to break bread with the chief while you have a look around. Not the way I wanted things to go, but we will simply have to adapt.

Giants are territorial under the best of circumstances, and this disease has only increased their hostility. They also appear no worse for wear, despite their affliction. Or perhaps because of it.\n\nThe more I see of this plague, the more I fear it.

Val and the Psijics, they're too set in their ways. We need a better plan.\n\nI'll return to Artaeum with her, because Meridia told me to cooperate. But as soon as I think of something more effective, I'll let you know.

Do we really need to go over this again? Mephala and the triad sought places of power—the Clockwork City, the Crystal Tower—anything they could use to change the rules of reality and remake the world.\n\nThey wanted to make things better!
The knight tests my patience, but I'll let his words pass for now.\n\nI promise you, if there's a way to utilize the diamonds to open the Crystal Tower, the Psijic Order will find it.

Wouldn't go any deeper if I were you, sap-friend. Darkness crawls along the walls of Eton Nir. Only thing you'll find here is an ugly death.\n\nThat, and the corpse of my former apprentice. Most likely.

Now that we have the writ of authenticity, the letter of recommendation, and the tickets to Enigma's performance, we should return to Courtier Vindilween so I can get my audience with the Proxy Queen.
I honestly never expected to see either you or Ambassador Rigurt again. Can I assume this means you acquired the items I specified?

Oh my! You're one of the newcomers! I wish I had time to chat, but there's so much to do, so much to do.\n\nFind me later, though. I'd love to ask you questions about who you are and where you came from.
Move along, newcomer. The Divine Prosecution has more important matters to attend to than whatever trouble you've gotten yourself into.
Whatever you're planning on doing, do it quick. I have to get word to the Proxy Queen. I won't wait forever.
Come now, let's finish this. While there's still time for Lilawen to come up with an excuse.
Manacar might not understand, but just know this is my choice. I'm willing to risk it all, if it means keeping him by my side.\n\nSurely you can make him see reason.
Keep it down! I don't want you drawing any more this way. Already broke my best quill killing the last one to sniff me out.
Just look at this architecture! And art! Oh, I just don't know where to begin. What should we drink in first?

The Ritemaster continues to seek the memories that were forgotten or altered by the Sea Sload's mind magic. I still find it hard to believe that they actually compelled him to steal the Heart of Transparent Law.\n\nWe need to warn the Sapiarchs.
Leythen needs a moment to come to grips with what happened here.\n\nGo find the shrine. I'll make sure he's all right and we'll catch up with you.
Now, if Raz was a member of this academy, where would he put a library, some books, and a few podiums?

Gather your companions and meet me in the Dreaming Cave. We must contact Vile and Mephala so you can enter the Crystal Tower, recover the Heart of Transparent Law, and repair the tower crystal.\n\nThat will require a burst of divine energy, though.
Don't let your guard down out there. Especially with Faidur at your back.
I trust you were able to discover enough evidence to convince the prosecutor of Eslion's guilt? I'd like to finally be rid of this pest sooner than later.

Hi again. In a bit of a bind, as you can see. I tried to apologize, I really did, but she's telling the Prosecution I've been terrorizing her.\n\nI could use some good news. How'd you fair with those stranglers?
If it weren't for you, I'd have wound up a husk like those … monsters. Withering in that pit for who knows how long. I owe you my life.

Excellent. Once you've finished, meet me near the Mages Guild in Shimmerene.\n\nOf course, discretion is key here. I want no word getting out about this little incident, not even to common folk. Rumours do tend to spread, after all.
Wait. You're not one of the pack. Why, you're not even a werewolf.\n\nYou need to leave now. It's far too dangerous here. They've already killed Brengas, and … it's too late for me.

Cainar should be our first priority, though don't tell him I said that.\n\nWe approach magecraft differently, but he's an accomplished practitioner of the art. He can assist us in rescuing the others, so find him and free him first.

Never seen you before. Guess no one told you that this is my spot. Been my spot nearly a century, and it'll be my spot a century more—gods willing—so don't go getting any ideas.\n\nPlenty of space down the coast, so off with you now.
Even in such disrepair, I can imagine how opulent this manor must have been. My relatives must have been very influential here.
Look, we don't have time to stand around and chat.
Ah, the putrid smell of burning, disease ridden flesh. Just can't get enough of it.

Things aren't going well, my friend. The Conclave's efforts to attune the Resolute Diamonds have failed, and news of the proposed alliance with Daedric Princes has the Psijics on edge.\n\nDid you really make a deal with Vile and Mephala?
You should check Lirendel's ancestral tomb. Got to get our hands on his full name if we want to start this fight!
Fairly met, nebarra. To what do I owe this profound pleasure?

Your Orc friend should be counting his blessings. If this business leads to a real duel, Lirendel will cut him to ribbons!\n\nBut of course you won't listen. Orcs only speak the language of violence. More's the pity.
What I wouldn't give for some mead right now. Once we have our strength we'll be leaving this damned place behind us, promise you that.
The shadow creatures are already flooding into this area.
I'm beginning to hate that sword-stealing witch!

Ah, there you are. I see you've been deputized by Chief Justiciar Carawen. It's quite exciting to see so many newcomers taking an interest in our little project.\n\nNow, I expect you're ready for your first assignment.
I've tried every reasonable argument I could possibly think of, and still Sapiarch Larnatille refuses to budge. Perhaps you can talk some sense into her.
With these supplies, Renzir now has the means to continue on. Karnwasten is of course no longer of use, but Summerset has many caves.

As a duly sworn deputy of the Divine Prosecution, your aid is required newcomer. Dangerous entities have appeared throughout Summerset and we could use the help of skilled adventurers such as yourself.\n\nWill you comply?

The work you did to bring us information on the Sea Sload, brilliant! That's only the beginning, however.\n\nNow we need to act on that information before the Abyssal Cabal can inflict too much damage on the island.

Thanks for retrieving Grog. He may be lazy, perpetually intoxicated, and a terrible cheat at Ancestor Draw, but he is one of my steadfast companions.\n\nWas he able to shed any additional light on the Sea Sload menace?
Thanks for getting me out of those chains. My wrists were starting to chafe.\n\nSo, what's the plan? How do we get out of this Oblivion pit?
Welcome back, initiate. I hope the swamp did not exact too high a toll on you. Josajeh waits for you in the Athenaeum.
Ah, my aching head. Where in Oblivion am I? Oh, yes, that's right. This is Russafeld. I came here to buy some … some wine! That's it. \n\nWait a minute. Oh no, don't-don't tell me I lost them!
These are perfect! Exactly what I needed! Now I can use these to … to … of course!\n\nStand back! With these particles, I can finally understand the meaning of these magnificent tomes!
Unlike other crafts, you will need no style materials for this task. Simply take your pewter ounces to a jewelry crafting station and create one.\n\nCraft your ring and bring it back to me.
It seems I am not only beset upon by my own indolent assistants, but by the curiosity of passing vagrants as well.

Move along, there's nothing to see here. Wait, you're not one of those Divine Prosecution types, are you? You have to tell me if you are.\n\nWait, what am I thinking. There's no way they'd let you into their ranks.
We must defeat Z'Maja, no matter the cost.
I'm beginning to think you two are connected in some way. I'll be watching.
Which way to the nearest tavern? No, don't tell me, I can smell it!
I'm sorry, but I have no time to speak at the moment. There are injured people here that require my assistance. \n\nIf you wish to help, go speak with Welkynar Olorime. She may have a task for you.
I'm fine, initiate. You should set out soon.

It's beautiful, isn't it? Even after all these years, I'm still in awe of this place. And now I'll never see it again.\n\nForgive me. We both know this is a fate I brought upon myself. Is there something you need, initiate?

You have made the right decision. There is no safer and more comfortable place than Relicmaster Glenadir's vault. Deliver the Augur to him at once.\n\nI will conclude matters here, gather Josajeh, and meet you at the portal back to Tamriel.

It's so good to see Lotus alive and well. I couldn't stop thinking of her scared and injured, or worse. If Vinelore had turned her into some kind of monster, I swear …!\n\nWe should flee before Vinelore and her rangers come after us.

Narazda did not stay in this Alkosh forsaken place to be ignored.\n\nListen well, walker. The garden that lies ahead is the only way forward, but dangers lurk within. Still, we must pass through if we ever hope to face Vykosa.
Jee-Lar brought me up to speed on what the Argonians revealed to you. He also gave me part of a map. Were you able to find the other two pieces?

Looks like you can take care of yourself. Good. Because this is far from over.\n\nYou'll need to head to the gardens next. Unfortunately, it's crawling with all manner of dangerous creatures. Don't let your guard falter.
So the Orc's name is Balorgh, is it? Looks like he's our last bit of competition. And the most dangerous too, if his attitude is any indication.
The black market is closed. This one has inventories to catalog and my assistant has yet to return. I sent him to retrieve a package, but he never came back.\n\nBother someone else, please.

As long as the cavern was sealed, the Wuju-Ka was trapped. It couldn't spread across Murkmire. But now that the caves are open ….\n\nThere's no one else my friend. We need to find the altar and perform the ritual to bind it to this cavern!

What a rollicking adventure I had! There were Blackguards—at least a dozen or so!—and an angry wamasu ….\n\nAnyway, I gave the part of the map I recovered to Concordia. Did you find the other two pieces? Well, go show her!
Don't you have somewhere to be?
We should not delay. The Remnant is within our grasp.

Part of me wishes I could go with you, but I'm sure I'd just get in the way.\n\nI can swing a book as hard as the next scholar, but I doubt even Wendel Castiene's prodigious Helstrom Codex could fell one of those Blackguards. Just be careful!
Another temple conquered, eh? Closest call this one has seen in years, though.\n\nYou did well in there, walker. Zadaza thinks you might have a future in this business!
Good luck out there, hero! We'll see you at the xanmeer, all right?
You look burdened, ojel. Please, sit and let the breeze carry your cares away. The Bright-Throats have brought us many nice things to share.
The practices of indigenous tribes fascinate me so! Many of them are so primal … so visceral!\n\nPardon my musings. Is there something you need?
This is not where I imagined we'd cross paths again. It seems we've both come a long way from Volenfell, but are we after the same thing?

Glad you took me up on my offer. It seems you're the only one of the Frostvault expedition willing to see this through. Ha. They were slowing us down anyway. \n\nI assume you're ready to get underway?
Impressive work in there. I wish I'd hired you sooner.
Wasseek eyes are watching. Can you feel them?\n\nI do not like it.
You've been gone awhile. You find those tablets or just get stuck in the mud?

I spit at tradition and the cowardice it breeds! The Dead-Water tribe is proud. Set in its ways. But those ways will be the end of us. Even a stupid outsider can see such things!\n\nI mean no offense.
Do not crowd us, ojel. You will disturb Ruxol's focus.
The outsider returns. Just in time to see the disgrace that clings to me like the mist that rises from the swamp.\n\nBut what of my egg-son? Does Kishi still live?
Do not keep the sap-speaker waiting, beeko. Tell her I am ready to guide these souls to the next life.

The season turns strange. First, I break the laws of the tribe to save lives. Now an outsider appears out of nowhere to rescue me from certain death. You have my thanks and my respect.\n\nUnless you seek a reward. Then I respect you less.
You are the ojel who helped our kaal, Jaxsik-Orrn, destroy the Blackguard wagon-snake, are you not? Hmm. It seems you did not kill enough.
We should find the others. I will search one way, you search another.
Good, you are here. Tell the Tree-Minder of the terrible things we saw. She must understand.
I think … yeah, I'm sobering up. Time for another round!

Oh good-good! I hoped our paths would cross again, and here you are.\n\nWant to help Cyrodilic Collections again? We need assistance with our next expedition to Murkmire. Things aren't going as smoothly as planned.
Got the skink, eh? Well done!\n\nYou should deliver him to Jee-Lar quick as you can. Don't want him running off again, right?
It pains me to deny the Hist to one of our own, but the rotting root is a danger to the whole tree.\n\nHaxara will have to find her way in the wider world.
Great day for a walk, eh? Just watch out for snakes!
No just go ahead and slaughter your way through. Don't mind me.
It's premature for a tour. We still have a lot of preparations to make.
Ah, is that the aroma of toad musk I smell? How delightful!\n\nI hope you were gentle with the little croakers. They need to be calm and relaxed to produce the most pleasing sounds.

Very well done. You must be half river-boa, beeko. Lozwug looked hypnotized! No … no, I give you too much credit. He has a brain like a bone-trout.\n\nBut my tongue wanders, let me read this. Oh. This is …. Yes, this may rattle the cattails.
There you are. I … I'm sorry, it's very hard … to concentrate. The Remnant called out to me. It … it wanted me to take it, but only for a short time.\n\nWe have to be quick.
Be quick in your interrogation. Jaxsik's tail is in a twist. She means to strike this woman dead very, very soon.
Sithis waits for this animal with an open maw, ojel. I will not make it wait much longer.

I'll admit, I'm a little jealous. To think, you're going to undertake a heretofore unknown dream-wallow ritual! Not even Xukas or Jaxsik-Orrn know what you'll encounter. Amazing!\n\nI'd say take notes, but I doubt you'll be in a writing state of mind.
Isn't she beautiful? My little girl.
After you, hero.

I fill my lungs. I always imagined I would fall in a spray of curses and blood, but I see now that my passing will be unlike any Dead-Water warrior before me. Quiet, but glorious all the same.\n\nI was born to die for my people. The duty is mine.
Don't wander off, all right? Fighting skeletons and dream-monsters is well outside my purview.
Come for the bonding ritual? Not to partake, obviously. You're early either way. You might want to make yourself scarce until it's actually time for the ceremony.

What a resounding victory! Keep this up, and we'll have Seeks free in no time.\n\nNow, the next arena is called the Hall of Beasts. Keep on your toes, all right? I heard that Tames-the-Beast has all sorts of nasty tricks up his sleeve.
I am once more indebted to you, beeko.\n\nShould Paraxeeh grow suspicious, tell him I wish to write about the ritual in my newest book. That should suffice.
Ranja expected such a vault to be laden with treasures. This one thinks the Dwarves had a sense of humor.
Thank you for all your help. I now see my fears were overblown. Sulahkeesh has been nothing but pleasant.
Have both Nurhei and Paheiza rub the oil into their scales, and tell them to meet at the town's entrance. There, the matter will finally be put to rest.
Dare I hope your search was finally successful?
I've no time to chat. It is a busy day, and I need to make sure this shipment is off before the next tide. Take your business elsewhere.
What do you want?
I believe we have no further business. May your travels be swift, and your heart firmly rooted.
Why do you hesitate? We must do before we can undo!

You picked the proper path through the quicksand. Well done!\n\nDangerous plants and carnivorous beasts fill the next section of the Path. They will do their best to end your trial with every step you take.

You should speak to Milzus, in Bright-Throat Village. She is the one who found poor Danlai. Be gentle with her. She was quite shaken by what she saw.\n\nI will await word from you at Dead-Water Village. It is the safest place I can think of.

I crossed paths with the Skin Taker by the Dead-Water pools near our village. I wish you better luck in your pursuit than I.\n\nI will maintain the vigil here. You have a safe haven among the Dead-Water.
May your path be peaceful and your days sun-blessed.

I erect the spine of awkward greetings. Perhaps you are lost?\n\nThis is the storehouse, ojel. Nothing but carefully organized goods and crafts here. You would find far more amusing things to occupy yourself with outside, I think.
So, that's the Wrathstone. I was expecting something more grand, but I'm too cold to be disappointed.
I erect the spine of welcome, beek-ojel. Do your currents wind toward Bright-Throat lands?
I don't suppose they'll give up now that their warlord is dead? Probably not.

I appreciate you accompanying me, but I must admit I have something of an aversion to insects. And snakes. And waterfalls.\n\nStill, Lady Laurent does know best when it comes to situations such as this. I'll meet you out in the swamp, my friend.

After you and Stibbons confront Many-Whispers, meet me at the Lodge of Renewal. It's north of the Bright-Throat Village, out in the middle of nowhere.\n\nCome to think of it, everything out here is in the middle of nowhere, but I'm sure you'll find it.
There is nothing you can say to change my mind, outsider, but at least you appear to be less … vociferous … than the demanding dryskin.
You will face the dream-wallow soon. I hope you did not eat a big meal. Tough on the mind, yes. But tougher on the belly.
Take it to the very center of the Glade, Xukas-friend—where the wind will catch it best!
I'm surprised to see you in this part of the world, old friend. Not that I'm complaining. It's always good to see you. But what are you doing in this land of mud and bugs?
Greetings, Beeko. I hope you enjoy your time in Bright-Throat Village.
You come from outside Lilmoth, yes? Then have you met Xukas? He loves to talk to travelers such as yourself.

Beehuna of the Root-House smiles shiftily. She has no doubt taken something of worth, but she has stopped pouting, so I will not complain.\n\nAll that is left is the suitor of the Moss-Skins. They are never difficult. I don't know why he delays.

These are the offices of Cyrodilic Collections. We're a society devoted to preserving Argonian antiquities, and that's a fact!\n\nIf you're looking to help, you should talk to Famia. She sort of runs things here, oh yes she does!
If you hurry, you can find Xukas by the Swallowed Grove. Moons guide you.

You helped give my people hope, five-claw. That is a debt I will be hard pressed to repay.\n\nLet us consult with Lord Gharesh-ri and Abnur Tharn. We have the rest of this war to plan out, not to mention Kaalgrontiid and the Dragons to deal with.

If those dung-heads had proper tails, what we did to their supply camps would put a kink in them!\n\nOne more small task, five-claw, if you are willing. This one would have you help the strange one named Cadwell.

So good to see you again! I missed you terribly. Now, mind where you step. I had no idea I could make such delightful murder toys. You don't want to stick a toe into any of them, though.\n\nBlew my little piggy right off.
Zamarak feels sorry for the undead. Forced to fight against their will. Such an abomination!
This one spits on the Usurper Queen and her soldiers! They have no right to pounce upon our land.
Give me good news, five-claw. I could use some right about now.

I must admit, your help was immeasurable out there. I had my hands full countering my half-sister's defenses. And when Nala-do fell, Khamira became useless for all intents and purposes.\n\nYou did … you did well. Considering.
You solved the first two puzzles easily enough. I'm sure this one won't give you any trouble. Do proceed.
Captain Saulinia and her assassins left the estate shortly before you arrived. If you're going to catch them before they find and kill the last Dragonguard, you really ought to get a move on.
There you are! Things seemed quieter, so Mara'dahni came to take a look around. Did you find Hadaz? And how about these cultists? I hope you gave them a swift kick in the tail!
Thank the Moons, you are back. The poachers! They—they took them!
Thank you, five-claw. With Saulinia dead, maybe the royal family can finally rest in peace.\n\nThe Dragonguard ran through that door, but he was wounded. We should help him.
With your help, my egg-mother's terrible mistake can finally be mended. Thank you, traveler-friend.\n\nFor now, I'll lead my companions back to camp.
You return. Good. Vazbi already loses too much today.\n\nSilhu-jo did not—Vazbi could not …. He is gone. His soul wanders the Sands Behind the Stars now.
This one is sorry you had to see that, walker.\n\nSilhu-jo does not like to issue commands like this, but Vazbi suffers a kitten's impatience sometimes. Perhaps you can talk some sense into her.

Khamira's parents would be proud of how she has stepped forward in these dark times. Moons, I am proud of her!\n\nWhile Khamira gathers her thoughts, the rest of us have work to do. Tell me, what happened in the palace?

I may not have figured out Khamira's true identity, but things have been hectic since I met her. Zamarak, though, he was easier to surmise. I recognized the bearing of the King's Claw the moment I saw him.\n\nDid you find us a way into the palace?

Welcome to this shrine, walker. It is dedicated to the ancient Khajiit hero, Khunzar-ri. If you are interested, this one recites the most popular tales of the hero on the first Morndas of every month.\n\nNext time it will be Khunzar-ri and the Dagi!

Cadwell's impulsive nature will be the doom of us all! He rushed headlong into danger without thinking! What am I saying? Cadwell does everything without thinking!\n\nWe have to get to him before Zumog Phoom completes his necromantic ritual.

May the Dark take Euraxia! She sent my own parents against us and killed the brave and honorable Nala-do!\n\nBut we have no time to mourn. We must determine what the Dragons seek at the ancient Moon Gate.

When Zamarak served as the King's Claw, he regularly patrolled these old passages. Whoever defends Euraxia doesn't appear to be quite as vigilant.\n\nWait. There is a scent … undead! Be careful, five-claw.

Nala-do never served at the palace, so this one wouldn't know Aneshi from M'aiq the Liar. Or Queen Khamira, for that matter, Nala-do is sad to say.\n\nWhen Euraxia attacked, this one was a new recruit assigned to a tower along the Cyrodiil border.
This disappearing act is getting very old very fast.
I'm practically my old self again! Well, not that old. I feel like me, not that other me from long ago.\n\nOh, this is so confusing! Let's just keep going. Tally-ho!
Welcome to the town of Hakoshae. I must say, it is not often I see a new face. \n\nHave you perhaps come to take part in our festival?

So, Garlas Malatar has been safeguarded by Meridia all this time. That explains why this place has remained relatively untouched for ages, and how the denizens are still around to make our lives difficult.
Hello, my friend! Pull up a patch of soil and sit for a spell.\n\nI'm just taking in the scenery before we're off to vanquish the next dastardly villain!
It is my sincere hope that Hakoshae continues to celebrate the Proving Festival for many years to come. I've honestly never felt more connected to my ancestors.
Lucky for you to arrive in Hakoshae just in time for the Proving Festival! Not many get the honor to see it in all its glory.
It's such an honor to lead the Proof of Wisdom for this year's Proving Festival. Though, I must admit, I'm not much of an academic!
Well, it seems that our investigation has come to a successful close. Though not quite in a way that Mizzik was expecting.

I think I understand. Not only do I hear the Moons sing, but I hear my ancestor, Anequina. The very walls echo with her memories. Good ones. Bad ones like the actions of the Betrayer.\n\nThey tell me we must seek the temple sanctuary to stop him.

Strange as it seems, Tasnasi is not only forgiven in the Stitches, she is looked up to. It will take time for the Stitches to be as it was. Maybe it will never get there, but even if she cannot live up to Dashing Dasalzo's legacy, Tasnasi will try.

A shame the gang's going their separate ways. Maybe this wasn't the cleanest job I ever worked, but it's always better to run with people you know.\n\nGuess I'll have to make a fresh start somewhere else. Again.
Huh. She actually did it. I would've bet my tail that Tasnasi would spare Khasda, if it came down to it.\n\nLooks like I underestimated her. Looks like Khasda did, too.

"Joyous is any reunion unexpected," spoke Renzi-jo to the Silent Disciple, "for to know the wheel of fate is to be bound to it."\n\nNazdar is glad to see you. Though he sees the burden this ordeal has had on Tasnasi's soul. He hopes she finds peace.
New face in the Stitches, then? I love new faces. I can front you a little money in exchange for … well, we can talk terms over wine. \n\nTo what do my brother and I owe the pleasure?

I'm positively fuming. Iulius has our entire wardrobe shipped here from Kvatch, and he still manages to pick out the exact same outfit I'm wearing. As if it weren't clear enough we're twins.\n\nBut you're not here to listen to a sibling's prattle.

The Wood Elf's name is … Mell? Yes, that's it. Mell the Musical, she always calls herself. You can usually find her toward the north end of town, near the sand gardens.\n\nIshu will pray for your swift success.
Greetings, walker. This one hopes your day is filled with long naps and fragrant breezes.
We did it, five-claw. We put the Moons back in motion and defeated both Mulaamnir and Kaalgrontiid.\n\nI … I want to thank you for everything. Elsweyr is safer today because of you.
This one is on a break, walker. Come back later, yes?

Would you like to hear the fragrant word of Azurah?\n\nIt was she who gave us shape and told us the three secrets. She who protected us from the wrath of Y'ffre and taught us the mysteries of the Moons.
Soon the Weeping Scar's tears will have run dry. Much like my own.
Be sure to protect the recruits you are asked to instruct. Your lessons will mean little if our soldiers are harmed in the process.

By the way, I believe I understand the purpose of the Dragonhorn. After much consideration, the use and function of the ancient instrument has become clear.\n\nThe Dragonguard were clever, I'll say that for them.
That path over there leads up to the top of the Moon Gate. We need to reach it before the Dragons break through our defenses.
Thank you for helping defend Riverhold from the Usurper Queen's forces. And killing a Dragon! That was … that was amazing.\n\nI just wish Khamira had not revealed herself in quite so open a fashion.
I'll remain here to ensure no more dark spirits escape.\n\nI know your souls well, now—yours and Shando-ri's. If I sense you've fallen into serious peril, I'll come to your aid. You have my word.

Gharesh-ri told me you found them. He filled me in on what happened during the battle at the Moon Gate.\n\nDragons and necromancers I understand. But politics and coronations? They twist my tail! And the regalia, it pinches! Moons, I miss my leathers!
You have the means to destroy Arum-Khal now. Azurah watch over you.\n\nTake care of Shando, child. Each of you will need the other before the end.
Welcome to the Prowl, friend! Lovely, eh? We sure could use some help to keep it that way.
Azurah's Gate. I had almost forgotten its beauty.
This is good meat. Rakhzargo would offer you some, but he dropped it earlier.
Perhaps you have been more helpful than this one's vagrant son. Tell Kideya, have you made any progress with our missing farmhands?
It is likely we are outnumbered, yes. But never underestimate the element of surprise. Or the gracious aid of Razum-dar, of course.

At this point, we need to come up with a plan that takes into account Euraxians, necromancers, and Dragons. I proposed a few options, but Gharesh-ri wasn't sold on any of them.\n\nTell me, what of Khamira and the source of the undead?

If you seek to enter this vault, I have a request. Several, in fact.\n\nI know how tiresome the pleas of strangers can be, and I have a low opinion of charity-work. I offer good pay for a dire situation. Interested in aiding the Fighters Guild?
Go ahead and have a look at the gravestone, would you? I'm curious to see what you make of it.

Hrrm. Another outsider comes to Elsweyr. As if we did not have enough problems between Abnur Tharn and the Dragons.\n\nAh, do not mind me. Great beasts rampaging through my homeland tends to put me in a foul mood.

You're responding to Abnur Tharn's letter? One of the promising adventurers? I hope you can help us.\n\nBut where are my manners? Welcome to Riverhold and the province of Northern Elsweyr, also known as Anequina. I am the Speaker of the Mane.
The war council has come to an agreement. It's time to take the battle directly to Rimmen.
Well, I suppose that could have gone better.
I'm lost in thought.
Greetings, walker. Forgive me if I seem sour. Ri'hirr strained his back climbing out of bed. Old age … it comes for all of us eventually.

So you have found the first piece of the Rithana-di-Renada. Impressive.\n\nBut Rajhin can't help but wonder if you have patience enough to find the other fifteen? After all, he has hidden them very well.

Please, don't mind the crowd. Izanji got a tad carried away when the mural was completed. He has invited wealthy nobles and merchants even from Pellitine in the south.\n\nWere you able to find the Singing Crystal?
Best to do as Rajhin's Shadow says, yes? It would not be wise to anger our unexpected guest.
Z'en's price! Maarselok's tough. We've got to take him out of the air to stand any real chance of hurting him. Keep helping Selene. If anyone can ground him, it will be her.
Alkosh's booming voice reaches farther with every passing day, bringing new pilgrims for me to greet! Come, bring your offerings and kneel before the Great Cat returned!
Ziss'vo! The constant nagging and judging and glowing and floating! This is why Saviwa avoids his family at all costs. Especially the undead ones.
This tomb is closer to our destination, but we move on. Jora-ri feels the Moons pulling his spirit. He hears his wife calling his name.
Cadwell should not have gone off without us. He's no match for a necromancer as powerful as Zumog Phoom.
Zamarak is pleased to see you are awake. You have slept for many days, and this one feared the worst.\n\nStill, it is not every day that one walks away from a Dragon attack.

Multiple Cadwells, necromancers, Dragons, and now Euraxian soldiers marching on Riverhold. This day just keeps getting better and better. \n\nRegardless, there's much to do and not a lot of time to do it.
I have a good feeling about this. Reminds me of the time I led an assault on Molag Grunda's dinner party. The roast Yaghra were delicious!

The great Tharn awaits you in Riverhold's K'har Zhab Hall. You will recognize him by his proud stance, his regal brow, and his penetrating eyes.\n\nAnd his air of authority. He wears it proudly like a Khajiit wears fur.
Did you find Marthine? Is he still alive?\n\nIf he's dead, I hope he succumbed to an awful illness. Peryite would want it that way.
Thank you, friend. Without your supplies and knowledge, we would never have made it out of Orcrest. We owe you our lives.
Hurry and unlock the door!\n\nI can't recruit more followers from the inside of this cage. Trust me, I've tried.
You blind fools. Only the Dark Behind the World awaits you now.
Ugh. Really should have seen that coming, Jakarn. Sneaky little bastard. Where did he even hide that gas bomb?\n\nYou know what, let's not think about that.
You showed spine when we spoke in Rimmen. We will see if your actions match your brave words, yes?
You return. Lightly singed, but no worse for the wear, eh?\n\nWhy do you come back to me? You have what you seek, yes?
No! Stay back! Don't touch me!

This one also hears that the Dragons gather near the Moon Gate as well. Bad times grow even worse, Lyrrsazhi fears.\n\nYou know, some believe an eclipse occurs when a Dragon eats the Moons. If that is the case here, I hope it chokes.
All right, we're in! Sugar-Belly and Milksop must be around here somewhere. Keep your eyes peeled.

Rigurt playing the lute of Frongeir the Giant is incomprehenstable! Is like holding Wuuthrad before it was shattered or drinking mead with Ysgramor himself.\n\nGet your drum, friend. It is time to become the stuffing of legends!
Welcome to Riverhold, friend. You should feel fortunate to have found the finest collection of cloth in all of Elsweyr. Let Thadarra know if you see anything you like.
What are you waiting for? Kill the dummy! It's not like it's going to kill itself. Or will it? Now you've got me thinking.
Look at you, scurrying around, lost as can be. Ever get a feeling like you're a rat in a maze? It's 'cause you are!
Jakarn! Where Jakarn? Stupid Breton! No tails to bite! None!
See if you can help Cadwell snap out of his latest vision. If he cannot break the connection, we may have to rely on more drastic means.
Don't be fooled by the Dragon's playful bravado. He's tasted our power and found it a bitter poison.\n\nWe must press our advantage while Maarselok is still off guard.

That went better than expected! Of course, I expected being ground to mush between a Dragon's teeth, so that's not much of a measure.\n\nGood work though, I got winded just watching you. Or maybe that was Selene's magic?
Hound. If that warlock believes he's tamed me, he's greatly mistaken.\n\nBe wary, Maarselok is leading us farther into his blight. He hopes to weaken us.

So much for … feeling like my old self again. It took every iota of energy I absorbed from the aeonstone, and all I accomplished was to wound the Dragon and drive it off.\n\nAnd now … I'm as used up and worthless … as an empty water skin.
Find the three glyphs in Othrenis. Let me mark the locations on your map, along with where I think the hidden tomb lies.\n\nI prepared notes as well. Feel free to take them with you.
You would think a life devoted to the Divines would make mother a bit more forgiving.\n\nWell? What did she say? Za'ji had trouble hearing your conversation from the other side of the gate.
Za'ji's rudeness aside, you cleansed the bell. Tadali will now perform the ritual and find the Dragon Yahgrondu, as promised. \n\nAnd then you and your companions will leave this temple, yes?
I never thought Za'ji would be so rude to his mother. When we get back to the sanctum, we're going to have words.
I'll never get used to a Dragon landing in front of me.
These Dragonguard sanctuaries, hidden for so long. How many more lie buried in the dust? How much knowledge remains lost to us?
The prospect of meeting Kaalgrontiid fills me with a mixture of excitement and dread. I want to see what happens when he experiences a blast from the Horn of Ja'darri.
Sai wishes to speak to you. There are plans to make before your next journey.
It is best just to calm him when he is like this. He is most confused when he is tired. Ka'ishka will put his mind at ease, she promises.\n\nBetter you speak to my sister right now.
This is not how Vijari imagined his journey would end, but he is ready to walk it.\n\nIf Vijari does not see you again. Thank you for coming this far with him.

My words … they are not enough, yes? You have done so much for my homeland. For me.\n\nGo to the Dragonguard Sanctum. Meet with the others. I wish to stay here a while longer. I will find you when I return.

You do not expect Zar to draw you a map, do you? Where is the fun in that? No, the tale must be relished, the adventure experienced. That is the way of momentous events.\n\nTake my claw and present it to the scion of Anequina. Just mind the skull.
I don't like the sound of any of this.\n\nThe more the Dragons destroy, the more desperate people become. And then the cult swoops in, promising protection and purpose. It's a never-ending cycle!
Before we can fight Laatvulon and his cult, we must learn all we can about them.
I'm not touching the remains of a Khajiit legend! You grab the claw.
See what this Dragon has to say, but be wary. I'll be prepared to strike if it moves against us.
The Darkness is seeping through this—this grotesque mural. Adara'hai cannot hold it back. We must snap Vijari out of the Bent Dance and go! Quickly!
You're on a hunt, yes? I'll join you.\n\nYou lead the way. I won't waste my time trying to decipher that mess of a map.
Oh! Greetings, walker. Apologies, but have we met before?
Many guards patrol Turo's warehouse, walker. Make sure you are ready, yes?
The next focal point is just up ahead. I can sense its power.

Talk to Nahfahlaar. See if he can shed any light on what happened up there at the end.\n\nAnd check in with the rest of the Dragonguard, if you have the time. They all want a moment with the hero of Dragonhold.
This one is sorry he missed all the action on Dragonhold. Za'ji expects to be part of the next assault on a floating island, yes?
This Dragonguard … it's good, but it needs work. Luckily, Sai Sahan has me to knock some sense into this sorry bunch.

When we saw the island begin to break apart, it was all I could do to stop Za'ji and Caska from leaping into the Pounce and sailing off to fish you out of the sea.\n\nCan you imagine, trying to navigate while parts of the island were raining down?
Why would she leave us? Lahini was our joy. We never thought of her as a burden.
The Shields stand ready to defend Senchal and Southern Elsweyr. I leave it to the Dragonguard to deal with the floating island.
Best to just walk away. I'm not in the mood to talk about that two-timing harlot.
Apologies, my father isn't usually this rude. I'm not sure what's gotten into him today.
Be gentle with the Perfect Pounce, yes? Za'ji doesn't want too much blood spilled on her! It stains the deck.
May the Dark Elf fill the belly of many hungry fish.
Blademaster Kasura awaits, wayfarer. Divines walk with you.
Let's get the bell and get out of this place.
Za'ji knew we could do it! And in record time, too.
What did the inscription tell you?
You have a distinctive scent, mask-bearer. It suits you.\n\nTalk to the Dragonguard. Find out why the letter he received unnerved him so.
This one hopes those Alfiq thieves get what they deserve for desecrating a masterpiece.
This is a bad idea.\n\nSoon as I step into that arena, every fighter will be on me like stink on a nix-ox. They all want a shot at Caska the Unconquered.
I think this is some kind of test. There's a shrine in each corner of the room, and those braziers look like they're part of a ritual.\n\nWhy don't you try lighting one?
You are with the Dragonguard, yes? Do you know who attacks our temple?

You are quite the patron of seedy port towns, aren't you? I jest. Who am I to judge?\n\nThis will be another challenging commission for us, though less dangerous than tangling with the Iron Wheel … or getting Velsa into a fancy dress.
You know, I never intended to come to Elsweyr. But now, looking out over these jungles and plains, I'm thinking it might be worth sticking around. For a little while, anyway.
Though Tadali can sense the winds of death, she is blind to your motives. Tell this one, Dragonguard. Why have you come?
What are you speaking with Sidura for? Sai Sahan is waiting for you back at the sanctum. You should head there at once.
Stay back, stranger. The shrines are shuttered and the sea waters stagnant and squalid.\n\nOr are you part of the syndicate, here to savage the Moonlit Cove?
Greetings, walker! Skordo says you helped him find us. A good thing, too. Skordo is brave and handsome, but prone to rash decisions. Not like Marekki!
I'll work with Captain Sai Sahan to formulate a plan of attack. We'll march north of Senchal as soon as we are able.
Thank you for everything, walker. Malahbu will admit, he had his doubts. But do not feel slighted. Malahbu has doubts about everything!
Whew! That was a close one.\n\nI wager we'll find ourselves in another pickle before long, but here's to today, eh? Cheers!
Speak to Nahfahlaar, my friend. He seems gravely injured.

Oh, friend, we were so worried! You were gone so long and we haven't been able to find the smuggler or the moon-sugar bound for Senchal.\n\nPlease tell me you had better luck. Even if you didn't, tell me anyway. I need some good news right now.
Why do we delay? We must … we must press on.
Is that truly Honoria? I haven't seen her since …. Speak with her, my friend. I haven't the words yet.
A Demon from the East, the Pride of Alkosh … what is mother going on about?
The Pride of Alkosh. Forgotten Manes who protect the threads of time, hidden away in this modest temple.
Let's hope Za'ji is still coherent. I'm sure he's so excited about his first Dragon kill he can barely think straight.
I did it! I convinced my father to join our cause. The Dragonguard now has the full support of the Shields of Senchal.\n\nBut what about your mission? Did you find the Mask of Alkosh?

Did you see the corpse, walker? A Dragon! Za'ji killed an actual Dragon!\n\nOh, the Moon-Singers will tell tales of our adventures for generations to come. Za'ji the Dragonslayer and his heroic associates!
