Maezi cannot believe she allowed these stinky smugglers to ambush us and take our cargo. This one is never so negligent in her duties, but Zhasim was so ….\n\nNever mind that now. Did you find the stolen moon-sugar?

Ha! You look like you've seen a ghost!\n\nOh, that business with Molag Bal, eh? Water under the bridge, Vestige. Breaking out of Coldharbour once is damn hard. Breaking out twice? Easier than you'd think. Anyway, chin up. We've got work to do.
It's strange for a Dragonguard to admit this, but Nahfahlaar has been invaluable to our mission thus far.\n\nLet's keep going.

Dragon spit's easy to come by. You won't even need to kill a Dragon to get it. Find somewhere a Dragon's attacked recently and look for any thing it might have gnawed on. They prefer to roast their meals so charred horse bones are a good bet.
So, what happened? Did you get too close? Did he attack you?
I wish we could have learned more before we killed Matron Urgala. I still don't understand what the coven has planned, and it's the not knowing that worries me.
Once my father understands that we have a way to protect against the harrowstorms, he'll have to take us seriously.\n\nLet's get back to the city as fast as we can.
Lyris will be all right. She's as strong as a mammoth and twice as mean.\n\nBut Svana, she was exposed to the full effects of the harrowstorm. Check on her while I finish up here.
Tell me … do I have a new scar?\n\nEnough with the coddling. Let's get back to the Blue Palace.
Brigvar! He's one of the people we thought we'd lost to the infection. He's injured, but he seems cured. I'll keep watch while you speak to him. We need to understand what happened here.
The information you brought back from Blackreach might give us a fighting chance.\n\nLet's put our heads together and figure out how to use what you learned—my father be damned!

The days are far too dull and dry since Svana started associating with the likes of you. Stop being a good influence and tell the lass to drown her troubles in a barrel of Orcish ale.\n\nI do so hate drinking alone.
Last we saw the captain and Drigsen, they were following tracks due east.
The Khajiit that took the captain has to be close.

The swordthane took the oil to Castle Dour. That's where all of the supplies for a siege are gathered during periods of strife.\n\nI pray that High King Svargrim receives the patience and wisdom required to see us through this crisis.
I don't have time for the princess's proclivities right now. The high king … we can barely keep up with the multitude of tasks.\n\nSo, speak quickly and let me get back to it.

Who are you? And why do you pursue me? First at Havil's farm and now you emerge unscathed from these accursed ruins. If Maxten sent you to bring me back to her, I won't go.\n\nEveryone should just stay away before I kill them as well.
Kyne give me strength! You better talk some sense into this fool before I cave in her skull.\n\nWe need to get into the palace and find Jorunn.
Well, friend of Svana? Are you as good as your word? Tell me what you discovered at the Morthal Barrow.
Fenn's been through a terrible ordeal. Go talk to him. And give him back his flask. It looks like he could use it.
We … we shouldn't remain here. \n\nYou go on ahead. I—I just need a moment.
The storm, it's fast approaching. There's no time to waste. Get the gate open now.
Unlock the gate and get to the top of the tower. Fenn and I will make sure the harrowfiends don't break through.
I failed Karthald once. I will not fail it again.\n\nI'll help Princess Svana get those who survived this atrocity safely to Solitude. I give you my word.
I fear the temple is lost. Our only hope lies in finding High Priest Varkour and Meridia's relic.
Queen Gerhyld needs to hear what we discovered at Kilkreath Temple. Hopefully, that will be enough for her to get us an audience with High King Svargrim.
I don't know a horker's arse from magic, but I know if you dam a river the lake dries up. Stopping the curse's source should have freed Bjora.\n\nLet's head back to that old tree and check on her.
Take Hafskjar to rescue Bjora and the others in the tower. I've got these two. We won't be drinking with Shor in Sovngarde this day, thanks to you.
Hmm … I remember your face. You spoke to me earlier.\n\nIt was like I was walking through a dream. Or a nightmare. What made it stop?
I don't know you. I don't want to know you. Get lost.
Remember: "A jewel of blue rules the view."

Tell Svana … tell her I'm here if she needs me. Of course, unless she wants to get tusk-faced drunk and wind up face-down in a ditch, I'm not sure what good I could do.\n\nAnyway, she's waiting for you at the Blue Palace.
Please move cautiously. Blood loss and grief make Shelaria … erratic. We really can't afford to take foolish risks in a tomb like this.
Just … give me a moment. I'll be ready when you need me.

So … you helped this one's sister, yes? Helped her find Adusa? You have the thanks of House Ravenwatch, walker. We have little to offer, but our memory is very long.\n\nNow, you killed that monster Essenia, yes?
Don't let this Nord off the hook until he tells us what we need to know.\n\nI know he was a captive, but I've got no patience for lies and equivocations. Unlike Count Verandis, my charity has limits.
Watch your step. Would hate for you to lose a foot when we've only just met.

I'm so sorry you had to see that. What a poor excuse for an assistant I am, a mere cat frightened me half to death!\n\nYou found something, didn't you? I think I need to collect myself, so I'll stay here and try to smooth things over with Elle.
My equipment isn't too far. Let's go retrieve my pack and find a safe place to analyze the residue we took from the witch pike.
Ah, hsst. Ever had a splinter you just couldn't work free? I can attest, they're much worse on the inside.
I—I'm not dreaming, right? You saw what I saw? I feel my ancestor's presence here.
We've got a good position here. Any Reachmen coming out of that hole won't get past us.\n\nDo what you can in there. I want the bridge to still be standing when this is finished.
Haven't seen the princess of Solitude in awhile.\n\nFunny, from what I've heard recently, I expected someone a little more … drunk.

Let's split up. Take a look around. Ask some questions. If the assassin passed through that ramshackle town, maybe someone saw him.\n\nCall out if you run into trouble, but don't make a move until we're all back together.
Remember to look for Vund's alchemical explosives. And if you see Ulang, please try to rescue him. If he gets hurt, I'll never forgive myself.
Go talk to Captain Hingrid. I'll make sure none of these bastards are still breathing.
Welcome back. Warm yourself by the fire and tell me about the reagents I requested.
Those witch pikes will be guarded, so be careful.

Thank you. For holding the line, I mean.\n\nI'm ready to do what I should have done a long time ago, to do what my father never could. I'll speak with the Skald-King. There's one more thing I'd like you to do while I entertain our guests.
You did it. I shouldn't be surprised, but things were looking rather bleak before the clouds parted.
Good to see you. Now work your magic before I have to teach these western Nords some manners.
Go on and talk with this eastern loud-mouth before there are two empty thrones today.
So this is the Skald-King? He's not the prancing dandy I expected, but if he wants a fight we will give it to him.
I know that there's little love between east and west, but now's not the time to be picking a fight.
It seems Princess Svana takes after her mother. That bodes well for the people of Solitude.
Where's Viggol? What's become of my husband?
See what you can find. There has to be something here that will point us in the right direction.

No one enters the mines! Least of all, some outsider.\n\nI'm not about to let Chief Urzikh endanger the entire stronghold by opening these gates. If she wants to cut me down, so be it! I'll die in service to the clan.

This isn't your business, stranger. Mauloch's jawbone, how did you even get in here?\n\nUgh. Doesn't matter. I've got this insubordinate worm to deal with. My people are trapped in the mine and need help. If he doesn't fall in line, it's his funeral.
Begone from here, outsider. I don't want your pity.\n\nI will take my punishment. If the chief demands the Blood Price, then I will pay.
<Pickle whines softly.>
I stand by my wife … no matter what the outcome.
Thank you for getting as many of us out as you did. Our people owe you a debt. \n\nWe have the luxury of fighting about who's right or wrong now because we're alive—thanks to you.
Remember, we're looking for a chillwind mushroom, deep lichen, and an unfertilized chaurus egg.\n\nBe on your guard. More dwells in the depths than just giant insects!
What are you staring at? Never seen a Nord hurl curses at a bunch of wretched bastards?

Thanks. There's no telling what's in there, and knowing Raynor, he'll wander into the wrong end of a blade while he's busy taking notes. \n\nI'll meet you inside as soon as I make sure nothing else out here is going to sneak up on us.
Don't worry about me getting underfoot. Kireth will have my head if I try to toddle after you, and I've no interest in entering the fray anyway.

If you want to save your companions, find those components I listed!\n\nBut be careful. The distortions are bringing all kinds of strange creatures from across Tamriel and beyond to this very spot! Be prepared for anything. And I mean anything.

You there! Don't run off screaming, there's a perfectly reasonable explanation for this.\n\nIt's rather humiliating, but my soul is trapped inside this ludicrous child's toy. I need someone with a corporeal form to help return me to my body.
Keep your wits about you, assistant. Dwemer technology is at best, unpredictable.\n\nAt worst? Perilous. In the extreme.
Let's keep moving. Morokei's tomb must be in the deepest part of the ruin.
Come on, let's get inside before anyone spots us!
More farmers and herders than fighters in Haafingar these days. Feh.
Thane Svyne loves Rigurt's cooking! Now, see if he will attend Rigurt's meeting, dear aide!
I can't believe you killed that thing. A Sea Giant!\n\nJust be careful, eh? Lord Falgravn will take notice. We've avoided his gaze so far. We should try to keep it that way for as long as possible.
So you found Freiwen alive did you? An unexpected, but welcome turn of events. We may yet be able to save her.\n\nWhat did you bring me from the ruins? I must know more about the necromancer's plans.
You shame yourself by cavorting around with these mindless street performers.
Please hurry and do what Mjolen asked of you. We must save my daughter. I refuse to let her suffer alone.

Can't believe that sneaky skeever gave me the slip. He won't do it again. Even if he does, so what? We break enough equipment and steal his research it won't matter if Arkasis escapes.\n\nHope Fennorian has better luck understanding these notes though.
I've never claimed to be above revenge. In fact, I kind of enjoy it. In moderation, obviously. Can't get too carried away.\n\nAnyway, I'm glad Talfyg's dead.
You've got weapons? Armor? Good … consider yourself conscripted.

Blackreach. If I were a little younger, I'd love to go with you. Do a little exploring. Ah, well.\n\nI suppose I'll stay here in the palace. Work on how to create more of the elixir once we know it's safe.
If the high king plans to stay on his throne, then he needs to lead. This inaction is infuriating! If he won't do something, then he should step aside. And the sooner, the better!

Hey, you found my master's book!\n\nYou should have heard him caterwauling about it a few hours ago. I told him I couldn't make sense of it, but boy was he mad. Good luck sorting it out. I'll be here when you get back. Promise.

It sounds like my dearest Fennorian suffered greatly at Tzinghalis's hands. Please, make sure he's all right before he rushes off into the next bit of danger.\n\nHe's too brave for his own good sometimes. Oh, but don't tell him I said that!
"What did this note say?" he asked, expecting a ludicrous response ….

For years, I gave prayers and offerings to the animal spirits that my family has honored for generations, expecting their blessing in return.\n\nAnd then this idiot throws a smelly mushroom in the river and catches my family's ancient quarry.
Remember what I said. If any harm comes to that book, you will not enjoy the consequences.

I wish I could join you in there. Killing this monster is all I've thought about for thirty years. I've lost my friends, farm, and legs chasing this thing. But, if this is the end it'll be worth it.\n\nKill it for my brother. Please.
You have the knack, that much is certain. Membership in the Antiquarian Circle is yours, should you desire it.\n\nSo? What is your decision?

Ah, you're here! Don't worry, I have your pay. I'm just finishing my notes. \n\nThough, if I'm being honest, I'm not as confident as I once was that my theory is correct. How can I really know that my spell worked?

Oh, it's you! What a welcome surprise! By Mara, that business with Angof feels like lifetimes ago. I'm glad to see you're still in good health.\n\nSo, Verita gave you an Antiquarian's Eye, eh? You mean to join the Antiquarian Circle?
Your friend … do you think he made it out?
Queen Gerhyld, dead? Is it true? Oh, these are dark days, indeed.

Such madness! The queen dead, murderers running free. Where's High King Svargrim in all this? Probably up in his ugly tower again!\n\nThe high king doesn't lift a finger while our city crumbles around us!
Did you hear? A strange storm killed all the priests at Kilkreath Temple! That's what happens when you fool around with the Daedra, mark my words!

You're not sick, are you? Be careful, if you hang around Tranya and her kind long enough, that might change. I'm truly sorry, but we can't risk letting anyone in. It's too dangerous. \n\nWe can't have more people getting sick.

Wow, you're the last person I expected to see down here. But, you have impeccable timing!\n\nAdusa's in trouble. You remember her, right? One of the vampires of the Ravenwatch. From Rivenspire? Anyway, she entered Greymoor Keep and hasn't returned.
We've wasted enough time in here. Come on, let's get moving.
What, you got more bad news or you just want to bother me for the fun of it?
Damn you and that idiot! Feeding me powdered hagraven squeezings … are you trying to kill me?\n\nAnd yet, by the Gods, that taste, the aroma! I can't get it out of my mind. It's haunting!
The meat's not curing correctly … these damn Nords wouldn't know a salted hock from a mammoth's stones. Probably tastes just as bad.

With my cure in circulation, those that brave the journey to freedom will be safe from the affliction. Dark Moon Grotto will continue to serve as a safe haven for weary refugees.\n\nWe could not have done this without your help. Thank you.

Hedrynne isn't well. A chaurus bit her, one of those giant cave bugs.\n\nThe bite of a chaurus, it carries an acidic poison. Very deadly. I don't think she's going to last much longer. Perhaps you can help us? Please, talk to my brother, Hamvir.
An outsider walking alongside the great and powerful Arana? That's not a sight I thought I'd see today. And she says you're an ally?\n\nTell me, outsider, why do you care what happens to the Reach?
That letter. Please tell me it's just an old to-do list or something, and not actually proof that the man I trusted with my life was involved with the Gray Host.
We're not done yet, my friend. This old vampire still has a few tricks up his sleeve.
The key to freeing the tortured shade lies in the manipulation of the dark energy. Rotate the void crystals until the containment field collapses.
If we can get my sister to talk to us, we can determine why the old prophecy is of such interest to Lady Belain.

Death was once a part of my clan's rituals. Long ago, we sacrificed enemies and innocents alike in these halls to receive the Spirit Queen's blessing. But to kill one of our own?\n\nWe need to find Nathari and the rest of my clan before it's too late.
By Tu'whacca's mercy! It's you! I am sorry, I did not recognize you in the shadows. \n\nIs Fennorian with you? No … you are alone. What adventure makes our paths cross again, my friend?
In order to stop the Darkstorm and save the Reach—perhaps all of Tamriel—I must enter Rada's sanctuary realm and take control of the ritual.\n\nIt's the only option.
That took a lot out of Verandis. I hope we got what we needed. \n\nTalk to him and see how he's doing.
I've seen a lot of things, but never anything like that.\n\nSee if the count learned anything useful. And make sure he's all right. He's not looking too good.
As fascinating and exhilarating as that was, I'm worried about Count Verandis. Please, see if he's all right.
So long as Ard Caddach rules this city, the Stonehands will support him.

Verandis has been studying that dark energy down in the Library of Arkthzand. Trying to figure out what Rada al-Saran and Lady Belain have planned. He thinks it might actually be related to the Darkness—the Void!\n\nIsn't that a terrifying thought?

The Dark Heart. A piece of the primal Void trapped in our world. No wonder it warps the very weave of existence all around it.\n\nLook up. We're directly beneath the Library of Arkthzand. The Dark Heart, it powers the orrery. But to what end?

I started looking for information about the Gray Host and discovered that my mentor had a hand in their creation.\n\nVerandis may have kept his past a secret, but at least we know he opposed their plans for conquest. He wasn't a part of their war.
I'll let you and Gwendis conclude your business. Then she and I will have a long talk.
You go on ahead. Fenn and Gwendis could use a moment. I'll make sure they make it to Markarth safely.
The shaman thinks you should be the one to present yourself to the spirits, and I agree.\n\nGo ahead. Once you stand before the ritual pyre, the wards will be restored.
The land, it sighs in relief. Whatever you and Fialyn did, it made everything whole again, I can feel it.
Freyleth claims that guard had to die, but I know her. She has never been able to control her impulses. \n\nTalk to Kathad. Tell him what you found in the Blinds and see how he wants to proceed.
What are you doing still talking to me, scamp? An Undaunted doesn't flap their lips! An Undaunted performs daring deeds while dungeon delving!\n\nSo, get out there and prove yourself, scamp!
Your arrival is fortuitous, as I have only just returned myself.\n\nWere you able to make contact with the rebels? Did you meet with Arana?
Hurry to Markarth. Warn Caddach of the danger he faces.\n\nAnd stop Belain and the Gray Host at any cost!

If you hadn't shown up, I don't know what we were going to do. Verandis and I, well, we didn't have enough hands to turn off that damn machine. Who makes something that requires three people to turn it off?\n\nDamn Dwarves ….

There you are! After all your talk, I was beginning to think you abandoned us.\n\nThe Gray Host raided my city. Killed more of my people than I like, but we held them off. Barely. Now those bastards are gathering in Nchuand-Zel for their next attack.
I hope that fits. With the rest of the servants already upstairs attending to the party, this was the best we could acquire.
Find Arana. Then I'll talk to you and the noble. Not a moment before.

The Gray Host came out of nowhere. Hit the city like a giant's hammer. Vampires and werewolves, rending and killing anyone they could catch.\n\nThe ard's folk thought they were safe in Markarth. Only fools put their trust in walls.
Is that the darkcap mushroom? No, no. You hold onto it. Really, I insist.\n\nTalk to Kathad. He'll tell you what we need you to do.
Not even this gloomy, old, stone keep can dampen my spirits. My dreams hold true. Markarth is alive with joy.\n\nBut you didn't approach to listen to me. What is it you wanted?
Ah, there you are. I hope you don't mind. I got a bit … sidetracked.\n\nSai and I were just catching up. Swapping stories of our travels with you, actually.

If you'd said only yesterday I'd play host to Nord rulers from across all of Skyrim, I'd have told you the dead would live again before that happened … and here we are—a day of miracles!\n\nTell me truthful, you had a hand in all this, aye?
So you're the partner that Lyris speaks so highly about. I'm glad to know she had such a stalwart ally during her time in Western Skyrim.\n\nIt is an honor to meet you.
These hills are Reach hills, outsider. Keep walking.

We're beneath the barrow. Reachfolk occupied this place long before the Nords came along and built a tomb over it. My ancestors were the first to sink their roots into this land.\n\nI feel something here … an emptiness, a darkness farther down.

Hey, you're an outsider. I guess when the ard made us put up those scratchings he called signs, it really worked. Attracted you right to my business.\n\nUnfortunately, we're closed right now. Come back later. And bring your gold!
Well, that was a pretty display.\n\nSay what you will about Hircine, but he's definitely got an eye for spectacle!
Shaman Ulvoch told you to offer yourself at the pyre again, did he? Go on, the ritual will work this time. We have to trust what we did was enough.
I hate places such as this. No birdsong, no fragrant breeze, and not a whispering creek to be heard. Just dead stone and stale air.\n\nLet's find the keystone and get out of here.

Between the Ravenwatch's expertise and Arana's knowledge of the Reach, we have a fighting chance against the Gray Host.\n\nJust stay mindful. Even sealed by a Daedric ritual, this alliance remains young and fragile. We must nurture it.

Curious. An outsider approaches. So rarely do we see one enter these Hollows. What could you seek? A challenge? Wish to test your strength against the spirits?\n\nTell us, outsider, what do you know of the Vateshran's Rites?
Keep searching, my friend. Rada and Lady Belain must be somewhere inside this library.

We must return the relic to its rightful place. Deactivate any Dwemer amplifiers so they can't exacerbate the tonal magic's effect, and I'll handle the transportation spell … at least, I think I will.
Didn't you hear? You and that fancy bastard aren't welcome here. Get, or I'll make a scarf out of your guts!
We can't let them destroy everything. Anything that we can save, we should. All this knowledge! I could read these books for years.
I'm sorry I wavered. This adventuring and danger … it's all brand new to me. So much death.\n\nBut I have faith in you. I know together we can find my father and get him to safety.

Should you find the Old Life shrine, a truly beautiful tradition awaits you. The written message gives form to our most personal thoughts. And burning them connects us through the flame to Aetherius. \n\nMight I ask you another favor, too?
The free clans of the Reach will never be safe until that tree is burned to the ground.
Roar … soar … what are these verses trying to tell us?\n\nThere must be another verse. Let's keep looking.

The first champion of Hircine falls! Thick bark and vines can't stop a true warrior.\n\nWe of the Reach value Hircine's lessons. Mastery of the hunt keeps us alive in the wilderness. Plus, it's fun! Outsiders could learn a lot from his teachings.
It's a song. Burn away more of that foliage, partner, and reveal the rest of the words.
Every moment that tree stands is a moment the Thornroot Hagravens can use to create a new briarheart.

Of course, now that I resolved to talk to them about my feelings, I have to actually figure out what I'm going to say.\n\nI feel like I can do this, though! Perhaps that heroic confidence of yours has rubbed off on me. Well, a little bit.
The ritual has to work this time. Please, help us finish it.
Good. You had me worried for a moment there, outsider.\n\nNow go. It's time we present the couple to their chiefs. Then we can put this whole business behind us.
The chief-of-chiefs looks angry. Whatever you did, outsider, tread carefully. If called to, I will bring the might of the Eagleseer clan down on your head.
Well, that was interesting. I'm not sure what's happening, but at least it's different.
If my chief-of-chiefs wills it, the Six-Ford will hunt you down. Take care, the next time you speak with her, outsider.
I heard you mention Madearn. Please, whatever you're planning, don't make him suffer.
The word of a Reachfolk isn't something you can just take back. Whether or not our love is true … Drisene is depending on me. \n\nI will think about what you ask. But I promise nothing.
It's now or never, outsider. Whatever happens next … you have my thanks. Always.

Passions do not die easily. It was too much to hope, maybe, that the chiefs would see the reason for the feud was simple foolishness.\n\nBut the way Eslyn and Madearn worked together today … it gives me hope for the future of these clans.
Something brings you to this sacred place, outsider. I sense your desire for knowledge. Speak and tell me what song you seek.
Arana's our king, queen, and clan-witch combined. So, mind your tongue or we'll cut it out.
For a third time, the wandering hunter graces this hall. Welcome. \n\nWhat tidings do you bring this time?

Ah, you showed. When I received Angair's message, I thought for sure he jested. A stranger from beyond the Reach would never agree to partake in the Vateshran's Rites.\n\nAnd yet, here you stand. Are you certain you want to do this?
They said Verandis was imprisoned in the Void, but he's here!\n\nForgive Adusa. You must be the one Gwendis and Fennorian spoke of. This one is honored to meet you.

Enter the now-accessible north wing and look for more floor plates. One of them must open the main doors.\n\nAnd take the remaining duplicates with you. Goodness knows Stibbons excels at standing in one place. Is it any wonder the duplicates do, too?

You and the long-haired dryskin must set things right. I do not know how, for we have no interest in the place of stone. You and the long-hair must figure this out.\n\nGo quickly. And know that, succeed or fail, Sithis will have us all in time.

I'm worried about Calia. Twins are close by nature, but growing up in that vault of theirs? Calia and Destron only had each other. I think you'd better check on her. Sombren, too.\n\nCome back when you're done. Keshu and I want to talk to you.
Forgive me, but I have a lot to think about.\n\nWe can talk some more later, all right?
I'll rally the Ivory Brigade here in Leyawiin and we'll meet you at Fort Redmane.\n\nWe'll stop Vandacia and his cultists. We have to.

Into the fort, mercenary. Stay with the Ambitions until you are needed. If Vandacia's army attacks, we will do all we can to stop them out here. But if Vandacia sneaks anyone past us, you must serve as the final line of defense.\n\nGood luck!

Commander Ortin won't listen. He insists that Councilor Abor gave him strict orders. Said she wasn't to be disturbed. You talk to Ortin and try to convince him.\n\nAnd I'm not sure why the servant is in an uproar. Something about a meal and his sister?

Go on. The portal will safely take you to a point near the marked location on the map. I shall follow along after I try to unravel the magic securing the Emperor's scroll.\n\nDo hurry. We don't want the cultists to ransack any caches before we do.
If you receive another invitation, or maybe just get bored, you're always welcome to come take a stab at King Boar!
Your timing really is impeccable. We've already packed up my records and were about to head out.\n\nBut what news of the other councilors? Did your warnings reach them in time?
My husband, Councilor Sophus, should return soon. You're welcome to wait. Or you can come back later, if you prefer.
That must be Arbitrator Gavos—who else could it be—but how? How could anyone survive imprisoned like this for so long?\n\nCould you speak with him? I feel faint.

If we destroy the Idol of Xulunaht, no matter how much death they have wrought, the Sul-Xan will not be able to summon their dark spirit.\n\nWe must find it and keep it from hurting anyone ever again.

Bloodrun Cave is a dangerous place, whether the Dark Brotherhood is present or not. You and Eveli should be on your guard at all times. Watch out for each other. I would hate to lose operatives as valuable as you two have been.

They're holding their own for the moment, but your army's taking a pounding. They were definitely not prepared to deal with a Daedric Prince the size of a tower.\n\nWhatever you're going to do, do it fast.

Gideon and Governor Keshu have worked with Leyawiin to keep Blackwood safe. I have every reason to believe that she will cooperate and tell you what she knows about the Argonian term, ojel-bak.\n\nMay the Divines walk beside you, mercenary.
Vandacia wants my power? Fine. I'll burn him to a cinder with it! Mark my words!
So? Will Councilor Abor be returning with you to Leyawiin? Am I finally going to be able to get my fort back in order?

We don't have much time if we're to save Drathas's people. And if I don't uphold my end of the deal, I fear the bargain may be void. And I need that lockbox.\n\nSo we should stop babbling and move on.
Go on. Show the scroll to Beragon. You can trust him and he's very good at deciphering coded messages.

If you want to slip past the Painted Eye undetected, you'll have to get into Borderwatch through its sewer. It drains into a ravine to the east.\n\nAnd you should know—you're not the first volunteer to try this. No idea what happened to the last.
Just once, it would be nice if Quistley showed some … appreciation … for having his chestnuts hauled out of the fire.\n\nI don't think he understands how much danger he was in.
See, I knew Seeks would let me stick around if I wore him down enough!

Right. I don't make a habit of diving feet first into trouble … but there's nothing good happening down there, and it's going to get worse the longer we wait.\n\nSo get in there. I'll be close behind—swear to Sithis.

Finally, proof of Phalevon's legend! I'll be the talk of Gideon once I bring these trophies home.\n\nAnd yet … I wonder. Did the Goblins here cause their own troubles by meddling with Phalevon's horn? Or is it dangerous to just keep around?
Did you get Sombren settled into the temple? Did you introduce him to the twins?
Damn her! Xynaa betrayed us and cast us into the Spidernest!
Is it wrong that I suddenly want to see another vision? There's so much that Destron and I don't know about ourselves. Maybe we're finally going to get some answers.
Vandacia … he performed the rituals that gave us our powers. And all for the glorification of a Daedric Prince?\n\nI think I may be ill.

We were looking for a pile of clouded glass and instead we found a limitless font of unstable magicka! Shame we have to destroy it. But let's be honest, I would have found a way to accidentally destroy it before long.\n\nAre you ready to save Tiras?
Quistley turns out to be exactly what I expected. Imagine my surprise.\n\nTalk to him and Bastian for a moment. I need to think about how we can resolve our little impasse.

So, Revus pins his failure on some disruptive anomaly. Ludicrous. There's only one thing standing in the way of the experiment's success—Revus's diminutive intellect.\n\nNevertheless, I am the student. Let's … let's get on with our search.
May Jad'zirri interest you in a jug of the freshest—no—the finest—er—the strongest swill our King Boar could ever ask for?
It seems I've finally paid my penance to Zenithar for letting this glorious place crumble. Oh, so many years, alone. But I never gave up.

Your Dark Elf friend watches me with no small amount of suspicion. Perfectly understandable, but I am not a slave to my hunger. \n\nWhy are you wandering around Deepscorn Hollow, anyway? The Daughter of Sithis is fond of sacrificing strangers.

While Governor Keshu takes care of Destron and Calia, we need to determine our next move. I wonder if Captain Rian has any news about Vandacia.\n\nOh, I almost forgot! Keshu mentioned that a courier arrived for us. They're waiting to deliver a message.

I've had people come to me for their ails. Looking for herbs and medicines, but … I've never had to see them suffer. Watch them die. Give my condolences to their kin.\n\nI wasn't prepared for any of this.

Councilor Vandacia … a traitor and a Daedric cultist … I can't believe he had us all fooled for so many years.\n\nBut that's a matter for another time. Eveli tells me you have a lead for finding these so-called Ambitions.
Ugh. Isn't this always the way? You find the man of your dreams, but it turns out he's the lost soul of a man your ancestor poisoned in a fit of passion two-hundred years ago.\n\nJust my luck.

So, what did we learn?\n\nCouncilor Abor was frightened, but that's understandable. Interesting that she was burning documents. Her journal indicated that she knew more than the others. And Talaise visited the pantry before heading to the watchtower.
Look around this chamber and see what you can learn. I wish to study these mortals for a few more moments. I sense … something ….
Come, friend. We must find the great fallen Shadowscale's remains and make sure to destroy them. The flat-toothed deviant will not use them.
Lady Yisara seems overwhelmed. I regret that I must place this burden on the woman I adore.\n\nWon't you help her along? She trusts you.

Has speaking with Cres convinced you, one way or another? I am growing fonder of sponsoring them for the House by the moment, but—I'll admit—I can be a hopeless romantic at times.\n\nWhat do you think we should do with Cres?
Well, she certainly acts like Annyce. I'll be keeping my eye on her all the same.

So, working with the mummers. They may seem strange, but you're safer resting at their camp than at the inn—not to say Bradon runs a poor establishment, mind, there's just strangeness afoot in our little village.

The frog pool. That's where the Nereid first transformed my brother. It's a bit farther into the ruins.\n\nOnce Deet-Loh starts singing, the other frogs are sure to join in. That should appease Sister of Pools.

I'm sorry I wasn't with you in Gideon when you confronted that Dark Brotherhood agent. Still, why did the assassin murder the servant at Fort Blueblood? The Dark Brotherhood never kills anyone without a contract.\n\nI'm very confused right now.
We will all be safer inside the walls of Leyawiin Castle. And Councilor Lovidicus must be made aware of these latest developments.\n\nI will gather my personal guard and meet you there.
I just want to celebrate victory with the Captain once before this is all over. Maybe steal a kiss before I go.

Welcome, welcome to our little shop on—wait a moment. I know you! Are you following me? I've had clients grow accustomed to my wares, but never has someone tracked me down from place to place.\n\nAre you with the young Wood Elf? How may I assist you?
Yes! Please! I didn't mean to cause any trouble. I won't cause anymore trouble.
Let's search around and see if we can get a look at Vandacia's surprise before he parades it before these corrupt nobles.\n\nOh, hey, look! Is that Lyranth? What's she doing here?
The letter said that death was the key. So, go and unlock the creepy black door!

Ah, you look strong and capable! I could use your help.\n\nTensions between my tribe and the Imperials who've set up camp nearby are close to a breaking point. While I often solve issues with my wamasu-like strength, I fear it will not be enough here.
If only they'd listen to me! I need to get out of here, my people are obviously in danger as well.
That shout! What's going on out there?
I knew I felt something strange. Like glass shattering in the distance.\n\nWho are you and why have you disrupted the wards?
Our quick wit and fierce determination will see us through, I know it. We will get to the bottom of this dark crime and find the one responsible.\n\nI will be right behind you!
Well? We won't get any closer to answers standing here. Let's see where that portal leads.

Don't feel too badly for <<1>>. She got me good last month when she swapped my milk drink with glue! I cursed her as soon as I could open my mouth.\n\nDrenching her in slime is a fair act of revenge! And it's hilarious!

I appreciate your willingness to help, outsider, but you must understand … Heem-Jas has a strong heart, but he often invents problems in order to test his heroism. \n\nThis matter with the Imperials is likely simpler than he insists.

Go meet Heem-Jas in the Northern Swamps. If he must continue his investigation, at least keep him safe while he does so.\n\nWho knows how many Imperials might lie in ambush waiting to claim another victim?
She's back. She's safe. It feels like I've pulled my heart from a vice. Sorry I troubled you with another of Annyce's tantrums.
I can't believe I fell for that ruse. You'd think my acorn just dropped out of its tree.
These are troubled times, but so far the Three Banners War has stayed out of Blackwood. I hope you're not one of those who has ideas about bringing it here.
The old ones say this town used to thrive. Our Hist was once healthy and proud. No more, though. Feels like we near the end.
Even in the daylight, the marsh throws shadows and holds mysteries. Be cautious as you travel.

So instead of agreeing to help us outright, Elossi sends us through the swamp for her daggers. She is a legendary hero. Could she just, I don't know, sneak around and get them herself?\n\nExcept—oh, I get it now. This is a test of our worth.

No response? I suppose Meer-Ta was right. This is the worst I have ever seen Otumi-Ra get. Maybe this is what happens when the life of the party no longer has something to celebrate.\n\nLet us see—wait! I have an idea on how to snap him out of it.
I have to know that I can trust those I go into battle with.
This group is nothing but ants on the bark of a great Hist. Breaking them won't be difficult at all.
You are headed into dangerous territory. I have reports of suspicious activity at some nearby ruins. You another adventurer looking for trouble?
This is it! We're going to save Liam and stop Xigira's plot here and now.\n\nLet's find the ritual's focal points and weaken it so we can set him free.
Less talking, more killing! Go, go!
Please, my wife risked her life to get us help. If there's any chance you can save Bevene, I beg you.
These monsters have been working us non-stop. I was this close to breaking before you showed up … but I would have taken one or two with me.
With moves like that, the Daedra doesn't stand a chance!\n\nYes, I'd say we're ready to set out.

The door ahead leads to a chamber under the xanmeer. Once inside, we can climb to the peak, where I believe Bahsei waits.\n\nBe cautious as we continue. I cannot predict what other powers these Sul-Xan possess.

We do not have many warriors left. Barely enough to hold this section of the city. If the Sul-Xan wanted, they could crush us at any time.\n\nIt seems they have what they want. I doubt they even consider us a threat.

If you get us a ledger, I'm certain we can put it to good use.\n\nRumor has it the Fang-Furls have a bookkeeper, Lirar Droth, who lives in town. I'd wager you could find a ledger in his home. It's just around the corner, across from the bridge.
I have my orders. No one is allowed into the watchtower without the express permission of Commander Ortin.

Sorry for keeping you waiting. I'm sure uncovering murderous cults and meeting your grandmother's ghost is run-of-the-mill fodder for you. But for me, this is a bit much to take.\n\nI guess there was something to those dreams after all ….
I've been all over Stormhaven, but somehow I never seemed to spend any time in Wayrest. The Silvelles occasionally traveled here, but not with me. Now I know why.

I remember you. It's fortunate that you're here. I have some information that may make Bastian angry, even though it's not my fault. \n\nHowever … I need help with a personal matter first. Perhaps a deal is in order?
The Winds have always protected us from threats that lay beyond the Stonewastes. Assembling what is left of them is our only hope.
Be cautious on the roads. Something dark is brewing in Leyawiin.
I wonder what Sombren and Calia want in some old ruin? And should they be wandering around on their own? There might still be Waking Flame cultists out there!
The Ivory Brigade will protect Leyawiin. It's what we were formed to do, after all.

Go ahead, just release that handsome little fellow right over the volcanic vent. He'll know what to do. \n\nI'll use his natural energy to guide this calming ritual. Nature can be willful, but it can also be coaxed so long as it is respected.

I thank you, stranger! Those slavers intended to demand a ruinous ransom for my return. Whether they meant to honor their word is another question entirely.\n\nLet's be on our way before more of them find us.

Now that we are out of immediate danger, I will say it is good to see you again. I only wish it was under better circumstances.\n\nI have good news, however. I deciphered the code in the documents you recovered.
Don't you dare lose that thing or I'll throttle you.
The Black Fin awaits you at the governor's mansion in Gideon. May the mud warm your toes as you travel.
I still can't believe it's over. You did what I couldn't … or wouldn't. I'm fortunate you came along.
This is a special place, traveler. Please take care not to disturb the remains that rest here.
A decision must be made. In this time of strife, do we remain overly cautious and refuse to act? Or should we recruit a powerful ally with intimate knowledge of Dagon's forces and the Deadlands?
I'm impressed. You return from Doomvault Porcixid and don't seem the slightest bit shaken.\n\nWe could use someone like you in the Black Fin Legion.
Why are you both watching me like hawks? I said I was sorry.
Find the trees bearing the rune-markings of Oblivion. The stone will do the rest.\n\nI am in no shape to fight alongside you. I'll stay out of sight, but I won't be far behind.
Greetings, traveler. Please, conduct yourself properly within these walls. This is a special place.
I don't have any business with you, stranger. \n\nWhat, can't a girl sit in a cemetery by herself?

It's worse than I ever could have imagined. This vast collection of items from Oblivion are seeping their energy into everything around them. All these chaotic forces are warping the world in unpredictable ways.\n\nWe can't leave things as they are.

That creature had the sense to flee. Did it value its life, or was it protecting the power it had siphoned away from this vessel?\n\nEither way, if we continue to destroy these Agonymium Stones it'll reduce the threat they pose.

Words flow and ebb. I wish I had a thousand buckets. Perhaps then I could collect all the stories up, put them in jars. \n\nNo. Water must flow. It must be ever changing. One cannot contain such things. It changes their very nature, does it not?
I can think of nothing good coming of leaving all of these artifacts in mortal hands. I am loathe to admit it, but helping Weylin cleanse this mess may be … necessary.

Now that we can confer in the relative safety of Madam Whim's establishment, tell me what you discovered on the Isle of Joys. Did the spirit of Emperor Moricar speak true? Is there a weapon that can be used against Mehrunes Dagon?

Pibiha's hare-brained adventures have gotten her into trouble in the past, but being kidnapped to the Brandfire Reformatory? If Pibiha is unharmed, this one may just maim her herself.\n\nPlease, find out what has happened to her.

Excellent. The effigy now radiates with the call of the Evergloam. \n\nHurry, place the effigy at a shrine. It will pull the Evergloam closer to our realm and the Crowborne Horror with it. Once the rift opens, enter it and defeat the creature.

What a mess. Martus would have gotten us all killed if not for you, unleashed that monstrous thing on the world and left the stain of this place to fester.\n\nHe can't get away with his part in this, but I'm worried that he will.
Lyranth … she took the power of the Ambitions. \n\nBut we defeated Dagon. The egonymic worked. I feel like I can finally breathe again.
I hope the Anchorite knows what to do with that strange relic. You found it in that chest in the vault, right?\n\nSombren was so enraged that he couldn't access it, but he never told me why.

We have done well, little mortal. The cataclysts are destroyed, Sister Celdina and Nokvroz are gone, and the Anchorite has learned her identity. It will take her some time to sort through her memories, but she is safe. You have seen to that.

So you're the mortal adventurer the Dread Lady seeks? I assumed you'd be, well, taller. Still, my mistress knows best.\n\nI bring you a message from Lyranth, the lovely and powerful Dremora. Hear the words her prophet speaks and be enthralled.
Are you ready to go explore the Isle of Joys?

Mortals. Always so unpredictable. As annoying as that is, perhaps that's what keeps me so interested.\n\nYou and Eveli head to the Isle of Joys. See what you can find there. I will follow the Anchorite. I want to keep an eye on Sombren.

The Ravener's hunt could end here. But my clan, my family. Because they still exist inside that orb, I still have Atrozu. These last remnants of them keep him alive.\n\nIf we destroy this, I lose them for good. And Atrozu leaves with them. But I live.

It's what the velvet pouch contains that matters. I'm still attempting to ascertain its purpose, but since the Dagonists want it, it must be important.\n\nMy coffer rests on the nearby pedestal. Check on it while I examine this accursed blade.

The potion of disguise is ready. It contains the ingredients you gathered, a few components of my own design, and just enough bits of the dead cultist to enhance the illusion. Take a heaping scoop from the cauldron and drink up, little mortal!
Stay alert, little mortal. The Dagonists are more dangerous than they appear.
I'll see this through, my friend, come what may.
You are my captor and I am your prisoner, little mortal. Remember that and play your role or we will both meet an unfortunate fate.\n\nNow, let's look around and find the cult's meeting place.
Lyranth awaits you in the Marbruk Outlaws Refuge.\n\nNow hurry. Every moment you delay brings us one step closer to ruin and disaster.
The charged lucents need to go in both of the discharge labrums. That should ignite the furnace.

Rynkyus and I will guard this place. Make sure nothing follows you to Deadlight. You can handle whatever awaits you in that shattered plane. \n\nJust gather what information you can and deal with Sister Celdina. And keep an eye on the Anchorite.

We—we did it! They're free! I can't believe this. After Mehrunes Dagon cut them both down outside the Temple and then trapped them in the Sever—unable to move on—it was too long. Thank the Three. And you! Especially you, Magician!

So they forced Elegian to have visions and create the cataclyst. As part of some deal between the Longhouse Emperors and Mehrunes Dagon.\n\nBut where Moricar wanted to ensure that his heirs ruled the world, Celdina wants to see the world destroyed.
We will avenge my fallen Kyn together, mortal.

Interesting. You appear to have survived Dagon's worst prison and suffered little to no damage. And your demeanor suggests that you succeeded in your mission, though the Anchorite seems distressed.\n\nTell me, what happened in the Blood Pit?
Regale the little Dremora with the story of your cleverness and determination, master! She should know all that you have learned about our enemies.
Our work is not quite done. We did not find the missing Bladebearers at Jynd's foundry or Zynoahz's gaol. They must have found their way to Annihilarch's Summit.\n\nOr were taken there.
With Faven dead … this does not bode well for Wretched Spire. Investigate the scene while I continue to decipher this text you found.\n\nSomething here must reveal who is behind these acts.
This place reminds me of where we found Destron and Calia, but in much worse condition. Could the Anchorite actually have lived here?\n\nWe better look around.

You heard the Dread Lady. Get on with your mission.\n\nI'm quite certain she'll provide me with something even more tantalizing to accomplish. Something truly befitting a prophet of my status. You'll see.

What happened back there? How did I do all that? I just sort of knew how to disrupt the cataclyst … knew what you needed to do to destroy it.\n\nLook, talk to Lyranth, all right? I need time to recover my strength. And I need to think.
My father can be quite unreasonable, as you can plainly see. I suggest you talk to Noroth while I try to sort this out.
Burn the seas and flood the skies. Then you'll get a big surprise!
Once we gather at the gates of Destruction's Solace, we must move quickly. We cannot hope to avoid the place's defenders for long.
I would offer advice if I had any to give, master. But in my time serving Mehrunes Dagon, I have never seen the city without its defenders. Do not trust this.
Time rarely concerns my kind, but I find myself growing anxious about Sister Celdina's progress. We must hurry and meet up at the base of Annihilarch's Summit.
Ask the Bladebearers what they can tell us about what the cult is doing here. And find out if they know where they're keeping the Riven Cataclyst.

Here you are—a freshly attuned portal key. Carry it with you and the portal will deposit you inside Ardent Hope. After that, matters are in your hands.\n\nI do hope Lyranth has a plan for what to do once you get there.

The path to the cataclyst lies ahead. But the Bladebearers are in trouble. If they fall, all eyes will turn toward us as we ascend. We will never reach the Anchorite.\n\nPerhaps now is the time to release the magic stored in the twisted rod.

The Bladebearers stand ready, mortal. I will wait until you pass through the portal, then I will join my clan and assault the front gates.\n\nToday we teach Valkynaz Nokvroz the cost of making the Bladebearers his enemies.
My scouts may have been captured, but they still have their eyes and ears. They may have learned something while immured in this fort. See what Dothaz can tell you before I lead them to safety.
I'm ready when you are. We're not going to let some spooky fog stop us, are we? \n\nLet's find Sombren!

I was once supreme among Lord Dagon's warlords. By the strength of my own hand I kept the Dremora of the Deadlands in line. \n\nThey feared me once. Now they have forgotten me. Curse that traitorous Nokvroz!
There is no time to speak! We must strike while Mehrunes Dagon is still transitioning to this plane.
Master. I smell blood. Mortal blood. It seems I have a very strong nose in this puny form.\n\nI smell Nokvroz, as well. He was here, I am certain of it.
Just wait until my brother hears about this. He's going to be so jealous.

Another down, my friend! There are still minstrels to recruit. Go on.\n\nI'm off to make conversation with that fine-looking fellow over there. How do I look? Ravishing? Devilishly handsome? Doesn't matter, I always look good.
Sorry, I can't read that. You should show it to Lyranth.

The order has camps throughout Fargrave and the Deadlands. Sister Celdina could be anywhere.\n\nBut tell the Anchorite to check the Shambles. Look for an abandoned building. Someplace hot. I heard one of the devastators complaining about the heat.

We should leave. The cult's forces may have scattered, but no doubt Sister Celdina will send a force to try to deal with us. We should not be here when they arrive.\n\nPerhaps the Anchorite can suggest a place for us to meet up, safe from prying eyes.
As glad as I am to see you, can we do more rescuing and less talking right now? I think if you shatter that glowing crystal behind me, that will do the trick.
A Watcher. I could never abide these abominations. You speak to the Collector and determine if they have anything in their collection that can assist us.
I don't mean to be short, it's just that I am very busy today. So if you don't need to talk to me, please just go away.
Ah, a fresh face is always welcomed around these parts. You grow your wealth. I'll stay in business. When you need me, you'll know where I am. Yeah?
There are so many fascinating subjects to learn about here in Fargrave. I just hope there's enough time to study everything I'm interested in!
You better not be here to beg me for an antidote. I'm fresh out of those for now. If you're here for a poison, then you're more bold than you seem.
If you want to talk to me, you better have an appointment.
I can't believe we defeated Mehrunes Dagon. I was there and I'm still having trouble wrapping my head around it.

Let's split up to look for Lyranth. \n\nIs it too much to hope that we find her and she says she's really sorry for what she did. That she's not planning to do anything evil with the stolen power? On second thought, don't answer that.
Sorry, I really don't have time for you at the moment. I'm scrying for magical items in the Sever. There are some strong leads. I think.
Tell Lyranth what we learned. The Waking Flame hides at Annihilarch's Summit.

Return the criminals to Fargrave once you have apprehended them. I will take care of things from there.\n\nI request that you proceed with haste. If their trail is lost, it will be difficult to pick it up once more.
I won't lie, I thought you'd turn right back around to Fargrave and give us up to the Grasp. Thanks for coming to hear us out. \n\nI'm glad Elisa is here but … what about Minwileth? Did you find her?

This is all my fault. Why did I have to be so weak? Why did I have to be the one to get the Drain? \n\nThere's no point in running. It's all … futile. I can feel myself slipping away. Maybe I should just accept it.

With that unpleasant business out of the way, I can authorize you to use the Undertaker's stones for yourself.\n\nThere is, of course, one more guardian that needs to be restored and reset before I can get out of here though.
It's good to see you safe and unharmed. You're looking well.
Ah, you look as appetizing as ever, mortal. It is good to see you.
You're the most reliable mortal I have ever worked with outside of official capacities. \n\nWould you like to take on a contract with me? It'll be the culmination to all you've done so far.
You will need fortitude and strength to find our Bladebearer Kyn. Follow Kynreeve Rynkyus and observe.
Speak to the kynreeve, mortal.
I have no interest in speaking to you.

Large bugs. Yes. And what trip to Vvardenfell would be complete without … larger mushrooms? Damn, damn, damn!\n\nSorry. I'm just … well, frankly, I'm cracking my acorns trying to write a decent travel brochure. Not as easy as it sounds. Trust me.
A second Ebony Blade. It appears Skrix was as good as his word … so far.\n\nExamine the sword. Perhaps we can determine the nature of this artifice.

I figured we wouldn't find everything all together, but I dared to hope. We should find Varallion and Sarydil and take back what they stole, but be careful. I recognize the name Varallion and it brings nothing good to mind.
Caska took such great strides getting here, Za'ji can't help but feel she was trying to strain his poor legs.\n\nZa'ji was built for grace, not speed!
More talking? Just get on with it. Sooner you find what you're looking for, sooner Fyr's out of my webs.
I don't normally crawl around in Daedric fortresses. Really. I don't.
I suggest we find the nearest exit and return to the House of Whims with all due haste. The Collector's attention span ebbs and flows like the tides of Topal Bay, but they could return at any moment.

Not what I expected, but then nothing about this journey has been thus far. The Banekin's—er, Master Rrvenk's—voice comes through clearly, but I don't understand. He's telling me he can't correct my alignment with this realm!
Thanks for the rescue. I'm Jakarn, by the way. We'll have to have a proper introduction later. Somewhere less drafty. Preferably with alcohol.
Have you heard the word of the Dread Lady? If not, allow me to share Lyranth's revelations with you. It shouldn't take more than a few days.
Gazmod must take steps to repair his notoriety after recent events. Vri imagines he will summarily obliterate all his sentinels, for a start.
Gazmod's got quite a few Peryitic curios in his collection: the Bilious Censer, the Toxicruciform, the Golden Scab. If I could somehow recover any of these, how the Blighted Lord would smile upon me!
There you are, mortal. I bring a message from Madam Whim. You should feel honored that she takes an interest in your activities.
The Bladebearers don't seem to have a taste for torture, as far as I can tell. That means they're good in my book.

I thought it might be good if a group of Dremora warriors sheltered here. Keep things like monsters and scavengers from troubling us. But now that I see them sharpening their blades, I think they might draw new troubles here.
One mortal, delivered as promised. Kaluzan involves the Grasp at his own peril.
Do not interfere here. Mortals should not meddle in affairs of the Stricture.

Something has certainly gotten Lyranth's dander in an uproar. What occurred on Annihilarch's Summit, my darling? You can tell Madam Whim.\n\nDoes it have something to do with Deadlight? She seemed very interested in that old legend.

To think the Ascendant Order accomplished all this. I thought the plans I put in place were so clever. How far does this Ascendant Lord and his Magus's reach extend, I wonder.\n\nLet's speak further at Mandrake Manor. I'll see you there.
You return alone? Ah. I take it the news is not good. Grenier and Danise were not just retainers—they were friends. The Steadfast shall miss them, and so shall I.\n\nPlease. Tell me what happened.
I'll keep watch. My scrying has led us here, but I won't be able to get us any closer. \n\nI hope you find Quentyn and that he's all right. Be safe.
Wind guide you, traveler. I hope you find the answers you seek.
The forests of High Isle hide many ancient secrets. Some are perhaps better forgotten. Go in peace, traveler.

Again, we are successful and our efforts are complete. Thank you!\n\nZenithar created a channel through which our paths cross, season after season. Continue learning your trades. Your skill is already much improved for your efforts.
I knew it'd be hot in here, but this is unreasonable. Did Tarrinore even bring water with her?\n\nLet's find my wife and the scoria we need. Quickly!

Za'ji is glad to see you, walker, but there will be no reunion with the Perfect Pounce. She is gone, this time for good. That terrible storm was the end of her.\n\nAnd that is not the worst of it. Za'ji has lost Queen Ayrenn and Caska, too!

I honestly didn't think we'd ever leave that cell alive. I owe you a debt of gratitude, friend. We all do.\n\nAnd I owe dockmaster of Gonfalon Bay payment of a different kind. I visit High Isle often and I considered Arnauld a friend. Bah!
I thank you for my rescue. I do not think the Ascendant Order had any more use for me. Once they realized I could not tell them what became of Prince Irnskar, they dragged me back to my cell.

The deeper we go, the more we learn about these Hadolids. I don't understand their ways at all. I thought maybe we could just talk to them. Come to an understanding.\n\nBut they clearly don't want to chat. We must keep looking for Privette.

Hey there, good-looking! If you're eager for an adventure, I have just the thing. It involves a secret mission, an intoxicatingly beautiful but missing woman, and a mystery straight out of the pages of an Investigator Vale story! \n\nCare to assist me?

I wonder pilgrim, if you'll be the one to face the horrors beyond.\n\nThat was the home of the long gone Knights of Death's Valor. Lord Leobert—sorry excuse of a knight commander that he was—turned on his oath and cursed us with undeath.
Mark my words, stranger, something as small as some of these scoria here can incite drastic and far-reaching change. \n\nOne foray into the unknown and we better our lives.

Jakarn and I will deal with the order's mage while you use your exceptional skills to stop the Ascendant Champion.\n\nIf all goes as planned, this should be over quickly. Then High King Emeric can decide who will represent him at the peace talks.
Not quite how I imagined that would go. But we faced the Mad Duke, walked with the spirit of Sir Brenvale, and lived to tell the tale! \n\nI'm sure the order will approve.
Let's get inside and find that lantern Tarazka mentioned. Valessea needs rescuing, and who better than a handsome rogue and his stalwart adventuring companion? \n\nUm, you go first.

Please tell me you've good news. I saw Sir Langley stomping around in a temper. \n\nHe's got a whopper of a bruise too. I do hope my Isobel didn't punch him. She's not usually the punching sort, but he is such a … well. A ninny!
Hmm, I could have use for you, but not this moment. I have a lot to consider first.
That powder will do the job. Just sprinkle a pinch over each of the alliance medallions and it will return them to their original state. Only the protective magic of the invitations will remain.

I admit, I didn't expect someone like the general to fall for the Ascendant Order's patter. Guess you never can tell. \n\nAnyway, you should hear Captain Kaleen's story. It made the hairs on my neck stand up straight!
You take care of those deep druid idols and I'll make sure we've got something to celebrate with afterward. Eye on the prize, right?

Anton's on the run for his life. He may have left signs of where he went. As we search deeper within, we should look for anything that points in his direction.\n\nIn the meantime, that winner's stage to the north seems like a good place to start.
State your business, adventurer. We don't let just anyone wander around the Palace of Kings.
I'll see you back at Mandrake Manor. While I have a moment, I thought I'd go and give that Tribute game a try.\n\nI'm a fair hand at cards, don't you know?

Like my new outfit? What better way to search Amenos Station than disguised as a jailer? \n\nI'll see what I can learn about our missing royals here in the stockade and around town. You head to the jungle. From what I already heard, you need to hurry.
Oh hello then. Figured out my barrier, did you? And is that little Izzy I see back there?

Damn the Ascendant Order! If they've harmed one hair on Lady Arabelle's distinguished head, I'll ….\n\nNo, no. I can't think like that. Lady Arabelle is crafty beyond reason. I'm sure she's fine. But we should hurry—just in case.

Ah, now here is someone worth my time. You helped rid Skywatch of the Veiled Heritance, did you not? \n\nI would ask you to speak with this uncouth ruffian. He does the Society of the Steadfast a disservice with his glib and scathing tongue.
You never think when they send you to prison that you'll be hunted to death. It's just not something they tell you about.
I know something of Lady Arabelle's adventures. She's dragged me along a time or two back in the day.
Get close and trap her with the censer, challenger! I believe in you!
This one doesn't want to cause trouble. But she won't let anyone get in her way. So, just don't?
It's surprisingly soothing in this little place.\n\nThe tranquility of the grave, I suppose. Haha.
This is definitely Sword's Rest, but where are the Lion Guard? Something's very wrong here.\n\nLet's look around and find Lady Arabelle.
Oh, dear. That was Jakarn's plan?\n\nWell, I must say that it's working. The guards aren't paying attention to anything else. You'd better put this distraction to good use while it lasts.

I'll ask around. See if my contacts have any clues as to where the dockmaster was taken. If I can find him, maybe we can make him talk.\n\nYou go with Lady Arabelle to meet with Lord Bacaro. I'll find you if I turn up anything useful.

If you don't have an appointment to meet with Commander Jourvel, make one. She's busy. As am I. \n\nThe Nord over there can make the appointment for you. If he's not writing that gods-awful poetry at the moment.
Oh hello! Do you need an appointment to meet with the commander?\n\nShe's a very busy woman. I should be able to find room in her schedule … how does next month sound?
House Mornard—generous lot that they can be—requires that we do our duty by them and look to improve ourselves. \n\nI'm afraid my recent mistakes undo all the progress I made toward both terms.
Sentries and jailers are always surprised when prisoners like me escape. Who wants to spend their life behind bars?

As I understand it, when the Evergrowth was bound, the core of its spirit was interred in a chamber somewhere within the Undergrove. The very first ward should be located there—and it's the last one we need to deal with.
I hope you are enjoying your visit to High Isle.
Very well done! We're like the heroes in all of Madach's old tales, now. \n\nLet's head to the tower and face down the bloodmage!
The ritual circle has a lot of innate magic, like I said. We should be careful. The angry motes and livestock aren't the only things affected by my spell.
Now's your chance. Find the prince. We'll cause a distraction to draw away as many Serpents as we can! Then we'll find a good place to cast my ritual and clear the storm for your ship.
There's our rescue. Time to go!

Za'ji has heard what you discovered at the Ascendant Order sites. A lodestone on my ship, a magical storm meant to kill us all. If Za'ji knew this beforehand, he would have made sure to bring more ale!\n\nLady Arabelle doesn't have nearly enough.
No time to waste.
Let's see what's waiting for us inside. Don't worry. I'll watch your back.
A launch! Just what we need to get to Silver Swan. We should hurry. If Count Damard is aboard, he could set sail at any moment!
Find out what he knows. I'll watch our backs.
Go on in and see if you can find Roslenn's notes. I'll make sure no one bothers you while you're inside.
Nature spirits can be capricious, dangerous. The Evergrowth is no exception. Tread carefully, stranger. And don't allow young Audrine to toss around accusations she can't confirm.
This is a place I'm not likely to forget in a long time.
Interesting. I've never visited a druidic ritual circle before. Let's look around and see if we can ascertain what sort of magic was performed here recently.

The spirits of nature have answered our call. It has been a long time since I last attempted such a ritual. I'm glad to see the spirits still recognize me as one of their own.\n\nFollow the trail. Valessea and I will be along shortly.

Good luck with your investigation. I know Armin is concerned about the unusual symptoms showing up among the patients, but the wounds of war take many forms.\n\nThose that a soldier carries in his mind may not surface for years.
Can you believe this steward? Who does he think he is?\n\nYou give it a try. I'm about ready to punch him.
Woo! you smell like … like kindlepitch! How much are you carrying? Mara's mercy, be careful with that!
You and Oblan better get a move on. Make sure that idiot doesn't fall off of any rock ledges or this whole plan goes belly up.
I never thought that madman was going to let me down. I'm still recovering from all of the blood in my body rushing to my head!
We should go back to the inn. I can't wait to see the look on <<1>>'s face when three large diplomats come back to settle scores with her!
It's simple. Get your Nord friend to settle the tab from last night, and I'll give him back his scepter of office or whatever.
There you are, my dear. I was beginning to worry. \n\nTell me everything. What did you find at the sites marked on Elea's map?
You go on ahead to the inn—I'll meet you there shortly. I'm afraid I will need a moment.
Give me a moment, and I'll get money from my rooms to pay the innkeeper. It's the least I can do to repay you.
I'm so glad it worked. Is she going to be all right?
Who are you, stranger? And where am I? What's happened?
Here, take the resonance crystals. These are the ones I took from the caravan site. They're the key to everything!
I see you found the letter. Don't keep me in suspense, dear. Tell me what it says.
Hello, friend! I'm an agent of House Dufort and my role here is to hook up able adventurers with tasks that require more than a single person to deal with.\n\nFor fair compensation, naturally!
Patience. That's the best weapon in a thief's arsenal. Remember that.
It's too damn hot and I'm too damn thirsty right now for troublemakers, so just move along.

Never could figure out why Jailer Zalzay keeps a footlocker up on the platform, but it provides a perfect opportunity. Just take something out of the footlocker and slip it into Yvara's bedroll. Simple as picking a cheap lock with a rusty nail.
You get the Daybreak Gem while I set up this ladder. That hatch up above should lead out of the vault. That's my theory, in any event.
Jakarn is looking for you, my dear. I think he wanted to have a word with you … most likely about me. Ah, well. I suppose he can have his little secrets.
I'm sure <<1>> spun you a sad tale. Criminals will say just about anything to avoid going to prison. He even told me he was a diplomat. \n\nI hope he's got a better story for the city magistrate.
There's a lot of logistics involved in a naval battle, especially while launching a beach assault. \n\nI don't think you'll be able to offer any insight worth my time at the moment.
Looks like the Ascendant Order's almost done loading the ship. If we want to seize the Nereid's Song, it's now or never.
Cut the mooring lines? I should have thought of that.\n\nWell, go ahead, dear. We don't have all day.
So far, so good. Now we see if the Ascendant Order falls for this trick. Just stand around and look like we belong.\n\nIt's all about confidence.
Your assistance on Amenos and All Flags will not be forgotten.

I assumed my father sent me here because he didn't want to be bothered. Now I think he really did want me to learn something. To interact with those we consider our equals … and our enemies.\n\nThis adventure has given me much to consider.

Don't tell anyone, but I was a tiny bit concerned out there. Shipwrecked, chased through a jungle, attacked by rogue knights. Then a castle shook apart around me.\n\nThings were simpler when all I had to deal with was the Black Drake and Ranser!
Hey, friend! I hoped to find you in Gonfalon Bay. Hard to resist its charms, eh?\n\nAnyway, Lady Arabelle wants a word with you. She says we're not quite done yet.

Za'ji thinks that the Ascendant Magus owes us a few ships, yes? Nereid's Song is a good place to start. Za'ji just wishes there weren't so many evil knights here.\n\nCaptain Kaleen has a plan, though. Za'ji can't wait to hear it!
You need to cut all three mooring lines. Check both the port and the starboard sides, then get on board!
You've been instrumental in salvaging our peace talks. That did not go unnoticed, my friend. I'm going to keep my eye on you.
We need to save Song! Don't waste time talking to me!
Hmm? What do you want? I own this inn, I'm not the help. If you're interested in dining or would like a room, speak with one of my associates.

You must be real. Not even in this one's wildest fevered hallucinations could I have imagined seeing Ember after all these years. What a gift.\n\nShe looks well. Healthy and strong. And she has found a strong companion. Jhaka is relieved.
This one let loose and ran through the sands. It felt good. \n\nDid you find anything in this place? Silverslip mentioned something about the Emerald Eye. But Song is not here.

Jhaka and I have been tailing you and Ember. Between his sense of smell and my eyesight, we make a good pair of trackers. \n\nEmber told us to stay behind, but we couldn't let the two of you go off on your own. Song is our friend too.

Stop swaying when you're talking to me, how am I supposed to take the measure of ya? Heh, this is pretty strong stuff. Good stuff. I want to keep drinking, why are you bothering me? \n\nI'm retired! Leave me to drink in peace.
I am still having trouble believing all that's happened. And that Ember, sweet, clever Ember, is here at all! It defies all logic. \n\nBut I am happy. Happier than I have been in a long, long while.

There is very little that escapes the Emerald Eye. You'd do well to make sure you're not being overheard when discussing something that has to do with them.\n\nIt may be the last discussion you ever have.
It'll be good to breath the salt air of the archipelago and hear the familiar sounds of the sea. \n\nThere's no place like High Isle, my friend.
I'll be fine, you two go on. You learn how to be quick and quiet when you lead a merchant crew, mark my words.
Well, if you're back again I suppose there's only one reason. What'd you find this time?
Hah, nice work down here! Go talk to that fetcher. Get what you need. Then we'll step in.
We will face this enemy together.

We're finally getting somewhere. I know, I know. I'm as surprised as you are, but Stibbons seems quite confident that the tools are in the graveyard.\n\nNow, put a little oomph in your step. We have a curse to break!
The Memorial Garden is just over there. We need to add Captain Renwic's name to the monument before the curse reasserts itself and we forget everything again.

I'm not sure how devout you are, but Zenithar's blessing is freely given. I'm sure, if you wanted, he'd look kindly upon you.\n\nSelf-improvement, betterment of commerce, and wealth are assured to all who kneel at his altar.
Glad to have your help. I might have taken the bark-wench alone, but not with the whole woods trying to kill me and Za'ji.\n\nLet's hope this map he found leads to treasure.
We shall be right behind you, adventurer. \n\nJust try not to hurt his beautiful face, all right? It's so pleasant to look at.
I said no, Tobin, and I meant it. Can't you see I'm in love with your brother, the captain?
Hello! I'm ever so happy to see you and Isobel. Would you mind cutting me loose, please?
Whatever happens, we'll be right behind you.
Good luck to you both. My little detective may be brave … but what if she's taken on too much too fast?
The way is clear. Let's go find Prince Irnskar.
I can't find Sorinne anywhere! Someone mentioned seeing her outside. Go check, will you?

The Roister's Club Novice Tournament is upon us! Canny opponents, unexpected strategies, fresh cards! Truly, this is what every Tribute player lives for!\n\nYou've clearly improved since last we spoke. Are you prepared to enter your first tournament?

Between Sorinne moping around and Brahgas chewing my ear off, I can't get a damn thing done.\n\nEveryone pours out their troubles to the barkeep when what they really need is a partner. Or a priest. Or a dog.
Remember, you represent the Gonfalon Chapter now. That means … well, Kishka does not know what that means. Just play well, yes?
Thanks for being there for me, friend. Really, it means the world.\n\nNow, let's teach Raenobi a lesson in humility!
I'm proud to fight at your side, friend. The Ascendant Order made a mistake when they picked a fight with the two of us!
If we just had the ingredients I'm sure I could whip up another batch of that drink. But we barely survived getting them the first time.

Well fought, friend!\n\nIf you're here, Lady Arabelle must be nearby. Now, what does she have up her sleeve? If I've learned anything in my long association with Lady Arabelle, it's that she always has a plan in the works.
Brahgas will play like his life depends on it. Because it does. Be careful.

Oh, sweetmeat, you look like the senche who swallowed the terror bird!\n\nAre you so surprised to see Raenobi? Surely, you would not blame this one for her good fortune. A dear friend and a tournament in the same place? It is so convenient!
It is good that you are here. I have been watching the dock—we won't take Nereid's Song without a fight.\n\nSpeak to Captain Kaleen. She will know what to do.
I've tended this grove for nearly fifty years, and the Evergrowth has never spoken to me.\n\nWell, not directly, at any rate.
You have been such an unexpected help to Lady Arabelle. I can't imagine where we would be now without you.
Well, you and Aspirant Isobel sure got the jump on me. Hah!\n\nNice work, second. You're doing good work out there.
Damn it! I thought Razhamad set the terms so Brahgas would go free after the match.\n\nCome on, we have to act fast!
I'm so sorry Razhamad put this on you, chum. I'm so … I'm so sorry about everything.\n\nI deserve this, but Razhamad and the chapter don't. Beat this bug-lover for them, not for me.
Your friend Brahgas has really stepped in the dung this time.\n\nIf I were you, I'd steer clear of him for a while. Trust me, you don't want to get pulled down into his mess.
So, this is the Gonfalon Chapter we've heard so much about. Hmm.\n\nI never judge my opponents by their appearance, but my, aren't you an unkempt bunch.
The tournament begins now. I wish your chapter good luck.\n\nSome of you desperately need it.
I just had the strangest dream. I think I was in a house full of cats but none of them could help me. \n\nWas that the wizard's magic? I have … I have a powerful urge to eat fish, suddenly.
I heard they found the broken pieces of Kamal's Bane on Shipwreck Shoals. A damn fine ship, she was. Good enough to carry that Nordling prince whatever-his-name.

Sounds like they found the ship of that Nord prince Burnscar. That'll make Perditte happy, I guess. She likes to daydream about princes. But where's the High King, Limerick? And what of that Elf queen Hayrend?
Was just about to meet with this Kiv Lindres and then these two show up. And now you.\n\nHeh. Busy time at the tavern.
One down, two to go! Keep it up. We'll celebrate our victory soon enough!
Hey! I knew you'd make it to the second round!\n\nJust don't let your guard down. This might be a novice tournament, but all it takes is one slip up and you're knocked out!
Some young whippersnapper asked me if I can turn people into salamanders. What an odd question.\n\nOf course I can turn people into salamanders.
I must prepare for the battle ahead. Go. I will see you at the Worm's lair.
Attacked? Here in the Earthen Root Enclave? This can't be happening.

These pipes all funnel magicka below us, deep into the pit of this old structure. But why?\n\nWe can assume it powers the storm we saw. Created it from nothing. But we've only encountered risen dead in these halls. What purpose does all this serve?

To help me evaluate my suggested itinerary, I'd like you to sample some local cuisine here in the Gaming Hall.\n\nThen, visit fishing holes and scenic spots around High Isle and Amenos. I'll mark locations on your map. We'll add the best to the tour.
By the root … the spirit, they're beautiful! I think they want to communicate with us. You saved them from Archdruid Michiel and the Firesong. Why don't you see if you can get through to them?
By seas and stars—the wyrds and the Druid King, they summoned this spirit? I assumed it would be more … insubstantial?\n\nGo on, see if you can speak to them.
Why must the druids involve us in their affairs? They return to the mainland after countless seasons just to cause trouble? Blight take them!
Please, find my sister. Those druids took her and threatened more violence if we got in their way.

Five-claw! In such a place? Jone and Jode must have sent you. Raz needs a small favor, if you can spare a moment.\n\nIt concerns the two large thugs over there. They try so hard to look intimidating. Almost adorable, yes?
Well, now we know who we are dealing with. That is both good news, and bad news.
