When you smashed that crystal, did you feel a tremor? At least we didn't drown in a fountain of burning lava. That's a good sign, right?\n\nWe should keep going. Let's find the other three druid crystals I saw.

With the Ascendant Magus defeated and that nasty business on Y'ffelon dealt with, we can get back to the matter at hand. It's time to move forward with Lord Bacaro's peace talks.\n\nI just wish I could be sure we were done with the Ascendant Order.

Za'ji is not sure how much longer Queen Ayrenn will agree to remain here. And if she decides to leave, the peace talks won't happen. All of this will have been for nothing.\n\nOh, Za'ji wishes he were smarter, but this one has no idea what to do!
Looks like someone else beat us to the door. Let's head in before any more Dreadsails wander by. Captain Siravaen won't keep them busy forever.
I must not let my forces move outside of Vastyr until Stefan is safe. But a mainland mercenary might be able to do the job my knights can't.\n\nRemember, I am trusting you with my son's life.

If you're about to walk up and bang on the front gate, let me stop you right here. The ruins are full of Dreadsails. You'll never get in that way.\n\nSealord Nalos seems to be mustering his forces for something big.

Count Mornard is slyer than I thought. The best way to disarm an enemy is to show them what they expect to see.\n\nGo talk to Rahval and Ellic. I saw them by the bridge east of the city. And good luck, mate.

Welcome to the Telling Stone, my friend. These runes tell the prophecy we call the Dream of Kasorayn. Almost nothing survives from the time of the Druid King, but we have this.\n\nAnd now Frii, as well.
I have given Archdruid Orlaith too much ground in an effort to keep the peace between our circles. No longer. The treachery of this day sunders all bonds.\n\nShe will pay for this.
I'll do what I can for these druids. You should go check on Tuinh, the village they were taken from. The Dreadsails must have struck a heavy blow there.

Ryvana told me to wait here. She wanted to make sure that Druid Laurel or whoever came after us knew where to go.\n\nShe doesn't know what the Ascendant Lord is up to exactly, but she's sure he came to this place for a reason.
This is a nice beach, yes? Maybe Za'ji should wait here. Keep the path back to the Pounce open. This one's fur is quite flammable and there is much too much lava around for Za'ji's taste.

Lady Arabelle said you'd find us. Told me to wait here and point the way. She followed Bacaro, the Ascendant Lord, through that door over there.\n\nGo help her. I'm still not sure she's fully recovered from the effects of the poison.
Can you feel it, the weight of countless seasons pressing down on us? This circle is old. Maybe one of the first established on the island.
We seem to find ourselves in the lap of luxury. As much as Raz would like to indulge his few, simple, vices … we must stick to the mission.

Good luck during your trials, warrior.\n\nThis one and Apprentice Taz will be eager to hear of your progress. Do not take unnecessary risks, but do not shy away from danger either. You will need balance in order to succeed.
I do not know if I am ready to lead House Mornard. But the people of Galen need me, so I will do my best.
The Sower of the Dream. The Druid King's crown, staff, and gauntlet regrown. I never imagined I would see the prophecy come to pass. \n\nGo on, friend. Frii wishes to speak with you.
Never you fear, mercenary. We'll bring the Mad Maiden into port. Just pray to your gods that the Firesong at Cinderwash Point don't notice us as we draw close.
Dream. Memory. I walked with Elder Aiven, just as you did. I saw the one who called me from the Green. Kasorayn, the Druid King. I understand much more now.\n\nWas not Urdiir the Guardian wonderful?

The very spirits all around us cry out in fear and sorrow. Even Frii says they sense a change in the sacred seeds. Tell me about the battle in Vastyr. Is Stefan all right?\n\nI fear something terrible has happened.
Dire times call for strength and commitment. We'll see this through and be stronger for the effort.

You've recovered some valuable knowledge. Are you willing to test your own?\n\nCaptain Samara asked me to present you with a series of questions that would baffle even seasoned scholars. If you're up to the challenge, of course.
House Mornard and its knights are with you. We'll follow in Captain Siravaen's vessel.
What's happening? Are we breaking the curse? I can't wait to be myself again!
Was this supposed to happen? The blasted druid didn't tell us anything about this! Just be careful, please. I don't want to catch on fire!
I'm glad to see you, friend, but where's Frii? No, talk to Lady Arabelle. Tell her what happened and the rest of us will listen in.

I've visited Y'ffre's Path many times. This passage used to be covered in thick vines and thorns. Lord Bacaro must have cleared them away to reach that door.\n\nLet's go inside and see what he's after.

Thank the Green I caught you here. I feared I might be too late. The message I bring was too important to give to just anyone, and I know paths across the island that only the druids can walk.\n\nBut first, what's the situation here?
I never ignore a warning, especially one written in stone. Talk to Druid Laurel and see if she can tell us more about these carvings.
I don't trust Umindior to make the delivery without me. He hasn't proven too reliable even once yet. Not like you.\n\nSpeaking of which, can I have the relic?
Outsider, you've been more help than even I anticipated. We're so close to finding my Gwenaelle and returning her to her original state. It's not much farther now to the Chronicle. Let's continue.
The seed is safe, thank Y'ffre. But we can't leave it here. Please, retrieve the seed and let's get out of here.
Many believe that we Maormer are cold like the deep. Truth is, our passion roils like a storm. We just need the right inspiration.
Perhaps I'll write a note to Neri. I must see her again. But how to get it to her?\n\nUm, yes, whatever you and Quen have planned, I agree entirely. Excellent work. I need to rest, but I'll catch up.
You'd rather sail with that puny cat on a sorry excuse for a fishing scow? Suit yourself. If it actually survives the voyage, we'll see you on Y'ffelon.
Clohaigh is just to the east. Please, hurry. If the Firesong find that cave, they'll stop at nothing to capture Frii and our sacred seed.
Go on ahead to Glimmertarn, my friend. Frii and I will be right behind you. I want to make sure they get out of here safely.
Count Stefan and his knights cleared out most of Bacaro's forces. Let's keep moving!
Hurry, my friend. We need the light of the moons to begin this ritual, and the Allwither Order may find their way into this chamber at any moment.

I never knew these markings were here. I don't think anyone did. But Frii was drawn to this place. I'm sure that's no coincidence. We need to find them.\n\nOnce we make sure Frii's safe, maybe they can explain all this.
Give Archdruid Rahval the sacred seed, Laurel-friend. He will keep it safe. Fire and sea will lash the walls of the city, but they will hold.\n\nHe has told me so.
One riddle down! That wasn't so hard. \n\nMaybe I was a little harsh on old Kiko. He's just doing what he was taught to, right? Not like he knows much else.
What do you think? Did someone send me the same gift that poisoned poor Lady Arabelle?

What brings a druid and Lady Arabelle's most-trusted assistant to Steadfast Manor? I'm afraid Lord Bacaro is still on Galen, leading the relief efforts there. \n\nIs there something I can help you with?
As always, I'd recommend taking on this foe with a group. \n\nThat said, the request from within House Mornard asked for discretion, so just … keep the details of this job among yourselves, will you?
I know this choice will be difficult, but only you can make it. I need to keep the ritual energy flowing or both of them will be lost.
Nicely done. Let's keep at it, these seeds won't plant themselves.

We only need a few flowers. Savage Systres Tours has a reputation of ruggedness and danger, but a few pretty things would not go amiss.\n\nDruid Yrene is down in the Vine District, if you'd like to know more about Fauns' Thicket or kingsblood.

I think Za'ji and Caska should get to see the negotiations unfold. But to have them participate? Oh, goodness no, dear!\n\nSo, invite Stefan, Laurel, and the rest. And remind Stefan I'm depending on House Mornard for added security.

How my father ever accomplished anything with the constant parade of supplicants and requests, I'll never understand. Or Archdruid Rahval for that matter. Now I know what it's like when everyone is constantly vying for a moment of your attention.
Talk to my father. I'll stand guard in case more Dreadsails get close.

I think that's everything, my friend. Thanks again for helping me honor Frii's request. I hope they find peace and happiness inside the volcano.\n\nAnyway, I think you should head back to High Isle now. I know Lady Arabelle is eager to begin the talks.

Za'ji worries about the leaders. Do you know Za'ji once saw Queen Ayrenn decapitate someone with a spoon. A spoon! Ah well. Out of Za'ji's paws.\n\nBut if you ever need us, five-claw, Caska will come running. Za'ji too, but definitely Caska.

Peace. I wonder if they'll really do it. I've grown to respect all three leaders in the time we've been assisting them, but I know these are not easy waters to sail.\n\nAnyway, if you ever need us, five-claw, just send word to the Perfect Pounce.
Now, friend! Strike at Archdruid Orlaith while the guardian distracts the Firesong!
I am not the same Frii who emerged from the bower. I will not be easily bound by the Firesong or their archdruid. Not again.
Please, not now, my friend. Find Captain Siravaen. Convince her that we still need the help of the Gilded Blades.\n\nYou and I, we … we can talk later. Back at the castle.
I won't let him leave here alive!

The cathedral! It happened so fast … I barely escaped the falling stone.\n\nI arrived with the last of the wounded when everything started to shake! The count and Archdruid Ellic, they were right in front of me … they … oh no. Damn it all!
The distortion's power has grown. Containment is no longer an option. Only destruction can untangle the knot.\n\nDestroy that creature, while I do my work.
Welcome, friend. I don't believe I've seen you around Vastyr before. How can the Society of the Steadfast help you?

I'm pleased that Lady Arabelle thought to include the druids of the archipelago in the peace talks. As you have seen, events on the mainland reach even to our distant shores.\n\nStill, I wish we had archdruids or elders available for the task.
The wind vortex. Step into it and it will get you to safety, friend of Laurel.
We've seen no Firesong or Dreadsails in the area for some time. And Frii says they can sense some sort of change with the sacred seeds.\n\nI fear something terrible has happened.
You're back! And that ultimatum from Archdruid Orlaith ….\n\nI thought this storm was bad before, but now it's damn near apocalyptic! You better speak to Sir Stefan, mate.
The plan worked! At least the part where Frii and I surrendered to Archdruid Orlaith.\n\nThen she took Frii to the temple and ordered her druids to toss me in here.
I don't know about you, but this whole affair has shaken my confidence in island living. I have half a mind to return to the mainland. I hear the Telvanni Peninsula is pleasant this time of year.

As much as I love this archipelago, too much violence and heartache has occurred for me to truly feel safe here again.\n\nI suppose it's time to pack up and return to my family estate in Camlorn. Nothing terrible ever happens there.
The Ascendant Order on Galen? Hard to believe. Then again, I've seen Dragons in Elsweyr and Dark Anchors in High Rock, so I suppose anything is possible.
Druid Laurel has mentioned how much you have done for the people of Galen, mainlander. I know it's a lot to ask, but I hope you continue to help us. For all our sakes.
Dralys was waiting for me when I entered this chamber. He actually employed violence to take the glyphics from me! I am glad you were able to overcome him, proxy.

Don't worry, Keshargo will see you in the study. \n\nThis one hid the Itinerant Staff in a sarcophagus within the Deadlands. Zilipif knows where to go. Let them guide you. And don't worry about Mazandi. She's a good scribe, possibly one of the best.
The Great Eye sees all. At least, that is what our scriptures teach us. It seems, however, something in this situation eludes his sight. Very curious ….

You know, I half-wondered if you were going to come back at all.\n\nRather, I thought you would—but I also thought I knew everything there was to know about the Lark of Rosgard. Loathe as I am to admit it, I was wrong.
After spending so much time underground, I never remember how good the air is out here.
If you have no business here, walker, this one suggests you keep moving.

This one mourns those lost when Shadeya's greed overtook her. But we would have lost so much more if it were not for you, walker. This one knows not how to express his thanks.\n\nThe Buoyant Armiger … she failed to catch our tricky friend, yes?
I don't know how it happened. That thief appeared out of nowhere—and took the talisman right out of my hands!\n\nWhy isn't Rilasi doing something about this?

I hope you don't work for my quarry. No, you don't look her type. \n\nHmm. I'd rather not have to do everything myself. How would you like to be a distraction? The Morag Tong are keen to see this writ taken care of, so there's plenty gold to share.
Gine was a very talented egg tender. Came highly recommended from one of our other mines.
We have collected all the required fragments, I cannot reconnect to Kemel-Ze's security apparatus here. We must return to the antechamber.
I wonder what happened to this Factotum. They're usually quite resilient.

Attend, mortal. Your arrival could mean not all is lost. We require aid.\n\nThe eternal hum of knowledge fades within our sanctum. Creatures of ignorance invade the Apogee of the Tormenting Eye. They come to consume.

What a troubling combination of permutations and crises. I perceive a nexus of … ah. Never mind.\n\nWe must discuss what we learned at the Necropolis, Tel Rendys, and Alavelis. Let us return to my refuge in Necrom.

Seeing my old friends always lifts my spirits. I haven't quite fixed my portal spell, but I have cleaned up my mess. Don't want to draw further mortal attention if at all possible.\n\nThere are still some of my creatures out there. Please see to them.
Another censer! Blightcrown must have sickened all the keepers in the Necropolis with those foul things.\n\nDestroy it, friend. I can't bear to see Abbot Ilvel in such pain.
I'm busier than an egg miner herding a clutch of scrib, stranger. Come back later and I'll try to assist you.
Well, if it isn't the liberator of Anchre in the flesh. It's good to see you again before we finally set off from this place.
If the foreman is confident about going back into the mine then I am too! Hopefully Cindieth can keep her promise to help, as well.\n\nAnd thank you so much for pulling us out of there!

Looks like I'll be able to take care of those little critters again after all. If my arm gets better, at any rate.\n\nThank you for the hand back there. Drinks are on me if we ever run into you again.

Uxunath is gone. She may return, of course. Eventually.\n\nA more pressing matter. Entering the Crux severed our connection to the Remnants. We don't understand. Let's examine the document at the center. That must be our pact.
Thank you. I know it is a difficult decision.

This will be fun!\n\nNow, the study is, well, "big" doesn't do it justice. Meandering perhaps? You'll see what I mean. Finding three books in all that won't be easy. It's great to have another pair of eyes. Especially since Vorm's down to just the one.

It means you have been given an impossible task. And it may taint my otherwise spotless record. This is not good. Not good at all.\n\nTake whatever you learned and bring it to Leramil the Wise. Hopefully she can make sense of this conundrum.

I'm not sure how all these books are going to help us recover the Fulcrum Obscura, but if Leramil believes there's something important to find, I'll do my part. \n\nWhile I help Leramil search here, why don't you deal with the stacks to the west?

The Loggia Infinitum contains ever-changing prophecies. The great many portents that are affected by the mundane and ordinary. From changing grain prices to new valleys created by shifting rivers, the everyday is foretold here.
Return the Atlas Obscurum to its pedestal. Doing so will hopefully undo the harm this infiltrator caused.
The querier isn't Huzmargo's finest work, but it is nonetheless quite sleek, five-claw. Follow its magic and we should find the rogue mind's pact.

I suppose I owe you my infinite gratitude for saving me from Master Shelreni. And for allowing me to use your body as a temporary refuge. It isn't at all a humbling experience for someone of my former stature.
Talk to the spirit of Meln the Mouthless and I shall stand ready to protect you. Even in death, a Telvanni magister can be dangerous.

You approach a mere shadow, mortal. The Remnants break under the assault of invaders. Perhaps this is our lord's will.\n\nDo you know the Dreamcarvers? The servants of Vaermina? As we speak, they tear apart our fortress, the Cenotaph.

Applying the dust to the three cairns I marked on your map will form a matrix of magicka. Gadayn shall use the relic on each, then I can perform a ritual to locate the Panopticon's entrance.\n\nI shall also give Gadayn a gift. Something to protect him.

I thought we had little to fear from old tricks and traps, but look what happened to my comrade. Dead as the last s'wit who stepped out of line or crossed the Dusksabers.\n\nSpeaking of, who are you and what are you doing here?
Is Scruut correct? Were you able to acquire the information that eluded Leramil? If so, you should tell her what you learned.
Not a good time to talk. We need to help Reynila.

Now, mind you keep my gem on you at all times. I can't help you save the world or advise you on matters of import if I'm not on your person.\n\nUnless I manifest, only you can hear me. Oh, and I can lend you certain abilities, such as my ghost sight.
The relic passed this way, proxy. We should follow the trail and locate it before the guardians of this place fully recover. We are as much intruders here as Blightcrown and Torvesard.

Beware, stranger! Madness stalks Quires Wind. Most of my fellow ciphers are lost—the Hush has taken them. And the Daedra of the Wind have turned on those few of us who kept our minds.\n\nThey killed mortals who have worked here for decades!
More questions? I'm happy to answer … for the right price.

Forget what you heard, stranger. Master Shelreni cares not what the other masters think of her. Or how difficult she makes things for me.\n\nSo, what brings you to Tel Vara, the tower of the Telvanni mouths?

As much as I dislike this foolhardy human, you'd better do as he says. We shouldn't linger in the Heart. And the sooner I have my master's glyphic back, the sooner I can return to sorting paperwork and archiving notes like a good Watchling.

There's no time to lose, meddler. Every passing moment sees that glyphic dissipate further. Even I won't be able to repair it if we take too long. Place the remnants on this altar. Then give me some space to work!
Fate chose us to save reality, yet it works against us at every turn.\n\nMost confounding, proxy.
Torvesard went to great lengths to reach this glyphic, but it refuses to reveal its contents to me.\n\nExamine the glyphic, mortal. Perhaps you'll have more success.

Looks like we're on our own to get Keshargo back. Everything's circling around the Spiral Skein and Mephala now. Zilipif would be in constant danger in Mephala's realm. And now with Valinna's allegiance ….\n\nI hope you're not afraid of spiders.

We'll take the portal pad to the cellar. Then the key will get us into the labs.\n\nFrom there, it's just making our way through the caverns to the isolation tower. As long as we don't cross Sathile, the others will be too busy to stop us.
Is she staying? Truly? I can't believe it!

Don't look at me like that. I tried to get her to leave, didn't I?\n\nAt best, it would come to this. At worst, she'd have ended up like the rest of the researchers. The choices that love demands of us are never easy.

Using Shelreni's body and a rite from a Black Book to mask the presence of a rival Daedric Prince? Even with such precautions, Apocrypha reels from the intrusion. But that doesn't explain the absence of Hermaeus Mora.\n\nI am quite concerned, proxy.
Go ahead, my friend. Talk to the magister and warn him of the danger they face.

Put on the cloak, my flesh-covered companion! Despite the condition of the components, it should work perfectly well … for a time.\n\nIt will mask your connection to Hermaeus Mora from anyone who attempts to scry or magically identify you.
I appreciate you and Sharp delving into this Ayleid ruin in our stead. Federo and I aren't exactly fighters like you two.

I'll be able to dig more deeply into these notes once we're back on the mainland. Perhaps I'll have a replica of Gorne's rotunda made. Hmm. Perhaps I should have drawn some sketches while you were dealing with Dreynis.

Oh, Straath's lieutenants likely have my notes. They enjoy the way my thoughts unravel on the page. Perhaps you will, too.\n\nBut let me give you two words of advice: First, what Garalo wants isn't worth the price! And second: flatulence!

Once I finish here, all that's left is the cleanup. Then maybe a drink or two. Actually, I'll leave the cleanup to the others.\n\nYou're a good investigator. Folsi chose well when she involved you in all this.
Freedom, at last. If only my mind would accept it as true.
Hezehk's finding spell muscles need more exercise. It never used to drain me in this way.\n\nYou remember the Intake Maw, yes? Head there so we can get that Boon of Mora.
He's gone. Let's make sure everyone else gets out of here.
Seeing you and Sharp together makes me miss my days as a job broker. Such efficiency! If only I'd known you back then. Oh well.\n\nTalk to Mevei. She's one with the plan.
Was there something else, outsider?

Doing this is Sharp's choice completely. But Mevei told me about what happened to Sharp in that abandoned lair, and I wanted to try and help.\n\nAlso, hello! It's good to see you again under much better circumstances.

I created this version of myself when the Probabilis was newly built, and now I see it after the ravages of time. The duality would have made my head ache before. But now I see only motivation to complete my work.
This should settle our dreams … for a time, at least.\n\nIt remains to be seen if this truly destroyed Ansuul, but if she attempts to break another mage's mind we'll know who to call upon.

Wizard Twelvane's just over there. She might look busy, but that's just her worried face. I can see why she's worried—Vanton's struggling more. I think the nightmare's getting worse.\n\nTalk to Twelvane. She can get you into Vanton's mind.
Master Shelreni is performing a rite from Meln's Black Book! You were supposed to stop that from happening! Let's hurry and see what we can do.

Hmm. You look like the sort who can handle just about anything. The Ordinators of the Tribunal Temple have need of someone like you. It's dangerous work, but you will be rewarded for your effort. Are you interested?
Just … just one more thing to do. Let's take the portal. It will return us to the beautiful, sun-dappled shores of the Auridon coast.
Count Stefan and his knights cleared out most of Bacaro's forces. Let's keep moving!
Look for a distortion in the air, stray flux.
I sense the aura of Hermaeus Mora upon you. I hope you haven't brought trouble with you.

A Known Thing. It's here! We're not going to sprout liar's fungi.\n\nBut those wiggly-faced Seekers protect it. I can hear them. They're laughing at me and my mortal memory. Just because I can't remember everything I read doesn't mean I'm a toad!
I'm unsure how you came to help my son, but I'm indebted to you, stranger. Give me the book so I may finish this.
Leramil … she opened a door that shouldn't exist here, but not without an extreme effort. I hope she's all right, friend.
I urge caution, mortal. My brief return to Apocrypha was torture. Whatever Vaermina and her allies are up to, it has a negative effect on natives of the realm.

No Telvanni master worth their weight in kwama cuttle would relinquish their hold on this plane without a fight. I have no doubt we can contact Master Shelreni's spirit.\n\nWhether we can get her to cooperate? Well, that's an entirely different matter.
The alterations to the Panopticon … it clouds my mind and sends agonies through my body.
The Mythos? No one ever goes to the Mythos. It's forbidden! But the Great Eye told fate's chosen to enter the Mythos. So I guess I should go with you, right?

The threads of fate converge ahead of you, proxy. Now is the moment for which the One Who Knows selected you. You must face Vaermina alone. Gadayn will be no use, and Scruut and I still suffer from the effects of the lingering corruption.
You did brilliantly. I couldn't have done it better myself! Yes, brilliantly!
It is dangerous to meddle in the affairs of House Telvanni. Llaro's fate means little to me, but his position must be filled. That is our way.
Blightcrown! He's positively disgusting! Deal with him, friend. I'll use the amulet Leramil gave me to aid you in the battle. Stand close to me and its power should protect you, too.

They say the dead have nothing to fear. Then why am I filled with a sense of unease?\n\nWell, as long as you carry my soul gem, I'll go where you go. Even if we're probably marching straight to our doom.

I, too, shall meet you at the Mythos. It will take all of us working together to end the threat posed by Blightcrown and Vaermina.\n\nJust know that the relief I granted your allies is fleeting. As long as the corruption persists, they are in danger.
If Leramil feels anything like I do, no wonder she's moving slowly. I'll stay with her while you and the curate go on ahead.
Fate has chosen a mortal to aid me. How strange this portion of the weave has become.

My inquiries finally bore fruit. I believe "A" is Akacirn, one of our own ciphers. He withdrew into his own studies years ago, but recently he's been in contact with all three dead ciphers.\n\nAnd I think I know why he wants the Numinous Grimoire.

I'll mark your map with the location of the Writhing Wastes gate, as well as where the Seekers flock.\n\nMora's foes control these Seekers. Find them, kill them, and take their ichor. Once you have enough, you can open the gate and enter the Bastion.

Not us, mortal. Just you. And Meln, I suppose. Only fate's chosen can resolve this, and that's still you.\n\nThe Prismatic Iris Shore is north of here. Meet us in Cipher's Hall after you deal with Torvesard. Then we can update the Chronicle.
I'm not sure what all this is about, but an inscribing ceremony for the Chronicle of Apocrypha certainly sounds exciting!

It is a great honor to have your name and memory recorded in the Chronicle of Apocrypha, proxy. You have made quite an impression on Scruut and the rest of the denizens of Hermaeus Mora's domain.\n\nNow, Gadayn has a request to ask of you.
All these problems at the Necropolis really have caused the keepers a headache. I really hope it's sorted soon.
The gall! Can you imagine? Not letting me, of all people, into the Necropolis? This better be sorted quickly!
I swear to you these hirelings seem more useless by the day. Find me a helpful hireling and I'll show you a miracle.
Tasks like these make me sweat so much I can barely hold a tome. What with this and those rumors in Necrom, how am I supposed to get anything done!
Eyes follow you here mortal, they follow us all, ever move we make is watched and recorded.
You smell strongly of the saline soil of the Peninsula, a land I knew so long ago. Bad memories.
You stand on shaky ground, mouth for the mouthless. What's so important that Magister Meln dares interrupt this closed session of the Masters Conclave?
You'd better shove off before Malkwug decides to really threaten you.
You enjoy having teeth? Then keep moving.

I don't like this feeling of the wolves at the door. Your confidence encourages me. Thank you for talking with me.\n\nNow I must go. I swear, my aide, Guitot is avoiding me. Just between us, he's let his grooming lapse. His odor is quite unpleasant.
Tread carefully in the halls of Bastion Nymic. Find the phylactery and bring it back as quickly as you can. The sooner we end this nonsense with Father, the sooner we can gather the scattered pages.

You're back! I hope that means you've acquired the necessary relics. Unfortunately, in my haste, I failed to consider all the tools necessary for the ritual. My deepest apologies.\n\nTraveler, I must ask you to venture into Apocrypha.

There's much to ponder and calculate. Tho'at Replicanum is a strange creature. How many copies of her do you think there are? \n\nI need to return to my notes. Come back tomorrow if you want to battle Tho'at. I should have time for it then.
Why do my bones ache? I don't even have any bones!
If you provide us with a bundle of these errant pages, I can ensorcell them for our protection. I for one would like to avoid any more needless curses.

Oh good, you're back. Master Malkhest's ready for you over there. He won't tell you this, but he went exploring without you and got bitten by a maligraphy. Kept screaming, "no, no, get it off my leg!"\n\nYour mortal appendages are hilarious!

I don't know exactly where the pages ended up. This place is a maze. So much to organize. So many books ….\n\nWithout the pages, I'll never complete my translation and the account of Fynboar the Resurrected will be lost forever. Find them. Please.
They have to be here somewhere. This is such a mess. Did I organize the shelves first? Clear the floor? Breathe? \n\nHave to remember to breathe.
Julianos be praised, a friendly face. It seems the roads are far more dangerous than I was led to believe. We stopped to enjoy the breeze when a crazed brigand came out of nowhere and robbed us!
Tread with caution, friend. Those ruffians may be the least of our worries. I didn't get a good look, but they had some vicious sounding creatures with them.
I had hoped to avoid this moment, but fate takes little account of mortal hopes as it chooses its course. Let us see what the One Who Knows can tell us about these events.
You must help me align the threads of fate to complete the ritual.
Be sure to follow Leramil's instructions to the letter.\n\nI'm pretty sure nothing bad will happen if you don't, but you never can tell with cobbled together rituals.
This one was not hurt too badly, but Mahkkin is in no haste to return to those caves. This one is no warrior. Mahkkin smushes grapes.

The alarum works! No surprises there. I'll go wait outside while you take the Alarum and find more shards. Don't want to get in your way.\n\nI might stand a chance facing down minotaurs if I was a necromancer, but I'm just a regular mage. Oh well.

My cohort, almost completely destroyed. The Rustwall staff, almost all dead. Even Shardmarshal Vargas managed to slip from our grasp. While we closed the portal and saved Skingrad, it feels like we failed, comrade.
It's a good thing we found Black-Glove Garm when we did. A few moments later and there'd be nothing left to save. Let's hope we have the same luck with Axeborn Khurga.

I can't say I followed all that, but after everything that happened in Necrom, I know a threat to Hermaeus Mora can spill into the mortal plane. And Ithelia looked very angry!\n\nTalk to Leramil. She must have a plan.
Poor Leramil. I wish there was something I could do to comfort her. It's never easy to lose an ally, especially one you care about.\n\nYou should talk to Scruut about the fragment, though, friend.

The shrines are here, in this courtyard. Old Ri'jhaad can tell you have a long journey ahead of you, fatewalker. You will need the blessings of the Two Moons.\n\nReturn after you have paid your respects.
I will reclaim Varen's Watch for the Legion. You can count on that.
Burn the rest of the mushroom planters. We need to reduce these strange fungi to ashes!
That strange mist wasn't there a moment ago. I'm certain of it. Go ahead and do whatever you're going to do. I'll watch.

With your aid, Mizzik is confident all questions will be answered! \n\nThe dog is affectionately called Betu and was beloved by the late Lady Weatherleah. This one sees tracks on the ground. Let us crouch down and follow them!
Please, traveler. The medicinal herbs are in the pantry, hurry.
Let us look at the window from the outside. Perhaps our suspect was sloppy in their haste to escape.
Mora's portal shall return us to Beragon's townhouse. I sense he has already sent our allies there.
Fate's threads led us to this old shrine for a reason. It is up to us to discern why. Look around, proxy. Something here is important enough to attract Torvesard's attention.

You and Fennorian. Never in the right place at the right time.\n\nSo, did you find what you were looking for? Share it with me and maybe I won't call down to the winery for my husband's army of mercenaries.
I wonder if Hermaeus Mora knew what we would find here. And if he did, why did he urge you to prevent Torvesard from reaching this place?\n\nPerhaps he'll explain himself now.

Greetings, champion. The Golden Eye, Hermaeus Mora himself, spoke to me in a dream. He told me you were coming here.\n\nI am Andor Indoril. It is my honor to serve as abbot and historian of this monastery.

No one ever wanted to try one of my experimental drinks before. All they ever ordered was mead or ale. Now I can finally put this apparatus to the test!\n\nJust follow along with my instructions. We'll make a great drink.
You're no legionary. But I don't think you're one of those bandits, either. And you're certainly not one of my raw recruits.\n\nSo, care to take on a commission from the captain of Fort Colovia?
I feel so guilty for not being here. Poor Lady Weatherleah.
If it's work you're looking for, you've no business with me, stranger. The over-anxious red-head is the one you want to talk to.

If it's true, and the cook and the gardener conspired to have Lady Weatherleah killed, then I must have been next. How ghastly. How positively ghoulish. I'll not sleep well knowing I was so close to death.

Our intrepid investigators! Pelena and I were just arguing over what to do with my mother's estate. Marriage squabbles. Have you made progress with that mysterious riddle? I can fetch her if you'd like, she just went into the kitchen.
Otho did his best to explain your findings, but is it really true? Pelena is to blame for this nightmare?

You've chosen a poor time to come and trade, traveler. Leftwheal is under siege by the Recollection and their bizarre beasts. If you can lend aid, tend to the wounded, if not, you best be on your way.

Now it becomes clear. The Recollection also seeks Ithelia. They hope to find her visiting places she once knew, just as we did.\n\nAnd Ithelia seems less confused than what you observed at the Outcast Inn. Her memories return and she grows confident.

Don't worry, friend. I can lead you to the communique, the bell tower key, and the cohort payroll. All part of my training as the captain's aide-de-camp.\n\nThis passage isn't used much, so it should be mostly clear. Well, except for the bears.
Hmm. The threads of fate reveal nothing to me—I cannot perceive them here. But the Daedric power I sensed outside is even stronger now. I am sure there must be a shrine below. We must press on.
No time to talk. Let's find Balandrus's lair and finish this.

Ah, the Hall of Barons. I usually content myself with appreciating my barons' work in the arenas, but the hall is magnificent too.\n\nStill, I don't dwell on the past. My arena challenges require much of my focus.

After you, proxy. In addition to hearing what Hermaeus Mora has to say, I wish to ask him about what Ithelia showed me. If there is a way to restore Curate Gadayn, the One Who Knows should be able to tell me.

I was worried when Nantharion got away from us at Hoperoot. It felt like we were a step behind our enemies at every turn. But by recovering the relics, we finally seized the initiative.\n\nThat's our advantage.
I'm beginning to think the Ayleids built this place specifically to protect the Skein until someone with both Abolisher and the Lamp of Clarity came along to reclaim it.

Beragon insisted on holding a celebration, but he refused every one of the suggestions I made. I'll have you know the ciphers consider me indispensable at all their social functions!\n\nAnyway, good work with the relics. The Great Eye is pleased.

Hermaeus Mora wants to speak with you? I hope that doesn't mean there's another reality-ending threat to deal with. No, of course not. Probably just wants to thank you.\n\nBut don't take too long. I rehearsed my speech and everything!

We need to figure out what happens now that Nantharion's dead and the Recollection is scattered.\n\nBut first, the strange High Elf has returned and wants to talk to you, comrade. You'd better see what she wants. And pray it's good news for a change.

I noticed the Ayleid ruins around Vashabar, but I never imagined it was built above ancient Miscarcand. Clearly, Nantharion planned to harness the Well of Miscarcand from the beginning. But he needed Ithelia's help to reach it.
You're clear, comrade! Go destroy that seed!
We learned how to close Mirrormoor portals using Abolisher, and we caught up with Tribune Alea. Ask her if she knows where we can find Nantharion and Ithelia.

I don't know how he did it, but Beragon managed to find us. Almost.\n\nOpen a portal so we can join our ally. We're going to need his help if we run into Shardmarshal Vargas and Nantharion at the same time. Or Ithelia, for that matter.

I sent word to Vashabar about Nantharion's fate, and Tribune Alea's scouts report that the Recollection's on the run. However, the Daedric incursions from Mirrormoor continue unabated. I don't think Shardmarshal Vargas is done with us yet.

Something funny is going on. Nantharion told us to come find him in Hoperoot if we learned anything about the wildburn seed, but the sentries at the gate refused to let us in!\n\nTribune Alea and I had to back off before it came to blows.
I sense the necromantic corruption is weakening, but we must not stop now. The ruins have not been fully exorcised yet.

As Hermaeus Mora feared, the Prince of Paths threatens the pillars of causality upon which reality stands. Yet Beragon's plan offers a glimmer of hope. A single thread of fate, spreading out from this moment.\n\nSee what the Skein reveals, proxy.
Torvesard somehow directed that reality tear right toward you. If Curate Gadayn hadn't leapt in the way …. \n\nWe won't let his sacrifice be in vain. Let's get that fragment to Leramil and Scruut.

I couldn't catch her. I've known Sorilen for almost my whole life. I cared about her. Considered her a friend … perhaps more. Why didn't I see that she had been taken in by the Recollection? Maybe I could have done something.\n\nBlight, this hurts.
Continue on, friend. I'll be right behind you.
Use the Echonir to reveal the memory here, proxy. It must be relevant to our current situation.

Nantharion's actions ensured that relations between Skingrad and Vashabar started on the brink of conflict. But you and Beragon have shown me that West Weald has room for all people. I think Count Calantius knows that now, too.
Ayleid ruins fascinate me. They're testaments to my people's history.
That carving looks important. It is some form of epitaph to the Five Loyal Retainers. I'd venture it's crucial to releasing the Emblem of the Last King.
I can tell you a little about the area, but I'm afraid full information on the task ahead should come from <<1>> himself. Please, go seek him out.
Abolisher survived? I admit I was not very optimistic about our chances. Let us make our exit while we can—and hope that we shall not need the relics again.

I know the history of our world is far from perfect, but I'm glad we stopped Ithelia from changing everything that happened since the time of the Ayleids. Not even a Daedric Prince could get that right, I think.\n\nAnyway, we've earned a rest.

If we allow the tangle in fate to persist, our localized reality could collapse. In short, we would all cease to exist.\n\nEnter the inn while I research this phenomenon. And, hurry, proxy. Even at this distance, the disturbance causes me great pain.
My scion … Torvesard. No, not mine. Just another reflection. Still, he wishes to speak. Talk to him, mortal. Ask about the final ingredient.
Terrible sight seeing Master Grander deflated like this. Perhaps some tea would raise his spirits.

I'm not one to judge the courtesy practices of others, but the Blind's gift seemed insincere given her current invasion of my master's realm. \n\nI can only hope that she won't give us any more gifts in the Hall of Barons.
My father wanted to clear this place out, but it was never a priority for the town leaders. Let's see what Carvain and Raxalee have hidden down here.
Constable Ulbren was a good friend and Yabren's like a daughter to me. If there's anything else I can do to help, let me know.
Fine. Lock us in irons and take us to the magistrate. I'll accept whatever punishment they decide.
I'm innocent, I tell you! I was just a pawn! It was all this damn lizard's idea!

You didn't hesitate to leap through the portal after me. You do this sort of thing pretty regularly, don't you?\n\nShardmarshal Vargas got away, though. That's on me. I swear I'll get her next time. But that place. The sky looked like cracked glass.

Inefficient as it may be to respond to every hostile event, the situation at Feldagard Keep is urgent. The report you recovered from Hoperoot indicates an attack is imminent. Do what you can to defend the fortress. We will speak when you return.
I don't care how those Daedra got in. I need them gone before they dismantle the rest of the barricade.
Let's hurry. If the village is waiting … well. Damn it, now I'm nervous!
Let's get back. And hopefully, this won't make our fathers any angrier than they already are.
The ruin with their little grotto is on the southern edge of town. You go talk to them, I'll find my brother and Minth.\n\nYou're getting the easy job here, I think.

Mmm. Must be Ciiril's new batch. No matter! A union between Laeni and that son of a Dawnway does not have my support. Not at all!\n\nI'll make sure Laeni knows that—as soon as I'm done with this jagga.
That Ciiril is a talented brewer. Hmph. Even still, the marriage will not go forward. And you can tell her I said so.\n\nNow, where is my son …?
I respect their choice … but the village just won't be the same without them.
I'm like a wading bird in a dried-up pond, traveler. Hoping for fish when all I have is mud.

The Wilderhall is just east of here. The rite may be just what Laeni and Clendagal need. What Vashabar needs.\n\nI suggest you take it over to Ciiril when you find the text. She'll be instrumental in enacting the rite.

My pie-flinging friend! I have a lot to do. You wouldn't believe how many Jubilee Cakes are required to fulfill our customers' orders. But whenever you get a craving for something sweet and delicious, think of Chef Donolon and his apprentice, Mogh!
Quickly, I can weaken the ward holding Hyacinth, but I need you to deactivate the focusing pillars! There should be a button on each, I think.
Zayabi didn't make it? \n\nYou and Zerith-var saved who you could. Thank you, walker. I will write an ode to your bravery. Just after I finish a hymn in remembrance of Zayabi and Ta'khida.
My faith and your strength will see us through this. I know it. Now, let us find the cantors.
I hate to admit it but Agmund is right. Our accursed debate on the Molag Bal Paradox is what got us into this predicament.
Strange. I can feel Wisteria's presence. This is rather remarkable. \n\nI have never experienced magic like this before. It feels … overwhelming.
Well done! I'll return to Beragon's townhouse. Good luck at the other locations, comrade.

This is my end, pathwalker. Hermaeus Mora has declared me a threat to reality and comes to imprison me. I am tired of fighting. It is the same on every path I have examined. If this is my fate, so be it.\n\nTake my tirum weed and go with my blessing.
Another daring rescue by you and Tanlorin? How impressive.

I'm glad we got the pest problem from earlier sorted. Llaren and Julian had me crawling under the most awful and dusty places looking for rats, spiders, you name it.\n\nNo more of that, thank you very much.
All that magic … you just transformed it? How?\n\nDon't answer that. I know you're in the dark as much as I am. Go speak to the Crow.
Hermaeus Mora's plan seems cruel, even for a Daedric Prince. Imprisoned, forgotten for an eternity. It is an unspeakable punishment that I cannot allow to stand!

My last publication was on the past major Goblin wars. What started them, the factors and variables that drove all these different Goblin tribes to war.\n\nJerntann is recreating the exact conditions of Bone Cliff Battle!
Place your hands on the altar. Feel the magic. Let it stain your fingers.
You've taken to this well, your early steps to master Scribing. But from here, I must take my leave. Return to the Scholarium.\n\nUlfsild, I believe, wanted her inheritor to walk this path alone.
Best not to overstay our welcome. Run along now before my niece decides to make us clean up this mess.
The fawn is safe. My strength returned. And you have had a moment, I hope, to reflect on power and its wise application.
You can't let the Recollection gain a foothold here. Wipe them out.
Julian and I placed bets on what the pest would turn out to be. Turns out we were both wrong. Which, really, is the second-best option to being right.\n\nDid you need my help with something?
If this Fox really was a friend of Ulfsild's, you'd think she'd have taught him not to deface books.\n\nSorry. Did you need something?

This is what Ulfsild's notes were pointing to. I know it. After everything we've learned about her, I don't think she would have sent you on this tome chase for nothing.\n\nI know this is what she wanted you to do. But, um. Just in case. Good luck.
I was sure hoping no Thalmor bastards would figure out I left a trail. Sorry to toss all this on you, Bogcup.
I think Pim was going to meet with my uncle. So, you might be able to find her at the family farm near Gray's Hollow. \n\nI really hope you can help this situation before things get too bad.
You listened to the echo? I think she's talking about the portal room, but we searched it three times over.\n\nThere's no fable in there.

I can't thank you enough. If only I'd been a hair quicker—but Val's alive. That's all that matters now.\n\nBack in the cellar, with Caelum and the fire. It might sound crazy, but I feel like that should have been me.
By the Eight, it's nothing less than a miracle! Valenia just survived the fatal blade, thanks to you and Hooke. But I see divine providence at work as well.

Thank you for what you did back there. It's my fault Caelum got his hands on Val and hurt her. Me and my drunken ideas about splitting up. \n\nI need to tend Val's wounds. Can't just drink my way through this one.
What do you have there, traveler? Something is wrestling about in your bag like a fellrunner on fire.

I'm sorry you had to see Naku struck down like that. If I hadn't been so distant, then maybe we would have come together to meet this threat sooner.\n\nPlease make sure Hooke doesn't do anything he will regret at Caelum Vineyard.
The mysteries and oddities of Oblivion will never cease to amaze. \n\nAre you all right? Keshargo does not know of anyone else who has been exposed to the knot and survived.

Keshargo's sending you into the citadel? Good. Xoryn doesn't deserve the knot, no matter what he thinks.\n\nJust remember to bring the arcane knot out in one piece. I can't test my null arca without it.
It's good to see someone who still knows how to follow orders. Did you make it to the fort? Did you find my squadron?
What's that? Ah, the Rite of Propagation. Only a very small number of copies are left in the world. Do go carefully.
The Dragon's challenges were particularly taxing for Ulfsild. I hope you're not losing too many feathers dealing with her.
With your allies at your side, seek understanding of my mind. Craft a riddle that will confound my thinking and ensure your success.
I am occasionally fond of the Netch's levity. However, if you are short on patience for playful antics, you may find this a difficult trial.\n\nWorth it, I think, on your path to master Scribing.
About to power up the altar again, are you? Don't let me stand in your way!
What a marvelous game we just played! And you did it without my lithe and stylish tendrils. \n\nEven I must admit I could not have done it better.

Are you a healer with the clinic? Please. We came as soon as we heard. I need my father to know I made the journey. The way I last spoke to him … it can't be the last time. It can't.\n\nI never wanted him to pass from this world alone.
I know this is a public clinic, but unless you're here to help, I'd ask that you leave my husband in peace.

I'm at the end, aren't I? Dragon Bridge. My blood warmed the icy water. I should have died that day.\n\nMaybe I did. Marielle. Blackberry mead. Borderwatch. Elic, my life's pride. Were all those warm memories just the dreams of a dying young soldier?
You're back! I assume that means good things? Or that the Daedric Princes are very angry with you.
Have you found Burnbiscuit yet?
I have never seen Viti so distraught. Talk to her, walker.

Years ago, these halls served as quarantine in times of plague and famine. Those who suffered from physical or spiritual illness were locked away, forgotten. Like this one's sister, Eifa.\n\nHer remains are … there. Where she fell.
This Wood Elf is so angry with me. I'm sure he has reason to be. I just wish I knew what drove my vanity to such crimes.
We make a pretty good team! Not as good as Gryphon and I, but still. Not too shabby.\n\nI'm glad you're trying to restore the scholum. The scholur. Ulfsild's library.
The Princes should cause you no trouble, if the Fox plays his role correctly. You have nothing to worry about.
Ulfsild gave up so much when she left the Scholarium behind. It sounds like she found her own path, in the end. \n\nMakes me feel better about … all of this.

Aut'arioth could meet no more fitting end.\n\nInheritor, you've come all this way on the wings of fables. Let me tell you one final story. In the last days of the Scholarium, Ulfsild's heart was filled with sorrow.
Even in my nightmares, I have never seen a sky like this.
I can't say I've ever crossed an invisible bridge before, but there's a first for everything right? \n\nRight. We can do this. No problem.
Ack, leave me be. There are others who could use your help.
Stay sharp. The monsters may be contained in Leftwheal, but there's nothing stopping them from breaching the outer walls.
Are you in need of healing? I'm stretched a little thin, but I can mend your wounds if need be.
My cubs, please, I don't know if they made it out.

Chronicler Firandil at your service. Chronicler of tomes, scrolls, scripts, and otherworldly delights! \n\nI'm glad that I was able to make the trip. I think you'll find my skills quite valuable on this most unexpected expedition.
It's a strange road, friend, but I'm with you all the way to the end of it. Let's finish what we came here to do.
It's not my choice of battlefield, but we have to make our stand somewhere. The Shardborn must be stopped.
No one's ever had any problems staying in Legion's Rest before. This is so bad!
Let's go talk to Snapdragon and make sure she's all right. \n\nAnd don't worry. Despite her name, she doesn't bite. Much.
If Wisteria is here, she's probably deeper in, searching for that nonexistent journal. Let's see if we can find her.
The Gardener is the Proxy Queen's uncle? That certainly clarifies some things. But it also raises even more questions!

Friend, I've been struggling. There's a traitor in the Garland Ring. I still can't understand it. \n\nI've been anxious to move, to do something. Well, thank Auri-El, the wait is over! I got a letter from Hyacinth.
Good, it's you! We must act quickly. Hollowjack is going to return!
Speak to Krin'ze, tamiit. Spirits rarely act as Talbira's did today. You should see what she has to say about her experience.
Please, tamiit. Let me have this moment.
Not now, tamiit!
Oh, hello! Are you here about the flier? Allow me to—bah, I'm sorry. I'm getting ahead of myself without even giving you a chance to speak. It's a stressful period.\n\nMay I help you?
This one knows better than to take the word of a necromancer.\n\nThe others may be lost, but Viti will not let your influence spread to young Krin'ze. She stays with me.

The Albus family is killing these soldiers. They're powerful and cruel. I trained with Cato Albus's nephew Vandorallen in the Battlespire and he buried nearly everyone he dueled.\n\nClear a path to those doors. I can keep watch.

Are you all the help that's coming? It didn't sound like there were many of you and we have a lot of enemies to fight.\n\nOrpheon the Tactician's army is tearing this island apart trying to get to my Elder Scroll.
Zerith-var seems overly protective. I suppose I cannot blame him. Not after what we saw in his memories.
Zayabi. I can't believe she's gone.\n\nSorrow fills me. But the songs of Krin'ze and Viti are a balm. I will not let this darkness eclipse my heart. Thank you for saving us.
The sound of the drums. It's gone. Thank Azurah.
Prince Azah and Gabrielle got the representatives here. Now it looks like the rest is up to you.

No more talking until I get those mistscrub leaves. It grows southwest of here. By the water. Bushes with jagged red leaves.\n\nCome back and then we'll talk. I'll be here. Not like I can get very far in this condition.

Go on, friend. Talk to your alliance's ambassador. Prince Azah and I will take the other two aside and do the same. We need them to see the benefits of working together to stop the Worm Cult and their soul reapers.

Last time, the Worm Cult sought to drag Nirn into Coldharbour. Now, Mezamma wants the souls of every living person to gain favor with Molag Bal.\n\nI still can't make sense of the whole picture. We need to keep searching.
I must see to it that Sister Chana comes to no harm. Garvin is a tracker, you will not evade his gaze for long. But you can defeat him. So do it.
Prince Azah insists that all of Tamriel is in danger. Would you care to elaborate? I need more details if I'm to make a recommendation of any sort to my superiors.

Shando-ri's story echoes my own. It is a relief to know I am not the only one of Azurah's children to be sent back from the Crossing.\n\nHe is as lucky to have your aid as I am. Let us continue, tamiit, and see to the deliverance of this Arum-Khal.
Prince Azah insists that all of Tamriel is in danger. Would you care to elaborate? I need more details if I'm to make a recommendation of any sort to my superiors.

Gabrielle tells a compelling tale of necromancy and Daedric cults, but I am not yet convinced that the Pact is truly in danger. Why don't you elaborate on why I should believe that the Worm Cult has returned and is a significant threat to the land.

I grew up around men and women such as these, comrade. I know how to lead opposing sides to equitable solutions—or thought I did. But these representatives confound me with their hardheadedness.\n\nSee if you can talk sense into your ambassador.

Don't get me wrong. You're very attractive, and I'm sure you're very nice. But I'm not seeing any new suitors. \n\nI have my hands full already with that pathetic young man you probably saw standing around outside.
Tell me, friend, tell me! Did Guendeline like the necklace? Will she finally accept that my feelings for her are real?
Lieutenant Harim was scouting near the lighthouse. Maybe he's figured out where the Bloodthorns are holding the Duke by now.
She belongs to me! Stay away, Intruder!
I appreciate your confidence in me. I'm sure Count Verandis can teach me to control my … urges.\n\nI just hope my sister can forgive me for deciding to live.

If you've come to Firebrand Keep to petition for help from the Knights of the Flame, I'm afraid you'll be disappointed. \n\nI'm ashamed to admit it, but the order's been divided. Myself and these others have been expelled from the keep.
I don't mean to be rude, but I'm in the middle of making a necklace for House Dorell. Please, let me focus on my work.
S'rashi never forgets a friend, and you have been a spotless friend.\n\nS'rashi will forever be in your debt. If you need anything in Wayrest, you tell S'rashi and he will make it good.
Count Hosni is in residence, but no one gets into the party without an invitation.
I've got my orders. No one gets in without an invitation.
I've been cooking and cleaning for the countess for six years. I can't understand why she would send me away.\n\nI'm not going to leave town though. I'm hoping she'll realize she's made a mistake.
What are you waiting for? Get those healing supplies to Heloise.
Oh, there you are! Are you ready to try again?
If Sir Hughes really wants us to go to war, I'd prefer he told us himself.
I didn't join the Knights of the Flame to sit on my hands. If I die in the coming battle, at least I'll go down fighting.
My first order of business now will be to shatter that mirror into a million pieces. \n\nNext, and possibly even more important, I need to find out which of my suitors gave me the accursed thing.
Though order has been restored here at the keep, the question of Sir Hughes' whereabouts remains unanswered.\n\nWe need him here. Our problems won't be fully resolved until he returns.
My sword is forged of consecrated steel, and dedicated to the cause of purging evil from these lands.\n\nTake it and finish what I started. It will aid you in your quest.
My book?

Ha! I was starting to doubt Captain's story, and you come sauntering up like some hero from the stories. It's perfect.\n\nThat nasty slaving outfit you embarrassed at the lighthouse—they took over this village, and they've got the rest of our crew.

So our sweet Breton sister has departed? So considerate! \n\nBah! Janne always planned to return to the road. This one is not surprised she left. Wish her well. Perhaps this is the way for Dro-Dara also.

More I think about it, the more I wonder why we stayed here this long. A true Nord dies with his axe in hand, not a pitchfork.\n\nBesides, this is more swamp now than farm. I spent years building that levee. Damn ogres!
I've never felt anything like that hunger, that compulsion. The things I thought of doing to Crelie ….\n\nHow long will my thoughts remain clear? I must take advantage of the time I have left.
Thank goodness Godrun's finally awake.
So you're the hero Grandmaster Durak keeps telling us about? You're here at the perfect moment. \n\nYou like to fight ogres?
The Cave of Dreams is on the rise north of here.

I would send one of the Spirit Wardens to Wayrest, but after everything we've been through, they need rest.\n\nI'm glad I can rely on you in these troubled times. The king trusts you, and I know you'll get the message to him quickly.
Now, let's see. I gather you want a piece of the Midnight Union's action. As for me, I have a family situation that needs to be sorted out.\n\nThat's where it might get ugly.
I won't hold you up any longer. As much as I enjoy your conversation, I think the situation in Gavaudon takes priority.
Do you have them? Do you have the relics?\n\nPlease. I must know. Show them to me.
She wavers in and out of consciousness. I hope we did not wait too long.

Once you get there, I'm sure the Reachmen won't know what hit them.\n\nLook for Sergeant Antieve in Northglen. He was just sent there, but with Captain Hjurrun dead, he's one of my most senior officers. I suppose I'll need to give him a promotion.
You've done it! The Seventh Legion will be our prey.
I wish there was another way, but if this allows me to rejoin my brother, so be it.
That smell … it's the same that's coming up from the johads. Is that what was in that bottle you picked up?\n\nJahi will never believe me, but I want to find out who did this as much as she.

Welcome to Sentinel, wayfarer. If you've come to tell me about the docks, rest assured, I already know. \n\nI regret that you visit during such times, but perhaps your arrival is fortuitous. Perhaps you can help us fight the Withered Hand.

I don't wish to sound ungrateful, but you should know that kidnapping me was just a distraction. \n\nThe Withered Hand has been planning this for years. If only we had heard the rumors sooner. At this point, I'm not sure we can stop them.
Do not ask Tu'whacca to wait any longer. He calls for Uwafa's blood. You must give it to him.

Do you understand why I am concerned? Some of the greatest heroes in history are buried here—kings, queens, legendary warriors …!\n\nIf they've risen, it is Ash'abah duty to kill them, and that's not going to be easy.

Tu'whacca guided your footsteps here at the perfect moment, brother. \n\nThere is Ash'abah work to be done—the Withered Hand has taken over the port. The situation is … strange though, to say the least.
The ward has been broken and the dead walk in Alik'r. Will my sacrifice be in vain?
Have you decided?
You have more experience than our other students. I would not have accepted you as one, but I trust the judgment of the disciples.\n\nAnd, of course, you've done well thus far.
To think it has come to this! Never in my years of study has such a case been brought forth! Never!
It pains me to see my master brought low by that fiend, but I know in my heart that this is what must be.\n\nThank you for making the hard decision. It was right and just.
Well … it seems my efforts to shield the Magistrate from security concerns have landed me in the stocks.
Oh! Have you come to help? Did my sister send you?
You now know the truth of your heart.
When the rest of the Alik'r desert falls to the Withered Hand, know that you will still be welcome in Bergama, wayfarer.\n\nYou will always be welcome in Bergama.
There's little in this world that I hate more than spiders. What a nightmare!
Despite your success, this is one report I'm not going to enjoy writing up.
Thank you for helping Master Muzgu see reason. \n\nHe's an important monk among the Spirit Wardens … and a good friend.
You're just like them. You're trash!
I can handle myself, all right? You just worry about those Supernal Dreamers.
That Adima is no lady. I doubt if she's even human.

I'm actually jealous, you know. I've always wanted to see the ruins of King Aphren's Hold.\n\nAll the stories I've heard about the sword, the hold, the king himself. I'd go along, but I have no stomach for fighting the spirits of the dead.
There isn't enough action in Daggerfall to keep an old soldier like me busy.
My house is just past the market. It's the only place I'm sure is safe enough to have this discussion. \n\nI'll be there as soon as I've settled matters here.
Whoever you are, you've got to help me.\n\nI know what this looks like, but I can assure you—I have committed no crime.
I hope they're at least asking for a decent ransom.

This young man is lucky to be alive, though I'm not sure he realizes it.

He told me about the message from the castle. The whole thing just seems a little too convenient, though, doesn't it?

I can't release Dame Dabienne. Not yet.
I do not understand why are we are still being prevented from coming ashore.\n\nSurely the constable doesn't still think we mean the village harm.
This is like some terrible nightmare!
Pascal has always been gruff, but just below the surface, he was a gentle man.\n\nI simply don't understand what's happened to him.
Thank the Eight you came back. Do you know what's going on? \n\nSome creepy man named Sentulus was here, and then my mother tied me up and left!

Yes. He said it was time to pay the Bretons back for what they did to Orsinium! He wasn't acting like himself at all ….\n\nI didn't know what to do. Luckily Abbot Durak was there. He zonked the general out with some kind of spell.
So Count Hosni kept his word. \n\nMaybe he hasn't changed as much as I thought.
Good thing you showed up. Now I've got a good story to tell back in Orsinium!
Gods, I hate waiting. Give me names and I can act!

You must meet with Wyress Ileana. She was the first to sense the disturbance and may know more about Reach magic.\n\nWe have to find a way to stop this or the very earth around us will perish. Please, find my sister on the road north of this mill.
We can help once you get those nobles out. My guards are itching to hunt down those brigands. Just be careful. And good luck.
May the Wyrd Tree shelter you and keep you safe.
All visitors are welcome to <<1>>. If the Daggerfall Covenant is to succeed, we must all respect one another.\n\nThe king and I are of one mind on this matter.
Word came back that Mother Murk was slain. Thank you.\n\nI was worried that she would come after us again. And she certainly would have attacked anyone else traveling through this forsaken bog.
I'm not sure I like it, but this may be the only way to reveal Faolchu's past. \n\nExamine the ripples in the battlefield and see if Sarvith's doorway is out there somewhere.
They'll be time for questions once we get paid.

Father's too old to have to deal with the johads. That's why it's fallen to me to take charge.\n\nIn truth, I've no interest in the business. But after the mess my younger brother made of this place, it seems I have to.
I am to blame for the curse on Westtry—and on my beloved Rosalind. My one desire is to see her freed from this terrible bondage.

I hope I needn't remind you to keep this quiet. Rumors will spread about the Withered Hand, but we should try to keep the theft of the Ansei Wards a secret.\n\nI have many political enemies who will try to turn this to their advantage.
I'm glad you're back because I wanted to thank you. Really. I did. Do.\n\nUm, thanks.
If we ever get back to town, the drinks are on me.
Ha! It worked! I knew it! Into the past and back again!\n\nEr … are you all right?
The next step is to take this information to Camlorn.
I heard a whisper echo through the forest. Was it the guardians? Did they talk to you?
You've done it. Camlorn is ours again.\n\nBut tell me, what happened with Faolchu?
If you can restore our relics, perhaps my faith will return, and we can restore the temple.
Another bandit in my house? Have at thee, I say! \n\nHow was that, my dear? Did I sound fearsome?
It worked! I was terrified and I don't mind saying so.\n\nOf course, my husband thought this was all just a grand adventure.
By Akatosh, that little trinket better be worth all the trouble we've gone to.
You're back. I could use your help with the Midnight Talisman.
If we retake Camlorn today, it will be because of you.\n\nBut keep your wits about you. It's not over yet!
Please, go talk to Dame Clarique. I need a moment alone.
The Lion Guard entered the city as planned. When Faolchu fell, his army broke. \n\nWent like clockwork. It would never have happened without me. And when I say me, I mean you.
Destroy the vines growing in the Wyrd blossom circles and the guardians will appear. Then do whatever they command of you.
You're back? That bandit finally convinced me to let him help out. I hope I didn't make a mistake with my generosity.
Ildani appreciates your admiration, but this one is spoken for. \n\nYou can still be Ildani's business partner though. Go on now.
If you really want to help, get us into that inn.
Ah, another adventurer! Of course you know who I am. I'm famous, as you know. When it comes to ancient artifacts, no one in Glenumbra has more expertise than I do.
Take the side gate just inside the walls. We can't risk opening this gate yet.\n\nIf Darien lives, he must be told of our plan.
You, my friend, are the hero of the day. \n\nHowever, though I hate to mention it, we still have Angof to deal with.
He came out and now he's begging us to kill him. Whatever happened in there, he seems to be himself again, but … I just wish it didn't have to end this way.
It is a privilege to meet you, I'm sure, but I am on official business for Queen Arzhela.\n\nI most humbly take my leave.
Did you get the pillars activated? As soon as you do, I'll sneak around and meet you in the lower ruins.
Don't think too long. I'll go down there and get the tools myself if I have to. \n\nThey're in backpacks, by the way. I bet Stibbons didn't even tell you that.
Can't … see. Is someone there?
You … don't I know you? It's so dark, and I'm simply too tired to think.\n\n<<1>>'s wandered away and left me to die. To think that the world might be denied my brilliance!
Our trust in you was well-placed. We do not celebrate the girl's death, but the life of the forest will finally grow to its true potential.\n\nWe know it was not an easy choice.
I know it's unlikely, but I'm hoping that if I'm alive, maybe my father is too?\n\nMaybe Dame Valyrie is right. Maybe the gods are giving us a second chance.
If I was younger, I could instantly purge the poison running through this young lady's veins.\n\nNow it takes all my strength just to keep her breathing, the poor dear.
I'm afraid you've come to our little hamlet during quite a rough patch. Keep a watchful eye on everything around you, my dear.

There's one more thing you should know. Lady Laurent hired this thuggish Tamien fellow, and I believe she already asked him to recover her tools.\n\nYou should speak with him up on the ramparts and tell him we have it taken care of.
Why … what happened? My head hurts.
That's good work, but we can't drink to it here. Darling Gabrielle can't hold this portal open for long, and I need you on the other side to pay my tavern bill.\n\nLet's go.
Anyone who stands up to Sternis Gelves ends up in the Crosswych mines. He works his prisoners to death down there.\n\nWe need to close the mines and take that resource away from the Red Rooks.

Thanks to this successful campaign by the combined forces of the Dragon Knights and the Lion Guard, I suspect King Casimir will finally throw his full support behind High King Emeric. \n\nThat will put the whole Covenant together.
Know this: like all things, the Pearl was covered in sand.\n\nThus, it came to belong to Zeht, who works the land.
You look like you could handle yourself in a fight. You should join up! \n\nI hear they're taking on new recruits in Daggerfall.
The negotiations are ongoing as we speak. Your job: stop them any way you see fit.
Good, you found the perfect spot for ….\n\nWait, where are the others?

Do you believe in fate, my friend? What if I said I was sitting here all my life waiting for you to come? That would be absurd, wouldn't it? \n\nNo … fate led both of us here at the perfect moment, and I can prove it.
That looked painful. I wish he hadn't been so stubborn.

Medya allowed her son to kill Sir Etienne, but you are right in requiring a trial before she is put to death.\n\nEvermore's people need to hear from her own traitor's lips what happened here—and why it happened!
You'll need to talk to the guard by the cave entrance before you go. They don't take kindly to unexpected visitors.\n\nDraven's my husband—tall, handsome fellow. Tell him I'm still waiting.
Some of the townsfolk have already turned back into their werewolf form. The spell is breaking faster than I thought.\n\nDraven must complete the ritual.
I'm not going to tell you anything.\n\nYou should throw out your stew, your warm ale, and whatever else you have.
I can't wait to enter my new lizard! Thank you again!
I know it's hard to tell what's wrong, but my hands are bound behind my back. Maybe you can do something about that?
I trust your lizard is still well. Please let it know I asked after it!
I meant what I said, wayfarer. Someday your song will be sung in the Chants of Praise.\n\nIn the meantime, you are always welcome in my court.

It seems all these years of mining still have yielded me nothing. I think perhaps it is time I considered a new career. \n\nHaidar would have been disappointed, but if he has passed, he will never know anyhow.
I am finally free!
I hope someday we'll be able to repay the favor for your services here today.\n\nThe Baandari are elusive. Without you, I'm sure their business would have continued to flourish in Sentinel.

If you're looking for <<1>>, I saw him run down to the beach a moment ago.\n\nHe goes down there sometimes, but I don't think he fully appreciates the site's history. He probably is just catching some fish for dinner.

Please stranger! We mean you no harm, yet you enter our domain with distrust, killing our disciples.\n\nMy mistress says you have been misled—that you should help rather than hinder us in our endeavors.
I hope you're enjoying your stay at the Sisters of the Sand.\n\nPlease be sure to let <<1>> know if you have any problems!
If you're looking for assistance, you should speak with <<1>>.\n\nI've just begun my apprenticeship.
Go, don't worry about me. My faith's been justified this day more times than I care to count.\n\nI'll be better presently. But this is the last adventure for the Sly Scarab.
You have chosen wisely. For a moment there, I feared the Nereid had affected your mind as well. \n\nI can see you are stronger than that now.
So, I'm going to take a wild guess here.\n\nAll that commotion coming from the ruins? That was you, wasn't it? Heh. Good work.
If even the tiniest drop of my family's blood is spilled, I'll kill you with my bare hands.\n\nRemember that.
The stolen goods are in the inn? Well, get back in there and find them!
Stop talking to me! Bad voice, go away! Mother, please help me!\n\nWe'll make you better, Mother! I promise!
You're here! Did you find my daughter?
That Breton needs to shut his word hole. Every time he opens it, vile lies bubble out. It's embarrassing.
I'll return to the alchemist shop on the other side of town once you go to meet with her.
The sands shift constantly, though the hearts of men should remain constant. Or so I've heard.
I never expected to see my daughter again, yet here she is! You are like sweet water from Tava's winds, stranger.
Speak to Tanval. He's been asking for you.
If we survive the next few minutes, you'll have my thanks. For now, there's no time for talk.
Pure rains make sweet rivers.\n\nYour wisdom is your strength.
Have you made your decision?
Tribunal curse you, s'wit.\n\nTo have wasted such a potent power. Remember this the next time Davon is attacked.
Girvas is wrong. <<1>> would never abduct a Dunmer.\n\nIf anything, she would slay the Dunmer and display its corpse with pride.
Did you find Strikes-from-Shadows, my fine f'lah?
Cracking through the husk of a fallen legend, your own tale will grow tall and strong.
Much better. That's one I owe you.
The soldiers have been warned. I think I know a way to find the assassins lurking about the fort.

There is one thing to know. I don't want to waste this opportunity because you made a foolish mistake. \n\nThose in the past will see you as one of Balreth's soldiers. Act the part. I can't say what will happen if you don't.
She's not with you? \n\nMuck water! She's gone off to do something brave, hasn't she?
Watch for Seeks-the-Night. He is like a vile mist that slips through the narrowest of cracks.
You're still here? Get moving. <<1>> should be able to get you started.
Somehow, I remember you. Your face is familiar. \n\nVunal has bound me in service. I am to provide you with aid. Are you ready for the vision to return?
You found the brothers? That's welcome news!\n\nThe only cave I know of is just west of the sulfur pools. I don't know where else the matriarch could be.
I know, my friend. I should help you, but you're so much braver than I am.\n\nGo, honor Mavos once more. We must know what he knows.
Kill the Goblin warchief and the spider queen. We'll never get a better chance.
You saved my life. I'll never forget the debt I owe you.
You've saved <<1>>! You have my thanks.\n\nSpeak to <<2>>. He wants to reward your service. And you deserve it.
I knew skeletons weren't enough. I should have summoned some Daedra to protect this place.\n\nOr a fire atronach. That would have been good.
We're saving Stonefalls again?\n\nOnce Balreth is dealt with this time, I pray I can rest.
You found my sons? I'm in your debt. I'm sure they're on their way here now.\n\nThis cave they spoke of must be the one on the western edge of the pools.
Get in there, my friend. We'll be right behind you. Blood for the Pact!
Unbar the gates and find <<1>>.
I'm glad to see that you returned safely.
And so it is done.
Those damn Maulborn! Look at the trouble they caused! I just hope we've seen the last of those dung-heads around here.
Find Rhavil's house. I'll follow your progress through the spell I cast on you.
So, Dark Elf. Have you come to gloat about our Hist? Are you its murderer?\n\nSpeak.
Excellent. Take those components to my wife, Merarii. \n\nShe's in the keep to the south.

Get me the weapons. Then we'll tell you where the Maulborn hold the missing villagers.\n\nYou look like you can handle yourself in a fight. Prove yourself, and you can come with us when we launch our rescue mission.
Naryu told me you found a note at the Maulborn camp. That might be a link to the creator of the Llodos plague.\n\nThis drastically changes our stance on the situation here.
Well, well! Aren't you the fancy lad? \n\nWhat do you want, Elf? Come to complain about the Daggers? Go hide behind your mother's skirt, not the Nords.
Do you have everything <<1>> needs?
I never knew kwama could be so vicious!
Ah, the Etheric Totem. Excellent. \n\nNow we can do some good around here.
The creators of the curse have been invoked. Now we can put an end to this catastrophe.
Let's get this over with.
Thank you for helping us end this threat.
You have my eternal gratitude for your gift. Thank you.
Our scouts let you through, yes? You have courage to visit <<1>> despite the necromancers who torment us.
The law requires all newcomers to check in with <<1>>.
If the Dominion sent a large force to infiltrate Stormhold, they must have a camp somewhere in Shadowfen. It's time we take the fight to them.
Go ahead. Make friends with that … whatever it is.
You trapped us like this forever. Keep away from me.
Please … don't tell me about my son. I must be strong. For Kragenmoor.
Caution, stranger. Speak quietly, lest one of the Vanguard hear us.
A shame you're flesh and blood. I'd let you train, but my warriors might forget your squishy parts.
My hands are betraying me. I can't believe I listened to you.\n\nDid you kill that monster?
Is something amiss? <<1>> wasn't fast, but he was persistent.
I see no lingering effects from the <<1>>. Aren't you a hardy one!
Troll's blood, novice. You have that ore yet? \n\nRemember. It's in the Old Mine south of the docks.
When I saw those Dres raiders closing in, I thought we were done for. But you sure sliced a path through them!\n\nMaybe you can help me figure out what those fetchers are up to.
