The female Hlaalu merchant seems to understand our ways. She doesn't seem so bad.
Dark Elves view Ra-shadda's people as animals. They butcher the ones they do not enslave.\n\nRa-shadda did not believe their wicked, cowardly blood ran through you. He was wrong.
The firesap gel used to be Hist-Tender's. Alas, he has rejoined the One.\n\nFind the gel in the camp. Look for a rucksack. That might have it.
Come back once you have both the key and the book. I'll be waiting right here.

So now we understand each other. My problems are your problems.\n\nThe crews in this town are loyal to one thing: gold. This Khajiit has been buying a little too much loyalty. She might even think she can threaten my power.
You've got a look in your eye like you're onto something. Don't let me keep you!
Not now, please. I have a great deal on my mind.
Do whatever <<1>> asks you to do. I will wait here and pray to Azura.
Have you found Eroni's killer?
Sorry, can't help you. Sayne's running the shop while I mourn my brother.
On your way, stranger. I have no patience for small talk.
I heard about Gethis. Such a tragic end.
You understand the wisdom of my plan. Even the dead will serve the Pact!
Why are you speaking to us? Address our citizens, captain of the royal army!
<<1>> is indisposed. He informed me you've been assisting us in our recent troubles. Are you any closer to discovering the killer?

Many dying soldiers are being tended on the grounds of the temple. Do what you can for them.\n\nThose draughts you recovered are rare and costly things. We traded a guar for each one! I'm sure they'll help.
If you were the one working with <<1>>, please see <<2>>.
Good to see you here, soldier. We'll need all the help we can get.
Defeat <<1>> while you have the chance!

The urn you carry once contained the cursed souls of those who can never return to the Hist. It was punishment for their blasphemies against the Saxhleel. \n\nIt's lost some of its power through the ages, but it will still serve our purpose.
It can't be. It's madness!
Balreth is my older brother. You could probably tell that. \n\nHe's not usually like this. The last few days have been very trying.
Stop, traveler. \n\nNone may enter the Hollow without the express permission of Lady Almalexia.
I've seen invaders in the tombs. They must not stop the ritual.
Welcome to Mournhold, muthsera. While events in the Temple remain secret, the Ordinators know of your deeds.
Word of the Fort Zeren's savior has reached the city. We were told to watch for someone matching your description.
Some of my own children have betrayed me!\n\nI am rarely an angry god, but this time there shall be a reckoning.
Newcomer, aren't you? You've got to check in with <<1>>.
No further. \n\nThe vicecanons require all newcomers to report to <<1>>.
Find a way to kill <<1>> and I'll reward you handsomely.
Wasn't I clear? Please report to Walks-in-Ash in the ruins beneath the fort.
Welcome to the Mages Guild. Is there something I can help you with?
Yes, what is it? Not much time to talk. Important magic to cast, here.\n\nThere's a Daedra loose, and a binding spell is our best chance for getting that beast under control.
My sister is home safe because of you. More than that, you doused the flame in her head. \n\nShe will always have fire, but she will no longer burn. She will control it.
The Eternal Flames sit below the north and south towers. Scatter the ashes there, and may Vivec guide your hand.
Welcome to the Fighters Guild! You look like the capable sort. Have you come to answer the Guildmaster's challenge?
Honor to you and your house. What can I do for you?
On my life, I'll make sure this Hlaalu Elf gets out of here safely.
The command staff is right behind you, soldier. Get in there!
Don't worry about <<1>>, I'll patch her up.\n\nDid you find the keystone? <<2>> is eager to proceed.
By Sithis, it's about time. I can't believe it's taken this long to send someone. \n\nYou're here to free me, right?
Have you learned anything about the keystone?
You have it! Ah, I can sense its vile nature from here.\n\nGive it to me, and we'll begin the cleansing.
<<1>> says you're no skin-stealer. Please forgive my manners before.

How did you find us? Unless you're a skin-stealer. Keep your hands empty, if you please.\n\nBut you don't stink of death. You're likely what you seem. What remains for you to share is why you came here.
<<1>> left before the Dominion pushed out to the surface. I never saw his face, but that doesn't matter when anyone could be a skin-stealer. Anyone!\n\nBut not me, yes?
The bindings unravel at a mortal's touch. Not unlike how mortals unravel at my touch.\n\nGo on, then. Unravel.
Are you executing a contract at the moment?\n\nHeh. Executing.
Lead on. The inn is in the northeast part of town.
My mother found her way to the inn. Did you help her get here?
I listen for your path's end. I don't hear it, yet.
The duel is in the ceremonial chamber, outsider. Any Shadowscale would know this.
Please, get me out of here before those cannibals rip me apart.
A bold, yet careful approach. Like our own.\n\nOutsider! Look to the fire. Tell me what you see.
Thank you for coming. It was a foolish thing to do, but we are grateful for your presence.
Have you come to stop this scaleless milk-sucker? He devours our unhatched kin!
We must release the stolen sap and restore the Hist tree.
Behold her devotion, supplicant. She yearns only to hear my voice, but you alone are blessed with my presence … for now.\n\nI admit, the treachery she plans for you is quite touching.
Another journal? Amazing it's still preserved. May I see it?
The little ones are cunning and cruel. No doubt, they'll think of something terrible to do to <<1>>.
After a few shows of strength, those Goblins will be eating out of your hand.\n\nOh, just make sure to count your fingers afterwards. Filthy beasts.
Friend! Stendarr had a hand in your return to us, I think.
What are you doing here? I have enough trouble without outsiders bringing more.
You've proven yourself to all Shadowscales. None shall doubt you're the walker in shadow and in light!
Doshia! That such a weakling could take one such as Merric ….
The dreugh are noble creatures. Do not blame them for their part in the death of my friends. The river of their fates was poisoned by the Dominion.\n\nMay you always find sweet water, my friend.
From the screams, it sounds like <<1>> is belowdecks.\n\nWatch it. We don't know how long the pirates have had that Fang. They could all be crazier than wamasu.
Shadowscales … these guys are trouble. Be careful!
I'm sorry. I'm dry with distraction. If you're looking for a recruiter, my aides should be able to help you.
I've got to get to Aldcroft. Meet me there.
What is that?
You've returned. What did you learn?
While you assisted my students, I had another vision. I see that your fate is fundamentally tied to the chaos-bringer, Magistrix Vox. However ….
I just wanted to make sure you were all right. I swear!
Welcome to the ruins of Abagarlas, comrade. Ancient home to a foul den of necromancers and Molag Bal worshipers.
Stendarr shield us! The Earth Forge overrun with undead.
I … don't feel well. My head hurts.
I can't wait to begin Ja-Reet's training.
Use the crystal, Adept.\n\nIt will prove you worthy … or lacking.
Well, what did you see?
Follow <<1>>! I think they're waking up!
They won't know what hit them.
I can hear the magicka singing with the talisman. The effigies are ready to receive your gift.
Leave me alone with my crystal. Only its sweet saccharine flavors can comfort me now.
Please get my crystal shards back.
Thank you again for saving the land of Test Realm! I couldn't be happier.
You have been amazing. Hopefully the Supernal Dreamersy will just drift away now.
You disappoint me.
Please deal with that witch quickly.
<cough> The pain flows away from me. Thank you.
The Egg must get to Mournhold. It's a symbol of our commitment to the Dunmer and the Nord, allies we sorely need in these times.
The touch of Molag Bal. Dries my scales just thinking about it. We have to stop their rituals, put an end to the abominations.
Destroy the totem. We'll be right behind you.
The third act always brings me down.

Let's get moving.\n\nThe ruins are just up ahead, and they won't investigate themselves! Just think—I might be the first to see them since the Yokudan! The first scholar, anyway. My captors wouldn't know a Yokudan ruin from an Imperial vault.
Our champion! My father would be so grateful, as I am.
Your kindness today … I can't repay it. All I can offer you is my thanks and the love of my family.
Without your help, we would never have been reunited. Thank you!
Without your help, we would never have made it. Thank you!
Please do hurry. She said it was important.
I'm afraid I don't have time to talk. I'm waiting for my husband to return to help me deal with this debt collector.

Andrin asked me to write a report on the damage to Riften. Then he forgot he ordered it. It's sitting in a pile of papers on his desk.\n\nI'm going to go drinking now. Because if I don't, I'm going to scream.
Ja-Reet and I will never have an easy life together, no matter where we go.
My clutch-brother may be no smarter than a Goblin, but he's family.
Goblins are odious creatures, and our poor egg-brother is trapped in there.
Remember, only one door leads to the right choice. Is there also a left choice? Directions! Who can tell?
My students return to the Hist, thanks to your help.
You're the one Holsgar pulled out of the water.\n\nI'm glad you're up. I could use your help.
Thank you for freeing me! Did Ulrich send you? Do you know where he is?
Look for a door inside the tomb with carved stones next to it. I'll find you after you unlock that door.
Follow squeak! I mean, follow me!
I'm trying to unravel the mysteries surrounding that book you brought me, but it'll take some time. Perhaps if you were to uncover other such books, I'd be more successful?
Sparkly crystals, sparkle in the sun. Rays of light from every one.
That cursed ship is the least of our worries. Bandits are plundering the mine, looking for artifacts.
Remember what I said, adept. Don't make the same mistake I did. A woman's life isn't worth personal power.
Lead the way. We're right behind you.
Tharn and I have much to discuss. His wheedling has not come as a complete surprise, but his value should not be discounted.
Forgive my mood, but I grieve for the Hist. It returns to the void, did you know?\n\nBut I must not dwell on this. The Pact is bigger than Shadowfen alone.
Ysgramor's heir indeed!\n\nThank you, my friend.
You've found <<1>>. No surprise that he'd be back first. He can never get enough to eat.
Ahh, Jofnir. I … wish the river's course had not flowed as it has. I shall be through the portal on your heels, comrade.
Go ahead, drink up! That mug of mead won't hurt you.
Lower Yorgrim is dying, stranger. We have nothing left to offer you. I suggest you find somewhere else to rest this night.
Come along. No time to waste. \n\nFollow me. Secret passage.
At last, I've found you! I've searched everywhere for you. I have an urgent message from <<1>> for you.
I don't want you to just find the assassins. I want you to hunt them down like the rabid dogs they are and dispatch them with haste and extreme prejudice.\n\nDo we understand each other, Champion?
Did you retrieve the flame atronach essences?
What are you doing? Don't stop to talk to me. Run!
It took you long enough.
Well glad to see you could make it. You think I like hanging around the docks with these people?
I hope you found the place all right.
<<AC:1>> must be prepared for travel. All must be merriment and good cheer!
I need to discuss strategy with the thanes and Pact leaders.
Ouze is safe from the Worm Cult. All we need to do is keep our heads down for a while.\n\nThey'll give up or wake enough of the guardians to get themselves killed. Works for me, either way.
Once you've empowered the totem, you will be able to use it. You will know when it is time.
Well, even if Spinner Indinael is going to stay for a while longer … I'm certain Gwilon and I will work things out.
Welcome to the Harvest Festival! Is this your first visit to Bad Man's Hallows?
I felt it. A shift in the planes. Is it done?
The village! I couldn't help them! So many dead ….\n\nOh Z'en, what have we done?
We'll watch over Scales while the cure does its work.
What do you think? Kireth trusts you, so I do, too.
If I ever get out of here, I will come after you!
Now that I have the key to operate the Dwemer memory device, we should locate the lore vault. If I remember correctly, the vault is hidden among the snowy chambers of the ruins. Let's go!
I can't believe this. It happened so fast.

There's one Keeper left, and I worry for her. Imiril guards the area closest to Rilis' prison. The two have a … strained rapport.\n\nOf all of us, the High Kinlord would bear the fiercest grudge against Imiril. The sooner you find her, the better.
Blood for the Pact!
Leave this place while you still can. We have nothing more to discuss. \n\nThe only reason you still live is because I gave you my word. Now go.
Still so much to do. So much death. Yes.

Have you dealt with the Steel Shrikes before? They're a nasty bunch of Redguards from Covenant lands. All about war, conquest and glory, and the rest of that rubbish.\n\nA complete nuisance on a good day, but today's looking worse and worse.

I suppose the Shrikes thought it funny to truss up a master of escape. Seems I'll have to practice with the rope a bit more.\n\nWe can't just let them get away with this. Luckily for everyone, I have a plan!
Lead the way. We'll be right behind you.
My axe! It feels good to have it back. It's part of me. Losing it was like losing an arm.
Hello, friend. I understand you continue to assist the Ebonheart Pact.
Well? Don't just stand there staring at me. I'm very busy and I don't have time to play seven questions.
With luck, we'll soon get reinforcements from Velyn Harbor.\n\nOnce Cirnean gets out, she'll want some entertainment. And by that, I mean she'll zap some Sea Vipers with lightning.
The magic of the Dreamstride weakens. You have one more chance to convince King Jorunn to wake up.\n\nFail and all three of you—you, the Dreamwalker, and King Jorunn—will be lost.
We've got their book and that blasted stone. We need to get under cover if you're going to do anything with them.
We need to take the book and the stone somewhere safe so you can examine them.
Yes. What do you want?
I'll stay here for a little while to fully recover my magicka. Thanks to you, I can shield us from enemies until then.
You dare address me? Insolent dog!\n\nThose who call themselves "stormwardens" are hardly fit for the title. They can barely control the storms, much less dispatch intruders from our sacred grounds!
We'd let the mammoths just sleep the effects off, but it might be dangerous for us to round them back up later. They're very docile in their pen. Honest.
The might of the Five Hundred is behind you, comrade.
Hakra and Valdur fighting at our side is a great honor. \n\nWhen we stop Thallik Wormfather, though, you will be remembered as the hero.

You've got the shards? Excellent! Keep them with you. They'll prove key to our victory, I'm certain.\n\nNow you need to defeat the guardian. Its power prevents me from any access to Silvenar. Do that, and I will contact you as I did in Jathsogur.
Is it safe? Did you find my husband?
If you seek an audience, I must apologize.\n\nThe King is busy and I don't know when he'll be available again.
You fought well and made us proud. Goodbye, friend.
Our ways are not your ways, outsider. Don't meddle in things you don't understand.
So. Aera was behind much of this, wasn't she? I don't pretend to know her reasons. All I want to know is whether you've dealt with her or not.
I'll never win any popularity contests with this group, but you should know that I'm grateful to you. You rescued me from the Castle of the Worm at great personal risk. I won't forget that.

I figured you'd be up here. Another contract completed by, well, you again. I wonder if the Tong is testing me or something.\n\nStill, a success is a success, right? I hope I didn't scare the ambassadors too badly.
You have been dismissed.
You have a sly look about you, stranger. I'm watching you.
Have you spoken with the thane's advisor, Borodin?
You're a scout, yeah? Sent by Gjakil? Quick, you've got to get word back ….
What luck. You denied me my vengeance in <<1>>. Had my beloved Silvenar still lived, he would have approved of your mercy.\n\nIt's your wisdom I need now. Tell me, would you aid my cause?
Sorry, need to focus. Imiril's going to be fine, but she'll need a healthy dose of restoration magic to get back on her feet.\n\nIf you must speak, speak with Cirion.
Taking coin from Turil. To steal from me? The Three take you!
This town is filled with criminals and cultists. Why did I think you'd be different? The silks I peddle would have been wasted on these barbarians.
That was her, Sage Tirora. \n\nI suppose I'll see her again, on the other side of the bridge.
Let's get out before any more spriggans are hurt.
My friend, I'm glad to see you again. We could have used you here.
The Worm Cult must not succeed.
So much remains to be done before <<1>> is safe.
Passion mustn't compete with duty.
Please, stop! I can't take this much longer.
Engling is right, we'll make sure songs are sung of your bravery here. I just hope this little event has taught these cubs a lesson about ancient lore. Some of those books bite back. Hah!
He's called a gathering of the Council of Province Generals at Fort Amol. You should find him at the Hall there.
Speak to <<1>>, <<2>>, and <<3>>. Choose one to fight by your side.
That must've hurt! Honestly, I didn't expect a barrier across the entrance.\n\nThe Cult must have set this up as a last line of defense in case they were attacked.
You'll find the Mistress of Incunabula in the snows of my homeland, at the Guildhall in Windhelm. Good luck, Adept.
How goes your tale, scribe of the spinners?
To the lighthouse! Finish off the Ra Gada captain! We'll take care of things out here.

The mercenaries wish to fight. Their blades must not be used against my people. So, we'll give them a new opponent.\n\nThey'll soon realize their courier's late. We must quickly return him to their ranks.
The lieutenant. Dead. I can't believe it!\n\nWhat are we going to do? Does the sergeant have any ideas?
Get in there! We need to know what the Reach are up to. Be careful though. Don't want to have to explain to Jorunn why you're dead.
By the light of Auri-El, you've returned.

<<1>> writes as fast as possible, but still these spinners come up with more to say! After uncountable generations, they still change the story.\n\nDo you know the story of the Silvenar and the Green Lady? Or I should say, one of the stories?
Luck. Pure luck. Happens once in a while. Don't let it go to your head.
You found the fire salts? Good job. Now find <<1>>'s kindlepitch and you'll be ready. Talk to him if you want to know more.
Please look for Lucius. Coldcorn Ruin would be the best place to start.
These ceremonies are important to my people, which makes them important to me. I guess.
Fair day. How goes the translations?\n\nWait. You're not one of Telenger's students.
I felt the cursed drawn back to these ruins. Just as I felt your touch release them back to Aetherius.
Something's happened. The spirits appear to be growing docile again.
Others doubted you, but I knew you could do it!
Without your help, we would never have killed <<1>>.\n\nUnfortunately, I've received word from the Smokefrost Peaks that forces me to ask more of you.
Now, to more pressing matters. Teldur has betrayed us!

All this standing around is driving me mad. I don't mean to question the king's orders, but I'm ready to strike back against these damn cultists.\n\nWell, if you're as anxious as I am to see us take back Honrich Tower, I could use your help.
A marvel such as I've never seen. If only there was a way to communicate with the beasts themselves!\n\nHm. I do hope their appearance won't attract attention.
What kind of an idiot carries a note around implicating himself? This kind, I assume.
You're not with the Houndsmen, are you? Are you one of Silvenar's loyalists? Please, I need help!
I'll meet you back at the camp. Go ahead and fight the Houndsmen! That'll distract them so I can escape!
Get over here! Before the Houndsmen sniff you out!
Stop! Get back! I tell you, I have friends, friends in high places!
Once the Queen has fulfilled her sacred duties I'll get her to safety in Firsthold. The sooner that happens, the better.
Now to ascend to the summit of <<1>> and defeat <<2>>!
Now on to the summit to kill <<1>>!
Each entertainer has a specialty, of sorts, that likely matches the tastes of the mercenaries. You'll just have to figure it out, I suppose.
We would never have made it this far without you. Now we must get to the summit and face <<1>>.
Eight watch over you. You'll find Urcelmo at the Mages Guild. Just follow the path behind me up and around. You'll find him no problem.
Hold there. Firsthold is under siege. We'll need you to head back to the main road.
I take it you spoke with Sinien? With the wards down, we can move on the castle. That's the key to retaking the city.
Just remember, it will take a moment or two for the ritual to do its work. I'd clear out the Daedra first. Assuming you don't want to be eaten.\n\nOh, and say hello to Razzie for me!
Stars guide you. Beware the spirits here. The dead do not rest as quietly as they should.
Make way for the champion, eh?
Nicely done, champion.
Is it done? Have the guards taken him away? I didn't hear any commotion.
I guess you've been of use. Good work helping them with that goo.
Amuur and I will be making the rounds soon enough. Check in on the people you spoke with.\n\nEverything's going to be all right. You'll see.
Last one! What's the answer?
Estre is vulnerable. But Tamriel is still open to the Deadlands. This must not be.\n\nWe must close her gates. End the threat of the Daedra.
Are you going to help me or not?
Please. Think before you make your decision.
Please. Just hurry. I can't stand the thought of those bastards dragging Nelulin around in that pit.
Very entertaining.
You sing like a dying goat. Nice work.
Move along now. Hendil and Amuur are the only ones allowed inside.
Good … good luck in here.
I'd swear we just left the battlefield at Boulderfall, eh? Blood and the Pact wait for no-one.
Thanks for the help, friend. At the least, those bastards won't be around much longer. And I get to keep all my treasures!\n\n<<1>> will get us to Anvil. She's a resourceful lass.
We'll get <<1>> to Anvil safely, don't worry.
Find anything?
No telling what would have happened in the Ragged Hills if you hadn't shown up.
At last! Someone with the power to aid my efforts.\n\nI am Farandare, and I've spent my lifetime trying to rescue the city of Falinesti. With your help, I may be able to do it.
Well, what are you waiting for?
I'm busy here. Away with you.
This place is an abomination. You can almost feel the hatred emanating from every rock.
Hail, my new friend! The touch of the divine inspired me, told me you'd succeeded in your task. Is it true?
Tread carefully. Remember, we need him alive.
So many good people lost these last few years. Don't let her death be meaningless.
Good luck in there.
Let us finish the task at hand. We can chat afterward.
What do you want? Wait, never mind. I don't want to know. I'm not taking on any fares today.
Do I know you? You look familiar. Could just be the spiced wine talking.
You need to leave this place, stranger. It will soon be crawling with Daedric shadows.\n\nWe've been in conflict with the Spider Cult for days, and it appears they have won.
Did you find <<1>>?
Today could have been worse. I could be dead.
Oh, I'm so little and helpless. I don't know what I'll do without someone brave and strong to save me.
You look like a capable sort. You haven't been eaten by draugr, at any rate.
Thank you for finding me. They were going to kill me too.
My daughter is found! And my no-good son as well, from what I hear.
You're back! You made it. Thank the Eight.
I hope the notes are still there!
It's all gone so horribly wrong. I only wanted to protect the village! But now ….\n\nMother, I can help you. Please, hold on!
Welcome to <<1>>. What can I do for you?
Ah, thank you for coming so quickly.
Moons guide you on your journey, my friend.
Anyone willing to hear us out is blessed by the Green in my book.
Sorry, my tiny friend, no room for you here. We've too many students of the Green already.
<He stares coldly at you.>
I'm led to believe you're the one to thank for Gorak's safe return. He even retrieved the General's dispatch.
You have outwitted or outfought the wayward Justiciars, no? You could not stand here otherwise.\n\n I, Bakkhara, wonder if you will lend me your skills. Great danger awaits below.
Don't test me. I'm in no mood.
I never thought I'd see my wife again!
Good luck. When you're done, meet me on the ship.
Choose. But choose wisely.
You've got promise, kid.
Hail the conquering champion!

The Bloodthorn attacked the town and took control of the place. We've been sent to keep an eye on things, but we're not to engage the enemy.\n\nStill, something about all this bothers me. I just can't put my finger on it.
Look at those dogs! Gathered around for a feast. Satakal take them all!
The archery range isn't far. I have more to tell when we arrive.
Succeed where I failed.
Let's go get my brother. Lead the way!
I may never understand why he did it, but I'll try to forgive my father for what he's done.
Quickly now, collect the skyshard so we can be gone from this place.
My poor Nelhilda. She hurts so much, but she refuses to drink more mead. Says she needs her head to be clear.\n\nI hope you found those flowers she went on and on about.
A ship has only one captain. I'm not used to taking orders.
What did you do? Why are the guards so hostile?
There you are. I've been looking for you.\n\nWhat in the Eight is going on? There was an awful commotion and then Angof disappeared.
This one thinks you need to be cautious. The champions are fearsome opponents.\n\nBut, please, try not to injure my fellow mages.
Ah, sweet freedom! Just as I expected.\n\nI wasn't expecting the cat and his friends, though. That's a bit of a surprise. Your doing, I take it? Well, pray tell, what shall we do now?

You know, you might just have to kill the Observer to end this game. I doubt you can do it, though, but I suppose you have to try.\n\nSorry. I have to tell it like it is. False hope can be so disheartening.
I really am sorry about your friends. Better them than me, I always say.\n\nNow, where are we going next, if I may inquire?
The outsider returns. And was your Trial of Spirit successful?
You again. Why are you still sober? What kind of a milk-drinker are you? Grab a mead and join the celebration.
Don't worry. A Proctor remembers those who were useful.
Horrible things … they've never done this before.\n\nI'm ruined. I should just let myself be eaten.
Thank you for dealing with the wamasu. Let's hope <<1>>  fixes the amulet before anyone else gets hurt.
Oh, hello there. Didn't see you approach.\n\nAre you looking for work? If so, I seem to need a new assistant for my research.
Some of <<1>>'s guard arrived to defend the fisher-folk and refugees. I thought to sneak along the beaches, see what I could learn. Then I saw you.\n\nSo, what should we do?
As always, Margot's totally blowing this out of proportion. Lucas is probably fine.
Please, this won't take long.
Ha! I just spoke a prayer to the Khenarthi for aid, and look who blows through the door!\n\nIt's always good to see you, even in a city riddled with pirates. But I must ask, why are here?
Leave me alone. I have nothing more to say to you.
<<1>> and I have a long journey ahead of us. In time, I hope she'll warm to me. I'm not a bad person. \n\nIn the meantime, I'll have to keep a better eye on her.

<<1>> was a hard-skulled fool, but convincing him to back down? Such wisdom … we could all learn from your example.\n\nOur fires are yours to tend, whether forge or hearth. You are always welcome in <<2>>.
Don't forget to touch one of the wisps. That's what activates the properties of the bark.\n\nGood luck. And I hope you find your friend before my clan kills him.
I'll look for you in the Hollow City. Who knows? Maybe we'll end up fighting side-by-side one day.

We run a delicate operation, and losing our workers to the marsh would have put our plans in jeopardy. Stranglers are harder to bribe than pirates, yes?\n\nBut if you're sticking around <<1>>, perhaps we could speak of  opportunity for coin.
Hello again, outlander. Your words remain with me. I find the challenge of building my own realm invigorating.
Ah, good! Everyone back in one place. I was beginning to worry!
Hey there, friend. You looking to run a frog?
Tin's a fussy metal to work. You want to chat, find <<1>> at the front gate.
<<1>> has enough excuse to flay my hide. I don't want to give her another.\n\nShe's looking this way. Leave me be.
<<1>> went to search for you in one of the collapsed passageways. You should try to find her.
I think this could be it!

Does the Pact-soldier need help to squash <<1>> flat? <<2>> helps! \n\nSwamp-lizards should be fought in battle, not destroyed in eggs. <<2>> enlisted to stop the Dominion's enemies, and Brute-vitar is bigger enemy than Pact or Covenant.
Don't delay too long. The Imperials usually kill prisoners.
You simply must come to the estate and perform like that for our guests. \n\nI know they'll relish it.
We watch. We wait. We pray these Orcs will go away.\n\nDon't tell Mistress <<1>>, but I can't help but think we are wasting our time.

Go on ahead. We're going to see if we can muscle through this door here while you search for an easier way to get it open.\n\nMy notes say that you'll find a mechanism in the Guardian's Helm that will help.
There is always more to learn where Dwemer are involved. Let us be off!

<<1>> burns bright. Once you've lit the fires, go after <<2>> while his mutineers focus on the dock.\n\nAnd don't be afraid to whistle for help. Those cretins stabbed my crew in the back. We're itching to return the favor.
The gods are fickle and not known for their patience. Please deliver those petitions.
Haskill, here again. Sheogorath is such a craven. Sending a toad like that one to do his dirty work.
The play is nearly done. Are you leaving the audience waiting? How avant garde.
Reinforcements at last! How did you do?
What was that? Head's still ringing. I … I think I'm going to lay down.\n\nOh wait, no … the captain said laying down was bad. I can't lay down. I'll keep counting my fingers until they add up right.
Go on with you, those chickens aren't going to roast themselves. Just remember to point the far end of the wand away from you. He's lost some followers that way.
Byz will not scream for help. Byz promises.
Some time this Era would be convenient.
Ha, good! Good! Don't let anyone tell you these spirit bastards don't know how to fight.
Come, let us find my sister. She gets up to all kinds of trouble if I leave her alone for too long.
Yes? Do you have something for me?
Keep it down!
What are you standing around for? I'm not proud of what we've decided to do, but we might as well get it over with.
Seems I've a lot to thank you for. I didn't expect you to go off and save my sister while I was away.\n\nGlad you made it here in one piece.
This one cannot take it again. I can't take losing to her again, I just can't.

Hello, hero. Good to see you got out of there in one piece. I understand that Almalexia can be a little rough on her toys.\n\nWhile you were getting cozy with the goddess, I discovered something interesting.
Accept my gratitude.
Who're you? You're not allowed in the chief's home! Get out!\n\nOh, I see. Yes, you'd better get out now.
You handle yourself well, champion.
Everyone here looks up to you and me. Can you blame them?
The Pact could use a soldier like you.
At last you wake. I was worried.
Some say I am obsessed with battle. They are wrong, I am obsessed with life. And life is war.
Crafty Lerisa, Jakarn, and Neramo are the ones I'm interested in. Recruiting any one of them would be great. Getting all three would be ideal.
Pains me to admit it, but you can handle yourself in a fight.

I overhead Feluz ask about his lucky pouch. That's where he kept his moon-sugar candy. I'm glad you didn't find it. \n\nFeluz said he'll never eat another piece, but I don't believe him. I'll be keeping a close eye on this one.
Excellent. Now you can stand around here wrestling idiots.
I've got such a problem.
I'm not sure you're supposed to be here.
If I found a handsome guy locked in a cell, I'd free him.
Great! <<1>> knows I have my treats. Why were you so obvious when you handed me the pouch?
This is the Blessed Crucible, where the fiercest fighters in Tamriel burn, bite, and slash each other for coin.
You did us a good turn. Rama owes his life to you.
She's dead! I can't believe it!
Seems like my guards let anyone in nowadays.
I hear you got Crafty Lerisa and her crew out of trouble. Good work. I can use someone with her skills.
You have my thanks, stranger! Truly!\n\nIt's paramount that the Ayleid warlord is not raised. I need you to check his body and—if he has returned—deal with him.
Kalari's a sweet kid. Reads to me sometimes. Hope you can help her out.
Hallowed, Khali is not prepared for what's required here. Choose me to contain the Dark Mane.
Damn it, old man! Apologies. That wasn't meant for you. You'd think that I'd be used to working with him, but ….
Hallowed, Shazah cannot contain this darkness. She does not have the strength. Choose me to take on this burden.
Looks like the plan was a success. Despite the collateral damage. Such is life, soldier.
Destroy the siege weapons, tents, and cargo first. Then go after the Colovian command. \n\nWe have a score to settle with these guys. We're going to take it personally.
Done already?
Watch what you track in here. This is Captain Kaleen's cabin!
You are very brave. May the Moons brightly shine down on your soul, as your soul shines out … in the night.
You will speak with the Clan Mother, yes? Shuzura will want to know all that you have done.
Welcome to the <<1>>! As you can see, the party is just warming up!
Bright moons guide your path. While you're in the field, keep your eyes out for a Khajiiti agent named Razum-dar. He's operating in the area as well.
I hope you recover our seeds before the Goblins eat them. Goblins aren't very bright.
Ahh, excellent. Andewen has finally sent me a stalwart assistant. We can set to work right away.
Bright moons, traveler. Welcome to our little town of S'ren-ja. \n\nTazia does not suppose you'd like to help her fix the bridge?
You help Kalari now, yes? Tazia tells this one you are brave, to face the spirits.
Raz feels he should say it has been nice to meet you. Do not worry, new friend. Just because you have killed him the first time you met him? This one will not hold it against you.
This one has found it is best not to keep Shuzura waiting.\n\nHe is just saying.
<<1>>'s not looking good. I need to get him out of here.\n\nDon't think either of us would've made it if you hadn't come along. I don't say this very often … thank you.
These cultists weren't much trouble. There was a portal open when we got here, but it closed when we attacked. Azlakha would know more.
Good thing you sailed in with Captain Kaleen. Outsiders aren't welcome on Betnikh, especially not now.
We need all the help we can get. \n\nI'd start with those enforcers. Someone has to stop them from harassing the townsfolk.
Hurry! Destroy the conduit.
Welcome to the Harborage, Vestige. This is as comfortable a home as an old dried-up husk like myself could hope for.
You … you are the Hallowed! You have come in our hour of need! Please, Moon Hallowed. We've been driven from the temple, and the Claw is in terrible danger!
Goblins. Don't you just hate them? I sure do. We work and they steal. There seem to be more of them every year too. When you get the chance, cut one in half for me.
The Daggers will find another way to get our start. Breaking the law for some pompous noble isn't how we'll get our reputation.\n\nJust keep Diel busy and I'll handle the rest.

As ugly as things may be out here, I heard a rumor that our real worries are inside the city. Someone said they're holding the Staff of Magnus in there.\n\nIf that thing fell into the wrong hands … well, I've heard it could destroy the Dominion.
Once the skulls are placed, I can speak with them to find out what they know.
I know Talmo wants his banner back, but I have a proposal for you.
Go! Travel to Moonmont, the ancient temple. You will learn what must come next, yes? Yes.
I can't thank you enough for helping me win my bet. I'd buy you a drink, but I need all my coin for …. cooking supplies. Yes, that's it, cooking supplies.
If anything has happened to At'avar ….
Thank you for exposing the cook's perfitudity! I'll make certain everyone knows she lets her intoxification rule her judgmentalism!
It was quite a thrill sneaking into Mannimarco's castle, embedded in the skin of Oblivion, crawling with the walking dead and soul-eating Daedric horrors.\n\nLet's never do that again, yeah?
You're very lucky. <<1>> risked her life by dragging you out of that poison gas. \n\nMost Imperials aren't so partial to members of the Pact, but she's naive.
Marius has grown very impatient. I'm almost certain he'll use the poison for personal gain. It can't fall into his hands.
Please find whoever you can and give them those potions. \n\nPeople won't last long out there. They need to be here, where it's safe.
I joined the Knights of the Flame to defend Alcaire, not for all this… politics.\n\nI don't even want to talk about it. You should speak with Sir Edmund before you go into the keep though.
Jone and Jode smile down upon us. Are you ready to enter the reliquary, the inner sanctum of Do'Krin?
Bright Moons above! The Hallowed! Please, if you have a moment. Would you help poor Felari?
I told you I never wanted to see your face again!
To have seen such things. The Path is truly a hard road to walk, Hallowed.
Clear the city, end the Daedric threat, and we can meet at the temple. We can usher in a new era of unity for this Aldmeri Dominion.
Very impressive, Hallowed. Very impressive indeed.
Your scent is one of victory. The city has been cleansed by your hand. You must bring the same closure to the Khajiiti people.
You have saved a precious jewel from devastation. My people thank you.
Walk carefully, you tread on sacred ground.
I am Hermaeus-Mora. The riddle unsolvable. The door unopenable. The book unreadable. The question unanswerable. \n\nI wonder if you understand why you're here.
Raz heard sounds of fighting. Did you catch up with Asteril? Were you able to question her about Pelidil?
Even if Asteril's fled the city, you might be able to find some clues about Pelidil's plans in her quarters. \n\nLet's hope you find something, because otherwise we don't have much to go on.
I could hear the fire salts exploding from here. Good work. My agents will make quick work of the Dominion's forces.\n\nNow, to end this. Do you still have the Relleis Lor keystone?

We're not overly fond of rules here in Bramblebreach, but I have to admit that it peeves me to no end when people come into my chambers and just loiter about.\n\nRun along now. I'm sure you have better things to do than sit around with me.
Keep staring, outlander, and I'll repay the sacking of Orsinium twice over. A few scratches don't bother me.
Welcome aboard! Let's get you disguised, and then it's onward to fortune and glory! And a bit of thievery.
Stay alert. I don't want to end up on that slab again.

You … I know you from Alcaire. You roughed up so many of my Bravos. Tamriel is a small place after all. I just returned from Alcaire myself. Back in my chair, drinking my wine with my wife ….\n\nWait. Please tell me you're not here to disturb me?
I can't stand the thought of that cultist directing Bruma's destruction from my old home. Kill him!
What's going on? Shadowscales, here? No—they can't be!
Tharn and the Dark Mane dare to tread on temple ground! Blasphemies against the Two Moons Dance. And corruption crawls the walls in Moonmont's inner chamber.

Welcome to my Court, outsider. Since you entered my domain, I have watched your actions with a keen interest. You have been generous with my people and more patient than I expected. \n\nBut I still cannot gather one thing—why have you come?
I'm so glad to be out of there. I never thought I'd see the sun again!
Show some respect. You don't want to make the boss angry, trust me.
Please! You must stop, listen to me. You have come to <<1>> for the games, yes? The gambling? My <<2>> is missing. I fear the worst and I don't know what to do.
Well … that one ran off even sooner than I expected. Come back some other time though.\n\nI'll figure out how to keep then under control. I know I will!
Speak to General Malgoth. I'll be right here.
Your lizard is the winner! You are an excellent judge of reptiles.

It is good to be back in this ancient city. I need to assess our strengths and weaknesses, determine how best to make our assault against Molag Bal.\n\nIf we strike before we build up a sufficient force, however, I fear we shall lose this war.

I recommend heading west first to find the Ayleid King, but the choice is yours.\n\nIf you wish to free King Dynar, you must recover the Lights of Meridia. The lights have the power to unlock his prison of darkness.
A noble effort, but this one thinks you could use a bit more practice.
I can't say I'm looking forward to seeing Tharn again.
You keep up nicely! I can't abide dawdlers.
The Elder Scroll of Ghartok has been captured by Dominion forces. A great victory!
I still don't trust the Dremora, but killing Ifriz would certainly make me feel better. Anything that shuts him up would be a welcome reprieve.
This one will behave. You have nothing to fear from Ezreba.
Now you must decide the outcome of Haj Uxith's long debate. Will the Hist tree live or die? The choice is yours to make, outsider.
You need to get back to it and help Captain Eilram. Go on.
You know how to choose a troll! Khaba congratulates you on your winnings.
Minwe was my friend and chief competitor when I started my gang. She was mean then and being dead has only made her meaner.
There is still the matter of Ezreba to consider. She betrayed the people of this village. And she's been a good friend for years. I honestly don't know what to do.
Can make it to safety. Don't wait for me.
The Sea Vipers must have dragged survivors out of the wreckage … but how many?
I can make my own way inland, gods willing.
Not quite ready to push my luck again. One brush with death is enough for the day. I'll move on shortly.
Deal with that bear as soon as you can. One fewer hungry mouth around here would be a good thing.
Nothing you say will convince me. I'm sealing myself in that tomb.
We should hurry. <<1>> won't be trapped for long.
<<1>> has time for you. I don't.
Here is the potion. I hope Zur didn't cut any corners. But knowing him, it probably tastes terrible.
Apologies, I can't be bothered right now.
The Green keep you! If you hadn't come along I don't know … I could have ….
Keep your wits about you in the embassy. The Maormer security is rather lax, but if they suspect your goal, they will not hesitate to run you through.
They hide our eggs in their filthy camps. You must enter their homes to rescue our children. But be very careful. Such an intrusion will result in great pain and death if they catch you.
The Collies are on the run, and Kazirra's thrilled. By the Green I wish we could stop for a brew. But no such luck. You have more work to do.
You're amazing. We could not have done this without you. Thank you, from the depths of my heart.
This diplomatic mission is a farce. The Dominion should've taken <<1>> by force, and sorted the rest out later.

Due to your efforts, the Prowler is free to sail once the tide comes in. Those marines did their part as well.\n\nI have no reinforcements, but I offer something better. I know who's killing the Dominion soldiers. And I know how to stop it.
We've taken <<1>> into custody, thanks to your quick action. No treaty will keep him from proper justice.
The only person seeking a compromise was <<c:1>>, and now he falls?\n\nThis is clearly the same Altmer treachery my people once suffered. Mark my words, the only "Dominion" is that of the High Elves!

The killer will share the pain my beloved's death has wrought. Hand down the throat, a kiss for my wrist; hand on the lungs, a kiss for my arms. Grasp, tear, yank … and one last kiss for the killer's own heart.\n\nNow. What have you found?
I'm sorry. My division isn't holding any fights at the moment. Come back soon.
Come back later. This division isn't competing at the moment.
There's a slight delay in my division's fights right now. Come back soon and we'll be ready for you.
Astonishing. The winner of all three divisions! You've done it! Now you must face Ishalga in the main arena to become Grand Champion!
Our clan's been through too much tragedy already. We lost our home, and now our Treethane. Damn it. We're trying to start a new life here. We can't let these Hollow stand in the way of that!

Please, you must restore my energy. Try to convince the slaves to return the energy willingly.\n\nBut if that doesn't work, you must use the Taskmaster's device to destroy the slaves and release my stamina.
<<1>> must be found. He's all <<2>> has left.
Welcome back. You were gone for longer than I expected.\n\nI trust you walked in the steps of Prince Sameer of Yath and experienced the events that led to his exile?
We need to find a portal stone to reach my clan's council of elders. There's one near the camp where we found the dead soldier. Let's get out of here and see if my clan will talk to you now.
Hmm. Mother looks upset. You will talk to her, yes?\n\nI did what was necessary. She must believe that.
I don't care how docile these Kwama normally are. I'll never look at them the same way again.\n\nHorrid beasts. I would be a hundred leagues from here if there weren't a Dwemer ruin to investigate.
Are you ready to go? I want to see how much the Mages will pay me to survey these ruins.

Thanks to you, we were able to perform the task we were sent here to do. We've opened stable portals to Nirn. Now we can get supplies and more forces into the Hollow City.\n\nI'd probably still be out there skulking about in Scamp-form if not for you.
Well? What did you find?
We share a common problem, little mortal. It only makes sense that we work together to solve it.
Please, you must bring the forbidden tomes to the shrine before they can be destroyed. No one else should suffer.
Welcome to Eagle's Strand, my friend. You have returned to help Razum-dar in his time of need!
Don't believe the spirit's lies.
You're truly one of the walkers. We would do well to learn from your efforts.

I swear, Xarxes himself has it in for me, or this is his idea of a joke. \n\nI've been complaining about how serving in the guard is a waste of my abilities, and now we're in a crisis that demands my skills, and I'm woefully out of my depth!
Tarrami can't thank you enough for getting us out of that predicament. We owe you one!
Kargand is here! It is beyond this Khajiit's power to help you defeat the Daedra in this realm, but please—free my brother from his torment.
Sorry. This one does not sign autographs.
I won't stand in your way. If you see anything out of place, let me know.
My father … he's gone.
Sorry, this lodge is off limits.
The crystal … Tashpir hears them inside. Inside his mind! Help!
I've prepared the ritual site, and I'll assist the vampire with her spell. But if she betrays us and our world is destroyed, I'll never speak to you again.
Guide the Lunar Champions well, Moon Hallowed.
The ritual is simple, even for the untrained. As you might have noticed, the Worms aren't exactly scholars.
Go, try the weapons, warrior.
Have you considered my proposal? Will you help me save my children and set them free?
My father … I should have known it would be one of our parents. Just like Mane Zebiden-jo four hundred years ago.
My mother … I can't believe it. Why?
If you reverse the flow of energy, it should free the poor creature trapped in the prism. That should disrupt the Shackle's power!
Talk to Aranias. She needs your support.
If anyone can get to the bottom of this, it's you and Aelif. She's gone outside to get some air. Stendarr guard your steps, my friend.
Our ancestors have left traces of their civilization across Tamriel. If we follow Queen Ayrenn, our empire will one day rival theirs.
So, you did it. I must admit, it's a relief.\n\nTraditionally you would now be in command of the militia, but is that what you want? If not, who should be?
I've no time for outsiders. I suggest you speak with Carindon, our leader. He's not neck-deep in work.
You look like the adventuring type. Speak with Warlock Carindon, if you'd like to join the expedition.
This area is saturated with magic. I believe we have found the mysterious Selene, however, our way ahead is barred.\n\nThis journey has been quite the burden.
We've seen you fraternizing with those Crown curs. Be cautious. You may be their next victim.
Crown law officers, ha! Dogs and sons of dogs, all of them.
Welcome, wayfarer. I trust you have not shared your cup with any Forebear scum.
You're doing the Green's work. On behalf of the Dominion, and my men. Thank you.
Forebears would bury the wells just to keep us from drinking. In all your travels, you will not find a more treacherous nest of asps.

Lives that have passed from the planes only go on in the memory of the living—and their stories only live so long as there are those who tell them.\n\nInspect the relics if you wish—each contains a story I can tell.
I will send word to Sentinel. Perhaps my father or someone else at court can recall the name of Suturah's daughter.\n\nLet's hope we can find her soon.
Congratulations, Hallowed. This one is not very spiritual … but even a fool knows we need a shield against the darkness.
Walk in radiance, my valiant friend. I hope that next time I am in battle I find you at my side once again.
Thank you for consecrating my sweet Zariya. \n\nPerhaps now she and I can be reunited on the Far Shores.
It is good to see you, my friend. Cariel has been updating this one on your work in Arenthia. Very nice. Razum-dar is impressed.
Though I respect my ancestors, I also agree they must be responsible for their actions.

We must work quickly, my friend. Clearly, the blight doesn't affect all Bosmer, but if anyone wanders into this area, I suspect there is a strong chance they will become afflicted.\n\nY'ffre forbid a scouting party of Vinedusk Rangers comes here.
My friend from the tent! How good to see you. Did you find the ritual components?
I saw the whole thing. You beat Gudarz fair and square. Congratulations. \n\nAnd thanks.
It's all very frustrating. I'm honestly not sure what can be done at this point.
Things are starting to shape up around here. You had something to do with that, didn't you?
Hmm … it feels like I've been waiting for Pircalmo for some time now. What … what day is it?
Thanks for the help, friend. They stole my clothes, my lady's jewels, and … and my dignity. But at least we can recover Lady Laurent's jewels.\n\nWill you help me?
I'll lead Stibbons to the exit. Find his lady's jewels and meet us there.
Let the Ayleid King know what an excellent and handsome companion you selected so we can get this mission underway.
Truly the Bright Moons shine down upon you. May your path be lit on the trail ahead.
With the door opened, we can proceed deeper into the Labyrinth.\n\nGo on! We'll be right behind you.
That's the dowry? That's better than I'd hoped—I mean, expected.
Really, I have no interest in matrimony. Maybe our matchmaker should work on finding a bride for my father instead.
What are you waiting for? Go and collect the dowry for my daughter.\n\nIf one of my bandits was this slow, I'd string him up.
Auri-El grant me strength. I hope you're the one Indaenir spoke of.
Travel to Stormhaven's eastern reaches and look for the Norvulk Ruins. I will be waiting for you inside.

Incredible. I've never seen such terrible power. But you didn't flinch.\n\nThe Shade is gone, but his corruption is not. Look at the Heart. It's overflowing with corruption, spreading the darkness all over Valenwood.
There is one other thing.
You're still breathing. Good! Breathing is good.\n\n<<1>> is deeper in the sea cave. She's trying to gain control of <<2>>. If she manages this, the Dominion soldiers won't stand a chance.
She is not in her right mind, filled with rage at our treatment. Please, if she comes at you … subdue her, don't kill her.
That harpy out there will give you a lift down to Kozanset. She's the one who carried me to this nest.
Is he the one who wrote all those notes? Thought he'd be uglier.
<<1>> believes his theories are infallible. From my own experience, this isn't the case.\n\nHe means well, but weigh his advice with care.
I've had enough of this place. Meet me outside!
Only those of Daedric blood may enter the pyramid, little mortal.
Sanguine's breath … I'm ruined. The relics are all gone. The papers are due today! Telenger will never take me on now.
Quite the brawl, eh? If that doesn't strike terror into the heart of the Wormies, I don't know what will!
I couldn't have collected the other village leaders without your help. Thank you.
I can't thank you enough for freeing me.

Do not hesitate to kill him—Erthas will grant you no mercy. That Oblivion Gate must be closed before something worse comes through.\n\nI was reluctant to ask you for help before, but I'm glad you followed through.
This one is one step closer to returning to the world of the living. Thank you, friend.
Welcome back. What can I get you?
If you're the one Indaenir was referring to, speak with Queen Ayrenn.\n\nBut no sudden moves.
The queen is frustrated. I am frustrated. To sit idly by while Valenwood is threatened. But anyone who nears Hectahame is corrupted.

Indaenir is dead? He is playing one of his Bosmer tricks. He must be. No … he really is dead.\n\nDark moons. Curse you Indaenir for being mortal, and curse us for being so slow to arrive after we saw the corruption recede.
Ah, you must be the one Ayrenn is waiting for.
This can't be right. It shouldn't have to end this way.
You look like the one Indaenir described. Speak with Queen Ayrenn.
We need to drive the Daedra out of the other fronts so that Gilraen and the others can have a fighting chance.
There's one more front to deal with.\n\nYou face the Daedra with an ease I've never encountered! Have you fought them before?
If I never see <<1>> again, it'll be too soon.
The summit's in your hands. It's up to you to determine how we move forward.
Intractable fools. Their pride will see us all dead.
Begone. I no longer take novices on the hunt. I've seen far too many die between the Senche's claws.
I'm not paying them enough to fight Orcs? They are Orcs! They should be used to it! And my betrothed is out there!

Planning to take a stroll in the Orchard? The denizens of that place are quite interesting.\n\nAnd by interesting, I mean they'll like as not try to tear your face off. We've a lot of that here in Coldharbour, for some reason.
Go, then. I will finish this without you.
Halt! I love saying that. But still, you, ah, probably don't want to go in there. Well, I guess even if you did, you couldn't. There's some sort of ward blocking the way.
Don't return until you've identified the Artisan. No one knows we're working together, and I want to keep it that way.
<<1>> is a master of security. I'm learning so much from him!
Our forces are back in control of the city. If you see any Imperial stragglers skulking about, let me know.
Kala welcomes you to her home. The Bright Moons watch over you.
I tried, but these thick-skulled bastards will not see reason.
This meeting feels like two wolves and a sheep discussing what to have for dinner. I will not sit back and let them pick at my bones!
With our combined strength we might have a chance, but our distrust runs too deep. I fear we'll never reach an accord.
Hope you don't mind a little song. Helps me stay warm and happy, you know?

Here to bet or another hopeful?\n\nThis one tires of those who arrive and who do not step inside of the arena. Come to fight, come to win. Come to celebrate with the first person you grab—to feel so alive you cannot breathe.

Hazazi brought me a report on Bramblebreach, including details about this "Aranias," and rumors of the Wilderking. Fascinating legends. \n\nYou did well there. Bramblebreach scouts will be of great help. No one knows the land better.
Everyone is assembled back in the meeting chamber to hear your findings, advocate.
I think it best if I move on from here soon. I may have been exonerated, but these Elves will never look at me the same. So many of them were so sure of my guilt.
The Green seems satisfied with the judgment, but I still think it was that damnable filthy Khajiit.

They're having an important meeting and asked if I'd give them some privacy. I mean, do you believe it? Where's the trust? Pop on out to the rubbish tip, Cadwell, there's a good lad. Do I mind? Oh, I have no mind. I'm the village bloody idiot!
To have seen such things. The Path is truly a hard road to walk, Hallowed.
Excellent. Well done. A fantastic experiment, if I do say so myself.
No matter what they throw at us, I'll keep our course steady.
Tread lightly now. The timber mammoth is as rare and skittish as they come. I nearly had it, but the damned birds spooked it.
The deepest cuts are from those you trust the most. Spinner Eranas was responsible for our spiritual guidance and he broke our most precious convenant. Hopefully we can learn from this and move on.
The sun bathes us in warmth by day, and the moon in shimmering silver by night. The whole forest rejoices, now that the Pact-breaker, Gathiel, is gone. Thank you, advocate.
Joining Brackenleaf's Briars is nothing to take lightly. Many have died attempting the trials, and there is always the threat of the Outsider.
Well? Are you going to let me do this? He's been a danger to himself, to Wayrest. And he killed my partner.\n\nYou know he deserves it.
I became Pellingare's guard for the pay. I owe money. A lot.
I truly believed … I truly believed my children would become champions of society; that they could, one day, lead this city into an age of prosperity.\n\nMy children were good. Once.
It's good to breathe mundane air again, but we have a lot to do to prepare. No time for dallying.
You should get back to Erunor quickly. The Orcs looked restless.
Let good King Dynar know what an excellent choice you made so we can get this caravan on the road.
The house is such a lonely place when my wife isn't here to make it all warm and comfortable.
Speak with Sai Sahan. He wishes to discuss the matters at hand.
Sai Sahan has something to ask you.
The greatest of the Sword-Saints, Divad, tells us that destiny is a chain, forged one link at a time. Our chain is nearly complete. There is but one link remaining.
Give the Redguard your time. He's probably the most sane of these people.
Sameer, my brother! Finally you stir! Did you drink too deeply from the starry well last night? \n\nThis is unlike you. Quickly, pull yourself together. We can afford no idle time today.
Almalexia smiles upon us, warrior! With her blessings, the Elder Scroll of Altadoon has passed into our hands.
Quickly! To the ancestral crypt!
Welcome to our hall. Are you familiar with the Guild?
Bright Moons go with you. May they light your path, always.
Good to see a competent traveler on the road. The March needs smart people these days.
I do not know how the guards allowed the Elder Scroll of Alma Ruma to be stolen, just that it must be recovered!
<<1>> and <<2>> made it to safety.\n\nDid you see <<3>> out there? I pray he's still alive.
Sai was right there. We had him! We were so close.
Well, that was unnerving. Can't say that I've ever had to kill a version of myself before. But, I must say, even as an evil doppelganger, I'm a very capable opponent!
The minds of some men can endure hardships far greater than anything the Daedra can concoct. The forces of loyalty, honor, and friendship are powerful indeed!
You have everything <<1>> had when she made <<2>> go to sleep.\n\nI don't remember how she did it. I'm sorry. But I know she used the altars in the Constellation Room.

Aranak. After being a member of our town, living as one of us for so long, it's unbelievable that he would do something like this. Please bring him to judgment quickly, so we can close this terrible chapter.
Oh, Eranas. This is all my fault. I never should have … well, it's too late now, isn't it?
Are you going to the village to find evidence? Be careful! Who knows what manner of beasts have taken up shelter in our homes.\n\nI'll try to have the trial chamber ready by the time you get back.
I don't want to believe the Khajiit is guilty, but I'm not blind. I can read the signs. Lightning struck in the village the night the Green Pact was broken. The Khajiit is involved in some way.
Your deeds have been nothing short of legendary. With the Planemeld at an end, Tamriel may yet endure.\n\nNow, the time has come to confront Molag Bal and reclaim your soul.
Lord Varen is waiting for you. It's time.

When Lord Varen revealed his true identity, you felt betrayed, and rightly so. In The Book of Circles it is written that when you forgive, you set a prisoner free, and quickly discover that the prisoner was you. Consider that, Vestige.
I highly doubt that the God of Schemes is engaged in banal conversation right now. Perhaps we should follow his example?

Have you spoken to Nithelin? I was inside that night, but I know she was out walking. Naeldil, too.\n\nI'm sorry. I don't really know anything, I guess—but the Khajiit fellow was always very nice. I don't believe it was him.

I think they all did it. All of them, collaborating with one another, broke the Green Pact intentionally. The real question is why.\n\nObviously they wanted the forest to attack us, to distract us from their real purpose. Think about it.

If you ask me, I don't really think any of them is entirely responsible. Magic's like that, sometimes it just turns sour on you.\n\nI saw some lightning in the village proper, and that's all I can really say.
What is your will, outsider?
You go first. Then Adusa shall sneak off. Less chance of both of us getting captured by these cursed creatures that way.
Please. I just need a moment to catch my breath.
I know how to deal with your kind! Come any closer and this goes straight into your heart!
I feel so empty. Torn. Where's Renoit? I'm so hungry.
Divines save me! Please, I'll join your army! Really I will! Just don't kill me.
I'm sure one of the soldiers saw where my sister got to. She couldn't have disappeared into thin air now, could she?
If you have business in <<1>>, you'd best turn back. The people are killing one another in the streets.
Come, we should retrieve the scroll. Shouldn't we?\n\nYes … yes, we should.

Well, if it isn't my old friend Hunts-For-Books! Now don't look so glum, or the skeevers'll notice. Then they hit you up for spare gold, a few shin bones, your best pair of cheese-filled slippers.\n\nInsufferable beasts! They can't hold a conversation.
Help Captain Janeve. The sooner we can hunt down Reezal-Jul, the better off we'll all be.
I will summon you again when the time is right. \n\nUntil then, walk in the light, Vestige.
Sancre Tor. Seeing these walls again brings a flood of memories. I do not even know how long it has been. Two years? Three years? Time had no meaning in the Halls of Torment.
Mannimarco, again? You know, after we've killed him, I'm really going to miss hating that skeever.
We've done it. We freed <<1>> from her torment.\n\nIt was worth the wait.
Cultists are gristle between the teeth of Cyrodiil. Claws must be used to remove them.
Death is the only answer to the horrors the Shadowed Path spreads across Cyrodiil!
Bah, cultists. They're of no use to anyone, especially these Shadowed Path scum.
Beware the forces of the Worm Cult. They may only be men, but they are the worst kind of men.
I've never seen such destruction and malicious violence. These vampires are terrible people.
Ah, the empty one returns.\n\nYour pardon, but, bereft of your soul, that's how I think of you. Don't be offended: I hope to repair your lack.
I've never heard of this Valley of the Blades. I do hope they have a tavern. I'm going to need a stiff drink after traveling with this lot.
Welcome to the Vault of Despair, my friend.\n\nLet's make our visit as expedient as possible. Saryne should be close by.
Something's different. There are much fewer soldiers than before.\n\nWe should speak with <<1>>. We may already be too late.
I knew I could count on your help! If you find that blasted cup, you will have my eternal gratitude.

Right now, we are in no position to offer anyone aid, and certainly not a city dweller.\n\nUela the Hagraven and her Reachmen have taken over this part of the forest and everything here—including the wyresses—are weaker as a result.
The Reachmen must have sensed Uela's death. They started to panic and fight amongst themselves.\n\nMade them easy pickings for me and my sisters. Now, the heart. You do have it, I hope.
I can't believe my eyes. You hold it in your hands!\n\nNow, to break my bonds from this horrid prison.

This place always makes me think of unfulfilled dreams: endless echoes of past lives, countless books unwritten, countless songs unsung. I hope that when I finally come to rest here, it is at the end of a life well-lived.
Ack … ook … gah! Now we can talk safely.
This is my first visit to Sancre Tor. I must say, I'm unimpressed. Alessia's holy city has seen better days, to be sure!

I hope you're here to help me. \n\nDuraeg and his Dark Witnesses attacked without warning. My best scouts go to gather information; only two returned. Isabeth disobeyed orders to look for them, and now she too is overdue. What else could go wrong?
You're not welcome here stranger. Move along.
Luck be with you.\n\nWe'll journey to the Evermore camp if you complete the job. We're closely tied to the land, so we'll know when you've been successful.
Are you here for Denille? I was curious if Isabeth would return herself or send someone.

You know, I was about to hike all the way to Wayrest to ask for aid, but maybe what we need is right here? Yes. You have the bearing all right.\n\nWhat do you say, want to save a soldier from having to walk halfway across Tamriel?

I don't see you carrying any poultices. Let me guess. The old cat wants us to fill his silver paws with gold, doesn't he? Greedy bastard.\n\nStraight-up robbery! I'd agree to it though, but we just don't have the coin.
What more is there to say? I deserve to suffer at least as much as those I harmed. Please, allow me to transfer the ring to myself.
Was it my imagination or did she say she was expecting the Baandari to pay for this mead?\n\nIf that's the case, that will be her last mug.
Well, that was surprising. At least she is gone now—right, <<1>>? \n\nThat was a clever approach, telling that guard the truth. She wasn't expecting that, was she?
That went better than I expected! Jode's Chariot will put the cartel's money to good use.\n\nThank you for your part in this. We are in your debt.
Find those traitors and make them pay! Let's show everyone what it means to betray the city of Shornhelm!
Alard means well, though he'd be happy to burn down an entire house rather than oil a squeaky hinge.\n\nStill, he is a brilliant strategist. Let him know what you learned in the upper city.
Head upstairs. <<1>> is looking for you.
When you asked for the gold, my heart nearly stopped. You have Sheogorath's own mouth, that is for sure!\n\nStill, this is wonderful news! We will be able to continue our operations, thanks to you.

Reezal-Jul knew about the Ayleid relic the entire time. He convinced me to give it to Wylon. Why didn't I remember that?\n\nAnd this memory. I recall our celebration, the toasts. But this moment, talking to Leila … I don't remember that happening.
It's a damn good thing you came out. I was just about to charge in there and find you myself. \n\nIf I had died, it would've been your fault. You don't want the death of a king on your head, do you?
You look like someone who appreciates a little excitement in your life. Well, friend, in that case you've certainly come to the right place.
You have to convince Leila to do this. It's the only way we can save her.\n\nTell her I'll love her, no matter what. She'll always be my wife.
Good. Four hunters is better than three, any day.
The prince has accepted the truth. The force that has brought him back from death is thoroughly evil.\n\nSay your farewells, and I will consecrate him. That will put his body and his soul to rest.
Tell the Knight Commander you want to help stop the Imperial raids.\n\nTell her Crazy Eye sent you too! Tell her this one deserves a little present, or several presents … several shiny presents.
Many more worthy than me have given their lives to protect this kingdom. My husband … my children …. \n\nI am not afraid to join them.
It is done. The Harvester of Souls' presence is receding from the land, though it is likely that this place will be forever scarred.
Give Adusa the good news. Tell this one that <<1>> is just a bitter memory.
If you care to quash the remnants of the Blacksap Rebellion, just say the word. I'll open a portal to a secure location.
Once you've departed, <<1>> will seal the portal. None must know we're holding <<2>> at this location.\n\nOr that he's alive, for that matter.

So here we are. Baron Montclair's dead and that damn artifact is destroyed. Yes. You can pat yourself on the back all right. You've saved Rivenspire and that's no small thing. \n\nYou do realize this creates a predicament for me, though, don't you?
Leave me be.
I haven't had this much fun since ….\n\nCome to think of it, I've never had this much fun!
Good hunting, Vestige. Keep your wits about you.
Ah! Come to do business? To browse our fine markets, perhaps?\n\nYou will find things in Redfur not sold outside of Elsweyr!
I can't speak right now. Please, come back later.
<<1>> doesn't give her recommendation lightly. If she thinks you can assist me, I take her at her word.
<<1>> is quite efficient. She'll give you no trouble, I'm certain of it.\n\nBut I must attend to more important matters. I'm sure you understand.
So Hircine chooses to speak to you rather than us, his faithful servants. I admit to a bitter feeling, but perhaps it is for the better this way.\n\nProvided you do not betray us.
Hircine speaks to you. Best not keep him waiting.
Our temple is overrun with Reachmen. Our guardians have turned against us. This is all my fault, and I'll do whatever it takes to get it back.

Ah, the prodigal pup returns. So you aid the wyrd who still lick their wounds of defeat. They fell prey to Brinarch and his Reachman, losing my favor. To earn it back, you must prove yourself once more. Show me what you've learned.
Ah, there you are at last! This daft old hermit is simply talking in circles. See if you can persuade him to be sensible. \n\nIf that doesn't work, have a look at these inscriptions yourself.
What can I do for you?

Countess Tamrith has returned from the west. She is understandably distraught, but grateful to you all the same. \n\nVerandis passed through here as well, on his way to the Lorkrata hills. I believe he was expecting to to join him.

I confess, I was nervous to come to Rivenspire, but Emeric felt it was important that he come and reassure the people, if nothing else.\n\nMy only condition is that we cannot leave until he crowns a new ruler. He should have done so long ago.
Nedras left me. I'd almost rather he were dead than hear he's run away and left me alone. I can't believe he's done this to me!
I'm very sorry, I'm waiting for someone. Would you leave me to my thoughts, please? I don't want to miss him … I've been waiting for so long.
Kala welcomes you to her home. The bright moons watch over you.

Well, kick an Elf and call me sunshine! I know you! From Shornhelm! Am I glad to see you!\n\nI was the Orc. In the cage. Not my most shining moment, but it's not like I'm a noble or anything. No matter. We could really use your help.
Keep low, and remain vigilant. The Imperials are thieves without honor.
Well, what have we here? A poor lost pup, looking for a pack? Heh. You want to run with wolves, you got to learn a few things first.

Remember, only when you have collected all three pieces of the Orrery do we have even a hope of getting it working. Not like it matters to me, although I'd like for <<1>> to come back. She has much to teach me.
That's it! It's working. It's actually working!
I've lost everything ….
We can't wait any longer. She's already free of her bonds! Please, in Ruptga's name, use the talisman and release her!
What's happening? It's as if there's another presence in the ruin.
Enter the pool and touch the symbol of life.

I hope Frandar lets you pass. I also hope he has more clarity than I do.\n\nI wonder why anyone would want to visit the Chamber of Passage, or even the Far Shores … aren't there some shores you could visit a little closer to home?

Ah! A fellow student of history? You must be. No other reason to visit these gods-forsaken ruins.\n\nFascinating place though. You realize this is where King Ranser made his last stand? Still haunts the place, in fact. And I intend to find out why.
Now this is more like it! I love a good battle! It really gets the blood flowing.
Given the recent troubles in the area, the people of <<1>> need a little entertainment to raise their spirits. Anything you can do to help my performers is appreciated.
You look like someone who seeks to travel while earning honest coin! \n\nWould you like to hear about a great opportunity for both of these ambitions?
You have my thanks for the help that you rendered unto us, and my sincere apologies that <<1>> was inflicted upon you through my absence.
Why didn't you say you were with Ufa?
I appreciate your help, but … don't think this changes anything. We're working together for the good of the Covenant. That's it.
Oh, you're still here? I don't suppose you'd be willing to help me on another grand adventure, would you?
You do the talky part. You're good at that. I'll make sure none of Naruk's crazies put a dagger in your back.
Given the befuddled expression on your face, I'm going to say you aren't Arrowhead. That means she's missing, and that's very, very bad.

I had no love for Larzgug and Thrug, but I didn't relish their deaths. I thought by leaving the stronghold I was leaving this bloodshed behind.\n\nAt any rate, we have everything we need to swear the oath.
Either I'm finally dead, or I'm dreaming. Either way, I want to give you a hug.
What in Mauloch's name took you so long? You think I got time to sit on my arse out here?\n\nThis job's hit a major snag, and I need your help!
I don't like your face.
Careful, milksop. There are some dangerous places around here. You might get squished.
Well done! Well done, indeed!
Consider yourself grateful the prince granted you an audience. He attends to crucial matters of state.
What do you say? Let's go find Lady Lleraya and Baron Montclair!
Why'd you tell their elder something like that?
Going to have to figure out how to turn this gold into more jobs. Maybe we should have some handbills scribed out? Hmm ….
We rarely use written contracts, but I'm glad our seer suggested one for these men. Their deceitful ways will cause them much sorrow.

Once you find them, get them back here right away. We've got to let the elder know how we're doing. She's been waiting on our progress report. And between you and me, I think she's getting a little impatient.
Whew! For a moment, I thought you'd tell … a different tale. Safe travels, friend!

Well met, friend. Tell me something. Say you knew someone who committed a truly heinous crime. You know, slaughtering innocents and such.\n\nCould they ever be forgiven? Or do they deserve to suffer for the rest of their lives?
If you can distract him and slip that draught into his drink, he should be snoozing pretty quick.
You are welcome to Fell's Run, traveler, but I'm afraid the town isn't at it's best right now. Perhaps you should move on and spend the night in Northpoint.
Who's out there? Turenn? Tell me that's you.

I've already spoken with the constable, and he agreed to release Martin if the young man will enlist. \n\nI simply can't understand why a criminal would choose the stocks over doing his duty for his kingdom.
We must be getting close. The secret of Lorkrata should be soon within our grasp.
It's time for me to make amends for the actions of my son. I shall accompany you and return honor to the Dorell name.
Just one more tile, I think. Now which one was it?
To think, it's nearly over.
I don't know how you managed it, but everyone's back! We're in your debt.
We're nearly there! Soon we can put this whole, terrible experience behind us!

When you destroy the <<1>> it will consume you in the blast, but don't worry! It'll bring you back to the place it was attuned to.\n\nAt least, that's what's written in the books … I'm sure you'll be fine!

I need a little time to say my farewells. Don't worry about me. I won't do anything stupid. I promise.\n\nBut you need to get back to Shornhelm. Without Verandis there, they're going to need your help to figure out what happens next.
The Doomcrag towers over this place. It is inescapable.
These are troubling times for Craglorn. The stars themselves have turned against us.
None of these defenses were active when Montclair and I first came here. I wonder if that would have made a difference in what happened after?
Not everyone reads the burnt bones anymore. My grandmother taught me how, but it's been so long since I've done it.
Blessed Arkay, take these poor souls under your care. May your brilliant light cleanse their immortal souls.\n\nOh, hello. Is there something you need, friend?
This situation has made for an abundance of paperwork. Now, if you'll excuse me.
All this talk of plagues and cultists. It's enough to make me want to move to Windhelm!
No one ever listens to what I have to say. Just make sure the ledgers are balanced. That's all they think I'm good for.
Green keep you, traveler. If you wouldn't mind, I have a favor to ask. I have a missive that must reach Vulkhel Guard.
It looks as if the Maulborn are losing control of the situation. We need to find a way to stop this!

What are they up to in there? And why won't they let me get a look at their curative?\n\nOh, sorry. I didn't see you standing there through the haze of my indignation. Can I help you? No, wait! You can help me!
Sometimes when we are in the dormant state, I dream. I dream that we have another purpose, that we work with the Bosmer to rebuild this place. I hope someday that comes to pass.
So tell me, my friend. Do you think the Maulborn pose a threat to the rest of Deshaan?
