Are you here for the choosing of our new caretaker? You've come at a good time for our village. This is an event held once in a hundred years, give or take. Very rare event. Very rare.
Find me those additives and return as quickly as you can. Now, please. I need to care for the afflicted.

I knew Nilyne could do it. I trained her well, and she was an apt pupil.\n\nOf course, we only have enough of the suppressant to aid the Serk. We have to hope that the Llodos plague hasn't spread too far into the Deshaan countryside yet.
Three keep you, traveler. Welcome to the Davon's Watch Guildhall.
<The statue stands before you, silent and unfathomable.>

I need you to catch torchbugs. I need five pairs of wings. No more, no less.\n\nI also need the satchel from my home—the intact building, the one with the sturdy lock. The key should be in an urn near the house. I tossed it in there when I ran by.
You've got all your limbs, and you're victorious to boot!\n\nMy Undaunted friends have yet to arrive. Roaring Ramavel must have found a tavern.
We must find a way to defeat the Anka-Ra and activate the beams that open the temple door.\n\nThen we can enter the Seeker's Archive and find the knowledge to defeat the Celestials.
Adept. You've done so much for the Guild. I couldn't let you leave without a final gift. This old Arch-Mage has a spell he's been saving just for you.
Thank you again for helping us defeat Yamanu-ko and her apprentices.\n\nIt's going to be a long time before the city is rebuilt, but it would have been lost without you.

You. My sister Gabrielle told me about you. She said danger doesn't faze you. Good.\n\nSee that large staff sticking out of the ground? It's emitting magical energy at unprecedented levels. If we don't stop it, it'll explode.

You—you've returned! My husband, Nerien'eth, has undone your defeat of his minions.\n\nYou need to flee from here. He will offer you no mercy, and I will not risk another life against him. The time for talk is over. I will put an end to him. I must.
I'm glad you've decided to join us. I try to help Hara with whatever I can, but right now she needs soldiers more than scholars. I hope you can help bring her some peace of mind.

A shame your kind doesn't fall from trees. With twelve of you, we'd accomplish wonders!\n\nAccording to Gilraen, the way out is forward. My books told me how to get in, but I—I thought we could go back the way we came. I was so wrong. About so much.
I feel the power pulsing within the Seeker's Sight. You have done well, mortal.
You have restored the Seeker's Sight. Good. \n\nWe have explained everything to Hara and she has agreed to help us. Speak to her when you are ready to proceed.
A mortal wandering here of its own volition? And it can fight! A daring soul! Perhaps you'd like to help me complete my day's work.\n\nI seek to attack this prison, lay low the Daedra who run it.
You look terrible. What did you do? Wrestle a Watcher?\n\nListen. If at first you don't succeed, stab your enemies in the back! Get up there and make your ancestors proud!

My friend, I will let you in on a little secret. One of our patrons—I cannot say who—is in Stormhaven even as we speak. It is truly an honor to show off this course before such an illustrious personage!
You should keep moving. These ruins are crawling with Iron Orcs. They beat the sap out of us and dragged off half my guards.\n\nIron Orcs have always been dangerous, but now … I just don't know.
You! Milksop! Turuk and his Undaunted need you. All Tamriel needs you! Warn the Guilds. The Alliances. Warn everybody!
This better be good.

I guess this is it. Cassi put her faith in me, but I'm not sure I could do this without your support.\n\nBraadoth's throne room is deep inside the Exarch's Stronghold. Come on. We've got to make sure this troll army never goes to war.
May the gods bless you and watch over you, and may you serve as the instrument of their holy wrath.\n\nGo forth, friend. Go forth and destroy in the name of Akatosh.
The Scaled Court tore us to pieces.
Escort me to the mantikora spawning pools and we'll see this done.

The Thief waits for us in the Sanctum of Farsight. That's where she must perform the ritual to locate the source of the magical disturbance.\n\nGo through the door to the left, then follow the river to the right. The Sanctum waits at the river's end.
The Scaled Court's venomous leader killed poor Kelmen without remorse or hesitation.\n\nBut the ritual worked. I know where to find her—Loth'Na Caverns.
You look a little flush. Did your romp with the vampires get your blood pumping?
I expected your frozen corpse would decorate Direfrost's halls. It is good to be wrong now and again.
Shaghila worries about what has happened to her scouts. She hopes you will find them soon.
Go to a woodworking station and deconstruct your maple bow.\n\nOr another piece of crafted wood, really—as long as you understand deconstruction, I'm happy.
Well? Have you mastered the art of roasting a pig?

<You notice a prominent handbill on the requisition board.>\n\n"The crafters of Leyawiin bids you welcome! Masters of the craft await you in <<1>>! New crafters shall be trained! Accomplished crafters will be certified! All at no cost to you!"

Fin can be such a primitive. A heavily defended keep lies ahead, containing a Daedric device called a Sigil Stone. Destroy it, and we'll find our way home.\n\nOf course, there's still a Daedric Titan and a Valkyn standing between us and the Stone.
Very good. Speak to Maj al-Ragath, and tell her to give you a bronze key. If you have the constitution, I will speak to you again when you are prepared to take a pledge.
Hey there! Welcome to the Undaunted enclave. You here to take a pledge?

I know it's here somewhere. I just know that it is. \n\nDon't you hate it when you're looking for a specific passage you read a long time ago and you just can't remember which book it was in? I know I hate it.

Fascinating! I never imagined the control mechanism would fit inside so small a space!\n\nIt will take me some time to master this device, but with it I'm sure I can suppress the outer defenses and return the quarry to a relatively safe state.
My son needs someone at his side who has nothing to prove.
Trinimac knows your heart, my friend.
I'm almost certain we can defeat Ice-Heart. Almost.

I'd appreciate any help you can provide. After what happened to the chief, the rest of the clan refuses to go anywhere near the quarry.\n\nIf you can get in there, find out what happened and make sure the quarry workers are safe.
Blow the horn at a snow mound and see if it rustles. Echatere kick in their sleep.\n\nOr you could kick the snow until you wake one of them. That'll work too.
You lied to me! You kept <<1>>'s challenge a secret. Why?
I'm not seeing visitors or hearing complaints today. If you need something, take it up with my forge-wife, Kharza.
Did you see Zhasim? He gets into all kinds of trouble when I'm not around.

Don't see many new faces at <<1>>. Our only neighbors are surly giants.\n\nSpeaking of which, <<2>> had a nasty encounter with a giant's club a short while ago. Best keep your voice low … we don't know how much time he has left.
Who are you?
I suppose the Scroll is never wrong, but I had hoped….\n\nGo. You have to find her. All the pieces are in place to bring about a conclusion—for good or ill.
Seems like everyone's been killing Daedra today. What about you?
You seem happy to see me. Doubtless it's my sunny personality and stunning good looks.
Where's my mother? Have you seen her? I can't find my mother.
It sickens me that we've resorted to curses and parlor tricks, but we do what we must. I must remind myself that those legionaries would do far worse to us.

<You notice a prominent handbill on the requisition board.>\n\n"Queen Ayrenn bids you welcome! Masters of the craft await you in <<1>>! New crafters shall be trained! Accomplished crafters will be certified! All at no cost to you!"
Today could have been worse. I could be dead.

The sheep are all over the city, but they are all being herded to the Arena. \n\nYou don't need to save all of them from slaughter, just a few really. Enough so the Rat can watch them suffer and feel better about himself.
There is still much to do in the city, walker. If you can take a break from your foolish banner war, I am certain that you can do some good.

Destroying the Dark Anchors is of critical importance, but for many people in this city, there are far more pressing matters.\n\nIt is not my place to tell you what you should do, but if you are interested, I know many who are in need.

Your general may want you to go out and win the war for the Dominion, but I have to tell you the truth—I'm not sure that's the priority. \n\nThe people in this city are in a dungload of trouble, and they could use your help, if you're willing.
You have the look of someone who has places to go and people to see. Is there something I can do for you, friend?
Now, what can I tell you about the Enforcers?
If you can determine the proper order of the story these panels tell, that's probably the key to solving the puzzle!

Most excellent greetings! I am Rigurt. They call me "the Brash," but you can call me "Ambassador!"\n\nThe Ebonheart Pact sent me to extend a piece of branch—no, wait—a branch of peace to glorious, brave, and beautiful Orcish peoples!
Feel free to visit us whenever you want. Our village isn't fancy, but it's warm, comfortable, and we make a strong rock-brewed ale. We use sparkle stones to give it an extra kick!

The look on Mazgroth's face when I handed her that pouch of gold … perhaps there's something to your unorthodox methods, my friend.\n\nNow if you'll excuse me, I believe the hunt-wife wants to hear my tale again. This time somewhere more private.
Stibbons will tell you what happened. That's what he's here for, after all.\n\nIn the meantime, I need to have another discussion with Kharsthun concerning the ultimate disposition of Torug's relic.
Between you and me, I'm glad Kharsthun decided to leave the dead Orcs where they fell. I have no idea how I would have dug proper graves in this ground. It's frozen solid!
Talk to Stibbons. I can't hear a word you're saying over Lady Laurent's insistent blabbering.

Don't worry, my partner will be all right. He just twisted his ankle running out of that damned ruin.\n\nBardun's pride will hurt more than his injury come morning. That and our empty gold pouch. Should have known this job sounded too easy!
Damn it! That rubble did something to my arm when it fell on me. I can't even swing a blade.\n\nWe need to find the ambassador. I want to make sure she's all right.

That was Coris, the mage that works for Captain Henrisa. Why did he try to kill you? I'm finding this whole situation to be very unsettling and extremely confusing!\n\nWe need to get inside that signal tower!
The spiders won't give me any trouble. Not while I have this forge-hammer!
Thanks for helping us. \n\nWe're hoping Orgotha will let us take a side trip to Orsinium before we head back to the clan. I want to visit an alchemist and get something for my head.
Do you think that scroll was left for me?
What's that look for? Haven't you ever seen an echatere before?\n\nOh, you have a letter from the Forge-Mother? Then Praise Trinimac and all that.
Hey. Judging by the soot on you, I'm guessing it's done?\n\nThat or you took a fireball to the face.
You found me! I knew you could do it.\n\nDid you like the trail I left for you? It was easy. Hide, release an arrow, move forward, repeat! And I was able to stay hidden the whole way.
I feel terrible about what happened to Unsulag.\n\nBut I'm as good as my word. I'll fight alongside you until we get out of this madhouse.
I feel terrible about what happened to Gahar.\n\nBut I'm as good as my word. I'll fight alongside you until we get out of this madhouse.

It worked! To be honest, I never know what's going to happen when it comes to Raynor's inventions.\n\nYou can follow the sphere now. Just head in the same direction as the after-image. I'll be along as soon as I gather up my brother's tools.
Well? What did <<1>> say?
It worked! I mean, of course it worked. Just like I designed it.\n\nYou can track the sphere now. Hurry after it. I'll catch up after I find my sister.
If you can find them in the catacombs, I'm certain the burial urns will open <<1>>'s tomb.\n\nAnd avoid the Winterborn if you can help it.
I just want to get out of here. I'm a cook, not a fighter.
I actually think we might get out of here, thanks to you.
I should have been at my husband's side. He'd still be alive and I'd still be his hunt-wife.
So she paid the blood price? Good, good. That's all I wanted.\n\nIt's strange. I thought I'd feel better. But I just miss my husband.
You are Tamahl, yes? My Knights of the Dragon have much respect for your order.\n\nBut I won't detain you with flattery when you need to speak with your master. A pleasure, truly.
Ah, it's the one who stabbed me in the back with such little effort. If I didn't know better, I'd assume you belonged to the Dark Brotherhood.

You'll want to look for <<z:1>>, preferably untouched by any echatere. It's the subtle glue which will hold the ogre heart and intestines together.\n\nThere's … no actual glue. It's just an expression.
Yeah, yeah. Tell Chief Bazrag I'll attend the funeral. Trinimac knows they couldn't start the ceremony without the innkeeper's daughter.
I don't know whether to stay here or go find help. If they hurt my Shalda, I don't know what I'll do.
Those giant woolly crab things are more aggressive than I thought.\n\nBut you should speak to Eveli. She's been waiting for you to arrive.
We brought in some very nasty opponents from the Spiral Skein, but you handled them well. \n\nLet's see how far you can go!
Maybe you should talk to that elder person before we go any farther. Figure out what we just walked into before we get too deep.
Just head downstairs and place the helmet in the proper display.\n\nWhen you're finished, come back and we can discuss your future involvement with the museum.
I hope you killed the madwoman who runs this place. This is no way to convert people to your cause.
We have to stop meeting like this. Maybe next time I could rescue you, what do you say?\n\nWhat in Malacath's name is Kurog up to, I wonder? This is brash, even for him.
I like the high priestess. I sure hope she's still alive. Go and check on that while I help the chief.

You really believed Youss's story? Over me? And if he does have a betrothed back in Sentinel, I feel sorry for her. He's been cheating on her from one port to another!\n\nI don't want to talk to you any more. Or to that lying dog who has my pendant.
Keep quiet—if my kinsmen see us together, they will kill us both.
I appreciate your help. The pendant holds a great deal of sentimental value to me.
Malacath's eye is upon you. Go.
I hear you're no friend to the Worm Cult. I have a plan to kick them in the metaphorical nethers.\n\nBut … my superiors think it's too risky. Care to prove them wrong?
You are not worthy of Malacath's fury. Away with you!
Didn't expect to see any mortal faces today—not living ones anyway. You must be new. Provincial militia, right? You've got the look of one.

Watching you perform so splendidly in the arenas is educational for our trainees—and so inspiring. They can hardly wait to start murdering atronachs on their own. \n\nIt must be so heart-warming to be regarded as a role model!
I need a few more moments to clear my head.\n\nI'll see you over at the keep before the funeral begins.
I shall represent Trinimac and the temple at Kurog's funeral. The people need to see that we're not all Vosh Rakh fanatics.
Feels like I missed most of the fun. Who knew an Orc city could be so exciting?\n\nI wonder if my crew could find work here? I'll have to ask Bazrag about that when I see him.

This land! It promised hope and opportunity, but it hides a basket full of biting snakes!\n\nDo not mind me. I must have hit my head. Now I need to find my partners. If only the land would remain beneath my feet and the sky stay above my head.

Oh, it's you. I was just looking for some tools. Wait, why aren't you in the Temple District? We need to get Father Egnatius out, remember?\n\nThere's work to do here, no doubt—but for now we need to focus on these priests. Lets get back to it.
What are you doing down here? Don't you know that Graystone Quarry is a disaster area?
It's good to have Master Dren back, all safe and sound! He told me all about his adventure in Exile's Barrow. It was so exciting!\n\nI can't wait to read the book! I love Master Dren's books!
I hear that those cultists are in full retreat. Good work. Lilyameh will want to hear the details. Go speak to her.
New in town? Try not to step on any toes. These Morkul Orcs are a temperamental bunch.
I thought you were one of those damn machines! You're just lucky I've got the reflexes of a snow bear or your guts would be decorating the floor.\n\nNow, care to explain what you're doing down here?

I was going to wait for the High Elf, but now that you're here I think I'll try to find my way out of this damn ruin.\n\nI may not be able to fight mechanical spiders, but I know how to move stealthy when I have to.

Back from the Kennel, huh? No offense, but you might want to scrape those boots. Smells like you stepped in something.\n\nThe company's already taken it's cut. You should check in with Arushna if you want to get paid.
Ow! Stupid ankle! Hurts like a skinned pig in salt water!\n\nCan't you see I'm in pain? Talk to Meram if you need something, why don't you?
Welcome to the grand Orsinium! I'm the master mason, responsible for all of the construction you see going on around the city.

You're here, and relatively unskewered. Next is the significantly harder part.\n\nFirst, we sneak into the warehouse. Next, we observe our surroundings. Finally, and this is the most important part, you do exactly what I tell you to do.
Find the Sanctuary. Open the Black Door. Your Brothers and Sisters wait to greet you with open arms.\n\nI look forward to watching your progress, Initiate. And once again, welcome to the family.

Bring Boethiah's word to the cult's initiates—if that doesn't get you noticed, nothing will! Once they detain you, we'll show my sister exactly how Surus treats those who disagree with him.\n\nAs long as you don't wind up disappearing along the way.
<<1>> sent word of your time at <<2>>. Said you slipped out from between the Iron Wheel's greedy fingers.
Back without <<1>>? Can't say I'm surprised. I've met camels less stubborn.

I'll go by and check on Anais in a few days. Make sure she's recovered from her trying ordeal. If she learned her lesson, that's great. If not, well, I'm sure I can come up with another plan—and this one will be even better than the last!
I don't know how long I can keep stalling them. Find Qamar's stash!
How terrible. Lyra was ordered to purify her own Sanctuary. To kill her own Brothers and Sisters. I never even imagined ….
Have you talked to Kor? Seems his little wolf-girl has run off. \n\nWill you … see if you can help? Someone should go look for her before anything … well, you know.
Just a few more days of honest work and we're off to Sentinel. My sister and I really do appreciate everything you've done for us.\n\nAnd, I suppose, we've been stuck in worse places than Anvil.
A little work, a little gold, and we'll be in Sentinel in no time!\n\nThanks to you.
The guild has given me so much. It's time to return the favor.
Who was that? What was all that about, with dowries and iron wheels?
<<1>> in a cell. Somehow, it feels right.
I'm not entirely proud of my … accomplished penmanship, but it was necessary to protect my business in Abah's Landing.
Big day for the guild, don't you think? It feels good to beat <<1>> at his own game.\n\nYes, we haven't done it yet. Call me an optimist.
I have to give her credit. Of all <<1>>'s bad ideas, her plan to crash the wedding is the most spectacular.
Have I mentioned how much I enjoy a good wedding? Even a bad one can be fun.
I recognize many of these faces. So few are from Taneth. As though <<1>> was too embarrassed to invite her family?
<<1>> and <<2>> are the same person?
There is too much space here. When the wedding guests leave, it will be as empty as the man who owns it.
Everyone here has so much to say, and absolutely none of it matters.\n\nNobles.
Learn what you can of <<1>>'s whereabouts. Do your best to mingle.\n\nBut mingle quickly. We need to reach her before the ceremony begins.

Good, you're here! The old book we found at Sulima Mansion was the key to my father's cipher. His ledger revealed directions to his "greatest treasure."\n\nIt won't bring him back. But if we find it, Abah's Landing will no longer have a hold on me.
That lamp definitely belonged to <<1>>.
My friend! What a happy coincidence! This one never imagined to find you skulking around an Ayleid ruin!\n\nSince you are already here, you will help Raz deal with a dangerous war criminal, yes?
<<1>> needs you. It's always important, but this time is especially important.

I used to dream of this place when I was a young cutpurse. I thought, if I can make enough of myself, one day I can go there. Hold my head high. Order a drink like a normal person.\n\nIt tastes the same as what we have in <<c:1>>.
<<1>>'s looking for you. Didn't seem too happy.\n\nNothing you did, she's just stiffer than normal. And that's saying something.
<<1>> and I have much to discuss. Don't you have guild business, somewhere away from here?
Velsa knows me so well! This one is as tired as a tiger with a belly full of tender meat.\n\nCome back and we can talk later, my friend.
Smashing! I do adore a cooperative accomplice!\n\nBesides, this will give us a chance to get to know each other better. You do want to get to know me better, don't you? After all, who wouldn't?
I hope this isn't what it looks like. I've never seen <<1>> so … taut.
If three of us survive, we'll be a greater success than the previous failed attempt.\n\n"Progress."
You ever notice that camel herders drive hard bargains? I always wonder if they learn such stubbornness from the camels.
Opportunity is a fickle mistress, boss, and our buyers are no less so. Hurry, before we miss them both!

I see you found my latest note. Thank you for responding so quickly.\n\nGo, speak with Narahni. She specifically asked me to contact you after she received a letter from Faradan. It clearly upset her, but she refuses to say anything to me.
Tashmin will grow strong and healthy again here with me and Velsa. This one is most content.
The arrest writ resides in the bounty hunter's pocket. Get it now while he's drunk on my precious skooma.
I'll get the gold. I just need a little more time.
It took some time, but I finally figured out the best way to teach Anais a lesson.\n\nI promise this will make perfect sense to you shortly, my friend.
That lizard has messed with the wrong noble! When I get out of this, I'm going to have him stuffed and mounted over my fireplace!
I don't believe I've had the pleasure. Spencer Rye, at your service. I have a friendly arrangement with the Thieves Guild. We're "business adjacent" you might say.
I've calmed Hilde down, but there's still so much we don't know about what happened and what she was thinking.\n\nYou should talk to her, Initiate. But be gentle. We've all had quite a day.
The next caravan will be ready to leave shortly. If that interests you, find a place nearby to sit for a spell and I'll call you when we're ready.
Now that it's all over, I feel like a fool for listening to the Chanter. I might have to pay him a visit one of these nights and even the score.
With your help, we'll be on top again in no time.\n\nSo get to work, recruit.
You'll get used to <<1>>. She always said I was particularly thick-scaled. Also thick-headed.\n\nI used to think she was complimenting my frills.
I'm not sure what I think of <<1>>. She knows what she's doing, but she's … prickly.\n\nDon't tell her I said that.
I never expected to be back here. Well, not here, exactly. Who ever expects to spend any time in a cistern? I'm sure this isn't very sanitary.
This isn't as nice as Velsa's house. But, it has a certain amount of charm.
I envy you, Brother.\n\nFew get to prove their devotion to the Night Mother and the Dread Father in so dramatic a fashion.
See? That didn't take too long. It's amazing what a skilled chef can do with the right ingredients and the proper equipment.
Getting more new faces around here. I guess that's a good thing, but I'm not letting my guard down. \n\nHow about you get back to that job and quit distracting me?
Well met, Assassin. I bring word from the Matron.
A contract has come our way that includes an unusual request. The client wants to meet the assassin assigned to carry out the task before paying our exorbitant fee.

You and the Nord seek the girl. Hmm. My research suggests she is a confused and tormented individual, prone to blaming herself when misfortune strikes.\n\nMy conclusion? She's going to get herself killed.
This killer behaves in most unexpected ways. Be careful. Raz thinks her brain has come loose and sloshes around inside her head.
What are we waiting for? Let's find the killer and end this!

You've proven yourself time and time again, my friend. I've gone from worrying that you might fall to the Black Dragon to believing you might just be the one to obtain vengeance for us all. Dread Father guide your blade.

Go to Knightsgrave and make sure that Green-Venom-Tongue succeeds. But if the Black Dragon manages to overcome him, then I expect you to end Lyra and make her pay for betraying her Brothers and Sisters.

I overheard Astara talking. She praised your skill and obedience, which is a rare thing. You're really making a name for yourself and she appreciates it, even if she doesn't always show it.\n\nKeep it up. Just stay safe, all right?
These are troubling times for Craglorn. The stars themselves have turned against us.
We have nothing else to discuss at this time, Seeker. Go about your business.
We must find a way to defeat the Anka-Ra and activate the beams that open the temple door.\n\nThen we can enter the Seeker's Archive and find the knowledge to defeat the Celestials.
You must be from outside. I'm glad to see someone's noticed us.\n\nA word of advice, though. Don't drink the water in here. Don't even touch it.
Thank you again for helping us defeat Yamanu-ko and her apprentices.\n\nIt's going to be a long time before the city is rebuilt, but it would have been lost without you.

You. My sister Gabrielle told me about you. She said danger doesn't faze you. Good.\n\nSee that large staff sticking out of the ground? It's emitting magical energy at unprecedented levels. If we don't stop it, it'll explode.
I'm glad you've decided to join us. I try to help Hara with whatever I can, but right now she needs soldiers more than scholars. I hope you can help bring her some peace of mind.
I feel the power pulsing within the Seeker's Sight. You have done well, mortal.
You have restored the Seeker's Sight. Good. \n\nWe have explained everything to Hara and she has agreed to help us. Speak to her when you are ready to proceed.
You should keep moving. These ruins are crawling with Iron Orcs. They beat the sap out of us and dragged off half my guards.\n\nIron Orcs have always been dangerous, but now … I just don't know.

I guess this is it. Cassi put her faith in me, but I'm not sure I could do this without your support.\n\nBraadoth's throne room is deep inside the Exarch's Stronghold. Come on. We've got to make sure this troll army never goes to war.
Escort me to the mantikora spawning pools and we'll see this done.

The Thief needs to perform the ritual at a site within the Howling Sepulchers. Go north and follow the path into the hills to the cave we seek.\n\nJust stay alert. Undead Nedes patrol the place and they have no regard for visitors—living or dead.
The Scaled Court's venomous leader killed poor Kelmen without remorse or hesitation.\n\nBut the ritual worked. I know where to find her—Loth'Na Caverns.
There you are. I was afraid you'd been compromised.\n\nWere you successful? Did Onthim have anything worth reading?
Look what the sea coughed up! Welcome to Vvardenfell, land of Dark Elves, lava flows, and slaves of all descriptions.\n\nSpeaking of slaves, let me get those manacles off you.
You return, after quite the journey.\n\nWell?

Ah, it warms my scales to see you once more, my friend. I wish I could thank you for my freedom, but as you can see, it was short lived.\n\nI see you still wear no shackles. Will you aid me once more? I know someone who needs help.
Mother should be at home, ordering the servants about and taking care of the family business.\n\nYou should go and ask her about buying Tirwin.
Were you able to get another Blessing Stone? We need to restore some of Lord Vivec's energy before the moonlet falls out of the sky!

Savarak's gone! Damn that slippery bastard! We tossed his manse, the gathering house, the wharf …. We turned the whole damned town upside down, and nothing.\n\nHe can't have just vanished. What did we miss?
Safe travels, friend. Go in peace.
Fair warning—Master Firuth may say some strange things. Do me a favor and try not to laugh, all right? He may seem odd, but he's still a powerful mage. Don't forget that.

I knew she would send you. Know that I do not blame you for your role in all this. We are, both of us, victims of Telvanni lies. This place deadens the soul—pure and impure alike.\n\nNow, let me guess. My heart sent you to counsel patience, yes?
Oh, that was just—did you see the look on his face? Ayem's mercy, he certainly wasn't exaggerating about that allergy. What a buffoon!
Did Theyo seriously lose one of his people?\n\nOne less person I have to pay.
Get away from me, you … you wretched scamp! Your fur is going to make it worse!
Hmm. Looks like the Daedra certainly put you through your paces. How did you fare? Do you have the stones I asked for?
Now there's a sight for sore eyes. The Scarlet Judge returns!\n\nYou wear it well! Better than Melar, even. But don't tell him I said that.

That skeeving Telvanni mage acts like he has good intentions, but the truth always comes out eventually. He's trying to sabotage Gnisis and bring down House Redoran!\n\nJust wait until my Redoran compatriots arrive. They'll put an end to his mischief.
I hope this new queen is sturdier than the last. She's got a big job ahead of her. We all do.

"The river drains into the sea, as my divinity flows out of me." Hmm. Needs some work.\n\nAs you can see, I continue to lose energy, and it has made me somewhat agitated. Have you made any progress toward discovering the source of my discomfort?
You smell like must and grave dust. Hope you showed those necromancers that death's not so pretty.

Get to Ald'ruhn and locate Seryn. She needs to tell us more about Chodala and then help us acquire his staff. Without it, we can't restore Vivec.\n\nMeanwhile, I need to placate the populace. The people grow concerned over Vivec's continuing isolation.

This project has been nothing but one disaster after another. How am I expected to get this ziggurat built on time when things constantly go wrong?\n\nDon't mind me. I'm just having one of those days.

The Wise Women cannot say if your quarry is what you think, but they have shared their knowledge of dreugh with me.\n\nThey offer a mixture to lure the creature out. Spill this in the Ruddy Man's den and it will show itself.
I was beginning to think the Ashlanders got you as well. Were you able to find evidence that they've been preying on the pilgrims? I can't spare a moment from these dreugh as it is.
Ah! Uh, yes … hello! What are you doing out in the middle of nowhere? Going for a walk? This one often walks … around here, I mean.

Lathdar's gone, right? Good.\n\nI have news … of the unpleasant variety. Based on the looks of the egg-heaps, I'd say our royal egg is near to hatching. If the queen emerges before we've put her in the mine, the workers will reject her.

Narsis still hasn't returned from the tomb. I don't suppose you'd … no, probably not.\n\nI'll wait for a few more moments and then send Borfree in to look for him. I'm sure all is well, but I can't help this feeling that something went wrong ….
This part of the structure dates back to before the time of the Dunmer as we know them. Isn't it amazing? I can't wait to see what's waiting for us down here!

Whew! Got it right the first time! No explosions … yet.\n\nGo ahead. You can take it. I'm sure it's stable. Mostly sure. Once the tonal inverter is in your possession, talk to me and I'll tell you how it works.
We don't know what my brother is doing inside Malacath's shrine, but we have to find out.\n\nI'm ready to enter the ruins whenever you are.
You have your task. Complete it and you will have the favor of House Hlaalu. You are free to refuse if your stomach isn't in it, but I will expect your complete silence on this entire affair.

Are those murmurs of approval I hear? Well done, my friend. I'm sure the Wise Women will speak to you now.\n\nAsani Atal probably knows the most about this area. I doubt she'll offer more than faint praise. You'll have to ask about the tomb outright.
Disturbing an Ashlander at prayer is unwise, outlander.

Lenarmen waits ahead, I'm sure of it. \n\nI do hope he hasn't found the Bthark Prism yet. The poor fool would probably mistake it for the Heart of Lorkhan. You may need to disabuse him of that notion … with violence. So be ready.

We sure are out in the open now, aren't we?\n\nI hate to admit it, but we're in over our heads. We have to do something to get Farwen back, but you heard what the spirit said. Sharz and I aren't warriors, there's no way we're defeating Galgalah.
We're really doing this, eh? I hope Kasouda and the others appreciate the effort.\n\nLotaeel will get this lot back to the surface. Neramo and I will be right behind you.
You mean to spend some time in Vos? I wouldn't linger if I were you.\n\nSavarak thinks we're little more than beasts. Cause any trouble, and his lackeys will put you in chains … or a shallow grave.
When next you see her, tell my daughter that I want to talk to her. Veya can set the terms, but I expect her to stop running away when things don't go her way.
Damn these scales. I'd be a spellwright by now, if not for these spines.
Thank you for letting me know about the argument. I'll check up on Father later today, just to make sure he's all right.
Yes? Do I know you? I'm trying to fish.
Ah, we meet again! By the Three, my rights and duties.\n\nWhat brings you back to Sadrith Mora? In town to further your friend's ambitions? Again?
Hey. You need something?
I'm not sure what's going on here, but I bet I'm not going to like the answer.\n\nTalk to my apprentice. She's eager to find her brother.
If anything goes wrong and you get caught, I have no idea who you are.
I am sure we shall meet again. I should go home, I have many things to do.
I assume you found the tomb without too much trouble. Were you able to take the rubbing as I directed?
We can't get this close and then lose the trail! You have to find out where my brother and the Ashlanders went. We'll keep an eye on the camp from up here.
So Councilor Dolvara does know something about Veya's brother. Damn it all! \n\nNow I suppose you want to actually talk to her before I execute the walking pile of pond scum?

So which soldiers are we talking about? I know most of the people my brother used to work with.\n\nEyewitnesses are better than notes in the House Registry—provided I can actually get them to talk to me.
I have the perfect mission for you, my doting vassal. You'll love it almost as much as me.

Seems this "Tommy Bones" fellow was duped by a Daedra named Dyzera. I've seen her before. Lurking in the shadows of my visions, just out of focus.\n\nShe must have put a hex on these "gifts." Cursed treasures … the bane of all thieves.
You are no ordinary fool, Jorunn knows a kind red spirit when he sees one! You must trod new ground where your feets can stand alone!\n\nI know just how to make you the sole hero of the day!
Your dazzlers are right here. Go on.\n\nDon't be sheepish! They'll only explode when you want them to, on my honor!
You're here. I'm here. The damn cultists are here. You know who isn't here? Vatola and his squad! \n\nThey're probably hiding. Or dead. They better not be dead.
The rush of battle, the glory of contest. There's no greater thrill! That's why we do what we do.

To save my people and the land itself, I was forced to sacrifice my brother. Chodala's own pride and ambition brought him down, but the blame falls squarely on Clavicus Vile and his damn hound, Barbas.\n\nAnyway, I am proud to call you my friend.

Veya killed Brivan. Without a writ. It was pure, focused rage. I never expected her to go through with it.\n\nIf Veya doesn't get herself killed up there, the Morag Tong will hunt her down and execute her. Like a rabid guar. Her and me both.
If you'll excuse me, I'm quite busy at the moment. Come back and see me later.
Give me some time and then look for me in Vivec, if you happen to be in the area. Once I finish adjusting my attitude, I'll make it up to you.\n\nI know a lot of ways to show my appreciation, hero.
So tell me. What did you discover my man-servant doing when you happened upon him? Did he provide an explanation as to why I'm still waiting for my afternoon tea?
Please, do get on with it. I'm afraid Lady Laurent will be dreadfully cross at my tardiness.
The shrinking sensation takes a bit to get used to. If you begin to feel ill, please make sure to point all of your orifices away from my general direction.

Maybe we should make things official and establish a formal business. Vvardenfell has so many old spirits, there must be droves of people just looking for someone to call on.\n\nWe'd need a name though, something catchy …
My husband has more faith than I do. I fear that despite your best efforts, Veya will refuse to meet with him, let alone return home.\n\nStill, I appreciate your work on our behalf.

Azura's champion … is correct. That was Barbas, faithful hound of Clavicus Vile. A shapeshifter. He killed the Archcanon … took his place.\n\nChodala … Sotha Sil's device … impersonating Tarvus … it was all part of some elaborate plan ….
Ah, another brave soul seeking the Blessing of the Whitestrake!\n\nThough I am not as knowledgeable as Sacerdote Aloisia, I do know the account of Pelinal's Midyear Massacre by heart.
Finally! I've been pacing a hole in the floor since you left. An engine can only idle for so long, you know?\n\nDid Luciana find you? Did you find that skeevaton, Gascone?
Thanks for the help. Got any questions? Let's just make it quick, all right? My friends can't very well outrun their own shadows.
Daedric relics in the Clockwork City … how could Sotha Sil allow such a thing? We must take steps. And soon.
Did you see? Bolin! It was him. He seemed … whole again.
The machines choke and wheeze less than they used to—as do the people. We have you to thank.\n\nMay you find still waters below and calm winds above, my friend.

I sent another apostle into the Shadow Cleft and he hasn't returned. I'm worried.\n\nNot only am I anxious about the fate of my colleague, I'm concerned about the disposition of his notes. Without them, his efforts will amount to nothing.
May Lord Seht bless these honest labors … hm. I'll take all the help I can get.\n\nEnough preparation. Let's go.
Lector Naril's notes should provide at least some hint as to what happened to the apprentices he selected before me. Let's keep looking.
Please excuse me. An urgent matter requires my attention. I'll have time to talk with you again later.
Perhaps I failed to impress the gravity of our situation upon you. If my shadow gets away, we may never escape this place. So if you have something to say, say it quickly.

I know my duty. My whole life has been devoted to this path laid before me. I know the risks. The repercussions to the Planisphere, should I refuse. The repercussions to my god.\n\nWhy then … why am I so scared?
Threw you in here too, did they? I knew I couldn't be the only one Constable Baldan got the drop on!
If you have questions, you should ask them now. Once we begin our investigation, We'll have little time to dawdle.
Such a pleasure when things go as planned, don't you think? Knowledge and strength of arms, working in harmonious concert.\n\nNow if only I could get Kireth to see it the same way.

Based on the schematics, I believe the vapor manifold and distillation initiator both need repairs. Easy enough for one of my talents! \n\nWe just need a ventilation gear and a cleansing crystal. They should be fairly straightforward to find.

Ah, I was beginning to worry. Not about you, of course. These apostles have been circling me like cliff racers—looking for an autograph no doubt. So tiresome.\n\nI take it you were successful in learning about these lights and constructing a new one?
You should know that great power brings its own sorrows, even for those with the wisdom to wield it.
My Knight of Marrow will protect you. Even so, you should keep your squishy peasant eyes open. We hear all kinds of terrible noises in here. Beast noises.

Ah, I hoped to see you again, assistant. Pray tell, what did Divayth Fyr have to say?\n\nI fear that he and I might have gotten off to a poor start. Did he ask about me? Any mention of my many exploits?
I really appreciate you volunteering for all this. Not many in Clockwork City who'd stop to spit on us down here, let alone do us a kindness.
You find the little thing we talked about?
Please use caution. Chance of severe injury remains high in the chambers ahead.
Another notch in our belts, hmm? Victory over a pile of garbage.\n\nLet's head back and get this over with.

Six stars refuse to answer my call, and the primary constellations remain incomplete. Their instability threatens the integrity of the entire Planisphere. \n\nUnless returned, I fear all memories will be lost. Even to the Clockwork God himself.
Fascinating! I believe we'll be able to communicate with it now. Why don't you give it a try?
By the word of Seht, I am bound.\n\nCurrent status: do not disturb.

By the word of Seht, I am bound.\n\nMy functions allow me to offer rewards to those who wish to complete combat contracts within Clockwork City. These tasks require individuals of great fighting skill. Additional allies are recommended.

I don't know what happened out there, but thanks for bringing my brother back. I suppose you had something to do with him finally growing a spine. I appreciate that, too.\n\nMaybe now I won't have to worry about him quite so much.

Did you notice the perfect symmetry, the total roundness of the form? And the way it reacted to simple magical impulses? Incredible!\n\nIf memory serves, the chimes sounded similar to the ones that ring in the Brass Fortress.
Back again? Not many return to Brengolin's kitchen, given a choice.
Much better now, in case you're wondering. Tongue went numb after about an hour and I can't taste a thing!
Queen Ayrenn will be disappointed that the Kinlady of Shimmerene allowed a false Aldarch to murder so many newcomers.\n\nSuch a scandal makes other travelers uneasy about coming here, yes?
The ritual bowls are over there. The sooner you place the correct items, the sooner we'll receive Marieve's message.
You! You're the one I saw in my vision! I knew you'd be able to puzzle out my clues!\n\nBut listen, I haven't much time ….
Razum-dar apprehended the Kinlady. They're at the west edge of the Coral Forest.\n\nWhat happened to Aldarch Tilcalar? Did he escape?
I believe I am closer to remembering where I hid the Heart of Transparent Law. Of course, without two tower sentinels, the path to the Crystal Tower may be closed to us.
If you insist on involving yourself in some vain investigatory charade, I won't stop you. But tread carefully. The Sapiarchs have little tolerance for amateur detectives.

The Mages Guild and Sapiarchs are united in accepting Haladan's guilt. No one else will help. You and I are his best advocates.\n\nIf you have any questions, please ask. You should know all the facts before you set out.

Look for Guard Milerond near the Lillandril docks. From everything I've heard, he's an honest, upright fellow. If you tell him you're looking into Haladan's murder, he'll provide all the answers he can.
New in town? Well, welcome to Lillandril, newcomer.\n\nA bit of friendly advice: have a care around the Sapiarchs. They can be … prickly.
I don't have anything to say to you or anyone else. Please, go.

I asked the Conclave of the Eleven Forces to ponder how we can learn more from the abyssal pearl. With the additional information you provided, I expect that Iradal or Amaleera will be able to develop a new avenue of investigation now.

I knew it the moment we met back at the ruins. I sensed there was something special about you. The fact that Valsirenn hasn't stopped talking about you just confirms my original assessment.\n\nI'm glad I was able to help you escape that mind trap.
Another successful rescue? Thank goodness.

Oh, hello! Sorry for wandering away. I've been so worried about finding my brother, I thought I'd take a moment to just breathe. I always find the sea so calming.\n\nHow goes your search? Were you able to discover which of the hopefuls is Larydel?
Has—has she left? Has Rinyde departed for Lillandril?

Welcome, fellow Hopeful! What's your talent? Ventriloquism? Dancing? Oh! Are you one of those illusionists I've heard so much about? \n\nNo matter! You're here to play the Game of Boasts, aren't you? First, we must perform together!
Well hello there! Good to see another Hopeful join us. Would you like to help me with my performance?
Where is your mask, Hopeful? If you wish to join the House of Reveries, you must first respect it.\n\nYou have come to play the Game of Boasts, no doubt. Very well, we will perform together.
Thank you for looking into this, ceruval. I just hope we're not too late ….
You did it!
This manor is closed by order of the Divine Prosecution, so I will keep this brief. Who are you, and what do you want?
I'm sure we have nothing to discuss.
Oh no, poor Glardir. You have to stop her before she does something dangerous!

I really thought I was going to have to do a lot more convincing. Helping strangers break into keeps a hobby of yours? Odd hobby.\n\nWhat I really need is a distraction. If you can keep Lindafwe, at the gate, busy for a minute I can handle the rest.
There's still power clinging to this Aldmer altar. It must be the bridge she's using to travel to and from the realm of that—thing.
Glardir! What has she done?
So you distracted one of my performers, ay? A bit of drama is fine, but don't overstep!
This is all so strange. I just … need a moment to think. Puzzle it all out. Come, let's head to that northern stone.
I just want you to know that even if the Conservator doesn't appreciate your efforts, I'm truly grateful for your help.
I really do need you to hurry along. Inspiration could strike me at any moment, and I simply must have the perfect colors when that time comes.
What is wrong with you? Why couldn't you just continue on your way?
Mind your step there, stranger! These little beauties are as delicate as they are delicious.
So you've volunteered to collect Tindoria's arduous list of artistic materials? How exciting. Do try not to get eaten by anything unpleasant.
That look on her face has me worried. She's never this … morose.
I can handle myself. Get to your gatehouse and I'll do the same.
Keep going. Valsirenn will make sure we aren't too far behind you.\n\nThe Heart is close. I can feel it.
I've never seen the Ritemaster like this. He's so … diminished. It's this realm. It's doing something to him.
I'm not usually the skittish sort, but those crows are starting to creep me out!
Just give me a moment. I need to process this …. Have to keep a clear head.
All ready to head out then on your big adventure?
Please, have a care with our things. We don't have much.
You have your instructions, yes? I can't imagine any of them involve talking to me.

How strange. I've never seen an illness give strength to those it has afflicted. You would think these poor creatures would barely be able to move, what with the state they're in.\n\nWhy would the cult put themselves at such risk?

The poor Sapiarchs. They tried to speed up their ritual despite the risks, and all they accomplished was to get themselves killed.\n\nI don't know about you, but I'm losing confidence in the Psijic Order's ability to see us through this crisis.
This is ridiculous! I had no wish to see Iachesis harmed. He was my friend! He tried to save my daughter!\n\nIf my wife wants a battle, though, tell her I'm ready to oblige!

I knew this wasn't going to work. Speeding up the Sapiarch ritual was a long shot, at best.\n\nWe should have had the Conclave working on a solution all along. The Psijics could have figured out how to attune the Resolute Diamonds.
Wouldn't go any deeper if I were you, dryskin. Darkness crawls along the walls of Eton Nir. Only thing you'll find here is an ugly death.\n\nThat, and the corpse of my former apprentice. Most likely.

Vindilween told me where she sent you. I've been having the most interesting conversation with this Divine Prosecution person here. Did you know the Tall Elves have at least three rules for every possibility?\n\nOh, did you find the stolen goods?

Bring me the items I specified and then we can discuss an audience with the Proxy Queen.\n\nRemember, I need a recommendation from the Sapiarch, a writ from the Justiciar, and tickets to Enigma's upcoming performance.
Vinelore must have been more shaken than she looked. She didn't hit anything vital, far as I can tell. \n\nI don't usually work on people, but if I can stitch up feuding echatere, I can handle this.

Don't tell me you've been swept up by such sentiment too? Tableau is a great artist. With her talent, she could ascend the ranks, perhaps even work for royalty.\n\nHer family line would forever be honored. I can't let her give that up.
This certainly … played out differently in my head.\n\nWell, I suppose the good news is I was never actually kidnapped, and no one was hurt! All around, not so bad of a turn out.
You're the first thing I've encountered that isn't a slavering beast or drooling savage. Begs the question what you're doing out here. Did that idiot Mehdze send you?

The site is close. I just know it. Dramatic instinct.\n\nMy antiquated directions said the entrance would be where two falls meet stone. Sounds more like an uncomfortable pratfall than landmark, but my guess is the site is near water.
Ah, there you are! Glad to see a few of our standard spells of finding still behave in expected ways.\n\nI could use your assistance if you have the time to spare.
Such accommodations! The life of a scholar seems so much more luxurious than what this Eye of the Queen is used to.\n\nMaybe Raz's next career will involve dusty scrolls and books, yes?

The Tribunal has been warned. They will make preparations in case the efforts here fail. I doubt that even they can weather the resulting storm if the worst comes to pass.\n\nAs I calculated, your actions will determine the outcome of these events.
Just thinking about what sits below us makes my skin crawl. We can't leave fast enough.

I don't know what fictions that Wood Elf has been filling your ear with, but I can assure you it's all an attempt to weasel out of punishment. If you hadn't intervened, he would have gone on doing what he was doing. His only regret is getting caught.
Dribble a bit of this in the water sources around here and the stranglers should die off in a few weeks. Just the stranglers though. Promise!\n\nI should go apologize to Vinafwe for this.

I must say, I've just had the most dreadful day.\n\nFirst my betrothed runs off with some Wood Elf, and then she manages to get kidnapped by werewolves! At this rate my reputation may never recover. To think Niralin would put me in such a position.
With my help, you were able to extract yourself from K'Tora's mind trap. I just hope that the techniques I used to assist you will work on the others.
Did you see that? Why did they run from us?

Are you really going to fight a Dragon Priest? Haven't you heard the legends about them? I may be an Undaunted, but I'm not a fool.\n\n Well, you're either incredibly brave or ridiculously stupid. Perhaps even both.
All right. Now that we've got a dueling foil and Lirendel's full name, you should grab his second by the collar and arrange our duel, eh?
Speak with your Orc friend, Ruguzog. I'll be along soon to teach him some respect.
How undignified! Clubbing a Mer over the head with his fist? This Orc is a savage!\n\nPlease don't tell him I said that.
Find out how the Sapiarch was able to survive when the rest of the sages succumbed to Nocturnal's magic.
I'm not big on libraries, either. Smells too much like old books.

Ah, another newcomer! Would you possibly be interested in helping the Divine Prosecution?\n\nWe need assistance with a sudden abundance of investigations and you seem perfect for the task. Compensation is generous, of course. What do you say?

Thank you for coming. I've called you here to discuss a matter of grave importance.\n\nThe Crystal Tower's defenses have been severely weakened. While it's still protected against Daedric influences, any mer or man can now enter its gates.
You return carrying nothing, and with no one at your side. Have you failed? Did you find this one's Nubani?

As a justiciar of the Divine Prosecution, I request your aid, newcomer. Dangerous entities have appeared throughout Summerset and, as much as it galls me to admit it, we could use the help of skilled adventurers.\n\nAre you interested?
You're back. Cainar returned and said you went in search of Miriya and the marines. Tell me, is the Sea Sload threat as dire as the Queen's cat intimated?

Find Grog and release him before the Sea Sload turns its attention his way. Meanwhile, I'll see if I can find out more about whatever these creatures have planned.\n\nWe can rendezvous on this spot after Grog is safe.

Hey … don't I know you from somewhere? Oh yeah, the bucket! I still haven't gotten the stink out of my favorite tunic.\n\nYou can make it up to me. Get me out of these chains before the big slug notices I'm here.

Do not concern yourself with this matter of the fragments. I am confident that a solution is near to hand.\n\nFor now, set your mind to the task laid before you. A Psijic, once committed, should never deviate. Farewell.
I'll continue to review these fascinating tomes while you collect samples of the mind magic particles. Between the two, ultimate understanding is within our grasp!

Though it may appear menial in nature, refining dust into ounces is a foundational and essential exercise for all practitioners of the art of jewelry crafting. \n\nFrom the raw means of nature, beauty is wrought.
I question the value of an interrogation in the state she's in, but at least she's more cooperative than usual.
He wants to take me somewhere private to talk. Can't let his friends know he's got a spine raised for me.
It's good to see you again, initiate. The Loremaster told you about the breaches in Valenwood, right? I have your equipment here.
I just need some time, initiate. To think. Be safe, all right?
The call of the Old Ways can sometimes be contradictory. The Relicmaster knows this better than most.\n\nTell him Josajeh will take the Augur with her under my authority. He will understand.

Jee-Lar's working on his boat again. Said something about wanting to talk to you before bringing me up to speed on your investigation.\n\nI look forward to hearing all about it when the two of you are ready to share.

We'll need to move further into the keep if we wish to confront Vykosa. \n\nDespite my previous misgivings, I feel it would be wise to speak to Narazda about what lies ahead. Her knowledge of the Moon Hunter Pack has proven useful so far.
We did it! We actually managed to collect the indrik's heart. Now we just need to deliver it to Hircine.

Another note? It talks about the altar where the elders prepared the ritual to bind the Wuju-Ka.\n\nHmm. I think my ancestor led the Imperials into this cavern and fed them to the Wuju-Ka! He saved our tribe, but made the voriplasm more powerful.

I marked locations on your map. That's where you can find two of the Blackguards that carry the maps that reveal where the expedition ship is moored. I'll get the third map piece, then we can meet back here and tell Concordia what we uncovered.

I trust you will keep a close eye on Famia, and the others.\n\nRemember, our party is bound by a desire to find the Remnant, but little else. Please, do not let your friends do anything that might jeopardize our work. The Remnant is too important.
Please, don't keep Kassandra waiting. She's eager to meet you!

Zadaza hopes you are not too fond of your boots. The marsh eats boots only slightly less often than it eats people.\n\nHopefully we will see you at the xanmeer soon. If not, well … this one is sure you will make some lucky crocodile very happy.

Is this your first treasure hunt, too? I'm so excited!\n\nI scrounged up my fair share of treasures in Valenwood, but root-caverns hardly measure up to a xanmeer! It's sure to be packed with all kinds of treasures. Maybe even some delicious new bugs!

Bright-Throat Village is very beautiful.\n\nDo you feel how these pilings sway in the wind? How the reeds peel from the frame ever so slightly? A reminder that this stability is fleeting. I will enjoy it to the fullest.

I feel so helpless, waiting here while Cyrodilic Collections searches through the kitchen midden of history on my behalf!\n\nBut you don't want to hear my complaints. I'm sure you came to see me for some important purpose. What can I do for you?
I expected it would be at least another week before anyone else reached this crevasse.\n\nListen, whoever you're working for, I'll cut you a better deal.
Enjoy the village? Much here is worth scavenging.
Did you make it in time, or did those Blackguards make off with the relics?
Bright-Throat Village is so breezy. How do their scales stay moist in such conditions?

You would risk life and limb for a stranger? Kishi believes that outsiders aren't intrinsically bad, so I accept his opinion and thank you for your help. \n\nKishi was taken to the ruins at the north end of the village. Save him and send him away.

So, one of us must remain here to guide these souls to rebirth? Well, my soul has made this journey countless times before. I will probably only have to ask the Hist for directions once or twice.\n\nI joke, of course. I would do this thing gladly.
I have no time for you. Leave me.
I spread my truth-spines. All doubt is dead. The Hist's will is clear.
We should take Haxara and go. Surely you've gathered enough to prove how dire the situation is?
Fine day for a drink, eh? What day is it, anyway?
We will do everything we can to restore Haxara and her child to unity with the Hist.
I don't know why I bothered signing up for this glorified treasure hunt.
Be mindful where you step when passing through the uxith.
Be very gentle when handling the sun-blessed toads. They can be quite fragile when they become excited.
Keeping Lozwug's attention will not be difficult. He is desperate to unload his belly-aches on someone. The hard part will be trying not to laugh, I think.

I can't believe you found another vakka stone! I'm glad you're back. I've been hearing some very distressing whispers, and I think I even saw a ghost! That's one archaeological hazard I'd just as soon avoid.\n\nLet's keep moving, all right?

As always, Jaxsik's beady Naga eyes see only vengeance and mayhem. I see opportunity.\n\nThis Blackguard is a survivor. Survivors are useful. If she returns to her sword-kin with tales of what she witnessed here, it could discourage future attacks.

This one is known to us, ojel—a Blackguard savage who led the raid on our people. Now, in our Hist's mighty name, I will hack it dead.\n\nIf you want to talk to it, be quick. Tsojei is thirsty, and Sithis is waiting.
Please, find Ree-Nakal. Every moment we waste is torture for my children.

Your sap-addled friends are going to wake up whatever's in this damn place, and then guess who's going to have to clean up the mess?\n\n'Course, that's what they pay us for, right? Cleaning up messes. And making new ones.
Go to Famia, ojel. I speak truth—I will be there soon.

If we really do intend to participate in some kind of dream-wallow, I'd stick close to Xukas and Jaxsik-Orrn. I'm sure they'll be able to guide us through it.\n\nI'm curious about how it works, but honestly, I've never even had a glass of wine!
Don't you just continue to amaze? From what I hear, no one's defeated the Hall of Beasts nearly as fast as you did!\n\nNext is the Vampire's Pen. Ugh. Talk about putting your neck on the line!
Welcome back. Dare I hope that Nisswo Paraxeeh agreed to help?

Thank you, beeko. You've at least given me time to work up some nerve.\n\nAnd please, be mindful to show Sulahkeesh only respect. It would be best not to invoke her anger, given her … past affiliations.
Welcome back. Your footfalls have a very peculiar quality, did you know? You bear much weight on your shoulders, I sense.\n\nNo doubt you have spoken to the claimants. Tell me, what have you learned?
The Bright-Throat elders have already given me permission to bury the branch. Just please be mindful not to harm the roots.

We of the Root-House tribe are proud travelers, roaming the swamp in search of that which will sustain us. \n\nAnd if someone else happens to be in possession of what we need? Well, hopefully they are clever enough to protect it.
How glorious! The chaos, the destruction! We have truly honored Sithis this day.
You are the one Xukas spoke of, yes? Friend to the Bright-Throats? I need your help. We need your help.\n\nOne of our tribe has been killed. Brutally.
I crossed paths with the Skin Taker by the Dead-Water pools near our village. I wish you better luck in your pursuit than I.\n\nKill this Skin Taker and I should very much like to hear about it.
Greetings and salutations. I was curious to know if your travels are soon to lead you through Bright-Throat lands.
I think we got what we came for, but I'm going to pull a few extra parts just to be sure.\n\nNo need for you to wait up. I'll be safe enough, now that you've demolished the sentries.
I have a deep aversion to conflict of any kind. I do hope the Argonians agree to m'lady's request sooner rather than later.\n\nThey must realize that Lady Laurent always gets her way.

A less-famous treasure hunter might think the Argonians wanted to foil her efforts to locate a renewal charm. But Lady Laurent is not so easily deterred!\n\nWe are going to find one of those charms—even if Stibbons has to search the entire swamp!

You should find friend-Jaxsik. She will have something for you too, I think. The Hist drives her, just as it drives me. Just faster … and with more angry hissing.\n\nCollecting the sap will take some time. I will join you as soon as I am finished.
The wind welcomes you, Xukas-friend. You have the Remnant Chime?\n\nPlease, settle an old lizard's spines. The beast Xukas mentioned. It did not gnaw or shed water on it, right?

It seems the Black-Tongues are finally prepared for the ceremony. I can smell the musk-reek from here. It seems, fresher somehow. Perhaps a new brew?\n\nIf that is your doing, I will wish you similar success with the Root-House suitor.
Zadaza knows of your goal. She comes to help.
Did I do the right thing, five-claw? In my heart of hearts, I think so, but in my head? I am not so sure.\n\nHrrm. Join the war council, my friend. I will be along in a moment.
Hurry. A handful of Euraxians often becomes a legion. Like stink fleas, they are!

Sunlight, flowers, fresh air. How do you people tolerate this dreadful place? There's no azure plasm. No comfy sounds of torment. There's not even a hint of the sweet scent of Oblivion!\n\nAlas. I miss the simple pleasures of Coldharbour.
Go, walker. Convince Tsazii to take her family and flee. Zamarak will find you later, after he completes the rite.
Tharn told me what you learned about Euraxia's final order. I suggest you get back to work, five-claw. We will need every advantage we can get when the time comes to face the Dragons.

Whether this Khamira agrees to work with us or not doesn't really matter. Is this ancient weapon any more dangerous than the ongoing war? I sincerely doubt it.\n\nLet's find the last triangulant and see where the map takes us.

Don't look so shocked. My Irregulars are very good at what they do. It was simple enough for them to sneak in and set me free.\n\nNow, what did you learn from the report? Anything that will help us stop Captain Saulinia and her assassination squad?
Kra! How did you hold this hammer so long? Like hot coal on the paws, right? Mara'dahni just can't drop it in a bucket of water and forget about it, can she? No, I guess not.

What this one would not give to see you kick those Bonechime bastards in the teeth!\n\nUnfortunately, Numaia cannot leave her beasts unguarded. Life on the ranch has made them fat and lazy. Especially this one. Yes, Milksop, Numaia talks about you!
The Dragonguard was gravely wounded. We must follow him.
Thank you for saving my companions. \n\nWere you also able to find my egg-mother's research notes? They would be invaluable to learning what occurred here.
Please, Silhu-jo. Please, Papa, do not go.

Silhu-jo has misgivings—many misgivings about letting young Vazbi investigate the aqueduct. The spirits sing of your strength. This one finds some peace in that, at least. \n\nPlease, just keep a close eye on her. Vazbi is precious to Silhu-jo.
We have a Dragonhorn, we just don't know what to do with it. I wish you had been able to save the Dragonguard, but we'll have to figure this out on our own.
My half-sister. She's not only a stain on our family name, she's the reason we're up to our necks in Dragons and the walking dead! The time has come to deal with Euraxia.\n\nPermanently.
Of all the foolish, idiotic, misguided things that Cadwell has ever done, this may be the worst of them all! He fancies himself a hero, but he's given Zumog Phoom exactly what he needed.
I will not linger long, but I want to spend a few moments with Aneshi. Find the master key, then rendezvous with us outside Rimmen.
Zamarak wishes Khamira had not rushed off with Abnur Tharn. It is this one's job to protect Rimmen's queen, and I desperately do not want to fail in my duty again.
A small strike force, like an arrow loosed at a specific target. Nala-do approves of this plan.
At least we have somewhere to search. Not much, but I'll take it.
You never know what you're missing until it's gone. I'm just glad to have that old bit of me back where it belongs!\n\nWhat say we go and find the rest?
We must follow Rideza if we ever hope to find Ishu's daughter.
Activate the final relic, five-claw, and my attunement will be complete.\n\nThen, no matter what else happens, we will have a chance to stop the Betrayer and the Dragons.
Tasnasi will lead Khasda to justice. Such as it is in the Stitches. Meet her and the others at the Goiter's Gulp, in town.
You have to free Tasnasi. Khasda's going to kill her!

Well, the Stitches are in for a rough time of it. Khasda's gone, and all that's left are a bunch of outlaws that see a mountain and an empty chair at the top.\n\nTime to find a keg, a room with sturdy locks, and ride this whole thing out.

"Wind will stop, dust will fall, and the foundation of something new will be laid." Stillness has come, at last, to Nazdar.\n\nTasnasi has more roads ahead of her, it seems. And you. Nazdar is no prophet, but knows a wanderer when he sees one.
Good luck finding a decent place to sit. Brother and I had to have these chairs shipped all the way from Kvatch.
Pour yourself a drink, if that's what you came for, but steer away from the reserve. It corked sometime after we left Niben Bay.
Are you here about this one's Zinthia? Has she been found?
If we must fight, five-claw, you must be our sword and shield. Both Tharn and I need to preserve what strength we still have for the final battle.
Do you mind? I'm trying to eat here.
Rakazsa is dead and the caravanners are safe. I can ask nothing more from you.

Greetings. You are the ally of Abnur Tharn, yes?\n\nZahari has been tasked by the Northern Elsweyr Defense Force to seek ways to prepare to safeguard against the Dragon threat. Perhaps you would be willing to aid us?

Wine used to rejuvenate me after periods of intense exertion and spell-casting. Now I can barely taste the stuff. A good thing, too. Khajiiti wine is cloyingly sweet. Like drinking candied plums boiled in moon-sugar.\n\nI presume you have news?

Look how the Moons converge in the sky. The time is not right for such an event. The Lunar Lattice has been altered, causing Jone and Jode to merge.\n\nLegends say that this occurs when a Dragon eats the Moon. This one hopes that is only a legend.
Abnur Tharn and I worked out our next move. Talk to him. He is much better at describing strategies and tactics than I am.
So, the Moonlight Blade opens physical doors, as well? Fascinating. Go on, sword-wielder. I'm keen to see how this works.
It is good to see Shando again. Speak with him, child. I am certain he has things to tell you.
We should begin our hunt, sword-wielder.
This one hopes his brother will be of help to you. Unfortunately, he is not very useful. Not like Rakhzargo!

It's about time Kideya's layabout son helped around here. He may be clever, yes, but when it comes to farm work? You would never believe he was born and raised in Merryvale.\n\nAt least Rakhzargo has the decency to help his poor mother.
Ah, just as Raz suspected.\n\nThese caverns extend below the entire valley. Farmers used them to store tools and equipment, before there was a series of cave-ins. They've been abandoned for decades.

Find the source of this army of undead. And if you see Khamira, send her back to Riverhold. She's as reckless as she is capable, which is a dangerous combination.\n\nI'll make my way back as well. After all, Gharesh-ri would be lost without me.

Ah, hello there! Good to see you again, old chum! Have you come to pay your respects, too?\n\nIt was the strangest thing. I dreamed I was looking at this very gravestone. So here I came and there it is, all solid and everything!

You killed a Dragon. Impressive, but don't let it go to your head. It was just one, and not even that large of a specimen.\n\nPlus, of course, no one will remember your feat. They're all going to be talking about the return of their queen.
See how the siege weapons sit upon the walls? When it comes right down to it, you're looking at the secret of my half-sister's success.

So you must now retrieve the Singing Crystal, yes? I have never heard of such a thing, but it does explain how the mural plays its song.\n\nIf I was a warrior, I would offer you my blade. For now, I will just wish you luck.
Rajhin's Shadow! Here in our museum! I cannot believe it.\n\nWell, what are you waiting for? Trust me, you do not wish to make the avatar of a trickster god impatient.
So that's a Dragon …. He's large. We have our work cut out for us. I pray to Z'en we don't toil in futility.
Thank you! Jora-ri can finally rest next to his beloved queen.
Zamarak feels like he should hit something in this situation, but the necromancer is not here.
No need to speak through these bars, walker. The key to your door can be found on the dresser.
The mystery of the two Cadwells must wait. Right now, we must prepare to defend Riverhold from Euraxia's forces.
As nice as these facilities are, I miss the boiling plasm pools of Coldharbour. Hot enough to melt the skin right off your bones. What an invigorating sensation!
Ah, I remember you! You did great work for me in the past. Perhaps you'd be interested in more work? This time fighting Dragons?
Ah, five-claw, good, good.\n\nThis one was told to watch for a person just like you.
You've done a great service for Peryite. If Tamriel ever falls to a deadly disease, it will all be thanks to you.
Ugh. Another stranger. Hopefully, you aren't obsessed with mucus like the last one.

Thank you for helping me escape Orcrest.\n\nI don't think Filbert could have found more followers for Peryite without me. Honestly, he probably would have just stood in this exact same place until vultures pecked his eyes out. He's not that smart.

Mind your fingers, chum. These old wrought iron traps can be more than a little squirrely. The slightest hesitation or tremor will absolutely set them off. But don't worry. I have complete faith in you.\n\nI'll be over here if you need anything.
You showed wisdom in Rimmen by telling us what you saw. Show the same wisdom here, and Ak'an may not have to kill you after all.

I would be careful in Darkpool Mine, sweetmeat.\n\nSoft-headed cultists took it over shortly after we sold your friend. That is how the slave trader died. The cultists tug on Merrunz's tail in hopes he will scratch their bellies. Pathetic.
Ah, five-claw, you are a tricky one, yes? Like a mouse hiding in the tall grass. But Lyrrsazhi found you. She always does.\n\nThis one brings a message from the queen.
Looks like there's a lever on the other side of the wall. Marmalade should be able to fit through the crack. Try giving the whistle a go, eh?

Welcome back, friend! Rigurt found Lady Izza! She's not as talkative as the women in Windhelm, but she's quite classy. Rigurt is sure a Nord ballad will convince her to help make peace between the Nords and Khajiit.\n\nWhere are the Screaming Mammoths?
Go find the other Xivkyn dummy! Show it what an enchanted Daedric warhammer can do!
Scrawny! Stringy! Will … will cut his ears off! Cut, cut, cut!
So much to do, so little to do it with. Moons give us strength!
Well, now we've seen the threat that's upon us.
Yep, death. On wings. Now I'm questioning my sanity, among other things.
This would be simpler if my physical form were restored. I could have easily woven a web to snare that Dragon.

We should return to the large chamber where we saw the Dragon. From there I can get my bearings and possibly detect the location of the aegis.\n\nWith the power I absorbed from the aeonstone, we should be able to handle anything.
Find the three glyphs in the Shrieking Scar. Let me mark the locations on your map, along with where I think the hidden tomb lies.\n\nI prepared notes as well. Feel free to take them with you.
Moonlit Cove is just south of here, right on the coast. A beautiful place to visit if you ignore the skooma dealers and pirates skulking about.
The Dragon you seek is somewhere to the south, near limestone cliffs and coastal waters. There should be a cave or mine nearby. Enter it, and there you will find Yahgrondu.

It sounds like the bells are playing the beginning of a song. Perhaps they're requesting a duet?\n\nUnfortunately, I don't think my pan flute will do the trick. There must be something nearby you can use instead.
Well, that went horribly wrong, didn't it?\n\nWe should let Sai Sahan know what happened. Maybe he'll have an idea about how we salvage this operation.
Did you find anything? Something about the Dragonhorn?
Stay quiet and keep close. At the moment, surprise is on our side. I'd like to maintain that advantage.
The warrior returns. Was your search of the Dragonguard sanctuaries successful?
We will see you at the Wall, walker. She will carry Vijari if she has to.
Are you really here, zha'al? Vijari cannot trust his senses any longer.
Tharn was a better teacher than I gave him credit for. When I needed to do it, I was able to open a portal.\n\nThe island. It exploded. But the blast spread no farther. Tharn did it. Elsweyr is safe.

Zar thought we would meet much sooner, dearest friend. Anequina always was too clever with her connotations, yes?\n\nStill, you are here now, and we have some small span of time to stop the rise of the Dark Aeon.
If we find Lahini, I'm sure we can convince her to come home. I just hope she hasn't been hurt … or worse.
You talk to the ghost cat. It seems to know you.
These banners, the motifs … there's no mistaking it. This is a Dragonguard sanctuary! How dare a Dragon desecrate these hallowed halls!
Strike the bell before we all succumb to the Heart of Lorkhaj!
Find anything?
Time to leave, yes? Let's get out of here.
You came for us! Truly, walker, Daini did not think she would see another sunrise.\n\nDid you slip past Turo, or …?
Keep moving, five-claw. We need to destroy the focal points before Kaalgrontiid can initiate his ascension.
We did it, my friend! We reformed the Dragonguard and put an end to Kaalgrontiid. Not bad, if I do say so myself.\n\nI do have one last favor to ask. It concerns Nahfahlaar.
This one is glad to see you made it back in one piece. At least, all the pieces I can see appear to be in the right place.\n\nAs for the rest of you … Za'ji will take your word for it, yes?
Aeliah was worried about you. Not me, of course. I had every faith in you and Sai. Every faith ….\n\nSo, tell me, was the view as spectacular as I imagined?
When we saw the floating island start to break apart, we assumed the worst. I'm glad to see that you and Sai made it back to us.

Well met. I hear you've been busy since we last spoke. Is it true you were on that island as it began to rise into the sky?\n\nNo, don't tell me. I'd prefer not to learn the no doubt insanity inducing details.
"He'll steal a thousand jewels! He'll even play the fool! Say you love him. Say you love him."\n\nHey, walker. Can't you see I'm busy?
That went exactly as planned! Which, honestly, may be a first for Za'ji.
I'd love some time alone with Nartise, but we wouldn't talk. So you should ask the questions.
Honor and faith, wayfarer.\n\nBlademaster Kasura awaits you at the Watch House in the city of Davon's Watch. She heard tales of your Dragon slaying skills and has requested to meet you at once.
See? Didn't Za'ji tell you it would all work out?\n\nLet's head back to Black Heights and see if mother will keep her end of the bargain.
Aeliah seems to have things well in hand! And after our adventure in Moonlit Cove, Za'ji thinks it's her turn to shine a bit.\n\nThis one will meet you back in the sanctum.
I know it may seem cruel, but we can't abandon our mission. We'll see to the Clan Mother's body once we out this cult.\n\nFor now, let's examine the statue she spoke of.
Your scent. It is rather distinctive, mask-bearer.\n\nTalk to the Dragonguard. He received a letter. Company comes and it has him unnerved.
This one still remembers when her city was a glittering jewel. There were artists, artisans, bards … everyone who was anyone came to Senchal.
If this trial is any indication, Pridehome must train their warriors in the use of grappling bows.\n\n I wonder …. Did Pridehome get the idea from the Dragonguard? Or was it the other way around?
This will certainly put my considerable skills to the test, but I'm honored Lady Bebbia believed me up to the task.\n\nI've never disappointed a client before and I do not intend to start now.
Hmm? Yeah, just give me a moment. Talk to Marekki, eh? She'll want to say thank you, I bet.
You need to hurry back to the sanctum! That nasty Dragon cult plans to attack Pridehome, and Sai Sahan wants us to defend the temple.
