Shazar soon hopes to shed his soiled clothes and scrub until he sparkles.\n\nThen, back to Senchal for another show. Only there, Shazar hopes to be showered in treasures.
You can thank my daughter for all this. She can be quite persuasive when she wants to be. Just like her mother.\n\nThe Shields of Senchal are ready to aid you, Dragonguard.
Malahbu appreciates everything you have done for him, but … Malahbu cannot swim! We will just hope Sormund's big boat does not sink, yes?
A Wood Elf out on the high seas! Ha! I can't wait!\n\nJust call me Captain Acorn! Tiny, yes … but unsinkable!
Let's make our way to the next chamber. With any luck, we'll find Nahfahlaar there.

I owe you a great debt for saving Maezi and finding Winks. Thank you so much, my friend.\n\nBut what was that about Senchal and the stolen moon-sugar? Is there still a chance to recover my uncle's goods?

The vampire judges me. Hmph. True, I break the Pyre Watch code by executing a prisoner. But then again, if our code of honor led us to this grim fate, of what use was the code?\n\nJustice sometimes demands a cold heart. Let's move on.
Mother wrote a letter to Pridehome's Clan Mother! Don't believe me? Look for yourself!
Read the scroll, then we'll talk.

Nahfahlaar was lucky we made it here so fast. He was surrounded by at least five other Dragons, but they scattered after we took this one down. Za'ji grounded it himself.\n\nI'd say I'm proud of him, but it was probably sheer luck.
Have you found the stolen moon-sugar? This one needs a moment and then Maezi will go find Zhasim.

By Kyne, it's great to see you.\n\nWay I hear it, you've kept very busy since that business in Coldharbour. It's good to know I'm not the only Companion still kicking down witches' doors and freezing her arse off.

Nahfahlaar may have dissuaded the Dragons from aiding Kaalgrontiid, but who knew he could call forth spirits of Dark Aeon to fight for him?\n\nBetween them and the remaining cultists, we're certainly working up a sweat!
All these Dragon hunts going on and not a single bit brought back but trophy pieces! Damn Dragonguard is all glory and no guts!
You lead. I'll guard our rear.
We can't allow that storm to do whatever it's doing. Destroy that witch pike. Quickly!
I think … I think it worked! I stood in a harrowstorm and … nothing happened!\n\nFenn's elixir is a success. And we took out another one of the Gray Host leaders. We've done good, my friend.
This is a bad idea. We barely got out of Tzinghalis's clutches with our lives and now Svana wants to take on two of them? It's madness!
Svana's as stubborn as a Skyrim winter … but she's definitely got the blood of a jarl coursing through her veins.\n\nI'll be fine. Go check on the princess.

Rasir's cure worked! But he's still in danger. If Skor attacked him, the affliction must already be driving him mad.\n\nGo, see if you can find Rasir. I'll stay to tend Brigvar's wounds as best I can and meet up with you.

By all the mead in Sovngarde, it's good to see you and the others. Your vampire scholar seems … out of sorts … but I'm glad to make his acquaintance.\n\nLyris tells me you ran into a bit of trouble. Care to explain?
We'll get about stoking a fire. The crew will appreciate some roasted meat, sooner the better!
The Khajiit seems to be collecting frozen corpses, but I didn't see the captain among them. There has to be another clue at that camp.
I'm surprised to see the princess here. As you can see, the influx of refugees has made this place much more hectic than usual.\n\nIs there something I can do for Princess Svana?
I loved growing up in Morthal. The kind people, the sound of lapping water, the smell of cut wood. It all just makes me feel safe.\n\nBeing close to home again brings me so much comfort.
The Palace of Kings! That's what the sentry said. Come on, we have to hurry!

If I were a few years younger and had more soldiers to spare, I'd march east to the Morthal Barrow and deal with this sorcerous nonsense myself. But I'm not, I don't, and I have other responsibilities.\n\nTake this key. It will get you into the barrow.
We need to get Fenn out of there. See if you can figure out how to release him from that machine.
My father really has become a monster. Let's end this, one way or another.
The temple, Castle Dour, the Tower of the Wolf … all of Svargrim's efforts have been on behalf of the Gray Host.\n\nWe can't let him unleash that storm!
Solitude's Temple of the Divines is legendary, even back in Windhelm. But look at it now, desecrated by the Gray Host.\n\nWe can't stop these bastards fast enough for my taste.
If only I recognized the threat sooner. Or realized what I had in my pocket. I could have saved my jarl.
The corruption has spread down here. How could Meridia allow such a horror to take hold in her holy temple?
So, what did your vampire friend discover?
I have to believe that Bjora is under the influence of magic. She'd never betray us like this.\n\nLet's find the witches responsible and end this.

No idea how you two fought through this camp, stranger, but thank the gods you're here.\n\nThe Reachmen hauled the other captives into that eastern tower. The Warleader kept demanding to know about a "stolen heir." I'm convinced he means Bjora.
I need not listen to an outsider like yourself. Soon, I shall be made Queen of the Reach.\n\nUntil that time, I ponder the secrets my sisters whisper to me from their ancient stones.
You found the invisible Petraloop! Apologies—skald humor. \n\nI'm sure you'll succeed, but do not delay. There is always a chance the Sapphire Society will recognize Petraloop's value.
All this talk of impending doom has rattled my nerves. Downed half a bottle of grog and my hands are still shaking!\n\nLook, Svana needs you. And I suggest you hurry.
We should move quickly. Shelaria's methods of interrogation are somewhat …. Just hurry. You'll see.
Go on and check that balcony for a release mechanism. Don't worry about me. I can handle myself.

Phebe convinced you to help us, did she? You have my thanks.\n\nBut I hope you're prepared to work. This is a very serious responsibility, we owe it to these people to ease their fears. This is my life's work. I do not take it lightly.

We identified a few spots with reported spiritual activity. Here, take Claudina's notes. \n\nThe hope is that placing traps here will increase our chances of capturing an entity, and figuring out what happened to the missing miners! Exciting, right?

I'll need to perform more tests, but from what we've seen I believe the storm affects mortals in three distinct ways.\n\nIt kills them, transforms them into harrowfiends, or leaves them mindless. I suppose I'd say it harrowed those poor pilgrims.
Don't let the pleasant atmosphere fool you, the Shadowgreen is full of dangers.

I only have a vague sense of where my ancestor's remains and possessions wound up. I just know his things have been scattered around by the Draugrkin's looting.\n\nLet's search quickly. The people buried here aren't the kind I want haunting me.
You have the materials? Go, quickly! I'll ready my people by the caves.
If you're looking for Lady Ninetha, she's gone to deal with a commotion in town. Something about a wolf attack.\n\nThere's not a moment's peace for our hold these days.
What a waste of time. These people have no clue as to what's going on down here. I wonder if being stupid was part of their service contract?\n\nDid you turn up anything?
The kindlepitch and fire salts are in the barn. Now go. You really need to hurry!
It's a good thing Ena found out about the surprise attack. We're still not prepared, but at least now we have a little warning. \n\nGood luck out there. We're depending on you.

Deathbell grows throughout the bog. You should have no trouble acquiring it.\n\nWolves are plentiful in the wilderness around Morthal as well, but be cautious. Many seem afflicted by a strange curse. I would hate for you to run afoul of it.
You're just in time. I spotted the vampire with the eye patch. He met with a coven witch who immediately ordered her lackeys to place witch pikes around the area.

The elixir has started being distributed. That should protect the holds from the harrowstorms.\n\nMy compatriots from House Ravenwatch are already on the trail of Rada al-Saran. Somewhere in the Reach, I think. They'll send word when they know more.
Find out if everyone in the Hall of the Dead is all right. I'll make sure Castle Dour is secured.
What should I make of this timely visit? Has Jorunn finally decided to attack?
Svargrim was right to fear you envoys from the east!
My father wishes to speak with you. Don't keep him waiting.
Ah, a familiar face. Maybe you can talk some sense into these western milk drinkers. We're not a damn invasion—we're here to help!\n\nDo you know what's going on?
Viggol? He's alive?\n\nOf all the ludicrous stunts to pull. I can't believe I shed tears over him!
Did you find something?
See what evidence you can find to prove who's at fault here.
She's … not punishing me? After everything I've done? It doesn't seem possible.\n\nI will not squander this second chance. I will work with Chief Urzikh this time, not against her.
<Pickle whines in distress.>
Did you talk to the chief? Please, I'm sure you could persuade her.

Chief Urzikh's always done what's best for the clan. I trust her judgment.\n\nI hate to see Mazog punished like this, but the Code demands it. And frankly, we could all use a reminder of who's in charge here.

Oh, thank you! I wasn't able to take three steps into the cave before something attacked me. I'm a healer, and not very good in a battle.\n\nWe need to find a chillwind mushroom, deep lichen, and an unfertilized chaurus egg. Then I can heal my sister.

Well, well, well! Look what the guar dragged in! What are you even doing down here?\n\nActually, scratch that, we'll catch up later. Raynor's insisted on getting into another mess, and we could use your help.
Oh, it's you! Good to see you, my friend. You have quite the knack for showing up at the most convenient times, did you know that?
You! Of course it's you. It simply couldn't have been anyone else, could it?
This is humiliating, but my soul is trapped inside this ludicrous child's toy. I need someone with a corporeal form to help return me to my body.
Keep an eye out for dormant spiders. \n\nIn a ruin so thoroughly, you know … ruined, they've probably taken refuge out of sight. In piles of scrap perhaps.
I don't understand. We lit all of the flames, but this one glows blue as a draugr's heart. It shouldn't look like this.\n\nDid we miss something?
See anything suspicious?
See to the meat, friend! Rigurt must tend to the fire!

Kyne bless you, friend.\n\nWe can't hold this position much longer. We need to push Lord Falgravn's forces back north. My swordthanes and I will be right behind you. But if we fall … well, I'll lift a mead to you in Sovngarde.

Ah, you return. I welcome any good news. Keeping this man from death tests the limits of my skill.\n\nBefore we speak, Lady Ninetha wants to see you. I told her of what you saw at the farm. This, understandably, distressed her.
I only did what I thought was necessary ….
After years of regret and worry, I can't believe Freiwen is still alive. It is almost too much to bear.\n\nPlease, find out if Mjolen can do anything to bring my daughter home.
It looks like this so-called Stone Garden is producing these giant stone constructs. I was sort of wondering what the deal with the name was.\n\nStill, that can't be all Arkasis is up to.
By all the gods … what kind of monster does this? \n\nSiphoning the very energies from living beings to reanimate vampires. They're just husks controlled by spirits.
Fennorian does exemplary work … despite his youthful exuberance and dashing appearance.\n\nOf course, we still aren't sure if the elixir will actually keep the effects of a harrowstorm at bay.

I hoped the words of the high priest would offer some comfort, but no. The poor man seems more in need of solace than the faithful of Solitude, and still the refugees pour in.\n\nMy jarl dead, our hold destroyed, and the high king does almost nothing.

Don't suppose you know anything about bottles? My master's stuck in one, you see.\n\nHe's probably terrible hungry. You think I should pour some of this stew in him? No, no … Stupid Borfree. He could drown in it!
There you are. It's a maze down here. I wasn't sure if I'd be able to find you, but they really want to see you up in the palace.
Go on. Better read it now, or I'm liable to put the damned thing to the torch.
That was Old Hjaalsdottir, I know it! \n\nWell, what are you waiting for? She's getting away!
Why do you loiter? I told you that you can borrow the text. Take it and be on your way.\n\nThis is a library, not an adventurers' lounge.

This must be the Pale Man's cave. See the bones? Wolves don't make patterns like this. And I've seen this before, at its old lair. A location this remote is perfect to grab folks who are alone. Told you it was clever.\n\nDid you get the draugr parts?

Well, well, well. It seems I underestimated you. With a reaction like that, you may well rival Gabrielle—our most accomplished antiquarian.\n\nI wonder what secrets you might find gazing through the Eye.
I'll meet you at the Antiquarian Circle in Solitude, near the Blue Palace. \n\nOh, and don't worry! I promised to pay you, and I will! I left my gold at home in case I got eaten by something.

Ah, you must be the Antiquarian Circle's most recent addition, eh? Greetings! Sorry for the mess. I'll tidy up down here, you know … eventually.\n\nBut I digress! Verita wants me to teach you to use the Antiquarian's Eye, yes?
What a relief. \n\nHe risked his life to save us. I'm glad he didn't have to pay with it as well.
Assassins in the city? How could this happen?
The assassin had one eye like fire, but the other one was covered by a patch! I swear, he nearly slashed me with his blade!
I'm not looking for a fight. I just want to find my sister, Adusa. She's stuck in Greymoor Keep, and I aim to get her out. Simple as that.\n\nNow, should I start swinging these axes, or can we talk?
This must be the arboretum that prisoner mentioned. We're getting close!\n\nI recognize some of these plants. Reagents for poisons, mind-twisting hallucinogens …. What is Essenia doing down here?
Well, now I suppose you want to be paid.
Are you sure you have time to talk to me? Shouldn't you be cooking with the frostheel?
Please … find the cure. It's the only way to save the pack.
The Gray Host won't stop until they drown the Reach in blood.\n\nIt's like the old Ghostsong prophecies. The end is coming soon.

I can't believe Verandis kept a secret study. I have to know the truth about him and the Gray Host, but at the same time I don't really want to.\n\nCould you check the desk, please? I … I can't quite bring myself to do it.
Might that be another observation by the Gray Host pentarch? What secrets does it reveal this time?

In the past Ghostsong witches made blood sacrifices to the Spirit Queen and the Lord of the Hunt in rooms such as this.\n\nMy foremothers believed that death pleased our gods. Nathari still holds that view.

My apologies, wayfarer. The shadows make it difficult to discern friend from foe. You do not look like my enemy. Perhaps Tu'whacca has not forsaken me after all.\n\nWhat are you doing in this wretched place?

I understand it all clearly now. Rada has opened the gateway to his sanctuary. In that distant realm, he can summon his Darkstorm using the power of the Dark Heart.\n\nHe'll consume the Reach to fulfill his promise.
Oh, sure, you get to pull levers while I have to work some kind of dark magic with the forces of the Void. That seems fair.\n\nGet on with it, the more I think about this, the less I want to do it.
Don't look at me. These hands weren't built to perform sensitive adjustments on Dwarven machinery.
We'd be better served having Old Mjolen do this, but I think I can handle it.\n\nOnce you start, I'll begin my part.
Arana needs to speak to you.\n\nDon't worry. I'll be around after you finish. I've got news, too, but it can wait.
It appears that the door ahead is also warded. Try the Nighthollow insignia again and see if it opens.

It's a miracle! Verandis, back from the dead! I can't believe we saved him!\n\nAll right, I need to calm down. Take a few breaths. You talk to him. I'm sure he has questions, but I don't think I can answer them right now.
Our clan fled to Markarth after we saw a village swallowed whole by one of those storms. Namira take me if I let that happen to my family.

I didn't expect to ever see you again, my friend. After we parted at the Doomcrag, I resigned myself to an eternity in Coldharbour.\n\nBut it seems my fate was not yet written. You and Gwendis saved me. I am more grateful than you can ever imagine.
Did I hear you right? Verandis brought that woman back to life? Not just raised her from the dead. Actually, restored her body and soul?
We need to get back to Karthwasten. Shaman Ulvoch should be able to begin the final ritual now that we've restored the wards.

I heard what you and my apprentice talked about. If something or someone has corrupted that plant so much that it can cause our rituals to fail … you must find the source of this corruption.\n\nMay the spirits walk with you, outsider.
Before we hand over the mushroom, this one feels she must tell you something.\n\nIt concerns my history with Freyleth.
Hello, scamp. You lost or are you here for the plunder?
It was only a matter of time before Rada and I crossed paths again. I just didn't think it would be this soon.

I will find a way to deal with Rada al-Saran. Lady Belain and the Gray Host, I leave in your hands.\n\nStop them from feeding the Dark Heart, and it should fall dormant again. Let us hope that it isn't too late to foil Rada's plans.
I'm ready. Use the keystone.\n\nWhatever Rada al-Saran and Lady Belain are doing in there, we have to stop them.
There was no reason for another member of the clan to die, but Freyleth refuses to see it that way. Still, we need to press on.\n\nWere you successful? Did you find a darkcap mushroom?

What fool do I have to behead for letting you in here? You're not of the Reach or the clans. You've either got the sense of a goat or the heart of a sabre cat. I'm eager to find out which. Now speak plainly. What brings you to the Despot of Markarth?

Remember, a darkcap mushroom. They grow below, in the shadows of the Blinds.\n\nThen look for a lift deeper in. It will take you to an abandoned corner of the servant's quarters. Kathad and I will meet you there.
There were a great many others drowning in that icy current. I'm certain I wasn't the only one pulled ashore. It's just a feeling, but a strong one.\n\nI want to see if that feeling speaks true.

People like us can't stay out of trouble very long, so let's share a few casks of mead while things are quiet.\n\nOh, Caddach is looking for you. He and the other rulers want to make some big announcement. I'll be along in a moment.

There's a lift in Nchuand-Zel that'll take you to the sundered land. I keep it sealed, for reasons that should be obvious, but I'll see you're granted passage.\n\nNow off you go, and take the prickly she-wolf with you.
It's been some time since our paths last crossed. I'm happy to see you again—and to know that Lyris was in good company during her time in Skyrim.
We must stop the ritual before it's too late.
We're not open for business quite yet. Come back later.

Don't look now, but something in your pack is leaking. Is that an eye? Eww!\n\nSeems I arrived just in time to watch some hedge-wizardry. I love watching hedge-wizardry—as long as it's not directed at me.
Tell Shaman Ulvoch we eradicated the corrupted plants. He should be able to complete the ritual of restoration now.
All right, I'm ready when you are.\n\nThere's something in there … something more than Dwarven tricks and devices. I'm not sure what it is, but I felt it.
Speak to Arana. Find out what she thinks the ritual showed her.
Did you find anything in the journal that might point us to Master Pythis's whereabouts?
Move along, outsider, before I put a buzzard-hole in you!

That cross fellow who set the fires, he called out that he's looking for a book. I bet all the berries in Black Marsh that he wants the same thing we do. So let's get there first!\n\nYou take the lower path and I'll head up top. We might cut him off.

Whatever that was, he's just too strong. I barely stood a chance. How in the world can we fight something like that, let alone defeat him? Even Lyranth stood powerless.\n\nPerhaps this is where my fight ends.

Excellent. I doubt you'll have much trouble finding this one, seeing as how you didn't have an issue with the last. \n\nThe ceremony is the same, regardless of the location. You will write your message and burn it.
If you find my father, tell him this isn't his fault. Nobody would have expected the Thornroots to sink so low.
Will the rest of this song fill in the missing pieces?\n\nKeep going, my friend. I feel we're getting close.

Hunter's Grotto holds a kind of a cozy warmth. It reminds me of the hours spent patiently waiting for my prey, then striking at just the right moment. Memories.\n\nIn a place like this you represent both hunter and prey. Be on your guard.
Burn away some of this dense foliage. Let's see what's hiding in this abandoned cave.

I don't know who you are, but right now I welcome anyone who comes to kill Thornroots. I'm Faorin, chieftain of the Hillhunters. Have you come across my people, traveler? Have they left anyone else alive?
Still running around out here, hmm? A lady might start to feel like I have a secret admirer.\n\nDon't I wish. As if I didn't have enough problems in that part of my life ….
I'm glad to you see you've returned safe with Fialyn. But if you found something in the mine, don't waste time talking with me. Speak with Shaman Ulvoch!

Where in Namira's hide have you been, outsider? You were supposed to fetch Eslyn and Madearn and bring them back quickly, not entertain this wild endeavor! The chiefs are about to come to blows as it is.\n\nWhat's the meaning of the vateshran's tale?
The chief-of-chiefs keeps us here like prisoners! And how dare the vateshran share the tales our elders told him in confidence. If this keeps up, I won't be held responsible for my actions.
If I knew we were to wait here this long, I'd have brought more provisions with me.
What games are the vateshran and our children playing at? I don't like this, outsider.
That story … there's so much to think about now.
Outsider, I've said all I need to say. Leave me to my thoughts, please.
I could see it in all of their faces. They weren't moved at all by the tale or the Lover's Coil. After everything we've done ….\n\nYou spoke with the chief-of-chiefs. What did she say?
The chief-of-chiefs certainly looks perturbed. How did your talk with her go? Did you make a decision?

First vampires and werewolves. Now a Nord.\n\nWhat brings you to this sacred place, outsider? I sense a desire for knowledge, but no imminent hostility. Very well. Speak and tell me what song you seek.
Ah, the wanderer. I remember you. You returned one of the sacred relics of Hircine to me.\n\nTell me, what brings you back to our as yet undedicated shrine?

Beyond this pass you'll encounter unimaginable creatures. Things no Man nor Mer should ever lay eyes upon. \n\nIf you believe yourself strong enough to face them, feel free to enter. Our Rites Matron can tell you all you need to know.
Verandis was wise to place his confidence in you. The Ravenwatch could use more with your spirit.\n\nNow, if you will excuse me, this one needs time to think about what's to come.

Whatever you did in the south wing caused the ancient mechanisms in this xanmeer to stir. But instead of unlocking the main doors, I heard the definite click of a lock sliding open by the door to the north wing.\n\nDid you find anything else in there?

I can't believe it! We defeated Vandacia, saved Sombren and Calia, and sent Dagon running with his tail between his legs. Does he have a tail? Anyway, we won!\n\nDestron would be proud of his sister. She fought bravely through the entire battle.

This old fort's in decent shape. The Black Fins have done a great job with their renovations. Governor Keshu was wise to move us here.\n\nI'll fight alongside you when the time comes. You can count on me.

The Ivory Brigade stands ready! \n\nI had to leave half my brigadines behind to protect Leyawiin, but every soldier here volunteered to come. We'll do our part to defend Fort Redmane and protect the Ambitions.

Like a storm drawing near, Vandacia's forces come. Time to take our places.\n\nI will command the outer defenses. Captain Rian and his brigadines will protect the gate. We will do our best to keep the cultists from getting past us and into the fort.
We better hurry. I came a long way to make sure none of these councilors died, and I've already let two of them down.\n\nI'll meet you at the fort. It's to the east, across the river.
You destroyed the wards. I felt each one shatter in turn. Well done, little mortal!\n\nNow tell me, what did you find?

I'll round up the brigadines and hunt down my old records in Tidewater Cave. It may take me a while. I stored all of the Imperial financial ledgers there during the confusion after the Empire's collapse.
It's no wonder the adytum's doors have weathered the neglect so well after all this time, there was a considerable amount of magic keeping it secure.\n\nI hope the same can be said for the anvil.

My egg-brothers and sisters are safe, thanks to you. There is one task left before us, if I have not yet reached the limits of your assistance.\n\nWe need to destroy the Idol of Xulunaht to ensure the Sul-Xan do not summon the spirit of destruction.
I'd deal with the Dark Brotherhood myself. Me and my brigadines. But I can't afford to leave Leyawiin unprotected. Not with everything else that has happened. The risk is simply too great.

Soldiers standing in a line, like roast guar legs all in a row? Not my kind of fight.\n\nBut I'm ready to make myself useful. The Dark Brotherhood owes Vandacia for the insults he wrought upon us. I plan to pay him back with interest.

Whatever the truth behind the murders of my fellow councilors, we can't allow the Dark Brotherhood to gain a foothold in Blackwood. I'd like you and Eveli to go to Bloodrun Cave to ascertain the situation there.\n\nTalk to Eveli and make your plans.

We're surrounded by an army of soldiers, but I feel more alone than ever. I can't stop thinking about the vision we saw in the Obelisk of Inevitability.\n\nI can't bear the thought of Vandacia doing that to me and Destron.

Well? Get on with it. Councilor Abor is in the watchtower.\n\nAnd if you find the missing servant, let me know. I suspect she's off, shirking her duties. Maybe even dallying with the councilor. Knowing Abor, it wouldn't surprise me.
It's agreed. I suggest you move ahead and clear the way of any of these obnoxious cultists and their pets. I don't believe we can rely on Drathas for any help in that regard.
A Daedric portal? Do you suppose it's safe?\n\nAll right, all right. If I wasn't in a hurry, though, I'd be looking for a different form of transportation. I'll see you in Elden Root.

Did my scouts send you, or did you slip past unannounced? Either might do.\n\nI'll be brief. I am—was—the commanding officer of Borderwatch, the fortress up the road. It's been overtaken by a mercenary outfit that calls itself the Painted Eye.
Thank the Divines for small favors. Quistley hasn't gotten himself killed yet.
Well, I guess I need to get used to skulking around these tunnels. Wading around in sewage isn't the daring heist I'd hoped for when we came to Borderwatch, but … oh, well.
The scholar said a tomb sits on the entrance. But whose? Time to bother the dead. For a good cause.
Phalevon may have been magnificent, but you are mighty, majestic, and, above all, magnanimous! Thank you for your help!\n\nI can't wait to get these historical pieces back to Gideon for study.
I can feel Calia and Destron's power growing with each passing moment. I won't be able to help them contain it much longer. We must enter Xynaa's sanctuary without delay. It's right over there.
Such a short vision, but it tells me so much. Our parents, I think they willingly gave us to the emperor and Vandacia.\n\nI suppose we should see what the next obelisk has to show us.
You might as well activate it and see what other terrible secret the obelisk plans to reveal.
No time to dawdle! Tiras's getting away!
I'm not sure that idiot actually wants to be rescued.\n\nI suppose I only really need his finger.
Oh, the experiment failed? If only someone could have predicted such an outcome!\n\nI can't wait to get out of here.

Now Jad'zirri has much stomping and squeezing ahead. She would talk to you as she works, but this one fears you would be sopping with splashed mash before too long.\n\nSee this one tomorrow and she will have fresh cider again!
Be careful … I might bite. Ha! \n\nI can see that your friend there doesn't know what to make of me. Go on, talk things over with her. I am a conundrum, aren't I?
Well, we found two of the Ambitions and kept them out of the cult's hands. Now we just have to find the other two and deal with Vandacia.

So, uh, that's an adventure, eh? Think I prefer my garden, if I'm honest. Does feel pretty good though. Helping folk.\n\nShame about that creeper, but I did finally get to meet a Hist, so that's something.
Gideon's resources are at your disposal. And you will always find a safe haven within our walls.
I can't wait to embark on my next adventure with Mathen at my side. Who would have guessed that a journey to some drafty castle would lead me to the love of my life?

Talaise the servant. She brought the councilor her meal, but never exited the tower. Yet, the councilor is dead and Talaise is missing. Hmm.\n\nAll right, let's start by talking to the other servants in the kitchen and dining hall.

An unexpected twist. Could these mortals be the Ambitions? Whatever the truth, I see only two, not four. Talk to them. See what they can tell us about Leovic's secret.\n\nBut hurry. I sense that the Waking Flame will soon arrive in force.

The remains of these renowned Shadowscales deserve the peaceful emptiness of the Void. Destruction must pass before creation and change can begin anew.\n\nHurry, we must find the remains inside the cave and destroy them.

I am sorry for absconding with dear Lady Yisara. I found myself … conflicted. Torn between two intentions. One in the cursed armor and another in the ring of Mara.\n\nYou sundered mother's curse, but it seems my soul remains tied to the ring.
So, this pitiable creature wants to escape its lot in life too. Even Daedra dare to dream. I'd be a hypocrite if I didn't feel some sympathy for its plight.
I want to know what happened to my brother. Whether he's alive or truly dead. Even if the truth says he really did die in that fire, at least I can put my doubts to rest.\n\nWhat do you wish to know?
Got a lot on my mind, stranger. If you're seeking hospitality, these carnival folk are better company than I.
Well, crispy cricket legs, I really thought this would work. My brother's doomed to remain a … whatever that is.\n\nWait a moment. Xuth! Deet-Loh's doomed, unless ….

Welcome back! Things started to get interesting the moment Councilor Vandacia showed up, but otherwise it's been kind of quiet around here.\n\nHey, Councilor Lovidicus has been waiting for you to return. You better talk to him.
So the mercenary from Leyawiin has returned.\n\nTell me, were you able to capture the assassin? Or perhaps you killed him in battle once you caught up to him? I am eager to hear the news.
Prince Vaugr's treasure was a book? Didn't know old dead eyes could read!\n\nWell, let's get it back to Captain Wereshark. Maybe it'll help break the curse!
Welcome, welcome to our humble shop on the boulevard. Are you with the young Wood Elf? She said her friend was coming by. How may I help you?
Wait! Don't hurt me! I didn't do anything! I just gave them what they wanted!
All right, this is weird. We're in freaking Oblivion and these cracked acorns are having a party!\n\nI wonder when Vandacia plans to make an appearance.

That creepy black door. That's got to be the entrance to the Dark Brotherhood sanctuary. I doubt it's as simple as turning a knob, because that door doesn't have one.\n\nLet me see that letter you found again. Wasn't there something about a key?
This is the perfect place to test my mettle. There are many adventures to be had!
Eveli says you have something for me to look at?

I heard what was discussed. I can hardly believe it. \n\nThey were so quick to pin the blame on us, and the whole time, it was one of their own people? I suppose it doesn't matter now. We've all lost friends. What we need to do is fix this.
Explain yourself. Who are you and why have you invaded our sanctum?
Interesting. I can't remember the last time Destron and I entertained guests.
Naheesh Nurwul will release the lieutenant and gather our warriors. For now, let us return to the xanmeer. We must enter Xal Irasotl.
Try using the amulet on the pedestal. Just be prepared for whatever happens. This is a terrible plan, but it's the best we've got.\n\nGo on, give it a try.

Klumbert is so very easy to prank. He can never resist a new book. The possibility that he hasn't read something will torture him if he tries to ignore it.\n\nI bet he's never read a book with a plot twist like this one!
Make no trouble stranger. Be as the wind through the branches of the tree, and pass through peacefully.

I understand that Heem-Jas asked for your help, but he can be … overzealous. We have the situation under control. Our prisoner feigns ignorance, but he does not tell the whole truth.\n\nThis dryskin was found trespassing in our swamps to the north.

How could I have not seen this from the start? Perhaps I've been too dismissive of Annyce's dreams. All these years and she's still been clinging to those damn pirate stories.\n\nBring her back, stranger. It's time I hear what she truly has to say.

We are looking for Elossi, the Sudden Gust. Her hut is northwest from the main village. \n\nEvery time I visited when trying to speak with her, she was never home. Sometimes I sneak the door open just to check, but I never see her.
That is Otumi-Ra, without a doubt. He … does not look good. Maybe try waking him? Or poking him hard?
There's no time to waste! Destroy the focal crystals so we can free Liam from the ritual!

This is really a Daedric plane? I've never been to Oblivion before.\n\nThe spinners told stories about Mehrunes Dagon. Called his realm the Deadlands. I guess that's where we are. Let's find the cultist before he does something terrible.

Let's be on our way.\n\nA word of warning, though: some of the golems may wander the halls ahead. There shouldn't be many of them, but as my master used to say, prudence is victory's prophet! Sorry. He was very keen on weird proverbs.

That tempest in the sky—it is surely the work of Flame-Herald Bahsei. Xalvakka's summoning has begun.\n\nYou have fought well so far. But we must hurry. Head toward the swirling cloud to reach the xanmeer's entrance.

Hmm. I recognize that swagger. You once darkened the door of an establishment my brother and I ran in Northern Elsweyr, did you not?\n\nMuch as I would relish renewing our acquaintance, I'm a bit too distracted. Damnable Fang-Furls!
Visitors aren't allowed to just wander about in Fort Blueblood. If you have business here, go see Commander Ortin.
I'll be right after you. Just need a moment to … you know, compose myself.

Lord Silvelle told me more than once that I should be grateful that he didn't just drop me off at some orphanage or another. But this whole business of buried secrets and deliberate lies is infuriating, regardless of the reasons for it.
I came by to find out what was keeping you and the Ambitions. Where are they? What happened to Calia and Sombren?

Meet me at the largest of the volcanic vents, it's close by. You can't miss it. \n\nI'll give you further instructions on how to help me with the ritual once we arrive. Come along, fresh legs! Nature waits for no one.
Whoever you are, untie me so I can get away from these villains! I can see to it that you are well rewarded for your help!
Despite the gravity of the situation, you should know that I was able to decipher a portion of the encoded documents before Vandacia whisked them away.

I can't say I understand what all the fuss was about. It's a box. A fancy box, but a box nonetheless. Hard to imagine that this piece of fetching garbage has caused my family so much anguish.\n\nI'll be happy to bury it.
Well met, adventurer. I bring you a message from Gideon.
The Shade Sickle is gone, my friends are employed by a necromancer, and Nocturnal continues to torment me. I hope you can set this to rights.
Well done. Xocin says you arrived at a critical moment. Thank you for bringing our egg-brother back.\n\nNow to decide what to do about this Xyria business.

It feels wrong asking you to head into that vault on our account. But I have my orders.\n\nI'm sure you can handle yourself, and I know Xocin can too. Still … got a bad feeling about this. Be careful.
Well, now I feel the fool. I made you all worry. Dragged you into this mess. Sorry to be such a pain in the arse, as my daughter would put it.
An adventurer? Wh … what are you doing in this cursed place?
The ward is deactivated, but I find that little comfort. The Daedric emanations feel even stronger without that barrier holding it back. We should prepare for the worst.

I doubt the Waking Flame expected us to get this far, but they're beginning to realize the threat we pose. Keep up the attack while they're still unprepared.\n\nThese corridors should rejoin beyond the room ahead.
Let's find the artifacts we came for and begone. The treacheries of the Knights of the Silver Rose are of little consequence to me.

I did not expect Sombren to turn against us. Or for him to try to take the power of the remaining Ambitions. He now possesses the power of Destron and Calia, as well as his own.\n\nIf he hands that power to Dagon, neither of us will like the results.
Get down! Don't let those entrail-suckers take you too.

Yes, good. A fine enough effigy you have made.\n\nIt must be imbued with the Evergloam fires created by the crowmothers. Take it to a brazier here in the brewery and douse it in the flames. That will give it the power to attract the Crowborne Horror.
Smug bastard. To think I used to look up to him as a mentor. He's more of a monster than the Daedra!
I'll follow you into the portal. I need to get close to Sombren. Pull the powers of the Ambitions from him and form the egonymic! And I have to do it before he gives his power to Mehrunes Dagon.

Mehrunes Dagon's egonymic. That sounds powerful.\n\nI remember Sombren was searching for something that would keep us safe from Dagon. He said it was the only way for us to escape our fates. But he never mentioned an egonymic.

All has turned out to my satisfaction. I learned what I needed to and you eliminated the threat of Incarnates laying waste to Fargrave and the mortal world. \n\nAnd with Sister Celdina and Valkynaz Nokvroz gone, none remain to build new cataclysts.
Have you heard the words of the Dread Lady? Would you like to?\n\nCome back later and I promise you'll be impressed.

I am not all right with what just happened! Lyranth and I managed to find Sombren and Calia. We convinced them to come with us. But I had no idea he was going to explode those poor ghosts!\n\nDid I hear correctly? The Anchorite is the last Ambition?

So, the Anchorite is the Fourth Ambition. Interesting. However, my tolerance for mortal emotions has reached its limit. Who knows what I could have learned had I been allowed to question the emperors?\n\nAt least we have the surviving Ambitions.

While training to become a wise woman, I learned some Daedric lore. Mostly how to avoid or banish them. But never have I heard of one that feeds on emotion like this. Or … a concept.\n\nProtect Atrozu at all costs. We will kill this creature.
Ah, little mortal, your timing is impeccable as always.\n\nOf course, if you had arrived just a few moments earlier, I might not have wound up with that damn blade stuck in my chest.
The root you found was a perfect specimen. And the tincture, just the right shade of distraction. The potion should work perfectly now.
This whole place feels temporary. Not a proper headquarters at all. I wonder what the cultists use it for?
Do not tarry, little mortal.
Place that lucent in one of the discharge labrums.
Since you found your way to this portal, I assume you also recovered a portal key and the cipher necessary to activate it?
My grandmother. I'd forgotten what she looked like. She sounded so peaceful. Thank you.

We've entered an archive of some sort. Maybe we can find secrets related to the Order of the Waking Flame. Secrets that Lyranth has been looking for, maybe. Let's look around and see what we can uncover.
The daedrat raises a good point. I shall wait at Wretched Spire. Find me there when you and the Anchorite have learned what you can from the blind seer.

Let me show you a secret exit from this place. A sewer, yes, but one that has not been used in a long time. It would be best not to be seen leaving—you do not want your enemies to wonder what the seer told you.

Many enter the Blood Pit. Few come out again. In truth, I did not know mortals were so resourceful. And more resilient than I had been led to believe.\n\nOr perhaps you are just an unusual example of your kind.
Faven must know what you learned. I refuse to allow my protection to fall. And I doubt you want to see the mortals here endangered by this cult.\n\nWe must return to Spire Hall.
Great, another portal. Just what I was hoping for.\n\nAfter you.
You dare speak to her lowly prophet when the Dread Lady herself stands nearby? I'm surprised she hasn't flayed you alive for such an insult!\n\nGo. My mistress has words for you.
I followed you into the Blood Pit. I'll follow you to Annihilarch's Summit, too. I'll see this through to the end.

With Tephilaz sent to Oblivion for a while, I feel uncertain about who can continue the treaty negotiations.\n\nIt took a while for my father to trust the Dremora. Without him, the council could get pressured to purge all the Daedra.
Can you hear all of them? I hear all of them. Pour the season on the coals, all good children get sweetrolls!
Do not let your guard down for even a moment. Mehrunes Dagon is not easily fooled and especially not for very long. Find Sombren, but be prepared for anything.
We march on Destruction's Solace! To victory!

Grab the daedrat and prepare yourself. The dangers of Annihilarch's Summit are enough to make even a Dremora pause.\n\nI assume we will have to deal with both Nokvroz's forces and the Order of the Waking Flame along the way.
More Bladebearers. We'd better free them, and let them know Rynkyus is here.

Such neglect! No one has cared for this dais in centuries, but its magic remains. Realign the stones to their proper sides and it will awaken. Simply turn them to match the glowing runes nearby. But be gentle. A caress is called for here, not a slap.
Arox says this way will get us to the volcano. If that's where Valkynaz Nokvroz awaits the Anchorite, then we can assume his Perfected Cataclyst will be there as well.

I would have preferred an army of Fargravians at our backs, but this will work, too. While you and Lyranth use Whim's portal to infiltrate the fortress, my Bladebearers will launch an assault on the front gate.\n\nThe battle will be glorious!

Hadri and these others are some of the missing Bladebearers. Why Nokvroz captured them and turned them over to the mortal Dagonists, I do not yet understand.\n\nGo. I will join you after I make sure they get back to the portal safely.
Come on, let's go! Destruction's Solace awaits. \n\nLet's end this, partner.
Lyranth explained her plan to me, master. I will accompany you on this mission of stealth and secrecy. No one knows the twists and turns of Ardent Hope as well as Arox the Mutilator!
I do not know what fate lies beyond that portal, but my Bladebearers will sing of the glory of this battle for eons to come.
You over-complicate things, master. Wherever Nokvroz hides, that is where we should go.\n\nLet him listen for the sound of our footsteps and know dread!

Take these. That's a list of exclusive vintages—along with directions to where I left them—and a rune of compulsion. Gather the wine and then you can summon and corral these fiery musicians. \n\nGo! Bring us music!
I hate that we let Sister Celdina slip through our fingers, but Lyranth's right. She probably did leave something important behind. Let's look around.
Tell me what you found and I shall determine if it has any significance to my quest—or to yours.
Go with Lyranth. Find the Arox or whatever it is. I'll try to keep the Collector busy.\n\nBut hurry. I really don't want to end up in a display case.
Away to the Collector's villa, little mortal. I want to hear more about the Anchorite and her missing memories. She has suddenly become more interesting. We will be along shortly.
Hey, you made it! I was just telling Madam Whim and Calia about what happened. Why don't you talk to Madam Whim now. I've taken up too much of her attention already.
I must meditate on this. It is mine, but I gave it away. I must have had good reason.

Mortal. You seem more capable than most. The Grasp of the Stricture has a task that you may be able to assist with—the apprehension of mortal criminals.\n\nI understand your kind enjoys material gain. I can pay you for your help.

What do you want? And better yet, what are you doing all the way out here?\n\nIf you don't mind, I'm actually running for my life at the moment. So, if you could let me get back to that, I'd appreciate it.
You should speak with Bakh. If you're going to decide what to do with us once you talk to him, please just make it quick.
That thing has always given me the creepy-crawlies. I don't envy you having to fight the Undertaker, but it's my only hope.

I employed a few prospective creatures to retrieve more of these planestones, but given how you discovered the last creature I sent … I do not have high hopes.\n\nIf you come across more ill-fated employees please bring the planestones to me.
The kynreeve is not one to trouble himself with mortal allies. Perhaps there is more to you than is immediately evident.
There appears to be a daedrat in your company. Filthy creatures! Why do you consort with such things?
So many places to see! I should get out of Grahtwood more often.
Are you waiting for something specific? You should pursue Skrix's scuttling companion. Just be careful not to get a knife in your back.
It's a real mess beyond that door. Looks like the yaghra and the order have been butchering each other for days. Make good use of that chaos unless you want to wind up another floater in the cove.
See! Nothing to fear where Caska is concerned, just as Za'ji said! Though he will stick close to his first mate from here on. Haha.
Waiting on someone?\n\nSignal line won't stay fresh forever. Happy to stay here. Got better things to do than chase fake swords with you, Nirnborn.

It seems I overestimated the Anchorite's resourcefulness. Or underestimated the Collector's need to possess whatever catches their fancy.\n\nRegardless, I suppose you should find a way to set her free. We must leave before Gazmod returns.
What's the saying? One step forward, two steps back? I feel like I'm on the end of a pendulum … and it's getting ready to swing back. Hard.\n\nLet's hurry to Master Rrvenk.
The mortals in this city may be little more than vermin, but even vermin has a place in the order of things. The Dagonists will no longer disrupt that with their petty schemes.

By Lord Peryite, these Dagonists are going to give all the other cults in Fargrave a bad name. Not all of us are bent on forcibly ensnaring the minds of mortals in the city. \n\nAt least, not at present.
The leader of those Dremora—think I heard his name was Rynkyus? According to the other Daedra in the Spire, he's bad news. Don't cross him.

Any day, Mehrunes Dagon might decide he's turned a blind eye to Wretched Spire long enough. It doesn't help when rogue Dremora clans and strange mortals keep coming in and out of here, doing gods-know-what!
Step aside, mortal. Unless you wish to challenge the authority of the Grasp.

Darling mortal, how nice to see you! Is it true? Did the Anchorite learn something about her past at Mehrunes Dagon's Blood Pit?\n\nCome, whisper me all the tantalizing details. Madam Whim's lips know how to keep a secret.

I didn't expect Guild General Quentyn to turn on us, and I certainly didn't desire his death.\n\nIt seems sympathy for the Ascendant Order is more widespread than I knew. We must be cautious. Particularly with whom we choose to trust going forward.
Search along the road to the south. I'm sure my retainers picked up the shipment from the Castle Navire docks and were on their way back here. \n\nI must know what happened to Grenier and Danise.
I'm sure the Ascendant Order won't just let us walk in and take Quentyn back. It's a good thing that you are coming with us. I have no great talent for the more destructive schools of magic.
Here we stand, ready to ignite the product of our labor in an act of devotion to Zenithar. Please, you do the honors. After all your work, it surely rests with you.

Here, one of the locals marked where some lava vents are in the Firepot, we should look for the scoria there. Finding the scoria will help convince Tarrinore to leave the Firepot.\n\nI want her out of danger before I talk some sense into her.

Must Za'ji tell this sad story again? The last Za'ji saw of Queen Ayrenn, she was struggling to launch a damaged skiff. Then Za'ji was swept away in the storm.\n\nZa'ji was entrusted with getting her safely to High Isle. But he lost her. Her and Caska.

Finding Privette's sash worries me. She'd never take that off. Unless she left it as a clue. She wants me to know she's here!\n\nThe bones we found looked … gnawed on. But none of them were sheep bones. So I feel confident Privette's still alive.
Woe to the cursed bones that lie here. Mercy to those trying to put the raging spirits to rest. And pity to the ones past their prime, who can do nothing.

I'm not sure what the Ascendant Order is doing here, but they seem determined to eliminate me and Emeric. I've been able to avoid most of their forces, and the few I couldn't—well, they hardly posed any trouble.\n\nHow did you know where to find me?
We've got the staff! The moment I heard Erlibru was representing the order I knew we might have a shot. \n\nWell done!
Thank you for assisting Isobel. I'm so grateful to you both.\n\nAspirant Mortens came by not that long ago and told me he already had a honeymoon trip planned! The audacity!
Place the Fighters Guild invitation medallion on my worktable while I mix the dispelling powder.

Hey, good-looking. Didn't expect to see me turn up again? Guess Lady Arabelle's got more for me to do than stand around on a street corner looking pretty.\n\nShe calls me her operative. Indentured servant is more like it.
All those old books make mention of the Commodore's fascination with deep druid idols and an old tome. Between that and what my ancestor showed us, I wager they're all the key to this curse.
Now we have a name for the person in charge—Jailer Mannick. I don't remember seeing him at Amenos Station. Sounds like he enjoys his work, though.
I'm glad you came when you did. Any longer, and I cannot say what might have happened. I do not wish to think about it.

Lady Arabelle only gave me a quick run-down before she sent me. But whatever you brought back from the Ascendant Order sites has her raring to go.\n\nI always wanted to save a royal. And not die in the process. I'm rather fond of life, you know.
This is one of the nicer prison transports I've had the pleasure to travel aboard.
Visitors? Oh yes, oh yes. A delightful change of pace!
Valessea! I knew she couldn't resist my charms!\n\nShe seems rather distressed, however. Must have something to do with those damned lethal medallions. Go ahead and speak with her.
Queen Ayrenn relies on me to sort through this kind of business in her stead. I take my job very seriously, you must understand.

I am certain we'll encounter Amunara at the shield hall. Be prepared to use the censer. It should have attuned itself to your unique energy by now. \n\nWe'll likely only have one chance. Let's make it count.
Oh! You're back. Um. How lovely. \n\nDid you manage to find my sword?
You always take me to the nicest places.
I see you've been making the rounds. Good! We'll compare notes after all this is over. Speaking of which, Jakarn is here. I think he has something in mind.

So much for finding anything useful. If you ask me, the Ascendant Order's covering their tracks. Could be they've already got what they wanted.\n\nTalk to Lady Arabelle. Maybe she can figure out what happened here.
If you don't have an appointment, then Commander Jourvel doesn't have time to see you. \n\nThanks for your consideration.
You and Isobel should just run along. Leave the tourney trials to aspirants of stature. \n\nAspirants such as myself, of course.
Go on, my friend. Destroy the final ward and set the Evergrowth free.
We've done it! Let's find Dame Madach!

The counterspell should set everything right in Tor Draioch. Things will be just as Magister Irin left them and I won't have to face his furrowed brow. \n\nI'll need your help at the ritual site. Casting a spell this big is a two-person job.
Now we just need to get inside without raising the alarm. Easy.
No time like the present, my friend. Attack!
This one is going to have his crew call him Za'ji, Bane of Ascendants, from now on! What do you think?
We don't have much time. Let's get to the docks!
Hey there, fish. We make it to the spot and what do you know? \n\nThere's some kind of cave here, just like the map suggested.
If the Ascendant Magus hopes to take the Silver Swan for his flagship, I'm concerned for Duchess Elea's safety. We must find a way to board that ship!
Right behind you. Let's get to that ship and find Dockmaster Arnauld.

The dispensary is a separate building out back. You'll find it by the terrace where our guests can rest and take in the sea air.\n\nOnce you get inside, I'll stand lookout and make sure no one disturbs you.
Welcome to Stonelore Grove, stranger. The druids of our circle care for this sacred land and embrace all who come to us in peace.
Follow where those torchbugs lead. I want to consult with Ryvana. Then I'll catch up with you.

Let's see … the flowers are in good condition, and the torchbug is alive and well.\n\nYou treated nature with deep respect and you have my thanks. Perhaps the grove will repay us in kind. Let's begin.
The Society of the Steadfast wishes to bring peace to Tamriel through understanding. I can do my part by effectively running this hospice. Lord Bacaro put me in charge and I shall not let him down.

From what Lady Arabelle has deduced, we might have a duchess-in-distress situation developing.\n\nDuchesses, damsels, dukes, dons, small dogs … I specialize in this sort of derring-do! Let's get going.
Well? What're you still standing here for? I've got, you know … thinking to do.\n\nUgh. For Eight's sake, Donel, I know! You'll have your supper in a moment! Never satisfied, this lot.
Ah, you made it. And with the kindlepitch, too! Good work.
Please hurry, all the blood in my body is now in my head. I feel like I'm going to pop.

Would you talk to <<1>> about my problem, friend? Now that she's awake, she might be more helpful.\n\nI will need her to pay her share of last night's tab to get my scepter of office back from the innkeeper.

Your friend seems to have a hard time understanding this, so maybe you can explain it to him using shorter words. Tell him that I'll give him back his scepter or whatever when he pays his tab. \n\nAll of it!

I hoped that by investigating the Ascendant Order, we'd uncover a clue as to how to find the missing alliance leaders. Now we have it on good authority that they may be on Amenos.\n\nFrom the cookpot to the campfire, as my Great Aunt Ales used to say.
I can't believe I drank rotmeth last night! What was I thinking?\n\nI feel terrible.
What an embarrassing episode. Let me catch my breath and I'll get the money to pay the innkeeper. It's the least I can do to repay you.
I think it's working! Your friend Roslenn looks like she's waking up. You'd better talk to her—she must be confused.
With all that's happened, I can only hope my patients are going to be all right.
I have a good plan, a good friend, and a whole mine filled with monsters to get through.\n\nA pox on everything father held me back from!

I listened carefully while you questioned Duchess Elea. I do not believe she said anything that was untrue.\n\nLet's see if we can find the letter Count Damard gave to the steward. I'd like to have a look at that.
You may be able to fool the less attentive jailers and inmates of this place, but not me.\n\nDon't worry, I won't reveal your secret. As long as you tell me why you're here, of course.
After you, my friend. I insist. Besides, I need to keep watch for the Daybreak Gem while you deal with any dangers ahead of us.

Royals! No concern for their own safety!\n\nThey each went off in search of a diversion—High King Emeric to the temple, Queen Ayrenn to stroll the harbor, and Prince Irnskar to the inn. I asked the Systres Guard to keep an eye on them. Discretely.
You know this petty criminal? He has an appointment with the city magistrate today. Impersonating a Daggerfall Covenant official is a serious offense. Not to mention the contraband I found.

Don't worry. We'll collect Lady Arabelle and Jakarn, then meet you at Jheury's Cove.\n\nWho knows? If I like the looks of this Ascendant Order scow, I just might make her the next Spearhead. I figure they owe me that much.

I've picked up many skills during my travels, but sailing isn't among them. Fortunately, we have several experienced captains on hand. I'm happy to defer to Captain Kaleen in this matter.\n\nTalk to her and see how she wants to proceed.
Good job! Now let's take the ship!
I love a good party! And nobles throw some of the best parties! Remember that one we attended at Castle Navire?\n\nOh, right. I wonder if they'll let me in.

Za'ji hoped we were done with this business. I was looking forward to a few days of rest on this lovely island. But now it seems Queen Ayrenn is in danger again.\n\nThis time, Za'ji will make sure she stays rescued!

It looks like the Ascendant Order's preparing that ship for sea. Check with Captain Kaleen. She's got an idea about how we can steal that ship right out from under them.\n\nAnd if I get to shred a few rogue knights along the way, so much the better.
Song's in trouble! We have to destroy those containment wards before we get to her. Come on, hurry!
The Gateway Inn boasts an impressive clientele. I do not remember seeing the likes of you or your … friend here before. I do hope you find everything to your liking.
Please, the bandits locked me inside this cage and left me here. This one wishes to be free.
Go. Find our little Song.

I've changed a lot since my days in Skywatch. I buried that life a long time ago out of necessity. But I never stopped loving my friends, not even for a moment.\n\nIf you and Ember are finding Song, I promise to do everything in my power to help.
I left mercenary work behind a long time ago. Got a few old injuries that won't quit, of course. That's why I drink.
What … I. What just happened?
I can't thank you enough. I spent most of my time in that cell worried Aurelia would raise a search party and come storming through the front door.
Didn't expect I'd see you again. Don't tell me you found another piece of my map.
Don't … yeah, don't kill him. Can't get revenge on him if he's dead.

Now the obnoxious little brother is inside my manservant? Unacceptable! Talk to him and find out where the tools are so we can end this damn curse already.\n\nHurry. Captain Renwic's will is quite strong and I can feel him asserting himself again.
This is the spot, I'm sure of it! The tools are buried here!

You're the one who recovered the blessed awl! Amminus Varo was so distraught when he discovered its theft. I only just convinced him to put his faith in Zenithar and the labors of others to see the awl returned.
The biggest of the tree-things is ahead. Maybe the mother of them all from the way they protect her.
I think this Goldleaf character got charmed by that damnable rogue just as easily as I did!
No, Tobin, you cannot offer me a drink. And I have absolutely no intention of dancing with you.
Captain Marso and I have grown … very close, while investigating here in Rivenspire. \n\nObsidian Scar is a terrible place, but I know if anyone can find him it's you two.
Go, walker. We'll keep the Green Serpents busy.
When Aurelia wrote to say she was conducting some kind of investigation, I was shocked.\n\nBut every letter since has shown me a woman changing for the better. I desperately hope she's safe.
No time like the present, my friend. Attack!
I'll see what I can find out down here. You go question that Khajiit!

Whatever the outcome, remember that you represent the Gonfalon Chapter now.\n\nWe steadfastly commit to the principles of fair play. We are gracious in both victory and defeat. And, win or lose, we always revel when the game is through!
Guess I can't complain, seeing everyone so damn happy. I just wish Sorinne would celebrate over there. Away from my bar, and off the tables.
I'm all right. Really. Talking to you helped clear my head, I promise.\n\nI just need a moment to think. Go on. I'm right behind you.
I'm glad you're here! I can use some help with these damn druids. We must disrupt their ritual to dissipate the storm!

Tall Papa's breeches, there you are. And victorious, yes? Good. One less burden on my shoulders. Unfortunately, the most difficult part begins now.\n\nI need your help, my friend. As does Brahgas, though he does not know it yet.
Why do they always pester Raenobi …?\n\nThis one already has a drink, walker. Tell your friends Raenobi is married. Or a celibate. Whichever you prefer.
Seizing an Ascendant Order ship is a bold plan. I am proud to be a part of it. And this time, we will end the threat of the Ascendant Magus once and for all.
Not now, stranger. The grove won't tend itself, you know.
My head hurts, my back hurts. That barrier packed a powerful punch. Stupid wizards.
There you are.\n\nYou talked to Razhamad, right? I love Brahgas like a brother, but you have to win this game. You have to.

Ha! I knew it! I knew you'd be the one. Teliv's little brown-nosers never had a chance against someone at your level. Er, no offense, Sorinne.\n\nHonestly, though, I'm glad it's you. Two of Gonfalon Bay's greatest players here in Razhamad's house!

Greetings. It seems your game-baron would like a word with you—to explain the particulars of our agreement, I hope.\n\nYou have a right to know what he and Brahgas stand to lose if you fail. I certainly don't envy your position!
I need a nap. Maybe find a nice sunny spot somewhere and close my eyes for a bit.
Never thought I'd see the day when the Gonfalon Colossus laid low. Every homeward voyage I looked for that sword raised to the sky. No more, I guess. No more.
Fighting at Castle Navire? Can't say I'm surprised. The peace talks were a bad idea. There's been nothing but trouble on High Isle since they were announced.
Hey there, chum! Decided I'd come cheer you on during your first official tournament match. The beginning of a legend, eh? Good luck!

With the harrowstorm cleared, my hunt nears an end. I've scryed the location of the Pale Worm, the vampire lord you glimpsed at the ritual site.\n\nAs you've no doubt surmised, tracking the Worm is what brought me to Skyrim.

Marunji has nothing to offer you at this moment, walker.\n\nYou will keep an eye on the floor for this one's candied grape, though, yes? It fell from Marunji's muffin and rolled … somewhere. It is still fine to eat!

I truly have fortune's favor today. Someone drew this map then left it behind for us to find. It traces a path to the station's central core. Perhaps there we'll learn how the storm rose from the island.\n\nOnce I get our bearings, we can move on.

Welcome to High Isle, traveler—the hidden gem of the Systres Archipelago! You must be here about my notice. \n\nI'm working on a plan to bring more visitors to our beautiful islands. And it's a very good plan, if I do say so myself!
Archdruid Michiel must be stopped. Once we find him, you know what has to be done. \n\nI'm sure he's already begun his final ritual. We don't have any time to waste. Let's keep moving.
Archdruid Michiel has to be in here someplace. We need to find him and make him pay for all the blood he's spilled.\n\nStay vigilant. We'll find rough seas ahead, I'm sure.
Hello, stranger. Interested in earning some gold in exchange for a small favor?\n\nIt concerns the two large thugs over there. They try so hard to look intimidating. Almost adorable, yes?
Keep an eye on our friends up there. They will lead us to their master … maybe Redblade! Who knows?

I never thought I'd need to understand magic. Basic tools like a pick and a shovel, that's all I needed to know. Now here I am making guesses about the purpose of glowing druid crystals.\n\nSmash all of them so I can get back to work.
Lord Bacaro believes we aren't done with the Ascendant Order yet. As much as I wish it were otherwise, I agree.
We need to find the shrine Niraya mentioned. We must retrieve the Eldertide seed before the Dreadsails find it.

I'm counting on you, mercenary. Save my son and you can name your price.\n\nDhulef says Rahval and Ellic are by the bridge east of Vastyr. Talk to them. They know parts of Galen no one else has even seen. They must have an idea where to find Stefan.

You're willing to talk? At least you're smarter than those knights outside. I suppose Sealord Nalos and his scum have taught the people of this island to fear anyone with blue skin.\n\nUnderstand this—I don't answer to that foul beast.
I trust Archdruid Orlaith about as far as I could throw her. She'll keep Sir Stefan alive only as long as it suits her. Which means we need to do something about this mess, and quickly!
You can find the Telling Stone on a high ridge north of Vastyr, at the very heart of Galen. The Draoife Dell is close by.
What perfidy is this? Orlaith dares to attack the Draoife? That path-traitor!\n\nBah! I do not need your help, stranger. Go assist Rahval's foolish students before they get themselves killed.
I'll look after these druids. You should check on the village of Tuinh … although I doubt the Sea Elves left any alive there. I heard rumors about fighting at Windwrack Fort, too.
I always thought that Lord Bacaro was too good to be true. I should have eaten him when I had the chance. Now we have to chase him down on Galen.

Druid Laurel said something about fighting an angry volcano spirit. She was joking, yes?\n\nPlease, walker, tell Za'ji that we will not be sailing the Pounce too close to the volcano! This one would rather not see his beloved ship go up in flames.
All my seasons as a druid, and this is my first visit to Y'ffelon. I just wish it was under better circumstances.
An even older set of tunnels beneath the cellars? And locked by a Shard of the Green? What's Lord Bacaro hiding down here?
Head inside. Do not worry, Raz will be quick behind.
This one is sure you will find the trials rewarding. \n\nSpeak to this one's apprentice, Taz, for more details. Samara must keep her eyes to the sky, lest a Dragon catch us unawares.
The guardian has the druids occupied! Now, friend, take the fight to Archdruid Orlaith! We'll protect Frii.
You fight like a Sea Elf. I'd sail into battle with you anytime. Now stay out of the way and let my Gilded Blades cut the Mad Maiden free so we can get underway again.
Drink from the cauldron. Drink and dream. We will remember what the warden remembered. I do not know what we will see, but we will see it together.
Blight and rootrot! The situation gets worse every time the wind changes direction!
Oh, there you are! Lovely to see you again. \n\nDo you have a tablet for me to inspect?
Well done, friend! With Captain Siravaen and the Mad Maiden beside us, we shouldn't have too much trouble getting to Y'ffelon.\n\nWe'll meet up on the Vastyr docks and make our final plans there.
Hi! Good to see you again! Do I know you?\n\nOh, I remember! You're the adventurer who's going to help us break this curse. Well, talk to Druid Fenas. I'm sure he knows what to do.

Why won't the druid talk to us? Why won't he let us help? This is so frustrating! I am turning into a tree and there's nothing I can do to stop it!\n\nArrgh! You talk to the druid. He seems to like you better, anyway.

We'll do our best to hold the Ascendant Order's attention while you and Lady Arabelle find another way into the mountain. Look for a cave to the right of the main entrance. I remember that from when Stefan and I visited as initiates many seasons ago.
Let's keep going. I won't feel better until we find Frii and figure out exactly what Bacaro is up to.

Archdruid Rahval is in the Vine District, the druids' section of the city. He should be able to tell you where to find Archdruid Ellic once you secure his agreement to help. \n\nMeanwhile, I have much to do to prepare the city for the coming assault.
Examine the stone carvings and see what Druid Laurel can tell us about them.

This job got a tad jumbled, didn't it? I'm glad we worked together again on this one.\n\nWait until Zeira hears who I ran into. I'll make sure she knows about all your help. And how lover boy here was useless.
Yet another room filled with poisonous plants?\n\nPlease, cleanse the air once more. I cannot risk being smothered now, not when my Gwenaelle needs me.
Wrath and ruin! The Sea Elves found the door to the shrine. Hurry, mainlander!

After my fun with Neri, walking all over the beach, climbing that cliff … I am so worn out. How could anyone expect me to keep up?\n\nI tried to fill Quen in on what we've learned. Now, just let me rest.

I can never get enough of the food you land-bound eat. It's so … delicious.\n\nThe lordling sent you over to convince me to help, didn't he? My answer is the same. Why should I care about your political drama?

Ah, druid-kin. Thank you for assisting Laurel. I spoke to Ellic and he agreed to bring his Eldertide to help defend Vastyr. So I made my way here to lead my own people to the city.\n\nBut first, we must attend to the matter of the sacred seed.
Retrieve the sacred seed and take it to Archdruid Rahval. Frii trusts you with it, and so do I.
Lead on, dear. Find us a way into that mountain that isn't quite as heavily guarded as the main entrance.
Speak with Elder Verline, my friend. I must prepare myself for what comes next.

The Stonelore seed, the Eldertide seed, and the Firesong seed … all in this drawing. And Frii makes the seeds grow to become … regalia?\n\nIs this what the Druid King created them for? There has to be more to this. Let's keep looking.
Glimmertarn calls. I hear the fury of flames, a song in the throat of the hills. I will join you soon. Once this form renews, once the leaves cease to tremble.\n\nGo to Archdruid Rahval. Hurry.

I'm sure you'll have an easier time than I've had with those riddles. Check that note I made if you need to read them again.\n\nI'll admit they make a lot more sense reading them than hearing them squawked from Kiko. Suppose he can't help it, though.

The knight-commander insisted that the anonymous gift be tested before I consumed so much as a drop. It's in her private chamber, waiting for one of my handmaidens to come by and taste it.\n\nFeel free to perform your own investigation.

The Society of the Steadfast will continue to provide help wherever it is needed. Whether war or disaster, we will be there to heal, to feed, and to shelter.\n\nI give you my word, Lord Bacaro's treachery was his alone. The society's mission remains.

This is what happens when those who spend too much time on Galen get too comfortable with the dangers that lurk here.\n\nMind that you don't repeat that to the mother that begged me to save her son, if you go speak to her, but it is true.

You performed the ritual perfectly. The curse should have been lifted. Joslin and Octin should be back to their old selves by now. Unless ….\n\nOh no. The word I was having trouble translating. I know what it means now.

I'll mark the places in Fauns' Thicket where you should plant the seeds. Once the Fauns start eating, the wolves won't go near them. They really can't stand the smell.\n\nWe'll be planting seeds as well, but we'll stop by to see how you're doing.

If you need to know more, talk to Captain Dervalas. He's usually down by the southern docks. And make sure you post those handbills where the Sea Elves can see them!\n\nSea Elves can read, right? Oh, no. Is that rude of me to even ask?

Captain Marguerite and I were just having the most illuminating discussion, dear. Other than some misdirection at the end, Lord Bacaro never allowed his clandestine activities with the Ascendant Order to spill over into the Society of the Steadfast.

Lady Arabelle told me to trust Captain Marguerite and so far so good. The Society of the Steadfast restarted their relief efforts and things have been moving smoothly ever since.\n\nBut what brings you back to Galen, friend?
I lost track of my father during the first wave of the attack. We need to find him.\n\nHe can tell us how the battle is going and direct us how to best defend the city.
Did you see what happened, friend? What Frii asked us to do with that pouch of soil? It's a miracle!
Wait. Give Frii a moment.
Laurel-friend, I have been thinking. How can we help Druid Laurel? I do not wish to see her come to harm, but no flowers blossom. No seeds of thought sprout. I am … sad.
Green preserve us … first Archdruid Rahval and now … now my father ….\n\nMy father's under all that rubble! Please, you have to help me. There must be survivors! Why are you just standing there?
My crew has the dock secured, so I decided to come looking for Sealord Nalos.\n\nYou're good at running into trouble. You have my blade, let's find some.

When you find the archdruids, send them to the cathedral. Count Mornard and I will head there shortly. It's the best place to defend the injured and the noncombatants in the city.\n\nStay safe, my friend!

That temporal knot, it's unlike anything I've seen. Threads of chance and potential tangled around a single point.\n\nI tried containing the distortion. But it … resisted. It had power, but also a will. We must track it down again.
Galen possesses such beauty, such history. To see it scarred by war and strife like so many places on the mainland, it breaks my heart.
As wind clears the air and rain washes the land, I will help stop the false king.
I don't know what madness has come over Archdruid Orlaith and the Firesong. But somehow we must burn out this rootrot. Before they do even more harm.
A dark day. I knew Archdruid Orlaith was dangerous. But I never imagined she'd inflict such reckless destruction on people who'd done her no harm.
I'll see Frii safely to Y'ffelon. If the Firesong show any sign they don't intend to keep their word, I'll get Frii away from there. Now go on down to the docks and find Sir Stefan.

After all this, I think I'm going to take Galphen up on his offer and find a quiet spot out in the wilderness to settle down.\n\nWhat do you think? Can a former knight and a druid find a place to be happy? Couldn't hurt to try.
Ah, friend! Thank you for helping to rescue the captives from Y'ffelon. Through your efforts, Dame Fayda has been returned to me. I mean, to us. Praise Y'ffre for small favors!
The glyphics that Dralys took from me. Recover them, please.
Valinna wanted the staff for Mafala? The staff is a tool—powerful, but a Magnastylus can lead without it. That is the truth that Valinna never learned. \n\nIs it all over?

I came as quickly as I could. As soon as I saw what happened at the camp, I followed the tracks here to the outpost.\n\nB'vek, what a terrible thing. If there are any others left alive, we need to save them.
This one is not injured, walker. Perhaps it is a better fate than he deserves.
I heard some sort of disturbance after I sent one of my priests to follow Rilasi into the crypts.\n\nMight you go investigate? We have no idea what she's doing down there.
I'd ask what you're doing or who you work for, but what would be the point? You're not my target \n\nIt'd be best that you leave me be. I can't be bothered for small talk right now.
I promise, I had no idea Overseer Ulfengar asked for aid. If I had known? Regardless, we're here now. We have to do what we can to help them.

Laboratory security and oversight protocols restored. Locating Apostle Nilphas Drethan. Dreaming … damp cloth. Polished key. \n\nApostle Nilphas Drethan and several unregistered guests approach the Clockwork Probabilis.
The Remnants stood tall, once. We strode across Oblivion, confident in our mission.\n\nHow we have fallen.

Vaermina's servants built a secret gate to Apocrypha beneath Alavelis? The village was not important, then—only the gate. The people were merely collateral damage to the Dreamcarvers and their Hidden Kindred allies.

Well done, now the compass will be sure to lead you to all of my little ones. Once you've located them, use the whistle to teleport them back to me.\n\nThis isn't the first time they've wandered off, sadly.
We need to get to Abbot Ilvel's chambers. If he's also in the grip of these foul censers, we need to save him!
Regardless of what the future holds, I'm glad you wandered by the mine when you did. Too many good people died in there, but the three of us might have joined them. We're grateful that we didn't.

Egg mining is all I've ever done. But if the foreman is sticking by our side, I know we can't go wrong.\n\nThank you so much for getting us out of there. It's actually a relief that I still have a future to worry about!

Looks like we aren't headed back into the mine after all. Maybe I should step away from the bugs for a bit. Seeing as one took a chunk out of me. Going to miss them, though.\n\nThanks for pulling us out of there. Didn't want to die in the dark.
Destroy her. Protect all we have left. The Remnants need this to remain a force in Apocrypha.
I understand that you wanted to respect my father's wishes, but losing him, even to save my life, was a horrible price.

The rime shard should keep you safe from the flames long enough to snatch the book without you getting roasted … I hope.\n\nI'll miss having that in my pack to keep me cool during those long treks in the Deadlands!

Once again the water of fate ripples with unnatural disturbances. As if some huge clod tossed a rock into a still pond.\n\nAnd what huge clod do I find at the center of these ripples? The Great Eye's mortal surrogate.
Traveling by portal is … disconcerting. I'm doing my very best not to spew right now.\n\nPlease, talk to Leramil while I compose myself.
You have a friendly look about you, Traveler. Even at a glance I feel that I can trust you. You must get that a lot.
