There's an overlook I think, we need to go and find it.

Welcome to the Chorus—or its lowest levels at any rate.\n\nWe call this the cognitive substrate. Few members of the Chorus visit this place, but it connects to all the Chorus' other regions. The perfect hiding place for a rogue mind, yes?
I suggest we reach the topmost level of the tower. That is where the sanctum is usually situated. I suspect that we will find what we seek there.\n\nLet us find a way to ascend, proxy.
We formed this order to enact Lord Hermaeus Mora's will. Does our fate still rest with him?

Is it true? Were you able to successfully gather research on the relic, the rite, and the lost dream? Every time I thought I found something relevant, it crumbled or burned up before I could examine it.
Lead the way, my friend.
Let's keep moving. Reynila and the one she's freed can't be too far ahead.

Whatever you did, it worked. The corruption dissipates even as we speak.\n\nAccording to Blightcrown's notes, they are using the corruption as some sort of method to avoid detection. Is that how they plan to elude the gaze of the One Who Knows?
We must find a way to save Quires Wind before those maddened Daedra tear all our hard work to pieces!
If this doesn't work I'll be no better off than the glyphic's remains. Just a shattered pile of useless detritus. Be gentle gathering them, won't you?

Let's hurry along, then! The Heart of Underweave can be found to the south, on the other side of the courtyard. I'll meet you there. Just wade across the detritus of failed fates, and go up the steps. Can't miss it.
Kynreeve Ryl stands in our path. I'll help you defeat him so we can examine the glyphic that Torvesard opened.
Valinna can command Daedric spiders? I know Keshargo has Zilipif, but they're a Watcher!\n\nIt doesn't matter now. We interrupted its meal, so hopefully Keshargo is all right.
The door to the labs is at the far end of the cellar. \n\nLet's just hope we don't meet anyone on their way out.
So she's chosen to go. I worry this is the beginning of the end. But it's for the best.
I can only hope she stays happy. I'll provide for her in every possible way.\n\nIf she tries to leave, after all, it's my life and research on the line.
Good, you are here. Both Scruut and I felt a sudden disturbance in the tides of fate. Something terrible has happened in Apocrypha, and Scruut and I no longer feel the presence of the One Who Knows.
Whatever you and Meln did, it seems to have worked. We can enter the main hall now.
Don't just stand there with your solid arms dangling uselessly. Pick up the cloak of omission!
My Reynila often shouldered the burden of her work alone. There's risk involving others. But without her here, it's a risk we have to take.
Well? Where did that fool's portal take you? Did you recover that prism Dreynis wrote about? Or at least some more of his research?\n\nI'd hate to leave this smoldering heap empty-handed.

Visitors! Why, I was starting to get lonely. Two warring legions of Daedra make for poor company, you know.\n\nThat worm behind you looks like one of the Givyns, by the curl of his lip. But you're a fresh face. What can I do for you?
If you're going to tell Master Sulis anything, get to it, hero. I want to finish this writ and get the stink of this place out of my hair.
Hehehe. What did Hezehk say? I find things. I can't believe you doubted me.\n\nUm, thanks for running around. It wouldn't have worked without you here. Except I would have found a way! Somehow.
This is where he dies.
I might have turned over a new leaf, but I'm still not crazy enough to explore old ruins like Senalana. Thank the Three we have people like you and Sharp to call on for that.

Naryu says she's ready to complete her writ of execution. I take great comfort that she revealed this to me before she finished her business. I mean, I know I'm not the spy, but it is good to know that she knows that, too.

So, I've been studying Reynila's notes and learning soul magic from my new tribe. Then Mevei told me what happened in that lab and—poof! Inspiration!\n\nAll we need is a sample of tyranite calx. I've actually traced some to a Daedric ruin nearby!

Go to Vanton—the gateway is ready for you. Prepare yourself, but don't take too long. Ansuul's powers only affect his mind now. But if she escapes into this realm, her evil could infect all the waking world. Everything we hold dear is at stake.
Come on, we're close. The restored statue and Master Shelreni must be somewhere nearby.
I cannot believe I am saying this, cohort, but you need to burn out the Fateweaver Key in the magicka font just there. \n\nWe'll never truly be rid of him as long as the relic still exists.
Lead on, dear. Find us a way into that mountain that isn't quite as heavily guarded as the main entrance.
Blast these frayed fates! Let's get in there and turn theory into practice, eh? \n\nSmooth these things back into the universe.
Well, this doesn't look too forbidden to me. There are Seekers here and everything.\n\nCome on, let's see if we can find the way out.
It seems my fate is now in your hands. Whatever this new bargain is, I beg you—do not let my son accept it.

Prior to this, my most complicated day involved misplaced grave urns, obnoxious relatives, and the occasional ancestor spirit who was out of sorts.\n\nI'm not sure what I have to offer once we return to Apocrypha, but I'll help in any way I can.
It was terrible, mortal. Some of the realm's Daedra have gone insane. And I still can't hear or make contact with the Great Eye.\n\nIf you have better news, share it with Leramil now.
The more I think about Shelreni and how we got to this point, the more I wish I could still spit.
Use Meln's ghost sight. When you find a flaw, point it out to me. Then I'll see if I can exploit it to reveal the true memory beneath.
Do not wait for Scruut and I. The corruption … it weakens us as it once again takes hold.\n\nWatch out for Gadayn, proxy. Please.
Why would you? You know what this means, right?
You've been honest, and Balver will now pay for your honesty. It'll be up to Llaro here to see to that. None of my business what happens now, nor do I really care.
I have no idea where we're going. I'm just following you.\n\nIf you're lost, too, I'd rather you keep it to yourself, all right?

Not to look a gift nix-ox in the mandible, but Torvesard's arrival is a little too convenient. That said, when two Daedric Princes oppose you, accept whatever help comes your way.\n\nBut don't worry. I'll keep an eye out for any sign of treachery.

Vaermina and Peryite have gone too far with their corruption. It works its way into the very fabric of Apocrypha. You only need to look to your two allies to see the harm it causes.\n\nI can ease their suffering, mortal.

I suffer, just as the Great Eye suffers. But I'll float alongside you into the very depths of Apocrypha. Which just happens to be where we're going.\n\nJust don't blame me if my tentacles fall off or I attack you or something.

A strange tale. Why would this mysterious "A" kill a cipher who did as they asked? What's behind the promise to read the book together?\n\nWell. If you find any other dead ciphers or missing books in your travels, come tell me.

I'll mark your map with the location of the Chthonic gate landing, as well as where the Seekers flock.\n\nMora's foes control these Seekers. Find them, kill them, and take their ichor. Once you have enough, you can open the gate and enter the Bastion.

My role has always been to observe and repair the lines of fate. Never to unduly influence them, no matter how sorely I'm tempted.\n\nSo, while I was waiting, it was just a nervous habit that I haphazardly started checking the nearby lines of fate.
Did you do it? Did you find Torvesard and recover the second glyphic? Wait, don't tell me. Not yet. Meln seems like he has something important he wants to discuss with you.
Speak to Scruut, Proxy. She won't admit it, but she's excited to tell you what's about to happen here.
The local Assembly of Masters thought to handle this situation in a private conclave, but the Telvanni Council saw the need to intervene. Hence, the archmagister sent me.
Hireling, I hope you have a strong sense of discretion. Talking to Master Sulis like that may not be wise. I have concerns about him.\n\nHave you and the assassin made progress?
It's horrible, seeing my father in this state. I did everything I could to ease his pain. If you have the relics, please give them to Tralise.

My sister and I will remain here and prepare the ritual to counteract the curse. While we won't be able to break it outright, hopefully we can lessen the pain. Speak with me again once you've gathered the relics.

I thought I had this all figured out at the start, but spend enough time contemplating the infinite and you realize that nothing is ever simple. \n\nAh well. That's one Tho'at Replicanum taken care of. I should focus on all the good work you did.
Welcome back. Are you willing to help us find more of the pages? I should remind you that time is of the essence.
Tho'at Replicanum isn't creating as many maligraphies right now. It might even be safe enough to start putting all the books she misplaced back in their proper spots.\n\nYou do good work, mortal.

How interested are you in the tale of Fynboar the Resurrected? Was this just something you did to get a Verse? Or are you dedicated to adding to Hermaeus Mora's collection?\n\nThere's more to do and I will pay you for it. It means a lot to me.
Be wary, traveler. A pack of tharriker stalks these woods. A ghastly sight, I assure you. Gnashing teeth and oily fur. My knees wobble at the very thought of them.

Securing four crates of Blue Aedral should be enough to keep our vineyard afloat. If we act fast, we might even find out how they knew to ambush us here. We traveled in secret, you know.\n\nAnd let's look for Lazen. I'd hate it if he were harmed.
The vault is empty? How long has it stood open? Where is Ithelia? This makes no sense!\n\nAt least Torvesard appears to be as confused as I am. See if he is willing to speak now, proxy.
The relics shall balance the energy we need to complete the ritual. Place them around the fragment.

Mortals die. That's literally the meaning of the word. I'll never understand your transient emotions. Whatever. We all face nonexistence if we don't do something about Ithelia and the reality tears. \n\nYou secured the fragment?
Legion's Rest has always been a safe place to rest. Very troubling to find it filled with rogues and beasts.

This Aetherial alarum will help untether the shards from their surroundings. I'll meet you at the first shard inside the ruins and show you how it works.\n\nJust don't break it. Or lose it. Or hold it too close to your face.

Do you see Shardmarshal Vargas up on those rocks? As much as I want to pay her back for Feldagard Keep, we need to close that portal. We can't let any more Daedra come through.\n\nFocus on destroying the anchors. Then we'll find a way out of here.

Look for Black-Glove Garm, the leader of the Lodge of the Fist. If the Recollection overpowered him, the rest of the pit is in real trouble. \n\nFollow the path there. I'll be along as soon as I get this youngster sorted.
Shh, I'm listening to this!
Curate Gadayn, he saved you from that reality tear. I didn't know him all that well, but he was clearly important to Leramil. And to you as well, I assume. I'm so sorry.
Old Ri'jhaad saw your coming in the tides. Hermorah wished this one to greet you here. So it is that our fates cross paths.\n\nWhat is it you seek, fatewalker?
You look like you've seen your share of battle. That's great, because the Legion could sure use some competent help right now.
Quickly, turn the flame valves all the way to increase the pressure in the fermentation vats. Meanwhile, I'll deal with Gallio's notes and papers.

Looks like we found the Recollection—or some of it. I didn't know Endegor well, but what I knew of him I didn't like. A bigoted radical, at best. I'm surprised he would work with any non-Bosmer at all.\n\nWhat's in that letter?

Ah, an old friend approaches! This one knows there are no coincidences in his line of work. Mizzik could use help solving a curious case. You wouldn't by any chance have seen a beast running about with a mouthful of parchment?
Something has made Betu terribly ill. I've never seen him so scared. If only I knew what was wrong, I could help him.
No blood. A broken window. And a fractured statue with no explanation as to how it was damaged. Mizzik feels that there is something just out of reach of this one's claws, but what could it be?
Not now, proxy. I want to observe this exchange.
A Daedric shrine, overrun by Goblins? Sometimes the threads of fate lead me into the most unpleasant sorts of places. Follow the trail, please. I have no wish to linger here.
Not now, friend of the Bogvir who isn't. I have more important matters to consider than whatever it is that interests you.
This is … not what I was expecting. And it looks like Torvesard is just as confused as we are. Perhaps you should talk to him and see what he makes of this empty prison.
You are welcome here, champion. We have few dealings with the Golden Eye, but here at Holamayan we acknowledge all Daedric powers who have guided our people down through the centuries.

Did you get lost down here? Yeah, that happens to me sometimes, too. That woman is back upstairs, sitting by the fire, so I came looking for you.\n\nI think I figured out how to make a Sage's Dream, even if we don't have the proper ingredients.
I just hope another cohort can hear the tower bell. We're spread thin and who knows who's listening these days.

Mind the shadows, adventurer. You never know when a wild tharriker might be lurking nearby. They might make for a good work beast, but you get on one's bad side and you'll become mighty familiar with their stinger.

Mizzik! Traveler. How fares the investigation? With so much still left to speculation, I've found myself wandering the grounds trying to keep my hands busy. I hope to have things settled soon, for all our sakes.
Go on then, ask me how I returned. It's the only question anyone seems to have for me. Uriel Weatherleah, back from the dead! It's laughable.
Thank you for helping save Betu. Seeing both you and Otho spring into action while I just stood here quivering. You've opened my eyes, traveler.

Hold a moment, traveler. I'm afraid the town isn't safe. As the Baroness of Leftwheal, I must insist you find shelter with the evacuated civilians.\n\nI won't risk anyone else getting hurt under my watch.

Now it becomes clear. The Recollection also seeks Ithelia. They hope to find her visiting places she once knew, just as we did.\n\nYet Ithelia seems confused. I do not think she has fully regained her memories or truly understands what happened to her.

This is the passage the captain suggested we use. He took me through it as one of my first training sessions. It's not the usual way we get into and out of the fort, so maybe the bandits haven't noticed it yet.\n\nBesides, it's full of bears.
Fate's guidance is not clear to me at the moment. Proceed as you are inclined to, proxy. No doubt the requirements of fate will make themselves known soon enough.

That takes care of the bloodfiend dens. But were those vampires lying about Tham? Damn it, I never wanted anyone to get hurt when I decided to leave the gang and throw off my curse!\n\nCome on. Let's find Balandrus's lair and finish this.
So, the Blind would rather move on than fight you? Don't be too insulted. If you kill this creature quickly, you can catch back up to her!\n\nWell, what are you waiting for?

I am still attempting to discern the meaning of the wisdom Ithelia shared with me, but Beragon insisted that this celebration go on. I found myself unable to refuse him.\n\nI admit that I usually avoid such festivities, but this is pleasant enough.

It's strange. When I first retreated from Niryastare, I wondered for years what was hidden in that vault. Never guessed it was the relic of a Daedric Prince.\n\nNow that you're here, let's take stock of our recent discoveries.
We did it! The great welkynd stone unlocked the vault. Let's get going, friend. Now that the door's open, there's nothing to stop the Recollection from following us inside.

I don't like the way your fellow mortals stare at me. You'd think they've never seen an emissary of the Great Eye before. So help me, the next one who squeaks in terror will get something that really scares them!\n\nTalk to Beragon. He asked first.
Don't forget, Scruut wanted to talk to you. And take your time and mingle with the other guests. They're all here because of you!

I may never get used to fighting Daedra and magic-users, but at least we put an end to Nantharion and his plot to destroy West Weald. That should finish the Recollection.\n\nNow is it too much to hope that Ithelia will take her power and just go away?
Take another look at the Skein of Secrets. If Ithelia exerts her power at Miscarcand, the map should show us the location.
Come on, let's deal with the greenspeaker and her pets as quickly as we can.
Miscarcand was described as big and important, but these ruins are far more impressive than I anticipated. We need to move quickly if we're going to find Nantharion in time.

Interesting. Was that the moment Hermaeus Mora finally crushed Ithelia's defenders? Is that what caused Miscarcand to fall?\n\nThe memory showed Ithelia's servants guarding the passage to the north. Let's see where it leads, comrade.

A few Recollection may linger, but their threat fades. Without Nantharion or the Staff of Many Paths, there will be no more wildburns. The mad dream of a new Ayleid kingdom replacing West Weald is dead.\n\nAnd that wasn't our only victory, friend.

I assumed the Recollection would be guarding the wildburn seed, but the tribune is right. They were expecting us.\n\nIf the Recollection does have a spy in Vashabar, then they're more dangerous than I thought.
We must not allow the undead's plan to come to fruition. Based on the necromancer's notes, I believe we can exorcise the spirits by interrupting their ritual. It's their last link to this place.
Speak to Beragon, proxy. Great events are in motion and the outcomes remain uncertain. Yet I can see a tenuous thread leading to Beragon. I think he has something in mind.
Check among the debris of the titan and try to find a good fragment.

Sorilen joined the Recollection? But they're murderers! This can't be right. I just need to talk to her. Blight and root rot! Maybe she's under a spell or a curse or something.\n\nLet's hurry. We need to get to her and that wildburn seed.

Shardmarshal Vargas sent us … somewhere. The Fargrave we were exploring faded away. I suddenly found myself in another version of our reality. A mirror world, dark and empty, full of soul-crushing dread. Like an iron fist around my heart.

I am sorry, proxy. I tried to shield our companions, but I could not. It took all the strength I could muster to prevent us from being banished along with them.\n\nIt seems Shardmarshal Vargas is much more powerful than when last we faced her.
Our esteemed guests want to speak with you, but you should check in with Beragon first. He wants to compare notes before we start handing out the laurels of victory.
Here we are. Pour what we've found into that altar's basin. It is an altar - we should feed it sacred water. Anything else would be disrespectful to the sanctity of this piece of Ayleid history.
It's you! Good fortune for all of us. Narsis Dren will be most pleased if you're the one to help him.

As this prison was once part of Mirrormoor, it is fundamentally connected to the Loom. As the Loom's power reaches its zenith, it absorbs the energy of other relics—as it did with the Skein and the Lamp. I fear for Abolisher, but you must try.

Through all we faced, it wasn't until I was lost in the Many Paths that I realized the true danger to the Weald. I think you saved everything when you destroyed the Loom of the Untraveled Road.\n\nOf course, Ithelia is still out there … somewhere.

I am glad you are here, proxy. Threads of fate tangle around the Outcast Inn in an ever-expanding knot, fraying the bonds of cause and effect with each bend and twist. Should they snap, the results would be catastrophic.

Mora's forces breached the shrine on this path. These Shardborn battle for their very existence, and the Ithelia of this realm's anger fills the air.\n\nI am safe from harm, but a mortal like you can die even when walking a different path. Be warned.
The journey to Skingrad is usually a calm and restorative one, but nowadays you always have to keep an eye over your shoulder. There are troublemakers lurking under every stone, I assure you.
I scoured my records and cannot find any description matching the Shattered Champion before us. Which means neither I nor my master have encountered this before. \n\nThey're probably thrilled.

I'm interested in what you found and you can tell me on the way. I want to check out Zeggar's Blind. I heard more than one of the hired mercenaries mention the name as I made my way to find you.\n\nIt's just to the northeast of the town.
If you're here to gamble, you're early. The tables don't get going until later. If you want a drink, head into the tavern.
I am an actual Colovian noble. Received my title and land from Emperor Leovic himself!
We provide meat and produce to the entire Weald. Finest in the land. Ontus would be nothing without my ranch.
Remind me never to leap into strange portals again. Is it normal to feel queasy?\n\nIt looks like Commander Merian wants to speak with us. You talk to him while I concentrate on not losing my lunch.

Clearly, defending Feldagard Keep is important. But if Ithelia visited the Outcast Inn, we must investigate. Besides, I sense a strange convergence of threads of fate there.\n\nYou must choose, proxy. I shall meet you at the inn when you arrive.
Don't dawdle while carrying out my orders. We don't have much time before the Daedra regroup and attack.\n\nGet going, mercenary!
Pod in hand. Thank Y'ffre! \n\nLet's get out of here so you can help Clen.
We've got it. Let's get out of here so you can head for the ritual site. Laeni needs her offering as well.
Singer be praised, you're back. What did they say?
Y'ffre's knees, a stranger. Welcome. What can this old greenspeaker do for you?
Ah, a visitor. Normally I'd welcome a chance to talk about the future of the Weald, but this isn't the best time. \n\nOur leader … well. We've had a setback recently.
Maybe there's still some way forward here. What is a marriage but a hope for a better tomorrow? And Vashabar itself is a symbol of hope.
I'm trying to keep hope alive in my heart, traveler. Like a Grahtwood fisher cub in a pen, I'm feeding it the fish of my soul.
I've seen you running to and fro, traveler. On a quest to help our young couple, I believe.\n\nHow goes the journey?
One day, I hope to be half the baker that my father is. No one makes cakes so moist or pies so delectable as Chef Donolon!
They're hurting Hyacinth! We have to rescue him!
Please! Save my fellow cantors.

I fear our little moon-singer is right. Her friends have been taken by the leader of all Rajaska. They will be bent, forced to join in a chorus of shadows. \n\nHer training has not prepared her to do anything about it. But mine has.

I have rarely seen Bogcup so animated. Outside of a tavern, anyway. The Gardener and I have had no luck in tracking Wisteria. She went to great lengths to hide her movements. \n\nSpeak with the Gardener. I am eager to hear what has Bogcup so excited.
Use Scruut's spell scroll to release the Lamp's energy and repair the tear.

A mortal pathwalker? Such a creature is quite rare. And I see you are accompanied by one of my reflections. An Ithelia from a different path.\n\nYou carry something else with you. It feels like … hatred. Tell me, why have you come to my reality?
Thank you for helping Tanlorin. They're a torchbug, that one. A bright light, but prone to wanderlust. \n\nThey needed a rock today, and you fit the bill. I'm grateful. More than you know.
Heard about the pest problem, have you? Quite confounding. \n\nTo think we've reclaimed this priceless trove of ancient resources only to fall victim to rats. Or what have you.
A talking crow? This just gets weirder and weirder! I suppose you'd better do what she says.
Bella said she wanted to see the knife you just found. Go talk to her. \n\nI think I know what's going on here, but if she says what I think she will, then I have the final piece of the puzzle.
Hurry! Put the crystal on the altar!
Did you have questions for me?
Such magic! This is exhilarating!

Seek the fawn and the hunter in a southern Auridon cavern. Del's Claim, I believe it is called today.\n\nRestore this ill-used power, and I will lend my strength to yours. A signpost on your path to master Scribing.
Even with this little page thief in residence I'm sure you'll find your way. We couldn't have gotten this far without you, no reason to think we won't get farther yet.
Didn't even get the chance to copy the Fable of the Gryphon for posterity, before it was ripped away from us. Damn it. \n\nWe'll keep looking for a solution here, adventurer.

That was certainly an adventure, wasn't it? A jaunt through ancient ruins to craft an unsolvable riddle. Not what I expected when I woke up this morning, but exactly what I needed.\n\nWhat was in her last notes? Anything that will help?

Ooh, you look like just the sort of heroic warrior I could use. My family's farm is facing some Goblin problems right now and I'm worried my uncle is going to do something terrible. Does that sound like something you could help with?

The others and I are trying to look at the Fable of the Dragon the way you do. You know, deciphering locations from the text. In case you need our help.\n\nIt's started a few arguments, but I don't mind. Helps that I like the work!

Sorry to put you through that, but Caelum never would have paused to listen to me. And I wouldn't have blamed him. I hoped we could make amends somehow. I guess it wasn't meant to work out that way.\n\nBut at least Val's alive, thanks to you.

The Divines finally put an end to this. I think they had some help from you, friend.\n\nEver since Caelum Vineyard years ago, my faith came from a place of fear. But you've given me a lot to think about. Thank you.

Thank you. Thank you for cleaning up after the drunken mess I made of things and saving Val. It's just … after that night, the fire, and now coming back here, it was all too much.\n\nI should have done better.
Looks like you have your hands full there, traveler. What's that squawking?
You're back. But where's Naku?\n\nI think you'd better talk to Hooke, friend. Quickly.

That creature held the arcane knot? How much of its power was its own? \n\nIt does not matter. The knot is out now. When you're ready, we should take it from this place. The null arca is the only thing that can keep it stable.

Talk to Keshargo over there. I'm busy. \n\nThat fool Xoryn may have knocked my null arca out of alignment when he attacked. It took me a century to get this far with the arca. I do not want to start over.

If you find my squadron, tell them that Captain Dartorius sent you. Order them to stay put at Fort Hastrel and wait for me to join them. I'll stay here until you tell me it's safe.\n\nIf you run into Ulrath, be careful. He's a cold-blooded killer!
Traveler. Hmm. It's been some time since we've had a new leaf blow into the Wilderhall.

You're on the path to meet the Dragon. This Luminary was a real challenge for Ulfsild, and might prove the same for you. \n\nJust remember to breath deeply, and stay calm. That's what she told herself, the first time through.

Your choices, the riddles you sought solutions to, were quite instructive. Gave me an intriguing peek within your mind. Well done.\n\nNow, for a real challenge. If I am to lend my power to the altar you must understand my thoughts as well.

Don't know about you, but that really took it out of me.\n\nI'll meet you back at the Scholarium, all right? I'll say goodbye to my friends and probably take the long way back. I'm too exhausted to summon another portal right now.
I look forward to speaking to the Votary, Not-Ulfsild. While I wait, make your way to Suran. Don't worry, she'll follow close behind.
I know you can handle yourself out there. Just make sure that Fox doesn't get caught, all right?\n\nAs far as I can tell, the Princes don't know about the Scholarium. Let's keep it that way.
A promotion? Is that what the count said? Thanks so much for helping me find Burnbiscuit, friend. I'm not sure I could have done it without you.
The reality appears much worse than the stories I have heard of this place. Please, walker. You and Zerith must hurry and find this cellar the high cantor speaks of.
We will wait here until Zerith-var calls for us to join you.
Let's make this quick, I want to get out of here.\n\nThere's only one facet left. I know which one it is now, and she's not going to be easy to capture.
You made it! Sorry about all the cobwebs and cult guys, but this is the closest I could get us to Nocturnal's realm. Let's make this quick so we can get out of here.
Move quickly and with courage as you steal these magics, mortal. The Fox is a stalwart ally, but where you are going the shadows run deep.
That sigil has been waiting a long time for us, friend. Go on. Take it.

Adventurer, welcome to the end. You've overcome innumerable challenges, and you stand poised to fulfill the legacy left behind by Ulfsild all those years ago. \n\nYou are the inheritor of the Scholarium.
Viti and I will be fine. Save the other Twilight Cantors!
It's the Fox! Every time I see that little guy I can't help but have a smile on my face.
This place is fascinating. Simply fascinating! \n\nI'll be just a moment, adventurer. I'm still getting set up.
Not sure I'll ever go back in Legion's Rest. Bugs. So many bugs.

We did it, friend! We found Snapdragon and rescued her!\n\nThis portal will take us straight to the Gardener's greenhouse. Once we're safe and sound we can talk to Snapdragon. Make sure she's really all right.
Did you hear what Wisteria said? This is all for us. What was she talking about? \n\nLet's get to Hyacinth's greenhouse. I need some answers.
Of course, there's still the matter of the Proxy Queen. How are we going to explain all this to her?

Hey there friend! I have so many questions about that last mission! How did the Ceythalmor know we'd be in Auridon? \n\nOr that Hyacinth would be alone at the Garland Ring base? And they had a hideout in Greenshade? Why didn't we know that?
I need your help! The Daedric Lord Hollowjack seeks new prey to add to his larder!
The portal, tamiit. Let us get to Cantor Krin'ze before anything else occurs.
Help me, tamiit! Focus on my moonclaw!
Fight at my side, tamiit!
I thought that death would be something peaceful, but this is just like being alive. Only I feel too weak to get anything done. By the frost in my staff, I'd get my revenge if I could.

I'm much too busy to talk right now—oh, bah. Forget it. It would write faster by itself at this point.\n\nApologies. Too much depends on this book's completion. My relationship with my publisher, my peers. Even the Dawnway.
This one heard what this Zerith-var said in Claw's Strike. Necromancy! Viti will not tolerate dark magic near her or her young sahida.
I thought nothing could rattle me after the Dread Cellar. Imagine my surprise when a noble family like the Albuses are the ones kidnapping alliance soldiers.\n\nYou don't work for them, right?
I want to fight back against Orpheon and his army as much as Khafdeed does. But the second I want to sling a spell or kick one of them from the shadows, Khafdeed pulls me back to safety!
Portal travel? I have rarely used such magic. Still, I am with you and Zerith to the end, walker. Let us step through it and see what awaits us in the necropolis.

Stirk again? I remember that place. It's where the guilds and alliances assembled to invade Coldharbour.\n\nGood thing that Prince Azah is there to speak for the Fighters Guild. I've been known to punch a politician or two during negotiations.

No more talking until I get those mistscrub leaves. It grows northwest of here. By the water. Bushes with jagged red leaves.\n\nCome back and then we'll talk. I'll be here. Not like I can get very far in this condition.

I wish Vanus hadn't been captured. He's so much better at making the alliance leaders listen to reason. Not that we're getting anywhere near the alliance leaders. The so-called ambassadors they sent to meet with us are minor functionaries at best.
As I expected, more secrets lay behind the illusion. Worm Cult security is no match for the great Vanus Galerion.\n\nGo on, read the scroll. I'll watch for enemies as you do.

I hope you wield your weapons as well as they deserve. Orpheon's army swept over us like the crash of the ocean against the rocks of the eastern cliff face. I almost thought they discovered our hidden passageways.
Prince Azah was quite adamant that there's imminent danger. You should talk to your alliance's representative while I see what else the Fighters and Mages Guilds have to say.
I knew I was not wrong about you. Azurah guides you.\n\nTake the blade, tamiit.

Gabrielle Benele attempted to convince me that the Worm Cult has returned. How preposterous! I suggest you speak with your alliance's ambassador. I need to have a conversation with Prince Azah. As a member of the Covenant, I trust he will speak true.

The members of the Fighters and Mages Guild have spun a fanciful tale, but it sounds like a trick to catch the Pact off guard. I suggest you speak with your alliance's ambassador while I give Azah and Gabrielle one more chance to convince me.

I'd prefer to head to the Earth Forge with you and Skordo, but I understand Gabrielle's concern. It will take both of us, each representing our guilds, to convince the leaders of the Three Alliances that the Worm Cult threat has returned.\n\nNow, go!
This business with Julien—I don't want to give him the wrong idea. I need time to think right now. I hope you can understand.

I can't believe this. The more I think about it, the more I realize that this was meant to be. Khalisah has always been kind and giving. What did I ever see in Guendeline?\n\nTell me though, did Khalisah understand? Will she give me another chance?
We have a bit of a … situation … with Duke Sebastien of Camlorn.\n\nPerhaps you'd be willing to help extract the Duke from a rather precarious situation.
Verandis and Gwendis have taught me so much. I know I can control the urges. Soon, I'll be ready to get back out there and help the people of Rivenspire.
S'rashi is very busy, stranger. Unless you have business of a most critical nature, you must come back at another time.\n\nS'rashi offers deepest apologies.
Took you long enough. Did you go all the way to Shornhelm to get those supplies?
<<1>> and his family are probably hiding inside the farmhouse.\n\nKnock on the door and see if they're all right, but try not to startle them.
Well, that was an adventure now, wasn't it? I'm fortunate that you came along. You certainly have my thanks.\n\nWhere is Mathias? Where are the other servants?
These have been dark times at Firebrand Keep, but my hope is that the Knights of the Flame will emerge from these events more united and with more purpose than ever before.
These caves have been quiet for so long, but the winds have returned and our spirits with them.\n\nYou walk among the living, yet you speak to the dead. Will you help return us to our rest?
Well?

Got a minute to help a girl out? This is a rescue that could go down in the history books.\n\nUp there is a village that's been taken over by one of the nastiest slaving outfits in all Tamriel and they've captured some of my fellow crewmembers.
Dro-Dara's companions … friends. Dungy bandits would have tied them up like this one.\n\nYou found them? You freed them, yes?
I owe you a debt of gratitude for freeing me, friend. \n\nYou should talk to Dro-Dara. He will want to thank you as well.
By the Divines, my head hurts.\n\nI feel like the morning after a corn whiskey binge, and the taste in my mouth is … you probably don't want to know. I wish I didn't.
I still can't believe we pulled it off. Brought down the whole mountain on those nasty brutes.\n\nIt'll be a long time before the Ironhand Ogres trouble us again.
You're just in time. I need every able-bodied man and woman. You're carrying a weapon, so I assume you're able.\n\nYou like to fight ogres?
I don't mean to rush you, but I'm worried. Are you making any progress against the fires?
I sensed a great weight lifting from Stormhaven. Vaermina's dire influence is gone. \n\nI believe we have you to thank for that.
Well, an unfamiliar face. I'm certain I didn't invite you. What's your business here?

Welcome back to Wayrest. It's good to see you again. Do you have any news?\n\nTo be honest, this whole matter with the Dream Shard has robbed me of a few nights' sleep. I'll be a royal grump if we can't get this matter resolved soon.
Be careful. The Primeval Seekers will protect their relics with their lives.\n\nDo what you must though. Regrettably, sometimes in nature, it is simply kill or be killed.
She wavers in and out of consciousness.\n\nI only hope returning the pure heartwood will invigorate her enough to recover.

I hope you'll forgive me being blunt, but under the circumstances, there's no time for social niceties.\n\nI am still in awe of what you've done to save the city, but did I just see you talking to a crow?
We need to work quickly. Who knows when the Imperials will decide to execute the grandeya?
If I don't kill myself, the Omen will possess me.\n\nVaermina will have my soul.
Father's dead. And for what? Some false sense of security that we won't sell the johads?\n\nI'll never understand!
I don't recognize you, but under the circumstances, I am pleased to make your acquaintance.\n\nIf you are here to render me aid, I can promise that you'll be well rewarded.
I do not see the head necromancer out here; this evil man Uwafa. He must have breached Tu'whacca's sanctum. \n\nHe will be in for quite a surprise when we light the final brazier.
This is not good, not good at all. I've killed a skeleton or two in my day, but this … this is worse than that. \n\nWe are going to need more Ash'abah.

Tu'whacca guided your footsteps here at the perfect moment, sister. \n\nThere is Ash'abah work to be done—the Withered Hand has taken over the port. The situation is … strange though, to say the least.
The Orc woman is strong-willed. A challenge, but one that I will conquer nonetheless.\n\nWhat do you think of my menagerie, mortal? Would you like to take your place within?
Go, tell the disciples what I've done before we open the door to <<1>>'s lair.\n\nAnd then, I must summon an arbiter. My guilt is known; my punishment is not.
How can we believe this strange jest?\n\nI'm afraid you've upset Tafa. Best be on your way until she calms down.

It had to be done. It had to!\n\nAnd yet, my heart is heavy. The old master taught me so much. I grieve for what's happened. I would have rather defeated her to win my post than take over the school this way.

Greetings, wayfarer. Our fair city has always been a sanctuary for those traveling across the scorching sands of the Alik'r desert. I hope you find it so.\n\nI am Justice Istah—the head of security here. I am pleased to meet you.

I hope you are here to help. I am here to assist Telenger the Artificer with research.\n\nWe were attacked by undead and had to fall back to our camp. Telenger suspects a necromancer's hand in this, and I hope to aid in dispatching such a foe.
Tu'whacca tells me the heroic spirits have returned to their slumber.
Do you like the Hall of Judgment? Feel free to look around. \n\nIt has been rebuilt a few times, but this building actually dates back to when the Ra Gada first settled in the Alik'r Desert.
Now we must bring Rama to justice.
Thank you for saving Master Muzgu. \n\nStar of Azura watch over you.
You showed mercy. Thank you!

I have to say it. I'm starting to feel like Azura's using you as her champion. First at Vanne Farm in Alcaire, now here. I know I'm grateful. \n\nI'd say goodbye, but I'll probably run into you again in a few days.
I hope you're not giving up. I'm not going to reward you if you only have the pieces. \n\nThe sword must be reforged, and we cannot assume the tomb will be here forever. What if it collapsed?
I wish I could say there was no longer cause for concern. Somehow, though, I just don't think that's the case.\n\nSomething about all this just isn't adding up.
I wouldn't hold out too much hope, my friend. \n\nAt this point, I can't imagine the slavers are looking to leave here with anything more than their lives.

The people of this village have no honor. When a ship comes into port with injured sailors, it is a sacred custom that those sailors be cared for. \n\nTo leave my men here bleeding on the deck is unforgiveable.
The forge is closed. With the slaver attack and everything else going on, we have enough steel in the town.\n\nTry back another day and perhaps we can do business.
That barn has always scared me. Thanks for checking there. \n\nCome to the house after and let me know if you found anything.
I don't understand why the general's holding us back, or what this glorious next battle is that he keeps talking about.\n\nIt's not my place to question orders either, though.
Well. So much for that.\n\nIf you're looking for Count Hosni, you'll find him on the dais above the central arena.
Even I know there's more to this than just Lerineaux.
Most of the royal family is safe, but his lordship is brave … and stubborn. He refuses to leave the throne room. \n\nI need more information to convince him of the danger he's in.
I didn't want to say anything with all these poor people around. They've already gone through so much.\n\nBut after studying the situation, I think I know what's going on in the forest.
The villagers won't be safe in here for long.\n\nGo help my sister, Helene. She has a way to protect this place.
Bloodthorn cultists are one thing, but this Mother Murk creature! What if more refugees take shelter in the Fens? What if Mother Murk captures more travelers?
We heard a scream. And then ripples of magical distortion started to sweep across the battlefield.\n\nWhat happened?

I couldn't help overhearing. I know the house that Granette told you about.\n\nI think I'll go with you. I want to make sure that Gelvin isn't having second thoughts. We really need to get paid for this job.
We'll mend our family here. We won't fail our father's dream.
Now you know how I brought this evil upon Westtry. \n\nToo weak to trust in Stendarr, I gave us all to Molag Bal.

I've done everything in my power to avoid calling on the Ash'abah, but I no longer have a choice. We must have their help to recover the Ansei Wards. \n\nI would avoid contacting them directly, however. Will you be my envoy, wayfarer?
Of course. Of course. Faolchu's weakness is fire. That makes so much sense when you stop to think about it.\n\nWe need to tell Camlorn about this immediately.
I cannot thank you enough, my friend. Without you, Camlorn … Glenumbra … it would all be in grave jeopardy.

If you're able to speak to the elemental spirit, find me at the Vale of the Guardians. It's north of this location. I'll wait for you there.\n\nAnd please, hurry! We need the wisdom and guidance of the guardians now more than ever.
Work with Shaza to cut a gap through those werewolves. We'll follow and take back what's ours. \n\nIf you get through, report to General Mandin.

You wear Imperial armor, but I can see in your face that you are not one of them. \n\nPerhaps you will understand my misery then. This was the most beautiful temple in all Alik'r … before the Imperials came. I do not know if it can be restored.
Oh! You're not a bandit. \n\nMy apologies, but we're not at our best right now.
I must say, this wolf's woe smells terrible. I hope this works!
Blast that mage! She's put us all at risk. That bauble had better be worth the effort.
Julianos! I was wrong about how powerful the thing in the talisman was. My apologies.
I … I failed him.
Oh no, you have something much more important to do.\n\nOnce the fires are lit, you confront Faolchu. Keep him busy long enough for our troops to take the city. I'll send aid as soon as I can.
We're close to victory. Destroy Angof's corrupting magic!
I'll keep an eye on the bandit. If he tries anything, I'll send a runner to let you know.\n\nIf you do go into Eagle's Brook, remember that we need to know what happened to the villagers.
Did you find Ildani's wares? This one was worried that the guards might lock you up also.
I've known Darien a long time. Don't judge what he'll do by the way he talks. He's a better man than he pretends to be.
Collect the keys and retrieve Anton's jeweled crown. I'll reward you handsomely. \n\nEven better, I'll mention you in my next book.
We must rebuild Camlorn—and make Angof pay.\n\nOf course, we can't just rush off to attack Angof. We need to prepare.
I hate to say it, but the General's right. We need to find Darien. \n\nMara protects fools and drunkards, so I'm sure he's still alive.

I was sworn to protect him. It was hard enough to see him die once. If I could've taken the death-blow on the battlefield, I would've done it without hesitation.\n\nHe would've made a fine king, you know.

You're a true hero—and I mean that. My camp is beside the ruins. That's where I left the book we need. \n\nGet the book, use it to activate the large pillars in the ruins, then meet me inside the west door to the lower ruins. The portal's down there.

What do we have here? You're the one who helped Lady Laurent clear out the Elves. What are you still dawdling about for?\n\nIs it Stibbons? The bootless coward. He's hoping Lady Laurent will forgive him for starting all this.
Many thanks freeing me to watch over him, for he needs much assistance.
The forest is its own master now. For too long, it has curbed its will to the Sentinel. To the civilized rather than the wild.\n\nI'm eager to see what becomes of it.

What's going on here? I don't understand any of this. \n\nLast thing I remember, we were fighting the Reachmen outside Northglen. I saw my father fall. I tried to get to him, and then everything went black. Dame Valyrie tells me that we died …?
She's awake, thank the Divines. Let her know she's safe, for now.\n\nThe forest will keep her safe.
Oh, hello there! I remember you … from that tomb in Glenumbra? My memory is so foggy, but I remember your face.\n\nYou won't believe this, but Lady Laurent has fired me! Now, I don't know what to do.
Stenwick would want me to persevere. If only he was here to tell me what I need to do.
I wish I could aid you, but I'm needed here. Lanis is good with a sword, but I'm better. I'll protect the survivors. \n\nLet Lanis know if you run into anyone else.

I'm glad to see you again. And I can certainly use your help.\n\nI came to Crosswych when I heard the Red Rooks had taken over the town. After what happened at Eagle's Brook, I vowed to fight the Red Rooks with every fiber of my being.

The conflict is dangerous here, my friend. We're looking for warriors with a little more experience to take on the tasks we have in Bergama. \n\nAdvance your standing in the guild. Then speak to me again.

<<1>>, we have a problem. That problem? The Withered Hand. Their necromancers have ravaged Lainlyn and killed many of our Guild members. \n\nNow they're trying to recruit a band of desert mercenaries. I plan to crush them beneath my boot instead.
Well, that was fun, wasn't it? All right, maybe fun isn't the right word. But you were glorious!\n\nAngof is finally dead. We can't thank you enough for what you've done.
If things are going badly, you can always stop questioning him for a bit.\n\nMaybe you should take a walk around the camp to clear your head. Take inspiration from what you find and try again later.
I watched him become such a knight that he might someday be sung of in songs and written of in the histories.\n\nIt's such a waste. A pointless and brutal death to glorious potential.
I didn't trust Kerbol before, and I certainly don't trust her now. But why didn't Draven trust me?
Go on. Tell Renoit. I must confer with the others on our next course of action.
You again? When you give me a little pat on the head, do you think I'll answer all your questions?\n\nYou're as bad as our own damn nobles.

You're not here for the lizard races, are you? I thought not.\n\nLizard racing doesn't draw the crowd it used to. They've seen the same lizards race time and time again. To stay in business, I need something to spice things up!
Why are we standing around when Imperial heads remain attached to their necks?

It may seem unappreciative to ask more of you, but I would be neglecting my duty to the Daggerfall Covenant if I did not inform you of the tragedy at Bangkorai.\n\nAny hope of peace there seems to have dried up in the wake of recent events.
Ah, Tamriel. I long to see your skies again.
This is a restricted area. I must ask you to leave, please.

You there! There's gold for you, if you'll lend me your time.\n\nI am a scholar of some import. Hah! Import. That is to say, I've traveled quite far, from Cyrodiil, just to study this forgotten shore. I sorely need an assistant.
Oh! Hello there! I think I recognize you. Didn't Lorelia have something special she wanted you to do?\n\nI-I just can't recall. Oh well.
Pardon my manners, I can't rise to bow.\n\nI'm afraid I'm not as spry as I was. Won't be for a while.

There is no other way for this to end. The Nereid has stolen forbidden secrets and committed crimes against nature and humanity.\n\nNow that you understand, will you repent for changing loyalties? Will you aid me in destroying this aberration?
All that commotion we heard from the ruins? That was you, wasn't it? Heh. Good work.
You got a key to the inn? Well, be careful in there. Those militia troops have been out of control lately.
He's near. I can feel it. He's looking for the camp.
I curse the day the harpies first attacked our town.
It's a pleasure to do business in the open once more. So to speak, of course.
Hmm. You appear new to <<1>>.\n\nI pray you hold little fondness for the Imperials; otherwise, we're done talking.
If I were to lose my husband as well as my daughter, there'd be nothing left for me in life. But what must be done, must be done.
I've been reviewing our defenses. It's not good. The Covenant is bringing up ballistae and siege ladders. \n\nTime to show them what we've got!
Follow <<1>> through the portal. I will cloak you in shadow so you may verify his destruction of the Covenant army.\n\nThe shadow will last only so long. Be quick.
You have their charms? \n\nWhen you are ready, place them on the brazier. Then I will begin the calling.
Reesa's got Argonian ways that don't always make sense.\n\nBut by Shor's bones, she always comes through when the battle gets thick.
It worked, but this was necromancy of the blackest sort.\n\nMy brother … it was his work. And I, s'wit that I am, helped him.
Captain Hjolm lost his life bravely defending the fort from that Covenant scum. He cut down a score of them, but eventually succumbed to his wounds.\n\nThat magnificent fetcher will be missed.
Did you leave any for me? \n\nI wonder if I can get any of these Elves in the silly helmets to lend me an axe.
You have spoken to the spirits. What did you learn?
Leel-Vata is a skilled mage, but she is still just one Saxhleel.\n\nPlease, find her and bring her back safely.
The villagers are still here—waiting to be shipped off as slaves.\n\nSeeks-the-Night walks in the shadow of the sun. This evil is his doing.
We have no time to lose. The sorcerers say that if we succeed, victory is assured. I have no choice but to believe them.
Blood for blood, their violence shall be repaid.\n\nSoldier, are you ready to begin?

I'd start with the sons, Dedras and Mevis. The last I saw, they were running for the sulfur pools.\n\nIt's dangerous in there. The water boils, and wild shalk come up from underground. May Vivec guide your steps, traveler.
By my egg! You startled me. Please, no more. \n\nWere you very humble as you sought the honor of Mavos' presence?
The attacks are faltering. You've driven the Goblins back.
My thirst for revenge has been slaked.
My sons Dedras and Mevis fled south into the sulfur pools during the attack. They're no cowards, but I worry about them.\n\nMaybe one of them knows where their mother and sister went.
Shor's Bones, Tanval's gone mad. I can't believe he took the Coral Heart. \n\nAnd Garyn! Curse the fates. The wolves are circling, my friend.
The thunder is stilled for now. But another storm is in the offing.
I'm pleased to call you clan friend.
It is done.
Someone will find you at the kinhouse when we're ready to make our move.
Have our town's fortunes improved?
I erect the spine of distress, egg-sibling. We have need of your aid, but I'm sure you already felt it as you approached.\n\nWe have a Hist here, and it's dying.
I must attend to the afflicted here. My wife, Merarii, could use your assistance. \n\nDisrupt the spirits and gather their dead hearts. It's grim work, but it must be done.

Narsis is sealed. Villagers are missing. Crates of Llodos plague arrive in the night. Now you discover the plague intensifies when it festers inside a corpse.\n\nMakes you wonder about Giron's plan, doesn't it?
I'm busy. Frankly, I'm overwhelmed. Please speak to <<1>>.
Remember, either aloe or redweed will do. I need enough to make more potions to deal with these noxious fumes.
When you're ready, place the items in the <<1>>.
Open the spell cages of the ancient sorcerers. When they appear, defeat them.
The pass is open again. House Hlaalu will keep it that way.\n\nBut watch yourself—I fear Vox isn't finished yet.
The Worm Cult will enslave us all without your help. Please, <<1>> must survive. We've already lost so much ….
If Dominion spies are aware of the murders, we have bigger problems than I thought.
Go on. Enter the stable cellar. Make friends with that … whatever it is.
Soon … I'll be with you soon, Valu ….
Don't … don't tell me about my son. I must be strong for Kragenmoor.
Things haven't been right in Kragenmoor since the Vanguard arrived.
<<1>> whimpers about a curse, but the real curse is allowing someone else to control us with the <<z:2>>.\n\nSomething must be done about it. Something permanent.
I want my Tiril back. He always knew what to do. How can I go on without him?
Pilgrim, the Trial of the Mind awaits below. Your goal is simple: show you comprehend our past.
You return! As Root Steward, I must say your vision remains a secret of the Hist and yourself. But for myself, I must ask ….\n\nWhat did you see?
Well done, well done. I told you I smelled the molten metal when you first came in here, yeah?\n\nOf course, it always smells like molten metal in here. Hah!
These Dres bastards attacked us. I demand blood for the lives we lost today.
Quiet. By seed and spleen, stranger, you must help me. \n\nMy people have been taken by a Daedra known as Fatestealer.
Thank the Three! You don't look like one of these mad Maulborn cultists.
The General acts stranger by the day. It's like I don't know him at all anymore.
Nothing will be the same, but at least I know what's happened.
Come to gloat? Sure, I understand. With Naldyn a few days cold, you're here to blather at me about every wrong he did you.\n\nGo on, say your piece.
Reesa's plan? You disappoint me, but I will not give up.
It's been far too long since we made a public declaration. Not since … isn't that odd? We can't recall.\n\nWell. Come now—to the castle tower!
Excuse my silence. I've as much on my mind as a hatchling looking for supper.
The injured soldiers started filing in as you worked.\n\nPlease, tell Brethis of your work, and tell him where you found the draughts.
On to Ebonheart, yes? The Covenant is retreating here, but there's lots of fighting still ahead.
We've defeated <<1>>, and we'll imprison him in <<2>>.
Leave our cursed cemetery, lest the spirit trick you again.
Give me a moment alone, please. I'll come speak to you outside.
I don't know if I can go through with this, soldier.\n\nThese sorcerers ask much. Everything, in fact.
I've never been in such a fight. We are bound by battle now.

Welcome to Mournhold, capital city of the Ebonheart Pact.\n\nWe track all visitors. Upon arrival, everyone must see a registrar, who will record your name and business in Mournhold. Thank you for your cooperation.
Greetings! We've heard that you were instrumental in helping the refugees off of Bleakrock.\n\nIt's good to see you in Mournhold. We were told to keep watch for you.
Welcome to Mournhold, my child. \n\nYour name is known to the Tribunal. You were wise to heed my summons.
Find a way to kill <<1>> and I'll reward you handsomely.
This is amazing. What a historic moment! And we have you to thank for it.
My sister has yet to return to town.\n\nShe's lusting for violence. There is poison in her head.
Almalexia sent you a messenger? \n\nNerathren and Faryon were Ordinators who served here long ago. The urns the messenger spoke of are behind the shrine in the chapel downstairs.
Quickly! Before the Vanguard catches wind of your plan.
I'll return these goods to the merchants' families, as promised. If I must.
The courtyard is ours. Now all that remains is to cut off the snake's head.
I hope you can retrieve the keystone. Until it's secured, our hands are tied.
Be welcome and wallow.
The Daedric corruption of our swamp is made manifest! \n\nThe creature must be destroyed, or our home is lost.
I have a lot on my mind right now. If it isn't pressing, <<1>> will hear you out.
Sometimes, it's simpler to turn a blind eye to those pirates' antics.
I go nowhere until that Dremora has her attention on someone else. Don't know if she could kill me with a look, but I'd rather not risk it.
Such an unexpected indignity. When I first devised this torture, I never thought it would one day be visited upon me.\n\nSmile and nod your head, mortal.
Excellent work with <<1>>. Let me know when you're ready for another contract.
There's an old temple on the hill overlooking the town. We're hoping that others have found sanctuary there.
You spoke with great acumen, blessed of the Night Mother.
Do you come to mock me, then?
We need that keystone. Don't waste time talking to me.
Your footsteps grow lighter. Your time spent here does you well.
Since the first egg cracked, the memories of the Hist have shown us our sacred role as keepers. <<1>> is eldest amongst us, and his wisdom will lead us through the Dominion menace. It must.
The madness fades, but so do we. Did anything go wrong?
How does it feel to weigh life and death? What brings pity for one, but not for another?\n\nNo matter, your offering pleases Sithis. What did you learn?
<<1>> was no scholar. She did nothing idly. \n\nThe river has brought us here for a reason.
A moment, stranger. I am Napetui. The wisdom of the Hist has guided you to me. Let us speak before it is too late.
Give that thing to Thragnar. He'll restore order in the mine. That's what he's paid to do.
You're welcome here, walker in shadow and in light. The Shadowscales will always count you as an ally.\n\nUnless the Night Mother commands otherwise. But you know this, yes?
You're alive? You surprise this one. You're stronger than she thought.
Patience, my friend. This storm will pass, and spring will come.
You're back! Did you stop <<1>>?\n\nAnd the Fangs … did you get the Fangs of Sithis?
I'm sorry for what happened in the ruins. Thank you for saving me from the Fang of Sithis.\n\nI hope you have more luck with it than I did.
I know you'll change the river's course, comrade. They're investigating the wilds nearby, at Riverden Falls.
Retrieve that journal for me. I only have enough energy to leave this place of my own accord.
Quickly, comrade. Check the body.
Welcome, my friend. We were just talking about you.

Now I must find a way to comprehend what monumental task you've been sent here to accomplish.\n\nUntil my visions reveal your ultimate destiny, I have a favor to ask. It may seem trivial, but I assure you it's important.
We have to trust the Arch-Mage. Right? \n\nGo with his familiar. We'll come as soon as you call us. Honest.
Comrade, you were the first person I thought of when it came time to explore a musty ruin. That is meant as a compliment.
This is … unbelievable. Stendarr's horn, we all thought the Guildmaster died in his sleep.
<Ja-Reet says nothing.>
The Dominion will take a dim view of Ja-Reet and Feyne: a Dunmer with an Argonian.
I will summon the focus crystals. They'll tap the power inside you and focus it.\n\nFollow me.
My deluge of natural skill keeps the ground of my mind moist with clarity. \n\nPerhaps I need to form more islands of learning before we can call this a hatchery.
If you hadn't come along, I'd still be hiding under the bed.
Sage Tirora is dead, tortured. I'll gut every Reachman I find, I swear it!
Too few have the strength to oppose the Reach shamans. Hurry, before they do more evil here.
I forgot how delicious crystals are.

You've ruined me! Now I and all my realm will be destroyed! I've seen the Supernal Dreamers preparing. They may look like they're fleeing, but it's just preparation for their final assault!\n\nJust leave me in peace.
Just one more thing.
That witch will pay for her crimes.
I die in pain. Give me rest under the oak tree.
I must be sentimental in my old age. All this death weighs upon me like a second set of scales, yet there is more of it ahead.\n\nAre you ready to show <<1>> he cannot break the Pact?
Have you learned why the Worm Cult is here?
The bravery of Vivec! Nicely … you have a little something on your mouth, there.
I can't wait for the climax of this play! It's a masterpiece. If only someone would hurry up and finish it.

The tablet mentioned three areas up ahead: "The Gauntlet," "The Lair," and "The Ruin." The Eyes must be somewhere within.\n\nBe careful out there! The Eyes are ancient jewels, and danger follows ancient jewels like mothers to their children!
Greetings! I have a message for you from Valaste, Mistress of Incunabula.
I'm sorry, I can't talk right now. I'm waiting for my husband.
I'm so worried. About my husband. About our future.
This was a sad day until you appeared. Are you a person who can be hired?
I erect the spine of welcome to you.\n\nIf you have time, I need assistance.
Ahh, my little mortal. I'm a man of many personalities, but I tell you what? They're all very fond of you.
Thank you for pitying an injured tree-minder. I pray for your success. It's all I can do, for now.
Darj went to Skyshroud Barrow. Eiman and Rolunda are out at Orkey's Hollow. My sergeant, Seyne, is at Hozzin's Folly.
We're almost out.\n\nI'll unlock the door at the bottom of the stairs. In the next room, there's another switch I'll need you to trigger.
Squeak! Squeak squeak squeak squeak squeak squeak!
I can do this, adept. I'm ready to do what must be done.
Poor Valaste. She was one of the finest minds I knew. It's a shame she got wrapped up in Sheogorath's madness. We won today, but at what cost?
I still can't believe it's over. I'm glad Colors is alive, but ….

Abnur Tharn's continued presence in the flow of events is curious. When I read the Scroll that spoke of this prophecy, there was always an odd, black thread alongside our own. I begin to wonder if it symbolized the chancellor.
Our people would be food for crows without you, my friend.
Thank you so much. My poor children! I don't know if I could go on without them.
Dawnbreaker's edge! You're all here! It's taken me so long … since we parted ways after Abagarlas. But I've found it: the Mortuum Vivicus.
My brother Skorvild and his warriors gather in a house north of here. I'm sure he'd appreciate any help you could provide.
Did you make it to the signal fires?
Greetings, Comrade! May you find all the fights you seek, and win all the fights you find!
Hadring murdered? In broad daylight? The assassins made their move while the entire city watched.\n\nI won't stand for this! Hadring's killers must be found.
Be careful in Ceyatatar. Legend says it was there that Pelinal Whitestrake slew Hadhuul the Ayleid Fire King. Who knows what evil lurks among those ancient stones?
If you're not participating in the Race of the Nine Holds, please stand back.
What are you looking at? Why don't you go throw rocks at a dog or something?
What are you messing around here for? Why don't you go home and give your mom a bath, heard she needed it.
Ok, these guys are pretty dull witted, so don't worry but don't do anything stupid either.
It was heartbreaking to see <<Ac:1>> robbed of its energy upon its return.\n\nBut you helped restore our legacy. We shall not forget.
I hope you can convince our allies of my commitment to the Pact.
The threads of Ouze are repaired. You've saved the Oathbreakers, and perhaps all of the Valenwood.
In my story, I'll be as strong as Indinael! Someday.

Ah, the hero of Bad Man's Hallows. Guess I owe my life to you.\n\nDon't worry, I told the guild all about the Dremora summoning. They've got me cataloging the library while they figure out what to do with me. Dull work, but it's better than banishment.
Z'en, what would you have me do? Blood for blood. Death for death … so much death.
Scales tried to escape, so we locked her up. Nothing to worry about. Just want to make sure everyone stays safe.\n\nIt won't be long before she gets that crazed look in her eyes, though.
The elevator works! Feel free to take it out of here whenever you need to.
I need to study this ancient memory device for a few moments. Why don't you take a look at that dusty journal over by that corpse. It might contain something helpful.
I should have been nicer to Kalogar. Told him his cooking wasn't too terrible.
Voranil is headstrong. The Daedra will have trouble breaking him.\n\nBut alive or dead, he should be close.
Blood for the Pact. The blood of these dogs, with any luck.
If you need more power, you only need to ask.\n\nOtherwise, leave me to my solitude.
It's just like <<1>> to be the last one left. Honestly, I don't know how he keeps up with the rest of us in the show.\n\nBut the crowds love him, so he stays on my roll.
We need to get back to Deepwoods before the cave fills with werewolves or Houndsmen.
That's definitely my axe, but be careful. Tharn said that Coldharbour won't give it up, easily.
Don't worry, I didn't kill them all. Plenty more up in the ruins, if you're interested in lending a hand.\n\nSeems these Sea Vipers want the sphere for themselves!
You need quickness for this trial. King Jorunn's dreams collapse around him. You must be fast. You must find him before the dreams end or you will be lost as well.
The Drublog must be aware of our escape by now! We have to get under cover so you can examine the ritual book and the runestone.
If the Drublog haven't caught on to our activities yet, they soon will.\n\nThere's a lodge, nearly identical to the one we were imprisoned inside. We could hide there.
My friend! Thank you again. We'll drink an entire month in your honor! A whole month!\n\nWait, that doesn't sound right ….
My comrade! Good to see you again so soon. The Skald-King will no doubt welcome your service.
We will meet in the Smokefrosts, my friend. If not there, then in Sovngarde.\n\nKyne speed you.
I believe those <<mz:1>> are physical manifestations of stories woven by the Bosmer's three most powerful spinners.\n\nIf you take them from the Houndsmen in the ravine below, we'll know for certain.
I'm so very tired.
Quickly! With Thallik's spirit merged into Sinmur's, all of Skyrim is at risk! \n\nTake the haft of Wuuthrad and use the portal to return to the camp at Honrich Tower. There is no time to waste!
My court is empty, and my people are frightened. What will tomorrow bring, I wonder?
There you are. Alive and well, just like I left you.\n\nI hope I didn't startle the ambassadors too much with that daring rescue I performed.
Didn't Thorulf tell you to leave, assassin? Be grateful I let you go with your head still attached. Go sniff the hindquarters of whatever Jarl sent you.
First the attack against the thane and now this. I've asked my soldiers to take a more active role in defending the hall. I pray it's enough.

The binding stones will not hold. I don't know what Cirion's thinking.\n\nWe should be finding a way to remove Rilis from Nirn. The High Kinlord has had a taste of freedom after all these years—he'll stop at nothing to achieve it again.
My silk. You gave him my silk ….
Why would you do that? That silk belongs to me!
I can't believe Tirora's gone.
Have you been to the Treehenge before? Even now, it's a beautiful place.
When the Worm Cult attacked, many of the delvers here were killed. Others were captured. We don't have the numbers to take the Worm Cult head on.
Leave this island, if you know what's good for you. Only nightmares hold sway at Skald's Retreat.
He's called a gathering of the Council of Province Generals in Vulkwasten. You should find him at the Hall there.
The pass is ours. We must push forward!
Thank you for sparing me such a death.
You'll find the Mistress of Incunabula in the depths of the jungle, at the Baandari Trading Post in Malabal Tor. Good luck, Adept.
I hope Shandi liked the story. It's the only writing I've ever done! With your help, of course.
You did it! The militia gave a good account of themselves. We managed to trap the Ra Gada captain in the lighthouse!\n\nI'll leave you the honor of gutting him.
Don't be tempted to try the powder or the drinks. I wish to work with you on more escapades!
We're holding our own out here, just barely. Get into that mine as fast as you can.
I'm going to tend to Meldil. We'll move to the room just behind me. We should be safer in there.
Mm …. The book smells good enough to eat!
You found the kindlepitch? Excellent. Now find the Maormer fire salts and you'll be ready. Talk to <<1>> if you want to know more.
Is it done? Did you destroy the Shadowed Path lich?
I'm afraid we're not finished here. Not yet.
The ancestral spirits appear to be at rest, but we've no way of knowing if the necromantic energy has dissipated completely. Tread carefully.
Help clear the path to the Trolhetta Summit. We must stop Sinmur and the Worm Cult!
Ysgramor really does watch over you. Hah! Welcome to the fight.
We need to get this madness under control.
This is not right. My friends are out fighting against the Worm Cult and all the damn Daedra they've summoned. \n\nI should be out there too, not cooling my heels here in the camp.
Search him all you like. I'm not stopping you.
Look out! Those Houndsmen are everywhere!
Someday, we will write a song about your exploits.
I'm going to the camp. Just give me a minute. Don't worry, I won't let Laen take over as lead singer!
Good to see you again, my friend.
You again. We seem to meet in the worst places.
The captain will have no one to support her should you attack. If there was ever a time to rescue Eraral-dro, this is it.\n\nPlease go quickly, and make sure he hasn't been harmed!
I knew we'd meet again. Perhaps I'll save you this time.
Get going, friend. Tendil will get you situated. And we could use a few more hands for the wall.
He's at the Mages Guild hall. Should be straight ahead, across the bridge. \n\nTrinimac's blade keep you safe.
Trinimac guide your hand. And may he protect us all.
Welcome to Firsthold! It's just so lovely this time of year.
Unfortunate, but Bar-Neeus was bound to be caught sooner or later.
Look, they don't need help from outsiders right now. My men can handle this. \n\nThese folks have enough trouble tending to their own. Don't need you getting sick too.
Sorry, can't talk right now. For your own health. Please get out of here.
You did very well, yes. Very well. Hard work.\n\nSorry, do you mind? This scroll needs translating. Such fascinating ink-work.
My friend. It is good to see you again. Your talisman? Razum-dar sees you have met Sinien.\n\nCheerful, isn't she?
I'll see you back in town when it's all over.\n\nGood luck.
I'll meet you at my home when you're done. I live just behind Hendil.\n\nAnd I know, you must think I'm mad. But I can feel it. This is all wrong.
Well done.
Stay back! This cave is filled with Daedra.
Welcome to the fight, my friend. I hope the road from Shor's Stone wasn't a long one.
Who's this? Ah, it's you. Found my treasure, did you?
I can't believe I fell for that scam. I'll never live this one down.
Buried the dead as best I could. I see you found that Rilyn character. Looks suspicious to me, but Raerana is breathing easier with him here.\n\nWhat's that you've got?
This is one of those times I wish I could be in four places at once. Instead, I had to send my sisters <<1>>, <<2>>, and <<3>>.
So what's your answer? Care to prove yourself?
Begone, insect. I've no time for your ilk.
The Prophet!\n\nHe's a prisoner here, too. It was very dangerous for him to speak to you, even for a moment. He must think you can help me.
I can feel Mara's smile on my face for the first time in hours. Good luck.
Kindly step back. We have a situation here.
And how is Fistalle, my friend? Raz loves her laugh. \n\nWhat did she learn?

Believe me, I meant what I said. I'd happily go in there myself. But in this dress? And the nobles here would probably lose their minds.\n\nPlease, friend. I'd see it as a personal favor if you would investigate with the battlereeve.
Best of luck finding <<1>>!
You've returned! And all in one piece. What a hero!
I can't believe this is happening.
Please, find her. Find her quickly.
Please, find him. He's kind of an idiot. But he's still my brother.
Excellent work. Let's get below.
Please hurry. If my mother falls to this curse as I did … I can't bear to think of it.
Welcome to Skywatch. Your message arrived just fine and they're expecting you up at the manse.
I bid you welcome to Skywatch.
Please, follow.
Nothing's worth this nonsense. Stuff the Thalmor! And the Dominion! And—
Please take your leave. We've already reached our limit on Khajiiti students.
You claim that Gorak killed dozens of villains? And a foul necromancer, as well?
Careful. The crystal has a bite. Not always so friendly when unattuned.
This range brings back memories! Everyone from the village learned how to use a bow in this very place.
Good. You're here. This is Qoramir, my patrol leader. \n\nHe isn't having a good day.
As soon as Raynor recovers his senses, we'll make our way out of this Daedric death trap.
I won't forgive my father for this. I can't!

The Dark Anchor's portal is high above us. I will prepare a spell to lift us to it.\n\nBut first, you must re-attune yourself to Nirn in order to regain your physical form. To do this, you will need a skyshard.
I want to be the Nord I used to be. I want to help my friends remember who they really are.
We don't know each other, stranger. But you have a mother's gratitude for your kindness.
Keep your wits about you and win this thing. Save us. Save yourself.\n\nI'm going to go and look for the others. Just … end this already. I've had just about enough of this terrible game.

Good, good! This one hoped he would find you. Mim worried that some terrible fate had befallen you.\n\nThere was a terrible commotion and then the Observer appeared. He seemed angry, but also kind of excited. What did you do?
Don't worry about me. Save your empathy for someone who needs it.\n\nI shall have no trouble making my way to this city of yours.
I should have known. What a useless gesture! Why did we even try to help you?\n\nLook at us! Caught like rats in a cage.
I hope this city of yours has suitable accommodations for one of my stature. I won't stay at just any ratty old inn, you know.
Are you ready to help us, outsider? Will you undertake the trials?
A Proctor doesn't concern himself with justice or right. All that matters is that things run smoothly.
<<1>> is determined to get me killed. I won't do it anymore.
<<1>> crossed the marsh with the others. This one remains until the fisher-folk are safe. It is an important task, of course, but my claws itch for battle.
It's lucky we were able to drive the slavers back this time.\n\nI'm worried about what might happen if they were to attack again, though.
The poison was in the well water. Even better, I know exactly what kind it is.
Without the weight of numbers, we can't retake <<1>> by direct assault. The key to victory is the fort.
I thought the Pact was full of people like <<1>>. I'm glad you proved me wrong. I won't forget your mercy, friend.
Have you found <<1>>? If he's working with the bandits, he may be to the north of here.
Go on. Head over to the bridge. I'll send Tzik'nith on her way. Hopefully, she won't get suspicious and alert her sisters about all this.
I can't believe it! All these soldiers and not a decent mess kit among them? If only I'd returned with some supplies.
Honor and blood. Why are you here, stranger?
When you went searching for my assistants, did you see anyone else?\n\nAnyone intelligent, I mean. Spectres don't count.
Sweat and blood are worth a sea of words.
<<1>>. Did you find her? Tell her to hurry back. I cannot wait to get away from this place.
The Hall of Might, then! I've been looking forward to plumbing its depths!
Lead on, friend of <<1>>.
The stones—have they been destroyed?
Two down. Only one champion left. \n\nIf you kill them all, I may pout.
I can't believe the Guardian's Eye is nearly in my—I mean our—grasp!\n\nI don't know what you're planning to do with your share, but I'm buying a gold-plated carriage.
There is a captain in town planning a profitable heist. If you drop my name, she may let us join her.

Nice work back there. <<1>> found an old vent that led to this chamber. More climbing than I'd have liked, but we made it through.\n\nMy crew is making short work of the mutineers behind us, but there are still plenty more in the cavern.
Having that heirloom back will lift my spirits more than a cartful of dead Imperials.
Now to retrieve that staff. The door to Prince Maleel's tomb must be open now.
Aren't you finished yet?
I'll cover you and then head back to the entrance to wait for reinforcements. Don't get killed.
Captain, are there two of you standing there?
Well, now, before we start with the fun … we need to do a little worship.
Please! Byz is small and only sweeps! Do not hurt Byz!
Another successful retrieval, I see.
Moons above, she likes to talk sometimes.
We'd best be sure that Khali hasn't destroyed the ruin while we were away.
This Dwemer sphere still has some missing pieces. If you find them, I can get it running.
There is no time. The door must be opened and you must go after Wormfather. \n\nI'll make the sacrifice. It's the right thing to do. It'll ensure my place in Sovngarde at least.
Good to see you made it here in one piece.

What happened? I saw you enter the Temple and now you're back out here, talking to me. Does the beautiful goddess scare you? She certainly scares me!\n\nBut get going. Climb back on the guar and all that. Mournhold is depending on you.
Nicely done.
Use the Duskstone to enter the king's dream. Hurry! There is still a chance!
So, what do you say?
I've had enough adventures for one day.
I'm not sure you're supposed to be here.
Hey. You're not a guard. You have to help me!
Welcome. It's a good day to sit by the fire and cook rabbit kabobs.
Greetings, Champion.
