You're the one who helped Neramo break into Bthzark, aren't you? That's the rumor anyway.
What is it? I've got some guards to hire, now that the Worm Cult is out of the way.\n\nBusiness can be good again!
I hope you can help <<1>> too. Fat cat won't shut up about his fields when we play cards.
Help my sister, please!
I don't know how much my sister can take of this! Don't bother with me, go help her!
It's a shame about the villagers. But they knew the risks of living with us.
Sneak attacks are a specialty of ours. Any fool can run headfirst into battle. \n\nA true soldier ensures victory before they even take the field.
I'm just glad to be in the field today. I was getting sick of ripping out shalk gizzards for this reagent. \n\nNo, never mind. I loved doing that, too. Almost as much as I enjoy killing people.
Hey, hello there friend! Can I beg your assistance today?
What? Why? Where has he gone? Kalari will drag him back here by his ears! Why would he do that to me?
You did a wonderful job with the pranks! Are you ready to party?
Good luck in there. We'll hold the line here until you return.
Good to see you again. Did you salvage anything from the Hedoran estate?
Ahh, excellent. I sensed you coming. It's good to see you again. We can set to work right away.
There is still more for you to do.
You are to help Ezzag, yes? So Tazia tells this one. Just know he is a cussed old cat.
It is good to see a friend in such a dark place.
So? Ezzag was right, right? It was not children?

The Red Rooks will scatter, now they've lost their leader. \n\nI wish … I wish I had never gotten involved with these bastards. I'll regret that decision always, but will try to make up for it as best I can.
The Canonreeves who authorized this invasion will be pleased we averted an absolute crisis.\n\nThanks to you, the heavy losses we suffered in this battle will not be for nothing.
And so, it falls to us, Vestige. We must stop Molag Bal and his Dark Anchors, or our world is doomed. \n\nAnd now, history seems to have caught up with us. Shall we return to the Harborage?
Please, traveler. You must help us. We've been driven from the temple, and the Claw is in terrible danger!
Few things bother me more than the thought of Goblins using our books for kindling or worse.
By the Eight, we've done it. The Daggers will live on!\n\nThank you, friend.

Indaenir said you might be coming. And you're here not a moment too soon. As our living soldiers fall, the ranks of the dead swell. \n\nAt this rate, we'll all be fighting for the other side by tomorrow's dawn. And that's not even the worst part.
Follow the torchbug.
Talmo and his banner. The dryskin fool will not shut up about it.
Hallowed … you have come, as Hunal saw reflected on the moons last night. This one sees the cool light of the moons reflected in your eyes. You have greatness in your future, yes?

If I've said it once, I've said it a thousand times … no more drinking! My head's splitting, my mouth feels like a kagouti nested in it, and I'm in serious trouble.\n\nI don't suppose you'd care to help out a down-on-her-luck chef, would you?
I remember you! You helped us on our last visit to this evil place. Thank the Divines you returned! I need your help. It's my son.
I don't like the idea of Tharn being involved at all. He's a cockroach looking for an open cupboard.
You gave Rhea the poison? Can't trust any of you provincials.
You made the right choice by giving me the poison.
Did you charge those restoration scrolls? I need them badly.
Together, we shall restore the altars. You wield the blessings of the Bright Moons, and Rid-Thar will attune their connection to Jone and Jode.
Traveler, Felari is very sorry to bother … but could she beg your help?
I never thought it could be this bad. I'm used to being able to think through my problems. Using my books and spells to … there's no solution to this in a book.
I'm sorry to ask for your service so soon. But after the loss of the Champion at Moonmont your valor could make the difference today.
The Khajiit are a noble people. To see their jewel in the desert brought low like this … it moves my heart.
What a disaster to befall such a fair city ….
My city. My beautiful, wonderful city.
Hermaeus-Mora sees and knows.
Razum-dar has relayed his suspicions to Treethane Fariel, but she has questions she would ask of you herself.\n\nHurry. We must go after Asteril and make sure she does not escape once again.
We have to just forgive Oromin's terse manner. He takes his position very seriously.\n\nSee what you can uncover at the residence. And be careful.
<<1>> is in the larger Ayleid ruins. Go quickly, before the Dominion realizes what they've lost.
You look like a proper pirate now. Get going.
It's terrible, wondering if you should trust your superiors.
So after three months of wasting time in Alcaire and three long days at sea, I finally return home. My chair, my wine, my wife, all here.\n\nPlease tell me you haven't come here to disturb me.
I keep waiting for the screaming to start. Did you find any portals?
You survived! Truly the Hist guides you.\n\nBut did you succeed?
You're alive! Cheers! I didn't know if I'd ever see you again.
<<1>> would like a moment of your time.
I can't believe it. I finally figured it out. This … this could change everything! \n\nOur lurcher guardians—I've found a way to give each of them special powers!

That was a harrowing experience all around. I'm glad it's over. I hope we have succeeded in weakening Naemon's grasp on Valenwood as a whole. \n\nOnly one thing remains … we must deal with the spirit of General Malgoth.
Bad luck. Ah well. You know what they say, "Nothing ventured, nothing … ventured." Hey, and at least your lizard is fit for the stewpot.

We have made excellent progress thus far, but there is still so much to do. Continue your efforts to fill this city and strengthen our army. We shall require every ally we can muster if we are to successfully challenge the Lord of Schemes.

And so it finally begins. We have waited so long for this moment, but the taste is bittersweet. We shall lose many fine men and women this day, I fear.\n\nMay the blessing of Meridia protect you, champion. Now, go. The Chasm awaits.
You look strong, sleek. Yes … come, come! Join the race! Try your hand at spikeball, the sport of champions.
This part's on you. I'm a dunce when it comes to magic.
I say, jolly good timing. Lyris, enchanted, as always. And you—you're looking fit for someone so … how can I put it? Deficient in the soul department?
It galls me that the enemy holds the Elder Scroll of Ghartok. We must capture it!
You have caught Ezreba, miserable wretch that she is. She will not fight you.
Let the Treeminder know that you made your decision, outsider.
Find out what's happening up above yet?
Khaba is afraid your troll has been "retired." You will try again later, yes? Perhaps your luck will change.
So, did you find them?
You've brought Ezreba out of the darkness. Well done. And those spirits seem to have gone back to wherever they came from. What did you do?
Glow juice? You find some?
These sailors work a lot harder than I thought. We'll stick with the Prowler, if <<1>> will have us.
Praise the gods, you're back! I thought you were an alit.
Did you find any glow juice? I got some sand in my wounds. Don't ever do that, even by mistake.
Imagine Tamriel without Goblins. Well, I can dream, can't I?
<<1>>'s plan is to let <<2>> possess him! They'll both be sealed in the tomb, forever.\n\nBut it doesn't need to be this way. Seal me inside.
<<1>> clearly has an opinion about my plan. I've learned it's best to hear her out.
That was fast. All right, there's room on the Prowler for your marine friends, as long as they work for their meals.

Teleportation was never this difficult before. The spell took so much out of me, I was afraid we would never materialize. But Zur has the key to this room. He acquired it shortly after we got here. Were you able to craft the antipodal rods?
Please … help me. The crystal. I can hear them in my head!
You think this one drinks on the job? Good, then so will everyone else.\n\nWhat is the word, my new friend?

I hope you find what you seek in this tower. I often wondered what was inside, but I never dared to enter the place.\n\nRemember, friend, we are allies now! When you require my help, all you have to do is ask.
We've done it! Once they saw Gavo's confession, most of them abandoned the city. They're running home to Colovia. The only ones still fighting are her loyalist core. How'd it go with Lavinia?
I can already hear them talking out there. We're so close, I can taste it.
I don't have time for you right now. The Prowler's damaged and unless we get some help, she'll founder at high tide.\n\nYou want to help? Talk to <<1>>.
Where is former Ambassador <<1>>?
We upheld our treaty with the people of <<1>> for generations, and this is how they repay our kindness?\n\nWe will not allow High Elf thieves to gain a foothold in our territorial waters!
You found him like this? What did you see? Answer me!
You again? Don't tell me you're serious about competing in the Sorcerer Division Championship. You'll be eaten alive!
Ah, my greenhorn friend is back and ready to have some fun. Did you bring a change of underthings?

Welcome back, lovely! Zara wondered when you would return. She missed you terribly. \n\nThe other contenders should thank Jone and Jode that championships are not won by physical attraction. Your sleekness would best them all.
Champion of the Swordmaster Division? You are a surprise!
You watch. Someday, these lands will be called Driladan Valley. The Spinners will even tell stories about us, and how we defended our lands and preserved the clan.
I sense the time to reforge the essences of the Great Mage has arrived.

A great man lies dying over there, and he has put all his faith in you. I hope it is not misplaced.\n\nI have finished mixing the potion for your initiation. Whenever you are ready, we can begin the trial.
I wasn't expecting any of the Shadow Walkers to be here. They haven't attacked yet, so that's a good sign. \n\nJust don't do anything to make them nervous, all right?
Thank you for helping me fulfill my promise. With <<1>>'s death, I showed mother I will follow in her footsteps.
By the Root, what happened here? I'd like to hear Nervyna's explanation.
The Dwemer ruins are further down the tunnels. Stay close. The automatons are everywhere.\n\nThere had better be some money to be made from this.

I arrived with a few other wizards. Conjuration masters. We helped open the portal to Coldharbour.\n\nUnfortunately, we didn't arrive where we expected. A defensive countermeasure, I think. Molag Bal's forces were upon us in an instant.
I trust you to get the information we need. However you see fit.
Ifriz is never far from his beloved barrier. Hurry and end this so that we can both get on with our existences.
The forbidden books remain. Please, bring them to the shrine so they may be purged once and for all.
This one does not understand. This shrine is supposed to be lit with an ever-burning flame!\n\nPerhaps <<1>> has thrown good money after bad.
We keep meeting in the most interesting places. Now, if only we weren't always fighting for our lives, that would be something.\n\nAnyway, thank you for setting us free.
This one has felt the blazing embers of Daedra torture. They attempt to destroy the mind and body together.\n\nWe must find my brother before we lose Kargand forever.
I should get back to our inspection. If you see anything suspicious, it's your duty to let us know. Fires don't start themselves.
My father, he keeps shaking. Why is he shaking?

I hope you know what you're doing. But just to be clear, I'm helping you, not the Crimson Matron over there.\n\nThat said, destroying the Harvest Heart is now our primary concern. I'll prepare this area while you help her start her ritual.
I was told you were coming.
Put everything in the circle and we'll begin.

My children will oppose us every step of the way. As long as the Harvest Heart continues to hold them in its grasp, they have no choice.\n\nProtect me from them, and I promise I will set them free of Molag Bal's evil!
Hmm. You know, that elixir was actually pretty tasty. They never mention that in any of the texts.
Ugh, that elixir. I can't get the taste off my tongue. Do you feel more enlightened? I just feel a little sick.
Well done! You reversed the flow of energy. Find the other conduits and let's return the stolen life force to that poor creature.
You should eavesdrop on the party guests and find out what they have planned for Aranias.
My comrade, I am very glad to see you again.
Valenwood's soil is, not surprisingly, very fertile. These specimens are bound for the royal gardens.
Still here? You're welcome to stay as long as you like.
Welcome aboard. Glad to have some new blood around. My fellow Guild mates can be stifling sometimes.
Hurry along now and see if you can find another way in.
Please, stranger. I'd like to drink alone right now.

I heard the commotion outside and somehow knew it was you. It is good to see you, my illustrious friend.\n\nYour arrival comes at a fortuitous time, as we are indeed in dire straits. And it will soon get much, much worse.
Good luck in there. Raz would not face a vision quest for all the moon-sugar in Elsweyr. But he is sure you will do fine.

Tales of today's battle will undoubtedly be told for generations! When soldiers of the Aldmeri Dominion face impossible odds, they will not retreat. \n\nThey will say "remember the Battle of Seaside Sanctuary" and they will press on, to victory!

I believe that the injustice done to Zariya has kept her spirit from making the journey to the Far Shores.\n\nI hope that if you perform this act of consecration, it will bring her the peace she deserves.
Cariel has been updating this one on your work in Arenthia. Very nice. Razum-dar is impressed.
That fool has no idea of the danger you have put him in. I can sense the ghosts approaching even now. Tu'whacca forgive him … and you.

I'm glad you're here. I've been trying to help these poor people, but it's futile. There is a blight here that's turned them into rabid beasts.\n\nThese Bosmer may be beyond aid, but we must find a way to stop the blight from spreading.
Oh, hello. You're not from Willowgrove. You're … looking through my things. Can I help you?
Malooc take Gudarz and his thugs. I'm about fed up with this place.
Ah, welcome. I'm entertaining a guest at the moment. Is there something I can help with?
Can't talk now, wayfarer. I have to make sure our recruits don't hurt themselves with the sharp ends.
Oh, hello! This mead is delicious. Did you know that bees made drinks? I didn't either.

It was all a trap! Who does things like that? I took off my clothes to get ready for the celebration and the sisters attacked me! They threw me in this cage and walked off with the key.\n\nAnd I'm naked!
What a stubborn, pig-headed fool Stibbons is! Can you talk some sense into him?

You ever get the feeling that you were meant to do something important?\n\nMe neither. But this … this could come close to that. We stop the Planemeld and save the people of Tamriel. Who wouldn't want to be remembered for doing that?
The Champions are here. They awaited your arrival with great enthusiasm! Are you ready to join them within?
Just look around until we figure out a way to either open that gate or get around it.
<<1>> has put up the dowry? Excellent!\n\nWe're finally getting somewhere.
Whoever you are, I'm not in a talking mood. Leave me alone.
Are you here to help arrange my daughter's marriage? She's got her mother's spirit! And her temper.\n\nSo! What does <<1>> expect in a bridegroom?
Head to Knife Ear Grotto, in the eastern mountains of Deshaan. I will meet you inside.
Get the Staff of Magnus from the Shade's remains. We need to make sure it gets returned to the queen.
Soldiers and barricades aren't exactly a welcoming feast. But unless the Argonians are willing to speak with us, they won't stay in <<1>> for much longer.
We should hurry. If any of <<1>>'s hunters attack Dominion soldiers, my tribe is doomed.
I will pay whatever you require. Just help me. I will give anything to get her back.
Meet me at my house. It's at the edge of town, past the smithy.\n\nI'll tell you everything I know. See you soon, I hope.
He wants you to use that magical toy on the totem that's covered in lightning? Good luck, I guess.
Hmm. I would definitely heed <<1>>'s advice about the puddles.
We can't get to the crystals!
Well, little mortal? What are you waiting for? Must I hand you an engraved invitation?\n\nGet inside and do what you came here to do!

Can't say I'll miss throwing back wave after wave of Wormies and their bony minions. But now I have a chance to see the world! Meet new and interesting people!\n\nOnly now I won't accidentally smash everything in my path. Rather embarrassing, that.
I thank you for your sacrifice, friend.\n\nI am … fading. Tamriel is pulling me back.
I certainly hope the real afterlife is better than this abomination.
That last assault nearly toppled us.\n\nBut you look alive. You've handled one of the fronts, I take it? I need the other end of town cleared of Daedra.
Suronii says this is not Coldharbour, but a "wound between planes." This one is glad. If this were Coldharbour, this one would be in nightmare landscape and subject to the tortures of Daedra.
If you're looking to buy something, you've come to the right place.
This one wishes there was more that could be done. Indaenir is certain you're the key.
When Raz told me about Hectahame, I couldn't get here fast enough. Now I can't even get inside.\n\nTo top it off, this Vinedusk won't leave me alone. Boys.
I need you to promise me you'll make the Daedra pay for taking Elolir.\n\nHe was a fool, but he was our fool. If you need an extra hand I'll pick up where Elolir left off.
Gilraen and her archers can hold the barrier at the center of town, but the north and south fronts are crawling with Daedra.\n\nThey'll close in on her if we don't stop them.
<<1>> is using you to test his theory!\n\nHave no fear. I'll tend any wounds you sustain.
This is going about as well as I expected, unfortunately.
These three will never reach an agreement. I swear, the head that wears the crown always seems to swell like an overripe melon.
Have you seen Erinel, my betrothed? She's been kidnapped, and these guards won't let me pass!
What a rousing adventure! I wonder what else awaits intrepid knights such as we?\n\nI think I'll commission a ballad to describe our exploits. How do you feel about iambic pentameter?
You can help me, or you can leave, but I will avenge the Faithful.
Pretend we're old friends catching up after a long absence. I don't want to blow my cover just asking for help.
There's more to be done, though. Always is, isn't there?\n\nI know Prince Azah is out hunting down the Ansei Wards. You should help him if you are able.
Save your breath. I will not be swayed by some Altmer lapdog.
This Queen of yours is spirited, I'll give her that. But she has no right to force her will upon all of Tamriel.

Your King needs to stop talking out of the side of his mouth. He has a lot of Dominion blood on his hands. We're not going to easily forget that, and we're certainly not going to fight by his side in Coldharbour.
The loss of the Staff of Marbruk troubles me. If Pelidil is behind it, he could also be involved in the theft of my brother's body.\n\nFor now, we must tackle problems we can solve.
Please return to the sacred cave and escort the convicted to the judgment chamber, advocate. The town can't move on until you do.
I am grateful that you believed in me. I wish I could say the same of the others here. Many still believe I am guilty, even though the forest has returned to normal.
Treethane Rolon will want to talk to you, outsider. I don't see why. We already know who's responsible for this mess.

Sancre Tor? Never been there, but I understand it's where the Reman dynasty is entombed.\n\nWhy do people even bother burying remains anymore? Seems rather a waste of time these days, what with everyone popping up from their graves. Cremation, I say!
I never thought it could be this bad. I'm used to something I can pin down and fight, you know? Something that my blade can solve. No blade can solve this.
I'm glad you proved me wrong, advocate. Losing our Spinner would've been unthinkably difficult on us all.
You aren't the first to be fooled by Gathiel. Eranas was fooled and it cost him his life.

Did you notice the tiger skulls on my wall? They belonged to a senche couple who stalked Khenarthi. Took me the better part of the year to track them. Tell me, stranger, have you ever seen tigers of such size?
If he makes one wrong move, just one misstep, I'll end him. You have my word.
We're under attack! The Orcs have attacked!
About time you got over here, old chum. Exercise is all well and good, but if I keep this up much longer I'll be useless in the actual battle!
Welcome back, Vestige. News of Mannimarco's demise spreads far and wide. Like worms, his followers burrow deep into the earth to escape the searing light of the coming dawn.
You've returned. We have a lot to discuss, but Lord Varen is anxious to speak with you first. We'll talk later.
Be welcome, my friend. I would have words with you, but my lord seeks your attention first.
Don't look at me. Varen called this meeting. Apparently he's got something to share. I, for one, am all aquiver with anticipation.
This is momentous. Our actions today will be remembered for many generations, my brother.
The enemy has held the Elder Scroll of Altadoon for far too long. Help us take it from them!
Kasura is injured. We must help her.
Hallowed! A pleasure. May the light of the Bright Moons bless and keep you.
All the Covenant rejoices that the Elder Scroll of Altadoon is now ours!
Some of the acolytes must still be alive. They must be.
Sai's alive, but he's far from safe. We need to hurry!
At least we know that Sahan is still breathing. I suppose we should press on.
When Sai Sahan has recovered, you must accompany him on a journey to the Valley of Blades, where his mentor Kasura resides. \n \nI will contact you as soon as he is ready to travel.
Once we find all the pieces we need, we can go to the Constellation Room. Then we'll make sure <<1>> sleeps for good!
It's never an easy thing to see, but justice must be done. I will pray for him.
I knew Aranak cut that flower. He always had a poor respect for our customs.
I'm sorry, I can't talk to you right now. I need to get this chamber ready for the trial.
I wonder if we can trust each other again after this.
Here we are, Vestige, in the belly of the beast. And each of us carries within us, an Oblivion of his own making.
No matter how this ends, I'm proud of how far we've come, and what we've accomplished.
Courage, my friend. That is the most important of all virtues. Courage is not a lack of fear, rather, it is the realization that there are things more important than fear.
You should speak to the treethane. I … I'm still trying to understand all of this. It's just too terrible to think.
Friend, you picked a bad time to come here. Nothing's right, right now. Nothing at all.
Someone's pissed all over the Pact. Unless you're of a mind to stick your nose into our business, better to just move on.\n\nI'm thinking about it. Better than dealing with all this nonsense.
There is something sinister going on in Rivenspire, five-claw. Keep your wits about you and stay fragrant. What you saw here is only the beginning.
What a disaster! These monsters need to pay for what they did to our town.
It seems Renoit is a bit … upset. Please, pay him no mind. He doesn't know what he's saying.
Why did this terrible thing happen to Moira's Hope? I've never been so scared in all of my life!
We didn't even have a moment's warning. By Arkay, the vampires. They struck so fast.
We should really stop whoever's causing this storm, shouldn't we?
I see you've reacquainted yourself with <<1>>. Unacquainted? Unrequited!\n\nThere, there … she'll come around to you. Like I did!

That stupid Captain Janeve! She threw me out of the camp! Wouldn't listen to a word I had to say!\n\nYou need to go in there and warn her. This isn't a refugee camp. It's a banquet table for bloodfiends!
Mannimarco has been watching our every move. We led him right to the amulet!
As my old Lieutenant used to say, "If all else fails, fight dirty!"
Are you ready to return to <<1>>?
How goes the Goblin killing, comrade? Sebazi hopes to hear good news.
It is good to see you again. Has your contract against the Goblins been fulfilled?
How did things go against the Goblins? I don't see any ears on your belt, but maybe you don't collect souvenirs.
Perhaps you can convince Tharn to reveal Sai Sahan's location. He refused to speak to me.
Now that I'm safe, all I can think about is what comes next. Moira's Hope is the only place I've ever known.
Had I known it was going to be this hot, I would have dressed for it.

By the Eight! Having your soul reinserted is just as painful as having it ripped out. At least I'm whole again. A reintroduction is in order!\n\nI'm Gasteau Chamrond—you won't find a better artisan this side of Oblivion. Mad Architect included.
Did you hear that? Was it a frost troll?\n\nWe should get to <<1>> as soon as we can.
I knew I could count on you! If you find that blasted cup, you will have my eternal gratitude.

Well that was the first—and the last—time we allow an outsider to take part in one of our rituals. I don't know what's gotten into Rashan.\n\nAll the same, I must confess that I misjudged you. I hope you accept my apology. It's rarely given.
Grisly as it may be, don't forget that I need the old hag's heart.
Be careful, she has <<1>>!
The ring is yours. Guard it well. I must return to my students to begin the long task of rebuilding.
Wait, you there! I'm not a … not a Goblin!
It would seem that in his own mind, our friend Sai never really left the Halls of Torment.
Curse these Reachmen. The Eight give us the strength to beat them.
Disturbing to say the least. So the Dark Witnesses would turn us all into their puppets to reinforce their army and take Evermore. \n\nWe can't allow that to happen.
Another distraction.
Try not to let that Baandari skeeve out of doing his part. Those damn cats have an excuse for everything.
I'm sorry, I'm retired.
I had a feeling coming here was going to be bad for business. Always trust your instincts! I should have listened to my mother more often.
Twelve curses for a flybitten shaveskin! I should never have listened to <<1>>. This is what comes of trusting a thief!
The Countess will speak to you. I must consider how best to deal with the traitorous Baron Montclair.

I returned to Shornhelm after my father's death to find a city divided and our land in peril. Baron Dorell means well, but he'd rather rush forward than take a moment to examine the path ahead.\n\nBut what brings you to Rivenspire, friend?
Best of luck, fellow Moon. What <<1>> has asked of you is no simple thing.
My good friend! You have done so much for us, and asked so little in return. If all my agents were so skilled and selfless, we might bring our services to the world!

Perhaps I should have done as Baron Montclair asked. Given Leila my gift. Maybe then this war would have never started. We'd all still be friends. Rivenspire would be at peace.\n\nIt doesn't matter now, though. What's done is done.

I'm not expecting you to get in over your head, but you never know what tricks Septima Tharn might have up her sleeve. \n\nIf you get overwhelmed, fall back here. We'll hold this ground come Oblivion or Coldharbour!

Verandis, my friend! You really must allow your charges to get out and have a little fun every now and then. Poor Gwendis here is having a splendid time, but it's like she's never tasted a fine wine before.\n\nWhy not pull up a chair and join us?
So that's it, then. The vampire lord is dead. As are Zungarg and Agalir.\n\nI've lost partners before, but you never get used to it. I feel responsible.
Damn it! I knew this would happen! If it had been anyone else, I would have put him to rest right away!\n\nWhat are you doing standing there? We have to get inside!

What does Crazy Eye see here? Another sleek walker? Good! These Knights of Saint Pelin need all the help they can get!\n\nCrazy Eye and the other Baandari have done all they can. Maybe it's your turn to help now?

You know, I really thought the years had hardened Emeric, made him cold, but since he arrived in Evermore, I've caught glimpses of the cousin I used to play with when we were kids. \n\nDifficult as all this has been, I think it's rekindled his spirits.
That Two-Blades, he has been a scourge on Rivenspire for years. But working for Montclair? That is the straw that broke the pony guar's back!
Our eyes have been watching you. They've been fixed upon you since you entered the <<1>>.

<<1>> is where the Blacksap Rebellion began. With your help, <<1>> will be where it ends.\n\nThe Vinedusk Rangers need you to flush out the Blacksap leaders. Killing them will only fuel the flames of rebellion. They must be brought into custody.
The Shrouded Pass that leads to the Doomcrag contains an ancient Ayleid ruin. I hate ruins. Never anywhere to get a decent drink or a hot meal.
Ah, the empty one returns.\n\nYour pardon, but, bereft of your soul, that's how I think of you. Don't be offended: I hope to repair your lack.
<<1>> doesn't give her recommendation lightly. If she thinks you can assist us, I take her at her word.
Yes? Quickly, now. Don't leave your mouth to hang agape.
Place her heart in the bowl on the altar.
Put it in the bowl.

You are not mere prey, mortal. Yet you aid the wyrd who still lick their wounds of defeat. Their fall to Brinarch and his Reachmen lost them my favor. To earn it back, you must prove yourself a true hunter.
You see? Quite maddening! \n\nAnd all I have to go on are these similarly arcane inscriptions from the ruins.

It seems the threat to other parts of the kingdom is far beyond our original estimations. \n\nCountess Tamrith sent a messenger from her camp south of Crestshade. It seems she is in desperate need of assistance. If you can go to her, please do.
These stone castles are always so drafty and damp. I long for the warm sands of the Alik'r desert. \n\nBut my place is at Emeric's side, and I am proud of that.
Yes? Can I help you? Did my brother send you?
With Rajhin's Mantle at hand and Daraneth returned to Elden Root, only an Ayleid source of power remains.
Well? <<1>> won't start itself.\n\nGood thing, too. I'd be out of a job.
I hope you can find her.
Don't believe Anexiel's lies. You must use the talisman. Quickly!
Onsi guide you.
The Blood Matron brought these cultist here for you to prey upon. You need the blood. Drink.
The others are going to give us a little time to find a safe location to use as a base. No point in all of us getting captured together.
These happy patrons wouldn't be here if it wasn't for your help. In these dark times, you've brought a little light into the world.
What could be holding up that shipment? This is terrible for business, just terrible!
I sense in you a goodness, whether you sense it yourself.
Please refrain from vulgar language nearby. I ask you pre-emptively, as I have no desire to hear coarse words today.
Mara's blood, am I glad to see you! What are you doing in Rivenspire?\n\nNo, never mind that. I need your help.

Ah yes, I recall you from before. You failed to find the relic I was hunting in the Alik'r. At least you didn't fail to find me though.\n\nI don't suppose you'd be willing to help me find something else, just to prove you're not entirely inept?
What a pleasant surprise.
We have the heads. Now we need a space to swear the oath.
I didn't expect to see you again. Ever. Then again, I didn't expect to get caught either.
If you'll sort all this dung-talk out, you don't even have to do the escort. I'll just do it myself. \n\nI'll still give you half the coin, of course. Anything to avoid dealing with this myself.
You've done it again, haven't you? You're a hero, twice over! Brilliant!
The prince is thoroughly engaged at the moment. Certainly too busy for the likes of you.
If the Countess has one of her famous healing poultices, I could sure use one. That'll have me back in fighting form in no time!
I hope I never have to bathe while surrounded by harpies again!
The entire village lives in these caves. Guess it saves on building materials, and gives them some protection from the harpies.
This is the strangest group I've ever hired.
It's you! Good to see you, mate. It's been a while since Shrieking Scar. \n\nSorry I didn't see you coming. I'm busy keeping an eye out for harpies. And those puny Breton brothers.

Sad times when I have to rely on a stranger, but I do appreciate you asking around. The mayor, the jeweler, the miller—they're all acting strangely. There's something they're not saying.\n\nI'll be back at the inn if you learn anything.
No one in here but the dead. Go away now.

I know Shuga's probably going to give you some lip, but keep in mind that kind of spunk can sometimes translate into real grit in battle.\n\nIf you run out of patience, though, just knock her out. We can wait and rouse her at the training camp.
The way is blocked. I assume this is another part of Lleraya's illusion. Look for another tear and see if you can show us the true path from here.
My own son … I can't believe it. He has placed a stain on the honor of House Dorell that I may never be able to remove.
I suppose we need to discern the pattern. Each spirit walked to a specific tile, if I recall correctly.
Please, my friend. If anyone can save Arlie's mother and father, it's you.
You saved them! You saved them both. Now please, end this nightmare once and for all!
Listen, this whole thing happened because Arlie's mother didn't approve of us spending time together. Even though things didn't work out for her, she might not be happy to see me alive.
Have you seen Allan?

I never really thought this day would come. But it is what Verandis has been training me for.\n\nI guess we're really going in there. Into the Doomcrag. It's a bit scary, but I'm with Verandis to the end.
Green keep you, traveler. I hope your visit to Skywatch is a pleasant one.
When the Maulborn attacked us for no reason at all, they showed their true colors. It's obvious they don't want anyone to know what they're doing down here.
You made it out of there. Good. Does this mean you took care of our Maulborn problem?
Who are you? You're not someone from the village. Please leave this area. It's a private place, and I've no wish to do you harm.
Yes? Nice to see you again, but I'm kind of in the middle of something here.
I'm sure it looks worse than it actually is.
I'll admit, I thought you were a goner when you went inside, but glory goes to you—for now. \n\nOnce Roaring Ramavel and the other Undaunted get here, I'm taking it right back. I'm the best!
Thank you for helping me reach the shrine. I would not have been able to do it without you.
You have come to us at a terrible time. Elinhir lies in ruins at the hands of wicked mages.

You there. You look like you know what you're doing, and that's just what I need right now.\n\nSee that large staff sticking out of the ground? It's emitting magical energy at unprecedented levels. If we don't stop it, it's going to explode.
Did you arrive from the surface? You need to take leave of this place. \n\nThere's a war on down here.
I apologize—I really shouldn't have run ahead. This whole ordeal has been very stressful for me.\n\nI won't do it again.
You will recognize the places where the magicka seeps through by the atronachs and spellfiends that are drawn to the power.
We would accompany you, but the danger is too great.\n\nThe Scaled One already holds most of our power. You would not wish to face him if he held all of it.
My clan and I would run this prison with an iron fist. The inmates would be put to work in Lord Bal's glorious name, not left to linger.\n\nSuch a waste.
That look on your face says you didn't get to the top of the Archive.\n\nAt least you got some horrendous wounds from it, eh? Get back up there. Those stairs aren't going to climb themselves.
Excellent riding. When I think of the day Emeric was crowned, I think it is something we all dream of—the chance to ride out bearing such important news.
For a Milksop, you are certainly an inspiring one.\n\nTuruk is old and wrinkly, but if he ever has a little Khajiit, he's calling it "Milksop!"
Go grab Oosh. She won't want to miss this.

Well, the armorer and her trolls certainly put up a fight. Alternate plan, indeed!\n\nThe runescriber should be on the western side of the valley, making his wriggly, squiggly patterns. Wait until you see them. Kind of pretty.
If you can stop the Serpent ….\n\nI suppose there's no use getting my hopes up.
I'll meet you inside the cave known as Serpent's Nest. From there, we'll go together to save the prisoners and eliminate the progenitor mantikora.

The Thief needs to perform the ritual at a site within the Howling Sepulchers. Go north and follow the path into the hills to the cave we seek.\n\nJust stay alert. Undead Nedes patrol the place and they have no regard for visitors—living or dead.
Please, I must hear what transpires.
You're back! So, which got the better of you: the simple thugs or the crumbling Dwarven junk?
You return resembling a drowned rat, but you are unbroken. The Maormer were not so fortunate I hope.
A good bow will get you far in life. Making good bows will get you farther.
Bring me your culinary creation so I might inspect it. I'll determine whether or not you deserve certification.

<You notice a prominent handbill on the requisition board.>\n\n"The Mane gives greetings! Masters of the craft await you in <<1>>. We offer training for all new to their craft, and certification for accomplished crafters. Free for all citizens!"
Hey there, scrub. You'd best stay back. We are speaking of blood and glory. For we are Undaunted!

This is one of the most complex Dwemer devices I've ever encountered.\n\nTo reiterate, we need to strike the kinetic resonators to rotate the rings and align the lenses to the beams. If you run into trouble, just use that lever to reset the rings.
Do you always just barge into the king's tent without so much as a "by your leave"?\n\nWho in the name of the First Forge do you think you are, troll breath?

Ramash may be too proud to ask for help from outsiders, but I'll take whatever I can get.\n\nOrcs don't scare easy, but the remaining members of the clan are getting restless. They want to know what happened to their friends and families. And so do I.
Hey, Chief. I hear Yazara roped you into doing the trials yourself. Ready to grab an echatere by the crest?
You've returned. Who is the new chief of Shatul?
You don't want to go in there, friend. The place is crawling with Riekrs!
Strange times we live in. I always thought Kurog was stronger than the mountains themselves.\n\nMaybe that was the problem.
The guards are innocent, they think they're defending their Empress. But we have no choice—we have to get past them. Make their deaths … quick.
Fire traps would be a nice accent for the base. They'd keep the Daedra and the cultists away too.\n\nDid you want to talk to me?
What is it, soldier? General Aklash has lots for me to do.

It is truly tragic what's happened to this city, yes? Aishah thinks so.\n\nBut … there is no cloud so dark that some light cannot be seen … by those who care to look. One might even find golden opportunities, yes?

<You notice a prominent handbill on the requisition board.>\n\n"The royal family welcomes you! Masters of the craft await you in <<1>>! New crafters shall be trained! Accomplished crafters will be certified! All at no cost to you!"
If nothing else, you have had practice blowing a horn, yes? Perhaps you have a future in music!

I fear we have lost sight of what really matters here. Molag Bal seeks to pull the city into Coldharbour. We say we want to "save it," but don't we really mean "control it?"\n\nWhile we squabble, innocent people are dying.
This is what it's come to. I was once a bodyguard for a member of the Elder Council, and now I'm in a sewer drain hiding from Daedra.
You were, were you? Yes, yes, you have that look about you. I think you'll do very nicely. We may just have a place for you in our organization.\n\nCome, my friend, we have many things to discuss.
Wish I could let you in, but orders are orders. Building will be open soon, I hope.
The trick with these old Nord puzzle locks is to activate the panels in the proper sequence.\n\nGo ahead! Your guess is as good as mine!
Climb fast, brave friend! Just find the Armlet and you'll be back before you can freeze solid, I'm almost certain!
I never could stand cold weather. Chills me to the bone! I feel like a frozen icicle!
I envy you. But don't worry. If the summit takes you, then I will be here to attempt the climb after you die.\n\nIt's the least I could do for someone who has shown such bravery.
Stupid ship started collapsing around me. Figured I was going to sink before I got out from under this mess.
Have you found my wife yet? Please tell me that you know where Sovelle is.
The Hand of Morkul isn't our forge-hammer. It's the cage around it! And if my clan's old word for "heart" also means "blood," then this wasn't our heart-forge.\n\nIt was our ….
Damn Riekr! I thought I could handle them, but there were so many of the jabbering creatures.
Learning about my past … it's good, but it also makes me sad.
Well? You forget something?
I'll use my magicka to help you fight. I can call down lightning. Just pick me!
Please, help me. Pick me! I can heal you as we make our way out of here!
If you stand near that wreckage over there and use the lightning prod, it should show you the direction the Dwarven sphere took off in.
I'll be grateful if you get through to <<1>>. I already wrote Orsinium about our findings.\n\nCan you imagine if she denies <<2>>'s tomb in front of the king's people? I could never live it down!
What are you waiting for? Use the lightning prod and follow the Dwarven sphere before it gets too far ahead of us.
I saw you speak with <<1>>. I know he's upset, but he's wrong about this tomb.\n\nThe remains of <<2>> are inside—not <<3>>.
I hope they still have a job for me at the tavern in Orsinium. I should have been there days ago.

I've never had to race through a battle zone before. I'm scared to death, but it's kind of exhilarating.\n\nMust be my Orc blood. I wonder if by living in a big city I've denied my heritage for too long? I have to think about that.
Did you collect the blood price? In gold or blood?
This one shouldn't be here! It was <<1>> who stole from the king, not poor <<2>>!
Too salty. One handful of salt, next time.
I'll wait right here for Talviah. Make sure he's safe.\n\nMeanwhile, you should get back to Orsinium as soon as possible and help Chief Bazrag and the Wood Elf.
The way you defeated those Argonians was so … baronial! Almost balletic, really, a joy to watch! \n\nReady for more?
The relic hunter returns! Tell me, was your search for Uzdabikh's Helm successful? There's a display case just waiting to be filled ….
Graguz laughed every time he stoked the flames. Said we would accept Trinimac when our flesh cooked and our lungs filled with heat. \n\nHe was a little too fond of the fire, if you ask me.
The temple, besieged by weapon-wielding fanatics twice in the same season. It's insane!\n\nKurog has set this avalanche in motion. Now it's up to us to try to stop it.
Isn't my pendant beautiful? Thank you ever so much for returning it to me!

I have nothing to say to you. Or to that conniving witch, Azeeda, either. \n\nBelieve me, I won't dally with another sea trollop ever again. No matter how beautiful she looks or how amazing she smells. Just Alani, from now on.
Malacath whispered of your strength. Those who remain true to the Daedric Prince of Vengeance must band together in these difficult times.\n\nYet they who share our faith now move against us.
If you're not here to help us fight off the Daedra, we have nothing to talk about. Leave my garrison while you've still got legs to carry you.

I must say, you're doing a very respectable job of carving your way through our arenas. \n\nAnd every time you do, it restores the baron who created that arena to the mind of the demiprince. So keep it up.
What are you doing traipsing around down here? Don't you know that Graystone Quarry isn't safe anymore?
Ushang is … eccentric—but he pays well and his totems are always reliable. If you take care of this corruption, I'm sure he'll make it worth your while.
Oh, thank Trinimac! You're not one of those Dwarven-Dwemer things!\n\nBut what are you doing down here? Did you come to help me escape from this damn quarry?
Don't show those bastards in Watcher's Hold any mercy. If one catches fire, you let him burn, all right?
Why are you still here?
We know that Quintus Jarol is dead. The Brotherhood has eyes everywhere.\n\nYou have done well. The covenant is sealed, signed in blood. Welcome to the family, Sister.

Isn't that funny. I was just thinking about you! What brings you to this pious city? No, wait, don't answer that. I don't think I want to know.\n\nOn the other hand, if you're interested in a little mischief, I could really use your help.
You can call <<A:1>> your new home. Look around, if you haven't already. There's plenty of work to be done.

What Anais said … I never realized I had caused her so much pain. I'm not excusing the slavery, mind you, but I didn't want to hurt her. We really were friends once.\n\nThere must be a way to remind her.

Oh, Jone and Jode, a friendly face! For a moment I thought you were another Red Sails extortionist come to get more blood from a stone. \n\nDoesn't take long for pirates to warm up to the idea of tariffs and taxes when they're the ones collecting them.

This place retains memories like my journals hold recollections. Everything we see happened. It seems Lyra did carry out the purification.\n\nLet's press on. We must see everything while the resin still burns.
Cimbar's dead. Do you really think I want to talk to you right now?
You don't know how glad I am to see a friendly face!\n\nYou probably won't believe this, but Kireth and I are in trouble. Again. We could really use your help.

Well, look who it is! Did you get marooned here, too?\n\nNow, before you ask: Yes, we're in trouble again. And no, I don't know how we're going to get out of it. Maybe you can talk to Raynor and help us figure something out?
Those tumblers must be the way inside.\n\nIf we match the proper combination, the doors should unlock.
Shh! It's me!
Who doesn't love a wedding?\n\nYes, nobles forced into political arrangements to secure alliances and land rights. But aside from that.
There's something you need to know about why I'm in Abah's Landing.\n\nWhen we first met, I said I needed a partner to steal the <<1>>. I never explained why. Not really.
<<1>> waits for us, but the doorman won't budge! Perhaps a distraction would bring him from his post?
I'm enjoying this a bit more than I should. To think, <<1>> does this sort of thing all the time.

We should look for ways to cause a distraction. Without <<1>>, we're dead in the water.\n\nDid you know that's an expression in Murkmire for "sleeping while floating on one's back?" Murkmire Argonians are strange people.
It falls on us to do <<1>>'s job for her. As usual.\n\nLook around. There must be something we can do to cause a scene.
Damn it! I should have put it together. <<1>> played us—he played everyone. There was never any "<<2>>" to begin with!

On the other side of Malooc's Path is "<<1>>"—a very fancy name for a big vase. According to the journal, we'll need sacred ashes from inside the vase to reach the treasure vaults.\n\nSo … this is it. We should … we should get going.

This one must respectfully request that you move along. Raz has dangerous business in these ruins and you would just get in Raz's way.\n\nUnless …. You would be willing to help stop a dangerous war criminal, yes?
<<1>> should be in <<c:2>>. Wouldn't keep her waiting.
<<1>>'s in <<c:2>>. Don't keep her waiting.
What are you doing here? Allow me to enjoy my retirement.
Smashing! I always enjoy working with you! We have a certain connection, you and I. Don't you just find it to be so … intense?
I thought <<1>> died here. How could he still be alive?
<<1>> should have known. She should have seen it.
Perhaps <<1>> was wounded. Maybe he's trapped, and needs our help.\n\nOr … well. I'd rather not think of that.
The hideout is just beyond. I would only be underfoot. Meet me here when you have the goods.

I'm surprised at how well Narahni has taken to life in <<c:1>>. She's treating it like another adventure.\n\nHalf the rogues that pass through here come by to talk or have a piece of one of her pies. She's the kindest soul I know.
This one is miserable.
Huh? I didn't do anything. Leave me alone.
Let's get moving. We can't let those Silver Dawn bastards find Hilde before we do.
Good to see you again! Tell that little Nord of yours that she should come by and say hello when she gets a chance.
When I was at <<1>>, I observed your approach from the manor. Not the way I'd have do it, but <<2>> is far more limber.
This is … different from my academy. Very, very different.\n\nEverybody sleeps in. Except for <<1>>, I don't think she ever sleeps.
You filled all fifteen pedestals and completed the Litany of Blood.\n\nThe Listener sent a new book. It's by the statue. I have a feeling it's also for you.

You must have smelled the deliciousness wafting out of my mixing bowl. Doesn't it make your mouth water?\n\nI can't talk right now, though. I have so many wonderful cakes to make! Don't want to disappoint my clients!
Rumor has it the guildmaster is grooming you for big things. Soon you won't bother with petty thieving anymore. It's really going to hurt our numbers.
Find Green-Venom-Tongue at the Sanctuary before he does something foolish. I think if he'll listen to anyone, he'll listen to you.

I need to think about these most recent events. Brothers and Sisters murdered. The priests of Akatosh preaching against us. It's like storm clouds are gathering over the Sanctuary, and I don't like it.\n\nBut you have contracts to deal with, I believe.
I hope your contracts go smoothly, Initiate. Kill well and kill often. Every soul you send to the Void pleases Sithis to no end.
Raz hates quiet in situations like this. Quiet never ends well.\n\nRaz just hopes the targets are still alive so we can rescue them. Tread carefully, sharp-claw.
I have an urge to just cut this woman's throat and be done with this, but I suppose we should find the missing targets first.
You helped bring Hilde back. I owe you for that. Thank you.
Until word comes back from the Black Hand, there's little we can do about Artorius or his Black Dragon.\n\nDeal with your contracts until I hear from the Speaker, Assassin.
Thank you for helping me see that I do belong here. That I belong with my family.
<The statue stands before you, silent and unfathomable.>
Thank you for helping me reach the shrine. I would not have been able to do it without you.
You have come to us at a terrible time. Elinhir lies in ruins at the hands of wicked mages.

You there. You look like you know what you're doing, and that's just what I need right now.\n\nSee that large staff sticking out of the ground? It's emitting magical energy at unprecedented levels. If we don't stop it, it's going to explode.
You will recognize the places where the magicka seeps through by the atronachs and spellfiends that are drawn to the power.
We would accompany you, but the danger is too great.\n\nThe Scaled One already holds most of our power. You would not wish to face him if he held all of it.

Well, the armorer and her trolls certainly put up a fight. Alternate plan, indeed!\n\nThe runescriber should be on the western side of the valley, making his wriggly, squiggly patterns. Wait until you see them. Kind of pretty.
I'll meet you inside the cave known as Serpent's Nest. From there, we'll go together to save the prisoners and eliminate the progenitor mantikora.

Ah, I see my message reached you. Have you encountered Kelmen in your travels by any chance?\n\nThe Thief reported a magical disturbance around Skyreach. Kelmen went in search of an old Mages Guild associate working in the area. He has yet to return.
Please, I must hear what transpires.
Would you help me? I know it might seem presumptuous but I need someone who can come and go freely from Sadrith Mora.\n\nAnd I can pay you!
Let's meet back here after you acquire the clothes and the key. Then we'll free the rest of the prisoners and make our escape.
I hope you enjoyed your time at Alcaire Castle. A shame I did not see for myself!
Walk with Sithis, my friend—and mind the Telvanni. They spin lies like an elder at the yarn-wheel.
Ah, love! How cruel the fates that keep me from my heart's desire and force me to lock away my true feelings. Chains bind my heart, yet it yearns to beat free!

You need to get the key to the construction site from the Overseer or you won't be able to get the Blessing Stone.\n\nThe energy in the stone won't fully restore Lord Vivec, but it should allow him to keep Vvardenfell safe for a while longer.
I know deception doesn't come easily to everyone. Just allow this Nerandas fellow do all the talking. Hlaalu agents tend to be chatty. It's one of their many, many shortcomings.
Did you find the deed? I'd hate to think that clumsy wizard, Jinrisa, outnixed me on this.
She is always busy these days. I worry she flirts with the flames of the sun and does not know to fear the fire.
I can't decide what's more satisfying—the thought of him making a public apology, or the thought of him curled up in a ball, sneezing his brains out.
I don't have time to speak to strangers, stranger.\n\nI need to get these imbeciles moving so I can get my property back!
Get away from me, you … you wretched scamp!

The task I've set before you won't be easy. These shrines lie near and far. Some are little more than piles of brickwork, while others extend deep underground.\n\nEven so, I'm confident you'll find what I'm looking for—the Stones of Cold Fire.

Constable Kren will snatch up a bribe without batting an eye. If you're short on coin, try convincing Suran's locksmith, Remas, to cut you a deal. Or you could talk to Dredyni down at Desele's. She might know something. Just be discreet, all right?
I'm sorry to have doubted you.\n\nWe've still yet to hear from House Redoran. If you hadn't gone in there, these people might not still live. My thanks to you.

I was wondering where you'd gotten off to. Thought you might have moved on. I certainly wouldn't blame you. Between Manore and this owl-brained Telvanni, I'm about ready to head back to Skyrim myself.\n\nHow're things in the mine?

My divine energy diminishes with every passing moment, but the ritual confirmed my affliction is not natural.\n\nI regret that I could not reveal the full nature of these dire circumstances until your trustworthiness had been demonstrated.
No boils or coughing, it looks like. Can I assume you were victorious then?
After taking a longer look at the documents you brought back, I have to agree with your assessment. The Ashlander Chodala has somehow siphoned divine energy away from Lord Vivec.
Me, among all these fine people! When I received Lord Vivec's summons, I didn't even change my clothes! I feel honored and embarrassed all at once!

If this creature is of the dreugh, it may share their weaknesses. I will consult our Wise Women, they may know something that will aid you in this hunt.\n\nConvince the pawns of the Three of what you have found. I will meet you at the mine's entrance.

Avoid killing the Ashlanders, unless they give you no choice. I don't need you starting a blood feud with my forces split.\n\nNow, I must be off to hold the heroic line, at a deeply fishy mine. Such is the life of a Buoyant Armiger.
Do be careful with Vigard. He lacks self-confidence. If he suspects we're using him to put a creature to sleep, he'll probably run off sobbing.
Have you and Narsis finished exploring the tomb yet? I can't wait to hear all about his amazing discoveries!
I'm just guessing, mind you, but I dare say that skull belonged to a son or grandson of Saint Veloth! What a spectacular discovery!
Ah, I remember! The components for the tonal inverter! Were you able to acquire them?

Here we are, on the Furious One's bloody doorstep, preparing to enter a Daedric ruin to try to stop my brother's march toward power.\n\nI hope that device you mentioned really can counter the invulnerability granted by the staff, Sunna'rah.
You don't appear to be holding my drink, so I'm sure I have no interest in you. Off with you.

Well, that's quite a bundle you're carrying. Some sort of plant, broken weapons … are those guar bones? Never mind.\n\nJust take those gifts to the tribes as quick as you can. Ashlanders hate waiting.
Fine work retrieving the device! Good help is so hard to find … no offense, Vimy.\n\nNow, the control rod, if you please.

You're not one of Lenarmen's thugs, are you? No, you look too smart for that.\n\nFull disclosure—this place is crawling with mercenaries and automata. I wouldn't linger if I were you. Unless you're the adventurous type, of course.
I'm sorry, but I'm up to my elbows in an important matter at the moment. \n\nI'm sure someone else in the kinhouse can help you if your need is urgent.
Always a pleasure to see you, sera. I'm glad you dropped by. I could use a friend right now.
My, you look like a well-traveled individual! If you're looking to give your mount a well-deserved rest, you've come to the right place.\n\nWe know how to pamper a loyal guar in Balmora.
Be on your way.
I'll slow down the main contingent of Redoran forces while you lead Veya out through the back tunnels. I'll find you once we're all clear of the House soldiers and their Khajiit mercenaries.
Unfortunately, the wreck of the vessel provided no additional clues. Were you able to discover anything during your investigation?
I feel as if my heart is breaking. How could I let him leave me?

Excellent! Let's start with a simple one. Head north of Vivec and travel to the Othrelas Ancestral Tomb. Look for a stone plaque near the tomb and take a rubbing of the words inscribed upon it.\n\nReturn to me with the rubbing and … well, you'll see.
I can't believe this! Why allow the Warclaws to run roughshod over the camp like this? What's House Redoran thinking?\n\nAnd what in the name of the Three have they done with the Ashlanders?
You had to kill a soldier, didn't you? I don't have a writ to account for that body! This reflects poorly on me and my abilities.\n\nThanks for making this more difficult than it already was.
Our show will be moving on soon, perhaps you'd like to continue your mission of merriment as part of our entourage?

So, the Twilight Queen's enemies lurk in Shadowfen. \n\nMy fellow oracles and I will prepare to travel at once. Between your strength and our sight, these monsters don't stand a chance. See you there.
Now that you have hogged all the glory here, I think we will be taking this party elsewhere. Will you follow our folly of fools down this honorous path?
My subjects await! \n\nJust try not to light anyone important on fire. I'll never hear the end of it.
You'll never understand the Battleground until you see the games firsthand. Get out there and participate!
Never mind me. I'm just in a foul mood.\n\nSee what you can find in the cellars. I'll work on opening this door.

I blame the Investigator Vale books I lent to Stibbons. He was never this adventurous before he became enchanted with her admittedly thrilling stories.\n\nBut what are you still doing here? I thought you were going to find Stibbons and the mages?
Should we follow her? Oh dear. What would Investigator Vale do in this situation?\n\nI know! I'll just wait here and let you see where she's rushing off to.
Look at the craftsmanship. The attention to detail. Sotha Sil is a true master. Amazing, isn't it? Such intricate work on something so small.\n\nWell, are you ready to go inside?
I received a report of a recent assassination. Councilor Dolvara. It was a legal writ carried out by Naryu Virian.\n\nNo sign of Veya, but they did see you.
Barbas … pet hound of the Prince of Bargains. I should have known.\n\nTalk to the Ashlander while I … compose myself.

Welcome back. I was just having a little chat with former-chancellor Gascone. He insists he's told me everything, but I know him well enough to know he's still hiding something.\n\nHonestly, I can barely stand to look at him.
I wasn't fast enough …. Damn it all!\n\nDid you see what happened here? Was it his shadow?

The images revealed by the Obscuros leave little room for doubt—the Daedric artifact we seek is somewhere inside the Clockwork City. Why would Sotha Sil allow such an item to enter his domain?\n\nI fear that something terrible has happened.
Don't even think about taking anything. I may not be an Apostle anymore, but I can still jolt you with enough lightning to cook the meat from your bones.

Slag Town is no wildflower meadow, but we find some modest joys. Fellowship keeps our eyes above water. Watching out for one another, you see?\n\nSo long as you remain a friend, we will watch out for you too.
You returned! I must admit, I wasn't sure you'd be able to do that. Do you have the perception tabulator? And what of Acolyte Variah? Were you able to locate her in there?
Tighten that armor and sharpen your weapons. Entering the Cogitum Centralis can prove deadly on the best of days. This is far from the best of days.
I don't feel perfectly aligned with sneaking into Lector Naril's private workshop, but we need to determine the truth about the apprentices that entered the Wellspring after Gathal died.
What are you waiting for? Go! After the shadow!
Now that we've returned the stars and recovered the memory fragments, the Astronomer can use the mnemograph here to play the full memory back. I'm rather curious about its contents.
Go on. Get going! I'll move on Baldan as soon as you're in position.

There you are. I prepared the device. All is in readiness. Prepared to see through the eyes of a clockwork automaton? Brilliant!\n\nJust activate the skeevaton, place it in the serviflume, and I'll instruct you further.
Brilliant! We really made short work of those spiders, didn't we?\n\nHere, you can carry the oil.
Isn't there some other adventure you should be off to?

While you investigate and acquire this lamp, I will make sure Sil stays off your scent. Keeping secrets in the Brass Fortress requires a spider's cunning and god-like vigilance. Luckily, you have me.\n\nFind Neramo and bring me that light.
The prisoner. At last.\n\nYou are early … or perhaps late. It makes little difference. I'm glad you've come. Tamriel owes you a debt.
We may have a complication.\n\nMy, my. This would be much easier if you had feathers ….
Hello again, friend! Don't mind the smell, just baking up a sort of clay soufflé. \n\nI, uh, am really scraping the bottom of the ingredient barrel right now. Any luck with those mushrooms?
I overheard you talking to Bren about the Root Liqueur and I had to intervene before you took off on some wild guar chase.
A manual override is required to proceed. Lower automata still adhere to trespass protocols. Use caution.
Just get the key so we can get out of here.
Do hurry up and install the integral of memory. I can barely contain my excitement!

There are a number of locations I want to examine. I added them to your map. Lead on and I will follow.\n\nDon't worry, I'll provide any assistance I can, but I have to admit I'm not much of a fighter. That's more Kireth's area of expertise.
Your concern for Tarnished is unusual, but appreciated. She will be fine once the heaving is through.
The oil, it's … ugh, it's coating my tongue. I can't get the taste out—ugh. I can't get it out of my—ulp!

A beautiful Psijic mage. Very interesting. Raz's instincts say that this situation troubles her, but she isn't afraid. Still, to draw the Psijics out of hiding after all this time ….\n\nGo meet Valsirenn at the Coral Forest. Raz will catch up.
It looks like you found items with ties to the Wyrd elements. Shall we proceed with Marieve's ritual?
Thanks again for helping me. Even though I foresaw your actions, you still had to make the decision to follow that path.
You take the lead. My combat spells are extremely limited. Just stay alert. We don't know what the Aldarch and the Kinlady are doing out here.

Thank you for returning so promptly. Before we get to other matters, tell me about your search for the tower sentinels. Valsirenn recounted the events at the College of Sapiarchs after she returned with Leythen, but I'm eager to hear your report.
Welcome to Lillandril. I do hope you won't follow this young docent's example and start hurling wild accusations about Sapiarch laws and customs. That would go poorly. For everyone.

Thank you for keeping an open mind.\n\nI promise, once you look into the details of this mess you'll see that Emile's innocent. With any luck, we'll clear his name. We might even teach the Sapiarchs a lesson in humility. Wouldn't that be nice.

I trust you were successful? My own inquiries were fruitful. I've learned where we must go next in this investigation.\n\nBut wait, I'm getting ahead of myself. Did you manage to break Galidor's wards? What did you find?
An alliance of Daedric Princes cavorting with a cabal of Sea Sload. Unheard of!
So you're the one that Valsirenn has been talking about, the same person I met back at the ruins in Summerset? What brings you to Ceporah Tower, my friend?
You're back, and so is Pavo! Look, I think you are onto something. More pages appeared in the book.
I do hope my journal is helpful. I'd never write down anything improper, so don't worry about my privacy. All that's important now is learning as much as you can about Larydel.

I seem to recall asking you not to come. I'm sorry, but I can't allow you to take the stage. I'll publicly withdraw my sponsorship if I have to.\n\nHowever … is everything with Rinyde all right? Did you come here to tell me something?
No mask? Really? Or is that just amazingly lifelike?\n\nNo matter. To each his own! You're here to play the Game of Boasts, aren't you? First, we must perform together!
Watch out for the workers and the warriors! They're always trying to ruin our fun!
Talk to that apraxic witch if you must. Personally, I'm done with this place.
Let's get to work on this curse! I've had enough begging for one lifetime. Just look at my knees! It will take days to wash out these stains!

Little busy at the moment … you know, now's not the time to be wandering around, what with the gruesome killings and clueless investigators. Could wind up dead, or answering questions until you wish you were.
I'm already recovering, but I might not be much good in a fight. Clear the bridge and I'll be right behind you.
I can't for the life of me figure out Glardir's persona. She's clearly some sort of troubadour. Or a playwright perhaps? We'll sort it out. We have to.
Who are you? One of Erudil's boring friends?\n\nHe's insufferable, that one! Not a scrap of drama to be found in that hollow bonce of his!
Grand Maestro Forte's here as well? Why, this just gets more curious by the minute. Come, let's speak with him.
So much for enlisting the help of other keepers. I just hope Elise's encounter with the lions will make her more cautious.\n\nRunning off like that isn't a promising start. What was her hurry anyway?
Now, you leave that bloom alone! It's very fragile!

Urlsar and his storm lie beyond this gate. No matter what happens, I want to thank you for standing by me. If it weren't for you I might never have gotten to see Castire again. If this is goodbye, at least it'll be one with closure.
May Mother Sea embrace you kindly until we meet again.
The crows serve as Nocturnal's eyes. She watches us through these annoying little creatures.\n\nThere's nothing to do about it except to keep moving forward until we find the hiding place.
I'm worried about Iachesis. He's still as weary as the moment when we first entered this damned realm.

Talking birds and half-naked Daedra. Now this is a realm I could get used to!\n\nI mean, except for the birds. And the fact that the half-naked Daedra want to kill us. But hey, it's better than most realms I've been trapped in.
This is a message. Everything in this room—it's all meant to tell us something. What's that on the wall?
Oh, did I forget to mention? I'm afraid we can't allow the Psijic Codex to leave Artaeum. No, it's far too important for that! Feel free to take some notes though.
So Tarnamir recruited you, eh? Well, I suppose we'll just have to make the best of it. \n\nFollow our instructions and we'll get along fine. You might even learn a thing or two.
Zaan the Scalecaller. They've taken over her temple, begun to invoke her name. I fear that these facts are no mere coincidence. This cult must be worshiping her, in some fashion. \n\nBut why?
I hate to say it, but I think your friend Valsirenn has lost it. She—well, you should go to her study and see for yourself.
Help Darien and Raz protect the ritual platforms. I'll do what I can here.
Courtier Vindilween told me who she sent you to talk to, and Rigurt always wanted to meet a famous High Elf thespian!\n\nLady Enigma, greetings and sanitations from the Nord Cultural Exchange.
Did I see you with that … that … Nord? You really need to reconsider the company you keep.
Those lions crept up on me while I was distracted. Thought I was done for.\n\nWho are you anyway? Some friend of Talomar's?
I have no idea what's happening here, but I'm sure I'm not going to like it. Go, talk to Tableau. Perhaps you can help make sense of this farce.

I've finally girded myself with the courage of my forefathers. I'm prepared to add my deeds to theirs, even if it means entering Oblivion itself! I will find Naliara!\n\nYou … haven't seen her, have you?
I was just on my way to deal with something for the Ritemaster when you happened by. Your timing is perfect as always, my friend!\n\nCare to lend me a hand?
If the Sapiarchs came to the Illumination Academy, someone in the guest wing must have seen them.

I never expected Eslion to show his face willingly around here again. Your search must have spooked him out of hiding.\n\nHe came here with his head bowed, hoping I'd overlook his transgressions. He can take his pleas to the court.

Hope those stranglers didn't hurt you! They're ornery buggers. Nearly ate my fool cousin one time, but he was so drunk—no, never mind, not the time.\n\nAs you can see, there's a bit of an infestation. Real mess. Has me a bit at a loss.
It gladdens my heart to see you awake and free, my friend. You're the first to respond to my help and escape from that entity's grasp.
I don't think that was one of your vagrant friends.
There's my favorite second. Feels like I've been warming these knuckles up for hours!\n\nSo, what's the story? That scrawny prig accept my challenge?
I honestly can't fathom why you're helping that tusk-faced brute. Some kind of misguided charity mission? These nebarra are like idiot children, friend. If you want to train something, get a dog.
Silence is golden. Be on your way, please.
I suspect that whatever has kept the shadow creatures at bay might also reveal our next path. Let's look around.
That should do it. I just need a crank, a rope, and some ballista bolts!

I'm afraid we still have work to do. While the Crystal Tower is protected against Daedra, any mortal can now walk right through its gates. \n\nWe must convince the Sapiarchs to gather allies in order to defend the Crystal-Like-Law.
Renzir sees you have his shipments, but no Nubani by your side. Did you not find her?
Pardon my presumption, but you're the newcomer who saved the Crystal Tower, aren't you?

It's good to see you again! Thanks for rescuing me and my companions from that insidious mind trap.\n\nBy the way, if you're working with these smugglers now, you should know that I deprived a number of them of their existence.
Are you one of those double-dealing smugglers? I'm going to take a chance and assume you're not, because I really need you to get me out of these chains. You know, before the big slug notices me.

Ah, initiate. What a welcome diversion.\n\nI assume Josajeh told you that our scryers are well on their way to locating the last four fragments of the staff. We have you to thank. Now then, can I help you with something?

The magic that went into creating this mind trap is truly remarkable. An opportunity to learn something new comes along so rarely in the realm of arcane academia.\n\nBut where are my manners? What part of my memories brought you into existence?
Take your pewter dust to any jewelry station. There, it can be refined into the ounces you require.
Pay no mind to the Argonian. She's so far gone she's practically out of my jurisdiction.
Hey! Hey, it's you. The … person I like. Wait … do I like you? I can't remember. Doesn't matter! I can like anybody right now! Even this stick in the mud! Help me loosen him up!
Did the Loremaster give you your next task? You should probably go speak to him.
Oh, it's you. I assume the Loremaster sent you to collect your things for the trip to Craglorn?
I understand that you entered into an arrangement with the Augur, but an object like that—particularly an object with its … unique disposition—cannot roam free.\n\nI am sorry.

<<1>>'s down by the water, working on his boat. He should be able to point you to the Argonians most likely to possess the knowledge that Margus needs.\n\nGet to them and find out what Margus questioned them about.
Vykosa awaits us just ahead. It's time to finally end this.

Let me see that. This is a Ninth Legion officer's journal! It mentions my ancestor, Gin-Rajul. And how the Legionnaires started disappearing.\n\nIt had to be the Wuju-Ka! It must have devoured the Imperials.

Life here is so very different from the way things work in Murkmire. I never realized how many Argonians have such a terrible existence. And now the Blackguards are just making things worse!\n\nWere you able to talk to the Argonians I suggested?
We set sail soon.\n\nOnce again, if you wish to make the journey overland, I won't stop you. Just try to move swiftly. Time is not something we have in abundance.
You're back! Excellent! Did you find Xukas? Any word on my missing explorers?
Best speak with Famia before she passes out. This one told her to lay off the fried wamasu, but some people enjoy being round and slow, yes?

History. Can we truly discover the truth of the past, or are we forced to view it through the eyes of the victors, the survivors, and the silver-tongued poets ….\n\nForgive me. My passion for historical knowledge often overwhelms me.
How's it coming with those remains? Famia's going to be disappointed if we can't verify her theories.

I state the obvious. You are ojel, not of our tribe. Coming here makes you either very brave or very foolish, but it has nothing to do with me.\n\nI display my fangs in warning. Now leave me to my thoughts.
A handful of Dead-Water kaals arrived just before you returned. Friend-Jaxsik is among them.\n\nI think they gather just north of the tree.

Jaxsik-Orrn, daughter and kaal of the Dead-Water tribe, will ride on a boat with the lukiul Kassandra. I shake my head.\n\nYesterday, Tsojei and I would have tried to kill all but one of you. The Hist makes fools of us all, I think.
We are in the den of the Veeskhleel now. My spines quake at the thought of what we will find in this place.

This is not a simple matter, nor a matter to be rushed. Take all the time you need.\n\nHaxara and Iskenaaz will both want to plead their case to you, but I will understand if you do not wish your judgment to be swayed.
You shouldn't have killed his people! Now he's going to kill and eat us—not necessarily in that order!
I hate to bother, friend-partner, but you have been gone for a long time. Are the frogs giving you any trouble? I only ask because striking a deal with Captain Jimila is terribly important to me.
Ah, sun's blessings, beeko. You come to discuss friend-Famia's missing explorers, yes?
Remember, vakka stones are bright yellow, like these on the sconces. But an empowered one will glow like the sun. Good luck!
It seems my friend, Jaxsik, has been playing with her food. You should speak to her before she does something stupid.
So many questions. It is a wonder you do not pass out from all the air you expend.
We can't let Ree-Nakal do this to anyone else.\n\nNo one should have to feel this kind of pain.
The Swallowed Grove, eh? Looks like I'll be adding a few scars to my collection.
I loosen my lungs. It is good to see you, sword-kin.\n\nTsojei screams the victory chant. You reclaimed the Remnant, is it not so?
Everything about this Remnant is so fascinating, wouldn't you say?

I overheard what the next arena is, and I don't like it one bit. They're going to have you fight all the champions from the first three arenas. At the same time!\n\nI knew the Blackguards were rotten, but this is just going too far.
The ritual worked! The Xinchei-Konu has regained its power once more.
I tell a truthful statement. I am a warrior of the Naga-Kur tribe. In your silly tongue, you'd say the Dead-Water. Now you know the truth of such things.
Huh? Ah, good-good day, traveler! Is there some-something that I can, ah, help you with?
The midge lingers. Do you seek anything else?
By your hands, my traveling has come to an end. \n\nThank you. A foolish thought, perhaps, but I feel … I feel as though a piece of my tribe is now a part of this village.
Have you any other questions for me? I am honor-bound to answer all who wish to learn of Sithis.
It's good to see you, beek-ojel. I have not forgotten your freeing me from the Blackguards.\n\nWhat brings you to Dead-Water Village?
I pulled all these parts and not one is what we need? Well that just figures.
Now we need to locate a waterfall. Go on, don't wait for me. I'll catch up.
How typical! Stibbons got himself into the mud without any help, but now he can't seem to extract himself.\n\nBe a dear and see if you can get him unstuck.
The root bleeds slow and dry, but this is definitely deep sap. We Bright-Throats use this in our dream-wallows. I think this is no coincidence.

The Wither-Vault is well north of the village. I would guide you, but my knees grow stiff as kindling-wood. Little Xukas can aid you, I have no doubt.\n\nBe warned. Even Bright-Throats, who know the mire like their own scales, face danger there.

Normally the Black-Tongue tribe are eager to participate—many a Bright-Throat can call the Black-Tongues their root-kin—but the only thing Waku-Mat has been quick to provide today are excuses. I hope he'll be more forthcoming with you.
Hurry, five-claw! Show my people that these creatures bleed. Show them that they die!
Ah, five-claw, just in time. Khamira told you what to do, yes?

Zamarak remembers Hursh. A rashness bubbles beneath his bravado. He is capable of doing something foolish regarding the Euraxians.\n\nThis one wonders what the soldiers search for though. What could the fields contain that they should care about?
