Hrrm. Who knew that being the queen would mean spending all my time in the palace? I envy you and Tharn, running around and getting into the thick of things.\n\nMake sure to keep me informed of your progress, five-claw.
Well? What say you? Do you agree with the speaker's agent or do you have a modicum of intelligence and compassion?\n\nDon't you see? We need to end this bloody conflict, one way or another.

I'm a reasonable man. I have no great love for this land, but neither do I want to see it destroyed. Dragons were the last straw. In other words, this is me making a stand.\n\nYou can find a copy of the Dragonguard report in my office upstairs.
Headed into Darkpool Mine? Good! For me, I mean. Not for … I mean, maybe for you, too. Who knows?\n\nMara'dahni could really use a strong set of claws.
Hold there, poacher! One more step, and my sweet boy will tear you apart!\n\nCome on, Milksop! Get up! Ah! You're useless.
Move, five-claw! We have to stop Saulinia!
If you find any research notes, please gather them for further study. The more we can understand what happened here, the better our chances to heal this land.

Please, walker. If there is any way to spare Hulzar, have mercy. Vazbi knows he is mad, but to lose two fathers at once …. S'rendarr help me. This one is so lost.\n\nMoons, why did Silhu-jo come here? He must have known the Stricken would kill him!

I must admit, your help was immeasurable out there. I had my hands full countering my half-sister's defenses. And when Nala-do fell, Khamira became useless for all intents and purposes.\n\nYou did … you did well. Considering.
Cadwell keeps moving around. He won't stand still long enough for me to cast a scrying spell. Talk to him and see if you can distract him.

I remember Aneshi. He and his wife were kind to me and they served my parents well.\n\nTell him that Khamira lives and plans to take back our kingdom. He will provide the information we need after that.
Zamarak does not like the idea of Queen Khamira going off alone with just Abnur Tharn to protect her.
Our people have someone to fight for, and that makes Nala-do purr with contentment.\n\nBut there is still much to do before Anequina is free.
Well, it seems we've confirmed that Feina-Darak is a descendant of the Potentate. Just in time for her to be whisked away by some vengeful spirit.\n\nJust my luck.
I may be weak, but I still have a few battles left in these old bones … or whatever stuff it is I'm actually made of.\n\nIf we can restore some of my energy, though, I'll be ever so grateful.
So, it appears that your stranger friend is Rideza the Rogue. Good to know.

The Betrayer attuned himself and hoped to align the Moons as Anequina did, but the Moon-Priests and the remaining champions stopped him. Now I see how he planned to do it. It is so simple!\n\nHurry, we have one more relic to activate.
He did it. Everything Tasnasi suspected him of. He killed Dasalzo. He had her take the blame. He was proud of it.\n\nNow that I have my claws at his throat he discovers the meaning of mercy.

I'm no healer, but even I can tell Nazdar's really ground his gears this time … maybe lost a few bearings while he was at it. The body's not so different from a machine, when you think about it. I can patch him up, I'm sure of it.
If Tasnasi's been taken, it won't be long before Khasda kills her.\n\nYou're the only one that can do something about it!
If Nazdar's body did not protest … if he had been a few years younger, she would not be in such danger. Forgive him. Please, find Tasnasi.
Oh, what could have happened to this one's sweet daughter?
Five-claw, we stand on the sacred Plane of Jode. The Dragons went down into the processional. They seek to breach Jode's Core.
You did what I could not, walker. Rakazsa is gone and his misguided beliefs along with him. I only wish the lesson hadn't come at so great a price.
Queen Khamira, attuned to the Lunar Lattice. Zamarak never expected to see such a miracle in his lifetime.\n\nThis one prays that it will be enough when we stand against the Dragons.
A direct hit! But why are you talking to me? Go finish off the Dragon!
Even I, a faithful servant of Azura, can't open a door bearing her likeness. More than a little frustrating, I can tell you.
You asked for a means to destroy Arum-Khal. It rests in the arms of Shando-ri. Take it, child.

So, Arum-Khal's orbs lead to a shadow realm of some kind? Moons' mercy. Is he so desperate to be free of Azurah—to be free of us—that he would cast himself into a prison of his own making?\n\nEnough of that. How can we strengthen the blade?
The farm is just up the road, north of here. And don't worry if Mother seems cross. Rakhzargo's brother came home for a visit and they have been arguing.
Kideya means no rudeness, but she hasn't time for visitors today. Best to seek company elsewhere, yes?
Best prepare yourself, five-claw. Whatever is on the other side of this tunnel is unlikely to be particularly welcoming.

I've spotted Dragons circling in the distance from time to time, but it doesn't look like the winged monster that attacked the camp will return today.\n\nWas your hunt successful? Did you recover the documents that Khamira sought?

Hello! Have you come to pay your respects to this poor fellow, too?\n\nIt was the strangest thing. I was looking at this very gravestone in a dream. So here I came and there it is, all solid and everything!

It may be hard to see, but the Khajiiti merchants struggle to keep their stalls open while the less-bestial business people rake in the profits.\n\nEuraxia would have you believe it's a matter of work ethic, but we know better.
I don't care if he is the avatar of a trickster god. If that muskarse thinks he can just steal the Rithana-di-Renada again, he has another thing coming.
Iraya believes the mural can actually sing? Bah. My sister takes the old tales far too literally.
I can't say I'm surprised Selene tried to take a swipe at Carindon. Thank you for keeping the peace.
Ah. Jora-ri feels at home again. Place his urn with the others.
The Moons sent Zamarak back home for a purpose. This one will make sure Queen Khamira's reign lasts long and proves fruitful.\n\nThis Zamarak swears.
I informed Gharesh-ri and Khamira about what happened in Rimmen. They're mobilizing our remaining forces even as we speak.\n\nNow tell me, what did you learn at the Desert Wind Adeptorium?

Hello! Come to partake in a before-the-battle cleansing? I find it prudent to make myself pristine prior to the start of a slaughter.\n\nIn my experience, the subsequent blood and gore adheres much better to a well-laundered body.
Why, hello! You do get around, don't you? I don't suppose you'd be interested in more work? This time the crisis at hand involves Dragons. We need them dead. Care to learn more?
Without you, I would have lost my best friend. Actually, my only friend. Honestly, we don't even get along very well.
There's an extra Peryite cultist outfit if you're interested. I'm fairly certain that I got all of the plague stains out of it.
You know, Fez still hasn't told us where the jewel is. Not trying to insinuate anything. Just an observation.
This one saw no guards as we left Rimmen, which tells Ak'an you kept your mouth shut. Good. Ak'an's list of enemies grows far too long.
Is what Ak'an says true? Do you find common cause with the Breton, Jakarn?\n\nI should warn you—people who travel with Jakarn rarely meet pleasant ends.

If you speak to the powerful Tharn while you're at the palace, let him know that Lyrrsazhi has been thinking about him. Isn't he just delicious? Like a honey pudding, he is!\n\nAnyway, the queen awaits you in the palace throne room.
Not a moment to lose, friend. Let's go save these animals!

Did you hear that, friend? Asaldak wants to know Rigurt's recipe! ! I'm sure he'll return after he wins his digestive battle.\n\nFind the Screaming Mammoths at Valenwood Gate so they can play for Lady Izza. We are finally on the verge of making peace.
Hit this dummy! Pretend it's someone you really hate. Or really love. Or both!
I hope that dispelled any doubts you had that Selene is not to be trusted. Remain on your guard. If she worms her way into the Bosmers' minds, they'll turn on us the first chance they get.
Now what has Allanwen signed me up for? I'm not sure what Selene means by draw on me, but I hope it doesn't involve giant spider fangs.\n\nAt least she asked first?
Carindon's attack dogs. Twice now you've made me his prisoner.
The ritual sites take precedence over removing the island's defenses. Whatever Kaalgrontiid hopes to gain, it seems only prudent that we put an end to the rituals.

It is good to see you again, warrior. I want to thank you once more for protecting our abbey the night that Mannimarco attacked. The fire of my gratitude still burns bright.\n\nAh, but I digress. I have need of your aid once more.
Once you return the bell, Tadali will call the winds of Khenarthi to lead you to what you seek. Should all go well, they will take you to this Dragon.
We're lucky that Za'ji's mother is so forgiving. After everything he's done, I'm surprised she hasn't thrown us all out of this temple.
The archives must contain information about the Horn of Ja'darri. Let's see if we can find anything useful in these stacks.
Tharn's stamina isn't as robust as I remember, but I'll never forget that acerbic tone.\n\nOnce inside, we'll need all our talents to navigate this nest of vipers, so stay alert.
Start on the ledge of the building behind us. Merely follow the grappling points until you reach the roof of the training hall.\n\nGood luck, warrior. And please, try not to injure yourself.
Ka'ishka wants nothing more than to shrink from it, yet she cannot look away. How can something be so terrible and beautiful at the same time?
The blood of my beloved made such a lovely speech. Now your tale will be spread far and wide.\n\nBut could she have not spared at least a word or two about the humble Khunzar-ri?
While I question the accuracy of this map, it's the only lead we have. We may as well follow it.
We came all this way. You might as well see what's inside.
The cavern passage lies to the northeast. See where it leads and prepare to defend yourself. We have no idea what dangers lurk on this island.
Adara'hai hasn't heard the Heart of Lorkhaj beat so forcefully in her head. Not since …. \n\nDon't worry, she just needs a moment to clear her head. We'll see you at Vijari's.

This cult recruiter expects you to prove yourself, and that won't be easy in the Black Kiergo. Fighters from all over Tamriel come to test their skills in that arena.\n\nNot that any of them were ever a match for me.
Oh dear, oh dear. What will we do now?
Why do you linger? Daini will be along soon. See to my brother, yes? South, past the walls. You cannot miss him.

What began in Anequina ends in the sky over Pellitine. I sense … power. A vast supply, building like a storm at the island's heart. Kaalgrontiid is close to achieving his terrible goal.\n\nLuckily, Nahfahlaar had the foresight to meet us here.
We stopped Kaalgrontiid and saved Elsweyr. Not a bad start for our new Dragonguard, right, my friend?\n\nI just wish Abnur Tharn were here to celebrate our victory.
Sai told us what happened. Za'ji is sorry he missed all the excitement.\n\nWell, not that sorry.
I heard the aeonstone shard cracking all the way down in Senchal! I wish I could have been up there with you. The battle must have been glorious!

My father and the Shields maintained order in Senchal while we made sure none of the remaining Dragons attacked. I understand we have you to thank for saving us.\n\nI'm sorry about your friend, though. Abnur Tharn was a legend.
I need to speak to Sai Sahan immediately. If Senchal is in danger—well, more danger than usual—I want to hear that directly from the Dragonguard's mouth.
Take it from me, walker. Don't fall in love with pretty, blue-eyed sweetmeats. It only leads to heartbreak.
Usually Za'ji is the one who does the talking, but his spellwork is a tad rusty. This one will keep the muskarse floating while you do the questioning.
First, our ship is stolen. Then, before we even know where it is, Za'ji agrees to sail a stranger to a Dragon's island.\n\nI should have just rolled over and gone back to sleep this morning.
Honor and faith, wayfarer.\n\nBlademaster Kasura awaits you at the Rosy Lion in the city of Daggerfall. She heard tales of your Dragon slaying skills and requests to meet you at once.
Let's make haste to the temple and find this Clan Mother.

Your order may not have the power or skill of the Dragonguard of old, but our alliance has proven far more useful. Laatvulon is destroyed. He shall never rise to face me again.\n\nVomindok fez. An unexpected outcome.

Bebbia feared that the damage to Khajiit of the Moons would be beyond repair, but now she dares to hope that we can do this, zha'al. Senchal's crowning jewel will shine once more and the city will soon follow.

Those poles certainly look like grappling points, don't they?\n\nPerhaps that's how we make our way across the cavern. Or, should I say that's how you make your way across the cavern. We only have the one.

You again! I'd recognize that sense of … style anywhere. It seems we're both far from Abah's Landing now and better for it.\n\nI'll be assisting in this restoration project, provided we acquire anything to be restored. A talent of yours, I recall.
All right, let's talk. What did you find in Auberic's house? Is this stinking event what I think it is?
Sidura told you all she knows. Speak to Sai Sahan if you want more information.

Ja'darri joined the Dragonguard to take down a fearsome Dragon. The Pride of Alkosh called him the Demon from the East, while the Dragonguard named him the Black Beast. \n\nBut his true name is Laatvulon.
Maezi will be all right. She has to be. She's strong and brave …. She's the best thing about my otherwise disastrous time in Elsweyr.
Yet another obstacle. Ironic how my order's defenses are preventing us from dealing with the true villains.\n\nPerhaps one day we'll look back on this farce and laugh …. No, of course we won't.

Lyris and the Vestige, together again. We should really stop meeting like this, you know?\n\nLet's make a deal. Next time, no fighting. We tear up a mead hall and drink until dawn. First round's on me. All other rounds are on the Prophet.
I agree with Nahfahlaar and Queen Khamira. Destroying the stones at these focal points seems our most prudent course of action.\n\nLet's get to it.

Why must sewers always smell so bad? When we find Ironbelly, I'm going to cave in his head for dragging us down here.\n\nMy armor will never be mistaken for a bed of roses, but sewer stink lingers like Thane Jeggi around the mead hall.
We can't stop that storm unless we deal with Matron Urgala! She won't stand aside, so you need to kill her!
We need to test the elixir, but maybe we can put an end to the Gray Host here and now by taking out two more of its leaders.\n\nIt's a long shot, I know, but we have to try.

So this is the place. The Undergrove. According to the orders you found, the Gray Host is experimenting with harrowstorms in there.\n\nAh, you should go first. Then we'll find a spot to test the elixir.
Two Gray Host leaders. This is an opportunity we can't let slip away.

Our non-werewolf allies barricaded themselves within the grotto. I need to speak with them and see if anyone might have seen where Rasir was last headed. \n\nI don't think they'll be eager to speak to me. But perhaps you can get them to talk.
I hope this scholar-friend of yours has learned something that can help us.\n\nGo find him and bring him back here.
The crew is starting to get a little color back. It's good to see Drigsen on her feet. I hope you're able to find the captain.\n\nWe've trusted you this far and you haven't failed us.
Let's look around. There has to be something here that will help us find Captain Mavvok.
Gods watch over you during these troubled times.
Assassinating the Skald-King would be a terrible blow to Skyrim and the Pact, but I assumed the Icereach Coven had a grander plan than that.\n\nNevertheless, we have to save Jorunn.
You're the one my wife spoke of. The one who returned our daughter to us. I owe you my deepest gratitude. For that, you have my ear.\n\nSo, tell me of this danger that threatens our realm.
Come on, let's make that bastard pay for what he's done to Fenn.
My father is at the top of the Tower of the Wolf. That's where he's calling the storm. We need to get up there!
If my calculations are correct, this tunnel will take us to the Temple of the Divines. From there, we can slip into the Castle Dour and the Tower of the Wolf.
We're close to the surface. You can feel the fresh air.
That's the Karthald Crown.\n\nJarl Olfwenn's gone then? I failed her.
Keep moving. We need to search the catacombs and find High Priest Varkour. Hopefully, she's already with Meridia's Brilliance.
No time to talk now. We need to get up to the cliff and find that witch.

I've known Bjora since we were striplings. The girl I grew up with adores her family and village. We've fought back Reachmen raids side-by-side from the moment we could hold knives. That's not the Bjora I know. \n\nWhat did she say to you?
Hmm? Who are you? Leave me be. I must wait here for my sisters to receive the blessing of my destiny.

I remembered something!\n\nI performed at a party where some drunk braggart rambled on about the Sapphire Society auctions. Didn't learn much except the person in charge is the Auctioneer. It sounded like he supplies the items too.

So much talk of brews and potions. A lot of nonsense, I say! Nothing keeps the constitution strong and healthy better than a good dose of Orcish ale. \n\nAnd by dose, I mean a very large and well-aged barrel.
I think Shelaria may have reopened some of her wounds. Go on. We'll catch up.
Look at these people. The skin … the eyes. What is Essenia doing to them? To Adusa?\n\nI know these vampires might have misguided loyalties, but no one deserves this. Whatever this is.
Is that the missing captain? Let's find out what happened to him.

Ah, hello! You're rather … strapping, aren't you?\n\nUm, if you're here about the traps, there's no need to worry. Claudina fixed them right up! She's really quite good at this. I can almost guarantee that they won't trip anyone else today!
I hate to leave these people like this, but taking them with us isn't an option. At least they're far enough away that they haven't drawn the notice of the vampires and harrowfiends.

My damned ancestor is the traitor-jarl, Hagridden. He was buried alive in the Midnight Barrow long before I was born. \n\nUnfortunately, he has no tomb and what's left of him has been scattered around by these Draugrkin thieves.

First the bridge, now an attack on the garrison? I don't have the forces to withstand an assault on multiple fronts! Do as Ena suggested. Seal those bolt holes, then deal with Vund. I'll make sure we're ready up here.\n\nWell, as ready as possible.
Lady Ninetha spoke highly of you. I'm sure the jarl would like to thank you himself, so present yourself whenever you're ready.
Lead the way. I'm right behind you.
I got back here as quickly as I could! The Reachmen, I heard something troubling as I made my way out of the camp!

If the supplies don't arrive soon, there won't be much of a garrison left. At least not a very good one.\n\nYou can find Captain Hingrid on the road outside of town. With our reduced numbers, I'm sure she'd appreciate any assistance you could offer.

I had thought after our dealings with bone wolves and curses, you would find other ways to amuse yourself for a time. Yet here you are again, right in the midst of more problems.\n\nWhat can Old Mjolen do for you this time?
I'll keep out of sight and check the surrounding area while you and Lyris investigate the town.\n\nMeet me on the far side of town when you're finished and we'll compare notes.

Last I heard, Swordthane Uthlet was gathering everyone he could at the Hall of the Dead. Head over there and see how they weathered the harrowstorm. I'll take care of securing Castle Dour.\n\nAs for Fenn, you might remind him we need a lot of elixir.

We can settle the matter of the crown when there's kingdom enough to rule. What remains of the holds are still ravaged by the harrowstorms. And I doubt we've seen the last of the Gray Host, for that matter.
I—when I first pledged myself to the Blue Palace, I never thought I'd have to defend my city from its own king.
You don't look like one of these western milk drinkers. Tell them we're not a damn invasion—we're here to help!\n\nMaybe you can tell me what's going on?
He better have a good explanation for this.
You made it! Not that I had any doubt. Pickle's sense of direction is unparalleled. Couldn't ask for a finer adventuring companion! \n\nDid you have any trouble along the way?
If you have a plan, you should get to it. Every moment we spend talking is another moment my people are fighting for their lives.\n\nTime is running out.
If you know the truth, just get it over with. I don't expect your sympathy or understanding.\n\nWhat happened was an accident. I don't know what more to say than that.
<Pickle wags his tail. He seems relieved to see Viggol.>
Look at this, do you think we will salvage this place? The mine is ruined.

I'm glad Chief Urzikh didn't invoke the Blood Price. What Mazog did was horrible, sure. But it wouldn't have felt right if we punished her for just trying to help her people. \n\nUrzikh is the best chief we've ever had.
You have done a great service for my family, traveler. Now my sister has a chance. I'll craft the curative and administer it to her as soon as possible.\n\nThank you again.

You don't look like you're keen to slit my throat, which is a vast improvement from my recent company. Keep your guard up. Something strange is going on around here.\n\nAnd of course my fool brother, Raynor, just jumped headlong into the middle of it.

Oh! You're not trying to murder me. Lovely. \n\nDid you happen to see my sister, Kireth, on your way in? I ran ahead while she bravely felled our assailants. She's much better equipped for that sort of thing, you see.
The list. On the ledge. Take it. It's important, I swear.\n\nUnless it's time shifted again. I say, keeping anything on your person through these trips is a hassle.
Once we head inside, we can scout out a few dormant spiders to do our bidding. \n\nLead on, assistant! I will follow and observe … at a safe distance. Can't let any harm come to my delicate tools!
We have to reignite this last warding flame. Hjarnam and my grandfather are counting on us. All of Skyrim is counting on us.\n\nCome, let's hurry.
Let's go before we miss our chance!

Friend! You are just in time! Rigurt is almost out of Nord warrior jokes. He told his favorite about the lusty horker but perhaps it was not explained well enough. Usually it gets quite the laugh.\n\nI see the meat is here. Do you have the howlwater?
Come to help us, eh? \n\nI hope you brought some sturdy friends. I wager Stuhn himself would struggle to turn back Lord Falgravn and his Giant allies.

With the knowledge I've gleaned of this curse, I can slow the curse in the afflicted farmers. Go to Kjenstag ruins. Bring any information about Maxten's curse to Morthal. \n\nAnd hurry. I do not wish to see all Morthal turn to bones.
Captain Ageran. He's … dead. How can he be dead?\n\nThis wasn't supposed to happen. None of this was supposed to happen.

Good, you're back. Old Mjolen told me of your discovery at the farm. She believes that Freiwen's … ghost somehow heralds this curse.\n\nI held out hope of her survival for years. Perhaps finally knowing her fate brings some relief, despite it all.

There's a lot to go through here, but you'll be of more use keeping Arkasis and his gang distracted.\n\nWhat are you looking so expectant for? That not clear enough? Seemed like you already got the hang of causing them trouble.

I knew that snake was lying. But I just wanted to see what he planned. What this was all about. I never expected he would catch me so unaware.\n\nHe hits harder than a giant. Cracked my ribs, probably. I don't understand how he's so powerful.

So the high priest let you have some of his precious oil? No, I don't want the details. Empty the flask into the cauldron and we'll see what happens.\n\nOh, and make sure to stand back when you do it. Just in case.

The desperation, the despair. More and more of our people have disappeared or become harrowed while the survivors crowd inside the walls for shelter.\n\nIf High King Svargrim doesn't act soon, there may not be a Skyrim left to save.
If you see a pretty bottle around, let me know. It talks, if that helps.

Speaking of Fennorian, I'm sure he isn't purposely sending me off to do these little errands. He's just busy with his research.\n\nWe get along splendidly. Everyone says so. He's just painfully shy. He'll come around. You'll see.
Come on then! Which door is it? Maelmoth's Mysterium is nearly within my … our grasp!
Rigurt the Brash, was that his name? What a strange little man.

Welcome to the Mages Guild library.\n\nPlease handle our books and scrolls with the care they deserve. I already cast out a careless Dark Elf. I pray that I will not have to ask anyone else to leave today.

The Pale Man likes to take people, so we'll make one for it. Using draugr parts treated with alchemy. This is where you come in.\n\nThere's a crypt nearby. Dead Man's Respite. Chop up enough draugr parts for a body, then meet me on the northern coast.

Admission to the Circle begins easily enough. Just place your hand on the Antiquarian's Eye.\n\nIf you possess the aptitude, you will attune to the Eye immediately. If you don't possess the aptitude, the Eye will reject you. Couldn't be simpler.
Thank you for your help. I had no idea field work was so invigorating. \n\nI can't wait to tell my peers at the Antiquarian Circle all about it!
We are in your debt, stranger. Thanks to you we can return to our hearths and hearts.
That storm we saw over Kilkreath, it wasn't natural! It was like something out of a nightmare!
Kilkreath got what it deserved, the lousy Daedra worshipers! The people of Solitude follow the true gods, so no storm will ever threaten our city!
Adusa has a strong will. Stronger than mine. She'll fight this transformation as long as she can, but no one can hold out forever.\n\nWe have to move faster.
Hold on … twenty-seven geode crates, fifteen pickaxes, five wheelbarrows, forty-two fresh tourniquets ….\n\nOkay, yeah. There's a lot to do, so I don't have much time. What is it?
If this lout thinks he can win me over with a simple roast boar, then he's going to be sorely disappointed.\n\nThough, it does smell good.
I doubt anyone's been down here in decades.\n\nPoke around and see if you can find another signet. It should look like the one we got at Viridian Watch.

Look how this strange apparatus appears to utilize the energy pockets. Was that shade imprisoned purposefully, or was it caught within the device by accident?\n\nNo matter. It's torture is evident. We must find a way to set it free.
I can't believe my sister led the clan back to this place.\n\nNow that I've seen it with my own eyes, I understand why my mother did what she did. Why she wanted to bury the old ways in the past.

Rada found it. A piece of land sundered from the Reach, caught between Mundus and Oblivion. It is both and neither. Outside the grasp of Bal, or any Prince for that matter.\n\nHe plans to gift the Gray Host with this sanctuary.
Don't get all cocky just because you found the laboratory first. Since you're so smart, talk to Verandis and figure out what we do next.
The bastard isn't here. Damn. \n\nSee what Verandis has to say so we can go back to hunting Rada al-Saran down.
I recognize some of Tzinghalis's work from what we encountered in Western Skyrim. It's not something I'd like to dwell upon. Count Verandis probably has better answers than I can provide.

How horrible. The Dark Heart gave the Nighthollow unbelievable power, but they were dependent on it. They lost the ability to draw sustenance from blood.\n\nAs the Dark Heart slowed and fell into slumber, they became diminished.
Well, Verandis's arrival was … unexpected. Why don't you talk to him. Since you're not officially part of House Ravenwatch, he can't do anything too horrible to you.\n\nI don't think.
We meet again. I see you've been helping Gwendis with her inquiries. If I had been completely honest with her, I could have saved you both the trouble.\n\nPlease, accept my apologies.
Who is this? One of Caddach's witches?

We need to place the offerings at the four wards. This will show the spirits we still honor them and will make it more likely that they will listen when Shaman Ulvoch performs the restoration ritual.\n\nYou place the offerings. I'll say the words.
You found something? Show it to Apprentice Fialyn. See what she can make of it.
That must be the lift Freyleth told you about. As long as it takes us out of this hole, Adusa doesn't care where it goes.
Before you run off, tell me about your audience with Ard Caddach.

Our enemies have put their plans in motion, and it's even worse than I feared.\n\nWe have to help the Reachfolk in Markarth, but I dare not leave Rada al-Saran free to pursue whatever terrible scheme he needs the Orrery for.
When I got here, Verandis was pacing around like a caged animal, trying to find a way to get inside the library. If you have any ideas, let him know.

Didn't I tell you? Freyleth has a plan for saving the Lothid clan. Do what she asked and then meet us upstairs, in the servant's quarters. \n\nWith that mushroom, we can even the odds and then challenge that terrible Boss Trenlor.
Not now, outsider. Away with you or I'll have my Stonehands turn you into a rug.
Adusa-daro? Here? Interesting.\n\nBut you should talk to Kathad. I am much too weak to carry on a proper conversation.
I'm no illusion. Flesh and blood. Alive as can be.
Had my fill of reekers gracing my presence today. Seeing as you've shed blood for me and mine I'll give you my ear, but make it quick. My bile's up and too much talk will likely make it churn.
You should move quickly. Verandis has a way with words, but he's still a verbose High Elf vampire noble from High Rock. Any and all of which can get you killed in the Reach.
We need to investigate Sanuarach Mine and see if we can find the source of that corrupted root. Let's hurry, I want to see the end of this mess.
Let me be, harrier. Just need to … just need to get my thoughts sorted.
Arana is ready to begin the ritual. You just need to give her the components you gathered.\n\nRemember, rituals have power. When the spirits speak, we should heed their words.
Let's have a look around. If Master Pythis was here, he might have left something behind that will help us find both him and the relic.
Somebody thought the knowledge stored down here was important enough to destroy. What kind of book did I get sent for? \n\nYou go ahead and find the people who did this. I need to look for this book.
We have to save my people—my father—from whatever horrible fate they plan for him. These monsters need to pay!\n\nI know I seem weak, but I won't be stopped. Not until I save anyone I can.

Wonderful! It really is a lovely way to reflect on the year itself and remember those who have passed on. \n\nOften I find that writing the message itself makes me feel at peace, even before sending it on.

You'll find the cages where my people are being held in the ruins, up the hill to the right. Send anyone still alive back here … and keep an eye out for Chieftain Faorin. He's my father.\n\nThe Hagravens have something special planned for him.
Interesting. The first stanza of an ancient Reachfolk song. \n\nKeep going, my friend. Hopefully, the pillars will tell us more about what Red Eagle shared with Rada al-Saran.

So you've cleared the Wounding. Head back through the portal when you feel rested.\n\nI can admit now that I hate coming through here. It's just so … blue. Why does Molag Bal keep his realm this color? Father of Torment indeed.
The vateshran was willing to open up a bit more. Must have been my shining personality.\n\nShe suggested that we'd find something important in this cave, but that we might have to work to uncover it.
Once again, you guide me through me problems. I stay in your debt.
If you're going into the mine … please keep Fialyn safe.

They must have gone north. Otherwise, they would have had to pass us and we would have seen them.\n\nSearch the area to the north of the Ring and track them down. I'll keep the chiefs distracted. Thank you for helping with this.
If I hadn't heard the chief-of-chiefs' words with my own ears, I'd think this another trick of the hated Six-Fords.\n\nStill, you have your task, outsider. Get on with it already.
The chief-of-chiefs is crafty, I'll give her that. Using an outsider to shame the Six-Fords. And us, too, I suppose.\n\nNot the best way to start a marriage, but I've seen worse.

First the chief-of-chiefs demands I offer my son to the cursed Eagleseers. Then she involves an outsider in the matter just to shame us.\n\nVery well, outsider. Offer your blessing to my son and the Eagleseer sow so we can finish this.
The chief-of-chiefs is allowing you to go to the handfasting cave?\n\nOutsider, when you see Madearn … no. Forget I said anything.
I'd say that I'll be glad when this is over and done with, but … it wouldn't be honest.\n\nWhat is it, outsider?

We … ought to stick to the plan. We have both fragments of the Lover's Coil. I'll take them to Hroldan Ring and get them repaired. Then we can end the feud and be done with all this.\n\nYou go ahead. I'd … like a moment to myself.

It is a difficult matter. End the feud today and you stop the violence right away, but there are other factors of the heart to consider.\n\nOr support Eslyn and Madearn to carry out their plan, but the feud will claim more lives until they can end it.

Eventually this place will serve as a proper shrine to the Hunt-Father, our Lord Hircine. Once all the relics are set in place.\n\nOnly now I worry for the safety of my other apprentices. I sent them to retrieve relics for this shrine.

While you seek the switch that unlocks the main door, I'll study these carvings. I recognize the iconography. If I can translate it, maybe we can learn more about the sorcerer and the curse we're facing. \n\nAnd take a duplicate with you, just in case.
Not carrying that book any more, it's like a weight has been lifted from my shoulders.\n\nI'll tell Sombren he should hang onto it. Keep it safe until we find the Fourth Ambition.
I'll make sure the twins are ready to move to Fort Redmane when Eveli gives the word.
Mercenary. You have news?
Eveli has been anxiously awaiting your return. \n\nShe's over by the command tent when you're ready to talk to her.

Let's take the documents we received from Councilors Jirich and Sophus and show them to Councilor Lovidicus. Maybe he can make sense of the Imperial code.\n\nIf not, I know someone I can contact. He's a wonder at these sorts of things.

I sense additional wards deeper within. Deal with them and see if the Imperial caches remain intact. I shall wait here until the danger is past.\n\nBut stay alert, little mortal. The Dagon cultists can be dangerous in large numbers.

Step back and state your business. \n\nI have every reason to believe that my life is in danger. If you so much as make a threatening gesture, the brigadine will dismember you. He has very strict orders on that regard.
This is it! With the sigil keys, we can unlock the temple's adytum. If Zenithar smiles on our labors, that's where we'll find the Golden Anvil.
This is a place where even the stones tremble in terror. We must get all of my friends away from here.\n\nLet us keep going, beek-ojel.

The mercenary returns! I dare say, you and Eveli make a good team. Once Councilor Lovidicus and the Chamber of Legates reach a decision, I expect that we'll call upon you again.\n\nIn the meantime, Councilor Lovidicus has been waiting for your report.

Whatever their actual involvement, a Dark Brotherhood sanctuary in Blackwood is cause for concern. But how they factor into Leovic's secret, the Ambitions, and the attacks on the councilors, I have yet to figure out.

We're moving again? I've barely had time to experience the world outside my vault, and now … well, I may not get much of a chance.\n\nI'll go with Eveli and Sombren. At least I'll get to see more of the countryside, right?

Another mercenary? Is our Ivory Brigade so enfeebled that Captain Rian must resort to hiring sellswords?\n\nLook, as I told the Wood Elf. Councilor Abor was quite insistent. She doesn't want to be disturbed.
Oh good. Someone competent arrives. \n\nI trust I can rely on you to fulfill this deal? You showed so much skill last time, I would hate to be disappointed.

Looks like your friend the Daedra wants a word with you. You can show her what you found, but don't let her take anything.\n\nHurry, though. I want to get that scroll to my contact in Elden Root before more of those cultists show up.
Well, at least you're still alive. Hope you've made some progress in freeing those hostages. The Painted Eye are bound to start losing their patience. I'm surprised they haven't already.
I'm ready to be done with this place. And Quistley, too, for that matter.
Shh, you talk to Seeks while I work on this lock and maybe he'll forget to yell at me.

When I first got here, I saw the door to the crypt was still locked tight and I thought we finally managed to get ahead of these bastards, but that's not my luck. \n\nI just saw a group pass clear through this door like it wasn't even here.

I can't believe it! All of Phalevon's known trophies—horn, helm, sword, and armor—retrieved from this foul cavern. And just in time, it seems. It looks like this place is filling up with water.\n\nNow we just need to get out of here!

The Obelisk of Inevitability reveals just one possible future. True, it's the most likely outcome, but it isn't the only one.\n\nNow that we know where things are heading, we can work to change the course.
I'm not sure what this oracle is going to show us. Is that why my palms are sweating?
I don't remember my parents. They never told us anything about them in the vault.\n\nI suppose this means they were loyal subjects of Emperor Moricar. That they were working with Vandacia.
Please hurry — we have to destroy these stones while Tiras is still strong enough to lead us to the central lode! I'll shield you from harm as best I can!
I suppose we shouldn't keep the Daughter of Sithis waiting.
Well? Aren't you and Revus meant to be chasing bright lights?
Good, you're just in time. I barely began to tell the governor everything that happened. Why don't you finish up? Talk to Keshu and tell her what we discovered in that vault.
Go on then. I've got to hurry if I'm going to do anything for Bevene. When I'm finished here, I'll meet you outside.
Quick, destroy it before I change my mind!
Let's keep looking. There are bound to be clues right under our noses!
Little mortal, I can proceed no farther. Another ward bars my way.\n\nDeal with it, will you?

You look quite capable. Might I be able to recruit you to help me?\n\nThis place was once an honorable tomb for fallen members of the Dark Brotherhood, but now it houses a perversion of death. The cycle which devours all has been corrupted here.
Do what you will, my friend. It seems my mother controls my fate in the afterlife as well.
Is that a Watcher? I've seen them in books. In diagrams, I mean. I expected them to be … bigger.
We're out of mead and no hot meals. If those are luxuries to which you're accustomed, you can keep on moving and find another inn.
Excuse me, stranger. Just me working the farm now, so I have no time for chit chat.

Honestly, Sister of Pools is really starting to annoy me. At least Deet's got scales again, but I can't take him home like this.\n\nLet's find one more pool and see if that works. If not, well, I can at least tell our egg-mother I tried.
The remaining councilors are safe, but our work's not done yet! We've still got a mystery to solve.
Dripping acid? Sloppy, but it leaves a trail you should be able to follow easily enough.\n\nI shan't leave Gideon until you have the assassin once again in custody.
Well, what are you waiting for? Find that treasure!
Go on. Head toward that large, ominous structure in the distance. I'll be right behind you.
Go on ahead and see if you can find the entrance to the Dark Brotherhood sanctuary. I'll be behind you the whole time, watching for any surprises.

I keep up with events in Cyrodiil. A habit from my days serving as a scribe in the court of the Longhouse Emperors. I can give Eveli a letter of introduction. Make it easier for her to approach Councilor Lovidicus and the others.
Go check the water for yourself. There's something going on in this accursed swamp and it's not our doing. Everyone is just too busy fighting to see it.
Explore our sanctum if you must, but know that I'll be watching.

Despite my yelping, I was not afraid, I assure you! There is no shame in being frightened, of course. If you were alarmed, do not worry. You are safe with me!\n\nAnyway, that was a great effort on your part, but perhaps hitting it is not enough.

This may work. It may not. We may open a portal that takes us to the cultists. Or we may open one to some dark and deadly corner of Oblivion. Still, nothing ventured, nothing gained.\n\nSo, ready to try something daring?

Make sure you stand a safe distance away once you place the kit. I promise you, I made that stink kit powerful enough to knock a Giant on its buttocks! Skurnd won't be able to get it off his skin for weeks! \n\nI bet I'll hear his screams from here!
Do not make trouble, stranger. We have enough already.
We don't have much, I know. Annyce never fails to remind me. Have you found anything that might lead to my daughter?
I believe in the Winds. I always have, even since I hatched in my nest. They will come around to reason and defend us once more.
We must find the Winds. Without them, we cannot drive the warlord from our village.
The barrier is down. Let's get through that gate and save Liam!
An ominous voice from nowhere, crazed cultists, and another portal behind that statue …. What is it with Daedra and portals, anyway?\n\nI suppose we ought to follow the cultist leader, right?
Stay on your guard, my friend. These golems can't be reasoned with, and there are lots of them!

By my spread claws, you bring some small hope. My waters may flow yet.\n\nGo east, through the old city. Push through the Sul-Xan to reach the xanmeer. I expect Bahsei prepares her summoning at its peak. I will follow behind as you clear the way.

Well now! Scipion can say what he wants about this city, but you don't have strapping, smoldering-eyed strangers walk into your suites in Cheydinhal. \n\nAlas, were I only in the mood for some distraction … damnable Fang-Furls.
That's a ghost. A real ghost! Like, of a dead person! How are you so calm about this?\n\nI guess we should see what it wants, right? You first.
I suspect things are going to be a bit awkward in the Auzin household the first time I come visit.
What an adventure this has been, right? I'm really building up a collection of stories!

Well, that was enlightening. I thank you for your help, you're quick on your feet! I remember when I could snatch an errant bug from the very sky. Those were the days.\n\nAh, my mind wanders. Let us focus on the task at hand.

I wish we were meeting again under less-stressful circumstance, but it's good to see you.\n\nThe cultists spilled out of portals shortly after I arrived at the castle. I barely got to look at the coded documents before Vandacia grabbed them!
The great mystery of where the fetching puzzle box vanished off to is the only one I care to solve. Let's get that damned thing out of here and be done with it as soon as possible.
Remember, Eveli Sharp-Arrow awaits you in the governor's mansion in Gideon. Safe travels and know that the Black Fin Legion stands with you and the Wood Elf! No matter what.
I can't thank you enough, Nocturnal is wise and powerful, but in her realm of Evergloam, forgiveness is in very short supply.

I know it's a lot to ask, but it means a great deal to us that you're willing to brave that vault to find Xocin. \n\nThis isn't just about helping the Black Fin Legion anymore. Now you're helping our family. We won't forget that.

By the Egg … we were all different after that battle. Fighting alongside Nords, Dunmer, even Daedra. Every one of us changed. We all lost something.\n\nI thought Xocin had finally moved on. I should've seen he was still in pain.
Don't hover over me like a mother netch. I can keep up with you two youngings.
I do not regret keeping secrets. There are some things that one has to handle on their own.
I have a bad feeling about what awaits us beyond that ward. I sense great and terrible power that it is struggling to contain. The Daedric influence we've seen thus far pales in comparison.

I've read theories suggesting that Daedra feed off mortal emotions. Fear, desire, hatred. Some more compelling than others. This is the first time I've seen it manifested so literally.\n\nThese vessels are soaking up all the Dread Cellar's misery.
Was there some confusion distinguishing your left from your right, little mortal?\n\nUntil we deactivate the ward on that door, we won't be getting any closer to our objective.
As long as there are still things I wish to learn, I will assist you, little mortal.
Hey! It's not safe to be out in the open here. If they take you inside, you won't leave.
Well? What of it? Did you craft the effigy? \n\nHand it over, child!

Martus was tight lipped from the start. He claimed it was for our mission's secrecy, but he just wanted to hide his involvement in all this. What else has Martus neglected to mention? He's put us all in danger.
This doesn't look good. But we didn't expect this to be easy, did we? I'll stand with you, no matter what happens.
Something feels wrong. Like part of me is missing. What did he take from me?\n\nOh, Sombren, how could you?
There are things I still wish to learn, little mortal. Continue to assist me and I shall make sure you are suitably rewarded.

If Lyranth is going to search for Calia and Sombren she's going to need my help. I'm practically an expert at finding Ambitions now! Also, I want to keep an eye on her. \n\nWe'll meet back up with you if we find those two.
Very well. You and the Anchorite explore Brandfire Reformatory. Locate the souls of the Longhouse Emperors and learn what you can. I will meet up with you after I locate Calia and Sombren.

This whole time, it was hunting Atrozu. Because of what he represents. The Ravener didn't just want to devour my clan mates. It craved the very idea of the Kalmur. Our unity. Our fellowship.\n\nIt would mean our complete destruction.

I sense you carry the pendant I gave my mortal servant. Yes, you are the one I instructed her to find and send to me.\n\nIf only you had arrived but a few moments earlier, you wouldn't have had to pull that blade from my chest.
You have the items I requested, yes? Then place them in the cauldron so I can complete the potion of disguise.
That lucent isn't charged with energy like the other one we found. There has to be a dynamus font we can use.

I asked Rynkyus to meet us here in Fargrave. You should find him in the Plaza of Portals. See if his scouts learned anything useful or if he requires your assistance.\n\nIn the meantime, I have investigations of my own to attend to.
Ordinator Nilera's spirit was so strong, even after being Mehrunes Dagon's captive for so long. You and the other Living Gods must have been sad to see her killed.

Lyranth and Rynkyus told me about this place. Mehrunes Dagon chased some long-forgotten enemy to this realm and laid waste to the plane. Then he awarded it to his mortal cultists and they built a citadel here.\n\nIt seems … familiar.
The daedrat proves useful yet again. See what else Arox can tell us about this Elegian. All I could help the Anchorite draw from her memories was his name and that he was some sort of seer.
Strange. I do not imagine the Anchorite came here to be fitted for that mask. So when did she get it from him? And where?
Much as I would like to test myself against Mehrunes Dagon's wardens, it would be unwise to draw attention to our interest in this seer. If you survive, find me at the Wretched Spire.
Regrets. I was detained. Did you find Vontan? What did you learn?

This is definitely the spot on the map. And those glowing runes look like the etchings on the ring we picked up on the Isle of Joys.\n\nTry using the ring on the runes or something. That's usually what I do in these kinds of situations.
Bow in the presence of the Dread Lady, adventurer. Grovel and be blessed by her penetrating stare.\n\nOh, and she still requires your assistance, so you should talk to her.

I hoped Elegian would be able to tell me who I am or how I knew him. It's disappointing. But at least he sort of explained my mask. And he told us where to find the Riven Cataclyst.\n\nI don't know what I'm supposed to do with this amulet, though.

Greetings, stranger. Is this about Tephilaz's death? Or, I suppose, not death. The Daedra tell me that is not really how it works with them. I imagine he will come back eventually.\n\nDo you know Noroth? The two of you spoke for some time, I saw.

I gathered allies, those who have fought by your side in the past. You certainly accumulated a lot of them in your travels. \n\nLet us hope that between them and the daedrat's knowledge of the fortress, it will be enough.
No matter what fate awaits us, I will fight with everything I have! It has been an honor to serve you, master. I won't fail you.

Look at us, little mortal. Forced to accept the word of a blind, old seer, imprisoned and driven mad in Dagon's Blood Pit.\n\nIf Elegian is to be believed, we'll find Sister Celdina and the Riven Cataclyst at the summit.

The captured Bladebearer we freed mentioned that the cultists were feeding their clan mates to some infernal device beneath the fort. That has to be the Riven Cataclyst!\n\nSister Celdina may already have her army of Incarnates. We should hurry.

I can't abide the Anchorite in Valkynaz Nokvroz's grip, not our darling of the alleys. Let me gather some materials and recall the proper incantations. Then I will collect Lyranth and meet you at the old portal dais in the Burn, south of Ardent Hope.
Blood adepts. It would make sense that Valkynaz Nokvroz would entrust them to harvest the Anchorite's blood.\n\nLet us look around and see if they can lead us to wherever the Anchorite is being held.
Madam Whim refuses to use her influence. She could easily raise an army of Fargravians to join me and my Bladebearers when we assault Valkynaz Nokvroz's fortress, but she adamantly denies my request.
Free my Kyn, mortal, before my anger becomes storm.
This is probably going to get ugly. Be careful, all right? I'll watch your back.

You plan to sneak into Ardent Hope, master? Then let me accompany Rynkyus and the Bladebearers! Arox the Mutilator should be at the head of our vanguard when they assault the front gates of the fortress!
We need to tread carefully. I do not trust any enemy that invites his adversaries inside.

Ah. You here to enjoy the hilarity provided by that King Emeric? Between the two of us, I wish I could say their dribble improves with copious intoxicants but … it hasn't so far.\n\nWhat would you say to helping me bring in some new talent?
All that and we let Sister Celdina get away. Well, if Lyranth thinks there's some way we can salvage this debacle, I'm all ears. Talk to her and see what she's got in mind.
Search the bathhouse, little mortal, while I do the same.\n\nIn her hurry, Sister Celdina may have left something behind that will shed more light on her plans.

So Gazmod the Collector is a Watcher, hmm? Never met one before. At least, I don't think I have.\n\nQuick, ask them about a way to decipher the code. Get them thinking about something—anything—other than adding me and my mask to their collection.

The Anchorite claimed she was going to assist with our negotiations, but she allowed the temptations of this den of iniquity to distract her.\n\nRouse her from her indulgences and see if she is familiar with this Gazmod the Collector.
I'm ready to stop moving, I think. I want a drink in one hand, a blood pie in the other, and my feet propped up on a table.
Speak to him, please. I feel… nervous about him, for some reason.
The Grasp has much to do in Fargrave. Each day, there are more who need the Stricture interpreted and maintained.
This is by far the biggest mess we've ever gotten ourselves into.\n\nPlease, leave me alone. I've got enough to worry about.
Stay back! Please, don't come any closer. I don't have the strength to fight you, or any money to give you, but please! I beg you to look the other way. Let me go.
Everything seems to be in order with the Undertaker's guardian stone. I can prepare it for you to activate whenever you're ready.

You again? You seem to be making a habit of this. Should I be flattered or just assume that you're the one killing my associates?\n\nI joke. Even if you were the one killing those who work for me, I'd still be flattered.
Did you not receive orders from Lyranth or Rynkyus? Why do you linger?
I have no interest in speaking with you, mortal. What would be the point? You likely will not survive the journey to Annihilarch's Summit.
A ghostly spider, hmm? A bit garish for my taste, but then, we can't all be squinty, desiccated Skein-spawn, can we?\n\nBefore you go, I have something to give you.

I did some scouting around the cove. It looks like this is the only entrance to the Ascendant Order's hideout that isn't secure. Unfortunately, the reason for that is a lot of angry yaghra trying to claw their way in. We'll have to push through.
Careful, walker. When Za'ji and Caska last came through the woods were all quiet, until we came to the old mill. Then it seemed as if the trees sprung to life and attacked us!
Not leaving yet. Talk to Fyr.\n\nElf's always talking. Going to die talking one day.

Congratulations, mortal. You are now the proud owner of a filthy, Oblivion-flea-infested daedrat. That talks. Let us hope it can actually do what it says and decipher the encoded note.\n\nNow we should find the Anchorite and depart this place.
I think Hyxo's very annoyed that he can't hurt me right now. Don't keep him waiting, or he might turn that frustration toward you.
Why are you mortals always drawn to Vri? Is it his height? Or an instinctive desire to address your betters?
Hello! Can you spare a moment to talk about Peryite, the Prince of—.\n\nOh. Hmm. On second thought … you might not be what we're looking for.
I don't care what Sunel says he heard. No storm I've ever seen in this forsaken place can topple a Daedric tower.
Better stay clear of Burning Gyre Keep. I thought the Sever's storms were bad, but the one I saw near Burning Gyre was enough to topple the keep!

I do hope the accommodations are to you and Lyranth's liking. Dylandra and her harem wanted to rent the space for one of her sensual encounters, but I had to tell her it was unavailable.\n\nI hope whatever you did at Burning Gyre Keep was worth it.

The Ascendant Magus disappeared while Quentyn kept us busy, and the Ascendant Lord left before that. I doubt we'll catch either of them now.\n\nCome, let's leave this place. There's nothing more for us here.

Lady Arabelle asks about the nobility while two of my retainers are missing. The Society of the Steadfast will do whatever is necessary to keep its people safe.\n\nShe mentioned the Ascendant Order might be involved. Do you think that's possible?
Quentyn isn't far. My scrying spell returned a strong and clear result.\n\nYou will come with us to rescue him, won't you? Talk to Lady Arabelle and she'll tell you what she's thinking.

Thieves are a blight to Zenithar's welcoming eye. He sees their continued disruptions of his festive day and will set fire to any who steal what they do not earn.\n\nPlease, retrieve the blessed awl from the Greycloak's as you did before.

You have no idea how long I've waited for someone like you to come by. There isn't much time!\n\nTarrinore went in there. By herself! She's been gone a long time. Something terrible must have happened to her!

It's much darker and … damper than I expected. Not sure I'd choose such a place to live, but who am I to judge? Hadolid culture probably has different values.\n\nSomewhere in here is my Privette. Let's look around.

Please be careful with those medallions, dear. It took a great deal of resources to craft them, and we don't have time to make any more.\n\nDeliver one to Arch-Magister Delric and then make haste to the Fighters Guildhall in your capital.
We did it! Redheart's hilt! As a knight aspirant, I know I should wish all of my competitors equally good luck.\n\nBut, Stendarr forgive me, I hope Langley gets bitten by every mosquito out here.

I am sure Nilsmon is hovering around somewhere. Tell him I took his poem to read. Later.\n\nHe's sent me an entire recital's worth of odes. Heaping praise upon my various features and body parts. Silly man.

Arch-Magister Delric! He's … dead! He just put the medallion around his neck and it jolted him with arcane energy! How could this happen? My work was perfectly safe. You don't think—oh, no.\n\nQuick, give me the Fighters Guild medallion.

Hey there, good-looking. Lady Arabelle said she hired some muscle, but she didn't tell me it was you. Anyway, I'm glad you're here. You know me—I'm a lover, not a fighter.\n\nBut I need to work off my debt, so here I am.
There's got to be more clues about this curse. We just need to find the other captains' logs.

Huh, I'm a little surprised no one's here defending the dock. Maybe they assume no one can come or go, so why bother? Makes it easy when they're arrogant.\n\nKeep a lookout as we head inland. We might run into the hunters playing the game.
I'm sure Lady Arabelle has something she needs me to do. Just between you and me, I don't mind the work too much. But don't let her know that.
Jakarn, do this. Jakarn, do that. Jakarn, put on a disguise so you can board a transport to a prison island from which you'll probably never return.\n\nThe things I do for gold.
Don't worry, I'll smooth things over with our disgruntled friend here once we're finished.\n\nYou just focus on dispelling the evil magic.

Finally. At long last, someone has accomplished Lady Garick's third test. She was not a brutal woman, but she did not suffer the weak. It was this attitude that let her ascend so quickly.\n\nNow I have met her equal.
Oh, I think there's a lantern in here. That's pleasant.

Here we are. Now go make your rounds, dear. Remember, I'm known in these circles, so chances are good they know you, too.\n\nDefinitely speak with Duchess Elea, Count Damard, and Viscount Jonne. And anyone else who happens to catch your interest.
Looks like someone left in a hurry. Guilty conscience, maybe?\n\nBetter take a look around.
I can't talk right now. Though you cannot see it, I am flexing both my sword arm and my off-hand muscles. \n\nA warrior such as I never stops training.

The wards would have been everywhere down here, but we know that many of them have already been broken. We need to find the remaining wards and destroy them.\n\nI have never done anything like this before, but I have an idea how to proceed. Let us go.
Excellent work. Now plunge it into the waters and we should have the weapon we need.
I didn't know the old man had it in him! He had something to target me specifically, what a sneaky old goat! Good thing I had you with me.\n\nYou managed to get the book, right? Let me see it.
I do believe I could stand here watching Emeric fret about Caska all day.\n\nI told him she's only eaten Bretons once or twice. That I'm aware of.
One door down, one to go. All good forts and castles have multiple points of defense.\n\nLet's see if we can do this without alerting the entire fortress.
The Magus and his Lord escaped. Damn cowards!\n\nGo on. Find a way outside and signal that ship you promised. I'll be right behind you.
We can't allow this functionary to delay us, dear. Reason with the steward. Or browbeat him if you must.\n\nWe need to get aboard the Silver Swan!

Hey! So, I did some skulking around while I was waiting for you. Remember Dockmaster Arnauld? The slimy skeever who sold out our ships to the Ascendant Order?\n\nWord on the docks is he's here. Sounds like his bosses aren't happy with him, either.
Maybe you heard—my talk with Master Healer Viralaine was unproductive. He always sticks to procedure. No sense of urgency with that one. \n\nWell, how did you fare? Learn anything from the patients?
That looks like everything we asked for. Nicely done.\n\nPass the reagents to Ryvana and we can get started.

Thank you for helping us. The bloomingsong flowers will strengthen my connection to the spirit of the grove, while the torchbug will light the way.\n\nJust be sure to take care with the little creature. They are fragile things.

Should've known Lady Arabelle could take care of herself, but it's still good we arrived when we did. Looks like she was starting to get winded. Anyway, tell Lady Arabelle what we learned about the Magus.\n\nShe's going to want to hear this.

The lads were making bets on whether you'd come back or not. I put half a potato on you. Looks like old Adwig's a few potatoes richer! Ha! You hear that, Donel? Put that in your pipe and smoke it!\n\nNow, how about it? You find what I asked for?
Ahh, I just want to look at my ship a bit longer. You never know how much you love a thing until it's snatched up by fin-eared corsairs, you know?
You should get a move on.
Ah, you have a mammoth ear leaf? Good! We should give a little of the juice to <<1>> and see if it makes her feel better.\n\nAnd perhaps stand back after we give it to her.
I'm sorry about that little scene. Some people are unbelievable.\n\nWelcome to the Ancient Anchor. What can I do for you?
Don't mind me, dear. I'm just jotting down a few notes. For my … memoir, yes.
Ugh. Surely death would be more preferable to … this. Still, I thank you for waking me. I was having the most horrific dreams.\n\nWho are you, again?
That's better! I can't thank you enough. Without your help, I'd still be under arrest.\n\nNow, what's all this about Rigurt and his missing scepter?
Quickly, give Roslenn the antidote. She doesn't deserve to have this curse. No one does.
We come all this way into the mine to save him and all he does is yell at us? I don't know if you'll be able to talk to my father, but I certainly won't!\n\nAnd he calls me childish!

Count Damard isn't here. But as we feared, he was planning to remove Duchess Elea from the picture. Talk to her. She may have seen or heard something that will help us. \n\nI'll be listening. And if she lies to you, I'll know.
What? This is my spot! I may not be a trusty, but I know my rights! Move along before I stab you with a sharp rock or something.
Now that we're free, we can finish what we started.
Were you able to meet with Lord Bacaro, dear? What did he say when you told him about our victory?
Enjoy your stay in Gonfalon Bay, mainlander … but not too much. I've had my fill of drunkards and fools today.

Good to see you, friend, but something is wrong. While you and Lady Arabelle were off, we scoured Gonfalon Bay for signs of the Ascendant Order. And we found nothing! Not even one of their damn pamphlets!\n\nThey're up to something, I know it!
We can't let the Ascendant Order win. Somehow, we must find a way to stop them.

Quite the crew we assembled here. I wish we had an army, but Kaleen and Tsuzo are good in a fight, and Caska is terrifying! Za'ji is … well, not so much, but then there's me and you.\n\nAnyway, Kaleen mentioned a plan? See what she has in mind.

The Ascendant Order is not in Gonfalon Bay and the alliance leaders are safe. So Za'ji considers his work done. But … Captain Kaleen does not seem satisfied with Za'ji's opinion.\n\nPerhaps you should talk to her, five-claw.
To think, the captains of three warring factions, working together to save their leaders from a common foe—the Ascendant Order. It gets me right here.\n\nOr it could just be a hairball.

The journal we found at the Emerald Eye's camp said the door to the Motalion Necropolis would be a tomb different from all the others, so keep an eye out.\n\nIt'd be helpful if it had a big green glowing eye on it, but I'm never that lucky.
It is good to breathe better air as a free Khajiit.

Jhaka is not fully well yet. He is sorry he cannot be of use in a fight. But this one and Silverslip will trail you and Ember so we can be there when you find Song.\n\nJhaka has no doubt that you will. But please, be safe.
I can tell Ember's getting restless. Hasn't changed a bit, she's got all the same tells. Go talk to her before she gets any more wound up. \n\nI'm not going anywhere, I promise.
Oh thank every single Divine, she's not hurt. Get her out of there, my friend. \n\nI'll keep an eye out for more of Vetitia's men.
Don't worry, we'll be careful. Now that I've seen what these people are willing to do, I'm not going to take any chances with Aurelia's safety.
That map fragment you found is worth a fair bit of gold to me. I assume you brought it to me for the reward.
Guess we'll see you in Belkarth. Don't worry, we'll get that fetcher. He's not going to get away this time.

Baron-Admiral. After years of preparation, we're finally ready to show those slug bastards what for! My ship was one of the first to join the fleet, and today it's ready.\n\nGive the word and we'll set sail on the next wave.

Poor Lady Laurent! I was only possessed by that foul Tobin for the briefest of instants, but Captain Renwic has been inside m'lady for ages!\n\nI saw where Tobin hid his tools, though. They're buried in the graveyard, right here on the islet.

I never understood why some folk chose not to believe in Zenithar. He exists in every action we take. He breathes life and strength into anyone who falters. I may be one of his priests, but Zenithar's light shines on us all.
I could smell Za'ji's craven musk the moment he set foot in the woods. I would have found him sooner if he'd cowered somewhere closer.\n\nThought he might have swam all the way back to the Pounce.
Honestly, I find this quite invigorating. Taking action against a scoundrel, seeking justice for the spurned!\n\nI rather do wish he hadn't been so dashing.
Please, go to the Monument Inn. It started there, I just know it!\n\nDamn, I can already feel what little I remembered slipping away. Blast this ancient curse.
I'm so grateful you've come … even if I was a bit of a beef-wit the last time you saw me. \n\nI'm worried sick. Captain Marso has been taken captive.

Bright Moons shine upon us, walker. Before you arrived I did some sniffing. A scent like the one that lingers on that axe you found. It's inside the coin lord's old fort.\n\nI'd bet Za'ji's left ear that it's Prince Irnskar.
Aurelia's last letter is just there. Read it and you'll see what I mean. She's changed, and for the better.\n\nI just hope she's all right.
One door down, one to go. All good forts and castles have multiple points of defense.\n\nLet's see if we can do this without alerting the entire fortress.

Today's the day! The Intermediate Tournament! I don't think I've ever had a sharper deck. I bet it could even beat one of those Mournhold decks! Not that I … I mean, there's no way we're playing them, right?\n\nSorry. Rambling. You need something?

I have it on good authority that preparations for the Roister's Club tournaments are well underway.\n\nContinue to refine your strategies, collect new cards, and increase your rank. If you work hard, I'm certain you will be ready when the time comes.
So, you all made into the mid-tier, eh? Guess that means I can start charging more for all this ale and tack!

Brahgas will give you the final details. Find him outside, yes?\n\nDo not forget to return to Kishka and Marunji, though. This one posted some very special challenges today! Like … well, Kishka forgets. But she is sure they are very sleek!

Hey, what are you—? Did you come out here to look for me? I'm sorry. I know the tournament starts soon. I just needed a moment.\n\nIt's complicated. I appreciate your concern, but really, I don't want to drag you into my mess.
Brave people are risking their lives to protect me and the other alliance leaders. We must not make their task any harder than it already is.\n\nWe should move before the Ascendant Order returns.

Tall Papa's breeches, what has Brahgas gotten himself into this time?\n\nTeliv is a fine player, but he has many connections to unsavory elements in Mournhold. House Dres, the Camonna Tong, you name it. If Brahgas made another bet … damn.
What a beautiful view. I long to set sail on the water once more, but I share Captain Kaleen's fears. The Ascendant Order is still out there, planning something new.\n\nSpeak with her, my friend.
Ugh. My head. Feels like a hangover without the fun drinking part beforehand.

Well, I never have a hard time watching one of the Mournhold Roisters lose. As much as I'd like to say and watch Dralcia's downward spiral, I need to figure out what's happening with Brahgas.\n\nI'll see you back at Gonfalon Bay.
Don't worry about me, chum. I've got this completely under control!
A cunning businesswoman like me has numerous other opportunities in the Systres. \n\nBut knighthood, and marriage to the Lady Aurelia, is a sure bet. And I never say no to coin.
What kind of fools would tamper with the lighthouse?\n\nThey're no sailors, I can say that. No tar-grip worth the name would put another sailor in danger.

My mother made her living picking at the flotsam that washed up in the loch. But she remembered those lost to the depths and said a prayer for them.\n\nShe'd weep to fill the ocean today. All those sailors, lost.
Locate a harrowstorm, and begin your assault. I will join the fray. Flank them while they're distracted.\n\nGood hunting. Partner.

Old logbooks, manifests, documents. All scattered here. I can read them, so not Dwarven. Many seem Breton, several High Elf. But most are soaked and illegible.\n\nI'd wager that others who crashed here left these. But what happened to them?

Greetings, traveler! Welcome to High Isle, the hidden gem of the Systres Archipelago!\n\nIt's a shame more people from the mainland don't visit our beautiful islands. Fortunately, I have a plan to address that!

They must have killed the wyress as soon as she opened the path. Archdruid Michiel is getting impatient. Rotten path-traitor.\n\nWhatever purpose this ancient spirit serves, we can't let the Firesong have it. Let's put an end to this.

Tava's breath, I wish we had arrived in time to save Wyress Sorcha. Damned Firesong. But they have nowhere else to run. Let the craven curs eat sand!\n\nWhatever happens in there, I'm with you, sailor. And I'm sure I speak for Druid Laurel, too.

Such an assemblage! Raz is practically overwhelmed with the sheer splendor of it all. And do you see Queen Ayrenn over there? Isn't she the most magnificent of the royals gathered here? No, do not say anything five-claw. Raz can see it in your eyes.

This one knew you would agree! Ninety percent of the time, Raz's instincts never fail him.\n\nYou remember the thugs you shook from Raz's tail? We must find them. The tails will become the tailed. Poetic, yes?

I'm a surveyor. Not a mage, or an adventurer, or even a brave farmer. But I still know magic when I see it.\n\nSo, when a glowing crystal mysteriously floats above a rapidly growing lava flow, there must be a connection.
It looks like Niraya's had an even tougher time of it than I have. Talk to her, friend. I'll keep watch.

I refuse to let Galen's enemies dictate my actions. Yet I dare not move directly against the Firesong Circle or their Dreadsails friends as long as they're holding Stefan hostage.\n\nWhat say you, mercenary? Ready to earn some more House Mornard gold?
Count yourself fortunate. I usually let my blade do the talking when I meet landers, but today I've got other things to deal with.

Good work getting Stefan back, mate. We're not out of the storm quite yet, though. Tava's breath … seems like we never get a moment to pause and collect ourselves. \n\nAnyway, Stefan's got something important he wants to talk to you about.
I hoped to see you again, my friend, but I need to prepare for the Draoife. The elders really must deal with the strife that has come between the circles.

Remember, we think the Dreadsails have prisoners in there. Maybe some knights, but certainly druids from the nearby village. Find them if you can and set them free. We'll join you as soon as my knights recover their senses.

You know that feeling when you just want to sink your teeth into something and rip it apart? Well, I'm having one of them right now.\n\nTalk to Lady Arabelle before I decide to go do something stupid.
Lady Arabelle is very brave. Barely recovered from nearly dying and already chasing villains into a desolate and scary valley. Hurry, five-claw, you must go help her!

May Y'ffre guide your steps, my friend. And keep Lady Arabelle safe. She won't admit it, not even to herself, but the poison took a lot out of her. She should be back at the manor resting, not on her way to battle the Ascendant Lord.
These creatures were summoned to protect this place. There's more of them than can just be explained by the natural attraction of the circle. But who could have performed such a summoning?
I saw it all, but do not worry. Even Raz loses a game sometimes! In a way, this is more fun! \n\nIt means we will have to do things the old-fashioned way.

Ah, are you here because of the summons? Excellent! It is good to know that heroes come from all over Tamriel to assist Elsweyr.\n\nOf course, this one cannot send people to die without proper training.
Be ready, friend. When Frii wakes the guardian, we'll have our chance.
The Firesong leader was hiding in his cabin! We won't get free of this tub as long as he's on his feet. Get over there and clear the enemy decks!
Place the herbs in the cauldron. Our guide made all this ready before the door to the Ivy Throne was sealed. So many seasons ago.

The trials can be difficult, but those who complete them are second to none when facing down Dragons. I've seen it with my own eyes! \n\nI'm sure you'll find the experience rewarding. I simply can't wait to see your progress!
Captain Siravaen's a mercenary, and every mercenary has their price. Figure out what that is and tell her I'll agree to pay it. We need her and her ship.
We're going back into Fauns' Thicket? Wonderful! It's nice and peaceful in there. Well, except for all the wild creatures that tried to kill us last time.\n\nOh, hi! What are you doing here?

Druid Fenas wants us to go back into Fauns' Thicket? Is that really such a good idea? No. No. No. I—I'm all right. I can do this. We have to if there's a chance to break this damn curse.\n\nThe way inside is right over there. That's how we got in.

Even though the Firesong surrendered after Archdruid Orlaith's death, it's evident that Lord Bacaro still has the support of some of the circle's more ardent members. Not to mention his own Ascendant knights.\n\nWe need to proceed cautiously, friend.
Y'ffre's Path is an Eldertide site. The druids of that circle tend to the ancient ruins on the western side of the hollow. That's probably where Lord Bacaro headed.

Ah, there you are. There's something we need to discuss.\n\nThe Dreadsails and their Firesong allies make ready to assault Vastyr's walls. We need more defenders to stand with us against this coming threat.
Damn my clumsiness! If not for the fact that we were delayed by that trap, we could have been here to help you with that creature. Then maybe Lord Bacaro wouldn't have been able to slip away.
Finally. It's finished. I can't thank you enough for agreeing to help. Lover boy here was certainly of no use.\n\nI suppose it was good practice for thinking on our feet, right?
All right, outsider. Let's go find my Gwenaelle and convince the Chronicle to transform her back into my beloved wife.
Go ahead, mainlander. Look for the ancient tree in the upper courtyard. I just need a moment to catch my breath, and then I'll be right behind you.

Well, we didn't find the relic. Shame. I'm tired of all this walking around. And I want to go back to Neri's room.\n\nThat carving does look druidic. So, we know this is the right place. Anything useful from what you collected?
Can't you see that I'm eating? It isn't often I get to feast on fresh food.\n\nGo talk to the lordling. He wants to speak to you.

Laurel and most of Galen's Stonelore Druids are in Glimmertarn. Inform her of the plan and tell her to prepare our circle for war. I'll meet you there after I convince Archdruid Ellic to do the same.\n\nThe village lies directly north of Vastyr.
Thank the Green, Frii doesn't seem to be hurt. Go ahead and speak with them.

Laurel, Ryvana, and I talked during the voyage. If Lord Bacaro truly means to awaken the spirit of the volcano, he's going to need to do it from inside Mount Firesong. And, since he knows we're coming, he'll throw everything he has in our way.

Elder Verline has the regalia and will begin the ritual. I hoped that when I laid down my authority, when I left the throne for the forest, the shadow over our people would have passed. Now I see that more is required.\n\nWill you aid me, old friend?

These marks are old. Similar to the tablet Dhulef found in High Rock. I doubt that's a coincidence. And it clearly shows Frii, or a spirit very much like them.\n\nLet's see if there are any more drawings while we look for Frii.
The seed rests just over there. Safe. Waiting. A quiet and strong thing, resting in different hands.\n\nGive it to Archdruid Rahval when we leave here. To take it into the unnatural walls.
Well? Is that what I think it is?
Lady Arabelle's assistant? How good to see you again, but I don't remember your name on my schedule today. Did we have an appointment?

You're Lady Arabelle's assistant, aren't you? Well, if you're here to talk to Lord Bacaro, you need to hurry. He plans to set sail for Galen with this last shipment of relief supplies. He's determined to lead the society's efforts to help the island.

Druid Calysa is a dear friend of mine. I want to do everything I can to support her research.\n\nGo ask her about it, if you like! She always gets so passionate when she has the chance to talk about her work.
Follow my instructions precisely. You need to ignite the fire shard, heat the sacred tree sap, and reforge the tablet in that order.
Do you have time to help some … well, Fauns aren't exactly defenseless creatures, but they are in danger.

The markers should be placed in Y'ffre's Path along the best, er, paths. Oh, you know what I mean!\n\nHmm, maybe you should talk to Sir Aval before you set out. You can find him near the Fighters Guild here in Vastyr.

This is the part of the story I hate the most. When we must inevitably say goodbye. As much as I try to avoid it, I have a terrible habit of growing quite attached to the people I work with. All that said, I will miss you most emphatically, my dear.
