I assume you're off on another adventure after this? Take me with you! I'm not sure I'm ready to deal with the responsibilities that come with my new title.
By the Green, it's good to see you and Captain Siravaen!
Go ahead, friend. Honor Frii's last request and sprinkle the soil around the base of the tree.
Archdruid Orlaith has Frii and has started the ritual. She's trying to regrow the sacred seeds into the Druid King's regalia. We have to stop her!
The Firesong know so much, and yet they are so lost. I do not know how to help them.
I still can't believe what happened. I thought it would be years until I assumed my father's title.\n\nI'm not … I don't think I'm ready.
We'll hold the docks. Then as soon as things are clear, I'll start my hunt for Sealord Nalos.
Count Mornard can tell you where you'll be most useful. I need to keep directing people away from the fighting. They'll be safer inside the cathedral.

Even with our combined ability, Bal Sunnar will be dangerous. But we must find the temporal distortion.\n\nOnce inside, we should split up. We can search faster that way. I'll observe your progress and contact you by projection.
Ah, there you are. Talk to Sir Stefan, mate. We might be in stormy waters, but he's got some ideas about which way we need to steer.
Sir Stefan is waiting for us in the throne room of Castle Mornard. I'll meet you there.
I heard about your involvement in ending the Firesong threat and dealing with Archdruid Orlaith. For saving our island and making sure Galphen and the other druids are safe, you have my thanks.
Be wary, friend. The islands grow angry. Something tries to fully awaken Mount Firesong and I fear what consequences that will bring.

I had hoped the letter would indicate who hired the mercenaries, but no. Anyway, the Shrine of the Golden Eye lies somewhere in Claw's Strike, proxy. I shall meet you there.\n\nOnce inside, we can use the three glyphics as Hermaeus Mora instructed.

This endeavor has made Keshargo realize that he is too old to be gallivanting across the planes. It's time he passed the mantle of Magnastylus to someone else. \n\nBut Keshargo will change the Itinerant Staff. He will remove the Umber Glyphic.
I'll ensure the elder makes it out of this outpost unharmed.\n\nWhen you rescue the others, tell them they can return safely to their camp.
Back again so soon, walker! Was there something else you wished to ask?
I'm a bit busy, but what may I help you with?
This was truly my worst fear, the worst fear of any auditor inspecting a mine. Without the queen these kwama are likely to stay crazed and a danger to everyone.

After analyzing the situation, I conclude that it is dire. We must protect Lord Seht's work from falling into unauthorized hands.\n\nPlease, reach the Clockwork Probabilis before the Painted Eye or Apostle Nilphas Drethan.

This thread led us to a powerful ally, the spirit of a Telvanni magister. And we learned that a Telvanni master aids our enemies—and plans to use one of Hermaeus Mora's own Black Books against him. The plot against Apocrypha becomes clearer, proxy.

Good, you found them. The compass will keep you apprised of my flock's whereabouts. The whistle's tune will deliver them back into my arms.\n\nWell go on, use it. Find my creatures so that the show can go on!
There's something foul inside those censers! This must be how the Peryite cultists made everybody in the Necropolis ill. We need to destroy the censers!
Have you found what you came here for? We patched up Barluk as best we can. Should be able to safely move him now. We'll meet you outside of the mine.
The way is open. Now, into the doorway!\n\nOur power fades, leaving only weakness. You may have to face her alone, outworlder.
Traveler, give me the book! I will gladly trade my memories for his life!
You're not burnt to a cinder or frozen to death! That's a qualified success in my book! I might need to take a detour through Takubar to grab a handful more of those.
You have an annoying tendency to disturb the course of fate, mortal. Makes my duties all the more difficult. I hope you're happy about that.

Leramil wouldn't tell me much, but we had a pleasant enough conversation. She told me about the spirit, Meln. And the Watchling Scruut. And she's very interested in what the keepers do in Necrom. Fascinating woman.\n\nShe's been waiting to talk to you.

Newer ciphers often begin their tenure in the Cloisters by studying in the Calamitous Gallery. Its particular portents can be quite … disheartening. Perhaps this is by design. To weed out the weak-willed, so to speak.

The Atlas Obscurum. A dangerous item in the wrong hands. The magic of the Cloisters flows through these pages. Inscribing and storing unsorted and unrefined predictions. To read this tome is to swim in the waters of celestial portents.
Do not worry. Huzmargo has performed this procedure hundreds of times. My record is flawle—er, my record is very, very good.

Since the vampire mercenary excused herself, we have the perfect opportunity to follow the thread of fate before Master Shelreni arrives.\n\nWe should find a way into the tower through that door. Lead the way, proxy.

Scour the stacks, proxy. The magicka I infused into your scroll shall assist you by retrieving any relevant tomes from their resting place.\n\nMeet me in my nearby study when you have completed your search.
You're here after all. I was about to reel in this piece of my past without you.\n\nI thought maybe you decided to move on.

A malignant substance permeates the very air of this endless shaft. I do not know how long we can withstand its effects. We must locate the source and disable it.\n\nPerhaps the ghost that haunts you can help us with this task?
This mortal is going to be the end of me. No, wait. Hermaeus Mora will be the end of me!

It's unfortunate we couldn't reach the glyphic before its unweaving, but all is not lost. If we work quickly, we should be able to salvage the magics still held within the fractured glyphic.\n\nI'll need your assistance once more, of course.

The Tranquil Archives hold many of Hermaeus Mora's oldest and most cherished secrets. They are tabulated in glyphics—stones of crystallized knowledge that endure for eons.\n\nLook for the intruders. They must be close by.
I'm … Magnastylus. Goodness. I don't even know what to say.
Something very wrong has happened here. There's a lab ahead—let's just keep fighting through.\n\nMaybe there we'll find out what's going on.
I can't believe she's chosen to stay. How did I end up so lucky to have someone like her find me?
Dacia's feelings may wither someday. But for now, she's found a path forward that will benefit everyone.
As terrible as the fabric of reality unraveling sounds, proxy, I imagine the actuality will be so much worse.
Do you really think Meln can assist us in circumventing the magister's ward? So few of the ancestor spirits I deal with are particularly helpful.
What? I told you I buried the components in different locations. Move your legs and I'll holler when I recognize something.

When Sharp contacted me about Dimik-ei, I knew I should have been doing much more, much sooner. My grief immobilized me too long. No longer.\n\nFedero and I found a solid lead on someone connected with Sondivel Ulres, the Reformer.
Don't dawdle! Who knows how many Daedra we'll have to deal with if Dreynis gets his hands on that prism again?\n\nAfter him, now! That's an order!
I've grown quite tired. The wonders of this world can be exhausting. Might I rest here? For a moment?
Looks like we got to that letter before Guitot. He never received his orders to slip away and make a break for the Dres camp. Makes my life easier.
It's right there, mortal! The spell worked! Go, collect the secret so I can finish this job.
A little further, and soon this will all be just another memory.

All right, try not to go on too much about how different I am from when you last saw me.\n\nUnless you're complimenting me. Oh, Federo! How brave of you to join us! Your skin looks stunning! Something like that would be nice.
A very informative update. Thank you. Now, you should get back to it. We'll all feel safer and more secure once this spy has been dealt with. Permanently.
There's so much to know about the world. I want to learn everything!

There's a chance Ansuul will return to the Dreamstone, but that will be a problem for a different time. For now, we celebrate Ansuul's defeat. This one has never felt Daedric presences retreat so quickly.
Was there anything in those papers about Master Shelreni or where we might find her?
Keep your eye on the adversary. Let's end this!

Laurel, Ryvana, and I talked during the voyage. If Lord Bacaro truly means to awaken the spirit of the volcano, he's going to need to do it from inside Mount Firesong. And, since he knows we're coming, he'll throw everything he has in our way.
That was rough, unrefined. I can do better. But we've got our first success, and a location. Fathoms Drift!

The entrance to the Forbidden Exhibits isn't too far away, but be careful. If there are too many Seekers we'll have to not be there. Does that make sense? First rule of surviving here: don't be where the Seekers are.
Go. See what my son has to say.
You tell Leramil what we learned from the spirit of Master Shelreni. I'm still trying to make sense of it and I'll just ramble and confuse everything.\n\nSort of like this, see?

I don't understand this death thing. Or spirits, either. Daedra aren't bound to such a limited and finite existence.\n\nBeyond that, spirit or no, can we trust anything Master Shelreni says? With reality hanging in the balance, I don't think so.

Listen carefully, mortal. Vaermina's power is limited here. This isn't her realm. It's only due to the necromancy they used on Shelreni's body that she made it this far.\n\nShe's placed a dream around us, but the true memory is still here.
Go. I sense that Gadayn and Scruut are in danger. I … shall catch up as soon as I can.
You're not going to, ehm- tell him about this, are you?
I work with Oathman Llaro, not for him. If you have business with him, get to it.
Poor Leramil! I hate to see her suffering like that! She'll be all right, won't she?\n\nI know, I know. Now is not the time. We need to find the manufactory. Right, right.
I've certainly made a deal or two with a Daedra in my day. And it's not like we have much choice. I don't think Scruut and Leramil can hold themselves together much longer.
While I too have issues with Hermaeus Mora, I have no desire to see his realm and its inhabitants suffer. Believe what you wish, but I speak true.
Whatever Torvesard did, it certainly helped. But I can still feel the constant throb of Apocrypha's pain. It won't be long before it incapacitates me again—or worse.
You return? Forgive me if I'm not pleased to see you, traveler. I have a feeling you bring me more unfortunate news. Let me guess: another dead cipher, and a volume of the Numinous Grimoire.

I was told to expect you, and here you are. Congratulations, traveler. You've been tended by the Gardener of Men. Plucked for a special task.\n\nHermaeus Mora requires your help in reclaiming a portion of his realm from his enemies.
Of course. Just when I think I can go and rest my weary tentacles, the Great Eye has another task for me.\n\nTalk to Leramil, mortal. I need to confer with the Prince of Fate.

I'm both relieved and a bit disappointed that we can't accompany you, my friend. I'll stay with Leramil and Scruut until you return.\n\nI'd pray that the ancestors walk beside you, but now that I think about it, you have Meln. So they already do.
I wish to hear all about what you found at the Prismatic Iris Shore, but I can wait my turn. Meln has manifested and wants to speak with you.

Did I hear correctly? Did Naryu hire you to help her complete her writ? Well, just be aware. That's not coming out of the assembly treasury! Any arrangement such as that is between you and the Morag Tong.
Take great care when handling these relics. They aren't simple trifles. Truth be told, I wish collecting them weren't necessary. Too much magical power in one place can be disastrous.

I love my sister, but she's wrong. Our focus should be on freeing our father from this curse. We can't afford to waste time searching for scattered pages just yet. Traveler, you may be our only hope. May I ask for your aid?

I did not devote myself to the realm of knowledge because I love mysteries. Still, Tho'at Replicanum isn't exactly a mystery anymore. We know what she is and how to deal with her.\n\nAll in all, this partnership we forged has been successful.
Traveler, the young Yensa may be on to something. Ah, forgive me. I am Gilvas Vedran, Mouth to Master Faras and his children.\n\nIf you'll lend me an ear, I have a proposal that may interest you.

Tho'at Replicanum, huh? Just when I thought I knew all the secrets this place had to share. \n\nI wonder how we're going to file her away. Not that I will file her, there's too many copies still running around. But, I should have a plan for it.

Are you real? With those clothes you must be. Next question. Can you find things? Have you lost things before? A sock, your memory, the love of the gods? \n\nDoesn't matter. I have and I will and I need to not lose that last one.

I was hoping for a cohort of legionaries from Skingrad, but you'll have to do. I don't even know where to begin. Our entire shipment of Blue Aedral is gone and my dear Lazen is still in there, chasing down whoever attacked us.
Ithelia was imprisoned here, in the heart of the Mythos? Has she been here all these centuries? That—no, there is no time for questions. We must stop Torvesard from releasing her!
We cannot let the loss of Gadayn deter us from our purpose. Place the fragment in the ritual circle.
There are a few temporal threads I need to account for while I finish determining the nature of the ritual Leramil and I developed. Talk to her for a moment and let me think.

Figures the one day I finally make it to these ruins they're overrun with danger. \n\nThis is what I get for procrastinating on collecting those Aetherial shards. Bad enough to handle Goblins and minotaurs without tossing necromancers into the mix!

I see Shardmarshal Vargas standing on those rocks by the portal. This is the portal my legionary wants us to close, and I couldn't agree more.\n\nWe're in for a tough fight, but we can't fail. Destroy those anchors, comrade. Then we're out of here.
Are you one of those Recollection? No. I don't know who you are, or if you're trustworthy, but you look like you can fight. \n\nHow do you feel about fighting for me if I pay you?
Scruut told me what happened here. Imagine, an apparatus that could change fate and alter history! How could even a Daedric Prince control such power?
You dispatched that creature? I'm impressed.
Valente's alchemical equipment is truly impressive. It's a shame we have to destroy it, but we need to make sure no one else can continue his experiments.
I used to be quiet as a cat walking on a mammoth-fur pelt. Oh, well. What did Endegor drop?
Careful now, a cunning and foul beast has made off with an important document and played Mizzik for a fool. Perhaps you can help retrieve it?
I was outside searching for Betu when I heard Aquilia scream. By the time I got here, the killer was gone.
We must study the scene carefully. Look for anything that seems out of place. This one's whiskers are already trembling with excitement. Or, perhaps it is the dust?

Despite the threat Ithelia poses, it was never her intention to cause the tears in fate's fabric and threaten the stability of reality. If prison is merely a stopgap, then your notion to leave this realm has merit.\n\nSee what the One Who Knows thinks.
The fraying of these threads has only just begun. Torvesard was here, and quite recently. Follow this trail with care—he may still be close by, or have allies here. I shall join you momentarily.
I believe we are done here. Let Fennorian know I wish a moment of his time. And tell him it has nothing to do with hurt feelings or a broken heart. I am above such petty concerns.
Hermaeus Mora imprisoned Ithelia right here in the middle of Apocrypha? Incredible! What happens if she gets out?\n\nNever mind. I guess that's exactly what we're trying to stop.

Don't know what you did, but the woman by the fire finally left. Sure, she just followed you downstairs for some unknown reason, but that's progress.\n\nStill seeing the strange stuff, though. Bring back some sugar so we can make her that drink.
Apologies. Recent events have been overwhelming to say the least. I needed some fresh air and my dear Uriel saw fit to join me. Is there anything I can help you with?

I'm Uriel, son of our dearly departed. I appreciate you and the Khajiit's help in fulfilling my mother's final wishes. If only Aquilia and Pelena were as focused. So much talk of conspiracy …. I'm certain it's the grief talking.
Please, don't worry about me. Save the dog. It's what my aunt would have wanted.

Between the Recollection and the dangers inherent in most ruins, I suggest caution. My research revealed that Elenglynn contains a maze filled with deadly traps. We must reach the heart of the maze to find a way through.\n\nI am ready when you are.
Do you think the Legion can hear the bells?
Same as last time. Place the canister and then stand clear.

I stored weapons beyond your comprehension in Bedlam Veil. \n\nIf you want to keep your appendages where they are, don't touch anything you don't recognize. You'll need your limbs intact to defeat the Blind and her cultists.

My interactions with the One Who Knows have been complicated and interesting in the century we have been associated, but never anything such as we have encountered.\n\nI am glad you were beside me in all this, proxy.

We know the Staff of Many Paths was used in a ritual to prepare the wildburn seeds. If Nantharion's using the staff in all those places, we could be looking at a massive wildburn event—something big enough to destroy Skingrad and all of West Weald.
Just think of it. No one's opened this vault in thousands of years! Place the lesser welkynd stones in their sockets, and we'll see what the Ayleids of Niryastare were so anxious to protect.

What a strange feeling! I'm not sure what to call it, but I'm definitely not sad that the Great Eye's plan actually worked. Not that I ever doubted it ….\n\nAnyway, the fabric of reality should totally restore itself now. Let's return to Beragon's.

I'm glad you're back, friend. Now that the worst of things is over, I thought a celebration was in order—and Count Calantius agreed! Everyone should know what you did for West Weald. \n\nCracked acorns, what you did for all of reality!

Even if we can see where Nantharion used the staff, there's no guarantee we'll still find him at those sites. I'll confer with my scouts and get help from Vashabar. The more eyes out there helping us look for the Recollection, the better.

Any adventurer who delves into Ayleid ruins knows the name Miscarcand. It was a great Ayleid city, but it's been lost for ages. If Nantharion is truly descended from its ancient rulers, that would explain the Recollection's fascination with Ayleids.
The Recollection had someone close to the king, all right. Nantharion's been laughing at us all along!\n\nCome on. We need to burn that seed and settle accounts with that two-faced skeever!
Now that we know what Vargas can do, I'll stand watch. We need to see what that memory wants to tell us.\n\nGo ahead, comrade. Use the Echonir.
Leramil's back! You should tell her what happened in Miscarcand, friend. Maybe she's got an idea about where Ithelia went or what she's likely to do next.

I spotted the seed in a clearing up the hill. It looked … I don't know, ready to burst or something! Go burn it. But watch yourself. There are more Recollection around.\n\nWe'll stay here and hold off any that try to pass.

Hesitation will not serve us now. Enter Nonungalo, traveler. I will be along after I consecrate the corpse. According to Arkay, mortality should be honored in all its forms, even when the deceased is a necromancer.

The people of West Weald owe you a great debt—as does the One Who Knows. I suspect your actions here are the only reason we still have a chance to avert disaster. Conclude your business with Beragon, proxy. The next battle awaits.
Was this Primordial Titan really one of Ithelia's first creations? No matter. Let's destroy it and grab a shard to take back with us.

These ruins are pretty amazing. If we weren't battling Recollection forces and trying to beat them to the wildburn seed, I'd love to just explore them.\n\nSome people find the weight of history to be crushing. I find it exhilarating!
The way forward is clear. I just hope that portal isn't going to drop us into the middle of a Shardborn war camp or a nest of hungry crystaljacks.\n\nI guess I'm ready when you are, friend.
This part of Fargrave seems more familiar, but I still cannot shake the notion that this demiplane has a deeper connection to Ithelia than I ever suspected.
Good work, comrade! I have a feeling our adversaries weren't expecting us to cut our way out of this strange prison. That means we have a chance to surprise them.\n\nThrough the portal!
Go on, place the items atop the altar so we can consider our next step.
Hello, my friend. Would you be interested in helping the great adventurer, <<1>>? He's busy exploring a nearby Ayleid ruin, and I fear for his safety.
The Lamp of Clarity can no longer help us. Pulling Tribune Alea out of the Many Paths used up the last of its power.\n\nWe cannot use it again in our efforts to escape this prison.

Hopefully, a private chat without stubborn nobles or proud treethanes around can give Calantius and Darolith the opportunity to talk frankly and be flexible in their negotiations.\n\nIf this goes well, I might have to add diplomat to my portfolio!

Proxy, your arrival is well-timed. A tangle in the threads of fate grows like a knot around the Outcast Inn. Something frays the bonds of cause and effect here. If they snap, the results would be catastrophic.

Like before, this path stirred up memories. I experienced the same dread before Hermaeus Mora's forces arrived.\n\nBut I did not collapse like a coward. I commanded my Shardborn to resist and they obeyed. The struggle I recall was … epic.
My master prefers it when the mortals they watch entertain them. If—over the course of stopping this invasion—you feel the need to die, please do it in an entertaining manner.

We can rendezvous at the Stonechip Gambling Den after you speak with Baron Carvain and Lady Raxalee. They have offices here in town.\n\nMeanwhile, I want to look into Healer Nevama's death. Find out exactly what happened.

It seemed like she sliced the air to open a portal. I don't know a thing about magic so I can't advise you on how to use Abolisher.\n\nMaybe just think real hard about the keep when you make the cut? Couldn't hurt.

Beragon has told me some of what occurred at Vashabar and Hoperoot. I am eager to hear more, but first you should speak with him. We are at a crossroads and must choose our path wisely or we shall court disaster.
I gave you an order, mercenary. Get to it!\n\nGrab that oil that's behind you first. I'll walk you through everything else.
The ritual still hangs heavy around this place. That's why there are so many sodding bugs.\n\nThe seedpod we need should be close by. Let's go find one!
Keep your eyes open. The Heartland Elves offer many lessons to those willing to listen. But other things live in these ruins now.
This whole situation is as foul as a midden the day before chores. I just hope Gundelion or Malaniel can help us out. \n\nAnd don't worry, I'll have those supplies sorted soon enough.
Green keep you, traveler. I hope you enjoy everything our village has to offer.
Ah, a visitor to our fair village. Perhaps you'd like to hear about the Dawnway, the new path forward for Bosmer and Vashabar? I can tell you all about it!
I have so much respect for Minth. It kills me to think he won't listen to his own son. And when everything we've worked for is so close at hand.

I'm like a litter of fisher pups on the inside, all flailing limbs and lashing tails. I can't believe Laeni thinks she has to leave town. Her father will be heartbroken. \n\nY'ffre's tears, I'll be heartbroken!
Well met. Vashabar … and Valenwood … welcomes you warmly.
No matter what we find in here, I'll be right beside you. Let's do this.

Walker! I am relieved to see you alive. I thought I could trust my mentor with what I learned about Zerith-var, but she turned right around and told the Inquisitors!\n\nThank Azurah you managed to evade them. But I fear you arrived too late.
I will tend to Krin'ze's wounds. Speak to her and learn of what transpired here. Try to ignore the mistrustful eyes of her companion.
Go carefully. Wisteria is a powerful mage. Diplomacy is likely out of the question, but perhaps Bogcup can reason with her.\n\nIn the meantime, I will make my way to the Gardener's greenhouse.
Go ahead. Place the Lamp of Clarity near the tear in reality. Just do so carefully.
After all my good works, they still come for me. What does Mora see that I do not?
Give me a moment to pull myself together. Tan's got that fidgety look that means they want to chat. Go talk to them.

Everyone keeps talking about these odd things happening to them. They're saying it's this Netch Luminary. Funny enough though, nothing's happened to me.\n\nWait. Does that mean the Netch doesn't like me?
You've got the crystal? Put it on the altar, and let's see what happens.
The voice is coming from over there. \n\nI hope it's not who I think it is. Bella shouldn't be here. The Sharp Tooth Goblins are in a dangerous mood, and she sounded way too close.
The east wing should still have a replacement crystal boxed up somewhere. \n\nDon't let the Scholarium's defenses stand in your way. Hurry now.
Peer through the lens, reveal the wards, and claim the key fragment. This may seem a small step, but an incredible path waits before you.
How were you able to find Wisteria? We've exhausted every method at our disposal in our search for her and came up fruitless.\n\nAnd did you discover the truth about her plans?
Well done, mortal. You have risen to the challenge. One task remains. \n\nIf I am to lend you my strength, you must lend me yours. Power for power. A wrong righted, and another step on the path.

Don't worry, a few wards around the library and we'll make sure the page thief doesn't strike again.\n\nIn the meantime, perhaps Nahlia has found something left behind by Ulfsild over in the east wing.
Perhaps I could put some protection runes on the most valuable tomes.\n\nThat's still, what? A couple hundred books or so? Not like I have anything better to do.
And here I was worried that I'd be finding you at a dead end. What did Ulfsild's echo have to say?
The path to master Scribing seems to be a winding one, eh? Fable upon fable.\n \nExcept, I know I've heard the story of Mizbi before and when I paged through earlier it seemed … off.
Caelum hasn't killed her yet, thank the Eight. But I have a feeling he's just waiting for an audience. Well, I'm not going to lose any more Scarlets.\n\nI know how to get her away from him.
Breaking down doors was easier twenty years ago. Go on, friend. It's up to you and Hooke now!
I'll look after Big Urm. Go with Hooke and get Val back!
Do you need something, traveler? I'm waiting on a friend of mine to bring me something very important.

Prison was harder on Naku than the rest of us. Something about being in chains or cages when he was younger. When we were released, he couldn't get away fast enough. He had to know he was free and clear, for certain.

This one has never experienced anything like that before. The weightlessness. The feeling of freedom! It was not unlike stepping though a portal, but prolonged. \n\nThe citadel is filled with many secrets.
You there! I'm a captain in the West Weald Legion and I require your assistance.
Please be gentle here in the Wilderhall, traveler. Some of these documents are hundreds and hundreds of years old.
Which riddles will you solve, I wonder? You need only complete some to prove yourself. But choices, as always, say much about the chooser.
We should hurry. I don't know how much time the ink will buy us before Jahones passes. The first piece of his soul is on the other side of that portal.
Soar suspended by your good intentions, Not-Ulfsild. The clinic is in the town of Suran, on the isle of Vvardenfell. \n\nThe knight will be an effervescent addition to your trial. I just know it.
The Fox told us about his plan when we chatted earlier. It sounds like an incredible project. \n\nJust be careful, all right? The Daedric Princes aren't known for their good humor.
Hello. I'm a legionary in the West Weald Legion. Have you had any experience tracking creatures? How would you like to perform a great service for Count Calantius of Skingrad?
I have heard only dark words spoken of the once-proud city of Orcrest. A place of danger and disease. May Azurah watch over us.
What a curious relic Zerith-var wields. Shearing doors between one location and another? This one feels the Lunar Lattice at work and looks forward to witnessing his powers when we reach Orcrest.
I'm stuck here while they tally my tab. It could be a while.\n\nTry looking for my fear somewhere secluded, like a cave or ruin. I think she's southwest of Ontus.
It makes sense, the way to the Deadlands being in a burnt-up village.\n\nI decided to hide up here until you arrived. I'm being careful, see?

Mortal! Welcome back. Standing against injustice is a reward all its own, but you have my thanks as well.\n\nThe time I've had with my oldest and dearest friend has been a balm on my heart. And together, we've come up with a plan.
Is this where she spent her final years? It's beautiful.

Welcome to my roost, to the Wing of the Crow. I am a Luminary just like the others. Though I'm the youngest of our number by far.\n\nRight now, my fable lacks a fitting end. I hope that you and Nahlia can change that.
Viti is safe, thank the moons. But where are the other cantors? This cannot be all that remains.
Let's press ahead. I've read and heard so much about this place, being able to walk the Labyrinthian, even a version of the Labyrinthian, is damned inspiring.
You're the one holding the key! Quick, unlock Snapdragon's cell.
Talk to Hyacinth, would you? I need to think about what happened in there. He'll understand.
Wisteria is dead. Despite everything she did. All the pain she caused. It still hurts.\n\nOleander. Snapdragon. Gladiolus. Was it worth it? All those lives. I wish I could ask her.
We are safe, my friend. For now.
Not now, tamiit! We must deal with Izalgo-morna!
No time for words, tamiit! Now is a time for song and combat!
This shrine is not as abandoned as it seems. Let us tread with caution.
Used to be branches I'd have to worry about being the death of me. Now it's deadlines.\n\nIf only I weren't so cheap about hiring an assistant when I first started this book.
Stay back from me, necromancer! My soul is not yours for the taking!

I came to this hidden fortress expecting Daedric portals or a cult performing ritual sacrifice. Not a noble family like the Albuses kidnapping soldiers.\n\nI prefer meeting allies, but I will fight you if you're with them.
Back at the trading post, I thought Zerith's concern was misplaced. But now ….\n\nI am glad he ended that last memory where he did. I feel shaken. Cold. Like we just saw the face of Namiira herself.

You fought good, pal. It was an honor to fight at your side and take out Mezamma.\n\nBut you should talk to Gabrielle. I don't like that look on her face. Last time I saw it, she made it rain on me for three straight days!

No more talking until I get those mistscrub leaves. It grows west of here. In the old village. Bushes with jagged red leaves.\n\nCome back and then we'll talk. I'll be here. Not like I can get very far in this condition.

Good job taking down Mezamma, but we're not safe yet. As Prince Azah and I were meeting with representatives of the Three Alliances, we received reports of soul reapers and Worm Cult attack squads appearing across Tamriel.\n\nIt's bad out there.

I feel the distinct crackle of illusion magic emanating from somewhere in this room. We must find whatever it hides.\n\nSearch carefully, though. I'd prefer that we both escape from this Worm Nest alive.
I am Sister Chana's shield. Just because my back is to her, do not think I am not protecting her.
My superiors in Elden Root demanded I keep accurate notes of everything said and done during these unusual proceedings.

Mazza-Mirri means to see if you are worthy of wielding the Moonlight Blade?\n\nMy moonclaw is a shadow of this most holy implement. I am not worthy of it. But you, tamiit? I would not be surprised. Face this test. I am with you no matter the outcome.

My superiors in Daggerfall gave me very strict orders. Do not commit to any definitive course of action, but at the same time avoid suggesting we will not cooperate. Which is to say, I'm firmly stuck between a rock and a hard place.
Why did they waste my time on this fool's errand? This is a task better suited to the Skald King's buffoon, Rigurt.
I came as soon as I received Gabrielle's summons, just in time to see you all return. But where's Vanus? And why do Gabrielle and Skordo look so haggard? What happened at that Worm Nest, comrade?
I'm sorry, but I'm not actually entertaining guests right now. Not much in the mood, really. You're welcome to come calling another time.
Please, take the necklace to Guendeline and let her know how I feel about her.
I take it you aren't one of the refugees.
Speak up and talk fast. After that surprise attack, I'm not feeling very trusting or hospitable toward strangers.
I'm ready when you are.
You have my thanks. If the Mages Guild found him like that, I'd have a lot to explain.\n\nFlaying, on the other hand ….
Blood. Blood. Blood. Blood. Blooooood!\n\nHear it rushing in your limbs. Smell it through your skin. Taste it in my mouth. Give it. Give it. Give it!
Leave me ….

I hesitate to ask you for further assistance, but if you're willing, your help would certainly be appreciated.\n\nOur leader, Abbot Durak, left some time ago and hasn't returned. I fear he may be injured … or worse.
Returning the Dream Shard to its rightful place is no small victory, but Vaermina attacks on several fronts.\n\nI kept this quiet, but Azura warned me. There is another Omen.
Ah! You've come from Pariah Abbey, haven't you? \n\nDon't worry about giving me the bad news. I'm already expecting the worst.
We must move quickly now to save the lake though.\n\nI have enough essences stored away to create the Water Stone, but I lack some crucial elements to complete the ritual.
I fear the time is running short. The poison has nearly consumed the poor little thing.\n\nIf we don't do something now, she will transform at any moment. Have you brought the heartwood?

The Imperial threat's over, for now at least … but the Reachmen are coming, and we've lost precious time when we should have been preparing.\n\nI think we'll need to stop the Reachmen's advance at Northglen. I would welcome your counsel though.
Hallin's Stand won't forget you, no matter how long the years. And neither will I.
Bring a dreaming Supernal—and hurry. \n\nRestraining the Daedra inside me grows difficult.
Whoever's sabotaged my family's work is going to have to answer to me!
You have done well, wayfarer. Tu'whacca is pleased.

I understand the Withered Hand's been driven away. That's good. We're out of the deep desert. \n\nBut we still haven't arrived at the oasis. Some of the dead that were risen—we can't just assume their going to return to their rest.

Hold up, wayfarer. The port has been taken over by necromancers—members of the Withered Hand.\n\nIt is good you have come, because we need your assistance. But you should know the situation before you go any further.
What desire brings you here, mortal? You seek the Orc female, perhaps?\n\nShe is now an ornament to my … collection.

My secret is revealed. I provided our old master with his life source, the blood of our students, but no more!\n\nThough it means my death, I'm glad you've witnessed this. Before you kill me, I must beg one favor of you. Destroy <<1>>.
When you understand the ways your opponent approaches battle, no strategy can overcome you.\n\nIf you can defeat all of my students, then I will count you as an equal to them. Are you prepared?
And now, we must be vigilant against the old master, who knows our secrets and our ways.\n\nIf I see her again, I will gladly fight her to her death, for the honor of Leki's Blade.

I regret that political disagreements between Crowns and Forebears should impede a criminal investigation, but recent events have increased tensions dramatically.\n\nI am confident that your assistance in the investigation will prove to be valuable.
Walk with Tu'whacca.

I welcome you to Bergama, wayfarer. I hope you brought your gold. Our markets have goods you can find nowhere else in all Tamriel.\n\nRegardless of any rumors in the streets, I can assure you the city is safe. So stay as long as you like.
Hm?
You've made the right choice.\n\nThat cultist would do the same to us, if he could.
You have my word. I'll have my men remove the eggs. \n\nFor Mara's sake, stop looking at me like that!
I promised to protect Tabakah, but I hope the road back to Pariah Abbey isn't too bad.\n\nI know a few enchantments, but they won't do me much good against a group of bandits.

Your timing is impeccable. I am on a critical mission for the Mages Guild, and I need assistance.\n\nThese ruins contain a powerful relic—King Aphren's Sword. With all the chaos in this region, the ogres, these cultists, the sword is not safe.

You're welcome to Alcaire Castle. I'm sure you noticed King Fahara'jad's army camped outside our walls. So you can understand why Duke Nathaniel is not entertaining guests. \n\nI should hope you're not here to add to our troubles.

You're welcome to Koeglin Village, traveler, but you'll have to excuse me. No time for idle chat.\n\nThe town's been attacked by slavers—and to make matters worse—they had help from people we would have expected to be on our side.
This doesn't make sense. There has to be something … anything … some sign of what happened to my father.\n\nCan you help me? Can you help me sift through these ashes?
So, you took out <<1>>. Nice trick, that.
Sasana is in one of the warehouses on the hill overlooking the docks. You can trust her.
My sister Jehanne has a plan to help the villagers, but we need your assistance. \n\nIf you're willing to help us, please talk to her.
You're back and you're safe. Thank the Divines. I was afraid we lost you.
I wonder what happened to Gelvin? He should have been back by now.\n\nMaybe his sister Granette knows where he might have gotten to.
If you see my idiot brother, cuff him on the ear for me. Our production falls behind with the johads so unreliable.

Find a keepsake of Rosalind's in order to strengthen your bond to her. Fight through the invaders, the walking dead you see around here, just as she once did. \n\nOne of them may have taken something from her as they battled.

Please, wayfarer, we must move quickly, lest our enemies steal the prize and slip away into the shifting sands.\n\nWhere is Gabrielle? This is why sorcerer-types make me nervous. They're just so unpredictable!
Can you believe it? My spell actually worked and you were able to uncover Faolchu's secret!\n\nSay, if you ever want to help me with another … experiment … I wouldn't turn you down.
The guardians are free, thanks to you.
You'll have to fight some werewolves, but you should be able to enter the city through the western gate. \n\nFind Darien and get his master key.

Believe it or not, this is the High Temple of Satakalaam. Everyone agreed it was the most beautiful temple in all Alik'r … before the Imperials came.\n\nBut they have defiled our sacred space. I do not know how we can restore its former glory.
Are you a guard? Have you come to rescue us?
Ah, a new recruit! If you're here to help, we could certainly make use of you.
Angof the Gravesinger is as good as dead. \n\nOr is he already dead? Or undead? Anyway, this is almost over.
Go. Stop the Bloodthorn. I'll go after my father.
Just make sure you protect that civilian. Volunteers don't grow on trees around here, you know.
The guardians will always be grateful.
I just let a bandit go on your word and he vanished in a cloud of smoke. If you're going to do something, do it. Don't make me regret this.
Did you find Ildani's wares? This one expected a much swifter recovery.
I thought you were here to help? I really need more werewolf blood if I'm going to make a cure.
Good day to you. You've heard of me, of course. I'm Glenumbra's foremost expert on ancient artifacts.
Gautier believes his son Darien is still alive inside the city. \n\nIf that's true, we can use it to our advantage—Darien is Camlorn's Captain of the Guard.
It's done then. He can now rest again … for good this time. \n\nI suppose I should be relieved, but somehow I feel like I've let him down.

Oh! Such a relief to see a familiar face in this ghastly desert! Particularly today.\n\nYou helped me get the Crown of Anton. Would you consider assisting in my archeological efforts again? I've encountered something of a setback here.

Well, well, well! If it isn't my old friend from Crosswych. Let me guess—Lady Laurent has you helping clean up this mess she made?\n\nOr is it Stibbons? The bootless coward. He's hoping Lady Laurent will forgive him.
Please, hurry! Who can say what <<1>> has gotten his paws on while I've been stuck?
Be wary in the woods. A distracted predator becomes prey in the blink of an eye.
I'll be all right in a few moments. Seems my old age is catching up to me. Happens to all of us eventually, I suppose.
Are the Elves all gone then? Praise the Eight! \n\nAll right then. Maybe I have a chance now. You won't believe this, but my boss, Lady Laurent, told me she no longer needs my service!
That woman looked at me as if I were an insect. I don't know what I did to make her angry, but I hope I don't run into her again.

Tavern, I said! Meet me in a tavern. There's no ale down here, just zombies and tentacles. And where are the serving wenches? You promised me serving wenches!\n\nAh well, at least your timing is perfect.
I don't have the time or the patience to deal with outsiders. \n\nIf you wish to join the Fighters Guild, get to Daggerfall.
And everything was just starting to go so well, too.
Well, that was the fun part. Now the real work begins. \n\nTell me, have you ever questioned a prisoner?
I haven't seen her come back here, but I will shout if she does return.
Forgive me if I seem rattled. Between Draven's illness and all this mystery, I'm jumping at shadows.\n\nPlease do what you can to find out how Kerbol cures these people.
If Draven remained alive, the spell over the whole town would have broken, leaving us all as he was - a mindless, slavering beast. I would not wish that fate on anyone.
You're the Covenant scum who knocked me out and tied me up.\n\nI'm going to slice you into ribbons.
I endured your imperial lashes. I endured your burns and the beatings. \n\nI—wait! You're not one of them, are you? What do you want with me?
Please don't disturb me. I know it's difficult to understand, but I am actually working here.
You ignorant half-wit! By the Golden Eye, what in Oblivion are you doing? \n\nSetting those poor, ensorcelled fools free? Don't you realize we were trying to help them?

That should cause some problems between the Bloodthorn and the Red Rooks. \n\nMaybe we'll get lucky and they'll kill each other off. I wouldn't mind going home to my family and leaving them to fight it out.
Keep up the good work and report back to me as soon as you have some solid evidence for me to act upon.
I've always known my daughter would be good with diplomacy. I said it all along.
With Ufa back, the Imperials don't stand a chance.
Burn the ballistae and ladders outside the gate. That'll set those bastards back.\n\nLook for me when you're done.
You have brought credit to your house. This is a great thing. \n\nHouse Indoril will always speak well of your actions here today.
You've chosen to water the land. This is good. \n\nFind the relics once owned by the spectral commanders. Then meet me at the nearby shrine. Go well along the river.
I don't understand any of this. Do what you must.
Vivec guide us, his scream … so much pain. \n\nIs it done?
Did you find Strikes-from-Shadows, my friend?
There's still the Orc warchief to take care of.
Mind the stories the spirits tell you. There's much to be learned from talking to the dead.
There is no hospitality here, stranger. Our village was attacked!
Have you found our stones? And the branch?
Halt, soldier! The Nedes are amassing just beyond the ridgeline. I need to speak to General Balreth. Have you seen him?
Go. And remember—try to sound humble when you chant Mavos' name.\n\nWhen you meet me at the center of Othrenis, be ready. There is more to do there.
The wretched Goblins must pay for the death they've brought upon my family.
The Goblin attacks have killed most of my kinsmen, and they've taken Hrogar's boys.\n\nThe skalds will sing a dirge about this day.
Go, my friend. Stop Tanval from getting himself killed. I've already lost too much today.
Poor Garyn. He did not deserve this. The current in the maelstrom pulled him under.
The merchant abides with the Ghost Snake now. It was his destiny.
Don't you have a Coiled Path to walk?
I hope your arrival will prove a boon to Ebonheart. Residents are at each other's throats.
There will need to be an accounting with this Rhavil.
Careful, traveler. A curse is loose on Heimlyn Keep. You walk her paths at your own peril.
Thank you so much for agreeing to keep my secret. I promise, I'll make it up to Boril and the miners. You have my word on that.
Who in Oblivion are you? This place isn't safe.
You shouldn't be here. A terrible curse afflicts these halls.
Seek the counsel of <<1>> and <<2>>. Their opinions reflect the thoughts of the villagers. As arbiter, we must abide your ultimate decision.

Three murders and Stormhold's about to boil over like my father's fish kettle! The Dark Elves blame the Argonians they owned before the Pact outlawed slavery.\n\nI miss the days of kicking arse. Now I'm expected to kiss them.
Say something. Speak, before I hack you apart.

You don't know what you've done, but how could you? Blood still pumps below the surface of your skin. You still feel hunger, desire, and the warmth of the sun.\n\nGo. May your life be as long as mine.
Don't … don't tell me about my son. Please. I must be strong. For Kragenmoor.
You're back, and with meat on your bones. Everything went well in there?
It's the creature! It's in Ulov!
You return?
You've done well. Communion with the Hist is the right of all pilgrims who complete their trials.
The sword is on the table just there. Don't worry, it's a cast-off from the military. That blade's already seen plenty of days in a scabbard.
Keep an eye out for anything suspicious. Something's not right here. I won't rest until we figure it out.
We no longer hear the wailing of our people. Have you freed them?
We're in your debt. What you've done here will reunite the people.
Excellent work. We're one step closer to imprisoning the Brother of Strife.
Go carefully as you head west, my friend. I fear the stormclouds are thickest where ash meets the sea.
I have not seen her attack prey so fiercely. What quarrel does she have with you?
Good news. I've been given a command. Tomorrow, we push the Covenant out of Stonefalls!\n\nI'll see you again on the long road to victory, friend.
Oh! Hello! You match the description of someone we were told to watch for.
You are a true hero to the Dunmer. I shall see that your praises are sung far and wide.\n\nThank you. For everything.
Has the target met an untimely end?
Father and I have broken the ward on the gate. Get in there, my friend.

The sanctuary is on this floor, just through that door. I must tell you truly, friend: I don't know if the Tribunal will answer you.\n\nI've asked for aid since the Ashlanders arrived, but they haven't responded to my pleas. Perhaps they will for you.
May the Three guard your steps as you do their work.
Good work rescuing the emissaries. Remember to speak to <<1>>. I'm sure she could use your help.
You've done it! Namira's been defeated! Look—the miasma is clearing.\n\nA few Dremora still lurk along the road, but their hold on Xal Ithix is broken.
So much death and treachery. These skin-stealers are criminals of war.
The Dremora will turn on you in a heartbeat, likely your last. I bet she'd pull your heart from your chest to show you.

It matters not what the lizard told you, our bargain stands. Release me and learn the skin-stealers' secrets, or don't and become <<1>>'s victim.\n\nDo you like my robes? I think they're named Okanil. A shame they stopped dripping.
I'm going to watch after <<1>>. Hopefully he'll wake up soon.\n\nDeal with whoever did this to him. We need to take care of our own!
Aimless wandering doesn't suit you.
You're always welcome here. You may not be a Shadowscale, but you have shown yourself to be a friend.\n\nWalk in Sithis' shadow, outsider.
Hopefully, the prisoners will let you in. We need that keystone.
We hear your decision, blessed of the Night Mother.
We lost many eggs today, yet some remain to bask in the light. May the sun warm you, wherever you go.
Will you protect the spirits from the Dominion during the ritual?
All of them slain! You aren't one to famish my darling Sithis. I will remember this, supplicant.\n\nBefore you culled their last breaths, what did you learn from the prisoners?
Let's go.
I'm not amused. Was this your scheme the whole time?\n\nNever mind. Get out of my sight and never come back. As far as I'm concerned, you're a traitor to the Pact.
I'll serve <<1>> as I served you, walker in shadow and in light. For truly, I only serve the Night Mother.
Aelif is sure she will see you again, hero.
Saervild must be stopped and the relics returned before the Dominion learns their secrets.
You're not with the Renrijra pirates, are you? No, you don't have their stink.\n\nI could use some help, and I swear by the sap of my Hist that it won't do your purse any harm.
We're hoping to put one over on these pirates before they sober up.\n\nGo talk to my partner, Looks, up at the camp.
I know you'll change the river's course, comrade. They're investigating the wilds nearby, above the Starved Plains.
Thank Stendarr! You're with the guild?
This is no time for talk!
You're back. Did you find my father?
Trust the Arch-Mage. Go with his familiar. \n\nWe'll wait right here. Really.
I see the messenger found you, comrade! We've discovered much since our adventure in Mzeneldt. The events of the past continue to stalk us.
The Earth Forge breached. Jofnir murdered! Stendarr give us strength.
<Ja-Reet does not respond.>
What has the fire revealed?
We're holding them here. Rally the others. Quickly!
The river runs with poison here. You'll want to stay back while we work our way inside.
You have my eternal gratitude for returning the shards of the Crystal of Power to me.\n\nOf course, I could still use more help, if you're willing.
Have you found the shards?
Bury me under the oak tree when I die.

The Dominion stirred up the lamias nesting within <<1>>. Keep your voice low, I understand they're quite sensitive to sound.\n\nYou were the one ray of sunlight to shine upon <<2>>. Come, brighten my day.
Do what you must, then see Belron. The less I know about it, the happier I'll be.
Well done!
Bravo! Author, author! Oh wait, that's me ….
This is going to change the fate of my people, friend. I'll take this to Sentinel immediately!
The Eight bless and keep you, traveler.
Ever since you rescued him, <<1>> won't talk. Look in his eyes. It's like he's not there at all.\n\nI had … harsh words with the tree-minder. She won't talk to me now. Would you ask her for help?
Thank you for lending your aid to a stranger. I will not forget you, nor will the spirits of my students. Nor will the Hist.
I'll prepare the town for evacuation. Find as many people as you can and send them back here.
The cove should be just beyond this door. \n\nI'll go on ahead. Wait for the rest of them here.
Uncle Sheo wants to take me to the Shivering Isles! So wonderful. The butterflies! They'll be everywhere! And he has so many books!
Don't worry. I'll speak with her. Go, face Sheogorath. You'll do her more good in there than out here.
I still can't believe it's over. Both of my closest friends, gone ….
With Lyris returned, the harborage is filled with life and music. She is a joy, a warmth in the encroaching chill winds of Coldharbour's looming presence.
Your choice must have been hard. \n\nMay Shor watch over Rana and the warriors on the docks.
I've lost my family! I don't know what I'll do.
What a race! I saw some of it and I was informed of the outcome. I have eyes throughout the city, of course.
Judging by the smell, you found some silver scales?
Thanks to you, my death was not the end for Ouze. We owe you a debt far greater than you can know.
We've got to save her before it's too late!
Don't worry. I've learned my lesson. Conjuring Daedra that powerful is a risky proposition. Next time, I'll have thrice the number of apprentices and soul gems with me.
Did you find anyone? Dalaneth …?
Rala waits for you at the other manor. She'll help you find the crypt.

Sorry, I'm a little busy here and—\n\nWait, it's you! You helped Kireth and I in Bthanual. It's good to see you again! Things didn't go so well for us after those ruins, so we're up north now. Kireth still talks about those light crystals, though.
We need an intact orb to make the memory device work. See if you can find one around here.
You've helped more than I could have hoped, stranger. Areldur will survive this.
You have done a great service for me. For that reason, I shall not feast upon you.\n\nNot this day, at least.
We'll open up the portholes from here and let the rest jump ship. No use keeping extra passengers!\n\nQuite a ride we've had! I thank our stars that you came along to help.
I don't know how I'll ever repay you for helping me rescue <<1>>.\n\nYou're a true friend. We won't forget this.
It's good to be back in my armor again.
To emerge from the Dreamstride is no small feat. The Three Old Gods surely favor you!
The Drublog clan has been making deals with Daedra!

The Drublog kept the book near a shrine to Malacath. A Daedra's power could prevent the Silvenar from escaping.\n\nThey put his essence into a runestone. I bet they took it to one of the actual shrines.
Well met, traveler. Your aid here will be most welcome.
Before you returned, our soldiers saw the ghost giant Sinmur. He came from the mountains and he went east, toward Riften.
My friend! I'm relieved you're here! It's a good thing you are. All is not well in Silvenar.
Have you found anything?
As a warmaiden, my sword and shield were my only concerns. Here, in this hall … the battlefield is much more uncertain.
Get in there and make sure King Jorunn and the others are safe.
Speak to my Housecarl. I have no time for another of the Jarl's hounds.
How goes your investigation?
My hero returns with my spun gold. I'll buy you a pint as soon as you …
My friend. You return, with my valuable property all in …
Can I ask more of you? An important task stands before me and I hope to enlist your help.
The matrons are awake. I … I almost don't know what to tell them.
You'd best move on. Taarengrav isn't safe.
She and Aelif await you at the hall in Shornhelm. Go well on your path.
You must clear the way. We have to reach Sinmur before it's too late!
Enter the sanctum and stop their ritual!
Adept. We need your support once again. Valaste has translated the book you earned in Sheogorath's mad play.
Blast it all, nothing stays! A thousand plagues on whoever invented this infernal device!\n\nI dictate the story to this parchment, but nothing happens!
I hope you'll cause a distraction in the warehouse district. The destruction of the pirates' booty should keep them occupied.\n\nWe'll get over to the docks as quickly as we can.
Go upstairs. See if his clothes fit. There's little time to set up our deception.
One of the scouts said you're heading in after them? Good luck.
The spirits have not been kind to him.
The spinners say their stories come true. What good fortune you changed this one, yes?
We haven't much time! You'll need fire salts and kindlepitch to destroy the beacon. Talk to <<1>>. He'll know where you can find them.
That lich must be destroyed. Hurry, please!
Careful, don't get too close to the stone! It appears to be emanating dark necromantic energies.
<<1>> is now dead, thanks to you. Whether he stays dead is another question.
Silsailen is under siege! We must get this madness under control.
Who in the nine holds are you, and what are you doing in my house?
Look, I'll go to the camp, all right? Give me a few moments to collect myself. Oh, and don't forget our instruments. If I'm risking my life, it had better be worth it!
Lead us to <<1>> and we'll send him back to the grave!
Perhaps <<1>> cannot be killed. What then?
The Baandari will see to it that your stay is pleasant, my friend.
I don't think we can win this battle. What happens if <<1>> kills us all?
Halt! Firsthold is no longer safe. We'll need you to make your way back to the main road.
Tendil's a good sort. He'll get you moving and get us the help we need.\n\nDon't worry about us here.
Stars above! You've no idea how relieved I am to see you. \n\nI hope you're resolved. We've got a hard road ahead of us.
Move along, stranger. We've got everything under control.
This one waits, and watches. When the barriers go down, meet Razum-dar near the castle gate.
There's a powerful Daedra nearby. I know it now. You have to kill it.
They took him! They took Nelulin. Now both of my boys are locked away.
Let's go.
Took us five days to carve our way out of that fish. Those bones mean a lot to me. I lost many a good sailor before it died.
There's treasure all over this rock. That's why the Maormer are here too.
I'll keep watch here for a while. Raerana deserves to feel safe tonight.\n\nThanks again for your help, traveler.
Fair day, visitor. Please state your name for the record.
Damn it! Destroying the Sentinel must have triggered these wards. We'll need to find another way in. \n\nHmm. Maybe Cadwell can help us.
Stars above, it's good to see a friendly face. Did one of my acolytes send you along?
The Heritance are racists, yes? Idiots. But dangerous, destabilizing racist idiots. We must act.
Let me finish speaking to Urcelmo, please.
Thanks for your help! The Companions are still in disarray after the Reach's attacks.
If you can truly slay <<1>>, I'll sleep much easier. Please, save me from this foul beast!
Who are you? Don't touch me!
Find her—as quick as you can.
Get out of here. I won't say another word, so you'd just be wasting your breath.
We need to find that ship. Post haste!
I should have trusted my mother, not my father. Look where our great plans led us!
Your reputation precedes you. Welcome to Skywatch.
Perhaps now you recognize Razum-dar, yes?
Away with you, outlander. We don't deal with your kind here.
So Gorak lied to me about how he got back here and how he retrieved the dispatch. That was all you?
You're an unexpected bend in the river. Not Veiled Heritance, yes? And obviously not Pact. Perhaps we may be of service to one another?
Let's return to the village for the last part of our tour.
I'm such a fool.
Hey, you made it! Telenger has been waiting for you. You should talk to him when you get a chance.
I love my father, despite the mistakes he's made. We'll gather what we can and start out for the Hollow City shortly.
Come. We must hurry to the Anchor mooring!
That silly, stupid boy. He's going to get himself killed.
Thank you for choosing us. I believe that I would have selected Angof if I had been in your boots, but I'm not disappointed to be away from the Observer and his game.
This one has a bad feeling about this. Be careful up there.
We'll make it to the city. Well, I will, in any event.\n\nFind me when you're ready to do something significant.
You … you did it! You got us both out of there!\n\nI'm glad that the guild sent you here. This could have ended much worse.
The path to the southwest leads to Haj Uxith's central plaza. I will follow behind you.
That ship … the Prowler, isn't it? I've heard tales of its captain and crew.\n\nIf things weren't so dire, I'd hope to meet them.
Have you collected everything on the list?
The pirates took <<1>>, but we'll get it back.
Please, don't hurt me! I have nothing of value!
<<1>> spits on his own honor. Poisoning the stronghold? He is no better than the bandits.

I know you can't forgive my clan for what it's done, but they adhere to an ancient promise that will never come to pass.\n\nI could help you, though. No one knows that tower better than I do. But I need to ask for your help in return. It's important.
If you see any workers in the marsh, keep them safe.
Be careful. If the <<1>> is here, it may be well guarded.
Can't help you. Maybe <<1>> can, if you're looking to buy some tin.
Bring old <<1>> back in one piece, would you?
The door is free to open, clever merciful friend. Soon <<1>> troubles Dominion and Pact no longer!
As the Empire's grip on Cyrodiil loosens, evil groups like the Shadowed Path crawl out of their holes. We cannot allow them to spread into Cheydinhal.
Come on, don't be coy. Finish the job. You know you want to.
I … can't believe the Eye is gone. And I have a bad feeling about those undead.\n\nI'm going to get some help. Warn the region. Who knows how many of them are in there?
Ah, there you are! I was just coming to, er, help you. \n\nI hope you found what we were looking for.
Don't go easy on <<1>>. If he didn't keep so closely to <<2>>'s shadow, I'd have keel-hauled him months ago. I'm sure the rest of my crew feel the same way about him.
That heirloom isn't going to walk over here by itself.
For such a superstitious, Mage-hating people … this place is a work of art.
That was a passable performance. For a mortal.
Good luck in there. Let's hope he sees reason.
Welcome to the Dance, my friend! What did I tell you? Baan Dar does love a good party!
Do not hit Byz!
If you please? I haven't all day to keep this portal open.\n\nWell … I do, really. But I don't want to.
Well. Don't see something like that every day.
That was deftly done. I'm reminded of a warrior poet from midway through the First … Era. Never mind.
Dwemer devices are so poorly understood. I've been trying to get this sphere running for weeks. I suspect parts are still missing.

Thank Kyne! King Jorunn said you'd be coming, but I was beginning to have doubts.\n\nWe thought we had Thallik Wormfather cornered, but these damn cultists put up a fierce fight. My soldiers were all killed … I am the only one left.
The Drublog refuse to tell me anything. After what happened in Velyn Harbor, I can guess why.\n\nMy sister's safe because of you. Can I count on you here as well?

You go on, meet up with the goddess. I'll see you at the Flaming Nix cornerclub when you're done.\n\nOh, and don't do anything I wouldn't do. Scratch that. There probably isn't anything I wouldn't do.
Hold a moment … you're no cringing diplomat.\n\nI really don't care who you are, as long as you can help defend <<1>>.
Azura has shown her favor to you before. I do not doubt she will do so again. I only pray she has the answers we need to save the king.\n\nGo now. I will await your return in Wayrest.
Look at that, Lambur! Our half-drowned friend is up and about. We weren't sure you'd make it.
Now we can finally head for <<1>>. It'll be good to sleep in a real bed again.
This is the Blessed Crucible, where the fiercest fighters in Tamriel burn, bite, and slash each other for coin.
I smell smoke. What happened?
The first Mane once again stands before Shazah! Bright moons indeed!
I'm glad you and Shazah are around. Altars, lunar phases … it's a little beyond me. \n\nJust shout if something jumps out at you.
That was marvelous work, soldier. Poetic slaughter.
You've done us proud today, soldier. It was a pleasure working with you.
Do you see that? This scene of destruction? It's so wonderful. Brings a tear to my eye.
Damn it Mathal, you stupid stupid Khajiit. Why would he do this to himself? Why would he do this to me?
Well met. Good to see you. Razum-dar said someone looking like you might turn up. I'm glad you did.
The Hedoran estate was once one of the nicest in the region. Shame it was destroyed. I hope you recover something from the ruins.
You have served this community with distinction.
You are to clear the rats for Milk Eyes, yes? Tazia tells this one so. He is sweet, on the inside. You will see.
You do not look like a Colovian soldier. It is good to see a friendly face.
What do you want? You are in Ezzag's light. This one has chores to do.

I apologize. I should have known one of their mages would be lying in wait. Maormer are known cowards.\n\nThat was Stormreeve Neidir. If the Maormer wanted to hurl a tidal wave at the Malabal Tor mainland, it would have taken power like hers to do it.
Leave me now. I must rest, and meditate. I will contact you when the time is right.
You need not worry. The Order of the Claw will protect our sacred charge. We will make Rid-Thar proud!
Please try not to get any blood on the books, either yours or Goblins'.

It's ugly and getting uglier out here. As our living soldiers fall, the ranks of the dead swell. At this rate, we'll all be fighting for the other side by tomorrow's dawn. \n\nAnd that's not even the worst part.

I think we're in luck. Though most of the local wildlife has fled from the undead, the torchbugs have remained. \n\nMany people do not know this, but torchbugs are among the most perceptive creatures in the forest. They're amazing.
If the Pact is here to bring peace to Vlastarus, I welcome them. If not, you should remain in Castle Brindle.
Ah … you have come. Hunal sees the cool light of the moons reflected in your eyes. You have greatness in your future, yes?
You! You have to help me! You have to help me find my son.
You pulled me from the pits of Oblivion. I owe you a debt of honor, small one. And Titanborn pays her debts.
What are you looking at? When Rhea's spell fades, she'll pay for this outrage!
The standing stones are southeast of here. Charge the scrolls there, then return to me as quickly as you can.
Be calm in the moonlight, Hallowed. Welcome to the Do'Krin Monastery. These stones were old even in Rid-Thar-ri'Datta's day as Mane.
Bright Moons! Now we're somewhere in the Summerset Isles?
My friend! It is good to see you, even here. I keep hearing reports out of the March. "Hallowed this" and "the Hallowed did that." Even on the fringes of the Dominion, you make your mark.
The Veiled Heritance and the Maormer… just like old times, yes?

Razum-dar explained how we were fooled by Laryaril. \n\nI wish I had time to show proper gratitude, but he also told me that an army of Maormer, led by Vicereeve Pelidil, is making landing on our shores. Is this true?
We can't let the Dominion have the keystone. It's too powerful.\n\nOnce it's in our possession we can shift our focus to taking back this town. Is there anything else?
Yes, excellent! Blackheart's treasure awaits!
This imposter must be found before he can fool anyone else. But I think I know where he's hiding.
I have just returned from a long and uncomfortable journey, and I would very much like to enjoy my home and my wife right now. \n\nI must request that you excuse us. The door is over there.
The Dremora will stop at nothing to take Bruma for their own. If they get in here, we're all dead.
From the screams, it sounds like <<1>> is belowdecks.\n\nWatch it. We don't know how long the pirates have had that Fang. They could all be crazier than wamasu.
Don't worry about me. I'll get going as soon as the damned walls stop moving.
Welcome to <<1>>. I'm <<2>>. I manage the games and the tavern. What can I do for you?
We're back in the Shadow Wood. I had hoped not to visit here again. But if this is where he is holding the general's bow, then it's just as well.\n\nWe need to find the Shade to get the bow back.
The next race is about to begin! Place your bets! Remember, the fine line between winning and losing is the finish line!
You carry the Light of Meridia. I can sense it! Soon, we shall strike back against the Lord of Brutality!

You shall require more than just the King and the Mage, of course. But they are as good a starting point as any.\n\nOthers in this realm, allies current and soon to be, all have important parts to play in this endeavor.
I can't believe we're doing this. Repulsive.
At long last, the Elder Scroll of Chim is ours. I can feel its powers strengthening our forces!
The crystal … you must destroy it! Quickly, or everyone will die!
The challenge grounds are to the west of the Hist tree. You will find our champion waiting for you there.
Find the captains and find out what's going on up there. The passage is right behind me. We'll catch up with you as soon as we can.
Witness a diabolical duel of death and destruction! Place your bets! Two terrifying titans face off in a bloody battle of bulk! Welcome to the troll arena!
The Black Daggers are a cunning bunch. You look like you can handle yourself though.
Marines do their part. No privateer will accuse us of shirking duty.
The fewer Goblins around, the safer I feel.
No time to talk! We have to stop the summoning ritual!
Despite all my knowledge, <<1>>'s influence over me was absolute. I'd be little more than a puppet without your timely intervention.
The sooner the Prowler's repaired, the sooner we get out of these musk-damned shoals.
The Overseer's in there. He put us into this Dwarven machine. He's dangerous.

Without Mistral's support, the Dominion will have precious little defense on its southern coasts. But we are not here to conquer anyone. <<1>> knows this. He's in the Chancery, seeking a peaceful resolution here.
We need both shards to gain access to the council's floating platform. Then we can recover the queen's precious eggs.\n\nMeet us at the central camp when you have completed this task.
I can already hear the chatter out there. The projections are working.
You'll do good work out there. I feel it in my bones. Once the Colovians are forced to face the truth, they'll scatter to the winds.
If you need anything from us, talk to <<1>>. He's handling repairs and personnel.
This is madness. There has been enough death in this city!
I don't care whose ear this High Elf covers with kisses, I won't let <<1>> fall to Dominion invaders!
Milksop.
I'm very busy and important, little fish. Why don't you swim on along?
I don't think you want to talk to me. I think you want a brew at one of the drinking halls. Move on!
Zara hopes for Bright Moons to light your path.
The entire arena is abuzz with talk of the Mysterious Stranger, Champion of the Summoner Division! This kind of thing is very good for business. Well played.

Well met! If you're made of flesh and bone, I'm calling you a friend. These abominations, the Hollow, they've killed our Treethane and a dozen others ….\n\nWhat in Oblivion are they and how do we get rid of them? Can you help us?
Ah, you have returned. I had almost given up hope.
You have the potion, initiate. Drink it. Experience the vision and become an Ash'abah.

The council will see you, but this won't be easy. You have one chance to convince them, so make sure you put your best foot forward.\n\nMy people … our future … depends on it. We can't continue to be prisoners in our own forest!
Those unclawed smugglers will spread no more filth on this island.
We should seek Nervyna Selos. Hopefully she'll be able to shed light on what's going on.\n\nIf she's still alive.
About time someone showed up … have we met before? Yes! You're the one who caught that rat, Tervur!
You do fast work. Ready to take on the lions?
Heed my words, you endanger more than your life should you approach.
We failed. We never halted the Canonreeve's ritual. The final altar was here, in this realm, all along. We have to find it. Destroy it.\n\nI … what happened?
I should get back to my investigation. If you find anything, I'll be around.
Let's return to the Harvest Heart. There's one more thing to do and then the ritual will be complete.
A vision of the First Mane himself. Rid-Thar-ri'Datta here, in the Clearing! You are the Moon Hallowed!
My projection will be waiting for you in the laboratory. Do hurry.
I appreciate what you did for my children. Most mortals see us only as monsters. But you were willing to look beyond that and set us free.
I just knew you had the makings of a Hallowed! I am very glad you're here. With you at our side, there are no questions we can't answer. No puzzles we can't solve.
Welcome to our cleansing, my friend. Eh, sorry … Hallowed. We were right about you, I hear. It is good we'll have someone so strong and trustworthy at our side today.
I believe that this is another one of the magicka conduits. How fascinating!

Aranias is not the only unusually talented Altmer the Veiled Heritance recruited. You should talk to Andur to learn more about what the Heritants have planned for Aranias.\n\nBut be careful, his temper is as fiery as his magic.
I have waited some time for your arrival.
You made it back. I see sending Draval did some good.
Hey. If you don't mind, I'd like to drink alone. Sorry.
I am grateful to see a friendly face. In desperate moments, we need all the assistance we can get.
Why … why are you still here? We have already said touching farewell. Go!

As dire as our circumstances may seem, I have only to think of Queen Ayrenn for the inspiration to fight on for a brighter future.\n\nVictory today may come at a great cost, but the strength of the Aldmeri Dominion is worth any price!
O, my heart grows weary! I beg of you to return when it is all over.
Yes, yes. Raz knows you'll do fine. Don't keep the moon-sugar-induced visions waiting.
Death comes to us all. May we face it with honor.

Be careful. There's a corruption here, friend. It's a blight that's tainted the minds of these Bosmer, driven them mad. \n\nThere's little I can do for them. All I can do is search for a way to stop the blight before it spreads any further.
Please, don't bother me. I'm doing some important work up here. I can't have distractions! Nothing is going wrong, I just … no distractions!
I pray to the Green you can help us resolve this. No one here wants to see this contract fail.
Did you get the key? Please, you must let me out of here. I'm freezing to death!
You should talk to <<1>>. Perhaps you can talk some sense into him.

It all comes down to this, my friend. The final fanfare. The last hurrah.\n\nI don't know the meaning of the word fear. Literally. I don't. But, damn, if the prospect of entering that gate doesn't twist my guts into knots.
The Champions are here, Hallowed. They awaited your arrival with great enthusiasm! Are you ready to join them within?

This room is so big. I never expected the Prince to be much of a reader. But all these books! Imagine the wealth of knowledge they contain.\n\nI could spend years in here. If we didn't have more important matters to deal with, I mean.
You'd better get to it. It's only a matter of time before the clients ….\n\nNever mind. Just go do your job.
Why are you here?
Remember: Wormroot Depths, Grahtwood. I'll meet you inside.
Let's get inside.
If you're here to complain about the Argonian refugees, there's nothing I can do. They're to remain behind the barricades until the Thalmor resolves their status.
I knew of <<1>>'s anger, but to murder <<2>>? Madness.
Go and see for yourself. Keep your weapon sheathed, if you please. And make no sudden moves.
As much as I hate to say it, the wizard knows what he's talking about. Maybe he knows how to stop the Sea Vipers.
His initial assumptions are rarely correct. I suppose lightning can strike twice.
Even by kyn reckoning, I have waited a long time to send Seris into the darkness. Allow me to savor this moment, little mortal.
Suppose you'll be moving on, then. You should come visit, tell us tales of your travels. We're a lot alike, you and I!
It's good to see you live. We didn't make it as far as Tamriel, but at least we're no longer trapped by Grexev.
Moons smile on you. Speak with Queen Ayrenn. She hopes that you and Indaenir will be able to accomplish here what you accomplished in the Driladan Pass. We all do.
I overheard your conversation with Gilraen. I'd love to help you tear those Daedra apart.
So you'll fight with us? \n\nLet me know if you need an extra bow, I'm itching to leap into this fray.
<<1>>'s plan worked. I don't know what to say.
Let's let the leaders make their opening arguments.
The summit is just ahead. The leaders should be arriving any moment.

The wee ginger mage can tell you more about the focus stones.\n\nMmm, ginger. You must try my clannfear haunch in pickled ginger. Exquisite! Not to brag, but I'm almost as good a cook as I am a warrior.
You found me. Good.
Do I know you?
Save your breath. I will not be swayed by Emeric's lapdog.
Your Skald-King has all the patience of a bull at mating season. This is a negotiating table, not a battlefield. Can't you talk some sense into that thick head of his?
Jorunn is being stubborn out of spite. He's your king. Can't you reason with him?
Our allies are few, and our enemies multiply.
Let me go! This is a mistake! I've done nothing wrong!
If you aren't here to help us, please just go. We don't need another outsider making things worse.

You're a fan of poetry, aren't you? How's this, then?

As I was going out one day
My head fell off and rolled away,
But when I saw that it was gone,
I picked it up and put it on!

I rather like that one.
Bright Moons! Now we're somewhere in the Summerset Isles?
I don't have anything to say to you, outsider.
Thank you for your help, advocate. The forest seemes to be restored to normal, even if Gathiel got away with her crimes.
So, you're still interested in joining Brackenleaf's Briars?
It's done. I hope it brought Yahyif some peace.\n\nI'll admit. Didn't do much for me.
I'm just gathering everyone before the ceremony starts. Go on ahead. The path is obscured by vines, but you'll see it where the passage narrows. See you there!
Every muscle must be properly stretched before we rush into battle. Wouldn't want to get a cramp when we make our heroic charge into death's chomping maw, would we?
Everlasting glory to those who captured the Elder Scroll of Mnem!
Watch the tail! I will try to distract it!
The light of the Bright Moons bless and keep you, traveler.
Will you help capture the Elder Scroll of Altadoon for us, warrior? This deed will not be forgotten!
This was supposed to be a simple assignment. I should never have allowed <<1>> to push us around!
That's not me! It's nothing like me! Why is she pretending to be me? \n\nWe need to destroy that shield. When I'm finished with her, she won't resemble me in the slightest!
One Varen is torture enough, but three of them? That would drive anyone insane!
Sai Sahan suffers from unfathomable torment. I can sense it. Find him, Vestige. Bring him to me.
