Shhh … be quiet in here. <<1>>'s servants don't like things with blood inside them. And they really don't like noise.

I still can't believe she's gone. I don't blame you, advocate. I blame myself that I missed it. \n\nI'm going to pass down the title of Spinner as soon as I find a suitable replacement. I can no longer be the spirtual light that Karthdar needs.
I am in the middle of something right now, sorry.
Get down, you fool! Do you want the bloodfiends to see us? Now hush, hush. Adusa needs her ears right now.\n\nNo, wait, strike that. Let's talk. You can help Adusa, yes?
I'm not going to leave Moira's Hope to those monsters. I promise you, we're going back home. Some day.
Thanks to you, we're alive. I hope that's the last I ever see of vampires and bloodfiends!

My sister thinks I don't trust her, but she's always been my shield and my sword. She has things here well in hand.\n\nJaneve wants to resume the hunt for Reezal-Jul, but not before she's certain this camp is secure.
We need to get to the highest point in town, that's probably where this storm is being conjured.
We must keep moving. The Inner Courtyard is just ahead.
I hate killing things that are already dead. It's just not as satisfying.
It is good to stand beneath the sky once more. To feel the breeze upon my skin. \n\nAnd I wouldn't have made it here without you. My home is always open to you, should you care to visit.
Goblins have no place in a decent world. They are not even good to eat.
Do not shy from killing more Goblins than called for in your contract. Even Stendarr grants no mercy to those creatures.
Goblins are nasty brutes. You watch yourself on the hunt.
We have an unexpected guest, Vestige.
Saryne will need your help, like I did.
<<1>> was certain she'd find <<2>> beneath <<Ac:3>>. She made the Falinesti Faithful dig for that frozen vault. It seems they have uncovered it.\n\nAnd it would certainly explain the frost trolls.
Ah, look who's here, Stibbons! While I've no idea why you'd be in this place, I daresay you've come at an opportune moment.

Keep your distance, outsider. The last thing we need is some rock-brained city dweller bumbling around.\n\nDarkness dominates this part of the forest—Uela the Hagraven and her Reachmen are encamped here. For now, at least.
It's not fair that you get to go in. I was so looking forward to tearing the old hag apart.
Watch for the icy tricks and traps. Though <<1>>'s soldiers tripped many, the magic of the inner vault restores them after a short time.
Guard the ring with your life! Without it, you will never retrieve the Amulet of Kings.
Are we done here? Honestly, the Inner Courtyard is just beyond the next door!
Wyress Asteria let you in? I trust she had good reason. What drove you to seek me in this house of stone?
Please, we need those poultices. Do whatever you have to. Without them, my knights don't stand a chance.
I had a feeling coming here was going to be bad business! Always trust your instincts. I should have listened to my mother more often.
Take care. That the Tomb of Anahbi remains undisturbed in this city of thieves after all these years should tell you all you need to know of the dangers.
The Countess is young and unproven. Yes, she was invaluable in our victory over Montclair's forces, but is she really ready to govern? She lacks the experience and boldness of her father.
I know that High King Emeric holds Verandis Ravenwatch in high regard. And I am not one to refuse aid when it is freely offered.\n\nStill, the man has always made me just a little … uneasy.
It is good to see you again, fellow Moon. No doubt your trial was a harrowing one.
Lies of Lorkhaj and all his thralls! We trusted you! We trusted you and you abandoned us in our hour of need!

I would never bring an outsider into my memories if I didn't believe it was imperative. \n\nThe memories we will revisit. They are … painful for me. It is with a heavy heart that I ask you to embark upon this journey with me.

I quite forgot how it feels. The rush of blood to the head; the sound and fury of battle! \n\nSo what if I've put on a few years? This is where I belong. I'm going to take back this garrison or die trying.

Leila doesn't have much time. I know it. She knows it. She's trying to be so strong, but ….\n\nI swore I would never ask this of you. It goes against everything I believe in. But damn it, she's my wife! I don't want to lose her.
I need to think about what I'm going to do next.
Oh divine protector, please … send me a sign ….

What does Crazy Eye see here? Another shaveskin? Good! These Knights of Saint Pelin need all the help they can get! \n\nCrazy Eye and the other Baandari have done all they can. Maybe it's your turn to help now?
So … what do you think of the armor? I'm still officially in mourning of course, and I don't want to disrespect Eamond's memory, but if we're fighting Septima Tharn I have to be there. \n\nI just do.
Have you discovered the identity of the informer?
Our eyes are everywhere in <<1>>. We've fixed them upon you for some time.\n\nWe're in need of an outsider, unknown in <<2>>. Someone with … versatility.

You're a bold one, to approach so fearlessly.\n\nGive me a good reason to speak with you. I'll make it seem like you're here at my request. Otherwise, my subjects will think you cut the line and start sizing you up for dinner.
The ratification ceremony is taking all of my time. Now I have to clean <<1>>'s mess?\n\nWe should have brought stonemasons from the Summerset Isles. Dependable, unlike these local work crews.
Cut out her heart. And work swiftly, so the blood of Hircine's faithful still flows.
The heart. Quickly!
The gargoyle's tongue! Of course, what a simply obvious answer!\n\nWell, let's get on with it. You'll be able to dispatch one of those beasts, I assume?

Shornhelm may be secure, but reports from other parts of the kingdom suggest Montclair is stirring up trouble everywhere.\n\nCountess Tamrith and Baron Dorell will each take a detachment of the Shornhelm Guard and go investigate these reports.
I'm sorry, I don't have time to talk. I'm not feeling very well, and I still have to earn enough gold for my dinner.
With the Heart of Anumaril safe in the Mages Guild and Rajhin's Mantle at hand, only a skilled operator remains.
Strange to see you, after <<1>>. Not bad, just … strange. But no matter.\n\nI can hardly believe we're about to breathe some life into this old girl. And before you ask, yes, I'm speaking of <<c:2>>.
Stendarr be kind. I hope they're both still alive.
It pains me, but we cannot take her pleas to heart, my friend. The Daedra will try anything. Speak to it if you want, but you know what we have to do.
Tu'whacca's breath. What have we done ….
Mother Lamae wants to speak to you.
You know what I hate more that a nasty bloodfiend? Two nasty bloodfiends!
I have couriers all over <<1>>, but running the borders has become rather dangerous. \n\nI hope none of them bumbled into trolls again. I can't afford any more delays!
Whether you helped me here for coin or for gratitude, you have both now in your possession.\n\nCoin from <<1>>, and gratitude from myself. Go in peace.
Apologies, but I've got no time for talk.
You? What are you doing here?\n\nForget it. I know we've had our differences in the past, but … I need your help.
Aha! I knew I recognized you from before. You retrieved that relic for me, from the site in the Alik'r. Splendid.\n\nI don't suppose you'd be willing to help me on another grand adventure?
This architecture … it's Daedric. I think it'll work.

Look, I don't know you, but I need someone who knows more about magic than I do, and frankly, that's just about anyone, so you'll do.\n\nThis damn mage hired me to do a job and now he won't let me get the job done!
Old chum! What have you been up to, then? Lots of derring do, I'd imagine? A fair dose of swashbuckling, perhaps? Excellent!
Did you hear what that monster did to the town of Crestshade? Reezal-Jul has to pay for these crimes!
Thanks, I guess.
These men will always have a place of honor among my people.
We'll never find work again.

Argh! My head is pounding. Three loaves of bread and I'm still foggy. I don't care what happens. Remind me to never drink that rum posset again.\n\nYou were asking around town though. About that toothless runt of a constable. Did you learn anything?
Have you made any progress with Martin? I hope you won't give up. For my sake, and for the sake of Shornhelm. We need soldiers.
Lleraya put a lot of effort into this veil. She really wants to keep us from finding whatever the Ayleids hid down here.

According to my waste of a son's own journal, he practically gave Lleraya the keys to the city. What happened here was Ellic's fault.\n\nI don't care what kind of powers Montclair's daughter possesses. A Dorell must be better than that!
I always loved puzzles as a child. I just hope we don't get struck by lightning if we make an incorrect decision.
You've done it! Arlie, she's … she's alive!
You are surely one of the Aedra, sent by Stendarr himself!\n\nBut that's silly, of course. Was … was it Federic who brought you? I'd worried he'd forgotten me.
I don't know how much help I'll be, but lead the way.
The Daedra! They took my little girl! Arlie. Have you seen my Arlie?

I never really liked this place when it was just a crypt, but between the quarantine and the plague husks it's gotten so much worse.\n\nLet's get moving. The sooner we figure out what's going on and find my brother, the sooner we can get out of here.

I appreciate you doing this for me. Talk to Nilyne. Just try to ignore her sharp tongue and insulting tone. That's just her way.\n\nShe really is an excellent alchemist. My uncle trained her, you know.
Who are you? How do you know about the Fading Tree?
I'm glad to see you and Aerona were successful. That young woman's got more guts than she knows what to do with, but I can't fault her intentions.

Keep a note on you if you're going out there. Write where you would like to be buried. I'll do my best to carry your body there, if I find it.\n\nWhat? An army of Undaunted vanished out there. I'm not morbid. I'm a realist.
Let's see, that's everyone from the Iron District, but we still have a few hundred unaccounted for.\n\nOh, I'm sorry, I didn't see you there. Our hands are full getting refugees out of the city.

You. You've been working with the Star-Gazers. That means you know what you're doing. Good.\n\nSee that large staff sticking out of the ground? It's emitting magical energy at unprecedented levels. If we don't stop it, it'll explode.

There are Daedra lurking ahead—if you can defeat them, we can get through! Save my wife and those mercenaries I hired. Whatever's left of them. I mean—you know what I mean.\n\nGo on, I'll catch up. I need a moment.
I sense that the gems have been recovered. But your work is not yet done, mortal.
We are pleased that you have decided to help us, mortal. But take care—the Serpent will surely discover your interference and try to stop you.
Those wounds are appalling. What have these mages secreted away up there?\n\nDon't tell me. I'll find out for myself once Brulo gets here.
It takes both skill and good fortune to enter the ranks of the Black Horse Couriers!
You know what this one has not eaten in a while? Battered fish heads.
Do you bring news?
How rude! Kulth refused to go down without a fight.\n\nLet's hope the armorer doesn't give us as much trouble. She should be working on the east side of the valley.
My grandmother used to tell me stories of a time when Tamriel was at peace. \n\nI'm not sure I believe her.

The Serpent and his Scaled Court would destroy Dragonstar … everything. These people mean nothing to him. And if they discover my betrayal, they will dispatch me without hesitation.\n\nBut tell me, have you dealt with the wamasu eggbearer?

Ah, I see my message reached you. Have you encountered Kelmen in your travels by any chance?\n\nThe Thief reported a magical disturbance around Skyreach. Kelmen went in search of an old Mages Guild associate working in the area. He has yet to return.
Titus and I shall prepare the ritual. You must light the fires atop the six pedestals. When the fires all burn, we can complete the ritual.
Well, you don't look crazy. I take it you smashed all that Dwarven machinery to bits?
Have you returned from your expedition with more to show than dust and dirt?
Craft a maple bow. Bring some sanded maple to a woodworking station, as well as a style material. Carpenters sell them, if you can't find any yourself.
I've always believed the hunt for ingredients is its own reward.

<You notice a prominent handbill on the requisition board.>\n\n"The royal family wishes it to be known that masters of the craft await you in <<1>>. We offer free training for all new to their craft, and certification for accomplished crafters."
Glirion really is a good sort. Once you start taking pledges, you'll get used to him. We all do … eventually.

Our paths cross again, thank the Eight! It's amazing how often good research leads to remarkable discoveries.\n\nSince we parted, I have come to the conclusion that this is an automated quarry. Like the Orc pit above, only much more sophisticated.

I love the smell of the siege camp. It smells warm and sweet. Makes me anticipate the battle to come.\n\nYou know what it smells like? It smells like muffins. Really soft, fresh muffins. Covered in bog-iron ale jam. Mmm. I love that smell.
Those soft city Orcs may have a use for the constructs, but who can tell? As long as they wind up far away from here, that's all I care about.
An outsider, huh? I sure don't envy you this task. Echatere can be nasty beasts at the best of times. Especially when you grab them by the crest.
The Bloody Knoll is a sacred place. Any Orc from Shatul who spots you inside is honor-bound to kill you.\n\nI trust you grasp the implications.
You've succeeded where the Imperial Legions have failed! the Daedra have defiled the Ruby Throne for months on end.\n\nCome! All proceeds as it should. We move for the Elder Scroll.
This is not a good time, soldier. Be quick.
I hope you're here to tell me that some Daedra's been banished back to Coldharbour.

<You notice a prominent handbill on the requisition board.>\n\n"Lord Vivec gives greetings! Masters of the craft await you in <<1>>. We offer training for all new to their craft, and certification for accomplished crafters. Free for all citizens!"
Anchors, and Daedra, and crazy dung-headed legionaries … there's much to do in the city, yes?
Ah, there you are! Take the broken pieces and see if you can fit them back into their panels!

Isn't this wonderful news! To protect his own tomb from looters and to ensure his legend among his people, Torug climbed to the summit. And he took his relics with him!\n\nNow be a dear and go up there and retrieve the Armlet of Torug for me.

You agreed to help my lady? That means we're going up into the cold and the wind again, aren't we?\n\nThe things I do for Lady Laurent. Perhaps this time she'll show some appreciation—if we survive, that is.

Torug! What an Orc! He abandoned his own tomb while obviously near death just to bury himself even higher on the mountain. What an inspiration!\n\nThe letters are worn, but I'm sure the inscription says "zugka" and not "zugra." I'm almost positive.
I need to go. The ambassador wants me to run to Orsinium and let them know she's on her way.\n\nThey'll negotiate with her or they'll have me to answer to. I owe her that much after all this trouble.
High King Emeric relies upon my dear Sovelle. If she were here, she'd know what to do.
The bellows and furnace should rekindle the forge. They must.
Hurry! See if my mother hid another note in that coffer.
You made it back. Excellent. Did you find Regilus? What did he have to say?
Don't touch the switches or you'll kill us!
Don't touch the switches! They're trapped!
If anything happens to Raynor, I'll never forgive myself! It's my job to protect that big brain of his—usually from itself.
<<1>> has doubted my work in the past, but she has never rejected my findings outright. Has the thought of <<2>> clouded her judgment?\n\nI would never do the same to her, surely.

This isn't good. The sphere's core is deteriorating at an alarming rate. If I don't reach it soon—\n\nOh, hello there! Nothing to see here. Feel free to move along. We can catch up later, say, back in Orsinium? Over drinks?
<<1>> and I have argued before, but never like this. He grew up with tales of <<2>>'s grand adventures—I didn't realize how personal this was for him.\n\nBut I'm certain he will come around.
They hit me and told me to praise Trinimac. Now I'm confused and my head hurts.
So far so good. Just mind the edge. It's quite a drop.\n\nWe'll keep behind you until we see a chance to move forward.
So? What did you find? What did she have to say for herself?
<<1>> prays this will be over soon.
The next dish calls for <<z:1>>, some <<mz:2>>, and <<z:3>> to tie it all together.
I'm sure Eveli will come around. Eventually.\n\nIt's you I'm worried about. The seeds of guilt are a heavy burden for anyone to bear.
Well, so much for Valkyn Tephra. \n\nYou move more and more like my barons. I can almost envision them ….

Remember, the last known location of Uzdabikh's Helm was in the vicinity of Sorrow in northern Wrothgar.\n\nI'm not sure how it got up there, but the oral traditions are surprisingly accurate for such an antiquated system.
There's water in a cistern along the wall. Hurry!
That storm came up so quickly. I've never seen anything like it.
This pendant is worth a fortune! I can't wait to get back to civilization so I can … present it to my fair Alani.

Your dexterity in that last arena was dazzling. You're really quite nimble for a mortal. \n\nMy master will tell you he learned some of his best moves from mortals. Tamrielics, he says, are always full of surprises.
I hear Corintthac's lackeys are half-mad with grief. Seems you've really set them back.\n\nTalk to Ushang. He'll want to hear that the job is done.

Thanks for helping us with this situation. I wish I could have spent more time getting to know you.\n\nI know! Next time you're in the vicinity, you can tell me all about your adventures. And, if we're lucky, maybe we can have an adventure of our own.

One of my mates said he saw smoke coming out of Watcher's Hold. That you? Ha! Good work!\n\nThe company's already settled accounts with Sergeant Oufa. If you want your cut, you'll need to track her down. She should be somewhere in Orsinium.

You need to talk to a skittish Khajiit about a missing ledger. I need to collect the few things I can carry with me before the Iron Wheel overruns my home.\n\nOr you could keep wasting everyone's time.
We know that Quintus Jarol is dead. The Brotherhood has eyes everywhere.\n\nYou have done well. The covenant is sealed, signed in blood. Welcome to the family, Brother.

You've got one of those faces, don't you? Nowhere near as pious as seems proper for this part of the world.\n\nIn that case, how'd you like to earn some honest gold for a little bit of dishonest work?

Ah, my friend. I have a small favor to ask of you, if you're willing.\n\nAn old friend of mine has been attempting to track me down. I don't particularly want to be found, but I can understand why she searches for me.
Well, what have we here? You certainly don't look like one of those Red Sails extortionists that have been bleeding me dry.

Truth tries to hide in plain sight and is often most elusive when you actively seek it.\n\nThe resin fumes provide an advantage in this regard. Let them fill you so that you can truly see. Spread out and search for anything out of the ordinary.

This is an absolute insult to Cimbar. The old Astara would never send other assassins to finish a job unless she knew the assassin had failed. We haven't even heard back from Cimbar yet. \n\nBut I shouldn't question the Matron. She is our leader.
You're back, I see. How could I not? You're standing in my light.\n\nSo tell me. How did you do?
Please. My sister and I find ourselves stranded in this city of pirates with no hope of rescue or respite.\n\nIt's like we're being punished for something we didn't know we did.
Back away slowly and I won't slug you.\n\nI've had more than enough attention from this nest of pirates for one day, thank you very much!
What's wrong?
I'll wait to change until you leave. I'm a bit self-conscious.\n\nHa, nearly had you. Really, I need to cut a convincing tail hole in the uniform. I'll be along shortly.
To see the interior of <<1>> with my own eyes? Truly spectacular.
Some people at weddings like to flaunt their latest jewelry. If we spot any, we should take it from them. Bet it would give cause to distract the doorman.
I wonder what they're serving for dinner.
I've seen better weddings.
What have you found?
<<1>> loved his riddles. His old journal talks about this room, Tu'whacca's Pillars.\n\nHe always taught me to look for patterns or differences. Things that stood out, or the order of placement.
Just got word. <<1>> wants to see you.
<<1>> needs you in <<c:2>>. Said she has something for you.

I suppose you're wondering, "Who is this beautiful masked woman and what is she doing sneaking about Kvatch?" The answer is as clear as that cute little nose on your face. I'm here to assassinate someone.\n\nWe have that in common, if I'm not mistaken.
If <<1>> is truly alive, I'll make him wish he was dead.
Faking his death … how could he do that? Why would he do that?
Fresh tip caught your interest? I know the place. Say the word and we can all be a little richer today.
This one thanks you for freeing me from those slavers. You've given me a chance to see my mother after all these years.\n\nAnd maybe even to start over again.
The news about the Silver Dawn has made me even more concerned about Hilde's safety. We have to hurry!
Caravans come and go, but none are available at this time. Come back again and I'm sure we can do business.
You've been given a sacred duty. Perform it well and bring honor to the Night Mother and your Sanctuary, Assassin.\n\nYour Brothers and Sisters would kill to have been chosen for such a task.
How about you go find something for me to count instead of interrupting my counting? Great. I really miss my abacus.
Oh, Assassin, am I glad to see you! He's got one of those ideas in his head again and it has me worried sick about him.
I understand we have you to thank for Hildegard's safe return. Are you going to tell me what happened or do I have to torture Kor until he sings?

A good showing, slaying the Grand Sermonizer. A pity Cimbar paid for his failure with his life. Keep your blades sharp and your wits sharper, otherwise we may see a similar end to your story.\n\nEven so, I've recorded it all. For posterity, of course.
Raz suspects that all this quiet hides unpleasant surprises. Tread lightly, sharp-claw.
I can't believe Cimbar is dead. And Tanek would've met the same fate if not for you.

Green-Venom-Tongue gave me his report on your little jaunt. What you discovered shows how the past sometimes comes back to haunt us.\n\nSince this concerns the Primate, Speaker Terenus and the Black Hand will determine our next move.

I've been taught that death is a gift. That to meet the Dread Father in the Void isn't a terrible thing if you lived a life of service to his bride, our Night Mother.\n\nEven so, I feel sad. Cimbar was … fun.

I can't tell you how relieved I am to find you. I'm Ibrula—a friend of the Star-Gazers.\n\nI'm trying to gain entry to this temple, but the Celestial Warrior's army of Anka-Ra have sealed the door. I need help to get past them and disable the seals.
Let's see, that's everyone from the Iron District, but we still have a few hundred unaccounted for.\n\nOh, I'm sorry, I didn't see you there. Our hands are full getting refugees out of the city.

You. You've been working with the Star-Gazers. That means you know what you're doing. Good.\n\nSee that large staff sticking out of the ground? It's emitting magical energy at unprecedented levels. If we don't stop it, it'll explode.
I sense that the gems have been recovered. But your work is not yet done, mortal.
We are pleased that you have decided to help us, mortal. But take care—the Serpent will surely discover your interference and try to stop you.
How rude! Kulth refused to go down without a fight.\n\nLet's hope the armorer doesn't give us as much trouble. She should be working on the east side of the valley.

The Serpent and his Scaled Court would destroy Dragonstar … everything. These people mean nothing to him. And if they discover my betrayal, they will dispatch me without hesitation.\n\nBut tell me, have you dealt with the wamasu eggbearer?

Friend, have you come across Kelmen in your travels?\n\nThe Thief reported a magical disturbance around Skyreach. Kelmen went to find an old Mages Guild associate he said was working in the area. He has yet to return.
Titus and I shall prepare the ritual. You must light the fires atop the six pedestals. When the fires all burn, we can complete the ritual.
Yes? Can I help you, serjo?
Back from <<1>>? I could never get used to the heat and sand.
Forgive me, friend. I cannot talk. Too many unfriendly eyes in Sadrith Mora today.
I've heard enough of your lies! I thought you were on my side! Just—get out of my sight!
By the Three, Lord Vivec looks terrible! Where's Archcanon Tarvus? He always seems to know what to do in situations like this.

Remember, Menwendel should be tending to her nursery just south of here. Show her that … thing. I'm certain she'll know what it is. More importantly, she'll know how to help my Mistress recover from its effects.

I doubt Jinrisa's been especially careful with the deed. There's a reason she's never advanced beyond the rank of wizard.\n\nUnless I miss my guess, you'll find the document tucked away in Tel Naga somewhere. Good fortune, sera.
Greetings, egg-kin. We must speak quickly. The overseers grow suspicious when I speak to free-scale Argonians like you. It is almost like they do not trust me.
So, did Menaldinion relent, or should we leave him to his wheezing?
Argh! Everything itches! Damnable cats!

Let me get a better look at you. Hmm. Your eyes are wrong, but your palms seem clean enough ….\n\nI have a task for you. If you succeed, you'll earn the favor of a Telvanni councilor and a treasure from my vault. Is this agreeable?
Sorry about this cloak and dagger nonsense. I can't be seen talking to anyone even remotely suspicious right now. Marshal Hlaren's watching me like a hawk.

I presume you've come here seeking work? I'm afraid the mine may be closed for some time yet. Not too long, of course! \n\nAnyway, feel free to stay as long as your coin-purse allows. Our innkeeper will no doubt appreciate the business.

With a couple days rest, and a few stiff drinks we'll be up and running again!\n\nI guess I should go check on the queen at some point. She's probably a nervous wreck. Always been a little skittish, that one.

The ritual confirmed my worst fears—divine energy flows out of me for no reason that I can discern.\n\nI felt the power imbued within my Blessing Stone get wrenched away as soon as you added it to the ritual. I couldn't stop it.
Well, you didn't get gored or trampled to dust. Can the same be said for Falkreath Hold?
After further examination of the documents you brought back, I have to agree with your assessment. The Ashlander Chodala has somehow siphoned divine energy away from Lord Vivec.
I don't know how we're going to get all this done. I miss the days when I could just request another contingent of slaves.
Was that the creature the pilgrims fear? This "Ruddy Man" of legend? It is skulking vermin inflated by the lies of a false god, nothing more.

If you're passing through, pay attention. I'll say this once:

"Pilgrims who ignore my warning,
Vanish from the roads by morning.
Whether you're from near or far,
Best keep your arse at Molag Mar."
There's my favorite hero! Everything is prepared. If you're ready, we can get started.

Think of the stone tiles set into the floor as a giant locking mechanism. We just need to determine the proper combination to open the way forward.\n\nOf course, there's probably some kind of conundrum built in.

Refer to the list I gave you and find my former hirelings in Molag Mar. They should be able to direct you to places where you can get the components I need to build a tonal inverter.\n\nAs for anything else they may tell you, it wasn't my fault.
I'll meet you at the Daedric shrine after I recover my weapons and make a few final preparations.
Kuamta's allowing you to take part in the celebration? Excellent!\n\nIt's essential that you follow her instructions to the letter. Ashlanders are sticklers for the rules, believe me.

I hope you're suitably prepared. Nchuleftingth promises to be quite a challenge.\n\nYou can rest easy knowing that Vimy and I will be right behind you. Well … a good distance behind you. But you can count on me for moral support.
Well, if it isn't Neramo's second favorite assistant. I'm assuming he told you to find me?\n\nAs you can see, the situation's not ideal. We could use some help.
Hello! Here to stable a mount? If your guar is getting a little rough in the scales you've come to the right place. \n\nYou'll find no better guar handlers than those in Balmora!
Do you make a habit of randomly accosting people while they fish?

Dealing with an arrogant, impatient, overconfident young woman … now I know how my mother must have felt!\n\nWe need to move. It won't take those damn cats long to find this place, not with their sense of smell.
Ah, and here's the outlander whom I have never met. What can I do for you stranger.
I hope Eoki's friends make it to the coast. If the House captures them, the punishment will be severe.\n\nNow, to settle this business with Eoki.

Between our detailed model, the genealogies, and the other tomes of knowledge discovered in the lost Library of Andule, the Dunmer shall gain a better understanding of the Great Houses and where we all came from.\n\nThanks to you, my friend.
Go on. Tell my father whatever you think will pacify him. As soon as everyone's attention is focused on you, I'll head out and meet you at the Ashlander camp.
See what you can find but do not, under any circumstances, compromise my job.
That's all for today, champion, but rest assured that your queen will call upon you again tomorrow.

I'm in no great hurry to return to Oblivion, I can tell you that. One day, I hope to see the Twilight Lady in all her radiance, reclining upon the throne of roses. But where they took me? Far from rosy.\n\nWe must find Azura's enemies quickly.
Today has seen enough boarish crime. You've earned your swill, so drink your fill, and leave my bride and I to some privates time.
Good luck finding everything on my list. \n\nI don't know that we've ever had a fatality at the Jester's Festival, but if you are the first, I'll make sure your name lives on in appropriate ignominy.
Welcome! You stand amidst the Circle of Champions, a guild formed to test the greatest fighters of the realm in games of skill. Do you have what it takes?
I haven't so much as heard or seen even a whisper of Brivan yet. Just lots of snarling Warclaws.\n\nIf we can't get through this door, there's only one other way to go.

Stibbons has a way of dropping a fetcherfly into the honey. It's a gift, I suppose. Don't worry. I'll figure out how to extract him from those webs … after I enjoy another cup of tea.\n\nSafe travels, my friend.

Merciful Stendarr! That creature was positively terrifying! I did manage to find one of Lady Laurent's hirelings, though.\n\nBut it's good to see you again, my friend. You'll save my lady's expedition, just as you've done in the past.
Vivec's energy, it flows through Sunna'rah! That's how Barbas is able to circumvent the city's defenses! But why is he waiting over there? I'll never understand what motivates these Daedra.

Is what you said about my son true? Ulran is … dead?\n\nUlran was good at getting himself into trouble, but I … I never thought it would come to this. Please, outlander, don't let the same thing happen to my daughter.
Gascone will turn these events to his benefit, I know it. Even so, he seemed very shaken. Ugh. My tolerance for surprises is past its limit.

I am sorry we can't have this conversation in person. I fear that I'm too tempting a target for this shadowy killer. I must remain hidden.\n\nYou have questions? I urge you to keep them brief. There's no telling when our enemy will strike again.

Step into the portal when you're ready. The perception tabulator will locate Variah and lead you back to Clockwork City after you complete your investigation.\n\nI'll study the phenomenon from out here and make sure no one else enters the portal.

You should get moving. I need to leave orders for the apostles before I make my way to the western gate.\n\nGears protect you in the Evergloam. Can't say as I've ever been to a Daedric realm before, but there is a first time for everything.
This is becoming more and more vexing. Why doesn't anyone in the Wellspring know about the last few apprentices that Lector Naril selected?\n\nWell, let's go see Apprentice Ohtowen.

My companion arrives at last. Now then, our journey begins in this dreary little cave. Quite a surprise, yes? Believe me, it won't be the last.\n\nWe can speak freely here, but do make it brief. All this natural splendor is just … tedious.

The stars have forgotten where they belong. Use the calibration guides on the floor to show them where to go. The matching constellation on the Planisphere's sky will show you the way.\n\nIn the meantime, I'll continue to keep the stars stable.
Ah, there you are! Done playing with Neramo's wind-up toys? I think I'm on to something.
So, ready to do a bit of sleuthing? I'm confident that we can find this elusive evidence, but it will require some skullduggery. Breaking and entering, to be specific.\n\nReady for the details?
Don't worry. I won't let those spiders blow up in your face. You focus on disabling them, and I'll handle the rest.
Oh! Ah, who would you be? Did the Clockwork Apostles send you?
Were you treated well by the menials? I assume they battered you with complaints. What have you learned?

Our victory over the Exarchs came at great cost. Quill and claw, our lost Knight was a true hero. We will not forgive and we will not forget.\n\nI do not know which lock the Shadow plans to poke with the key he stole, but we will help you stop him.
Mind yourself around Salas. He's a mean one with friends in high places. Helps him keep his monopoly on the mushroom trade. He won't take kindly to anyone poking around.
Can't say I trust those mushrooms, but maybe horning in on Salas's business could be our ticket out of this pit.
Lead on, crow killer. I'll be right behind you. Trying to rationalize why I'm helping.
You've returned in one piece! How gleaming.\n\nIn your absence, I've set up a framework to contain the factotum while we assemble its parts. I'll have you do the honors.

Kireth doesn't appreciate my contributions to our partnership. She thinks I'd be lost without her. Well, I'll show her. My superior intellect easily outshines her bravado and derring-do.\n\nBut what brings you out here, my friend?
This one doesn't have much, but her space she values. Do not crowd her.
Sorry, I should try and finish this while it's still warm …. You think it might taste better cold?
Pretend you are adjusting your boot or admiring the architecture. As hard as it may be, look anywhere but directly at Raz. Good, good.\n\nNow, tell Raz what you learned at the Kinlady's manor.
This is where we need to perform Marieve's ritual, I'm sure of that. Look around for any items that might be used to represent the elemental constants. That's the key to unlocking the message.
I appreciate your efforts on my account. Even though I foresaw your actions, you still had to decide to follow that path.
One of Summerset's more unique environments, the Coral Forest. I used to love coming here when I was growing up.\n\nWe need to find out why the Aldarch asked Kinlady Avinisse to meet him out here.

You! You're a member of the Mages Guild, aren't you? Please, you have to help me.\n\nThe Sapiarchs accused one of our compatriots, my best friend, of a murder he didn't commit. They won't even consider the possibility that he's innocent!

My contacts tell me that Galidor left the city on business. Goodness knows what kind. No one will accost you while you investigate.\n\nJust be careful. It cannot become known the Mages Guild is investigating this matter after the Sapiarchs forbid it.

Ah, friend of Valsirenn. I've been informed that you encountered a Sea Sload in a sinkhole beneath Rellenthil. That bodes ill for Summerset. Perhaps all of Nirn.\n\nI fear there are difficult days ahead.

You must be the adventurer that Valsirenn was going on about. Allow me to be the first to welcome you to our secret island.\n\nOh. I suppose you already talked to the Ritemaster, seeing as you're here in Ceporah Tower.
Whatever's taken hold of Glardir is clearly not pleased. I hate to cause her more distress, but I think we should keep freeing my friends.

I heard your audition was a success. Of course, I knew my daggers would impress. \n\nNow, you need to mingle with the other potentials and figure out which one is Larydel. No easy task, given this troupe's traditions.

Look for Rinyde along the beach. Tell her this news of her brother. From all Larydel has told me, I know she is a talented mage, and longs to join the Sapiarchs.\n\nShe must recognize her brother simply does not wish to join her.
I'm so glad everything is back to normal.
That was such a stupid, reckless—dammit, Silurie! I can't let her lord this over me. We have to save them!
Finally, I can get back to work.
Let's hear what this mer has to say. Perhaps he'll know what's going on in this forest.
We have to do something, but I can't take on a pride of lions ….
Off with you now. I have a lot to do, and you're not helping by stomping about my delicate plants.
Rulotar was our ranking battlemage. I served alongside him for more than a century, but I left him to die here. Alone. \n\nThis should have been his command.
Don't expect the courtesy that Nocturnal's earl showed you earlier to extend to this place. We're intruders in Evergloam. The denizens won't take kindly to our presence.
Go on ahead. I'll make sure we're not far behind.
Talking crows? What will these Daedric Princes think of next?
You're back—and not a moment too soon. Do you have something for me?

You'll find the Psijic Codex on that table over there, whenever you're ready.\n\nThe codex will help your search immensely. It's bound to every item in our collection, so it should be able to tell you each relic's location.

Ah, here's one now. By all means, talk to Tarnamir, glan'nt. Apparently we're just recruiting people off the street now.\n\nI'm joking, of course. Please don't talk to Tarnamir. He might actually let you help.
Have no worries. Ila and Lodiss may kick up a fuss, but they are trained warriors. They won't leave their post.\n\nI advise you take all due caution, my friend. I doubt this will be a clean fight.

Time is running out. The Sapiarchs still haven't completed their ritual, and now Nocturnal has launched an attack against them. I sent Darien and Razum-dar to defend the Sapiarchs, but the Daedra keep on coming!

Courtier Vindilween was kind enough to tell me who she sent you to perform favors for. I've been sitting here, drinking and having a most pleasant conversation with <<1>>.\n\nWere you able to acquire the items of cultural significance he requested?

You may have forced my hand, but that doesn't mean the Nord ambassador will be successful in his quest. Not that it matters to me.\n\nBut I hope you realize you made an enemy in the court, newcomer. I will find a way to pay you back, mark my words.

I didn't want to get you two involved, but I need help and there's no one else I can turn to.\n\nI was the one who drugged the animals. The plan wasn't for them to break loose, just stir up a fuss so I could slip into the Conservatory unnoticed.
You're the first soul I've seen coming out of King's Haven. Tell me, were there any signs of the Blackbirds at all?
Hi! Hello! It's such a relief to see a friendly face out here. I haven't had anyone to talk to in—oh, I don't know. Hours?\n\nYou wouldn't happen to be an experienced adventurer, would you?

The Ritemaster has me running all over the place. Seeing as how you're here now, maybe you could assist me in this matter. Even a Psijic sage has a hard time being in more than one location at a time.

After Raz spoke to the pretty Psijic Oriandra, whispers reached me about the illustrious Illumination Academy. They said that the Court of Bedlam hunts a Sapiarch there, so Raz had to come and see.\n\nDidn't expect to find you here helping out, though.

Stranglers are a stubborn breed. Hacking them up would only be a temporary solution. What I need is proof that that Wood Elf is responsible, so he can't do any more damage.\n\nPerhaps Eslion left something at my gardens that could be incriminating?

I must return to the Eldbur Ruins to the north and aid the others caught in K'Tora's mind trap. If you find yourself in the area, you might be able to assist me. Stay safe and remember you have a friend in the Psijic Order!
What do you think came first: the caverns or the construction?
Ha! By Malacath, that felt good!\n\nYou know, I've never punched a High Elf before. Felt like punching a pillowcase full of pudding. Almost feel bad for the little runt. Almost. Heh!
We have nothing more to discuss. Give your stumpish friend that book—or don't. It makes little difference to me.
It's a tower, so now we climb.
This ballista will pack a punch big enough to open a path out of here. Just find any pieces that look like they might be part of a siege engine like this.
This one should have been more suspicious of Madja from the start. Her skill as a first mate blinded him to her greed.\n\nNow Renzir only wishes to retire and live peacefully with his Nubani.
I have no time to deal with whatever issue concerns you, newcomer. I recently received word that all of Summerset faces an imminent threat from a source we believed had disappeared long ago.
Haven't you lot learned by now that I have more than enough magicka to deal with the likes of—wait a moment. You're not one of these smugglers.\n\nWhat brings you to this enchanting little hideaway?
I know there's important work to do, but I perform better when my stomach's full of Orsinium ale.
Welcome back, initiate. I trust your adventures in Valenwood were fruitful? Go speak to Josajeh. She will want to hear the details.
We'll track down the rest of K'Tora's Sea Sload, you can count on that! Hunting down these creatures is quite within our area of expertise.\n\nOf that, I'm almost certain!

Excellent work. Even now, I see a hint of the gem you shall surely become.\n\nNow that you have the necessary materials, it's finally time to craft. The first step is to refine your pewter dust into ounces.
I doubt the farmer will be pleased with this verdict, but those chickens were as likely to be eaten by wolves as anything.
Thanks for watching my hind-scales. You ever need chickens caught, or eaten, you find me!
You're back! And you have the staff fragments? Well done! You should take them to the Loremaster at once. Go! Go!
I'm sorry … I'm still recovering from the Loremaster's decision. You should talk to him—I can't bear to right now.

Ah, it does my heart good to see you, initiate. The events of the last few days … I must admit, they have taken a toll.\n\nI was just preparing Josajeh's proclamation of banishment. Not a simple task, I can tell you.

All right, time to get back to work.\n\nWe need to figure out how to keep Margus Derius from finding the Golden Skull of Beela-Kaar before we do. The survival of Cyrodilic Collections depends upon it, not to mention Murkmire. Maybe all of Black Marsh!

Let me take a closer look. Gin-Rajul, that's my ancestor! And look, it mentions the Ninth Legion by name. This proves they visited this cave.\n\nWe need to keep looking. There must be more clues as to what happened in here.
Head out and talk to the Argonians on your list. I'll do the same. We can meet back here when we're done.

Just look at us. A Bright-Throat negotiator, a Dead-Water kaal, an alley-tough Naga, two scholars, and a hero. As unlikely a party as any I've seen before.\n\nI can only hope that discovering the Remnant will tighten these bonds of fellowship.

Xukas's message said to meet him at the teeba-enoo field in Alten Meerhleel.\n\nTeeba-enoo's a local sport. I've no idea how it's played. There's a ball involved, I know that. I'm babbling. Sorry! I do this when I'm nervous. Please, be careful!
Any other questions for Zadaza? Or do you simply wish to get to the running, dodging, and screaming?

You can find Tia Doran at the Mages Guild. You know, in case you want to ask any additional questions before you head into a mysterious and probably dangerous cavern in search of Imperial antiquities that may not even exist.\n\nIf you want.
Beeko! You are back! As mud is my mother, it is good to see you.\n\nThe lightness in my chest tells me the Remnant is safe, but what of friend-Famia? Or the sick-minded Kassandra?
I tighten my fist. We know where to go. Why do we delay?
Oh, Haxara what have you done ….

Beek-ojel, I have heard much of the tragedy of our loss, and the part you played in ending it. The Hist chose wisely to entrust our troubles to you.\n\nWe owe you much already, but I have one last request for you, if you would hear it.
Am I the only one who gets the feeling that maybe the Dwarves sealed the vault for good reason?

Best luck hunting frogs, beeko. I wish I could join you, but I cannot leave my shop unattended for long.\n\nI remember my first hunt! Wading waist-deep in bog-water, slapping reeds on hollow logs, croaking until my throat ached …. Truly, I envy you!
So, she found a use for the Kajin-Jat Crystal after all. Damn! Goodness, language. Sorry, I meant … no, no, I did mean it! Damn!\n\nWithout an empowered vakka crystal of that scale, we're stuck here.

I am right behind you, beeko.\n\nWhile you focus on the plants, I will focus on the water. Many haj mota and bog-blights lurk beneath. Good for Saxhleel who make wooden legs—not so good for people who want to keep their feet.

I grind my fangs. Following a Dead-Water kaal is the act of a fool or a maniac. Tsojei says fools and maniacs both bleed red.\n\nI will repeat myself. Once. I do not need your help. I hunt these Blackguards alone. Our business is settled. Leave.
He was suffering, wasn't he? This is all we could do for him.
Got business? Take it up with Kassandra.

Keep your claws sharp. In the xanmeer, Blackguards will be the least of your worries.\n\nOld deaths stalk the halls near the Remnant. Ghosts from the Ayleid elves, beasts of vine and stone, and worse. Even so, Tsojei shouts your name. You will succeed.
Let's see … I'll need my knapsack, my mess kit, and my journal, of course. Extra set of sandals … oh, oh, and a canteen! Can't forget that. \n\nWait, did you need something?
All right, it's time for your grand finale. The last chapter in your epic tale. It's time to fight Drakeeh the Unchained, and win back Seeks-the-Dark's freedom once and for all!
How joyous it is to see you return unharmed! Tell me, were you able to find the Vakka tablet?
No need to come any closer, stranger. I can hear you just fine from there.
Now is the time to work towards the prosperity of my village. \n\nI've already offered my services as a healer, of course. I have quite a bit of experience in the field, given my various travels.
To honor change is to honor Sithis. All Saxhleel know this, but sometimes it is forgotten. As nisswo, it lies upon my shoulders to remind them.\n\nWould you help me in this endeavor?
I remember you. You freed me from the Blackguards. What brings you to our village?
That little contraption sure is useful. Cute too. Folks back home probably wouldn't approve though.

Lady Laurent awaits us at the Renewal Lodge. You leave the cave first. I'm much more stealthy when I'm on my own.\n\nBesides, I need another moment to recover. The thick air down here has left me rather peaked.

That hand-mirror is a family heirloom. I can't bear the thought of never seeing it again.\n\nIn the meantime, I need to keep prodding my manservant. If I give Stibbons even a moment's reprieve, he'll find a way to laze about. He's ever so good at that.
Perhaps I lack Jaxsik's flair for sudden disappearances. This is so. But I am thinking I move swift and silent all the same.\n\nYou go on. I will make my way. We will meet if I find anything.

Is that …? Ha! Little Xukas, come to visit your old friend in the Glade of Chimes? He is always so busy now. I recall when he stood only as tall as the keppo grass!\n\nAnd you, egg-savior. What can this stiff-legged crafter do for you?

This is what I'm talking about. How hard is it to boldly strut up to a stranger and express some interest? You get it. If we had more suitors as stiff-spined as you, the ceremony would be well underway!
Hurry, five-claw! Use the ballista and bring that Dragon to the ground! We need to show my people that these creatures can be defeated!
Tsazii is the matriarch of the family and the nominal head of the farmstead. She is the one you need to convince or none of them will leave the farm.

I'm beginning to question my own magnificence, if you can imagine such a thing. Despite multiple attempts, I still haven't been able to identify or catch the damnable prowler who has been following me!\n\nIt's really becoming quite irksome.

I'm Prefect Calo, commander of the Cygnus Irregulars. And you're that outsider working with the Khajiiti militia. I expected you hours ago.\n\nWell, let's not dawdle. You have an assassination squad to stop, I assume, so if you'd open my cell .…
That was the Dragonguard. Captain Saulinia must be closing in.
Remember, you must drink the antidote before heading inside the oasis. I do not wish you harmed by the fumes within.
Silhu-jo, no! This is my fault. S'rendarr forgive me ….

I assume you recovered the master key? Fragrant, my friend!\n\nHrrm. I have waited a long time to return to the palace … my home. Tharn will describe the plan to you. I need a moment to collect my thoughts.
Zamarak never much cared for necromancers. Dragons? No, this one doesn't like them, either.
Nala-do has pledged her service to Queen Khamira. This one will do everything in her power to keep the royal heir safe and secure.
I've generally found that most doors have a way to be opened, magical barriers not excluded. Let's have a look around and see if there's some way to take it down.
I'm afraid I bungled this one royally, old friend.
Mizzik will admit, this case is heading in a rather … unexpected direction. Which is a bit worrisome, if he's being honest.
The temple relic, five-claw. Activate it so the process of attunement can continue.

Take care getting the keys. The thugs in this palace are Khasda's most loyal, and just as vicious and cruel as he. Expect no mercy, and give none.\n\nSereyne will help keep things quiet, in case fighting breaks out.
Upstaged by a gray-maned grandpa. Next time I'll have to pick locks blindfolded and with my teeth.
All right we've got … six—I mean three keys. That should do it. We just need to meet Tasnasi at the vault and the loot is ours.

"No rest," wrote the Ascetic Vula-do, "is sweeter than one following great exertion." Nazdar thinks perhaps he did not stretch properly before his climb. He is no longer the spry eighty-year-old he once was.

See how the Moons align with the ancient gate? The Lattice opens a path to Jode's Core!\n\nBut how did you get the Dragonhorn? Where's Gharesh-ri? And why are the sounds of battle so close? Did the Euraxians overrun our defenses?
Put an end to this, walker. Let's not keep Rakazsa waiting.

Quiet moments to meditate have been rare since Zamarak returned to Elsweyr. This one needed some time alone, especially after helping Tharn with the Dragon at the Shadow Dance Ruins.\n\nBut you look like one who has important news, my friend.

I can't believe Khamira revealed herself. This isn't how we talked about that.\n\nShe's right, however. If we run now, we might as well leave our land to Euraxia and the Dragons. Help her show our people that the Dragons aren't invincible, walker.
Shando-ri seems pleased. Good.\n\nWhile you restore the blade, I'll make my way to the temple's central gate. Meet me there, all right?
Your hesitation does not fill old Mazza-Mirri with confidence. If you want the blade, you must enter the next chamber and face my test.
She is not of the ja-Kha'jay, but I can sense a deep devotion to Azurah from this ally of yours. Mother is guiding us, as she always does.
Rakhzargo never gets letters from tiny Elves. Why does Brother get to have all the fun?

Kideya did not think Razum would be leaving so soon. But it seems he has important matters to attend to. Who is Kideya to deny the High Elf queen?\n\nThis one wonders … what exactly does her son do for the queen?
This must be how the thieves could steal the moon-sugar without being spotted. They tunnel directly into the storage cellars of the farms. \n\nIf it wasn't highly illegal, Raz would be impressed.
Go. Do as Khamira asked. I'll stand guard and discourage the Dragon if it decides to return.

The workhouse serves to snare the poor and the destitute … those who fall behind on their debts. They come here to find employment and earn a decent wage, but the costs deducted to pay for room and board leave them worse off than they were before.

Good idea. No harm in having a look, now that the mural is complete.\n\nThe Song of Kingdoms …. I always wondered what it sounded like, ever since I was a kitten. I've read so many stories, but never was the song actually described.
Finally, the mural is whole once more! I can already hear our lovely patrons gasping in awe.

Selene is in Carindon's study, a cave down this path. Not far, but the blight has the wildlife on edge. Even the ones who aren't sick are terrified and ready to attack anything that comes near.\n\nIf you could clear a safe path for us, I'd be grateful.
How can Jora-ri's only living descendant be such a fool? It's a wonder he even survived this long!

If you told me a year ago that I would be wandering Elsweyr on behalf of the Khajiit to deal with a rage of Dragons, I would have turned you into a newt for spouting such nonsense.\n\nYet here we are.
Wait! Didn't we meet once in Summerset?\n\nI can't believe I prayed to Peryite for help and he blessed me with your familiar face! He usually only blesses me with abundant pus.
It takes a special sort of person to follow Peryite.

You shouldn't have much trouble finding this chest. I sincerely doubt the Ruddy Fangs made any effort to hide it.\n\nJust don't take too long, all right? Guards could wander by at any moment. Plus, Fez is a terrible conversationalist.
You there! Did you see a puny Breton run this way? Answer Ak'an!
Ah, five-claw, good, good.\n\nThis one wore out two pairs of sandals prowling the streets looking for you.
Hurry, friend! You do not want to miss Asaldak by the Merryvale Farms fountain! This is a perfect opportunity to share Nord delights with a culminating legend!
I know there's no one to murder at the moment, but that will change when you take Volendrung. Trust me, mortal. Would the Prince of Madness lead you astray?
Is there a reason you are standing here expectantly?
Huh, you really came. All the way from the Abbey of Blades. Well, welcome to our merry band. Wait until you hear Allanwen's plan. You'll see why we're all so cheery.
Expect no apology. Carindon deserves to suffer for what he's done to me. You should have let me kill him. Between us we have the strength to kill Maarselok without the oathbreaker.

I came across another one of the secret moon-singer myths during my research. It predicts the coming of a powerful new moon, the Dark Aeon. I think Kaalgrontiid seeks to make this ancient prognostication a reality.\n\nNow, let's find the aegis!
Ah, you received my summons.\n\nHmm. The set of your shoulders, that look in your eyes …. Yes, I see I chose well. You will aid me with this most important task.
You have proven yourself a true friend to this temple, despite your choice of companions. Tadali thanks you.
We should go to this mine and find Yahgrondu. It should be just south of here, along the coast. I'll meet you there.
There must have been a reason that Dragonbone powder was kept near the entrance of the sanctuary. Try using it on the altar.

Tharn will be fine. He just needs to catch his breath. Which means I get a few blissful moments without listening to his scathing observations.\n\nNow let's move quickly. Kaalgrontiid must be dealt with before he can complete his ascension.
Ready to train with the grappling bow?
Ka'ishka knows her sister has Azurah on her side, but she will pray for you both … and keep Khenarthi's bells close.
Za'ji and Caska seem to be enjoying themselves.\n\nWell, we're not here to scold anyone. We should talk to Kazahn and see if he knows where we can find Lahini.
Be cautious. It never pays to disturb the dead.
Judging by that docked ship, we're not the only ones who have business on this island.

We arrived not a moment too soon, walker! Vijari is losing his struggle with the Bent Dance. The Dark grips him like none other she has seen. Her songs hold them back, but she cannot exorcise their darkness with prayer alone. Adara'hai needs help.
You still have the pendant, yes? Show it to the nice guard before I get irritated.
I have so many question to ask Khunzar-ri. About his stories. About Anequina. But we have no time to satisfy my curiosity, yes? We have a Dragon to put down.\n\nCome, five-claw. Dragonhold awaits.
Good to see you up and walking about. You were dead to the world after we escaped Dragonhold.
Za'ji doesn't have to go to Dragonhold? Fragrant!\n\nUm, this one means, how unfortunate. Za'ji was so looking forward to assaulting the floating island. Good luck to you, five-claw.

Did I hear the queen correctly? She doesn't want me to come with you?\n\nVery well. The Dragonguard will remain in reserve until you need us. But I was really looking forward to the view from the floating island.

Such magic never ceases to amaze me!\n\nI'm both disappointed and relieved not to be going to Dragonhold. I hope you don't think less of me for that. But never fear. The Dragonguard will be ready should the need arise.

We must head to South Guard Ruins and search for Nartise. It is a coastal town of sorts, just south of Senchal.\n\nWith some persuasion, that clawless Dark Elf should let slip the location of the Perfect Pounce. Then we steal her back!
Move along, walker. Our captain is in a mood.

Honor and faith, wayfarer.\n\nBlademaster Kasura awaits you at the Vulkhel Guard Manor in the city of Vulkhel Guard. She heard tales of your Dragon slaying skills and has requested to meet you at once.

The cultists moved through Pridehome swiftly. I suspect more await us beyond this gate.\n\nThe Moon-Priests here didn't even possess weapons to defend themselves with. Why would the Order of the New Moon attack this peaceful place?

You have certainly proved yourself worthy of the Mask of Alkosh.\n\nJust do not expect it to ensure all your victories. Its power was only awakened through our connection. With my departure, it shall be but a mask.
You're back! Did you find Nishzo? Did he cough up his piece of the tapestry?
I feel there's more to Clan Mother Tadali's words than pure ceremony.\n\nStill, no time to stand around wondering. We have a mask to find! Let's enter the Halls of the Highmane.

I'm honored to help with this restoration. They simply do not make works of this quality and ambition anymore. If you're able to find the remaining pieces you'll be doing a great service for not only Senchal and the Khajiit, but for all of Tamriel.
Did that—? That drunk Khajiit just took off his clothes. Why did he take off his clothes?\n\nWe're supposed to deliver a token, not some soused cat's dirty laundry.
Sai Sahan not so humbly requests your presence. Seems he has another mission for you.
We need to find the rest of the braziers and ignite their flames.
I knew Winks could do it! I asked her to find Maezi and she led us right to this spot!
My ancestors were clever indeed. Come. Let's keep moving.
You know, where I come from, we call this sort of thing "clever magic." Gods know why. Maybe we call it that so we feel smarter when we kick a wizard's teeth in.

Islands were not meant to fly and we were not meant to walk upon them while they do so! Let's get this over with before everything comes crashing down.\n\nNahfahlaar arrived shortly before you did. With a Dragon beside us, we may just stand a chance.
What are you waiting for? Follow Ironbelly! But don't get too close. I already made him nervous enough for the both of us.

You'd think with all the truly bizarre events of my life, not much would unnerve me. Yet, an enormous arcane storm roiling in the sky still manages to do the trick.\n\nIf we hurry, we can find the source.
I know this is our best course of action, but I can't help worrying about Lyris. I'm not sure I can forgive myself if something happens to her.
Go on. You and Lyris deal with any hostiles and find the Undergrove. Then we can finally test the elixir.
Let's go inside and get this over with before I change my mind.\n\nYou know, I tried to convince Fenn to add some mead into the mix, but he totally ignored me.
I think they'll listen to you. Try speaking with them.

Take the message from the table, then see if you can convince Fennorian to join us. Maybe with his help, we can devise a defense against the storms.\n\nI'll stay here and continue to annoy my father until he gives this threat the attention it deserves.
We've got the crew working on cutting the Cormorant free from the ice.\n\nI don't think I've ever seen them this eager to work. Now that they have their strength back, they're practically tireless!
That note troubles me. If that Khajiit really was collecting corpses … what's become of the captain? And the rest of the crew? \n\nLet's keep looking.
That wound's bad. He doesn't have a lot of time. Quick! Talk to him and find out what happened here while I keep watch.

Hmm. You're not a subject of this realm. And that woman with you—she's the Giantess of the East. The high king warned us to beware of Pact spies.\n\nIf Princess Svana trusts you, however, you have my ear. Tell me about this threat.
Whatever they were doing to this strange plant, it looks like we put a stop to it.\n\nNow let's go find Fenn.
Open the gate. We need to reach the tower's pinnacle before it's too late.
Svargrim's gone up into the city. We'll have to stop him there.
Let's put Blackreach behind us and follow these tunnels to Solitude.
No matter what you find down in the cellar, please recover the jarl's crown.
Did you retrieve the key from the chamberlain's sanctum? We need it to open the door to the catacombs.
Looks like I made it back just in time. This place is crawling with vampires and that one was about to make a meal out of you.

I'll join you soon. It's important I protect the path for Helsi and the others. Hopefully we find a safe place to recover. I owe them for my … last failure.\n\nScout ahead beyond the tower. With any luck, you'll find Bjora.
You've returned! Have you brought back the Petraloop? Will my fingers glide over its gentle curves once more?
I finally figured it out. Svana's problem. It's you. You're a bad influence.\n\nAll this so-called heroics. It might inspire the princess, but all you really did was kill my fun.
I'll search around here. Why don't you take a look at the door on the other side of the chamber.
A laboratory, eh? Fair enough.\n\nOur informant will be all right. Or he won't. We gave him a fighting chance. What he does now is up to him. Let's go.
You're going to talk to Elle?\n\nGood. You have my gratitude. The less people I have to deal with, the better I can concentrate on my work.
I was so worried about you and Claudina! I'm glad you're back safe.\n\nYou can regale me with the story later! Go and talk to Elle!
Did you find anything of interest in the crate?
Ah! Oh, thank Kyne, you're not one of these tomb robbers. Or another ghost. I've had my fill of ghosts.
Don't talk to me. Find out what Ena's going on about.\n\nAnd do hurry. We still have to save the bridge.
We think this old mine is where our assassin fled to? Good a place as any to bury him.
You'd better hurry. There isn't much time.
Hail stranger. I don't suppose you've seen a caravan on your travels?\n\nWe've been expecting one, stocked to the brim with supplies for the Dragon Bridge garrison, but it never arrived.
Local wisdom dictates that only the very brave or the very foolish seek the counsel of vampires and old crones. Which are you, I wonder?\n\nWell, out with it. What can Old Mjolen do for you?

My research into Skyrim included the legends of Blackreach, of course, but I never expected to see it. It's massive!\n\nThat letter you found in the assassin's hideout. It mentioned a mining consortium in the darkness below. Could this be the place?
So, is it over? What happened to Svargrim? And where's Svana?
I regret we didn't throw a parade to welcome you back, but I'll cheer enough for a hundred souls if you tell me you put that back-biter of a high king to the sword!\n\nBut what of Svana? Is she …?
We seem to have survived, thank the gods.\n\nI thought for certain we were all about to witness the end of the world.
Thank you for assisting my fool husband. \n\nI hope he's ready for warmer weather, because I plan to drag his sorry arse to Summerset and keep him there permanently.
Excellent work, my friend. And Pickle, of course.\n\nCome, we must not waste time. I've found our way out of here.
Did you recover the key?
Get on with it. There is no need to prolong this.
<Pickle sniffs the air.>
You don't have to be a mine foreman to see how unstable those tunnels are. If Chief Urzikh uses more of her stonemelt, we're all going to die!

Oh, traveler, you must turn back! Chillwind Depths, it's crawling with giant insects!\n\nI need to go inside and gather ingredients to heal my sister, but the things in there … they keep chasing me out!

Just the adventurer I wanted to see. You look well! And you're just in time.\n\nI need a strapping assistant to help me traverse this ruin. It is less than pristine, I'll grant you. But the Dwemeric treasures within should be quite splendid.
Hjarnam is another of our order. He's gravely injured … there's so much blood. \n\nPlease, talk to him. I cannot bear to see him this way.
Avoid detection if at all possible. The workers are fearful and may react to trespassers with aggression.

Rigurt's friend Farethor, a butcher from Greenshade, is wintering in Dragon Bridge. His meat is divine! And we can season it with Orcish howlwater. Rigurt knows Mahgrok, in Mor Khazgur, brews it.\n\nWhile you get those, Rigurt will get the final item.

The ritual bears out my fears. I recognize the curse corrupting life around Morthal. \n\nYears ago, a death-mage named Maxten killed a group of town guards at Kjenstag ruins. The same magic she used then now animates these undead.
I hope you demonstrate more sobriety in your report than what I've grown used to since arriving in Morthal.\n\nYou'll find me attending to Brun's injuries over at the Whispering Axe when you return.
Judging from the smell, I'd say Stone Garden is probably just a little farther down this chasm.\n\nHow about you take the lead?

Nicely done diverting the castle's patrols towards the front hall. We didn't encounter any trouble slipping in the side entrance.\n\nWhich is likely for the best. My confidence that Talfyg will betray us grows stronger by the second.
To the Hall of the Dead with you, hurry along. Ingurt still serves as high priest, I believe.\n\nWe're much the same, he and I, yet he gets the fancy temple. And I? I get a hut in the woods.
Hey there. Do you know anything about bottles? Ah, never mind.
Oh, there you are. I was supposed to deliver a message for you from Fennorian, but I couldn't find you. I gave it to Princess Svana in Solitude.

Had you going there for a moment, didn't I? I … I just wanted to illustrate the perils of overconfidence! A critical lesson for dashing heroes like us.\n\nNow, feel free to solve the puzzle. I'll observe … from over here.

I hear someone convinced Svyne to stop gorging himself on pork-pies and do some work for a change. \n\nIf you're here to try and convince me to meet with that unbearable oaf, forget it. I swore to never set eyes upon that man again, and I meant it.
These books contain the collective wisdom of Skyrim's greatest thinkers. So, please … wash your hands before browsing.

For years, I have tracked the location of every Pale Man attack. Each one brought me closer to its lair. These last two confirm it—the Pale Man must be on the northern coast between Dragon Bridge and Solitude.\n\nIt won't escape me again.

Let me guess. You found one of those ridiculous handbills Reginus posted all over town. Gods, it's like we're holding auditions for children's theater.\n\nPlease understand, this is a serious commitment. You really wish to join the Antiquarian Circle?
Let's move quickly, before a big bug or something worse shows up.
The sooner we get out of this place, the better.

You're not from around here, are you? Pardon my rudeness, but there's been talk of strange travelers in the wilderness. People disappearing from their homes.\n\nYou can never be too careful, especially around outsiders.
Ghost stories, the lot of them! People don't just up and disappear! And storms don't turn people into monsters. At least not any storm I've experienced in Skyrim.
Sorry, I know we don't have much time. I just need to prepare myself, you know?\n\nAnd I need something from you.
Walk off, pal. No time for useless chatter.
Maybe I misheard over the roiling of my belly. Did that oaf say he was going to make a meal worthy of my tastes?\n\nIf he wants to try and face my palette, so be it!
Keep moving. There's a ladder at the end of this tunnel that leads up to the castle.

You did it, my friend! We traveled through these so-called void portals and are hardly the worse for the wear.\n\nWe may catch up to Rada and Lady Belain yet! Let's see if the doors over there can be opened.
My clan is somewhere beneath this barrow. We must find Nathari before it's too late. Convince her that nothing good can come from trying to fulfill the prophecy.

Fennorian will reproduce the Reach alchemy while Gwendis performs the Nighthollow rites. You must manage the Dwemer machines controlling the tonal, aetheric, and kinetic energies.\n\nI will attempt to scry the stone and direct you accordingly.
I'll admit, tracking down Arkasis's laboratory was a lot simpler. I don't smell anything alchemical around here, just a lot of metal and steam.
I wish we had more to go on. I'm about to try my luck by swinging my axe into the walls.
I haven't had any success as yet. Though my method so far has just been to systematically prod things, so I can't say that I'm too surprised.
Use the insignia at the door. Let's see if it dispels the ward and grants us access to the Dark Halls.
The journal was still here? Amazing! What did it say?
So you're the one who helped my ward Gwendis with her inquiries? If I had been completely honest with her, I could have saved you both the trouble.\n\nPlease, accept my apologies.
Feel like I got stepped on by a mammoth, but I guess that means I'm alive.\n\nWhat's going on? Why's the Darkstorm still going?
Keep watch for the offerings we need, but remain alert for those monsters created by the storm. They prowl outside the village like hungry wolves in search of prey.
Please, examine the ritual pyre for me. Tell me what you find. I need to compose myself for what comes next.
We have the mushroom Freyleth requested. Now let's find that lift she mentioned and get out of here.
If you still have things to do in the throne room, please deal with it. We need to make a good impression on Ard Caddach if we're going to gain his trust and cooperation.

Hang on, hero! I did a bit of scouting and you need to hear what I have to say.\n\nNchuand-Zel is crawling with Gray Host soldiers. Not to mention all the Dwarven constructs that clank around down there, too.
Freyleth can tell you more about her plan, if you're really interested.\n\nI hope that you and Adusa decide to help us, but either way, we can't leave until we see this through.
I apologize for my horrid appearance. I assure you, if I wasn't half-starved because of that bastard, Trenlor, I'd make a much better impression.\n\nWill you and Adusa help us save the Lothid clan?
Verandis said he sent you to talk to the scrap dealer, and here you are. Good to see you, by the way.\n\nAnyway, Verandis needs to talk to you. Right away, he said. So, let's go.
Did you find anything to explain why the ritual failed?
Damned Dwarves, am I right?\n\nDevices aren't natural, what with all the gears and cogs and everything.

This sounds like some sort of summoning ritual. Interesting.\n\nAn alliance with Arana and her rebels is essential. We will need to add their strength to ours to defeat the Gray Host, so do as she asks.

Let's hurry. We need to contain all the pockets of tonal disturbance before they're allowed to spread! I shudder to think what this strange magic could do if left unchecked.\n\nWe must find Master Pythis as well and warn him. He'll know what to do.
All right—here we are. According to the map, this hatch opens to a walkway that leads to the Grand Archive. Once we're in, let's find the book and get out of here.
Please, go on ahead without me. I'll catch up in a moment.\n\nAll these people. Friends, loved ones—snuffed out. For what? It's all just too much.
A good Old Life to you! I'm happy to see you again, traveler. To what do I owe the pleasure? Are you here to inquire about participating in the ceremony again?
You've come to the wrong place, outsider. Briar Rock belongs to the Thornroot clan. They kill anyone they catch here—or worse.
Do as Snow Lily suggests. Burn the dense foliage and reveal what's hidden on those stone pillars. We will react to whatever you uncover.
The first half of the Wounding is clear and look at you! I can already see your strength growing.\n\nLet hardship be your teacher—a demanding, unforgiving mentor—and you will be stronger for it.

As long as we're welcome here, I'm going to take advantage of the situation and have a brief conversation with the vateshran. Compare what she knows with what I learned at Hroldan Ring.\n\nWe'll see you down in that cave.

Oh! Hello again. Wow, I was just thinking of you.\n\nLook, about the last time we spoke, when I was having a … well, a moment. In the middle of nowhere. And then you came along—I wanted to say I'm sorry.
If you have something to show Fialyn, get on with it. The longer we wait, the more dangerous this becomes.
Is it done, outsider? Did you offer your blessing to the intended couple?
My daughter and the misbegotten son of the Six-Fords are in the handfasting cave. Go and do as the chief-of-chiefs instructed and let's get this over with.
If we must participate in this handfasting, the least you could do is hurry up and get to it. The cave lies to the north, outsider.
We have exchanged enough words, outsider. If you have more to say, talk to the chief-of-chiefs.\n\nBetter yet, go to the handfasting cave and give my son your blessing.
Do what the chief-of-chiefs asked, outsider.
I don't know how much longer we can wait here. Did you discuss things with the chief-of-chiefs?
Well, you made quick work of that. \n\nYou already found the coil fragment at Karthspire Lea, aye? All that's left is to go to Hroldan Ring and … see the end of this.

I thought it might come to this. \n\nIt seems the decision rests with you now. Either force the handfasting to end the feud, or support Eslyn and Madearn and hope their time together signals hope for it to end another way.

You approach with purpose, wanderer. Hircine has sent you to me for a reason, it would seem.\n\nMy apprentices should return shortly. I sent them to retrieve the sacred relics needed to dedicate this shrine. Until then, what can I do for you?

Nothing is ever simple when it comes to Stibbons. Why should I have expected anything different from these pale imitations?\n\nEven if the floor plate didn't open the main door, it does seem to have unlocked something. Look how the blue fire blazes.
I can't believe we lost Destron. I should have been there. Maybe together we could have saved him.
Something's going on, isn't it? It seems like every Black Fin legionnaire is in a hurry today.\n\nLet me guess. Vandacia is coming for us again.
My Black Fin Legion will be ready. See who else will come to our aid.
Technically, you work for the captain, so you should tell him what we uncovered.
You see, little mortal? The amulet worked perfectly.\n\nNow let us enter, deal with the Dagonists, and see what secrets Emperor Leovic left behind.
Please. I have no time for either constituents or admirers. My life may be in danger!

We're close to freeing the Golden Anvil from the clutches of greed, I can feel it. We just need to figure out the trade-ministers' hiding spots from the clues they left behind.\n\nI pray the sigils are still in place and intact.
As mud is my mother, I know that with your help, we can save my friends from this horrible fate.\n\nLet us head quickly inside. Keep your teeth sharp.

Commander Ortin oversees the Fort Blueblood brigadines. Tell him I sent you and he'll give you his full cooperation.\n\nMeanwhile, I'll recall Ivory Brigade squadrons from the surrounding countryside. The city and this castle will be defended.

All of the remaining councilors in Blackwood are gathered here in the castle—Faleria, Vandacia, and myself. While we await the arrival of the scribe I sent for, tell me what you uncovered in Gideon. I'm not sure I agree with Vandacia's assessment.
The wine is exceptionally good here in Gideon.\n\nI need something to calm my nerves after what happened to us in the Deadlands.
Fort Blueblood is under my protection. I take such a position quite seriously, as you might imagine.
More people showing up. Did the weakling Drathas recruit assistance in retrieving his people? You do appear more capable than that feeble creature.\n\nI assume our deal stays the same?
Well, what was inside the cache? Have we finally discovered the secret of the Longhouse Emperors?

You put the fear of the gods into our captive cultist. He was sobbing on the floor when I gave up and left. I did meet a surprisingly talkative vampire, though. He told me which way you went.\n\nAnd seriously, do not turn your back on Tenarei.
I think Seeks took off that way after the commotion started. I think. You should probably take the lead.
If the Painted Eye knows about the crypt and the sarcophagus, then they're ahead of us. We need to catch up.\n\nYou get the crypt key. I'll keep watch on the Painted Eye while you do.

These relics … damaged or not, they're still amazing, fascinating, fantastic. But we have to locate the horn if we can. It's the one thing that can prove Phalevon's legend beyond any doubt.\n\nAnd it may be dangerous to leave it here.
Come, friend. This is no place for us to linger!
