What a bleak and terrible place! The sooner we're done in Dagon's realm, the better. I don't think mortals are welcome here.
This must be the Obelisk of Origin. Impressive!\n\nYou need to activate it so you can bear witness to what we see.
This plan will work. Right? Of course it will work. Just follow that mote!
Try to remember not to kill Quistley Silvelle. If he's wearing cultist robes and singing the praises of Sithis, it might be tempting. But he's somewhat more useful to me alive than dead.
Well? Aren't you supposed to be helping Revus with this folly?
I'll get the twins to Gideon. Meet me there so we can tell Governor Keshu what's going on.
I'm just a gardener. I can't decide who lives and dies. That's too heavy for me.\n\nYou're the adventurer here. What would you do?

Did I just get a proposal from a ghost? Up until now, the only man who ever wooed me was a stable hand in Bergama!\n\nI know I should recoil at this. It's profane! Blasphemous? Right? But, gods he's cute. And the way he speaks! It's like a dream!

Remember, while the wards are in place, none of us can enter the vault. Use the book the Wood Elf carries to disable them and open the way. Once the wards are down, I shall meet you inside.\n\nNow, hurry. The Waking Flame could arrive at any moment.

Where are we? It's been so long since I walked the grounds of the castle, I scarcely recognize it.\n\nWhatever the place, it is good to speak to someone again. And to see the fair image of my lost love.
Now might be the perfect time for a little Seemly Justiciar, Surly Justiciar? Go ahead and question Cres, I'll follow your lead.
Welcome to the Happy Crow. I haven't much hospitality to offer you. Better you move on.
Well that didn't work. Perhaps we chose the wrong pool?\n\nLet's keep looking. One of these will show Sister of Pools my brother has repented. It has to.

I told Keshu not to dismiss my personal guard. Now look what happened!\n\nNever underestimate the cunning of the Dark Brotherhood. The assassin must be found and brought to justice. Please, if you truly want to help, you must apprehend him.
If you came to help, you have my thanks—but it's not needed. Looks like Prince Vaugr is going down with his ship.\n\nNot that the ship is going down, I mean. It just—you know what I mean.
How could you sleep through that? Everyone else has already disembarked. We need to hurry!
So this is Bloodrun Cave, huh? Creepy.\n\nYou go on ahead. I'll follow behind you. Make sure nothing tries to ambush us. I'll catch up farther in.

Eveli is as brave as the graht-oak is tall, but someone else will be interested in this secret. Someone dangerous, most likely.\n\nYou'll need to be careful for the both of you, because my sister doesn't know the meaning of that word.

Ugh, not another one. Look, I already told you ….\n\nOh, wait, you're not from this tribe, are you? Thank the Divines! I've tried telling these others that my brigadines have nothing to do with their disappearing people, but they won't listen!
Go ahead, strike the totem with all your might! \n\nI honestly do not know if this will work, but it cannot hurt. I will stand … back here.
We can't get to the pedestal where we saw the cultists open the portal, but there must be another one of them somewhere within these ruins. Let's try to find one.

I knew I had you pinned right! You're in luck, I already have a kit made up with everything you'll need.\n\nAll you have to do is find the target and set everything up when the time is right. Comedic timing is everything, as I'm sure you know!
Our house is just over there, on the west side of town. There may be something among Annyce's things that points to where she ran off to, but my nerves are too frayed to see it. I'm at my wit's end.
That s'wit's locked us out! We aren't getting that gate open by force, but I bet that mechanism plays some part in getting it open.
Let's find that shrine before anything really awful happens.\n\nWhat kind of a cracked acorn thinks it's a good idea to summon up a Daedric Prince?

Jephre's bones. The surge of magicka created by the portals you came through … it must have cracked this skyshard. Without a functioning skyshard this gate remains locked and there's no way for us to proceed.\n\nDamn.

Did you see that? His soul, drawn from his body. As if pulled by some force. My scales parch with fear from the implications.\n\nAttacks from these Sul-Xan grow like weeds across this region. But they may have greater plans here than mere savagery.
I'm afraid to ask, but I've got to. What did you find?
Count Auzin told Clairene I was dead? And he conspired with Lord Silvelle to keep me in ignorance, too? What kind of life would I have had if these cowards had just told my sister and I the truth?
I communed with the spirit successfully. But the mystery merely deepens.

I knew things were tense, but I didn't think a war would break out the moment I reached the castle. The cultists spilled out of portals like ants erupting from anthills.\n\nIt was all I could do to get out of the way and reach a place of safety!
Onimiril's writings said he brought the puzzle box here for some kind of ritual. Considering he was ousted from the Mages Guild, let's assume whatever he was doing was bad news.
Well met, adventurer! I carry an important message from Eveli Sharp-Arrow!
The torment I face is my burden to bear, if only my lady would show me mercy.
Xyria. It's been a few years since I've heard that name.\n\nI take it things went better for you with Melyn Drad than they did for Vos. No surprise there. Tell me what you know.
Tee-Wan went off to do a bit of investigating on his own, but he said he would return soon.\n\nDid you manage to get anything out of that idiot Melyn Drad?

Don't mind Mirri. She takes too much after her father. I've been dying to finally meet the person my daughter's been adventuring with.\n\nThough I hadn't planned on being chained up like a common criminal upon our first meeting.
I'm afraid things will only grow more difficult from here. If what the seneschal wrote is true, the Knights of the Silver Rose have begun to covet the dangerous items they once swore to lock away.
Another piece of the puzzle. The question is where it fits in.\n\nWe'll gather what we can carry and be right behind you.

That imbecile we just killed reeked of the Mad God's influence. All those trinkets in his bag of tricks must have come at the cost of his sanity.\n\nWhat won't you creatures trade away for a little power?

Once you have enough cursed feathers, you must fashion them into an effigy in the likeness of a Wraith-of-Crows. It should be close enough to the Crowborne Horror to work.\n\nYou can do this at any of the workbenches in Olyve's Brewery.
It ran. Every other Daedra here has lunged right for our throats. I don't find that as reassuring as you might think. It might mean they're regrouping. Preparing for us.
I'm ready to end this. Let's go to Destruction's Solace.
Please, I need a moment to think.
That went too far. Did they really need to torture the Anchorite to get answers? There has to be another way.

The Wood Elf had no right to stop the ritual. It was not her decision to make. Without any other lead, the Anchorite's memories were our best chance to determine Mehrunes Dagon's plans. \n\nNow we have nothing!
Why would they hide just more books behind such a lock? There must be something important here. \n\nSearch around. But quickly. We can't afford to lose the trail.
When a lair becomes violated, the best thing you can do is burn it to the ground, move on, and find a new sanctum.\n\nPity. I was just getting used to this location.

So many avenues to ponder. Sister Celdina and the Waking Flame. The cataclysts. Valkynaz Nokvroz and Mehrunes Dagon's role in all this.\n\nI shall return to Fargrave and see what else I can learn. I'll call upon you when I need you, little mortal.
I see another lucent up on that ledge. Let's find a way up to it.

Ah, the messenger found you. Good. Sister Celdina has the means to create more cataclysts, so the danger to Fargrave and Nirn remains.\n\nWe must ascertain the location of Deadlight and the hidden stronghold the Bladebearer prisoners heard mentioned.

How can I decide who should be free? The woman who died after a lifetime of service to the Tribunal or the one who knew she would die but still did what was right? Nilera or my grandmother?\n\nSotha Sil, free the spirit you choose, I won't stop you.
We're not likely to find Celdina or her next cataclyst device out here. Let's get inside the citadel and see what we can learn.\n\nLead the way. I'll stand ready to heal you if we run into trouble.

You and Rynkyus can chase his missing Bladebearers. I will return to Fargrave to sift for rumors about Sister Celdina or the cataclyst. And perhaps see if the Anchorite has remembered anything new.\n\nI will find you when your work is done.
Bah, it's likely a mortal ruse. He merely pretends to be mad until he gets the elixir he wants. Shall I torment him until he confesses, master?
We have a task that awaits us within the Sever, yet you linger. Mortal curiosity must be exhausting.
Vontan. This one is not known to me. We must learn more. Go to the Fleapits District. I will follow shortly.
You brought the map of the vault with you from the Isle of Joys, right? Let's go to the location it specified. There has to be something there that can lead us to the egonymic.
That seems to have worked! Quickly, ask him about the Riven Cataclyst. We don't know how long he'll remain lucid.

Tell Noroth I'll face whatever punishment the town devises. It will give the Daedra and the mortals something to work out. Together. Maybe in that way, something good can come out of all this.\n\nI really was just trying to help.
We should get moving, little mortal.
Even facing terrible and certain death, your allies come! You have built this army. Now you must lead it to glory! My whiskers quiver in anticipation of the coming battle!
There are things I still wish to learn, little mortal. Continue to assist me and I shall make sure you are suitably rewarded.
Looks like we found at least some of the missing Bladebearers. Let's let them out before Rynkyus tries to chew through the bars himself.

Ah, my favorite mortal returns. I do appreciate when Lyranth deigns to share you with me.\n\nDon't mind Rynkyus. He believes that every problem can be solved with a sword. I do hope you have a more interesting topic to discuss with me.

I was hoping the portal key would have gotten us deeper into the fortress, but we will have to make do.\n\nLet us hurry and find the inner keep. I do not expect the Bladebearers to hold the attention of Nokvroz's main force for very long.
Valkynaz Nokvroz will pay for his transgressions against the Bladebearers clan. This I so swear!

I will follow shortly. After I confer with my scouts and Lyranth. \n\nLook for my Bladebearers, mortal. You cannot spot the signs we leave, but they themselves will be visible to you. I will be highly agitated if my search for them comes to naught.
Well, here we are. It's strange remembering how all this started, but we're going to end it now, right? We'll stop Sombren, and we'll stop Mehrunes Dagon, too.

Whim thinks Fargrave is safe. She is wrong.\n\nMehrunes Dagon has no interest in Fargrave's denizens, but he understands the usefulness of bridges between worlds. Nokvroz would be well rewarded if he can deliver Fargrave to him.
The time has come. Let us go to Destruction's Solace.
With performers like this, you'd think more people'd get crocked.

Let's find Sister Celdina and determine the exact nature of her plan to take over Fargrave. I want to figure out how to stop her votive runes before they harm any more of the city's mortal population.

I did not think Sister Celdina capable of performing such a powerful ritual. You did well, mortal. A few more moments and the magic would have exploded across Fargrave, leaving the city defenseless and destroying all of the Daedra.\n\nIncluding me.
I'll finish this and meet you at the Collector's villa. It's on the west side, in a neighborhood that's strictly Daedric. So be careful and watch your step until I get there.

Show Madam Whim the encoded note and get her to provide us with the name of a proper scribe who can decipher it.\n\nThe short time I've subjected myself to this establishment has left me feeling both infuriated and disgusted.
Give him the spring elixir. I am sure it is the right one. I hope it works.
My mind feels like a dry flower. If I touch it, I'm sure it will break apart … it will crumble.
With the Undertaker's arcane matrix restored we'll be able to summon it as well. Go ahead and restore the power to that blue stone and we can continue.
I don't know whether your return here is the sign of good news or bad. Did you find another ill-fated entity under contract with me?
You are the mortal that Rynkyus has allied with? We will see if he has made a wise decision if you manage to find our missing Kyn.
You have not come here to speak to me. Nor have I come here to converse with a mortal. Away with you.
So, he's agreed to help? Excellent. You see? Simple threats can be very effective motivators.\n\nPlace the sword on the table. Let's see how this ritual plays out.
Your timing is impeccable as ever. Did the Covenant send you? I could use some help with the mess Jakarn has left me this time.

Za'ji suggests a second look at the shipwrights' village then. He did not get so good a look when he and his first mate skulked through before, for fear of stirring up the dead, but since they are already well stirred now, we may as well be thorough!
Put the sword on the table. Get this over with.
It scurries in a most unpleasant manner. Talk to the vermin, little mortal. Find out what it is and whether it can help us decipher the encoded note.
I'm sure Master Rrvenk was speaking of volcanic rocks with this analogy. There must be geological activity nearby that would prove his point. See if you can gather stones that are as Hyxo described.
Don't mind Sunel if he speaks with a barbed tongue. That means he likes the look of you.
I don't know you. And I don't see why I should try to change that. Adventurers just cause trouble for everyone else.
Back again? Why is it that mortals can't seem to get enough of what Madam Whim has to offer?\n\nMy establishment and its many wonders are always available … for the right price.
I'm afraid we don't have a choice. Lower your guard against a fighter of Quentyn's skill, and he'll cut you in half.\n\nDamn the Ascendant Magus for twisting the general's mind!

Lady Arabelle wastes no time, I see. I suppose that's why I asked her to assist the Society of the Steadfast with this conference, although I'm not really sure there's a problem to solve quite yet.\n\nAh, well. What can I help you with?

Report back to Lady Arabelle and tell her about Quentyn's plight. I'll be along shortly. \n\nI want to try to convince Ryvana to take shelter at Stonelore Grove one more time. While the Ascendant Order is active, she's in danger out here by herself.

The nearby Greycloak camps are a good place to start looking for the blessed awl.\n\nDo be careful of ferocious beasts. I've heard them howling. The favor of Zenithar won't fall on these laborers if their skill is only used to craft a funeral pyre.
I'll never regret marrying Tarrinore, but after nearly a century together, I wish that she absorbed some of my level-headedness.

I knew you looked friendly! There goes a true friend to animals, I said.\n\nNow, with you to accompany me into the cave, our negotiations can begin. They may get rough, but I refuse to leave without my Privette.

Now that we recovered the medallions, it's time to deliver them to the various delegations. \n\nYou know about the peace talks and the stakes we're facing. Are you willing to help us finish this, despite the threat posed by the Ascendant Order?
We've done it! All three trials done and all three trophies in hand. Well done!\n\nLet's meet at the tourney pavilion. We'll raise a flagon after, all right?
Hello again! Did you manage to find that key?

I knew the Mages Guild was sending their chosen representative, but I didn't expect it to be Arch-Magister Delric. He was my mentor. And he created the master medallion I used as a template for the invitations.\n\nGo ahead and give him the medallion.

Hey, good-looking! I don't think you've had the pleasure yet. I'm Jakarn. I'm more of a lover than a fighter, which is why Lady Arabelle brought you into the fold, I suppose.\n\nAnyway, here I am, working off my debt, one lockpick at a time.

She's … not so scary, I guess. Is this what it's like for Dark Elves? Just a casual chat with their late, great ancestors. \n\nWell, it's not so common a thing where I come from, so I better make the most of it.

So here's my plan. We ride the raft over to Whalefall, find Anton, then leave. Now that I've said it out loud, I see it's not much of a plan. But it's what I got.\n\nI'd like to get a move on, though. My partner is clever, but not especially tough.
Go ahead. Ask her to take us to Amenos. She'll think we're crazy. \n\nAnd she won't be wrong.

Hey, good-looking! I wasn't expecting to see you again so soon. \n\nOh, and I wasn't giving this fine seneschal a hard time. I was just … building a trusting rapport. Anyway, I delivered the Aldmeri Dominion medallion. We can be on our way.
Congratulations, challenger. Surviving the Trial of Constitution is no mean feat!\n\nExamine the tablet. The last of the three words you need is inscribed there.
Whoever you are, I was here first. You've got to hang back. Tourney honor demands it!

It's a shame the Ascendant Order got to Lord Bacaro's retainers before you could. What could they have seen that warranted their deaths?\n\nPerhaps we'll learn more at Castle Navire … although I'm certainly not in the mood for a party.
I'll accompany you and Lady Arabelle to the dockmaster's home. But don't expect too much. If you ask me, Arnauld didn't seem too concerned about finding those ships.
We need to enter the Undergrove and set the Evergrowth free.\n\nCome. There's an entrance in the northern section of the grove.
We're here! Use one of the workbenches to make the hammer!

Once we find The Mirrored Way in Magister Irin's library, I can finish my counterspell. I just hope the old man wasn't serious about putting something dangerous inside to keep me out.\n\nHe was definitely kidding. Had to be. Come on, let's go.
See what Emeric wants. He gets grumpy if his wishes aren't immediately obeyed. I can wait until you're done to find out what happened in there.
Lead the way, captor my captor. Those Green Serpents will never see through our clever ruse!
With Suungir once more in hand, I feel better already!\n\nLet's find this Ascendant Lord and his Magus. I want to show them what it means to attack a Nord warrior!

Count Damard—or should I say the Ascendant Magus—wouldn't have left me to rescue unless he was sure we couldn't do anything to stop him. I'd like to prove him wrong.\n\nLet's get to the Navire Docks and get aboard the Silver Swan before it sails.
See you when I see you, good-looking. \n\nHmm. I wonder if Lady A would mind if I borrowed one of her horses ….

I'd suggest you talk to some patients who are feeling its effects. Try Erebil Vules, by the fountain. Or Milagi—he likes to watch the sea. Oh, and speak with Mender Teliel too. She's inside.\n\nI'll be waiting upstairs when you're done.

Between the two of us, we can have the ritual prepared and ready to perform by the time you return.\n\nWith it, we'll hopefully find the source of the disturbance and learn more about the Ascendant Magus in the process.
Valessea told me of your ongoing investigation into the Ascendant Order. I think these insurgents may be the cause of at least some of the grove's anguish.
Let the Magus go, damn it. That bastard did something to Lady Arabelle! We have to find her before it's too late!

The lads were making bets on whether you'd come back or not. I put half a potato on you. Looks like old Adwig's a few potatoes richer! Ha! You hear that, Donel? Put that in your pipe and smoke it!\n\nNow, how about it? You find my pack?
Ha! I knew this island couldn't break the Prowler! She is sleek, and strong, and beautiful, just like her captain!
Could you please talk with that Breton and bargain for my release?

I don't see Lord Bacaro here, so I am sure he wouldn't mind if we borrowed the leaf from one of his plants. But … I don't know if I would recognize a mammoth ear. Unless it was attached to a mammoth.\n\nPerhaps you could look?
I'm sorry, but I'm very busy. I'll get to you just as soon as I can.
You will have to forgive me. I have never felt more sick in all my life. Did we meet last night?\n\nI'm afraid I can't remember.
Please tell me you found out where <<1>> hides his illicit goods? And that you brought back proof for <<2>>? I can't feel my fingers anymore!
There's a table in Viralaine's laboratory where you can use my blood to brew the antidote. Please, you must hurry.
I hope Yvelle and the others make it out of here safely. \n\nWe still need to find father. Who knows how long he's been in here fighting the Hadolids. He must be getting tired.
Oh, well done, my friend! Of course, most of the credit goes to my hammer and chisel, but still ….\n\nAnyway, I'm done with this place. Let's get out of here.

Lord Bacaro should be at Steadfast Manor. Do hurry before he strikes off with an army of hired knights to join a battle that's already over. \n\nBesides, it's not often I get to send someone good news.
I've got unfinished business with the Ascendant Order. The sooner we settle that debt, the happier I'll be.
Did I hear Lady Arabelle correctly? She wants to steal a ship and sail through hostile waters? And hope nobody notices?\n\nAll right, I'm in.
Don't worry. Za'ji is here to help!

It's the duneripper you can't see that's the real danger. Za'ji might think the worst is over, but I have a feeling Captain Kaleen is right. The Ascendant Order isn't finished. I can feel it in my paws. \n\nYou better talk to her.
We have to get to the Motalion Necropolis! If the Emerald Eye is holding Song there, then we have a chance to rescue her! Come on, hurry!
Oh, hello. This one apologizes if he and Silverslip surprised you. We wanted to follow you and Ember to make sure you were safe, but we will not get in the way.
I always figured it would be Ember who came looking for me. That girl doesn't know when to quit. \n\nGo on, talk to her. Apparently she isn't ready to speak to me.
Stendarr give me the strength to survive amateur detectives. \n\nAurelia's friend said she was taken northeast towards an Ayleid ruin. Let's move.
Isobel is protective of our High Isles lady. I understand that. Aurelia is just … lovely.\n\nAhem, and intelligent. And … detail-oriented. Sailing together teaches you a lot about a person.
I've no time for pleasantries. I'm up to my ears in cargo manifests. You have some business with me?
Hey again. Bet you thought I was kidding about following you.
Do you mind? I want to spend every moment before I sail with my beloved Janne. So, go bother someone else and leave us to our dalliance.
My big brother. So proud, so famous. But not anymore! I made sure he'll never be remembered!

I am a foolish, foolish man who thought himself smart and worldly. \n\nI was taken in by a pretty face and a jawline that could cut glass … I'm still a bit stung by the whole affair. Do forgive me my mood.

I read these plaques all the time, but I never remember a word. Just that history has forgotten my love, and even I can only remember bits and pieces. Until today. \n\nI remember Tobin Moorcroft and I spit on his memory!

Thank you for talking to Isobel. I know how this seems. But I truly believe we're close to finding something here. \n\nAnd don't worry, I'll write to my mother. If I don't, she'll send half the knightly orders after me.
Thanks to Queen Ayrenn, my wounds are healed and my claws are sharp. I'm ready to do what's necessary to get us off this island!
Thank you for coming to speak with me, both of you. I've been in regular correspondence with Aurelia since your last adventure. \n\nUnfortunately her letters have stopped, and I'm worried.
Lead the way, captor my captor. Those Green Serpents will never see through our clever ruse!

You keep winning games like that and you'll be in the advanced tier in no time.\n\nJust keep training, completing Kishka's challenges, and gathering new cards. We all need to prepare for the next tournament!

Welcome back. You return wiser and hungrier for competition, is it not so? Tribute has that effect on people!\n\nNow, I have something for you. A gift and formal welcome to the Gonfalon Chapter of the Roister's Club. I know you will put it to good use.
Welcome to the Gonfalon Gaming Hall! We got drinks, food, and lots of good times. Especially if you order a lot of drinks.\n\nFunny how that works.

Forgive this one's baby brother. He was weeping about … wait, what was he—? Never mind.\n\nWelcome to the club! This one assumes you seek new challenges and amazing rewards. This is true, yes? If so, you have come to the right place!
So, do I celebrate with a High Rock Dark Ale or one of Gelekh's delicious mushroom stews?\n\nWait, we won our last round of matches. I'm doing both!

Teliv Fels. Hmm.\n\nI will not lie to you, Teliv and his apprentices are some of the greatest Tribute players currently competing. They will put your every strategy to the test. Stay focused. And wary.
Whatever Lady Arabelle needs, I am here to help.
Being a squire takes a lot more hard work than you'd think, watching knights parade about on their horses. \n\nIt's taken me a long time to get here! Hah!
Now, are you ready for your match? Dralcia's been perched on her chair like a cliff racer, hungry for a meal. Why not give her something to really sneer about?
The Mournhold Chapter. Z'en's price, I was worried this would happen. I don't mean to rattle you, but these bug-lovers almost never lose.\n\nBut this time is different. This time, I'm going to win!
Seems like the seas around High Isle are more troubled than usual. Be careful not to get caught in the current, mainlander.
I'd ask if you want some fresh-caught fish, but I didn't have much luck today. None to spare, I'm afraid.

Murmurings amongst the Host speak of a mortal hunter carving through one of their deepest dungeons. One of their champions destroyed, just ash in the wind.\n\nImmediately, I knew it was you. You have impressed me.

After many years in the Mages Guild, I worried the thrill of fighting was behind me. But, oh, friend, it certainly was not! I feel twenty years old again.\n\nI hear my blood pumping like the roar of waves. It feels fantastic.

We need to enter the Sunken Road and find that ritual site before Archdruid Michiel frees the nature spirit. And we have to save Wyress Sorcha. Roots and thorns, why are the Firesong so intent on all this violence and mayhem?\n\nCome on, let's go!
Well done. I didn't think the old bird was going to budge. Now we've got a destination and a goal. \n\nLet's follow that Sunken Road and breathe some hot air down the Firesong's necks!

Raz is impressed. You stopped an insurrection, a hostile takeover, and a volcano? Raz was busy at the time, but you could have asked for help. And now you managed to get Queen Ayrenn to talk to the other royals?\n\nRaz is so jealous, five-claw!

Such an effective distraction! Raz could not have done it better himself. What do you say we continue this collaboration? \n\nThis one promised you gold, and he would like to make good on his promise.

Smell that? Like a mix of old eggs and dead skeevers? That's the telltale odor of molten lava. Didn't expect to run into druids, though.\n\nThe first crystal I saw was to the southeast. We can discuss what to do once we find it.
I can't leave anyone in the hands of these cutthroats. And I'd like a chance to cause a little trouble for Sealord Nalos before I leave. I owe him that much.
I told Stefan it was a bad idea to entangle our house in the bickering of these druids. And now he went and made himself a hostage!\n\nTell me again. What were Archdruid Orlaith's exact words.
Count Mornard's not happy about any of this. Not happy at all. And when he's not happy, he can get reckless. Talk to him before he does something that gets Sir Stefan killed.
Thank you, friend. If you have any other tasks, take care of them swiftly and report back to Sir Stefan in Vastyr.\n\nIf the Firesong and the Dreadsails are working together, he needs to know.
Can you believe this? I came to check on my knights when I found them … indisposed. House Mornard's finest, pah!\n\nNow, who are you?
This time we're going to put an end to the Ascendant Order—and that traitor, Lord Bacaro!\n\nAscendant Lord is just another name for dinner, yes?

Oh, five-claw, Lady Arabelle looks better already! But what are we going to do about Lord Bacaro? Za'ji still cannot believe he is actually the Ascendant Lord!\n\nTalk to Lady Arabelle. She always knows what to do.

How did you manage to calm the spirit of the mountain, my friend? And how did you contain the volcano's eruption? The damage should have been much greater.\n\nGo on, talk to Lady Arabelle. I can't wait to hear what happened over there.
This place feels sacred, ancient. Did Lord Bacaro know it was down here? And why keep it a secret? Instead of answers, suddenly we have more questions.
You are quite the gambler. And since Raz took a chance on you, he is clearly a good gambler, too!\n\nNow, into the high-stakes suite and let us confront Grandvache.

Who's this? Another valiant defender of Elsweyr? Good, it is strong warriors like ourselves who stem the tide of Dragons that washes over these lands.\n\nBut this one cannot send people to die without proper training.
You heard Laurel. There isn't a moment to lose. We must reach Druid King Kasorayn's tomb and stop Archdruid Orlaith!
We're not out of this squall yet. Get over to the enemy deck and deal with that last Firesong warship!
The herbs in this chamber were preserved for this moment. Gather them, friend of Laurel. We must make the elixir to see why the song drew us here.

I see you've agreed to the trials, how exciting! \n\nYou will not regret your efforts, I promise you. Captain Samara has put her heart and soul into the Elsweyr Defense Force. Each trial was thought through with care.
My knights are ready, but Captain Siravaen isn't convinced she wants to join us in this particular fight.\n\nBut never mind that. Is Druid Laurel all right? Is the sacred staff safe?

I think I'm finally mastering this floating thing. I can mostly go where I want now. Except when the wind blows. Still need to get the hang of dealing with a strong breeze.\n\nOh, hi! What were we talking about?

I hope Druid Fenas knows what he's doing. Just be careful of that fire shard. I've seen what a single spark can do to a forest, and I have no desire to become a bonfire!\n\nDamn it all, I don't want to be a tree!
I'm worried about Frii and what Lord Bacaro may be doing to them. The sooner we can get to Y'ffelon, the better as far as I'm concerned.
That Khajiit was with Lady Arabelle when she arrived at Glimmertarn, and he went with her when she chased after Lord Bacaro. Let's find out what he knows.
The Dreadsails think to breach Vastyr's walls? Never! But they might have the numbers to overwhelm us, especially with the Firesong at their side. We need more defenders to stand with us.
I appreciate the concern, dear, but now isn't the time. Lord Bacaro took Frii farther into the ruins. You must find them.
Even if Umindior got himself into this bind, he's still in pain. Let's set him free then grab the relic.
My Gwenaelle. My guiding light. We were so close to reaching her. Then she slipped through my fingers. The spirit turned her into a forest wraith.
You and Sir Stefan are too late. I was … weak. I told the Dreadsails about my circle's most-guarded secret. Leave me behind and stop them. Before they escape with the Eldertide relic.

You're a strange one, mercenary. You help a Sea Elf enact revenge with one hand and smite an evil Druid King with the other. Not to mention saving the islands from the volcano!\n\nI'm not sure what they feed you here on dry land, but I want some.

Ah, druid-kin. I heard what you did. How you secured the Eldertide seed and returned it to the care of Archdruid Ellic. Once again, you prove to be a true friend of the druids.\n\nBut what is this I hear of an impending attack on the city?
Let's get inside and find Frii.
Chat later, dear. Right now, we need to find Lord Bacaro.

The ritual chamber lies to the south. Take the passage that leads up.\n\nBe on your guard, old friend. The followers of the Allwither are already inside the temple. We must return the regalia to Y'ffre before they stop us.
I didn't know these markings were here. They're extremely old. But that's Frii, or a spirit very much like them.\n\nLet's keep an eye out for more drawings while we try to find Frii.
They gnash with sharpened teeth. Claw at the doors. But now … Druid Laurel, lavender and woodsmoke. Familiar. And you … battle and the touch of leaves.\n\nI kept seed safe. But protections wither.
Don't keep me in suspense! Where's our next heading?
You'd think the knight commander would have a nicer office. Well, if I must work here while my own wing of the castle undergoes repairs, I may just have to do some redecorating ….
I'm proud to be a part of the important work being done here and on the mainland by the Society of the Steadfast. I don't consider this a job. More like a calling.
This is where Octin found and broke the tablet. We'll perform the ritual here.\n\nLet me see … fire shard, sap, and tablet pieces … everything's in order. Oh yes, I almost forgot about the warning.
Don't mind me and Mohair. We can take care of ourselves.\n\nIt's all the other Fauns I'm worried about.
Now here's an intrepid explorer if I've ever seen one! How would you like to help Savage Systres Tours get on its feet? I've got a satchel of coin ready to reward anyone brave enough to step up!
I think I may finally be getting the hang of this stewardship of Galen thing.

So much death and destruction because a man spoke a few words in the ancient past. I think I may have learned as much as I care to about the Druid King. Now I need to look to the future. We all do.\n\nAnd we can, thanks to you.
I knew you and Stefan would find me. Open this cage, there's no time to waste!
As soon as you head below decks, we'll set sail for the city. I don't want you up here and getting in the way of my crew.
Ah, good. I've heard of you. Another Psijic will help immensely. But we haven't met before. Despite that, those Dark Elves recognized us. Called us a scourge.\n\nWe need to get inside.
I heard how you handled Sealord Nalos—good work there. But damned if I know what to do about the Firesong.\n\nTalk to Sir Stefan, mate. He's going to need your help.
Come on, mate! Sir Stefan needs the two of us up at Castle Mornard.

Druid Galphen is … interesting. We've exchanged pleasantries in the Vine District, of course, but this is the first time we've really had a chance to spend time together.\n\nI find his insights into our current situation … quite fascinating.

The spirit of Mount Firesong has quieted and the volcano has been destroyed. I assume we have you to thank for that?\n\nNow that peace is restored, I've asked Fayda to come away with me. I hope she agrees. I think the life of a druid will suit her.

Dralys's presence here … the One Who Knows never suggested they had any of their faithful dealing with this threat. Hmm.\n\nNo matter. With Bassian's help, I was able to decipher the letter Dralys gave you.

This one will stay here and help Mazandi transition into her role. Exploring the planes may be beyond his capabilities. But, staying in Scrivener's Hall? Reading all our records and offering advice? Keshargo can't think of anything more perfect.

Keep an eye on that elder. If he's really involved, he may not know the danger he's put himself in.\n\nBelieve me, even if only one of the Khajiit is conspiring with the Lark, the high priest will make sure the entire caravan suffers for it.
Perhaps with some strong tea and many sweetrolls, this one will find the strength to talk more. For now, walker, this one is very weary.
Since Rilasi isn't keeping me apprised of your movements, I'd appreciate it if you could.\n\nTell me if you have any other questions I might answer.
The smell really just hits you right in the face, doesn't it? Not all together displeasing, but certainly potent. Let's get a move on, shall we?
Apostle Nilphas Drethan reached the Clockwork Probabilis.\n\nWe must stop him before he fully controls its power.

I studied the threads of fate and this location is resolved, proxy. You stopped the agent of Peryite from destroying the Necropolis and recovered part of a relic we will need to complete our quest. That the enemy also has a part could not be helped.

You'll need my whistle and compass to retrieve the creatures. The compass shows their location and I can speak to you through it. Blow the whistle near the creatures to send them back to me.\n\nFind these tools among my possessions on the hill nearby.
Now that we can enter the chapel, let's go find Abbot Ilvel.
Finally, place the book on the center pedestal. That should open the portal.
My father will not budge, but neither will I. You will have to choose.

It looks like a handful of pages got up and ran away from that tiresome tome. Can you blame them? Probably looking to get thrown into something a bit more exciting!\n\nHopefully they didn't get too far. Have a look around and see if you can find any!
Everything that happened at Necrom Abbey was only part of someone's master plan? I don't like the sound of that.\n\nWhat's Leramil going to do about it?
I believe the Calamitous Gallery is our first stop. A ghastly collection of troubling predictions, so please do try to avoid peeking. Best not to worry yourself.

The Divinatory Forums are a closely kept secret. All magical portents from the Cloisters' orreries first travel through the Divinatory Forums. This is where pure, unrefined predictions are scryed and sorted. This intruder should not have access.

After witnessing that vessel speak, I fear I now understand the source of our problem.\n\nIt seems a rogue mind is traveling through, and tampering with, the Chorus. A crisis Huzmargo did not think possible until now.

A very useful lens indeed. This missing magister clearly was concerned about blundering into his own traps.\n\nTry the illuminated object, proxy. It should be safe. At least, I sense no overt danger from it.

I trust your trip through the Endless Library was not too unsettling. The winding paths of Apocrypha can prove troubling to those unfamiliar with its preternature.\n\nCipher's Midden contains a wellspring of knowledge. Shall we begin our research?

I don't want to talk about what we just heard from Mevei. After so long knowing nothing about who I used to be, it's a lot to take in. \n\nStopping those mercenaries is more important anyway. I'm heading to Gorne.
I did not expect us to be deposited directly into one of the Halls of Secrets, but I sense ….\n\nProceed with caution, proxy.
Wait, who is that strange mortal? He can't just step into the Prince of Knowledge's domain like that! It's absurd!\n\nYou—you go talk to him, yes? I hope he can tell how deeply annoyed I am.

Good! You're always one for action, aren't you?\n\nThe nemesis looms are powerful devices that unweave bits of reality. For example, these failed fates. You'll find them contained in the nullifactory, just ahead past the cells. I'll meet you there.
The pool opens a portal to the place we need to go. We will find whatever the invaders seek through that gateway.
Is it over? Is Keshargo all right? That spider ….\n\nPlease go talk to Keshargo. I need a minute to gather my thoughts.
There's books and papers scattered everywhere. Let's check everything. Maybe there's something that can explain or help with what's happened here.
I don't know what to say.\n\nDacia is my world. I wouldn't want her to curse herself forever just to be with me. But I … I don't think I'll meet anyone like her ever again.
Dacia has chosen to make her home at Tel Dreloth. She brings Nathyn a comfort I could never hope to give him.\n\nI will make sure to show her how thankful I am for that.

You arrived not a moment too soon, my friend. Before they decided to seal the hall and I was trapped in that dreadful conversation with Mouth Elar, I found what we needed. Master Shelreni is here and being held under guard until the conclave begins.
What are you waiting for? Lending you my ghost sight isn't easy. Look around for my sigil.

Be careful out there, you two. I feel better knowing that you have each other to rely on.\n\nAnd keep in touch, will you? I want to see the Reformer's downfall as much as either of you. Call on me, if you should need my help.

Activating the magical foci above us will be like unleashing a raging river. It will require all of my vast skill to anchor the flow into a stable portal. Do be quick, though. I detest the stench of this place.
I smell like a kagouti, this place smells like a kagouti, and you definitely smell like a kagouti. Let me see that letter you found.
You have your task, mortal, and I have mine. One of us is doing their part and the other isn't.\n\nGo, follow my spell so we can find Madam Whim's secret.
This should work. And if it doesn't … I guess we'll have to turn over every corner of this crypt.
Talk to Mevei—she's the one with the plan. We can catch up afterward.
Ah, you're assisting the Morag Tong agent, correct? As busy as I am, I can always spare a moment for the hired help.
Vanton's mind is yet unbroken. And this one felt Ansuul's presence retreat. You've done more than you know.
Hidden Kindred fill this cavern, but still no sign of Master Shelreni. Let's see if anything in this chamber might suggest where she got off to.
There it is. Let's get in there.
Chat later, dear. Right now, we need to find Lord Bacaro.

I'm curious what we might find at Fathoms Drift. I'll meet you there, in the far northern part of the region.\n\nAt this point we're well beyond the bounds of my original experiment. The next step is rigorous field research. Hah!

Frielvi's glass is nearly empty. Grains of sand spilling out on the floor. Running out of time.\n\nMy sand's inside, but my eyes leak. No cage, no friends, no one to make plans for me. I'm not good at being alone anymore.
These items represent my past. Place them in the sacred flame to finalize my pact and seal my fate. Should Herm'us Mora rescind his offer, Landolvel will perish!

That was much more intense than the ancestor visits I've participated in at the catacombs.\n\nAnyway, let's go find Leramil and tell her what the spirit said. She'll be able to make sense of it, I know she will.

We freed the Great Eye from Vaermina's dream, but we weren't able to preserve the first part of the secret. Not only that, but I still feel the effects of Blightcrown's poison. And Hermaeus Mora suffers even more. I could see it in his eyes.
Oh, wonderful. Vaermina corrupted this memory. Doesn't she realize it's sacrilege to tamper with the remembrances of the Great Eye?\n\nLet's look around, but be careful.
Now to find the western manufactory. It looks like the path has been shattered. Let me see what I can do.
Give Llaro the tincture and all will be well! Just a quick jaunt. He's nearby! Honestly, I envy you! A brisk daily walk is excellent for the humours!
If you've nothing worth saying, go bother someone else.
Another portal, ah well. I guess if it gets us to the foul device we must destroy, so be it. Lead on, my friend.

It seems our little Watchling and Leramil have finally succumbed to Blightcrown's corruption. The next stage, as we have seen, involves a massive amount of violence.\n\nLet's try to help them before it comes to that, yes?
I'm in agony, mortal. It's like curtains are drawn across my many eye sockets. Did I hear Torvesard? Why can I barely sense him? And do you smell sweetrolls baking in the distance?
We meet again, traveler. Have you found another one of our missing ciphers? Or a volume of the Numinous Grimoire, perhaps?
Look, I'm unhappy and always disappointed by nature. But I have to admit, you do sort of bring a smile to my depressed ocular sockets. Every so often.

Did I hear Leramil correctly? We can soon return to Necrom? That would be splendid! I can't wait to put the Fulcrum Obscura back in its proper resting place in the Necropolis.\n\nStill, if we're almost finished … I might not see Leramil again.

I wish I could go with you on this, but Scruut is correct. This is a task for fate's chosen, and fate's chosen alone.\n\nGo, but know that I have faith in you. You can recover the glyphic and preserve reality. It is what destiny demands.

Your heroics may have impressed some here, perhaps even deservedly so. That doesn't give you permission to interrupt Telvanni masters who are deep in conversation.\n\nExcuse me while I try to talk sense into Sulis's thick head.

Did you see the curse scatter the tome's pages? Any number of those secrets could raise our family from obscurity. Father would want us to do everything we could to gather them.\n\nPlease, speak with Mouth Gilvas, he'll know what to do.

It was foolish to tamper with the tome without the right precautions, but Father and Yensa wouldn't hear of it. Fruit from the same zealous and over-eager branch. \n\nSorry, traveler. You're owed coin. I haven't forgotten.

As soon as I locate a place of suitable power, we'll be able to use this nymic to summon Tho'at Replicanum.\n\nI know this has been a journey, but we're so close to being able to get rid of this version of her.
Oh my. Quite the spectacle, wasn't it? Apologies, a Mouth shouldn't speak ill of his Master. Do speak with Tralise while I relish Faras's silence.
If you still need help finding Master Malkhest, I can give you a fun hint. He's right behind me, up those stairs.\n\nWell, I suppose that's not a hint. Can't take it back now.
I know they're here somewhere. This is such a mess. Do I organize the shelves first? Find the pages? Clear the floor? \n\nBreathe. Have to remember to breathe.
Torvesard found the Glyphic of Shattered Reflections? I am beginning to believe he is fated to succeed. But still, we must stop him if we can.\n\nAfter him, proxy!
Leave me, proxy. Talk to Scruut.

Obviously, we're going to need something connected to Ithelia!\n\nI spotted a Primordial Shattered Titan in the ruins of Ceyond while I was scouting instabilities. Retrieve a fragment of that ancient Daedra. We can use it to create the relic.
It's hard to miss Silorn. The whole place has a stench about it, doesn't it? Musky, but almost sweet? I abhor how hungry it makes me.

I think we found the source of those bugs in the garden. Somewhere down here is that portal Legionary Caepio spotted. For the security of Skingrad and West Weald, we need to close it.\n\nKeep pressing forward. Don't let any obstacles deter us.

Under better circumstances, I'd sit you down and talk until we drank an alehouse dry. \n\nUnfortunately, the Recollection has put a stop to our plans. If you help me out here, I can pay you enough to buy your own drinks.
Another corner of Oblivion I never expected to visit. And it makes me just as uncomfortable as the other places we've traveled.\n\nI suggest we make haste, my friend.
I was hoping to get a better look at these ruins, but Tribune Alea is correct. Someone needs to watch our flank. Good luck in there!
Lord Valente's alchemical laboratory must be through the caverns ahead. Let's keep looking.

A shrine to the Twilight Queen, just as we thought. It appears the Recollection forces searching the Reliquary are using this room as a temporary headquarters.\n\nLook around, friend. See what you can find.
The murderer has been apprehended and will face justice. You should speak to Aquilia about the family fortune.

Betu seems to have run off again. It's embarrassing really. You'd think I'd be better at keeping a handle on him, but the dog is a free spirit. How are things? Made any progress since investigating the library?
We must speak to <<1>>. He discovered <<2>>'s body.
Once again the Daedric Princes seek the counsel of a mortal. But what else can we do besides reseal her prison?\n\nTalk to her, proxy, and see what inspiration strikes you.

It is a vexing conundrum. I am not without a certain amount of sympathy for Torvesard and his cause. Yet I have learned that Hermaeus Mora does not lie. If he says Torvesard must be stopped, then we must stop him.
Another one of my husband's guests? No, you're either an attendant or a servant, I'd wager. Who brought you to my husband's little affair, pray tell?
Torvesard must be getting close to the glyphic he's looking for. We'd better hurry, friend.

Reproducing a Sage's Dream sounds like a fun challenge. It'll certainly take my mind off of what's happening to my inn.\n\nYou'll find stairs to the cellar in the room behind you. It opens up into an old ruin, but don't mind that.

All this waiting and for what? A riddle? It's absurd. The sooner you and Mizzik solve this riddle the sooner our family can move on from this nonsense. To think we haven't even had a chance to celebrate Uriel's return.
I hope to put this nonsense to rest. I only wish to start making up for my long absence. I do hope the investigation is wrapped up with haste.
I'm sorry. I've just, I've never seen …. I'll gather my wits, I just need a moment.

This is Elenglynn, an Ayleid ruin. I expected to find the Recollection here, as they have been searching similar ruins throughout the area. They did not disappoint.\n\nI sense an aura of Daedric power, as well. Perhaps that aura drew them here.
You're here to help, right? Those bandits came out of nowhere. We barely escaped. But you should talk to the captain.
Well, those bloodfiends won't be joining the Terror's army any time soon. Let's see if we can find another den.

You. You emerged victorious from my arena challenges!\n\nThe Blind and her army of cultists are here. I was just thinking about how to best deal with them, but I believe you're the answer I was looking for.
The Ayleids loved magical portals even more than clever traps. I bet the remaining three stones are hidden in places we need portals to reach. A good thing you've got Abolisher for that.
Another nexus point tear healed, but you aren't done yet. Go place the remaining relics. I'll meet you at Beragon's mortal domicile when you're done.
That was the last relic and the last reality tear. Let's head back to my townhouse and check with Leramil and Scruut. They can tell us if we preserved reality or not, right?
I see Legionary Caepio delivered the message. Good!\n\nBeragon thinks he's found a way to locate Nantharion. I won't try to explain. Beragon can do it better. Talk to him, comrade.
More wildburn seeds, just as I feared! And an Echonir memory, as well. It looks like Nantharion has been busy here. Better burn those seeds and see what the Echonir reveals.
Wait and watch, comrade. We might learn something if we practice a little patience here.
That was strange. Vargas appeared and threw you into that memory with a wave of her hand! I'm glad you found your way out, comrade.\n\nI chased Vargas but she escaped me again. Let's keep going.

With Nantharion's death at Miscarcand, any remaining Recollection forces should be in disarray. But the Mirrormoor Daedra are another matter entirely.\n\nWe need to deal with Shardmarshal Vargas to stop the incursions I suspect.

I feel better having warned King Nantharion about the dangers posed by the Recollection. Now let's go find that cart!\n\nOh, and I know you want to ask about Ninglenirre Pass. Can we save that for later? It's somewhat embarrassing.

I hope you're prepared for what lies ahead, traveler. The undead are not to be trifled with. Give me a moment to cremate this corpse. She may have been a necromancer, but everyone deserves a proper sendoff.

I have been scouring the planes for hints of Torvesard's doings. I sensed ripples of probability flowing across the Daedric realms.  Imagine my surprise when I traced them to their origin—ancient Miscarcand.\n\nWhat happened there?
Stay alert. We have no idea what we're going to encounter in here.

Sorilen was always good at sneaking around. She would have made an excellent scout if she hadn't become a greenspeaker. Still, how she avoided all these Recollection fanatics is beyond me.\n\nWell, let's talk to her and see what she wanted to show me.
I don't see any sign of Vargas or Ithelia here, but that manifestation looks like a point where you could use Abolisher. Try it and see what happens.
It seems Beragon and Tribune Alea are safe. They just emerged from the portal in a different place than we did. Let us continue our search.
That looks like a place you can use Abolisher and make us a path out of this accursed maze. Go ahead and open it!
Thanks to my dazzling intellect, I have deduced that we should anoint the altar with sacred water. Assistant! Apply the sacred water.
Pardon, but I'm a bit busy transcribing notes for my employer, Narsis Dren. He has much to say about the old Ayleid ruins of Wendir.
I wish I better understood the risks of using the Lamp of Clarity here, but we have no choice. We cannot leave the tribune trapped in her current predicament.

I know losing the use of the relics is bad, but at least we destroyed the Loom and stopped Ithelia from changing our reality. You know, I can't even conceive of what that actually means.\n\nBut now that we're back in West Weald, on to local matters.

Greetings, proxy. I see that you too have been drawn to this place. Do you sense the tangled threads of fate converging upon the Outcast Inn? Already the bonds of cause and effect fray here. Should these bonds snap, the result would be catastrophic.

With each remembrance, the storm calms a bit more and my power returns to me. You see how I opened a doorway into the Many Paths? I am gaining more control with each passing moment. All I need is Sage's Dream to complete the process.
My master, Fa-Nuit-Hen, expressed a desire to speak with you. It's not wise to keep them waiting.
Deputy. Were you able to interview the townsfolk I suggested?
I have no idea where we are or when she'll be back. Maybe we can use the blade she called Abolisher to get back? Grab it and see if you can make it work like Vargas did.
The One Who Knows remains silent. I believe we are now passing through another conjunction of threads of fate in which he dares not interfere.

We thought the barricades would hold longer. Those blasted Daedra broke through when our backs were turned and damaged our last ballista. My legionaries set up another barricade, but it may not last for long.\n\nThat's where you come in, mercenary.
The site where Vashabar's growth began isn't far. Just refer to your map and I'll meet you there. \n\nAnd don't worry, traveler. You'll have a damned greenspeaker-to-be at your side!
There are mosaics aplenty in the old ruins marked on your map. I'll meet you near the entrance. And … thank you again, traveler. I still can't believe we have this chance.
Gundelion and Malaniel should both be near the center of the village.\n\nDon't be surprised if they find the news about as welcome as a timber pig in the roots cellar.
Hmm. Yes, hello. I'm sorry, I'm a bit busy at the moment. Vashabar is newly grown and we still have much to do. \n\nI hope you understand.
Traveler. Are you looking to practice the blade? In the mood for a sparring match?
A new face in Vashabar! Beautiful, like the pelt of a senche-tiger cub. Fresh from the den and curious about the world.
Look at us. Rushing to save the day. Or, at least in the process of it. I can't wait to see Hyacinth's face when we storm in!\n\nNow let's find that red banner and go cause some trouble.
Viti is fine, thank goodness. And were you and Zerith-var not here to drive off our fallen sister, I am sure we would have been next.

The blessing on the black pearl restored some of my moonclaw's power, but with it comes a warning. Another incursion of Rajaska awaits us. Let us find them quickly, before more Khajiit are bent to her dark song.
Wisteria is the traitor. I suppose I should have seen it sooner. Talented. Self-determined. A natural leader. Blast.\n\nWhat is the Garland Ring now? Just childish dreams and dead friends.
I stand ready to assist you, comrade. We must place the Lamp near a reality tear before you cast the spell. There should be one inside this cavern.
A new friend of Tanlorin's? They do have a propensity for picking up strays.\n\nSorry, that's rude of me. Blame it on the blood loss and broken ribs. Thank you for coming to my rescue.
Do you think any of these Luminaries want to meet me? I'll have to pop my head in those doors and introduce myself soon.
I thought smashing the crystal on the altar would fix things. \n\nIn my line of work, hitting things with a sword usually does the trick!

I've been watching these Goblins for a while. They're worried. And worried Goblins can be unpredictable. \n\nI haven't seen their shaman either. Let's look around. Hopefully my theory is wrong and everything is fine here.
This is a fine way to wake after centuries of restless slumber! Did she send you? \n\nYou're not at all what I was promised. It wasn't enough to break in, you had to smash the altar too?

Ah, what a flight! I almost didn't want to land. But, to business. \n\nThe Luminaries are beings of great power. Each has a domain they have shaped to their choosing. Each domain has a door and each door, of course, has a key.

I may act the fool on occasion, but I can listen to reason. I reached out to the members of the Ring in part to ensure they would respond. Now look where we are.\n\nI dearly wish that Snapdragon had been wrong.

Other Luminaries see themselves as shields, or thieves. I am a blade. No more, no less. To wield power you must have this clarity of purpose.\n\nBut as you seek that clarity, you will have questions. Mortals always do.
Ho there, friend! I know the path of Scribing beckons. You're no doubt hoping to contact the Gryphon Luminary.\n\nUnfortunately, it seems we have a page thief in the Scholarium.
Who would have thought we'd lose a crucial tome like this to pests, of all things?\n\nThe Daedric Prince of Madness works hard, but apparently vermin work harder.
Whatever the riddle is, I want to help. You just tell me where we need to be, and I'm there.
If we have any hope of saving Val, we have to act now. Let's go!
No time to talk! I've got to get this door open!
To think Marcan Caelum was holed up down here for years, plotting to pick us off one by one. And I let him snatch Valenia like a bottle off the shelf. \n\nWe have to save her!

These guzzards remind me of home and how important it is to have a flock. I lost my pet wormmouth on the journey here. I can't imagine he's still alive, but I'd give anything to have him back.\n\nPlease let me know if you see any sign of him.

I had hoped to move on from all this. To never look back. But it's been a long time since I've seen Hooke this driven. It reminds me of the good things I found among this group.\n\nNot everything about those days was evil.

In all his travels, Keshargo has learned that Oblivion is filled with things no mind can anticipate. \n\nThe ghost lights are headed up with some determination. There's a chance that they are the key to leaving the sunken ruins.
I just … need to catch my breath.
This world has changed much since last I walked it. Let us hope I can find my place in all this.
Which riddles will you solve? Which ones will you seek help to solve?\n\nChoices made are so instructive, so … revealing. Don't you agree?
I had no idea Elic's father was even sick. We're old friends, so I'm eager to help however we can.\n\nDid the Netch explain how I'm going to help you? Back to where we began, with portals?

How are you here, Not-Ulfsild? Surely this wasn't Nahlia's doing. You're meant to be helping the fragments of a lost soul make their way back to Suran.\n\nOh! Is this a trick of your own? Cleverly done! Now go on, and let Nahlia be your guide.
That Fox came around, and he's maybe the sweetest person I've met in years. Who would have thought a Daedric creature could be like that?
We must find the count's lost bear cub. He's somewhere in the devastated area.
Please, friend. I need a moment to speak to Viti alone.
Please, let Krin'ze and Viti speak in private, walker.

That was mortifying, I'm sorry you had to see that. I never did learn to hold my drinks.\n\nAfter all that, I would understand if you want to leave. But I could still use your help, if you're willing.

I know this place doesn't look all that bookish, but Hermaeus Mora is actually digging around here somewhere below us!\n\nNever mind that. What's important is we're here because Apocrypha is close. So close I can smell the ink!
These safeguards, these tasks, are a chance to right what has gone wrong. To stand against injustice. \n\nThank you mortal. I can't wait to return to the skies, to my own patrol.
Ulfsild wanted a legacy, and now I'm to be the Scholarium's librarian? What would she say to that? \n\nShe had to give up everything that mattered to her. Would she want me to do this?
You perch atop a mountain of accomplishments, an interloper no longer.\n\nYou've unlocked the wings of the Netch, the Dragon, the Gryphon, and the Indrik. Now only a final door remains.
Please hurry, walker! The Bent Dance beats quickly, but the songs of the Rajaska work much faster!
Let me re-read that quick. Right, spreads from brazier to brazier. Lighting one can ignite or extinguish others in the circle. \n\nI guess that could mean a lot of trial and error.
That takes care of the warden. There's got to be a key to the cells around here somewhere. Let's look around.
Let's just get out of here.
Don't hold back. Not for me. We have to stop Wisteria.
The spirit of Moon-Singer Talbira, did it enter Cantor Krin'ze?\n\nSpeak to her, tamiit. Talbira is still here, I can sense her … somewhere.
Even in a plane this dark there is beauty. But let not your eyes wander, tamiit. Be on your guard!

We are fortunate to have won the trust of two Twilight Cantors. To have them singing for us now, when they are at such risk.\n\nBut we must keep them safe. Let us enter this shrine to Namiira and call for them only when their songs are needed.
Stay back from me, najeek! My soul is not forfeit to you or your necromancer!
Daedric worship and dark magic rituals, I can understand. But the air here doesn't stink of Oblivion or anything more sinister than blood. It's unsettling in ways I did not anticipate.
What happened here … it chills me to my very soul!
Let's destroy these tusking soul reapers, find that damn snake, and send her back to Oblivion!
That Fighters Guild warrior was a storm of fury! Left me alive so I could tell some prince what happened here. But neither of you looks much like a prince to me.

The portal's open. Go help the Fighters Guild. Just watch out for Skordo. He still seems rattled by Mezamma's spell.\n\nAzah and I will do our best to rally the alliances. With any luck, we can make them see that working together is our best option.
Now that I witnessed a soul reaper firsthand, the scope of the danger becomes quite clear.\n\nThis goes beyond the threat to the Fighters and Mages Guilds. But what is the Worm Cult's ultimate goal?

In my life before, I lost the way from my order. What you learn here, I endeavor to learn as well. To see how the Hidden Moon fell from its twilight path.\n\nLead on, tamiit. This place has need of us. I am with you.

My heart screams for vengeance, but Vanus's words ring true. I've been trained to take the throne of Hammerfell when King Fahara'jad, hopefully many years from now, steps down. I am most qualified to serve as interim leader of the guild.
What a fool I've been! Beautiful, talented Khalisah. How could I not see how she felt about me?
I'm still not sure I can trust you, but it's not like I have a lot of choices at the moment. \n\nCome back with those healing supplies and maybe I'll change my mind.
I just … I just need a moment. I'll meet you outside.
I'm still deciding what to do with my apprentice. \n\nNo, I'm not going to eat him. The guild would disapprove, though Vivec knows he deserves it!
Closer. You come closer.\n\nIf you don't come closer, maybe I'll eat juicy woman instead. Taste the liquid copper inside her skin.
Is it done?
I don't look forward to informing the King about this, but we must let him know as soon as possible.\n\nHe will not be pleased.
One way or another, I'll escape this tired place and get to Rivenspire soon. \n\nWhatever you can do to help get matters under control before my arrival … it will be most appreciated.

I am Lorelia, water spirit of Halcyon Lake and caretaker of these lands. I have been watching you from afar, and I like what I see.\n\nYou are brave, you are not afraid to stand up for what's right, and you have chosen to help me.
We shouldn't get our hopes up too much, but with the pure heartwood, there is at least a chance our little friend can be healed.\n\nHave you been able to find any?
There was a time when the people of Evermore admired me. I hope my folly hasn't cost me their faith.\n\nEven if it has, though, I will dedicate myself to earning it back.
Every moment that passes gives the Imperials time to regroup. Without their leader, they'll lose their focus and be easy prey for my people.
I'll reassure Gerard.\n\nI'm trading my life for the defeat of a vile Daedra. He'll understand … in time.
Selling the johads is the only way to end our bickering, I think. After this, I feel like we need to be a family again. And my sister's the only one I've got.

For each direction the wind blows, there is a brazier. Light the first three and meet me at the west brazier. I will light that one.\n\nThen we will light the central brazier together, and soon see Uwafa and his Withered Hand destroyed.
This is not good, not good at all. I've killed a skeleton or two in my day, but this … this is worse than that. \n\nWe are going to need more Ash'abah. We are going to need help from somewhere.
Only those who prove themselves beneath Leki's Blade can be taught by its masters.\n\nYou will find the ones who've failed your mission. Be wary, lest you become one of their number.
Here, the best blades of our generation train and hone their skills.\n\nYou've seen many things, but do you think you can count yourself among them?
You're no raw recruit. I can see you've handled challenges before.\n\nWe could use a student with experience, if you have time to study with us.
Mind yourself in our fair city. We have no tolerance for troublemakers. \n\nI will personally see you escorted to the edge of town if I learn of any illicit activities.
You have performed very well in your trials, my friend, but Tu'whacca says the spirits of this place have more to share with you.
Please, talk to him. He's mad if he thinks I'll leave here without him. \n\nThere's something he's not telling me.
I see no point in debate. Take my money, and be on your way.
Shh! Just keep moving. I don't want to be freed just yet.
I'm sorry. We have a crisis unfolding at the castle gates and I simply cannot waste time in idle conversation right now.\n\nI hope you understand.
I just don't get it. How did the slavers recruit so many of our people?\n\nYou just never know who you can really trust.
There has to be something, some trace ….\n\nI'm not leaving until I know what happened.
And there she lies, all eight legs pointed at the sky. \n\nSay, you're not bad.
Such loyalty to Daggerfall will be remembered. And not just by the King.
Your help in this matter is greatly appreciated. Soon, the land shall return to normal and the creatures of the forest will settle down.
Now we know Faolchu's weakness. We must share this knowledge with Camlorn. \n\nI just hope there's still time to save the city.

No matter what Lord Diel has done, his gold will provide us with homes and food. We can become a real mercenary group that actually takes on contracts and makes even more gold.\n\nRemind Gelvin of that.
And to think I almost got away from the family business. Father giving it to my younger brother seemed like the perfect compromise, but look where it's brought us.\n\nHave you found anything?
Don't recoil from me, traveler. I mean you no harm. I'm a spirit of regret, not malice.
What must we do? \n\nWithout the aid of the guardians, we can't regain control of our Wyrd Tree.
Camlorn is ours again, but Angof still threatens us. \n\nHe's said to be up near Cath Bedraud. As soon as the city is secure, I'm taking my knights north.
My husband thinks this is some kind of grand adventure. He's so … exuberant.
Will you help me recharge the Midnight Talisman?

Dame Clarique didn't expect you to go charging in here. She cut me free and told me to follow you. I heard you talking to my father. I hope you're not going to pursue his foolish plan.\n\nIt's too dangerous!
If we're going to hold the inn, we'll need more warm bodies to wear this armor.\n\nTalk to Alinon. He's working on a way to cure those afflicted with Faolchu's lycanthropy.
What? Who? Damn it all! The last person who snuck up on me got a sword in the gut for their trouble!

As if the problems in Camlorn weren't enough, we have cultists and bandits harrying our flanks!\n\nI've been assigned to keep an eye on the situation here and my vigilance paid off. We captured one of those Red Rook bandits.
Did you find Ildani's wares? This one was worried that the guards might sniff our plan out.

It's a priest of Arkay, but something's wrong with him. He's just completely ignoring me.\n\nI'm not sure how I might have offended him, but if the blessing on Prince Adrien comes from Arkay, the priest should be able to help us.

Aha! Perfect! You look like the fit sort. I wonder if you can assist me in an archeological project of considerable importance. \n\nI came here searching for some rather valuable relics, but I've encountered something of a setback.

What do we have here? Looks like someone else who knows how to swing a weapon. Let me guess—you're helping Lady Laurent clean up this mess? \n\nOr is it Stibbons? The bootless coward. He's hoping Lady Laurent will forgive him for starting all this.
I know how it may seem for me to speak ill of the one who pays me my wages, but he is unable to see the desert for the grains of sand.
And now another young one puts the forest under her heel. We will see if she is strong enough to survive on her own. The wyrd will have no part in this Sentinel's charge.
Make sure to watch your step. These woods are not as friendly as they used to be.
Oh, hello! I was just … tidying up. This was our camp before the Elves came. Well, it was Lady Laurent's camp.\n\nI shouldn't say "our" anymore. Oh goodness! What will I do? She fired me!
We've found the spriggan, but now how do we get it to give us what we need?

We manage to meet each other in all the nicest places.\n\nYou know, we could be carousing at an inn somewhere. But no. Here we are instead, up to our necks in danger and adventure. Just like old times.
<<1>>, I need someone proven to deal with the Withered Hand. See me when you've reached the rank of <<2>>.

We've been through quite a bit together, haven't we?\n\nIf you ever pass this way again, feel free to stop by and visit. I can think of a few other rituals that you can help me with, if you're interested.

We saw few campfires, poorly defended walls, and patrol patterns with gaps so large Molag Bal and Vivec could dance a ronde through them without being noticed.\n\nWhat would you conclude from all this?
I know the fate of one man seems unimportant after so much death, but Sir Etienne was a good man. He didn't deserve this.
I can't go any closer. What's up there? Is she going to kill Draven? You've got to save him!
If we must spill his blood to ensure the safety of the village, then that is what we shall do.
I endured their lashes. I endured the burns and the beatings. I will endure the humiliation.\n\nI see the look in your eye, brother. I will endure your disgust and pity as well!
Didn't I send you to find something?

Wisps serve the entity below, drawing the essences of the enslaved Rain Disciples and depositing these essences in troughs. \n\nSlay one of the wisps and take the essence it carries to the troughs. I believe this will expose the entity's intentions.
I'll send word to you if any other hapless spies or agents wander into our camp.

You would do this? Then I accept your offer. Talk to the townsfolk. See if there is any truth to these accusations. Then come back and tell me what you found.\n\nIf any real crimes have been committed, I'll make sure the guilty are punished.
We've been watching and waiting ever since the Seventh Legion took our city. Now's the time to act.\n\nIf you'll forgive my initial rudeness, I need your help.
I heard the horns. I saw the flames. Are you done?
You've done well here, soldier. You're a credit to the Pact. I'm certain you'll be of use to my son.
You've chosen Furon's plan.\n\nJust remember. Flowers do not bloom in poisoned soil.
I'm not saying I understand Reesa, but if she has a plan, and you think it's a good one, try it out.
My brother has other matters to attend to, but I followed his instructions to prepare the ritual. \n\nAccording to him, we start by placing the bones in the fire.

Well met, my fine f'lah! I am Captain Llaari, commander of the forces stationed at Fort Arand.\n\nWe're primarily a training outpost. I had to put the recruits on alert with all these Covenant troops nearby. What do you have there?
Where in Shor's name did you come from?\n\nNever mind. Get me out of these ropes!
Honor to you, stranger. Your appearance is most fortunate. \n\nMy situation here has taken a distressing turn, and you could be of great assistance to me.
Hurry. The Khajiit do not care about what they stole. They could damage the relics. \n\nCan you get them back before that happens? If you do, meet me at the large rocks to the north of the village.
Have you learned how to stop Balreth?
I'll never forget how you helped to defend my hold.
We've got to keep the Pact together. We must preserve the alliance we've spent blood and men to forge.
The storm is broken, and the sky is clear. But another cloud looms on the horizon.\n\nYou must find Tanval. You must stop what he plans.
Find the Serpentbound. Hurry!

The Argonian quarter is north of Ebonheart. The Nord camp is just beyond the main gates to the south.\n\nThe best place to gauge the Dunmers' feelings is the Tribunal Temple. When you leave, it'll be the building on the right.
You told Boril, didn't you? Very well. I will accept whatever happens next.
Beron's recruited you to help? Good. \n\nHurry, now. We need those components to help the afflicted.
You've chosen what we couldn't for ourselves. Without the fate of the <<z:1>> held over us, we can finally begin to think of our future.\n\nThank you, arbiter. You are always welcome in <<2>>.
Found the killer? No? The bounty pays when you do.
We're not going to survive this, are we?\n\nFine. I don't care about dying. I just want to see that creature dead.
It's over. It's finally over.
<<1>> is the only one who can be of assistance at present. Please speak to her.
We can't thank you enough for what you've done. With the <<z:1>> sealed away forever, we need not fear necromancers. We need not fear death!
Why should I care about his wife's death? Look at him. He's an animal. He's the enemy!\n\nMy Tiril. He took my Tiril.
I know, taking apart a blade is strange at first. By steel and stone, novice: trust me.\n\nYou'll never learn anything without looking to the work of others.
What fresh madness has the General come up with today?
We can't let those monsters attack our people. You must free them. \n\nThat is our decree.
Now we'll get things done. By Vivec, Balreth will be bound again!
We are fortunate to walk the river's edge with you, my friend. I do not know how we would have fared without you here.
Are you well? All around you, I see marks of that spirit's tendrils.\n\nYou have been to the Altmer's camp. What did you find?
The Covenant is inside the city. Stay close.
Welcome to Mournhold.\n\nPatience, please. We're doing our best to sort order from chaos, but there are those who defy categorization.
You have done much for my city and its people. Thank you.\n\nBut one more task requires your attention. You must harry Vox and run her to ground.
Looking for advice about your current contract?
Get in there, friend. We'll be right behind you.

There's a long history of bad blood between the Ashlanders and our order. Hedranna and I can't impose peace on our followers, however we might feel.\n\nIf we could stem the tide of violence, even for a moment ….
I'm on important business for the seneschal. I have no time for other affairs.
Those Dominion dogs will pay for what they've done to these people.
The source of the corruption is gone. Our swamp is whole once more. Thank you again.
You fight the Dominion. You haven't tried to cut off my head yet. You aren't here to worship Daedra, then.\n\nSo what in Oblivion are you doing in a Daedric temple overrun by Dominion skin-stealers?
Curious. You dabble in their spells and break into their outpost.\n\nOh, how he misjudged you! How grand!
Excellent work with <<1>>. Let me know when you're ready for another contract.
Things must have gone well with <<1>>'s guards.\n\nDid things go well with the general, too?
You have nothing to say.
This is my first hatching season as an assistant keeper. Every day I learn how little I know. It is … humbling.
Unnatural spirits haunt this hamlet. Be careful.
All of the prisoners, set free. Do you think to defy me? If you showed mercy, it's only because I allowed you to do so.\n\nNow. What did you learn?
Patience like the calmed pool, comrade. I'll have the portal open in a moment.

Excellent! You're a bit slow, but you got the job done. You showed these scaleskins what a real citizen of the Pact will do for the cause.\n\nWe'll get things back on schedule in a few days. The mine's already back to work!
Place the bedding in the reliquary, and stand back.
If the pirates figure out how to use the puzzle stones, we'll be in trouble.\n\n<<1>> might know where the Renrijra keep the stones. Talk to him.
Back off, pirate! I'm not after your loot.
I know you'll change the river's course, comrade. They're investigating the coastline, down the beach from the Guard lighthouse.
Be ready.
I must concentrate, or the portal will close. Excuse me.
I really owe you.\n\nCome find me when you get a chance. Maybe we can study together or something.
Go carefully along the river, my friend. The forge may be our secret, but enemies are everywhere.
Cast the book into the arcane fire. Fear not. The pages will not burn.
Are you ready for this?
The King's Arrow. Your arrival is a wind that lifts my spirit.
How goes the search?
<cough> The blood flows from my mouth, but I die happy knowing that you recoved the shards. \n\nBut there is one last thing you must do in order to stop the Dreamers.
Disrupt the other rituals. And be careful.
I hope you're not waiting around for some kind of encore performance. We only do that sort of thing on alternating weekends.
I already told you, you flea-bitten … oh, you're not one of my captors. Have you come to help me?
