What did they do to him? What's wrong with my husband?
It's time to get off this island.
I'll lead the refugees out and secure the beach. Wait here until everyone's out. Then join me on the beach.
I want to go with Uncle Sheo! I want to go with Uncle Sheo!
We've done it! We're finally ready to take back my island.
I'm thinking a pint of Sentinel Sundown. Do you think they stock Redguard brews here in town?
Worry not for me. My sight is gone, but I am not defenseless. This place shelters us from the elements, and there is enough food to get by.
Hurry! Speak to Lenning the Hawk and enter the race.
Those silver scales are worth a lot to me. I can't stand Nayya's whining anymore. The poachers at Silverscale Pond should have plenty.

I've been watching over Ouze for so long, it's hard to think of it going on without me. Even under Gwilon's care.\n\nI think I'll wait a little while before going to sleep. Perhaps I can still be of help ….
Gods, I can't stand all this mud. I feel like a filthy Argonian.
I will see the chief dead for this!
We can't thank you enough. My father was evil. He abused the gifts we've been given.\n\nWith him gone, we have a chance to live peacefully … well, as peacefully as our kind can.
No time to talk. My sister and I are working here.\n\nWell, unless you're interested in Dwemer ruins. But not too interested. This is our find.

Raynor and I are certain there's something of value down here, but it's locked up tighter than any of the ruins I've ever crawled through.\n\nWe have to find it. Otherwise, this entire trip has been nothing but a big waste of time.
If Areldur yet breathes, she'll be just up ahead. Hurry!
Doesn't look like we'll be using our old ship. Those brigands foundered her!\n\nI hope you cut a few of those Shrikes down while you were looking for Sal.
One day I'll find a way to repay you for helping me rescue <<1>>.\n\nYou're a true friend. We won't forget this.
Did you find something?
I can't imagine what awaits you in the dreams of King Jorunn.\n\nHis dreams turn to nightmares. What once was pleasant is now twisted and dark. You must help him overcome these trials.
That's it! The Ritual of Unbinding!\n\nBe careful. The Drublog used it when they attacked us. <<1>> weakened when the shaman read from it.
What's Sariel saying about a cook? My head's still ringing.
The Worm Cult infests that place. We will need every warrior when the time comes to strike.\n\nFor now, speak to Holgunn One-Eye. He needs your help.
My friend! I was certain you'd arrive. And it's a good thing you did. All is not well in Silvenar.
We still aren't any closer to finding my husband.
You've never let me down, so don't start now. Save King Jorunn, hero.
Who are you, then? Another spy from the Jarls? Eh? Sent to put a knife in me, I'll wager. Well? Speak, dog!
You think me a peddler. That I'm not a threat. You don't know me, but you will.
Are you mad? Now I wish I'd wasted my life stabbing things or learning magic. If I had, we'd be having a different conversation!
The necromancers pulled <<1>> away! What could they want with her?
She and Aelif await you at the hall in Stormhold. Go well on your path.
With <<1>> dead and the Worm Cult shattered, perhaps peace will return to our lands.
Without you, the Worm Cult would've succeeded.\n\nYou saved Malabal Tor from the bloody curse of Mauloch. And you saved me when you didn't need to. I will never, never forget your kindness.
Valaste is working the problem out of the Shornhelm Guildhall. See you there, Adept.
I hope you've had as much luck as we have. Is the Drublog's leader dead?
Let's see these clothes, then. Rejmina is deft with needle and thread, should they need adjustment.
<<1>> is a clever little lizard. If anyone can find a way past their magics, she can.
I made a bet with Hanthaerin on the way back to camp. Did you find the runes?

<<1>>, the lighthouse keeper, was spared. I don't think they considered him a threat. \n\nHe says the Maormer are using the lighthouse beacon to send messages to their ships. We can't wait for reinforcements. We need to take action, now.
Did you taint the Black Daggers' food?
The final hurdle is ahead of us. Are you ready?
Look, I'll head to our camp when the Houndsmen aren't looking. How about you kill a few? That'll distract them.
You are a true friend to the Baandari.
<<1>> is off limits. You're going to want to get yourself back to the main road.
Hold, there. Firsthold is under siege. We'll need you to head back to the main road.
Stars above. Glad to see a friendly face. You're one of Raz's agents, aren't you?
The barriers fall, and our victory will be in sight.
This will not do. Something here is very wrong.
There's just something not right about this.
Can't believe the lengths some folks will go to for a little treasure.
See if you can find this Rilyn character. Even if he doesn't know anything, it wouldn't hurt for Raerana to have someone to help her through this.
I'll make sure news of the Maormer is passed on to the appropriate parties. Don't you worry about that. Now, what's your name? I'll need it for the official register.
There's a trick to opening the cell. The only way for a prisoner to leave is for another living soul to take their place. I need to swap places with the Prophet.
Thank the Eight and all the Stars in the sky. You've got to help me. \n\nI can't keep them contained much longer.
Ah. This one was just thinking he wanted some company.
Fair day, citizen. I'm sorry, I'm making last minute notes for my speech. I'll be happy to talk as soon as I'm done.
Please, you have to help me. They've got my daughter. My Palith!
Ah, good! I'm famished. Let's see … I'd like a breast of pheasant, some wine, and a wheel of cheese.
I never properly thanked you for coming in when you did. I might still be hiding out there, in the woods.\n\nAnd my mother … well, it's no use thinking thoughts like that.
Looking for Razum-dar? Follow th—me.
Sorry, I'm far too busy and important to speak with you right now.\n\nRun along.
So Gorak exaggerated, then? He was wounded when you found him?
Here we are, back where we began.\n\nIsn't it amazing how often we travel to distant places, only to end up right where we started?
It hurts.
I can't believe they blundered right into this trap. How stupid was that?\n\nAs usual, I guess it's up to us to save the day.
My father can rot here, for all I care! We'll gather what we can and head for the Hollow City shortly.
Quickly, now! We must not let Lyris's sacrifice be in vain!
You … you got all of us out?\n\nI don't know how, nor do I care. You are amazing.
You must pick Mim! Do not select that one over there.\n\nHe is evil. Pure evil! Do not make such a terrible mistake.
I just need a moment before I head out. Everything that's happened has been so sudden.\n\nThat and my head is still pounding from whatever Estre gave me.
The time has come to end the suffering. I pray that the cursed shard crumbles at your touch.
We will drive the Jackdaws from <<1>>. With <<2>> here, I have no doubt.
Yes, I'll have the poultice ready in a moment.\n\nWait, who are you?
What have you found?
The lamia needs to calm down and back off. I can provide more help to the Khajiit than she can.
I left the inn to pick up supplies. Now, look at me. Trapped in a house with a bunch of suicidal soldiers.\n\n<<1>> would know what to do.
I'll return <<Ac:1>> to <<Ac:2>>, don't you worry.
Nice to sit down again. I suppose I'd have rotted away if you hadn't come along.
You smell like someone who's been in an Ayleid ruin. Did you find anything in Vahtacen?
You're a thrilling performer. I'm really quite stimulated. \n\nBut you knew that about me. Didn't you?

My crew and I are collecting Dwemer samples to, uh … sell them. You should explore. \n\nNow that I've seen this place, I'd guess the Dwemer were not kindly creatures. Only a sadistic culture would build the constructs and traps we've encountered.
The crystals are the key. The door itself would easily open if I could only—hello!\n\nI hope you're not planning to rob me. I've nothing of value and you might not like being incinerated.

You work fast. <<1>> found us and told us what happened. All we had to do was follow the trail of corpses and disarmed traps.\n\n<<1>> said you went after the treasure that had <<2>> so worked up. Did you find it?
Did you find him and deliver my orders?
This place is incredible. The ancient Redguards were a noble and accomplished people.
All done? Very good.
Good, you're here. I found this little runt snooping about. I was just about to put him out of his misery.
Ha ha ha. The looks on their faces! Dollie ran so fast, I thought she'd fall on her face. And that old cat, chasing his tail! Oh, thank you. I haven't laughed this hard in years.
I see you have the fork. \n\nCompetently done. Impressive, even.
If Khali were not holding the doorway, she surely would have the barrier down by now.
Well done, well done. Khali is even impressed with you. This one did not think that was possible.
About time you showed up. I was going crazy waiting out here.\n\nThis place isn't exactly on my list of favorite places to hang out, you know.
You're heading the wrong way, aren't you? Everyone's fleeing Velyn Harbor but a few diehards.\n\nWait … you don't look like the running type. Perhaps you can help us defend the city.

You are truly favored by Azura. Wherever you go, and whatever you do, I hope you will not take her blessing for granted.

I should add that, personally, I am honored to have walked at your side in her light. 

May she continue to watch over you.
Hello? Who's there? Tazia? Tell your busybody Clanmatron I'm not here.
Hallowed … we are here. Within the walls of Moonmont.
This place reeks of corruption. Hallowed, this temple is unclean.
Any day we can share victory over our enemies is a fine day. When there's the smell of burning bodies in the air, it just makes the day that much finer. Thank you, soldier, for making my day.
Very good, soldier. Looks like you're ready to come with us on the next mission.
What happened? Was Mathal in Rakhad's house?
Well met, traveler. Good to see a friendly face out here. You look like the capable sort. Would you be willing to do some aggressive message running?
This one feels confident that you will be a great help to S'ren-ja. Only the wisdom of a Clan Mother could see that kind of potential in you.
Ahh … on second thought do not bring Ezzag a severed head. He would almost certainly throw up.
Ah, the empty one returns.\n\nYour pardon, but, bereft of your soul, that's how I think of you. Don't be offended: I hope to repair your lack.
The only good Goblin is one that's been minced to pieces and then the pieces smashed with rocks.

I appreciate the Mane's sentiment … and the support of the Dominion, but ultimately, it falls on us to protect Valenwood. \n\nSince the Silvenar's death, I get the sense that Queen Ayrenn feels she owes us something, but we Bosmer are not helpless.
Leave this place. There are enemy troops in town and we need no more trouble here.
Just need a minute to catch my breath.
Did you stop the Dremora reinforcements? We're barely surviving the ones here already.
Be calm in the moonlight. And welcome to Do'Krin. You tread upon ancient stones here.
The texts never made it sound … like that. What we did. We killed the Silvenar! The heart of the forest, the Green Lady is dead.

Fancy meeting you here! I keep hearing all these reports out of the March. "Hallowed this" and "the Hallowed did that." Even on the fringes of the Dominion, you make your mark. With another city ablaze, I'm glad you're here.
This one looks forward to pouncing upon an unsuspecting Pelidil. This nonsense is becoming tiresome.

I'll send word to the other clans and to Queen Ayrenn in Marbruk. If the Maormer are attacking in force, we are going to need all the help we can get.\n\nI just hope we can hold out until some help arrives.
You must be the one <<1>> spoke of. Our agents owe you their lives.
Have we met before? Hmm ….\n\nNever mind.
Did you find them? Are they still alive and fighting?
Ugh … my head.
Welcome to <<1>>. If you plan to leave us with a small fortune, please show up with a large one!

Did you hear the voice …? He called this the "Shadow Wood." It seems to be some dark realm that parallels Valenwood. \n\nIf the Shade of Naemon has created this, he's more powerful than I realized. This is … horrifying.
You made it this far, just as I had predicted. I am glad to see that my calculations were not in error.\n\nNow, if you are ready, we have a prison to break out of.
Let's not tell any bards about this part of our adventure, agreed? This is not what I want to be remembered for.
I long to see the Elder Scroll of Chim in Dominion hands.
Oh, hello there. What can Ezreba do for you?
I saw what you did, outsider. Your convictions must be powerful indeed!
If Aruz comes out of this dead, I might just break into a smile.
Good to see you again. What's the word on my supplies?
These aren't Dominion sailors, they're privateers. Just our luck.
Is it done?
If <<1>> is truly in danger, we should tread carefully.
Thank you, friend. I need a moment to recover. If you wouldn't mind disabling the traps, <<1>> can make it through without fear of perforation.
You aren't a slick-arsed Sea Viper or a cabbage-mouthed castaway. State your business with the crew of the Prowler.
The end draws near. It was an interesting and unexpected journey. That's how I prefer to look at things.
Complete your duties on the island with all haste. When you are done, return to this one and we will deal with the Maormer.

We shall help you enter the tower. But first, you must help us against these foul Wood Elves. Do not listen to their lies!\n\nThey murder our children! For no reason! Please, you must help me save the little ones!
Good luck out there. We'll get the troops ready to go.
I knew he'd be the weak link we needed. Well done.
Your friend <<1>> showed me what you found, but the treaty binds me! Unless the ambassador himself was involved, I am powerless.
The Dominion's invasion of <<1>> will not end well.
No wine. Stringy meat. My beloved Silvenar, cooling these squabbling children instead of warming our bed.\n\nIf there's a more tiresome place in all of Tamriel, I haven't found it.
Keep winning Division Championships and you may get your chance in the main arena!
The thieving vampires can be found throughout this area. Please be quick about it and hurry back.
I am still mixing the ingredients. You will have to wait. \n\nIt takes great patience to be an Ash'abah. You might as well start getting accustomed to it.
Go on! See what my father has to say.
What in Oblivion happened here?
About time someone showed up. Thought I'd die here under a pile of kwama.
I'd start with the Dragons. The Pact only ships their dullest, weakest soldiers off for diplomatic guard duty.

This one remembers you. You fought Canonreeve Oraneth with us.\n\nWe failed to stop her ritual. The final altar was in this Daedric realm all along. We need to find it. Destroy it. At least you survived. They killed Dracien to mock Bakkhara.
So, any luck? Did <<1>> mention anything about the fire you didn't hear from me?

The blood you placed has set the reverberation aspects for my ritual's spell matrix. Now I'm ready to unleash the magic to fill the matrix and power the ritual.\n\nJust make sure nothing interrupts me while I'm working.
Bright Moons hang above us, child. What brings you all the way out here?
There you are. I was beginning to think you were captured.\n\nWe've a bit of a problem, I'm afraid.
I hope that you will prove to be more reasonable than your companion. My offer makes perfect sense, considering the alternatives.
You are our Hallowed, yes? It is good to meet you. I've heard of some of your adventures, asked around. You seem very wise … I hope we have a chance to talk later.
So you are to be the Hallowed, yes? Good, you look like a strong one. It is a pleasure to meet you. I'm certain we will learn much of each other here in the temple.
Lead on. I'm right behind you. Let's see what secrets this installation holds.
Andur intends to kill you. You should see he doesn't.
Hail, chosen of the queen. We have been expecting you.
The knowledge we will obtain from the soul of this creature will be immensely beneficial.\n\nI can think of five different potions I'd like to attempt from Selene's aura alone. Glorious!
Get gone, my friend. Don't keep the moon-sugar-induced visions waiting.
Apologies, traveler. This isn't the best time. If you're here to talk about buying some mead, Donniel will help you out.
<<1>> always sets out a wonderful spread. The food is excellent! Even better than my cooking, I must admit.
<<1>> is trying to deceive you. If you listen to me and do exactly what I tell you, I'll help you see through their illusions.
We will enter the temple together, Hallowed. You are sure you are ready to begin the trial?
Remember, we need you to close that reinforcement portal before you unlock the Labyrinth. As long as the portal is functioning, Molag Bal has the ability to overwhelm us with Daedric forces.
Who are you? You don't look like one of the Ungodly.\n\nWait, are you here to help the matchmaker? Because that's me!
Ah, excellent, you got my message. Apparently, that little creature isn't completely useless. Banekin can be such children.\n\nI hope you've nothing pressing. We could be here a while.
Hopefully this will work.
I imagine it will take a few days to pack this tribe up and escort them out of <<1>>.\n\nI'll make sure it's done with dignity.
I was dreaming of speckled fish. Now I'm hungry and wet. Explain yourself.

Who knows how long those fiends kept the harpies agitated, just to take advantage of this town?\n\nIf I hadn't returned when I did, and gotten your help, they'd continue to terrorize my people and these harpies.
The wizard seems agitated. We need to drain those <<m:1>>.
<<1>>'s theory is arguably sound. We should channel the energies from the <<m:2>>.
The Labyrinth key is in the chest, little mortal. Take it and be about your business while I'm still inclined to be friendly.
I'm sure I'll see you around. The world's only so big! Bigger now, I expect! How exciting!
Everyone's story must be told. Everyone's.
We've got to keep moving.
Let's get in the fight.
<<1>> may be right. We should channel the energies away from those <<m:2>>.
Let's get to the summit point. Lead on.
I'm just here as security. You should talk to the great mage, Vanus Galerion.
You there. You're not one of these savages. Free me, quickly!

It is good you have come. The Bosmer here have yet to swear loyalty to the Dominion, and our enemies seek to sway them. Worse, the Staff of Magnus was stolen from Marbruk before I arrived.\n\nI hope you will aid the Dominion in this dark time.
I understand you visited the Halls of Torment? Marvelous place. Marvelous. I'm not a fan of the tortured screaming, but otherwise it's quite lovely.
The monks never made it sound … like that. We killed the Silvenar! The heart of the forest, the Green Lady is dead.
If you're not here to help, leave us alone.
You're one of Brackenleaf's Briars now. You're free to come and go, but whatever you do in the world reflects on us. Don't make me hunt you.
A guard's life is a thankless one.
Wait!\n\nAh, you're not one of those Wood Orcs, thank Y'ffre! Welcome to our humble home!
How is it that the Elder Scroll of Mnem still remains in enemy hands? Where are the Pact's brave warriors?
They will pay for the innocent lives they have taken!
The strength of the Elder Scroll of Mnem belongs to the Covenant now!
I don't understand. I observed all the proper protocols. How could so many have … have perished?
The shield's down! Let's get her!
Another doppelganger? I didn't think Titanborn could be less appealing. Looks like I've been proved wrong. That's a first.\n\nPerhaps if we take out that shield we can release Sahan.
Stop! Don't make me go back. I was so close to escaping him forever!
It's unfortunate that Aranak needed to meet such a terrible end for his crimes, but his lesson will help others avoid the same fate.
You have given me much to consider. Unfortunately, I fear such thoughts may keep me up at night.
We won't make it inside my laboratory unless we stop the lightning.
Mannimarco calls forth the dead! Send them back to their graves!
One of these days, Mannimarco's going to have to fight for himself. I'm really looking forward to that.
We should keep moving. It isn't safe here.
Greetings, comrade. The Fighters Guild has entrusted Sebazi with contracts, if this is of interest.
I greet you, comrade. The Fighters Guild has contracts to offer in Cyrodiil. Would you like to hear of them?
The Fighters Guild is helping out here in Cyrodiil, trying to rein in the chaos. Interested in a contract?
Do not judge me too harshly. I will spend the rest of my days making amends for what I have done.
If Reynelle remains here, she'll be just up ahead.
Who is Lady <<1>>? Was that truly <<2>>? He seemed rather obsessed with her.\n\nWe must get to the bottom of this.
Look, Stibbons, it's our friend … you know, the one who helped us in Alik'r! How good to see you again, and at such an opportune moment too.

Here I was, just starting to feel like you're one of the pack, and now we have to part ways.\n\nObviously, I'll have to be the one to break the wards on the door. It doesn't seem fair. You get to go in and chew the old hag's face off.
I've been trapped here for so long. To feel the sun upon my face again … just to think of its indulgence.
May the blessings of Stendarr go with you, my friends.
My goodness, undead! How unexpected. How utterly original. Bloody necromancers.

There's a sight for a sore eye! Someone who looks like they can spill blood for a righteous cause!\n\nThe Imperials have just about licked us. I've only got a few knights left who are fit to fight. I've had to recruit Baandari to defend the camp!
Thanks again. Jode's Chariot regards you as an honorary member.
Baron Dorell can be so reckless. I fear that his approach will lead Rivenspire down a dangerous path.\n\nOf course, his style of leadership hardly matters if we can't put a stop to Baron Montclair.
What you have done is unforgivable, but it will not stop us.
I am sorry, but managing an organization of this size takes time. Please. Return later and we may talk.

I apologize if the scene before you makes you uncomfortable. I did not expect you to arrive during our meal time.\n\nAs for why I kept my true nature hidden? Well, let's just say that Emeric insisted. And one does not refuse the High King lightly.

Just so you know, while you're slogging through sewage, we won't be napping out here. \n\nWe'll go ahead and assault the main gate. It'll create a good distraction. It'll also mean that if you fail, we'll all die. Just so you know.
This will work, my old friend. We're going to save Leila, I just know it!
Remember, seek out Sahil at the inn. But tell him Adusa sent you, or he might try to kill you or something.
The Aldmeri Dominion is a reality, but it's still quite young. We must remain its caretakers so it may flourish into adulthood.\n\nI'm glad <<1>> shares my views.
I'd expected you would solve problems at the embassy, not cause them! Do you realize what's happening out here?\n\nNever mind. Explain what you were doing in that storeroom.
<<1>>'s sacrifice should be the extra edge we need to call upon Hircine.
Wyress Nyronie is brave to undertake such a task.
Off with you, now! If the Goblins have their dinner before you administer the potion, why, who knows how long we'd have to wait for them to ingest it?

The bickering of nobles. It can try even the most stoic king's patience. But at least Tamrith and Dorell have the kingdom's interests at heart.\n\nBaron Montclair has gone well beyond the extent of my patience, into the realm of loathing, I think.
With Daraneth returned to Elden Root and the Heart of Anumaril at hand, only a divine spark remains.
Tall Papa, help me …. What have I done?\n\nPlease—you must help!
Adeena? She must be here somewhere ….
Listen to me. Wayfarer, please. That is not my sister—not anymore. You can't believe its lies. It's … it's manipulating you!
We share the blood of Mother Lamae. We are now kin. I will watch out for you from the shadows.
You've done me a great service in returning me to my vigil.
Finally, we can return to our normal way of life without entertaining any more Imperials than necessary.
I don't suppose you'd be willing to help me on another grand adventure? \n\nI won't accompany you on it, of course, but I'll be there in spirit nonetheless!
Place the heads on the pikes around the dais. Then I'll begin the ritual.\n\nBrace yourself. This could be … unpleasant.
Go on, then. Simply reach out and touch Meridia's Light. You'll be whisked off to new adventures, quick as you please!
Come on, help me out of this mess. I've been stuck for hours.
The winds bring us strange tidings. Fortunately, we can always find a way to cope.
You're a true friend to us. We'll never forget you!
You're a really good person for helping me. I hope you know that.
While we're waiting for Shuga to finally get here, what do you say to taking on the most unlikely prospect of the bunch?\n\nIf you can recruit this young man, I'll eat my dagger. He's … awkward.
Go ahead and examine the tear. The veil may hinder me, but I believe you can guide us through here.
I pray to the Light that we have the will and the strength to end the threat of Baron Montclair.
Do you think we'll be all right, going through there? I have to admit, all this fire and brimstone business. I'm a bit … flustered.
Thank the Eight! When we found the portal closed, I feared the worst.
A thrice-damned hero, you are. If my ribs weren't so bruised, I'd give you a hug!
Something is very wrong here. Where did all these plague husks come from?
About what I said. About kissing you on the lips. You know, that was just the heat of the moment, right?\n\nAnyway, thanks again for your help.
Now that you're here, I'm sure Dethisam is going to make it. Even Aerona seems glad to see you, and she's rarely happy to see anyone.\n\nTalk to Nilyne. She'll tell you what she needs.

They say something terrible has awoken—or occupied—Hel Ra Citadel, abandoned by the Yokudans since they invaded Tamriel.\n\nScholars have been disappearing inside since the door to the Citadel, sealed by the Yokudans for thousands of years, opened.

I was up in that tree for hours! Damned senches. Thank you for the assistance, stranger, I—it's you! \n\nYou helped me before—saved my village. What brings you back? I—never mind. I need your help again. Will you give it?
Find the gems that power the Seeker's Sight and we may still foil the Serpent's plans. Start your search north of this settlement, and good luck to you.

You have restored the gems to the Seeker's Sight. Good. But we are running out of time. The Scaled One has found another of our aspects. We felt her turn.\n\nHe is creating a corrupted version of ourselves—and this Lost One grows ever stronger.
You've been up there for quite a while. Did you—did you make it all the way to the top?
I'm glad you made it! I don't think the runescriber or armorer will see reason any better than the trainer. I'm afraid the time for talk is behind us.\n\nLet's go dismantle an army!

Damn it! I'd rather die fighting than be stuck down here. The Temple may be lost, but we mustn't lose heart!\n\nGood will always triumph over evil, and Molag Bal's minions are no exception. We can stop them, I tell you. We must.
Find the cave and destroy the wamasu eggbearer. Just remember not to reveal my involvement. Neither of us will benefit if the Scaled Court discovers my betrayal.

Friend, have you come across Kelmen in your travels?\n\nThe Thief reported a magical disturbance around Skyreach. Kelmen went to find an old Mages Guild associate he said was working in the area. He has yet to return.
Regent Cassipia and Little Leaf wanted to change the world, but the cost was too high.\n\nThe Serpent, the Viper … whatever you call it, a snake is still a snake.
I knew you'd come back from this one. I just had a feeling about it. Glirion owes me 50 coins. Hah!
You return. I had expected you to be carrying armloads of plunder. Does Blackheart still live?
I prefer to work with maple. It's reliable, plentiful … rarely full of wasps.
Once you return with the ingredients, we'll determine whether you know how to combine them.

<You notice a prominent handbill on the requisition board.>\n\n"Lord Vivec gives greetings! Masters of the craft await you in <<1>>. We offer training for all new to their craft, and certification for accomplished crafters. Free for all citizens!"

I'd love to accompany you, but I have more research to complete. Mzindyne has its own idiosyncrasies and unique features.\n\nGive me enough time and I'm sure to discover something that will benefit us in the long run.
Can't a king have a meal in peace around here? You'll have to wait until I'm done.\n\nIf you're bored, go do something useful and kill a few Reachmen or something.
Have you happened to see an Elf around here? Tall, spindly, talks way too much for his own good?
Get going. I've got to look for more people.
My son …. <<1>> is dead.\n\n<<2>> waits at the Bloody Knoll. Is <<3>> on his way?
Help us re-take the throne room! I promise all will be revealed soon. \n\nWell, relatively soon.
Unless this is about Taebod or her portals, I don't have time for it.
You've got an eager look on your face. Who'd you kill?

<You notice a prominent handbill on the requisition board.>\n\n"King Emeric offers greetings! Masters of the craft await you in <<1>>! Free training for all new to their craft; certification for accomplished crafters! All at no cost to you, citizen!"

New to the city, are you? Yes. The Rat can tell by your scent—clean with no fear. Everyone else here reeks of their own waste.\n\nThey made sport of the Rat, but now the Daedra make sport of them. Now they need help, and no one cares.
I'm going to be the envy of Nord scholars everywhere! These carved images are simply remarkable!

Ancient tombs can be tricky. Always hiding remains or treasure so as to discourage looters and genuine scholars.\n\nAnd then there are the ogres. My man-servant is useless in the face of such creatures. I do hope that you're made of sterner stuff!
This expedition has really proved to be more troublesome than Lady Laurent anticipated. I hate to say it, but I think this time Sorrow might be more than she bargained for.

Incredible! Legends say that Torug sacrificed seven clans to build his tomb, and I can see why!\n\nAnyway, the second stanza talks about Torug's relic and Sorrow's kiss. Read my translation and see for yourself.
Good to see that you survived Coldharbour, too. I figured after all that craziness, a little trip to Wrothgar would be kind of like a walk in the park.
First the storm. Then we crashed upon the ice. And those terrible little monsters attacked us!\n\nI just wish my wife wasn't still out there. I don't mind admitting that I'm lost without her.
The Hand of Morkul is held in something called the … I think it said "heart-forge?" Also, um … "endless breath and untold rage lets purest heart release the hand."\n\nHuh. Poets.
My mother … I think she made these puzzles so that her child … so that I … could find her.\n\nCome on, let's figure this one out.
I'm sorry, were you saying something? I was just … just thinking. Sorry.
Lead the way, my friend. I'll fight alongside you every step of the way.
Lead the way, my friend. My healing magic will sustain you no matter what the Vosh Rakh place before us.

Don't worry about Raynor. He'll yell at me for awhile, but something will come along eventually and require his undivided attention.\n\nAnd if it doesn't come along soon, I'll toss him in the next Dwarven ruins we find and see how he likes it.
Ten years. <<1>> and I spent ten years looking for the tomb of <<2>>. Now that we find it, she says it's not his!\n\nOur moment of glory … why would she ruin it?
My work … all those valuable Dwemer components … all ruined!\n\nJust so you know, I'm going to be upset with you and my sister for a long time over this.
"Paired vessels" … it must mean burial urns.\n\nI'm sorry, I have to translate. Have you spoken with my colleague? <<1>> can assist if you have any questions.
Go ahead. We'll be right behind you.
<<1>> will pay the blood price, I'm sure of it. I don't want her dead, but she'll suffer as I do.
Thank you for your advice. I never knew how much I'd miss my home until I departed!
Did I overcook the meat? Just should have taken it off the fire sooner.
That's a relief. I really thought that might be the arena that would break you. But you did it!

I appreciate your help. You wouldn't believe how much goes into getting the museum ready for visitors. Just preparing the displays was a tremendous amount of work!\n\nIf you're interested, I have a lead on another piece we're seeking. Uzdabikh's Helm.
For the love of Malacath, put out that fire before we roast!
Did I hear correctly? Will you be visiting the wrecked ships? If so, perhaps I could impose upon you for a small favor?
I hear some of the trainees are already trying to duplicate your best arena moves. \n\nYou've definitely made an impression on the realm of Maelstrom!
If you manage to reassemble one of those books, take it back to Cirantille. We've no use for books covered in ogre dung.

So did you find those weird eggs? What do they look like? Actually, you know what—forget I asked. \n\nThe company's already settled up with Nednor. You should go talk to him to get your slice. Good work.
You made it past my traps. You're lucky, stupid, or quite skilled. I haven't decided which.\n\nWell? My garden needs tending. Out with it, and be on your way.

Excellent. The noble's estate can be found northwest of Anvil, along the Gold Road.\n\nHow you perform the execution is up to you. Just make sure Lord Quintus Jarol dies by your hand. Then your initiation into the Dark Brotherhood will be complete.
I'm glad you joined our humble little guild. You take to the life very well. Very well indeed.
Have you ever seen as the Hist sees? Have you ever looked beyond the barrier of time? We're going to need to see with more than our eyes to find the truth in this place.
You're like a dark gift from the Night Mother herself.
What are you standing around for? I'm not much to look at and neither is this room.
The <<1>> must be inside the treasure room. We're almost there!

Here we part ways. Once I'm in uniform, I'll see how well I blend in.\n\nIf I may suggest a course of action? The journal you brought contains the entire dowry heist as planned by <<1>>. I think we can use it to our advantage.
It's a bit much in here. Whoever built this palace was trying too hard.
Perfect timing. I can't exactly climb the palace walls in this outfit.
The last time I was here, the Iron Wheel wasn't camped in front of the tomb.\n\nPerfect.
Don't keep <<1>> waiting.
You should meet <<1>> in <<c:2>>. Seemed important.

Hello, hero. I'd say I'm surprised to see you, but I've been watching you for days. Acting surprised would be so disingenuous.\n\nLet's just say I'm pleased to once again be graced by your company. You're exactly who I hoped to meet out here.
<<1>> can move things from place to place when a boss needs. Goods, coin, people too sometimes. Find me if you have such a need, boss.
This one has a wicked thirst. Perhaps some generous stranger would be kind enough to part with some gold?
If the caravan master hasn't seen her, meet me at the docks. Otherwise, I'll meet you over there.\n\nNow, hurry, Initiate. Hurry!
New member? Great, we could use the coin coming in. Any work the Guildmaster's approved get posted to that board over there.\n\nSee something you like, get it done and I'll handle the books.
The Sanctuary is that way, in case you've forgotten. I'd tell you that Astara was in a good mood the last time I talked to her, but truth is I can never really figure out what the Matron is thinking.
So you decided to help find Hildegard, eh? Well, there's no shame in helping your Brothers and Sisters. Just don't let it interfere with your other duties, Initiate.
Make no mistake, Initiate. Astara sends you to Kvatch not because she trusts you. She's decided to test you. Do not fail her.

Just between us, don't let Elam or Astara get under your skin. They've got to be tough on initiates to prepare them for life in the Brotherhood. But you're family now, and we're all here to support you. Remember that.

You don't need to say anything. I see and hear more than you might think. This is my Sanctuary, after all. \n\nGo with your scaled Brother. Follow the journal's trail to its end. Just don't do anything foolish. I expect a full report when you return.
Oh, hello. Sorry about not greeting you earlier. I … wasn't exactly in a talkative mood when you arrived.
Find the gems that power the Seeker's Sight and we may still foil the Serpent's plans. Start your search north of this settlement, and good luck to you.

You have restored the gems to the Seeker's Sight. Good. But we are running out of time. The Scaled One has found another of our aspects. We felt her turn.\n\nHe is creating a corrupted version of ourselves—and this Lost One grows ever stronger.
I'm glad you made it! I don't think the runescriber or armorer will see reason any better than the trainer. I'm afraid the time for talk is behind us.\n\nLet's go dismantle an army!
Find the cave and destroy the wamasu eggbearer. Just remember not to reveal my involvement. Neither of us will benefit if the Scaled Court discovers my betrayal.
Follow the river to the right. It flows directly past the entrance to the Sanctum.
Regent Cassipia and Little Leaf wanted to change the world, but the cost was too high.\n\nThe Serpent, the Viper … whatever you call it, a snake is still a snake.
Be cautious in the Council House, sera. House Telvanni is not just some beast you can slay. In this place, subtlety will serve you better than any shield.\n\nWe have to play the game.
Is that a bit of mud on your hands? How was your visit to Skywatch?
Barilzar will figure something out. He's brilliant and quite capable, despite his bizarre behavior.
You still have your head on your shoulders, so it can't have gone all that poorly. Did you manage to learn anything?
Back so soon? Well, you're quite the negotiator!\n\nI trust you found a suitable property outside Vos?
Greetings. We must speak quickly. The overseers grow nosy and suspicious.
Thank you for helping me, sera. Honestly, it means a lot.\n\nThe rascal's name is Menaldinion. You'll find him sliming around that new shop of his—the gauche High Elf clinic just south of here.
Well, it tastes like roast guar drippings … but I do feel a bit better. Hmph. I can't believe I'm doing this.

Llayne tells me I have you to thank for unearthing Savarak's plot on my life. Interesting. \n\nSpeak with her. She'll make sure you are properly rewarded. Then we can determine if you might be of further use.

Did I hear that right? The queen is… she's dead?\n\nNo, that can't be right. Perhaps she's just sleeping? With all the sounds messing with their heads in those mines, I'm… I'm almost sure it must just be exhaustion.
Something creeps through the shadows of my realm, and so far all my efforts to discover the nature of this darkness have come to naught.\n\nIf you are willing, I have more tasks to ask of you.
You stink of blood, sweat, and iron. I like it. Did you work up that musk in the Bloodroot Forge?
I need a few moments to review these documents. Report to Lord Vivec and tell him what you found. I'll meet you inside shortly.
The tracks will tell us what we need, but step cautiously on this hunt. I will not be your minder here.
Manore is right. The resonator activating, the queen getting killed, that poor bard losing his life … it's all my fault. I deserve everything that's coming to me.
Remember to examine the panels on the walls to each side. I'm sure they provide a clue as to how we need to go about solving this puzzle.

So hard to concentrate and maintain schedules when interruptions constantly occur. Don't they know the Great Gear never pauses in its rotations?\n\nSo that was you up there? I appreciate the assistance. Daedric entities can be very unpredictable.

If that old idiot is what passes for a Tribunal leader, it's no wonder the Houses are in such disarray.\n\nNo time to dwell on that, though. I found my brother! And it's worse than I feared. Chodala's quest for power has led him down a dark path.

First, pay respect to Farseer Kuamta. She walks the Red Path this year, and it's customary to wish her well. Request to take part in the offering to the First Ashkhans. \n\nDo that, and you should be able to ask their Wise Woman about the tomb.

With the exception of capable bodyguards like Vimy Lacroix, finding competent assistants has proven difficult. Unfortunately, she and I were separated during our escape.\n\nI suggest you begin by searching for Vimy at our camp inside the ruins.

We've got a horde of mercenaries searching for us, and scads of Dwarven death-machines prowling around, but hey, at least we've got a broken control rod now, right?\n\nWell … enough talk. Off we go, eh?

Get to the swamp and find Veya. She's eager for any information about her brother, so she's really going to appreciate getting that registry.\n\nJust try not to be too charming when you meet her, hero. She has enough distractions as it is.
I need to check in with the overseer. His workers are searching the wreckage and I want to know what they've uncovered.
Thank you for talking to Eoki. I only hope that he'll listen to reason.

As you recover more rubbings, return here to me. With every detail we add to our model, the closer we get to discovering the location of the lost library!\n\nI prepared a list of the tombs you need to find. Refer to the note as you conduct your search.
Father ruins everything! I'm so close to finding my brother and he shows up to drag me back home.\n\nWell, I'm not going back without a fight!

We need to be invisible. These things work best when no one but the target knows we're there.\n\nIf you get spotted, you're on your own. I even cough on anyone without a writ and the Morag Tong will have my head.

Azura's champion returns!\n\nI saw you in my visions. You stood atop a mound of corpses, destroying Daedra by the hundreds. It was … cathartic. That sounds horrible. Let's just say it was a welcome distraction from what else I've seen.
Come! The realm needs a champion and you happen to be standing here, so I dub thee my hero in the making.

I'm working without a writ on this one. Find Brivan and make sure Veya doesn't kill him. Stay focused on that and we might just pull this off.\n\nI hate spilling blood without a contract, but we might not have a choice. We just have to stop Veya.

It's about damn time you Buoyant Armchairs arrived! I requested assistance almost an hour ago and—oh, hello. I was just thinking about you!\n\nYou may not be a Bouncing Armiger, but you've never disappointed me before. Perchance you're here to help?
Merciful Stendarr! That creature was positively terrifying! But at least I found one of my lady's hirelings ….

Look at those factotum. Remarkable creations! That one over there, for example. It's rallied to the defense of the Clockwork City and is keeping the skaafin at bay.\n\nObviously, you'll need to destroy it before we can enter the city.

Naryu and I rarely see eye to eye, but she has always been good to my children.\n\nI just hope that once you bring Veya home, we can find a way to expunge this dark stain from her record. No Redoran daughter should take up with those murderers.

I … I can scarcely believe what we just witnessed. How could this happen? How could a shadow masquerade as Lord Seht?\n\nThe Father of Mysteries would never let such a thing happen. There must be another explanation.

Do not be alarmed. Only you can see me. I am Lilatha, Psijic master of the gazing glass.\n\nI have watched you from afar, and I believe we share the same goal. You seek to destroy these vengeful shadows, yes? I believe we can help each other.
I want you to know how much we appreciate all you've done for the Clockwork Apostles. If you ever need anything that we can provide, I'm sure we can come to an equitable arrangement.
I don't often admit surprise, but I'll be candid—that was one of the weirdest journeys of my life. And I've lived a very, very long time.
Those mushrooms look plump and delicious! Let's go see Apprentice Idrono and find out if he knows anything about the apprentices that entered the Wellspring after Gathal's accident.

So, you've chosen to join me. Excellent.\n\nI seek a powerful Daedric artifact. It lies hidden in a distant land—a gleaming city filled with danger, curiosity, and contradiction. In such a place, diverse perspective is vital. Thus, you.
Well, it appears we have the teensiest of problems.
Thanks for the help. Raynor's smart, but you can't smart a spider to death, you know?
You did bring a gift, correct? Give it to Varuni without delay!

Hello again. So strange. I'm glad to see you, but I must admit, the statistics are staggering. What are the odds of us meeting here, again, in an extra-planar space? Rhetorical, of course.\n\nHonestly, I'm glad you're here.
You have questions, of course. Ask what you must. The forces at work here are cunning indeed. You should be prepared for anything.
Welcome, crow-friend! Rest here in Blackfeather Castle as long as you like … but next time bring meat.

I hate the way people look down on Slag Towners. Maybe it's not enough that I help feed these people something worth eating. We're always going to be struggling until the snooty folks on high see we have something to contribute.
Don't know why Bren's so obsessed with trying to get folk down here when we should be trying to get up out of this gutter.

The journey to the Mnemonic Planisphere is riddled with dangers, so it's best to prepare. Shouldn't be any issues once you head inside though!\n\nMy research leads me to believe the integral of memory will resemble a crystal.

What a day! We saw some amazing sites and we did it without my sister's help. Still, I'm glad we settled things and we're back to being partners again. I suppose I really do rely on Kireth's skills and abilities.\n\nAnyway, thanks again.

Go on. Pretend you belong and no one will notice you, especially once you put on those elegant clothes.\n\nMeet Raz nearby after you talk to her. This one looks forward to hearing what she has to say about all of this.
You decided to utilize the medallion of summoning. Very well. Then you might as well tell me how the search for the Oracle goes.

We were warned that Daedric Princes had their eyes on Summerset, but I didn't expect that level of danger from what was supposed to be a simple investigation.\n\nI suggest you tell the Eye of the Queen what we discovered. I'll catch up with you later.
You're an adventurer, aren't you? Please, you have to help me.\n\nThe Sapiarchs accused my best friend of a murder he didn't commit. They won't even consider the possibility that he's innocent!

I am Calawende, chief diplomat of the Mages Guild. I apologize for my tone. This has been a trying time.\n\nThe Sapiarchs consider this matter closed, you know. What are you doing, exactly? Who sent you? Our interests may align.

We must discover what this Court of Bedlam is up to in Rellenthil. Valsirenn will meet you there and you can present yourselves to the Canonreeve. If there's anything obvious we need to know, the Canonreeve should be aware of it.\n\nGood luck.
You see? The Illuminus changed again!\n\nI don't know about you, but this is really starting to give me the shivers. Who knew a book could be so unsettling?

I heard that you were able to procure Alchemy's sponsorship. Excellent. \n\nI see you've been given a Hopeful's mask as well. Such a quaint practice. Auri-El knows our task would be far easier if they weren't a tradition.
When you next speak to Rinyde, ask her to abandon her search. Larydel has chosen his path, and will not be swayed from it.
Pity is my crown and sorrow my kingdom.
I won't interfere with whatever it is you're investigating, but don't expect my cooperation.
Can't talk now, I'm hot on the trail of the pie thief!
You'll want to keep close. The pathways in this forest seem to be … broken somehow. In the metaphysical sense.
Elise is a junior keeper. She's lucky we found her when we did. She's not ready to handle animals unsupervised, let alone something like this.
I bet you've come here for an aurialis bloom. Well, tough luck. Fresh out. Last one was nabbed a fortnight ago.\n\nCome back in about a year. Maybe I'll have another one by then.
Sealing the last of those Magicka Fonts should have reduced the flow of magicka to a trickle. We should get to the courtyard and see if it's affected the storm.
I expected the pathway to lead to some obscure corner of Oblivion, but this is Nocturnal's realm!\n\nI wish I could remember what compelled me to hide the Heart here.
It took considerable effort for the Ritemaster to open this pathway through the Dreaming Cave.\n\nI'll help him along while you and Darien clear the path ahead.
First Mephala and now Nocturnal. I'm really getting good at stumbling into the realms of hostile Daedric Princes!\n\nLet's do what we have to do and get out of here.
I suggest you let Soravil do the talking. He may play the role of the insufferable ass, but he can be very persuasive—charming even, when he puts his mind to it.

Oh! Was it today that you would arrive? Well, it certainly seems like it.\n\nWelcome, welcome! I expected you would come, though perhaps not quite so soon. You're here about the missing relics of course.
I'm so sorry, my friend. When I first asked you to help me, I never thought …. \n\nAm I mistaken? To think that Zaan the Scalecaller has risen again, why, it strikes me to my very core.

Meet Darien and me at the Crystal Tower Gatehouse. It lies to the northeast of Lillandril.\n\nI just hope the Sapiarchs have found a way to speed up their ritual. We really need the tower sentinels right now.

Who knew getting an introduction would be so complicated? You perform the favors and Rigurt will wait for you to return.\n\nYou are a good friend to Rigurt. We will drink mead and sing songs of battle when this is done!

Many greetings. My time is precious, friend, but I can spare a moment or two. The Proxy Queen's court is not in session due to unforeseen circumstances. I'm sure whatever business brings you here can wait a day or two.
Start digging through the records. There has to be something here I can use to bring down Vinelore.
Go, speak to Ghrum. I believe he has some information to share with us.

I didn't see where they went while I was fleeing, but I have very keen ears and I distinctly heard Naliara's screams over the pounding of my own heart. They were echoing out of the mouth of a nearby cave through King's Haven Pass.

After Raz spoke to the pretty Psijic Oriandra, whispers reached me about the illustrious Illumination Academy. They said that the Court of Bedlam hunts a Sapiarch there, so Raz had to come and see.\n\nDidn't expect all the crazy people, though.

If you've come to bask in the splendor of my latest outdoor arrangement, you're too late. They're ruined. Cast into unsightly disarray by a barbaric vandal.\n\nJust go home and spare yourself the disappointment.
You're just in time, my friend. I could use your help to free these people from K'Tora's mind trap.
I'd like to spend some time with Arillas. If these people really are descendants of Corgrad's populace, there's a lot I could learn from them.
We've got to figure out how to challenge that pompous elf to a duel!
Ugh. I see stars…
Well, we're not going to accomplish much standing around out here.
Now what? I hate these kind of puzzles!

Oh noble stranger, would you help Renzir?\n\nKarnwasten has been captured by Madja, this one's former first mate. She betrayed Renzir and turned his crew against him. There is no hope left, save your kindness.

Find Cainar and his companions in the caves of Karnwasten. That's where the last report said they were going. I even provided a squad of marines to assist them, so something significant must have happened for them to have gone completely silent.
While you deal with the geysers head on, I shall endeavor to find a more permanent solution to the problem.
May the Old Ways guide your steps, initiate. Be cautious in Valenwood. Forces far more dangerous than wolves and bears stalk those woods.

We'll find K'Tora, you can count on that! We've been adventuring long enough to know our capabilities, and hunting down a dark entity is certainly within our area of expertise.\n\nAt least, I'm pretty sure we can handle this. Almost positive.
Have you the sufficient pewter dust?
Seeing how she'll be fed in jail, I fail to see how it'll deter her from foraging in the future.
I hope the food's better than last time.
May the Old Ways guide your steps, initiate. And have a care around those fragments of the staff, all right? Items of power often draw dangerous creatures.
I'm sorry, I can't … I just can't right now. You should go talk to the Loremaster.
If you catch her … when you catch her, please exercise mercy and restraint. As you well know, Josajeh is not evil—only misguided.\n\nMay the Old Ways guide your steps, ceruval.
The necklace and tablet led to the idol. And something inside the idol ….\n\nWhatever Margus found inside the idol could lead him closer to his final goal. We're running out of time!

My egg-siblings only care about the here and now. But I always believed that history was the key to exonerating our disgraced ancestor.\n\nI know we'll find something in the cavern, I just know it! As long as the Wuju-Ka doesn't object to our presence.
The cursed skull scares the wind out of my sails and that's a fact!\n\nDoes Concordia have more work for us to do?
A dream-wallow in the Swallowed Grove? Fascinating. And timely. Very well done, both of you.
So, Zadaza finally found you, eh? Thank goodness!\n\nI need your help. It's grave business, you know? Not trying to apply undue pressure or anything … but, yes. Serious business.
So Famia reels in another adventurer, eh? This one admits, you seem stronger than most. Hmm. Zadaza gives you … two in three chance of surviving. Fair odds, yes?

I'm not sure why Tia wants us to perform this Argonian ritual, but as long as she keeps donating to Cyrodilic Collections, I won't complain. At least not to her.\n\nIf you want to ask her about it, feel free. You can find her at the Mages Guild.
I am sorry I cannot join you, beeko. My heart was torn at first—but now, standing beneath the tree, I see the task is yours. And friend-Famia's.\n\nTake care of her, and trust in the Hist.
I flare my nostrils. No trophies, stacks of dead-word books everywhere, ugly square-drawings …. How do ojels live this way?
We should not linger, lest we fall ill to the same blight as those warped branches shedding all of their leaves.
I have discerned nothing new from the Hist. I hope you and Iskenaaz fare better at the uxith. It may be wise not to keep him waiting. He is prone to rashness when worry gets the better of him.
Once we've overcome the durzog obstacle, I'm certain I'll be able to reach an accord with the Goblins in short order.
Ah, my friend and partner! Were you able to find out about Captain Jimila's likes and dislikes? Anything that will improve our chances to make a deal would be helpful.
Just place the stone in that sconce there. With any luck, the gate will spring back to life!

So, it is true. The Blackguards take hostages from the Dead-Water tribe as well.\n\nAs I said, Jaxsik is very proud, but she would be a valuable ally if we could convince her to let us help. Too bad she runs away, yes? At least we have a lead.
I need to find my children. I failed them once. I can't fail them again.
Take a walk or I'll make a coat out of you.

I flare my nostrils and fill my lungs. Do you smell it, ojel? The dryness of the branches? The loosening of the soil? This Hist slumbers like the dead. But it is not dead yet.\n\nIts strength lies in the Remnant. In the souls of its tribe.
An expedition to the Swallowed Grove—how marvelous!\n\nGoodness, I guess I should start packing.
You did it! Of course, I expected no less from the ally personally chosen by Lady Twilight.

What a sun-blessed hour this is! All of the tablets have been returned.\n\nNow, there is one more task before the Xinchei-Konu is fully restored. I must evoke the Vastei-Sei, otherwise known as the Ritual of Change.

Pardon me, traveler, but have you a moment?\n\nI was recently attacked by a flock of hackwings, and lost a possession of grave importance as I fled. If you would but help me retrieve it, I would reward you most greatly.
Someone ought to run after Tharayya, right? Sounds like a job for you. I think I'm going to sit this one out.
I have not shirked from my duty! Never has a more steadfast gaze been fixed upon a scoundrel such as Many-Whispers.\n\nFinish this business so that we may return to m'lady with all due haste.

Despite his best efforts, Stibbons actually did something right. I have plenty of material for my book, including the first eyewitness account of an actual ovum-transformation!\n\nBut there's work to be done! I wonder what happens if I crack the shell?
Kassandra moves quickly for someone who is usually so … deliberate.\n\nWhat is the rush? That is what I ask.

Is that …? Ha! Little Xukas, come to visit your old friend in the Glade of Chimes? He is always so busy now. I recall when he stood only as tall as the keppo grass!\n\nAnd you, Blackguard-slayer. What can this stiff-legged crafter do for you?
Euraxia thinks to frighten us with flying lizards? I do not think so!
This one would go with you to the Greenleaf Farm. The farmers there were kind when Zamarak passed that way on his return. He would help you convince them to find safety inside the town.

So far, my elusive stalker has only followed and observed. I'm beginning to think they want us to do all the work before they swoop in to steal the weapon. I assure you, I won't let that happen.\n\nNow, let's head to Jode's Light.
The assassins! They stalk the southern passages. We must hurry. There may be another way past this door deeper in the complex.
My antidote is nearly complete. All I need now is the Arkay's lash blossom. Were you able to get one?
Why do you hesitate, rhook? Whoever that was, we cannot lose them!

I will spend a little time with Aneshi, five-claw. There are things we need to talk about. Old friends we need to remember.\n\nTake the note and recover the master key. Then meet me and the others in Rimmen.
Well? Head on in, before anyone notices.
This one hopes you have found something of interest, walker. Mizzik cannot afford to keep Tajirri distracted any longer. And he means that most literally.
Time slips away, my friend. Please, activate the relic.
Nazdar did well to get us inside, but it looks like the strain was more than he could handle. He needs rest.\n\nWhich means Tasnasi needs to change her plans.
This place smells awful. Maybe it was never pristine when Dashing Dasalzo ran things, but he had the decency to keep the mildew in check.\n\nSome of this mold looks like it may start talking soon.

Well, better I'm paired up with you than the ancient adept or the smarmy Wood Elf. You look like you can handle a scuffle.\n\nI'm only good at knocking myself out with a bottle, but I know a spell or two to muffle the noise of a brawl.

Nazdar advises patience. We can avoid the sentries, if we are calm.\n\n"Heed the tenants of the Whispering Claw, and no one will pay you any more mind than they would a lark's shadow." The words of Nazdar's master, the venerable Pellu-dar.

Our companions left the palace to wander Rimmen and consider what is to come. Find Abnur Tharn, Zamarak, and Prefect Calo. Cadwell, too, if he is still around.\n\nI would like them to join us at the Moon Gate, but will understand if they decide not to.
There's no going back for him. Neither Rakazsa, nor the Tenarr Zalviit clan. Their only care now is the taste of the blood on their tongues.\n\nThere's only one way this ends now.
Zamarak thinks he can disrupt the necromancer's spell. Meet him at the Temple of the Purifying Moons.

The undead outside should provide the power you need. If you strike them down, I'm confident the sword and the spirit within will do the rest.\n\nYou should share this with … Shando-ri, was it? I doubt he'll object. He seems more than ready to fight.

Make no mistake, child, Arum-Khal's power and hatred have only grown since we first locked him away.\n\nThe remnants of our order spent their waning years looking for a way to destroy him permanently. We found one. But it carries great risk.
We should seek out this sword-mender as soon as possible. Arum-Khal has spent centuries plotting this escape. If he regains his full strength, even the powers of the Moonlight Blade may fall short.
You saw Rakhzargo's fliers, yes? Mother had him post them across the valley. Help wanted for Sweetwater Farmstead! Ah, Sweetwater, our home sweet home.\n\nAre you interested in a job?
Mother would never hang a tapestry like that in her cellar, of this Raz is certain. Best for us to examine it.
Go on. See how you can help Khamira. I'll keep watch in case the Dragon returns.
Let's take a moment before we head to the palace so I can show you how Euraxia has bent the Khajiit of Rimmen to her will.

The Rithana-di-Renada is finally complete! Oh, I can't believe you were able to complete such a task, five-claw. My brother and I will be forever in your debt.\n\nThough, I am a little disappointed there is no music.
Please, you must find the other mural pieces. Our museum's reputation is on the line!
You made it! I'm afraid this is everyone I've managed to pull together. Hopefully, it'll be enough to deal with the Dragon's blight.\n\nYou can see—ugh—smell the problem right there.
This must be punishment for all of the times I clawed mother's furniture.
O, great Lord of Abundant Pus and Bountiful Vomit, why have you forsaken me?

Thank you again for finding accounts of the flu outbreak in Orcrest. I can easily twist their words to make it seem like Peryite was responsible. Because he was responsible. Probably. Maybe. All that matters is recruiting new followers, all right?

Once we get inside, we'll cover more ground if we split up. Don't get too concerned if you don't see me around. Think of me as your loyal, rakishly handsome shadow.\n\nAs for any rough stuff with the bandits, I'll leave that to you.

Perhaps you will put in a good word for Lyrrsazhi? Let the new queen know that this one's talents are wasted as a common messenger, yes?\n\nAnyway, Queen Khamira can be found in the palace throne room.
Rigurt's sweetbread turned out better than expected! It's perfectly brown and tough enough to break a mammoth tooth!
I don't mind you mortals constantly murdering each other, but would it kill you to crack more skulls? I think I have just the thing.
This Dragon situation is interrupting my research with Selene. Unacceptable.

I'm not so sure I feel honored by this current assignment. First, it involves a Dragon. So, death. Next, it involves Selene. So, again, death. Finally? It involves Carindon. So, unrelenting annoyance.\n\nI can't decide which is worst.
Obviously of Khajiiti origin. Old. Maybe as ancient as these ruins. Perhaps older.\n\nI think this depicts one of the forbidden legends.

I have trained many honorable warriors, wayfarer. As I look upon your stance, your eyes, the set of your shoulders ….\n\nYes, I see it clearly. You are the one who will aid me with this most important task.
Welcome to the temple of Khenarthi's Breath.\n\nWhile you may walk our grounds and hear our bells, we ask that you take nothing. Our temple has had trouble enough with thieves in the past.

Does this count as a Dragon hunt? I mean, we're not going to hurt the Dragon. More like a search and rescue mission, perhaps? Though I don't want to imagine what would a Dragon would need to be rescued from.
Why don't you use your grappling bow and see what's in that urn?
I expected the New Moon cultists to disperse after the death of Laatvulon. I suppose Kaalgrontiid has other ideas.\n\nWe need to determine how the cultists reach the Dragon's protected island.
I expected you to rise to the challenge. You'll find the grappling bow behind the statue near the stables.
You are not intruding, walker. We are honored to have you at our side.
Caska can certainly be persuasive when she wants to be.

When I said the name, Khunzar-ri, the aura that surrounded the door disappeared. If that isn't an invitation, I don't know what is.\n\nGo on. I expect we're about to enter an ancient Khajiiti tomb. Let's see what waits inside.
We can set sail as soon as you're ready.

Adara'hai must remain with Vijari. Without her holy incantations the darkness will overtake him. She'll hold out as long as she can, but her singing can't go on forever. Learn everything you can about Vijari's connection to that horrid mural.
What are you waiting for? Head inside and speak to Zayri.
This is even more spectacular than Jode's Core!\n\nWe must listen to Khunzar-ri and follow his directions, five-claw. We do not want to get lost in this place between all places.
All this talk of Dragons makes for a powerful thirst. Got any honey wine hiding in your pack?
Does the bearded one look tense to you? He look very tense to me. Like a taut string about to snap.
Queen Khamira has news? How exciting! You should talk to her before I think better of assaulting a floating island and its resident Dragon.
Can't you see that Za'ji is grieving?\n\nHe has lost everything! His home! His heart! His one and only lady love! Oh, how can he go on?
Honor and faith, wayfarer.\n\nBlademaster Kasura awaits you at the Vulkhel Guard Manor in the city of Vulkhel Guard. She requests you join her there at once.
I've sent the others ahead. I want you to check in with them and see if they've uncovered anything about the cult's motives.\n\nI'll meet you deeper inside.
An excellent battle, Ahkahtuz. Your might helped seal Laatvulon's fate. He shall never challenge me again.

Please place the piece you found on the tapestry frame. \n\nOur expert crafter Percius Loche will make sure it is properly stitched to the backing. He has seen many sketches of Khajiit of the Moons, from before the dark times.
Let's not keep the Clan Mother waiting. It sounds like she has something important to speak with you about.
Yeah, that's him. Hehe. Don't let him get away!
You need to head back to the sanctum and speak with that Dragon. We don't want to make the Dragon angry, yes?

The Mask of Alkosh should be able to create a flame of some sort, which will allow us to learn about a battle with the Black Beast. Once we've lit all the fires, the path will open.\n\nOr so the inscription tells us.
Don't lose sight of Winks! She's faster than she looks!
These sigils do look familiar. Just be wary. There is more to those stone guardians than meets the eye.
This one is busy. We speak later, yes?
You just wash in on the tide or something? Talk to the burly walking beard if you've got business here.
Ugh. To Oblivion with this place.
Another portal! If we survive this, I swear to never step foot in one of these again.

Ironbelly's note suggested he'd meet with the coven after he did some business in this inn. When he arrives, don't do anything to alarm him.\n\nWe want the merchant completely at ease when he leaves to go rendezvous with the witches.
Sometimes you have to throw caution to the wind and go where the investigation leads you.\n\nLet's catch up to Matron Urgala and see what we can learn.
I hate being treated like I need protection … but Lyris is right. Fenn and I will just get in the way if a battle breaks out.\n\nClear us a path to the Undergrove. Then we'll catch up with you.

From what I could tell, the Midnight Barrow sank into Blackreach in the distant past. Somewhere in its chambers, we'll find the Undergrove.\n\nThe ruined barrow is in the Lightless Hollow, in the northwest portion of the cavern. We'll meet you there.
Come on. Let's clear a path for the others and find this Undergrove.

From what Onda said, it sounds like Rasir was closer to a cure than I even thought. \n\nIf he was searching for an ingredient out here, he may have been attacked by one of the afflicted ones. We need to find him.

We returned to find that my father is finally doing something about the coven threat, but it's not enough.\n\nExtra patrols and rounding up the harrowed is all well and good, but what we really need is a defense against the harrowstorms.
We're all humbled by your help, stranger. It's good to know there's still good people in this accursed world.
That amulet seemed to calm the storm … how is that possible? \n\nAnd that note, that list of corpses. What kind of monster is this Maxten Favrete?
This Sister Balra … I'm going to enjoy ending her miserable existence.
More of that netherroot. What in Shor's name are they doing to it?
Mother loved this temple. It was her favorite place in the city. To see it so abused ….
The power pulsing through the keep, it's getting stronger. I think the harrowstorm is imminent.\n\nWe need to find Svargrim and fast!
The air, it tastes like copper. Just like it did at Kilkreath and Karthald.\n\nThe harrowstorm is coming. We need to find Svargrim now.
The cellar door is over there. Please hurry. I haven't heard a word out of the jarl since I sent her downstairs.
Go ahead. I'll catch up. Just get that key from the chamberlain's sanctum.
Kilkreath Temple lies to the west. Be quick, but not reckless.\n\nI'll head to Solitude as soon as I finish up here.
Hopefully that key we found works for the tower. Let's free the rest of my people and be rid of these raiders.
Word will spread that Petraloop belongs to us once more, but this is just the start. If you can recover all of the instruments, I think it will heal the divide within the college.

Svana giving orders … thinks she's a proper princess now, she does!\n\nWell, I am an expert at procuring all sorts of … procurements. I'll get what the pale Elf needs. After I finish this drink. For medicinal purposes, you understand.
Well done!\n\nHopefully we don't encounter any more locked doors. But if we do, we'll know what to do!
I'm glad to see you made it out of that place in one piece.\n\nI had to carry Adusa half the way. After everything she's just been through, she needs her rest. And a meal.
Don't let your guard down for a second. We don't know what we'll find in there. Phebe gets … excitable, but make no mistake. Whatever we're dealing with will likely not go easy on us.
Did you tell Elle what you found? This is so exciting!
This … isn't good. The pilgrims don't appear to have suffered any physical injuries, but they seem … out of sorts.\n\nTake a look inside their crates and see if they contain any of the funerary urns.
Report. What did you find at the waterfall camp? Did you locate Ena?

Morthal lies to the southeast of Solitude. Bog farmers mostly. The clever woman's camp is probably northwest of the town.\n\nYou shouldn't have any trouble finding it. Not a lot out there but mud and marsh.
Look, we don't have much time. These curs plan to destroy our bridge, and I just gave them exactly the information they need to do so.
We really gave those Reach bastards what they had coming!\n\nThanks for your help, we couldn't have done it without you.
Don't mind Old Mjolen. I'm not nearly as scary as most people think.\n\nExcept, that is, when I want to be.
Don't worry about me. I assure you, I'm fully recovered from the assassin's cowardly attack.
We may have waited too long. The high king revealed his true colors and Solitude begins to fall. If they're already inside the city, there may be no way to stop them.
Let's keep moving. Pickle will point us in the right direction.

The collapse is farther down, but some of the survivors might be nearby. Thulsgreg and I will take one path, you take the other. Save as many as you can.\n\nAnd keep an eye out for the foreman, Mugha. If anyone knows what happened, it would be him.

Please, just listen.\n\nMazog would never put the clan in danger on purpose. She was misguided, and she acted rashly, but she was only trying to meet the chief's demands. When Urzikh finds out …. Mazog shouldn't suffer for trying to protect her kin.

By the set of your jaw, I'd say you're the hardy sort. You're just in time!\n\nI am in need of a brave protector to help me traverse this ruin. It is less than pristine, I'll grant you. But the Dwemeric treasures within should be quite splendid.
There should be one final flame to light deep within the ruin. Perhaps we will find who's been tampering with them there, too.
We're so close to solving this, hurry!

Rigurt knew from the moment he saw Thane Svyne's belly, this is a Nord that acts with his gut, not his head! Rigurt is much the same, only he looks worse with his shirt off.\n\nBut if a Nordic feast will make Thane Svyne listen, then he'll get one!

The scent of death enters my nose. Your time with the cursed creatures has marked you. Let's hope not permanently.\n\nWhile you hunted, my studies proved fruitful. Do you have the blood and skin I require? They will complete my understanding.

The rubes and oafs that reside in this town see spooks under every fish barrel. Normal animal attacks become works of supreme evil in their minds. My husband and I have too much on our plate to spend time investigating every wolf bite.

Arkasis does his work out of a place called the Stone Garden. Used to be some Dwarf ruin. I heard he's been out here for years building up a cult of followers. That wouldn't be so bad, but he's got some werewolf guard dogs as well so be careful.

Talfyg claims there's a secret door that he and I can use to slip in. But Lady Thorn's creatures heavily patrol the area around it. If you fight your way past the front gate, the racket should draw them away.\n\nThis is going to be fun.
Fennorian has an amazing mind. His thoughts and theories wind up in the most interesting places.\n\nGo ahead. Talk to him and see for yourself. An amazing mind ….

Please let Fennorian know I was asking about him when you see him. He's such a mysterious and interesting fellow. As wards of House Ravenwatch, you'd think there'd be rules against us fraternizing, but no. Gwendis assures me it's perfectly fine.

Let's not dawdle, assistant. I don't trust that shifty librarian for a moment. She may have put another historian on Maelmoth's trail, just to thwart me!\n\nNo matter. Scaly book hoarders will never get the better of Narsis Dren!

By the Whale, this frostheel is insufferable. How am I supposed to make my offerings while he babbles about meeting with Jarl Morryn?\n\nIf you're also treating with Thane Svyne, then leave me be. I'll do no business with associates of his.
You're back! Wasn't certain I'd see you again. Well, have you talked to Eyfja and Hautgerd?

So, what brings a … sturdy hero like you to the Gwylim Annex? I can't imagine you're looking for a book.\n\nThen again, I do see a glimmer of curiosity in your eyes. Perhaps you seek admission to the Antiquarian Circle?
It worked! At least I think it worked. No rumblings, no explosions; so that's promising.\n\nBut that spell took a lot out of me. Could you help me out of here? Maybe as far as the road?
All right, enough hand-wringing. Let's kill this hag and get my sister back.
I swore that the next meal I ate would be a Nordic feast. And I keep my oaths, damn it!\n\nBesides, my sodding vassals left our provisions back home.
Good. You made it. \n\nSo, I've had some time to think. I know this may seem a little unorthodox but I want to go into the castle through the secret passage.

Look for the smaller void portals. With any luck, we can use these pockets of energy to access the library.\n\nJust don't lose your grip on that shard. And try to avoid the larger breaches. We don't want to get pulled into some nether realm.
Help me search. There used to be a concealed entrance around here. My clan used it long ago to bypass the Nord door and all its traps.
Rada has taken my research in directions I never imagined. Dwemer machines, Nighthollow rites, Reach witchcraft—all arrayed around that pedestal.
If Rada al-Saran's hidden a laboratory somewhere in the Library of Arkthzand, I'll find it. I've had plenty of practice locating hidden laboratories.
If Rada al-Saran's hiding around here somewhere, we need to find him. I just hope the bastard's home when we come knocking.

It's troubling to think Rada al-Saran may have been somewhere in this structure the entire time. Everything we've said and done in this chamber—he could have been privy to all of it.\n\nWe should proceed cautiously.
Did you see? Rada and Belain made some sort of deal centuries ago. And now the conditions of that deal have almost been fulfilled.\n\nWe can't let them fully awaken the Dark Heart!
See if you can find the journal you saw in Verandis's memory. It might contain the truth that I'm seeking.
Now's not the time! We need to stop Rada al-Saran!
Go ahead, Shaman Ulvoch will speak with you now.
I don't understand. The ritual … failed. I've never felt such darkness, such fury. How is this possible?
Check near the walls for a darkcap mushroom. While Adusa isn't familiar with this type, most fungal growths don't bloom out in the open.
The sentry granted you an audience with Ard Caddach? Then go and talk to the man. The sooner he agrees to cooperate with us, the sooner we can deal with the Gray Host.
A lot of Reachfolk died in the first rush. Now the Gray Host is bleeding Markarth dry with hit-and-run attacks. Don't think they expected Arana's rebels to be here, so that's something, at least.
You and Adusa shouldn't be down here. Boss Trenlor … he's not the sort of vampire who's quick to forgive and forget.
You look more or less the way Verandis described you. More or less.\n\nHe said he sent you to talk to the scrap dealer, and here you are! Amazing. Anyway, he wants to see you. Right now.

I've never seen Shaman Ulvoch so troubled. I don't blame him. Something is very wrong here. The ritual didn't just fail, it reacted in a way I've never seen before.\n\nThere has to be some kind of explanation.
I've no mind to rush you, harrier, but if you want to snatch up this keystone, you might want to hop to it.

I take it you received my message from Gwendis? Good. I could use your help.\n\nI've made some progress getting through to Arana, but she isn't completely ready to fully trust a vampire. She seems to like you, however. Talk to her, if you would.
Careful, now. Don't be tempted to eat that. You're not tempted, are you? Now, might I take a closer look at the specimen you gathered?

Farrul Lupus's agent—go-between, really—warned that others might be on their way here as well. People who wished to destroy the place and take the book for themselves.\n\nI hope whatever is burning doesn't mean they beat me here.
No sign of my father or uncle. We must keep going deeper.

I hope your journey to the shrine is a safe one, friend.\n\nWhen you write your message of remembrance, think of someone who has passed on. A friend, a foe, a hero. Perhaps even a poor soul who was lost and could not find peace.
This cave … I can feel it. This place was important. Sacred. \n\nTalk to Lyris while I look around.
