Ah, the Wounding. I named it so because a banekin caught me in the thigh with a spear the first time I explored the area. Never walked right after that. But I did make a fine necklace from the banekin ears I took as revenge.
We got here just in time to hear the very end of your conversation with the vateshran, partner. Want to fill me in on the parts we missed?
Thanks again for your help. I don't get a lot of chances to talk to people in my line of work—at least, people who aren't other Ravenwatch members. An outside perspective provided some clarity.
This is your fault, outsider. You have angered the spirits!

Eslyn and Madearn wait to the north, at the handfasting cave. We isolate them for a time so they can learn about one another. Hopefully, they haven't killed each other.\n\nGo and offer your blessing. Then return to me and your task will be done.
You dare interrupt one of our sacred ceremonies, outsider? If the chief-of-chiefs hadn't summoned you, we'd be doing more than talking right now.
The chief-of-chiefs wants to talk to you, not me.
An outsider, here? You are an affront to both the ancestors and the spirits. Away with you!
Why the chief-of-chiefs wants to involve an outsider in our affairs is beyond my understanding. It's bad enough we have to deal with the Eagleseers!\n\nRegardless, I have nothing to say to you.
I guess I was worried for nothing. It's the strangest thing, I felt such a strong need to be at Eslyn's side. Like something put a hook around my waist and yanked me all the way here.

I'm familiar with the old cairns in these hills. When the vateshran mentioned the coil fragment lay in Faolan's Ire, I knew it had to be here. The giant is a problem, I'll admit, but you've proved yourself quite capable. I'll wait here with Madearn.
Chief Eagleseer and Six-Ford are about as friendly as I remember.\n\nTalk to the chief-of-chiefs, outsider. Everything depends on what she decides, after all.

Forgive me, wanderer. I would offer you sanctuary under the watchful eyes of Hircine, but this shrine remains sadly incomplete.\n\nMy apprentices should return shortly with the sacred relics we need to dedicate the shrine to the Hunt-Father.
Simply find the correct spot to make the duplicate wait, then get the vine-tongue to pull him across.\n\nAnd yes, it does sound a tad ridiculous when I say it out loud.
Let's hope Sombren knows what he's doing. If we get this wrong now, Mehrunes Dagon gobbles us all up like so many spice bugs. And all of Tamriel, too.\n\nI don't want to be a spice bug.
I do not relish leaving Gideon so lightly defended, but this is the best way to safeguard the Ambitions. If we fail to protect them, then what happens here will not matter much.
I'll meet you at Leyawiin Castle. We can talk to Councilor Lovidicus together.

The amulet should allow you to remove the ward so we may enter the concealed annex. I had it specifically constructed just for this purpose, but it will only function for a mortal.\n\nHurry now. I haven't got all day.
That directory should lead us to the holdings of the three prominent trade-ministers. We'll need their sigils to open the sealed adytum.

I erect the spine of fear, formidable stranger. I need your help. \n\nThe Sul-Xan captured me and my friends in order to use us for a cruel ritual. I managed to escape, but my friends remain inside. I intend to go back and rescue them.
Quickly, Councilor Lovidicus is in the chamber just ahead. Show him what you uncovered and let him decide how best to proceed.
Everything we do now must be swift if we are to get ahead of this. Go to Fort Blueblood and convince Councilor Abor to return to the city. She'll be safer here than at the fort.
Relying on mortals time and again feels so … demeaning. How is it that I can hold so much power and yet still find myself stymied? One of the great mysteries.
Don't look at me. I don't know what I did! But the ward's gone so you might as well see what's inside the cache.\n\nMe? I'm going to keep an eye on the Daedra-lady over there.
The Daughter of Sithis? The Fane of Scorn?\n\nI don't believe it. Quistley's fallen in with … with … death-worshipers?
Wait—I remember you! Of all the places in Tamriel for Lady Twilight to bump into her erstwhile deputy, it's in an arse-aired sewer beneath some crumbling garrison!

I know there's an Ayleid ruin beneath Borderwatch, but I don't know how to access it. \n\nThat scholar the Painted Eye is interrogating—we need to find out where he's being held and ask a few questions of our own.

Hmm. The armor, helm, and sword are all badly damaged. Skeptics might say these could have belonged to anybody. We need to find <<1>> to settle the question for good!\n\nBut where is the horn? Why isn't it here?

I wish I could help, but I've already walked this path. I can't walk it again. This is something Destron and Calia have to do on their own, but I'm glad you'll be there to help them.\n\nBe safe and finish quickly. We haven't a moment to waste.
I hope this attunement process isn't too painful.
So these are the Deadlands? I admit, I'd feel a lot better if I learned how to use our powers before I came to a place like this. I feel like we're going about this in the wrong order.

Tiras is trying to resist the pull of the clouded varla stones, but his strength is waning. Luckily he's running into these smaller stone clusters. Sort of like falling out of a tree and hitting all the branches on the way down.
I stumbled headlong into a bad situation once already. I do try to learn from my mistakes.\n\nI've been thinking. There's a good chance we won't find Quistley Silvelle alive.
Revus's little art project is well in hand, hmm? Well, by all means, deliver the good news.

Destron and Calia, the twins. They're the Ambitions! Well, at least they're two of them.\n\nI have to say, I did not expect the weapons to be people! Whatever, Vandacia and his cult still want to get their hands on them.

Huh? Oh, sorry. Was just listening to our new tree friend. And a Hist tree at that! Been wanting to talk to one for ages.\n\nIt says thanks by the way. Well, it doesn't really say anything. But I get the impression it's right grateful you saved it!
Mathen's still here. I don't understand. You should talk to him.
There you are, little mortal! It seems we once again find ourselves on the trail of the same mystery.\n\nI expect we can aid one another in the events that are about to unfold.
This light … it offers some respite from my sorrows. You have my thanks.\n\nI am Mathen Galenus, heir to the Duchy of Giovesse. What brings you to this place?
Wasn't that small shrine to Hermaeus Mora off that direction? I'd wager that's where Cres is headed.

Look for impressive pools of water. Pools that seem appropriately penitent. I think if we bathe Deet-Loh in at least three such pools, the Nereid will see he's sorry and lift her curse.\n\nJust watch out. This place is crawling with creatures.

Governor Keshu locked the prisoner in the holding cell in the courthouse basement. Question the villain and find out why the Dark Brotherhood is trying to wipe out anyone who was part of the Imperial Elder Council.\n\nI'll head for Leyawiin afterward.

We should get a move on. The Councilors are safe for the moment, but all this Ambitions nonsense seems a little time sensitive. If it is the Dark Brotherhood, we don't want them getting their hands on Daedric artifacts. \n\nLet's get to Bloodrun Cave.

Dibella's sacred buttocks! Am I glad to see someone that's not a part of this tribe. Maybe you can do something. \n\nI've tried telling these lizards that my soldiers have nothing to do with their disappearing people, but they won't listen!

I think I understand. These totems … the dye was used to paint runes upon them, which must have activated their latent magic. \n\nBut those runes are only known to this tribe. The Imperials could not have done this. It had to be one of our own.

Sometimes listening provides the answers we seek. It seems their high priest is actually one of your councilors. That explains how they knew your movements. And they found whatever they were looking for in the sanctuary.

Now you look like someone who knows what the Jester Festival is really about. I can spot a true prankster just by the way they walk. And you, my friend, I saw coming from very far away!\n\nWhat do you say? Are you up for a little mischief?
So, you're the one's been asking questions about the people who've gone missing, then come back wrong?
We've come this far. We have to find Liam. We have to.

We need to find the caches before the cultists steal everything out from under us.\n\nI want to know what was so important that Farrul Lupus had to die. And what any of this has to do with the book I'm still carrying.
I don't know why, but skyshards tend to fall in inconvenient places. Just one of Tamriel's cruel jokes.\n\nLet's snatch it up quick.
Sul-Xan break with the ways that I have always held dear. They offer no tail for peace to any of their kind. Only blood and poisons.

Look there! The carriage.\n\nI heard the water out here's been drying up for years. It would have been deeper a decade ago. Black Marsh is like that. It must have been hidden beneath the surface! Let's have a look around.

That must be Count Auzin. I confess that I've got a pit in my stomach over all of these … these family matters.\n\nHuh. Is it just me, or does he look upset about something? I wonder if I'm catching him at a bad time.
Now that you have the creature, all you need to do is release it toward me and concentrate your own energy. I will do the rest.
Looks like trying to solve that puzzle box took its toll on Onimiril. Why were he and my grandfather so enamored with this thing?

Find Melyn Drad at the Egg and Hammer Inn. See if you can get him talking. We need to know what he discussed with Xocin.\n\nI can't imagine what Xocin would need to hide from the Black Fin Legion. This sudden secrecy isn't like him. Not at all.

Thanks for your help. Word of advice? Step lightly around the Dark Elf when you speak with him. He scares easy. I think he soiled his robes when I first asked him about Xocin.\n\nTee-Wan says that's my fault, though I do not see how.
Friend of my daughters? Or maybe … well, you look nice. We'll get properly introduced after I'm out of these shackles.

This house belonged to the keep's seneschal it seems. There would have been no one with more knowledge of its affairs, except perhaps the knight-commander.\n\nBuy us some time to look over these records.
That's a Daedra the likes of which I've never seen, or even heard of, in my time at the Battlespire. Its corpse still pulses with the same energy as within these stones. They are connected.

Weylin knows the affairs of these people better than I, so when it comes to the merits of digging through this wreckage, I suppose I'll give him the benefit of the doubt.\n\nIf I deem it a waste of time, I'll be sure to drag him along.

Do not delay. The Crowborne Horror must be defeated or it will inflict its destruction upon Nirn.\n\nGather the cursed feathers to form the effigy. If you are clever, you will have no trouble finding them. And I have no doubt of your fighting prowess.

Something is not right with this place, and I'm not just talking about the Daedra. All these vile energies aren't some byproduct of their presence. The Dread Cellar is the source of them.\n\nHow did this place become so steeped in corruption?
There's no telling what's going to happen once we enter Dagon's city. I just hope I'm ready when the time comes.
So that's the Anchorite, huh? Neat mask. I hope she's all right with this.\n\nYou better follow this Madam Whim's instructions and start the ritual.

Madam Whim has agreed to try to untangle the Anchorite's restored memories. Since we have no leads on the Fourth Ambition or where to look for Sombren and Calia, we must resort to this.\n\nLet us get on with it, mortal. Stop wasting time talking to me.
Get in. I want you to go first. Make sure that you don't try to back out on me. Plus, who knows what's waiting for us on the other side.
Time is short and we have much to do, little mortal.
We need to free whoever is trapped inside that metal. Let's find a way to ignite that furnace.

The secrets I seek rest with Sister Celdina. She still has the means to create more cataclysts, so the danger to Fargrave and Nirn remains.\n\nWe must ascertain the location of Deadlight and this hidden stronghold the Bladebearers heard mentioned.
I—I—you're right. Ordinator Nilera and grandmother Sovisa would never leave the helpless to suffer. \n\nI can do this. Let's free them. Quickly.
Don't worry, my friend. I won't fail you. The memories remain distant, confusing, but I won't let them get in my way. I'll help you find Sister Celdina and put an end to the Waking Flame. I swear it.
Rynkyus dislikes mortals and isn't thrilled to see me. No matter. He has a keen mind. He will see the benefit of sharing information. Talk to him and tell him what we found in Burning Gyre Keep.
What more advice do you require from me, master? Pour out a libation for the old lunatic, and be done with it.
If that … daedrat … is Arox the Mutilator, then I am a two-headed Scamp. Was that in your backpack all along?\n\nWhatever it is, it wants to talk to you.

Faven holds power in Wretched Spire. Too much. His word could convince other mortals to attack Daedra. Try to force us out. They will fail. And die.\n\nSpeak with him. Learn about what he and Tephilaz talked about. Calm him down.

Let's meet at Doomvault Vulpinaz. You can get back to Nirn through the Plaza of Portals in Fargrave if you want. If the egonymic is in that doomvault, you and I will definitely find it!\n\nBring that ring and the map with you. We might need them.
Try pouring the green elixir on the braziers. I'm sure it's the right one. I think.
A new person in Wretched Spire. Seems we grow all the time. Who knew a town in the Deadlands could attract so many people?
Thank you for freeing me again, mortal master. I shall shred the ankles of your foes once more, claw out their eyes and snip at their hair. Whatever you ask of me!
So this is Nirn? I don't remember ever walking upon this strange world, but the sky … it seems familiar, somehow.\n\nLet's look around and see if the cataclyst and the Bladebearers are here.
Do enjoy the many pleasures available here in the House of Whims. I have gone to great lengths to make my offerings truly unique.
Go on, step through the portal. I shall be right behind you.
I do not trust open portals. Especially those of my enemies. Speak with Lyranth and see how she wants to proceed.
As much as I can't wait to meet a talking daedrat, I better help Lyranth gather allies. I'll see you when we meet at Wretched Spire.\n\nGood luck. And be careful!
Champion. As promised, the Bladebearer clan will fight by your side.

I assume that's Lyranth the Dremora. Which is why our hands are glowing again, I guess.\n\nYou talk to her. Find out why she didn't wait for us at the original meeting site. And see if she knows any more about the votive runes.

Even a Dremora of my talents cannot hope to stand alone against the Dagonists and an army of living disasters. I seek to learn Sister Celdina's secrets. You want to protect the mortal realm from total destruction.\n\nTogether, we can accomplish both.
I know I said I was going to help with the negotiations, but … look, I don't want to talk about it.
I find you more interesting than other mortals, but not so much that I want to talk to you constantly. Don't you have something better to do?
We will find the right elixir, never fear. Although… there are so many things in here.

I'll have the Purgator's summoning spell updated shortly. You'll be able to call upon it at similar stones placed strategically throughout the prison.\n\nWe can do the same with the other guardians once you restore their magical matrices.
Ah. I expect this is you posturing for payment. Very well, you have done me a service, I'll repay you.
You are still here? Did you not understand your task?
Is it common for you silly mortals to loiter when a superior has given you a task? No wonder your lives are so short. Be off!
I'll let you take the lead here. My history with Skrix will only complicate matters.\n\nLearn what you can. Just remember that he's far from trustworthy.

I'm guessing, since you're sailing up to this secluded cove in that little dinghy instead of the main entrance, you aren't part of the Ascendant Order.\n\nI won't ask your business here, but helping me with mine could turn you a tidy profit.

Zha'al! You are a ray of moonlight piercing this fog! Surely you remember the handsome rascal, Za'ji? He remembers you! And your daring-do! He could use some of that right now.\n\nWhat say you, join Za'ji for some treasure hunting? For old times' sake?
You with the Ash-Elf, Fyr? Got no business with you. Got no business with him. Better scuttle off. Stomp you, otherwise. And peel you off the boot flat.
It appears we were seeking not a what but a who. Release the daedrat. Determine if it can actually help us decipher the coded message.
Hyxo does not seem the talkative type. Careful. If you anger him there's not much I can do to help you like this.
I do so enjoy dealing with mortals. Despite their short, meaningless lives, they can be quite fascinating.

I don't know what to make of that. Quentyn is clever enough to feign an interest in joining them, but that didn't feel like an act. He lost his wife in the war, and he never got over that.\n\nStill, we can't leave him here with those terrorists.

Ah. A visitor? Or another one of Lady Arabelle's associates? Either way, welcome to our island.\n\nBacaro Volorus, founder of the Society of the Steadfast, at your service. I hope you find your visit to High Isle restful and profitable.

I owe you a debt of gratitude for coming to my aid. It seems once again that Lady Arabelle chose well. \n\nNow to see if I can find Guild General Quentyn, and by extension, the rogue knights who carried him away.

The speed and discretion with which you work … Zenithar be praised! \n\nI'll prepare the wood for weaving, but I won't be able to continue without the blessed awl. Those lamentable Greycloaks have it, yet again.

Oh, good! A kind face. I have tried, time and again, to ask politely for my friend's safe return. But they rudely mock me in response.\n\nWould you help me retrieve Privette? They took her away into Breakwater Cave. Didn't even ask my permission!
About those medallions you recovered, my dear. May I have them now?
Well done, well done. Let's get out of this dreary place.
Any luck finding the catacombs key?
Recovering the invitation medallions was only the beginning. my friend. Talk to Lady Arabelle. I'm sure she has another use for your impressive abilities.

Hey there, good-looking. The name's Jakarn. Glad you're here—I'm more of a lover than a fighter. Guess I'm not the only one paying off a debt to Lady Arabelle.\n\nOr did you actually volunteer for all this excitement?
Arkay's ashes, I never expected to cross paths with a real ghost. Let alone my own ancestor. I—I don't know what to say! You talk to her.

If you came to judge my raft too, I don't want to hear it. I only need to get to Whalefall and back. \n\nI know the waters are dangerous, but my partner Anton got selected for the game there. He's not the type who can survive it.

If I were the alliance leaders, I'd take my chances with the sharks. Anything to avoid Amenos. \n\nAh, well. Let's get on with this before I come to my senses. When we get there, I'll investigate the stockade and town. That leaves the jungle for you.
This hero business is sort of growing on me. I think it suits me, don't you?\n\nDon't answer that. Just let me have this.
Good luck, challenger. I'm really hoping you'll pull through.
The Runel family line, while not as illustrious as some, is certainly a name that is well known. \n\nIf you haven't heard of it, that is a you problem. Not a me problem.
You're back! And alone, I see.\n\nI was afraid of something like this. You'd better speak with Lord Bacaro and let him know what happened to his retainers. He's been anxiously awaiting your return.

It kind of goes against my nature to tell anyone to hurry up, but Lady Arabelle made it sound like she was anxious to get started. And there's the whole thing about the missing royals and all.\n\nHead over to Mandrake Manor as soon as you can.

The spirit wants us to enter the Undergrove and release its bindings. It claims that will allow it to overcome the Allwither.\n\nI sensed no duplicity while we were connected. I believe the Evergrowth spoke true of its intentions.
Let's head inside. There we can finish the creation of this macabre weapon and ready ourselves for the final confrontation. \n\nHuh, Madach was right. This will make a good story.

I have good news and bad news. The good news is that I've nearly finished my counterspell. But I need to find a tome called The Mirrored Way to complete it. I know Magister Irin has it, but it's not with the rest of his books. That's the bad news.
Don't worry about me. If I could survive the politics of Summerset, I can handle an inhospitable island.\n\nI'll retrieve Caska and we'll meet up with you in a bit.
Remember, we're here to find Prince Irnskar.
The King's Arrow? Is that really you, my friend? Where you fly, victory is sure to follow. But what are you doing here? How did you find me?

I met the Ascendant Magus, dear. He was smug and annoying, and definitely a noble. But his helm disguised his voice.\n\nI thought I was fine when he only left four knights to guard me, but then two more arrived. If you hadn't drawn them away ….
Just who I was looking for. Lady Arabelle wants you back at Mandrake Manor.\n\nAnd yes, you guessed it. She has another task that requires our precise expertise.

You look healthy. Walking about on your own, no shadows in your eyes. You're better off than most of the patients here, which means you're just who I need.\n\nOur patients have fallen prey to a strange malady. We could use some help.

Hello, my friend. You're just in time. I met Ryvana here just as she was starting to look into an arcane disturbance.\n\nIt can't be a coincidence we're so close to one of the Ascendant Order sites marked on the duchess's map.
The forests of High Isle hide many ancient secrets. Some are perhaps better forgotten. Go in peace, traveler.
The Ascendant Magus! If he's smug enough to stand there and gloat over us, go ahead and let him run his mouth. Maybe we'll learn something.

Fine, fine! I'll gather my own damned tack. Been doing it for years, why stop now?\n\nWhat I won't do is go trawling for my pack! I lost it in that big wreck down there while running from some Sea Elves. Find my pack, then we'll cut down the cat.
Let's make our way to this cove. Just keep a sharp eye for those dungy Sea Elves!
This is very embarrassing.
A note from a healer? That could be important. Perhaps it is a clue as to what ails poor <<1>> there.\n\nRead it, friend.
You heard <<1>>. Find this skooma dealer and trail him to wherever he keeps his illicit goods. He'll free me if you can help him bring in the real criminal.\n\nPlease! You've got to help me!
There should be a vial of my blood in Viralaine's laboratory. It's just through the doorway.
The song's done. Phew. That took more out of me than I was expecting.\n\nTalk to Yvelle there. See how she's feeling.
That hammer and chisel are the key to our escape, my friend! I always carry around the proper tools. You never know what might come in handy.
Welcome back, my dear. I take it Jakarn found you, then? Good.\n\nAs our handsome rogue no doubt informed you, I have one more favor to ask before I release you from my service.
The Ascendant Order thinks they've won. But we aren't out of the fight yet.
Just point me to the fight. I'm anxious to get my claws into the Ascendant Order for what they did to the Perfect Pounce. And maybe my fangs, as well.
You found something, what does it say? Is there anything in there about Song?
This one thinks about food great deal since being freed. A nice cheese pie would be lovely right now.

You read my journal, so now you know all my sordid secrets. Like how this was all my fault, and I'm the one that got my friends taken away. Did you come here to shame me? Well you're too late. You can't say anything I haven't already told myself.
Oh no. What now? You'd better talk to him.
I know, I know. It's a bit unusual. But I wouldn't have come all this way out here if I didn't think there was something to Aurelia's story. This business is worth looking into, I think.
Unless we've got business, I've got no more time to talk. I'm not a rich man and I got work to do.

I don't have a potion or tonic that can help me find my common sense. I'm going to be mad at myself for a long time over falling for his … style.\n\nI do have some things that could make Kiv Lindres feel pretty uncomfortable for a while though.
Is that my scrumptious little turtle dove I see? Arrgh!

The ancient sea captain thinks you're Baron-Admiral Bendu Olo. Talk to him. Er, her. Whoever. And, and see if you can get them to reveal their name. Or at least find out if the Pristine Halberd was his ship.
Is there something you need? This is a rather difficult time.
Did my love say we were to meet by the big tree? I remember … something, but everything seems caught in a fog.
I just know that Marso and I can find something. We just have to spend a bit more time together in Rivenspire.
Be careful out there, walker. And tell the queen I'll be all right. She's much too important to worry about a few cuts and scratches. I'll be fine. After I lie down for a bit.
I trust Isobel is doing well?
Remember, we're here to find Prince Irnskar.
Poor Varnauld. After losing to you, he could barely bring himself to shuffle his cards. He blubbered the whole time. It was like playing a toddler!\n\nI'd say you're just what this chapter needed!

I am glad you returned, my friend. I have exciting news from the Roister's Club! Several club chapters are preparing for a series of tournaments—ours included.\n\nThe initial matches are a ways off, so we should use that time to prepare.
Kishka has nothing to offer you right now, walker. Come back later, though, yes? This one may have a challenge for you.
Sooner we knock that smug grin off Varnauld's face, the better! Let's get to it!

We do not have much time before your final opponents arrive. You should find Sorinne and Brahgas in town and wish them good luck.\n\nBrahgas could be anywhere, but Sorinne often visits the statue of Kynareth before big matches. Check there first.
I knew you'd make it! Well, I didn't know, but I certainly hoped!

You always catch me at my best, don't you? Look, this was just … just a little disagreement about a side bet. It's nothing. Or it soon will be.\n\nWith how well I've been playing, not even Razhamad could beat me! This tournament is in the bag.
My informants tell me the rank and file of the Gray Host shudder, as tales of a mortal hunter swirl through their midst.\n\nYou have done well. You have delivered them fear.

Praise Tava's breath. She had one more adventure to offer me.\n\nSo! See the cliffs at the island center? We'll split up to survey them. You take north, I'll head east. Keep watch for anything that could summon that storm. Or anything … druidy.

The Firesong have been here, those poisonous thorns. I don't blame the wyress for being cautious. The distinction between myself and them might not be so obvious to these wyrds. \n\nCould you speak with her? Try to convince her we're here to help?
They raised their hackles as soon as they spotted Druid Laurel. Got a feeling the Firesong already made an appearance. Maybe you can talk to the wyress? Get her to trust us somehow?

Guess this makes you my contractor now. Finally, I'm not the lowliest employee.\n\nWe'll meet inside and I'll point you toward the crystals. I think shattering them will stop the fissures from expanding. Then I can finish my survey and get paid.
Oh, it feels good to be out of that cell! I heard quite a commotion earlier. Something about heads and traitors and kings. Was that your work?
Dhulef tells me you played no small part in repelling the Dreadsails and foiling an attack on the druid council, mercenary.\n\nHas the Firesong Circle truly made an alliance with the hated Sea Elves?

I told Count Mornard about the attack at the Draoife. I'm not sure he entirely believes me. The Firesong allying with Sea Elves against other druids? It's unheard of.\n\nBetter tell him what you saw, mate.
Root and rot! That was Archdruid Orlaith, leader of the Firesong Circle. I think I know what really happened here, and I don't like it at all!
This isn't what I was expecting. Lord Bacaro, a traitor? Well, now that we know, let's go find him and show him what happens to liars and murderers.

Za'ji's newest Perfect Pounce is the most perfect Pounce yet! This one promises to get Lady Arabelle to Galen without alerting Bacaro or his Ascendant Order. Za'ji is good at being quiet, like a shadow he is—no matter what Caska might tell you.
Please find Lady Arabelle. She still isn't fully recovered from the effects of that poison.

Go on. I'll meet you at Steadfast Manor after I get the antidote started. It will need time to steep before it's ready to administer to Lady Arabelle. I gave Za'ji and Caska enough of my tincture to keep her stable until we can get back to the city.
Somewhere nearby will be the entrance to the high-stakes suite. \n\nLet's stay alert. It could be anywhere.
The Elsweyr Defense Force will be this one's greatest accomplishment. It will save lives for years to come. Hopefully.
Laurel is alive! Quickly, my friend, release her!
That scow alongside is in our way. Get over to her deck and use one of their outboard ballistas. Stop that Firesong warship from bombarding us!

The elder foresaw this day, when I would be drawn to his song. And that I would not be alone.\n\nThis elixir. It is the same as a potion the wyrds used to commune with me while I slumbered. It connects the now to the then. The here to the there.
Oh, hello! Are you here from the summons? You look rather strong. Ha, I knew the posting would be worth it!\n\nPlease, speak with Captain Samara if you wish to lend your aid to Elsweyr's people.
Then those imposters must have been looking for the Druid King's crown. Come, we need to check the library at once!\n\nAnd later I want to hear more about your accusations concerning Lord Bacaro.

Druid Fenas? He's not here. He's back at Fauns' Thicket. But how come the tree didn't curse you? If I took some sap, it would have blasted me six ways to Sundas!\n\nSundas? Is it Sundas already? I thought it was still Midyear.

The druid told him. Or maybe he can sense it with his new glowing ball of light abilities. I don't know! All I know is you should hurry to the north and find him.\n\nHe shouldn't be left alone for too long.

Lord Bacaro's going to Y'ffelon. There, he will attempt to use the Druid King's regalia to awaken the spirit that slumbers beneath Mount Firesong. We need to warn Stefan and reach the island before that happens.

As soon as I explained what happened, Lady Arabelle and her companions went after Bacaro. I told them we saw him leading Frii toward Y'ffre's Path.\n\nI stayed behind to tend to the wounded, but this smacks of the Green Scourge! I'll go with you.

A storm is gathering, friend. Thanks to you, I'm here to meet it instead of languishing in a Dreadsail cell. And we managed to save Druid Niraya and secure the Eldertide seed. You have proven your worth yet again.

Now don't be alarmed, dear, but I happened to step where I shouldn't have. I suppose I owe Druid Ryvana an apology. The lingering effects of the poison do seem to have made me somewhat discombobulated.
Somewhere in these caves we'll find the relic. Just keep your head down and your ears open. We'll be gone soon enough.\n\nIf you spot Umindior, let me know. I guess.
Y'ffre's rain worked as well as I hoped on the bloated muse-mouth plants. Let's keep going. I want to find my wife.
The Dreadsails have much to answer for. They overpowered me once. I won't give them a chance to do it again.

So those two activated the relic with their little romp? I suppose that explains the Sea Elves' more lusty behavior. And here I thought it was me.\n\nI can release them if you go find the druid chamber. Let's hope no one moved it.
The more time I spend on land, the more entwined I become in the affairs of Galen. Things are a lot less complicated on the open sea.
Neither the Firesong or their allies will get the best of the Stonelore Druids. I promise you that.

Blight! I saw a group of Dreadsails and Firesong enter the cave just as I arrived. Not sure if they spotted Frii or simply got curious, but this isn't good.\n\nWe need to get in there. Frii and the seed are in danger!

The day I hoped to avert is upon us. A hunger for power will destroy everything we hoped to build here in the archipelago. Now druids slay druids, fighting over a throne like the very Elves we left behind on the mainland.\n\nI must end this.
Stay focused and be on guard. The Firesong I saw could be anywhere in here.
I won't spoil the answer if you want to figure it out for yourself, but I think I know exactly where the final riddle is leading!
Go. We'll meet you inside. \n\nJust clear a path for us. I don't think either Joslin or Octin will be any help if I need to defend them from something.
We're aboard my ship and I have my crew. What about the harbor chain? If it's still in place, this will be a very short trip.

Why won't they listen? They must know the danger they're in.\n\nAnd you—have we met before? No, I would remember. But, those Dark Elves recognized us. You heard them call us the Scourge. This confirms my fears.

I was out fighting when the cathedral collapsed. I've never heard such a sound … and the quiet that came after, it was like drowning. \n\nSo many druids lost their lives. And the archdruids, they didn't deserve this. Tava's breath, what a mess.
I thought the storm had passed once Sealord Nalos and the Dreadsails were beaten. Seems like Archdruid Orlaith and the Firesong Circle have other ideas, though.

Dame Fayda … intrigues me. Oh, we've smiled and said hello in the Vine District, of course, but we've never had an opportunity for such long and lively conversation before.\n\nI find her outlook on life to be most … refreshing.
I shall meet you at the camp. I want to make sure Mildanor is taken care of. Then I need to do a little more work to decipher the coded letter.\n\nTravel safely, proxy.

Nobody saw me. How could the Lark have known? He has the talisman. The real talisman. \n\nI made a replica of the original, switched it out without the high priest knowing. Then, I hid the real one down here to keep it safe.
Rest and be welcome, walker.

If you're here to bask in the presence of the Talisman of Saint Vorys, I humbly ask that you do so out of arm's reach!\n\nIf you have any questions about the relic's history, I'd be more than happy to answer them.

That's everything I needed to conduct my audit, though it doesn't take a professional to know the mine is in a disastrous state. Let's get out of here and meet up with Ulfengar and the others outside.
Apostle Nilphas Drethan's threat is neutralized. Quickly to the Probabilis, we must return it to a dormant state.

The threads of fate lead to three locations in this region. The Necropolis of Necrom, the old tower of Tel Rendys, and the town of Alavelis. I shall open a portal to each. Investigate them and return here to the Necrom Bindery when you are done.

Are you surprised to find someone of my immense renown sitting here, weary and injured? And on Nirn of all places? \n\nThere will be no show this day, no spectacle for entertainment. Not with my escaped lesser Daedra roaming free.

This must be where the keepers are being held. Why else would the chapel door be locked?\n\nI read somewhere that adventurers can pick locks. Is that true? If not, Curate Zankan sometimes leaves his key on a shelf in the far corner of this hall.
First, place the spyglass and key. They will be core components to accessing the energy stored in the book.
How is this possible?

Mother absolutely loved reading us snippets from this book when we were young! She would even have us read out the important speeches and quotes to really get into character.\n\nThat was a long time ago, though.

Leramil is a remarkable woman. So intelligent and vibrant. But she won't tell me anything. She says we had to wait for you to return.\n\nTalk to her, friend. Put in a good word for me and see if you can get her to tell me what this is all about.
Very good! Yes! There are only three books, an easy enough task for someone of your stature! Please, follow me!
Go ahead and trace the sigil. Unfortunately I cannot do it for you.
Quickly, walker, reset the focus! Mora willing, it will quiet these poor vessels!

In the right hands, an enchanted lens can reveal things hidden to the naked eye. I suspect Meln's wards prevent the device from functioning for Master Shelreni's minions. But it may work for us.\n\nTry it, proxy.
The more time we spend together, proxy, the more I understand why the One Who Knows specifically selected you.
You talk to Mevei. She's just as much a stranger to me as she is to you. You seem better at that sort of thing, anyway.
Tread carefully in this hallowed place. Forbidden knowledge and secrets of this magnitude are fraught with peril.

Stupid Ogle, stupid! Master keeps the most dangerous fates down here. Of course it would be difficult to navigate. Numerous paths, endless options. This was a hopeless endeavor from the start. \n\nI'm a useless Watchling who deserves to be unwoven!

Ah, we meet again, just as I intended. Not because of your bumbling about the planes.\n\nYou're just in time to help me. I know where the fated glyphic is, so there's no need for that silly boon. Besides, you look ridiculous.
Oh the terrible burdens that bring tears to the many eyes of the Abyssal Cephaliarch. Place them in the pool, mortal.

The scribes are my entire life. If I wasn't exploring some new place in Oblivion and bringing new records into the hall, I don't know what I'd do!\n\nValinna … her heart is in a good place, but interfering? That's not our way.
What did you find? Anything that explains what's happened?
Keep your distance, stranger. I am unwell.
So, she keeps her freedom. And she'll aid me in finding a cure, so long as her heart remains anchored to Tel Dreloth.

While you go to Tel Rendys to create Meln's enchantment, I'll head to Ald Isra and make sure we're on the list to attend the conclave. Find me inside Tel Huulen when you're ready to proceed. In the meantime, I'll try to learn more about Shelreni.
I don't recommend being dead. So many of my memories have become tattered and frayed. Still, I remember enough. When we get close to a spot I recognize, I'll make my ghost sight available to you.

I'd been wondering how I could possibly continue my wife's work. I'm just a document forger. I'm not strong like she was.\n\nBut you and Sharp finding me here feels like a sign. Like Reynila showing me the way. And I don't have to go forward alone.
I hope you found everything I'm looking for. The sooner I can leave this place behind, the better.
Smell that? Just like the jar of musk but a thousand times worse.\n\nSearch around. We know the message exchanges happen somewhere around here. Just watch out for Dres agents and angry kagouti.
After so many years, Hezehk feels uncertain about this. Do I still have the skill? What if it turns me inside-out? Or I fall through a portal into the lap of a Havocrel?
This place is a dangerous, winding maze. We could get killed just searching for the secret entrance.\n\nLet's use a tracking spell to help us find it.
So, after you fished these clothes out of the latrine that you found them in, what'd you do? Dry them over a bonfire of mammoth fur?\n\nThe style I'll just have to work with. But the smell ….

I couldn't help overhear. I think it's excellent that Naryu selected you to assist her in this matter. More hands means we can get back to the usual business of the assembly that much faster.\n\nAnd by usual business, I mean I can return to my tower.
This one doesn't sense Ansuul here either. That's good. Without her influencing his mind, Vanton should recover quickly.
Look, see those markings? They indicate that this ancient ruin was dedicated to Vaermina, the Daedric Prince of Dreams and Nightmares. We should proceed with caution.
We must move quickly, cohort. Let's make our way to the back of the cave. \n\nJust … ugh. Forgive me if I fight with my eyes closed. Can't stand the spiders down here.

Martina's research lives on. I believe, with further development, I can adapt her methods and modify the Fateweaver Key itself.\n\nBut let's crawl before we walk. First, we confirm if scrying for frayed fates is even possible.
She's leaking like a broken cup. But where is the chip? We can't put her back together without it. Frielvi—she can't be bleeding now. This is a crisis! We need her.
I will tell you everything. Of my relationship to the Daedric Prince. Of what I did to save my son.
I've done what I can. Talk to her and see if you can convince her that she hates her betrayers more than she despises us.
What did you do, mortal? The screams of Apocrypha are like needles in my eyes!
Ready, mortal? Just touch the Eye of Mora and we'll slip into the memory it contains. Just like daedmites hopping from one clannfear to another.\n\nAnd yes, we're the daedmites.

Torvesard has departed, but not before he indicated what we need to do.\n\nWhile Scruut and Gadayn handle the corruption manufactory to the west, let us find the one to the east and destroy the crystal that tethers it to this realm.
Ah, excellent! Yes, I see you've found the remaining ingredients. Knew you could do it. Knew you could! Give them to me, if you please. Everything else is prepared.

When I embarked on this quest with you, I never expected to be working alongside Daedra—let alone be marching into the very heart of Apocrypha.\n\nI admit I'm afraid, but I'll stand by you. By you and Leramil both. You have my word.
Why are you talking to me? Do I look like I dabble in forbidden secrets and the mysteries of the universe? Well, sure, but not nearly as intensely as Leramil! Go see what she has to say.
Flee, mortal. The pain overwhelms me. Soon I won't be able to tell friend from foe.\n\nAnd my many beguiling eyes … each blinks out and goes dark in turn. Soon I'll be totally … blind!
The Numinous Grimoire is a very dangerous book. I'd better take custody of it, traveler. I'll make sure it's kept under lock and key from now on.
I really should return the Fulcrum Obscura to Necrom, but I also promised to see this through. I'll do whatever I can to assist.

Scruut can tell you all about the process for inscribing her records in the Chronicle of Apocrypha. You should talk with her.\n\nMeanwhile, I shall discuss arrangements for returning to Necrom with Curate Gadayn.

I cannot believe the lax state of security around here. Who allowed you to approach me? Are the sentries all asleep again? \n\nMake no mistake, I will speak to someone about reprimanding the lot of them.
We took every precaution before breaking into Apocrypha's vaults. I thought we were being so careful.\n\nSpeak with my sister. I need a moment to think.
How lucky you are to witness my family's century-defining triumph. If you're looking for a role in a powerful Dunmeri house, now's your chance. Speak with my father.

There could be copies of Tho'at Replicanum in the archive. Which feels predictably unfair right now. You can fight multiple maligraphies, but I can barely research the one.\n\nNo matter, we're so close to retrieving all the nymic fragments.
I have my misgivings, but Master Faras is determined to conduct his ritual now. Who am I to stop him?

I'm staying. Malkhest can stand as close to the door as he wants, but not me. You're a mortal. I suppose you're going to want to go walk to him and see what he's doing. But I'll tell you, he's risking the only life he has.
That Daedric monster does not belong in the Mythos. Somehow Ithelia's influence is leaking into Mora's realm. Dispatch it, proxy—there is no time to waste!
I see you and our allies have returned safely with a fragment of the Mirrormoor titan … but where is Curate Gadayn?

I've been doing my best to keep morale up while you were gone, but even my usually cheerful mood is under assault. More and more of those tears in reality keep appearing. We're running out of time!\n\nDid you learn anything useful at the Loom?

Legionary Caepio made it this far. We need to trust that he can continue to evade the enemy for a while longer.\n\nLet's find these ruins he spotted down below and find a way to deal with that portal.
No one respects Orc sites, not even in our own lands. Well, it's a good thing I'm here to deal Malacath's revenge.
I came … as fast as I could. Scruut's trinket got me from Apocrypha to Nirn, but it deposited me some distance from this location.\n\nAnd I meant what I said. I want to help, anyway I can.
I'm ready to set out for these ruins whenever you are, friend.
Go ahead and scout the path to the laboratory. I'll make sure these three get to safety, then follow right behind you.
A door hidden by a waterfall, just as that fellow Endegor said. We'll need to be careful. Anybody we meet from here on in is likely to be Recollection.

Many lives were lost despite our best efforts. There is certainly joy to be found in our success, but this one will spend many a night wondering if there was more that could be done. Perhaps he is not as good an investigator as he thought.
I would never do anything like this. You must believe me.
While you speak with the family members, Mizzik will observe with his keen senses and fine-tuned whiskers. No deception, however small, will escape this one.
Let us enter Ithelia's prison and finish this once and for all. Use the portal.
Who's that vampire you came in with? He looks so familiar.
I don't know how I can help you against such a fearsome foe. But I will do my best, friend.

She hasn't moved once since you left. I tried talking to her, but she only muttered quietly to herself. I'd almost feel bad for her if I wasn't losing sales.\n\nDid you find that book on obscure drinks?

I was under the impression <<1>> worked alone. But I'm sure it can't hurt to have another bright mind on the case. I hope he finds <<2>>'s death to be a tragic accident. Anything else is too horrible to imagine.
I was in the study when I thought I heard an argument. I came to investigate, but it was too late. Uriel was on the floor and someone dashed out of the entryway. I, I don't know what to do.

Let me mark your map. Frayed threads of fate point to Rustwall, the Elenglynn ruins, and Ostumir. And take this relic, the Echonir. You might find it useful.\n\nMy friend Beragon offered his townhouse in Skingrad. Let us meet there when we are done.
Bandits. The captain says there was a time when those kind of scum would never challenge the Legion.
Place the combustion canister in front of the door and I'll take care of the rest. \n\nI do suggest you take a few steps back before the boom, though.

I know you, challenger. I've seen you in Maelstrom, no?\n\nI hope you haven't given up combat. I'm being invaded by the Blind and an army of cultists. I could deal with them, of course, but I'm intrigued. My realm sees invaders so infrequently.
We've made more progress here in a day than any explorer in centuries! Let's take the lesser stone back to the great welkynd stone and see if it fits into one of the sockets.
Get on with it, mortal. Use the spell scroll I gave you. That's the only way to release the relic's energy and repair the damage to reality.
I think we did what was needed here, friend. Finish placing the remaining relics. I'll see you back in Skingrad when you're done.
We may have won a few victories, but Nantharion and the Recollection are still out there, and these Daedric incursions are getting worse. West Weald isn't safe yet, comrade.

Burning lights are a sure indication that someone's been here recently.\n\nKeep going, friend. The Skein already pointed us to two wildburn seeds. There might be another one below. And maybe Nantharion, too.
Let's keep looking. If Nantharion is still alive and somewhere in Hoperoot, we'll find him.
Another lingering memory? We should see what the Echonir can show us here. It might be something we need to know.
One diplomatic incident averted. So far, so good.\n\nGo ahead and speak with the king, friend. Tell him about the threat the Recollection poses to Vashabar. And about the corrupted seeds.

I must warn you, traveler, the writing contained in the journal is blasphemous. Still, it provides some insight as to how the other necromancers were killed and what we must do to stop the ritual. \n\nArkay watch over us, this will not be easy.
The One Who Knows will not speak to me. A sure sign that Hermaeus Mora dares not offer us guidance for fear of engendering the very outcome he desperately hopes to avoid.
The ruins of Ceyond lie to the west of Skingrad. I'll meet you there.

Delving into old ruins feels so familiar. Sure, I hung up my adventuring gear long ago, but you never forget the basics.\n\nLet's focus on finding Greenspeaker Sorilen and this seed. We can trade stories of our best adventures later.
This is by far the strangest journey I've ever been on. But I'm not about to turn back now.
The trail leads to that door, proxy. Let us see what lies upon the other side.

When Vargas attacked, I saw a flash of light and suddenly I was somewhere else. It looked sort of like Fargrave, but everyone was gone—including Beragon. I wandered until I found those mirrors.\n\nThanks for getting me out of there, comrade.
This is a marvelous opportunity. A learning experience. Now let's head back to that altar.
Proceed, proxy. Your guess about which direction to try is as good as mine. Sooner or later, we will find an end to these corridors. And Tribune Alea, if fortune favors us.

Leramil is convinced that the Lamp, the Skein, and Abolisher have been depleted. Still, we should be safe and put them in the display case. Daedric relics shouldn't be left lying about, I don't think.
This inn remains a point of convergence. Even before this day's events, this location thrummed with fate's energies.

This reflection has given up. But she has no plan, no hope for the future as the last one we met. The Many Paths show the consequences of every action, every choice.\n\nGather some harkfruit and we will leave this wretched path.
It has been a while since an army mustered enough forces to invade my master's realm. I wonder how long this incursion will last.

My father's letter said he was planning to question Ghrakug at the Stonechip, Ranch Overseer Merrarq, and Quarry Boss Laurina. Let's start where he left off and talk to them. \n\nThen, check my father's office. I … I haven't been able do that yet.
No time to talk. We need to defeat these Shardborn and secure the blade that Vargas dropped!

You'll have to cut down an enemy or two, no question. But your primary objective is to reset those traps and burn those ropes. My legionaries can handle the rest. After that, meet me in the main courtyard.\n\nIf you have questions, make them quick.
This place is beautiful, isn't it? You should talk to Clendagal. He's normally easy going, but he's so tense right now I'm worried he's going to bud.
I see Ciiril found you. This is a happy place for us, traveler. \n\nI hope you've come with news to match.
There you are. I've got a good start on gathering supplies for Laeni and Clendagal. How was your chat with the old goats?
Looking to learn how to handle a blade? You've come to the right place, but I'm not taking on new students right now.
Welcome, welcome, welcome! Newly grown, fertile ground. Vashabar is a place to put down roots.

Bottles of musk, spore pods, and a ballista. I wish I'd been here to see this. Knowing Hyacinth, he was taking notes about how effective each was on his attackers.\n\nWhat did you find on that corpse? Anything telling?
Viti is hurt! I have to try to help her!

Please, let me see that note. Perhaps it will distract me from the knowledge that these once-holy catacombs are now a midden.\n\nMy eyes are … glowing? Huh. I did not know that. Small wonder these Inquisitors seek to kill me.
A weed among the flowers? How appropriate. Destructive growths, choking out all around them with no remorse. \n\nHow best to root out this pest? Hmm.
I've decided to assist you here in West Weald. I'll meet you at the location Scruut marked on your map.
You know, I'd like to find a way to help out around here. Everyone's got their assignments, and they're all just telling me to stay out of the way!\n\nI do that well enough, but I'd like to do more.
This place is incredible. We'll have to explore when we're not in mortal danger. \n\nAll this unstable magic seems to be flowing from those doors to the altar.

Goblins are highly territorial, that's why the Sharp Tooth camp is a little ways away from this Bitterfish Goblin camp. Still, they're nearer than most other Goblin tribes, and that makes for interesting research. \n\nYou'll see what I mean.
I'll meet you at the Lady's standing stone in Auridon. \n\nHow nice it'll be to really stretch my wings again.
A traitor? Just saying the word out loud causes a pit to open in my stomach. I took such care in recruiting every member of the ring. \n\nTo think someone among us would be willing to … to betray us!
Rest easy, I would not set you to task without cause. There is method to my mindset.\n\nIn the meantime, you have many questions. Mortals always do.

Everything I've heard about this Gryphon makes him seem like a knight, one who's taken a vow. Righting wrongs, upholding justice. \n\nKnights of the Lamp don't often go on errantry, but this Gryphon … hmm. Soup for speculation.
The texts Ulfsild gathered about the Gryphon are interesting. He seems surly, very focused, single-minded.\n\nI like the sound of him.
I promise if I remember anything about Mizbi's riddle, I'll tell you as soon as it comes to mind.

Breaking down doors is Big Urm's specialty, but it looks like she'll need a moment to find her rhythm. See if you can find anything Marcan Caelum left here while she's busy with the door. Maybe it will help.

Arkay forgive me, it was like a spirit was among us. We split up just for a moment, and suddenly I heard Val scream.\n\nFallen-Knives feels responsible, but I should have said something. I just stood there like a statue.
Sneaky tzilnech! I took a good swig to steady my nerves, and this is the brilliant idea I came up with? We should have stuck together.\n\nLead the way. We can't leave Val alone with that monster.

Versidue and the young guzzard get along better than I dreamed! Still, my little guzzard could use an adult to learn from. I asked Marcien for one, but that was ages ago.\n\nI'll gladly pay you for your trouble if you find an adult guzzard for me.
Merchants make the journey to Skingrad regularly for supplies. I'll join one of their caravans and travel as part of a group. See you at the Outlaws Refuge.
Scrambling down an incline of this magnitude will not be a simple matter. \n\nYou take it at your own pace and Keshargo will take it at his.

Mortal, it's been some time since I had the pleasure of real conversation. I may have begun this relationship on the wrong wing. What do you say we begin again?\n\nI am the Dragon. A being of purest magic, intellectual, and enjoyer of riddles.
How do you talk to a Luminary? Should I be formal? Or tell it a joke? \n\nThe Votary Commander's training didn't prepare me for magical Netches.

You are most impressive, Not-Ulfsild. I will ensure the mortals I have in mind are aided by your buoyant deeds. \n\nIn the meantime, let us talk about your proper trial. And another mortal all together.
I'm so glad we were able to overcome this little … hiccup. That first page should be enough to get you going.\n\nI just hope you'll find some clue that will lead you to the next set of wards.

I would accompany you to Pa'alat if I could, but I should keep my distance. It will only spell trouble if we're spotted together by the Inquisitors.\n\nIn the meantime, Ja'kh can keep me company, yes?

This one is sorry you had to witness that muskarse dull claw, but Viti is thankful you are here nonetheless.\n\nThis one summoned you here to make amends and to ask for your help. She did not expect the Inquisition to follow her, though.

Please, go on ahead. I don't have the strength to deal with people right now. \n\nHead to Ontus and look for my delight in Stonechip Tavern. When I'm in a good mood, I'm drawn anywhere with drinks and noise and crowds. Ugh.

You and I are heading to Rootwater Grove in Greenshade, Dawnbreak in Auridon, and an old fort called Faldar's Tooth in the Rift. Oh, and … make sure you bring some lockpicks.\n\nAnother adventure. With you! This is going to be so much fun!
Injustice did not rest while I slumbered. Your time will be well used on these tasks.\n\nAnd while you are gone, the Fox and I will have some time to catch up. I missed him, dearly.
Nothing's tried to kill us, yet. Let's just be ready for anything, some of my most memorable patrols started all nice and calm.\n\nBefore the screaming and running.
Ravith-morna is near. I can feel her darkness. But the Inquisitors, what were they thinking?\n\nIf they hunted the Rajaska down, they would never attack without ….
Do you need my help with something?
That's the prison warden. What do you say we do a little interrogating of our own?
Forget her. We need to get Hyacinth out of that contraption. Looks like those levers there should set him free.
I know what needs to be done. I just don't know if I'll have the strength.\n\nThank you for being here. Let's put an end to this. Once and for all.
Check that urn. Make sure it still holds the remains of Moon-Singer Talbira. Once you make the confirmation, I shall invite her spirit to return.

We must walk into the Dark Behind the World. Where Ravith-morna makes a den for a beast as old as light and shadow.\n\nOnce we cross this threshold, there will be no one to help us. We must look out for one another.

Forgive my haste, tamiit. I hoped if we moved quickly enough, we could outrun my thoughts about … all this. Dispatching the shadow that resides in Ravith. In doing so, we will deliver her from this world for good.
<<1>>! What did he do to her?
That … that was … I do not have the words! Talk to Zerith and see what he has to say about what we just witnessed.
Look at what Mezamma and her worms have done! More of my comrades, dead! I want to gut every last worm and leave them drowning in their own blood!\n\nThis is my fault. All my fault.
Between the terrible beating I received and the lingering pain, I have a lot to think about.

No matter what we do, Mezamma and the Worm Cult has been a step ahead of us. Maybe she even led us to that Worm Nest on purpose.\n\nWe need to figure out where she went. Talk to Prince Azah. See what he thinks.

Soul reapers, what a grotesque invention. Waylaying one soul on its way to the afterlife is bad enough. To do so at this scale is unthinkable.\n\nWhenever we encounter one, exploit this design flaw and tear out its core. That should destroy it safely.

Arum-Khal, a lich of the Hidden Moon? I do not know this name. He must have been hadaliit far after my time. But he rises again now.\n\nVastarie is a witch of Azurah. We should do everything in our power to aid her here.

I remember Vanus Galerion visiting my father's court when I was a child. He always made a spectacle of things.\n\nBut with Merric dead, it will be good to have another guildmaster beside us when we face Mezamma and her cultists.
Did you get it? Oh, let me see! I know that if Khalisah made it, it has to be beautiful.\n\nShe's amazing.
You just entered a war zone and I have absolutely no reason not to cut you down where you stand. We barely survived that surprise attack, and I'm not going to let anyone get the drop on us again.
What do you want? Can't you see all these wounded, all this blood? I feel like I'll never be clean again, and I still have so much to do here.
Go on. I'll limp back down the mountain on my own.
So my brother is dead …. \n\nAlas, I will find no time to grieve while we're still threatened by Vaermina.
Either Hosni's trying to ruin my reign, or there's something seriously wrong with the man.\n\nIf you'll snoop around his estate, we might just figure this thing out.
I'll stay here and do whatever I can to keep the poison from consuming the spriggan.\n\nIf she transforms into a lurcher, we'll have no choice but to kill her.

Thank you for dealing with that situation. I know it wasn't pleasant, but life just isn't always a pleasant thing. Certainly not in my case.\n\nNevertheless, we have responsibilities we cannot simply ignore. Glarikha taught me that, and you, of course.

Captain Dhakir's men are very loyal. Their information resources are almost as good as mine. They know I seek them, but not why.\n\nAnd they will have heard of you, and how you helped their leader. Fortuitous indeed, as it will bring them to light.
Bless you, but neither of you needed to risk your lives for me. What I need is strength of will. \n\nI need you to kill me.
My sister believes I'm lazy and incompetent. She may be right, but I wouldn't ruin my own family's livelihood!

Satakal's Wrath, wayfarer … unless you want to wade through an army of undead, go no further.\n\nThese dogs—the Withered Hand—they seized control of Tu'whacca's Throne and now they are raising the consecrated dead! How is this even possible?
<<1>> is a holy training ground for those learning the sword.\n\nOnly those who have endured a proving may learn from its masters.

It is good to see you again, my friend! Now I understand why Tu'whacca bid me to come here to HoonDing's Watch. \n\nIf you are to save the Alik'r desert from the Withered Hand, there are things you must learn from the spirits of this place.
I knew you'd see things my way. These people are scum.
We've got a serious situation here in the village, stranger.\n\nWhatever your concerns may be, they'll have to wait until we've dealt with the slavers and anyone who was conspiring with them.
Guess this arena's going to need a new Scourge. \n\nYou know, you're pretty good.
Our work isn't done. Daggerfall's still in danger.
Fire. I can't believe the terrible Faolchu was afraid of fire.
Just tell Gelvin you found those gems on his lordship's body. If he knew I acquired it, he'd want me to return it or give it away or something unselfish like that.
I can't sell the johads. Not after all this.\n\nIt'll be hard work, but together we'll do it. As a family.
I can't talk long. As you know, things are not well in our woods.\n\nThe guardians have gone silent and this corruption spreads.
We sent word to Aldcroft for reinforcements. I'll take anything they can send my way. \n\nNow if I could only reach my son ….
I'm glad to see the spell worked. That should keep these villagers safe.\n\nI heard you talking to my father, though. I hope you're not going to pursue his foolish plan. It's too dangerous!
When you opened the last gate, the Lion Guard charged in.\n\nAnd when Faolchu fell, his army turned and ran. They ran! All's well again, thanks to you.
I served in the Lion Guard before coming to the wyrd, so I know more about the world.\n\nI think it's time my sisters stopped hiding. We could benefit from more outside contact.

Guards are holding Ildani's wares in the customs house on the hill overlooking the docks.  \n\nIf you help Ildani recover them, it will be worth your time. The Baandari take good care of their friends.
Please, you must … handle this. I am sworn to protect the prince. I could not bear to do … whatever it is that needs to be done.
Sorry, friend. This is my perch. If you want to get a bird's eyes view of the ruins, you'll have to climb up on those rocks over there.
Truly the gods smile upon me to return you to my path.\n\nCan you free me, and allow me the burden of watching over <<1>>?
Before long, the woods will come alive again. My sisters will warn off unwary travelers. We have no want for any more deaths. We simply wish for nature to take its own course.
I can feel the earth. I can taste the wind. It's like every piece of this forest is a part of me.\n\nCould I even command the beasts? It seems like it would be a trivial matter!
Well, look who's here! I should've known you'd be making Angof's life miserable. Camlorn wasn't enough for you, eh? \n\nSay, these mists are poisonous. Why aren't you affected?

You won't be able to just walk into Angof's parlor and challenge him to a duel. He has minions. His kind always has minions. \n\nBut don't let that stop you. We've come too far not to try to finish this.

I wondered where you'd gotten to. Glad to see you're all right.\n\nWe need to capture an Imperial scout for interrogation. If you're willing to try again, I've still got a <<z:1>> you can use to bash them on the head.
He's dead. Stendarr have mercy on us all.
I'm glad we put a stop to this madness. And look! Draven knows me. He knows both of us. That gives me hope.
You! You've endangered us all with your meddling!\n\nWell? What have you got to say for yourself?

You heard the call, didn't you? You have been chosen to help stop the blasphemy in the ruins below, to stop the laws of nature from being broken.\n\nI too was carried here on the tides of fate for this reason. We must work together.
An adventurer, from the looks of you. Live by the sword and die by it, as they say.\n\nWhat brings you to our humble camp?
Look at these fools! My town is ready to tear itself apart, and I can't find a way to stop it.
I don't think we've met. And I don't think we need to.
Get your arse into the tombs and protect Tanval.\n\nI'll join you as soon as we plug the breach.
Balreth has done its job. The Covenant has been driven from Davon's Watch! \n\nNow to put it back where it belongs: in the depths of Ash Mountain.
Choose your waters wisely.\n\nWe'll all join these men in death one day.
Furon's experienced, and his brother is clever. Any ideas they have are worth considering.
Excellent! This plan will save many lives. You'll see.\n\nThere's an ancient altar nearby. Gather the skulls. My brother and I will join you there.
Use the flasks of blinding light to reveal those n'wah assassins and slay any you find.\n\nWhen you're done, meet up with Strikes-from-Shadows at the tower to the east.
Why, egg-brother? Why couldn't you be content to stay with us in this warm, fertile place?
I'm not trained for this! Copying papers. I could do that. Or maybe read scrolls behind the front line. Not this.\n\nGo, talk to Mavos, so I can leave this dry place.
We must save <<1>> before it's too late.
We'll have this courtyard cleared of Covenant skeevers in no time. \n\nThen all that remains is to deal with that treacherous dog, Serien.
Serien waits nearby, listening to the storm of our coming. He wonders and worries.
Vivec keep you, soldier. What can I do for you?
The curse came out of the reliquary, and that's where we'll stop it. What was done must be undone.
And so it ends. You made the choice we could not. My people are now at peace.
You're a new face in Stormhold. As vicecanon tasked with today's duties of audience, it is my solemn duty to warn you of the killer loose in our fine city. Be on your way, travel in pairs, et cetera.
So maybe I'm not crazy after all, eh?\n\nNow back off. You start acting funny, and I'll burn every piece I chop off you.
If we are to have any peace, we must destroy the soul gem array.
I'm sorry I can't be more hospitable at this time. Speak to my seneschal <<1>>.
Outstanding! When you hand the <<z:1>> to <<2>>, I'll make sure nothing like this ever happens again.
He was so good to me. I can't believe he's really gone.
Take the Apprentice Sword scroll out of your backpack and read it.\n\nIf you lost the scroll I am sure my apprentice has one for sale.
Careful, friend. The General has been acting strangely and there's no telling what he's going to do today.
Now then, the crown. Hmm. A little tight around our temples, but the pinch reminds us of kingship's burden.\n\nHow does it look?
Victory is like a cooling rain, yes? But still the storm rages on.
If you can, don't hurt him. He's a troubled creature, but no harm to anyone. And he is very courteous.
My father requires you again.
Walk in wisdom, child.
You've proven can handle yourself. I'm going to need your help on a sensitive contract. We already sent <<1>> but he didn't manage to get the kill.
This is a grim business, but I'm proud to fight by my father's side.
Another stranger in my temple? You must be the Ashlanders' chosen emissary.
Step lightly. The Dominion fills the swamp like rotted weeds.
Excellent work with <<1>>. Let me know when you're ready for another contract.
The ritual is complete. Are those mammal-lickers still attacking?
What have you learned, supplicant?
Good to see you again, comrade. You recall our encounter with Doshia, yes? When we found her encoded journal?
Get out before I have you thrown out.
<<1>> should be at his camp. I'm sure he'll know what to do.
Excellent. You found all three puzzle stones and learned how to use them.\n\n<<1>> and I slipped past the pirates while you fought your way through the camp.
Those puzzle pieces are somewhere in the pirate camp.\n\nI saw some of the pirates playing with one, tossing it around like a ball.
Good luck in the field, comrade. I know you'll do your Guildmates proud.
Well. That did not go as planned.
I hope you're not here to attack me. If I die before I stabilize this portal, you'll be trapped here.\n\nSince killing me is off the table, I could use some help.
Comrade! The river has returned you at the perfect time. We've discovered much since our adventure in Mzeneldt. The events of the past continue to stalk us.
Were you successful? Do you have the tomes?
We must reach the Hall. It's my home, and my charge.
The river runs with poison here. You'll want to stay back.
I won't lie to you. You won't like this. Just think about all the lives you'll save today.
You're back! Is it true?
Our shellback friend here will get us to safety. He's a hero of the Pact!\n\nAnd for what I've promised to pay him, he'd better be.
How did the butterflies get inside my head? They're swirling around my words and drinking my mind honey.
Damn it. What was I thinking, attacking the Prince of Madness?
I'm thinking a pint of … Sentinel Sundown. Sees-All-Colors developed a taste for it, drinking with me.
Ah, the empty one returns.\n\nYour pardon, but, bereft of your soul, that's how I think of you. Don't be offended. I hope to repair your lack.
I can't believe the Stormfist clan threatens my city. What a ludicrous notion!\n\nBut the evidence you collected gives me cause for concern.
Hmm. These runestones aren't powerful enough. Perhaps the summoning ring would respond to some type of imbued gem.
So much bloodshed! Curse Mauloch, curse the Drublog! May they suffer a thousand deaths!

My father must be stopped at all costs. He's already targeted the Winterland hunters. He's about to turn them into his puppets.\n\nJaruk downstairs can tell you how to save them. That's our first step.

Hi there. It's great to see someone who isn't made of metal and trying to chop me to bits.\n\nAre you just exploring? I hate to tell you, but we were here first. But good job getting this far without one of Raynor's crazy devices.

Three of my comrades remain somewhere in these halls.\n\nThey serve as Keepers under me, sworn to guard the High Kinlord's prison for as long as they are able. Find them … and help them, if they live.

Looks like everyone's mostly in one piece. Only one we're missing is Sal. Of course. I bet he's hiding in one of these buildings.\n\nWe've got to move before the Shrikes regroup and attack. Maybe we'll go with <<1>>'s plan after all.
Do you think this is a test of some kind? I'm not sure why the Daedra would pick this moment in my life ….
Their shaman ensnared the Silvenar. His book drained the Silvenar's essence, immobilizing him.\n\nThe last thing I saw, the shaman took the tome toward one of their Daedric shrines.
Is that the Ritual of Unbinding that Sariel was talking about? It looks … strange.
My friend! I was certain you'd arrive. And it's a good thing you did. All is not well in Silvenar.\n\nThere's a barrier in place, invisible to the naked eye. Its energy keeps me out of the city.
Oh! You startled me! \n\nYou look a capable type. Are you a sellsword? I need someone to help me get past the barricade inside the crypts.
Be careful, you hear?\n\nI'd hate to see someone I … respect … get hurt.
If we were in the Ashlands, I'd have you clapped in irons on one of father's plantations!
He steals everything he sells. It makes sense he'd hire bandits to ambush me.
I'll pray for <<1>>.
She and Aelif await you at the hall in Marbruk. Go well on your path.
Our alliance has never been stronger thanks to you, but your work is not complete.\n\nI have a message for you—from Vanus Galerion of the Mages Guild.
Were you talking to the stone? What happened?
Valaste is working the problem out of the Stormhold Guildhall. See you there, Adept.
I've sent word to the militia to gather here. Once they're together, we'll head toward the warehouse district.\n\nMeet me at the bridge after you've killed the Drublog chief.
We must close the net, and quickly. If their second courier arrives from Colovia, we'll lose the advantage you've given us.
Well, what is it? I'm organizing our defenses here. If you need supplies, talk to Garri in the Tapped Vein.
Good luck. We all need it.
Well met, stranger. As you may have noticed, I'm not at liberty to stand and greet you properly.
The Black Daggers understand nothing but force. Harsh measures are called for here.
The Ebonheart Pact armies are assembled. It's time to defeat <<1>>!
The Baandari owe you a great debt, my friend.
I don't know how much longer we can keep this up. If we can't get those portals closed, the first hold of Auridon may fall.
The energy subsides. But the animals are still savage monsters. We'll have to try something else.\n\nWe need a bear.
Something's wrong. More than just the illness. I just think. Something's not right here.
Fair day. I'm Astanya, watch captain. With the Queen in town we have extra security precautions to see to. Where are you traveling from?
Ah, my friend. This one was just thinking about you.\n\nNothing personal, of course. Raz threat-assesses all of his assets.
I'm sorry, citizen. I have to focus on my upcoming speech. Fair day.
Follow the moons, my friend.
Thus ends the story of the most sacred sites here in <<1>>.
Good luck out there.
I can't believe you found me out here! Did you come from the Hollow City?\n\nCould you help me, please?
I wish I had tried to do something sooner. Maybe then Gamirth would still be with me.
Thank the Divines, you are safe! There is that, at least. \n\nLyris sacrificed everything, that we might go free. Her sacrifice must not be in vain.
I'm not looking forward to finding my way to this city, but I'm at least thankful that I'm not in that battle anymore.
At first, Mim was excited to be free.\n\nBut then he saw who was standing next to him. You couldn't just leave him, no?

This realm is cruel, my friend.\n\nThough you may have saved us here, things may not always work out as well. You must be willing to lose those you care about if you hope to win. That's the only way we'll beat Molag Bal.
You have completed our trials, outsider. Now we ask you to settle our long debate.\n\nWill you side with the scholars or with the warriors?
The Prowler, here in <<1>>? They sail with the Gold Fleet!\n\nThey picked a poor time to visit this fair city.
I don't hear the sounds of battle. Are the bandits driven off?
Where is <<1>>? Was it her?

I get it. My people killed one of your own. They aren't evil, though.\n\nYou have to understand. We signed a pact to protect this forest. The Shadow Walkers believe that if they fail to honor that agreement, we're all doomed.
I've captured one of the books. It mentions this ruin specifically. All very exciting!
Bring me whatever you find in Vahtacen. If it's interesting, I'll buy it from you.
I just wish we had another of those monsters so I could watch you do it again. \n\nYou would do it again, wouldn't you? For me?
Send any survivng crew my way. I'll see if I can find more help, but you may be all we've got.
You still have the note. It needs to be delivered!
As I expected. Another resting place for the dead.\n\nSheogorath has a sick sense of humor.
Watch your back in here. The Goblins are well-armed for their breed.
I'll be honest, dearie. Those tricks are funnier than the ones we've seen the last few years. But for your entrance into the Boast? We can do better.
I'd say "at your leisure," mortal. But I expect I have more time ahead of me than you do.
Just so you know, after this Khali will drink that brandy—whether or not you are still alive. So, stay alive.
Everyone dead and an ancient relic destroyed. I see Khali has been here.
So you're the one that everyone's talking about? I expected you to be bigger or something.
I almost lost faith there. I don't know why I doubted Azura, why I doubted you. \n\nMaybe it's from being so close to the king. He's consumed by terror in his dream.
All right, you know what's what. Now stop jawing at me and get rid of those rats!
This one prepares herself to crack the ward. A moment, Hallowed, and she shall be ready.
With the beacons cleansed, this ward is just an annoyance. Shazah is preparing to crack it wide open.
We're going down the skeever hole, recruit. Up for the challenge?
Go! Mathal is … damn it. He's so stupid. But he is all Kalari has. Parents dead, uncle Enak-do dead. Ezzag old and angry. \n\nDo not let Kalari's brother do something so stupid.
<<1>> really is sweet, you shall see. Tell him Shuzura said "Bright Moons."
So, Jone and Jode have chosen you to solve Ezzag's problem. Which problem are you here to solve?
I fear these Timberscar Goblins will be a problem for a long time to come.

We should hurry. From what I understand, the Mane's party has been cut off for several hours. \n\nWe've already got an undead Altmer prince to deal with; we certainly don't need an undead Mane as well!
Alliances—bah. We have no need for any of them. Death and destruction is all they bring.
You'll find Aluri along the north road. She'll know where the Dremora are.
Come, my friend. Let's return to the temple.
Don't worry. Raz has suffered worse.
The best route to the sanctuary is through Serpent's Grotto to the northeast. \n\nGo quickly, if you can. The more time we give the Maormer, the more difficult it will be to drive them back.
I hope you can assist <<1>>.
You got past the front door. Impressive. Perhaps you're my way off this damned isle.
We need every warrior if Bruma is to be saved. Find Methas and Halfara, please.
They took Bowenas! My wife is gone!

Be wary in there. Nereids wield dangerous magic and can never be trusted. It's no surprise they helped the villagers in their suicidal plot.\n\nIn fact, the Nereids probably consider General Malgoth's bow a prize. They will defend his remains.
Have a look around. I'll keep watch.
