Our warriors have prised the Elder Scroll of Ni-Mohk from the clutches of our enemies. We are one step closer to victory!
Ezreba is just waiting for her friend.
You have completed the Trial of Spirit. Are you ready to undertake the Trial of Body now?
How did it go? Are my companions safe?
Once my caches are full, I might spend some time on the road, see what kind of trouble I can get into.
The crew of that beached ship may be on edge. Let them know you're with the Dominion.
I wish I could put Juras to rest myself, but I'd never survive the trip, let alone the undead that infest that ruin.

When we entered the temple, that skeleton made it sound as though <<1>> was in grave danger.\n\nI won't let vague threats keep us from my master, but <<1>> is too important to lose. Perhaps we should think before we act.
What luck! The Prowler was untouched by the hurricane. Then, as we sailed past these shoals, a storm came out of nowhere and beached us!\n\nWait, what are you doing here?
I can feel my strength fade faster now.
Keep your wits about you, my new friend. Mistral's houses cast deep shadows, and vipers lurk in the tall grass.

The vile and ruthless Wood Elves smash our eggs just because they feel threatened by our numbers.\n\nThey even hold some in their dwellings, using them as hostages against us. This is not a way to live. We must get our eggs back.
They don't even know what they're really doing here. Idiots. I can't wait to see how they react to Gavo's little speech.
Just point the crystal in his direction. Cariel and I will do the rest.
Not again. Please, I understand what <<c:1>> desires, but I already told you. We cannot provide him with our copy of the treaty.
May the light of Jone and Jode bring you luck in the Division Arenas, my friend.
You there, please. I need your assistance.
I fetched my father's instructions and marked on your map where he believes we might find these things.\n\nPlease—he is very weak—we must move quickly. You lead the way and I will follow.
I have nothing more to say to you.
Behind you are the luxury guest lodgings. Covenant and Pact agents, thick as thieves.\n\nThe troops here aren't even bothering to hide their colors. Sloppy.
Bakkhara welcomes your strength.
I haven't seen you around the island before. In the name of the Thalmor, what's your business here?
You can't seriously be considering her proposal, can you? She's a confounded vampire, for Magnus's sake!
Go, Hallowed. You know what must be done. Protect the souls of the Khajiit in all that you do.
You appear to have arrived in the Wretched Squalor, a shanty town of soul shriven outside Mannimarco's castle.
Hallowed, without your wisdom I don't know if I could stand to be here. Thank you.
Hallowed, you are my strength today. I couldn't do this without you.
This won't be easy. Is there anything else you want to ask me before we move out?
It looks like the injured Wood Elf has something he wants to say to you.
The queen will want to hear about Vicereeve Pelidil's actions. I'll prepare a letter for the next courier.
You're the only one left to challenge Selene.
You don't want to keep the moon-sugar-induced visions waiting, do you?
Go on and start without me. I must catch up with this beautiful woman! We have so much to discuss.\n\nI'll meet you at the manor house after you've had a good soak.
Pour the <<1>> into the basin and prepare yourself. The truth of this place can be disturbing. \n\nAnd be careful. Once the illusion breaks, you will be in danger.
Ahh, the Moon Hallowed. Welcome to the Temple of the Two Moons Dance. The Champions are here, and await only your arrival. Are you ready to join them within?
The Mages Guild stands ready to do our part for this effort. I just wish I had as much confidence as Vanus Galerion. We're facing some overwhelming odds here, you know.
The welkynd stones are the only way to break the barrier and enter the heart.
I'm relieved this tribe can call <<1>> their home. If the Dominion can't honor the promises of its members, what good is it?
<This Argonian matches the description of <<1>>, one of the tribe's leaders. He appears to be sleeping.>

I rescued her from them. The mercenaries killed her mother, and the other chicks in her brood. This creature had done no wrong, yet they would kill her to be paid for her feathers!\n\nI couldn't stand by and let that happen. Could you?
Did you hear that? It's like the wizard spoke directly to my mind. What's a "sijick projection?"\n\nI don't know what any of that means, but it sounds like we should find a way out.
Did you hear <<1>>'s message? We should locate his Psijic projection as quickly as we can.

You proved very useful and earned the assistance I provided you.\n\nBut I wouldn't recommend lingering in my territory, little mortal. I cannot vouch for the patience or control of my newly awakened kyn.
I'll let you talk with the spinner. I tend to infuriate her. No idea why.
Speak with Gilraen if you have something to say, stranger. I've got wounded to rip from death's jaws.
I'm a bit busy—speak to Gilraen if you must.\n\nThough why you aren't running from here, screaming, I don't know. Haven't you heard there are Daedric cultists attacking?
I heard <<1>>'s message. If we find his Psijic projection, we can stop the ritual.
Welcome to the island of Stirk. Representatives from all three alliances are gathering at the meeting place. It's just up ahead, through the ruins.
They're waiting on you. Good luck. You're going to need it.

You know, Tharn's not such a bad chap, once you get beyond the sour expression and the condescending attitude. And the sarcasm, of course. That's rather a bother.\n\nCome to think, he is a bit of a twit, isn't he?
Come, my friend. Let's return to the temple.
Who are you? What do you seek?
At last, the Elder Scroll of Ni-Mohk is ours. All honor to the brave warriors who won this relic for the Pact!
Do you smell the scent of burning embers in the air? We may be in for a treat if Kasura is teaching the firewalk!
You have your orders, soldier. Capture the Elder Scroll of Mnem for the Covenant!
When I get my hands on Mannimarco, I'm going to slice that traitor stem to sternum and wash my hands in his body cavity!
The shield is gone. Kill the doppelganger and grab Sahan before they take him again!
I'm sorry, I'm not interested in talking with anyone at the moment.
We will win this for my sister, for the shield of Tamrith! For Captain Janeve!\n\nMay the Light shine on us all!
My house isn't far from here. We'll slip into my basement laboratory, grab the scroll, and use it to unlock the cathedral.
We are almost at the Inner Courtyard. Make haste!
I can't shake the feeling that we're being watched.
Sebazi greets you, warrior. An army camp is an exciting place, no? Sebazi wonders, of every face she sees, if that face will ever return.
Soon I too will return to war. Perhaps someday we will fight side-by-side.
Mercenaries, huh. I don't trust warriors who fight for anything other than the thrill of battle.

Let's make haste. There's no telling what the Architect will do to us when he finds out we're free.\n\nIt's a great thing you've done for us, my friend. I didn't think Saryne and I would ever walk free.
<<1>> can't have been interested in ancient dinner invitations.\n\nNo, there must be more to this. We should find another welkynd stone and see what we can learn.

How splendid! Look, Stibbons, it's our friend … the one from Glenumbra! What good fortune. I was just saying to Stibbons, "Stibbons, I do wish someone would come along who has proven their worth!" And then you turned up, in answer to my summons!
So Uela's hiding away in the island tower? Let's go scout it out.
My prison holds me in complete solitude for centuries, yet two visitors arrive on the same day.\n\nBut we have little time. <<1>> has pushed deeper into the prison.
It is not safe for you here. Go quickly, and walk in the light.
Shall we keep moving, or did you wish to continue prattling on endlessly?
After a few more drinks, I think I'm headed back to my tent. I think I'll take a nap … a very long nap.
Hello again, traveler. Watch your pockets—things have a way of disappearing from them in Redfur.

I plan to lead House Tamrith with the same committment and devotion as my father. We will not see Rivenspire under another despot's thrall.\n\nThat's why I sent my sister Janeve and her troops west. The people of Rivenspire must be protected.
It went well, then? Good. <<1>> will be so relieved.
I have much to learn in your shadow, my friend. You have done more for the Hollow Moon than most could ever claim.
Why are you still here? I need to concentrate if I'm going to learn anything important. And you need to go talk to High King Emeric.

This is a bit more than I expected. Did I say we would hold this ground come Oblivion or Coldharbour? I didn't mean that in a literal sense.\n\nIf you told me you thought we should retreat … well, I might consider such counsel.
Adusa was just thinking of you! Did the courier reveal anything important?
I have nothing to say to you.

As much as I hate to admit it, Tiria is right. Nyronie's willing sacrifice is priceless compared to yours. \n\nI raised her, you know? We found her, abandoned, a lost child that the wood kept safe until we discovered her.
Impressive for an outsider.
You're rather useful, in your own way. Meritorious work!\n\nNow according to my notes, I just need to combine these reagents, and shake the vial ….
Brelor and Nairume delivered Rajhin's Mantle to Elden Root. Now we must recover an Ayleid source of power and a skilled operator.
I know you have the strength to see this through.
Please believe me. I can't be certain the talisman will work, but you must act quickly!
Please speak to my attendant. From now on, you will need to go through him. Do you understand? From now on, I do not wish to be seen with you.
We need to find a suitable place to swear an oath to Malacath. We'll see how Osgrikh handles an oath on his head.
Well! Isn't this delightful! \n\nWorld saved, heroes gone their separate ways, and this knight has a new mistress to serve. Bravo! Couldn't be happier! Smashing! Truly!
Travel cautiously. There is trouble in the air, and in the land.
Oh! Hello there. Sorry I didn't see you coming. I'm keeping my eye out for harpies. And a pair of puny Breton brothers.
I think I'm going to train up a few of the townspeople so next time bandits come into town, they'll be in for a rude surprise.

You really have the knack for this. While I'm getting Martin released, I wonder … would you be at all open to taking a crack at another one of my stubborn prospects?\n\nHer name's Shuga. She's got a mouth on her, but she'd make a good soldier.
As I feared. The delay caused by my missing memories allowed Montclair to reach this place before us.\n\nThis veil … it has Lleraya's deft touch about it.
I will pray for poor Ellic. And for Alard, as well. Perhaps Arkay will grant them peace.
Why would the Baroness do this?
Thank you ever so much for getting us out of that terrible place.
Plague husks? Here? Where did they all come from?\n\nAre these really all the people that came here looking for help?
Glad to see you managed to make it out of the quarantine, too. Does that mean those Maulborn fetchers have been dealt with?
What's this? Another motley band come to steal my glory? You don't have the guts!
Those beasts had me up there for hours! Thank you for the assistance, stranger.\n\nListen—can I trouble you for more help? I promise you this forest isn't as tranquil as it appears.

Now you know what the Serpent has done to us. How he split us into pieces.\n\nHe intends to locate our weakened aspects and forge them into a being he can control—one poisoned by his corruption. You must find our aspects before the Serpent does.
The service in this tavern is frustratingly slow.
No, don't tell me what's up there. I'll find out all on my own.\n\nOnce Brulo gets here. If he survives the gutting I give him.
I tried to be polite, but you see how far that got me. Let's meet up at the Valley of Scars. We'll probably need to go with our alternate plan again.

These scorpions were specifically selected for their compatibility with the mantikoras. With the matron slain and her nests destroyed, this portion of the process can't be duplicated.\n\nI wouldn't have been able to do this without your help.
Were the stories true? Did you encounter an army of nightmarish Daedra, or was the threat nothing more than Scamps frolicking the wood?
You hold your head a little higher. Is that due to pride or a neck injury?
Bring some rough maple to a woodworking station and refine it into sanded maple. It's easy work.
Roast pig is an easy recipe to learn, but difficult to master.

<You notice a prominent handbill on the requisition board.>\n\n"King Emeric offers greetings! Masters of the craft await you in <<1>>! Free training for all new to their craft; certification for accomplished crafters! All at no cost to you, citizen!"

Ah, what a surprise! Bthzark! Seems like we explored that place only yesterday! \n\nYou do remember? Stros M'Kai, Dwemer ruins, that adorable animunculus Clanker? Those were good times. But now, to business!

I'm Kurog, king of the Orsimer. Thanks to me, Wrothgar is ours again. We will rebuild Orsinium, make it stronger.\n\nWhoever dares oppose the uniting of the Orc clans will feel my wrath! Welcome to my war!
Hey, have you seen an Elf anywhere around here? Talks a lot, kind of opinionated, looks a little like you?
Yazara said she needs you.
<<1>> should be at his tent.\n\nAnd thank you for the <<z:2>>, blood-kin. Sometimes the smallest favors are hardest to repay.

The relic is an Elder Scroll, sequestered in the library of the White-Gold Tower. It's surrounded by minions of <<1>>. But they can't get to it—not yet. \n\nWe hope to get to it first. But we need you to take us through the throne room to reach it.

<You notice a prominent handbill on the requisition board.>\n\n"King Jorunn extends an invitation! Master crafters await you in <<1>>! They offer free training for those new to a craft, and free certification for accomplished crafters!"
Well, isn't this intriguing? Look at the attention to detail, the complex composition ….\n\nI can tell that a dedicated artist created this work!
I can't believe we're just going to leave those poor Orcs out here in the open for all the world to see.\n\nIf you ask me, that's no way to treat the dead.

You, again! You make a habit of showing up when my lady needs you. I suppose that means we're going to make another attempt to reach that wretched summit after all.\n\nGo present yourself to my lady. She should be coming down the trail at any moment.
The rubbing came from a stone plaque of some sort. There should be two more somewhere that contain the rest of Torug's epitaph. If you find them, I should be able to translate the words.
I remember you. During that trouble with Montclair back in Rivenspire. It's always good to see a familiar face.
My wife, she's out there somewhere! On the ice!\n\nShe could be injured, dying. Or worse, those hideous little creatures might have gotten her.
Give me a moment to translate this. You can look around, just … don't touch anything.\n\nMy ancestors guarded their forge's secrets. Best not to find out how.
Did you see that! That coffer appeared out of nowhere! I wonder what's inside?
So Molag Bal thinks he can keep the Dragonfires from lighting …. That is cause for serious concern.
I plan to make it up to Unsulag's family. Somehow.
I've had enough of ruins and mad cultists. I just hope Orsinium lives up to its reputation.
Oh, my head—hey! Where's my brother? Have you seen Raynor anywhere around here?
Can't say I paid a lot of attention, but back in Shornhelm the Eight never used torture as a method for recruiting people.\n\nCan we get out of here now?

Try the giants' camp where <<1>> fell. Or <<2>>—ask what he heard the night before the attack. And search <<3>>'s tent.\n\nConfront her with anything you find. I want to know what she has to say for herself.
I'll need some <<z:1>> and <<az:2>>. There should be some nearby, but watch for the wildlife.
You're welcome to return here any time. Another exhibition of your combat skills can only benefit my minions. \n\nUntil then, remember to Move Like This!

Place the shield on the proper display downstairs. In the meantime, I'll write out a list of the historic relics we're hoping to secure for the museum.\n\nCome back and speak to me after you're finished and I'll give you the list.
I am glad you killed that terrible Azhnura. She was the one pulling the strings here.
I thought the sandstorms back home were bad, but the blizzard that struck just before we crashed into the ice was unlike anything I've ever seen.
Remember, in the arena, an attack might come from anywhere—and everywhere. \n\nKeep that in mind, and you'll do fine.
Ugh. That books smells like it was dug out of a Black Marsh latrine. Even so, I'm sure Cirantille will pay you for it. She takes her work very seriously.
Be careful around that hagraven, pal. They're slipperier than greased eels. Uglier too.
Are you ready to accept the task that awaits you? To prove your worth to the Dark Brotherhood and take your first steps into the Night Mother's cold embrace?
This horse and cart will get us to Blackwood, where Cyrodiil flows into Black Marsh.\n\nClimb aboard when you are ready. We can wait if you still have things to do before we depart.
Back so soon, darling? I suppose I'd miss me, too, if I were gone too long.
Once we're inside, the rest should be easy.
Do you see the sentry? He keeps looking through the gate, rubbing his lips. Waiting for one of his mates to come by with a drink.\n\nLet's relieve him of his thirst. Then his uniform.
Do what you can to get through the camp. If you find a good route through, we'll follow your lead.\n\nOr, clear the way—I'm not picky about what happens to the Iron Wheel.
<<1>> sent me to find you. You're needed in <<c:2>>.
<<1>> said to keep an eye out for you. Ha!\n\nShe needs to speak with you. Wouldn't keep her waiting.

Troll's blood, can these people gossip! They're worse than the Rat Master's informants, and he pays them to dredge up secrets!\n\nHilde was here, but no one could say where she went or when. Tell me you had better luck, Initiate.
Long is the night, Brother.
Ah, you just missed Mirabelle. She was heading back to the Sanctuary in such a hurry we barely had time to talk.

I don't suppose you have a little wolf trailing behind you? No? Seems Hildegard has gone missing again. If she seeks to abandon the Brotherhood, she'll have to be put down.\n\nI suppose I can give her a little more time before I write up the contract.

I was almost certain that we had concluded our social interaction, but these customs have always confused me.\n\nIs there something else expected of us? An ever so brief embrace perhaps? Or the firm clasping of the wrists and hands?

Green-Venom-Tongue studies that journal with deadly intensity, but he hasn't shared any of his findings with me. I trust him, but I can also tell when he's plotting something.\n\nKeep an eye on him for me, Assassin.

Now you know what the Serpent has done to us. How he split us into pieces.\n\nHe intends to locate our weakened aspects and forge them into a being he can control—one poisoned by his corruption. You must find our aspects before the Serpent does.
The service in this tavern is frustratingly slow.
I tried to be polite, but you see how far that got me. Let's meet up at the Valley of Scars. We'll probably need to go with our alternate plan again.

These scorpions were specifically selected for their compatibility with the mantikoras. With the matron slain and her nests destroyed, this portion of the process can't be duplicated.\n\nI wouldn't have been able to do this without your help.
Ah, you return from a land of grass and sweetrolls to one of snow and mead!\n\nHow was your visit to <<1>>?
You should talk to the Archcanon. I think Lord Vivec is running out of time.
You're back? I admit, I didn't expect you to return. Forgive me. It's hard to know who to trust these days. It seems you actually do mean to help us. Did you find anything?
I hate to be pushy, but you really should make haste to Vos. That purse contains my entire life savings. Pick-pockets will take notice, I assure you.
I wish I could do as much for Sun-in-Shadow as you have done.
There goes another client who's known me for years.\n\nNot a proper mage, they say! Rubbish. By Vehk, if I get my hands on that fetcher from Summerset, I'll wring his scrawny golden neck.
I keep normal consultation hours, but honestly, people just pop in whenever they feel like it. It's a bit disrespectful, don't you think?

Between the cryptic warnings of the ancestor spirit and the unexpected result of the divination ritual, I fear there may be more astir than I imagined. We solve the greatest mysteries by accident, I suspect.\n\nHmm. I should write that down.
You don't look dead enough for a Daedra plaything. I suppose you bested the Imperial Prison?

At last! Did you see what's happening outside? Red Mountain rumbles louder and more frequently, the sky grows dark, and, worst of all, the people are beginning to notice!\n\nSoon, I'll have to muster the Ordinators to keep them from the palace doors.
In hindsight, the wailing was too pathetic to have been the angry dead.\n\nWhat did your sniveling pilgrim have to say for himself?
I'll meet you in the nursery. I just have to retrieve the egg first.\n\nWe'll need to hurry though. I don't know when the Houses will be arriving. Time is working against us.
Damn these trapped spaces and their tempting gaps! I hate to be a bother, but could you get me out of here please?

I've been away from my tower for much too long. Hopefully, none of my experiments exploded in my absence. I do love watching a good explosion!\n\nIt was a pleasure having you as an assistant. Much better than those so-called hirelings I usually employ.

That was … glorious! Lady Azura's presence filled me with such … wonder. She actually spoke through me!\n\nI heard everything she said and I felt her sense of urgency. You need to return to Vivec City immediately.

Drelyth Hleran of House Redoran, at your service—though I doubt I'll be very useful here. This is Ashlander country, and they've made it clear I'm not welcome.\n\nIt's my fault, really. I made a mess of their customs when I arrived.
Ah, my second favorite assistant! What a pleasant surprise. We may salvage this expedition yet!\n\nI'm afraid things are going very poorly inside this ruin.
So many ramps …. Long, steep ramps. Just give me a moment to catch my breath.

Still alive, I see. And since you're here, that means you weren't captured and hauled off to a Redoran dungeon. Good for you!\n\nWere you able to acquire the registry? And does it contain any information about Veya's brother, Ulran?
By order of the deputy governor of Seyda Neen, which happens to be me, the lighthouse is closed until further notice.\n\nOn the other hand, I seek an outlander who's willing to do a little work.
I'm not sure if I should be here. I wanted to see Eoki, but if the House Councilors catch wind of this, I'm ruined.

Have you come to see our wonder in miniature? Our magnificent tribute to Morrowind?\n\nAlas, the work is not yet complete. And, truth be told, there is more to our miniature Vvardenfell than simply a representation of our land at a reduced scale.
I'm ready for anything. Well, except if the tunnels cave in on top of us.\n\nWhat? Nobody's ever ready for a ton of rock to fall on their head!

I was wondering how long it was going to take Veya to convince you to follow me. Bet she thought I didn't notice when she glanced at my writ, didn't she?\n\nWhere is my overly curious apprentice, by the way?

I do hope you'll hurry to Pariah Abbey. I see the other oracles, my friends, languishing in chains. A prison that hurtles through space and time—filled with Daedra and choking steam.\n\nUgh. Gives me vertigo just thinking about it.
I'd say our work here is done. There are other kingdoms in desperate need of our merrymaking talents and I won't be one to let them down.

Like many Redoran structures, this place is huge and designed to serve a multitude of purposes. We're going to need to split up to cover it all.\n\nWe must find Brivan and keep him alive until I can talk some sense into my damn apprentice.

It's about bloody time you Buoyant Armchairs showed up! I sent a request for assistance almost an hour ago and—oh, hello.\n\nYou don't look like a Bouncing Armiger to me. Still, my man-servant is missing and I could use the help.

Look at that! Daedric creatures in such a sacred place! Makes me so angry I can barely calculate our odds of survival.\n\nWe need to deal with Barbas's minions. And by we, I definitely mean you. I'm a thinker, not a fighter.

Welcome to Balmora, outlander.\n\nHouse Redoran governs this town and asks all citizens and visitors alike to abide by its laws and regulations. We brook no trouble, especially from those who espouse different beliefs and traditions.
What is Gascone thinking? Honestly?
If the Clockwork Apostles had more people of your quality and worth, there wouldn't be anything we couldn't accomplish.\n\nI look forward to working with you again sometime.
Tell me you have something.

Chirrhari says there haven't been any other apprentices in years. That can't be right! I saw Novice Marico enter the Wellspring last season.\n\nLet's gather the safe mushrooms and go talk to Apprentice Idrono.

Did you think I would not expect you? I already know all that occurred with Lilatha and the murderous shadows. Rest assured, I will find this mysterious Daedric artifact.\n\nPerhaps you'd like to assist me.
We are in a bit of a hurry here, but if you have any questions feel free to ask. I know the Planisphere can be endlessly fascinating, especially to newcomers such as yourself.
So, that pompous High Elf got his hooks in you too, huh? I told my brother, Raynor, we should go it alone, but any house in an ash-storm, right?\n\nSpeaking of Raynor, he might need your help.

This promises to be a fruitful collaboration!\n\nI tasked Kireth and Raynor with acquiring gifts for Varuni, but they tend to wander. Kireth's just there by the cliff. You should speak with her. In the meantime, I'll conduct more research. Questions?

Ah, greetings. Please, don't mind me.\n\nActually, do mind me. I'm conducting an experiment on these firepot spiders and so far the results have proven … explosive. You should probably give this place a wide berth for the time being.

We will leverage your hard-earned citizenship to make inquiries.\n\nFirst, I will make it known that in light of your recent exploits, I offered to take you on as my aide—an offer you eagerly accepted.
I shall gather my vassals to plot and conspire. The Shadow will pay for what he has done! Pay!
Now that I've got the base for a marinade, it'd be nice to have something to use it on. \n\nI'm afraid I used the last of the meat in our larder on that misbegotten stew.
Hello there. Are you here in response to the bulletin about my factotum research?
I should have done that ages ago! It feels good to stand up for myself and give my sister a piece of my mind.\n\nNow we can get back to exploring and being partners again. Thanks to you.
Ah, this one's new partner returns! What interesting scandal did you uncover in the monastery? Tell Raz every juicy detail!

Hmm. You might want to get a move on. The enchantment I placed on that boat has a tendency to fade quickly when it gets wet. And Oracle Marieve indicated that she could use your help on that obscure, possibly apocalyptic matter she mentioned.
Those poor people. This wasn't just about newcomers and opposing the Queen's decree. That was Daedric magic back there! I just wish we had arrived a few moments earlier.

Greetings, my friend, and welcome to Lillandril. It's always good to see another member of the Guild.\n\nI'm afraid I have other business to attend to, but please, feel free to avail yourself of any Guild resources you need while you're in the city.

That … was unnerving. It seems the false Aldarch belonged to an alliance of Daedric cultists called the Court of Bedlam. Imagine, the faithful of Clavicus Vile, Mephala, and Nocturnal working together.\n\nThis is more serious than I anticipated.
Glardir's persona seems tied to the Illuminus in a more explicit way than the others, but I still haven't managed to identify her character. We're making progress though! I think.

You'll find the House of Reveries' amphitheater just up the road. Simply take the stage and juggle my enchanted knives for those observing your performance. I'm certain you'll draw Alchemy's attention.
It's not my place or yours to tell Larydel the path he should walk. Nor is it Rinyde's.
This keep has been ordered sealed by the Divine Prosecution pending the completion of our investigation. Please be on your way.

Now, I need you to keep a look out for inscriptions—strange symbols, carved into stone. As soon as you see one, just call me over and I'll take a rubbing.\n\nYou'll also need to handle any malicious creatures we come across.
I don't see any sign of her here. Did you find anything?
Please, be careful where you step. The plants I've cordoned off here are both rare and fragile.

Defeating Urlsar won't be as simple as rushing up the battlements and driving a sword through his heart. He has all the power of Sea Keep at his command. It wouldn't even be a contest, but I have an idea to put us on equal footing.

The old wizard doesn't look so good. I think the trip into Oblivion took a lot out of him.\n\nBut we're here, right? Can't he just say the magic words so we can find the Heart and get out of here? No, I suppose not. That would be too simple.

Sorry, I don't mean to be checking up on you. I just think better when I walk and the blood is still simmering in the alembic. It will be some time before I have the results.\n\nDid you find anything of use in Halimorion's villa?
I advise caution in all things, but this fight will take all your skill as a warrior. I fear this enemy is our most powerful foe yet.\n\nMay the Eight protect you all.

Leythen is a shell of the man I fell in love with. We can't trust anything he says.\n\nNo, we have to deal with this ourselves. And the key is reaching the Crystal Tower before Nocturnal can accomplish a similar feat.

You would help Rigurt? That makes my heart dance like young ones at a Mara's Day ball!\n\nSpeak to Courtier Vindilween and find out how we get one of these proper High Elf introductions. Remember, I brought gifts! That's sure to open a few doors.
My time is precious, newcomer, and you're wasting it. If you require something from the Proxy Queen's court, official request forms for appointments can be obtained from the court clerk.
Did you find a key? I dropped my lockpicks when those lions came after me.
I'll meet you in the Alinor Outlaws Refuge. We'll take care of this Blackbird threat, once and for all.
You're a welcome sight, my friend! I could use some help to free these people.
You've been a great help to me. I hope you find Ruliel's friends quickly.
Think I'll stick around a while. Great view, eh?\n\nSore knuckles, a stiff salt breeze …. Huh. You know what? I take it all back. Summerset's not so bad after all!
I have no time for the likes of you.
Go ahead. See what Vile's servant wants to tell you before we try to enter the tower.
I'll let you ask the questions.

It has been one disaster after another since the Queen issued her damn decree! Still, the possibility of a Sea Sload invasion … it chills me to my core.\n\nCainar's group represents our best chance of determining the threat. You must find them.
Josajeh will see reason, I know. She just needs reminders every now and then.
I shall await your return here. Come speak with me when you have the required pewter dust.
Stand aside—you look familiar. You're not wanted are you? No, I think not. Anyway, I'm in the middle of an arrest. What do you want?
Well! I'm running into all my old friends today.\n\nLook, before that reed-licker tells you otherwise: I thought those chickens were wild.
You spoke to the Loremaster, right? You should be setting out for Tamriel.\n\nWhat brings you?
I'm sorry, I can't talk right now …. You should go speak to the Loremaster.

Josajeh was very thorough in her preparation. Apparently, she mastered the art of ghostly passage without my knowledge. A feat as impressive as it is frustrating.\n\nAttempts to scry her location have failed. We must take a more direct approach.

Finally! You don't know how worried I was for you and Jee-Lar! After I heard about the murder in the Outlaws Refuge, all I could imagine was you and my agent lying in a ditch somewhere.\n\nI don't suppose you learned more about Margus's plans?
Beeko-friend! Didn't I see you talking with the explorers from Cyrodilic Collections? Are you one of them? Can I ask you to help me with a crucial and sacred task?
Quickly, quickly, Concordia will want to see that idol you found at the Chid-Moska ruins!

Welcome back. As you can see, we have visitors. Xukas has been quite pleasant. Jaxsik-Orrn? Less so. Nonetheless, all those who help us find the Remnant are welcome here.\n\nPlease, discuss your findings with Famia. I think she may be on to something.

Now then, are you ready to discuss my offer? I certainly hope so!\n\nI honestly don't know what I'll do if you turn me down. It's grave business, you know? Not trying to apply undue pressure or anything … but, yes. Serious business.

Armor. Specifically Imperial armor. From Tsofeer Cavern. If there's even any to find in there, which I somehow doubt.\n\nLook, if you have other questions, go talk to Tia Doran. You can find her at the Mages Guild.
We should leave this place and find the tree. It will clear the waters, I know it.
I must talk to Grave-Singer Ki-At for a bit longer. Go now. I will meet you in Lilmoth soon.
We mustn't let this trail go cold. This may be our only chance to find the vile den of the Veeskhleel before they unleash more foulness upon us.

The chimes speak of pain. Our children are suffering, but they are not hatched. The egg-tenders have brought me no concerns about the clutch's well-being, but the Hist always speaks truth.\n\nGo with Iskenaaz. See what I am blind to.

First, we must learn everything we can about Captain Jimila and how to make a good impression. Talk to people who have dealt with her before, such as Tolwin, Claws-the-Ghosts, and Ruja-Wan.\n\nI'll catch up with you so we can plan our next move.
Know what you're looking for? Look for a blue crystal, about the length of my forearm, with a faint glow. There has to be one around here somewhere.
The meeting point is west of the village, beneath a great cypress. We should go quickly. I do not know how long my Naga friend will wait.
It was all a lie, wasn't it? She never intended to help my children live.
Nice little party you've got here. And look at me … under dressed, as usual.
Branch and seed. Sap and stone. Root and soul. Dream, in dream, in dream.\n\nI widen my eyes. Do you see? The four of us—tied at the tails. For the sake of mending …! We must see the tree. The tree!

Thank Mara you're here. I haven't seen a gathering go this poorly since my sister Concordia's seventh birthday. Marinus put slugs in her pudding. I can still hear the screams! Ugh.\n\nFor the record, I did offer tea. But what's needed is answers.
If you have a tablet, feel free to place it back into the Xinchei-Konu.
All this trouble for a hunk of broken stone? There has to be more to it, surely.
I'll stay here and keep an eye on Many-Whispers while you go and get the key. We wouldn't want him running off before he turns over the charm, now would we?
What fortuitous timing! My manservant is absolutely useless when it comes to recovering historic artifacts.
I have been to the Swallowed Grove only once before, beeko. It is a beautiful place, but not a welcoming place. Make sure you are prepared.
Welcome! Welcome to Bright-Throat Village. Splay your toes and wallow, friend. All ojels of good will may find rest and respite, here beneath the chimes.
You heard the Speaker. Go warn Nala-do about the necromancers!
This one thought to leave violence and anger in the past, but Jone and Jode follow their own path.\n\nZamarak suspects you really want to talk to Khamira, though, yes?

This new moon-singer shows a modicum of promise, but she hasn't yet reached her full potential. Still, the story was interesting and it points us toward the final triangulant required to make use of the map.
It is a very big door. Perhaps the shrine and the Dragonguard wait on the other side, yes?\n\nExamine the stone pedestal and see if you can determine how to lower the barrier.
Thank you once more for your aid, traveler-friend.\n\nAfter I create an antidote, we can enter the oasis caverns and rescue my companions. Perhaps even find my egg-mother's research notes as well.
Stay close, yes? Vazbi hears that it is very easy to lose one's way in Baan Dar's Litter.

Hrrm. I do not want to shock the old castellan. You speak with him first. Prepare him so that when he learns a member of the royal family still lives, he does not faint or run away or do anything rash.
Very well. Let's get moving, then.
Quickly, head to Tajirri's house. This one does not know how long he can delay her.

That relic, it is connected to the Lunar Lattice. When you touched it, something spoke to me. I am becoming … attuned.\n\nHelp me find the remaining Lattice relics and complete my attunement. It is the only way to stop the Betrayer and the Dragons.
Tasnasi admits, she was not certain the old one still had it in him. You should have seen Nazdar before age caught his tail.\n\nWe should get inside before anyone notices our presence.
As dumb as Khasda is, he never did skimp on security. Those locks he has in his dungeons are Dwarven-make. No one gets through those.\n\nUnless you're me, of course.
Tasnasi's gotten tense. More tense than usual.\n\nThings could have gone smoother so far, sure, but she's not one to get rattled.

"And Buri-do, waking from the dream, kissed the earth until his mouth was full of mud." The Scrolls of Companionship, Moon Passage. \n\nNazdar channels Buri-do at this moment. Though his back feels nice and loose.

Five-claw, I am glad you are here. We may have stopped the Betrayer, but not before he set the Moons in motion and started the eclipse. Soon the Moon Gate of Anequina will open and grant access to Jode's Core.\n\nExactly as the Dragons desire.
The Tenarr Zalviit Ossuary is deeper within the chasm, to the east. I will meet you inside.\n\nFirst, I must slake my thirst as best as I can. I'll need all the strength I can muster.
Undead swarm in the town square! Hurry, five-claw, Nala-do needs you!

Azura's will resonates within that Moonlight Blade, but it's so faint. Like a voice at the far end of a darkened hallway … or the other side of a stone door.\n\nThat's it! This sword, Arum-Khal's phylacteries—they're not vessels. They're gateways!
You mean to face a dark lich, but shrink at the sight of my cozy portal? Ha!\n\nWe cannot enter the temple through normal means, child. Not yet. Trust old Mazza-Mirri and step into the light.
So. Mazza-Mirri's champion arrives at last. Then the battle is upon us. Azurah be praised.\n\nI am Shando-ri of the Hidden Moon. Together, we will destroy the Dark Spirit of Arum-Khal.

Raz used to come down here all the time. It was one of the few places he could hear himself think. This one even taught himself to play the lute. \n\nMother never did like the sound of music. Reminded her of Father too much.
Oh, now you show up! Left me to deal with a Dragon all by myself. It's a good thing I'm Abnur Tharn and not, well, some lesser mage.
I expected sorrow and despair, but the situation here goes beyond even my prophetic inklings.

To think that the Rithana-di-Renada was snatched away by Rajhin's Shadow! Never would I have thought that to be the case.\n\nGood luck finding the rest of the pieces. My brother and I will pray for your swift success.
There's Iraya now. Go see what she thinks of your tale.
Poor creature. But, oh, that stench. Why must this Dragon's blight smell so bad?
I'm not upset with you. Most people don't respect Peryite's power until they contract a terminal illness.
So, are we headed into the Tangle, or what? I'll admit, this is a romantic spot, but we should probably rescue Fez first, eh?
Ah, five-claw, good, good.\n\nThis one has walked to Dune and back looking for you. Well, maybe not quite that far.

Ah! You must have been drawn by the scent of my rising dough. And don't be shy about staring at Rigurt's muscles as he stirs.\n\nDid you bring the honey flowers? If there's one thing Rigurt knows about the cats, they love their sweets.

Well, look who got their soul back from Molag Bal! And is that Meridia I smell? You've been a busy little vestige!\n\nDon't worry about these levelheaded losers. No one can see me but you. You possess a special untapped talent for unhinged insanity!

Everything I learned about Kaalgrontiid came from a few oblique references in the Khajiiti myths. Let's see if we can find anything to add to our knowledge while we search for a way to dispel the aegis.
Do you hear that? The bells sound like they're playing a song. It's faint, but … it's definitely there.
The path leading farther into this sanctuary is hidden from us. I see neither grappling points nor braziers to light. \n\nThere must be another way.

A Dragon that wants to be a god? As ridiculous as that sounds, Tharn's reaction tells me that this Kaalgrontiid poses a serious threat not just to Southern Elsweyr. He endangers the entire world!\n\nWe'll meet you at the New Moon Fortress.
Warrior. Did Sai Sahan find the maps as interesting as I expected?
Ka'ishka would like a moment alone, walker. She has prepared for this for a long time, but it does not dull the pain.
Let's see what Ranza has to say.
Other than dealing with a few stray pirates, things have been quiet here.\n\nTell me, were you able to find the missing fragments of the tablet?
It never hurts to get to know your companions, especially on the cusp of battle.\n\nJust don't take too long. Our mission is urgent. The sooner we set sail the better.

This one hopes you bear good news, walker. Adara'hai has managed to wrestle Vijari back from the brink, but the force that tugs at him through the mural will not let go. She does not know how much longer she can hold it back.
You found green stones in the quarry, yes? Where you fought Yahgrondu's corpse?
I should have realized earlier. Tharn, Sai. You and me. We are kra'jun. Just like Khunzar-ri and Anequina.\n\nNow, through the portal, five-claw. Go, go.

Big beard told us all about the ghost of Khunzar-ri. Za'ji loves those stories!\n\nNow tell this one the truth. How much spiced whiskey did our oversized leader imbibe before the ghost appeared to him, hmm?
I'm still waiting to hear how we're going to reach the floating island. Until then, all this rallying of the troops is just a waste of effort.

Sai gathered us and we're ready to go, but it seems like we're destined to simply hurry up and wait.\n\nAnd my father arrived a short time ago. He wants to know whatever we can tell him about the floating island.
Honor and faith, wayfarer.\n\nBlademaster Kasura awaits you at the Watch House in the city of Davon's Watch. She requests you join her there at once.
Situated to the north, Pridehome sits on the outskirts of Tenmar Forest. I'll note the location on your map.\n\nHopefully, Nahfahlaar can shed some light on what the cult might want there.
Maybe this is a blessing in disguise. Restoring the tapestry will prove to the people of Senchal that we can bring beauty back to our city.

If you press the pedal in front of the bell stand, the lanterns should start to glow. Then you need to hit the larger bells in the same order. That will cleanse the little bells.\n\nAll you have to do is remember the pattern.

Haven't seen someone that drunk since my niece's forge-lighting ceremony. Good thing she didn't have a beard. Would have caught fire along with that pretty hat she was wearing.\n\nHere's some free advice: don't get drunk at an anything-lighting party.
There you are.\n\nYou must hurry back to the sanctum. The Dragon wishes to speak to you, and this one doesn't think you should keep him waiting.

It seems there's more to Doomstone Keep than first meets the eye.\n\nThe inscription says to create light with a divine mask, which I can only assume refers to the Mask of Alkosh. Did the Pride of Alkosh occupy this keep?
I really hope Maezi and Winks are all right. Knowing Maezi, she's probably more worried about me. And I don't blame her.\n\nI'm so out of my element here.
Every step we take in this place feels like a blasphemy, but we have no choice. We cannot allow these graverobbers to escape.
This place … I do not trust what my eyes see … and neither should you, my friend.

Our only lead is a note from a merchant named Goharth Ironbelly. The note suggests we can find him at the Withered Tree inn. Let's go and get him to lead us to the coven.\n\nReady to travel to Riften?
That was Urgala, leader of this branch of the Icereach Coven. She's the witch who locked us in the barrow. The others take their orders from her.
This has to work. The safety of my people depends on it.\n\nBesides, I don't want to see Lyris get hurt.

With the addition of the sacred oil, the elixir is complete. Before we produce enough to distribute to the people of Western Skyrim, we need to test it.\n\nI'm confident in my work, but we're dealing with powerful forces here.
Blackreach again? And a flask of foul-smelling elixir waiting to be guzzled down? Oh joy.
No sign of Rasir, but that paper on the ground … perhaps it's his? If he left it behind, there might be something written there that will lead us to both him and the cure.

Welcome to the princess's chamber, my friend. I don't remember the last time I spent more than a few moments in here.\n\nAnyway, Jarl Reddharn and Magister Fridelja are here, giving my father an ear full. Thanks for helping me at the holds.
Mamdahan was our cook … what did that monster do to him?
I got back as quick as I could. Other than a few skirmishes, I didn't uncover anything important.\n\nWhat about you? Tell me you found something.
We can pour over these mysteries later. Fenn's in trouble. We need to get to him.
These tunnels … how long have they been here? Is this why my father sealed off his precious tower? To hide them?\n\nSvargrim has much to answer for. Much to answer for, indeed.

Rada al-Saran, he's treating this entire structure the way the Icereach Coven treats the witch pikes. But he's added a new element into the attunement process—Svargrim!\n\nMaybe I can unravel the spell before the attunement is complete.
The way is clear. Move, move!
I thought this was the end for me. I barely have the strength left to conjure a light breeze.\n\nWait a moment … is that Princess Svana?
They're mad. Beyond all reason. Even in this temple, Meridia's light does nothing to help those afflicted with this feral curse.\n\nWe need to reach the catacombs and find High Priest Varkour.

All I found were these Reachmen stalking the pass. Decided they'd rather die than talk, so I obliged. They don't look like they're from Icereach, but they are wearing the coven's medallions.\n\nAnyway, did you find the lodge?
So Bjora was from the Reach this whole time? My best friend, one of these barbarians?\n\nI suppose it shouldn't matter. But, it's still a lot to think about. Let's keep going for now.

Oh my, yes. Petraloop looks perfect in such a place of honor. Do you see how the light sparkles off its lacquered finish? Delightful.\n\nTake a gander at Nel's Hidden Loves. I placed it on the table for you. Perhaps the clues will speak to you.

Look at you, all high and mighty. Places to see and people to go, am I right? Living in the lap of royalty like some sort of … royal.\n\nWell, I got important persons to speak to myselfs. Just got to find them ….
Those smaller sigils must have a role to play here ….
There's a darkness to this place ….
Elle must see so many peculiar, inexplicable things down here in Blackreach. This is wonderful for my research!
The pilgrims headed south along the main road. If they were caught in the storm they may still be in the area, otherwise we'll have to assume they made it to safety.
While you check out that camp Ena mentioned, I'll go and ready the garrison. Come find me if you learn anything.

Damn Svargrim and his distrust of Jorunn! How many more of his people have to die before he accepts the truth and lets us help him?\n\nForget that for now. Tell me about the assassin. Did anyone get a good look at the murderer?

Never trust a Reachman, that's what I always say. Or … at least that's what I say now. I swear to you, this won't happen again. I'll deal with more trustworthy sources from now on. \n\nAnd thank you for saving Ulang. I'd be lost without the old oaf.
If the coven intends to perform another harrowstorm at that mine, there's no time to waste. You go on ahead. I'll get word to Solitude and meet you there with your very large friend in tow.
Svargrim, you bastard! People are dead … holds destroyed … and our high king had a hand in it?\n\nHow will we survive this betrayal?

Sorry if I gave you a bit of a scare! That was closer than I'm proud to admit. But it all worked out, didn't it?\n\nThis has been a memorable conclusion to a long and storied career. Thank you for your fellowship, and your indulgence!
Thulsgreg mewls like a dog while our kin fight for their lives!\n\nAttacking this stone with pick and spade is asinine. We have to make our way through with the stonemelt solution.
Please … you could have a hand in determining Mazog's fate. Encourage the chief to show mercy.
Thank you for taking on this new task. Had I known how dire the situation was, I would have brought more priests.\n\nWe need to find the braziers, and quickly. They must be spread about the ruin.
Rigurt's beard is going to go gray by the time he's done dealing with these thanes. Can you try talking sense into him? He makes Rigurt's head hurt.

You can find the creatures you need to the east and west. The fleshless wolves wander in packs, mimicking the life they lost. Finding the shriveled people may be more dangerous.\n\nRemember — bring me skin and blood.
Morthal used to be such a quiet town. A simple place to make a living. Never had all the trouble that my husband and I have dealt with recently.
Glad you caught up. Thought I might have to try sneaking by a bunch of smelly werewolves all by myself, but since you're here now we can probably take the direct route.
Oh, good. You made it. Wasn't quite sure I could sneak into Lady Thorn's eerie old castle without your help.\n\nThough, you might not entirely like my plan to get in.

High King Svargrim isn't making it easier for the refugees flowing into the city. He's never been an inspiring leader, but lately he's been cold. Distant.\n\nI suppose watching your love die in front of you will do that.
Finally! I've been looking all over these lovely caverns for you.
So? What's next on the agenda? Sorting pigs by ear-size? A guar steak-eating contest? At this point, nothing would surprise me.

Find Eyfja in Morthal and Hautgerd in Dragon Bridge. Tell them Aerolf sent you. Ask them where they saw the Pale Man and who it stole.\n\nThanks for hearing out an old man. Most just think I've lost my mind. But I know the truth.
So far so good. Let's get up there. Whenever you're ready.
Come on. We have to find Adusa!

Orkey's gullet, the Skald-King's got some persistent sods working for him! If you're here to ask me to meet with Jarl Morryn and that milk drinker Hraldi, then kindly clear off!\n\nThane Hraldi's such a horker, he almost ruins my appetite. Almost.
I need to see if there's anything we missed.\n\nGo on to Rivenspire. Meet me outside Ravenwatch Castle. I'll catch up with you as soon as I've torn this place apart and put it back together.
Another note and a strange shard. What do you think, my friend?

The door to the barrow was sealed many years ago, but I remember the way well enough. We'll find it at the top of the hill. My sister and the rest of the clan should be inside.\n\nWe need to find them and stop my sister from carrying out this ritual.
A concealed wing of the library? What a perfect location for a hidden laboratory.
I'm too mad to deal with this right now. Besides, you completed the entire journey. You tell Verandis what we discovered at each of those sites.
Don't let Verandis change the subject. I can't trust any plan the Elf comes up with if he doesn't reveal the whole truth.
I trust my father, no matter what. But Lyris doesn't trust easily, and Gwendis's faith has been shaken too many times.\n\nPlease, convince Count Verandis to put his trust in us as well.

More than likely, the Dark Halls lie below us somewhere. See if you can find a way down while I attempt to trace the currents of void energy that radiate throughout this ruin. \n\nOne of us should find a way through.

If Verandis's study is still intact, maybe we can find that journal you tried to read in the dream-walk. It might give us some insight on the Gray Host and how to defeat them.\n\nGo ahead. I'll follow you.
We need to keep moving and find Verandis before Rada al-Saran or those shades do. Heading for the Darkstorm is the best course for now.

This is Karthwasten, outsider. I wish we could give you a proper welcome, but we still haven't recovered from the storm.\n\nShaman Ulvoch is just inside this building. I'll introduce you when we go inside.
Go now, approach the pyre and make the offering. I promise no harm will come to you. \n\nI will begin the ritual.

Strange, this one has never heard of darkcap mushrooms before. I will need to see what they do and bring that information back to the Ravenwatch.\n\nIn the meantime, be on your guard. There's something about Freyleth's plan that doesn't ring true.

Speak with the ard's sentry. You'll need to convince her to gain an audience with Caddach.\n\nI think the information you uncovered about the rebels will be enough to interest the Despot of Markarth, but you can never be too certain with Reachfolk.

I'm going to scout around. Try to determine where Lady Belain is hiding.\n\nRemember, let Bradan know our goal isn't to die defending Markarth. It's to save as many lives as possible. Then go tell the same thing to Ard Caddach.
Something's wrong. That wasn't supposed to happen. \n\nQuickly, speak with Shaman Ulvoch. He might know more.
Storytellers say the Dwarves knew the stars better than anyone. Strange passion for people who lived underground, eh?\n\nAnyway, let's get to this final location.
These Reachfolk … they are proving more difficult to deal with than all the nobles of High Rock put together.

I greatly appreciate your help, friend. I'm not much of a fighter myself, if you couldn't already tell at a glance. \n\nMaster Pythis is much better equipped than I. Which actually has me more concerned, since I haven't heard from him in some time.

An old-fashioned alliance, just like in the stories!\n\nAll right, here's our plan. That sewer grate ahead should get us inside. If you could scout ahead, I need to prepare some arrows. Just in case, you know?
At least some people are alive. And they saw my uncle and father! But their warning ….\n\nNo, no, I can't lose hope. We must keep going.
Well met, traveler.\n\nAre you interested in participating in the Old Life Remembrance ceremony? I sense some heaviness in your heart. Perhaps this could help.
We're close to learning the secret of Red Eagle's connection to Rada al-Saran. I can feel it in my bones.\n\nI will wait with Lyris and then meet you in the cave beneath the redoubt.

Even more of this darkness within the Choosing. Spreading like an infection. I honestly don't know what to make of it.\n\nLet's get you into the final wing. The sooner you complete the Rites, the faster I can work on curing this.
Finding this story, it's important to Sai. I haven't seen him like this in a long time.\n\nThanks for helping us with this, partner.

Oh! My apologies, I was lost in thought. You see, I thought … no, never mind.\n\nHave … we met before? Gods above, how can the Ravenwatch ever trust me with more assignments with a memory like mine ….
I knew something like this would happen. The spirits have forsaken Karthwasten! We need to leave this place!
Your arrival at this moment is most fortuitous, outsider. Come, help me teach these wayward clans how to behave like proper warriors of the Reach.

If something's happened to Eslyn, I won't make it in time to help her. I'm too winded. So I must turn to you. Find Eslyn in Faolan's Ire, make sure she's all right.\n\nI'll follow as quickly as I can.

See if you can find the fragment at Karthspire Lea. I'll look at Faolan's Ire. Meet me there when you're finished.\n\nI never imagined an outsider would go out of their way for us. Part of me wonders if this is even worth all the trouble.

Looks like I've been conscripted! Will this plan work? Only the spirits know for sure, but I'm willing to help. After all, if not for you, I'd still be at the mercy of the Thornroots and their hagravens.
May the Hunt-Father guide your path and lead you to the most worthy prey, wanderer.

Have you seen the prank the locals play on one another? They get a friend to stand within a circle of flowers, then they kick a nearby vine-tongue. The vine-tongue reflexively grabs anything inside the circle.\n\nPerhaps we can use that here.

Well, I ran into a lot of Daedra, but no Ambitions. Sombren must be trying to stay one step ahead of Vandacia's forces.\n\nLet's split up. You check the inner bailey, and I'll backtrack to make sure we didn't miss anyone in here.

Tell the Ambitions we will defend them with our lives. Just not here, where so many civilians could be endangered. Let us use Fort Redmane as the tree against our backs. \n\nEveli will see the Ambitions safely to the fort. Talk to her before you go.
A hidden compartment? I love it! I mean, I hate that people have died, but …. \n\nAhem. So, what did you find?

Ah, here you are, and not a moment too soon. As you can see, the same cultists from the Cauldron have come to this desolate place. Despite a minor setback due to the fragility of the mortal form, I will learn the reason for their interest.

Many of these bazaars had a directory to allow patrons to find goods and shops. We should see if we can find mention of the three trade-ministers: Ralos, Quentin, or Esdir. That should give us an idea where each of them did business.
I need your report, mercenary. Word reached me that Councilor Jirich was murdered. What about Sophus and Faleria?\n\nAnd did you find definitive proof that the Dark Brotherhood is our culprit?
You must be the mercenary that Captain Rian told me about. And I see you're working with Eveli Sharp-Arrow. Good, good.\n\nI assume you have something to report? I'm listening.
Well, this place isn't at all scary looking. See if you can open the cache while me and my trusty arrows keep watch.

Could you talk to him? When I'm upset I can't seem to put two words together. These … cultists … have me riled.\n\nLady Silvelle says if I want to be treated like a noble I shouldn't let my temper get the better of me.

You better stay back—whoever you are—or you'll have the distinct honor of Lady Twilight wearing your guts for garters! And—and your skin for stockings! And your bones, for … bonnets? I haven't worked that out yet, but I'll have them!
I was expecting this scholar to be a little more roughed up … though maybe he's nursing a papercut I can't see.

Phalevon's possessions could be scattered or sunken or stuck just about anywhere in this cavern. The people of Leyawiin buried him with great honor, befitting his magnificence. But that was before the ground swallowed his mausoleum.

Welcome to the Ashen Forest, my friend, deep in the heart of the Deadlands.\n\nTalk to Xynaa. She'll tell you what you need to do. Unlike when I did it, the twins will have each other and you when they walk the Path of the Obelisks.
Sorry you had to see that. Destron treats everything like a grand adventure.\n\nAnyway, you should talk to Sombren so we can get on with this. I don't want to lose control of my power again.
Look how Sombren manipulates the forces of magicka! I hope I can control my power like that someday.
Lead the way, sera. I'll keep working on a plan. Three willing, it won't cast us into Oblivion or make us grow third arms or anything.

A hidden switch and a concealed passage? Hmm. I wonder if these fools have a secret handshake, too.\n\nWell, try the switch. It should take us to the inner sanctum. The Fane of Boring, or whatever fancy name they gave it.

Soul gem-infused runes slathered on Ayleid walls? The poor condition of the stone combined with imprecise template virtually guarantees a lack of efficacy. What is Revus, an amateur?\n\nWhat am I saying, of course he is.
Don't look at me! I didn't know they could do that!\n\nGo on. Talk to Destron. I think he has some explaining to do.

You ought to find the harrada creeper just past that door. I can hear it struggling with the tree from here. I should get going, too. I don't want to be anywhere near it when it dies. The hissing is bad enough. Brrr.
There you are! I'm fine, don't worry. Just a little dizzy is all.\n\nI suppose you should set these spirits free. I hate to see Mathen go, but this is the right decision, right?
Little mortals, have no fear. I have no particular desire to inflict harm upon you.\n\nQuite the contrary. I suspect we may be able to aid one another in the events that are about to unfold.
It appears our imposter has slipped the net. Bradon may know something that can put us on Cres's trail.

I appreciate the help. You don't know how many people walk right on by when they see an Argonian talking to a pig.\n\nNot sure if bathing Deet-Loh will work, but how else do you apologize to a water spirit? Let's go inside before he digs up more grubs.
One attempt on my life today is more than enough. If you're another one of those Dark Brotherhood bastards, I assure you. You won't find either myself or Governor Keshu to be easy prey!
You need to convince them to let me go, please. Our people have done nothing to them, I swear it.

I am not sure what this all means. How does it all connect? I have an uneasy feeling in my belly, like it is infested with root-worms.\n\nI say we follow these footprints. We must be getting close to understanding all this.
Get down and listen! This could be important!
So many pranks, so little time! One of the great woes of life, don't you think?\n\nNothing to do but keep coming up with more, I suppose!
Deejos and I were not close. Truth told, I think she merely tolerated me and my brother. Not that I can blame her.\n\nI hope she finds some rest with her Trees.

Damn it, wasn't there supposed to be a ward on this door? If it's gone, that must mean the cultists have already gotten inside.\n\nLet's get in there. If they get to the emperor's secret before we do, we could lose the trail entirely.
There's the skyshard! We'll have to bring down that stone guardian if we want to reach it!

I can't stop thinking about these black soul gems. Can you imagine being snared in one? Being sold to some evil necromancers? Awful.\n\nThis killer's victims have waited sixty years for justice. Let's find this carriage and shine a light on the truth!

If Count Auzin's in Wayrest, we'll probably find him at the Cloudy Dregs Inn. Visiting nobles often stay there.\n\nI hope he can tell me something. After what I've learned about my mother's last wishes, I don't know what to think.
That one will do, if you can catch it. Go ahead, then we can begin the ritual.

I don't much care for Dwarven ruins. It's an over-saturated field of study and full of more speculation and theory than established fact.\n\nSay what you will about Daedra, they're more predictable than you think. Even Sheogorath.

Your punctuality is appreciated. I am Tee-Wan, spymaster of the Black Fin Legion. I serve General Keshu in all matters of intrigue.\n\nThough the matter I need help with is of a more … personal nature. I hope I am right in trusting you with it.
Tee-Wan summoned you. Not me. Speak to him.

You will make a wonderful addition to our cause. Lyranth is quite powerful, but I doubt we'd be able to recover the artifacts entirely on our own.\n\nVisit the wrath of Azura upon any of the order who stand in the way of our holy work.
We're on the right trail. This wreckage is saturated with lingering sorcery. Whatever this used to be, it held enormous power when it was intact.
Ah, we meet again. I'll admit I'm pleased to see you. You've proven yourself useful. Weylin has yet to earn that distinction.

You must gather the cursed feathers. They may be found growing upon the most vile creatures throughout Tamriel and hidden among the feathers of crow-like beings. I sense them everywhere. \n\nOnce you collect enough to make the effigy, we can begin.

It… It seems like this Cataclyst is why the Waking Flame are here. It doesn't look like anything of mortal design. Are the Daedra building it?\n\nThis investigation is turning up more questions than answers.
This is a pretty impressive force. Lyranth didn't seem too optimistic about finding allies, but I think she underestimated your influence on people.

Is it just me, or is Lyranth a little more … intense than normal? I mean, she's always scary, but it feels like something's off.\n\nAnyway, I'll meet you at the House of Whims. I can find it, don't worry! How hard can it be?
Go on, little mortal. Ask Eveli what she's found.

Based on the runic arrangement, I'd guess this thing creates a portal. A lock this complex surely leads to an area worth protecting.\n\nWe need to know where it goes. Find a way to power it. See how that crystal glows? We need more like that.
There's no doubt about it. The voice came out of that chunk of slag. And it sounds just like Emperor Moricar's voice from my memory.\n\nHe wants us to free him. Do you think we should?

I hoped Madam Whim would have collected a rumor or two about Deadlight over the centuries, but she knew nothing to point us to its location. And the twisted rod you found, while interesting, is no help in this matter. We must find another way.
Well … here we are. Can't put it off any longer. Time to make the difficult decision.\n\nGods, I can't really damn myself to save them. Can I? But then, how can I leave one of them here?

While you were out there looking for a portal key, Rynkyus and his scouts found the Deadlight portal. Unfortunately, like the portal to Fort Grief, it's warded. Not only against Lyranth, but all Daedra.\n\nWe might be on our own in there, my friend.

Mind yourself in Wretched Spire. Just because Dagon ignores it doesn't mean it isn't without danger. And tell Arox to keep quiet. We don't want to attract attention to ourselves. And I'd rather keep the daedrat in reserve, just in case.
Looking for an elixir? There are many bottles and vials and such things in here. Whether any of them would prove poisonous to a frail old mortal, I could not say.\n\nTry them all?
You have found information? Perhaps you have proven yourself a useful companion after all.\n\nWhat have you learned?
This conversation goes as expected. Faven has a simple mind. Surprised Tephilaz hasn't killed him yet.\n\nThe blighted tree, did you find it? A sample of poison may help us identify our target.
All right, this was a productive trip. At least Emperor Moricar's ghost didn't lie about leaving stuff here. Let's review what we found.
There's meaning in Elegian's babble. Perhaps he's trying to describe whatever visions plague him. The elixir Nokvroz mentioned. It sounded like he used it whenever he came to interrogate the old man.
Oh, master, groveling is beneath you. And so is paying a bribe.\n\nThen again, I'd rather not be inside this cage longer than necessary. So do whatever you think is best, master.
It figures. Not even Mehrunes Dagon's fanatics would try to live up here. But it's the perfect place to hide a permanent portal. The cataclyst must be on the other side.

We must reach the Anchorite before Valkynaz Nokvroz can use her blood to fuel his Perfected Cataclyst. Obviously, he seeks to create his own Incarnates. I'd prefer not to have to face such a creature.\n\nNow collect Arox and let us be off.
Enough questions for now, mortal. Let us proceed to the top of Annihilarch's Summit. I wish to confront my foes without delay.

So, the relic was some sort of memory stone? Was that a message for the Anchorite or Moricar's heir? Wait a moment, she is Moricar's heir!\n\nHey, if the egonymic gives the Ambitions their power, we only have one of them now! Sombren took Calia's!
We stand ready to join the fight.
All right, let's see where this door takes us.

Ah, my simple spell finally yields results. I was hoping it would bring you to me again, little mortal. I do so appreciate working with known quantities.\n\nBut who is this other mortal who also carries my glowing brand upon their flesh?
I want you to know, I appreciate the help you've provided up to this point. I really do.
There is a rythym to his speech. A pattern, I mean. He is trying, I think, to communicate.
The Purgator won't hesitate to destroy you once it's detected you. I recommend destroying it first unless you wish to join me here.
I hope you're not the sort to interrupt those busier than you for no reason. \n\nWell? I don't have much time. Out with it.
I still smell Nirn's reek on you. Most mortals manage to lose that sickly stench. Eventually.
Why does it approach me? Kynreeve Rynkyus and Lyranth stand just over there. Can it not tell the Kyn apart?
Let's make our way to the tavern. It's never wise to linger in the Shambles for too long.

Apologies that Za'ji thought to run you through! He was not expecting company that does not moan and groan and gnaw at your flesh. Rrrrnng, you know? Haha.\n\nSay, walker, are you interested in doing some treasure hunting?
Got nothing to say to you.
I have no idea what sort of relic an Arox might be, but if it can help us decipher the encoded note we must find it.\n\nKeep looking, mortal.
That is so disorienting! This alignment is still unstable. I can already feel it slipping out of ph-phase.\n\nPlease, let's find Hyxo before my condition w—worsens.
Jakarn and Valessea can get the captains safely away from here, but we still need to find Quentyn. \n\nCaptain Kaleen said he was being taken for questioning. We should keep looking.
Ah, my friend. How glad I am to see you again! This island is far more dangerous than I expected. Especially after what just happened.
My skill at weaving grew with diligent practice, but I've not had the chance to restock my supply of wood. Please gather some maple wood for me.\n\nYour work will not be in vain.

In all my years of seeing to the needs of this island's animals, I have never encountered such trouble. Then these Hadolids appear and behave quite rudely!\n\nWell, I don't know how they do things at the bottom of the sea, but this is unacceptable.

Ah, so you're the darling Jakarn was just telling me about. The one who helped him complete the mission I specifically told him not to bungle. Thank you for rescuing Valessea. I prefer that no harm comes to my associates—especially the lovely ones.
Good luck finding that key!

I'm surprised that Lady Arabelle brought you into her confidence, but I suppose she knows what she's doing. These peace talks are so important. The future of Tamriel is at stake!\n\nHmm. Shouldn't you give those medallions to Lady Arabelle now?

Lady Arabelle will appreciate an outsider's perspective. She's at the Gonfalon Bay docks with Lord Bacaro if you want to introduce yourself. The problem I mentioned? It involves some missing ships.\n\nAnyway, tell her Jakarn sent you. I'm her favorite.
Phew. Never seen so much rock overhead in my life. I knew a cavern that could harbor ships would be big, but standing in it makes a man feel small, you know?

What do you think? This raft will hold together with two people on it, right? I don't have to go far. Just over to Whalefall.\n\nSorry to sound rushed, but my partner Anton got selected for the game. And I'm pretty sure he won't survive it.

It's weird, right? Lady Arabelle denies that she's the author of the Investigator Vale books, or that those stories are really about her. Yet her manor is full of them.\n\nOh, this is a good one! Fowl Play. I especially like the twist at the end.

Normally I would not have allowed a challenger to use secret passageways. But Amunara's minions changed the nature of this trial. It is no longer as Lady Garick designed. So perhaps I can allow some improvisation. Are you prepared for the next trial?

Do be careful out there, my dear. If the Order can strike out at a benevolent association such as the Steadfast, then no one is safe from these villains.\n\nMeanwhile, I'll discuss matters with Lord Bacaro. See if we can narrow our list of suspects.
Hey there, good-looking. Lady Arabelle wants you back at Mandrake Manor as soon as you can get there. Looks like she has more work for you.\n\nWhich means more for old Jakarn, too, I expect.

The archdruid has returned to the Undergrove. Even now, the Allwither compels her to speed up the spread of corruption so it can consume us. In our weakened state, we cannot stop the Allwither from becoming the prominent spirit of the grove.
That's it! We've got the water moving! Now to put this damnable thing together, we just need to find the blacksmith shop. It's southwest of the tower, I believe.

Just look around for people making animal noises, I'm sure they won't be hard to find. And tell them I'm sorry when you change them back, would you?\n\nAs for Huldressa, I'm all in favor of leaving her as a guar. Just kidding! Kind of.
Emeric isn't here, but he left behind a number of Green Serpents. For a man of his advanced years, he can still swing a powerful sword.
Did I mention how unusually large that cat is? Startling, even. Quite brave, though. I can see why Ayrenn values her company.\n\nAnyway, she wants to speak to you. I wouldn't keep her waiting.
I am Prince Irnskar, heir to the throne of Windhelm and Skyrim. And judging by your looks and the way you fight, you must be a loyal warrior of the Ebonheart Pact. How did you find me?
I'll wait out here and keep watch. I'm too well known. If someone were to recognize me in there, things could get … unpleasant.
She's a taskmaster, our Lady Arabelle. But I just can't refuse that twinkle in her eye or when she calls me dear.

You seem healthy, or at least healthier than most of the manor's patients. Maybe you could help us out.\n\nThe patients here have fallen prey to a strange malady. None of the menders recognize it. And they can't find the cause.
I may be a delegate to the peace talks, but that doesn't mean I can't assist you and Lady Arabelle with your investigation.

Lady Arabelle guessed that map you found at Mistmouth Cave showed an underground river. She really is good at this investigating stuff.\n\nHmm. No sign of the Ascendant Magus though. Take a look around and see what you can find.

Glad to see there's still some decency out there in the world! Decency, you know? It's not that hard!\n\nI need shellfish, spices, and leafy greens. For the lads' digestion, see? Find my pack too. I lost it down there running from those damned Elves!
We're done gathering flotsam for the stinky Breton now, yes? \n\nWe have Oblan back, but now there's the matter of getting off this rock.
Perhaps you could get me down from here?

Good work, friend. Our diplomacy is very strong today! \n\nTalk to <<1>>, please. Now that he's free, he should be happy to pay his share of last night's bill. I need to get my scepter of office back!
Please talk to <<1>>. We've got to straighten this out. I represent the Daggerfall Covenant here! How in the world can I explain this to High King Emeric?
You're not Viralaine.\n\nMy name is Seraphyne. I am what you see, although I long to be free of this curse. What are you doing in this awful place?
Please hurry! The injured won't make it out of the mine like this.
Marcelle is stealing my stolen treasure? Again? I seriously don't know why I still love that woman ….

Nothing about this peace conference has gone as planned, but the Ascendant Order might have given us something we didn't have before—a reason for the alliance leaders to cooperate.\n\nCan I ask one more favor of you, dear?
We need to look around for any sign of Song. There has to be some kind of clue here that can point us in the right direction.
I've never stopped thinking about Ember, Jhaka or Song. Not even for a moment. Just because I buried my past doesn't mean I forgot it. \n\nBut I suppose that doesn't count for much, does it?
It's obvious they're sweet for each other. I think they make kind of a cute couple. Don't you think?\n\nHmm. Let's get back to Fell's Run so I can tease Aurelia mercilessly.
Aurelia is quickly becoming … a good friend. Thank you for saving her. Probably best if you hear from her what brought us to Rivenspire.
Oof. I'm gonna have to lay off the shein. \n\nYou know that weird taste at the back of your throat when the shein goes bad? I've got that. Yech.

It seems the only way to rid myself of this insistent and amorous spirit is to help Janne's ghost remember what transpired.\n\nTake Stibbons and see what you can learn at the inn. I'll keep the sea captain at bay for as long as I can.
Oh, go on. You read the plaque. I'm so nervous I can barely see straight!
Oh cruel fate! The curse of Monument Islet has claimed another poor soul!
Please, won't you talk to Izzy for me? I know she'll listen to you.
Wait, there is something on the ground here. Take a look.
I'd wish you good luck, but I don't think you'll need it. See you back here for drinks!

Remember, in these early days, winning and losing mean little. Regardless of a match's outcome, you must see every game as an opportunity to hone your skills.\n\nIt may sound nonsensical, but sometimes, losing is the surest route to improvement.
Now, that is a punchable face. He's got a punchable face, right?\n\nI can't wait to beat him!
The time has come, my friend! The final tournament! Your chance to take your place among Tales of Tribute legends!\n\nI hope you have been practicing. This last contest presents … unique challenges.

What is going on? Razhamad is using that voice. Do you think Brahgas really stepped in it again? Gods, why can't he keep himself out of trouble?\n\nThere's not much we can do for now. Let's just try to focus on the tournament, all right?
Good to see you again, hunter. Pity we could not save them. But then, every victory against the Host extracts a toll.

Ho, wayfarer! Care to join an old pirate's crew for a quick voyage?\n\nI'm off to explore Graven Deep. It's a mysterious patch of the Abecean Sea that no ship ever returns from. Jump aboard if you wish to help find out why.
Wyress Tola gave us a faster way to Bangkorai. Good. Let's take that and make our way to the Glenmoril Wyrd camp near the Viridian Woods.\n\nWe'll deal with whatever we find at the camp together.
Looks like we've got a way to Bangkorai. Maybe this will get us there in time to stop those Firesong bastards.\n\nLuck and clear seas to you. Go on ahead. Druid Laurel and I will meet you there soon.
