Oh no, no. This can't be happening. Embervine is flooded with lava and angry druids and … If I go in there I'm going to die.\n\nI knew this job sounded too easy. A quick trip through a cave on a beautiful island. But, no. Now I'll never get paid.
Good! Now let me out of this cell, friend, and we'll figure out our next move.
I doubt you'll learn much watching druid elders argue among themselves. But if Stefan thinks it's important, then I suppose you should go.

I never imagined the Firesong Druids would join up with murderous scum like the Dreadsails against their own kind. And they pulled House Mornard into it, too.\n\nWe should head back to Vastyr. Someone needs to tell Count Mornard about his son.
Let's look inside the lodge. That's where the village elders gather. Maybe we'll find out more there.

You and Ryvana returned just in time. We're almost out of the tincture she gave us. Hopefully the antidote works and Lady Arabelle's health improves.\n\nBut go on and talk to her. I, too, want to hear what you have to say.
Lord Bacaro is the Ascendant Lord? No one makes a fool of Za'ji and his friends! We will bring this traitor to justice, yes?
I'll accompany Lady Arabelle to Glimmertarn and make sure the Druid King's staff is safe. We'll catch up with you in Vastyr.\n\nBe careful, my friend.
I gathered enough of the plant to craft an antidote for Lady Arabelle. She will soon be on her way to a full recovery!\n\nDid you find anything interesting in the druid ritual box?
Heh, it's fun to do things the old-fashioned way. A nice change of pace.
Head south. Druid King Kasorayn's Tomb is supposed to be farther inside the temple. \n\nBe careful, friend. The Firesong here are more powerful than I expected.
Of course the Firesong have portal magic. I should have expected that. Clear my decks of those miserable druids!
Elder Aiven spoke of betrayal. Punishment. Hateful words. What did the druids choose to forget? What must I remember?\n\nTouch the mote, Laurel-friend, and we shall see together.

Captain Samara is truly a genius when it comes to Dragon-slaying. I must make sure to write everything she says down. For posterity!\n\nYou look like a rough sort. If you're interested, you should speak with her about joining the Elsweyr Defense Force.
I'm glad to see you again, friend. I just wish your arrival didn't coincide with another crisis.
Hi! Good to see you again! How do I do that, I wonder. See you, I mean.\n\nOh, wait. Sap! You were looking for sap! Did you find any?

I saw how you cast that spell. You're a natural! How's the fire shard? Not too hot, I hope. Nah, you're not screaming or bursting into flames or anything. The druid's spell worked, just like he promised it would.

Ancient druids called upon the spirits of the Green at their own peril. Only the Druid King was ever able to do so safely. It's why we abandoned the practice long ago.\n\nThis is where they did it. At least, where some of them did it.
Rot and damnation! Lord Bacaro, he betrayed us!
I'm glad to see you, friend. We have much to talk about. First, though, get the Eldertide seed to Archdruid Ellic. He's waiting for you in the Vine District.
Time is not on our side, dear. We have to stop Lord Bacaro.
Wouldn't be a proper thief if we didn't pick up something shiny along the way, right?\n\nOh no. This doesn't belong to the Sea Elves. That buffoon.
Douse those plants with Y'ffre's rain. Only then will we be able to traverse the room unimpeded.
I'm so sore, I can't think straight. Why don't you see if one of them will talk to us.
I'll meet you at Clohaigh. It's a cave almost directly east of Glimmertarn. Wait for me by the entrance and we'll head in together.
Alas. We cannot be certain how far the Allwither's corruption has spread among the Firesong. Be on your guard, my friend.
Well, we're two riddles further than we were at the start of all this, thanks to you!\n\nWhat's next?

You gathered the fire shard and the sap from a sacred tree? Very good. Now we have what we need to perform the ritual.\n\nWe just need to find the right spot to perform the ritual. And I'll need your assistance. These two are in no shape to help.

Remember, the moorings need to be cut and the harbor chain needs to be dropped or we're not going anywhere. Take care of that, then we can sail for Vastyr. Your lordling will need all the help he can get to withstand the coming assault.
On the list of people who should not play with time, the Telvanni rank high. Their thirst for power makes them dangerous.
I've sailed some stormy waters in my time. But today is about the worst I have ever been caught up in. Count Mornard was a hard man to like, but he didn't deserve what he got.
Hopefully Bassian can tell us how to reach the Shrine of the Golden Eye. I shall meet you at his location. I just hope we get there before the traitor silences him as well.
We've almost got him. We're so close, I can feel it.

Luck be with you, walker. This one is Eilirsu-dro, caravan elder. Our wares and coin are in short supply, but our camp is open to all who may seek to rest and be at ease.\n\nWhat does your heart seek that we may provide?
I commend your persistent efforts in searching for any suspicious activity.\n\nBut I will reiterate—I am most suspicious of that band of Khajiit and their eyesore of a camp nearby.

Please, can you speak with Ulfengar? I respect whatever decision he comes to, but without him, the mine may never recover.\n\nWe have a real chance here. With the queen's gland and a steady hand like Ulfengar's we can save Anchre Egg Mine, I know it!
Your work here is complete. I thank you for your service. If you would not mind returning to Thoryn Armas, please tell him that his presence is no longer needed in Kemel-Ze.

Meeting Hermaeus Mora represents a rare honor. The One Who Knows materializes in a delimited projection … ah. He chooses to manifest before few mortals. The threads upon which reality dangles are precarious indeed.\n\nWhat did Mora impart to you?
I've traveled with creatures for ages and still can't master the portal spells. Never crashed on Nirn before, though.

We should head for the chapel. If they actually set up a quarantine, that's the best place to do it.\n\nThe chapel is through the door and up the stairs. We'll need to be careful, though. The false prelate brought a lot of attendants with him.
Place the relics where I tell you. Once complete, our power shall flow through them. Hurry, our power wanes. We can feel it.
My head is spinning. My father is dead, a ghost trapped to this land? There must be some way to free him!
You know, flying around like Vorm would be a pretty useful trick. Think of all the pressure plates I could avoid! Although, not having hands would be tricky.
I made a promise to Abbot Ilvel. I can't return to Necrom Abbey without the relic those cultists stole. He's counting on me.
I think that should be all of them. Yes, one, two, three. Three books, I think. I don't remember, did I have more? It is probably fine.

This mysterious cipher mentioned the Divinatory Forums, a hidden wing of the Cloisters only known to overseers like myself and a privileged few ciphers.\n\nIt seems our best course of action is to follow in their footsteps.
Huzmargo will try and learn a bit more here. Go ahead, and he will catch up with you.
Question the mercenary. We must find our way past this obstacle. She may also reveal more of her employer's true intentions if she is willing to talk to you.
Ald Isra is on the west side of the peninsula. Home to the Mouths of the Telvanni Council.\n\nLet's hope our Mevei isn't one of them. I can only do with so much talking in one day.
Glyphics under consideration for unweaving are first sent to the Glyphic Assemblage. Yes, I know it's a misleading name. Now go on in! We haven't found the fated glyphic yet.

I was wondering if this was the day you meet me for the first time. You'll be pleased to learn you're just in time to help me.\n\nI know where the fated glyphic is, so there's no need for that silly boon. Besides, you look ridiculous.

Handy that the ciphers left those instructions. Each portal must lead to the shrines mentioned in the note. You can replenish the sacred tears at each of those shrines.\n\nKnow that the pool will reveal nothing until we add the tears.
Thanks for keeping me safe through all this. I don't think I could fight my way through these caverns on my own.
Surely you have better things to do than interrupt my research.
I defer to Meln regarding the inner workings of House Telvanni. See what he has to say on the matter.

Curse this incorporeal existence! I can see why most ancestors move on instead of haunting their descendants. My mortal memories are much harder to recall than I anticipated. I don't remember where to find those components. Not exactly ….

After I saw Dimik-ei to safety, I was lost. I remembered that Reynila and I came to Windhelm on a holiday, once. I just sort of drifted here.\n\nBut I tried to keep my head down. I must not have hidden well enough. How did you manage to find me?
Ah, this really is a lovely room. Truly Dunmeri, ancestral overseers abound. Now then, I must prepare. Maintain your distance.

The clues indicate that Tredecim is an aide to one of the masters who also sleeps in the servant quarters. They use kagouti musk to approach the northern nests to exchange messages with House Dres.\n\nUpdate Master Sulis, then join me at the nests.
That's everything. I need space to craft the spell. Deeper into the Forum we go!
So the Reformer's moved his operations to a crypt in Deshaan. Such an inviting prospect. I wonder if he's finished decorating yet?

I'm sure you and Sharp both find it very funny that I stayed out in the wilds, jumping at every noise, thinking it might be the last thing I hear!\n\nMy poor nerves. But I'm ready to put all this behind me. Did you get what I asked for?

Ah, the mouth of the mouthless. Couldn't quite get enough of the Telvanni halls of power, I see.\n\nWhile I appreciate what you did during the Conclave of Masters, I'm rather busy at the moment. Perhaps we can speak later?
Master Shelreni must be somewhere in this cavern.

The passage from Entila's Folly is the best chance we have of getting into my sanctum and stopping the adversary. \n\nIt's grown in power, cohort. I can already feel its ritual tugging at my fateline. Be ready for a fight.

I wish I could say this was the first time I found an old friend dead. But I cannot.\n\nFrom the spell lattice surrounding them, I believe Martina's research may have followed a similar path to my own. Let's take a look at that journal.
It's rude of Frielvi not to welcome us in. Well, we'll just have to find her and let her know.
This must be a shock to my son, but we must see this task through. Seek the Unquenchable Brazier that marks the entrance to this place.
Meln is right. I sense a malignant presence here. Be very careful.
Blightcrown's a threat, but Vaermina's a Prince! We should follow Vaermina and Torvesard into the Eye of Mora.

While the corruption still threatens me, I shall not turn away from my obligation. I started this with you. I plan to finish it with you, as well.\n\nBut we cannot understate the danger. If Scruut or I succumb, turn to Torvesard to aid you.
Once you collect the ingredients, I'll make the necessary preparations at my work station in Ald Isra. You know, getting the viscosity right and all that.

I don't like this any more than you do, but Torvesard went out of his way to show good faith. At least for a Dremora. And he helped Leramil. I appreciate that.\n\nI wonder if I can get him to tell me where to find the other half of the Fulcrum Obscura.
Damn this incorporeal existence I find myself trapped in! I'd give anything to be able to scratch my back or rub my nose. Who knew spirits could itch?
Of course. Just when I think I can go and rest my weary tentacles, the Great Eye has another task for me.\n\nTalk to Leramil, mortal. I need to confer with the Prince of Fate.

Have you found any ciphers or strange grimoires in your travels, stranger? There are tomes missing from our collection, and several ciphers as well. If you come across them in your travels, bring them back. I would be grateful.

Did I do all right, friend? I didn't seem too nervous or ramble or anything, did I? No, but I'm doing it now, aren't I? Of course I am.\n\nIf your travels ever bring you back to Necrom, please come and visit. I'll never forget our adventures!

While we contemplate the best method for tracking down Torvesard, there are two other tasks we must accomplish, proxy. One concerns updating the records of Apocrypha. The other requires us to return to Necrom and rectify the original anomaly of fate.
Away with you! I'm a Telvanni master and I have no time for the likes of you.
You've come at a wonderful time, traveler. That tome my father holds contains secrets the likes of which no mortal eyes have ever seen. Speak with him if you wish to know more.
I knew there was more to be done to prepare. I knew it.

More questions and fewer answers. I feel like I'm back in school.\n\nTho'at somehow became living ink. But how? And why? What a delightful mystery. Well, back to the books. Maybe they hold the answers.
As a Mouth it pains me to see the Master of my house in such a terrible situation. A sorry state of affairs really.
No question, I'll have a lot of filing to do after this.
We must find our way to the Mythos Vaults. That is where Torvesard found the first two glyphics. The third is there as well.
Proceed with caution, proxy. Ithelia's first creation shall not fall easily.\n\nScruut and I shall consult the appropriate texts and be prepared when you return with the shard.

Go on. Leramil opened a perfectly good portal. It'll get you to Fargrave and close to the Loom. Just watch out for those Mirrormoor Daedra. They're popping up everywhere lately.\n\nI'll wait here. Apprise your other allies when they arrive.
That's one of my legionaries. Listen to his report, comrade, while I keep an eye out for any of those Recollection bastards.
Was that the last relic? I was told to meet you and Leramil in Skingrad. Scruut provided me with a way to get there, so don't wait for me.
An unknown ruin, filled with potential perils? I'm excited already.
Splash them through the bars, quickly! The counteragent can be administered topically and this is the safest way. For us and for them.

I overheard a Recollection mage named Endegor mention a hidden shrine in the ruins. Something about a waterfall in the Flesh Gardens. Not the most pleasant appellation, but maybe we should start there?\n\nIt's somewhere to the north.

Mizzik hopes news of this case strikes fear in the heart of all criminals who think they have gotten away with their crimes. No matter how many years go by, justice is still hunting. And Mizzik will find you in the end.
It's remarkable seeing the famous Mizzik Thunderboots at work. He's already noticed more than I ever could have. If only the situation weren't so grim.
Let Mizzik see the note. An anonymous letter warning Lady Weatherleah of a traitor? This one wonders if they were able to meet before her death. It paints a disturbing picture of her final moments.
Use the Mirror of Truth! Show Ithelia how the power of the Loom has corrupted her.
Be careful, friend. Even with Hermaeus Mora's blessing, this is a dangerous place for mortals. The sooner we find Torvesard, the sooner we can return to our own world.

Gilraedal's Book of Obscure and Ancient Spirits. That's the book's name! Search around the courtyard behind the inn. Also, try the outbuilding in the far back. I found junk in there, too.\n\nBring me the book and we'll see if it has the recipe we need.
<<1>>'s death has saddened us all. I do hope we can settle this confusing matter of the will soon. She wouldn't want such stress and confusion lingering over her death.

It seems I was right to ask for your help. Despite the mysterious contents of the will, this is the most progress we've made all day. I trust you and Mizzik will see things through and we can proceed with this unpleasant business.

I greet you, chosen of fate. Hermaeus Mora calls upon you to defend this world and all of reality. A secret contained for ages is now free. Where the once-forgotten Prince walks, disturbance and disorder follow.\n\nAnd that is how we will find her.

If Balandrus is turning the townsfolk into bloodfiends to create a vampire army, then he must be keeping them in dens until he's ready to set them loose. Let's use the remaining alchemical components to destroy those dens.\n\nListen for their wails.

I know you, mortal. I followed your exploits and your fighting style is intriguing!\n\nThe Blind and her army of Blind Path cultists are here. I could easily deal with them, of course, but I'm curious. Are you interested in helping me?
Use the Lamp. I've got a feeling it might have something to reveal to us here.
Place the Skein of Secrets near the reality tear. Just try not to get sucked into the gaping maw. I don't have time to go back and fetch another mortal.

That was simple enough. Now I guess you need to use the spell scroll. That's supposed to release Abolisher's energy and heal this portion of the fabric of reality.\n\nYou know, I never knew such a thing existed. Well, other than a metaphor.
Beragon just turned up with a story about relics and welkynd stones and a Recollection stronghold in some Ayleid ruin. I had a hard time keeping up with it all. Maybe you should talk to him, comrade.
I wouldn't have noticed that passage if we hadn't examined that poor beast. We'd better see where the passage leads.
That stone you carry triggered a vision! How did you do that? Who was the woman?
Plenty of Recollection and Shardborn, but no sign of Nantharion or Vargas yet. I say we press on.

When we talk to King Nantharion, you take the lead. Tribune Alea is just as likely to start a war as an argument, and Vashabar isn't quite sure what to make of me. You, on the other hand, are an unknown quantity. That could work in our favor.

I found a journal among the necromancer's things. It revealed how the ritual began. Interrupting their spell should subdue the spirits and put an end to their plot. Read the journal, but be wary. Whatever killed the necromancers may still be inside.
Stay alert, comrade. There may be more than the Primordial Shattered Titan to deal in these old ruins.

We're off to face the Recollection again, my friend. Those fanatics seem to be everywhere these days.\n\nWe dealt with them once, so this should be easy, right? Let's head into the ruins and find Greenspeaker Sorilen.
I believe these crystals are manifestations of Ithelia's power. Her mere proximity is beginning to reshape her surroundings.\n\nWhether she intended to or not, Ithelia has left a trail we can follow.
We've come this far, comrade. Wherever that portal leads, It's time to finish this. Let's go.

The hunt is on, faithful assistant! With those notes, it's clear that the Recollection is stymied by that altar. I, of course, know how to activate it. We'll need a vial of blood, some sacred water and/or wine from the things they've dug up.
Beragon is free! Ask him what became of Tribune Alea, and what he found in his journey through the Many Paths. I doubt we can escape the way he came, but it is worth asking.

The Ithelia of this realty cannot even stand. She looks fully defeated, but I do not see any signs of an enemy.\n\nMaybe she can tell you what happened here. And make sure to ask about an ingredient for Sage's Dream.
You examined the newest grave markers. Give me your impressions, deputy.

I could still leap this railing and rush her if you think that would work. No, let's stick with the plan I outlined.\n\nOnce you're in position at the gateway, I'll distract the shardmarshal. Let's do this.

Stendarr's blood, it's good to see you. We need all the swords we can get. And anyone traveling with Tribune Alea is always welcome in a fight.\n\nThose Daedra are pummeling us. I need something done to hold them back.
Ciiril's my aunt. She owns the beer garden at the center of town. You can't miss her. \n\nY'ffre, the Singer himself, must have sent you. Thank you, traveler.
Hey, thanks. Not every Man or Mer that comes up the road would help a couple in the middle of a family fuss.

Those old mammoths should be in pod houses around the village. And don't worry if they get cranky. They're more bark than branch, if you take my meaning.\n\nWas there something else you wanted to talk about?
We're too late. Look at this place. And that smell, gods. \n\nSpread out. I don't think Hyacinth's still here, but maybe we can learn something about what happened.
Normal dro-m'Athra are challenge enough, but beyond that door lies something from my nightmares.\n\nIf any of my sisters or the Inquisitors remain standing, please, save them.
Inquisitors of the Torval Curiata hunt us? With help from one of the Twilight Cantors? Hrrm.
A traitor? An informant? Impossible. Unthinkable. \n\nThough if there is, perhaps a spellcraft of some kind could ferret them out. Hmm. Much to consider.
Once more into the breach, eh comrade? I still can't quite wrap my head around the end of reality, but if our actions will spare us from that fate, you can count on me.
I read that Fable of the Dragon too. This Luminary in the Wing of the Dragon … she's not a real Dragon, is she?\n\nA real Dragon in here! Can you imagine? No, no. Surely not.
I have no idea where we are. Stay close, traveler.
Losing a shaman is enough to cause uncertainty within a Goblin camp. But losing their totem too? No wonder this camp is so violent. \n\nI have some theories but nothing conclusive ….
You've seen the hidden annotations, then? And you know where you are going?

Snapdragon hasn't changed, not one iota! Her will remains as strong as the largest oak in the forest. \n\nThere's much I wish to discuss with her, but it seems she would like to have a word with you first.

Power can mean many things. Its meaning may change with each new day, each turn of the season. Ulfsild learned this hard lesson when the Scholarium slipped away.\n\nIf I am to teach you as I taught her, I must learn what power means to you.

I know that look. You've been tasked with busywork, haven't you?\n\nWell, it seems we're in the same boat. At least I'm fortunate to have it confined to the library, not wherever some mystical being decides to send me on a whim.
It seems like the Netch has stopped its pranks. Thank Magnus, and thank you. \n\nI suppose even children get tired of the same gag over and over.
I've been dying to ask you about your trial. Please tell me the Dragon gave you some sort of riddle to solve. I'm right here if you need me.
Keep your wits about you. Marcan Caelum is down here with us. I'm sure of it. And it's his territory.

The Divines can be harsh in their judgment. So they were when we were imprisoned, and so they are now that I know why my old comrades are dead.\n\nMy heart tells me there is one more judgment to come. I will see you at the vineyard.
Naku's dead? He owed me a drink. Wouldn't stop talking about all the plum brandy waiting for him after we finally got out of prison.\n\nWell. Maybe there's something left at the vineyard.

I adore my little menagerie, but I've always wanted to hand raise a young guzzard. Marcien still hasn't returned with my new baby.\n\nYou've already done more than enough. But if you do happen across a young guzzard, well, you know where to find me.

I convinced Regomor to take Noraine and return to Marbruk. He didn't need much persuading, so long as I promised to stay away until I was sure it would be safe. I suppose it's for the best.\n\nWas anyone waiting in the woods?

Xoryn cut off the route to the upper levels of the citadel. But, we can always search the sunken ruins.\n\nAnd—if the maps are accurate—there is a route from the ruins up to the ramparts. We won't be cut off for long.
So interesting, you are. What goes on within that mind of yours? What shapes your mind in just such a way? \n\nHmm, I suppose we will see. Place the fable upon the altar.
The Crow has warmed up to me, which is great. But now she wants to start tutoring me. It's like I'm back in my mother's home again.\n\nHow goes your trial with the Netch?
No tricks to these games. When people see what you've done it will inspire joy and floating.\n\nI believe Ulfsild herself would have approved, Not-Ulfsild.
Ulfsild must have left it behind with the annotations already visible. For some reason? Maybe if you meet that fox you can ask him about it.\n\nI put it on the table just over there. Give it a look.

How sweet to see this little spirit cat again. Ja'kh, yes?\n\nWe should keep this reunion brief, walker. The Inquisitors see you as the cause of the Rajaska outbreak. They have forbidden all contact. At the urging of High Cantor Viti, perhaps?

Why could you not keep hidden until that dull claw had departed? You have given him more to use against us.\n\nKnow that this one summoned you here to make amends and ask for your help. But since Grand Inquisitor Arsalan saw you, we must talk fast.
Good work. That's one less facet to worry about.
We've barely thawed out the Gryphon and now we're going on an adventure to steal magic from Daedric Princes! Isn't that exciting?\n\nOh, oh, I'd better start some stretches. Don't want to cramp up.
It's so good to be able to stretch my limbs, to breathe deep again. I need to go flying soon to truly shake off this chill.\n\nBut first. We have business, you and I.
You did it! They're pointing but I don't see anything. Maybe there's one of those focal points nearby?
I may tremble, walker, but I am not afraid. Talbira has walked this path before. She and Azurah guide me now.
This is amazing. The Labyrinthian, the real one anyway, was built by Shalidor to test potential archmages.\n\nAnd now here we are. Hah!
That journal says they're holding Snapdragon in a cell on the lower level. Let's go find her!\n\nAnd Auri-El help anyone who gets in our way.
Underlings first. Then, we deal with Wisteria.
She's really going to make me do this.\n\nMaybe we can follow them using their own ritual. Let's see what we can do.
Moon-Singer Talbira was entombed here when she passed. For me to invite her spirit to talk to us, we must locate her remains.\n\nLet us search quickly, tamiit.
Azurah must have seen the void in my heart when she sent you to me, for your heart surely beats for both of us.\n\nLet us resolve ourselves. Darkness has consumed too much this day.
Let us search carefully for Ravith-morna and her Rajaska chorus, tamiit. No doubt the path will be strewn with unimaginable dangers. My moonclaw tells me the darkness is strongest to the east.
So this is the meaning … of the fallen star? Do … what you can, stranger.
It seems young Zerith-var had quite a high opinion of himself.\n\nI can see how someone like Ravith would have been good for him back then. Just as you are good for him now.
In a way, I hope Prince Azah is wrong about Mezamma attacking the Earth Forge. But, my gut tells me he's spot-on.\n\nHead through the portal. And be ready. I won't let us be defeated again.
We'll return to the Mages Guildhall and regroup. We need to find Vanus and stop whatever else Mezamma is planning.
I don't know who the Worm Cult expected to fool with such a simple illusion spell. Certainly not the great Vanus Galerion.\n\nExamine the journal. Let's see what it contains.

I do not feel wary of this Vastarie, tamiit. She seems wise in her wanderings.\n\nWe need not tell her of my connection to the Hidden Moon. It is not only difficult to believe, but we clearly have more pressing matters to tend to now.

Welcome back, comrade. Before, you helped me realize that the world doesn't stop just because someone we respected and cared about is no longer with us.\n\nNow that we know the enemy, the time has come to take the battle to the Worm Cult.
If you find some gems, take them right to Khalisah. She does great work and she's always been a really good friend. \n\nShe'll make something that will impress Guendeline, I just know it.
Heloise was such a kind soul. I can't believe they turned her into a monster!\n\nDamn the Montclairs! Damn them all to Oblivion!

You know, there was a time when I was young when I thought being a king would just be a barrel of laughs. The coin, the power and all its trappings—it looked like such fun.\n\nIt's not, though. If I don't escape these stone walls soon, I'll go mad.
I'll stay here and do whatever I can to slow the poison.\n\nIf the spriggan turns into a lurcher, we'll have no choice but to kill her.

Can you believe this? The duke's apparently run off to avoid facing me. After what he's done, I suppose I shouldn't be surprised.  \n\nTell me though, is the city safe? Have the Imperials spies been dealt with?
There's no time to waste. We must strike now, or the Imperials will have time to make preparations.
I know what to do with them as well. I'm selling them to another family to run.\n\nThis place has seen more than its fair share of strife. I'm done.

Before you alert the king, speak to Vizier Bolura. She is a trusted friend, and she can tell you how best to approach the king with such news.\n\nTu'whacca's Throne is sacred and if necromancy is involved, this will disturb the king greatly.

Hello. I am glad to meet you. Tu'whacca, in his wisdom, bid me to come here and await your arrival.\n\nTu'whacca says you will save the Alik'r desert from the Withered Hand, but first, there are things you must learn from the spirits of this place.
Must be off. More dreugh could arrive at any time.
Just one more to go. Only <<1>> remains.\n\nYou've saved the best for last.
The ghosts of the Alessian army still haunt this place. \n\nIt's been an age since the Battle of Glenumbra Moors raged here, yet the spirits linger.
It's best this way. I did not want the responsibility, and <<1>>'s decision seemed wise to me.\n\nPerhaps my little brother is smarter than I've given him credit for.
My father's alive! What have those Bloodthorn bastards done to him?
You were too successful, my friend, and now Faolchu is—pardon the pun— howling mad.
We cleansed the land around the tree, but this isn't over. Corruption still festers at the Wyrd Tree's heart.
The dead have returned to the sea, yes?\n\nIldani's moment is slipping away quickly, moment for a good opportunity. Are you interested in a good opportunity?
I'd pray to Arkay, but at this point, I'm not exactly sure what that means, so I'll just say … good luck!
You again! Truly, the gods have afflicted me with a terrible burden.\n\nIf you release me, I expect <<1>> will appreciate my return. You are so very good at returning things to him, are you not?
The woods welcome you. Know that the creatures here are neither enemies nor friends. There are hunters … and prey.
I thought he'd be here by now … where is Stenwick?
Well, now, wasn't that fun? I'd fight alongside you anytime. \n\nBut I'd rather carouse. You do carouse, don't you?
Ah, you're back! I was worried.\n\nYou want to try scouting to the south again?
I cannot trust myself to make this choice, the loss of Sir Etienne is too near to my heart.
There's a lot I don't understand about what happened, but at least Draven and I are together, the way we belong.
Remember, Draven isn't quite himself yet, and in this state, he endangers the entire town.\n\nI know it sounds harsh, but only severing his link to the village will spare the rest of us.
You look like you've got something on your mind. Make it quick. I've got my hands full already.
Tanval's at the tombs. Guard him! I've got invaders to repel.
With my ancestor's skull, I have a powerful weapon—the ultimate weapon!\n\nI just need a little more time.
You made the right decision.
If Furon's plan works, we'll have a defense like the Covenant has never seen.
I see. That soft Argonian convinced you. Will we throw away our weapons next? Just remember what might have been.
Honor to you and your house, f'lah. For all you've done, there's nothing I can do to repay you.
A stranger? Here?
Um, don't wait for me. I'll find Mavos when my bravery returns.\n\nIt should be back any moment now.
The Covenant smells the storm on the air. Are you ready to bring down the sky on General Serien?
Have you honored your ancestors recently?\n\nThe Tribunal demands we remember our heritage.
Now the long task of restoring Heimlyn Keep begins. My thanks, traveler.
I will join my people soon. Thank you again.
When <<1>> has the soul gem array in her hands, we'll see to the salvation of our village.
Who are you? What gives you the right to barge into my home?
Outstanding! Once you hand the <<z:1>> to <<2>>, we can make sure something like this never happens again.
There's something wrong with Tiril. I … I'm afraid to go near him.
I can already tell you've learned something. Opens your eyes, doesn't it novice?
The magic wielders spend their time conjuring spells and digging in the mud. As if binding our citizens wasn't enough, they also defile our land!
This is magic I do not understand, far from the waters of my home. You are brave to walk the river's edge.
<<1>> will be safe for its pilgrims once again. I am saddened for the Altmer. I will see that his body is properly buried here. \n\nHe has suffered enough. Perhaps now there will be peace for him.
If you're looking for work, you should speak with <<1>>. She's in charge of teaching the new recruits the ropes.
We've managed to infiltrate the fort, but there's still more work to be done.
Keep your voice down. The Dominion has taken <<1>>. We can't afford to be caught.
Excellent work with <<1>>.Let me know when you're ready for another contract.
The spirits are returning to the Hist tree. Soon, I will follow. Our bodies may be gone, but we have been saved.\n\nMay friendly branches shade your path.
The mine's up and running, thanks to you! Those little Goblins are as busy as little bees.\n\nCould I interest you in some bulk iron ore? I'll make you a good deal.

Who are you? I saw you using the puzzle stones … how did you unravel their secrets? You don't look like one of the Renrijra, but I warn you, you may be playing with things you can't possibly understand.
Curse it, why can't I pry this open?
Comrade! We have need of you. Will you fight by our side?
Are you well, comrade? Did it harm you?
Hmm, these runes were drawn in the eighth … no, the ninth house. Have to take that into account.
It will take time for the Companions to recover. But we will, as we always have.
We've got to get to Stral. End Stral, and we end the Reachmen's threat.
Have you spoken with any of the villagers?
We're here. The villagers are safe, for the moment, but the Covenant's still coming.\n\nWe've got to get word to Davon's Watch.
Hee hee! Did you see the butterflies? They all flew away!
I'll keep working to open this door.\n\nGo close the portals. Hurry!
Well, comrade. We still live. And I now—ha! It's almost too ridiculous to say out loud.\n\nI am the Guildmaster.
You've been gone for a while. Tell me you found something useful.

You've saved me. Saved me from myself. And in some way, you've saved my daughter too. I feel her love again, like a balm upon my heart.\n\nThere's nothing in this world that could repay you in kind. I will pray for you for the rest of my days.
Rala will release Scales when the sun sets. We'll give her the potion and hope for the best.\n\nNow to more important matters. We must discuss my father's creations.
Well met. I thank you for the assistance, but this place is teeming with Daedra.\n\nYou should leave if you value your life.
<<1>>'s charms claim another fool. I don't know how she does it.\n\nWell, now that you're here we can get on to the next part of Sal's plan.
This started out as a nightmare, but now … everything's different. I never thought I'd get the chance to tell my father how I felt. It's like a weight has been lifted.\n\nWe should keep moving.
We must rescue the Silvenar. Free Ambassador Raen!
We did our best to save the Silvenar; now we must work together to free him!\n\nPlease, free Ambassador Sariel. Perhaps the three of us can save the Silvenar.
You've collected the shards! Good. Please, talk to <<1>> while I prepare myself for the confrontation to come. She knows what needs to be done.
My, don't you look all spiffy! I have to say, you do look good in a uniform.
Get back my silk from Turil. Hopefully he puts up a fight and you have to murder him.\n\nYou know, I'd pay you extra if that happens.
The bandits could move their camp at any moment. Don't let them get away!
I'll never forgive myself if <<1>> comes to harm.
You can find her in the hall in Wayrest, comrade. May the Eight protect you.
That was the first step. We still have much to do.
The stone on the pedestal holds something. An ancient evil. Be careful.
Valaste is working the problem out of the Marbruk Guildhall. See you there, Adept.

Lieutenant Ehran's gone. Damn idealistic bastard … I tried to protect him, but he wouldn't let me.\n\nLook, we've got to do what he asked. We must free Velyn Harbor. But do something for me first. Kill the bastard that killed him.
You have the heart of a true trickster!
You're not dead. That makes you my new friend.
<<1>> is off limits. Please make your way back to the main road.
When that Daedric influence is gone, it should be safe to restore the village. My poor neighbors.
A town full of ill folk. Mercenaries patrol the streets, and my boy is in the quarantine cave. Good thing I don't believe in curses.
Fair day, visitor. I'm Astanya, watch captain. I'll need you to state your name for the record. \n\nExtra precautions with Queen Ayrenn in town. You understand.
You ready for a harder task, my friend? Ready for a mission worthy of the Queen's Eyes?
Thank you for hearing our stories. I look forward to hearing your own one day.
Well, this isn't good.
The future holds our salvation, and you have a part to play.
I will ensure Angof finds safe passage into the city.\n\nAnd do not fear him. He can be trusted. I … I just know it.
Ah ha! Mim knew you would make the right decision. Let the evil one rot in there. \n\nBut this one wonders, what do we do now?
Speak to me again when you have completed An-Jeen-Sakka's trial.
The antidote will be ready soon. Then we can get everyone back on their feet.
Please see <<1>>, if you have questions. I don't know you, outsider.

Just think about it. Please.\n\nDon't kill any of the Shadow Walkers and I promise I'll go with you when you leave. You could use someone like me! And I want to make Molag Bal pay for what he's done to my people.
Ah, you've returned.
Could you do that again? \n\nBut with more blood. More.

If you're serious about stopping <<1>> and freeing my crew, I won't turn down your help.\n\nBut from everything we saw, <<Ac:2>> is a series of death traps. If the undead guarding the place hadn't surprised the mutineers, we'd never have escaped.
I should also be able to join you in Hammerfell. Here in Tamriel, Sheogorath has no power to contain me.
Good timing. You saved my neck, whether you meant to or not.
Dollie thinks it'd be funny to kill everybody. I don't think she understands the meaning of the word.
I was beginning to wonder if you'd ever show up. My lord seems to derive amusement from my annoyance.\n\nYou are here to retrieve a tome for that … Shalidor person, correct?
Damn this place. Another dark fire door.
Go, my new friend. We will be fine for now. Knowing Khali, she is hip-deep in bodies and her sword arm grows weak. Just the way she likes it.
You're standing a little close, don't you think?

King Emeric falling ill cannot be a coincidence. Vaermina is raising the stakes, making a final bid for power by assaulting the king himself. \n\nI am out of my league. I will go to the king's side, but we must seek Azura's help.
All right. Now, on to my problem. There are some rats in my well. I can hear them scraping around down there at the bottom.
Hallowed, this one is glad you are here. This beacon has an intensity to its corruption …. It is teeming with the energies of the Dro-m'Athra. \n\nShazah must perform the purification.
Better you than me, Hallowed. I've never been much for the spiritual.
Did you get any of those ghosts to talk? What did you find?
Shuzura is sure it will turn out to be nothing, but <<1>> must always get his way. Luck to you.
What do you want, stranger? You are in Ezzag's light. This one has chores to do.
This is not a good time. I have to focus right now.
This seems to be some horrible vision of the future, yes?

Razum-dar simply cannot believe a little weasel like Pelidil could come up with such a genius plan, but we will find a way to stop him.\n\nThis one will make his own way to Seaside Sanctuary. He will see you there.

Feel like I spend more time in the damn Thalmor Headquarters than I do outdoors these days. \n\nThey need to get their arses in order and secure the city or I'm going to ask the queen to send them packing.
Perhaps you can help my agents in the field. If you can find Vadeem-Kal or Silent-Moss, I'm certain they can use you. Look on the far side of the Dominion camps.
Thank you so much! Has anyone ever told you you're pretty great? Because you are.

What a sacrifice! To think the villagers actually poisoned themselves in order to poison the Blackroot clan … it may be morbid, but it's also brilliant.\n\nOf course, that really doesn't help us return the Blackroot warriors to their graves, does it?
Cadwell's plan worked! We might actually pull this off!
I await word on the Elder Scroll of Ni-Mohk. Surely our warriors will not fail in this challenge.
Have you made a decision, outsider?
Rescue my friends from the ogrims and then we'll deal with the Overseer.
Turns out my squad were the ones who found me. Ever consider a career as a Dominion marine? You'd make quite the scout.\n\nMy squad said you were looking for <<1>>. Have you found him?
That barrier must have activated when the dead began to rise.\n\nIt looks like the cycle of the two moons is important, somehow. Perhaps that's the key to disrupting the barrier!
You disappoint me outsider, choosing to side with murderers and thieves instead of us.\n\nMy people will no longer sit back and hope for peace. We will take our children back! You just watch and see!
I can't wait to hear this. This should be good.
Cari was right about you.
It's hard to keep track of the new faces since the hurricane, but I don't believe we've met.\n\nWelcome to <<1>>. May your stay here be full of warm winds and soft sand.
The crowds can't get enough of you, Mysterious Stranger!

Then come quickly. I left my father's instructions in my tent. I was gathering ingredients one-at-a-time, but together we can gather everything much faster.\n\nMeet me at my tent in the camp and we will go from there.
My friend, I could not be happier to see you again. A veteran Eye is just who I need by my side today.
Do you work here? Are you a field hand?
We can't trust this one. Her pleasing form hides a hideous and powerful monster.
You must not linger here, Moon Hallowed. Now that you know your place in the world, you must go to Fort Grimwatch. You must stand against the darkness with the Lunar Champions.
Could you progress any slower through this installation full of deadly Daedras?
Hm. You killed Andur? That's not supposed to happen.
These are uncertain times. Without our queen to guide us, we would be lost. I pray our enemies don't get their way.
Be mindful of your step. This forest has been most unkind to guests.
Enjoy your bath. We'll meet you at the manor when you're finished here.
Keep your wits about you. Things are not as they appear.
Ahh, this one can see the light of the moons reflected in your eyes. The Moon Hallowed walks among us.
How many did we lose today? I … I can't even count.\n\nI fear going back home. Seeing who survived and who didn't. It's all just so … overwhelming ….

This is the entrance to the Valenheart. It seems the Shade of Naemon has taken care to ensure his work is not disturbed.\n\nThis is an ancient Ayleid barrier. We'll need to activate the pedestals to pass.
Are you here about the refugees? I've already explained this to three inspectors from Elden Root. Until their status is resolved, the Argonians are to remain within the enclosure.
The meeting! I nearly slept through it. <<1>> wants to discuss the grumbling about the barricades.\n\nYou should come, see how we govern ourselves.
You're quite light on your feet. Let me see the eggs.
So we stop the ritual or die trying? All right.\n\nAn honor to fight beside you. You'd make an outstanding marine.
After trapping <<1>> in his crypt, this "<<2>>" will be no trouble at all.
Don't mind me, little mortal. It's just that I find you so … fascinating!
When <<1>> sees me, she'll be surprised! Hopefully not enough to scatter me across <<Ac:2>>. Again.\n\nIt'll be fine!
Speak with Gilraen if you have something to say, stranger. I've got wounded to rip from death's jaws.
Gilraen's our leader. She speaks for us.
We should stop the Sea Viper ritual before they destroy all life on <<1>>. It never gets easier, does it?
Everything's been prepared. Are you ready to travel to the summit?
Well met. The Fighters Guild will handle security for the summit on Stirk. As a neutral party, we were the logical choice.
I say, you do get into some wild adventures, don't you?\n\nThis place is so odd. Did you know that the fire here is actually warm? Brilliant!
This is some horror. A vision of the future, right?
Know that this is <<1>>'s forest and we are his Briars. If you want to join us, you'll need to pay your respects.
The Elder Scroll of Ni-Mohk still rests in enemy hands. How can this be?
We should get to the abbey. Kasura and I have much to discuss.
The Elder Scroll of Ghartok is ours at last. The eyes of Akatosh shine on the Covenant!
First a doppelganger of Tharn, then one of me? What are these horkers playing at? \n\nIt's a wonder Sai hasn't lost his mind, completely. Let's keep moving and hope he still has a soul to save.
Well, well, well. Wasn't that a charming little scene? I can't wait to mock … to tell Titanborn all about it.
I had to see this with my own eyes. These refugees tell a savage tale.
Bears leave rather distinctive tracks, don't they? I can't imagine they'd be hard to spot.
Onward to the Dragonguard Tomb. The first shrine is there, and we must consecrate both before the vault door can be opened.
I've heard stories of this place, but I've never had the opportunity to come here. I trust Sai had good reasons for placing the amulet in a place such as this.
All that remains is to deal with the Mad Architect himself. \n\nHe waits deep below us, heavily defended and well-armed. But I'm a betting man and I think you can beat him. You're our only chance.
<<1>>'s soldiers spoke of welkynd stones in the area. If you can get me there safely, perhaps we'll learn how they relate to <<2>>.
Ah, wonderful! You're just in time.\n\nI'm in urgent need of assistance. In fact, I just said to my man Stibbons, "Stibbons, we are in urgent need of assistance." And here you are!
I don't think Uela's going to see this coming. Once the crows tell us how to find her, we'll soon be gnawing on her rotten little bones.
Swear you will free me, and I will allow you entry to my prison. I would speak to you with my true face.
The Dragonguard? As I recall, their primary purpose was to enforce the delusions of whomever sat upon the Ruby Throne in any given week.
Conniving cat, bargaining for those bows! I hope I don't come to regret this!
Jode's Chariot keeps <<1>> safe for trade. Keep your nose clean, or end up in the stocks.
While I am glad the Thalmor have not intervened, Jode's Chariot has been insufferable of late! We will need to adapt—and soon—if we are to keep up!
With the portal closed, we've stopped Reezal-Jul from sneaking more Montclair troops into the city. \n\nIt is frustrating, though, that Reezal-Jul slipped away. That Argonian is sly and cowardly.

There you are. If you expected to find us scaling the walls already, I'm sorry to disappoint.\n\nDon't get me wrong—we considered taking a stab at it, but with our … limited numbers, I don't really think that plays to our strengths.
Oh, don't look so shocked. Haven't you ever seen anyone enjoying a meal before?\n\nDo not give Adusa such a look! We are not all Montclairs, you know.
I am busy with matters of state. Go trouble someone else.
The wards are back, and the bears are no longer hostile to us.
Your journey is dangerous. Be wary of the guardians. They guard the temple fiercely with their lives.\n\nI take comfort in knowing their death is for a good cause.
Stendarr smite them, the Goblins took my reagents! It would serve them right if they ate them, the wretches!\n\nHmm, that gives me an idea.
Laranalda sent word. The Heart of Anumaril shall be held by the Elden Root Mages Guild until we require it. Now we must find a divine spark and an Ayleid source of power.
Now—we have some grim business to discuss. I pray that you will have the strength of will to see this through.
Oh, stranger … what have you done?

Swearing that oath was never going to bring Esmaeel back, but I hope he's comforted in knowing I've avenged his honor.\n\nHe never quite understood the fiercer side of my Orc tendencies. What those fiends did to him—I pray he rests in peace.
Good to see you again, old chum! Truly!
We can't let that maggot-eating bastard Gavendien get away with this!\n\nOld Sagabar wasn't so tough after he got into the stocks. He told me where Gavendien went, where their camp is.

What will I do now? Without the Shornhelm Guard I'm nothing. I told the general. I'm a soldier, not a recruiter. But now I'm to be discharged if I fail? It's not right.\n\nI've tried to do my duty, but I can't force people to enlist.
You found a key? Very good. Enter the ruins and I'll follow right behind you.
The Baron can be a harsh man, but I always thought him to be fair and even-handed. To throw his own son in the dungeon for crimes he doesn't remember—that may be extreme, even for Alard.
Gods! It's like something out of a story!
It's been horrible. Thank goodness help arrived.
That key should open the old gate and let us into the quarantine. Let's go see what the Maulborn are hiding in there.
My brother is gone. And I fear that my uncle doesn't have much longer. This plague … it's taken so many good people.
This is horrible. I wanted to save my wife, but I never expected it would be like this.

Ah, you're here at last. Do not be confused. We foresaw your arrival, the one who has walked across the planes and faced down gods.\n\nOr do we speak of things still to come? Time is much more fluid among the stars.
Your aura is different, stronger, more connected to this world than others I have met.\n\nMost interesting.
I wish there had been another way. Poor, stubborn Ilthag. He should have taken the gold.
We're not finished here yet. We still need to destroy the nests to make sure this part of the process can't be duplicated.
You're back! Hoo, that's quite a smell. Make sure to talk to me later if you want to burn that … everything.
Have the itching ivies and nibbling bugs laid you low, or do you return from Selene's Web Undaunted?
You should avoid cutting a rough maple log with a wasp nest inside.\n\nIt's rather unpleasant. So are the lotions you'll need for the stings.
Return to me when you learn the recipe. Commit it to memory. Then we'll speak of ingredients.

<You notice a prominent handbill on the requisition board.>\n\n"King Jorunn extends an invitation! Master crafters await you in <<1>>! They offer free training for those new to a craft, and free certification for accomplished crafters!"
Amazing! You were actually able to navigate the Dwemer defenses? You must either be exceptionally strong or exceedingly lucky. Either way, I can make use of that.
I am Kurog, king of the Orsimer.
Look at you, not an Orc!
Did you find <<1>>?
You're finally here! You stink of blood, but I thought you'd smell fouler with everything you've been through.\n\nYou'd think I'd be used to it by now.

<You notice a prominent handbill on the requisition board.>\n\n"Queen Ayrenn bids you welcome! Masters of the craft await you in <<1>>! New crafters shall be trained! Accomplished crafters will be certified! All at no cost to you!"
Let's keep searching the barrow. I'm sure the missing pieces are around here someplace!

And here we are again, at the foot of Sorrow's insidious climb. With your help, I hope we can make it farther up the mountain this time.\n\nIf all goes well, we should reach Torug's shrine before Stibbons sets out our evening meal.

Oh, splendid, more fodder for the mountain. I suppose that means we're going to make another attempt to reach that wretched summit.\n\nGo present yourself to my lady. She should be on her way down the trail any moment now.

Most of the monuments up here are inscribed with three-stanza epitaphs. It was a common practice.\n\nThis rubbing appears to be Torug's first stanza! It's written in Old Orcish, proclaiming the memorial's inaccessibility. They found Torug's shrine!
The arse end of Wrothgar was never high on my list of places to visit. But here I am.\n\nLucky me.
My ancestral home … beyond that wall?\n\nWe're in this together now, right? Let's go.
What do you think? Have you figured out how to solve the puzzle? I'm still working on it myself.\n\nThere's an old Orc fable about a torch, an owl, and a hammer, but I don't remember the details.

Given all that we've uncovered, I think Molag Bal's plan is clear. He wants to breach the Dragonfire Cathedral to destroy the Sublime Brazier. If he succeeds, the Dragonfires will never be relit, and Mundus will be exposed to Daedric attack forever.
My mother warned me. She said that Wrothgar was cold and dangerous and would be the death of me. I should have listened to her.
Cold … so very, very … cold!
Now I know what roast horker feels like!\n\nThey kept stoking the fire, making it hotter and hotter. I was almost ready to agree to whatever they wanted. Almost.
So you're to replace my husband as chief? You owe it to <<1>>'s memory to solve his murder.
Did you happen to see a tattooed Breton on your way here? Stupid hat, droopy moustache … carries a mage staff he doesn't know how to use? Answers to "Hamelyn Serpe?"
Very well, then! Let's see how long you can last. \n\nGive us a good show, won't you?

Welcome! It makes me smile to meet an Orc with an interest in the history of our land and its people. And you found the notice! Wonderful!\n\nOf course, the House of Orsimer Glories will be even more impressive once all the exhibits have been filled.
Who knew Wrothgar had a problem with crazed cultists? I certainly didn't!
Behold, master—it's that belligerent young mortal whose career on Nirn you've been following.
Well, well … that's quite a bundle you've got there! Get that meat to Bagrugbesh as soon as you can. We've got a lot of mouths to feed.
<<1>>'s been waiting for you. Talk to her and she can release your reward.
I have extended my invitation and offered a gift of worth beyond counting. Do you accept?\n\nTurning your back on me now would be most … unwise.
I'll arrange our transport to my former Sanctuary. Meet me near the gates of Anvil when you are ready to depart.\n\nAnd thank you for agreeing to help me.
So you're the new initiate. Hmm. You're certainly cuter than the last one.
Yes, I'm still here. But don't worry. I plan to be in on the action when you get inside the Cathedral. As a matter of fact, I'll be leaving to meet up with Astara shortly.
Dry land, finally. Colder than I expected … very, very cold.\n\nThe manor should be up ahead. Are you ready?
If we're going to <<1>>, I can help.\n\nThe Iron Wheel can always spot imposters. It's not the uniform, it's the mannerisms and protocol they follow. It's all part of their training.
Go with Loche if you think you can get us in another way. Otherwise the only way is forward.\n\nWe'll be in the shadows waiting for our opportunity.

Hilde isn't here. Where could she be? I'm certain this is where she was headed when she left the Sanctuary.\n\nLet's ask around and see if anyone saw her. Hopefully someone can point us in a new direction.
Long is the night, Sister.
Get moving, Initiate. The Matron has a task for you. She expects you at the Sanctuary.

Ah, Initiate. I should be more pleased that the Grand Sermonizer is dead, but I can't help feeling that a storm gathers on the horizon.\n\nElam mentioned that the contracts were stacking up. I suspect he'd appreciate your help, if you'd be so kind.
Ah, I heard we had a new initiate on the premises! I was just checking my notes and realized that details concerning you are sorely lacking.\n\nWe'll need to rectify that before too long.

If there are secrets to glean from the Black Dragon's journal, Green-Venom-Tongue will find them.\n\nGo and complete a contract or two. By the time you return, I'm sure we'll have decided on our next course of action.

Ah, you're here at last. Do not be confused. We foresaw your arrival, the one who has walked across the planes and faced down gods.\n\nOr do we speak of things still to come? Time is much more fluid among the stars.
Your aura is different, stronger, more connected to this world than others I have met.\n\nMost interesting.
I wish there had been another way. Poor, stubborn Ilthag. He should have taken the gold.
We're not finished here yet. We still need to destroy the nests to make sure this part of the process can't be duplicated.
You're looking hearty and hale! And a bit frosty at the edges.
An Ashlander? Could a heathen actually threaten one of the Tribunal? Such a thought makes my stomach hurt!

Savarak's Black Snail mercenaries are everywhere, so be careful. At least a few of them will be patrolling the halls of the manse.\n\nYou'll more than likely have to do a lot of sneaking, so don't forget to stretch?

Welcome, sera. Sorry about the mess. Believe it or not, this place feels like a palace compared to my old slave quarters.\n\nWith any luck, I won't stay here long. I've hatched a plan that might catapult me to the rank of House retainer!
"The battle ends before it begins when you control the field of battle," according to my Odes of War.\n\nThat means it's time to take your place now so that we can perform the divination ritual.
I expected to hear the White-Gold Tower topple from here. I suppose you'll tell me you left it standing.
Haven't you left yet? The sites at Balmora, Ald'ruhn, and Barilzar's tower aren't going to investigate themselves.
Be quick about your work in there and be wary of traps. Ancestor spirits are not known for their hospitality.
Our little queen-to-be is stirring! No time for pleasantries!
When we find something valuable, make sure you wait for me to examine it before you do anything rash.\n\nI'd hate to see something unfortunate happen to you.
I need to record my observations of the experiment you just helped me complete, but I can spare a few more clicks of the Great Gear for such an able assistant.\n\nIs there something else you need?
Chodala has been revealed as a failed Nerevarine, but that hasn't dissuaded him from his reckless course of action. As long as he wields the staff, he shall be unstoppable.
If you've come to plunder these ruins, I'm afraid you'll be disappointed. One of my competitors has really made a mess of things.
We'll be right behind you, or at least Neramo will be. I'll be busy keeping him alive.\n\nKeep your guard up and watch for traps.

You can find Lord Drono's townhouse right here in Balmora. He's away on business, but that doesn't mean you don't have to be careful. Just get in, get the registry, and get back out again.\n\nI'll be here, anxiously awaiting your return.
I hope to bring honor back to the station of governor and shall do my best to restore the people's faith in us.\n\nThank you again for your part in all this.
I always thought my worst humiliations were behind me. I guess I was wrong.

Ah, right on time.\n\nI'm joking, of course. Honestly, I feared you wouldn't come. Divination and prophecy yield few certainties. Still, this vision was clearer than most. You and I. This room. The scent of ale and woodsmoke. Yes, this was meant to be.

Best not to be found conspiring against my wife anymore today. Easier to deny having ever met you when you're not standing right there, you understand.\n\nBut if she happens to corner you, take our secret to the grave for your liege!

How much longer do I need to stay here? Social situations have never been my strong suit.\n\nI want to get back to my tower and experiment with this wonderful gift Vivec bestowed upon me. I already have ideas on how to improve magical transportation!
I hope you catch Gascone soon. We need to know what he knows. Immediately.
Once again, you emerge from the Shadow Cleft unscathed and aglow with the luster of success. The apostles remain in your debt.

We have that bastard, Gascone, jailed in the east wing. He's spent most of his time sulking, but he might speak to you. You did spare his life, after all.\n\nAsk him about this shadowy pool you described. If there are others like it, we need to know.
Chirrhari taught me so much before she was selected to enter the Wellspring. If anyone can alleviate my concerns about this place, it's my old friend.

No, don't bother relaying your warning. Your concern, while touching, is unnecessary. I've been seeking the artifact for months now. I know the dangers well.\n\nI'll need a strong hand to continue the search, though. I think you will do nicely.
I believe the primary stars were attracted to the chambers they were formed in. Try searching the halls around these chambers for the ones we need.\n\nAnd trust me, the stars are pretty hard to miss.
Followed us all the way to the Clockwork City, huh? Look, I'm flattered, but if you wanted to talk to us you could have just sent a letter.\n\nJoking, of course. It's great to see you.

Well, if it isn't my second favorite assistant! What a fortuitous turn of events. I shouldn't be surprised. You have a knack for appearing when I need you most. \n\nI take it you haven't found a sponsor yet? Maybe we can help each other.

So you're a citizen now? Well done.\n\nI heard something about a constable tossing people down sewer drains. Even in this shrine to knowledge, drooling idiots bumble their way to power. Ludicrous. Moving on, I require your services once more.
Destroy our foes, the Exarchs of Dross, and I will take you to the Great Prize! Go!

Come in search of a hot meal? Hard to come by here, I know, but mark my words, one day there'll be more than just the aroma of bubbling brass wafting out of Slag Town. People are going to come from far and wide to try what's making it.

Oh, hello there. Didn't notice you came in.\n\nAfraid I'm quite busy at the moment with my newest discovery, so I don't have much time for idle chatter. Unless you're interested in factotums and their creation process, it's best you leave.

You have no idea how much Raz appreciates a good assistant. In this line of work, decent help can be the difference between life and death. Not that the work is dangerous. Much.\n\nNow, let's go investigate the monastery!

Well, I was about to portal to Alinor for a proper meal, but since you're here now, we might as well discuss that message.\n\nIt came from Marieve, an Oracle of the Wyrd. I usually avoid soothsayers, but Marieve possesses a genuine talent.
I must inform you that I'm not trained in battle. My magical talents lean more toward teaching and healing than anything as crude as combat.\n\nJust so you understand ….
Can I help you with something? I'm sorry, it's been a trying week and I have little time for pleasantries.\n\nIf you wish to join the Guild, you can speak to the leader of our local chapter, <<1>>.
Go ahead. Just pour the elixir onto the pearl. Our magic will do the rest.
There you are! I have wonderful news … maybe! The book—it changed!

Auri-El himself would smile on your kindness. \n\nNow, we haven't a moment to waste. The House of Reveries is hosting auditions this very moment. You must present yourself to Alchemy, the audition master, and impress her with your performance.

I know who you seek, Hopeful, but you will not find fair Rinyde here. She has departed for the moment, which means we can speak freely of your quest to find her brother, Larydel.\n\nYou wish to stop him from joining the House of Reveries.

Thank you for accepting my offer. I'm quite excited to be heading my own expedition. Telenger may have a great mind, but sometimes he's a bit … much.\n\nIt's nice to finally be able to break free from being just his assistant.
I don't see any new tracks. She didn't try returning to the enclosure.\n\nFind anything that might put us on her trail?
Once we've unbarred the battlement gates, we'll be able to strike at Urlsar.
I'm sorry, but my experiments on the blood may take a while. I'm sure you can handle this house-search without me. Just keep a keen eye out for anything suspicious.

Oriandra doesn't trust me right now, and I can't blame her.\n\nYou interrogate Leythen. Get him to tell you why they killed the Ritemaster. We need answers! Otherwise, I—I'm not sure what we should do.

Thanks again for all the help, my friend! We may not have a treaty yet, but the Proxy Queen seems extremely eager to see Rigurt again.\n\nJust between us, for a haughty High Elf, she handles mead almost as well as a Nord battle maiden!
See if you can find a way into the Conservatory. I'll try to keep Talomar out of trouble.
Were you able to speak to Tableau? Did she mention me? Ah—I mean, is she all right?
Don't just stand there, help me! I can't do this by myself. The mind trap is just too strong.

I thought I heard something down here, but the sound must have carried up from this tunnel. It looks formed by erosion. Maybe related to the sinkholes?\n\nWhat about you? Did you find anything else upstairs?

Hey, stranger. Been wondering where you got off to. It's good to see you again.\n\nSorry if I'm a little on edge. That Elf, Lirendel, just dumped a barrel of insults on my head. Mark me—I'm going to knock that loose tongue right out of his mouth.
If Vile and his Hound have already betrayed us, I'll turn that mangy mutt into a throw rug!
Don't look at me. I've never had a lot of luck in museums.
Are you ready for another journey to Tamriel, initiate?
Let's get started, shall we? After all, a good polish takes time.\n\nFirst, you must gather the required materials needed to create your ring. A true artisan starts from scratch, after all.
You've saved me some headache, newcomer. My thanks.
Thanks for your help. If you ever need me to hold your place in line or something, I'm your girl.
Have you spoken with Loremaster Celarus? I'm certain he has a task prepared for you.
Be cautious in Rivenspire. I hear there are more vampires than people out there.
We haven't a moment to lose. If Josajeh activates the Staff of Towers, the results could be cataclysmic.

Eshundir the smuggler considers Cyrodilic Collections to be bad for his business, but he knows an awful lot about obscure Argonian antiquities. While you show him those relics, I want to refer to a book on the legends of Black Marsh I read once.
Dryskin! Didn't I see you talking with the explorers from Cyrodilic Collections? Are you one of them? Would you be willing to help me with a crucial and sacred task?
You found something? And you made it out alive! You continue to surprise me, my friend.\n\nHop in the boat and we'll head for Concordia's camp outside Stormhold.
Safe travels.\n\nWhen you've concluded your business with the Dead-Water tribe, meet me back at Cyrodilic Collections Headquarters, in Lilmoth. We're getting close. I can … I can almost feel it.
You're here! Excellent! Welcome to the headquarters of Cyrodilic Collections.\n\nNow, we have business to discuss, right? I hope our experience in the xanmeer hasn't put you off adventuring for good.

That's all I've got for you. If you want to know more about what you're getting into, you can talk to my source. A local by the name of Solni. Whether her information is good, I can't say, but she seems to know what she's talking about.

You dealt with that snake, Whiptail, yes? Good. My belly churned with worry for friend-Famia—and for you.\n\nWe have … less-good news. We used the waterways and nearly caught Kassandra, but she escaped.

I see them return. You destroyed Etra? Good. Let that victory rattle the roots.\n\nGrave-Singer Ki-At tells me what we seek is not in the grave-stake's symbols, but in the wood itself. I do not know how to read wood, but he says I must.
Another of these twisted branches dies among our roots. This is no coincidence. These things must be the work of the Veeskhleel! Sent to poison our Hist with their corruption!
The chimes spoke of a visitor's approach. Our Hist welcomes you within its boughs, and so do we.\n\nI regret that you arrive for what should be a joyous occasion to find only worries and troubles.
Ah, clutch-sibling from a distant shore! I have a business opportunity that I think will intrigue you. Much profit! Will you hear me out?
I'm right behind you, friend. Let's just hope we can still catch up to Kassandra!

Welcome to my home, beeko. You arrive just in time. I arranged a meeting with my Dead-Water friend, Jaxsik-Orrn.\n\nShe is very proud, so we must use a breeze-light touch. This will be a brief and probably bloody meeting if we do not.
She promised me she could save them. She promised me! We were going to care for them and they'd live. \n\nI just wanted them to live!

You know those Dead-Water Nagas make weapons out of their friends' corpses right? Goodness knows what they do to people they don't like.\n\nMaybe something functional. A weather vane, or furniture? Hmm. I'm no artist, but I admire their creativity.

I tighten my fist. Whiptail takes Famia to the Xul-Thuxis temple. He toys with old magic he does not understand. Tsojei thirsts for his blood, but we cannot let Kassandra escape.\n\nI talk too much. We must continue the hunt.
Well, you certainly have a spring in your step. Your work with the Bright-Throats went well, I take it? Splendid!
Please let me know as soon as the eleven remaining tablets have been found.
I'm glad you agreed to accompany me. I had a bad feeling about Many-Whispers from the first moment we met.

I remember you. As I recall, you were somewhat helpful the last time my manservant got into a spot of trouble.\n\nI won't turn away good fortune. You know how useless Stibbons can be when it comes to recovering historic artifacts.
Did friend-Famia say something about a dream-wallow? Kaoc …. Sorry—do not worry about me. I will be fine. Go speak to Kassandra.
Are you ready, five-claw? Euraxia's forces are almost upon us. It is time to defend Riverhold from the approaching assault.
This one never expected to return to this part of the world.
The next triangulant should be in that chest. Take it and we can be off.
Zamarak smells freshly polished armor among the lingering scents of dust and decay. Saulinia and her soldiers are here.\n\nIf we hunt in silence, we may take them by surprise.
I am glad to see you unharmed. Were you able to gather the samples?
Thank you for helping Vazbi face Baan Dar's Litter. Truly, this one could not do it alone. Even when the answers are so close.

Euraxia hoped to appease her Dragon allies by assassinating the last Dragonguard of Elsweyr. He died, but at least you acquired the Anequina Dragonhorn and avenged his death.\n\nNow if we only knew what to do with the damn thing!
I'm sure you've heard a great deal about Akaviri culture today. But tell me, did you learn anything about the magnate herself?

Bright Moons look over us today, walker.\n\nTajirri has just settled down for a round of gambling. While Mizzik distracts her, you can sneak into her home and search for another clue. It's just a bit north of the tavern.
That relic. Look at the craftsmanship. It is beautiful!\n\nI sense something … a power. Examine the relic, five-claw, but do it carefully.
Vole did good. You as well. Tasnasi knew this would be the easiest part of the plan.\n\nThings get harder from here. We have the courtyard to deal with on the other side of the door.
Haven't seen the old crew in a while. Nazdar's looking spry as ever and Sereyne still … smells like a distillery.
Ugh. Sorry, I thought I was going to vomit again. \n\nWhere's Nazdar? Did I miss something?
"Do not fear a dark passage, for from them it's easiest to see light." Nazdar is happy to see the way to the courtyard is just ahead.

We stopped the Betrayer, but not before he set the Moons in motion. Soon they will align. When the eclipse occurs, the Moon Gate of Anequina will open and grant access to Jode's Core.\n\nWhich is exactly what the Dragons desire.
Rakazsa toys with us. He is drunk with power.\n\nWhat of the caravans? I have found no one alive.
Too much Khajiiti blood has been spilled to allow Euraxia to retake this city.

I didn't gather up any ancient spirits, like you. But, I did make a vital discovery.\n\nIn studying the phylactery you destroyed, I identified three more orbs hidden deep within the temple catacombs. We should make destroying them a priority.

Do you see now, child? We servants of the Hidden Moon protected and guided the people's souls—both true souls and bent. Guardians and redeemers.\n\nNow, all that remains of our order are old stones and old spirits. Spirits like me.
You should head to Mother's cellar while Raz clears up this … misunderstanding.

I was formulating a spell to track the Dragons when I noticed several surges of arcane energy not far from here. They reminded me of an old acquaintance. Has a way with portals. \n\nIf it is him, I want you to secure his help against the Dragons.
I see you've collected a missing piece! Sleek work.\n\nNow, if we only had clues for the other fifteen pieces. Makes finding them particularly difficult for us, no?
Go on, go on. Place the mural piece back in the frame.
I know Peryite will come to my aid. At least, I hope he will. Daedric Princes aren't always known for their dependability.
Well, that looked promising. Any conversation with a crime boss you can walk away from, right?\n\nSo, where's Fez? Did she cut him loose?
Things are looking upward, friend. Gather honey flowers from Merryvale Moon-Sugar Farms for Rigurt's sweetbread, and there will be peace between the Khajiit and Nords in no time!

Well, if it isn't the wielder of the Wabbajack. We won't be turning anyone into cheese today, but all is not lost.\n\nDon't worry about these levelheaded losers. No one can see me but you. You possess a special untapped talent for unhinged insanity!

It appears that the portal deposited us inside an ancient structure. I assume we're somewhere beneath the island of Dragonhold.\n\nThe architecture reminds me of both the Halls of Colossus and the barrows of Skyrim. Interesting.
The journal says that we'll find Dark Water Temple in Eastmarch, just south of Windhelm. We should depart as soon as you're able.
Tharn … he casually picks up right where he left off.\n\nYou talk to the man. He appears to have some modicum of respect for you.
Efforts to rebuild the abbey are well underway. One day soon, we'll restore its former glory. \n\nBut you should head inside. My student awaits you.
Ka'ishka cannot thank you enough for protecting Vijari's soul. She has little to offer aside from gratitude, but you are welcome to all she can muster.
If we can find the cultist who recruited Lahini, we might be able to convince him to recruit us as well.

Moonlit Cove? Some sort of holy place, if I recall. Then again, you can't walk ten steps without running into a Khajiiti holy place. This land is full of them.\n\nIf that is where we must go, so be it. I will meet you there after I see to the queen.

Now that we've secured a vessel, our next step is to infiltrate the Dragon's lair.\n\nZa'ji will stay on his ship in case we need to make a quick retreat. Caska, on the other hand, has asked to join our hunt.

What you describe are more reagents for a ritual than pigments for paint. Adara'hai needs you to decipher what Dak'radhi used for his mixture and gather those same ingredients.\n\nBring them to the Colorworks and she will make offerings of her own.
Don't follow Zayri. Let's see if there's another path to the great hall.
Five-claw, I think I understand. I can draw upon the power of the claw to open a portal to the Jonelight Path.\n\nI think I can do this, yes.
Za'ji can't help but notice that Aeliah's father, the general, has come to the sanctum.\n\nRemember, walker, you never saw Za'ji. Never.
Welcome back. Was the Moonlit Cove everything you hoped for? From what Za'ji has described, I don't think I'd find the place to my liking.
My father, the general, come all this way to visit me? You'd think, right? But, no. He's here to see Sai. Official business.\n\nI'm just his daughter, after all.
Honor and faith, wayfarer.\n\nBlademaster Kasura awaits you at the Rosy Lion in the city of Daggerfall. She requests you join her there at once.

We now know that the Order of the New Moon plans to strike against Pridehome.\n\nWhile I don't doubt your information, I have no idea why the cult would target such a place. What could they possibly hope to gain by attacking a peaceful temple?
If there was any justice in Senchal, the thieves who did this would be cut to pieces as well.
Clan Mother Tadali was right. The bells are tarnished from neglect.\n\nWhy don't we perform the cleansing ritual? You just need to press the pedal there to start it.

Hey, there you are. Did you find that Selloe lady?\n\nI asked a few of the shopkeepers about Lady G. Got a lot of weird looks and not much else. I get the feeling she doesn't spend a lot of time with the common folk.
Sidura certainly hopes this doesn't become a habit. She would rather not run around all of Pellitine delivering messages for your bearded friend, if it's all the same to him.
An inscription in a cavern like this could hold great importance. Let's read it before we proceed.

This is where it happened. They came out of nowhere. I remember getting hit and knocked to the ground. When I recovered, Winks was gone. But I heard Maezi shouting. She was chasing after those tuskless thieves.

Mara bless you, friend.\n\nI must warn you. The invaders stole an enchanted lantern. It will allow them to bypass the traps that await us inside. Our road will not be so easy. Then there is this vampire. He may offer aid, but undead cannot be trusted.
You try to find those missing pieces of the tablet while I make sure those pirates keep their distance.

Nothing like a quick battle to get the heart pumping, but I'm surprised we haven't faced more opposition. The coven must be preoccupied. Wasn't expecting to fight vampires, though.\n\nDid you find anything interesting at the sites I marked on your map?

The witch who captured us belongs to something called the Icereach Coven. These caverns make the perfect hiding spot for the group. Not sure I would have ever found it if they hadn't dragged me down here.\n\nWe should keep going.
There's only one way to know if the elixir actually works. We have to test it.\n\nTalk to Fenn and see how he wants to proceed.
Please, don't get too close while you're carrying the sacred oil. I have an … adverse reaction to such ointments.\n\nIf you'll pour it into the cauldron, I can complete the elixir.
Well, it didn't explode. That's a step in the right direction.\n\nI just hope it doesn't taste anything like it smells when I test it.
I think I see another page up ahead! Let's hurry!
