I'll see you and Lyris at the Blue Palace as soon as I can.
What kind of horrible place is this?
Look at it, my friend. I thought it was just an old legend, but it's real.\n\nIt's real.

Uh, that smell! Like what we encountered at Kilkreath. The poultice spread on the witch pikes, only stronger, more concentrated.\n\nTake a look around and let's try to figure out what they're using this makeshift laboratory for.
There's no time to lose. We must stop my father!
Rada al-Saran, the Ashen Lord. Whatever he's doing, it's powerful. I've never seen anything like it.
Fenn needs time to open that door. Let's get to work!
Poor Croble, torn apart by one of our own. I don't know how it's possible, but the storm is to blame. It's turned both priest and pilgrim alike into some sort of fiend.\n\nWe need to keep searching.
Brondold had good instincts. We're definitely on to something. Our mystery buyer is hiring locals to haul these urns and Reach fetishes out of the city. But for what purpose?
This isn't everyone who was with us in the barrow. I don't see Bjora.\n\nSpeak to Helsi. Maybe she knows where to find the rest of our people. I'll keep an eye out for Reachmen.

Wonderful! Look at the proud Petraloop, in its proper place once more. And we're a step closer to undoing Nel's folly!\n\nBut there are many other priceless instruments lost somewhere out in the world. They need to come home.

I'm sorry if I appear nervous. It's just that … well, I'm nervous. From the looks of it, these brigands have already smuggled many of these urns out of the tomb. What more could they want?\n\nUnless I miss my guess, it's something horrifying.
Go ahead and use the whistle. Phebe's eagerly waiting.

You did it! I can't believe this was only your first case, you were incredible! You remind me of Claudina. I want to be more like both of you. Fearless. Strong. Unbeatable!\n\nThank you for stepping up to help. We couldn't have done this without you.
These depleted witch pikes expended a lot of power to summon the harrowstorm. Now they're just ordinary sticks, but even in this state, they tell us much about the ritual that flowed through them.
Any luck? Did you find any sign of Ena?

I'd rather not leave Svana alone. We don't know if any more Icereach Coven agents are lurking about. Besides, you're better at talking to people than I am.\n\nFind witnesses. Track where the assassin fled to. I'll make sure Svana gets someplace safe.

Good, you've got them. Now go collapse those bolt holes and get to the caverns to stop Vund!\n\nMy partner, Ulang, is still missing … he might be down there. I hope that big idiot hasn't tried anything heroic.
As I said, your large friend is easy to spot in a crowd. We got here as quickly as we could.

High king or not, we have to make Svargrim listen to reason. He sees conspiracies in every shadow, but refuses to accept that Princess Svana has something that will actually help our people.\n\nThe man makes my blood boil!
Those geodes would almost be beautiful if monsters weren't using them to climb into my mine. What a disaster.\n\nNo time to lose. Get going.
Are you really going to participate in her madness? Damn it. Maybe Mazog shouldn't have trusted you after all.\n\nWell, I'm not going anywhere. I guess we'll all die together.
Oh, grandfather. I'm sorry I didn't come sooner. May Kyne carry his spirit to Sovngarde.\n\nDid you find something? What was he even doing here?
Ha! Rigurt and his friend have cornered the beast! Though it looks less like a fish and more like a horker. \n\nRigurt sees why people enjoy fishering. He should do it more often.
Ah, so you come to me again. Were our dealings with your pale friend not enough?\n\nWell, get close to the fire. Warm up. Pose your question.
We've got to stop meeting like this. I promise dank caves aren't where I spend all of my time.\n\nCome in search of more evil vampire experiments?

What are the odds? Here I am about to sneak into yet another mysterious castle filled with vampiric threats and then you trot up. Is hanging around ancient architecture just your idea of a good time?\n\nThough, to be honest, it's good to see you.

Have you heard the whispers in the streets? Solitude is safe. The high king has decreed it!\n\nI wonder what Svargrim will mandate next? An end to winter? Maybe replace the water in my well with mead?
Well, go on and read the scroll, assistant. More absurdities await, I'm sure.

If you come to rob me, you will leave disappointed. All this land and only weeds to show for it.\n\nDo you ever regret your choices, wanderer? Ever feel certain you are on the just path, only it leads nowhere? That's where you'll find this old farmer.
I'm not sensing any strange energies. I don't know if that's good or bad. Are you ready to head inside?
I … recognize this signet. But, that doesn't make any sense.
Do you see that shard sticking up from the rubble? Like a piece of solid darkness.\n\nTake a look and see what you make of it.
Well? Do those scratchings on paper tell you anything about what the Gray Host is doing in Lost Valley Redoubt?
Rada has been working in secret for a very long time. His laboratory will no doubt be well concealed. Our search must be thorough.

Even though Verandis told us about his time with the Gray Host, seeing these memories of him and Rada al-Saran together are kind of disturbing.\n\nAnyway, we got what we came for. Let's hope this creepy old book can help us stop the Darkstorm.

I don't know what a chunk of Oblivion or that memento have to do with Rada al-Saran's Darkstorm, but maybe Verandis can explain it when we get back.\n\nSpeaking of which, did you know he used to be friends with our enemy?
I thought Tzinghalis, one of Rada al-Saran's exarchs, came up with the plan to return the Gray Host to life. But it was Verandis? Why didn't he tell us?

I think I understand what happened to the Nighthollow clan. I suspect Lady Belain is the survivor of a long decline. While the rest of her clan slid into madness, she alone remained to carry on their legacy.\n\nSuch a bitter pill for a proud vampire.
You cried out in your sleep just before you woke up. What happened? Are you all right?
You don't know how glad I am to see you. Thought I might have been the only one to make it to this ugly hunk of rock.

Meet me in Karthwasten so I can introduce you to my master, Shaman Ulvoch. He can explain the restoration process better than I. Besides, we need his blessing for you to aid me.\n\nThe spirits sent you. They answered my prayers. I'm sure of it!
I sense the outsider has returned. I feel energy flowing through the land.\n\nI suspect you and my apprentice were successful in your task. Am I correct in this assumption?
Freyleth has a plan? Be wary, five-claw. Her words drip like honey from her lips, but taste of dust and ash.

You couldn't have timed your arrival any better. Ard Caddach holds court as we speak. We'll never have a better chance to gain an audience with him.\n\nDid your investigation uncover anything we can use? What did you learn?

The war has started! The Gray Host attacked once and a larger force is marching toward the city!\n\nVerandis sent me to tell Ard Caddach to fall back. To save as many of his people as he can. But the ard won't listen to me. He wants to fight back!
Go ahead, lend yourself to the ritual. Don't be afraid. It won't hurt.
I knew it would come to me. Eventually!\n\nThe ritual, the plaques, the map … it finally makes some sense now.

Ah, hello! You look incredibly capable, if you don't mind the observation. That's not strange to say, is it? I only bring it up because I'm in need of some help, preferably from a brave and strong sort. \n\nI have a little problem here.

Well aren't you a sight for chapped leathers! Didn't know if I'd see you again after all that Orcy business.\n\nHold on, why are you here? Were you hired, too? I told them I could handle it just fine.

So you agreed to help us? Oh, thank you. I … I am not really prepared for this type of thing.\n\nMy village tries to stay peaceful. Just keeps to themselves, you know? Until all this started. Now, well things are different.

I hope you will celebrate again when the time comes. And that you share this tradition with any you think could benefit from it. \n\nThe Old Life ceremony is deeply personal, but those who participate feel a sense of connection. As I'm sure you felt.
It took me longer to find my Snow Lily than I expected. Still, it appears you found a vateshran.\n\nTell Lyris what you have learned and see if it matches what she found at Hroldan Ring.

In a thousand years, nothing like this has ever made its way into Vateshran Hollows. It … burned when I touched it. I don't know that I've felt pain since I died! Strange.\n\nHmm, well, you completed the first challenge! Where to next?
This ritual is sacred to the Crow-Eye clan. I hope you understand that getting to participate is a privilege.

I ran all the way from Hroldan Ring … only to realize I'm in the wrong place. Damn it all. \n\nI was supposed to be helping Eslyn, but I might have gotten the two places mixed up. Serves me right for trying to accomplish anything with a muddled head.
Glad to see you rescued the vateshran. You handle yourself well, for an outsider.\n\nLet's see what he has to say about how our clans started feuding.

I really do like this camp. Perfect location. I expect I'll have to move, though. Can't depend on outsiders delivering me from the Thornroot witches again, can I?\n\nBut before I move on, I owe you a tale. About the Eagleseers and the Six-Fords, yes?

I told those duplicates to wait in the hut. But did they listen? And that door back there. It was open when we came through the first time. The broken seal lies in that direction.\n\nI suppose it's good the duplicates followed after me.

I thought the idea was to fight the fanatics outside the fort! Sombren ran off with the twins. They headed through the door to the west, toward the inner bailey.\n\nWe need to find them before Vandacia does!

The Order of the Waking Flame has cast a net around Gideon. Vandacia is gathering an army, including guards from the garrison who were loyal to him all along. He knows the Ambitions were here.\n\nAnd that they have now returned.
Well, don't keep me in suspense. See what you found and then we can talk.

Ah, you have arrived. Excellent. I found you both mildly interesting and suitably helpful in the past. Let us endeavor to continue that streak.\n\nThis Mehrunes Dagon cultist refused to answer my questions and I may have insisted a bit too vigorously.

Let me see those documents for a moment. These confirm that Arbitrator Gavos hid the anvil, but not where. There was a rebellion led by the trade-ministers that even Gavos's guards sided with. And he locked himself in the abbey's adytum.
To Gideon, mercenary. If Governor Keshu can identify the location of the hidden vault, make your way there with all due haste!

Leyawiin is a shining jewel rising from the banks of the Niben River.\n\nLet the so-called alliances fight over who gets to sit on the Ruby Throne. As long as they keep the fighting to the north, we'll stay out of that particular free-for-all.

Go on. I'll find another path down and we'll take the cultists from two directions. They don't know we're here, so we can surprise them. Just like finding a worm in a tomato.\n\nNot that we're worms … you get the idea.
I saw one of the cultists slink away. Let's see if we can catch them and find out what they know. If Quistley's marked for sacrifice, they might know where we'll find him.

Think I had damn near every Painted Eye on my tail at one point. The good news is I'm faster than a fireball. Barely.\n\nI already ordered Erilthel back to Commander Axius's camp. Lead these folks out through the sewers and meet her there.

No one in Leyawiin realizes that Undertow Cavern is the final resting place of a great hero.\n\nLet me secure my belongings, and I'll meet you inside. Time to grab the bull by the horns and wade right in. Ha!
We'll join you at the top of the hill after I finish attuning Calia and Destron.\n\nJust make sure the path is safe for when we follow after you.
We have the strange bits of Oblivion that Sombren said we need. Let's find him and get this over with.
Show Sombren the slivers. I'm eager to see what we have to do next.

These clouded varla stones … the Ayleids wouldn't have carved imperfect stones in this quantity by accident. There's intention here. They're meant to attract spectral energy like moths to a flame. That's why we keep finding Tiras among them.
I'm still weak as a kitten from that sacrificial ritual. If your new vampire friend attacks, I'm not going to be much help.
Now, why are you still talking to me? Don't you have some expensive finger-painting to do?
Let's split up and go deal with those cracked acorns before they find the weapons. I really hate Daedric cultists!
That's all the caravanners except Bevene, but there's still one more in need of a rescue here.
Gods he's gorgeous. Sorry! Taking notes.
Once you deal with the wards, I shall meet you inside.
We should return to the Happy Crow at once and question Cres. I'd like to know just what was the cause of all this.

Oh, you saw that. Probably think I'm talking to this pig. And, well, fair. Because that's what I'm doing. But I have a perfectly good explanation.\n\nYou see, this pig is my brother. And I desperately need to give him a bath.
Another time, perhaps.
Let us hurry. We need to look around for any sign of my missing people and what might have happened to them.\n\nAnd not to worry, if we run into any trouble my quick reflexes will save us.

Let's see if something deeper inside this ruin points us to the identity of the cult's high priest. Figure out who they are and you may learn more about this secret than you ever imagined.\n\nOh, and you still have that amulet? It might come in handy.
We managed to save her. I don't know if that'll improve her opinion of me—well, my kind—but I'm glad. I wouldn't wish what happened to poor Ghalor on anyone.
This is a sewer, all right. Smells worse than the vats of fermenting rotmeth back home!\n\nLet's find this annex and see what the Longhouse Emperors hid down here.
Well fought! Grab the skyshard and let's get moving.
It wasn't enough that the murderer killed the novitiates, she had to steal their souls, too?\n\nHow would someone even do that?

I've been thinking about my sister Clairene. Why would Lord Silvelle tell me she was dead all those years ago? Why didn't I end up with her after my mother's death?\n\nI think it's time to get some answers. I'm missing some part of the story.
A concerning piece of information, but a piece all the same. Come, let us continue.
No sign of a Dwarven puzzle box. Let's look through his things. Maybe we can figure out where he took it.
There is much to do. Information does not simply cease to flow once a crisis is done with.

I would not pass that threshold unless you seek bloodshed. The Knights of the Silver Rose declared their stronghold off limits to outsiders and I can attest to their willingness to use violence to have their way.

Then your first orders are to act as vanguard and secure the entry to the Dread Cellar. Consider anything or anyone you encounter inside a threat. We'll catch up to you once I've tended to Lucilla's wounds.
If you are expecting a warmer welcome from the Knights of the Silver Rose than ours, I wouldn't stake your life on it. Were I you.

Dark tidings are upon us. The Crowborne Horror encroaches upon our realm. If it is left alone, it will ultimately pierce the veil and threaten all the inhabitants of Nirn.\n\nWhether for altruism or reward, I sense you will be the one to defeat it.
Is this what Oblivion feels like? It's how I imagine everything antithetical to our world would feel. I suppose I'll have to get used to it, if I'm to have any hope of surviving there.

We'll go with Lyranth and gather as many allies as we can. And I'll talk with Calia. She was with Sombren for a long time. She must have some idea how he stole her power. If not, maybe together we can figure it out.

This place is incredible! Investigator Vale never went to Oblivion in any of her stories, so I wasn't sure what to expect. I was nervous when Lyranth said I had to use a portal to get here, but this is great. And you're here now, so it's even better!
When in doubt, speak with Madam Whim. Perhaps she has some insight.
We're deep within the citadel now. No doubt Dagon's brutes patrol every corner. Keep sharp.
That did it. The door's open. But all I see is a chunk of iron slag.\n\nWhy don't you take a look. It has to have some connection to the voices we heard coming out of the furnace.
I assumed we'd find answers here in Fargrave. Some way to salvage the opportunity denied me at Fort Grief. But no, even Madam Whim seems at a loss as to the location of Deadlight.
Selveni, you're grown now, you can handle disappointment. Find the statues and don't cry in front of Sotha Sil.

Sorry, I was just thinking. Ever since we returned from Fort Grief, I've been having strange visions. More forgotten memories bubbling to the surface.\n\nAt least, I hope that's what it is. Some mortals who linger in Fargrave for too long go insane.

The Bladebearers are nomads, but we should find them at a settlement called Wretched Spire. That's in the Sever region of the Deadlands. We must talk to their kynreeve, Rynkyus. I will meet you there.\n\nAnd bring Arox. We may have a use for him.
Look at this place. Does it reflect the old mortal's madness?

Xivilai are reckless creatures. They rely on wild emotion and brute strength instead of skill and strategy. Dangerous to the weak or the unwary.\n\nYou … are still here. Was I not specific enough in my warning?

Daedric bodies not the same as mortals'. Toxins from your plane have little effect. What this poison Miksotet knows of consists of … hrmph.\n\nSearch for the blighted tree in the northwest. Collect this substance. Bring it to me at Spire Hall.
This place is falling apart. Let's see what we can find, but step carefully.

How could anyone in Elegian's state create these cataclysts? It's crazy, but I can't help feeling that there's meaning in his nonsense.\n\nI think he's trying to tell us how to help him. Look for anything related to spring.
Master! What are you doing here? Pay no attention to this cage. Arox will be free momentarily.

Lyranth wants me to hang back until we determine if there's any connection between my mask and the cataclyst. Elegian did create both, so I understand her concern.\n\nPlus, I still don't know why he gave me this amulet. Many mysteries remain, it seems.

Retrieve the key from Madam Whim and prepare yourself to enter Ardent Hope. Every moment we tarry gives Valkynaz Nokvroz more time to extract the blood he needs from the Anchorite for his cataclyst device.
The key you found in the tunnel. Use it on the windgate's pillars. It is not difficult to figure out.

I hope the Anchorite can figure out that relic. We need this egonymic more than ever now that Sombren turned against us. It's the one advantage we have—provided we can actually find it and figure out what to do with it.
Perfect! The crystal looks charged and ready.\n\nNow place it in the discharge labrum near the door. That should release the energy, dispel the ward, and let us through.

Who knew that a simple spell would take so long to yield results? Or that my request for mortal help would deposit multiple options at my feet?\n\nBut the brand is unmistakable. That glow certainly contains my arcane indicators. Who are you, mortals?
I have been here before. How can I know this but not remember it?

Congratulations. You restored the arcane matrix of that guardian stone. The good news is I can now activate the stone to revise the summoning spell. The bad news is we need to reset it first by summoning the guardian, which will try to kill you.
If you're looking for Madam Whim, she's entertaining the Dread Lady Lyranth on the upper level.
Bother one of my betters, mortal.
Does it want a treat? Rynkyus says mortals covet such things.
The fabled Sword of Leeches, here, within my grasp. I have my doubts. May I?
Hurry, little mortal! We must determine what's happening here.
Would you please talk some sense into him? Shiro-dar's coming apart faster than I am! Or that's what he'd like me to believe.

According to that document, the captains of our missing ships are being held here. But then where are the delegates?\n\nWe need to find the captains, as well as Quentyn. Let's make our way to the crypts south of here.

You're the one Lady Arabelle spoke to at the docks, aren't you? You volunteered to help investigate the ships that failed to reach port.\n\nIt's good to see a friendly face. Especially after what just happened.

The first step is the same as it was last season. Zenithar delights in the exalted common ingredient. Sadly, my skill at the cook fire is as poor as it was before. \n\nPlease, prepare some baked apples so that we may honor the great Zenithar.

I'm no stranger to adventure, my dear. But this undertaking truly is shaping up to be my most daring exploit yet. I really must remember to record the details in my journal.\n\nFor posterity, you understand.
Well, we've got his sword. Here's hoping he holds up his end of the bargain. \n\nMortens, I swear to Stendarr ….
Good luck in the catacombs. And tell Isobel to be careful.

Jakarn said you found all five medallions. I can't thank you enough, not only for recovering the medallions, but for rescuing me from those horrid Ascendant Order ruffians. \n\nBut don't let me keep you. Lady Arabelle wishes to speak with you.

Well, aren't you a sight for sore eyes? Remember that bit of trouble we had with the stolen medallions? Looks like we've got a new problem now. We could use your help again.\n\nLady Arabelle will be happy to see you, too, I'm sure.
A cavern as big as they claim has to have a way in we can use. We just have to find it!
You seem like the sort who understands life's twists and turns. Maybe you find yourself among nobles of High Rock one day, then the next you're here.\n\nNot what I planned for, but what can you do?
I'm sure Lady Arabelle has something she needs me to do. Just between you and me, I don't mind the work too much. But don't let her know that.
Careful in there. As you can likely deduce, I haven't used the passage in centuries. It probably has more than a few inhabitants that won't offer a warm welcome.

Satisfying our curiosity will have to wait. Two of Lord Bacaro's couriers have run into trouble. If the Ascendant Order is involved, we need to do what we can to help them. \n\nSpeak to Lord Bacaro and offer your services. I'll add it to your pay.
I'm sure Lady Arabelle has something she needs me to do. Just between you and me, I don't mind the work too much. But don't let her know that.

The Evergrowth implied that the archdruid is as much a victim as it is. Its darker aspect, the Allwither, somehow broke free and is trying to fully emerge by consuming the grove in corruption. We need to warn the elders. I'll meet you in the village.
Let's hurry. We have to get to the smithy if we're going to put the weapon together.
You're back! The traps worked, didn't they? See, I told you I know what I'm doing … mostly. \n\nSpeaking of which, I think I figured out a way to return the livestock to their original forms.
Have no fear, I'll be along shortly. I just need to … never mind. It's complicated. Magicka. \n\nDon't worry, I've got this. Go find Emeric.
Don't worry about me. I'll meet you at the coin fort. It's just west of here, if I remember my maps.\n\nI'll just spend the walk thinking about the choices I've made. A little retrospective.
I am Prince Irnskar, heir to the throne of Windhelm and Skyrim. Since you don't appear to be one of these Green Serpent bastards, can I assume you're a friend?
Put on your disguise, dear. You can't go to the Ascendant Order meeting if you're not dressed to blend in.

The dream of the Society of the Steadfast is a noble one. Soldiers removed from the battlefield can learn to lose the hate they feel for the enemy.\n\nBut somehow I doubt that good wishes alone will stop our leaders from seeking the Ruby Throne.

Lady Arabelle was right. The Ascendant Order's going to strike at the alliance leaders again. And they somehow knew where we were safeguarding them, and with enough notice to assemble a fleet.\n\nWe need to follow the Magus and try to stop him!
If you want this cat freed, you better hurry along! Ain't that right, lads?
I managed to convince Adwig to let Oblan down, but you should hold up your end of the bargain so we can get a move on.
It's awfully easy to get lost on this island.
I am glad you're here to clear this up. And I am glad the skooma smuggler did not murder you and leave your body in an alley. \n\nTalk to the guard. <<1>> is as good as free!
Can you help me? There's been a terrible mistake. I'm with the Daggerfall Covenant diplomatic mission, but this guard doesn't believe me.\n\nI'm not what he thinks I am!
I want out of this nightmare.
Yvelle and the others are too hurt to fend off the Hadolids outside.\n\nI took some resonance crystals from the caravan, they should amplify my calming song. Do you still have the medical supplies?
Insert the two keys we recovered and unlock the vault, my friend! I've already used mine.
Despite all the Ascendant Order's plots and efforts, the delegates to Lord Bacaro's peace conference remain alive. Which means the hope for peace does as well.

Not surprised Silverslip and Jhaka wouldn't be content to just sit around.\n\nBut that place Azamel marked on your map, it's not too far from here. Let's hurry. We're so close to finding Song, I can feel it! I don't want to waste any more time!
Hah, another daring rescue. We're getting quite good at this, aren't we?
Gah, I just cleaned these boots, too. Blast.\n\nDon't worry about me. Find Aurelia, quick as you can. They went southeast down the coast.
Want some food or drink? Someone in the inn can get it for you. \n\nBe warned, the cook is terrible. I should know, I used to work there.

Quickly, while I have some modicum of control. Talk to the ghost woman before I give in to the sea captain's desires and try to rip the bodice away from her lovely breasts.\n\nUgh! These feelings are very confusing!
Port Sargo is located on the eastern shore of the All-Flags Islet. Let's see what we can find there.
Oh cruel seas! You stole my love and left me with nothing but this endless pain.
I never got a chance to thank you after Stros M'Kai. And here you are, riding to my rescue once again.
Let's look around. If I catch a familiar scent, I can follow it.
Varnauld Broch? Seriously? This guy couldn't beat a cross-eyed kwama!\n\nGood practice, regardless. Let's crush these twerps!

You joined the Roisters Club at an opportune time. Smaller club chapters are preparing for a series of tournaments—ours included.\n\nThe contest will not begin for some time, though. So, I suggest you get some more practice in the meantime.

Hey! I knew you'd join us. Excited? Of course you're excited! But try to stay loose. A tournament's no different than a back alley match. Except for the prizes, of course. Mmm. Prizes.\n\nJust don't get twitchy like Brahgas.

Advanced play is not for the faint of heart. Players who commit themselves to the game at this level do not make mistakes. So, collect more cards and further hone your strategies.\n\nThe final tournament approaches quickly!

We're in trouble. The Mournhold Chapter has produced some of the greatest Tribute players alive. Razhamad beat this Teliv character once, but only barely.\n\nBah. All we can do is try our best, right?
Familiarize yourself with the map over there. I've heard rumors of unwary travelers being used in dark rituals, drained of blood. \n\nMark the locations well. And then … the hunt begins.

Such luck! We've shipwrecked. On an uncharted island. We might never be found! Ha!\n\nNo time to bask in fortune's blessing. That storm that hit us—did you see how it sprung from this island? I may have crashed onto the answer I seek.

So the Druid King didn't just meet with the Beldama Wyrd to perform a ritual, he had the help of the Glenmoril Wyrd, too? And the Firesong somehow knew this as well? Blight! Was I the only one who didn't know about this? We need to stop them.

The Glenmoril Wyrd. Interesting. You know, wyrds and druids were once tied very closely together. Some think they grew out of the same tradition. Whatever we're dealing with, it must be ancient.\n\nBut talk to Laurel. She's the captain of this voyage.
This job has taught me a valuable lesson. Always practice due diligence. No more contracts that don't include hazard pay.
Find the gaoler's key, my friend. Then we'll see whether we can make the Dreadsails regret their lack of hospitality.
Welcome to Castle Mornard, mercenary. Make your report to Stefan. He's been eager to hear from you.

I knew there were some rats in the Firesong Circle, but I never imagined treachery like this. Good thing you were here!\n\nGo make sure Laurel and Stefan don't bite off more than they can chew. I'll protect these two.
We may be too late to save the Eldertide Druids here, but we can try to learn what attracted the Dreadsails to this village. Let's look around.

I've never seen Lady Arabelle so … weak. She's in a bad state. But she's a tough old bird. I know she'll pull through.\n\nYou should head upstairs and talk to her. Just seeing you will do her a world of good.

Za'ji has not left Lady Arabelle's side while you were gone. Well, except for when she sent me to warn the alliance leaders. And when Ryvana sent me to fetch you. And when Caska made me go outside because she said my worrying was making her fur itch.

When you speak with Lady Arabelle, remind her that she's still recovering from the effects of a powerful poison. The antidote I provided won't totally neutralize it if she doesn't give it time to do its work.

I just need a moment to gather samples of this plant. I spotted a druid ritual box over there. They're meant to hold important components and sacred relics. You should examine it and see what it contains.
You will play well, five-claw, Raz is sure of it. This one will stand by, looking casual.\n\nHe is very good at this. Raz has had a great deal of practice.

We stand in the Temple of Y'ffelon. The tomb of Druid King Kasorayn is somewhere in here, according to the legends. Archdruid Orlaith defiles this sacred place with her violence and rage.\n\nDid you find the captives? Druid Laurel?
Get to the bow and use the ballista! We don't need another enemy alongside us.
The Ivy Throne. Once the Green blessed this place and those who reigned here. It sleeps, with dreams dark and dim. But it is not dead.\n\nLook around. There is another message for us here.

Every day, I ask Tu'whacca to help guide my blade against the scaled beasts that plague this land. I have been luckier than most. \n\nI have seen far too many fall to feel comfortable. I won't rest until there is safety for all.

What amazing things you accomplished, friend. You saved the leaders of the alliances, stopped the Ascendant Order, defeated the Firesong, killed Lord Bacaro, and calmed a volcano.\n\nWhat will you do next, I wonder.

Hi! Good to see you again! What are you doing out here? Me, I'm looking for some sap from a sacred tree.\n\nHey, maybe you can help me, seeing as you have hands and all. Just watch out for the forest wraiths. They're mean!
Well, the freezing spell did something. See if you can pick up the fire shard now. Just be careful! If this goes bad and your hands start to melt …. Don't blame me, all right?
Examine the carvings and I'll tell you what I think they mean.
Blight and rootrot! I can't believe Lord Bacaro betrayed us. He's not worthy to even look upon the regalia, let alone claim the title of Druid King!
We must act quickly now and prepare as much as we can. I just hope we can weather the coming attack.
With all this trouble, you deserve a little extra to sell off. Go ahead and grab that medallion. Then, we'll keep going.
Such a high concentration of spirit motes is dangerous. The blessing won't protect us from this. Worse, vines seal the doors beyond.\n\nI think I have an idea, though.

Ugh, standing hurts. My arms hurt. My … everything hurts. I really miss Neri.\n\nOh, right. She could come back soon. Talk fast if you have questions. Otherwise, I'll meet you at the cell on the beach. We'll ask those Sea Elves about that relic.
Archdruid Rahval has arrived, and other Stonelore will show up shortly. Go ahead and talk to the archdruid. He wants to speak to you.
A tide of curses upon this feathered fiend and whatever dank corner of Oblivion he flapped from! \n\nHe owes his thanks to you, traveler. I was just about to kill him. Even though he can't die.

I hoped that this would be simple, but no. The writing is complex and made all the harder to translate because of the broken stone. \n\nFind Joslin by the lava pools to the east, near Embervine. Then go north to meet Octin by the sacred tree.

Ah, so the lordling got my message. I doubted he'd turn down the idea of having my ship at his side, but one can never be too certain.\n\nNow, I hope you came prepared to fight. Things are about to get ugly. I intend to make sure of it.
Bassian has a talent for ancient languages and obscure ciphers. I want to consult with him about the letter Dralys gave you.\n\nI shall meet you at Naraheida's camp in due course.
We can't let him get any farther, do you hear me?
This one greets you, walker, and wishes you a pleasant journey.
Welcome to the Shrine of Saint Vorys the Immolant! How nice to see a new face.
That sounded like it went well. Please tell me you have some good news. I really need something to soften the blow of this report to my superiors at the Consortium.
My security measures will ensure that whatever Painted Eye remains here is dealt with. The rest of my routines are set, I will care for Kemel-ze and ensure that it is protected.

The One Who Knows instructed me to give you this. A condensate of planar potentialities—ah, you will not understand. It is ink.\n\nTake it to the Redrith Cistern, a ruin near the city. Pour the ink into the water and your path will be made clear.
Go on. That trapdoor is our way into the Necropolis.
These are all we need. Now, let us hurry to where Uxunath had that portal. The longer we leave her alone, the more damage she can do.
This brazier really is a bit odd on second glance.

Vorm told me the stacks like to rearrange themselves, so that "map" he passed us could be useless. Guess we'll find out!\n\nYou follow the map, and I'll apply my Gleaner's intuition. Between his inky mess and my nose, we'll find these books eventually!
Hmm, let's see. 'Fathomless Gaze', 'Portents of Celestial Bodies', 'Encyclopedia Praedictionem.' Strange, why do I feel like I'm missing something?\n\nAh! Traveler, could you lend me a hand?
Blast this endless cycle. I was certain returning this book would end it. The sigil taunts me with even more projections.

Ziss on these archives! Huzmargo doesn't see anything useful in these books. Did you have better luck?\n\nTell Huzmargo what you learned from yours. Anything that would explain what's happening to the vessels? Why some move and speak?
Tel Rendys must have been grand in its day. Head inside, proxy. There is usually a tunnel or portal to the tower in these outer structures.
The trail ends here. I'm guessing the two who escaped managed to hide their tracks from here with magic.

Watch your step as you make your way through Underweave! The guards and administrators won't stand for anyone interrupting their work.\n\nAnd don't get me started on the dangers posed by some of these fates.

The Pool of Inquiry's waters of scrying won't function without the sacred tears of Hermaeus Mora. The invaders left none behind, but search the chamber anyway.\n\nIt's hopeless, but maybe you'll find something useful.
Sathile thinks she's protecting Nathyn, but now he could be in more danger than ever. We need to figure out what happened here.

Scruut and I uncovered the most interesting news. The Assembly of Masters learned of Master Shelreni's recent activities and has called for a conclave. They plan to strip her of her rank and expel her from the house!
When we get to Tel Rendys, you'll need to be careful. The same defenses hampering Shelreni's mercenaries will target you as well.
My heart may never recover from losing Reynila. I should have been with her. \n\nI'll finish this final mission of hers, and then I'll be gone. I won't look back.

Dreynis wasn't quite what I'd imagined. He didn't even seem the slightest bit bothered by the veritable Daedric war going on behind him. Regardless, we're here for research, not feuding Daedra. The sooner we find it, the better.

Aides to the masters train to become invisible unless called upon. One could stand quietly, listening, absorbing details without notice.\n\nGo check out the servants quarters. I'll catch up with you there.

Everything I listed should be plentiful here. Tomeshells are everywhere, so finding a feather is easy. For red mold, it grows in dark corners. And a quill? Look on a desk.\n\nI'll stay with you to make sure you get the right things.
Tell Mevei what we've learned.

Please hurry. I'm really not built for this climate.\n\nI just need passable documents and some clothing that doesn't make me look quite so Telvanni. Then I can be on my way. Remember, I'll meet you in the Windhelm Outlaw's Refuge after, all right?
Though my colleagues would take great offense at your unbidden approach, I choose not to. That said, I must ask you leave me be. Calming my tempestuous associate requires my full attention.

The adversary has locked us out of the sanctum! My sanctum! Quickly! We must find a way back inside before eldritch forces are loosed in the city!\n\nWorse, I might have to explain all of this to Telenger the Artificer. I can't bear the thought.
I'll see you back at Cipher's Midden, my perspicacious collaborator.\n\nJust need to see to Martina, here.
Light the fire. Those rocks look so cold.
You brought my son here. I thought I lost him! For that you have my thanks.
Dealing with displaced spirits is very much frowned upon by the Keepers of the Dead. I'll help because the stakes are great, but it goes against every iota of my training.
Whatever's happening to Apocryha is making my orb sockets burn. We need to get inside that Eye of Mora!
The One Who Knows has requested your presence, proxy. Do not spurn such an honor.
Thank the ancestors you stopped!\n\nRight. Well. I'm in a bit of a predicament here. I need to collect ingredients for a medicinal tincture, and I simply don't have time. I need someone to help.
This affliction is beyond my meager healing talents. If Torvesard has a solution, we at least need to hear what he's offering. We can't let the corruption take Leramil and Scruut. We just can't.
Apocrypha's agony is my agony. Back here in the realm, it's like fire burning across my tentacles, like acid in my orb sockets.\n\nMortal, I don't feel very good.
Be careful, traveler. In Apocrypha, the danger is not that you might fail to find what you seek. The danger is that you might succeed. And be destroyed by it.
I can't believe it's almost over. I'm going to really miss Leramil when I return to my duties at the Necropolis.\n\nOh, I'll miss you, too, my friend! Really!

Go on with your life, proxy. When Hermaeus Mora needs us to resume the chase, I shall send word.\n\nUntil then, I believe I shall remain here in Necrom for a time. Restore the bindery. Explore the Necropolis. Get to know Curate Gadayn a little better.
Blasted Mora and his curses. Father is bound and the pages of the tome are scattered to the winds.
I've never seen a maligraphy leave anything behind when they die. But then, I also never recognized a maligraphy before. Today holds many revelations.\n\nThis course of action is working. Keep it up.

The very gate Hermaeus Mora created to bring the mortal vessels of his allies to Apocrypha provided Torvesard with the door he needed. Fate is not without a sense of irony.\n\nFollow Torvesard, proxy. We do not have much time.
Tell Scruut what we saw and explain your idea. Let us see if it sparks any ideas of her own.
Talk to Leramil. All this thinking and planning and sensing instabilities has put me in a foul mood.

That was Shardmarshal Vargas down there, ordering these Recollection cultists like she did the Daedric troops at Feldagard Keep.\n\nAt least we took that blade from her. We need to find out what she's doing here.

Torvesard? Were you expecting him, friend? He did help us in the end, against Peryite and Vaermina the last time we were in Apocrypha.\n\nMaybe he's had another change of heart? It appears he only does want to talk to you.

I'm not sure what I'm going to do once this is all over. I've grown used to all the hustle and bustle in my townhouse.\n\nAnyway, you shouldn't keep Scruut waiting. She's eager to hear what you learned.
You speak with the captive. I'll make sure no one catches us by surprise.

Why, if it isn't my sister Eveli's friend! Good to see you! I'm dealing with a real mystery, almost as convoluted as that Waking Flame affair.\n\nI'm tracking a group of troublemakers called the Recollection. I don't suppose you're after them, too?
Everything is just as I found it. Aquilia was very clear that she did not want to disturb any evidence. I hope you find some answers.
Of course, the painting of the dog is a clue! There seems to be something behind it.
Though the odds are against us, we must confront Ithelia and try to find a way to defeat her. Reality itself depends on what we do next, proxy.
I had a feeling this was going to end up with another journey into Apocrypha. At least it's not overrun by the minions of Vaermina and Peryite anymore. I hope.\n\nGo on. I'm right behind you.

Well, at least she's finally talking. That's better than I ever managed.\n\nI hope you told her to get out of here. My remaining customers are starting to talk about settling their bill and finding someplace less strange.
Don't look at me like that. You would have done the same thing in my shoes.
If you are looking for the stranger who calls himself Uriel, he went to walk the estate grounds with Pelena. And not a moment too soon. I was growing tired of their bickering.

Greetings, proxy. I knew fate would draw you here. New troubles emerge in these lands—the footprints of the once-forgotten Prince now free. And where the Prince walks, disturbance and disorder follow.\n\nBut that is how we shall find her.
The entrance to the mine is on the southeast side of town. Let's go find Balandrus. It's time to put an end to the Terror of the Weald—one way or another.

I could handle this invasion on my own, but what's the point in that? I am a connoisseur of combat, and so many new opportunities present themselves with the Blind Path. \n\nI wonder, what will they do? How will they fight?

Good idea, friend! The Lamp and Abolisher give us an advantage previous explorers didn't have.\n\nI suggest we start with the east passage and look for a way up to the north. The Recollection mage's notes suggest we might find something there.
The nexus point lies inside this cave. As does the reality tear. Come on. The sooner we get this done, the sooner I can stop worrying about the end of everything.
Place Abolisher near the tear, friend.
I don't know what our enemies are planning next for West Weald. But whatever it is, I'll meet it blade in hand. We're not defeated yet.
There must be something here. Look around, but carefully. According to the Skein, Nantharion used the Staff of Many Paths here not long ago.
That wisp in the air … what is it? What does it mean? I've never seen anything quite like it.
I'll stick with you, comrade. We need to locate Nantharion before he reaches that well. I just hope Beragon can find us again.

Now that she mentioned it, I've heard of greenspring seeds. If the Recollection was able to corrupt the sacred seeds of the Green with Daedric magic … that's unthinkable!\n\nBefore we go look for that cart, we should talk to King Nantharion first.
Stay back! Oh, apologies. I found this necromancer dying of vicious wounds. Arkay has her now, but you should be careful, traveler. There are dark things afoot here.
Scruut told us you went back to the Loom. I'm glad to see you all returned unscathed. Go, tell Scruut what you found there.

The Recollection consists mostly of Wood Elves, fanatics to a cause I haven't quite pinned down yet. If there are more of them in there, we'll probably need to fight.\n\nCome on. Let's head into the ruins and find Greenspeaker Sorilen.
Whether Ithelia remains in Fargrave or simply passed through on her way to some other plane, our path is clear. We must explore these ruins and see what we discover.

I can see the Legion is going to have to clean up these ruins … later. Right now the mission is to find Shardmarshal Vargas, wherever she's hiding. Open a portal with Abolisher, comrade. I'm right behind you.

Let me see those papers we gathered. I see. The Recollection found an altar, but could go no farther. Sounds magical. There's mention of finding vials of blood, some sacred water and a bottle of ancient wine. Yes. Yes! Those are our keys.

Beragon must have found his way through the Many Paths to this concurrent spot between realities. I think we can help him escape. Illuminate the mirror with the Lamp of Clarity, and let us hope it reveals the path we all seek.

The Lamp led us to the same location as the first path, but in a much different reality. I see my loyal soldiers line the halls, but despair fills the air.\n\nWe are not welcome here. Tread carefully as you search for the ingredient we need.

Your first task is to familiarize yourself with what's happening here. The graveyard is a good place to start. Notice the number of recent markers and the similar causes of death.\n\nGo on. We can talk again after you examine the newer grave markers.

I wondered when Shardmarshal Vargas would turn up again. I still owe her for Rustwall.\n\nAnd she has a new sword. Did you see how it opened a portal? Brought in reinforcements from someplace she called Mirrormoor. We need to take that blade.
Feldagard Keep must not fall to these invaders. We must protect it at all costs!

Root rot and ruin, of all the days. I'm sorry you had to see that, traveler. Our family drama is a poor welcome to Vashabar. \n\nThose two old timber pigs were our fathers. My beloved Clendagal and I simply can't get them to see reason.
Hey there, traveler. You've found us at an awkward time. \n\nYou'd better talk to Laeni. She can explain better than me.
Welcome, traveler! This is the Vashabar Garden of Ale. I'm the owner and host, Ciiril.\n\nDid I hear raised voices just now? Was that Laeni and her father?
You're amazing. I've known it since I first laid eyes on you. \n\nHyacinth's greenhouse is near Serpent's Grotto. But before we get moving, I just dropped a lot on you. I'm sure you have questions.
Walker? And that strange Khajiit from Moonmont.\n\nIt is too dangerous for you to be here. These dro-m'Athra, the powerful ones leading them. I have never seen the like before. None of us have!

I pray that searching through the ruins below results in more than sorrow and lost time. \n\nI should focus on the blessing of you and Ja'kh to guide me. Just think. I could have been found by someone with far less patience, like that nomad there.
You and Bogcup performed admirably, as expected. Well done. I never doubted young Bogcup for a moment.\n\nYou, I'm coming to appreciate as well.
Well, the little ball of eyes certainly seems flustered. Not that I've ever seen her particularly calm, mind you. I suggest you see what she wants.
This is all so exciting! I can barely keep myself from spreading it around the rest of the guild.
It's been a while since I've had to charge in blind and hope for the best. \n\nI'm ready if you are.
These Goblins are really agitated. Let's investigate the camp quickly and with as little interaction as possible. I don't want to make anything worse than it already is.
Ulfsild's annotations have been revealed. \n\nRead the fable once more to learn its hidden meaning.

Snapdragon has a commanding presence. If she wasn't captured and is simply ignoring me, it won't take you long to find her. But a word of caution. She didn't leave the Ring on the best of terms. Make sure she understands I just worry for her safety.
You have many questions, I am sure. Place the fable on the dais to open the Scholarium door. \n\nWe will speak more, on power. Its meaning. And the art of Scribing.
There are so many awe-inspiring creatures whose shape this Luminary might have taken. Indrik. Dragon. Gryphon!\n\nAnd yet, it's a Netch. It's rather silly. But perhaps that's the entire point.
Something keeps tugging on my robes! Like a child playing a game. But no one's there.\n\nIt's the Netch, isn't it? This blob of yours is testing my patience.
How goes your dealings with the Dragon? Any more riddles to solve?
Marcan Caelum can't have gotten very far with a captive to manage. He must be hiding nearby, and the cellars of the old house are our best bet. Inside, quickly!

Hooke found these notes with the other Scarlets who were killed. They were penned by the killer to lure out our old comrades.\n\nSpeaking of which, I don't see Naku. Hooke's waiting to hear what you found, friend.
Hooke is the one you want to talk to. Unless you want a moment-by-moment report of how this hangover's treating me.

Thank you for bringing Versidue back. He's my little king, I couldn't imagine life without him!\n\nStill, I'm missing a piece of home. I asked Marcien to trap some guzzards for me, but they haven't returned. I'll reward you if you catch them for me.

I need to get my son and Norraine away from Vashabar. Away … from me, where it's safer for them. I'll make the arrangements. But I'll still be here when you're back.\n\nIf you want to read the note, I think I tossed it somewhere beside my home.

The null arca is too heavy to bring with you, so you will have to carry the arcane knot back here. This one hopes you find it quickly, Xoryn and his mercenaries have had a good while to explore on their own.\n\nKeshargo will join you when he can.

Mortal. Let us dispense with pleasantries. You are here to master Scribing. To amplify the power of the altar, and walk in the footsteps of the Archmagus Ulfsild.\n\nIn short, her inheritor. Do I have that right?
Thanks for all you're doing to help restore the Scholarium. If there's anything I can do to help, just let me know.

Let us see what you make of my little games. The best games are ones that others don't know they are playing. \n\nMakes for much more bubbly responses when they discover the joyful tricks we played on them!
She sounded so sad. Losing Eyevea and the Scholarium to the whims of Sheogorath must have been devastating.\n\nAnd it sounds like the Gryphon didn't much like it either.
My connection to Moon-Singer Talbira feels so natural. But I expect if the Inquisitors were to learn of it, they would consider it some sort of heresy.
Now you decide to show up ….\n\nQuickly! The Inquisitors are coming. Find a place to hide and remain still while this one deals with them.

I wish I didn't need my petty emotions. They only cause trouble.\n\nI'm still linked to my facets. I sense one near a river south of Skingrad. It's probably my despair. I can be rather dramatic when I'm in a doleful mood, and the water is comforting.
You've done it! I knew you would! I could smell it on you. \n\nAnd grapes, but that might just be what I ate for breakfast.
The fable … lightly chewed, I see. Oh, Fox.\n\nThe fable will open the path between my domain and the Scholarium. And then we can discuss the future.
Maybe there's something in the tome the echoes pointed out.

This is the ritual that led you to Claw's Strike when all this started? I remember how surprised I was to see you!\n\nI will watch and try to learn what I can. Perhaps Zerith does not need to be the only one to revive the rites of the Hidden Moon.
We're in the Labyrinthian? Fascinating! Or some version created by the Crow's domain, anyway.\n\nI can't wait to find out why.
Let's keep an eye out for anything that might tell us where they're holding Snapdragon. \n\nPrison logs, arrest warrants, scribbled notes—that sort of thing. You know what I'm talking about.
There's no need to go in quiet. In fact, let's make as much noise as possible. I want them to know we're coming. \n\nLet's find that base and get Hyacinth out of there.

I feel like I got hit by a speeding carriage. But it worked. This must be Dusk Keep. I can sense Wisteria, somewhere nearby. Too bad there wasn't enough energy to bring Hyacinth and the Garderner with us.\n\nAre you ready to cut down some Ceythalmor?
The Tomb of the Moon-Singers. It lies to the northeast of the main atrium.\n\nBe wary. I sense this place is not as quiet as one would expect a tomb to be.

Ravith was always strong. But this power she has amassed. I have seen nothing like it.\n\nShe seeks to disrupt the Crossing. Azurah's planes. I had not thought to see such destruction also blemish the face of Nirni.

A den of darkness hides beneath the dunes of Elsweyr, and now we know its location. Predator Mesa.\n\nWe have everything we need. Twilight Cantors. Talbira's song. The element of surprise. We must use this opportunity and move at once.

You agreed to satisfy Krin'ze's curiosity about this fallen star?\n\nThis one would sing you a song of gratitude, but I must save my voice for other matters. Be on your way then, with Azurah's blessings.
How strange to see Zerith-var without his glowing eyes. And the way he holds himself. Very different from the Zerith we know now.

Mezamma's spell hits like a durzog. I still can't see quite straight.\n\nTell Prince Azah what you learned in the Worm Nest. And let him know what happened to Vanus. Then we need to figure out what Mezamma meant by the Fighters' heart.
I was too late. Again. We lost another leader because I wasn't here. I should have ….\n\nNo. This isn't time for recrimination. Talk to Skordo and let's figure out how to get Vanus back.
Once you attune to the feeling, illusion magic becomes quite recognizable. A sensation like crackling dried leaves in the air around it.\n\nFind this illusion. It might hide something important.

We are near the temple of the Hidden Moon. I sense the movements of the undead. Some dark portent shrouds this place, tamiit. \n\nPerhaps we can attend to it together and learn more about the fall of my order.

You helped me realize that the world doesn't stop just because someone we respected and cared about is no longer with us.\n\nNow that we know the enemy, the time has come to take the battle to the Worm Cult.
Don't worry. I'm not going to back out. I just need a few moments and then I'll be along.
Thank you for sparing Heloise's life. I'll find her and we'll figure this out. Together.\n\nWe just need to deal with these traitorous Montclairs first.

I need heartwood. From inside the lurchers. It's the only thing that will help the little spriggan at this point.\n\nI hesitate to ask more of an outsider, but we could do more than just ease her passing.

After you've ensured the city is safe, meet me in the castle, and we'll deal with Duke Renchant. The poor fool probably doesn't even realize he's committed treason.\n\nMay the gods keep you, my courageous friend.
You've been a great boon to the resistance. Once we have the traitor in our hands, we'll have all the pieces we need to assault the Seventh Legion.

Whatever drew the beetles here is making them aggressive too. If one of them gets near you, I'd say kill it before it kills you.\n\nI hope Jahi finds some way to get rid of them before Sentinel runs out of water.
Satakal's Wrath, wayfarer … unless you will enjoy wading through an army of undead, I would go no further.\n\nThe dead have risen at Tu'whacca's Throne.
Remarkable performance. Only <<1>> remains.
With so many barrels of water wasted, it will take us many weeks to gather enough water to replenish our stores.\n\nBut Sentinel will not go thirsty!

I honestly didn't expect Dame Clarique to let me go. You're my only hope now. My father's notes should be in our house. It's the one on the hill.\n\nGet the villagers to safety and then cast the spell. I'm sorry I can't help.
Have a look around, if you must, but we need to act soon.
Great chaos down at the docks, yes? An army of dead rises from the sea and storms the shore ….\n\nCan be very dangerous, or can be a good opportunity? You are interested in opportunity, yes?
Thank you for stopping that thing—whatever it was. I wish we could've saved his life, but at least we saved his legacy.

I beg of you to release me, for I am the unfortunate guide of a man named <<1>>, a scholar who explores these very caves.\n\nI must return to watch over him, for I fear he may take precious relics from these tunnels.
Hurry back to Stenwick. I have a bad feeling something's happened.
Let's get him back to camp as soon as we can. There's an empty tent on the hill. We'll take him there.\n\nTry to keep us away from the Imperial patrols. I don't think this fellow will go quietly.
Have you found something? Anything to indicate who killed Sir Etienne?
Who does she think she is? She'd better cure Draven as she promised.
The guest house is adjacent to our village center. Draven's resting there before the final ceremony.
This probably isn't the best time to visit Fell's Run, stranger. You don't want to get involved in our trouble.\n\nI suggest you find someplace else to spend your time.
Help me protect Tanval! He's got to complete that ritual.
I can feel it. The talisman has been used.
I'll be honest, I wasn't sure what I was going to do out here. Thank you, traveler.
Make your decision.\n\nWe must act before the enemy returns.
Assassins in the fort? It's unbelievable what these flat-heads are capable of.\n\nIf they're already within Arand's walls, we need to flush them out. And I think I know the way.
Safe travels. I must stay here on orders. Believe me, I'd rather be returning to Davon's Watch with you. The undead never sit well with me.
Excuse me, but I'm very busy.\n\nTalk to my husband, Beron.
Not all of us can thank you for preserving the <<z:1>>, but I hope we come to do so in time.
You recovered the <<z:1>>, yes? Then inform <<2>>, so <<3>> can finally achieve its salvation.
Who are you? What gives you the … oh! The hero of Fort Virak. Honor to you and your house.
If we can protect the <<z:1>>, our village will have nothing to fear from anyone!
If you see Tiril, tell him to meet me back at the house.
The sword recipe is just on the table over there.
Do you have our new crown? Is it ready? We are beside ourselves!
<<1>> will be safe for its pilgrims again.\n\nAnd the Altmer may remain here, if he wishes. He's suffered enough. Perhaps here, he will find happiness once again.
I 'm ready to start. Just give the word.
The Hist key should let us enter the xanmeer, but we must be careful.
This door won't budge! My partner might know how to open it, though. He's at the top of the xanmeer now.
Comrade. I have urgent matters I must attend to at the moment. \n\nPerhaps, in time, we will have more to discuss.
Aelif is certain this ruin will yield answers.
Take care finding the tomes. Take even more care to bring them back unharmed.
One thing always leads to another, and change can often be difficult to accept. However, we must continue. It's the only way.
It worked. Good.\n\nNow, speak to this memory of Stral. We'll spy the conversation he had with the cultist whose memory you stole.
I'm short on good help, and I could use someone capable. Someone like you.
That man … that Sheogorath. Can you … can you hear him? He's whispering in my head, I hear his voice. Why is his voice in my head?
They're all closed? Good, now place the crystals and the barrier should fade.
It's not an easy task we have ahead of us, comrade.
You look strong and capable. Good in a fight and brave enough to travel the world in search of adventure.\n\nIf my assessment is even close to correct, I could use your help.
What next? I don't know. I'll see to the dead, Bosmer and Drublog. It is all I can do. Simply … continue on.\n\nPerhaps Z'en will show me a new path while I pay penance. Perhaps I will find my own.

I promise we'll look after Scales. We'll make sure that she's safe and that she doesn't hurt anyone.\n\nNow I need your help. You saw for yourself. Vampire abominations prowl the springs. Those are my father's toys—sick creations of his evil mind.
Sal's got the heart of a senche, and possibly the brains of one. It's a long shot, but I'm willing to see his plan through.
Why is this happening?
Please, help us! The Silvenar's been captured. They want his life-energy! If they take it, the Bosmer are doomed!
The Silvenar! Where is he? Have you seen him?
I sense that you've completed your task. You've questioned the Houndsmen witches about the spinners and their bonds?
A little sneaking, a little destruction. Do what you need to in order to get that wine from the barracks.\n\nJust don't get caught.
Don't eat the bread; it's stale. Stick with the drinks. At least they're still potent.
<<1>> can't stay with me for long. If she weakens much more, she'll never take root in Treehenge.\n\nAnd if that doesn't happen, well ….
You can find her in the hall in Mournhold, comrade. May the Eight protect you.
I see Captain Warhammer tracked you down. Good.
Well met, Adept. We … we are in need of your assistance.
I arrived too late. By the time the latest recruits and I got here, the lieutenant was already on the ground.\n\nI saw the bastard that did this to him. Oh, yes. I saw him.
I'd prepared myself for death. I'm glad it was unnecessary.
Bit busy here. Please, can you ask the others for help? They're just up at the camp.
Hmm? Who are you? Wait. Not important.\n\nYou're new. And not a statue. I can use that.
You'll be perfect for this. You'll see. Raz has an eye for this sort of thing.
You've done us all a service, rescuing <<1>>.\n\nWould you like to hear more about her sister, the Green Lady?
I saw some of the townsfolk making for the cordon. How did it go?
When we found ourselves here, Mim wasn't sure what to do.\n\nThat mistake will not be made again. Mim will find this city and wait for the others.
The Trial of Spirit will demonstrate whether or not you understand the heart and mind of my people. May the river flow quickly as you undertake this endeavor.
I don't want to believe the poisoner was one of us. Maybe it wasn't. But someone must know something.
If anyone gives you trouble, tell them they'll answer to me.
I can't believe you decided to help those monsters instead of us. My people need you!
If you're trying to sneak up on me, you have some competition.\n\nThese flying books can be maddeningly silent, when they want to be.
That fight made me quite excited.
You aren't with the Dominion, are you?
And Haskill has arrived. Sheogorath's manservant, here to move us along. Hmph.
Dearie, do you think dirt in a barrel is funny? I don't.
Nicely done! Shazah really does have her tail on straight today. Get in there. Khali will be right behind you.
That light … the first Mane. What did he say? What did he want?

Praise Azura! I was losing faith. You were right about General Godrun. The Omen of Betrayal has the general in its grips. He was going to betray Emeric and attack Wayrest! \n\nThis was Vaermina's ultimate plan—to destroy the Daggerfall Covenant.
Hello? Who's there? Tazia? Tell your busybody Clanmatron I'm not interested.
Bright Moons, Hallowed. Good to see you. Khali is champing at the bit. She has grown tired of these Dro-m'Athra, and hungers for bigger game.
Once, when I was a cub, I caught one of the priests fashioning a sort of neck-cone out of cane bark. He said it allowed him to catch the moonlight better. They are strange, strange creatures.
Be careful in there. Whatever they are, get too close to them and they'll send you flying. Kalari found that out the hard way.
The moons have not been kind to <<1>> lately. Shuzura hopes you can brighten her sky.
Ohh. This one's back was not cut out for this.
Now we're in the Valenwood! Look at this place!

Bah! This Thalmor mage will drive Razum-dar mad! Stand here! Hold this! Everything so exact! \n\nThis one prefers more flexibility. He hopes you agree, because we must move quickly here if we are to protect the Dominion.
Did you find … erm … Gonlas! Yes, you were going to see about the strangers.
We should go to the cave temple of the Nereids.
I think Cadwell has something to tell you.
A great day for the Dominion! The Elder Scroll of Alma Ruma is ours, won by the might and will of our soldiers.
You need to finish Treeminder Xohaneel's trial before you can undertake mine.
Taking care of Aruz felt good. I'm happy to finally be doing something about this mess.
I'm sure my squad made it to shore alive. Dominion marines constantly defy the sea's attempts to drown us, but hurricanes are another matter. I fear my squad is banged up worse than I am.
The wards blocking the temple doors are located on opposite sides of the courtyard. We should hurry.
I actually hung back a bit to watch you two moving through town. It took all of my training not to laugh at those troops saluting you.
All of <<1>> prays <<Ac:2>>'s killer is found, and quickly.
Well done, Swordmaster!
My father would speak with you. I need a moment to myself.
My friend! Good to see you again. I need your help.
What are you still doing here? The vampires won't bleed themselves, you know.
You must not linger here, Moon Hallowed. Now that you know your place in the world, you must go to the people of Arenthia. The sons and daughters of Jone and Jode call for your aid.
Perhaps I shouldn't have attempted this by myself.
You should watch Aranias' demonstration.
Welcome. Marbruk may look like a small frontier town, but be assured, it is the work of the finest Altmer artisans.
Have you met <<1>>? She's an excellent host. Made me feel very welcome.
There is something different about you. I knew it! You saw through the illusion, didn't you?
We have heard of your victory in Arenthia. The moon's light flows in your wake! Now it is time you embraced your destiny.

I never expected to be standing in Coldharbour, helping command a force of elite mages. It's every little girl's dream come true! \n\nI'm just glad you're here. We never would have gotten this far without you.
We must get back inside the Grotto.
You drifted off there for a moment. Or maybe I did.\n\nSo what do you need?
The desert has enough trouble in it without anyone to stir things up.
It's done. The Sea Vipers are defeated.\n\nI should feel like we won, shouldn't I?
Don't ever doubt the scale of your victory. Everyone on <<1>> lives because of your actions.\n\nSafe travels. I hope our paths cross again.
The Barrowbough's roots are a bit dank, aren't they? A bit creepy?\n\nI know I shouldn't say it, but all the talking skeletons in one place are a bit unsettling. It's not just me, is it?
You're quite handy at defeating Maormer sorcery.\n\nI hope to see you again. Hopefully, with <<1>> at my side.
All three leaders have agreed to join us on Stirk. Now comes the tricky part.
Another important strategy meeting, is it? Excellent! Do pop by and say hello after you've finished, won't you?
And now we're in Valenwood? What in Nirn is going on?
Tread carefully. This is Brackenleaf's forest and we are Brackenleaf's Briars.\n\nIf you want to hunt here, you'll need to pay your respects at the shrines and join the Briars.
A glorious day, warrior! The Elder Scroll of Alma Ruma is ours at last.
Once we've spoken with Kasura, I hope to retrieve a suitable weapon for the battles that lie before us. The Valley of Blades has some of the finest swordcrafters in Hammerfell.
Where are the warriors who will take the Elder Scroll of Ghartok from our enemies? Surely you will be among them.
There she is! Let's show this duchess the meaning of the word anguish!
Foiled twice in a row. Let's end it next time, shall we?
Soldiers turned into bears? People setting themselves on fire? And now a mad mayor, locked in a cathedral!\n\nI know I should be horrified, but it all sounds so exciting.
The shrine is on the far side of the room. We must be cautious.
I've never seen Sai like this. He's in a lot of pain.
We are close—so very close to freedom. I have no qualms with leaving now that we are all gathered.\n\nThe Architect waits up ahead. If you can defeat him, we—all of us—will be free to leave.

You aren't with the pilgrims, are you? Then perhaps you can be of assistance.\n\n<<1>> scours this place for <<2>>, but the relic must be kept from her hands. Either she misunderstands the dangers, or she thinks they don't apply to her.

Listen. I-I was wrong to be so hard on you before. You've certainly proven now that you deserve my trust.\n\nI appreciate your help more than I can express, especially if you'll see this thing through.
Are you another soldier, come to loose trolls upon the Valenwood?
Where is this shrine? Let's find it and be done with this place.
You don't need two eyes to see how ugly things have gotten around here!
Hm?
I'm surprised Baron Dorell didn't accompany you here. He's never been one to shy away from getting his hands bloody in defense of House and country.
Follow the courier and see if he leads you to the informant.

You must be near an inactive ward upon the bear's death. The ward will empower you when you are close, so the bear's spirit will sense it and know where to go.\n\nOtherwise, the spirit is more likely to simply ascend, to be reunited with the earth.
These Reachmen sour the land. It's a slap in the face that Hircine allows them to take over our temple.
Julianos' little teapot! Where could they be?
Daraneth has returned to Elden Root. Now we must find a divine spark and an Ayleid source of power.
Ah, you made it. And I sense that the focus stones have been dealt with? Well done, hero.
Honor is satisfied. For all that it will do in the grand scheme.\n\nMy husband is gone.
What's this? Another stranger strutting into my town? Perfect! They'll probably give you the mayor's job!\n\nExperience? Bah! You don't need that! Just ask the new constable!
What are you still doing standing there? We have to find a way to get that trap door open!
Arkay preserve us! I don't relish the idea of climbing that cursed peak. But if that's where Montclair hides, then the Doomcrag is where we must go.
Something's definitely wrong, here. It used to smell of herbs and spices, now it's just brimstone and ash! We need to hurry.
The back gate is around the left side of the quarantine fence. If the Maulborn are using that old gate, then one of them must have the graveyard key.
The Maulborn may have fled the Serk, but the problems they brought with them still linger.
I tried to convince Ilthag Ironblood to stop training trolls with the gold Cassi gave me.\n\nSince that didn't work, I guess I'll have to beat him repeatedly with my pretty staff.

I'll accompany you to the scorpion matron's den and help you destroy the creature and its nests.\n\nHopefully, my disguise will hide my identity. I prefer not to kill any more of the Scaled Court than absolutely necessary.
Whew! That smell might be the most daunting thing I've ever faced! I hope you have good news.
You do not howl, or claw at your face. Is it possible you bested the Vaults of Madness Undaunted?
Look for rough maple in forested areas. Sometimes you'll see logs washed up on beaches.
Provisioning is a rewarding, yet grueling profession. "Gruel," you see? I am capable of levity … on occasion.\n\nFirst, you'll need a recipe and some ingredients. Then, you shall roast a pig.

<You notice a prominent handbill on the requisition board.>\n\n"Queen Ayrenn bids you welcome! Masters of the craft await you in <<1>>! New crafters shall be trained! Accomplished crafters will be certified! All at no cost to you!"
Thanks to me, Wrothgar is ours again.
<<1>> won't be far from Shatul. Unless he's truly witless.
The fate of the Empire, perhaps all Tamriel, hinges on what you do next. If we don't stop the forces of Molag Bal here and now—well, the prophecy in the Elder Scroll is … not encouraging.
I must determine how to safely remove one of these wonderful depictions!
Why are you still here? Do you need directions or something?
Once you clear the path, we'll be able to follow you up the mountain.\n\nHopefully by the time we catch up to you, you'll have found the missing members of our expedition.
These statues must lead the way to Morkuldin.
You look like the hearth-mother whose horker roast comes out of the oven and the nose ring she thought she lost is poking out of the gravy.\n\nSo, what did you find?

You look awful! I'm sorry, that sounded bad. You look … unkempt? To be honest, neither of us should have been standing that close to an explosion. My ears are still ringing.\n\nSo Molag Bal's dig is completely destroyed, yes?
Azhnura the Proselytizer needs to be killed. Maybe that will stop these cultists from torturing innocent people and forcing them to join their ranks.
So now we have a new chief. Everyone is ready to forget <<1>>. To ignore his murder.
I don't know what kind of feast <<1>> plans, but I cannot wait to share classic Orc cuisine with the king!

I've been wondering when you would show up on my doorstep. I've been following your progress for some time, and with great interest. \n\nYou show promise. I know talent when I see it. Are you interested in challenging yourself … to the utmost?

Welcome! It gladdens my heart that you have an interest in the history of our land and its people. And you found the notice! Wonderful!\n\nOf course, the House of Orsimer Glories will be even more impressive once all the exhibits have been filled.
The baron who built that last arena was one of the demiprince's favorites. I'm delighted to see that your performance has restored the baron to Fa-Nuit-Hen's memory. \n\nSo, please, don't stop now.
Take the meat to Bagrugbesh when you're done. You'll be well compensated for the effort, I assure you.
Look who's back! Doesn't look like you got gnawed up too bad.\n\nThe company has already taken its cut. <<1>> will give you the rest. Good work.

Come closer and let me look into your eyes. No remorse, no mercy. Yes, you do have the eyes of a killer. How many lives ended looking into those eyes? Enough that the Night Mother has noticed, obviously. \n\nWhich brings us both to this place and time.

That journal you recovered. The contents are … disturbingly intriguing. You reported that my old associate, Lyra Viria, is the Black Dragon. The journal, however, claims the Black Dragon killed Lyra.\n\nI need to determine the truth of this matter.

Silencer, is it? I suppose that's fitting. After all, your name is on four of my top contracts now.\n\nThat's just a Dark Brotherhood joke, my friend. I see your sense of humor is still in a distressing state of disrepair.
This little tub will get us to a blockade runner off shore. They'll bring us to <<1>> and back.\n\nI hope you don't get sea sick. I get sea sick. I'm … sure I'll be all right.
I've never stolen a guildmaster before.
Not now. I can't ….\n\nWe need to keep moving.

I'll meet you at the Chapel in Anvil. Hopefully, we'll find Hilde curled up and sleeping under Dibella's statue.\n\nJust be careful when you get to the city. The Pirate Queen hates the Brotherhood almost as much as the Sermonizers do.

Have you seen the Naughty Nereid Players? They're performing in Anvil, apparently at the Pirate Queen's request. They're a little crass for my taste, but that Torolon is the elk's antlers!\n\nOh, and Matron Astara wants to see you in the Sanctuary.
The news you brought suggests there's more to our recent troubles than I suspected.\n\nI'm sure I'll need you again soon, but in the meantime, Tanek would like to talk to you.
What else, Assassin? I need to know everything that occurred at the Order's enclave.
I tried to convince Ilthag Ironblood to stop training trolls with the gold Cassi gave me.\n\nSince that didn't work, I guess I'll have to beat him repeatedly with my pretty staff.

I'll accompany you to the scorpion matron's den and help you destroy the creature and its nests.\n\nHopefully, my disguise will hide my identity. I prefer not to kill any more of the Scaled Court than absolutely necessary.
Off you go. See the celebration for yourself!
You really got our investigation moving in the right direction! I know it's just a matter of time until Lord Vivec returns to his old self.\n\nI suppose you'll want to talk to the Archcanon, though.

She can be curt, but trust when I say we need Mistress Dratha—and not only for the sake of Vos and Tel Mora. Despite her temper, my mistress truly seeks the best for Vvardenfell. She cares too much, as the cliche goes.\n\nJust help her, please.
I am always glad to see you, my good friend. You are my good fortune talisman.
I sense that you have one of my Blessing Stones. Well done! Let the Archcanon know and we can begin the divination ritual.
Quite a musk you've acquired. Attractive. Was perfume all you acquired from the Ruins of Mazzatun?

I performed that ritual countless times and it never exploded in my face before! If I discover that you sabotaged the divination ….\n\nNo, I shouldn't take my failure out on you. It's not your fault that things are … difficult.
You have investigated the camps? Do you still believe we are to blame?

I thought the foreman was going to strangle me with his belt, but now we part company as friends? Remarkable.\n\nI owe it all to you. Without your help, my head would be decorating some Redoran's parlor. I'm at a loss.
Isn't it exciting? We're the first living creatures to set foot down here in more than a hundred years! This will definitely get an entire chapter in my next book!

Perfect! Such are the benefits of an extra set of appendages! The energy flows freely and without disruption, allowing the rods and the pistons to align in a most pleasing manner. Thank you.\n\nNow, why do you want to know about divine energy?

The Wise Woman returned from the Cavern of the Incarnate and went right into Skar to meet with the tribes. Chodala's in there, too, about to be named the Nerevarine.\n\nTell me you came back with something to stop my brother's rise to power.
Sorry about all the subterfuge, but we can't be too careful when it comes to security around here.
The sermons never prepared us for something like this. Perhaps, when this is all over, Lord Seht can write an addendum on what to do when talking crows and Daedric monsters come calling.
Explore that strange portal and locate my missing associate. Do this for me and I'll certainly make it worth your while.

I have an idea. Full disclosure—you may find this eerie.\n\nI suspected that Gascone's brain might contain some useful information, so I ordered a factotum to mine it. Speak to the Clockwork Clinician in the east wing. Maybe it found something.
This was supposed to be a special day, but it turned out all wrong. There's something not right with this oasis.

You've arrived. I am Divayth Fyr, wizard-lord of Tel Fyr. I trust no further introduction is necessary?\n\nI seek a Daedric artifact. It lies hidden in a brass city filled with danger, curiosity, and contradiction. You will accompany me, if you wish.
