Yes, much easier to explain now.\n\nThis is the Mnemonic Planisphere, where Sotha Sil's memories take the form of stars. We need your help to reclaim the stars that have fallen and place them back in the sky. If not, all shall be lost.
Quite a view, eh? Almost makes you forget you're shrunk down to the size of a beetle's toenail.

I must say, I'm surprised to find another newcomer here at the gate. Entering the city is no mean feat.\n\nMay I assume that you seek a citizen sponsor? My associates and I find ourselves in a similar predicament. Maybe we can help each other.

Such anger! Raz never expected to hear such words from the Queen's loyal subjects. The sentiment isn't universal, but enough feel this way for Raz to be concerned.\n\nDid you learn anything interesting from the people I sent you to talk to?
Good to see you again, my friend! I sent that message stone days ago. I was worried it hadn't reached you.\n\nLet me set aside what I was working on and then we can get down to business.
A Daedra? Here? And that's a Skaafin, if I remember my Daedric recitations correctly. Very curious.
Was Oriandra able to direct you to the proper elixir? Without something to amplify the magic, our ritual is going to fail.
Selynia! She's back to normal, thank goodness. How did you manage it?

You there! You're new to Rellenthil, aren't you? You certainly look like an outsider.\n\nI regret the necessity, but I must beg your aid. My brother is about to make a terrible mistake and join an appalling organization.

You'll find the other potentials inside the Manor of Masques. We have a talented crop this week, but I'm certain you'll fit right in.\n\nOh, and don't forget to wear your mask! We can't force you, of course, but why not get used to it?

Thank you for accepting my offer. I'm quite excited to be heading my own expedition. Usually I work under Telenger the Artificer, but sometimes he's a bit … much.\n\nIt's nice to finally be able to break free from being his assistant.
This is the only place she's ever known. She won't have wandered far. I hope.
The Aldmer fonts are throughout the keep's interior, but we should be able to reach them on our way to the battlements.

You found something? So did I. It looks like Farril was strangled, not stabbed. This blood must be the attacker's.\n\nA sickle? Hmm. Blood on the blade. She must have used it to defend herself—then the attacker hid it. This blood could be the key.

I'll start making preparations for the Dreaming Cave. In the meantime, Sotha Sil asked me to send you to his study the moment you arrived. I'm not sure what he wants, but you should tell him about your interactions with the betrayed Princes.

Most excellent to be seeing you again, my bestest friend! It is me, Rigurt! The Ebonheart Pact sent me to extend a branch of peace to snooty, rude, and very tall High Elf peoples!\n\nUnfortunately, my mission has ended before it has even begun.
You'd never know he'd just been shot by the way he's acting. He really does care about that indrik more than anything.

Lilawen should be able to tell you where you can find Tableau. Just look for a noble type who looks like she has a stick up her arse. Well … more so than usual.\n\nMeet me behind the vineyard afterward. I'd rather not overstay my welcome here.
I'll keep close. Don't want to get lost down here.

That gutless High Elf, Lirendel, thinks he can call me a pig-faced brute and walk away? I'm gonna knock that loose tongue right out of the back of his head! Just watch me.\n\nBy Mauloch, these Alinor pigs really twist my tusks.
I'm not sure what I expected, but it wasn't this. Are you sure we're in the right place?\n\nWhat am I saying? Of course you're sure!
Our search for staff fragments continues, initiate. But we require more information …. Information that only you and the Psijic Seals can provide.
I see something within you. A glistening jewel, ready to be polished. A passion teeming with brilliance, though not yet realized.\n\nTell me, do you wish to be certified in jewelry crafting?
Rest easy knowing such a dastardly fiend is being kept off the streets tonight.
Well. At least I'll get a roof over my head tonight.
Welcome back, initiate. The Loremaster has news you should hear. Go speak to him, all right?

Ah, welcome back initiate. I can't believe you collected all eight fragments of the staff! I know that we intend to render it inert … but there's no harm in learning more along the way, right?\n\nNow. I hear you're setting out for Rivenspire?
Thank you for returning so quickly, initiate. Our situation is dire.\n\nShortly after you left, the fragments of the Staff of Towers disappeared. Stolen, I'm afraid, by one of our own.
Tell me your trip to Sunless Hollow was successful, my friend. I could use a little good news right about now.
I can't wait to tell my egg-siblings all about our ancestor! They're going to be so proud!
You need to enter the ruins if you're going to find out what Margus and the Blackguards are up to. Go on. You can do it. I believe in you!

Pages torn from Heetzasi's journal? I do not mean to speak ill of the dead, but I must admit some surprise. He never struck me as someone committed enough to keep a journal.\n\nIf he knew about the Remnant, this could prove invaluable.
I'll see you back in Lilmoth, right? My office. Talk to you soon!

Try to be quick about it. If the Blackguards get away with those items, tracking them down will be next to impossible.\n\nIf you need more to go on, find Solni—here in town. She's the one who tipped us off.

That Kassandra would use friend-Famia as a lure to trap us. It dries my scales, beeko. Even so, we cannot leave her to die.\n\nLet us hope the river carries us where we need to be. For now, we must make for the Xul-Thuxis temple.

Why do you slump? Bristle your war-spines! Etra was a legend, true. But what you fight is not Etra. It is the pieces not needed, bound together by slime and old-time magic. A beast to crush and cleave!\n\nTake your weapon and strike true!
Gracious Roots, it just died. Why are these sickly creatures coming here?
The chimes spoke of a visitor's approach. Our Hist welcomes you within its boughs, and so do we. \n\nI regret that you arrive for what should be a joyous occasion to find only worries and troubles.
You look like someone who knows a good business opportunity when you see one. Much profit! Will you hear me out?

Stopping Kassandra won't be simple. With the Sap-Speaker's staff and such a long headstart …. No, no—can't think like that! I'm here to supply valuable historical information and boundless optimism. So that's what I'll do!
Why? Why did she do this to us?
What are you looking at me for? Talk to Kassandra.
Why do you stop? Every moment we delay widens the gap between us and our quarry. \n\nBesides, everything in this city means to do us harm. We should not stay in one place for long.

Smoke and sunless sap …. Strange that the Bright-Throats' Hist would speak in such dour terms. Maybe it describes some dark age? The Alessian incursion of the First Era? Or perhaps a dark age yet to come ….\n\nEgads. Let's hope it's not that.
Many apologies, traveler, but the Xinchei-Konu is not able to take visitors at this time.
I think I swallowed … enough mud to fill … a pitcher!

Ha. You arrive just in time, beeko. Kassandra watches us like an old mother-turtle, Jaxsik paces like a caged wamasu, and poor friend-Famia just tries to make friends ….\n\nAnd I thought throat-song night at the Lusty Argonian Footman was awkward!
We must get inside and prepare to defend the town. Euraxia's forces are on their way.
The problem with hiding your valuables behind complex mechanisms is that if those mechanisms break, your treasure is lost forever. Let's hope that's not the case here.
This place … this must be the entrance to the hidden Akaviri shrine. Zamarak just hopes we have arrived in time to save the Dragonguard from the assassins' blades.

Thank you for the aid, traveler-friend. The undead walk the ruins of Cicatrice, directly to the west. I would advise caution.\n\nAh, so much trouble for my egg-mother's research notes. I now wonder if traveling to this town was the right decision.

The bloody bandages, the cameo, and swaddle cloth—all these trinkets and mementos lead to a forbidden place. Baan Dar's Litter.\n\nVazbi has not been totally honest with you, walker. This one has a very personal stake in this business.

Why don't you begin by speaking to the lady in question? The magnate should be in the town square. Strike up a conversation and see what she reveals.\n\nIn the meantime, I'll begin my own investigation. See what I can dig up.
A missing daughter, a hidden note, and now a band of skooma smugglers. This investigation becomes messier with every step we take.
No time to explore this place. I just picked up a scent.\n\nI think the Betrayer is ahead of us!
Tasnasi begs you keep your voice down. She knows Khasda keeps no guards down here, but there might still be someone—or something—listening.
The Bowel? Well, that's ironic.\n\nI'll head there after I get my tools … and find another pair of smallclothes.
Tasnasi wants you and Nazdar to make your way to the base of the south tower. That's where we're waiting.\n\nShe also was very insistent: avoid killing any of the guards.
"The mind can overcome any discomfort," sings the Lamentation of Dis. Clearly they didn't consider how an old Khajiit feels in the cold.\n\nNazdar feels the damp in his bones. How can you stand it?

The eclipse approaches, and with it the opening of the Moon Gate of Anequina. We have a short amount of time before the way to Jode's Core appears.\n\nAt least I am attuned. And I was able to charge the Dragonhorn.

Yushiha is grateful. This caravanner she saved was not alone. Help her check on their camps. Warn them. Protect them if necessary. We must save them from my clan before we can save my clan from themselves.\n\nShe only hopes it is not too late.

I sent Khamira out to coordinate the city's defenses while Tharn and I continue to refine our strategy. Can we hold the city or should we fall back? I hope the battlemage can pull a miracle out of his ear, but we cannot count on that.

I think we can trust this Mazza-Mirri. Do as she asks and learn what you can.\n\nI'm going to head back to the tomb where you destroyed the phylactery. I can't shake the feeling that we missed something. We'll meet again soon. Azura guide you.
Why do you linger, child? Go. Learn.
If M'zum and J'dathal have been robbed, then Mother is likely the next target. And with luck, her cellar will show evidence of the theft.

I was beginning to suspect you were never going to arrive. After Calsivius and my half-sister manipulated us into inadvertently releasing a rage of Dragons, Elsweyr has been overrun by the beasts.\n\nWe do bear some responsibility, I suppose.

Thank you for offering to help.\n\nOddly enough, the thief did leave a note mentioning a "grave of snake men." I suspect it refers to the Tomb of the Serpents, an old Akaviri crypt. Hopefully, that is where you will find the missing pieces.
Greetings, greetings. Were you able to find the missing mural pieces?
Don't worry, good looking. I've got this handled. Go do what we talked about, eh?
My helpful friend! Rigurt is pleased to see you returned from the desert with your limbs intact. Did you find the misplaced package in Riverhold?
I know you! You're that soulless drifter, right?\n\nDon't worry about these levelheaded losers. No one can see me but you. You possess a special untapped talent for unhinged insanity!

I remember when spells such as this … took barely any effort.\n\nWhile Sai rallies the Dragonguard, our job will be to reach the island and find a way to lower its defenses. Then we can take on Kaalgrontiid with our full contingent.
Were you able to find the Horn of Ja'darri?
I've seen Abnur Tharn use portals. That does not look like one of his.\n\nBe ready for anything, my friend.
My student waits inside. I'm sure the maps we found will prove useful to his endeavors.
I'm not scared, I'm just trying to be cautious. One of us has to be reasonable here.
I heard rumors that Queen Khamira was moon-touched, but that was … disconcerting.\n\nTell me, my friend. Does she fall into trances like that very often?
It seems that young Aeliah has joined us. See what she has to say.
Did you find Dak'radhi's ingredients, walker? We are preciously short on time. Vijari's health is failing him.
That must be Laatvulon. He's an ugly beast.\n\nHe mentioned aeonstone, yes? That must be what they call those green rocks. The trial master spoke about them as well.
It is a claw, that is definite. I will study it, search Anequina's memories. It must have a purpose, even if the meaning initially eludes me.\n\nDid Khunzar-ri say anything else, five-claw?
Za'ji proudly claimed that the Perfect Pounce could navigate any waters to reach any island. And that is true.\n\nBut no waters surround an island in the sky. Sadly, that is also true.
Queen Khamira? When did Anequina put a Khajiit back on its throne? The state of heralds and couriers these days, it's a wonder we hear anything at all down this way.
I'd offer to help if I could, but I'm afraid I know next to nothing about magic.
I'll meet you by the statue of the Forgotten Mane. It should be just south of Black Heights.
Huh? Oh. Sorry, pal—still a little woozy. The Dragonfire swept the kidnappers' tracks pretty good. Frustrating.\n\nHow about you? You find anything useful?

Sai Sahan requires your attendance. Sent this one all the way here to collect you.\n\nSidura thought about telling him no, of course. But then she thought that it never hurts to get in good with a man such as him.
By Leki's Blade, I just hope Nahfahlaar is still breathing. Without his aid, defeating Laatvulon and his forces becomes a far more difficult task.

Our camp isn't far from here. Just over that rise and across the river.\n\nI looked, but I'm terrible at finding clues. Maybe you'll have better luck figuring out where the thieves went after they took my uncle's gourmet moon-sugar.
These … these wounds won't keep me from cutting you down if I have to, wayfarer.\n\nWho are you? Are you in league with these dead-summoners and graverobbers? Speak quickly!
I'd say placing an ancient corridor and its matching door behind a waterfall counts as hidden. I wonder what's behind it that will help us reach Dragonhold?

The witches called forth freezing weather at Icereach. Now fire? It's almost like they're experimenting with different effects.\n\nHead to the next location and see what you can find. I'll catch up soon.
I've heard tales of Skyrim's enormous frost spiders. But to see one up close … quite disturbing!
Go ahead. Do as Fenn asked and pour the oil into the cauldron. We need to find out if this protective elixir is going to work.

Svana's associate, Maugh, will procure most of the supplies I need, but there's one final ingredient required. For various reasons, I can't simply walk into the Hall of the Dead and claim it myself.\n\nI need you to acquire Arkay's sacred oil.
You have the oil? Then toss it in the cauldron.\n\nYou don't want to know what else Fenn and the old witch had me drop in that pot.
Karthwatch is gone. No people. No jarl. The seat of the entire hold. Wiped out, just like that.\n\nI have to get my father to take action!
That looks like an entrance, but it's all iced over. What about the amulet? Can you use it on the door?
Go back and talk to him. My size tends to be more frightening than reassuring.\n\nI'll keep watch and try to figure out what this place is.

That door's sealed tight. And since we can't climb up on the pipes and crawl in the way Edjar got out, we're going to have to be creative.\n\nThere's got to be a mechanism to open it. Take a look around and see what you can find.
Do you feel that? The hairs on the back of my neck are standing on end.\n\nWe're getting closer to my father, but the harrowstorm is coming.
There's no time! We need to ascend the tower and catch up with Svargrim and the Ashen Lord!
The stone husks are moving! We'll have to fight our way through.
Poor Larilvor held such promise. His faith in Meridia was so strong. How could he have died this way?
No harm in talking. Lots of harm in the alternative. For them, anyway.\n\nGo ahead and converse with the smuggler.
A Reachmen camp, right on our borders! With a horde of this size, Karthwatch never stood a chance.\n\nStill no sign of the captives, though. Let's keep searching.
Petraloop is just the start of your noble journey!\n\nOnce you collect all the instruments, I will stage an epic, "An Adventurer's Triumph," to celebrate their return. You will star in it, of course.
This site is vital to the investigation … perhaps we should break down the door. Talk to Phebe. I need space to come up with a solution.
Let's look for more witch pikes. The more I can learn, the better chance I have of understanding the nature of this ritual.
Search the other end of the overlook while I continue to look around here. Let's see if Ena left anything behind to suggest where we might find her.
You remember Princess Svana. From the Lonely Troll. Talk to her but go easy on her. She just lost her mother.
Let me take a look at what you found.

The harrowstorms continue to ravage our land, filling the city walls with people crying for protection. And what does the high king do? Next to nothing!\n\nOh, he makes small gestures, but still things worsen.
I'll help Mugha. You find the other missing miners!
Don't do it! You'll bring the rest of the mine down upon us!
I'm sorry. I thought I'd prepared myself for this. Just … give me a moment.
Friend, we need to catch Old Hjaalsdottir! Let's run!
Visitors come so rarely to visit this old woman. But fate has a way of making one suddenly useful.\n\nWell, get close to the fire. Warm up. Pose your question.
Didn't expect to run into you down here. Are you following me? You're following me aren't you?

What excellent luck. Never thought I'd see your face ever again. But here you stand, just when I need you.\n\nIf you can believe it. I'm trying to stop another vampiric threat endangering all of Tamriel. Don't pretend to act surprised.
Don't you have some flower petals to pluck, or something?\n\nGo on, assistant! Maelmoth's Mysterium awaits!

Let's go. The mound is just past that hill. I need to get a feel for the energy there before I start. I don't want to accidentally turn you into a frog or something. \n\nThat was supposed to be funny.
Even thousands of years later, I smell faint traces of blood, sweat, and fear. A Gray Host survivor definitely hid out here.\n\nLet's have a look around.
That appears to be another sheet of rather pristine parchment. See if it's another note left by the pentarch.

Did the Gray Host arrive after the clan entered the barrow? Are they waiting to slaughter them when they emerge, like a wolf gobbling up baby birds as they leave their nest?\n\nWe need to reach Nathari and warn her that the clan's in danger.

What you discovered doesn't tell us much about the Darkstorm. At least not yet. But a picture is beginning to form in my mind.\n\nRada's letter provided one more clue. He claims to have a laboratory inside this very structure. We just have to find it.

This is one of those trinkets with auramancy on it, isn't it? Like the one you and Fennorian found? Does that mean Rada al-Saran was here? Then why did he leave the book? Just so Verandis could find it?\n\nI'll let you examine the enchanted memento.
Rada al-Saran must have left this for Verandis to find. We should see if it sheds any light on what he's up to.\n\nDo whatever you and Fenn did the first time and see what happens.
More auramancy. Strong, too. Rada al-Saran's magic might be more powerful than Verandis's.\n\nNo, what am I thinking? It's probably just … different.
My explorations have turned up very little, but it looks like you've had better luck. What did you find?

Don't worry, I'll watch over you. I won't let anything harm you while you're dream-walking.\n\nRemember, you'll experience Verandis's memories of this place. If he has any. Learn what you can and then look for the potion again when you want to wake up.

Outsider, you approach Fialyn, apprentice shaman of the Crow-Eye clan. That cursed storm may have disrupted our wards, but make no mistake—this is still Reach land, defended by brave Reachfolk.\n\nWe will not give up without a fight.

Go with Apprentice Fialyn and gather the offerings. You should be able to find them around the old tower, right outside the village.\n\nReturn to me after you place the offerings at the four wards. Then I will complete the restoration ritual.
That's Kathad, five-claw. And the vampire behind him, that's Freyleth.\n\nThis one will keep watch while you talk to him, yes?

I heard what the sentry said. Why would Caddach recall his soldiers and leave the Gray Host unmolested? That makes no sense.\n\nGo. Learn more about these so-called witch-rebels. We can use what you find to get us into Ard Caddach's throne room.
Speak with Shaman Ulvoch. Let him know the offerings have been placed and everything is ready for him to start the ritual.
An image of the Headsman. In many tales, he cuts off the head of a great serpent in defense of lesser star spirits. Curious.

A fellow Psijic! Did the Order send you, my friend?\n\nI'm a new recruit, but perhaps you know my mentor, Master Pythis? I could actually use a bit of help in that regard. I'm currently looking for him, and I'm a bit concerned.

Oh it's you! We keep running into each other at the funniest spots. You wouldn't be following a lady, would you? Nah, I'm just teasing.\n\nThough, now that I think on it, why are you here? Were you hired too?

I feel just a little winded from that fight. And a little, um … embarrassed. I have no idea how I can possibly fight through more of these creatures.\n\nYou should talk to Lyranth. She's in charge here.

Lyris went to Hroldan Ring to talk to a vateshran—a Reach lorekeeper—to find a local version of this story.\n\nI suggest we go to the source. A sacred site dedicated to Faolan—Red Eagle Redoubt. Look for a vateshran and I'll meet you there.

An outsider! I haven't seen one of you in here for … it must be centuries. Well, as the local ghostly guide for Vateshran Hollows, welcome to the Choosing.\n\nI hear deciding on your first wing can feel daunting. Ask away if you have questions.

I don't approve of an outsider being involved in our sacred rites, but it seems you and Fialyn managed to place the offerings at the wards. That's something, at least.\n\nSpeak to Shaman Ulvoch if you insist on interfering in clan business.

Eslyn's plan is a good one. I don't like her going off on her own, but she can take care of herself.\n\nI'll make sure the vateshran gets to Hroldan Ring. Then I'll go to Faolan's Ire and help Eslyn … if she needs it.

I know this is a lot to ask, but the vateshran is at the mercy of the Thornroot clan.\n\nPlease, enter the ruins and get him out of there. If he can tell us about the origins of the feud … well, the important thing is rescuing him.
You go on ahead. After all that running and sneaking, I need to catch my breath.\n\nMy camp is up on the ridge, to the east.

A sorcerer? That explains a lot. And from the sounds of things, my manservant isn't the only one endangered by this so-called curse.\n\nMeet me inside the xanmeer and we'll find a way to put this evil back in its prison.

I already feel better about all this. Thank you!\n\nNow, you should talk to Governor Keshu about her plans for the battle. Find out where she wants us and what we're going to do with Sombren and the twins.

You return at a grim moment, mercenary. While you were gone, word reached us that the Waking Flame is gathering an army. I fear it will soon march on Gideon.\n\nBut Eveli said you took the Ambitions to learn about their powers. Did you succeed?
You said there was a hidden compartment under the nightstand? Let's see what it contains.

I sense … yes, you are the mortal I sent for. And not a moment too soon. Good.\n\nI attempted to get this Mehrunes Dagon cultist to enlighten me. He refused. I may have insisted a bit too vigorously, but it was his own fault.

The history of this abbey and its fall into ruin remain clouded in mystery. All I know for certain is that the Golden Anvil was never recovered.\n\nWe should search for surviving records from Gavos's time. Some trail to follow, however waterlogged.
Keep an eye out for any suspicious activity. The threat could come from anywhere.
What took you so long? Never mind, never mind. Look down there!\n\nThat's the cult leader and the scholar-lady I told you about. And that must be the Imperial cache!
I know I grumble a lot about the pains he puts me through, but I don't want to see Quistley hurt. On the other hand, a scare might be good for him. He could use a hard lesson or two.

I'll leave finding the hostages to you. Erilthel can lead them out through the sewers. And I'll … be the distraction. Again.\n\nStart by checking the tower, southwest of the fortress. I overheard that they were holding a group of captives there.

You look like a hearty soul, unconcerned with the prospect of death by trick, trap, or misadventure. How do you feel about helping a defenseless scholar from Gideon unearth a little history from Undertow Cavern?\n\nOh, and can you swim?
You found the Deadlands slivers? Good.\n\nI set up the portal at the top of the hill behind me. I'll attune Calia and Destron. Then we can make our way to the summit.
I suppose we must trust in Sombren's experience. He knows quite a lot more about our powers than we do.
That wasn't so hard. Now, let's hurry and join Sombren on the road. The Deadlands await!
Dislodge the stones, friend. I don't want to weave this spell any longer than necessary!
I think we would have been fine without the vampire's help. He must have been caged up for a reason, right?
Please be so kind as to talk to Revus, and leave me be. Self-reflection is the closest I get to decent conversation, these days.
Portals opened all around me and suddenly there were cultists everywhere!

Would you look at the size of that weed! I'd never let it get like this in my garden, I can tell you that.\n\nLooks like they've got their prisoners working all over the place. We should split up and make quick work of freeing them.
Before you light the lantern, does my hair look all right? Oh, never mind.

Try not to judge them too harshly for their grouchiness. We just ripped them from the most pleasant slumber they've ever experienced.\n\nWe should be off at once to detain Cres. I'll be right behind you.
I knew we shouldn't have come here. Old ruins are nothing but trouble. Especially for someone as reckless as my brother.

I know Olik means well, but assuming the Imperials took our people could lead to unnecessary bloodshed. Not that I have ever shied away from such a thing, of course! I am no stranger to gruesome battle!\n\nBut … if we can avoid it, maybe we should.

So the Order of the Waking Flame killed your councilors and placed the blame on the Dark Brotherhood. Then their high priest sent his followers to kill us.\n\nCare to enlighten me as to what this is actually all about now?
The ritual must have several focal points nearby. We need to find them if we hope to save Deejos. Barring that, we need to stop the ritual before it consumes her like Ghalor.
Did I hear that correctly? Sewers? Do you know what's in sewers? Sewage! It's disgusting!\n\nAll right, all right. Let's just get going before I change my mind.
We should hurry back to the gate. We don't have the skyshard, but we do have a spark of Aetherial energy. That's the important bit!
What have you got there? A letter?\n\nHere, let me have a look at it. Oh, and can I have my stone back? I think I've had my fill of grisly memories for now.

I'm not far off any time you need me … but I'm anxious to learn more about my mother and sister. And I want to make sure Inalieth has somewhere safer to stay. I'd like to think the Hallixes owe her that much for her service.
Now then, just release the dragonfly in my direction. Concentrate on the vital energy that connects both you and it. I will perform the ritual quickly!
So a master mage who murdered my grandfather was expelled by the guild for practicing forbidden arts and has a reclusive hideaway. That sounds promising, in the worst way possible.

This area is off limits. Only those with the highest authority are permitted here. Though there's no one left aside from these cultists and Daedra to enforce such restrictions.\n\nIf you're here to explore, perhaps we can come to an arrangement?
Do not linger here if you have no business with the Witchmothers. It is a dark place not meant for all.

Whatever this used to be, it was magically active until recently. I can feel residual energies, like Martus said. It doesn't so much make my skin crawl as make it want to peel off and run screaming away from here.

Now that I know what to call it, I can feel the egonymic within me. It's been a part of me for my entire life, but I just accepted it without ever knowing what it was. \n\nI'm not sure what we can do with only my piece of it, though.
If there's a way to stop Mehrunes Dagon, we'll find it.

I expected none of this. The Ravener speaks? And what's the purpose of a tower full of books?\n\nAfter everything I went through to get here, I still don't understand what we face. What is this creature?
We need to find a lucent and place it inside that discharge labrum. Hopefully we're on the right track and that will unlock the furnace door.
There are secrets I still need to learn, little mortal. As long as you continue to be more of a help than a hindrance, we will get along smashingly.
My lord, please take the remaining Mother Stones from the altar. We'll need them when we find the statues, and I'm clearly not meant to touch them.

I know the threat posed by the Order of the Waking Flame isn't over. As much as I wish that destroying the Riven Cataclyst was the end of it, I know that it's not. Sister Celdina won't be stopped that easily.\n\nTalk to Lyranth and see what she thinks.

So, Madam Whim's obnoxious little assistant actually found you? I'm pleasantly surprised. I assumed his incompetence matched his lethargic nature.\n\nNow that you have returned, we can resume our hunt for Sister Celdina and the Riven Cataclyst.

Not so long ago, the Blood Pit trembled at the mere rumor of my approach. They cowered before me!\n\nI first encountered Elegian there. He was quite mad. Probably still is. I'm not sure what he'll be able to tell you, master.
Zynoahz is one of Valkynaz Nokvroz's most fearsome underlings. He commands many Dremora. I do not know if he and Jynd work together for their master, or if they compete for his approval.
Curious. A poison that affects Daedra. Hrmph. This is new to me.\n\nWe know more now. Not a random attack from a hater of Daedra. Someone able to apply this to Tephilaz. Got close. This was planned.
Come on, we need to search those ruins for clues.
That poor man. I'm not sure if we can get anything useful out of him in the state he's in. But we came all this way. You might as well talk to him.
My teeth clatter in anticipation. For blood! For tasty flesh!
Time to move out, my friend. I'll meet you at the base of Annihilarch's Summit.

Madam Whim does nothing unless she believes it benefits her interests. We are much alike in that regard.\n\nWe would be wise to remember that Whim's loyalties are for sale. I will keep an eye on her while you align the rune stones.
A new obstacle, simple but effective. The wind-gate blocks anyone from following the path to the summit. Unless they have a way to open it, of course.\n\nTry the key you found, mortal.
With everything that's happened, I almost forgot about the relic. Lyranth is right. The Anchorite might recognize it. Go on and show it to her.
That's a lucent. You need to charge it to dispel the ward.\n\nPlace it in the dynamus font nearby to fill it with energy.
Come, little mortal. There is work to do.
From the map, Blind Elegian is in his own prison within this place. He is important to Dagon, it would seem
Once you've lit the braziers we can get started, so don't dawdle. I've been stuck in this miserable place long enough as it is.
It's rather rude of you to interrupt someone who is clearly quite busy.
This is what we came for. Collect the sword.
I don't like assisting the likes of Gilfrex, but at least we'll spare one person from his grasp.

Pay no attention to the Ascendant Order's lies. They work in the shadows to undermine the ruling bodies of Tamriel, and they don't care who gets hurt.\n\nKeep searching. See if you can find where they're holding Quentyn.

I've learned to trust Lady Arabelle's instincts, even if others sometime believe that she overreacts. \n\nAs long as we're waiting, I plan to head inland and talk to a druid I've heard about. Maybe she'll be willing to discuss arcane practices with me.
Seasons turn and months continue, but Zenithar's adoration of all who labor never ceases. \n\nPerhaps that's why I encountered you again. With your aid, we appeased Zenithar and set all to rights!
I know Stendarr preaches patience. But that man is insufferable. Tch.\n\nLet's find his sword, shall we?
I'm sorry to follow you both here. I just … wish there was something more I could do.\n\nI'll be ever so grateful if you can get me out of this.
We need to make sure these peace talks are successful, no matter the cost.

You're a sight for sore eyes! I've been looking for someone to help with a problem, but I wasn't expecting you to come by!\n\nMy patron needs someone like you—competent and unknown here on High Isle. I promise, it will be worth your while.

This is it. This is really it. The place where my ancestor's legend came to an end. Feels a little strange to be picking over her leftovers like some harpy … but it's not like I'm just some scavenger. I'm family. This is—uh, an inheritance. Yeah!
It pains me to think that I'm going to the castle's once beautiful gardens just to find necromancers and undead there.

I'll have Jakarn look for the dockmaster, although I don't expect he'll be easily found.\n\nYou and I should head to Steadfast Manor and check in with Lord Bacaro. He needs to know what we've learned so far. And let's hope he has a lead for us.
We are the Evergrowth. The one you sought, she carries the taint of our corruption. We remember her from the Undergrove. She performed the ritual that released this blight upon the land.
There should be a lever or a pulley or something around here. Hopefully we can just get it unstuck to get the wheel turning again.
I'll be by the livestock pens once you're finished setting the traps. Hopefully, I'll have a solution by the time you get there. \n\nFingers crossed!

While portals to and from Amenos are prohibited, I can teleport within the confines of the island. It just takes more effort. Interesting.\n\nThank you for procuring these items. With them, I can clear the storm when we're ready to depart.
I washed up alone and now I'm surrounded by allies. At least, allies for the nonce.\n\nIt's funny how fate can change in a moment, eh? Let's talk about the things we found in the cave.
The Ascendant Order has made a grave enemy this day. Mark my words!

Jakarn and I have been watching the entrance. There are definitely people going into the dungeons and not coming out. They must be throwing quite a party down there.\n\nNo sign of the Ascendant Magus, though. He may already be inside.
You have that invitation you found, right? Try showing it to the sentry at the door.
Another intruder, eh? You come for my nets? My buckets? Speak quickly!\n\nAnd don't you go telling tales. Me and the lads … we'll know!
You should go collect the smelly man's pack so we can get Oblan down from here.
See? This is all working out. Trail <<1>> back to his den and bring back proof he has skooma there. We need to free <<2>> so he can pay his tab!
You're a friend to those in tight spots. I appreciate that. I only wish I knew what exactly happened last night!
Walk carefully. This place is crawling with those Hadolid creatures. \n\nI won't get in your way once the fighting starts, promise.
That's it, my friend! We have all three keys. Now to go and open the vault!

So, not only did Song's family kidnap her, but they did it so they could force her to commune with some creepy relic that makes them more powerful?\n\nThose Emerald Eye bastards! We have to get her away from them.
I'm so glad he's safe. We'll follow your lead. Let's get out of here.
Heh, I don't know why you're here, but you are a handsome sight.
Ah, fair Janne, you were always my light, guiding me home. Just like this lighthouse once did.

Janne's ghost implies that one of us has done her some wrong. Why don't you talk to her and see if this is another replication of a past event. Perhaps we'll learn something new.\n\nJust remember to play along so as not to shatter the illusion.
Walker? Is that you? What are you doing here? Are you a prisoner?\n\nNo matter. Just seeing you makes me feel hundred times better.

Tell me you signed up for the tournament. You did, didn't you? Great! That's great! You're going to do great. We all are! Just got to focus, right? It's all about focus … and, oh, and breathing.\n\nWhy are my ears sweating?

So, have you thought it over? The chance to join the Gonfalon chapter of the Roister's Club … well, it is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity.\n\nI jest, of course. It is nothing so serious. Still, we would be glad to have you!
Kishka will tell you everything you need to know about our daily challenges. I do them every chance I get, and I'll tell you, it's always worth the effort!\n\nHave fun out there!
The first time I met you, I knew that greatness dwelt in your heart. Now, we see it in full bloom!\n\nAn advanced player unlike any I've seen before!

Just going to take another moment with my old friend Kynareth here.\n\nNone of the Eight really take an interest in games, as far as I know. But I like to think the old girl will nudge things in my favor at least a little.
Ah, traveler. We meet again. It's nice to see a friendly face for a change.\n\nMy last few visitors were intent on tasting my blood.
Sea-tossed. Sand in my britches. Unsure where I am.\n\nI'll tell you, this sure takes me back.

Archdruid Michiel, that unrelenting parasite! Good thing we showed up when we did. \n\nGo check on Wyress Tola. After what the Firesong put her through, another druid is probably the last person she wants to see. Dhulef and I will keep watch.
Slimy urchin! Archdruid Michiel was too much of a coward to deal with us, eh? I'm sure we'll get our chance eventually.\n\nGo check on Wyress Tola. We'll make sure the danger's passed.
By the Green, how did you find me, friend? No, I don't care. I'm just glad you're here.\n\nYour timing is excellent. I'm not sure I could endure another round of my gaolers' torture.
You understand your task? The Sea Elves aren't standing about here, so go find them. I look forward to reports of your success.

You don't know how lucky you are. I spent years on this island before I was invited to attend a meeting of the Draoife. It's hard to win the druids' trust.\n\nGive Laurel my regards. She's the best of them all, if you ask me.

I didn't expect to see you again so soon, friend, but I never refuse the gifts that Y'ffre is willing to give me.\n\nI came to help the Eldertide Druids, but I was too late. This battle is already lost, blight take it!
Poison is a coward's weapon. I should have smelled it the moment Lady Arabelle uncorked the wine.\n\nGo, five-claw. Find the coward and make them pay. We'll watch over Lady Arabelle. I promise.
Za'ji will return to Gonfalon Bay now. Caska will be lost without this one's steady presence to calm her.
The antidote is working faster than I expected. Lady Arabelle should be back to her old self before the next torchbug blinks.
Let's see what they're growing down here.

Keep your voice down, my friend. And take a moment to appreciate this one's subtle disguise. \n\nNow, let's focus. Raz heard the waitstaff say that Grandvache's office is through the high-stakes suite. That … could pose a problem.
Remember, your first task is to find our captive townsfolk and free them. If Archdruid Orlaith threatens them, I will have no choice but to lay down my sword.
Looks like the coast isn't quite clear yet. Ring the bell and alert the crew. This fight's not over!
Follow the passage. Elder Aiven said the Ivy Throne is ahead. Watch for more motes. Dreams. Memories.
Why do I get the feeling that our troubles are far from over?
The druid said to follow the stream. Or was it the trees?\n\nWell, I followed something and I spotted you, so this must be the right spot. I think. I hope. How are you?

Remember, you're after a rock in the middle of the lava fissure. It's going to be too hot to touch if you don't use the freezing spell.\n\nI don't mean to nag, but I'd really like to keep both of us from bursting into flames.
Ancient druids used places like this to call upon the spirits of the Green, but such techniques were lost a long time ago. I wonder how Bacaro accomplished it.
The shadows in here can help us. Stay low and quiet.\n\nHopefully we'll get this done in a flash. Find the relic, put on the cloth, lift it, then leave. Easy.

The Chronicle blessed us with another vision. We saw the Firesong attack Eldertide. Threaten us to gain possession of the Chronicle. All this bloodshed … that could explain why the spirit feels so guilty.\n\nBut the motes. It saved Gwenaelle.
I'm still wet. And really cold. I don't like it, friend of Quen's. Quen friend.\n\nWhat's the note say? It made my delightful Neri leave.

Let's head back to Glimmertarn. I need to give the druids instructions and make preparations to depart for Vastyr.\n\nBe on your guard. The trees hide many evils. The Dreadsails and Firesong get bolder by the moment.

You look the type to have solved a riddle or two. Now, to get that bird talking, you'll need to prompt him with the passphrase. \n\nIt's from an old Abecean freebooter saying. "No prey" to hear his first riddle. "No pay" to hear the second.

It's good of you to offer to help, outsider. Fire and foliage, that's the key to reversing the curse. If we repair what's broken, then the curse will be lifted. \n\nAt least, that's what I can make out from the text carved into this stone.
Bassian has a talent for ancient languages and obscure ciphers. I want to consult with him about the letter Dralys gave you.\n\nI shall meet you at Mildanor's home shortly.
He's taunting us at every turn. We can catch him. Keep moving!
Long roads has this one traveled to get to where we are now.
Just tell me quick, please. The sooner I know their intentions, the sooner I can write this dismal report and start looking for a new job.
Protus is stable. Kemel-Ze is unknown. Additional information is needed. \n\nError. Proceed with caution.

The One Who Knows instructed me to give you this. A condensate of planar potentialities—ah, you will not understand. It is ink.\n\nTake it to the Menos Cistern, a ruin near the city. Pour the ink into the water and your path will become clear.

The entrance to the underways is on the west side of the Necropolis. You'll find the cellar door in an alcove on your right.\n\nI'll post a notice about the closure and join you there. We can't let Peryite's cult rummage through the catacombs!
We must hurry and check the state of the pact. There is no telling what damage the Dreamcarvers could do to the Remnants and Hermaeus Mora if left alone in the Crux.
I remember. The cold waves dragging me down. And my father, dead! Gods, this is a lot to grapple with.

Glad you made it out of there! Vorm's been so excited since we collected all three books, he's practically shedding pages!\n\nHand me those books and we'll see if Vorm's actually got a plan or if he conned us into doing his bookkeeping.
The Sidereal Cloisters are a marvel, aren't they? I've been gazing at the stars since I was a little hatchling. I suppose you could say we're old friends.
Do please return the book. I'd very much like to get to the bottom of all this. Not that I haven't enjoyed our time together. A delightful reprieve to be sure.
We need to understand what could be waking the vessels. Tide-King willing, the archives will have what we need.
Master Shelreni has more to do with all this than she lets on, but I sense that our goal here is within the tower.\n\nLet us head to the old hall and see if we can access the tower from there.

Well, if Deredrien came here to help Reynila, it doesn't seem like she did a very good job. And no other sign of Reynila, or the one she was traveling with. \n\nWhat are those notes? What did you find out?

Wonderful! My master's treasure was mistakenly marked for unweaving, so we must hurry and find it before it's destroyed. My Watchling's Sight should help you navigate Underweave.\n\nThe entrance is close by. You can take the lead.
The invaders broke the seal and entered the Pool of Inquiry. As much as it pains me to say this, we must follow them, mortal.

I'm glad Tun-Shei is all right, but he's just given us more questions than answers.\n\nI know he's one of her most trusted assistants, but if this Delmon is one of Sathile's experiments, how does Tun-Shei not blame her for what happened here?
I can't return to Necrom while the entire peninsula is in danger. Besides, Leramil said my help was required for a desired outcome in this ripple of fate—whatever that means.

Underestimate Shelreni at your own peril. And do not think to just walk into a Telvanni stronghold reeking of Hermaeus Mora. Either Shelreni's Daedric allies or the conclave's own protections will spot you the moment you step across the threshold.
I'll carry on Reynila in my memories, always.
It seems Dreynis suspects my motives already. Why don't you speak with him? Sound him out, if you will?
Folsi's report didn't do this place justice. This isn't a camp. It's a House Dres foothold in House Telvanni territory.\n\nAny chance you found anything that will help us find the spy in there?
All the Voidprowlers are dead. Stuck in the Obscured Forum. And the secret's still lost. I'm a failure, mortal. I let Madam Whim down.\n\nShe's going to add more years to my debt, I mean.
Don't tell me you've found another creepy note like before.

Please—I didn't reveal anything to the Reformer about Sharp. I just ran!\n\nSharp never mentioned being a former Telvanni slave. On the souls of my ancestors, I didn't know! I'd never have put him on the job if I had, I swear!
With all the chaos recently, at least the bickering and backstabbing among my peers remains predictable.

I don't look forward to Tem asking for this favor repaid in kind. But … it's done. Swirling within my mind is the Runeform of Unmaking.\n\nLet's return to my sanctum. We shall grip the adversary's fateline and put an end to this.
She must've realized her experiment was spiraling out of control and tried to contain any damage. As I said, a professional to the end.
Careful! Careful. You wouldn't want to spill. \n\nPut that down by the rocks there.
I made my pact. I'll honor my deal.
I'll meet you at Tel Baro after I collect my ritual kit.
I don't think we should be in here. No one should. This place feels ancient. Sacred. But if you insist on pressing forward, I'll stay with you.\n\nReluctantly.
I need your help to align the last threads of fate or the portal shall not open.
My work is never done, but these tinctures won't make themselves, I suppose.

Shortly after you departed, both Leramil and Scruut fell ill. It has to be the corruption. It's growing stronger.\n\nCheck on Scruut while I see if there's anything I can do to ease Leramil's suffering.
Fate made us allies, but circumstances made us friends. You have done well, proxy.

So, now you've encountered the maligraphies. You handled them better than I did. I can see why you were rewarded with a Verse for your efforts.\n\nThe filers helped me locate another orb of maligraphies. You need to take this portal to get there.
The One Who Knows wishes to speak with you, proxy. Let us hope he anticipated the possibility of Torvesard using one of his allies' relics to activate this gate.
This portal shall take us to Beragon's townhouse. We should depart immediately, proxy.

Go on, I marked the locations on your map. I'll tell Gadayn, Beragon, and Tribune Alea exactly what you need to do to restore the relics. As soon as I figure that out.\n\nDon't worry, we've got this. I think.

That Dremora giving orders, they called her Shardmarshal Vargas. And those Wood Elves, they're part of that Recollection cult that's been spotted in the area.\n\nWe need more information, comrade. Let's press on.
Scruut said to hold the map close to those bolts of silk. That should restore—what did she call it?—the Skein of Secrets?
Be careful, friend. Daedra have a way of twisting words and disguising meanings. Hear what he has to say, but remain wary.
Just pick up the bucket and splash the victims with what's inside. No need to be delicate about it.

A fellow adventurer? The name's Beragon, friend. I could use a hand.\n\nI'm on the trail of a group known as the Recollection. I'm not sure what they're after in these ruins, but I intend to find out. I don't suppose you're after them, too?
The library door is to the left when you enter the manor. No one has touched the scene, on Aquilia's request.
A glittering secret? Certainly the fortune. Loyal paws? Must mean Betu. But still, clarity eludes this one. How can a dog hide a secret? There must be something this one is missing.
I sense Hermaeus Mora ahead of us, but also another, stronger presence. Since she absorbed the power of the Loom, Ithelia has become an engine of chaos and destruction. Proceed cautiously, proxy.
You'll have to forgive me. The presence of a Daedric Prince is not something I'm ever going to get used to. \n\nYou'd better see what Hermaeus Mora wants.
Finally, she speaks! I think the woman wants something from you. Go talk to her. Maybe she'll tell you what she wants and we can finally get her to leave.

A friend of Mizzik's is a friend of mine. After all, my aunt was quite fond of him and she was always an excellent judge of character. I won't mince words. I hope you and Mizzik find my aunt's killer. I'm certain this was no accident.

Ah, proxy, I bear grim news. The secret Hermaeus Mora guarded has escaped and Ithelia is forgotten no more. Strange disturbances and disorder now wrack these lands.\n\nWest Weald suffers, but by following these occurrences, we may just find her.
Let's find those weapon stockpiles and blast them straight to Oblivion!

I've got no talent for spells, but I picked up a bit of arcane lore in my time. The ancient Ayleids were fascinated with light. They devised ways to harness its magicka. Or draw it from aetherial crystals, like this burnt-out stone.
I'll meet you in Apocrypha, mortal. I much prefer my master's realm to any of the frail, insignificant locations in this pitiful plane of existence.
Scruut explained that we need to find a reality tear inside this cave. That's where you need to set Abolisher and use the spell scroll.\n\nI'm here to help in any way I can!

The Skein marks another use of the Staff of Many Paths at Fort Dirich. It's an old Imperial ruin, abandoned for centuries. With any luck, it will take Nantharion some time to plant his wildburn seeds. Maybe this time we can catch him in the act!
I'm pretty sure we didn't miss Nantharion on the way up. That means he must be above us in this tree-fort … assuming the Recollection hasn't taken him somewhere else already.\n\nOr simply killed him.
Go on. See if you can use Abolisher to open a portal. We need to get moving again!

That was exactly the wrong approach to take with Greenspeaker Darolith.\n\nI'll try to calm Tribune Alea down. You talk to the greenspeaker and see if she can tell us anything about the wildburn seed.
Necromancy is a scourge. It must be eradicated.
I believe that was the last relic you needed. You should meet back up with Leramil and Scruut at Beragon's townhouse.

The handwriting at the bottom of the note is definitely Sorilen's. Running into ruins alone is just like her.\n\nBut I didn't expect the Recollection to be here. She's heading into more danger than she realizes.

The portal deposited us in the demiplane of Fargrave. It is a realm without a Prince that serves as a crossroad through Oblivion. A thousand doors lead in and out of Fargrave. Or so it is said.\n\nBut the fate of Beragon and the tribune concerns me.
We'll meet you at the Wendir ruins, comrade. We'll follow you wherever Ithelia's trail takes us.
Let's be on our way now, assistant. The entrance to the catacombs of Wendir is nearby. Why are we dallying?
We are fortunate this prison was not made to hold mortals, proxy. If we can navigate this maze of broken mirrors, I think we may find an escape route.

So much of the path we just walked was familiar to me. The shrine, my scions. I remember it now. When Hermaeus Mora and the others arrived. Took my power. Locked me away.\n\nI had a plan as well, but I do not remember just surrendering like that.
You've come to the town of Ontus at an unfortunate time, traveler. I myself have only just returned. Coming home to bury one's father is never an easy thing.

That has to be their commander. Shardmarshal Vargas. Did you see how she opened a portal with that sword? Reinforcements emerged from some place she called Mirrormoor. That's how they got in down here.\n\nWe need to get that blade to stop the assault.
Thamech, traveler. That's an old way of saying hello. Welcome to the village of Vashabar.
Best of days to you, traveler. I hope you've come to Vashabar in good mood.
Welcome! We have an incredible variety of beers, wines, ales, and meads. Let's find something that suits your taste.

Oleander was kind. Maybe a bit too dashing for his own good, but you would've liked him. The greenhouses won't be the same without his laughter. His smolder.\n\nLook at me. Spoiling the mood. I'm not usually this serious. Promise!

Walker? And that strange Khajiit from Moonmont. Zerith-var, was it?\n\nIt is too dangerous for you to be here. These dro-m'Athra and the powerful ones leading them. I have never seen their like before. None of us have!

Loss after loss. Were it not for my Hidden Moon training, my heart would be Namiira's already for all the darkness these discoveries bring me.\n\nIt is only because of you and the appearance of Ja'kh here that I do not let grief overwhelm me.

As I said, Bogcup is more capable than they realize. The portal curio I provided should open a doorway from Sunhold to the Gardener's greenhouse in Malabal Tor. Sunhold's protections deter portals in, not out.\n\nGood luck. For Snapdragon's sake.

I'm not sure I appreciate being whisked through Oblivion portals without so much as a by your leave!\n\nStill, it appears our efforts were successful. Talk to Leramil, then you can fill the rest of us in on what exactly happened.
Excellent. The anomaly is in an old complex called Sunnamere beneath the Sunhold Mages Guild.\n\nGood luck. Hopefully the rest of us won't be far behind you.
This is just like what happened when I first found the portal.

It'll be hard to miss the Bitterfish's camp. It's just west of here. Look for the campfire. Or walk until you smell fish. Watching the Goblins and studying their mannerisms would be a lot easier if their camps didn't smell so strongly.
Ulfsild's secrets are all around us. You need only know where to look.\n\nRead the Fable of the Indrik, then use the lens and re-examine the tome. You'll see what I mean.
A pleasure to meet you! Apologies for all the subterfuge, but caution is advised in these trying times.\n\nSpeaking of which, the Garland Ring could use your assistance once again.

I sense the power of the Scholarium within you. Your ink-stained hands have touched the altar's magic. \n\nI sensed, too, when Ulfsild's essence faded from this realm. After all these years, do you hope to be her inheritor?

Nahlia's opened up quite a lot recently. I can't tell if it's because of the riddles, the work in the Scholarium at large, or because of you.\n\nWhatever the reason, I'm glad to see her in such high spirits. What can I do for you?
Oh no. You're going to ask me to help you with whatever that is your holding there, aren't you? It's not a riddle, is it?
Any luck finding what you need? Anything I can do to help?
I doubt we can get to the cellars through the sewer gate—it's locked from the other side. But we should be able to find an entrance somewhere near the ruins of the main house. Let's look around.
Please, find Naku and bring him to us quickly. Something about all this puts a fire of worry in my gut.
Feh. Of course Naku is working a mine. Probably the only cat in Tamriel who doesn't fuss over being sleek and clean.\n\nDon't tell him I said that.

That old guzzard has a true Craglorn soul, the look in its eyes says it all. I think we'll get along just fine.\n\nI asked Marcien to find two other creatures for me. I haven't seen them in a while, so I'd be happy to pay for your help again.
This is not a good time, stranger. If you have business with me, make it quick.

A friendly face is always a welcome sight, Keshargo only wishes he could enjoy it. \n\nThe Lucent Citadel was supposed to be empty, so Keshargo hired explorers, not warriors. But, we have just been attacked. So, he would like to hire you.

A slightly irritated face, the smell of gas about you … you're dealing with the Netch's idea of funny, aren't you? \n\nDon't worry, if you just keep nodding along with its vacuous ramblings, eventually it stops talking.
Let's follow the squirrels! I really do think this Netch wants to be found.

I'm supposed to test you. But tests are weighty, not good for floating. I prefer games. Easier to win and just as easy to prove how clever you are. \n\nListen to me, droning on like the Dragon! Anyway, I have some games for us to play.
It only took cross-referencing three tomes to figure out this echo might be about the Gryphon. Best find out what it has to say.
Be careful, friend of Zerith-var. You never know who may be listening.

Ugh, I'm such a screaming ninny when I panic. I suppose you saw that whole debacle? \n\nIt's embarrassing enough for me to witness my own base emotions, let alone anyone else. I've got to pull myself together. Literally.
The Gryphon has always been quick to the point. Righting wrongs and bringing you along to do it. Look at him go. \n\nStill shivering in his feathers and he's almost back to his old self!
Mortal. Greetings and defiance. My companion has clearly adopted you. But then he's always seen the best in people.\n\nWhy should I stay my claws?
These echoes must be from Ulfsild's final days here. They're so personal. And, unfortunately, none are quite as instructive as the ones she left in the Scholarium.

Viti brought me here. A good place to hide and dispel the darkness, yes?\n\nTalk to Zerith, walker. His training keeps his soul from bending, but his guilt is an open wound to the Void that Ravith-morna draws from. He must understand that to end her.
All right. The reeve's journal said that Snapdragon was going to spend the rest of her days in a musty cell on the west side of Sunhold. So that's where we'll start looking. Let's go!

We might have to do some searching once we get to Crimson Cove. I expect the Ceythalmor base will be well hidden. \n\nCrimson Cove isn't my favorite place in the world. But it's worth the trouble to save Hyacinth.
Hurry, friend. Add your connection to our own and open the portal. I don't know how long I can hold this!
I need a moment, tamiit. Please. Speak with Cantor Krin'ze.
We have seen the Twilight Cantors to safety. We must find Ravith-morna before she awakens this moon beast.\n\nTo the south, quickly!
Ravith-morna's plan is hideous, tamiit. We must make haste and find this shrine beneath Predator Mesa.
We are strangers, yes? And strangers shall we remain. May Azurah guide you on your journey.
We must meditate, walker. It is necessary for the ritual.
No more talking. Not right now. All I want to do is clear my head and find Mezamma.\n\nLet's head through the portal and get out of here.
The Fighters and Mages Guilds together again. Our combined strength will easily take down the Worm Cult.\n\nI'll see you on the northern coast after we gather some forces.

I sympathize with the Fighters Guild's desire for vengeance, but let's not ignore the bigger picture. We need a clearer understanding of the cult's goals. Their return serves a darker purpose, I'm sure. And we must learn more about the soul reapers.

Your strong reproach made me realize that the world doesn't stop just because someone we respected and cared about is no longer with us.\n\nWe know who the enemy is and where to find them. The time has come to take the battle to the Worm Cult.
I can't believe it. After all the years, I've spent courting her, just a handful of words and she casts me aside!\n\nHow could she be so heartless?

Heloise wants permission to check on the Hinault family. If you're going to help her, I guess I'll have to trust her judgment.\n\nJust keep an eye on her, please. She looks a little pale to me. I'm worried she may be working too hard.

Of all the travesties against nature, this is the most foul. This is the last one, the last spriggan.\n\nThere used to be hundreds in Jackdaw Cove, frolicking about in the grass and the water. They were beautiful.

If the Imperials take Bangkorai, it will be a fatal blow to the Covenant. We can't allow Renchant to do this.\n\nDamn it. He's leaving me no choice but to take back the throne. I know Glarikha will be pleased to hear that. Where is she, by the way?
I'll put up with sand. I'll put up with sun, but I will not tolerate beetles! I cannot work under these conditions.\n\nThe constant clicking of their shiny little mandibles drives me insane!
Satakal's Wrath, wayfarer … unless you will enjoy wading through an army of undead, I would go no further.\n\nThe dead have taken over Tu'whacca's Throne.
You've bested the warrior and the mage, but how are you with eight-legged beasties?
If you've come to buy water, I apologize for the sorry state of the johads. My idiot brother has all but ruined us.\n\nI suppose it'll fall to me to dig the family out of this sand-pit.
You'll find Dame Clarique up the road. She's the knight in charge of this Lion Guard unit. Since she's the one who had me tied up, you'll need to convince her to let me go.
I thought the gods had abandoned us, but I couldn't have been any more wrong! \n\nAkatosh, forgive my lack of faith!
Fine. Let's get this over with.

Once you've roughed up one of their scouts, knock him out with the <<z:1>> I gave you.\n\nWhatever you do, don't kill your target! We can't interrogate the dead. Well, maybe Sabie … uh, Lady Lancarl … could, but I can't. Anyway, the dead smell bad.
Her apprentice <<1>> is at the docks, tending my wounded soldiers.\n\nI'll stay here and say some final words for my friend.
He's exhausted! I really wish we'd never come to this place.
You've endangered the lives of everyone here. I hope you understand that.
You fight like the great hero Ysgramor, my friend.\n\nYou've done the Pact a great service this day.
Use the talisman. Release a soul from its misery.
Keep it short, stranger. I've got a skeever's nest of problems on my hands.
Make your decision, and decide well.\n\nOur plan ensures the safety of Davon's Watch. Will you throw that away?

Well met, my fine f'lah! I am Captain Llaari, commander of the forces stationed at Fort Arand.\n\nWe're primarily a training outpost. I've had to put the recruits on alert with all the Covenant troops nearby.
Who sent you? Holgunn? No, I'm sure it was Tanval.
Due to the theft of the <<z:1>>, the war chief and shaman asked me to step down. But as they dispute our future, it's my right to appoint an arbiter. So I appoint you.
Our village is not a place for casual visitors.\n\nYou should speak to <<1>> before you decide to stay.
A new warrior to join our ranks? I'm afraid you don't meet the physical requirements.\n\nIf you need to know more, speak to <<1>>.
I felt him die. I choked him and choked him and I felt him die. Why should I forgive him? Mercy is weakness.\n\nThe monster. Is it dead?
If you're looking for some charcoal, my apprentice will set you up. Stone and flame, friend. Stone and flame.
You can use the old forge north of us to craft the crown.
You may need help from <<1>> to reach the wispmother.\n\nI don't think <<1>> will want to help you, though.
Wait, stop! There's great danger!
We're here. Are you ready?
The Inner Sea Armature is a dangerous place. Tread carefully, Adept.
Fallowstone Hall has seen some hard times, but none worse than these days.
You've seen combat, and I need all the help I can get today.\n\nVillagers are scattered across the island. We need to warn them.
He left us! Why did he leave us? Let's go, let's go! Can't keep the Archmage waiting!
Thanks to you, the island is ours! Now you'll just need to claim the hall and kick Sheogorath back to the Shivering Isles.
Comrade. Good to see you again, even if it is under these circumstances. \n\nI still can't believe Sees-All-Colors would do this to us.
Let me know what you find. I don't trust these Stormfists. They were trouble a decade ago and I know that they're trouble today.\n\nI feel it in my bones.
Hrm. His clothes don't fit you very well at all. \n\nDon't draw too much attention to yourself. WIth luck, no one'll give you a second glance.
Be careful. The Daedra love to toy with prisoners.
Please, don't worry about me. You must rescue the Silvenar!
My ears still ring from the clout they gave me. Blasted Drublog took my weapons and Sariel's staff!\n\nWhere's the Silvenar? Is he safe?
You've questioned the witches and now it's time to free the spinners. Do you need to talk about their bonds some more?
It's unusual to stand here in the open, all visible and vulnerable and everything. I've spent my life lurking in the shadows. Staying out of sight.\n\nIt's kind of nice, actually.
You can find her in the hall in Elden Root, comrade. May the Eight protect you.
What a collection of Pact warriors! The time has come to end this!
Valaste will be expecting you at the Wayrest Guildhall. I'll see you there, Adept.
Head across the bridge and meet the lieutenant. I'll give these civilians a quick course in handling weapons and follow as fast as I can.
The Gold Coast may attack, but it will be without a heart.
It's not safe here. Get out of here if you want to see tomorrow.
Hmm? Oh! A living person. You should probably get clear, living person. It's not safe in this part of Auridon.
Ah, Raz's friend. The newest member of the Eyes of the Queen. You busy, rookie?
Good luck in there. And mind the Banekin. They're like little Daedric rats.
Do you wish to start the Trial of Spirit?
I'm distilling the antidote. All we need now is time.\n\nAnd with the bandits driven back, we can turn to the poison's source.
You've proven yourself bloodkith to our stronghold. If any here would call you outsider, you are welcome to answer with the back of your hand.\n\nNow. What is it you need?

In order to help my people, you're probably going to have to do some things you may not like.\n\nYou need to accomplish a deed of honor before they'll even let you near them. Otherwise, you'll be greeted by a hail of arrows.
Let's see if you can give a good account of yourself against a genuine champion.
Don't tell me. You're with the Dominion, aren't you?
We must defeat Korthor!
Let's start by chatting with the Bosmer and Khajiit. Get you introduced around. \n\nYou'll see what we're up against.
Well? Are you waiting for it to reach out and give you a cuddle?
Bright Moons light your path. You have chosen a particularly poor day to visit the Grimwatch.
I'll be watching Godrun closely. You should do the same.
Who's there? Tazia? Tell your busybody Clanmatron I'm not interested.
Khali has been champing at the bit. She has grown tired of these Dro-m'Athra, and hungers for bigger game.
Good to see you again, my friend … what's wrong? You have a strange look on your face.
Kalari wishes she had never told anyone of her troubles. Perhaps she should just sell the house and move away.
Shuzura will hear your problem, but you must wait your turn. Do you not see all these people before you?
Quickly, Hallowed. After her!

Bah! This Thalmor mage will drive Razum-dar mad! Stand here! Hold this! Everything so exact! \n\nThis one prefers more flexibility. He is glad another Eye is here who understands, because we must move quickly here if we are to protect the Dominion.
Gonlas lives in the house right by the front gate. You can't miss it! \n\nThank you so much, stranger. You're not like those … other strangers.
It is my hope that by watching these visions, we might learn more about what happened here … and how to return the undead to their rest as well … of course.
Can we try to keep it a little quieter? It's a wonder the whole castle doesn't know we're here!
The Elder Scroll of Alma Ruma is on my mind. Why is it not in Dominion hands?
The entrance to the vat chambers is at the top of the north pyramid. Destroy the vats and you shall pass the Trial of Body.\n\nNow go!
This isn't the easiest thing for me to say, but I appreciate the help you provided back at the Tower of Lies. I owe you one.
Please, I need your help. My master's life is in danger!
Not bad, if I do say so myself. He went down like a sack of eel jerky.

That part of the city is named for the large tower at the back of the district. Cariel will meet you there once you've found what we're looking for. Go quickly. We have much to do … and we still have the Mane to sort out.
I won't endanger generations of relative peace with the Maormer. Not for some faraway ruler who is freshly installed on her throne.
You must acquire the proper credentials if you want to compete. Speak to my staff if you're interested.
You approach the camp of the Ash'abah ….\n\nWait … I recognize you from Fahara'jad's palace. Hmmph! He would not listen to us, and now we all pay for his stubbornness!
Ah, you're just as Raz described you. I need your help.
While you were lollygagging, we secured the area.
You must not linger here, Moon Hallowed. Now that you know your place in the world, you must go to the temple at Rawl'kha. The Bright Moons await the beginning of your journey.
Ah, here it comes. The big moment. The bang finish. In real life, this is when the Veiled Heritance acquired its newest recruit.\n\nBut in real life, Aranias was alone. In this story, she's not.
I could really use a good soak. Let's go over to the pools and wash up.
Be careful. Your eyes will play tricks on you in this place and you'll need to pay attention to save Stibbons.
The Khajiit needs your help with the Colovians in Arenthia.
Hold on, this will just be a moment.
Hmm? Sorry, these guar aren't for sale. You're welcome to pet them, if you want.\n\nIf you don't mind, it's time for my nap. Wake me if they grow agitated.
Being a trader taught me how to get along with people, no matter what their form.\n\nI'll make a good magistrate myself someday, don't you think?
They can't have uncovered all this so quickly.\n\nWe should hurry. If <<1>> still stands, she'll let us through. She has to.
I didn't think it possible. Well done! We must return and begin the preparations.
Quickly, Hallowed. After her!
The challenge before the Pact is to capture the Elder Scroll of Alma Ruma. Help your comrades, warrior!

Honor and faith to you, my friend. We are nearly ready to depart. My Lord Varen requested that Tharn and Snow Lily join us, for safety's sake, though I have seen fewer places as tranquil as the Valley of Blades.
Word of our triumph preceded you. The glory of Covenant warriors delivering the Elder Scroll of Chim into our hands has inspired the entire army!
Sai, it's Lyris! \n\nHe looks terrible. We need to get out of here, fast! See if he can walk.
That vile daedra appears to be our host, The Duchess of Anguish. What say we settle our dispute, Tamriel style? Kill her!
We should find those scouts before anything happens to them.
We have one more shrine to consecrate. Onward!
One shrine left. Let's move! I don't know if Sai can take much more of this.

I'll take any help you can offer. <<1>> has a reputation for being incredibly thorough, whether on the battlefield or off. If the rumors are correct and <<2>> is truly here, she will find it.\n\nUnless we were to find it first.
Whoah! I can actually feel the forest again …. \n\nThis is good. The natural order is re-emerging already. It's still very weak though; it has to be nurtured back to health.
One more shrine to consecrate, yes? Can we please get to it?
I can feel the magic. There's a portal close by. We need to close it before we're overrun by more Montclair soldiers.
Adusa has always liked this old castle. It has personality.
This can't be right. Reachmen in the grotto. Why has Hircine allowed this to happen?
I do hope those horrid Goblins didn't mistake my notebook for something edible!
Please don't mind <<1>>. <<2>>'s betrayal is a shock to us all.\n\nBut no matter. <<3>> must work flawlessly for the queen. That's what we will ensure!
Good luck.
Ah, I take it Gwendis found you? And I assume that you dealt with Reezal-Jul?\n\nThen we are ready to begin. Let's find out why they tried so hard to hide this place from my memories.

Arlie's grandma was a powerful mage. When we were children, she used to show us things—marvelous things you could scarcely imagine.\n\nWhen she died, the Baroness locked up the Undercroft. She said it was too dangerous. Perhaps now we know why.

The sicker people get, the more incoherent they become. And now it looks like the rumors are true—the Llodos plague does turn people into monsters!\n\nI don't think we're ever going to find my brother.
The Maulborn have been dealt with, but I could use a little more of your help, if you don't mind.

The Iron Orcs have figured out a way to turn a trollop of trolls into an army. It involves training, armor, and magical runes carved right into their skin.\n\nI'll meet you in Ilthag's Undertower and we can deal with the troll trainer first.

My position is tenuous, but as long as I remain in charge of the Court I can continue to oppose the Serpent.\n\nI'll disguise myself and meet you at Fearfangs. Once inside, we need to find the scorpion matron and her nests.
What are you waiting for? Go put an axe in that Daedra-scum's head! Aim for the neck, and follow through with your shoulders. That's what I'd do.
You're here and still breathing. I assume the Oblivion Gate is shut?

I want to know if you can craft a maple bow. First, go harvest some rough maple. You'll refine it into sanded maple at a woodworking station.\n\nLast, you'll take the sanded maple and turn it into a maple bow.
How may I enlighten you this day?
We will rebuild Orsinium.
You avenged my son. I will not forget what you did for Shatul today. Nor will the clan.\n\nIf you are willing, I have need of someone so capable.
Isn't it remarkable? I love finding this kind of stuff!

Damn you, Kharsthun! How am I supposed to make a great discovery when—oh, hello! I was just thinking about you!\n\nYou do have a habit of showing up whenever I need help. Perchance you've brought a small army with you as well?

Who in the name of Malacath's third tusk are you? Don't you know this is sacred ground?\n\nBesides, it's also one of the most dangerous places in all of Wrothgar. You shouldn't be wandering around up here.
These statues should open the hidden door. It seems so obvious, but it isn't working for me.
You look for the hunters and I'll find Winks. Deal?

I've been looking through some of the Dragonguard's older texts. There are cryptic references to the Dragonfire Cathedral, but it will take time to find. \n\nAt least Molag Bal narrowed the search for us. That's why he'll lose in the end. He's sloppy.
Just throw water on the fire. Please don't make me try to run through it!
The chief is no more. Leave me to mourn my husband.
Thanks to your efforts, I have ingredients for everything but the main course.\n\nWe've come this far. If it's no trouble, I'd like you to procure what I need.
I've been watching your progress with interest for some time now. I have a challenge to offer that might test the abilities of … even someone who has foiled a Daedric Prince. \n\nInterested?
Remember to check the list. We have very specific needs here at the House of Orsimer Glories, distinctive portions of history that we want to put on display.
Ah, so you're the one who gave old Molag Bal a black eye. We've been following your career with great interest. A warrior of your quality was bound to turn up here eventually.
Good work on that last assignment. Things are quiet for now, but that never lasts. Come back and see me later. I might have something for you.
Never skinned a werewolf myself. Sounds like more trouble than it's worth. Unfortunately, that Menninia's sharp as a Morkul blade. I doubt we could fool her with old ragged wolf pelts.
The entries in this journal go back more than a decade. It will take some time to make sense of it all.\n\nDo not worry, Assassin. Whatever I learn from this tome, you'll be the first to know.
Well? Are you ready to get started, Initiate? Speak up. I don't have all day.

You made it. I wasn't certain you … well, I'm glad you're here. So, the details!\n\nWe're headed to a remote patch of land called <<1>>. It's owned by some thane from Eastmarch. He's at war, but his staff and guards remain.
I'll move carefully. If anyone spots me, they'll find themselves speaking with a befuddled servant.\n\nThat's not how you see me, is it?
I'll meet you at the hideout.
Ah, friend, am I glad to see you. It's Hildegard. She never came back after she went to say a prayer for Tanek.\n\nI think I could use your help.
I hate to see Kor so out of sorts, but he does dote upon our little Hilde. Go talk to him and see if you can help out the big Nord.
Kor brought Tanek home, injured but alive. He told me you went after the Grand Sermonizer.\n\nTell me, has the deed been done?
What else, Assassin. Tell me everything that occurred at the Order's enclave.

The Iron Orcs have figured out a way to turn a trollop of trolls into an army. It involves training, armor, and magical runes carved right into their skin.\n\nI'll meet you in Ilthag's Undertower and we can deal with the troll trainer first.

My position is tenuous, but as long as I remain in charge of the Court I can continue to oppose the Serpent.\n\nI'll disguise myself and meet you at Fearfangs. Once inside, we need to find the scorpion matron and her nests.
It's not really a good idea to keep Lord Vivec waiting.

Find Archcanon Tarvus in his office and do as he commands. Help the Archcanon and you help me.\n\nRemember the words of my Seventh Sonnet. "Time is neither ally nor enemy. It simply is. And then it has passed." Now go before it passes you.
I got your word that you'd delve the Cradle of Shadows. Don't tell me you're afraid of the dark.
My respect for you know no bounds. Now get over there so we can begin the ritual.
I will seek my own answers. When you have seen what I have seen, meet me at the Helan Ancestral Tomb.
