Ah, welcome to my home.\n\nIt's quaint, but sufficient. I can study in peace here and my practices don't disturb the people of Gnisis. Not that I'm working on anything capable of causing a fuss, mind you. Not after the mine incident.

Yes, yes, you figured out which offerings pleased the ancestors. Makes you feel all tingly inside, doesn't it?\n\nBut I still don't see an entrance to the hidden passages. Didn't the inscription mention something about a harp?

You activate the crystals. Look for pure light, not muddled. I'll modulate the energy fluctuations, make sure nothing explodes. If color confounds you, look at the shape. Fewest sides to most.\n\nBut the Great Gear turns, so be quick, be quick!

The tribes won't decide anything before the Wise Woman returns, but Chodala's followers could start causing trouble if she's gone too long.\n\nWhen you get to the Cavern of the Incarnate, tell her I sent you to talk to her.

Obviously, we need to recover this mysterious key. I don't know where it is, or what it does, but if Daedric Princes intend to mount an invasion over it, we can't afford to let it slip through our fingers.

According to your tabulator, that portal leads to the Shadow Cleft—a region in the Evergloam. How Nocturnal attached a portion of her realm to the Clockwork City defies my understanding.\n\nMaybe a more experienced apostle can make sense of this.

We arrived too late. As soon as the Shadow of Sotha Sil claimed the Skeleton Key, it slithered into the Fundament and sealed all the doors leading to the Cogitum Centralis.\n\nFyr and Varuni tried to break the seal. You can see how that turned out.
Welcome, friend! Come, join our celebration on this glorious and special day.

Aha! I knew that if I called out long enough someone would find me.\n\nQuickly now, come inside. Cultists have knocked the stars from our sky, and we have to put them back before all of Lord Seht's memories are taken for good!

While you ask questions around the city, Raz can take care of some other business. It may or may not involve scratching and clawing.\n\nLet's meet near the entrance to Shimmerene when you have something to report.
I sent you that message stone days ago. I thought you were never going to respond.\n\nHere. Let me set what I was working on aside. We have much to discuss, you and I.
I noticed you skulking around while I was engaged in some skulking of my own. I suppose we both came to the monastery with a similar purpose in mind.

Oriandra should be in Sotha Sil's chambers, cataloging his old research and experiments. Tell her I need the amplification elixir to strengthen our augury ritual.\n\nThat should help us determine what the pearl is and where it came from.

I know she doesn't seem the part, but Glardir's my best friend. She was with me when I opened the Illuminus, and now she's … well, frankly I don't know what she is.\n\nExecuting this plan is going to be harder than I thought.

Now that you've proven yourself a competent performer who can accomplish simple tasks it's time for you to take on a name. It may seem obvious, but I believe we shall go with Gryphon. Yes I rather like that. Well Gryphon it's time for your next task.

Greetings, my friend! Fancy meeting you all the way out here.\n\nSay, have you met with another High Elf around here? Heavy armor, sour disposition? I hired her as an escort for my expedition, and unfortunately I cannot start without her.
The good news is, we found Lotus. The bad news is, the Conservator is in an even more foul mood than usual. Be polite, please.
I last saw Cas in the dungeon. With any luck she's still there … and unharmed.
Two victims now. I can't let this happen again.

Most sincere salutations, newfound friend! I am Rigurt the Brash, ambassador-at-large for the exceedingly excellent Nord Cultural Exchange!\n\nI fear my mission to this beautiful island of snooty Elves has ended before it has even begun.
It's going to take a lot more convincing for Talomar, I can tell. I don't know that he'll ever forgive me for the mess I've made here, but maybe you can get him to hear me out?

So we meet again. Always nice—and rare—to see a friendly face.\n\nI'm afraid I don't have time to chat at the moment. I'm trying to seek entrance into this winery, but the guards refuse to let me in … despite my invitation.
He seems like he wants to talk, but this whole situation has me on edge. I'll hang back for now, if it's all the same to you.
All realities, huh? I can't even imagine. \n\nWell, go ahead. I'll be right behind you.
Welcome back, initiate. I see you have recovered all the staff fragments. Such a collection of artifacts … it is difficult to miss.
I have this under control. Please, keep moving.
Say, you speak mud-for-brains? I could use some help translating for this obviously under worked officer of the law.
Safe travels, initiate. We'll share our findings with you as soon as you return.
From what I hear, there's still more to do in Tamriel. You should speak with the Loremaster.
Safe travels, ceruval. Craglorn is an unforgiving place. Make sure you are prepared.

I'll send word to Jee-Lar and get him to meet you at the Sunless Hollow.\n\nIn the meantime, please be careful. Margus is dangerous, and what my sister has told me about the Blackguards would make your skin crawl!
We shouldn't be seen talking to each other. My egg-family's reputation is tarnished enough as it is.
The ruins are up ahead. I'll wait here and make sure the boat stays safe. There are all kinds of horrible creatures in the swamp and some of them eat boats. That's a fact!
Please let me know when you find something. I would help, but I'm afraid my eyes are not what they used to be.

That Xukas is always so polite. I don't know where I'd be without him.\n\nDespite the mishaps, we have the Kajin-Jat Crystal—thanks in no small part to your contributions. Cause for at least modest celebration, right?

Better you than me.\n\nIf you want to get a better idea what you're walking into, there's a local by the name of Solni who's got more than a passing interest in Sithis. She's here in Lilmoth if you decide to speak with her.
We should not linger here, beeko. This city hisses with dark intentions, old as the stones. We should look for signs of Kassandra's passage, then leave. Quickly.
I know I spoke of fighting as one, but these two were too loud and foolish. Tsojei and I had to kill them.\n\nBefore they died, they spoke of the Remnant, and the Hist wood grave-stakes.
What happened here? That dead man is one of the Veeskhleel, the Ghost People tribe! Are they responsible for our troubles?
Welcome to Nesh-Deeka's Shop of Musical Wonders! Please, have a look around. But touch nothing. Some of these instruments are very old.

They're not coming with us, are they? Goodness.\n\nJust when you think you know everything there is to know about the Bright-Throats and the Dead-Water, they throw you for another loop! These Murkmire Argonians are remarkable people.
I'm sorry. Did you need something?
I've got the corpse covered, swamp slug. Why don't you do what the nice lady says and look for clues about the Remnant.

The Blackguards lurk here, true—but so do dangerous beasts and vicious plants.\n\nNo matter! Bare your fangs and know that you will crush these foes. Tsojei calls for blood, and we will see that it drinks its fill.

It seems Kassandra is as impressed with you as I am. Please, consider her offer.\n\nIf this Remnant of Argon is as important as Xukas says, we cannot allow the Blackguards to get their hands on it. You can help us. You can help all of Murkmire!
I've watched over the Xinchei-Konu for several years now. I find its power endlessly fascinating. To my knowledge, there's no other monument like it in all of Murkmire.

I heard my lady ask you to recover her favorite hand-mirror. I'll have you know I only dropped it because that wild beast frightened the hair right off my head! It's a monster!\n\nBe ever so careful or it will tear you to ribbons.

Sun light your path, beeko. And keep a sharp eye for snakes—not just the ones without legs.\n\nToo many eyes look for the Remnant. They would know what you know. At the edge of a knife if that is what it takes.
Searching for body parts. Gruesome work. The Euraxians are scavengers, five-claw. No, worse than scavengers!
Try not to let the carnivorous plants consume you. Getting eaten by mostly stationary creatures doesn't help one's reputation. Or so I've heard.

The guides from the Stitches. We must be close. Saulinia had them killed because she no longer needed them and she wanted to keep whatever secrets they learned along the way.\n\nThe hidden Akaviri shrine must be nearby. Hurry, but be cautious.

You have come to Cicatrice in a time of great danger, traveler-friend. \n\nToxic fumes permeate the air and corpses walk among the ruins. It is best to turn away now, before you share the fate of my dear companions.
Vazbi smells more blood on the wind. We must keep looking, yes?
Well, look at that. If it isn't Naryu's little hero. Who'd have thought we'd meet again, in Elsweyr of all places.\n\nHmm. You wouldn't happen to be traveling to the town of Hakoshae, would you?
The Sleeping Badger. Eh. To Mizzik, it always looked more like a stretching rabbit.
This is the right place. I can sense it. But nothing in this chamber looks like it can make the Moons move or open a path to Jone or Jode.\n\nWhat are we missing, five-claw?
You have any questions for Tasnasi? Otherwise, we go.

Thanks for your help back there. Jubani and her thugs are a bunch of hammers who think everything is a nail. Geniuses included.\n\nAltruism isn't a thing in the Stitches. So what do you want? Need a lock picked? Something repaired?
Moons—you're not hurt, are you? All your limbs in place?
"To know the road you walk is a joy," was recorded as the last words of Ophine Dentreaux.\n\nOur road is now known to us. It will be a joy to walk it.
That's close enough, walker. The Weeping Scar is no place for you to feed. My former clan are preying on anyone who passes through the canyon and I cannot protect you.
The war council has met and plans are in motion. Abnur Tharn will catch you up on the situation and tell you where you are needed.

So, these Hidden Moon adepts used necromancy to guide and redeem lost Khajiiti souls. Seems their good intentions had unintended consequences.\n\nNow that we know the Hidden Moon adepts' story, maybe Mazza-Mirri will agree to help us.
Trespasser or pilgrim? Hmph. Both, I think. But you walk this path aimlessly, child.\n\nI am Mazza-Mirri, Clan Mother of the Hidden Moon. Why are you here, I wonder?
Raz knew something was sour in sweet Merryvale. \n\nWell, at least we know what happened to the missing farmhands. But why does a daedroth care about moon-sugar?

Ah, Vestige, how good of you to attend me. As I was saying to Lord Gharesh-ri and Khamira, competent help remains at a premium in this remote province. Which is why I sent for you. We must once more join forces to save Elsweyr from a rage of Dragons.

Welcome to the House of Histories. You'll find no grander collection of curiosities and memorabilia in all of Elsweyr.\n\nI would offer you a tour, but we're currently investigating a most unfortunate theft.
You have agreed to help us? Thank Jone and Jode.\n\nPatrons have been few and far between of late. We need that mural if the House of Histories is to keep its doors open.
Hey, you're back! I was just wrapping up my business with these fine Khajiit.\n\nDid you find the note? Where's Tu'heiba?

Thank you, friend! Retrieve Rigurt's package from Thadarra in Riverhold Marketplace, and meet me after in the Stitches. Rigurt's diplomacy waits for no man! Or woman! Or cat!\n\nBut be careful. Sweaty threats fill Elsweyr's deserts.

It's really you, isn't it? I haven't seen you since we had that wonderfully psychotic time in Southpoint!\n\nDon't worry about these levelheaded losers. No one can see me but you. You possess a special untapped talent for unhinged insanity!
As I said, I did some research. Approach each aeonstone and I'll siphon a little of your vitality into them. That should provide the energy I need to activate the portal to Dragonhold.
Let us hope we can find the Horn of Ja'darri within the halls of this sanctuary.

I appreciate you dealing with Nahfahlaar. The Dragon senses my unease over Tharn's letter, which only makes his own anxiety more pronounced.\n\nMeanwhile, I need to keep myself from thrashing the old battlemage the moment I see him.
Be careful on your journey, warrior. And may Leki guide your path.
As the daughter of General Renmus, it's a little difficult for me to keep a low profile in a place like the Black Kiergo. You should go with Caska.\n\nZa'ji and I will head back to the sanctum.
Talk to Queen Khamira. You're no Abnur Tharn, but you were with her when she gained her powers. Maybe you can help her come to grips with her portal magic.
We'll attempt to draw the slavers away from the ship, but it's likely some will stay by the docks. Prepare yourself for a fight.
We won't be far behind you, walker. Please hurry to the Wall of Life and cleanse the path. Adara'hai does not wish to bring Vijari there until Khenarthi's bells have drowned out the Heart of Lorkhaj.
Laatvulon is sacrificing my people to empower himself, by Jode and Jone!\n\nHow many must die for this New Moon? Desperate and deceived, giving their lives so the Dragons can destroy us all.
Tell me, my friend. What did you find behind the hidden door? Do we have a way to reach Dragonhold?
This one had hoped to fly upon the back of the great Dragon all the way to the floating island. Now? If Za'ji must walk, he will be one unhappy pirate.

We lost the old wizard and the relatively friendly Dragon? Now we have to rely on just … us? I don't like our chances.\n\nThat said, I do want to set paw on that floating island. I can't wait to see what Pellitine looks like from up above.
A floating island? What keeps it from falling out of the sky?
The Halls of the Highmane. Sounds rather ominous doesn't it? I don't think this will be a simple jaunt through some ruins.\n\nLet's just hope Ra'khajin doesn't find the mask first.

Ah, that's better. Swore off fighting shirtless years ago. Almost losing a nipple … it gives you some perspective, you know? Story for another time.\n\nLet's have a look around, eh? Hopefully we can get a sense of where those kidnappers took my pals.

Zha'al. You are the one who got us back the Perfect Pounce, yes?\n\nThank you for that. She may not be much, but the Pounce has been this one's home for a long time. Even before Za'ji was her captain, in fact.
If you have anything to say to our companions, I suggest you do so now. The battle ahead will be long and arduous, and we may not all survive.

Is that really you? My friend from Wrothgar? It is you! Something has finally gone right in this hot and sandy land.\n\nI lost my uncle's goods, my guard … I even lost my cat! Mother was right. I never should have come here.
These … criminals! How dare these pirates desecrate this holy place!\n\nUnfortunately, we have a bigger concern than a gang of pirates. Let's find that waterfall and the hidden door.
So? Find anything that will help us locate the Icereach Coven?
The witch's attack left me nearly senseless, but I recall that I was dragged this way.\n\nYou take the lead and I'll help you the best I can.

My father's never been what I'd call a warm and caring parent, but this crisis has made him even more distant. \n\nLet's get the sacred oil to Fenn. My father will certainly change his attitude once we present the protective elixir to him.

Oh good, you're back. Mjolen and I have been discussing the various ways to turn what we've got into a protective elixir.\n\nI'm hesitant to get too excited, but I think we've figured out how to defend against the harrowstorms.
Go ahead. Get what Fenn needs from the Hall of the Dead. I'll make sure Maugh follows through on procuring the rest of the supplies. He can be easily distracted, in case you haven't noticed.
Give me a moment. Speak to Magister Fridelja, if you would.
Gods … these frozen corpses, they were people once. What are they now?\n\nWe need to be careful.
They must have taken the people they lured to the inn down here. Let's look around but be ready for anything.
Edjar said he'd show us how to get into Tzinghalis's lair. Let's get after him.
You want to talk now? I'd much rather you get in there and help defend Fenn. If he doesn't get that door opened, Solitude is doomed!

I … I'm not sure we can destroy this tower. We need to keep going. Find a way to disrupt the ritual. But I think I understand what they're doing.\n\nTzinghalis found a way to release the Gray Host from Coldharbour by using the harrowstorms.
Come on. Svana's plan is sound. While they attack one front, we attack the other. With any luck, one of us will figure out how to stop this coming storm.

Vampires have overrun the temple. How is this possible? Our master hates the undead!\n\nWe need to search the temple. Make sure the temple priest and her acolytes are safe. Then we must find the high priest and pray she can help us end this nightmare.
Search the crates. I want to know what Brondold got himself killed over.
How long has the Reach burrowed underneath Karthwatch and we never knew? \n\nWe have to find out where these caves lead. Keep an eye out for any sign of the captives.
As you fill the museum, bards from all over will make their way to Solitude.\n\nKeep working on the clues in Nel's poem. Once we have all the instruments collected, the performance can begin!
So, you mean to aid us with this Draugrkin business? Thank goodness. Shelaria seems like a competent warrior, but her injuries are pretty severe.
Try the whistle, but ready yourself. We still don't know what we're dealing with here.

I could use your help to examine the strange pikes erected around the temple. Harrowfiends and vampires roam the area, making it difficult to get close, hence the need for your assistance. You see, I'm not that confident in my combat prowess.
Ena uses this camp to conduct business she prefers not to deal with in town. Whoever was here last certainly left in a hurry. Not exactly encouraging. \n\nDid you find anything?

Svana's taking this pretty hard. I suppose most daughters feel close to their mothers. Not that I'd know. I never knew my mother. Sorry. Don't mind me.\n\nDid you find anything that might lead us to the assassin?
I don't think the assassin will risk returning. Search around and see what you can learn.\n\nI'll be up and around in a moment, after I drink from my flask.

For all his protestations, Svargrim still modeled Solitude after the decadence of the east.\n\nA jarl should live in a longhouse, just as our fathers before us. Still, anyone who can solve our problems can drape their palace in lace for all I care.

The clan survives. Barely. We couldn't have done it without your help. I don't say this often … but, thank you.\n\nNow, tell me. Did you find anything while you were down there? Anything that might explain how this all happened?

Thank you, outsider! You've saved this clan from ruin and my wife from unimaginable pain. I don't know how you convinced the chief to have mercy, but I don't care! This is great news.\n\nMaybe I misjudged Urzikh. We'll see.
Come, let us search for my grandfather. He has to be here somewhere. \n\nAnd don't worry about me, I can protect myself.

Yes! Rigurt swears, no fish in Tamriel can resist such a mushroom! If only it grew more frequently, it would be used by people everywhere, my friend.\n\nNow, lead the way. Rigurt will follow. He will use his keen nose to find the prize we seek!
Ah, company. You're a long way from safety out here. Get close to the fire and tell Old Mjolen a tale.
You're trespassing. Which is good, so am I. The question is: are we snooping around for the same reason?

If Talfyg here doesn't stop complaining, I'll toss him into one of these graves.\n\nHere I am trying to discover if an ancient vampire threatens all of Tamriel, and I need to rely on this insufferable toad.
Blooms for grieving widows? Dragon's Tongue for ancient throats? Nonsense, the lot of it!
Well, I've made it this far with no catastrophes. That has to count for something, right?\n\nIs the area safe? I'm so nervous.
Let's both keep an eye out for more of those sigils. I'll call out the ones I see and the direction.
Let's approach these pockets of energy and void portals with caution, my friend. We still don't know exactly what they're capable of.

Bradan must have gotten here ahead of us. I'd recognize his handiwork anywhere.\n\nIt seems that the redoubt is overrun with Gray Host troops. We'll need to get past them to reach the old ritual site.

The others see conspiracies where there are none. Just past sins that I thought long buried.\n\nThey say you found everything that Rada wanted me to discover. Tell me about the sundered land, the Nighthollow's studies, and the secret of the keystones.
I don't like it. It reminds me of a chunk of meat in a skeever trap.\n\nGo ahead. You see if that's the right book. I'll keep watch.

Rada al-Saran and the Gray Host were here. Damn it, we almost caught him! \n\nSeems they were only interested in this strange stone. Like a piece of Oblivion caught in our world when the land was sundered. Break off a piece and we can get out of here.

As I surmised, this chamber was where new keystones were crafted and stored. Nothing remains, however, except component pieces. Does Rada al-Saran expect Verandis to assemble a keystone?\n\nGather the pieces and we'll bring them to the orrery.
This room is better preserved than most of the others I've explored. It was apparently the suite of someone important.	\n\nLook around. Something here must hold a strong memory.

This place must have been impressive back in the day, but now it's just decrepit. Looks like it's been abandoned for centuries. Luckily, I came prepared. \n\nHow do you feel about trying something unconventional?
Karthwasten is rightfully ours. The land ached for our return.

Come, outsider, let me feel your spirit ….\n\nI sense no deception. I think you may be able to help us. Since my apprentice trusts you, I will as well. The Crow-Eye clan needs aid. There are evils in this land that we cannot defeat on our own.
Quickly, five-claw. Let us search this Deep Tombs prison and locate Kathad.\n\nAnd Freyleth, too, I suppose.

Remember, remain respectful but wary when dealing with Reachfolk. They don't suffer long speeches—or even short ones. Keep your conversation with the sentry brief and to the point.\n\nOnce you find something, meet me in Markarth at Understone Keep.
So Shaman Ulvoch agreed to let you help me? Good, good.\n\nI'll meet you outside the village and then we can gather the offerings for the wards.
Sky tales … the Witch is one of the guardians that protects the lesser stars ….
They warned me some competition might try to get in my way. And then you saunter up just as I find the place. A mite suspicious if you ask me.\n\nWhy did you come here? Who sent you?
These terrors that came to our village … I never experienced anything like this. I just want to craft my tools, not fight beasts!
You must be Lyris's partner. She told me about your adventures up in Solitude and I am happy to have your support.\n\nI see you opened the coffer. Did you happen to find a letter?
If I can speak honestly, I wish the sisters would come in for a chat more often. Eternity can get lonely, and the spirits here grow tired of my stories.
The spirits have abandoned Karthwasten, outsider. Fialyn should never have dragged you into our affairs.
It's good to see the vateshran safe and sound. Now, let's ask him about the feud and how it began.
We finally have an idea about how to end the feud without forcing either Madearn or me to get married. We can't stop now.\n\nHelp us figure out where the vateshran has gotten to.

Hircine's hind, I appreciate the help, wanderer! I'm in your debt.\n\nAre you in the habit of wandering into dangerous ruins and delivering old storytellers to safety, or was there something you needed of me?
Just so we're clear, I need you to talk to the priest. She's become rather cross with me and refuses to tell me anything of substance. Let's see if you have better luck with her than I did.

You play the army you're dealt, right? Or march with the army you have? I'm terrible at metaphors!\n\nA solid fort at our backs, brave soldiers at our side … now we just need to wait for Vandacia and his cultists to show up.
I'm glad you're here! I've been searching all over, but I could use your help. This place is huge! Why do rich people need so many rooms?\n\nOh, but tell me. Did you warn the councilors like I asked?
The Golden Anvil was hidden away by the bazaar's arbitrator, Gavos Douar. We should search the abbey and learn all we can from Gavos's fall. It may lead us to the anvil's ultimate resting place.

The cache has to be somewhere inside. Clear a path through the soldiers and cultists and I'll join you after I get these Wood Elves to safety.\n\nJust between us, they aren't cut out for the adventuring life. But a seed's got to sprout, am I right?

Cultists? That explains some of the decoration in here.\n\nSo much for the smuggler hypothesis. I didn't expect to have to fight through a nest of cultists to extract Quistley from this mess, but so be it. What's he gotten himself mixed up in now?

You again? I can't tell if you're a jinx or a good luck charm. What in the name of Sithis are you doing down here?\n\nLet me guess. Commander Axius sent you after us because we're missing and presumed dead. Correct?

Our powers interact strangely with the natural forces of the Deadlands. That's why we need to be attuned. Of course, I underwent the process years ago. Now we must help the twins do the same.\n\nKeep them safe. Then meet me on the road south of Gideon.
Slivers of the Deadlands? Attunement? This is way beyond what we were taught in our sanctum!
Let's find these objects from the Deadlands as Sombren's mentor suggested. If it helps keep me and my sister alive, we've got to try it, no matter the risk.

I've proven beyond shadow of a doubt that I can't be trusted with that thing.\n\nFor anyone who is not me, using the censer is quite simple. Activate it and a mote of spectral energy should coast toward Tiras. Just follow the mote!
I would have sworn the map I saw showed a passage here. Unless … could it be a hidden passage?\n\nI'll look around a bit. Why don't you see if the vampire knows anything?
This is easily the most important experiment in Revus's unremarkable career, and he's soliciting aide from random passersby? Of course he is.\n\nIt would be depressing if it wasn't so predictable.

Can you believe it! Another warded door! Emperor Leovic was certainly determined to keep people out. Or I suppose these precautions could be to keep something in?\n\nWell, we won't find out by just standing here. See if you can disrupt the ward.
Are all adventures like this? All tragedy and death? Give me a warm hearth any day.
Sorry, sorry. I feel like we've assembled most of the clues to this mystery, but I just can't shake the feeling that we're missing something here.
Much as I love a happy ending, we haven't quite reached the conclusion just yet. You should speak to Annyce's mother about the imposter. We mustn't let Cres escape.
This definitely has a sense of Daedric cultist about it.\n\nLet's look around and see if we can find their high priest. I really do want to loosen his tongue … before I slice it off.
Come on, the ones who did that to Ghalor must be nearby. We should destroy their ritual site, if nothing else.
Did the scary Daedra lady say I was cute?\n\nWell, if she has something to say, I think you better talk to her.
Even a spark of Aetherial energy should be enough to open the way for us. Reach out to the skyshard and let's hope it responds.
These skeletons must belong to the missing novitiates. Gods, this is horrible.
I have so many questions for Inalieth—about my mother, my sister, the friends and servants and more distant relations who knew my family before my father's disgrace. I hardly know where to start.
That dragonfly right there should do the trick. Quickly, capture it!
I certainly hope we're done fetching fowl today. Give the chicken to Takaano and let's see what he knows about Onimiril.
You're going to be our new escort? After seeing what happened to our retinue? You must have a confidence I don't share. We should head back. Get reinforcements. An actual attack force.
Go ahead. Put the relic on the table. I want to examine it. Maybe if I touch it, or concentrate on it, something will happen.\n\nMy memories have to start making sense to me at some point, right?

That voice we heard came from in here. We need to catch up to the Ravener. Destroy it for good.\n\nI don't care what gets in our way, you handle it. I refuse to let anything stop me. The Kalmur will get their justice.

I think we can open the furnace door by using lucents. I want to see what's inside. See if that voice really belongs to Emperor Moricar. It certainly sounded like the voice from my memory.\n\nLet's find some lucents and figure out how this works.
I don't know what went wrong. I started praying to Mehrunes Dagon and then—the Tribunal, you, my family. I've brought shame to everyone!\n\nWe only have two stones now. We need three.
I still have no clue as to how I knew what to do back at Fort Grief. You don't know how disconcerting that is. How … scary.\n\nYou better talk to Lyranth now, my friend.

Are you ready to resume our hunt for the Riven Cataclyst, little mortal? I assumed you'd want time to sample Madam Whim's delights or explore the splendors of Fargrave.\n\nNo? Very well. Let us go before more Incarnates are unleashed upon the city.

You are unlikely to find any of Mehrunes Dagon's servants in Wretched Spire, master. Long ago the Prince of Destruction commanded that no Daedra among his legions should look upon that place. Or even speak of it.\n\nHe was … quite insistent.

I do not like this talk of Dremora being used to power some sort of mortal machine. The servants of Dagon have much to answer for.\n\nZynoahz's gaol awaits, mortal. You will find it to the west, near Burning Gyre Keep.
Good start. First results are curious. But promising.\n\nThere's more to learn from the shell. Continue with the ritual. Follow Miksotet's instructions. Easy enough.

Imperial structures in the Deadlands! This has to be the Longhouse Emperor's retreat. Let's look around and see what we can find.\n\nI don't think Emperor Moricar had any reason to lie to you. Do you? There must be something here to help us.

Spend any amount of time scavenging in Fargrave or various realms of Oblivion and you'll run into a few of these Daedric devices. Lucents are usually easy to find. The tricky part is locating a dynamus font that still works.
If Elegian devised both the cataclysts and my mask, did I know him before my memories disappeared? And did I know about the cataclysts?\n\nIt seems I wound up with more questions than answers.

Soon, little mortal, soon. I shall have the answers I seek and you shall save Fargrave and the mortal realm.\n\nUnless, of course, Nokvroz turns out to be more powerful than I anticipated. Then we are lost.
Let us be on our way. Whatever awaits us at the summit, we should make haste.
I thought Sombren was our friend. I can't believe he would do something like this. How could he turn to Mehrunes Dagon? How could he betray us?\n\nI'm so mad I can barely see straight!

Remember, find a lucent, charge it in the dynamus font, then place the charged crystal in the labrum beside the door.\n\nOnce you understand how lucents function, you can use them to accomplish all sorts of things throughout the realms of Oblivion.
Let us hope the Warden does not return any time soon.
Thank the Eight, I thought I'd be trapped down here for all eternity. Did the Spire send you?
Go on, then. Let's search the vault.
This entire area is teeming with unwholesome energies, but there's something here that feels out of place with the rest. That must be what we're looking for.
Let's take a look around—carefully. Guild General Quentyn is here somewhere. And we might be able to find out more about what the Ascendant Order is really after on High Isle.

Oh, hello! Good to see you again, my friend!\n\nI'm here to represent the Mages Guild at Lord Bacaro's conference. I wonder if I'll have time to find a druid before Lady Arabelle needs me. I'm quite interested in their approach to magic.
Your efforts will not be forgotten. Zenithar remembers all who work and serve him. \n\nMay his good fortune be bestowed upon you throughout your lifetime, friend.
Do you mind talking to him? He's a rather irritating man.

I am going to have one more go at convincing my mother … excuse me, the knight commander … to see reason.\n\nMaking a promise like that for me, what was she thinking? Have you seen the other aspirants?

Fresh off the boat, eh? High Isle is a good place for an adventurer to earn some gold—provided you have the right connections.\n\nThe name's Jakarn. My patron needs someone like you. An unknown, so to speak. It'd be worth your time to befriend her.
One lost article doesn't seem like much, but it means she was here at some point. We're on the right trail. Let's keep looking out here.
My apologies for not remembering the exact location of the key. I'm certain it is in this room, though.

Nothing packed, food left on the table, and signs of a recent scuffle. I think it's safe to say Dockmaster Arnauld found that his Ascendant Order friends weren't entirely satisfied with their arrangement.\n\nThey've obviously spirited him away.
I do not like where this is leading, my friend. Come. We should be able to find the archdruid in the northern part of the grove.
Let's find that mill, which I believe lies southeast of the tower.\n\nWe'll need the waters around the spire flowing again if we're going to finish the weapon.

I finished the traps. Once we set them up, they should take care of the motes. Then I can sort out the livestock and Huldressa … and at some point create a counterspell to fix everything for good.\n\nDid you learn anything useful?

Gather the claw, a feather, and the bones, and I'll make sure the rescue ship can reach the shore safely.\n\nWhile you're gone, I want to take a look at Caska's wounds. She won't admit it, but I can see that she's hurt pretty badly.

I suppose it's time to reunite with Queen Ayrenn. Let's be off. \n\nMaybe this news about Prince Irnskar will keep us from wandering into more sensitive waters. She really does like to argue, that one.
There's an entrance to the Navire Dungeons in the cemetery east of Castle Navire.\n\nLet's hurry, my dear. If the Ascendant Order is planning something spectacular, I'd just as soon spoil their fun.

Don't tell Lady A, but this is actually one of the better schemes I've been involved in. We've got a good chance to corner the Ascendant Magus. Assuming we don't get recognized. And killed.\n\nNow stick close and follow me.
Who are you and what are you doing in my camp? Get out! Out!
I'm not losing this fool again. I'll stay here with Oblan and try to convince the Breton to let him down while you gather his things.

I am sure the guard will be happy to help us sort everything out. \n\nBut it might be best if you talked to him. I don't know how moon-sugar got into the dessert I ordered for my friend <<1>>. I only paid the bill!
Ah, my trusty adventurer friend! I felt rather foolish the moment I ran in here without you.
One more key and the Daybreak Gem will be ours! We're so close.

Keep your guard up, I don't like this. Maybe it's just being in an enclosed space or following a random man we don't know, but this seems like a good time for a trap.\n\nI also might be paranoid. Let's just talk to Azamel.
Get him out of that cell, my friend! I'll stand watch.
I've heard good things about you, traveler. I'm glad Isobel has someone she trusts by her side. \n\nHopefully you can find the signet ring before the thief flees Stros M'Kai.

Off with you. Take Stibbons and investigate the lighthouse. I'll be along in a moment. I need to compose myself.\n\nIt's clear that this randy sea captain has strong feelings for the ghost that's inside you. Maybe we can use that. Let me ponder ….

Oh dear, this is beginning to sound like some lurid romance novel. Not that I would know anything about such things. Or that Lady Laurent would.\n\nUm, perhaps we should investigate Monument Inn and see if we can learn anything there.
Careful, walker. All that swimming and fighting has made me hungry. \n\nAnd you look pretty tasty, I must say.

This is just the beginning! There are more decks to acquire and more—slightly less handsome—players to defeat!\n\nNow, I know our lesson went quickly. So, if you're confused on any details, check out the handbook there on the bar!

You return victorious, yes? Ha! I hope you enjoyed the match. I have played countless games of both luck and skill, and truly, Tales of Tribute is the best by far.\n\nSo, now that you have learned the rules, do you wish to continue your gaming journey?

Not bad for your first game. Not bad! Better than my first, that's for sure. I did see you hesitate once or twice. If you need a refresher on the rules, you can always check the rulebook downstairs at the bar.\n\nNow, I think it's time you met Kishka.

Welcome back, my friend! I hear you skinned that cat, Raenobi. A fitting end to her unscrupulous strategies!\n\nI applaud your victory, but in truth, you achieved something far greater than advancing in a tournament.

Hey! You taking a pre-match stroll? I've always loved sitting up here … watching people hustle this way and that. Everyone with their own stories. Their own little adventures.\n\nWe've had our own share of adventures, haven't we?
I must finish my prayers, traveler. My spirit must be pure before I meet my foes in battle.\n\nMy blade has thinned their ranks. But I am only one soul standing against the darkness.
Don't waste time talking to me! We need to help the wyress! I won't let the Firesong hurt another innocent!
That bastard! Let's get down there and give him a real fight!
The Draoife awaits. Come, friend. Let's see what the Firesong Circle has to say for itself.
I see our call for assistance did not go unanswered. Good. House Mornard rewards those who serve us well. Now, speak to my son Stefan. He can tell you where you're needed most.
I told Sir Stefan about Windwrack Fort, but he wants to hear your report. You'd better get to it before the poor lad bursts.

Blight take it! I came to help the Eldertide Druids defend their village, but I was too late. This battle is already lost.\n\nYou're not an islander, and you're certainly not a Sea Elf. What are you doing here, stranger?

Politics! If there's one thing I hate more than those Ascendant Order bastards, it's politics.\n\nHopefully, between you and Lady Arabelle, we can finish this business. Then Za'ji and I can finally turn our full attention to restoring the Pounce.

Lady Arabelle wasn't improving, so Za'ji went to find Druid Ryvana. Do not worry, five-claw. Caska stands guard at Mandrake Manor!\n\nInstead of giving this one more medicine, Ryvana sent me to find you.

Tell Lady Arabelle what we learned. And remind her to give the antidote the time it needs to work. I'm sure she's going to want to be in the thick of things as soon as possible, but her body must recover from the affects of the poison.
Let's find the alchemist's garden and finish with this dreadful place.
Captain Siravaen was as good as her word and got us to Y'ffelon, but we must assume we lost the element of surprise.
A good fight, eh? Now get to the rail and keep watch. These Firesong might have called for help before they grappled us. There could be more enemy ships on the way.
The song I feel in these old stones. It comes from somewhere ahead. We should keep going. Explore. Listen. Learn.
You should talk to Druid Fenas. He's the expert here. I think? Expert in … translations! He's helping us! Yes, you should definitely talk to him.

My ideas rarely work out for the best, but I can tell that getting you involved was one of my better ones. \n\nThat's a fire shard out there, just what Druid Fenas wants. But you'll need to get it unless you want me to go up like kindling.

So much death and destruction over a few ancient words carved into stone. I longed to learn the truth of the last Druid King, but now ….\n\nThanks for all your help, friend. I just wonder if the druid circles can recover from these events.

I watched several sea witches come and go through this door. My gut tells me that's the right spot. High above all the other Dreadsails, just like Veshin said.\n\nYou still have the key, right? Otherwise we're in trouble.
Another muse-mouth plant. It has a story to show us as well, outsider. Examine it again while I stand ready to assist you should something go wrong.
My legs are sore. And my head is swimming. But … worth it.\n\nThe note on the table. It was for Neri. I can't remember what about. Get it, would you?
Go ahead, my friend. Use the everflame torch to ignite the beacon.
Not now. I'm trying to translate ancient writing off this broken tablet.
Speak with Bassian, proxy. Discover the location of the Shrine of the Golden Eye. As a devoted follower of Hermaeus Mora, he is sure to know where the shrine can be found.
Why are we stopping? He's getting away!
Oh, it's a delight to see you, friend! So much has changed since you stepped up to help me at Anchre, but I'm confident things will work out for the best!

The One Who Knows instructed me to give you this. A condensate of planar potentialities—ah, you will not understand. It is ink.\n\nTake it to the Ulvano Cistern, a ruin near the city. Pour the ink into the water and your path will become clear.
If I have to turn away one more family ….\n\nDid you learn anything at the Stormwing about a sickness or a plague? And did the Temple really send Prelate Faram to the Necropolis?
No! After everything, we were too slow. They have entered the Crux and can access our pact with Lord Hermaeus Mora.\n\nThe Remnants may actually end.
All this time I had been searching for my father. He can't be dead! He's faced the jaws of a sea serpent and lived!

I can't wait to hear how this dolt managed to turn himself into a book. It must have been a novel experience, that's for sure!\n\nBut no, really. Thank you for your help getting my brother back. We owe you.
Help Meenai-Shai through the dangers of the Empyrean Ascent. I hope that returning this final book will free us all from this trap.

The Rectory Archives are housed nearby.\n\nJoining minds is a delicate process. To think something could interfere with the Rectory's apparatus and freely access the Chorus …. Huzmargo hopes the archive will shed light on it.
Speak with the Telvanni master … but take care. Find out why she is here, but do not give away any more than you must about our own purpose in Tel Rendys.
Let's keep following this trail. We can't be too far behind.
Ah, have mercy! You've been sent to capture me, haven't you? It was an honest mistake. I'm working to get Hermaeus Mora's fated glyphic back, I promise!\n\nPlease don't imprison me!

What a mess. These dead mortals will just lie around and smell until someone removes them. Why can't your kind dissipate graciously the way Daedra do?\n\nBut let's keep moving. The way to the Pool of Inquiry is straight ahead.
The researchers, too. I didn't want to believe it. Tun-Shei said what did this to them is back in isolation, but let's be on our guard just the same.
I only have your best interests at heart—mainly because I'm stuck with you for the time being. One of us being dead is more than enough for right now.
How can I go on without Reynila?

Odd. The estate here isn't as illustrious as I was led to believe. And do you smell that? There's a strange stench in the air here. Like something is burning?\n\nLet's get moving and look for Dreynis.
See what you can learn at the House Dres camp to the south. I'll go back and keep an eye on things at Tel Huulen.
I found him! Search his pockets for the secret.
Mevei said she'd meet us by the bridge outside of Arenthia. Let's get there quick.
I must focus on the ritual, cohort.

I can't believe Martina is dead. She was … well. Strange. But one of the best colleagues an old man could ever ask for.\n\nAhem. Let's … let's focus. We're here to do a job. Look for notes or a journal, would you?
I can't read spider scratch, but their carapaces don't look that deadly. Still, it's best to follow what the spider said. I don't know why it would lie or if it even can. One way to find out!

Dealing with spirits can be dangerous! Even more so when the spirit is newly deceased! Working alongside Meln is one thing, but bringing back Master Shelreni ….\n\nBe careful where this path leads, my friend.
Don't ask me. I've never been inside the Infinite Panopticon before. But Vaermina and her allies stepped through that portal, so it must lead somewhere.
Align each of the threads of fate and I shall weave them together to open the path to the Mythos. Hurry, proxy. Already I can feel the corruption once again taking hold of me.
I really should return the Fulcrum Obscura to Necrom, but I also promised to see this through. I'll do whatever I can to assist.

That door will take you into the archive. The maligraphies are the best lead we have, so head toward orbs of unstable ink and you'll find them. \n\nI'll watch and offer advice when I can, but I'll leave the fighting to you. It's not my forte.

I should have expected the portal to send us to a demiplane.\n\nI am sorry, proxy. The effort of maintaining the arcane shield was more strenuous than I remembered. I am not ready for a fight. Go on ahead. Find Torvesard.

The power Ithelia absorbed when you destroyed the Loom, it has turned her into the very monster Hermaeus Mora foresaw. And now she plans to challenge him and take Apocrypha for herself.\n\nI fear we may not be able to change these spiraling fates.

What started as instabilities in the threads of fate have become tears in the fabric of reality itself! The Great Eye's worst fears have come to pass! Somehow, someway, Ithelia is responsible for this disaster. I can feel it in my seventh appendage!
I want to find my legionaries and the estate staff. They have to be down here somewhere. Let's push forward and see what lies ahead.

As luck would have it, Scruut knows of a ship here in Fathoms Drift called Stormspinner. It was carrying items sacred to followers of Mephala and she thinks you can use them to restore the relic.\n\nThe ship should be to the north. Let's go find it.
Now that all of the relics have been restored, we should meet up with Leramil and Scruut back at my townhouse.
I'm glad you're back. Did you find everything we need?
And here I thought I left the life of an adventurer behind ages ago.
Apologies for Betu's earlier mischief. I hope he didn't damage the will. He's normally better behaved, but the Lady's passing has certainly got him on edge.

This one has read many wills in his time, but a riddle? And one that hides a fortune? This is a first. Mizzik could use another set of keen eyes. Perhaps you will see something that this one has missed.
The wards are destroyed. We should return to the door and see if we can access Hermaeus Mora's private sanctum now.

I don't know who they are or how they got here, but it looks like we've got company!\n\nYou'll need to deal with this, friend. Leramil is exhausted from maintaining the spell that got us here. And, well, I'm not much of a warrior.

The well's out back in the courtyard. Bring me a bucket of water and I'll mix up a Skyrim Sunrise. That should get her talking.\n\nThen I can ask her to move along and take this strangeness with her. She's scaring my customers.
I'll remain here until my aunt's affairs are resolved. I won't rest easy until I know justice has been brought to her killer.

Welcome, proxy. I searched Tamriel for signs of Torvesard or his Prince to no avail—until now. Strange disturbances and disorder trouble this land, occurrences that threaten West Weald and all of Nirn.\n\nBut through them, we will find her.
Rosalyn said we could use components in her shop to create an explosive. Look for alchemical oil and combustion canisters.\n\nJust don't put them together until we're ready to use them.

I spent a lot of time staring at this welkynd stone the last time I was here. Our party's mage was sure it controlled the vault door to the south … somehow.\n\nLet's look at those notes. Maybe the Recollection got closer to solving it than I did.

My tasks never end! I'll mark your map. The locations where you need to place the relics are in West Weald, the Telvanni Peninsula, and Apocrypha.\n\nLook for one of your allies when you get to each spot. And make sure to bring the scroll and relics!
Since I have some familiarity with the area, I'll meet you in the Telvanni Peninsula.
Take a look at the Skein, friend. It's right over there.
It's clear the Recollection has turned Hoperoot into a major stronghold. Take the map and the notes—they might tell us something about the Recollection's plans.

Glad you found us, comrade. I was meeting with Greenspeaker Darolith when Nantharion walked into the village like he still owned the place. Marched straight to these ruins.\n\nHe had a strange cloaked woman with him. I think that was Ithelia!

Here. Just to be safe, you should carry the wildburn seed. Greenspeaker Darolith in Vashabar should be able to tell us something about it. Just follow the Gold Road into Dawnwood and turn north. Tribune Alea and I will meet you there.
Torvesard? The Dremora that serves Ithelia? Be on your guard but see what he has to say.

Sorilen said she'd meet us here, but I don't see her. And that dead body, I'd recognize that gear anywhere. They're part of the Recollection.\n\nExamine the note next to the body. Maybe we'll learn what's going on here.
These crystalline growths are clearly of Mirrormoor. Evidence of Ithelia's passing, I suspect.
I don't know what our enemies are planning next for West Weald. But whatever it is, I'll meet it blade in hand. We're not defeated yet.

We must search these surface ruins for two types of things: my own irreplaceable notes, and any information of the Recollection's doings. Those Wood Elves must have some papers about here; mission orders, reports, or correspondence.
I hesitate to employ another relic after our mishap with the Skein of Secrets, but I see no other alternative. We must risk the Lamp of Clarity if we wish to escape.
I see how my reflection opened a path and I understand. The Many Paths are mine to control. Perhaps I open a doorway next time.\n\nLet us return to our reality, mortal.

I hope my father can rest easier now. I finished what he started and brought the murderers to justice. I'll see them get whatever punishment the magistrate deems acceptable, whether life in a dungeon or the executioner's blade.\n\nThanks again, deputy.
I refuse to let Daedra take this keep, comrade. Let's hunt down the hole they climbed in through and plug it.
We were too late for Oleander. But there's a chance we can still help Wisteria. Let's find her.

Ziss'vo. I wish I could go with you, but my song is needed elsewhere. \n\nI will try to find you again. Perhaps the high cantor can give guidance once she hears of this soul sent from another time. Be well!
The Temple of the Dark Moon … it is gone?
Transposing conduits of magicka like this was not easy. But I never shy away from a challenge.\n\nYour goal is to reach Sunhold. The magic circle I created will aid you in this venture.
When I took up the blade and shield, I never imagined battling Daedra for the fate of reality.
You stopped, amazing! The adept that helped return Eyevea to Nirn ….\n\nAh, sorry. Vanus Galerion himself asked me to find you. We have a bit of a predicament.

Now that we have a moment, allow me to introduce myself. Nahlia, Votary knight in the Order of the Lamp. \n\nI know of your impressive work for the guild, of course. It's a pleasure to make your acquaintance. Irnard briefed you on our situation?

Hiring hunters isn't the way to solve this problem. I know that Goblins can be unnerving if you aren't used to them, but wiping out two camps is going too far. \n\nDo you have a moment to help me with this Goblin problem?

Good! You found the lens. It will be your most important tool in tracing a path to the Luminaries. \n\nMerely holding the lens will attune you to the flow of magic. You will begin to see focal points, impressions left behind by these mystical beings.

Remarkable feats of magic wait for you beyond that final door. All of it designed with you in mind, to allow you to prove your worth.\n\nAll you have learned in our many wings converges there. Make haste, fable-bearer. Reclaim what passes to you.
I've never seen a Dragon myself, but I've seen the damage they can cause.\n\nPity they can't all have an appetite for riddles over destruction, like in that fable.

I won't lie. I was envious that you had first rights to exploring this place with Nahlia. To restoring the altar. Especially after seeing how much she's opened up with you around.\n\nNow that I know it involves riddles? Not so much.
What happens next is up to you, be it Gryphon, Netch, or Dragon. We've gathered their fables in the main hall.\n\nIf you have any questions, let me know. Except for what's beyond the unmarked door.

I think the headstones and the locked sewer grate confirm what we expected to find—Marcan Caelum spends a lot of time here. But I can't see him living in the ruins of the house. There's just nothing left.

Hello, friend. Thank you for helping us gather here.\n\nHooke just told us what he's learned, and he's right to worry. I fear a sudden knife from every stranger I pass. But perhaps it is meant to be, Eight keep me.
I admit, I wasn't sold on the story Hooke sent you with. But … he's changed. His eye's sharp like it used to be, but honest now.\n\nWhatever plan he has in mind, I'm in. Provided he buys the drinks.

Look at the wings on this little guzzard! They're so tiny, and the skin is so pink! The guzzards back in Craglorn were never this cute.\n\nI'm still waiting on two other quarries from Marcien. If you find them, I'd gladly pay you for the extra help.

This one wishes he had good tidings and something more welcoming than a simple fire. The Lucent Citadel is supposed to be empty. If Keshargo knew we would be attacked, he would have hired warriors. Now he must hire who he can.

Off in search of some abstract idea of justice and truth, aren't you? The Gryphon is a one note song, over and over again. \n\nI grew tired of that tune long ago, but good luck listening through to the end.
Any luck finding the real fable?
With my glorious tendrils, I could place the fable on the altar from all the way over here!\n\nI won't, of course. That would be no fun for you.
I'm here whenever you need me. Just let me know how I can help.
He's got you doing safeguards for him? See? He likes you!
Dealing with the Netch, are you? I can tell by the expression on your face. Send it my regards. \n\nBut please do so in a way that does not imply any sort of invitation to my domain.
The domain of the Crow, magic as far as the eye can see. Amazing. \n\nKind of reminds me of Ulfsild's study back in Sunnamere.

It is good to see you, my friends! I came here to commune with spirits. To find a path through the darkness. They taught me so much. Epiphanies on history, songs, and faith.\n\nAnd Zerith! Has the truth dawned on him yet? Is he finally ready?
I did it! Hah! Who knew? Hyacinth, I guess.\n\nLet's get on the boat, head to Sunhold, and rescue Snapdragon! Then just an easy portal back to the greenhouse. What could go wrong?
Auri-El, that makes me happy! Did you hear that? Hyacinth isn't the traitor! \n\nI'm happy, but also feel sort of sick at the same time. Weird.

I have no idea how taxing this will be. But given that I've never done anything like this before, I'm guessing it won't be easy. I'm going to focus, gather my strength. \n\nYou talk to the Gardener while I get ready.
I am sorry, tamiit. I cannot continue this ritual. The pain of this memory, it burns like a wound reopened.\n\nPlease. Do not ask me to continue.

Ziss. It was not enough for these Inquisition idolaters to hurl themselves at the Rajaska, but they also brought the Twilight Cantors right to them.\n\nWe must save who we can before these spirits finish their feast, walker!
I had not thought the spirit of the High Cantor's sister would share words with us. See what she wants, tamiit.
All is in readiness, walker. Do as Zerith said and ignite the two braziers.
Mezamma ambushed me. Cast a spell and I blacked out.\n\nI woke up feeling wrung dry, like how you described Magister Andrelo. I guess that's what it feels like when the snake takes your appearance.

Vanus is up to date on everything we know about the Worm Cult attacks, but he likes to hear things directly from those with first-hand experience.\n\nJust tell him everything. He's battled the worms for centuries and will have insights that we don't.

Gabrielle will join us shortly. I tasked her with reestablishing the wards protecting our guildhall, just in case the worms attack again in our absence.\n\nNo need for an invitation. Let's head inside.

Your lighthearted tone helped me realize that the world doesn't stop just because someone we respected and cared about has died.\n\nNow that we know the enemy and where to find them, the time has come to take the battle directly to the Worm Cult.

It worked! Can you believe it! She said that she loves me! And she said she'll wait for me!\n\nI never thought it was possible. I'm so happy, I could … take a nap. All this wooing has made me really tired.
Halt! In case you haven't noticed, you walked into the middle of a war zone. Why shouldn't I just assume you're one of Montclair's soldiers and cut you down where you stand?
I-I can't believe what I'm reading …. How could Renchant be such a fool? \n\nHas he given up on defending the kingdom and decided to accept the lesser of two evils? This is simply mad.
You've made quite a stir. I've got a message from the Phantom for you.
This is the worst shut down in Sentinel's history. The city's reserves will be bone dry any day now.

Please, they won't listen to me. It's true that I used to run with the Red Rooks, but I quit! I hate all the chaos they're causing in Glenumbra. \n\nNow I just want to help save my town, but the guards don't believe me.
I didn't think we'd be able to pull through at the end. But we did. We did!\n\nYou can't imagine how this feels. I had no idea Stenwick had this kind of … power!
I didn't want to tell you this before we left, but ….\n\nPeering at the Imperials from a distance? Not enough. We'll need information that's closer to the source.
Did they send anyone else from the city? No, I can see you're not part of Evermore's militia.
As soon as Draven's feeling better, we should leave this village. Whatever cure Kerbol's got in mind isn't for us.
Though you've certainly gone out of your way to help us, I ask that you keep your stay here brief. The townsfolk need time to recover from this ordeal.
Have you come from Bal Foyen? What news do you have?
Please, talk with me. What the Rii brothers plan is wrong.
You have given away our best defense. Pray there are no further attacks.
You're a brazen one, to wander into <<1>>. We won't negotiate with necromancers.
I fear there's little time before the Worm Cult discovers the secrets of the <<z:1>>. Be quick, before they add us to their ranks.\n\nYet another benefit of this damnable curse.
Don't hurt him. He's just frightened.
The feel of metal beneath your hammer, the sound of the forge, the smell of the blaze … why I wake up in the morning, recruit!
We eagerly await our reforged crown. We would not dare ask you to fashion glorious-looking hawk wings on each side. We prefer you surprise us.
I wonder if this has something to do with our new visitor? We've never entertained an Altmer before.\n\nOr it may just be coincidence.
There's trouble brewing among the pirates.\n\nI thought they were angry about the ones you killed, but it's more than that.
Welcome to Ragnthar. The barrier here is a relic of its builders. They did something very … strange to this place.
The ruins of Ondil are a dark and dangerous place. Tread carefully, Adept.
Shalidor seems very upset. Best talk to him! Don't want him telling father.
We've done it. The island is ours. We've won!
You look strong and capable. Good in a fight and brave enough to travel the world in search of adventure.\n\nIf my assessment of you is even close to correct, I could use your help.
I've no time for pleasantries, friend.
You! You're alive! \n\nAre you really here, or is this another trick?
I won't let the Silvenar stay a minute longer than necessary. As soon as he's ready, we'll be gone.
I won't delay the Silvenar one moment more than I must. We'll be gone soon.
You've done it! The barrier is almost broken. As you broke each of the spinners' bonds, I could feel the energy dispersing. I'm almost through.

Oh, whatever may I assist you with? Perhaps you need your pillow fluffed? Or maybe you need me to cut up your food for you? Wait, I know you. From Deshaan!\n\nDon't say a word. No one must know who or what I am.
She's running things out of the Guildhall in Daggerfall at the moment. The Eight guide you, comrade.
Valaste will be expecting you in the Mournhold Guildhall. I'll see you there, Adept.

Nice work. I'll train our volunteers as quick as I can.\n\n<<1>> wouldn't wait for us. He took a few of the more hot-tempered civilians and headed across the bridge. He thinks the captain is still alive.
It's too dangerous for you to be here. Tabil … I told him to run for home, not for help!
Ah, hello. Perhaps you would be willing to help old Raz with a quick errand?
Hold. Dawnbreak is in the middle of an evacuation. No one's allowed back in.
The bandits attack our stronghold. Go, keep them from breaching the longhouse!
No matter their schemes, the chief's other wives didn't deserve their fate.
What are you waiting for? Let's see some blood. We don't come here for the refreshments, I assure you.
Defeating the draugr opened the way into Korthor's tomb. \n\nThe fork is certain to be either within the tomb itself, or in Korthor's bony hand.
Haven't had this much fun at a Boast in years, dearie.
You have any more miracles in your pocket? We need to get through this door as well.
I'm with you. Strange, how this one feels an instant connection with you. Fast friendships formed in battle, yes?
Please. Give me a moment. I must finish my prayer to Azura.
Shazah and Khali are grateful for your guidance at Rawl'kha, Hallowed. We have a tremendous task ahead of us.
Shazah and I are ready. We are prepared, focused, honed. Are you?
Bright moons, stranger. Can Kalari help you?
Shuzura will hear your problem, but for now you must wait your turn.
Have you ever seen a place like this, Hallowed? Even in my dreams, I never imagined it would look like this ….
Whoa, there! Watch yourself! Something is terribly wrong in Greenhill.
This place smells like dead slaughterfish.
You are near the end of your training, soldier. We have yet to explain the tactics used to capture the enemy's castles and resources.
I have no doubt <<1>> can protect himself, but if he's trapped inside we need to get him out.
Well met. How did it go?
The lunar clergy of Rawl'kha are wise. This one is certain they will know what to do. Moons above, pray with me now.
You approach the camp of the Ash'abah. \n\nUnless you are here to help us, I suggest you turn around and go the other way.
You are a sight for sore eyes. I need your help.
Thanks to you, the vampires are no longer controlled by Molag Bal. I hope we don't live to regret this outcome.
Ahh, it is you. You drove the Colovians out of Arenthia, and freed Akkhuz-ri from the grip of the Dark Mane! This one feels the cool light of the moons flowing from your aura.
Watch Aranias' demonstration.
I can't believe how many strange woman have tried to capture me since I got here.\n\nThanks for helping me, by the way.
Thanks to you, and I can return to the service of Meridia. And I'm grateful you were able to save Stibbons. He's an … interesting fellow.\n\nI'm in your debt.
You're the one we've been studying! I need to speak to you.
Now we just need to find the Shade of Naemon … and destroy him.
Come on, we need to get to the Barrowbough!
That went well, I think. Shall we move on?
Have you ever seen a place like this, Hallowed? Even in my dreams, I never imagined it would look like this ….
You near the end of your training, soldier. Now to tell you of capturing the enemy's keeps and resources.
I'm grateful for your rescue. Time twisted in ways beyond my comprehension and it felt as though my torments would never end.
Capturing the Elder Scroll of Chim should be every Covenant soldier's top priority!
Help me with his bonds!
Sahan seems to been left in a rather awkward position. A bit rude of us to chat while he writhes in pain, don't you think?
Did <<1>> send you to mock me? Did you come to tell me I don't know the work of a Daedric Prince when I see one?
The shrine is on the other side of the chasm. We must find a way across.
Don't look at me. I'm terrible at puzzles!
Frost trolls. Why did they have to go and stir up frost trolls?
Let us keep moving. The longer we delay, the more difficult this will become.
A lever puzzle? How utterly pointless.
I assume you have come to rescue the nobles and stop Montclair's reinforcements. But if Reezal-Jul is here, you shouldn't have to face him alone.
House Montclair's hold on Shornhelm has been broken, but our job isn't done yet.
Please, pay me no mind. I didn't expect to react so strongly to seeing poor Stibbons in this state.\n\nNow, where did he put those notes?
Did you know your entire future is mapped out in the stars? One must only know how to read them.\n\nNot such an enviable skill, though. A mystery that kills the mystery, if you catch my meaning.
Damn these spiders ….
I expect that Baron Dorell and his troops will have found a good vantage point outside the city.\n\nWhile you help them liberate Northpoint, I'll continue to study the Ayleid book we discovered.
I had hoped <<1>> was mad, but if the Baroness knew ….\n\nCome on. Let's keep moving.
What happened to poor Grell? Is this what the plague does to people? How horrible!
I wonder, since we're basically best friends now, could you do a favor for me?
Your help in this task was invaluable. Would you be willing to help me deal another defeat to the Serpent's schemes?
Are you going to let some insubstantial geriatric Elf give you pause? Get to the Banished Cells and kick the Kinlord's hind straight to Oblivion!
Do the cries of eternal damnation root you to this place? Who but the Undaunted can break the chains of undeath? Go and do your duty!
You're more than capable with needle and thread. I'll be proud to call you my colleague.
Glyphs are powerful things. They transform potential into certainty.\n\nAlso, you can sell them for coin. I once bought a fine pony with my proceeds. And before you ask, it was delicious.
Make it stronger!
This is a private matter. I must tend to my son.
The broken pieces for the three panels must be around here somewhere. Let's explore the eastern and southern portions of the barrow and see if we can find them.

Damn you, Kharsthun! How am I supposed to make a great discovery when you—oh, hello!\n\nAre you with the House of Gory Details? The Glorious Orcs? The … oh, you know what I mean! The Orc museum! Have you brought the extra help I requested?
I'm a little worried about getting Stibbons back to the Mages Guild. Orcs don't have a word for "fragile" or "handle with care."
Who are you? It doesn't matter, the Hand of Morkul is mine!\n\nOnce I find it. Which … is harder than I thought. That's why you're here, isn't it?
Have you happened to see a small, golden cat run by? She's ever so obstinate and loves to explore.\n\nSometimes I think she's a better Orc than I am.
I might pay your friend Caudex a visit, now that you've smoothed things over. We can always use more true-believers. Especially immortal ones.
Please, put out the fire. I don't want to burn to death.
I have a drink and an appetizer, but I need a few more dishes before I'm ready to enter the competition.
Well done, challenger. It's always a pleasure to see you in action. Such precision! Such consummate skill!

Welcome! It's good to meet an Orc who shows an interest in the history of our land and our people.\n\nOf course, the House of Orsimer Glories will contain much more to examine once all of our exhibits are in place.
Your achievement will be enshrined forever in our memories!\n\nWell, in mine, anyway. Fa-Nuit-Hen will forget it the next time he goes Dreaming. But fear not, I'll remind him!
Thank Mala—I mean, thank Trinimac you're back. Got another crisis for you. Interested?
Hmm? Sorry, I'm up to my arse in contracts here. You looking for work? Come back and see me later. I might have something for you.
Please, Assassin, not now. I need to record that exchange between Mirabelle and the Matron word for word.\n\nDoes "cold-hearted oligarch" have one "g" or two?
Are we going to help <<1>>?
Well, look who it is! And right on time for a change, too.
Tanek will meet you in Kvatch. I expect the two of you to deal with the Grand Sermonizer and show the people of that hypocritical city the real power of the Dark Brotherhood.
So, Assassin, was the Count's information worth all the trouble he put us through?
I wonder, since we're basically best friends now, could you do a favor for me?
Are you ready to hear my proposition now?
That is all I know of the New Life traditions found throughout Tamriel.\n\nBut return here tomorrow if you want to celebrate anew!
I couldn't help overhear what you and the Archcanon discussed. Good luck out there. The fate of Vvardenfell may depend on your actions in service to my lord Vivec.

Canon Llevule says you helped him in his mission. As I have written, "The one who helps my ally becomes my friend."\n\nDespite the Archcanon's concerns, I greet you with sincerity and pose a simple question. Will you assist us further, outlander?
Don't care much for undead. No joy in killing something with no will to live.

The outlander returns. I understand there was trouble at the construction site, but you were able to save a few of the workers. Lord Vivec always draws the straightest arrow from the quiver, praise the Tribunal!\n\nDid you bring the Blessing Stone?
You invade our camp. Assault my kin. Desecrate our sacred rites! No outlander would do these things for their own sake.\n\nThe slaves of the false gods sent you, didn't they? Answer me!

More advice? Very well.\n\nIt's obvious from the inscription that we need to honor the memory of these departed souls by making appropriate offerings to each. That book over there may provide additional clues if you need them.

Such displeasure and disappointment! Nothing works even though every calculation is precise. And now an interruption. How infuriating!\n\nWait, wait. Sometimes the Great Gear turns from frustration to opportunity ….
My brother Chodala is about to do something foolish—and dangerous. But by dusk and dawn, Azura put you and I on the same path for a purpose. I just hope we have enough time.
When a Clockwork Apostle discovers an unexplainable phenomenon, it can be a moment of unbounded joy or utter terror.\n\nThat strange portal over there definitely falls into the second category ….
What an incredible place.

Shimmerene serves as the arrival point for newcomers to the island. It's the perfect place to ask a few leading questions and determine what the people think of the Queen's decree.\n\nRaz would go, but many know his face, yes?

Good to see you again, my friend. I was beginning to think I miscalculated your trajectory and missed you entirely. But no, the Great Mage never makes those kinds of errors.\n\nNow come closer. We have something important to talk about.
Something is amiss in Summerset, but I can't quite put my finger on the cause.\n\nNo matter. I'm sure my investigations will turn up something. I just need to be patient.

Good, you're back. Valsirenn suggested you would be invaluable in our efforts to extract information from the abyssal pearl, and I concur.\n\nWe've started the augury ritual, but the pearl has proven resistant to our efforts to reveal its secrets.

I don't even know where to start with Glardir. Maybe she's the Gale Player? Or the Masked Madrigal?\n\nIt doesn't make a whit of sense. Hopefully my other friends, Pavo, Tanelwen, and Selynia can help … once you break their enchantment, of course.

You've returned intact! How wonderful. I was worried the gryphon might have been a bit too much, but I see you're not one to be easily deterred. Good.\n\nTell me, how did you acquire your most lovely feather?
Greetings, traveler.\n\nSay, have you met with another Elf around here? Heavy armor, sour disposition? I hired her as an escort for my expedition, and unfortunately I cannot start without her.
So, we're really doing this …? For Lotus's sake, I hope Elise is wrong.
We made it … ah, too many years on dry land.\n\nThere's a secret door in these ruins that will lead us directly into Sea Keep's dungeon. I can unseal it, but there's something you should know first.
Take a look around the grape fields and let me know if you find anything. You may also want to speak to some of the witnesses here. They may be more forthcoming with you than they have been with us.

I knew they were up to something here. Smells awful. Alchemical.\n\nThis equipment isn't incriminating enough on its own though. Vinelore could justify it for medicinal uses. We need to find evidence that can't be explained away so easily.
Vile's dog-man wants to talk to you, not me!
The thoughts and intentions of the Psijic Order go with you, initiate. Farewell.

Thank you, initiate. I honestly don't know what we'd do without your help. I keep telling the Loremaster I can assist you. I mean, I did spend my entire childhood on the continent after all.\n\nI suppose he knows best.
Were you successful? You were, weren't you? Go tell the Loremaster! Quick!
Safe travels, ceruval. Let us both hope that when you return, this business of the Staff of Towers will be concluded.

Oh good, you're back. I just returned from my own investigations. I followed a lead, but the trail ran cold. Very disappointing.\n\nSo tell me what happened in the Outlaws Refuge. Were you able to learn anything new about Margus Derius?

There you are! Was the smuggler able to tell you anything about those antiquities you found? Concordia certainly seems to think they might be important.\n\nI'm still learning to understand dryskin emotions, but I'm pretty sure she's concerned.
You found us. Good. As you can see, we've met with some difficulty. I apologize for the … unsightliness.\n\nWere your inquiries in Bright-Throat Village fruitful?

Another successful expedition! We'd all be suffocated or dissolved if Xukas hadn't come along, of course. Even so, we got what we came for—the Kajin-Jat Crystal!\n\nYou should speak with Xukas. He rarely intercedes like this. We're very fortunate.
My Bright-Throats and the Dead-Water tribe will send warriors to see this Remnant soon, I think. But they will not arrive in time. We must stop Kassandra on our own.
This time, we attack as one. One serpent—two heads.
I don't like the look of this, beek-ojel. I will keep my distance until you know it is safe.

I … I wasn't sure anyone would come for me. I didn't think anyone even knew where I was. I owe you my life. Again.\n\nThe bindings on my wrists were painful, but what really hurts is the betrayal. Do I really mean so little to Kassandra?
I—I just need to focus on my work right now.
If you've got something to say, say it to Kassandra.
Xukas? As mud is my mother, what is he doing here? This place requires sharp weapons, not sharp tongues.\n\nStill. We may need some cleverness before long. Talk to him. See what he wants.

So, you're off then? That's all to the good, I guess. I could do with a bit less peril, and I've got a lot of reading to do! The Remnant of Argon—what an adventure!\n\nGive my best to Xukas, and be careful out there, all right?
Good to see you, friend! Just mind where you step. I'd rather not have to start my search all over again.
I am confused. Shuvu is the wisest listener in the tribe. How could he hear nothing when I heard it so clearly?\n\nHe is very old. Maybe he just needs his ear-cavity flushed.

I hoped to catch you before you were done here. I need you to head west. Nala-do's scouts identified a number of Euraxian supply camps set up near the mountains.\n\nI want you to help Nala-do and her soldiers disrupt the Euraxian supply lines.

My stalker remains focused on me, but I urge you to stay vigilant. Be on your guard and don't trust anyone you meet on the road.\n\nSomeone with the power to hide from Abnur Tharn is not to be trifled with.

The dead Euraxian wears the insignia of Saulinia's assassination squad. Whatever creature brought the soldier down, they obviously decided to leave him where he fell.\n\nCaptain Saulinia must be in a great hurry to find and kill her target.
We could start by searching around the columns that hold the aqueduct up. Someone gravely injured may have rested in the structure's shadow.\n\nNo time to waste, walker. Let's go.
Hmm. You wouldn't happen to be traveling to the town of Hakoshae, would you?
The stables, hmm? Developed a sudden interest in horsemanship, walker?

I think you are right, five-claw. The Betrayer must want to finish what he started in the ancient time. But the Dragons also want that power. Are they working together?\n\nEither way, we need to get to the temple ruins.
Tasnasi has not seen her old crew in some time. Not since … never mind.\n\nYou were not followed, yes? Tasnasi is not welcome in the Stitches. Associates of Tasnasi, also not welcome.

You can do it, Sereyne. It's just moving yourself and four other living people with one of the most complex spells known. \n\nIt's not like you could, you know, mix up peoples' arms, or legs, or anything.
To see Tasnasi, Sereyne, and Vole once more warms me from ear to tail.\n\n"The joy of friendship is best known by the heart in a reunion," so the fifth song of the Pellitine Verses goes.
Sheath your claws, walker. This one does not want a fight, but you've walked into a dangerous feud. You should leave the Weeping Scar. Yushiha cannot protect everyone from her former kin.

Riverhold remains free, thanks to your efforts and the blood and sweat of our people. What happens next may just determine the fate of all of Elsweyr.\n\nAbnur Tharn wants to talk to you. He does so love the sound of his own voice.
Well, we did come here for a history lesson. We'd best do what she says, for now.
Azurah guides us, child. You only need to listen.
Raz will make sure she gets to safety. Best if you go on ahead, yes?

You must be here about my summons. Good, good. I was just telling Lord Gharesh-ri and Khamira that someone would answer my call.\n\nSince you're here, I presume you will wholeheartedly agree to help us save Elsweyr from a rage of Dragons.
Go speak to my sister if you seek help. I am far too distraught to deal with any patrons today.
