By the time you get back, I'll have all the gold we need to buy Fez'skar's freedom.\n\nIt hurts me to think about my friend being stuck in a cage somewhere. I mean, he kind of deserves it, but still. We need to hurry.

Rigurt's favorite diplomatic assistant! How have you been? Rigurt has been busy bringing cultures together like a delicious stew made of strangers.\n\nNow Rigurt could use your help. After our past success, it would be good to work with you again.

You there! With the rippling muscles and confused face! Do you enjoy jumbling fun with violence? Of course you do!\n\nDon't worry about these levelheaded losers. No one can see me but you. You possess a special untapped talent for unhinged insanity!

I know Sai was hoping for a confrontation, but I doubt we could have survived an encounter with Kaalgrontiid. He looked even more powerful than when we saw him at Jode's Core.\n\nNow, about that portal ….
You must try to find a pathway to the archives. If you fail, return to me and try again.
Just in time, my friend. When my old companion arrives, I'd prefer to have someone I trust at my side.
Welcome to the Abbey of Blades. Mind the debris. Repairs and renovations are still under way.

I refuse to be stymied by a hovering land mass!\n\nThe floating island could be part of Kaalgrontiid's plan, but it could also mean he wanted privacy for his final push toward ascension. Either way, we need to find a way to get up there.
Against my better judgment, I think we should follow Za'ji's plan. Besides, it's best if you help secure the boat. We wouldn't want our new friends sailing off without us.
We've arrived, walker. This is where the battle for Vijari's soul will be fought. Do not doubt for a moment that Dak'radhi will not give him up without a fight.
Head to the sanctum and report to Sai Sahan. Moons willing, he has a plan.

These episodes … are draining.\n\nGo to Moonlit Cove. I am certain the way to Dragonhold will be revealed. Just keep your eyes open and let the Moons guide you. The Moons, and the spirit cat, if you see it again.

Better get going, friend. The great bearded one had a look in his eyes. For some reason that this one will never understand, Za'ji thinks he really can't wait to engage the Dragon in battle.\n\nSome people have a death wish, yes?

We have a few more tasks to attend to, then we'll meet you back at the Dragonguard Sanctum.\n\nJust don't head for the floating island without us. I really want to see what Pellitine looks like from way up there.
Complete whatever preparations you require. We'll meet you back at the sanctum.
You go ahead. Clan Mother Hizuni and Nahfahlaar both confided in you, and I don't believe that's a coincidence. You should tell Tadali why we're here.\n\nI'm behind you all the way.
Hey! Look who it is! Long time no see, pal.\n\nI'd love to catch up and swap war stories, but these damned ropes really … knock the wind out of the reunion, you know? You want to give me a hand?
This one has much to do. If you have business, speak to Captain Za'ji.
Damn that Dragon's pride. If Nahfahlaar had only broken off and regrouped with us.\n\nIt seems we have no choice but to rescue the beast. Are you with me?

Mother told me this was a bad idea, but did I listen? No. I had to come and see the place my Khajiiti family came from.\n\nAnd could things go any worse? I lost my uncle's goods, the guard he sent with me. I even lost my cat!

Queen Khamira recalled one last thing before I left her side. It took her a moment to understand what the vision was showing her, but she shared that knowledge with me.\n\nI know what we're looking for in this place.

Don't look at me. It's not like Nords are known for being great mages, so whatever the Skald-King's wizards did may not work. Or it could explode.\n\nHold up the medallion and see if you can make it work.
You handled yourself well. Not sure I would have made it past that savage without your assistance. We'll be out of these crypts soon enough.
Let's hurry back to the Blue Palace. The sooner Fenn creates this elixir, the sooner we can distribute it.
I now know enough about how they create the medallions to move my research along.\n\nI'll return to the Blue Palace and start putting an elixir together.

I'm not sure I completely follow what Fenn and the clever woman are talking about, but it sounds like they may have made a breakthrough.\n\nWhat about Svana? She took a big risk going to Blackreach with you.
I … I hoped we would have been in time to save her.
I'm scared, but I'm not leaving. I need to know if Mavvok survived this.
Through the secret passage! Let's go!
Looks like you made good on Fenn's promise. Now talk to Edjar and get him to do the same.

I'll stay with Fenn. Help him break the Ashen Lord's spell. It may not stop the harrowstorm, but we have to try.\n\nYou and Lyris search for my father. If we fail, you need to be in position to do … whatever is necessary.
This book, I recognize the handwriting. It's Tzinghalis's.\n\nIt's more of his research. Harrowstorms, witch pikes, netherroot brew … how it all works together for the benefit of the Gray Host.
I know war preparations when I see them. Harrowstorm or no, the Gray Host is ready to march.
Did the storm kill all these people? Or was it the vampires we've seen roaming around?\n\nI just hope High Priest Varkour is safe inside.
Good job with the sentry. You got rid of him and I didn't have to bash him or anything.\n\nSee if you can pick the lock while I keep watch.

I'm with you. Let's find out where those Reachmen came from. They dragged Bjora and the townsfolk deeper into the barrow, so we should start there.\n\nWith any luck, we can save them before it's too late.
There are many fine places to post handbills around Solitude.\n\nYou should only need to post four of them, but make sure people see them. We need to get the word out!
You should speak with Shelaria. I'm afraid she'll have nothing to do with me for now.
Hurry, push forward! There's something in the cave!
It's good to see you again, but what are you doing here? Have you followed the Draugrkin's plunder to this hold, too?

Look for the missing caravan. See if you can determine what happened to it and who's to blame.\n\nI need to check on Ena, the caravan agent. She has a camp on the overlook, south of the bridge. Meet me there if you find any sign of the caravan.
Let me know if you find anything. I'm going to keep an eye on Svana. The last thing we need is for something to happen to her as well.
Once again, I prove that I'm a scholar, not a warrior. I don't think he expected another vampire, though.
So, you think I should take the Blood Price from Mazog?

Damn it! Mazog doesn't deserve this. She's a good, honest Orc. She only wanted to help! \n\nChief Urzikh will rip out her tusks, and Mazog will forever bear the mark of shame. I … I wish I could have protected her.
Thank you for accompanying me. I will feel better having someone by my side while I search for my grandfather. \n\nWe should head inside whenever you're ready.

Rigurt has long heard tales of the strange caves near Solitude! The tales did not say they were so eerie. But Rigurt does not scare easily! He is a proud, unflinching son of Eastmarch! \n\nNow, let's get what we came for and leave. Quickly.
After dealing with one evil monster after another, I understand better why Verandis brought us together in House Ravenwatch. The threat our kin poses to normal folks of Tamriel worries me.
Do not lose heart, assistant.\n\nYes, these riddles are infuriating, but you know what I always say: the more numerous the puzzles, the more numerous the rewards!

There's a Dragon mound farther down the road, a big one. When I first entertained this theory, I made a warding spell. One that should seal whatever's inside, permanently. It's difficult to cast, however.\n\nI need someone to watch my back.

Don't lose that blood pendant. Since you're not a vampire, it's the only way for you to see the sigils. Besides, it contains some of my blood. I'm trusting you with that.\n\nCome on, let's follow the sigils.
That parchment appears relatively fresh and intact.\n\nWhat does it say?
Dark days are upon us, harrier. I fear for my people.

I'm sorry to put this all upon your shoulders, but it's better that I remove myself from this journey. You can see what Rada intends to show me with impartial eyes.\n\nLearn the secrets of the Darkstorm and together we'll unravel Rada's plans.
The entrance to the archive should be nearby. Let's get out of the open before we start gabbing.

So this is where Mannimarco made his first offering to Molag Bal. It's exactly what I'd expect from a place swallowed by Oblivion and yet so much worse. It feels wrong. Down in my bones wrong.\n\nLet's find what we're searching for and be done with it.
You are surprisingly willing to throw yourself into extra-planar phenomena. On the whole, I respect that. \n\nNow come. The repository is through here.

These insignias must have been important to the Nighthollow. Hang on to the damaged one. The magic I cast on it may rouse more memories as you explore these halls.\n\nIf you find an undamaged insignia, bring it to me. A whole one may reveal more.

Either that just opened the way into the big, ominous castle, or we awakened some unthinkable horror that's on its way to devour us.\n\nI suppose either would be interesting. Let's go check the castle first, though, all right?
Do not tarry here, outsider. The rest of my clan takes a dim view of those not of the Reach.
Adusa loves it when a plan comes together! This worked out better than I expected! Now, we just have to find Kathad.\n\nAnd Freyleth.

With your help, we may save the Reach yet. While I continue to exert diplomatic pressure, I need you to find information the ard will consider valuable. Something concerning the rebels that plague his rule, perhaps.\n\nStart by talking to the sentry.
Karthwasten has been home to the Crow-Eye clan for as long as anyone can remember. We won't abandon it because of this unnatural storm.
We find these from time to time. We think they're Dwarven. Sky tales etched into metal. Pretty, isn't it?
Whoever lived in a house this grand probably packed it with traps and secrets. Perfect! Just like a treasure hunt from the old stories.
It warms my heart to see you again, my friend. I take it you came at Lyris's behest?\n\nNow tell me, did you happen to find a letter in that coffer?
I have nothing to say to you, outsider.
I've heard stories about this clan. They're fierce. And deadly. Be careful as you search the ruins.
Asking the vateshran about the origin of our feud, that's as good an idea as any. At least, it's better than this handfasting.\n\nI just hope he's still using the camp near here.
This isn't the time or place for a long discussion, friend. Get me out of these ruins and then we can talk about whatever's on your mind.
Finally! One Stibbons is bad enough, but a gaggle of them? It's like trying to herd cats!\n\nBut where's the duplicate that slipped away? Did you find it?
What are you doing here? Get back out there and make sure Captain Rian and the Ivory Brigade come to help us.\n\nWe won't be able to defend Fort Redmane without them.

I'll get the city guards to come and gather the councilor's body. She shouldn't just be left out here. Then I'll head to Councilor Jirich's manor.\n\nWhen you're done checking on Councilor Faleria and Councilor Sophus, meet me there.

It's hard to imagine, but that abbey was once a thriving bazaar, bustling with commerce and teeming with people. Nothing left but rot and overgrowth—and an abundance of dangerous beasts.\n\nWell, there is one thing that I hope remains from that time.

Hey, you're that adventurer who helped me at Black Drake Villa! How'd you know I was going to be here?\n\nNever mind that for now, I'm just glad to see you! Between the Covenant soldiers and the cultists, I could use the assistance.
Ask the Wood Elf about Quistley. Maybe they've seen him.
Well, things don't always go to plan on a job, but this is getting ridiculous.\n\nLet me guess. Commander Axius sent you in after us because we're missing and presumed dead. Correct?
As I said. Xynaa helped me. And she can help Calia and Destron. We just have to trust her. And if you can't trust her, trust me.
Why didn't Sombren tell us his mentor was a Dremora? What else hasn't he told us?
We had Dremora teachers in the sanctum at times. They could be cruel, but they were very knowledgeable.

Please forgive me, sera. While I was wallowing in self-pity, you were out here trying to clean up my mess.\n\nAnd by the Three, Tiras still lives! Or, exists at any rate. What happened when you found him?

I thought I'd slip in, knock out a smuggler or two, grab this Quistley fellow and be back in Leyawiin in time for dinner. No such luck. I run into principled competition and deluded cultists praying to Sithis.
Ah, yet another inferior intellect bumbles into Veyond. You're in good company with Revus around.
Let's keep moving. We still need to find whatever this vault is protecting.
You heard that, right? The Sul-Xan aren't just harvesting the harrada vines, they're cultivating it! It's worse than I thought.
That's definitely heartsbane.\n\nTake a peek underneath. I'm half expecting the Duchess to pop up and yell at us to hurry up.
Give me a moment … to catch my breath. I'm out of practice. I'm very much out of practice.
After you. But do hurry. I'd rather find out where those cultists were fleeing to before the portal closes.

He's gone. Soul shriven. I've read accounts of this happening, but I've never seen it myself. This ravaged body is all that's left of Ghalor. His soul … gone somewhere far worse.\n\nThis is what will happen to the others. To my little brother ….

What do you think? Did the Dark Brotherhood really assassinate Farrul Lupus? Is this book he sent me to retrieve really that important?\n\nI'm not sure what we should do next, so if you have any ideas, I can't wait to hear them.
I'm afraid we've reached the really scary bit. The Daedric creature responsible for all these portals waits just beyond that gate.\n\nIf you have any other preparations to make, make them now.

Where in Oblivion's name did that door come from? Was it here this whole time? Sixty years, and no one notices a scary portal to gods-know-where is tucked away in a corner?\n\nShould we—? Yes, we should go through. Um, you first, though, all right?

All these years I assumed my mother had preferred to die instead of living with her disgrace, even if that meant leaving a small child alone in the world. But she didn't.\n\nAnd the sister I thought was dead is alive? I am … stunned.
That was … somewhat enlightening. Insect nature spirits are a peculiar kind. They always communicate so quickly, it's near impossible to parse.
Maybe while were out hunting down this chicken we can stop somewhere for a bite to eat. I'm feeling a bit peckish.\n\nSorry, that's not funny. Maybe a little funny.
I—I'm all right, traveler. Nothing I can't tend to. I wish I could say the same for our retinue.\n\nI'm sure you have questions, but Martus is the one in charge. Speak to him.

It's just one thing after another, isn't it? I've barely had time to process the fact that I'm an Ambition or even learn what that really means.\n\nI'm sorry I couldn't stop Sombren from taking Calia's powers. It all happened so fast.

That worked just as we needed. Daedric security must get pretty sloppy around this area. Let's pray that our luck holds up. \n\nLet's get into that tower. And keep your eyes open. We're deep in Dagon's territory now.
I'm not sure what we're going to find in here, but let's look around. The amulet must have led us here for a reason.
Selveni, don't lose your head. All you need to do is go on a nice stroll through a monster infested fiery plane looking for an altar. It'll be fine.
I can't decide if I want my memories to fully return or not. Not knowing is bad, but knowing could be worse. It's all very confusing, and I hate that.

Sister Celdina said something at Burning Gyre Keep that intrigued me. She admitted that the cult has another device to create Incarnates. The Riven Cataclyst. \n\nI would like to examine this machine … before you destroy it, of course.

Master, shouldn't we be seeking Sister Celdina and her Riven Cataclyst? I may spend most of my time in your pack, but I hear every word.\n\nTalk to Lyranth. The clever little Dremora must have a plan. She seems to have hundreds of the things.
Mortals have too many expressions—your face tells me nothing. Did you find anything at the foundry, or did you fail at your task?

Miksotet claims he requires a mortal. Your life is limited. Best way to connect to an empty shell. I still need you, though. Stay unharmed.\n\nHe said to begin with the dead Banekin. Toss it in the brazier. We'll see the results.
We're close to something big here, I just know it!

If Arox is right, Elegian is behind that glowing door. That's a lot of security for one old blind seer, though.\n\nI guess we need to figure out how to open Elegian's cell if I really want to talk to him.

I can't stop thinking about Elegian. Why did he give me this amulet? And why did he create my mask?\n\nDamn it! All these questions! And they need to wait until we finish our business at Annihilarch's Summit. Save Fargrave, then worry about myself.

I've seen only a few dead mortals during our stays in Wretched Spire, but it's obvious that this cultist died recently. I do not need the nose of a daedrat to smell freshly spilled blood.\n\nWhat did you find?
Destruction's Solace it is. I'm with you to the end, no matter what!
Unlike the door outside, this area contains everything we need to disrupt the magic sustaining the ward and dispel it.\n\nI've seen the Daedra use these crystals to do all sorts of things.
I imagine you have questions for me. I have questions even for myself. How did I ever know of this place, yet there is indeed an air of familiarity.
This spellcraft is crude … but effective. A loathsome combination.\n\nTry that key you found in the auction house. It might do the trick.
There, see if you can remove the collar from that poor soul. You should be fine so long as you don't try it on.

We'll rendezvous at Abhain Chapel, on the north side of the loch. I've already sent an operative ahead to scout the area.\n\nBe prepared to defend yourself. The Ascendant Order won't give up Guild General Quentyn without a fight.

Oh, hello. I'm a representative of the Mages Guild to Lord Bacaro's conference. \n\nThis is my first visit to High Isle. I wonder if I have time to find a druid before Lady Arabelle needs me. I'm quite interested in their approach to magic.

I believe Zenithar is pleased with our efforts. I couldn't have done this without you. \n\nIt is Zenithar who teaches us that collaboration leads to the greatest achievements. No one is above asking others to lend their skills to a task.
You'll help Isobel in the tourney? Oh, you are the dearest person! I don't know what I'd do without her.
Glad to have you at my back. This place is already sending chills up my spine.\n\nLet's have a look through all this detritus. See if we can't find something belonging to my ancestor or her ship.

I had forgotten what exhaustion feels like. In fact, I died so long ago that I think I'd forgotten that I'd forgotten the feeling. I have mixed opinions about this.\n\nGo ahead to the library. Find the key for the hidden route. I will see you there.
No sign of Dockmaster Arnauld, yet plenty of evidence that something is amiss.\n\nTake a look around, please. See if you can find any clues as to where our absent dockmaster might have gotten to.
I think we have everything we need to convince the archdruid. Let's review what we discovered.
Perfect, we have everything we need. Now we just have to make the damned thing work.
I'm glad you're here. It's a relief to have someone sensible and calm to help me fix this mess. I owe you after this is all over.

Auri-El bless my crown, but it's good to see you my friend. Don't tell me you got washed onto this Oblivion-cursed rock, too?\n\nYou have my apologies, old friend. I must smell like a three-day-dead guar right now.

Come to think of it, I also heard these Serpents mention a captured noble. I suppose that's what whoever's behind this told them. No reason to reveal we're royals. Instantly raises the bounty.\n\nReally wish I'd taken one of them prisoner, though.

So let's review what we found. First there was a map of Castle Navire that showed a river that doesn't exist. At least, it's not on the surface.\n\nIf it depicts an underground river, it could also indicate a hidden passage beneath the castle.
Nice of Lady Arabelle to provide the disguises. I was afraid we were going to have to waylay a couple of stragglers and hope their armor fits.
This island is a death trap. Unless you're me, of course!
It seems that talking to that smelly Breton is the only way to get Oblan out of this.
This is terrible. The Daggerfall Covenant cultural delegate in the manacles of a common criminal?\n\nTalk to <<1>>, please. There must be explanation!
Let's look for father. But we should be careful, this place is overrun with those Hadolid creatures.

The tanna leaf is considered sacred in some cultures, including among the local druids. Should be easy enough to find.\n\nLignite is a particular type of coal, a rock formed by naturally compressed peat. It's common to the area. Let's look around.
Oh good, we have to follow a drunk man, do we? This is promising.\n\nAzamel better know something about Song. I don't enjoy being led around by the tail.
Marso has to be safe. He just has to be.
Bah, I wish I'd found Lady Aurelia before she went to confront the thief.

Ah, fair Janne, how I've longed to hold you close again! You were never far from my thoughts, even while I sailed across the stormy seas.\n\nAnd here I am, just as I promised! Back from the war for an intimate rendezvous under our favorite tree!

M'lady has always found history more fascinating than me, I admit. At least that forgetful sea captain remembered that Tobin Moorcroft, the memorial's master builder, was his brother.\n\nYou should talk to that ghost woman. She seems to know something.
These clawless runts will regret attacking a warrior of Elsweyr.
Ha! You're making me nervous standing around like that. Come on, have a seat. Let's get started!

Dear Brahgas often strays, but never for long. His coin rarely holds out. He must be back by now—safe within the confines of the gaming hall where he can be … supervised.\n\nDo not worry, though. Brahgas is a fine player. He will teach you well.

Remember, everybody's got to start somewhere. Win, lose, it doesn't matter. Just focus on learning the game—getting into the rhythm, right?\n\nI'll cheer you on from here. It's not everyday I get to see an aspiring champion cut their teeth!

The three of you represent the Gonfalon Chapter's best hopes for a title—I would hate for Sorinne to miss her chance. She's worked so hard to reach this point!\n\nI did not see where she went, but someone in the hall might know.
I sense a strange energy here. The plants tremble with it. Blight, be careful in there. The Firesong are dangerous.

Be on your guard in there, sailor. No telling what the Firesong have prepared for us. And when we find Wyress Tola, do whatever you must to keep her safe.\n\nDruid Laurel and I will follow behind and back you up.

A nature spirit? I saw a lot of amazing things during my time with the Stonelore, but nothing like this!\n\nDruid Laurel explained it to me, but I can't say I completely understand. You should talk to her. And to Frii, too, if you like.

Supplies for the Society of the Steadfast? Give them to Lord Bacaro. I wish he'd brought knights instead of bandages, but I'll take whatever help he offers.\n\nAt least he showed up, not like those ivy-robed beggars.
You've made a difference here, mate. I'm sure House Mornard won't forget that when the time comes to collect your pay.
Talk to Za'ji, friend. All these delays are beginning to ruffle my fur and I'd just as soon get on with things.

When Za'ji and Caska returned, we found Lady Arabelle unconscious on the floor! We got her to bed and sent for Druid Ryvana. She can help her, yes? Druids have healing magic, or so Za'ji has heard.\n\nUpstairs, five-claw. You must go to Lady Arabelle.
It appears Lord Bacaro has a few secrets of his own. Let's see what awaits us through the now-revealed door.

We didn't expect the Ascendant Order to wither away, but I had no idea its roots ran so deep. And it seems they have crept into our most trusted circles. Someone at Steadfast Manor diverted this armor shipment here.\n\nLet's review what we uncovered.
That was quite a battle. Three ships against one seemed like daunting odds, but that's why we hired Captain Siravaen.\n\nLet's go below, friend. The real battle is still before us.
That cursed volcano blanketed the waters around Y'ffelon in brimstone and murk. The Firesong found us while we were groping along half-blind. Well, get out there and make them sorry they did!
I have never been here. Yet it feels … familiar. These stones were told to remember King Kasorayn. And to wait for me.
I have the tablet in my hands one moment, and the next? No hands at all!

I don't care what that druid says. I'm not going near the lava pools. I'll meet you here. Where it's safe.\n\nDon't worry. I can cast a spell if it's written down clearly. You should be able to retrieve one of these fire shards after that.
I never suspected the leader of the Society of the Steadfast had such ill intentions. We were all deceived.

Head east to the ships and find that cloth. And try to keep it quiet. Let's not give the Dreadsail sea witches any reason to think someone else wants that relic.\n\nHopefully Umindior doesn't let anything slip in the throes of … whatever.

I never suspected the Chronicle could fall so completely into despair ….\n\nGwenaelle, my worry grows stronger with every passing second. We have to find her, no matter how far into these tunnels we must travel.

Why did you go and do such a thing? Now I'm all wet. I was so happy—happy and sore. But you ruined it.\n\nI expected a Sea Elf. A beautiful, sensuous, vigorous Sea Elf. Instead, it's you. Where did you come from?

It's worse than I thought. I saw more than my fair share of bodies on the way here. I'm sure you did, too. If we don't hurry, those poisonous thorns will have the numbers to overwhelm Glimmertarn. \n\nBlight!

Mildanor set wards to protect this chamber, but their energy was burned away by those runes. Only a powerful devotee of the One Who Knows could utilize such magic.\n\nA follower of Hermaeus Mora killed Mildanor. Perhaps even someone he knew.
I just saw him. The Lark of Rosgard—he's in the crypts! Just need a moment to catch my breath.

Thank goodness you came across me when you did! I'd have completely lost my head in there without you. And I just know I'd never have been able to convince the miners to stay on by myself. The people of Necrom have you to thank, mercenary.

As Hermaeus Mora, the One Who Knows, foretold, we meet again, proxy. Many diverse twists of fate have led us to this nebulous—ah. Too complicated.\n\nI come with a gift. A purpose, dark and heavy. An opportunity to fulfill the contract you signed.

Fate must have led you here, friend. Prelate Faram arrived aboard the Stormwing. If you can find out where they boarded the ship, it might tell us something.\n\nTalk to the port master at the harbor while I deal with any pilgrims that come by.

Without those rituals, the Dreamcarvers' plans should move drastically slower. \n\nOur next task is obvious. We find Uxunath and stop her from entering the Crux. If we ascend the tower, we can get a better view. Perhaps see where she hides.
Keep your eyes peeled, my friend! Finding my father's belongings would help locate him and our ship.

It seems I knew of Meenai-Shai's transgressions and yet acted too slowly. Why did I hesitate? Did I suspect more at play. Perhaps this is why I've been cursed to observe. A reminder of my inaction. Regardless, we have one more book to return.

I've been tending to the vessels in the Corporea for many, many years, and never before have I seen a thing like what just happened. That vessel—it just talked to us! It moved! That should not be possible.

I wish to survey the tower and its grounds. The threads of fate hang over this place like cobwebs of possibility and consequence. Let us explore the center of the compound and see where those threads take us.
Stay ready, all right? Those mercs don't let up easy.

Only Hermaeus Mora's most trusted followers and scribes are allowed access to the Tranquil Catalog. But if the Hidden Kindred and their Dremora allies know about the Pool of Inquiry ….\n\nWe must hurry, mortal.
We can't waste time. We need to get to Nathyn as quickly as we're able.
I always knew it could have ended this way. But I never thought ….\n\nAt least I was with her in her final moments.

Wonderful! I had a good feeling about you. I prepared this boat to take us up to the island. We'll be a bit snug, but it'll do. And do be on guard. I have heard the island isn't the most welcoming of places.

Notice how the servants around here love me? They know I'm here for bigger scribs than them. Well, come to think of it, I have had a writ or two for servants over the years. Three, actually.\n\nAnyway, find anything useful in there?
Sure glad I remembered to use this mirror. Certainly didn't need a mortal to remind me.\n\nFine, fine. Good idea. I'll guide us based on what I see. You just keep us safe.
Let's show this slaver how we negotiate.
Let's get to Riften, quick as we can. I'm not eager to speak to Tem again. \n\nBut we must do what we must. Onward and upward!
I'm not sure what I was expecting to find here, but it wasn't this. Martina was always so meticulous. This place is … chaotic.
You can't just walk away from knowledge, it'd be rude. Read it. See what the spiders have to say.

The scene we witnessed at Vaermina's shrine … I've never seen anything so horrifying! First Blightcrown sacrificed Master Shelreni. Then her corpse got up and walked through a portal into Apocrypha!\n\nThis is beyond what they taught me as a keeper!
Such disregard for the work of the Great Eye, such rampant destruction! But at least the hole reveals the path our enemies took.\n\nI suppose we should see where it leads.

The twists of fate can be confusing at times, but if Torvesard speaks true, we have to try, proxy. I shall meet you at the Mythos entrance. You shall have my assistance for as long as I am able.\n\nI just … I want to thank Gadayn for his concern.
The corruption. It's spreading and growing stronger. We need to do something, but I'm not sure what.
Was Tho'at Replicanum always here? No, there've been rumors of creature and monster in the archive for a while, but I never encountered them before the maligraphies.
Ah! A dilapidated edifice, retaining an exudation of—never mind. \n\nThe portal in this sunken structure looks promising. I sense the lingering power of the One Who Knows. Go on inside, proxy.
We must observe this memory, proxy.
The instability is a reality tear! I hate being right all the time. We need to learn all we can, so go take a look.\n\nBut do be careful. Nonexistence probably isn't a pleasant experience.
Now that we have the key, let's go unlock the catacombs and find what's left of my cohort. The door is across from the barracks.

It's good to see you, friend. I was surprised when Scruut appeared, and I hoped she would send me somewhere not quite so otherworldly, but I never hesitated. I'm happy to assist you.\n\nStill, if we can avoid those reality tears, I'd be grateful.
Go on. Plunge the blade into the hot coals. If anything is going to restore Abolisher, it's the fires of Boethiah.
Go and find the items I mentioned. I'll prepare the equipment for your return.

I'm Otho, the gardener. Betu must like you if he followed you back. He's a good judge of character, you know. Lady Weatherleah loved him dearly. I worry about what will become of him when all is said and done.

As Mizzik suspected, the imposter may not know about Lady Weatherleah's search for Uriel. Let us keep it that way. Before we close the curtains on his performance, this one wishes to speak with Pelena about the confession's talk of tea.
The Skein showed us that the Mirrormoor wards are on the upper level. We must destroy them to reach Hermaeus Mora's private sanctum. Let us find a way to ascend, proxy.
I've seen many strange wonders since I became tangled up in you and Leramil's business, but this is surely the strangest. I just hope that once we reach the shrine things are a little … drier.

Yes, uh, please come in. Stay for a while. Just pay no mind to the crack in the sky outside or those … shadows? Ignore them and have a drink.\n\nAll right, I can't ignore them either. It all started when the woman at the table by the fire came in.
The threads of fate converge here in West Weald. Yet I cannot untangle them or see where they lead. It is a sign the Prince of Paths walks these lands.

I don't know what's worse—Grivier's family learning what he did to save them or never finding out.\n\nAnyway, not our problem. Let's see if we can find something we can use in Rosalyn's alchemy shop. It's east of the stables.
I didn't come this way before. We'd better be careful here, friend. I have to imagine the Recollection knows about this passage. If they aren't guarding it, something else might be.

Ithelia exiled, Torvesard defeated, but the danger to existence persists. The tears in the fabric of reality, we need to repair them!\n\nHow? I suggested a needle and thread, but my master has a different solution. So he sent me to find you. Again.
I should've known. Scruut never seems to show up with good news, does she? Anyway, I'm ready to help wherever I'm needed.

I had a feeling you'd return soon. The Skein of Secrets changed while I was studying it. The sites I sent you to investigate faded away. I presume you accomplished something at both locations?\n\nTell me, what did you find?

There's more going on here than an attack on the Dawnwood king. This place isn't a settlement, it's a damned fortress! And the Recollection have an army in here!\n\nWe need to look around and figure out what's actually going on here.
Lead the way, comrade. I'm right behind you.

I've been thinking about Ostumir and your investigations with Leramil and Tribune Alea. The Recollection was involved each time. We need to determine what they're planning next.\n\nMaybe the wildburn seed we found in Ostumir can help us do that.
We've reached the shrine. Hold the Lamp close and Leramil says Azura will restore its energy.
Sorilen asked us to meet her at the Ayleid ruins, southeast of the village. Let's head there now. I'm curious to see what she invited me here to show me.
Hush! Can't you see I'm busy blending into my surroundings?
Ithelia's true prison was being forgotten. Once Torvesard remembered her, she escaped this doleful place easily enough. I am confident we can find our way out, too. Look around, proxy.

Ithelia … she is a reflection of me. She knew about Sage's Dream. I remember now. My followers praised me in this chamber while I drank from a goblet.\n\nGather the tirum weed that she offered so we can make the drink.
You've come to the town of Ontus at an unfortunate time, traveler. I myself have only just returned. \n\nComing home to bury one's father is never an easy thing.
We crushed the Daedra's frontal assault and stopped them from getting past the barricade. But the ones who emerged from the barracks—where did they come from?
Oh, Oleander! Divines above, I didn't expect these bastards would go this far.
Walker, that Khajiit … was that the person in need?
Let us head to Khenarthia. Or … what I knew as Khenarthia. Perhaps it is called something different now.\n\nKss. This is going to take some getting used to.

I can't help but notice the drab interior behind you. The office of some minor functionary, I presume? Bogcup certainly loves to burgle.\n\nWere you able to procure any information as to the whereabouts of Snapdragon?
You stopped! Thank you. Vanus Galerion himself said you could help us with this predicament. I don't know what I'd do if I couldn't flag you down.

Now that we have a moment, allow me to introduce myself. Nahlia, Votary knight in the Order of the Lamp. Pleasure to make your acquaintance, you're just as Vanus described you.\n\nIrnard briefed you on our situation?
I hope no one does anything rash until we can calm down these Goblins.
The echo spoke of the east wing. Heed the word of Archmage Ulfsild the Evergreen. Find the lens.
The Gryphon sees power as a weapon, to be pointed at those that might harm the weak. I believe you will offer him insights, new avenues of thought. Especially with the aide of his little friend.

Quite the adventure we're on together, eh? I hear Nahlia's conversation with Archmage Galerion went surprisingly well. \n\nDon't take my word for it though. She'll have much to say on the matter, I'm sure.
Not the first time Nahlia's gotten herself in over her head. I suppose that's why I'm here. To help keep her head above water.
With time and patience, we'll learn everything there is to know about the Luminaries, Scribing, and the Scholarium.\n\nAs long as you're with me, friend.

I don't think I have to tell you that we caused all of this. But it's high time I take responsibility for everything that happened.\n\nCome, friend. Let's search for any sign of Marcan Caelum's whereabouts.
I'll meet with Hooke, as you ask. Although I don't have much reason to enter the Outlaws Refuge these days. May the Eight know my honest intentions!

I'll amble over that way, sure. Hooke can buy me a round or two for my trouble. Of course, if there's really a killer on my tail, and they see me wobbling on the road … eh, I'll just hide in some tall grass.

Adjusting to this new area has been difficult. I had to leave behind many friends and beloved pets in Belkarth. But I suppose I knew that would happen when I came here. Still, I miss those familiar faces.

You've really done it, haven't you? You've gotten the others to donate their power, and the Crow has deemed you worthy. I admit to surprise, pleasant surprise.\n\nThink your way through her trials, mortal. And you'll be just fine.
Hey there, I thought you could use some help tracking down the fable.\n\nIt seems like this Netch has a very distinct sense of humor. I'm willing to play along for now if you are.
Behold! My beauty! My splendor! A gift to you, Not-Ulfsild.\n\nYou have worked hard to find me. I know why, of course. I always know why. Confirm for me please, Ulfsild is gone. Yes?
Poor guy, look at how tense he is. \n\nDon't worry, he's a really good person when he's not mad about being frozen solid for centuries.
You face the Dragon's riddles. I cannot help you, but rest assured her eccentricities are outweighed by her wisdom.\n\nMost of the time.
I'm ready when you are. If past patrols have prepared me, I'd square away what you need to before we head in.
Hyacinth has that look. He thinks he's being very clever right now. And he wants to talk to you, not me.\n\nThat makes me kind of nervous.
Hopefully that disk will give us a glimpse into Hyacinth's dealings with the Ceythalmor. Toss it into the fire, the anticipation is going to give me hives.

I know my idea is strange. But what I felt as I manifested those memories was so strong. Strong, like the bond we share. Like the bond I shared with Wisteria. \n\nWe can use that. I know it. Let's get to the greenhouse and I'll prove it.
I brought you to observe, tamiit. Witness now what I do not have the strength to put into words.
High Cantor Viti remains strong for a cat of her age. Though I suppose I am technically her elder … no matter.\n\nShe knows the situation here. Speak to her, tamiit, and learn what you can.
You should speak to Viti. I might gloat about the Hidden Moon, and that would just ruin this touching moment.
My travels were safe, and I haven't been waiting long. Let us see what Zerith wants to show us about this Ravith-morna.

The longer it takes for this nest of worms to notice us, the safer we'll be. Learn everything you can in here. And if you see their Daedra leader, the one who tried to capture Merric? Hurt it. Hurt it bad.
We're gathering at the Fighters Guild in Shornhelm. I'll summon a portal for easy transit.\n\nCatch up with Prince Azah. I'll meet you there. I have one more person I need to collect first.

Skordo mentioned that your investigatory powers impressed him. Naturally, he didn't phrase it quite that way. He used fewer syllables.\n\nNonetheless, I have confidence that between the two of us, we'll find the entrance to the lair.
My mind is clear and our goal is set. We must find Mezamma and stop the plans of this resurrected Worm Cult. It's what Guildmaster Merric would want to do … if he were still with us.

The more I think about this poetry idea, the more I like it. It's the perfect way to show Guendeline both the strength of my mind and the depth of my passion.\n\nI think I'll call her outside and serenade her in front of the whole town!
Somehow, I had a feeling I'd see you again. Tell me, has Glarikha gotten herself into trouble this time?\n\nOr is it that the duke didn't take kindly to you questioning his decisions?
Don't keep the Phantom waiting. He doesn't like it.
I was … asleep? What am I doing in this hovel? And who are you?\n\nNo, I remember. Stenwick brought me here. I was … sick. Apologies, but I still don't remember who you are.

We'll need to patrol the entire northern perimeter of <<1>>. It's the only way to get a complete picture of the Imperial positions.\n\nOkay, it's not really the only way. If you want to attack them, I'll just wait back at the camp.
Sir Etienne is all right. That puts my mind at ease.\n\nNow I do need your help. This is more of a challenge than I expected.
I don't trust anyone in this town. Why won't they tell me exactly what the cure is? Why can't we leave town afterwards?\n\nAnd if they have a remedy, why can't they tell me what's wrong with Draven?
We are a peaceful town, but we are not without our defenses. I'll ask that you keep on your best behavior while you remain in our village.
You've fought like a true Nord. The skalds will remember your deeds in story and song.\n\nAnd I'll remember you. <<1>> always remembers his friends.
Ah! You see these miserable spirits? They need not suffer this way.
Make your decision.\n\nThese men are already dead. They are beyond mortal concerns.
I don't care anymore. I've lost everything now.\n\nIf you want to stop that monster, you'll need to find Ra-shadda.
Kynareth's blessing, recruit. Do you have the blade?
You've proven yourself worthy of becoming one of our subjects. What is your name?
Did you find <<1>>?\n\nAnd the Fangs … did you get the Fangs of Sithis?
Keep moving, comrade.
The ruins of <<1>> are a dark and dangerous place. Tread carefully, Adept.
I'll be right behind you. Don't worry.
This is our refuge and our sanctuary. We all owe you a debt of gratitude.
Enjoy your stay with the Dancing Scrib. You're as good a friend as anyone's ever been to me.
The audience hall is above us. I'll be there as quickly as I can. If you can challenge the Hound, I'll have time to break through the barrier.
She's running things out of the Guildhall in Davon's Watch at the moment. The Eight guide you, comrade.
Valaste will be expecting you at the Elden Root Guildhall. I'll see you there, Adept.

If you get the civilians to the Fighters Guild, I'll give them weapons and a little training.\n\nIt'll be along the lines of "pointy end goes that way," but that's better than if they just run around panicked.
You'll be known as a friend of the Baandari wherever your travels take you.
It's been one thing after another, lately. Sickness, bandits … I can't remember a fouler time.
I'm sorry, I didn't mean to ignore you. Is there something you need?
No matter what the Phantom decides to do about you, I think you're fascinating.
No time for talk. Kill the draugr!
Oh, hello dearie. Here for the Boast? Of course you are. Everyone wants a chance to visit the Five Finger Dance.
By the moons! You made it through the gate! Who in Oblivion are you?
Bright moons, walker.
We never really got to say thank you, Hallowed. You stood beside us at Rawl'kha. Saw our parents, saw our past. Thank you for your guidance and friendship. It means a great deal to us.
Don't worry about Kalari. Just mulling what she should do next.
That was fascinating, Hallowed! If I had my way the whole Path would be learning about history. Heh, I'd bet if Khali were here she'd be bored silly about now.

Did she tell you? One of the greatest mysteries of Valenwood has finally been solved! Decades of conflicting rumors have been put to rest. \n\nWe finally know what happened to the Blackroot clan! They died … right here in Vullain!
That cistern sounds like our best bet. Let's hope Cadwell knows what he's doing.
Stay sharp out there, and stay clear of their patrols. If you lose your disguise, you'll probably be able to find a new one in one of the houses. Don't worry, you'll do fine.
Bright moons light your path. If I am wrong, you have a thousand of my apologies. But … I do not think I am wrong.
The Harvest Heart has been destroyed and the vampires are no longer a threat to our forces.\n\nAll in all, I'd say we earned our pay this day. Thanks for your help, my friend.
Ahh, it is you. You stood beside the Champions at Fort Grimwatch and drove off the Dro-m'Athra. This one feels the cool light of the moons flowing from your aura.
Fancy meeting you here, my friend! It's good to see you again.
Don't let your eyes deceive you. They trick your senses and tempt your soul.
Bright moons guide your path, traveler.
Let's get inside. The Grotto will be on the other end of the bridge.
The dig site's not too far away. Just around the bend! One of these bends.\n\nI don't mind if you take your time. I'm just happy to be walking again.

Thank you for coming so quickly, champion. \n\nI've been consulting with Countess Hakruba of the Fighters Guild. Both of our guilds believe the time has come to take the fight to Coldharbour, but this places us in a delicate political position.
Finally, we're done. Hopefully we'll get to the fighting soon. Heh, I'd bet if Shazah were here she'd be happy as a cub in moon-sugar about now.
We did it. We got him. Sai's going to be all right. \n\nThank you.
Sahan is injured, but it appears that he can walk on his own. He's stronger than I thought.
We have received the blessings of Stendarr. The door to the Vault of Kings is the only thing that stands between us and the amulet!
That's the last shrine. Let's get the amulet and get out of here!
We aren't in the habit of trusting outsiders, but the suffering of the forest seems to have softened my sister's heart.\n\nIf you really wish to help us, I suppose that's an offer we can't refuse.
Are we finally done with that shrine nonsense? Can we please get what we came for and leave this wretched hole in the ground?

Now you know how this sordid situation began. And you know how I, to my great and everlasting shame, helped Baron Montclair reach the Lightless Remnant.\n\nBut now to more immediate matters. I know where Reezal-Jul can be found.

You have been extremely helpful, Five-Claw. We unraveled the threads of this plot with skill and daring. Like unrolling a spool of yarn. Yarn ….\n\nSorry. This one gets easily distracted sometimes. What were we talking about?
All my best things are at my second camp, through these ruins. \n\nThen we'll need to make our way over to my first camp, by the dig site. Unfortunately, its overrun by Goblins.
We need to clear this portion of the veil so that we can move forward.\n\nSee if you can rip open a tear and shred this illusion.
I don't understand. Arlie loves me. She told me so! And what could the Baroness possibly have to hide in that windmill? I'm so … confused.

Look at this place. How could Grell let it get this bad? He was never what you'd call neat, but he wasn't a slob, either.\n\nHe stocked up on the Maulborn curative, gathered his friends, and was going to ride out the plague. I wonder what happened?
I don't know about you, but I had fun working alongside you. Maybe we can do it again sometime.
I'll stay here and make sure the spawning pools can be used again. Until the Serpent's plans have been thwarted, I'm sure our paths will cross again.
Don't let some overgrown sea-bug get the best of you! Get out there and start cracking. Chop the seam on its back, and don't forget the butter!
Do not tell me Daedra trouble you now? Perhaps it is the sad tale of the Crypt that puts you off. Don't trouble yourself, Undaunted. See this through.

Take the homespun gloves you made and deconstruct them at a clothing station. Let me know when you're done.\n\nYou could deconstruct another piece of clothing—it's fine, as long as you grasp the concept.
Craft a glyph using a rune of potency, essence, and aspect. Return when you have forged intent into form.
Whoever dares oppose the uniting of the Orc clans will feel my wrath!

I think …. Yes, I'm sure it is! This must be the primary tomb's antechamber! Look at that artwork! Definitely from the Nord neo-strife period!\n\nIf this place follows the usual construction, the main burial chamber is right behind that door!

I hope Kharsthun can get Stibbons back to the Mages Guild without dropping him too many times. I'm not sure what they can do if poor Stibbons gets cracked or even shattered.\n\nAnyway, thanks again for your able assistance!
Thanks again for helping me in there. It's good to finally know where I came from.\n\nIf you're ever in Orsinium, look for me. I'm going to apprentice myself to whatever merchant will have me.
Father Egnatius should be arriving any minute. I'll make sure he's comfortable. Well, I can't promise he'll be comfortable, but at least he won't be dead. That's something, right?
These cultists are crazy. They're completely mad.
Still no sign of my assistant. Want to make some more coin? I prefer to work with people who finish the job.

You did it. You did it. Tutor, I can envision all my barons again! I see them so clearly!\n\nPlease, accept your reward. You've earned it, many times over. And now, I must go reconstitute my Barons Who Move Like This!
Welcome, welcome! Come in and see all the wonders that the House of Orsimer Glories has to offer!\n\nOf course, there will be much more to see once all of our exhibits are in place.

It's a shame the only parts of the Maelstrom pocket plane you'll get to see are the arenas. The rest of the realm is a charming gallimaufry of random beasts and biomes from all across Oblivion. It's quite stimulating. \n\nThat is, if you're a Daedra.
Looking for work? If not, move along. I haven't got time for idle chit-chat.
Ah, look who's back! I've got a whole new batch of contracts here if you're looking for work. What do you say? Interested?

I'm so glad you came along! I've chartered a ship—when you're ready, meet me there. Here, I'll mark your map.\n\nBring some lockpicks. They sell them here, if you don't have any. Oh, and wear something warm!
Matron Astara specifically requested your presence in the Sanctuary.\n\nYou need to learn that the Matron doesn't like to be kept waiting.
Once again the pious idiots of Kvatch dare to provoke the anger of the Dark Brotherhood. Such an insult cannot be allowed to stand unchallenged!
Don't dawdle, Assassin. I gave you a job and I expect you to handle it.
I don't know about you, but I had fun working alongside you. Maybe we can do it again sometime.

Speak to my seneschal, Little Leaf. You'll find her to the east, along the road through the northeast passage between Upper and Lower Craglorn.\n\nI would be eternally grateful if you make sure no harm befalls her during her mission.
You should really talk to the Archcanon. He knows much more about Lord Vivec's … situation … than I do.
Don't come back with some incurable disease, you hear? I'd hate for it to start spreading around camp.
Overseer Shiralas supervises the construction of the unfinished ziggurat. I'm sure she'll let you borrow the Blessing Stone for Lord Vivec, provided you ask nicely.

Is this why you sneak through our camp, to desecrate our sacred rites? Do the slaves of the false gods fear us so much they won't even face us themselves?\n\nWhy are you here, outlander? Answer truthfully and I may only hobble you.

Do you require supervision already? Very well, let me ponder the particulars ….\n\nMy instincts tell me you should look for some sort of ancient inscription. Or maybe you should just read that book over there.

I've been thinking about my brother's claim that he's the Nerevarine since we last spoke. No matter how I try, the word tastes false on my tongue.\n\nAnd now I fear he's about to convince the Wise Woman that his quest for power will benefit the tribes.

My friend! Raz is happy to see you, but surprised you didn't help me with these creatures. Not that Raz needed any help.\n\nYou must tell me what brought you to Summerset … after you agree to assist Raz with his usual cloak-and-dagger business.

Glad to see that my calculations and speculations proved correct. I assumed you'd eventually show up here, and as usual the Great Mage was right.\n\nNow come closer. We have much to discuss, you and I.

Ah, friend of Valsirenn. You're just in time. This pearl resists our ritual. It's reluctant to give up its secrets.\n\nI believe your assistance will be required to unravel this mystery, provided you're willing to help.
Well, there it is. Take a look for yourself.

I see no gryphons in this area, do you? Pity. You may have to range a bit farther afield to find a decent feather. I'd suggest searching the lake behind Rellenthil. I leave the means of acquisition up to you.

Greetings, my friend! Fancy meeting you all the way out here.\n\nPerhaps you could help me once more? I need an escort for my expedition. I expect we'll encounter some Daedra along the way, but I'm sure it's nothing you can't handle.
Let's hurry. Whatever's going on here, I don't want Lotus to be a part of it.

See that whirlpool? The currents are being drawn into the flooded ruins beneath Sea Keep. We should be able to follow them inside, just as the Sea Elves did. It's that or we drown.\n\nIf you want to back out. I understand.

So you'll be joining us? Good. Call me Lorne. No need for flowery titles. We Altmer have too many names already.\n\nI'm glad you're here. Outsiders often make the best admanens. A fresh pair of eyes will be essential here. More essential than usual.
I suppose I'm ready. As long as you're ready, that is. You are ready, right? Of course you are. You're always ready.
We can only hope that no lesser mages have discovered these staff fragments. Even a single piece could prove dangerous.
Are you prepared for your next task? I'm afraid we need to quicken the pace.\n\nWas that too pushy? Sorry, I'm just a bit anxious, you know?
Good luck finding those fragments!\n\nCan you believe we'll have all eight soon? Remarkable!
Are you prepared for one last journey to Tamriel? I believe our final success is nearly at hand.

While I've never visited an Outlaws Refuge myself, I have it on good authority that all manner of ne'er-do-wells frequent such places. Scoundrels, black marketeers, and smugglers of ill repute!\n\nJust the sort of company that Margus keeps.

I am glad you've taken an interest in our cause. Concordia and Famia know the ruins. I know Murkmire's swamps and rivers. And you know how to get things done! The four of us will accomplish great-great things!
Thank you for your efforts thus far, and your achievements to come.\n\nI have business in Alten Meerhleel—perhaps we can reconvene there once you've made your inquiries with Xukas.
I'm sorry … spiders are just the worst part of the job. I'm afraid I'll be of no use down there. Varo needs our help, though! Please, do what you can!

You look surprised. I told you, I swim like a harpoon-fish. Typically a nap follows, but that will have to wait.\n\nYou found Jaxsik. Good. All are warned of Kassandra's treachery. Many Saxhleel come to aid us, but they will arrive too late, I think.

Here already? You are swift, ojel, I will give you that. But enough flattery, I think. From now on, all is war-talk.\n\nWe seek the grave-stakes of several Dead-Water kaals … and vengeance. I know how we can claim both.
Oh, my, Haxara … she's not still angry with me, is she?
I'm not here to talk. You wanna talk to someone, talk to Kassandra.
Ojel. I hiss fire! I nearly caught that lukiul hag, Kassandra, but Blackguards emerged from all sides. Tsojei and I cannot kill these greels fast enough. We will never catch up at this rate!\n\nKaoc!
Mind your step, please. If you disturb the mud, I'll have to start my search all over again.
Something touches my ears, but it is very faint. Focus on that prayer-stone, beeko. I know the Hist has something to tell us.

Take the big adept and go to the Greenleaf Farm. You must convince them to seek the protection of the city walls before the Usurper Queen's forces arrive.\n\nMeanwhile, I have other preparations to check on.

You know, the legend of Khunzar-ri is more interesting than I remember. It must be Moon-Singer Mizbina's delivery. Marginally entertaining.\n\nShe made the location of the next triangulant quite clear to one of exceptional intellect. Such as myself.
The Scar can be a treacherous place, five-claw, even without the addition of a Nibenese assassination squad.\n\nWe need to hurry, but we should also proceed with caution.
This scrap of cloth. Vazbi knows it well. It is part of a S'rendarr adept's habit. One of the old ones we don't wear anymore.\n\nCould an adept have been out here?
Greetings, walker. Any luck with Ishu? This one was hoping for more information.

I learned the stories of Khunzar-ri from my mother. Did I tell you she was a moon-singer before she married my father? She said the pendant once belonged to Anequina.\n\nI am related to Anequina. Direct descendent, according to the Moon-Priests.

We also need Tasnasi's old crew. Vole, Sereyne, and Nazdar.\n\nVole just did a job for Jubani. He'll be at her junk shop. Sereyne's likely at the Goiter's Gulp. And Nazdar … caterwauling somewhere. We'll meet in the Bowel at the bottom of the Scar.
These old barrels smell like wine. Maybe brandy? Might have started as fresh fruit as long as they've been left here. Gone now, whatever it was.\n\nShame. I could use a stiff drink right now.

Your kindness reminds Nazdar of the love Dashing Dasalzo had for the Stitches in life. This one recalls many joys in the company of Tasnasi and the others. He would like to feel them again.\n\nNazdar will go where Tasnasi bids.

Euraxia seeks to divide our attention, what with Dragons and undead and such. Well, never pick more than one pocket at a time, I always say. Save Riverhold, then deal with the rest.\n\nBut tell me, what did you learn at the Desert Wind Adeptorium?
An elderly Alfiq? That's a stroke of good fortune. Few Khajiit speak with more wisdom than an Alfiq Clan Mother.\n\nSpeak with her, but try to be diplomatic. Remember, we're the intruders.

The power of Hidden Moon rests in your heart now, child. Walk the path with humility and compassion. But in times of darkness, do not hesitate to mete out Azurah's wrath.\n\nRedemption waits on the far side of war. Arum-Khal is proof of that.
Go, find J'dathal. Raz will see to the injured farmhand.

Hey there, good looking. I hope Ak'an and Eljhan didn't give you too much trouble. They're both wanted by the city guard, so I doubt we'll be seeing them in a reputable establishment like this.\n\nNow, ready to make more gold than you've ever seen?

Hello! Rigurt was just asking this merchant which mound of colored powder he should eat first. Rigurt says red. Merchant says please go away. We find ourselves as stale mates.\n\nBut Rigurt has bigger problems than what to eat for lunch.
Kaalgrontiid! I recognize that monster's voice from our encounter at Jode's Core. We need to find him!

It appears this sanctuary has fallen into ruin, blocking our path to the archives.\n\nAs the Dragonguard say, every path is worthy of pursuit. Though it seems the path we seek is a rather tricky one. Hmm.
My friend, you're just in time. I'd rather not face my old companion without someone I trust nearby.

That Dragon has no sense of propriety. Flying off without so much as a "by your leave!"\n\nWithout him or Tharn, we'll need to devise our own method for reaching Dragonhold, but by the Sword Saints, I have no idea what that might be.
Za'ji certainly has a flair for the dramatic.
The Passage of Dad'na Ghaten is just through the overgrowth to the right of the Wall.\n\nLet's put an end to this once and for all.
That was … intense. Anequina did not so much as show me her memories … she spoke through me.\n\nAnd her words, five-claw. They were directed at you.
The great Dragon flew off, taking our most obvious means of conveyance to the floating island with him.\n\nIf Za'ji has to walk all the way, he will be one unhappy pirate.
Without the old wizard or the relatively friendly Dragon, we must rely on ourselves to solve this dilemma.\n\nFrankly? I don't like our chances.
Sai Sahan needs you back at the Dragonguard Sanctum.
Clan Mother Tadali may still be upset with Za'ji, but she came across as very wise. I'm sure she'll help us if we explain the situation.
Damned ropes! You want to give me a hand here? I'm not going to bite you or anything. Orc's honor.
You should go on ahead and travel to this sentry tower.\n\nMeanwhile, I'll discuss our battle plans with General Renmus. We'll meet with you as soon as we can.
This is the place. Can't say I know what Reach witches would be doing here, but the Skald-King's scouts have never sent me on a wild guar chase before.\n\nLet's see if the trek out here was worth it.
My education involved combat training, though I never mastered the finer points. I still remember my lessons. I'll do my best to guide you through this.
Swordthane Uthlet … what a good soldier. I'll remember what he's done for us this day.

Well, we've both been over the headstones with a fine-toothed comb.\n\nIf we can determine why the coven dug up these particular bodies, it will tell us something about how the medallions were enchanted.
We got what we need from this camp. And since Fenn and Svana are already on their way back to Solitude, we might as well head there, too.\n\nGo on. I'll meet you at the Blue Palace.
The court wizard survived, so there's still hope that the jarl did, too, right? Let's check the cellar.
The captain said that dais is how she amplifies her power! You must do something to disrupt it!
Looks like they dragged whoever showed up for the promised wealth downstairs. At least one of them put up a fight. Well, always follow the blood.\n\nLet's continue our search in the basement.

Edjar looks a little worse for wear. I'll make sure he makes it to the Lightless Hollow.\n\nVampire allies, now werewolves. I can imagine what Sai would think. Worse, I know what Abnur Tharn would say.
That's Rada al-Saran, but where's my father?

You heard Lyris. We need to find the ritual site. I'll go with you. \n\nIf the harrowstorm will be as large as Svargrim claimed, the ritual site must be equally enormous. It shouldn't be too difficult to spot.
That bastard's right in front of us, but he might as well be in Windhelm, for all the good it will do!\n\nTalk to him. Distract him. Fenn and I will try to deal with the barrier.
Poor Eivina. I pray that the high priest can remove this strange affliction.\n\nI just hope we don't find more victims of this unnatural storm as we head toward the temple.
See what the sentry has to say. If he doesn't cooperate, I can always hit him with my axe.
Well, I don't recognize you and you're not a Reachman. How did you find your way down here? Don't tell me you came just to pick our town's bones.
Our hard work has paid off. Finding all the instruments, posting all those flyers.\n\nAll right, I admit it was mostly you. Perhaps the college will make you an honorary bard?

The culprit clearly went through that trap door … but the Overseer was adamant about keeping us out of the mines. \n\nI don't see what choice we have. If we are to solve this disturbing mystery, we must press on!
Didn't I send you to Solitude? This place isn't safe!\n\nThe Icereach Coven performed a ritual and summoned one of those harrowstorms. Now Kilkreath Temple is crawling with harrowfiends!

An intricate plot by the Reachmen. This doesn't bode well for Western Skyrim. I need to warn Solitude.\n\nAfter this, they have to provide the support we were promised long ago. For their own sake, if not for ours.
Gods … what a disaster. The queen's been assassinated and Svargrim still refuses to listen to reason.\n\nWe need to find a way to set things right.
I'm going to tend to the victim's body. You go on ahead. I'll be right behind.
Thulsgreg seems anxious to talk to you. Go on and speak with him. I need to hear the truth.
If we don't have tradition, what do we have?
If you're looking to rob me, I'm afraid I have nothing of value.\n\nI'm merely out here searching for my grandfather, Keldnyr.
Rigurt has been trying to get Thane Hraldi to listen to him, but the thane wants nothing but fishing!\n\nIt's the worstest sport, friend. Just standing and fishing. There's not even a ball!

Let me guess—another array of tiresome clues? Ugh. Do you have any idea how many clues I've worked through thus far? That bottle-nonsense from before? That was just one of many chapters in this ridiculous saga!\n\nEnough grousing. Out with it.
You're back! I'm so glad to see you. I hope it wasn't too dangerous. I feel like I should have gone with you, but I probably would have slowed you down.\n\nOh, the rubbings. Did you get them?
It makes so much sense! The riddle. Only those worthy can find the way to safety … only vampires and werewolves can see these sigils! That explains why no one ever found anything.
This is where Rada and Lady Belain entered the structure, but I can't find any way to open the doors. I suspect this may be why they needed the keystone.

The Dark Heart … the episodes grow more frequent. Each time the currents swell, it's like I'm losing myself to the darkness.\n\nWe must uncover Rada's plans before that happens. Perhaps this coded message will tell us more about the Darkstorm.

Remember, get keys off the patrolling vampires or find another way to get inside. Either way, let's get into the archive, find this Nighthollow Testament, and get back to Verandis, all right?\n\nI'll scout around on my own and catch up to you.
Keep up your guard. We don't know what Mannimarco might have left behind, or the Dwarves for that matter.

May I suggest trying to reach the void portal at the top of that tower first? It seems like a good vantage point to survey the layout of this ruin.\n\nI'm sure you'll figure out a way past the blockage in no time.

I sensed that Lady Belain was ancient, but the vision confirms she was not only part of the Nighthollow clan—she was their leader! The Dark Heart gets more interesting at every turn. How did they drink from it? For that matter, what did they drink?

They're protective wards, all right. Count Verandis once used something similar to guard an evil vampire clan's storehouse of dangerous relics until we could destroy them.\n\nLet's go deactivate the other crystals.

Adusa has scouted these ruins and come up with a plan. This one will barge in through the front door, confront Boss Trenlor, and try to determine where Kathad is.\n\nMeanwhile, you go in through the sluice gate along the wall to the southwest.

Good to see you, my friend. I could use an ally in this desolate place. The Gray Host has turned its attention upon the Reach, but the local ruler refuses my help. This so-called Despot of Markarth thinks walls and sentries will hold back their fury.
Come on, harrier, let's keep searching. Dwarven ruins don't find themselves, you know.
There must be something here that can tell us what's become of the vateshran.
This whole situation makes me so angry! I don't want to talk to you anymore, outsider.
I don't know what you're doing in this terrible place, friend, but would you oblige an old man and undo these bindings? Those damned hagravens were talking about flaying the skin from my bones!

Thankfully, these duplicates lack even Stibbons's pitiful amount of drive and coordination. It shouldn't have wandered very far. Once you find it, you need to induce it to return. Try mentioning my name. They seem attracted to me for some odd reason.

Tell Sombren and the twins I'll be with them shortly. I have a few more details to work out with the governor. After that, go see Captain Rian and then meet me at Fort Redmane. But don't take too long. I'd rather you were there when the cult attacks.

Damn it! Looks like we were both too late. It's just like I expected when we found that list with all the councilors' names on it. I hate being right when somebody dies.\n\nGlad to see you made it here, by the way. Did you happen to see who killed her?

You're not a Covenant soldier or one of those damn cultists—you're … you!\n\nBy Bazrag's chilly nethers, am I glad to see you! Between the soldiers and the cultists, this is almost as bad as that business in Orsinium. But what are you doing here?
Prisoners? What exactly is going on here?\n\nWe'd better help them.

Despite appearances, Xynaa is a friend. She took me in and mentored me. Taught me to control my power when I thought it was going to tear me apart. She's the only reason I'm standing here today.\n\nTalk to Xynaa. She'll explain everything.
Thank you for listening. I feel better now. I don't think I'll try to summon my flames again until I know I can control them.

Sombren's mentor is a Dremora? I remember they brought Daedra into our sanctum sometimes to teach us about Oblivion and the Princes, but I never expected to meet one out here.\n\nI guess you should talk to her and see if she can actually help us.
Ugh. I can hear Tiras's cries like he's right here beside me!\n\nI deserve it, don't I? A shameful, ghostly reminder of my failure ….
Ugh, my skin still feels like I've got a thousand tiny spiders biting me. That was horrible.\n\nOh, and thank you. I don't know what someone like you is doing here, but I won't argue with providence.
That drawbridge is the only way across the chasm. We need to find a way to lower it into place.
She's not looking so good. Can you do something? I've got some herbs, but they'll only dull the pain.
You found Duchess Astella's notes that quickly? Thank Ruptga I can rely on your eyes. Can barely see a thing in this place!\n\nWhat do they say?
You're awake! Good. It's been awhile since I've worked any magic that didn't involve sleight of hand.\n\nAnnyce is still soundly asleep. Could you not get through to her in the dream?

I assume this will satisfy your masters in Leyawiin? The Dark Brotherhood is not your enemy.\n\nThe Order of the Waking Flame invaded our sanctuary and killed my brothers and sisters. I can't let them get away with that.
Three alive, I can't look at him. Can you see if—if there's anything left of him in there?
Farrul Lupus is … dead? I … I can't believe someone killed him over some secret.\n\nCan you talk to Renna? I'm not very good at condolences.
Come on, then. Let's face this thing before I lose my nerve!
You saw that ghostly killer flapping their hands about, right? Do you think you can repeat those gestures? I didn't quite follow, but it looked like magic to me.

Is that her? I wish I remembered her better. \n\nYou know, she might think I ignored the letter she sent years ago—and she might feel hurt by that. Why don't you talk to her? Ask if she's the Inalieth who once worked for the Hallix family.

Now that you have the creature, go stand over there and release it in my direction. Your life energy and my spell will hold it in place until I can commune with the spirit itself. Come now, let's hurry!
I thought I heard that Khajiit mention Onimiril. Let's have a chat with him.

I want to apologize. I never should have went with Sombren and Calia. Never put all of us in that situation. I just wanted answers, you know? \n\nWhat happened at the end. I still can't believe I did that.
That hole certainly looks wide enough for us to slip through. I can't see the other side, but I say we take the chance. Can't see any better options.\n\nHope you don't mind tight spaces.
Well, the wisp led us to this door. Let's go through it and see what's inside.
I don't want to tell you what to do, but please be careful with those stones. They look … erratic. \n\nYou may be the Magician. But for someone like me, holding onto erratic power seems unwise?

We stopped Celdina's ritual and forced her to retreat to Burning Gyre Keep. There, instead of allowing her to summon Nokvroz's promised army, we defeated her Incarnate. Now she's on the run, back to her Riven Cataclyst.\n\nThat device intrigues me.

That Incarnate was a worthy foe, mortal master. Next time you face one, you must promise to let me out of your pack. I want to show you how Arox the Mutilator destroyed the Banekin Brigade at Dreadfire Cove.
I have had few dealings with Kynmarcher Jynd. But I have … reservations … about any Dremora who dabbles in mortal inventions. It is an unseemly habit.

I mentioned a necrologist. Miksotet's the one. If the shell holds clues, he can find them. His ritual requires your aid. I promised you would give it.\n\nFirst, tell me what you learned. Did a mortal see what happened?

The prisoner roll indicates Elegian is detained in a cell called the Durance Vile. And the map shows the Durance Vile to be in the southwest portion of the prison. We just need to get over there and then we can talk to Elegian.
The first Incarnate we ran into was bad enough. I'm not eager to meet another one, let alone an army of the things. We'd better stop Sister Celdina and the Waking Flame while we still can.
My scouts did not notice this passage. Perhaps the daedrat is useful after all. Or his nose is, anyway.
There has to be a way to get inside the bathhouse. Keep looking.
I know most people would not want to go to a place that has earned the name The Blood Pit. But I feel a sense of urgency, that I should go there.
We should make our way to the Shambles at once. There's no guarantee that the Ebony Blade will remain in that vault for long.
I heard what Gilfrex said. It's off to the False Martyrs' Folly for this Slave Choker, I suppose. Lovely.

Valessea apprised me of the situation. I believe I know the place where she thinks they're holding Quentyn. It must be the crypts below Abhain Chapel, on the northern shore of the loch.\n\nWill you accompany us on this rescue mission, my dear?

This basket is the sum of our collaborative efforts. Your diligent work and the mastery of my craft displayed in one precious gift for the one who most deserves the fruits of our labor. \n\nIn Zenithar's name, set it aflame.
You've got a key? Wonderful!
How could my mother do this? She should have known better, I'm not some prize!

Finding the loot might not be as easy as it sounds. A lot of ships vanished here besides my ancestor's, and Ghost Haven Bay is supposed to be haunted, if that weren't obvious from the name.\n\nLet's start by searching for signs she was really here.

I have not felt pain in so long. How cruel a villain who causes suffering in an innocent spirit! Before, I was defending Lady Garick's honor. Now, mine is at stake.\n\nSince you passed the Trial of Wits, you may proceed. With one alteration.

The dockmaster's home overlooks the harbor to the west. Jakarn and I will meet you there.\n\nFirst Quentyn, now this. I hardly know who to trust. Times like these, I take a moment to contemplate the Colossus in the harbor. It helps clear my thoughts.

Hopefully we can find evidence that leads to the source of the corruption. Archdruid Agathie will never turn against one of our circle without absolute proof of recklessness or wrongdoing.\n\nCome, let us look around the village.
All right, we're here. We need to find a sturdy chopping block. It won't be pretty, but it will work for what we need.

I forgot to put an enchantment on Huldressa to protect her from the magic. Don't look at me like that! It wasn't on purpose. \n\nThese motes are becoming a real knot in my tail. I'll work on these traps while you rifle through Magister Irin's things.

Fair day to you, friend of Caska. I don't believe we've had the pleasure, but you look like a true hero of the Dominion.\n\nI am Ayrenn Arana Aldmeri. You have my apologies, I must stink worse than a barrel of rotmeth right now.

My friend! What a turn of fate to meet you here, of all places. I didn't accidentally banish you to Amenos, did I? No, of course not. I'd remember if I saw your name on one of those prison writs.\n\nBut what are you doing here, pray tell?

They came here because of the vents! The Ascendant Magus wanted to experiment with harnessing volcanic power even after his missteps at Stonelore Grove. But what does he need such power for?\n\nIf only the rest of the note wasn't burned!
Lady Arabelle said she didn't want me to miss all the fun. \n\nSilly me. Skulking around a graveyard looking for people who want to kill me. That's clearly better than anything else I could be doing.
That fool should be near … oh, look up.

I can't believe <<1>> got himself arrested! Ha! That will be some story. Now we just have to find <<2>> and convince her to pay her portion of the bill from last night. <<3>> seemed pretty angry about it all!
Go. Tell father what happened here. I need to finish the song. \n\nSee you at the mine when I'm done?

The book I snuck into the keep to read indicated that the keys are hidden in the jungle—one in the south, the other in the west. They even provided a map!\n\nWould you like to hear the legend concerning the vault? It really is quite riveting.
Let's see what Azamel has to say. I'm not exactly optimistic about our chances of finding Song through this drunkard, but right now it's all we've got. \n\nI really hope this isn't a wild guar chase.
If Captain Marso is being held in some dungeon we have to save him.\n\nI've known that man for years. I won't leave him to moulder in some cell.
I'm one of the youngest captains in the Veloise fleet. But know, I take my responsibilities seriously.
My darling Janne, seeing you makes my loins stir and my—ouch!

While we know it as All Flags Islet, it was originally referred to as Monument Islet. Intended to serve as a memorial, the place was abandoned when the undead claimed the island.\n\nThe plaques in this lighthouse tell some of the story.

Hey! If it isn't my new old friend! Found the place easy enough, eh? Pull up a chair, have a drink! As long as you're buying, of course. I'm, uh … well, I'm a little light in the purse at the moment.\n\nSo, you talk to Razhamad yet?

Greetings, my friend, and welcome to the Gonfalon Gaming Hall! Please, drink and make merry! We have many strong players gracing the hall today—lots of action. Tales of Tribute is free to watch but far more fun to play.\n\nDo you play, wayfarer?

Hey, it's our newest recruit! You made the right choice signing up here. The Gonfalon chapter's produced some of the best Tribute players in … well, Gonfalon Bay!\n\nThat's why we're bound to start winning again! Eventually.
