Eager to begin the next tournament? Then I have good news! The Roister's Club just sent word that our new opponents will arrive soon!\n\nWe have time, though. I imagine they are in no hurry to face defeat at the hands of our chapter's newest prodigy.

The mark on the map is quite clear. Shouldn't be too hard to find that spot in Hag Fen. I wonder what's there.\n\nI'm sick of being one step behind those blighted cowards. First they tried to take our sacred seed and now this? What does it all mean?

What do the Firesong know that we don't? Dogs and sons of dogs. Let's not waste any more time. We have to get to Wyress Tola.\n\nDruid Laurel and I will meet you at this cave in Hag Fen with full sails and a strong wind.
I'll see you at the Telling Stone, my friend. It's something every visitor to Galen should see at least once before they leave the island.
We'll take it from here—you're needed up the coast, sailor.\n\nWhen you're finished with the work Stefan Mornard gave you, report back to him in Vastyr. I expect I'll see you there.

All right. Get ready. I don't do this very often, so pay attention. You did good, five-claw. I'm proud to have fought by your side and I'm even prouder to call you my friend.\n\nThat's it, enough. If I get any more sentimental, I may start crying.
Poison! You must find who would do such a thing to Lady Arabelle!\n\nZa'ji and Caska will not leave her side. You have my word on that!

A crystal such as a Shard of the Green. Some ancient druid sites could only be reached by placing the proper shard into a locking mechanism. I wonder ….\n\nLook around. The locking mechanism could be anything.
Take the key. We might need it to reach the alchemist's garden.
Pay heed to Captain Siravaen, my friend! This is her element, not mine.
If you intend to go to Y'ffelon with the rest of us, climb in the skiff. The Mad Maiden's anchored just around the point.\n\nOtherwise, it's a long swim.
The door is open. Let us enter and hear the song.
There's something wrong, but I don't know what. I'm just different. It's like my mind is ….\n\nOoh, feel that? It's going to storm later. You can tell by the energy in the air.

You're willing to help? That's perfect! I'm not really sure about Druid Fenas, and Octin usually handles the logistics. I was worried I was going to have to rely on myself, and that never turns out well.\n\nTalk to the druid. See if he has any ideas.

I can't keep chasing after Umindior. We have a job to finish. Good thing I partnered up with someone competent.\n\nLet's get back into Llanshara and find that magic-infused cloth Veshin described. The gorgeous, sensual Veshin.
Outsider, this is the Chronicle. The spirit we communed with. But it's grown dark. Can you feel the anger radiating from it? The sadness?\n\nI don't like the look of this.
Please. Not yet.\n\nAt least bring me the water. I'm parched. And sleepy.

Head to Broken Oar Cove and retrieve the everflame torch. There's a path to the east that leads down to the shore. Then meet me at the beacon at Veil's Bluff.\n\nBe careful. Our enemy is as thick as weeds once you leave the safety of this village.
Examine the evidence and I shall do the same. We must determine what befell Mildanor.

High Priest Trilam will be your point of contact at the shrine. He seems insistent the Khajiit are involved in the heist somehow. I have a feeling they're only guilty of poor timing.\n\nMeet me back here when you're done.

Ulfengar is right to be concerned. The Consortium might very well try to sell these tainted eggs, but I can fight bureaucracy with bureaucracy. Even if they fire me, I'll make sure these eggs never make it to Necrom without a proper cleansing.

Fate has noticed your talent for altering destiny. Reality hangs in the balance, as does the future of Apocrypha and Nirn. Hence, I bring a message from Hermaeus Mora, the One Who Knows.\n\nMora offers you a purpose. An aspiration dark and heavy.
This is all so strange. A little exciting, but also nerve-wracking. I'll meet you at the Necrom Bindery, friend.

That creature, Uxunath, she leads these invaders. We know her reputation—savage and impatient. No wonder she managed to take the Cenotaph by force.\n\nTo use her own vestige as fuel for the ritual presents a massive risk.

Thank you! I fled from ghosts and Daedra when I came ashore, and heard one of them call it Fathoms Drift. I will not leave this place before I've tracked down my father and our ship. Surely he survived the storm!
There is a plot here to undermine my Prince and somehow Meenai-Shai found himself in the middle of it all.
We shouldn't wait to reset the focus. Huzmargo does not know what will happen if the Rectory remains discombobulated, but he doubts it's good for the vessels!

The threads of fate draw both of us to this place, proxy. Tel Rendys. Once the home of a powerful Telvanni magister named Meln the Mouthless, but now abandoned. From what I could ascertain, no one knows what happened to the wizard of this tower.

I scouted ahead. That campsite is crawling with the mercenaries that attacked me. Seems like they're searching or waiting for … something.\n\nBut that got me thinking. Why would those mercenaries be after both me and Reynila?

This is a terrible development. If the Hidden Kindred know about the Tranquil Catalog, then they know it contains an index of every secret and bit of knowledge stored in Apocrypha.\n\nQuestion the scribe and find out what happened here.

Delmon was her husband. That's right. I must have heard it from her once. Long ago, when she first brought me on. He died from the Knahaten Flu—the thing she's trying to cure.\n\nI've never seen her like this before.
Please, just give me a moment to grieve.

Hmm. Drab attire, sharpened blades, a dangerous glint in the eye. An adventurer, I take it? I could use someone with your particular skill set. Let's speak for a moment. I promise to make it worth your while.

Congratulations, you're my new Folsi. First, go to the servants quarters to the west and ask Aki-go about the spy. Then visit the Dres camp to the south and see if they have any connection to this Tredecim.\n\nI need to keep watch here, just in case.
The Obscured Forum is too big! Ugh, why can't you summon portals? Hezehk's can only fit one person.\n\nI don't want to leave your side. Too dangerous. For you. So, we search on foot. Miserable.
Senalana, kill the Starflower, then meet at Arenthia.\n\nLet's move quickly. Dimik-ei's been on the leash of that rotten skeever for too long. She deserves the sun on her scales again.

Exhausting but superlative work, cohort. Now that we have the anchors, we will transform them into a weapon. A means to unmoor the adversary from my fateline.\n\nSuch magic would normally be a lengthy and unstable process.

Spiders sit in the eaves and listen in on private conversations. They know everything. Like how to find the dormitory door. Ha, dormitory. Door-mitory. \n\nWell? What are you waiting for? Ask the spiders.
Leramil needs to know what happened at the conclave and the Vaermina shrine. \n\nYou tell her, friend. I'm too nervous to speak coherently.
More of Blightcrown's corruption. We're going the right way.\n\nOh, if I suddenly turn violent and attack you, it's nothing personal.
I concur with Gadayn. I sense no deception from Torvesard. Strange … I sense nothing at all. An effect of the corruption, perhaps?\n\nSpeak with him. What other choice do we have?
I rarely have a reason to walk across the bottom of the sea, but it does have a certain beauty. Let us proceed, proxy.
Use the Echonir, proxy. If any recent memories of Ithelia remain, they may tell us where she and Torvesard have gone.

Do you know what that mortal just described? A tear in reality! If that's the instability I sensed, then no wonder my tentacles are quivering!\n\nI suppose we need to go into that cave and take a look. You first.
I'm pretty sure that's the statue Gaius marked on his map.\n\nSearch around it for any place he could have hidden the catacombs key. Maybe a secret compartment.
That wasn't so difficult. When you see Leramil again, tell her that I asked about her. I mean, if she brings it up.
The entrance to Boethiah's forge should be somewhere in the northeast section of the mine.
These workers must be some of the subjects Gallio mentioned in his journal. They're on the verge of turning into bloodfiends. \n\nI might be able to mix a counteragent with the proper ingredients.
Oh, are you helping the investigator? We could certainly use the help finding Betu! He's usually better behaved when we have guests around. I think I heard some barking along the outer wall.
Could Otho have assisted in poisoning Lady Weatherleah? He made no mention of serving tea that day. Another thread to pursue in the search for the truth.
Ithelia had Torvesard place and hide wards to seal the door to the sanctum, proxy. See if the Skein can lead us to these unseen wards.
I admit, I was sincerely hoping that Leramil could just conjure a portal to take us to the right spot. I'm not eager to meet any of the creatures that call those depths their home.
I just wanted a nice inn where I could serve normal customers. Instead, I got a mysterious woman, wandering shadow people, and cracks in the sky.
I knew Balandrus was angry when I left the gang. But to destroy a town and raise an army ….\n\nHe's really trying to live up to his new name—the Terror of the Weald.
Things look different from what I remember, but I'm sure I'll recognize the right path as soon as I see it.\n\nLet's keep moving.
Beragon calls that collection of parchment and bindings in his townhouse a library? He really ought to let me reorganize them from pointless to even more pointless.
I'll be glad when this is over and that Watchling finally stops entering my townhouse unannounced. All those eyes and squirming tentacles are … unnatural!

If we had taken a little longer to get here, that wildburn seed would have … what? Sprouted? Exploded? Whatever you call it, it would have been just like Ostumir. The beginning of another new forest!\n\nTalk to Beragon while I deal with my rage.
The more I learn about the Recollection, the less I understand their motives and intentions. It's all secrets within secrets.
The shrine to Azura should be on the east side of the lumber camp. Let's go find it.

Such a relief to find Sorilen safe and sound. We grew up together, you know. And though we lead very different lives, we still exchange letters from time to time. She's a good friend.\n\nLet's finish searching for other survivors before we go meet her.

Ah, my old assistant! An unexpected occurrence, but a welcome one. I need some help exploring the nearby ruins of Wendir. You may not think yourself capable of such a task, but worry not, for I'll be with you every step of the way.

Another trap! I have no idea if Ithelia is aware of us, but Shardmarshal Vargas certainly is. I doubt she plans to release us any time soon … if ever.\n\nAt least the Echonir has something to show us. Let us see what we can learn from this memory.

Another Ithelia? Another … me? She wishes to speak to you. Perhaps she has answers we seek. \n\nAsk her about Sage's Dream, mortal. Ask her why the very thought of it spins within the storm in my mind.
Something is very wrong in the town of Ontus. I feel it in my bones.
More Daedra, emerging from the north door. That leads to the barracks beneath the keep. How did they get in there?\n\nNo matter. Let's go deal with this, comrade.
This place has a bad feeling to it. We need to find Wisteria and Oleander, quick as we can.

Thank you, walker. Watch for the spirit of a little cat. Azurah often sends such messengers when the need is great.\n\nAnd do be careful. Rumor has it that Moonmont is overrun with dro-m'Athra. May Azurah keep the dark from ensnaring your spirit.
Let us deal with this Rajaska before it is too late for the other rithantiin. We can talk later.
Thank you again. For saving me. It was quite the sight, you and Bogcup dealing with my captors.\n\nThrilling, even. I imagine your adventures with Bogcup are similarly exhilarating.

You stopped! Thank you, adept. I've been asked to find one of our more adventurous members, someone that could lend a situation fresh eyes.\n\nYou look like just the person to help with our predicament.
Now that we have a moment, allow me to introduce myself. Nahlia, Votary knight in the Order of the Lamp. Pleasure to make your acquaintance, adept.\n\nIrnard briefed you on our situation?
The echo at the base of the altar is just one of many. Much of the Scholarium's knowledge has been lost to time.\n\nBut, if Magnus wills it, Ulfsild's preparations should be enough to see us through.

The Dragon and I have spoken the most since Ulfsild took her leave. She thinks me pompous, talks in riddles, but it is time well spent, I think.\n\nYou have the strength to find the worth in her whorls of logic and thought, adventurer.
Plenty to do in a place of this size. Corridors to patrol, books to organize. Keeps me busy! Though likely not as busy as you.
I'm sure it doesn't look like you're interrupting me, but you are. \n\nI've got things to tend to, and I'm sure you do too.

It's good to be back! I know it took some time to get us all down here, apologies.\n\nArchmage Galerion and the Votary Commander needed significant convincing to turn this into a full-fledged expedition. How did it go with the Crow?
Caelum Vineyard isn't much more than a ruin these days. But everything goes back to that place, that night. I have a feeling Marcan Caelum is waiting for us there.\n\nWe'll talk more at the vineyard.
You're still alive, thank the Eight. I began praying for you the moment I saw you enter the Watch.\n\nDid you find the thief who took my ring?
Well, stranger, you're back. Let me guess: This time you're here to tell me my brother wants me to come visit his family in Stormhold! As if I'd put up with his cooking.

Ulfsild would be proud of you, I think. She and I never truly saw eye to eye. How could we, when she was so much smaller than I am?\n\nDespite that, we held a deep respect for one another. So take the value of my words, or do not. But you've done well.
Normally, I'd be more wary of something as powerful as a Luminary playing tricks. But the Netch's sense of humor seems harmless.
So you're chasing the Dragon's favor now, Not-Ulfsild? What a pity you played my games first. You must find the Dragon terribly boring by comparison. Should have saved the best for last!
Sorry again about ripping up the fable. Hopefully my slobber didn't mess up the magic.\n\nI wouldn't know what to do if it did. Maybe … more slobber? No no no, that can't be right.
You are on your final trial. The Wing of the Crow. Your time with us, your mastery of Scribing … you're so near the end. Good luck.
Did I hear the Crow say she's a Luminary? I thought she was Ulfsild's familiar. I suppose she could be both. \n\nWait, hold on. Congratulations! You're heading in to your final trial!

Told you Hyacinth would have an idea! This one time he smuggled Oleander, Wisteria, and me into a Khajiiti monastery using only an old Dwarven cookpot and a handful of sulfur.\n\nLet's go to South Beacon as quick as we can.

No surprise, they were behind the attack that killed Snapdragon. Hmm. They're moving Hyacinth to Crimson Cove in Malabal Tor … but it's hard to tell if he's a prisoner or working with them. \n\nDo you still have that metal disk?

The Proxy Queen! Wisteria you … all right. Focus. To take on the Proxy Queen of Alinor, she'd need an army. That's why the Ceythalmor are gathering at Dusk Keep. \n\nThey're consolidating their forces for one final mission. We have to stop them!

Azurah commands that we love ourselves. We cannot resist who we are, what we feel. But emotions that fill us so completely invite the Void to creep in.\n\nYou just saw the first time Ravith channeled that darkness. And opened a door for Namiira.
We must find any remaining Twilight Cantors and save them. We cannot allow the Rajaska to grow their ranks any larger! Especially not now.
A moment for focus, tamiit.

Ku-ji'zho! I have read about it but to see it performed! I will meet you at Jode's Light after I gather what we need for the ritual.\n\nDo not worry. No dark dreams trouble me. And I know how to keep myself safe from danger on the roads.

We have one goal. Find Mezamma and make sure that Daedra never bothers us again. And I know Vanus and Gabrielle want to learn more about the soul reapers.\n\nSo let's get on with it. I want to hit as many worms as possible, very, very hard.

Ah, there you are! I hope you're rested after that fight under the Mages Guildhall. You'll need your strength.\n\nPrince Azah plans to set out for the Worm Cult nest soon. He wants you there when we launch our assault.

I know that lighthouse well and am aware of a cove to the south. Let me mark it on your map.\n\nWe'll meet you there after I conclude my business with Prince Azah and Skordo. No guild can function without a guildmaster. Not even the Fighters Guild.
Skordo's correct. This is bad. How are we going to stop Mezamma and the Worm Cult without Guildmaster Merric to guide us?
Maybe when Guendeline hears that I died in battle, she'll regret turning me away. Maybe she'll finally love me. Even in death, that would be worth it.\n\nAt the very least, I hope she feels guilty.
Again, thank you for understanding my position. \n\nDuke Renchant is a very intelligent man, and he will make the right decisions to ensure that Evermore does not fall.
Put the amulet on the altar. If he told you to bring it, it must be for something important.
How did you get here? Wait, don't answer that. Just tell me that you can help.\n\nThere are so few of us left, we could use another able-bodied soldier in our ranks.
It's the waiting that's the worst. If Kerbol has some magic cure, why doesn't she just give it to my husband? To all of these poor souls!\n\nAre you also waiting to see Kerbol?
The Covenant's inside the city! Let's hope your blade is thirsty.
Make your decision. These men are already dead. Why give up power we could harness today?
My recruit has returned. How did you fare?
You there! Untie us.
How could I have let this happen? Maybe the Fangs got to <<1>> through his natural greed.\n\nI should've known … should've warned him.
Welcome! This one is anxious to get moving. Aelif will lead the way to Ragnthar, if you're ready?
You received my message! Excellent. I appreciate your prompt attention.
Well done, adept! The shine off of the gleaming floor, so beautiful! We'll have a real party today.
At last, the Hound is dead.\n\nI stripped away Hircine's influence from the Green Lady, but only because you kept the Hound occupied.
She's running things out of the Guildhall in Vulkhel Guard at the moment. The Eight guide you, comrade.
I'd hoped to find you here, Adept.
Where's the captain? I can't believe she and the rest fell to the Redguard Ra Gada that quickly.
We have the advantage. The mercenaries know only what they can hit with their swords. We Khajiit know when to put down the sword and take up a rose.\n\nOr in this case, a keg of rich drink.
My husband is cursed. I have no time to speak with outsiders.
So, did you kill those pitfighters just for the fun of it? \n\nI hope so.
This place is known as Vuldngrav, the final resting place of Korthor the Dragon Priest. Tread carefully. Where there are Dragon Priests, there are sure to be draugr.
Sharp claws.
Shazah is happy to see you again, my friend. Khali is champing at the bit. She has grown tired of these Dro-m'Athra, and hungers for bigger game.
I've heard of these! Mane Jinninji-ri had them installed almost six hundred years ago during one of the many temple refurbishings. They were thought lost!
Sir Cadwell always seems to turn up when we need him the most. Maybe he really is a knight.
There is much to do. We need every warrior out in the field.
Uplifting stuff, huh? That Lavinia has a way with words.
Bright moons, traveler. I am Kazirra, Clan Mother of the Arenthia. Cari tells me we can expect great things out of you. That's good. We'll need all the help we can get.
As soon as you're ready, we have another mission that could use your unique approach.
Ah, a new guest has come to the manor! Welcome, my friend!
I can't bear to watch someone die again. Oh, Stibbons, that poor, poor man!

There. We're in Shadow Wood again, as foul as it ever was. We should be able to bypass the blight though … and all the feral guardians that would block our way.\n\nOnce we get in there, we need to head for the Grotto—that's where the Heart is.
While others handle the preparations on Stirk, you and I have the most important job.
Great, a history lesson. As if I didn't get enough of those growing up. I think Shazah told me about these things. One of the old Manes … Jinninji-ri? Had them installed years and years ago.
Greetings, warrior. Are you ready for a mission of critical importance to the Pact?
The Covenant has great need of your services, warrior!
There he is! Let's finish this!
Nice of you to check in with me, but I think Sai is more in need of your attentions.
It is done. Through the antechamber, quickly! The Amulet of Kings is close at hand, I can feel it.
Sai went on and on about how this was supposed to be a sacred site. Bull sausage! Place makes my blood run cold.
This really is the most ridiculous security imaginable for such a priceless artifact.
We must go through this all again, but that doesn't make it any easier.\n\nI hate seeing my good friend's wife suffer as she did before.
These assassins. They thought they were hunting us. Now Adusa turns the tables. Now we hunt them!

Now that Stibbons is on the mend, we can pack up the camp and move on to our next expedition!\n\nYou were quite adequate, for a temporary assistant. But you're no Stibbons. If I were in your position, I'd consider pursuing another line of work.

While I continue my research, you should head to Northpoint. Gwendis caught wind of Lleraya in that area, and I had her direct Dorell and Tamrith to take their troops north.\n\nI'm sure they'd appreciate any help you can provide.
I can't believe it. Dulkhi has always been the sweetest thing.
What was my brother thinking, keeping uncle's condition from me.\n\nWhen we find Dethisam, he's going to get a piece of my mind. Right after I give him a good, swift kick.
I'm not here to fight you. You're the one who helped Cassi, aren't you? She told me all about it.\n\nAre you busy? Maybe you can help me with something. It's rather important.
Are you ready to hear my proposition now?
That musty grotto attracts all manner of vermin. Look on the bright side, maybe those evil cultists cleaned out the Goblin filth.
Do you doubt if you are the predator or prey in this cautionary tale? If you are Undaunted, you know the answer. Now prove it.
You know, I'm a master clothier, yet I still own a pair of homespun gloves? They keep my hands warm at night. Sometimes simple is better.
You likely noticed their distinctive flares of light.
Welcome to my war!

I'll follow along and critique your adventuring skills. I like to stand back so I can take in every minute detail, but I'll be close enough to provide guidance and advice.\n\nNever fear, however. Since you're assisting me, my usual fee won't apply.
I need to rest. If Kharsthun is feeling so sprightly, he can warn you about the dangers ahead.
That Winks! I can't get that cat to stand still for even a moment!
Regilus's work won't be in vain. We'll put his report to good use. Same with this key. Don't worry.
That was exciting! I just need you to do that a few more times. Are you ready …?

You're looking for work, yeah? Good. We can use you. Folks around here have all kinds of problems that a good sellsword can solve. These contracts are piling up and my crew is booked solid.\n\nSo what do you say? Want to get your hands dirty?
Too proud to pay for a bite? We hear people sell these. Here is hoping you are not too poor — well, because… This one wants your money, yes?
Speak with me a moment, Initiate.
Elam will provide your initial contracts. They're standard fare. Find the target and eliminate them as you see fit.\n\nReport back to Elam when you finish the job and you'll be rewarded.
Assassin, it's time to collect a payment past due.
I'm not here to fight you. You're the one who helped Cassi, aren't you? She told me all about it.\n\nAre you busy? Maybe you can help me with something. It's rather important.
Wait, I'm not your enemy. I need your help. If we work together, we can put an end to the Serpent's threat once and for all.\n\nShould I continue?

Archcanon Tarvus carries the burden of Lord Vivec and the entire palace atop his shoulders. He'll serve as your guide in this undertaking for Lord Vivec.\n\nAnd, if need be, you can always find me somewhere near the palace.
Nothing like fighting off a horde of beastmen to keep you warm. Better than any fire!

Ah, outlander. Lord Vivec trusts too much to put his faith in one such as you, but who am I to question my God?\n\nI suppose he sent you to me so I could put you to work? Did he say which task he wants us to accomplish first?
According to the old scroll, there's a secret entrance that leads to the hidden passages somewhere in this chamber.

Chodala stopped confiding in me, but he's still my brother. I don't know where he goes to meditate, but he has to visit the Wise Woman eventually. I'm sure we'll find him in Ald'ruhn.\n\nDespite your "civilized" ways, I am proud to call you my friend.

Have you ever seen such creatures? Raz has not. Probably neither have you. \n\nYou are a newcomer, yes? New to this island of High Elves? This one has an eye for such things. And you look capable. So, can Raz interest you in some cloak-and-dagger work?

You see? It's empty! It's as if the words just scampered off the page!\n\nI thought maybe the enchantment rendered the words invisible, so I tried to recover them. I used gazing lenses, welkynd revelation-stones—even a bit of lemon juice. Nothing!
My, you certainly do have a talent for juggling. One might almost say your hands work like magic. Tell me, why do you wish to join the House of Reveries?

Hmm. Rugged individual, obviously well-traveled. Yes, you should do quite nicely.\n\nAre you available for hire? I need an escort for an expedition. I expect we'll encounter some Daedra along the way, but I'm sure it's nothing you can't handle.

You've picked a bad day for a stroll in the park. Something's got into the animals. They're running wild. Frenzied.\n\nDon't suppose you saw an indrik on your way here? A tame one. She's my charge and pride of the queen's menagerie. I need to find her.

I don't need another death on my conscience, but I can't afford to refuse your help.\n\nA direct assault on Sea Keep is impossible, but if the Maormer can infiltrate it, then so can we. Meet me at the ruins down by the water. I'll show you what I mean.
Step back, if you please. There's a murder investigation underway. Unless you have something to contribute? In that case, talk to Tarnamir.
Now our work begins in earnest. The Staff of Towers must be recovered. Shall we begin?
Welcome back, initiate. I hope the Augur didn't give you too much trouble.\n\nSo? Was your journey a success? Is Alik'r safe?
Don't just stand there, initiate! Go speak to the Loremaster. I'm anxious to see these new fragments!
Josajeh is one of my greatest pupils, but removing her from this undertaking was essential to its success. I'm sure you understand.

You must be here about the leaflet. I could use the help, as long as you're not afraid of a dastardly scoundrel.\n\nLet me start again. I represent Cyrodilic Collections, a society dedicated to retrieving the lost treasures of the Argonians.
You should get back to Concordia with those items. I'll be right behind you!

You've done a great deal for us already. I wonder if you're willing to do a bit more.\n\nWhile Famia has proven a steadfast companion, I believe our current predicament requires someone a bit more … adroit, when things take a turn for the perilous.
You have the flint vine? Thank goodness! Wind it into a ladder so we can save our friend!
Be swift. Friend-Jaxsik would build a ladder to fight the sun if it crossed her. An endearing quality that will someday get her killed.\n\nHopefully today is not the day.
Of all the things these savages could steal, they choose our grave-stakes. My rage-spine shivers, ojel. They will pay in blood.
This is the uxith. It is normally bustling with activity around bonding time. My egg-kin must be preoccupied with the disturbing events of the day.
Take care of yourself. No one else will. Count on it.
Why do you hesitate? Hang the chime, beeko.

Hrrm. I knew nothing good would come of Abnur Tharn's efforts to make peace with the Usurper Queen. Now she turns her attention to Riverhold.\n\nWe must protect the city, no matter what Euraxia throws at us.

Prisms and light, ingenious! These obstacles annoy me, but the engineering is impressive.\n\nI expect we'll see more of these puzzle-locks before we reach the hidden weapon. Now collect the map coordinate while I open a portal to Baandari Trading Post.

Tharn sent Zamarak to assist you against the Euraxian officer, Saulinia, and her assassins. The locals say that a group matching their description passed through here a short time ago.\n\nTharn explained that we seek a hidden Akaviri shrine.
This looks familiar. Take a closer look, yes?

A chance meeting turned fated partnership. Fortuitous for this one, yes?\n\nYou should speak to Ishu first, see if he has any new information for us. His house is just south of the marketplace. Can't miss it.
I am happy to see you and the others, five-claw, and am eager to hear what happened.\n\nWait, where is Cadwell?

Tasnasi does not know you. That's good. She knows everyone in the Stitches. Those who aren't in Khasda's pocket she can count on one paw. This one has a job for someone who'd rather pick it. An unknown face like yours is just what she needs.
Ugh. Teleporting. I should have eaten breakfast today … instead of drinking it.
As Zubacha the Hermit said to Intasi after returning from his grand pilgrimage: "hello."\n\nThis one is cheered to see you without the blemishes of harm.

Abnur Tharn told us the news of Rimmen. We're preparing for the arrival of Euraxia's forces, but I wish we had more troops to defend the city with.\n\nWhat of you? What occurred at the Desert Wind Adeptorium?
I'm going to take a moment to make sure we didn't miss anything here. I'll meet you at the temple summit soon. Unless you needed something?
Raz does not like the look of this.
Well, if it isn't my old friend! Been a while, eh? Stros M'kai? Remember? Ah, never mind.
For a bearded mammoth, Sai Sahan is surprisingly stealthy. Good thing, too. I expected his clomping footsteps to alert the entire cult to our presence the moment we stepped inside.
I recommend you show your respects to the Grandmasters before you depart. We owe them all a great deal.
My friend, you arrived just in time. I'd prefer to not face our old companion without you.
Queen Khamira speaks true. We must return to the Dragonguard Sanctum and gather our forces.\n\nGo on. We'll meet you there.
It was a good call to split our forces. Let's just hope our friend here is feeling cooperative.
This one won't lie. She's only seen one place more corrupted by the Great Darkness in her time as a cantor. Cleansing this path will not be easy.
No answers appear before my eyes, my friend. I seek a path for us, but find nothing but dead ends.\n\nI have one last idea. Moons willing, it will work as it did at Jode's Core.
Were you truly on that island when it rose into the sky? This one wishes he could have been with you.\n\nWell, except for all the cultists. And the Dragons. And the rising into the sky thing.
Did I hear correctly? Did you leave the old wizard alone on the island as it floated into the sky?\n\nMates don't abandon mates, mate. Bear that in mind the next time we work together.
An island in the sky. It sounds like a dream … or maybe a nightmare.
Nahfahlaar doesn't seem very happy to be here.
Hmph, I could use a good, strong drink.
I'm glad the general has come around. With Imperial soldiers at our side, we might just be able to defeat Laatvulon's forces.
The cart I chartered will take us where we need to go to continue my investigation of the Icereach Coven. We can travel together or meet there, whichever you prefer.

I'd prefer to avoid any fighting that we can. It's not really a strength of mine. I mean, I can hold my own, don't you worry. But, well, I don't have a great deal of experience with violence.\n\nEquip your weapon is my point.

Has my father found a way to use the sacred oil against the Gray Host? Perhaps he's doing more than I thought.\n\nThe swordthane has helped me in the past. He'll be reasonable. He has to be. Let's let him know what we need.

A graveyard. The Icereach Coven certainly enjoys defiling graves.\n\nThey exhumed some of the bodies buried here, but not all of them. The ones they dug up must be important to the creation of the medallions. We need to learn why.

Fenn has proven himself, especially after what happened in Blackreach. House Ravenwatch … they're unusual, as far as blood-suckers go. As for Svana, she's braver than I originally thought.\n\nAnyway, meet me in Solitude after you finish up.
Gods, what happened in here? It looks like a massacre!\n\nThat's Magister Fridelja, Jarl Olfwenn's court wizard. Talk to her and find out about the jarl.
Look around for clues but stay alert. This could have been an elaborate ploy to lead us into an ambush.

None of the locals really wanted to talk. One or two admitted to seeing Fenn, but no one witnessed any kind of disturbance at his lodgings. At least, no one saw anything they were willing to tell me about.\n\nIs this Edjar? Does he know anything?
This place … it makes my skin crawl.\n\nBut we need to keep going. We need to find my father and stop the harrowstorm.

As I understand it, a vampire called Lady Essenia controlled Greymoor Keep. She was working with the Gray Host to undermine Western Skyrim before you put her down.\n\nThe very stones of this keep … I sense … something. We need to be on our guard.

We've seen some amazing things in Blackreach, but this castle … it's beautiful and disturbing at the same time. And it's full of Gray Host warriors, so be careful.\n\nNow take Fenn and see if you can find the ritual site.
Let me say a prayer for Eivina, make sure she's comfortable.\n\nI'll meet you outside.

Kasalla must have some security at her warehouse, so you take the lead when we get there.\n\nI tend to lose my temper in the face of physical opposition, and I'd prefer not to draw the attention of the guard by slaughtering any belligerent hirelings.
Time for the salskap to begin! \n\nYou of all people should stay for the entertainment. I wish I had time to hear how you found all the instruments.
I feel Overseer Urlvar knows more than he told us. The last thing we should do is heed his advice to quit now.
Don't be alarmed. I mean you no harm, but there are harrowfiends swarming around Kilkreath Temple who do. Head back to safety before they find you!

This is the third caravan this month that never made it to Dragon Bridge. And the soldier I sent to look for it, dead! I'm at my wit's end. \n\nTroll's blood! The garrison's remaining reserves won't last a week without an influx of fresh supplies.
Blackreach … again! It must be vast to extend this far from Eastmarch. I can't believe people are living down here.

Is it wrong to find these visions so intriguing? This one showed your assassin again, eye patch and all, by a cave near a waterfall. And the ball of magicka drifted toward the west again.\n\nI suggest we go that way as quickly as possible.
So, you really think I should spare Mazog the punishment of the Blood Price?
I'm done arguing. Use the damned potion if you want. Let's just get out of here.

Thank you, friend! This makes Rigurt happier than a hairy skeever in the larder!\n\nEnding this feud will be simple for us. Rigurt has overcome many trials that others said were hopeless. Like that time he fell in the latrine at Fort Amol!
Go on and read it! I've had my fill of enchanted scrolls for now, thank you.

Thank you for helping. It's a big relief. \n\nI need rubbings from two Dragon mounds; one south of here and another off to the east. I'm particularly interested in any symbols that look like Dragons, but anything you find will help.
Move slow and keep an eye out for anything that might point to the Gray Host or their elusive survivor.
These pockets of dark energy—I've never seen anything like them. I sense … well, I sense nothing. A void.\n\nWe should be cautious, but we must continue the search.

Investigate the Gray Host activity in the foothills north of Markarth, near Bthardamz. Fennorian will meet you there.\n\nGwendis and I will return to the orrery at Arkthzand. Join us once you uncover Rada's plans.

Nighthollow Keep is down this path. The archive should be right inside.\n\nIn writings we recovered from Lady Belain, she mentioned a Nighthollow Testament. That's probably what we're looking for. Just watch yourself. The place is locked down tight.
Did you get a location? Give me the details and you go on ahead. I want to chase down a few leads about the Worm Cult while we're here in Markarth. Shouldn't take long, I'll catch up.

Bthar-Zel is more intact than the few other Dwarven ruins I've visited. I spotted a chamber that appears related to the keystones.\n\nBut more intact doesn't mean completely intact. The path ahead is blocked.
What did you find? My auramancy works best on a personal possession, something with an emotional aura or even an arcane residue clinging to it.
Go ahead, just fiddle with the crystal and see if you can deactivate it.\n\nIf I'm right, it's part of a complex ward protecting the castle. We won't be able to get inside while the wards are active.

The Dwarven apparatus will take us into the bowels of the mountain. To the Reachwind Depths, the ruins that now serve as the lair of the Lothid clan and their leader, Boss Trenlor.\n\nMeet Adusa there, five-claw, and we will find Kathad together.

Reachfolk. I don't believe I've ever dealt with a more distrustful lot. I'm here on urgent business, but the Despot of Markarth refuses to see me. While the Gray Host gathers, he hides behind his sentries and his walls, thinking to escape their fury.
I need to speak to Tayfaern before I set out.\n\nGo on, harrier. I'll find you on the trail.
It's a thin hope, but if we can find Barth, he might know more about the feud between my clan and the Eagleseers.
Why are you following us, outsider? We may be young, but we're still warriors of the Reach! You won't find us to be easy prey.
You see what I'm dealing with? How can I return to the xanmeer and set things right when I have my hands full simply keeping all these … Stibbonses … under control.

Tell the Ambitions no army of crazed cultists is going to sacrifice them on our watch! But try not to alarm them … which might be tricky. Hmm.\n\nAfter I send out the call for allies, I'll escort Sombren and the twins to Fort Redmane.

Damn it! I'm too late. Poor Councilor Jirich. She didn't deserve to die like that. At least, I don't think she did.\n\nGlad to see you, by the way. Did you happen to get here in time to see who killed her?

Damn it all to Hermaeus Mora's nether regions! If you aren't one of the damn cultists and you aren't one of the Covenant soldiers, then what in the name of Oblivion's stinky armpit are you doing down here?
This is different for Quistley. He's not one for any sort of rough living, other than maybe going to gambling dens and taverns in the seedier parts of town.

Find us in the marsh to the northwest. I'll take Calia and Destron and meet you at the shrine. Don't worry, I'll protect them. The cultists won't surprise me again.\n\nJust let your Wood Elf friend know that we have the twins and will keep them safe.
That was terrifying! I've never felt anything like that. Ever!\n\nNothing like that ever occurred during our training in the sanctum. What's happening to me?
Our power seems to be getting stronger. Harder to control. If not for Sombren, Calia's own power might have consumed her!\n\nIs this our punishment for abandoning our sanctum?
The sorcerous impact knocked the censer right out of my hands. So much the better. Vehk knows I'd just end up killing someone else with it!
Your friend certainly doesn't seem happy to see me. Maybe he still has a headache. Tell him I promise not to hit him over the head again, however tempting that might be.
Rotate the cubes to match the symbols. Just like you did outside. That should disrupt the ward and open the door ahead.

I heard the Sul-Xan were raiders, but I didn't imagine they'd be interested in this sort of equipment. Looks like they're using it to refine the harrada they're collecting into some kind of concoction.
Let's find these notes. Catching Mathen's eye gave me butterflies, but catching Astella's eye gives me the shivers!

This is no normal sleep, but it's oddly benign for a curse. None of these people appear to be in distress, in fact they seem to be dozing quite serenely. Some of them have been missing for weeks, yet they show no signs of poor health.
Those cultists dared invade our sanctuary? That's an insult I cannot allow to stand.
This ruin is not like any other I've seen and I've seen a lot of Daedric ruins. Sil knows I would have loved to study it. Liam too. Damn Xigira and her fanatics.
We need to get inside and help Farrul Lupus! He sounds like he's badly injured!\n\nDo you know how to pick a lock? If not, let's see if there's an open window or something around back.
Remember what you learned before. Send this creature back to Oblivion!
Another memory. I don't know how many more of these I can take.\n\nJust go on and use the stone. I'm ready.
I suppose it would have been too easy if Inalieth was still working at the inn. Let's go find her, then.
Go on, that little one there should be a fine conduit. If you can catch it for me, we can begin!
My grandfather said Onimiril was a guild mage from Vulkhel Guard. Maybe we'll find him there, or at least find someone who knows where he is.
I'm with you, my friend. No matter what.
Atrozu tells me the trail continues beyond that gate. I just don't see any way to get through.\n\nLook around. Maybe we can find an easier way than climbing the wall.
When you used the amulet, that wisp appeared. Let's follow it and see where it leads.
That's one stone attuned. There's still more to do before we can move on from finding these energy fonts. I hope we can make our way to the next one quickly.

Fargrave is a strange mix of mortals and Daedra. But I do not think we can learn much more from this realm. Not about the Order of the Waking Flame or the devices they use to create their Incarnates anyway.

Such violence! Oh, master, you make me so proud! You dispatched that Incarnate abomination with a ferocity worthy of Arox the Mutilator!\n\nAnd did you see the look on Nokvroz's face? Like a lava crab crawled up his nose and died! Ha!

I expected you to be killed on your way here. Perhaps you are more capable than you appear. \n\nThis is the foundry of Jynd, Kynmarcher under Valkynaz Nokvroz. Here she supervises Dremora who study and devise things of interest to the valkynaz.

Several mortals stand about, gawking. Two will tell what they saw. Ruldzara speaks freely to anyone. And Tarvyn, on the hill. Ally to Daedra.\n\nI'll take Tephilaz's shell to a necrologist in the Daedric area. Meet me there with what you learn.
There must be something around here that can lead us to Elegian—preferably before the warden or the overseers notice our presence. A map? A list of prisoners? Something.
Do not look to me. Evidently the daedrat's whim is our command.
I never met a building with only a single entrance and exit. Let's look around the courtyard. There's got to be another way to get into the bathhouse.
I shall make my own way to the Blood Pit. It feels safer to me if I only have myself to watch out for.
Ah. Timely as ever. What did you discover in the auction house?
You'll have to handle Gilfrex yourself, I'm afraid. They don't seem to be aware of me. Can't say I mind being beyond the notice of such low-life scum.

Ah, you caught that, did you? My missing cargo is more delegates for the conference—perhaps the most important ones.\n\nBut I need you to check on the guild delegates right now. They went to visit a druid named Ryvana. Her hut lies to the west.
I prepared the wood and am ready to weave it into a basket. \n\nWere you successful? Did your wondrous labors bear fruit? Has my faith in your skills been rewarded?
I still can't believe someone took the key. So childish. I bet it's Mortens. \n\nMortens!
I don't know what I'd do without Isobel.
Got a proposition for you, mate. Could earn you a tidy share of treasure or, better still, a place as first mate on my ship—soon as I've got one. Interested?

You may not always have a map to guide you in life. Sometimes you need to learn from the stories of those who came before. Then use your wits to chart a path.\n\nRead the tablet to learn the next portion of the pass phrase to gain the Sacred Shield.

Just as the Colossus watches over Gonfalon Bay, I was supposed to keep the alliance leaders safe. I failed in that, but at least they aren't in the Ascendant Order's hands. Not yet, anyway.\n\nWhat did Captain Kaleen and the others have to say, dear?

The circle elders cannot accept that one of our own may be responsible for this disaster. And I could hear the doubt in their voices concerning the Evergrowth. \n\nWe need to prove that one of our circle has caused this unbalance.
For the hammer's head, I suggest we go to the prison warrens.\n\nAn executioner's block would be perfect for what we have in mind … macabre though it may be.

I know my rogue spell is to blame for most of the weirdness happening around Tor Draioch, but it almost seems like these damned motes are becoming dangerous. They're doing more than just mischievous magic.\n\nFish biscuits! I need to figure this out!
Fair day and Auri-El's blessing to you. I am Ayrenn Arana Aldmeri, Queen of the Aldmeri Dominion.\n\nYou have my apologies, friend of Caska. I must stink worse than a three-day-dead guar right now.

I'd know a fellow member of the Covenant anywhere! I'm not sure what you're doing in this damn jungle, but I'm thrilled to see a friendly face.\n\nI'm High King Emeric and it's a pleasure to make your acquaintance.

I wondered how the Ascendant Order suddenly appeared inside Castle Navire at Duchess Elea's banquet. The river shown on the map, it must be underground. That could mean there's a passage hidden beneath the castle.
Let's get this over with before I change my mind.
I know that angry shouting anywhere. Oblan must be just up ahead. Let's hurry and see what's got his tail in a knot this time.

I'm glad to see that <<1>> is just fine! Now we have to convince <<2>> to pay his portion of our bill. Otherwise the innkeeper won't return my scepter of office.\n\nMaybe we should check his house in Gonfalon Bay?
Monsters! Hadolids! \n\nThere was blood on their claws. Were they coming to kill me?

Brilliant! According to the book, the keys were hidden separately. One in the southern jungle, the other in the west. Here, I'll mark your map with the locations specified.\n\nHave you heard the legend of the hidden vault? It's quite fascinating!

Hopefully this Azamel will be willing to speak with us. Maybe you should do the talking when we find him? You're better at … people than I am. You might be able to appeal to his conscience.\n\nIf he has one, that is.
Well, she's safe. But whatever they were talking about, that didn't sound good.\n\nQuick, find out what's going on.
Yes, yes, we're ever so grateful. Now if you could leave us, I really do have a particular task for my manservant to take care of.

I knew m'lady was still in there, ready to order me about!\n\nThe lighthouse is on the eastern shore of the islet. It's part of the old museum I mentioned. I remember polishing its historic plaques quite clearly. Let's go see what they contain.

Razhamad's the game-baron here in Gonfalon Bay. You won't find a kinder or more knowledgeable player west of High Rock. Not that he'll go easy on you, mind!\n\nHe expects the best from the players he trains. Trust me. I should know!

Please enjoy yourself within my Gaming Hall. Drinks, food, and games can be found throughout.\n\nIf you have any interest in learning about the game we play here, Tales of Tribute, please seek out my associate Brahgas.
What are you waiting for? Head back to Gonfalon Bay and talk to Razhamad. I'll be along shortly. I wouldn't miss this tournament for the world!

Roots and thorns confound it! What took you so long? I had half a mind to go after the two of you myself for a moment there.\n\nDid you find anything? Do you know where the Firesong took Wyress Tola? Is she all right?
Go ahead and tell Druid Laurel what we uncovered at the Firesong camps. That map indicating a spot in Hag Fen seems particularly important.

The Vine District lies on the east side of the city, near the harbor. It's a small druid conclave. I'll join you there shortly.\n\nI need to confer with my father and send scouts to search for Sealord Nalos while we attend the Draoife.

Well done. These Dreadsails may be fierce, but they lack loyalty. Even though they've got numbers on their side, they won't stick their necks out for their mates.\n\nThat's something we can use against them.
Not our usual line of work, but I'll tell you this. Helping Lady Arabelle out is never boring.
Za'ji is proud to have played a part in defeating the Ascendant Lord and saving the Systres! Oh, not as large a part as you, five-claw. But Za'ji had a significant role just the same.
The Shard of the Green, clearly a druid relic, belongs to Lord Bacaro? I wonder how he came to possess such a rare and ancient item.\n\nLet's see what else we can learn in the manor's cellars.

It's clear from that letter that the Ascendant Lord ordered the attempts on Lady Arabelle and Duchess Elea's lives. I suspect this garden he mentions is the source of the poison. We need to find it so I can devise an antidote.
We sail when you're ready, my friend. I'm proud to fight at your side again.
So the lordling convinced you to go on this little excursion, too? Good. We can use another steady hand. Just try to keep your lunch down once we reach the open water.
Come, friend of Laurel. The druid stones are awake. The door in the hillside will answer me now. We can go inside.

See this? I'm covered in bark! I'm turning into a tree!\n\nDruid Fenas is doing his best to determine the nature of the curse, but we're going to need more help. I'd give everything we ever stole to fix this.
The most worthless, unreliable, lecherous … ugh. I'm ready to be rid of him. Once we get paid, I'll never work with him again.
That was neither story nor ancient history! The Chronicle showed us the recent past. That's never happened before!
Mmm, no more, my sweet. Just need some rest. \n\nSo energetic. Quite wore me out.

Damn those path-traitors and their Dreadsails lackeys! They're everywhere! The Firesong attacked these Eldertide before they could reach the shelter of this camp. But you look like you came with a purpose. Tell me what news you bring.

Let me mark your map. Two of the faithful I am acquainted with reside in these places. Talk to Mildanor and Bassian. They should be pleased to provide fate's chosen with the location of the shrine.\n\nI shall meet you at each to make introductions.

The Lark of Rosgard is so smug when he's got the high ground. He won't be so smug when he's level with my boot!\n\nAnd his little disappearing act. Let me get my hands on him, and I'll make him disappear!
Great tides of fate swirl around us, proxy. We must move carefully or risk being dragged under.

Sorry, friend, but the Necropolis is closed today. And by order of the abbot, it seems. We've never turned away the families of the dead before, but if the rumors about illness are true ….\n\nPlague isn't something to be treated lightly.

A ritual that would breach the walls of the Crux requires enormous power. The Dreamcarvers may have left signs of how they constructed this focus.\n\nSearch the grounds. I can no longer hear our injured, so we must learn more.

I need help. I was swept overboard in a storm and found myself washed up in this terrifying land. What happened? I must find my ship. I must find Naanurrel, my father. Are you real, or just another spirit?
As before, I believe we should return the book. Perhaps then we will learn more about this strange cipher and this blasted trap.

Tide-King be praised! It seems the beasts did not breach the Secretus completely, and the vessels are in good health.\n\nResetting the focus should bring them back into harmony with the rest of the Rectory's occupants.
In the century I have been allied with Hermaeus Mora, I have never known him to be so … concerned … as he seems to be now. We are dealing with an unprecedented set of circumstances, proxy.
Great. If all goes well, then we can both get paid and … go our separate ways, I guess.

It's almost imperceptible. If I didn't know what to look for, I would have missed it completely. It's sort of like an absence carving a path through the realm. No wonder the Great Eye hasn't noticed the intrusion yet.\n\nWe must hurry, mortal!
Thank you. I know I wouldn't last long on my own, but I've known that for a while.\n\nIt's why I couldn't leave Tel Dreloth in the first place.
I came as quickly as I could. But I fear we're too late.
Do leave me be. Once I get a hold of all the knowledge this island keeps hidden, no magister would dare deny me an audience.
Well, look what the nix-ox dragged in! What are you doing here, hero? Are you following me again?\n\nSeriously, what brings you to this house of arrogance and whining?

Madam Whim described this place as large. She understated it!\n\nWhat the injured Voidprowler said about the Darkreaves—do you think she lied? To scare you, I mean. Since you're a mortal. I don't care.

Is this what it's like having friends? Helpful people coming out of the woodwork to give leads on how to track down and murder some tyrant slaver that stole my memories?\n\nNot stole, but—you know what I mean.
Let's not spend any more time in this place than we have to. \n\nI can't even imagine what my library fees have compounded to.
Not to belabor the obvious, but we'll need to be careful here. We should make haste to the Heart of the Underweave and find Martina's sanctum.\n\nOnward and upward!
Fastest way to travel is by tunnel and bush. But we won't both be able to fit. \n\nThe bristleback lords slumber, we should be safe to take the slow route to Frielvi.

How do you do this, friend? Face the unknown and unknowable on a daily basis? Both you and Leramil are certainly braver than I am.\n\nI'm with you to the end, but I must admit I long for the peace and quiet of the chambers of the dead.

I don't understand it either. But like it or not, we're the only thing standing between Vaermina and the utter collapse of reality.\n\nSo, let's get moving. We need to find a Daedric Prince wearing a mortal meat suit while we still can.
I … I thought I could resist it … the corruption. But here in Apocrypha … it is too much.
Enter the sea when you are ready, proxy. Then I shall weave an arcane shield to protect us from the crushing depths.\n\nAnd do not fear. We shall not get very wet.

The ripples in the matrices of magicka are more chaotic than I expected. My portal opened farther from the Loom than I hoped.\n\nLet us make our way to the Loom. We can use the Echonir there to see if any recent memories of Ithelia remain.
I can clearly see the frayed and shredded threads of fate surrounding that mortal. Very peculiar. Go talk to it.\n\nI'd do it, but most mortals react poorly to all my beautiful eyes and tentacles.
Gaius said he hid the key to the catacombs inside a statue. No doubt the garden has a lot of those. This is a Colovian estate, after all.\n\nHopefully the map he drew for us is accurate.
No matter how many times I assist you or Leramil, I don't think I'll ever get used to all the Daedra.
Leramil and that floating ball of eyes told me to meet you here. They explained all about the reality tears. They sound terrible! What's going to befall us next, I wonder.

I provided Ursilia with a common antidote for most poisons. Not sure it will do anything about the wine, but it shouldn't hurt.\n\nWatch out for the vampires Gallio mentioned in his journal as we make our way to his alchemical laboratory.

At first swipe, Otho seems genuine, but one mustn't leap blindly. All evidence must be found and this pot of poisoned tea could be the key. Quickly, let us investigate Lady Weatherleah's room for clues.
The Echonir, proxy. If Ithelia's presence changed the door, the Echonir might show us a recent memory.
Those ancient priests just … walked into the sea? I hope Leramil can think of an alternative. I'm not much of a swimmer.

Damn it, I thought I could do this, but you should talk to Grivier. Find out what he knows. \n\nJust the sight of him makes me want to run him through. If I try to make him talk, he won't last long enough to tell us anything.
The Ayleids made a habit of keeping their most-valuable treasures safely underground. We're looking for a way down—the stairs in the middle of the ruins, or maybe a cave.
I'm not sure what happened. After we defeated Torvesard, I stepped through that portal and found myself back here.\n\nI'm dying to know what became of Ithelia, but you should talk to Leramil first.

The Recollection was waiting for us. If Beragon hadn't spotted them, their ambush would have been flawless. Beragon's good in my book. Those Wood Elves got the drop on me, but he saved my sorry arse.\n\nDeal with the seed. We'll hold off any others.
The friendly Daedra, Scruut, sent me to meet you, comrade. She and Leramil told me some strange things, but after everything that happened in West Weald …. \n\nAnyway, I'm here to help.
I can't tell you how relieved I feel to find Sorilen safe and sound. I'm not surprised that she'd stay to help survivors.\n\nLet's talk to her. Maybe she'll explain her invitation to come here.

You there! Can I interest you in participating in a valiant exploration of an Ayleid ruin? I find myself in need of a strong, able assistant. It's a chance you can't miss out on! I'll mention you prominently in my next book!
I admit, I was not entirely certain that would work. Enter the portal, proxy. We can do nothing more here.
That lamp led us onto the Many Paths. But why would the lamp bring us here? And why do I hate it so much?\n\nPerhaps the answers lie at the end of this path.
Like an old-fashioned Colovian skeever hunt. Take out every last one of those Daedra, comrade!
Tread carefully, friend. I don't know what we might find in here. So stay on guard.

Ah, you received my summons, good! I am Krin'ze of the Twilight Cantors, in service to Azurah.\n\nDid you see the falling star? A sure sign from the Mother of All Khajiit that someone is in great need. I am certain of it.

Now you see what I was trained to do. Khajiit that fall to the Bent Dance of Namiira, I can straighten their tails.\n\nThe Hidden Moon's purpose was to tend to the immortal souls of all Khajiit, even those that fell to darkness. Do you understand?
The Gardener will see you now.

You stopped! Thank you. There are plenty of you adventuring types running around, but everyone else seemed eager to ignore me.\n\nThe Mages Guild is looking for someone with an explorer's grit to help us with a bit of a predicament.
Now that we have a moment, allow me to introduce myself. Nahlia, Votary knight in the Order of the Lamp. Pleasure to make your acquaintance. \n\nIrnard briefed you on our situation?

I'm glad you've chosen to stay, interloper. The path to master Scribing is not an easy one, but its rewards are innumerable. \n\nYour knight appears to be leaving. Did I ruffle her feathers with my caws?

To live a mortal life is to carry a burdensome weight. The Netch understands that better than any of us, I think.\n\nIts methods in making things lighter for your kind are whimsical, to be sure. But its calling is admirable.
Talk to Firandil, if you have a minute. He can be a bit of a big personality but he's the very best at what he does.
You're back! But where's Naku?
You were right to convince me to move on from my ring. Too often do we shackle ourselves to physical things for reasons beyond the value they offer us.
Luckily, the road to Skingrad has plenty of bends and curves. I'm not entirely sure I could manage a straight line right now.\n\nHmm. Maybe I'll wait a spell before heading off to meet Hooke.
I continue to mull your riddle. Its simplicity and circular nature delights me, mortal. A pearl of an idea I can polish and hold up to examine again, and again.

We knew there was something off about that book. But we've been searching for material to support your investigation of the Netch's wing, and this was the best we could find. \n\nAlmost like someone's keeping the real books stashed away somewhere.
Ah, the Gryphon! I hope you don't freeze up on this one. But if you do, I'll bet you can fox your way out of it.
You did it! I haven't been this happy since I got stuck in that barrel of fermented figs. Ooh, ooh! I made such a mess.\n\nAnyway, go talk to him! Go, go! Shoo!
When I look back on our quest for justice together, when I see all that you've accomplished. \n\nI can't help but be impressed in spite of myself. Well done, mortal. Very well done.
That unmarked door unlocked after you completed your last trial. Maybe the Crow knows something about it. We're nearing the end, my friend!
You tell Hyacinth what we found out while I try to keep the magicka lattice from unraveling. I did mention that magic doesn't always work the way I want it to, didn't I?
I won't lie. That felt good. \n\nLet's check the captain's quarters. Even if we can't find out where Hyacinth went, maybe there's something else in there we can use.

This place feels so familiar. I'm not sure why. Like it's on the tip of my tongue. Maybe Wisteria mentioned it once?\n\nShe certainly had her secrets. I mean, we all did. But now I look back on our time together and wonder what else I missed.
This next memory … well, touch the light when you are ready to see it.
Cantor Krin'ze looks as stricken as I feel. Worse, perhaps. Speak to her, tamiit.
It will take some effort to draw Eifa's soul to her remains. I cannot do it without your help.\n\nDispel the darkness while I perform the ritual.
Your tamiit has gone awfully quiet, walker. You should see what holds his tongue and make him tell us about Ravith-morna.
The note said a cove on the north coast, right? It should be around here somewhere.\n\nIf you find it before I do, just holler.

Merric's arrival and your intervention saved the lives of many members of my guild. That's a debt we'll repay.\n\nGo on. Head to the Fighters Guildhall here in Shornhelm. We'll take care of Merric's remains and the soul reaper and be in touch later.

A pleasure to see you again, friend, despite the dire circumstances. Thank you for purging our sanctum of the Worm Cult infestation. Reliable as ever, I see.\n\nPlease, describe everything you experienced during the attack. Spare no detail.
Tell Skordo what happened, friend. I'm not sure I can coherently get through the specifics of the terrible tale, not while the wound in my heart is still raw.
You gave her the daisies? Was she happy? Did she swoon? What did she say? \n\nTell me. Tell me. Tell me.

So much suffering. So much death. Like my husband and my children, this soldier gave her life for Evermore. \n\nI wish I could offer her more comfort, but I can only pray with her to gods whose mercy I have come to doubt.
<She seems to be sleeping, but her heartbeat is weak. It doesn't seem possible to wake her.>
Tanval's looking for you again.
These people are my ancestors. Why let them wallow in the past when they could protect our future?
Purchase the charcoal and start using that anvil!
You don't look like one of the Renrijra. What are you doing here?
Windhelm is difficult to miss, east of here. It's a fair trip along the river.\n\nThe bridge will be obvious. This one will wait for you on the southern end.
Well met, Adept. I believe I may have a task for you.
I'll be able to rest soon enough, adept. Shalidor is the only reason I was able to finish. His enthusiasm and energy sustained me through this difficult trial.
Thank you for helping Merric at-Aswala and the Fighters Guild.
I overheard. He's sending you back to Tamriel.\n\nMy power is bound within Sheogorath's realm, but I'm at my full power on Nirn. I will be at your side.
The First Mane! To see him again as we take our first steps onto the Path … this must be a good sign.
I don't go around smashing things like a guar in a pottery shop. We don't want to attract the wrong kind of attention.
Your training is complete, soldier. You are ready for the battles of Cyrodiil!
I have absolutely no idea why a lunar priest would send you to me. But I'll take all the help I can get. We've got a lot of work to do.
The Orchard is overrun! The damned vampires are too strong and we can't get through.
Give me a moment into tap into Green … it fights the corruption madly, making it more difficult for me to do this.
Old Rid-Thar! Good to see him again. This has got to be a good sign, right?
If you're ready, we can use your skills, soldier.
I can't believe Sai's back. I … we owe you so much.

Sahan looks relatively healthy, but there's no telling what sort of toll years of torment will take upon the mind. It will be interesting to see. \n\nI do hope we're done here. I have an assignation with a young lady.
Send these abominations back to their graves!
How many more doors are between us and this vault?
Dear me, more skeletons? Makes you wonder if Mannimarco's heart is really in this, doesn't it?
We are the targets? Well, that only proves we are doing something right!\n\nIf no one wants to kill you, you're not trying hard enough, this one always says.
Let's get on with it, shall we? Stibbons isn't going to revive himself!
Ah, you made it. I was hoping you'd find your way to these forlorn hills.
Without you I'd never have known what happened to my bride.
Look at her! Bili usually keeps herself immaculate, but now she looks ten seasons older and like something the guar dragged in.\n\nMaybe she knows where Dethisam went, though.
Let's not start something we'll both regret. I could use some help, and you're going to want to hear what I have to say.
Wait, I'm not your enemy! I need your help. If we work together, we can put an end to the Serpent's threat once and for all.\n\nShould I continue?
Aww. Is you scared of the little bug-ums? Don't worry, if you get bit I'll give you a bandage for your cut.
Does the smoke and scent of burning dreams not appeal to you? Face the holocaust. Extinguish the flames consuming the City of Ash. Return Undaunted!
Craft a pair of homespun gloves. You'll need refined jute and a style material. Clothiers sell those, if you can't find any yourself.
Once you recover three runes—one each of potency, essence, and aspect—we shall begin the enchanting process.
It's a good thing you happened by! And in an old barrow, no less!\n\nBut tell me, are you a simple admirer or a true devotee of my work?
Don't make any noise! I'm tracking Riekrs!
Hey there. Still no luck with the Sublime Brazier book yet. I've got some thoughts, but nothing solid yet.
Even the simplest contract represents a pact one enters into with the Dark Brotherhood.\n\nTake each contract seriously. After all, we built our reputation on … customer satisfaction.
Are you here about the job? To forestall any confusion—yes, we split the proceeds equally.\n\nAnd no, I will not budge on that point.
I see our family has grown. Good, good. But mind what you say. Our connection to the family is a closely guarded secret, and I prefer to keep it that way.

Finished exploring the Sanctuary? Good. Now go and see Elam.\n\nHe'll start you with a few easy targets, just to get your blade bloody. With a little practice, you'll be ready for something with more meat on its bones in no time.
Let's not start something we'll both regret. I could use some help, and you're going to want to hear what I have to say.

My Lord Vivec wants to meet you. I know the honor might seem overwhelming, but try not to faint when His Holiness talks to you.\n\nI speak from experience. I swooned and passed out the first time we met.
Break me off a piece of the Bloodroot Forge while you're there. It'll get you farther than flowers.
I find that escaping from an ancient trap really gets the heart pumping—provided it doesn't take too long, of course.\n\nI couldn't have done it without your relatively minor contribution. Thank you.
You seem to have survived your visit to the Red Exiles camp. Did you find my brother?
Just have a look at the book. I get the feeling it's not all that happy about our progress.
Another performer? Take the stage whenever you're ready, sweet. I'm not going anywhere.
Best head inland, traveler, far as you can manage. It is only a matter of time before the tempest over Sea Keep moves down the coast, leaving ruin in its wake.
You learn quickly. An invaluable skill. Are you prepared to continue your education?
Be careful, initiate. The fields and deserts around the Iliac Bay present their own risks—even on the best of days.\n\nFarewell.
Welcome back, initiate! No shortage of mud on your feet, I see. Did you manage to seal all the time breaches in the swamp?
Tranquil greetings, initiate. You carry yourself with a victor's confidence. Did you seal the breaches in Rivenspire?

You look capable. I could use some help, if you aren't afraid of a ruthless, dastardly scoundrel.\n\nLet me start again. I represent Cyrodilic Collections, a society dedicated to finding, retrieving, and restoring lost treasures of the Argonians.
Answer quick! Are you a Blackguard or are you the friend Concordia sent me to assist?
We don't have any immediate business to discuss that I know of. What do you want?
I'll stay here and try to keep Kirstaleth calm. I'm shouting, aren't I? I'm sorry!\n\nJust find that flint vine, all right? We'll need quite a bit to reach her.

Kassandra moves quickly for a lukiul of her age. She has more sap in her than I expected.\n\nFriend-Jaxsik will fight Kassandra and Whiptail alone if she catches them. On any other day, I think she would win. But with this staff …. What should we do?

I narrow my eyes.\n\nI know what you seek—you and the Blackguards both. Tsojei and I hack, and cleave, and stab, yet more ojels swim over our borders every day. All looking for the Remnant of Argon. I must find it first. I will find it first.
Satisfied with your visit here? There is no rush.\n\nAnything in particular that caught your interest?

So you're Famia's caretaker, eh? Don't envy you. She's weak. Here in Murkmire, the weak wind up as wamasu food.\n\nName's Whiptail. Kassandra's bodyguard. Don't need your name. You won't be around long enough. Famia's helpers never are.
Have a care with that chime, beeko. Remember, it is older than Shuvu, and Shuvu is topee-rajta … you would say, older than dirt, I think?

Did my revelation surprise you, five-claw? Is it so hard to believe that I am the heir to the throne of Rimmen? Let people think what they will. I know the truth.\n\nNow, let us confer with Abnur Tharn and the rest of the council of war.
Judging by the scope of these security measures, the demon weapon must be even more powerful than I imagined.\n\nLet's see if we can unravel this particular puzzle, shall we?

This one will watch over Queen Khamira. She may not have agreed to let Zamarak resume his post as the King's Claw yet, but she will come around in time.\n\nUntil then, no harm will befall the queen. This Zamarak so swears.

This one is glad you are unharmed. The gate that we need to check should be nearby. It is funny. Vazbi sees the adeptorium from here, but it is so small. So vulnerable, out here in the khaj. \n\nWe should restore the water soon.

By Mara's thighs, if it's not the hero of Riverhold.\n\nMizzik Thunderboots, at your service. This one would offer to buy you a drink, but he has caught the scent of a most curious investigation. No time for taverns while this one's on duty.
Zumog Phoom attempts to raise the Betrayer and Cadwell ran off to face him on his own? The Soul Shriven's brain must have rotted in his head!
Hurray, everybody's here. Could we maybe keep the reunion to a whisper? This cave echoes and my head is killing me.
To quote Wise Reranzar: "in places where many do not walk you find those you do not wish to walk with."\n\nThe beasts that pursued Nazdar may yet remain. Please, be cautious.

It's as I thought. Spirits cling to practically every stone up here. Some more sociable than others. One in particular … it feels welcoming, but old. Wary.\n\nHave a look around. With any luck, at least one of these entities will present itself.
Go ahead and leave while you still can. If only Raz was so lucky.
Hey, I recognize you! Ran a few jobs in Abah's Landing, right? Welcome to Rimmen, where the drinks are sweet and the ground is very, very hard.
Would you like an engraved invitation or can we enter the fortress now?
Have you found anything useful? Dragon hunting techniques, perhaps? Maybe even a weapon?
An island … in the sky? I have no words to make sense of that.
Prepare to defend yourself. It's likely these pirates will give no quarter.
Adara'hai has only seen one place more corrupted than this: the Temple of Seven Riddles. She prays that our foes will not possess the same strength as Rakkhat.
I need time to think, five-claw. Go talk to Sai Sahan.
As excited to hear what news Abnur Tharn brings, this one has no desire to actually stand in the infamous battlemage's presence.
May the Moons protect you on your mission. If you need a helping claw, come find me.\n\nAfter my nap.

I hated leaving Sai Sahan alone with Nahfahlaar, especially in the mood he was in. Get to the Dragonguard Sanctum as soon as you can.\n\nOh. And it's good to see you again. Za'ji and Caska feel the same, even if they won't admit it.
You go on ahead and search for the Clan Mother. We'll make sure no one tries to follow.

With his Dragon priest defeated and his plans foiled, Laatvulon is more vulnerable than ever before. We can't let this opportunity pass us by.\n\nThe time has come to put an end to this Order of the New Moon.

Meet me in Grahtwood. The Skald-King's scouts spotted members of the coven near Boar's Run. We'll start there. Meet me near the overlook at the Elden Root Temple.\n\nAs for the magic, I'll tell you more about that when we're away from prying eyes.
This place. Does all this equipment belong to the people buried here?\n\nIf you can find a weapon, I believe it will benefit us.
I came here after my mother's death. Someone had to handle … arrangements. \n\nTalk to the high priest and ask about the sacred oil. I … I need a moment.

Determining how they create these medallions will be an enormous help.\n\nThe Gray Host has accelerated their plans. They need more medallions for a reason. A big harrowstorm is coming. We need to be ready.
Luck was with us. If we had reached this camp even a few moments later, Sable-Eye would have gotten away with the netherroot brew.
We denied the coven those gray reliquaries, but the harrowstorm … gods, look what it did to Karthwatch!\n\nCome on. The jarl's hall isn't far. It's up on the hill. I hope she's all right.
Nothing waiting to impede our progress? No guards, no witches, nothing. Just a lonely inn on a desolate hillside.\n\nIf Ironbelly's flier led us astray, we're going to head back and kill him again.

We have no idea who Edjar is. Or who took Fenn, for that matter. It could be this Ashen Lord we heard mentioned, or maybe the Icereach Coven.\n\nThe question is, why take Fenn at all? Why not just kill him? Does he have information they need?
Kyne's breath, this place … nothing in the Blue Palace even comes close! Who built it and why? The wealth alone! Is that how they tempted my father?

As I understand it, a vampire called Lady Essenia controls Greymoor Keep. She welcomed the Gray Host and has been working with them to undermine Western Skyrim.\n\nThe very stones of this keep … I sense … something. We need to be on our guard.

Fenn and Svana weren't as helpless as I imagined. Still, it took all my skill not to draw the entire Gray Host down upon us.\n\nLet's get inside and look for that ritual site. We need to destroy the witch pikes or Solitude is doomed.
Acolyte Eivina can't hear me. She's standing right here, but she's … gone.

So we've got a mysterious Breton, possibly working with Reachmen, recruiting workers for some unknown purpose. Plus, there's a smuggler hiding unknown contraband in a warehouse down by the docks.\n\nI say we deal with the smuggler first.

You have done the Bards College a great service. Look at all my fellow musicians playing these fine instruments in concert. Already it is healing old wounds. \n\nMaybe I just finished Maestro Nel's plan. Who can say?

Though we weren't dealing in spirits today, I have no doubt you'd make a fine ghost hunter. It was an honor to work with you.\n\nI think Phebe looks up to you, you've become a point of inspiration for her. I know we both hope our paths cross again.
This is impressive, and that's coming from someone who's been to Oblivion and back.\n\nI can't believe there's someone living down here, but at least it gives us a place to start looking.
Judging by the state of her body, she hasn't been dead very long. \n\nUse the medallion again. The assassin might be nearby.

I've never seen anything like this. That fissure …. Did the stonemelt really do all this? Doesn't matter. We have miners to save.\n\nBy my count, three Orcs are still missing—including the foreman, Mugha.

Jarl Morryn wants Rigurt's help to get the thanes to put aside their silly feud so they can negotiate!\n\nIt's just like the Skald-King always says: you always find Rigurt at the heart of a problem! Because he is so good at fixing them!
I just … need a moment, assistant. I do hope you appreciate that bit of instruction. Puzzles can … puzzles can really, really hurt. Yet another lesson, free of charge.

Oh, hello! Please don't laugh … I'm having a terrible time and this cart isn't even the half of it.\n\nThough, you look rather experienced. Maybe it's fortuitous that you came along! You might be just the right person to help me.
I wasn't joking about Scholar Diel. That woman can talk! Let's get out of here.\n\nWe need to reach Viridian Watch and see if we can locate some evidence of this mysterious survivor.
Keep looking, my friend. We can still catch up to Rada al-Saran and Lady Belain if we hurry.

A moment. Sometimes the intensity of the currents flowing through the darkness can be … overwhelming. There.\n\nFennorian reports that Gray Host leaders gather north of Markarth. I believe Rada is there, preparing them for what's to come.

Verandis is certainly entrusting you with a lot of responsibility. You better not fail him, especially while he's dealing with whatever the Dark Heart is doing to him.\n\nI'll meet you at Nighthollow Keep and we'll learn what we can about the Void.
