The ard is in his throne room. We just need to know where to find the land sundered from Tamriel. According to Rada al-Saran's letter, it's somewhere in the Reach.\n\nOh, and I'm not apologizing. Not to Caddach, anyway. Sorry.
Gods, I've never seen Verandis struggle like this. How can he expect me to go to Bthar-Zel and leave him to deal with this on his own?\n\nDon't worry. I know my duty. It's just … hard sometimes.
A study, from the looks of it. See if you can find something I can draw a memory from.
Did you see that? That crystal thing clearly reacted. It pulsed as I approached it!

Five-claw? Adusa doesn't know what twist of the tail brought you here, but she finds your presence most fortuitous.\n\nI could use an extra set of eyes to watch my back. What say you, my friend? Are your eyes still sharp? Will you aid this one again?

The ritual was a success. Our union has been blessed by Hircine himself! I'm not certain what the spirit showed us, but I'll figure it out eventually. I always do.\n\nAre you ready to search for the keystone now, harrier? I think I know where to begin.
If you don't mind, stranger, talk to Eslyn. I have a lot to think about right now.

Removing curses is never an easy endeavor. And with Stibbons in his current state … well, you should see for yourself.\n\nThe priest graciously provided a hut where I could store the results of my manservant's latest debacle. We can start there.
Governor Keshu and I were talking. I think we have a plan, but you should talk to her. She's going to want to fill you in on the details herself.
Damn it! I'm too late. Poor Councilor Jirich. She didn't deserve to die like that. At least, I don't think she did.\n\nDid you see what happened? Who attacked her?
This place, something's not right. I have a feeling this is no smuggler's cave.
When I was freed from my vault, it took months for my own power to reach such levels, and then it nearly destroyed me. I'm surprised Calia's gotten to that point so quickly after her release.
Oblivion take me, he's dead! Tiras is dead! This is a catastrophe! What are we going to do?
There's another ward on the door ahead. Ready to see if we can open it?

You waiting for me? Figured you'd take the lead, seeing as I don't know the first thing about exploring ruins. \n\nDon't worry, I'll follow close and listen for any ornery plants looking to get the drop on us.
Duchess Astella? What is she doing here?\n\nGo on and talk to her, but be careful. Something about this doesn't feel right.
When you're ready, place a hand on Annyce's forehead and start counting sails.
It looks like Ardia will be all right. Hopefully she can make a successful escape this time.
What did Renna say? Oh, right. You need to knock two times. No more, no less. It's a code so he knows that it's safe to open the door.
Well, that was thrilling! Now, we should make our way to the central chamber of the Keywright's Gallery!

There's no doubt. Someone murdered the novitiates here and stored the memories in this stone.\n\nThat's why Granna Cerise gave the stone to Grandpa. She knew something. She was hunting the murderer! I guess we should search the top floor. Gods help us.
Maybe someone on the inn's staff knows Inalieth? Or remembers her, anyway.

The creatures you catch at each vent will be my conduit to their nature spirits. Then, I'll need your help to perform the ritual. \n\nNow, let's hurry. Time is short and we don't want to try and dance with lava!
What an arse. I can see why mom wasn't keen to visit all these years.\n\nI can't believe she's spent so many years trying to please that fetcher.
We still need to find the Ravener. Let's hope we learn more about this mysterious prey of its along the way. We might use that against it.
Madam Whim said to use the amulet to guide us, right? Let's do that and look around. I doubt she'd mislead us.

You made it! I was only a little worried that you'd disappear and make me face the Folly alone. \n\nRight. Are you ready to head for the energy fonts? They're probably where the lightning is striking the most. I'd say over in that direction.
My enemies will rue the day they crossed me! Rue the day, I say!\n\nOh, hello, mortal master!

We have a common goal. Surely there is no need for elaboration or further discussion.\n\nOr do mortals frequently trouble others with random questions? Feel some special need to express irrelevant thoughts?

Perhaps you have questions, mortal? You wonder about this Dremora's shell? Why it's important? We don't die, of course.\n\nSomeone chose to send Tephilaz to Oblivion. This could bring chaos. Disrupt the town's stability. I need to find who.
Valkynaz Nokvroz mentioned a blind old fool. Could he have been talking about Elegian? And what was that about an elixir? Let's keep looking.
The daedrat ran off. I expected as much.

We're not getting in through the main door.\n\nLuckily, I spotted three potential entry points—another door to the east, a cave to the west, and a bridge overhead that connects to the roof. One of those should lead to the bathhouse courtyard.
Do not be offended, but I have learned at some point in my buried past, to move quietly and carefully alone, no matter where I am.\n\nNever fear, I will meet you outside the Blood Pit.

Our first order of business is investigating the auction house. It's just there, near the Nereid's fountain. Gather testimony, correspondence, anything you can.\n\nWhen you've discovered enough, meet me in the market near the Shambles' north entrance.

He saw me and panicked. He keeps going on about Gilfrex, but I don't know who that is. Perhaps he'll be more cooperative for someone less … transparent.\n\nOn the bright side, I seem to be more substantial than we initially thought.

Good, you found my field office. I thought I'd keep an eye on the loch while awaiting your report.\n\nMy own investigations have turned up little about our missing ships. Tell me, did you uncover anything useful? Did the lighthouse keeper spot them?

I believe the Greycloak encampment is just outside the town's limits. Gather reinforcements, if you see fit, but look for the blessed awl. I'm not sure what use the bandits have for an object given by Zenithar, but his faithful need it back.
We've got a small hitch in this rope. The key to the catacombs entrance is usually right near the door … but someone took it.
The worthy must stay clear-minded in unfamiliar situations. They devise solutions to unexpected conundrums. Think through the challenge and keep your wits.\n\nGood luck, challenger.
Meet me at the ritual circle, on top of the rise that overlooks the village. We can talk there.
Somewhere within the warrens should be an executioner's block. Just what we need for this weapon.

The last ward is inside the cave. I hate caves. They're usually wet and dark and full of creepy crawlies. Eugh.\n\nBut once we restore that ward, my spell will at least be contained within Tor Draioch. Then we can concentrate on fixing it.
Since you're the first person I've encountered in this damn jungle who isn't trying to kill me, let's assume we're going to be friends.\n\nI'm High King Emeric. Pleasure to make your acquaintance.

Mistmouth Cave is known for its hot springs. The locals sometimes visit them … when there isn't some band of smugglers hiding out here. But judging by the steam, the springs must be boiling now.\n\nWhat would the Ascendant Order want here?

Excellent work finding that last mark from Oblan. Perhaps you've worked in the smuggling business before, hmm? Surely you don't keep secrets from me, do you?\n\nHa, no, keep your privacy. Oblan's mark says he went east. Let's follow him.
This is very embarrassing. We have to ask <<1>> and <<2>> to pay their portion of the bill. Or else the innkeeper won't return my scepter of office.\n\nI guess we should go find them.
She—they're … gone. Dead. How could this happen?

Oh, hello. If you're one of those horrid prisoners come to rob me, I'm afraid my current situation has left me quite destitute.\n\nBut come to think of it, if you'd be willing to help me out, I can promise you a sizable chunk of gold. What do you say?

I thought I knew Song so well when we lived together in Skywatch. But I had no idea she was part of such a powerful family. I suspected she came from wealth, but she never even mentioned the Emerald Eye.\n\nI guess we need to go talk to this uncle.

Fell's Run … that's northeast of Shornhelm, I think. I looked at a lot of maps growing up.\n\nWe had better find her alive and well in Rivenspire or the princess detective is going to have a whole different problem to investigate.
Not now. I'm having a rather trying day and would prefer not to be bothered at this particular point in time.

The ancient sea captain has brought you and I into his fancies. He thinks I'm his brother. And he's given you the role of his long-lost love. I suppose her ghost did flow into you.\n\nTalk to m'lady and play along. Try to learn more about this curse.

Heard all that, eh? Guiffa's a palms-up cardsharp. One of the best Tribute players in town. But, like I always say, if you want to take the measure of a graht, you've got to climb!\n\nThat nose ring gibe was unnecessary, right? I'll get her next time!
You should have seen the look on Varnauld's face when I beat him. I wanted to punch him in the face when I first met him, but this was so much better!

Investigate the camps. Try to find any trace of Wyress Tola or where the Firesong might have taken her. And if you find any Firesong, run them through. Those path-traitors need to be cut down like the invasive weeds they are!

We didn't find Wyress Tola, but we did learn that Archdruid Michiel seeks a nature spirit and is interested in Hag Fen. Not to mention that strange totem inscribed with the word Frii.\n\nMaybe that's enough to point our bow in the right direction.

Well met, friend! Dhulef tells me you handled yourself well at Windwrack Fort. Now, what news of the other two locations?\n\nLaurel seemed troubled when she returned. But she went to find Archdruid Rahval before I could speak to her.

Take a right when you get into the fort. There's a path that leads down to the docks. You'll find the ballistas there.\n\nMy guess is the Dreadsail ships will flee at the first sign of resistance—they won't risk their ships to ballista strikes.
Za'ji is beginning to think that piracy is less dangerous than politics. This one definitely chose the safer occupation.

Captain Marguerite has a reputation for fairness and honesty. Even among the Society of the Steadfast, she's considered an exemplary knight and leader.\n\nTalk to her and find out what she knows about the shipment and the Shard of the Green.
The crates the courier delivered were intended for Steadfast Manor. I wonder why she was hired to bring them here?
Sailing into battle aboard a Sea Elf pirate ship? I never imagined I'd do that.\n\nTalk to Captain Siravaen when you're ready to board. My knights and I will be right behind you.
I don't know if the lordling's mad plan has any chance of success, but I'll get you to Y'ffelon. \n\nI think Sir Stefan wants to talk to you before we set sail, though.
Listen to the song only I can hear. Find the three druid stones and awaken them. On the hills around us. Search north, west. Find. Turn.\n\nThen the door will open. Open, for me.
Do you think you can tell Octin to stop flitting around? He's making it really hard to think and I'm in enough pain already,

With Veshin's key, we can slip into the sea witch lair and grab the relic. Once we contain it, that is.\n\nI should give Umindior another chance. Go back to camp and tell him what we learned. I'll stay behind to make Veshin a little … cozier.

The muse-mouth plant. It is through the spirit motes they exude that we can commune with the Chronicle. Druids can sense when the spirit has a story to share with us. I sense that now.\n\nYou should experience this, outsider. My gift to you.
I always believed the Sea Elves to be standoffish. But now I find them quite passionate indeed. A pleasant surprise.

Thank Y'ffre it's you. I need someone I can trust. The Eldertide ran afoul of the path-traitor Firesong and their parasitic Dreadsails in the area.\n\nI'm doing what I can to help their wounded. Blight. You look like you have news. What is it?
I observed the effluvium of possibility and noticed a proliferation of sudden potential. I assume that indicates you were successful? Did you have any trouble acquiring the Emerald Glyphic?
One day, I'll get that slippery eel. If we're lucky, that may be today.
See there? The ritual formation. A battering ram through the door into the Crux.\n\nHelp us shatter it. Then we can find others like it.
I 'm sorry. I don't have a clue of where I am or where I'm going. I must think about things.
You should catch up with Meenai-Shai. I will think more on this situation, and hopefully there will be more answers than questions soon.

Such disarray! Huzmargo had only just finished a deep cleanse of the facilities last week, and now these creatures shamble all over it. The work of a cipher never ends.\n\nResetting the focus should help get things back in order.
Let me see that letter.\n\nSo, Reynila came by, pestering this Deredrien for help. Why?

I followed a disturbance in the threads of fate to this location, mortal. Now we hover over a precipice. Enemies of my master have invaded his realm. As much as I hate the idea, we need to follow them and protect Apocrypha.\n\nNow, enter the portal.
Nathyn must be all right. With Sathile protecting him—if something terrible had happened to him, we'd know. Right?

You two go on ahead. I need to gather Reynila's research and … prepare to travel light for a while.\n\nWe always knew this day might come. Thankfully, we always tried to remain ready for just such an occasion.

I know the effect I have on people. I either scare them or attract them. And they can't take their eyes off me. But few ever dare approach me, let alone try to strike up a conversation.\n\nSo, what do you want to say to me, hero?
Voidprowler Zavaal. The clan leader probably has Madam Whim's secret, yes? Let's go, then.
You talk to Mevei. I'll make sure we don't have anyone following us.
This is everything I feared. Sweet Mora's eyes this is embarrassing.
The Underweave is a powerful nexus of fated potential in Chroma Incognito. Terribly powerful, terribly dangerous. \n\nSounds just like Martina to set up a lab there. Onward and upward!

The bristleback lords seem like overgrown swine while they're asleep. It's strange—I don't like it. Everything's different here now. \n\nWe have to find Cipher Frielvi. She's the only one who knows how I can get past the barrier keeping me here.
I'm not sure how much more of this Daedric mischief I can take.
I'm not a hero. Just a minor Watchling functionary in service to the Great Eye. So you'll have to excuse me if I appear incapable of rational thought right now.

What started in the Panopticon has spread beyond into other parts of Apocrypha. Gadayn and I have seen its effects here among the stacks.\n\nWhile you investigate the corruption in Cipher's Midden, I shall try to determine where to find Vaermina.
Obviously, Anudnabia's lost shrine sunk into the sea ages ago. A fitting end for a place dedicated to the Master of the Tides of Fate, but that will make it difficult to reach.
Go through the portal, proxy. I need a moment with Curate Gadayn. We shall follow in due course.
Let's go, mortal. Those instabilities won't investigate themselves.
Glad we found Gaius among the living. Grab that map and we'll track down the key to the catacombs. I want to make certain the staff and remaining legionaries are safe.
I think it worked! Abolisher certainly looks full of energy now to me! I'll see you back at my townhouse in Skingrad.

Head downstairs and scout the area. I'll follow along shortly. I need to try to … make things right with Ursilia. And maybe I have something in my alchemy kit to deal with the wine in her system. Just the smell of it makes me … hungry.

A bittersweet ending. This one appreciates that Otho and Betu will be looked after, Mizzik only wishes there had been less bloodshed along the way. To think all this began with Uriel's death all those years ago.
We must be close, proxy. Keep moving.
That manifestation is like the one in the library at Holamayan. It appeared the moment you came into sight. Who knew there were so many ancient memories just lying around everywhere?
The stables are nearby, right on the edge of town. If Grivier's there, I'll make him talk.

Looks like we've got multiple options for getting inside. From what I recall, we'll find the stairs to the buried halls in the middle of the stockade. Assuming the Recollection hasn't blocked them up, that is.

I've had my share of strange adventures, but helping you battle Daedra and save all of existence? That's beyond even the stories my little sister Eveli enjoys so much. Wait until I tell her all about it!
You were in there for a while. What did Nantharion have to say?
The Lamp of Clarity's energy has been restored. I'll see you back at Beragon's townhouse.
I don't hear any more calls for help. We helped everyone we could. That'll have to be enough.\n\nLet's keep looking for Greenspeaker Sorilen. I need to know if she survived the disaster.
I fear I'm very busy at the moment. Unless you have business with me, please feel free to carry on.
I am surprised you were not injured, proxy. Unrolling the Skein of Secrets appeared to precipitate a reciprocal paroxysm that—that is, it triggered a backlash. As I am sure you noticed.

I know this. It is a doorway to the Many Paths. I cannot describe the relief that comes with even a modicum of understanding.\n\nThat lamp wanted to reveal that doorway. Step through and I will follow.
The commander gave you some critical tasks. You need to hurry.\n\nDon't worry about taking your eye off the enemy. I have your back, comrade.
Look at it fly! Do your best to keep up with it. We don't want to get lost in here.

Greetings, wanderer. I am Krin'ze, a Twilight Cantor. A singer in service to Azurah. \n\nDid you happen to see the falling star? A sure sign from the Mother of All Khajiit that someone is in great need. I am certain of it.
These are the Twilight Cantors you told me of? Their methods leave me speechless. Instead of helping the dro-m'Athra, they destroyed it!\n\nGive me a moment and speak with the ja'rithantii there.
There is much to understand about what went wrong today. How were the Ceythalmor able to find us? There's much to consider. \n\nThe Garland Ring will take its time before we make a move again.
If you'll excuse me, I've got Mages Guild business on the mind. I'm sure you're keeping busy, too!
Thank you for coming. The guild will make this worth your time, rest assured. \n\nHead through the door over there, I'll be right behind you.

The Indrik has given you a series of challenges? Excellent. Things are proceeding apace. Do your best to fulfill his wishes. \n\nGaining the Indrik's favor may help you connect to the other Luminaries.

You have restored the altar. May you stride forward with an understanding of the power you wield.\n\nYour magic will leave marks on this world. Whether they be scars or fingerprints remains to be seen.

Naku's as stubborn as a stump. But if you got Knives to part with his drink—however briefly—and come here, then this shouldn't be too hard.\n\nWe'll keep looking for leads on the murderer while you're gone.

The Imperial Legion gave me that ring back when I served as a proud member of the Scarlets. It ordained me as chaplain of the squad. The ring is proof before the Divines of who I once was. I can't bear to lose it.
I have to say, you're the first stranger I met who was willing to pay off my bar tab. Well, there was that trapper in White Rose, but it turns out—you know what? That's a story for another time.
My advice, mortal, is not to jump to action. Careful thought is in precious short supply in the world.\n\nTake a seat, or a perch. And see if a solution does not present itself.
Nable of the Fetch! Hah! That got me.
I would never tell you to stay away from my beauty, Not-Ulfsild. Bask in it. Be humbled.\n\nBut if the Crow's wing is unlocked, waiting for you … perhaps the basking can wait.
It should be easy enough to unmake the ward and free my friend. For you, at least! \n\nMagic isn't my thing.

Our time together has been most impressive. Perhaps in a past life, you walked this world as a gryphon. \n\nIn the meantime, I'll try to keep the Fox from meddling too much in your other affairs. I make no promises.
The moment people like this Reeve Nardarmor sit behind a desk, they start looking for a way to get rich. Or more rich. It's like this everywhere! Ugh.\n\nAnything good in that journal?
If he knows what's good for him, he'll talk.

Echo Pond is north of Marbruk, just beyond Driladan Pass. Hopefully we can find something I can work with there. It's the last place Snapdragon lists in her journal. \n\nThe last place Wisteria went before … well. Yeah.
You have now seen how I first met Ravith. It was … an inauspicious start.

We must go to Star Haven Adeptorium. The Twilight Cantors are key to the Rajaska's plans. I am certain that we will find Ravith and her kindred attempting to find purchase there.\n\nWe have little time. We should depart swiftly.
Not now, tamiit! We fight!
I was about to come looking for you when High Cantor Viti found me.\n\nShe demanded to know what I was doing here. Do not worry. I did not mention either of you.

The little prince—Prince Azah—he'll do fine. He's a born leader. Me, I'm just a street brawler in a nice suit of armor.\n\nHead for the Worm Nest. I'll meet you there after I talk to Azah and round up a few Fighters Guild comrades to help us.

So much death, and I can sense the residue of necrotic energy clinging to the remains of this vile contraption.\n\nShow that note you found to Prince Azah. Then you might want to go to the Fighters Guildhall in Shornhelm to tell Skordo what happened.

Obviously, I need no introduction. Everyone has heard of Vanus Galerion, founder and leader of the Mages Guild.\n\nI understand that you were instrumental in driving the Worm Cult from our sanctum. Describe what you saw, please. I require every detail.

Go on to the Fighters Guildhall here in Shornhelm. We need to let Skordo and the others know that Guildmaster Merric is … dead. I'll meet you there after Gabrielle and I … take care of things here.\n\nAfter that, though? We hunt worms.
I have a really good feeling about the daisies. I don't know why I didn't think of them before. After you've given them to her, please come let me know right away what she says.
If these are to be this soldier's last moments, praying with her is the least I can do. Please. Leave us be.
Let's hurry. Stenwick needs our help.
Virmar sent you just in time! I'm glad she did, too. You look very capable.
Ah, you brought a spectral friend. Nicely done.
You've mastered a number of recipes. It's time for a test, wouldn't you say?\n\nAre you ready to become an apprentice?
<<1>> is near the log bridge to the pirate camp. He's been watching them, waiting for our chance to get those relics.
Ogres Bluff is east of Bergama in the Hallowed Wastes. It's a fair trip from here along the southern border of Alik'r.\n\nThe bridge will be obvious. This one will wait for you on the western end.
If you want to join the Mages Guild, please see the magister. I have pressing issues I must attend to.
Adept. Shalidor must have found you.\n\nVery glad to see you again. I've translated the final book, and we're ready to monkey rum butter.
I have an urgent message for you!
This place. It's familiar, yet not. As if Sheogorath stole a piece of the Summerset Isles.\n\nHe must be mocking me. My long-lost Sanctuary shares some similarities to this place ….
We'll walk the path together, yes. I'll be relying on you, Hallowed. To be brave for me, for her.
Improvise, he says. I can't believe we're risking our lives to rescue that skeeving horker.
My friend. You cannot imagine how grateful I am to see you. I have need of a veteran in the Queen's service today. What brings you to Arenthia?

I'm relieved you're here, my friend. As dark as my fears may have been, they pale in comparison to the reality.\n\nIf the Shade of Naemon corrupts the Heart of Valenwood, then the realm he calls the Shadow Wood will soon consume this one.
We'll walk the path together, yes. I'll be relying on you, Hallowed. To be wise for me, for her.
Sai's been through a lot, but it looks like he can walk on his own. That's a good sign.
Our little tour of Sai's doubts, fears and desires was fascinating, wasn't it? Who knew that in the solitude of his own bedchamber, he dreams of large women?
You have done it! Open the vault door, Vestige!
The sooner you get that door open, the sooner we can get out of here.
I don't believe those doors are going to open themselves.
You make Rivenspire a safer place with every task you complete. You had a taste with Two-Blades. Ready for something with a little more meat on its bones?
My expedition is ruined! One catastrophe after another! \n\nOh, we meet again! You wouldn't happen to be interested in performing a few light duties, would you? I'm in need of a temporary assistant.
Thank you. I'm fairly competent with a dueling blade, but I'm out of my element here. Let's start in the manor house. There has to be some clue there.

Someone in town must know what happened to Dethisam. He loves to visit and chat with all of our neighbors.\n\nCome on. The sooner we find my brother, the sooner I can start thinking about dealing with the plague.
Don't worry, if you happen to be turned, we'll be sure to come looking for you. Swords in hand.
Has the cold rooted your feet from this great distance? Go to Direfrost Keep. Free it from the ice witch's grasp and return Undaunted!
When I'm refining jute, I sing to help pass the time. Not too loud—I don't want to disturb the other clothiers.

Potency, essence, and aspect. All beneath the stars bear these component concepts. When combined they form glyphs, which add enchantments to items.\n\nFirst, you'll find these component runes. Then, I will have you create a glyph.
What a tale you'll have to tell, adventuring with the famous Narsis Dren!
I never thought I'd be acting on the advice of a dirty lunatic who talks to rodents. If The Rat is wrong about this Dragonfires business, I'm going to track him down and put him out of his misery.

Not everyone appeals to the Dark Brotherhood through the Black Sacrament. For those with copious amounts of gold to spare, we usually indulge their more mundane requests.\n\nAre you ready to take on your first contract?
Looking for more work? That's the spirit! Head back to the Sanctuary. I'm sure Elam or the Speaker know someone that needs killing.

Explore the Sanctuary, meet the others. At least the ones currently at home. I believe Green-Venom-Tongue, Kor, Hildegard, Mirabelle, Cimbar, and Tanek are available.\n\nWhen you're done, Elam should have a new task for you to accomplish.
I'll be along shortly. When you get to Vivec City, head directly for Lord Vivec's Palace. Once there, I'll make introductions and we can tell the Warrior-Poet everything we've learned.
Those Daedra will strip you of everything you hold dear. Makes winning it back all the sweeter.
Who's out there? No, never mind. I don't care. I just want to get out of here.\n\nIt's dark and it's cramped and it smells like an Argonian's armpit.

Chodala went to meet with the Red Exiles leader and hasn't returned. If I enter the camp and have to kill any of those foolish outcasts, it could have serious repercussions for our negotiations.\n\nFind my brother and I'll help you with your quest.
Thank you so much for lending a hand. Honestly, if I had known this tome would cause so much trouble, I never would have opened it!
We need to keep moving.
Ah, greetings, initiate. You arrive not a moment too soon. I assume that Josajeh gave you a summary of our predicament?

May the Old Way guide your steps. The Loremaster was very impressed by your work in Summerset. He's a hard mer to know, but he's always been generous with his praise.\n\nI just wish I could be a better student.
Old Ways protect you, initiate. Hopefully we'll have something for you when you return.
May the Old Ways guide your steps, my friend.\n\nThis phrase is doubly important in Rivenspire, initiate. In the shadow of Doomcrag, a single misstep can result in bloody disaster. Be cautious.

Ah, friend! How good to see you again!\n\nWe'll be heading to Murkmire soon to join my sister. If you want to help Cyrodilic Collections prepare for the expedition, talk to Jee-Lar. I'm sure he could use your assistance with something or another.
You were quick, though not as quick as Jee-Lar, and that's a fact!
Now, to my offer.
The symbols on the columns and the counterweights are the key, I'm certain. It's just a matter of figuring out the sequence!

Beeko! Thank the Hist. I thought I had lost you. I am sorry I left you behind, but I had to give chase. Kassandra took the staff—a gift of the dream-wallow, and the key to the Remnant of Argon, yes?\n\nJaxsik chases her, but I could not keep up.
Famia … smarter than some ojels, but still scratching to get into wisdom's egg. Without stronger claws, she will never succeed.
This is the egg-tenders' dwelling. Please, take a look around. Speak with our root-kin. We Bright-Throats are gracious hosts.

The Wither-Vault? Seizo …. I would not go there if there was any other way, beeko. I tumbled into it once as a hatchling. I vowed I would never go back.\n\nIt is a bad place full of bad things. The perfect place for a sacred chime, right? Ha.
Our people grumble, but they will help prepare Riverhold's defenses. I just hope we can get everything in place before the inevitable attack arrives.

We're looking for anything that appears to be Khajiiti in origin. Perhaps a new addition or alterations to an existing structure.\n\nI still haven't pinpointed my shadow, so I'll be saving my energy for an emergency. Any lesser threats I leave to you.
Vazbi hopes we can find the problem soon. Otherwise, we may have to investigate the Baan Dar Span.
A crowded marketplace, a chance meeting. Unexpected, unannounced … and perhaps just the thing this one needs to solve a most curious investigation. \n\nMizzik Thunderboots, at your service.
These episodes of Cadwell's, they are disturbing.\n\nTalk to him, five-claw. Get him to explain exactly what he sees.
I need a moment. Or two. Look, I'll meet you at the Bowel … once the world stops spinning.
Said Nalitha the Avuncular: "Even in somber times must the wayfarer be offered greetings."\n\nNazdar greets you, wayfarer, though his times are somber indeed. What brings you to this one?
The Khajiiti spirit called Arum-Khal the Dark Adept and the ancient defiler. Could Arum-Khal's fate and the fate of the Hidden Moon adepts be intertwined?

The farmstead is just across the bridge, on the southern side of the valley.\n\nIn the meantime, Raz will try to convince his family to stay out of the fields. Perhaps they will be reasonable today. That would be a welcome change, yes?
Great day for a stroll, eh? Or, you know … a thrilling leap.

I'll be fine … magic just takes more out of me than it used to.\n\nGo with Sai and find a way into the fortress. The sooner we learn how the cultists move between here and the island, the sooner we can put an end to Kaalgrontiid.
It seems that we have use for that grappling bow, after all.\n\nYou should search the archives above. Gather anything you believe may prove useful to our efforts.

Our new companions certainly love to quarrel.\n\nZa'ji wants to infiltrate the encampment and take Nartise by surprise. Caska, on the other hand, suggests we launch a frontal assault and deal with him directly.
Vijari wants to see you, walker. He doesn't have much time left.
I do not want to imagine Tharn alone on that island. We must gather our forces and get back to him quickly, five-claw.\n\nI fear time is running out for all of us.
If Za'ji knew that delivering messages was part of official Dragonguard business, he may have refused membership. Ah, well.\n\nAeliah can fill you in on the pertinent details.
Don't you know that interruptions at nap time cause mange of the fur?
We've been tracking you for hours! Luckily, Caska never forgets a scent.\n\nSai Sahan needs you back at the Dragonguard Sanctum. Something about a letter and a new threat to Pellitine.
Sai Sahan is just up ahead. You should speak to him before moving on to the inner temple.
My friend, you look like you've been to Oblivion and back. What matter of trial did you face?

Meet me in Deshaan. The Skald-King's scouts spotted members of the coven near the Shrine to Saint Rilms. We'll start there.\n\nAs for the magic, I'll tell you more about that when we're away from prying eyes.

Yes … that was blood. But, I swear there's no cause for alarm. Not every vampire is a monster.\n\nI'm part of a group that only drinks from willing donors. We regulate the actions of less scrupulous vampires.
Knowing the orders my father has been issuing of late, you might need my help to acquire Arkay's sacred oil. I'll meet you at the Hall of the Dead.
Lyris was right. This camp is crawling with the Icereach Coven. And they're definitely producing the medallions here. I was even able to slip away with one.\n\nWe need to get closer, though.
Sable-Eye has the netherroot brew! We need to go after him.

Let's find the rest of the gray reliquaries before that coven witch can harvest them.\n\nEven if I'm wrong about their purpose, it's obvious the reliquaries are important to the coven. For that reason alone, we need to destroy them.

We need to walk the rest of the way from here. According to the flier, this path up the mountain leads to the Grinning Horker inn.\n\nYou go first but be ready for anything. We don't know how long the coven has been using this place.

Burnt journal pages, Fenn's flask, and a strange, old key … all found among clear signs of a struggle. But other than what's in the flask, we didn't see any blood. That means Fenn was probably taken alive.
I'm not sure what's in these flasks, but Fenn told me not to shake them. Or drop them. Or breathe on them too hard.\n\nLet's get inside and find the ritual site before the harrowstorm begins.

Stay calm, stay calm. Lyris knows what she's doing. As long as we stay by her side, we'll be all right. Won't we?\n\nNever mind me. I'm just trying to come to terms with a plan that has us rushing headlong into a fortress full of Gray Host warriors.

Cross the bridge or use the sluice gate to get into the inner courtyard. Then find the keep's side entrance, east of the main stairs.\n\nI'll stay with Svana and Fenn. Make sure they don't get themselves killed. We'll meet you inside as soon as we can.

Look for Hjolt, Direnna, and Roligmolf at the stables, then meet me at the Pilgrims' lodge. I will head there after I finish caring for these injured souls.\n\nMeridia's light shine upon you, good friend.
Sometimes you charge ahead and sometimes you step in a steaming pile of mammoth dung. I'll let you deal with the princess.
You should get moving. We don't know how long the assassin will stay in one place.
You still have the stonemelt right? Use the rest of it to unblock the door!

Oh, thank you, friend! Rigurt wouldn't want these thanes to think less of him for something so silly.\n\nMeet Rigurt at Jarl Morryn's hunting lodge. There, we broker a great peace treaty between Eastern and Western Skyrim!

Hesitating? Well, that's a bit uncharacteristic. Honestly, where's your sense of adventure? Go on. Pull the lever.\n\nI'll be right over here if anything happens, so you have nothing to worry about. I'm behind you, assistant. One-hundred percent!
Good, you're back. I found Jeanard and I see you managed to return with the rest. Show-off. \n\nNow that we settled that matter, what did the Pyre Watch warrior tell you about the Gray Host?

Your defeat of Lady Belain has ended a great danger to the people of the Reach. Well done, my friend.\n\nHowever, I have heard worrisome rumors from Western Skyrim. You might want to visit Solitude and determine if that's where Rada fled to.
I knew something was wrong. He's been trying to hide it, but the Dark Heart is doing something to him.

I've got bad news and worse news. Caddach and I already exchanged words, most of them insults.\n\nThe only agreement we came to was that he'd stop sending his Stonehands to toss me out if I stopped breaking their noses.
Count Verandis seems … not his usual self.\n\nBut he wants to talk to you. Please, hear what he has to say.

Let's you and I split up and search the keep while Gwendis returns to Markarth. We know Lady Belain has something in mind for the city and one of us should be close at hand.\n\nInside, look for personal items. I can use them to glean information.
Stay close and follow me.
Hmm. This one requires an extra set of eyes. To watch her back, you understand?\n\nWhat say you, five-claw? Are your eyes sharp? Will you aid Adusa-daro?
Go on. Toss the components you gathered into the fire. They're our offering to the spirits.

This may seem like the perfect spot to ambush us and take our belongings, outsider, but don't let the desolation fool you. Our clan warriors are hiding right behind those rocks.\n\nSo, what do you want from us?

You there! Are you for hire? What am I saying? Of course you are. Just look at you! You have the desperate appearance of a mercenary and the swagger of an adventurer.\n\nI regret to admit that my manservant has left me with an indomitable mess. Again!
You're back! I want to hear everything that happened, but you should talk to Governor Keshu first.
Something very bad is going on here. We need to be cautious.
I wonder what Quistley's gotten himself mixed up in now. It's the first time he's led me to somewhere other than a disreputable tavern or a bedchamber where he didn't belong.

Right. I'll stay here and inspect the instruments. Again. If I didn't find any flaws the first three times, I doubt I'll find any now, but who knows?\n\nMaybe Tiras is right. Maybe this is just a huge waste of time.
I want to find out what's so important that Leovic had to stick it in a warded and sealed Daedric vault.
These Argonians seem to be doing something with the harrada creeper. They've got a nasty reputation, too. I think we should see what they're up to.
Don't stray too far. I've handled these ghostly encounters well so far, but something about this chapel really chills my blood.

I'm afraid I only have a cursory knowledge of the Captain Wereshark series. I find adventure stories rather shallow for a genre that professes to explore great depths.\n\nTry flipping through that book for inspiration, or improvise.
Damn it, Ardia. If only you'd managed to escape.\n\nAt least we were able to end the ritual before it consumed her soul. May she rest with her kind.

This is sounding more and more like an Investigator Vale novel all the time!\n\nLet's find Renna's house. I want to finally meet Farrul Lupus in person so he can tell me everything he knows about the emperor's secret.
Can you believe this? Just look around. With this arcane helix exposed, the chamber is positively crackling with magic!\n\nThe Keywright's Gallery has come to life! And I finally think I know why.
Go on. Use the stone again! Let's see what memory it reveals.

This all would have been much easier if Lord Silvelle hadn't concealed so much from me. I imagine he'd say that he did it for my own good, but I admit, I've got some ugly suspicions about his motives. \n\nWhat game was he playing?

Ah, my butterfly found me a strong helper!\n\nIf you're out here chasing butterflies, perhaps you have time to assist the druids of the Stonelore Circle with a matter of great importance. I'm not as young as I used to be and could use your help.
Getting the cold shoulder from a corpse. That's a new shame for the books.\n\nMaybe he'll speak to you.

The Ravener completely drained this man's life spirit. Not only can it speak, but it uses magic as well. I thought I understood what it was. But I knew nothing.\n\nDoesn't matter. We still need to destroy it. Show me what you found.
I don't like this place at all. Let's find what we need and get out of here.

Thank the three! I have the Mother Stones I got from Almalexia's priest—though we do still need to attune them with the energy fonts inside. But, with your help, we'll free Nilera and Sovisa's spirits in no time! \n\nNow, to enter the Folly ….
Kynmarcher Jynd's foundry lies just to the north of Wretched Spire. You can find Zynoahz's gaol east of Burning Gyre Keep, in the Burn.\n\nI will meet you at each site.

What do you see, mortal? A Dremora shell on the ground? What does that matter? We don't die, after all.\n\nCould bring chaos. Disrupt the town's stability. Someone knew this and sent Tephilaz back to Oblivion. I need to know who. You can help.
The Blood Pit. If names are omens, then this is a dire one. After what Arox told us about the place, I admit I wouldn't want to set foot there until we exhausted every other lead we had.
You brought the daedrat? For what purpose? In case you have forgotten, battle awaits us at the top of this mountain. I have no patience for the antics of your pet.
See if we can use that door to get into the bathhouse. I'll stay here and keep watch.
Imagine that, Arox knows of Blind Elegian as well. He's anxious to speak to you.
Ah, my dauntless companion from the Clockwork City. Bounding from one mysterious realm to another, I see. This is fortuitous.\n\nI find myself in need of someone with your skills.
I'll go on ahead to Wretched Spire and attempt to locate Shiro-dar. Hopefully, he's more cooperative than Morah.

Lord Bacaro's conference can't proceed without that cargo. Here's what I need you to do.\n\nCheck the inn, the lighthouse, and the Loch Abhain Shallows. See if anyone knows or saw anything. Then meet me outside the north gate to compare notes.

With a work ethic like that, you have to be a special child of Zenithar! I'll begin the work to prepare this wood for weaving. \n\nBut you—your diligence has proven your worthiness. I'd be honored to explain what happened to the blessed awl.

The catacombs are beneath the castle's chapel. We should just be able to grab a key near the stairs. I'll meet you there.\n\nWith luck, this one should be fairly straightforward. Not counting the ghosts, of course.
Continue south out of this room and through the caves. You will find the Trial of Wits just beyond.\n\nOr you can take the shortcut through the east wall, if heights don't scare you.
Our village lies at the center of the grove. Once we get there, I will tell the archdruid and the other elders what we learned.
The prison warrens should have what we're looking for. It's on the north side of the tower, sunken deep into the earth.

I really should have paid more attention to Magister Irin when he was explaining how these protective wards work. I should have paid more attention to him in general, actually.\n\nThe next one is in the glade. It's just across the way to the west.

I don't like the looks of that volcano! As if we didn't have enough trouble already. \n\nCould this be related to what Valessea and you discovered at the druidic circle? Could the Ascendant Magus really affect the volcano to such an extent?

Good thing I made Oblan teach me these symbols of his. He mentioned them in passing once when talking about his old life. They sounded like a smart idea.\n\nThis mark here tells me he went north. Such a smart old cat to leave a trail.

You found the scepter! That is good.\n\nAnd I remember now. I wanted to pay the bill to impress the other delegates. But now I don't have the coin to do that again. We have to get them to pay their shares. I can't lose another scepter!
See? Father acts like I'm a burden to be locked away and dealt with later. Not an adult who has some capacity to help!\n\nHe probably told you to see if I was in my room, didn't he?
Breaking into a prison. That's a new one, even for me!

That must be Izbadd. No way he's a merchant. Look at him, he's working way too hard to convince everyone he's doing nothing more than relaxing at a tavern. \n\nI know his type. Be careful with that one.

Well, look at this. She sounds so sure of herself, investigating crime in Fell's Run. And she's so friendly with her mother.\n\nI told myself that I wouldn't rush off to rescue her again. She clearly didn't want my help.
Quickly! After her! Lady Laurent can't be left alone with that … that … infiltrator!
There you are! I've been looking all over for you.\n\nWe've got to get back to Gonfalon Bay Gaming Hall. The tournament is about to begin!

Those blighted Firesong attacked the Beldama wyrds! Just like they attacked my people at Earthen Root Enclave. \n\nSpeak to Wyress Joslin. Find out what she knows. I don't think she trusts me, and I can't say I blame her.
That's a wyrd totem. Were they studying it? And that word inscribed upon it. Frii. Is that a name? Something related to the nature god, Y'ffre? Maybe Wyress Joslin can tell us more.

All three locations I need you to investigate lie to the east. Chase away any Sea Elves you find at the fort and the village, and see if you can figure out what they're up to at the cove. Report back to me in Vastyr when you're done.

I thought I might see you here. Looks like a band of Sea Elves got ashore and seized the fort. Now more of those sea-dogs are on their way.\n\nI was hoping for some druid help, but they never arrived. So it's up to us.
I can't tell if whatever was dragged here came out of those doors and went inside them. Perhaps both?\n\nProceed with caution, but I definitely want to look around in there.

Rebuilding his ranks with disillusioned druids. The Ascendant Lord will say anything to recruit his army.\n\nBut to allude to a druidic prophecy … what exactly is the Ascendant Lord promising his followers?

Captain Siravaen and I reached an agreement. She's happy to let me hire the Mad Maiden … especially if she gets another chance to bloody the Firesong Circle. She isn't quite done settling scores.\n\nIs Frii willing to go to Y'ffelon?
Sealord Nalos was a fool to trust those Firesong Druids. But I'm caught in this tangled net, too. l guess I'll just have to cut my way out. Preferably with excessive bloodshed.
This place remembers the one who called me from the Green. Let us look upon the door the Firesong could not open.
Have you found the silverbloom? He's starting to open up about the relic. Just one more treat and he's ours.\n\nGive Veshin some silverbloom. It will make him so happy, he'll tell us anything.
A forest wraith? I expected to find Firesong Druids in here, especially given the size of their invading force. But the wraiths?\n\nThose creatures only appear in the most dire circumstances.
For the first time in all my dealings with the One Who Knows, there is a portion of this plight that the Prince cannot see.\n\nYou do not know how much that notion troubles me, proxy.
The Lark of Rosgard thinks he's clever. But he'll slip up. One day, he'll slip up, and I'll be there to catch him when he does.\n\nVivec willing, that day will be today.
You may not feel it, but we do. A shift in the power that flows through the Cenotaph. The Dreamcarvers may soon breach the protections around our pact.\n\nWe must hurry to the courtyard!

Portents and clues. A trap befitting the Cloisters. There is no questioning it. Mora has trapped us in this cycle and these visions are beginning to reveal why. Meenai-Shai was aiding a new Cipher, one that said he worked for Mora himself.

First, we need to reset the magicka focus in the Corporea Secretus—an outbuilding to the northeast. Tide-King willing, that will reduce the instability.\n\nI only hope we're not too late. The chorus cannot endure these conditions for long!
What? I said I'd find you after you were done with Harn. Your trail led here.\n\nWould have caught up sooner, but I had to shake off another mercenary after you left.

I suppose we have no choice. We need to activate the gateway and follow Hermaeus Mora's enemies to Apocrypha. Such heroics aren't usually part of my duties, but so it goes.\n\nI'll open the portal, then in we go.
What does he mean, his mother was right? She can't be. She just can't be!\n\nPlease, speak with him—see if you can understand what's happening.

I don't know you, and I've never met Sharp. But the way my Reynila spoke of him, I'd recognize him anywhere!\n\nAre you one of her connections? Have you been watching over him all this time? Did he finally remember Reynila?
The politics of the Great Houses will always be deadly. Whether I hold the blade or someone else, it always ends the same.
That's one of them. Voidprowler thief! Yeah, you heard me! Hezehk isn't afraid of you.\n\nYou go talk to her, mortal. I'll just stand back and supervise.

I remember our last real lead with Federo brought us to that abandoned lab of the Reformer. Mevei's lead might not be much more than that.\n\nBut it's something. Any step forward at this point is progress.
Ahh, the halls of Shad Astula. Elydrina should be around here somewhere, likely in the Arch Mage's office.\n\nLet's not take long here, cohort.

Ah, my new collaborator. Good to see you again. By Mora's Eyes these frayed fates are becoming increasingly annoying. I look forward to putting them to bed, as it were.\n\nDo you have the items we need to summon our Daedric consultant?

Sleep potions. They sing a song of smoke and calm even the angriest of the bristleback lords. Powerful concoctions there. I used to know how to make them. Back before I fell into ink.\n\nLet's go, before anything else decides to get in our way.

Secret and forbidden knowledge. Something so terrible that Hermaeus Mora wiped the very memory of it from all existence. But now Torvesard has plucked a thin sliver from the darkness, urging us to remember.\n\nThough it pains me, we cannot allow that.

Interesting. The memory showed the priests allow their Daedric Princes to possess them and then they waded into the water, but I see nothing they could swim to from this point. Where did they go? \n\nLook around, proxy. We must find the path.

With the three relics that were once used to imprison Ithelia restored, we must determine where to even begin our search for the Forgotten Prince.\n\nBefore we discuss the idea that Scruut and I derived, do you have anything else to report?

Before we depart, gather the Daedric relics—Abolisher, the Lamp of Clarity, and the Skein of Secrets. Even though they're depleted, the Great Eye has seen that you will need them in the trials to come.\n\nAnd I'm certainly not going to carry them.
Finally, a living person. Find out what he knows and get the catacomb key. I'll keep watch, just in case.
Leramil's waiting in my townhouse in Skingrad. I'm going to try to find Tribune Alea, then I'll meet you there.

Lord Valente is well and truly into the auction now, so we have a bit of time. I never expected to find Ursilia here with you, though.\n\nWhat did you discover? And what did she mean by deal with her husband?

Truth be told, this one was ready to write the fortune off. Lady Weatherleah spent so long trying to find her son, Mizzik imagined the fortune dried up. A rare instance where Mizzik is glad to be wrong.
One more obstacle to bar our path. Hopefully the Lamp of Clarity shall show us the way, as it has done previously.
Anudnabia is a place with a bad reputation, friend. Old Daedric ruins, half-drowned in the Inner Sea. It's hard not to see it as something of an ill omen if your path leads there. Be careful.
That's Balandrus's handwriting all right. Looks like he made a deal with Grivier to sacrifice the rest of the townsfolk to the Terror of the Weald.\n\nIf Grivier's still alive, I can make him talk.
I knew the Recollection was interested in Niryastare, but I didn't really expect to find a whole new fort blocking access to the ruins. Maybe we'll find a way in that they overlooked.

I'm still not convinced these Vashabar Wood Elves are innocent, but I'll take Beragon and meet you at the spot the greenspeaker indicated. \n\nI know the Colovian Hills well. If there are Recollection or anything else out there, I'll find it.
I'm not used to taking orders from a floating ball of eyes and tentacles.

Inside the village, listen for any calls for help. People could be buried under rubble or trapped inside collapsed buildings. Just watch out for the strange beasts. They appeared after the ground shook.\n\nAnd, keep an eye out for Greenspeaker Sorilen.
I suspect this structure once housed another portal, but I see nothing here now. Perhaps we should refer to the Skein of Secrets, and see if it indicates the way to Ithelia.

That hated lamp reacted to your touch. It revealed that cluster of lights by this wall. Once again, I feel recognition, but not clarity. I sense the Many Paths, and this is a signpost.\n\nShine the lamp's light there. Show us what it does.
I'll start repairing the ballista. Not my first time putting one of these weapons back together. Go talk to Commander Merian and find out what he wants you to do.

Go ahead, pour some of that resonating fluid into the tracker. Don't be stingy with it either. It has to resonate with the essence of Wisteria to find her.\n\nI think that's what Hyacinth said, anyway. To be honest, I wasn't really listening.
Hmm? Apologies, walker. I have a song stuck in my head. I was trying to remember the next verse.
My moonclaw's pull tells me this is the right place. Besides the beasts and bandits, I sense a stronger darkness to the east. Let us search in that direction.
How does one go about healing internal injuries? A tincture? Perhaps a restorative spell? I should consult my textbooks.\n\nOh, excuse me. You should speak with Bogcup.

I have enjoyed the peace, the solitude. But it warms my heart to hear footsteps echo through the Scholarium once again. \n\nUlfsild learned many lessons about power and its application here. I hope you, and your cohorts, do the same.

Good, you're back. My old comrades showed up shortly before you did. Thank you for getting them here.\n\nWe all came to an understanding. If the law won't deal with whoever's killing the Scarlets, the job falls to us.
Akatosh take me, but I grow tired of waiting!\n\nHmm. I do not know you. Is there something you need, stranger? I can't talk long, or else the thief hiding in that ruin might give me the slip.

If you part with your coin for me, I'll follow you anywhere. But the swill they serve here isn't worth a sacrifice like that. A Scarlet would find the ledger in Laurina's house and trim its leaves. No record—no debt. Simple.
Already missing my fabulous tendrils? No wonder. Few who gaze upon it can resist my splendor for long. Float easy, and know I will always be here if you need me.

Welcome to the Wing of the Gryphon! As you can see, the Gryphon himself isn't quite ready to talk just yet.\n\nI've kept him company ever since the library disappeared. I'm not sure if he can hear me in there? But I talk to him every day.
The struggle for justice never ends, mortal. Always be prepared to fight. To defend what matters most to you.
There must be a record of Snapdragon's arrest. Where she was taken and why.\n\nDon't be shy. We can tear this place apart if we have to. I'm not leaving until we find something!
I don't care what he wants. I'm sure we can convince him.

Did you see that? I'm amazing!\n\nBut this is so strange. Seeing Wisteria like this. She's stressed, I can tell. She's mustering the Ceythalmor at this Dusk Keep. Whatever they're planning, it must be big and it must be soon.
Tamiit. Together we will walk the path of my memories so you can see the events of which I cannot speak.\n\nWhen you are ready, touch the light of memory. Then this memory will unfold.

I must center myself to call upon Azurah while you pour the moon-sugar into the ritual basin.\n\nI know Azurah listens to her followers, but somehow … I feel her gaze turned upon us now. Waiting. May I meet her eyes in honest communion.
Speak with the high cantor. Perhaps she is finally ready to reveal why she has brought us to this desolate location.
Good luck finding Izalgo. Azurah guide your path.

Vanus Galerion. One of the most powerful mages in Tamriel. I'm not going to turn down his help, but be aware that he's arrogant, pompous, and an annoying pain in the arse.\n\nGlad he wants to talk to you and not me, pal.

Such a disaster. So many great mages died down here. And now, Merric. I should have gotten here sooner. Been here to help.\n\nDo as the prince asked and gather Merric's weapons. I'll take a look at what remains of that device.
The Mages Guild faces many challenges, both in Tamriel and beyond. Few have felt this dire.

What a loss. Merric was our leader. My mentor. Practically a father to me since I joined the Fighters Guild. Thank you for gathering his sword and shield. Strange, though, that a Daedra was leading these Worm Cultists.\n\nWhat was that note you found?

I've been thinking. Guendeline says I don't really love her. It's just some kind of silly infatuation.\n\nI think I need to make a grand gesture to prove my love to her. Something spectacular to show her how I really feel.
We met only briefly, but the forest will remember your deeds forever. I will make sure of it.
Onuja sent you just in time! That lizard has an eye for capable people.
Go bind a spirit. I need to know if the ritual can work.
Are you ready to learn, novice? Fire and steel await. \n\nI can teach you to gather and refine raw materials, research new techniques and craft the metal into useful objects.
The relics beneath the xanmeer could be of inestimable value. We need to proceed cautiously.
The Trading Post is to the north, along the border with Reaper's March. I'll be waiting for you outside the west gate. See you there, comrade.
Adept. Very glad to see you again. I've translated the final book, and we're ready to monkey rum butter.
Comrade. A message for you. The guild has need of your unique talents.
The brazier is ready. Valaste prepared it precisely. According to my instructions, of course.
The Bright Moons will see us through this, my friend.
Don't ask me. I don't like this any more than you do.
Thank the Green! My friend, it's good to see you out here. What are you doing at Arenthia?
Good, you're here. If you haven't already, please speak with Queen Ayrenn.
The Bright Moons will see us through this, my friend.
Sai needs to rest. Don't say anything that might upset him, all right?

Sahan seems to be relatively unharmed. Can we wrap this up? \n\nI've an appointment with a certain young lady and I need to stop by the moneychangers first. Women of that stripe seldom do anything on credit.
There is no time. The amulet! Get to the amulet!
If I were a necromancer, I wouldn't raise up skeletons. No guts and you can see right through them.
Get the amulet! Go!
So many things to do! Adusa doesn't have enough hours in the day.\n\nPerhaps you could lend a hand, my friend. You help Adusa, yes?
My expedition is ruined! One catastrophe after another! \n\nOh, hello. You wouldn't happen to be interested in performing a few light duties, would you? I'm in need of a temporary assistant.
Traveler, please. Have you heard tidings of the Edrald family? I've just come from their manor and they're gone! Just gone!
Where have you been? I've been waiting for you to arrive for days now. \n\nHold on. Are you all they sent?
Don't tell me a few disorganized thugs are putting you off? Get out there and fight! Win!
Are you afraid the open air will seem too much like a vacation? Do not soften your resolve. Maormer sorcery will rob the island of its charm, I promise you.
Before you make the gloves, you need to bring raw jute to a clothing station and refine it.
What do you require? Does the matter demand urgency?

I wonder where the pull of adventure will take me next? Maybe someplace warmer. I hear it's nice in Abah's Landing this time of year.\n\nAnyway, despite your strange predilections, you were mostly helpful in the barrow. You have my thanks for that.
I see you're still alive, still killing. Good. Have you learned anything else about what our Daedric friends are planning here?
Well met, Sister. I coordinate our family's more mundane contracts. I suggest you get used to this face, because you're going to be seeing a lot of me.
Watch yourself out here. Danger lurks around every bend once you leave the beaten path.
This Sanctuary shall serve as a safe haven, a place where you and your Brothers and Sisters can relax between contracts and other duties. In time, you will come to consider it your home.

Thank you for helping me complete my task. Now I need to return to Vivec City. Have you been there? It's amazing! Ziggurats rising out of the water, the moonlet hanging in the sky above.\n\nYou should meet me there so I can introduce you to Lord Vivec.
Scaling the White-Gold Tower shouldn't be hard for you. Unless I've misjudged.\n\nHah, I wouldn't do that to you! Only the bloodiest, most grueling tasks for my favorites.
Don't you just love exploring ancient places? I must admit I have a fondness for antiques and enticing mysteries. But not Old Lady Ezira. She's too old and mysterious even for my tastes!

Ashlanders once respected each other, helped one another. You'd think these were House wolves or Tribunal dogs, the way they treated me.\n\nSpeaking of the Tribunal, you have the smell of dog about you. I wonder why that is?

Eye of Magnus, another one …. That's a very convincing costume. What are you supposed to be? Some gallant hero? Trinimac in disguise?\n\nWait … you're not one of my classmates. You really are a hero, aren't you? Thank Auri-El! I need your help!
Tranquil greetings, initiate. I assume that Josajeh has prepared you for your next task?\n\nRemember—a careful approach and prudent action will serve you better than any shield. Safe travels.
Thank goodness, you're back. I hope the Augur didn't give you too much trouble. I know it can be a handful.\n\nNow, the Loremaster asked me to give you something. The first of many gifts.
With all the pieces of the staff gathered, we can begin our task in earnest. The Staff of Towers will be rendered harmless soon enough.
Ah, friend! How good to see you again!

Back in Murkmire, I always felt like I was fighting the current. Trying to force my way upstream instead of going with the flow.\n\nSince joining Cyrodilic Collections, though, my life has a purpose. It reminds me of warm mud oozing between my toes!
The Saxhleel of Murkmire deserve better than to be kidnapped and accosted by those footpads from Blackrose. We will put them to heel soon, I promise you.

Stendarr bless it, Famia! You never pull a bijum-release! You push! Always push!\n\nI'm dreadfully sorry. But don't despair! I mean, clearly, this isn't an ideal start. But in the grand scheme of things, falling into a pit is a fairly minor setback.

Ah, beeko. I am sorry to have left you, but I had to give chase. Kassandra took the staff—a gift of the dream-wallow, and the key to the Remnant of Argon, yes?\n\nI grew too weary, but Jaxsik still chases them like a stiff wind, I think.
Stay quiet. All predators listen well.
I am Iskenaaz, voh-vastei to Tree Minder Pavu. I am at your service. I promise to leave you with a fine impression of our tribe.
Why do you hesitate? Talk to Old Shuvu.\n\nHe will not bite. And even if he did, it would not hurt because he has no teeth.
Make your way to Wormroot Depths and look for anything that appears to be Khajiiti in origin.\n\nI'll join you there after I deal with our mysterious follower.

Vazbi will be right behind you, but be careful, walker. Silhu-jo can be overprotective, but he would not resort to lies to hold us back. The dangers of the wastes are real, as you know.\n\nTruly, I hate to worry him, but Vazbi must do this.
Riverhold. A town of broken dreams and broken people, where the common folk face injustice at every turn.\n\nThat is why Mizzik Thunderboots has come, of course. To protect the unprotected.

Gharesh-ri and I will do what we can to uncover the secrets of the Dragonhorn. Take Tharn and the others and stop Zumog Phoom. The Betrayer must not be restored to full power.\n\nI just wish we knew how this all ties into the plans of the Dragons.
Bleh. Can't get the taste out of my mouth. It's awful.

Well done. I had hoped to glean a bit more, but that name is enough. Arum-Khal, the dro-m'Athra. Arum-Khal, the Moon-Slayer.\n\nMages whisper his name as they do that of the Worm-King, Mannimarco. I thought him long gone. Seems I was wrong.
Old M'zum is dealing with missing moon-sugar, scared farmhands, and a mysterious beast. Perhaps he and Mother suffer the same problem, yes?
Talk to Sai … I need a moment.

I suspect we must light the braziers in a specific order.\n\nHave you a chance to read the plaques? "First of the Grandmasters, laid to rest." That describes Ghelin-Brol, the Akaviri warrior who helped Reman establish the Dragonguard.
We don't need another complication. Especially when we have no idea when this Dragon will strike.\n\nStill, we can't set sail without a ship. Let's make our way to South Guard Ruins.
Vijari flies with Khenarthi now. He was a good young man. My sister chose well.
How did the Dragon's island get into the sky? And where is Tharn?\n\nFive-claw, tell me what is happening!
Tell Sai and the sky-lizard not to worry. Caska shall return to the Dragonguard Sanctum all in good time.
The cult cut down anyone who stood in their way. What could they want with such a peaceful refuge?
The time has finally come to defeat Laatvulon once and for all! He falls this day or we do.

Meet me in Stormhaven. The Skald-King's scouts spotted members of the coven near the lumber mill at the Bangkorai border, by the Weeping Giant. We'll start there.\n\nAs for the magic, I'll tell you more about that when we're away from prying eyes.
Please, retrieve the flask. It must be nearby. I can sense it. We can talk after.

It's all kind of Dwarven to me, but I think Fenn and the clever woman have figured out the elixir.\n\nTalk to Fenn. See if I understand them correctly. And tell him the sooner the elixir is ready, the better.

Svana is heading to Blackreach and Lyris wants to take the midland camp, so I'm going to the coastal camp. I'll see you there.\n\nWe should hurry, though. Once the Gray Host realizes we have this map, they might scatter like leaves in the wind.
Let's be quick. They loaded the jars of netherroot brew onto a cart for transport.\n\nUnfortunately, I lost track of which cart when things in the camp became hectic. We'll need to check them all.

Sorry. Guess I'm not completely used to the fighting and all. That urn, though. The gray reliquary. The witch was adamant about protecting it. Gathering it up. She said something about our life energy.\n\nOh gods, I think I know what they're doing!
Place looks deserted. Check around. Maybe we can find some indication of where Fenn has gone.
Lyris takes command of a situation so easily. I wonder if she can teach me how to do that?\n\nAnyway, do be careful. We'll stick close to Lyris and meet you inside.

That's Greymoor Keep. House Ravenwatch has been investigating the place. From the reports I've received, the Gray Host is working terrible magic here.\n\nBut you already knew that, didn't you? I've seen your name in Gwendis's notes.

That's our target. The ritual site must be somewhere inside that horrid structure. I scouted the area before you arrived. It's full of Gray Host forces.\n\nAnd from what I could tell, Svargrim and Rada al-Saran are both inside.
Another pilgrim, seeking shelter from the storm?\n\nNo, you don't appear to be a pilgrim. What brings you here?

Not how I expected that to go. Thanks for smoothing things over. Hard to believe we ran into her royal princess in the local drinking hall.\n\nWe should pay a visit to Greyga before we wander out into the wilds in search of this mysterious Breton.

What an interesting use of primitive magic! That was clearly your vampire assassin. He even wore an eye patch. It looked like he was at a small camp.\n\nAnd you saw that ball of magicka? It went to the west. That must be where you'll find the camp.
Bile, then resin, then powder. Don't give Overseer Thulsgreg any more excuses to oppose my techniques!

Bestest friend! Rigurt was just thinking about his past diplomatic successes with you! It helps distract from his current predicament.\n\nOh! But you can help Rigurt as you did before! You are his greatest assistant, after all.
This looks like the right place. Meditation garden? Grotto? Perhaps part of that old temple over there.

Hmm. This scholar's research doesn't go back to the First Era, and the other scholars fled? That puts a wrinkle in our plans, all right.\n\nThis Pyre Watch warrior is a promising lead, though. Let's go find her and the other scholars.

Ah, my friend. I wish I bore better news, but our paths seem to cross only in times of great crisis.\n\nRada al-Saran has reemerged from the shadows. That can only mean one thing—he believes his true goal is at hand.

Verandis is certain that Rada al-Saran has set his final plan in motion, so get to Markarth and talk to him.\n\nWhen you do speak with Verandis, don't let him pretend everything's fine. I think it's the Dark Heart and the connection he feels to it.

For the record, this plan sounds like a symphony of horker farts. I haven't got a better one, so I'll pinch my nose and go along with it. Especially if I'm headed to Understone Keep. Hope Caddach isn't half the rotten bastard I've heard he is.
I'm greatly looking forward to seeing Count Verandis again, but auramancy visions weren't what I had in mind.

The pockets of energy we discovered in the Library of Arkthzand, they're even stronger here. The Void energy permeates that ancient keep.\n\nI suspect the Dark Heart hides somewhere inside. And I fear that it's growing stronger.

This is where the map led us. A lovely and ominous spot for a foreboding Gray Host castle, don't you think?\n\nIf we can't find something about Rada al-Saran and Verandis here, then I'm not sure where else to look.
The Lothid clan is as bad as they come. Ravenous vampires with a thirst for blood and gold. This one must get Kathad away from them. She must!
The harrier returns, swift as a crow on the wing.\n\nI have prepared the ritual fire. Did you bring the components I requested?

A familiar face, thank the stars! I seem to remember you providing assistance the last time Stibbons made a mess of things. Or was it the time before?\n\nNo matter. You're here now and I am more than willing to compensate you for your time.
A letter? I knew I saw something fall out of Tenarei's satchel when she ambushed me.\n\nWhy, this is a contract! Tenarei Vels is bringing Quistley in to pay debts in Leyawiin.

Damn it all! I triple-checked the pylons last night. I field tested the runes. I've read everything Barilzar's ever written aside from his fetching diary. And it still doesn't work! Still!\n\nWhy won't it work? It needs to work!

We open the door and Lyranth just rushes ahead without us? Figures!\n\nWell, I guess we should start looking around, too. Everything we learned so far indicates that the Daedric weapons should be in here somewhere.
We've got to get deeper into the ruins if we're going to find the harrada creeper's roots.
What's that you've got there? Not a golden helm by any chance?
Ancient ruin protected by fictional guardian is a twist I never saw coming. Was this Annyce's doing? Regardless, I believe you'll need to convince the guardian to let us pass.

We need to free Ardia from that ritual before it drains her soul completely, even if it kills her.\n\nStill, we should look for focal crystals nearby that are drawing power from her. Destroying them is the only way to save her life and her soul.

Renna's sitting in the main hall. Get her to set up a meeting with Farrul Lupus so I can deliver this book.\n\nAfter that, we can decide if we want to keep looking into the emperor's secret or not. I guess it depends on what Lupus has to say.
The Keywright's Gallery roars back to life, and I'm the one who sees it first. Plain, boring Norianwe! Can you believe it?

I thought the stone would bring us some answers, but it's only raising more questions! Who did we just see murdered in this study? Who murdered them? Is it the same person who murdered Priestess Rolaine?\n\nLet's search the upstairs rooms next.
You don't look horrified, so I suppose I should screw up my courage and read it for myself. \n\nLet me see it, please.
If these volcanic vents insist on staying imbalanced, Y'ffre's fearsome power will raze everything to ash. Lava is a beautiful, but destructive force. It seethes like anger and drinks from the land.
I've never actually done this before. Don't judge. You can help me out by lighting some votive candles. I'll pray to the three that my grandfather feels like listening.

That creature! It was the Ravener. You see how it tortured that man. The beast is capable of intense cruelty. Strange that it just ran off though. Not what I'd expect from it.\n\nLook around. See if anything explains what happened here.
You're a s'wit, Selveni.\n\nYou just have to power magic rocks made by a Living God. Find some spirits. Free them. Oh, and leave the False Martyrs' Folly without dying painfully. It'll be fun!

Mortals in the Deadlands exist only at Mehrunes Dagon's sufferance. They grovel in his cult, toil as his slaves, or skulk and hide in places such as this in the hope he will forget about them.\n\nWhich are you? And why do you seek the Bladebearers?
A complicated game at play. Mortals rarely offer Daedra anything of worth. But, here I must concern myself with them. Hrmph.
Arox mentioned a prison within the prison. The Durance Vile. Let's look around and try to find it.

As we ascend the summit, know that I can protect you from the worst of the lightning and the wind shears, provided you do not stray too far from my side.\n\nAs for any other threats, you will need to deal with those of your own accord.

This is the Shambles, one of the most dangerous regions of Fargrave.\n\nThe old bathhouse is to the north. We can get there via the western warrens, through the central plazas, or by crossing Skein Row to the east.
I remembered something. I think I know the man who designed the Riven Cataclyst. Or.. know of him?
What have we here? One of the warriors I conscripted to help tidy up the Halls of Fabrication, I believe? This is fortuitous.\n\nOnce again, I find myself in need of someone with your skills.
I think we piqued Morah's interest, despite her attitude. See if you can convince her to tell us where to find Master Rrvenk.

So good to see you again, my dear. Remember that little predicament we dealt with not too long ago? Well, now I have a related but larger problem, so let me tell you about my proposition. It pays exceedingly well, I assure you.\n\nCare to hear more?
I'll need you to collect some wood. Once you do that, I'll endeavor to strip it and weave it into a basket. There should be logs nearby to harvest. Return to me once you have the wood.
Just need to grab that staff now, and the Oaken trial is in the bag. \n\nI mean, not literally, I don't have a bag large enough for the staff. But you understand my point.

Lady Garick rose from a low-born child to become a highly respected captain in the All Flags Navy. She knew the value of pushing past any obstacle, even when you believe all is lost.\n\nYou demonstrate this same tenacity. I am impressed.

Pardon that display …. I've never been forcibly taken over by a spirit of nature before.\n\nI wasn't sure if the corruption was connected to the Evergrowth, but now we know. And we know a druid is somehow involved. That … troubles me.
A lot of grim celebrations happened here. Yech.\n\nLook around for a bone we can use. It has to be large and sturdy, with just the right sort of necrotic properties. I'll know it when I see it.

The first protection ward we need to set is in the meadow. There are two more after that. Hopefully, restoring them to working order will help keep the bad, bad spell inside the boundaries of Tor Draioch.
Lead the way, dear. Neither of us is getting any younger.
That mark scratched onto the rock wall looks very familiar. Before I get my hopes up, we should take a closer look.
You should talk to the innkeeper. Every time I ask about my scepter she only wants to talk about the bill from last night.\n\nI know I paid, because my coin purse is almost empty today.
Father acts like he has the final say in what I do, but it's my life!

This letter says we'll find Izbadd near the Anchor's Point Inn in Evermore. I think he was expecting Jhaka and Silverslip to show up, so hopefully we won't scare him off.\n\nIf he knows something about Song, we have to talk to him. Let's go.
Did … did she just thank us for making her relationship with Aurelia better? Stendarr's grace, what's in that note?

Please, my friend. You talk to m'lady. I'm much too discombobulated to carry on a meaningful conversation. \n\nJust make sure you know who you're dealing with—Lady Laurent or that obnoxious sea captain.

Dhulef and I will meet you at the Beldama wyrd camp. I just want to examine this tablet first. That's definitely a drawing I've seen used in connection with the Druid King before. Hopefully the wyress can tell us more about the rest of the tablet.
There has to be something around here. What's that sticking up out of the dirt over there?

Well met, adventurer. If you're looking for work, I need all the help I can get.\n\nSea Elf raids are nothing new on Galen, but never have they attacked in such numbers. The whole southeast shore is under siege.
Hey, mate! Glad to see a friendly face. If you're looking for some action, we've got Sea Elves here.\n\nThey chased House Mornard's knights out of this fort. But if we work fast we can take it back.
Do you see? The ground is disturbed, suggesting heavy crates were dragged up and down the hillside. And see over there? Debris.\n\nLet's take a closer look.
Someone is definitely using this place. Let's look around.
Archdruid Orlaith has much to answer for. She underestimates us at her peril.
The seeds … gone. So close, but now out of reach. Archdruid understands nothing. The seeds cannot be commanded. They must be asked. Invited. \n\nI sense another song here. Very old. It calls to me.

Do you see how his eyes squint when he laughs? It's really cute.\n\nAh, right, the silverbloom. It's on the trees, up the hill to the southwest. Take a few, then come back. He's almost ready to tell us their plan to contain the relic.
My Gwenaelle must be somewhere in these tunnels. Let's find her before the spirit motes or the animals take her from me.

With the traps powered, we should find navigating the Cenotaph much easier. They should destroy most of the invaders with ease.\n\nHowever, they won't get them all. We need to determine how close they are to reaching the Remnant pact.

Remarkable. The Sigil of the Great Eye is Mora's magic made manifest. It seems I was correct. The sigil is holding us captive, but returning the book seems to have undone one of its magical locks. And now, a vision? Or, perhaps a memory.

Thank the fathoms! My name is Cipher Huzmargo and I watch over the nearby Rectory Corporea. I am in desperate need of an adventurer who can help me reestablish order here.\n\nThe chorus is in disharmony, you see? Watcher's whiskers, what will we do?
