Fair warning, Harn might ask you for a favor in return for information. \n\nI can pay you back, but you don't get paid until I get paid, and I don't get paid until I find Reynila. Make sure you get something good. I'll find you after you're done.

We're too late. It seems the Hidden Kindred and their Dreamcarver allies have already used the gate. They're probably stomping through my master's realm now, causing all sort of contradictions. How rude of them! Look around and see what you can find.
Nathyn was the one responsible for what happened in the caverns?\n\nI … don't believe it. This has to be some kind of mistake.
I'm a rather busy woman and my time is limited. Speak your business or leave me alone.
Head south and you'll find the Obscured Forum. Hard to miss. Look for the books. We'll catch the Voidprowlers there and take back my secret.
When we first met Dimik-ei, she said I'd made a promise I would come back and rescue her from the Reformer.\n\nI'm going to make good on that promise. I just need time.
I'm actually somewhat surprised that Lillirhuza remembers me. I certainly didn't make a good impression with her group.
The tomedust should be found in the Cipher's Midden expungatory, while Seekers tend to congregate around those resin plants to the southwest. \n\nEasy enough, and soon we'll be talking to Tem!

After decades of plotting, the porcine hegemony will become the vassals of the slumbering … erm, hegemony! Which is a different and much better hegemony if you ask me!\n\nAre you ready to watch the coup unfold?
I have recovered, proxy. Now tell me. What occurred after we parted ways in the Infinite Panopticon?
Another sign that we are on the right path. The Echonir has revealed a lingering memory. Bring it forth and let us see what happened in this grim ruin long ago.

Do not worry, proxy. Scruut's plan is sound, if a bit incomplete. We shall work out the pertinent details and relay them to our allies before they meet up with you.\n\nWe shall rendezvous at Beragon's townhouse after you restore the relics.

Mortal, something's wrong! Hermaeus Mora senses fates, futures, winking out of existence. Potentials he predicted that will never be! I feel these instabilities rippling across reality. This must be Ithelia's doing, but we need to be certain!
Groundskeeper Gaius's home is just down the hill to the east. Whether he's there or not, we need to find that key.
I'm glad I caught up with you! Leramil sent me out to look for you and cracked acorns if I didn't get lucky! I was afraid I was going to wander around for hours.
Don't worry. We can talk more later. In the meantime, go and search Lord Valente's office. He must have one inside the manor.
You've done great work today, traveler. The air is heavy with death, but just like the sun, truth will come out. If only Lady Weatherleah could see Pelena beaten at her own game.
We must be getting close to the source of Ithelia's power. Look how much of the Mythos has … changed.
No, I haven't heard of this place either, and I thought I knew most of the shrines and holy places in Morrowind. Go on and ask around. I'll see if I can find a map or a book or something.
Doesn't look good. Something killed these bloodfiends, but at least I don't see Grivier or Tham lying among the dead.\n\nSee if that piece of paper contains anything interesting.
That's Niryastare over there … surrounded by a Recollection stockade. I guess it's nice to know I correctly interpreted the map we found in Hoperoot. But it does pose a problem.
I see my reputation precedes me. Well, someone needs to get some answers from these people!\n\nGo on, talk to the so-called king of Dawnwood. Maybe ask him who exactly crowned him while you're at it.

Didn't get enough of me while fighting the Recollection in Grahtwood, hmm? No time to catch-up, though, friend. I have injured people here and more still in the village of Ostumir.\n\nHow about we get them out safely before the ground shakes again?

This is what Mora feared. Ithelia devised her Loom to undo fates she did not agree with. She could destroy everything we know in her desire to restore what she lost—to create a reality where she was never imprisoned and forgotten. We must stop her!
An odd feeling—hatred and dread without knowing why. But I know that lamp somehow.\n\nOnce you pick up the lamp, I can study it. Maybe it will help me remember.
We reset the traps and burned the ropes. That should slow the assault like Commander Merian planned. He wants us to meet him in the main courtyard. Let's get going.
Once we find a spot, I'll just need a moment to activate the tracker fly. It's a finicky little gadget. Delicate wings and all that.

Once you reach what is now called Claw's Strike, head inside. I will find you there. I hope I am not wrong in thinking you can defend yourself. \n\nThere is no telling how much of my fighting skills remain after being dead for so long. We will see.
These Ceythalmor are ruthless foes. I'm grateful that you arrived in time. I'm not sure how much longer I would have lasted. Thank you.\n\nBogcup has found a capable ally in you.
You are welcome in my glade any time adventurer. \n\nUse this calm and thoughtful place as a chance to consider the power you wield. And how it might be applied wisely.

I think we'll get along, friend. Here, let me mark your map. I know where you can find three of the surviving Scarlets: Big Urm, Fallen-Knives, and Valenia.\n\nTell them to go to the Skingrad Outlaws Refuge. I'll be waiting there.
It's a strange thing. After twenty years, are the Divines giving us a chance to make amends? Or is this their judgment on what we did?\n\nIt would only be just.
My scales are dry enough to make a Veeskhleel blush. And the barkeep says I can't afford the good stuff. Spare a coin so a self-loathing wretch can drink himself into Oblivion?
I sense that you're a particularly buoyant soul. Is it because of me? My mere presence has been known to make the world seem lighter, brighter. More netchy.
Go on, last page. You're almost there!

Only the Ceythalmor would dare to arrest Snapdragon in the Mages Guildhall. She may have a temper, but she only yells at the people she cares about. \n\nLet's search the Reeve's office and see what we can find out.
Burn marks. I bet he's one of the Ceythalmor agents that ambushed Snapdragon. Let's see what we can learn. Talk to him while I keep watch.

I think Snapdragon's journal said the next site was near the Labyrinth, not in it. Friend, if we can find something else Wisteria left behind …. \n\nThis is amazing! Wait until I tell Hyacinth about this.
Kneel before the altar and meditate on Ravith and my past.

So this was the lesson in restoring Khenarthi's Rise. Forgiveness.\n\nI knew how to fix this place. To tend to old bones, lost scrolls, ancient weapons. But mending what lies inside me, what has been part of me for so long. That is not as simple.
The high cantor is surprisingly quick-footed for a cat of her years. Let us keep up!

Meet me behind the temple northwest of the trading post when you finish. Cantor Izalgo is a Cathay Khajiit with spotted fur and sweet brown eyes. \n\nI suppose it seems too much to hope that he just ran off for a tryst with some honey-tongued local.
Good, you made it. Now we can get around to beating on the Worm Cult.\n\nThey attacked our guildhalls, killed our comrades. It's time to fight! Talk to Prince Azah and he'll fill you in on the plan.

I can't believe it, the Worm Cult has returned. But we stopped them once. We'll do it again.\n\nThe door behind the guildhall leads to underground chambers where the battle is taking place. Skordo and I will secure more help and join you shortly.

Merric. My friend and mentor. Dead. It hardly seems possible. He was always so strong. So capable. Forgive me, but this is … difficult.\n\nPlease, gather Merric's weapons and see if anything that remains can tell us about the device that killed him.
You can tell her I'll stand out here as long as it takes. I'm not going anywhere until she accepts my love.
Hold there, travaler. I'm Holgunn, the commander here in Davon's Watch. I must warn you, the city isn't safe right now.
The Hist key should allow us inside the xanmeer, but we must proceed cautiously. I need to review my notes. <<1>> is at what I think is the entrance to the underground ruins.
What have you found?
Comrade! I must speak with you about an urgent matter.
You do the guild credit with your bravery and dedication, Adept.
My friend, the Moon Hallowed. Thank you for all you've done here today. And all you will do.
I don't like this. But if it's the only way to find Sai Sahan, I'm with you.
Ah, you're just as Razum-dar described you. I'm on a vital mission here. What are you doing at Arenthia?
My friend the Moon Hallowed. Always getting me out of the hard scrapes. Thank you. For all you've done and all you're about to do.

We did it. Sai's going to be all right.\n\nI have a favor to ask. Let's not talk about what happened with that doppelganger. Not yet, anyway. I … I had no idea Sai had feelings for me. I just need time to sort it all out.
Yes, yes. Well done, and all that claptrap. Are we done here?
There it is. The door to the Vault of Kings.
We're almost there. Let's finish this!
Nearly there now, I'd imagine.
Ah hah! So you are the one Verandis talked about earlier?\n\nAdusa should have known when she met you at Moira's Hope. You are different from the others. Adusa approves of this partnership.
I find all this sun and sand quite fatiquing. I look forward to a nice, long bath once this is all over!
Afraid that ancient Dwarf engine will drive you mad too? You're Undaunted! Being a little crazy comes with the territory!
Did you get lost on the way to this new found ruin? If you are thwarted by your map, what hope have you of defeating the dangers within?
Raw jute is plentiful, if you know where to look. Just don't chew on it. It can really do a number on your …. \n\nWell, just don't chew on it.
Discovering the effects of potions comes with trial and error.\n\nOften, far too much error.
Well met, Brother. I coordinate our family's more mundane contracts. I suggest you get used to this face, because you're going to be seeing a lot of me.
You must be the new initiate. The Speaker sent word that you were on your way.\n\nI'm the Matron of this Sanctuary. Obey me without question and I'm certain we'll get along just fine.

I was worried I was going to have to try to deal with this on my own. My faith in the Tribunal is strong, but I don't think it would have been enough to get me past those Daedra.\n\nWhenever you're ready, we can enter the tomb.
I love Black Marsh. Every step is a dance with death! Every stinking breath may be your last! I ever settle down, it'll be there.

My brother—duped by the hound of Clavicus Vile!\n\nThis is bad. Very bad. And the Tribunal god isn't in any shape to assist us. How can we find this Clockwork City without Vivec's help? Perhaps that priest can tell us more.
We'll sort this out yet. I know it!
Please, go talk to Josajeh, initiate. She will no doubt be pleased to see you.
First rate work in Summerset. Really, first rate. Unfortunately, we have another problem.\n\nAre you ready to set out again?
Old Ways be praised. Welcome back, initiate. I hesitate to ask, but I must—were you successful? Did you recover the remaining staff fragments?

So, you return victorious. You have my most sincere gratitude—and that of the explorers you rescued.\n\nNow, as to the Blackguards. We should assume that they learned a great deal from our friends and the Dead-Water warriors. Wouldn't you agree?
Go on. I'll be fine. I'll catch up.
You will like Chime-Maker Shuvu, I think. Very wise, and very pleasant—like one of your gray-muzzled bark-dogs.\n\nLet's make our way to the Glade.
What an interesting story. If only I could shake my shadow as easily as Khunzar-ri does … well … anything.\n\nAt least now I know where to find the first triangulant.

We should find a gate that controls the flow of the water nearby.\n\nJust be careful. Beasts gather here often to lap up water from leaks and overflow. They thirst as much as we do, now, and a thirsty beast is a grumpy beast, yes?

You might try sweet-talking the Avernos out of the focus. It doesn't take much to lead their minds into the gutter … if you don't smell like one.\n\nOtherwise, they've probably got it locked up somewhere.
I can't hold this forever. Please, hurry.
Let's return to Mother's farm and discuss what we learned.

I need a few moments to confer with my old companion, Sai Sahan. Privately.\n\nWe'll meet you at the New Moon Fortress in short order. If you need a reminder about your time there, why don't you seek out this Caska you mentioned?
It appears the sanctuary's archives are out of reach. There doesn't even appear to be a place to use the grappling bow.\n\nI … I don't know how to proceed.
Seems our smuggler is a bit distraught. Let's hope it's nothing serious.

Now that the Wall of Life is cleansed, many more souls can continue on their journey with Khenarthi.\n\nThis one will resume her own journey as well. As the Great Darkness recedes here, it creeps out elsewhere seeking to ensnare more souls.
Delivering messages is thirsty work and the grog here is damn expensive. Be a good mate and give us a gold piece.
Vestige? You're the help the Skald-King promised? Suddenly, I feel a lot better about our chances.\n\nStill, this threat is bigger than King Jorunn imagined.
You were on the cart. I saw you before those witches caught us and tossed me in this stone box. Glad you're finally awake.\n\nApologies for my ghastly appearance. I'm … not feeling my best.
I'm glad I got to look around Blackreach, but I can't wait to see the sun and sky again.\n\nNo matter how big these caverns are, it still feels like we're buried alive down here.
Lyris knows this part of the world better than I do. See which locations she thinks stand the best chance of providing us with the items I need.

A bold move, setting up camp in the midst of the western holds. I'll say this for the Gray Host, they aren't afraid to draw attention to themselves.\n\nI learned a few things while I was waiting for you to show up.
The witch wants to keep us away from the gray reliquary. I say we can't let them have it.\n\nSmash that damn thing into a thousand pieces!
Dusktown? I wonder what Fenn's found that led him back down there? \n\nDoes his message give any indication of where we can find him? The settlement isn't big, but it's not exactly small, either.

Did you know there was a castle down here? Right underneath Solitude? It's disconcerting to think about, to say the least!\n\nLyris has been scouting while we waited for you and she just got back. Talk to her and see what she found out.
That's Greymoor Keep. House Ravenwatch has been investigating the place, but I haven't heard anything from our operatives as of yet. I suggest we proceed with caution.
Jorunn sent me with a warning for Solitude. Now I'm about to march into the starless depths of Blackreach to try to avert a massacre.\n\nHow do I keep getting myself into these kinds of situations?
Another pilgrim, seeking shelter from the storm? No, you have a harder look about you. \n\nGood. The priests and pilgrims of Kilkreath Temple could use the help of someone such as you.
Let's stop by the Lonely Troll before we head to Kasalla's warehouse. If we can find him, this Maugh mentioned in Brondold's journal might know something about Kasalla's operation.
Fascinating! Every divination appears to be unique.\n\nGo ahead and use the medallion. Old Mjolen and I need to get back to our study of the harrowstorm ritual.
The stonemelt mixing instructions are over there by the table. I'm trusting you to show everyone just how simple the process is.
Hello, strange person! Rigurt was just thinking about his past diplomatic successes! It helps distract from his current predicament.\n\nOh! But you can help Rigurt with his problem, maybe!

To be frank, this seems too good to be true. A single riddle leading to our prize? Too easy. Then again, things often come easy to an adventurer of my caliber.\n\nI have some business to conclude here. I'll meet you at Kilkreath once I'm finished.

I didn't expect to find our historians outside the walls, or to find this place so disturbed. Was someone foolish enough to attack Bangkorai Garrison? \n\nNo matter. That's Scholar Diel over there. See if she can tell us about the Gray Host.

I know you have only had a moment's peace, but we must renew our hunt for Rada al-Saran with all due haste. The setbacks will not slow Rada for long, and he's likely closer to his true goal than we know.
Verandis sent me to keep watch for you, which I hope you appreciate, because it is both boring and a huge waste of my talents.\n\nAnyway, he wants you to meet him in Markarth right away.
This just keeps getting better. Check on the count. Find out what we need to do.

We're going to meet Verandis? Right now? I—um—yes, that would be prudent, I suppose. Do I … look presentable to you? Befitting of an audience with the count?\n\nI don't imagine there's time for a bath before we head to the orrery?
We should keep pressing forward, my friend.

Without the blessings of the spirits, it would be unseemly for this alliance to go forward. The ritual begins with the preparation.\n\nGather a briarheart seed, a Hagraven's eye, and a handful of bright river-shale. Check to the east, west, and south.
I find the lizard folk to be quite fascinating. Also, they perturb me.\n\nThen again, most people do.
I guess the Dark Elf thought she'd be back before I freed myself.\n\nI should count myself lucky that she didn't simply murder me, but it feels like a Daedra is dancing inside my head.

It's nice to have a willing pair of hands to assist me. Tiras seems well-acquainted with instruments like these. He could make a real contribution, if he wasn't so set on observing all the time.\n\nI wish I could convince him to help. Ah well.
Nice work! Now let's see if that actually opened the door.

Hello? No, not you. Shush a moment … ooooh, I get what all the hollering was about!\n\nThat creeper's strangling a tree around here. It's calling for help, but no one's answering. Well, except us now.
Call out if you see anything.\n\nI don't know about you, but I can't bear the idea of disappointing Mathen. He's got it hard enough already!

Well, this old ruin certainly sets the stage. I can feel the tension rising just looking at it.\n\nIt's been some time since I've felt a bit of stage fright. Please, you take the lead, I am simply the understudy in this adventure.

It's getting to the point that I hardly recognize this place. It's like the sky is on fire and everything's scorched. Did the cult come here just to destroy this place? That hardly makes any sense, but Daedra worship too often doesn't.
You made it! I'm glad you're here. I wasn't looking forward to facing Renna alone. Not after what we found out.
So, have you chosen where to go? What region of the world strikes your fancy? Not everyone gets to pass instantly from one side of Tamriel to another, you know. This is quite a gift!
By the Eight, what was that? A murder? Someone recorded a murder in that stone? Why would anyone do that?\n\nWait …. Could this be related to the disappearances Grandpa Lierre told me about?
I know it's ridiculous, but … would you read that letter for me? I've faced all kind of dangers at your side, and now I find that I'm afraid of a bit of old yellowed parchment.

My grandfather should be interred in our family tomb in Othrenis. At least I think that's what mom said. She's never taken me to see him. I don't think she's been back there since the day he was buried.\n\nShe doesn't want to face him empty handed.
You saw it? We got so close! That monster killed my whole clan and we let it escape.\n\nThis man doesn't have long. I'll try to ease his pain, but you need to talk to him. Learn what he knows.
This is just silly. You came this far, Selveni, but you are too much of a flat-head to go farther!
Except for those here in Wretched Spire, I have met few of your kind, mortal. And those I have seen left me unimpressed.
I'll meet you at the Blood Pit. It's safer if we travel separately and don't call more attention to ourselves than absolutely necessary.
We waste time here, mortal. Do what you need to do and proceed to the base of Annihilarch's Summit. I am eager to discover the fate of my missing Kyn.
Once we enter the Shambles, we can work our way together to the old bathhouse.
I sometimes feel such weight - within my mind. Not a true headache, but it is a burdensome feeling.

And as if by fate, a solution presents itself.\n\nGreetings. I am Divayth Fyr, wizard-lord of Tel Fyr. I find myself in need of a partner. You seem well-equipped for the role. The position is yours if you wish.

Somehow our meddling with the End Times ash affected my asynchronous state. I was fully aligned with myself again, if only for a brief moment. Puzzling.\n\nI'm afraid I don't understand the implications, but Rrvenk might. We should return to Morah.

I have a keen eye for talent, my dear, and you're practically oozing it from your pores.\n\nI am Lady Arabelle Davaux. If you're looking for gainful employment, I have a proposition for you that pays exceedingly well. Care to hear more?

Ah, the breeze carries the sweetness of your success to my senses. \n\nBut I'm afraid your work is not yet done. Before I can tell you about the blessed awl—which was unceremoniously stolen from me—you must complete one more task.
Now that we're inside, I don't suppose you'd chat with the old man for me?

After each trial, I'll present you with a tablet. Every tablet has words of honor from Lady Joslin Garick herself.\n\nRemember these words. They will form the pass phrase needed to open the wards that protect the Sacred Shield.

Let's find a few concentrated areas of corruption. My spells will cleanse the impurities, then you burn them. \n\nHopefully we can determine the source of the corruption before this malady spreads to the rest of the island. Just keep your guard up.
The tower statuary was used for a number of debaucherous celebrations in the ancient time of the Coin-barons. \n\nI expect a number of stained, pitted bones will be available for procurement.

Hold still—you'll need this unless you want to spend the next few hours as a sheep. Not as glamorous as it sounds. And here, take these crystals, you'll need them to restore the wards. The first one is in the meadow just up the hill to the north.

Even if we do find the Prowler, I won't take off without Oblan. A captain never leaves a sailor behind.\n\nWhen we split up, he took a northwest path to the beach. We'll start there. Look for any sign of where he went.

I have been thinking very hard and it hurt. We should begin at the Ancient Anchor. That is where I went last night with the other diplomats.\n\nThe innkeeper was angry with me this morning, but she might talk to you. Meet you there!

The mine camp is just over that hill there. This is going to be fantastic! Can you imagine the look on father's face when I arrive with you to help? He'll be so impressed. \n\nMaybe we don't mention that I left Amenos Station without an escort, though.

I have news about my friends. Silverslip and Jhaka have been working to track down that strange eye symbol, remember?\n\nI'm not exactly sure what they've been up to, but Silverslip got a threatening letter from a merchant in Bangkorai. I'm worried.
Let's see what the knight commander has to say.

Oh, thank you! You've lifted a great weight off my shoulders. Come along. Lady Laurent is along the southern coast. \n\nDo prepare yourself. The curse has made m'lady a different person. Literally. She's been possessed by an ancient sea captain!

Looks like I was worried about nothing. Dhulef has weathered far worse storms than a handful of Firesong. Still, those druids are ruthless. I feel better now that we're all together.\n\nTalk to Dhulef. See what he's found.
Hag Fen? Not exactly a place of clear skies and a fair breeze. Hang onto that map and we can investigate it more thoroughly after we consult with Druid Laurel and the Beldama Wyrds.

Are those supplies for the Society of the Steadfast? I'm sure Lord Bacaro will put them to good use. Give them to him, then come talk to me.\n\nYou look like someone I could very much make use of right about now.

I don't know where you came from, mate, but I'm glad to see you. The cursed Sea Elves chased our soldiers out of this fort. I don't see any druids around to help out—must be busy with their own quarrels.\n\nSo it's up to us to take this fort back.
We'll need to proceed carefully once we get to Garick's Rest. If we are dealing with a powerful druid, we won't be able to avoid them for long.
Lady Arabelle is counting on us! Let's get moving.

These ancient stones have a song of their own to sing. Memory. Mourning. A lesson to teach, yet the druids in this place do not listen.\n\nThat way we must go. Where the sun rises. The seeds are not far.

We're doing great. Veshin's relaxed and bragging. Exactly what we want. Also, have you noticed how handsome he is? \n\nHe already let slip that he has a key. Eventually he'll spill their plan to control the relic. I think we need some silverbloom.

Remember, outsider. The Chronicle's tunnels are a sacred place to the Eldertide. Please be respectful.\n\nAnd keep alert. We don't know who or what else the spirit motes have exerted control over in there.

These caves wind through the Cenotaph's lower levels. Many of our defensive measures originate here and extend through the fortress.\n\nThe Dreamcarvers disabled our wards as they invaded. We must reset them.
See if you can return that book. I'm curious as to what the outcome will be.
You … You're not one of these third-rate assassins. I can tell.\n\nBut if you or anyone else puts a hand on me, I'm answering with my axes.
A place where mortals pass their pitiful lives breaking large rocks into small rocks. How depressing.\n\nThe arched gateway must be in here somewhere. I suppose we should keep looking.

Nathyn and I could finally be together. But the way to do so means becoming his mother's … experiment.\n\nBut I'd be safe. Provided for. I'd get to dance and sing every day with the one I love. Some would kill for such a gentle life.

The mortal keeps Hezehk waiting with anticipation. I can stand here forever! You're the one who grows old.\n\nBut you found my mirror and that's what matters. I'll use it to track the Voidprowlers. Assuming you found something of theirs as an anchor.
Dimik-ei was just trying to help me. She wanted to see the end of Sondivel, and she wanted her brother back.\n\nAnd I let her down in every possible way.

There was window, a small one, when I thought perhaps the path of a Star-Gazer was my fate. To sit, watch the heavens, and work with the heralds until I figured everything out. \n\nA few months later I ran out of skooma. And promptly left.
Hah! That was bracing! Pity the tome will smell like transliminal parasite now. Let's see what it says.

Everyone likes treats. It's one of those things. The powerful secrets. Known Things!\n\nFirst, bristleback lords! We have to put them to sleep. You can find sleep potions down in the gazebo. You toss 'em. They take a whiff. Then, bam! Snores galore.

While we contemplate the best method for tracking down Torvesard, there are two other tasks we must accomplish, proxy. One concerns updating the records of Apocrypha. The other requires us to return to Necrom and rectify the original anomaly of fate.

I never realized there was a shrine of Hermaeus Mora connected to the ruins of Anudnabia. We are in luck, proxy—it is not far from this monastery, just to the north.\n\nGadayn and I shall meet you there.
Both Scruut and I gleaned much from your examination of the reality tear. Since this is Scruut's area of expertise, I shall let her explain it.

The bloody clothes and the warning candle suggest someone or something attacked Rustwall. And we know Captain Leronus was working on a plan. I hoped to find him alive, but the letter from the groundskeeper tells us more than we knew before.

It would be easy to blame Daedra for everything, but there's plenty of evil to go around across Tamriel that has nothing to do with Oblivion.\n\nI wish we could be dealing with some of that right now, truth be told.

This wine is specifically meant for the mortals here, not the vampires. So why are the vampires bidding on it? And why is my flask doing little to curb my rising hunger?\n\nTell me you learned something more, my friend.
There she is, Pelena Weatherleah. Our killer. Quickly, while we have her cornered.
Is Ithelia purposely obscuring the path? Perhaps. Perhaps not. Either way, the Lamp of Clarity should reveal the way forward.
Imagine how long that testament has been here! Centuries upon centuries. I hope Leramil can make sense of it.
Not sure if the fabric got caught on something or if it was lost in a struggle. Either way, I think we're getting close. Let's keep moving.
The ruins of Niryastare lie in the far western reaches of the Colovian Highlands. I'll secure a few things here, then meet you there.
If Beragon insists we go see this so-called king, let's make it quick. We don't know how much time we have before the Recollection strikes again.

What perfect luck, my friend! You're exactly who I need right now. These people are safe, but there's others in the village of Ostumir still trapped by rubble or worse. Can you help me find them?\n\nThe quakes could start again, so we need to hurry.
I suppose we should not be surprised that the Loom would harbor memories relating to Ithelia. Let us take a moment to observe this one.

When you left, I was compelled to follow. I saw an image of you entering this chamber and I knew I had to be here with you.\n\nBut then this awful lamp appeared. Rudely popping out of nowhere. I hate the damned thing!
We have our orders. Reset the traps around the keep and burn those ropes. I have one more order. Take down as many Daedra as you can.\n\nLet's get to it.
And here we are, Toothmaul Gully. Let's head inside and find a suitable place to activate the tracker fly. Once it's on the move, we'll have to race after it.

Blue flames? That is a call to arms, a signal for the Hidden Moon. A sign that a dark spirit of great power has pierced the veil of Nirni.\n\nThat tablet you found in my tomb. It said those spirits were vanquished. What could this mean?
Another lattice broken, Bogcup? Those aren't easy to weave together, you know.\n\nAre you with Wisteria and Oleander? No one has checked in. We need to make our move now, before we lose our quarry.

Well, I suppose you saw that. It's been twenty years, and Sergeant Corvus is still a stuck-up Colovian prig. Two lives cut short—but we were deserters, so he thinks we got what we deserved.\n\nDamn it all. Maybe he's right.
This is all too much. I was happier when I was drunk. Safer, too.
That's three, right? You've really got a knack for this kind of thing! Is it possible … have you ever been a fox?
Those adepts mentioned Lirinisse was arrested by a reeve. Lirinisse is Snapdragon!\n\nLet's talk to them and find out what happened.
Eyes sharp and daggers ready. If Hyacinth is the traitor …. He's not getting away.
It's like Wisteria was right there. I just thought of her, focused on her, and there she was. \n\nI could feel the connection between us, stronger than it's ever been. All I had to do was reach out.
Once you ignite the braziers, kneel before the altar. The vapor will open our minds to visions of times past.
Krin'ze seems returned to her senses. Speak with her, tamiit. I would, but I am concerned it would be … too much.
Once we find a clear spot, I can open a portal with my moonclaw and bring the cantors here.

I am relieved to see you both. I could not say much in my letter, just in case it was intercepted.\n\nIzalgo, a cantor from my order, was tending to an exorcism nearby. An escort of Inquisitors accompanied him, but now they are all missing!
All right, let's stop chatting about our emotions and get on with taking down the Worm Cult.\n\nThey attacked our guildhalls, killed our comrades. I'm done talking. It's time to fight!

It's good to see you, friend, but we have a situation. Somehow assailants infiltrated a private meeting beneath the guildhall and caught some of our most influential mages unawares. Merric arrived and raced to help, but—did Skordo say Worm Cult?
We must find Guildmaster Merric and stop the Worm Cult invaders before another guildhall is lost. Let's push forward, comrade.

I've been watching you. Going around town, cleaning up the mess that beastly soldier-woman created by offending everyone.\n\nYou must have a golden tongue, getting folks to enlist after that. You won't persuade me, though. I can't leave town. Not now.
Aelif knew she could trust you.
Comrade, I have an urgent message for you.
The shrine of Lorkhaj is old and decrepit. I'll need to focus my energy on it. Go cleanse the other shrines and meet me afterward.
A friendly face, at last. I'm on a mission on behalf of the Queen herself. What are you doing out here?
The shrine of Lorkhaj is old and decrepit. I'll need to focus my energy on it. Go cleanse the other shrines and meet me afterward.

After he came through the portal, Tharn made a wisecrack about Sai being in love with me, and Sai actually blushed. Now he can't even look at me!\n\nWhat happened in there? Wait, I don't want to know. Sai's safe, and that's all that matters, right?
I swear, I haven't heard such bickering and whining since the last Tharn family gathering at Mid Year's Feast!
This is no projection. It is Mannimarco, himself! Stop him! He must not reach the Amulet of Kings!
Let's kill that traitorous bastard!
Mannimarco. Well, it's not like we didn't see this coming. I suppose we'll have to kill him.
What's a few more foul-breathed Daedra to one such as you? Get out there, you're going to do great!
I hold pirates in the same esteem that I hold bandits and other vermin. The chore of clearing them out is a necessary burden. Get to it!
Search grassy areas in the wilderness for raw jute. You should find enough if you look around.
Blend the solvent's purity with the reagents' traits. Return to me when you've crafted a potion.
What do you think? Glass, it is so scarce in this day of days. Very fine, very light. Not at all heavy.

You must be the new initiate. I've heard some unbelievable things about you. Still, you can't be too good. Your name hasn't appeared on one of my contracts yet.\n\nWhat? Oh, that's a Dark Brotherhood joke. Don't you have a sense of humor?

Did Canon Valasa send you? She did, didn't she! That means she made it to Seyda Neen. Vivec be praised!\n\nWill you help me complete my mission? It would be sacrilege if I don't enter my family's tomb and make Lord Vivec's inquiries.
How scary can a Lady of Lace be? Bring me her head and we'll drink to it. Or out of it.
Thanks for your help.
Welcome back, initiate. Have you done as I asked? Are the time breaches on Summerset Isle truly sealed?
Thank you for agreeing to this. The map's just there on the table.\n\nNow, you should hurry to Wasten Coraldale before those Maormer bandits do something stupid with the Augur.
Are you prepared to set out again, initiate? As I said, this threat to Nirn is far from settled.
Welcome back. We have a great deal to discuss, but you should speak with Famia first. She is anxious to hear what you discovered.

I just need to take a moment to speak to Xukas about Eshraf and Dinia. Hopefully he knows something, or knows someone who does.\n\nIn the meantime, why don't you head to the xanmeer? It's just east of here. I'll meet you there as soon as I can.
Ah, beeko. I would be lying if I said this is unexpected. Welcome to my home—Bright-Throat Village. Cozier than Lilmoth, I think.\n\nWhat brings you? Let me hazard a guess ….
I see you made it to the old loremaster's camp. Were the dusk mushrooms to his liking?

Thank you for helping, rhook. We should investigate the nearest gate of the aqueduct—just south of here. S'rendarr willing, we will find whatever blocks the water there.\n\nVazbi will meet you soon. This one must speak to Silhu-jo before she leaves.
Ugh—my fur! What was in this bucket? Whatever your death-wish is, it's granted!\n\nOw, my head. Just tell me what you're doing here before I turn your heart into a tomato.
Place the stone in the very center of the tomb, friend. Once the ritual begins, things will move quickly. So, be ready.
Remember, we need evidence of M'zum's involvement in the missing farmhands. Documents, ledgers, contracts—anything that makes him a suspect.

I see that my instructions were followed to the letter. The Champion of Anequina, Sai Sahan, and the Dragon Nahfahlaar, together in the same place. And I have brought Khamira.\n\nWe have much to discuss. It concerns … Kaalgrontiid.
Though we may search for the Dragonguard's secrets, we must be careful not to disrespect their sanctuary. Take only what you believe will be useful to our cause.

Let's see if this Za'ji fellow is as honorable as young Aeliah believes.\n\nWould you care to walk there together? There's much about Senchal I can tell you. Otherwise, we can meet in the city's outskirts.
You must be the help the Skald-King promised. I just hope you're up to the task.\n\nThis threat, it's bigger than King Jorunn imagined.
Fennorian has the right idea. Come up with a defense against the harrowstorms. After that, we can take the fight directly to the Gray Host.\n\nThanks for assisting me. I'll see you back in Solitude.
I wonder what Lyris has in mind. Roll out the map and let's see.

Svana, Fenn, and I will divvy up the camps and scout ahead. Fenn should investigate the coastal camp. I'll take the midlands camp. That leaves Svana with Blackreach.\n\nMeet up with each of us when you're ready. Then we'll hit each camp in turn.
That witch … what did she mean about the gray reliquaries?\n\nCome on, we should hurry.
The message said Fenn found lodgings on the south side of Dusktown. We should look for him there.

My father … a vampire! He sat on his throne, pretended to mourn for my mother, and said he had a plan. But all the while he was preparing the city for the Gray Host!\n\nHe's worse than a monster … he's a traitor and a liar!
As a junior member of House Ravenwatch, I never expected to be in the thick of things like this. I have to say, it's a tad overwhelming.
It's a long shot, but it makes sense that the Gray Host would attack Solitude from below. Let's get down there and stop the harrowstorm. My axe is thirsty and it craves those vampires' black blood.

The injured still need to be treated and the temple's corruption needs to be dealt with. Despite the way I feel about Meridia now, I still have a responsibility. I won't walk away from it.\n\nNot like Meridia walked away from us.

Brondold mentioned some locals we should have a talk with. A snitch named Greyga who likes to gamble in back alleys, and an Orc named Maugh who frequents the Lonely Troll inn.\n\nLet's find them and see what they can tell us.

The old ways of the Nords revolve around primordial animal spirits. Such totems were all the rage before the coming of the new gods. I must ask Mjolen to share her thoughts on the nature of the Divines.
Good work! Throw the solution on the rocks, then step back and watch!
Ah, assistant. It's about time.\n\nSo? Any luck with that cold-blooded librarian?

Everything I learned up to now points in the same direction. Bangkorai Garrison. There's a scholar named Laurette Diel there who may be able to tell us more about the Gray Host and how they were defeated.\n\nCart's over there when you're ready to go.

The Dark Heart … what does Rada plan to do with the Void energy? And why has he caused it to flow through his Gray Host like water through a mountain pass?\n\nI must explore this connection. See if I can find meaning in the currents of darkness.
I don't see how we figure out where Rada al-Saran went from here. Let's hope this Count Verandis of yours is as smart as Fenn claims.

Count Verandis said that? That he wants us to come meet him? All of us? Including me? I must put my notes in order! Wash the grime from … everything.\n\nSorry, could you talk to Lyris for a moment? I need to gather my thoughts.

I see Verandis's word is good. He said I could treat with you, and here you are.\n\nThe count tells me that Lady Belain and the Gray Host leader, Rada al-Saran, seek some powerful relic. The Arkthzand Keystone. Is that correct?

Thank the Eight Divines! I could really use some help. The name's Bastian.\n\nWatch yourself, friend. I was accosted by a Dark Elf at this very spot. She went into the cave over there hours ago, but she might return at any moment.
Ah, welcome back!\n\nThe runes are in place, right? I'm anxious to begin the experiment.

What did I tell you? Isn't she a ray of sunshine on a cloudy day?\n\nI placed the book like she said. And those cubes … they're just like the ones in my vision. Let's see if we can figure out how to remove the ward on that door.
Just a dizzy spell. Comes on strong when the trees don't know how to use their inside voice—and most don't.\n\nWe should take a look around these ruins. See what all the commotion's about.

Sweet Morwha's left tit, what was that all about? Sorry for the language. But … phew! Right? Have you ever met a ghost that gorgeous? Gods, I'm sweating right through this blouse.\n\nWe should head to the Giovesse chapel and look for Mathen's armor.
If we follow the coast northwest, we should reach the ruin soon enough. I don't think we'll have much trouble spotting it. Ayleid architecture tends to be conspicuously luminous.
Well, I'll be. Ardia actually made a break for it. She's the last one I'd have expected to escape. Two left feet, that one. Much as I'd like to believe she made it out, somehow I doubt it.
Nothing prepares you for moments like this. I'm glad you're here with me.
I saw that stone flash like a torchbug. There must be a memory tucked away in here somewhere!\n\nTry to conjure it up, all right?

I suppose the gambler's luck ran out. She should have been more careful about the company she kept. \n\nLet's get out of here. The sooner we bring this ring to Quistley, the sooner I'll get some answers.
Othrenis is in Stonefalls. I can't speak for the condition of the tomb, so we should assume it's dangerous.

Mauloch's breath. Look at this place! All of Mehrunes Dagon's fury on display.\n\nWe shouldn't stand around chatting. The sound could bring the entire citadel's forces down on our heads. Keep close to Atrozu. And move quickly.
I can sense the truth of what Arox said. The name Elegian tugs at my mind. Talk to Arox—I want to know more.
I cannot imagine what further need you have for the daedrat. Does your backpack require soiling?\n\nThey are not clean creatures.

These new Dagonists are barely worth the effort. I followed them into the plaza and destroyed the votive rune before they even noticed I was there. And the Grasp decided to get involved, finally!\n\nHey, did you learn anything from my contacts?
Give me a moment. I have much to consider.
See that mound of ash? I think the apocalypse seed is just under the surface. Try digging it up.

It's good to see you again, my dear. If you have the time and the inclination to help an old friend out of another problematic situation, I have a proposition for you. \n\nIt pays exceedingly well, I might add.

I am a master weaver, but my skills at the hearth are sadly lacking. Luckily, Zenithar teaches us to collaborate with others. If you could make baked apples, enough to fill a basket, he will surely be most pleased.
We made it. Let's go say hello to the old man.

A person of honor demonstrates that they will overcome any obstacle with tenacity. The Trial of Perseverance challenges you with unending foes who will attack ceaselessly until you escape.\n\nOr … it did until Amunara's lackeys wrecked the trial.

Traveler, I advise caution. A corruption has gripped Stonelore Grove, turning the wildlife aggressive and spreading an impurity unlike anything our circle has ever seen. Nature itself has fallen out of balance.

I've extensively studied this ruin. The spire's statuary gardens should be littered with bones from ancient rites. \n\nA large one, possibly a femur, would be a good handle for our sympathetic weapon.

I hope you don't mind me saying so, but you look like someone who's good at cleaning up messes. I've got a big one for you, if you're up for it. I'd pay you for your time. \n\nBut I need someone quick on their feet. This mess is turning into a crisis.

You! I hoped it was Oblan approaching, but you make a welcome sight. How strange to meet again on such a dangerous island.\n\nI could use your help again. Some pirate stole the Prowler. Have you seen Oblan? We split up to search for our ship.
Why, it is you! Bestest friend! I never expected to see you here on High Isle! This is most fortunate, because I have little problem again.\n\nI am large delegate! But I lost my scepter.

A dust-covered warrior. Finally! My father is the overseer at Brokerock Mine. He defends the prisoners laboring inside the mine from the gangs outside its camp. \n\nHe's struggling though. He thinks I can't help. I'm a thaumavocalist now!

It's funny seeing Jhaka and Silverslip together again. We've all changed a lot, but some things are still the same.\n\nI wonder where we would be if not for that awful day. Would I still be living in Skywatch, lifting wallets when I needed coin?

It will be good to catch up with Commander Jourvel. I've been thinking about her and Aurelia quite a bit lately. \n\nJust, whatever you do, don't order any All Flags rum at the tavern. I've seen sailors use it for paint remover.

Oh, what a fortuitous turn of fortune! Once again, you appear when Lady Laurent and I need you most.\n\nYou see, I find myself in something of a pickle and could use a modicum of assistance. Tell me, friend. How good are you at breaking ancient curses?

According to Dhulef's letter, he headed inside here. We need to find him before the Firesong do … if they haven't already. Root and thorn, let's hurry and get inside! I'll hang behind just a bit and watch your back.
Beware of shifting sands, sailor. I don't trust this place. Let's look around, but quickly.
Trouble gathers around Galen like clouds before a storm. I'm glad to have an adventurer such as you beside me, friend.
Go find Sir Stefan Mornard—he can tell you what needs doing. Last I saw, he was meeting with Lord Bacaro from the Society of the Steadfast.

I thought that I'd be able to replicate an antidote using some of the old recipes in my ancient herbal apothecary. But nothing I've concocted thus far has worked. This poison is proving very resistant to our tried and true elixirs.

We are close. The seeds sing loudly here. Yet the hearts of the druids in this place are dark. Filled with death and hate. They do not hear the song.\n\nSpeak with Druid Laurel. She will know what to do.
Oh, you're here! My friend Veshin studies under the sea witches. Isn't that interesting! \n\nHand him the treats, then ask where the sea witches reside. This could work.

It appears that the spirit motes do more than just tell us stories, outsider. That Firesong druid's mind was clearly being influenced if not outright controlled.\n\nBut why is the Chronicle doing this? It never exhibited hostile behavior before.

We may run into Dreamcarvers as we search. Do not hesitate to dispatch them with prejudice. Remember, they will reform in Oblivion over time. You will not.\n\nLet us move north through the tunnels. We will alert you when we find a ward.

Thanks to you, Meenai-Shai actually made it through the Calamitous Gallery. It's almost cause for celebration, though admittedly the bar is low.\n\nSince I am unable to lift the books I ask that you complete the task before we investigate.
I'm not used to having someone around all the time. Chatty, aren't you?

Most of the time, the research I undertake is wasted, but my study of the area indicated that the mine runs underneath the village. The entrance lies to the east.\n\nHmm. Why do you bear the mark of my master, mortal? You don't seem to be a devotee.
After I lost everything in Cyrodiil, Tel Dreloth became my home.\n\nI can't possibly leave it behind me. But does that mean I should stay here forever?

Hezehk is many things—courier, housekeeper, poet. But I am no fighter. If I roam about in search of the mirror myself, I'll get eaten.\n\nThis is why you are here. Find the mirror. And if you see any items the Voidprowlers left behind, grab them.

He said he felt my resistance. As soon as I saw him, I tried to resist. And it called him right to us.\n\nAnd now, he has Dimik-ei. She was safe and free, and she just wanted to help us. It's all my fault.
Damnit. Of course he's going to lord the bloodstone over me. \n\nI suggest you find some way to convince him, cohort, before we end up drawn into some elaborate Nilvon scheme.
That book acts as host for a tomeshell, a creature indigenous to the realm. Get after it!

Those Dreamcarvers came in here, opened all the exhibits, but didn't bring down the barrier? Rude! Inconsiderate! They didn't even clean up after themselves.\n\nThe Feral Gallery is a mess. It's untidy and strewn with cipher … bits. I want to leave!
The corruption eats away the very fabric of Apocrypha while Vaermina roams free. Will this path lead to our success? Indeed, will any of them? I suppose they must. The alternative is unthinkable.

Gadayn and I shall comb through this library and see if we can find any additional information about the Shrine of Inevitable Secrets.\n\nYou, however, should talk to the monks here and see if any more of them received a vision from the One Who Knows.
Reality simply doesn't break down like this, proxy. Not unless …. \n\nQuickly, we must examine that tear!
That's Captain Leronus lying on the floor. He commanded the cohort when I wasn't with them. He was a good soldier.\n\nI found that letter clutched in his hand. You should read it.
A single, very small sip, for experimental purposes only, and already my guts burn with fire. This wine is definitely dangerous to my kind, so why are these vampires here to bid on it?
I think Betu wants to show us something. Come on!
We stopped Ithelia from using the Loom to restore her realm of Mirrormoor. Now she seeks to remake Apocrypha in her own image. The more it changes, the weaker Hermaeus Mora will grow.
Incredible! Those priests certainly looked ancient! Merethic Era, I'd say. And that old book, it's the same one we saw in your Echonir vision! Just incredible!

Packs like that are a common sight in Sutch. Miners from the town of Ontus and around the region pass through here on a regular basis.\n\nTough decision to toss it, but better to lose your livelihood than your life.

Niryastare lies in the western Colovian Hills. It's rather dilapidated. And haunted. I had a harrowing experience there back when I was actively adventuring.\n\nLeramil wants to speak with you. Talk to her, then meet me at Niryastare.

I'm not sure what to make of everything the greenspeaker told you. Dawnway, Green Pact, wildburn … sounds like a lot of words that tell us absolutely nothing.\n\nYou'd better talk to Beragon and see if he can make any sense of all this.

I'm glad you happened by. This woman will be fine, but there's plenty more injured in what's left of the village of Ostumir. Maybe you could help me find them.\n\nThe ground could shake again at any moment. We need to hurry and save whoever we can.

Incredible. I thought the portal from Fargrave would take us to some Daedric apparatus. But it appears the Loom of the Untraveled Road is a place, not a machine.\n\nCome, proxy. Ithelia and Shardmarshal Vargas must be here somewhere.
Thoughts keep swirling through my mind. They move too fast to grasp. So confused, so lost.\n\nOnly one phrase makes sense. Sage's Dream.
It's good to see Commander Merian alive and barking orders. We can trust his leadership.\n\nFind out what he needs from us. I'll defend against attacking Daedra.

The tracker fly can't follow Wisteria's resonance until we're inside Toothmaul Gully. I'll activate the little guy when we get there.\n\nI wonder who you'll like more. Wisteria or Oleander? I want to say Wisteria, but Oleander has such a great smolder.
Yes, I traded my burial rags for armor belonging to those of my order. But let us discuss it after we tend to this ritual. Pour the moon-sugar water into the basin, please.
You're so much quicker than I was expecting. I thought I'd have to come out and show you where it was.\n\nI'm one step closer to talking to the Gryphon again!

Snapdragon? I haven't seen her in ages! A force of nature, that one! I saw her conjure a storm during an argument with the Gardener once. Petals and papers everywhere!\n\nIt shouldn't be hard to find her in Skywatch. Provided she hasn't been captured.
If I try to make sense of this. If I try to understand why Hyacinth would do this. I'll fall apart. \n\nLet's get to Southpoint and reach those tunnels. We do that, we find him. We get our answers.
Would you look at that. A Ceythalmor encampment. Let's see if we can turn up anything interesting.
How could the moon bishops allow this place to fall to such a state? Shameful. Just shameful.\n\nThe ritual chamber is in the western half of the temple, tamiit. Lead the way.
Let us return to Cantor Krin'ze. We did what we could to restore this place. Let us hope this satisfies my former partner.
Orcrest is little more than a fetid pit in this age. I weep for the life that once flourished here.\n\nLet us tread carefully as we make our way to the town hall cellar.
I have a song to practice, walker! Let us speak some other time.
What you said to the little prince. I couldn't have phrased it better myself. Nice work, pal.

Time is short so speak quickly. Somehow assailants infiltrated a private meeting beneath the guildhall and some of our most influential mages were caught unawares. Merric arrived and raced to help, but—did Skordo say Worm Cult?
Merric is my mentor and guildmaster. If he battles the Worm Cult in the bowels of a Mages Guild sanctum, then I should be at his side.\n\nLet's go deal with these cowardly invaders.
Why are women so complicated? It's maddening! Maddening!
You have spoken to Merric, then? Seen the council? It is about time we acted.
Well met, comrade. I have an urgent message from the Guildmaster.
Hallowed … you saved my life.
My friend. You cannot imagine how grateful I am to see you. I have need of a veteran in the Queen's service today.
Hallowed … you saved my life. Your claws get sharper every day.
I'm glad you're here. I'm about to punch Tharn in the teeth again, and I didn't want you to miss it.
It is finished. Mannimarco's fate is well deserved. \n\nIt's time to take the Amulet of Kings and leave this befouled place.
We did it! I … I don't believe it! Mannimarco is gone!
I'll admit, Vestige. I never thought you'd be the one to kill the worm.\n\nTake the Amulet of Kings and let's be gone from here.
If the Daedra prove too much for you, rest easy knowing that you'll be fertilizing Grahtwood's greatest landmark.
Mortal combat awaits. There will be no retreat available. That should not concern one who is Undaunted. Claim your victory!
Show me you can craft a pair of homespun gloves. First you'll collect some raw jute, then return here and refine it.\n\nFinally, you'll use refined jute to make the gloves.
An apprentice of mine tried to use sea water as a solvent. I had him drink the results.\n\nHe agreed it was a terrible idea … after he finished retching.
What do you think? The tailoring, it is exquisite. It feels as though one is wearing nothing at all, yes?

Archcanon? I don't think I'll ever get used to that.\n\nStill, it's been a grand adventure, hasn't it, my friend? I suppose if I could survive everything that happened, I can certainly serve as the high priest to Lord Vivec! How hard could it be?
Ayleids are lucky they're all dead. I hate short-toothed wimps who kneel to Daedra. You find any in Garlas Malatar, give them a good thunk for me.
Have you spoken to my apprentice yet?\n\nI would never counsel against prudence and careful planning, but this is a matter of some urgency.
Yes? Can I … can I help you?
The hopes and intentions of the Psijic Order go with you, initiate. You will overcome this threat. Of that I have no doubt.
You should take this moment to introduce yourself. I need to speak with Xukas, but it can wait until you've met him. No time like the present to start making new friends!

The brightest, loudest throats croak your name, beeko! This makes it difficult to sleep, but under the circumstances, I think I can forgive you. That business with the egg-tenders was no mid-day wallow.\n\nNow, we have something to discuss, I think.

The Halls of Colossus, a place as mysterious as it is ancient. I never imagined I'd have a reason to seek it out, let alone explore it. Let's hope the item we pursue lives up to my expectations.\n\nAnd that we reach it before my half-sister, Euraxia.
Vazbi cannot understand. Only puddles remain in the adeptorium's cisterns, but still Silhu-jo forbids this one to act!

Thank you for acting quickly, friend. The situation appears much worse than I thought.\n\nThe being you just encountered—it was the shade of a dark lich. An undead Khajiit possessing unimaginable power. You just shattered one of his phylacteries.
Lead the way, five-claw, but be stealthy! Raz will be right behind you.
Let's be on our way, then. Kasura has agreed to let us borrow her horses.\n\nThe sooner we search these Dragonguard sanctuaries, the sooner we can uncover their secrets.
Well this is unexpected. Why would a member of the Shields of Senchal wish to speak with us?\n\nBest if we see what she has to say.

Orders from Rada al-Saran. His words send a chill down my spine. Their plan for Solitude, it might even be more dreadful than an all-out attack.\n\nWe need to get back and determine the exact location of this Undergrove place.

I … I know what you need me to do. Put my … experience behind me. Focus on the mission. Just like Verandis taught me.\n\nCould you show me the research you recovered from Exarch Tzinghalis's laboratory?
I know a commander's map when I see one. Each of those marks matches a location mentioned in the communique from Rada al-Saran, the leader of the Gray Host.\n\nI can already see where we need to go.
I hope that Jarl Olfwenn got somewhere safe.
Fenn's message is on the table. It's addressed to you, partner. Read it and find out what it says.
Enough talk. Let's enter Blackreach and find the ritual site. I won't let my father and the Gray Host destroy Solitude. I simply won't!

I had hoped to secure the sacred oil and make enough elixir to distribute throughout the city, but we're running out of time.\n\nOur best bet now is to find the ritual site beneath Solitude and stop the harrowstorm before it's unleashed.
Well, the soldier spoke true. The temple gates are sealed shut. If the Gray Host's forces are inside, I wonder what they're planning.\n\nTalk to the swordthane. Maybe he has more information.
Who invited that abomination?\n\nWe're here to burn away the forces of darkness, not befriend them.
You handled that better than I expected. Now, what in Mara's name happened to Brondold?
Ancient Nord magic is a rare thing to observe. You should take the opportunity while you have the chance.

This was a tragedy, but even disasters like this are opportunities for growth.\n\nI won't take any pleasure in Mazog's punishment. But hopefully this small cruelty will help prevent another catastrophe. She might even learn something. I know I have.
Don't let that prickly lizard push you around, assistant. Remember, the eyes of history are upon us! Her concerns pale in comparison.

What? Saving Skyrim wasn't enough for you? Had to sign on for even more heroics?\n\nIt's good to see you. I could use your help. You know better than anyone what we're dealing with. We need to figure out exactly what the Gray Host is up to.

We stopped Lady Belain from gorging the Dark Heart with all the souls of Markarth, but we can't bring back the dead. Still, the Heart awakened but never reached full power.\n\nWe turned back the Gray Host and killed Belain. That's a victory, my friend.

Yeah, a lead that's dragging us in circles.\n\nLook, Fenn can tell you more. I'm sure he'd love to talk to someone other than me. Brilliant conversation isn't one of my better-known graces, as you've experienced firsthand.

What? Oh! Sorry! I was fixated on this trinket.\n\nWhen Verandis said he would send someone, I assumed he meant Adusa. We weren't supposed to make a move, but Lyris feared we'd miss our chance. I don't think we ever had one, but don't tell her that.
What say you, harrier? Ready to give up your civilized ways and join a Reach clan? I can put in a good word for you.

I don't know which of the Eight Divines sent you this way, but I'm glad to see you. The name's Bastian. Be on your guard, friend—I was accosted by a Dark Elf. \n\nShe went into the cave hours ago, but she might return at any moment.

Remember, precision is of the utmost importance! So, no loafing or dawdling, you!\n\nUgh. I'm sorry. We're supposed to use harsh declaratives like that to motivate people. Are you—? Yes, I can tell you're motivated. Great. That's great.
Oh great, her again! You talk to her, all right?
Well, the good news is I think the rumors about that creeper seed were true. The bad news is it took root.

Rugged, isn't he? Ugh! Get it together, Yisara!\n\nYou're fairly normal, right? Is it weird to swoon over your great-great grandmother's long-dead murder victim? It's weird. Sorry. Just get him talking. I'll take notes.

The ruin I spoke of is north of town. Not too far. I'll have a word with the innkeeper and Heseph about keeping Annyce occupied while we work, but if you wish to speak with anyone else before we head out I'll wait here.
Ardia was a proper researcher. She was always scribbling in her notebooks. The klutz must have dropped it.\n\nBut when? Of the group, I'd say she's the least likely to escape on her own.
I figure we should start at the bottom of this place and work our way up. With any luck, we'll see that stone light up soon enough.\n\nCome on. Let's explore the ground floor.
I have another favor to ask, if it's not too much trouble?

Now we stand a chance with you here. I saw a drainage grate on the northern wall that we can use to slip into the citadel. We'll meet you inside. From there, we just follow my bear.\n\nKeep your eyes open and weapons ready. It'll be a hornet's nest.

I think I'll stay here while you, Lyranth, and the talking rat return to the Deadlands. A memory swelled up when the Collector examined my mask. It isn't clear and I don't understand it, but I want to try to recall my first few days in Fargrave.
Lyranth the Foolkiller wishes to speak to you … although what need she sees for discussion is beyond me. We should move against Annihilarch's Summit at once. My missing Kyn may be there.

I need you to talk to my contacts. Madam Whim's establishment is here in the city. Initiate Tilgo meets me in the Burn, out in the Deadlands. See what they know about the votive runes and the cult's plans. Then meet me in the Fargrave Crafting Plaza.
I've managed to conjure some elements for you to use on the End Times ash tree.\n\nNow you just need it to sprout new seeds.

Welcome to High Isle, adventurer. I am Lady Arabelle Davaux. My keen eye for talent can practically see it oozing from your pores. Care to hear my proposition? \n\nIt pays exceedingly well, I might add.

Zenithar, lord of trade and commerce, have you turned your favoring eyes toward me? \n\nHave you sent me the means to recover your blessed awl and bring your teachings to the weavers on this holy day?
Looks like you've found them! Just place them on the pillars, there. That should lower the wards.

Words from a hateful creature such as her can only poison your heart. Even attacking someone so lowly would bring dishonor.\n\nYou must continue on to the Trials of Worth without fail. Let none break your stride!
It was so good to see Dame Madach in fighting form. She's gone after the bloodmage?
Magic can be so fussy. I just love messing with it! Is that a crime?\n\nActually, now that I think about it, it might be.

Hmm. I hoped the sound of approaching feet meant my quartermaster had returned. Some fish wart of a pirate stole our ship. We split up to search to find it, but I haven't seen him since.\n\nTell me, any chance you spotted a dour Khajiit on the beach?
Hello there! I am Rigurt, sometimes called the Brash. And I am large delegate for the Ebonheart Pact Cultural Exchange!\n\nOr I would be. If I had my scepter.
None of the accounts I studied mentioned clothes being so uncomfortable! I'll have to see if the tailors can do something about this.

Vampire or not, we found Silverslip, that's what's most important. It's been so long since I've heard her voice. There was a time I thought I'd never hear it again.\n\nNow that I've had a moment to collect my thoughts … I'm really happy.
Hey, friend. So … I received another letter from the knight commander. I haven't opened it yet. I wanted to wait until we were together.
You there! I hate to impose, but I'm in something of a pickle and could use a modicum of assistance.\n\nDo you happen to have any experience dealing with ancient curses?

In his letter, Dhulef mentioned he was headed to the Ebon Crypt in northern Glenumbra. Let's move as quickly as wind between bare branches. We must reach him before the Firesong do. I refuse to lose another friend to them.

So Archdruid Michiel is taking orders from another archdruid? Probably someone back on Y'ffelon. They're after some sort of nature spirit, and they need Wyress Tola to reach it. \n\nWhat happens when she's served her purpose? Nothing good, mate.

Sir Stefan is outside Vastyr with Lord Bacaro, the leader of the Society of the Steadfast. Which reminds me, I've got the healing herbs he asked for. Give these to Lord Bacaro, mate.\n\nNow I'm off. Got Sea Elf raiders near Windwrack Fort to deal with.

Hopefully this merchant can tell you who poisoned Lady Arabelle. Meanwhile, I'll give Za'ji her orders before I head back to my workshop to create an antidote.\n\nAnd I'll make sure Caska keeps an eye on things here. Arabelle is still in danger.
Go, friend. Toward the sunrise. Toward the song. I will walk with Druid Laurel, and we shall meet you by the sanctum of the last Druid King—Ivyhame.

Don't worry. Veshin won't refuse my offer. I barely shook him loose to come back here. Plying him with food and drink? A bit riskier.\n\nGather those blue-backed siltcrabs in the tidepool and join my little date. I have to practice my seduction skills.
The spirit motes latched too deeply into this Firesong druid for my blessing to disperse them.\n\nQuickly now. Talk to the druid before my spell gives out.

Dreamcarvers roam the halls of the Cenotaph, seeking a path into the Crux. Resetting the fortress defenses shall be our first task.\n\nYou can enter through a cave system to the north. We will secure this camp, then meet you inside.
You should keep him close. Don't want him to die again. Well, that's likely inevitable, but let's hope he doesn't die too soon.

I assumed this would turn out to be some pointless mortal delusion. A minor contradiction, easily resolved. But Oblivion gateways and Daedric shrines? And plans to invade Apocrypha?\n\nUgh. This might take longer than I thought.
I feel at peace with my decision to stay. Thank you for helping me make the right choice.

I can track the Voidprowlers with my mirror, but I lost it when they chased me. Look around some stairs by the shore. And grab anything that might belong to the thieves. That'll be helpful.\n\nThat's it. Get walking. I hear mortals require exercise.
She's gone!
Hmm. Nilvon looks as though he's been taking care of himself since our time together. Brilliant.
Stay close. Mortal magic of any kind is dangerous in Apocrypha. Especially when cast in search of knowledge.
Square cheese. Cheese squared. Round cheese is inferior. Circles contain less space. Must remember to ask the chilly islands. \n\nOh! No. Can't be. Yes. Wasn't a glub. It's safe here. Safe.
Those devout priests offered themselves so their Princes could meet in secret. We must find the gate they used. It could be the access to Apocrypha Torvesard is seeking.
A tear in reality would certainly explain the frayed and shredded threads of fate. We must examine this tear, proxy.

Rustwall Manor is usually pristine. The staff would never leave so much as a chair out of place. Not willingly, at any rate.\n\nLet's look around. We need to find anything that suggests what happened here.
I see vampires and mortal servants, but no obvious guards. I wonder where Valente is hiding them?

Our imposter is dead and our killer nearly succeeded in taking Betu's life as well. It is also not lost on Mizzik as to who is missing from this room.\n\nThe note you found with imposter Theophan's body, what does it say?
The Lamp of Clarity might serve us here. Unleash its light and let us see what secrets it reveals.

Um, what's an Echonir? It has something to do with the strange glowing mist that appeared the moment you walked into the room, doesn't it?\n\nNever mind. Just do whatever you're going to do and I'll catch up later.
I was a tracker long before Balandrus inflicted me with that damn curse. That trail is as clear as day. Group of folks left the bank and headed southwest, trying to be quiet.\n\nLet's keep moving.

I'm still deciphering the map from Hoperoot. I can't yet make sense of all the notes, but I figure that any location marked on the map must be important to the Recollection.\n\nHow did your investigations go?

We're standing in a forest that grew overnight. Pointing out that the Wood Elves of Vashabar occupy land that belongs to West Weald isn't an accusation. It's a simple statement of fact!\n\nAh, never mind. You talk to her. Find out about that seed.
What's happening across West Weald threatens everyone, Wood Elves and Colovians alike.
I suspect no mortal has ever set foot within the Loom of the Untraveled Road. Imagine the secrets waiting to be discovered here, if only we had the time to study it properly.
I don't know where the name comes from, or why it's clear while the rest is chaos. But the drink called Sage's Dream is important.\n\nPlease, find the answer for me.
We made it in easily enough, but that's just the beginning. Tracking down Commander Merian is our objective now.\n\nI don't know what we'll find inside, so stay alert.
Just grab that fluid and meet me outside Toothmaul Gully. \n\nOh. And if the bottle feels a little warm, that just means I got the mix right. Just try not to shake it too much.

This blessing requires moon-sugar water, yes? So long as things have not changed too much, you should find some in the cloister at the front of the temple. Retrieve some and return to me.\n\nDo not worry. The portal will admit you as it did before.
It's a little dirty. I can clean it off if you like? No, I … I've done enough already. You just take it.
This place is gorgeous! Like he took a slice out of a mansion and dropped it into this cave.\n\nYou talk to the Gardener while I have a quick look around.
Snapdragon's hurt! You talk to her, friend. I'll … I'll watch for more Ceythalmor.

Let's work down the list, starting with the area southwest of Seaside Sanctuary. I marked your map. Greenshade's coast is all coves and inlets. Plenty of spaces to hide. \n\nNow let's go. This authoritarian plot isn't going to unravel itself.

Jode's Light. I did not think to translate it. But this is a different time, yes? \n\nLet us make haste, tamiit. There may still be a way to save Izalgo and the other cantors if we can figure out where Ravith-morna lairs.

Curious. Cantor Izalgo's words echo a parable of the Hidden Moon. Of a necromancer who lived his entire life in cloister, devoted to Azurah.\n\nWhen he died, she took his soul and mourned the life he swore only to her.
I have opened the way. Let us get to Orcrest and get on with this display.

Talk to the little prince and help him pull his head out of his arse. Merric's dead, but the rest of us are still here. So we need to get our shite together and figure out how to stop the Worm Cult. It's what Merric would want us to do.
It often seems as though the Mages Guild careens from one crisis to the next. What I wouldn't give for a few days of blissful peace!
I came as soon as Skordo's message reached me, but apparently Guildmaster Merric beat us all to the battle. Tell Gabrielle what you learned and then we can get below to help as best we can.
Bright Moons, comrade. Good to see you again. Go on inside, Merric is waiting. We have much to discuss, but Aelif can wait a few moments more.
If you'd like to join the Fighters Guild, you should talk to someone who gets paid more than I do.
Come back later. We can talk some more!
Hallowed. I take it you've restored order to the Merchants District?
Thank the Green! My friend, it's good to see you out here. Can I beg your assistance?
Hallowed. I take it you've restored order to the Merchants District?
At long last, the Amulet of Kings! My Lord Varen awaits our return. Let us leave this befouled place.
Finally! We've got the damned thing. Now can we get out of here?
Ah, the Amulet of Kings. Well done.\n\nI never should have let Sai get his hands on it. This was the worst possible place to hide the amulet!
Listen, I know what you're thinking. You're never going to get the stench of the sewers out of your tunic. And you're right. Don't worry, I know just how to burn it, after.
Does the thought of the creatures of the dark forest give you pause? Do their hungry fangs and sharp claws make your skin crawl? No beast is the match of the Undaunted. Find that truth!
You certainly know your way around a forge. You're a blacksmith, and let none tell you otherwise.
Locate a solvent and some reagents so you may craft a potion.\n\nI'll remain here. For now.
What do you think? The gloss of ebony, it is like staring into a distant, dark lake. Engrossing, yes?

Who knew what we were getting into when we met at my ancestral tomb, eh, my friend?\n\nI'm just sorry that poor Archcanon Tarvus is no longer with us. I mean the real one. Not the Daedric hound. He really was a good man. And an excellent priest.
Frostvault is far in the north, so bundle up! On the bright side, cold weather is good fighting weather. Takes all the sting out of the blows.

The first cluster of time breaches appeared on the Isle of Summerset. You should start there. \n\nGo speak with my apprentice, Josajeh, in the Athenaeum. She will provide the tools you need: a map, Psijic Seals, and the Augur of the Obscure.
All right, you look prepared!\n\nRemember, the Augur is somewhere on the coast near Wasten Coraldale. My visions revealed more than a few Sea Elves, but it's nothing you can't handle, right? Right.

We use this hut as a gathering place of sorts. For now, I suppose. Nothing lasts forever out here in the marsh.\n\nIf Eshraf or Dinia got into trouble, they'd definitely come here. Maybe they were here and left something behind?
There is still much to do, I think.

This pointless war has gone on long enough. It's time to put a stop to it.\n\nGather the dusk mushrooms and head for Dagaril-dro's camp. As soon as I take care of the shadow that's been following me, I'll meet you there.
We must hurry, walker.
What brings you back here? The answers lie in that tomb at the center of the Scar. Move swiftly, friend.
Raz is glad you made it. He was about to proceed without you.\n\nNow, remember, we need to be stealthy. The fewer guards that notice us, the fewer guards we'll have to kill, yes?

This old warrior has deciphered the first map. It leads to the Wind Scour Temple, hidden atop the ruins of HoonDing's Watch.\n\nI saw the light of the brazier. I take it you were able to utilize the grappling bow?
It seems the general isn't eager to speak with me. Best if you explain our request.

We heard them talking about orders. Something about getting more netherroot from a place called the Undergrove. And something about an attack on Solitude.\n\nWe need to acquire a copy of the orders. Let's check in the command tents.
I … just give me a moment. To collect myself. I'll be ready to do my part when you need me.
The map we found in Tzinghalis's sanctum. Put it on the table where everyone can see it.
These people. They're from Karthwatch. They … might be all that's left of the town.
I should probably send word to Jorunn the Skald-King while I'm at it. Let him know the current situation.\n\nProvided, of course, I can find a courier willing to carry a letter to Eastern Skyrim.
The swordthane. He was a constant presence when I was growing up. Always so strong and brave at my father's side. I've never seen him this distraught.
I didn't want to believe it, but the temple gates are locked. And without the sacred oil, I can't make more of the elixir.\n\nTalk to the swordthane and see if he knows what's going on in there.
Now's not the time to lose your nerve, partner. Introduce yourself to the queen.
Did you acquire the reagents Mjolen requested? Then give them to the clever woman so she can perform the divination.

I have a good feeling about the stronghold's future. \n\nHopefully, this leniency will set us on a new course. Maybe Thulsgreg will even thank me. That would be a change of pace. Honestly, this is an opportunity to start fresh. We need that.

Oh, it's you. My under-eager assistant of adventures past. Well, any port in a storm, yes? We need to find Maelmoth's Mysterium quickly!\n\nFirst, we need his journal. A bullheaded librarian refused to share it with me. Can you believe that?

Haven't had enough of me yet, have you?\n\nGood. Because I could use your help again. You were with me for the first part of all this. It's only right that you should be here for the culmination, when we learn all of the Gray Host's secrets.

I was this close to finally planting my axe in Rada al-Saran's face. If Fenn hadn't insisted we wait for his Ravenwatch friends, that monster wouldn't have slipped through our fingers. Again.\n\nYou're still on the hunt for him, too, I see.
Finally, we can get started! There's a lot riding on this experiment's success. So … yes, let's all stay focused and diligent.\n\nAnd also very, very careful.
Remember to avoid the Sul-Xan. But keep an eye out for the Waking Flame cultists. I wouldn't be surprised if we run into them before too long.\n\nNow, let's go find the pit of the outsider!
Can't even hear myself think. Let's have a look around. See what the racket is all about.
I'm ready when you are!
So, that's Annyce Favraud. What do you make of her?

I recognize these corridors. The expedition hadn't split up just yet. Everyone aside from Eolaf would have been lead somewhere beyond.\n\nThe exit wasn't far, but it's sure to feel like farther now that the place's crawling with cultists and Daedra.

Ugh. Look at this place. These Dibellites fancy themselves free spirited bards blown by the wind, but they've got enough gold to make Zenithar blush.\n\nBah. Doesn't matter. This is where we'll find our answers.
