Remember, rooting out a nest of bandits is a secondary concern today. We just need to find this Grenetta and convince her to give back the Silvelle heirloom ring … one way or another.\n\nThen we'll see what Quistley found.
Again, sorry for dragging you into the middle of all this, but at least everything turned out all right in the end.

Glad to see someone who's not Daedric. My friend and I need your help.\n\nA beast lives in this citadel. The Ravener. It slaughtered my clan. Only a few of us lived. So we found our way into the Deadlands to destroy it in our clan's name.

Lyranth's been waiting for you. We've been discussing what we can do to find Sister Celdina and the Riven Cataclyst, but she's been frustratingly reluctant to share her thoughts.\n\nThe Deadlands is huge and they could be anywhere! Talk to her, please!
I will not pause until I have found the missing members of my clan. And if they have been harmed, I will punish the curs responsible. This I so swear!

Damn these Waking Flame cultists, bringing their Mehrunes Dagon madness to Fargrave. Their votive runes infect mortals with dark magic. I came to meet someone about all this when I spotted that cultist and my hands began to glow.\n\nJust like yours.

This is an End Times ash tree, but it appears to be like most things in the Deadlands—dead.\n\nAll is not lost, though! I remember that these trees have a particularly volatile life cycle. Growth, destruction, regrowth. It just needs a nudge.
The path to good fortune is muddy. Zenithar teaches that the first step toward wealth begins by putting on your boots.

Everything we're looking for should be nearby. You should find the heron's feather south along the coast. Cat's paw grows beneath some trees east along the road. \n\nSpriggan's veil … hmm. Maybe check around Breakwater Cave? It's to the southeast.

Already you show more virtuous character than Amunara ever will. Your compassion will go remembered.\n\nNow, enter Garick's Rest to begin the Trials of Worth. Pass with honor, but move quickly. I cannot allow Amunara to cheat her way to the shield.
That was the Bloodmage, Cassel! You should talk to Dame Madach, adventurer.
The Prowler's crew has faced many dangers. And we always win the day. I have no doubts that our track record will hold up. We can't be beat!
I'm not sure what I'd do without your help. You should be large delegate too!

For years, I've carried the guilt of losing my friends. But hearing Silverslip's story helps a little. I think her burden of guilt is much heavier than mine. How can she bear it? My heart hurts for her. \n\nStill, we found her. That's a victory.

I have no idea what I'm going to say in that letter.\n\nDear Dame Jourvel, I let your daughter stay in the dodgy part of High Rock with a merchant captain. I'm sure she's going to be fine investigating a criminal conspiracy. How are you?

You, my friend, are a true hero. You always seem to ride to the rescue when Lady Laurent and I need you most. If there's ever anything a humble manservant can do for you, you only have to ask.\n\nNow if you'll excuse me, m'lady has need of me!

In his letter, Dhulef mentioned he was headed to the Ilessan Tower just outside of Daggerfall. Let's move as quickly as wind between bare branches. We must reach him before the Firesong do. I refuse to lose another friend to them.
I don't see the wyress anywhere, but the Firesong aren't exactly tidy by the looks of it. I'm sure we can find something here that will help us locate her. How about we start with that note?

Why, it's you! I should have known you'd turn up on Galen. Good timing—we have plenty of trouble to go around today.\n\nI took a post as mage-for-hire to Count Mornard, but he needs all the help he can get. And he pays well for it.
Go ahead. Tell Lady Arabelle what you uncovered. We don't want her to get overly agitated right now. It could speed up the progress of the poison.
That which dreamed through seasons uncounted now awakens. The sacred seeds sing to me. Together now, they find their voice. They tell me to come to them. Soon I must answer.
Good, you're here. And you found Umindior. Based on his state I can guess why he went missing.\n\nHe mentioned you found something. A ritual cave? Did you learn something there?

Not finding my wife could mean anything. All we know is that she's not here. She could be anywhere!\n\nBut yes, let's go check the waterfalls to the north. That's where Druid Senna's note said the Firesong Druids went after the spirit motes descended.
Greetings, outworlder. We know why you came. And we offer gratitude for your timely assistance.
And now this mortal is staring at me like they can actually see me … like they recognize I'm here. Wait, can you actually see me? You know I'm here?
I have read of places such as this. Mortals drown their wits in drink, rather than confront the crushing despair of existence.\n\nLook around. Something here might provide a clue as to what happened.
I feel at peace with my decision. Thank you for helping me make the right choice.

And now you're here. That mortal I chased after in Fargrave. Perfect.\n\nDo you enjoy seeing Hezehk in the dirt? Robbed of the one thing Madam Whim asked me to keep safe? My debt to her will never end after this.
You're not backing out now, are you?

Thank you, for the infiniteth time cohort. Your support is what makes this journey of mine possible.\n\nWe'll need the bloodstone, rubric, and paper if we're going to confront the adversary. Just let me know if you have any questions.
I've no idea where in Aurbis to look for my old colleague, Martina. But! I know she was working with a Daedric consultant, a creature named Tem. \n\nIf we can summon Tem, we can find Martina.
Ah, now we seem to be getting somewhere. Retrieve that old tome, proxy. I want to know what instructions those ancient priests chose to leave behind.
That man … I see it, too. His connection to the threads of fate is tenuous at best. Talk to him, proxy.

Once more, I designate you as a temporary agent of the West Weald Legion. Keep this up and I may just make you enlist.\n\nWe'll search the manor house first. I'll meet you there. Just stay alert, comrade. We don't know what happened here.

A large gathering of vampires typically means trouble, but I've seen no evidence of violence as yet.\n\nLet's be very careful in how we proceed. We don't want to accidentally set off a blood frenzy, now do we?
We have everything Otho needs to save Betu, let's hurry back.
Be wary, proxy. The One Who Knows got us close, but as we saw at the Loom, the energy now contained in Ithelia makes portals behave strangely. We still need to reach Mora's private sanctum.
Abbot Andor is renowned throughout Morrowind for his scholarship in ancient myth and lore. I'm sure he'll be able to help us. Speak with him, friend.
Let's find Grivier's trail and follow it.
Tribune Alea can use a hand. She went to Feldagard Keep to warn them about the attack plans we found at Hoperoot.\n\nMeet her there and provide any assistance she requires, then return here.
I don't know if it's a good idea to take that seed to Vashabar. We could be handing it right back to the Recollection. Who knows how many friends they have there?

I remember so little about myself. Why is that? Did someone … yes, Mora! He did this!\n\nBut Sage's Dream. I know it can help me, even as the details slip away. Please ask the innkeeper. I feel certain he knows something.

The door is recessed between a gap in some rocks. I wouldn't call it a hidden entrance, but it's easy to miss if you don't know about it. I'll point it out.\n\nOnce inside, we'll find Commander Merian. He'll tell us how we can help.

I hope Chirrabi didn't give you a hard time. She's quick to show her claws, but you should hear the way she purrs when …. \n\nYou know what? Never mind. I'll take those ingredients now, if you please.
I am like sand in a dust storm, zha'al. All out of sorts. Thank you for being patient with me. Check the prayer book and help my weary mind grow clear.
Oh my gosh, I was right! You're trying to fix Ulfsild's library! You're trying to talk to the Gryphon aren't you?\n\nI am so sorry about tearing all the pages out of that book.
Understated but still a bit flashy. Classy, in a restrained sort of way. Almost dignified, even.\n\nLet's head inside and see what this new greenhouse looks like!
I can't believe this is happening. Let's find them. Before ….

This is it, friend. I can hardly believe it! These are the notes the Ceythalmor burned back at Firsthold. Snap made a copy!\n\nLook at this, a suspect list and all of our recent movements. I'm impressed, a little scared, and kind of hot and bothered.

I will tell you what I know. Before she fell to the Bent Dance, Ravith-morna was Moon-Singer Ravith. In my time, moon-singers were not so different from Twilight Cantors.\n\nMy memory of her holds a sorrow I have trouble putting into words.

Cantor Zayabi fell to Ravith-morna's corruption in the Vile Manse. We arrived only in time to save her soul.\n\nShe likens me to a sword that has lost its edge, but she is mistaken. I am no blade made blunt from overuse.

Thank you for handling that, tamiit. I might have said something that would cause more harm than good.\n\nI am curious about this change of heart and request to witness my skills, but if she seeks to make amends with Krin'ze … I will listen.
That can't be right. What Prince Azah said. Merric can't be dead. Tell me this is some sort of bad joke, pal.
Whenever you're ready, Wimi can take you to rendezvous with our scout. She's reliable and good on long trips.
The guild's spear returns. Aelif has been thinking of you.
No messages for you right now, but I'll let you know as soon as I hear otherwise.
You did it! Bright moons hang above us.
Ah, you're just as Razum-dar described you. I'm on a vital mission here. Will you lend me aid?
Sharp claws on you! All the Atronachs are gone!
You have outdone yourself, my friend. Mannimarco is defeated and the Amulet of Kings is ours.\n\nMy Lord Varen awaits. Speak with him and tell him of our victory.
We got the Amulet of Kings and sent that traitorous bastard to Oblivion where he belongs. All in all, I'd say that's a good day's work!
The Amulet of Kings is ours. The companions are victorious, again.\n\nI'm sure Varen will be eager to hear all about our fantastic and amazing victory.
I'd say breathe through your mouth, but that sewer air might be so thick you could taste it. Take your time coming back!
You value your sanity, unlike many our cohort. But to deny this task is to lose yourself to cowardice. At least a lunatic suffers no shame.

Bring the iron dagger you made to a crafting station and deconstruct it. Return to me when you're done.\n\nYou can deconstruct something else if you want—I just need to know you understand the concept.

As with master chefs, every alchemist must assemble the right components before crafting a special concoction. Are you so capable? We shall see.\n\nI require you to locate a solvent and some reagents. Then, you shall craft me a potion.
What do you think? It is a considered thing, to wear the wealth one seeks. Like a magnet for money, a wealth attractor.

Tranquil greetings, ceruval. You will forgive me if I seem awkward. We rarely entertain guests here on Artaeum. I am Celarus.\n\nRitemaster Iachesis told me a great deal about you. I suspect he has plans for you … within the Psijic Order.
You're back! Good. You should go talk to the Loremaster—he's expecting you! We can speak after, all right?
I think you'll enjoy this little jaunt into the marsh, truly! Just keep an eye out for crocodiles. Salamanders too. And also … well, just keep an eye out generally. Can't be too careful, right?

We must hurry. Even now, someone follows me, resisting my best efforts to identify them. \n\nWhile I deal with this threat, I need you to begin the process of locating the triangulants. Without them, the map is worthless.

The three stones act in concert, so be sure to place them in a broad pattern that encompasses the whole area.\n\nNow, you should set out. The sooner you place the descrying stones, the sooner I can locate the source of this evil.
At last! Something here that's worthy of Raz's attention. Let's get to the Fragrant Moons Plantation and see what we can dig up!
Find Kasura near the entrance to the training hall, just north of here. She has a grappling bow that you can train with.\n\nMeanwhile, I'll study the maps you found and make ready for our journey.
Were you able to secure a meeting with General Renmus?

Messages have been coming and going since I arrived. I've heard the name Rada al-Saran, the Ashen Lord, spoken in hushed and revered tones. His name was on the communique you found, remember?\n\nWe need to get down there and see what else we can learn.
That device they strapped me in … it was horrible.
When you talk to Fenn, go easy on him. He's been through a lot.

I want to discuss a few details with the jarl before he heads to Solitude.\n\nI'll meet you near Karthwatch, the major settlement in Karthald. There's an inn southeast of town. The Eversnow. Let's meet there.

The high king's finally doing something, but Svana doesn't think it's nearly enough. Can't say that I do, either.\n\nThe princess wants to discuss options. Talk to her and let's come up with a battle plan.
Jorunn didn't mention he was sending you to Solitude. Not that I'm sorry to have you along. An extra blade is always welcome.\n\nAs soon as Brondold shows up, we can get things started.
Gather the reagents for Mjolen quickly. Divination spells are more potent when the item in question carries the fresh scent of its owner.
This clan doesn't abandon its own. We fight to the end.

A pleasure to meet you in the flesh. As I said before, I am Narsis Dren. You are … whoever you are. Charmed. Now, to business! We need to find Maelmoth's Mysterium!\n\nFirst, we need his journal. A librarian refused to share it with me. Ridiculous.

It's been awhile, hasn't it? I almost didn't recognize you. Last time I saw you, we saved Rivenspire. The stakes are even higher now. And this time Verandis isn't here.\n\nI need your help, my friend. We need to find out more about the Gray Host.

Oh, I'm so relieved you agreed to help. Before you arrived I feared my overseers at House Telvanni really might—\n\nAhem. No matter. Tiras and I already set up a small field laboratory in the ruin, Veyond. Meet us inside and we'll get started!
Ready to make our way into hostile territory? We need to find this pit of the outsider, see if the vault is there, and reach the Ambitions before the Order of the Waking Flame beats us to them.

Guess I should introduce myself then. Unless you're some sort of vision guide. Then you probably know who I am … what was I saying?\n\nOh, right, I'm Adrahawn. Herbalist, arborist, all around friend of the Green.
Nothing but creaky floorboards and old weeds for me. I knew I should have brought my spectacles.\n\nWhat did you find?
If Annyce does return to Farmer's Nook, be careful confronting her. The last thing we want is for her to do something drastic and come to harm like those who came before her.

It worked! Sorry if that sounds too much like surprise, but I couldn't be sure that would be enough to save Eolaf's life until we tried it.\n\nIf the cult is doing this to the others, we should be able to free them too. If we're careful.

Thanks for the help. Not easy for Gemains to make friends around here.\n\nThe Dibellites use that manse in the center of town as their Dibellaseum—sort of a consecrated love-nest. If there's proof of Granna's innocence in Gideon, we'll find it there.

I'm half-ready to strangle Quistley for making me play his little game to get what should have been mine. But … it shows a bit of initiative on his part. Bargaining rather than demanding. \n\nMaybe he is trying to do better.

I know it probably seems like I'm being harsh, but mom's been at this more times than I can count. She promises to give up on it, but then she catches some whiff of a lead about that damn box and she's off like a race guar.
I've very little to lose anymore. The Ravener destroyed my clan. It took everything I knew.\n\nAtrozu reminds me of them. The times when we were all together.
We need to find the device that Sister Celdina mentioned. The one that creates the Incarnates.\n\nTalk to Lyranth and see if she has any ideas on where we should look for it.
Fargrave is the only home I've ever known. I'll do whatever is necessary to protect it. If you understand that, you'll understand me.
I'm sorry you had to endure that, but considering most Daedra's temperaments, Morah's caustic personality isn't so bad.\n\nI think we might be able to make some headway with her.
That old man … I know exactly how to bring down the barrier. \n\nHe's lifted the pillars and the symbols from a story he told me as a child.

Perhaps you are the very soul I've waited for all these years. Someone worthy enough to earn Lady Garick's most treasured possession.\n\nPlease pick up the censer and extinguish it. I suspect that should end the necromancer's binding.
I'm sure Dame Madach hasn't gotten far ….

It's not like I think Silverslip is going to kill us or anything, I'm just not … ready to talk with her. Not like this. I need to let everything sink in. She looks so different.\n\nPlease, talk to her. I'll get myself together in the meantime.
It wasn't until I met you that I really started thinking about friendships. About how much they give and take, about how they can change.\n\nThanks for helping me walk this path.
Oh, poor Lady Laurent! Whatever will I do?

In his letter, Dhulef mentioned he was headed to the Mines of Khuras in eastern Glenumbra. Let's move as quickly as wind between bare branches. We must reach him before the Firesong do. I refuse to lose another friend to them.

I intend to follow along behind you as you search. I'll scour the areas around the camps just to make sure we don't miss anything. \n\nDon't worry, I won't step on your toes. I'll meet you wherever you decide to stop first. Let's find Wyress Tola.

You look like someone who knows trouble. Adventurer by trade, am I right? I'm Dhulef of the Mages Guild. Spellslinger-for-hire and court mage to Count Mornard of Galen, at least for now.\n\nWe could use your help, and we've got the gold to pay for it.
Lady Arabelle is fortunate that Za'ji sent for me and not one of the Society of the Steadfast's menders. They wouldn't have been able to counteract the poison.
The forest sings a song of grief this day. A rain of tears and hurt. The Firesong have lost their way. How can I help them hear the song?

Why did Umindior have to leave me like this? He should have told me what he knew.\n\nIf you can track him down, that will make our job go faster. If he's dead, well, at least I didn't wait to look for the relic. Start where I marked your map.
We found the last notes of Druid Senna and a group of dead Eldertide, but my Gwenaelle is still among the missing. What do you think, outsider? What do your non-druid senses tell you?

Mortal? Your corpus, it sings like you are one of us. Yet, you are not. What are you? Perhaps the Great Eye sent a champion to aid us.\n\nOur fortress, the Cenotaph, now swarms with raiders. Vaermina's agents, the Dreamcarvers, come to take our gifts.
This place is beautiful and haunting, and I've seen it all. At least I think I have.

I'd like to learn more about this arch and statue the villager spoke of. But first, we should visit this Green Glass Inn. I would very much like to see a structure of that sort. And we might learn something about the cultists, too, I suppose.
Finally, a place to call home again. Thank you for helping me see the right decision.
Yet another creature approaches poor Hezehk. This time a mortal. Will you rob me as well? I have nothing. Less than nothing once Madam Whim adds to my debt.

I don't even want to be stuck with my bad memories. I wouldn't wish them on you.\n\nIt might not even work. But it's the only lead we have—the only one we've had in ages. And there's no one else I'd trust with this besides you.
Exceptional. I'll take a quick perusal, here. One of my favorite pastimes, really.\n\nReading an ancient tome to find an inscrutable answer while someone stares at me expectantly.

I'm looking forward to our collaboration! As I said, we'll need a book on Daedra summoning to get us on the right track. Let's convene in the center of Cipher's Midden. \n\nIs there anything I can clarify for you before we begin?
As we hoped. Something in this chamber harbors a memory or impression of the Forgotten Prince. Let us see what the Echonir has to show us.
Scruut's portal appears suitable. I shall meet you on the other side, proxy.

I hereby designate you a temporary agent of the West Weald Legion. Just until we find my soldiers. We'll search the manor house first. I'll meet you inside.\n\nKeep your eyes open, comrade. We don't know what happened here.
I've talked to some of the guests. Certainly many vampires, and wealthy ones at that. Let's keep questioning.
You heard the gardener, retrieve the herbs!
Hermeaus Mora opened a portal to the Mythos. We must hurry and reach his side. Who knows what damage Ithelia and Torvesard can cause at the core of Apocrypha.
We'll meet you at the monastery soon. Just give me a chance to catch up with Leramil. I've been worrying about her ever since Hermaeus Mora called her away.

I don't like what Rosalyn told us. Imagine, a vampire army.\n\nLet's head outside. Grivier's a good scout, but even the best leave a trail if you know what to look for. We follow Grivier and we find Tham—and maybe learn where Balandrus is hiding.
Leramil can use your help. She wants you to assist her in investigating the Outcast Inn.\n\nHelp her out, then check in again.

I see you got my message. Good. The Wood Elf was just telling me about a strange seed you found at Ostumir. If that can explain how that new forest grew up so quickly, we should look into that. \n\nTalk to Beragon and find out what else he knows.

I don't know if you can understand me. My mind is a storm of images and voices and memories. I can see every reality all at once—the Many Paths. But my grip on this realm keeps slipping.\n\nBut you, I see that you are real.
Damn! The Daedra have surrounded the keep and breached the fort's outer wall. The situation is worse than I thought.\n\nWe need to get in there and help them!
Shouldn't take me more than a moment to get this mixed. Add a touch of oil … and we're ready to go!

How little is left of the world I knew. My clan is … gone. Our bones and sanctuaries left to crumble to dust.\n\nI do not understand. Why was I sent here? I would rather have gone to the Sands Behind the Stars than be sent back to see this.
You're doing fine. Trust me!

That bowl was definitely set there by the Gardener. Not only is it his style, I saw one just like it on a table at a greenhouse in Reaper's March. Or was it Auridon? \n\nAnyway, I'm sure that's where we need to put the lavender to reveal the door.
Gods, look at this place! No sign of Hyacinth, but I think Snapdragon's magic set everything on fire. I think I'm going to be sick.
Let's find out what Snapdragon left us. Fingers crossed this gets us closer to figuring out Wisteria's plan.\n\nOr I guess, failing that, we're eating and drinking very well tonight.
High Cantor Viti speaks of us with venom and contempt. Just as she did when we saw her at Vile Manse. Perhaps it was foolish of me to expect better from her.\n\nLet us speak to Krin'ze.

Cantor Ta'khida. The first Twilight Cantor we saw fall to Ravith-morna in Claw's Strike. Moons, our journey has been a long one.\n\nHer spirit said that the creed of the Hidden Moon lives in me. Am I truly fit to embody this charge?
High Cantor Viti knew we were hiding? My stealthy maneuvers were so much sharper back in my time.\n\nSpeak to Viti, tamiit. I will remain vigilant in case this grand inquisitor returns.
Go, pal. Get down there and kick around those evil cultists. I'll work with Gabrielle to get us some more help. We have no idea how many of those necromantic bastards are down there.

Wimi is a fast and faithful mount. She can get you to the location quickly. I'll send word to the guild scout. They'll meet you and help you search for Merric. Then they can get word back to me while I follow up with the other reports.\n\nGood luck.
Hail, comrade!
I know you have what it takes to see this through, Hallowed. You always have before. Khali loved that about you. You're almost as brave as she was!
A friendly face, at last. I'm on a mission on behalf of the Queen herself. Will you lend me aid?
You're brilliant, Hallowed. You have the smarts to see this through. You always have before. Shazah loved that about you. You're almost as wise as she was!
I wasn't prepared for such an ordeal. Without your help, I … I don't know if I would have survived. Thank you, Vestige, for all you have done.
Speak with the Prophet. I need to catch my breath. It's been a long day.
I wasn't sure Sai would be able to keep his feet under him through all that. It seems the old fool is tougher than I suspected.
You haven't left. Would you leave the task of closing that Oblivion Gate to others? As the Dagon cultists would say—embrace the new day. Fight their lord. Ruin his machinations.
The trick is the style material … but I'm sure you know that.
Mastery of three crafts is its own reward.

Tranquil greetings, my friend. You seem duly prepared for the task ahead. Excellent. Foresight and prudence provide a stronger defense than any shield.\n\nMay the Old Ways guide your path. And again, thank you.
Greetings and welcome, friend. I'm glad you've come! Seeing a new face is a refreshing change of pace.
So, you found our fellow travelers? Excellent! I think we're almost ready to depart.\n\nThere is one thing I need your help with before we begin our adventure in earnest, though.

I see my summons reached you. Good, good.\n\nYou may wonder who I am and why I sent for you. Don't. Just trust me. I have only the best interests of the Empire in mind. But we must leave now if we're going to take advantage of the situation.
Forgive me. I didn't expect to face such resistance.

Five-claw? Raz thought he recognized you! Moons only know what brings you to this backwater place, but it is always good to see a friend. \n\nRaz would offer you wine, but he's unfortunately drank it all. Perhaps you have some?
It's good to see you again, Vestige. By the look on your face, I suspect you never expected to encounter your friend Sai Sahan again.

Leki be willing, all will go well and our meeting with General Renmus will commence without issue.\n\nMeet me at the palace when you're done. Meanwhile, I'll learn all I can about our upcoming Dragon hunt.

I came here to learn what the Gray Host has planned and what did I find? Good citizens of the holds, afflicted by the harrowstorms and kept prisoner for some ungodly purpose.\n\nNo matter how many I set free, the harrowed will not leave this place.
You risked so much to save me. Why would you do such a thing?
Fenn's fighting a battle with himself right now, but he'll be ready when we need him.\n\nIn the meantime, the princess wants to talk to you.

With you and Lyris's help, we've gained the trust of Jarl Reddharn. My father respects the jarl. That will go a long way in convincing the high king to take the coven's threat seriously.\n\nNow we need to do the same thing at Karthald.
Let's go to the Blue Palace and find out what the princess is planning.
You have a habit of turning up wherever the Icereach Coven appears. On another witch hunt?\n\nWe should catch up later. I've got urgent business to take care of, as soon as my contact arrives.

Old Mjolen isn't an expert on vampire clans. She is, however, a diviner. \n\nThe clever woman can learn the most interesting things studying melting snowflakes and mammoth teeth. Talk to her and see what she can tell you about that medallion.

Well, look who it is. And just when I thought I was going to have to investigate the Gray Host all by my lonesome.\n\nThe Ravenwatch said it was sending someone to assist me. I'm glad it turned out to be you.

Well, here's a turn of luck! It's me! Revus! You helped me out of a scrape in Gnisis some time back. Remember? Kwama mine, tonal resonator … devoured bard. Good times.\n\nAnyway, here we are again. You, me, and an experiment going poorly.

I knew Governor Keshu would be helpful. I'll meet you at the edge of Sul-Xan territory. Then we can find this pit of the outsider together.\n\nThat name sends shivers up my spine. I suppose that's fitting for a place full of Daedric weapons.

Oh, hello there. You know if this is the Silent Halls? A willow said I could find it out this way, but trees aren't great with directions, what with staying in one place their whole lives and what not.

Not exactly the luxurious love nest I was expecting. I suppose a couple hundred years of neglect will do that to a house. \n\nLet's look around before we try to summon Mathen. Always pays to prepare before an interview! That's what I've heard, anyway.
I believe Annyce came here and performed some sort of ritual, and not the sort conjured from an overactive imagination. Whoever she followed here convinced her to make an offering to this place.
Eolaf … that's what I was afraid would happen. The strain of snapping that connection to his soul was too much to take.\n\nIf we aren't more careful, the others will meet the same fate.
Ugh. Look, I've got just as much right to stand here as anyone else. If those scantily-clad Dibellites want me to leave, you tell them to come out here and say it to my face!

Quistley actually looks sober. And worried. Whatever trouble he's in, he's taking it seriously for once. Hmm.\n\nWhy don't you speak to him? You're a neutral party. He won't be as defensive or, well, weasel-ish with you.
Let's just get out of this dump. We can talk outside.

Sister Celdina … twice now you helped me stop her from harming Fargrave and its people. Thanks for that.\n\nI'm not sure why Lyranth chose us, or what she really cares about in all this, but as long as the cult threatens my city, I'll stand by you.
Unbelievable. I spent hours trying to get her attention, trying to figure out how to communicate with her, and she was ignoring me. The nerve!
Just brute forcing the barrier is not the way to go. Let's see if the pillars hold any clues.

I have honorably guarded Lady Garick's trials for more lifetimes than I can recall. And this necromancer thinks she can cow me? I'll have none of it!\n\nApologies. Thank you for stopping. Would you kindly douse that censer and unbind me?
Dame Madach is incredible, isn't she? I'm so glad she's in fighting form.

That's Silverslip for you. Quick and to the point. \n\nI'm glad to see her alive. Er, sort of alive, that is. I knew this was a possibility but still … seeing her now and remembering that girl she was? It stings. Let's go meet her outside.
I'm trying to focus on the fact that we found Aurelia safe. That's the important thing, here.
Ah, you got my letter? Thanks for meeting me. My good friend, Dhulef of the Mages Guild, is in danger. I can't protect him from the Firesong on my own.

Lass looks pretty shaken up. But why would the Firesong attack a band of peaceful wyresses? Did they follow me? Did I lead them here without realizing it?\n\nGo ahead and talk with Wyress Joslin. Ask her where the elder wyress is.
Stefan's idea is a good one. Archdruid Rahval is in the Vine District. Just head east once you leave the castle.\n\nGood luck and clear seas to you.
I came as quickly as I could when I received Za'ji's message. I've done what I can, but ….\n\nYou should talk to Lady Arabelle. She won't rest until she explains what happened.

You and I working together solves a lot of problems for me. If we find Umindior—great. He can tell us what he knows about the relic. If not, then we've spent that time looking on our own. Efficient.\n\nSo, we should split up!
Dead. All dead. My friends and family. Only my Gwenaelle remains unaccounted for.\n\nLet's keep looking. She has to be here somewhere.

Outworlder. You come upon us exactly when needed. Perhaps the Great Eye still watches.\n\nInvaders swarm our fortress, the Cenotaph. Dreamcarvers devoted to Vaermina come to wrest the gifts we have guarded for countless millennia.
A mortal, damaged by a glimpse of the meaninglessness of the infinite. You should speak with them. I don't want to get any of that on my tentacles.
I feel better having a path forward so both Nathyn and I can be free.\n\nWe'll find a cure soon, I just know it!
Madam Whim sends me on so many tasks all over Oblivion. I never want to do them, but I don't want the trouble from not paying my debt.
Not thinking about the memories. Just thinking about when we get to destroy that stuff you're carrying.
Keep your eyes open, cohort. We'll find that tome.\n\nAh, and if you see a book with a stitched-up cover on a special dais, don't go browsing. I went blind for a month the last time I was here.

Greetings! You have a sharp look to you, traveler. My name is Azandar, I'm an arcanist, and I'm hoping we can help each other out.\n\nI've decades of esoteric knowledge, a bit of coin, and a convivial attitude! What do you say?
It seems we are expected. I was wondering when and how the One Who Knows intended to speed our journey. Speak with the abbot, proxy.
I, too, am at a loss as to what possible use the depleted relics may serve. Still, if the One Who Knows suggests you shall have need of them, then we should take them with us.

The hero of Feldagard! Great timing. Seems you have a knack for showing up when I need assistance.\n\nLook around. No people. Strange, right? I detached an entire Legion cohort to guard this estate, but no one's here. Where could they all be?

I can sometimes discern the alchemical properties of a compound by tasting it. Not the most advisable tactic, but when no other alternative presents itself ….\n\nI find myself straining against the temptation to consume this entire glass.
Nothing more can be done for our imposter. Tend to Betu, Mizzik refuses to lose another life under this one's watch.
The Whispered Path. I have come across vague references to such a place in my studies, but I never imagined I would walk its secret corridors. Let us see where it leads.

I finally resolved to see the world beyond Necrom … with some assistance from Leramil, of course. Then Hermaeus Mora called her away again. I'm glad to see you're still helping her, friend.\n\nDid I hear correctly? Torvesard has returned?
You talk to her while I keep watch. I got along with Tham and a few other townsfolk, but most were wary once they figured out what I was back then.

Tribune Alea and Leramil can use your help. The tribune is worried about an attack at Feldagard Keep. And Leramil thinks it's important to investigate the Outcast Inn.\n\nSee what you can do to help them, then come back here.

The Wood Elf mentioned a strange seed the two of you found at Ostumir. If that can explain how that new forest grew up so quickly, we should look into that. \n\nTalk to Beragon and see if he knows anyone who might be able to tell us more.
I don't understand what's happening. All of it. Occurring simultaneously. It won't stop.

We need to take stock of the situation before we head inside. Stumbling into a fight blindly never ends well.\n\nThere's an overlook east of the keep. Locals usually run a small market there. We can get a good view of the keep from that location.

There's a big rock just west of Skywatch, near the road. I'll set up a little alchemy station there. We can use it to combine the lilies and silver dust, whip up some resonating fluid, and find my friends!\n\nHey! I can feel my toes again!
This is it, the entrance to the sanctuary is here. I am both eager and fearful to see what we will find inside. Let us go in, yes?
I don't want to say anything about the Netch! It could be in here. Floating. Listening to us. Right now!

Royal lavender is a flower. What can I say? The Gardener loves his flowers! We can find some growing near the Ritual Mundus Stone. It's the purple one, right?\n\nJust teasing! I know my flowers. The Garland Ring makes us take a test and everything!
Let's look around. They have to be here somewhere!
That's Lahathril, the clerk that wrote to me. I'll keep an eye out for any Ceythalmor on the off chance this is a trap.\n\nHeh. If things go sideways, grab as much gold as you can and run.
Our missing cantor wrote of dark dreams and a darker melody. Ravith-morna. At least he is not here. Hope remains until it does not.\n\nLet us return to Krin'ze while I ponder Izalgo's words.
There is more to Khenarthi's Rise that we have not seen, tamiit. Let us keep exploring and see what we can do to bring order to these ruins.
Quickly, tamiit. We need to find a place to hide.

Gabrielle Benele is one of the few mages I actually like. She's much less arrogant than her boss, Vanus Galerion. Lucky for us she's here and not him.\n\nTell her what we learned and that we'll help in any way we can.

I've received conflicting reports from trusted guild scouts. Merric has supposedly been sighted in Malabal Tor, northern Alik'r Desert, and Eastmarch.\n\nObviously, he can't be everywhere. Choose a location to investigate and meet the scout there.
Hallowed! Bright moons, it's good to see you. I've been conferring with this Mage from the Guild, working on a way to solve our portal problem.
Hallowed! Bright moons, it's good to see you. This mage here has an idea of how to deal with these portal-gate … Daedra things.

The Amulet of Kings is in our possession and the traitor Mannimarco has been defeated. But we are not yet finished. The blessings of Akatosh must be restored if Nirn is to remain safe. \n\nBut tonight, we rest.
I can't believe there's still more to do. But whatever the future holds, come Oblivion or high water, the Five Companions will face it together.

I know what you're thinking, Vestige. You want to thank me for my noble and heroic effort in helping you defeat that treacherous worm, Mannimarco. No need to laud me, though. The world already knows of my brilliance. But you're welcome nonetheless.
Craft an iron dagger. You'll need some iron ingots and a style material. You can buy those from any blacksmith if you can't find them yourself.

You show promise in every discipline I certify. Perhaps you seek to challenge my position as thrice-accredited master craftsman.\n\nIf so, <<1>> offers blacksmith, clothier, and woodworking certification. I last saw her at the local Fighters Guild.
Old Ways protect you, initiate. Hopefully we'll have something for you when you return.

You've made a great choice in joining us, friend!\n\nThe other members of our expedition have already gathered near the western gate. I'll be along shortly—just need to check on a few things. This is exciting, right?

Ah, Vestige, how good of you to attend me. Information has come to my attention that could significantly change the future of Tamriel and the Empire. If we're going to take advantage of the situation, we need to leave immediately.
I'm glad to have your company. As I said, something about this place puts me ill at ease.\n\nNow, are you ready to proceed?
Hmm. You do not look like a robber, so Raz would appreciate it if you kept your voice down. I need a moment to clear my head.\n\nSay, why have you barged into Raz's den unannounced?
It's good to see you again, Vestige. Ready to once again answer Tamriel's latest cry for help?

Now, meeting with an Imperial general is faster said than done. The paperwork alone would take days to file, and the Dragon we seek could attack the city at any moment.\n\nSo I found an … alternative method.
We just arrived ourselves. I introduced Fenn to Svana, but I haven't had a chance to give her our report. Why don't you do it, partner?
There's an order to these things, my friend. Give your news to the jarl first. We're in his hall, after all.
Glad to see you're alive and well. I was getting worried with all the harrowed they've been bringing into the city.

Vestige? You're a sight for sore eyes. It feels like it's been ages since … well, you know.\n\nI'd invite you for a drink, but I'm about to present myself to royalty. Just as soon as my contact arrives.
Welcome to the middle of nowhere, my friend. You must be freezing. Warm yourself by the fire and tell me how your audience with the high king went.
You here about the contract? Investigating the Gray Host is like trying to wrestle an angry spirit! Anyway, the Ravenwatch could certainly use the help.\n\nAnd by the Ravenwatch, I mean me.

Ah, praise Vivec! You're here about the notices I posted, yes? Even if you're not, you're welcome all the same.\n\nMy student and I need help with an experiment, and the situation is rather desperate. Well, really desperate. Really, truly, desperate.
Good to see you! I just finished telling the governor what happened in Leyawiin. Why don't you ask her about the Argonian phrase we need translated?
Let's make our way to the cottage. If the lantern worked once, it will work again, right?

This is rather quaint for an Ayleid ruin. Almost cozy. I'd half be tempted to settle in with a book and a cup of tea for some leisure reading if it weren't sitting in a moldering swamp.\n\nMost of these books should have rotted away long ago ….

We need to stop that ritual, the sooner the better, but Eolaf's chances of surviving go up exponentially if we try picking it apart carefully instead of smashing the central array right at the start.\n\nThe grapple bow should help us search around.
He'll be in the Rosy Lion. It's his home away from home.
Just … talk to her. The last thing we need is her making a scene right now.\n\nThis is why I never bring friends home.

How do we even start to figure out where to look for Sister Celdina and her Riven Cataclyst? The Deadlands is huge. And they could be anywhere! And what does the Bladebearers clan symbol we found have to do with anything?\n\nMaybe Lyranth has an idea.

The only lead I have is one of Rrvenk's disciples, Morah, in Windswept Crag. I've been trying to communicate with her for hours, but I get no response. If you speak on my behalf we may finally get somewhere.
Oh dear, Snegh and Brelannal got here first.
I remained in Garick's Rest far beyond the expectations of Lady Garick. But she gave orders and following them was my duty.\n\nI pray she knows of my loyalty wherever she may be.

There might be a clue in Silverslip's journal. Maybe she wrote about where she went last!\n\nYou flip through and read it. I'll keep an eye out and make sure no one comes and sinks their teeth into us.
Stendarr help me, she's an adventurer now. You'd better talk to her, my friend.

My friend! You're a welcome sight. You remember Dhulef of the Mages Guild? That old barnacle is pursuing a lead for me and apparently ran into some Firesong. I need to go help him, but I can't take on the Firesong by myself.

The camp is just to the west of the Beldama Wyrd Tree. I'll stay with Druid Laurel and make sure she gets there safely.\n\nLet's hope the wyress has remembered something. Or can at least tell us more about the carvings on this tablet.

That someone was so craven and cowardly as to poison the good Lady Arabelle ….\n\nGo on, my friend. Find out who the culprit is while I return to my workshop and prepare something to counteract the poison.

Partner! What a relief to see you. Much better than another strange Sea Elf trying to woo me.\n\nDid Zeira send you? She paired me with someone new, Umindior, but he's gone missing. I started to worry I'd have to do this job on my own.
Druid Senna, the animals tore her life away. Still, her account mentions the motes settling quickly—that's highly unusual.\n\nWe should keep looking. I worry my Gwenaelle might suffer a similar fate.
We did not choose our fortress. It arrived when we needed it most. Once, sounds of training and discussion echoed through the halls. As our numbers dwindled, the Cenotaph fell quiet.

I'd prefer to sit back and wait for entropy to claim us all, but I suppose we must do something. Let's survey the town. See if anyone survived and try to determine what the cultists want here.\n\nOh, and despite my size I'm good in a fight. You'll see.
Love makes one willing to consider the most impossible things.
Quires Wind is deep within Apocrypha, the far eastern side of the region.\n\nWe'll need to be wary. As with so many cases in Mora's realm, the books are just as dangerous as its denizens.
There is nothing quite like the smell of Apocrypha. Knowledge, fear, books and … cinnamon, perhaps? Delectable.
I did not expect Gadayn to give us the answer we seek. But I was confident he would know whom we should ask. And, well, I wanted to check on him.\n\nWe will meet you at the monastery.
You must hear what Scruut has to say, proxy. We do not yet know if this latest doom is tied to Ithelia and Torvesard, but I suspect the chances of that are very good.

Look around. No people. Strange, right? I detached an entire Legion cohort to guard this estate, but I haven't found a single legionary. Not even a servant.\n\nWhat's your story? Do you know what happened to my legionaries?
So, do I look like a Master Bogvir? Probably not, but we work with the tools we're given.\n\nLet's split up and mingle. Talk to servants, guests, whoever's willing to chat.
Quickly, we must look for clues. Whoever did this couldn't have gotten far and any lead will help us track them down.
Keep going, proxy. The path presented by the Skein is clear enough to follow.
I'm barely a junior monk from Necrom. Surely there must have been someone more qualified than me to deal with feuds between Daedric Princes and the threat they pose to reality!
Let's open the door nice and slow. Would hate to startle the survivors into doing something foolish.

Tribune Alea's legionary found you? Good!\n\nThe map we found at Hoperoot contains a valuable clue—I just need some time to decipher the code. But one thing is already clear. King Nantharion and his allies aren't done with West Weald yet.
Whoever's behind these attacks on West Weald—Daedra, Wood Elf, or Recollection fanatic—I mean to make them answer for what they've done. This land is my home, and I'll fight to protect it.
I know something is wrong, but I do not have the words to express what that may be.

Good, you came. After we finished at Hoperoot, I raced to Feldagard Keep to warn them about the report we found. But as you can hear, the battle already rages on. If only we found that Recollection report earlier.

Why would they go to Toothmaul Gully without me? And leave behind their scarf and charm?\n\nRemember I said we like to cause trouble for ne're-do-wells high up in Summerset society? There's this group we've been tracking. We think they're dangerous.

Look to the southeast side of the temple's base. An entrance to the Hidden Moon sanctuary should be there.\n\nTo think, even the Temple of Two-Moons-Dance could be left in such disrepair! My fur falls out just looking at it.
Ah, the Dragon! We can all learn something from her. Some of us more than others.\n\nMe, for instance. I have a lot to learn. Please don't ask me to solve any of her riddles for you.

I much prefer illusory birds to rings of mushrooms. That rhyme was terrible, though. \n\nLet's consider the clue. An egress revealed by royal lavender? Sounds like a hidden door to me! That must be the entrance to the new greenhouse!

The old meeting site is near the Bone Orchard. I can't remember the last time I was there, but I'll know it when I see it.\n\nI'm so glad you're here. I'm beside myself. Is this happening again? Is the Ceythalmor going after my friends?

I'm trying not to get my hopes up. But Snapdragon is—was—meticulous. If anyone could have uncovered Wisteria's plan, it's her.\n\nLet's head to Marbruk. We need to ask for a clerk named Lahathril. Hopefully, this will get us back on track.
If only these Inquisitors were as helpful in life as they are in death.\n\nBehind the stables, he said. Quickly, tamiit. Before Cantor Izalgo bends to the shadow with the other Rajaska.

Talbira appears and requests we restore this place to find our path. I failed her before. I will not fail her again.\n\nDoes she seek to humble me? This place serves as yet another reminder of the mistakes I have made.

So the Inquisitors seek Viti. They followed her here, just as they chased after Cantor Izalgo in Goldfolly.\n\nLet us proceed to the meeting spot, tamiit. But be wary. The meaning of that message does not make our danger any less real.

If you need quick transport to Shornhelm's Mages Guild, take Wimi. I'm sure Prince Azah won't mind. And even if he did, he's not here to stop you.\n\nI'll send word to the little prince and meet you there. It's about time I punched something.

Friend! Your timely arrival gives me hope that the sands of disaster can finally be turned.\n\nThe Fighters Guild is under assault. Four guildhalls have already fallen and now Guildmaster Merric has disappeared. We need to find him before all is lost.
This is it, Hallowed. We stand on the threshold of our final challenge. The end of the Path.
This is it, Hallowed. We stand on the threshold of our final challenge. The end of the Path.
Hey there, scrub. You'd best stay back. We are speaking of blood and glory. For we are Undaunted!
Refining ore into ingots is a good way to build your muscles. Well, in one arm.\n\nBest to switch every now and then. Otherwise, you'll be lopsided.
Your command of the crafts is impressive, but not yet in totality. I am still capable of instructing you.
Today's pledge is not for you. Come back tomorrow.

Hello there! Always a pleasure to see a new face.\n\nWelcome to Lilmoth, the festering jewel of Black Marsh. Argonian words, not mine. Doesn't strike me as all that fester-y. But I digress! How would you like to join an exciting expedition?

A fellow wanderer on the path. Greetings. I'm Vastarie.\n\nIf you plan to explore the Ashen Scar, I'd advise caution. Some dark intention has this canyon in a vise-grip. An inopportune time for a visit, hmm? Then again, perhaps we're meant to be here.
Greetings, warrior. I am Sai Sahan, former captain of the Imperial Dragonguard.

The time has come at last, my friend. We now have the means to fight back against this Dragon invasion and save Elsweyr from certain destruction. This is where we start, in the city of Senchal.\n\nIf you still wish to join me, that is.

I knew the jarl would be reasonable. And it was good to hear my father has finally taken action. If he sent orders about the witch pikes, he at least heard some of what I said.\n\nGo check on the barrow. I need to tell the jarl about my mother.
Karthald? Well, I can't be in two places at once, so you need to keep the princess safe.\n\nIf you run into any trouble, send word to Solitude and I'll meet you as fast as I can.
I'm accustomed to stares, but I reached my threshold for gawkers a long time ago. Move along, I'm waiting for someone.
We'll meet up in Gideon. We can talk to Governor Keshu there. She has to know about this ojel-bak thing. She has to!

It worked! I told you it would work!\n\nTall Papa's breeches, what a tale. A ghostly duchess! Lusty, young nobles! Betrayal and murder! This story's got it all! Phew. Is it getting hot out here or is it just me?
I don't know who Annyce met out here, but the clues suggest that she wasn't in danger. Yet. We shouldn't dawdle.

That's Eolaf! One of the other adventurers Xigira duped with this setup. They've got him strung up like a New Life pony guar. Survey stones, my ashy arse. That's a sacrifice if I've ever seen one! We've got to do something.
Here—you can read the letter for yourself, if you're curious. I wonder what sort of mess Quistley's managed to get himself into this time?
I don't know what I expected. Whatever it was, it didn't include my mother making a fetching cake.
I've met Sister Celdina twice now, and both times I had to help stop her efforts to destroy Fargrave. But that Incarnate creature … if she can create an army of those things, what chance do we have?
Gods, it's good to see a fellow Psijic! You can see me, right? What about hear me?
Right. If I remember correctly, I think he lives in a little grotto to the south, near the coast. He likes his privacy, our oaken elder.
This place makes my fur stand on end.\n\nLet's just look for any signs of Silverslip and then get out. I don't want to linger here.
Untie her, quick. I'll keep watch for more pirates.

My friend! What a relief. Are you familiar with these lands? Blight, even if you're not, I could use your help. My friend, Dhulef of the Mages Guild, is in danger. I can't protect him from the Firesong on my own.

Good to see you again, sailor! When I sent Laurel that letter, I never expected you to be the capable help she'd hire. Ha! \n\nYou're just in time, too. I managed to give the craven Firesong the slip long enough to find this.

Are you here to woo me as well? Oh, not that I'd mind! No, wait, I mean … ugh.\n\nCan I start over? That Sea Elf keeps bothering me. Then my partner, Umindior, vanished. It's left me a bit unbalanced. I might need to do this job without him.
The spirit motes …. I'm glad I blessed us against their effects. I have no idea what such concentrations would do to our minds.
Farewell. I—wait. My master. Hermaeus Mora wants to speak with you, mortal. He will use me as his vessel ….
Let's not waste more time. Just go in and grab that metal, assuming Dimik-ei's hunch is right. \n\nHope there's not some mad cultists doing bizarre rituals.

Cohort, I need a word. In truth? Probably several hundred. You have my assurance each will be selected for maximum expository and rhetorical effect.\n\nMy research has progressed as far as I am able. It is time we concluded the Fateweaver experiment.

I hoped Gadayn would still be here. I am sure he can illuminate the obscure religious traditions of his people, or at least tell us where answers may be found.\n\nTell him what we have learned so far.

It seems we go from one doom to another, proxy. But Ithelia and Torvesard are out there somewhere. I suspect they are the source of Scruut's agitation. \n\nSpeak to the Watchling and find out what doom she wants us to deal with this time.
Colovians have grown familiar with conflict. These last few years hardened us. We'll deal with whatever trouble comes our way.
The invitation indicates we're to head to the walled garden just east of the manor. I suppose that's where they're letting the guests gather prior to the start of the auction.\n\nShall we proceed?
There's no time to waste, we must find the source of that scream!
Follow the path the Skein has set before us. While it cannot pinpoint Ithelia's exact location, we know it can lead us to places where her power has recently been active.
No lockpicks? First rule for outlaws and adventurers—always come prepared.

The map we found at Hoperoot contains a valuable clue—I just know it. Give me some time and I'll decipher the code and figure it out.\n\nOne thing is already clear. King Nantharion and his allies aren't done with West Weald yet.

What good fortune that you're here, comrade. That report we found in Hoperoot was a reconnaissance of Feldagard Keep. That could only mean an attack was imminent. I raced to warn them, but I arrived too late from the sound of it.

This note you found mentions the ice trap, and Wisteria and Oleander aren't here. Something is definitely wrong.\n\nMembers of the Ring are always ready for trouble, but …. What if our rivals got the better of them?

I recognize the bones. But the rest? Hahl fajh'na! My ancestors did not defy the Striped Death just to let this holy ground be stamped down to simple tents and stalls.\n\nI must be very far from my own time if this is what Rawl'kha is reduced to.
You did it! The … thing everyone wanted you to do. I forget.\n\nAnyway, I'm happy to call you my friend!
The Gardener loves his illusions! I wonder what this one does? You don't think it explodes, do you?\n\nNo, that would be silly. Still, why don't you examine it and see what happens.
Damn and blast and arse!\n\nThis is not good. In Snapdragon's letter she says Hyacinth asked her to meet him alone at Bone Tree. But why would he do that if he sent us here to rendezvous with her?
Var. I sense dro-m'Athra nearby. Maaz'koh ska'ell, tamiit. Be on your guard.
Krin'ze does not respond to my voice. And High Cantor Viti, why is she not here beside her? I do not like this, tamiit.\n\nSee if you can get through to Krin'ze while I stand guard.

There is something on my mind, tamiit. Krin'ze remains in sympathy to our cause, and for that I am thankful.\n\nBut only now do I see that course might divide her from her order. Our influence may be isolating her.
I think I demonstrated a lot of restraint, waiting out here and not going inside for an ale or two.\n\nAny luck finding Magister Andrelo?

Comrade, the Fighters Guild is under assault. As a member, you deserve to know that four guildhalls have already fallen. And now Guildmaster Merric has disappeared. \n\nAs much as it pains me to admit, I need assistance to track him down.
I'm frightened, but I won't let fear hold me back.
I'm not afraid. I'm ready for this.
I can see you are not Undaunted. Don't waste your limited time on Nirn standing where you're not wanted.
Bring some iron ore to a blacksmithing station. You can refine it there to get iron ingots.
Your command of the craft is impressive, but not yet in totality. I am still capable of instructing you.
It is good to shop now, you see, for it is nearly time for this one to leave and sleep upon her gold for a time.
Come back when you've got some scars worth admiring.
Azura is with us, my friend.
The Dragons are a pox upon the land. A giant, death-dealing, fire-breathing pox.

It's good to see you again, Vestige. And good to be alive, I must admit.\n\nI'm sure you have questions, but first a more urgent matter. Dragons ravage Elsweyr and I need your help against these vile beasts.
Well, that didn't go too badly. Tell the jarl what we're facing. Hopefully, he's willing to listen.
Don't worry about Jarl Reddharn. I'll make sure he gets to Solitude safely.

I'm glad you made it. The information left behind by the former councilors pointed to an Argonian location. Someplace called the ojel-bak.\n\nWe need to determine what that means and where it's located before Vandacia and his cultists beat us to it!
What are you talking to me for? Talk to the ghost! Who knows how long she'll linger?
I believe I have thrust to the heart of the matter. Hear me out.
There should be a basecamp just ahead. Where we setup before splitting off to explore the ruin.\n\nI imagine the cult's using it now, but we should search it regardless.
A messenger just brought me this letter. It's from my foster brother Quistley, of all people. I wasn't even sure he could write legibly.\n\nAnd I have to say I'm not sure what to make of it.
I swear, if these s'wits have done anything to my mother I'll—well, you'll fetching see.
Are you really here? In the Deadlands, or am I merely perceiving you from Summerset? Can you hear me?
Ugh. I thought I heard Snegh yelling in the distance. He's another aspirant, and a complete donkey's arse. \n\nNever mind him, we're on a quest!

I can't believe those monsters handed Silverslip off to vampires. There are too many scenarios to count now … none of them good.\n\nLet's go. I intend to scour every inch of the Shrine of the Black Maw if that's what it takes to find her.
We have to find her. Let's move!

You there, are you familiar with these lands? Blight, even if you're not, you look capable. I need assistance. My good friend, Dhulef of the Mages Guild, is in danger. I can't protect him from the Firesong on my own.

Ha, I asked Laurel to find capable help, and it looks like she delivered! Exquisite. The name's Dhulef, of the Mages Guild. I managed to give those craven Firesongs the slip earlier, but I'm sure glad to have you with us now. Look what I found.

I wanted a simple job. Get in, get out. This one sounded easy enough. But one important detail escaped my notice—it's on an island.\n\nI almost got sick three times on the boat ride here. The deck hands forced me to keep a bucket handy.

The entrance to the path is just over there. I'll meet you on the steps down into the sacred valley. There we can find out what happened to my Gwenaelle.\n\nBut first, let me bless you against the dangers within.

Mortals. You scurry around obsessed with your petty affairs and then you die. But you bear the mark of Hermaeus Mora. Have you come to replace me in my task? That would be typical.\n\nWait. Were you sent to help me with the cultists? Before you die?

I'm just going to say what's on my mind because it's been eating at me the whole trip over.\n\nI read through Reynila's notes. If we do this, and you're my conduit, you're going to experience my past memories with me. My whole lifetime.
I will throw myself into this research with the full force of my faculties. You'll be the first I tell when the fruit of knowledge blooms.

Gadayn and I were visiting ancient sites in Vvardenfell when the One Who Knows summoned me to our current task. I think I know where to find him.\n\nThrough the portal, please. Time is of the essence.

The One Who Knows was wise to put his faith in you. With the Loom destroyed, Ithelia's plan to rewrite history has been thwarted. Enjoy this moment, proxy. The threads of fate rarely weave such a victory.

Just as Count Verandis taught me, there is always something to learn if you simply pay attention.\n\nThe field hand was attacked by a death hound, a sure indication of vampiric activity. And he provided a wealth of information, don't you agree?

This note seems to confirm that Pelena Weatherleah had her husband killed while he was away from the estate. Did Lady Weatherleah read it first and confront Pelena with the truth? And what is Pelena left to do when cornered?
Can you not sense it, proxy? A foreign power is loose in Hermaeus Mora's realm. Ithelia is here, somewhere.\n\nUse the Skein of Secrets and let us see if it can provide us with a trail to follow.

Either the Terror and his gang haven't checked here yet, or they haven't been able to breach the vault. That doesn't mean they won't be back though, so let's be quick.\n\nHelnzin the clerk kept a spare key to the vault in a box by her desk.

We dealt the Recollection a hard blow when we stopped Nantharion's ritual and destroyed their fortress. And we won another victory at Hoperoot nearly as important. One that may end the distrust between Skingrad and Vashabar.

Ah, my comrade from Rustwall! What luck. I need your help once again. Do you hear the sounds of combat? The fight for Feldagard Keep already rages.\n\nWhen I learned of an impending attack, I raced to warn them, but I arrived too late.
I was hoping that ice trap at Vulkhel Guard would be the worst of it. Just something to delay me, but now ….\n\nLet's look around. Maybe Wisteria and Oleander left us a clue.
I will meet you in Rawl'kha. Gazing upon Boethra's stone colossus again will bring me some comfort in wake of this troubled news. I hope.
I can't wait until the rest of the wings are open again! I'll have so much more space to run.\n\nNot that I couldn't get into the other wings before. It's just much easier when doors are unlocked.

Hmm. A riddle and a sketch. So far these clues all point to spots in Malabal Tor. I wonder if that means the new greenhouse is around here somewhere.\n\nAnyway, let's find that arch and see what the Gardener left for us this time.
I think you did it! I can see letters appearing on the paper. Read what it says already! The suspense is killing me.
Speak to the spirit quickly. I hold it in cupped claws. If he decides to depart, I will not stop him.
Of everything I expected to find here, Cantor Krin'ze was not among them. But if something drew both of us to this place ….\n\nWe must find her and learn why we were guided here.

Once again, you prove yourself a blessing from Azurah, tamiit.\n\nYou take the lead on questioning the Pa'alat townsfolk. Even after all our travels together, I am still learning how to talk to people of this age.

I never expected the enemy to be the Worm Cult. Thought they were finished after we stopped the Planemeld.\n\nObviously Merric has a plan to crush them. Let's get to Windhelm and the Cold Moon Inn and see what this magister can tell us.

Honor and faith, traveler. I could use your assistance. The Fighters Guild is under assault. Already, four guildhalls have fallen. And now, Master Merric, leader of the guild, has disappeared.\n\nIt pains me to admit it, but I need help.
Find Esan. I'll try to muster some troops to support you in the district. This one trusts you to get the job done.
You're back! I take it you found enough ore?
There is much more I can teach you. What else do you hope to learn from me?
You! You are among the very first to view my goods this sale, be proud! And be certain to spend literally all of your money!
I think I'll stay here a while. The adepts of the Hidden Moon still have a great deal to teach us, it seems.\n\nNever forget what we accomplished here. I surely won't. Azura guide you, friend.

It's good to see you again, Vestige.\n\nI know how much you've already done for Tamriel, but I must request your aid once more. Dragons ravage Elsweyr. I need your help to fight back against these vile beasts.

We should visit Jarl Reddharn of Hjaalmarch first. If we can convince him of the threat, at least his hold can take steps to protect itself. We'll find him in his hall in Morthal.\n\nI'll leave word for Lyris with Maugh so she'll know where to find us.
Good to see Svana and the jarl getting along. Give him the news about the barrow and maybe we'll finally gain some ground with these western Nords.

So, the information from the former councilors points to an Argonian location. Someplace called the ojel-bak.\n\nVandacia ran off with the documents before we could learn more. Now we need to figure out what it means before his cultists beat us to it!
The lantern works! This is so exciting!

A little island of wonder in an ocean of hum and drum. Marvelous.\n\nThe House of Reveries has some of the best set builders in the world, but there's a life to this you won't find on any stage. Let's see what captivates Annyce about this place.

This place has shifted, just a bit, but it's changing. Still, this is definitely where I crossed to escape. \n\nLet's just take this one obstacle at a time. That support will hold your weight, I promise. We can survey better from the other side.
I've never been to the Inner Sea Armature, but it must not be too far from Edvilda's camp.\n\nThree, I hope mom's all right ….
Hmm? Oh! You can see me! That's a relief. Can you hear me, too?
I'm no mage, but I think I might have a leg up here. Either way, it's going to make for a good story.\n\nThat wayshrine near the coral river is our starting point. I'll see you there!
See if this guy can remember anything at all about his old mercenary group, and the job in Skywatch. He's our only hope of finding Silverslip and Song.
Quickly, talk to Captain Marso. We need to know what's going on here.
The druids of the Firesong Circle are dangerous. Nature teaches us that water erodes even the strongest stone over time, but can we truly reason with them? I'm just not sure.
I've spent the better part of the last ten years studying magic and learning about the druids. They saved me when I was young and thought I knew the world. Least I can do is help them out now, right?

Outsider, I fear for my wife—my Gwenaelle. A group of Firesong Druids attacked our home in Y'ffre's Path. I managed to escape the slaughter, but Gwenaelle's still in there. I tried to go back for her, but the path has grown more dangerous.

I get why Mevei didn't put this in her letter, but this is a big thing I've been ambushed with. \n\nI didn't think I could get my memories back. I was going along fine without them. Now I'm getting a whole lifetime back in the span of an afternoon?
Inquiry asked and answered, I suppose. The adversary came here for a dwemeric device to modify his Fateweaver Key.\n\nI'm at a loss. To think this is where my experiment might have led.
As I thought—this is about ancient relics. Torvesard believes they can lead him to Ithelia, the Forgotten Prince. But I do not yet see how he hopes to make use of them.

Savor this moment, proxy. In saving West Weald from Ithelia's servants and destroying her Loom, you won a great victory. But I foresee this respite will not last long.\n\nNow, I believe Beragon is waiting to thank you.
Death hounds are vampiric creatures. What are they doing sniffing around a vineyard when there's bound to be far more blood at the manor?
See what <<1>> has brought us.
Not even the realm of the One Who Knows is safe from the unraveling of existence.

The Sutch Depository is across from the tavern.\n\nBalandrus always had ambitions. But to become the Terror of the Weald … I saw all the signs but didn't want to believe he was capable of such atrocities. Still, I left at the first opportunity.

I can't make sense of it. What do Ithelia and her Shardborn seek to gain here? Why assist the Recollection and allow them to use wildburn seeds to transform West Weald?\n\nWhat are we missing, friend?

Hear that, traveler? The crash of swords on shields, the roar of soldiers? A battle already rages for Feldagard Keep.\n\nI rode at breakneck speed to deliver news of an impending attack. Seems I arrived too late.

I knew I could count on you the moment you wandered by. You've got that twinkle in your eye.\n\nMy friends, Wisteria and Oleander, should have set up camp at Monkey's Rest. Let's go and make sure they're all right. I'll meet you there!

You found it! I thank you, zha'al. Like the moons above, my strength returns to me in phases.\n\nAhh, there. It fits like it once did, though its magic seems to have waned. Did you find anything else?
Any friend of the Gryphon's is a friend of mine!

A sketch hidden in a ring of mushrooms? Curious. I find mushrooms disturbing. Did you know they're alive? That they talk to each other? Isn't that horrific?\n\nAnyway, what do you make of the drawing? Some sort of map, maybe?
The blank sheet of paper is right there on the table. Just pour a bit of the ink wash onto it and see if it reveals any hidden writing. \n\nA little goes a long way, so don't get too wild.
This place is not as deserted as it seems. My gauntlet reacts when it gets close to dro-m'Athra, and it is reacting very intently right now. Be ready for anything, tamiit.
Past this waterfall, tamiit, are the clawholds that lead to the training ground. \n\nMind yourself. The fall from the climb can bruise one's tail.

Let us follow Cantor Krin'ze's wisdom. We may understand more about what to expect from the meeting with High Cantor Viti if we speak to the townsfolk in Pa'alat. Let us see what they have to say about recent events in their area.

I never expected the enemy to be the Worm Cult. Thought they were finished after we stopped the Planemeld.\n\nObviously Merric has a plan to crush them. Let's get to Sentinel and the Sisters of the Sands Inn and see what this magister can tell us.

I was raised in King Fahara'jad's court and am equally comfortable crossing the Alik'r Desert or the Abecean Sea. But it has been the Fighters Guild and Guildmaster Merric that have hammered me into shape and tempered me into the man I have become.
No hurry—I'll wait here until you do.

At times I wonder if I should have remained a chef rather than join the Mages Guild. Perhaps I'd have served the Emperor. "Served" … a jest, you see?\n\nBut I have no regrets. Mastery of three crafts is its own reward.
Please, friend, please! Look all you like, spend freely, spend it all!

I'm glad you were able to answer my summons. \n\nWe have much to do if we want to fight back against this Dragon invasion. And with so many lives currently at risk, the sooner we begin our preparations, the better.
Damn the man! He wouldn't let me get a word in edgewise!\n\nMother always knew how to talk to him. Me? Not so much.
No sign of that witch or the reliquary she ran off with. We should get back to the jarl's hall.

Damn! I can't believe Vandacia is a traitor and a cult leader! And he killed Faleria … almost killed Lovidicus!\n\nHe's been ahead of us the entire time. We can't let him get to the Ambitions. We just can't!

So, here we are. The city gardens! Now, I guess it's time to, uh … time to rouse the spirits, eh?\n\nI'm ready! Are you ready? If you're not, we can wait a while. In fact, maybe we should come back tomorrow. Start fresh, you know?
You've been gone for some time. You managed to persuade the locals to share their stories with you, yes? Did their firelight tales share any common themes?
I've seen a lot of Daedric ruins in my life, but never ones quite like this.
Mom was definitely here. She had to have gone in a hurry if she left this scarf behind. Did Edvilda write down anything that would clue us in on where my mother's gone?
The hilt should be somewhere around here. \n\nLet's find it before Langley makes it past those trees!
Once Guruz is sober, we need to probe him for information about Silverslip and Song. He has to remember something! If he can point us in the right direction, we may have our next lead.
Why go to Rivenspire? What are they up to?
There's so much suffering across Galen right now. I fear we will all carry the scars of this unrest until the end of our days.
We might have to swim a bit to get to Broken Tusk. \n\nI don't mind it, but I know swimming in crocodile-infested marsh water isn't everybody's cup of greef.
Oof, that knocked the wind out of me.\n\nWe have much to discuss. Let's do that breathing some fresh air, under an open sky, if you don't terribly mind.

Torvesard departed and took Boethiah's blade with him. If only we arrived sooner … yet perhaps we were not meant to stop him here. Fate often takes many turns before it reaches its destination.\n\nI wish I knew why he wanted the relic, though.

Look about you, proxy. West Weald is safe. I played only a small part in setting things right—the true credit belongs to you and Beragon.\n\nYou should speak with him before you continue your journey.
The new grapes are certainly unusual. Let's keep looking around before we jump to any conclusions.
It seems Betu has more to show us. Let's follow him deeper into the tunnels.

It's obvious there was trouble here. Tham's tattered cloak, his bloodied sword. And the note he managed to leave for me. Clever of him to tell me where to find the surviving townsfolk without alerting the vampires.
I'm beginning to think I don't understand the Recollection at all. Everything we learn about them only raises new questions.
If Feldagard Keep falls, so does the Colovian Highlands. We must defend it at all costs.

When we get to Monkey's Rest, don't tell Wisteria you found me frozen in ice. She still hasn't let me live down that time I got stuck in a window on the third floor of Cey-Tarn Keep.\n\nYou'll love her though. Like a viper with killer eyelashes.

Please. The moonclaw. It is a … what is the word? Armlet? Metal hoop for your wrist. With a stone like moonlight.\n\nI would search with you, but I feel very weak. I am not yet ready to get to my feet.
An illusory mushroom! I knew this was going to be fun! Go ahead and examine it. Let's see what the Gardener has left for us.
You can mix the ingredients for the ink wash at the workbench. Just there, by the fireplace.\n\nNo trick to it. Just combine the oil and petals as evenly as you can.
I am beginning to think Cantor Izalgo was drawn here by a ruse. A trick of the Rajaska to isolate him and turn him to their ranks.\n\nWe should get to this Goldfolly as soon as we can.

Caverns so often contain monsters, or those driven to become monsters. Watch your step.\n\nIt has been some time since the faithful walked these tunnels to the training ground. We must re-find the path.
You speak to Krin'ze and see what she thinks of the high cantor's summons. Between the two of us, it is no secret that you are easier to talk to.

I never expected the enemy to be the Worm Cult. Thought they were finished after we stopped the Planemeld.\n\nObviously Merric has a plan to crush them. Let's get to the Tall Trunk Tavern in Vulkwasten and see what this magister can tell us.
I want you to craft a simple iron dagger. First you'll mine some iron ore, then refine the ore into iron ingots.\n\nYou'll use those ingots to make the dagger.
It's a shame. Dragons ravage nearby villages and Senchal fears the approach of Dragonfire. Yet no one seems willing to fight back.\n\nHmm. You seem like a warrior of worth. Perhaps you can aid me?

I—I just need a moment to think about how to approach this. Consider the words to use. My courtly manners are a bit rusty and I've never been much for diplomacy and fancy speeches.\n\nShor's bones, I could use a drink!
There it is! Let's smash the pike and get after that witch!

I heard what Beragon told you. Ojel-bak. I never heard of it either, but my brother sure picked a terrible time to admit that with all his vast knowledge, he doesn't know the word we need the most.\n\nHey, Councilor Lovidicus wants to talk to you.
Go on! Let's see if this lantern is worth what I paid for it.

I find the idea of a play fort quite quaint. I never had any such thing as a child. Nor much of a childhood, for that matter. I suppose I've resolved to have one now, in a sense, but we have more grown-up matters to attend to. Let's get after Annyce.

We didn't get far with our expedition before things went sour, but the ruin was in pretty bad shape. You'll need a grapple bow to get anywhere quickly. Fortunately, I have a spare.\n\nThey're simple enough to use, if you've never tried one.
I didn't really expect to find my mother here, but I at least thought Edvilda would be able to tell us where she went. We have to find out what happened here.
Here we go! Just up the path, here.\n\nThis brings back some memories ….

All right, there. It's done. \n\nWould you mind carrying it back to Guruz? I'm struggling not to hack up my last meal. It smells like … no, forget it. If I even say it out loud, I'll hurl. Let's just go.

We picked smelly plants, to give to a thief, so he'd return the wine he stole and the clerk won't get in trouble with her smuggling partner. All so she'll tell us where Marso went.\n\nI know I've read something like this in a story before.
Did she just say what I think she said?\n\nTalk to her, will you?
Don't worry about me! Deal with the fates!

It seems our investigations have led to the same place. Use the portal to enter the hidden shrine.\n\nWe must determine what interest Torvesard has here. How he expects a Boethiah shrine to lead him back to Apocrypha and the final glyphic.

I imagine the leaders of Skingrad and Vashabar want to thank you for saving West Weald from the Recollection and the Shardborn. Saving reality itself by destroying Ithelia's Loom probably escaped their notice.
Let's keep looking around. I'll try to make sure nothing catches us by surprise. Plenty of places to lurk unnoticed in this vineyard.
You should share what you discovered with <<1>>. She is the only inheritor left for her aunt's estate.
