I gave that sword to Tham after he had a bit of trouble with some very drunk caravan guards. He kept it on a hook behind the bar. Never once saw him draw it while I was around.\n\nObviously, it got some use recently.

I may never feel warm again! But where are my manners? Nice to meet you! Name's Tanlorin. And that ice trap was definitely not on my schedule today.\n\nNow, I suppose I owe you an explanation. Have you ever heard of a group called the Garland Ring?
Kra, my head. Azurah, forgive my cursing in a holy place. Is this a holy place? Where am I? And who are you?
I'm sure there's more to this puzzle than a single riddle. I can't wait to see what the Gardener leaves for us next!
All we need are some flower petals and a little oil. Ideally linseed, but any old oil would do fine. \n\nWalnut, poppy seed, bugloss. You get the idea.

Cantor Izalgo readily came to Redfur to answer a plea for help. And when he disappeared, Krin'ze dropped everything to come after him.\n\nIt warms my heart to see such kindness, but I worry it may be the undoing of these cantors. Let us ask around.

Khenarthi's Rise was ancient even in my age. I trained there as a young adept of the Hidden Moon.\n\nIt lies in the southwest reaches of Reaper's March. I wonder if I will even recognize it after all this time.

Ja'kh will find our little moon-singer and lead her to a safe location outside Dune. I would worry about danger on the road, but Krin'ze has proven quite adept at moving like a shadow.\n\nAll the same, let us not keep her waiting too long.
Looks like I'll be squashing this little worm after all.\n\nNo Merric yet, but it feels like we're getting closer. Go over what we just learned.
Truly, I never expected to master three crafts.

Thank the gods! If I had to sit in here one more moment without a drink in my hand, I'd lose my mind!\n\nBut I promised myself I wouldn't touch the stuff. Not a drop until this Icereach Coven business is finished.
Barrows are creepy enough without this clinging, red mist. Let's keep searching.

Now that Vandacia and his cultists have run off, you should talk to my brother, Beragon. He's the scribe that Councilor Lovidicus sent for.\n\nI think he was able to translate at least part of the coded documents before Vandacia grabbed them.

Thank you for agreeing to accompany me. With your help, my next romance novel will be a masterpiece!\n\nHere, take the lantern. Now, fair warning—I've never actually used it. But I heard a ghostly woman wanders the city gardens. We can test it there!

Heseph mentioned that two of his neighbors also had loved ones vanish: Bradon Davaux and Jahhouz. Speak with them. They may be more open with a less … grandiose traveler.\n\nYou might also speak with Heseph directly, if you wish.

There were five, in addition to me who got duped into this. My brother, Liam; Eolaf, a Nord warrior; Ardia, a High Elf researcher; Deejos, an Argonian scout; and Ghalor, a Wood Elf adventurer.\n\nOther than my brother, I don't know a lot about them.

Steamfont. I know of it. Dwemer ruins re-purposed by some resourceful types for perfecting certain kinds of crafts. Never had reason to go there myself. It shouldn't be too hard to find though.\n\nLet's head to Stonefalls before Edvilda moves on.
We can get to the ruin before them if we hurry. The path around to the ruins is off to the east. Let's move.
Phew! That's strong. We're going to be stinking like this for a few days, I guarantee you. But that should be enough for what I need.\n\nGuh, sometimes I really hate having a keen sense of smell.
These outlaws lurking beneath the city … gives me a bad feeling. Let's get in and out as quickly as possible. All right?
Then we're off to the swamps. Wonderful. \n\nTry not to catch anything. Unless it's fish.

The Interval Chamber is deep within the complex, past the approach and on the southern end of the ruins.\n\nLet's be cautious, calm, and clever cohort. The constructs of the long-departed Dwemer are extraordinarily dangerous.

We have been led to the ancient city of Dune. Interesting.\n\nDo you see the threads of fate glowing before you? Follow them and see where they lead. There are subtler clues here I must examine, but our paths will converge again soon.

Even if the relics no longer contain any power, they should be preserved. Honored for their part in preserving our world. Put them away for now. Perhaps we can figure out a more permanent solution later.
Don't let the beauty of this place fool you. I sense a darkness beneath the light.
This one briefly inspected the library before the will became the investigation's focus. We have learned much since then. Perhaps we will discover there's more to the scene than Mizzik once thought.
I'd know that cloak anywhere. It was Tham's favorite. Said it made him look wealthy and successful.\n\nIt's definitely seen better days, but at least it's not covered in blood.
Look at you. An eye-catching adventurer with an ambiguous smile.\n\nI could really use your help. I was on my way to meet some dear friends when I got caught in this trap.

I'm glad I waited until you were available. We make an excellent team, if I do say so myself! Let's meet in Malabal Tor and find this ring grown in loam near Belarata.\n\nAt least this wasn't a Hyacinth riddle. Those always involve math.
Ha! Snapdragon, you angry genius! I don't know how the Ceythalmor beat us here. Or what happened to Snapdragon, or what was in those burnt pages. But this blank piece of paper has my heart racing.
You speak to Cantor Krin'ze while I watch for any lurking Inquisitors.

Something is in the wind, tamiit. Can you sense it? A song, a scent … no, a memory. From well before I was interred.\n\nKhenarthi's breath bears a secret missive from the twilight. My moonclaw pulls, like someone taking my hand. I am being summoned.

I received an interesting summons, tamiit. Sent by High Cantor Viti, who has been advising the Inquisitors that sent assassins against us. The one who mistrusts my necromancy.\n\nShe wants us to visit her at a camp just southwest of Pa'alat.
This little worm claims he's renounced his evil ways? Guess I won't gut him like I planned.\n\nNo Merric yet, but feels like we're getting closer. Go over what we just learned.
I have nothing left to teach. Have you spoken with <<1>>? He can certify you in enchanting, alchemy, and provisioning.\n\nLast I heard, he was in the local Mages Guild.

You and Lyris risked your lives for my kingdom and have been met with nothing but suspicion. You counted on my mother to be your advocate, to convince my father of the coven's threat. Now she's gone.\n\nI'm no substitute, but … I'll speak for you.
You know what I hate about Nord barrows? Draugr! Let's make this quick.
Sometimes our adventures are just like the stories … but most of the time, they're not at all like them.

Are you from around here? Sorry, I'm not familiar with Gideon and … wait! Are you here because of my fliers? Thank Ruptga!\n\nCall me Yisara. I'm here on a thrilling, inspirational journey! And I could really use a sturdy companion.

My, my, you're as free roaming as a traveling circus. I wouldn't have expected we'd cross paths on the other side of Tamriel. I would invite you to join us as a guest performer, but our show is canceled indefinitely.\n\nOn account of drama. Ironically.
Who are you? Another of these useless Leyawiin layabouts? \n\nNo, you're an adventurer, like me. Don't tell me Xigira roped you into this mess too.
Mirt better have worthwhile information about my mother, or I might need to add assault to my list of crimes for the day.

It's not worth a row with Langley over who can search the woods first. I'd best him easily, don't get me wrong. \n\nBut blatant fighting between aspirants is frowned upon. Doesn't matter, I have an idea.

If we can get this guy to sober up, hopefully he'll be able to tell us more about Silverslip and Song. It's amazing Jhaka was able to track him down at all. We can't waste this chance.\n\nLet's get that sour algae!
Doesn't anyone ever just do something helpful, without asking for favors first? \n\nI know, I know. That's not how the world works.
Glad you were there to smash that stuff. That tyranite calx.\n\nWhy can't these wizards just name things in a normal way?
Let's head inside. We must reach the adversary before they do anything catastrophic or cataclysmic. \n\nAlso, dibs on any soul gems we find inside.

A Skein of Secrets, somehow used to defeat Ithelia long ago? I cannot help but wonder what became of it. Daedric relics have a way of causing trouble wherever they appear.\n\nEven the Echonir could be dangerous in the wrong hands.

I am relieved to see our world remains whole. I was reasonably certain you destroyed Ithelia's Loom before she could weave a new history, but it is good to have that belief confirmed.\n\nSpeak with Beragon, proxy. He is waiting for you.

First, let's look around the vineyard. I want to examine the grapes they grow here. Besides, it's a good idea to get a feel for the grounds before we head into the auction.\n\nNever fear. This is exactly what House Ravenwatch trained me for.

Let me see that. Definitely Tham's letters, though obviously written in a hurry. He says one thing but means another. Very clever!\n\nHe's not talking about wine, that's for certain. And I know exactly where he wants me to look when we're done here.
Whoa, a brand new greenhouse! The Gardener must be taking this Ceythalmor threat very seriously.\n\nThat must be why he used a riddle to disguise the location. Could you make any sense of it?
They must have missed something. Let's look around.

Redfur Trading Post. Hmm. I remember Grahtwood from my travels as a young cub. \n\nThe hot days in those jungles could make paste of our moon-sugar stores. If anything has changed since my time, I hope it is the weather.

I don't know much about plants or leaves or whatever. No idea if you got actual mistscrub or not. Don't really care either. All that matters is he thinks you have the right stuff. Then, he'll talk.\n\nIf not, I've got another idea.
I have nothing left to teach. Have you spoken with Danel Telleno? He can certify you in enchanting, alchemy, and provisioning.\n\nLast I heard, he was in the local Mages Guild.

Some of the blame for all this lies with my father. If Svargrim would have listened, we could have mobilized our kingdom's forces before that assassin struck.\n\nBut tell me more about the coven. What can you tell me about this threat?
Go ahead and explain the situation to the jarl. I'll stand back here and try to look friendly.

Hi! Are you from around here? Sorry, I'm just … you know. I'm flustered! Gideon's positively labyrinthine!\n\nCall me Yisara. What brings me here, you ask? I'm here on a thrilling, inspirational journey! And I could really use a well-sculpted friend.

Greetings, traveler. If you've come to witness the marvels and mysteries of our troupe, I hope you haven't traveled far. Our performance is postponed indefinitely.\n\nOn account of drama, ironically enough.
I can't believe I have to steal from a bank for my own fetching mother. This is why no one takes our house seriously.
I'll see you there! I'm hoping we can beat the other aspirants to the hilt.

If we can sober Guruz up, he might be able to tell us where they took Silverslip and Song. But we're going to need a pretty powerful concoction. \n\nThere should be some sour algae near the shore. I can make a brew that'll singe his eyebrows off.

I had no idea Aurelia and Captain Marso kept in touch. And my parents are out of town right now, so I can't ask them where he's gone.\n\nLet's go see what that shipping clerk has to say. They work out of a building back across the bridge.

We don't have much more than we started with at the beginning of this. But we have a name, and we're in no danger of running short on reasons to kill him.\n\nAnd I'm glad we helped Federo, even if it's going to be quite the rough transition for him.
We stand before the entrance to the Dwemer construct known as Nchuleftingth. The adversary must be inside. \n\nIt's imperative we discover his purpose here, cohort.
Stay your blade. Whatever Torvesard was hoping to find here appears to be gone. But he might be willing to explain his purpose if you simply give him the opportunity.
The Forgotten Prince, no longer forgotten. We must find Prince Ithelia before the fate Hermaeus Mora foresaw comes to pass.

Fancy meeting you here, friend! I hope you're not here for the auction at the Valente Vineyards. I'm certain the event bodes ill but I'm reluctant to enter that nest of vipers alone.\n\nWould you be willing to join me? For ample compensation or course.
Those bloodsuckers were hunting. That means they think there's still someone or something to find.\n\nLet's look around and see what they were searching for here in the tavern.

Go ahead. Reach into the sparkles and take the note from the messenger-bug.\n\nYou know, the Gardener never summoned me before. Usually Hyacinth sends the briefings. And his aren't nearly as flowery. A shame, too, considering all our flower references.
No sign of Snapdragon, but there's soot all over the floor. Someone burned something here, and not too long ago.
Ah, tamiit. Cantor Krin'ze sent us a letter. She wants to meet, though she avoids saying exactly why.\n\nYou remember her, yes? The Dagi Twilight Cantor? She is much like the Moon-Singers of my day.

Those Worm Cult bastards are back? I thought we crushed them after the Planemeld crisis.\n\nCan't believe you agreed to get something to relieve his pain when I just want to end it—permanently. I suppose we need to hear what he has to say though.
There's only one more certification I can provide. If you need training, I have time!
Why, if it is not her best friend in all of the world! You are here to make us very happy, again?

Finally! Waiting in a tavern without a drink is maddening! How do other people do it? And Maugh hasn't been helpful. His solution to every problem involves a great amount of alcohol.\n\nWhat news of the bastard who murdered my mother? Did you find him?

I caught the gist of that. That s'wit actually wanted my mom to rob a bank? I'm glad she had enough sense not to go through with it. Unless the reason we haven't heard from her is because she's in jail … no, no, she, she wouldn't ….
Berjo was my previous second. A good man, but too ambitious by half.\n\nGood luck to him. Langley's a bit of a prat.

I would bet good coin that's our guy, Guruz. Mercenaries have a certain way of standing, even when they're older. You can tell from the way they hold themselves. Go on and speak to him. Ask him about Kestrin's Blades and if he knows about my friends.
I … ugh. I can smell the rum from here.

Sondivel Ulres. There is a bitterness to his name that I didn't taste before. I hated him. I'm sure of it.\n\nAnd his lab was deserted, so we have nothing else to go on. And what was that metal? Have you ever seen anything like it before?

I hate entering a portal without knowing where it might end up. But it's occasionally an occupational hazard. \n\nA tip: hold your breath. A memorable excursion saw me stepping from a portal into the middle of the Nibenay Bay. Disaster.

Curious. There was a relic of Azura here, a lamp. No doubt the mages who removed it feared this place would be sacked by the Alessians. A memory preserved since the early First Era.\n\nI wonder what Torvesard wants with the lamp.

You're not planning to attend the Valente Vineyards auction, are you? I'm sure something untoward is going on in there.\n\nHmm, you seem capable. Would you be willing to help me investigate the situation? House Ravenwatch can be very generous.

If you're reckless enough to stand with me against Balandrus's gang, who am I to say no?\n\nLet's make our way to the tavern at the center of town. An old friend, Tham, owns the place. I want to find out what happened to him.
Let's go find Snapdragon and her research. Maybe it'll finally get us on the trail of the traitor.

This is the spot marked on the map, but other than a wounded man and some bodies, there's no sign of Merric. You talk to him while I watch for a trap.\n\nAnd be careful. If his armor means what I think it does, we're in real danger.
Let me know if you have some time. I can train and certify you in something else!

Dad's letter claimed old Mirt over there was highly peeved about whatever deal he made with my mother falling through. I'd just as soon avoid catching an earful, so if you could ask about Irenni as a neutral party he may be more willing to cooperate.
The book was already open … I bet my old second Berjo offered the same advice he gave me to Aspirant Langley. Draigh!
I'm not really familiar with Betnikh. But if there are Orcs around, I'm sure there's some kind of tavern around? Let's try there first and see if we can't find our mercenary friend.
Maybe Nilsmon is down on the docks?\n\nWait, is his awful poetry saying Aurelia set sail somewhere?
Let's get out of here. Please. We can talk outside.
I spent a summer studying these ruins from top to bottom, and learned very little for my trouble. \n\nLet's stay alert for that frayed fate!

I saw the memory. You and your Bosmer friend discovered more than I did. I do not know why Torvesard would seek an old relic of Azura's, but it appears he met with failure. Our search, however, is not yet over.\n\nSay your goodbyes and let us go.

I'm at a loss, friend. I was so focused on stopping Balandrus and saving Tham, I never gave a thought as to what comes next. I guess I need to figure it out.\n\nI told you I hate owing favors, but I can't help feeling that suddenly I owe a whole lot.
Last I heard, Firsthold is a mess. We might have to fight to get to Snapdragon's cottage. But if it means we can track down the traitor, it will be worth the effort.

You'd think a guildmaster wouldn't be as reckless as Merric, but I'm not in any position to criticize his actions. Seems he found the attackers and planned to pay them a visit. That map indicates a location north of here.\n\nLet's go find Merric!
I can train and certify you as a blacksmith, a clothier, or a woodworker. Which would you like to start with first?
Come, come! Our goods are clearly lonely. Come and spend some time, and also money. Spend the money first.

Dad's letter said that the one raising a stink was an old client of theirs named Mirtulivon, a member of the Stormhold Mages Guild.\n\nLet's get to Shadowfen and see just what sort of trouble Mom got herself into this time.
My previous second, Berjo, had a good thought. To look for the early history of the Duforts. \n\nHe likes reading dry texts. I like hitting things with a sword.

So, it's off to Betnikh, is it? I like the name of the place. Full of Orcs, isn't it?\n\nCome on, let's go see if we can find Guruz and get him to tell us more about Kestrin's Blades. Hopefully, he can point us toward Song and Silverslip.

The Ancient Anchor is just south of the main gate. It's been quite some time since I was down there. \n\nHmm. I wonder if they still do amateur bard nights on Fredas. You haven't lived until you've heard Stagger and Sway performed by a drunk Argonian.
Chains. Cages. Darkness.\n\nMaybe forgetting a place like this isn't the worst thing.

Hmm. I wonder if the frayed fate we'll find at Ilayas is a version of me that actually learned something useful from studying those ruins. \n\nAll I had to show for my time there was a few snakebites and an ill-advised romantic entanglement.

You should see the threads of fate as I do. It has taken me a lifetime of study to understand their significance and permutations, but all you need do is follow where they lead.\n\nI will search the area, then join you.
Turn back, traveler. There's trouble in the town of Sutch that you want no part of.\n\nVampire trouble.

You'd think a guildmaster wouldn't be as reckless as Merric, but I'm not in any position to criticize his actions. Seems he found the attackers and planned to pay them a visit. That map indicates a location northwest of here.\n\nLet's go find Merric!
This one has heard the bite is profitable, yes? A strange business, to be sure.

I got a letter from my father. About my mother, Irenni. She's gone missing.\n\nShe has a habit of running off on an adventure at the drop of a hat and being gone for weeks at a time, but dad says she's been out of touch for a while now. He's worried.
Let's meet up at the castle library, in the knight's wing. I've spent many an hour there studying up on monsters, history, and healing.\n\nMy only complaint is there aren't a lot of novels.
Jhaka looks much better, doesn't he? That's a relief. I knew the big boy would pull through.\n\nTalk to him for me, would you? You know me and cities … I want to keep a lookout.
Look at this place. Yech.
I wonder if this lair is where the Reformer kept Dimik-ei before Reynila rescued her. \n\nI wonder if it's somewhere I've been before.

This frayed fate has been hollowed out like a Witches Festival pumpkin. The adversary did this. Must have been his goal at the Lost City of Na-Totambu. \n\nAlso, can you hear the sound of the Dreugh chitin rubbing against itself? I'm fairly sure I can.

Hermaeus Mora cannot see Torvesard, but he can sense threads of fate disturbed by Torvesard's actions. The threads are fraying in Grahtwood, Reaper's March, and Stonefalls.\n\nI will open a portal to each place. Choose one and we shall go.

I know what you are, night hunter! If the Terror of the Weald or whatever Balandrus calls himself these days sent you, know that I'm still the warrior I ever was.\n\nI'm heading into Sutch, and I'll go through you if I have to.

Hard to tell one deserted camp from another, but the Tava's loop knots used to secure the canopy tell me that Merric was here. I've seen him tie those knots in his sleep.\n\nTake a look at that pile of papers and see if they're important.
When this one was young, her tiny father once said: In any given crowd, there is always at least one customer. Is that you?

The Eight must have me in their hearts. My second just left my service, and here I was thinking I'd have to do it alone.\n\nAll right. There are three knightly orders here on the Isle. Let's decide what task to tackle first.
I think I like Marbruk. Lots of Khajiit here, by the looks of it. \n\nCome on, we need to find Jhaka. He's around here somewhere. Big guy like him won't be hard to spot.

I cannot believe Aurelia ran off. What was she thinking?\n\nLet's follow the knight commander's suggestion and see what we can find in Nilsmon's bunk. The way he follows Aurelia around, maybe he knows something.
I'm compiling a list of places I never want to go to again. This place is at the top.
Erroneous. Fallacious. This seems quite wrong. \n\nAs if it was left here for us. A warning?

Thank you for answering my summons, proxy. I am afraid our respite has reached its end. We saved Apocrypha from Vaermina and Peryite, but it seems Torvesard has embarked on a new design.\n\nHermaeus Mora has need of you again.
What Balandrus and his gang have done to Sutch … he's really trying to make a name for himself as the Terror of the Weald.

Trappers warming themselves in a Windhelm tavern claimed to see someone who looked like Merric out this way. Said he was intense, like a man on a mission. I got this far and decided to wait for you.\n\nThe trail leads east, so that's where we're going.
In a bazaar, this is known as a lull. In a store, this is a crowd. For us, this is a good time to pursue individual sales, yes?

I'm sorry, this isn't the best time. My friend Aurelia has a bit of a problem. Her mother has promised her hand in marriage, and I need to get her out of it … somehow.\n\nHmm. Actually you look quite capable. Would you mind lending me a hand?

Once we find Jhaka in Marbruk, I'm sure he'll have something for us to do. He told me to be patient but he knows me well enough to know that's like asking him to change his stripes. \n\nI've been patient for a long time. I'm done with that.
Why don't you talk to the knight commander first? See what she wants?

Let's see. Gnisis nearby, check. Bridge to some Dwarven ruins, check. Secret door, could be anywhere between here and the coast.\n\nLook, instead of wasting our time searching, I have something that might help us.

I tell you, cohort, I thought standing here would have shaken something loose. But … nothing!\n\nWe'll have to follow my tried-and-true method for magical investigation: poke things until they do something interesting.

At last, you are here. Welcome, proxy.\n\nHermaeus Mora, Daedric Prince of Forbidden Knowledge, has marked you as fate's champion. His adversary, Torvesard, once more moves against Apocrypha, threatening not only Mora's realm, but our world as well.

I spotted someone who was the spitting image of Merric moving deliberately through the outskirts of Sentinel and trying not to be seen. I couldn't catch him, but I followed his trail to here.\n\nThe path leads west, so that's where we're going.

I'm sorry, this isn't the best time. My friend Aurelia has a bit of a problem. Her mother has promised her hand in marriage, and I need to get her out of it … somehow.\n\nHmm. Actually, you look quite capable. Would you mind lending me a hand?

You remember Jhaka, right? I got a letter from him. Messy, that thing. It's probably hard to hold a pen in those big mitts of his. \n\nAnyway, apparently he's made good on his promise to research the mercenaries who grabbed him, Silverslip, and Song.

It will be nice to see Castle Navire again. The commander will likely be in her office, off the Knight's Wing.\n\nMy parents have been asking after you, by the way. I've told them you're too busy to go to dinner any time soon.
The letter's not worth discussing. Let's just keep going.

I recall disliking my time in Stonefalls … but I'm having difficulty remembering why. I suppose that's moon sugar for you.\n\nLet's head to Ebonheart. I know I began my time in the region there, so it's at least a place to start.

It is a vexing conundrum. I am not without a certain amount of sympathy for Torvesard and his cause. Yet I have learned that Hermaeus Mora does not lie. If he says Torvesard must be stopped, then we must stop him.

Hunters informed me that they had seen someone matching Merric's description exploring the north. Said he seemed intense, like a man on a mission. I got this far and decided to wait for you.\n\nThe trail leads north, so that's where we're going.
I think my nerves are as settled as they're going to be. I get more anxious doing formal things like this than I do fighting werewolves!\n\nCome on, Izzy. Deep breaths.

Poor Jhaka. I'm glad we got to him when we did, I don't think he would have lasted much longer. I can't imagine the amount of suffering he's been through.\n\nEven still, he's determined to help us in the search for Song and Silverslip.
I have news! I've received a letter from the Knight Commander. \n\nShe asks that I return to Castle Navire at my earliest convenience.
Find anything worthwhile? Or do we need to go back and shake down Federo for something better?
Another set of frayed fates. Here's hoping they're a bit more luminous than those in Kozanset.\n\nI believe we should start with Stonefalls.
That little prince Azah never mentioned he was sending you to meet me! How the tusk have you been, pal?\n\nNo, hold that thought. We've got work to do.
What would you like to do next? We still have the Iron Knot trial and the Order of the Albatross to hammer out.

Thanks for talking with him. I didn't trust myself not to cry. \n\nWhen I was small, hanging around Jhaka always made me feel safe. Even now that I'm grown, I have that same feeling. I can't believe we found him … after all this time. Thank you.
Next chance I get, I'll stop home again. Have some proper time with my parents.\n\nAnd try to talk my mother out of forcing you to dinner. Stendarr help me.
Let's go dig up that cache.
You're almost as accomplished at this scrying ritual as I am. Hah!\n\nPrepare the site, and I can locate the frayed fates we seek.
That little prince Azah sent word that I should meet up with you. Not like I couldn't handle this on my own, but who am I to argue with a tusking prince?

We've only got the Iron Knot trial left. Let's meet up in the Castle Library. \n\nBerjo, my previous second, suggested that the early history of the Dufort family was a good place to search for clues.
Keep Jhaka talking while I try to get him healed up a bit more.\n\nHe always hated being coddled. Distract him while I at least stop him from bleeding out.
I had no idea we'd end up wandering the length and breadth of Tamriel just to get that ring back! \n\nI guess it's true like they say in the stories. Adventure is around every corner.
Don't know about you, but I'm ready to see what's in that cache.

Back at it again! I was quite pleased with our last outing, threats to my very existence aside. \n\nThe arcane bobbin … ugh, wish we'd come up with a better name … was a smashing success. My sagacity astonishes me sometimes.
Good thing the Fighters Guild exists. They let me punch people and get paid for it.

The Order of the Albatross is the only trial left. I've been dreading this one. \n\nNot so much because we're going to have to go into a crypt, as because they're going to expect me to recite a poem when this is all over.

Fish biscuits! What kind of bastards would take someone so sick down into a place like this? I hate them!\n\nCome on, we can talk more once we're out of here. We need to get this big boy some fresh air.
So … now you've met my parents. They really are the sweetest people. Even if they can be a little much.

Yeah, Federo is going to whine about the clothes, but I don't really care.\n\nIf his information pays off in some way, I'll make sure he's paid off appropriately. But I want to see what he gives us first.
In your own time, cohort. The Skywatch sanctum will be well protected by Gubbins in the meantime.\n\nHmm. Hopefully he still recalls the proper steeping interval for a cup of Orcrest rooibos.
All that's left is to go to the tourney pavilion and present our trophies. \n\nMy nerves are jangling like horse barding!
Go ahead and talk to Jhaka while I try to heal him a bit. He's in rough shape.
My parents live down by the harbor. I'm sure they'll be happy to see me. Less happy when they hear about the ring, probably. But we have a good relationship. \n\nI'm not nervous. Nope.
Now to the hard part. Clothes shopping.\n\nLet's make this quick. And spend as little coin as we can. Federo's really in no position to be fussy.

Cohort, I need to be transparent with you. Not literally, of course. All that line of inquiry led to was some traumatized street children in Sentinel.\n\nI can't stop thinking about my adversary. The frayed fate that wants to replace me.
Place each item as I announce the trophy, if you please.
Don't waste time talking to me! That's Jhaka! We need to get him out of that cage.
Finally holding it again … this little thing caused so much trouble. Damn. \n\nI can't tell you what it means to have this back.
You should talk to him. I can smell his anxious panic from here.
My research will take time. And I like to be considered in my stitching on dear old Gubbins. \n\nYou know how pets can be.
I've always wanted to be a knight. Fighting for justice, righting wrongs. \n\nActing as a shield for those who have none.

Keep your eyes and ears open. Remember, Jhaka's a Pahmar, so he's probably going to be hard to miss. Even still, let's stay vigilant. I'm not wasting this chance. I have waited too long to lose track of him now.
If the ring isn't where he said it would be, we're going to go back there. I'll hold him up by his greasy hair and you'll whack him like a Witches Fest candy totem.

A while back, I said I'd write Mevei about finding more of that metal we discovered in the Reformer's lab.\n\nWell, she finally got back to me. Not about the metal, but about Dimik-ei. The one Reynila was helping escape when she … you know. Died.
Just when I thought we had this experiment under control, an evil reflection threatens to consume my fate and replace me.\n\nHmm.

If Osithos was telling the truth and Jhaka is really sick, then we need to rescue him quick. I have no idea what a bunch of bandits would want with a sick Pahmar. I can't imagine they're nursing him back to health out of the goodness of their hearts.
I'm not entirely comfortable with Julles and Galedra taking justice into their own hands. \n\nBut they're not the murderous type, it seems. I suppose Stendarr would approve.
Remember I told you to be ready for the day we were going to find and kill the Reformer and rescue Dimik-ei?\n\nWell, I hope you're ready. Today's the day.
I need to think and ambulate, cohort. Let's get out of these damned ruins.
Let's get to Pulk and find those bandits. If Jhaka's sick, that's the last place he should be. Plus, I need somewhere to direct this … energy. Clawing my way through a few mercenaries might help.
Of course he gave up quickly. Can you find out where my ring is? \n\nAnother moment and I might pick him up and shake him to see if it falls out of his pockets.

Federo ran instead of trying to turn me over to the Reformer. I didn't expect that from anyone. Let alone someone like him.\n\nWe'll see how reliable this forger is in Adept's Retreat. As for clothing, I have no idea what we're going to do.
Panic! Terror! Consternation! Let's stop that thing!
Come on, let's go give Osithos his damned bracelet. Hopefully, he'll make good on his word at the very least and tell us where to find Jhaka.
That skeever is going to want to bargain, isn't he? It makes me so angry, he should be arrested. \n\nBut if he'll give us the signet back ….
Eastmarch, of all places. The armpit of Skyrim.\n\nFedero must be really desperate to hole up at this Tinkerer Tobin's place. I'm sure he's just miserable.
I can sense a perturbation in my fateline. My adversary is close.

Heh, you were a little too good at that. You make a pretty cute monkey, anyway.\n\nI got the bracelet. It's just as ugly as I imagined. It'll be perfect for that overblown bastard's wife. Come on, let's get back to the inn and throw it in his face.
If I wasn't so worried about getting the signet ring back, I'd laugh.\n\nKiv's problems are coming home to his doorstep.
Federo and I were complicit in Reynila's death, but Mevei doesn't seem to be holding it against us.\n\nI'm relieved, even if part of me still feels like she should hold it against us.
My adversary has followed us, somehow. Quickly, cohort. Let's get inside.

Go on, just approach Varvisi. Be casual about it. It'll be over before you know it! Dance like a good little monkey and we'll have the bracelet in no time.\n\nOh, don't look at me like that. You'll love it.
I am so sorry, this was supposed to be a quick trip to Stros M'Kai. \n\nNow we're running off to Craglorn after a thieving skeever with my family's signet ring.
She's lying. She's not Federo's type.\n\nAnd again, I hate that I know that much about him.
The threads will lead us where we need to go. I'm sure of it.

That must be Varvisi there. A merchant like that always has their most valuable wares on their person. No problem. I can rifle around in her pockets without her ever suspecting a thing.\n\nBut for that to work, I'm going to need your help.
Aurelia is going to go beet red when she hears what an absolute scoundrel she got herself involved with. \n\nAnd now his other victims are along for the ride!

So, Federo's not just a coward, but a liar, too. As if I cared about him enough to track him down and kill him. He should be so lucky.\n\nThe Elf is too drunk for me to understand most of her story. What'd you get out of her?
Much to discuss from the fates we've seen. Commendable work. But … something's not quite right.\n\nLet me see the Fateweaver Key a moment.
I heard, I heard. Typical Telvanni. \n\nIf we have to get him his damned bracelet, let's just do it fast. He said Varvisi Uleni sells outside Tel Naga, right? Let's go. I've got a plan brewing.

Kiv must be something else. The way the barmaid talked about him, the tone of that letter from the fellow in Wayrest ….\n\nDon't get me wrong, I'm still going to punch him in the throat. But he seems interesting.
Federo's a lot more tidy than this. If someone's living here, it's not him.
Let the threads of fate lead us. Let's keep at it.
Ugh, this place is awful. You can just smell the misery.\n\nCome on, let's ask around about Jhaka. I don't want to spend any longer in here than we have to.
Wayrest is a pretty big place. Didn't that letter say Julles is often at the Temple of the Divines? Let's try there.

Probably better that I don't go to the seat of House Telvanni in Vvardenfell alone when there is someone in the higher ranks obsessed with my capture.\n\nI know I don't say it a lot, but I appreciate you sticking with me.
Let's keep at it! The threads of fate will lead us where we need to go.

We need to get to Gateway Inn and rescue Jhaka. If he really is a Telvanni slave, I intend to free him. \n\nBut let's be smart about it. I want to get him out of there as quickly and as painlessly as possible.
We're looking for a double-crossing, two-timing thief and rogue … who is also apparently quite the charmer!\n\nUgh! Let's take a look at Kiv's things. See if they hold any clues.

I need to tell you something. You're the only one I know who's nosy enough to care.\n\nIt's about my former job broker, Federo. I've been wanting to have a word with him ever since everything went tail-up on my last job. You know, the one where we met.
Distressing to think I'd ever take up … clerical vestments. Ech. Use the key, quick as you please.

I cannot picture sweet, gentle Jhaka in a fighting pit. In Sadrith Mora of all places! If he's truly a Telvanni slave, I will tear out every throat I find. \n\nThis is my fault. If only I'd been faster that day. Come on, let's get to the Gateway Inn.
Vvardenfell has always sounded so mysterious to me.\n\nI mean, I'm from an island country as well, but the Dark Elves, their culture … it seems so very different than the Systres.
If I can kill Sondivel, I don't care if the rest of my memory never comes back. I'll remember that he's dead, and that will be good enough.
Go ahead and use the key. We'll return this poor researcher to the weave of the Aurbis.
Talk to Brisha for me, would you? \n\nBeing back here makes me uneasy. I feel like all my hair is standing up. I prefer to keep a lookout.
I hoped this would be a quick trip to a distant port. Retrieve the ring, then share a drink at the docks.\n\nInstead … I have to ask if you'll sail to Vvardenfell with me.
Eyes open, ready for anything!
Brisha should be around here somewhere. I'll let you know when I see him.
Maybe someone here on the docks will know where this Kiv Lindres went off to. \n\nDockworkers always know what's going on. Well, at least they do in stories.
Let's keep an eye out for those frayed fates.\n\nAh, and if by chance someone shouts my name? Just say "where?" and start looking around like you don't see anyone.

The tip came from an old friend, Brisha. We'll find him near Skywatch. Big softie never left the place. \n\nThis is the first lead on my friends I've had in years. I'm afraid to get my hopes up. It's been so long. Is this really my chance to find them?
I cannot believe she followed some Dark Elf knave with a wink and a grin to the far side of the world!
Smell that? This place reeks of camel spit and unrealized potential. Hmph.

So, I'm not good at this sort of thing, but there's something I want to talk to you about. Did I ever tell you I grew up in Skywatch? I was raised on the streets, but not alone. I had friends. Good ones. \n\n And I want your help finding them.
There she is, with … oh, is that Captain Marso? Marso works for my parents, a good man. \n\nCould you talk to her first? Let me get my thoughts in order.
There's a lot of places to see in this world.
I'd honestly hoped never to have to return to Kozanset, cohort. Hoped with the incandescent fire of Magnus himself. Hah!
Thank you so much. Hopefully Aurelia will exercise a little wisdom and stay put.\n\nAccording to her letter, we should find her at the Screaming Mermaid inn on Stros M'Kai.
Scrying has provided us direction, focus. Even if I am unexcited about the prospect of returning to the Alik'r Desert.\n\nI suppose I should have seen this coming, at some point.
My friend, I am not in the habit of asking for favors. But … well. I just got some news from Aurelia. \n\nYou remember her, my childhood friend we helped during the tourney?
We've pierced the esoteric veil of reality and forged the tool of our own self-liberation! \n\nWho's an amateurish rune-scratcher now, Telenger? Hah!
Don't worry, it didn't hurt. Just reach into the leftover Gubbins goop and grab that bobbin. \n\nReally wish I'd come up with a better name for that.
I don't like standing around. Let's get to it, shall we? Magister Irin used to say it was dangerous to leave me idle for too long.
Gesticulate wildly in Gubbins' general direction. Don't worry, this won't hurt him.
The expertise and aptitude it took to imbue the stencil with such a complex spell …. Heh.\n\nI'm quite good at this, you know.
It's such a breath of fresh air, being out in the world with you. The Systres are beautiful, but Tamriel is so vast! And wonderous!
I appreciate you taking on the legwork, cohort. Fashioning the stencil took some considerable effort.\n\nThink of this as an opportunity to walk in the well-heeled slippers of Azandar al-Cybiades!
Welcome to my sanctum sanctorum! I've been meaning to invite you over before now but something always seemed to come up.\n\nMind the books, now. Some of them bite.
My sanctum is in a ruin at the center of Skywatch. Can't miss it.\n\nDon't mind the sentinels posted by the entrance. A compromise between myself and Telenger of the Mage's guild. Feh.
Cohort, I have exceptional news. My preparations are completed and the time is now! \n\nTime to return to our fateweaving adventure!
